| 2026-09-04 | **CR-068 WAVE C SHIPS ITS FIX AS `2.137.2`, AND ALL THREE FAULTS WERE FOUND BY CLICKING — hard-won law 6, three times in one hour.** **(1) THE FUTURE-DATE CHECK ON `portal_consent` MEANT THE WRONG CLOCK AND REFUSED EVERY HONEST SUBMIT (`DEF-CWP-3709`).** `portal 0003` wrote `CHECK (agreed_on <= now())`; in PostgreSQL `now()` is the TRANSACTION'S start time and never moves again. The submit numbers the service request and stamps the draft before it writes the consent, so Python's clock is a few milliseconds past that fixed instant by then and the database answered *new row for relation "portal_consent" violates check constraint "ck_portal_consent_agreed_on_not_future"* — which the applicant saw as *"Something went wrong on our side. Nothing was saved."* **`portal 0005` rebuilds the same constraint name around `clock_timestamp()`**, the wall clock, re-read per row, which is what `03-field-map.md`'s *"May never be in the future"* always meant. Proved on a scratch database BEFORE the migration was written: with `clock_timestamp()`, a row inserted 0.05 s into a transaction is accepted and `now() + interval '1 day'` is refused. The RULE did not move — a consent nineteen days out is still refused, in the database's own words — and an applied constraint cannot be edited in place, so the repair is a new migration and `0003` is stamped SUPERSEDED rather than changed. ⚠ **THE WHOLE SUITE WAS GREEN ON BOTH ENGINES AND COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT:** SQLite has no such constraint at all (law 14) and the one PostgreSQL case wrote the consent as the FIRST statement of its savepoint, where transaction start and wall clock are the same instant. The new case writes it AFTER other work in the same transaction — RED on `0003` with the database's exact sentence, GREEN on `0005`. **(2) THE PORTAL'S OWN IN-FLIGHT GUARD REFUSED THE PORTAL'S OWN FORM, AND ONLY THE LAST FIELD WAS LOST (`DEF-CWP-3710`).** `PORTAL_INFLIGHT_MAX` admits two requests at a time; a save per field puts six in the air in eighty milliseconds and the third is answered `429` with `Retry-After: 1` — correct, and the guard saying *the door is full* rather than *no*. `DEF-CWP-3706`'s repair (send the whole form every time) makes a dropped save harmless for every field EXCEPT the last, because nothing follows it; the draft was missing `requested_start` and *Send* answered *"Finish an earlier step first."* about a step that was finished. **The judgment: ONE save in flight, coalesced, rather than a wider door or a slower form.** A save asked for while another is running is merged into the pending patch and sent the moment the first returns, so the newest value always wins and the last field is always sent; a refused save is re-queued ONCE after the second the guard asked for; and *Send* waits for anything still on the wire, with the button held in its sending state so nothing on screen claims more than is true. Widening the guard was rejected because the guard is right — it is `NFR-39`'s answer to one visitor costing a utility its whole capacity — and the form was the thing behaving badly. Measured after: the walkthrough's saves fell from **8 PUTs with one `429` to 4 PUTs with none**. **(3) A COMPUTED-STYLE CHECK THAT READ A PAGE AFTER IT HAD MOVED ON REPORTED `null` AND WOULD HAVE PASSED OR FAILED FOR THE WRONG REASON.** Fixed by measuring the errand card while the cards are on screen. A check whose output cannot distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check — the same shape as `DEF-182`. | the CR-068 wave C build lane | `12-governance/10-defect-log.csv` `DEF-CWP-3705`–`3710` · `06-backend/apps/portal/migrations/0005_consent_not_future_by_the_wall_clock.py` · `CHANGELOG.md` 2.137.2 |

The premises always exists; the account is where a person usually starts. This does not touch `OQ-373` and must not wait on it. **(2) THE SIX VIEWS SPLIT BY WHAT OWNS THE FACT** — Overview · Units · Assets to the premises, Charges · History to the account (they are the account's existing `bills`/`adjustments` and `audit` tabs, so nothing new is built for either), and **Work orders on BOTH**, because both are anchors and the question is asked from either side. **(3) THE LIST IS SCOPED BY PATH, NOT BY A SEVENTH FILTER** — `GET /accounts/{id}/work-orders` and `GET /premises/{id}/work-orders`, **so `BR-WRK-026` does not move**: the dispatcher keeps exactly six filters and still answers `400` on a seventh. Two new filters would have made it eight and put a signed rule in the way of a screen. **(4) THE FLOW STAMP IS `source` + `source_ref`, AND NO NEW ANCHOR.** A flow-raised job already stands on an anchor it has — the move-out's visit on the account it closed, the request's install jobs on the premises it resolved to; what is missing is only a reference back, and every flow record already carries a number a clerk quotes (`MVO-…`, `SR-…`, `TRF-…`, `DSC-…`, unique per tenant). **Worked against the alternative: one nullable FK per flow takes `work_orders` from 4 anchor columns to 9 and `ck_work_orders_has_anchor` from a four-way CHECK to a nine-way one, and adds four cross-module FKs to B2 §2's reviewed interface set for a link only ever read to print a reference. The CHECK does not move.** **(5) `/connections/<uuid>` REDIRECTS, IT DOES NOT 404** — the New Connect wizard's completion, the *New connects* tab, `AccountsListPage.tsx` and every bookmark point there today; a 404 breaks a working link to punish a screen. **(6) MOVE-OUT'S VISIT HANGS OFF STEP 2, NOT STEP 4.** `MOVE_OUT_STEPS[3]` carries `conditional: true` (`moveShared.tsx:216–221`) and renders greyed and *skipped* whenever the account settles, so the plan's control would have been invisible on the ordinary move-out. Filed as `DEF-WRK-3725` before it was moved. **(7) A FLOW OFFERS THE JOB AND NEVER RAISES ONE SILENTLY, AND COMPLETES WHETHER THE RAISE SUCCEEDS OR NOT** — `BR-WRK-055`'s posture, written for move-out, applied to all five; a flow that failed because a work order could not be created would let the field module block a customer's move. **(8) A REQUEST WITH NO RESOLVED PREMISES CANNOT RAISE A JOB.** `resolve_address` (`service_request_service.py:968`) can leave a request with no unit and no premises — one taken by phone for an address not yet in the system — which has NONE of the four anchors, so the CHECK would refuse the row. The judgments made where the rules ran out, each decided and written here rather than put back to the PO (law 13):** **(1) THE APPLICANT'S DRAFT IS ITS OWN TABLE, NOT A `service_requests` ROW.** Two CONFIRMED statements collide and the code settles it: `US-CWP-013` §2 says *"a draft holds no allocated number until submit"* and TC-1 asserts *"no reference has been issued"*, while `BR-CUS-093` (PO 2026-08-24, *"At creation — every draft is numbered"*) makes `create_request` allocate `SR-26-nnnn` inside its own transaction. Wave B's `report_a_problem` became one `shape` of `raise_service_request`; its body is unchanged and private. A portal write nobody declared is the alternative, and it is worse than a rename. **(4) THE CONNECTION FEE IS A CHARGE CODE AT ITS CATALOGUE AMOUNT, AND THE PLAN ONLY BINDS IT.** `US-CWP-012` §5 maps *To connect* to *"the connection fee on the effective tariff"* and there is no such column (`DEF-CWP-3703`). The product's fee is a `one_time` charge attached through `PlanChargeRule`, and **`amount_override` is NOT consulted** — PO 2026-08-19 ruling 1, *"no plan cannot override prices"*, which `rating.resolution` already honours. A public price read that consulted it would quote a number the bill would not charge. Effective dating is the PLAN's, so a plan that is not PUBLISHED or whose window has not opened quotes **nothing** rather than next quarter's price. **(5) THREE CELLS THAT ALL LOOK LIKE "nothing" ARE THREE DIFFERENT FACTS, AND THE FIXTURE SEEDS THEM SEPARATELY.** Water `$185.00` is a priced charge; Sewer **Included** is NO one-time charge attached at all; Trash **$0.00** is a charge the utility configured and priced at zero; Electric **NOT HERE** is the absence of a service point, drawn as an em dash. `US-CWP-012` TC-4 is explicit that the fourth must not read `$0.00`, *"which means free"*. **(6) THE DEPOSIT QUOTED IS THE RESIDENTIAL ONE, AND THE SCREEN PROMISES NOTHING.** `plan_deposit_rules` is one amount per plan per customer class and a visitor on `CWP-008` has not said what kind of customer they are; somebody moving into a house is residential, and the box says *"$150.00 deposit on your first bill"* rather than a final figure. **(7) RECOGNITION ANSWERS TRUE OR FALSE AND NOTHING ELSE CROSSES THE SEAM.** `US-CWP-013` TC-7 asks that the existing matcher be used; `identity_match.recognise` returns a verdict, a tier, a basis sentence and the candidate rows, and the seam keeps **only whether it found anybody**. A boolean cannot be leaked into a response body by a later serialiser and a list of half-matched customers can. | 2026-09-03 | **THE LOCKBOX IMPORT IS BUILT, AND THE FIVE JUDGEMENTS IT NEEDED WERE DECIDED AND WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN PUT TO THE PO (`CR-059` CS-2, law 13).** A utility on a bank lockbox gets one file a day carrying hundreds of cheques and types every one by hand; `apps/payments/lockbox.py` held the statement parser and said in its own docstring that the remittance family *"arrives with US-PAY-003"*. It has now arrived: the parser, two staging tables with RLS and a freeze, a staged service and six routes. **The two new rules are built as written** — nothing is applied on upload, and a name-and-amount match never commits on its own. **THE FIVE JUDGEMENTS, each because the signed rules stop short of it.** **(1) THE REMITTANCE PARSER'S ERROR POSTURE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE STATEMENT PARSER'S, IN THE SAME FILE.** `parse_bank_statement` refuses a WHOLE FILE on one bad row and its lifecycle block says why: *"a statement is not a list of independent rows: half of one reconciles to nothing."* A remittance file IS a list of independent cheques and `BR-PAY-023` says *"per-row errors skip with a report"*, so one smudged amount must not cost a clerk the other 399 cheques. The error travels ON the row. **(2) THE 🔒 TAG FIELDS ARE THE LOCKBOX ACCOUNT AND THE DAY THE FILE COVERS**, authored under `BR-PAY-028`'s own *"key mechanics Eng-Lead 🔒"* delegation and mirroring the statement half's shape. Its hole is named rather than hidden: the same file lodged against a different bank account is a different key and imports — right when a clerk picks the wrong lockbox first, and the one door a determined re-import could walk through. The database closes what a key can: UNIQUE (tenant, file_hash, tag_fingerprint) over COMMITTED batches only, exactly the scope `uq_read_import_batches_idempotency` already uses under `OQ-044`'s closure. **(3) AN UNMATCHED ROW IS `review`, NEVER `error`.** An unplaced cheque is WORK, not a fault; `error` is reserved for a row that could not be READ. A screen that conflated them would tell a clerk that four hundred perfectly good cheques are broken, and the preview counts a person decides on rest entirely on that line. **(4) A BILL NAMED IN THE FILE IS PROVENANCE, NOT AN ALLOCATION INSTRUCTION.** `allocation._check_targets` treats a named bill as a STAFF instruction (`specific`/`split`) that overrides the tenant's own order, so passing the bank's reference field through as a target would silently override every utility's allocation policy four hundred times a morning on the strength of what a lockbox operator typed. `US-PAY-003` §5 says the rows are *"each allocated per `BR-PAY-010`"* — the tenant's order — so `invoice_id` stays on the staged row as provenance and the allocator runs its ordinary course. **(5) THE NAME HEURISTIC IS DELIBERATELY NARROW** — it matches only a legacy `external_ref`, because the published account index carries no customer name and payments may not fetch names row by row for a 400-line file. A wider net produces more suggestions, and a suggestion this module cannot justify is a row a person must read and dismiss. When customers publishes a name index the way it publishes `account_import_index`, one function changes. **WORKED, so the figures are concrete:** a three-row file of `292.87` + `1,204.55` + `57.13` where only the first and third quote an account number previews as **2 clean, 1 review, `350.00` matched** — not `1,554.55` — and the commit records two payments. | 2026-09-03 | **ONE CHEQUE THAT PAYS SEVERAL ACCOUNTS IS BUILT — CS-12 FIRST AND CS-27 ON TOP OF IT — AND THE SIX JUDGMENTS INSIDE IT, NONE OF THEM PUT BACK TO THE PRODUCT OWNER (`CR-059` CS-12 task 49, CS-27 task 51, law 13).** **(1) THE SILENT TRAP IS FIXED BY DESIGN AND THEN GUARDED AGAIN, AND BOTH GUARDS ARE ASSERTED SEPARATELY.** `CR-059` CS-12 flags it in terms: the duplicate guard is keyed on **tenant + token, NOT on the account**, so a form minting one token and reusing it across three accounts has payments two and three treated as replays — *the server returns payment one, reports success, and writes nothing*. **Worked: in the drawer `$520.00`, recorded `$184.20`, errors raised none.** The fix is `tenders.tender_part_reference(submission_key, account_id)`, which shapes the REFERENCE half and hands it to `idempotency.inbound_payment_key` unchanged, so one place still builds the stored string and one unique index still catches a duplicate. **A fourth `SOURCE_` namespace was considered and declined:** it would separate a multi-account submit from an ordinary one, and a clerk who recorded 184.20 on the S22 form and then submitted the same cheque through the customer form would take the money twice. **The second guard — a NEW tender may not own a part that already existed — exists because `DEF-058` is what happens when one guard silently stands in for another**, and it is what turns the silent failure into a loud refusal. Both were broken through `monkeypatch` first (never by editing a live file, `DEF-3101`); with both off the suite records $184.20 against a $520.00 cheque and raises nothing, which is asserted deliberately so the pair cannot be removed as a simplification. **(2) TWO PARTS ON ONE ACCOUNT ARE REFUSED BY NAME RATHER THAN MERGED.** Both rows would derive the same part key, so the second would be stored as a replay of the first — the same trap wearing a different hat. Merging them would silently change what the clerk asked for on a money path with no record; adding two figures up and entering them once is what one payment on one account has always meant. **(3) N JOURNAL ENTRIES, NOT ONE PER TENDER — AND THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THE TWO SPECS PULL AGAINST EACH OTHER.** `CS-27`'s narrative says *"ONE balanced entry per tender: DR undeposited 742.60 / CR AR ACC-1042 184.20 + …"*. What is built is **four entries whose debits and credits sum to exactly that**: the receivable that falls is the UNIT's in both readings and the trial balance is identical, but the ledger holds four entries and not one. Three reasons and none is convenience — **`CS-12` rules in terms that the per-payment entries *"must not be rebuilt"*** (*"three balanced journal entries are not an error (each settled a different account's receivable)"*); **CS-27 is built SECOND and *"extends CS-12 rather than repeating it"***, so it may not reverse CS-12's own ruling; and composing a new multi-account entry shape is a change to the 🔒 ledger-posting path, which is its own review surface. **Stated in the module docstring with the figure rather than left to be discovered** (hard-won law 1). **(4) A LEFTOVER IS REFUSED ON THE PREMISES PATH AND REPORTED ON THE CUSTOMER PATH, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE POINT.** `BR-PAY-1130`: a landlord typing **$200.00** against a flat that owes **$184.20** would leave **$15.80 of their money as that tenant's credit**, auto-applying to the tenant's next bill — refused, whole, with the figure named. The run is sequential rather than parallel so the server sees the order the clerk sees; a failure is RECORDED and the loop CONTINUES, so nine successes are not thrown away by the tenth refusal; and every row ends with an outcome of its own — done, refused before it was sent, or failed with the server's own sentence. **The successes are then DESELECTED and the failures stay SELECTED**, so pressing the button again retries only what did not happen. That is not a nicety: a second refund raised over a first is money out twice, and a retry that re-ran the whole selection would do it. **Each row's idempotency key is minted once per bulk session and REUSED on a retry**, because a network failure is ambiguous — the write may have landed and the answer been lost — and only a stable key makes the retry safe. **JUDGMENT 3 — BULK REFUND IS ACH-ONLY, AND THE CHEQUE'S ABSENCE IS A SERVER RULE READ OFF THE SERVICE, NOT A SCOPE CUT.** `refunds.request_refund` refuses a cheque refund with no cheque number, verbatim: *"a cheque refund needs its cheque number ... without it the refund cannot be matched to the bank line when it clears"*. Three selected payments are three refunds and therefore three cheques, and one number cannot serve them; inventing a run of numbers would be this screen writing cheque numbers nobody wrote. So the bulk modal offers ACH, says in one sentence that a cheque refund is raised one at a time, and `S58` keeps the cheque path. **JUDGMENT 4 — THE CHECKBOX RIDES IN THE IDENTITY CELL AND NOT IN A NEW COLUMN, AND THAT IS `CS-43`'S PREREQUISITE TOO.** A new column key is invisible to any user who has ever saved a column set: `columnsFromPreference` filters the stored list against the config and a key that was not stored is simply not shown, so the whole feature would be missing for exactly the clerks who customise their list, silently, with every test green. `BR-SHL-013` guarantees the identity column can never be hidden, so the tick sits beside the payment number it selects and no preference can lose it. **AND THE SELECTION IS A SNAPSHOT MAP, NOT A LIST OF IDS — WHICH IS WHAT MAKES `CS-43` HONEST WITHOUT THE SERVER ENDPOINT.** `S34` holds ids and filters the CURRENT PAGE by them, so a row selected on page one vanishes from the total when page two is shown: the figure silently shrinks and nothing says so. It is NOT repeated: `reporting.revenue_by_service` is the ONLY place in the product that filters on a type rather than printing one, and it filters on REVENUE — a discount typed wrongly put 10.00 of revenue the utility never earned into three surfaces, while an accumulated-depreciation row typed `asset` changes no figure anywhere, because the trial balance takes each row's side from its own NET DEBIT. Accumulated depreciation is also presented within the asset section of a balance sheet, as a deduction. **(2) NO `normal_balance` COLUMN.** CR-061 §5 finding 3 names it as a column the product does not store; it stays unstored, because for every value in `LEDGER_ACCOUNT_TYPES` the normal side is decided by the type, and a column would be a second source of truth for a fact the type already states. **(3) `1290 Allowance for doubtful accounts` IS LEFT TO ITS NAMED OWNER**, `CR-060` T15, whose own words are *"only if IFRS or Ind AS markets are in scope"*; write-off is direct today, `DR 6900 / CR 1200`, and seeding an allowance account offers a policy this product does not implement. **(4) SEEDING A PAYABLE IS NOT ACCOUNTS PAYABLE, AND SEEDING A TRANSFER ACCOUNT IS NOT FUND ACCOUNTING.** `OQ-200` (PO 2026-08-16) rules that capture posts NOTHING because `CR accounts payable` would leave $37,200.00 of settled-elsewhere liability standing after twelve months at $3,100.00 of purchased water — **that objection is about POSTING and is untouched here**, since nothing credits 2000 and the account reads $0.00 until a human writes a manual entry. `CR-060`'s DERIVED sentence *"no `2500 Accounts payable` is proposed in the chart"* is **SUPERSEDED** by the PO's own reference chart, which contains the block, plus their instruction to complete this CR. `T1b`'s fund ruling is the same shape: it ruled on a fund TAG, a dimension on a journal line, and a chart heading is not a dimension. **WHAT DID NOT MOVE:** no price, no rate, no B4/B5 figure, no golden test — `G61` reads 130 frozen money figures unchanged, `03-golden-verify.py` 33 PASS / 0 FAIL and `G64` 14 of 61 engine-verified, before and after. Summing the cost ACCOUNTS instead would report drift on a correct book the first time an accrual or a manual entry touched 5110 — the same trap `_ar_row` avoids by not summing `accounts.balance`. **JUDGMENT 4 — THE COST ROW TAKES NO WINDOW**, like the deposit row and for `DEF-2250`'s reason: the register side has no book date, and a July-windowed control would read 0.00 against a full register for the ordinary purchase paid in August. **NO SIGNED FIGURE MOVED.** LE-11's nine purchases carry no `paid_on`, so US-LED-021 TC-1's five rows and **$51,902.50** are unchanged and asserted so; LE-1's **598.69** is untouched; `G61` reads 130 frozen figures unchanged. **TWO STALE CLAIMS RETIRED WITH IT, BOTH HARD-WON LAW 1 IN A PAYLOAD RATHER THAN IN A COMMENT:** the drill-back still rode `posting_shape_is_not_ruled` — a code SUPERSEDED on 2026-08-16 when the PO closed `OQ-200` and removed from `cost_section` the same day — so it told a finance officer a ruled question was open for a fortnight, and the test pinned the stale value; and the section label named **52,501.19** as *"where the trial balance moves the day a supplier-payment path ships"*, a day that will never come (the boundary moved by a paid-on date instead) and a figure the T6 lane had already measured **150.00 high**. **PROVED RED FIRST, BOTH ROWS.** T6c: `assert Decimal('3100.000000') == (Decimal('3100.00') - Decimal('1240.00'))`. T6d: the drift row sabotaged to compare the control against itself went `assert 'agreed' == 'drifting'`. **NOTHING WAS PUT TO THE PRODUCT OWNER** — `CR-060` C1 and the T6c/T6d rows are already written, no signed figure moves, and law 13 makes a judgment recorded here the deliverable rather than a question. | the `CR-060` T6c/T6d lane | `CR-060` T6c · T6d · `DEF-3380` · `DEF-3381` · `BR-LED-007` · `BR-LED-039` · `OQ-1350` |

Keeping a stylesheet alive purely to declare names nothing styles would be worse — a rule that exists to satisfy a gate. So the handle became what it always was in spirit: an ATTRIBUTE. `data-wizard="frame|rail|content|actions|blocked"`, and `data-wizard-step={n}` with `data-state="active|done|upcoming"`. **26 assertions across 6 test files were rewritten to match, each preserving what it asserted** — including the two counting tricks, where `class="br-step"` used to match the RAIL as well as its buttons (hence the `5 + 1`) and `data-wizard-step=` matches only the buttons (hence `5`). **⚠ THE BREAKPOINT IS `max-lg:`, NOT `lg:`, and that is not a style choice.** Our scale is DESKTOP-FIRST and Tailwind's own is min-width, which is exactly why `--breakpoint-*` is cleared and re-declared with `--breakpoint-lg: 1024px`. `max-lg:` IS the ported `@media (max-width: 1024px)` rail-scroll rule (A12, US-SHL-010 TC-7); `lg:` would compile happily and mean the opposite viewport. **And the migration bought headroom the CR-023 build needs:** `g31`'s declared-class count fell **891 → 885**, and the ceiling was lowered to 885 the same commit to hold it. It had been AT 891 with no room at all, which is what a lane building new UI under rule 21 would have hit first. Verification: **1,867 frontend tests in 110 files**, `tsc` clean, the Route B utility check 9/9 — *"every class token compiles as a utility or is declared by a stylesheet"* — and `g13 g31 g34 g35 g36 g37` green. |

Recording an unlooked-up address as `no_email_address` would put a figure on the dispatch home claiming N customers have no email address when the question was never asked — the same lie `apps/billing/release.py` refuses about mandate coverage. **This is engineering vocabulary, not a business ruling; if the PO wants the two collapsed, say so and it collapses.** **(6) NO EMAIL/SMS ROW IS WRITTEN WHILE THE ELECTION IS UNREADABLE.** `accounts.paperless` / `.sms_reminders` are PROPOSED-SCHEMA and unbuilt. Writing an email row for every bill would assert an election no column records, for every account at once; writing none is what a missing election honestly produces. So **every bill today produces exactly ONE row — the print floor** — and the gap rides the result as `delivery_election_unreadable`. J17's finished shape (240 print + email rows for paperless accounts) arrives with no code edit the day customers publishes the read. **(7) `template_code` is OPTIONAL on a queue row; the PIN is required for a bill.** `bill_templates` (r10 #4) does not exist, so a bill's writer holds only the id+version frozen on the invoice — and BR-BIL-026 makes that pair the thing a reprint renders from. | 2026-08-11 | **THE S31 BILL-RUN ROUTES ARE SERVED — and the NINE engineering calls behind them, none of which is a PO ruling, recorded here so the next agent does not re-derive them differently.** What shipped: `POST /billing/runs` · `GET /billing/runs/{id}/findings` · `GET /billing/runs/{id}/exceptions` · `POST /billing/runs/{id}/exceptions/{caseId}/resolve`, in `06-backend/apps/billing/api.py`, against services that had existed and been tested since 2026-08-11 morning with **no route reaching any of them** — the S31 wizard's steps 2 and 3 rendered their shape with no contents for exactly that reason (hard-won law 2, from the API side). **(1) THE CREATE ANSWERS 201 WITH THE ID INLINE, NOT 202 + job_id.** 11b marks that row STALE against B12 r1's async law; the reading taken is that the law governs ASYNC operations and creating a `bill_runs` row queues no work — and TD-17 means there is no worker to queue it to. `job_id` is served **null** under its contracted name rather than omitted or invented. `run_id` is deliberately not ALSO served (`billRunIdOf` reads `id ?? run_id`; two names for one value is DEF-014's shape). **(2) THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY IS `"<cycle uuid>\|<period ISO>\|<period ISO>"`** — a 🔒 mechanic, ledger row opened, worked figure in it, and the three sub-choices (cycle UUID not code · ISO not locale · tenant by constraint not by string) are argued in `core/idempotency.py`'s own docstring. **(3) THE RUN'S SERVICE DATE IS THE CYCLE'S `bill_date`.** Not chosen freshly: `issue.derive_due_date` already ruled and ships *"the only bill date in the schema is `cycles.bill_date`"*, and following it keeps the pricing pivot and the due date on one date. | 2026-08-11 | **BILLING IS CONNECTED TO THE BOOKS — BR-BIL-011's stage 7 is emitted for the first time, INSIDE the issue transaction.** Two complete engines existed and nothing connected them: `apps/ledger/posting.py` (837 lines, the sole writer of journal lines) and `apps/billing/issue.py` (which froze a bill and deliberately emitted nothing, saying so on every result via `posting_handoff_not_emitted`). **So a bill could issue — immutably, with a number a customer can quote — and its money never reached a single ledger account; the meter-to-cash loop was open at its last step.** `apps/billing/posting_seam.py` closes it: it reads the ISSUED invoice and the lines BR-BIL-010 has just stamped, groups the line amounts by that frozen `gl_account_id`, resolves the tenant's AR account BY DESIGNATION, and hands ONE balanced request to `apps.ledger.posting.post` — resolved BY NAME, so billing never imports the ledger (B1) and writes no journal line (CLAUDE.md rule 5). **THE SIGNED FIGURES IT REPRODUCES, read back out of `journal_lines`:** US-BIL-005 §7 / US-BIL-009 §7 (CONFIRMED, WE-1/BS-1) — electric usage **88.60** + electric base **12.00** + water usage **39.50** + water base **8.00** post as four separate credit buckets (4100 · 4105 · 4110 · 4115) against **DR 1200 AR 148.10**; GT-1's frozen 82.08 + 18.50 posts **DR AR 100.58**; and the three-authority bill of BR-BIL-069 posts **three separate 2200-series buckets** rather than one merged tax credit. **FIVE DECISIONS A REVIEWER SHOULD RULE RATHER THAN APPROVE, each recorded here because the conversation does not survive and the repo does.** **(1) THE HANDOFF RUNS INSIDE THE ISSUE TRANSACTION, which REVERSES billing's own written argument.** `issue.py` said emitting here would put *"two money events with different failure modes in one transaction"*. They are not two events: one bill issuing IS the money event, and the journal entry is where it is recorded. Committing them apart produces the two states nothing can repair — an issued, immutable bill whose money is in no ledger account (hard rule 4 leaves no path to add the entry later), or an entry whose bill rolled back. Measured under mutation: with the call wrapped in a `try/except`, the surviving state is **`assert ('issued', 0) == ('draft', 1)`** — bill ISSUED, journal entries ZERO. **(2) THE BOOK DATE IS THE BILL'S `service_date`, NOT THE DAY IT ISSUES.** In plain English with the figure: *the June bill you issue on 3 July is recorded in the books under 30 June.* Read off US-BIL-009 §1, which states the handoff as *"{invoice id, account, service_date, per-GL bucket sums, AR total, currency}"* — `service_date` is the only date in it — and made possible by the PO's OQ-107 ruling that posting and actual dates differ. **§7 does not restate it, so it is flagged for the PO.** **(3) A BUCKET NAMES THE INVOICE, NOT ONE INVOICE LINE.** §7's bucket is a SUM (WE-1: **15 stamped lines → 9 buckets**), so BR-LED-001's per-line `source_type`/`source_id` is satisfied with `invoice` + the invoice id. `apps/ledger/models.JournalLine` comments that an issue entry's lines trace to individual `invoice_line` rows — both cannot describe these rows, and the finance-signed bucket shape was chosen; | 2026-08-11 | **THE FOUR NON-CYCLE BILL TYPES ARE BUILT (US-BIL-011/012/013/014) — and the NINE engineering calls behind them, none of which is a PO ruling, recorded here so the next lane does not re-derive them differently.** Shipped: `apps/billing/single.py` (the bulk wizard in single-account mode), `backbill.py` (per-sub-period tariff versions), `final_bill.py` (deposit-first + the five-path settlement matrix), `penalty.py` (assessed reads priced by back-billing), `settings_seam.py` (the S71 finance controls, typed). **(1) THE BACK-BILL'S SUB-PERIODS ARE THE CALLER'S AND ARE NEVER DEFAULTED.** `cycles` carries a single window with no recurrence rule, so "the six months Jan–Jun" cannot be derived from this database at all; the wizard knows which periods were missed. A whole-window default would reset tiers ONCE instead of per period (BR-RAT-002) — worked on the WE-10 tariff: 6 kgal x 6 months as ONE period puts 31 kgal in the top block (5 x 4.00 + 31 x 6.50 = **221.50**) where six monthly groups put 1 kgal there six times (6 x 26.50 = **159.00**), a **$62.50** overcharge nobody would question. **(2) THE WHOLE BACK-BILL IS PRICED IN ONE `price_bill` CALL, NOT ONE PER GROUP.** B4.2 taxes Σ(rounded taxable lines) ONCE: WE-10's frozen taxable **278.82** gives tax **26.36**, while taxing its six months separately and summing gives **26.37**. One cent, every back-bill, forever. **(3) `months_spanned` COUNTS CALENDAR MONTHS TOUCHED**, conservatively — BR-BIL-018 caps a window in months and no signed document defines the count, so a window reaching into a 13th calendar month is 13 against a 12-month cap even if it is one day long there. Conservative is the right direction of error for a consumer-protection limit: it refuses a case a human can approve as theft or shorten. **(4) `bill_run` IS REQUIRED ON EVERY AD-HOC CALCULATE**, not optional. Stage 6 replaces an existing draft keyed on (tenant, account, bill_run); with `bill_run=None` an interim bill for July and a back-bill for Jan–Jun both key on NULL, so drafting the second SILENTLY DELETES the first. **(5) DEPOSIT INTEREST IS READ FROM CUSTOMERS, NEVER COMPUTED IN BILLING, and a deposit whose interest cannot be read REFUSES.** BR-CUS-057 is a customers rule whose accrual engine (US-CUS-023 §7) is unbuilt — customers' own move-out handoff says so. Applying the principal alone was the available shortcut and it shorts WE-7's customer by **$3.50** (150.00 credited where 153.50 is owed) and GT-61's by **$22.25**, on a bill that foots and an account nobody looks at again. An account with NO deposit answers zero without the seam. **(6) THE WRITE-OFF BRANCH IS TESTED BEFORE THE REFUND BRANCH.** A remainder inside the tenant threshold writes off in BOTH directions (US-BIL-011 TC-5), so a **$3.20** overpayment is a write-off and not a refund — issuing a cheque for it costs more than it returns and leaves an open refund on a closed account. **(7) THE TRANSFER TARGET IS ALWAYS A SEAM'S ANSWER, NEVER A CALLER'S ARGUMENT** — which makes US-BIL-011 TC-6's "transfer forged to an arbitrary account" unrepresentable rather than merely rejected. Today the seam does not exist (OQ-069's landlord-agreement link has no table anywhere), so the path is simply not offered and says why. **(8) A PENALTY BILL IS A BACK-BILL WITH A DIFFERENT NAME** — BR-BIL-019 says assessed reads are *priced by back-billing*, so `penalty.py` composes `backbill.py` and holds no arithmetic; a theft bill and a catch-up bill can therefore never round differently. **(9) FROZEN FIGURES ARE ASSERTED ONLY WHERE THE ENGINE CAN REACH THEM.** WE-10's water half (26.50 / 8.00 on v3, 28.10 / 8.50 on v4) is asserted exactly; its sewer line is not, because the engine has no percent-of-service model. WE-11 is asserted NOWHERE — it is TOU and the engine has no TOU model, and its TAMPER $500.00 needs a charge-code reader rating does not publish. Auto-deriving it is **OQ-160**, refused by name. (b) **Ambiguity never matches**: two batches tying one line, or two lines tying one batch, leave both alone. (c) **A bank line is not paired by its reference text** (`CARD SETTLEMENT STRIPE`) — parsing a method out of a bank's prose is a guess, and BR-PAY-023 forbids silent guessing. (d) **The BOOK date of the reconciliation is the BANK's posting date**, because that is the day the bank confirmed the money and confirmation is what the ruling makes decisive. (e) **Unreconcile reverses the entry** (**OQ-163**, raised): leaving it shows CASH for a batch the product calls unmatched, and the next reconcile would realise the same money twice; the replay key therefore carries an ATTEMPT number so a corrected re-reconcile posts rather than replaying. (f) **A resolution's amount is SIGNED** (bank − recorded), and the posting turns the sign into a SIDE, because `journal_lines` cannot carry a negative. (g) **The batch code is COMPOSED, not allocated from `number_series`**: BR-TEN-035's grammar has no method token and demands a sequence token, and one batch per day per method is not a counter. **Which exposed OQ-162 / DEF-066: `DEP-{MMDD}-{METHOD}` has no YEAR, so 8 Aug 2027 renders PE-10's frozen `DEP-0808-CHK` and the second year's money cannot be banked** — refused by name rather than renumbering a ❄️ figure. (h) **The method token uppercases the method code**, with PE-10's two frozen abbreviations (check→CHK, cash→CSH) as the only exceptions — which reproduces the prototype's DEP-0805-ACH and DEP-0804-CARD and exposes that the prototype's own DEP-0802-**CASH** contradicts PE-10's **CSH**. (i) **Batch membership is WRITE-ONCE** — migration 0005 opens the door `payments/0002` deliberately shut and narrows it to NULL→a batch, so a payment joins one batch forever and **no regroup path exists** (US-PAY-020 TC-5 mentions one; nothing ratifies its shape). So in July the invoice IS **$292.87** — real lines, real per-service GL stamps, tax on the real taxable base — and **$242.00** is the collection schedule printed beside it. **Under "tax follows the amount billed" the built model is therefore already correct, and there was never an under-remittance to fix.** The ruling does not move a line of code. **WHAT IT DOES MOVE IS MY OWN RECORDED ARGUMENT, WHICH WAS WRONG AND IS STRUCK ABOVE (2026-08-12 row).** I recorded the fork's second branch as *"move revenue to the level billed and need no account (simpler books; wrong with the tax authority)"*. **That parenthetical no longer holds.** If revenue moved to the level, the level would BE the amount billed, and taxing it would be lawful in a jurisdiction that taxes billings. The tax authority no longer decides this fork in either direction — the PO is right about that, and the correction is theirs, not mine. **THE TWO REASONS THAT SURVIVE, NEITHER OF WHICH IS TAX, and they are why the recommendation is unchanged:** **(1) A LEVEL HAS NO LINES.** $242.00 is one blended number. Tax needs a TAXABLE BASE and the GL needs a PER-SERVICE split (BR-BIL-067 maps service → revenue account). A level carries neither. **Worked, on the reference bill's own shape:** of a **$128.88** total, only **$100.58** is taxable — usage; the **$15.00** service fee and **$5.00** late fee are not. Taxable is **78%** of that bill, not 100%. Bill a level and tax it whole and you OVER-remit by roughly a fifth of the tax on every budget customer; tax none of it and you under-remit; apportion it and you need a share rule nobody has written, derived from actuals the level does not know. **(2) THE CUSTOMER CANNOT READ IT.** A bill that says only *$242.00* does not tell them what they used, which is the one thing a utility bill exists to say. **WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS NARROWER THAN IT WAS, AND IT IS NOT A TAX QUESTION (OQ-142).** With revenue on actuals and cash asked at the level, July leaves **$50.87** standing as an ordinary RECEIVABLE. It is not revenue (counted), not tax (taken) and not an arrear (the customer paid exactly what we asked — OQ-140 already stops the late fee and the dunning ladder). **But nothing stops it reading as an arrear on the BOOKS:** it sits in AR and lands in the 1–30 ageing bucket on the finance reports, where a $50.87 budget variance is indistinguishable from a $50.87 delinquency. The frozen chain is **−50.87 → −40.27 → +2.98** (WE-8), so the balance swings both ways across a year and can end as money the utility OWES. **That, and only that, is what a separate budget-variance account would fix** — a reporting question for finance, not a compliance one. ## 2026-09-11 — CR-085 STEP 2 LANE 4 · HOME AND ACCOUNTS: THIRTY STRINGS THAT WERE NEVER TRANSLATED, AND THE ADDRESS A UTILITY PRINTS ON ITS BILLS SERVING THE GUEST PAGE TO ITS OWN CUSTOMERS

**What a person can now do that they could not this morning.** A customer who
opens `yourutility.example/brazosbend/portal` — the address the utility prints on
the bill and puts in the email — **lands on their own home page** instead of the
public errand grid with a *Sign in* bar on it. A German, Japanese or Korean
customer reading Home sees **twenty-six labels in their own language** that were
English yesterday, the label on the biggest number on the page included. A
landlord on a phone can see **what each property owes and whether it is past
due** without swiping a table sideways. A customer who owes nothing reads *"You
are all paid up."* instead of a bare `$0.00`. A customer whose balance fails to
load gets a **Try again** beside the message instead of a grey sentence and
nothing to press. And the screen about one property — *Your account* — went from
**one inbound link in the whole portal** to three.

### 1 · THIRTY USER-VISIBLE STRINGS HAD NO CATALOGUE ENTRY IN ANY LANGUAGE, AND THE GATE THAT EXISTS TO CATCH THAT HAS AN OPT-OUT

`DEF-CWP-4899`. Every one was `t("some.key", { defaultValue: "English words" })`
where the key was in **none** of the eleven locale files, so i18next rendered the
English default for every reader. Twenty-six were on Home.

**Why nothing went red, and it is a check-that-does-not-check of a particular
kind: the check is correct and it was told not to look.** `G18`'s own docstring:
*"A `t()` call carrying `defaultValue` is excluded and that is not a courtesy:
i18next renders the default, so the author has stated in code that a missing key
is the expected path."* That is defensible for a probe; it is not defensible as
the only rule, because **`defaultValue` is also exactly what a lane writes when
it is in a hurry**. Thirty strings sat in that exemption.

**Fixed, and the shape of the fix is the durable half:** twenty-five keys written
into all eleven catalogues through `10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py` (eleven or none),
**seven not minted at all** because the product already ships those words —
`portal.accounts.colBalance` for *Balance*, `portal.bills.colBill/colPeriod/
colUsage/colAmount/period` for the bill panel's five, `portal.tab.usage` for the
usage door, `portal.documents.channel.pdf_print` for *Post* — and **every
`defaultValue` on a static key removed from the six files**, so `G18` can see
them from now on. Four remain and all four are computed keys where the fallback
is a real data value.

⚠ **THE ELEVEN LINES ARE `NATIVE-REVIEW-OWED` (B14 rule 35).** One author, not
eleven fluent ones. They were written per language rather than translated, taking
the register from the neighbouring keys already in each file — `de`/`es`/`fr-FR`

## 2026-08-31 · "ASSERTED BEFORE AND AFTER EVERY WAVE" WAS ASKING A QUESTION THE TOOL CANNOT ANSWER — CR-052 task 19, and the answer is a new gate rather than a habit

**This is a LANE judgment, not a PO ruling** (law 13 — a judgment call recorded with its reasoning is
the deliverable; a question is the failure to make one). Nothing here reaches the PO.

### THE TASK, AND WHY IT LOOKED ALREADY DONE

CR-052 task 19 reads *"Golden suite unchanged, 33/33, asserted before and after every wave"*. Every
lane has honoured it by hand all day — run `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` on both sides and report
both — and `G4` already runs that harness AND `pytest -m golden` on every gate run. So the first
honest answer looked like *"this is satisfied; record it and move on."*

**IT IS NOT, AND THE REASON ONLY SHOWS UP IF YOU MEASURE IT.**

### WHAT RUNNING IT TWICE ACTUALLY PROVES, MEASURED

`10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` opens **exactly one file** — `04-docs/02-decisions/05-golden-tests.md`
— and recomputes the arithmetic that document states about itself. It never imports the engine and
never reads `06-backend/`. Two things follow:

1. **Around a CODE change the "before" run cannot say anything.** The harness cannot see code, so of
   course it answers the same twice. The ritual is a no-op over the wave it brackets.
2. **A frozen figure can be edited INLINE and it still reports `33 PASS, 0 FAIL`**, because it checks
   the document against ITSELF — and a lane that moves an input and its result together leaves the
   document perfectly consistent.

**Two mutations, both run on the real file and both restored byte-for-byte afterwards:**

* **`GT-3`: base charge `$30.50 → $31.00`, proration moved with it (`15/30 × 31.00 = 15.50`).** The
  harness's ENTIRE summary line came back **byte-identical** to the unmutated run —
  `33 PASS, 0 FAIL | ruling-derived: 6 PASS, 0 FAIL | GT-1..16 self-consistency: 12 PASS, 0 FAIL,
  4 NOT-CHECKABLE | self-test: 8/8 guards bite`. **`$30.50` is the empty-unit charge CLAUDE.md's own
  CR-052 section quotes** (*"Six empty units at `$30.50` is `$183.00` against `$30.50`"*), so this is a
  live cited number and not a dormant one.
* **`GT-1`: rate `$0.12 → $0.13/kWh`, all four dependent figures moved with it.** The headline
  `33 PASS, 0 FAIL` **still did not move.** The harness noticed only in two counters no lane quotes —
  `GT-1..16 self-consistency` went `11 PASS, 1 FAIL` off **GT-10's cross-check**, and its own self-test
  degraded to `7/8 guards bite`. **A GT with no cross-check has neither tripwire**, which is exactly
  why GT-3 was completely silent.

### THE JUDGMENT

**The question "before and after" is reaching for is a good one and it is not "is the suite green":
it is DID THIS WAVE MOVE A SIGNED FIGURE.** CLAUDE.md already states the law — *"Changing a signed
rule or figure needs a finance re-sign via HUMAN-GUIDE §6, never an inline edit"* — and **nothing in
the repository enforced the words "never an inline edit"**. `G1` comes closest and disclaims it in its
own docstring: *"NOT checked here: recomputing the packet hash against the CURRENT story+rules."* The
frozen-source hash is written into every lifecycle trailer and verified by nobody — hard-won law 1 in
its purest form.

**So task 19 is neither "already satisfied" nor "run the suite twice, automatically". It is
`G61 frozen-figures`**, which records the "before" ONCE, in the repo, instead of in each lane's memory.

### WHAT WAS BUILT, AND THE THREE CHOICES INSIDE IT

`10-scripts/gates/g61_frozen_figures.py` + `g61_frozen_figures.txt` + two `.figures` sidecars.

* **It pins the FIGURES, not the file.** A whole-file hash would go red on a typo fix, an added
  superseded stamp or a reading-order note — all things these two documents legitimately gain, and all
  of which are how a gate earns the reputation that gets it switched off. Prose is free; a number is
  not. **That half is proved on every run** by a second self-sabotage that must NOT bite.
* **The manifest is not self-updating and a lane may not re-pin it to get green.** A gate that
  rewrites its own baseline agrees with everything — the guard-list lesson of 2026-08-30 one layer up.
  It changes only with a recorded re-sign, in the same commit.
* **The failure names the figures, never a hash.** `gone: 15.25, 30.50, 30.50 | new: 15.50, 31.00,
  31.00` is something a reviewer can act on; "the digest differs" is not. The manifest and its sidecars
  are two copies of one fact, so the gate checks that they AGREE before trusting either — otherwise a
  stale sidecar would name the wrong figures with total confidence, which is DEF-182's shape.

**PROVED BOTH WAYS ON THE REAL FILE.** On the GT-3 mutation, side by side on one tree:
`golden-verify: 33 PASS, 0 FAIL` and `G61: FAIL — a ❄️ FROZEN figure MOVED — gone: 15.25, 30.50, 30.50 |
new: 15.50, 31.00, 31.00`. On a prose-only edit to the same line: `G61: PASS`. `04-docs/` was restored
byte-for-byte and re-verified at `33 PASS, 0 FAIL` afterwards.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM

It does not check that the ENGINE still produces the figures — that is `pytest -m golden`, which `G4`
already runs, and the two are complementary rather than overlapping: **G4 asks whether the code still
computes the signed answer; G61 asks whether the signed answer is still the one that was signed.**
Neither can be inferred from the other, and until today only one of them was being asked.

## 2026-08-31 · THE VACANT HALF OF THE 2026-08-30 MINIMUM RULING IS BUILT — OQ-1166 closed as (b), and the ruling had reached every document except the code

**PO ruling, 2026-08-30, verbatim** (recorded that day; this entry is what was DONE about it):

> *"when units are vacant - at that time, we are only charging base rates. minimum rates are applied when
> consumer is suppose to use minimum usage, but they end up using less than what they are suppose ot use"*

### WHAT WAS WRONG ON THE MORNING OF 2026-08-31, MEASURED

The ruling was recorded correctly on 2026-08-30, in this file, with its analysis and its four owed items.
**It did not reach the code, and it did not reach the question registry.** On 2026-08-31:

* `06-backend/apps/rating/pricing/stages/apply_charges.py` still topped a base-only service up like any
  other, and said so in its own docstring — *"the rule is applied AS WRITTEN and the consequence is filed"*;
* `12-governance/01-open-questions.md` still read `OQ-1166 · Status: OPEN` under the sentence
  *"Implemented as (a) — the rule as signed — and flagged"*, which is **the option the PO ruled against**;
* so every landlord bill in the product was still charging the `$42.00` the decision log had already called
  money that *"should never have been charged"*.

**This is r11 step 0's named failure mode, one day old rather than three** — *"a PO ruling that reached
every document and not the code"*. It is recorded rather than tidied away because the interval is the
finding: the entry of 2026-08-30 says in its own last line *"Nothing is changed in code … by this entry"*,
which was honest and correct, and nothing carried that sentence forward into a task anybody owned.

### THE JUDGMENT THAT WAS THE LANE'S, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE

The 2026-08-30 ruling covers two different things and they are separable: a minimum **QUANTITY** (a new
column, four owed items, one of them a ❄️ FROZEN `GT-19` re-sign) and the **VACANT** case. **Only the
vacant case is built here**, and the reasoning is that it needs none of the four: no new column, no seed
move, no time-of-use ruling, and — measured, not assumed — no frozen figure. `WE-3`/`GT-19` is a METERED
water household at `0.4 kgal`; it prices a usage line, so it is not base-only and cannot reach the new
branch. `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` reads **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** before and after, and the case is
re-priced inside the new test file so that claim is a measurement in the repo rather than a sentence in a
commit message.

### WHAT SHIPS, AND THE WORKED FIGURE

`apply_charges.minimum_adjustment_line` takes `base_only` and returns None for it. `engine.price_bill` is
the only caller that knows the flag and hands it down; it is **passed, never inferred**, and the reason is
a case in the test file: a base-only service and a metered service that consumed nothing both arrive with
no usage line and **bill differently** — the metered zero is a consumer who was supposed to use a minimum
and used less, which is the PO's own test, so it is still topped up.

    one vacant unit   15.00 - 8.00 = 7.00 no longer charged
    six vacant units  8.00 x 6 = 48.00, where it was 15.00 x 6 = 90.00
    the difference    42.00 a month off one owner's bill   <- OQ-1166's own figure

**Proved RED first (law 7)**, by restoring the pre-ruling behaviour and re-running:
`AssertionError: Left contains one more item: RatedLine(kind='minimum_adjustment', description='Minimum
bill adjustment', amount=Decimal('7.00'), taxable=True, … service='water')`, and
`assert Decimal('90.00') == Decimal('48.00')`.

### WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT, WITH ITS ARITHMETIC

**`DEF-2822` — mode B, the PLAN FLOOR, is unchanged and still tops up a bill made entirely of vacant
units**: `8.00` of base under a `40.00` plan floor is still `40.00`. `OQ-1166` costed the PER-SERVICE
minimum and that is the figure the PO worked; the floor is a fact about the PLAN, and a landlord bill
mixing common areas with vacant units is a third case again. It is filed with its own arithmetic and
pinned by a test that says in its docstring that it asserts a KNOWN GAP and not a desired behaviour — so
the day it is ruled, that is the test to re-point rather than a green test quietly pinning a reversed
rule (DEF-705's lesson).

**The minimum-USAGE half is untouched.** All four owed items from 2026-08-30 stand: the `GT-19`/`WE-3`
re-sign, the time-of-use ruling, the schema decision, and the seed move.

## 2026-08-28 · WHICH DATE AN ALREADY-PUBLISHED UNDATED PLAN GETS — a LANE judgment the ruling deliberately left open, and the two it rejected

**The PO's ruling** (same date, *"A PLAN CANNOT BE PUBLISHED WITHOUT A START DATE"*) says the state stops
existing and *"any published plan today that has no date gets one"* — and says nothing about WHICH date. The
entry recording it stated that gap explicitly: *"What date to give them is NOT ruled here and must not be
guessed."* This is that judgment, made and recorded rather than reported in chat.

**THE RULE: the earliest `effective_from` among the ACTIVATED versions of the rate schedules the plan itself
binds.** A date a human at the utility typed, about this plan's own prices, that the product already stores.

**Worked, on the seeded tenant — and the last column is what makes it right rather than merely plausible:**

| plan | date given | earliest period it actually billed |
|---|---|---|
| SCW-RES | 2026-06-01 | **2026-06-01** — 90 invoices |
| SCW-COM | 2026-06-01 | **2026-06-01** — 4 invoices |
| RES-STD | 2026-08-01 | never billed |
| COM-SM | 2026-08-01 | never billed |
| IND | 2026-08-01 | never billed |

**The two plans that have really billed customers land on exactly the day their first billed period starts.**
Nobody arranged that; it falls out of deriving the date from the utility's own prices. A rule that reproduces
a fact it was not given is a different quality of evidence from one that merely looks reasonable.

**Rejected, each for a stated reason:**

* **Today.** SCW-RES has **90 issued invoices** whose earliest service period starts 2026-06-01. Stamping today
  puts every one of them OUTSIDE its own plan's window, so the ruled path would refuse to explain bills the
  utility has already sent and been paid for. That is the ruling entry's own objection — *"picking today
  restates history"* — and it is the shortcut anyone in a hurry would take.
* **The epoch, or `rate_plans.created_at`.** Both claim the plan priced periods it never priced. On the seeded
  tenant `created_at` is today for all five rows, so it fails in the other direction too; on a migrated tenant
  it would be a draft's first keystroke, months before anything was publishable.
* **The publish date** (`plan_versions` v1, BR-RAT-111). Honest about assignability, wrong about pricing: the
  seeded plans were published today and carry June invoices, so it reproduces the "today" failure exactly.

**Fallbacks, narrowing in order:** earliest dated version of a bound schedule → the v1 filing record's date →
refuse. It does not invent a date when the product holds none.

### ⚠ THE RECORD FOR THIS WORK WAS FINISHED BY THE MERGE LANE, NOT ITS AUTHOR

The authoring lane was terminated by an API rate limit **after pushing the code and before writing any of the
record**: no version bump, no changelog, no business rule, no decision row, and its own `DEF-494` row left
reading `open`. All of it is later than the code it describes, and this note exists so nobody reads the
timestamps as evidence the process ran in order.

**It is also the second demonstration in one hour of `DEF-2103`** — that nothing in this repo asks whether a
row still marked open has already been fixed. `G51` read `DEF-494`'s row and reported PASS, correctly, because
it asks only the forward question. **The structural fix is the one already on the PO's desk: flip the row in
the same commit as the fix**, which would have made this unmissable rather than a thing a human happened to
notice.

## 2026-08-28 · A PLAN CANNOT BE PUBLISHED WITHOUT A START DATE — PO ruling, and it closes DEF-494 by REMOVING the state

**Put to the PO in plain English, with the two readings and their costs, and the PO chose the third option:**
*"Require a date to publish"* — you cannot publish a plan without saying when it starts, so the situation stops
existing; any published plan today that has no date gets one.

### WHY THIS WAS THE ONE QUESTION LEFT, AND WHY IT GATED EVERYTHING

`DEF-494`, high, open: **the live path and the ruled path mean opposite things by "a plan in force", and the
same plan splits them.**

* `rating.selectors.plan_ref` filters on `status="published"` and **consults no date at all** (verified on the
  tip), so a published plan whose `effective_from` nobody typed bills **forever**.
* `resolution.PlanVersion.in_force_on` requires a stated `effective_from`, so that same plan is in force
  **never** and **R1 refuses the account outright**.
* `RatePlan.status` is `draft | published | archived` (BR-RAT-030) and `effective_from` is a SEPARATE nullable
  column, so draft-ness is carried by the status and the date is genuinely optional. (`BR-RAT-031`'s *"a NULL
  `effective_from` IS the draft"* is about `tariff_versions`, a different table, and does NOT settle this — it
  was checked before the question was asked.)

**R1 is the gate in front of every other step.** With the two paths disagreeing there, the comparison refuses
at R1 and **R2–R7 cannot be compared at all**. So this single question blocked the whole measurement, which is
why it was the one thing worth the PO's time.

### WHAT THE RULING BUYS THAT THE OTHER TWO ANSWERS DO NOT

The two obvious answers each pick a winner and leave the ambiguous state in the product:

* *"an undated plan bills"* (today's live behaviour) leaves a plan published mid-setup charging customers
  immediately and forever, with nothing to notice;
* *"an undated plan does not bill"* (the ruled behaviour) halts billing for any real utility whose plan is
  missing a date.

**The ruling removes the state instead of choosing which reading of it wins.** Both engines then agree at R1
**without either changing its meaning**, and *"nobody typed a date"* stops being a silent condition — it
becomes a thing the publish step will not let you do.

### WHAT MUST BE BUILT, AND WHAT IS NOT DECIDED

Required at publish; existing published-and-undated plans given a date. **What date to give them is NOT ruled
here** and must not be guessed: a plan already billing customers has been in force since *something*, and
picking today would restate history while picking the epoch would claim it priced periods it never priced.
That is a migration question for whoever builds it, to be decided with its worked figure and recorded — or
raised if it cannot be.


## 2026-08-28 · BANK ACCOUNTS ARE CAPTURED IN SETTINGS → CONFIGURE — PO ruling, over this lane's revised advice

**PO verbatim:** *"capture bank account in configure. Keep them in section which is logical"*.

**This OVERRIDES what this lane last recommended, and the record should say so plainly.** The lane first
proposed Configure on the reasoning that *"a bank account carries a GL account, so it belongs with the GL
family"*. That reasoning was **wrong** — `bankrec_models.BankAccount`'s own docstring says *"No GL account
hangs off this row"*, because reconciliation resolves `cash` BY DESIGNATION instead (OQ-110's closure). The
lane then revised to *"put it on the statement-import screen where it is selected"*. **The PO reaffirmed
Configure.** That is the decision; the argument the lane built was wrong in both directions and the ruling
stands on its own.

### THE LOGICAL SECTION IS THE REFERENCE-DATA CARD GRID, AND IT NEEDS NO NEW LAYOUT

`CONFIGURE_SUB_TABS` holds four sections — **Reference data** (the default), Routes & Cycles, Numbering,
Templates. A bank account is a tenant-maintained named list with an active flag that is deactivated and never
deleted — the exact shape and lifecycle of every card already in that grid (BR-TEN-034's shape, which this
model's own comment cites).

`BR-SHL-035` makes this **data, not a screen**: *"new reference data = a new card + its config, never a new
layout"*, and `referenceDataConfig.ts`'s own header states the consequence — *"adding a card is data, so every
card in the grid is a row here and there is exactly one management view"*. So this is a `kind: "list"` card
with a `detailField` for the display mask, and **no new screen ID is minted**.

`BR-TEN-031` then fixes the module boundary and it is not negotiable: **tenancy RENDERS, the OWNING module
validates and writes.** `bank_accounts` is owned by payments, so payments validates and writes it.

### WHAT THE ROW ACTUALLY IS, AND WHAT IT IS FOR

Three fields: a **name** (*"Chase Operating"*), a **mask** — the last digits a human recognises, and
deliberately **not** the account number, because B2 §6's posture is that a column you do not store cannot leak
— and **active**. Unique on (tenant, name).

Exactly two consumers, both in bank reconciliation: **S38 step 1's select** (*"Chase Operating ••4021"*), and
the **tag half of the statement import's idempotency key** (file hash + bank account + period), which is what
stops one statement being imported twice. Nothing else in the product references it — not deposit batches, not
payments, not the ledger.

**So it is NOT on the path to a first bill.** A utility can sign up, configure, load, read, bill, issue,
deliver and take payment without ever creating one; it gates the bank half of reconciliation only. This lane
had ranked it 4th on the go-live path and that was too high — it belongs after the four already in flight.
Recorded so the ranking is not re-derived wrongly.

**One writer for one fact:** the card writes it, and S38 step 1 SELECTS from it. Two places that can create a
bank account is how two screens come to disagree about which accounts a utility has.


## 2026-08-28 · THE DISCOUNT RULING, BUILT — and the five judgments that were the lane's, not the PO's

The ruling below is implemented (`DEF-536` and `DEF-537` closed at `f191a8d`). **A discounted bill
can now be issued; before today none could, for any customer, on any tenant.** What follows is
every place the ruling ran out and this lane decided, each with its worked figure — because a
signature covers only what was shown, and none of these five was shown to anybody.

**What a finance person now reads on the frozen GT-1 bill with a 10.00 reduction**, straight out of
`journal_lines`:

    DR  1200 accounts receivable                 90.58
    DR  4300 customer discounts (contra-revenue)  10.00
    CR  4100 electric usage                       82.08
    CR  4105 electric base                        18.50
                                                 ------
    debits 100.58                        credits 100.58

The bill asks the customer for **90.58**; the entry is **100.58** on both sides. That difference is
what contra-revenue IS, and it is the one thing about this entry that will surprise a reader who
knows the old shape, where every entry footed exactly to `invoices.total`.

**Nothing already issued changes.** No existing bill could carry a discount line and issue, so there
is no historical entry of this shape anywhere; the tie-out on every undiscounted bill is byte-for-byte
what it was (`Σ signed_amount == invoices.total`, and `signed_amount` IS `amount` with no discount),
and golden-verify holds at 33/33.

### 0 · DRIVEN, NOT ONLY ASSERTED — a real enrolled account, end to end

The figures above are the ❄️ frozen reference bill. Here is the same thing on a **seeded Silver
Creek water account enrolled in a real SENIOR −10% programme**, gathered by the real gather, priced
by the real engine, issued into the real books, and then put through `corrections.recompute` —
printed straight out of `journal_lines`, not off a result object:

    DRAFT
      usage     water usage tier 1 (0–5 kgal)      20.00
      usage     water usage tier 2 (5–15 kgal)     65.00
      usage     water usage tier 3 (15+ kgal)     280.00
      base      water base charge                   8.00
      discount  Senior citizen discount           −37.30
      TOTAL                                       335.70

    JOURNAL ENTRY  invoice|…|issued
      CREDIT  4110 Water usage                            365.00
      CREDIT  4115 Water base                               8.00
      DEBIT   1200 Accounts receivable                    335.70
      DEBIT   4300 Customer discounts (contra-revenue)     37.30
      debits 373.00   credits 373.00   bill total 335.70

    CORRECTION (recompute)
      … the same four tariff lines, and Senior citizen discount  −37.30

**Read 4110.** It says **365.00** — what the water actually sold for. Netted, it would have said
**327.70**, and the 37.30 the utility gave away would exist nowhere. And the correction carries the
identical −37.30, which is `DEF-537` closed: before today it re-priced at full tariff and would have
handed this customer back 37.30 less than they were owed.

### 1 · THE ACCOUNT IS NUMBERED **4300** AND NAMED **"Customer discounts (contra-revenue)"**

The ruling says the code is created *as required* and the chart is the tenant's. So this is a SEED,
not a decision about anybody's books: `signed=False`, listed in `PENDING_FINANCE_RE_SIGN`, awaiting a
HUMAN-GUIDE §6 finance re-sign of the code and the name — the exact posture 4160/4170 (2026-08-11)
and 4180 (2026-08-17) were declared under. **4300 is a THIRD block on purpose**: 4100–4190 is service
revenue, 4200–4210 is fee revenue, and a reduction belongs to neither — which is this chart's own
vocabulary for the PO's *"create differnt category"*. A tenant renumbers it on **Settings → Configure**
(PO 2026-08-12, *"Confirm: under Configure"*), and code reads the DESIGNATION and never the number
(OQ-106).

### 2 · IT IS SEEDED RATHER THAN LEFT TO REFUSE — the opposite of `budget_variance`

`budget_variance` was ruled into existence in 2026-08-15 with NO account, and
`posting_seam.budget_variance_account_id` refused by name until the account arrived. **The same choice
here would have reproduced DEF-536 for every fresh tenant** — a discounted bill still would not issue,
which is the defect this ruling exists to close. The difference that justifies the divergence: OQ-142
had DECLINED both candidate accounts, so there was nothing lawful to land on; here the ruling itself
says to create the code. The seeded chart is **34 accounts** (was 33).

### 3 · `type` IS **revenue**, NOT A NEW SIXTH ACCOUNT TYPE

`LEDGER_ACCOUNT_TYPES` is `asset · liability · equity · revenue · expense`, and the type drives the
S56 trial-balance grouping and its sign convention. Adding `contra_revenue` would change how EVERY
account in the product is grouped and signed on that screen — far more than the ruling asks — and
every mainstream chart files sales discounts under revenue as a contra account. So the account sits in
the revenue category and carries a DEBIT balance. **Reported for the reviewer**, because "category" in
the PO's sentence could reasonably have meant this field.

### 4 · THE SIGN TRAVELS AS A **SIDE**, AND THE BILL'S TIE-OUT READS THE SIGNED SUM

`PostingBucket` gains `side`; a debit bucket carries the ABSOLUTE value, because B2 §2 is
`CHECK (amount >= 0)` and the ledger takes no negative figure at all. `_refuse_unless_balanced` reads
`signed_amount`, so 82.08 + 18.50 − 10.00 = **90.58** = `invoices.total`, unchanged arithmetic on every
bill without a discount. **`OQ-152`'s refusal is NOT weakened**: a negative bucket on any account that
is not the tenant's discount account still refuses by name, and
`tests/test_def_536_discount_gl.py::tc4` is the case that holds it there — it was GREEN before this
lane and is GREEN after, deliberately, and must never be softened to make a discount pass.

### 5 · TWO HALVES OF DEF-536 ARE NOT BUILT, AND THE REASON IS A MISSING FIELD

No `discount_grants` row is written at issue (`DEF-2430`) and nothing flips a programme to
`suspended_funding_exhausted` (`DEF-2431`). **Both are blocked on the same fact: the discount LINE
names no programme.** `apply_discounts` stamps the customer-facing NAME as the description (DIS-02
step 1) and no code, and `gather` carries no enrolment id, so an issued bill cannot say which enrolment
to deplete. Matching back by DESCRIPTION was option D of OQ-116 and the PO declined it; resolving it by
*"the account has exactly one enrolment"* would deplete budgets for single-discount accounts and not
for others, which is worse books than not depleting at all. The fix is to carry `discount_code` onto
the priced line and onto `invoice_lines` the way `service`, `tax_id`, `charge_id` and
`tariff_version_id` already are — a rating-pricing change (🔒) outside this lane's ground — and then
call one published rating write from inside the issue transaction. Filed, with that fix written out,
rather than approximated.

### AND `DEF-537`, WHICH COULD NOT BE VERIFIED UNTIL THE ABOVE EXISTED

`corrections.recompute` and `backbill._priced_pass` both called `price_bill` with **no `discounts=` at
all**, so a corrected or back-billed period for an enrolled account re-priced at FULL TARIFF while the
original bill carried the reduction. Both ends built since DEF-502, the CALL missing — hard-won law 2,
one door over from DEF-502 itself. **One extra rule the back-bill needed:** `price_day_weighted` makes
one `price_bill` call per proration FACTOR (OQ-155) and R6 is bill-level (BR-RAT-071), so the discount
rides the FINAL pass only, exactly as the taxes and fees do. Passed on every pass, a six-month catch-up
spanning a tariff change would reduce the customer two or three times.

**Rules written:** BR-BIL-790 (the designation), BR-BIL-791 (the side), BR-BIL-792 (the two callers),
BR-LED-790 (the thirteenth designation and its seed).


## 2026-08-28 · A DISCOUNT POSTS TO ITS OWN GL CODE, IN ITS OWN CATEGORY — PO ruling, and it dissolves DEF-536

**PO verbatim:** *"you will need differnt GL code for these - dont keep them in same, create differnt category
as required and keep them in it"*, answering the designation question `DEF-536` was blocked on.

**What it settles.** A discount line does NOT reduce the service's own revenue account. It posts to a
**separate GL code**, in a **separate category created for it**. That is standard contra-revenue, and it is
option **(a)** as `OQ-152` itself enumerated it on 2026-08-11: *"post it as DR 10.00 to the discount GL
(standard contra-revenue; the entry still balances against DR AR)"*.

**⚠ AND IT REMOVES THE FAILURE MODE RATHER THAN ONLY NAMING AN ACCOUNT.** `OQ-152` closed on 2026-08-12 with
*"a bill whose GL bucket sums below zero REFUSES to issue"*, and `posting_seam.posting_buckets` refuses by name
(`posting_bucket_is_negative_oq_152`). A discount netted against the service's own account is what can drive
that bucket below zero. Posted as a DEBIT to its own account, **no bucket ever goes negative**, so the refusal
cannot fire on a discount at all. The two rulings compose; neither is superseded.

**Worked, on the frozen GT-1 bill** — the same figures `OQ-152` used, so the two can be compared line for line:

| | old (netted against the service) | ruled (its own GL) |
|---|---|---|
| electric usage `4100` | CR **72.08** | CR **82.08** |
| base charge | CR **18.50** | CR **18.50** |
| discount account (new) | — | **DR 10.00** |
| accounts receivable | DR **90.58** | DR **90.58** |

Both balance at **100.58**. The difference is that the ruled form states the discount as its own figure a
finance person can read, instead of hiding **10.00** inside a revenue account that then reports **72.08** of
electric revenue the utility never earned at that price.

**What was NOT ruled and stays open:** which category the new code sits in and what it is numbered are the
tenant's chart of accounts, not ours — the code is created *as required*, per the ruling's own words, and the
GL mapping surface is already ruled to live under **Settings → Configure** (PO 2026-08-12, *"Confirm: under
Configure"*).

**On the asking.** The PO's reply opened *"I already answer this question before"*. `OQ-152`'s closure of
2026-08-12 settles the NEGATIVE-BUCKET half and names this option; a separate ruling on the designation itself
is not in the log. Recorded either way, verbatim and dated, so it is not asked a third time — CLAUDE.md law 13:
a re-ask manufactures inconsistency and then blames the human for it.


## 2026-08-27 · OQ-741 CLOSED — AI TRANSLATES, ONE LANGUAGE AT A TIME, AND THE FIRST CUSTOMER IS THE REVIEWER

## 2026-08-27 · FOUR MORE RULINGS — tax scopes · a close-out act · the reconnection fee as a real charge · branding everywhere

Four replies, taken in the order they arrived. All four match the recommendation, and
**one of them ratifies something that already shipped** — recorded as a ratification
rather than as new work, because the difference decides whether a lane builds it twice.

### 1 · DEF-273 — tax scopes: BUILD BOTH ✅ **and both are ALREADY BUILT**

**PO verbatim:** *"Tax cannot be limited to a customer type or an area - Build both."*

⚠ **THIS RATIFIES SHIPPED CODE, IT DOES NOT COMMISSION WORK.** The stale-defect audit of
the same day closed DEF-273 with evidence: `apps/rating/models.py:820,845-846` carries
both scopes and `ck_taxes_premises_scope_kind` constrains the geography one; the
conditional Texas rows seed with their condition; `TaxWizard.tsx:965-975` and `:431`
write them and `TaxesFeesTab.tsx:124-135` renders them.

So the answer and the code agree, and **the value of the ruling is that it CONFIRMS the
built behaviour is what the PO wanted** — the row was closed on evidence that the feature
exists, not on evidence that anyone had asked for it. A lane picking this up must build
NOTHING. What remains is to satisfy the reason the defect was filed: that three of the
five ruled Texas rates **would overcharge exempt customers if seeded as written** — so
the check is that the seeded rows now carry their scopes, not that the columns exist.

### 2 · DEF-724 — a cut customer gets a SEPARATE CLOSE-OUT ACT ✅ as recommended

**PO verbatim:** *"A disconnected customer can never be closed - Add a separate close-out
act — Cleaner in the record"*.

Today the only terminal path is a **move-out**, and a move-out refuses anyone who is not
currently occupying — so an account cut for non-payment stays open forever and nobody can
finish it.

**The reasoning the PO endorsed, restated so the implementation keeps it:** a close-out
writes a date **nobody can un-write**. Once an account is closed, correcting it means new
rows, never an edit (hard rule 4). Relaxing move-out to accept a cut customer would file
a **disconnection as a move-out** in the permanent record, and to a regulator those are
not the same event. The extra act is the cheaper mistake.

**DEF-701 is unblocked by this** — *"a cut account still reads 'marked disconnect /
billable'"* was blocked on DEF-724 plus billing's `CLASSES_THAT_BILL`. The close-out is
the terminal state that row needed.

### 3 · DEF-708 — the reconnection fee becomes a REAL CHARGE ✅ as recommended

**PO verbatim:** *"A customer can be reconnected $75 short - Make the fee a real charge —
It becomes a line that can be billed and paid, so the gate has something to check."*

**The measured defect:** a reconnection requires the fee to be paid; the **`$75.00`** is
recorded on the case and **posts nowhere**, so the gate has nothing to test and lets the
customer through. The utility does the work and never collects.

⚠ **THE HALF THAT MUST NOT BE SKIPPED, and it is why the other option was rejected:**
checking the case record would make the gate *work* and leave the money *uncollected* —
the wrong half of the problem. The fee must reach the customer's balance.

**This is a BILLING change, not a customers one.** The audit records the blocker in those
terms: `BILL_TYPES` has no fee type and `issue._gl_account_for` **refuses every `fee`
line**. So the work is a billing lane's, and a one-line change in customers would
deadlock every reconnection instead.

### 4 · DEF-195 — the utility's logo and colours are used EVERYWHERE ⚠ OVERRULE

**PO verbatim:** *"A utility's logo and colours are never used anywhere - Use them
everywhere — Bills, notices, the app header, the customer portal."*

**Ruled: everywhere.** The recommendation was the narrower *"customer documents first"* —
bills and notices only, on the reasoning that it is where branding earns its keep and is
a smaller change than theming the whole app. **The PO took the wider option**, naming all
four surfaces explicitly: bills · notices · the app header · the customer portal.

**Today a utility uploads a logo and picks two brand colours and nothing in the product
ever draws any of it** — not the settings preview, not a bill, not a notice.

⚠ **THE COLOURS ARE THE HARD HALF AND THE RULING DOES NOT MAKE THEM EASY.** A logo is an
image dropped into four templates. **Two tenant brand colours applied to the app header
collide with `tokens.css` and B8's no-hex-literals rule** — every colour in this product
is a token, and a tenant-supplied colour is data, not a token. There is also a contrast
obligation nobody has ruled: a tenant may pick two colours that make their own text
unreadable. **That is a real question and it is minted rather than guessed** — see
`OQ-800`. The logo half and the document half proceed regardless; nothing waits on it.
