**PO verbatim:** *"Can you do 1 langauge at a time and push the changes - About 1,200
sentences per language, ten languages. German alone has 564 full sentences plus shorter
labels. Around 12,000 pieces of text in total. Ai will write it - when AI write it
consider practical language - how local will speak it, the choice of words should be in
like with local , country specific - human cannot review it right now; when customer
will come for that language they will ask the changes we will do it that time until
then it is AI translated; you can write rule how to do a transation in lnaguages"*

### ⚠ THE PO HAD ALREADY RULED THIS ONCE, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT

`BR-SHL-043` has been **CONFIRMED since 2026-08-10** — *"machine for time being; later I
will get it edited by human"*, ratified the same day. **Machine translation of the
staff-UI catalogues was never actually open.** OQ-741 was raised because the option
table put to the PO on 2026-08-27 offered machine translation as option (b) and the PO
chose (a) over it, which read as a refusal — and a lane may not translate 12,000 values
on an inference either way. The right move was to ask; the answer shows the earlier rule
still holds. **Recorded so the next agent does not re-open a question that was signed
seventeen days ago.**

### WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW, AND IT IS THE REVIEW POSTURE

BR-SHL-043 promised *"later I will get it edited by human"*. **That is SUPERSEDED.** The
PO's words today: *"human cannot review it right now; when customer will come for that
language they will ask the changes we will do it that time until then it is AI
translated"*. Review is now **demand-driven** — the first customer in a language is the
reviewer, and their requested changes are made then.

**THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: the product will ship text no native
speaker has read**, in ten languages, indefinitely. That is the PO's decision taken with
the figure in front of them, and it is written into `BR-SHL-251` clause 8 in those words
so that nobody later reads the absence of review as an oversight.

### THE QUALITY BAR THE PO ADDED — the reason this needed a rule and not just a yes

*"consider practical language - how local will speak it, the choice of words should be
in like with local, country specific"*. That is not a restatement of "translate it": it
rules out the literal rendering a machine produces by default. **A literal translation
that a native would not say is a FAILURE of this rule even though every word is
correct.** Worked: a German meter reading is `Zählerstand`, never a literal rendering of
the English; `es-ES` and `es-419` are different catalogues and must not be copies.

### THE CARVE-OUT WAS VERIFIED BEFORE ANY TRANSLATION BEGAN, NOT ASSUMED

`BR-SHL-043` forbids machine-translating **customer-facing documents** — TD-16(5), and a
machine-translated disconnection notice carries statutory exposure in several US states.
**Measured on the tree before the first language was dispatched:** the customer's bill
wording is composed in `apps/billing/documents.py` and notice bodies in
`apps/notifications/template_service.py`; the catalogues' **101 `templates.*` keys are
the template MANAGEMENT SCREEN, not the sent text**. Five keys whose NAMES suggested
legal text (`settings.numbering.series.collections_notice`,
`dashboard.todo.item.disconnect_eligible`, `rating.taxWiz.statutory.title`,
`rating.discountWizard.recertNoticeLabel`, `settings.numbering.series.disconnect_case`)
were each read and are **all staff form labels**. So the ten catalogues are staff UI and
lawful to machine-translate; nothing a customer receives is touched.

### THE WORKFLOW, AND WHY IT IS NOT CEREMONY

*"do 1 langauge at a time and push the changes"*. **One catalogue, one commit, one
push.** Ten lanes editing ten shared JSON files is the exact shape of `DEF-165` and
`DEF-1280` — both of which happened on this branch today — and one-file-per-commit makes
that collision impossible rather than unlikely.

**German is dispatched first** (1,226 untranslated values, the largest). Its output is
put to the PO as before/after pairs **before the other nine are commissioned**, so the
bar in `BR-SHL-251` clause 2 is judged on real output rather than on a promise.

### The rule itself

`BR-SHL-251`, in `04-docs/05-modules/00-platform-shell/02-business-rules.md`, written
**before the first language was dispatched** — eight clauses covering scope, the
local-voice bar, what is never translated, length constraints, plurals, formatting,
the one-language-per-commit workflow, and the review posture.

## 2026-08-16 — DEF-153: the sample data loads, and four judgments were made where the rules ran out

**Lane:** DEF-153 sample-data lane. **Where the code is:** `core/sample_fixture.py`
plus a `sample_data.py` in rating, metering, assets, customers, billing and
payments, the four `is_sample` migrations, and
`manage.py load_sample_data --tenant <subdomain>`.

**Measured, brand-new tenant through provisioning, one pass:** 8 plans-and-rates
rows · 92 premises/units/service points (44 premises, 48 units, 5 named streets)
· 49 meters · 48 ACTIVE accounts · 189 meter reads · **95 issued bills** · 81
payments = **562 rows, every block loaded**. Repair path measured separately on
a tenant created before any of this existed: **554 rows; a second run writes 0**.

### The four judgments, each with the figure that decided it

1. **Sewer is seeded as a true percentage of water, and the spec sentence is
   amended.** The spec said *"until it lands, seed sewer FLAT"*; it landed the
   same day and the PO ratified the figure — **40% of the water USAGE charge,
   $15.80 on $39.50, deliberately NOT counting the $8.00 base, which would give
   $19.00**. A test asserts both numbers, so drift goes RED.
2. **48 water meters, not the spec's 96.** 96 was *"water + sewer per unit"*,
   written while sewer was still going to be metered. A percentage of another
   service's money reads no register. 48 unread sewer meters would put 48
   phantom missing-reads into every bill run and bury the THREE deliberately
   unreadable ones the spec asks for, which is acceptance item 8.
3. **Three premises are seeded with no unit yet.** 44 premises AND 48 units means
   units exceed premises by 4; one 6-unit block contributes +5 alone and two
   duplexes +1 each, which is +7. With the stated mix the two headline counts
   cannot both hold, so three premises are newly platted with no service — a real
   state of a growing utility, and both numbers become true.
4. **The Senior plan is NOT seeded — OQ-240.** No signed figure states its
   discount anywhere. On the reference bill a 10% senior discount would make the
   water lines $35.55 + $7.20 and a 20% one $31.60 + $6.40 — a **$9/month**
   spread on one ordinary bill, and spec rule 7 forbids choosing between them.

### Two signed rules amended, both by a later PO ruling and not by this lane

* **BR-TEN-056 clause 1** — the sample set no longer stops at reads. PO verbatim:
  *"if we are able to seed the data refernece as well as transaction data, then we
  can test the application end to end and see what are the issues; thiswill be
  human checking"*. **The price, stated rather than discovered:** removal becomes
  PARTIAL — issued bills and payments can never be deleted (hard rule 4) and are
  reported BY NAME (BR-TEN-066).
* **BR-TEN-065** — sample accounts are seeded **Active**, not `Pending
  activation`. The 2026-08-10 rule stated its own consequence: *"the sample set
  therefore cannot demonstrate a bill run"*. That consequence is exactly what the
  2026-08-16 ruling removes.

### What the fixture makes VISIBLE rather than hides

**DEF-161 (critical, filed here):** a plan carrying any non-metered service
cannot be billed at all — 48 of 48 accounts broke at measure-consumption, and the
only decision that unblocks one *deletes the service from the bill*. So the
seeded bills carry their water lines and **no sewer or trash line**, and the
decision that made that true is recorded in the audit trail with its reason. The
alternative — recording an *estimate* of zero — would fabricate a meter reading
for a meter that does not exist.

## 2026-08-16 — DEF-166 / DEF-167: the demo tenant's bills ISSUE, and three judgments made where the rules ran out

The sample data reported *"OK — Bills (June and July) — 95 row(s)"* and every one
of the 95 was a **draft**. Payments then reported *"OK … 0 row(s)"* over that.
Measured on a live Postgres, clean database, before and after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `invoices` | `draft \| 95` | **`issued \| 93`**, zero drafts |
| `payments` | 0 | **80** |
| `journal_entries` | 0 | **173** (626 lines) |
| August reads | present | **present and still unbilled** — 96 committed, 93 billed |

**The cause was never in billing.** Two tax authorities had no 2200-series
liability account, so BR-BIL-010/BR-BIL-069 refused to stamp their tax line and
*every* bill broke at issue. `seed_demo` provisions `Texas State` and `Local`;
rating's `_map_liability_account` ran only inside its own create loop, so an
authority the fixture did not create never got one.

### Judgment 1 · a liability account is minted for EVERY unmapped authority, not only for the ones the fixture creates

The PO's ruling (2026-08-12, OQ-145/147) is *"make them choose"* — the tenant
chooses the authority's account and the product **generates its code**. That
ruling is about an authority that NEEDS an account; it says nothing about who
created the authority. So the sample load now mints one for any authority whose
`liability_gl_account_id` is NULL, the tenant's own included.

**Why this is not a rule change:** it fills a NULL and changes no rate, so
BR-TEN-012 (*a tenant that already priced its taxes is not overwritten by a
fixture*) is untouched. **The alternative was to leave them and report the
refusal by name** — which is what the product already did, and is precisely the
state that made the demo undrivable.

### Judgment 2 · the fixture adds NO tax authority to a tenant that already has one — and this one was costing money

`seed_sample_taxes`'s own docstring said it creates its pair *"only when the
tenant has NO tax rules of its own"*. The code checked **per name**, so the
fixture's `State water tax` 6.25% and `City utility tax` 2% landed **beside**
the tenant's identical pair. **Worked, on the seeded reference bill:** water
base 8.00 + tier 1 20.00 + tier 2 19.50 = 39.50 taxable, and the bill carried
**four** tax lines — 2.97 + 2.97 + 0.95 + 0.95 = **7.84**, i.e. **16.5%** where
the tenant's own rates say **8.25%** and the correct tax is **3.92**. The check
is now on the SET. Hard-won law 1 in its plainest form: the comment claimed the
guarantee and nothing implemented it.

### Judgment 3 · a seeder block that cannot do its job RAISES, and a period that did not bill fails the whole block

`core.sample_fixture.BlockCannotRun` carries the sentence a human reads. This is
the repo's own seam rule — *an unanswerable read reports that it cannot answer
and never answers 0* — applied to seeders rather than selectors, which is why
nobody had written it down for this path. Three states, rendered differently:
**wrote N** · **nothing to do** · **COULD NOT RUN**, the last naming the upstream
block.

**The judgment inside the judgment:** a period that issues nothing fails the
block *even when the other period issued*. BR-BIL-055 lets a real run issue the
clean bills and hold the rest — but a FIXTURE that cannot produce the bills it
specifies is a broken fixture, and reporting a short count as success is exactly
what DEF-166 was. Each block is its own transaction, so the failure rolls back
and the tenant is never left half-billed.

### Found while proving it, and NOT fixed here — DEF-171

**`bill_runs.status` never leaves `draft`.** The tuple has five values past it
and a repo-wide grep finds one assignment of any of them, on a *correction* run.
So a run that authorised, released and issued all 48 of its bills is
indistinguishable from one nobody touched. The product behaves correctly; only
its reported state is wrong. Filed rather than fixed: it belongs in
`runs.py`/`release.py`, both being edited by other lanes at the time.

## 2026-08-16 — DEF-161: sewer bills at last ($15.80 on $39.50), and trash is OQ-246

A plan carrying a non-metered service could not be billed. The run asked for a
meter read for every service on the plan, and a service that is **not measured
by design** was indistinguishable from a meter nobody could reach.

### What was decided, and what was deliberately NOT

**DECIDED — because signed law already said it.** A `percent_of_service` tariff
prices no consumption of its own. BR-RAT-015 is **CONFIRMED**: sewer is a *"% of
water usage-charge dollars (excl. base, excl. tax)"*. Its plugin says the same
in its own words — *"`usage` is ignored ON PURPOSE … a sewer service point often
has no meter at all"* — and BR-RAT-066 enumerates the one case where such a
tariff refuses: when its **basis service** is not on the bill. Never for want of
a reading of its own. **So this was not a judgment about what the rule should
be; it was a correction of code that contradicted the rule.**

**Measured, on a booted three-service tenant, both ways:**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| sewer usage lines | **0** | **93** |
| sewer billed | **$0.00** | **$2,979.68** |
| the reference bill | 8.00 base + 39.50 water | + **sewer 15.80** = 40% × 39.50 |

**$15.80 on $39.50 is B5 GT-17 ❄️** — the frozen figure — produced by the
product's own five-phase bill run for the first time. The golden harness is
**33 PASS / 0 FAIL**, unchanged: GT-17/20/25/26 all price sewer from a MEASURED
water service and never reach the branch that changed.

**NOT DECIDED — OQ-246, minted rather than chosen.** Trash is a flat monthly
charge on a service point with no meter, and **its tariff DOES price
consumption** (`flat`, seeded at $0.00/unit, with the $18 as a plan base charge).
No signed rule anywhere says what an absent meter means for such a tariff, and
guessing has a specific cost in the other direction: a WATER meter nobody ever
installed would silently bill base-only. So `PRICES_NO_CONSUMPTION` carries
**exactly one model**, its comment names the OQ as the reason a flat tariff is
not on it, and the fixture keeps recording the real `bill_without_service`
decision a clerk can take. **The figure the OQ puts to the PO:** $18.00 per
account per month — **$1,728.00** across the demo tenant's 48 accounts and two
billed periods, reaching no customer today.

### The one line in the 🔒 money path, and why it is safe

`if base_only:` became `if base_only and not _is_percent_of_service(tariff):` in
`engine.price_bill`'s usage-line drop. BR-BIL-028's clause is about a **meter**
— *"usage lines bill through the day before the hold"*, i.e. a register stopped
being read. A percent-of-service line is not read off a meter at all.

**The vacation hold BR-BIL-028 governs is protected by the engine's own
construction, not by this line:** a base-only WATER service records no
`usage_dollars`, so the sewer tariff still reaches pass B with no basis and
REFUSES BY NAME (BR-RAT-066) rather than pricing 40% of nothing as $0.00. The
amendment is written into the `apps/rating/engine.py` review-ledger row, stating
plainly that the 2026-08-11 blanket signature does **not** cover it.

### Still open on DEF-161, and named rather than left to be noticed

`decisions.record_bulk` takes no `service_id`, so two per-service decisions for
one account collapse into one row and the second supersedes the first. The
fixture works around it with per-service `record_decision`; the **S31 bulk
action still cannot resolve per-service missing reads.** Untouched by this lane.

## 2026-08-17 · CR-006 SET-05/06/07 Routes & Cycles — BUILT at 2.6.0

**The five PO rulings of 2026-08-16 are implemented, and four of them reverse
the reading a lane would otherwise have taken.** Each is written into the
metering rule register (BR-MET-066b, 071–081, 035b) with its verbatim quote
before any code was written; this row records the judgments the rules did not
settle and the worked figures shown.

### What was measured first — the gap list overstated again, and understated once

Three CRs running have proved that a gap list built from the design overstates.
**CR-006 is the first where it also UNDERSTATED**, and both halves are worth the
record:

* **Already built, needing no work:** `Cycle`, `Route` and `RouteMembership`
  tables, their full CRUD service layer, `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)` on every
  write, five mounted endpoints, the audit rows, the delete guard on membership,
  BR-MET-010's cycle move, and `ROUTE`/`CYCLE` rows already sitting in CR-005's
  `SERIES_CATALOG` (`RT-{000}`, `CY-{000}`).
* **Understated:** the CR reads as "add two wizards to a shipped screen". The
  shipped screen could not put a single premises on a route. Its own header
  comment said so — *"the picker for it needs the Premises & Units screens
  (US-MET-001) that do not exist in this app yet"* — so a route could be
  created and never populated, from this screen or any other. That is not a
  wizard, it is the feature.

### The judgments this lane made, each with the number that decided it

**1 · Membership uniqueness moved to PER SERVICE and needs TWO constraints.**
A route now carries a service, so a house on water and electric is read by two
crews on two routes. The obvious single `unique(tenant, unit, service)` is
WRONG: SQL treats NULLs as distinct, so two legacy all-service routes could both
hold the same unit — the exact thing the original `unique(tenant, unit)`
existed to stop. Shipped as two partial uniques, one per branch. **The
migration cannot lose a row:** every membership in every tenant today has
`service_id = NULL`, so all of them fall under the NULL-branch constraint,
which IS the old one.

**2 · A conflict MOVES rather than refusing — and the old refusal made the
requirement unbuildable.** `_set_route_membership` raised
`metering.route.unit_on_another_route`. The CR asks for *"selecting moves them,
with confirm"*, and the server refused before any confirm could be reached, so
the badge could only ever be followed by an error. The move is the server's and
the confirm is the UI's, exactly as BR-MET-010 already splits them for cycles.
**Two existing tests asserted the old behaviour and were AMENDED, not deleted**
— the invariant survives, only its mechanism changed.

**3 · Reads history is hunted through `read_import_batches.route_id`, not
through service points.** The obvious source is wrong on the exact case
BR-MET-079 exists for: removing a route's members UNSTAMPS its service points,
so an emptied route would report ZERO read history and become deletable. The
batch link is never cleared by a membership edit.

**4 · A due day on or before the bill day is ACCEPTED, and this is a deliberate
divergence from r10's own hint.** SET-07.3 reads *"Dates must land in order:
read → bill → due → late"*. A cycle that bills on the **26th** and is due on
the **5th** is a normal Net-10 arrangement wrapping into the following month;
enforcing the hint would refuse a real cycle to satisfy a sentence written
about one example. Order IS enforced for read-from ≤ read-to ≤ bill day. The
wrap is shown in the preview instead.

**5 · `cycles.status` could not be overloaded.** `cycle_dict.status` has always
been the OPERATIONAL progress of the current period — scheduled / in progress /
billed — and S27 draws it. BR-MET-076's DRAFT is a different fact about a
different thing, so it is served as `lifecycle_status`. Overloading one key
would have silently changed S27 the day this shipped.

**6 · The legacy DATE columns stay.** `window_start`, `window_end` and
`bill_date` are no longer written by this screen (BR-MET-077 makes the stored
shape day-of-month DEFAULTS), but `read_schedules` and the shipped billing
seams read them. Dropping a column billing reads is a change with its own
blast radius, not a tidy-up riding a settings CR.

### The money boundary, and why this CR needed no finance re-sign

Ruling 1 removed the `Late / penalty date` control. Nothing on either screen
names a fee, a rate, an amount or a currency — asserted structurally, so adding
one goes RED. **The preview strip keeps every clause except the last**, and the
last is not computed here, not derived from Billing defaults and not displayed
here from elsewhere: a fee date rendered on this screen reads as this screen's
field however it was sourced. Grace keeps its single home on Billing defaults
(BR-BIL-002/008). **No ❄️ B4/B5 figure is touched at any point.**

### Twelve guards broken FIRST and quoted (hard-won law 7)

Money-field refusal · draft-stamps-nothing · reads-history delete guard ·
parent-matches-sub-areas · the two-level depth cap · the endpoint permission
class · per-service membership scoping · the schema's new columns · the icon's
accessible name · the pagination footer · the late-fee clause in the preview ·
the empty-state action.

**Two are worth reading rather than counting.** The reads-history guard, when
removed, does not silently allow the delete — it produces a raw
`ProtectedError`, i.e. an HTTP 500 where the rule wanted a sentence. And the
**empty-state check STAYED GREEN** when its button was deleted, because the
page header carries the same `+ Add route` label: DEF-182's shape a sixth time,
found only by breaking the guard. The assertion is now scoped inside the
`settings-empty` cell and fails on the same deletion.

### B14 applied, including three rules this surface was breaking

Row actions were TEXT LINKS (rule 15), neither table had a pagination footer
(rule 16), and the empty states were a bare sentence with nothing to click
(rule 17) — all three are on B14's own highest-yield audit list, and this
surface was among the *"every other list table in the product is unaudited"*
set. Also applied: 3 (the shared WizardFrame, not a twelfth stepper), 4, 5, 6,
9 (the area filter is removable chips, which is what *"1 to many"* forces),
10, 11 (the move and coverage consequence boxes), 12, 18, 20.

### What is NOT claimed

**NO BROWSER WALKTHROUGH HAPPENED.** CR-005 is BUILT-NOT-CLOSED for exactly
this reason and CR-004 met the bar only after a walkthrough found five screens
answering HTTP 500 with every test green. Recorded as an `it.todo` in the suite
rather than implied by a green run. Also not claimed: the reader/tech assignee
on SET-06 step 1 is not wired (`routes.assigned_to` exists and the wizard does
not offer it — no user picker exists on this surface); walk order is stored and
is not editable here; and *"Dispatch can filter work orders by route/area"* is
a downstream link, not a deliverable — Work is R5.

### Version

**Change 6, shipped in build `2.7.1`** — and the two are not the same number
on purpose. CR-007 landed first at `2.7.0`, so `2.6.0` would move the on-screen
version BACKWARDS and let two builds share one number, defeating exactly what
step 7 exists for. The merge kept it monotonic (`2.7.0` + four defect fixes:
DEF-197, DEF-199, DEF-207, DEF-208). Bumped in `06-backend/pyproject.toml` and
`07-frontend/package.json`, the two sources. **The scheme cannot be both "the
middle number IS the CR" and monotonic — raised as OQ-258, not settled here.**

## 2026-08-17 — CR-007 / DEF-210: *"please define it for this product"*, read narrowly on purpose

**PO ruling, verbatim.** Shown the walkthrough finding — *"34 of 36 template
types have no content, so the email subject line and SMS counter you asked for
have never rendered for anyone"* — the PO replied: **"please define it for this
product"**.

**What was built.** Twenty-six bodies and twenty subject lines, authored, plus
merge-variable palettes for the twenty-six classes that had none. A new tenant
goes from **2 usable letters to 28**. Version `2.7.2`, commit `eb2e8c3`.

### The judgment, because this is where the rules ran out

**A PRODUCT RULING WAS TREATED AS DELEGATING PRODUCT WORDING AND NOTHING MORE.**
Eight of the thirty-six were left unauthored, and the reasoning is the decision
worth recording:

* **The three disconnect tiers.** BR-NOT-015 is CONFIRMED and says, in as many
  words, that the rights footer's *"SENTENCES are NOT settled by this rule and
  must not be invented"*. A19 §2's tier sentences are signed; the five clauses
  around them — dispute rights, medical hold, weather suppression, weekend and
  holiday suppression, the commission complaint line — are the paragraph that
  tells a customer their legal rights before their service is cut off. **A
  ruling that says "define it for this product" is a product instruction, not a
  legal sign-off**, and reading it as one would have converted the PO's sentence
  into approval of text they never saw. OQ-253 stays open and BLOCKING.
  **Concrete consequence, stated so nobody has to infer it: no disconnection
  notice can be produced on any tenant today.**
* **The four contracts.** Documents somebody signs, and one of them
  (NACHA autopay authorization) is prescribed by a payment scheme this repo does
  not hold.
* **`plan_notice_void`.** Not an authoring gap — **the event was abolished**.
  BR-PAY-016 already records it: *"the third variant (the plan-void notice) has
  nothing left to announce."* OQ-260 (a) asks whether to withdraw the class.

### The palettes are OQ-206's own option (b), not a new invention

OQ-206 offered *"(b) a smaller v1 palette is ruled — every email/SMS class gets
the shared account/customer/money set and nothing class-specific, and the
distinct content lands as fixed copy rather than variables."* That is exactly
what shipped, and **every token is marked `derived_spelling`** because no signed
document writes any of these names in braces. OQ-254 CLOSED; OQ-206 narrowed to
three contracts; OQ-207 narrowed to one class.

### Three figures the letters deliberately do NOT state

Prototype r10 is the design handover and its STRUCTURE and TONE were followed;
its DATA never was. **No authored body states an NSF fee (r10 draws `$25`), a
deposit-refund period (`12 months`), a refund settlement time (`3–5 business
days`), a reconnect fee (`$60`), a rate-change notice period (`60 days`) or a
regulator rule (`PUC rule 25.29`, `TCEQ`).** None of the six is ruled anywhere
in this repo. A test asserts sixteen such phrases absent from every body, so
closing OQ-260 means adding a merge token — not editing prose past a guard.

### Two things found while doing it

* **Six citations of `OQ-250` in the notifications code pointed at the wrong
  question** — OQ-250 is CR-005's counter-pad length; the rights footer is
  OQ-253. Corrected. A refusal that cites the wrong open question sends its
  reader to the wrong page, which is the whole value of citing one.
* ⚠ **`OQ-253`, `OQ-254` and `OQ-255` EACH MEAN TWO DIFFERENT THINGS** — minted
  twice by two CR-007 lanes on one day, with shipped code citing both meanings
  (one of them inside an API response string). **DEF-226**, filed and
  deliberately not fixed here, because the prescribed remedy edits another lane's
  API strings and e2e spec. **The instructive part is that G17 already catches
  it and was already RED**: `run_gates` ends *"19 PASS, 8 FAIL — MERGE BLOCKED"*
  with six long-standing failures, so a genuinely new one is indistinguishable
  from the wall. **Print each FAIL's age, or split the summary into "new since
  `HEAD~`" and "known"** — that, not another gate, is what would have caught it.

### What is proved and what is owed

A real provisioned tenant now holds **19 published email variants with non-null
subjects** and **4 published SMS variants** (measured at 101 · 129 · 105 · 128
characters), where before it held two print classes. Both CR-007 acceptance
items are gated on `channel`, which stays null until a variant is published — so
the reason neither had ever rendered is gone. ⚠ **That the subject FIELD and the
character COUNTER appear on SET-10 is NOT proved**: no gate in this repo reads
rendered output. DEF-210 is `fixed-in-part` and the browser check is owed.

## 2026-08-17 · CR-008 SET-11 Settings → Accounting — five judgments made where the rulings stopped

The PO answered all nine CR-008 questions on 2026-08-17 (recorded verbatim in
`12-governance/11-change-requests.md`). Building against those answers still
needed five calls the rulings do not make. Each is written here with its worked
figure, before the work that depends on it, so the next agent can disagree with
a decision rather than reverse-engineer one.

**1 · The bank-match amount tolerance is seeded `0`, and `0` is not "unset".**
The PO ruled *"Okay. We can take it as threshold from user"*. Today
`apps/payments/reconciliation.auto_match` compares `batch.recorded_total ==
line.amount` — penny-exact, three times over. The new parameter's comparison is
`abs(recorded_total − amount) ≤ tolerance`, and **at 0 that is character-for-
character the same test**, so a tenant who never opens the screen sees no change
at all. r10 draws `$0.05`; seeding 0.05 would mean a **$412.30** deposit batch
auto-matching a **$412.27** bank line — and RECONCILING and LOCKING it
(BR-PAY-004) — for every utility in the product on the day this shipped. The
cap is **$5.00**: a tolerance is for a rounding or a bank's cent, and one wide
enough to swallow a small payment is a fee derivation, which OQ-160 forbids.

**2 · The manual write-off approval threshold posts money, behind three locks.**
Ruling 2 was delegated (*"decide for me"*) and the previous lane fixed the
default at **$0.00**. Shipping the number without wiring it would be a control
that does nothing — the exact fault ruling 1 removed the accrual/cash switch
for. So `request_write_off` now posts immediately when **all three** hold:
(a) `amount ≤ threshold`; (b) the actor holds System Admin, the same role
`approve_write_off` requires; (c) the caller supplied a posting instant, because
there is no clock in that module (BR-TEN-043). **At the seeded $0.00 lock (a)
can never open** — the service refuses an amount that is not > 0 — so every
write-off of every size still needs its separate approval, exactly as before.
A tenant typing **$50.00** has decided that a $12.40 residue is a clerk's
decision, and both acts land in the audit log under their own name.

**3 · A chart import SKIPS a code the tenant already has; it never updates it.**
The CR asks for *"dedupe on code"* and does not say which way. Skipping is the
safe direction: an existing account carries a DESIGNATION the posting service
resolves every journal entry through, so letting column B of a spreadsheet
rename `1200 Accounts receivable` would move money by side effect. Renaming
stays the one-row audited act it already is.

**4 · A commit refuses a file with any bad row — all or nothing.** A chart
half-loaded from a file with three bad lines leaves a utility unable to say
which of 180 accounts arrived, and the obvious remedy (fix the file, import
again) is then unusable, because every good row now reports `existing`.

**5 · The import is System Admin only, which is TIGHTER than typing one row.**
`create_account` allows System Admin or Billing Clerk. Ruling 4 puts the whole
Accounting screen at System Admin, and this is that screen's door. One account
typed by a clerk is one audited act somebody reviews; 180 arriving from a
spreadsheet is a chart of accounts. Stated because the asymmetry is real and
would otherwise read as an oversight.

**What would falsify #2:** if the PO says the threshold was only ever meant to
label a queue and never to post, lock (a) should refuse instead of posting.
It is written down here so that can be checked rather than assumed.

## 2026-08-17 · CR-006 area-tagging lane — five judgments the PO's sentence did not settle

**The ruling being implemented, verbatim:** *"when we add premises you should
allow to select areas and sub areas on premises"* — plus BR-MET-082's *"any
change any movement make the changes to downstream"*, which is what makes it
more than a form field.

**The number the PO would recognise:** ticking an area chip on the SET-06 route
picker took it from **"9 premises match" to "0 premises match"**, every time, on
every tenant, because `premises.area_id` had never held a value anywhere. The
acceptance test asserts the same shape at three premises: two tagged NORTH,
filter returns **2**, not 0 and not 3.

**1 · A cascade never takes a unit off another route.** BR-MET-074 says a
conflict is a MOVE, and CR-006 requires that move be confirmed on screen —
*"selecting moves them, with confirm"*. A move triggered by a dropdown on the
premises form is a move nobody agreed to and nobody sees. So tagging only ever
FILLS A GAP: a unit already routed for that service stays exactly where a human
put it. Cost, stated: a utility that re-draws its areas will find some premises
still on their old routes and must open the wizard. That is the correct place to
be told.

**2 · Only ACTIVE routes gain from a tag.** DEF-219 was ruled the same day —
*"a draft is a thing that has not happened yet and must not have consequences a
person can see"* — and SET-05's Members column counts memberships, so a draft
growing from the premises form is exactly that shape one screen over.

**3 · Re-tagging a premises never REMOVES it from a route.** DEF-219 was a draft
emptying a live route from a screen nobody expected to do it; a tag change that
un-routed a premises is the same defect with a different trigger. Removal stays
the wizard's act, where it is confirmed and audited.

**4 · A unit joins the routes its PREMISES is on, read from BOTH directions —
its siblings' memberships AND its premises' area routes.** The sibling-only rule
looked sufficient and is not: a premises created straight into an area has no
units yet when the tag lands, so every unit added afterwards is a "first" unit
with no sibling to inherit from, and the building would silently never be routed
at all. Found by a test, not by review.

**5 · ⚠ THE BIG ONE, AND IT IS A DELIBERATE PARTIAL. Membership is still a
STORED answer kept correct by two more write paths — NOT derived at run time.**
BR-MET-082 Amendment 1 asks for derivation, and DEF-225 stays OPEN for it. What
this change buys: the two symptoms a utility would actually hit are gone — a
premises tagged into an area is read and billed by that area's routes, and a
unit added to a serviced building is read and billed (both were previously
*never*). What it does NOT buy: a premises moved between areas keeps its old
routes (judgment 3, deliberate); a route whose `area_id` is CHANGED does not
re-derive; **accounts still have no path to a route or a cycle in any form**, so
BR-MET-082 clause 4 remains unmodelled and *"how many accounts does this run
cover"* is still unanswerable through the chain.

**And the tension Amendment 1 names is untouched rather than resolved.**
`units_in_cycle` promises *"a run scoped twice covers the same accounts in the
same order"*, which is about one run's preview-to-issue window, while the PO's
rule is about run-to-run. Because membership stays stored, that promise holds
today exactly as written and **no freeze mechanism was built or needed**. A
future lane doing the run-time derivation must build the freeze in the same
change — this lane neither resolved that nor made it harder.

**What would falsify #5:** if the PO says a route drawn for an area must
re-derive its whole membership whenever the area's premises change — including
dropping premises that leave the area — then the stored answer is the wrong
model and DEF-225's derivation is the fix, not this.

**6 · The fourteen new UI strings were TRANSLATED into all ten other languages
rather than added to DEF-215's pile.** DEF-215 records 309 English values
already sitting in each non-English catalogue, CR-006's own route-wizard area
strings among them, and the supplier order has no date. These fourteen are on
the premises form, which every tenant uses. G15 still reports 309 — unchanged.
**Reported rather than hidden:** the Routes & Cycles siblings (*"Area ·
sub-area"*, *"No area"*) stay English, so that surface reads half-translated in
ten locales while the premises form reads fully translated.

## 2026-08-17 — CR-008: ONE EDITOR for a GL code, a tender's own cash account, and validation at the pick

**PO rulings, verbatim** (change register, *"CR-008 — PO RULINGS 2026-08-17
(second set)"*): *"editing and chaigng will be done in setting only"* · *"we
will display it every place where it make sense"* · *"Im okay with this ; I
agree"* on the architecture · *"Im good with all"* on the three things to build.

**What was shown to the PO in plain English, with figures**, and what the repo
now says, so the next agent can build the same thing from the repo alone:

**1 · The gap that started it, worked.** A utility takes $412.30 by card through
Stripe and $85.00 in cash at the counter on the same day. The card settlement
arrives two days later net of the processor's fee; the drawer is counted that
afternoon. `payment_methods` held code · name · is_system · active and **no GL
column at all**, so there was nowhere to say the two land in different accounts.
`clearing_gl_account_id` is now that column.

**2 · ⚠ THE COLUMN IS NOT WIRED TO POSTING, AND THIS IS A JUDGMENT WITH A
MEASURED REASON — not a deferral.** `post_payment_cleared` debits **undeposited
funds** for every tender (PO ruling 2026-08-11, OQ-143); `reconciliation.py:68`
posts *DR cash / CR undeposited funds* when the bank confirms it. **If the
receipt leg debited a per-tender clearing account while reconciliation kept
crediting undeposited funds, reconciliation would credit an account that was
never debited — the trial balance goes out by the amount of every card
payment.** So the two legs must move in one change, both on the 🔒
ledger-posting path, on their own review. **Shipping half of it is worse than
shipping none.** OQ-264 stays OPEN carrying exactly that half, and the screen
says in words that nothing posts differently yet.
**What would falsify this call:** if the PO's intent was that setting the column
must change where the money lands *now*, then this lane under-delivered and the
posting change is CR-008's, not a follow-on.

**3 · The name is `clearing_gl_account_id`, not `gl_account_id`.** Every other
GL pointer in the product is the REVENUE side (`charges.gl_account_id`,
`plan_services.gl_account_id`, `tenant_services.revenue_account`); this is the
CASH side. CR-008 already had to resolve one near-identical-name collision this
week — the $5.00 automatic small-balance write-off beside a $5,000 manual
approval threshold — and a name is the cheapest place to prevent the next one.

**4 · ONE EDITOR is only true once the one editor exists.** Making
`ChargeCodesTab` read-only *without* adding a charge → account editor to
Settings → Accounting would have left a late fee with **no editor anywhere**,
and BR-BIL-010 fails the WHOLE bill at issue when a fee line cannot resolve an
account. Section 4 of the GL-mapping tab therefore gained the row action in the
same change that took the picker off Plans & Rates. The tax half already had
one; adjustment reasons and tenders have theirs.

**5 · ⚠ A read-only field must OMIT its column, never send `null`.** Both rating
forms previously posted the GL pointer on every save. Left as `null` they would
have **cleared a mapping every time somebody renamed a charge or corrected a
filing form** — the one way a read-only field can still destroy data. `PATCH`
treats an omitted field as *leave it*, which is what both forms now do.

**6 · The storage did not move, and this is not a migration.** A charge's
account is still a column on the charge; a tax authority's still on the tax. One
mapping table would force every bill into an extra lookup and lose the property
that makes it safe — the account travels with the item it belongs to. The PO
agreed this explicitly. **The change is to the DOOR, not the room.**

**7 · Validation at the pick — and the brief's own count was half wrong, which
is recorded because the next reader will otherwise repeat it.** Four GL pointers
were said to be bare uuids with no referential integrity. **Measured: two of the
four already validated** — `taxes.liability_gl_account_id` since 2026-08-11
(BR-BIL-069's lane) and `reason_codes.default_gl_account_id` since that morning.
**The two that genuinely did not are `charges.gl_account_id` and
`plan_services.gl_account_id`**, each `_uuid_value` and nothing else, so any
well-formed uuid was stored — another utility's account id included — and the
first thing to notice was BR-BIL-010 refusing the whole bill on billing day.
Both now ask the ledger. **The issue-time check STAYS**: an account live today
can be deactivated tomorrow, so this is an earlier refusal, never a replacement.

**8 · Five pointers, two implementations, and both are single.** rating's three
share `_validated_gl_account`; tenancy's two share the new
`GlPointerLookupMixin`. Copying five times would put five statements of one
money rule in the tree, and the copy that drifts is the one nobody reads.

**9 · What was NOT done, said plainly.** The posting wiring (above). No screen
in the product writes `plan_services.gl_account_id` — there is no picker for it
anywhere, and CR-008 did not add one, because the PO ruled a plan service is
*displayed* read-only; the wizard now says so instead of claiming the chart is
unbuilt (**DEF-231**, the fourth screen carrying DEF-206's expired claim).

## 2026-08-17 — CR-009 IN-APP: the first channel this product can deliver on, and six judgments made where the ruling stopped

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"We can confirm it whether it is working on not
if we get in APp Notifcaition, which does not require any integration and it is
proof that notification is working; for single notification send 1 message and
for bulk action also send 1 message only saying nulk action is completed"* —
and then, plainly: ***"can you build the in-app?"***

Two rules came out of it and are written where rules live, not here:
**BR-NOT-019** (in-app is a real channel and the platform is its provider) and
**BR-NOT-020** (one message per bulk action, with its failure count). What
follows is the SIX places the ruling ran out and this lane had to judge, each
with the worked figure that was in front of it.

**Shipped in version 2.9.0.** Proved end to end on a booted stack, in a real
browser, before this row was written — the transcript is in §7.

### 1 · The in-app adapter sits BEHIND the existing provider seam, not beside it

`apps/notifications/in_app.py` implements
`dispatch_outbound_batch(channel, messages) -> {id: answer}` **verbatim** — the
same contract `apps.integrations.services` is owed for the other three channels
— and `provider_seam.adapter()` resolves it by channel. It would have been a
third of the code to have the bulk-summary writer insert an inbox row directly.

**Why not:** the PO's claim is that a message arriving is *"proof that
notification is working"*, and that is only true if the message travelled the
REAL path. A direct insert would have proved that a row can be written to a
table, which nobody doubted. Measured on the booted stack: the message went
queue → claim → batch id → template pin → render → seam hand-off → inbox, and
`dispatch_outbound` printed **`dispatched: yes`** for the first time in this
product's history.

### 2 · In-app is always active, with no tenant flag — the shape print has, for a different reason

`channel_is_active("in_app")` returns True unconditionally. Email and SMS have
columns because their SEND waits on the platform or the tenant; in-app waits on
nothing — no vendor, no credentials, no connection, no cost.

**The judgment:** a flag here would be a switch with nothing behind it in the
OTHER direction from the usual defect — not a promise of a missing feature, but
an **off-switch for the only channel that works**. A utility turns notifications
off per EVENT on SET-12, which BR-NOT-017 made the one door; a tenant-wide kill
switch on a different screen would silently disable every event's delivery and
re-create the two-doors problem that ruling closed.

### 3 · In-app is EXEMPT from quiet hours — a reading of BR-NOT-009, not a quotation

BR-NOT-009's own words are *"tenant-config send window for **email/SMS**"* and
its stated harm (T5-23) is *"a utility texting late-payment reminders at
23:00"* — a message that wakes somebody.

**The judgment:** an in-app message wakes nobody. It is a number on a bell that
a staff member sees when they next open the product, and it goes to the
utility's own staff rather than to a customer. **Worked:** a billing run that
fails at 22:00 would otherwise be reported at 08:00 the next morning, which is
the one thing this channel exists to prevent. Recorded here because it is a
reading; if the PO disagrees, one frozenset in `dispatcher.py` is the change.

### 4 · The bulk summary is addressed to the ACTOR — and **OQ-261 is NOT answered**

The one message goes to the staff member who RAN the bulk action and to nobody
else: deliberately the narrowest possible audience, and the only one that needs
no ruling, because whoever pressed the button is definitionally involved.

**What it is NOT:** an answer to OQ-261, which asks who receives a
RULE-CONFIGURED staff alert (*"SLA breach (Owner copied)"*, *"all Email +
In-app to the relevant role"*). A job with NO signed-in user — a nightly
reconciliation — is **REFUSED by name with the open question's id** rather than
addressed to the tenant's first System Admin, because that guess would answer
OQ-261 in code, for every utility on the platform, in a file nobody would think
to look in. `in_app` therefore STAYS listed as unavailable on the five staff
events in `rule_catalog.py` — with its reason rewritten, because the old one
(*"there is no in-app notification surface"*) is now false and the real
blocker is the addressee.

### 5 · `outbound_messages.render_context` — a new column, and why it is not the thing the renderer refused to add

`rendering.render_for_dispatch` has REPORTED this gap since 2026-08-15: *"the
merge context is still empty on this deployment unless a caller supplies one …
so a dispatch-time render produces the template's text with its catalogued
tokens marked as NAMED ABSENCES."*

It became load-bearing the moment a channel could deliver. **Measured, by
breaking it deliberately:** with the column ignored, the delivered message read
**`—— finished. —— processed · —— failed`**. With it, the same message read
**`Billing run finished. 1204 processed · 3 failed 08/17/2026`** — and the date
is in the tenant's own Regional format, which is the typed codec working.

**Why this is not the invention the old docstring refused** (*"inventing one
would mean this module deciding what a bill says"*): **BR-NOT-012 already names
this store** — *"the notification's own stored render context for non-invoice
notices"*. The column is NULL unless the writer that already held the facts
stamps them; no writer that existed before today passes one; a NULL context
renders exactly as it did yesterday. **An invoice's figures still do not go in
it** — a bill's numbers live on the invoice, and a second copy of a money figure
on a queue row is free to disagree with the document it describes.

**One mechanic worth recording:** JSON has neither `Decimal` nor `date`, and
`_rendered_value` formats BY TYPE. So the context is TAGGED on write and
restored on read (`encode_context`/`decode_context`), and a **float is refused
at the WRITE** (CLAUDE.md rule 2) so the bad value never reaches the database
rather than failing one dispatch cycle at a time.

### 6 · The bulk summary carries NO masthead — the only body in the library that does not

Every printable class carries `_PRINTABLE_MASTHEAD` because *"every one of
these documents is a LETTER FROM THE UTILITY"*. This one is the PRODUCT talking
to the utility's own operator, inside the product they are signed in to.

**Measured, and it is why this is here rather than in a comment:** the first
cut of the body ended with `{utility_name}`, and on the test tenant it rendered
**`——`** under every run summary — because the tenant had no company profile
filled in. The token is now out of the class's whitelist, so a body that uses
it cannot be saved.

### 7 · What was PROVED, on a booted stack and in a real browser

The PO named in-app as how they would confirm notifications work, so an
unproven claim here would be worse than a partial one. Measured 2026-08-17
against `boot_stack.sh` (Postgres + Django + the BUILT SPA on one origin):

| Step | Measured |
|---|---|
| A staff event fires | `send_bulk_summary --total 1204 --failed 3` → **1 queue row** |
| The dispatcher drains it | `dispatch_outbound` → **`dispatched: yes · sent 1`** |
| It reaches the inbox | `GET /in-app-messages` → `unread: 1`, body carries the real figures |
| The bell shows a count | **badge reads `1`** in Chromium at 1440×900 |
| The popover reads it | **"Billing run finished. 1204 processed · 3 failed 08/17/2026"** |
| Opening it marks it read | badge **gone**, item class becomes `bell-item read` |
| No send route exists | `POST …/in-app-messages/send` and `…/test-send` → **404** |
| A retried run cannot double-report | same `--operation-id` twice → **"ALREADY QUEUED (rule 6)"** |


## 2026-08-17 · CR-010 item 9 — fixture version grammar becomes V<a>.<b>.<c>.<d>
**PO, verbatim:** *"it should ve V1.0.0.0 something like this and then increment"* — closing the question the
seed-map artifact put (the artifact showed the current `YYYY.MM[.N]` grammar, `2026.08.2`, against the PO's
requested `V.X.x.y`, and asked whether that meant a V-prefix on three parts or a genuine four-part number).
**The worked figure shown:** the shipped fixture re-declares as **V1.0.0.0** with content byte-identical to
2026.08.2 (same digest `0c203b16…`, two keys in the pin). **The one non-obvious engineering fact, recorded so
nobody "simplifies" it away:** `version_key` gained an epoch element because plain numeric comparison sorts
V1 (1, …) BELOW 2026.08 (2026, …) — backwards — which would have left every existing tenant reading as AHEAD
of V1.0.0.0 forever and the sweep delivering nothing. Legacy rows in `reference_seed_runs` are NOT rewritten:
they are the honest record of what each tenant received; ordering, not migration, is what maps them forward.
BR-TEN-077's grammar sentence amended the same commit. Build 2.10.0 (CR-010's first landing slice).

**PO verbatim:** *"1 · Account types & sub-types (full tree) - all these are okay , where you will add Hospital, Church etc; - seed this list; 2 · Charge codes (13 = 6 seeded + 7 NEW) - these are good; can you extend this list to 25 items - show me all 25 items on screen ; 3 · Meter size classes (9 = 7 seeded + 2 NEW) - these are good; you dont need Base charge - we agreed; 4 · Premise & unit types (one card, two levels) - this is correct; you can alos make them Govtment building also ; 5 · Areas (4 parents, sub-areas left to the tenant) — plus a fix I found writing this - this is okay - seed it ; 6 · Tax jurisdictions (keep 1, my recommendation) - can you give me more options; 7 · Regional defaults (the 11 blank fields) - yes this is good;"*
What each ruling does: **(1)** the four-type sub-type tree is RATIFIED as proposed and gains a home for Hospital and Church — placed under Commercial as `Institutional & non-profit` (church, temple, private school) and `Healthcare` (hospital, clinic), shown back on screen for amendment; needs the sub-type schema slice. **(2)** charge codes grow 13 → **25**; the 12 additions are drafted (worked rows on the artifact) with every unruled dollar flagged. **(3)** size classes ratified at 9 AND the base-$ figures come OUT of the display names — *"you dont need Base charge - we agreed"* — which also retires the money-figure-smuggled-into-a-name defect class for this list (base is priced by plans, stated once). **(4)** premise types gain `government_building` (BR-MET-034 amended, 5 → 6) and unit types become editable rows on the same card (schema slice). **(5)** the four areas seed with CLEANED names — the seeded strings carried r10's "· 3 sub-areas" counts, claiming sub-areas no tenant has. **(6)** more options owed on tax jurisdictions — a six-option menu goes back. **(7)** the US-first regional default set is RATIFIED and seeds at provisioning; `accounting_method` stays unset (the control was removed by the PO's own CR-008 ruling 1).

## 2026-08-18 · CR-010 schema slice 1 BUILT — the account sub-type tree, and the three judgment calls inside a ruled change
**What landed (ruling: "Part-10 confirmations" 10.0, PO 2026-08-17 *"add them"* + A-section item 1):** `account_subtypes.account_type_id` (customers 0011, PROTECT), BR-CUS-067, the 12 rows seeded per tenant through the customers seed seam (`SEED_ACCOUNT_SUBTYPES` — the fixture deliberately carries no copy, the DEF-026 premises_types posture, so there is no second source to drift), a full-CRUD `AccountSubtypeLookupHandler`, and the S8 `account_subtypes` card whose table names each row's parent type and whose editor picks among the four platform types.
**Judgment 1 — the parent FK is NULLABLE in the DATABASE and REQUIRED at the HANDLER.** The table has been writable since W2, so rows may exist that predate the ruling; a NOT NULL backfill would invent which of four types each old row belongs to. New and edited rows cannot save without a parent (`customers.lookups.parent_required`), so the tree is two-level everywhere a user can reach. Worked figure: 12 seeded rows, every one with a parent; a create with no parent refuses BY NAME.
**Judgment 2 — "renders two levels in the SAME frame" is built as TWO cards in the SAME S8 frame and group**, not one card with two tables: the read-only platform `account_types` card and the tenant-editable `account_subtypes` card sit side by side under ACCOUNTS, and the sub-types table's first data column after code/name is **Account type** — so opening either card shows the tree's two levels. One card holding two lists would have needed a new view shape (against BR-SHL-035's one-list-one-view frame) and would have broken the DEF-236 join guard, which pairs every declared list with its own card. The `account_types` card is retitled "Account types" (it had carried "…& sub-types" as an E3 stand-in since 2026-08-09); the PAIR is S65.
**Judgment 3 — DISCRETIONARY, not structural (BR-TEN-067):** nothing schema-required references a sub-type (`accounts.account_subtype_id` is NULL by r5 #19), so the S111 toggle governs the list like other vocabulary. A toggle-off tenant gets an empty, fully usable card.
**Mechanism note:** the frontend gained `parentList` on ReferenceCard — the cross-list form of `areas`' `hierarchical` flag (parents fetched from ANOTHER list, per-card copy keys). `areas` is untouched. i18n: 9 new keys × 11 catalogues, translated (G15 clean on the new keys; the 308 pre-existing untranslated CR-006 values in each non-English catalogue are another lane's and are NOT touched here).


## 2026-08-18 · CR-008 B-10 BUILT — tender→GL posting, both legs in one change, and three judgments where the ruling stopped

**The ruling implemented, PO verbatim (2026-08-17):** *"10 - A inside CR-008
now"* — OQ-264's second half, the one its own record called *"the half that
moves money"*.

**The worked case, end to end (the CR record's own figures):** a utility takes
**$412.30** by card through Stripe and **$85.00** in cash at the counter. With
`card → 1015 Merchant clearing — Stripe` mapped and cash unmapped, the receipt
entries are **DR 1015 412.30 / CR AR** and **DR 1010 85.00 / CR AR**; when the
bank confirms the card day, reconciliation posts **DR 1000 Cash / CR 1015** —
and 1015 nets to ZERO, which is the tie-out the 2026-08-17 record said goes
out *"by the amount of every card payment"* if either leg moves alone. Both
legs moved in this one slice; the arrival-signal test
(`test_cr008_setting_a_tender_account_changes_NO_posting`) fired exactly as
designed and is INVERTED, not deleted.

**Three judgments the ruling does not make, each with its figure:**

1. **Reconciliation credits what was DEBITED, read from the ENTRIES — never
   from today's mapping.** A clerk re-points card from 1015 to 1016 between
   two receipts: crediting today's mapping would strand the earlier $412.30
   in 1015 forever. So the credit split comes from the member receipts' own
   journal entries, through a new published tenant-scoped ledger read
   (`entry_debit_totals`), and the re-point case is a test that nets BOTH
   accounts to zero (412.30 → 1015, 85.00 → 1016).
2. **A mapping to a dead account REFUSES the payment whole — no fallback.**
   Pick-time validation (CR-008 ruling 3) cannot see a deactivation that
   happens after the pick. Falling back to undeposited would silently move
   money to an account the tenant told us not to use; posting anyway puts
   cash in a row the trial balance treats as retired. The refusal names the
   tender and the GL mapping page, inside `record_payment`'s transaction, so
   no payment row and no entry survive it.
3. **A member with NO journal entry (pre-2026-08-11 legacy) credits
   undeposited funds** — the only lawful answer for that era and byte-for-byte
   the old behaviour — and the seam then refuses the whole request unless the
   split foots to the batch's recorded total, so a membership the entries
   cannot account for stops the reconcile instead of plugging a difference.

**What did NOT change, by name:** OQ-143's law (money is not realised until
the bank confirms it) — only WHICH holding account holds the unconfirmed money
is now the tender's choice; NULL mapping = undeposited funds, unchanged; NSF
mirrors whatever was posted (BR-LED-003), so the mapped leg unwinds for free —
asserted, not assumed; posting keys unchanged, so idempotency is untouched and
re-asserted on the mapped path; Unreconcile still mirrors the reconcile entry,
multi-credit included, by construction.

**Proof discipline:** the whole test file was written and run BEFORE the
wiring existed — 8 of 10 cases RED, failures quoted in its trailer (tc1
`assert Decimal('0') == Decimal('412.30')`; tc7 `TypeError: … unexpected
keyword argument 'undeposited_credits'`) — then green after; the SET-11 §3
screen sentence changed in the same slice (hard-won law 1, the other
direction); golden harness 33 PASS / 0 FAIL after the change.

## 2026-08-18 · CR-010 schema slice 2 BUILT — unit types become rows (BR-MET-084), and the fixture serial moves so existing tenants get BOTH new lists
**What landed (ruling: A-section item 4, PO 2026-08-17 *"this is correct"* on "Premise & unit types (one card, two levels)"):** the `unit_types` table (metering 0011, RLS ENABLE+FORCE in the same migration), the five US-MET-002 §5 codes seeded `is_system` per tenant from `SEED_UNIT_TYPES`, a full-CRUD handler, and the S8 "Unit types" card in the PREMISES group.
**Judgment 1 — r10's ONE "Premise & unit types" card is built as the PREMISES group's TWO sibling cards** ("Premises types" · "Unit types"), for the same reasons as slice 1's judgment 2: the ONE list view is one-list-per-card (BR-SHL-035) and the DEF-236 join guard pairs every declared list with its own card. Least invention; the design's surface, the frame's shape.
**Judgment 2 — `units.unit_type` stays TEXT, no FK.** The column predates the table, importers and the sample fixture write bare codes, and a backfill would guess nothing but risk plenty. Validation is table-FIRST (a deactivated row is not pickable and the legacy fallback may NOT resurrect it — worked: deactivate `commercial`, a unit with `commercial` refuses even though the tuple still lists it), legacy-tuple second (a toggle-off tenant with zero rows still creates units; every stored value stays valid). Consequence owned in code: the handler itself enforces BR-TEN-030/034 by live count, because no PROTECT will.
**Judgment 3 — DISCRETIONARY (BR-TEN-067)**, and therefore NOT seeded from `ensure_reference_catalogs()` (which runs on premises writes regardless of the S111 toggle) — only through the reference seam.
**Judgment 4 — display names are the product's existing `metering.units.type.*` copy** ("Residential · sub-metered", "Commercial · master", …) — the seed invents no naming, and the card and the unit-form dropdown can never disagree about what a code is called.
**The fixture bump, stated as item 3 of the task demanded:** `lookup_defaults.json` → **V2.13.0.1** (serial bump, content digest IDENTICAL to V2.13.0.0 and pinned under both keys — BR-TEN-077's fourth part exists for exactly this: no product digit was assigned to this landing, so `<seed-serial>` moves). The bump is not cosmetic: without it the sweep never revisits a tenant already at V2.13.0.0, and `account_subtypes` + `unit_types` would reach only NEW tenants.
**REPORTED, not built:** the S16/S14 unit-form dropdown still offers its own five-entry constant, so a tenant-ADDED type is API-valid but not yet offered there — the wiring belongs to the unit screens' territory (see BR-MET-084's ⚠ note). **Also fixed in passing:** test_us_met_001_002_lists' stale `len == 5` premises-types pin (red on the branch since item 4's 5→6 amendment) and test_us_ten_002's TC-5 synthetic "newer" version, which was hardcoded to exactly V2.13.0.1 and is now V99.0.0.0 so it can never collide with a real bump again.
