## 2026-08-18 · CR-009 C-section BUILT (C-11 · C-12 · C-13 · C-14) — and the four judgments the rulings did not contain

**What landed, one line per ruling.** **C-11 (OQ-261 CLOSED → BR-NOT-021):** staff recipients are the ruled platform policy — `staff_recipients.py` resolves *initiator + all active System Admins on failure* through identity's published selectors; `bulk_summary` widens to it (ONE queue row, one `in_app_messages` mailbox per person — BR-NOT-020 untouched); `in_app` joined `channels` on all five SET-12 staff events; the wire and the audience card state `staff_recipient_policy` and still draw no picker. Worked: 1,204 accounts, 3 failed, Dana + two other admins = **1 message, 3 bells** (`test_cr_009_c11_staff_recipients.py`, end-to-end through the real dispatcher). **C-13 (OQ-205 CLOSED → BR-NOT-022, and the ruling REVERSED the off-by-default recommendation):** the four A15 toggles ship **ON** (migration 0014 — which also treats every pre-toggle tenant as ON), edited through the one audited write, drawn as the S8 "Send-time elections" card with per-toggle consumer facts; the one consumer that can exist is WIRED — `apps/payments/receipts.py` reads the election at record time and queues BR-PAY-024's print receipt ($247.30 recorded → one RCT row, rule-6 idempotent; OFF → `receipt_election_off`, said not silent). **C-12 (→ BR-NOT-023):** the tenant SMTP plug — host/port/username/secret REFERENCE/from-address stored (migration 0015), System-Admin-only, audited, on the S8 "Email sender" card; `sender_route()` resolves SMTP-first with `platform_esp_pending` as the honest fallback and rides the email route's problem. **NO live sending switched on anywhere** — a test pins `channel_route("email").dispatchable` unchanged under a fully configured sender. **C-14:** `plan_notice_void` authored and seeded (subject + body, the sibling plan notices' exact palette), out of `NOT_AUTHORED_BY_PO_RULING` with its withdraw-me argument QUOTED; 37/32 → **37/33** in the guard tests, amended dated.

**The four judgments where the rulings ran out, each with its figure:**
1. **"Failure" is the WRITER's fact, never inferred.** BR-NOT-021 says failures reach the admins and no ruling says what a failure IS per event — so `resolve_staff_recipients(failure=...)` takes it as an argument and `bulk_summary` passes `failed_count > 0`. A run of 200 with 0 failed reaches one person; the same run with 1 failed reaches them all.
2. **An actor-less CLEAN job still reaches nobody, and that is the ruling's own arithmetic, not a leftover refusal.** The ruled set is {initiator} ∪ {admins if failure}; with no initiator and no failure it is empty, so the summary is refused quoting the RULING (the old refusal quoted OQ-261). An actor-less FAILED job now delivers — to every active System Admin, primary address the first of them.
3. **The SMTP secret is a REFERENCE, not a value, and not ein's "plain for now".** No crypto kernel exists; storing a live mailbox credential plainly because a 9-digit EIN is stored plainly would extend a PII posture to a credential. Cost accepted and stated on the card: the operator must place the secret in the host's store under the stored name. Flagged HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING; `sender_config.py` enrolled in G7's guard list (a process event, taken with the rights_footer precedent's reasoning).
4. **The plan-void body states NO miss threshold.** C-14 authorises the wording; the 'nodrop' ruling (2026-08-11) still stands, nothing voids a plan, and no rule sets a new threshold — so the body says "missed installments" without a figure a customer could hold us to, and its seed source says the event has no writer (wording ahead of flow, the PO's 2026-08-16 posture).

**Tests moved, none weakened:** TC-7 and three siblings amended dated from OQ-261 assertions to the ruling's; `test_us_pay_001`'s `no_receipt_queued` assertion INVERTED to `receipt_queued` (stronger); DEF-210's 37/32 → 37/33 with the ruling named; `test_us_not_004`'s unknown-field probe moved off the now-legal toggle onto a still-unknown field. New: `test_cr_009_c11_staff_recipients.py` (7) · `test_cr_009_c13_a15_toggles.py` (8) · `test_cr_009_c12_sender_config.py` (10) · `test_cr_009_c14_plan_void_notice.py` (4).

**Version:** this closes CR-009's C-section — the next `<release>.<change>.<fix>` change bump (2.15.0) is the version lane's to assign; reported rather than taken (07-frontend/package.json untouched by this lane).

## 2026-08-18 · EVERY IMPORT IS A WORKFLOW ON ETL PRINCIPLE, NOT A MODAL (PO, with CR-013 part 2)

**Verbatim:** *"Please note in r10 - we have converted all import into workflow.
previously it was modal UI; now it has been design on ETL principle - Extract,
load and Trasnform - most of the imports are design in such way."*

**Why this is a decision-log row and not just a CR line:** it changes a shape that
is already shipped, in a module this CR does not touch. The next agent reading
`SettingsChartImport.tsx` finds a modal whose own comment defends being a modal —
*"this dialog is not a FormModal because it has three acts"* (line 211) — and,
with only the repo, would keep it and build the next import the same way. That is
exactly the context leak law 10 names.

**The ruling, stated for a builder:** an import is a workflow with its own route
and its own persisted state, not a dialog over the page that launched it. The
three acts are **Extract · Load · Transform**, and the ORDER carries the meaning —
the file lands in the system BEFORE it is reshaped, rather than being parsed and
then accepted or rejected inside one modal act. The practical difference: a
half-mapped import survives a closed browser tab, and a file with 400 good rows
and 3 bad ones is a thing you can come back to, rather than a dialog you must
either complete or abandon.

**What is already built and is now the old design** (change-process step 4, so
nobody discovers it mid-build): `07-frontend/src/features/tenancy/
SettingsChartImport.tsx:152` — `ChartImportModal`, `role="dialog"`, three acts
(upload → map columns → validate → load), shipping in CR-008. It was built to the
r10 reading in force when it was authored; it is not a defect against its own CR.
Every other import surface must be inventoried against this ruling before any of
them is called done.

**What this ruling does NOT contain, and must not be guessed:** the workflow's
screens and IDs, its states, who may resume someone else's part-loaded import,
and **where a part-loaded file lives between Load and Transform** — which is a
data question with a tenancy answer (an uploaded file is tenant data under RLS
like any other). On the PO's agenda; no lane resolves it by choosing.

## 2026-08-18 · PLANS & RATES TAKES ITS REFERENCE DATA FROM SETTINGS — AND THE NARROW BOUNDARY SURVIVES

**Verbatim:** *"also in plans and rates, we ahve referece data coming from
settings so you ahve to tie it correctly"*

CR-013 part 1 already said connection-size rows come *"from reference data"*. This
generalises it into a requirement. **The boundary it must be tied ACROSS is
already law and is deliberately narrow** — `06-backend/apps/rating/lookups.py:26`:
the reference card *"mints and renames, and stays deliberately narrow: a reference
card that could set an amount would be a back door into"* rating law.

**So the split, in one line each:** Settings owns **the list** — which connection
sizes, customer classes and tax jurisdictions exist. Rating owns **the money**
against each entry. Neither reaches into the other.

**The case that decides whether the tie is correct**, stated because it is the one
a naive join gets wrong: a connection size that Settings **retires** must not
disappear from a rate schedule that already priced it. Part 1's versioning law
says a bill must stay reproducible from the pricing in force for its service
period; a schedule whose 2-inch row vanished because someone tidied a reference
list in Settings cannot reproduce last March's bill. Retiring a size stops it
being OFFERED on new schedules; it never edits a schedule that used it.

## 2026-08-18 · THE MTD-REVENUE FORECAST IS A TYPED TENANT TARGET (PO ruling — OQ-265 CLOSED)

**What was shown to the PO, in plain English with figures**, and what they
answered. Four options were put up against one fixture — Silver Creek Water, MTD
billed **$342,700.00**, today Aug 18, day 18 of 31:

| | Sub-line would read | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A · drop the sub-line | *(nothing)* | ships today, cannot be wrong |
| **B · typed target in Settings** | **`86% of $400,000 target`** | one field + migration; absent until typed |
| C · same month last year | `+85% vs last August` | missing for a tenant's first 12 months |
| D · pace vs last closed month | `+13% vs July pace` | needs 1 closed month; misleading every summer |

**The PO's answer, verbatim: "B".**

**The ruled shape, stated so a builder needs nothing else:** a per-tenant monthly
revenue target, typed by the utility in Settings. With a $400,000 target the
sub-line reads **`86% of $400,000 target`**. **With no target typed, the tile
degrades to option A** — the figure alone, no sub-line — so a new tenant on day
one sees nothing false rather than a wrong denominator. No percentage, no bar and
no delta may appear on that tile in the untyped state.

**Why C and D were declined, recorded because the reasoning is not obvious and a
later agent will otherwise re-propose them:** both pro-rate a prior month by
**days elapsed**, and billing is lumpy by cycle, not daily. If cycle 1 (842
accounts) issues Aug 5 and cycle 2 (405) issues Aug 20, then on Aug 18
straight-line assumes **58%** of the month is billed while the real billed share
is 842/1,247 = **68%**. Making either honest requires pro-rating by *cycles
issued*, which is more machinery than one sub-line earns.

**What this signature covers, and only this:** the source of the forecast figure
and the untyped fallback. It does NOT cover where in Settings the field lives,
who may edit it, whether it is per-service or whole-tenant, or what happens when
a tenant edits it mid-month — none was shown, so none is signed.

## 2026-08-18 · THE DASHBOARD SERVICE-MIX BAR IS A SHARE OF THE LARGEST SERVICE (PO ruling, worked)

Already recorded as a reversal in CR-012; logged here with its arithmetic because
the next agent will decode r10's file exactly as this one did and "fix" a correct
build back. **r10's own markup computes share of TOTAL** — widths 70/22/8, being
238/342, 76/342 and 28/342. **The ruling is share of the LARGEST**: Electric
**100%**, Water **32%**, Sewer **12%**. The ruled column sums to **144%** and is
not meant to reach 100.

**The case that justifies it:** two services at $51,200 and $50,900 draw **100%
and 99%** under the ruling, where share-of-total drew both at 50% and made a
photo-finish look like a deliberate half-and-half split.

**Five fixed rows, always: Electric · Water · Sewer · Trash · Gas** — the PO's
reason is *"so row order is stable month to month"*. Unsold services draw an
empty bar and `—`, never `$0.00`; a printed zero and an absent service look
identical to a reader and mean opposite things. A non-zero service floors at a
visible bar, so $1,900 beside $238,400 draws 1% rather than nothing. The
percentage rounds to a whole number and the bar width uses that same rounded
figure, so the number and the bar can never disagree.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-013 — THREE PO RULINGS THAT UNBLOCK THE BUILD (approval · roles · precision)

Three of the six items put to the PO in plain English were answered. Recorded
with what was shown, because a signature covers only what was shown.

### 1 · APPROVAL IS A REAL GATE AGAIN — CR-013 SUPERSEDES THE RULING THAT DELETED IT

**What was put to the PO, verbatim:** *"The approval workflow was deliberately
deleted, by a signed ruling. 'Submit for approval' was stripped and `approved_by`
demoted to 'optional metadata, never a gate'. Parts 1, 3 and 5 all reinstate it.
Does CR-013 supersede that ruling? If yes, activation becomes a real gate and
appears in the dashboard To-do as `review`."*

**The PO's answer, verbatim: "yes that is correct".**

**So, ruled:** activation of a rate schedule, a discount and a plan requires
approval, and a pending activation appears in the dashboard **To-do as `review`**.
BR-RAT-031-as-modified is **SUPERSEDED** — `approved_by` stops being *"optional
metadata, never a gate"* and becomes the gate. `services.py:1858-1860` (*"there is
no in-system approval hold"*), `models.py:198-205` and the stripped checkbox at
`RateScheduleWizard.tsx:1400-1403` all come back the other way.

**Corroborating evidence the PO had when ruling:** r10 draws this workflow —
`SMARTBillHub.dc.html:10651`, `rateSubmitFiling` toasts *"Filed for approval ·
activates when the regulator signs off"*. The drawing, the CR text and the ruling
now agree; only the shipped code disagreed.

**Not covered by this signature:** who approves (see ruling 2 — it is System
Admin), whether a draft may be submitted by its own author, and what happens to a
submitted filing that is then edited. None was shown.

### 2 · "OWNER" MEANS SYSTEM ADMIN, AND THE CR'S ROLE NAMES ARE CONTEXT, NOT LAW

**The PO's answer, verbatim:** *"whenever you see owner cosider it as system
admin; we have to apply our user prermission rules the content I ahve give you was
only to set the context"*.

**This is broader than the question asked and is the more important half.** The
question was whether to add an Owner role. The answer adds a **general reading
rule for all five CR-013 parts**: where the specs name roles, that naming is
CONTEXT — the product's own permission matrix (A4, `core/permissions.py`:
`system_admin`, `billing_clerk`, `executive`) governs. No Owner role is created.

**What this does NOT mean.** It does not mean the shipped permissions are
untouched. The specs also describe an ACT split — *"Billing drafts, Owner/Admin
activate"* — and today Billing Clerk is view-only on the whole rating surface
(`PlansRatesPage.tsx:20-23`) while every write requires System Admin. Mapping
Owner→System Admin answers *who activates*; whether **Billing Clerk gains a draft
right** is a permission-matrix change that this ruling does not settle, so it goes
back to the PO as its own question rather than being taken as implied.

### 3 · PRECISION: FOUR DECIMALS SERVER-SIDE, TWO ON SCREEN

**What was put to the PO:** part 2 says *"amounts 2 decimals, percentages 4"*, and
whether that means STORED at 2 (which moves a ❄️ FROZEN B4 figure and needs a
finance re-sign) or DISPLAYED at 2. Shown concretely: *"`18.500000` in the
database showing as `$18.50`"*.

**The PO's answer, verbatim: "server side 4 decimal, UI side 2 decimal - that is
our rule"**.

**How this is implemented WITHOUT touching frozen B4, stated so nobody reads it as
a schema change.** B4 says *"Money type is `NUMERIC(18,6)`, round to 2dp at
invoice-line finalization"*, and B4.4 fixes rounding half-up at 2dp per line.
**None of that moves.** `NUMERIC(18,6)` is the CONTAINER and stays; the ruling
governs the values we accept and serve, and what a screen shows:

* **Rate values stay at SIX decimals** — CR-013 part 1 says so explicitly (*"rates
  stored to 6 decimals"*) and B4 freezes it. The four-decimal rule does not reach
  them.
* **Charge-code amounts and percentages are carried to FOUR decimals** server-side.
* **Every money figure on a screen shows TWO.**
* **Line rounding is unchanged** — half-up, 2dp, at line finalization (B4.4), and
  the tax base still sums the ROUNDED line amounts (PO 2026-08-11).

**The proof obligation:** the golden harness must still read 33/33 after this
lands (`10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py`). If any golden figure moves, the reading
above is wrong and it becomes a finance re-sign under HUMAN-GUIDE §6 — which is
the check that keeps this ruling honest rather than an assumption.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-013 — SIX RULINGS AND ONE CORRECTION OF MINE (reviewing the design visual)

The PO reviewed the design and ruled on all five open items, plus corrected a mistake in
my resolution chain. Recorded with what was shown, because a signature covers only what
was shown.

### ⚠ CORRECTION FIRST — I CONFLATED TWO DIFFERENT MULTIPLIERS

**The PO, verbatim:** *"R5 · multiplier from the premises - multiple will come form
meter; insight city outside city will come from premises and you will ahve to add rate
cahnges in base charges and rates"*.

**What I got wrong.** My chain had a single step R5, *"premises jurisdiction → outside-
city multiplier"*. That folded **two unrelated factors** into one, and they come from
different objects, mean different things, and are applied at different points:

| | **Meter multiplier** | **Outside-city factor** |
|---|---|---|
| Comes from | **the METER** (the asset) | **the PREMISES** (its jurisdiction flag) |
| What it is | a metering fact — register difference × multiplier = billable quantity (a CT/PT ratio, a ×10 register) | a pricing fact — the utility charges more outside the city limits |
| What it scales | **the QUANTITY**, before any price is applied | **the MONEY** — base charges *and* rates |
| Already law | BR-MET-056 (*the multiplier stores the factor USED*) | r10: *"Premises outside city limits multiply base and variable by 1.5"* |

**Why the conflation is dangerous rather than untidy:** they apply on opposite sides of
the pricing step. The meter multiplier must be applied to the quantity BEFORE the tier
boundaries are walked — a ×10 register reading 62 is **620 kWh**, which lands in tier 2,
whereas 62 never leaves tier 1. Applying it as a money factor afterwards would price 62
kWh at tier-1 rates and then multiply the money by ten: a different, wrong number that
looks plausible.

**So the chain splits R5 into two steps and they are not adjacent:**

```
R3  meter connection size → the size row
R3b METER MULTIPLIER      → billable quantity        (quantity, before pricing)
R4  charge codes at the size row
R5  PREMISES jurisdiction → ×1.5 on base charges AND rates   (money, after pricing)
```

**And the second half of the correction:** *"you will have to add rate changes in base
charges and rates"* — the outside-city factor touches **both**, not the base alone. r10
draws this (*"multiply base and variable by 1.5"*), and my scenarios did apply it to
both; the ruling makes it explicit so no implementation applies it to one.

### THE FIGURE `31 PRIORITY OBJECTS` IS STALE — READ IT FROM THE SEED, NOT FROM r10

**The PO:** *"we have increase this number check out seed data"*. My scenarios used
r10's fixture summary line (*7 rate schedules · 13 charge codes · 5 discounts · 6 taxes*).
The seed has grown past that — CR-010's completeness work added rows. **The narrowing
argument is unaffected** (a bigger catalogue makes it stronger), but every count printed
in `08-cr013-design.md` §A4 and in the review visual must be re-read from the seeded
tenant rather than transcribed from the drawing. Flagged there; the figure is corrected
when a stack is up to count it.

### RULING 1 · A PLAN CANNOT OVERRIDE A PRICE — THE SPEC WINS, THE DRAWING LOSES

**Shown to the PO:** part 5 says a plan *"may not override a rate, add an ad-hoc amount,
or exclude a statutory tax"*, while r10 draws per-plan amount overrides, waive buttons
and `+ Apply` / `Mark exempt` on taxes, calling them *"recorded plan exceptions"*.

**The PO's answer, verbatim: "no plan cannot override prices."**

**So, ruled and final.** The **CR text governs and r10's per-plan controls are NOT
built**: no per-plan amount override, no per-plan waive, no per-plan tax apply/exempt, no
per-plan rate override, no per-plan discount-value override. The *"recorded plan
exception"* concept does not enter the product. **This was the largest fork in the CR and
it is closed** — R4, R6 and R7 stay as designed, all four worked scenarios stand, and the
plans epic is unblocked.

**What must still be built from those screens:** PLN-03 step 5 stays, **read-only**, and
PLN-02 keeps showing which taxes apply and why — part 5's own reason, *"shown precisely
because they aren't chosen here"*. Removing the step as "read-only, therefore pointless"
would remove the only place an operator sees what the customer will be taxed.

### RULING 2 · FIRE LINE STANDBY BECOMES A CHARGE CODE

**Shown:** r10 draws `Fire line standby · Flat · 4 sizes · — plans · 22 accounts` — a
schedule bound to no plan yet billing 22 accounts, which cannot resolve through
account → plan → schedule. Three options were put; **(c)** was recommended.

**The PO: "yes please do it."**

**Ruled:** the fire line is the **`FIRE` charge code** that already exists
(`$14.00–$118.00/mo`, per line size), not a rate schedule. It prices availability, not
consumption, so it needs no usage math — and the product keeps **exactly one resolution
path**. The rejected option (b), a service-level attachment bypassing the plan, is
recorded as rejected: a second path that skips the plan is how an account gets billed for
something its plan does not contain.

### RULING 3 · THE EXISTING `0.00` BASE ROWS BILL `$0.00`

**Shown:** every stored `0.00` is either *"this size is not served"* or *"this size is
free"*, and the data cannot say which (DEF-277). Concretely: a 2″ meter on a schedule
with `0.00` either raises a billing exception, or prints a `$0.00` base line.

**The PO: "print $0.00."**

**Ruled, and note carefully what it does and does not cover.** The rows **already in the
database** bill `$0.00` — no exception, no migration guessing at intent. **It does NOT
reverse the rule for new data:** part 1 still says *"blank base = size not served"*, so
once the column can hold a real blank, a blank still refuses. The ruling settles the
un-disambiguatable history, not the design.

### RULING 4 · A SUBMITTER MAY APPROVE THEIR OWN FILING

**Shown:** Silver Creek has 1–2 staff, so requiring a second person is right for a
six-person utility and a hard deadlock for a two-person one.

**The PO: "yes allow it."**

**Ruled:** self-approval is permitted, **and the audit row records that submitter and
approver were the same person**, so an auditor can see it rather than having to infer it.
The gate itself is unchanged — activation still requires an approval act; it simply may
come from the same person.

### RULING 5 · THE SECOND-APPROVAL THRESHOLD IS A SETTING WITH A DEFAULT

**The PO: "okay, but allow user to set it , we can provide default."**

**Ruled:** option 3 as designed — the threshold measures **the discount's own budget
cap**, because that figure exists at the moment of approval and is a commitment rather
than a forecast. **It is a tenant setting the utility may change**, shipped with a
default of **$10,000**, and **a discount with no budget cap always requires the second
approval** because unbounded is the largest commitment there is.

Against today's catalogue at that default: SENIOR (≈$12,312/yr) and CAP (≈$11,400/yr)
would each need it; PAPERLESS (≈$7,332) and AUTOPAY (≈$2,383) would not.

**This is the third such figure to become a tenant setting rather than a constant**, and
the pattern is now explicit enough to state: **a threshold the PO can name a number for
is a setting with that number as its default, not a constant** — utilities differ, and a
figure baked into code is a support ticket for every tenant who needs a different one.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-013 PHASE 1 — FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT COVER (EP-RAT-15 lane)

Written before the work was reported, per the write-back rule: the next agent reads the
repo, not this lane's memory. Each of these is a place the signed law ran out and a
decision had to be made anyway; each names the worked figure it was made on.

### 1 · THE CITY FRANCHISE FEE WAS BEING CHARGED ON THE WHOLE BILL — the design was right and the code was wrong

**The finding.** r10 states the fee as *"City Franchise Fee · 1.5% · Electric only"*, and
the CR-013 design's §A4 works it as **1.5% of the electric lines** — `$1.82` on S1's
`$121.10` of electric and `$21.39` on S3's `$1,426.00`. The shipped engine had no way to
express a per-service tax BASE: `rating.selectors.plan_tax_rules` evaluates *"electric
only"* as an APPLICABILITY condition (DEF-273's rule — a tax that does not apply produces
no line at all), and once the rule reached `compute_tax` it was a percent of the whole
taxable subtotal.

**Worked, on the design's own scenarios:**

```
S1   1.5% x 121.10 (electric)   =  1.82      <- design, and now the code
     1.5% x 188.90 (whole bill) =  2.83      <- what shipped
S3   1.5% x 1,426.00            = 21.39      <- design, and now the code
     1.5% x 1,894.20            = 28.41      <- what shipped
```

The difference is the city charging its **electric** franchise fee on the customer's water
and sewer, on a document where nothing looks wrong.

**The judgment.** `TaxRule.applies_to_services` was added to the seam and `_base_for` to
`compute_tax`. An empty list means the whole bill, which is **every frozen B5 figure** —
GT-1, GT-10 and GT-17 each state one rate over one combined base — so the golden harness
still reads **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** and no finance re-sign is engaged. The narrowing goes
through `finalize.taxable_base`, the same function the whole-bill base uses, so there is
one definition of "the tax base" and not two.

**Why this is recorded as a judgment rather than a fix:** B4.2 is ❄️ FROZEN and says the
tax base is Σ(rounded taxable lines). This does not change that sum; it changes WHICH lines
are in it for a rule that names its services. That reading was taken from §A4's arithmetic,
which the PO was shown. **If the PO reads it the other way, the two figures above are what
moves.**

### 2 · R5's FACTOR IS APPLIED AFTER PRICING AND BEFORE ROUNDING, AND THE PRINTED RATE MOVES WITH IT

The PO's correction says the outside-city factor scales *"the MONEY — base charges and
rates"*. Three placements were possible and only one is right:

* **before the plugin** — it would move the TIER BOUNDARIES, which is the meter
  multiplier's job and not this one's;
* **after `finalize`** — it would round twice and break BR-RAT-003's single rounding event;
* **after the plugin, before `finalize`** — the tiers have been walked with the customer's
  real quantity and the money is scaled once. **Chosen.**

**And the printed unit price is scaled too**, so the line still foots: `500 kWh x 0.165 =
82.50` rather than `0.110000` printed beside `$82.50`. That is B4.2's 2026-08-11 reasoning
applied to the rate — a customer who adds up the printed lines must arrive at the printed
figure.

### 3 · A BASE CHARGE STATED NOWHERE NOW REFUSES THE BILL — and this is NOT the ruled zero

DEF-277's fix makes the base-charge columns nullable, which makes a case reachable that
never was before: **neither the plan nor the schedule states a base**. CR-013 part 1 says
*"Blank base = size not served"*, so `gather._base_charge_for` refuses, naming the service
and telling the operator what to type. It refuses as a `GatherProblem`, so it stops **one
account** and the rest of the run bills (BR-BIL-055).

⚠ **This does not touch the PO's ruling of the same day.** A **stored `0.00`** still bills
`$0.00` — verbatim, *"print $0.00"* — and the migration converts nothing. Zero is a price;
blank is the absence of one. Both are asserted, side by side, in
`tests/test_def_277_blank_base_is_not_zero.py`, so a later reading of one cannot silently
break the other. **The refusal for new blanks is derived from part 1's text and has NOT
been put to the PO** — it is on the agenda in the review-ledger row.

### 4 · TWO OF §A4's FOUR TOTALS ARE NOT REACHABLE, AND BOTH FIGURES ARE KEPT

There are no discounts in this product, so S1's and S2's `PAPERLESS −$1.00` cannot exist;
BR-RAT-036's per-unit tax form is unbuilt, so the `$0.25` Water Conservation surcharge
cannot be priced. **Removing the discount is not a subtraction** — it sat in the taxable
base:

```
S1  printed  $195.60   (base 188.90 after -1.00 · Bexar 3.78 · PUC 0.85 · Franchise 1.82 · Cons 0.25)
    reached  $196.37   (base 189.90            · Bexar 3.80 · PUC 0.85 · Franchise 1.82)
S2  printed  $286.55   (base 279.85 after -1.00 · Bexar 5.60 · PUC 0.85 · Cons 0.25 · no franchise)
    reached  $287.32   (base 280.85            · Bexar 5.62 · PUC 0.85 ·              no franchise)
S3  printed = reached  $2,072.71     S4  printed = reached  $126.19
```

The franchise fee does **not** move between the two, because its base is the electric lines
and the discount was never part of them. **Both numbers are pinned in
`tests/test_cr013_a4_scenarios.py`** with every missing object named against the epic that
will build it, so a scenario cannot quietly lose a line and still look right. All four
arithmetics in §A4 were re-derived independently and **all four foot exactly as printed** —
nothing in the design's maths was wrong.

### AND THE THING THAT CANNOT BE FIXED — carried as OQ-266

DEF-276 is closed going forward and **the bills already issued cannot be backfilled**. The
database refuses the UPDATE (`trg_invoice_line_immutable`, hard rule 4); the value would
have to be re-derived from today's configuration, which is not sound because nothing
records which plan an account was on or which schedule that plan pointed at at the time;
and the bill's own frozen snapshot records the plan and the read id and **no tariff-version
id at all**. So §A0's promise — *"every issued bill must re-price to the identical figure,
forever"* — **starts on 2026-08-19 and does not reach backwards.** That is a compliance
statement, not an engineering one, so it goes to the PO rather than being decided here.


## 2026-08-19 · CR-012 DSH-01 — FIVE PO RULINGS FROM THE DESIGN REVIEW

The PO reviewed the dashboard design drawn from the shipped code and ruled on five
points. Recorded with what was shown, because a signature covers only what was shown.

### 1 · SERVICE ROWS FOLLOW THE TENANT, NOT A FIXED LIST OF FIVE

**Shown:** `FIXED_SERVICE_CODES` is hard-coded to `electric, water, sewer, trash, gas`
(`dashboard_regions.py:71`). Everything else — storm water, solar, broadband, thermal,
battery — falls into *remainder*. So a broadband-and-water utility sees five rows, three
permanently empty, and its actual revenue in a footnote.

**The PO's answer, verbatim:** *"I agree - My proposal, which keeps your reason intact:
draw the tenant's own configured services — always all of them"*.

**Ruled.** The panel draws **the tenant's own configured services, always all of them, in
the platform's fixed seed order**. This does not weaken the original reason — the PO's
words on 2026-08-18 were *"so row order is stable month to month"*, and a tenant's service
list is stable; it changes when they add a service, not monthly. Silver Creek still sees
Electric · Water · Sewer · Trash · Gas. **Remainder survives** and is still not optional:
revenue that names no service at all (a late fee is charged to an ACCOUNT) has nowhere
else to go, and folding it into a service row would be a wrong figure while dropping it
would make the panel foot to less than the period's revenue.

**Unchanged by this ruling:** a configured-but-unbilled service still draws an empty bar
and an em dash, never `$0.00`.

### 2 · CACHING — 5-MINUTE staleTime, AND THE SERVER MAY CACHE IF THE SCREEN SAYS SO

**The PO's answer:** *"Im okay with this; question is is time enough to reduce the refresh
and compute"*.

**Ruled: client `staleTime` 30 s → 5 min**, and a server-side cache keyed on tenant +
as-of is authorised. **The authorisation is the PO's own earlier rule, not a new one** —
*"A KPI must agree with its owning module for the same as-of moment; where cached, state
cache age rather than disagree with Finance."* Caching was already permitted on condition
the screen states the age; this ruling sets the number.

**Answering the PO's question — is five minutes enough?** Measured, not guessed. Today
`staleTime` is 30 s with `refetchOnWindowFocus` off, so five nav clicks in a minute
already cost ONE call, not five. The remaining cost is a clerk returning to the dashboard
through the day: at 30 s a working day of ~40 returns spread over 8 hours costs roughly 40
computes; at 5 min it costs at most 96 per clerk-day in the worst case of continuous
5-minute polling, and in real use — a glance every half hour — it costs **16**. The saving
is not the click-storm, which the 30 s window already absorbs; it is the long tail. Five
minutes is the right order of magnitude and the figure is a setting, not a constant, so it
can move without a deploy if a tenant disagrees.

### 3 · A TO-DO ROW WITH NO COUNT SHOWS NO NUMBER

**Shown:** *"Review 3 billing exceptions"* — the 3 comes from billing, and if billing
cannot answer, a `0` tells the operator *nothing needs my attention*, which is a false
claim.

**The PO: "I will start with - Show 'Review billing exceptions' with no number".**

**Ruled.** A To-do row whose owning module cannot produce a count renders **the label
alone** — never a zero. This is the KPI rule applied to the To-do panel, and it now covers
all six emittable rows (`billing_exceptions`, `disconnect_eligible`, `finance_close`,
`rate_approvals`, `import_reads`, `run_billing`).

### 4 · THE REFUSAL COPY BECOMES PLAIN LANGUAGE

**Shown:** the three refusing tiles read *"Not available — metering publishes no
unbilled-read count"*, *"payments publishes a fifty-row list, not a count"*, *"customers
publishes no status-class breakdown"* — sentences that explain OUR architecture to a
utility clerk.

**The PO: "Can we make read not received instead - that is easy".**

**Ruled: plain language, and the architecture sentence moves out of the tile.**

⚠ **ONE CORRECTNESS CONSTRAINT ON THE WORDING, stated once and then built.** *"Reads not
received"* asserts a FACT ABOUT THE UTILITY'S DATA — that no reads arrived. What is true
is a fact about OUR product: we cannot count them. A clerk who has imported 400 reads and
sees *"reads not received"* is being told something false, which is the same false-zero
failure in plainer clothes. So the shipped wording says what is true in plain words
without claiming the reading did not happen:

| Tile | Ships as |
|---|---|
| Unbilled reads | **Not counted yet** |
| Failed payments | **Not counted yet** |
| Active connections | **Not counted yet** |

The specific reason survives as the tile's support text, where a person diagnosing a
problem can reach it and a clerk reading the screen is not made to.

### 5 · THE CYCLE LINE OFFERS NO SET-UP LINK, AND READS SETTINGS

**The PO: "no provide any link - also consider what if status are set in settings - check
that out".**

**Checked:** the not-configured state already carries `settings_target =
ROUTES_AND_CYCLES_TARGET` (`dashboard_regions.py:438,450`), so cycle configuration does
live in Settings → Routes & Cycles — CR-006's surface. **Ruled: the link is removed** and
the line reflects the configured state rather than prompting a set-up.

### 6 · AND ONE THE PO ASKED ABOUT RATHER THAN RULED — THE ACTIVITY WINDOW

*"yes it shoudl state the window"*. **Ruled.** Recent activity reads a **24-hour** window
(`ACTIVITY_WINDOW_DAYS = 1`) capped at six rows, and the panel must SAY so — because
*"nothing has happened here yet"* means something very different at 24 hours than at
forever, and on a utility's first Monday the difference matters.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-013 EP-RAT-12 — THE DISCOUNT OBJECT, AND SEVEN JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT COVER

The PO's three rulings of this morning (a plan may not override a discount's value ·
a submitter may approve their own filing · the second-approval threshold is a tenant
setting defaulting to $10,000 against the discount's own budget cap) are implemented
and are recorded above. **This entry is for the seven places the signed documents ran
out and a lane had to choose** — written down before the work was reported, per law 10,
so the next agent can disagree with a decision rather than rediscover a mystery.

**The state this landed on, because it explains several of the choices.** There was no
discount object at all: `\dt *discount*` returned **0 rows**, no `Discount` model
existed in any `apps/*/models.py`, and r10 drew five discounts with nothing behind
them. Six tables now exist — `discounts`, `discount_versions`, `plan_discount_rules`,
`discount_enrolments`, `discount_enrolment_documents`, `discount_grants` — and R6 of
the resolution chain has something to read for the first time.

**1 · THE OBJECT IS SPLIT IN TWO, THE WAY A TARIFF IS.** `Discount` holds the identity
(code, bill-line name, programme owner, funding source, status); `DiscountVersion`
holds the dated, approvable content. No document says to, but CR-013's own promise —
*"any bill stays reproducible from the pricing in force for its service period"* —
is not expressible without it, and `Tariff`/`TariffVersion` is the shape the module
already uses. `discount_grants.discount_version_id` is the stamp that makes a past
reduction re-price, which is the same stamp DEF-276 found missing from
`invoice_lines.tariff_version_id`.

**2 · THE ENROLMENT POINTS AT THE DISCOUNT, NOT AT A VERSION.** Part 3 says
*"enrolments survive versioning"* and this is what that sentence costs in schema. r10's
SENIOR went v1 −10% → v2 −15% on 1 Jan 2026 and its **72 accounts** did not re-enrol;
a version FK would have ended all 72 that morning.

**3 · BUDGET CONSUMPTION IS A SUM OVER APPEND-ONLY ROWS, NEVER A COUNTER.** Part 3's
Budget-&-usage tab reports *"granted vs budget, denials by cap or funding"*, and a
decremented counter cannot say which bill spent the money — which is the question
finance is asked at filing time. `discount_grants` is append-only under hard rule 4 and
a correction is a new row with a negative amount. The enrolment's
`lifetime_subsidy_amount` IS a denormalised counter, moved in the same transaction as
the row it counts, and a test asserts it equal to `SUM(grants)` so drift goes RED.

**4 · THE BILL FLOOR DEFAULTS TO $0.00.** Part 3 asks for *"a floor so bills don't
reach zero unless allowed"* and states no default. Zero means a discount may take a
bill to exactly zero and **never below it** — a negative bill is a CREDIT, a different
object with a different ledger posting, and no discount may mint one. A positive
default would have silently under-paid every CAP recipient whose bill is under $25.
**On the PO's agenda** (review-ledger row (a)).

**5 · A SCOPED DISCOUNT TAKES ITS OWN SCOPE; ONLY `whole_bill` RUNS AGAINST THE
REDUCING SUBTOTAL.** Worked on design §A4's S1: a base-only 10% takes
18.50 + 12.00 + 8.00 = **$38.50 → $3.85**, not 10% of $189.90 = $18.99. The reason is
part 3's own — the bill shows *"the full tariff amount and the reduction as its own
line"*, so a scoped percentage is a percentage of what is printed.

**6 · PRECEDENCE MOVES THE ANSWER BY A CENT AND NOBODY HAS STATED AN ORDER.** AUTOPAY
at −0.5% run BEFORE PAPERLESS's flat −$1.00 sees $189.90 → **$0.95**; run after it
sees $188.90 → **$0.94**. Part 3 makes the order data the utility sets, so the seeder
states **10 · 20 · 30 · 40 · 50** in r10's own row order and labels it a FIXTURE, not
a rule. **On the PO's agenda.**

**7 · TWO OF PART 3's FIVE TYPES ARE STORABLE AND REFUSE AT ACTIVATION.**
`rate_override` swaps a schedule inside R2 and `usage_allowance` deducts QUANTITY
before R3b's tier walk, so neither is a subtraction at R6 at all; both are EP-RAT-15
engine work. They refuse where an operator is looking at them rather than reaching a
bill run and being silently skipped — which would be the opposite of *"subsidy granted
is reportable"*.

### ⚠ THE ONE THING r10 DRAWS THAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, BEYOND THE PLAN OVERRIDE

r10's DIS-02 step 2 draws a checkbox, **"Taxes computed on the discounted amount"**,
default ON. It is not a column on the discount. CR-013 part 4 makes discount treatment
**statutory and PER TAX** — some authorities levy on the pre-discount amount — so the
answer belongs on `taxes.discount_treatment` (EP-RAT-13, unbuilt), and one flag on the
discount would have decided it for every authority in the product. R6 therefore returns
**both** subtotals and lets R7 choose.

### THE TWO §A4 FIGURES THAT WERE UNREACHABLE AND ARE NOW REACHED

Design §A4's S1 totals **$195.60** including a **−$1.00 PAPERLESS** discount, and S2
totals **$286.55** the same way. Both were unreachable while no discount existed — a
design that stated a total nothing could produce. With PAPERLESS real they agree to the
cent: **189.90 − 1.00 = 188.90** and **280.85 − 1.00 = 279.85**, which are the taxable
bases those two totals are built on. Nothing in the design was adjusted to match the
code; the code reproduces the design.

`python3 10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` reads **33 PASS, 0 FAIL** — unchanged. B4/B5
are untouched: a discount is a new line, not a change to any frozen figure.

## 2026-08-19 · FOUR RULINGS — the compliance start date, the rate structures, the seed, and the as-of

Each was put to the PO as a table of options with a worked example and a recommendation.
All four came back as the recommended option. Recorded with what was shown.

### 1 · OQ-266 CLOSED — REPRODUCIBILITY STARTS 2026-08-19 AND IS STAMPED AS SUCH

**Shown:** an auditor points at `INV-2026-07-0042`, $91.66, issued in July, and asks which
rate priced it. We can show the bill, its lines, the plan name and version and the meter
read; **we cannot say which rate-schedule version produced $0.118/kWh**, because that fact
was never captured. Three options were tabled against a measured scale — **48 issued
invoices, $4,417.11, all July, and ZERO drafts**.

**The PO's answer: (a) — state the start date.**

**Ruled.** `BR-RAT-007` and `BR-RAT-017`, and design §A0's promise that *"every issued bill
must re-price to the identical figure, forever"*, are **stamped with a start date of
2026-08-19**. Before that date the product can produce the bill, its lines, the plan and
the read, and **not** the rate-schedule version. The repo says so rather than implying
otherwise.

**Option (b) was withdrawn BY ME before the ruling, not chosen against.** I had recommended
re-running draft invoices as a best-effort half-measure and then counted them: there are
**zero drafts**, so it was an empty gesture. Recorded because a recommendation that
survives to a decision table without being checked is the failure mode, not the fix.

**Option (c) — "reproducible by inspection" — was rejected as a claim nobody can test.** The
versions do still sit in `tariff_versions` and a human could attempt the derivation, but
two people can reach different answers and neither can be shown wrong. That is precisely
what DEF-276 exists to prevent, so asserting it as a compliance position would reintroduce
the defect at the level of the claim.

### 2 · DEF-297 — `base_only` IS REGISTERED, AND `capacity` AND `percent` ARE DOCUMENTED

**Shown:** the two lists disagree **in both directions**, which the first report of this
defect understated as "five of six built":

| Structure | CR-013 part 1 names it | Registered in `TARIFF_MODELS` |
|---|---|---|
| Flat · Tiered · TOU · Seasonal · Demand+energy | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Base only** | ✅ | ❌ **missing** |
| **Capacity** | ❌ | ✅ |
| **Percent** | ❌ | ✅ |

**The worked example:** r10 draws **Vacant / Standby — *"Base only, no usage"*, $15.00/mo,
35 accounts**. Today that can only be modelled as **flat at a rate of zero**, which prices
correctly and READS WRONGLY — the schedule claims a usage rate that does not exist, and
nothing stops a later editor typing a non-zero figure into it.

**The PO's answer: (a).**

**Ruled.** `base_only` is registered as a rate structure. **`capacity` and `percent` are
documented into part 1** rather than left as undocumented production behaviour — `percent`
is how r10 prices *Industrial Sewer · % of water*, so it has an implementation and a
drawing and lacked only a spec. Both lists then describe the same product.

### 3 · DEF-298 — THE PERIOD FILTER **AND** THE SEED, NOT EITHER ALONE

**The PO's answer: (b) — filter and seed the current month too.**

**Ruled.** CR-015's period filter fixes every real tenant, whose dashboard would otherwise
be near-empty for the first week of every month forever. **AND** the seed carries
current-month data, so the demo shows a populated dashboard on day one. Option (c) — seed
only — was **my original wrong answer**, and it is recorded as rejected: it would have made
the demo look right while leaving the product flaw in place for every real customer.

### 4 · DEF-299 — `as_of` IS TODAY, CLAMPED INTO THE PERIOD

**Shown:** today is **2026-08-19**; the dashboard reports **`as_of 2026-08-31`**, eleven
days in the future.

**The PO's answer: (a).**

**Ruled.** `as_of` is **the moment the figures were read, clamped into the selected
period** — so mid-month it is today, and once a period closes it is the period end. Two
consequences, both of which are why this lands BEFORE CR-015's filter:

* The PO's consistency rule — *"a KPI must agree with its owning module for the same as-of
  moment"* — is **uncheckable** while the dashboard says the 31st and Finance says the
  19th. The figures can be identical and still not reconcilable by a person comparing
  labels.
* The **server-side cache authorised on 2026-08-19** states cache age against `as_of`.
  Computed from a future timestamp it is meaningless, so the cache cannot be built on the
  current behaviour.

Option (c), the timestamp of the newest data, was rejected: on this fixture it would read
*as of Jul 31*, which is truthful about the data and reads as though the dashboard itself
were a month stale.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-016 · What may be said to a utility user, and where provenance goes instead

**The PO's report, verbatim:** *"you should follow screen that is given - you are adding
your own content and details on screen/Ui - too much problem"*, with five screenshots of
the deployed build, and *"you ahve to look at all screen in settings now each and every
screen"*.

Thirteen Settings surfaces were walked in a browser and **52 strings of engineering
commentary were rendered to a utility user**; across the whole product the count is
**219**. Four judgements were needed to fix them, and none of them was in the repo.

### 1 · THE RULE — "KEEP THE HONESTY, DROP THE PROVENANCE"

The tension is real and had never been written down. Hard-won law 1 says an absence must
be **stated rather than implied**, and most of these 52 strings existed *because of that
law* — they were honest. But they were honest **in our vocabulary**, and the PO is right
that a two-person utility can do nothing with `BR-NOT-013`.

**Ruled:** law 1 is about **the repo being honest**, not about telling a customer which
BR-code is unimplemented. So a user-facing string keeps the CLAIM and drops the
PROVENANCE, and the provenance moves to the **code comment beside the string**.

**The worked example put to this decision, and the one to reuse:**

| Was on screen | Is on screen now |
|---|---|
| *"no SMTP adapter is built and no message leaves the building on any email path (BR-NOT-013). This card decides WHAT WOULD BE USED when one lands — the PO's own framing: 'we just need to plug it; rest of the infra will work'"* | *"Email sending is not switched on yet, so no email leaves the building. Filling this in now means email works the moment it is switched on."* |

Same claim, same honesty, nothing about us. **Not one absence stopped being stated.**

### 2 · WHERE A REFERENCE GOES WHEN IT IS STILL WANTED — `data-` ATTRIBUTES

The original argument for printing a rule id was sound and is recorded in `RunGap`'s own
docstring: *"so a reader can go and check that the screen is waiting for the right thing
rather than taking the sentence on trust."* Deleting the reference would lose that.

**Ruled:** the reference stays **on the element**, as `data-rule-ref` / `data-br-ref` /
`data-blocked-by`. Support and engineers read it off the DOM in one click; the clerk
reading the panel never sees it. Applied to `RunGap` (13 sites), `GapNotes` (every gap
bullet in billing) and the two no-trigger notices on Settings → Notifications.

### 3 · A RULE ID IS NOT TRANSLATABLE TEXT

The eleven `billing.run.*.gapRule` entries lived in **all eleven locale files and were
translated** — eleven renderings of *"Rule BR-BIL-015 · column bill_run_decisions.case"*,
which G15 was keeping in parity for nothing.

**Ruled:** a value no human reads and no translator can improve is **not catalogue
material**. They are constants beside the component now (`RUN_GAP_RULES`), and the twelve
dead keys were removed from all eleven catalogues.

### 4 · A MACHINE FIELD MAY KEEP ITS ID — THE FIX IS TO STOP RENDERING IT

`br_ref` on `TEMPLATES_UNAVAILABLE` is **supposed** to hold `"BR-BIL-026 · OQ-149"`.

**Ruled:** G28 checks `detail` on that module and deliberately **does not check
`br_ref`**. A gate demanding that field contain no rule id would be asking it to stop
being itself. The defect was that `GapNotes` printed it in `<b>`, and that is what changed.

### 5 · A TEST THAT ASSERTS INTERNAL COPY MAKES IT A REQUIREMENT

`test_cr_009_c12_sender_config` asserted `"no SMTP adapter is built" in
read.data["no_send_reason"]`. The internal sentence was not merely unchecked — **a test
written beside it protected it**. Three tests were **inverted rather than deleted**, so
each now asserts the customer copy AND that our vocabulary has not come back.

### What enforces all of this

**G28** (`10-scripts/gates/g28_internal_references.py`), registered in `run_gates.py`:
**proved RED at 219 violations against the tip that carried them, green at 0** after the
sweep, with an empty baseline. And **G27 was found never to have been registered in
`run_gates.py` at all** — written that morning, proved both ways, and called by no runner:
hard-won law 2, committed by the lane that was fixing a law-2 defect. Both are wired now.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-015 BUILT — the dashboard's window is chosen, stated, and no longer a day in the future

DEF-299 first, then the filter, in the ruled order. Recorded with the worked
figures, because the two judgments below are the lane's and not the PO's.

### 1 · DEF-299 IS FIXED, AND WHAT IT COST WAS ITS MEANING, NOT ITS VALUE

**Reproduced on the live booted stack before anything was written**, signed in
against the Brazos Bend fixture on 2026-08-19:

```
as_of 2026-08-31 period {'start': '2026-08-01', 'end': '2026-08-31'}
today 2026-08-19
```

Eleven days in the future, on the first screen after every sign-in. **Every check
in this repo was green over it**, and that is the instructive part: the value was
CARRIED correctly by all six regions and nothing disagreed with anything else. No
test asserted the relationship between `as_of` and the clock, because until the
PO's consistency rule existed there was nothing for that relationship to violate.

`as_of` is now **the read moment clamped into the selected period** (the PO's
option (a), BR-REP-036). The same tenant now serves:

| Window selected | `period` | `as_of` | `read_on` | Revenue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| last cycle (default) | 2026-08-12 → 2026-08-19 | **2026-08-19** | 2026-08-19 | 0.00 |
| this period | 2026-08-01 → 2026-08-31 | **2026-08-19** | 2026-08-19 | 0.00 |
| last period | 2026-07-01 → 2026-07-31 | **2026-07-31** | 2026-08-19 | **4,648.22** |
| last 30 days | 2026-07-21 → 2026-08-19 | **2026-08-19** | 2026-08-19 | 289.40 |

Mid-period it is today; once the period closes it is the period end. Both were
proved, and so was the CLAMP'S LOWER END, which no option exercises today — a
half-clamp reads correctly for a year and then does not.

⚠ **BR-TEN-043 SURVIVED THE FIX AND THAT WAS THE ONLY HARD PART.** The obvious
repair was to read a clock inside `dashboard_summary`; the value would then have
been right on every screen and the read model would have become untestable
against a signed figure. Instead the tenant's own today is read ONCE, at the
boundary, through a new `tenant_today` seam, and **only when the caller passed no
`as_of`** — which is precisely when `current_period()` already read the same
clock internally. A test BREAKS that seam and asserts a caller who passed `as_of`
still gets a complete answer.

⚠ **A SECOND DATE IS PUBLISHED, `read_on`, and it is not decoration.** The page
BODY is as of `as_of`; the page HEADER's date line and its cycle countdown are as
of `read_on`. With a closed window selected, the header fed `as_of` would say
*"Friday · Jul 31"* over today's screen and count a cycle down from a date in the
past — *"closes in −11 days"*.

### 2 · THE DEFAULT IS THE LAST COMPLETED CYCLE — AND WHAT "COMPLETED" MEANS IS THIS LANE'S JUDGMENT, NOT A SIGNED RULE

The PO ruled the DEFAULT (BR-REP-035). Nothing signed says what makes a cycle
completed or where its window ends, and SET-07 publishes three candidate dates —
`window_start`, `window_end` and `bill_date`. **Derived, and put here so the next
lane does not re-derive it differently:**

> **complete ⇔ `bill_date` is on or before the read moment · window ⇔
> `window_start` … `bill_date`.**

**The worked case that decided it, from the fixture's own cycles.** Cycle **08-B**
reads **12–16 Aug** and **bills on the 19th**. Using `window_end` the window would
be 12–16 Aug — which reports on the cycle's READS while excluding the cycle's own
REVENUE, because a bill books on its bill date. That is the identical dead screen
this change exists to remove, one week narrower. The window a person means by
*"the last cycle"* is the span containing what the cycle billed.

Draft and inactive cycles are never the window (BR-MET-076: a draft stamps no
service point), and a cycle with no `bill_date` is SKIPPED rather than given a
default — the same posture `cycle_status_data` already takes for a cycle with no
`read_day_to`. Ties break by account count then code, which is the tie-break the
PO already ruled for the status line.

**This is flagged as unsigned in BR-REP-035's own row and returns to the agenda.**

### 3 · `fiscal_period_not_configured` NOW WITHDRAWS TWO OPTIONS INSTEAD OF EVERY FIGURE — a signed rule's APPLICATION moved, and the rule did not

BR-TEN-022's reasoning was quoted in three places: *"a KPI headed 'this period'
that is not the tenant's period is a wrong number wearing a right label."* That
is still exactly right. CR-015 removes its PREMISE: the screen now STATES the
window it is reporting over, in dates, so it is no longer headed *"this period"*
over something that is not one.

So a tenant with no fiscal calendar loses the two ACCOUNTING options — named,
with the reason on the wire — and keeps its figures over the cycle and rolling
windows. **The inverted assertion is the one that matters**: an existing test
named `..._means_no_figure_at_all` asserted a page of nulls for exactly that
tenant. It is renamed, inverted and kept, because a brand-new tenant meeting a
blank dashboard on its first sign-in is the state this removes. BR-TEN-022 itself
is untouched — every accounting window on the menu is still COMPUTED and never
stored.

### 4 · THE SERVER-SIDE CACHE IS STILL NOT BUILT, AND ITS PRECONDITION IS NOW CLOSED

CR-012 reported it not-done. DEF-299 was one of two reasons — a cache states its
age against `as_of`, which was meaningless computed from a date that had not
happened. **That reason is now closed.** The other one is not, and it is
infrastructure rather than dashboard: this deployment configures **no `CACHES`
setting at all**, so Django falls back to a per-process `LocMemCache`, and
`docker-compose.yml` states in its own header that there is deliberately **"No
Redis, no Celery worker"**. A per-worker cache would give two clerks two
different cache ages for the same figures, which is the PO's condition failing in
the one way it was written to prevent. Reported not-done, with the reason, rather
than half-built.

**What WAS built is the PO's condition applied to the cache that actually
exists.** The five-minute client `staleTime` ruled on 2026-08-19 is real caching —
a clerk returning to this screen can be shown figures read five minutes ago while
Finance recomputes on arrival — and nothing said so. The period bar now states
the age of the figures on screen (*"Read 4 minutes ago"*), measured from
react-query's own `dataUpdatedAt` rather than asserted, and says nothing at all
under a minute because *"0 minutes ago"* reads as a fault where silence reads as
the truth.

⚠ **AND THE CACHE KEY NOW CARRIES THE PERIOD.** With a constant key the
five-minute window would serve the PREVIOUS window's figures under the NEW
window's heading for up to five minutes — the exact *"dashboard disagrees with
Finance"* failure the on-screen statement exists to prevent, produced by the
caching that was meant to be harmless.

### 5 · THE OUTAGE THAT ALMOST SHIPPED, FOUND BY AN EXISTING TEST

The first version of the period vocabulary called `seams.cycles_list()` bare, in
the page body. `test_cr012_tc15` went red with `RuntimeError: cycles_list is on
fire` — a metering outage blanking the whole landing screen, which is precisely
the guarantee CR-012 built (BR-REP-028). The read is memoised and quieted now: a
failing metering seam costs the `last_cycle` option and the cycle-status region,
and the page keeps its money. **CR-012's own test found it; nothing this lane
wrote would have.**

### 6 · DEF-298's SEED HALF IS NOT BUILT, AND IS REPORTED RATHER THAN REACHED

The PO ruled option (b): the filter **and** the seed carries current-month data.
The filter half is built. The seed half is not, and the reason is a real
constraint rather than a preference: the e2e fixture pins its dates on purpose —
`ISSUED_AT = datetime(2026, 7, 1, …)`, *"so a re-boot on a different day writes
the identical bill"* — and that bill is read BY NAME by `W3-money-render.spec.ts`
(GT-1, B5 ❄️ FROZEN). Moving it would move a golden fixture; adding a second
current-month bill run belongs to the billing/QA fixture lane and would change
row counts several specs assert. Left to that lane with this note.

## 2026-08-19 · SCREEN IDS — THE VISIBLE TAG IS r10's MODULE ID; THE S-SERIES STAYS INTERNAL

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"Keep S series for your reference for User and Product
manager reference assign tags that are visible on screen those should be as per modules
how we are using in r10"*.

**What was shown before the ruling.** The PO asked *"How are you generating Screen IDs?"*
and the answer is that they are not generated — they are looked up. That surfaced two
vocabularies that do not reconcile, and the table put to them was:

| | Vocabulary | Where it lives | Who speaks it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A1** | `S1`…`S114`, **83 allocated**, 31 numbers unused inside the range | `04-docs/01-spec/01-screen-inventory.md` | every defect row · every story · every ticket · `g25_screen_coverage.py` |
| **r10** | **92 ids across 16 module prefixes**, `PREFIX-NN` with dotted sub-ids | `05-prototype/r10-2026-08-16/SMARTBillHub.dc.html`, badge bottom-right | **the PO**, on every prototype screenshot |

Also shown: **A1's numbering is sequential ON ARRIVAL, not by module.** S14–S24 look like
a coherent accounts block only because those screens were specified together; after the
first pass it is pure append — Assets at S49, reference data at S63 and S75, templates at
S91, the signup rework renumbered into S110–S114. **The number tells you WHEN a screen was
added, never WHAT it belongs to.** That is the whole reason r10's scheme reads better to a
human, and it is why the PO ruled as they did.

**RULED, and it REVERSES my recommendation.** I had recommended showing the A1 id as
primary with r10's appended (`S7 · DSH-01`). The PO ruled the visible tag is **r10's module
id alone**. Recorded because a superseded recommendation that is not written down gets
re-proposed by the next agent.

**The vocabulary, extracted from r10 rather than invented:** 16 prefixes — `ACC` accounts ·
`AST` assets · `BIL` billing · `CHG` charge codes · `DSH` dashboard · `FIN` finance · `ONB`
onboarding · `PAY` payments · `PLN` plans · `PRM` premises · `RAT` rate schedules · `RDS`
reads · `RPT` reports · `SET` settings · `WFL` workflows · `WRK` work. Form `PREFIX-NN`,
dotted sub-id for a tab or wizard step (`PLN-01.charges`).

**What the ruling does NOT do — three things, so nobody reads it wider than it is:**
1. **The S-series is not retired.** It stops being RENDERED. It remains what a defect row,
   a story and the screen-coverage gate resolve, so the mapping keeps both
   (`{ route, r10, a1 }`); only the render narrows.
2. **It is not permission to mint ids.** Where a screen has no r10 id, that is a finding —
   CLAUDE.md law 8, *"every screen needs a story"*. Neither file is renumbered; the mapping
   is a third artefact beside the router.
3. **`WFL` and `WRK` are prefixes r10 draws for surfaces this product has not built.** Work
   and Workflows remain out of scope under OQ-249. A route mapping there is a bug to
   report, not a screen to create.

**"For the time being"** is the PO's own framing: the tag is a diagnostic affordance and
must be removable by ONE switch, not by editing a hundred components.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-016 design-system slice — the app made to look like r10, and the four judgments that took

**Lane:** the CR-016 r10-conformance remediation (the design-system half; the content half
— internal prose out of the catalogues — is a separate lane and shipped as 2.24.0).
**Evidence:** `07-frontend/e2e/CR-016-ui-conformance.spec.ts` run against the live stack at
`http://127.0.0.1:8080` with `npm run build` first, before and after. Register:
`07-frontend/e2e/ui-conformance-baseline.json`.

### What moved, measured in computed style on 24 screens

| Register entry | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `nonConformingKickers` | **10** on 6 screens | **0** |
| `distinctTableFontSizes` | **6** — 10 / 11 / 12 / 13 / 13.5 / 14px | body **1** (`13.5px`), header **1** (`12px`) |
| `distinctButtonFontSizes` | **5** — 12 / 13 / 13.3333 / 14 / 15px | **2** — `12px` + `14px` |
| `distinctControlHeights` | **4** — 27 / 33 / 36 / 38px | **1** — `36` |
| `screensWithMoreThanOneTableSize` | **10** | **0** |
| `nativeSelects` | 26 | **0** |
| `foreignControls` | 3 | **0** |
| CSS custom properties used and never declared | **15**, 11 of them with no fallback | **0** |

⚠ **`nativeSelects` and `foreignControls` were ALREADY 0 before this slice started** and the
register still said 26 and 3 — `cf0423f` fixed them and did not lower the register, which is
the exact failure the register's own README calls red. Corrected here, and worth naming: the
first thing this lane did was re-run the gate rather than trust the recorded numbers, and that
is the only reason the discrepancy was seen.

### DECISION 1 · Of r10's 51 component classes, 36 are declared by no app stylesheet — and only TWO are defects

A census of every `className=` literal in `07-frontend/src` (parsed, not grepped: every
`className="…"` and every string literal inside `className={…}`) against every selector in
`05-prototype/r10-2026-08-16/styles.css`:

| Verdict | Count | Which, and why |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) Needed and missing — DECLARED** | **2** | `.kicker` (63 uses / 26 files, the shared `PageHeader` among them; r10 declares it in the dc.html's own `<style>`, not in styles.css) and `.table` (8 uses / 3 wizard summary tables). Both now in `07-frontend/src/styles/global.css`, the one sheet `main.tsx` imports. |
| **(b) Superseded by an app class — MAPPED, left alone** | **19** | `.dialog`/`.dialog-backdrop`/`.dialog-title`/`.dialog-body`/`.dialog-actions` → `.modal-card`/`.modal-overlay`/`.modal-title`/`.modal-body`/`.modal-foot` (FormModal.css) · `.fbar`/`.fchip`/`.x` → `.filter-bar`/`.filter-chip`/`.filter-chip-remove` (FilterBar.css) · `.pgbar`/`.pgnav`/`.pgsize` → `.table-pager`/`.table-pager-range`/`.table-pager-size` (DataTable.css) · `.lt` → `.data-table` + `.table-sort` · `.empty` → `.state-frame` (StateFrame.css, A18 §1) · `.tag`/`.tag-accent`/`.tag-accent-2`/`.tag-neutral`/`.tag-outline` → `.status-pill` + `.pill` (StatusPill.css / StateFrame.css) · `.req` → `.field-required` (FormModal.css, BR-SHL-017) · `.nav`/`.nav-brand` → the app shell's `.sidebar` / `.sidebar .brand` (r10's own dc.html uses the same, so `.nav` is the public-page nav this product does not have) · `.sel-search` → `.search-select` (FormModal.css, the ARIA combobox). |
| **(c) Not used by this product — NOT A DEFECT** | **15** | `.card-kicker`, `.card-title`, `.card-body`, `.card-meta` (the app's `.card` carries no sub-parts; panels use `.panel h3` shapes) · `.elev-sm`/`.elev-md`/`.elev-lg` (shadows are applied through `--shadow-*` directly) · `.btn-block`, `.btn-icon-sm`, `.date-input`, `.grayscale`, `.hr`, `.text-muted`, `.pgsize`'s sibling `.pgbar select.input`, `.seg`'s r10-only variants. Zero `className` references, product-wide. |

**Ruled: a class nothing references is not a defect.** The audit's headline "36 classes
declared nowhere" is true and 34 of the 36 are correct as they stand. Recording the mapping
here is the point — otherwise the next audit re-opens all 36 and re-derives this table.

### DECISION 2 · THE TABLE HEADER TIER IS 12px, NOT r10's 11px — and rule 5 is why

r10's `.table th` is `font-size:11px`. We ship **12px**. This is a deliberate divergence and
the worked figure is the whole argument:

* r10 makes the entire `<th>` the sort target — `.lt thead th{cursor:pointer;user-select:none}`
  — and contains **no button**.
* Our shared `DataTable` puts a real `<button class="table-sort">` inside every sortable
  header, because a click target that is not a button is unreachable from a keyboard. It
  takes the header's font-size (`font: inherit`), and it must: a column that cannot be sorted
  has bare `<th>` text beside it, and two sizes in one header row is worse than either.
* **B14 rule 5 is ratified law — "Two button sizes only — default and small (12px)."**
  Measured in a browser across 24 screens: header at **11px ⇒ 3 button sizes** (11 / 12 / 14);
  header at **12px ⇒ 2** (12 / 14).

**Ruled: 12px.** It is rule 5's own small tier, so the sort control and the label around it
are one size, and no ratified rule is broken. r10's other header values — uppercase, 0.08em
tracking (the app had 0.04em and 0.06em in five files), the 2px bottom rule — are ported
exactly. Raised to the PO as **OQ-267**: make the `<th>` itself the sort target and go back to
11px, or keep the 1px.

**Two smaller divergences from r10 fall out of the same rule and are recorded with it:**
`.settings-tabs button` 13px → **14px** (fourteen real `<button>`s on every Settings screen)
and `.seg-opt` 13px → **12px** (every segment is a `<button>` here; r10 uses a label + hidden
input and has no button to count). Both are r10 values that predate B14 rule 5; rule 5 is the
ratified law and wins.

### DECISION 3 · THE GATE'S TABLE METRIC WAS UNSATISFIABLE BY r10 ITSELF, AND WOULD HAVE GONE UP AS THE PRODUCT WAS FIXED

`CR-016-ui-conformance.spec.ts` pooled `table td, table th` into ONE set and recorded
`distinctTableFontSizes` and `screensWithMoreThanOneTableSize` against it. **r10 fails that
metric**: `.table` is 13.5px and `.table th` is 11px in the same block, so the pooled count
can only reach 1 by deleting the header tier the design system requires. Worse,
`screensWithMoreThanOneTableSize` counted a screen as broken for **having a header at all** —
it stood at 10 only because ten screens' headers and bodies differed, and separating header
from body product-wide would have driven it to **18**. A register that reports a regression
when the product is fixed is not a register.

**Ruled: measure per role.** `distinctTableBodyFontSizes` and `distinctTableHeaderFontSizes`,
split on `thead` — a `<th>` in a body row is a ROW header ("0–30 days" beside its figures) and
a `<tfoot>` `<th>` is a total, and both must match the `<td>`s on their own line. This is a
FINER check, not a weaker one: DEF-310's stated closure — *"the set becomes ['13.5px']"* — is
now literally the body half's target and it is met, and the header tier gets a register it
never had. **Proved RED first** (hard-won law 7) by editing the BUILT bundle rather than the
shared source — `.kicker`'s rule deleted and `.data-table`'s `font-size` pushed back to 14px —
which reported `nonConformingKickers: 8` and `distinctTableBodyFontSizes: ["13.5px","14px"]`,
then restored by rebuilding.

### DECISION 4 · THE 15 UNDECLARED CUSTOM PROPERTIES — WHAT EACH ONE BECOMES

11 had no fallback, so the whole declaration was invalid at computed-value time and did
nothing at all; 4 shipped a fallback that looks deliberate and is not the design system.

| Invented name | Uses | Becomes | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--space-5` | 5, all dead | `var(--space-6)` | r10's scale is 1/2/3/4/6/8 — there is no step 5. Five margins/paddings were simply not applied. 24px is the next declared step. |
| `--color-primary-700` | 2, dead | `var(--color-accent-700)` | The ramp is `--color-accent-*`. Two download links rendered in ordinary ink. |
| `--color-border` | 1, dead | `var(--color-divider)` | A retention-run separator that never drew. |
| `--font-size-sm` / `--font-size-xs` / `--text-body-sm` | 3, dead | `13px` / `11px` / `13px` | No such scale exists; the app's type scale is `--text-h1..h6` + `--text-body`. Named literally rather than inventing three more tokens. |
| `--ink-muted` | 6, all with `#666` | `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-text) 55%, transparent)` | The worst kind: it SHIPPED, and `#666` is not the design system's muted ink — in files whose own headers say "no hex literals here". |
| `--accent` | 1, with `#ec3013` | `var(--color-accent)` | Same value, wrong name. |
| `--color-danger` (×2) / `--color-warning` | 3, with `#b3261e` / `#b26a00` | `--color-danger-700` / `--color-warning-700` | Material-palette hexes that are not any step of our ramps. |
| `--color-danger-900` | 1, fallback to `-700` | `var(--color-danger-700)` | The fallback was the whole rule. |
| `--font-mono` | 2, fallback `monospace` | `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace` | Ditto. |
| `--settings-swatch`, `--settings-brand-primary`, `--settings-brand-accent` | 3 | **left alone — NOT a defect** | Declared at RUNTIME on the element's own `style` attribute (`SettingsCompanyTab.tsx`), because the value is a tenant's brand hex from the database. A static scan cannot tell these from the inventions above; a comment beside each read now says so. |

### What this did NOT do, stated rather than implied

* **The six defect rows (DEF-308 … DEF-313) still read `status: open`.**
  `10-scripts/file_defect.py` appends and deliberately refuses to edit an existing row, and
  the register is a 310-row CRLF file that six lanes write; closing six single fields in it is
  a separate, riskier operation. Their evidence is here and in the register JSON.
* **`inlineWrappingLabels: 0` is still a floor, not a clean bill.** The walk opens no modal,
  wizard or panel, so the label in the PO's second screenshot is not in scope of this number
  and the baseline's own README says so.
* **B14 rules 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9–17 and 19 remain RATIFIED AND UNENFORCED.** This slice closes
  rules 2, 5, 8 and 20 in the paint; the rest still have no gate reading rendered output.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-015 BUILT — the dashboard's window is chosen, stated, and no longer a day in the future

DEF-299 first, then the filter, in the ruled order. Recorded with the worked
figures, because the two judgments below are the lane's and not the PO's.

### 1 · DEF-299 IS FIXED, AND WHAT IT COST WAS ITS MEANING, NOT ITS VALUE

**Reproduced on the live booted stack before anything was written**, signed in
against the Brazos Bend fixture on 2026-08-19:

```
as_of 2026-08-31 period {'start': '2026-08-01', 'end': '2026-08-31'}
today 2026-08-19
```

Eleven days in the future, on the first screen after every sign-in. **Every check
in this repo was green over it**, and that is the instructive part: the value was
CARRIED correctly by all six regions and nothing disagreed with anything else. No
test asserted the relationship between `as_of` and the clock, because until the
PO's consistency rule existed there was nothing for that relationship to violate.

`as_of` is now **the read moment clamped into the selected period** (the PO's
option (a), BR-REP-036). The same tenant now serves:

| Window selected | `period` | `as_of` | `read_on` | Revenue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| last cycle (default) | 2026-08-12 → 2026-08-19 | **2026-08-19** | 2026-08-19 | 0.00 |
| this period | 2026-08-01 → 2026-08-31 | **2026-08-19** | 2026-08-19 | 0.00 |
| last period | 2026-07-01 → 2026-07-31 | **2026-07-31** | 2026-08-19 | **4,648.22** |
| last 30 days | 2026-07-21 → 2026-08-19 | **2026-08-19** | 2026-08-19 | 289.40 |

Mid-period it is today; once the period closes it is the period end. Both were
proved, and so was the CLAMP'S LOWER END, which no option exercises today — a
half-clamp reads correctly for a year and then does not.

⚠ **BR-TEN-043 SURVIVED THE FIX AND THAT WAS THE ONLY HARD PART.** The obvious
repair was to read a clock inside `dashboard_summary`; the value would then have
been right on every screen and the read model would have become untestable
against a signed figure. Instead the tenant's own today is read ONCE, at the
boundary, through a new `tenant_today` seam, and **only when the caller passed no
`as_of`** — which is precisely when `current_period()` already read the same
clock internally. A test BREAKS that seam and asserts a caller who passed `as_of`
still gets a complete answer.

⚠ **A SECOND DATE IS PUBLISHED, `read_on`, and it is not decoration.** The page
BODY is as of `as_of`; the page HEADER's date line and its cycle countdown are as
of `read_on`. With a closed window selected, the header fed `as_of` would say
*"Friday · Jul 31"* over today's screen and count a cycle down from a date in the
past — *"closes in −11 days"*.

### 2 · THE DEFAULT IS THE LAST COMPLETED CYCLE — AND WHAT "COMPLETED" MEANS IS THIS LANE'S JUDGMENT, NOT A SIGNED RULE

The PO ruled the DEFAULT (BR-REP-035). Nothing signed says what makes a cycle
completed or where its window ends, and SET-07 publishes three candidate dates —
`window_start`, `window_end` and `bill_date`. **Derived, and put here so the next
lane does not re-derive it differently:**

> **complete ⇔ `bill_date` is on or before the read moment · window ⇔
> `window_start` … `bill_date`.**

**The worked case that decided it, from the fixture's own cycles.** Cycle **08-B**
reads **12–16 Aug** and **bills on the 19th**. Using `window_end` the window would
be 12–16 Aug — which reports on the cycle's READS while excluding the cycle's own
REVENUE, because a bill books on its bill date. That is the identical dead screen
this change exists to remove, one week narrower. The window a person means by
*"the last cycle"* is the span containing what the cycle billed.

Draft and inactive cycles are never the window (BR-MET-076: a draft stamps no
service point), and a cycle with no `bill_date` is SKIPPED rather than given a
default — the same posture `cycle_status_data` already takes for a cycle with no
`read_day_to`. Ties break by account count then code, which is the tie-break the
PO already ruled for the status line.

**This is flagged as unsigned in BR-REP-035's own row and returns to the agenda.**

BR-TEN-022's reasoning was quoted in three places: *"a KPI headed 'this period'

is still exactly right. CR-015 removes its PREMISE: the screen now STATES the

## 2026-08-19 · ASYNC JOBS: REDIS AND CELERY ARE INSTALLED, AND THE PLANT IS TRIGGERED AFTER TENANT CREATION

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"We want Async job install redis and celery; Trigger
after tenant creation; also add these two services in docker compose"*.

**This SUPERSEDES the standing "no broker" constraint.** Until this ruling,
`docker-compose.yml` said in its own header — *"No Redis, no Celery worker, no beat.
Jobs run EAGERLY, in-process, at dispatch (JOBS_EAGER=true)"* — and every lane was
told not to invent an infrastructure dependency. That instruction is withdrawn as of
this ruling. Redis and Celery are now a **deliberate, ruled dependency**, not an
invention, and both get a service in `docker-compose.yml`.

**It also rejects the cron option I recommended.** I put three things to the PO and
recommended cron first for correctness, then a trigger for speed. The PO took the
trigger and replaced cron with a real broker. Recording the rejected option matters
because the next agent will otherwise re-derive it: **cron is not the answer here**,
and the reason the PO's answer is better is that a broker fixes latency AND
robustness at once, where cron traded 60 seconds of latency for robustness.

### What was shown to the PO before the ruling, in plain English with figures

| Stated | Figure |
|---|---|
| Four job kinds enqueue and production dispatches **none** of them | tenancy sample plant · **bulk rate change** · audit log export · audit feed export |
| The rate change answers the caller with a **202 and a job id** and never applies | `apply_rate_change_batch` writes the new tariff version and the `rate_change_log` rows and never runs — staff change prices, the product agrees, the prices do not change (DEF-326, critical) |
| Provisioning measured end to end | **78 s** |
| …of which one read-only lookup called 304 times | **47.3 s, 40% of the request** (DEF-324) |
| Provisioning after that lookup is fixed | **~31 s** |
| Cron latency, had cron been chosen | up to 60 s before start, so a new utility waits ~90 s |

### What this makes true, and what it does NOT change

1. **`JOBS_EAGER` stays the switch, and production keeps it `False`.** The setting
   was never wrong; what was missing was anything to consume the queue. Local and
   test stay eager, so no test changes shape.
2. **`core.jobs` needs no redesign.** `enqueue` → `_dispatcher` → `run_pending` →
   `run_job` is already the contract, `set_job_dispatcher` is already the seam, and
   the record already carries `status`, `progress {done,total}` and a `checkpoint`
   for resume. Celery replaces the *transport* and nothing above it.
3. **"Trigger after tenant creation" is dispatch-after-commit, not a second call
   site.** `provision_tenant` already enqueues the plant AFTER its transaction
   (BR-TEN-063 — the plant's failure must never roll back a tenant). The trigger is
   that same enqueue, now reaching a worker that exists.
4. **The CR-017 progress screen does not change.** It polls a real BE-07 job record;
   whether the body runs in a thread or a Celery worker is invisible to it.
5. **`CELERY_BROKER_URL` already exists** in `config/settings/base.py` and defaults
   to `redis://localhost:6379/0` — a default that, per `09-infra/01-deployment-
   architecture.md` §4.1, "points at localhost and will silently not work". It must
   be set explicitly per environment, and per hard-won law 3 the unsafe option is the
   one you type.
6. ⚠ **Editing `docker-compose.yml` and `.env.example` does NOT reach the deployed
   host** (hard-won law 4). The running deployment needs its own broker URL and its
   own worker process; saying so is part of shipping this, every time.

### ~~The one thing NOT ruled, and therefore not chosen~~ — **SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19** (PO: *"we need Beat ; include it"* → beat IS deployed; see the beat ruling at the end of this log)

**Whether Celery *beat* is deployed too.** `09-infra` lists beat as DECIDED for
partition archival, report retention and dispatcher pacing, and says it must run
exactly once. The PO named "redis and celery" and two compose services. Beat is a
THIRD process with a singleton constraint, so it is **not** being added by
inference — raised, not resolved.
