## 2026-08-19 — CR-017 · the signup wait names the work (build 2.26.0)

**PO, verbatim, twice:**

> *"after this step at the time of new tenant creation you need new screen
> showcaing data migration is going on so that User wil know whats going on in
> the background - add new screen after this"*

> *"We want to display confirmation to user process is taking place in the
> background and data seeding is in progress, that you for wating your Utility
> will be provision soon; that will help business user to udnerstand what we
> are doing - otherwise they are left hi and dry"*

### 1 · THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE SHAPE, AND THE ONE THAT UNDID IT

`POST /api/tenants` was timed at **78.35 s** against the live local stack. The
first reading of that was *"provisioning is synchronous and slow, so make it
async"*. **Profiling said otherwise, and the profile is the decision here:**

| Phase | Time | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `_provision_inside_context` — the whole atomic transaction | **1.5 s** | tenant, owner, session, trial, 20 reference lists, chart of accounts, number series, holidays, both template catalogues, security + read-validation rows |
| the CR-010 sample-data plant, run **eagerly inside the request** | **76 s** | 50 premises, 68 meters, 1,674 reads, 48 invoices, 246 lines, 45 payments, 93 journal entries |

**The transaction is not slow. The sample plant is, and it is already a BE-07
job with a real poll endpoint** — it runs in the request only because
`JOBS_EAGER` defaults to True outside production and `dispatch_job` then calls
`run_eager`. So there was nothing to make asynchronous: the async path exists,
and the deployment decides whether it is taken. **That is DEF-320 and it is now
OQ-270's ruling to make** — this lane measured the three options and chose none,
because a half-built async path is worse than an honest synchronous one.

### 2 · WHAT WAS ACTUALLY SLOW — 47 of the 78 seconds were one read (DEF-324)

`apps.metering.seams.enabled_service_codes()` answered *"which services does
this tenant sell"* by building `services_overview()` — the **S8 screen payload**:
ten catalog rows, four `select_related` FKs each, plus a rating seam and a
customers seam per row. **~150 queries and ~155 ms, and provisioning called it
304 times: 47.3 s, 40% of the request.** `apps.tenancy.selectors.
enabled_service_codes()` has answered the same question with one indexed query
since 2026-08-11, published for the ledger. The seam now resolves that, and the
selector gained `service__active=True` so the two definitions cannot disagree.

**Measured, not asserted:** live `POST /api/tenants` over HTTP went **71.3 s →
44.6 s** on the same stack with nothing else changed. The remaining ~41 s is
genuine seeding work with no single dominant hotspot left.

### 3 · JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT

Each of these was a choice, and none was ruled by anybody, so each is written
down with its reason rather than reported as done.

**(a) It is NOT a new screen id.** CLAUDE.md: *"where a screen has no A1 id,
that is a finding to report, not a licence to mint one"*. It is built as S114's
post-commit STATE — no route, no inventory row. **OQ-269** asks the PO whether
one should be allocated, and notes that CR-016's live screen-id tag already
labels this surface **ONB-04.5** in the running app, which is an id A1 does not
carry.

**(b) The screen appears at the CLICK, not at the response.** `committing` flips
synchronously before the await. A screen that rendered only after the commit
resolved would narrate a 41-second wait that was already over — which is the
exact failure the CR exists to fix.

**(c) The handover is automatic after 4 s on success, and NEVER automatic on
failure.** The old behaviour navigated to the checklist the instant the commit
resolved; leaving the user on a completed summary they must dismiss would be a
new click for everyone. Four seconds is long enough to read four ticked lines,
and the *Go to your utility* button is live from the first frame. **A failed
plant does not auto-navigate**: something did not land and the person has to see
which block before they leave.

> ⚠ **SUPERSEDED IN PART (PO ruling 2026-08-28 → `DEF-2370`, decision row of the
> same day).** The sentence *"the Go to your utility button is live from the
> first frame"* is **NO LONGER TRUE AND MUST NOT BE BUILT FROM.** PO verbatim:
> *"dont enable go to utility until all jobs are completed"* — the button is now
> DISABLED WITH ITS REASON (`BR-SHL-025`) during `committing` and `seeding`, and
> both it and the timer read one exported predicate, `handoverReady(phase)`.
> **The rest of clause (c) stands unchanged:** 4 s on `ready`/`waiting`, and a
> failed plant still never auto-navigates — indeed `partial` is deliberately the
> one phase where the button STAYS usable, for the reason this clause's own last
> sentence gives.

**(d) There is no progress bar and no percentage.** Provisioning has two halves
with different denominators — one atomic transaction that cannot report a
fraction of itself, and a ten-block job that can. A single bar over both would
have to invent the ratio between them. The screen shows named work with a state
word per line instead, and the sample line carries the job's real
`progress.done / progress.total`.

**(e) A failed plant offers no retry button, deliberately.** Provisioning is
idempotent on the subdomain (BR-TEN-010), but a signup REPLAY returns the
existing tenant early and enqueues no plant — so a "try again" on this screen
would do nothing. The true repair is the S8 *Sample data → Load* action, and the
copy names that instead of offering a button that cannot work.

### 4 · WHAT THE SCREEN SAYS, IN FULL (walked in a browser, twice)

During the wait: *"We are building {name}"* · *"Thank you for waiting. Your
utility is being set up and your data is being seeded right now — this usually
takes under a minute. Please keep this page open."* · four named lines, each
with its own state word — **Your utility and your owner login** · **Reference
lists** · **Chart of accounts, number series, taxes and document templates** ·
**Sample data so you can see it working** — and the reassurance the PO asked
for: *"You do not need to do anything. Nothing you typed is lost, and we will
take you to your setup checklist as soon as everything is in place."*

At completion, the same four lines carry the SERVER's own counts: *Created, and
you are signed in* · **20 lists, 149 rows** · *Ready to bill against* · **All 10
blocks loaded**. Every figure is read off `reference_seed` and the job record;
none is typed into the screen.

### 5 · THE WALKTHROUGH FOUND A DEFECT THAT EVERY TEST MISSED (DEF-325)

The first browser run showed *"Not loaded — Not requested at signup"* on the
sample row **for the whole wait**, about sample data that was being built at
that moment. `sample_plant` is null in two different situations — the S111
toggle was off, and the commit has not answered yet — and the copy branched on
the value rather than the phase. Thirty unit tests were green over it. **Found
by taking a screenshot mid-wait and reading it**, which is hard-won law 6
charging its rent again.

## 2026-08-19 · ASYNC JOBS, ADDENDUM: JOBS MAY BE CHAINED, AND THE CHAIN IS SEQUENTIAL BY LAW

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"you can do 2 or 3 or 4 jobs run them one after
another in case there is dependecy between data that needs settings"*.

**And on Celery beat — ⚠ THIS READING WAS WRONG, SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 by the PO's correction at the end of this log. Left in place, not deleted, because the mechanism that caught it is the point.** Verbatim: *"i agree with this"*, quoting the paragraph that
said beat was **raised rather than added by inference**. Read as: **beat is NOT
deployed now.** Two services — Redis and a Celery worker — as the first ruling said.
Recorded as a reading rather than a quotation because the agreement was to a
paragraph rather than to one of the two options offered; it is reversible in one
sentence, and nothing in the product currently needs a schedule. If the reading is
wrong the correction is cheap; building a singleton process nobody asked for is not.

### What the ruling authorises

Provisioning may be **2, 3 or 4 job records run one after another** instead of one,
where a later stage depends on data an earlier stage wrote. The PO's stated reason is
the dependency itself — *"data that needs settings"*.

### What is ALREADY true, and must not be rebuilt

The dependency the ruling protects against **is already satisfied**, in two places,
and the next agent should not "fix" it twice:

1. **Settings and reference data are committed BEFORE the plant starts.**
   `provision_tenant` seeds the tenant, the owner, the subscription, `TenantSettings`
   and the twenty reference lists inside its own transaction, and only enqueues the
   plant **after** that transaction commits (BR-TEN-063 — the plant's failure must
   never roll back a tenant). A worker therefore cannot begin before settings exist.
2. **The plant's ten blocks are already a strict ordered sequence**, and each depends
   on its predecessor: identity → rating (plans, tariffs) → metering (premises, units,
   service points) → assets → customers (accounts, agreements) → reads → billing
   (invoices, lines) → payments → payment plans → plan payments. `SAMPLE_MODULES` is
   that order, `seed_sample_data` walks it with `enumerate`, and progress is reported
   per block.

So splitting is **permitted, not required**. It is worth doing where a stage needs to
be **retried on its own** — the job record already carries a `checkpoint` for exactly
that — and not worth doing merely to have more job records.

### THE BINDING RULE, if it is split

**Sequential, never parallel, and a stage may not start until its predecessor has
COMMITTED.** This is the trap and it must be written down before anyone builds it:
Celery's natural shape is concurrent. A `group()` would run these blocks at the same
time and a worker picking up "billing" while "rating" is still inside its transaction
reads **no tariffs** and seeds **no invoices** — silently, because an empty result set
is not an error. Use a **chain**, and hand off only after commit (`transaction.
on_commit`, the same discipline `provision_tenant` already uses for the plant).

⚠ **And the screen must still see ONE thing.** CR-017's provisioning screen polls a
single BE-07 job record for `progress.done / total`. If provisioning becomes four
records, the screen must not be made to poll four — either one parent record spans
the chain, or the screen is given a chain id it can poll as one. **Whichever is
chosen, the screen's contract is the constraint, not an afterthought**: the PO asked
for it so a user is not *"left hi and dry"*, and a progress bar that resets to zero
three times is worse than the one it replaced.

## 2026-08-19 · CELERY BEAT IS DEPLOYED — the PO corrects a reading I recorded as mine

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"we need Beat ; include it"*.

**This SUPERSEDES** the beat reading in the async-jobs addendum earlier today. Both
places are stamped rather than deleted.

**What I got wrong, stated plainly so the mechanism is visible.** I asked the PO an
either/or — *"Do you want beat in as well, or hold it until something actually needs
a schedule?"* — and they replied *"i agree with this"* against the paragraph saying
beat had been **raised rather than added by inference**. I read that as *hold it*. It
meant the opposite. **The reading was wrong; the way it was recorded was not.** It
was written into the log as *my reading of an ambiguous reply* rather than as the
PO's words, with the sentence "if the reading is wrong the correction is cheap" — and
the correction cost one line from the PO and this row. Had it been recorded as a
ruling, the next agent would have inherited a fabricated decision with a verbatim
quote attached to it. **When a reply is ambiguous, record the reading AS a reading.**

### What is now deployed: THREE services, not two

| Service | Purpose | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `redis` | Celery broker, and only that in v1 (TD-3, TD-17) | — |
| `celery` worker | job bodies: the tenancy sample plant, the bulk rate change, both audit exports | may scale to N |
| `celery-beat` | the schedule | ⚠ **EXACTLY ONE. Never two.** |

### The singleton constraint is the whole risk, and it is not advisory

`09-infra/01-deployment-architecture.md` §4 states beat must run exactly once and
that liveness must be alarmed on. **Two beat processes do not fail loudly — they
double-fire every scheduled job.** For this product that means, concretely: partition
archival running twice over the same range, report-retention deletion running twice,
and the notification dispatcher pacing at double rate. Each is a data-affecting
operation, and none of them errors when it runs twice; they just do it twice.

So beat's compose service is **`deploy.replicas: 1`, and scaling it is a mistake, not
a tuning knob.** That sentence belongs in the compose file itself, next to the
service, because the next person to scale the worker pool is the person who will
scale this one too.

### What beat is FOR here — three schedules already decided, none yet built

Beat is not speculative infrastructure: `09-infra` already names three recurring jobs
it was decided for, and **none of them exists in code today**:

1. **Partition archival** (NFR-6 / NFR-28) — detach and archive aged partitions.
2. **Report retention** (NFR-9) — delete generated reports past their retention.
3. **Notification dispatcher pacing** (NFR-1).

⚠ **Adding the beat PROCESS does not add these three jobs.** A beat container with an
empty schedule is a running process that does nothing, and — per hard-won law 1 — a
compose service named `celery-beat` is not a guarantee that anything is scheduled.
Whoever lands beat must state, in the handover, which schedules exist and which of
these three are still unbuilt. **If the answer is "none are built", say that**: an
empty beat is honest; an empty beat described as "scheduling is now handled" is a
context leak of exactly the kind law 10 forbids.

### Unchanged by this ruling

The trigger after tenant creation, the sequential-chain rule, and the CR-017 progress
screen's one-record contract all stand exactly as ruled earlier today. Beat schedules
recurring work; it has nothing to do with provisioning, which is event-driven.

## 2026-08-19 · SERVER `detail` TEXT NEVER REACHES A CUSTOMER SCREEN (DEF-322)

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"server detail text should not reach customer
screens"*.

**What was asked.** DEF-322 found 422 refusal responses carrying internal ids inside
`params.detail` — the free-text field a service attaches to a `BizError` to say
exactly what went wrong, in engineering terms. The lane deliberately stopped rather
than rewrite 422 sentences, because rewriting them would have answered the underlying
rule by default. The rule is now ruled.

### THE RULE

A refusal's customer-facing text comes from **the catalogue entry for its
`message_key`, and from nothing else**. `params.detail` is diagnostic: it goes to the
audit trail and the server log, where support can still reach it, and it is never
rendered.

### ⚠ THE COST, MEASURED BEFORE ANYONE STARTS — and it is the whole of the work

Suppressing `detail` does not make 27 messages tidier. It changes what happens when a
key has no catalogue entry, and **48 of them have none**:

| Measured 2026-08-19 at `44e963e` | Count |
|---|---|
| Distinct `message_key`s the backend raises | **319** |
| …that resolve to a customer sentence in `en.json` | **271** |
| …that resolve to **nothing at all** | **48** |
| Refusals that attach a `params.detail` | 27 |

For those 48, `detail` is currently the ONLY text carrying any meaning. Suppress it
without writing the sentence and the refusal goes from **ugly to silent** — the user
clicks, nothing happens, and no explanation appears anywhere. **That is worse than the
defect being fixed**, and it is the exact shape of DEF-320: a path that looks handled
and communicates nothing.

**So the work is not "stop rendering detail". It is: write 48 customer sentences,
THEN stop rendering detail.** In that order. A gate must hold it: no `message_key`
may be raised that does not resolve in the catalogue, ratcheted at 48 so the number
can only fall.

### What this does NOT mean

1. **Absences must still be STATED.** The rule that closed the last content sweep
   stands: law 1 is about the repo being honest with itself, not about hiding a
   limitation from a utility. *"Email sending is not switched on yet, so no email
   leaves the building"* is customer-facing and correct; the BR-code that explains why
   is not.
2. **Support does not lose the diagnostic.** `detail` keeps going to the audit row and
   the log. Nothing is deleted — it moves.
3. **This is not only about ids.** The ruling says *detail text*, not *ids in detail
   text*. A detail string with no id in it is still engineering prose written for us,
   and it still does not reach a screen.

## 2026-08-19 · REFUSAL COPY: SHORT SENTENCES — the house style, with a checkable number

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** shown the three replacement sentences below and asked
to judge them, they answered *"these kind of messagesa re okay; you need shorter
sentences not long ones"*.

**What was shown, and approved as the right SHAPE:**

> *"A budget-level override needs a reason. Enter one and we'll record it against the account."*
> *"That override is outside the allowed range for this plan."*
> *"This bill has no account number yet — it gets one when the draft is created."*

Against what they replace, which is the same refusal today:

> *"a per-account budget level override requires a REASON (BR-BIL-017 as OQ-068 closed it: allowed with reason + audit)"*

So the ruling has two halves and both are binding: the SHAPE above is right — plain,
second person, says what to do next — **and the SENTENCES must be shorter.**

### THE RULE, as a number a check can hold

**No sentence over 12 words. At most two sentences per message.** Twelve is not
arbitrary: it is the current median longest-sentence length rounded up from 9, so it
codifies what the good messages already do rather than inventing a target.

| Measured 2026-08-19 at `bec921e`, over the 271 refusal messages that resolve | |
|---|---|
| Median sentence count per message | **1** |
| Median longest sentence | **9 words** |
| Messages with a sentence over 12 words | **57 (21%)** |
| Messages with a sentence over 20 words | 5 |
| Messages with more than two sentences | 4 |

**So this is a small job, not a rewrite of everything.** 79% of the catalogue already
passes. The work is 57 messages plus the 48 that have no sentence at all.

The four longest, as the shape to break up rather than to shorten by deletion:

- `metering.read.not_billed` — 23 words: *"This read is not on an issued bill, so it is corrected with a normal supersede — not through the billing correction path."*
- `ledger.cost.redate_after_close_refused` — 22 words.
- `ledger.export.does_not_foot` — 22 words.
- `payments.as_of_required` — 22 words: the second sentence is an ESSAY about whose clock a business day belongs to. That is a design rationale, and rationale belongs in the docstring, not on the screen.

### The failure mode to avoid while shortening

**Do not shorten by removing the next action.** *"A budget-level override needs a
reason. Enter one and we'll record it against the account."* is two sentences and
should stay two: the first says what is wrong, the second says what to do. Cutting the
second gets under the limit and makes the message worse. **Shorten by deleting
RATIONALE, not by deleting INSTRUCTION** — `payments.as_of_required` is the model:
keep *"Choose the day to report on."*, drop the sentence about the server's clock.

### Where this rule applies

Every catalogue value a refusal resolves to — the 48 being written and the 57 being
shortened. It is a **copy** rule, not a translation rule: the eleven locales follow
their own language's natural length, and a gate must count English only.

## 2026-08-19 · A SYSTEM ERROR SAYS SO, AND GIVES THE USER AN IDENTIFIER TO REPORT

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"if it is system error then you tell user it is system erro
this is error number or some identifier that they can report to support"*.

**What was put to them.** About a dozen of the 48 refusals with no customer sentence are
things a user can never trigger — `customers.payload_not_object`,
`customers.account.addresses_not_a_list`, `customers.account.lock_outside_transaction`.
They are programming errors, not user mistakes, and I proposed one shared honest line
with no identifier: *"Something went wrong on our side. Nothing was changed. Please try
again or contact support."* The PO accepted the honesty and **rejected the missing
identifier**: a user told to contact support must be given something to quote.

### THE RULE

A refusal the user cannot act on says, in plain words, that it is a **system error**,
that **nothing was changed**, and gives an **identifier the user can read aloud to
support**. A refusal the user CAN act on keeps the ordinary shape ruled earlier — what
is wrong, then what to do next — and carries no identifier, because an id on a
correctable mistake is noise.

### ⚠ THE IDENTIFIER ALREADY EXISTS AND IS RENDERED BY NOTHING (DEF-328)

Do not invent an error-number scheme. `trace_id` has been in the envelope contract since
B12 §3 and it is REAL, not documented-only:

| Layer | State |
|---|---|
| Generated per refusal — `06-backend/core/errors.py:331`, `uuid.uuid4().hex` | ✅ works |
| Written to the audit attempt row — `_write_attempt_row(exc, context, trace_id)` (BR-AUD-018) | ✅ works |
| Returned in every envelope — `_envelope(... trace_id=trace_id)` | ✅ works |
| Declared on the frontend type — `FormModal.tsx:88`, `trace_id?: string` | ✅ declared |
| **Rendered to a user** | ❌ **by NOTHING, anywhere** |

So support can already look up any refusal by trace id, and the user has never been able
to tell them one. **This is hard-won law 2 — built is not wired — and it is invisible to
every check we own:** `tsc` is clean because the field is declared, eslint is clean, and
three tests mention `trace_id` while asserting only that the envelope *carries* it, never
that a person can *see* it. G13 catches an unwired PROP; nothing catches an unwired FIELD
on a typed object. Filed as **DEF-328**.

The backend half being complete is what hid it: every review of the error path found a
trace id present at every layer it looked at.

### What to build

1. Render the trace id **only on refusals the user cannot act on** — not on validation.
2. Make it **readable aloud**: the raw value is a 32-character hex string, which nobody
   can dictate over the phone. Shorten it for display and keep the full value in the
   audit row, or shorten what is generated. **Whichever is chosen, the displayed string
   must be the one support can search by** — a shortened id that support cannot look up
   is worse than none, because the user reads it out and the call stalls.
3. Assert it **in a browser**, not in a type. DEF-328 exists because the type was the
   only thing asserted.

### The sentence shape, obeying the 12-word rule

> *"Something went wrong on our side. Nothing was changed — quote {{ref}} to support."*

Two sentences, longest is nine words, and the identifier is the thing the second sentence
delivers.

## 2026-08-19 — CR-017 · REDIS AND CELERY ARE INSTALLED, AND THE QUEUE IS FINALLY CONSUMED (build 2.27.0)

**The PO's rulings, verbatim, both of them:** *"We want Async job install redis and
celery; Trigger after tenant creation; also add these two services in docker
compose"* and, the same day, *"we need Beat ; include it"*.

### 1 · THE PROOF, WHICH IS THE ONLY PART THAT MATTERS

DEF-320 was never a code bug. Every job body has a passing unit test and always
did — **because every one of those tests turns `JOBS_EAGER` ON**, which is the
one configuration production does not use. What shipped broken was the space
between three processes, and one process cannot see it.

So it was proved with three. `10-scripts/verify_celery_transport.py` starts a
real `celery -A config.celery worker` against a real Redis, sets
`JOBS_EAGER=false` — production's own value — enqueues one job of every kind and
waits on the database record:

```
tenant under test: brazosbend
  PASS  tenancy.sample_data_plant        succeeded  progress={'done': 10, 'total': 10}
  PASS  rating.bulk_rate_update          succeeded  progress={'done': 0, 'total': None}
  PASS  audit_export                     succeeded  progress={'done': 1071, 'total': 0}
  PASS  list_export                      succeeded  progress={'done': 53, 'total': 0}
```

**All four. Under production dispatch. With a worker actually running.** Before
this commit all four would have read `queued`, forever, which is what a new
tenant's missing sample data (DEF-320) and a bulk rate change that changed no
price (DEF-326) both were. The plant's `10/10` is the same field the CR-017
signup screen polls, so that screen now narrates a real worker rather than a
job that had already finished inside the request.

### 2 · WHAT WAS BUILT, AND HOW LITTLE OF IT IS NEW

`core.jobs` was not touched. `enqueue → _dispatcher → run_pending → run_job` was
already the contract and `set_job_dispatcher` was already the seam; Celery
replaces the transport underneath and nothing above it.

* **`apps/tenancy/tasks.py`** — ONE task for EVERY kind, because `run_pending`
  already resolves the body from the record's `kind` through the registry each
  module fills at `AppConfig.ready()`. A task per kind would duplicate that
  registry in a second place and the two would drift the first time a kind was
  added and its task was not.
* **`dispatch_job`'s second branch** — it used to be a comment describing a
  worker that did not exist. A comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee
  (hard-won law 1), and nothing in this repo read that comment.
* **`docker-compose.yml`** — `redis`, `celery`, `celery-beat`. Its header said in
  its own words that none of them existed; that header is rewritten, not left to
  contradict the file it heads.
* **`06-backend/.env.example`** — `JOBS_EAGER=false` and an UNCOMMENTED
  `CELERY_BROKER_URL=redis://redis:6379/0`. Both were the unsafe value before:
  the broker line was commented out with *"uncomment on the day a worker
  exists"*, and inside a container the library default's `localhost` is the
  container itself — nothing listens, the worker retries forever, and the only
  symptom is jobs that never finish (hard-won law 3).

### 3 · THE TENANT HAD TO TRAVEL IN THE MESSAGE, AND THIS WAS A REAL BUG WAITING

`run_job` enters tenant context **from the record** — but it must LOAD the record
first, and on Postgres `jobs` carries RLS FORCE. A worker with no `app.tenant_id`
reads zero rows and every worker-run job fails as "unknown job". Eager dispatch
never hit it because the caller is mid-request and already in context;
`core/jobs.py`'s own trailer has carried this as a REPORTED gap for the worker
lane since 2026-08-10. The dispatcher now sends `tenant_id` beside `job_id` and
the task enters the context before anything touches the database.

**The test for it was VACUOUS on the first attempt, and that is worth recording.**
The obvious assertion — run the job, check the body saw the right tenant — stayed
GREEN with the `tenant_context` deleted, because sqlite has no RLS and `run_job`
enters the context from the record it just loaded. Proved by deleting it and
watching the test pass. The assertion is now on the context **at the moment the
load begins**, which is the actual property, and that one goes red.

### 4 · THE PLANT WAS **NOT** SPLIT INTO SEVERAL JOBS, AND THAT IS A DECISION

The PO permitted it — *"you can do 2 or 3 or 4 jobs run them one after another in
case there is dependecy between data that needs settings"* — and permitted is not
required. It was not done, for three reasons, so that nobody splits it a fourth
time believing the dependency is unprotected:

1. **The dependency is already satisfied twice.** `provision_tenant` commits the
   tenant, owner, subscription, `TenantSettings` and all twenty reference lists
   inside its own transaction and enqueues the plant only *after* it
   (BR-TEN-063). A worker cannot start before settings exist.
2. **`SAMPLE_MODULES` is already a strict ordered chain of ten blocks** — identity
   → rating → metering → assets → customers → reads → billing → payments →
   payment plans → plan payments — walked in order, one transaction each, with
   per-block progress.
3. **The screen's contract is one record.** CR-017's screen polls a single job for
   `progress.done / total`. Four records means four polls or a progress line that
   resets to zero three times, which is worse than the blank browser it replaced.

**If a stage is ever split out for independent retry** — which is the only reason
that would justify it — the rule is binding and is written here because Celery's
natural shape is the wrong one: **`chain()`, never `group()`, and hand off on
`transaction.on_commit`.** A worker picking up "billing" while "rating" is still
inside its transaction reads no tariffs and seeds no invoices, **silently**,
because an empty result set is not an error.

### 5 · BEAT IS DEPLOYED AND HAS NOTHING TO RUN, AND BOTH HALVES MUST BE SAID

`celery-beat` is a third service with `deploy.replicas: 1`, and the reason is
written in the compose file beside the number rather than in a document the
person scaling the worker pool will not have open: **two beats do not conflict,
they both fire.** Partition archival over the same range twice, report-retention
DELETEs twice, dispatcher pacing at double rate — none of the three errors when
run twice, they simply do it twice.

⚠ **AND THERE IS NO SCHEDULE.** There is no `beat_schedule` anywhere in
`06-backend/config/`, and the three recurring jobs `09-infra` decided beat for —
partition archival (NFR-6/28), report retention (NFR-9), dispatcher pacing
(NFR-1) — **are none of them built**. The container connects and fires nothing.
An empty beat is honest; an empty beat described as *"scheduling is now handled"*
is the shape that produced DEF-320 in the first place — a path that looked
provisioned and consumed nothing.

### 6 · ⚠ NONE OF THIS REACHES THE DEPLOYED HOST (hard-won law 4)

Editing `docker-compose.yml` and `.env.example` changes nothing already running.
The deployed build needs, and does not have: **a broker it can reach at its own
`CELERY_BROKER_URL`**, **at least one process running `celery -A config.celery
worker`**, and **`JOBS_EAGER=false` in the `.env` that host already has** (a
template change never reaches a host with an existing `.env`). Until those three
are true on that host, DEF-320 and DEF-326 are still live there — the code is
correct and nothing is running it.

## 2026-08-19 · DEF-327 — the 125 undeclared classes, and what the PO's patch stylesheet was actually worth

**Context.** The Product Owner uploaded `smartbillhub-fixes.css` alongside DEF-327
(125 classes referenced by components and declared by no stylesheet, eight screens
rendering as flowing text). This records what was done with it, because the next agent
handed that file will otherwise re-run the same evaluation and may reach a different
answer from its header text alone.

### ⚠ THE FILE'S OWN STATED REASON IS FALSE, AND IT WAS MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS ADOPTED

Its header says `class="pill err"` *"already exists in 11 places"*. Measured:

| String | in `07-frontend/src` | in `05-prototype/r10-2026-08-16/SMARTBillHub.dc.html` |
|---|---|---|
| `pill err` | **0** | **11** (14 counting `.pill.err` selector text) |
| `chooser` / `chooser-option` / `co-*` | 0 | **0** |
| `kv` / `kv-k` / `kv-v` / `status-count` | 0 | **0** |

So the file was written against the **prototype's** markup, not ours — and its two
headline patterns are **not r10 vocabulary either**: they are that file's own coinage.
**"Adopt these names to converge on r10" is therefore not a reason that survives
checking, and must not be repeated.** Of its 27 classes, **zero** are among our 125 and
**25** are referenced nowhere in this app. All 12 design tokens it uses are real here, so
it is token-compatible — it is simply aimed at a different codebase.

`.pill.err` in particular is **not** adopted: `StatusPill.tsx` maps `danger → .pill.past`,
which `StateFrame.css` declares. Adding `.pill.err` would be dead CSS.

### WHAT WAS ADOPTED, AND ON WHAT REASON INSTEAD

Two patterns, on their merits, and both because **two different feature folders ask for
the same shape** — the condition `global.css` already records for `.kicker`: *"putting it
in any one of them is how DEF-244's shape recurs."*

1. **`.kv` / `.kv-k` / `.kv-v`** replaces THREE private copies of the label/value row —
   `kpi-list`/`kpi-label`/`kpi-value` in notifications AND customers, and
   `cus-modal-fact*` in customers. The deciding argument is not sharing but a **name
   collision**: `kpi-*` collided with the real `.kpi` stat tile in `KPIStrip.css`, and
   `payments.css` already carries a `.kpi .v .pay-absent` rule aimed at that other one.
   The same prefix meant two different components.
2. **`.chooser` / `.chooser-option` / `.co-title` / `.co-desc` / `.co-meta`** replaces
   `bil-layout-*` (billing) and `rd-source-*` (metering), which were the same option-card
   grid drawn twice. `is-selected` is the one state name; billing's `active` was renamed
   to match metering's, rather than declaring both.

One correction was made to the PO's rules while adopting them: `.chooser-option` is given
`position: relative`. The supplied file absolutely-positions the hidden radio without it,
which would position the input against whatever ancestor happened to be positioned.

### THE UNPREFIXED-GLOBAL RULING, RE-APPLIED — AND WHY IT HAD TO BE

DEF-244 (2026-08-18) already ruled this, in `SettingsPage.css`: `.badge` and
`.preview-strip` *"are NOT declared under those names: they are unprefixed globals, and
claiming `.badge` app-wide from a settings stylesheet would style anything that ever uses
the word."*

**Eight months of commits later `DisconnectRightsFooterCard.tsx` was still asking for
`class="badge badge-muted"`** — because the RENAME reached the two files being fixed and
the RULE behind it reached nothing. That is the lesson worth keeping: a fix applied to
instances does not generalise; only a rule written down does. Ten of the 125 were
resolved this way — `badge`/`badge-muted` → `settings-badge`/`settings-badge-muted`,
`muted` → `settings-muted`, `two-col` → `pay-two-col`, `see` → `pay-see`.

`.muted` was deliberately **not** made a global, even though four namespaced copies of the
identical rule exist (`.cus-muted`, `.met-muted`, `.rating-muted`, `.ast-muted`).
Consolidating five copies into one global is a product-wide restyle and belongs in its own
change with its own walkthrough — the same call `--table-font-size` made in leaving
`DataTable` at 13px (DEF-223).

### A GATE WRITTEN FOR A DEFECT COULD NOT SEE THE DEFECT'S OWN WORST CASE (DEF-329)

G31 skipped any `className={` template containing `${`, so on the upload-reads wizard it
reported `is-selected` and `is-blocked` and **not `rd-source-card`, the class that draws
the card**. A lane fixing DEF-327 from its `--list` output would have declared the three
classes *around* the card, left the card undeclared, and shipped S28 still broken with
every gate green. **The general rule: when a gate is written for a defect, run it against
that defect's own worst example and check it sees the whole of it.** G31's docstring
named `.bil-layout-card` — a plain quoted string — and every hand-check used one too.

### THE BASELINE IS NOW ZERO, WHICH CHANGES WHAT G31 IS

125 → 0. At 125 it was a debt register; at 0 it is an **invariant**, and the next
component that asks for an undeclared class turns it red on the commit that adds it —
the first time that has been true in this repo. Six recurrences (DEF-244, DEF-305,
DEF-308, DEF-314, DEF-315, DEF-327) were each found by a human reading a screenshot.
**Do not raise it back:** a class that genuinely cannot be declared does not exist — if a
component asks for a name, either a stylesheet owes it a rule or the component should not
be asking.

### DEF-316 IS DELIBERATELY HALF-CLOSED, AND THE HALF MATTERS

Its prevention names two things. **(1) is done**: `expandInnerScroller` in
`07-frontend/e2e/support/app.ts` records that `fullPage: true` is silently a viewport shot
in this app — measured on Settings → Notifications at 1440×900, `document.scrollHeight`
**900** against `main.view.scrollHeight` **8624**, so nine of every ten screenfuls are
absent from an image that looks complete. Releasing `main.view` alone does **not** work;
its ancestors hold the document at 900px and the height must be released all the way up.
Without this, none of DEF-327's before/after evidence was obtainable — DEF-314, DEF-315
and DEF-317 all lived below the fold of a screenshot that reported success.

**(2) is NOT done and the row stays open naming only it:** balancing the unequal columns,
or letting each scroll independently, is a layout decision for the PO (which of the two)
on a screen this pass only restyled. Closing the row on the half that was done would be
claiming a review that never happened.

### ⚠ NO VERSION WAS BUMPED, AND THAT IS A GAP THIS LANE COULD NOT CLOSE

The change process step 7 says a defect fix records a version. The two sources of truth —
`07-frontend/package.json` and `06-backend/pyproject.toml`, both at `2.27.0` — are inside
this lane's **do-not-touch** set: another lane is mid-build on Redis/Celery in exactly
those files. So this fix ships at `2.27.0` with the version unbumped, and it is written
down here rather than left silent, because "the step that depends on someone remembering
is exactly the step that is many times not followed correctly" is the reason step 7 exists.
Whoever lands the Redis/Celery work should carry the bump.

## 2026-08-19 · BUILDING THE THREE REFUSAL-COPY RULINGS — five judgments the rulings did not settle

The three PO rulings of this date (`bec921e` detail never reaches a screen · `6baa846`
short sentences · `3340c68` a system error hands over an identifier) are law and are
recorded above. **Building them raised five questions the rulings do not answer**, and
each was decided here rather than in a reply, so the next agent inherits the reasoning
rather than the result.

### 1 · A grep finds 48 unwritten keys. An AST finds 51.

The brief's own command — `grep -rhoE 'message_key="[^"]+"'` — returns 319 keys, 48 of
them unwritten, and both figures reproduce exactly. **An `ast` walk returns 324, and the
five extra include three keys absent from all eleven catalogues:**
`errors.identity.password_too_short`, `…password_needs_mixed`, `…password_needs_symbol`.

They are invisible to the grep because they are written as **dict entries inside
`field_errors`** —

```python
{"field": "new_password", "code": errors.VAL_RANGE,
 "message_key": "errors.identity.password_too_short", "params": {"min_length": min_length}}
```

— and `envelopeErrors()` renders exactly those, under the input, on the change-password
form. So a System Admin choosing a six-character password read the literal string
`errors.identity.password_too_short` beneath the box. **51 sentences were written, not
48**, and `G32` reads the AST for this reason, stated in its docstring.

### 2 · Twelve of the 51 are the system-error group, and here is the list

The `3340c68` ruling says "about a dozen" and leaves the call to whoever reads the raise
sites. Judged per key by reading the code, twelve are refusals a user **cannot** trigger
and now share one sentence — *"Something went wrong on our side. Nothing was changed —
quote {{ref}} to support."*:

`billing.customer_name_unavailable` · `billing.payload_not_object` ·
`customers.payload_not_object` · `customers.account.addresses_not_a_list` ·
`customers.account.lock_outside_transaction` · `customers.account.numbering_unavailable` ·
`customers.account.tenant_currency_missing` · `customers.reference_fixture_invalid` ·
`rating.reference_fixture_invalid` · `metering.plan.history_unavailable` ·
`notifications.rules.channelsNotObject` · `notifications.templates.contractCannotBeSeeded`

**One that looks like the group and is NOT:**
`billing.customer_name_search_unavailable` fires when the customers seam is unwired.
That is a system state, but the user CAN act on it — so it says *"Searching bills by
customer name isn't available yet. Search by bill number instead."* The ruling that
absences must be STATED (`bec921e`, clause 1) decides this one, not the system-error rule.

### 3 · The support reference is shortened for DISPLAY, because it cannot be shortened at SOURCE

The ruling offers both: *"shorten it for display … or shorten what is generated."*
**Shortening what is generated is impossible, and the reason is a column type.**
`audit_log.entity_id` is a `UUIDField`, and the BR-AUD-018 attempt row writes the trace id
into it. A twelve-character token would fail to parse as a UUID, and that write is inside a
`try/except` that logs and continues — so the audit row would silently stop being written
for every refusal in the product. The generated value stays `uuid4().hex`.

So the display form is the **first eight hex characters, uppercased, grouped 4-4**:
`5F2B-9C1D`. Four billion values; the audit window is two years and one tenant.

**And the ruling's trap is the other half of the change.** *"A shortened id that support
cannot look up is worse than none."* `apps/audit/selectors.audit_queryset` matched
`f.entity_id` as a whole UUID or returned `.none()`, so the reference on screen would have
found nothing. It now accepts a hex PREFIX, case- and dash-insensitive, via
`Cast("entity_id", TextField())` — a `LIKE` against a `uuid` column is
`operator does not exist: uuid ~~ unknown` on PostgreSQL, so the cast is what makes it work
at all. Proved by `tests/test_def_328_support_reference.py`, which was proved RED first.

**Seven characters is refused deliberately.** The displayed form is always eight; accepting
a shorter prefix would let a near-empty filter sweep a support answer.

### 4 · The sixteen catch-all `*.refused` keys LOSE information, and that is the cost of the ruling

`billing.budget.refused` served five distinct refusals and said *"That cannot be done:
{{detail}}"*. With `detail` suppressed, one catalogue value must answer all five, so it now
reads *"This account can't be put on budget billing as asked. Check its billing history and
settings."* — the area and what to check, not which rule fired.

**This is a real loss and it is not hidden.** The right end state is a distinct
`message_key` per refusal, which is a sweep of ~500 raise sites across 87 modules and is
not this lane's. What is shipped instead is the ratchet: **G28 Part 3** counts every raise
site whose prose names an internal reference, so the number can only fall as those sites
are split.

### 5 · G28 Part 3 measures 498, where DEF-322 recorded 422 — and the number is not reconciled

DEF-322's count came from a one-off script that is not in the repo. It cannot be made to
agree by inspection, only by guessing at its exclusions, so **the baseline is what the gate
in the repo measures**: a ratchet whose starting number came from a script nobody can re-run
is not a ratchet.

Two exemptions were added, each because it produced a real false positive (573 → 498), and
both are the machine-field lesson DEF-322 itself recorded:

* **`NotImplementedError` is exempt entirely.** CLAUDE.md's prime directive REQUIRES the id
  in it — *"stub the gap as `raise NotImplementedError("OQ-###")`"*. A gate flagging those
  would be flagging the law it serves.
* **A positional argument that is NOTHING BUT an id is exempt.** `deny_as_not_found(
  "BR-TEN-003")` is `br_ref` passed one argument slot over — 150 of them. Prose that
  *mentions* an id still counts; a bare id is not prose.

### Two things found while building this, filed rather than fixed

* **DEF-331** — seven `message_key`s used in code resolve in no catalogue and two catalogue
  keys nothing renders, all nine unregistered. They were always there; they were hiding
  inside G18's headline of 26 missing + 8 dead, of which 3+6 were DEF-323's plural false
  positive and 16 were DEF-322's unwritten sentences. With both closed, G18's failure is
  now exactly those nine and cannot hide.
* **DEF-332** — `RefusalNotice` appends the server's `br_ref` to every Settings refusal, so
  a clerk reads *"… You can't deactivate this one. (BR-IDN-013)"*. **Two PO rulings point
  opposite ways here** — 2026-08-10 asked for a support-grade identifier line after the PO
  could not see what had failed, and 2026-08-19 refused BR-codes on screen. That is a rule
  question for the PO, not a sweep, so it is filed with the concrete sentence to put to them.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-018 TAKES ROUTE B — the styles go in the markup, and the class names go away

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"Route B"*, answering the question *"Route A or Route B. My
recommendation is B."* put to them in the CR-018 plan.

### What was shown before the ruling, measured at 2.28.0 and not estimated

| | |
|---|---|
| React components | **127** (124 write at least one class name) |
| Places a class name is written | **3,020** — of which **2,944 are plain strings**, only 76 conditional expressions |
| Classes declared | **921**, across **40** stylesheets, **9,284** lines |
| Distinct classes referenced | **868** |
| …used in **exactly one** component | **689 (79%)** |
| …shared across components | **179** |

**The 79% is the finding that shapes the plan.** Most of our CSS is private to a single
file, so migrating that component touches nothing else and a mistake breaks one screen.
The risk lives in the 179 shared classes, which is why they get their own phase and it
is deliberately EARLY: a mistake there shows on every screen at once and is therefore
found at once, rather than in a corner nobody opens.

### The two routes as they were put, and why B

- **Route A — keep the class names**, Tailwind generates the CSS behind them. Rejected in
  the recommendation and by the PO. **It is not a migration.** The class name remains the
  only contract between a component and its styling, so a component can still name a class
  nothing declares and `tsc`, eslint and `toHaveClass()` all still pass over it — DEF-327's
  exact failure mode, the one that left eight screens as unstyled text and recurred six
  times in five months.
- **Route B — styles in the markup.** ✅ RULED. It removes the failure mode by removing the
  thing that fails: there is no class name to get wrong because there is no class name.

### ⚠ THE CONSEQUENCE THE RULING BUYS, STATED PLAINLY

**Route B makes G31 obsolete.** That gate refuses a class no stylesheet declares, and it
ends this change with nothing to refuse. It must be **retired deliberately, with a written
reason**, not left passing vacuously over an empty set — a green gate measuring nothing is
worse than no gate, because it reads as protection that is no longer there. That is the
same failure this repo recorded in G26's and G27's docstrings and again in DEF-323.

**And Route B is the larger job by a wide margin**: 3,020 rewrite sites against Route A's
roughly zero. The PO chose the expensive route with the cost in front of them.

### What the sequencing still is

**Unchanged: CR-018 does not start while CR-016 is open** — the PO set that themselves
(*"After 16 is closed - we will do tailwind CR"*). CR-016's remaining blocker is a single
rule question, DEF-332, and the PO's deploy confirmation.

**One exception, and it is stated rather than assumed: Phase 0 touches ZERO screens.** It
is the theme file and the build chain. It cannot regress a screen because it renders none,
and it is the phase that de-risks all the others. Starting it early does not breach the
sequencing, which was about screens changing under a CR that was still open.

### Still open, still not decided by inference

- **Tailwind v4 or v3.** The attached file targets v4 (`@import` + `@theme`) and carries a
  v3 fallback config. A build-chain decision; v4 is the current release and the file's
  first-class target, so v4 is the RECOMMENDATION with the reason stated — not a silent
  default.
- **The Archivo webfont.** `tokens.css:22` imports it from Google Fonts and CLAUDE.md
  records that it "was decided with the AppShell packet" and **was decided by nobody**
  (hard-won law 1). Phase 0 re-declares `--font-heading`. It must not silently re-ratify a
  font nobody chose.

## 2026-08-19 · `(BR-IDN-013)` STAYS ON SCREEN **FOR NOW** — a deferral, not a reversal (DEF-332)

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"for time being okay"*, answering *"Should the
`(BR-IDN-013)` be there?"*

**Read it as written: this is a DEFERRAL.** *"For the time being"* accepts the string
today; it does not rule that internal ids belong on customer screens, and it does not
reverse the 2026-08-19 ruling that *"all these messages should not be on screen for
user"*. **DEF-332 therefore stays OPEN**, and closing it as *"PO said it was fine"* would
convert a temporary acceptance into a permanent rule the PO never gave.

### What the two rulings actually are, now that both are settled

| Ruling | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-10 — a refusal must carry a support-grade line, so a user can say what failed | the identifier | **stands**, and is now served properly by the shortened trace reference (`9DAD-5054`) shipped in 2.28.0 |
| 2026-08-19 — `detail` text never reaches a customer screen | the server's free prose | **stands and is enforced** (G28 Part 3, G32, G33) |
| 2026-08-19 — `(BR-IDN-013)` may stay for now | the BR-id appended by `RefusalNotice` | **deferred**, DEF-332 open |

**The conflict is smaller than it looked, and that is worth recording**: the 2026-08-10
ruling asked for *an identifier a user can quote*, and the product now has one that is
not a BR-code. So when DEF-332 is finally taken, the support need it was serving is
already met elsewhere — the BR-id can be dropped without losing anything the PO asked
for. **That was not true when the two rulings collided; it is true now.**

### The consequence for CR-016

DEF-332 was CR-016's last open item and it is **no longer a blocker** — under the closing
rule the PO themselves forced (2026-08-18: *"why you are not closing it and every time
keep something open we are losing time"*), a defect blocks its CR only when it is that
CR's own requirement **not working**. The PO has ruled the current behaviour acceptable
for now, so it works as ruled. **CR-016 closes over it, naming it by ID** — which is
exactly what that rule prescribes.

Also still open and also not blockers, both named rather than dropped: **DEF-316** (the
Notifications left column runs far past the right; a layout decision, raised not guessed)
and **OQ-271** (ten of the twelve system-error refusals write no audit row, so a printed
reference is answered by the server log rather than by the audit screen — the no-rule-
change fallback shipped, the rule change was not made by inference).

## 2026-08-19 · CR-018 PHASE 0 — the Tailwind theme, and the seven judgments the ruling did not settle

**The ruling this builds under is `"Route B"`** (PO, 2026-08-19, recorded above). Phase 0
is the one part the PO's sequencing lets start early, for the reason that row states:
**it renders nothing**, so it cannot regress the CR-016 build they are verifying in a
browser — and that is measured in §11, not asserted. Everything below is a judgment the ruling did not make, written down before it
was reported (hard-won law 9/10).

**Version 2.29.0.** `07-frontend/package.json` and `06-backend/pyproject.toml` moved in
the same commit, which is still the only thing keeping them equal (DEF-242).

### What was measured, not estimated

| | |
|---|---|
| tokens in `07-frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` | **76** |
| …crossed into the Tailwind theme | **76 — all of them**, proved by rendering |
| …under their own name, as a theme key | **63** (48 colours · 2 typefaces · 7 type sizes · 3 radii · 3 shadows) |
| …as a Tailwind-namespaced alias derived from ours, both names emitted | **6** |
| …by a proven-equal mapping with a written reason and no key of their own | **7** (6 spacing · 1 font weight) |
| Tailwind defaults deliberately neutralised | **17 rendered checks**, all green |
| bundle cost of Phase 0 in the app | **0 bytes — the production CSS is byte-identical**, `index-DSjCOfdd.css`, 125.25 kB, `sha256 6ab0e6ad…85f123ed`, built twice at one commit with nothing changed but the plugin line (see §11) |
| the theme's own floor, compiled with zero utilities used | **4.22 kB raw / 1.50 kB gzip** (Preflight + the `:root` block) |

The 4.22 kB is the number Phase 3 is judged against. The 0 bytes is the number that says
the PO's running build has not moved.

### 1 · TAILWIND v4, CONFIRMED — checked, not assumed

`tailwindcss@4.3.3` + `@tailwindcss/vite@4.3.3`. The one thing that could have forced v3
is the build chain: `@tailwindcss/vite` declares `peerDependencies { vite: "^5.2.0 || ^6
|| ^7 || ^8" }` and this app runs **Vite 5.4.21**, so v4 installs clean with no Vite
upgrade and no override. v4 is also the PO's attached file's first-class target
(`@import` + `@theme`), and `@theme` is what makes the token crossing a CSS-level fact
rather than a JS config object. **No reason to switch was found, so the v3 fallback
config in the PO's file is not used.**

### 2 · THE THEME KEEPS OUR TOKEN NAMES — `--color-text` is NOT renamed to `--color-ink`

The PO's attached file spells our ink colour `--color-ink`, and the CR-018 capture called
it *"one rename"*. **Rejected, with the figure:** `var(--color-text)` is written at **252
sites across 32 stylesheets** (measured 2026-08-19; the 76 tokens are read at **1,788**
sites in all). Route B ends with `tokens.css` deleted and the `@theme` block as the
single declaration of every token — so a key spelled `ink` kills all 252 of those sites
on the day that deletion happens, in a commit whose subject is "delete tokens.css" and
whose blast radius is the entire product.

So the rule for the whole theme is: **a token crosses under its own name wherever the
Tailwind namespace allows it.** The cost is that the utility reads `text-text` /
`bg-text` rather than `text-ink` — uglier in 3,020 markup sites, correct in the one
commit that matters.

Where a namespace prefix genuinely differs — Tailwind says `--leading-*` and
`--tracking-*`, we say `--line-height-*` and `--letter-spacing-*` — **both names are
emitted and the Tailwind one is written as `var(--our-name)`**. A derivation, not a
second literal (hard-won law 5). Six tokens are in that shape, and a test asserts they
stay derivations rather than hardening into copies.

### 3 · FIVE NAMESPACES ARE CLEARED, BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT ROUTE B WAS BOUGHT FOR

Route B was chosen to make a wrong style **unwritable**. That only holds if Tailwind's
own defaults cannot smuggle in a value the design system never ratified. So `@theme`
opens with `--color-*: initial`, `--text-*: initial`, `--radius-*: initial`,
`--shadow-*: initial`, `--font-*: initial`, and then declares ours.

**Clearing `--text-*` is B14 rules 5 and 20 enforced by the compiler**, and it is the
strongest thing in this file: `text-lg` on a table cell is 18px and breaks rule 20;
`text-base` on a button is 16px and is a third button size against rule 5. Neither
utility exists any more. Seventeen rendered checks assert that `bg-red-500`,
`bg-blue-500`, `text-lg`, `text-base`, `text-xs`, `font-sans` and `shadow-2xl` are inert.

**Not cleared, each for a stated reason:** `--leading-*`, `--tracking-*`,
`--font-weight-*`, `--breakpoint-*`, `--container-*`. **B14 ratifies no rule over any of
them, and clearing a namespace no rule governs is inventing law.** The breakpoint half of
that is a real gap and is raised as **OQ-274** rather than decided.

### 4 · `rounded-full` IS LEFT ALIVE, AND THAT IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE

Every radius key is re-declared as `0px` — all nine, not only the three we have — so a
`rounded-xl` typed in Phase 3 renders square rather than rendering nothing. The PO's
attached file does the same for seven keys, and its v3 block also zeroes `full`.

**We do not zero `rounded-full`, deliberately.** In v4 it is a static utility
(`calc(infinity * 1px)`), not a theme key, and it is **load-bearing**: the A12 service
dots are `border-radius: 50%` circles (`features/rating/PlansRates.css:137`), and three
more affordances elsewhere are the same shape. *"The system is square"* is a rule about
boxes and cards; it was never a rule about a 6px status dot. Zeroing it would have broken
a design element **while looking like compliance** — the exact shape hard-won law 1 warns
about. A rendered check asserts it is *not* 0px, and the specimen draws three dots.

### 5 · TWO KEYS THAT ARE NOT AMONG THE 76 — `--text-btn: 14px` and `--text-btn-sm: 12px`

**These are not new design decisions.** B14 rule 5 is RATIFIED — *"Two button sizes only
— default and small (12px). No inline font sizes."* — and the CR-016 conformance register
locks the pair at `["12px","14px"]`. Neither number has ever been a token: both live
inline in component CSS, which is what rule 5's second sentence forbids. Clearing
`--text-*` removes `text-sm`, so without these two keys a Phase 3 lane has no way to
write a conforming button except an arbitrary value nobody can grep for. Same move
`--table-font-size` and `--desc-measure` already made for rules 20 and 18.

Two more additions in the same category, both tokenising an existing literal rather than
choosing anything: **`--font-mono`** (`ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace`,
written bare in `features/ledger/finance.css:283` and `features/billing/billRun.css:210`
and declared nowhere — the `--table-font-size` / DEF-198 shape exactly), and
**`--container-measure`**, which is what makes rule 18's 80% reachable as `max-w-measure`
instead of 23 hand-written caps.

### 6 · `--font-heading-weight` GETS NO UTILITY, AND THE REASON IS A HARD TAILWIND COLLISION

A font-weight key would have to be spelled `--font-weight-heading`, whose utility class is
`font-heading` — **the exact class `--font-heading` (the font FAMILY) already owns.**
Tailwind resolves `font-heading` to the family, so the weight key would be permanently
unreachable: a theme entry that looks declared and does nothing, which is hard-won law 1
inside a config file.

So the value crosses two ways instead, both proved by rendering: as the
`--text-h1..h6--font-weight` modifiers (so `text-h2` alone reproduces `global.css`'s whole
h2 rule), and as `font-extrabold`, which is Tailwind's own `--font-weight-extrabold: 800`.
The test asserts 800 == 800 so a retune of one without the other goes RED.

### 7 · SPACING CROSSES ONTO TAILWIND'S MULTIPLIER RATHER THAN GETTING SIX KEYS

`--space-N` is N × 4px and v4's `--spacing: 0.25rem` makes `p-N` = N × 4px at the 16px
root this app runs at — nothing sets `html { font-size }`; `global.css` sets `body`, which
`rem` ignores. Declaring `--spacing-1..8` would be six second literals for numbers
Tailwind already has right. The raw `--space-N` names are still emitted so existing
`var(--space-N)` sites survive `tokens.css` being deleted. **This is the one that nearly
slipped — see §8.**

### 8 · THE PROOF IS A RENDERED PAGE, AND BREAKING IT FIRST IS WHAT MADE IT HONEST

`07-frontend/tailwind-specimen/` is a throwaway page — not in `src/`, not routed, the only
thing that imports the theme in this phase. For each token it paints one element with a
**Tailwind utility** and another with the **literal parsed out of `tokens.css` source
text**, then compares `getComputedStyle` on both. `tokens.css` is deliberately never
imported there: if both sheets declared `:root`, the comparison would be a variable
against itself.

Four values were sabotaged in the theme and the page rebuilt (hard-won law 7). **Three
were caught and one was not** — `--space-4: 16px → 17px` changed nothing, because `p-4`
comes from Tailwind's multiplier and not from our key, so the utility check walked past a
token that had drifted by a pixel. **A second section was written because of that
failure**: all 76 raw variables are read off `:root`, *used* through the same real
property their utility drives, and compared. Re-run: all four sabotages caught. The guard
has the shape it has because breaking it exposed the hole — it was not designed in.

Two further findings, both recorded in the page's own source because each will bite a
Phase 3 lane:

* **55 of 76 first reported `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`** — the classes had been built as
  `` `bg-${name}` `` and Tailwind generates only what its scanner can SEE in source. The
  theme was correct the whole time. Any interpolated class name in Phase 3 is this bug.
* **Lightning CSS resolves a static `color-mix()` at build time**, so the theme side
  spells `--color-divider` as `rgba(32, 30, 29, .4)` and the browser spells the literal
  side `color(srgb 0.12549 … / 0.4)`. Same colour, two spellings, four false FAILs. The
  page canonicalises colours to 8-bit RGBA rather than accepting them as different.

Final, exit 0 from `node tailwind-specimen/verify.mjs`: **utilities 76/76 · variables
76/76 · neutralised defaults 17/17**. A second, source-level guard — `tailwindTheme.test.ts`
— runs in `npm test` and was itself proved RED on five separate sabotages.

### 9 · WHAT PHASE 0 DID NOT DO, said plainly so nobody reads more into it

* **Nothing imports `tailwind.css`.** Importing it pulls in Preflight, which resets every
  base element and would restyle the whole product in one commit. Phase 1 adds the
  import, deliberately, with a walkthrough. The byte-identical bundle is the proof that
  this phase reaches no screen.
* **No `.tsx`, no existing `.css`, and no `main.tsx` import was touched.**
* **G31 is untouched and still load-bearing.** The Route B ruling says it must be retired
  deliberately when there are no bespoke classes left to refuse. There still are, so
  retiring it now would be a green gate measuring nothing — the failure that ruling
  itself names. It retires at the END of Phase 3.
* **The drift check is a vitest test, not a `10-scripts/gates/` gate, and that is
  deliberate.** The next free gate number is contested: another lane is registering
  `g34_rls_policy_guard` for DEF-333 and its registration was not yet on the branch.
  Editing the shared `run_gates.py` to claim a number is how two lanes collide in one
  working tree (hard-won law 11). `npm test` already runs, so the assertion landed where
  it will actually be executed.
* **`verify.mjs` is not wired into `run_gates.py` either.** It needs a browser and a built
  page. Claiming a gate the repo does not run is hard-won law 1; the script exits non-zero
  and is ready for Phase 1 to adopt.

### ⚠ 10 · THE PROCESS FAILURE IN THIS PHASE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT COST THE WHOLE FIRST BUILD

**Phase 0 was built once, completely, and lost — every file, before a single commit.** The
shared working tree was ~170 commits behind origin for the entire first run; it was then
brought up to date and the uncommitted work went with it, together with the scratchpad the
screenshots were in. Nothing was recoverable and the phase was rebuilt from scratch.

**Two lessons, and the second is the one that is not already written down.**

1. CLAUDE.md hard-won law 11 already says it: *"commit small and commit often. Work you
   have not committed is work any of six other lanes can erase."* The first run held eight
   files for its whole length and committed none of them. The rebuild committed in three
   pieces — build chain, theme, proof — each pushed and verified from HEAD before the next
   began.
2. **A stale working tree does not announce itself, and it silently poisons MEASUREMENTS,
   not just merges.** Every figure taken in the first run came from files 170 commits old.
   Three of them were wrong and would have been published as fact: `var(--color-text)` at
   *253 sites in 33 files* (really 252 in 32), the 76 tokens at *1,819* sites (really
   1,788), and the bare monospace literal attributed to `metering.css` and `PlansRates.css`
   when it actually lives in `features/ledger/finance.css:283` and
   `features/billing/billRun.css:210`. `tokens.css` itself was byte-identical between the
   stale tree and the tip, which is exactly why the error was invisible — the file the
   whole phase is about had not moved, so nothing felt stale. **Every figure in this row
   was re-measured against the current tip before it was written.**

### ⚠ 11 · HOW "ZERO BYTES" IS PROVED, AND THE WRONG WAY THAT WAS TRIED FIRST

The claim is that wiring Tailwind into Vite adds nothing to the running app. The first
attempt proved it by building the app, recording `125.21 kB / sha256 06c80632…`, adding
the plugin, building again and getting the same hash. **That proof does not survive a
shared working tree.** Re-run a few hours later it reported a DIFFERENT hash —
`index-DSjCOfdd.css`, 125.25 kB, `6ab0e6ad…` — and the cause was another lane's edit to
`features/tenancy/SignupWizard.css`, which has nothing whatever to do with Tailwind. Had
that been read the other way round it would have been recorded as a 45-byte Tailwind
regression, and the number would have been wrong in the direction that looks like
diligence.

**A bundle hash is a fact about the WHOLE TREE, not about one change.** So the proof is
done by holding the tree fixed: a `git worktree` at one commit, built twice, with nothing
different between the runs but the `tailwindcss()` line in `vite.config.ts`. Both builds
emit `index-DSjCOfdd.css` at 125.25 kB with sha256 `6ab0e6ad…85f123ed` — identical, and
the isolation is what makes it mean anything. A worktree is also the only way to look at
a different tree state without moving the shared one, which hard-won law 11 forbids
outright.

**The same shape as law 11's own history:** every mechanism recorded there is a check
that passed while measuring the wrong thing. This is that in a build artefact.

### What goes to the PO, in plain English with figures

1. *All 76 of your design tokens now exist as Tailwind utilities, and we proved it by
   drawing them on a page and measuring the pixels rather than by reading the config —
   76 out of 76 match, including awkward ones like the 40%-transparent divider grey.*
2. *We kept your existing token names instead of the ones in the file you sent. That file
   renames the text colour to "ink"; 252 places in our stylesheets say "text" and would
   all break the day we delete the old file. The trade is that the shorthand reads
   `text-text` rather than `text-ink`.*
3. *Tailwind ships about 250 colours and 13 text sizes of its own. We switched them all
   off, so nobody can accidentally use a blue we never chose or an 18px table row. That is
   your "two button sizes" and "one table size" rules enforced by the build instead of by
   review.*
4. *This adds zero bytes to the running app — the built CSS is byte-for-byte identical to
   before. Nothing you are looking at in the browser right now has moved.*
5. *One thing we will not decide for you: the Archivo font was never actually chosen by
   anyone — it was copied from the prototype and a comment claimed it had been decided. We
   carried it forward unchanged and raised it as OQ-272 rather than making it official by
   accident.*

**Raised, not decided:** OQ-272 (the Archivo webfont) · OQ-273 (four of the ten services
have no colour token) · OQ-274 (six ad-hoc breakpoints, no ratified set).

## 2026-08-19 · CR-016's OPEN DEFECTS ARE ABSORBED INTO CR-018 — with two pulled forward

**The PO's ruling, verbatim:** *"Lets fix all these defect using CR18 - we will do trailwind
change and in that we will take up all these issues"*.

### The reasoning behind it is sound and is recorded first

CR-018 Route B rewrites the markup of **every** component. A lane already inside
`TemplateDetail.tsx` replacing its class names is the cheapest possible moment to also fix
what that file renders. Fixing them separately means opening the same file twice, and the
second visit lands on markup the first visit rewrote. **The PO is right that these should
be one pass.**

### ⚠ THE CONCERN, STATED ONCE — TWO OF THE FOUR ARE NOT CSS DEFECTS

| Defect | What it actually is | Does Tailwind touch it? |
|---|---|---|
| **DEF-335** — BR-ids, `OQ-252`, `apps/customers` on the Templates screen | **backend Python strings** (`templates_api.py:670,679`) + a **gate allowlist** blind to them | **No.** Not one line of CSS. |
| **DEF-336** — every BILLING card shows no count | **data/wiring** — the tenant's own audit trail proves the rows exist | **No.** |
| **SET-08 Numbering vs r10** — a RESTART column r10 does not have, the intro split in two, `"Next number will be…"` vs `"Next: …"` | **markup + copy**, screen-shape | Partly — this belongs with the rewrite. |
| **Audit log** — raw uuids, `notification_template_version`, `code: staff_bulk_summary` | **presentation logic**, what the cell prints | Partly. |

**Coupling a live customer-facing bug to a multi-week migration means the bug ships when
the migration ships.** DEF-335 is prose a water utility is reading today; DEF-336 makes a
correctly-provisioned tenant look unconfigured. Neither improves by waiting, and neither
gets easier because the file's class names changed.

### THE STRUCTURE, which does what the PO asked without holding those two hostage

**CR-018 absorbs all four — the PO's ruling stands.** They are CR-018 work, tracked under
CR-018, closed by CR-018. What changes is only WHEN inside CR-018:

* **Phase 1 stays a SPIKE and is not touched.** It migrates one screen to produce a cost
  number. Loading defects onto it corrupts the measurement — the number would then include
  bug-fixing that the other 126 screens do not need, and Phase 3's estimate would be built
  on it.
* **Phase 1.5 — the two non-CSS defects, immediately, independent of Tailwind.** DEF-335
  (rewrite both backend strings; widen G28 from a named list to **every** string an
  endpoint serialises, ratcheted) and DEF-336 (the missing count). Neither touches a
  stylesheet, so neither can collide with any migration lane.
* **Phase 2+ — the r10 divergences, folded into each screen's migration**, exactly as the
  PO described: when a lane rewrites a screen's markup it fixes that screen's divergence
  from r10 in the same commit.

### The rule this sets for every remaining CR-018 phase

**A screen is not migrated until it matches r10.** Route B was bought to make an undeclared
class impossible; this ruling adds the second half — a screen whose markup is being rewritten
is compared against `05-prototype/r10-2026-08-16/SMARTBillHub.dc.html` in the same pass, and
divergences are fixed or filed, never silently carried into new markup.

**That is a real scope increase to CR-018 and it is stated rather than absorbed quietly.**
It also removes the separate CR-016 remediation lane, so the total work falls; what rises is
CR-018's own size and therefore its duration.
