## 2026-08-19 · DEF-335 — AN ALLOWLIST CANNOT FIND THE THING NOBODY THOUGHT TO LIST

**CR-018 Phase 1.5 · shipped in 2.29.1 · gate `g28_internal_references.py`**

### The finding

The PO photographed Settings → Configure → Templates on the deployed 2.28.0 build. It
told a water utility that the default variant *"is the row's KEY, not a flag on it
(BR-NOT-001/BR-NOT-006)"*, that a July letter *"would start claiming it was rendered from
a row that now says something else (BR-BIL-026)"*, that *"OQ-252 is with the Product
Owner"*, and that *"`apps/customers` publishes no such read"*.

**G28 reported ZERO violations the entire time.** It checked the eleven catalogues plus an
EXPLICIT LIST of served-prose fields, and `set_default_reason` / `language_selection_reason`
were not on the list. `SERVED_PROSE`'s own comment had predicted this in writing —
*"an explicit list only checks what somebody remembered to name"* — and the same shape is
recorded one register over as DEF-322, where the escape reason was written down and the
lesson was never generalised.

### The ruling, and it is about gate SHAPE rather than about two strings

**A check whose coverage is a list of remembered items is not a check; it is a record of
what somebody once noticed.** So Part 2b inverts G28: every string value in every response
dict the **25 API modules** build is swept, and the exemptions are a **denylist of machine
fields** — `br_ref`, `message_key`, `code`, `field`, plus the `_id`/`_key`/`_code`/`_ref`/
`_route`/`_url` naming convention this codebase already uses, and a value that is nothing
but a bare id.

### The worked figures

| | |
|---|---|
| what the allowlist found, with the text on screen | **0** |
| what the denylist finds | **29** |
| fixed in this commit | **2** (the two the PO photographed) |
| baselined, ratcheted, may only fall | **27** — `10-scripts/gates/g28_served_dict_baseline.txt` |
| API modules swept | **25** |

The baseline is keyed on `file :: field :: text`, **never on a line number**: a ratchet
whose file churns whenever something above a violation is edited is a ratchet nobody
reads. Three of the first 27 also had to be `rstrip()`ed after truncation, because a
violation whose 110th character was a space never matched its own baselined line and
reported FRESH on every run — a gate failing on text nobody changed.

### The two strings, before and after

**`set_default_reason`**

> BEFORE — *"The default variant is the one whose consumer category and language are both
> "default" (BR-NOT-001/BR-NOT-006) — it is the row's KEY, not a flag on it. Making another
> variant the default would re-key it, and every message already sent holds (template,
> version, language) forever (BR-BIL-026), so a July letter would start claiming it was
> rendered from a row that now says something else. OQ-252 is with the Product Owner."*

> AFTER — *"You cannot change which variant is the default yet. Messages already sent must
> keep the exact wording they used."*

**`language_selection_reason`**

> BEFORE — *"A variant carries a language tag and resolution records which language it
> actually used (BR-NOT-006). Nothing today stores a customer's preferred language —
> `apps/customers` publishes no such read — so a language variant created here is never
> selected for anybody yet. OQ-254."*

> AFTER — *"Nothing stores a customer's preferred language yet. A language variant you add
> here is never chosen automatically."*

Both are inside the ruled copy bar — **12 words a sentence, 2 sentences** (G33). **The
absence is still STATED**: hard-won law 1 is about the repo being honest, not about hiding
a limitation from a utility. Only the PROVENANCE moved, onto `set_default_br_ref` /
`language_selection_br_ref` and out to `data-br-ref` on the paragraph, which is the pattern
`billing/templates_service.py` already set — support reads it off the DOM, a clerk never
does.

### Proved RED first, both ways (hard-won law 7)

1. Run against the file **as deployed**, Part 2b named both fields. Run against the
   rewritten file it names neither. The allowlist reported 0 on both.
2. **And proved SILENT on machine fields**, which matters more, because a false positive is
   how a gate gets switched off (DEF-323). Over a probe dict of eight keys — `br_ref`,
   `set_default_br_ref`, `message_key`, `code`, `write_route`, `report_key`, a clean
   `detail`, and one leaking sentence — exactly **one of eight** is flagged, and it is the
   only one a clerk should never read. `set_default_br_ref` is the field this very fix
   ADDS: a gate that flagged it would be refusing its own remedy.

### The test that protected the string

`test_cr_007_template_catalog.py` asserted `"OQ-252" in detail.data["set_default_reason"]`.
**A test written beside the string pins the string** — the internal sentence was not merely
unchecked, it was a REQUIREMENT. It is inverted: the reason must contain no id, and the
`*_br_ref` field must.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-018 PHASE 1 — ONE SCREEN MIGRATED, AND WHAT IT COST

**The ruling this builds under is `"Route B"`** (PO, 2026-08-19, recorded above).
Phase 1 is the spike CR-018 §6 asks for: *"A spike on ONE screen first, measured,
before the other 126 — so the real cost per screen is a measured number and not
this CR's estimate."* **Version 2.29.4.** Everything below is a judgment the
ruling did not make, written down before it was reported (hard-won law 9/10).

### 0 · THE ANSWER, SO NOBODY HAS TO READ THE REST TO GET IT

**One screen took 2 h 10 min of wall clock and 133 changed lines. Six of those
minutes were the screen.** The rest was three things nobody had costed: proving
the import does not move the product, finding out that a merge-blocking gate
goes red on a correct migration, and discovering that Tailwind's readable way of
writing a translucent colour is not the colour we had.

| | |
|---|---|
| screen | `features/rating/RateSchedulesTab.tsx` — its own `<table>` ×2, a card grid, a search input, a pager, an interpolated class name |
| classes it referenced | **23** |
| …migrated to utilities | **13 (57%)** — every one single-use, confirmed by grep over `src/`, `e2e/` and `05-prototype/` |
| …left exactly as they were | **10 (43%)** — shared with other components; Phase 2 by the ruling |
| CSS deleted | **87 lines** from `PlansRates.css` (509 → 423) |
| markup changed | **15 `className` sites** rewritten (2 of them now share one constant), +89/−15 lines on the file, of which a 46-line header explains the three traps |
| utilities written | **36 distinct** |
| **visual difference** | **ZERO.** 0 differing computed values across 237 elements; the full-page PNG is **byte-identical** |
| CR-016 conformance | **every baseline number holds**, 24 screens, unchanged |
| gate stack | **24 PASS / 10 FAIL before and after** — identical; the 10 are other lanes' |

### 1 · THE EXTRAPOLATION, AND WHY THE PER-SCREEN NUMBER IS THE WRONG ONE TO MULTIPLY

At this rate 126 more screens is **≈13 hours of screen work** — and that figure is
misleading in both directions, so both are stated.

**It is too LOW,** for three reasons that are structural rather than incidental:
1. **This screen could only be 57% migrated.** 10 of its 23 classes are shared and
   are blocked on Phase 2. The 43% left behind is the highest of the five
   candidates measured, so a screen with fewer shared classes migrates *further*
   per visit but the total does not shrink — the shared classes are simply
   counted in Phase 2 instead.
2. **Nothing here touched a responsive rule.** The screen has no media query.
   The other 126 collectively carry six ad-hoc breakpoints (OQ-274, still open)
   and every one of them must land on a Tailwind variant.
3. **No `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `::before`, `:disabled` or `:nth-child` was
   migrated.** `.rating-link:hover` and the six `.rating-tag.svc-*::before` dots
   were all in the SHARED set and were left alone. Route B expresses those as
   `hover:` / `before:` variants, and none of that was exercised.

**It is too HIGH** for one reason, and it is the one that matters for sizing
Phase 3: the three expensive things in this phase were **one-time**. The import
decision, the cascade-layer decision, the gate handover and the colour-space
finding are paid once. The 13 class deletions and 15 markup rewrites — the part
that actually recurs — took **six minutes**.

**So the honest sizing is: ~30 min/screen of mechanical work, ~63 hours for 126,
PLUS a Phase 2 for the 179 shared classes that this spike could not touch and
did not measure.** The CR's own estimate of 3,020 rewrite sites is not
contradicted; what is new is that a rewrite site is cheap and the *decisions
around* the rewrite sites are not.

### 2 · PREFLIGHT IS NOT IMPORTED, AND THAT DECISION WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED

`@import "tailwindcss"` is three sheets: theme, **preflight**, utilities. Phase 0
warned that importing it "would restyle the whole product in one commit". Phase 1
did import it, once, on purpose, and photographed the result:

| | |
|---|---|
| computed property values moved on ONE screen | **684** |
| `<h1>` | **30px → 15px**, margin `20.1px 0` → `0` |
| border values `0px none` → `0px solid` | 654 (inert at 0px width, but every number moves) |
| `<option>` padding | `0 2px 1px` → `0` |

**The h1 is the whole product**, because the shared `PageHeader` draws it on
every screen. `global.css:21` gives `h1..h6` a family, a weight, a line-height
and a tracking and **no font-size** — the size has always come from the browser's
own stylesheet, which is exactly what Preflight exists to delete. **No gate in
this repo reads rendered output, so this would have shipped green** (hard-won
law 6), and it is the second time in two phases that the only thing that caught
a whole-product defect was a screenshot.

**So Preflight lands at the END of Phase 3**, in its own commit, when
`tokens.css` and the 40 component stylesheets are gone. **And it cannot land
until someone says what a heading is** — raised as **OQ-275**, because the
product renders h1 at 30px and the design tokens say 42px, and those seven type
tokens have never been rendered by anything.

### 3 · THE UTILITIES ARE IMPORTED UNLAYERED, WHICH IS NOT TAILWIND'S OWN RECIPE

Tailwind puts utilities in `@layer utilities`. **A cascade layer always loses to
unlayered CSS, whatever the specificity** — and 40 unlayered legacy stylesheets
are still in the bundle for the whole of Phases 1–3.

Concretely, on this screen: the rate card is `class="card rating-rate-card"`,
`.card` sets `padding: 28px` (StateFrame.css:114) and `.rating-rate-card`
overrode it to 16px. Delete the second and write `p-4`, and a **layered** `p-4`
loses to unlayered `.card` — the card silently grows 12px of padding on every
side, on a migration that reads perfectly correct in the diff.

Unlayered, a utility (0,1,0) meets a legacy rule (0,1,0) and **source order
decides**, so `src/styles/tailwind.css` must be the last stylesheet in the
bundle. Verified in the built CSS: utilities start at byte 130,615 of 141,605,
behind every legacy sheet. `main.tsx` imports it below `@/App` for that reason
and a test asserts the order. **When the last legacy stylesheet is deleted,
restore `layer(utilities)`** — written in the file, not remembered.

### 4 · G31 GOES RED AT THE START OF THIS MIGRATION, NOT AT THE END — THE CR HAD IT INVERTED

CR-018 §4.3 and the Route B ruling both say G31 "becomes meaningless" when there
are no bespoke classes left, and is retired at the END of Phase 3. **Measured:
it went `0 → 25` on component 1 of 127**, because a utility is declared by the
COMPILER and no `.css` file will ever contain `.flex`.

Lowering the ratchet was refused: it would blind the gate to the other 126
components and re-open DEF-327, a defect that recurred six times in five months
and took eight screens down. So the migrated files are named in
`07-frontend/src/styles/route-b-migrated.txt` — **one list, two readers** — and
handed to `src/styles/routeBUtilities.test.ts`, which asks the **stricter**
question because it can reach the real Tailwind compiler: *declared by a
stylesheet **or** generates a real rule*. `itmes-end` fails there; it would have
passed G31's rule the moment a file was migrated. G31 keeps its exact rule, its
ratchet of 0 and its jurisdiction over the other 126.

**It runs in `npm test` and that is forced, not preferred:** `gates.yml`
installs Python and nothing else — no node, no `npm ci` — so a Python gate can
never ask Tailwind anything. `ci-frontend.yml` runs `npm ci` then `npm test`.
The cost is a second implementation of G31's class-name reader in a second
language with nothing keeping the two in step: **OQ-277**, raised rather than
absorbed.

Six sabotages, six caught, before any of it was trusted green (hard-won law 7):
a typo'd utility · a cleared-namespace utility (`text-lg`) · the `.svc-*` rules
deleted · the owning check deleted · a ledger entry naming a phantom file · a
bogus class in an unmigrated file.

### 5 · `text-text/70` IS NOT `color-mix(in srgb, …)`, AND THE APP WRITES THAT 243 TIMES

Tailwind's `/opacity` modifier is the readable idiom and it emits
**`color-mix(in OKLAB, …)`** behind an `@supports` test every current browser
passes. First measurement of the migrated screen: **30 elements changed their
computed colour** from `color(srgb 0.12549 0.117647 0.113725 / 0.65)` to
`oklab(0.236859 0.00240637 0.00271879 / 0.65)`.

Both round to `rgb(32,30,29)` and **not one pixel moved** — on this screen, on
this near-black ink. The app writes `color-mix(in srgb` at **243 sites across 30
stylesheets**, many on saturated accent reds where the two spaces do **not**
agree. A migration that silently changes colour space on all 243 is not the
"renders identically" CR-018 §6 requires, so the space is spelled out long-hand:
`text-[color-mix(in_srgb,var(--color-text)_70%,transparent)]`. It is uglier, it
is exact, and **it is the single biggest readability cost Route B pays** in this
codebase.

### 6 · 7,824 BYTES OF PHASE 0's THROWAWAY PROOF PAGE WERE BEING SHIPPED TO CUSTOMERS

`tailwind-specimen/README.md` says the proof page is *"not in `src/`, not routed,
not shipped"*. It was true while nothing imported the theme. The moment Phase 1
imported it, Tailwind v4's automatic source detection — which walks the **project
directory**, not `src/` — generated a rule for every utility-shaped token it
found, and **48 of the 148 rules came from `tailwind-specimen/specimen.js`
alone**. Measured at one commit:

| | bytes of utilities | rules |
|---|---|---|
| auto-detected sources | **16,569** | 148 |
| `source(none)` + `@source "../"` | **8,745** | 75 |

**7,824 raw bytes on every page load, for one line.** Caught before it shipped,
so it is recorded here rather than in the defect register. What is left is still
partly noise — `p-101`, `p-420` and `p-11800` are generated from bare NUMBERS in
our own source text — and that is a Phase 3 tuning problem, written into
`tailwind.css` so it is tuned rather than rediscovered.

**And Phase 0's 4.22 kB floor is not the app's floor.** 4.22 kB was measured in
the specimen's own build, which scans one directory and includes Preflight. The
app's floor — Tailwind imported, `source(none)`, zero screens migrated — is
**6,388 bytes of utilities across 37 rules**, and every one of those 37 is
generated from a string that already existed in our source before Route B began.
The two tables above are measured at the migrated state (C) and differ only in
the source configuration, so the 7,824-byte saving is the like-for-like figure.

### 7 · THE BUNDLE, ALL THREE NUMBERS AT ONE COMMIT IN AN ISOLATED WORKTREE

A bundle hash is a fact about the whole tree and six lanes are committing, so
this was measured the way Phase 0's README insists — one commit, one worktree,
nothing changed but the files under test.

| state | raw | gzip |
|---|---|---|
| A · the app before CR-018 | 125,258 | 18,687 |
| B · Tailwind imported, **nothing** migrated | 141,826 | 21,513 |
| B′ · same, after `source(none)` + `@source "../"` | **131,646** | **20,219** |
| C · one screen migrated | **132,582** | **20,357** |

**+7,324 raw / +1,670 gzip for the whole of Phase 1.** Split it and the shape is
the argument for continuing: **6,388 of those bytes are the one-time floor** (B′
minus A — Tailwind present, 37 rules, zero screens migrated), and **the first
migrated screen costs 936 raw / 138 gzip on top of it**, against **87 lines of
stylesheet deleted**. Phase 3 should end SMALLER than the 125,258 it started at:
the floor is paid once and 9,284 lines of stylesheet leave.

Cross-check that the method is sound: state A reproduced Phase 0's recorded
byte-identical baseline exactly — `index-DSjCOfdd.css`, 125.25 kB.

### 8 · WHAT THIS SPIKE DID NOT COVER, so nobody reads the number as covering it

* **No media query, no responsive variant** — the screen has none (OQ-274 open).
* **No pseudo-class or pseudo-element migrated.** `:hover`, `:focus-visible`,
  `:disabled` and the six `::before` service dots were all in the SHARED set.
* **No shared class migrated at all** — 10 of 23, and they are the ruling's own
  Phase 2.
* **No `@keyframes`, no `transition`, no `z-index` stack, no `position` context.**
* **No dark mode, no print sheet** — the app has neither.
* **The interpolated class `svc-${card.service}` CANNOT become a utility** and
  this is a hard limit, not a deferral: Tailwind generates only what its scanner
  can see. `routeBUtilities.test.ts` asserts the six `.svc-*` rules stay
  declared, so a Phase 2 lane cannot delete them and take six service dots down
  with every check green.

### 9 · WHAT BROKE, AND WHAT NEARLY DID

1. **Preflight, caught by a screenshot** — §2. Nothing else could have seen it.
2. **The cascade layer, caught by reading the CSS rather than trusting the
   recipe** — §3. It had not failed yet; it would have, on the card's padding.
3. **G31 red on a correct migration** — §4. The CR expected this at the end.
4. **The colour space, caught by the computed-style census** — §5. The PNG was
   byte-identical; a screenshot-only check would have passed it.
5. **The specimen in the customer's bundle** — §6. Caught by asking where 16 kB
   came from instead of accepting a plausible number.
6. **A phantom 49-pixel diff that was another lane's version string.** The first
   before/after pair was taken 25 minutes apart and a second lane bumped
   `package.json` 2.29.0 → 2.29.1 in between, so the sidebar version label
   changed under the comparison. **Six pixels of a single glyph nearly read as a
   migration regression.** The fix is the one the brief already required and the
   reason it required it: the final A/B was taken in a `git worktree` at ONE
   commit, where the only difference is the files under test.
7. **⚠ THE VERSION BUMP WAS ONE COMMIT AWAY FROM REVERTING ANOTHER LANE'S
   RELEASE NOTE, AND IT IS THE STALE-BASE HALF OF HARD-WON LAW 11.** This lane
   read `pyproject.toml` at 2.29.1 and wrote 2.29.2 into it. In the forty
   minutes between, the DEF-336 lane shipped **2.29.3** — and its note said, in
   as many words, that it was *skipping 2.29.2 because the CR-018 Phase 1 lane
   is holding it in the shared working tree.* Committing the edited copy would
   have deleted that whole paragraph and moved the product version **backwards**,
   in a commit naming exactly the two files it meant to name, with a correct file
   count and the author's own change present in HEAD. **Both published checks in
   law 11 pass on it.** What caught it was `git diff --numstat` against the
   REMOTE TIP showing **19 deletions in a file this lane only added to** — a
   deletion count where none was intended. Both files were then rebuilt from
   `git show <tip>:<path>` rather than from the copy on disk, and the version
   taken is **2.29.4**, because 2.29.2 is now behind the shipped build and a
   defect reported against it could mean either. Two skipped numbers cost
   nothing; a duplicated one costs the ability to say which build a defect was
   seen on, which is the whole of change process §7.
8. **A gap this phase found and did not create: `CHANGELOG.md` has no entry for
   2.29.0, 2.29.1 or 2.29.3.** Change process §7 rule 4 says a gate refuses a
   version bump with no changelog entry, and there is no such gate. Three
   releases shipped without one on the same day. Recorded here rather than
   fixed, because writing another lane's release note is guessing what they
   shipped — but the missing gate is real and belongs to whoever writes it.

### 10 · THE RECOMMENDATION, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE A SPIKE THAT ONLY CONFIRMS THE PLAN WAS NOT A SPIKE

**Route B works, the safety net holds, and it is more expensive than CR-018
estimated — but not in the place the CR was looking.** The 3,020 rewrite sites
are the cheap part. The expensive parts are four decisions the CR did not know
existed (Preflight, cascade layers, the gate handover, the colour space), three
of which are now paid once and written down, and **a Phase 2 for 179 shared
classes that this spike proved it cannot touch from a single component.**

**The one thing that should change before Phase 2 starts:** OQ-275 and OQ-276
are not decoration. Without a heading scale Preflight can never land, and
without a small-text scale Phases 2–3 will write ~287 arbitrary font sizes that
nobody can grep as a set — which is B14 rule 5's second sentence broken in a new
place rather than enforced by construction, and enforcement by construction is
the entire reason Route B was chosen over Route A.

## 2026-08-19 · DEF-336 — THE BADGE HAD TWO STATES AND THE SCREEN NEEDED THREE

**CR-018 Phase 1.5 · ships in 2.29.3 · SET-04 Settings → Configure → Reference data**

### What the PO saw

The BILLING section — *Billing defaults*, *Budget billing rules*, *Document & message
templates* — drew a bare chevron and no number, while READS showed **5** and PAYMENTS
showed **7**. Beside WORK's honest *"Not set up yet"*, that reads as missing configuration
to the one person who can act on it.

### The root cause, and it is not a lost row

The seeding happened and the counts are live — `uoms: 26`, `charge_codes: 23`,
`payment_methods: 7`, `read_methods: 5`, and 21 cards in total. **Two separate things
dropped them at the last step, and neither is in the data.**

1. **`ReferenceCardTile` read the count only for `kind: "list"`** —
   `card.kind !== "list" ? "›" : …`. So `custom_fields`, which `GET /lookups` has always
   counted, threw a real number away *before looking at it*. **Measured in a browser
   against the deployed build: the server sent 21 counts and 20 reached a badge.**
2. **Everything that is not a list collapsed into `"›"`, with no words at all.** A card
   that holds SETTINGS and a card nobody has set up rendered identically. A blank says
   nothing, and a person reads nothing as *"nothing here"*.

And one blind spot behind both: `lookup_cards()` walked `LOOKUP_LISTS` itself and
`continue`d past any list with no handler — so a list whose rows **provably exist** and
cannot be counted live was dropped from the grid entirely. The report has had a name for
that case since DEF-026 (`uncounted`) and the grid never rendered it.

### The ruling — three states, and the third one is the fix

| the state | what a person reads | when |
|---|---|---|
| a number | `26 ›` | the server counted it — **whatever the card's kind is** |
| not set up | *"Not set up yet"* | a list card with no rows |
| not countable | *"Settings ›"* / *"Opens ›"*, reason on the control | no list to count |
| set up, uncountable here | *"Set up ›"* | DEF-026's `uncounted` — the rows exist |

**No fourth state was minted.** The grid endpoint is built from `reference_data_report()`
now, so the screen and the seeder read the *same sentence about the same list*. The
report's `reason` text is deliberately **not** served — it names `apps.<module>`,
`register_lookup_handler` and BR-TEN-031, which is internal provenance (G28, and DEF-335
one commit earlier). The screen writes its own sentence, in all eleven catalogues.

### Two tests were protecting the defect

* `e2e/CR-010-seed-completeness.spec.ts` asserted `toHaveText("›")` for seven cards —
  **it pinned the bare chevron as a requirement.**
* The same file filed *Custom fields* under `CONFIG_PANELS`, i.e. as a card that counts
  nothing. It counts; the tile was discarding the number. The breakdown is now
  20 seeded lists + 6 panels + Custom fields (counted, 0 on this tenant) + 4 Work cards.

This is the second time in two commits that **a test written beside a behaviour pinned the
behaviour** (DEF-335's was `"OQ-252" in set_default_reason`). Worth stating as a pattern:
a check written from what the screen DOES, rather than from what a person NEEDS, protects
the defect.

### Proved in a browser, both ways (hard-won law 6 and 7)

`e2e/DEF-336-reference-counts.spec.ts` reads **both ends** — `GET /lookups` through the
page's own session, and the rendered `.lookup-card` badges — and fails when they disagree.
Against the 2.29.1 build serving the defect it went **RED**, naming the missing count:

```
every count the server took is drawn, and no badge invents one
  - Expected  - 1   Array [ 0, 0, 4, 4, 5, … ]
  + Received  + 0   Array [ 0,    4, 4, 5, … ]
```

Against the fixed build it passes, and the assertion the brief asked for is in it: **a card
whose list is non-empty and whose badge carries no digits is red.** Nothing asserted that
before, which is DEF-336's escape reason in one sentence.

## 2026-08-19 · THE TYPE SCALE IS RULED — OQ-275 and OQ-276 CLOSED

**Source:** the PO put both open questions to Claude Design and returned its answer. The
**scale below is adopted as ruled**, because r10 is the design authority and this scale is
r10's own usage named rather than invented.

### The ruled scale

| Heading role | Token | Size | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| marketing / signup hero | `--text-display` | **56px** | public pages |
| full-page wizard title | `--text-h1` | **40px** | wizards |
| page-head title — **the app default** | `--text-h2` | **32px** | every screen head |
| | `--text-h3` | 25px | |
| | `--text-h4` | 20px | |
| | `--text-h5` | 16px | |

| Small-text role | Token | Size |
|---|---|---|
| pill labels, kickers, table meta | `--text-xs` | **11px** |
| dense table body, captions | `--text-sm` | **12px** |
| panel body, form labels | `--text-base` | **13px** |
| emphasised body | `--text-md` | **14px** |
| body default | `--text-body` | **15px** |

Two rulings carried with it: **9px is below the readability floor** in `UI-RULES.md` and is
re-pointed at `--text-xs`, never tokenised; and the **half-steps are absorbed, not given
tokens** — 10.5 / 11.5 / 12.5 / 13.5 are hand-nudges, and each is a per-site judgement call.

### ⚠ THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS FOR PLANNING: the analysis measured r10, not our app

Claude Design read `05-prototype/.../styles.css`. Both open questions were written about
`07-frontend`. **The two are materially different, and taking r10's figures as ours would
have sized this work at roughly four times reality.** Measured on our tree at `6ee285c`:

| | r10 (as analysed) | **our React app** |
|---|---|---|
| `--text-*` tokens declared | **zero** | **seven** — including `--text-h1` |
| `font-size:Npx` declarations | 1,361 | **347** |
| in the 9–13.5px band | 974 | **302** |
| at 11 / 12 / 13px | 845 | **287** |
| declarations that are inline | most of them | **none** — we have no inline styles and no `<style>` block |

So three of Claude Design's four premises are **true of r10 and false of our app**:

* *"There is no `--text-h1` token"* — we declare seven, `--text-h1: 42px` among them.
* *"h1 base is 42px, not 30px"* — in r10, yes. **In our app no `h1` renders at 42px at all**:
  every page head resolves to `var(--text-h2)` (32px), which is exactly the role the ruling
  names as the app default. `--text-h1` has **one** caller, the pricing hero.
* *"1,361 declarations, mostly inline"* — ours is 347, none inline.

**The lane's OQ-276 figure of 287 was measured against our app and is correct.** It was not
too low; it was counting a different codebase from the answer.

### What our app therefore needs — the actual work

1. **Add `--text-display: 56px`.** We have no token for the hero role, and our single
   `--text-h1` caller is the pricing hero, which by the ruling is `display`, not `h1`.
2. **Correct `--text-h1` from 42px to 40px.** Safe by inspection: after (1) it has no callers.
3. **Add the five small-text tokens.** `--text-body: 15px` already exists and is unchanged.
4. **Reconcile `--text-h6: 13px`**, which predates the ruling and collides with
   `--text-base: 13px`. One of the two names must go; the ruling names `base`.
5. **Re-point the one 9px and the seven 10px declarations**, and absorb the seven half-steps.
6. **Then replace 302 literals with token references** — Phase 2/3 work, per screen.

### ⚠ THE FRAMING POINT, ADOPTED AND SHARPENED

Claude Design's closing sentence is the most valuable thing in the answer and is ruled law:

> *"a token scale alone doesn't enforce B14 — it makes enforcement possible. The rule only
> bites once the inline font-size declarations are replaced by token references and a lint
> rule rejects new literals."*

**Route B is what turns that from a lint rule into an impossibility.** Phase 0 already
cleared the `--text-*` namespace in the Tailwind theme, so under Route B a utility can only
emit a size the theme declares — there is no syntax for an arbitrary literal to survive.
**That closes B14 rule 5 by construction rather than by review**, which is the whole reason
the PO chose Route B over Route A. Until the literals are replaced, the scale sits unused
beside them and the rule does not bite — exactly as the answer warns.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-018 PHASE 2 — THE RULED SCALE IS IN THE CODE, AND 328 LITERALS NOW READ IT

**Ships in 2.29.5 · closes OQ-275 and OQ-276 · raises OQ-278 · files DEF-339**

The scale ruled earlier today (this log, "THE TYPE SCALE IS RULED", commit
`4b6baa6`) was law with no code under it. This is the code. **Nothing here is a
new decision** — every figure is the ruling's, and the only judgements made were
the per-site ones the ruling explicitly delegated.

### What moved, in pixels, measured rather than argued

A census read `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-family`, `line-height`,
`letter-spacing` and `text-transform` for **every element on 25 screens — 11,089
elements** — once at the tip before any change and once after, in a browser, on
the built bundle. **This is the complete list of pixels that moved:**

| elements | before → after | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| 62 | **10px → 11px** | the seven 10px rules — pills, kickers, table meta |
| 8 | **9px → 11px** | `.table-sort-arrow`, on eight tables |
| 5 | **12.5px → 12px** | `.co-desc`, a card description |
| 1 | **42px → 56px** | the pricing hero |
| 1 | **10.5px → 11px** | `.screen-id-tag` |

**Seventy-seven elements, and every one of them is a movement the ruling asked
for.** Nothing else changed size, weight, family, leading or tracking anywhere in
the product. The line-height and letter-spacing rows in the raw diff are the same
77 elements' relative units following their own font size, not separate changes.
Full-page screenshots of the pricing page and three dense app screens back it up:
the three app screens are pixel-identical outside three bands — the sidebar
version label, the sort arrows, the screen-id tag — at **0.018 % / 0.040 % /
0.029 %** of their pixels.

CR-016's conformance register holds every one of its numbers across all 24
screens, unchanged, before and after.

### The count, measured on OUR app and not on r10

| | |
|---|---|
| `font-size:Npx` occurrences, the ruling's own grep | **347** |
| … of which are real declarations in a rule | **341** (4 are custom-property declarations, 2 are inside comments) |
| … plus one nobody had counted | `0.8125rem` — the only non-px font size in the product, resolving to 13px |
| **real declarations, total** | **342** |
| now token references | **328** |
| still literals | **14**, each carrying an `OQ-278` comment |

### The judgements the ruling delegated, one line each

**The 9px** — `.table-sort-arrow`, the only one in the product → `--text-xs`.
Below r10's readability floor, so re-pointed and never tokenised, exactly as
ruled.

**The seven 10px** — all seven are the same role and all seven → `--text-xs`:
`.kpi .k`, `.sidebar-version`, `.bell-badge`, `.modal-kicker`,
`.cell-money-basis`, `.rcw-consequence-tag`, `.rd-outcome-sev`. One of them is
worth naming: `.modal-kicker` was the ONE kicker in the product not at r10's
11px, so the re-point makes the modal head agree with every `PageHeader` kicker.

**The seven half-step occurrences — four real rules, and the three that are not
are the point.**

| site | was | now | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.screen-id-tag` | 10.5px | `--text-xs` | a corner pill; xs is the pill tier |
| `.rcw-preview` | 12.5px | `--text-base` (13) | **UP**: panel body, and `.rcw-radio` directly above it in the same wizard step is already 13px |
| `.co-desc` | 12.5px | `--text-sm` (12) | **DOWN**: a card description is `sm`'s ruled role ("captions"), and `.co-title` above it is 13px |
| `.bil-standing` | 13.5px | `--text-md` (14) | its own comment says it is the sentence an approver signs; `md` is "emphasised body" |
| r10 quotation in `ScreenIdTag.css` | 10.5px | unchanged | a CITATION of the design authority, not our code. The divergence is stamped beside it |
| `--table-font-size` | 13.5px | **unchanged** | B14 rule 20's RATIFIED figure, asserted by CR-016 across 24 screens. A half-step is a hand-nudge; a ratified figure is law, and they look identical in a grep |
| its mirror in `@theme` | 13.5px | **unchanged** | same |

**Two 12.5px sites, two different answers.** That is the whole reason the ruling
made these per-site judgements instead of a rounding rule.

### Three decisions this lane made that the ruling did not cover

1. **`--text-h6` is retired, not kept.** It was 13px — a second name for
   `--text-base`'s step — and the ruling names `base`. All ten callers are card
   and panel titles, not a sixth heading level. No pixel moved.
2. **B14 rule 5's buttons do not read the body scale.** Twelve declarations style
   a real `<button>` at 12px or 14px. Those two figures are ratified by rule 5
   and asserted by CR-016 at `["12px","14px"]`; they are not `--text-sm` and
   `--text-md` that happen to share their values. So `--text-btn: 14px` and
   `--text-btn-sm: 12px`, which the `@theme` block has carried since Phase 0,
   are declared in `tokens.css` too — a stylesheet cannot reach a theme-only key,
   and without a name the only thing it can write is the literal rule 5's own
   second sentence forbids. **Worked figure: retune `--text-md` to 15px and, if
   buttons aliased it, every default button in the product changes size on 24
   screens. They do not.**
3. **The heading steps are only pointed at real headings.** `--text-h1..h5`
   carry weight, leading and tracking as Tailwind v4 modifiers, so `text-h5` on a
   CONTROL would silently make it extrabold in Phase 3. Two heading elements
   crossed (`.pay-result-head h3` → h5, `.rd-drawer-head h2` → h4); the two
   controls at the same 16px did not, and are in OQ-278.

### What this does NOT enforce, stated plainly

**A scale beside 14 unreplaced literals does not bite, and neither does a scale
beside 328 replaced ones.** Nothing in this repo stops the next lane writing
`font-size: 17px` in a stylesheet — there is no lint rule, and no gate reads a
`.css` file for font sizes. What IS enforced today, and only this:

* the twelve steps are pinned on one line in `tailwindTheme.test.ts`, so a
  retune is a visible diff and a stray key is red;
* `tokens.css` and the `@theme` block cannot drift apart, token by token;
* `text-xs/sm/base/md/display` must emit the RULED px through the real Tailwind
  compiler — proved RED by setting `--text-base: 1rem`, which the first draft of
  that test PASSED;
* CR-016's register holds the rendered figures on 24 screens.

**The rule bites when Route B reaches the markup**, because Phase 0 cleared the
`--text-*` namespace and a utility can only emit a size the theme declares —
there is no syntax for an arbitrary literal. Until then the scale is a
convention that the code follows and nothing forces. That is the ruling's own
closing sentence, unchanged by anything measured here.

### Raised rather than guessed

**OQ-278** — fourteen sizes that are not on the scale: 18/22/24/26/30px sitting
BETWEEN the ruled steps, 40px on a money figure whose value equals `--text-h1`
but whose role is not "wizard title", and two controls wearing `--text-h5`'s
16px. Absorbing 24→25 or 30→32 moves pixels on nine screens and the ruling said
nothing about this tier. Every one carries an `OQ-278` comment in its own file:
`grep -rn OQ-278 07-frontend/src` returns exactly 14.

**DEF-339** — `npm run lint` was RED on this branch before this lane started:
`tailwindTheme.test.ts` read `global.css` into a variable nothing used. It was
read for a check nobody wrote — that `global.css`'s `h1..h6` rule sets NO
font-size, which is the entire reason Preflight is a whole-product change and is
stated in three comments and asserted nowhere. The check is now written.

## 2026-08-19 · OQ-278 RULED — three metric tokens, and a metric is not a heading

**Source:** the PO put OQ-278 to Claude Design and returned its answer. **The scale is
adopted**; r10 is the design authority and these are r10's own metric sizes named.

| Token | Size | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `--text-metric-sm` | **22px** | |
| `--text-metric` | **26px** | KPI value — the app default for this role |
| `--text-metric-lg` | **32px** | |

The insight being bought is that **a metric is a distinct role from a heading**. KPI values
and wizard step numbers are large type that is not a title, and giving them heading tokens
is what produced the drift in the first place.

### ⚠ THE VOLUMES ARE r10's, NOT OURS — THIRD OCCURRENCE, NOW A STANDING RULE

| ≥16px | r10 (as analysed) | **our app** |
|---|---|---|
| 22px | 34 | **5** |
| 24px | 100 | **2** |
| 26px | 112 | **1** |
| **all ≥16px** | **291** | **16** |

The answer's *"212 load-bearing sites"* is **3 sites** here. The proposal to tokenise rather
than absorb is still right — the role is real — but the case for it cannot rest on volume we
do not have.

**STANDING RULE, because this is the third consecutive answer it applies to:** Claude Design
reads `05-prototype/…`. It is the **design authority** and its scales, roles and namings are
adopted on that basis. **Its counts are the prototype's and must be re-derived against
`07-frontend` before any of them is used to size, justify or schedule work.** Prior
occurrences: OQ-275 (*"there is no `--text-h1` token"* — we declare seven), OQ-276 (1,361
declarations vs our 347), and now this. In every case the design judgement was sound and the
arithmetic described a different codebase.

### TWO DIVERGENCES THIS RULING EXPOSES — both are r10 conformance, not tokenisation

**1 · Our KPI value is 30px; the ruled KPI role is 26px.** `KPIStrip.css` `.kpi .v` is
`font-size: 30px`. Adopting `--text-metric` is therefore **a visible change** on the
dashboard and every KPI strip, not a rename. It is the right change — the standing rule is
that a screen is not migrated until it matches r10 — but it must be photographed, and it is
the only intended pixel movement in this phase.

**2 · The answer's ruling on the 40px is CORRECT FOR r10 AND WRONG FOR US.** It says *"it's
the wizard-title h1 override, so it is a heading… There's no non-heading 40px in the file."*
True of the prototype. **Our 40px is `payments.css` `.pay-today-amount`** — a money figure,
`font-weight: 800`, no heading element in sight. So by the answer's **own** logic it is a
**metric**, and putting it in `--text-h1` would file a KPI as a title, which is the exact
mistake the three new tokens exist to stop. It is absorbed to `--text-metric-lg` (32px),
which is also what r10 does with its largest metric.

### The remainder, absorbed not tokenised

The ruling's nudges apply, scaled to our 16 sites: **30 → 26** (the KPI, above), **40 → 32**,
**18 → 20 or 16 per site**, and 16/20/22/24/26 already land on ruled steps. Each is a
one-line change and each is a judgement made by looking at the site, never a blanket round —
the two 12.5px sites in Phase 2 took **opposite** answers for good reasons, and that is the
precedent.

**With this, the ≥16px tier is closed.** OQ-278 is answered.

## 2026-08-19 · CR-018 PHASE 2b — the metric tier BUILT, and the escape hatch closed (v2.29.6)

**What was decided by building it**, against the ruling of the same day (OQ-278,
commit `6a13828`). Three things, and the third is the one that outlives the phase.

### 1 · OUR CENSUS IS FOURTEEN. NOT 16, NOT 212, NOT 291.

Re-derived against `07-frontend` before a line was changed, and **read from the
pinned tip rather than from disk**, because the shared working tree had reset to
an Aug-18 snapshot 184 files behind the branch:

| ≥16px literal | ours |
|---|---|
| 16px | **2** |
| 18px | **2** |
| 22px | **5** |
| 24px | **2** |
| 26px | **1** |
| 30px | **1** |
| 40px | **1** |
| **total** | **14** |

**There is no 20px literal in the product and 16px appears twice, not three
times.** The brief this lane was given said *"16 sites: 16px ×3 · 20px ×1 · …"*
and was two sites high; OQ-278's own registry row says fourteen and is right.
Claude Design's `291` and its *"212 load-bearing sites"* are r10's, which is the
third consecutive occurrence and exactly what the standing rule of `6a13828`
predicts. **The rule now has a fourth data point and it is our own brief** — a
count is worth re-deriving even when it comes from inside the lane.

### 2 · EIGHT BECAME REFERENCES · TWO PIXELS MOVED · SIX DELIBERATELY DID NOT

`--text-metric-sm` 22px · `--text-metric` 26px · `--text-metric-lg` 32px, plus
`--line-height-metric-sm` 1.15 and `--line-height-metric` 1.1. **They carry a
leading and NOTHING else**, and that asymmetry is asserted in
`tailwindTheme.test.ts`: the heading steps set size + weight + leading +
tracking, but every metric site in this app already sets its own weight — 800 on
the KPI value and the "Today" total, 600 on a net-pair figure — so a
`--font-weight` modifier would silently overwrite each of them the moment Phase 3
turned the site into a utility.

| site | was | is | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `KPIStrip .kpi .v` | 30px | `--text-metric` **26px** | ⚠ **VISIBLE.** The KPI role's ruled default. 68 elements across 9 screens |
| `payments .pay-today-amount` | 40px | `--text-metric-lg` **32px** | ⚠ **VISIBLE.** A money figure at weight 800, not the wizard-title `h1` r10 has at 40px |
| `RoutesCyclesWizards .rcw-stat-figure` | 26px | `--text-metric` | same pixel, role exact |
| `SettingsPage .lookup-card .v` | 22px | `--text-metric-sm` | same pixel, role exact |
| `reads .rd-figure-value` | 22px | `--text-metric-sm` | same pixel, role exact |
| `FormModal .modal-title` | 22px | `--text-metric-sm` | same pixel — **value right, ROLE WRONG**, see below |
| `RoutesCyclesWizards .rcw-head-title` | 22px | `--text-metric-sm` | same pixel — same caveat |
| `billing .brun-h` | 22px | `--text-metric-sm` | same pixel — same caveat |

**The caveat is written into all three files rather than smoothed over.** Those
three are TITLES; the ruled heading scale runs `--text-h4` 20 → `--text-h3` 25
with nothing between, and `--text-metric-sm` is the only ruled name at 22px.
Nothing renders differently — in plain CSS the token is a size and nothing else —
but **a title filed as a metric is a KPI filed as a title, pointed the other
way**, which is the very mistake `6a13828` refused to make with the 40px. Raised
as OQ-279 rather than left as a comfortable silence.

**Six were NOT converted, and each refusal is a judgement with a reason on the
line above it:** the two 16px (a control and marketing prose at `--text-h5`'s
value, where `tailwind.css`'s standing rule forbids pointing a non-heading at a
heading step), the two 18px (no step; and r10 sets the sidebar brand at exactly
18px, so moving it diverges FROM the authority), and the two 24px (no step; h3 is
a pixel up and metric-sm is a metric name). All six are OQ-279.

### 3 · THE MEASURED PROOF: THE ONLY THING THAT MOVED IS THE TWO THINGS THAT SHOULD

Before and after, against the booted stack with the bundle rebuilt between runs:

* **census diff: 217 rows, and all 217 are the two movements.** 68 × `font-size`
  30→26, 3 × 40→32, and their DERIVED `line-height` (1) and `letter-spacing`
  (−0.02em) rows, which move because they are relative to the size:
  −0.02em × 30 = −0.6px and × 26 = −0.52px, exactly as recorded.
* **`accounts.png`, `pricing.png`, `settings.png` and `routes-cycles.png` are
  BYTE-IDENTICAL** before and after. `dashboard.png` and `payments.png` differ.
* **CR-016's register held every number on all 24 screens.**

### 4 · THE ESCAPE HATCH WAS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — IT WAS ALREADY OPEN

**Clearing the `--text-*` namespace is half a fence.** It kills `text-2xl`; it
does not touch `text-[12.5px]`, because arbitrary values come from a namespace no
`@theme` block can empty. Three documents describe the cleared namespace as *the*
enforcement point. **G34's first run found seven live uses** — `text-[13px]` ×5
and `text-[12px]` ×2 in `RateSchedulesTab.tsx`, the ONE component Route B has
migrated, written one commit after the phase whose whole purpose was removing
numbers. Both values are ruled steps, so they are now `text-base` and `text-sm`;
the census diff across that swap is **zero rows**.

**And a rule nobody runs is not enforcement (DEF-339).** So this phase did both:

* `10-scripts/gates/g34_type_scale_escape.py`, wired into `run_gates.py`, which
  `gates.yml` runs **on every push to every path**. It also reads `.css`, which
  ESLint never opens. Three checks: no arbitrary type value, no inline
  `fontSize`, and **the count of literal `font-size:` declarations EXACT at 6** —
  the `surface_debt.txt` discipline, so a new hand-written size is RED and
  quietly fixing one without lowering the number is RED too (DEF-077).
* `npm run lint` is now a step in `ci-frontend.yml`. It had run in **no workflow
  at all**, so every rule in `.eslintrc.cjs` — including `no-explicit-any`, which
  B8 calls *"CI-gated"* — was enforced by habit. It was wired today because the
  tree was already clean, which is the cheapest moment to close a hole.

**Both were proved RED first and proved GREEN on the false positive that would
have got them switched off:** `text-[color-mix(in_srgb,var(--color-text)_70%,transparent)]`
is an arbitrary COLOUR, three of them are live in the tree, and it is the
**correct** spelling here because the opacity modifier that would replace it
(`text-text/70`) emits `color-mix(in oklab)` while this system writes `in srgb`.
Only a LENGTH in the brackets is a type value. A rule that fires on the right
answer gets a `// eslint-disable` within a week.

### 5 · WHAT CAN STILL PUT AN OFF-SCALE SIZE ON SCREEN — the honest list

1. **A `var(--text-h5)` on something that is not a heading.** The value is on the
   scale so no counter fires, and no regex can tell a control from a title. This
   is OQ-279's territory and a human's.
2. **The six literals themselves**, if someone edits one in place — the ratchet
   counts them and does not read their values.
3. **A size that arrives at runtime** — a computed style set by JS, or a `font:`
   shorthand, neither of which G34 parses.
4. **Anything a `.tsx` outside `07-frontend/src` renders**, and anything in a
   sibling repo. The prototype is deliberately not scanned.
5. **Preflight, when it is finally enabled** — `global.css`'s `h1..h6` rule sets
   no font-size, so every heading's size comes from the browser today. Turning
   Preflight on changes all of them at once. Deferred to the end of Phase 3, on
   purpose.

**Not on that list any more:** `text-[17px]`, `leading-[1.3]`, `font-[900]`,
`style={{ fontSize }}`, and a seventh `font-size:` literal in a stylesheet.

## 2026-08-19 · OQ-272 ANSWERED — the webfont is not a blocker, and two costs swap owners

**Source:** the PO put OQ-272 to Claude Design. **The answer is adopted**: the font choice
does **not** block Phase 3 or Preflight. It must be settled **before type-locked spacing
ships**, and until then it is a small change any time.

**Also adopted:** keep `--font-heading` and `--font-body` as separate keys so a future
decision can change display type without touching body type. **We already do.**

### The measurement, against our app (fourth application of the `6a13828` standing rule)

**"Archivo lives in exactly two places" is three places here, and all three are guarded.**

| | |
|---|---|
| `tokens.css:22` | the `@import url(...)` that actually fetches the face |
| `tokens.css:100,102` | `--font-heading` / `--font-body`, the CSS custom properties |
| `tailwind.css:240,241` | the same two as `@theme` keys — **a second literal, deliberately** |

The `@theme` block duplicates literals rather than aliasing (`--color-bg: #f3f2f2`, not
`var(--color-bg)`) — that is how the whole theme is built, and **Phase 2 added a
`tokens.css`↔`@theme` drift test**, so the copies cannot diverge silently. So a swap is
**five lines across two files, guarded**, not one line — still a half-hour change with
**zero markup churn**, exactly as the answer says. The conclusion holds; the arithmetic is
ours.

### ⚠ THE TWO "COSTS IF THE CHOICE CHANGES" SWAP OWNERS — this is the useful part

The answer names two things tuned to Archivo that a different face would break. **Measured,
one is theirs and one is ours, and neither is where it was expected:**

| | r10 | **our app** |
|---|---|---|
| the optical nudge `margin-left: -0.04em` on every `h1` | **6** | **ZERO** |
| heading tracking `-0.015em` | **ZERO** | **3 files** (`dashboard.css`, `tokens.css`, `tailwind.css`) |

* **The optical nudge is not a cost to us at all.** We never had it. One item off the list.
* **The heading tracking is ours alone** — the answer could not have known, because it is not
  in the file it read. So the re-tune risk it warns about is real for us, and it attaches to
  a value **r10 does not have**.

### The divergence that leaves, filed rather than smoothed over

Our headings are tracked at `-0.015em` and **r10's are not tracked at all**. Under the
standing rule that *a screen is not migrated until it matches r10*, that is a divergence
from the design authority which nobody has ruled — and it is exactly the kind that gets
carried silently into new markup, because Phase 3 will copy it into a `tracking-…` utility
without anyone deciding it should exist. **Raised as ~~OQ-280~~ → RENUMBERED **OQ-281** (see the renumber entry at the end of this log — CR-018 Phase 3 had already taken 280 in the registry)**, not fixed here: removing it
moves pixels on every heading, and that is a design call.

### Status

**OQ-272 is CLOSED as answered.** It does not gate Phase 3, Phase 4 or Preflight. The gate
it *does* set — settle the face before type-locked spacing lands — is recorded on the
Preflight row, which is the last phase and the only one that touches heading metrics.

## 2026-08-19 · OQ-273 — THE PROPOSAL NAMES SERVICES WE DO NOT SELL. **NOT APPLIED.**

**Source:** the PO put OQ-273 (four services with no colour token) to Claude Design. **The
reasoning is adopted. The palette is NOT, because three of its four services are not ours
and three of ours are not in it.**

### ⚠ THE MISMATCH, and this is the fifth application of the `6a13828` standing rule — the first where it is not arithmetic but IDENTITY

`06-backend/apps/tenancy` declares the canonical ten (CLAUDE.md's *"ten, not six"*, BR-RAT-024):

```
electric · water · gas · sewer · trash · storm_water · solar · broadband · thermal_heat · battery
```

`tokens.css:90-95` declares **six** colours: electric, water, gas, sewer, trash, **broadband**.

| The proposal offers | We sell it? |
|---|---|
| `--color-svc-stormwater` | ✅ yes — `storm_water` |
| `--color-svc-reclaimed` | ❌ **no such service** |
| `--color-svc-irrigation` | ❌ **no such service** |
| `--color-svc-broadband` `#a8256b` | ⚠ we already have broadband, at `#6b3d8a` |

And it renames our existing `#6b3d8a` from **broadband** to **bundle** — which is not a
service at all — then mints a second, different broadband. Applying this would have put
**Reclaimed** and **Irrigation** swatches into a product that bills **Solar**,
**Thermal/Heat** and **Battery**, and given broadband two colours.

**Our actual gap is `storm_water`, `solar`, `thermal_heat`, `battery`.** One of the four
proposed lands.

### What IS adopted, because it transfers and is the valuable half

1. **The two constraints** — clear of the `#ec3013` accent, and distinguishable at **8×8px**.
2. **`--color-svc-stormwater: #2f4a7a`** — the argument is exactly right: keep it in the
   water family by hue and separate it by **value**, so it reads as related rather than
   confusable.
3. ⚠ **THE FILL VARIANT, which is the best idea in the answer and outlives its palette:**
   > *"Three cool blues plus a teal is the practical limit for an 8px dot… Add a fill variant
   > rather than a fourth blue. Shape carries where hue can't, and it also gives you a
   > colourblind-safe distinction inside the water family — which hue alone does not."*

   **Adopted as a rule, not a one-off.** Any service family that outgrows safe hue separation
   gets a shape variant, and the colourblind argument makes it correct even where hue would
   have worked. This is ratified independently of which services exist.

### The three still open, and why they are genuinely hard

`solar`, `thermal_heat` and `battery` all want hues that are already taken, which is why they
must not be guessed:

* **solar** → amber/yellow, but `gas` holds `#c47a1d`.
* **thermal_heat** → red/orange, but `electric` holds `#ec3013` **and that is also the brand
  accent**, so this is the most constrained of the three.
* **battery** → green, but `trash` holds `#3a6b3d`.

Three services, three occupied hues, one 8px dot. **Put back to Claude Design with the real
ten**, together with the fill-variant rule, which may be the answer for more than one of
them. **OQ-273 stays OPEN.**

### The standing rule, updated

Four prior occurrences were **counts** — the design judgement sound, the arithmetic
describing the prototype. This one is **identity**: the answer names entities the product
does not have. So the rule is widened: *before adopting any proposal, check its **nouns**
against the repo, not only its numbers.* A wrong count wastes an estimate. A wrong noun
ships a feature for a service nobody sells.

## 2026-08-19 · OQ-274 — BREAKPOINTS. THE DIRECTION IS RATIFIED; THE NUMBERS ARE NOT OURS.

**Adopted without qualification — this is the important half:**

* **Desktop-first, `max-width`, ratified in B14.** *"Mixing the two directions in one codebase
  is where breakpoint bugs come from, and Tailwind's defaults are min-width, so the mismatch
  is silent."* Authoring reads `max-xl:grid-cols-1`, never `xl:grid-cols-2`.
* **Replace Tailwind's defaults, never extend them** — extending leaves two colliding scales.
* **Declare the small steps and leave them empty.** Naming them stops the next person
  inventing a seventh; leaving them unfilled stops anyone inventing untested mobile layouts.
* **The contract is 1024→1920 with no horizontal scroll.**

### ⚠ AND WE ARE ALREADY MIXING DIRECTIONS — the warning is not hypothetical here

Measured across `07-frontend/src`: **10 `max-width` rules and 2 `min-width` rules.** The
silent mismatch the answer warns about **exists in the tree today**. Ratifying desktop-first
means those two are defects, not style.

### The numbers are the prototype's — sixth application of the standing rule

| proposed | ours, measured |
|---|---|
| `2xl` 1440 | ✅ **1440** ×1 |
| `xl` 1200 | ❌ we use **1100** ×1 |
| `lg` 1024 | ✅ **1024** ×2 |
| `md` 768 | ❌ we use **720** ×2 |
| `sm` 640 | ❌ absent |
| — | ⚠ **900px ×6 — our MOST-USED breakpoint, and the proposal has no name for it** |

The advice to *"fold anything at 1280 and 1536"* does not apply: **we have neither.** We have
five distinct widths already, not six, and the heaviest by far is the one the scale does not
name.

**So the shape is ratified and the values are re-derived.** Either the ruled scale is adopted
and **eleven rules move** — 1100→1200, 720→768, and six rules at 900 to whichever step —
which changes layout at real viewport sizes and must be photographed; or the names are fitted
to our actual widths. **That is a design call, not an engineering one, and it is the only
part of OQ-274 still open.** The direction ruling stands either way and is the part that
prevents bugs.

## 2026-08-19 · OQ-279 RULED — absorb, don't name. And the hazard becomes live *because of* OQ-274.

**Adopted.** *"Three sites is not a role, and 22px sits 2px from `h4` and 3px from `h3` — that
difference isn't carrying meaning, it's carrying a leftover."*

| the three titles | becomes |
|---|---|
| `.modal-title` · `.rcw-head-title` · `.brun-h` | `--text-h3` **25px**, or `--text-h4` **20px** where the panel already has an `h3` |

The two genuine metrics at 22px — `.lookup-card .v` and `.rd-figure-value` — **stay**
`--text-metric-sm`. That was always the right filing; only the three titles were wrong.

**And the metric keys are locked with a comment that says what they are for:**
`--text-metric-sm: 22px; /* KPI values only — never a heading */`.

**Revisit threshold recorded:** if a 22px title recurs past **~8 sites** it is a role and
deserves `--text-h3-sm`. Three does not.

### ⚠ THE ARGUMENT'S MECHANISM IS r10's — AND WE ARE ABOUT TO IMPORT IT

The reasoning is: the metric keys are retuned as a set when KPI density changes, *"they
already move at the `xl` and `2xl` breakpoints — 30→26→22"*, so a heading resolving through
one would move silently and no test would catch it.

**Measured: our KPI does not resize at any breakpoint.** Not one `@media` rule in
`07-frontend/src` changes `.kpi .v`. Seventh application of the `6a13828` standing rule.

**But this is the case where the correction strengthens the ruling instead of weakening it.**
The OQ-274 answer, ruled in the entry above, states the breakpoint behaviour we are adopting:

heading move silently is **exactly what we are about to build**. The hazard is not live today

**Which makes the ordering load-bearing: absorb the three titles BEFORE the breakpoint steps
are wired.** Do it after, and the first density retune drags three panel titles with it, on

## 2026-08-19 · OQ-274 and OQ-281 (was OQ-280) DECIDED BY THE ENGINEERING LANE, NOT THE PO

**The PO's instruction, verbatim:** *"Complete Cr 18 - dont wait for my instructions"*.

⚠ **Both rulings below are MINE, not the Product Owner's, and are marked so deliberately.**
A signature covers only what was shown (HUMAN-GUIDE §6). Neither was put to the PO with a
worked figure, so neither may later be cited as a PO decision. Both are reversible in one
line and both are recorded with the condition that would reverse them.

### OQ-274 · The breakpoint WIDTHS — **fit the names to our widths, not our widths to their names**

| name | width | what it owns today |
|---|---|---|
| `sm` | **720px** | 2 rules |
| `md` | **900px** | **6 rules — our heaviest** |
| `lg` | **1024px** | 2 rules |
| `xl` | **1100px** | 1 rule |
| `2xl` | **1440px** | 1 rule |

**Zero pixels move.** The alternative — adopting 640/768/1024/1200/1440 — moves **eleven
rules** and changes layout at real viewport sizes.

**The reasoning, and it is a distinction worth keeping:** r10 is the design authority for how
a screen **looks** — its layout, copy, flows and states. It is not the authority for **which
viewport widths our React app happens to break at**; those are a property of our own grid and
were never designed. Adopting the prototype's numbers would move six rules off 900px — a
width that carries more of our responsive behaviour than any other — onto a width nobody
chose, purely for tidiness, and would change what a customer sees at 900–1100px with no
design intent behind it. **Movement for symmetry is not conformance.**

What we DO take from the ruling is the part that prevents bugs, and it is ratified unchanged:
**desktop-first `max-width`; replace the `--breakpoint-*` namespace rather than extend it, so
Tailwind's `min-width` defaults cannot form a second colliding scale; declare all five names
so nobody invents a sixth; the contract stays 1024→1920 with no horizontal scroll.**

**Reverses if:** a responsive design is actually authored for this product, at which point the
widths become a design decision and go to the PO with the layouts that need them.

---

### OQ-281 (renumbered from OQ-280) · Heading tracking `-0.015em` — **keep it, stamp the divergence**

Our headings are tracked at `-0.015em` in three files; **r10 tracks headings not at all.**

**Kept.** Removing it moves pixels on **every heading in the product** to satisfy a
prototype that is silent on the subject — silence is not a specification. No defect has been
reported against it, nothing looks wrong, and CLAUDE.md's own rule for a spec/r10 conflict is
*file it, don't follow it blindly*.

**Stamped as a known divergence** in the three files that carry it, so Phase 3 copies it into
a `tracking-…` utility **as a recorded decision** rather than by accident — which was the
whole risk, and is now closed either way.

**Reverses if:** r10 is ever revised to specify heading tracking, or a reader reports the
headings look tight. Then it is a design call with a real trigger.

---

### What "CR-018 COMPLETE" now means — the closing bar, written before the last phases run

1. Every screen renders as it did, proved by **all 24 `CR-016-ui-conformance.spec.ts`
   baselines holding**, with the only exceptions the ones ruled and photographed.
2. **G31 retired deliberately with a written reason**, not left passing over an empty set —
   Route B ends with no bespoke class for it to check, and a green gate measuring nothing
   reads as protection that is gone.
3. **Preflight enabled last**, with OQ-275's heading sizes settled first — it moved 684
   computed values on a single screen when Phase 1 measured it.
4. The bundle finishes **below** its 125,258-byte starting point.
5. Every OQ CR-018 raised is closed or explicitly carried, **with its owner named** — and the
   two above are marked as the lane's, not the PO's.

## 2026-08-20 · OQ-277 CLOSED — one grammar, two readers, and the half option C could not have (v2.29.8)

**The question.** The regex that pulls class names out of a `.tsx` file existed
**twice, in two languages, in two workflows that share no runtime**:
`10-scripts/gates/g31_declared_classes.py` (Python, `gates.yml`, which installs
Python and **nothing else**) and `07-frontend/src/styles/routeBUtilities.test.ts`
(JS, `ci-frontend.yml`, which runs node and **nothing else**). Deleting one was
never available — they ask different questions (*is this class declared by a
stylesheet?* vs *does the Tailwind compiler accept this utility?*) and both are
load-bearing.

**The cost was measured, not feared. Three corrections, each landed in ONE
language:**

| # | the bug | the number it moved |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | a comparison operand counted as a class (`row.state === "auto"`) | **130** reported where **125** were real |
| 2 | an interpolated template consumed whole, **silently losing** `is-selected`/`is-blocked` while gaining a false name | **871 → 870**, which reads as an improvement |
| 3 | G34's `^\s*` matching across a newline | the wrong line number |

### What was built — option C, plus the half option C did not name

`07-frontend/classname-grammar/`:

* **`patterns.json`** — the **five** regex SOURCE STRINGS both readers compile:
  `classname`, `comparison`, `quoted`, `template`, `interpolation`.
* **`corpus.tsx`** — a ten-case golden fixture; every case is a bug that has
  already happened.
* **`corpus.expected.json`** — the ruled extraction, plus the case-to-defect
  mapping in prose so a failure names the old bug rather than printing a diff.

**Option C as the registry wrote it said "run the Python reader over a fixture
and assert the TS reader agrees" — and that needs both runtimes in one place,
which is the very thing that created this question.** So it was inverted: each
reader asserts the **same** corpus **in its own workflow** —
`grammar_corpus_selftest()` inside G31's `run()`, and two vitest cases in
`routeBUtilities.test.ts`. Neither needs the other's runtime; each goes red in
its own CI.

### Why BOTH halves, and this is the load-bearing sentence

Sharing the sources catches **textual** drift. The corpus catches **semantic**
drift. **Not one of the three bugs above was a wrong character of regex** — all
three were in the code *around* it, so sharing `patterns.json` alone would have
caught **none of them**.

Asserted as **SET EQUALITY, not `contains`**: bug 2 GAINED a name while losing
two, and every assertion that only looks for the names it expects passes it.

### Portability was VERIFIED per pattern, not assumed

Each pattern carries **probes** whose expected matches were produced by Python
`re` and then asserted, unchanged, in JS — both readers re-run all of them. A
**construct blacklist** refuses `^`, `$`, `\A`, `\Z`, `(?P`, `(?<`, `(?#`,
`(?i`, because **Python's `$` matches before a trailing newline and JS's does
not**, and `^\s*` spanning a newline is bug 3 verbatim. The blacklist needed a
real scanner rather than a substring search — `[^"]*` appears in every pattern
here and trips a naive `^` check on its first run; `_bare_and_escapes()` /
`bareAndEscapes()` skip character-class bodies and escape pairs and are written
identically in both languages. **One residual difference is recorded rather than
hidden:** `\s` is not byte-identical between the engines (Python's includes
U+001C–U+001F, JS's includes U+FEFF and the Unicode Zs set); no `.tsx` in this
repo contains either, and the probes prove they agree on real source.

### One pattern is deliberately NOT shared, and that is a ruling

`TOKEN`. G31 must reject `sm:foo` and `text-[13px]` **forever** — accepting them
reports every Tailwind utility as an undeclared class, which is the false
positive that gets a gate switched off (DEF-323). The vitest reader must accept
exactly those or it cannot ask the compiler anything. Merging them breaks one.
**Unshared is not unwatched:** corpus case **C10** gives the divergence an exact
size of **one token**, asserted on both sides, so it cannot grow in silence.

### Which corpus case catches which historical bug

| case | catches |
|---|---|
| **C2** `className={row.state === "auto" ? undefined : "…"}` | **bug 1** — `auto` must not be a class |
| **C3** `` className={`cg-tpl-base ${sel ? "…" : "…"}`} `` | **bug 2, both directions** — all THREE names required, so neither the narrow reader nor the single-alternation widening passes |
| **C7** the same expression **spanning newlines** | **bug 3** — proves `\s*` and the negated classes cross a newline identically in both engines, with no anchor anywhere |
| **C8** a comparison **split across a newline** | **bug 3 × bug 1** — the combination neither single-language fix could have found |
| C1, C4, C5, C6, C9, C10 | plain attribute · a class named in prose · a template with no interpolation · the trailing-dash prefix rule · the honest limit of C4 · the sanctioned divergence |

### RED-proved in both languages before being trusted green (law 7)

Three sabotages of `patterns.json`, each turning **both** readers red and each
naming the corpus case by id:

1. `template` → `` `([^`$]*)` `` (the narrow first reader) — Python: *"corpus
   case C3-interpolated-template: did NOT find ['cg-tpl-base']"*; vitest: *"corpus
   case C3-interpolated-template lost \"cg-tpl-base\""*.
2. `comparison` made unmatchable — both: *"corpus case C2-comparison-operand
   wrongly found 'auto'"*.
3. `^\s*` prepended to `classname` — **both refuse to start**: *"shared pattern
   'classname' contains '^', which patterns.json forbids"*.

Restored, both green.

### The bar it had to clear, measured

**G31: 908 declared, 863 referenced, 0 undeclared — identical before and after.**
`routeBUtilities.test.ts`: 5 passed → 7 passed, the original five untouched.
`npm run lint` and `tsc --noEmit` clean. `run_gates.py` lost no gate and
`_assert_registry_sane()` passes (35 rows, unchanged — no new gate module was
added; the corpus check lives inside G31, which is also the only way it could run
where `gates.yml` can see it).

**Options A and B were NOT taken and remain available.** A (node in `gates.yml`,
delete the TS reader) costs `npm ci` on every gate run; B (retire G31 at the
start of Phase 2) contradicts the Route B ruling's sequencing and needs the PO.

### One thing found on the way, recorded and not filed

At tip `e1a652c`, `07-frontend/package.json` read **2.29.7** and
`06-backend/pyproject.toml` read **2.29.6** — commit `8ea7847` (CR-018 Phase 2c
step 1) moved the frontend literal and not the backend one. That is **DEF-242's
shape, third occurrence**. It is **recorded in `pyproject.toml`'s own comment and
here, not filed as a defect**, because the Phase 2c lane is mid-change and may
yet move it — filing against unfinished work would convert someone's in-flight
step into a defect. This lane could not leave them unequal either, so both went
to **2.29.8**, skipping 2.29.7 for the reason the 2.29.2 note already reasoned
out: *a skipped number costs nothing, a duplicated one costs the ability to say
which build a defect was seen on.* Both files moved forward; neither moved back.
**If the Phase 2c lane does not move `pyproject.toml`, this is a defect and
should be filed.**
