## 2026-08-26 — CR-039 Wave B: three engineering judgments where the rules ran out

The PO's ruling that started it, verbatim: *"Can we write all failed job
detialsin audit log of that tenant along wt=ith error code so that we can trace
it back later?"* — written as **BR-TEN-083**. Building it forced three
judgments that no signed document answers, and each is recorded here with its
worked reason rather than left in a lane report.

**1 · An additive `blocks` column, NOT a re-keyed table — because re-keying
would have re-shaped a signed rule to make a screen easier.**
`sample_data_runs` is keyed `(tenant, module)` and **four of the eleven plant
blocks share a module with another** (customers owns three, metering two,
payments two), so the worst-first merge reconciles their outcomes away and the
panel cannot say which block failed. The obvious fix is to re-key per block.
**BR-TEN-060 says in its own words *"a row per module with a machine-readable
reason_code and a sentence"***, so re-keying is an amendment to a signed rule,
and amending a rule because it makes a screen harder is exactly backwards. The
module row, its worst-first merge and its `ck_sample_run_reason_required` CHECK
are UNTOUCHED; the per-block breakdown rides in one additive `blocks jsonb`
column beside them. **No backfill** — a merged verdict cannot honestly be
attributed to one block, and inventing an attribution is worse than an absence.

**2 · The append-only audit row carries the CATALOGUE sentence for its code and
never the seeder's own text.** Measured, not assumed: four seeders interpolate
live customer data into failure messages — `apps/payments/sample_data.py:213`
renders an invoice number plus the raw text of whatever `record_payment`
refused, `apps/metering/sample_data.py:2407` up to three validation messages,
`apps/customers/sample_data.py:776/816/948` account balances and tie-out
figures, `apps/billing/sample_data.py:356/404` four hundred characters of
per-bill detail and tax-authority names. `audit_log` cannot be deleted (hard
rule 4), so a row that carried those would put customer data beyond reach of
*Remove sample data* forever. The operator's full sentence stays in
`sample_data_runs`, which that button DOES delete. Enforced structurally:
`audit_safe_sentence(code)` takes only a code, asserted by `inspect.signature`.

**3 · ROOT vs CONSEQUENCE is derived only from dependency edges already STATED
in code, and the direction of the error is deliberate.** Seven edges, each
carrying the file and the verbatim words that already stated it, greped back
out by a test. **Four blocks declare no edge at all and can therefore only ever
be reported as ROOT — that is a REPORTED GAP, not a claim of independence.** A
missing edge makes a block look like a root cause (noise the operator can
dismiss); a wrong edge would mark a real fault a CONSEQUENCE and tell them to
ignore it. `apps/assets/sample_data.py`'s own DEF-660 comment is the measured
motivation: *"a chain of five failures that read like five separate bugs."*

**⚠ One judgment is flagged for reversal rather than settled:** a
`seam_not_wired` SKIP writes no `sample.block_failed` row, on the reasoning
that a skip is a platform gap identical on every tenant and one row per tenant
per run would bury the tenant-specific failures. That is the lane's reading,
not the PO's words. BR-TEN-083 clause 4 carries it as PROPOSED.

## 2026-08-26 — the version bumps on EVERY WAVE, and the first number moves only on a named release

**PO verbatim:** *"We have to bump version when major when minor so we are able
to keep track of"*.

Put to them with the state that prompted it: the merge lane had **deferred**
CR-038's and CR-039's bumps until each CR closed, and had written that deferral
down as *"one bump per CR, not one per wave"*. Both halves of that are now
**SUPERSEDED** by this ruling.

**Two questions, both answered.**

**1 · What moves the FIRST number — ruled: a NAMED RELEASE ONLY.**
`2 → 3` happens when the PO declares a release milestone — a demo to a customer,
a go-live, a scope boundary they name. **Nothing automatic.** Not a breaking
migration, not a signed-rule change, not a round-number boundary. The worked
consequence: **today's 52 changes all stay inside release 2**, and `2.x` keeps
meaning one thing to everyone who reads it. A number that moved on engineering
events a customer never sees would stop being a release.

**2 · What moves the MIDDLE number — ruled: EVERY WAVE, not every CR.**
The worked figure put to them: **CR-038's nine merged waves would each have
bumped — 2.53, 2.54, 2.55 … 2.61** — instead of one 2.53.0 covering all nine.
The reason the PO gave is the reason: *"so we are able to keep track of"*. A
defect reported against `2.53.0` under the per-CR rule would name **eleven waves
and dozens of files**; under this ruling it names one wave.

**⚠ THE COST THIS RULING ACCEPTS, STATED WHEN IT WAS PUT.** Parallel waves
collide on the four version literals G35 holds in lockstep (`package.json`,
`package-lock.json`'s two copies, `pyproject.toml`). So: **a wave bumps at MERGE
time, in the order waves land — never in its own branch.** A lane that bumped in
its branch would produce two branches both claiming 2.54.0 and a merge
resolution that is somebody picking a number, which is exactly the failure this
scheme exists to prevent.

**What this does NOT change:** the scheme itself, `<release>.<change>.<fix>`,
and the third number still counts fixes since the change. The PO chose per-wave
over per-wave-plus-per-defect-fix, so a defect fix moves the third number as it
always did and does not get its own middle bump.

**Applied, and the retroactive half is deliberately NOT invented.** Nine CR-038
waves and CR-039 Wave B merged BEFORE this ruling existed, as a single stream
with no bumps between them. Assigning them 2.53 through 2.62 after the fact
would put ten build numbers on ten deploys that never happened — a record that
reads precise and is fiction. So: **one bump to 2.53.0 now**, whose changelog
entry NAMES every wave inside it, and **per-wave bumps from the next merge
onward**. The seam is stated in the changelog rather than smoothed over.

## 2026-08-26 — CR-038 W7: four engineering judgments the signed rules did not answer

The W7 lane built the three write modes the PO asked for by name. Four decisions
had to be taken that no signed rule reaches. Each is recorded here **with its
worked figure** so the next agent, with only the repo, would build the same
thing — and each is on the PO's agenda through the review-ledger row for
migration 0036, because a signature covers only what was shown.

**1 · `insert` IS THE DEFAULT WRITE MODE.** Nobody was asked which of the three
a clerk who never touches the control should get. The lane chose `insert` on
hard-won law 3 — *the unsafe option must be the one you type* — because it is
the only one of the three that cannot alter a reading already on file, and
backfilled **every existing read batch** to it. **The worked reason the backfill
is a statement of history rather than a reinterpretation:** until this column
existed, a committed duplicate was an ERROR that gated the whole post, which is
exactly what `insert` means. So `default="insert"` says what those batches
already were.

**2 · THE BILLED REFUSAL IS SEVERITY *WARNING*, NOT *ERROR*.** BR-MET-127 says
*"refuse"*, and the obvious implementation of "refuse" in this module is an
ERROR. That would have been wrong, and the rule's own next clause is why: *"the
refusal is a row outcome, never a batch failure"*. **Worked:** a 1,180-row
corrections file in which ONE row names a billed reading. As an ERROR,
`_unresolved_errors` gates the commit and **1,179 other customers' readings do
not post**. As a WARNING carrying `action: refuse_billed`, the one row is
skipped and named and the other 1,179 land. The severity is therefore derived
from the rule's second sentence, not from the word "refuse".

**3 · THE PREMISE IS RE-DERIVED AT COMMIT, NOT READ OFF THE STAGED ROW.** The
validate pass stores what each row WOULD do; `commit_read_batch` throws that
away and asks the head again, inside the locked transaction. **Worked:** a clerk
validates a batch at 09:00 and commits at 11:00; the bill run issues at 10:00
and `mark_read_billed` moves the head to `billed`. Acting on the 09:00 rehearsal
would supersede a billed reading — the exact money correction BR-MET-127 forbids
— and every test would still pass, because the rehearsal was correct when it was
taken. The dry run is a rehearsal; it is never the authority.

**4 · THE WRITE MODE MAY CHANGE A RULE'S SEVERITY, AND ONLY IN ONE PLACE.**
`write_modes.apply()` downgrades the engine's committed-duplicate ERROR to a
WARNING under the superseding modes. That is severity laundering unless it is
bounded, so three bounds are built and asserted: it touches the **committed
scopes only** (an intra-batch duplicate — the same key twice in one file — stays
an ERROR under every mode, because no premise makes a file that contradicts
itself acceptable); the engine's original verdict is **stamped into the outcome
rather than erased** (`engine_severity`, `superseded_by_write_mode`), so a
committed read never claims a clean bill of health it did not get; and WARNING
is not a pass — BR-MET-129 posts the row **with the flag attached**. The
sanction for doing it at all is CR-036 (g), verbatim: *"The severity and the
action of a rule may legitimately DEPEND on the write mode"*, over the PO's own
screenshot of `PRM.ADDRESS_ON_FILE` firing **9,881** times with action *Skip on
load* under a mode where "already on file" is the expected state of every row.

**And one thing the lane REFUSED to decide.** `replace` and `insert & update`
behave identically for reads, because CR-038 R2's two sentences describe the
same set of rows. Making them differ means deciding what `replace` does to
readings on file and NOT in the file, and the two options that would give the
control its name are both unlawful here — delete is forbidden by hard rule 4,
and supersede-by-nothing leaves a meter with readings and no live head. So both
modes are offered, they are recorded on the batch, the screen says in a clerk's
words that they do the same thing today, and **OQ-418** carries the question
with a five-option table. Two identical modes are a poor control; inventing the
difference would have been worse.
## 2026-08-26 — BR-MET-132 built: two lane judgments inside a one-sentence ruling

BR-MET-132 is one sentence — PO verbatim, *"Keep counting until the run
consumes the period — those are the chase days"* — and building it forced two
choices the sentence does not make. Both are recorded here because the next
agent, reading only the rule, would not arrive at either.

**1 · HOW FAR BACK. The chip looks at ONE window: the most recent occurrence
to have OPENED.** The rule says *"windows"*, plural, and drops a period *"only
when its bill run has consumed it"* — read at its widest, an occurrence a run
skipped in March is still unconsumed in August and would still be counted.
That reading was rejected for two reasons, the second decisive:

  * The PO's worked case is a single period. *"Those are the chase days"*
    names the gap between one window closing (**20 Aug**) and that same
    period's run (**25 Aug**) — a backlog is a different problem.
  * **The wide reading has no floor.** A tenant that has never completed a run
    — and, importantly, a tenant whose billing module simply cannot answer the
    seam, where every period reads as unconsumed — would have every occurrence
    since its first run counted, at one full coverage computation per period.
    A chip on the landing screen whose cost grows without bound is a chip that
    stops loading.

Worked, so the consequence is on the record rather than discovered: cycle
CY-001, window **16–20 Aug**, meters unread. Asked **22 Aug** → counted.
Run completes **25 Aug** → asked **26 Aug** → not counted. If instead the
August run never happens and **16–20 Sep** opens, the August gap stops being
counted by the chip and is reachable only through the chase-list endpoint,
which answers any NAMED period. **If that is wrong, it is one predicate in
`completeness.current_window` and it should be overturned deliberately.**

**2 · WHAT "CONSUMED" MEANS, AND WHICH WAY THE UNKNOWN FALLS.** Nothing in the
repo marked a period as billed, so the predicate is new
(`billing.selectors.period_consumed_by_run`): a bill run on that cycle whose
status is `completed` and whose period OVERLAPS the window. Two sub-choices:

  * **`completed` only.** A `draft` or `previewing` run has issued nothing and
    can be thrown away; an `issuing` run can still land on `failed`; `failed`
    and `cancelled` produced no bill. A period under any of those has not been
    billed and its meters still need chasing.
  * **Overlap, not equality.** The wizard proposes the cycle's own occurrence,
    so the two normally match — but a clerk may widen a run to 1–31 Aug, and
    that run really did bill the 16–20 Aug window's reads.

And when the seam answers `None` — billing publishes nothing, or cannot tell —
that reads as NOT consumed and the chip stays LOUD. The two errors are not
symmetric: a chip counting a period that was in fact billed costs a clerk one
look; a chip silent over a period nobody read is DEF-046 again, where a silent
zero read as good news.

**3 · THE PENDING LIST FOLLOWS THE CHIP.** The rule is written about the chip
and says nothing about `GET /reads?f.status=pending`. Both now share one
predicate (`CHASEABLE_WINDOW_STATES`), because the alternative is a chip
reading "60 missing" on 22 Aug that drills into an empty list — a number with
nothing behind it (hard-won law 2, in the one place the two surfaces meet).

## 2026-08-26 — BR-MET-133 clause 4 built: what a $25.00 floor does to a $60.00 bill with $40.00 disputed

BR-MET-133 clause 4 is CONFIRMED — PO verbatim, *"Bill stands, resolution
through the billed-correction door, and the disputed amount doesn't age into
late fees while open"*, with the rule adding *"the undisputed remainder of the
bill ages normally"*. Building it produced one judgment and one refusal, and
both belong on the record.

**1 · THE JUDGMENT: BR-BIL-001'S $25.00 BALANCE FLOOR TESTS THE REMAINDER, NOT
THE BILL.** BR-BIL-001's base is *the overdue portion*; clause 4 removes the
disputed money from ageing, so the overdue portion the fee is assessed on IS
the undisputed remainder — and the $25.00 precondition (PO 2026-08-11, OQ-137's
fee half) therefore tests the remainder. **The combination was never put to the
PO** and it changes a customer's answer from "a fee" to "no fee":

  * A bill of **$60.00** with **$40.00** disputed leaves **$20.00** ageable.
    That is under $25.00, so **no late fee is assessed at all**, where the
    un-excluded $60.00 earns the $5.00 minimum.

The alternative reading — test the floor against the WHOLE overdue balance and
then subtract — charges $5.00 to a customer whose entire undisputed balance is
$20.00, while we investigate the rest. That reads against the sentence the PO
actually said (*"a customer is not penalised for the days we investigate"*), so
it is not what shipped. `test_clause4__the_remainder_can_fall_under_the_25_dollar_floor`
is what goes red if the PO reads it the other way.

Two more worked figures, so the arithmetic is on the record and not only in a
test: **$184.20** with **$47.00** disputed ages **$137.20**; **$1,000.00** with
**$400.00** disputed pays **$9.00** where the un-excluded bill pays **$15.00**.

**2 · THE REFUSAL: NOTHING RECORDS A DISPUTED AMOUNT — OQ-418, MINTED.**
Measured across the repository on 2026-08-26: no model, no column, no service
writes one. It is the same measurement `apps/customers/move_out_settlement.py`
recorded on 2026-08-24 for BR-CUS-096, unchanged. `meter_reads.disputed_at` is
**a quantity in dispute, not a sum of money** — a customer saying *"the meter
says 684 kWh and the property was empty"* has disputed a READING, and wiring
that consumption in as an amount would price the dispute at 684 dollars.

So an open dispute with `amount=None` **raises `NotImplementedError("OQ-418")`**.
It does not fall back to zero and it does not fall back to the whole bill: those
two are **$137.20 apart on Sarah's bill alone**, and picking one would be an
engine writing money law. `assess_late_fee` still has no production caller
(S31.2/US-BIL-002 is unbuilt), so the stub blocks nothing today.

**And an unknown falls the same way.** When metering publishes no dispute
selector, `open_dispute_for_account` reports the SAME shape as a real open
dispute and the assessment refuses — `runs._dispute_hold_for`'s own posture:
*"we could not tell"* and *"there is no dispute"* are different facts and only
one of them is safe to charge a late fee on.

**3 · WHAT CLAUSE 4 DOES NOT REACH, STATED SO IT IS NOT ASSUMED.** The rule
says *"excluded from ageing AND from late-fee assessment"*. Only the late-fee
half has an implementation to exclude from: billing publishes no
`account_aging_state` (customers' seam has been resolving a function that does
not exist since W2) and `customers.selectors`' ageing reads OPENING BUCKETS,
which predate any bill. The collection ladder is untouched for a separate
reason — OQ-137's ladder half is still open and BR-MET-133 names late fees and
ageing, not dunning.

**4 · EVERY SURFACE STOPPED CITING A CLOSED QUESTION.** `billed_bill_effect`
was the code `issued_bill_untouched_oq_245` and the S29 banner rendered *"its
late fees keep running. What a dispute should do to a bill already sent has not
been decided."* Both were true until this ruling and false the moment it
landed. The code is now `issued_bill_stands_br_met_133`, no alias is kept, and
clearing a dispute records `outcome: "reading_stands"` where it used to record
a null verdict citing OQ-245(c) — clause 3 says which of the two outcomes
clearing is.
## 2026-08-26 — a consumption sum has no default branch (DEF-798, CR-038 W5 t8)

**Not a PO ruling — an ENGINEERING judgment where the rules ran out, recorded
here because the next agent would otherwise re-decide it, and would probably
decide it the other way.**

DEF-798 reported that `monthly_usage` summed across registers unit-blind:
**684 kWh of energy + a 14 kW demand peak-delta = 698 kWh, where the truth is
684.** Fixing the arithmetic was mechanical. The judgment was what to do with a
register nobody has classified.

The obvious fix is a subtraction — *drop `export`, `generation` and `demand`,
keep everything else.* **It is the wrong shape, and `generation` is the proof.**
BR-MET-059 makes the channel vocabulary deliberately extensible (*"adding a
register means adding a string"*), and `generation` was minted by BR-MET-135 on
**the same morning** this defect was filed. Under a subtraction rule, a solar
device's 612 kWh of production would have joined every site's usage on the day
that string landed, silently, with every test still green — the identical
mechanism as the defect being fixed, one register later.

So the rule is stated positively and closed: a read is `total`, a listed TOU
window, or a listed never-consumption register, **and a fourth kind raises
`UnclassifiedChannel` (an `OQ`-free `NotImplementedError` subclass) rather than
joining the sum**. A new register now forces a decision in the commit that mints
it, which is where the person minting it has the context to make one.

**The second judgment, same fix:** the total-vs-windows choice is made **per
ASSET**, not per account and not per service. One account can hold a flat meter
and a TOU meter on one service — a replaced meter, a sub-metered common area —
and choosing once for the service would drop the flat meter's real `total`
because a *different* meter reported windows. That would lose a real month of a
real customer's usage while fixing an over-count, which is a worse defect than
the one being fixed. `test_def_798_register_blind_usage` TC-4 is that case: 100
+ 60 = 160, and it is red under a per-service rule.

## 2026-08-26 — only ACCEPT is a bulk disposition (CR-038 W5 task 7)

**The PO asked for bulk operations and for accountability in the same breath**
(verbatim): *"We will need bulk operation"* and *"keep the rule — speed comes
from the bulk button… an auditor asking 'who chose to estimate M-4412?' gets a
name"*. Neither sentence says which verbs may be bulk.

BR-MET-023 lists six fix actions per flag. **This lane offered exactly one —
accept — and the boundary is a judgment worth the paragraph.** An override is a
SUPERSEDE: it needs a new register value and its own reason for each individual
reading. A bulk control taking one typed reason and applying it to forty
different readings would be recording a sentence that is **untrue of
thirty-nine of them** — and the reason is not decoration, it is what the auditor
reads. Accept is the one verb whose meaning survives being said once about a
set: *"I have looked at these flags and they are fine."*

The screen SAYS this rather than leaving a clerk to hunt for Override. If the PO
wants more verbs in bulk, the question to settle first is what a single reason
means when it is applied to readings that differ.

⚠ **THIS IS A CONTEXT LEAK BEING CLOSED, NOT A NEW RULING.** The PO said this on
2026-08-26 while reviewing the tenant-provisioning walkthrough. It went into an
HTML page that is deliberately not in the repo — at their instruction for THAT
artefact — and never into the repo at all. Then CR-039 wave F was written as
*"gated on PO figures"*, **which is false: the figures were already given.** A
wave sat marked blocked on a decision that had been made, because the decision
lived in a chat window. That is hard-won law 10 exactly, and it cost this CR a
wave's worth of standing still.

**PO verbatim, 2026-08-26:**

> *"we have 2 or 3 busines smodel - 1 we have self serve, 6 months, 9 months,
> 12 months and custom implementation plan, then we have subscrption plan -
> currently we ahve $1000,$5000,$8000 plan and then we have add-on"*

**What is settled by those words, and is buildable now:**

| Piece | What the PO said | State in the product |
|---|---|---|
| **Subscription plans** | *"$1000, $5000, $8000"* | **ALREADY BUILT AND SEEDED** — `tenancy/migrations/0005` holds starter $1,000.00 (≤300 accounts) · growth $5,000.00 (300–1,000) · scale $8,000.00 (1,000–3,000), all USD, verified on a live cluster. These are not new. |
| **Implementation terms** | *"self serve, 6 months, 9 months, 12 months and custom"* | **NOT BUILT.** Five options, of which `self serve` and `custom` are not durations. |
| **Add-ons** | *"and then we have add-on"* | **NOT BUILT**, and no add-on is named or priced. |

**⚠ THREE THINGS THE WORDS DO NOT SETTLE, and they are not guessed here:**

1. **Is the 6/9/12 a CONTRACT TERM on the subscription, or the DURATION of an
   implementation project?** The sentence puts them beside *"implementation
   plan"*, which reads as the latter; wave F's task 24 was written as *"term on

2. **What IS `self serve`** — a fifth term of length zero, or the ABSENCE of an

3. **No add-on is named or priced.** *"we have add-on"* establishes that they

**So wave F's gate moves rather than lifting: it is no longer waiting on the
MODEL — the PO gave that — it is waiting on those three, which are much smaller

## 2026-08-27 — four PO rulings from the nineteen-decision batch

### 1 · A demand reading carries kW — and a NEW general rule comes with it

**PO verbatim:** *"A demand reading carries kW - we have to match utility service
unit and meter reading unit - if it does not match then we have intriduce
multiplier factor on meter. you will ahve to seed that data."*

Closes **OQ-391** on option (a), and **fixes the money in DEF-797**: a **412 kW**
peak billed as 14 kWh charged **$154.00** where the correct charge is
**$4,532.00**.

**The ruling has two halves and the second is bigger than the question asked.**

* **(a)** A demand reading carries **kW**. The unit is recorded per REGISTER
  rather than per meter, so one meter holds kWh on its energy register and kW on
  its demand register.
* **(b) THE GENERAL RULE, new:** the **utility service's unit** and the **meter
  reading's unit** must MATCH. Where they do not, a **multiplier factor on the
  meter** reconciles them, and that data is **seeded**.

**⚠ ONE CONSEQUENCE OF APPLYING (b) HONESTLY, STATED RATHER THAN RESOLVED IN
SILENCE.** A multiplier is a **scale** factor — it reconciles ccf → kgal, or a
×10 register, or raw gallons → kgal (which B4's own OQ-004 already describes:
*"register stores raw gallons; billed unit per-service config … convert at
rating input"*). **It cannot reconcile kW → kWh, because those are different
physical quantities** — power against energy — and no multiplier turns one into
the other.

So the rule is applied as: **a reading's unit must match the unit of the thing
that PRICES it.** An energy register's kWh matches the energy charge; a demand
register's kW matches the demand charge, which is already per-kW. Where two
units differ by SCALE, the meter's multiplier reconciles them and is seeded.
Where they differ by DIMENSION, they are different quantities priced by
different charges and are never summed (CLAUDE.md hard rule 3).

That reading is the merge lane's, not the PO's words, and is flagged here so it
can be corrected rather than discovered later.

### 2 · A corrected jurisdiction is FORWARD ONLY, and owes nothing backwards

**PO verbatim:** *"(a) Forward only, and nothing else"*. Closes **OQ-423**.

A premises marked on the wrong side of the city line and corrected six months
later affects **the next bill and no earlier one**. The roughly **$350** already
billed the other way stands. No automatic adjustment is raised and no flag asks
a clerk to consider one — *"and nothing else"* is the operative half of the
ruling. This is consistent with hard rule 4 (an issued invoice is immutable) and
now settles the question that rule left open.

### 3 · Sewer takes 40% of the PRE-surcharge water figure

**PO verbatim:** *"(b) Sewer takes 40% of the pre-surcharge water figure"*.
Closes **OQ-424**. Worked: an outside-city address bills sewer at **$43.60**,
not $65.40.

**⚠ THIS IS NOT A CHANGE TO A ❄️ FROZEN FIGURE, AND THE CHECK WAS RUN BEFORE THE
RULING WAS APPLIED.** The 40% is untouched. What moves is what *"water
usage-charge dollars"* MEANS when a surcharge exists — and B4 could not have
said, because **B4 was frozen on 2026-08-08 and the outside-city surcharge
(BR-RAT-101/102) was ruled on 2026-08-21, thirteen days later.** B4 line 70
reads *"percent of water usage-charge dollars (excl. base/tax)"*: it excludes
base and tax and is silent on the surcharge. **No golden test covers sewer**, so
GT-1..61 does not move.

So this is the PO resolving what two signed sentences mean together, which is
exactly what OQ-424 raised. It is recorded as an amendment to **BR-RAT-015's
SCOPE** — the base the percentage is taken of — and not as an edit to a frozen
number.

#### ⚠⚠ CORRECTION 2026-08-27 — one sentence above is FALSE, and it is the one that cleared the freeze (`DEF-860`)

The paragraph above reads *"**No golden test covers sewer**, so GT-1..61 does
not move."* **Golden tests cover sewer in five frozen workbook composites.**

· GT-28 (WE-12) — and at least two of those sewer amounts are frozen figures

10.60 (was 15.80)`** (`04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/08-worked-examples.md`
lines 50 and 80).

**The repo already contradicted the claim.** `apps/rating/engine.py`'s

**THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES — the evidence does not, and the difference matters

## 2026-08-27 — OQ-394 built, OQ-424 STOPPED at the freeze check that was supposed to clear it

**One lane, two rulings, and only one of them shipped.** Recorded together
because the reason the second did not ship is the useful half.

### OQ-394 — the move-out box opens with the last reading, and its AGE rides with it

PO verbatim: *"(a) Box opens with 42,864 in it"*. **BR-CUS-021 said *prefill*
all along**, so this restores the written rule and reverses the CR-038 W9 lane's
divergence rather than changing anything. Built for BOTH move wizards through
one hook (`useReadsDraft`), because a prefill that shipped on move-out and not
move-in is how BR-CUS-021 came to mean two things in the first place.

**THE COST IS ON THE SCREEN, because the PO ruled WITH IT IN FRONT OF THEM.** A
clerk in a hurry presses Next; an eight-day-old number closes the account, bills
the final invoice and becomes what the next occupant is measured from, and those
eight days bill as **zero**. So the reading's DATE travels with the number on
the control — *"Last read 42,864 kWh · read 8 days ago"* — and the panel says
once, up front, that the numbers were typed by nobody here.

**THREE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE where the ruling ran out, stated rather than
smuggled:**

1. **The prefilled value is TRIMMED and never GROUPED.** The wire carries
   BR-MET-019's `NUMERIC(18,6)`, so the register arrives as `42864.000000`; the
   PO was shown `42,864`. The box gets `42864` — DEF-646's rule, extracted to
   `UnitCell.trimQuantity` so there is ONE derivation. It is deliberately NOT
   the grouped form, because `42,864` in an input reaches the server inside the
   decimal the clerk submits.
2. **The consumption clause was dropped from that line.** It used to read
   *"…· 684 kWh since the one before"*. The ruling's whole safety is that the
   age is SKIMMED, and a third clause is what a skim loses. The full inventory
   panel above still shows consumption.
3. **A register with no committed read still opens EMPTY.** The prefill does not
   weaken *"nothing is invented"*: a blank register reaches no payload row, not
   as `0`, not as `null`.

**AND THE FIRST BUILD OF IT HAD A HOLE THAT EVERY TEST WOULD HAVE PASSED.** The
obvious shape is a `useEffect` that seeds the draft once the assets land. It
renders correctly and it runs AFTER paint — so for one frame the box shows
`42,864` while the state the payload is built from is still `{}`, and a submit
in that frame posts NOTHING while the screen shows a number. **Nothing here
would have caught it**, because `renderToStaticMarkup` runs no effects at all
and reports green. The prefill is DERIVED instead (`effectiveReadsDraft`): the
prior finals are the floor, the clerk's entries are laid over them, and the
value on screen and the value in the payload are the same expression at every
instant. **The transferable half is the diagnosis, not the fix:** an SSR test
suite cannot see a race that lives between paint and effect, so state that a
SUBMIT reads should be derived rather than seeded.

**NO BACKEND CHANGE, AND NONE IS OWED** —
`metering.selectors._last_read_position` has served `read_at`, `current_value`
and `unit` since W5. Nothing in `apps/metering/` was touched.

### OQ-424 — ruled, recorded, and NOT BUILT

See the correction above. The lane was told to verify three freeze checks and to
stop if any was wrong; the third was wrong. **The rule it protects is worth the
stop:** the sewer basis produces GT-17's signed `$15.80`, and a lane amending
the basis of a rule that feeds a frozen figure on the strength of a false
coverage claim is exactly the failure HUMAN-GUIDE §6 exists to prevent — even
though, in this instance, the figure demonstrably does not move.

## 2026-08-27 — two more rulings, both AGAINST the lane's recommendation

Recorded as such deliberately. A recommendation is advice; the ruling is the
decision, and a log that only records agreement is a log nobody can audit.

### 5 · The move-out box OPENS WITH the last reading in it

**PO verbatim:** *"(a) Box opens with 42,864 in it"*. Closes **OQ-394**.

⚠ **This RESTORES the written rule and reverses a lane's divergence.**
BR-CUS-021 said *prefill* all along; the CR-038 W9 lane read it as ambiguous,
built the empty box with the prior read in the help line, and flagged that it
had chosen. The PO has now chosen, the other way, and the written rule stands as
written.

**The cost that was put to them, restated so it is not lost in the closure:** a
clerk in a hurry presses Next, and an eight-day-old number closes the account,
bills the final invoice and becomes what the next occupant is measured from —
those eight days bill as **zero**. The PO ruled with that in front of them.

**What the build must therefore carry:** the prefilled value is only safe if the
clerk can SEE it is old. The reading's **date** travels with the number on the
control rather than in a help line below it, so *"42,864 kWh · read 8 days
ago"* is what a person skims. That is the merge lane's reading of how to
implement the ruling safely, not an amendment to it, and it is flagged as such.

**PO verbatim:** *"(b) Store it per meter too - otherwise we will ahve to
calculate it again and again"*. Closes **OQ-421**, with the reason given:

content of the question.** Adding the dimension is a migration; removing it

## 2026-08-27 — items 3, 14 and 18: a delegated choice, a confirmation, and a half-answer

### 3 · The three unmapped read-method words — the PO DELEGATED the choice, and here is what was chosen and why

**PO verbatim:** *"(a) Rule each onto one of the five or you can add new
categories"*. Closes **OQ-392**, and hands the lane an authority it did not have
before: the vocabulary may GROW.

**The three words are `drive_by`, `self_read` and `field_visit`**, and the
question was whether each is really one of Manual · Walk-by · AMI · AMR · Mobile.

**CHOSEN: add all three as new categories, taking the vocabulary from five to
eight.** The reasoning, recorded because the choice was delegated rather than
made:

* **Each records a genuinely different fact.** `self_read` is about **who** read
  the meter — the customer did. `field_visit` is about **why** somebody went —
  a technician attended. `mobile` is about **what device** was used. Folding
  self-read into Manual would assert that a customer's own reading and a clerk's
  are the same kind of record; folding field-visit into Mobile would assert a
  technician's visit is a device choice. Neither is true.
* **Mapping would RE-LABEL history that nobody verified.** Every reading already
  collected under those three words would silently become something it was not
  recorded as. Adding categories keeps every historical reading exactly what it
  said it was, and **turns "not stated" into an accurate value rather than a
  guessed one** — which is the outcome the W3 lane refused to fake and the PO
  originally left open.
* **It costs nothing that mapping saves.** Both answers close the question and
  unblock the backfill; only one of them can be wrong about a reading.

⚠ **The repo contradicts itself on one of these and that stays a finding, not a
justification.** A demo fixture comment calls Mobile *"the seeded read-method
code for a drive-by round"* — asserting drive-by ≈ Mobile by comment. That
comment was never a decision and is now simply wrong; the build corrects it.

### 14 · A cutover opening read is an ORDINARY UPLOAD

**PO verbatim:** *"a) An ordinary upload that happens to be first"*. Closes
**OQ-419**. No sixth event context is minted; the five stay five. Onboarding
uses the reads rail exactly as it stands, which is what it already does — so
this ruling REMOVES a task rather than adding one.

### 18 · The transfer gets `TRF-26-0001` — and the disconnect half is NOT answered

**PO verbatim:** *"Transfer TRF-26-0001 recommend it is one job spanning two
accounts, and neither account number names it - follow same logic that we are
following for other numbers we have did in settings."* Closes **OQ-426**.

The transfer series joins the numbering catalogue the same way every other
series does — a catalogue row, its list of offered formats with the seeded
default first, editable per tenant in Settings, allocated inside the transaction
that creates the record. Day one is **TRF-26-0001**.

⚠ **OQ-427, THE DISCONNECT, IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOT ASSUMED CLOSED BY THIS.**
The ruling names the transfer and gives the transfer's reason — *"it is one job
spanning two accounts, and neither account number names it"* — and that reason
is precisely what does **not** transfer to a disconnect. A disconnect belongs to
**one** account, whose number already names it, and **r10 draws a disconnection
as a WORK ORDER — `WO-4833`**. So "don't give it a series, it is a work order"
remains a live and possibly correct answer, and reading the transfer ruling as
covering both would put a series on a record that may not want one. It goes back
to the PO as a single question.

## 2026-08-27 — item 2: the cap uses the VEE thresholds, and the second objection is still open

**PO verbatim:** *"We have high and low consuption rule in VEE engine - we ahve
to use that data"*.

**This answers the objection that mattered most, and answers it well.** The
prototype's *"Cap at 2×"* button was refused by the W8 lane on two grounds, and
the first was **BR-MET-020: no threshold is ever hardcoded.** A literal `2×` in
a bill run is exactly that. The PO's answer removes the objection rather than
overriding it: the thresholds **already exist**, per utility service, in the VEE
rules a tenant configures on S64 — high consumption and low consumption, with
their own ratified figures and their own per-service overrides. **A cap that
reads the tenant's own configured high rule invents nothing.**

That is the right shape and it is now the rule: **any consumption bound a bill
run applies comes from the tenant's configured VEE high/low rules for that
service, never from a number written into the bill run.**

### ⚠ The SECOND objection is not answered by this, and is not being treated as if it were

The W8 lane refused that button on **two** grounds. The second was that a cap
**edits a measured quantity** — and that is a hard-rule question, not a
threshold question.

**The worked case, restated:** a meter reads **26.24 kgal** against an **8.40
kgal** average. A cap bills less than the meter says. The **9.44 kgal**
difference is either water the utility never charges for, or a leak nobody
investigates — and which it is cannot be decided by a threshold.

**The lawful shape, which the product already has for estimation:** the READING
is never edited — it is measured, committed and append-only (hard rule 4). What
a bill run may do is record a **disposition** that bills a different quantity,
with a stated reason, an acting user and an audit row, leaving the reading
exactly as measured. Estimation already works that way.

**So the question that remains is not "what threshold" but "what quantity":**
when a reading breaches the configured high rule and a clerk chooses to cap,
**what is billed** — the trailing average, the threshold value itself, an
estimate, or the reading with a flag? Each is defensible and the product must
pick one. That is minted as **OQ-480**.

### And the ruling addresses ONE of the three buttons

Item 2 covered three: **cap at 2×** (answered above), **"Override" on an
estimated reading** (a clerk types a quantity that replaces a measured one), and
**"Change to ×1" on a meter factor** (writes the multiplier on the METER from
inside a bill run, silently repricing every future reading on it). The VEE-data
answer reaches the cap and does not reach the other two, which stay out pending
their own rules — **OQ-390 stays open for those two** rather than being closed
by a ruling that did not mention them.

## 2026-08-27 — items 4 and 8

### 4 · The read method JOINS the double-post key 🔒

**PO verbatim:** *"allow it if we are doing insert and update then we will use
same file"*. Closes **OQ-393** on option (b).

**The reasoning the PO gave is the requirement:** under **Insert & update**,
re-uploading the same file is the *expected operator workflow* — that is what
the mode is for — so a block that refuses the second upload is refusing the
thing the mode exists to do.

**⚠ THE COST WAS STATED IN THE BATCH AND THE PO RULED WITH IT IN FRONT OF THEM,
so it is recorded here rather than re-argued:** adding a field changes what an
identical re-upload computes, so **every batch posted before this change stops
colliding with itself** and the double-post block stops protecting the history
already on file. This is 🔒 idempotency — CLAUDE.md rule 6 — which is why it was
never a lane's call.

**⚠ ONE THING THE RULING RAISES THAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and it comes from the
PO's own sentence.** They justified it by naming **the write mode** — *"if we
are doing insert and update"*. The write mode is now a column on every batch
(CR-038 W7). So there are two ways to get the behaviour they asked for:

* put the **read method** in the key, which is what the question asked and what
  is ruled; or
* put the **write mode** in the key, which matches their reasoning more directly
  — a re-upload in a *different mode* is a different intent, and a re-upload in
  the *same* mode arguably still is a double post.

They are not the same rule and they refuse different things. The ruled one is
built; the second is raised as **OQ-481** rather than assumed, because guessing
here changes what the product refuses.

### 8 · A SKIPPED setup step DOES get an audit row

**PO verbatim:** *"(b) Record skips too - yes we need to know what is skipped as
well"*. **Reverses BR-TEN-083 clause 4**, which was the CR-039 wave B lane's own
judgment, flagged as PROPOSED for exactly this reason.

The lane's reasoning was that a skip is a platform gap identical on every
tenant, and a row per tenant per run would bury the failures that are actually
about that tenant. The PO has weighed that and wants the visibility anyway:
**what was skipped is something an operator needs to know.**

**⚠ WHAT THE BUILD MUST THEREFORE DO, so the cost the lane named does not
materialise:** a skip and a failure must be **distinguishable in the trail at a
glance** — a different audit action, not the same action with a different code
buried in its payload. The lane's concern was that skips would drown failures;
the answer is not to omit them but to make them separable, so an operator asking
*"what went wrong on this tenant"* is not reading through a platform gap every
tenant shares.

Clause 4 of BR-TEN-083 is amended from PROPOSED to **CONFIRMED, reversed**.

## 2026-08-27 — item 11: REPLACE is removed, and the protection inside it stays

**PO verbatim:** *"we actaully needs Insert new only · Insert & update; repalce
you can remove"*. Closes **OQ-418 by removal** — the question was what `Replace`
does to a reading on file and not in the file, and there is no `Replace`.

**⚠ THIS REVERSES THE PO'S OWN EARLIER REQUIREMENT, AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING
PLAINLY.** On 2026-08-26 they asked for three modes by name: *"we need insert,
insert update, repalce option in step 1 of wirzard"*. CR-038 W7 built all three.
The mode is now withdrawn. Nothing was wasted that can be avoided next time —
W7's own report is what surfaced that two of the three behaved identically, and
that finding is what produced this ruling.

**Why it is the right call, in the product's own terms.** W7 measured that
`replace` and `insert & update` do the same thing to readings, because
*"supersedes a committed duplicate"* and *"supersedes everything the file
carries"* describe the same set of rows. A mode that cannot be distinguished
from another mode is a control that teaches an operator a difference that does
not exist.

### ⚠ The protection that lived inside Replace — CHECKED, and it survives

BR-MET-127 was written as *"Replace mode meets a billed read: the row is refused
by name"*. The obvious risk of deleting a mode is deleting the rule attached to
it.

**Measured rather than assumed:** `apps/metering/write_modes.py` reads
`SUPERSEDING_MODES = ("upsert", "replace")`, and BR-MET-127's own text already
says *"A Replace (or Insert & update) row…"*. **So the refusal was never
Replace-specific** — it attaches to any superseding mode, and `upsert` remains
one. Removing `replace` removes a mode, not a protection.

**Also checked: no seeded or demo data carries `write_mode="replace"`**, so the
removal strands no fixture.

**What the build must still do:** amend BR-MET-127's text so it stops naming a
mode that no longer exists — a rule describing a control nobody can reach is the
stale-comment failure (hard-won law 1), and this one would sit in the money
rules. And `read_write_modes` drops to two everywhere it is pinned: the
constant, the wizard's step 1, the batch column's accepted values, and the
eleven catalogues.

## 2026-08-27 · Item 7 — the true-up figure is RATIFIED, and item 9 is a decision NOT to build

Two rulings arrived together and they pull in opposite directions — one says
*build the proof*, the other says *leave the guard*. Both are recorded the same
way, because a decision not to build is a decision.

### Item 7 — RATIFIED. PO, verbatim:

> *"Item 7 Ratify the true-up figure - Confirm the figure and its refusal
> behaviour are ratified and pinned by a test"*

**What was shown, in plain English with its figures** (standing PO instruction
of 2026-08-11 — never an ID to go and look up): an account billed on two
estimated cycles totalling **1,236 kWh**, whose actual reading lands at
**1,410 kWh**, is trued up by **+174 kWh**. The money shown beside it is what
the pricing engine charges for that 174 on **that account's own tariff** — never
a rate `apps/billing/read_analysis.py` holds. It writes nothing. And when
pricing refuses to answer, the clerk sees the **quantity** with the refusal
**named**, rather than a number nobody computed.

**Both halves are ratified** — the figure AND the refusal behaviour. The PO
named the refusal explicitly, so it is inside the signature rather than beside
it. *A signature covers only what was shown*, and this one was shown both.

### What "pinned by a test" required, and what was actually missing

The instruction is part 2 of this repo's own definition of a human sign-off
(CLAUDE.md sensitive paths): *"a test asserts the ratified figure so drift goes
RED"*. Checked rather than assumed — and **the ratified figures were NOT
pinned**:

* `test_cr038_w8_read_analysis.py` TC-10 pins **53 ccf → $60.95**. That is
  **WE-13's** worked example, not the PO's. Neither 1,236 nor 1,410 nor 174
  appeared anywhere in the test suite.
* **No test covered the refusal path at all.** The behaviour the PO has just
  ratified — quantity shown, refusal named, no guessed amount — was
  implemented, documented in the file's own docstring, and asserted nowhere.

So the ratification landed on a figure a drift would have moved silently. Two
tests now hold it:

* **TC-15** — the PO's own case end to end: `estimated_total` 1,236,
  `register_delta` 1,410, quantity **174 kWh** carried on this bill, and its
  worth from the ENGINE's own usage line — 174 × 1.15 = **$200.10**.
* **TC-16** — pricing refuses: amount and currency are `None`, the quantity is
  still 174 kWh, the refusal names itself in `pricing_gap`, and the row does
  **not** vanish (a clerk who cannot see the reading cannot act on it).

**Proven RED first** (hard-won law 7), and without disturbing the shared working
tree: the engine's answer was drifted by one cent through a pytest plugin, and
TC-15 failed verbatim `AssertionError: assert '200.11' == '200.10'`.

### Item 9 — NOT BUILT, by ruling. PO, verbatim:

> *"Item 9 Two checks this repo specified and never built - leave it"*

The two were **(a)** nothing runs the migration-safety check (`makemigrations
--check` is a line lanes type in a report, and it had been failing for days
under a green claim — DEF-801), and **(b)** a version could be cut with no
changelog entry (DEF-806, `2.52.0`).

**Recorded honestly, because half of it already exists.** **(b) was built and
pushed before this ruling arrived** — it is clause 4 of
`10-scripts/gates/g35_version_lockstep.py`, it went in with the DEF-806 fix, and
it is green today. It also became load-bearing in the meantime: the PO's own
per-wave versioning ruling multiplied the number of bumps by roughly ten, and

"leave it" is read as *do not spend more work here*, and tearing out a working

**(a) is not built and will not be.** So the standing position, written down so

## 2026-08-27 · The seeded utility gets a financial history — and the celery answer is "no cron"

Four PO messages in one review of the provisioning trace. Captured whole as
**CR-040**; two things belong here rather than only in a CR.

### The reversal, named — because the same person signed both sides

**CR-010 Part-10.4, PO 2026-08-17: *"do 1 month billed na dkeep other month
ready"*** is **superseded** by **PO 2026-08-27: *"I want you to complete 2
billing cycle and create data for 3rd billing cycle"*.**

Three artefacts implement the old shape — the demo spec §3,
`core/sample_fixture.PERIODS` and `apps/billing/sample_data._periods_to_bill()`
— so a lane that "corrected" them without this entry would be erasing a signed
decision rather than executing a new one.

**Checked, not assumed: it is NOT a ❄️ FROZEN figure.** B4/B5 say nothing about
how many months a demo carries. No re-sign, no golden test moves.

**And the old ruling's INTENT survives.** *"everything done leaves nothing to
evaluate"* is why one period stays unbilled, and acceptance item 4 is *"run the
August billing run"*. August is still the PO's own run. The count rises; the
acceptance test does not move.

### The design answer, written down because it was asked in chat and would evaporate

The PO's question, verbatim: *"if you want to run 2 billing cycle then you will
need multiple cron jobs run by celery … how will you handle this"*.

**No cron jobs, and no second worker.** A bill run is an **inline service call**
— `apps/billing/runs.py` says so in its own docstring: *"It runs INLINE. There is
no job runner in this project."* All five phases are ordinary functions that
return when done, and the seeder **already drives all five** through the doors
S31 uses (`create_run` → `prepare_run` → `calculate_run` → `authorise_release` →
`release_run`). It writes no invoice rows.

So a second cycle is **a second pass of a loop that already exists**:
`_periods_to_bill()` returns the fixture periods flagged `billed`, and today
exactly one is.

**What celery IS for here:** the seed itself (CR-017, `apps/tenancy/tasks.py`),
so signup returns immediately. One background job walking blocks in dependency
order — which is precisely the ordering the PO's own sentence describes. **Beat
is deliberately unconfigured** and that is recorded, not accidental: scheduled
billing for a live tenant is a different feature with a run-exactly-once
constraint.

**The ordering is the requirement, not the contents.** A refund written after
both runs is a row; a refund written between them is a history, and only the
second bills differently. An overcharge correction cannot exist before run 1 at
all — it corrects a bill that has issued.

### Two defects the audit found, both filed

* **DEF-890** — CR-039 captured *"you need master accounts and regualr acconts …
  there will be opening balance on the account"* verbatim on 2026-08-26 and its
  28-task list carries no task for either. The capture step worked; the
  carry-into-scope step dropped two sentences, and **the PO repeating themselves
  is the only detector that exists.**
* **DEF-891** — the 33-account chart IS seeded at provisioning (so the PO's
  *"part of Step 1 itself"* is already satisfied for the chart), but every reason
  code and every tender seeds with a **NULL GL pointer**. Lawful — NULL falls
  back to Undeposited funds by design — and it means every seeded payment sits in
  1010 and never reaches a bank account. `BILLERR — Billing error correction`,
  the reason an overcharge would use, points at no revenue account at all.
## 2026-08-27 — items 12 and 13 BUILT, and the four judgments the build had to make

The rulings themselves are recorded above (item 12, store the twelve-month usage
per meter; item 13, a counter reading on a meter with no cycle is accepted and
warned). This section is the **build lane's** own judgments — the places where
the ruling did not reach and somebody had to decide. Each is recorded with its
worked figure, before it was reported to anyone.

### A · The stored per-meter figure is a CACHE, and the screen falls back to computing

**The ruling did not say what happens when no row has been written yet**, and
that state is reachable on every real tenant today (see DEF-871 below). Two
options were live: serve an empty strip, exactly as the account tab does when it
has never been recomputed, or compute the figure on the spot and say so.

**Decided: compute and say so.** The payload publishes `source: "stored"` or
`source: "computed_from_reads"`, and a reader always knows which they are
looking at.

⚠ **This is not a hedge, it is the answer to the asymmetry the PO ruled
against.** OQ-421 put it to them that adding the dimension is a migration and
removing it later is a dropped column with data in it. The fallback makes the
reversal cheap in MEANING even though it is not cheap in SCHEMA: every column is
derivable from `meter_reads`, so **dropping the table returns the product to its
2026-08-26 behaviour and loses no statement about any customer**. A test deletes
every row and asserts the payload comes back point for point identical.

### B · The register is part of the key, so DEF-798's 698 is unrepresentable

DEF-798 measured **684 + 14 = 698 kWh where the truth is 684** — a demand
peak-delta landing in an energy total. It was fixed at the source on 2026-08-26.

**Storing a figure freezes whatever the derivation gets wrong**, so this build
did not merely inherit that fix, it made the wrong answer impossible to write:
the stored grain is (tenant, **asset, channel**, period_month), so Sarah's meter
M-4412 stores **two rows** — `total 684.000000 kWh` and `demand 14.000000 kWh` —
and there is no code path in the writer that adds two registers together,
because the bucket key IS the register. Her account's own row still reads
**684.000000 kWh**.

### C · One derivation held by CONSTRUCTION, not by discipline

The ruling's one constraint is that the stored row must come from *"the SAME
functions the computed figure uses, not a second implementation"*. A comment
saying so would have been a comment (hard-won law 1), so it is structural:

  * `monthly_usage_service._fact_rows` is now **the single place a `meter_reads`
    row becomes a `ReadFact`** in this product. The account grain groups those
    pairs by SERVICE; the meter grain groups the same pairs by (ASSET, CHANNEL).
    Neither can see a read the other cannot.
  * `asset_usage._series_for` is **one serialiser** taking `MonthFigure`s.
    Below that line the payload cannot tell a stored month from a computed one,
    so they cannot be rendered, rounded or measured differently.
  * Both grains are written by **one `recompute_account` call in one
    transaction**, so they can never be stale relative to each other — the S21
    tab and the S50 strip cannot tell one customer two stories about one July.

### D · Two BR ids minted, and one of them because an id had already collided

**BR-MET-141** is the per-meter stored grain. **BR-MET-140** is the counter-read
warning — **not BR-MET-139, which the OQ-422 closure line pointed at and which
CR-039 wave E had already taken** for the seeded-premises rule. Filed as
**DEF-870** and corrected in place with the collision stamped, because a reader
who remembers "139" must be able to see what happened.

⚠ **ONE THING WAS FOUND AND NOT FIXED, AND IT IS THE LARGER OF THE TWO:
DEF-871.** Measured across the whole backend, `recompute_account`'s only
non-test caller is `sample_data._recompute_cr030_monthly_usage`. **Nothing
recomputes when a read is committed.** So on a real tenant the S21 Usage tab
serves an empty series and every month absent however many reads have posted,
and the new per-meter rows fill only for the demo estate. Hard-won law 2 —
built is not wired — and it is older than this build. The trigger belongs in
`services.commit_read_batch`, which is a shared file two sibling lanes hold
today and which wants a performance judgment on a 1,247-row batch that this
lane cannot make alone. **Filed, reported, not fixed.**

### E · Migration 0039 depends on 0037, and the integrator must re-point it

A sibling lane holds `0038` in the same session and its file is not on this
branch, so `0039_oq421_asset_monthly_usage` depends on the highest number
actually present here. **At merge the dependency must be re-pointed at 0038**
or Django refuses with *"multiple leaf nodes in the migration graph"*.
Linearise, do not add a merge node — rating 0018 records the same call and the
reason: a merge node is a no-op that documents nothing, and both migrations are
purely additive so the order carries no meaning to recover.

The DDL and the RLS policy are in **one** migration rather than the 0024/0025
and 0033/0034 pairs, because one number was allocated to this lane. The
un-split form is strictly safer: there is no instant at which the table exists
without `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.

### F · The NARROW recompute path moves both grains too, scoped to one month

`recompute_month` is the entry point a read CORRECTION uses — it exists so a
late read can restate the month it touched without walking an account's whole
history. Wiring the meter grain only into `recompute_account` would have left
the ruling's constraint holding **on the path nobody takes**: a corrected July
would leave the account saying 700 kWh and the meter saying 684.

So `recompute_account_assets` takes an optional `only_month`, and
`recompute_month` passes it.

⚠ **AND THE SCOPE HAD TO COVER THE WITHDRAWAL SWEEP, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT
WOULD HAVE BITTEN.** That sweep asks *"which stored heads did I not see this
run?"* and withdraws them. An unscoped sweep inside a scoped call would have
answered "every other month" — May's 412 kWh would have gone silently ABSENT
while the caller was told `"restated"`, and nothing would have failed. Both
halves are filtered by the same value, and TC-9 asserts the May figure survives
a July correction.

### G · Two frontend/backend gates were RED before this lane started, and stay red

Recorded so the next lane does not spend an hour on them or, worse, assume this
build broke them:

  * **G18** (i18n call sites) — 1 key used in code and defined in no catalogue
    (`settings.routes.detail.unitsOnStop`) and 181 catalogue keys with no call
    site. Identical before and after this lane, key for key.
  * **G33** (refusal copy length) — 31 over-long messages against a baseline of
    0. None of them is this lane's; the keys added here are warnings rather
    than refusals and G33 measures only keys raised by a backend
    `message_key=`.
  * **G7**, **G15** and **G27** are likewise red on rows this lane does not
    own, and **G38** reports its ratchet is one BELOW its baseline (71 vs 72)
    on a gain earned by somebody else's commit — this lane touched no
    `ArrivesWith`, so turning that ratchet is not its edit to make.

`makemigrations --check`, `G23`, `G26`, `G31`, `G35` and `G40` are green.

## 2026-08-27 — items 3, 14 and 18 BUILT: what the build found that the rulings could not

The three rulings above are the WHAT. This entry is the HOW and, more usefully,
the four things the build discovered that nobody could have known when the
rulings were written. Written by the lane that built them, in the same commits.

### 18 · The transfer series is in the catalogue — `TRF-26-0001` on day one

`core.numbering.TRANSFER` joins `SERIES_CATALOG` as
`("TRF-{YY}-{0000}", "TRF-{YYYY}-{0000}", "TRF-{0000}", "XFR-{YY}{MM}-{000}", "{000000}")`
in group **`customers_premises`**. The catalogue grows **25 → 26** and
`apps.tenancy.services.SERIES_DEFAULTS` derives from it, so a provisioned tenant
holds a `transfer` row at `TRF-{YY}-{0000}` and the FIRST transfer it starts is
numbered **`TRF-26-0001`** — asserted as a literal exactly once, in
`test_the_first_transfer_on_a_new_tenant_is_trf_26_0001`, and re-derived
everywhere else so no test and no catalogue can pick independently (DEF-615).

**Three judgments the ruling left to the build, each recorded because a later
reader will otherwise read them as arbitrary:**

* **GROUP — `customers_premises`, not `work`.** `connection` sits in `work`
  because a new connect is a FIELD job: somebody is dispatched. A transfer is an
  ACCOUNT-lifecycle job — nobody goes anywhere, the record lives in
  `apps/customers/transfers.py`, and S89 is a Customers screen. An admin hunting
  for *"Transfer #"* looks where accounts and premises are.
* **APPENDED AT THE END OF THE DICT.** This dict's order IS the order S8 prints,
  and the frontend buckets the flat list by group — so a `customers_premises`
  row appended last renders last inside *Customers & premises* and **moves no
  shipped row at all.** `CUSTOMER`'s own comment made this argument first; this
  is the second time it has paid.
* **`MV-` IS NOT OFFERED, not merely not defaulted.** OQ-426's option B noted
  that *move* is the product's own word but that it PRE-EMPTS CR-039 tasks
  17–19. That warning applies to OFFERING it as much as to defaulting to it: a
  tenant who picks `MV-` for transfers has decided a vocabulary question the PO
  has not been asked. `XFR-` is offered instead — an abbreviation of the same
  word this series already owns.

⛔ **`disconnect_cases.case_no` WAS NOT TOUCHED.** `OQ-427` is open;
`disconnects.py` still allocates by name, still reports `numbering_series_missing`
with its OQ id, and `test_the_transfer_series_is_catalogued_and_the_disconnect_is_still_not`
now guards exactly that asymmetry.

**A FIFTH HAND-PINNED PLACE, AND IT FOUND ITSELF.** OQ-426's closing paragraph
listed four places that move together. There were five:
`tests/test_cr039_wd_transfer_and_case_numbers.py` held a guard written *to* go
red on this day, whose failure message was the checklist — *"delete it and add
the prefix to EXPECTED_PREFIX, the size in test_cr005_numbering_set08, and the
`wired` set + both counts in test_cr005_numbering_reaches_records."* It fired
first and it was right. **A guard that names its own successor is worth more
than a guard that merely fails**, and it is the cheapest thing in this commit.

⚠ **AND A SIXTH THAT NOBODY LISTED: THE LABEL. See DEF-880.** Adding
`settings.numbering.series.transfer` to eleven catalogues surfaced that the
family held **22 labels for 25 series** — `connection`, `customer` and
`bill_run` each added a catalogue row and none added its label, so three rows of
a shipped S8 table printed `settings.numbering.series.connection` and its two
siblings at a System Admin, in every language. **G18 cannot see this and that is
its design:** any literal that is a proper dotted prefix of a catalogue key names
the whole family, so ONE member existing satisfies the gate; nothing compares a
family's members to the enumeration that generates them. All three are fixed and
`test_def880_every_catalogued_series_has_a_label_on_the_settings_screen` now
walks `SERIES_CATALOG` against `en.json`, RED-proved by removing the transfer
key (*"1 catalogued number series has no label on S8 and will print its raw key:
['transfer']"*).

### 3 · The read-method vocabulary is EIGHT, and `not_stated` became honest

`SEED_READ_METHODS` grows **5 → 8** with `drive_by` "Drive-by", `self_read`
"Self-read" and `field_visit` "Field visit", and
`read_import.LEGACY_READ_METHOD_BY_DETAIL` grows **3 → 6** so that all six
legacy `source_detail` words now map — **each to its own word, none to a
neighbour's.**

**⚠ NO COMMITTED READING IS REWRITTEN AND NO MIGRATION BACKFILLS ONE.** Hard
rule 4 makes an issued reading append-only and several of these are billed; the
translation stays where BR-MET-123 put it, in a declared dict applied ON READ,
and `read_method_origin` still says `derived` for every one of them. What
changed is that the derivation can now be EXACT. Before today a reading tagged
`drive_by` served **no method at all** (`not_stated`) because the W3 lane
refused to guess; today it serves `drive_by`, which is what it always said.

**Delivery, and why there is no migration for it either.** The fixture serial
moves (see the entry in `reference_sweep.RATIFIED_FIXTURE_DIGESTS`) so the sweep
revisits existing tenants — but the load-bearing path is
`ensure_reference_catalogs()`, a `get_or_create` safety net that runs on every
asset write AND on `reference_list_options`, which is what the S28 wizard calls
to draw the picker. So the three words reach a tenant the first time anyone
opens the screen that would use them. `account_statuses` needed
`customers.0025` because nothing on its write path re-seeds it; this list has
exactly that, and a migration would be a second delivery mechanism for a job
already done.

**THE STALE COMMENT IS CORRECTED, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS WAS EVER
AMBIGUOUS.** `core/sample_fixture.py` called `mobile` *"the seeded read-method
code for a drive-by round"* — asserting `drive_by ≈ Mobile` **by comment**,
which OQ-392 flagged as the repo contradicting itself. It was never a decision
and the ruling makes it simply wrong. The fixture's water meter now carries
`drive_by` on both the meter and the batch, which is what its own
`source_detail` said all along. **A comment claiming a rule is not the rule**
(hard-won law 1).

### 14 · The opening-reads rail needs nothing, VERIFIED rather than assumed

The ruling — *"a) An ordinary upload that happens to be first"* — removes a task,
and a "nothing to do" that is wrong is worse than a task, so it was measured:

* `models.EVENT_CONTEXTS` still holds **five** values and gains none. A cutover
  read carries `event_context = NULL`, which is what every ordinary import and
  manual batch already carries — no branch, no default, no sixth word.
* **The reads rail genuinely is the target.** `import_runs.TARGETS` is
  `(premises, units, assets_meters, assets_submeters, assets_devices, accounts)`
  — six, ending at accounts — and opening reads do NOT belong to it: they post
  through the S28 stage → validate → commit pipeline, which is a different rail
  and a complete one.
* ⚠ **OQ-419's own claim that the documented order *"STOPS at Accounts"* in all
  three places was WRONG WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, and this is worth more than the
  ruling.** Measured on 2026-08-27, all three name the fifth step:
  `account_import.TEMPLATE_NOTES` — *"Import order (BR-CUS-047): premises ->
  units+plans -> assets -> ACCOUNTS -> opening reads."*, present since the file
  was created; `import_rules.py:786` and `import_runs.py:648` say the same. So
  option **D**, the half that *"needs no ruling at all"*, was **already built**
  and had been all along. What stops at accounts is the RUNNER's target list,
  which is a different fact and the correct one. **The lesson is not that the
  question was wasted — it is that a measurement quoted from a neighbouring
  module's prose is not a measurement.**

**Nothing was built for item 14 and nothing is owed.** The confirmation is
written into the OQ, into CR-038's coverage row and into CR-039's own list so the
next agent does not re-open it.

## 2026-08-27 · OQ-490 — every tender clears through Undeposited funds, and reconciliation is named as a separate problem

**PO, verbatim:**

> *"reconcilaition is a seperate problem - (a) Undeposited funds is the answer
> for every tender — no chart change, nothing to re-sign, and the demo's cash
> sits in one bucket by design"*

**What was put to them, in plain English with the measured figure:** every
adjustment reason and every payment method a new tenant gets points at **no GL
account at all** (DEF-891), and the signed chart holds only **two** cash-side
accounts — `1000 Cash` and `1010 Undeposited funds` — with **no per-tender
clearing account**. The cost, measured on the seeded tenant: **every payment
ever taken, all of June's ~95% collection, sits in 1010 and never reaches a bank
account.** Three options were shown: (a) rule Undeposited funds the answer for
every tender; (b) add per-tender clearing accounts and take a **finance
re-sign**, because that adds rows to ❄️ FROZEN B5 line 74; (c) leave both
columns NULL and drop the task.

**Ruled (a).** So CR-040 **task A2 is unblocked and needs no schema change and
no re-sign**: the tenders are seeded pointing at the `undeposited_funds`
designation, which is the account the code already falls back to. The behaviour
does not move; what moves is that the value becomes **stated** rather than
absent, and a gate can then hold it.

### ⚠ The PO named the cost in their own words, which makes it a decision

*"reconciliation is a separate problem"*. That is exactly the consequence option
(a) carries — one cash bucket, and bank reconciliation with nothing to
reconcile against per tender — and it is now **accepted deliberately** rather
than shipped by omission. Written down here because the difference between those
two is invisible in the database and total in review.

### ⚠⚠ THIS CLOSES THE TENDER HALF ONLY — the reason codes are NOT ruled

The question carried two halves. The ruling names one: *"the answer for every
**tender**"*. **A signature covers only what was shown** (PO 2026-08-11), so
**A1 stays open** and returns to the agenda rather than being folded in.

**And the argument for it is different in kind, which is why folding it in would
be wrong:** the right revenue account for a billing-error credit is the
**service's** — 4110 Water, 4100 Electric — a property of *the bill being
corrected*, not of *the reason a clerk picked*. Choosing one revenue account per
reason code would state something the money does not agree with. On top of that,
`reason_codes.default_gl_account_id` has **no backend reader anywhere** today:
no posting path consults it, so seeding it would set a value nothing uses.

**What the build does now:** A2 and A3 (the tenders, and the guard that keeps
them mapped). A1 waits.
## 2026-08-27 — BR-MET-143 built: the demand ruling, DEF-797's money, and one id collision

⚠ **RENUMBERED FROM `BR-MET-141` TO `BR-MET-143` AT MERGE (DEF-892).** This
section was written as `BR-MET-141` and the lane was right to think that free:
it read the register, found `BR-MET-140` already taken by a sibling and moved
on. **A THIRD lane had taken `141`, uncommitted, nineteen minutes earlier.**
Three lanes, four rules, two ids — and every branch internally consistent, so
no lane's own tests, gates or review could see it. By the resolution rule
DEF-892 records, the rule written first keeps the number: `BR-MET-141` is the
per-meter stored grain, and this rule is **143**. **Not one word of the rule
changed; only its identifier.**

Implements §1 of *"four PO rulings from the nineteen-decision batch"* above. That
section RECORDED the ruling; this one records what building it decided.

### The worked number, because a rule without one cannot be checked

A **412 kW** peak on the seeded Industrial schedule's **$11.00/kW**:

| | quantity | unit | charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (DEF-797) | `14.000000` — the delta 412 − 398 | `kWh` | **$154.00** |
| after (BR-MET-143) | `412.000000` — the peak itself | `kW` | **$4,532.00** |

**$4,378.00 on one commercial account in one month**, and the wrong unit was
printed on an issued document. Both halves were separate defects sharing one
line of code, which is why DEF-797's own row warns *"Do NOT 'fix' this by
changing the stored unit alone — the quantity is wrong, not only its label"*.

### Three judgments this lane made where the rules ran out

**1 · A DEMAND REGISTER IS A MAXIMUM, SO IT HAS NO DELTA — and that is
BR-MET-051 read literally, not an invention.** *"Manual demand-register value at
cycle read"*. `validation.compute_consumption` ran BR-MET-019's `(current −
prior) × multiplier` on every channel; a maximum register now returns its VALUE.
The precedent is already in that function: CR-038 W6's DEVICE branch does the
same for an inverter's period quantity. ⚠ **The multiplier IS applied to a peak**
— a CT ratio scales kW to kW, the same dimension, which is exactly the case the
new ruling covers. It is 1 on every seeded and every imported meter, so no
existing figure moved; it is named here because a reader is entitled to know a
peak is scaled and why.

**2 · WHERE `kW` COMES FROM.** It is TRANSCRIBED from three statements the repo
already held — `rate_schedules.demand_rate_per_kw` (B2's own column name),
`SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS["electric"] == ("kWh", "kW")` with `kW` scoped to electric
in the seeded UoM catalog, and r10's screen string *"Demand (peak kW)"*. **An
energy unit with no declared demand unit gets NONE**: a tenant metering demand in
kVA is refused by the existing `unit_missing` integrity rule rather than stamped
`kW`. Hard rule 3 has no assume branch and hard-won law 3 says the unsafe option
is the one you type.

**3 · ×1 IS THE RECONCILIATION, NOT A PLACEHOLDER.** The PO asked for the
multiplier data to be seeded. `EstatePlan.multiplier` is now DERIVED from the
tenant's own `primary_uom` against its `billed_uom` rather than typed as the
literal `"1"` `meter_plan` carried. **It resolves to `1` on every tenant alive**,
because r6.4 made `billed_uom` an option and nothing seeds it — so the two units
are the same string and there is nothing to reconcile. A SCALE mismatch seeds the
tenant's OWN `conversion_factor`. **A scale mismatch with no factor, a DIMENSION
mismatch, and an unknown pair each seed NOTHING and name the reason on the Sample
data panel** — OQ-004's closure is *"no silent conversion"*, and a plausible
`0.748052` typed into the fixture to make ccf → kgal come out would ride into
every demo bill looking like somebody had chosen it.

### What was NOT built, stated as loudly as what was

**The demo still bills no demand charge — OQ-440.** DEF-797's prevention asks for
a seeded demand read. There is no figure to seed it with: no signed peak for this
estate (GT-20's 14.2 kW and GT-21's 182 kW are ❄️ FROZEN *rating* fixtures for
accounts it does not have), no signed load factor to derive kW from the seeded
kWh, and a service-shaped estate that must be told which tenants get a demand
register at all. The CODE path is proved instead, by a test that walks a real
read through `billing_reads_for_unit` to 412 kW.

### The id collision, recorded because the next lane will hit it (DEF-850)

**OQ-391's own closure text said `→ BR-MET-138`, and BR-MET-138 is the shipped
premises-area filter.** A lane following its closure pointer would have written
this rule on top of a live one. This lane then minted **BR-MET-140** and found,
while remediating DEF-851, that a **sibling lane had already claimed BR-MET-140
uncommitted** for OQ-392's read-method closure. So the rule is **BR-MET-143**.
Lanes are handed reserved DEF and OQ ranges precisely because those collide;
business-rule ids have no such reservation, and a sibling's uncommitted row in a
shared file is invisible to the next lane **by construction**.

### ❄️ Nothing frozen moved

`10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py`: **33 PASS, 0 FAIL**, 8/8 self-test guards bite.
`pytest -m golden`: 23 passed. GT-20/GT-21 price a demand quantity handed to them
by a frozen dataset, so they neither moved nor could have — which is DEF-797's
escape reason, and why a test now walks the seam instead.

## 2026-08-27 · DEF-894 — a quantity displays at two decimals, trimmed. And what to do about the reason codes.

### The display rule, ruled

**PO, verbatim:** *"2 decimals max, trailing zeros trimmed - this is correct"*,
answering the case put to them with its figures: the live app printed
`1008.000000`, `1016.000000` and `8.000000 kgal` on the reads list and
`1016.000000 · 8.000000 kgal` on all 41 stops of a printed route sheet, while
`05-prototype/r10` — the ratified reference — draws `684 kWh`, `3.72 kgal` and
`26.24 kgal`.

Written as **BR-MET-144**, built as `apps/metering/quantity_display.py`, and
pinned by 17 cases. **The half worth naming is the TRIM**, because a fix that
reached two decimals and stopped would pass a careless reading and still be
wrong: `$8.00` is right and `8.00 kgal` is noise. A currency's precision is a
property of the currency; a quantity's is what the meter measured.

**Why it took a customer to find it:** hard rule 2 fixes display at 2dp for
money and percentages and is **silent on consumption**, so there was no figure
for any gate to check against, and `readsShared.tsx` had written that down
rather than guessing. It was right to. The answer was on screen in r10 the
whole time, and nothing in this repo reads rendered output (hard-won law 6).

### The reason codes — the PO asked *"what to do in this case?"*, so this is a DELEGATED CHOICE and it is recorded as the build's, not theirs

**The position, measured.** `reason_codes.default_gl_account_id` shipped as
configuration under CR-008 ruling 9. Three facts about it today:

1. **Nothing in the backend reads it.** No posting path consults it — grepped
   across `apps/`, and the only non-test references are the settings CRUD that
   writes it and the screen that shows it.
2. **The right account is not a property of the reason.** A billing-error
   credit reverses the revenue it originally credited, which is the
   **service's** account — 4110 Water, 4100 Electric — a fact about *the bill
   being corrected*, not about *the word a clerk picked from a list*.
3. **There is no account it could point at anyway.** The signed chart's revenue
   rows are per-service plus 4190 *Minimum-bill adjustment* (a specific
   designation), 4200 *Late-fee* and 4210 *NSF & other fee*. **There is no
   general adjustments account**, so seeding one would mean adding a row to
   ❄️ FROZEN B5 line 74 — a finance re-sign, for a column nothing reads.

**THE CHOICE MADE, AND THE REASONING SO IT IS NOT RE-ARGUED: leave it NULL, and
stop treating that as a gap.** CR-040 task **A1 is closed as NOT TO BE SEEDED**.

**What is built instead, because "leave it blank" must not read as an
oversight:** the settings screen says WHY the column is empty rather than
showing an empty cell — *no adjustment posts through a reason code yet* — which
is the same honest-absence posture the read-validation page already uses for a
service with no figures. An empty cell invites someone to fill it in; a
sentence tells them there is nothing to fill in yet.

⚠ **AND THE REAL DEFECT UNDERNEATH IS FILED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER.** A
column shipped as configuration, rendered on a settings screen, with **no
reader anywhere** is hard-won law 2 — built is not wired — in its data form. It
should either gain the posting path that gives it meaning, or say on the screen
that it has none. Until then, seeding it would set a value nothing uses and
make the screen look configured when it is not, which is strictly worse than
blank.

**A2 and A3 are unaffected and proceed** on the PO's own ruling of this
morning: every tender points at Undeposited funds.
