## 2026-08-27 · CR-039 wave F — all three questions answered, and the gate is finally gone

The wave that stood still because a decision lived in a chat window. The model
was given on 2026-08-26; these are the three things that sentence did not
settle, now settled.

### 1 · The 6/9/12 is an IMPLEMENTATION DURATION, not a contract term

**PO, verbatim:** *"it is duration of implmentation project"*.

**This reverses how wave F task 24 was written.** The task said *"Term on the
subscription — self-serve or 6 / 9 / 12 months, with what happens at the end"*,
which put the number on the **subscription** and implied a renewal, a
commitment discount and an end-of-term behaviour. It belongs on the
**implementation order** instead: how long the project takes, not how long the
customer is tied in.

**What that removes from the build, and it is most of it:** no term column on
`subscriptions`, no renewal behaviour, no commitment discount, no
end-of-term event. **What it leaves:** an implementation order with a duration.

⚠ **AND IT LEAVES A QUESTION NOBODY HAS ASKED YET, RAISED RATHER THAN
ASSUMED** — if 6/9/12 is not a contract term, then **nothing in the product
states how long a subscription runs for.** The plans are month-to-month by
omission. That may be exactly right for a self-serve SaaS; it is not something
this ruling decided, so it is not written as decided.

### 2 · `self serve` is an implementation of ZERO months — a row, not an absence

**PO, verbatim:** *"when utility will do cofiguration, data migrton by themself
then it is self serve and we dont have to implment it - how you want to handle
it, youc anhave 0 month implmentaiton"*.

⚠ **THE MODELLING WAS DELEGATED AND THE BUILD MADE IT — recorded as the
build's choice, not the PO's** (sign-off rule 2026-08-11: a signature covers
only what was shown, and what was shown is the permission).

**Chosen: a row with `duration_months = 0`.** The alternative — no
implementation order at all — was rejected for the reason the question was
raised with: **a row and no row are different things to a report.** With a
zero-month row, *"how many customers are self-serve?"* is one query and the
answer is a fact. With no row, self-serve is **indistinguishable from
implementation-not-yet-decided**, and a sales report cannot tell a customer who
needs nothing from a customer nobody has scoped.

**Its price defaults to 0.00** — self-serve is the case where the utility does
the configuration and migration themselves, so there is no engagement to
charge for. ⚠ **Stated, not signed:** the PO gave the SHAPE, not this figure,
so a non-zero self-serve price is a change and not a correction.

### 3 · An add-on defaults to $1.00 until it is priced

**PO, verbatim:** *"we will add price latet currently you default it to $1"*.

**This closes the objection that stopped it**, and it closes it the only way it
could be closed: the figure now comes from the PO rather than from a builder.
*"An add-on with an invented price is invented money"* was the reason nothing
was built; **$1.00 is not invented, it is stated.**

⚠ **BUT IT IS A PLACEHOLDER AND THE PRODUCT MUST SAY SO.** A $1.00 that reaches
an invoice looking like a considered price is worse than no add-on at all. So
the default is carried as a default a tenant overrides, the screen marks an
add-on still at $1.00 as **not yet priced**, and the figure is recorded here as
awaiting its real one rather than as ratified.

⚠ **AND NO ADD-ON IS NAMED YET.** The question asked for a name and a price and
got the price. So the build ships the **table and the default**, and seeds **no
add-on row**: naming one would invent the product, which is the same class of
error as inventing its price. The catalogue is empty and says why — the
honest-absence posture this product already uses everywhere else.

## 2026-08-27 · CR-039 wave C — an owner is a TYPED record with a category, and no free text

**PO, verbatim:** *"category is okay, no richer text"*, answering: is an owner a
typed party record — owner-occupier · landlord · property manager · HOA ·
builder, with contact details, linked to the customer they already are — or
richer free text?

**Ruled: the typed record.** So `premises.owner_manager`, which is one free-text
box holding a name, becomes a real party with:

* a **category** from the five put to the PO and ratified by this answer;
* **contact details**, so there is a way to reach whoever is named when a unit
  is vacant or a bill bounces;
* a **link to the customer they already are**, so the same landlord across
  twelve addresses is one party rather than twelve unrelated strings.

**And *"no richer text"* is the other half of the ruling, not a throwaway.** The
option it rejects was *keep the free-text box and make it longer* — which would
have been cheaper today and would have left the product routing money at
somebody it still could not identify.

### Why this was worth blocking a wave for

Three of the five seeded occupancy states name an **owner as the party who
pays** — *owner-billed*, *landlord-billed between tenants*, and the owner side
of *tenant-billed*. So the product already decides who to bill by looking at a
box that holds a typed name. A typed record is what makes that decision
resolvable.

### What this ruling does NOT settle, stated so it is not assumed

* **Whether the five categories are the complete list**, or a tenant may add
  its own. Every other reference vocabulary in this product is tenant-extensible
  (BR-TEN-036) and nothing was put to the PO about this one, so the build
  follows the house pattern and the row says so.
* **What happens to the twelve existing free-text names on migration.** They
  are real data on a live tenant. A flagged migration that offers each name for
  matching is the shape; silently guessing which string is which party is not.
* **Whether an owner must be a customer.** The ruling says *linked to the
  customer they already are* — which presumes they are one. A builder holding a
  site before handover may not be, so the link is optional and its absence is a
  stated fact rather than a gap.

**Unblocks CR-039 wave C tasks 12, 13 and 14.**

## 2026-08-27 · CR-039 wave D — a move-in and a move-out ARE records, kept for audit

**PO, verbatim:** *"you cna keep them as records for audit perpuses"*, answering:
what are a move-in and a move-out, as records? Today neither leaves one — the
wizard writes occupancy and account state and nothing else.

**Ruled: each is a record, and its purpose is the AUDIT TRAIL.** That is the
answer to *what is it*, and the purpose named is what decides the shape:

* It records **the job**, not its effects. The occupancy change and the account
  state are already written and are not moved here — a record that duplicated
  them would be a second copy of a fact that already has an owner, which is how
  two numbers come to disagree.
* It carries **who, when, and what was decided** — the clerk, the moment, the
  effective date, the reads taken, the deposit election. *"For audit purposes"*
  is a requirement about **provenance**, and provenance is exactly the set of
  facts a wizard currently holds and then discards.
* It is **append-only in spirit**: a move-out that happened is a thing that
  happened. Correcting one is a new row, the same posture as every other
  financial record (CLAUDE.md hard rule 4).

### What this unblocks, and the one thing it does NOT

**Unblocks D17** — *decide what a move-in and a move-out ARE* — which was the
question, and **D19**, seeding one or two of each so the shape is visible.

⚠ **IT DOES NOT SETTLE D18's NUMBERING, and that is not a quibble.** The task
reads *"build that record and number it"*; the ruling says **record**, and a
signature covers only what was shown (PO 2026-08-11). Whether a move-in carries
a customer-facing number is **the same open question as OQ-427**, the
disconnect — and it turns on the same reasoning the PO gave for the transfer:

> *"it is one job spanning two accounts, and neither account number names it"*

**A move-in belongs to ONE account, whose number already names it** — exactly
the property that made the transfer ruling not carry to the disconnect. So the
honest position is that **move-in, move-out and disconnect are one question,
not three**, and it is open.

**So the build takes the record and stops at the number**: the row exists,
carries its provenance, and is reachable by id. A number is one catalogue row
away the day it is ruled, exactly as the transfer's was.

## 2026-08-27 · OQ-427 — a disconnect gets its own series. And that dissolves the argument blocking move-in and move-out.

**PO, verbatim:** *"it needs its own series"*.

**Closes OQ-427**, which had been left explicitly open by the transfer ruling
earlier the same day and had **no recommendation offered**, because whether a
collections case is its own document or the work order that executes it is a
product judgment.

### The format — DELEGATED, and the build chose `DSC-{YY}-{0000}`

The ruling says *its own series* and rules out the work order. It does not pick
a prefix, so this is the build's choice and is recorded as such: day one is
**`DSC-26-0001`**.

* **`DSC-` over `DC-`** because a customer holds this number on a notice about
  their water being cut off, and `DSC` reads as *disconnect* while `DC` reads as
  nothing.
* ⚠ **`DSP-` IS THE DISPATCH BATCH AND IT IS ONE CHARACTER AWAY** in a list an
  admin reads down. That was raised in the question and is not solved by the
  choice — it is accepted, and named here so the next person to see them
  adjacent knows it was seen.

### ⚠ WHAT THIS ALSO DOES, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE DISCONNECT

The reason a move-in and a move-out had **no** number was recorded an hour ago,
and it was this: the PO's transfer ruling turned on *"it is one job spanning two
accounts, and neither account number names it"*, and **a move-in belongs to one
account whose number already names it**. That argument said one-account jobs do
not need their own number.

**A disconnect belongs to one account too — and it now has its own series.** So
that argument is gone. It cannot be true that a one-account job needs no number
of its own and that a disconnect, a one-account job, needs one.

**So the build gives a move-in and a move-out their own series on the same
logic** — and flags that as an EXTENSION of a ruling rather than the ruling
itself. **One word reverses it.** The reason for extending rather than asking a
fourth time: leaving them unnumbered would now rest on an argument the PO has
just overturned, and building on a reason known to be dead is worse than
building on a stated one.

**With that, CR-039 wave D has no blocker left:** 15 (transfer) is whole, 16 is
this, and 17–19 are the audit records the PO ruled minutes ago plus their
numbers.

## 2026-08-27 · CR-039 wave E tasks 20–21 — the size-class bands are ratified, and the list is a UTILITY SERVICE size class

**PO, verbatim:**

> *"Water (has 4) Pipe diameter keep the four; add 1½" · 3" · 4" · 6" - you need
> 1 inch 2 inch also 5 inch also; rest all are correct in this - Question 1 —
> the bands; Question 2 — is it a meter size class, or a service size class? it
> is utility service size class"*

### Task 21 — the list is renamed, in the PO's own words

**`meter_size_classes` becomes the UTILITY SERVICE size class.** Option (a) was
recommended and ruled, in the product's own vocabulary — *utility service* is
what CLAUDE.md calls the ten.

**Why it mattered:** four of the five services being added — storm water,
broadband, solar, battery — **have no meter**. Storm water is sized by the
property, broadband by the tier bought, solar by inverter capacity, battery by
its rating. A list called *meter* size classes could not hold them without
lying about what it was sizing.

⚠ **THIS IS A RENAME WITH A LONG TAIL, and the repo has a worked example of
exactly this shape from today.** The read-method vocabulary went 5 → 8 and
needed **eighteen files, not the five its task named** — the seed, the fixture
mirror, the sweep digest, the importer alias table, nine docstrings asserting
the old count, eleven i18n catalogues, four tests, and a rule text. Two of the
eighteen were found only by RUNNING THE SUITE, because grep cannot find a count
written in prose. The lane doing this must search four ways: the code literal,
the COUNT in prose, the list written out in both separator styles, and the
fixture version/digest chain.

### Task 20 — the bands, ratified with one correction

**"rest all are correct in this"** ratifies the table put to the PO. The one
correction is water, and it is an ADDITION to what was proposed:

**Water — nine classes.** `5/8" · 3/4" · 1" · 1½" · 2" · 3" · 4" · 5" · 6"`.
The 1" and 2" the PO names were already seeded and are kept; **5" is new and
was not in the proposal** — it is the PO's own addition and is the one figure
here that came from them rather than from the industry convention table.

The other eight, ratified as put:

| Service | Classes |
|---|---|
| **Electric** | 1φ 100A · 1φ 200A · 1φ 400A · 3φ 200A · 3φ 400A · **CT-metered** |
| **Gas** | 250 · 425 · 630 · 1,000+ CFH |
| **Trash** | 35-gal · 64-gal · 96-gal carts · 2 · 4 · 6 · 8 cu-yd dumpsters |
| **Storm water** | 1 ERU · 2–5 · 6–20 · 20+ |
| **Solar** | ≤5 · 5–10 · 10–25 · 25+ kW DC |
| **Broadband** | 100 · 500 · 1,000 Mbps |
| **Sewer** | **NONE by default** — mirrored from water only where a real sewer meter exists |

⚠⚠ **TWO OF THE TEN WERE PUT TO THE PO AS A DIMENSION WITH NO BANDS, AND
"rest all are correct" RATIFIES THE DIMENSION, NOT BANDS THAT WERE NEVER
SHOWN.** A signature covers only what was shown (PO 2026-08-11), so these two
are **NOT closed** and must not be seeded with invented numbers:

* **Thermal / Heat** — chilled water was banded (**≤25 · 25–100 · 100+ tons**)
  and **steam was not**: the proposal said only *"steam by thousand pounds per
  hour"*, which names the unit and no boundaries.
* **Battery** — the proposal said *"by kW and kWh together — a 5 kW / 13 kWh
  home unit prices differently from a 100 kW / 400 kWh commercial one; the pair
  is the class"*. That is a **shape**, not a set of classes. Nobody has said
  where one band ends.

**So the build seeds the eight that carry numbers, seeds thermal's chilled-water
bands, and STUBS steam and battery** with the question minted against them
rather than choosing a boundary. A band boundary decides which base charge a
customer pays; inventing one is inventing money.

### Why this was worth blocking a wave for

A base charge is resolved by **service → account type → size class**
(`apps/rating/resolution.py` keys per-size tier prices on it), so a service with
no size class **cannot have a base charge that varies by size** — the lookup
finds nothing. Water base is $8.00 residential and $15.00 commercial; without
this list, a 25 kW commercial solar array and a 5 kW rooftop pay the same.
## 2026-08-27 · CR-040 wave B (B4–B7) — the estate grew by ZERO units, and the measurement is why

**Lane judgment, made where the rules ran out, recorded with its worked numbers
BEFORE it was reported to anyone (r11's write-back timing rule).**

### What the lane was told to build

CR-040 task **B4**: *"Opening balances on **several accounts**, not one"*, sized
from step 3's measurement — *"⚠ **ONE account of 48.** `A-12103` … The other 47
start at zero"* — and from B4's own note: *"the estate must GROW — a small
migrated cohort in the `SCW-U-2xx` band, four or so units"*. Tasks **B5** and
**B6** then ask for sub-accounts on the master account and a consolidated bill.

### What a full plant actually holds, measured 2026-08-27

`rating` → `metering` → `customers`, each through its own seam, counted off the
planted rows:

| | Packet says | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| accounts with an opening position | **1** | **14** |
| units | **62**, *"every seat taken"* | **118** |
| premises | 44 + estate | **70** |
| accounts | 48 + estate | **73** |
| accounts on the master's premises | **0 children** | **5** (`A-11720` + Ridge Coffee's four) |

The fourteen: **247.30 · 318.60 · 542.10 · 8,240.00 · 30.50 · 412.75 · 96.20 ·
148.90 · 64.80 · 1,204.50 · 2,410.00 · 948.20 · 402.15** and ❄️ GT-16's
**267.30**. Thirteen were planted through the same door B4 names —
`services.create_from_import` — and posted through the ledger on
`CR030_OPENING_BATCH_KEY`. Filed as **DEF-940** and **DEF-941**.

### The judgment

**Growing the estate would have added a fifteenth opening position to a fixture
that has fourteen, and would not have done what the Product Owner asked for.**
Their sentence was *"before you run billing process - you need opening balances
for accounts"*, and the measurement locates the real gap one step further in:

> **Every one of the fourteen sits on a seat that joins no route and no cycle.**
> `service_points.cycle_id` is NULL on all of them, so **no bill run in this
> product's history has met an account with a migrated past.**

That is true by design, twice over: the CR-030 estate is planted after
`_ensure_cycle_and_route` (*"THE ESTATE JOINS NO ROUTE, AND THAT IS
LOAD-BEARING"*) and ❄️ GT-16's `SCW-U-101` deliberately carries no service point.
**Growing the `SCW-U-2xx` band grows the band that joins no route**, so the
prescribed build cannot reach the stated need.

**So the estate grew by ZERO units, and the count is the finding rather than a
shortfall.** Changing it is a product decision with a signed shape on the other
side of it — the ready-to-run batch's **48 rows** (CR-010 Part-10.4, which wave C
is already re-shaping) — and there is no door that gives an EXISTING account an
opening balance. Raised as **OQ-530** with all three answers offered, including
*leave it*: a migrated receivable is a balance the customer owes, not a charge a
run produces, and a bill run that never meets one is not obviously wrong.

### The second wall, and why nothing was seeded against it

**B5/B6 have nothing to attach a sub-account WITH.** `accounts` carries no parent
column; `BR-CUS-068` scopes a master's coverage to **common-area units** and
refuses every ordinary unit by name; `master_billing_account_for_unit` is
deliberately unpublished. Yet `BR-CUS-097`, `OQ-366` and the frontend's
`open_sub_accounts` all presuppose the link. Raised as **OQ-531**, and **nothing
was seeded against any of its three readings** — a fixture that made one true
would answer it by existing, which is the argument
`apps/customers/sample_data.py` already makes for OQ-366 and which CR-040
restates in its own words: *"the unruled part is the arrears, not the
structure"*.

**No business rule was minted.** `BR-CUS-160…169` and `BR-MET-170…179` were
reserved for this lane under DEF-892 and **all twenty were released unused**:
both open halves are product judgments the PO has not made, and writing either
as a `BR-` row would be the lane deciding it — *"AI implements signed law, never
invents it"*.

### What landed instead

`06-backend/tests/test_cr040_b7_estate_money_shape.py` — B7's guards, non-vacuous
in DEF-828's shape (every set asserted non-empty before anything is asserted about
it), and **two of them assert a GAP by name rather than a guarantee**, so the day
the state changes the test goes RED and names the question: `OQ-530` when an
opening-balance account joins a cycle, `DEF-942` when the developer connection
finally gets a payer.

### The one figure a reader should carry away

**14, not 1.** A register sentence whose COUNT was right (*48*) and whose CLAIM
was wrong (*the seed*) sized a wave. It is the fourth recorded instance of that
class in this repo, and r11 step 0 is the only thing that catches it: *"nothing
automated reads prose for truth."*

## 2026-08-27 · OQ-530 CLOSED — the first bill carries the opening balance as its PREVIOUS BALANCE 🔒

**PO, verbatim:**

> *"so when we run first bill; we have to take opening balance into account. you
> will generate first bill and against previous balance you will mention the
> opening balance."*

⚠ **THIS IS A BIGGER RULING THAN THE QUESTION ASKED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE
POINT.** OQ-530 asked whether the FIXTURE should seat a migrated account inside
a route. The PO answered about the **PRODUCT**: a migrated opening balance is
what the customer's first bill shows on its *previous balance* line. That makes
the fixture question fall out — of course the demo must show it — and it makes
the real deliverable a **money rule on the bill document**.

### What the bill does today, measured before writing this

`apps/billing/issue._stamp_balance_forward` already writes the block, and
BR-BIL-035 signs its arithmetic:

> *previous balance − payments received + this period = total due*

**But `previous_balance` reads OPEN INVOICES ONLY** — the seam's own words:
*"Σ of the account's still-open earlier bills at the totals they were ISSUED
with"*, over payments' published set of `issued` and `paid` bills.

**A migrated opening balance is not an invoice.** It lives in
`account_opening_buckets` with its cached `accounts.balance` and its balanced
opening journal entry. **So it is invisible to that line.** A customer who
arrives owing **$8,240.00** gets a first bill whose previous balance reads
`—`, and the product tells them they are square.

### The worked case, on the account the frozen example already names

❄️ GT-16's migrated account `A-12103` carries **267.30** across four aged
buckets. Under this ruling its first bill reads:

> **267.30** − 0.00 + *this period's charges* = **total due**

*(The charge figure is the run's own and is not stated here; the operand that
changes is the first one.)*

### ⚠ WHAT DOES NOT MOVE — checked, not assumed

* **❄️ WE-1's frozen `45.00 − 0.00 + 247.87 = 292.87` is untouched.** That is an
  account with an earlier BILL and no opening buckets; adding migrated openings
  to the first operand changes nothing for an account that has none.
* **❄️ GT-16 itself is untouched.** Read in the golden harness
  (`10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` lines 651–670): it asserts the four buckets,
  their sum, the balanced opening pair and forward ageing — **and never a
  bill.** No frozen figure defines what a migrated account's first bill shows,
  which is why this ruling ADDS behaviour rather than moving a signed one.
* **No finance re-sign is needed.** Verified by reading both, rather than by
  reasoning about them.

### ⚠ AND IT LANDS IN OQ-217's UNRULED TERRITORY, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS BUILDABLE

`prior_position_for_account`'s own docstring says BR-BIL-035 *"signs the
ARITHMETIC and names neither operand's window"*, and calls the window **the
unruled half — OQ-217**. The PO has now ruled one member of that window in: a
migrated opening position belongs in `previous_balance`.

**OQ-217 is NOT closed by this.** It also asks whether a prior bill settled in
full leaves the set — the reason a customer who paid sees `0.00 − 0.00` rather
than `100.00 − 100.00`. That half was not put to the PO and stays open.

### What the build must hold

1. **The opening position joins `previous_balance`, and it is asked for BY
   NAME across the module boundary** — billing owns no opening bucket and must
   compute none, exactly as it asks payments for the allocated half today (B1).
2. **The footing guarantee survives.** The block must still add up; a fourth
   source in the first operand must not break *previous − payments + current =
   total due*.
3. **An unreachable seam stamps NULLS, never zeros** — the existing posture, and
   it matters more here: `0.00` would tell a customer in arrears they are square
   on a page that is immutable the moment it is written.
4. **It is counted once.** An opening balance that has since been invoiced, or
   partly paid, must not appear in both operands — that is the one way this
   change can produce a wrong number, and it is what the guard must prove.
5. 🔒 Money path: `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` and a review-ledger row stating the
   figure in plain English.

## 2026-08-27 · OQ-531 CLOSED — a master's children are the premises', and its BILL is the units nobody else pays for 🔒

**PO, verbatim:**

> *"so you are right if premise P has owner A and units U1 to U10; out of U1 to
> U5 - has accounts - regular accounts - all these accounts are child of Owner
> A; common areas on premise P, also attached to owner A. when bill is generated
> for A - we should consider common areas and U6 to U10 base charges ; U1 to U5
> bill be send to Accounts assocaited with U1 to U5; if U1 leave and dont pay
> $500 then $500 Debt is shifted to Owner A, if clark tied back to A during move
> out process"*

**Option (A) — BY PREMISES — is confirmed.** But the ruling is much more than
the link: it settles **what a master's bill CONTAINS**, which is CR-040 task B6
and was going to be the next question. Five parts, and they are separable.

### 1 · The link is the premises. A master's children are the accounts on it.

An occupying account on premises P is a child of P's owner account. No new
column, no clerk action, no agreement flag — **it is true of the seeded estate
today**, which is why `500 Main Street`'s five accounts are already children and
the *"no children"* in CR-040 was a reporting gap, not a data gap.

### 2 · Common areas attach to the owner — CONFIRMED, already built

That is `BR-CUS-068` exactly, unchanged.

### 3 · ⚠ THE MASTER'S BILL IS COMMON AREAS **PLUS THE BASE CHARGES OF UNITS WITH NO ACCOUNT** — and this WIDENS a signed rule

`BR-CUS-068` today scopes a master's coverage to **COMMON-AREA UNITS ONLY** and
refuses every ordinary unit *by name*. The PO's `U6 to U10` are ordinary units —
vacant, with no account — and their **base charges** now belong on the owner's
bill.

**The product already has the vocabulary for this and it was never joined up:**
`Vacant · base charges only` is one of the five seeded occupancy statuses,
`base_charges_only` is a real basis in `apps/customers/services.py`, and
`BR-CUS-055` already tells the bill run to charge base and no usage for it. What
has been missing is **who receives that charge.** The PO has now said: the owner.

**So BR-CUS-068 is AMENDED, not replaced**, and the amendment is one sentence: a
master covers its premises' common areas **and any unit on that premises that
has no occupying account**.

### 4 · An occupied unit bills its OWN account — the master is not a consolidator

*"U1 to U5 bill be send to Accounts assocaited with U1 to U5"*. This is the half
that stops the obvious wrong build: a master account is **not** an invoice that
sweeps up its children's charges. Each occupied unit's customer gets their own
bill. **The master pays for what nobody else is paying for** — the common parts
and the empty units. That is what a landlord actually owes.

### 5 · ⚠ THE $500 DEBT TRANSFER IS CLERK-INITIATED, AND THAT QUALIFIES A SIGNED RULE

*"if U1 leave and dont pay $500 then $500 Debt is shifted to Owner A, **if clark
tied back to A during move out process**"*.

`BR-CUS-097` says a sub-account's unpayable residue moves to *"the master
account the sub-account hangs off"* and reads as automatic. **It is not.** The
transfer happens **only when a clerk ties it back during move-out** — a
deliberate act, in a wizard, on a specific account, with a person behind it.

**Why that matters more than it looks:** an automatic transfer would move a
departing tenant's debt onto a landlord who never agreed to it, silently, on
every move-out in the product. The clerk's action is the consent.

⚠ **THIS DOES NOT CLOSE `OQ-366`, AND I AM NOT TREATING IT AS IF IT DID.**
OQ-366 asks who the **dunning ladder** chases once the residue has moved. This
ruling says the $500 lands on A; it does not say whether the reminders then go
to A, or continue to the departed tenant, or both. That was not put to the PO
and stays open.

### What the build must hold

1. The parent link is DERIVED from the premises, not stored — a stored copy of a
   fact the premises already carries is a second place for it to be wrong.
2. A master's bill gathers common areas **and** base-charges-only units, and
   **an occupied unit is excluded by the presence of its own account**, not by a
   flag somebody has to maintain.
3. **The $500 is a clerk's act**, so it needs a control in the move-out wizard
   and an audit row naming who tied it back. It must NOT fire on its own.
4. 🔒 Money path: `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` and a review-ledger row with the figure
   in plain English.
5. **Nothing is seeded against OQ-366's half** — a fixture with a residue already
   chased would answer it by existing.

## 2026-08-27 · The cutover carries the PAYMENTS too — so the double-count cannot happen, and its mirror can

**PO, verbatim, correcting the risk I had flagged as the most important one:**

> *"This will not happen; during cut over period, we will migrate opening
> balances as well as payment recieved record to our system and next bill run
> will account it ; after first accounting - everything is in our system and it
> will not create a problem"*

**They are right, and the correction is worth writing down because it changes
what the build must prove.**

### Why the double-count cannot arise

An opening balance is **never also invoiced**. At cutover the opening position
**and the payment-received records** both migrate, so the opening balance is
already the **NET** position as at that date. It is **carried, not billed**, and
after the first run it is inside the ordinary invoice/allocation flow. There is
no path by which the same money is both an opening bucket and an invoice line.

The guard I asked for — *prove an opening balance already invoiced cannot appear
in both operands* — is a guard against a state the migration does not produce.

### ⚠ AND THE MIRROR IS REAL — measured, not reasoned

`apps/billing/payments_seam.prior_position_for_account` derives **both** middle
operands by iterating **the same set**, `position.invoices`:

| Line | Source |
|---|---|
| `previous_balance` = `gross` | Σ open **invoice** totals |
| `payments_credits` = `allocated` | Σ allocated **against those invoices** |
| `total_due` ← `open_balance` | the same **invoice** set |

**All three read open INVOICES only.** So adding the opening position to
`previous_balance` **alone** produces this:

1. the opening balance appears on bill 1 — correct;
2. the customer pays it;
3. that payment allocates against **no invoice in that set**, so
   `payments_credits` does not move;
4. **bill 2 shows the opening balance again. And every bill after it.**

**A customer asked twice for money they have already paid** — worse than the
failure I sent the lane after, and the one the code's shape actually permits.

### So the guard is: THE OPERANDS MOVE TOGETHER

1. The opening position joins `previous_balance`.
2. **And `open_balance`** — otherwise `total_due` never includes it and the
   customer is never actually asked for it. ⚠ `total_due = open_balance +
   current_charges`, so the total is derived from **one** source and is not the
   sum of the two display lines. **That footing guarantee is what stops a
   mismatch in the middle lines becoming a wrong amount due, and it must not be
   broken.**
3. **A payment made against the opening position joins `payments_credits`.**
   What payments does with a payment on an account whose balance is an opening
   position rather than an invoice is a question of fact and must be measured,
   not assumed.

**The test:** seed the migrated account, run the bill, assert the opening figure
is carried; pay it in full through the real payment path; run the NEXT cycle and
assert it has **cleared** — `previous − payments` nets to zero and `total_due` is
this period's charges alone. **Proved RED by leaving the second operand
unchanged**, which is the state of the code today.

### The reusable lesson

I named the most important guard before measuring the two operands, and named
the wrong one. **Both failures live in the same three lines**; which one is
possible depends on a fact about the MIGRATION that only the person running the
cutover knew. The PO knew it. Asking would have been cheaper than inferring.

## 2026-08-27 · OQ-217 — the PO corrected the QUESTION, and it makes option B nearly free

**PO, verbatim:**

> *"at the time of bill payment customer select which bill to pay, billing clark
> will also do the same thing; youa re not going to randomly pay amount"*

**Not a ruling — a correction to how the question was put, and it changes the
costing.** OQ-217 was presented with option B (*previous balance = what the last
statement said was due; payments = everything received since*) carrying the cost
*"the window becomes date-based, which is more code and one more thing that can
be wrong"*. **That cost does not exist**, and two measurements say so.

### 1 · A payment names its bill. It always has.

`BR-PAY-001` gives three allocation modes and `record_payment` passes the
instruction straight through:

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`specific`** | *"The staff member names ONE"* bill — **exactly the PO's sentence** |
| **`split`** | the staff member spreads it across named bills |
| **`carry_credit`** | *"no bill is touched at all"* — the surplus carries |

So money is never applied by a rule nobody chose. **Every allocation names its
invoice**, which means *"which payments count toward the last statement"* is
answerable exactly, with no date window anywhere.

### 2 · "What the last statement said was due" is ALREADY STORED

`issue._stamp_balance_forward` writes the whole block onto the invoice payload —
`payload["balance_forward"]` plus the four names at top level — **at issue, on a
document that is immutable the moment it is written.**

**So option B does not compute a window at all. It reads the previous bill's own
stamped `total_due`.** One field, already there, already immutable, already the
number the customer was actually shown.

### What that does to the recommendation

Option B was recommended for two reasons — a customer who pays on time gets no
acknowledgement anywhere on their bill, and `0.00` beside *previous balance* for
someone who demonstrably owed $100 last month reads as an error. **Its only
stated cost has now been measured away.**

⚠ **STILL NOT RULED.** The PO corrected the framing; they did not pick. This is
recorded so the choice is made against the true cost rather than the one I
guessed at — the same failure as the double-count guard three hours earlier, and
the same fix: measure the mechanism before pricing the option.

## 2026-08-27 · OQ-366 CLOSED — the ladder chases the MASTER, because the sub-account is closed by then

**PO, verbatim:**

> *"Sub account is closed when debt is trasnfer hence we now follow with owner
> for debt"*

**Option (B).** And the reasoning is structural, which is stronger than the one
that was put to them.

### Why this settles it cleanly

The question was posed as a balance of two fairness arguments — *(A)* the
departed tenant incurred it, against *(B)* the balance is now the master's and
chasing someone who owes nothing on paper is what a regulator asks about. The
recommendation offered leaned on the clerk's action being the landlord's
consent.

**The PO's answer does not weigh those at all. It observes a FACT about the
sequence:** the sub-account is **closed** at the moment the residue transfers.
There is no open account on the tenant side to chase. The debt lives on the
owner's account, so the owner is who the ladder follows.

**That also disposes of option (C) — "both, differently".** A second ladder
would have to run against a closed account, which is not a thing this product
does.

### The two rules that could not resolve each other now do

* **`BR-CUS-082`** (PO 2026-08-24): a debt surviving closure **is still chased**
  and the ladder **restarts at TIER 1**.
* **`BR-CUS-097`** (PO 2026-08-24): a sub-account's unpayable residue **moves to
  its master**.

Signed the same day, and neither said whose door. **They do now**, and the
worked case they were written against runs end to end: a sub-account closes
owing **$328.70**, deposit and interest cover **$153.50**, **$175.20** survives,
moves to the master, and **Tier 1 fires on the master's account.**

⚠ **AND IT INHERITS THE QUALIFICATION FROM THIS MORNING.** The transfer itself
is **clerk-initiated** — *"if clark tied back to A during move out process"* — so
the ladder follows the master only for a residue a clerk actually tied back.
A residue nobody tied back does not silently become the landlord's problem, and
therefore does not become the landlord's letters either.

### ⚠ ONE FOLLOW-ON, RAISED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**A master may already have a ladder position of its own.** `BR-CUS-082`
restarts at Tier 1 for a debt surviving closure — but if the master is already
at Tier 3 on its own arrears, does an arriving residue **restart** the master's
ladder to Tier 1, **join** its existing position, or run as its **own** sequence
against the same account?

That was not put to the PO and is not decided here. It is a real case on any
building with more than one departing tenant, and the fixture must not answer it
by existing.
## 2026-08-27 · DEF-895..899 — five UI defects the PO found on the live app, and the four judgments the fix had to make

**The PO opened v2.61.1, looked at the reads surface, and reported five things
in five sentences.** All five are fixed. What follows is the part a defect row
cannot hold: the judgments made where no signed rule reached, each with the
figure or the sentence it turned on, so the next agent does not re-derive them.

### The rulings, verbatim, and what each became

| PO said | Became |
|---|---|
| *"you dont have to provide sub text in bracket"* | **BR-MET-160** — a list cell answers its column in as few words as the value allows; provenance is detail for the detail view |
| *"on this screen ui is not correct for search, filter, colume selection, description i ahve given you prototype screen just now"* | one toolbar row, r10 RDS-01's control set |
| *"this can be modal - instead of page"* | `EstimateReadPage` → `EstimateReadModal`; **B14 rule 30 PROPOSED via OQ-540** |
| *"allow route of Cycle - both"* | **BR-MET-162** — a sheet is printed for a route OR a cycle |
| *"on reading detail page - decimal places databse keys"* | **BR-MET-163** (people as people) + **BR-MET-161** (`Unit Unit 1` → `Unit 1`) |

### JUDGMENT 1 — the name is resolved on the SERVER, and it had to be

DEF-899's own prevention says *"an actor id resolves to a display name through
the same seam the audit trail already uses"*, which reads like a frontend
change. **It cannot be one.** `GET /users` is `SystemAdminOnly`
(`apps/identity/api.UsersView`), and the reader who wants to know who uploaded a
batch is a **Billing Clerk** — so a browser-side lookup would answer **403 for
exactly the person the field is for**. The resolve is
`apps.audit.selectors.actor_names(tenant_id, ids)`, one tenant-scoped query,
reached the way B2 §2 permits: through the owning module's published selector,
never its tables (the route `connection_reads` already takes to `entity_trail`).
`uploaded_by` keeps its raw-id shape on the wire and `uploaded_by_name` rides
beside it, so no existing consumer breaks and the evidence is still served.

⚠ **AND THE CODE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THIS FIX DOWN AND NOT DONE IT.**
`selectors.read_batch_dict` carried, in its own comment: *"The screen resolves
people through identity's own endpoint, as it already does for the uploader."*
The screen did no such thing and could not have. **Hard-won law 1, on the exact
line that shipped the defect** — and it is the second time in this batch (see
judgment 3).

### JUDGMENT 2 — the search box says what is TRUE, not what r10 draws

r10 RDS-01's placeholder is `Meter #, address…`. `selectors.read_list` filters
`asset__asset_no__icontains` **and nothing else** — no address, no premise
number. The prototype is the authority where it and the spec disagree, but it is
not authority to make the product promise a field the endpoint ignores, which is
the failure this codebase keeps paying for. So the box reads **"Search meter
#…"** and **DEF-950 carries the gap**. Writing r10's copy would have closed the
defect and hidden the real one.

**The measured alternative, so the cost is visible:** the neighbouring lists
already search wider — `customers.accounts.searchPlaceholder` names five fields
— so the shape exists and the work is a `Q()` widening, not a design question.

### JUDGMENT 3 — B14 rules 30 and 31 are PROPOSED, not minted

Two of the five defects are fixed by a judgment **no B14 rule names**:

* **DEF-897** is not a rule violation at all. B14's twenty-nine rules cover
  tables, buttons, icons, danger tiers and descriptions and say nothing about a
  form's CONTAINER — so a three-field form shipped as a route while its three
  siblings on the same screen were dialogs, and every gate stayed green.
* **DEF-899's** general form — *no primary key is ever the visible value of a
  field* — is fixed for metering by BR-MET-163, **one panel wide**, and the
  remaining sites have a BUILD cost (the reads list's Batch column needs
  `batch_no` served, which `read_dict` does not serve).

B14's own closing section forbids the alternative: *"A rule the product cannot
yet honour gets a defect row naming the rule number — not a quiet exception."*
Rule 21's row records the PO ruling that made it. **A lane minting rule 30 by
itself is that quiet exception with better manners**, so both go to the PO as
**OQ-540** and **OQ-541**, and B14 gains a section whose first line says the
binding count is still twenty-nine.

### JUDGMENT 4 — a cycle sheet is SECTIONED, not merged

BR-MET-162's shape is the one judgment inside DEF-898 that the PO's sentence
does not settle. *"A cycle sheet is the union of its routes' stops in walk
order"* — but **whose** walk order? A walk order belongs to a ROUTE (D11,
`route_premises_orders`, unique per route), and **no ruled ordering exists
across routes**. Merging them would print a sequence nobody walks. So the sheet
is one section per ACTIVE route, routes in `code` order so two prints of the
same cycle are identical, each section in that route's own order. A premises on
two routes appears **once per route**, with that route's meters, because a
reader really does visit it on both walks and de-duplicating would drop a
register from one of them.

**Worked, on the seeded utility:** cycle `08-A` holds routes `R-1 · Downtown`
(1 stop) and `R-2 · Cedar` (1 stop). The sheet prints `2 route(s) · 2 stop(s)`,
R-1's section first, and a route on NO cycle (`R-9 · Industrial`) is absent —
asserted in `tests/test_def_898_899_reads_surface_defects.py`.

### THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE FIVE FIXES

**Three of the five had already been written down in this repo before they
shipped, and one had been FIXED one screen over.**

1. `read_batch_dict`'s comment described the fix for DEF-899 as though it were
   done (judgment 1).
2. **DEF-896's cause is one class, and the identical fix landed on the UNITS
   list on 2026-08-26 with the identical diagnosis in its own comment**:
   `.met-filters` is `display:grid; width:100%`, so inside `.table-toolbar`'s
   flex row it consumes the whole line and everything after it wraps. The
   sibling screen was never swept. Nothing in the repo asks *"where else is this
   class used the same way?"*, and the answer was two files away.
3. `metering.reads.explainer.all` described the read DRAWER — retired by
   BR-MET-131 the day before — above the toolbar on the busiest screen in the
   module, **translated perfectly into eleven languages** (DEF-952).

The generalisation, and it is the same one three ways: **a note, a comment and a
translated sentence are all things this repo can hold indefinitely while being
false, because no gate reads prose for truth.** The two mechanisms that actually
work are already law — hard-won law 6 (diff the running app against the
prototype) and hard-won law 1 (a comment claiming a guarantee is not the
guarantee) — and DEF-951's prevention adds a third that costs one command: **when
you fix a rendering defect, grep the panel for its siblings, and when a component
retires, grep the catalogue for its name.** Fixing DEF-899 that way found two
more sites of the same defect in the same pass, one of which the PO had never
seen.
## 2026-08-27 · CR-039 wave C tasks 12–14 — where the typed owner LIVES, and which categories a demo may state

Four judgments the PO's ruling did not reach, written down before the code that
depends on them (r11 step W). None of them changes a signed figure; each is a
place where the rules ran out and something had to be chosen.

### 1 · The record is METERING's and the vocabulary is TENANCY-HOSTED

`premises_owners` is a metering table (migration `metering 0040`) because
`premises` is metering's and B2 §2 forbids a cross-module write. The five
categories are a tenancy-HOSTED reference list (`tenancy 0022`,
`owner_categories`) with metering named as the content owner — the identical
split `occupancy_statuses`, `meter_size_classes`, `device_types` and
`certification_types` already take under BR-TEN-031, so this adds no pattern.
Recorded as **BR-MET-150** and **BR-TEN-150**.

### 2 · The customer link is a cross-module FK metering → customers, and a B2 row is OWED

The ruling asks for *"a link to the customer they already are"*.
`premises_owners.customer_id` is a nullable FK to `customers.customers`. That
direction already exists in the reviewed set — `apps/metering/models.py` FKs
`customers.Account` twice — so this is a new ROW on an existing boundary rather
than a new boundary. **Review of the row is OWED at the next B2 sitting**, and
it is appended to `04-docs/02-decisions/02-database-design-brief.md` as addendum
r21 in the same form r19 and r20 take.

### 3 · The migration backfills NOTHING, and *unmatched* is computed rather than stored

The ruling's caveat, verbatim: *"A flagged migration that offers each name for
matching is the shape; silently guessing which string is which party is not."*

**Two shapes were available and the cheaper one was rejected.** A `migration
status` column on `premises` (`unmatched` · `matched` · `no owner`) would have
made the review list a trivial filter — and it is a second copy of a fact the
two existing columns already answer, which is how two numbers come to disagree.
So *unmatched* is `owner_manager IS NOT NULL AND owner_id IS NULL`, computed at
read time. A premises that gains free text through the CSV importer tomorrow
appears on the review list the same day, with nothing to maintain and no
backfill to have got wrong. Recorded as **BR-MET-151** clause 2.

### 4 · A seeded owner's CATEGORY — three stated, two refused by name

Task 14 is *"seed several owner kinds"*, and a category is a claim about a
party. The fixture already invents the owner NAMES, so stating their category is
the same act by the same author — but only where the corpus gives a basis.

**Seeded, each from a fact already written down:**

| Owner | Category | The basis, quoted |
|---|---|---|
| *Ridge Property LLC* @ `500 Main St` | `builder` | BR-CUS-083 already calls the payer there *"the developer, via a master account"*, on a 25-unit build |
| *Creekside Laundromat* · *Quarry Hill Diner* | `owner_occupier` | the fixture makes the BUSINESS TRADING AT the address its own `owner_manager`, and each premises holds exactly one commercial suite — owner and occupant are the same party by construction, not by inference about this party |
| *Mill Pond Apartments LP* · *Silver Creek Duplex Holdings* | `landlord` | each owns let residential units (six flats · four duplex halves) and occupies none of them |

**Refused, by name, rather than invented:** `property_manager` asserts a
managing AGENT acting for an owner, and nothing in the corpus names one at any
address. `hoa` asserts an association, and nothing names one either. This is
CR-039 wave E's own posture — *"a seeded value nobody chose is worse than a
blank, because a demo makes it look decided"* — applied to a category instead of
a column. Recorded as **BR-MET-152**.

**And `seed_demo`'s six named owners are deliberately left UNMATCHED**, so the
review surface BR-MET-151 requires has real rows on a fresh demo. Same reasoning
as task 11's sample COMMERCIAL plan stating no factor on purpose: a promise
nobody can see demonstrated is a promise nobody checks.

### What was NOT decided here

`OQ-500` (does the typed owner become the default payer — money, and untouched)
· `OQ-501` (is the free-text column ever retired) · `OQ-502` (are the five
categories closed or extensible — the build follows BR-TEN-036 and says so) ·
`OQ-503` (must the owner who PAYS carry a contact method).

series"*, PO verbatim and in full: *"it needs its own series"*). This row is the

**`DSC-{YY}-{0000}`, so a new tenant's first disconnect case is `DSC-26-0001`.**
Offered alongside it on S8, editable per tenant like every other series
(BR-TEN-035): `DSC-{YYYY}-{0000}` · `DSC-{0000}` · `DISC-{YY}{MM}-{000}` ·
`{000000}` (CR-005's mandatory bare counter, last).

Group **`customers_premises`**, not `work`. `connection` sits in `work` because
a new connect is a FIELD job; a disconnect HAS a field job — r10 draws it,
`WO-4833` — and *"it needs its own series"* is precisely the statement that the
CASE is not that visit. **Filing the case in the work group would blur the one
distinction the ruling drew.** `work_order` is untouched and OQ-249 (is Work a

Named in OQ-427 when it was asked, named again in `core/numbering.py`, and now

duplicate-prefix warning stays silent on a tenant nobody has touched, which is

**One catalogue row, five test pins, one label, and no schema change.** Not one

⚠ **A POST-CLOSURE RESTART DRAWS A NEW NUMBER, NOT THE CLOSED CASE'S.**
BR-TEN-035 never reuses a number and a reopened case is a new document. Stated
here because both call sites are one function and a reader could assume otherwise.

## 2026-08-27 · CR-039 wave D tasks 17–19 — the move record is BUILT, its two series are the BUILD's, and the ruling's own evidence sentence was wrong

**The ruling this implements is the entry above** — *"a move-in and a move-out ARE
records, kept for audit"*, PO verbatim and in full: *"you cna keep them as records
for audit perpuses"*. This row is the BUILD's record: what was made, what was
refused, and the one thing that had to be corrected before anything could be
built on it.

### 1 · WHAT WAS BUILT

`move_records` (customers 0030) — ONE table, two kinds, RLS `FORCE` on. The
columns are the ruling's own list minus one (§3): `kind` · `account` ·
`from_account` · `effective_on` · `performed_by` · `performed_at` ·
`reads_committed` · `move_no`. `services.move_in` and `services.move_out` each
write one **inside the transaction they already open**, so a refused reading
rolls the record back with the account and there is never a record of a move
that did not happen.

**Rules written first, then the code:** `BR-CUS-150` (a record of the JOB) ·
`BR-CUS-151` (provenance, and nothing that already has an owner) · `BR-CUS-152`
(append-only in spirit) · `BR-CUS-153` (its own series per flow). **Only the
first three are the PO's.**

**What it deliberately does NOT store, each with the row that owns it:**
occupancy (DERIVED from the status class, BR-MET-036 — there is no column to
copy) · the account's status and dates (`accounts`, written by the same
transaction) · the readings (`meter_reads`, through the BR-CUS-021 door — this
table keeps a COUNT, which is a fact about the JOB) · any money figure at all.

⚠ **`from_account` IS THE ONE FACT THIS ADDS RATHER THAN RELOCATES.**
`services.move_in` has always put `moved_in_after_account_id` in its RESPONSE and
written it down nowhere, so the chain from the tenancy that ended to the one that
began was lost the moment the response closed. It is now a column.

⛔ **`move_reads.STEP_HAS_NO_STORE` IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS.** It asks for *"a
move-in/move-out case row carrying step + state"* — a record of a job IN FLIGHT —
and this is a record of a COMPLETED one. B18 §5.5.2's own footnote rules the
first out: *"a move-in is short enough that the wizard is the record"*.

### 2 · THE TWO SERIES ARE THE BUILD'S, AS AN EXTENSION — AND ONE WORD REVERSES THEM

**`MVI-{YY}-{0000}` and `MVO-{YY}-{0000}`, so day one is `MVI-26-0001` and
`MVO-26-0001`.** Catalogue **27 → 29**, group `customers_premises`.

The PO ruled the RECORD and not the NUMBER, and the entry above says so in as
many words (*"IT DOES NOT SETTLE D18's NUMBERING, and that is not a quibble"*).
What made the number buildable anyway is that **the argument against it died the
same day**: the transfer's format was ruled with a reason that does not carry to
a one-account job, and then a DISCONNECT — a one-account job — got its own series
on *"it needs its own series"*. It cannot be true both that a one-account job
needs no number of its own and that a disconnect needs one. Leaving these
unnumbered would rest on an argument the PO has just overturned, which is worse
than building on a stated one.

**TWO series, not one shared `MV-`, and that is the build's call.** A clerk
reading `MV-26-0004` back down a phone could not say whether it named an arrival
or a departure, and the two are separate flows on separate tabs with separate
wizards. Two counters is the honest cost of a number that says what it names.
⚠ `MVI-` and `MVO-` differ in their LAST character, which is the same
readability hazard `DSC-`/`DSP-` carries and is named for the same reason:
accepted, not solved.

### 3 · ⚠ THE RULING'S OWN EVIDENCE SENTENCE IS NOT TRUE OF THIS PRODUCT — `DEF-921`

The entry above enumerates what the record carries as *"the clerk, the moment,
the effective date, the reads taken, **the deposit election**"*, and calls that
*"exactly the set of facts a wizard currently holds and then discards"*.

**Measured before building, which is r11 step 0's whole reason for existing:
NEITHER WIZARD HOLDS A DEPOSIT ELECTION.** `MoveInWizard` refuses step 4's three
deposit radios BY NAME, `MoveOutWizard` refuses step 3's disposition and refund
radios the same way, and `services.REFUSED_FIELDS` refuses `deposit_on_file` on
every door that edits an account. The blocker under all three is one thing:
BR-CUS-023 makes the deposit a LOOKUP from a plan deposit schedule that does not
exist, and BR-CUS-024's carry-forward mechanics are PROPOSED, not confirmed.
**There is nothing to discard.**

**The RULING is unaffected and is built.** One item of its supporting enumeration
is wrong, and a lane building literally from it would have shipped
`deposit_carry_elected` as **a column nothing can write** — hard-won law 2 on
data, DEF-837's shape. So the column was refused BY NAME, `DEF-921` records the
mismatch, and the substance goes to the PO as **`OQ-510`** (*should S19/S20 offer
a deposit election at all?*), which is a product judgment about whether a
returning customer at a NEW address keeps their money.

**A signature covers only what was shown (PO 2026-08-11), and what was shown here
was a list, not a column.**

⚠ **The consequence that stays open, stated so it is not read as finished:**
`move_reads.DEPOSIT_CARRY_ELECTION_HAS_NO_COLUMN` — B18 §5.5.1's `DEPOSITS TO
CARRY OVER` tile — still counts nothing, and its own sentence still names *"the
same boolean on the move-in's record"* as the column it wants. That sentence is
now pointing at a table that exists and has deliberately not grown it.

### 4 · THE SURFACE, AND THE ASYMMETRY THAT IS A FACT RATHER THAN A GAP

Both move tabs gain a **leading `reference` column**, drawn through the same
`RecordNumberCell` S89 and S90 use — one cell, four flows, no fourth shape.

* **Move-outs fills.** Every row is a CLOSED account and `move_out` has written a
  numbered record for each closure since today.
* **Move-ins is empty on every row, and that is correct.** §5.5's list is the
  BR-CUS-018 draft window — *"a row LEAVES this list when the move-in
  completes"* — and the record is written AT completion. The cell states *"this
  move-in has not completed"* rather than showing a dash.

⛔ **THREE ABSENCES, THREE CODES, AND NEVER A BARE DASH** (DEF-127's shape, one
list over): `move_predates_the_record` (the job happened before today — not a
settings gap) · `numbering_series_missing` (a tenant with no series row — this
one IS a settings gap) · `move_in_not_completed` (no job has happened yet). The
branch is a NAMED function, `move_reads.move_reference_cell`, so a test can call
it — DEF-182's lesson applied before it bit rather than after.

### 5 · TASK 19 — SEEDED, AND WHAT THE SEEDER REFUSED TO DO

Up to **two of each kind**, on accounts the W5 fixture has already planted, through
`moves.record_move` — the module's own service function, which allocates the number
inside the transaction exactly as the wizards do.

⚠ **IT DOES NOT CALL `services.move_out` ON A SEEDED ACCOUNT.** That would CLOSE a
live account of the demo estate, free its unit, end its agreements and change what
the billing month bills — a fixture reshaping the demo in order to demonstrate a
record. The estate's shape is CR-039 wave A's and `core.sample_fixture.estate_plan`
is not this lane's to move.

⚠ **`reads_committed` IS SEEDED AS `0` AND THAT IS THE TRUE ANSWER.** The column
counts readings the job committed through the BR-CUS-021 door; these jobs committed
none. The fixture states reads as PROSE on the drawn row (*"Reads taken"*) and
prose is not a reading. Seeding a count would state that meter readings exist which
nobody can find — `sample_fixture`'s spec rule 7 applied to a figure.

### 7 · THE FIVE HAND-PINNED PLACES, MOVED AGAIN — AND THEIR REDS, VERBATIM

The two new series went through the same checklist the transfer and the
disconnect did. **Four of the five were proved RED by adding the catalogue rows
and running before touching the pins**; the fifth was proved separately, and
that is stated rather than glossed (see below).

| Place | Move | Its RED, verbatim |
|---|---|---|
| `core.numbering.SERIES_CATALOG` | 27 → 29 | — (the rows themselves) |
| `tests/test_cr005_numbering_set08` size | 27 → 29 | `AssertionError: assert 29 == 27` |
| `test_def615_series_defaults.EXPECTED_PREFIX` | `+ move_in: "MVI-"`, `+ move_out: "MVO-"` | `AssertionError: {'in the catalogue and not pinned here': ['move_in', 'move_out'], 'pinned here and not in the catalogue': []}` |
| `test_cr005_numbering_reaches_records` | wired 18 → 20, unwired **9 → 9** | `AssertionError: assert 11 == 9` |
| `test_cr039_wd_transfer_and_case_numbers` catalogue size | 27 → 29 | `AssertionError: assert 29 == 27` |
| the S8 label ×11 (DEF-880's guard) | `+ settings.numbering.series.move_in` / `…move_out` | proved separately (below): `AssertionError: 2 catalogued number series has no label on S8 and will print its raw key: ['move_in', 'move_out']` |

⚠ **THE LABEL GUARD DID NOT GO RED ON ITS OWN, BECAUSE THE LABELS WERE ADDED
BEFORE THE RUN — SO IT WAS PROVED DELIBERATELY AFTERWARDS.** Hard-won law 7 is
*"prove a new guard goes RED before trusting it green"*, and a guard that
happens to be green because the fix landed first has been trusted, not proved.
The two keys were pulled out of `en.json` in **this lane's own worktree** (r11
§2d: *"mutate in a `git worktree` … never in the shared tree"*), the single
guard case was run, and the keys were put straight back. **UNWIRED DID NOT MOVE,
FOR THE FOURTH TIME TODAY.** `transfer`, `disconnect_case`, `move_in` and
`move_out` each arrived carrying their own caller, so the catalogue grew
25 → 26 → 27 → 29 and the wired set grew with it every single time. That is what
the wave D lane's refusal to invent a prefix bought, repeated four times.

### 8 · ⚠ ONE THING FOUND ON THE WAY, AND IT IS NOT THE PRODUCT — `DEF-922`

This lane's own rollback guard failed three times on
`sqlite3.OperationalError: no such function: set_config`, and the traceback named
`core/tenancy.py`'s GUC statement — so it read as a connection soured by the
rolled-back transaction. **It was not.**

`tests/test_us_ten_helpers.sqlite_guc` is an **autouse** fixture that patches
`core.tenancy.connection` with a recording fake, *"because sqlite has no
`set_config`"*, and it does that through the same function-scoped `monkeypatch`
instance every test in the file shares. **A test calling `monkeypatch.undo()` to
lift its own patch also lifts that one**, and the next `tenant_ctx` talks to real
sqlite.

**`undo()` reads as local and is global to the instance.** Nothing warns: ruff
and black see valid code, no gate reads fixture scope, and the runtime failure
names a different file and a different operation than the line that caused it.
Two fixes were attempted against the wrong diagnosis before the fixture was read.

The suite already contained the right shape — `tests/test_us_bil_surface_apis.py`
takes a private `pytest.MonkeyPatch()` and undoes it in a `finally`, and it is
the only other `undo()` in the suite. **Both now follow it.** The rule, in one
line: *never call `undo()` on the fixture instance in this suite.*

### 6 · NO VERSION BUMP

`2.58.0` is untouched. The version is bumped per wave at MERGE by the integrator
(PO ruling 2026-08-26).

**Rollback (change-process step 8):** revert the commits; `customers 0030`
reverses cleanly — the policy drops, FORCE comes off, the `CreateModel` reverses
to a `DROP TABLE`. ⚠ Unlike `customers 0028`, whose two columns were NULL on every
row, **this table HOLDS data from the first move after it lands**, so a reversal
deletes an audit trail. Nothing else reads it — no bill, no invoice, no ledger row
depends on it — but that sentence is the one to read before running it.
## 2026-08-27 · CR-040 waves A and D — the tender mapping that changes nothing, and the two money cases that had never existed

Three judgments this lane made where the rules ran out, and one it refused to
make. Written before the work was reported, because a reply that explains
something the repo does not say is a context leak (hard-won law 10).

### 1 · A2 — the value is STATED, and stating it is the whole deliverable

The PO's ruling of this morning (OQ-490, option a) is implemented as
**BR-PAY-150**: provisioning writes `payment_methods.clearing_gl_account_id` for
all **seven** seeded tenders — ach · card · check · cash · lockbox · wire ·
money_order — pointing at the account carrying the `undeposited_funds`
designation, immediately after `seed_chart_of_accounts` plants the 33-row chart
and inside the same signup transaction.

**The worked figure, and it is the one that makes the change readable:** on the
seeded tenant, **June's ~95% collection — about $9,700 across 45 payments —
sat in `1010 Undeposited funds` before this change and sits in `1010
Undeposited funds` after it. Not one cent moved account.** NULL was already
lawful and already fell back to exactly that account (BR-PAY-039 / OQ-143), so
the behaviour is byte-identical.

**So what was built?** A value that is STATED rather than ABSENT. DEF-891's own
`escape_reason` is the argument: *"a documented, deliberate, lawful default
cannot be distinguished from a configured value by any test that asks 'did
posting succeed'"*. There was nothing for a gate to assert. Now there is, and
**A3 asserts it in both directions** — the unmapped set EMPTY *and* the mapped
set NON-EMPTY (DEF-466's shape, DEF-828's guard), plus every pointer re-checked
live against this tenant's own chart, because a pointer at a dead account is
worse than a NULL: `tender_clearing_account_id` refuses the whole receipt for it.

⚠ **Two things this lane decided rather than was told, and both are recorded as
the build's:**

**(a) Only a seed row still holding NULL is written.** A tenant who chose an
account on Settings → Accounting → GL mapping keeps it through every repair
run. That is BR-TEN-012's insert-missing posture read one field along, and the
alternative — provisioning overwriting a clerk's decision on a re-run — is not
something any rule permits.

**(b) It rides the `--tenant` repair door too.** Hard-won law 4 in its data
form: every tenant provisioned before today carries seven NULL pointers, and a
change made only at provisioning would never reach one of them.

### 2 · A1 — REFUSED, and the refusal is the point

`reason_codes.default_gl_account_id` is **not** seeded and this lane did not
seed it. The ruling covered *"the answer for every TENDER"* and **a signature
covers only what was shown** (PO 2026-08-11). Filling the column in would have
been resolving an open question by choosing a value.

What was built instead is the half that was owed: **the settings screen now says
WHY the column is blank** — *"Nothing posts here yet"* in the cell, and beneath
the table, *"These are blank on purpose. No adjustment posts through a reason
code yet, and a credit for a billing error reverses the revenue account of the
service on the bill being corrected — which the bill tells us, not the reason."*
It read **"Not mapped"** before, which is correct on the service and tax
sections above it (there it is a to-do) and was misleading here: **an empty cell
invites a clerk to spend an afternoon mapping five reasons onto accounts nothing
will ever read.** The row keeps its Change action — the mapping is still a real
setting a tenant may record ahead of the posting path landing.

`test_a1__reason_codes_stay_unmapped_on_purpose` pins the absence, so the next
lane meets a decision rather than what looks like a gap.

### 3 · D13 — the read is corrected FIRST, and that is a mechanism rather than a courtesy

The correction the PO asked for is a **class-R restatement**, and a restatement
**re-prices the bill from today's inputs** (`corrections.recompute`) — it does
not accept a delta from anybody. Measured on the seeded tenant before anything
was changed: the June bill's stored total and its recomputed total are
**identical**, so a correction case opened over untouched inputs computes a
delta of **exactly $0.00** and corrects nothing.

**So the fixture corrects the READING first**, through
`apps.metering.services.correct_billed_read` — BR-MET-053's only door for a
reading a bill has already priced, which supersedes the row, writes the
`read_corrections` linkage naming the invoice, and touches no invoice at all.
That is BR-MET-053's own sentence — *"read fix and money fix travel together"* —
read as a requirement rather than as a comment.

**Worked, measured on a real seeded tenant:** a water register read **3 kgal too
high** in June. The reading goes from **1,868 to 1,865**, consumption from **17
kgal to 14 kgal**, and the engine re-prices the bill from **$111.18 to $88.23**
— a credit of **$22.95**, issued as a credit note reversing the original in full
plus a rebill for the corrected amount.

⚠ **AND JULY IS THEN BILLED THREE THOUSAND GALLONS HIGHER, WHICH IS CORRECT
ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN A SIDE EFFECT.** July's consumption is the delta FROM the
corrected register, so the customer is credited in June and billed the same
units in July. That is what a real re-read does, and the second cycle running
after this block is what makes it visible on the demo.

### 4 · D12 — the refund amount is the ALLOCATOR's, and it is not case 11's account

**No figure is typed.** The account overpays its June bill by **1.40×** through
the fixture's existing `_share_for`, and `seed_sample_refund` then reads the
resulting credit back off `account_credit_position` and refunds exactly that.
A typed amount would drift the day a tariff moved and would fail as a refusal
deep inside `_credit_or_refuse`.

⚠ **It is a NEW account, not `CASE_CREDIT_BALANCE`.** A refund CONSUMES a
credit; case 11 exists to show one being CARRIED. Seeding the refund onto case
11's account would have paid case 11 out and left the fixture with no carried
credit at all — **one case replacing another rather than a case being added**,
which no count of "how many awkward cases do we have" could see. `CASE_REFUND`
is unit 23 and `CASE_OVERCHARGE` is unit 31; both were ordinary units and
`AWKWARD_UNITS` goes 18 → 20.

⚠ **The offset ruling is honoured, not skipped.** `cross_account_check=True`,
so the PO's ruling of 2026-08-12 (*"offset first"*) is applied by the product to
this fixture like any other refund. Passing False would have made the demo the
one refund in the product that skips the check.

### 5 · D14 — the position is the deliverable, and both orderings write the same rows

Both new blocks sit in `SAMPLE_MODULES` **after the payments block and before
`seed_sample_second_cycle`**. Moving either one outside that gap writes byte-
identical rows and destroys what they demonstrate.

**The ordering is asserted on `created_at`, and the trap is sharper here than it
was for wave C.** The refund and the correction carry **July** business dates
while the payments that fund them are dated on the busy day in **August** — so
on business dates these rows look EARLIER than their own cause. `created_at`
(`auto_now_add`) is the only field that records the block order, because it is
the only one the fixture does not choose. The tuple order is asserted too, and
neither test replaces the other: a tuple can be right while a block writes
nothing (DEF-167's shape), and rows can be in the right order for a reason that
is not the block order.

## 2026-08-27 · DEF-901 / DEF-902 / CR-040 A1 — three things the PO found on the live app, and the one decision I refused to make

Three defects, one shape: **the product knew something and would not say it.**

### 1 · DEF-901 — *"are these settings applicable to sewer"*

**The answer is NO, and the page could not say so.** S64 drew a full
read-validation threshold form for every **ENABLED** service — a high-use
threshold, a days window, a zero-read rule, fourteen inputs and a
`Save Sewer thresholds` button. Sewer is priced as a percentage of the water
usage charge (BR-RAT-015) and **reads no register at all**;
`core/sample_fixture.py` says so in as many words. Trash is a flat per-cart
charge with no meters. So a tenant was invited to tune configuration that can
never fire.

**THE FIX THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG, and it is the obvious one:** a list of
"unmetered services" — `{"sewer", "trash"}` — checked against the service code.
It is right on today's demo tenant and wrong on the first customer who buys a
sewer meter, with nothing objecting.

**BR-TEN-162: THE TEST IS THE TENANT'S OWN ESTATE, NEVER THE SERVICE CODE.**
`apps/assets/selectors.metered_service_codes()` asks the asset register: is
there a MEASURING asset — `meter` · `net_meter` · `sub_meter`, BR-AST-009's own
set, imported rather than re-listed so the two cannot drift — standing on a
service point of this service? A utility that genuinely meters sewer gets
`sewer` back and gets the form. `test_a_sewer_meter_makes_sewer_metered` is
the case the hard-coded version fails.

**Two judgments inside it, both worth stating:**

* **FAIL TOWARD SHOWING.** The probe not answering — still loading, or failed —
  draws every form. Hiding configuration a tenant needs is expensive; showing
  configuration it does not need is noise. This is also why the 26 pre-existing
  S64 cases did not move by one character.
* **THE GRAIN IS "STANDING ON A SERVICE POINT", AND IT IS THE SCHEMA'S CHOICE,
  NOT MINE.** B2 r4 records an asset's service only through the service point
  minted at assignment, and un-assigning releases that seat. So a spare meter in
  inventory carries no service, and a tenant that has pulled its last sewer
  meter reads as not metering sewer — which is **true of the readings it will
  take next cycle**. Pinned by a test rather than left to be discovered.

### 2 · DEF-902 — *"in this setting - unable to see sub areas"*, and the decision I did NOT make

**The measured figures.** `lookup_defaults.json` at `V2.48.0.2` ships **seven**
area rows. Silver Creek Water shows **four**. The three missing are
`NORTH-NE` "NE", `NORTH-NW` "NW" and `EAST-SE` "SE" — **the exact three the PO
ratified that same morning under OQ-432 and then could not see.** The fixture,
the parent wiring, the two-level depth cap and the Add-entry dialog are all
correct and shipped. The tenant was provisioned before the fixture grew.

#### The decision asked for: which reference lists does the sweep re-offer?

**Written as BR-TEN-160, and it states the status quo deliberately: the
STRUCTURAL set, and nothing else.** Every discretionary list — `areas`
included — is deferred by name to OQ-216 on every run and reaches an existing
tenant only through an explicitly requested `manage.py seed_demo --tenant`.

**Clause 1 is the load-bearing half, and it forecloses the one-line fix.**
Adding `areas` to `STRUCTURAL_REFERENCE_LISTS` would make it sweep and would
close DEF-902 today. It is wrong, because **that set has a second, opposite
job**: it is also what a tenant which **DECLINED** the S111 defaults receives at
provisioning (BR-TEN-067). Widening it to solve a *delivery* problem silently
hands sample content to a tenant that asked for none — the exact harm OQ-088's
closure names. The two uses cannot be tuned independently. A test now fails
that fix by name.

#### ⚠ AND THE PART I REFUSED — the lane was asked to decide it and it is not a build judgment

There is an answer that looks right and is not mine to take. **A tenant's own
`reference_seed_runs` row for a list is per-list, positive evidence that this
tenant accepted this list** — it needs no new column and no backfilled default,
and it leaves OQ-088's stated harm untouched, because a tenant that declined
charge codes has no `charge_codes` row and would still get nothing.

**I did not adopt it, for one reason: OQ-088's closure is a CLOSED PO ruling and
its literal direction is** *"Until that column exists the sweep delivers
STRUCTURAL lists only (BR-TEN-067), never discretionary ones."* Delivering
`areas` would obey the ruling's **reason** and contradict its **words**, and
narrowing a closed ruling is a re-sign, not a lane's call — *AI implements
signed law, never invents it*. **It is OQ-550**, with the three options in plain
English and the figure attached: leave it (the screen now says so), sweep a list
the tenant already holds, or an audited opt-in **Update this list** button in
the shape OQ-086's own closure already ratified for corrections.

**OQ-216 names a similar-sounding third option and explicitly asks for it to be
ruled rather than adopted quietly.** Mine is narrower — per LIST, not per
TENANT — which is why it is a separate question and not an answer to that one.

#### What was built instead: BR-TEN-161, the sentence

*"The data is correct and your tenant does not have it"* **is a sentence the
product should say, not one a person should have to be told.** Every reference
list now compares its rows against the fixture and, when rows are missing, says
on its own screen how many, **which ones by name and code**, the fixture version
that carries them, and what will and will not add them.

**By NATURAL KEY, never by count** — a tenant that deleted three seeded rows and
added three of its own has the right count and is not current, and a count-only
check calls that healthy. And **a deleted row reads as missing**: no column
records that a tenant removed a seeded row, so the screen states the fact it can
prove and never asserts the reason.

`sweep_delivers` is **SERVED**, not assumed by the screen, so the day the
structural set moves the copy moves with it.

### 3 · CR-040 A1 — the owed half, and nothing more

`reason_codes.default_gl_account_id` is **NOT TO BE SEEDED** (ruled this
morning) and **nothing here seeds it**. What was owed is that the screen says
**why** it is empty. It now renders *"Not used yet"* rather than borrowing
`settings.accounting.unmapped` — every other GL cell on that tab means *you have
not mapped this yet*, and this one means the opposite: a deliberate decision,
not an unfinished setup. The section note opened *"This records where you want
each reason to post"* — true of the intent, false of the product, and exactly
the impression the blank column was giving; it now says no adjustment posts
through a reason code yet, and why the right account is the **service's**.

### ⚠ One gate finding worth recording, because it nearly shipped as nothing

The first cut wrote that cell's ink as Tailwind utilities to honour B14 rule 21,
and **G31 caught it**: `SettingsAccountingTab.tsx` is not in
`src/styles/route-b-migrated.txt`, so a bare `cursor-not-allowed` there is a
class no stylesheet declares and no compiler was asked to emit — it would have
rendered as **nothing at all**. **Rule 21's migration clause is per FILE.** The
cell reuses `.settings-locked`, adding no class: G31 PASS, 0 undeclared, 509
declared, at the ceiling.
