## 2026-08-27 — CR-042: two write modes, on step 1, on EVERY import — and the ruling that never reached the code

**PO verbatim:**

> *"in all imports - we need 2 option on step 1 insert, insert & update; replace
> option is not required; currently many places this option is at step 4 of
> import- can you check all imports and make the corrections"*

### ⚠ FIRST, THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART: WE WERE ALREADY TOLD THIS

On **2026-08-27**, earlier the same day, this PO ruled: *"we actaully needs Insert
new only · Insert & update; repalce you can remove"*. That ruling was written into
`01-open-questions.md` (OQ-418 → **CLOSED BY REMOVAL**), into this log (item 11,
with BR-MET-127's survival measured), and into `CHANGELOG.md`.

**It reached no line of code.** `replace` was still offered by both rails when the
PO looked at the product again and asked a second time — this time widened to
*every* import. Filed as **DEF-1020**, whose escape reason is the useful part:
**no gate can read a decision-log entry and ask whether the code agrees with it.**
The r11 step-0 packet check is the only thing that catches this, it is explicitly
a human step, and it caught this one — but only because a lane happened to run it
on this topic. Every other closed-by-removal ruling in this file is exposed to the
same failure and nobody has checked them.

### The measurement, and the finding the report did not ask for

**Nine import surfaces exist. Seven are ONE component.** Full table in CR-042.

**Statement 1 of the report — "the option is at step 4 in many places" — is not
true of HEAD and has not been since 2026-08-26.** CR-036 (g) moved it to step 1 on
both rails; DEF-770 removed the duplicate that stayed at step 4. Step 4 now
*states* the premise and offers `Change it`. What the PO is looking at is a
deployed build older than `2.55.0`, or the r10 prototype, which still draws all
three as a segmented control under *Stage 4 of 5 · Load*
(`SMARTBillHub.dc.html:6644`). **Reported rather than silently "fixed", because
"fixing" something already correct is how a lane burns a day and reports success.**

**What IS wrong, and it is the standing complaint in miniature:** the two rails ask
the same question with two different controls. The shared runner drew a three-across
`SegmentedField` labelled **"Write mode"**. The reads rail drew radio cards labelled
**"What does this file mean?"** with a consequence sentence under the choice.
One decision, two shapes, two vocabularies. **That** is what this CR fixes, and it
is fixed by extraction: `components/workflow/WriteModeChoice.tsx` is now the one
control, and both rails mount it.

### ⚖️ THE JUDGMENT CALL — the option goes, the behaviour stays

The PO's sentence is about an **option**: *"replace **option** is not required"*.
It does not say the deactivate-what-is-missing behaviour was wrong, and they ruled
that behaviour into existence six days earlier with a worked figure.

* **Reads** — `replace` did nothing `insert & update` did not do (that is the whole
  of OQ-418). **Deleted outright.** Nothing is lost.
* **Premises and units** — `replace` is the ONLY thing in this product that retires
  a record the utility's file no longer carries (**BR-MET-099**, PO 2026-08-21:
  *500 on file · 431 in the file · 69 not in it · 41 occupied → 28 deactivated*).
  So: **the option is withdrawn from every screen and refused at the API boundary
  by name**, and **the behaviour is left standing, unreachable**, with BR-MET-099
  amended to say exactly that, and **OQ-580** put to the PO.

**Why not delete it:** destroying a signed capability on an inferred scope is not
reversible in one line. **Why not leave it reachable by API:** a mode no screen
offers but any POST can reach is a destructive write with no consequence preview in
front of it — the opposite of what BR-MET-099 itself requires. The refusal is the
honest middle, and it is the **exact shape already ratified for the assets targets**
(`_refuse_replace_for_assets`, OQ-326, 2026-08-22), generalised rather than invented.

### What was CHECKED rather than assumed

* **BR-MET-127's billed-read refusal survives.** `SUPERSEDING_MODES` contained both
  `upsert` and `replace`; removing `replace` leaves `upsert`, and the rule's own
  text already read *"A Replace (or Insert & update) row…"*. Re-measured on this
  branch, not taken from the earlier entry. Its wording is amended so it stops
  naming a control nobody can reach (hard-won law 1).
* **No migration.** `ImportRun.write_mode` and `ReadBatch.write_mode` are plain
  `TextField`s with **no `choices=`**, so the constant is not in the DDL.
  `makemigrations --check` stays clean.
* **No seeded data carries `replace`.** `sample_data.py:725` writes `"insert"`.
* **Historical rows still render.** A run or batch already written with
  `write_mode="replace"` keeps its value; the display list carries a withdrawn-label
  fallback so it prints a sentence rather than a raw id.

### BR-MET-210 — the rule that makes it STAY consistent

Minted by this CR: *every import in this product offers exactly two write modes, in
this order, with these words, at step 1, through one shared control.* Without it,
the eighth import target adds a third mode or a different label and nobody notices —
which is precisely the history above.

**Version `2.64.0`.**

## 2026-08-27 · CR-040 B5/B6 BUILT — the link was already true, and the bill now refuses rather than under-billing 🔒

**The lane that executed OQ-531's five parts and OQ-366's closure. Three
judgments were made where the rules ran out; each is here with its worked
figure, because a judgment explained in a report evaporates (hard-won law 10).**

### JUDGMENT 1 — B6 SHIPS A REFUSAL, NOT A BILL, AND THAT IS THE HONEST HALF

`BR-CUS-170` is ruled: a master's bill is the common areas **plus the base
charges of every unit with no occupying account**. The coverage READ is built
and published. **The priced lines are not, and could not be from this lane's
files.** Three facts, each measured on this tree:

| What blocks it | Measured |
|---|---|
| One bill cannot carry TWO base charges for one service | `apps/billing/contracts.TariffConfig` has no per-tariff base-only flag; `tariffs` is one config per SERVICE |
| A base-only tariff would steal another unit's read | `stages/measure_consumption._reading_for` matches a reading **by service code alone** — a second electric tariff picks up the common area's read and bills its usage twice |
| Widening `covered_units` reads the empty unit's METER | `runs.readings_for_account` walks `gather.covered_units`, so the owner would be charged USAGE the ruling did not ask for (*"U6 to U10 base charges"*) |

⚠ **THE ENGINE'S OUTPUT SIDE ALREADY SUPPORTS IT.**
`rating.engine.price_bill(base_only_services=…)` prices each tariff to its own
base line with **no usage line** — BR-BIL-028's split, which exists precisely
because *"a base-only service is known to have no billable usage"* while a
missing read is *unknown*. **What is missing is the ROUTING, not the
arithmetic**, and the routing lives in three files this lane was scoped away
from. Filed as **DEF-990** and REPORTED as owed.

**So the choice was: issue the short bill, or refuse.** It refuses, and the
figure is why:

> **1408 Elm with one empty flat still connected: the owner owes $69.60 +
> $12.00 = $81.60, and the product produces $69.60.** Measured, by removing the
> guard and issuing the bill through `runs.calculate_account`:
> `AssertionError: THE SHORT DOCUMENT: the owner is billed 69.60 and owes 81.60`.

That is **DEF-571's shape one rule-widening later** — a document that foots, is
short by a covered unit, and says nothing about it. Hard-won law 3: the unsafe
option must be the one you type.

⚠ **AND THE REFUSAL IS DELIBERATELY NARROW, WHICH IS WHY NO SIGNED FIGURE
MOVED.** It fires only where a unit with no occupying account carries **both a
plan and at least one service point** — i.e. only where money is actually being
omitted. `1408 Elm`'s three ordinary units are unplanned and unmetered, so
`BR-CUS-068`'s signed **$41.20 + $28.40 = $69.60** reproduces byte for byte and
is asserted doing so.

### JUDGMENT 2 — THE PARENT LINK IS A SELECTOR, AND `accounts` GAINS NO COLUMN

CR-040 sized B5 as *"the master account gets sub-accounts"*, which reads as a
migration. **It is not one.** The PO ruled the link is the premises, so it is
DERIVED — `master_account_for` / `sub_accounts_for_master` — and the test
asserts the SCHEMA as well as the answer (`parent_account_id` is absent from
`Account._meta`). Two reasons, and the second is the operational one:

1. a stored copy of a fact the premises already carries is a second place for it
   to be wrong;
2. **it would need maintaining through every move-in and every move-out.** The
   derived read keys off `occupying_accounts_for_unit`, so a tenant becomes a
   child the moment they activate and stops being one the moment they close,
   with nobody ticking anything.

**And it was already true, which is the finding:** `500 Main Street`'s five
accounts have been children of `AC-2026-00052` since the day both were seeded.
CR-040's *"the master has no children"* was a **reporting gap**. The proof is
the field: `open_sub_accounts` has been TYPED AND RENDERED in
`07-frontend/src/features/customers/moveShared.tsx` since 2026-08-24 with **no
backend serving it** — hard-won law 2, filed alongside as **DEF-992**, because
`closeImpactPort()` still returns `null` citing a grep that went stale on
2026-08-25 when both routes were mounted.

### JUDGMENT 3 — THE DUNNING SUBJECT IS PER-DECISION, NOT A CONSTANT

`DUNNING_AFTER_CLOSE` carried `subject_unresolved` for three days, honestly,
because BR-CUS-082 and BR-CUS-097 did not resolve each other. OQ-366 closed
them — **the ladder chases the MASTER** — but the same morning's qualification
means it chases the master **only for a residue a clerk actually tied back**.

**So the subject cannot be a constant on the panel.** `_dunning_for(target)`
resolves it from the decision: a `transfer` names the master and cites OQ-366; a
write-off, a collection or a payment plan names *"the closed account itself"*
and **no master appears anywhere in the answer**. Worked, end to end:
**$328.70 − $153.50 = $175.20**, and TIER 1 fires on the master — but only
because a person chose it.

### WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE

**`OQ-580` is minted and nothing is seeded against it.** A master already at
TIER 3 on its own arrears: does an arriving residue RESTART, JOIN, or run as its
OWN sequence? Not put to the PO. The prohibition is carried **in the code**, in
`LADDER_ON_A_MASTER_WITH_ARREARS_UNSIGNED`, and a test asserts the sentence is
still there — so a later lane deleting it goes RED rather than quietly choosing
one of the three.

### THE PROCESS FAILURE THIS LANE OWES (DEF-991)

⚠ **This lane wrote its first four edits into the SHARED checkout**, by
prefixing its commands with `cd /home/user/SMARTBillHub` while running in
`.claude/worktrees/agent-a8db13de539d883b1`. Nothing was lost and nothing was
published — the file was restored and verified byte-identical to
`git show HEAD:<path>` before any other lane committed — but for a few minutes
four rule-cell edits sat in a tree seven other lanes were committing from.

**The reusable line, and it costs nothing: never `cd` to an absolute path.** The
working directory already IS the worktree and it persists between calls. `pwd`
and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` must be equal, and a lane that never types
the repo root cannot write into another lane's tree. **The recovery generalises
too:** reverse your own edit in place rather than restoring from HEAD — a
restore would clobber whatever another lane had uncommitted in that same file,
which is the very damage being repaired.

## 2026-08-27 · The asset import: what the PO reported, what reproduced, and the one rule that changed (DEF-935 · DEF-962 · DEF-963 · DEF-964 · DEF-965)

**The report, verbatim, twice.** *"Asset -Import Asset is not working - Template
does not have a unit field so he is not going to link it . - please raise defect
and evalate why asset - meters, sub meters and behhind the meter is not
working"*, and then *"you dont have Unit field in CSV file that is downloaded;
when you upload assets you iwll need Units field mapping - please chekc out"*.
The screenshot: v2.52.0, `/ottumwa-water-works/assets/import?target=assets_meters`,
**stage 4 of 5**, dry run reading `Will create 20 · Existing records updated 0 ·
Rows rejected 0 · Target Meters`, and a red strip saying **"Something went wrong.
Nothing was saved — try again."**

### The judgment that mattered: a clean rehearsal followed by a dead commit is a CLASS, not an incident

The engine is not broken. All three targets were driven through all five stages
on a rebuilt Ottumwa Water Works tenant (water · sewer · trash, the PO's own
mix) and every one committed: 20 meters with units → 20 created / 20 tagged;
20 with blank units → 20 created / 20 to inventory; 5 sub-meters under 5
masters → 5 created; 5 devices → 5 created; 5 devices naming only a premises →
5 created.

**What DID reproduce is the SHAPE of the report**, and it is DEF-618 and
DEF-619's class on a third input: *a condition stage 3 never checks, refused
inside the one stage that writes.*

`tenancy.selectors.service_default_uoms` has said so in its own docstring the
whole time: **"Four of the ten catalog services — sewer, solar, thermal/heat,
battery — have no design-stated default, so a tenant that enables one carries a
NULL."** A meter naming one of those four passes every rule in the import
catalogue, rehearses `Will create 20 · Rows rejected 0`, and is then refused by
`_check_measuring_requirements` at LOAD time with `VAL-001
assets.uom_required`. The load is ONE all-or-nothing transaction, so **nothing
is saved and no row is named.** Ottumwa sells sewer.

**The refusal is right and was never in question.** CLAUDE.md rule 3 and
BR-AST-009: a measuring asset carries an EXPLICIT unit, and there is correctly
no assume-kWh branch anywhere in this product. The ruling here is about
**where** the question is asked, and the worked figure is the one above: 20
rows rehearsed, 0 rejected, 0 written.

### The rule: `AST.SERVICE_HAS_UNIT`, TIER 1, ERROR, reject_row

*"The service a meter measures has a unit on file — a service with no unit
cannot carry a reading."* On `assets_meters` and `assets_submeters`.

**TIER 1 (structural, not configurable)** for the reason `AST.SERVICE_AT_PREMISES`
gives verbatim one rule up: the loader refuses the row whatever the rule table
says, so a switchable rule would tell an operator the load succeeded when it
did not (BR-MET-090).

**The sentence names the SERVICE and Settings → Services**, not the field. The
load's own copy renders as *"Choose the unit this asset reads in."* — which
points at `unit`, a field the assets import does not offer as a column at all,
so an operator holding the CSV cannot act on it.

**This is not new law.** It enforces a signed rule (BR-AST-009 + hard rule 3)
one stage earlier. Nothing was chosen that a signed statement did not already
decide, and no open question was resolved.

### The template: it was built for a utility that is not ours

Two separate defects, both measured on the bytes:

* **DEF-963** — `assets_meters` / `assets_submeters` declared
  `sample="electric"`. On Ottumwa the product's own template is rejected by the
  product's own import: *"This utility does not sell electric."* — 1 in, 1
  error, 0 will create. **This is CR-036 (i) / DEF-754's ruling, which was
  applied to `services_available` on premises and never carried to the target
  whose entire job is attaching a meter to a service.** The cell is now the
  tenant's own first enabled service **that can actually carry a meter** — the
  same map `AST.SERVICE_HAS_UNIT` judges with, so the sample and the rule
  cannot disagree.

* **DEF-962** — every reference cell in all three assets templates shipped
  BLANK. Measured header and row:

      asset_no,meter_type,service,read_method,multiplier,unit_ref,manufacturer,…
      M-9001,ami,electric,ami,1,,Sample Meter Co,MX-100,…

  `unit_ref` on all three targets, the REQUIRED `parent_asset_no` on
  sub-meters, `premises` on devices. **Root cause:** `_asset_column` wrote a
  `sample` key unconditionally and `sample_csv`'s `cell()` reads that key
  first, so the kind-aware worked-value logic beneath it was dead for all four
  explicit targets.

  **The harm is SILENT, and that is the whole judgment.** BR-AST-045 makes a
  blank unit lawful — it loads to inventory — so a file built on that template
  rehearses clean and loads **20 created / to_inventory 20 / 0 rejected / 0
  flagged**. Twenty meters, no complaint anywhere, attached to nothing. That is
  the PO's *"he is not going to link it"*, and it is exactly the sentence
  `sample_csv` already carries about `services_available`: *"the ONE input in
  the whole importer that fails silently"*.

  **The fix is CR-036 (i)'s test, applied to a reference instead of a
  vocabulary:** a row THIS TENANT ALREADY HAS is not a guess — it is the same
  index `AST.UNIT_ON_FILE` / `AST.PREMISES_ON_FILE` / `AST.PARENT_ON_FILE`
  judge every imported row against. So the cells carry the tenant's own first
  unit, premises and ACTIVE master, and are blank **only** when the tenant
  genuinely has none of that kind — which is the honest way to state the build
  order Premises → Units → Assets.

### What is NOT closed, and is not being narrowed away

**DEF-965 — the commit failure in the screenshot is NOT reproduced on HEAD**
and stays open. DEF-935 produces the same symptom on the same tenant and may
well be it; that is a candidate, not a finding, and the register says so.

**DEF-964 — and this is why the question cannot be settled from the repo.** The
import wizard renders `refusalOf(failure, t)` and never `diagnosticOf()`, so a
body that is not the ratified envelope becomes *"Something went wrong. Nothing
was saved — try again."* with no HTTP status, no code and no trace reference.
`diagnosticOf` exists **because of the PO's own ruling of 2026-08-10** —
*"unable to see what is the error on screen — hence as user I'm unable to see
what is happening"* — and it was wired to `StateFrame` and the pricing page and
not to the only screen in this workflow that writes. The strip in the
screenshot is that gap: the product had nothing to hand back.

### The property nothing in this repo asserted, and now does

`test_cr025_sample_csv` drives the round trip for **premises only**. DEF-616's
guard walks all six targets and asserts stage 1 **detects the headers** and
stops. **Nothing drove a shipped template to a WRITE**, and nothing at all
tested any of it on a tenant that sells something other than electricity —
which, on the evidence of this report, is the tenant we actually have.
`tests/test_def962_def963_assets_template.py` is that property: download →
upload unedited → **commit**, on Ottumwa, for all three targets, asserting the
row that arrives is ATTACHED and not sitting in inventory.

## 2026-08-27 · CR-040 E17 — the seeding panel's dependency graph, and the edge deliberately NOT drawn

**A lane judgment, not a PO ruling.** Recorded because the next agent looking at
`BLOCK_DEPENDENCIES` will see three blocks with edges and one billing block whose
edge points somewhere surprising, and the surprising one is the decision.

### What was measured before anything was written

The Sample data panel (S8 → Company profile) has rendered one line per BLOCK
since CR-039 wave B, so the three blocks CR-040 waves C and D added — a refund, an
overcharge correction and a second billing cycle — **did each get a line.** What
they did not get is an **edge**. `BLOCK_DEPENDENCIES` held ten of the fourteen
blocks; none of the three new ones was in it.

`_root_for` walks declared edges only, and its own docstring chooses that
direction on purpose: *"a missing edge makes a block look like a ROOT, never like
a consequence"*. So on a tenant whose first bill run could not issue — the
commonest real failure, an unmapped tax authority — the panel drew **four
"Start here" markers over one cause**, on the screen whose entire job is to say
which line to read first. Wave B built that screen to answer *"we need to look at
what of 1 job fails"*; two waves later it was answering it four times.

### The three edges, and where each came from

Not invented. CR-039 wave B task 7's standard is that the graph is derived from
what the code already says, and all three seeders **already stated their
upstreams in the sentence they print at a person when they refuse**:

| Block | Upstream | The words already in the file |
|---|---|---|
| `payments:seed_sample_refund` | `customers:seed_sample_records` | *"overpays does not exist. The Accounts block above has to load first."* |
| `payments:seed_sample_refund` | `payments:seed_sample_records` | *"The Payments block above is what records it"* |
| `billing:seed_sample_correction` | `customers:seed_sample_records` | *"June bill was over-read does not exist. The Accounts block above has to load first."* |
| `billing:seed_sample_correction` | `billing:seed_sample_records` | *"The first Bills block above is what issues it"* |
| `billing:seed_sample_second_cycle` | `metering:seed_sample_reads` | *"The Meter reads block above has to"* |

### ⚠ THE JUDGMENT: cycle two does NOT depend on cycle one

The obvious edge is `billing:seed_sample_second_cycle → billing:seed_sample_records`,
and it is **wrong**. Both billing blocks call the same `_preconditions`, so a
tenant with no cycle, no attributable actor or an unmapped tax authority fails
**both** — but that is a **COMMON CAUSE, not a dependency**. July bills from
July's own reads and needs no June invoice; the second cycle exists to bill an
estate with a financial past, which is a matter of ORDER (task D14) and not of
prerequisite.

**What the wrong edge would have cost:** the panel would have told an operator
that fixing the first bill run fixes the second, and marked cycle two a
CONSEQUENCE — *"retry the root first"* — when the thing to fix is the setup fact
underneath both. `_root_for`'s stated preference is the tiebreak: an unmarked
failure is at worst noise, a **wrongly-marked consequence tells an operator to
ignore a real, separate fault.** Two roots and one fix is the honest report.

### `ROOT_BLOCKS` — the half of the graph that had nowhere to live

Four blocks genuinely depend on nothing (identity's staff users, rating's plans,
metering's estate, the parked move-in). In a dict that only holds edges, *"this
block needs nothing"* and *"nobody has looked at this block"* are the **same
absence**, which is exactly how three blocks landed edgeless with two tests over
the graph and neither able to object: both ask *is every declared edge true?*, and
a graph can be perfectly honest and half empty.

A root carries **no quote** where an edge carries one, deliberately: an edge is a
CLAIM about the code and must be greppable back out of it; a root is the absence
of a claim, so what is checked instead is that somebody decided.

### What this found on the way — `DEF-1090`

`test_cr039__a_retry_that_fails_again_records_the_new_failure` asserted
`len(row.blocks) == 1` on the **billing module's** ledger row. Billing owned one
block when that was written and owns three now, so the suite guarding this very
panel had been **red since waves C and D landed** — over a product behaving
correctly. Its own failure message was always about the retried BLOCK; that is
what it asserts now, plus a second assertion, derived from `SAMPLE_MODULES`, that
a retry does not quietly drop the module's other blocks off the row.

## 2026-08-27 — CR-043 findings 12 + 16: Continue starts the bill run, and a wizard step can refuse in its own words

**Lane:** CR-043 · the Run bills wizard. **Closes DEF-936 (blocker) and DEF-939.**

**What the PO said, verbatim, two messages about one screen:**
> *"all inputs are provided continue button dont work"*

> *"why two button at botton , I can not save and exit"*

### THE JUDGMENT THAT NEEDED MAKING ON PURPOSE — where the fix lives

CR-043 asked for this one explicitly: *"if the answer is written once, into
`WizardFrame`, the other five wizards inherit it; if it is written into
`BillRunWizard`, this CR will be re-opened from a different screen."*

**It is written into `WizardFrame`, and the reason is that the frame was half of
the defect.** `WizardStep.validate` returned `boolean`. Step 1 of the bill run
refused on `runId !== ""` — a condition **no field on the screen carries** — and
the frame, knowing only that a boolean came back false, printed *"This step
isn't finished. Fill in what's marked above, then press Continue again."*
**There was nothing above to fill in.** The step knew the reason and had no
channel to say it; the frame had the channel and no way to know. Any future
wizard with a non-field precondition lands in the identical hole.

So `validate` now answers `boolean | string | Promise<boolean | string>`:

| It answers | The frame does |
|---|---|
| `true` | advances |
| `false` | blocks, and says the generic sentence — **still correct**, because the unmet condition is a marked field and *"fill in what's marked above"* points at the mark |
| a **string** | blocks, and says **that sentence instead**, at the button that refused |
| a **Promise** of any of the three | single-flights the press, renders the A18 §3 working state, then acts on the answer |

The generic sentence becomes the FALLBACK it should always have been. That is
DEF-936's own recorded prevention (b), verbatim: *"a step whose validate can
fail for a reason no field carries must be able to supply its own sentence, or
the frame will keep telling people to look at fields that are already correct"*.

### AND THE ANSWER TO "WHICH BUTTON" IS: THERE IS ONE

DEF-939 and DEF-936 are one knot, so they are untied once. Step 1 drew a primary
**"Start this run →"** directly above the frame's primary **"Continue"**, with
the *"What this step no longer asks you"* panel wedged between them. Two red
buttons, one screen (B14 rule 2 gives a screen ONE primary slot), and the one a
clerk reads as *proceed* was the one that could not.

**Continue now creates the run. The step draws no commit control of its own.**

⚠ **BR-SHL-019 IS NOT WEAKENED, AND THE COMMENT THAT SEEMED TO FORBID THIS WAS
ANSWERING A DIFFERENT QUESTION.** The source read: *"The run is CREATED here,
not by Continue: BR-SHL-019 gives a wizard ONE transactional commit and this
wizard's is the release (step 6)."* True — and an argument for the run-create
not being **the frame's commit**, never an argument for it needing **a second
button**. The one transactional commit is still `commitRelease` at step 6.
Nothing about the write changed: the same `POST /billing/runs`, the same body,
the same BR-BIL-005 idempotency, from a different control. Pressing twice is
safe: the frame single-flights Continue, and a duplicate is a 409 carrying the
existing run's link.

### THE BUG THE FIX WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE INTRODUCED, AND ITS FIGURE

One press of Continue now writes **two** URL params — the run id, then the step.
`setSearchParams` composes against the params of the **render whose closure
called it**, so the naive form wrote `?step=2` onto a base that never had the
run id, and the clerk landed on step 2 reading *"Start the run on step 1 first.
Until it exists there is nothing to gather and nothing to show."* **about the
run it had just created.** `setParams` merges through a ref advanced
synchronously by every write. Proved by reverting exactly that one expression:
`TC-DEF936-3` goes red on the sentence above.

### WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT COVERED, AND SAID SO RATHER THAN CLAIMED

`handleContinue` early-returns on `continuing` as well as disabling the button.
While the button carries `disabled`, React never delivers a click to that
handler, so **no DOM event this suite can dispatch will exercise the
early-return** — a test written for it passes whether or not the guard exists,
which is what happened when `TC-FRAME-5` was first written the other way round
(DEF-182's lesson: a check that cannot distinguish pass from fail is worse than
none). The guard stays as the belt to the disabled brace; the test asserts the
brace, and the comment names the belt as uncovered.

## 2026-08-27 — WHICH SERVICES A BILL CHARGES IS DERIVED FROM THE UNIT, NOT FROM THE PLAN (PO ruling, closing OQ-601 on mechanism)

**PO verbatim, in full:**

> *"how do you decide how many services to be billed on that account? You look at
> account, then you look at unit asscoaited with that account, how many meters and
> how many services are atatched to it and decide how you bill the services on
> account. - your logic need to fix here"*

**And, closing OQ-317 in the same exchange:**

> *"option A is correct; where do you see the carts - they are not on accounts theya
> re on Units."*

**WHAT THIS REVERSES.** `billing.gather._tariffs_for_plan` iterates
`rating.plan_rate_schedules(plan_id)` — the PLAN's schedules — and narrows them by
the run's service scope. The unit is read only to resolve the connection SIZE. So
the set of services on a bill has been a property of the **plan**, and the account's
own service points have never been consulted. That is why Ana Alvarez's badges read
WATER · SEWER · TRASH and her bill charged **$64.57** for water and sewer with no
trash line, no run exception and no note (DEF-1060).

**THE RULING, restated as the product will implement it:** the services a bill
charges are the services **attached to the unit the account occupies**. The plan
supplies the PRICE for each; it no longer supplies the LIST.

**THE CHAIN ALREADY EXISTS IN THE SCHEMA** — nothing here needs a new table:

    account → unit → service_points (one per service) → assets (meter · cart · …)

* `metering.selectors.service_points_for(unit_id)` already returns
  `{id, service, route_id}` per point and is already published to billing (it is
  what `_coverage_facts` calls today).
* `assets.Asset.service_point` is a reviewed cross-module FK with an index on
  `(tenant, service_point)`. A meter is an asset of a MEASURING type; a
  `container_cart` is an asset of a non-measuring type (BR-AST-042), and four are
  already seeded (DEF-496).

**WHY THE RULE IS SERVICE POINTS AND NOT METERS, stated because the PO's sentence
says "how many meters and how many services".** Keying on meters alone would leave
trash exactly where it is: a cart has no register. The service POINT is what says
*this unit takes this service*; the ASSET on it says *how it is measured and how
many*. Both halves of the PO's sentence are used, for different jobs — the point
decides WHETHER, the asset decides HOW MUCH.

**OQ-317 CLOSED — option A.** `$15.00` per cart, and the workbook's `$18.00`
monthly trash base is **retired**. A three-cart household is **$45.00**, not
`$63.00`. And the quantity is read from the UNIT: the carts are assets on the
unit's trash service point, not a number on the account.

**WHAT IS NOT YET RULED and is going back to the PO before any code lands** — the
four cases where the unit's services and the plan's schedules disagree, and what a
bill should do about each. They are listed in the reply that carried this ruling
and are the subject of `OQ-601`'s second half. Nothing is implemented until they
are answered: a bill that guesses at one of them is a bill that charges the wrong
money quietly, which is the defect this ruling exists to remove.

## 2026-08-27 — THE PREMISES OWNER **IS** THE MASTER ACCOUNT (PO ruling, closing OQ-500)

**PO verbatim, in full:**

> *"so premises owner is master accountin system. you ahve to showall details form
> account - Bascially Premises -> owner = Master account - it can be existing master
> account also so at the time of premises creation we should check - how you will
> handle this"*

**WHAT THIS SETTLES.** `OQ-500` asked whether a premises' typed owner is the default
payer. The answer is stronger than the question: the owner is not merely *the payer*,
it **is the master account** — one party, one record, shown with an account's full
details rather than as a name beside one.

**WHAT IT REPLACES, and this is the part that matters.** `BR-CUS-171` derives the
master **geometrically**: the `kind='master'` account anchored on one of the premises'
COMMON AREAS (`customers.selectors.master_account_for`). That derivation has two
stated weaknesses, both now answered by the ruling rather than by a tie-break:

* it **refuses by answering `None`** where two masters cover one premises — *"naming
  the first would make the owner of one building's hallway the parent of another's
  tenants on a tie-break nobody chose"*;
* it needs a common area to exist at all, so a premises with no common area has no
  master even when it plainly has an owner.

Under the ruling the link is **declared, not inferred**: the premises names its owner,
the owner is the master account, and geometry stops being the evidence.

**MOST OF THE CHAIN IS ALREADY BUILT** — this is not a new schema:

* `Premises.owner` → `PremisesOwner` (FK, CR-039 wave C task 12, BR-TEN-150).
* `PremisesOwner.customer` → `customers.Customer` (FK) — the owner already resolves
  to a party.
* `uq_premises_owners_tenant_name_ci` on `(tenant, lower(name))` — **an owner name is
  already unique per tenant, enforced by the database**, which is exactly the
  "check at premises creation" the PO asks for: the match key exists and the
  constraint already prevents twelve premises creating twelve copies of one landlord.

**THE ONE MISSING LINK is `owner → master ACCOUNT`.** Today nothing joins a
`premises_owners` row to an `accounts` row of kind `master`.

**NOT IMPLEMENTED. Four decisions are owed to the PO first**, each of which decides
who is billed, and they were put to them in the reply that carried this ruling:
when the master account comes into existence, what happens to a premises whose owner
has no master yet, what a clerk sees when the name nearly matches an existing owner,
and whether the geometric derivation is retired or kept as a fallback. A guess at any
of them routes a bill at the wrong party.

## 2026-08-27 — FOUR RULINGS IN ONE MESSAGE: OQ-570, OQ-532, OQ-580, OQ-590

**PO verbatim, in full:**

> *"4 · OQ-570 — what clears a migrated balance? 🔒 this is correct - B — migrate
> the balance as an invoice at cutover — Payments allocate against it like any bill;
> fully visible; closest to 'we will migrate opening balances as well as payment
> recieved record'; 5 · OQ-532 — a residue lands on a master already in collections
> - this si correct - B — join the existing position — Tier 4, on a larger balance;
> 6 · OQ-580 — retiring premises you no longer serve - this si correct - a for now,
> c if it bites. 7 · OQ-590 — parked billing runs - B — a Parked section on the
> Billing list — Real queue, real work"*

### OQ-570 — CLOSED, option B, and it has a ❄️ FROZEN collision that must be settled first

A migrated opening balance becomes an **invoice at cutover**, so a payment allocates
against it exactly as it does against any bill, and the settlement is a row rather
than an inference.

⚠ **THIS SUPERSEDES PART OF `BR-BIL-160`, WHICH SHIPPED THE SAME DAY.** That rule
puts the opening balance on the bill's `previous_balance` line and derives the
settled part as `min(account credit position, opening balance)` — a cap that exists
*only* because a payment against an opening balance met no invoice. Under option B it
meets one, so the cap becomes dead code rather than a rule.

⚠⚠ **AND IT COLLIDES WITH `GT-16`, WHICH IS INSIDE THE ❄️ FROZEN B5 FILE.** GT-16
pins three things about account `A-12103` (buckets `84.20 / 62.10 / 0.00 / 121.00`):

1. `accounts.balance` = **267.30** — Σ buckets, exact, no recompute;
2. the day-one ageing report reproduces **the four buckets verbatim**;
3. **ONE opening JE** dated `2026-08-31`, `source_type` **`opening_balance`**,
   DR AR 267.30.

**One invoice cannot hold four ages** — an invoice has a single date, so a single
migrated invoice collapses the four buckets into one and breaks (2). Four invoices,
each dated into its own bucket, preserve (1) and (2) — and then **(3) is the
question**, because four invoices that POST are not one opening JE with
`source_type opening_balance`.

**The reading that satisfies all three, put to the PO and finance rather than
adopted:** the opening JE stays exactly as GT-16 freezes it — the money is already on
the books — and the migrated invoices exist as **allocation targets that post
nothing new**, so nothing is double-counted and no frozen figure moves. If that is
right, option B lands with no re-sign. If the invoices must post, GT-16 assertion (3)
changes and that is HUMAN-GUIDE §6, never an inline edit.

### OQ-532 — CLOSED, option B: JOIN the existing position

A residue arriving on a master already at Tier 3 does **not** restart the ladder and
does not run its own sequence: it is more money on an account already in collections,
so the next letter is **Tier 4** on the larger balance. This narrows `BR-CUS-082`,
whose literal words restart at Tier 1 — and the PO's reason for narrowing it is the
one the question named: restarting *relieves* a landlord already deep in collections
by resetting the clock on arrears they have not paid.

### OQ-580 — CLOSED: (a) now, (c) if it bites

`Replace` stays withdrawn from every import. Retiring premises a utility no longer
serves stays a per-record act. If the manual work becomes real — the PO's *"if it
bites"* — it returns as **its own control outside the import** (option c), never as a
side effect of uploading a file. `BR-MET-099`'s implementation stays in the code,
refused at the boundary by name, so (c) needs no rebuild and no data migration.

### OQ-590 — CLOSED, option B: a real Parked queue

⚠ **This is the one where the PO overruled the recommendation, and the reason is
worth recording:** the lane recommended (A) *the save-and-exit link is enough*, on
the grounds that a billing run is usually finished in one sitting. The PO chose (B) —
*"Real queue, real work"*. A parked run gets its **own section on the Billing list**,
so it is findable by someone who did not park it. That closes `DEF-1043`'s open half
and gives `WizardParkFlow` its sixth flow — which the CR-043 wizard lane refused to
invent precisely because no such surface existed to invent it against.

## 2026-08-27 — STEAM AND BATTERY SIZE BANDS RATIFIED (PO ruling, closing OQ-560 and OQ-561)

**PO verbatim, in full:**

> *"8 & 9 · Steam and battery size bands - a — ≤1,000 · 1,000–10,000 · 10,000+ lb/hr
> (mirrors chilled water's three steps) and a — band on kW, carry kWh in the display
> name (one axis, like every other service) - this si correct"*

**These were the two dimensions the 2026-08-27 size-class ruling could NOT ratify**,
because they were put to the PO as a UNIT and a SHAPE with no boundaries — *"steam by
thousand pounds per hour"* and *"by kW and kWh together … the pair is the class"* —
and a signature covers only what was shown (PO 2026-08-11). Both have been refusing
by name with `raise NotImplementedError` since; both can now be seeded.

**THERMAL STEAM — three bands, mirroring chilled water's three steps:**
`≤1,000` · `1,000–10,000` · `10,000+` **lb/hr**. The worked case that made it visible:
a **12,000 lb/hr** hospital header and a **900 lb/hr** office riser have been sharing
one base charge, because thermal seeded three chilled-water classes and zero steam
classes.

**BATTERY — banded on kW, with kWh carried in the display name.** This is the one
place the PO chose *against* the shape they had earlier described: battery was put to
them as a PAIR, and the ruling makes it **one axis like every other service on the
card**, with the energy figure surviving as text a person reads rather than as a
second dimension the resolver keys on. **Why that matters and is recorded:** a base
charge resolves on `service → account type → size class`, so a second axis would have
made battery the only service whose class is not a single reference row — and the
lane that raised OQ-561 said in terms that expressing a pair in a flat `code`/`name`
row would be choosing the data model as well as the numbers. The ruling removes that
choice. The worked case: a **5 kW / 13 kWh** rooftop unit and a **100 kW / 400 kWh**
commercial pack no longer share one base charge.

⚠ **THE kW BOUNDARIES THEMSELVES ARE NOT IN THE PO'S SENTENCE.** They ratified the
AXIS (kW, not the pair) and the display treatment (kWh in the name). Where one kW
band ends is still unstated, and a lane may not pick it — that is the same trap this
pair of questions was minted for. It goes back as the one remaining half.

**The ten services' size-class count moves from 40 to 43 once steam is seeded**, and
battery moves from zero classes to however many the kW boundaries turn out to be.

## 2026-08-27 — THREE MORE RULINGS: OQ-550, OQ-502, and the self-serve stamp (OQ-610)

**PO verbatim, in full:**

> *"10 · OQ-550 — the sweep and your three sub-areas - option B please that is
> correct; 11 · OQ-502 — owner categories - A — extensible (ships today); 12 & 13 ·
> Self-serve - Sales can create the teant - but they will use same path that we have
> provided - why they ned seperate pth;"*

### OQ-550 — CLOSED, option B: the sweep re-offers a list the tenant already holds

The reference sweep may re-offer a **discretionary** list to a tenant that has a
`reference_seed_runs` row for **that same list** at an earlier fixture version. That
row is per-list, positive evidence that this tenant accepted this list; it needs no
new column and no backfilled default.

**What it delivers immediately, and why the question existed at all:** Silver Creek
Water shows **4** area rows against the fixture's **7**. The three missing are
`NORTH-NE`, `NORTH-NW` and `EAST-SE` — **the three the PO ratified on 2026-08-27
under OQ-432 and then could not see on the screen they had just approved** (DEF-902).

⚠ **THIS NARROWS `BR-TEN-160`, WHICH SHIPPED TODAY**, and the narrowing is exactly
what that rule's own clause 3 said it was not settling: *"Whether the sweep should
re-offer a discretionary list a tenant demonstrably already holds … is OQ-550, routed
to the PO. It is NOT adopted here."* The lane refused to adopt it and routed it; the
PO has now ruled it. **`OQ-088`'s stated harm is untouched** — a tenant that declined
charge codes has no `charge_codes` seed-run row, so it still receives nothing.
**`OQ-216` is NOT answered by this** and stays open: it asks a tenant-level question
about `reference_defaults_opted_in`, where this is per-list.

### OQ-502 — CLOSED, option A: owner categories stay tenant-extensible

The five seeded categories — owner-occupier · landlord · property manager · HOA ·
builder — are a starting set, not a closed vocabulary. A utility may add
`executor_of_estate`, `trust` or `receiver` exactly as it may add an area.

**This ratifies what already ships**, and the decision log of 2026-08-27 had recorded
the gap honestly at the time: *"nothing was put to the PO about this one, so the
build follows the house pattern and the row says so."* It has now been put to them.
`BR-TEN-036` / DB-14 stand; the cost the question named is accepted — a platform
report cannot count landlords across customers, because the vocabulary is the
tenant's.

### OQ-610 — the self-serve stamp: SAME PATH, and the residue is now a different question

> *"Sales can create the teant - but they will use same path that we have provided -
> why they ned seperate pth"*

**The question as asked is answered: there is no second path and none is wanted.**
Sales uses the public signup, so the code that stamps `IMPL-26-0001` · **0 months** ·
**$0.00** at signup is correct for every tenant it will ever meet, and nothing about
the provisioning transaction changes.

⚠ **WHAT THE ANSWER DOES NOT SETTLE, and it is a smaller question than the one that
was asked:** the row a sales-created tenant receives says *self-serve, zero months,
zero dollars*, and for a customer who has bought a nine-month implementation that is
false the moment it is written. Since the path is the same, the correction cannot
happen AT creation — so it has to be an **edit afterwards**, which means the
implementation order needs somewhere to be edited from. Today it has **no screen at
all** (`DEF-1092`): a tenant carries an implementation order no human can see.

So the two are the same piece of work, and that is the useful thing this ruling
surfaces: **the self-serve stamp is right, and it is only safe once the order is
editable.** Put back to the PO as the remaining half, together with the still
unanswered price question — the PO gave the shape (*"we will add price latet
currently you default it to $1"*, then a self-serve default of $0.00) and has not
confirmed the figure.

### DEF-965 — the PO will supply the evidence

> *"14 · DEF-965 — not a decision, a request - okay I will give you"*

Recorded because it changes how the row should be read: `DEF-965` is **not
abandoned and must not be closed against `DEF-935` as a presumed cause.** The
2.52.0 asset-import failure does not reproduce on this build; `DEF-935` (a sewer
meter passing the rehearsal and failing inside the commit, because four of the ten
services carry no default unit of measure) is a *candidate*, not a finding. The PO
has undertaken to supply the run reference, and with `DEF-964` fixed the next
occurrence will carry a quotable diagnostic instead of *"Something went wrong."*

⚠ **The row annotation was attempted and abandoned deliberately.** The register is
887 rows with mixed CRLF/LF terminators from earlier hand-appends, and a byte-exact
edit of one record could not be matched; rewriting the file through `csv` would have
produced the whole-file diff another lane already hit today. The fact lives here
instead, which is where a reader looks for *why* a row is still open.

## 2026-08-27 — THE FOUR EDGES OF UNIT-DERIVED BILLING, RULED (OQ-601's second half)

**PO verbatim, in full:**

> *"1 Unit has a service, plan has no schedule for it - this will never happen, in
> such case bill base only; 2 Plan has a schedule, unit has no service point - this
> will also not happen pratcially; - we have to bill it; 3 Service point exists, no
> asset at all - this can happen practically, when units are created and installaition
> is not complted; in such cases you ahve to see the status of Unit, you will also
> consider status of unit whether to bill that unit or not; 4 A cart on a service the
> plan prices per usage - price per usage is not correct, we will ahve to set rprice
> for utility service and cosnider that it is for 1 cart"*

**EDGE 1 — unit has the service, plan has no schedule → BILL BASE ONLY.** Not a
refusal. The PO's reason is that it will not happen in practice, so the product
should degrade rather than stop a run. ⚠ Recorded because it reverses the lane's
recommendation: the lane proposed refusing by name, on the grounds that this silent
case is what hid trash. The PO's answer keeps the bill flowing and the base charge is
the honest floor.

**EDGE 2 — plan has a schedule, unit has no service point → BILL IT.** Also not
expected in practice. ⚠ **This qualifies the mechanism ruling rather than
contradicting it:** the unit decides which services are billed for services the unit
KNOWS ABOUT, and a plan schedule with no matching point is still billed rather than
dropped. So the unit is the source of truth for ADDING a service the plan missed
(trash), never for REMOVING one the plan carries.

**EDGE 3 — service point, no asset → LOOK AT THE UNIT'S STATUS.** The stated case is
*"when units are created and installation is not completed"*. ⚠⚠ **AND THIS NAMES A
FIELD THAT DOES NOT EXIST, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART.** `apps/metering/models.py`
says so in its own header: *"`units` still has NO occupancy or status column:
occupancy derives from the active account (BR-MET-036 — a deliberate design
decision)"*. What DOES exist is the `occupancy_statuses` reference list, and its five
names already carry the billing consequence the PO is asking for:

| code | name |
|---|---|
| `OCC-T` | Occupied · tenant-billed |
| `OCC-O` | Occupied · owner-billed |
| `LNDLRD` | Landlord-billed · between tenants |
| `VAC` | **Vacant · base charges only** |
| `VAC-OFF` | **Vacant · service off, no billing** |

So the rule the PO wants is **already written into the vocabulary** — `VAC` bills base
only and `VAC-OFF` bills nothing — and two things stand between that and a working
bill: the status is DERIVED from the active account rather than stored, and **nothing
in the bill run reads it**, because the bill has never looked at the unit at all.
**And the PO's own case fits none of the five**: a unit awaiting installation is not
occupied, and calling it *vacant* is a stretch when it has never been in service.
Routed back as the one remaining question.

**EDGE 4 — DISSOLVED, and the PO corrected the premise.** *"price per usage is not
correct, we will ahve to set price for utility service and cosnider that it is for 1
cart"*. Trash is not priced per usage at all: the **utility service carries a price,
that price is understood to be for ONE cart**, and N carts multiply it. That is the
same shape as the `$15.00` ruling (OQ-317) seen from the pricing side rather than the
counting side, and it means the mismatch edge 4 asked about cannot arise.

**NOT IMPLEMENTED.** Edges 1, 2 and 4 are complete and buildable. Edge 3 is blocked on
one question — what a unit awaiting installation IS — and it is the only one of the
four that can stop a bill, so nothing ships until it is answered.

## 2026-08-27 — PREMISES → OWNER → MASTER ACCOUNT: the four decisions answered (OQ-500's second half)

**PO verbatim, in full:**

> *"1 When does the master account come into existence? when presmies are created you
> have owner for it, without owner how you can create premsies = owner = master
> account - we will need to careful what we do when we upload presmies in the system
> first time. also what if premises as only 1 unit which is single family home, in such
> cases how you will treat the master account. o will it be regular account. 2 A
> premises whose owner has no master yet - we have to create one. 3 Near match on the
> name - (b) offer the match, clerk decides - 4 The geometric derivation - idid not
> understand"*

**DECISION 1 — THE OWNER IS MANDATORY AT PREMISES CREATION, and the master account
comes into existence with it.** *"without owner how you can create premsies"*. This
makes `Premises.owner` a required field where it is nullable today, and it makes the
owner's account the master from the moment the address exists.

⚠ **THE PO RAISED THE FIRST-TIME UPLOAD THEMSELVES AND THEY ARE RIGHT — MEASURED.**
The premises importer maps an incoming `owner` column to **`owner_manager`**, which is
FREE TEXT (`import_runs.py:372`, `importers.py:53`). It creates no owner record and
therefore no master account. So a utility's first bulk upload — the one that creates
every premises it has — produces a tenant where **not one premises has a typed owner**,
and the rule above would refuse every row. **The matching machinery already exists:**
`premises_owners.source_owner_manager` is the provenance column for exactly this —
*"this owner row was created from that free-text string"* — and the CR-039 wave C lane
built the matching path around it. What is missing is that the IMPORT does not use it.

**DECISION 2 — a premises whose owner has no master yet: CREATE ONE.** *"we have to
create one."* No premises is left in a half-state waiting for someone to notice.

**DECISION 3 — near match: OFFER IT, THE CLERK DECIDES.** Never auto-merge. Two
landlords with similar names are two parties, and merging them bills the wrong one.

**DECISION 4 — the question was not understood, and that is a fair criticism of how it
was asked.** Restated plainly, with the answer that follows: to find a building's
master today, the code does not look at the owner at all — it looks at the building's
COMMON AREAS (the hallway, the car park) and finds the account that pays for them.
Whoever pays for the hallway is treated as the owner. That is what *"geometric"* meant:
the answer is worked out from the shape of the building rather than read from a stated
fact. **It breaks in exactly the two places this ruling cares about:** a building with
no common area — *a single-family home, the PO's own next question* — has nothing to
look at and therefore no master at all; and where two accounts pay for two different
common areas the code cannot tell which is the owner, so `master_account_for` answers
`None` and the building has no master either. **The ruling replaces all of it:** the
premises names its owner, the owner is the master, and nothing is inferred from
hallways. The old path is retired rather than kept as a fallback, because a fallback
that disagrees with the declared owner would silently bill a different party.

**THE SINGLE-FAMILY HOME — put back to the PO with a recommendation, not decided.**
The PO asks whether a one-unit premises has a master account or a regular one. The
answer the product already contains is that **master-ness is not a property of the
owner, it is a property of whether anyone ELSE occupies the premises** — and
`occupancy_statuses` already draws that line: `OCC-O` *"Occupied · owner-billed"*
against `OCC-T` *"Occupied · tenant-billed"*. So: a single-family home the owner LIVES
IN is one party paying one bill and should be **one regular account**; a single-family
home the owner RENTS OUT has an owner and a tenant, which is the same master/child
shape as a block of flats that happens to have one unit. **Recommended: the owner
RECORD always exists, and the owner's account is a MASTER only where some other
account occupies the premises — derived, not chosen at creation.** Not implemented
until the PO confirms.

## 2026-08-27 — GT-16's binding assertion, and a CAPACITY-MULTIPLIER pricing model for solar

**PO verbatim, in full:**

> *"⚠ OQ-570 has a frozen collision - 1 balance = 267.30, exact; ⚠ OQ-561 is closed in
> part - we want to solar base unit - how much charge it priduce then unit might have
> capacity to product multiple of base charge and then based on number of chanrge uinit
> it product and we wilmmultiple base charge - for example 1 solar unit product 1 KWH,
> on given unit we have installed 10 Kwh capacity. so on Unit solar capacity is 10 KWh;
> if 1 unit cost $10 then for this unit charge will be $100"*

### GT-16 — assertion 1 is the binding one

The PO was shown three things `GT-16` freezes and answered with the first:
**`accounts.balance` = `267.30`, exact — Σ buckets, no recompute.** That is now the
constraint any migration-as-invoice design must hold, and it rules out every scheme
that would RECOMPUTE the balance from the invoices rather than carry it.

⚠ **IT DOES NOT YET SETTLE ASSERTIONS 2 AND 3, AND THOSE ARE THE TWO THAT DECIDE
WHETHER A FINANCE RE-SIGN IS NEEDED.** Recorded so nobody reads a partial answer as a
full one:

* **(2)** the day-one ageing report reproduces the FOUR buckets verbatim
  (`84.20 / 62.10 / 0.00 / 121.00`) — one invoice has one date and collapses them;
* **(3)** ONE opening JE dated `2026-08-31`, `source_type` `opening_balance` — four
  posting invoices are not one opening JE.

Both go back as the narrow remaining question. Nothing is built until they are
answered, because getting either wrong moves a finance-signed figure.

### OQ-561 → the answer describes SOLAR and a MULTIPLIER, not battery bands

The question asked where a **battery** kW band ends. The answer describes **solar** and
does not use bands at all:

> one solar unit produces **1 kWh** · a given unit has **10 kWh** installed · if one
> unit costs **$10** then that unit is charged **$100**.

**This is `capacity × unit price`, not a size class.** A size class picks a different
FLAT rate from a band; a multiplier takes one price and multiplies it by an installed
quantity. They are different mechanisms and they cannot both apply to the same service
without counting size twice — a 10 kW system would sit in the `5–10` band AND be
multiplied by 10.

⚠⚠ **SO IT COLLIDES WITH A RULING THE PO MADE THE SAME DAY.** `BR-TEN-171` ratified
**four solar size classes** — `SOL-5` ≤5 kW DC · `SOL-5-10` · `SOL-10-25` · `SOL-25P`
25+ kW DC — and they are seeded. If solar is priced by capacity × unit price, those
four bands are superseded, and that is a reversal of a signed figure rather than an
addition to it. **Not adopted; put back to the PO.**

**AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME THE PO HAS DESCRIBED THIS SAME SHAPE**, which is the
useful observation and is why it is recorded as a pattern rather than as one service's
quirk:

| service | the PO's own words | shape |
|---|---|---|
| trash | *"1 trash can $15 - if you have 3 you multiple by 3"* | price × number of carts |
| trash again | *"set price for utility service and consider that it is for 1 cart"* | price × number of carts |
| solar | *"if 1 unit cost $10 then for this unit charge will be $100"* (10 kWh) | price × installed capacity |

**The open question is therefore bigger than solar:** is `capacity × unit price` the
general model for capacity-based services — solar, battery, and possibly thermal —
replacing size bands there, while bands stay for services sized by a physical
connection (water pipe diameter, electric amperage, gas CFH)? A lane may not decide
that: it would supersede ratified figures across several services at once.

## 2026-08-27 — "NOT IN SERVICE" IS DERIVED, NOT A NEW STATUS (PO ruling — OQ-601's last edge)

**PO verbatim, in full:**

> *"C — derive it: a service point with no asset and no account means not in service"*

**A unit awaiting installation gets NO new status value and NO new column.** It is
recognised by the two facts that are already true of it: a service point with **no
asset** standing on it and **no account** occupying the unit. Both are already
readable — `assets.Asset.service_point` is an indexed cross-module FK, and occupancy
already derives from the active account (`BR-MET-036`, which the units table's own
header calls *"a deliberate design decision"*).

**WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND NOT JUST THE CHEAP ONE.** The alternative offered
was a sixth `occupancy_statuses` value — *Pending installation* — and it would have
been a value somebody has to SET and therefore a value somebody can forget to set, on
exactly the units nobody is looking at yet. The derived form cannot go stale: the day
an installer fits the meter the asset appears, and the day a customer moves in the
account appears, and the unit starts billing because the facts changed rather than
because a clerk remembered to change a dropdown.

**WITH THIS, `OQ-601` IS FULLY ANSWERED AND BUILDABLE.** The complete rule the product
will implement:

    account → unit → service points          ← WHICH services are billed
                   → assets on each point    ← HOW: usage · quantity · base only
                   → no asset AND no account ← NOT IN SERVICE: bill nothing

    1. a unit service the plan has no schedule for  → base only      (PO)
    2. a plan schedule the unit has no point for    → bill it        (PO)
    3. a point with no asset and no account         → not in service (PO, this ruling)
    4. a cart on a per-usage service                → cannot arise; the service
                                                      price IS per cart            (PO)

**AND THE OCCUPANCY VOCABULARY ALREADY CARRIES THE REST OF THE ANSWER**, which is why
nothing new is minted here: `VAC` is *"Vacant · base charges only"* and `VAC-OFF` is
*"Vacant · service off, no billing"*. A unit that HAS been in service and is now empty
is one of those; a unit that has never been in service is this ruling's derived case.
The three are distinguishable without a new field.

⚠ **WHAT STILL BLOCKS NOTHING BUT IS WORTH SAYING:** the bill run does not read the
unit at all today, so *"nothing in the product consults occupancy when billing"* stays
true until this lands. That is the same gap that let Ana Alvarez's trash disappear,
and it is now one piece of work rather than four questions.

**Bands stay** for services sized by a physical connection: **pipe diameter** (water),

## 2026-08-27 · BANDS AND THE CAPACITY MULTIPLIER **COMBINE** FOR TRASH, STORM WATER AND BROADBAND — CONFIRMED

**PO verbatim:** *"This is correct - im okay with it; please accept ti t- Recommend:
keep bands for trash / storm water / broadband and multiply by the count. The capacity
multiplier replaces bands only where you already ruled it — solar, battery, thermal."*

This closes the ⚠⚠ paragraph left open earlier the same day under *"THREE SERVICES THE
RULING DOES NOT NAME"*. The reading proposed there — that the two models are orthogonal
rather than competing — **is adopted**.

### The rule

A **band** and a **count** are different mechanisms and occupy different slots:

| | what it is | where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **band** (`service_size_classes`) | picks WHICH PRICE ROW applies | stated on the asset; `apps/rating/resolution.py` resolves service → account type → size class, and `schedule` carries per-size tiers as `size_class -> tiers` |
| **count** | MULTIPLIES that price | the billed quantity of a quantity-priced service |

So for a unit with **three 96-gallon carts at $18.00 each**:

> band `CART-96` selects **$18.00** per cart · count **3** → **$54.00**

That is the PO's own earlier ruling — *"1 trash can $15 - if you have 3 you multiple by
3"* (OQ-317) — with the band choosing which per-cart figure is multiplied.

### Why solar, battery and thermal are the other way round

There the multiplier **REPLACES** the bands, as already ruled, because capacity is a
**continuous nameplate number with no natural size classes**: the PO's own figure is
*"if 1 unit cost $10 then for this unit charge will be $100"* — a 10 kW array at
**$10.00/kW = $100.00**. A band would only quantise a number that is already exact.

### What this does and does not change

* **Nothing ratified is superseded by THIS ruling.** The ten band rows already
  superseded by the capacity ruling (solar 4, thermal chilled 3, thermal steam 3) stay
  superseded; battery still seeds none.
* **The fourteen band rows for these three services are CONFIRMED, not merely
  unrepealed** — `trash` 7 (`CART-35` · `CART-64` · `CART-96` · `DUMP-2` · `DUMP-4` ·
  `DUMP-6` · `DUMP-8`), `storm_water` 4 (`SW-1ERU` · `SW-2-5` · `SW-6-20` · `SW-20P`),
  `broadband` 3 (`BB-100` · `BB-500` · `BB-1000`).
* **B4/B5 are untouched.** No frozen figure is contradicted: this rules which INPUT
  selects a price, not how the money is computed or rounded, so no HUMAN-GUIDE §6
  re-sign is required.
* **A test must assert the worked figure** so drift goes RED: `CART-96` × 3 = `$54.00`
  with the band-selected unit price, beside the existing capacity case
  10 kW × $10.00 = $100.00.

### Still NOT ruled — unchanged from §4 above

The **self-serve implementation price** ($0.00 versus a setup fee) is still open. It was
put back to the PO with a recommendation — *confirm $0.00 as the stamped default, and
make the implementation order editable so a sold engagement can carry a real fee and a
real month count* — and this message answered the bands question only. **A price is
money and a likely reading is not a ruling.**

## 2026-08-27 · THE TOOLBAR STANDARD IS RATIFIED — ten rules, all 27 lists (CR-045)

**PO verbatim:** *"Standard propose by you is good with me; Search — page by page -
most fo these are good; in account you will need phone numner of email ID also ; I
agree with all - The standard, if you confirm it; I want to write another CR - prepare
all tasks for all screens and excute in waves - also all tsks an dwaves update in HTML
document"*

Ratified against the published standard (artifact *SMARTBillHub Toolbar Standard*,
measured at v2.73.0). **A signature covers only what was shown** (PO 2026-08-11), so
what was shown is written out here: the ten rules, the 27-row page-by-page search
table, the filter/download table, and the live before/after of the search box.

### The ten rules, as ratified

1. One toolbar order, every list: search · filters · spacer · `↓` · `▥`.
2. One search width: wants 320px, grows, floor 240px, ceiling 512px.
3. Never name a field the server does not match.
4. Never match a field the prompt does not name.
5. Every list whose rows have an address names **address**.
6. Grammar: `Search <term>, <term> or <term>…`.
7. At most **five** named terms — see the amendment below.
8. Every list has filters, as chips in the toolbar.
9. Download is `↓`, icon-only, with its name in the tooltip.
10. Numbers first, then names, then address.

### ⚠ RULE 7 WAS PUBLISHED WRONG AND IS AMENDED IN THE SAME BREATH AS ITS RATIFICATION

It read **"at most four named terms"**. The same document marked Service requests —
*"Search request #, name, address, phone, or email…"*, **five** terms — as CORRECT,
because it is: every one of those five is matched by
`customers/service_request_reads.py:223-227`. A rule contradicted by a row its own page
calls correct is not a rule. **Amended to FIVE**, which is what the working screen
does. Recorded rather than quietly fixed, because the PO ratified the text that said
four.

### The PO's one addition, and the figure it needs

*"in account you will need phone numner of email ID also"*.

**Measured:** `customers.selectors.account_list` matches `account_no`, `customer_no`,
contact `full_name` and unit ids. It matches **neither phone nor email**.
`Contact.email` (CITextField) and `Contact.phone` (TextField) exist; both are PII.
Searching them is already ratified posture — service requests does it today.

**The worked case, and why the leg is not a plain `icontains`:** a clerk holding
`555-1234` against a contact stored as `(555) 123-4567` gets **no results** from a raw
match — a silent wrong answer, which is worse than an absent feature. **The phone leg
compares digits only, on both sides**, so `5551234` finds `(555) 123-4567`. Email needs
none of this: `citext` is already case-insensitive.

**Accounts now names seven things and rule 7 allows five.** Resolved without breaking
either rule: the prompt names the five a clerk reaches for —
**`Search account #, name, address, phone or email…`** — and a help affordance carries
*"Also finds a customer # or a meter #"*, so nothing is matched that is not stated.

### What this does NOT touch

No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure, no money rule, no rounding, no golden test, no migration and
no data write. **No HUMAN-GUIDE §6 re-sign is required.** B14 rules 4 and 19 are
*enforced* by this, not changed.

### One ratified test is reversed by this ruling

`07-frontend/src/features/metering/ReadsPage.test.tsx:409` asserts the Reads prompt does
**not** contain `"address"`. Correct when Reads searched only a meter number; reversed
by the PO's *"i want search by address as well"*. The assertion is **rewritten citing
this ruling and its date — never deleted**, so the reversal stays legible.

## 2026-08-27 — THE BILL'S TWO OMISSIONS ARE BUILT: `$81.60` ON A LANDLORD'S BILL, AND A SERVICE CAN NO LONGER LEAVE AN ACCOUNT'S BILL IN SILENCE (engineering, under PO rulings of the same day)

**WHAT THE PO ASKED FOR, verbatim:** *"B6's priced lines (DEF-990); the rest is
built or superseded — can you resolve this by building"*.

**Two defects, one missing capability, and neither was arithmetic.** The rating
engine has been able to price a base charge with no usage line since it was
written — `price_bill(base_only_services=…)` — and every figure it produces is
❄️ frozen and untouched. What was missing was the **routing** that reaches it,
and it was missing in exactly one place: *base-only* was a fact about an ACCOUNT
(`SubscriptionContext.base_only`, BR-CUS-055's vacation hold — every service at
once) and there was no way to say *this ONE service bills base only while the one
beside it prices usage*.

### DEF-990 — the landlord's bill was short and stopped rather than going out short

`BR-CUS-170` (PO 2026-08-27, closing OQ-531) widened a master's coverage from
*common areas* to *common areas AND any unit on that premises with no occupying
account*. The coverage READ shipped that day; the priced lines did not, and the
bill refused by name instead.

**❄️ THE FIGURE, on BR-MET-101's own building.** 1408 Elm: hallway lighting
**`$41.20`** + shared irrigation **`$28.40`** = **`$69.60`**, and with Unit C
empty, planned and taking electric its **`$12.00`** base joins them —
**`$81.60`**. The product now produces `$81.60`.

**The three obstacles DEF-990 named, and what each became:**

| named obstacle | what closed it |
|---|---|
| one bill cannot hold two base charges for one service | `TariffConfig.base_only` — a per-TARIFF fact. Nothing keys a bill's tariffs by service code |
| `measure_consumption._reading_for` matches by SERVICE CODE, so a second electric tariff picks up the first connection's read and bills its usage twice | the stage branches on the flag **before** the lookup. Not a filter on the result — the only form that cannot do it |
| `runs.readings_for_account` walks `covered_units`, so widening that tuple reads the empty unit's meter and charges USAGE the ruling did not ask for | it is deliberately **NOT** widened. Empty units arrive as base-only tariffs and their meters are never read — *"U6 to U10 BASE charges"* |

**WHERE THE EMPTY UNIT'S BASE COMES FROM, stated because it is a money choice
and not an obvious one:** the EMPTY UNIT'S OWN PLAN. `BR-CUS-014` (*the account
derives its plan from the unit*) and `BR-RAT-012/027` (*the base charge is
defined per service within a plan*) put it there, and it goes through the same
`_tariff_config_for` every other line on the bill uses — the version in force at
the SERVICE date (BR-RAT-007), the size ladder, the jurisdiction factor. What
stays the ANCHOR's is everything the BILL carries once rather than per service:
the taxes, the fees, the discounts and the plan snapshot, exactly as BR-CUS-068
already settles for the covered common areas.

**AND *NOT IN SERVICE* IS APPLIED HERE FOR THE FIRST TIME.** PO verbatim: *"C —
derive it: a service point with no asset and no account means not in service"*.
Every unit in this coverage satisfies the second half by construction, so the
test that remains is the first: a point with nothing standing on it bills
**nothing at all**, and a newly created premises therefore costs its owner
nothing until the installer arrives. ⚠ An **unreadable** assets seam is not the
same fact as an empty point, and answering *nothing* to both would quietly drop
a base charge off every owner's bill — so that case REFUSES by name
(`GATHER_UNBILLED_UNIT_UNREADABLE`).

### DEF-1060 — a service the account holds and the plan never priced

`billing.gather._tariffs_for_plan` iterated `rating.plan_rate_schedules(plan_id)`
and read the unit only to resolve the connection SIZE. The PO's ruling of the
same morning reverses that: **the services a bill charges are the services
attached to the UNIT; the plan supplies the PRICE and no longer supplies the
LIST.** The reconciliation is now in the code.

⚠ **IT IS PURELY ADDITIVE, AND THAT IS EDGE 2 RATHER THAN AN IMPLEMENTATION
CHOICE.** *"2 Plan has a schedule, unit has no service point … we have to bill
it"*. Read the mechanism ruling alone and a build would DROP a plan service the
unit has no point for — silently un-billing customers on every tenant whose
service points are incomplete, and moving ❄️ frozen figures. So the plan's
schedules are still priced in full and the unit can only ADD. **Golden verify
33/33; GT-17's five-service reference bill reproduces byte for byte.**

### THE ONE THING NOT BUILT, AND IT IS A QUESTION AND NOT A DEFERRAL — `OQ-670`

Edge 1: *"1 Unit has a service, plan has no schedule for it - this will never
happen, in such case bill base only"*. **It has happened, on the PO's own demo
tenant, and there is no base to bill.** `rating.sample_data` writes the trash
rate schedule AND the trash `plan_services` base row together, both behind
`_enabled('trash')` at seed time, while `metering.sample_data` seeds trash
service points regardless — so Ana Alvarez's plan states, for trash, **no
schedule, no base charge and no billed unit**. `$18.00` was retired by OQ-317
the same day; `$15.00` per cart lives on the schedule that does not exist; and
CLAUDE.md rule 3 forbids inventing the unit a cart count would be quoted in.

**CR-013 part 1 already rules the other way on this exact fact** — *"Blank base
= size not served"*, on which `_base_charge_for` refuses (DEF-277) — so edge 1
and a signed rule collide, and only on accounts like Ana's. **The bill refuses
by name with the service and `OQ-670` in the message** rather than choosing; the
alternative (print a trash line at `$0.00` and keep the run moving) tells 48
customers they owe nothing for trash, which is DEF-1060's own silence wearing a
line item. **Money either way: `$15.00` a cart, `$720.00` a month across Silver
Creek's 48 trash accounts, uncollected since the demo was seeded.**

### What is now RED that was not

Both guards were broken first and the failures quoted:

* neutering `if bills_base_only(tariff)` in stage 2 →
  `AssertionError: assert 2 == 1` — both electric tariffs measure the same
  **684 kWh** and the hallway's usage bills twice;
* neutering the `_refuse_unpriced_unit_services` call →
  `Failed: DID NOT RAISE GatherProblem`, twice — which is precisely the product
  that shipped Ana's **`$64.57`**.

**Review-ledger row written before review** (`12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md`),
stating in plain English with figures what would be shown to the PO: the
landlord's `$81.60`, the `684 kWh` that must not be billed twice, and — as a
QUESTION, not a ratification — Ana's trash. A signature on the first two does
not cover the third.

## 2026-08-27 — CR-044: THE THREE WORKFLOWS ARE DEFINED, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS BLOCKED ON THE PO

**The PO's sentence, verbatim, in full:**

> *"One time bill, budget bill, fix bill, can you define suer friendly process -
> workflows - that take carae of bill generation data, steps, data colelctions,
> impact of such action on finance, reading open balance etc - you also need to
> fien UI for it as per tailwind components - test it it works"*

The design is `04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/10-cr044-workflow-design.md`, and it
answers all five named things for each of the three tabs. **Three judgments were
made in writing it that the next agent could not re-derive from the code alone,
and each is recorded here with its worked figure.**

### 1 · "Reading open balances" is a READER, not a gather — one piece of work, four surfaces

`DEF-1081` says the bill run's step 2 *"cannot show what a customer already
owes, because nothing gathers it"*. **The gather exists.**
`payments_seam.prior_position_for_account` computes the position and FOOTS by
construction — `previous_balance − payments_credits == open_balance` — from
three operands owned by three modules, each asked for BY NAME under B1.

**What is actually missing is that it answers about an INVOICE.** Its totals
argument is built by `issue._prior_bill_totals(invoice)`, and it has exactly one
caller: `issue.py:1306`, inside the issuing transaction. All four surfaces that
need the figure have no invoice to ask about — step 2 is a pre-flight before any
draft is reviewed, the one-time preview prices nothing, budget eligibility is a
question about an account, and a correction's balance section is about the
customer.

So the work is `apps/billing/open_balance.py`: change the QUESTION, delegate the
ARITHMETIC unchanged. **Worked, and the second figure is the reason it is worth
building rather than reusing payments' own AR read:** an account with one unpaid
**45.00** bill answers **45.00 − 0.00 = 45.00** (❄️ WE-1's arrears half, byte
identical to what its bill prints); an account MIGRATED in owing **267.30** with
no invoice at all answers **267.30**, where `payments.outstandings` — which is
over invoices, for S34's collections list — answers nothing and would tell a
clerk about to bill that customer they are square.

**Why in billing:** the four callers are billing's, the seam that already asks
payments and customers is billing's, and billing owns the third operand outright.

### 2 · The Budget Bills blocker was measured as MISSING DATA and is a WIRING gap (DEF-1180)

The tab's own copy says *"No account records which plan it is on, so there is
nothing to work through."* The first clause is true — `accounts` has no plan
column, and BR-CUS-029 says the account plan snapshot has no table because *"the
account derives its plan from the unit"*. **The conclusion does not follow.**
The chain is `accounts.unit_id` → `units.rate_plan_id` → `rate_plans.budget_billing`,
and BOTH ENDS ARE ALREADY PUBLISHED: `metering/selectors.py:492` serves
`rate_plan_id` on the unit read, `rating/selectors.py:421` serves `budget_billing`
on the plan read, and `billing/gather.covered_units` walks account → units today.
What is missing is one seam function in `apps/billing/rating_seam.py` and one join.

**That changes the question put to the PO** from *what data do we add* to *is
derivation the rule* — `OQ-640` — which is smaller, and leaves a great deal that
is already buildable. **The cost of deriving, worked:** a customer enrolled at a
level of **$242.00** a month carrying a variance balance of **−40.27** becomes
ineligible the day somebody changes their unit's plan from another screen, with
no audit row against the account and nobody told.

### 3 · Cancelling a bill is proposed as its OWN act, not a fourth correction class (OQ-641)

A correction restates a bill that is wrong and always nets to a new PAIR of rows
— ❄️ WE-9: a credit note of **−$247.87** fully reversing the original's GL
stamps plus a rebill of **+$227.95**, leaving the customer **$19.92** in credit.
A void says the bill should never have existed: it is US-BIL-027, it has no
endpoint in this build, and its GL shape is a different question. **One confirm
dialog cannot front two different ledger consequences.** The proposal is to keep
it out and move the sentence from a paragraph above the form to a named,
disabled choice ON the reason list, so the answer reaches the clerk where the
question is asked. It is a scope call, so it is registered rather than taken.

### And what is genuinely blocked

**One thing, and it was already asked: `OQ-241`, when a one-time bill falls due.**
A cycle bill takes its due date from the cycle's payment terms and a one-time
bill belongs to no cycle. Worked: a move-out final bill for **$184.20** dated
**6 Aug 2026** falls due **27 Aug** on 21-day terms, **5 Sep** on 30, or **6 Aug**
if billed at period end — overdue the day it is printed. The tenant's late fee
between those readings is **$8.13** (❄️ GT-8). Steps 1–4 of the one-time wizard
are buildable; step 5, sending it, is not.
