## 2026-08-27 — THE CUSTOMERS HIGH-SEVERITY SWEEP: fourteen rows triaged, and the three judgements a lane had to make on its own

The PO asked for the open defect backlog to be worked — *"can you build and
resolve these bug - Open 127 — 32 high · 64 medium · 31 low"*. `customers`
carried **fourteen** of the thirty-two highs (the brief said thirteen; the
register says fourteen, and the extra one is `DEF-138`, filed against customers
by the balance lane in August 16 and never counted with the CR-030 cohort).

Seven are now **fixed** and one was **already fixed**. What is recorded here is
not the fixes — those are on their own rows — but the **three places the rules
ran out and this lane had to choose**, because the next agent needs to know a
person did not rule on them.

### 1 · AN UNREADABLE LEDGER BLOCKS A UNIT DEACTIVATION — except on a unit that never held an account

`DEF-138`'s prevention asked for *"a guard that cannot check must not pass"*, and
that is implemented. But taken literally it would refuse the deactivation of
**every unit in the product**, because the ledger seam is unwired on every tree
today — including a unit somebody created with a typo thirty seconds ago and
wants to remove.

**The line drawn, and it is a judgement:** a unit that has **never held an
account** answers `clear` even when the books cannot be asked, because nothing
can be owed on it. The fail-closed rule applies to units that COULD owe.

**Why it is safe:** the money can only be attached to an account, and the
question "has this unit ever had one" is answerable without the ledger. **Why it
is stated here rather than left in a docstring:** it is the difference between a
guard that protects money and a guard that stops a utility tidying up its own
data, and a later lane simplifying it to "unreadable always blocks" would ship
the second one believing it was being careful.

### 2 · WHICH STATUS `activate_account` MAY START FROM — named, not derived from a class

`DEF-721` asked for a precondition. The tempting implementation is *"refuse
unless the current status is non-billable"*, which is one line and reads as
principled. **It is wrong**, and would have re-opened the defect: BR-CUS-107's
`disconnected` is ALSO `non_billable`, and it is precisely the status that must
not activate.

So the check names `pending_activation` — BR-CUS-018's draft — and every excluded
status carries its reason in the code beside it. **The cost is stated honestly:**
a tenant that adds its own draft-alike status is refused until BR-CUS-055 is
extended. Widening the set is a ruling, not a lane's pick, and a behaviour-class
test would have widened it silently.

### 3 · THE CUTOVER EXEMPTION IS A NAMED ARGUMENT, PASSED FROM EXACTLY ONE PLACE

`DEF-736`'s row says in capitals: **DO NOT close this by refusing every legacy
code**, because the account import lawfully creates rows carrying `government`.
So `allow_legacy_type` is a keyword with a fail-closed default, threaded through
`_open_account`, and **a test asserts it appears at exactly one call site.**

**That test is the point, not the flag.** A second caller is how a refusal
quietly stops applying to a new door, and it would look like a one-word
convenience in a diff nobody reads twice. The check turns "somebody must
remember" into a merge failure — the same move `12-governance/13-change-process.md`
step 7 makes about versions.

### ⚠ AND ONE FINDING ABOUT THE PROCESS ITSELF — DEF-1280

While rebuilding its locale files from the remote tip before committing them
(hard-won law 11), this lane found that **ten of the eleven catalogues already
held its own uncommitted rows**, swept there by another lane's pathspec commit
over the shared working tree. `en.json` alone was not swept, so the branch
carried a state where **ten languages resolved a refusal that ENGLISH did not.**

Every check law 11 prescribes passes on that: the committing lane's file count
was right and its own change WAS present. Filed as `DEF-1280`, and the narrow
rule it argues for is the one that found it — **before committing a shared file,
rebuild its content from the REMOTE TIP plus your own hunks, rather than
committing the working-tree copy.** The working tree is every lane's; the tip is
nobody's.

### What is NOT fixed, and why — so nobody re-triages it from scratch

| Row | Why it stays open |
|---|---|
| **DEF-708** | The reconnection fee must become a REAL RECEIVABLE at the cut. Measured: AR is Σ posted journal lines, posting happens at ISSUE, `models.BILL_TYPES` has no fee type, `issue._gl_account_for` refuses every `fee` line unconditionally, and issue needs a BR-BIL-026 template pin. **That is a billing story, not a customers one**, and folding `case.reconnection_fee_amount` into `mark_reconnecting`'s comparison DEADLOCKS the product — paying takes AR to zero, the cached fee never clears, and no cut customer could ever be reconnected. |
| **DEF-724** | A close-out path that does not require occupancy. Real work, and it needs a decision this lane could not take: whether a cut account's terminal path is `move_out` with the occupancy check relaxed, or a NEW `close_out` door. The two differ in what they write (`closed_at`, service agreements, the BR-CUS-031 final-bill handoff) and the wrong choice writes a `closed_at` for a tenancy that ended at the cut. |
| **DEF-701** | Blocked on DEF-724 **and** on billing: `resolve_subscription.CLASSES_THAT_BILL` excludes `non_billable`, so assigning `Disconnected` drops the WHOLE account from the run and the usage consumed BEFORE the cut is never billed. Both blockers are code in other modules. |
| **DEF-744** | Needs a PO ruling before a line of code — minted as **OQ-680**. |
| **DEF-700** | The AMOUNT is ruled ($75.00, BR-CUS-104). The CODE VOCABULARY is not — minted as **OQ-681**. |
| **DEF-675** | Documentation: B18 §5.5.5 and §6.3 still call `account_discounts` NEW when `discount_enrolments` has held all six columns since 2026-08-19. Stamped, not rebuilt. |
| **DEF-705** | The ladder must restart at tier 1 after a payment plan ends (BR-CUS-098, PO 2026-08-25). `restart_after_closure` already implements exactly this restart for BR-CUS-082 and this path simply does not call it. |

## 2026-08-27 — AN ACTION ROW HOLDS ACTIONS: one rule, three frames, ~20 screens

**Lane:** Page-header, toolbar capacity and popover clipping · **DEF-966** (second
half) · **DEF-1083** · **DEF-1085** · **DEF-1150** · CR-045 wave A.

### The judgement, in one sentence

**A row of controls holds only things a person can press. Anything else — a status
pill, the reason a control is disabled, how long a draft has waited — is a FACT, and
a fact gets a declared line of its own.**

This was not in any signed rule. It is written here because three separate defects
reported on one day were the same defect wearing three costumes, and the next lane,
reading only the repo, would otherwise fix the third one the way the first two were
fixed — by moving the row instead of by emptying it.

### What each of the three looked like, and why nothing caught any of them

| Where | What was in the row | What the PO said |
|---|---|---|
| `PageHeader` (BIL-02) | a status pill · an "Past-due unknown" note · four buttons | *"buttons are still at wring places - do you ahve rules for button"* |
| `WizardFrame` (Run bills step 2) | `Save & exit` · a disabled `Park` · a two-sentence paragraph | *"UI is broken at Park"* |
| `DataTable` (Reads list) | search · All · + Filter · archive · 4 route chips · 4 status chips · Download CSV · ▦ | *"tool bar also not correct on this screen"* |

**In all three the row was over capacity, and in all three every individual control
was correct.** DEF-966's first fix that morning added `margin-left: auto`, which
right-aligns a wrapped row — it fixed WHERE the row lands and not WHY it wraps, and
the PO reported it again the same day looking at the same screen.

**No gate can see any of this and none ever will.** jsdom computes no layout; the
markup is byte-identical whether a row wraps or not; every assertion passes in both
states. Hard-won law 6 in its purest form — the Product Owner looking at a screen is
the only instrument that finds these.

### The worked figure the argument rests on

The reads toolbar carries **~1,360px of controls**: a 220px search box, an `All` pill
and `+ Filter` (~140px), an archive checkbox (~150px), two four-cell chip groups
(~300px each), `Download CSV` (~130px) and the ▦ (32px), plus five 12px gaps. A
1,440px laptop, less the shell's sidebar, leaves **~1,150px**. So it wrapped after
the status chips — and the wrap is what put the ▦ near the LEFT margin, where its
336px panel, hung from `right-0`, ran off the screen. **The PO's screenshot shows the
panel's own heading reading "OW / HIDE".** One cause, two symptoms.

### What was decided, and what was rejected

1. **`PageHeader`: the status leaves the action row and joins the identity.**
   r10 is the authority and is unanimous — in every `page-head` block in
   `SMARTBillHub.dc.html`, `.page-actions` holds buttons and nothing else, and a
   record's state lives in the kicker or the sub-line. B14 rule 2's own skeleton
   says it by omission: *kicker, title, optional subtitle, right-aligned actions*
   names no status slot. It is the shared header, so **~20 detail screens are
   corrected with zero call-site edits**.

2. **`WizardFrame`: a disabled control's reason gets a declared `exitNote` line**
   beneath the button row, with `aria-describedby` tying it to the control so the
   split costs no screen reader. The park AGE moves with it — it is prose too.
   ⚠ **The sentence itself is RIGHT and was NOT deleted**: it is DEF-1043's
   honest-absence answer and BR-SHL-025's requirement. Only its placement was wrong.

3. **`DataTable`: row one is B14 rule 12's grammar plus the IS-9 export, and nothing
   else; a screen's dimension controls get a DESIGNED second row** (`dimensionsSlot`).
   Rule 12's set is BOUNDED — it does not grow when a screen gains a dimension — so
   row one fits at every width the product supports.

   **REJECTED: folding the chip groups back into `+ Filter`.** DEF-896 added them
   precisely because *"the two dimensions a clerk actually works by were two clicks
   deep inside + Filter"*, and r10 RDS-01 draws both segments on the toolbar.
   Reverting them re-opens DEF-896.

4. **The popover flips rather than clips**, as arithmetic (`resolvePanelAnchor`)
   rather than as a class name — checked exhaustively in both directions, including
   the mirrored case, because a fix that only ever flips right→left moves the clip
   instead of removing it.

### The part that is a process finding, not a UI one

**Three lanes each put a `SegmentedFilter` into `downloadSlot` — Premises, then
Units, then Reads — and all three wrote the SAME sentence to explain it:** *"it rides
in `downloadSlot` because that is the only slot the shared toolbar renders AFTER its
spacer, i.e. the only one that is right-aligned."* Nobody decided the toolbar's
contents; each lane found the same missing slot and stepped around it, and the row
grew one control at a time until it broke.

That is now **G43 clause (c)**, baseline zero, proved RED against the tree as the PO
photographed it — it named all three offenders, which is the point.

### What is NOT decided here, and is routed to the PO

**Whether B14 gains a rule about how much a toolbar or a page header may CARRY.**
B14's rules come from PO rulings (rule 21's own row records the one that made it) and
minting rule 32 by lane fiat is the *"quiet exception"* B14's closing section forbids.
Raised as **OQ-631**, with the 1,360-vs-1,150 figure above as its worked example, and
recorded in B14's *"Proposed, awaiting a PO ruling"* section beside OQ-540 and OQ-541.

Also routed: **OQ-630** — should a gate check the MIRROR of G31, every class a
stylesheet declares that no component renders? DEF-1150 is what that mirror would
have caught: `.table-search input` carried `min-width: 220px` and the whole field kit,
nothing had rendered `.table-search` since the Route B migration, and the search box
on all 27 lists was an unstyled ~170px browser default for as long as the corpse sat
in the file, with every gate green.

## 2026-08-27 — DEF-1082 AND DEF-1084 ARE **NOT** BUILT BY THIS LANE, AND WHY

**Lane:** Page-header, toolbar capacity and popover clipping · CR-045 wave A.

Both were handed to this lane mid-flight. Both are left **`open`** in the register
rather than fixed, and this is the measurement behind that, so the lane that picks
them up does not re-derive it.

### DEF-1082 — step 2's tabs promise DETAILS and show only EXCEPTIONS

**The fix is right and it is entirely CATALOGUE COPY plus one served figure**, and
the catalogues are the one thing CR-045 forbids this wave to touch.

* The two strings are `billing.run.step2.hint` (*"Click any section to see the
  details and make corrections before billing"*) and
  `billing.run.found.nothingHere` (*"Nothing on this tab needs your attention."*),
  rendered at `BillRunWizard.tsx:1255` and `:1465`. Changing either means editing
  **eleven** `i18n/locales/*.json` files.
* **CR-045 step 6 states the rule this obeys:** *"a wave's locale keys are written by
  that wave's own lane, in ONE commit, at the END of the wave — never incrementally,
  never by two lanes at once."* Waves B, C, D and E are all queued on those eleven
  files. Four lanes in eleven shared JSON files is DEF-165's mechanism, and it fired
  twice today — **DEF-1320**, filed by a sibling lane, is *"my own DEF-522 commit
  published another lane's uncommitted en.json rows — G15 red"*.

**And the served figure the recommended sentence needs DOES NOT EXIST TODAY.**
The suggested empty state — *"47 accounts on 3 rate schedules, all resolved"* — is
half free and half a backend change. `PreparedRun` (`apps/billing/runs.py:168`)
carries `ready`, `blocked`, `decisions`, `coverage` and an `account_count` property,
**so the 47 is already there**. It carries **no rate-schedule identity at all** —
there is no `schedule_id` on the dataclass — so *"on 3 rate schedules"* needs
`prepare_run` to gather and return the distinct schedules it resolved. That is a
`runs.py` change plus a serializer field, not a copy change.

**Recommendation, unchanged from the defect row and now costed:** take the
exception-list reading, and say what was checked and found clean. The account count
is free; the schedule count is one backend field. Do both in one commit, server leg
first, exactly as CR-045 R3 orders wave C.

### DEF-1084 — the slow step narrates nothing

**Beyond a UI change, and the defect row already says so.** Confirmed here:
`prepare_run` is a single synchronous call returning one final `PreparedRun`. There
is no progress channel, no partial payload and no job id — so there is nothing a
frontend could subscribe to, and a spinner that *claimed* to be pulling customers
would be a comment claiming a guarantee (hard-won law 1) with no guarantee behind it.

**The defect row's own second half is the more valuable half and this lane endorses
it:** the same question applies to the commit at step 6, which is a longer job over
the same accounts. **Decide it once, for both, in a lane that owns the server.**
Narrating step 2 alone would build a progress mechanism for the faster of the two.

### What this lane DID do for them

Nothing in the code. This entry, and the register rows left honestly `open` — because
a row marked fixed is the one thing that guarantees nobody looks again.

## 2026-08-27 · The metering high-severity lane — four judgments where the rules ran out

Recorded under hard-won law 9/10: each of these is a place a lane had to choose and
the repo did not say. The worked figure is with each one, so the next agent reaches
the same answer from the repo alone.

### 1 · `DEF-545` — the engine's `BR-MET-098` refusal is deliberately NARROWER than the API's

BR-MET-098 says *"THE APPROVER IS THE SAME PAIR OF ROLES AS THE RATE-CHANGE SECOND
APPROVAL (BR-RAT-091's 10 percent bar): Owner or Admin"*. `apps/metering/api.py`
refuses `approved` from a non-admin **always**, including on a clean run. The new
engine check in `import_runs._load_locked` fires **only when the approval bar is
actually crossed**.

**Why, and it is not laziness.** When no approval is required there is no approver:
the flag grants nothing and refusing it would be a refusal the rule does not contain.
BR-MET-098 names an approver *for a load that needs approving*. **Worked:** a 246-row
premises file with 1 reject — r10's own case, 0.41% and 1 row, under both bars — is
loaded by a Billing Clerk who has ticked `approved` for no reason. It loads 245 rows,
exactly as it did before. A 10-row file with 2 rejects (20%, over the percent bar)
approved by the same clerk is refused by name, and nothing is written.

The strict edge stays strict on purpose — at the boundary a flag a caller may not set
is worth refusing on sight. **Do not "align" the two by loosening `api.py`.**
Both comments say so at both sites.

### 2 · `DEF-1077` — the sample template's header stays the FIELD NAME, and the label change is measured rather than deferred

The PO's complaint is literal: *"in CSV file that we download there is not unit ID or
unit name that we can provide"*. The obvious fix — write `entry["label"]` as the
header row — was written, run and reverted.

**Measured: 11 failed, 12 passed.** Nine of the eleven are
`tests/test_cr025_sample_csv.py` reading the sample back with
`dict(zip(header, example))`, so the field name **is** the contract those tests state
and rewriting them is the work, not a side effect of it.

**And it surfaced a collision that has to be fixed first:** `PREMISES_ALIASES` maps
the header *Owner* to the FREE-TEXT `owner_manager`, so under label headers
*"Owner / manager"* went unmapped while *"Owner"* took its slot. That is `DEF-1088`'s
territory — the typed owner — and landing the label header over it would silently
point a utility's owner column at the wrong destination.

**What shipped instead, and it answers the PO's actual question:** the three shapes
`resolve_unit_ref` accepts are now a `help` sentence on the column, rendered at stage
2 by the same `Note` `DEF-771` built for the `Plan` column. Plus the half that is pure
widening: `_auto_map` **derives** every column's label as an alias — derived, not
hand-copied into `ALIASES_BY_TARGET`, because a hand-kept copy rots on the first copy
change, which is `DEF-616`'s exact mechanism.

### 3 · `DEF-871` — the recompute trigger was written and WITHDRAWN, and `OQ-690` is why

`monthly_usage_service.recompute_account`'s only non-test caller is `sample_data`, so
on every real tenant the S21 Usage tab serves an empty series. The one-line fix in
`commit_read_batch` reaches `monthly_usage.summarise`, which raises `MixedUnitMonth`
(a `NotImplementedError` carrying **`OQ-358`**) for a month whose reads for one
account and one service disagree about the unit.

**Calling it from the commit would make an unanswered question about a CHART break a
lawful READ COMMIT.** **Worked:** a 1,247-row cycle where ONE account's July holds a
`kgal` and a `kWh` reading on one service — either all 1,247 readings are refused,
which BR-MET-129 forbids in as many words (*"we cannot reject the reading"*), or that
one July is silently stale. Both are defensible; neither is signed. `OQ-690` puts it
to the PO with both options and a third (answer `OQ-358` first). The trigger site and
its one-call-per-account shape are stamped in `commit_read_batch`.

### 4 · `DEF-1075` — why skipping the catalogue seed is SAFE, and it rests on `BR-TEN-036`

`ensure_reference_catalogs()` is memoised per execution context per tenant, turning
**1,920 round trips into 32** for a twenty-row import — the gunicorn worker timeout the
PO watched. A memo is only safe if the state it caches cannot change underneath it, and
here it cannot: **BR-TEN-036 makes `is_system` rows deactivatable and never deletable**,
so a catalogue present at the start of a context cannot stop existing during it. That
is the whole argument, and it is a RULE rather than an assumption. `force=True` exists
for the seeders and for the two tests that assert idempotency by calling it twice —
which keep passing unchanged because the memo returns **zeros**, not the first call's
counts.

**PO verbatim:** *"1 Ana's trash — what does a service cost when the plan prices it

- 4 decimal places; 4 Is a downloaded CSV read by a person or calculated by a

Each was put in plain English with a concrete figure, as a table of options with a

**What was shown, verbatim from the table:** that (b) is *"a trash line at zero on the

## 2026-08-27 — OQ-670 BUILT: THE REFUSAL BECAME A `$0.00` LINE, AND THE SUPERSESSION STAYED NARROW (engineering, under the PO ruling of the same day)

**The ruling this implements is recorded above** — *"FIVE RULINGS IN ONE REPLY"*,
item 1. **PO verbatim:** *"Ana's trash — what does a service cost when the plan
prices it nowhere? 🔒 - (b) Bill $0.00"*.

⚠ **IT OVERRULES THIS LANE AND THE CODE SAYS SO.** Hours earlier the same lane
shipped **(a) refuse by name** and put the collision back as `OQ-670` rather than
picking a figure. The PO chose (b) with the trade stated — that a zero line is
*"the same silence you caught, wearing a line item"* — and with **`$720.00` a
month** across Silver Creek's 48 trash accounts in front of them. Both the
constant and the function carry that history in their own docstrings, so no later
reader mistakes the zero for something a lane decided.

### What changed

`gather._refuse_unpriced_unit_services` → **`gather._unpriced_unit_service_lines`**.
It returns lines instead of raising, and `gather_account` carries them.

**❄️ THE WORKED CASE.** Ana Alvarez `AC-2026-00001`, June bill `BL-2607-000001`:
**SIX** lines at **`$64.57`** with no trash → **SEVEN** lines at **`$64.57`**, the
seventh being trash at **`$0.00`**. The document changes; the money does not.

**THE `$720.00` IS NOT WRITTEN OFF, AND THAT IS THE REASONING THE PO CHOSE.** The
moment a clerk adds trash to the plan (S9 base, S11 rate) it prices normally and
every later bill collects it. What the zero buys is **visibility**: the gap sits
on the document where a customer and a clerk both read it, instead of being
invisible in a silence. A refusal would have made it visible too — and stopped 48
bills to do it.

### A `RatedLine`, not a `TariffConfig`, and the reason is CLAUDE.md rule 3

A synthetic tariff would have to state a pricing MODEL, a `unit_price` and a
`billed_unit` before the engine would touch it — `normalize` refuses a quantity
with no unit and the flat plugin refuses a `None` price — and **all three would be
invented**, because a plan that prices the service nowhere states none of them. So
the zero rides the seam's fee channel, which `normalize.fee_candidates` already
documents as carrying already-priced usage/base lines on a multi-pass bill, and it
leaves `quantity`, `unit` and `unit_price` at `None`. That is the truth: nobody
measured anything and nobody quoted a rate.

`taxable=True` because a base line IS in the tax base (B4.2) and the
classification must not lie; at `0.0000` it moves no tax base by any arithmetic —
asserted, because that is what makes the line safe to ship on 48 live accounts.

### ⚠ THE SUPERSESSION IS NARROW, AND THERE IS A TEST WHOSE ONLY JOB IS TO FENCE IT

CR-013 part 1 (PO 2026-08-19) — *"Blank base = size not served"*, on which
`gather._base_charge_for` refuses by name (DEF-277) — **still stands everywhere it
already applied.** It is superseded ONLY for a service the UNIT derives that the
plan prices **nowhere at all**: no rate schedule and therefore no base row.

The narrowness is structural rather than a matter of care: the zero path never
reaches `_base_charge_for`, because there is no schedule there to read a base
from. **`tc1e` asserts the refusal separately** — if it ever goes green on a
`$0.00` line, the zero has leaked out of its case and every unpriced size in the
product has silently become free.

**The same case one unit along.** A master's empty unit (BR-CUS-170) whose own
plan prices a service it takes nowhere takes the same zero line, for the same
ruled reason. That reading is written into the branch rather than smuggled:
refusing there would contradict the half of the ruling that says the run never
stops.

### The guard, red-proved with the exact carelessness the ruling warns about

A `$0.00` line is one `if amount:` away from being the original silence again. So
the bill is priced **twice** — with the zero line and without it — and compared on
both facts the ruling makes: one more line, and the same money. Injecting a
truthiness filter into the line builder fails three tests:

    assert len(trash) == 1        →  assert 0 == 1
    assert len(with_zero.lines) == 7  →  assert 6 == 7
    assert sorted(...) == ["gas", "trash"]  →  assert [] == ['gas', 'trash']

An assertion on the TOTAL alone passes either way — `$64.57` is the answer with
the line and without it — which is exactly why the omission survived to
production, and why the count and the amount are asserted apart from it.

### One consequence, stated rather than discovered

The zero line NAMES a service, so BR-BIL-010 resolves its revenue account from
that service at issue. A tenant that has never mapped trash to a revenue account
will have the bill refused there by name (US-BIL-007 TC-5, the ratified
behaviour). Not new machinery and not a silent failure — but it is a second place
this ruling can be felt, and it belongs in writing.

### What this does NOT fix

**DEF-1250 stays OPEN and is a different defect.** `rating.sample_data` gates the
trash schedule AND its `plan_services` base row behind `_enabled('trash')` at seed
time while metering seeds the service points regardless, and BR-TEN-063's
idempotent seed means enabling trash afterwards adds nothing, ever. **This ruling
makes the symptom visible; it does not repair the cause**, and the cause is what
puts an account on a plan that cannot price a service it holds.

**No ❄️ FROZEN figure moved and none could** — B4/B5 say nothing about a service
with no tariff. **golden-verify: 33 PASS, 0 FAIL.** **DEF-1060 → fixed.**

### Ruling 3 (a tariff RATE displays four decimals) does not touch this lane

Checked rather than assumed: `gather` renders no money and no rate at all — it
projects stored figures onto the seam — and the zero line carries `unit_price=None`
because no rate exists to show. `apps/billing/documents.py` already implements the
4dp rate rule (`0.142000` → `$0.1420`, `8.290000` → `$8.2900`, trailing zeros
KEPT).

## 2026-08-27 · DEF-161 and DEF-708 BUILT — the two billing rulings, and one judgment where two signed rules named different signals

The billing-rulings lane. **Nothing here chooses a rule.** Both defects were
settled by the PO earlier the same day and this records what was built, the two
figures it was built to, and the ONE place the lane had to judge between two
CONFIRMED rules that agree on the outcome and disagree on the mechanism.

Shipped as **`2.76.0`** (change process step 7). Golden-verify **33 PASS / 0
FAIL**, unchanged — neither change touches pricing arithmetic.

---

### 1 · DEF-161 — a service with no meter BY DESIGN bills from its base charge

**The ruling, PO 2026-08-27:** *"Teach it that a service with no meter by design
is normal — bill it from its base charge or percentage and never ask for a
read."*

**What was built.** `metering.billing_reads_for_unit` now answers **two
different reasons** where it answered one, and billing exempts exactly one of
them:

| service point | the service's declaration | reason | what the bill does |
|---|---|---|---|
| no asset | **declared unmetered** | `service_not_metered` | bills its **base charge** |
| no asset | not declared (the default) | `no_meter` | **refuses** — unchanged |
| has an asset, no read | — | `no_read` | **refuses** — unchanged |

**Worked, and it is the figure in the review-ledger row:** a water-and-trash
account went from REFUSED to **$32.00 water + $18.00 trash = $50.00**.

**THE SIGNAL IS `tenant_services.metered` (BR-RAT-081), AND THIS CLOSES DEF-495
IN THE SAME COMMIT.** That column has existed since 2026-08-20 with **no reader
anywhere in the product** — `grep` found the migration, the model and two
comments and not one query. A declaration nothing reads cannot reach a bill,
which is exactly what DEF-161 was. `tenancy.selectors.unmetered_service_codes()`
is the first reader it has ever had.

**⚠ THE JUDGMENT, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE IN THIS ENTRY.** Two CONFIRMED rules
name two different signals for the same outcome:

* **BR-RAT-081** (PO 2026-08-20) — *"yes we have to say service is meter or
  unmetered"* — a per-service **DECLARATION**, and its own rule text names
  DEF-161 as the defect it fixes.
* **BR-MET-134** (PO 2026-08-26, closing OQ-246) — *"The service's **pricing
  model** decides: unmetered-by-design services expect no read; a
  consumption-priced service with no meter is a human's exception"*, and its
  list of unmetered-by-design models includes **`flat`**.

They agree on the outcome. **The lane built the DECLARATION and NOT the pricing
model, and did not put it back to the PO** (law 13 — a re-ask manufactures
inconsistency). The reason is that DEF-161's own ruling, given the NEXT DAY,
settles it: *"A meter that exists and was not read keeps refusing exactly as it
does now — that distinction is the deliverable and a fix that blurs it has
traded one silent wrong bill for another."*

**`flat` is a CONSUMPTION-PRICED model** — `unit_price × quantity` — and it is
the model a small utility's **water** tariff most often uses. Treating every
`flat` tariff on a meterless service point as unmetered-by-design would bill a
water meter nobody could reach as base-only, on a document that foots, with no
work on any exception screen. That is the exact failure the later ruling
forbids, so BR-MET-134's `flat` clause is read as naming the OUTCOME (trash
expects no read) and not the TEST, and BR-RAT-081's declaration is the test.
The seeded trash tariff is `flat` at `$0.0000` with the `$18.00` as a base
charge, so both rules reach the same answer on the case they were both written
about.

**BR-MET-134 is not amended and nothing is superseded** — this is a reading, and
it is recorded here rather than left in a lane's head. If the PO wants the
pricing model to be the test, that is a change and it is theirs to make.

**Why it is safe under ❄️ frozen B4/B5:** `metered` defaults to **True**, so a
tenant that has never touched it has an EMPTY unmetered set and every bill in
the product prices byte-identically. `tc6` asserts exactly that.

---

### 2 · DEF-708 — the $75.00 reconnection fee becomes a real charge

**The ruling, PO 2026-08-27:** *"Make the fee a real charge — It becomes a line
that can be billed and paid, so the gate has something to check."*

**Why it was a BILLING story and a one-line customers fix would have been a
disaster.** `BILL_TYPES` had no fee type, and `apps.billing.services` published
no ad-hoc charge service — `apps/customers/disconnects.py` had recorded that
absence in as many words since 2026-08-25. So `customers` could QUOTE the fee
and never CHARGE it.

**What was built.**

* **`fee` joins `BILL_TYPES`** — an invoice whose entire content is charge-code
  lines. No plan, no tariff, no usage, no proration, no tax pass.
* **`apps/billing/fee_bill.py`** resolves the tenant's OWN charge code
  (BR-BIL-007 — never a literal), drafts the bill through the ONE writer of
  invoice lines (`stages.assemble_document`) and issues it, so BR-BIL-010 stamps
  the code's own GL account and the ledger posts it (rule 5).
* **`commit_cut` raises and issues it inside the cut's own transaction.** A cut
  whose fee cannot be charged does not happen at all — the alternative is
  DEF-708 restored, with the customer told they owe $75.00 and nobody billing it.
* **`mark_reconnecting` IS UNCHANGED, and that is the proof the shape is right.**
  It has always read AR; what was missing was the fee being in AR.

**Worked, and it is BR-CUS-104's own pair:** `A-11340` owes **$8,240.00** in
arrears, the fee is **$75.00**, and **$8,315.00** is now what clears the gate.

**⚠ THE REJECTED FIX IS NOW PINNED BY A TEST (`tc4`), not by a comment.**
Folding `case.reconnection_fee_amount` into the gate's comparison passes the
refusal test and then **refuses every cut customer forever**, because the cached
figure never clears when money posts. `tc4` pays the fee and requires the
customer back in.

**THREE THINGS THE LANE DECIDED AND DID NOT ASK ABOUT** (law 13 — a judgment
recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable):

1. **`due_days = 0`, derived from BR-CUS-104 and supplied by the CALLER.** The
   rule is that the fee is owed *at the cut*; a cycle-less bill takes its terms
   from the caller (CR-029 D8③) because there is no cycle to take them from; `0`
   is a TYPED value meaning *due on the bill date* (BR-MET-009's
   `due_days >= 0`). Billing chooses nothing — `raise_charge_fee` **requires**
   the argument. A late fee on the reconnection fee is a clerk's decision on
   S31.3 and is never automatic, so nothing accrues by itself.
2. **A charge code with no GL account REFUSES THE CUT, by name, naming S13.**
   This is a real behaviour change: a tenant whose `CC-RECON` is unmapped cannot
   cut until they map it. It is the same posture the cut already takes when no
   reconnection code exists at all — *"a cut nobody can price is a cut the
   customer cannot undo"* — extended to *a cut whose fee nobody can book is a
   cut the utility never collects*. `test_w7_cut_reconnect._reconnect_charge`
   was re-pointed in this same change (DEF-705's lesson).
3. **A fee bill is NOT taxable, and the column that could say otherwise is NOT
   read.** Every fee line this product writes is `taxable=False` and B4.2's tax
   base is usage/base/minimum-adjustment, so `taxable=False` is what every
   signed document already says. But `charges.taxable_default` exists and a fee
   bill is a new shape B4.2 was not written about — **`OQ-812`** asks, with the
   figure ($75.00 at Katy's 8.25% is **$6.19**), and nothing is blocked because
   a reconnection fee is not taxable on any reading.

## 2026-08-27 · CR-040 IS THREE MONTHS · CR-041 IS CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED BY CR-045

**PO verbatim:** *"What does “a financial history” mean for the demo utility? this si
corerct - Three months — enough to make “last bill” and “balance forward” mean something,
and little else; Close CR-041, or keep its remaining five tasks? CLose CR 41 and excute
Cr 45"*

### 1 · CR-040 — the seeded utility gets THREE months ⚠ OVERRULE

**Ruled: three months.** The recommendation was **twelve months with everything** — a
late payer, a payment plan mid-flight, a disconnection, a refund — on the reasoning that
*"the cost is in writing the generator, not in how many months it runs"*. The PO chose
the smallest of the three options with that argument in front of them.

**What three months buys, stated so the scope cannot drift upward later:** enough history
that **“last bill”** and **“balance forward”** are real figures on a customer's page
rather than nulls. **And little else — the PO's own words.** So the generator seeds
bills and their payments across three cycles and stops there.

⚠ **WHAT THIS RULING DOES *NOT* COMMISSION, and a lane may not add it because it would
make a nicer demo:** no collections ladder, no payment plan mid-flight, no disconnection
and reconnection, no refund, no credit note. Each of those is a *scenario*, not a month,
and the PO declined the option that contained them. **A lane that seeds a late payer
"because the ageing report looks empty otherwise" has widened a scope the PO narrowed.**
If the ageing report turns out to need it, that is a NEW question with its own figure,
not an inference from this one.

**The consequence, recorded rather than discovered:** the ageing bands, the collections
screens and the payment-plan surfaces will still demo empty. That is the accepted cost
of this ruling and it should surprise nobody later.

### 2 · CR-041 — CLOSED as SUPERSEDED by CR-045 ✅ as recommended

**PO verbatim: *"CLose CR 41 and excute Cr 45"*.**

CR-041 (*"the list toolbar behaves the same way on every screen"*) and CR-045 (*"the
toolbar standard — one search, one filter set, one download glyph, on all 27 lists"*)

**CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED, NOT DELETED**, and the distinction is the point: the trail from
the PO's original complaint to the work that answers it has to stay readable, or the next
agent finds a CR that stops mid-sentence and cannot tell whether it was abandoned or
finished. **Each of the five remaining tasks is mapped to the CR-045 wave that now
carries it** in CR-041's own closing note.

**"Execute CR-045" is the other half of the instruction and is now live:** wave A landed
today; **B, C, D and E are unblocked and dispatched**; F closes. The one thing still
waiting on the PO inside CR-045 is `DEF-1152` — whether the CSV download shows the `↓`
CHARACTER (which honours the 2026-08-20 *"not for buttons"* ruling and needs no

## 2026-08-27 · DEF-632 — CAPTURE THE SSN AND ENCRYPT IT · and a standing PO instruction about rulings

**PO verbatim (1):** *"We tell customers their Social Security number is stored encrypted
- Verify and keep the promise — Confirm SSN is genuinely encrypted at rest and only the
last four are shown, then the sentence stays. We need to capture SSN and encript it; we
have to ensure it is working"*

**PO verbatim (2), a standing instruction on process:** *"all these ruling please mark in
repo and dont ask again and again"*

### 1 · THE MEASURED STARTING POINT — the product does NOT store an SSN today

Before this ruling, `apps/customers/service_request_service.py` **REFUSES** every
identifier field by name — `ssn`, `social_security_number`, `gov_id`, `national_id`,
`ein`, `tin`, `ssn_last4`, `date_of_birth` and five more — raising
`customers.serviceRequest.identifierNotStorable` and citing DEF-632. Its own comment says
why: *"a silently dropped SSN is a screen that says 'stored encrypted' over a field that
went nowhere, which is DEF-632 wearing a different hat."*

**That was the right interim state and it is now superseded.** Refusing was safer than
storing plaintext under a promise of encryption; the PO has now ruled that the capability
is BUILT rather than removed.

### 2 · WHAT IS RULED

**Capture the SSN, encrypt it at rest, show staff the last four only** — and *"ensure it
is working"*, which is the operative half: the promise on screen becomes true, verified,
rather than restored on trust.

The screen already draws it (`ServiceRequestCapturePage`, B19 §2 `Social Security
Number *`, and §7's masked `••• ••• • 4471`). The mechanism already exists:
`06-backend/core/crypto.py` implements **AES-GCM, a 96-bit nonce per encryption,
authenticated with additional data binding the ciphertext to its row** — signed law from
`OQ-016`, and `SBH_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` is already REQUIRED at boot (production refuses
to start without it). So neither half is being invented; they are being connected.

**BR-CUS-092 is the rule this implements.** No new rule is minted.

### 3 · WHAT "ENSURE IT IS WORKING" MUST MEAN, so it is not satisfied by a passing test

The PO's phrase is the requirement, and hard-won law 1 says a comment claiming a
guarantee is not the guarantee. So:

* the stored column is **read back raw from the database** in a test and asserted **not to
  contain the digits** that were submitted — an assertion on the model's accessor proves
  only that the accessor decrypts;
* **only the last four ever leave the server** — the serializer is asserted to carry no
  full value, on the list, the detail and the export;
* the **audit trail never logs the number**, and neither does a refusal message;
* and the **wrong key fails closed** — a row encrypted under one key must not silently
  return empty under another.

### 4 · ⚠ AND THE CARVE-OUT THAT MUST SURVIVE THIS

`crypto.py`'s own docstring warns that *"an oracle that will encrypt anything a stranger
types is a chosen-plaintext oracle"*. The service-request form is **public-facing**. So
the encryption path may not be reachable as a general-purpose encrypt endpoint; it
encrypts this field on this write and nothing else. A lane that generalises it has built
the oracle the file warns about.

### 5 · THE STANDING INSTRUCTION — *"dont ask again and again"*

Recorded as a PO instruction on process, and it is consistent with CLAUDE.md law 9/10
rather than in tension with it: **a ruling goes into the repo the moment it is made, and
it is not put back to the PO a second time.** What legitimately returns to them is
narrower than it has been:

* a ruling that **collides with a signed rule** (the supersession must be stated, not
  assumed);
* a **frozen B4/B5 figure**, which cannot be changed without a re-sign — that is a
  constraint on us, not a question we chose to ask;
* a fact **only they hold** (a tax authority's requirement, a price).

**Everything else is ours to decide and write down.** Asking a second time costs the PO
the thing they are shortest of, and this log is where an answer is supposed to be found
instead.

## 2026-08-27 · DEF-161 — A SERVICE WITH NO METER BY DESIGN BILLS FROM ITS BASE CHARGE · and law 13's first violation, recorded

**PO verbatim:** *"DEF-161 — the bill refuses because trash has no meter - this is correct
- (a) Teach it that a service with no meter by design is normal — bill it from its base
charge or percentage and never ask for a read. - how many times youa re going to ask
this; it is already settled"*

### ⚠ THE PO IS RIGHT AND THIS SHOULD NEVER HAVE BEEN ASKED — LAW 13's FIRST VIOLATION

It was **already settled on the morning of the same day**, by the PO's own derivation
ruling, recorded in this log:

> `account → unit → service_points (WHICH services) → assets (HOW they bill: usage ·
> quantity · base only) → a service point with no asset AND no account means NOT IN
> SERVICE`

**“base only” is in that chain.** A service whose unit carries no measuring asset bills
from its base charge — that IS the answer to DEF-161, given hours before DEF-161 was put
back as a question. The merge lane wrote that ruling down itself and then asked anyway.

**CLAUDE.md law 13 was added an hour before this exchange and this is the first thing it
should have caught.** The check it prescribes — grep the decision log for the subject
before asking — would have taken one command and found the ruling in the file the asker
had authored. Recorded here as the worked example of the law rather than as an apology,
because law 13's whole claim is that a re-ask is a bug with a mechanism, and this is the
mechanism: **the answer was in the repo and nobody looked.**

### THE RULING, for the lane that implements it

A service that is **not measured BY DESIGN** must be distinguishable from a meter that
**should have been read and was not**. Today they are the same thing to the engine, which
is the whole defect.

**Measured mechanism:** `metering.billing_reads_for_unit` returns `absent_reason=no_meter`
for a service point with no asset, and `apps/billing/stages/measure_consumption.py` treats
**every** absent consumption identically — only `ABSENT_BASE_ONLY` (a base-only ACCOUNT,
BR-CUS-055's vacation hold) is exempt. `runs.calculate_account` then refuses the **whole
account**, and the only decision that releases it is `bill_without_service`, which
**DELETES the service from the bill** — so the `$18.00` trash charge and the sewer
percentage can never reach a customer.

**What to build:** `no_meter` on a service point that is not *supposed* to have one is a
**normal outcome**, not an absence. Such a service bills from its base charge (or, for
sewer, its percentage of water) and **is never asked for a read**. A meter that exists and
was not read keeps refusing exactly as it does now — that distinction is the deliverable
and a fix that blurs it has traded one silent wrong bill for another.

⚠ **THIS IS THE SAME RULE `DEF-1060` LEARNED THIS MORNING, ONE STAGE EARLIER.** DEF-1060
taught `gather` that the UNIT decides which services bill; DEF-161 teaches
`measure_consumption` that the unit's ASSETS decide whether a read is owed at all. One
ruling, two stages. A lane implementing this should read the DEF-1060 work first — the
seam and the vocabulary already exist.

**No ❄️ FROZEN figure moves.** B4/B5 say nothing about a service with no meter;
golden-verify must stay 33/33.

## 2026-08-27 · DEF-652 NEEDS NO RE-SIGN — the PO's tax answer is CONFIGURATION · and DEF-493 decided without them

Two things I told the PO would come back to them. **Neither does**, and the reason is worth
recording because both were nearly escalated on a wrong reading.

### 1 · DEF-652 — the PO ALREADY RULED, and it is a data change, not a frozen one

**PO verbatim:** *"Does a discount come off before or after tax? Tax the full amount before
discount — The utility remits tax on the full service value; the discount is the utility's
cost, not the tax authority's. - what does the tax law in the US say - lets go with it"*

⚠ **I TOLD THE PO THIS WOULD NEED A FINANCE RE-SIGN. That was WRONG, and the error was
mine for not reading the schema before escalating.**

`rating/models.py:923` — **`discount_treatment = models.TextField(default="before")`**, a
**PER-TAX column**, constrained to `before|after` by `ck_taxes_discount_treatment`
(migration `0018_cr013_p4_tax_fields`). `before` applies the discount **before** tax (tax on
the reduced base — today's `$3.19`); `after` applies it **after** (tax on the full base —
the PO's `$4.26`).

**So the mechanism the PO asked for already exists and is already signed.** `BR-RAT-071`
states the treatment is *"statutory and per tax"*. Setting Silver Creek's 6.85% tax to
`after` is **configuration of one row**: no code change, **no ❄️ FROZEN figure moves**, no
HUMAN-GUIDE §6 re-sign, and **nothing already issued changes** (hard rule 4 — issued
invoices are immutable, so a correction would be a new run, never an edit).

**Worked, both figures:** a **`$62.14`** bill with a 25% senior discount of **`$15.54`**.
`before` taxes `$46.60` at 6.85% → **`$3.19`**. `after` taxes `$62.14` → **`$4.26`**.
The difference is **`$1.07` per discounted bill per cycle**.

⚠ **AND THE GOLDEN TESTS DO NOT COVER THIS AT ALL** — `03-golden-verify.py` has **zero**
occurrences of the word *discount*. A golden test combining a percentage discount with a
taxable base is genuinely missing, which is why two readings could both look right for so
long. **The fix must add one**, and adding a case is not touching a frozen figure.

### 2 · THE DEFAULT STAYS `before` — decided here, NOT put to the PO

The tempting second question is *"should the default flip too?"*. **It must not be asked,
because `BR-RAT-071` already answers it:** the treatment is **statutory and per tax**. A
global default asserts a single answer for every authority nobody has examined — and
flipping it would silently re-price every discounted bill on every tax no tenant has
configured, reversible only by another billing run.

**So: the stored default is unchanged, and the real fix is that nobody should ever
INHERIT it silently.** `discount_treatment` becomes a **visible, required choice when a tax
is created**, naming what each option means in money. That is applying a signed rule, not
making a new product decision — which is exactly the class law 13 says is ours.

### 3 · DEF-493 — decided without the PO: `recurring` AND `auto_apply` gate a periodic bill

**The measured problem:** Silver Creek's price list holds 23 charge codes totalling
**`$799.95`** — a `$250.00` tamper fee, a `$45.00` connection fee, a `$30.00`
returned-payment fee and eighteen more. An ordinary monthly water bill has an **`$8.00`**
base. R4 cannot today tell a one-off connection fee from a recurring paper-bill fee, so
wiring the R1–R7 chain as it stands would **add `$799.95` to every monthly bill**.

**Decided: a charge rides a periodic bill only when it is marked `recurring` AND
`auto_apply`.** Both columns **already exist and nothing reads them** — they were built for
this and then never wired, which is hard-won law 2 (built is not wired) rather than a gap
in the design.

**Why this is not a PO question**, though it decides what every customer is charged every
month: the alternatives were a new per-code flag or a per-plan staff choice, and **both
invent a vocabulary next to one the schema already carries**. Choosing between an existing
signed mechanism and a new one is a build judgment. **Recorded here with its reasoning and
reversible in one line if it proves wrong** — which is the standard law 13 sets for
everything that is ours.

⚠ **This does NOT unblock DEF-438 or DEF-498 on its own.** DEF-498 (R4 refuses every bill
five times over, because `resolution.ChargeCode` carries only `flat_amount` + `amounts` and
cannot express `percent` or `per_case`) is paired with this: **fixing either alone turns a
refusal into an overcharge.** They ship together or not at all.

## 2026-08-27 · DEF-632 BUILT — the SSN is captured, encrypted, and PROVED; the widening is exactly one field name

**What was ruled** is the entry above (*"DEF-632 — CAPTURE THE SSN AND ENCRYPT IT"*).
This row records **what was built against it, and the four judgments the lane made
where the ruling was silent** — so the next agent does not have to re-derive them.

### The worked number, followed end to end

An applicant types **`123-45-6789`**. The database row holds about sixty
characters beginning `sbh1:insecure-dev:` and — read back through a **second raw
cursor**, not the field accessor — contains no `123`, no `456789` and no
`123456789`. Staff see **`••• ••• • 6789`**. The audit trail holds
**`•••••6789`**. Nothing else leaves the server.

### Four judgments, none of them in the ruling

1. **ONE COLUMN. NO `ssn_last4` COLUMN.** The last four is a READ projection
   (`crypto.last_four()` at serve time). A stored last-four would put four of the
   nine digits back in the clear beside the ciphertext, and would make *"the row
   contains no part of the number"* false while every test still passed. This is
   also why `ssn_last4` **stays in `IDENTIFIER_FIELDS`** — a caller-supplied one
   would do the same damage through the front door.
2. **NO BLIND INDEX.** `crypto.blind_index()` exists and BR-CUS-089's match tiers
   will need it, but no matcher is built (`suggest_matches` refuses by name), and
   an equality-searchable token nothing queries is surface with no caller. The
   lane that builds the matcher adds it, because that is the only lane that can
   prove it works.
3. **THE WIDENING IS EXACTLY ONE FIELD NAME.** `ssn` left `IDENTIFIER_FIELDS`.
   `social_security_number`, `gov_id`, `gov_id_number`, `id_number`,
   `national_id`, `ein`, `tin`, `gov_id_last4`, `ssn_last4`, `date_of_birth`,
   `dob` and `acting_for` still answer `BIZ_STATE` by name. **`social_security_
   number` is refused deliberately** — one canonical name, because an alias that
   silently works is how two payload shapes start.
4. **THE ONLY FORMAT CHECK IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN.** A value must normalise to at
   least four characters, because the last four is the only projection the product
   offers. Nothing asserts *nine digits*: that would refuse an ITIN, refuse a
   business applicant (B19 §8.7) and refuse a non-US deployment, and it is
   **OQ-781**, not a lane's call.

### The carve-out held, and it is asserted rather than promised

`crypto.py` warns that *"an oracle that will encrypt anything a stranger types is
a chosen-plaintext oracle"*, and **the service-request form is public-facing**.
So `apps/customers` encrypts THIS FIELD ON THIS WRITE and offers nothing general:
no `encrypt_field(name, value)`, no caller-chosen crypto context, no endpoint
taking a column name. A test greps `service_request_service`,
`service_request_reads` and `service_request_api` and fails on any direct
`crypto.encrypt(` or `crypto.blind_index(` call, so the carve-out survives the
next lane that has not read this row.

### What did NOT happen, said plainly

* **The DRIVING LICENCE is not captured.** BR-CUS-092(a) names both identifiers;
  the ruling of 2026-08-27 named one. `capture_applicant_identifier` still raises,
  retargeted to that half, and the detail screen still states the absence. An
  unbuilt half must never become a silent one.
* **The identity MATCHER is not built.** REQ-03.1 tells the applicant their
  identifier is *"used to match you against any account you have held before"* and
  that is still not true.
* **`de.json` was not touched** — the German translation lane owns it under
  OQ-741 / BR-SHL-251. Six catalogue keys are handed over in **DEF-1550**, and
  **G15's key-parity assertion is RED on `de.json` alone** until they land. The
  gate is right and is not loosened.

### The reversal this closes, stated as a reversal

Three artefacts asserted the OPPOSITE and each was correct when written, because
the encryptor did not exist: `test_cr031_service_request.py`'s
*"the identifier is refused until its encryptor exists"*, `ServiceRequestDetailPage
.test.tsx`'s *"the words 'stored encrypted' appear NOWHERE"*, and `J26.spec.ts`'s
*"an identifier must be REFUSED, not accepted"*. All three now assert the round
trip, each carrying the reason it flipped. **The unavailable declaration was
NARROWED, not deleted** — `applicant_identifier_needs_an_encryptor` became
`applicant_drivers_licence_not_captured`.

**Ids used:** DEF-1550 · OQ-780 · OQ-781 · migration `customers 0031`. **No BR was
minted** — BR-CUS-092 has been CONFIRMED since 2026-08-24 and this implements it.
🔒 sensitive path: `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING`, with the plain-English row and its
worked figure already in `12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md` — written
*before* review, so the reviewer reads the repo the next agent will.

## 2026-08-27 · PREMISES → OWNER → MASTER ACCOUNT, **BUILT** — and the one place the ruling runs out (`DEF-650` · `DEF-1088` · `DEF-1247`, v2.76.1)

**NO NEW PO RULING IS CLAIMED HERE.** Everything below implements statements the
PO made on 2026-08-27 and that are already recorded above; what is new is the
BUILD and the judgments underneath it, reported rather than decided.

### What was actually missing, measured before anything was written

The decision log of this morning said it exactly: *"THE ONE MISSING LINK is
`owner → master ACCOUNT`. Today nothing joins a `premises_owners` row to an
`accounts` row of kind `master`."* That was still true. `Premises.owner` →
`PremisesOwner` → `customers.Customer` all existed; the account did not.

**The cost of the gap was a signed rule that could not be obeyed.** `BR-MET-105`
(PO 2026-08-24) sends the empty-unit base charge — **$30.50/month** — to *"the
owner / landlord"*, and the owner was a string on a premise row. The move-out
wizard printed the limitation in its own shipped copy for three days.

### The judgment that matters, and it is the one the ruling does not settle

⚠ **THE PO RULED BOTH HALVES OF THE ACCOUNT QUESTION AND THE TWO DO NOT MEET.**
This is recorded as a collision rather than resolved, because resolving it decides
who is billed.

| ruled, same day | says |
|---|---|
| decision 2 | *"A premises whose owner has no master yet - we have to create one."* |
| closing `OQ-500` | *"(b) — an owner-occupier"* → master-ness is **derived from whether anyone else occupies the premises**, and **"never chosen at creation"** |

**At premises creation there are no units, so nobody occupies anything and the
kind cannot be derived.** Both ways out take a decision the ruling reserved: a
`master` gives a single-family owner-occupier the master/child shape the PO
explicitly ruled against, and a `regular` needs a promotion path that does not
exist — `kind` is a REFUSED input on every account door except
`POST /accounts/master` (BR-CUS-068). A third obstacle is mechanical:
`create_master_account` attaches through the premises' **common-area units**, and
a brand-new premises has none.

**So `OQ-790` is minted and stubbed at its OWN door.**
`ensure_owner_master_account` raises `NotImplementedError("OQ-790")`; the
premises-creation path never calls it, because a `NotImplementedError` there
would refuse an address in order to ask a question — which is the stated reason
`OQ-500` itself was deliberately NOT stubbed. `link_owner_master_account` is the
door that works today, and it covers the PO's headline case verbatim: *"it can be
existing master account also"*.

### Existing free-text owners — kept, and the reasoning is the point

`metering 0041` writes **no data**, which is the same call `metering 0040` made
this morning for the same rows. The two wrong answers were both available:

* **drop the text** — it is often the only record a utility has of who owns an
  address;
* **invent parties from the strings** — *Whitfield Rentals LLC* and *Whitfield
  Rentals, L.L.C.* are one party or two and no algorithm knows which. BR-MET-151
  clause 3 already forbids it in as many words.

So the rule is: **the free text is kept, and the link is required going FORWARD.**
A premises created from today needs an owner; one created before today does not
retroactively become invalid, because a rule that invalidates rows already on disk
is a rule that stops a utility saving an address it has had for ten years. Those
rows stay on `unmatched_premises_qs()` until a person matches them.

### The `Owner` header changed meaning, and that is stated rather than slipped in

`PREMISES_ALIASES` gave the header `Owner` to the FREE-TEXT column. Under the
ruling the owner is an account, so `Owner` now reaches the TYPED owner and
`Owner name (legacy)` reaches the free text.

⚠ **`DEF-1247` raised the right objection — *"flipping it silently re-points every
existing customer template at a different column"* — and it is answered rather
than accepted.** The load writes **both**: the typed link when the party exists,
and the operator's own string into `owner_manager` as BR-MET-151 provenance. A
utility whose CSV has always carried an `Owner` column gets everything it recorded
before **plus** a resolved party. It is a strict addition on the same header, not
a redirection, and that is the whole reason the re-point is safe.

**The two stage-3 rules are asymmetric on purpose**, and the asymmetry is the
design: a NEAR match is an **ERROR** that rejects the row (an import has no clerk
in front of it, and both merging and creating-a-second-party are forbidden); an
UNKNOWN name is a **WARNING** that loads, because a new tenant holds no typed
owners at all and an error would refuse **every row of every first upload** — the
PO's own concern, verbatim: *"we will need to careful what we do when we upload
presmies in the system first time"*.

### What became of the geometric derivation

`BR-CUS-171` is **superseded in its mechanism and confirmed in its link**, and it
had **no rule row anywhere in `04-docs/`** — it lived in a docstring and a
paragraph of this file. It has one now, written by the lane that changed it.
`master_account_for` reads the declared link and no longer calls
`common_area_units_for_premises`. **Retired, not kept as a fallback**, per
decision 4: *"a fallback that disagrees with the declared owner would silently
bill a different party."*

One reading IS kept and it is not a fallback about the owner:
`sub_accounts_for_master` still uses the master's own anchor unit's premises where
nothing declares that account as an owner. Those are the pre-ruling masters, still
covering the common areas they were attached to; it answers *which premises this
account covers*, never *who the owner is*.

### The near-match key, and why it was narrowed

Normalisation strips **legal forms only** — `llc` · `inc` · `corp` · `ltd` · `lp`
— and collapses runs of single letters first, so `L.L.C.` survives the punctuation
strip as `llc` rather than as three one-letter words. An earlier draft also
stripped `property`, `rentals`, `holdings` and `group`, and it collapsed *Ridge
Property LLC* and *Ridge Holdings LLC* onto one key. **Offering two unrelated
landlords never merges anything** — nothing auto-resolves — **but it teaches a
clerk to dismiss the offer, and an offer nobody reads is decision 3 defeated by
noise.**

### Still owed

* `OQ-790` above — the account's creation timing and kind.
* `OQ-501` — whether `owner_manager` is retired. It is now *provenance plus the
  import's own write target*, so it has one more reason to exist than it had this
  morning, and the question is unchanged.
* The wider prevention `DEF-650` named for itself and that is **still not built**:
  a ruling that names a PAYER should be checked against whether that payer can
  hold a ledger position **at the moment it is written into a rule row**. Nothing
  in this repo does that, and it is why this defect existed for three days.

## 2026-08-27 · DEF-724 BUILT — the close-out act, and the ONE judgment the ruling did not settle

**PO verbatim and in full:** *"A disconnected customer can never be closed - Add a
separate close-out act — Cleaner in the record"*.

The ruling is recorded above with the other three of that batch. **This entry is
for the part the ruling did NOT settle and that a lane had to decide**, written
down before it was reported to anyone (law 10's timing rule).

### THE RULING SETTLED THE DOOR. IT DID NOT SETTLE THE COLUMN.

`DEF-724`'s own triage named the hazard: *"the wrong choice writes a `closed_at`
for a tenancy that actually ended at the cut, which is a date on a customer's
record that no correction row can un-say."* A close-out has TWO candidate dates —
the day the service was cut, and the day a clerk performed the paperwork — and
nothing signed says which one lands in `accounts.closed_at`.

**DECIDED: the CUT date. → `BR-CUS-431`, stamped as a BUILD decision, not the
PO's. One word from the PO reverses it.**

### THE WORKED FIGURE THAT DECIDED IT — 43 DAYS OF A LETTABLE UNIT

It is not a preference; it is a measurable consequence of two CONFIRMED rules.

`accounts.closed_at` is the **only** thing `BR-CUS-056` measures the next
occupant's start day against: `selectors.last_closed_account_for_unit` takes the
greatest `closed_at` among terminal accounts on the unit, and
`services._refuse_if_start_lands_on_the_prior_move_day` refuses any incoming
start **on or before** it. `BR-CUS-110` (PO 2026-08-26) releases the unit **at the
cut**.

On `A-11488`, the account all three rules were put with — cut **2026-08-18**,
closed out **2026-09-30**:

| what goes in `closed_at` | the next occupant's `earliest_start` | what it costs |
|---|---|---|
| **2026-09-30** (the clerk's day) | 2026-10-01 | **43 days** of a unit the utility was entitled to re-let are refused, 2026-08-19 → 2026-09-30 |
| **2026-08-18** (the cut) | 2026-08-19 | exactly what `BR-CUS-110` grants |

`BR-CUS-103` agrees from the money side: base charges stop at the cut, so the cut
day IS the last day the outgoing account is charged for — which is precisely
`BR-CUS-056`'s *"the outgoing account pays the move day"*.

**The act's own date is not lost.** It goes to `disconnect_cases.closed_out_on`
with `closed_out_by` beside it, so the record reads *the service ended on the cut
date and the account was closed out on this later day, by this person*. Two dates,
on purpose. **That is what *"cleaner in the record"* asks for**, and it is why
nothing is written to `move_records`: a `kind="move_out"` row would be the exact
falsification the ruling forbids.

### THE SECOND HALF A LATER LANE WILL WANT TO DELETE

`close_out` **refuses an OCCUPANT** (`customers.account.close_out_still_occupying`).
That looks like a needless restriction on a working door and it is not: an
occupant leaving IS a move-out, and admitting them here would file a departure as
a disconnection — the same falsification pointing the other way. **A door that
accepts everybody is `move_out` with a longer name.** `move_out`'s own
`not_an_occupant` refusal is CORRECT at every line and is untouched.

### WHAT WAS **NOT** ASKED, BECAUSE THE REPO ALREADY ANSWERED IT (law 13)

*May an account with an outstanding balance be closed out, and what happens to the
debt?* **`BR-CUS-082` (CONFIRMED, PO 2026-08-24, *"(b) continue, ladder restarts"*)
already rules it** — a debt surviving closure is still chased and the ladder
restarts at TIER 1 as a COLLECTIONS sequence, never a service one. Closure with a
balance is the case that rule was written for. So the close-out CONSUMES
`disconnects.restart_after_closure` and adds no rule of its own. Worked: `A-11488`
closes owing **$612.75**, the account reaches `closed`, the **$612.75** stays owed,
and TIER 1 fires against **the account itself** — nothing is tied back to a master,
because `BR-CUS-097` as qualified 2026-08-27 makes the tie-back a clerk's act in
the S20 wizard and this door does not collect that consent.

### MINTED: `OQ-830` — a sentence or a fixed list?

The close-out asks the clerk WHY, and `accounts.close_reason` has been
PROPOSED-SCHEMA since 2026-08-08 with no ruled vocabulary. **Built as a REQUIRED
FREE SENTENCE and nothing is stubbed**, because a stub would break the act the PO
ruled; what is missing is the ability to COUNT closures by reason, and that is the
question. The three words that keep appearing in defect rows — *settled · written
off · gone* — are a lane's phrasing, not a ruling, and are offered in `OQ-830` as
a starting list rather than as a recommendation.

### BOUNDARIES HELD RATHER THAN CROSSED

* **`OQ-680` / `DEF-744` (OPEN)** — whether a payment plan, an open dispute or an
  unbilled cycle must BLOCK a terminal act was never put to the PO. The close-out
  performs **no clearance** and says so on every response and on the screen. A
  blocker invented here would give the product a dead end with no documented way
  past it — which is `DEF-724`'s own failure, one flow over.
* **`DEF-701`'s billing half (OPEN)** — re-measured on this tree rather than taken
  from the row: `billing.stages.resolve_subscription.CLASSES_THAT_BILL` still
  reads `(CLASS_BILLABLE, CLASS_BASE_ONLY)`. Assigning `BR-CUS-107`'s seeded
  `Disconnected` status today would drop the WHOLE account from the bill run and
  leave the usage consumed BEFORE the cut unbilled — trading a wrong LABEL for a
  wrong BILL. Customers may not change it (B2 §2). `DEF-701` stays OPEN on that
  half alone, and a test asserts the blocker is still there so the row becomes
  closeable the day it goes RED.

### TWO THINGS FOUND ON THE TREE AND REPORTED, NOT REACHED INTO

1. **`commit_cut` raises `TypeError` on this tree** — `apps/billing/fee_bill.py`
   is staged-but-uncommitted and calls `issue.issue_invoice()` without
   `issued_at`, `template_id` and `template_version`. The DEF-708 lane's to fix.
2. **`make_premises` refuses every W7 fixture** — `BR-MET-401`/`DEF-650` made the
   premises owner mandatory and the shared W1 helper still supplies only the
   free-text `owner_manager`, so `tests/test_w7_cut_reconnect.py` is red before
   this lane added a line. That lane's helper to fix.

### AND ONE OF THIS LANE'S OWN, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS LAW 11's FIFTH MECHANISM

The first push of this work **published the DEF-708 lane's uncommitted
`disconnects.py`** — a pathspec commit takes the whole file, and that file was
clean at `git status` when this lane started. It shipped a `commit_cut` whose
callee is not on the branch. Caught by the post-push check law 11 prescribes —
`git show <commit> -- <the shared file>`, reading the HUNKS and not `--stat` —
and repaired in `20b5465` by rebuilding the file as tip-content plus only this
lane's four hunks. Nothing was lost from anybody's working tree.

## 2026-08-27 · DEF-161's RED PROOF FOUND DEAD CODE IN THE FIX ITSELF — recorded, because the branch looked exactly like the answer

The billing-rulings lane, an hour after the entry above. **No rule changes here.**
This is r11 step 2d doing the job it exists to do, and the result is worth a row
because the dead code was in the shape everybody would have accepted on review.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** `measure_consumption` got an explicit branch:

    if reading is not None and reading.absent_reason == ABSENT_SERVICE_NOT_METERED:
        services.append(MeasuredService(..., absent_reason=ABSENT_SERVICE_NOT_METERED))
        continue

It reads like the fix. It names the rule, it names the defect, it is where a
reader would look for DEF-161's behaviour, and it has a comment explaining why
it must not be widened.

**WHAT THE RED PROOF SAID.** Disabling that branch and re-running the case that
bills the `$18.00` trash charge:

    1 passed, 4 warnings in 228.87s

**Green with the fix removed.** The branch changed nothing: the BR-BIL-015
fallback three lines below already forwards `reading.absent_reason` verbatim, so
metering's `service_not_metered` reached `MeasuredService` either way. The real
fix is one file over — `runs.calculate_account` (and `midperiod`) exempting that
reason from the unresolved-read refusal, which is what routes the service into
`base_only_services`.

**SO THE BRANCH WAS DELETED**, and a note naming `runs.calculate_account` as the
line to break replaced it. Keeping it would have been hard-won law 2's failure
inside a single function: code that looks like the mechanism, passes every test,
and is not the mechanism — so the next lane "fixing" DEF-161 would edit the
wrong place and watch nothing change.

**THE GENERAL POINT, and it is why this is a decision-log row and not a commit
message.** r11 step 2d says *break every guard FIRST, quote the failure*. The
usual reading is that it protects against a test that cannot fail. **It also
catches a FIX that cannot fail** — code whose removal changes no behaviour —
and that failure mode is invisible to every other check in this repo: ruff
passes, the tests pass, the diff reads well, and a reviewer sees the rule quoted
beside the branch. **Only breaking it on purpose tells you.**

Both proofs are on the record: with the exemption removed, the same case fails
with the engine's own refusal — *"account …: trash still has no usable read and
no decision"* — which is DEF-161 as filed.
