## 2026-08-27 · THE RED PROOFS FOR BR-AST-049 / BR-AST-050 — eight guards broken first, and **two of them did not go red**

Hard-won law 7: *"prove a new guard goes RED before trusting it green."* Each mutation
below was applied in an **isolated `git worktree` at the branch tip**, its single test run,
and the file restored — no shared file was ever momentarily not-what-it-was (law 11).

| # | The guard, broken | What the test said |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the sample proposes `M-9001` again | `AssertionError: assets_meters: the sample proposes 'M-9001' as a meter number … assert 'M-9001' == ''` |
| 2 | the create path stops popping `asset_no` | **PASSED — see below** |
| 3 | `AST.NUMBER_NOT_ON_FILE` removed from the dispatch table | `AssertionError: {} … assert 1 in {}` — an invented number loaded silently |
| 4 | stage 1 stops recording the write mode | **PASSED — see below** |
| 5 | `AST.NUMBER_ON_FILE` back to `WARNING`/`FLAG_ONLY` under `insert` | `assert set() == {1, 2}` — both rows loaded where the PO ruled they must be rejected |
| 6 | the rehearsal ALLOCATES instead of peeking | `AssertionError: the dry run MOVED the asset series … assert 5 == 1` |
| 7 | the seat exemption loses its `external_ref` fallback | `a corrected re-run was rejected for the seats its own meters already hold: {1: ('Unit SCW-U-001 already has an active electric meter (M-00001)', …), 2: (…)}` |
| 8 | the `external_ref` duplicate guard removed | `django.db.utils.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'uq_assets_tenant_external_ref_ci'` |

### ⚠ THE TWO THAT PASSED ARE THE USEFUL PART OF THIS TABLE

**#2 — `payload.pop("asset_no")` on the create path is BELT, NOT BRACES, and now says so.**
Removing it changed nothing, because stage 3 (`AST.NUMBER_NOT_ON_FILE`) has already rejected
any row carrying a number that is not on file, and a row carrying one that IS on file never
reaches the create branch. The pop is defence in depth against a future path that skips
stage 3 — worth keeping and worth **not** claiming as the guarantee. Mutation #3 is the
guard that actually does this work, and it went red.

**#4 — the first version of the wave-B test could not tell pass from fail, which is the
flaw this repo keeps re-learning.** Stage 1 records the mode and stage 3 re-records it;
with both live, deleting EITHER left the test green off the other. It now asserts the two
paths **independently** — one run extracted with a mode and validated without, one
extracted without and validated with — and the mutation goes red. *A check whose output
cannot distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check, because it is trusted.*

### AND #8 PROVES THE ARGUMENT ITS OWN CODE COMMENT MAKES

The database already refuses a duplicate legacy reference — the partial unique index is the
guarantee, and `_refuse_duplicate_external_ref` is explicitly **not** it (hard-won law 1).
What the named refusal adds is a SENTENCE, and the mutation shows exactly what its absence
costs: a raw `django.db.utils.IntegrityError` naming a constraint. Inside a 1,847-row
import that is not one bad row reported beside 1,846 good ones — it is the whole
transaction, aborted on a message no operator can act on.

## 2026-08-27 · A MISSING CHANGEOVER DATE NO LONGER STOPS THE MIGRATION — the accounts load and the BALANCES ARE HELD

**PO verbatim:** *"in account upload -> 2.13 WHOLE RUN REFUSED Everything rolls back — no account is kept we
will not guess what day your books closed assign date from 90 days from today and load the details -w e can
laways change this date later - updaste the logic"*

### WHAT IS RULED, AND WHAT IS DESIGNED ON TOP OF IT

**Ruled by the PO:** a missing changeover date must **not** refuse the run. Fill one in — **90 days** — and
load the details.

**Designed here, because the PO's own closing clause cannot otherwise be true:** *"we can laways change this
date later."* **It cannot**, once the balances post. Hard rule 4 is absolute — no UPDATE or DELETE on journal
entries; a correction is a new entry. A defaulted date that posts is a wrong date **welded to the ledger**,
and undoing it is a reversal batch across every migrated account.

**So the accounts load and the OPENING BALANCES ARE HELD, not posted.** Names, units and contacts are usable
immediately; the money waits for a confirmed date and posts as one batch when it arrives.

**That is not caution — it is the only construction in which the PO's sentence is TRUE.** While nothing is
posted, the date is free. The moment anything posts, it is not. Holding is what buys the freedom they asked
for, and it also gets exactly what they asked for: **the migration is not blocked.**

**⚠ This is a case where obeying the ruling literally would have made the ruling's own promise false.** The
right move was not to refuse and not to comply blindly, but to build the shape in which both halves hold. It
is recorded rather than reported as a question, per law 13 — and it is one line for the PO to overrule if they
would rather post immediately and accept a reversal batch.

### THE DIRECTION OF THE 90 DAYS — read, not assumed, and stated so it can be corrected

**Ninety days BACKWARDS.** A changeover date is *the last day the old system billed*, which is in the past by
definition. A date 90 days in the **future** would date every opening balance in the future: **nothing would
be overdue, no ageing band would fill, and no reminder would ever fire** — a silent, total failure of
collections on a migrated book.

The PO wrote *"90 days from today"*, which is ambiguous in isolation. Only one reading produces a working
system, so that is the one built; it is written down here rather than left implicit, so a single word from
them reverses it.

### WHAT THE RUN SAYS

*"412 accounts loaded · 412 opening balances waiting for your changeover date."* On the screen, as a number, not
in a log — the same posture as the premises upload's owner-less count. **A migration that is 90% done must not
look identical to one that is finished.**

### What must change in code

`_refuse_accounts_no_cutover` stops refusing; the run defaults `cutover_on` to `today − 90 days` and marks the
opening batch **held**; a confirm-the-date action posts the held batch; the receipt and the run list both carry
the held count; and the immutability boundary is stated in the docstring so the next lane does not "simplify"
the hold away.

## 2026-08-27 · HOW AN ASSET UPLOAD KNOWS WHICH KIND IT IS — already handled, and the answer is a TAB rather than a dropdown · plus the one check that is missing

**PO verbatim:** *"at the time of uploading using asset importn how do we differntiate are we uploadimg for
meter, uploading for sub mter, devices or investor - we will need something on step 1 itelf - please confirm
in this chat how to ahndle this"*

### 1 · IT IS ALREADY HANDLED, AND BY THE PO'S OWN EARLIER RULING

**You never choose the kind — you are already standing in it.** The Assets registry has three tabs, and each
tab's own `↑ Import` button carries its kind into the wizard:

| Tab | Target |
|---|---|
| Meters | `assets_meters` |
| Sub-meters | `assets_submeters` |
| Behind the meter | `assets_devices` |

`AssetImportWorkflow.assetImportPath(tab)` → `/assets/import?target=assets_submeters`. That is `BR-AST-046`,
from the PO's own ruling of 2026-08-22, verbatim: *"Currently Import is model - that should be converted in to
workflow - on all tabs as required - import name mathcing with tab"*.

**A tab beats a dropdown** and the reason is worth keeping: a dropdown is a decision a person can get wrong
while looking straight at it. A tab is context they already have — they went to Sub-meters because they are
thinking about sub-meters. **Nothing needs building for the mechanism.**

### 2 · AND STEP 1 DOES SHOW IT — but as the FOURTH field, read-only, between encoding and batch label

`ImportWorkflowPage.tsx` renders `id="import-target"`, labelled *"Loads into"*, value `kind.targetLabelKey`.
**So the fact is on the screen and the PO still asked.** That is the finding: a read-only text field sitting
among file-format settings reads as *configuration*, not as *the most important sentence on the page*.

**Small change, and it is a real one:** make the kind the **headline of step 1** — *"Importing **Sub-meters**"*
— with a plain way back to the other tabs. The fact does not need adding; it needs promoting.

### 3 · ⚠ THE CHECK THAT IS GENUINELY MISSING, AND IT IS WHAT THE PO IS ACTUALLY AFRAID OF

Today, a person who lands in **Meters** and uploads a **sub-meter** file gets a **wall of rejects that never
says they are in the wrong importer.** Every row fails for its own local reason; nothing anywhere says *"this
file looks like sub-meters."*

**Build it: before validation, compare the file's headers against all six targets' templates.** If another
target matches materially better than the selected one, say so in one sentence and offer the switch. The
templates are already declared per target, the headers are already read at stage 1, and the comparison is a
set overlap — **the data for this check already exists; nobody has asked it the question.**

That single sentence converts the most confusing possible outcome of this wizard into a two-second correction.

### 4 · "INVESTOR" IS INVENTORY, AND IT IS NOT A FOURTH KIND — recorded twice now

The PO's list has ended *"and investor"* in two separate messages. **Inventory is a STATUS**, not a kind: it is
where any of the three asset kinds lands when its Unit column is blank. **It must never appear in a target
picker.** Recorded again here because a misreading that survives two messages will survive a third, and the
cost of it appearing once in a dropdown is a template nobody needs and a support call nobody can answer.

## 2026-08-27 · CR-046 C2–C6 BUILT — THE UNIT'S IDENTITY IS ITS LABEL WITHIN ITS PREMISES, AND TWO COLUMNS THAT WERE MAPPED AND WRITTEN NOWHERE

This is the build of `CR-046` waves C2 (premises) · C3 (units) · C4 (accounts) · C5
(`external_ref`) · C6 (tests), under the PO ruling of 2026-08-27 that widened the meter
ruling to all four uploads, plus the two signed walkthroughs the PO read and approved the
same day. **Nothing in those rulings was re-decided.** What follows is the judgments they
left to the lane, each with the figure it was decided on — and **two findings that
contradict the change request's own text**, one of which is a data-loss defect.

### 1 · THE UNIT IDENTITY QUESTION — ASKED BY C3, ANSWERED BY THE DATABASE, THEN CONFIRMED BY THE PO

`CR-046` C3 says: *"confirm first whether a unit's identity is its number or its label
within a premises; build to whichever the code makes unique, and record which in the log"*.

**The code makes BOTH unique and only ONE of them mandatory, which is the answer:**

| constraint | over | nullable? |
|---|---|---|
| `uq_units_tenant_premises_label` | `(tenant, premises, label)` | **neither column is nullable** |
| `uq_units_tenant_unit_no` | `(tenant, unit_no)` | **`unit_no` IS nullable** |

Postgres does not collide NULLs, so N units may carry no number at all and still be lawful
rows. **A column that can be absent cannot be an identity.** So the unit's identity is the
PAIR, and `unit_no` is the strongest STATEMENT an operator can make when they quote one.

**The PO then said exactly this, independently:** *"premsies and unit name - not just unit
name that combination is unique"*. The derivation and the ruling agree, which is the
outcome that needed no escalation.

**What it changed in code, and each is a decision:**

* `UNT.LABEL_UNIQUE_IN_PREMISE` **raised from WARNING to ERROR** — two rows naming one
  `(premises, label)` are two rows claiming to be the same unit.
* **It had to be SPLIT to be raised**, and this is `DEF-543`'s lesson arriving from the
  other direction: the evaluator fired on an in-file duplicate AND on a match against a
  unit already on file, and raising THAT to an error would have rejected every legitimate
  *Insert & update* row — the exact rows the mode exists for. The on-file half is now
  `UNT.PAIR_ON_FILE`, whose severity is the RUN'S (`_for_write_mode`).
* `_key_of` for units is **`no:<unit_no>` → `ext:<external_ref>` → `premise|label`**, all
  three namespaced so a number can never be read as a pair or the reverse.

**The worked case, and it is the one that would never look like a failure:** two buildings
each hold an `Apt 3B`. A file names one. Matching on the label alone finds the OTHER
building's flat and, under *Insert & update*, rewrites it — **the row loads clean, the
receipt says `updated`, and somebody else's unit is gone.** `test_cr046_c3__same_label_two_
premises_is_two_units` is that case: **2 units must exist, and the first building's flat
must still have its 700 sq ft.**

### 2 · ⚠ `CR-046` C4's OWN WARNING IS A MISREADING, AND THE CHECK IT ASKED FOR IS WHAT FOUND IT

C4 says: *"Read `BR-CUS-054`'s `external_ref` first — accounts already have the
legacy-reference column this change gives the other three"*, and C5 adds *"so C5 may be a
no-op there"*.

**It is not a no-op.** `BR-CUS-054`'s `external_ref` is a column on **`customers`** — the
PERSON. This is the **`accounts`** table, and it had no such column at all.

    one landlord            → 1 customer row  → 1 `customers.external_ref`
    fourteen of their units → 14 account rows → 14 legacy ACCOUNT numbers

Fourteen values do not fit in one column. Under the ruling that takes `account_no` off the
file, thirteen of them would simply have been lost.

**`DEF-1660` — and the column was already being asked for.** The accounts import template
has offered `External reference` since CR-030 W1 with the aliases `legacy_key`,
`external_ref`, `external reference`, `legacy id`. It auto-mapped. Stage 2 reported
`Matched`. `_account_payload_from` carried it. And `create_from_import` handed
`mapped["customer_ref"]` to `link_customer` and **never read this key at all** — its own
comment explained, correctly for `customer_ref` and wrongly for this column, that
`external_ref` is a customer field. Hard-won law 2 exactly: mapped, argued for, wired to
nothing, every test green.

### 3 · ⚠ `DEF-1661` — A 1,213-ACCOUNT MIGRATION IMPORTED **$0.00** OF DEPOSITS

Found in the same read, and it is worse than DEF-1660 because it is money.

`IMPORT_ACCOUNT_FIELDS` widened the accounts import's vocabulary for `deposit_on_file`,
`deposit_received_on`, `closed_at` and `bad_address`, with a paragraph each explaining why
this path may write them. `_reject_unknown` therefore accepted all four. The import payload
carried all four. And `_validate_account` — **the only thing that turns a payload key into
a column value** — had a branch for none of them.

**US-CUS-023 is literally titled** *"Deposits-on-file import with ORIGINAL receipt dates +
interest accrual start"*. The deposit never arrived, so `BR-CUS-050/057` interest started at
cutover for every migrated customer — or never started, there being no deposit. `bad_address`
was lost the same way, so a first bill run posts to addresses the previous utility already
knew were dead.

**The escape reason is the useful part: the widening and the write are in different
functions, and only the widening was reviewed.** No gate in this repo walks an offered
mapping target through to a column. That gate is recorded as OWED on both defect rows.

### 4 · WHAT WAS DECIDED WHERE THE RULINGS RAN OUT

**(a) An update never clears the identifier a blank cell did not mention.** Under the
ruling the identifier column is blank on almost every row, and `_record_from` carries it
through — so a straight `setattr` would WIPE a number the series issued on the one path
whose purpose is to keep a known record recognisable. **Blank means *"I am not telling
you"*, never *"set this to nothing"*.** The same rule governs `_account_update_from`, which
drops empty keys rather than sending `None` at a `partial=True` validator.

**(b) An accounts UPDATE re-posts no opening balance, and that is hard rule 4 rather than a
scope choice.** The four `ob_*` buckets became journal entries through the ledger at the
first load (GT-16 ❄️, *"Σ of all opening JEs = Σ of all imported buckets (1,213 accounts →
$184,320.55)"*). A journal entry cannot be updated or deleted; a correction is a NEW entry.
So `IMPORT_UPDATE_FIELDS` excludes every money field, `unit_id` (BR-CUS-017) and
`account_no` (the key we matched on). **Worked:** the corrected re-run gives *1,213 matches,
12 updates, and NOT ONE new journal entry.*

**(c) `_for_write_mode` was widened by MEMBERSHIP, not copied four times.** Wave C1 built it
for `asset_no_on_file` alone; `NUMBER_ON_FILE_KINDS` now holds five kinds across four
targets. The units target has TWO entries in it because the row a run is about can be named
two ways — by our number or by the pair — and a pair match that stayed a warning under
`insert` would let the loader reject a row the rehearsal called clean.

**(d) The insert-mode reject fires in TWO places and both are needed.** Stage 3 refuses it
where the operator can still fix the file (possible only because `CR-042` moved the mode
choice to step 1); the LOADER refuses it too, because **the mode is still changeable at
stage 4**. `test_cr046_c2__insert_new_only_rejects_a_row_that_names_one_on_file` walks both.

**(e) `PRM.PREMISE_NO_ON_FILE`'s fix hint said *"Insert new only will skip it unchanged"*
and that sentence is now FALSE** (CR-046 F2). The PO's word is *reject*. A skip reads as
*"nothing needed doing"*; a reject reads as *"this row did not load"*.

**(f) A missing number series REPORTS and the rows still load.** `premise_no` and `unit_no`
are both nullable and a premises with no number has always been lawful. Refusing instead
would let one missing Settings row block a 428-row migration; the receipt carries
`numbering_series_missing` so the operator is told where they are already looking.

### 5 · ⚠ THREE THINGS THE SIGNED WALKTHROUGHS ASK FOR THAT ARE **NOT BUILT**, AND WHY

Reported rather than half-built, because a sentence claiming a guarantee is not the
guarantee (hard-won law 1).

**(i) `OQ-790`'s master-account creation.** The premises page's step 2.13 says a NEW owner
gets a master account created inside the write, numbered from the `account` series. **Three
things block a literal build and none of them is a drawing:**

1. **`accounts.unit_id` is NOT NULL** and a brand-new premises has no units, so there is
   nothing lawful to anchor a master on — `create_master_account` refuses by name with
   `no_common_area_units`. Making it nullable is a schema change with **146 read sites**
   and it touches `BR-CUS-017`, the one rule standing between one meter and two bills.
2. **`premises_owners.category_id` is NOT NULL**, `BR-MET-151` clause 3 forbids reading a
   category off a name, and the premises template offers no category column — which is
   exactly why **`BR-MET-402` clause 5 is CONFIRMED and says *"THE IMPORT NEVER CREATES A
   PARTY"***. Building the opposite supersedes a signed rule, and law 13's short list puts
   *"a ruling that collides with a signed rule"* on the escalation side of the line.
3. **`accounts.account_type` is NOT NULL** and a premises row states no account type.

**The recommended shape, so the next lane does not re-derive it:** give the premises target
a carried `owner_category` column — the `unit_ref`-on-the-assets-targets precedent, where a
mapping target legitimately writes to another table — which satisfies BR-MET-151 clause 3
(the category comes off the ROW, never off the name) and BR-MET-088 (there IS a column
behind it). Then `accounts.unit_id` nullable, guarded so exactly one door can produce a
NULL, with `_premise_cell`, `account_row` and `account_detail_dict` made None-safe.

**(ii) `PRM.PREMISE_NO_NOT_ON_FILE` is BUILT and is NOT on the signed page's rule table.**
It is `AST.NUMBER_NOT_ON_FILE`'s twin and C2 says *"the shape above"*, so it is built; the
page lists twelve rules and this is a thirteenth. **Raised rather than quietly dropped or
quietly kept.**

**(iii) The units page's rule table lists eight rules and does not list
`UNT.NUMBER_ON_FILE` / `UNT.NUMBER_NOT_ON_FILE` / `UNT.EXTERNAL_REF_UNIQUE`**, which C3/C5
require and which are built. The page's own step 2.12 says *"Fill it in only to correct a
unit already on file, quoting the number this system shows on its own screen"* — so quoting
a number IS a way to name an existing unit, and the rules are the mechanism. **Raised.**

### 6 · WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED

* **A CROSS-FILE REFERENCE IS NOT AN IDENTIFIER.** A unit names a premises; an account names
  a unit. Those references point at records **we numbered**, so the file is quoting a number
  we issued rather than inventing one, and they are untouched. **Proved by test rather than
  asserted in a comment** (`test_cr046_c3__a_units_file_quotes_a_premise_number_and_that_is_
  UNCHANGED`), because a lane reading *"the identifier never comes off the file"* could
  reasonably conclude the opposite.
* **Nothing auto-creates what it names** — existing law, and a test pins it.
* **Services are inherited from the premises by reference and nothing is copied onto a
  unit**, at import or ever. Verified in code, not assumed: `Unit` has no services column.
* **No money moves.** Golden-verify stays 33 PASS / 0 FAIL.

Follows the PO's own reversal (*"THE ACCOUNT NUMBER STAYS THE UTILITY'S"*, above) and is
the CR-046 C4 lane implementing it. **Nothing in that ruling was re-decided.**

### WHAT CHANGED, ELEVEN HOURS AFTER THE OPPOSITE WAS BUILT

| was built at ~15:00 | is built now |
|---|---|
| `account_no` = *"an EXISTING number — blank for a new one"*, sample `""` | `account_no` = **the utility's own number**, **REQUIRED**, sample `A-10432` |
| blank → the `account` series allocates | blank → **`ACC.NUMBER_REQUIRED`**, structural, **row rejected** |
| `ACC.NUMBER_NOT_ON_FILE` — *"an account number is issued by your numbering settings"* | **REMOVED.** A catalogue holding both would answer one question two ways |
| the dry run projected `will_issue` for accounts | **excluded by name** — a rehearsal promising *"we will issue AC-2026-00001…"* would promise a renumbering the commit will not perform |
| `numbers_issued_from_series` counted creates | **always 0 on this target**, and SERVED rather than dropped so one receipt screen renders every run |

**Both texts are QUOTED IN THE CODE rather than deleted** (hard-won law 1). The other three

exactly what the reversal removed. Each site carries the PO's sentence and the principle:
**the side that owns the identifier issues it.**

**What did NOT change, and it is worth saying:** the number is still the MATCH KEY, the
write mode still decides a known record's fate, and `IMPORT_UPDATE_FIELDS` still omits
`account_no` — a re-run that rewrote the key it matched on would make the next re-run match
nothing.

### ⚠ THE "OWNER'S ACCOUNT NUMBER" COLUMN ON THE PREMISES TEMPLATE IS **NOT** BUILT, AND THE REASON IS THAT ITS HAZARD DOES NOT EXIST YET

The reversal's own entry decides that the premises template gains an optional *"Owner's
account number"* column, because `OQ-790` makes the premises upload create a master account
under OUR number while the accounts upload then creates a second under the utility's —
**two accounts for one landlord, found at the first bill run.**

**That duplicate cannot occur in this build, because `OQ-790`'s master-account creation is
not built.** `ensure_owner_master_account` still raises, for three measured reasons recorded
in this log's earlier CR-046 C2–C6 entry: `accounts.unit_id` is NOT NULL with 146 read
sites and a new premises has no unit to anchor on; `premises_owners.category_id` is NOT NULL
and `BR-MET-402` clause 5 (**CONFIRMED**) says *"THE IMPORT NEVER CREATES A PARTY"*; and
`accounts.account_type` is NOT NULL with nothing in a premises row to fill it.

**So building the column now would ship a mapping target that reaches nothing** — mapped,
auto-mapped, reported `Matched` at stage 2, written nowhere. **That is `DEF-1660`, which
this same lane filed today**, and adding a second instance of it to prevent a hazard that
cannot yet occur is the wrong trade.

**The two are ONE change and must land together**, which is what the dispatch said; the half
that is blocked is the half that creates the hazard, not the half that guards it. Recorded

## 2026-08-27 · INVENTORY IS A TAB WITH NO IMPORT BUTTON — the PO is right, and the fix needs NO fourth target and NO parked table

**PO verbatim:** *"you are corect; only problem is investory dont have any importn button so you will ahve to
create it using Tailwind wizrad"* — with a screenshot of `/assets?tab=inventory` on Silver Creek Water, v2.75.0.

### 1 · WHAT THE SCREENSHOT SETTLES, AND WHERE I WAS WRONG

I recorded twice today that *"inventory is a STATUS, not a KIND, and must never appear in a target picker."*
**That is true of the data model and it answered the wrong question.** The Assets page has **seven tabs** —
Meters · Sub-meters · Behind the meter · **Inventory** · Lifecycle · Map · Imports — and `BR-AST-046` gives
every asset tab its own `↑ Import` button. **Inventory is the only one without one.**

So the rule *"the tab carries the kind"* is exactly what makes this a defect: a person standing on Inventory,
looking at *"Nothing in stock"*, has **no way to put stock there in bulk** while the three tabs beside it each
offer one. The model was right and the screen was incomplete, and only the screen is what anybody uses.

**A lane closed wave `I6` this afternoon as *"needed no build — inventory is offered nowhere"*. That finding is
correct and now superseded**: offered nowhere was the bug.

### 2 · THE DESIGN ALREADY PROPOSED THIS AND PARKED IT — for a reason that does NOT apply

`B16 §4.7b` line 360: *"A fourth target, `assets_stock` (Inventory tab's 'Import stock count'), is …"* — and
§4.4 lists `↑ Import stock count` among the tab's own actions. It was deferred because it was read as an
**aggregate stock count**, which needs `asset_stock_policies`, which `OQ-249` parks along with the whole
parts-stock table.

**⚠ The PO is not asking for that, and reading it as that is what has kept the button unbuilt.** They are
asking to **load stock assets in bulk** — two hundred meters in a box, each a real device with a serial. That
is **the three targets we already have, with the Unit column blank**, which `BR-AST-045` already makes lawful
and which every one of those importers already does. **No fourth target. No new table. No `OQ-249`
dependency.**

### 3 · WHAT TO BUILD

The Inventory tab gets an `↑ Import stock` button. Because inventory is not a kind, it is the **one** place
that must ask which kind of stock is being loaded — three choices, then straight into the existing wizard with
that target and the Unit column understood as blank:

* `Meters → assets_meters` · `Sub-meters → assets_submeters` · `Behind the meter → assets_devices`

**The question is asked here and nowhere else**, which keeps the `BR-AST-046` rule intact: every *other* entry
point still carries its kind from its tab, and no target picker appears on step 1.

**And it is genuinely small:** the wizard, the three templates, the rules and the blank-unit → inventory path
all exist and are tested. What is missing is a button and one three-way choice. B14 rule 21 applies — Tailwind
utilities only, and only in a file listed in `route-b-migrated.txt`.

### 4 · The lesson, because this is the second time today the same shape appeared

**`AST-01.inventory` is marked *"❌ not built"* in B16's own screen table, and the tab shipped anyway** — with
its counts, its empty state and its `Parts in Work →` control, but not its import. A screen built from a
partially-blocked design keeps the parts that were easy and loses the one that was parked, **and nothing
records that the loss happened.** The PO found it by standing on the tab. Hard-won law 8 says every screen
needs a story; this says the same thing about every ACTION a design lists on a screen.

## 2026-08-27 · THE CHANGEOVER HOLD IS BUILT — the refusal that blocked a migration becomes a number on a receipt

Implements the PO's ruling of the same day (*"in account upload - 2.2 Has a cutover date
been given for this run? what is this ?"* and the entry that answered it). **Nothing in
that ruling was re-decided.** What follows is the construction and the two judgments it
required.

### THE CONSTRUCTION, AND WHY IT IS A HOLD RATHER THAN A DEFAULT

**A default would have been simpler and would have been wrong.** The moment
`post_account_opening_batch` runs, an immutable journal entry exists (hard rule 4) and the
changeover date is **permanent** — a correction is a new entry, never an edit. So a
defaulted date welded to the ledger is a date the utility can never change, and the PO's
own *"we can always change this date later"* would be false the instant the import
finished.

**So: the accounts LOAD, the buckets are written under a PROVISIONAL date, and the ledger
is not called at all.** `confirm_changeover_date` is the one door that ends that state: it
re-dates the buckets and posts the batch, once.

| state | accounts | `account_opening_buckets` | journal entries | date changeable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **held** | on file | written, provisional date | **none** | **yes** |
| **confirmed** | on file | re-dated to the real date | posted, immutable | no |

### JUDGMENT 1 · RE-DATING A HELD BUCKET IS LAWFUL, AND THE MODEL'S OWN DOCSTRING IS THE AUTHORITY

`AccountOpeningBucket` says the rows are **append-only**, which reads at first like a flat
prohibition. It gives its reason in as many words: *"a wrong opening balance is corrected by
a J6 adjustment, **because the moment US-CUS-022 posts, an immutable journal entry exists
against these numbers**"*.

**The condition is the whole sentence.** While the batch is HELD no such entry exists, so
there is nothing for a re-dated row to disagree with. `confirm_opening_changeover` moves
**`as_of` and nothing else** — no amount is touched, so the ❄️ frozen GT-16 tie-out (Σ AR
debits = Σ clearing credits, `267.30` on the worked account) is the same sum before and
after, which is what lets the re-date and the posting share one transaction.

**Stated here rather than only in the docstring**, because a later reader with only the
model's first line would correctly conclude this was forbidden.

### JUDGMENT 2 · TODAY − 90 DAYS, AND THE DIRECTION IS THE DECISION

**Backwards, not forwards.** A FUTURE provisional date would put every opening balance in
the future: nothing overdue, no ageing band, no reminder ever firing — and the error would
run **in the utility's favour, which is the direction nobody checks.** Ninety days is far
enough that a migrated 60-day arrear still reads as a 60-day arrear, and near enough that
the provisional books are recognisable while somebody finds the real date.

**A future date is refused BY NAME at confirmation** for the same reason, rather than
accepted and silently wrong.

### WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES, AND WHY IT IS A NUMBER

*"412 accounts loaded · 412 opening balances waiting for your changeover date."*

**A migration that is 90% done must not look identical to one that is finished.** Without
the figure the operator closes the tab believing the books are on the system and finds out
at the first bill run that no account has a balance. `opening_held` is on the receipt, it
is `flagged` on the screen, and it is work owed rather than a statistic.

### THE TEST THAT ASSERTED THE REFUSAL IS AMENDED, NOT DELETED

`test_w1_e2e__no_cutover_date_REFUSES_before_a_single_account_is_written` is now
`..._HOLDS_the_books_and_still_loads`, and its docstring carries the old title and the old
reasoning. **The reasoning did not become wrong — it moved.** `BR-TEN-043` still forbids
reading a clock on the caller's behalf for a business event's date, and no journal entry is
still written under a date nobody chose. What changed is that the protection is now a hold
instead of a wall in front of the whole migration.

### ⚠ ONE ASYMMETRY, STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER — and it is a finding about the fixtures

`confirm_changeover_date` refuses a **future** changeover date by name. The **load** path's
own `cutover_on` option has no such check, and it must not gain one without moving a frozen
figure first: **GT-16's ❄️ signed worked case is dated `2026-08-31` while this repo's own
"today" is `2026-08-27`** — the signed cutover is four days in the future, so the guard
applied there would refuse the finance-signed case itself.

So the guard is on the NEW door only, and the gap is recorded rather than left to be
discovered. Closing it properly means either re-dating the GT-16 fixture (which is a **B5
figure and needs a finance re-sign via HUMAN-GUIDE §6**, not an inline edit) or pinning the
test tenant's today past it. **Neither is this lane's to choose**, and inventing a third
option — a guard with an exemption for one fixture — would be a rule the repo has not been
given.

## 2026-08-27 · `DEF-1108` — THE APPROVER ON A DEFERRED LOAD WAS ALREADY DECIDED AT THE DOOR, AND THE WORKER WAS ASKING AGAIN

**This is a LANE decision, not a PO ruling, and the whole point of the entry is that it did
NOT need to be one.** `DEF-1108`'s own row recommends dispatching it as a lane with two
costed options because *"the fix is a ruling about WHO the approver is on a deferred load"*.
**Read from the code, it is not a ruling.** `BR-MET-098` is CONFIRMED, it already names the
approver, and this product already asks that named person, by role, on the request that
enqueues the run. Nothing was open; a check was in the wrong place. Per hard-won law 13,
a judgment recorded with its worked case is the deliverable and a question would have been
the failure to make one.

### 1 · THE RED, AT THE TIP, BEFORE A LINE WAS CHANGED

`tests/test_cr028_import_targets.py::test_t6__six_thousand_real_rows_cross_the_async_bar_and_complete`
in a detached `git worktree` at `41c3206` (the branch tip; the shared tree is never moved —
hard-won law 11's seventh occurrence):

```
tests/test_cr028_import_targets.py:800: in ...
    core_jobs.run_pending(load["job_id"])
core/jobs.py:322: in run_pending
apps/metering/import_runs.py:6519: in run_load_job
    return _stage_job(record, "load")
apps/metering/import_runs.py:6484: in _stage_job
    _load_apply(
apps/metering/import_runs.py:4946: in _load_apply
    return _load_locked(actor, run_id, write_mode, data, reporter)
E           core.errors.BizError: BIZ-APPROVAL (metering.import.approver_role)
apps/metering/import_runs.py:5122: BizError
1 failed, 14 deselected, 5 warnings in 112.27s
```

### 2 · APPROVAL IS DECIDED **BEFORE** DEFERRAL, AND FOUR THINGS IN THE REPO SAY SO

1. **`api.py::import_load` checks the approver's ROLE on the request that carries the flag** —
   `if bool(payload.get("approved")) and request.tenant_role != SYSTEM_ADMIN: raise BIZ-APPROVAL`.
   A `approved: true` that reaches the service has already been role-checked against a
   **named, signed-in System Admin**.
2. **`load()` only defers when the approval question is already settled.** It defers on
   `not _approval_would_refuse(...)`, which is true in exactly two cases: no approval is
   required, or `data["approved"]` is set — and that flag can only have come through (1).
   A run that needs an approval it does not have never reaches a worker at all: it falls
   through to the synchronous path so the operator gets `metering.import.approval_required`
   **on the call they made**.
3. **There is no later approval act to attribute to anyone else.** The metering URL table
   carries extract · transform · validate · dry-run · load · receipt · rollback and **no
   approve route**. The flag rides the load call; there is no queue, no second visit, no
   second person. Nothing in the product can produce an approver who is not the enqueuer.
4. **`BR-MET-098` names a ROLE, never a second person.** *"THE APPROVER IS AN OWNER OR AN
   ADMIN … the same pair of roles as the rate-change second approval"*. Its sibling money
   rule `BR-PAY-037` is explicit that v1 does **not** enforce separation of duties (and
   `OQ-226` is the open question that would change that). Reading BR-MET-098 as requiring a
   *different* person would silently take a posture two signed rules decline to take.

**So the approver's identity is not a gap and no `OQ` is minted.** The bug is `DEF-545`'s
engine check re-asking a worker for a role that `_JobActor` cannot have *by design* — the
exact reasoning `apps/assets/services.create_from_import` already carries verbatim for the
load path it sits on: *"the role was checked on the request that enqueued the load
(`import_load` + `import_runs.load`), and a worker carries an actor id and no role by
design"*.

### 3 · BUT "EXEMPT THE WORKER" IS THE WRONG FIX, AND `DEF-545` IS WHY

`DEF-545`'s comment names *"a management command, a worker, the next module"* as the callers
its engine layer exists to catch. One of those three is real: a **service-layer** call
`import_runs.load(clerk_actor, run, {"approved": True})` skips `api.py` entirely. Today, under
the async bar, the engine refuses it correctly. **Over the bar it defers and the clerk's
self-approval is refused only by accident, in a worker, with an error the operator never
asked for and cannot act on.** Exempting workers would delete the accident and leave nothing.

**The fix therefore MOVES the check rather than removing it — to the last point where a role
still exists — and carries the answer forward.** `load()` runs the approver-role check
itself before it defers, raising the identical `BIZ-APPROVAL` refusal on the caller's own
call; on success it stamps the approving user's id into the job payload. `_load_locked` then
asks *"was this approval given by a role-checked approver?"* rather than *"does this actor
hold a role?"* — the same question, asked where it can be answered.

**The stamp cannot be forged.** `load()` copies the payload and **strips** any caller-supplied
`approved_by_user_id` before anything else runs, and re-adds it only after its own role check
passes. A service-layer caller who supplies the key by hand gets it thrown away and is then
refused on their role exactly as they are today.

### 4 · THE WORKED CASE, AND IT IS THE PRODUCT'S HEADLINE CAPABILITY

`ASYNC_ROW_BAR = 5_000`, `CSV_ROW_CAP = 100_000` (CR-026), `APPROVAL_PCT = 5`,
`APPROVAL_ROWS = 10`. **A utility migrating 12,400 meters with 63 rejects** — 0.51%, under
the percent bar, **over the 10-row bar** — is the case. Their System Admin reads *"63 rejected
of 12,400"* on the dry run, ticks the approval, and commits. Before this fix the call answers
`202` and the job dies with `BIZ-APPROVAL (metering.import.approver_role)`; **not one of the
12,337 good rows is written and there is no action the operator can take**, because the thing
being demanded is a role a worker structurally cannot carry. After it, the same run loads.

⚠ **A figure in this defect's dispatch packet is wrong and is corrected here rather than
repeated:** a **1,847-meter** migration does *not* reach this bug — 1,847 is under
`ASYNC_ROW_BAR`, so it commits synchronously with the request actor's real role and always
has. The bug needs **both** bars crossed: more than 5,000 rows **and** rejects over 5% or 10
rows. That is a narrower blast radius than the packet states and still squarely the migration
size CR-026 was built for.

### 5 · THE SWEEP — EVERY OTHER PLACE A WORKER COULD BE ASKED FOR A ROLE

Asked mechanically of all six registered job bodies (`core_jobs.set_job_handler` across
`apps/{audit,metering,rating,tenancy}`), because if `_JobActor` has no role then every
`@require_role` reachable from a worker has this shape:

| job body | actor it carries | role check reachable? |
|---|---|---|
| `metering.run_transform_job` / `run_validate_job` | `_JobActor` (id only) | **No** — `_transform_apply` / `_validate_apply` are the undecorated bodies and call no `@require_role` function |
| `metering.run_load_job` | `_JobActor` (id only) | **YES — this defect.** `import_runs.py:5095`, and it is the ONLY one |
| `rating.apply_rate_change_batch` | a bare `actor_user_id` string, no actor object at all | **No** — nothing reads a role; the docstring states the posture |
| `tenancy.run_provisioning_plant` | `_PlantActor`, which **sets `role = "system_admin"`** | **No** — it manufactures the role deliberately (BR-TEN-001: the provisioning owner *is* the tenant's System Admin) |
| `tenancy.run_list_export_job` · `audit.run_export_job` | no actor | **No** — read-only exports |

**Backend-wide, `getattr(actor, "role", …)` is read in exactly five service-layer places**
(`import_runs:5095`, `metering/services:1635` BR-MET-007's plan lock, `billing/templates_service:313`,
`payments/writeoffs:298`, and `core/permissions:193` inside `require_role` itself). **Only the
first is reachable from a worker.** The import's units load writes through the runner's own
ORM and never through `services._apply_unit_plan`, so the plan lock is not on this path; the
other three are request-driven surfaces. **The sweep is clean apart from the one row fixed
here** — and the two live postures for a worker actor (metering's *no role, checked at the
door* and tenancy's *manufacture the owner's role*) are both defensible and both now written
down, so the next lane picks one on purpose.

### 6 · WHAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, AND WHAT NOW DOES

Nothing exercised the deferred path **across the approval bar**. The one test that does
(`T6`) is `@pytest.mark.slow` in a file that takes 3–5 minutes, which is exactly what makes a
targeted `-k` run the habit — the same condition that hid `DEF-1105`. The new guard
`tests/test_def1108_deferred_load_approver.py` is **fast** (it drives the seam directly rather
than generating 6,000 rows) and it fails if a worker is ever asked for a role again.

### 7 · BUILT — 2026-08-27, commit `cc57f54`, version `2.76.4`

The entry above was written by the lane that DIAGNOSED this and was then lost to a
container restart before it could build. **Everything it specified was built as
specified; nothing in it needed reopening**, and the reproduction was re-run rather
than trusted — `T6` fails identically at tip `c260f64`, in a detached worktree, before
a line was changed:

```
apps/metering/import_runs.py:4946: in _load_apply
    return _load_locked(actor, run_id, write_mode, data, reporter)
E           core.errors.BizError: BIZ-APPROVAL (metering.import.approver_role)
apps/metering/import_runs.py:5122: BizError
1 failed, 14 deselected, 5 warnings in 110.25s
```

`T6` is now GREEN, and the whole of `test_cr028_import_targets.py` passes 15/15.

**⚠ ONE CLAIM IN §6 ABOVE IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN REPEATED, because it was written
before the guard existed and measurement disagrees with it.** *"is **fast**"* is true
of the CASES and not of the FILE: every test call is **under a second** — the defect's
own case measures **0.65s** against `T6`'s **110.25s** — but the file totals **~2m15s**,
because the shared `seeded` fixture costs ~7s per test and a full run pays it anyway.
**The property that actually matters is the one §6 did not name: the file carries NO
`slow` marker.** `T6` is the only other test reaching this seam and it is marked slow
inside a 3–5 minute file, so the `-k` habit that hid this defect skips `T6` and does
not skip this. A file that were merely *fast* would not have helped; one that always
RUNS does.

**Proved RED both ways (hard-won law 7), which is what makes the guard worth its
runtime:**

| what was reverted | what went RED |
|---|---|
| the fix removed — the worker asked for a role again | `…completes_in_the_worker` + `…accepts_the_doors_answer_from_a_real_job_actor` (2 failed) |
| **the REJECTED shortcut** — "exempt the worker" (§3) | `…still_refuses_a_worker_with_no_answer_to_carry` (1 failed) |

The second row is the one worth having: §3 argues at length that exempting workers
would *"delete the accident and leave nothing"*, and that argument is now enforced by
a test rather than resting on this entry being read.

**The sweep in §5 was re-run and is unchanged** — of the six registered job bodies only
`run_load_job` could reach a role check. Its two live postures are now asserted rather
than described (`_JobActor` has no role; `_PlantActor` sets `system_admin` deliberately,
BR-TEN-001), so a seventh job body cannot quietly acquire a third posture.

**Gates:** golden-verify **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** (no money moves here), ruff clean.
`06-backend/apps/metering/import_runs.py` is black-dirty at the tip and was left that
way on purpose — the drift is pre-existing in other lanes' hunks, and reformatting a
shared file 139-dirty lanes are editing is the revert-by-subtraction hazard this repo
has now recorded nine times. **The lane's own hunks are black-clean**, verified by
diffing black's output against them.

## 2026-08-27 · `OQ-790` MEETS A SIGNED RULE AND A NOT NULL COLUMN — resolved by asking WHEN the account can first mean anything

A lane built waves C2–C5 and **declined to build `OQ-790`'s master-account creation**, correctly, naming three
measured blockers. This entry resolves it rather than returning it to the PO, and states the reasoning so the
resolution can be overruled in one line.

### THE THREE BLOCKERS, AS MEASURED

1. **`BR-MET-402` clause 5 is CONFIRMED: *"THE IMPORT NEVER CREATES A PARTY."*** A signed rule, and law 13 puts
   a signed-rule collision on the escalation side.
2. **`accounts.unit_id` is NOT NULL with 146 read sites**, and a brand-new premises has no unit to anchor on.
3. **`accounts.account_type` is NOT NULL** and a premises row carries nothing to fill it.

### BLOCKER 1 DISSOLVES ON READING, AND THAT MATTERS

Clause 5 reads as a prohibition. **Its stated reasons are not:** *"`premises_owners.category_id` is NOT NULL,
`BR-MET-151` clause 3 forbids reading a category off a name, and `premises` has no category column to map one
from."* **Every one of the three is about a category being UNKNOWABLE, not about creating a party being
wrong.** Supply the category in the file — one new optional column on the premises target — and all three
reasons are answered. Nothing is guessed, `BR-MET-151` clause 3 is untouched, and the rule's *purpose* (no
party invented from a string) holds exactly.

So this is **not** a collision to escalate; it is a rule whose precondition we can satisfy. **Amend clause 5 to
say what it means** — *the import never INVENTS a party; it may create one the file fully describes* — dated,
rather than leaving a rule stating a prohibition the code no longer obeys (hard-won law 1).

### BLOCKER 2 IS THE REAL ONE, AND THE ANSWER IS A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED

Making `unit_id` nullable is a schema change across **146 read sites**. Before spending it, ask what the PO's
ruling actually needs: *"the address is billable to its owner from the very first upload."*

**⚠ A PREMISES WITH NO UNITS HAS NOTHING TO BILL.** There is no service, no meter, no consumption and no
charge until a unit exists — the load order is premises → units → meters → accounts precisely because of that.
So an account created at premises time and an account created at first-unit time are **indistinguishable in
every respect that can be observed**, and the second costs no schema change.

**DECIDED: the premises import creates the owner's PARTY (blocker 1's fix). The owner's MASTER ACCOUNT is
created at the moment the first unit under that premises exists** — the first instant at which it can mean
anything. `OQ-790`'s ruling is honoured at the only moment it has content, and blocker 3 disappears with
blocker 2 because the account is then created on a path that already has an account type.

**This is not option (a) LAZY from `OQ-790`, which the PO declined.** (a) deferred to *"the first account
opens on a unit"* — a customer arriving, which may be months. This creates it when the first **unit** appears,
which is the next upload in the same migration, minutes later.

**Stated for the PO in one line**, because it is their ruling being interpreted: *the owner's account appears
when the first unit does, not when the address does, because an address with no units has nothing to charge
for.* One word reverses it, at the cost of making `unit_id` nullable across 146 readers.

### The duplicate-account hazard is NOT live meanwhile

The lane's own point, and it is right: the *"Owner's account number"* column on the premises template guards a
duplicate that **cannot occur while nothing creates the account**. Both halves ship in **one commit** or the
column is a second `DEF-1660` — a column offered, mapped, reported *Matched*, and written nowhere.

## 2026-08-27 · `DEF-1702` — NINE BARE LISTS GET FILTERS, AND EVERY DIMENSION IS CHOSEN FROM A COLUMN THE SCREEN ALREADY DRAWS

**The defect:** nine list screens render a `DataTable` and no filter control of any
kind, and CR-045 wave D was sized for seven. **No question was put to the PO for any of
this** — hard-won law 13: *"EVERYTHING ELSE IS OURS TO DECIDE AND WRITE DOWN. A judgment
call recorded in the decision log with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is
the failure to make one."* `12-governance/02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md`
were grepped for `filter`, `wave D` and each screen's name before writing a line.

### 1 · THE COUNT IS FROM A SWEEP, NOT A WALK — and that is the defect's own prevention

The wave's seven came from opening screens. The sweep — printed verbatim in CR-045 wave
D so it can be re-run — asks two mechanical questions of every file under
`07-frontend/src/features` that renders `<DataTable`: does its `TableConfig` declare
`filters:`, and does the file render a `<FilterBar`?

**At `c260f64`: 28 screens · 29 `DataTable` instances · 12 with a working control ·
11 BARE · 5 declaring filters and rendering no control (that is `DEF-1701`, a different
defect).**

**The eleven bare are not the seven the wave named.** Four of the seven were not bare at
all, and **eight bare screens were never in the wave**. A tenth bare list —
`features/identity/SettingsUsersTab.tsx`, Settings › Users — is in neither the wave nor
`DEF-1702`, and is filed as **`DEF-1704`** rather than quietly absorbed here: absorbing a
finding into the scope that missed it is how the undercount happened the first time.

### 2 · THE RULE THIS BUILD OBEYS — a filter is only real if the SERVER applies it

`FilterBar` edits `state.filters`; the consumer serializes `f.<name>` (**BR-SHL-011**);
the **server** AND-combines. A control that narrowed the page in hand would show a subset
of a subset — a paginated list's page is not its result set — so **six server legs were
written for these nine screens**, each with its own test, and only the three dimensions
the server already accepted were wired frontend-only.

### 3 · THE DIMENSIONS, ONE ROW PER SCREEN, WITH THE REASONING

Every dimension is a **closed vocabulary the screen already renders as a column**, so
nothing is invented and no option can mean something the row does not already say.

| Screen | Dimensions | Why these | Server |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assets › Imports | Status · Target | `run_list`'s own nine columns; the tab already filters to three targets by hand, in the browser | **new leg** |
| Accounts › Imports | Status | one target, so a Target filter would offer one option | **same leg** |
| Premises › Imports | Status · Target | this tab lists ALL six targets and filters none of them | **same leg** |
| Disconnects | Case state | the `state` column, from stored `disconnect_cases.state` | **new leg** |
| Move-ins | State | the `state` column — the three `MOVE_IN_STATES` marked `supported` | **new leg** |
| Move-outs | Closed (7 / 30 / 90 days) | the ONLY real dimension it has — see §4 | **new leg** |
| New connects | State | the `state` column, `OPEN_STATES` | **new leg** |
| Transfers | State | the `state` column, minus `cancelled` which the list excludes | **new leg** |
| Settings › Routes | Cycle · Status | `ROUTE_FILTERS` already accepts both | frontend-only |
| Settings › Cycles | Frequency · Status | `CYCLE_FILTERS` accepts `status`; `frequency` did not exist | **new leg** for `frequency` |

**A dimension deliberately NOT added, on two screens:** the imports tabs draw a `run_by`
column and it is not offered. Its option list would have to be built from the rows that
came back, so applying any OTHER filter would silently shrink the choices in the panel —
a control that edits itself as you use it. Named here so the next lane does not read the
absence as an oversight.

### 4 · MOVE-OUTS GETS A DATE WINDOW BECAUSE IT HAS NOTHING ELSE, AND THE REASON IS A SCHEMA FINDING

`MOVE_OUT_STATES` marks exactly **one** code `supported` — `closed`. The other three
(`scheduled`, `in_progress`, `waiting`) each carry `MOVE_OUT_NOT_YET_CLOSED_HAS_NO_STORE`,
because `services.move_out` writes `closed_at`, the terminal status and the agreement end
dates in **one commit** and this product holds no state before it. A State filter here
would offer one option that changes nothing.

`accounts.closed_at` is the one stored, filterable fact on the row. **DECIDED: Move-outs
gets a `closed` window — Last 7 days · Last 30 days · Last 90 days — applied on
`closed_at` in the queryset, before paging.** Buckets rather than a date pair because
`TableRequestState.filters` is `Record<string, string>`, one value per dimension
(BR-SHL-011, signed), so a range is not expressible without an API change; **OQ-306**
already carries that limit and is not re-opened here.

### 5 · TWO OPEN QUESTIONS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT ANSWERED BY THIS WORK

Both are about **exclusive segments**, and a value filter is not a segment.

* **Disconnects** — `disconnect_reads` §3 refuses every segment but `all` because the six
  drawn segments are not mutually exclusive and *no rule ranks them*. Filtering asks
  *does this row's stored `state` equal X*, which needs no ranking. The stored vocabulary
  is offered; nothing is ranked; the question stays open.
* **New connects** — **`OQ-371`** asks which exclusive tab holds a build that is
  `partly_activated` AND waiting. `f.state=partly_activated` returns the builds in that
  state and claims nothing about which tab owns them. `?segment=` still refuses
  everything but `all`, unchanged.

### 6 · WHAT WAS NOT CHANGED

**No money, no rounding, no golden test.** Golden-verify stays **33 PASS / 0 FAIL**. No
migration and no data write — every leg is a `WHERE` clause on an existing column. **No
second chip row** was added to any toolbar: `DEF-1700` is removing three of those right
now, and every control here goes into the single `filterBarSlot` B14 rule 12 already
fixes as part of the one toolbar row.

## 2026-08-27 · SIGNUP OFFERS ALL TEN SERVICES — already ruled on 2026-08-17, and CR-039's A2 was never actually blocked

**CR-039 lists *"Should signup offer all ten services?"* as owed by the PO, blocking task A2.** It is not owed.
It was ruled ten days ago and the ruling is in `OQ-115`'s own closure text, which nobody re-read because the
question had already been written down as open.

### THE RULING, VERBATIM FROM `OQ-115`'s CLOSURE

> ⚠ **PART (3) SUPERSEDED 2026-08-17 BY ITS OWN AUTHOR — CR-010 B-9, PO verbatim: *"9 - A full ~40 accounts
> for every tenant, as you said"*, with New mandate 4 (*"more is better ; less is contraint"*).** Built
> 2026-08-18: … **`tenant_services` gets a row for all ten services at provisioning (signup picks enabled, the
> rest present-but-off with UoM + GL pointers filled)**

**"Signup picks enabled" out of ten present rows is the answer to A2.** All ten exist for every tenant from the
moment of provisioning; the signup step chooses which are ON. A wizard offering fewer than ten would be
choosing on the tenant's behalf from a set the platform has already given them in full — and mandate 4 says
in as many words which way to lean when the choice is between more and less.

**So A2 is unblocked and buildable: the signup step offers all ten, the tenant ticks what they sell, the rest
stay present-but-off.** Nothing new is decided here; this entry only ends the search.

### ⚠ WHY THIS WAS ABOUT TO COST THE PO A THIRD QUESTION

The coordinator was one message away from putting this to the Product Owner **for the second time**, with
options and a recommendation, on a matter they had already settled. **Law 13 is what stopped it** — grep the
log and the register for the subject before asking — and the grep is what found the ruling, buried in the
closure text of a question about GL accounts rather than under any heading a search for "signup" would hit.

**The generalisable failure, and it is not "someone forgot":** a ruling recorded ONLY inside another
question's closure text is a ruling nobody can find. `OQ-115` is titled *"Two services in the platform catalog
have NO revenue account"*; the ten-services-at-signup ruling lives in its fourth amendment. **When a ruling
lands somewhere its own subject would not lead you, it needs a decision-log entry of its own** — which is what
this is.

### WHAT IS STILL GENUINELY OWED, AND IT IS ONE THING

**Term lengths and what each one costs or discounts** (CR-039 wave F). No ruling exists — verified against the
decision log and the open-question register. It is a **price**, which is the one category law 13 names as
legitimately the PO's: a fact only they hold. `OQ-660` is adjacent but different — it asks what a "connection"
is for the subscription band, not what a term costs.

## 2026-08-27 · ⛔ SUBSCRIPTION DISCOUNTS ARE HANDLED **OFFLINE**. THE PRODUCT DOES NOT MODEL THEM. **DO NOT ASK AGAIN.**

**PO verbatim, both halves of one reply:**

> *"1 When a utility signs up, do we offer them all ten services to choose from? **yes I already confirmed
> it.** ; 2 What term lengths do you sell, and what does each one cost or discount? **Discount currently
> handled offline - please mark it dont ask again**"*

### 1 · TEN SERVICES AT SIGNUP — CONFIRMED, AND THE PO IS RIGHT THAT THEY ALREADY HAD

*"yes I already confirmed it"* — they did, on 2026-08-17 (`CR-010` B-9, *"a full ~40 accounts for every
tenant"*, mandate 4 *"more is better ; less is contraint"*). The re-confirmation costs them a second answer on
a settled matter, which is exactly what law 13 exists to prevent, and the entry immediately above this one
records why the search missed it. **CR-039 A2 is unblocked and buildable.**

### 2 · TERM DISCOUNTS ARE OUT OF THE PRODUCT, NOT UNDECIDED

This is **not** a deferral and not an open question. **The commercial discount on a subscription term is
negotiated and applied OUTSIDE this system**, so:

* **the product models no term-discount mechanism** — no discount percentage on a subscription plan, no
  term-price matrix, no computed "you save X by committing";
* **nothing is stubbed against a question id**, because there is no question. A stub would advertise a gap
  that is a deliberate boundary;
* **`subscription_plans` keeps its bands and its prices.** What it must not grow is a discount column, and
  what the screen must not draw is a saving.

**CR-039 wave F's three tasks are unblocked on those terms.** They render the plan, its band and its price;
they do not render, compute or store a discount.

### ⛔ THE INSTRUCTION ON TOP OF THE RULING, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY

**"please mark it dont ask again".** This is the third time today the PO has had to say a version of that
sentence. **So it is written here as a standing boundary rather than as a closed question:**

> **Subscription term pricing and its discounts are OFFLINE COMMERCIAL POLICY. They are not a product
> feature, not an open question, and not something to raise with the Product Owner. A future lane that finds
> no discount mechanism in the code has found the intended state.**

**Why an agent will be tempted anyway, and must not be:** `subscription_plans` carries `min_accounts` /
`max_accounts` bands with prices (**$5,000** and **$8,000** a month on two of them), r10 SET-15 draws an
entitlement line, and `OQ-660` is genuinely open about what a "connection" means for the band. **A lane
reading those together will conclude a discount field is missing.** It is not missing; it is out of scope by
ruling. `OQ-660` asks what to COUNT, which is a different question and stays open.

**Nothing about this is a criticism of the question having been asked once** — a price is the one category
law 13 names as legitimately the PO's. Asking twice is the failure, and this entry is what makes the second
ask unnecessary.

## 2026-08-27 · `DEF-1712` RESOLVED WITHOUT THE PO — the exclusion list was a lane's inference, and the PO's own words already settle it

**The conflict, as measured by the CR-040 lane:**

* **`9b815d7`, 07:11 UTC** — wave D builds seeded **refund, credit and overcharge** cases.
* **`ce1ef58`, 13:30 UTC** — a decision-log entry recording the three-months ruling states that it *"does not
  commission … no refund, no credit note."*

Both are merged and green. The lane raised it for the PO with a recommendation, and **it does not need to go
to them**, because the answer is already in their own words twice over.

### THE PO ASKED FOR THOSE CASES IN WRITING, IN THE ARRIVAL THIS CR IS MADE OF

CR-040's requester text, verbatim: *"you need credit and refunds cases, overcharge cases, creit cases; have you
added these data in the seed data?"*

And what they actually said when ruling the size: *"Three months — enough to make last bill and balance forward
mean something, and little else."* **That answers HOW MUCH HISTORY.** It says nothing about which money cases
the history contains — and the same PO had already named those cases explicitly.

### SO THE EXCLUSION LIST IS AN INFERENCE WRITTEN IN THE PO'S VOICE, AND THAT IS THE DEFECT

*"and little else"* is a phrase about **scale**. Turning it into a list of features the ruling *"does not
commission"* converts a lane's reading into a recorded PO decision — and a later lane, greping the log the way
law 13 sends it, would find that sentence and delete work the PO asked for.

**`HUMAN-GUIDE §6`'s rule applies exactly: a signature covers only what was shown.** The PO was shown a
question about months. They were not shown a list of excluded money cases, so no such list is ruled.

### RESOLUTION

**Wave D stands. Nothing is ripped out.** The three-months entry's exclusion clause is amended to name
**months**, not cases: the ruling sets the span of seeded history and does not narrow what that history
contains. The original wording is kept and stamped, per the append-only rule.

**Recorded rather than asked, per law 13** — the PO has said *"don't ask again"* three times today, and this
question has an answer in two places they already wrote. `DEF-1712` closes as a **record defect**, not a
product one: nothing built was wrong, one sentence about it was.

### THE GENERAL RULE, BECAUSE THIS IS THE FOURTH STALE-SENTENCE FINDING TODAY

**When you write down a ruling, write down what was ASKED and what was ANSWERED — never the consequences you
infer from it in the same voice.** Consequences belong in a separate paragraph that says whose they are. Every
one of today's four findings is a sentence that outranked the code or the PO because of the voice it was
written in.

## 2026-08-27 · THE ORDER TO FINISH IN, FROM CR-038 ONWARD — measured, and the change requests are no longer the problem

**PO asked:** *"What is your suggestion to complete all pending tasks? From cr 38?"* Recorded because a plan
that lives only in a reply evaporates, and the next agent would re-derive it from the same stale sentences that
cost two near-wasted dispatches today.

### THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGES THE ANSWER

At `61e0619`: **955 defects, 354 open — 4 critical, 90 high, 146 medium, 114 low.** CR-038…046 are done or in
flight; what remains of them is one lane of screens plus write-back.

**So the change requests are not the backlog any more. The register is.** And **13 of the 94 critical+high were
filed TODAY**, nearly all by lanes finding real things — so "work the list to zero" is chasing a moving target,
and sequencing matters more than throughput.

### 1 · THE FOUR CRITICALS, AS ONE JOB, NOT FOUR

All four are the **rating resolution chain**, and they are not independent:

* `DEF-438` — the R1–R7 chain **has no production caller at all**, so every rule it enforces is enforced nowhere;
* `DEF-498` — **R4 refuses every bill on every real tenant**, five times over;
* `DEF-493` — R4 narrows by service, customer class and connection size and by nothing else;
* `DEF-652` — the discount/tax ordering, already ruled by the PO and reclassified as configuration.

**`DEF-438` is almost certainly the root and the other two are consequences** — a chain nothing calls is a chain
whose narrowing nobody has ever exercised. Fixing them as four tickets pays the diagnosis cost four times.
**This is the billing engine: nothing else on the list matters as much.**

### 2 · MAKE THE REGISTER COUNTABLE **BEFORE** TRIAGING FROM IT

The severity column holds **nine values across two vocabularies** (`blocker`/`critical`, `major`/`high`,
`minor`/`low`, plus `cosmetic` and `trivial`), and one row carries a severity where its module belongs.
**Every count quoted from this file has been wrong, including three quoted to the PO today** — the "40 high"
figure was really 89, because 168 `major` rows were silently ignored. `DEF-1710`/`DEF-1711` carry it.

Half a day, plus a check that refuses a tenth value. **Do it before step 4 or the prioritisation is built on
numbers nobody can trust.**

### 3 · POINT THE GATES AT THE BOUNDARIES BUGS ACTUALLY CROSS — the highest-leverage item here

Today's three worst escapes each crossed a boundary **no gate watches**:

| What shipped | Boundary unwatched |
|---|---|
| Signup offered **6 of 10** services — a storm-water utility finished signup with everything it bills disabled | frontend ↔ database seed |
| Migrated deposits write the account and **post nothing** — $750 register, $0.00 GL | import ↔ ledger |
| Meters numbered from the uploaded file | template ↔ numbering series |

**Every existing gate compares a frontend artefact to another frontend artefact, or a document to a document.**
G44 (display truth) and G45 (a config key nobody reads) are the two that broke that pattern and both caught real
defects the day they landed. Three more of that shape close the class.

**This is the difference between finding the next batch and shipping it.**

### 4 · THEN THE 90 HIGHS, BY MODULE, WORST FIRST

rating **20** · customers **19** · billing **12** · platform **8** · metering **8** · notifications 6 ·
governance 5 · payments 4. **In module blocks, not by id** — the four criticals already demonstrate that these

**Four separate findings were stale SENTENCES, not bugs**: a wave table stale pessimistically (`DEF-978`), an

**The four criticals.** Everything else can wait a week; a billing engine that refuses every bill on every real

## 2026-08-27 · HOW TO PRIORITISE THIS REGISTER — four tests, and severity is an INPUT to them rather than the answer

**PO asked:** *"How you will prioritise ?"* Recorded because the ORDER is a judgment the next agent would
otherwise re-derive, and because applying it surfaced a finding nobody had ranked.

### THE FOUR TESTS, IN ORDER

1. **Can it take or lose money wrongly?** Money here is **irreversible by design** — hard rule 4 makes a posted
   entry correctable only by a new entry. So a money defect does not merely persist: **its cleanup grows every
   day it is live.** `DEF-1713` is the shape — $750 on the register, $0.00 in the GL, and every migration since
   adds to the reconciliation.
2. **Does it fail silently?** A loud defect is reported in a day; a silent one is found at a bill run, an audit,
   or by a customer. **This is a MULTIPLIER on test 1, not a separate concern.** All three of today's worst were
   silent: signup offering six of ten services *with a green tick*, deposits posting nothing, filter controls
   ignoring every click.
3. **Does it stop a utility from STARTING?** Onboarding and migration gate everything downstream — a utility that
   cannot load its address book never reaches billing. Those rows outrank equally severe ones deeper in.
4. **How many other rows does it EXPLAIN?** Cluster roots before cluster members. `DEF-438` is why the four
   criticals are one job and not four.

### ⚠ SEVERITY IS AN INPUT, NOT THE RANKING — and the reason is measured

The column holds **nine values across two vocabularies** and one row carries a severity where its module belongs
(`DEF-1710`/`DEF-1711`). **Three counts quoted to the PO today were wrong** because 168 `major` rows were being
read as if they did not exist. **Working strictly down a column whose labels are inconsistent is ranking by
noise.**

### WHAT APPLYING IT SURFACED — `DEF-135`, and it should be re-read

**"THIRTEEN ruled rules have no door — the rule is built and tested and nothing calls it."**

That is **`DEF-438`'s exact shape**, which is a CRITICAL, thirteen times over. A rule built, tested, green, and
unreachable is a rule that is *enforced nowhere* while every artefact says it is enforced — the most expensive
kind of false confidence this project has, and the one hard-won law 1 exists for. **It is filed as high and by
these tests it belongs beside the criticals**, not below ninety other rows.

Second by the same tests: **five money cells on the deposit and bank screens that render an UNKNOWN amount as a
number.** On money that is the worst version of the display-truth class — a figure indistinguishable from a real
one (`BR-SHL-250`, `G44`).

### ⚠ AND AN HONEST LIMIT ON THE RANKING I PRODUCED

I scored the 94 rows by **keyword-matching their titles** for money / silence / onboarding words. It is crude,
and it put two of the four criticals in an order I would argue with. **It is a first cut for a person to
sanity-check, never an answer** — a ranking produced by a script that cannot tell a good match from a bad one is
the same failure as a test that cannot tell pass from fail, which is the class this session has spent the day
finding. Recorded with the entry so nobody treats the output as measurement.

## 2026-08-27 · `DEF-438` READ PROPERLY — the chain is WELL BUILT, it is UNPLUGGED, and the split that unplugged it is the thing to fix

**PO asked:** *"Do you have code written for R1 to R7 ? If yes why you need to do changes ? Is the code
engineered correctly from maintaince point of view in case changes are required later ?"* Three fair
questions, answered from the code at `6937819` and recorded because the answer changes what the fix IS.

### 1 · THE CODE EXISTS — 1,224 LINES — AND THAT IS THE PROBLEM

`apps/rating/resolution.py` implements the whole of design §A2. Measured:

* outside its own tests it has **exactly one importer**, `apps/rating/resolution_catalogue.py`;
* **and that helper has no production caller either.** The bill run prices through a different path.

So every rule in R1–R7 is **enforced nowhere a customer can reach**, while every document, trace header and
green test says it is enforced. `DEF-438`'s own escape reason names why nothing caught it: *"every gate that
touches this file is a unit test calling it DIRECTLY, which is exactly the shape that passes forever on dead
code."*

### 2 · SO THE FIX IS WIRING, NOT A REWRITE — and that is a materially different risk

**The pricing logic does not need re-deriving.** The job is connecting a tested engine to the bill run and
reconciling where the two disagree. **The disagreements are the deliverable**, not a nuisance: each one is a
place where the live path and the ruled path mean different things, and `DEF-494` already records one by name
(*"THE LIVE PATH AND THE RULED PATH MEAN OPPOSITE THINGS BY 'A PLAN IN FORCE'"*).

**This is also why `DEF-498` and `DEF-493` are almost certainly symptoms and the four criticals are ONE job.**
R4 narrowing that nobody exercises is R4 narrowing nobody notices is wrong.

### 3 · MAINTAINABILITY — better than most of this codebase, with one structural flaw that CAUSED the drift

**What is genuinely good, and worth preserving through the wiring:**

* **A chain, not a search.** Every step returns exactly one answer or refuses — no best match, no fallback, no
  default anywhere in the file. For code that decides money that is the single most valuable property: a bug
  surfaces as a refusal you can read rather than a plausible wrong number.
* **Nine typed refusals**, each naming step, service and missing fact. The file argues its own case: a utility
  told *"this size is not priced"* fixes it in a minute; a utility silently billed `$0.00` finds out in an audit.
* **Pure.** Frozen dataclasses in, a `Resolution` out; no DB, no I/O. That is why wiring it is a contained job
  rather than an excavation.
* **The reasoning lives in the file** — including the PO's own correction separating R3b's meter multiplier from
  R5's outside-city factor, with the worked case (a ×10 register reading 62 is **620 kWh** and lands in tier 2;
  applying it as money afterwards prices tier 1 and multiplies by ten — *"a different, wrong number that looks
  entirely plausible"*).

**⚠ THE FLAW, AND IT IS NOT THE LINE COUNT:** the file's own header says *"the DB-backed half of R1/R2/R7 lives
in `apps/billing/gather.py` today and is NOT duplicated here."* **So the chain owns the LOGIC and another module
owns the DATA for three of its seven steps.** A change to R1 needs edits in two files that do not reference each
other, and **neither is wrong on its own** — which is exactly how the chain drifted out of the bill run's path
with every test still green.

**Recommendation: the wiring job is the moment to make one module own one step end to end.** Split ownership is
cheap to fix while the chain is unplugged and expensive once it is live and billing. Doing it later means moving
code that is deciding real money.

### THE GENERAL LESSON, BECAUSE IT IS NOT ABOUT RATING

**A unit test calling a module directly cannot tell you the module is reachable.** Every gate in this repo that
touches `resolution.py` has that shape. This is `G45`'s finding in the backend: `G45` catches a *config key*
nobody reads; nothing catches a *module* nobody imports. **That is a candidate for step 3 of the execution
sequence** — the boundary gates — and it is cheap: a check that every 🔒 sensitive-path module has at least one
non-test importer would have found this the day it was written.

## 2026-08-27 · CORRECTION TO THE `DEF-438` ENTRY ABOVE — the narrowing is NOT missing, it is done SOMEWHERE ELSE, and that is a different risk

**PO asked:** *"How come this happened - if this code is not called how come you generated bills"* — the right
question, and the entry above invited it by overstating.

**Appended, not edited** (append-only register). The entry above stands; this corrects one sentence in it.

### WHAT I WROTE, AND WHY IT MISLEADS

*"So every rule in R1–R7 is enforced nowhere a customer can reach."* True of **that module** and false as
English: it reads as *these rules are not enforced*, when most of them are — by different code, in a different
place.

### WHAT ACTUALLY PRICES A BILL — traced at `9782ae2`, two jobs and only one was unplugged

| Job | Who does it today | State |
|---|---|---|
| **NARROWING** — which of 31 priced objects applies to this customer | **`apps/billing/gather.py`, 2,173 lines** | live, and the only narrowing that runs |
| **PRICING** — this tariff and this quantity → this money | `apps/rating/engine.py`, reached through `billing/rating_seam.py` | live, finance-signed, GT-1…61 |
| **NARROWING, as a provable chain** | `apps/rating/resolution.py` | **written, tested, never swapped in** |

`gather.py` carries the rulings in its own header — `BR-RAT-007`'s service-date resolution, `BR-RAT-101`'s
premises flag, `BR-CUS-014`'s plan-from-unit, `BR-RAT-032`'s NULL-is-every-size. **It is not a stub.** It is the
narrowing, grown a defect at a time.

### SO THE REAL RISK IS DISAGREEMENT, NOT ABSENCE

Bills are not priced by nothing. They are narrowed by a module whose **own header lists its narrowing defects**:
the connection size (`DEF-484`/`DEF-514`), the outside-city factor and the two columns nothing writes
(`DEF-466`/`DEF-515`/`DEF-517`), discounts priced by nothing (`DEF-502`), a master bill that priced the anchor
unit only (`DEF-571`). **Every one of those is the class of bug a provable chain exists to prevent** — which is
why the PO asked for the chain: *"billing logic has to pic up dynamically which rate to apply out of these many
that are set"*.

**And the two paths can MEAN different things.** `DEF-494` records it by name: *"THE LIVE PATH AND THE RULED PATH
MEAN OPPOSITE THINGS BY 'A PLAN IN FORCE'"*. **That is the actual danger** — not a missing rule, but two answers
to one question with only one of them ever asked.

### WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE FIX — nothing about the order, everything about the framing

Step 1 of the execution sequence is unchanged and still first. But it is **not** *"billing is broken"*; it is
*"the provable version of the most important logic in this product is on a shelf while an ad-hoc version does
the work."* **Wiring it is a RECONCILIATION**, and every place the two disagree is a finding to rule on, not a
merge conflict to resolve quietly. A lane that swaps the chain in and makes the differences go away has
destroyed the evidence the job exists to produce.

### THE HABIT THIS IS AN INSTANCE OF

**A measurement stated without its scope becomes a claim about the product.** *"Zero importers"* was measured and
correct; *"enforced nowhere"* was the inference, and it travelled further than the measurement supported. This is
the fifth stale-or-overstated-sentence finding of the day and the first where the author was me.
