## 2026-08-27 · HOW R1–R7 GETS WIRED INTO BILLING — run both, compare, rule, then switch. Never swap and hope.

**PO asked:** *"How you will fixed r1 to R7 code is used during billing ?"* This is the METHOD for step 1 of
`12-governance/19-execution-sequence.md`, recorded before the lane starts so the approach is arguable rather
than discovered in a diff.

### WHY A SHADOW RUN IS POSSIBLE CHEAPLY — three facts, verified at `8444d57`

1. **`resolution.resolve()` is PURE** — frozen facts in, a `Resolution` out. No DB, no I/O. Running it beside
   the live path costs CPU and nothing else.
2. **`gather_account()` has ALREADY loaded every fact the chain needs.** This is a mapping job, **not a data
   job** — no new queries, no new selectors, no migration.
3. **The run already has a stage that shows every input before anything commits** (S31.2, *"Check what we
   found"*), and `BR-BIL-039` makes the preview and the real run **the same code** — `gather.py`'s own header
   says *"two implementations that agree until they don't is the classic way a preview lies."* That is the
   right place to surface a disagreement, and it already exists.

### THE SIX STEPS

| # | Step | What changes on a bill |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Adapter** — map `gather_account`'s facts into the chain's dataclasses. The only genuinely new code | nothing |
| 2 | **Shadow** — run the chain beside the live path on every account. Record agreed / disagreed / chain-refused-where-live-priced | **nothing** |
| 3 | **Surface** the disagreements on the pre-commit screen, by step and by account | nothing |
| 4 | **Rule** each class of disagreement — PO's call, not a lane's | nothing |
| 5 | **Switch one STEP at a time** (R1, then R2, …), each only when its class is at zero. **Move that step's DB half out of `gather` as it goes live** | one step's narrowing, once proved identical |
| 6 | **Delete `gather`'s narrowing half** for switched steps only, after a full billing cycle on the chain | nothing |

### ⚠ STEP 3 IS THE DELIVERABLE, NOT A PHASE TO GET THROUGH

**The disagreements are the point of the whole job.** `DEF-494` already names one: *"THE LIVE PATH AND THE RULED
PATH MEAN OPPOSITE THINGS BY 'A PLAN IN FORCE'"*. Every other one is the same kind of fact — a place where the
product answers a question two ways and only one has ever been asked.

**The chain's nine typed refusals do the work here.** *"R3 — this size is not priced"* is a sentence a utility
acts on in a minute; the live path's equivalent silence is found in an audit. A disagreement where the chain
REFUSES and the live path produced a number is the highest-value row in the report, not an inconvenience.

### ⚠ WHAT A LANE MAY NOT DO, STATED BECAUSE IT IS THE TEMPTING SHORTCUT

**Swap the chain in and reconcile the differences quietly.** A lane that makes the disagreements go away has
destroyed the evidence this job exists to produce, and has done it inside the one system where a wrong answer
is irreversible (hard rule 4). **Each class is ruled or it is not switched.**

**And step 5 is per STEP, not per chain.** Switching all seven at once makes every disagreement arrive in one
diff with no way to attribute it.

### THE MAINTAINABILITY FIX RIDES ALONG WITH STEP 5

`resolution.py`'s own header records the flaw: *"the DB-backed half of R1/R2/R7 lives in
`apps/billing/gather.py` today"*. **Moving each step's data half as that step goes live is nearly free; doing it
afterwards means moving code that is deciding real money.** One module owning one step end to end is what stops
the next drift, since split ownership with neither half wrong is exactly how this one happened.

### GUARDS THROUGHOUT

* **Golden-verify stays 33 PASS / 0 FAIL at every step.** A moved signed figure is a FINDING, never a fixture
  to adjust.
* **The new importer gate** (step 3 of the sequence): a 🔒 sensitive-path module with no non-test importer must
  fail. That check, existing, would have caught `DEF-438` the day the chain was written.

## 2026-08-27 · HOW THE SCREEN PROVES R1–R7 IS WIRED — the test must FAIL when the chain is unplugged, or it proves nothing

**PO asked:** *"How you will test it from Screen that it is wired in ?"* The acceptance criteria for step 1 of
the execution sequence, recorded before the lane starts because **this is the part most likely to be done
badly**: a screen test showing a bill working proves nothing, since the bill works today.

### THE PROPERTY THE TEST MUST HAVE

**`DEF-438`'s escape reason names the trap exactly:** *"every gate that touches this file is a unit test calling
it DIRECTLY, which is exactly the shape that passes forever on dead code."* So the only test worth writing is
one that **goes red when the chain is unplugged**.

### WHAT MAKES THAT POSSIBLE: THE REFUSALS ARE THE CHAIN'S SIGNATURE

The chain has **nine typed refusals**, each naming its step and the missing fact — *"R3 — this size is not
priced."* The live path refuses the same situation in different words (`GATHER_SIZE_UNRESOLVED`,
`connection_size_unresolved_for_sized_schedule`) or does not refuse at all. **Both sentences cannot be on the
screen at once**, so the screen is a probe for which path ran.

### THE TEST

1. Seed **one** account whose meter carries a **connection size the schedule does not price**.
2. Drive the bill run **in a real browser** to *"Check what we found"* (S31.2, the pre-commit stage).
3. Assert the screen shows the **chain's** sentence, naming its step and the service.

**Prove it RED first** (r11 step 2d, hard-won law 7): break the adapter, run the same test, quote the failure.
A guard never seen failing on the thing it was written for is a guard nobody should trust.

**In a browser, not a mocked suite** — the repo already runs Playwright against a live Django + Postgres. This
matters here specifically: **a mocked test asserts against a fixture the lane wrote**, so it passes while
nothing server-side ran, which is the same failure mode as a unit test on dead code. The wave-E lane proved the
point today: a mocked suite could not tell whether help text rendered whole or was silently clipped; the browser
could.

### THREE MORE SCREEN CHECKS ONCE SHADOW MODE IS ON

* **The disagreement count is on screen** — *"the ruled path and the live path disagree on 14 of 1,247
  accounts."* Seed a known disagreement and assert it is counted. **A count that is always zero means the chain
  is not running**, and nothing else would say so.
* **A refusal beats a number.** Seed the case where the chain REFUSES and the live path produces an amount;
  assert the screen shows the refusal, not the money. **That is the highest-value row in the exercise** — a bill
  that would have gone out on a guess.
* **The refusal reads as a SENTENCE, not a code** (`BR-SHL-020`). This also fails if someone renders the
  exception class name, which is the lazy way to make the first test pass.

### ⚠ ONE CAUTION ON THE ASSERTION ITSELF, FROM TODAY

A lane found a test passing **on a column heading**: it waited on the text `"Loaded"` and the only match was the
table header, so it would have passed on an empty list. **Assert against the refusal row's own element, never
text that also appears in the page's furniture.** A screen test that cannot distinguish the data from the chrome
is the same defect as a unit test that cannot distinguish live code from dead.

## 2026-08-27 · `DEF-1702` WAVE G — A SEGMENT IS NOT A FILTER, AND FOUR SCREENS WERE DRAWING THE ONE THEY COULD NOT SERVE IN THE SLOT RESERVED FOR THE ONE THEY COULD

**No question was put to the PO for any of this.** Hard-won law 13: *"EVERYTHING ELSE
IS OURS TO DECIDE AND WRITE DOWN. A judgment call recorded in the decision log with its
reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make one."*
`12-governance/02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md` were grepped for
`segment`, `filter`, `DEF-1700`, `DEF-1702`, `OQ-371` and `OQ-374` before a line was
written. **`OQ-371` and `OQ-374` are still OPEN and nothing here touches them** — see §4.

### 1 · THE FINDING: `inert` IS NOT A SMALLER `bare`, IT IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT

`DEF-1702`'s remainder was five screens. Four of them —
`DisconnectsTab`, `MoveInsTab`, `MoveOutsTab`, `NewConnectsTab` — handed
`DataTable`'s `filterBarSlot` a `WorklistSegments` strip whose handler was
`onSelect={() => undefined}`. The fifth, `TransfersTab`, passed no slot at all.

**On every one of the four, exactly ONE option was `supported`, and it was the one
already active.** The handler was not an oversight: there was nothing for it to write.
So the control was a row of buttons that could not be pressed, sitting in the slot B14
rule 12 reserves for `[All | chips ×] [+ Filter ▾]`, **immediately after the search
box** — which is why a screenshot of any of these four reads as *filtered*.

That is how `DEF-1702` was sized by WALKING the screens, twice, and missed all four
both times. The sweep says it in one line: *"a control that occupies the filter slot,
reads as a filter in a screenshot and narrows nothing"* is a different finding from a
bare toolbar, **with a different fix**.

### 2 · DECIDED: THE STRIP IS DELETED, AND THE RULE THAT DECIDES IT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN IN THESE VERY FILES

Three of the four screens carry this sentence, verbatim, about their missing
`downloadSlot`:

> *"Not drawn DISABLED either — **BR-SHL-025 is for a control this ROLE cannot use, not
> one the PRODUCT does not have.**"*

Ranking B18's segments is a capability **the product does not have** — no rule ranks
them (`OQ-371`, `OQ-374`). So BR-SHL-010 leaves it undrawn, **by these files' own
reasoning about the control four lines further up the same JSX.** Until this commit
each of them argued both ways at once.

Two supporting reasons, neither of them the deciding one:

* **`DEF-1700`'s ruling.** The PO, from a screenshot walk: *"as per our stadard first
  raw of tookkit is more than suficient"*. Those rows were a SECOND row and these strips
  are inside the one row, so the letter of it does not apply — but adding
  `[All] [+ Filter ▾]` **beside** a six-button strip would have put two filter-shaped
  controls in the one row that ruling was about.
* **Capacity.** `DEF-1085` measured the Reads toolbar at ~1,360px against the ~1,150px a
  1,440px laptop leaves. Six dead buttons plus a live panel re-creates that.

`SegmentedFilter` was deleted the same day for the same reason (`DEF-1700`), and G40 —
exact count, baseline 1 — is what stops a component nothing mounts from lingering.
`WorklistSegments` and `WorklistSegmentOption` go with the last mount.

### 3 · THE DISTINCTION, STATED ONCE SO IT DOES NOT HAVE TO BE RE-DERIVED

> **A SEGMENT is an exclusive partition of the list: every row belongs to exactly one
> tab, and the set is a cover. A FILTER is a predicate: it claims nothing about the rows
> it excludes.**

That is the whole of why the segments are blocked and the filters shipped today. A
partition needs a PRECEDENCE for a row that satisfies two tabs; a predicate needs none.

| Screen | Segment strip (removed) | Filter dimension (built) | Are they the same dimension? |
|---|---|---|---|
| New connects | All · In progress · Waiting · Partly activated · Done | `f.state` over `OPEN_STATES` | **No.** `OQ-371`'s own text: *"the segments are not the state tokens — not one drawn row carries `Waiting` or `Done` in its STATE column, and `waiting_on` is a separate column beside STATE."* `Waiting` is derived from a DIFFERENT COLUMN. |
| Disconnects | six, incl. `On hold` | `f.state` over `DISCONNECT_FILTER_STATES` | **No.** `On hold` is COMPUTED from the account's protections and is not a stored state at all; the other five are `disconnect_cases.state`. |
| Move-ins | five `MOVE_IN_STATES` | `f.state` over the THREE marked `supported` | **Same dimension, different membership** — and that is the one case where folding the strip in was even arguable. It is not offered whole: see §5. |
| Move-outs | four `MOVE_OUT_STATES` | `f.closed` — a WINDOW on `closed_at` | **No, and this tab is the proof.** Only ONE state is servable, so a State group would offer one option that changes nothing (B14 rule 9's own objection). The panel had to ask a different question over a different column. |

**Three of the four could not have been "moved into the panel" even in principle.** The
strip was never a filter wearing a different shape.

### 4 · WHAT IS NOT DECIDED — AND THIS IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS

`OQ-371` and `OQ-374` are **OPEN and untouched.** Concretely:

* `payload.segments` / `unavailable[].segments` still travel on every response with
  every `supported` and `unavailable` field intact. Nothing on the server changed.
* `?segment=` still raises `NotImplementedError` for everything but `all`, and both
  screens still **never ask** — asserted by a new case in each suite, because a screen
  that discovered the refusal by CALLING is what the payload exists to prevent.
* When either question closes, **the strip comes back — as a control that works.**

Removing a control that cannot be operated is not answering the question it was
standing in for. It is declining to draw the answer before there is one.

### 5 · THE ONE JUDGMENT INSIDE THE JUDGMENT: AN UNSERVABLE OPTION IS **NOT OFFERED**, NOT DISABLED

Move-ins draws five states and can serve three; `in_progress` and `done` carry
`STEP_HAS_NO_STORE` and no retention window. A disabled SEGMENT could say why on its own
tooltip. **A filter OPTION has nowhere to put that sentence** — and an option that
returns an empty list forever reads as *"there are none"*, which is a false statement
rather than a missing one. So the panel offers the three, and the absences stay served
and stay rendered in the cells that already state them.

Same rule, applied twice more, both times by SUBTRACTION on the server so the client
cannot drift: Transfers cannot offer `cancelled` (`list_queryset` excludes it —
`DEF-1004`), and Disconnects cannot offer `stopped`/`restored` (`open_cases` excludes
them, so the row has left the list).

### 6 · THE DIMENSION IS DECLARED ON THE CLIENT; THE VOCABULARY IS THE SERVER'S

`TableConfig.filters` declares the NAME only — that is what makes `?f.state=cut`
survive a reload (`parseTableParams`/`serializeTableParams` read `filter.name` and
nothing else). The OPTIONS are read off `payload.states` / `payload.closed_windows` on
every response (BR-SHL-010), so a state added to a workflow, or a fourth window added to
`MOVE_OUT_CLOSED_WINDOWS`, reaches these panels **with no edit here**. Before the first
response the group is empty and `offerableFilters` drops it — no legend over nothing
(`DEF-782`).

### 7 · WHAT WAS NOT CHANGED

**No money, no rounding, no golden test — golden-verify stays 33 PASS / 0 FAIL.** No
migration, no data write, no backend change of any kind: all five server legs landed on
2026-08-27 (`ec4d9f8`) and this is the frontend half only. **No second toolbar row was
added**; every control is in the single `filterBarSlot` B14 rule 12 fixes.

### 8 · THE SWEEP, RE-RUN — and the two numbers that are NOT this wave's

`python3 10-scripts/cr045_toolbar_sweep.py`

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| screens with a `DataTable` | 28 | 28 |
| `DataTable` instances | 29 | 29 |
| filter **wired** | 19 | **24** |
| filter **custom** | 2 | 2 |
| filter **declared** | 0 | 0 |
| filter **inert** | **4** | **0** |
| filter **bare** | **3** | **2** |

The two bare are `DEF-1704` (Settings › Users) and **`DEF-1783`, filed today** —
Settings › Reference data, the ELEVENTH bare instance, which `DEF-1702`'s own sweep
named on every run and no wave ever carried. Filed rather than absorbed, for
`DEF-1704`'s stated reason.

**`7 no search` and `16 no download` did NOT move and were not this wave's to move.**
Reported so the next dispatch is sized from a measurement rather than a look:

* **7 with no search box** — `AssetImportsTab`, `AccountImportsTab`,
  `PremisesImportsTab`, `MoveInsTab`, `AuditLogPage`, `TemplateCatalog`,
  `SettingsUsersTab`. **Not one is obviously exempt.** The three imports tabs each list
  runs with a file name and a `run_by`; Move-ins is the only worklist of the five with
  no box while its four siblings have one and `move_ins_list` accepts `q` **today**,
  which makes it the same shape as `DEF-1701`: a server capability no screen reaches.
  `AuditLogPage` and `TemplateCatalog` carry bespoke panels and may genuinely search
  through those. **A real gap on at least four, and B14 rule 19 makes each one a
  sentence to write as well as a box to draw.**
* **16 with no download slot** — this one IS mostly a stated absence rather than a gap,
  and it is already carried by **`DEF-1005`**: `POST /exports` resolves only the
  resources a module REGISTERS, eleven are registered, and BR-SHL-010 keeps an
  unregistered capability undrawn. Four of this lane's five screens say so in their own
  JSX, in the same words. **So the number to chase is not 16 — it is "which of the 16
  have a registered export they do not draw", which is what `CR-045` wave E asked and
  answered for routes and cycles.** Sizing the rest from this count without that
  distinction would repeat exactly the mistake `DEF-1702` records.

## 2026-08-27 · R1–R7 STEP 3, DELIVERED: THE CHAIN CANNOT BE RUN ON A SINGLE REAL ACCOUNT, SO THERE ARE NO DISAGREEMENTS TO RULE — THERE ARE FOUR MISSING FACTS TO SOURCE

**No question was put to the PO for any of this.** Hard-won law 13: *"EVERYTHING ELSE IS OURS TO DECIDE AND WRITE
DOWN."* `02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md` were grepped for `served_sizes`, `connection size`,
`multiplier`, `DEF-438`, `DEF-494`, `DEF-498`, `DEF-493` and `DEF-652` before a line was written. **`DEF-652` was
found ALREADY RULED and was NOT re-raised** — see §5.

This is step 1 of `19-execution-sequence.md`, executed by the six-step method recorded above
(*"HOW R1–R7 GETS WIRED INTO BILLING — run both, compare, rule, then switch"*). **Steps 1, 2 and 3 are done.
Steps 4, 5 and 6 are NOT started, and §3 is why.**

### 1 · WHAT WAS BUILT — the adapter, and what makes it different from the harness

`06-backend/apps/billing/resolution_shadow.py` (NEW) is step 1's *"only genuinely new code"*: it maps
`gather_account`'s `AccountBillingData` into `resolution.resolve`'s frozen dataclasses, runs the chain beside the
live path, and returns a typed report. It prices nothing. Billing does not import rating at module scope — every
cross-module read is late-bound through `_seam`, the posture `rating_seam.py` sets and `gather.py` already takes.

**`tests/test_def_438_parity.py` already existed and is excellent, and it could not have found any of this.** It
compares the two paths with the hard facts passed in **as test arguments** — `_price_chain(account, sizes={"water":
"5/8"}, multipliers=…)`. It had to: there was no adapter, so the facts had to come from somewhere and the author
supplied them. **Supplying them is exactly what hid the four findings below**, every one of which is about a fact
the PRODUCT cannot produce. It is `DEF-498`'s own escape reason one level up: *"a hand-built code always states an
amount because the author is thinking about the case under test."*

### 2 · THE ADAPTER REFUSES TO INVENT, AND ONE REFUSAL IS THE WHOLE JOB

There is **no default anywhere in the adapter**. Four facts the chain needs and the live path does not carry are
reported by name — `MISSING_CONNECTION_SIZE`, `MISSING_MULTIPLIER`, `MISSING_ASSET_COUNT`, `MISSING_PLAN` — rather
than filled in.

**The multiplier is the one that matters and it is worth stating why, because the fix that suggests itself is the
worst option available.** `resolution.billable_quantity` scales the REGISTER DIFFERENCE by the meter multiplier
(BR-RAT-001). `metering.selectors.billing_reads_for_unit` publishes a `consumption` that is **already
post-multiplier** and publishes **no multiplier**. So:

* feeding the chain `consumption` bills **100×** on a ×10 register — measured: register difference **50**, stored
  consumption **500**, chain output **5,000**. Asserted RED before it was asserted green;
* defaulting the multiplier to **1** is worse, because it is silent: ×1 of the register difference equals
  metering's stored figure **exactly when the multiplier really is 1**, so R3b would report **parity by
  construction on every account** and the shadow report would read as the best possible news while measuring
  nothing. `resolution.MeterMultiplierUnstated` already says it: *"an absent factor is not 1"*.

### 3 · THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE PLAN — measured, 1 of 1 accounts

**The chain cannot be run on a single real account of any tenant** (`DEF-1811`, critical). `MeterFacts
.connection_size` is typed `str` and R3 narrows on it; `gather._connection_size_for` returns `None` for every
account because **the product stores a connection size on no table at all** (`DEF-514`; `DEF-255` checked
`information_schema` for `%size_class%` and found nothing). The full report, through the production adapter on a
provisioned tenant:

    accounts 1 · attempted 0 · agreed 0 · disagreed 0 · chain_refused 0
    not_attempted 1 · blocked_by_reason {connection_size_unresolved: 1}

⚠ **READ THE THIRD AND FOURTH NUMBERS TOGETHER OR THEY LIE.** *"0 disagreed"* is also what perfect agreement looks
like. `summarise()` publishes `attempted` beside it for that reason, and the screen must show both.

**THIS REFRAMES `DEF-438` AND MOVES ITS OWNER.** The register says the chain has *no production caller*. It is
worse: **a caller could not be written today even if someone wanted one**, because a required input to R3 does not
exist as data. Wiring the chain is blocked on a **metering column**, not on billing work — a different module and a
different order of work from the one the execution sequence assumes. Two more of the same shape sit behind it: no
multiplier crosses billing's read seam (`DEF-1812`) and no billable asset count crosses at all (`DEF-1813`).

**And a fourth, which is the sharpest (`DEF-1810`): R3's *"this size is not served"* refusal is UNREACHABLE through
any correct adapter.** `size_rows` is built as `served_sizes ∪ size_classes_for(version)` with the version's scalar
`base_charge` repeated per key, and `served_sizes` is the caller's — *"normally the one size the account's meter
actually is."* So the size R3 looks up is, by construction, one the catalogue was just told to serve. **Worked, same
tenant and same plan: `served_sizes=('5/8',)` resolves `$8.00`; `served_sizes=('3-inch',)` — a size nobody
configured anywhere — resolves `$8.00` too.** The only reachable R3 refusal is a NULL `base_charge`, which is a
statement about the VERSION, not the size.

⚠ **AND IT INVALIDATES THE RECORDED ACCEPTANCE TEST AS WRITTEN.** The screen entry above says *"Seed one account
whose meter carries a connection size the schedule does not price."* **That scenario cannot be constructed** — the
seeding serves the size. The proof-of-wiring test is therefore built on the blank-base refusal instead, with a
comment saying why, and it IS proved red: breaking the adapter three ways produced three quoted failures.

### 4 · WHY STEP 3'S SCREEN HALF WAS NOT BUILT — a judgment, recorded so it can be argued with

The screen entry warns: **"A count that is always zero means the chain is not running, and nothing else would say
so."** Today that count is always zero **and** the chain is not running. Shipping the S31.2 panel now would ship the
exact reading the decision log says to distrust, with nothing on screen able to distinguish it from a wiring fault —
and it would be the fourth *"built is not wired"* instance in a repo that has hard-won law 2 for this. **The panel
lands with the first fact that lets one account be attempted**, and `summarise()` already returns the shape it needs.

### 5 · WHY NOTHING WENT TO THE PO — including the one that looks overdue

Step 4 is *"rule each class of disagreement — PO's call, not a lane's"*. **There are no disagreements to rule yet.
There are four missing facts to source**, and asking the PO to choose between two numbers we cannot compute would be
a question standing in for a decision we have not earned.

**`DEF-652` was NOT re-raised, and this is the law-13 case.** Its own row already carries the ruling, PO verbatim:
*"this is correct - A $62.14 bill with a 25% senior discount of $15.54 — is the 6.85% tax charged on $62.14
($4.26)"*. That is the **`after`** treatment; `taxes.discount_treatment` exists, is built, and defaults to `before`
(`$3.19` on the same bill). What remains is **not a question for the PO** — it is (A) change the default vs (B)
configure this tax, both already written down in the row with both figures. **A lane must not re-ask it.** ❄️ No B4
or B5 figure was moved and none needs to be: the ruling is about which stored treatment applies, not about a frozen
number.

### 6 · WHAT THE NEXT LANE SHOULD DO, IN ORDER

1. **Source the connection size** (`DEF-1811`/`DEF-514`) — a metering column plus `connection_size_for`, the seam
   `gather.py` has been wired to since `DEF-484` and which has never had a source. **Nothing else in this job can
   start until this lands.**
2. Publish the multiplier on `billing_reads_for_unit` (`DEF-1812`) — one key, no new query, the same row.
3. Publish `billable_asset_count` (`DEF-1813`) — a new seam, `None` meaning *nobody looked*.
4. **Then** run the shadow across a real run, and step 4 finally has something to rule.

**Only after that does step 5 (switch ONE step at a time) become meaningful**, and it stays per-step: switching all
seven at once makes every disagreement arrive in one diff with no way to attribute it.

### 7 · ⚠ THE NEW MODULE WILL TRIP THE IMPORTER GATE STEP 3 OF THE SEQUENCE IS ABOUT, AND THAT IS CORRECT

`19-execution-sequence.md` step 3 plans *"a 🔒 sensitive-path module with no non-test importer must fail — that
check, existing, would have caught `DEF-438` the day the chain was written."* **`apps/billing/resolution_shadow.py`
is exactly that shape today**: it is sensitive-path, and its only importers are its two test files. Stated here
before the gate exists so the next lane does not read it as a fresh `DEF-438`.

**The difference is the reason, and it is not a lane's opinion — it is the method's own rule.** The chain is
unwired because nobody wired it; the shadow is unwired because **steps 1–4 may not change anything on a bill**, and
its first legitimate caller is the S31.2 preview, which §4 explains cannot be built until one account can be
attempted. **A lane that "fixes" this by calling `shadow_account` from the bill run has not wired a module — it has
started step 5 without step 4, which is the one thing the recorded method forbids.**

So when the gate lands, `resolution_shadow.py` needs an **exemption keyed to `DEF-1811`** — not a caller — and the
exemption expires the day the connection size exists. If a future reader finds this module still uncalled and
`DEF-1811` CLOSED, that is a real finding and it should be filed.

## 2026-08-27 — THE THREE BOUNDARY GATES, AND WHY THERE IS NO FOURTH

Step 3 of `19-execution-sequence.md`, PO-approved. The finding it rests on, verbatim from that file:
**"Every existing gate compares a frontend artefact to another frontend artefact, or a document to a
document."** Three gates landed — `G47` (frontend↔seed), `G48` (import↔ledger), `G49` (template↔series).
Suite **32 PASS / 15 FAIL → 36 PASS / 14 FAIL**; nothing broken.

This entry holds the JUDGMENTS. The mechanics are in each gate's own docstring, which is where a reader
of the code will look for them.

### 1 · `G47` — ORDER WAS WRITTEN, RUN, AND WITHDRAWN ON THE EVIDENCE

CLAUDE.md fixes the ten services **"in that seed order"**, so an order clause looked obvious and was
built first. It fails two places that are deliberately and correctly out of seed order:
`features/rating/ratingShared.tsx` groups **r10's six before the four `OQ-273` added later** — the six
carry r10's own one-letter badges and the four carry two-letter badges precisely *because* they are a
later group — and `apps/ledger/chart.py` orders services by **GL account code**, which is the chart's
order and not the catalogue's. Both are ruled. G45's docstring states the principle and it decided this:
***"a gate that argues with a ruling gets switched off."*** Order on the one list where it is signed —
the signup chips — is already asserted by `signupServices.test.ts`, which is the right instrument for a
per-file rule. **The gate checks MEMBERSHIP only, and the withdrawal is recorded so nobody re-adds it.**

**Four backend files are partial BY A RULING** and are named in `PARTIAL_BY_RULE` *with* that ruling:
`tenancy/services.SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS` (six — r10 SET-03 draws a primary UoM for six, and inventing the
other four would break hard rule 3), `metering/services.RATIFIED_SERVICE_SEED` and its migration (seven —
trash and storm water are never READ, broadband is deferred under CR-038 Open 7), and
`core/sample_fixture.CR030_OVERFLOW_SERVICES` (eight — B18 TC-ACC-4's `+3` chip needs exactly eight).
The exemption lives in the CHECK and not in those files' comments, because **a comment claiming a
guarantee is not the guarantee** (hard-won law 1).

### 2 · `G48` — TWO WEAKER READINGS WERE TRIED FIRST, AND NEITHER COULD TELL PASS FROM FAIL

Recorded because the discarded attempts are the useful part:

* ***"some module names both the column and a posting entrypoint"*** — PASSES on `deposit_on_file`,
  because `customers/services.py` is 4,000 lines and mentions both.
* ***"the ledger app names the column"*** — FAILS on `ob_current`, which correctly reaches the ledger as
  a SUMMED balance and never by name.

DEF-182: *a check whose output cannot distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check, because it is
trusted.* What survives is **"a money column the shipped template accepts must be NAMED by a module that
posts"** — a NECESSARY condition, not a sufficient one, and the docstring says so rather than implying
more. It is worth having because it is exactly the condition `deposit_on_file` fails: nothing that posts
has ever heard of it. Hard rule 5 keeps that universe to **two modules**, which is what makes the check
possible at all.

**`deposit_on_file` is BANKED, not fixed, and banked BY NAME rather than as a count.** `DEF-1713` is open
at high and its fix is a ledger posting for migrated deposits — 🔒 sensitive-path work owned by step 4,
not by a gate lane. Shipping hard-RED would put the whole suite on the floor for every lane over a known
defect nobody in flight is fixing, and *"a gate that is red from birth earns a `# noqa` instead of a
fix"* (G44's own words). **A named set beats a baseline of `1`**: a SECOND unposted column fails at its
own name instead of hiding inside the count, and the gate goes RED as STALE when `DEF-1713` lands and the
row is left behind (DEF-490).

### 3 · `G49` — I WROTE THE ONE-WORD FIX AND THEN REVERTED IT

Clause (d) found **`DEF-1840`** on its first run: five served strings say *"Settings › Numbers"* while
`settings.tab.numbering` — the label `SettingsPage.tsx` actually renders — is **"Numbering"**, and
*"Numbers"* is not a settings label anywhere in `en.json`. Premises and units name the screen correctly
(they go through `_issued_number_column`); the three ASSETS templates, the ones the PO walked through,
do not.

**The fix was made and reverted, and that is the recorded judgment.**
`tests/test_br_ast_049_external_ref.py:630` asserts `"Settings › Numbers ›"` **is in** the `asset_no`
help, `tests/test_cr046_identifiers.py:287` asserts it in a `fix_hint`, and this log at line 14904
records the click path as *"Settings › Numbers › Meter"*. **Three artefacts agree with each other and
disagree with the product**, so the suite is GREEN ON THE BUG — the same shape as CR-039 A2's *"exactly
the six signup services render as chips"*, where a test written from the same misunderstanding as the
code could not catch it. **Which of the two names is the product's is the CR-046 owner's to rule**; a
gate lane silently turning two tests red and overruling a sentence in this log is not that ruling. The
five are banked by name; a sixth still fails, and a fix left in the list goes RED as stale.

**The accounts EXCLUSION is checked, not skipped.** Accounts take their number from the file by PO ruling
(*"ACCOUNTS ARE EXCLUDED BY NAME (PO ruling 2026-08-27)"*), so that column is required to be the
OPPOSITE — a declared sample and `required=True` — because a file-issued column shipping a blank sample
is `DEF-962` in the other direction. **The ruling lives in the check so nobody re-asks it (law 13).**

### 4 · ⚠ WHY THERE IS NO FOURTH GATE — A JUDGMENT, WITH THE MEASUREMENT SO IT NEED NOT BE REDONE

The dispatch asked whether `G13`/`G40` already answer *"a module imported only by tests"*. **They do
not** — both are frontend-only — and `G20` covers only DECLARED seam contracts. **The question is
genuinely uncovered.** It was still not built, and here is the whole reasoning.

**The first measurement said nineteen modules were dead, including seven of `apps/reports/`. It was
wrong.** `reports/api.py` reaches them by **relative import** (`from . import dashboard`), which the
reader did not resolve. That is DEF-182's failure committed by the very lane quoting it, caught only
because the result was too dramatic to believe. Resolving relative imports raised the candidate count to
**69**, now dominated by Django conventions: `apps.py`, `tests.py`, `models.py`, `urls.py`, `*_api.py`
mounted by STRING in `config/urls.py`, and management commands discovered by NAME.

**Scoping to the 🔒 sensitive-path set is the fix, and it works: 69 → 6**, of which four are
`__init__.py`, one is string-mounted and one is a management command. **Zero real offenders today.**

**But that scope has a hole, and the hole is now `DEF-1841`:** the R1–R7 chain
(`rating/resolution.py`, `rating/resolution_catalogue.py`, `billing/resolution_shadow.py`) is rating
math, carries `HUMAN-OWNED` in its own docstrings, and **no glob in `human_owned.txt` matches it**. So a
gate scoped to that list would have reported a confident green over 1,755 lines of unwatched arithmetic
and **would NOT have caught `DEF-438`**, which `19-execution-sequence.md` says it would. Building it on
that scope now would ship false assurance; building it unscoped ships noise.

**So: fix the scope first (`DEF-1841`, and the globs are the PO's to add — `human_owned.txt`'s own header
rules that changing it is a process event, *"who watches the watchers"*), then the gate is small and
worth having.** The step-1 lane has already written the exemption it will need — decision log 2026-08-27
§7 — keyed to `DEF-1811` and expiring with it, because `resolution_shadow.py` is unwired BY THE METHOD
(steps 1–4 may not change anything on a bill), not by neglect.

**Nothing went to the PO from this lane, and `OQ-880–889` are unused.** Law 13: a judgment recorded with
its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make one. The one thing that legitimately
needs a person — which name the numbering screen has — is `DEF-1840`, filed rather than asked, because it
belongs to the CR-046 owner's next pass and not to a fresh interruption.

## 2026-08-27 · STEP 1 DELIVERED — THE CONNECTION SIZE AND THE METER MULTIPLIER NOW REACH BILLING

*(connection-size lane · branch `claude/meter-reads-70rxcc` · ids `DEF-1900–1929` ·
`BR-AST-500` · `BR-AST-501` · `BR-MET-500` · shipped as **2.79.5**)*

### 1 · The number that moved, and it is the only headline here

The R1–R7 lane finished step 3 of `12-governance/19-execution-sequence.md` and **stopped**, because it
had proved the chain could not be run on a single real account of any tenant. Its measurement, and the
same measurement after this lane, on the **same fixture** through the **same production adapter**:

| | accounts | attempted | agreed | disagreed | chain_refused | not_attempted | by_step | blocked_by_reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **before** | 1 | **0** | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | `{}` | `{connection_size_unresolved: 1}` |
| **after** | 1 | **1** | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | **`{R4: 1}`** | `{}` |

⚠ **READ `by_step {R4: 1}`, BECAUSE IT IS THE THING THE WHOLE CUTOVER EXISTS TO PRODUCE AND IT HAS NEVER
BEEN VISIBLE ON A REAL ACCOUNT BEFORE.** The chain now runs on production rows and refuses at R4 — which
is `DEF-498`'s filed finding (*"R4 refuses every bill five times over"*) arriving for the first time as a
**measurement off real data** instead of a hand-built harness. **It is deliberately NOT fixed here.**
Step 4 of the recorded cutover is where each class of disagreement is RULED, and this lane's own charter
says the opposite of tidying: *"A lane that makes the disagreements go away has destroyed the evidence
this job exists to produce."*

⚠ **AND `disagreed` IS 1, NOT 0 — WHICH IS THE PROOF THE MULTIPLIER WAS NOT DEFAULTED.** `DEF-1812`
warned that a defaulted 1 would make R3b report parity by construction; a run coming back `disagreed 0`
here would have been the symptom of that default, not good news.

### 2 · What landed

* **`assets.Asset.size_class`** (migration `assets/0010`) — TEXT, NULL, holding `service_size_classes
  .code`. **DEF-514's own prevention, verbatim**, including the reason it is on the ASSET (BR-RAT-108,
  PO verbatim *"based on Asset and Account type you will have select 1 base charge"*).
* **`assets.selectors.assets_on_unit` publishes it** beside `qualifier` and `type` — the dict
  `metering.selectors.route_meter_picker` has read `asset.get("size_class")` out of since SET-06 step 3
  was built, and which published no size, so that screen's Size column has drawn a permanently empty cell
  for its entire life.
* **`metering.selectors.connection_size_for(unit_id, service_code)`** — the seam `billing/gather.py` has
  resolved BY NAME since 2026-08-21 and which has never had a source. **`gather.py` is UNCHANGED**, which
  is the evidence its own docstring asked for: *"the day metering publishes `connection_size_for` the
  size reaches the bill and nothing here changes."*
* **`metering.selectors.billing_reads_for_unit` publishes `multiplier`** — one key off the row it already
  read (`DEF-1812`) — and **`billing_multiplier_for`** answers the shadow's seam for a caller holding no
  reading row.
* **A WRITER**, so the column is not `DEF-515` one table across: `size_class` is accepted on asset create
  and update, the demo estate seeds a ratified band, and it joins `BILLING_AFFECTING_FIELDS`
  (`BR-AST-501`).

### 3 · The vocabulary was ALREADY RULED and was NOT invented here (law 13)

Grepping `02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md` before minting anything found it: **`BR-TEN-170`
+ `BR-TEN-171`, PO-ratified 2026-08-27** — the list is `service_size_classes` (*"it is utility service
size class"*), the seeded set is **forty** codes across eight services, and `apps/tenancy/
service_size_classes.py` is its authority. So **no OQ was minted for the vocabulary and none was needed**;
`OQ-900–909` are **unused**. The column holds those codes (`W-58`, `W-2`, `E-1P-100` …).

⚠ **THE CHAIN'S OWN TESTS USE A DIFFERENT-LOOKING VOCABULARY AND IT IS NOT A CONFLICT — SAY SO ONCE SO
NOBODY "FIXES" IT.** `DEF-1810`'s worked case reads `served_sizes=('5/8',)` and `('3-inch',)`. Those are
**test arguments**, and that is precisely the defect `DEF-1810` records. In the product both ends of the
comparison come from the same place: a rate schedule's sizes are `RateTier.size_class`, typed through the
wizard's picker off the live list, and the meter's size is now the same list's code. They match because
they are one vocabulary, not because anyone translated between two.

### 4 · Four judgments this lane made and did not put to the PO (law 13)

Each is ours to decide and write down; none collides with a signed rule, none is a ❄️ frozen figure, and
none is a fact only the PO holds.

1. **TWO METERS ON ONE SERVICE POINT RECORDING DIFFERENT SIZES ANSWER `None`.** One connection has one
   size; two different recorded sizes is a data error, and the seam's only options are *pick one* — which
   selects a tier ladder and therefore **prices a bill on a coin toss** — or *say it cannot tell*. It says
   it cannot tell, and `gather`'s existing named refusal carries that to a human.
   **Absence is not a competing claim:** a meter with no size beside a meter with one is not a
   disagreement, so the recorded size wins and the account bills.
2. **THE MULTIPLIER IS NEVER DEFAULTED TO 1**, at the source as well as in the adapter — see §1.
3. **THE COLUMN IS TEXT, NOT AN FK.** `RateTier.size_class`'s own stated reason, reached one table
   across: *"a size Settings RETIRES must not vanish from a schedule that already priced it"* — and it
   must not vanish from a meter bolted to a wall either. It is likewise **not validated against the live
   list**, because an existence check would refuse exactly that case (which is what
   `rating.services._size_rows` already says about its own copy).
4. **THE SEEDER PLANTS THE SMALLEST RATIFIED BAND** for the tenant's backbone service (water `W-58`,
   electric `E-1P-100`), taken from `BR-TEN-171` and never from a string a lane typed. **It moves no
   money:** no seeded rate schedule carries a per-size override, so `pricing_inputs` returns the NULL
   *"every size"* group either way and every seeded bill is byte-identical. It is seeded anyway because
   the alternative is `DEF-515`'s exact shape — a column NULL everywhere prices identically to no column,
   the demo tenant would still report `blocked {connection_size_unresolved}`, and a reader walking the
   product would conclude the fix had not landed.

### 5 · What this lane deliberately did NOT do

* **`DEF-1810` IS NOT RESOLVED.** Whether `served_sizes` means *what this account needs priced* or *what
  the tenant has configured* is a design question with money behind it — the second reading makes R3
  refuse real bills that price today — and the prime directive forbids a lane choosing. It goes to the PO
  through the consuming lane, not through a sourcing one.
* **`apps/rating/resolution.py` and `apps/billing/resolution_shadow.py` ARE UNTOUCHED.** Sourcing a fact
  and consuming it are different lanes on purpose; a lane that did both could not be checked by the
  measurement in §1.
* **`R4` IS NOT FIXED** — see §1.

### 6 · Two defects filed rather than fixed

* **`DEF-1900`** — the column has an API writer and **no control and no import column**. AST-05, AST-01/02
  and the meters import all lack a size field, so the only way to record one today is a hand-made API
  call. Worked: a utility that types r10's 2" ladder (`3.45 / 5.10 / 7.70` against `3.20 / 4.80 / 7.20`)
  and loads 1,847 meters gets every one billed on the every-size ladder, because there is no column in the
  file and no box on the screen. Not fixed here because both halves are other lanes' files, and the
  frontend half is governed by B14 rule 21's **per-file** migration clause (`DEF-974`).
* **`DEF-1901`** — `route_meter_picker` reads `service` and `read_method` out of `assets_on_unit` too, and
  that dict publishes neither. **Three of that table's five columns were null; DEF-514 named one because
  the size was the one with money behind it, and fixing it is what made the other two visible.**

### 7 · Evidence

Golden **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** before and after — no ❄️ B4/B5 figure is asserted or moved. Full
`manage.py migrate` on an **empty Postgres 16** applies clean, and **DEF-255's own probe**
(`information_schema` for `%size_class%`) now returns `assets | size_class | text | YES` where it
returned nothing. All eleven cases of `tests/test_def_1900_connection_size.py` were proved **RED first**
at `1a7b52d` (law 7) with `core.errors.ValidationError: VAL-002 (assets.unknown_field)` and
`AttributeError: module 'apps.metering.selectors' has no attribute 'connection_size_for'`. `DEF-1812`'s
own pin fired **by name** on the fix — *"billing's read seam has GAINED a multiplier"* — and is now the
parity assertion it was written to block.

Migration ordering is a CLAUDE.md 🔒 sensitive path: `assets/0010` carries `HUMAN-OWNED` +
`HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` and its row is in `12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md`, stating in plain
English with a figure what is owed to the PO.

**Lane:** the service-request / move-out surface (step 4 of `12-governance/19-execution-sequence.md`).

`DEF-637` · `DEF-638` · `DEF-640` · `DEF-648` · `DEF-649`.

### 1 · The diagnosis collapsed, and it collapsed onto the register

The cluster's shared root is **not** a product fault. **Seven of the nine were already
fixed at the tip** and the register still read `status: open` with an empty
`fixed_commit`. The evidence is not an impression — the code says so in its own words:

### 2 · `DEF-628` — REAL, AND ITS OWN PRESCRIBED FIX WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A WORSE DEFECT

`DEF-628`'s `prevention` (2026-08-24) reads: *"the cell should key off `non_billable`
rather than off the amount."* **`BR-CUS-107` landed the next day** (PO 2026-08-25,
migration `customers/0025`) and put a sixth status — `Disconnected` — into that same
behaviour class. That migration's own worked row is **`A-11488`, cut 2026-08-18 owing
$612.75**. Keying the balance cell off `non_billable` alone would render *awaiting* over
that **$612.75**, hiding the arrears on precisely the account the disconnect ladder
exists to chase. A prevention note is a statement about the world on the day it was
filed; r11 step 0 is what catches one that has been overtaken.

**→ `BR-CUS-510` (this lane's judgment, not a PO ruling — nothing here collides with a
signed rule, moves a ❄️ FROZEN figure, or needs a fact only the PO holds; law 13).** The
cell may say *awaiting* only when ALL FOUR hold: **(1)** the ledger answered · **(2)** the
amount is **exactly zero** · **(3)** the status **behaviour class** is `non_billable`
(never a code — `BR-CUS-055` is tenant-extensible) · **(4)** **no bill has ever been
issued**. The figure is never hidden and never nulled: `balance` still serves the ledger's
`0.000000` and `balance_not_yet_billable` is served beside it.

**Worked, three rows:**

| Account | Ledger says | Class | Billed? | Cell renders |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pending-activation `A-10001` | `0.000000`, answered | `non_billable` | never | **Awaiting** ✅ (was `$0.00`) |
| cut `A-11488` | `612.750000` | `non_billable` | yes | **$612.75** ✅ (clause 2 saves it) |
| active `A-10003` | `0.000000` | `billable` | — | **$0.00** ✅ — settled is an answer |

RED proof (law 7): patching `selectors.py` to the prevention **as written** turns three
cases of `tests/test_def_628_awaiting_balance.py` red with `assert True is False` on
`balance_not_yet_billable`, `A-11488` among them.

### 3 · `DEF-638` 12.c — ONE FIELD, ONE LABEL, DECIDED FROM THE AUTHORITY ORDER

The capture form labelled the identifier **`Social Security Number`**
(`customers.serviceRequest.capture.ssn`) and the detail labelled the same column **`ID`**
(`customers.serviceRequest.applicant.identifier`). `models.py` recorded the name as
*"unruled as well as its storage"*.

**It needed no PO question.** `B19 §7` — the design this surface is built from — draws the
detail row as `Social Security Number → ••• ••• • 4471 · stored encrypted`, and CLAUDE.md
puts the design above a spec label. The generic `ID` was DEF-632-era caution (*"the
product cannot encrypt it, so the generic label may be the safer one"*) and **`BR-CUS-092`
removed the premise** — the value is stored, encrypted, and served as `ssn_last4`.
The detail now asks for the capture form's own key: translated in all eleven catalogues,
**no catalogue edited**, and the same reach into the `capture.` namespace this row already
makes one line down for `ssnStoredEncrypted`. `applicant.identifier` is left unused rather
than deleted from eleven files (`G27` asks that a wanted key EXISTS, never the reverse).

### 4 · What is NOT a defect, and what is still owed

* **`DEF-638` 12.d — the em-dash where the quote total belongs — is not a live fault.** The
  Fees tab renders `Connection quote · Not raised` with the sentence *"A quote is raised
  after review, once you know what work the request needs"*; there is no fabricated total

### 5 · `DEF-648`'s DURABLE HALF STOPPED AT THE LANGUAGE BOUNDARY, AND NOW DOES NOT

`BR-SHL-046`'s own words: *"THE DURABLE HALF IS THE MECHANISM, NOT THE NUMBER —
both bars must be driven by ONE declared step list. **Two literals that happen to agree
today is precisely the state this was found in**, and it recurs the day a seventh step
appears."* The fix honours that **within** the frontend (`moveShared.MOVE_OUT_STEPS`
feeds the rail) and **not across the wire**: the Move-outs tab renders the SERVER's `of`,
and `apps/customers/move_reads.py:416` carries `MOVE_OUT_STEP_COUNT = 6` as a literal.
Two literals, two languages, agreeing by luck — `tsc` cannot see a Python constant and
pytest does not read `.tsx`.

`06-backend/tests/test_def_648_step_count_parity.py` closes it: the server constant must
equal the number of entries the frontend list declares, and the ruled **6** is pinned so
that agreeing on the wrong number still fails. **Proved RED** by setting the constant back
to `MVO-01`'s shipped `4` — *"the server says a move-out has 4 steps and the wizard
declares 6"*. Move-in's five is pinned beside it, because the failure mode is the boundary
and not the flow.

**Nothing was put to the PO by this lane.** Every disagreement in the nine resolved from
r10/B19, B14, `02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md`.

**seven of nine** open `high` rows in one customers cluster already fixed at the tip and
still reading `status: open` with an empty `fixed_commit`, and wrote the caveat itself:
*"That is one sample and it is not a rate."* Every triage figure in
`12-governance/19-execution-sequence.md` — the module blocks the merge lane has been
quoting all day — rests on those open counts being true. So: draw a sample that is
visibly not cherry-picked, decide each row on evidence, and publish the rate with what
it can and cannot support.

### 1 · THE DRAW — SEED `19300827`, PUBLISHED BEFORE ANY ROW WAS OPENED

Population, at tip `002dada`: the **broad** reading of open — `status` in
`open`/`reported`/`fixed-in-part`/`partially-fixed` — at `severity: high`. That is
**84 rows** (`defect_report.py` prints 84 broad / 77 narrow; the 7-row difference is
`fixed-in-part`-style statuses and this lane uses the broad one, because a
`fixed-in-part` row is exactly the kind that goes stale).

648 · 649` — because they have already been re-triaged and counting them would inflate

```
python3 10-scripts/retriage_sample.py        # seed 19300827, hardcoded
```

`random.Random(19300827).sample(eligible, 15)`, where `eligible` is the population above
sorted ascending by numeric id. **The seed and the ordering are both in the script**, so

**3 already-fixed / 15 decided = 20%.** **0 undecidable** — every row resolved on code,
a register file, a run, or direct observation. **0 "not a defect"**, which is itself a
result: `DEF-1930`'s cluster had four, and this sample has none.

**Wilson 95% interval on 3/15: 7% – 45%.** Over the 84 open highs that is **≈17 rows
stale, and anywhere from 6 to 38.**

**What that supports, stated plainly:**

* **`DEF-1930`'s 78% is NOT the repo-wide rate.** 7/9 sits outside the interval. The
  triage numbers in `19-execution-sequence.md` are not four-fifths fiction.
* **Nor is the register clean.** Zero is outside the interval too. About one open high
  in five is already done, so a module block of 17 probably contains three or four
  rows that need closing rather than fixing.
* **What fifteen rows CANNOT support: any per-module rate.** The sample has 4 rating,
  3 billing and one each of seven other modules. **Do not read a module figure out of
  this table** — with one or two rows per module the interval is the whole range. A
  lane wanting to trust `customers 17` should re-triage customers, seeded, and the
  method above is reusable as-is.
* And the interval is wide because n=15 is small. **The honest summary is "roughly a
  fifth, and the uncertainty is a factor of six."** A 40-row draw would roughly halve
  it; nothing else about the method needs to change.

### 5 · THE SYSTEMATIC CAUSE — AND IT IS NOT FORGETFULNESS

All three fixes were read back to their commits, and they split two ways:

* **`DEF-357` — the lane KNEW.** `7a6932d`'s body opens *"DEF-357 fixed."* and
  `sample_data.py:602` says *"DEF-357 — give ONE schedule a real version history"*. A
  lane fixed a named defect, said so twice, and **never touched the row**. r11 step 4
  says *close the record*, and every lane reads that as the record of ITS STORY.
* **`DEF-136` and `DEF-461` — nobody could have known.** `a3623f1` is the `DEF-155`
  sweep; it repaired the credit-note sign as one of six assertions that had not been
  running, naming `DEF-085` and `DEF-155` and never `DEF-136`. `c234144` is a
  `DEF-731` frontend copy lane that carried `BEYOND_THE_NINE` along with it —
  plausibly law 11's fifth mechanism, a pathspec commit PUBLISHING a neighbour's work.

**So two of three were COLLATERAL: the fix was a side effect and no human was ever in
a position to close the row.** That is the mechanism, and it explains `DEF-1930`'s 78%
without contradicting this 20% — one lane rebuilt a whole surface and satisfied seven
rows it was not working from. **Staleness concentrates where a sweep or a rebuild
crosses a surface many rows describe, and runs at roughly a fifth everywhere else.**

**Why no gate catches it, and this is the part worth keeping.** `G50` checks a claim
that a defect was FILED; `G51` checks a claim that one is CLOSED. **Both read code and
ask whether the register agrees.** The failure here is the exact inverse — the register
is silent about a fix nothing claims — and no static check can see it, because
answering it means asking whether the described behaviour still reproduces. That is
hard-won law 6's territory (*diff the running app*), and it is why three of these
fifteen took a pytest run to decide and twelve did not.

**The cheap prevention, not built here:** at step 4, ask of the files a commit
touched whether any OPEN register row names them, and print the hits. It is a
reminder, not a gate — a lane that fixes something incidentally cannot be *required*
to know what it fixed, but it can be shown a five-line list.

**Nothing was put to the PO by this lane, and nothing needed to be.** Every verdict
came from the tree. Per law 13, `02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md` were
both grepped before writing this — `OQ-302` (for `DEF-423`) and `OQ-206`/`OQ-244` (for
`DEF-665`) are open and were left open; no new question was minted.

**Closed by this lane, and nothing else in the register was touched:** `DEF-136`
(`a3623f1`) · `DEF-357` (`7a6932d`) · `DEF-461` (`c234144`), each through
`10-scripts/close_defect.py`, three lines changed for three rows. **Open highs read 81
after this lane, not 84.** No product code was written and no defect was fixed — twelve
rows were confirmed still open and left exactly as they were, `DEF-079`'s stale *five*
included.

## 2026-08-28 — G52, THE FOURTH BOUNDARY GATE THE LAST LANE COULD NOT BUILD

*(service-reachability lane · branch `claude/meter-reads-70rxcc` · ids `DEF-2030–2059` ·
`OQ-950–959` and `BR-<MOD>-550–569` UNUSED · shipped in `499a060`)*

The 2026-08-27 entry "THE THREE BOUNDARY GATES, AND WHY THERE IS NO FOURTH" left this
one measured and unbuilt, correctly, over a hole the PO closed the next morning. This
is the fourth gate. The measurement that lane recorded is not the measurement that
worked, and the difference is the point of this entry.

### 1 · THE SCOPE CHANGED FROM A FILE TO AN ACTION, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING

That lane's question was **"which module does nothing import"** — a FILE-shaped
question. Unscoped it gave 69 candidates dominated by Django conventions; scoped to the
🔒 set it gave 6, *"all explainable, zero real offenders"*. Both numbers are correct and
neither finds `DEF-478`, because **`DEF-478` is not file-shaped.** Its six unroutable
discount services live in `apps/rating/discount_services.py`, a file that IS imported,
IS mounted, and serves routes for its other functions.

So the question was asked one size smaller — **"which ACTION has no door"** — and
scoped to `@require_role`.

**Why that scope and not another:** it is a DECLARATION, not a convention. No framework
requires it and no generator emits it; a lane writes `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)` to
say *a human with this role performs this action*. If nothing a human can reach calls
it, the declaration is false. **Not one of the 229 in the tree is a Django artefact**,
which is what the 69-candidate sweep could not say about itself. It is also literally
`DEF-478`'s own probe — *"a probe over every @require_role write function in
apps/rating/discount_services.py against every path() in apps/rating/api.py"* —
generalised from one file to the repo and taught to resolve imports.

**Measured at the tip: 229 role-gated actions across 31 backend files in 10 modules.
200 reach a route a person can get to. 29 do not, in 7 files across 5 modules —
1,838 lines of built, tested, role-gated write behind no door.**

### 2 · THE DEFINITION IS `DEF-438`'s, DELIBERATELY, AND THREE THINGS ARE NOT DOORS

Reachable means what `DEF-438` is being settled on: **a route a person can actually get
to.** The include graph is walked out of `config/urls.py` with G27's own regex — two
gates disagreeing about which routes are mounted would be worse than either — and a
call graph is followed from each mounted module's top-level statements, where
`urlpatterns` lives.

Checked against the tree and **deliberately not counted as doors**: a management
command (that is an operator with a shell), a demo-data seeder (`sample_data.py` calls
`disconnects.schedule_cut`, which means the DEMO can schedule a cut, not that a clerk
can), and a test.

⚠ **It does NOT cover `DEF-438` itself and the docstring says so.** The R1–R7 chain
carries no role decorators; a whole subsystem with no production caller is a different
mechanism at a different scale. `19-execution-sequence.md` expected this gate to catch
it and it does not.

### 3 · THREE FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES, EACH FOUND BY READING THE OUTPUT

Recorded because this is what separates the gate from the version that got thrown away.
**Each of the three read as a confident finding.**

1. **Class-based views. Seven of the first twenty-nine were wrong.** Every user-admin
   action in `apps/identity/services.py` — `add_user`, `deactivate_user`,
   `issue_temp_password` — was reported doorless. They have doors:
   `apps/identity/urls.py` mounts `api.UsersView.as_view()` and the seed only followed
   `path("x", some_function)`. This is `DEF-182` in miniature and it is the same
   mistake the previous lane made with relative imports, one construct over.
2. **String-keyed seam dispatch.** `apps/customers/discounts.py` reaches
   `discount_services.enrol_account` through
   `seams.resolve("rating", "enrol_account", kind="discount_services")` — a name that
   exists in the source only as a STRING. A string constant in reachable code now
   counts as a reach. **That is a deliberate over-approximation**: it also excuses any
   action whose name is an ordinary English word, and it did — `transfers.review` is a
   false negative, named as one in the baseline file so nobody concludes it has a door.
   A gate that cries wolf is worse than one that misses.
3. **`__all__` is not dispatch.** With clause 2 in, `apps/payments/refunds.py` went
   silent, because `payments/services.py` re-exports `"approve_refund"` and
   `"void_refund"` in an `__all__` list. An export declaration is not a call. Both are
   real: **no refund route in the tree reaches either**, so `BR-PAY-014`'s
   second-approval control on money going OUT is enforced nowhere a person can stand
   (`DEF-2032`).

### 4 · THE FIRST RED PROOF PASSED, AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE

Hard-won law 7 says prove a guard RED before trusting it green. The first attempt added
a `@require_role` action with no route to `apps/billing/services.py` and **the gate said
PASS.** The mutation had written `from core.permissions import require_role as _rr`,
and the universe was matched on decorator TEXT — so the aliased action walked out of the
universe in complete silence. Nothing errored; the count simply stayed at 229.

`_is_role_gate` now resolves the decorator through the module's imports to
`core.permissions.require_role`, so both live spellings and any alias are caught, and a
look-alike local `require_role` is not. Two self-test clauses were added for exactly
those two cases. **The live measurement was identical before and after** — 229 and 29
either way — which is corroboration, and it is also why nothing on the tree would have
revealed the hole. Only a mutation did.

### 5 · THE BASELINE IS A NAMED SET OF 29 AND IT EQUALLED REALITY THE DAY IT LANDED

`10-scripts/gates/g52_no_door_baseline.txt`. Not a hard zero: there are 1,838 lines
behind no door, no lane in flight is opening them, and *"a gate that is red from birth
earns a `# noqa` instead of a fix"* (G44's own words). Not a count either — the
`G48`/`G49` ruling applies unchanged: a THIRTIETH action fails at its own name instead
of hiding inside a number, and an action that gains a door turns the gate RED as stale
until its line is deleted, so the list cannot outlive the defect (`DEF-490`).

**There is no exemption file, and that is a decision.** Reachability is computed, so an
action is excused only by a reference a machine can point at. §6 is what exemption
prose costs.

Four failure branches were proved RED against the live tree, one mutation at a time,
and the verbatim transcripts are in the gate's docstring.

**Suite: 39 PASS / 13 FAIL when this lane started; 41 PASS / 12 FAIL at the commit
above.** G52 is one of the two new passes; **the other movement is a sibling's, not
this lane's** — nothing here was fixed and nothing here turned green. The FAIL count
did not rise.

### 6 · THE CHECK `DEF-478` SHIPPED IS GREEN ON A SENTENCE THAT IS FALSE (`DEF-2034`)

`06-backend/tests/test_def400_discount_lifecycle_routes.py:69` excuses
`suspend_discount_for_funding` with the reason **"called by the bill run, never by a
screen"**, and `grep` finds **no caller anywhere in 06-backend outside tests** — not in
the bill run, not anywhere. Its only occurrence is its own `def` line. A discount whose
funding budget is exhausted cannot be suspended by anybody or anything.

Two lines down, the same dict excuses `enrol_account` with *"DEF-478 — the account
discount panel is not built"*, and a door for it now exists. **One exemption list, two
entries, both wrong, one each way.**

This is hard-won law 1 living inside the exemption list of the check written to enforce
it: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. **An exemption reason is prose
and nothing reads prose for truth.** The correction belongs to the `DEF-478` owner and
is filed, not taken.

### 7 · WHAT WAS FILED, AND NOTHING WAS FIXED

`DEF-2030` the disconnect ladder — eleven role-gated actions, 930 lines, and
`customers/api.py` mounts `path("disconnects", disconnects_list)`, a LIST and nothing
else, so a clerk can see the queue and cannot act on one row of it · `DEF-2031` the
transfer wizard, seven actions, 386 lines, same shape one file over · `DEF-2032`
`approve_refund` and `void_refund` · `DEF-2033` three singletons (`close_read_window`,
`delete_version`, `save_and_exit`) · `DEF-2034` §6.

**Nothing went to the PO and no open question was minted.** Law 13:
`02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md` were both grepped first. Every judgment
here is ours — a scope, three false-positive rules and a baseline — and none collides
with a signed rule, none is a ❄️ frozen figure, and none is a fact only the PO holds.
`OQ-950–959` and `BR-<MOD>-550–569` are **unused**.

## 2026-08-28 · THREE WORKFLOWS GET THEIR DOORS — AND THE TWO WIZARDS GET **OPPOSITE** ANSWERS TO THE SAME QUESTION (lane DOORS, `DEF-2030` · `DEF-2031` · `DEF-2032`)

G52 landed the day before this lane started and named **29 role-gated actions that no
route reaches**, 1,838 lines of built and tested write behind no door. Twenty of the
twenty-nine are the three workflows below. Every judgment here is this lane's under law
13 — `02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md` were both grepped first, nothing
collides with a signed rule, nothing touches a ❄️ frozen figure, and nothing is a fact
only the PO holds. **Nothing was put to the PO.**

### 1 · THE QUESTION, ASKED ONCE AND ANSWERED TWICE

Both wizards post ONE payload to ONE address. Both sit on a service layer that exposes
a STAGED sequence — five writes for a transfer, eleven actions for a disconnect ladder.
So the same question falls out of each: **does the one door run the stages server-side
inside one transaction, or does each stage get a route of its own?**

`BR-SHL-019` — *"ONE transactional commit per wizard"* — appears to settle it for both.
**It does not, and reading it as though it did would have built a machine for cutting
somebody's water off without a certified letter.** The rule constrains what ONE WIZARD'S
COMMIT does. It says nothing about whether a sequence of acts spread over three weeks is
one wizard.

The deciding test is not the shape of the service layer. It is **how much real-world time
separates the stages, and whether a precondition of a later stage is a document that
arrives in the post.**

### 2 · THE TRANSFER IS ORCHESTRATED SERVER-SIDE, IN ONE TRANSACTION — *ruled*

`POST /transfers/commit` takes the wizard's whole plan and runs `start_transfer` →
`set_target_unit` → `set_dates` → `elect_money` → `commit_transfer` inside a single
`transaction.atomic()`. The five staged functions get **no routes of their own.**

Three reasons, and the second is the one that decided it:

**(a) The five stages are one clerk at one screen for ninety seconds.** Nothing separates
them but keystrokes. `TransferCommitPlan` already carries exactly the five stages' inputs
and nothing else — `from_account_id` · `to_unit_id` · `out_date` · `in_date` ·
`deposit_carry` · `arrears_follow` — so the orchestration is a re-ordering of a payload
that already exists, not a new contract.

**(b) `uq_transfers_open_from` ALLOWS ONE OPEN TRANSFER PER OUTGOING ACCOUNT, AND THERE IS
NO TRANSFER DETAIL SCREEN.** This is the reason. Staged routes mean five transactions, so
a failure at stage 4 leaves a `transfers` row in `in_progress` against the outgoing
account — and that row **blocks that account from ever being transferred again**, because
the unique index refuses a second open one. `cancel_transfer` is the only way back and
`US-CUS-027 §8` records that no screen shows a transfer in flight, so nobody can find the
row to cancel it. **The failure is silent, permanent per account, and needs a DBA.**
Under one transaction the same failure rolls the `Transfer.objects.create` back with
everything else and the clerk simply retries.

**Worked, with the figure:** a clerk moves `A-10650` to unit `U-4021`, out **2026-09-01**,
in **2026-09-01**, deposit **$153.50** elected to carry and an arrear of **$542.10**
elected to follow. One POST, five writes, one transaction. A second clerk takes `U-4021`
200 ms earlier, so `BR-CUS-017`'s advisory lock inside `_open_account` refuses at stage 5.
**Rows surviving: zero.** `A-10650` has no open transfer and the clerk picks another unit
and goes again. Under five routes the same race leaves **one** `transfers` row on
`A-10650` and that account is un-transferable for the life of the database.

**(c) Django nests `atomic()` as savepoints**, so each staged function keeping its own
`transaction.atomic()` is correct and unchanged — the outer block is what makes the run
all-or-nothing. No engine code was touched.

`money_statement` and `cancel_transfer` DO get routes, and neither is a stage:
`GET /transfers/{id}/money` is `TRF-02.4`'s read, and `POST /transfers/{id}/cancel` is
the way out of an open transfer the **demo seeder** leaves behind — the seeder calls
`start_transfer`, so open rows exist in this tree today that the one-door commit did not
create and cannot clear.

### 3 · THE DISCONNECT LADDER IS **NOT** ORCHESTRATED — EACH ACTION GETS ITS OWN ROUTE — *ruled*

The opposite answer, from the same test, and the code proves it rather than an opinion.

**`schedule_cut` refuses unless `case.tier == TIER_3` and `assert_service_proved(case)`
passes.** Tier 3 is reached by `advance` after statutory waits. `assert_service_proved`
demands `record_proof_of_service` — **a certified-mail receipt, signed by the recipient,
that arrives days later in the post.**

So orchestrating the ladder into one door would mean manufacturing, inside one HTTP
request, a signed receipt for a certified letter that was never sent. That is not a
transaction-boundary preference. It is the one thing `BR-CUS-039` (*certified mail is
REQUIRED on the final tier, and SMS never stands alone*) and `BR-CUS-100` (*a tier-3 cut
must not be schedulable on an unrecorded service*) exist to prevent, and it ends with a
household losing water on a letter nobody posted.

**`BR-SHL-019` IS NOT VIOLATED, AND THIS IS THE POINT THE RULE TURNS ON.** The disconnect
WIZARD's one commit is `schedule_cut`, and that is exactly the one address
`DisconnectWizard.tsx` already posts to. The other ten actions **are not wizard steps.**
They are separate acts by different people on different days, and the ladder is not a
wizard at all — it is a case file.

**Worked, with the dates:** Bramble Bakery `A-11812`, owing **$2,410.00**. `open_case`
**2026-08-14** at tier 1 · `advance` to `TIER 2 · 10-DAY` **2026-08-24** · `advance` to
`TIER 3 · 48-HOUR` and `record_notice` **2026-09-03** · the green card comes back signed
and `record_proof_of_service` records it **2026-09-08** · only now does `schedule_cut`
accept a cut date of **2026-09-14**. **Five acts, twenty-five days, five doors.** The
wizard's own commit is the last one and it is a single call in a single transaction,
which is all `BR-SHL-019` asks for.

### 4 · WHAT THIS LANE DID **NOT** DO, EACH FOR A NAMED REASON

* **No open question was resolved by choosing a value.** `OQ-374` (which segment holds a
  protected row), `OQ-382` (which of the five cut reasons may lawfully cut), `OQ-383`
  (what a crew records when it attends and does not cut), `OQ-384` (whom a new-service
  block binds) and `OQ-385` (what a restricted service is charged) are all still OPEN and
  the engines already refuse correctly on each. **These routes pass those refusals
  through and soften none of them** — in particular nothing here consumes
  `new_service_block_for()`, whose whole point is that `OQ-384` has no subject yet.
* **No `NotImplementedError` stub was added**, because the engines already carry the
  refusals at the right boundary. Adding a second copy in the transport layer would be a
  second place for them to drift.
* **No money figure moves and no rounding happens in this layer.** Every figure on every
  response is the service's own `{stored, display}` pair.
* **`restart_after_closure` gets no route** — it is not one of G52's 29 and already
  reaches one through the close-out path.

### 5 · `DisconnectRuleError` IS TRANSLATED AT THE BOUNDARY, AS ITS OWN DOCSTRING ASKS

`disconnects.DisconnectRuleError` is deliberately not a catalog exception, and its
docstring names the fix verbatim: *"the API boundary that mounts S90 translates this
exception into one catalog code carrying `br_ref` and this sentence, exactly as
`apps/payments/api._as_catalog_refusal` already does for its own."* That is what the new
boundary does, one code — 422 `BIZ_COMPLETENESS` — for the reason payments and billing
both give: picking among the nine BIZ codes per refusal would be the transport layer
interpreting rules it does not own. **Without it every refusal in the ladder is a 500**,
and a clerk meets `BR-CUS-100` as a stack trace.

`G32` is a ratchet — no `message_key` may be raised that does not resolve — so the
refusal travels in `params.detail` under keys that exist, and no new locale key is minted
by this lane.

### 6 · REFUNDS: THE APPROVAL QUEUE IS A READ THE MODEL ALREADY REQUIRED

`approve_refund` and `void_refund` get routes keyed by refund id. They need a third
thing to be reachable at all — **a person has to be able to find the refund** — and that
is not this lane inventing a screen: `apps/payments/models.Refund`'s own docstring
records it as a requirement, verbatim, *"J15 steps 2–3 require the row to be VISIBLE in
an approval queue between the request and the execution"*, and `selectors.refund_row`
was written for S58 and reaches no route either. So `GET /refunds` serves that queue
over the existing row selector and adds no new read model.

**`BR-PAY-014` is Admin-only and stays Admin-only.** Both writes mount `AdminOnly`, not
`AdminOrClerk` — the service's own `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)` mirrored rather than
widened, on the `transfers_list` precedent of matching the layer below instead of
promising a reach the service denies.

**Worked:** a $57.13 refund on `ACC-1042` sits `requested`. An Admin opens the queue,
sees it with **both** acts rendered separately (`BR-PAY-037` — one person may request and
approve in v1 *as long as both acts are recorded separately*), and approves. The cheque
is lost in the post, so the same Admin voids it with a reason; the credit comes back by
exactly **$57.13** through the ledger's own reversing entry and **no row is deleted**
(hard rule 4). Before this lane, none of those three acts had an address.
