## 2026-08-28 · `DEF-2310` + `DEF-2311` — A UTILITY CAN NOW SAY WHAT KIND OF SERVICE IT SELLS, AND THE $45.00 IS REACHABLE WITHOUT A DATABASE CLIENT

**Nothing was put to the Product Owner.** Hard-won law 13: *"EVERYTHING ELSE IS OURS TO DECIDE AND WRITE DOWN. A
judgment call recorded in the decision log with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make
one."* `02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md` were grepped for `BR-RAT-081`, `BR-RAT-090`, `BR-RAT-038`,
`metered`, `unmetered`, `billed_uom`, `OQ-283`, `OQ-303`, `OQ-317`, `DEF-161`, `DEF-495`, `DEF-515` and `DEF-1813`
before a line was written. Every figure below was taken from the repo. **No open question was minted, and §3 says
why the one question that looked open is not.**

### 1 · WHAT A UTILITY CAN DO THAT IT COULD NOT

A refuse utility opens **Settings → Services**, sets trash to **Unmetered**, states its billed unit as **cart**, and
saves. Its next bill for a property with three carts is **`$45.00`** — `3 × $15.00`, priced off the carts standing on
the unit, with nobody typing a quantity anywhere.

**Before this commit that declaration could be made by exactly one thing in the world: somebody typing an UPDATE
against `tenant_services`.** `BR-RAT-081` was ruled on 2026-08-20 (*"yes we have to say service is meter or
unmetered"*), `DEF-495` gave the column a reader on 2026-08-21, `DEF-1813` built the whole bill run behind it on
2026-08-28 — and `grep metered=False` across `apps/` found **one test helper and nothing else**, whose own docstring
said so: *"written on tenant_services directly because no screen writes it yet"*. Eight days of signed rule and
finished engine that no customer could switch on.

`tenant_services.billed_uom` was the same column one over (`DEF-2311`): read by metering, assets and rating through
`selectors.service_billed_uoms()`, **written by nothing**, so every tenant in the product answered `None` and r6.4's
register→billed gate had only its refusing half.

### 2 · WHAT WAS BUILT, IN ONE SENTENCE EACH

* **One write path, extended — never a second one.** `services.update_tenant_service` accepts `metered`,
  `billed_uom` and `conversion_factor` beside the fields it already took, on the same endpoint, in the same
  transaction, tenant-scoped, audited. Two write paths for one fact is how two screens come to disagree.
* **The S8 table shows the declaration on every row, on or off**, and the row's Edit modal is where it changes.
  A setting a tenant cannot SEE is what let this column sit unwritten for eight days.
* **The demo fixture declares trash unmetered and billed per `cart`** through that same audited service — never by
  writing the row — so a fixture cannot reach a column the product cannot.

### 3 · THE FIVE JUDGMENTS, EACH WITH THE ALTERNATIVE THAT WAS REJECTED

**(a) CHANGING THE DECLARATION AFTER BILLS EXIST IS ALLOWED, FORWARD-ONLY, AND WARNS — `BR-TEN-810`.** This is the
question the dispatch called *"a real question, not a detail"*, and it is answered from law already signed rather
than invented: issued bills, lines, payments and journal entries **do not move** (hard rule 4 — a settings screen is
not a correction to anything already billed); reads already recorded **do not move and keep billing** (`DEF-1813`'s
ruling on `DEF-161`: *"a declared-unmetered service that nevertheless has a meter and a GOOD read still bills the
read"*); and it takes effect on the next unpriced bill **in full**, because `BR-MET-710` observes the count at the
SERVICE-PERIOD END DATE, so there is no half-metered period. **Worked: trash declared unmetered on 15 September,
three carts, the 1–30 September cycle unbilled → September bills `3 × $15.00 = $45.00` off the count seen on
30 September; August's issued bill is untouched.**
**REJECTED: locking it once a bill is issued, the way `BR-TEN-042` locks the currency.** A currency lock protects
figures ALREADY STORED from being re-read in a different unit; this changes only how the NEXT quantity is obtained,
and a utility that starts collecting carts in its third year must be able to say so. Instead the save returns
`accounts_on_next_bill`, the same shape `BR-TEN-027`'s forward-only UoM warning already has. **No OQ was minted:
the behaviour is determined by signed law, so a question would have asked the PO to restate their own rules.**

**(b) `BR-RAT-038`'s CONVERSION FACTOR IS REQUIRED ONLY FOR A METERED SERVICE — `BR-TEN-811`.** The rule's own words
are *"read/register unit must match the billed unit…"*: no read, no register, nothing to reconcile. **Trash's default
`primary_uom` is `month` and it is billed per `cart`, and no number converts a month into a cart** — so requiring one
would have made the single declaration `BR-RAT-081` exists for impossible to type. ⚠ **`DEF-1813` hit this from the
other side and its report is the evidence:** it built a version gating the cart count on the declared billed unit and
abandoned it, because *"it turned `DEF-161`'s ruled base-only outcome into a REFUSAL for any tenant that had declared
a service unmetered without declaring its billed unit"*. **REJECTED: applying the gate unconditionally** — it reads
as the safer option and is the one that breaks the feature.

**(c) THE PAIR IS REFUSED AT THE DECLARATION, NOT ONLY AT RATING.** `BR-RAT-038` says a mismatch blocks *rating*;
blocking a bill run three weeks later for a sentence somebody typed on a settings screen is the same refusal
delivered at the worst possible moment. A metered service billed in a different unit with no factor is refused in
the field (`settings.services.factor_required`, `VAL-004`), and **nothing is written** — a refusal that half-wrote
would be worse than none.

**(d) THE DECLARATION IS ACCEPTED ON A PRESENT-BUT-OFF SERVICE.** Since New mandate 4 (PO 2026-08-17, *"we will
provdie full list for all services - they can always select what they want out of it; more is better ; less is
contraint"*) every tenant carries a row for all ten catalog services, so a utility can say how it will bill trash
before switching trash on — the order a real utility works in. **It cannot move a cent while the service is off**:
`unmetered_service_codes()` and `service_billed_uoms()` both filter `enabled=True`. This is the posture
`primary_uom`/`alt_uom` have always had on this path; nothing was loosened.

**(e) AN UNDECLARED SERVICE READS *METERED*, NEVER A DASH.** `service_row` answers `True` for a tenant with no row
at all, which is the column's own safe default and what every bill in the product already assumes. The table prints
"Metered"/"Unmetered" and never the "—" the unwired COUNTS use, because one glyph meaning two things is how a clerk
comes to read an unmetered service as merely unconfigured.

### 4 · ⚠ WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, AND WHO OWNS IT

**THE DEMO TENANT'S TRASH SERVICE IS STILL OFF, AND TURNING IT ON IS ANOTHER LANE'S WORK.** Brazos Bend signs up for
`electric + water`, so `seed_demo` declares trash unmetered and per-cart and **does not enable it**. Switching a
seeded tenant's service on after the fixture has run is `DEF-1250` / `DEF-2490`, in `apps/rating/sample_data.py`,
where a lane is working today; editing that file from here would have been two lanes on one file. **What this
guarantees is that the declaration is ALREADY TRUE the moment that lane switches trash on** — no second migration of
anybody's database and no hand-edited row. It is on the seed's own omissions list, printed by every run.

**REPORTED, NOT FIXED:** an unmetered service still carries a `primary_uom` (`month`, for trash) describing a
register that does not exist. It is harmless — nothing reads it for an unmetered service — and changing
`SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS` would move a default for every tenant provisioned after it. Stated here rather than absorbed.

**NOT TOUCHED:** how the cart count gets its unit. `DEF-1813` took it from the TARIFF and this work is what would
make the alternative viable; re-opening it is a separate decision and was not taken here.

**FOUR NOW-UNUSED CATALOGUE KEYS** — `settings.services.editUom`, `uomTitle`, `uomSave`, `uomSaved` — are left in all
eleven locales rather than deleted. Removing 4 × 11 lines from the highest-churn shared blobs in the repo, on the day
`DEF-1706` lost 44 locale keys to exactly that, buys tidiness with risk. Left for a quieter commit.

### 5 · WHAT DID NOT MOVE

**No money math, no rounding, no golden figure — `golden-verify` stays 33 PASS / 0 FAIL.** No migration and no new
column: all three fields have existed since r6.4 and `BR-RAT-081`. **Every tenant that has declared nothing prices
byte-identically**, because `metered` defaults `True` and `billed_uom` defaults `None`, which are the values every
reader already assumed.

## 2026-08-28 · R1–R7 STEP 3, THE SCREEN HALF: THE DISAGREEMENTS ARE IN FRONT OF A PERSON, AND THERE IS EXACTLY ONE CLASS TO RULE

**No question was put to the PO for any of this.** Hard-won law 13: *"EVERYTHING ELSE IS OURS TO DECIDE AND WRITE
DOWN. A judgment call recorded in the decision log with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure
to make one."* `02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md` were grepped for `shadow`, `disagree`, `summarise`,
`DEF-438`, `DEF-494`, `DEF-1811`, `DEF-1813` and `BR-BIL-039` before a line was written. **`DEF-652` and `OQ-317`
were found ALREADY RULED and neither was re-raised.**

This is **step 3** of the six-step cutover recorded on 2026-08-27 (*"HOW R1–R7 GETS WIRED INTO BILLING — run both,
compare, rule, then switch. Never swap and hope"*): *"**Surface** the disagreements on the pre-commit screen, by
step and by account | what changes on a bill: **nothing**"*.

### 1 · THE JUDGMENT THIS DISCHARGES, AND WHY IT EXPIRED RATHER THAN BEING OVERRULED

The 2026-08-27 lane withheld this panel on a recorded judgment, §4 of *"R1–R7 STEP 3, DELIVERED"*:

> *"A count that is always zero means the chain is not running, and nothing else would say so. Today that count is
> always zero **and** the chain is not running. Shipping the S31.2 panel now would ship the exact reading the
> decision log says to distrust… **The panel lands with the first fact that lets one account be attempted.**"*

**That fact landed the next day.** `DEF-1813` closed on 2026-08-28 — the fourth and last of the four missing facts —
and the shadow now attempts a real account. The judgment was not overruled; its own stated condition was met. That
is why this entry exists rather than an argument.

### 2 · WHAT AN OPERATOR SEES BEFORE COMMITTING A BILL RUN — the actual words

On S31.2 *"Check what we found"*, under a heading **Compare the new pricing**:

> *"We worked out 1 of 1 customers both ways. 1 came out differently. 0 could not be worked out at all."*

Then one table, headed **What came out differently, and how many customers**, with the columns *What differs ·
Where · Customers · Billing today says · The new rules say*.

⚠ **THE FIRST SENTENCE CARRIES FOUR NUMBERS AND THEY ARE ONE STRING.** *"READ THE THIRD AND FOURTH NUMBERS TOGETHER
OR THEY LIE. '0 disagreed' is also what perfect agreement looks like."* They are in a single translated sentence,
in all eleven catalogues, so **no future edit can leave the disagreement count on screen without the attempted
count**. A test asserts it on that element and not on the page.

⚠ **AND WHEN NOTHING WAS COMPARED THE SCREEN SAYS SO IN WORDS**, rather than printing a zero: *"Nothing was worked
out twice, so nothing matched either. Read this as a gap, not as good news."*

### 3 · THE ONE CLASS THERE IS TO RULE, MEASURED THROUGH THE ROUTE ON A REAL RUN

    accounts 1 · attempted 1 · agreed 0 · disagreed 1 · chain_refused 1
    not_attempted 0 · by_step {R1: 1} · blocked_by_reason {}

**Class `R1 · NoPlanInForce` — 1 account (ACC-1042).** The ruled path's own sentence: *"R1: account ACC-1042 has no
plan version in force on 2026-07-01. BR-RAT-007 prices a period on the terms in force AT THE SERVICE DATE; there is
no fallback to today's plan, because that would silently re-price history."* And what the path that bills TODAY was
about to use, on the same row: **Residential Standard (v1) — electric base 18.50 on version 7**.

**THIS IS `DEF-494` ARRIVING AS A MEASUREMENT OFF REAL ROWS** — *"THE LIVE PATH AND THE RULED PATH MEAN OPPOSITE
THINGS BY 'A PLAN IN FORCE'"* — and it is the shape the 2026-08-27 entry calls **the highest-value row in the
exercise**: the chain refuses where the live path produced a number, which is *"a bill that would have gone out on a
guess."* **Ruling it is step 4 and it is the PO's.** Nothing here chooses.

### 4 · SEVEN JUDGMENTS THAT WERE OURS, EACH WITH THE ALTERNATIVE THAT WAS REJECTED

**(a) A SEPARATE ENDPOINT, NOT A MEMBER OF THE FINDINGS BODY.** `GET /billing/runs/{id}/pricing-shadow`. The
findings are the stage a clerk cannot bill without; the comparison is advisory. `compare()` RAISES rather than
reporting parity when it compared nothing (*"an empty comparison is a failure, not a pass"*), so folding it into
`findings_dict` would let an unruled comparison 500 the billable stage. **The separation is structural, not
promised: `runs.py` does not import `shadow_report`**, so a fault here shows an empty panel and cannot stop a run.

**(b) THE REPORT IS OVER THE RUN, AND THE CLASS ROW CARRIES AN ACCOUNT COUNT.** One account disagreeing at R1 and
four hundred disagreeing at R1 are the same class and a completely different decision, so the count travels with
the class and the list is ordered by it, biggest first. Rejected: a per-account list, which is not something a
person can rule from; and a count of OCCURRENCES, which would double an account that disagreed twice.

**(c) A REFUSAL CLASS CARRIES WHAT TODAY'S BILLING RESOLVED, AND IT IS NOT A BILL TOTAL.** A refusal has no chain
figure to put beside a live one, so without this the row would say the new rules will not price the account and say
nothing about the bill that was going out on the old ones. **Phase 1 computes no money** (`exceptions_dict`: *"phase
1 computes no money at all"*), so what is served is the PLAN and, per service, the tariff version and its base
charge — named as what they are. Rejected: composing a total from them, which would invent the figure the run has
not worked out.

**(d) AN ESCAPED EXCEPTION IS `not_attempted`, NEVER `agreed`.** `compare()` raises on purpose when nothing was
compared. Recording that as *"could not be worked out"* with its own sentence puts it in front of a person; letting
it propagate would blank the panel for every OTHER account in the run, **including the ones that did disagree**.

**(e) THE DISPLAY STRING IS A LABEL AND MAY NEVER DECIDE THE COMPARISON.** `$8.0000` and `$8.0049` both display
`8.00` (BR-RAT-087 — the server formats money, the client never does). A panel that compared the DISPLAY strings
would report agreement on a disagreement. The comparison is made inside `resolution_shadow.compare()` on the stored
values; a test pins the pair.

**(f) NO DIFFERENCE IS COMPUTED BETWEEN THE TWO FIGURES, ANYWHERE.** Both are printed side by side and neither is
chosen. `22.00 − 18.50 = 3.50` on screen would be the client deciding which figure is right, which is step 4's
ruling. A frontend test asserts `3.50` is absent from the rendered panel.

**(g) AN AGREED ACCOUNT IS COUNTED AND NOT LISTED.** Its count is in the sentence above the table, so nothing is
hidden — only un-listed. Printing 1,200 rows with nothing to act on is how a screen that matters stops being read;
that is `accounts_for_bill_run`'s own recorded reasoning about closed accounts, applied here.

### 5 · WHAT THE MODULE'S OWN TRAILER SAID, AND WHY IT WAS AMENDED RATHER THAN LEFT

`resolution_shadow.py` carried, in its Lifecycle trailer: *"**THIS MODULE HAS NO PRODUCTION CALLER AND MUST NOT BE
GIVEN ONE YET** … the first legitimate caller is the S31.2 preview withheld above."* **This lane built that
preview**, so the sentence is now false, and a file claiming a guarantee it no longer holds is hard-won law 1 in
reverse. It is amended — **comment only, not one line of logic** — and the amendment is named in the review ledger,
because the file is 🔒 `HUMAN-OWNED` by PO ruling of 2026-08-28 and its markers are unchanged.

**The importer-gate exemption `19-execution-sequence.md` step 3 planned is no longer needed.** That file says the
module *"needs an exemption keyed to `DEF-1811` — not a caller — and the exemption expires the day the connection
size exists."* The size exists (`BR-AST-500`/`BR-MET-500`) and the caller is now the one the method allows, so the
gate, when built, should find it CALLED. Recorded here so the next lane does not add an exemption for a hole that
has closed.

### 6 · WHAT THIS COSTS, MEASURED RATHER THAN CLAIMED — and one thing filed rather than absorbed

`resolve()` is pure and `gather_account` has already loaded the facts, so the comparison itself is CPU and no I/O —
which is the property the whole method rests on. **The ADAPTER is not free**: `resolution_shadow.adapt` resolves
the connection size, the multiplier and the unit row through metering's seams **per account**, and on a 1,200-
account run that is a per-account query pattern. **It is filed (`DEF-2401`) rather than hidden.** Two facts bound
it: it is on no path a bill travels, so it cannot slow a bill run; and the account rows themselves cost ONE query
for the whole run (`prepared.coverage`'s anchors through the seam `prepare_run` already used), not one per account.

`accounts_detail` is unpaginated, deliberately and for `findings_dict`'s own recorded reason — *"a page of it would
make `ready.length` a page size, and the screen would confidently report the wrong number of accounts."*

### 7 · A GUARD THAT PASSED ON ITS OWN MUTATION, AND WHAT FIXED IT (`DEF-2400`)

The frontend case *"renders BOTH figures and computes no difference"* was written asserting `18.50` and `22.00`
**against the page**. Deleting the live-figure column entirely left it GREEN — because `18.50` also appears in the
example SENTENCE two cells to the left. **The check could not distinguish pass from fail, which DEF-182 names as
worse than no check because it is trusted.**

It was caught by mutation before merge and never shipped. The fix is the decision log's own caution, one scope
wider: *"assert against the refusal row's own element, never text that also appears in the page's furniture"* — it
was written about a column HEADING and applies just as exactly to a sibling CELL. The two figure cells now carry
`data-brun` markers and the test reads them; re-run, the same mutation goes red with *"expected `no amount` to
contain `18.50`"*.

### 8 · WHAT DID NOT MOVE

**No money math, no rounding, no golden test — `golden-verify` 33 PASS / 0 FAIL before and after**, and no ❄️
FROZEN B4/B5 figure is read, asserted or moved anywhere in this work. **No migration, no new column, no data
write.** No bill, invoice line, decision or exclusion row is created by reading this panel — asserted twice over,
on a doubled read. Steps 4, 5 and 6 of the cutover are NOT started, and step 5 stays per-step when it is.


## 2026-08-28 · BANK ACCOUNTS ARE NOW CAPTURABLE — DEF-203 built, and the four judgments it needed

**The PO ruling this executes is above** (*"capture bank account in configure. Keep them in section which is
logical"*). Nothing here re-opens it; these are the calls the build had to make underneath it, each written down
with its worked figure so the next agent does not re-derive them differently.

### WHAT A UTILITY CAN DO NOW THAT THEY COULD NOT

**Settings → Configure → Reference data → Bank accounts.** Add *"Chase Operating"* with the last digits
*"4021"*, and it appears in the bank-statement import's step 1 as **Chase Operating ••4021**. Before this, that
picker was empty on every real tenant and could never stop being empty: `bank_accounts` had a model, a unique
key, an RLS policy and two readers, and **the only thing in the whole repo that ever created one was a test
fixture**. Every bank-rec test passed for eleven days because each minted its own.

**No new screen ID was minted and no new layout was written.** The whole frontend half is one row in
`referenceDataConfig.ts`, which is what `BR-SHL-035` means by *"new reference data = a new card + its config"*.

### JUDGMENT 1 · THE MASK IS CAPPED AT FOUR DIGITS, AND THAT CAP IS THE POINT

The model's docstring already said the mask is *"deliberately NOT the account number"*, on B2 §6's posture that
**a column you do not store is a column that cannot leak**. That posture is a comment until something refuses.
A free-text field is a field a well-meaning clerk fills with the whole account number — and then the column we
refused to store is holding it.

**Worked:** `4021` is accepted; `123456789012` is refused with *"Enter the last 4 digits only, or leave it
blank."*; a blank mask is accepted and stored as NULL, so the picker renders the bare name. Four is r10's own
rendering and what a bank statement prints. **This is a build judgment, not a ratified figure** — no signed rule
names a length, and if a utility ever needs five, moving the number is one line and this row is the place that
records why it was four.

### JUDGMENT 2 · THE LIST IS PERMANENTLY IN `UNSEEDABLE_REFERENCE_LISTS`, AND THAT IS NOT A GAP

`DEF-016`'s rule is that a declared reference list is either seeded or carries a written reason. Every entry in
that register so far has been **temporary** — an owning lane that had not landed yet — and both previous entries
came out when their lane shipped. **This one never will.** Nobody but the utility knows what their bank accounts
are called, and a seeded example would be a fake bank account sitting in a picker that imports real money. So
the reason is written out in full and the entry is expected to be permanent. The card shows **0** on a fresh
tenant, honestly, and the reference-data report calls it `empty` rather than `UNEXPLAINED`.

### JUDGMENT 3 · THE FRAMEWORK'S CODE SLOT IS SERVED BY THE NAME — AND IT SHOWS

`bank_accounts` has no `code` column; its identity is `UNIQUE (tenant, name)`. The shared list view draws
Code · Name · <detail> · Used by · Status, so the code slot is served by the NAME — **exactly what
`tax_jurisdictions` has done since 2026-08-09**, not a new idea invented here.

**The consequence is real and is filed rather than hidden.** On an account that has had a statement imported
against it, `used_by` is 1, so the shared Edit form renders **Code read-only** (*"read-only once used"*,
BR-TEN-030) beside an **editable Name** — and because both address one stored column, editing Name still
renames the row. The rename is CORRECT (identity is the row id; the import's idempotency tag is
`bank_account_id`, never the text), but a person reading that form sees a frozen field change anyway. Filed as
**`DEF-2520`** against the shared view, with the fix named there: let a card declare that its identity IS its
name, so the one list view draws a single Name field for the two lists in that shape. **Not fixed in this lane**
— it is another module's screen and it changes what two shipped cards look like.

### JUDGMENT 4 · NOTHING ABOUT A GL ACCOUNT WAS ADDED, AND NOTHING WAS ASKED

`OQ-110`'s closure already rules it: reconciliation resolves `cash` **by designation**, one account per tenant.
So which ledger account a bank account maps to is not this row's business, no field was added, and the question
was **not put back to the PO** — CLAUDE.md law 13. A `gl_account` sent to this list is refused as an unknown
field, by name, rather than dropped silently: a silent drop looks exactly like storage to the person who typed
it. An account number, a routing number and a bank address are refused the same way.

### CAN BANK RECONCILIATION RUN END TO END NOW?

**The bank half can, and that was the defect.** A utility can create the account, import a statement against it,
and see the review with *"Chase Operating"* and *"••4021"* on it — proved by
`tests/test_def_203_bank_account_crud.py`, which mints no `BankAccount` anywhere and reaches the import only
through the card's own door.

**What still stands between a real tenant and a full reconciled month is not this row**: money has to have been
taken and batched first (deposit batches are cut from cleared payments), which is the ordinary payments path and
is unchanged by this lane. Nothing else about `bank_accounts` blocks it — the two consumers named in the PO's
ruling are the picker and the import's idempotency tag, and both are now reachable.

### ONE WRITER, ASSERTED BY A SOURCE SCAN AND NOT BY BEHAVIOUR

The PO's own sentence — *"one writer for one fact"* — is guarded by a test that greps `apps/**` for
`BankAccount.objects.create(` and asserts the answer is exactly `apps/payments/lookups.py`. **A behaviour test
cannot see this failure:** a second writer on S38 would pass every test on the day it landed and only show up
when two screens disagreed about which accounts a utility has.

**Rule written:** `BR-PAY-850`, in `04-docs/05-modules/08-payments/02-business-rules.md`.

### JUDGMENT 5 · TWO RATIFIED REGISTERS NOW COMPOSE — "ROUTED, **OR** WRITTEN DOWN"

`tests/test_reference_data_completeness.py::…def017__every_declared_list_is_routed_by_the_seeder`
asserted **plain equality**: every list in `LOOKUP_LISTS` also has a row in `SEED_LIST_OWNERS`. That was
true of every reference list this product has ever had, and `bank_accounts` is the first one for which it
can never be true — nothing seeds a utility's own banking relationship, ever.

**The amendment is that the two registers DEF-016 and DEF-017 built now compose:** a declared list is
either **routed by the seeder** or **written down in `UNSEEDABLE_REFERENCE_LISTS` with its reason**, and a
list carrying **neither** still fails, which is exactly what DEF-017 asked for. The escape hatch is not a
flag: a sibling test refuses a reason under 120 characters, so using it costs a paragraph a reviewer reads.

**The alternative was worse and is recorded so it is not re-tried.** A fake seed route — a
`seed_reference_list` in payments that handles `bank_accounts` by returning 0 — would have kept the equality
and written a seed-run row saying the list was seeded, which is a claim about a list nothing can ever fill.
It would also have put this lane inside `apps/payments/services.py`, a 🔒 human-owned money path, to add a
function that does nothing.

### THE ONE MEASURED COST, REPORTED RATHER THAN SILENCED

`G14` counts every column heading in `en.json` whose text the r10 prototype does not draw, against a
baseline of **195**. It stands at **228** at this lane's merge point and this lane takes it to **229** —
the *"Last digits"* column on the new card.

**It cannot be avoided and it is not a mistake.** r10 was drawn on 2026-08-16 and is frozen; this card
exists because of a ruling made on **2026-08-28**, and r10 draws no bank-accounts table at all. The gate's
only moves are *fail* or *lower the baseline on a fall*, so a lane doing exactly the right thing must either
worsen a red gate or silence it. **The baseline is NOT raised** — silencing a gate is not a lane's call —
and the gap is filed as **`DEF-2521`** with the fix named there: a written exemption list, the way
`human_owned.txt` and `surface_debt.txt` carry theirs.
### 6 · TWO GATE NUMBERS THIS LANE MOVED, BOTH STATED RATHER THAN BASELINED

**`G12` went RED and is FIXED.** Amending `J1-tenant-lands.md`'s handoff row left
`08-qa/01-e2e/01-journey-story-index.{md,json}` stale; `10-scripts/07-e2e-wiring-index.py` regenerates them and
G12 is green again (308 journeys, 53 activated). Worth knowing for the next lane that touches a journey file: the
index is generated and the gate checks its freshness, so an edit to a journey is two files, not one.

**`G14` ROSE BY EXACTLY 2, AND THE BASELINE IS NOT RAISED.** Measured by removing the two keys and re-running:
**236 with them, 234 without.** The two are the new S8 column headings, `Metering` and `Billed unit`. G14 fails a
heading r10 does not draw — and **r10 was drawn on 2026-08-16, four days before the PO ruled that a service is
declared metered or unmetered**, so there is no r10 column for it and there cannot be. This is `DEF-2521` in its own
words — *"G14's column-heading ratchet has no way to say 'this screen postdates r10', so every post-r10 ruling
raises it"* — filed by another lane the same day. Raising the baseline is how a rule quietly stops being one
(`g31`'s banner says so in terms), so the number stands and the reason is written here instead.

### 6 · ⚠ AND THIS LANE REVERTED TWO REGISTER ROWS ON ITS OWN FIRST PUSH — `DEF-2460`

Stated here and not only in the register, because the next lane reads this log. Commit `462a9df` carried
`10-defect-log.csv` and `14-id-reservations.md` built from a worktree derived at `178aac8` while the tip it was
parented on had moved to `a1f5a46` four commits later. It **deleted the `DEF-2400` and `DEF-2401` rows** another lane
had appended and **put the `DEF-2490` block back to `ACTIVE`** after that lane had marked it `RELEASED`.

**Every check in hard-won law 11 passed on it.** The file count was exactly the 42 paths named; every one of this
lane's own hunks was present; `git show <commit>` displayed only this lane's changes; `git status` was clean; `tsc`
and the suites were green. **The one thing that saw it was `git diff --numstat <pinned-tip> <commit>` read as
ARITHMETIC** — `2 insertions, 4 deletions` on a file where exactly two rows had been edited in place, so two
deletions belonged to somebody else. Restored in `ef5c2c3` by rebuilding both files from `a1f5a46`'s content with
only the two row edits re-applied.

**The fix is not another paragraph.** Law 11 already says all of this — *"PINNING THE TIP DOES NOT PROTECT YOUR BLOB
— IT ONLY PROTECTS THE TREE"* — and this lane had read it and shipped the bug anyway, because the remedy is
something a person must remember at the moment they are busiest. The lane's push helper now resolves
`BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` and the tip once and **REFUSES to build a tree** when
`git diff --name-only $BASE $TIP -- <the named paths>` is non-empty. The general form worth building once is a
shared push script in `10-scripts/` so the check is not re-derived per lane — a helper written for a first push,
when base and tip are the same commit, is a check its own first run cannot test.

### 9 · ⚠ AMENDED THE SAME DAY — TWO THINGS THE LIVE STACK SAID THAT THE TESTS DID NOT

**(a) DRIVEN BY CLICKING, ON A BOOTED STACK, AND IT PRINTS THIS** (hard-won law 6 — *"diff the running app; no gate looks at rendered output"*). Signed in as the seeded utility's own user, a real bill run on cycle `08-E2E`, the pre-commit stage:

> *"We worked out 1 of 2 customers both ways. 1 came out differently. 1 could not be worked out at all."*

and, on the class row: **NoPlanInForce · For example ACC-1101 · customers 1 · billing today: E2E Flat Residential (v1) — electric base 12.00 on version … · the new rules: no amount.** Both readings of *"0 came out differently"* are on ONE screen here — one customer really disagrees, one could not be asked at all — which is the pair this panel exists to keep apart.

**(b) ⚠ AND BEFORE A SIZE WAS TYPED IN, THE SEEDED UTILITY COULD NOT BE ASKED AT ALL.** Measured across every cycle of the demo tenant through the same code the endpoint serves: **9 cycles, 11 ready customers, `attempted 0`, `not_attempted 11`, every one `connection_size_unresolved`.** Recording one connection size through the real write path (`PATCH /assets/{id}`, `size_class: 5/8`) moved that run from `attempted 0` to `attempted 1 · disagreed 1 · chain_refused 1 · not_attempted 1`.

**So step 4 has one class to rule and it rests on one customer, because a size has been typed in for exactly one meter.** The cause is already filed — `DEF-1900`: no control on the asset screens and no SIZE column on the meters import, so only an API call can set one. ⚠ **CORRECTED THE SAME DAY, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE CLAIM: `DEF-1900` IS CLOSED AND BOTH DOORS SHIPPED AT 2.79.7, HOURS BEFORE THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN.** Verified on the tip: a connection-size control exists on `AssetAddWizard.tsx`, `AssetDetailPage.tsx` and `AssetRegistryPage.tsx`, and `import_runs.py` emits a **`Connection size`** column on the meters template. So a utility can load its size backlog **in bulk, today, through an ordinary import** — the comparison is waiting on DATA, not on a build, and this sentence would have sent the next lane to build a door that already exists. The lane that wrote it measured its own starting point and did not re-measure at the merge point, which is the ordinary hazard of five lanes pushing in one afternoon and is not a criticism of it. **The rule this is the third instance of today: a statement about what the product CANNOT do decays faster than any other kind, because it is exactly what the next lane is trying to change** — re-measure it at push time, not at dispatch time. **The consequence is new and is stated here rather than left to be discovered: the comparison cannot be run at scale on any tenant until sizes are loaded**, which is the order `BR-RAT-120`'s own ruling named (*"load the sizes first, switch this on afterwards"*).

### 10 · ⚠ AND THE PANEL COULD TAKE DOWN THE STAGE IT SITS ON (`DEF-2402`, high)

§4(a) argues the comparison is a SEPARATE request so an unhappy comparison can never stop a clerk billing. **The rendering defeated that by the other route.** Over a body without its keys — what a server that predates this endpoint answers — the panel read `accounts_detail.filter(...)` and threw, and React unmounted the whole of *"Check what we found"*.

**Nothing in this panel's own six cases could see it**, because every one of them hands it a well-formed body. What found it was an EXISTING test on a sibling screen (`BillRunWizard.dom.test.tsx`) whose stub answers every request with one generic envelope — before merge.

**The fix is a type guard, and what it does NOT do is the load-bearing half:** an unreadable body renders **nothing at all**, never a row of zeros. Defaulting the counts would print *"We worked out 0 of 0 customers both ways. 0 came out differently."* over a server that never answered — **the exact reading this whole entry says to distrust, manufactured by the client.**

## 2026-08-29 — TWO RULINGS ON THE ACCOUNT UPLOAD, AND THE FROZEN FIGURE THAT DOES NOT MOVE (`CR-047`)

**Context.** The PO read the account-upload walkthrough, stopped at the step that says *"Accounts are on
file either way"*, and gave three instructions in a row. Two of them are rulings and one of them turned
out to be a rule we had already signed and not built.

### Ruling 1 — an account that is created inherits from its unit, whatever its status

PO verbatim: *"if account is created then we need to inherit details form units - otherwise upadling it
later will be big tasks"*.

Recorded as **`BR-CUS-672` (CONFIRMED)**, closing **`DEF-2518`**. `_open_service_agreements` — the only
writer of `service_agreements` on the import path — sat behind `if is_occupying(status)`, and a blank
Status cell resolves to `pending_activation`, which is not a billing status. So the easiest file a
utility can produce loaded accounts wired to nothing, and the receipt counted them as created.

**The judgment this lane made, and it is ours rather than the PO's, so it is written here.**
`_make_occupying` bundled two unrelated things and the ruling only asks for one of them. The
**occupancy guards** — one live account per unit, the boundary day, a start date to activate — belong to
a billing status and stay there, because `BR-CUS-018` says in as many words that a draft never blocks the
unit. The **inheritance** becomes unconditional. `create_account` (S18) and `move_in` (S19) are left
alone: the ruling is about a migration, and widening it to the hand-typed doors would be a scope the PO
did not widen.

**Checked before relying on it, because the obvious worry is two accounts on one service point:** the
bill run selects by billing status, so a draft's links are read by nothing; and `service_agreements` has
no unique constraint on (tenant, service_point), only `ix_sa_tenant_account_started`. Both verified in
the schema, not assumed. What it buys is the whole point of the ruling — **switching a draft on is a
status change and nothing else.**

**Consequence, decided here:** `BR-MET-040`'s plan check moves out of the import path onto activation.
The rule's own text already says *"plan REQUIRED at account activation"*, so this is a correction of
where it is applied, not an amendment, and no re-ratification is entered.

### Ruling 2 — if the account lands, the money lands

PO verbatim: *"if account is created then money is also lands"*, answering the one question this lane
put to them: whether opening balances should post for a partial run or wait for a clean file.

**Worked, so the ruling has a figure attached to it.** A 1,213-row file in which 29 rows are refused
leaves **1,184 accounts** on file and a trial balance showing exactly **those 1,184 opening balances**.
The operator corrects the 29 in `failures.csv`, uploads that file alone, and its balances post as their
own small batch on top. Nothing double-counts, because a refused row contributed nothing the first time.

### ⚠ THE ❄️ FROZEN CHECK — `GT-16` WAS RE-READ AND IT DOES NOT MOVE

`13-change-process.md` step 2 says a frozen B4/B5 figure means STOP and re-sign. One was in range, so it
was read before a line was written. `GT-16` (finance-signed 2026-08-08) says:

> batch check: Σ of all opening JEs = Σ of all imported buckets (fixture batch: 1,213 accounts →
> clearing credit = total migrated AR $184,320.55); re-posting the same batch is idempotent

**It holds exactly, and the reason is specific rather than reassuring.** `write_opening_buckets` writes
the four `ob_*` buckets **only for an account that was created**. A refused row produces no account,
therefore no buckets, therefore nothing on either side of the identity. Both sides shrink together. What
changes is that the FILE may now contain rows contributing to neither side — which the equation never
mentioned. The **$184,320.55** is unchanged because that fixture has no failing rows. And re-running
`failures.csv` is a different run with a different batch id, so it posts its own entry set: not a
re-post.

**So no finance re-sign was entered and HUMAN-GUIDE §6 was not opened.** A later lane that disagrees must
re-derive those two sentences rather than take this entry on trust.

### And the part that was never a change

**`BR-CUS-051` is CONFIRMED and reads *"staged → per-row errors → skip-errors ON → \"N created · N
failed\" summary"*.** That IS the per-record behaviour the PO asked for. It was signed when the import
was specified and never built — stage 4 shipped as one `transaction.atomic()` around the whole file.
Filed as **`DEF-2519` (critical)**, not as a change, because `13-change-process.md` step 1 is explicit
that filing our own misunderstanding as a change converts our error into the customer's requirement.
**The transferable lesson, and it is hard-won law 1 one layer up:** a signed rule that no test asserts is
a comment. `BR-CUS-051`'s test would have been three lines — *a file with one refused row still loads the
other N-1* — and it has never existed.

## 2026-08-29 — THE 500 AFTER THE AUTH ERROR IS LEFT UNDIAGNOSED, BY THE PO'S RULING (`DEF-2515`)

**PO verbatim, closing the question this lane had put to them:** *"Leave it"*.

**What was asked.** The PO reported *"When we tried to upload accounts yesterday with 9000 accounts - it
gave us Auth error and then 500"*. The auth half was traced, filed as `DEF-2515` (critical) and fixed:
above `ASYNC_ROW_BAR` (5,000 rows) the load is deferred to a worker carrying `_JobActor` — an id and no
role, by design — and `customers.update_from_import` demanded one, so every row already on file raised
`AuthError AUTH-002`. The decorator is removed; the permission error is measured as gone.

**The 500 is a SEPARATE fault and was never diagnosed.** The lane offered two ways to pin it — a server
log line or a rough time, or reproducing a 9,000-row run against the demo utility — and the PO ruled to
leave it.

**Recorded here for one reason: so nobody later reads the gap as an oversight and re-opens it.** It is a
deliberate decision not to spend the cycle. What is honestly known:

* the worker records a failure in English and re-raises (`import_runs.py:7653`), which should surface as a
  FAILED JOB on the poll surface rather than a 500 — so the 500 is probably not the auth error's own
  propagation;
* `core.permissions.require_role` reads `getattr(actor, "role", None)` with a default, so the auth path
  raises `AuthError` and never an `AttributeError` — **the tempting "the worker crashed on a missing
  attribute" explanation is ruled OUT**, and a later lane should not re-derive it;
* nothing else about it is known, and this entry does not guess.

⚠ **IF IT RECURS, THE CHEAPEST EVIDENCE IS THE LOG LINE AT THE MOMENT IT HAPPENS**, not a re-reading of
the code — this lane read the code and could not narrow it further. `DEF-2515`'s row carries the same
note so the register and the log agree.

## 2026-08-29 — PRINT IS THE FLOOR ON EVERY CUSTOMER DOCUMENT, AND CANNOT BE SWITCHED OFF (`CR-048`)

**PO verbatim:** *"this is correct - don't switch of print for any document it is awayls on"*, answering the
question this lane put to them: when a utility switches a notification event off ENTIRELY, does the printed
copy survive?

### What was wrong, and it was live

`CHANNEL_FLOOR_BY_SOURCE` carried **one** entry — `invoice`. The reasoning shipped in its own comment and
was correct about the signed documents: `BR-BIL-036` speaks about BILLS, a receipt is marked *"(opt)"* in
A15, and no signed document said a notice must go on paper. **It was wrong about the product.** It left a
utility able to switch off the `notice` kind, which carries the **DISCONNECTION LETTER** — a document the
law makes a precondition of cutting somebody's water off. A setting about reminders could suppress a legal
instrument, and nothing on screen would say so.

### The rule now

**Print is the floor on all four customer document kinds** — `invoice`, `payment`, `notice`, `plan` — and no
rule, no per-channel toggle and no master switch can remove it.

**A15's *"(opt)"* on a receipt is SUPERSEDED by this ruling.** `BR-BIL-036` is unchanged and is now the
narrowest case of a wider rule rather than the only one.

### The judgment this lane made, because the ruling does not state it and law 13 says decide

**The other four source kinds get no floor, and that is not "switching print off" — they have no postal
surface at all.** `bulk_action` is a summary for the clerk who ran a job (its own comment already says *"a
summary for a clerk is not a bill and nothing forces it onto paper"*); `report` and `ledger` are internal;
`test` is the send-test row addressed to the signed-in user, and printing a rehearsal would spend a stamp to
prove nothing. A staff alert has no envelope to go in. The ruling's context was the disconnection letter and
its words are *"any document"* — a bell notification is not a document.

If that reading is wrong, the fix is one line in `CHANNEL_FLOOR_BY_SOURCE` and this entry is where to argue
with it.

### What it costs, stated rather than discovered

Every payment receipt, notice and payment-plan letter now queues a print row it did not queue before. **No
provider is connected — nothing leaves the building** (PO instruction, `CR-048` scope) — so the visible
effect today is a larger print queue on the notifications screen, which is the honest picture of what a
utility would actually be posting.

## 2026-08-30 — A utility's own mark, and what we do when their two colours are unreadable

**Decided by:** the CR-048 wave-D lane. **Not put to the PO**, because law 13 says a judgment call is ours
to make and write down, and because the thing it settles was already raised as an open question with a
recommendation attached (`OQ-800(a)`).

### What was built, in one sentence each

**A utility's logo can now be read back.** Uploading one has worked since 2026-08-09 — it is sanitised,
hashed and audited — and until today **nothing in the product could draw it**. There was no route that
served the bytes, so the app header could not show it, a bill could not print it, and the Settings screen
that says "your logo is on file" showed a plain coloured square instead of the picture. That is
`DEF-192`. `GET /settings/company/logo/file` is that route.

**A utility with no logo now has a mark.** The PO ruled this on 2026-08-16 — *"Create name based or initial
base dummy logo"*, and on how many letters, *"2 letters"* — and it was never built (`DEF-195`). A utility
called **Silver Creek Water** gets **SC**, in its own brand colour. The letters come from the trading name,
falling back to the legal name, then to the name on the signup form, so there is never an empty corner and
never a blank mark.

### The judgment call: their colour, our ink

A utility can choose a pale yellow. White letters on pale yellow cannot be read, and on a bill that is a
legal document a customer cannot read. Three ways out were on the table: accept anything and let them see
the result; **compute the contrast and choose the text colour ourselves**; or refuse a colour pair below a
threshold and tell them so.

**We chose the middle one.** A billing product does not tell a utility that its brand colours are wrong —
they will not accept it, and they are not wrong. What is ours to choose is the text drawn on top, so that
is what moves.

**The figure, and why it makes this safe rather than merely nice.** Picking whichever of black or white
reads better on a colour can never score worse than **4.58 : 1** — for any colour that exists. The
accessibility standard for ordinary text asks for **4.5 : 1**. So the rule cannot produce an unreadable
mark, on any colour any utility will ever pick, which is why it never has to refuse one. A test walks the
whole colour space and checks that 4.58 floor; if anyone changes the rule, that test goes red and names the
colour that broke it.

Concretely: a navy `#1B5E9E` gets **white** letters at 6.68 : 1. The pale yellow `#F5E9A0` gets **black**
letters at 17.05 : 1. Both keep the utility's own colour behind them.

**To overrule this, one number moves** — the threshold and its derivation are in
`06-backend/apps/tenancy/brand.py`, and the Settings screen says the rule out loud to the utility: *"We
never change your colour. The two letters are drawn in black or white — whichever stays readable on it."*

**What is still NOT done, said plainly so "the logo problem is solved" cannot mean two things:** the mark is
drawn **on screen**. Turning it into pixels at print resolution for a PDF is a separate, unbuilt piece of
work — the half of `OQ-257` that stayed open — and bills and notices are a different wave's templates.

## 2026-08-30 — CR-048 wave B task B11: the last thirteen customer messages get a rule, and seven get a sender

**What was true before this, and it is the whole reason the task existed.** Thirteen customer messages had
their wording written, seeded on every tenant, editable on the template screen — and **no switch anywhere
that could send them**. A utility could open *Refund issued*, change the sentence, save it, and no refund
this product ever paid would produce a letter. The settings screen did not list them at all, so nobody
could see what was missing.

All thirteen now have a rule. **Seven of them also send something.** The other five say, on the screen,
that nothing fires them yet, and each names the question that has to be answered first.

**The seven that send, and the moment each one fires:**

| The message | It goes out when |
|---|---|
| Payment-plan instalment reminder | a few days before an instalment is due |
| Refund issued | the refund is actually paid |
| Credit issued | a goodwill credit is put on the account |
| Write-off letter | a write-off is approved |
| Account closed | the account is closed for good after a disconnection |
| Deposit received | a deposit clears |
| Rate plan changed | a clerk moves the account to a different plan and ticks *notify* |
| *(and the payment receipt now also goes by text as well as by post and email)* | |

**The five that are drawn and refuse, and why each one cannot fire yet.** These are not oversights; each is
a thing the product genuinely does not have, and putting a working switch on the screen would be a promise:

* **Statement** — this product has no statement. Not a bill; a statement. Nothing produces one (OQ-1160).
* **Planned outage** — nothing records an outage, and nothing knows which customers are on one (OQ-1161).
* **Autopay set up** — autopay is a tick that records what the customer said, and nothing charges it, so the
  confirmation would promise a payment we cannot take (OQ-1162).
* **Payment plan cancelled** — no plan can be cancelled. The PO removed the only automatic cancellation on
  2026-08-11 (*"nodrop we chase for payments until write off"*) and no staff action replaced it (OQ-1163).
* **Door hanger** — field work is R5, which the PO already ruled (OQ-249). Nothing new is asked here.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE THREE JUDGEMENTS THIS LANE MADE, WITH THE FIGURE OR THE ALTERNATIVE EACH
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**1 · Which "kind" each message rides, decided by a rule rather than one at a time.** Every queued message
declares what kind of document it is, and that decision controls one thing that matters: whether print can
be switched off. The PO ruled on 2026-08-29 that print is always on for four kinds — bills, receipts,
notices and payment-plan letters — so **a message filed under one of those four can never be switched off
completely, and a message outside them can.**

Rather than choose thirteen times, the kind is read off the filing the template library already publishes:
a message the library calls a payments message is a payments message. **The one new kind is `account`**, for
the three letters about an account's own life — closed, deposit, rate change — and **it deliberately has no
always-on print.** BR-NOT-024 names four kinds and adding a fifth would be this build writing a rule only
the PO can write. **The visible consequence, stated rather than smoothed over: a utility that switches
*Account closed* off receives nothing at all, which is what switching it off means.**

**2 · What each message is keyed on, so a second one is never silently swallowed.** The queue refuses to
write the same message twice, and it decides "same" from four things — the utility, the kind, the ROW the
message is about, and the channel. **Get the row wrong and the second message vanishes with no error.**
That is the defect this repo filed on 2026-08-29 (DEF-2512): every payment-plan letter was keyed on the
PLAN, so a customer on a twelve-month plan was chased once and never again.

So each of the seven names the row for its own occasion, never the account: the refund row, the credit note,
the write-off, the disconnection case, the payment that cleared, the plan-assignment row. **A customer can
be given two deposits and moved between plans four times; they get two letters and four letters, because
those are two rows and four rows.**

⚠ **One of them could not use a real row, and that is worth reading.** The instalment reminder and the
missed-instalment letter are two different documents about the SAME instalment — one three days before it is
due, one the day after it is not paid. The queue has no column saying WHICH document, so the two would share
a key and the missed letter would silently disappear into the reminder written four days earlier. The
reminder therefore takes a derived id instead of the instalment's own. **The cost is stated in the code: that
id points at no row in any table.** The durable fix is a column on the queue saying which document a row is,
and every writer that sends two documents about one thing has the same problem waiting.

**3 · Two figures moved, and neither was typed in.** The number of events this platform can notify about
went from **18 to 30**. The number of messages with wording and no rule went from **13 to 0** — and that
second figure is computed from the two catalogues, not stored, so it fell on its own as the events landed.
A tie-out written when the gap was first measured still balances exactly: **0 left, plus 16 adopted, is the
16 the 2026-08-29 teardown counted.** Both ends of that bridge are exercised for the first time.

⚠ **ZERO IS NOT A PROMISE OF THIRTEEN NEW MESSAGES, and the code says so in both places it is reported.**
A message leaves that count when a RULE names it, and a row that refuses by name is a rule. The question
*"how many of these can actually fire"* is a different one, answered per row on the same screen.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WHAT THIS LANE FOUND WHILE DOING IT — five defects, three fixed
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
**The same mistake was already in the product five times, and it is the kind nothing can see.** A queued
message names the wording it will be rendered from, by a short code. Five writers named a code that no
catalogue declares — so the message would have been rendered from nothing at all, and every test passed,
because the column accepts any text.

Three are fixed here: the instalment reminder, and the rate-plan letter, which had **four faults at once** —
undeclared wording, an account-wide key so a second rate change vanished, filed under the payment-plan kind
so the always-on print rule started putting a rate-plan email on paper, and no event at all, so the switch
on the settings screen did nothing. **Its own test passed over all four**, because it checked the shape of a
returned value rather than the message.

Two are NOT fixed and are filed instead (DEF-2500): the two manual notice modals on S35 build their wording
code by joining strings at the call site — *reminder + tone*, *disconnect + tier* — and neither result is a
code this platform seeds. **One of them is the disconnection letter.** Neither modal has a screen behind it
yet, so nothing reaches them today; both belong to the story that owns those modals, not to this lane.

**And a check now exists that would have caught all five**, in one place, over every writer: each pinned
code must be a member of the seeded set. It was proved to fail before it was trusted.

## 2026-08-30 — DEF-2487 / CR-050: the import bar is per target, because a row is not a row

A 1,048-account upload failed on a screen share with four people watching. The dry run was
clean — *"Will create 1048 · Existing records updated 0 · Rows rejected 0"* — and Commit load
answered **HTTP 500** with *"Something went wrong. Nothing was saved — try again."*

### What it actually was, reproduced rather than reasoned about

Under a real gunicorn at the product's own `--timeout 60`
(`06-backend/docker-entrypoint.sh:168`), driving the real load stage over the real accounts
engine against live PostgreSQL:

```
[harness] load stage ARRIVED ref=AB90-4944 run=01a051d7-…
[2026-08-30 08:46:43 +0000] [CRITICAL] WORKER TIMEOUT (pid:27872)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  …/apps/metering/import_runs.py:6958 in _load_accounts_rows
    result = seams.create_account_from_import(
  …/apps/customers/services.py:2022 in _open_account
    _audit(actor, audit_action, account.id, after=selectors.account_detail_dict(account))
  …/apps/customers/selectors.py:1330 in account_row
    positions = _ar_positions_for([account.id])
  …/apps/ledger/reporting.py:1265 in ar_positions
    ar_account_id = _designated_account_id(chart.AR)
  …/gunicorn/workers/base.py:199 in handle_abort
    sys.exit(1)
SystemExit: 1
"GET …/imports/RUN/load HTTP/1.1" 500 0
```

**There is no application exception.** The web worker was SIGKILLed at sixty seconds with the
transaction still open, Django never formed a response, and the browser therefore fell back to
`api.error.unexpected` and printed the reference the CLIENT had minted (`ref AB90-4944` is
`newRequestRef`, not a server trace id — which is why nothing could be looked up against it).
Afterwards the run was still `validated` and **zero accounts existed**, so the sentence on
screen was true and useless.

⚠ **The arrival line WAS in the container log with that exact reference and no closing line** —
`_trace_import_stage` has logged it since `DEF-965`. The diagnosability gap that defect was
filed for is closed; what was missing was anybody reading for *"a stage that opened and never
closed"*.

### The measurement, and why the requester's number is also the right one

`10-scripts/def2487_accounts_bar_benchmark.py`, live PostgreSQL, one transaction per size,
rolled back so it can be re-run at will:

| accounts | load stage | per row | against the 60 s web-worker timeout |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 100 | 12.7 s | 127 ms | 4.7x |
| 500 | 60.5 s | 121 ms | 1.0x — level with the wall |
| 1,048 | 130.6 s | 125 ms | 0.5x — killed |

`ASYNC_ROW_BAR = 5,000` was ratified on 2026-08-22 from a PREMISES measurement of 2.03 ms/row.
An accounts row is sixty times that: it opens an account, inherits its unit's services, plan
and meters, writes an opening balance, posts to the ledger and snapshots the whole
account-detail payload for its audit row — 45 database queries. One bar for five targets is
the arithmetic that produced this defect.

PO ruling 2026-08-30, verbatim: *"can we run anything above 100 recors directly using worker
batch job"*. **The accounts LOAD bar is 100.** At that bar the load finishes in 12.7 s with
better than four times' margin; the cost per row is flat across a tenfold range, so there is no
useful bar between 100 and 500.

### Four judgments this lane made, because no rule covered them (law 13)

**1 · The bar is keyed on (target, STAGE), not on target alone.** Measured on the same
1,048-row file: transform 0.2 s, validate 0.2 s, load 130.6 s. A bar of 100 across all three
stages would push a 101-row file's fifth-of-a-second validate into a worker and make an
operator poll for it. Only the load carries the cost, so only the load gets the low bar;
transform and validate keep 5,000.

**2 · A deferral REFUSES when nothing would run it.** This is the one that could have made
things worse. In production `JOBS_EAGER` is False and `apps/tenancy/tasks.send` swallows a
broker failure by design, so on a deployment with no worker the lower bar would have turned a
visible 500 into an upload that reports success and never happens. `core.jobs` now carries a
dispatch probe; tenancy answers it by pinging Celery's control channel with a **1-second**
timeout, cached for **5 seconds** on a positive answer and never on a negative one (the fix for
*"no worker"* is to start one, and the next thing that person does is try again). A probe that
raises is read as NOT ready — law 3.
Verified live against a real Redis with the worker stopped: `BIZ-STATE
metering.import.no_worker`, **0 job records created**, run left `validated`.
⚠ `JOBS_REQUIRE_LIVE_WORKER` defaults to **True** in `base.py` and is False in
`config/settings/test.py` and nowhere else — the suite is its own worker, and a deployment must
not be able to lose the check by getting one line wrong.

**3 · A queued stage is called STALLED after 30 seconds.** A worker can die in the second after
it answers the ping. A healthy queue claims a message in well under a second, so thirty seconds
is not a threshold anyone healthy crosses; it is small enough to be useful and large enough
that a slow start is not reported as a fault. The server decides it, for the reason it already
computes `pct`: two clients would otherwise each pick their own idea of how long is too long.
The screen's first sentence is the fact a person actually needs — *nothing has been written* —
because the load is one transaction and a job that never ran wrote nothing at all.

**4 · The FAILURES file is served from `validated` onward; the SUCCESSES file still needs a
load.** Both result CSVs hung off the stage-5 Result screen, and a commit that fails never
reaches stage 5 — so the one moment somebody most needs the list of what failed was the one
moment we would not give it to them. Stage 3 has already written `outcome`, `problem` and
`fix_hint` on every row it refuses, so that file has real content before the commit. The
successes half is deliberately unchanged: before a load it would be a header with no rows,
which reads as an answer (`_refuse_results_not_loaded`'s own argument). This SUPERSEDES the
CR-047-widening reading that both halves share the predicate `run.status != "loaded"`; the
predicate was always the successes half's, and two cases in
`tests/test_cr047_per_record_load.py` and `tests/test_cr047_widening.py` were amended to say so
rather than deleted.

### What was proved, and how

* **Before:** HTTP 500, HTML body, 60.8 s wall, `[CRITICAL] WORKER TIMEOUT`, 0 accounts.
* **After, same 1,048-row file, same tenant, same `--timeout 60`:** the request answers in
  **1.175 s**; a real Celery worker runs the load in **128.9 s** and writes **1,048 accounts,
  1,048 service links and $46,814.00 of opening AR**; the gauge reaches 100 % done, `stalled`
  false, run `loaded`.
* That run also answers the third precondition: a deferred stage runs as `_JobActor`, which
  carries an id and **no role** — `DEF-2515`'s defect and `DEF-1108`'s before it. The whole
  accounts load was walked by RUNNING it that way, with an opening balance and a deposit so the
  ledger posting is included, and then again through the real worker on 1,048 rows. Nothing on
  that path demands a role today.

### What this does NOT fix, stated rather than left to be discovered

The per-row cost is untouched: **45 queries and ~125 ms per account**, and a large part of it
is that `_open_account` builds `selectors.account_detail_dict(account)` **twice on consecutive
lines** — once for the audit snapshot, once for the return value — and that dict asks the
ledger for an AR position on an account that cannot have one yet. Moving the work to a worker
means nobody is waiting on it, so it is now slow rather than broken. Filed as **`DEF-2480`**
with the measurement, not fixed here.

## 2026-08-30 — DEF-2496: the pin guard is a trigger, because the foreign key does not exist

**The rule was written and nothing enforced it.** `BR-NOT-025` says a template version that
any sent document points at is archived and never deleted. It is CONFIRMED-derived — it
executes hard rule 4 and `BR-BIL-026`, both already signed — and until today it was a
sentence in a document. Both pins are plain columns, so the database would not refuse the
delete, and the two application checks disagreed about what they refused.

**Two candidate fixes were recorded on the defect and they are not equivalent.** (a) make the
pins real foreign keys with `ON DELETE RESTRICT`; (b) a delete trigger on both version tables
refusing any row with a pin. **We chose (b), and the reason is a measurement rather than a
preference.**

**WHY (a) WAS REJECTED — it is not expensive, it does not exist.** Counted on the development
database before anything was written:

| table | rows | pins that resolve | pins that DO NOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invoices` → `bill_template_versions` | 94 | 94 | **0** |
| `outbound_messages` → `notification_template_versions` | 181 | 87 | **94** |

Those 94 are not corrupt. **`outbound_messages.template_id` is POLYMORPHIC and no document
said so**: every one of the 94 is a `pdf_print` row whose `source_type` is `invoice`, and all
94 resolve cleanly against `bill_template_versions`. So the column carries a letter template's
id on 87 rows and a bill layout's id on 94, and **a single foreign key cannot point at two
tables** — `ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT` would be REFUSED today, on live rows, on 52% of that
table. Two further facts make it worse rather than better: the version tables' unique key is
three columns (`tenant_id, template_id, version_no`), so even the `invoices` side would need a
three-column composite FK written in raw SQL, and `MATCH SIMPLE` leaves a row carrying a
template but no version number unchecked — a hole in the guarantee rather than the guarantee.
And both are money-path tables, so `ADD CONSTRAINT` takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and a full
validation scan on each.

**WHAT WE BUILT.** One `BEFORE DELETE` trigger per version table, the same shape as the
invoice immutability trigger in `billing/0006` and the append-only trigger in
`notifications/0006`. `billing/0025` counts BOTH `invoices` and `outbound_messages`;
`notifications/0017` counts `outbound_messages` alone, because nothing else pins a letter
template. Neither is `SECURITY DEFINER` and each migration writes out why it fails closed
under RLS in every reachable case.

**⚠ THIS OVERTURNS THE REASONING IN `billing/0019`, DELIBERATELY.** That migration wrote:
*"A trigger could count the pins, but it would then be a second implementation of the rule."*
The clause is true and it is not a cost — and it is the argument the notification side had
ALREADY answered when `0019` was written. `notifications/0006` runs a service check and a
trigger and says so in its own words: *"The check here is the readable half — it names the
reason a person can act on — and it is deliberately NOT the only one: a shell, a data
migration and a future endpoint all bypass this function and none of them bypasses the
trigger."* Two implementations is the ratified pattern here, not a smell.

**A SECOND DEFECT FELL OUT OF THE MEASUREMENT AND IS FIXED IN THE SAME BREATH.**
`templates_service.pin_count` counted `invoices` alone, so a bill layout pinned by a printed
bill and by no issued invoice read as **UNPINNED** — and `delete_version`, the function whose
whole job is to refuse that, allowed it. It now also asks notifications by name through
`delivery_seam.template_print_pin_count` (billing never reads `outbound_messages`, B1). **An
unaskable count RAISES rather than returning the invoice figure alone**: deleting a version
because a question could not be asked is DEF-127's mistake pointed at a document instead of at
money.

**WHAT WE DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO, so the next lane does not read it as an oversight.** The two
sides still refuse different things for an UNPINNED version: the letter side refuses to delete
anything that is not a draft (NFR-8, retained forever), the bill side lets an archived-but-
unpinned layout go. Harmonising them would NARROW a ratified delete path, which is a change to
a rule and not a defect fix. `BR-NOT-025` protects a version a document POINTS AT and says
nothing about one nothing points at, so both sides are lawful today. Flagged in the review
ledger row instead.

**PROVED RED FIRST** (hard-won law 7), against live PostgreSQL with no trigger present —
`Failed: DID NOT RAISE Exception` twice, and `assert 0 == 1` on the print-row pin. Five cases
green afterwards; the template suites read 26 passed / 12 skipped on sqlite and green on
Postgres.

**WHO RULED.** The Product Owner, in the working chat session, looking at the deployed

**THE RULINGS, VERBATIM.**

> "i agree - please remove - "Send-time elections" — you're right, it should go. Four switches.
> Three of them do nothing and say so in their own text: "your choice is saved, but nothing
> reads it yet." We built the switches ahead of the features. Only the receipt one is live, and

>
> "Which letter each tone sends" — no good reason to be here. It's a reference table about the

>
> "Letters this utility can produce" — no good reason. That's the Templates screen, duplicated.

> paragraph inside a table cell, repeated on every such row, wrecking the layout. My proposal:
> keep the fact, kill the paragraph — a small greyed marker on the row, and the full sentence
> only when you open that event. Same protection, no wreckage."

> "on template scgeen - why we are showing two names under template name ; autopay - why you
> are howing text - this is internal not required ; used by - why so much text - just show some
> status; past due reminder - you created email SMS print, you can also do that by havng action

**THE COMMON CAUSE, and it is one sentence: PROSE IS BEING RENDERED INSIDE TABLE CELLS.** Every

column ("Not in use yet — closing an account does not send this."), a compliance essay put in a

that reference, and a multi-word kind ("PDF + e-signature") put in a column narrow enough to
wrap it to three lines. A table cell holds a **value**; the sentence explaining the value
belongs in the row's detail. Fixing the nine items without fixing that habit buys a week.

**BR-NOT-018 IS NOT WAIVED — ITS FORM CHANGED.** The unfireable-event fact survives as a small
grey row marker plus the full sentence in the opened event. That is what now satisfies the rule

**ONE LIVE SWITCH MUST NOT BE LOST WITH ITS SECTION.** The receipt election is real and reads
today; it moves into the rules table above as an ordinary row. The three dead switches lose
their UI and **keep their backing fields** — the features they were built ahead of are still
coming, so this is a hide, not a migration. Stated here because a later lane finding an unread
column is otherwise entitled to drop it.

**WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE.** Nothing in this ruling touches a money rule, a B4/B5 frozen
figure, or any stored value. It is nine screen changes and one field-visibility decision, so it
runs the change process' fast path (`13-change-process.md` §5) inside the open CR-048 rather
than opening a new CR.

## 2026-08-30 — DEF-2480: the account snapshot is built once, and the ledger question is left alone

**WHAT WAS WRONG, IN ONE SENTENCE.** `_open_account` ended with two calls to
`selectors.account_detail_dict(account)` on CONSECUTIVE LINES — one for the audit
after-blob, one for the return value — with nothing mutating the account between them.
That dict is the whole S18 detail payload and measures **26 queries** on live PostgreSQL.

**MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER, ON LIVE POSTGRESQL.** The wall-clock half is
`10-scripts/def2487_accounts_bar_benchmark.py`; the query half is the accounts import
LOAD stage timed at 45 rows with the marginal per-row cost taken across a 5-row and a
45-row run.

| | before | after | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| queries per imported row | 107.6 | 83.6 | **−24** |
| ms per imported row (with query capture) | 128 | 95 | −26% |
| 100 accounts | 12.1 s | **9.4 s** | −2.7 s |
| 500 accounts | 59.3 s | **45.2 s** | −14.1 s |
| 1,048 accounts | 128.1 s | **94.6 s** | **−33.5 s** |
| ms/row, benchmark | 121 · 119 · 122 | 94 · 90 · 90 | −26% |
| one account through the S17 door, PostgreSQL | 73 queries · 133 ms | 49 queries · 101 ms | −24 |
| the same door on the sqlite test tier | 64 queries | 40 queries | −24 |

**The delta is 24 on both tiers**, which is what a duplicate looks like when it is real
and not an artefact of one engine.

**THE AUDIT ROW IS BYTE-IDENTICAL AND THAT WAS THE CONSTRAINT, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT.**
Hard rule 7 makes opening an account a money action that writes `audit_log`, and the
after-blob is still the COMPLETE account-detail snapshot. What was removed is a second
build of it, not a field of it. `core.audit.write_row` calls `jsonable(after)`, which
converts eagerly into its own structure, so one dict shared between the audit call and
the return value cannot let a caller reach back into the recorded row.

**Two sibling call sites had the identical adjacent-line shape and were fixed with it** —
`create_master_account` and `activate_account`. `update_account`'s audit is INSIDE an
`if fields:` branch, so hoisting it is a restructure rather than a one-line change; it is
one account at a time on no bulk path and is deliberately left alone.

**⚠ WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY — THE LEDGER QUESTION.** The defect proposed a second
saving: an account being created cannot have an AR position (`write_opening_buckets` runs
after `_open_account` returns), so the snapshot's ledger call could be skipped by handing
`account_row` a supplied `positions`. **We measured it and left it.** It is **3 queries of
the 26** — about 7% of what the duplicate was worth — and taking it means fabricating an
`ArPositions` that says `available=True`. **That is a claim the code would not have
checked.** `available` is not *"this account has no lines"*; it is *"the books could be
asked"*, and a tenant with no AR designation would have an audit row stating the ledger
answered zero when the ledger was never asked. That is DEF-127's exact mistake — an
absence spelled the same way as a zero — written into the audit trail instead of onto a
screen. **Seven percent is not worth a false statement in the evidence**, and the
instruction this lane worked under said so in as many words: if it cannot be removed
without weakening the trail, leave it and say so. It is left, and this is the saying so.

**⚠ THE ASYNC BAR COULD COME DOWN AND WAS NOT TOUCHED.** `ASYNC_ROW_BAR_BY_TARGET` for the
accounts load is **100**, set by a PO instruction on 2026-08-30. The guard behind it is
`bar × ms-per-row ≤ 60 s ÷ 3`: at the old 127 ms/row, 100 rows spent 12.7 s of a 20 s
budget; at the new 94 ms/row it spends 9.4 s, and **the same 3× margin would now justify a
bar of 222.** That is arithmetic about the engine, not a decision about the product —
moving a number the PO named needs their word, so the bar stays at 100.

**`MEASURED_MS_PER_ACCOUNT_ROW` WAS RE-MEASURED, 127 → 94**, in
`tests/test_def2487_accounts_async_bar.py`, with both figures and both dates kept in the
comment. A constant documented as a MEASUREMENT that no longer matches any measurement is
hard-won law 1, and the direction matters: lowering it LOOSENS that guard, which is
correct — the guard's job is `bar × ACTUAL cost`, and refusing a safe bar for a stale
reason is a check that cannot tell pass from fail.

**PROVED RED FIRST** (hard-won law 7). The new guard —
`tests/test_def2480_account_snapshot_budget.py` — was run against the pre-fix code,
verbatim:

    AssertionError: opening ONE account built the S18 detail payload 2 times
      assert 2 == 1
    AssertionError: opening ONE account now costs 64 queries, over the budget of 45
      assert 64 <= 45

**GREEN AFTER:** 17 passed across the new file and the bar suite; 42 passed across the
import suites; 269 passed across the customers suites.

**⚠ TWO PRE-EXISTING FAILURES ON THIS BRANCH ARE NOT OURS AND ARE NOT FIXED HERE.**
`test_us_cus_schema_and_seed.py::…no_reference_list_is_unexplained_or_empty_any_more`
fails on `assert {'bank_accounts'} == set()`, and
`test_us_cus_004_005_move_in_out.py::…the_chain_works_through_the_real_endpoints` errors on
a `move_records.performed_by` foreign key at teardown. **Both were confirmed identical on a
pristine worktree at the branch tip before any of this lane's changes**, so they predate
this work; they are recorded here rather than silently absorbed into a green report.
