## 2026-08-30 — EVERY CUSTOMER DOCUMENT IS FROZEN AT SEND. The twenty unmapped classes are kept, not judged one by one

**THE RULING, VERBATIM.** Put to the Product Owner in plain English with the
recommendation stated first, and answered:

> "My recommendation is to keep all of them. - OKY KEEP THEM"

**WHAT WAS PUT TO THEM, WORD FOR WORD, so a later reader knows exactly what this
signature covers.** They were told: the product has 41 kinds of letter and message;
their own scope table names 21; the other 20 — the "your bill is ready" email,
statements, refund and credit confirmations, deposit and account-closed letters,
autopay confirmation, write-off notice, and four field-service messages — have never
been ruled on; the dispatcher currently REFUSES to send those rather than guess,
which costs nothing today because no email, text or print provider is connected. And
the recommendation, with its reasoning: **keep all of them, because storage is a few
kilobytes a message and the risk runs one way only — keeping a document you did not
need costs almost nothing, and failing to keep one you did need loses it permanently.**
No id was quoted to them and no figure was left for them to look up. This closes
`OQ-1164`.

**⚠ THE IN-APP STAFF MESSAGE IS STILL OUT, AND THIS RULING DOES NOT PULL IT BACK IN.**
Twenty classes are unmapped and only NINETEEN are frozen by this. The twentieth is the
in-app staff summary, which the same PO ruled out by CHANNEL **earlier the same day**, verbatim:
*"we dont have to worry about in-app message those are mostly FYI ; hence we dont have
worry about them"*. A ruling on a LIST does not silently overturn a ruling on a CHANNEL.
A lane that reads "keep all of them" and freezes the in-app channel has contradicted a
live ruling — the exact failure hard-won law 13 describes, where the same subject
answered twice produces two genuine answers that disagree.

**WHY THE PO'S OWN REASONING ALREADY POINTED HERE, which is why this was a
recommendation and not an open question.** Their ruling of 2026-08-30 that created
`BR-NOT-027` said, verbatim: *"otherwie everytime we reproduce it using data in table,
we might change something about it and that is not correct"*. That reason is about
REPRODUCTION FROM DATA and says nothing about legal category — it applies identically
to a refund confirmation and to a disconnection notice. Asking them to sort 19 classes
into legal and not-legal would have been asking them to do work our own recorded rule
had already made unnecessary.

**WHAT THIS COSTS AND WHAT IT BUYS.** A migration: the store's kind list is a CHECK
constraint, so nineteen new kinds is a schema change, not a configuration edit —
which is precisely why the lane that found this refused to widen it on its own and
raised the question instead. That refusal was correct and should be the pattern.

**⚠ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ENTRY, BOTH FOUND BY THE LANE THAT IMPLEMENTED IT.**
It said the in-app ruling came *four days earlier* and dated it **2026-08-26**. Both were
wrong and I introduced them: the repo already held the correct date in two places — a
decision-log row from the `CR-049` lane and a comment in `document_models.py`, both
**2026-08-30, the same day**. Corrected in place rather than footnoted, because a confident
wrong date on a ruling is indistinguishable from a right one to the next reader, and that is
the drift this register exists to stop.
And it said *three* field-service classes; the catalogue has **four**
(`# ── Service & field (4) ──`). The nineteen is unaffected either way.

**WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE.** The four field-service classes are R5 scope (`OQ-249`)
and nothing in this ruling authorises BUILDING them — it says only that when they
exist, they are kept. No print-floor question is touched: freezing a document is
about keeping what was sent, and the channel floor is about which channels a document
must go out on. `BR-NOT-024`'s six kinds are unchanged by this.


## 2026-08-30 — NINETEEN RULED CLASSES BECOME SEVENTEEN FILING CATEGORIES, not nineteen. A lane judgement, with both figures

**THIS IS NOT A NEW RULING AND NOTHING WAS PUT BACK TO THE PO.** The ruling is the
one recorded above the same day — *"My recommendation is to keep all of them. -
OKY KEEP THEM"*, closing `OQ-1164`. This row records a judgement the implementing
lane had to make underneath it, because the rules ran out at exactly one point and
hard-won law 13 says a judgement recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable,
while a question is the failure to make one.

**THE ARITHMETIC, RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN TRANSCRIBED.** The lane computed the sets
from `apps/notifications/catalogs.py` itself instead of reading the prose list:
`CATALOGS` (11) + `AUTHORED_CATALOGS` (27) + `CONTRACT_CATALOGS` (3) = **41 distinct
template classes**, no overlap. Minus the 21 named by `CR-049` step 5b = **20
unmapped**. Minus `staff_bulk_summary`, which is the ONLY class in the catalogue
carrying `CHANNEL_IN_APP`, = **19**. Every figure the PO's signature was given
against reconciles exactly, and a test now re-derives all four on every run so a
forty-second class announces itself instead of quietly inheriting a decision
nobody made.

**THE JUDGEMENT: 19 CLASSES, 17 KINDS.** `OQ-1164`'s closing note says *"Nineteen
new kinds go on the store's CHECK constraint by migration"*, and **the lane did
not do that, deliberately.** A `kind` names the DOCUMENT; `channel` is a separate
column on the same row. The twelve already-ruled kinds are built that way and
collapse 21 template classes onto 12 values — `disconnect_notice_10_day`,
`disconnect_notice_5_day`, `disconnect_notice_48_hour` and `sms_disconnect` are
all `disconnect_notice`; `dunning`, `email_past_due` and `sms_past_due` are all
`dunning_letter`. Two of the nineteen collapse identically:

  * **the printed `statement` and `email_statement` are one document.** A19 rule 1
    legislates for both in a single sentence — *"both the printed statement and
    the statement email must say nothing is due, or customers pay twice"* — so
    they are the same document on two channels, not two documents.
  * **`email_bill_ready` and `sms_bill_ready` are one document**, for the same
    reason `email_past_due` and `sms_past_due` already share a kind.

So the store's list grows **16 → 33**, not 16 → 35. Splitting either pair would
encode the CHANNEL into the KIND, which is the one thing this column is designed
not to do: the model's own docstring says *"a regulator asks for a KIND — 'the
disconnection letter' — never for a table"*, and a regulator asking for "the
statement" would have had to know to ask for it twice. The `(tenant, kind,
stored_at)` index would also have split one document type across two values.

**WHY THIS IS A LANE JUDGEMENT AND NOT A PO QUESTION (law 13).** The PO was shown,
and signed off on, WHICH DOCUMENTS ARE KEPT — nineteen of them. They were never
shown a count of CHECK-constraint values, which is an internal filing detail they
have no way to have an opinion on and which changes nothing they can observe: all
nineteen classes are kept either way. Putting it back to them would have been the
re-ask law 13 forbids. **It is nonetheless written into the human-review ledger
row in plain English, as the second of three things to confirm**, because a
signature covers only what was shown and this was not shown.

**⚠ AND THE PROSE IN THE RULING ABOVE HAS A LOOSE END, RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN
SILENTLY TIDIED.** The decision-log entry and `OQ-1164` both describe *"four
field-service messages"* inside the nineteen and, a paragraph later, *"the THREE
field-service classes are R5 scope (`OQ-249`)"*. The catalogue has **four** and
labels them so — `# ── Service & field (4) ──` — `service_appointment`,
`service_work_completed`, `service_outage_notice` and `service_door_hanger`.
**The nineteen is unaffected either way** (all four sit inside it, and the count
was verified against the catalogue, not the prose), so nothing was reconciled and
no figure was changed; the "three" is a slip in a narrative sentence and the
"four" is correct. All four are treated as R5-gated: each gets a kind and nothing
else, because none of them has a writer that queues it.

**WHAT WAS NOT BUILT, AND WHY THAT IS THE RULING BEING FOLLOWED RATHER THAN A
DEFERRAL.** The four field-service classes have wording and no flow (`OQ-249`,
R5). The ruling says only that when they are sent they are kept. Mapping the class
was the entire cost of honouring that, so no `NotImplementedError("OQ-249")` stub
was needed — there is no boundary being stopped short of, because nothing calls
into one. `catalogs.py` already records the PO's posture here (2026-08-16:
*"wording can exist before the flow that sends it"*). A later lane that finds it
needs more than a kind stops there and raises the stub.

**WHAT ELSE WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE.** The freeze itself is unweakened:
`_mark_sent` still takes the freeze answer as a required argument, and a template
class with no ruled kind still HOLDS rather than being guessed. That hold is now
unreachable from the catalogue — every one of the 41 classes either has a kind or
is in-app, and an in-app row exits as exempt before a kind is read — and it was
kept anyway, because the next class somebody adds will have no kind.

## 2026-08-30 — the rights wording and the email sender each get their own tab under Notifications

**THE TWO RULINGS, VERBATIM.** The Product Owner, walking `v2.86.0` on
Settings → Notifications:

> "Create a seperate tab for this - under notification only"  *(of the "Customer rights wording" block)*

> "Email sender (SMTP) - create seperate tab under notification"

**WHY THESE ARE THE SAME FINDING AS THE OTHER TEN, AND NOT TWO MORE ITEMS.** The
PO has spent today naming one fault on screen after screen: **prose rendered where
a value or a control belongs.** These two are that fault at SECTION scale rather
than cell scale. Neither block is too long for a page; **each is a different
page**, stacked under six cards of ordinary configuration on a screen a clerk
opens to change a sender address. This is the third and fourth instance of the
same move in one day — "Messages needing attention" was the first — which is the
useful thing to notice, because a fifth is likely and the answer is already known.

**WHAT MUST NOT BE LOST IN THE RIGHTS MOVE, and it is the whole reason that block
is verbose.** `BR-NOT-015` says the rights footer's sentences are **not ours to
invent**: disconnection rules differ by state and by utility, the five clauses are
a starting point rather than a regulator's words, and the red warning saying so is
a deliberate refusal to imply otherwise. **The warning travels with the clauses.**
Leaving it behind on the settings page, or softening it in the move, would turn
platform-supplied placeholder wording into apparent legal advice on the most
consequential document this product produces.

**WHAT MUST NOT BE LOST IN THE SMTP MOVE.** Two facts on that card are load-bearing
and neither is decoration: that **configuring it sends nothing** — email is not
switched on, and that is a separate setting on the dispatch card — and that the
secret field holds the **NAME** of a secret in the deployment's own store, never a
password, because this product's database never contains one. Both survive the move
as short labels with the sentence on hover.

**AND ONE SENTENCE ON THE SMTP CARD IS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A LAYOUT PROBLEM.**
It reads: *"no tenant SMTP is configured (a host and a from-address are the
minimum), so under C-12's rule email would fall back to the platform ESP — which
has not landed either. Configure SMTP on Settings → Notifications, or wait for the
platform sender."* It quotes an internal rule id at a water clerk, and it directs
them to the page they are already standing on. That is `DEF-335`'s rule broken
twice in one sentence — the provenance belongs in the code comment and on a
machine field, and an instruction must name somewhere the reader is not.

**SCOPE.** *"under notification only"* — two more tabs on the Notifications
sub-strip that already carries the rules tab and the messages tab. Not new
top-level Settings tabs, and nothing else moves with either.

## 2026-08-30 — THE BACKEND SUITE'S 26 STANDING REDS, TRIAGED. Twenty-four were tests, two are defects, and telling them apart is the whole finding

**THE MEASUREMENT.** On the branch tip, the customers/notifications/templates/accounts
selection ran **26 failed · 1,072 passed**. Every one of the 26 had been standing for at
least a day: the identical selection at `66d3c90`, before the day's four lanes merged,
failed the same cases. **None was a regression from that day's work.**

After this lane: **2 failed · 1,094 passed**, and both remaining reds are filed defects
with the reason written into the test that catches them.

**WHY IT WAS WORTH A LANE.** A suite with 26 standing reds has stopped being a signal.
The next real regression arrives as a 27th red in a list nobody reads — and this triage
found exactly that shape twice. `DEF-738` (a tax cannot be restricted to four of the
platform's eight customer categories) had been reporting itself in plain words since
2026-08-24 and was read as noise; `DEF-2473`, filed today, had never been read at all.
**A red test is not evidence of a bug and it is not evidence of a stale assertion. It is
the ABSENCE of evidence, and the two are indistinguishable in a summary line.**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WHAT THE 26 ACTUALLY WERE — and the pattern is one thing, not twenty-four
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**Twenty-four of the 26 were a test pinning a fact that a later, CORRECT change moved.**
Not one was a stale hand-built fixture of the `DEF-2475` kind, and not one was flaky —
every case failed identically when its file was run alone. Grouped by the ruling that
moved under them:

| The ruling that moved | Cases |
|---|---|
| **PO 2026-08-27 · `DEF-650`** — *"Bascially Premises -> owner = Master account"*; the hallway derivation RETIRED, not kept as a fallback | 2 (`BR-CUS-171` tc1/tc4), plus the premises `owner` column in the import measurement |
| **PO 2026-08-27 · BR-AST-049 / CR-046** — `asset_no` means an EXISTING SMARTBillHub number; a legacy number goes in External reference | 4 (`METER_NO`→`external_ref` auto-detect, two assets-template loads, the units `external_ref` column) |
| **PO 2026-08-27 (REVERSING CR-046 C4)** — *"we use utility provdied account number here … if row dont have account number reject it"* | 2 (the accounts sample must NOT ship a blank identifier) |
| **PO 2026-08-27 · BR-MET-144** — *"2 decimals max, trailing zeros trimmed - this is correct"* | 1 (`412.000000 kWh` → `412 kWh`) |
| **`DEF-630`, 2026-08-24 · G28** — the citation travels as DATA beside the clerk's sentence, never inside it | 5 (four contract classes + the provisioning report) |
| **`DEF-2479` / CR-048 wave I, today** — *"A TABLE CELL HOLDS A VALUE"*; ids off the screen and onto a `*_br_ref` field | 3 (merge-field panel, version history, sample-PDF refusal) |
| **CR-048 wave B task B11, today** — the payment receipt also goes by TEXT, on the SAME event | 2 |
| **`DEF-1713`** — the migrated DEPOSIT is a second money column on the same handoff | 2 (an extra opening JE; two extra receipt keys) |
| **`DEF-545`/`DEF-1108` · BR-MET-098** — the approver is an Owner or Admin, in the engine as well as at the door | 2 (a Billing Clerk was ticking `approved` on a run that crossed the error bar) |
| **`DEF-536` ruling, 2026-08-28** — `4300 Customer discounts` seeded unsigned, awaiting a finance re-sign | 1 |

**THE JUDGMENT APPLIED TO ALL TWENTY-FOUR, and it is the one worth keeping.** A test
amended to a ruling is amended to be STRONGER than the line it replaces, or it is not
worth amending. Three worked examples: `pending_finance_re_sign == []` could only ever
say *nothing is pending* — it went red for a correct change and would have gone GREEN the
day somebody marked 4300 signed with no ruling behind it, so it now pins `["4300"]` and
fails in both directions. The whole-dict equality on the opening-batch receipt said
nothing its three field assertions do not, and made a correct addition look like a
regression. And `test_def962`'s twenty rows now leave `asset_no` as the shipped template
ships it — blank — which is a CLOSER reproduction of *"a person copies the worked row
down"* than the version that typed twenty numbers in.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE TWO THAT ARE DEFECTS, LEFT RED ON PURPOSE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**`DEF-2473` (NEW, this lane) — a returned-payment letter is PRINTED from the EMAIL
template, and the receipt says it went by email when it did not.**
`queue_failed_payment_notice` asks for one channel — email, template
`email_payment_failed` — and BR-NOT-024's print floor (PO 2026-08-29, *"don't switch of
print for any document it is awayls on"*) adds `pdf_print` to the SAME queue write.
Measured on the tip with the email switch OFF: **one row, channel `pdf_print`,
template_code `email_payment_failed`, status `queued`**, and the outcome carries
`payment_failed_notice_queued channel=email` **beside** `channel_switched_off_by_rule
channel=email`, with no email row in the table. S22's result panel groups on exactly
those codes. The receipt path one function up gets this right — it calls per channel with
`receipt` / `email_payment_receipt` / `sms_payment_received`; the bounce path never got
the same treatment. **Not fixed here:** the real fix needs a PRINT class for
`payment_failed`, which `catalogs.LISTINGS` does not have, and touches payments' queue
outcome codes that other suites assert on. The proposed patch is on the defect row.

**`DEF-738` (already filed 2026-08-26, second site of `DEF-684`) — no tax can be
restricted to Agricultural, Institutional, Municipal or Builder-developer.**
`BR-CUS-094` (CONFIRMED, PO 2026-08-24) expanded the signed four to seven plus
`government` as legacy; `rating.TAX_CUSTOMER_CLASSES` is still the pre-ruling four and
rating refuses the other spellings outright. Its own guard has said so in words since the
day the migration ran. Widening it is a money surface owned by rating with BR-RAT-103 to
be read first, so it stays reported rather than patched — and the docstring now says
DO NOT FIX THIS TEST, with the reason, so the next reader does not spend the same hour.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE PROCESS FINDING, which is bigger than either defect
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**Every one of the twenty-four was a lane that changed the product correctly, wrote its
ruling down correctly, and left a test asserting the old world.** The rulings were all
findable — each is quoted verbatim in the code that implements it, which is how this
triage was possible at all. What nobody owned was *"is the full suite green on this
branch"*. `DEF-630`'s own prevention note asked for that on 2026-08-24 and it is still
not built.

**The cheap half of the fix is a habit, not a gate: when a ruling moves a fact, grep the
test suite for the fact — not for the rule id.** `412.000000`, `== (EMAIL,)`,
`"BR-TEN-017" in`, `entries_before == 1`. Every one of the twenty-four would have been
caught by one `grep` in the commit that moved it, and every one cost a later reader an
hour instead.

## 2026-08-30 — CR-049 task 3: THE ROUTE THAT SERVES A FROZEN DOCUMENT, and the three judgements it needed

**The task-2 lane closed with the gap in its own words**, and it is the reason this
lane existed at all:

> *"no endpoint serves a frozen document yet, so a screen could still re-render one
> and nothing I wrote would notice. The guarantee is worth only what the route
> eventually does with it."*

Everything `CR-049` had built by that point — a write-once store with RLS and a
trigger, a dispatcher that freezes before every provider hand-off, `reproduce()`'s
honest two-state answer, 145 passing tests — amounted to **nothing a person could
open**. That is hard-won law 2 with a legal guarantee as its subject rather than a
feature, which makes it the sharpest instance of that law in this repo.

**WHAT SHIPPED:** three routes and one panel.

| | |
|---|---|
| `GET /outbound/{id}/document` | One sent message, reproduced. `AdminOrClerk` — a reprint sits beside the re-send on S35. |
| `GET /documents/{id}` | One frozen document by its own id, hash-verified on the read. |
| `GET /documents/register` | Every document sealed between two dates — the regulator request. `SystemAdminOnly` and audited (step 5f: *"the MOST SENSITIVE OPERATION IN THE PRODUCT"*). |
| The screen | Settings → Notifications → Messages: every queue row carries **"Show what we sent"**, measured at **50 rows** in a real browser. |

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGEMENT 1 · A SINGLE-DOCUMENT READ FETCHES **AS WELL AS** LINKING
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**The rules ran out here and this is the call, with its reason.** `CR-049` step 5d(e)
gives two instructions that pull in opposite directions for a one-document read:
decision 5 says *delivery is a pre-signed URL*, and decision 7 says *the content hash
is verified on read*.

**A PRE-SIGNED URL IS A DIRECT CLIENT-TO-CLOUD READ. OUR CODE IS NOT IN THAT PATH, SO
NOTHING HASHES ANYTHING.** Handing a screen only a link would therefore have quietly
retired the one check that catches a document replaced years after it was written —
the exact hazard decision 7 names — and **every test would still have passed, because
the link works.** That is the shape of hard-won law 1: a guarantee whose failure is
invisible.

So a single-document read **fetches** (verified, refusing loudly on a mismatch) **and
also** issues the four-hour link. The two are not redundant: the fetch is the
guarantee, the link is the delivery.

**THE BULK EXPORT KEEPS THE OPPOSITE TRADE, deliberately.** Step 5f forbids proxying
24 GB through the application, so it hands out links and verification moves to the
consumer. **One document is kilobytes; half a million is a terabyte** — the same
decision cannot serve both, and the split is by size and not by taste.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGEMENT 2 · A TAMPERED DOCUMENT MUST NOT DEGRADE INTO "re-rendered from data"
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The tempting implementation is one fallback: if the bytes cannot be served, answer
`re_rendered_from_data_not_the_original` and let the honest-state sentence cover it.

**That would be wrong, and it would look right.** The two are different facts with
different remedies:

* *"no copy of this was kept"* — nothing was ever stored. Nobody is at fault and there
  is nothing to investigate.
* *"a copy WAS kept and its bytes are now wrong"* — a sealed legal record is damaged,
  and somebody has to be told **that specific thing**.

Collapsing them hides a corrupted seven-year record behind a reassuring caption. So a
hash mismatch and missing bytes are **refusals** carrying `BR-NOT-027` and their own
message keys, never a provenance answer.

**Proved by corrupting the stored object and watching the route refuse**, and asserted
in both directions — one case proves the refusal, a second proves it does NOT arrive
as the honest state.

⚠ **AND THE RUNNING APP PRODUCED THIS STATE BY ACCIDENT, WHICH IS THE BEST EVIDENCE
FOR IT.** During the browser check a fixture wrote its bytes to `/tmp` while the
server reads `06-backend/var/documents`. The panel said, in plain words: *"We have a
record of this document but the file itself is missing, so there is nothing to show.
Please report it."* Nobody designed that walkthrough; the distinction earned its place
within an hour of being built.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGEMENT 3 · THE DATE RANGE'S UPPER BOUND BELONGS IN SQL, SO TENANCY'S SERVICE GREW
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`document_store.manifest()` took `since` and no upper bound. A regulator asks for a
PERIOD — *"the disconnection letters you sent last July"* — and filtering the upper end
in the notifications module would mean reading **every row from July to today** into
the application to draw one table. Seven years in that is most of **532,000 rows**, and
it is precisely the four hours of avoidable latency step 5f says the design exists to
avoid.

So `manifest(until=…)` and `reference()` were **added to tenancy's published service**
rather than reached around — the table is tenancy's and B2 §2 forbids the alternative.
Both are additive with defaults, so no existing caller changes.

`reference()` exists because the register lists **500** records for every **one**
document opened: *"what is this document"* and *"give me its contents"* have different
costs and needed to be separable.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WHAT IS ASSERTED, and the one that would be easiest to lose
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**THERE IS NO RE-RENDER PATH, ASSERTED STRUCTURALLY.** A test parses `reprint_api.py`'s
AST and fails if it imports `rendering` or `template_preview` at all. *"It does not call
the renderer today"* is a fact about today's control flow; `BR-NOT-027` needs a fact
about the module, so that a lane adding a kind-looking fallback — *"if nothing is
stored, at least show them something"* — breaks a test rather than the rule.

**A CROSS-TENANT READ IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO A MISSING ONE**, asserted as equal response
bodies rather than as two refusals. The measured result is worth recording: the only
field that differed was `trace_id`, a per-request correlation id derived from nothing
about the document, which differs between two calls for the same missing id. Every
field that could carry a signal — `code`, `message_key`, `params`, `field_errors` — was
equal. **The assertion finding exactly one benign difference is the evidence the
guarantee holds**, not a reason to relax it.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE PROCESS FINDING, and it is about the tests rather than the code
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The panel was built and its nine DOM cases written. With the panel **not rendered by
the tab** — a control that does nothing, the exact `DEF-007..010` shape — **seven of the
nine still passed.** Only the two that mount the real dispatch home and click the button
went red.

**A component suite cannot see law 2, by construction: it supplies the component
itself.** So a screen half is not proved by testing its component; it is proved by
mounting the surface a person actually reaches and finding the control there. Both
kinds are cheap; only one of them can fail for the reason that matters.

## 2026-08-30 — `DEF-2554`: THE TAMPER TEST WAS FLAKY, THE HASH CHECK WAS NOT. Naming the object a destructive test destroys

**REPORTED AS A CODE DEFECT AND IT WAS A TEST DEFECT, and the distinction was one
command away in either direction — which is why it is written down rather than
quietly fixed.**

The merge lane re-ran `CR-049` task 3's suite on the branch tip and reported the
single most consequential case red:

    tests/test_cr049_t3_reprint_route.py::test_cr049_t3__corrupting_the_stored_bytes_makes_the_route_REFUSE
    E   AssertionError: the route served bytes whose hash does not match the record —
    E   a silent byte change is the one thing BR-NOT-027's store exists to catch
    E   assert 200 >= 400

The same commit passed here three times, including under `-p no:randomly`.

**THE CAUSE:** the filesystem document backend writes **TWO files per document** —
the payload at `<key>` and a `.meta` sidecar carrying the content type and the
digest, because a filesystem has no object metadata. The case reached for
`next(p for p in docs_dir.rglob("*") if p.is_file())`, **whichever the directory
yielded first.** When that was the sidecar, the letter was untouched, the route
recomputed the payload's hash, matched it against the row, and correctly served
the document — and the assertion failed **over correct behaviour**.

**PROVED, not argued.** Forcing the selector to take the sidecar reproduces the
merge lane's failure verbatim (`assert 200 >= 400`); taking the payload refuses
with `notifications.frozenDocument.hashMismatch` on both routes. Five new cases in
`tests/test_cr049_t3_tamper_diagnostic.py` pin **both directions separately**,
because *"it refused"* means nothing without *"it did not refuse when nothing was
wrong"*.

**THE THREE THINGS THE MERGE LANE ASKED, ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE:**

1. **Is the hash verified on read?** Yes. `document_store.fetch()` recomputes it
   and raises `ContentHashMismatch`; the route turns that into a refusal naming
   `BR-NOT-027`, and **does not degrade into `re_rendered_from_data_not_the_
   original`** — asserted, because *"we never kept it"* and *"what we kept is not
   what we stored"* are different facts with different remedies.
2. **Does the pre-signed URL bypass it?** No, and this is now pinned as an
   OBSERVABLE PROPERTY rather than as the order of two statements: a tampered
   document's response carries **no `download_url` and no `http` at all**, with an
   intact-document control beside it so *"no link"* cannot pass on a route that
   never issues one.
3. **Is the checksum on the OBJECT as well as the row (decision 7)?** Yes, on both
   backends: S3 sends `ChecksumSHA256` on `put_object`, and the filesystem backend
   writes the digest into the `.meta` sidecar — which is the very file whose
   existence caused this.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE RULE THIS LEAVES BEHIND, and it generalises past this file
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**ANY TEST THAT MUTATES A FILE IT FOUND BY ITERATION IS ASSERTING ABOUT AN OBJECT
IT DID NOT CHOOSE. CHOOSE IT.** The fix selects the payload by excluding `.meta`
**and asserts exactly one match**, so a backend that later writes a third file
fails loudly instead of silently testing the wrong one.

**AND THE NEAR-MISS IS THE REAL LESSON.** A flaky check is worse than a failing one
because it is trusted, and this one was the proof of the sharpest guarantee in
`CR-049`. Its failure reads *exactly* like a broken hash check, and the obvious
response to *"your tamper test is red"* is to go and fix a hash check that was
never broken — adding a defect to a correct file while the actual fault stays.
**The instruction that came with the report — *"do not weaken the assertion to make
it pass"* — was the right instruction and it was followed: the assertion is
stronger now, and the code it was pointed at needed no change at all.**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

## 2026-08-30 — `DEF-738`: A TAX COULD ONLY BE WRITTEN FOR HALF THE CUSTOMERS THE PLATFORM HAS. The fix is to delete rating's copy of the list, not to widen it

**The defect, as a person would say it.** The platform gives a utility eight kinds
of customer. A tax rule could only be restricted to four of them. So nobody could
write a tax that applies to an **Agricultural, Institutional, Municipal or
Builder-or-developer** customer — the four categories the PO added on 2026-08-24
when they said *"Expand the signed list to seven"*.

**Why nothing ever broke, and why that is the dangerous part.** It failed CLOSED.
`rating.services.TAX_CUSTOMER_CLASSES` was a hand-typed four-tuple and rating
REFUSED any code outside it, so the tax was never stored at all. On screen that
looks exactly like a tax somebody forgot to configure. The nearest thing that
*did* save is an empty class list — which means **every** class, so the workaround
for *"I can only tax farms"* was a levy that reached everybody.

**THE TWO RULES WERE READ BEFORE ANYTHING WAS TOUCHED, because this is a money
surface and the lane that found it deliberately did not patch it.**

* **`BR-RAT-103`** (CONFIRMED 2026-08-21) is *"a tax has four statuses, three of
  them derived — and it prices a bill only inside its effective window"*. It is
  about `is_draft`, `selectors.tax_status` and the `effective_from`/`effective_to`
  predicate. **It says nothing whatever about WHO a tax may be scoped to.** The
  defect row's pointer to it is the pre-merge numbering: the rule that owns the
  customer-class dimension is **`BR-RAT-108`**, renumbered from 103 on
  2026-08-21 when `g17` found five ids each naming two rules (`DEF-490`).
* **`BR-RAT-108`** is the one that governs this, and it *asks for* the widening
  rather than forbidding it: a base charge is narrowed by service → **ACCOUNT
  TYPE** → meter size, `NULL` or `[]` means every class, and *"an unknown class is
  REFUSED, never dropped"*. All three still hold. An account type that the
  platform creates and no charge or tax may name is a dimension with a hole in it.
* **`BR-CUS-094`** (CONFIRMED, PO 2026-08-24) makes the four new codes *"REAL
  categories a plan can be priced for, not display labels"*. A category that can
  be priced and cannot be taxed is half a vocabulary.

**So the four were a stale copy, not a deliberate tax-law subset.** That is the
finding the triage lane asked for, and it is why this did not go back to the PO:
`BR-CUS-094` is already ruled and already seeded, and aligning a validation list
with a vocabulary the platform itself creates is closing a gap a ruling left, not
inventing a rule (hard-won law 13).

**THE FIX IS A DELETION.** `apps/rating/seams.account_type_codes()` reads the
vocabulary from `customers.AccountType.SEVEN_CATEGORIES` + `LEGACY_CODES` — the
module that owns it, through the seam rating already uses for that table. There is
now **no typed copy of the list anywhere in rating**, and a new scan
(`test_def738_rating_holds_no_hand_typed_copy_of_the_vocabulary`) fails the day
somebody writes one. A widened literal would have been the same defect with a
later expiry date.

**FOUR JUDGEMENTS, each with its reason, none of them a PO question:**

**(1) THE MODEL'S DECLARED CONSTANTS, NOT ITS ROWS.** Deriving from the seeded
`account_types` rows would have been the obvious reading of the defect row's
own prescription, and it would have **destroyed the guard that reported this
defect**. `test_def273_the_class_vocabulary_mirrors_the_platform_account_types`
compares rating's vocabulary against the live table; derive from the table and
that assertion can never fail again. Reading the constants keeps it asking a real
question — *does the seed match the ruling?* — and it also keeps a database query
out of a validator that runs once per field, per fixture row. A check that cannot
distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check (`DEF-182`).

**(2) `government` STAYS IN THE LIST.** BR-CUS-094 closes the picker for a
**record's own category**; the same ruling keeps a legacy code *"still a valid FK,
still filterable, still priceable"*. This control is a FILTER over accounts, and
accounts still carry the code. Dropping it would have deleted the restriction from
every tax already scoped to it the next time a clerk opened one — a silent
re-pointing, which is the one thing the ruling forbids by name.

**(3) NOTHING EXISTING IS RE-POINTED, AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN SO THE NEXT READER
DOES NOT HAVE TO RE-DERIVE IT.** BR-CUS-094 says of the CATEGORY ON A RECORD that
*"every existing record keeps its code"* and that re-pointing is a human act per
record. **Widening a list of ALLOWED values re-points nothing.** No stored tax
changes: one saved for `commercial + industrial` is still exactly that afterwards,
`[]` still means every class, and a misspelling is still refused rather than
dropped. Asserted, not asserted-about:
`test_def738_no_stored_tax_is_re_pointed_by_the_widening`.

**(4) THE FRONTEND STAYS A MIRROR, AGAINST `DEF-684`'s OWN POSTURE, FOR A MONEY
REASON.** DEF-684 deleted the account-category tuple and fetched the catalogue
instead, and that was right *there*. Here it would be dangerous: on this control
an **empty list means EVERY class**, so a fetch that failed would render no boxes
and a clerk re-saving a tax restricted to two classes would silently widen it to
all of them. A static list cannot fail that way. What it CAN do is drift — so it
is pinned against the backend **in order and in both directions**, which is the
half nothing had. `endpoints.ts` keeps its entry in `KNOWN_SECOND_SITES` and the
comment there now says why staying is not a deferral.

**THE WORKED FIGURE, and it is the one put in the review ledger.** A 6.25 % levy
restricted to Agricultural, on a $100.00 taxable bill: the farm now pays
**`$6.25`** and the house pays **`$0.00`**. Before the fix the levy could not be
saved, so **the farm paid `$0.00` too** — the register's own words, *"a tax simply
never applies, which looks like a tax that was not configured"*.

**NO SIGNED FIGURE MOVED.** `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py`: **33 PASS, 0 FAIL**,
identical before and after. GT-1..61 unchanged. Nothing here touches a rate, a
base, a rounding or a B4/B5 figure — it changes only which class CODES a
restriction may name.

**PROVED RED FIRST (hard-won law 7), three ways.** The service path fails with
`VAL-005 rating.taxes.unknown_customer_class` on
`applies_to_customer_classes[0]`, once per new code. The derivation case fails on
the four-tuple. And the cross-stack mirror case — which passed at HEAD, because
the two copies agreed with each other while both disagreed with the platform —
was shown RED with the backend widened and the frontend not:
*"the tax wizard's restrict-to control offers `['residential', 'commercial',
'industrial', 'government']` and rating accepts `['residential', 'commercial',
'industrial', 'agricultural', 'institutional', 'municipal', 'builder_developer',
'government']`"*.

**`DEF-748` NEEDED NOTHING — IT WAS ALREADY CLOSED, AND THE INVENTORY IS RED FOR A
DIFFERENT REASON NOW.** The task packet named it as the same drift seen from the
other side (`account_types: (4, 8)`), and it is; but its expected count was moved
to 8 on 2026-08-26 with the PO's *"this si corerct"* quoted inline, and
`test_cr010_reference_list_inventory` no longer mentions `account_types` at all.
What it reports today is `{'owner_categories': (None, 5), 'bank_accounts':
(None, 0)}` — a **new** seeded list with no row in the table, which is already
filed as **`DEF-2522`** and belongs to the lane that seeded it. Left alone, and
said so rather than tidied into this commit.

**THE LESSON, and it is not "add a gate".** The guard for this existed, was
correct from the day the migration ran, and was **red for six days while nobody
read it** — the difference `DEF-748`'s own escape note draws between a check that
is missing and a check that is unread. A second guard would have been a second
thing not to read. So the fix removes the thing the guard was watching: there is
no copy left to drift, and the cross-stack pin fails on the day a divergence is
*written* rather than on the day a ruling makes it wrong.

*Recorded by the DEF-738 lane (claude). Fixing commit `c943e72`, v2.87.2.*

## 2026-08-30 · DEF-2473 · The printed returned-payment letter gets its own class, and the receipt stops claiming an email nobody sent

**THE DEFECT, IN ONE SENTENCE.** `queue_failed_payment_notice` asked for one
channel — email, template class `email_payment_failed` — and BR-NOT-024's print
floor added `pdf_print` to the *same* queue write, so the printed copy of the
bounce letter was pinned to an EMAIL class. Measured on the branch tip with the
email switch off: **one row, channel `pdf_print`, template_code
`email_payment_failed`, status `queued`.**

**THE FLOOR IS NOT THE BUG.** BR-NOT-024 is a signed rule (PO 2026-08-29, verbatim
*"this is correct - don't switch of print for any document it is awayls on"*) and
it was widened from four source kinds to six on 2026-08-30 on a further PO ruling
(*"Im okay with your suggestions, you are correct"*). Both stand untouched. What
the widening exposed is that **a queue write carries ONE template pin for every
channel it names**, so any floored write whose class has no printed form pins the
floor's row to the wrong document. `queue_receipt_for_recorded_payment` has always
had this right — three writes, one class each — and the bounce path was simply
never given the same treatment.

**JUDGMENT 1 — A NEW CLASS, AND IT SHIPS BLANK.** `payment_failed_letter`, kind
*Print*, listed on SET-09 as *"Payment failed / NSF · letter"*. It carries **no
wording**, on BR-NOT-015: a class with no authored body is drawn, named, and
refuses rather than printing something we made up. This is a letter telling
somebody that money they believed had cleared came back; a lane drafting that in
order to close a defect would be inventing exactly what the rule forbids. It is
in `test_def_210`'s `STILL_EMPTY`, so authoring a body goes RED and the lane doing
it has to say which ruling let them.

**THE FIGURE THAT MOVED, AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH A SECOND LOOK.** The SET-09
arithmetic goes from **37 listed · 33 published · 4 offered · 0 with no wording**
to **38 · 33 · 4 · 1**. That last number was put at zero by the PO's 2026-08-18
contracts ruling (*"provide default and allow user to change"*), and this is the
first class to move it back off zero. **That ruling is not reversed**: it was about
the four contracts, all four still carry their offered wording, and none of them
changed. What changed is that a fifth kind of unpublished class now exists — one
held by wording nobody has written rather than by a date only a human can pick.
The assertion *"every listed class must now carry platform wording"* is replaced
by the rule it was standing in for — a listed class has a body **or** a stated
reason, never neither — which is strictly stronger on the 37 it already covered.
Recorded here, and in the review ledger in plain English, because it is a figure
a person may want to overrule.

**JUDGMENT 2 — THE OUTCOME MUST DESCRIBE WHAT WAS QUEUED.** `_queue_one` read
`messages[0]` and reported the channel it *asked* for, so any row coming back was
reported as the email one. With the email switch off that put
`payment_failed_notice_queued channel=email` beside
`channel_switched_off_by_rule channel=email`, with no email row in the table — and
S22's result panel groups on exactly those codes. It now finds the message for the
channel the call is about and reports nothing when there is none. This also closes
a latent version of the same fault on the receipt path, where a later write finds
the earlier one's floor row already queued and would have reported it as its own.

**NEITHER OUTCOME CODE WAS RENAMED, DELIBERATELY.** Both were grepped first.
`payment_failed_notice_queued` has four consumers (two assertions in
`test_cr048_b3_payments_fires_its_events.py`, `receipts.py` itself, and a sentence
in `reversal.py`) and `channel_switched_off_by_rule` has six across three test
files plus its producer. Renaming either would have widened the blast radius past
this defect for no gain, so the printed copy got a **new** code —
`payment_failed_letter_queued` — exactly as the receipt path already gives print,
email and SMS a code each. Every existing consumer keeps working unchanged.

**WHY THIS WAS WORTH DOING TODAY, WITH NOTHING CONNECTED.** No print, email or SMS
provider exists (BR-NOT-013), so no wrong letter has ever been posted. But the
document freeze landed the same morning: a message reaching `sent` has its
artefact stored write-once for seven years under the kind its **pinned template
class** names (`frozen_documents.DOCUMENT_KIND_BY_TEMPLATE_CLASS`). The moment
print is switched on, this stops being a mislabelled queue row and becomes a
permanent legal record filed under the wrong document class — the exact sanity
BR-NOT-027 exists to protect. The new class is mapped to the already-ruled
`failed_payment_notice` kind, which is the PO's own scope line (*"Payment receipt
· failed-payment notice"*) applied rather than a new ruling: the same document on
paper, exactly as `receipt` / `email_payment_receipt` / `sms_payment_received`
already share one kind.

**THE DURABLE HALF, AND WHY NOTHING HAD IT.** Every assertion in this repo names
the class it expects, so it is satisfied by exactly the wrong row. Nothing could
ask *"is this class a form for this channel?"* — `kind` was prose on a catalog row
that only ever reached a screen. `catalogs.CHANNELS_BY_KIND` /
`channels_for_kind` / `class_serves_channel` give that question an answer, keyed
on the exact kind strings and **failing closed** on an unknown one, and
`test_def2473_a_queue_row_matches_its_class.py` reads the whole
`outbound_messages` table after each scenario rather than the rows it went looking
for — because the defect was an extra row nobody had named.

**PROVED RED FIRST (hard-won law 7).** The named case
`test_cr048_b3__switching_payment_failed_email_off_stops_the_letter_not_the_bounce`
was left exactly as written — its docstring says DO NOT WEAKEN THIS — and failed
with `AssertionError: assert 'payment_failed_notice_queued' not in {…}`. The new
guard was then proved by restoring the single-write version: **3 failed, 4
passed**, on `a 'pdf_print' row is pinned to 'email_payment_failed', which is a
form for ('email', 'sms') and not for 'pdf_print'`.

**WHAT WAS NOT FIXED, AND IT IS EIGHT MORE — `DEF-2555`.** The enumeration asked
of it found this is **one of nine**. Safe: `notice` (dunning is Print, the three
disconnect tiers Print + email, writeoff_notice Letter), `invoice` (billing's own
registry), `email_move_out_final` (PDF + email), and `payment_received` — the last
only because its print write goes FIRST, so the floor's addition on the email and
SMS writes dedupes into a correctly-pinned row. **That ordering is load-bearing and
nothing asserted it until today**, which is why the bounce fix writes print first
and says so. Open: `email_refund_issued`, `email_credit_issued`, `email_welcome`,
`email_account_closed`, `email_deposit`, `email_plan_change`, and the two plan
notices — the last two possibly a *different* bug, since `payments/notices.py`
asks for print on purpose against a class catalogued as *Email*. **Left open on
purpose:** closing them needs six print classes nobody has written wording for,
which is a template-library decision and not one lane's to take on the way past.

*Recorded by the DEF-2473 lane (claude). Fixing commit `4de9e7fbaab64489b73884f4a9141dd9e8e9ed9a`, v2.87.3.*
