## 2026-08-30 · THE FRONTEND AND THE GATES TRIAGED — FIVE RED TESTS AND ONE RED GATE, AND FOUR OF THE FIVE WERE THE SAME SHAPE THE BACKEND TRIAGE FOUND

**No PO ruling is claimed.** This is a triage and three judgment calls, recorded
because the rules ran out at the third one.

The backend suite went from 26 standing failures to 3 earlier today, and its
lesson was that **24 of the 26 were one shape: a lane changed the product
correctly, wrote the ruling down correctly, and left a test asserting the old
world.** The frontend and the gates had never been looked at. Two lanes had each
reported the two standing reds as *"not mine, needs an owner"*, which is the
point at which a thing becomes nobody's.

**Measured on the untouched tip before touching anything**, and again after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `npx vitest run` files | 3 failed · 208 passed | **211 passed (211)** |
| `npx vitest run` tests | 5 failed · 3409 passed | **3414 passed · 0 failed** |
| G28 Part 3 | 576 against a baseline of 498 | **541 against 478 — still RED, deliberately** |
| G29 screen-ids | PASS at 103 routes / 96 screens | **PASS at 104 / 97 — and now TRUE** |
| G35 version lockstep | FAIL (lockfile 2.87.2 vs package.json 2.87.3) | **PASS at 2.87.4** |

### 1 · The four import tests — category 1, exactly as predicted (DEF-1693, now closed)

`CR-042` (PO 2026-08-27: *"in all imports - we need 2 option on step 1 insert,
insert & update; replace option is not required"*) withdrew the third write mode.
The code was changed correctly and completely; four tests kept asking for the
radio the ruling deleted, and had been red on the branch for three days.

**DEF-1693 said they could not be fixed without a decision** — two of them assert
`BR-MET-099`'s three numbers, which is kept-and-unreachable code. **That decision
had already been taken the same day:** `OQ-580` CLOSED 2026-08-27, PO verbatim
*"this si correct - a for now, c if it bites"*. Law 13's rule earned its keep
here: the answer was in the repo and re-asking would have manufactured a second,
possibly different ruling.

⚠ **THE REUSABLE FINDING, AND IT COST THE MOST TIME: THREE FACTS HAD MOVED AND
ONLY ONE OF THEM WAS THE RULE.** As well as the withdrawn mode, the radiogroup's
accessible name changed from *"Write mode"* to *"What does this file mean?"* and
the help sentence changed, both because the rail's local `SegmentedField` was
replaced by the one shared `WriteModeChoice` — the consolidation that CARRIED the
ruling rather than the ruling itself. A lane that fixed only the mode would have
gone red twice more. **This is the backend triage's lesson sharpened: grep the
suite for the FACT, not the rule id — and expect a ruling to arrive wrapped in a
refactor that moved three other facts with it.**

### 2 · The close-out screen — category 2, a real defect the test was catching (DEF-2469)

`/:tenant/accounts/:accountId/close-out` was mounted on 2026-08-27 under DEF-724
with no `SCREEN_ROUTES` row. `screenIds.test.tsx` named the missing path in its
own diff and was read past. **This is DEF-710 for the second time**, and that
row's prevention — *"the route and its row are ONE commit"* — is restated.

⚠ **THE HALF NOBODY HAD NOTICED, AND IT IS THE MORE USEFUL ONE: G29 REPORTED
PASS THROUGHOUT.** A route with no row is invisible to every count in
`screen_id_baseline.txt`, so the register read 103 routes / 96 screens over a
product that routed 104 / 97 — and the one gate whose job is *"does every screen
name an id an authority defines"* could not see the screen it was being asked
about, **because it derives its corpus from the very list that was short.** All
four counts rise by one in the fixing commit with that reason written beside
them: the rise is the register catching up with a screen that already shipped.

**Judgment recorded:** the row carries NO A1 id and NO r10 badge. The act is
eleven days younger than r10 and A1 was extracted from r9, so neither authority
numbers it; allocating one would be this lane extending a vocabulary that is not
ours. The visible tag draws nothing on that screen, which is hard-won law 8's
finding and is reported rather than invented.

### 3 · G28 Part 3 — the judgment call, and the one where the rules ran out (DEF-2468)

Part 3 read **576 raise sites against a baseline of 498**, and two lanes had each
measured that same 576 before their own work.

**NONE OF THE 78 IS A LEAK, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** Since the PO's 2026-08-19
ruling, `07-frontend/src/api/client.ts`'s `refusalParams` does
`delete rest.detail` before any catalogue interpolation, so a raise site's prose
reaches the audit row and the server log and **nothing renders it**. The
population is ~390 refusals naming the rule they enforce — the convention this
repo asks for everywhere else. Reconstructed by dumping both sides in a detached
worktree at the baseline commit and diffing on (file, kind, text), because the
stored line carries a line NUMBER that churns: **83 added, 5 removed, net +78**,
reconciling exactly.

**Two real problems underneath, and the count was only the symptom.**

**(a) The corpus was wrong.** Part 3 walked every `.py` under `06-backend/apps`,
sweeping in three classes that cannot reach a screen by any path: `sample_data.py`,
`management/commands/` and `migrations/`. A refusal in any of them surfaces in a
terminal or a deploy log, where an engineer is MEANT to read a rule id. The corpus
already excludes `06-backend/tests` for exactly this reason. Excluding them,
**measured on both sides rather than adjusted by arithmetic** — the corrected gate
was run in a detached worktree at `2d70f19`, the commit that set the baseline:

    baseline commit   498 → 478   (20 excluded)
    today             576 → 541   (35 excluded)

**The ceiling falls further than the measurement does, so this is a tightening.**
Subtraction would have been wrong on the other side — a grep estimate said 539
where the real count is 541, which is why 478 is measured and not computed.

**(b) The instrument is wrong, and this lane only mitigated it.** Parts 1, 2 and
2b each carry a baseline FILE, so a fresh violation fails BY NAME. Part 3 carries
an integer, so *"ROSE to 576"* states the size of the problem and nothing about
its location. **Three lanes have now paid to rediscover the same drift** — the
same cost DEF-1693 and DEF-2164 record for unclaimed red TESTS, in a gate instead
of a suite. Added: a `--list` flag printing every counted site without its line
number, so two commands and a `comm` answer *"is this mine"*; and a FAIL note
naming the five heaviest files.

⚠ **LEFT RED AT 541 AGAINST 478, ON PURPOSE, AND THIS IS THE JUDGMENT.** Clearing
it would mean deleting BR-code citations from ~63 refusal messages across 31
files — destroying engineering value for no customer benefit, in files two lanes
are live in. **Raising the baseline to 541 would have made it green and would
have been making the gate quiet**, which is the precise failure another lane found
earlier today when two real leaks turned out to have been "fixed" by entering
them in this gate's own baseline. A red that is explained is worth more than a
green that was manufactured.

**The durable ask, recorded and NOT done here:** give Part 3 the identity baseline
file Parts 1/2/2b already have. **A count ratchet over a population that correct
work necessarily grows can only ever be red, and a gate that can never pass stops
being read** — which is this repo's own 2026-08-27 gate-family finding, arriving
for the second time at the same gate.

### What is still red, stated rather than left to be discovered

**G28 Part 3 only**, at 541 against 478, for the reason above. Parts 1 and 2b are
green at 0/0 and 24/24 and were not touched. The frontend suite is fully green.

*Recorded by the frontend + gates triage lane (claude). Fixing commits
`7181a31` (DEF-2469) and `ce3ebb8` (DEF-1693); G28 in `c1ba3c1` (DEF-2468, open).
v2.87.4 — which also repairs a version-lockstep breach already standing on the
tip, where the lockfile read 2.87.2 against a package.json of 2.87.3.*
## 2026-08-30 — CR-049 task 4: THE BILL IS KEPT AS THE BILL. Five judgements, and the first one is why the whole task existed

**The task-3 lane closed with the gap in its own words**, and it is the reason this
lane existed:

> *"THE BILL STILL RE-RENDERS. Task 4 has not stored a bill artefact, so
> `BillDocumentPage.tsx` — the page titled *view the bill as sent* — rebuilds it on
> every open."*

That was `DEF-2553`, filed rather than half-wired. It is now **fixed** (`v2.88.0`).

**WHAT SHIPPED:** every bill's HTML and its printable page are frozen at issue into
tenancy's write-once store, keeping them is a precondition of issuing, and
`GET /invoices/{id}/document` serves the kept copy with a provenance a screen must
branch on.

⚠ **AND ONE FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN THE TASK: HALF THE HOLE WAS ALREADY
PLUGGED, AND A REAL POSTGRESQL IS THE ONLY THING THAT SAID SO.** The case that
decides this task first used the obvious lever — a System Admin edits the
`layout_key` on the version a bill is PINNED to. It passed on SQLite, which
`config/settings/test.py` hardcodes. **On PostgreSQL it is refused**, by
`billing_template_version_frozen` (billing migration `0019`), whose own message
is the argument this CR makes: *"only status may change once a version leaves
draft … changing it here would rewrite what those customers were sent without
touching a single invoice row."*

**So the boundary is narrower and sharper than this lane first wrote it:**

| | Protected, and by what |
|---|---|
| the bill's DATA | `billing/0006`'s immutability trigger |
| the tenant's chosen template ROW | `billing/0019`'s trigger — already, since 2026-08-16 |
| **the CODE that draws the page** | ⛔ nothing |
| **the platform's LIBRARY of layouts** | ⛔ nothing — a build that stops publishing a key a pinned row names sends the bill down `_layout_for`'s stand-in door |

**The freeze is still necessary and the proof still holds**, on the two rows a
trigger cannot reach: `tc2` drops a published layout (a rollback) and a re-render
loses the whole "Services this period" band from a bill a customer is holding;
`tc3` changes the layout code. `tc2b` now asserts the trigger, so the protection
that exists is recorded rather than mistaken for a gap by the next lane.

**This is CLAUDE.md hard-won law 14 in a second costume** — its subject is a
poisoned transaction, but its mechanism is the general one: **the suite's
database is not the product's database, so a case can be green and wrong about
production.** Every document this lane had already written led with the edited
template row; all of them were corrected, including the sentence the Product
Owner would have been asked to sign. `apps/billing/frozen_bill.py` · `issue._mark_issued` · `documents_api` ·
`BillDocumentPage`. 13 backend cases, 3 DOM cases, golden 33/33 unchanged.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGEMENT 1 · **THE BILL FREEZES A PDF AND THE LETTER DOES NOT, AND THAT IS NOT AN
INCONSISTENCY**
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The notifications lane recorded, correctly, that print freezes the **TEXT** it hands
the vendor and not a PDF, because *"rendering a PDF at freeze time would freeze a
document the customer never received"* — the exact substitution `BR-NOT-027` forbids.
A lane reading only that sentence would conclude the bill must freeze text too.

**It must not, and the difference is a fact about the code rather than a preference.**

| | The letter | The bill |
|---|---|---|
| What the shipped path produces | the letter TEXT the dispatcher hands a print vendor | **HTML *and* a printable US Letter PDF**, both from `documents.render_invoice`, since 2026-08-11 |
| Would a PDF at freeze time be new? | **YES** — nothing renders one, so freezing one would invent a document | **NO** — `GET /invoices/{id}/document.pdf` already serves exactly those bytes to a clerk |

So the bill freezes both, and **nothing is rendered for the store that the product
does not otherwise produce.** It is the same `render_invoice` call `issue.py` has made
on every bill since `BR-BIL-033` landed, and used to throw away.

⚠ **AND `OQ-149` IS UNTOUCHED AND STILL OPEN.** The page that gets kept is the Base-14
print FLOOR — no logo, no usage graph, no barcode, no tenant CSS — because this product
has no HTML/CSS engine and adding one is a deployment-image decision. **What is frozen
is what is produced.** The day a designed page lands, that is what gets kept, with no
change to the rule. Reporting this as "the PDF is frozen" without that sentence would
overstate it.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGEMENT 2 · **THE FREEZE HAPPENS AFTER THE DUE DATE IS ON THE ROW, NOT BEFORE**
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`issue._do_issue` rendered the bill as `BR-BIL-033`'s precondition **before** writing
`due_date`, and `documents._meta` reads `invoice.due_date` — which is NULL on a draft.

**So freezing that render would have frozen a bill with a dash where the due date
belongs**, while `GET /invoices/{id}/document` served one with the date a minute later.
A frozen document that differs from what every reader sees is worse than no frozen
document: it looks like the guarantee working.

**The fix is one line and it is load-bearing:** `locked.due_date = due_date` is now
assigned on the in-memory row *before* the render. Nothing is saved by that assignment;
it only makes the render honest. **The worked check:** the frozen HTML and a re-render
taken immediately after issue are byte-identical, asserted in `tc1`.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGEMENT 3 · **THE POINTER LIVES ON THE DOCUMENT, NOT ON THE INVOICE**
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The obvious shape is a `document_id` column on `invoices`. **There is none and this
lane added none.** Hard rule 4 forbids an UPDATE on an issued invoice, so a column
written after the status moves would either need the freeze to happen before issue (and
then point at a document for a bill that may not commit) or a carve-out in the
immutability trigger.

`stored_documents.source_type = 'invoice'` + `source_id` already answers it, over the
`(tenant, source_type, source_id)` index, and it is the same shape the letters use. **So
keeping a bill touches no financial row at all** — there is nothing for hard rule 4 to
refuse, and a corrected bill is a new invoice and therefore a new document with no
special case anywhere.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGEMENT 4 · **`require_frozen` CHECKS THE ARTEFACTS, NOT ONLY THE VERDICT — THE
OPPOSITE OF ITS NOTIFICATIONS COUNTERPART**
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`notifications.require_frozen` reads `may_send` alone, and must: an in-app alert and a
send test are EXEMPT, so they legitimately pass with nothing stored.

**A bill has no exempt case. Every bill freezes, every time.** So an outcome that says
yes and kept nothing is a bug rather than a state, and `frozen_bill.require_frozen`
refuses unless BOTH artefacts are present. Two modules, two different checks, one rule —
written down here because the next reader will otherwise "align" them and delete the
stronger one.

**The precondition itself:** `issue._mark_issued` is a new function whose only reason to
exist is that `frozen` is a REQUIRED argument. The status move used to be five
assignments inline. **The ORDER is still the first guarantee; this is the second**, and
it exists because a guarantee enforced only by the order of two statements is one
refactor from being gone (hard-won law 1).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGEMENT 5 · **THE S30 PAGE KEEPS ITS STRUCTURED BANDS; THE NOTIFICATIONS PANEL DRAWS
NOTHING. Same rule, two answers, and the reason is what the screen is FOR**
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Task 3 ruled, correctly, that a reprint panel with no original draws **no document at
all** — *"a re-render under a caption is the defect, and a caption is what nobody
reads."*

**This page is not that page.** Its bands are S30's long-standing view of a bill's own
frozen data, and a clerk on a phone call needs the figures — every one of which is the
frozen figure, because `BR-BIL-030` holds them in a trigger. Deleting them for every
bill issued before today would remove working function to make a point.

**So the split is: the ORIGINAL is drawn when there is one, first, in its own frame;
the bands are always labelled as a rebuild.** What must never happen — a rebuild
presented AS the bill — does not happen in either state.

⚠ **AND THE ORIGINAL IS SHOWN IN A `sandbox=""` FRAME, WHICH IS A REVERSAL OF THIS
FILE'S OWN STANDING REFUSAL.** `BillDocumentPage` has always refused to inject the
server's HTML (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` over customer-supplied text) and that refusal
is still right. A frame with no `allow-scripts` and no `allow-same-origin` is a
different trade: the kept bytes render as their own inert document with no access to
this page. **And it is the only honest way to show the original at all** — re-deriving
the bands and calling that the original would be the defect wearing a better label.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated rather than discovered
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. **The kept page is not handed to a print vendor.** That is the last clause of
   `BR-BIL-036` and it is now the only half still owed; both stated absences that used
   to read *"nothing stores it"* were rewritten to say so.
2. **`OQ-149` is open** — see judgement 1.
3. **Every bill issued before `v2.88.0` is a rebuild and says so.** The precondition
   makes that state unreachable for anything issued from now on, and it is kept because
   a guarantee with no visible failure mode is what hard-won law 1 warns about.
4. **`DEF-2466` was filed, not fixed**: the S30 pin panel labels the frozen PAYLOAD
   *"Locked copy saved"*, which is the data-versus-document confusion this CR records
   being made twice — and it is now doubly wrong, because a real kept copy exists
   beside it.


## 2026-08-30 · THREE FAILURES A PERSON FOUND AND NO CHECK COULD — the build we do not run, a fix list that says "open", and a database two lanes share

Three things went wrong today that every gate, every suite and every lint were green
over. Two were found by a lane reading its own output; one stopped the Product Owner's
deploy. They are one class — **a check that measures something adjacent to the thing
that matters** — and this entry records what was built, what was measured, and the one
place the rules ran out.

Version **`2.89.1`**, all four literals plus `CHANGELOG.md`.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1 · THE GATES DID NOT RUN THE COMMAND THAT BUILDS THE IMAGE (`DEF-2464`, critical)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The PO ran `docker compose build` and it stopped:

```
src/features/notifications/templateChangeTrail.dom.test.tsx(57,3):
error TS2459: Module '"@/api/endpoints"' declares 'ApiClient' locally, but it is not exported.
```

The lane that wrote that file reported `tsc` clean **and was telling the truth about the
command it ran**. `vitest` passed too — it never type-checks at all. What fails is the
image's own command, `tsc --noEmit && vite build`, which type-checks the test files as
well. **So a green branch and a buildable branch were two different things and nothing
could tell them apart.**

**`ci-frontend.yml` already ran `npm run build`, and that is the interesting part.** It
runs only on pushes touching `07-frontend/**`, in a workflow separate from the gate suite
every lane runs before merge. So the one check that would have caught this was neither
reached by the change that broke it nor read by the person who shipped it. **A check
existing is not a check running.**

**BUILT — `G54 image-build`, registered in `run_gates.py` and merge-blocking.** It does
not carry the command: it reads `RUN npm run <script>` out of `07-frontend/Dockerfile`,
resolves that script through `package.json`, and executes it. Change the Dockerfile and
the gate follows; delete the script and clause (a) fails without running anything,
because an image that cannot resolve its own build command is already broken. **A gate
that ran a SIMILAR command would be this defect wearing a different hat**, which is the
whole reason nothing here is typed from memory.

**Measured runtime: 44.5 s** — `tsc` about 33 s, `vite build` 11.06 s over 391 modules;
`npm ci` from a warm cache 3.9 s. For scale the suite already spends 94 s in G4 and 134 s
in G5, so this is the third-most expensive gate and not the most. **It is 45 s and not
the 25 s the ask estimated, and the number is recorded rather than rounded down.**

**THE BACKEND HALF, and what it honestly covers.** `06-backend/Dockerfile` has one
build-stage step nothing else in this repo runs: it derives `requirements.txt` from
`[project].dependencies` with an inline `python -c`. If `pyproject.toml` stops parsing,
the image dies there while `ruff`, `black`, `pytest` and every gate stay green, because
none of them reads that table. The payload is EXTRACTED from the Dockerfile and run
verbatim. ⚠ **It does not cover `pip install`** — resolving the pins needs an index and
minutes — so the clause proves the image can COMPUTE its pin list, not that the list
installs. Said here rather than left to be assumed.

**IT IS NOT `docker build`, and that is deliberate.** No daemon exists in the
environments this suite runs in, so a gate needing one would SKIP everywhere and enforce
nothing.

**RED PROOF (law 7)** — replayed in a scratch worktree at `4e385f0~1`, the tree the PO's
build broke on, not a planted fault:

```
G54 FAIL — the frontend image build command failed: `npm run build`
(`tsc --noEmit && vite build`) in 07-frontend, exit 2. > tsc --noEmit && vite build |
src/features/notifications/templateChangeTrail.dom.test.tsx(57,3): error TS2459:
Module '"@/api/endpoints"' declares 'ApiClient' locally, but it is not exported.
```

Clause (a) proved RED by pointing the Dockerfile at `npm run buildx`; the backend clause
by breaking the `[project]` table header, which reported the real `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError`.

**WIRED, because a gate nothing invokes does not exist (law 2).**
`.github/workflows/gates.yml` now installs Node 20 and runs `npm ci` before the suite —
without it G54 could only ever SKIP — **and a following step fails the job if the G54 or
G55 row in the results reads SKIP**, because `run_gates.py` exits 0 on a skip and nothing
else would say so.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2 · A DEFECT ROW CAN READ `open` WHILE ITS FIX IS ON THE BRANCH — **AND THE JUDGMENT
CALL IS HERE: REPORT, NOT MERGE-BLOCKER**
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Today's status report measured eight `open` rows whose fix is on this branch, three of
them critical. **`DEF-2464` itself was a ninth** — its row read `open` with an empty
`fixed_commit` while commit `4e385f0` carried the fix. Step 4 of
`19-execution-sequence.md` triages FROM these numbers, so a stale row aims a whole lane
at work already shipped (`DEF-1930`, the same shape one surface over).

**THE NUMBERS, measured at tip `4e385f0` over 1,863 commits and 1,088 rows:**

| population | count |
|---|---|
| open rows | 392 |
| **(A)** open + id appears in ANY commit subject | **119** |
| **(B)** A, and `fixed_commit` is empty | **118** |
| **(C)** A, and a fix VERB appears anywhere in the subject | **28** |
| **(D)** A, and the subject CLAIMS THE FIX of that id | **1** |

**(B) is the narrowing the ask proposed and it does not narrow.** A row reading `open`
has an empty `fixed_commit` by construction — 391 of the 392 — so it removes exactly one
row. Measured rather than assumed, and the measurement is why it is not the gate.

**(A) at 119 is a gate people learn to ignore**, which this repo has already ruled about
in as many words (`G44`: *"a gate red from birth earns a `# noqa` instead of a fix"*).

**(C) at 28 cannot distinguish pass from fail.** Read the real subjects and the verb
usually belongs to a DIFFERENT id in the same sentence — `"CR-045 wave G — DEF-1702
CLOSED, and the eleventh bare list is FILED as DEF-1783"` puts a closure verb beside a row
that is correctly open. Shipping it would be `DEF-182` again.

**SO THE DECISION, in two halves:**

* **BLOCKING — `G55 fix-claims`, at (D), hard zero with ONE offender banked by name.**
  A commit subject that claims a fix is a checkable promise about the register, exactly as
  `G50` (prose claims a defect was FILED) and `G51` (code claims a defect is CLOSED) are.
  This is the third member of that family, on the one surface where a claim is timestamped
  and immutable. It finds one row today and that is the honest yield — `G50`'s own docstring
  records the identical choice, where the broad version reported 24 dangling ids that were
  nearly all artefacts of the check and was thrown away for the narrow question.
* **REPORTED — (A) at 119**, printed in G55's own detail line on every gate run, listed by
  `g55_commit_fix_claims.py --report`, and added to `10-scripts/defect_report.py`, which is
  the script step 4 triages from. **A report that reaches the person doing the triage is
  worth more than a red nobody reads.**

⚠ **AND THE CHECK SAYS WHAT IT DOES NOT KNOW, in its own output.** An id in a commit
subject is NOT proof of a fix. Six of the nine known-stale rows are named by subjects with
no verb at all — `"DEF-2515 (critical) — the worker carries no role, so the import writer
must not demand one"` is a fix and `"DEF-2487 — the accounts import commit 500,
reproduced"` is not, and no regex separates them. **Two of the nine (`DEF-2503`,
`DEF-2476`) appear in no commit subject whatsoever**, so the report is not even a complete
list of what is stale. Every one of those sentences is printed with the number.

**BANKED, BY NAME AND NOT BY COUNT:** `DEF-1712`, claimed fixed by `e3adf2e6` and still
reading `open`. Banked rather than closed because closing it is a governance judgment
about a PO ruling on the CR-040 exclusion list and not a tooling lane's call — the posture
`G48`/`G49` already take, and the reason they bank by name: a SECOND offender fails at its
own name instead of hiding in a count, and a bank left behind after its row closes goes RED
as stale.

**`DEF-2464` WAS CLOSED** through `close_defect.py` against `4e385f0` — one line changed,
`1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)`. It is the first row this work corrected and it was found
by the report it justifies.

**RED PROOF (law 7), on real data with the bank emptied:**

```
G55 FAIL — 1 commit subject(s) claim a fix for a row that still reads open, baseline 0
(0 banked by name): commit e3adf2e6 claims DEF-1712 is fixed ("DEF-1712 resolved without
the PO — the exclusion list was a lane's inf") and the register row reads 'open'.
```

A mistyped bank entry and a bank whose row has since closed were each proved RED too.

⚠ **AND THE FIRST DRAFT WOULD HAVE SKIPPED EVERYWHERE, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING.** It
refused to run on a shallow clone, keyed on `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` — and
**this repo's own checkouts report that flag `true` while holding 1,863 commits.** The
gate SKIPped on the machine it was written on and would have SKIPped in CI: a check whose
only reachable outcome is SKIP, which is the family of failure G50/G51/G55 exist to close.
It reads DEPTH now (`< 50` readable commits is a truncation, not a branch), and
`gates.yml` sets `fetch-depth: 0` so the enforcement point never takes that branch.
Proved by running it in a three-commit repository.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3 · A `git worktree` ISOLATES FILES AND REFS AND NOT THE DATABASE (`DEF-054`, filed
2026-08-11, recurred 2026-08-30)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The full backend suite could not be measured today. Two lanes were running it against the
same PostgreSQL — one without `--reuse-db`, which creates and drops the test database, and
one with it, which depends on that database existing. **Fifty minutes, nothing written**,
against eleven files that take 2m56s alone.

**The old mitigation was a sentence in four places — "point `DATABASE_URL` wherever you
like", counted: `08-qa/01-e2e/stack/README.md`, the header of
`tests/golden/test_gt16_opening_journal_entry.py`, the CR-011 status note in
`11-change-requests.md`, and `DEF-054`'s own prevention column — and every one of them
asks a person to set an environment variable.** So the SHARED name was what you got by
typing nothing, and hard-won law 3 says the unsafe option must be the one you type. The
first two are rewritten in this same commit to say the default does it; a sentence
describing a mitigation that has been replaced is hard-won law 1 waiting to happen.

**BUILT: `config/settings/base.py` derives `DATABASES['default']['TEST']['NAME']` from the
checkout's own path** — `test_sbh_smartbillhub_<hash>` in the main tree,
`test_sbh_agent_a10dce0b730636_<hash>` in a lane's worktree. Same directory, same name every
run, so `--reuse-db` still reuses and costs nothing. `SBH_TEST_DB_NAME=test_smartbillhub`
goes back to a shared database deliberately, which is now a thing a person types on purpose.

**Derived from the PATH and not from the PID**, which `DEF-054`'s own prevention column
offered as an option: a per-pid name is unique and it destroys `--reuse-db`, because every
run would build a fresh database. The path is stable per checkout and unique across them,
which is the property actually wanted.

**CI IS UNAFFECTED AND THAT WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED.** `pytest` defaults to
`config.settings.test`, which hardcodes in-memory SQLite and ignores `DATABASE_URL`
entirely (law 14) — so `ci-backend.yml`'s `pytest -q` never reaches this. No workflow runs
pytest under `local`: the Postgres steps in `ci-backend.yml` and `qa.yml` are
`manage.py migrate` and a booted stack against explicitly named databases (`sbh_ci`,
`sbh_e2e`), and Django reads the TEST name only when it CREATES a test database.

**MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER, on `tests/test_be07_job_runner.py` (13 cases):**

| run | result |
|---|---|
| alone | **13 passed in 108.94s** |
| two concurrent, ONE shared name (the 2026-08-30 configuration) | run A **13 errors in 2.16s**; run B 13 passed in 110.79s |
| two concurrent, two checkouts, NOTHING TYPED | **both passed — 109.11s and 110.20s** |

The verbatim failure, which is the signature the next lane will meet:

```
Got an error creating the test database: database "test_sbh_lanedemo_a" already exists
django.db.utils.IntegrityError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "pg_extension_name_index"
DETAIL:  Key (extname)=(pgcrypto) already exists.
13 errors in 2.16s
```

Every one of those thirteen errors is in FIXTURE SETUP, so it lands on whichever file
happens to be running and reads exactly like a defect in code that is fine — which is why
`tests/golden/test_gt16_opening_journal_entry.py` already carried the diagnosis in its own
header, and why a sentence in a header was not enough.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated rather than discovered
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. **G54 does not run `docker build`.** It runs the image's build COMMAND against the
   working tree. The image's own `npm ci` is not re-run, so a lockfile that cannot install
   is out of scope and `ci-frontend.yml` remains the check for that.
2. **G54 SKIPs without `npm` or `node_modules`**, and a SKIP is not a pass — it is printed,
   counted in the runner's summary, and made a hard failure in CI by the step above.
3. **G55 cannot tell a fix from a mention** and says so in its own output. The 119 is a
   list to look at, never a list to act on.
4. **The per-lane database does not help two runs in ONE directory.** Two pytest processes
   in the same checkout still share a name — they also share the files, so that is a
   different problem.
5. **The full backend suite is still unmeasured.** This lane fixed the cause of the
   contention; it did not run the suite. The last recorded figure remains the eleven-file
   run at 2m56s.

## 2026-08-30 · CR-054 W1 (tasks 4, 5, 7) — THE READING SHEET: five judgements a lane made, and the one it did not have to

**What was built.** `apps/metering/reading_sheet.py` — a CSV the clerk is handed instead of
being asked to build, holding one row per expected meter per required register for one
cycle and one reading month, with the previous reading and its date already in it. Plus
`read_import`'s new `row_key` column and the rule that judges it, so a swapped meter is
caught by name (task 7).

**Why the judgements below are ours and not the PO's.** Hard-won law 13: a judgment call
recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make one.
`12-governance/01-open-questions.md` and this log were grepped for each subject first —
none of the five had been ruled, and none of them collides with a signed rule, moves a
❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure, or needs a fact only the PO holds.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1 · THE READ DATE IS PRE-FILLED WITH THE CYCLE'S WINDOW START
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CR-054 task 5 says the date is *"pre-filled and correctable"* and names no day. The
worked figure: cycle CY-001 has start day **1** and **5** days to complete, so
`schedule.derive_read_window` places its August window at **1 Aug 2026 … 5 Aug 2026**
(that arithmetic is the module's own worked example, not this lane's), and every row of
the August sheet is pre-filled **2026-08-01**.

Why the START and not the end, and not blank:

* It is INSIDE the window by construction, so a row the clerk does not correct never
  manufactures an `out_of_window` warning about a date **the product itself supplied**.
  A blank would instead give `read_date_missing` on every untouched row.
* It is derived from signed schedule law (B17 §2, through `completeness.window_for_period`),
  not invented — BR-MET-020 has nothing to govern here because no threshold is being set.
* A route walked over five days is corrected per row. That is what "correctable" means,
  and CR-054's own task 25 (added in the same day's amendment) says so from the other
  side: *"The sheet pre-fills the date precisely so this edit is rare."*

**The cost, stated:** a clerk who corrects nothing files every reading on day one of the
window. On a TIERED plan that is not cosmetic — B4.4 scales tier boundaries with the
prorated period — which is exactly what task 25 exists to flag, and it is a W4 screen job,
not something this generator can fix by choosing a different default.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2 · `read_method` IS BLANK UNLESS THE CALLER STATES ONE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The obvious pre-fill is *"how this meter was read last time"* — it is a real fact, it is
on the head read, and CR-054 asks for the column to be pre-filled.

**It would have quietly retired the batch tag.** BR-MET-014 is CONFIRMED and verbatim:
*"Batch tags (month/cycle/route/service/source) inherit to every row unless a row-level
column overrides"*. A method on EVERY row is an override on every row, so the method the
wizard asks for at stage 1 would be chosen and then ignored, for the whole file, silently.

So: `build_reading_sheet(..., read_method=...)` writes the stage-1 choice onto every row
when the caller passes one — which restates the batch tag and therefore changes nothing —
and otherwise the column is EMPTY and inheritance does its job. The clerk still types a
method on the rows that differ, which is the case BR-MET-014's override was written for.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3 · `demand_reset` AND `reading` ARE BOTH LEFT EMPTY, AND THE EMPTINESS IS THE ANSWER
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`reading` is obvious — it is the one fact only the clerk holds.

`demand_reset` is the one worth writing down. Pre-filling `no` on every demand row looked
helpful and is a **claim**: `read_import` already argues the case in its own words —
*"`false` is a claim ('the register was not zeroed'), and a demand customer whose reset
went unnoticed is billed against a peak that belongs to the previous cycle"*. A blank cell
parses as False anyway (`_parse_demand_reset`: an absent cell is an absence), so writing
`no` buys nothing and asserts something nobody checked.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4 · A METER WHOSE REGISTER SET CANNOT BE RESOLVED STILL GETS A ROW
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`completeness._meter_rows` DROPS such a meter, and is right to: it is computing a
percentage, and a meter with no plan contributes no required records (US-MET-018 TC-5).

A reading sheet is a **work list**, not a percentage. The meter is physically in the cycle
and somebody is going to walk to it, so dropping it is the silent pass this whole CR
exists to remove. It gets ONE row with the `channel` cell EMPTY — nothing is guessed into
it — the reason named in the `issue` column (`no_plan`, `window_channel_not_stated`, …
`completeness`'s own absence vocabulary), and an entry in the sheet's `unresolved` list so
the summary cannot report a clean sheet over four meters nobody can bill. That is the
DEF-075 posture: *"rating cannot answer" must not read as "this meter expects nothing"*.

Worked: a cycle with one TOU meter and one plan-less meter is **5 rows** — four registers
plus one — and the summary says `unresolved_meters: 1`.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5 · THE REGISTER'S PLAIN-ENGLISH WORDS LIVE IN `read_import`, NOT IN THE GENERATOR
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CR-054 requires the sheet to print **On-peak**, because `tou_on` appears on no screen in
the product. The moment it does, the words stop being copy and become a PARSING problem:
a label the writer knows and the parser does not is a file that cannot be re-uploaded,
which is the second importer CR-054's hard constraint forbids.

So `CHANNEL_LABELS` and its folded inverse both live in `apps/metering/read_import.py` —
the module that already owns `READ_TYPE_VALUE_ALIASES`, the same shape — and the round
trip is a property of one dict instead of an agreement between two files.

**It duplicates the locale catalogue, and the duplication is made safe rather than
hidden.** The seven strings are a transcription of `metering.reads.channel.*` in
`07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json`, and `test_cr054__the_channel_labels_are_the_
screens_own_words` reads that catalogue and asserts them against it, so drift goes RED.

⚠ **This DEPARTS from `apps/metering/exports.py`'s stated precedent** — *"the file writes
the same machine token … rather than the screen's translated copy, because copy belongs to
IS-8 and a CSV must stay parseable"*. That precedent is for a LIST EXPORT, read by a
spreadsheet. This file is read by a PERSON and typed back in, and the parseability
objection is answered by the alias map: every word it prints is a word the parser reads
back to its code. Recorded here so the divergence is a decision and not an oversight.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6 · THE ONE JUDGEMENT NOT TAKEN — THE KEY'S REGISTER HALF
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The row key is `<cycle code>|<channel code>|<meter number>`, so it carries the REGISTER as
well as the meter, and a clerk can move a value onto the wrong register row as easily as
onto the wrong meter. CR-054 task 7 rules the METER case — *"row 412 was M-4021, now
M-4099 — was the meter replaced?"* — and says nothing about the register.

So the channel is carried in the outcome detail where a screen can show it, and the
SEVERITY is decided by the meter comparison alone. Ruling on the register case would be
this engine answering a question nobody put to it, which is the posture
`generation_channel`'s own note takes three rules above it in the same file.

**Severity is WARNING and that is borrowed, not invented.** BR-MET-122 is the nearest
signed statement — *"flag as warning, clerk accepts with a reason"*, for the same class of
fact (the file says one thing, the registry says another, and only the clerk can settle
it). ERROR would refuse a legitimate meter replacement; OK would be the silent import.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
AND ONE DEVIATION FROM THE DISPATCH, REPORTED RATHER THAN QUIET
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The task names `PlanRegisterResolver.for_asset`. **It is not used**, and the reason is the
other hard constraint in the same dispatch: `for_asset` resolves the unit's plan itself,
caching per unit — **one query per UNIT**. That is right for an import batch of 500 rows
standing on a handful of units and wrong for a cycle of three thousand meters behind one
download button (DEF-324). `for_meter_row` is the SAME resolver and the SAME cache fed
facts already in hand, and it is what `completeness._meter_rows` calls for exactly this
reason. Four bounded queries total, and a test pins the ceiling so it cannot move with the
meter count.

## 2026-08-30 · CR-053 W0/W1/W3 (tasks 1–5, 10–12) — SIX JUDGEMENTS, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE THE SAME SHAPE

The lane's brief was seven tasks on two screens. What it actually found was four
controls that **existed, rendered, passed every test, and did nothing** — which is
hard-won law 2 at screen scale, and is what the change request says of itself
(*"this CR is largely about reaching work that is finished and unreachable"*).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1 · THE PRINT BUTTON'S REASON IS NOW THE SERVER'S ANSWER, NOT A SENTENCE WE WROTE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

*Print bill* was disabled and said *"Re-printing the saved copy needs the endpoint
that renders it, which has not been built."* The endpoint has existed since
2026-08-16. Measured over real HTTP before a line was written, for
`BL-2608-000094`: **200 `application/pdf`, 4,110 bytes, `%PDF-1.4`,
`Content-Disposition: inline`, `X-Document-Provenance: original`** (DEF-2451).

**The judgement is not "turn the button on" — it is where the reason comes from.**
The old key was retired from all eleven catalogues rather than reworded, and the
control now branches on four states that are all facts somebody else owns:

| state | what says so |
|---|---|
| a draft | the ROW: no template version is pinned (BR-BIL-030) |
| issued, no locked copy | the ROW: `has_payload` is false (DEF-116's distinction) |
| the document read is in flight | this screen, for the half-second it lasts |
| the document read FAILED | the SERVER's own sentence, verbatim |

The fourth is the one that matters. On this branch the development store answered
`BIZ-STATE billing.document.bytesMissing` for every bill until the store was pointed
at the main checkout, and a clerk needs to read exactly that — not a refusal this
file invented. **A disabled control's reason is a claim about the product, and the
only safe author of that claim is whoever owns the fact.**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2 · THE DOCUMENT TAB SHOWS THE DOCUMENT, AND THE PANELS SERVE IT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The tab is called *Document* and held five panels ABOUT a document and no document.
CR-053 task 3 rules the order — *"the output is the screen, controls serve it"* — so
the server's printable page is embedded at the top in a frame and the five panels
follow it in the order CR-043 finding 8 ruled.

**It embeds the SERVER's page and re-draws nothing.** BR-BIL-026/BR-CUS-040 put the
render on the server precisely so a reprint in December shows July's name and
address; anything this file drew from the payload would be a second renderer, which
is hard-won law 5 with a customer's bill in it. A frame also brings the browser's own
PDF viewer, so print and save — BR-BIL-036's floor — cost us nothing.

**Where there is no printable page, the frame is not drawn at all.** An empty grey
rectangle asserts *this bill is blank*, which on a financial record is a different
and more alarming claim than *this bill has no printable page yet*.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3 · THE CHAIN ROUTE IS CALLED, AND THE DETAIL'S OWN FIELDS STAY AS THE FALLBACK
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`GET /invoices/{id}/chain` has been mounted since 2026-08-15 and **no screen had ever
called it**. It answers the one question the Corrections tab could not: *is the bill I
am looking at the one that counts?* `is_latest` is BR-BIL-048's gate and `head` is the
bill a new correction would be opened on.

**The tab does not stop drawing when that request fails.** It falls back to
`rebill_of_invoice_id` / `corrected_by_invoice_id`, which are the same column read in
the two directions and therefore cannot disagree with the chain — one is simply
richer. What it never does is claim the bill is current when it could not ask: that
would be a statement about a customer's money made from a network error.

**And it does not walk the chain itself.** One hop from A in A→B→C is B; the head is
C. `corrections.latest_in_chain` already computes it and a second implementation
would get exactly that case wrong.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4 · THE DOWNLOAD GLYPH IS DRAWN, DISABLED, WITH ITS REASON — AND THAT IS NOT A
    REVERSAL OF THE PO'S 2026-08-27 RULING
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

There is still no bills export: `POST /exports` resolves a registry that assets,
metering, rating, reports and ledger populate, and **there is no
`apps/billing/exports.py` at all** (re-measured 2026-08-30). So nothing here produces
a file, and the control cannot act.

B14 rule 12's toolbar is *one search, one filter set, one download glyph*, and
BR-SHL-025 says a control that cannot act renders **disabled with its reason**. That
is the shape `GeneralLedgerPage`, `RemittancePage`, `DepositsPage` and the two report
screens already use, and it is what this list now does.

**The distinction from the ruling the PO made on 2026-08-27** — *"you ahve to remove
- Filters that arrive later … Export and column choices"* — is WHERE the absence is
stated. That ruling removed a paragraph that occupied the page on every visit. This is
a 36px control in the slot the toolbar already reserves, silent until hovered.
`DEF-1063` still carries the gap in the register.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5 · TWO ROW ACTIONS AND NO OVERFLOW, BECAUSE THE OVERFLOW DOES NOT EXIST
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

B14 rule 15 reads *"Max 2 visible + `…` overflow"*. **No overflow component exists in
this product** — `RowActions.tsx` exports three things and none of them is one — and
**G37 clause 1 admits only `RowAction` and `RowActionLink` inside the cell**, so
building one there would take the gate down with it. Filed as `DEF-2453` rather than
worked around.

So the bills list ships exactly two: **open this bill** and **print this bill**. The
third candidate, *Fix this bill*, is deliberately left off — it is a WRITE, it is
RBAC-gated, and it has its own tab on the same screen with its own bill picker.

**Print is a `RowAction` and not a `RowActionLink`, and that is G37's doing too.**
An anchor would give middle-click and *open in new tab* for free, but `RowActionLink`
is a ROUTER link and cannot address `/api/…`, which is not a route of this app. The
`window.open(…, "_blank", "noopener")` idiom is the one `ReadsListPage` already uses
for the identical problem.

**The path is composed in one place.** A list row cannot read `pdf_url` off the
document without one request per row, so `billingOpsShared.billDocumentPdfPath`
mirrors `documents_api._rendered_dict`'s own `f"/invoices/{id}/document.pdf"`, with a
test pinning the two together. Composing an API path is what the whole client layer
already does; what it must never do is hand that path to an `<a href>` — see 6.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6 · PAGE SIZE IS REMEMBERED BY THE SCREEN, NOT BY THE SHARED TABLE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

B14 rule 16 says *"Page size remembered per table"* and its "Enforced by" column says
`shared DataTable`. **Nothing remembered one** (DEF-2452): `DataTable` persists
`table.<screen>.columns` and nothing else, and `parseTableParams` falls back to 50 on
every visit.

**Fixed in the CONSUMER and deliberately not in `DataTable`.** The page size lives in
the URL (BR-SHL-011) and the URL belongs to the screen; a preference hook inside the
shared table would rewrite 27 screens' query strings from underneath them, in a file
three lanes are editing. `BillsListPage` reads `table.S30.pageSize` on mount and
writes it on every change.

**A `per` in the URL always wins.** A shared link must open the page it names;
silently resizing somebody else's link to a size this browser once chose would make
one URL mean two things. The remaining 26 lists still forget, and the register says so.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
AND ONE THING THE LANE DID NOT DO, REPORTED RATHER THAN QUIET
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**No version bump.** `13-change-process.md` step 7 and the PO's ruling of 2026-08-26
(*"We have to bump version when major when minor so we are able to keep track of"*)
both ask for one per wave, and this lane covers three waves' frontend halves. It did
not bump, for one reason: G35 requires `07-frontend/package.json` and
`06-backend/pyproject.toml` to hold the SAME literal, and this lane was dispatched
with an explicit instruction to touch no backend file. Bumping one of the pair turns
G35 red for every lane on the branch, which is worse than either alternative.

**So the bump belongs to whoever merges CR-053's waves**, and it is named here so it
is not lost. The frontend halves of W0, W1 and W3 are in; W2 (tasks 6–9) and W4
(tasks 13–14) need backend that does not exist yet.

## 2026-08-30 — CR-054 W0 task 1: THE DEMO UTILITY GETS REGISTERS IT CAN BE JUDGED ON. Seven lane judgements, and the first one is why the task existed at all

**In one sentence, for anyone reading this without the register open:** the demo utility had
**199 meter readings and every single one of them was the meter's plain total**, so the three
checks the product runs on a reading's registers had nothing to look at — and this change adds
**24 readings** that give them something.

Measured on a freshly provisioned PostgreSQL 16, 2026-08-30, before anything was changed:

    select channel, count(*) from meter_reads group by 1 order by 1;
     channel | count
    ---------+-------
     total   |   199

`read_import.parse_row` defaults an absent channel to `total` (*"BR-MET-059: absent ⇒ the flat
meter's one channel"*), and nothing that has ever seeded a reading has stated one. The
consequence, per rule:

* `plan_register_completeness` — the warning that tells a clerk *"expects
  total/tou_on/tou_mid/tou_off, file has total only"* — had **no meter short of its set**, and
  in fact could not have judged one: `select count(*) from units where rate_plan_id is null`
  counted **all ten** of `seed_demo`'s own units, so the resolver answered `no_plan` for every
  meter on the demo estate.
* `tou_sum_sanity` could only ever return `not_evaluated: incomplete_group`.
* No `demand` register existed anywhere, so the whole DEF-797 path — a peak in kW that is a
  MAXIMUM and not a delta — was undemonstrable.
* No `export` register existed, which `apps/metering/selectors.py` already recorded in its
  CR-028 debt-sweep note.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1 · EVERY DEMO UNIT GETS A PLAN, AND THE PLAN IS DECLARED PER UNIT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

This is a prerequisite and not a nicety. A planless unit breaks two things that fail quietly:
`create_account` REFUSES to activate an account on one (BR-CUS-014 — *"the account derives its
plan from the unit"*), so nothing could ever be connected at a demo address; and
`completeness.PlanRegisterResolver` returns `no_plan`, so the completeness rule is computed,
stored, and says nothing, on every reading, for ever.

**Which plan a unit is on is FIXTURE AUTHORSHIP, not signed law**, and it is declared on each
unit in `PREMISES` rather than derived from `unit_type` in the seeder. The reason is one row:
77 Gulf Fwy Industrial's Bldg 1 is a `commercial` unit type on the **Industrial** plan, so any
derivation would need a special case — a rule nobody wrote, buried in a seeder. Seven
residential units go to `RES-STD`, two commercial to `COM-SM`, one industrial to `IND`.

`effective_from` is `SCHEDULE_EFFECTIVE_FROM` (2026-08-01), the same date the plans and their
rate schedules start: a unit on a plan before that plan has prices is a unit nothing can bill.
Idempotent — a unit that already carries a plan is left alone, including one an operator moved.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2 · THE READ DATES ARE CONSTRAINED BY THE PLAN, NOT CHOSEN FOR LOOKS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`PlanRegisterResolver` asks rating for the plan version **as of the read date**, and the demo's
plans are effective from 2026-08-01. A read dated earlier resolves `no_version` and the
completeness rule reports `not_evaluated`.

So each meter gets a PAIR: a July read that is the prior register the product derives
consumption from (BR-MET-019), and an August read that is the one carrying the verdict. The
July read's own completeness verdict is a truthful `not_evaluated` for want of a plan version,
and that is left as it is rather than dressed up.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3 · THE TIME-OF-USE TOTAL IS 424, WHICH IS §4's THREE WINDOWS ADDED UP — NOT §4's OWN 430
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`EP-MET-03 §4` names the meter and gives it its figures, verbatim: *"TOU M-7450 (E, kWh —
deltas tou_on 210 / tou_mid 118 / tou_off 96 / total 430 → sum-sanity 1.40%)"*.

210 + 118 + 96 = **424**. Against a stated total of **430** that is a **1.40 % deviation**, and
the tenant's seeded `tou_sum_tolerance_pct` is **1 %** — so §4's own pair is the FLAGGED case.

**The fixture seeds the healthy one** (total 424, deviation 0.000000 %, verdict `ok`), because a
demo whose only time-of-use meter is permanently flagged teaches a clerk to dismiss the flag
that matters. The three window deltas are §4's, unchanged; only the total differs, and the
flagged case is **one number away** — 8634 → 8640 — which is exactly how the guard for this was
proved red. Recorded here so the divergence from §4 is a decision and not a transcription error.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4 · THE DEMAND REGISTER IS READ ON THE SECONDARY SIDE OF THE ×10 CT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`EP-RAT-02 §4` makes M-7210 the Industrial demand meter (*"18 accounts, meter M-7210 ×10"*) and
`EP-MET-01 §4` gives it its multiplier. `register_units.billable_quantity` scales a MAXIMUM
register by that multiplier, and `BR-MET-143` says so in as many words.

So the dial reads **39.8 → 41.2** and the committed peak is **398 → 412 kW** — DEF-797's own
measured pair on this very schedule, the one that prices at 412 × $11.00 = **$4,532.00** and
that the defect billed as 14 kWh for **$154.00**. Nothing in `seed_demo` prices it (there is no
account and no bill run), so **no money moves**; what the seed proves is that the committed read
carries 412 in **kW** and not a difference of two peaks.

The `total` register's raw delta is **2,754**, `EP-MET-03 §4`'s own figure, and the product
applies the ×10 itself: the committed consumption is **27,540 kWh**, which is what §4 says.

`demand_reset` is set on the August demand row and nowhere else. It is BR-MET-051's *"reset
noted"* — the seventh published template column, which nothing on any tenant has ever set —
and it is lawful only on a demand row (`demand_reset_not_demand_channel`).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5 · THE NET METER IS M-7302, AND THE FLAG IS A RULE WHILE THE METER IS A CHOICE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`BR-AST-010` makes `net_metering` OPTIONAL on an asset of type `meter` and unavailable on a
non-measuring one (`assets.services.NET_METERING_OPTIONAL`), so setting it invents no rule.
WHICH meter carries it is this fixture's choice: Apt 102 at 2200 Riverbend Ct, a residential
solar household on a time-of-use tariff, which is the ordinary shape of that customer.

The consequence is `BR-AST-029`'s: its required set becomes its plan's four registers **plus
`export`**, five in all, and the fixture seeds five. `M-NET-01`, the sample estate's net meter,
was deliberately NOT used — it is `is_sample` and sits in inventory precisely so it mints no
service point in the ready-to-run July batch, and reaching across from `seed_demo` to assign it
would undo that on every tenant.

The flag is applied create-or-COMPLETE: adding it to the ASSETS table reaches no tenant that
already carries M-7302, so `_seed_assets` corrects a declared-net asset the database says is
not, through `update_asset`. Hard-won law 4 in its data form.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6 · THE BATCH NAMES ITS CYCLE BY NAME, NEVER BY `CY-###` — AND THIS BIT BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`create_cycle` allocates from the `CY-` number series when the preferred code is taken, and the
sample-records plant runs BEFORE `seed_demo` and takes `CY-001`. On the measured tenant,
*"Residential monthly"* is **CY-002** and *"Industrial bimonthly"* is **CY-005**.

The first draft tagged its batches with the constant's `CY-001`, which is the SILVER CREEK
cycle, and the product said so correctly and twice on all 24 rows: `out_of_window` warning
(*read 2026-08-01, window 2026-08-14 … 2026-08-14*) and `cycle_membership` warning
(*"M-7301 belongs to CY-002, file tagged CY-001"*, BR-MET-122). Resolving by NAME turns both to
`ok`. This is the identical trap `_seed_cycles_and_routes` already records for its own
idempotency key (CR-029 RC-W5-T1) — the note existed and the new code did not read it, which is
worth more than the fix.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7 · WHAT IS STILL FLAGGED AND IS LEFT FLAGGED — `vacant_unit`, ON ALL 24 ROWS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Every one of the 24 readings carries a `vacant_unit` WARNING, and the detail says exactly why:
*"no active account on the unit (BR-MET-036)"*. That is true — `seed_demo` seeds no customers
and no accounts, and says so in its own closing summary — so the read STATUS a clerk sees on
S25 is `vacant_unit` rather than `ok`.

**Not fixed here, deliberately.** Making it `ok` means seeding accounts, which is the customers
lane's work and a much larger change than a demo-data task should take on its own authority.
It is stated here so the next reader knows the flag is the product being right about a fixture
gap, not a fault in the readings.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
AND ONE THING FOUND ON THE WAY, FILED RATHER THAN FIXED — `DEF-2447`
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Two of the three Postgres-only cases in `tests/test_seed_demo.py` have been RED on a real
database and nothing notices, because the suite runs SQLite and skips them. Both were already
red at `c669ef81`, before this lane touched anything, and both are the TEST being stale rather
than the seeder: `assert 25 == 7` compares the live charge count against the seven codes this
command completes while provisioning had already written twenty-five, and `KeyError: 'TX State
Utility Tax'` is a fixture key that no longer matches a seeded tax name. Not corrected here —
rewriting another lane's expected figures from inside a demo-data task is how a wrong number
gets ratified by accident.

## 2026-08-30 · CR-052 W1 + W2 — THE MINIMUM BILL IS CHARGED, AND THE BILL CARRIES A YEAR OF USAGE AND THE TENANT'S OWN WORDS. Eight lane judgements, one question put to the PO, and two defects filed rather than absorbed

**Lane:** CR-052 backend, tasks 4–8 and 10 (W1 and the back half of W2).
**Nothing here is a PO ruling.** Every item below is a judgement this lane made
because the signed rules ran out, recorded with its worked figure so the next
agent builds the same thing from the repo alone (law 10). The ONE thing that is a
question for the PO is `OQ-1166`, and it is stated as a question and not as an
answer.

### What was built, in one paragraph

`BR-RAT-028` — the minimum bill — has been CONFIRMED for weeks and had never been
charged on any bill, because the two amounts a clerk types could not reach the
pricing engine. They reach it now. A water-only household using 0.4 kgal is
charged `1.60 + 8.00 = 9.60`; a `15.00` minimum adds a **`5.40`** line called
*Minimum bill adjustment*; tax is charged on the **`15.00`** and comes to `1.42`;
the bill is **`$16.42`**. That is `WE-3` / `GT-19`, reproduced by the code.
Separately, every bill now freezes **twelve months of the customer's usage** and
**the tenant's own bill message and ways-to-pay** into its locked snapshot at
issue — two blocks A19 designed, the document has always asked for, and the
snapshot has never carried.

### Judgement 1 — the plan floor rides on every tariff rather than on a new argument

`plans.minimum_bill_amount` is a fact about the PLAN and not about a service, so
the obvious home is a new argument to `price_bill`. It rides on `TariffConfig`
instead, repeated identically on every one of the plan's tariffs.

**Why.** `price_period` — the single-service door every ❄️ B5 fixture is written
against — takes no bill-level arguments at all, so a floor carried beside the
tariffs could not be stated through it, and the same tariff would then price
differently through two doors. Carrying it ON the tariff means both doors see it
and there is one contract, not two.

**The cost of that choice, stated:** the field can now disagree with itself. A
master's bill legitimately carries tariffs from more than one plan
(`BR-CUS-014`), so two different floors can arrive on one bill.

### Judgement 2 — two different plan floors REFUSE, they do not pick a winner

`apply_charges.plan_floor` raises `RatingInputError` naming `BR-RAT-028` when the
bill's tariffs state two different floors. It does not take the first, the
lowest, or the anchor's.

**Why.** The rule says the plan floor tops up *the total* — one total, one floor
— and nothing signed says which plan's floor governs a combined total. Taking
whichever figure the code reached first is exactly how every bill in this product
came to charge `$0.00` for base (`DEF-154`). It surfaces to billing as the seam's
`PricingRefused`, so the account lands on the exception screen and the other 499
bills issue (`BR-BIL-055`).

**Today it fires on nothing:** every plan in the database states no floor.

### Judgement 3 — the comparison is UNROUNDED, and the ambiguity is reported

`apply_charges` runs upstream of the single rounding boundary, so the minimum is
compared against full-precision Decimals and the adjustment is rounded once, with
every other line, by `finalize`. **No signed figure distinguishes the two
readings** — `WE-3`'s `1.60 + 8.00` and `GT-13`'s `6.10 + 12.00` are exact at both
precisions — so the documented order is implemented and the ambiguity is written
into the file's own exceptions line rather than left implicit. This is the
identical posture `finalize.py` already records for the tax base.

### Judgement 4 — one label for both modes, and the service is carried as DATA

Both the per-service top-up and the plan floor print **`Minimum bill
adjustment`**, which is `WE-3`'s own wording. The per-service line carries its
`service`; the plan-floor line carries `None`.

**Why not two labels.** Inventing a second wording for the same charge is
inventing customer-facing copy, in one language, on a money document. Which of
the two a reader is looking at is on the line as data, where a document or a
screen can use it; the sentence stays the one the workbook signed.

### Judgement 5 — a service that priced NOTHING is not topped up

`minimum_adjustment_line` returns `None` when the basis holds no line of a
measured kind at all, rather than emitting the whole minimum.

**Why.** A minimum tops UP charges. With no charge to top up, emitting the full
figure would charge a customer the floor for a service that priced nothing, and
no signed rule asks for that. It is a refusal to invent, not a rule.

### Judgement 6 — the twelve-month block is stamped AT ISSUE and its window ends at the BILL's period

`documents.py` has carried a named absence since it was written saying the eleven
earlier periods are not in the snapshot and that reading them from `meter_reads`
*"would be the live join `BR-BIL-030` forbids"*. Both clauses were true. The way
out is neither a join nor a recompute: `BR-MET-106`'s **stored** monthly grain —
the same payload the account screen draws — is asked of metering by name and
frozen onto `bill_payload.usage_history`.

**Stamped at issue and not at draft**, for the reason `BR-BIL-035`'s arrears are:
a draft is written when the bill is PRICED and may sit for days.

**The axis ends at the bill's own period end, never at today** (`BR-TEN-043`).
Worked: a June bill issued in July reports a window of **2025-07 to 2026-06**, and
so does the same bill reprinted in 2033. An axis read off a clock would silently
redraw every historical bill.

### Judgement 7 — the tenant's bill copy comes from the PINNED TEMPLATE VERSION, not from a setting

`BR-BIL-021` names a tenant bill message and footer. `settings_families.py` says
in as many words that this one *"already has a different ratified home"*, and
`template_models.BillTemplateVersion.options` is it — *"what the tenant
legitimately chooses: its bill messages and footer (BR-BIL-021)"*. So issue reads
the version the bill is PINNED to, never "the current template", and freezes the
words with the bill.

**Two consequences, both wanted.** A tenant who rewrites their message next year
has not rewritten the bill they sent this year (asserted through the render). And
reading a tenant-wide setting instead would have created a SECOND home for one
value — the drift `settings_seam.py` refuses for the finance controls.

**The option keys are `bill_message` and `ways_to_pay`, stated in `issue.py` and
pinned by a test.** `templates_service.save_draft` takes whatever dict it is
given, so there is no validator and nothing else declares a vocabulary; a message
saved under a third name reads exactly like a tenant who typed nothing.

### Judgement 8 — the platform does NOT compose the late-fee sentence

`CR-052`'s own diagnosis is that *"the late-fee terms the product is required to
print are charged correctly and never disclosed on the paper."* The fix is
judgement 7: they are the tenant's words and the bill now carries them. This lane
did **not** compose the sentence from the tenant's late-fee settings.

**Why.** It is a customer's legal disclosure. Composing it would mean writing one
English sentence for every utility in a product that ships eleven locales, and
the figures it would quote (`1.5%`, `$5.00`, a 5-day grace) are tenant settings
that no billing code reads today — `assess_late_fee` has no production caller at
all. A tenant who has typed nothing gets a **named absence** on the bill, not a
blank line, so the gap is visible to the clerk and to the customer.

### The one question, and it is the PO's — `OQ-1166`

A BASE-ONLY service — a vacation hold (`BR-BIL-028`) or a landlord's empty unit
(`BR-CUS-170`) — is charged its standing charge and nothing else, deliberately.
`BR-RAT-028` states **no exception** for it, so the rule is applied as written and
those services are topped up like any other.

**What that costs, worked:** on `BR-MET-101`'s building, six empty units each take
water at an `$8.00` base; under a `$15.00` per-service minimum each is topped by
`$7.00`, so the owner is charged **`$42.00` a month** for units nobody occupies.

Implementing the exception would have been as much a guess as inventing the
threshold was. The consequence is filed with its figure and the code names the
row.

### Two defects filed rather than absorbed

* **`DEF-2446`** — `rating.selectors.pricing_inputs` has published a
  schedule-level `minimum_bill` since it was written and **nothing reads it**.
  `BR-RAT-028`'s field map names the two PLAN columns, and nothing signed says
  what a schedule that ALSO carries one means. It is `OQ-238`'s shape one rule
  along — the base charge stated twice — except that `gather` REFUSES there and
  here the second figure never reaches the engine at all. Left unread and filed.
* **`DEF-2445`** — `test_br_cus_170_tc4` is RED on the branch tip and is not this
  lane's. Reproduced at commit `2f1b521a` in a detached worktree with no lane
  edits present before attributing it, which is the step that separated a
  pre-existing break from a regression.

### What did NOT move, and it was verified rather than assumed

`10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` is **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** before and after; the
golden suite plus the two engine suites are **43 passed / 1 xfailed**. Every plan
in the database states neither threshold, both new seam fields default to `None`
(absence, never a floor of zero), and `apply_charges` returns a tuple that is
byte-identical to the one it returned before when no minimum is stated.

### What is deliberately NOT in this lane

**Tasks 20–23 — the R1–R7 cutover — are untouched, and that is the point.**
Task 20 is the PO's call. No `ShadowOutcome` prices anything here, no R-step is
switched, no disagreement was reconciled, and no new narrowing logic was added to
`gather.py`: the two thresholds are a **projection** of stored figures with no
precedence to apply, which is why the third figure (`DEF-2446`) is REPORTED
instead of merged in.

## 2026-08-30 · CR-054 W5 — the reads upload adopts the shared kit (frontend)

Tasks 6, 11, 12, 13, 18, 19, 20, 21 and 22. Every judgement below is this lane's,
made where the rules ran out, and each is written here rather than left in a
comment somebody has to find.

### THREE OF THE KIT'S PANELS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT MOUNTED, AND EACH REFUSAL IS TASK 19's OWN ARGUMENT

CR-054 task 18 lists eight panels to adopt. Five are mounted — `SourceCards`,
`DropZone`, `MappingTable`, `RuleResultsTable`, `ReconcileStrip` — plus
`WriteModeChoice`, which reads already mounted. **Three are not, and mounting
them would have been the DEF-623 failure the same change request is fixing three
tasks later: a shared component saying something false about the target it is
currently rendering.**

* **`DryRunPanel`** draws an approval note, a `create_rollback_point` checkbox
  and a `notify_on_finish` checkbox. Reads has **no dry run at all** — that is
  task 19's own finding, and the reason stage 4's heading changed — no rollback
  point (a posted read batch is immutable, BR-MET-017) and no notification
  endpoint on this path. Three controls that change nothing is hard-won law 2,
  in the kit's own words. Its FIGURE LIST is what the composition needed, and
  that is `ReconcileStrip` in `rows` layout, which is the same component
  `DryRunPanel` uses internally.
* **`Receipt`** prints six fields and two of them cannot be true here.
  `mapping_used` is `null` by law (BR-MET-032 keeps no mapping) and would render
  *"Not recorded"*, which reads as a gap rather than a rule. `rollback_point`
  would do the same over a target where rolling back is a REFUSAL — the sentence
  `WORKFLOW_KINDS.reads.rollbackBody` already carries. And `file_hash_verified`
  is a claim: `true` renders *"Matched the file you uploaded"*, and nothing in
  the reads pipeline compares two hashes. The compliance stamp stays as it is.
* **`RejectList`** has no disposition control, and stage 3's whole job is to
  give every flagged row one (BR-MET-015). Mounting it beside the review table
  would list the same rows twice, once without the control that resolves them.

### `MappingTable` GAINS A READ-ONLY MODE RATHER THAN A DEAD PICKER

BR-MET-032 forbids a remembered mapping and `apps/metering/api.py` serves no
route that remaps a staged read batch. A live `<select>` over that is a control
that changes nothing — hard-won law 2 — so the component takes `readOnly` and
renders the target as text. The other four columns are unchanged, which is the
point: the clerk gains the SAMPLE VALUE and the status chip without being handed
a fake control. Every existing caller is untouched.

### THE SAMPLE VALUE COMES FROM THE CLERK'S OWN BYTES, AND ONLY READS CAN DO THAT

`ImportWorkflowPage` leaves that column empty and files `DEF-521`, correctly: its
file lives on the server and stage 1's answer ships no sample row. Reads is the
opposite case — the clerk either picked the file in this browser or pasted it, so
the first non-empty cell under each header is real evidence and costs no
endpoint. The splitter is a comma split and not a CSV parser, deliberately: it
reads one header row and one sample row FOR DISPLAY, and the file is parsed by
ONE parser, which is the server's.

### THE 36-WORD SERVICE NOTE IS DELETED WITH NO REPLACEMENT

CR-054 task 20's rule is *delete every sentence that explains what is not built*,
and this was the longest string on stage 1: a paragraph telling a clerk why a
field they never asked about is absent, ending *"Reported."*. The gap itself is
unchanged and is CR-054 task 8 (the endpoint) plus task 9 (the control). **The
register is where a reader finds an unbuilt thing; a clerk's screen is not.**
This is a narrowing of BR-SHL-020, which is about a plain-language absence of
DATA — *"not recorded"* beside a value — and not about explaining unbuilt
features, and it is recorded here because the two are easy to confuse.

### THE `Missing records` TILE IS A REAL FIGURE NOW, AND ITS 33-WORD NOTE WAS FALSE

The tile printed an em-dash under a sentence beginning *"How many readings a
cycle should have is worked out from each unit's plan, and that calculation is
not built."* **CR-038 W1 built it.** `validate_read_batch` has answered
`cycle_coverage` since, and the stage-4 shortfall panel has been rendering it.
The tile now prints `missing_after_batch`; the em-dash survives for the case the
second half of that note was actually about — a batch with no cycle, which has
nothing to measure against, and where the server sends its own reason.

### TASK 13's BULK ACTIONS ARE A CLIENT LOOP, AND THAT LIMIT IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN

`PATCH /read-batches/{id}/rows/{row_no}` is the only disposition writer; there is
no bulk route, unlike BR-MET-051's demand reset which the server loops itself. On
a shortfall group of a few dozen meters that is a few dozen round trips. On a
four-figure one it would not be good enough. Recorded rather than wrapped in a
spinner; the honest fix is a server-side bulk disposition and it is not this
lane's.

A reason is written on EVERY row the group touches, including `estimate`, which
BR-MET-015 does not require one for — a bulk action that stored no reason is the
rule with its evidence removed. A row that already carries a decision is skipped,
so pressing twice cannot overwrite a clerk's own call.

### THE COPY, MEASURED BOTH WAYS

`metering.upload.*` in `en.json`, at commit `2f1b521a` and after:

| measure | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| every string | 1,312 words · 147 keys | 818 words · 137 keys |
| prose only (5 words or more) | 1,127 | 643 |
| **the five stages** (prose, excluding the write-mode, coverage, co-sign, refused-billed, superseded and result-breakdown panels the CR counted separately) | **860** | **425** |

CR-054's own figures were *931 today, roughly 430*. The third row is the
comparable one and it lands at **425**. 25 keys are deleted, 25 sentences
shortened and 17 added, in all eleven catalogues, in parity.

### THE ID NUMBERS IN TWO PUSHED COMMIT MESSAGES ARE WRONG, AND HERE IS THE MAP

This lane wrote `DEF-2559`…`DEF-2564` into its comments and two commit messages
BEFORE allocating them, and `10-scripts/file_defect.py` does not take `max + 1`:
`12-governance/14-id-reservations.md` holds `2520-2549` and `2550-2579` for other
work, so the allocator steps DOWN to the first free id below a reserved block.
That is `DEF-1787`'s lesson one register over — **an allocated id is a blob too,
and a number you assumed is not a number you hold.** Every reference in code and
in the render check is corrected; the two commit messages cannot be, so the map
lives here:

| written in the commit message | actually filed | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| DEF-2559 | **DEF-2443** | the read date rendered as a raw ISO instant |
| DEF-2560 | **DEF-2442** | the commit-tree push that reverted 40 catalogue keys |
| DEF-2561 | **DEF-2441** | the completeness table grouped on a function name |
| DEF-2562 | **DEF-2440** | the cycle-coverage sentence printed three blanks |
| DEF-2563 | **DEF-2439** | a table caption rendered below its header row |
| DEF-2564 | **DEF-2438** | no count in the workflow kit was ever right-aligned |

### WHAT THE BROWSER FOUND THAT 3,485 TESTS DID NOT

Four of the six defects above were found by `10-scripts/render-checks/
cr054-reads-upload.mjs` on its first run, and **three of them are in the shared
kit and were true on all six importers**. Two are only visible in COMPUTED STYLE
— a caption's Y against its header's, and `text-align` on a cell whose class
attribute says `text-right`. That is hard-won law 6 charging its rent again, and
it is the argument for the PO's rule of the same morning: *"All UI screen should
be confirm using real broswer testing and not just based on test cases"*.
