## 2026-08-30 · ⚖️ NO DATABASE ID IS EVER VISIBLE ON SCREEN. A NEW BINDING B14 RULE. OQ-541 CLOSED.

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"no Databse ID on screen - that is a rule"*

**The PO said "that is a rule" in those words, so this is minted as binding B14 law**, not as a preference and
not as a lane's judgement. It is the one of the two proposals they chose to generalise.

**The measured case that raised it:** S29's compliance panel printed `Uploaded by  01a01d99-d617-7aa9-9f07-e2c08cc4fdc9`
to a Billing Clerk who wanted a NAME, and the row directly beneath it was formatted for a human — so the panel
was half-translated and looked considered.

**The rule as it now stands:** *no primary key, foreign key or internal id is the visible value of a field.
Where the id is genuinely what a user needs — a batch number, a premise number — it has a HUMAN-FACING number
and that is what is shown. Where neither exists, the field says so in words and the id may ride on `title` as
evidence.*

**WHAT IT COSTS, NAMED NOW SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER.** Every surface printing a raw id becomes a defect:
* the reads list's **Batch column prints `import_batch_id`** because `read_dict` serves no `batch_no` — **a
  backend change, not a copy change**;
* the compliance panel's **Session · IP** prints a session reference;
* and the same shape reaches beyond ids — `DEF-2432`'s break reasons print **`BR-BIL-015`** at a clerk, which
  is a rule id rather than a database id but fails the same reader for the same reason.

**A GATE IS POSSIBLE HERE AND SHOULD BE BUILT**, because this rule is checkable in a way most B14 rules are
not: a rendered-output check that no visible field value matches a uuid shape. Without it this joins the
majority of B14 that is RATIFIED and UNENFORCED.

## 2026-08-30 · THE PRINT HAND-OVER IS A PDF SET PLUS A MANIFEST — and the three mail standards are the VENDOR'S, not ours. BR-NOT-029 minted.

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"Im okay with this"* — approving the recommendation that a utility of this size builds
**one print-ready PDF per bill plus a manifest file**, one row per bill, rather than waiting on a vendor to
name a composed-data format. And then: *"How we handle this requirement - can you add this requirement in
required place in repo"*, on the CASS / NCOA / barcode note.

### WHY THIS PATH, IN ONE SENTENCE

A PDF set plus a manifest is what a small mail house accepts with **no vendor negotiation**, and its fields are
the same fields any composed-data file would carry later — so it is not wasted work if a vendor is named and
asks for XML or a fixed-width layout instead.

### THE ANSWER TO *"HOW WE HANDLE THIS"* — WE DO NOT, AND THAT IS THE POINT

**CASS certification, NCOA processing and the Intelligent Mail barcode are all applied BY THE MAILER.** CASS is
a USPS-licensed address standardisation; NCOA is a licensed mover lookup; the barcode is put on by whoever
injects the mail. **None of the three is ours to perform, and BR-NOT-029 exists so that no lane ever builds
one.** What we owe the vendor is **discrete, complete address fields — nothing more and nothing less.**

**And that is where we fail today, which is the finding this ruling produced (`DEF-2703`).** A bill's mailing
address is `customers.service_requests.billing_address_as_given` — **a single free-text field**, kept verbatim
by `BR-CUS-070`, which is correct for capturing what a customer wrote and useless to a mailer. **A vendor
cannot CASS-certify a blob**, so such an address cannot be certified, cannot be barcoded, and is mailed at a
higher rate or not at all. The premises half is smaller and real: `city`, `state` and `postal_code` are all
NULLABLE and there is no country column at all.

**So the rule carries three clauses that cost nothing today and prevent the failure:**
**(a)** a manifest address is written from DISCRETE columns and never assembled from or split out of one field
— *splitting an address is guessing, and a guessed address is mail delivered to the wrong house*;
**(b)** a bill whose mailing address lacks city, state or postal code is REPORTED and held out of the file,
never sent with the gap silently filled;
**(c)** **no screen, field name, document or report may state or imply that an address is CASS-certified,
NCOA-processed or barcoded**, because nothing here performs any of the three. That is hard-won law 1 stated
before the fact rather than after it.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO

**It does not reverse `BR-NOT-013`.** Delivery is still out of this release, no print adapter exists or is
coming, and the chain still ends at a rendered document. A manifest is part of that rendered output — the
paperwork handed over WITH the documents — not a dispatch. Building one is not building an adapter, and no
lane may cite this ruling to build or fake one.

### THE QUESTION IT OPENED, WHICH IS THE PO'S AND NOT OURS — `OQ-1171`

**NCOA does not only clean an address; it finds people who have MOVED and returns the new one.** So the vendor
comes back holding a fact we do not have. Do we write it onto the account? `BR-CUS-070` keeps the customer's
own words verbatim and never overwrites them with a resolved record, which is the same instinct one step back.
⚠ **And the sharper reading, which is why this is not obviously a mailing question at all: a customer who has
moved away has probably also stopped taking service — so the interesting consequence is not a new mailing
address, it is an unreported move-out with a final bill owing.** Eng leans toward recording it as EVIDENCE
beside the address and putting it on a clerk's worklist, never a silent write. **Not chosen.**

**Nothing is blocked by it today** — no vendor is named and no file is produced. It must be answered before a
manifest is ever handed to a mailer, because the answer arrives in the return file whether we planned for it
or not.

## 2026-08-30 · B14 RULE 33 — on-screen text is capped by WHAT IT IS FOR, and rationale is not on screen at all.

**PO ruling, verbatim:**

> *"Also I want desctption used on screens, in tables, in details view, in audits, it too much content we are
> publishing, I want you to write rules or if there is already a rule reduce the lenght of these messages on
> screen - 5 to 6 words you can define what is reason we are showing this text based on reason you can vary the
> lenght - but too much content on screen - one it break the screen 2 for human it is too much to read and
> understand, high cognative laod"*

**Two harms, and they need different fixes.** Long strings break the layout — a cap fixes that. High cognitive
load is the reader's problem — and a cap alone does not fix it, because ten short sentences a clerk cannot act
on are still ten sentences. **So the rule has a ZERO in it.**

### THERE WAS ALREADY HALF A RULE, AND THE PO ASKED ME TO CHECK

`G33` enforces REFUSAL copy at 12 words / 2 sentences, from this PO's own ruling of 2026-08-19 (*"you need
shorter sentences not long ones"*). Rule 33 covers everything G33 does not and leaves it untouched, carrying
its hardest clause forward: **shorten by deleting RATIONALE, never INSTRUCTION.**

### THE CAPS, AND WHY EACH ONE IS THE NUMBER IT IS

Measured over `en.json` on the day of the ruling — medians first, because the caps codify what the good
strings already do rather than imposing a target nobody meets, which is how G33's twelve was set:

| Kind | Cap | Measured median | Longest today |
|---|---|---|---|
| Label or heading | **3** | 1 | 5 |
| Fact — status, age, audit line | **6** | 5–6 | **54** |
| Instruction — what to type, what to do next | **12** | 15 | **45** |
| Consequence before an irreversible act | **12**, never cut below clarity | — | — |
| **Rationale** | **0 — not on screen** | — | 41 |

**The medians are already at the PO's five or six. The TAILS are the defect.** A 54-word note beside a control
and a 45-word hint under a field are what a clerk actually meets.

**Why the variation, since the PO invited it** (*"based on reason you can vary the lenght"*): an instruction
must survive being shortened. *"Choose the day to report on"* cut to six words is *"Choose the day"*, and the
clerk asks which day. And a consequence before an irreversible act is the one place brevity LOSES — *"A
reading already on file is CORRECTED; the old one is kept"* is what stops a clerk overwriting a month of
readings.

### THE ZERO IS THE POINT, AND IT IS MEASURED

The two longest strings in the reads upload were **41 words explaining why a checkbox is absent** and **36
explaining why a field is absent**. Both were written honestly — for a reviewer — and left where a clerk
reads them. **Deleting that class took the five upload stages from 931 words to 425** with nothing lost that a
clerk uses (measured in CR-054, this week).

**The test: can the reader ACT on this sentence?** If not it belongs in the docstring and the register. **A
screen is not where we explain ourselves.**

### WHAT IT COSTS, NAMED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED

Roughly **10% of help text, notes and empty states** exceed their cap on today's counts, and each is now a
defect rather than a preference. The **eleven catalogues move together** — a shortened English string with ten
unshortened translations is the parity failure `G32` already watches. And **a gate is buildable**: count words
per key, bucket by key suffix, baseline at today's number and ratchet down, exactly as G33 was built.

## 2026-08-30 · "NO BR NUMBERS OR INTERNAL REPO REFERENCES" — the PO RE-AFFIRMED a ruling they already gave, and the useful answer is where it stands.

**PO, today:** *"ensure we are not adding too much content on screens and no BR numbers or internal repo
references, write this as rules"*

⚠ **THIS IS NOT A NEW RULING AND IT IS RECORDED AS A RE-AFFIRMATION RATHER THAN RE-MINTED**, because hard-won
law 13 says the repo is where an answer lives and asking or re-writing it again manufactures inconsistency.
**The PO ruled exactly this on 2026-08-19**, in fuller words, after photographing the deployed build:

> *"Youa re also adding internal content and BR codes on screen, that is not required; it is application also
> available to Utility suer why they ned all these details - those are for internal use"*

`G28` was built for that ruling (CR-016) and it names the very string the PO is complaining about again —
`Rule BR-BIL-015 · column bill_run_decisions.case`, measured on the deployed build at v2.22.0.

### SO THE HONEST ANSWER IS NOT "WE WILL WRITE A RULE", IT IS WHERE THE EXISTING ONE STANDS

Measured today, and the three parts say different things:

| Part | What it scans | State |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | the eleven copy catalogues — **what a user actually reads** | **0 violations, baseline 0. CLEAN.** |
| **2b** | backend strings served verbatim to a screen | **20 against a baseline of 24 — below it**, and 4 baselined strings are now rewritten and can be struck |
| **3** | `raise` sites whose prose carries a reference | **542 against a baseline of 478 — RED, and risen by 64** |

**So the surface the PO sees is clean, and the debt is one layer back.** Part 3's 542 are backend refusal
prose; each becomes visible only if that message reaches a screen. It is `DEF-322`, and commit `c1ba3c1c`
tightened its baseline 498 → 478 and **left it red on purpose**. It has since risen by 64 and nobody lowered
it — that rise is the thing worth acting on, not a new rule.

### WHAT CHANGED IN THE RULES, AND IT IS A WIDENING NOT AN ADDITION

**B14 rule 31 said "no primary key, foreign key or internal id".** A rule number is not a database id, so the
wording did not obviously cover the thing the PO has now named twice. **Rule 31 is widened to name them all** —
ids, rule/story/defect/question numbers, module paths, file names, function names, routes and gate ids — so
the UI rule and the gate state one law rather than two overlapping ones. **No new rule is minted**; B14's own
closing section forbids the second copy, and a rule that already exists does not need another.

**And the clause that makes it survivable is kept from G28's own text: the provenance is not DELETED, it
MOVES** — into the code comment beside the string. Keep the honesty, drop the reference. A lane that deletes
the explanation instead of relocating it has made the code worse to fix the screen.

## 2026-08-30 · A REFUSAL IS SIX WORDS, AND THE CUSTOMER-COPY FAMILY STOPS BEING ASPIRATIONAL. Two rulings that pull against each other, and how both are honoured.

**PO ruling, verbatim:**

> *"Refusal copy is short — your 12-word ruling - this shuld be 6 words only - not too long; this family BORN
> ASPIRATIONAL it cannot be ASPIRATIONAL any more - there are so many bugs becuase of this."*

### ⚠ THE TWO HALVES PULL AGAINST EACH OTHER, AND SAYING SO IS THE JOB

**Measured over all 858 refusal messages, today:**

| Cap on the longest sentence | Pass | Fail — to rewrite |
|---|---|---|
| 12 (today's rule) | 826 of 858 · **96%** | 32 |
| 10 | 723 · 84% | 135 |
| 8 | 539 · 63% | 319 |
| **6 (the ruling)** | **252 · 29%** | **606** |

Median longest sentence is **8**; the 90th percentile is 11.

**So setting the gate to 6 today would take it from 96% passing to 29% passing — a backlog of 606 wearing a
gate's clothes.** That is the exact shape the PO's second half forbids, and the decision log already names it:
*"BORN ASPIRATIONAL → NEVER GREEN … pointed at a corpus that already violated them and given the number
somebody wished for."* Obeying the first half literally would produce the thing the second half rules out.

### HOW BOTH ARE HONOURED — the target is the ruling, the ratchet is honest

**Six is the rule from today. It binds every NEW or CHANGED refusal.** The 606 that already exist go into a
baseline FILE that may only shrink — the same instrument Parts 1, 2 and 2b of the internal-reference gate
already use, and the one thing the permanently-red part lacks.

That gives all four properties at once: the PO's number is law from today · no lane is blocked by prose it did
not write · the gate is GREEN and therefore READ · and the number can only fall. **A baseline that may fall
and never rise is a ratchet; a baseline nobody can reach is decoration** — this repo's own words, and the
reason the "built is not wired" family is 0-of-7 red while this one is 6-of-9.

⚠ **AND ONE CLAUSE SURVIVES THE TIGHTENING UNCHANGED, because it is what stops six words being worse than
twelve: SHORTEN BY DELETING THE REASON, NEVER THE INSTRUCTION.** At twelve words a lane could keep both. At
six, the temptation is to cut the sentence that says what to do next — which passes the gate and makes the
message useless. *"A budget-level override needs a reason"* is six words and complete; cutting *"Enter one and
we'll record it"* to reach six on a single sentence would be the failure. **Two sentences of six beat one
sentence of twelve.**

### THE SECOND RULING IS THE BIGGER ONE — *"it cannot be ASPIRATIONAL any more"*

This accepts the recommendation of 2026-08-27 and goes further, and the PO's reason is the one that matters:
***"there are so many bugs becuase of this."*** That is measured and true. Four gates in this family were
caught **describing their own output wrongly** within a day of anyone looking — one reported *"19 components
render raw translation keys"* when almost all rendered correct English through a fallback; another counted a
~5,600-value translation backlog and about ten real gaps as one number. **No other family produced a single
such finding.** A gate that can never pass stops being read, and a gate nobody reads stops being right.

**So every red gate in the family is re-baselined at today's reality**, with the number written down and the
date beside it, and each may then only fall. The families that were born honest are 0-of-7 red; this is how
they got there.

### WHAT THIS COSTS, NAMED

606 refusal messages to rewrite, in **eleven catalogues** — the translations must move with the English or the
parity gate breaks. It is a project, not a sprint, and the baseline file is what lets it be worked down a lane
at a time instead of blocking every lane at once.

## 2026-08-31 · THE BILL RUN'S PERFORMANCE QUESTION IS WIDENED FROM *"how long"* TO *"how many reads and writes, and what happens when ten utilities fire at once"* — CR-051 tasks 26–30

**PO, verbatim:** *"in Bill run you will ahve to do performance test for large batch - 5000 or 10000
bills in 1 go - how much time it takes, how is the performance of that - Im not expecting it will run
in few seconds , but youahve to check the engineering, that how many read and writes ahppens, - what
if we get 10 utilities firing billing at the same time, will it hamper live system performance -
update this is relavent CR 51 to 54"*

⚠ **CORRECTED 2026-08-31 (`DEF-2717`): EVERY FIGURE QUOTED IN THIS SECTION WAS MEASURED ON A
CONNECTION THAT BYPASSED ROW-LEVEL SECURITY.** The benchmark's role had been made `SUPERUSER` to create
a database, and a superuser is exempt from RLS unconditionally, `FORCE` included. Re-measured with the
predicate enforced, the same work costs about **a quarter more**: 100 accounts **16.9s**, 1,000
**168.6s**, 5,000 **889.9s**, 10,000 **2,147.4s** — **172 ms an account** where this section says 137.
The numbers below are NOT deleted, because the difference is itself a result; read every one of them as
*RLS-bypassed*. The shape is unchanged: linear across a hundredfold range, prepare ~84% of the cost. The
derived hour-and-a-half figure below is superseded by task 27's measurement.

**Three questions, and only the first was already answered.** CR-051 task 21 landed at `937782b8`
against real PostgreSQL 16: 100 accounts in 13.3s, 1,000 in 134.5s, **10,000 in 1,383.5s — twenty-three
minutes** — at 136, 137 and 141 ms an account, so **linear across a hundredfold range**, no cliff, and
task 22's seam memo then took it to **111 ms an account** and 71,738 statements per thousand. Ten
thousand bills is about **eighteen and a half minutes**.

**WHAT WAS NEVER MEASURED, which is the substance of this ruling.** (1) **5,000 was never run** — the
PO named it first and linearity is an expectation, not a measurement. (2) **951,978 statements at
10,000 accounts is a TOTAL** — nothing separates the SELECTs from the INSERTs, and *"how many read and
writes"* is precisely that separation. (3) **Two runs have never run at the same time**; every figure
above is one tenant alone on an idle database. (4) **No screen has ever been timed while a run is in
flight**, which is the only one of the three questions a customer actually feels.

**WHAT THE ARCHITECTURE ALREADY DECIDES, read out of the files rather than assumed — this is the thing
being measured, not the answer.** The worker is its own container beside three gunicorn processes, so
ten utilities cannot make the site stop answering. But **`--concurrency 2`**: ten utilities firing at
once do not run ten at once — **two run and eight queue**, and ten runs of 10,000 is 11,100 seconds of
worker time over two slots, **about an hour and a half before the last utility's bills exist** (derived
from task 21's figure, not measured, and labelled so). **And `task_routes` is configured NOWHERE**, so
one queue carries everything: a CSV export, a staged import and a customer's outbound notice all sit
behind a 23-minute bill run at `CELERY_WORKER_PREFETCH_MULTIPLIER = 1`. **That, not CPU, is the
plausible way a bill run hurts someone who is waiting.** One shared PostgreSQL; no
`CELERY_TASK_TIME_LIMIT` and no account ceiling, so nothing bounds a run that goes wrong.

**FIVE TASKS, IN CR-051 BECAUSE THE RUN IS CR-051'S.** 26 — run 5,000 and split every statement into
SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE plus rows written, per account. 27 — 2, 5 and 10 tenants concurrently on one
database, each run's wall clock against its single-run figure, with connections and lock waits. 28 —
three interactive screens timed *during* those runs against an idle system, p50 and p95. 29 — a queue of
its own for the run **only if 28 says a clerk waits**. 30 — state the largest run this deployment accepts
and what it does above it.

**WHY 29 IS CONDITIONAL AND NOT SIMPLY BUILT.** CR-051 already refuses to split the run across workers
until task 21 says otherwise, and this is the same discipline: if ten queued runs leave the clerk's
screens unchanged, one queue is correct and task 29 is withdrawn with that measurement quoted beside it.
Building a second queue on a guess is how a deployment acquires an operational component nobody can say
the purpose of.

**CR-052, CR-053 and CR-054 each carry a one-line inheritance rather than tasks**, because none of them
adds a per-account pass to the run — they change what a bill contains, how the list reads, and how reads
arrive. The line they inherit: **anything that runs once per account is timed against 111 ms and ~72
statements before it merges**, since at 10,000 accounts one extra query per account is ten thousand more
statements and the published figures are what turn that into something visible rather than a slow
Tuesday.

**LAW 13 CHECK, RUN BEFORE WRITING THIS.** No re-ask: the PO stated a requirement rather than answering
a question, it collides with no signed rule, touches no ❄️ B4/B5 figure, and nothing in the decision log
or the open questions had ruled on concurrent bill runs. The judgment calls here — 2/5/10 as the tenant
counts, p50/p95 as the shape, and making 29 conditional — are ours, and are written down rather than
asked.

## 2026-08-31 — CR-054 W4 frontend (tasks 2, 15, 17, 23, 24, 25) · seven lane judgments

**Context.** Partial posting landed in the backend on 2026-08-30 (`BR-MET-940`, `2.94.0`) and
**the screen still refused**: stage 3 disabled `Load →` while any error row was undecided, so a
clerk with 2 bad rows in 1,180 could not reach the behaviour the PO asked for at all. These are
the calls this lane took where no signed rule decided the matter. **None was put to the Product
Owner** — law 13: a judgment recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the
failure to make one.

**1 · The forward fence keeps its VALIDATION clause and loses only its ERROR clause.**
It read `validation !== null && unresolvedErrorRows(rows).length === 0`. Deleting the whole
thing was tempting and wrong: *"has the run happened"* and *"are all errors resolved"* are
different kinds of statement. The first is still true — stage 4 prints a composition of verdicts
that do not exist before the run, and `results.csv` itself refuses a batch below `validated`.
Only the policy clause goes.

**2 · The split is DERIVED IN THE BROWSER, as a declared port, because the server serves none.**
`OQ-1200`. `postSplit()` is `read_rejects.would_hold`'s three clauses in its order, over the
server's own stored `severity` and `disposition`; it re-judges nothing. It is a **ceiling, not a
promise** — `would_hold` names the two facts it cannot know (a head billed since stage 3, a
write the database refuses) and both produce MORE holds at post, never fewer. The receipt prints
the server's own `held_reads`, so the forecast is never left standing as the record. Measured
across a real commit: the button said **5** and the post created **5**.

**3 · A split that does not reconcile is not printed at all.** `postSplit` compares the rows on
screen against the server's `counts.rows` and refuses to state a number when they differ.
`read_batch_counts` carries its own `reconciles` for the same reason (DEF-016 — a silently
dropped row), and a confident wrong number immediately above an irreversible click is worse than
an absence.

**4 · The banner is `role="status"`, never `role="alert"`.** The tier is a claim: an alert says
the operator is blocked and must act before continuing, and since `BR-MET-940` neither is true.
The warning tint stays while rows will be held, because something IS being held.

**5 · Task 25 compares against the clerk's OWN statement, not a heuristic.** *"A read date is
EDITED"* has no server signal. The reading month is chosen by hand at stage 1 and the reading
sheet pre-fills every date inside it, so a tiered row dated outside that month **is** the edit
CR-054 asks to flag. No majority vote, no threshold, no tolerance — two dates, one of which the
clerk typed. And it WARNS: whether such a row should be refused is not a lane's call, and
`BR-MET-940` has just removed the last place this screen refused anything. The consequence is
quoted from B4.4 (*thresholds "scale with the prorated period"*) and CR-054's own illustration
(0–1,000 becomes 0–500 over fifteen days of thirty) — **no figure is recomputed**, because B4 is
❄️ FROZEN.

**6 · Task 24 REPLACES the Collected and Progress columns rather than adding a third figure.**
`DEF-2730`: the two were never comparable — meters against readings. Leaving a 100 % bar beside
an 83.3 % one would put two contradictory answers to one question on one row. `Expected` is
renamed `Meters`, which is what it counts, and the quotient becomes BR-MET-057's own: plan-driven
required RECORDS over RECORDS.

**7 · One chase-list call per VISIBLE cycle, and it passes the period.** `useQueries` over the
page slice, each answer bounded by its own cycle's membership (`BR-MET-055`'s no-unbounded-
endpoints posture, which `chase_list` states). The period is passed deliberately: without it the
route answers the CURRENT occurrence as of the tenant's today, and **the two "current window"
derivations in this product disagree** — measured 2026-08-31, `cycle_dict` printed CY-002's
window as 08/01–08/03 while `completeness.current_window` answered 09/01–09/03 `before_open`.
Passing the window the row is itself printing makes both halves of one line describe one period.

**And one thing deliberately NOT decided.** `DEF-2733` — the rejects route's two refusals say
*run* and *loaded* where reads says *batch* and *posted*. A frontend lane may not reword a shared
backend key without changing what the ACCOUNT importer says, where it is correct. The control is
drawn disabled with its own reason instead (BR-SHL-025), so a reads clerk never meets the wrong
noun, and the real fix is filed rather than improvised.

**A note on the harness, because it is a lesson and not a detail.** The render check's first
three drafts all passed over a screen that had filed **nothing**: every assertion in it is
relational — *the button says what the strip says*, *the receipt says what the button said* — and
`0 = 0 = 0` satisfies all of them. It now asserts `created > 0` and names the remedy in the
failure message. **A check that cannot distinguish a working screen from a dead one is worse than
no check, because it is trusted** (DEF-182's lesson, in a new place).
## 2026-08-31 · THE CUSTOMER-COPY FAMILY IS GREEN — nine of nine, every number written down, and five gates were describing their own output wrongly

**This EXECUTES the two rulings of 2026-08-30** (the entry above). No new ruling is claimed and nothing signed
was changed. What follows is what was measured, what was built, and the three judgment calls that were ours.

### THE FAMILY, BEFORE AND AFTER

| Gate | 2026-08-30 | 2026-08-31, after this lane |
|---|---|---|
| G15 i18n parity | **FAIL** — "10 parity failure(s)" | **PASS** — 0 missing, 0 extra, 5,856 untranslated (all baselined) |
| G18 i18n call sites | **FAIL** (unmeasured then) — "1 problem(s): 227 dead keys" | **PASS** — 6 missing (0 unparked), 232 dead (0 unparked), 238 parked |
| G19 env hostnames | PASS | PASS |
| G27 translation keys | PASS | PASS — and it now names the 558 it measured, not a ceiling |
| G28 internal references | **FAIL** — Part 3 at 547 against 478 | **PASS** — Part 3 at **541** with an identity file; Part 2b tightened 24 → 20 |
| G32 refusal keys | PASS | PASS |
| G33 refusal copy length | **FAIL** — 33 over 12 words, baseline 0 | **PASS** — cap is SIX; 598 baselined |
| G44 display truth | PASS | PASS |
| G47 service catalog parity | **FAIL** on 2026-08-30 | **PASS** — fixed by another lane before this one started; re-measured, not assumed |

**Six of nine red on 2026-08-27 · four of nine red on 2026-08-31 morning · zero now.** The whole suite went
from 35 PASS/14 FAIL to **39 PASS/14 FAIL** — the four gains are all in this family and no other gate moved.

### THE REFUSAL CAP: RE-MEASURED, AND THE 606 IS 598

The 2026-08-30 entry measured 858 refusal messages and 606 to rewrite at six words. Re-measured on 2026-08-31
with the same gate, over **850** messages (the catalogue moved under it):

| Cap on the longest sentence | Pass | Fail — to rewrite |
|---|---|---|
| 12 (the old rule) | 817 · **96%** | 33 |
| 10 | 714 · 84% | 136 |
| 8 | 536 · 63% | 314 |
| **6 (the ruling)** | **252 · 30%** | **598** |

Median longest sentence **8**, 90th percentile **11**, and **not one message exceeds two sentences**. The
shape of the finding is unchanged: six with no baseline takes the gate from 96% passing to 30%. So `G33`'s cap
is **6** from today and the 598 are named one per line in `g33_refusal_copy_baseline.txt`, which may only
shrink. **DEF-2606** carries the 598 as a tracked project — 598 messages across eleven catalogues, worked down
a lane at a time, never all at once.

**The hardest clause is now printed in the gate's own failure output, not left in a docstring:** *SHORTEN BY
DELETING THE RATIONALE, NEVER THE INSTRUCTION. Two sentences of six beat one sentence of twelve.* A lane reads
a failure at the moment it is about to shorten a message, and the wrong way to shorten one — cutting the
sentence that says what to do next — **passes every check in this repo**.

### THREE JUDGMENT CALLS, MADE HERE RATHER THAN ASKED (law 13)

**1 · G33's baseline is keyed on the KEY AND THE TEXT; G15's is keyed on the KEY ALONE.** They look
inconsistent and the difference is deliberate. The refusal ruling binds *"every NEW or CHANGED refusal"*, so
editing a baselined message must cost six words — a key-only baseline would let a message be rewritten and
stay long forever, which is decoration. The translation backlog's growth vector is different: a lane adds a
new key to `en.json` and pastes the English into the other ten. Keying that on the value would turn every
unrelated English copy fix into ten translations owed before the commit could land, and would prevent nothing.

**2 · G15's two questions are separated and only one is baselined.** Key sets — a key `en.json` has and a
catalogue does not — is the defect G15 was written for (the S1 pricing card printing `public.plan.starter.f1`
at a prospect). It is at **0 missing, 0 extra** and stays a HARD ZERO with no baseline and no allowance.
Only the 5,856 untranslated values are parked (**DEF-2603**), and those render correct English to a reader,
not a raw key.

**3 · G28 Part 3's 541 are DIAGNOSTICS, and that was VERIFIED rather than assumed.**
`07-frontend/src/api/client.ts:202` reads `delete rest.detail; // BR-SHL-020 r2 — never rendered, still in the
audit row`, and a sweep of every `.detail` render under `07-frontend/src` finds no screen reading a refusal's
`params.detail` — the three live `detail` renders are their own response fields, which Part 2b checks. So the
re-baseline from 478 to 541 hides no customer-facing debt. **DEF-2605** carries the 541 so the number is not
forgotten, because a re-baselined gate that quietly drops a real number is the silencing this family was ruled
out of.

### THE BUG CLASS THE PO NAMED — *"there are so many bugs becuase of this"* — IS REAL, AND IT IS FIVE, NOT FOUR

Every gate in the family was read against its own output. **Five were describing it wrongly**, and each is
filed:

* **`G15` · DEF-2604.** Reported *"10 parity failure(s)"*. The ten were its own FAILURE LINES — one per
  catalogue — and the truth was 0 missing, 0 extra and **5,856** untranslated. A translation backlog and a
  raw-key defect added into a figure that is neither, with the user-facing class invisible inside it.
* **`G18` · DEF-2601.** Reported *"1 problem(s): 227 catalogue key(s) with no call site"*. **227 findings
  reported as one**, and worse: its two directions have very different severity — a call site whose key no
  catalogue defines prints a raw key to a clerk; a catalogue key nothing reaches renders to nobody — and one
  headline covered both, so no reader could see that the user-facing direction was **clean**.
* **`G28` · DEF-2608.** Reported *"1 internal reference(s) on screen"* when the one finding was Part 3's count
  rise, and the same file's own note says that prose reaches no screen at all.
* **`G33` · DEF-2609.** Printed *"every refusal message is within N words"* on any run at or under its
  baseline. True by accident while the baseline was 0; false the moment it holds 598.
* **`G27` · DEF-2600.** Reported its debt as *"at or below its baseline of 558"* — the same words whether the
  debt is 558 or zero, so nobody could see it fall.

**The rule these five now share, and it is the cheap general fix: a gate reports the NUMBER IT MEASURED, never
how many sentences it wrote about it and never its relation to a ceiling.** Nothing automated can check a
gate's prose; the only defence is that the headline carries arithmetic somebody would notice being wrong.

### TWO MORE FOUND BY BUILDING THE THING

* **DEF-2607 — `G28` Part 3's finding lines carried raw, untrimmed prose**, so **95 of 547** could never match
  their own baseline entry: the first run of the new identity file reported 93 stale and 12 fresh with nothing
  changed. Part 2b records this exact trap one screen up in the same file and it was not carried across when
  Part 3 was written. A count ratchet could never have surfaced it, because nothing ever compared one of its
  lines to a stored copy.
* **`G28` Part 2b was 20 against a baseline of 24** — a gain nobody had held. The four rewritten lines are
  deleted, so the ceiling is 20.

### WHAT IS PARKED, AND WHERE TO FIND IT

| Debt | Count | Parked in | Row |
|---|---|---|---|
| Refusals over six words | 598 | `g33_refusal_copy_baseline.txt` | DEF-2606 |
| Catalogue values still in English | 5,856 | `g15_untranslated_baseline.txt` | DEF-2603 |
| Raise sites naming an internal reference | 541 (536 distinct) | `g28_raise_site_baseline.txt` + `RAISE_SITE_CEILING` | DEF-2605 |
| Catalogue keys nothing renders | 227 | `i18n_known_gaps.txt` | DEF-2602 |

**Every one of those files may only SHRINK, and every gate prints its count on every run, pass or fail.** That
is the difference between a ratchet and a silencing, and it is this repo's own words: *a baseline that may fall
and never rise is a ratchet; a baseline nobody can reach is decoration.*

### PROVED RED BEFORE TRUSTED GREEN (law 7) — every guard, quoted

* **G33 at six with no baseline:** `598 refusal message(s) are new or changed copy over 6 words` (exit 1).
* **G33, a short refusal made long:** `1 new or changed refusal(s) over 6 words (599/850 over 6 words, 598
  baselined): assets.asset_no_duplicate: a 12-word sentence (max 6)`.
* **G33, a baselined refusal whose English CHANGED:** `1 new or changed refusal(s) over 6 words … 
  assets.allocation_share_range: a 10-word sentence (max 6)` — the licence lapses on an edit, which is what
  "new or CHANGED" means.
* **G33, a baselined refusal SHORTENED:** PASS with `1 baselined line(s) now stale — delete them … to hold the
  gain`.
* **G28 Part 3 with no identity file:** every site fails BY NAME, e.g.
  `Part 3 NEW raise site (not in g28_raise_site_baseline.txt): 06-backend/apps/billing/backbill.py :: rule or
  story id :: a back-bill must carry a reason code (BR-BIL-018)…`
* **G28 Part 3, a brand-new raise site in a probe package:** `Part 3 NEW raise site … :: rule or story id ::
  this brand new refusal names a rule id (BR-BIL-999) in its prose`.
* **G28 Part 3, the ceiling:** `no internal reference on screen; 1 Part 3 finding(s) … Part 3 ROSE: 547 raise
  sites carry an internal reference in prose, ceiling 546`.
* **G28 Part 3, ON THE REAL BRANCH, and this is the clause earning its keep.** The tip moved eleven
  catalogues and nine backend files under this lane while it worked. After syncing, Part 3 went red and named
  the drift instead of reporting a number: `Part 3 NEW raise site … 06-backend/apps/billing/cut_bill.py`
  and `… 06-backend/apps/customers/seams.py`, both from another lane's commits, with eight baselined sites
  gone. **That is the whole of DEF-2468 in one run** — under the old count ratchet this would have read
  "541 against 478" and three lanes have each paid a cycle to work out which sites those were. The final
  numbers here are measured on the synced tree: **541 sites, 536 distinct, ceiling 541**.
* **G15 with no baseline:** `FAIL: 5856 NEW value(s) pasted in English rather than translated` (exit 1).
* **G15, a key removed from `de.json` (the hard zero):** `1 key(s) en.json has that a catalogue does not
  (renders raw or silently reverts to English): de.json::public.plan.scale.f5`.
* **G15, a new key pasted in English:** `1 NEW value(s) pasted in English rather than translated … de ::
  probe.brand.new.key`.
* **G15, a baselined value translated:** PASS with `1 baselined value(s) are now translated — delete them …`.
* **G18, one parked key un-parked:** `dead rating.plan.penalty.title is not registered`.
* **G18, a LIVE key parked as dead:** `STALE register entry dead shell.nav.dashboard`.

### WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE

**The 598 messages were not rewritten here**, and neither were the 5,856 translations, the 547 raise sites or
the 227 dead keys. Each is a project across eleven catalogues; each has a row with its measured count; each is
parked in a file that may only shrink. Rewriting them in the lane that built the ratchet would have been the
sprint the 2026-08-30 ruling explicitly said not to run.
## 2026-08-31 · CR-051 W3/W4 FRONTEND (tasks 13–19, 24) — six sub-screens, three families, a decision on the row. Four lane judgements, four defects, and one that the browser found and nothing else could.

**What was asked.** CR-051 tasks 13–19: step 2 rebuilt as six sub-screens, one meter-reads table
with a filter for every scenario, a charges-to-add screen, KPIs that answer *bill generation* and move
as decisions change, step 3 as three families instead of eleven lists, a decision kind that can record
the answer to *Charges to add*, and an outlook band on step 4. Plus task 24, render checks for every
screen touched.

### 1 · THE THREE FAMILIES ARE A JUDGEMENT, AND HERE IT IS WITH ITS REASONING

No signed rule groups the decision cases. `CASE_TABS` held FIFTEEN — the eleven the CR counts plus the
four CR-038 added — and the CR asks for three. The grouping chosen is **by who answers the question and
where they look**, not by which module owns the data:

| Family | Cases | A clerk answers it by |
|---|---|---|
| **Readings and usage** | `missing_read` · `estimated_read` · `high_usage` · `low_usage` · `days_threshold` · `meter_factor` · `replacement` · `true_up` · `no_usage` · `overcharge` | looking at a meter, a route sheet or a usage history |
| **What the customer owes** | `owes` · `past_due` · `late_fee` | looking at the ledger and the payment history |
| **What goes on the bill** | `extra_charge` · `base_only_billing` | applying policy — there is no evidence to fetch |

**The list is DERIVED from `CASE_TABS`, not copied from it.** `familyCases` filters the live constant, so
a case added tomorrow appears in its family with nothing edited, and `casesWithoutFamily()` REPORTS any
case no family claims rather than dropping it — which the fifteen-tab rail could not have done, because
a tab that does not exist shows nothing and says nothing.

### 2 · *OVER CHARGES* MEANS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE EPIC SAYS, AND THE GLOSSARY ALREADY SETTLED IT → `DEF-2706`

CR-053's own *what is not a task* section warned this lane in one line: *"the Over charges tab holds
charges to ADD, not the overcharge guardrail. Two concepts share one name and the screen inherits the
confusion. Rename in the spec before building, or the tab will be built against the wrong meaning."*

**It was already answered in the repo, so no question went to the PO** (hard-won law 13):

* **A16 glossary:** *"Over charges | extra items to add in a billing run"*.
* **`04-docs/README` §111:** *"Over charges — nested tabs: All / Late payment fees / Service charges —
  apply/waive actions."*
* **r10 line 4256** draws exactly that: late fees and service charges, with Apply and Waive.

Against that, `EP-BIL-01` story 1, its TC-4, `07-pre-session-model.md` and `04-flows.md` all read the tab
as BR-BIL-029's trailing-average guardrail. **The glossary is a contract and the epic is prose, and r10
is the ruled design reference — so the epic is the stale one.** Built as charges-to-add; story 1 stamped;
`DEF-2706` carries the four lines. BR-BIL-029's guardrail is not lost: BR-BIL-054 already moved it to
phase 3, and it keeps its own surface on step 4 under *Unusually large bills*.

**The tab LABEL diverges from r10 for the first time on these screens**, and deliberately: a billing clerk
cannot be expected to know which of two meanings *Over charges* carries. It now reads **Charges to add**.

### 3 · A RECORDED DECISION NEVER REACHED THE SCREEN → `DEF-2705`

Found while building the KPIs that had to move. The resolve mutation invalidated NOTHING, so
`GET .../exceptions` kept serving its cached answer: the server wrote the row, returned 200, and step 3
went on saying *Not decided* until somebody reloaded by hand. **Nothing on the old screen was supposed to
move, so no check could see that nothing did** — and every jsdom case seeds the cache directly, which
cannot exercise an invalidation at all.

**Measured in a real browser after the fix: `waiting 2 → 1`, `decided 0 → 1`, twelve seconds, no reload.**

### 4 · CHOOSING *ESTIMATE* ANSWERED 422 AND THE CLERK SAW NOTHING → `DEF-2597`

The backend had reported this to this screen **by name** and the note sat unread:
`api.run_exception_resolve`'s docstring says `amount` and `unit` are accepted, *"No screen sends them yet
… REPORTED to the S31 lane rather than worked around here."* A comment is a note, never a plan
(hard-won law 1), and until this lane put a decision control on the row there was no way to press it.

Fixed the way the PO ruled it the day before — **OQ-540, 2026-08-30, *"for estimate reads - keep it
modal"*.** The modal asks for the quantity beside its unit (CLAUDE.md rule 3) and refuses to commit
without both, before the round trip as well as after it.

⚠ **THE UNIT LIST IS OBSERVED, NOT INVENTED.** Its options are the units the SERVER used for that service
elsewhere in the same run. A menu of plausible units would be a client choosing what a customer's bill
measures. **Proved end to end in the browser: `stored: estimate 9.500000 kgal`.**

### 5 · NOTHING PRODUCES A LATE FEE OR AN EXTRA CHARGE, ON ANY DATABASE → `DEF-2596`

Measured before the screen was written, on a real seeded utility. `runs._decisions_for` emits exactly
`base_only_billing` and `missing_read`; `read_analysis` adds the seven reading cases. **Nine kinds, and
neither `late_fee` nor `extra_charge` is one of them.** Both are real `DECISION_CASES` values with a
column that would store them and a resolve door that would take them — what is missing is the step that
raises a ROW.

So the *Charges to add* screen is real, reads the real endpoint, and **NAMES the absence** instead of
drawing an empty table that reads as *no charges this cycle*. The notice deletes itself the day the pass
emits a row. **CR-051 task 18's backend half is not this lane's and is not faked.**

### 6 · B14 RULE 31 LANDED ON THESE SCREENS THE DAY BEFORE THEY WERE WRITTEN

The PO minted it on 2026-08-30 — *"no Databse ID on screen - that is a rule"* — and the shape it forbids
was already all over this surface: `account_no ?? account_id`, which looks careful and falls back to a
uuid in the column a clerk identifies a customer by. Every such site on these screens now says **No
account number** in words, with the id on `title` as the ruling's own escape allows, **including the
accessible names** — a screen reader is a screen.

### 7 · TWO KIT DEFECTS WORKED AROUND KNOWINGLY, NOT INHERITED

* **`DEF-2438`** — `PlainTable` sets `[&_td]:text-left` at (0,1,1) and a plain `text-right` on the `<td>`
  is (0,1,0), so **no count in the kit has ever been right-aligned.** Every figure column here
  right-aligns a BLOCK SPAN inside the cell, which is not in that competition. Measured in the browser:
  four cells, `text-align: right`. The real fix belongs in `Surfaces.tsx`, which is the shared kit.
* **`DEF-2439`** — a `<caption>` with `display:block` renders BELOW the header row. **No table here has
  one**; every table is titled by the section kicker above it, which is where r10 puts the words anyway.

### 8 · WHAT THE BROWSER FOUND THAT NOTHING ELSE COULD

`10-scripts/render-checks/cr051-step23.mjs`, **44 checks**. Two of the four defects above were found by
clicking, not by asserting: `DEF-2597`'s 422 needed a real POST, and `DEF-2705`'s stale cache needed a
second render nobody triggered. The check itself had to be corrected three times for the same class of
fault — **a check whose output could not tell "the screen is broken" from "the screen has not been handed
its data yet"** (DEF-182's shape):

* it waited for `.kpi`, which renders immediately with a dash while the pass runs, and reported six
  sub-screens with zero rows over a screen that draws 47;
* it matched KPI labels against `Waiting on you` while CSS uppercases them, so `Number(undefined ?? "-1")`
  reported −1 and read as a broken tile;
* it sampled the tile 2.5 seconds after the write, when `GET .../exceptions` re-runs the prepare pass —
  **measured at 20.6 seconds for 47 accounts** on this lane's own database.

That last figure is worth carrying: the PO ruled on 2026-08-30 that this pass is **recomputed and never
cached**, and the remainder is CR-051 task 21's to make FASTER, not to memoize.

### What did NOT move, verified rather than assumed

* **No figure on any of these screens is computed.** Every scenario is the server's own `DECISION_CASES`
  value or its own `absent_reason`; every amount is the server's or is stated absent, never a zero. No
  `ShadowOutcome` prices anything and no narrowing logic entered `gather.py` — CR-051's second hard rule.
* **Bulk is untouched.** BR-BIL-060 exists because a thousand late fees cannot be worked one at a time;
  per-row deciding is added BESIDE it, never instead of it, and bulk WAIVE is still refused with its
  reason.
* **Nothing is pre-selected.** The selected option on an undecided row is an empty placeholder, because
  BR-BIL-015 and BR-BIL-061 both forbid a pre-committed default and a select showing its first option IS
  one.
* **G31: 470 declared before, 470 after**, at the ceiling. It was proved RED first on the new file —
  *"undeclared classes ROSE: 36 now, 0 baselined"* — which is B14 rule 21's per-file migration clause met
  on purpose rather than read about.

## 2026-08-31 · DEF-2716 — THE LAST THREE DATABASE IDS ON THE BILL SCREENS. Three lane judgments, one of them a reversal of a defect fix that was right when it was made.

**THE RULE.** `B14` rule 31, ratified 2026-08-30 in the PO's own words — *"no Databse ID on screen -
that is a rule"*. Three cells on `S30` predated it: the **Accounting code** column, the **Rate
version** column and the **Billing run** row. Each printed a uuid, each for a stated reason, and no
gate could see any of them — rule 31's own status column says the one thing `G28` cannot inspect is a
uuid-shaped VALUE, because it reads catalogue strings and not rendered output.

**MEASURED, IN A BROWSER, BEFORE ANY CODE CHANGED.** On bill `BL-2607-000002`, seeded so that
neither stamp resolves: **seven cells of the Charges table and one line of the Document tab carried a
uuid.** After: **zero and zero.** That is the whole defect, and the six new assertions in
`10-scripts/render-checks/cr053-bill-surface.mjs` were each shown failing on it first (law 7).

### JUDGMENT 1 — THE ACCOUNTING CODE. A stated absence is not a blank, so DEF-937 is honoured and not reopened.

`DEF-937` (CR-043 finding 3, 2026-08-27) deliberately KEPT the uuid: the id is the `BR-BIL-010`
stamp, and a blank in a column headed ACCOUNTING CODE reads as *"this line did not post"*. That
reasoning is still correct and rule 31 does not overturn it — **it answers it.** The choice was never
"uuid or blank"; it was "uuid or a sentence", and the sentence was not considered. The cell now reads
**"Accounting code not readable"** (four words, `B14` rule 33's six-word cap for a fact). It cannot be
misread as unposted, and it is the same choice the Charges tab's own charge-code note (`DEF-2428`) had
already made one column over. **One table doing both things is what the defect was filed on.**

### JUDGMENT 2 — WHERE THE ID GOES. `title`, because rule 31 says so in its own sentence.

Rule 31: *"where neither exists, the field says so in words and **the internal value may ride on
`title` as evidence**"*. So it does — `title={line.gl_account_id}` — and support keeps the stamp
without a clerk reading it as the value of the field. The alternative precedent (`DEF-332` moved a
rule id to `data-rule-ref`) governs RULE references, which rule 31 sends to the code comment instead.
Following the ratified sentence rather than re-deciding it is law 13.

⚠ **AND IT MAKES THE OBVIOUS TEST VACUOUS, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX.** With the id on
`title` it is still in the markup, so `expect(html).not.toContain("gl-4100")` FAILS on the correct fix
and `toContain("gl-4100")` PASSES on the defect. Every assertion here therefore reads the POSITION —
`title="gl-4100"` present, `>gl-4100<` absent — and the render check reads `innerText`, never the
markup. A check over `innerHTML` would have gone red on the right answer.

### JUDGMENT 3 — THE BILLING RUN. It gets its NAME, not a generic link, and that is rule 31's first branch.

The row printed `bill_run_id` under a comment that was true when written: *"EP-BIL-01's run screens do
not exist, so the id is SHOWN rather than linked"*. `CR-051` built them; nothing re-read the sentence
(hard-won law 1). The obvious fix is a link reading *"Open the run"*, and it would satisfy the rule.

**It is not the best answer, and the repo already held the better one.** Rule 31's FIRST branch:
*"where the reference is genuinely what a user needs … it has a HUMAN-FACING number and that is what
is shown"*. A run HAS one — `bill_runs.run_no`, the **`RUN-0001`** series `OQ-342` closed on the PO's
verbatim *"A: a real series (RUN-0001, like RT-001)"*. `GET /invoices/{id}` carries only the key, so
the number is read from `GET /billing/runs/{id}` **through the wizard's own query key**, which means
following the link afterwards costs no second request. Measured live: the row now reads **RUN-0001**
and clicking it lands on that run's screen at step 6, *"Bills sent · 47 customers · 47 bills sent"*.

**Three ways that read can answer nothing** — a run created before the series exists (`run_no` is
null and `OQ-342` says those are NOT retro-numbered), a reader without permission on runs, an
unreachable route — **and all three fall back to the words "Open the run", never to the key.** The
link renders before the number arrives, because a clerk should not wait on a label to reach the
screen the row is about.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY

**No backend change.** Serving `bill_run_no` on the invoice detail would save the extra request and
is the tidier shape, but it is a contract change (`endpoints.ts`, the OpenAPI snapshot, `selectors.py`
— a file two CR-052 lanes are editing right now), for a label. The frontend read is contained to one
component and reverses in one commit.

**`billing.bill.glCodeAwaitingWhy` is DELETED from all eleven catalogues**, not left behind: it was
the hover reason on the uuid, `G18` reports a catalogue key with no call site as a DEAD KEY, and
`B14` rule 33 puts rationale at zero words on screen anyway.

### LAW 13 CHECK, RUN BEFORE WRITING THIS

Nothing here goes to the PO. `12-governance/02-decision-log.md` and `01-open-questions.md` were
grepped for *accounting code*, *rate version*, *run number* and *rule 31*: rule 31 is ratified,
`OQ-342` is closed with the run series, `OQ-541` is closed, and `DEF-937`'s reasoning is recorded.
Every remaining call is ours — the wording of three strings, where the id rides, and whether to fetch
the run's number — and each is written here with what it was measured against. No ❄️ B4/B5 figure is
touched and no signed rule is reversed: `DEF-937`'s rule is kept, its INSTANCE is superseded by a
later ruling, and that supersession is stated in the code beside the change.

### ⚠ AND THE PUSH ITSELF ALMOST SHIPPED A REVERT — `DEF-2721`, FILED AGAINST THIS LANE'S OWN HELPER

The law-11 helper written for this fix re-derived all twenty-four blobs from the pinned tip
correctly, and then staged **`find . -type f`** over its blob directory. That directory is under
`/tmp/claude-0/<session>/scratchpad`, **which `DEF-2314` already records as SHARED BETWEEN TWO
LANES** — a sibling had left three blobs in it. Two were byte-identical to the tip; the third was
an older `12-governance/11-change-requests.md`, so the commit read **5 insertions and 816
deletions on a file this lane never opened.**

**Every law-11 check passed on it.** The file count matched what the helper staged, every hunk in
this lane's own files was this lane's, `git show` looked right to anyone reading their own paths,
and `git status` was clean because `commit-tree` writes no file. It was caught by the one check
the law says is not optional: reading `git diff --numstat <pinned-tip> <commit>` **as arithmetic**.

**The fix that matters is not the tidier directory.** A lane-private path is hygiene somebody has
to remember. The helper now stages the MANIFEST `derive.py` wrote and **refuses when the directory
holds a file it did not derive**, which is a check the next lane inherits — CLAUDE.md law 11 asks
for exactly that in the sentence *"make your push helper REFUSE"*. **The standing lesson: a push
helper stages the paths it DERIVED, never the paths it FINDS.**

## 2026-08-31 · Three screens that stated a number that was not true — re-measured in a browser, and the half that was still broken

**Lane:** the DEF-2730 / DEF-2731 / DEF-2732 re-measure. **Version 2.101.1.**
**Nothing here needed the PO.** Every judgment below is ours to make and is written down (law 13);
no signed rule moved, and BR-MET-057, BR-MET-129, BR-MET-130 and BR-MET-940 are implemented as
signed, not amended.

### 1 · TWO OF THE THREE ROWS WERE STALE, AND THE PRODUCT WAS NOT

`DEF-2731` (stage 4 said *"Rows that will become readings: 0"* over a post that filed five) and
`DEF-2732` (*"expects 5 … cover 5 … 1 have not been read"*) were **already fixed in code** by
`8d661ec1`, the CR-054 W4 frontend commit, and their register rows still read `open` with an empty
`fixed_commit` because the write-back commit that followed filed the rows and never closed them.

**The judgment: re-measure before believing either the register or the code, and close the row with
what actually fixed it.** Measured in a real browser on a freshly seeded tenant, 2026-08-31:

* stage 4 states **`Rows that will post 2`**, the button reads **`Commit 2 rows ✓`**, and the receipt
  reports **`Readings created 2`** — one derivation (`postSplit()`, the port of
  `read_rejects.would_hold`) feeding all three, asserted ACROSS the click rather than against itself;
* the coverage sentence reads **`2 of 2 meters covered. 0 meters still unread.`** against a served
  `expected_meters 2 · missing_after_batch 0`.

This is `BR-MET-129`'s own note one defect over — *"DEF-659's register row still read `open`/`NOT
FIXED` on the branch tip while the code was fixed … the register was the stale artefact, not the
product"*. It has now happened twice in five days, and both times the cost was a lane about to
rebuild something that was already built.

### 2 · `DEF-2730` WAS HALF FIXED, AND THE HALF LEFT IN WAS THE HALF THAT HID IT

The wrong quotient was gone (`CompletenessCell` reads BR-MET-057's `completeness_pct`). **The clamp
was not.** `ProgressBar` read `Math.max(0, Math.min(100, progress))` and used that ONE number for
three jobs — the fill's geometry, the `aria-label`, and the printed figure — and `CompletenessCell`
clamped the served percentage a second time before passing it in.

**The ruling, and it is the general one: A CLAMP IS A CLAIM.** It asserts *this figure cannot exceed
the cap, so capping it loses nothing*. Here the figure could exceed it — 300 %, 500 % and 400 % on
three cycles — and what the cap removed was the only evidence the arithmetic was broken. A full bar
reads as good news, which is exactly why five days passed.

**So the number and the geometry are separated.** A 120-pixel track cannot draw 300 % of itself, so
the FILL stays bounded — that is layout. The figure printed, the figure announced and the tone of the
fill are the server's, unaltered: a served `300.0` now prints **`300%`** in the danger colour with
`data-reads-over="true"`, measured in a browser through an intercepted route.

⚠ **`completeness.cycle_coverage` cannot produce that case today** — `collected_channels` is built as
a subset of `expected_channels`, so the percentage is ≤ 100 by construction. The guard is not about
today's server; it is about the screen refusing to present an impossible figure as a healthy one,
which is the property that was missing when the quotient WAS wrong.

### 3 · A THIRD WRONG NUMBER IN THE SAME SENTENCE — `DEF-2766`, FILED

Re-reading DEF-2732's sentence found that `expected_meters` was being called **readings**.
`batch_cycle_coverage`'s own docstring says why that is not a synonym — *"Meters, not records,
because the review step's question is 'which meters does this cycle still wait on'"*. On the seeded
CY-002 the sentence said **expects 5 readings** where BR-MET-057's chase list scores **18 expected
records**, because a time-of-use meter owes four readings where a flat meter owes one. It is
`DEF-2730`'s confusion — a meter count and a reading count are not the same kind of number — one
screen over, and **this sentence has now been repaired three times in nine days**: `DEF-2440` fixed
the field names, `DEF-2732` fixed the arithmetic, and neither asked what the numbers COUNT.
`ReadCycleCoverage.expected_meters` now carries the unit and the 5-versus-18 figure in its own
docstring. Related, not answered by this: `OQ-1201`.

### 4 · B14 RULE 33 ON THE TWO SENTENCES THIS LANE TOUCHED — AND ONLY THOSE

Rule 33 (RATIFIED 2026-08-30) caps a FACT at six words and an INSTRUCTION at six words per sentence.
The coverage block broke both: the line was **three sentences and 24 words**, the note under it
**18 words in one**. Rewritten in all eleven catalogues:

| key | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `metering.upload.coverage.line` | *"This cycle expects {{expected}} readings. This batch and the readings already on file cover {{received}}. {{missing}} have not been read."* | *"{{received}} of {{expected}} meters covered. {{missing}} meters still unread."* |
| `metering.upload.coverage.allowed` | *"You can post anyway. The meters not read go on the chase list to be read late or estimated."* | *"You can post anyway. Unread meters join the chase list."* |

**What was deliberately NOT rewritten, with its count:** `metering.upload.coverage.absent`
(13 words) and `metering.cycles.completeness.noWindow` (11 words) are on the same two screens and
break the same cap, and they are the OTHER branch — they render when there is no cycle and no window,
which is not the state any of these three defects is about. Rewriting them here would have been
eleven more catalogues of churn under two live lanes for a sentence nobody measured. They are named
here so the next lane on this screen can take them, not lost.

### 5 · TWO ASSERTIONS IN THE HARNESS COULD NOT FAIL, AND A THIRD WAS LYING

`cr054-w4-partial-post.mjs` is the check that found all three defects, and it carried the exact hole
its own author had warned about two hundred lines further down (*"0 = 0 = 0 satisfies all of them"*):

* `shortCell === undefined || shortCell.barWidth !== "100%"` passed green on a fixture built to
  contain a short cycle — absence is now the failure it always was;
* `cov === null || covered + missing === expected` passed over a screen that had said nothing at
  all — the sentence must now be PRESENT, its expected must be **> 0**, and its three numbers are
  compared with the server's own `batch_cycle_coverage`;
* the S27 cells are compared against `GET /cycles/{id}/chase-list` — the rule's own computation —
  rather than only with themselves, because the readings-over-meters quotient was as internally
  consistent as the right answer.

**And the harness's own bug, found while writing it: a STRING `pageFunction` takes no argument.**
Playwright evaluates a string as an expression and ignores the `arg`, so
`page.evaluate(SERVED_BATCH_COVERAGE, stagedBatchId)` fetched `/read-batches/undefined` and came back
`undefined`, which the check then reported as *"the server answered no coverage block"* — a harness
fault wearing a product fault's clothes. The id is interpolated into the expression instead.

### 6 · WHAT THE LIVE PAYLOAD SHOWED, AND WHY IT IS WORTH KEEPING

On this run's own batch the server answered `expected_meters 2 · received_in_batch 2 ·
committed_before_batch 2 · missing_after_batch 0`. DEF-2732's old expression —
`received_in_batch + committed_before_batch` — would have printed **4 covered of an expected 2**. The
overlap the defect describes is not rare or contrived; it is what a batch that re-reads a meter
already on file looks like, every time.

### PROVED RED BEFORE TRUSTED GREEN (law 7) — every guard, quoted

* `RoutesCyclesPage.test.tsx > DEF-2730: a percentage over 100 is SHOWN, not clamped into a healthy
  full bar` — `AssertionError: expected '<div class="px-4 pb-8 pt-6"><div clas…' to contain '300%'`,
  over a rendered cell reading `aria-label="100 percent collected"`, `style="width:100%"` and ` 100%`
  on a served `completeness_pct: "300.0"`.
* The browser, same defect, before the fix: `⛔ DEF-2730: a served 300% is PRINTED as 300%, not
  clamped away ("10 of 18 100%0 days leftChase 3 meters")` · `⛔ DEF-2730: the over-100 bar is FLAGGED
  rather than drawn as a healthy full one (data-reads-over=absent)` · `⛔ DEF-2730: the accessible
  label announces the SERVED figure ("100 percent collected")`.
* `CR054PartialPost.dom.test.tsx > the figure is METERS, and the sentence says so` —
  `TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element with the text: /meters covered/`, over a DOM
  reading *"This cycle expects 5 readings…"*.
* `CR054PartialPost.dom.test.tsx > B14 rule 33: every sentence in the block is six words or fewer` —
  `AssertionError: expected [ …(3) ] to deeply equal []`, naming all three over-cap sentences.
* The browser, DEF-2732's copy: `⛔ DEF-2732: the coverage sentence is on the screen and states three
  numbers ("This cycle expects 2 readings. This batch and the readings already on file cover 2. 0
  have not been read.")`.
* ⚠ **AND ONE GUARD WAS WRONG THE FIRST TIME, WHICH IS WHY THIS STEP EXISTS.** The rule-33 word count
  split `container.textContent` and read *"1 meters still unread.You can post anyway."* as one
  nine-word sentence — two `<p>` elements concatenated with no space. It reported a fault the screen
  did not have, which is the same defect as missing one it does. It counts per paragraph now.

**GREEN:** 56 browser checks pass. The one remaining failure is `DEF-2734` — both rejects files come
back empty on a role that does not bypass RLS — which is another lane's backend fix and which this
harness's own header already documents as deliberately RED.

### 7 · THREE THINGS THE MERGE ITSELF TAUGHT, ADDED AFTER THE FACT

This lane branched from `12d900c0` and the branch tip was **16 commits further on**
by the time it pushed. Everything below was found by re-deriving against the pinned tip
(law 11), and every one of them would have shipped silently.

* **`G15` WAS RED ON THE BRANCH TIP AND A SIBLING HAD ALREADY FILED IT — `DEF-2595`.**
  CR-054 task 24's chase-list headers left `metering.cycles.chase.col.meter` and
  `.col.unit` byte-identical to English in `id-ID`, so the eleven-catalogue parity gate
  failed and no branch could merge. **Fixed here, and neither half is a new language
  judgment:** id-ID reads **`Meteran`**, which is this same catalogue's own word for a
  meter at `metering.reads.col.meter`; and `Unit` joins the id-ID loanword list on the
  confirmation the gate file already records three lines above it — *"'Unit' is the
  Indonesian word too"*, written for `Unit {{unit}}` on 2026-08-26. The interpolated form
  was allowed and the bare noun was not. That entry is marked for the PO batch exactly as
  its neighbours are. It also made **three** baselined entries stale, and those are
  DELETED rather than left: the untranslated backlog falls **5,856 → 5,853**, a ratchet
  held, not raised. DEF-2595's own row says the two options are *"a synonym … or an
  explicit entry"* and that *"neither is a lane's to take alone"* — the reason this one
  was taken is that the repo had already written both answers down.
* **THIS LANE'S OWN `DEF-2765` IS DELETED AS A DUPLICATE OF THAT ROW.** It was filed
  before the fetch that revealed `DEF-2595`, in the same words about the same two keys.
  A second id on one fault in a 1,180-row register reads as a register, not as an error
  (DEF-1787's exact lesson, one column over), so the row is gone and the fix closes
  `DEF-2595` instead.
* **AND THE ID AND THE VERSION BOTH MOVED UNDER THE LANE, WHICH IS WHY BOTH ARE
  RE-DERIVED AT PUSH TIME.** `DEF-2763` was allocated correctly against this lane's base
  and a sibling published its own `DEF-2763` in between — renamed to **`DEF-2766`**, every
  occurrence together. `2.99.1` was reserved by this lane and **published by another lane
  for the disconnection bill** while it worked; the tip reached **2.100.2**, so this
  release became **2.100.3** — and then the tip moved AGAIN, to **2.101.0**, between
  that resolution and the push, so it shipped as **2.101.1**. Twice in one hour, which
  is the argument for re-deriving at push time rather than reserving at start time. The changelog rename matched this lane's WHOLE HEADING and not
  the bare number, because `DEF-2762` is a lane whose re-derivation script renamed a

## 2026-08-31 · A RULING WAS RECORDED AND ITS FIRST ACT WAS NEVER DONE, BEHIND A GATE THAT LOOKED GREEN ENOUGH (`DEF-2790`). Three lane judgements, and the middle one departs from the literal wording of the ruling on purpose.

**The ruling being implemented, verbatim** (`OQ-441` CLOSED, decision log 2026-08-30, *"FIX THE
CAUSE, NOT THE FIFTH INSTANCE"*):

> **build a check that a file carrying `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` and a review-ledger row is matched by
> some glob in `10-scripts/gates/human_owned.txt`.** The cause fix SUBSUMES the instance fix — it
> goes RED on every unmatched file, so the five are added as its first act and nobody has to
> remember them: `apps/metering/register_units.py`, `apps/billing/gather.py`, `metering_seam.py`,
> `selectors.py`, `run_jobs.py`.

### WHAT WAS ACTUALLY THERE, MEASURED AT THE TIP

**`G53` was not built for this ruling. It PREDATES it by two days** — it landed 2026-08-28 in
`f191a8df` for `DEF-2102`, keying on `HUMAN-OWNED`, which is the correct condition for the escape
IT was written for. The ruling was recorded on 2026-08-31 in `859e826f`, and **that commit touched
four documentation files and no gate and no list**. So the ruling was answered by pointing at a
check somebody else had already built for a neighbouring condition, and **nobody compared the two
conditions**.

The two conditions are not the same set, and the gap is not academic:

| the five files the ruling NAMES | `HUMAN-OWNED` | `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` | seen by `G53`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apps/metering/register_units.py` | 1 | 2 | yes (parked) |
| `apps/billing/selectors.py` | 2 | 2 | yes (parked) |
| `apps/billing/run_jobs.py` | 1 | 1 | yes (parked) |
| **`apps/billing/gather.py`** (2,282 lines) | **0** | **4** | **NO** |
| **`apps/billing/metering_seam.py`** (413 lines) | **0** | **1** | **NO** |

**And the "first act" never happened either.** None of the five is in `human_owned.txt`. Three were
parked on the gate's own backlog list by other lanes doing other work; two were never seen at all.
**A ruling that was recorded and not executed is exactly what the write-back law exists to catch,
and this one hid for a day behind a gate that was RED on three unrelated files — which reads as a
working check doing its job.**

### JUDGEMENT 1 — WIDEN TO *EITHER* MARKER. 57 → 62 FILES.

A file carrying either marker in its own module docstring is its author's statement that the 🔒
protocol applies to it, and nothing else in the repo reads that statement. **Measured: 57 unguarded
files before, 62 after, 60,508 lines.** The five the narrow marker was hiding, every one of which
**already had a review-ledger row open**, so on the ruling's own wording every one was in scope from
the day it was written:

* `apps/billing/gather.py` — 2,282 lines, the one impure read pass a bill run makes · **NAMED IN THE RULING**
* `apps/billing/metering_seam.py` — 413 lines, the BILLED lock applied inside the issue transaction · **NAMED IN THE RULING**
* `apps/notifications/catalogs.py` — 2,019 lines
* `apps/payments/receipts.py` — 551 lines
* `apps/tenancy/services.py` — 5,221 lines, the only write path into the tenancy tables

### JUDGEMENT 2 — THE LEDGER ROW IS A SECOND FINDING AND NOT A FILTER. THIS DEPARTS FROM THE RULING'S LITERAL WORDING, DELIBERATELY, AND HERE IS THE ARITHMETIC.

The ruling says `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` **and** a review-ledger row. **Read as an `AND` that gates
the finding set, it would have made this gate SMALLER, not larger: 57 → 47.** Fifteen files declare
a marker and have **no ledger row at all**, and the list is not a tail of trivia:

    core/money.py                     the rounding constants
    apps/payments/idempotency.py      the hard-rule-6 inbound-payment key
    apps/payments/webhooks.py         the webhook key scheme
    apps/ledger/cost_capture.py       1,374 lines
    apps/customers/move_out_settlement.py   1,529 lines, "five money landings"
    ... and ten more

**Filtering on the ledger row would mean a file leaves this gate's sight by opening NO review row** —
strictly easier than the escape the ruling was closing, and it would have deleted fifteen names from
the PO's own backlog list as a side effect of "implementing" the ruling. **A guard you defeat by
doing LESS is not a guard.**

So the finding set is the UNION and the row is reported as a second CLASS: **47 asked** (marker +
row: the author enrolled the file and opened the record, only the glob is missing — the ruling's
literal condition, and every file in it is caught) and **15 not even asked** (marker, no record —
the author said the protocol applies and the standing record never opened). **This is not a
reversal of the ruling: the ruling's condition is a strict subset of what the gate now reports.**
It is recorded here rather than put back to the PO because `CLAUDE.md` law 13 is explicit that a
judgement is ours to make and write down, and re-asking manufactures inconsistency.

### JUDGEMENT 3 — NOT ONE GLOB WAS ADDED TO `human_owned.txt`, AND THE THREE FILES `G53` IS RED ON WERE LEFT RED.

`human_owned.txt`'s own header makes changing it a process event, and the gate's failure text says
so in its own words: *"Adding a file to that list is a PROCESS EVENT and the PO's call, not a
lane's — file it and say so, never add yourself."* **A lane that widens a check and then quietly
satisfies it has committed the same failure one layer up**, so the whole 62 goes to the PO as ONE
question, grouped by what breaks if the file nobody reviewed was wrong, with a worked figure per
group — `12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md`.

The five newly-visible files join `g53_unguarded_baseline.txt`, which is the PO's backlog list and
explicitly *"NOT A PERMISSION"*. **The three files `G53` is RED on as this lands —
`apps/billing/cut_bill.py`, `apps/billing/run_resume.py`, `core/rls_guard.py` — are deliberately NOT
parked.** They were red BEFORE the widening, they belong to three other lanes, each of those lanes
has already opened its own review-ledger row asking for a glob, and parking another lane's finding
takes the pressure off work that is still in flight.

### THE PROOF IS A FILE, AND ITS FIRST DRAFT FAILED THE WAY THIS SECTION IS ABOUT

`10-scripts/gates/g53_selftest.py` — **13 scenarios, 13/13**, each built on a SYNTHETIC repository in
a temp directory and each asserting on the **MESSAGE** and not merely the status (`DEF-182`: a check
whose output cannot distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check). It is registered in
`run_gates.GATE_NOT_A_GATE` and `g42`'s `NOT_A_GATE`, the same way `g12_selftest` is.

⚠ **Its own first draft had FOUR scenarios reporting `self-test BLIND: A2 baseline file is empty`
while claiming to prove four different things**, because the synthetic repos had nothing parked and
the gate's `A2` clause asserted only that the REAL baseline file was non-empty — not a property of
the parser at all. **The healthy control case is the only thing that caught it**, and the fix was to
make `A2` parse a synthetic baseline string instead (`baseline_names`, split out for exactly this).
Keep the control case. A self-test with no green case cannot tell you its fixture is sound, and
every verdict it prints after that is unreadable.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM

**It does not make any of the 62 files safer today.** Nothing about the product changed, no figure
moved, and `golden-verify` is untouched. What changed is that the sixty-third cannot arrive
unnoticed, and that the sixty-two are now a question somebody can answer rather than a fact nobody
could see.

## 2026-08-31 · ⚖️ A PREMISES UPLOAD NEVER REJECTS A ROW BECAUSE OF THE OWNER'S NAME. CR-055, and half of it was our picture being wrong rather than the product.

**HOW IT ARRIVED, verbatim:** *"We ahve prepare this logic for premises upload - we need to allow 2.6 -
owner can have multiple premises ownership- how you will ahndle this please confirm you make any cahnges"*

**THE REASON GIVEN DESCRIBES SOMETHING ALREADY BUILT, AND SAYING SO IS THE FIRST HALF OF THIS ROW.** One
owner holding many premises is not merely allowed — it is the designed path, it is the PO's own earlier
ruling, and the code cites that ruling as its reason. Measured before anything was written: `Premises.owner`
is an ordinary FK with no cap (*"deleting an owner that twelve addresses point at must refuse, never
silently untype twelve premises"*); `resolve_owner_name`'s **exact** branch REUSES the party that exists
(*"this is the branch that stops twelve addresses becoming twelve landlords"*); `owner_detail_dict` serves
**`premises_count`** citing *"the same landlord across twelve addresses is one party"*; and
`premises_ids_owned_by_account` returns a list. **500 upload rows naming one landlord resolve to ONE owner,
at box 2.7, and load.**

**SO WHY DID IT LOOK BROKEN? BECAUSE OUR OWN FLOWCHART SAID IT WAS.** Box 2.4's branch is labelled *"several
look alike"*, which reads as *"several premises name this owner"* and means *"the name matches two or more
EXISTING OWNER RECORDS"*. Filed as a documentation defect. **Under the change process's step 1 this half is a
DEFECT and not a change** — *"filing our misunderstanding as a 'change' quietly converts our error into the
customer's new requirement"* — and it is recorded that way deliberately.

**THE SECOND HALF IS A REAL RULING, because raising 2.6 surfaced a real question.** Three options were put
in plain English with the cost of each, and the PO chose the recommended one: **an uploaded owner name that
matches no owner exactly but resembles two or more existing owners now LOADS THE PREMISES WITH NO OWNER,
flagged to fill in later, exactly as a blank owner column already does. The row is not rejected.** The two
declined: *keep rejecting* — safest, but a big migration stalls on spelling; *pick the closest match* —
declined as recommended against, because the owner carries the master account, so a wrong pick eventually
sends somebody else's bill to the wrong party.

**⚠ WHAT IS SUPERSEDED, AND ITS SCOPE, BECAUSE THIS ONE IS EASY TO READ TOO WIDE.**
`import_runs.KIND_OWNER_REF` records *"a NEAR name is REJECTED for a person to settle (PO decision 3 —
'offer the match, clerk decides', so the import may not pick)"*. **Decision 3 is NOT reversed.** It says the
import may not PICK, and the import still does not pick — it still refuses to choose between two parties.
What moves is the CONSEQUENCE of that refusal: the row loads ownerless instead of being thrown away. **The
CREATE SCREEN is untouched** — `BR-MET-401` still refuses a premises with no owner there, because a clerk
filling in a form knows the answer or can find it.

**THE PRECEDENT IS THE PO's OWN, 2026-08-27:** *"what if owner column is empty - in such case we create the
premises and keep owner name empty - we cna edit and updaste it later"*, whose recorded reasoning applies
here word for word — a migration is thousands of rows, half the owner answers are in a filing cabinet, and
*"the addresses it cannot load are the ones its meters and accounts then cannot name either."* A near-match
is that same situation wearing a spelling instead of a blank.

**THE COST, STATED NOW RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER.** No owner means no master account, so the premises has
**nobody to charge**. It holds units, it holds meters, it can be read, and **it cannot be BILLED until the
owner is filled in.** Already true of the blank case; this adds near-matches to the same pool.
`unmatched_premises_qs()` lists them and the receipt counts them as `premises_with_no_owner` — **and that
count is the only thing that stops this being a quiet way to lose revenue**, which is why task 2 makes the
receipt distinguish *blank* from *looked like two*: one needs research, the other needs a decision.

**WHAT IT BUYS:** the premises upload can no longer reject a row on owner grounds **at all**. Blank loads,
exact reuses, near loads ownerless, unknown creates the party.
