## 2026-08-31 · `DEF-2824` FIXED — the ruled pricing chain now charges the state tax to the commercial customers who owe it, and stops charging it to a customer holding an exemption certificate

**Nothing a customer is billed changes today.** `resolution_switch.SERVED_BY_CHAIN_DEFAULT` is still the
empty string, so no rule prices any real bill through the ruled chain. Under the PO's ruling of this
morning — *"product is not live yet so we dont have to re-bill anything - just correct the logic and we are
good to go"* — the whole remedy is the logic, and this is it. `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` reads
**33 PASS / 0 FAIL** before and after, run both times rather than assumed. **v2.106.3**.

### 1 · WHAT WAS WRONG, IN ONE SENTENCE

`apps/rating/resolution_catalogue.tax_facts` called `apps/rating/selectors.plan_tax_rules(plan_id,
service_date)` **positionally** — with no customer class, no premises and no service list — and every one of
those restrictions **fails closed** by ruling (`DEF-273`, PO 2026-08-18). So the only taxes that ever reached
the ruled bill were the UNRESTRICTED ones, and `resolve_taxes` was then handed nothing to narrow.

The comment beside the call asserted the opposite, verbatim: *"EMPTY ON PURPOSE, AND IT IS NOT A DROPPED
FIELD. `plan_tax_rules` has ALREADY applied the customer-class narrowing (DEF-273) before it returns; the
rows that reach here are the ones that survived it."* Hard-won law 1, in the one step of the chain where
nothing else could contradict it: **R7 publishes no refusal class by design** — a failed applicability
condition means no line, never an error — so its only possible output was silence, and until `DEF-2798`
landed nothing compared it either.

### 2 · THE TWO COMMERCIAL ACCOUNTS, BY AUTHORITY, BEFORE AND AFTER

Measured on 47 seeded accounts of `Brazos Bend Utilities`, July 2026, real PostgreSQL, connected as
`smartbillhub` with **`rolsuper = false` and `rolbypassrls = false`** and deny-by-default proved at runtime
(0 account rows visible with no `app.tenant_id`). Nothing was written: `prepare_run` writes nothing by its
own contract, no draft is assembled, and the pass is additionally rolled back.
Harness: **NEW `10-scripts/def2824_tax_by_authority.py`**, which runs the LIVE engine twice over the same
account with everything identical except the tax rule set.

| account | authority | live | ruled BEFORE | ruled AFTER |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AC-2026-00047` (commercial) | Local | **$6.64** | $6.64 | $6.64 |
| `AC-2026-00047` | Texas State | **$20.76** | *no line at all* | **$20.76** |
| `AC-2026-00047` | *total tax* | $27.40 | $6.64 | $27.40 |
| `AC-2026-00048` (commercial) | Local | **$4.77** | $4.77 | $4.77 |

### 3 · THE EIGHT-STEP TABLE — R7 IS THE ROW THAT MOVED

### 4 · WHAT `plan_tax_rules` NEEDED, AND WHERE EACH FACT NOW COMES FROM

| fact | what it narrows | where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_class` | `taxes.applies_to_customer_classes` — r10's *"Comm, Industrial only · Residential exempt"* | `AccountFacts.customer_class`, already resolved by the chain's caller |
| `premises` | `premises_scope_kind` / `premises_scope_value` over FIVE mechanisms | `PremisesFacts`, through the new `_premises_scope_facts` — the three keys `premises_in_scope` reads by name (`inside_city_limits`, `city`, `state`) and no others |
| `services` | `taxes.applies_to_services` | **R1's own answer** — `plan_version_facts`' union of `plan_services` and `plan_rate_schedules`, via the new `_plan_services`. Not a second reading of the tables |
| `account_id` | `DEF-383`'s exemption CERTIFICATE | `AccountFacts.account_id`, **new** |

**`account_id` is the "anything else", and it is the one that runs the other way.** The three restrictions
fail CLOSED, so forgetting them UNDER-charges. An exemption is a claim the customer made, so an absent
`account_id` reads as *"no certificate"* and the tax APPLIES — the ruled chain was **CHARGING** the state tax
to an account holding a live certificate. Under-charging five ways and over-charging a sixth, from one line.
This is asserted as a case (`TC8`) and it is the one that fails in the opposite direction on the broken tree.

**Two facts had nowhere to travel and now do:** `AccountFacts.account_id` and `PremisesFacts.city` / `.state`.
Without the last two, a tax scoped by STATE — or by a city NAME on a premises whose boundary flag nobody has
drawn — is dropped from every ruled bill, and `resolve_taxes`' two booleans
(`inside_city_only` / `outside_city_only`) cannot express either. `resolution_shadow._inside_city_limits`
became `_premises_facts` and reads all three off the SAME premises read, for the reason
`gather._premises_geography` already gives: *"billing reads a premises in exactly one place, and a second
reader is how two answers to one question start."*

### 5 · THE JUDGMENT: WHICH LAYER NARROWS — DECIDED, NOT ASKED

`DEF-2824` states the choice: *"PASS THE NARROWING FACTS, OR DO THE NARROWING IN THE CHAIN — one or the other,
never the present arrangement where each side believes the other did it."* **The facts are passed**, and the
reasoning is recorded here rather than put to the PO (law 13 — a judgment call recorded with its reasoning is
the deliverable):

* **The selector is the only layer that CAN decide two of the four axes.** It evaluates all five premises
  mechanisms and the exemption certificate; `resolve_taxes` has two booleans and no account id. Doing the
  narrowing in the chain would mean re-implementing `premises_in_scope` and `account_holds_exemption` inside
  a pure module that may not query, which is a second implementation of a money rule.
* **Making the selector return restricted candidates would be a fail-open API.** It is shared with the LIVE
  path; a `narrow=False` mode is one forgotten argument away from attaching a tax to a customer who does not
  owe it, which is the direction that is a refund rather than a catch-up.
* **`TaxRule.customer_classes` therefore stays EMPTY, and the comment now says why with the call visible
  above it.** Copying the classes across would narrow the same fact twice with a DIFFERENT comparison — the
  selector case-folds (`str(code).strip().lower()`), `resolve_taxes` matches exactly — so a tax stating
  `["Commercial"]` would pass one gate and fail the other. That is a new disagreement, manufactured by a
  defensive copy.
* **The SERVICE axis stays with the chain and is genuinely narrowed twice**, and that composition is asserted
  (`TC6`). `applies_to_services` has to travel anyway because it also narrows the tax BASE (`DEF-465`), and the
  service set handed to the selector is the PLAN's, which can only ADMIT a candidate; `resolve_taxes` then
  narrows to the services that actually resolved. A tax scoped to electric on a plan selling electric and
  water does NOT attach to a water-only bill.

### 6 · THE DURABLE HALF — A SIGNATURE, NOT A COMMENT

`tax_facts` takes the four facts as **REQUIRED keyword arguments**, and `build_catalogue` requires `account`
and `premises`. A default would restore the exact arrangement the defect names and would fail closed and
silently again, on money, in the step that publishes no refusal. A caller that cannot name the bill's facts
now gets a `TypeError` at the call site instead of a customer under-charged. Six call sites updated:
`resolution_shadow`, `resolution_switch`, `cr052_r1r7_shadow_measure.py` and three test files.

### 7 · THE RED PROOFS, AND WHAT THEY DO NOT COVER

**On real rows, before the change:** R7 `45 agree / 2 disagree`, `by_step {R7: 2}`, the chain's own sentence
unedited — *"R7: the live path says ('Local', 'Texas State'), the ruled path says ('Local',)"* — plus the
per-authority dollar table in §2.

**The unit suite, RED first (law 7):** the defect was re-introduced as the one line it was
(`plan_tax_rules(plan_id, service_date)`, positional, nothing else changed), the suite run, and the file
restored and verified **byte-identical by sha256**
(`46d42e20db29dddca98ae517a2353d8cecb08e4a1d14d2480f3a825789ab6565`). Result: **6 failed, 7 passed.**
The six are the cases asserting a tax the utility charges is PRESENT — customer class, premises state,
premises city, services, the exemption certificate and the catalogue itself:

> `E  AssertionError: ('Testland County',)`
> `   assert ('Testland County',) == ('Testland County', 'Testland State')`

and the exemption case fails the OTHER way, which is the over-charging direction:

> `E  AssertionError: ('Testland County', 'Testland State')`
> `   assert ('Testland County', 'Testland State') == ('Testland County',)`

⚠ **THE OTHER SEVEN CANNOT GO RED ON THIS DEFECT AND ARE NOT CLAIMED TO.** Three assert a restricted tax is
ABSENT — which the broken code also does, for the wrong reason — and they exist so the tempting fail-open
"fix" breaks in the suite instead of on a bill; four are structural and fail at the signature. Saying which
cases bite and which do not is the point; *"13 red first"* would be a check that cannot fail wearing better
manners.

**THE SABOTAGE, AFTER THE FIX:** `--sabotage R7` removes one tax the live path attached on
`AC-2026-00001` — a residential account, deliberately not one of the two the defect was about — and the
table moves to **R7 46 agree / 1 disagree**, `by_step {R7: 1}`, with the sentence *"R7: the live path says (),
the ruled path says ('Local',)"*. The comparison still bites.

### 8 · IS ANY OTHER STEP STARVED THE SAME WAY? NO — AND IT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

`plan_tax_rules` was the **only** selector call in `resolution_catalogue.py`; every other fact builder reads
rating's own models directly and carries the restriction ONTO the frozen fact, where the chain narrows it:

* **R4** — `charge_code_facts` sets `ChargeCode.customer_classes` from the row, and `resolve_charge_codes`
  narrows on it by service, class and size. The opposite pattern, and correct.
* **R5** — `money_factor` narrows on `premises.inside_city_limits` and the plan's exempt services.
* **R6** — `_discount_facts` publishes what the plan OFFERS; `resolve_discounts` narrows by
  `AccountFacts.enrolments`.
* **R1 / R2 / R3 / R3b** — configuration plus the meter facts the caller supplies.

R7 was the only one where a restriction was evaluated in the selector and the fact was withheld from it.

## 2026-08-31 · ⚖️ THE CHARGE CODE NOW OWNS THE BASE ON BOTH PRICING PATHS — `BR-RAT-088` reaches the code eleven days after it reached every document. `DEF-2823` CLOSED, and no bill moved.

**Nothing is switched and nothing is ruled here.** `resolution_switch.SERVED_BY_CHAIN_DEFAULT` is still the
empty string, no step of the cutover is flipped, no narrowing entered `gather.py`, and no ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5
figure is read, asserted or moved. `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` reads **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** before and
after, run both times rather than assumed — and it is deliberately **not** offered as evidence for this
change, for the reason `gather._base_charge_for`'s own docstring already records about `DEF-154`: *"B5 hands
the base charge to the engine directly, so the ARITHMETIC over it was right and the SOURCING was wrong."*
This is a sourcing change; the frozen suite is blind to the whole class.

Version **`2.106.4`**, in all three places that declare one.

### 1 · WHAT WAS WRONG, IN ONE SENTENCE EACH

`BR-RAT-088` (PO ruling 2026-08-20) says *"the CHARGE CODE owns the base amount; a plan displays it, never
defines it."* It reached the rule register, both superseded rules, the resolution engine's contract, the
charge-code wizard and the plan screens. **It reached neither pricing path.**

* The **live path** read `plan_services.base_charge` — `BR-RAT-012`/`BR-RAT-027`, both stamped SUPERSEDED
  in the same register the code was citing by number to justify itself.
* The **ruled chain's R3** read `tariff_versions.base_charge` — the column this very ruling RETIRES, and
  which `RateScheduleWizard.tsx` dropped the control for in the same move (*"CARRIED, NEVER EDITED … no
  control, no editing, no loss"*). `decimalOut("")` omits the key, so **every schedule version a real
  utility creates through this product stores NULL there, unavoidably.** R3 refused it by name.
* **The charge code's own per-size table was read by nothing.** `grep size_amounts` across
  `apps/rating/resolution*.py`, `apps/rating/pricing/` and `apps/billing/` returned nothing.

Measured on the seeded utility, 47 accounts, real PostgreSQL, `rolsuper = false`, `rolbypassrls = false`,
deny-by-default proved at runtime: **R3 refused 47 of 47** while the live path billed all 47 correctly at
`$8.00`. That is `DEF-2823`, and it was high and open.

### 2 · THE SAFETY ARGUMENT, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS SWITCHED

`10-scripts/def2823_base_source_agreement.py` prints, for every account and every service, what the PLAN
states beside what the CHARGE CODE states — the second resolved through the chain's own R4 narrowing
(service, customer class, connection size, recurrence), never a hand-rolled query.

**Two populations, and the second is the one that found something.**

| population | agree | disagree | charge code silent |
|---|---|---|---|
| **the run** — every ready account, every service | **47** | **0** | 0 |
| **the configuration** — every `(plan, service)` the tenant has | **5** | **1** | 0 |

**Where they agree, switching the source cannot move a bill. That is the whole safety argument and it
covers every account that exists.** The one configuration disagreement touches no account: plan `IND` states
`$180.00` for electric where `BASE-E` states `$12.00` — a **`$168.00`** gap — and **0 accounts are on `IND`**.
It is filed as `DEF-2831` and fixed in the fixture rather than reconciled by preferring a figure.

**And the traversal was measured too, because the PO named it.** PO 2026-08-31, verbatim: *"We already
agreed that it will be in charge code, per utility services , you ahve to take it from there, and plan will
bind it , so plan -> charges code -> base scharges"*.

### 3 · WHAT `plan_charge_rules` IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT — the judgment this lane had to make

The plan is the BINDING and the traversal is followed exactly: the account resolves to a plan (R1), the plan
lists its SERVICES, and each service's base is the code that DECLARES itself that service's base
(`charges.is_base`, never inferred from the code string), narrowed by the account's customer class
(`BR-RAT-108`) and its connection size.

**`plan_charge_rules` is NOT the base's binding, and that is evidence rather than an opinion:**

* `rating.selectors.billable_charge_codes` — the live fee route — excludes `is_base` rows **by name**, in its
  own words: *"the base charge already reaches the bill as the service's base through R4 … the base has its
  own route."*
* `PlanWizard.servicesMissingBaseCharge` and `PlanDetail.baseChargeCodesFor` both find a service's base code
  by `is_base` + `service` over the tenant's catalogue, through no binding row.
* **Measured on the shipped fixture: 9 `plan_charge_rules` rows, of which 0 are `is_base`** — while all 47
  accounts resolve a base. Narrowing the base to bound codes would take every one of them to *no base at
  all*: `DEF-154` again, in the other direction.

**`plan_charge_rules.amount_override` is not consulted, and that is a signed ruling rather than an
omission.** PO 2026-08-19 ruling 1, verbatim *"no plan cannot override prices"* — *"no per-plan amount
override, no per-plan waive, no per-plan rate override"*. The column survives only so no stored figure is
destroyed. The order is now written into `resolve_base_charge`'s own docstring, because the next lane meets
three tables and no file stated the precedence.

### 4 · WHAT LANDED

**R3 and R4 are two questions again, which is `BR-RAT-088`'s own consequence clause read literally** —
*"R3's refusal semantics are unchanged … but the base itself now resolves through R4;
`ScheduleVersion.size_rows` stops carrying money."*

* **R3 · `resolution.resolve_served_size`** — *does this schedule serve this size*. Membership, no money.
  A size absent from the axis still REFUSES, in the same words, because the PO ruled that refusal correct
  twice (`BR-RAT-120`, and again on 2026-08-28: an unpriced size is REFUSED and never substituted).
* **R4 · `resolve_base_charge`** — the amount, from the `is_base` code, per size where the code prices per
  size. A size the CODE does not price refuses there, which is the blank-base refusal re-homed to the step
  that owns the money rather than deleted.
* **The legacy scalar survives as R4's fallback only**, never as a gate, with `base_source` recording which
  object priced the line — so a tenant provisioned before the ruling goes on billing exactly what it billed
  yesterday and the migration stays observable.
* **The live path asks the same question through `rating.selectors.base_charge_from_charge_code`.** It is a
  SECOND narrowing over the same table and deliberately **not** a call into the chain: the shadow compares
  the two answers at R4, and a comparison whose two sides are one function is a check that cannot fail.
* **A plan or schedule figure that DISAGREES with the code REFUSES the bill by name**, quoting both amounts.
  It does not silently prefer the code. `BR-RAT-088`'s own words about the third claimant — *"a migration
  artefact and must be refused once the charge code owns it"* — apply to the plan too, since the ruling
  superseded the rule that put a figure there.

### 7 · THE R3/R4 SPLIT — the design question, settled, with what each row can and cannot say

**The rule already answered it and the answer was not being followed:** `BR-RAT-088` states that R3's job is

* **R3 compares the connection SIZE.** `TariffConfig.size_class` was added for it — the live path already

  account it agrees by construction. It is genuinely independent in two cases and both move money — a

## 2026-08-31 · ⚖️ STEP 4 OF THE CUTOVER, ANSWERED: SWITCH THE FOUR STRONG STEPS FIRST. R1, R2, R4, R7 go; R3, R3b, R5, R6 wait for better evidence.

**PO ruling:** *the four strong ones first* — switch **R1 (which plan), R2 (which rate table), R4 (the amount)
and R7 (taxes)**, and hold **R3 (connection size), R3b (billable quantity), R5 (jurisdiction) and R6
(discounts)** until their evidence is widened.

**⚠ THIS IS NOT THE QUESTION STEP 4 WAS WRITTEN TO ASK, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT.** The step
says *"rule each class of disagreement"*. **There are none.** All eight steps read **47 agree / 0 disagree /
0 could-not-evaluate** on 47 accounts, under `rolsuper=false, rolbypassrls=false`, with the
could-not-evaluate column empty for the first time. So what was put to the PO instead was the honest
question underneath: **the classes are all zero, but the EVIDENCE behind those zeros is uneven — is it good
enough to start switching?**

**WHY EACH OF THE FOUR IS STRONG:** R1 and R2 each have a real comparison whose sabotage moves only its own
row. R4's two sides are **two independent narrowings over one table**, not a call into the chain — the
alternative would have been a check that cannot fail. R7 is the strongest of all, and for the best possible
reason: **it carried a real disagreement this morning** (`DEF-2824`, the ruled path dropping every
restricted tax and charging an exempt account), it was root-caused and fixed, and it now agrees. A step
that has been observed catching a live fault is a step whose comparison is known to work.

**WHY EACH OF THE FOUR IS HELD, stated as measured limits rather than doubts:**
* **R3** — its comparison is **partly circular on an ordinary account**: both paths read
  `metering.connection_size_for`. It is genuinely independent for a master account and against the chain's
  own refusal, and the lane that built it said so rather than claiming more.
* **R3b** — a thousandfold sabotage moves it, so the comparison bites; but **no demand meter is in this
  run**, and a zero register difference hides a multiplier error.
* **R5** — 47 agreements, of which most are `1 == 1`.
* **R6** — can only ever find a code the chain **drops**, never one it wrongly adds.

**WHAT STILL GOVERNS THE SWITCHING, unchanged:** one step at a time, one commit each, each moving that
step's DB half out of `gather` as it goes live (`CR-052` task 21 for the first, task 22 for the rest).
**Four commits, never one.** `BR-BIL-873` still binds R3 and R4 to switch together — so **R4 cannot go
until R3 does**, and that is a constraint on this ruling that the ruling did not know about; it is recorded
here rather than discovered in a diff, and it may reduce the first wave to R1, R2 and R7.

**WHAT WOULD RELEASE THE HELD FOUR:** run the comparison over more than one seeded utility, and over a
period containing a demand meter. That is the same instrument, pointed at a wider population — not new
machinery.

**AND ONE DISAGREEMENT IS OPEN IN A CASE THESE 47 DO NOT COVER.** `DEF-2830`: the live path and the ruled
chain read a stored schedule `0.00` differently — one as *"no charge stated"*, the other as *"the charge is
nothing"* — worth **$8.00 a month** where it applies. It is not in any step's class because no account in
the run configures it. **It must be ruled before R4 switches**, since R4 is the step that reads that figure.

## 2026-08-31 · ⚖️ CR-054 task 9 · THE READING SHEET's `key` COLUMN IS LAWFUL UNDER B14 RULE 31, AND THE SERVICE CONTROL STATES A CONSEQUENCE RATHER THAN A MISSING COLUMN

**Two lane judgements, both taken rather than put to the Product Owner.** Law 13 is explicit that
what legitimately reaches them is a collision with a signed rule, a frozen finance figure, or a fact
only they hold. Neither of these is any of the three: rule 31 is already ratified, the decision is
how it applies, and *"a judgment call recorded in the decision log with its reasoning is the
deliverable; a question is the failure to make one."*

### 1 · The `key` column carries `CY-002|tou_on|M-7450`, and that is not a database id

**The question, in plain words.** The reading sheet a clerk downloads carries a column called `key`,
so that when they type a different meter number over the pre-filled one the product can say *"row 15
was M-7450, now M-7210 — was the meter replaced?"* rather than importing it in silence. B14 rule 31
says nothing internal is ever the visible value of a field, and **a CSV a clerk opens in Excel is a
screen**. So: is that key lawful?

**Ruled: yes, unchanged, and now checked rather than asserted.** Three reasons, in the order they
matter:

1. **There is no id in it.** `CY-002` is the cycle's issued code — the value the picker on stage 1
   shows. `M-7450` is the meter's asset number, the number stamped on the meter. Neither is a
   primary or foreign key and there is no uuid anywhere on the sheet.
2. **The one internal token has its plain word in the next cell.** `tou_on` is the register's enum
   value, and it is the exact word the PO complained *"appears on no screen"*. Rule 31's own escape
   covers this: where the reference is genuinely what a user needs, the human-facing value is what is
   shown — and it is, in the `channel` column, reading `On-peak`.
3. **A key made of words would break the feature it exists for.** The labels come from the locale
   catalogue and there are eleven catalogues. A key spelled `On-peak` changes when a copy edit lands
   or when the clerk runs in Spanish, and a key that changes cannot round-trip. The consequence is
   not cosmetic: the rule would then report *"was the meter replaced?"* against a meter nobody
   touched, which is worse than the silence it was built to remove.

**What changed, since the answer was "leave it alone".** `06-backend/tests/test_cr054_w1_sheet_rule31.py`
now holds all three as three cases, each proved RED first by putting an id in the key. **This is the
half `G28` cannot see:** that gate reads catalogue strings, backend strings and `raise` sites, and a
uuid-shaped VALUE is none of those. `DEF-2716` built the same missing half for the bill surface one
day earlier, in Chromium; this one is in pytest because the sheet is generated server-side.

**And one thing NOT taken.** The sheet's headers are `row_key`, `meter_id`, `unit_of_measure` —
snake case, which is a database spelling on a clerk's screen. **They stay**, because BR-MET-032 says
one published template and one parser and `detect_mapping` matches by NAME: renaming them changes
the published file and every collector export written against it. Recorded here so the next reader
knows it was seen and weighed, not missed.

### 2 · A service subset stores nothing, and the screen says so in six words

**The question.** CR-054 task 9 asks for a multi-select of the utility's services on stage 1,
defaulting to all of them, and the PO's own words are *"utility service - 1 or more in cycle"*. But
`read_import_batches.service` is one text column whose empty value means *every service*, so a batch
can record **one service or all of them and nothing in between** (`DEF-2673`).

**Ruled: build to the two shapes the server holds, and state the CONSEQUENCE on screen — never the
cause.** Choosing one service sends it, and it inherits to every row that does not name its own.
Choosing all of them, or any two or more, sends nothing — and the screen reads **"Each row states
its own service."** Six words, and TRUE of an empty tag; nothing on screen is a fiction.

**Why not widen the column.** It carries hard rule 6's `tag_fingerprint`, which is what decides
whether the same file has been uploaded twice. Adding a field to that hash changes the answer for
every batch already posted, so a corrected re-upload of an old file would stop matching and could
post twice. No CR-054 task asks for the widening and `DEF-2673`'s own closing sentence tells this
lane to build to the two shapes rather than discover the third at integration.

**Why not explain it on screen either.** The control replaces a 36-word note that told the clerk why
a field was missing, and CR-054's copy rule deletes exactly that kind of sentence. A twenty-word
paragraph about a text column would be the same mistake in better manners. **The gap belongs in the
register, which is where a reader finds it** — that is what the register is for.

**One consequence of the empty tag, taken deliberately.** With no tag, `service_coherence` has
nothing to judge a row against, so a gas meter in a file the clerk said was electric-and-water is
not warned about. That is the state the product was already in before this control existed; the
control makes the useful case — one service — reachable for the first time, and does not make the
other case worse.

**And the last chip cannot be removed.** An empty control and a full one send the identical payload,
so *"no service"* and *"every service"* would be one state wearing two faces and nothing downstream
could tell the clerk which they meant. The last remove is drawn disabled with its reason.

### 3 · WHY THE HONEST ANSWER IS "STOP", AND NOT "BUILD THE THREE FORKS TODAY"

`FORKED`'s own docstring says what each missing step costs, and the three the ruling names are not one

The ruling calls R1 strong because *"R1 and R2 have real comparisons whose sabotage moves only their own
row."* **R1's comparison cannot disagree at all.**

`compare()` tests `str(data.rate_plan_id) != str(resolved.plan.plan_id)`. The catalogue is built as
`build_catalogue(plan_id=inputs.plan_id, …)` where `inputs.plan_id` **is** `data.rate_plan_id`, and
`resolution_catalogue.plan_version_facts` filters `pk=plan_id` and then stamps `plan_id=str(plan.id)` on
every `PlanVersion` it yields. **Both sides are the same value by construction.**

Measured on the seeded tenant rather than argued: over its **5 published rate plans → 5 `PlanVersion`
rows, 0** carried a `plan_id` different from the one passed in. And the harness's own reason counters say
the same thing from the other end — across the clean run and the `--sabotage R1` run, **94 account
evaluations produced `figures_match` 93 times and `figures_differ` NOT ONCE**; the sabotaged account left
the agree column as `chain_refused:NoPlanInForce`, a **refusal**, not a comparison difference.

**So R1's `47 agree` is not evidence that the two paths agree about the plan — it is 47 restatements of one
value.** The sabotage does move R1's row, which is why this was not visible: it moves it through the
refusal path. (It also does not move *only* its own row — the refusal cascades, and R2..R7 for that account

## 2026-08-31 · CR-053 TASK 13 IS BUILT — the print hand-over, and four lane judgments the next reader should not have to re-derive

**The ruling this executes.** PO, 2026-08-30, verbatim: *"Im okay with this"*, on the recommendation
that the print hand-over be **one print-ready PDF per bill plus a manifest, one row per bill**. The
fourteen manifest columns are `BR-NOT-029`'s and are not restated here; the file is
`apps/billing/print_set.MANIFEST_HEADER`, in the ruled order, and there is no fifteenth.

**What was actually produced, on real rows.** The seeded sample utility, 93 issued bills:
**93 PDFs, 93 manifest rows, 0 held**. One row was checked against the bill it names —
`AC-2026-00001`, Ana Alvarez, `BL-2607-000001`, **$48.45**, bill date 2 July, due 22 July — and the
PDF that row names was opened and its own page count read out of its bytes (**1**) and compared with
the number the manifest claims. A second run with **one** address deliberately short of its state
produced **91 PDFs, 91 rows and 2 held bills**, each carrying a sentence naming the missing part.

**MEASURED, and the figures are published rather than reasoned** (`10-scripts/cr053_print_set_benchmark.py`,
real PostgreSQL 16 with row-level security enforced, three runs: 0.0118 · 0.0071 · 0.0080 s a bill).
**The slowest is the one published — 0.012 s and 6.01 statements a bill** — because the two fast runs had a
warm cache and a print set is a rare act, so the run a clerk waits through is the cold one; an optimistic
estimate is worse than none when the screen says *"about N seconds"* out loud. At **10,000 bills** that is
**2.0 minutes, 60,108 statements and a 12.8 MiB archive**; at the 25,000 ceiling, about five minutes and
32 MiB. For scale, the bill RUN's published figure is ~72 statements an account, so producing the print set
costs about a twelfth of producing the bills — which is the shape to expect from a pass that writes nothing
and re-prices nothing.

### FOUR JUDGMENTS, EACH WITH ITS REASONING, SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES THEM

**1 · THE BILL DATE IS `invoices.service_date`, AND THAT IS NOT AN APPROXIMATION.** `BR-BIL-070` (PO
2026-08-11 closing `OQ-122`, verbatim *"A Store what they type and use it"*) makes the clerk's typed bill
date the RUN'S SERVICE DATE, and stage 6 stamps it on every invoice the run writes. So the date the run
billed on is a stored column on the bill itself: no join to a cycle, no per-row re-derivation through
`runs.effective_bill_date`, and no clock. `documents.py`'s own `_meta` says the snapshot does not stamp a
`bill_date`, which is what makes this the only lawful source. Checked in a browser against
`GET /invoices/{id}`: manifest `2026-07-02` == the bill's `service_date`.

**2 · `address_line_2` AND `country` ARE EMPTY AND ARE NOT INVENTED (`DEF-2847`).** `customers.addresses`
has `line1`, `city`, `state` and `postal_code` and nothing else, and no customer-side table in this product
has a country at all. Two options were available and both were rejected: **carving a second line out of the
first** is exactly what `BR-NOT-029` clause (a) forbids — *"splitting an address is guessing, and a guessed
address is mail delivered to the wrong house"* — and **using `TenantSettings.country`** would assert where a
CUSTOMER lives from a fact about the UTILITY. Clause (b) names city, state and postal code and deliberately
does not name either of these, so their absence does not hold a bill; it is stated, in the archive's own
README and on the screen. The fix is a schema change and needs the same ruling `DEF-2703` needs.

**3 · NOTHING STREAMS, AND THAT IS THE ANSWER TO `DEF-2734` RATHER THAN A GUARD AGAINST IT.** The archive is
written to disk by a job body running inside its own tenant context, and the download is the platform's
existing `GET /api/exports/{job_id}/file`, which streams a FINISHED FILE with `FileResponse` and touches no
database. There is no lazy generator anywhere in the feature, so the mechanism that made two CSV downloads
arrive as a header with no rows is absent rather than defended against — which is why `G58`'s call-site list
is unchanged and this paragraph exists instead of a third entry on it. `G58`'s own summary already says
*"FileResponse and HttpResponse are out of scope by design"*.

**4 · THE MANIFEST STOPS AT FOURTEEN COLUMNS.** How many pages came from the copy kept at issue versus a
re-render from the bill's pin is a fact a HUMAN wants and a print vendor does not: a manifest is a file
specification somebody's loader is written against, and an extra column is a change to their spec. Both
counts are in `README.txt` instead. The same reasoning keeps the held-back report out of `manifest.csv` and
in a file of its own.

### TWO GAPS THE BUILD FOUND, BOTH FILED

**`DEF-2847`** — `customers.addresses` carries no second address line and no country, so two of the ruled
manifest's nine address fields can only ever be empty. `DEF-2703` filed the same shape one table over —
the service-request blob and nullable premises columns — and named the country gap there, but it did NOT
name `customers.addresses`, which is the table a bill is actually posted from. A lane reading `DEF-2703`
would have fixed premises and left the mailing address exactly as broken.

**`DEF-2848`** — the sample utility's 49 mailing addresses had a town and a postcode and **zero states**, so
the first real run held **every single bill** and the archive had nothing in it. That is `BR-NOT-029` clause
(b) working exactly as ruled, and it is also a fixture that cannot demonstrate the feature. `core/
sample_fixture.py` gains a `STATE` constant beside `CITY` and `POSTAL` (`NE`, because `68901` is Nebraska's
and there is a Silver Creek in it, so the three parts now name one real place), and both seeded address
dicts carry it. That is fixture data for a fictional utility and asserts nothing about any real person —
`BR-CUS-674` is about a customer's own record, and **nothing in this product writes an address on anyone's
behalf**, which `G60` enforces and which this lane did not change.

### WHAT WAS NOT BUILT, AND WHY

**Task 14 stays not built.** `OQ-1167` — the machine-readable vendor extract — is unchanged by this lane and
the decision of 2026-08-30 stands: the format question carries the field list with it, so choosing the shape
and choosing the contents are one decision and it is the vendor's.

**No delivery adapter.** `BR-NOT-013` keeps delivery out of this release and `BR-NOT-029`'s own last clause
says a manifest is part of the RENDERED OUTPUT — the paperwork handed over with the documents — not a
dispatch. Nothing here sends anything anywhere.

**`apps/billing/exports.py` still does not exist**, so `CR-053` task 10's bills-list download glyph is still
disabled with its reason. That is a list CSV for a bookkeeper; this is a print hand-over for a mail house.
Merging them would answer a request for a spreadsheet with a zip of PDFs.

### AND ONE OF THE THIRTEEN RED PROOFS WENT GREEN, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING

Law 7 says prove a new guard RED before trusting it green, and on this lane it caught **a test of this
lane's own that could not fail.** `test_the_pdf_renders_from_the_bills_own_pinned_version` pinned a bill to
layout version **1** and asserted the renderer was asked for **1** — and `documents.LAYOUTS` holds exactly
ONE layout, so `LATEST_REGISTERED_VERSION` **is** 1. The sabotage that made the print set render "on latest"
therefore changed nothing at all, and the test reported success over the exact defect it was written for.

**A pin and a latest that are the same number prove nothing**, and that is the general form worth carrying
forward: a test of *"the stored value wins over the computed one"* is worthless while the two agree, and
nothing about the test's shape says so.

Rewritten to hold two things, both of which now go red on their own sabotage: the bill is pinned to **3**,
which is neither the latest nor the built-in, and the renderer must be asked for **3**; and
`render_invoice` must be called with **no template argument at all**, which is the property `BR-BIL-026`
actually rests on — `documents._pinned` takes the pin off the invoice row precisely when the caller supplies
nothing. The test also asserts that the pinned version is NOT the latest, so the day a second layout is
registered and somebody sets `LATEST_REGISTERED_VERSION` to 3, this test says so instead of going quiet.

## 2026-08-31 · 🔧 STEP 5, STEP ZERO: R1's COMPARISON COULD NOT DISAGREE AND NOW CAN (`DEF-2839` CLOSED). R2 CHECKED FOR THE SAME FAULT AND IS CLEAN — BUT HAD NO MUTATION AT ALL, SO ITS ZERO WAS UNPROVED TOO

**NOTHING WAS SWITCHED IN THIS COMMIT AND NO BILL MOVED.**
`resolution_switch.SERVED_BY_CHAIN_DEFAULT` is still the empty string and `FORKED` is unchanged.
`10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` reads **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** and `G61 frozen-figures` **PASS** (130 signed
money figures across the two finance-signed documents unchanged, 2/2 self-sabotages behaved as stated),
both before and after. The by-name proof is byte-identical: **`AC-2026-00001` water `$8.00`**, **47
base-charge rows, `$390.00`** for 2026-07-01–2026-07-31.

### 1 · WHAT WAS WRONG, IN PLAIN WORDS

The pricing cutover switches one rule at a time, and a rule may only switch when the two paths have been
measured to agree. **R1's measurement was comparing a number with itself.** The shadow asked the ruled path
*"which plan is this account on?"* — and it asked using the plan the live path had just told it. So of
course the answer came back the same, 47 times out of 47, and that was recorded as evidence that the two
paths agree about the plan.

**Measured rather than argued.** Over the 47 accounts of the seeded utility, the old expression's two sides
were identical 47 times and different **0** times, and they can never be different: `adapt` hands
`data.rate_plan_id` to `build_catalogue`, and the catalogue stamps that same id back onto the row it
returns. The mutation the harness carried for R1 *looked* like it worked — it moved the account out of the
agree column — but it moved it through the **refusal** path (`chain_refused:NoPlanInForce`), never through
the comparison. Across a clean run and a sabotaged run, **94 account evaluations produced a figure
difference NOT ONCE.**

### 2 · THE REPAIR, AND WHY THIS HALF IS REAL EVIDENCE

R1's answer is a plan version, and its identity is a pair: **which plan**, and **which version of it**.

* **The plan is an input.** It is now asserted as an invariant instead of counted as agreement — if the two
  sides ever differ, the shadow is comparing two different accounts and every other figure in that run is
  meaningless, which is a louder thing than a pricing disagreement and is raised rather than reported.
* **The version is re-read.** It never reaches the ruled path at all — the object the shadow hands over
  carries the plan and nothing else about it — so the ruled path looks the version up for itself while the
  live path looks it up its own way. Two independent answers to one question, which is what a comparison
  needs.

**PROVED RED FIRST, and the failure is quoted.** Before the repair, two paths stamping **version 1** and
**version 2** on the same bill produced **zero** divergences: `AssertionError: []`. After it, the same case
produces exactly one, carrying both figures.

**PROVED ON REAL ROWS, not only in a unit test.** A new mutation rewrites one account's live plan version
and the run reports:

    R1   46 agree   1 disagree   0 cannot evaluate   figures_match=46; figures_differ=1
    e.g. AC-2026-00001: live plan version 42, ruled plan version 1
    whole-run totals: chain_refused 0

**`chain_refused 0` is the whole point** — it is a figure difference and not a refusal, which is the thing
that was unreachable before. R2 through R7 stayed at 47 agree, so the mutation moves only its own row.

### 3 · THE LIMIT OF THE REPAIRED ROW, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED

Both paths read the same version column of the same plan row under the same published-only filter. So this
comparison bites where the two paths **treat** that column differently — the ruled path substitutes 1 for a
blank, the live path does not — and on the ruled path's date test, which the live path does not apply at all
and which shows up as a refusal rather than as a figure. **It is strictly stronger than comparing an input
to itself and it is weaker than R7, whose two sides are narrowed by different code.** That sentence is the
honest content of R1's agree column and it belongs beside any decision taken from it. This is the same
posture R3 and R6 already take about their own circularity.

### 4 · R2 WAS CHECKED FOR THE SAME FAULT. IT IS CLEAN — AND ITS ZERO WAS STILL UNPROVED

**R2 is not circular.** The object handed to the ruled path carries the plan and nothing about a schedule,
so the ruled path derives the rate-schedule version itself from the plan's binding and the service date,
while the live path carries the version the bill run resolved. Two derivations, as R2 needs.

⚠ **BUT R2 HAD NO MUTATION IN THE HARNESS AT ALL** — the switch offered R1, R3, R3b, R4, R5, R6 and R7 and
skipped R2 — **so its `47 agree` was an unproved zero of exactly the kind this harness exists to refuse.**
One is added and run:

    R2   46 agree   1 disagree   0 cannot evaluate   figures_match=46; figures_differ=1
    e.g. AC-2026-00001: water — live version 00000000-…-00000000d2f0, ruled version 01a0549c-…af5887d99ef5
    whole-run totals: chain_refused 0

**R7 was re-confirmed** with its existing mutation and still bites, as a figure and not a refusal —
`live ()` against `ruled ('Local',)` — which is consistent with its having caught a real fault this morning.

`--tenant <subdomain>`, a comma-separated list, or `all`, plus `--list-tenants`. The default is unchanged, so
every figure already published from the script still reproduces. `--sabotage` REFUSES across several tenants:
it mutates one row and its entire meaning is *"this row's step moved and no other"*, which cannot be read out

|---|---:|---|

### WHY, AND IT IS A PRODUCT FACT AND NOT A FIXTURE ACCIDENT

`resolution_shadow.adapt()` asks `metering.connection_size_for(unit, service)` for **every metered service**

at all** — it is priced as a share of the water usage charge — and `tenancy.service_size_classes` returns an

(which raises). **The adapter asks neither question.** It conflates two different `None`s:

* *nobody recorded a size for this connection* — `DEF-514`, a data gap a human fixes on a screen;
* *this service has no size axis and never will* — a ratified rule.

**And R3 would refuse it even if the adapter let it through.** The sewer schedule version's `size_rows` dict
is correctly empty, so `resolve_served_size` raises `SizeNotServed` for a size that does not exist. So the
hole is in the chain as well as in the adapter, and it is one hole: **R1–R7 has no answer for a service ruled
to have no size axis.**

**The population excluded the failing case.** `brazosbend`'s 47 ready accounts carry exactly ONE
service-size pair — `water · W-58` — which the script has printed all along under *WHAT THE RUN'S ACCOUNTS

the run does not bill. **`47 agree` was true and it was one utility's worth of one service.** That is exactly
the doubt the PO's hold expressed, arrived at from the other direction and now measured rather than
suspected.

repairs it. Proved both ways on a real result body — the line appears at 0 rows and is silent at 75.

## 2026-08-31 · ⚖️ B14 RULE 32 — A SCREEN HAS A DESCRIPTION BUDGET, AND A STATED ABSENCE IS NOT A PARAGRAPH ON THE WORK SURFACE

**PO, working the deployed bill run, four times in twenty minutes:** *"descriptions are not following
rules"* · *"too much desciptions"* · *"too much content - what we found and reading missing"* · *"too much
content - desctiption is too much for clark to read"*.

**COUNTED, BECAUSE THE COMPLAINT IS A FIGURE AND NOT A FEELING.** Step 5 of the bill run carries **nine
explanatory paragraphs and two titled *"what this cannot show you"* panels**, around five checkboxes and four
figures that all read *Not worked out*. Step 4 carries nine more. On step 3's `Reading missing for one
service` list, the same 24-word sentence — *"account AC-…: no usable read for water in this period. Estimate
it, hold the account, or bill without this service — nothing is assumed."* — is printed **93 times**, and its
second half names the three options that are already the row's own dropdown.

**THIS IS OUR OWN LAW, APPLIED WITHOUT A BUDGET, AND THE LAW IS NOT WRONG.** Hard-won law 1 and BR-SHL-025
say a thing the product cannot do yet must be SAID, never left to look like good news — that is why every one
of those paragraphs exists, and each is individually correct. What was missing is that **a screen is a finite
surface and prose competes with work for it.** A clerk running bills is not reading; they are working down a
screen.

### RULE 32, ratified by this ruling

1. **One description per section, one sentence.** A second sentence is a sign the first is doing two jobs.
2. **A stated absence is CLOSED by default.** `RunGap` is now a `<details>`: the title is the one line on the
   surface, the sentence is one click away. Nothing is deleted and nothing is hidden from anyone who wants
   it. ⚠ **The title must still say there is a gap** — it is the only thing visible when closed, and a title
   that reads as decoration puts us back where law 1 started.
3. **A row never repeats what its own control offers.** *"Estimate it, hold the account, or bill without this
   service"* is the dropdown, printed as prose, 93 times.
4. **No rule id and no internal code in clerk-facing copy.** Live today on the run screen and on the ISSUED
   BILL: `BR-MET-121`, `BR-MET-028/029`, `trailing_3_avg`, `cycle_span`, `no_read`, `no_meter`,
   `tariff_prices_no_consumption`, `missing_read`, `account_held_by_disputed_read`. A rule reference belongs
   in the repo, which is what the repo is FOR.
5. **Rule 18 is unchanged** — descriptions still cap at 80% of the content width (`--desc-measure`). Rule 32
   is about HOW MANY and HOW LONG; rule 18 is about how wide. Neither implies the other, which is why the
   screens above satisfy 18 and still failed.

**WHAT IS ENFORCED TODAY: nothing.** Like most of B14 this is RATIFIED and UNENFORCED, because no gate in
this repo reads rendered output. The `<details>` change is structural and therefore holds by construction;
clauses 1, 3 and 4 hold only while lanes remember them, and a gate that counts paragraphs per screen and
greps clerk-facing catalogues for rule ids is the honest way to make them stick.

## 2026-08-31 · ⚖️ R1'S FORK IS BUILT AND R1 IS NOT SWITCHED ON — the gain is a stamp and the risk is a bill

**A lane judgment, taken and recorded rather than put to the Product Owner** (law 13: *"a judgment call
recorded in the decision log with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make one"*).
The PO's cutover ruling of this morning says **switch R1**. This entry does not reopen that. It records what
the first half of executing it found.

**WHAT WAS BUILT (CR-052 task 21).** `resolution_switch.FORKED` was `{R3, R4, R5}` and is now
`{R1, R3, R4, R5}`. The module's own docstring had said R1 could not be forked because *"the chain is HANDED
gather's plan id today, so substituting it would substitute nothing"* — **true of the plan ID, false of the
plan VERSION.** `DEF-2839` separated the two: `adapt` hands `plan_id` to `build_catalogue`, which stamps it
back onto the row it yields, so comparing it compares one value with itself; the VERSION never reaches the
chain, so the chain re-reads it against `BR-RAT-007`. R1's fork substitutes `rate_plan_version` and asserts
the plan id as an invariant — a mismatch REFUSES rather than being reported, because it means the two paths
are looking at different accounts and no figure in that run means anything.

**WHY IT IS NOT SWITCHED ON TODAY, with the two facts that decide it:**

1. **What R1 changes on a bill is the version RECORDED, never an amount.** `rate_plan_version` reaches the
   document payload and prices nothing.
2. **Switching ANY step subjects every account to the WHOLE chain's refusals.** `apply()` calls `resolve()`,
   and `BR-BIL-872` makes a chain refusal refuse the ACCOUNT with no fallback to the old implementation. The
   chain refuses a master account outright (`BR-CUS-068` — it resolves one connection and a master account
   covers several).

**So turning R1 on today would stop billing every master account in order to record a plan version.** That
is not a trade this lane may take on a ruling that was given without that consequence in front of it —
which is the same shape as `DEF-2838`, where four steps were put to the PO as if each could move alone.

**WHAT RELEASES IT:** the shadow reading zero over the widened population — the work `DEF-2851` opened, and
the release condition the PO's own ruling named. It is our work and it has a date attached, not a decision
owed by anyone.

**AND `CR-052` IS AT 21 OF 23, NOT 19.** Task 17 was completed the same day by the two PO rulings that closed
`OQ-291` and `OQ-292` (`BR-RAT-960`, `BR-RAT-961`) and its row still said BLOCKED — the ninth unrecorded
completion this month. Task 22 is three units of work (R2's and R7's forks, and R4 behind R3). Task 23 is
time-gated by its own text — *"after a full billing cycle on the chain"* — and no step is live on the chain.
