## 2026-09-01 · Step 2 of the bill run: one number per fact, every figure with its unit, and a count you can open

Three defects the PO reported working the deployment, all on the strip above step 2 and the
band above the wizard. **No rule was put to the PO and none needed to be** — the first is
settled by a ruling the PO already made, and the other two are judgment calls, which law 13
says are ours to make and write down.

### 1 · DEF-2891 — two numbers labelled *Accounts* on one screen, disagreeing

**What the PO saw:** the band at the top of step 2 read **Accounts 0** while the KPI row
below it read **Accounts 48**.

**Both numbers were right.** `run_detail_dict.counts.accounts` is distinct
`invoices.account_id` on the run — the selector says so in its own words, *"how many accounts
did this run produce a bill for"* — and before the calculate pass that is **0**.
`findings.account_count` is what the prepare pass GATHERED, which is **48**. Two facts, one
word.

**The ruling that decides it is the PO's own, already on file** (decision log 2026-08-19,
§2 of the dashboard caching entry): *"A KPI must agree with its owning module for the same
as-of moment; where cached, state cache age rather than disagree with Finance."* Two numbers
wearing one name cannot agree by construction, so this is that rule broken rather than a new
question. Asking again would have been law 13's exact failure.

**Ruled: the band draws no account count at all**, and the past-runs column is renamed
**Accounts billed** so the figure it carries is named where it is still useful.

**Why deleted rather than relabelled, since relabelling was the obvious move.** The band
already draws **Draft bills** beside it, which is the same population counted in bills. A
fifth tile reading *Accounts with a bill* next to *Draft bills* would be one number twice
under two names — the defect wearing a hat. **Worked on the seeded run:** the band now reads
Period 07/01/2026 · Draft bills 0 · Bills sent 46 · Still broken 1, and the only account
count on the page is step 2's **48**.

### 2 · DEF-2892 — three units in one row, and no unit stated anywhere

**What the PO saw:** `48 · 47 · 1 · 95 · 0 · 31` under *Accounts · Ready to bill · Cannot be
billed · Waiting on you · Decided · Days in the cycle*, and said the fourth tile *"reads as
customers and is bigger than the total"*.

It does. The fourth counts **case rows**, not accounts — one account can raise several
questions — so 95 undecided questions sat beside 48 accounts in a row a person reads as one
kind of thing.

**The PO offered two remedies: *"Say the unit, or split the row."*** **Ruled: both, done as
one thing.** Every label now opens with the unit it counts —

| tile | label | counts |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Accounts in this run | accounts |
| 2 | Accounts ready to bill | accounts |
| 3 | Accounts that cannot be billed | accounts |
| 4 | Decisions waiting on you | decisions |
| 5 | Decisions you have taken | decisions |
| 6 | Days in the cycle | days |

— so a clerk scanning the row reads **accounts accounts accounts decisions decisions days**,
and the row splits into three families by eye without becoming three components.

**The unit is also declared in the type**, `GenerationTile.unit`, so a seventh tile cannot be
added without answering the question, and a case asserts the three units are GROUPED rather
than interleaved. The unit is not put beside the number: `.kpi .v` is 26px with
`text-overflow: ellipsis`, so *"48 accounts"* would be clipped at the 180px tile width.

### 3 · DEF-2893 — *Cannot be billed 1*, and nothing said who or why

The run had already worked out both halves. `runs.AccountProblem` carries the account, a
reason and the sentence a person acts on, and those rows WERE drawn — split across the six
sub-screens by the stage that owns each (BR-BIL-040). So a clerk reading **1** had to open up
to six tabs to find out which account.

**Ruled: a disclosure under the strip, closed by default (B14 rule 32), listing every blocked
account with its reason in words and the sub-screen that fixes it.** It draws nothing at all
when nothing is blocked — an empty disclosure invites a click that answers nothing.

**It does not duplicate the sub-screens and that is the test it had to pass.** A sub-screen is
by definition a PART of the set; this is the only place the whole set appears. *Where to fix
it* is derived by re-reading `findingTabForStage`, the one map that already places these rows,
rather than by writing a second one.

**Worked on the seeded run:** *cannot be billed 1* opens to `AC-2026-00008` — *A reading is
disputed and not yet cleared* — *Meter reads*.

### What the browser found that the test cases could not

The render check was written first and the first draft of it FAILED on correct code: a closed
`<details>` hides its content, and `innerText` reads what is RENDERED, so all three cells came
back empty over a perfect table. `textContent` would have passed and taught us nothing.
**The check now clicks**, which is also the only way to learn that the disclosure opens.

**And it found a real fault nothing else would have — `DEF-2895`.** The blocked row's own
sentence, composed in `apps/billing/runs.py` line 840, prints **`BR-MET-024`** and
**`OQ-043`** at a billing clerk, and a raw ISO timestamp `2026-07-31T00:00:00+00:00`.
`DEF-2432` is the same fault in the same FILE, and its recorded surface is line 1160 and step
4's break list — so a lane fixing DEF-2432 by what it says would have left this one printing.
It is REPORTED and not failed by the check, because the copy is backend-composed and a
frontend lane may not edit it; a red check nobody can clear is a check people stop reading.

### Proved RED first, twice, on the exact shipped shape (law 7)

Five jsdom cases and four browser checks were each run against the code as the PO saw it.
The browser output of that run is the PO's screen: band **accounts 46** beside strip
**accounts 48**, and labels *ready to bill · cannot be billed · waiting on you · decided*
naming no unit.

**A flaw in one of my own checks was found this way and is worth recording**, because it is
DEF-182's shape: *"the units are grouped, not interleaved"* PASSED on the broken row, since
every unknown unit shares one `indexOf` and the sequence stays monotonic. It now reports
**NOT EXERCISED** when any tile names no unit, and the assertion above it is the one that
fails. A second flaw: the check clicked unconditionally and threw a Playwright timeout on the
broken screen, so the four checks after it never ran — it reports now instead of dying.

## 2026-09-01 · ⚖️ CR-056 W0 · THE FIVE RULINGS OF THE ANALYSIS SESSION, WRITTEN DOWN — ONE QUOTED, FOUR RECONSTRUCTED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS STAMPED ON EACH

**Why this entry exists at all.** Five rulings were made on 2026-08-31 while the session was reading
*Who Gets Billed, and Under What Number*, and **not one of them reached the repository.** That session was
instructed *analysis only, no repository writes*, so it was right at the time, and its own closing words say
so: *"None of this is in the repository yet … Say the word and I will capture all of it properly."* Nobody
said the word. `CR-056` is the capture; this is its first task.

⚠ **ONE IS QUOTED FROM THE PRODUCT OWNER'S OWN TYPING AND FOUR ARE RECONSTRUCTED FROM AN ARTIFACT THAT IS
NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY.** Recording a paraphrase as if it were a quotation is exactly how two contradictory
rules end up in one repo, so each one below carries its form, and a reconstruction is never dressed up as a
quotation anywhere it is cited.

| # | The ruling | Form | Confirmed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R1** | *"Duplex should be linked to master account of Ajinkya → link this account to customer # that already exist"* | **VERBATIM** | yes — the PO's own words |
| **R2** | A Master Account attaches to the PREMISES itself, not to a unit inside it | **RECONSTRUCTED** | **yes, in substance** — see below |
| **R3** | The Customer # is keyed on IDENTITY (SSN · phone · driving licence) and reused, never allocated twice to one person | **RECONSTRUCTED** | **NO — still owed** |
| **R4** | A common area gets no account of its own | **RECONSTRUCTED** | **in substance for W1 only** — see below |
| **R5** | A premises row with a blank owner column is still created; the owner is flagged, not invented | **RECONSTRUCTED** | **yes, in substance** — see below |

### WHICH OF THE FOUR RECONSTRUCTIONS THE REPOSITORY ALREADY RATIFIES, AND WHICH IT DOES NOT

This matters more than the table: **`CR-056` says all four "must be confirmed before anything in W1–W6 is
built on them", and by the time W1 started, two of them had been.** The Product Owner ruled twice on
2026-08-31 in this same log, and those two rulings assert the substance of R2 and R5 in the repository's own
record. Naming that is not a loophole — it is the difference between building on a paraphrase and building
on a ruling.

* **R2 is ratified in substance.** The 2026-08-31 ruling *"the owner-occupier holds two accounts and receives
  one bill"* states, in the repository, that **"every address gets its owner a Master Account, whether or not
  anything is shared, and whether or not the owner lives there."** An account that exists for an address with
  nothing shared cannot hang off a shared unit, because there is not one. **W1 rests on this sentence, not on
  the reconstruction.**
* **R5 is ratified in substance.** The same day's second ruling: a premises naming an owner nobody has on
  file **"creates the premises and creates no party. The address loads, the owner is flagged for a human to
  search, and nothing is invented."** That is R5 in the PO's own decision.
* **R4 is ratified only as far as W1 needs it.** What W1 does is stop a Master Account ANCHORING on a common
  area; it does not decide whether a common area may ever hold an account of its own. The first follows from
  R2 (the account is at the address); the second is not ruled and nothing here assumes it.
* **R3 is NOT confirmed by a quotation, and this lane does not build on it** — identity on the customer is
  `CR-056` W2, which a DIFFERENT lane built in a different worktree in the same hours. The reconstruction
  stands as a reconstruction; what that lane built rests on `BR-CUS-089`'s and `BR-CUS-092`'s own signed
  rules, which is the right footing for it either way.

### THE SHIFT, IN ONE SENTENCE

> **FROM:** a Master Account is the bill for shared space.
> **TO:** a Master Account is the owner's account at an address.

### WHAT THIS SUPERSEDES, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**`BR-CUS-068` and the 2026-08-27 ruling closing `OQ-500`.** That ruling made master-ness **derived from
occupancy** — owner-billed against tenant-billed — and *"never chosen at creation"*, so an owner-occupier got
one Regular Account and no master shape at all. **Both rules cannot be true at once**, and under both
together an owner-occupier holds two accounts and receives two bills for one house. R1 and R2 replace it, and
the 2026-08-31 ruling settles what the customer receives: two accounts, **one** bill, because an account with
no charges produces no document. Both rule rows are stamped SUPERSEDED **at the sentence** — `BR-CUS-068` in
`04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/02-business-rules.md`, `BR-MET-400` in the metering file, and the `OQ-500`
row in `12-governance/01-open-questions.md`.

### THE MONEY THAT MUST NOT MOVE, AND DID NOT

**`1408 Elm Street` still bills `$69.60`** — `$41.20` of hallway and exterior lighting plus `$28.40` of
shared irrigation, on one document to the owner. Under the old plumbing the account hung off the hallway and
reached the irrigation through a service agreement; under the new plumbing it hangs off the address and
reaches **both** through service agreements. Same figure, different plumbing, and
`tests/test_br_cus_068_master_bill.py` proves it from typed prices rather than from a constant, with tc2
still showing the anchor-only answer as `$41.20` and NOT `$69.60`. **No ❄️ frozen B4/B5 figure is touched:**
golden-verify **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** and `G61` **PASS (130 frozen figures)** before and after.

### THE OPEN QUESTIONS — AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THERE ARE NONE LEFT

⚠ **THIS SECTION WAS WRITTEN TO RAISE SEVEN QUESTIONS AND RAISES NONE, BECAUSE THE REPOSITORY MOVED UNDER IT
WHILE THIS LANE WAS BUILDING — AND THAT IS THE FINDING, NOT AN APOLOGY.** `CR-056` task 3 says nine questions;
its §3 lists nine; the 2026-08-31 entry above says *seven remaining* and then lists six. **All nine are ruled**,
six of them by rulings recorded between this lane's base commit and its first push:

| # | Question | Where it was answered |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | An owner who lives in his own house — one account or two? | 2026-08-31 — **two accounts, one bill** |
| 2 | An owner name nobody has on file | 2026-08-31 — **load the address, create nobody, flag it** |
| 3 | Empty-unit charge per unit or per premises | 2026-08-31 — **per unit**, `$183.00` on six flats at `$30.50` |
| 4 | Move-out — automatic or confirmed | 2026-08-31 — **part of move-out, stated explicitly in its impact section** |
| 5 | He sells the property | 2026-08-31 — **the account transfers to the buyer** |
| 6 | Two shared spaces on one service | 2026-08-31 — **one standing charge for the address** |
| 7 | Addresses on file with only a typed-in name | 2026-09-01 — **the account appears when the owner is identified** |
| 8 | May the owner point at a tenant's account | 2026-09-01 — **yes, as a choice the clerk makes on purpose** |
| 9 | Unallocated usage | 2026-09-01 — **deferred**, its own change request when it is picked up |

**SO NO NEW OPEN QUESTION IS MINTED BY THIS LANE, AND THAT IS LAW 13 APPLIED RATHER THAN A GAP LEFT.** Three
ids — `OQ-1230`, `OQ-1231`, `OQ-1232` — were drafted for questions 4, 5 and 8 against a tip that predated their
rulings, and were withdrawn unwritten when the push helper refused a moved file and the tip was re-read. Two
more were never minted at all: questions 6 and 9 are already carried by **`OQ-334`** (raised 2026-08-22) and
**`OQ-327`**, both older than this CR, and minting new ids for them would have made the register count one
question twice and split its answer across two rows. Both rows are stamped with their rulings in this commit.

⚠ **THE MECHANISM IS WORTH NAMING BECAUSE IT WILL HAPPEN AGAIN.** Two lanes worked `CR-056` in separate
worktrees and neither could see the other until a push. This one drafted three questions the other was having
answered in the same hours. **What caught it was `push_paths.sh` REFUSING a moved path** — law 11's blob
re-derivation clause doing exactly what it was written for — and the fix was to re-read the tip and rewrite,
not to push harder. **An allocated id is a blob too:** `BR-CUS-1000`, `BR-CUS-1001` and `BR-MET-1000` had been
taken by that lane as well, so this work carries `BR-CUS-1010/1011/1012` and `BR-MET-1010/1011`, and migration
`customers 0036` became `0037`. Content and ids were re-derived in one act, which is what law 11 asks for.

### AND ONE ANSWER THAT WAS ALREADY OWED SOMEWHERE ELSE

`OQ-350` closed on 2026-08-24 with *"(a) the owner/landlord"* pays an empty unit's base charge, and its own
closing note left two things unsettled by name — **"whether the owner is billed PER EMPTY UNIT or ONCE PER
PREMISES"**, and what happens before an owner account exists. The first of those is the 2026-08-31 ruling
exactly: **per unit, `$183.00` on six empty flats at `$30.50`, not `$30.50`.** That half is stamped closed on
`OQ-350` and on `BR-MET-105` in this commit, because a question answered in one register and left open in
another is how the same thing gets asked twice (law 13). **The second half narrows and does not close:**
`ensure_owner_master_account` can now create that account for a premises with nothing shared, so the gap stops
being structural — but nothing calls it yet, which is said out loud rather than implied (hard-won law 2).

### WHAT W1 BUILT, AND THE THREE JUDGMENTS IT MADE RATHER THAN ASKED

**The schema.** `accounts.premises_id` — a plain UUID, not a ForeignKey, because B2 §2's cross-module FK set is
REVIEWED and this link is not in it; `template_override_id` on the same table and
`service_requests.resolved_premises_id` are the two standing precedents for exactly that posture.
`accounts.unit_id` becomes NULLABLE, and two CHECK constraints replace what the `NOT NULL` was carrying: an
account names a unit or a premises (`ck_accounts_anchored`), and a `regular` account still names a unit
(`ck_accounts_regular_has_unit`). Migration `customers 0037`, 🔒 HUMAN-OWNED, HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING.

**JUDGMENT 1 — the backfill fills the address IN and re-anchors nothing.** `CR-056` task 6 is one sentence,
*every existing Master Account bills exactly what it bills today*, so every existing row keeps its `unit_id`
and gains its address. Two shapes live in one table on purpose, and every read that decides money answers
identically on both. Re-anchoring live accounts would change what a money path reads in order to tidy a column.

**JUDGMENT 2 — one owner account per address (`BR-CUS-1011`), enforced in the service layer and not in the
database.** Two Master Accounts at one address are two owners of one building, and every *who owns this
premises* read would then have to break a tie; `BR-CUS-171` records what that felt like while ownership was
still geometric. It is a lane judgment rather than a question because it follows from `BR-CUS-1010`, moves no
frozen figure, and needs no fact only the PO holds. It is service-layer-only for `OQ-092`'s stated reason and
for one more: premises carrying two masters already exist, and a database constraint would refuse to migrate
them.

**JUDGMENT 3 — `ensure_owner_master_account` refuses rather than picking when an owner owns two addresses.**
`premises_owners.master_account_id` is a link on the OWNER and an account is per ADDRESS, so the caller names
the premises and the door resolves it only where the owner owns exactly one. Guessing would open an account
for a building nobody asked about.

**THE MONEY, BOTH SIDES.** `1408 Elm Street` bills **`$41.20`** of hallway and exterior lighting plus
**`$28.40`** of shared irrigation = **`$69.60`** on one owner document, on the new plumbing; the inversion
beside it still measures the short answer at **`$41.20`** and asserts it is NOT `$69.60`. Golden-verify **33
PASS / 0 FAIL** and `G61` **PASS, 130 frozen figures**, before and after. No ❄️ B4/B5 figure is touched.

## 2026-08-31 · ⚖️ CR-056 W2/W3/W5 — THE FIVE JUDGEMENTS A MATCHER FORCED, AND THE ONE THAT IS A ONE-WAY DOOR

**None of these is a question for the Product Owner** (law 13: a judgement recorded with its
reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make one). Each is written down with the
alternative it beat, because the next lane will meet the same fork.

### 1 · THE MATCHER EMITS `strong` AND `weak` AND NEVER `probable`

`BR-CUS-089`'s tier vocabulary holds three words. The PO ruled what earns `strong` — *"Name + date
of birth + one government ID"*, 2026-08-25, closing `OQ-364` — and ruled **nothing at all** about
where `probable` begins. A machine handing one out would be minting a second threshold nobody made,
on the one path that moves somebody else's money. `probable` stays a HUMAN's word: a clerk may
still record it through `service_request_service.link_customer`, and it moves no money there either.

### 2 · A PHONE MATCH ON ITS OWN IS `weak`, THOUGH R3 CALLS THE PHONE IDENTITY EVIDENCE

`CR-056`'s ruling R3 names *SSN · phone · driving licence* — and R3 is **RECONSTRUCTED**, stamped so
in the CR's own §0 table. `BR-CUS-089` is **VERBATIM** and says *one government ID*. A telephone
number is not one. So the phone is indexed and a phone hit SURFACES a candidate for a human to look
at; it can never make one `strong`. Reading a reconstructed ruling as licence to loosen a signed one
is how a paraphrase becomes law.

### 3 · NAMES ARE COMPARED EXACTLY, CASE-FOLDED — NEVER FUZZILY

`CR-056` §4's own example is `A. Kulkarni` against `Ajinkya Kulkarni`. **Every rule loose enough to
unite those two also unites two real strangers**, and where the line sits is an unruled threshold.
Case-folding and whitespace-collapsing is the posture `customers.external_ref` and
`premises_owners.name` already take (`CUST-118` and `cust-118` are one customer in any legacy
export); anything beyond it would be this lane picking a number.

### 4 · NO UNIQUE CONSTRAINT ON THE SSN BLIND INDEX — AND THIS IS THE ONE-WAY DOOR

**The worked case.** A clerk opens an account and types a Social Security number a customer already
on file holds. Under a unique index the save is REFUSED, at the counter, on digits that may have
been mistyped, and the refusal cannot be relaxed without a migration. Under the built behaviour the
account opens, the two are NOT merged, and the clerk is shown who looked similar.

R3 — *"the Customer # is keyed on IDENTITY and reused, never allocated twice to one person"* — is
the ruling that would license the constraint, and **it is reconstructed**; CR-056 §0 says a
reconstructed ruling *"must be confirmed before anything in W1–W6 is built on them"*. So R3's
BEHAVIOUR is built in the service layer, where it is reversible, and the constraint is not. **It is
named in the review-ledger row as the one thing that needs the PO**, in those words.

### 5 · `premises_owners.customer_id` IS RULED OUT AS A PATH, AND THE COLUMN IS NOT DROPPED

Two paths reached the same person and one skipped the account — the only row that holds a balance.
`BR-MET-1020` shuts the door and derives the read through the master account. **The column stays**,
because `BR-MET-150` is a PO ruling that asked for the link in its own words (*"linked to the
customer they already are"*) and that intent is fully served one hop further along; removing the
column would reverse the ruling's own sentence, which law 13 says only the PO may state, and would
destroy existing rows. Raised as **`OQ-1240`**, open and blocking nothing.

### AND ONE CORRECTION, WHICH IS HARD-WON LAW 1 IN ITS SECOND FORM

`discounts.CARRY_FORWARD_NO_MATCH_RULE` told every caller that *"nothing in this repository defines
what makes a match strong … No open question covers the criteria; one is owed."* **Both clauses
were false when written** — `OQ-364` was minted for exactly that question and closed on 2026-08-25,
the same week. A stated absence that has been filled is a lie with a rule id on it, so the text is
corrected rather than left standing, and what remains true is narrower: the criteria cannot be
assessed on a SERVICE REQUEST, because `REQ-03.1` still collects no date of birth (`DEF-638(2)`).

### THE ID COLLISION, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS `DEF-1787` HAPPENING AGAIN

This lane and the CR-056 W0/W1 lane both computed `max + 1` correctly, at the same time, in separate
worktrees, and both got `BR-CUS-1000/1001`, `BR-MET-1000` and `OQ-1230`. Neither allocator was
wrong: a sibling in its own worktree has rows in no ref the other can read. It was caught by
re-deriving at push time, and this lane moved to `BR-CUS-1020/1011`, `BR-MET-1020` and `OQ-1240` —
because `14-id-reservations.md`'s rule is about CITATIONS, that lane's W0 wave is the one that
DEFINES the CR-056 model rules, and this lane's four ids were cited in four files and nowhere else.

## 2026-09-01 · CR-051's own browser evidence had been failing on correct screens

**`10-scripts/render-checks/cr051-step23.mjs` is what makes CR-051 tasks 13–19 DONE.**
The PO's rule of 2026-08-30 is that *"All UI screen should be confirm using real broswer
testing and not just based on test cases"*, and that file is the evidence. Its own
shipped note reads **43 checks, all passing**.

**Re-run on 2026-09-01 it failed EIGHT times, and not one failure was a broken screen.**
Found only because this lane changed a KPI label and went to see what else read it.

### DEF-2899 — seven failures from markup and copy that moved

| what failed | why |
|---|---|
| the twelve reading scenarios are chips | the PO ruled *"the bill-run tabs are filters now"* on 2026-08-31 (`35ae9e5b`) — they are a `<select>` |
| every chip carries its own count | same control |
| the three kinds of charge | same control |
| three families, not fifteen tabs | same control |
| the cases inside the open family are a filter | same control |
| the absence is NAMED (`DEF-2596`) | **B14 rule 32**, ratified the day AFTER the check last passed: a stated absence is a `<details>` **closed by default**, so `RunGap` hides its own sentence and `body.innerText` — which reports what is RENDERED — stopped finding it |
| the URL names the open family | it compared the open option's WORDS against *"What the customer owes"*, and the bill run stopped saying **customers** (`06682551`, v2.109.1). The screen honours the URL perfectly and reads *What the account owes* |

**Every requirement asserted is unchanged. Only where each is drawn, and what each is
called, moved.** The repairs read the pickers, read the closed panel's sentence from the
markup, and — for the family — key on the **option's VALUE, which is the family id the
URL itself names** and the one part of that control a reword cannot touch. That last one
is the general lesson: **a check should key on the id and print the words, not the other
way round.**

**Measured after the repairs, on a real browser against real PostgreSQL:**

    scenarios  All (47) · Collected (46) · Missing (1) · and nine more, each with a count
    kinds      All (0) · Late payment fees (0) · Service charges (0)
    families   Readings and usage (2) · What the account owes (0) · What goes on the bill (0)

**Why this is worth a decision-log entry and not just a defect row.** The failure prints
as `chips: undefined` and two red lines. **That reads exactly like a broken screen**, and
the cost lands on whoever runs it next — which for this file is twenty minutes of browser
time before the first result. This is `DEF-524`'s shape one instrument along: *G14's
hardcoded path outlived the file it named and reported PASS through six UI defects*. Same
cause, opposite sign — there a stale check said everything was fine, here it says the
screen is broken. **A check pinned to markup or to copy is pinned to a decision a
one-sentence ruling can reverse**, and nothing in this repo tells you when that happened.

### DEF-2900 — two failures the check caused itself, and its own comment knew

Section 6 **records a decision** to prove the KPIs move without a reload. A decision is
durable. Measured on 2026-09-01, this run held **four `bill_run_decisions` rows, every one
written by an earlier run of this same file**.

So from the second run onward it re-answered a row that already carried that answer:
nothing moved, nothing could, and it reported **`waiting 1→1, decided 1→1`** as a failure
of `DEF-2705`'s fix — the very thing the section exists to protect. The assertion beside
it read the same leftovers as a screen **pre-selecting a choice**, which is a
`BR-BIL-015` violation and would have been chased as one.

⚠ **THE FILE'S OWN COMMENT STATED THE PRECONDITION** — *"The row must still be UNDECIDED
for the movement to be observable. A rerun of this check would otherwise measure a tile
that was already at its final value and report a pass that proves nothing."* — **and the
code never checked `value === ""`.** That is hard-won law 1 exactly: a comment claiming a
guarantee is not the guarantee, on a file written to BE the guarantee. It even predicted
the wrong direction; the leftovers produce a false FAILURE, not a false pass.

**Both are now asked in ways a run history cannot change:** the move records against a
control whose value is empty, and *"nothing is pre-selected"* asks whether every control
offers the empty placeholder FIRST and at least one row is showing it. **Measured after
the fix: `the KPIs MOVED without a reload: waiting 2→1, decided 0→1`.**

**`cr051-step23.mjs` measured after the repairs: 45 checks, 0 failing.**

### DEF-2921 — the sibling check waits for a quiet network that never comes

`cr051-run-screens.mjs` navigates the wizard with `waitUntil: "networkidle"`, whose
budget is **30 seconds**. `GET /billing/runs/{id}/findings` re-runs the whole prepare
pass on every call — the PO ruled it recomputed and never cached on 2026-08-30 — and
**measured 20.6s for 47 accounts**. So the check passes on an idle machine and fails with
`page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded` the moment anything else touches the database,
which is what happened when it ran beside its sibling today.

**`cr051-step23.mjs` had already diagnosed this and written the fix into its own `open()`
helper, with the reasoning.** This file never got it. All seven wizard navigations now
wait for the run band; `/signin` keeps `networkidle` because it fires no run read. **Two
sibling files, one lesson, learned once** — which is the thing a repo is supposed to make
unnecessary.

### And a fault in the repair, kept because it is a trap in this file's shape

`READ_STEP2` and `READ_STEP3` are **template literals** — browser code carried as strings.
Four comments added above were written the way every comment in this repo names an
identifier, in backticks, and **a backtick inside a template literal ends it**. Node
refused the whole file with `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'RunGap'`.

That is the good failure mode — it did not run, rather than running wrong — but the
repair now **asserts** it rather than remembering: it re-reads both literals and refuses
if either still holds a backtick.

⚠ **AND A GATE IS MISSING, RAISED RATHER THAN TAKEN: nothing in this repo parse-checks
the `.mjs` render checks.** A broken one is discovered by running it, and running this one
takes twenty minutes. `node --check 10-scripts/render-checks/*.mjs` is seconds. It belongs
with whoever owns the gate set, not with a frontend lane adding itself a gate.

### DEF-2879 — and the sibling had a stale assertion of its own, pointing the other way

`cr051-run-screens.mjs` asserts *"every retry control is DISABLED and carries its
reason"*. That was exactly right while `DEF-2557` stood: `runs.retry_account` was
reachable from no route, so BR-SHL-025 made the control **drawn-and-refused** rather
than absent, and the check pinned it.

**`881c1d37` mounted `POST /billing/runs/{run}/breaks/{account}/retry` and closed
DEF-2557 in the register with that commit.** `breakRetryReason` returns null, the
control is live, and the check went on demanding the refusal — reporting a working
screen as broken, in a message that opens with the id of the defect it was wrong about.

⚠ **A CHECK THAT PINS A STATED ABSENCE HAS AN EXPIRY DATE AND NO WAY TO KNOW IT.**
Nothing tells an assertion that the gap it guards has been filled. **The register knew** —
the row says `fixed` and names the commit — **and the register is not what runs here.**
That is the same distance between two records that made `CR-051` under-report itself by
five tasks, and it is worth stating as a general shape: **a stated absence is a claim with
two homes, and only one of them fails when it stops being true.**

**`cr051-run-screens.mjs` measured after all three of its repairs: 34 checks, 0 failing**
— against **6 and a crash** when this lane first ran it.

### What the four together say

`DEF-2899`, `DEF-2900`, `DEF-2921` and `DEF-2879` are one lesson in four shapes:
**a browser check is a second copy of the product's own decisions, and it goes stale
exactly where the product moves fastest** — the copy a PO rewords, the control a PO
reshapes, the absence a lane fills, the timing a measurement changes.

**None is a reason to trust these checks less; all four were found by running one.**
But two things follow for whoever writes the next one:

* **key on the id, print the words** — the family assertion failed on a noun and passes
  on `owes`, which is what the URL names;
* **assert the requirement, not the markup** — *twelve scenarios each carrying a count*
  survived the tab-strip becoming a select; *a `[role="tablist"]` of twelve buttons* did
  not, and they were the same sentence in the CR.

## 2026-09-01 · ⚖️ CR-056 · IDENTITY IS PER KIND: A PERSON IS KNOWN BY SSN, LICENCE OR PHONE; A COMPANY BY ITS TAX ID. And a duplicate identifier REFUSES TO LINK, never refuses to save

**Two PO rulings, and the first one changes what was built this morning.**

### RULING 9 — a customer is a PERSON or a COMPANY, and each is identified by different things

**PO verbatim:** *"Customer can be person or company - in case of person , if we have SSN, or DL or Phone
number, we create the Customer ID and attached these to custoemr ID ; if it is Company then we ask for Tax
ID"*.

**⚠ THIS COLLIDES WITH `BR-CUS-089` AND THE COLLISION MUST BE STATED, NOT SMOOTHED (law 13).** That rule is
signed and verbatim — *a strong match is **name AND date of birth AND one government identifier**, PO
2026-08-25 closing `OQ-364`* — and `CR-056` W2 built the matcher to exactly it this morning. **A company has
no date of birth.** Read literally, `BR-CUS-089` makes every company permanently unmatchable, which nobody
intended and which this ruling now exposes.

**SO `BR-CUS-089` IS A RULE ABOUT PERSONS, and is narrowed to say so rather than reversed.** Its three-part
test stands unchanged where the customer is a person. **A company is matched on its Tax ID**, which is the
identifier the PO has now named for that kind.

**THE MODEL ALREADY CARRIES THE DISTINCTION** — `customers (kind person|company, …)`, B2's own words — so
this is a narrowing onto a column that exists, not a new concept.

**WHAT MUST BE BUILT, and the second half of it does not exist:**

| Kind | Identified by | State today |
|---|---|---|
| **Person** | SSN · driving licence · phone | **BUILT** — encrypted with a blind index beside each, migration `customers 0036` |
| **Company** | **Tax ID** | **NOT BUILT — no such field on `customers`** |

⚠ **`tenancy.ein` IS NOT IT.** That column is the UTILITY's own tax number, on another module's table. A
customer's Tax ID is a different fact about a different party, and reusing the utility's would be a
cross-module read of the wrong row. **A new encrypted field with its own blind index, on `customers`, matching
what W2 built for a person.**

**AND THE CAPTURE MUST FOLLOW THE KIND.** A person is not asked for a Tax ID and a company is not asked for a
driving licence — asking for both and leaving one blank turns a rule into a habit, and the blank field
eventually gets filled with something.

**⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE, so nobody infers it:** whether a company ALSO gets a date of birth equivalent
(an incorporation date), and whether a sole trader is a person or a company. Both are real and neither is
ruled; a lane meeting either stubs and asks.

### RULING 10 — a duplicate identifier refuses to LINK, and never refuses to SAVE

**PO chose the reversible half**, which is what W2 built: a second customer carrying an identifier already on
file **saves**, and the system **refuses to link them**, flagging it for a person to resolve.

**WHY THE ALTERNATIVE WAS PUT AND DECLINED.** A database uniqueness rule is a **one-way door**: a clerk who
mistypes one digit of a real customer's number is stopped at the counter and cannot open the account at all,
and undoing the rule later means finding and merging whatever was created while it stood. The rule that would
have licensed it is one of `CR-056`'s **reconstructed** four rather than a quotation, and §0 of that CR says a
reconstruction is confirmed before it is built on. **The stricter rule can still be added once real data shows
how often a duplicate actually happens; the reverse is not true.**

**WHAT IS ENFORCED INSTEAD, and it is not nothing:** the match is computed, the collision is visible, and the
LINK — the thing that would carry a deposit — is refused by name. **A weak match shows no figure at all**, so
nobody can read a maybe as a balance.

### THE TALLY — ten answers, and the last two are the first that changed prior work

`CR-056` now carries **eight rulings, one deferral and one narrowing of a signed rule.** Ruling 9 is the
narrowing, and it is the first of the ten that makes something already built incomplete rather than merely
guiding what comes next. A task for the company half belongs in the CR before anyone reads W2 as finished.

---

## 2026-09-01 · A RENDER CHECK FOR A BRANCH NO DATA ON THIS BOX CAN REACH IS BUILT ON A STUB API, AND SAYS SO IN ITS OWN HEADER (CR-053 task 15)

**The judgment, in one sentence:** where a screen state cannot be produced by the product and cannot
be produced by any database we have, a render check may drive it from a **stub API** — and it is
only honest if the file states, in its header, the four things it therefore does not prove.

**WHAT FORCED IT.** CR-053 task 9 serves `charges_by_service` with a tie-out that **reports** a
disagreement and never reconciles one (`BR-BIL-032`). The screen draws that disagreement in the
danger tier — *"These lines add up to $258.28 and the bill says $260.00. Nothing here changes either
figure."* **That branch had never been drawn in a browser**, and the existing end-to-end check
cannot reach it: its tie-out assertion compares the server's verdict with the screen's, which is
right, and on every bill it has ever opened both are `true`. **A check that only ever sees a zero
delta cannot tell a working tie-out from an absent one.**

**AND IT IS UNREACHABLE FROM DATA, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** A drifted bill is not a state the
product can be driven into — `invoice_lines` carries `trg_invoice_line_immutable` (hard rule 4) and
the engine writes lines that foot — so reaching one end to end means corrupting a bill in a
throwaway database. **There is no bill to corrupt: all 35 databases on this box hold ZERO
invoices**, counted on 2026-09-01. That is `DEF-2901`, and it is re-measured here rather than
inherited. ⚠ **PostgreSQL itself is UP** — the note this lane was handed said it was down; it
answers on 5432 and every one of those 35 databases was read.

**THE ALTERNATIVES, AND WHY EACH WAS DECLINED.**

* **Wait for a real issued invoice.** `DEF-2901` is open and is somebody's provisioning project. A
  money branch stays undrawn until it lands, and it has already been undrawn since the day task 9
  shipped.
* **Assert the branch only in `jsdom`.** `BillChargesTab.test.tsx` already does, over
  `renderToStaticMarkup`, and it is worth having. It cannot answer *"is it visibly a warning"* —
  jsdom performs no layout and computes no style — and the PO's rule of 2026-08-30 is explicit:
  *"All UI screen should be confirm using real broswer testing and not just based on test cases"*.
* **Weaken the end-to-end check so it passes on any verdict.** That is `DEF-182` — a check whose
  output cannot distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check, because it is trusted.

**THE PRECEDENT IT FOLLOWS.** `10-scripts/render-checks/def2826-bill-layout.mjs` made the same trade
for the same reason and stated it in the same place. This is the second file to do it, so it is
recorded here as a pattern rather than left as one file's improvisation.

**THE CONDITION THAT MAKES IT HONEST, and it is not optional.** The header must name what the file
does NOT prove. `cr053-charges-tie-out.mjs` names four: nothing about the server (the API is a
stub); nothing about whether a real bill can drift; not the join between the real endpoint and the
shape the stub serves; and not the rest of the Charges tab. Each is named with the file that DOES
own it — `cr053-bill-surface.mjs` and `test_cr053_charges_tab_backend.py`. **A stub check that does
not say what it is standing in for reads as end-to-end evidence, and that is the failure this
paragraph exists to prevent.**

**WHAT WAS PROVED, with its figures.** 44 assertions on the shipped `vite build` bundle, over five
bills — a control that foots (`238.60 + 19.68 = 258.28`), the drifted one (`260.00`, delta `1.72`),
a bill with no service-bearing line, `DEF-2429`'s misfiled minimum-bill note, and a server that
omits the block. The load-bearing assertion is arithmetic: **the difference between the two figures
a person reads must equal the server's own stated delta**, and the per-service cells on the drifted
bill must be byte-identical to the control's — the evidence `BR-BIL-032` exists to surface, still on
the page. Proved RED first (law 7) by making the tie-out unconditional: **9 failures, exactly the
drift half, every other assertion still green.**

## 2026-09-01 · 📐 THE R3 RELEASE CONDITION, EXECUTED — AND IT CANNOT BE MET, BECAUSE R3's COMPARISON WAS COMPARING A NUMBER WITH ITSELF (`DEF-2878` CLOSED). WHAT REPLACES IT IS THE REFUSAL, AND IT NEEDS NO POPULATION AT ALL

**NOTHING WAS SWITCHED AND NO BILL MOVED.** `resolution_switch.SERVED_BY_CHAIN_DEFAULT` is still the
empty string, `FORKED` is unchanged, `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` reads **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** and
`G61 frozen-figures` **PASS** (130 signed money figures unchanged, 2/2 self-sabotages behaved as
stated), both before and after. Version **2.110.4**.

### 1 · WHAT WAS ASKED, AND WHY THE ANSWER IS NOT THE ONE THE QUESTION EXPECTED

The PO's cutover ruling of 2026-08-31 holds R3 and states its own release condition: *"run the
comparison over more than one seeded utility, and over a period containing a demand meter. That is
the same instrument, pointed at a wider population — not new machinery."* This lane was sent to
gather exactly that.

**The instrument does not measure what its column says it measures.** `DEF-2878` (filed by the PO's
own question — *could R3 be released without the comparison?*) traces the size through four hops:

    gather._connection_size_for   -> metering.connection_size_for
    resolution_shadow.adapt       -> metering.connection_size_for   (the SAME seam)
    adapt puts that value on MeterFacts.connection_size
    resolution.resolve_served_size ends `return meter.connection_size`
    compare() then tested the first against the last

One value, four hops. **Every additional account adds one more agreement of X with X**, so the
release condition could not have been met by any population, of any size, ever.

### 2 · PROVED ON REAL ROWS, NOT READ OFF THE SOURCE — `--sabotage R3-seam`

Every other `--sabotage` in the harness breaks ONE side after `prepare_run` has returned. This one
breaks **the shared source, before the pass opens**: `metering.selectors.connection_size_for` patched
for the whole run to answer `'W-2'` wherever it would have answered `'W-58'` — a 2-inch ladder
pricing a 5/8-inch connection on every account, in BOTH implementations at once.

| run | R3 agree | R3 disagree | R3 cannot evaluate | `by_step` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| clean | 47 | 0 | 0 | `{}` |
| `--sabotage R3` (live side only) | 46 | **1** | 0 | `{R3: 1}` |
| `--sabotage R3-seam` (the shared source) | **47** | **0** | 0 | `{}` |

**Read the last row.** The wrong price ladder on all 47 accounts, and the table reports perfect
agreement. `WHAT THE RUN'S ACCOUNTS ACTUALLY CARRY` even printed `water · W-2 on 47 account(s)` — the
wrong ladder, named, beside 47 agreements. On this fixture every water size carries the same base, so
the AMOUNT did not move; that is a property of the seeded ladder and is stated rather than claimed
away. The finding is about the comparison, which cannot see a wrong size on a flat ladder or a
stepped one, because it is not looking at two answers.

### 3 · WHAT CHANGED, AND IT IS `DEF-2839`'s TREATMENT ONE STEP OVER

`compare()` **asserts** the size instead of comparing it. If the two ever differ, the adapter mapped a
different CONNECTION from the one the live path priced — the known way to reach that is a MASTER
account, where `gather` resolves each service against the covered unit that serves it (`BR-CUS-068`)
and the adapter asks the anchor — and then no figure on that account is about the same meter. The
account is reported `shadow_comparison_raised` under COULD NOT ASK AT ALL, carrying the invariant's
own sentence. `--sabotage R3` now produces exactly that, and its sentence was rewritten to say so:
**a mutation whose stated expectation no longer matches its behaviour is a check that cannot
distinguish pass from fail** (`DEF-182`).

`comparator_coverage()` drops R3 from the compared set, so the harness reports it as **cannot
evaluate** with the reason printed in the row. The harness's own bidirectional scan — a step claimed
and not emitted FAILS — was the RED proof: it bit before the set was changed, with its own sentence.

### 4 · WHAT REPLACES IT, AND IT IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN THE POPULATION WOULD HAVE BEEN

**R3's REFUSAL is not circular and is exhaustively enumerable.** `resolve_served_size` raises
`SizeNotServed` for a size absent from the SCHEDULE's own axis; the axis is the schedule's fact and
the size is the connection's, so neither side supplied the other. And the live path does NOT refuse
the same pair — `gather` refuses only when the schedule names size groups and NO size resolved
(`GATHER_SIZE_UNRESOLVED`, `DEF-484`); a size that resolved and is simply not one of the named groups
falls through to the every-size ladder and is billed.

`06-backend/tests/test_def2878_r3_refusal_is_independent.py` — **92 cases**, every ratified size class
of all eight banded services, read from `service_size_classes` rather than listed, so a class the PO
ratifies later is covered the day it lands. Five RED proofs, each turning exactly its own cases red:
break the identity · delete the refusal · make the live path refuse too · empty the register · let an
unruled service (battery) answer.

### 5 · THE SECOND FINDING, AND IT IS WHAT THE WIDER POPULATION WAS ACTUALLY GOOD FOR — `DEF-2875`

`DEF-2851` taught `adapt()` to ask the ratified register whether a service HAS a size axis before
demanding a size. **Three statements later it demanded a meter multiplier from the same service with
no such question**, and metering answers `None` for the same reason: sewer has no meter
(`BR-RAT-015`). So the 116 accounts `DEF-2851` unblocked stayed blocked and merely changed their
sentence — which read as a fresh finding rather than as the same one renamed.

The fix is an ORDERING in `resolution.billable_quantity`: **nothing to multiply is answered before the
factor is asked for.** The guard is untouched where it matters — a register difference with no factor
still refuses, and `Decimal("0")` is a meter that was read and showed nothing, which still needs one
(`if register_quantity is None`, never `if not register_quantity`; that spelling is one of the four
RED proofs). `adapt()` reads metering's own `absent_reason`, which already distinguishes `no_meter`
(no asset — this) from `service_not_metered` (declared unmetered — BR-RAT-090's count) from `no_read`
(a meter nobody read — still blocks, correctly).

### 6 · THE MEASUREMENT, WIDENED, WITH ITS POSTURE

    database        sbh_r3rel — a clone of the shared development database, migrated to HEAD
    connected as    smartbillhub  ·  rolsuper = false  ·  rolbypassrls = false
    deny-by-default 0 account rows visible with no `app.tenant_id`
    RLS             ENABLE + FORCE verified on accounts, units, meter_reads,
                    plan_versions, tariff_versions
    population      3 utilities — brazosbend (47), perf-utility-1 (58), perf-utility-2 (58)
    period          2026-07-01 → 2026-07-31, service date 2026-07-01, every cycle
    precondition    rate_size_rows 75 / 45 / 45 — the size axis present on all three
    switch          SERVED_BY_CHAIN_DEFAULT = '' — no rule prices any real bill

    163 accounts entered the shadow · 163 attempted · 0 not attempted (was 47 / 116)
    21 more were blocked by the RUN before it: 15 `unit_has_no_billable_account`,
    5 `account_held_by_disputed_read`, 1 `cycle_has_no_service_points`

| step | agree | disagree | could not evaluate | switch? | why |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| **R1** | 163 | 0 | 0 | yes | the plan VERSION, re-read by the chain (`DEF-2839`) |
| **R2** | 163 | 0 | 0 | yes | the schedule version in force |
| **R3** | **0** | **0** | **163** | with R4 | **`DEF-2878` — not compared; both sides were one seam call** |
| **R3b** | 163 | 0 | 0 | **NO** | the billable quantity — **and no demand meter is in this run** |
| **R4** | 163 | 0 | 0 | with R3 | the base amount, two narrowings over one table |
| **R5** | 163 | 0 | 0 | yes | the jurisdiction factor — most of them `1 == 1` |
| **R6** | 163 | 0 | 0 | **NO** | the discount set — can only find a code the chain DROPS |
| **R7** | 163 | 0 | 0 | yes | the tax rules — the strongest, and the only one ever observed catching a live fault |

The `switch?` column is **`DEF-2838`'s**, which landed at the tip while this lane was measuring, and
it answers a different question from the three beside it: **can this build serve the step from the
ruled path at all.** It is read from `resolution_switch.FORKED`/`JOINT` at runtime, not from the
agreements — a step reading **NO** has no seam, so naming it refuses however clean its agreement
looks. `BR-BIL-873` is why R3 and R4 read *with each other*: the chain produces ONE base charge from
the pair, so they switch in one commit or not at all.

`by_step` is `{}`. **The zero in R3's disagree column is the absence of a measurement, and the
harness now says so in the row rather than in a paragraph somewhere else.**

### 7 · IS R3 RELEASED? NOT BY THIS EVIDENCE, AND THE HONEST STATEMENT OF WHY

**No.** Two things are true at once and both have to be said:

1. **The comparison will never release it and has been retired.** There is no population, no number of
   utilities and no demand meter that would have made `47 agree` mean anything. The PO's release
   condition was written against a measurement that did not measure — **that is our fault and not a
   flaw in the ruling**, and it is recorded here rather than handed back as a question.
2. **The refusal is proved independent and enumerated, and that is real evidence** — but it is
   evidence that R3's rule BEHAVES as ruled, not evidence that switching it is safe on a live tenant.
   The two are different questions and the second one has a measurable answer nobody has taken:
   **on every tenant, does every (service · size) pair its accounts actually carry have a row on the
   schedule version pricing that service?** Where it does, R3 resolves; where it does not, R3 refuses
   the bill and the live path prices it today. On this database the pairs are `water · W-58` on 163
   accounts and `sewer · (no size)` on 116, and all of them resolve — but that is three utilities that
   share one seeded ladder, which is one fixture's answer and not a product one.

**WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY RELEASE R3, stated as work with an owner:** a run of the harness's
`WHAT THE RUN'S ACCOUNTS ACTUALLY CARRY` report over every tenant, showing zero pairs with no row —

⚠ **AND THAT SENTENCE NAMED THE WRONG TABLE WITHIN THE HOUR. THE PRODUCT OWNER READ THIS SECTION AND
RULED ON IT** (*"rate schedule will not provdie the size, charge code will provide"*, decision log,
2026-09-01, **THE CHARGE CODE STATES WHICH CONNECTION SIZES ARE PRICED**). This section said the
coverage check asks whether every `(service · size)` pair has a row **on the schedule version**; the
axis is the **`is_base` CHARGE CODE's**, with the schedule ladder surviving only as the fallback for a
service that has no such code. **So the check to run is the same check pointed at a different object**,
and it narrows rather than widens: a service WITH an `is_base` code takes that code's sizes and no
others. Corrected here rather than left for the next lane to discover, because this paragraph is the
one somebody acts on. The ruling is RECORDED AND NOT YET BUILT — `configured_sizes_for` still asks the
schedule — and `charge_code_amounts` is empty on every tenant of this database, so today's fallback
answers exactly as it did when the figures above were measured. **No figure in this section moves.**
⚠ **AND IT WAS BUILT THE SAME DAY — the two sentences above are kept as written and this one dates
them** (`BR-RAT-1010`, `CR-057`, `v2.112.0`): `configured_sizes_for` now asks `base_code_sizes_for`
first, and the coverage check named here was rebuilt to read its verdict off it. See the entry at the
foot of this log. No figure in that section moves either — `charge_code_amounts` is still empty on
every tenant of this database, so the fallback answers exactly as it did.
— and that is now the ONLY thing left, because R4's other blocker closed while this lane was
measuring: **`DEF-2830` is `fixed` at the tip** (`v2.110.3`, `6a166848` — a stored schedule `0.00`
reads as NOT STATED on both paths, the judgment taken as ours on 2026-08-31 and executed in code,
live path unchanged at `$8.00`). `BR-BIL-873` binds R3 and R4 into ONE commit and R4 is the step that
reads that figure, so with `DEF-2830` closed the pair is waiting on R3's per-tenant coverage check and
on nothing else. **Neither is a decision owed by the Product Owner**, and the harness's own `switch?`
column confirms the build can serve the pair: R3 and R4 both read *with each other*.

### 8 · AND THE OTHER HALF OF THE RELEASE CONDITION CANNOT BE PRODUCED AT ALL — `DEF-2874`

The ruling names a demand meter and (in its reasoning for R3) a master account. **Neither can enter a
bill run on this fixture, and the objects both exist**, which is why nothing noticed:

* **The demand meter.** `M-7210`, ×10, electric, on unit `U-00420` *Bldg 1* of *77 Gulf Fwy
  Industrial*, cycle `CY-005 Industrial bimonthly`. Its two reads are correct and committed —
  39.8 × 10 = **398 kW** and 41.2 × 10 = **412 kW**, `DEF-797`'s own pair — and both carry
  `vacant_unit`, because `seed_demo` deliberately creates no accounts (its own 2026-08-30 amendment
  says so). `prepare_run` on CY-005 returns `ready=0 blocked=1 unit_has_no_billable_account`.
* **The master account.** `AC-2026-00052` exists on all three utilities and its unit is in **none of
  the seven cycles**, so it is in no run anywhere. Across 163 accounts measured, not one was a master.

**This matters beyond the fixture, because the PO's hold on R3 named the master account as R3's one
non-circular case** — and no master account can reach a bill run at all. So even the case the ruling
identified as independent was unreachable. R3b's hold has the same shape and the same cause: *"no
demand meter is in this run"* is true, was true before this lane, and remains true, and a zero
register difference hides a multiplier error.

Two fixes, both in the sample-data path and neither in a measurement script: give `U-00420` an
occupying account (it is already on the `IND` plan, which `create_account` requires), and put the
master's unit in a cycle. ⚠ **Watch the signed count** — `seed_sample_records` documents *"one ACTIVE
account per seeded unit — 48, which is spec acceptance item 2's"*, so a 49th seat is a fixture-count
change and the tests pinning 48 move with it deliberately rather than being discovered red.

## 2026-09-01 · ⚖️ CR-056 W2b BUILT · A COMPANY IS MATCHED ON ITS TAX ID, AND THE KIND STOPS BEING A SILENT DEFAULT

**The two PO rulings of this morning are built.** This entry records what was built, and the ONE
judgment the rules did not make for us: **when a door states no kind, does it refuse or default?**

### WHAT WAS BUILT, in one table

| kind | strong when | asked for | never asked for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **person** | name **+** date of birth **+** (SSN **or** driving licence) | SSN · driving licence · phone · date of birth | a Tax ID |
| **company** | name **+** Tax ID | **Tax ID** · phone | a date of birth · an SSN · a driving licence |

`customers.tax_id` is a new app-layer-encrypted column with a keyed blind index beside it —
migration `customers 0038`, exactly the shape `0036` built for a person's SSN. `tenancy.ein` is NOT
reused and must never be: that is the UTILITY's own tax number on another module's table, and it is
the **counter-example** rather than the precedent, because it holds nine plaintext digits against a
closed ruling and says so in its own docstring.

**No unique index on the Tax ID.** The PO ruled the reversible half this morning — *a duplicate
identifier refuses to LINK and never refuses to SAVE* — so a clerk who mistypes a digit still opens
the account, the collision is visible, and the LINK is refused by name showing **no figure at all**.

### THE JUDGMENT WE MADE — REFUSE THE IDENTITY, NEVER THE ACCOUNT

The brief was that a silent default to `person` is wrong, because the kind decides which identifier
is even asked for. **It is wrong, and a blanket refusal would have been wrong too**, so the line is
drawn at the harm rather than at the field:

* **Identity presented with NO kind → REFUSED, by name.** This is the money hazard and the whole
  reason the kind matters: a government identifier filed under a party nobody has classified is
  stored in a column the matcher for the other kind never reads, and a guess of `person` would judge
  a business by a date of birth it does not have. The form asks *"Is this a person or company?"*
  before it accepts the number.
* **No identity presented → the account OPENS, and the kind falls back to `person`.** Two real paths
  do this and neither has a human to ask: the bulk import matching on a legacy reference, and the
  master-account door carrying a premises' free-text owner name, which may equally be a person or a
  limited company.

**WHY NOT REFUSE BOTH.** The PO's other ruling of the same day is the reason, and it is the same
shape: refusing to open an account over a missing dropdown is the one-way door they declined this
morning wearing a different coat. A spreadsheet that imported yesterday would stop importing today.

**WHAT WE FIXED INSTEAD OF THE DEFAULT — the SILENCE, which was the half that could be fixed.** The
`person` is now WRITTEN by the service, not inherited from the model's column default, and every
create records **`kind_defaulted: true|false`** in its `audit_log` row and returns it to the caller.
So *"opened as a person because nobody said"* and *"opened as a person because somebody chose"* stop
being the same fact. On the seeded utility nothing changes: the sample data already states a kind on
every customer it creates.

### THE COLLISION WITH `BR-CUS-089`, STATED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED

`BR-CUS-089` is signed and verbatim — **name AND date of birth AND one government identifier**, PO
2026-08-25 closing `OQ-364` — and a company has no date of birth. **It is NARROWED onto persons, not
reversed**, which is the direction this morning's entry already ruled; `BR-CUS-1022` carries the
company half and the rule's own row now carries the narrowing beneath it.

**The narrowing is DIRECTIONAL and a later lane must keep it so.** It removes a clause a company
cannot satisfy and adds nothing to a person's test. Unioning the two lists — letting a Tax ID count
as *one government ID* for a person — would turn a narrowing into a loosening of a signed money
rule. `tier_for` is two explicit booleans over named constants for that reason, and all four corners
are asserted.

**No signed figure moved and no ❄️ frozen B4/B5 number was touched.** The deposit `BR-CUS-089` gates
is still **$150.00** principal (**$153.50** with interest) and still moves only on `strong`; golden
verify is 33 PASS / 0 FAIL and `G61` PASS on 130 frozen figures, before and after.

### WHAT WE DID NOT DECIDE, and stubbed rather than chose

* **`OQ-1241` — does a company get an incorporation date**, the date-of-birth equivalent? A company
  is matched on two facts where a person needs three, and whether that is deliberate or merely what
  was available is a real question. A door supplying `incorporation_date` meets
  `raise NotImplementedError("OQ-1241")`; the value is neither stored nor silently dropped.
* **`OQ-1242` — is a sole trader a person or a company?** They trade as a business and are a natural
  person, and the two readings ask for different documents. `normalise_kind` RECOGNISES the spellings
  and raises rather than folding them into either kind. ⚠ `CR-033` §4 contains a lane's sentence
  *"a sole trader is a person on a commercial account"* — that paragraph is about
  `service_requests.applicant_kind`, a different column CR-033 itself insists is not the same fact,
  so it is context and not an answer. It is named here so the next reader does not mistake it for one.

### THE RED WE SAW FIRST (law 7)

The kind requirement was proved by running the existing W2 suite against it before anything was
adapted: **14 of 21 cases went red**, every one on
`VAL-001 customers.customer.kind_required_for_identity`, and every one a door that presented a
person's identity without stating whose it was. Those tests now state `kind: "person"` — which is
what they always meant — rather than the guard being softened.

### ONE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN PASSING — `DEF-2873`

Opening a second master account on one address is correctly refused (`BR-CUS-1011`), and the refusal
had **no sentence in any of the eleven catalogues**, so it arrived on screen empty: `params.detail`
is suppressed by the PO ruling of 2026-08-19, and a key that resolves to nothing renders as silence.
`G32` was already red on it at the branch tip and was found by running that gate over this lane's own
three new keys and reading the fourth line. Filed, then fixed here because the eleven files were
already open. It now names the account that is already there.

## 2026-09-01 · ⚖️ CR-056 · A CUSTOMER # NEEDS A NAME **AND ONE IDENTIFIER**. A name alone no longer creates one

**PO verbatim:** *"Customer ID - minimum name and one ID - minimum - please make this rule and apply"*.

**WHAT IT REPLACES.** Today the minimum is **a display name and nothing else** — `link_customer` allocates the
number inside the create, `kind` silently defaults to `person`, and the identifiers fill in afterwards into
empty columns. **From this ruling a name is not enough.**

| Kind | Minimum to create a Customer # |
|---|---|
| **Person** | a name **AND** one of: Social Security number · driving licence · **phone** |
| **Company** | a name **AND** its Tax ID |

**⚠ THE ONE DISTINCTION THAT MUST NOT BE COLLAPSED, and it will be by somebody within a week:**

> **What is enough to CREATE a Customer # is not what is enough to MATCH one.**
> A **phone alone CREATES** — the PO's own list names it. A **phone alone is a WEAK match and never carries a
> deposit** (`BR-CUS-089` and this morning's lane). Both are true at once, they are different questions, and
> a lane that "reconciles" them will either refuse to create a customer the PO said to create, or move
> `$150.00` on a phone number.

### THE CONSEQUENCE NOBODY WILL SEE COMING: THE BULK IMPORT CAN NO LONGER CREATE A CUSTOMER

**The import is the ONE door that has been creating Customer #s since the beginning**, and it carries a name
and a legacy reference and **no identity at all** — its own code says `customer_ref` is a reconciliation key
and nothing more. Under this rule it has nothing to create a customer with.

**THE ANSWER IS ALREADY RULED, THREE TIMES OVER, AND IS NOT PUT BACK TO THE PO (law 13).** *"Load the address,
create nobody, flag it"*; *"the account appears when the owner is identified"*; *"a name in a cell is not a
person."* **So: the ACCOUNT loads, NO Customer # is created, and the row is flagged for a human to identify.**
The import never invents a party — a fourth application of one principle, which is what makes it a rule
rather than four decisions.

⚠ **THAT IS A REAL COST AND IT IS STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED:** an import that used to produce a numbered
customer per row now produces accounts whose customer is blank until somebody identifies them. **It is the
same trade the PO has now taken four times** — fewer invented parties, more rows waiting for a human.

### WHAT IT GOVERNS, AND WHAT IT LEAVES ALONE

**It governs what is WRITTEN from now on, not what exists.** Customers already on file with a name and no
identifier stay lawful, exactly as the money rule's *"existing 18,6 columns stay lawful containers"* does.
**No migration invalidates a row, and no screen refuses to display one.** A lane proposing a backfill that
deletes or blocks them is reversing this sentence.

**AND `kind` STOPS DEFAULTING SILENTLY.** It already had to be explicit for identity (this morning's lane);
now it is load-bearing for CREATION too, because it decides which identifier satisfies the minimum. A door
that presents a name and an identifier but no kind cannot be resolved — a Social Security number does not
satisfy a company and a Tax ID does not satisfy a person.

### WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN

* **No door may satisfy the rule by inventing a value** — a placeholder phone, a zero Tax ID, the account
  number reused as an identifier. The refusal is the product; a filled column that means nothing is worse
  than an empty one, because the matcher will read it.
* **The refusal names the missing thing in plain words** at the door where the clerk is typing, never a rule
  id (B14 rule 32 clause 4), and never after the account is created.
* **An account may still be opened.** This rule is about the CUSTOMER #, not about service: a person standing
  at the counter who will not give an identifier still gets their water. What they do not get is a Customer #,
  and every consequence of not having one — no deposit carry-forward, no recognition on return — follows from
  that rather than from a refusal to serve them.
✅ THE MINIMUM-IDENTITY RULE IS BUILT — `BR-CUS-1023`, five doors, `v2.113.0`

This is the BUILD half. The RULING is recorded above under **A CUSTOMER # NEEDS A NAME AND ONE
IDENTIFIER**, and nothing in it was re-put to the PO (law 13).

### 1 · WHAT WE SAW GO RED FIRST (law 7)

The three doors were proved on a clean detached worktree at the branch tip, with none of this
lane's files present, before a line of the fix existed:

    a name and a kind at the counter   ->  minted C-00001
    an address owner's name            ->  minted a customer for "Ruiz, Marisol"
    an import row with a legacy ref    ->  minted C-00001

All three now open the account and mint nothing.

### 2 · WHAT EACH OF THE FIVE DOORS DOES WITH LESS THAN THE MINIMUM, AND WHY THAT IS FIVE ANSWERS
AND NOT ONE

**They differ because they carry different data, and one blanket behaviour would be wrong at
three of them.**

| door | what it carries | what it does now |
|---|---|---|
| **S18, the counter** | a clerk typing | asks person-or-company and the right ID for each, and **says so before the save** |
| **the master account** | an address's free-text owner name | opens the account, mints nothing, names the missing fact |
| **S19 move-in** | the same payload as S18 (`MOVE_IN_FIELDS ⊃ CREATE_FIELDS`) | the same as S18, through the same one writer |
| **the bulk import** | a name + a legacy reference, **no identity** | **the ACCOUNT loads, no number, the row is FLAGGED** |
| **the service-request link screen** | a customer a clerk already found | **unchanged — it never created one** |

⚠ **THE FIFTH DOOR IS NOT A DOOR, AND THAT IS WORTH WRITING DOWN RATHER THAN LEAVING FOR THE
NEXT LANE TO RE-DERIVE.** `service_request_service.link_customer` writes
`service_requests.matched_customer` — it points an application at a customer row that already
exists, chosen by a human, and it has no `Customer.objects.create` anywhere in its reach. The
minimum gates CREATION; there is nothing here to gate. It was checked rather than assumed.

### 3 · THE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE, WHERE THE RULING RAN OUT

**(a) A PHONE DOES NOT CREATE A COMPANY.** The PO's list for a business is *"if it is Company
then we ask for Tax ID"* — one item. A phone stays CAPTURABLE for a business (`BR-CUS-1022`
already allows it and the matcher indexes it) and does not satisfy the minimum. **The reason,
concretely:** a business's phone is answered by whoever is at the desk, so a customer number
minted on it names an office and not a party. `CREATE_IDENTIFIER_FIELDS` and
`KIND_IDENTIFIER_FIELDS` are therefore two tables that differ in exactly one cell, and the
difference is commented at both.

**(b) THE REFUSAL IS A SKIP AND NEVER AN EXCEPTION.** Every door links its customer inside its
own `transaction.atomic()`, so raising here would ROLL THE ACCOUNT BACK — which fuses the two
outcomes the PO separated in as many words. This is the single most likely thing for a later
lane to "tidy", so it is stated in the code at the point of the skip, in `link_customer`'s
docstring, and asserted by a test that checks **the account row exists** rather than that no
exception was raised (an exception assertion passes on a silent rollback).

**(c) THE OLD `display_name_required` REFUSAL IS FOLDED IN, NOT DELETED.** A customer reference
with no name used to raise and fail the whole import row. It is now one of the three things the
minimum can be missing, it keeps its own sentence — *"That customer reference is new here. Give
the customer a name."*, already translated in all eleven catalogues — and it skips the number
instead of failing the row. Same rule, one shape.

**(d) THE IMPORT'S FLAG IS THE ROW'S OWN `raw` JSON, AND NO MIGRATION WAS TAKEN.** The ruling
says the row is *"flagged for a human to identify"*, and a count that lives only in the commit
response is gone the moment the wizard closes. `account_import_rows.raw` is this table's own
JSON column and already holds `{"source": …, "resolved": …}`; the flag joins it as
`customer_not_identified`. The receipt also carries a per-row `unidentified` list in the same
shape as `allocations` and a count in `summary` — **a SUBSET of `created`, never an addend**, or
a clean cutover would read as a failed one.

**(e) THE DEMO FIXTURE'S PEOPLE KEEP THEIR CUSTOMER NUMBERS, AND NOTHING WAS INVENTED TO DO IT.**
Every seeded person would otherwise have lost their number, which would have emptied the
customers screen the W5 lane had just built. The identifier used is **`entry["phone"]` — the
value the fixture ALREADY holds and already writes onto that account's contact row**, a `555-`
number in the reserved-for-fiction range, exactly as `SAMPLE_COMPANY_TAX_ID` is `99-0001234` in
the IRS's. **A seeded person with no phone gets no customer number, deliberately:** inventing a
digit to keep the fixture tidy is the one thing the ruling forbids by name.

### 4 · WHAT WE FOUND AND FILED — `DEF-2818`, and it is why the frontend half existed at all

**The S18 wizard had never sent a `customer` block.** The server has accepted one since
`CR-056` W3 (2026-08-31) and no screen ever posted one, so every account opened at the counter
went on having a blank customer column — the exact state `CR-056` §4 was written to close.

**Its escape is the interesting part.** `G13` reads unwired PROPS on components; this is an
unwired REQUEST FIELD on a payload builder, which no gate looks at. And the screen's own test
made it invisible: it asserted `customer` was a REFUSED field, which was TRUE before W3 and was
never revisited — so the suite was green on the opposite of the truth. That assertion is now
the block's exact contents, per kind.

### 5 · WHAT DID NOT MOVE

No signed figure and no ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 number was touched. The deposit `BR-CUS-089` gates is
still **$150.00** principal (**$153.50** with interest) and still moves only on `strong`.
`10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` is **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** and `G61` PASS on **130** frozen
figures, before and after. `G35` PASS at `2.113.0` across all four literals.

### 6 · WHAT WE DID NOT DECIDE

Nothing new was stubbed and no open question was minted. `OQ-1241` (does a company get an
incorporation date) and `OQ-1242` (is a sole trader a person or a company) are the W2b lane's
and are untouched; both still raise `NotImplementedError` naming the question, and the creation
minimum inherits both refusals through the same `IdentityEvidence`.

### 7 · ⛔ AND ONE CLAUSE OF IT WAS SUPERSEDED **WITHIN THE HOUR** — WHAT THAT COSTS, AND WHY THE FIX IS NOT HERE

**PO 2026-09-01, verbatim:** *"Without identifier we cannot create Customer ID or master account ot regular
account"* — recorded by another lane in the entry **AND NO IDENTIFIER MEANS NO ACCOUNT EITHER**, a few
minutes after this build was pushed.

**IT REVERSES ONE CLAUSE OF THE RULING THIS LANE BUILT, AND ONLY ONE:** the morning ruling's *"An account may
still be opened"*. The identifier now gates **the account**, not the Customer # alone. Name alone creates
nothing at all — no customer, no regular account, no master account.

**WHAT SURVIVES, WHICH IS ALMOST ALL OF IT.** The minimum and its per-kind tables, the create-versus-match
distinction, the kind requirement, the refusal wording at the door, the no-invented-value prohibition, the
audit row, the S18 capture and the toast — all unchanged, and `creation_minimum` is EXACTLY the predicate the
new ruling needs. **Only the consequence moved: from *no number* to *no row*.**

**WHAT THIS LANE DID ABOUT IT, AND WHY IT IS A STAMP AND NOT A BUILD.** The stale clause is stamped where a
reader will meet it — `BR-CUS-1023`'s row, `link_customer`'s docstring, the comment at the create,
`creation_minimum`'s docstring, and this file's test header, which says in terms that TC-6/8/9's *"the account
exists afterwards"* assertions encode a reversed clause and will FLIP when the refusal is built. **The refusal
itself is deliberately NOT built here**, for two written reasons:

* **It belongs to the lane that recorded it**, which said in its own commit *"Nothing is built on any of these
  in this commit — the record goes in first."* Two lanes building one ruling is how a repo gets two answers to
  one question.
* **Its second half is migration-blocking and that lane already flagged it for the PO** — with the rule at the
  account, **the bulk import can create no accounts at all**, and its record says that *"must be put to the PO
  before it ships, not discovered by a utility mid-migration."* Shipping it from here would ship exactly the
  thing that record set aside.

**AND THE HONEST NOTE ABOUT PROCESS, BECAUSE IT IS THE USEFUL PART.** Step 0 of the build process asks *was
this ruled since the doc I am about to build from was written?* — and it is read at the START of a lane. This
ruling landed at the END of one. **Nothing in the repo catches that.** The cost was small here only because
the reversal was narrow and the predicate was reusable; a wider one would have been a day's work built on a
superseded sentence, with the PO the first to notice.
