### 13 · ⛔ CORRECTION, SAME DAY: SECTION 12 SAID THE FAILURES WERE UNATTRIBUTED. THEY ARE OURS, AND THE PROOF ARRIVED MINUTES LATER

**Section 12 above says *"NOT ONE OF THESE IS PROVED TO BE THIS CHANGE'S"*. That sentence is now
FALSE and is superseded here rather than edited, because the way it became false is the lesson.**

**THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON, and it is clean.** Two worktrees on the **same base commit**
(`70a49e30`), differing only by this change's patch:

| tree | `test_br_rat_094_plan_cannot_price.py` + `test_cr014_round3_cohorts.py` |
|---|---|
| base only (`wt-tip70`) | **13 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** |
| base + this change | **13 failed** |

Fourteen tests; every one that can fail, does. **These failures are this change's.**

**THE MECHANISM, confirmed by reading the fixtures rather than by guessing.**
`grep -c is_base` returns **0** for both `tests/test_us_met_helpers.py` (which provides the `brazos`
tenant) and `tests/journey_cohort_fixtures.py`. So those tenants have **no `is_base` charge code for
any service**, and with R4 served the charge code is the ONLY source of a base amount
(`BR-RAT-088`) with no fallback (`BR-BIL-872`) — so every account they bill is refused by name.
This suite's own `test_br_bil_870_...` had to call `_declare_a_base_charge_code()` explicitly for
exactly this reason; the other files never did, because until today they never had to.

⚠⚠ **AND THIS EXPOSES A REAL LIMIT IN THE `DEF-2923` FIX THAT §3 OVERSTATED. THE GATE FIRES AT
SCHEDULE ACTIVATION, SO IT ONLY PROTECTS TENANTS THAT HAVE NOT ACTIVATED YET.** A tenant whose
schedules were ALREADY ACTIVE before the switch, and which has no base charge code, is **not**
warned by the gate and still has every account of that service refused on its next bill run — which
is `DEF-2923`'s original harm, untouched, for exactly the population that cannot be re-gated. The
test estate is that population, which is why it went red. **`DEF-2923` is therefore only PARTLY
closed: the gate closes the door for new configuration and does nothing for configuration that is
already through it.**

**WHAT PROTECTS A REAL DEPLOYMENT IN THE MEANTIME, and it is not the gate:** the per-utility
preflight, which now counts services with no base charge code and refuses the switch by name —
`cr052_r1r7_shadow_measure.py --tenant <sub>`, proved able to print *"R3 + R4 must NOT be switched
on here"* under its `no-base-code` sabotage. On the three measured utilities that count is **0**, so
those deployments are safe; an unmeasured one is not, and must be run before the pair is enabled
there.

**WHAT IS STILL TRUE FROM §12, and it is the part that matters for money:** the engine-verified
golden suite is **identical with the pair on and with it off — 23 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed both
ways.** No signed billing figure moves. What breaks is fixtures that never declared a base charge
code, not arithmetic.

**WHAT THIS LANE DID NOT DO, said plainly.** It did not fix the fixtures. The cure is to declare a
base charge code in `test_us_met_helpers.py` and `journey_cohort_fixtures.py` (and any other tenant
builder that bills), which is a **shared-fixture change reaching dozens of files while three sibling
lanes are running in the same tree** — the exact shape law 11 exists to keep out of a busy branch,
and it needs a quiet tree and a full sweep to land safely.

**SO THE BRANCH IS CARRYING RED TESTS THAT ARE OURS.** The one-line rollback
(`SBH_BILLING_RESOLUTION_STEPS=` emptied) makes the branch green immediately and keeps every other
part of this work — the gate, the amended rules, the tests, the preflights — in place, with the
switch one environment variable away. **Whether to hold the switch on and fix the fixtures, or roll
it back until they are fixed, is a call that reverses a PO ruling either way and is therefore put up
rather than taken quietly** (law 13's *"a ruling that collides with a signed rule — the supersession
must be stated"*).

### 7 · A RED PROOF THAT DID NOT BITE, AND WHAT IT FOUND — law 7 earning its place twice in one wave

**THE FIRST MUTATION FOR `DEF-2951` PASSED, AND A PASSING RED PROOF IS THE WORST
POSSIBLE RESULT** — it certifies a test that cannot fail. Restoring the retired
hallway walk in `transfer_target_for` alone left **every case green**, because
the single-family fixture DECLARES its owner and `owner_target_for` answered
instead. The defect is BOTH halves together: the walk, and an owner target that
was hard-wired to refuse. **Mutating both reproduces it, and the measurement is
`4 failed, 4 passed`** — `tc4`, `tc5`, `tc6` and `tc7` red, and `tc1`, `tc2`,
`tc3` and `tc5b` still green, which is what makes it a MUTATION rather than a
rewrite: a building that HAS a common area is priced identically either way.

**AND THE FRONTEND HAD THE SAME SHAPE, FOUND THE SAME WAY.** Putting the port
back to its pre-change all-`null` mapping left **all 34 wizard cases green**,
because every one of them hands a `CloseImpact` object straight to the component
— they prove the PANELS and say nothing about whether the server's fields ever
arrive. That is hard-won law 2 hiding inside a green suite. **Two port-level
cases were added because proving the others red found the hole**, and the
mutation now fails on `expected null to deeply equal { occupied: 1, total: 3 }`.

**THE GENERAL LESSON, worth more than either defect:** a red proof that passes
is not a reassurance, it is a finding. Both times here the mutation was aimed at
the right line and the test was reading somewhere else.


## 2026-09-01 · 📐 CR-058 W3 + W4 — SIX JUDGMENTS THE RULINGS DID NOT MAKE, AND ONE LIMIT WORTH NAMING (AI lane, tasks 10–19)

The PO's rulings of this morning and this afternoon are quoted in full in the two entries above
(*"SEVEN CORRECTIONS…"* and *"THREE MORE RULINGS…"*). This entry records only what the rulings did
**not** decide and this lane therefore decided, with its reasoning — law 13: *"a judgment call
recorded in the decision log with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to
make one."*

### 1 · THE PREMISES IMPORT NEEDED A SIXTH COLUMN THE RULING DID NOT NAME

**The ruling names four identifiers:** *"DL, SSN, Phone or Tax ID"*, plus the person-or-company kind
that decides which of them counts. **Building it needed a sixth: the OWNER ACCOUNT TYPE.**

`customers.create_master_account` refuses a missing `account_type` by name, and it is right to: the
account type is the **consumer category the bill is priced and reported by**. There is no lawful
default — guessing `residential` for a builder's site or `commercial` for a family home is a money
decision taken by a shrug, and the premises row's own `premises_type` is a PROPERTY type, not a
consumer category. Deriving one from the other would be inventing a money-bearing default and
calling it a mapping.

**So the column is offered, it is optional, and a row that names an owner and an identifier and NO
account type creates nothing and is flagged** — `PRM.OWNER_ACCOUNT_TYPE_MISSING`, counted apart from
the missing-identifier rows because the work is different: this is a thirty-second choice from a
list, that is a trip to a filing cabinet.

**Worked:** a file with `Marisol Alvarez · person · 555-0140` and a blank account type loads the
address, creates **no** customer and **no** account, and the receipt reads *"No account type given —
needs a choice · 1"*. Fill the cell in, upload again with Insert & update, and she gets both.

### 2 · THE IMPORT STILL CREATES NO TYPED `premises_owners` PARTY, AND THE ACCOUNT HANGS OFF THE ADDRESS INSTEAD

`BR-MET-402` clause 5 — **the import never creates a PARTY** — is CONFIRMED and is not reversed by
this ruling. `premises_owners.category_id` is NOT NULL, `BR-MET-151` clause 3 forbids reading a
category off a name, and the premises template offers no category column.

**The ruling is still buildable because `BR-CUS-1010` moved the owner's account onto the ADDRESS**
(`CR-056` W1, 2026-09-01): `accounts.premises_id` exists and `accounts.unit_id` is nullable. So a row
whose owner name matches no typed party still gets the ADDRESS an account, and the typed party is
left for a person to settle on `PRM-04`. Two branches, and **both end at the same door** —
`customers.create_master_account` — so there is no second creation path anywhere.

**What it costs, stated:** for such an address `owner_master_account_for_premises` still answers
nothing and the owner-matching worklist still shows it. The response says `owner_linked: false` out
loud rather than being silent about it.

### 3 · A SELLER WHO IS NOT ON FILE — THE REFUSAL IS SETTLED, NOT REMOVED

`CR-058`'s own table lists *"it refuses an account with no customer"* as **to be settled in CR-058**,
and the shape of a sale argues for allowing it: what matters is who owns the account NEXT.

**Kept, for three reasons, and the first is the PO's own:**

1. *"Without identifier we cannot create Customer ID or master account ot regular account"* (PO,
   2026-09-01). **No account may exist with nobody identifiable behind it.** Handing a live ledger
   from nobody to somebody creates exactly the half-anonymous account that ruling closes.
2. **The fix is thirty seconds and a clerk can do it** — link the account to its customer on the
   account screen, then sell it. A refusal that names a recoverable fix costs a minute; a wrong
   reassignment is a live account whose history nobody can attribute.
3. Relaxing it means making `transfers.customer_id` nullable, which is **migration ordering** — a 🔒
   human-owned path — to buy a case that is already recoverable.

**What changed is the refusal's WORDS.** It now carries `fix: link_this_account_to_its_customer_first`
so the screen can say what to do rather than only what went wrong.

### 4 · A BUYER WHO PRESENTS NO IDENTIFIER IS REFUSED, AND A REASSIGNMENT IS NOT LITERALLY A CREATION

The PO's ruling gates **creation**: *"Without identifier we cannot create Customer ID or master
account ot regular account"*. **A reassignment creates no account**, so the letter of that rule does
not reach it.

**Its POINT does**, and that is what was built. The rule exists so that no account is owned by
somebody nobody can identify; handing a live account to an unidentified buyer produces exactly that
state by a different route. The safe direction is to refuse — a refusal is recoverable by asking for
a phone number, and a wrong reassignment is not.

**Refused twice, at step 2 and again at the commit**, because a service-layer caller — a management
command, another module, the next lane — does not have to pass through step 2. `BR-SHL-025`'s
defence-in-depth posture.

### 5 · THE SELLER'S LINK IS DELETED, AND `customer_accounts` IS NOT ONE OF HARD RULE 4's FOUR

A reassignment removes the seller's `customer_accounts` row so the account has exactly one customer.
**That is a link table, not an invoice, an invoice line, a payment or a journal entry** — hard rule 4
does not reach it, and every document the seller was ever sent still says exactly what it said.
Leaving both links would make *"who owns this account"* ambiguous on every read that asks.

⚠ **AND THE MIRROR IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN PROMISED.** The ruling's own record warns that a lane
could read *"the debt follows the property"* as licence to re-address the seller's documents.
`reassign_account` writes to `customer_accounts` and to `transfers` and to **nothing else**, and
`test_cr058_w4__nothing_issued_to_the_seller_is_rewritten` is what makes that a fact rather than a
sentence.

### 6 · `premises.owner_id` DOES NOT MOVE WHEN A PROPERTY IS SOLD

The account changed hands; the premises' TYPED owner record did not. It is metering's table and
customers may not write it (B1), and the owner record carries a **category** nobody stated at a sale.

**Said out loud rather than left silent** — `premises_owner_record_not_updated` rides the response —
because a clerk who is not told will believe the owner record moved with the account. The door that
does move it is `PRM-04`'s owner matching.

### ⚠ A LIMIT WORTH NAMING, BECAUSE THE NEXT LANE WILL MEET IT: A **PERSON** LANDLORD STILL GETS ONE NUMBER PER ADDRESS

`CR-058` task 5 says *"a landlord with three buildings must end with ONE Customer #"*. **For a
COMPANY that is now true and the premises import proves it**: `tier_for` makes a company a `strong`
match on name + Tax ID, so three buildings uploaded under `Whitfield Rentals LLC` end with **three
accounts and one Customer #**.

**For a PERSON it is not reachable from a premises file, and no lane may make it so by choosing.**
Two signed rules meet here and both are deliberate:

* `BR-CUS-1023` — a **phone alone CREATES** a Customer #. The PO named it.
* `BR-CUS-089` — a person is a `strong` match on **name + date of birth + one government ID** (PO
  2026-08-25, closing `OQ-364`). A phone or an SSN **without a date of birth is a WEAK match**, and a
  weak match opens its own number rather than linking.

So `Marisol Alvarez · person · SSN` across three addresses ends with **three Customer #s**, and that
is correct under the rules as signed. CLAUDE.md states the trap in as many words: *"a lane that
reconciles them either refuses a customer the PO said to create or moves **$150.00** on a telephone
number."*

**What would change it:** a date of birth on the premises template. **That is not in the PO's list**
(*"DL, SSN, Phone or Tax ID"*), so adding one would be this lane widening a ruling.
`test_cr058_w3__a_PERSON_landlord_gets_one_number_per_address_and_that_is_the_signed_rules` pins the
behaviour with this reasoning attached, so the next lane finds it instead of discovering it.

### 7 · A SIGNED RULE WAS NARROWED, AND THE SUPERSESSION IS STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**`BR-MET-085` (PO ruling 2026-08-21, `CR-023`) says: *"A PREMISES IMPORT LOADS PREMISES AND NOTHING
ELSE."*** PO verbatim at the time: *"We we load premises - it will be only premises."* **The ruling of
2026-09-01 makes that headline no longer literally true**, and the change process (step 2) says the
reversal must be quoted with its chain rather than left for a reader to notice.

**WHAT CHANGED:** a premises import now creates an owner's **master account and Customer #** where
the row carries a name and one identifier.

**WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, AND IT IS THIS RULE'S OWN STATED REASON — WHICH IS WHY THE NARROWING IS SAFE
RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION.** `BR-MET-085` explains itself in one sentence: *"an auto-created unit is
a row the operator never supplied and never reviewed, and a unit is what an ACCOUNT attaches to — so
181 unreviewed billing anchors would have entered the tenant in one commit, inside a run whose
receipt reported only premises."* Every clause of that still holds:

* **No unit is auto-created**, then or now. `BR-CUS-1010` hangs the owner's account off the ADDRESS,
  and this lane creates no `units` row on any path.
* **Nothing is created that the operator did not supply.** The account exists only where they typed
  the identity it is built from; a name-only row creates nothing, which is the PO's own *"otherwise
  dont create anything"*.
* **The receipt reports what happened.** `BR-MET-085`'s sharpest phrase is *"inside a run whose
  receipt reported only premises"*, and the two new figures exist precisely so that cannot recur.

`BR-MET-402` clause 5 — *the import never creates a PARTY* — is untouched for the same reason, and is
what keeps the typed `premises_owners` record a human act (judgment 2 above).

**Stamped at its own sentence, dated, in `04-docs/05-modules/04-metering/02-business-rules.md`, and
in the Trace header of `apps/metering/import_runs.py` where a lane reading the code will meet it.**

### WHAT THIS LANE DID NOT DO, NAMED

* **The bulk ACCOUNTS import** carries no identity at all, so under ruling 4 it can no longer create
  accounts. Migration-blocking, flagged to the PO by another lane, and **deliberately not touched
  here** — widening scope onto somebody else's migration path is how two lanes end up disagreeing
  about one door.
* **New Connect** (`CR-056` task 23) is the OTHER caller of the master-account door and is a
  different lane's. Between the two of us both entry points reach `create_master_account`; neither
  wrote a second one.

### 14 · ✅ THE PREFLIGHT NOW NAMES THE SERVICES IT LOOKED AT, SO IT CAN NO LONGER PRINT `MET` OVER ONE IT NEVER SAW (`DEF-2965` prevention 2, BUILT)

`DEF-2965`'s second prevention is done, because it is the one that would have caught the electric
case and it is a change to our own report rather than to anybody's product code.

**WHAT IT DID WRONG.** Everything the report knows is derived from accounts that reached the
adapter, so a service the utility BILLS whose accounts never got that far contributed no pair, no
verdict and no complaint — it was simply absent from the answer, and the verdict said **MET**.

**WHAT IT SAYS NOW.** Each utility's line carries `services examined:` and, where the two differ,
`ENABLED BUT NOT EXAMINED:`, read from `tenancy.selectors.enabled_service_codes()` — *"the services
this tenant actually SELLS"*, enabled only. A bare `MET` is no longer reachable while a billed
service is missing from the examined set; it becomes **`MET for what was measured · SILENT on
electric`**, with a paragraph naming the cost:

    brazosbend   1 pair(s) · 0 unpriced · 0 undecided · 0 service(s) with no base charge code
                 ->  MET for what was measured · SILENT on electric
      services examined: water  ·  ENABLED BUT NOT EXAMINED: electric
      'electric' is enabled on this utility and NO account of it reached this pass, so R3 and R4
      are UNTESTED for it here. If it is banded, a meter with no recorded connection size is
      refused by name and that bill stops (BR-RAT-120).

**PROVED BOTH WAYS, and the RED half is the point.** Rendered against a synthetic result with no
database: with `enabled={electric, water}` and `measured={water}` all three new strings appear; with
`enabled == measured` **none of them appears and the verdict reads a bare `MET`**. A warning that
fires on every run is worth no more than one that never fires — this one was shown to do both.

⚠ **WHAT IT STILL CANNOT DO.** It reports that a service was not examined; it does NOT price it. To
clear `electric` on a utility, that utility needs electric accounts on a cycle in the pass — the
report now says so in its own words instead of leaving the reader to notice the absence.

### 15 · ⛔ AND ON THE REAL DATABASE IT IMMEDIATELY CAUGHT ONE: `brazosbend` SELLS ELECTRIC AND NOTHING HAS EVER MEASURED IT

Section 14 proved the new clause against a synthetic result. Run against `sbh_r3rel` — the same
clone every figure in this entry comes from — it fires on the **first utility**, and the case it
names is the one this whole day has been circling:

    brazosbend      1 pair(s) · 0 unpriced · 0 undecided · 0 service(s) with no base charge code
                    ->  MET for what was measured · SILENT on electric
      services examined: water  ·  ENABLED BUT NOT EXAMINED: electric
    perf-utility-1  2 pair(s) · … ->  MET
      services examined: sewer, water
    perf-utility-2  2 pair(s) · … ->  MET
      services examined: sewer, water

**READ THE THREE LINES TOGETHER, because that is what makes this evidence rather than noise.** The
two perf utilities still read a **bare `MET`** — the clause is silent where everything a utility
sells was examined — and `brazosbend` does not, because it **sells electric and not one electric
account has ever entered this measurement.** A warning that fired on all three would have proved
only that it fires.

⚠ **SO EVERY EARLIER `MET` IN THIS ENTRY WAS OVERSTATED FOR `brazosbend`, AND THE FIGURES ARE NOT
WRONG — THEIR SCOPE WAS.** `163 accounts · 163 unchanged · 0 moved · 0 refused` is true, and it is a
statement about **water, sewer and trash**. It never included an electric account, so it never could
have said anything about electric, and the report said `MET` anyway. That is `DEF-2878`'s shape for
the third time in one day and the third time the same lesson was learned by a different route: **a
measurement whose population cannot contain the failing case will report success.**

⚠ **AND THE TEST ESTATE ALREADY SHOWED US WHAT THE UNMEASURED CASE DOES.** `DEF-2965` records eight
failures whose message is *"service 'electric' has no connection size … R3 cannot be resolved and a
size may not be guessed"* — electric accounts, refused by R3 by name, bills stopped. That is not a
prediction about `brazosbend`; it is the same rule doing the same thing to the same service on the
first accounts that ever reached it.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY.** It does not say `brazosbend`'s electric would refuse — nobody has priced
that question, which is exactly the complaint. It says the question has never been asked, and that
the answer must be obtained before this deployment is trusted with the pair on.

**WHAT TO DO WITH IT, in order:** put electric accounts on a cycle in the pass and re-run the
preflight; if they refuse, the sizes are loaded before the chain is switched on (`BR-RAT-120`'s
sequencing clause, which was honoured for water and never tested for electric). Until then the
honest state of this deployment is **water/sewer/trash measured, electric unknown**, and the
one-line rollback (`SBH_BILLING_RESOLUTION_STEPS=` emptied) is what covers the unknown.

### 16 · ⚖️ CORRECTION AGAIN, AND THIS ONE IS IN OUR FAVOUR: THE ~77 FAILURES ARE A **MIX**, NOT ALL OURS — AND THE RULE THAT SEPARATES THEM IS ONE LINE

Section 13 said the sweep failures "are ours". **On the evidence then available that was right; on the
evidence now it is an OVERSTATEMENT, and overstating our own blame is a reporting fault like any
other** — it sends the next lane to fix three tests that were already broken.

**THE SECOND CONTROLLED COMPARISON, same tree, switch on against switch off:**

| file | pair ON | pair OFF | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `test_br_ast_049_external_ref.py` (3 cases) | 3 failed | **3 failed** | **PRE-EXISTING — not ours** |
| `test_br_cus_068_master_bill.py` (2 cases) | 2 failed | **0 failed** | **OURS** |
| totals | 5 failed / 20 passed | 3 failed / 22 passed | 2 of 5 ours |

**THE RULE THIS GIVES THE NEXT LANE, and it has now held on every file tested:**

> **A test that BILLS an account fails because of us. A test that does not, does not.**

`test_br_cus_068_master_bill` prices a master bill — R3 and R4 run, and a fixture with no base
charge code or no recorded connection size is refused. `test_br_ast_049_external_ref` is the asset
IDENTIFIER law and prices nothing, so the switch cannot reach it; it was already red and stays red
with the pair off.

**THE TALLY OF WHAT IS ACTUALLY ATTRIBUTED, so nobody inherits a guess:**

* **15 failures PROVED OURS** — 13 in `test_br_rat_094_plan_cannot_price.py` +
  `test_cr014_round3_cohorts.py` (§13), 2 in `test_br_cus_068_master_bill.py` (here).
* **3 failures PROVED NOT OURS** — `test_br_ast_049_external_ref.py`, red with the pair off.
* **~59 STILL UNATTRIBUTED.** Triage them with the billing rule above first; it costs a `grep` and
  has been right every time so far. Then confirm with the same two commands (§12).

⚠ **WHY THIS KEEPS HAPPENING, AND IT IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY.** Three times today a conclusion was
drawn from the evidence that had arrived rather than the evidence that was still running, and three
times the next result moved it. The failures were "unattributed", then "ours", now "a mix". **Each
statement was honest when written and wrong within the hour**, which is the cost of reporting a
long-running measurement from its first slice — and the reason every one of those sections is
SUPERSEDED IN PLACE rather than edited, so a reader sees the correction as well as the conclusion.

## 2026-09-01 · 📐 THE BULK ACCOUNTS IMPORT GETS IDENTITY COLUMNS TOO — THE NO-IDENTIFIER RULE IS NOT RELAXED FOR IT (PO ruling)

**THE QUESTION, AND IT WAS RAISED BECAUSE THE RULE BLOCKED A MIGRATION.** The PO's ruling of 2026-09-01 —
*"Without identifier we cannot create Customer ID or master account ot regular account"* — reaches the bulk
accounts import as a wall: that import carries a name and a legacy reference and **no identity at all**, so
under the rule it creates nothing, and a utility migrating in would discover that mid-load. Two lanes
flagged it independently as migration-blocking rather than build it around the rule.

**Put to the PO with three options and their costs. They chose: GIVE IT IDENTITY COLUMNS TOO.**

**THE RULE: the accounts spreadsheet gains the same identity columns the premises spreadsheet gained**
— person or company, Social Security number, driving licence, phone, Tax ID — and behaves the same way:

    name + at least one identifier  ->  the account loads AND its customer is matched-or-created
    name alone                      ->  NOTHING loads for that row, and the receipt counts it
    (the row is not silently dropped: it is reported as needing an identifier)

⚠ **THE TWO OPTIONS DECLINED, RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-PROPOSES THEM AS IMPROVEMENTS.**
**(a) Load the accounts with the customer blank and flag them** — declined: it would make the rule stop
applying at the one door that creates the most accounts, so the rule would govern the counter and not the
migration, which is where the volume is. **(b) Load them as drafts that cannot be activated** — declined,
though it was the most defensible of the three: it completes the migration and bills nobody unidentified,
but it leaves a utility with a queue of thousands to work before going live, and it invents a new meaning
for the draft status that no rule gives it.

**WHY THE CHOSEN ANSWER IS THE CONSISTENT ONE.** The premises import took exactly this shape hours earlier
(`CR-058` W3, shipped `v2.118.0` with six optional columns). A utility now fixes its FILE once, before
loading, rather than working a flagged queue row by row afterwards — and the two importers ask for the same
facts in the same way, which is the difference between one rule and two doors that each learned it
separately.

⚠ **`customer_ref` IS NOT AN IDENTIFIER AND MUST NOT BE PRESSED INTO SERVICE AS ONE.** The import's own
code says it is a reconciliation key to the utility's old system and nothing more. It identifies a ROW in
somebody else's database, not a PERSON. Satisfying the rule with it would be exactly the invented value the
ruling forbids, and the matcher would then read it as identity evidence.

⚠ **AND THE ALREADY-KNOWN DEFECT ON THIS SAME FILE IS THE ONE TO FIX WHILE IT IS OPEN.** The published
template offers a **"Customer #"** column whose help text promises it is used, and **nothing reads it** —
a utility migrating with its own customer numbers loses every one and cannot reconcile against their old
system. The identity work opens this exact file; fixing the discarded column at the same time costs almost
nothing and leaving it costs a migration.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE.** Accounts and customers already on file without an identifier stay lawful —
the rule governs what is WRITTEN from now on. No migration invalidates a row and no screen refuses to
display one.

---

## 2026-09-01 · 🔧 BUILDING THE ACCOUNTS-IMPORT IDENTITY RULE — FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULING DID NOT MAKE FOR US (`CR-058` W7, `v2.121.0`)

The ruling of this morning — *THE BULK ACCOUNTS IMPORT GETS IDENTITY COLUMNS TOO* — settles WHAT the
accounts spreadsheet does. Four things it does not settle came up while building it, and each is
written here with the option that was not taken, so none returns as an improvement.

**1 · THE PHONE IDENTIFIER IS THE TEMPLATE'S EXISTING `phone` COLUMN, NOT A NEW `customer_phone`.**
The premises file gained `owner_phone` because it had no phone column at all. The accounts file has
carried the customer's phone since `BR-CUS-046` — it is the number that becomes the account's
contact — and the PO named a phone as enough to create a person's Customer #. **The option not
taken was copying the premises column list literally**, which would have put two phone columns on
one row: a utility fills one, the matcher reads the other, and the bill contact and the identity
evidence disagree with nothing objecting. The cost of the choice is stated rather than discovered:
a file that carries a phone and does **not** say whether the customer is a person or a company now
loads nothing, because which identifier counts depends on the kind (`BR-CUS-1022`) and an unstated
kind cannot be judged at all. That is the same answer the premises import gives, and the same
answer `identity_match.creation_minimum` has given since it was signed.

**2 · STAGE 3 REJECTS THE ROW; IT DOES NOT FLAG IT.** On the premises import the identity rules are
warnings, and correctly: the ADDRESS still loads and only the owner's account is skipped. Here
nothing loads at all, so a warning would let a rehearsal print *"will create 1,213"* over rows the
commit refuses — `DEF-965`'s exact complaint and `DEF-544`'s law (*"a load that resolves against a
different world than stage 3 showed is a defect in its own right"*). **The option not taken was
counting the rows in the loader**, where every other accounts figure is counted; the count is taken
at validate instead, from the same verdict function stage 4 would have asked, and rides `run.counts`
into the receipt. **The receipt is the whole mitigation and it is a number, not a statistic:**
without it a migration that identified half its customers looks identical to one that identified all
of them, and the utility finds out at its first bill run.

**3 · A ROW WHOSE ACCOUNT IS ALREADY ON FILE IS EXEMPT.** An *Insert & update* re-run creates no
account and no customer — it updates a handful of fields — so requiring identity on it would refuse
the corrected re-run of a file that loaded lawfully yesterday. The rule is about MINTING, exactly as
`BR-CUS-1023` is.

**4 · THE `Customer #` COLUMN IS A KEY AND NOT AN IDENTIFIER.** Fixing the discarded column
(`DEF-2593`) puts a second exact-match path into `link_customer`, and it would have been easy to let
it satisfy the new rule — a row *has* a customer number, therefore it is identified. It is the same
mistake as `customer_ref` in different clothes: both name a ROW, neither evidences a PERSON. A
quoted number LINKS or CREATES-WITH-THAT-NUMBER and contributes **nothing** to the creation minimum.
**The worked figure:** a file of 1,213 rows quoting `C-00001`…`C-01213` with names and no
identifiers loads **0 accounts**, and the receipt says *1,213 rows need an identifier*.

## 2026-09-01 · 📐 THE OLD THREE-STEP ACCOUNTS IMPORT IS CLOSED, NOT LEFT MOUNTED (`CR-058` W7, `DEF-2592`)

**THE FACT.** There are two accounts-import doors. The live one is the five-stage runner every other
upload uses. The other is the pre-`CR-030` three-step importer: **its screen was deleted** when the
runner replaced it (`DEF-611` — the shipped wizard had three of A1's five steps), and **its
endpoints were left mounted and working** — `POST /accounts/imports`, `GET .../template`,
`GET .../{id}`, `POST .../{id}/commit`. Nothing in the frontend calls any of them; a script or an
integration pointed at them still works today.

**WHY IT COULD NOT BE LEFT.** That door hands out rules the PO has since reversed. It **allocates an
account number when the cell is blank** — reversed on 2026-08-27, *"we use utility provdied account
number here - we dont create our own number … if row dont have account number reject it"* — and it
**requires no customer name**. After `BR-CUS-1041` it would additionally have been the one door in
the product that creates accounts with no identity at all: the rule would govern the counter and the
live migration and not the door a script uses.

**THE DECISION, AND IT IS OURS TO TAKE (law 13).** Nothing here collides with a signed rule, moves a
frozen figure, or needs a fact only the PO holds. **The two WRITE endpoints refuse**, by name, with a
sentence naming the live import; `GET /accounts/imports/{id}` keeps working, because reading a batch
somebody staged last week is not a write and the rows are real. **The template endpoint refuses
too** — it published a column set no live door reads, which is the same fault as the discarded
`Customer #` cell one file along.

**THE OPTIONS NOT TAKEN.** **(a) Bring it under the same rules** — build the identity columns, the
verdict and the receipt a second time, on a door with no screen. That is precisely *"two importers
that each learned the same rule separately"*, and the second copy drifts first. **(b) Delete the
routes** — a 404 tells an integration nothing about what happened or where to go, and the staging
tables hold real rows. **(c) Leave it** — which is the only option that ships a door quietly
disagreeing with the ruling being implemented.

**WHAT A CALLER SEES:** `409` with `customers.import.retired_use_import_runs` — *"This upload has
moved. Import accounts from Accounts › Imports, which checks every row before it writes any of
them."* No id, no route name in the sentence.

**THE ROLLBACK, stated before shipping:** the refusal is two guard clauses at the top of two service
functions. Removing them restores the old door exactly, and no data is migrated, dropped or
rewritten by this change.

## 2026-09-01 · ⛔ A REPORT WHOSE POPULATION CANNOT CONTAIN THE FAILING CASE — THE THIRD OCCURRENCE, NAMED ONCE AND PROPERLY (`DEF-2965`, `CR-057`, `v2.120.1`)

**This has now happened three times in this repo in eight days, and each time the report said
so in the language of success.** It deserves a name and a test, not a third fix.

| | what was measured | why the failing case could not appear | what it printed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEF-2878` | R3's live size against the chain's | both sides are ONE call to `metering.connection_size_for` — four hops, one value | `47 agree` |
| `DEF-2923` | base charge codes on three utilities | all three carry seeded base codes (`DEF-455`), so a tenant with none was not in the population | `163 unchanged · 0 refused` |
| `DEF-2965` | R3's release condition on three utilities | none of them bills electric, so no electric account was examined; and the population is the accounts already in a CYCLE, whose meters already have sizes | `MET` |

**THE SHAPE, stated so the next lane recognises it before writing the check rather than after:
a measurement is a statement about a POPULATION, and a report that names only its FINDINGS lets
the reader supply a population of their own — invariably the whole product.** Every one of these
three reports was accurate. None of them was wrong about anything it said. They were read as
clearances because nothing on the page distinguished *nothing is wrong* from *nothing was
asked*.

### 1 · THE TWO BLIND SPOTS ARE DIFFERENT, AND FIXING THE FIRST DOES NOT TOUCH THE SECOND

The obvious reading of `DEF-2965` is *"electric was not in the population"*, and the obvious cure
is to name the services examined beside the services the tenant bills. A sibling lane shipped
exactly that on 2026-09-01 (`51a73a79`, `94162fe0`) and it is right: `brazosbend` sells electric
and nothing has ever measured it.

⚠ **IT IS HALF THE FINDING, AND THE HALF IT MISSES IS THE ONE THAT READS `MET` WHILE BILLS
STOP.** Measured on `sbh_r3rel` the same day:

* **electric** — 37 connections, 37 with no recorded size, **21 billable accounts**. Caught by
  the services-examined clause, because electric was never examined.
* **water** — examined on all three utilities, reported `PRICED`, and `perf-utility-1` and
  `perf-utility-2` each hold **21 billable water accounts** whose connection has no recorded
  size. **Not caught by anything**, because water *was* examined.

**So the blindness was never "a service was missing from the population". It is that the
population is drawn from the PREPARED RUN, and a prepared run holds only accounts already in a
cycle — whose meters already have sizes, because that is why they are billable today.** The
failing case sits one join outside it and no amount of care about which services were seen will
reach it.

### 2 · THE DECISION: THE CHECK ASKS THE ESTATE, AND IT ASKS THE ENGINE'S OWN SEAM

`cr052_r1r7_shadow_measure.py` gains `what_the_estate_holds`. For every service point the utility
holds that a live service agreement attaches to an account, it asks
`metering.selectors.connection_size_for` — **the function R3 itself resolves** — whether a size
comes back, and reports per service: connections, connections with no recorded size, and **how
many BILLABLE ACCOUNTS that touches**. It needs no prepared run, which is also why it can be
asked of a utility that has no cycle yet.

**Two judgments inside that, both stated rather than left to be inferred.**

**(a) It asks the SEAM and does not re-join the tables in SQL.** A second implementation of
*"does this connection have a size"* would be free to disagree with R3: the seam answers `None`
for two meters that disagree about the size, and counts only meters CURRENTLY assigned, and a
hand-written join missing either rule would report a clean estate over accounts R3 refuses.
**This is a CENSUS, not a comparison, so asking one source twice is not `DEF-2878`'s tautology** —
there is no second answer here for the first to agree with. What it buys is that the report
cannot come to a different verdict from the step it is clearing, which is `what_the_run_carries`'
own reason for calling `resolve_served_size` rather than reimplementing it.

**(b) It reports ACCOUNTS, not only meters.** Eight accounts is the number a person acts on;
twenty meters is trivia until it is joined to who stops being billed.

### 3 · THE VERDICT IS `NOT MET` OVER FOUR PRECONDITIONS, AND THE FOURTH IS NEW

1. a `(service · size)` pair nothing prices → R3 refuses;
2. a service with no `is_base` charge code → R4 refuses — **and asked of every service the
   tenant's own `tenant_services` rows say it BILLS**, not only of the ones the run carried. With
   `--sabotage no-base-code` on `sbh_r3rel`, `brazosbend` now names ELECTRIC as well as water;
3. a service the tenant bills that this run never examined → `MET for what was measured · SILENT
   on <service>`, the sibling lane's wording, kept;
4. **a billable account on the ESTATE whose connection has no recorded size, on a BANDED
   service** → a hard `NOT MET`. It outranks (3)'s softer wording deliberately: (3) is a silence
   about something unmeasured, (4) is a measured refusal.

**On the three utilities on `sbh_r3rel` that is 84 billable accounts, and all three now read
NOT MET where all three read MET this morning.**

⚠ **THE BANDED GATE IS LOAD-BEARING AND IT IS THE ONLY THING KEEPING THIS HONEST.** Sewer is
ruled to have no size class — it is a share of the water usage charge and reads no register — so
every sewer connection has no recorded size and **none of them stops a bill**. Reporting `61 with
NO recorded size` beside sewer is a true number that reads as an alarm, and a reader who acts on
it goes looking for a size the product will never hold. Sewer prints a dash. Thermal steam and
battery are `OQ-560`/`OQ-561` and are not banded either — *"nobody has said"* stays a third answer.

### 4 · WHY THIS IS CONFIGURATION AND NOT A DEFECT IN THE ENGINE, SAID ON THE PAGE

A banded service's meter with no recorded size MUST refuse. The PO ruled on 2026-08-28 that we
charge on the size the account actually has, and **you cannot charge on a size you do not have**.
`BR-BIL-872` gives a switched rule no fallback, so R3 stops the bill rather than pricing a size
the utility never priced. **The only question this check settles is whether they find out on the
preflight or on billing day**, and the report says so in those words rather than reading as an
accusation against the engine.

### 5 · PROVED RED, TWO WAYS, BECAUSE A VERDICT THAT CANNOT SAY THE FAILING WORD IS NOT A VERDICT

* `--sabotage estate-unsized` patches the seam to answer `None` for every water connection: every
  utility billing water must read `NOT MET` and name the accounts. It does.
* `--sabotage service-coverage` drops every water meter from the facts the shadow reads, so the
  run stops examining a service the tenant still bills. The report names it and does not read
  `MET`.
* **Five source mutations, each biting exactly one new test case** — the estate condition removed
  from the verdict, the banded gate removed, the estate counts assigned instead of maximised, the
  banded list hardcoded instead of read from `BR-TEN-171`, and `services_measured` assigned
  instead of accumulated. A sixth mutation was tried first and **passed**, which is how the
  merge-level cases came to exist at all: the render-level case could not see a gate that lives
  in `_merge`, and a check whose output cannot distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check
  (`DEF-182`).

⚠ **THE LIVE MEASUREMENT IS THE STRONGER HALF AND THE SABOTAGE CANNOT REPLACE IT.** The real case
— an unsized meter on an account the run never contained — is a property of which accounts are in
a cycle and cannot be manufactured by patching a function. It was measured instead, on real rows:
water read `MET` on two utilities holding 21 unsized water accounts each.

### 6 · THE FIXTURE HALF: FOUR MECHANISMS, AND EACH WAS HIDDEN BEHIND THE ONE IN FRONT OF IT

`DEF-2965` named two. There were four, and **the failure COUNT does not move as they are cured —
only the sentence does**, because a chain of narrowings prints one refusal per account:

| | mechanism | the sentence it prints |
|---|---|---|
| A | no `is_base` charge code | `rating.schedules.no_base_charge_code` |
| B | no connection size on the meter | *"service 'electric' has no connection size"* |
| C | a published plan with no start date (`DEF-2816`) | *"has no plan version in force"* |
| D | a schedule version stating no size axis (`DEF-2816`) | *"connection size 'E-1P-100' has no row"* |

**THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON, and it is worth more than the four fixes: on a chain of narrowings,
one fixture gap hides the next, and *"the failures did not go down"* is indistinguishable from
*"the fix did not work"*. Re-read the traceback after every fix; do not re-read the count.**

Two more findings came out of the same re-reading: `DEF-2817` (a test asserting the pre-switch
semantics without saying so — it needed the same treatment twice in one wave, which is what makes
it a pattern) and `DEF-2815` (**`resolution_switch.apply` runs the chain END TO END before
substituting anything, so a refusal at R1, R2, R3b, R5 or R6 stops a real bill even though none
of those steps is switched on** — every document describes a narrow change and the code runs a
wide one).

**EVERY FIGURE ADDED TO A FIXTURE IS ONE THE REPO ALREADY SIGNED**, which is the rule that keeps
this from being a defect wearing a fixture's clothes: base amounts from `core.sample_fixture`
(`[W] §1` — water `$8.00`, electric `$12.00`), connection sizes from `BR-TEN-171`'s ratified bands
through the assets seam, plan start dates by rating migration `0024`'s own rule, size axes from
`apps/rating/sample_data.sample_size_rows`. **And no gate was weakened: every test whose SUBJECT
is an absence now ASKS for that absence** — `declare_base=False`, `size_class=None`,
`make_plan(dated=False)` — so the refusals stay reachable and are reached deliberately.

### 7 · WHAT DID NOT MOVE

`06-backend/tests/golden/` — the engine-verified billing contract — is **23 passed, 1 xfailed, 0
failed, IDENTICAL with the pair on and with it off**, run both ways because running it once could
not have said so. `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` **33 PASS / 0 FAIL**. `g61_frozen_figures.py`
**PASS at 130 frozen figures**. `G26` back to its baseline of **56** — it was FAILING at the tip on
one empty `fixed_commit` cell (`DEF-2922`), which is filled with the commit its own prevention
field already names, and that single-line edit to another lane's row was declared out loud in the
commit message and in the cell itself.

**THE ROLLBACK, stated before shipping:** every change here is test-fixture code, one measurement
script and register rows. Reverting the commit restores the previous fixtures exactly; no
migration, no column and no shipped behaviour is touched. The switch's own rollback is unchanged
and still one line — `SBH_BILLING_RESOLUTION_STEPS=` emptied.
## 2026-09-01 · 📐 MATCH FIRST MEANS A NAME AND ONE GOVERNMENT ID REUSE A CUSTOMER NUMBER — THE JUDGMENT `CR-058` RULING 0 LEFT TO US (`CR-058` W1 · `BR-CUS-1024` · `DEF-2587`)

**Nothing here was put back to the PO (law 13).** `CR-058` ruling 0 is quoted and signed; what it
does not say is what the word *matching* means, and the rules already in the repo give two
different answers. This entry records which one this lane chose, the figure it was chosen on, and
the signed rule it deliberately did not touch.

### WHAT WAS MEASURED FIRST, BECAUSE THE RULING WAS WRITTEN AGAINST A DIFFERENT PICTURE

`CR-058`'s own decision log says the master door *"creates a brand-new Customer # from a free-text
owner name every single time"*. That half had already closed hours earlier: `BR-CUS-1023` landed
the same morning, so a free-text owner name with no kind and no identifier now creates **nothing**
and says which fact is missing. Confirmed by running the door three times: three buildings, **zero**
customer numbers, each answering *we need to know whether this is a person or a business*.

**The half that was still open is worse, and it is the case the ruling is actually about.** Give
the same landlord a name, the kind, and a real Social Security number — an identifier, which is
what ruling 0 asks for — at three buildings, and the product writes:

    C-00001   Okonkwo, Adaeze   person   SSN ****3333
    C-00002   Okonkwo, Adaeze   person   SSN ****3333
    C-00003   Okonkwo, Adaeze   person   SSN ****3333

Three customer numbers over one Social Security number. Filed as `DEF-2587`. The matcher had
surfaced the earlier row each time and reported `matched on name and Social Security number` —
it FOUND the landlord and created a duplicate anyway.

### WHY IT DOES THAT, AND IT IS NOT A BUG IN THE MATCHER

The matcher is correct. `BR-CUS-089` is signed and verbatim — a returning customer is recognised
only on **name + date of birth + one government id** — and a date of birth was not given, so the
verdict is `weak`, which is exactly right. **The mistake is that every door used that verdict to
answer a second question it was never written for: *should a new row be created?*** One test was
doing two jobs.

### THE JUDGMENT, AND THE COLLISION IS STATED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED

There are now **three** questions and they need three tests:

| the question | the test | what it decides |
|---|---|---|
| may a number be MINTED? | `BR-CUS-1023` — name + one identifier, a phone included | whether a row exists |
| is a number ALREADY ON FILE? | **`BR-CUS-1024`, new** — name + one GOVERNMENT identifier (a person's SSN or driving licence, a company's Tax ID) | how many rows exist |
| may MONEY follow it? | `BR-CUS-089` / `BR-CUS-1022` — the `strong` tier, **unchanged** | whether a deposit moves |

**The signed money rule is not widened.** A reused number records **no tier and no confirmer**, so
`discounts.carry_forward_offer` still refuses and **$0.00** moves. The **$153.50** of `WE-7`/`GT-23`
— $150.00 principal plus $3.50 interest — still needs the full signed test, date of birth included.
This lane changed how many customer rows exist and nothing whatsoever about what they may do.

**Why reuse is the conservative answer and refusing is not.** Refusing writes three rows holding
one Social Security number, which is the database stating as fact that three different people share
it. Refusing is only the safe direction when the evidence is ambiguous, and an exact agreement on a
government identifier plus an exact, case-folded agreement on the name is not ambiguous.

### THE THREE THINGS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, EACH WITH ITS REASON

* **A PHONE MAY NOT REUSE A NUMBER**, although it may create one. Two adults share a household
  line and the repo already says three times over that a phone is nobody's government identifier.
  Creating a spare row costs a merge; handing a stranger an existing customer's file does not.
* **A NAME ALONE MAY NOT**, and never could — `A. Kulkarni` and `Ajinkya Kulkarni` are two
  landlords, which is the paragraph `CR-056` §4 already wrote.
* **AMBIGUITY REFUSES AND STILL SAVES.** Where two customers both agree, nothing is reused: the
  door mints its own number and hands back both candidates for a human. The PO ruled the same day
  that *a duplicate identifier refuses to LINK and never refuses to SAVE*, and choosing one of two
  would be a coin toss over somebody's file.

### THE OTHER JUDGMENT: ONE FUNCTION, AND THE OUTCOME IS NAMED RATHER THAN INFERRED

`CR-058` task 3 asks for one function every door calls. The logic already existed inside
`services.link_customer` and the doors each re-assembled the answer around it, so the function
added is `resolve_customer_for_account(...)` and it **delegates rather than duplicating** —
`link_customer` stays the only writer of `customer_accounts`.

**It returns the outcome as a WORD, and that is the part that was missing.** The server knew
whether it had linked or created and never said so: `created` existed only inside an audit blob,
so no screen could tell a clerk which of the three things had happened. The answer is now
`linked` · `created` · `none`, and both wizards read it.

### WHAT WAS NOT DECIDED HERE — AND THEN WAS, WITHIN THE HOUR

This entry originally closed by saying that **whether a master account is still created when the
owner has a name and no identifier** was `CR-058` task 2's open question, that this lane would not
touch it, and that *"the account opens, as it does today, and only the customer number is withheld."*

⚠ **THE PO ANSWERED IT WHILE THIS LANE WAS BUILDING, AND THE ANSWER IS BROADER THAN THE QUESTION.**
PO verbatim: *"Without identifier we cannot create Customer ID or master account ot regular
account"*. The paragraph above is therefore **WITHDRAWN**, and the ruling is recorded in its own
entry of the same day (*"THREE MORE RULINGS"*, section 4), which quotes in full the clause of
`BR-CUS-1023` it supersedes.

**WHAT CHANGED IN THIS LANE'S WORK BECAUSE OF IT.** The resolver was designed with three outcomes
and an account that opened regardless. It now has three outcomes **and a door that refuses**:

    name + at least one identifier  ->  match, else create; the account opens
    name alone                      ->  nothing is created, and the ACCOUNT DOES NOT OPEN
    no name                         ->  unchanged; nothing was ever created

**The reuse judgment recorded above is untouched by the reversal** — it is about how many customer
rows exist when an identifier IS present, and the new ruling is about what happens when one is
absent. The two compose: match first, create where no match exists, refuse where there is nothing
to match on.

### THE JUDGMENT THE REVERSAL FORCED, AND IT IS ABOUT BLAST RADIUS RATHER THAN ABOUT THE RULE

The ruling names *"master account ot regular account"*. Taken at its widest, every path that
creates an account is gated — and four of them are not counter doors: the bulk import, the tenant
sample seed, New Connect and the premises-owner door. **This lane wired the rule at the doors a
clerk presses and reported the rest rather than breaking them**, which is the shape `CR-047`'s four
keywords already use on the same function: the exemption is a named argument at a traceable call
site instead of a hole in the rule.

* **Wired and refusing:** `POST /accounts`, `POST /accounts/{id}/move-in`, `POST /accounts/master`.
  New Connect and the premises-owner door reach the master door through the seam, so both inherit
  the refusal, and both now pass the customer block through instead of a contact alone — which is
  ruling 2 of the same day, *"we have to create it if not matching customer ID not available"*,
  said of New Connect.
* **NOT wired, in writing, with the reason at the call site:** the bulk import. It carries a name
  and a legacy reference and no identity, so the rule read literally refuses every account row of
  every migration file. **That is migration-blocking and is already flagged for the PO**; a lane
  shipping it quietly would take a utility's cutover down. Its call site passes the exemption
  explicitly and names this paragraph.

**A DEFAULT THAT FAILS OPEN WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WRONG WAY ROUND HERE.** The gate defaults to ON at
`create_master_account` — the door the PO's question was actually about — so a caller that cannot
identify its party has to say so in writing. The two counter doors pass it on explicitly for the
same reason: a ruling that reaches every document and not the code is build-step 0's own worked
example of a documentation failure.

## 2026-09-01 · ⚠ A NEAR-MISS IN THE LAW-12 SYNC ITSELF: THE HELPER THAT BRINGS A TREE TO THE TIP WILL REVERT THE LANE'S OWN UNCOMMITTED WORK (`CR-058` W7 lane)

**WHAT HAPPENED, IN ONE SENTENCE.** After a `push_paths.sh` push this lane ran its own
"bring the working tree to the tip" helper — the one CLAUDE.md law 11 asks for after a
`commit-tree` push, because that push updates **no file on disk** — and the helper wrote the tip's
bytes over **every path that differed from the tip**. Two test files this lane had rewritten and
not yet pushed differed for exactly that reason. **They were silently reverted, and `git status`
was clean afterwards.**

**NOTHING WAS LOST**, because the rewrite had been done from a heredoc that could be re-run and the
second edit was a six-line patch. That is luck, not a check.

**WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW.** Law 11 and law 12 both prescribe *"write the tip's bytes over every path
that differs"* — and both are describing the recovery from a **rewind**, where every difference IS
staleness. **After an ordinary push the same sentence is wrong**: the differences are (a) staleness
from siblings' commits AND (b) **the lane's own in-flight edits**, and the two need opposite
treatment. The helper cannot tell them apart, because the thing that distinguishes them is *"who
typed this"*.

**THE RULE, and it is one line of code:** **a sync helper takes an exclusion list, and the lane's
own live paths are on it.** `git diff --name-only HEAD` names them exactly — it is what a lane has
touched since its last commit — so the exclusion is derivable rather than remembered.

⚠ **AND THE SYMPTOM IS THE ONE LAW 11 ALREADY WARNS ABOUT.** A clean `git status` after the sync is
not evidence of anything: the index was just told to match the tree it wrote. What found this was
looking for a marker string in a file the lane had just written and getting `0`.

## 2026-09-01 · 📐 THE SPREADSHEET CARRIES THE WHOLE SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER (PO ruling) — AND THE TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT FOLLOW ARE OURS, DECIDED HERE

**PO verbatim:** *"in spreadsheet we will porvide entire SSN number if required"*.

**What was put up:** that an uploaded spreadsheet keeps Social Security numbers **in plain text while it waits
to be committed**, and the checking screen **shows them back**, while the closed rule that only the last four
digits are ever displayed applies to the customer's record and nowhere else. Three things are tangled in that
sentence and the PO has answered the first.

### 1 · THE FILE — RULED, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE THREE THAT NEEDED A PERSON

**A migration file may carry the whole number.** It has to: a blind index cannot be built from four digits, so
an import that received only the last four could create a customer but could never match one, which is the
whole purpose of collecting it. **CONFIRMED**, and nothing in the two consequences below narrows it.

### 2 · THE SCREEN — SHOWS THE LAST FOUR. **A build judgment, not a question put back (law 13).**

The PO ruled on the FILE. The screen is a different object and the rules already in this repo answer it: the
encryption ruling is closed, `ssn_last4` is what every other surface serves, and **B14 rule 31/32's posture is
that a screen shows what a clerk needs and not what the system happens to hold.**

**What the operator needs from the checking step is *did the right row match*, not *what did I type*** — and
they are holding the file that says what they typed. Last four answers the first question completely. So the
staging grid serves `••••1234`, identically to every other surface in the product, and the operator who needs
the full value opens their own spreadsheet.

⚠ **AND THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS NOT WEAK.** A row REFUSED for a malformed identifier
is harder to diagnose from four digits. It is accepted, for two reasons: the fix happens in the file, not on
the screen; and the refusal names the cell (`"'Alvarez, Rosa' has a name and no way to identify them"`), which
is what an operator acts on. **If that turns out to be wrong in practice it is a defect to file, not a licence
to widen the display.**

### 3 · THE STAGING TABLE — ENCRYPTED, LIKE EVERY OTHER COPY. **Also ours, and this is the one that matters.**

A parked upload is not a transient: it sits in OUR database until somebody commits or discards it, which can
be days. **The encryption ruling is closed and says nothing about a row being temporary** — `tenancy.ein`
holding nine plaintext digits against that same closed ruling is already recorded as this repo's
counter-example, not its precedent.

So a staged identifier is stored the way a committed one is: **app-layer encrypted with its blind index
beside it**, which is the mechanism migrations `customers 0036` and `0038` already built. Nothing new is
designed; an existing kernel gains a second caller.

⚠ **THIS IS NOT MERELY TIDINESS AND THE COST OF LEAVING IT IS WORTH NAMING.** A migration file is the single
densest collection of government identifiers this product will ever hold — every customer a utility has, at
once. *"It is only staging"* is exactly the reasoning that leaves the largest such collection as the one
unencrypted copy.

### WHAT THIS COSTS AND WHO PAYS IT

**Both import doors, because both copied the same shape** — the premises upload built it earlier today and
the accounts upload deliberately followed it rather than half-fixing it, which was the right call and is why
one decision now fixes both. It is not a refusal, a migration blocker or a change to any receipt: what an
operator may **send** is unchanged, and only what the product **shows back** and **keeps** moves.

**Nothing already staged is invalidated.** This governs what is written from now on, like every other rule in
this family. A parked upload from before it stays readable and committable.

## 2026-09-01 · 📐 THE DEMO SEED GOES THROUGH THE NO-IDENTIFIER RULE INSTEAD OF AROUND IT — THE SAME ANSWER THE IDENTITY LANE ALREADY GAVE, APPLIED A SECOND TIME (`CR-058` W1 follow-up · `BR-CUS-1024`)

**Nothing here was put to the PO, and that is the point of the entry.** The question had already been
answered in this repo, hours earlier, by another lane. This records that one rule was applied twice
rather than two lanes each deciding for themselves (law 13).

### WHAT WAS LEFT OPEN, AND WHY IT WAS NOT A PO QUESTION

When `BR-CUS-1024` landed — *"Without identifier we cannot create Customer ID or master account ot
regular account"* — the tenant sample seed was **exempted at its call site**, with the reason written
there: its 48 entries stated no customer KIND, so the rule refused every one of them, and a demo
tenant with no accounts has no bills, no payments, no payment plan and no refund. The cost was
reported rather than shipped.

⚠ **THAT WAS THE RIGHT CALL IN THE MOMENT AND THE WRONG PLACE TO LEAVE IT, BECAUSE THE ANSWER
ALREADY EXISTED.** The identity lane had ruled the same day, in the decision log entry *THE DEMO
FIXTURE'S PEOPLE KEEP THEIR CUSTOMER NUMBERS, AND NOTHING WAS INVENTED TO DO IT*:

> *"The identifier used is `entry["phone"]` — the value the fixture ALREADY holds and already writes
> onto that account's contact row, a `555-` number in the reserved-for-fiction range, exactly as
> `SAMPLE_COMPANY_TAX_ID` is `99-0001234` in the IRS's. A seeded person with no phone gets no
> customer number, deliberately: inventing a digit to keep the fixture tidy is the one thing the
> ruling forbids by name."*

**The kind was never missing either — it was being derived two functions away**, in the seed's own
`_link_customer`: `company` where the entry's account type is `commercial`, `person` otherwise. So
every fact the rule asks for was already in the fixture and already being read. **Nothing was
invented then and nothing is invented now.**

### WHAT CHANGED

`_customer_block(entry)` builds the block once, from the fixture, and the account **payload** carries
it — so the seed's 48 accounts go through `create_account` and meet `BR-CUS-1024` like every other
door. `require_identity=False` is gone. The separate post-hoc `link_customer` call is retired: it ran
**after** the account existed, in its own savepoint, **swallowing its own failures**, so a seeded
account could end up with no customer and nothing said so — which is precisely the state this ruling
says may not exist.

**MEASURED, AND NOTHING MOVED.** All 48 entries carry a `555-` phone, 46 person and 2 company, so no
account is refused and no seeded figure changes: **961 rows, June 48 bills, July 47, the next cycle
44 bills for $3,762.22, the books balancing at $35,466.09 on both sides, 221 live readings.** The
identity is additive.

### THE TWO REASONS THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN A TIDIER FIXTURE

* **It is the only end-to-end proof the rule survives 48 accounts at once.** An exemption at one line
  left the path this repo exercises most as the one path the rule never ran on.
* **A demo where every account has a customer is the demo the PO looks at.** They rebuild the
  database at will and judge the product from what comes out of it.

### ⚠ AND PUTTING THE SEED THROUGH THE RULE IMMEDIATELY FOUND A HOLE IN THE RULE

`refuse_account_without_identity` carved out a door that hands over a legacy reference, on the
reasoning that such a caller *"is pointing at a row that ALREADY EXISTS"*. **Its comment said *a
reference that resolves*; its code only checked that a reference was SENT.** So any string in
`external_ref` — including one the tenant has never seen — walked an account past the rule. That is
hard-won law 1 exactly: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee.

**Every seeded row carries a `customer_key`, so all 48 would have taken that exit** and the claim
that the seed proves the rule end to end would have been hollow. The carve-out now checks that the
reference resolves. A reference that resolves to nothing is not an identification; it is a value
nobody has checked.

### WHAT IS STILL NOT DECIDED, AND IS NOT THIS LANE'S

The plain-text Social Security number shown on the staging screen of an uploaded spreadsheet. Another
lane raised the identical thing on the premises upload, it needs its own decision about what an
operator may be shown of their own file, and it is going to the PO separately. **Named here so the
next reader does not read this entry as having covered it.**
