## 2026-09-02 · "No bill generated" for Electric + Water + Sewer — the engine bills, and the build is not the difference

**What was reported.** The Product Owner, verbatim: *"We tried to create tenant
with Electric, Water and Sewer - no bill generated ; that means our Billing
engine is not working"*.

**What was measured, and it answers the question the version was supposed to
answer.** A tenant with exactly those three services was provisioned through the
real signup service on PostgreSQL 16, twice:

| build | premises | accounts | issued invoices | seeding blocks failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the branch tip | 70 | 70 | **95** | 0 of 17 |
| **2.125.5** (`ad1a9369`, the build reported) | 70 | 70 | **95** | 0 of 17 |

**So the billing engine is not broken, and it was not broken on their build
either.** That is the finding, and it is worth stating plainly because the
obvious hypothesis — that they were running something older than the six
bills-stopping fixes closed that day — is **wrong**. Every one of those fixes is
in 2.125.5, and the CHANGELOG names each in plain English at the version it
landed: refuse collection at **2.124.2** (`DEF-2414`), electricity/gas/storm
water at **2.125.1** (`DEF-2397`), the four services with no demo estate at
**2.125.3** (`DEF-2396`), and solar/broadband/battery at **2.125.4**
(`DEF-3156`). A person on 2.125.5 has all four.

**What they would actually have seen, and it is a real defect (`DEF-3224`).**
The sample estate puts ONE metered register on a unit, and `water` is first in
`core.sample_fixture.METERED_ESTATE_SERVICES`. So a utility that ticks Electric,
Water and Sewer gets a **water** estate: water and sewer bill, and **electric is
refused as a second register — no service point, no meter, no read, and no line
on any invoice, not even its `$12.00` monthly base.** Across 48 units that is
**`$576.00` a month that is simply not on the bills**, on a tenant where 95
invoices issue and every seeding block reports success.

**The backbone rule itself is deliberate and was NOT changed here.** Its own
refusal text gives the reason — seeding a second metered service would double
the ready-to-run billing month the demo exists to let somebody press — and the
frozen `GT-17` figures are water figures. Widening it is a fixture design change
with money behind it and belongs to the Product Owner, not to a lane.

**What IS ours, and it is the whole cost of this round trip: the product knew
and did not say.** `apps/metering/sample_data.py` composes a correct, readable
sentence naming electric and why it was dropped — and writes it to
`logger.info`, a server log a clerk cannot open. The comment beside it says *"a
utility that cannot see gas in its demo will ask why"*, which is CLAUDE.md law 1
exactly: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. The Sample data
panel on S8 already renders a server sentence for any block that carries one —
including a SEEDED block — so **no screen work is needed**; what blocks it is
that `apps/tenancy/sample_data.py` hardcodes `detail: None` on every successful
block. Handed to the lane that owns those files rather than edited from here.

**And why no check caught any of it.** Three, and each was green:
`test_service_billing_coverage.py` measured **thirteen** signup shapes and the
most ordinary combination a small utility ticks was not one of them
(`DEF-3223`); the seeding block **succeeded**, so the panel was entirely green;
and the scoreboard counts **invoices per tenant**, so a tenant that bills water
correctly and drops electric entirely scores as a pass. **A count of invoices
cannot see a missing service on those invoices** — which is why `Expected` now
carries `bills_for` and `sold_but_absent`, and why the failure table prints the
services that reached a bill for every row.

**And the production transport was measured too, because until it was, nobody
could say it billed (`DEF-3222`).** Every bill figure in this repo had been taken
with `JOBS_EAGER=True`, which runs the sample plant INLINE; production runs
`JOBS_EAGER=False`, where the plant is a message, a broker and a separate worker
process that must re-enter the tenant itself against a `jobs` table carrying RLS
FORCE. The two existing proofs (`verify_celery_transport.py`,
`verify_billing_queue_split.py`) show a worker CONSUMES the queue and **neither
counts an invoice** — and `BR-TEN-063` makes a partly-seeded plant a soft
success, so a run in which every billing block collapsed still ends `succeeded`.

`10-scripts/verify_plant_bills_through_celery.py` is that measurement and it was
RUN: three processes on one box — PostgreSQL 16.13, a real `redis-server`, and a
real `celery -A config.celery worker -Q celery,billing` — provisioning the same
electric + water + sewer tenant with `JOBS_EAGER=False`.

| | inline (`JOBS_EAGER=True`) | through a real Celery worker |
|---|---|---|
| premises | 70 | 70 |
| accounts | 70 | 70 |
| **issued invoices** | **95** | **95** |
| services on bills | sewer, water | sewer, water |
| sold but absent | electric | electric |
| blocks failed | 0 of 17 | 0 of 17 |

**Identical on every figure.** So the transport is not the difference either, and
`DEF-3224`'s missing electric reproduces through the worker — it is a fixture
fact, not a transport one. ⚠ **That is one run of one shape on one build, and it
is a measurement rather than a guarantee** (law 1): it says nothing about a
worker that is DOWN or a queue with no consumer, which stay `DEF-320`'s territory.

## 2026-09-02 · 💵 A UTILITY THAT SELLS ELECTRIC AND WATER NOW GETS BOTH ON ITS BILLS (`CR-062` group C + H1)

**Plainly, and this is the whole result.** A utility that ticked Electric, Water
and Sewer at sign-up used to receive water and sewer and **no electric line on
any bill at all** — not the usage, not even the $12.00 monthly base. Across 48
homes that is **$576.00 a month that was simply not on the documents**, on a
tenant where 95 bills issued and every one of the 17 seeding steps reported
success. The demo now plants a meter, three months of readings and a bill line
for **every** metered service the utility sells, so the same tenant gets electric
and water side by side.

**The Product Owner ruled it, in these words:** *"this is not correct - you
cannot drop electricty or gas - can you tell me what corrections you will ahve to
do"*. That was said after being shown the finding read out of the code, and the
corrections were put back in plain English before any of this was built.

**What was actually wrong.** The demo estate was written to hold ONE meter per
home. When a utility sold two things that need a meter, the first one won and the
second was refused with a sentence that said, honestly, that a second register
would double the size of the demo. That was a reasonable design call about demo
size and it is now overruled: a utility that sells electric and sees no electric
anywhere has a broken product, not a slow demo.

**WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHY THAT IS ACCEPTED.** A water-only utility is unchanged —
48 meters, 192 readings. One selling electric and water gets 96 meters and 384
readings; electric, water and gas gets 144 and 576. Nothing renumbers: the water
serials stay `W-5000 … W-5047` exactly as every existing tenant already carries
them, and the new ones arrive as `E-` and `G-`.

**FOUR JUDGMENTS MADE HERE RATHER THAN PUT BACK TO THE PO (law 13), each
reversible and each named so it can be reversed.**

**1 · The awkward cases stay on the FIRST metered service only.** The demo
deliberately contains three meters nobody could read, one disputed reading and
one meter swapped mid-history — they exist so the estimation screen, the dispute
flag and the meter-change history have something real to show. They are NOT
repeated per service. Worked: on an electric + water utility there are **49 water
meters** (48 plus the swapped one) and **48 electric**, one unreadable set and one
dispute, not two of each. Three copies of the same story makes the demo harder to
read, not richer. *To reverse: repeat them per service.*

**2 · Storm water stops getting a meter.** The Product Owner ruled on the same
day that storm water is billed on the size of the property rather than on a dial
(*"Storm water - it is capacity based not unmetered"*), and the price list was
corrected that morning — but the demo was still planting a storm-water meter and
three months of readings for it, so the demo tenant contradicted its own price
list. The meter, its `SD-` serial and its reading scale are withdrawn. This
closes `DEF-3231`. *No money moves: the storm-water usage line was $0.00 on both
paths, because nothing has priced it yet.*

**3 · The field that says which service the estate is metered in was RENAMED so
that every caller breaks loudly.** Twenty-four places in three modules read it. A
compatibility shim that quietly kept seeding one service would be exactly the
"built is not wired" failure that hid this for weeks — the code would go on
working and the second service would go on being absent — so the rename is the
point rather than a side effect. *Nothing to reverse; this is a mechanism, not a
policy.*

**4 · The multiplier that reconciles a meter's unit with the unit it is billed in
is now resolved PER SERVICE.** The rule never said otherwise — a factor
reconciles ONE service's register against ONE service's billed unit — but the
code held a single factor for the whole estate, which could not be seen while the
estate had one meter. A consequence worth stating: a utility whose electric units
cannot be reconciled now keeps its water estate and loses only electric, by name,
instead of losing the whole demo. `BR-MET-143` is amended, dated, with this
recorded in it.

**NO FROZEN FIGURE MOVES, AND THIS WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The
reference bill finance signed states its water charge (**$39.50**) and its sewer
charge (**$15.80**) as figures on their own LINES, not as a bill total. Adding an
electric line to that bill adds a line and moves neither, and sewer is 40% of the
water charge so it is untouched. A test now asserts both figures **on a bill that
also carries electric**, so the day anything moves them the run goes red rather
than the number going quiet.

## 2026-09-02 · 📐 SEWER HAS NO UNIT, AND SETTINGS REFUSED TO SAVE IT — THE RULE THAT SAID "ALWAYS REQUIRED" NARROWS TO TWO OF THE THREE BASES (`DEF-3232`, `BR-TEN-1181`)

**The defect, in one sentence a clerk would recognise.** Open Settings → Services
& UoM, click Sewer, press Save, and the screen answers *"Pick a primary unit."* —
**and there is no unit to pick.** Sewer is a percentage of the water charge. It
reads no meter and counts nothing. The Product Owner ruled that themselves on
2026-09-02: a share service has *"no register, no count, and no unit of its own"*.
So the product was asking for something it had already decided does not exist,
and it refused the save until it got it.

**Why nobody saw it, and it is worth stating because both halves were correct.**
The rule that requires a unit was signed on **2026-08-09**, when every service the
product sold was measured in something. The rule that gives sewer no unit was
signed on **2026-09-02**. Three weeks apart, by two different people, and neither
is wrong. **Only their overlap is**, and no test in the repo drove a SAVE of the
one service where the two meet: the backend suite asserts the refusal, the
frontend suite renders the row, and the seed test asserts sewer has no unit. All
three were green.

### THE DECISION, AND IT IS A LANE JUDGMENT RATHER THAN A QUESTION FOR THE PO

Two shapes were honest. **The unit becomes optional everywhere**, or **it stays
required for the two bases that have a quantity and is refused for the one that
does not.** The second was chosen and this is the reasoning, recorded so it is not
re-litigated:

* **`metered` keeps it, and this is the half that must not move.** A meter's
  reading is a consumption, and CLAUDE.md hard rule 3 is *a consumption always
  carries an explicit unit, never assumed*. Metering's own validation errors
  `unit_missing` on exactly that row. Dropping the requirement everywhere would
  let a utility save an electric service with no unit and meet the consequence
  three weeks later inside a bill run.
* **`capacity` keeps it too, and this is the one that is easy to get wrong.**
  A capacity service reads no register either — so *"it has no register"* is NOT
  the test, or trash would lose its unit as well. Its quantity is a **COUNT, and
  the count is counted in something**: **3 carts × `$15.00` = `$45.00`**, and the
  unit is `cart`. The PO said it in those words — *"Cart sizes will decide price X
  how many Cart"*.
* **`share` alone has no quantity at all.** The worked figure: on `$28.75` of
  water usage, sewer bills **40% = `$11.50`**, computed from MONEY. Nothing is
  measured, so there is nothing for a unit to be the unit OF.

**And a share service may not be GIVEN a unit either — it is refused, not merely
optional.** Allowing one would leave two spellings of one fact (`NULL` and
`'kgal'` both meaning *sewer has no unit*), and every reader downstream would have
to know which. That is the same ambiguity `DEF-2409` was filed about one column
over, six hours earlier.

### THE CLAUSE THAT MAKES IT INSTALLABLE ON A LIVE TENANT

**Refuse what the caller supplied; clear what it did not.** Migration
`tenancy 0031` moved sewer's basis to `share` and deliberately moved no unit — a
data migration that rewrote declared units would have been doing more than the
ruling said. So a tenant provisioned before today holds sewer as `share` **with a
stored `kgal`**. Refusing on a stale value nobody mentioned would be this same
defect again in a different field: a refusal with nothing a clerk can do about it.
With this clause the ordinary Save on that screen is the repair path, and the
form sends the four nulls itself.

### WHAT A CLERK SEES

The four unit fields are **not shown** when the basis is *% of another service*.
Not disabled, and not shown with a sentence explaining themselves: B14 rule 33
puts rationale at zero words on screen, and the control directly above already
reads *"% of another service — a share of its charge"*. Move the radio and the
units go. The server's refusal exists for a script or a replayed request, not for
a person — **"This service has no unit. Leave the units empty."**, five words and
four, both inside B14 rule 33's six-word cap, in all eleven catalogues.

### PROVED RED FIRST, ON BOTH SIDES

Backend, against the branch tip before any change — `3 failed, 2 passed`:

    core.errors.ValidationError: VAL-001 (settings.services.primary_required)

⚠ **and one failure was more interesting than "it did not refuse".** Sending
`kgal` for sewer came back `settings.services.uom_unknown` — *"we don't recognise
the unit"* — which is accurate about the outcome and **wrong about the cause**.
The unit is real; the reason it cannot go there is that sewer has no unit. The new
check runs before the lookup, so the refusal now names the actual rule.

Frontend, by putting the tip's own `SettingsServicesTab.tsx` back under the new
DOM test — `3 failed | 1 passed`:

    AssertionError: expected <select id="primary_uom" …> to be null
    AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0

The second is the defect in one line: **the list of requests the server received
was EMPTY.** The client refused the save and nothing ever left the browser.

⚠ **AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT TEST COULD NOT HAVE FAILED**, which is the more
useful half. It asked for the label `"Primary unit"` exactly, while the form
appends a required asterisk — so the query returned null whether the field was
rendered or not, and `toBeNull()` was green on the broken build. `/^Primary unit/`
is what makes it a check. **A query that cannot tell pass from fail is worse than
no check, because it is trusted.**

### WHAT DID NOT MOVE

No ❄️ frozen figure. `BR-RAT-015`'s 40% is untouched, `BR-RAT-090`'s
`3 × $15.00 = $45.00` is untouched, and the golden numbers are where they were:
**33 document self-consistency checks, and 14 of the 61 signed golden tests
engine-verified** — both unchanged by this work, which touches no billing math.

## 2026-09-02 · 🔧 THE PRODUCT KNEW WHY A SERVICE GOT NOTHING AND WROTE IT TO A LOG FILE — A SEEDED STEP CAN NOW CARRY A SENTENCE (`DEF-3224`)

**What it cost, and it is the reason this one matters more than its size.** The
Product Owner created a tenant selling Electric, Water and Sewer and reported
*"no bill generated ; that means our Billing engine is not working"*. **The
engine was fine — it produced 95 bills.** What had happened is that the demo
estate put one meter on a unit, water took it, and **electric got no meter, no
reading and no line on any of those 95 bills — not even its `$12.00` monthly
charge, which is `$576.00` a month across 48 units.** Every setup step reported
success, 0 of 17 blocks failed, and a whole round trip was spent proving the
billing engine innocent.

**The product knew.** `apps/metering/sample_data.py` composes a correct,
readable sentence naming electric and why it was left out — and sends it to
`logger.info`, a server log no clerk can open, beside a comment saying *"a
utility that cannot see gas in its demo will ask why"*. That comment is
CLAUDE.md law 1 exactly: **a comment claiming a guarantee is not the
guarantee.**

### WHY NO CHECK NOTICED, AND IT IS THE USEFUL PART

Three, and every one of them was green:

1. **The step SUCCEEDED.** The estate WAS built, so the block outcome is
   `seeded` and the Sample data panel is entirely green. The panel has rendered
   a sentence for a FAILED step since it was built; a step that succeeded had
   `detail: None` hardcoded, so there was nowhere to put one.
2. **The sentence existed and was good.** It went to a log.
3. **The coverage test counts INVOICES PER TENANT.** A tenant that bills water
   correctly and drops electric entirely scores as a PASS. **A count of invoices
   cannot see a missing service on those invoices.**

### WHAT WAS BUILT

**A step that succeeds can now carry a note.** The orchestrator resolves an
optional `<step>_note` function on the owning module and records what it says as
that step's sentence. A module that publishes none reports exactly what it
reported before — the ordinary case, and a panel that grew a sentence per step
would teach people to stop reading the sentences. Metering publishes one today;
it is `estate().refused` — the same text the log line carries, so a screen and a
log cannot come to disagree.

Three things it deliberately does not do, each stated so the next lane does not
"simplify" one away: **it never fails the run** (a note seam that raises is
logged and treated as silence — narration that can break seeding is worse than
no narration); **it never turns a good step red** (the step DID what it was
asked); and **it never puts an internal reference on a screen.**

### THE ONE JUDGMENT THIS TOOK, AND ITS COST

**The sentences were written for a log and three of the four name something
internal.** B14 rule
31 is ratified and enforced — the PO's words, 2026-08-19: *"Youa re also adding
internal content and BR codes on screen, that is not required."* The sentences
live in a file this lane does not own, so the reference comes off **at the
boundary where a log sentence becomes a screen sentence**: a rationale sentence
carrying one is dropped whole, and what remains is the fact and the instruction.

⚠ **AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT RULE DELETED AN INSTRUCTION**, which is worth
recording because the repo already had the law and the draft broke it anyway.
One reason string carries its reference in its FINAL sentence, and dropping that
sentence deleted *"set the factor on Settings → Services & UoM and load the
sample data again"* — leaving a message that says what is wrong and nothing
about what to do. `G33`'s own failure output says it in as many words:
**"SHORTEN BY DELETING THE RATIONALE, NEVER THE INSTRUCTION."** The rule now
never drops the last sentence; it cuts the reference out of it instead and
accepts the small grammatical scar. **A rule that CAN delete the instruction is
the dangerous one, however good its prose is the rest of the time.**

**This is a boundary, not a licence.** The durable fix is for those reason
strings to lose their references at source, with the provenance in the code
comment beside them — one edit for whoever owns `core/sample_fixture.py`.

### THE SHAPE THAT REPORTED THE DEFECT NO LONGER ARISES, AND THE MESSAGE STILL HAS TO EXIST

**`CR-062` group C landed while this was being built.** The estate now meters
EVERY metered service a utility sells, `_NOT_THE_BACKBONE` is withdrawn from the
fixture, and electric is no longer refused on the PO's own three services.

**That does not close this.** Services are still legitimately refused, and the
standing example is **sewer without water**: `BR-RAT-015` ❄️ prices sewer at 40%
of the WATER usage charge, so a utility selling sewer and not water has no basis
for the percentage and gets no sewer service point. **That is CORRECT rather
than a fault, and it is precisely the thing a clerk will ask about.** So the
end-to-end proof provisions Electric + Sewer, runs the whole plant, and asserts
the general property — *every service this tenant sells that the estate does not
speak is NAMED on the panel* — while naming no service itself. Written against
electric it would have passed today and silently stopped testing anything the
day `CR-062` landed.

### PROVED RED FIRST, AND MEASURED RATHER THAN IMAGINED

The branch tip's own orchestrator was put back under the new tests and they were
run against PostgreSQL 16. `2 failed`:

    AssertionError: a SEEDED block cannot carry a note — DEF-3224
    assert None

    AssertionError: the panel says nothing about the services this tenant
    sells and the estate does not speak — DEF-3224
    assert ''

The second is the end-to-end one: a real tenant, provisioned through the real
signup path, with the whole plant run against a real PostgreSQL. The empty
string is the panel.

### AND ONE MORE TRAP, FOUND WHILE WRITING IT — CLAUDE.md law 14

The note function reads the tenant's own tables, so what it raises in real life
is a **database** error, and **on PostgreSQL any failed statement aborts the
whole transaction.** The first draft caught it and carried on — and the write
that records the step's outcome would then have failed too, so **a step that
seeded perfectly would have been reported FAILED because its narration broke.**
The fix is a SAVEPOINT (a nested `atomic()`), and the comment beside it says so,
because it looks exactly like a line somebody would tidy away.

⚠ **The whole suite passes either way**, because the tests run on in-memory
SQLite and SQLite has no aborted-transaction state. There is now a case marked
`requires_postgres` that raises a REAL failed statement, and it was run against
PostgreSQL 16: **1 passed.** That is the second time this month this trap has
been met, and both times it was invisible to the default suite.

⚠ **The end-to-end case also asserts that the fixture is refusing something at
all**, and says which. Without that it would be a check that cannot fail the day
the fixture stops refusing — `DEF-182`'s lesson: a check whose output cannot
distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check, because it is trusted.

### THE MEASUREMENT HALF IS NOT BUILT HERE, AND IS SAID RATHER THAN LEFT

`DEF-3224`'s own prevention column asks for two things. This is the PRODUCT
half. The MEASUREMENT half — teaching the coverage test to record which services
actually appear on the issued bills, so a service that is sold and appears on no
line is an asserted fact — belongs to `test_service_billing_coverage.py` and is
not touched here.

### WHERE THIS IS WRITTEN DOWN

`BR-TEN-1182` in tenancy's business rules, which EXTENDS `BR-TEN-060` rather than
changing it: that rule (PO, 2026-08-10) already says a gap is a NAMED LINE and
never a silent skip, and it was built for the two outcomes where a step did not
run. `seeded` was the one outcome it could not express, and it is the one that
reached the Product Owner.

### WHAT DID NOT MOVE

No billing math. **33 document self-consistency checks, and 14 of the 61 signed
golden tests engine-verified** — both unchanged.

## 2026-09-02 · 💵 A BATTERY OR SOLAR CUSTOMER CAN BE BILLED AGAIN — THE CODE WAS ASKING "DOES THIS SERVICE HAVE SIZES?" AND MEANT "DOES ITS PRICE VARY BY SIZE?" (`DEF-3098`, `CR-062` group A handover)

### THE FIGURE THAT MATTERS, BECAUSE IT IS A BILL THAT DID NOT EXIST

A battery schedule with no per-size rows — the shape every real tenant has, because
`rate_size_rows` is empty on every tenant in this product — priced **nothing at
all**. Measured, beside the identical sewer schedule which has always worked:

    assert battery.size_rows == sewer.size_rows
    AssertionError: assert {} == {'': Decimal('8.000000')}

An empty size axis is not *"no sizes configured yet"*. It means **this version
prices no size**, so R3 refuses every meter by name and the bill is never
produced. Solar, storm water and broadband were in the same state. **`DEF-2408`
is the same outage one week earlier, from the opposite direction:** battery could
not be billed for five days because its bands had *never been ruled*; this time
it could not be billed because it had *too many rows*.

### THE JUDGMENT THIS LANE MADE, AND WHY IT IS NOT A QUESTION FOR THE PO

Nothing here needed a ruling. Every rule involved is already signed; what was
wrong is that the code asked the wrong one of two questions that used to have the
same answer:

    "does this service have size class rows?"       a fact about a LIST
    "does this service's price vary by size?"       a fact about MONEY

Until `CR-062` only banded services had rows, so the first was a sound proxy for
the second. `CR-062` group A broke it **deliberately and correctly**: solar,
battery, storm water and broadband gained a **catalogue of installable
equipment** — ten panel types, six battery blocks, five property sizes, three
broadband tiers — and a catalogue is not a rate axis. Such a service has rows and
does not band: its price is one flat figure per kW (per ERU, per Mbps) times the
**sum** of what is installed. Three panels of 2 kW, 4 kW and 8 kW are ONE 14 kW
array on ONE connection, not three connections of three different sizes.

**The decision was which question each caller needed**, and the answer was the
same for all three: the money one. So it is asked once, by name —
`apps/rating/resolution.service_prices_by_size_class(service)` — reading tenancy's
exact answer (`capacity_uom_for_service`, which returns the summing unit for a
capacity service and `None` for a banded one) instead of counting rows.

**Nothing names a service anywhere in the fix.** Special-casing battery would
have left solar, storm water and broadband broken, and would have broken again
the day an eleventh service arrived — which it did, this morning, when `CR-063`
added Fire.

### IT WAS IN THREE PLACES, NOT ONE — AND THAT IS THE PART THE HANDOVER MISSED

The defect row named `resolution_catalogue.configured_sizes_for`. Reading the code
found the identical inference twice more, both on the money path:

| Where | What it did with a capacity service |
|---|---|
| `rating/resolution_catalogue.configured_sizes_for` | published an EMPTY size axis, so R3 refused every meter |
| `rating/resolution._assert_service_is_ruled_sizeless` | refused the whole account — *"'storm_water' DOES have a ratified size ladder"* |
| `billing/resolution_shadow._service_is_ruled_sizeless` | reported every solar and battery account **unevaluable**, `MISSING_CONNECTION_SIZE` |

The third is the shape of `DEF-2851` — *116 of 163 accounts NOT ATTEMPTED* — one
service family further on, in the harness the PO put on the sensitive-paths list
precisely so it would be watched **before** it touched money.

**Why one grep would not have found them:** none of the three names a service.
They were reachable only by reading every caller of `size_classes_for_service`.

### WHAT MUST NOT MOVE, AND WAS PINNED SO IT CANNOT

* **Trash still refuses to be summed.** Trash is *capacity based* in the PO's own
  words and is **banded** in this product: the size picks the rate and the count
  multiplies it — *"Cart sizes will decide price X how many Cart"*. Its three
  carts are GALLONS and its four dumpsters are CUBIC YARDS, so no total exists in
  any unit at all. `capacity_uom_for_service("trash")` answers `None`,
  `total_capacity` raises by name, and trash keeps the banded axis.
* **`BR-RAT-120` is unchanged.** A BANDED service whose schedule configures no
  size still serves none and still refuses by name — the reading the PO chose
  with its cost stated: *"Read the second way, the system refuses bills that
  price perfectly well today."* All five banded services are pinned.
* **The three readings still do not collapse.** *Ruled to have none* (sewer),
  *nobody has said* (thermal steam, `OQ-560`, still raises), and *here is a
  catalogue* stay three different answers.

### THE PO'S OWN ARITHMETIC, ASSERTED

Three panels of 2 kW, 4 kW and 8 kW are **14 kW**, and at their stated rate of
**$14.00 per kW** that array bills **$196.00**. Their message reads *"14 X 14 =
156 $"*; 14 × 14 is 196, they were told so in the same session and did not
dispute it, and **$156 appears nowhere in this repo** — a wrong figure copied
into a fixture becomes a wrong figure asserted by a test, and then it is the
product's answer.

### PROVED RED FIRST — nine cases, on the code before the fix

    9 failed, 9 passed

    FAILED test_TC1_a_bare_capacity_schedule_serves_one_ladder_not_none[battery]
    FAILED …[broadband]  …[solar]  …[storm_water]
    FAILED test_TC1b_the_bare_capacity_axis_is_identical_to_sewers
    FAILED test_TC2_R3_accepts_a_blank_size_on_a_capacity_service[battery]
    FAILED …[broadband]  …[solar]  …[storm_water]

    apps.rating.resolution.SizeNotServed: R3: no connection size was resolved for
    'storm_water', and 'storm_water' DOES have a ratified size ladder (SW-SF,
    SW-DUP, SW-APT, SW-COM-S, SW-COM-L). …

The nine that passed are the ones that must not move — trash, the five banded
services, the three readings, and the two figures.

### WHAT DID NOT MOVE

No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure. `GT-15`'s **$40.00** solar and **$24.00** battery are
untouched and still price through the whole chain, and the golden numbers are
where they were: **33 document self-consistency checks, and 14 of the 61 signed
golden tests engine-verified** — both unchanged, because this work touches which
size a schedule serves and never what anything costs.

## 2026-09-02 · 📐 A TEST THAT PINS AN ALLOCATED NUMBER FAILS EVERY TIME SOMEONE ELSE ALLOCATES ONE — `DEF-3104`'s PREVENTION, BUILT ON THE THIRD OCCURRENCE

`test_br_ten_171_tc8` asserted the platform fixture's serial as a literal string.
The serial is **allocation, not law**: two lanes can each take the next free one,
and a merge renumbers whichever loses. So every bump made an unrelated suite go
red over a version STRING — `V2.48.0.3`, then `V2.48.0.4`, and this lane's
`V2.48.0.5` for the 40 → 60 size classes made it three. (60, not 53: `CR-063`'s
seven fire bands landed while this lane was regenerating, and the mirror delivers
whatever the ratified list holds.)

`DEF-3104` diagnosed this exactly and **recorded the general fix as reported, not
built** — the instance was repaired by moving the literal. It came back within the
day, which is the durable lesson: *a fix that repairs the instance and reports the
mechanism will be back.*

**The pin is gone.** The case now asserts the RELATIONSHIP `BR-TEN-077` actually
requires: the declared version is well-formed under the current grammar, and the
fixture's content hashes to the digest ratified for **that** version.

**This is strictly stronger than the literal was**, which is the only reason it is
a lane judgment rather than a question. A content change with no version bump —
the defect `BR-TEN-077` exists to catch, and the one that left a corrected
vocabulary undelivered twice — still fails, loudly, naming the rule. What no
longer fails is a merge-time renumber, which was never a defect in the first
place. **A gate that is permanently red is a gate that is off** (`DEF-490`), and
this one had been red three times for a reason that was never about the fixture.

## 2026-09-02 · 📐 WHAT THE SECOND METER COSTS, MEASURED — an addition to the `CR-062` group C row above, written BELOW it on purpose

The row above says what the change does and states the estate's new size in
meters and readings. **This is the same change measured in seconds**, because
"the demo will take longer" was the argument the withdrawn rule rested on and it
deserves a number rather than a shrug.

Two utilities were signed up through the real sign-up screen on one build, one
tick apart, and both were timed:

| what the utility sells | the whole demo build | **the bill run** | readings | bills | lines on those bills |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Water + Sewer | 111.9s | **30.2s** | 194 | 95 | 492 |
| Electric + Water + Sewer | 240.3s | **77.4s** | 387 | 95 | 683 |

**The second meter costs the bill run about 47 seconds — two and a half times —
and the whole demo build about two minutes.** The first row is exactly what the
Electric + Water + Sewer utility used to receive, because its electric was
dropped; the second is what it receives now.

**The same 95 bills come out either way.** The customers do not multiply — their
bills simply carry more lines, 492 becoming 683. That is the change stated in
one sentence: the same people, billed for everything they buy.

⚠ **The seconds are not a benchmark and must not be quoted as one.** They were
taken on a machine running several other test suites at the same time, so both
figures are inflated; what the pair is for is the RATIO, and the ratio tracks the
readings almost exactly (194 → 387). Nothing about how a bill is produced
changed — the engine has always priced whatever the price list carries — so this
is the cost of billing more, not of billing differently.

**Anyone can re-run it:** `10-scripts/cr062_billrun_cost.py`, kept for that
reason rather than deleted with the answer.

## 2026-09-02 — A solar array is billed by what it adds up to, and what decides that is the service's own settings rather than its name (`CR-062` D1/H2)

**What was wrong.** A customer with three solar panels of 2 kW, 4 kW and 8 kW was
billed for **three panels**, not for the **14 kilowatts** they had installed. At
the price the Product Owner set — **$14.00 per kilowatt** — that bill said
**$42.00** where it should have said **$196.00**. Every solar customer was being
undercharged by **78%**, and the bill looked completely normal.

**Their own words, 2026-09-02:** *"on given Unit we have installed 3 panels with
2Kw, 4Kw and 8 Kw , it means the totla capacity will be 14 Kw ; rate will be for
1 Kw = 14 $ per KW then bill should be 14 X 14 = 156 $"*. Fourteen times fourteen
is **196**, not 156; they were told so in the same conversation and did not
disagree, and **$156 appears nowhere in this product.**

**Why it happened, which is worth more than the fix.** The code that adds the
panels up already existed. It was written a few hours earlier, it was tested, and
its own notes gave this exact example with the right answer — and **nothing
called it.** The bill run still asked *"how many panels?"* rather than *"how many
kilowatts?"*. Nothing went red, because both questions have perfectly good
answers.

---

### THE JUDGMENT THIS LANE MADE, AND ITS WORKED FIGURE

Since this change request, *capacity based* means two different sums:

| service | what it bills | worked |
|---|---|---|
| Trash | how MANY are installed | 3 carts × $15.00 = **$45.00** |
| Fire | how MANY are installed | one 6" line + two hydrants = **$110.00** |
| Solar, Battery, Storm water, Broadband | how MUCH is installed | 2 + 4 + 8 kW × $14.00 = **$196.00** |

**Nobody was asked which list a service goes on, and nobody should have to be.**
The obvious way to build this is a list of service names in the billing code, and
that list is wrong the day an twelfth service arrives — as Fire proved when it
arrived as the eleventh, six hours earlier. **So the product works it out from two
settings it already holds**, and a service has to answer yes to both before its
capacities are added up:

1. **Do this service's sizes add up to anything?** Solar's panels are measured in
   kilowatts, so ten of them add up. Trash's are three CARTS measured in gallons
   and four DUMPSTERS measured in cubic yards — *"a 96-gallon cart plus a 4 cubic
   yard dumpster"* is not a quantity in any unit, so the answer is no and trash
   keeps counting. Fire is the same, which is what the PO's *"exactly like
   trash"* means in practice.
2. **Is that the unit this utility charges by?** A price list reading *$14.00 per
   kilowatt* bills the kilowatts. A price list reading *$10.00 per panel* bills
   the panels — and charging a per-panel price for a kilowatt total would be a
   number that looks right and is out by a factor of five.

**That second question is why a signed figure did not move.** One of our
finance-signed reference bills prices solar per *panel*: four panels at $10.00 =
**$40.00**, with a battery line of **$24.00** beside it. Neither moves, because
that utility is not charging by capacity — and the $40.00 sits inside another
frozen figure, so moving it would have needed a finance re-signature rather than
a code change.

### WHAT HAPPENS WHEN NOBODY RECORDED WHAT A PANEL IS

**The bill for that one customer stops, and it says why.** It does not add up the
panels it does recognise: a unit with three panels where only the 2 kW one was
ever recorded would bill **2 kW** for a **14 kW** array, and that document would
foot, print and post. The clerk is told to go and record each panel's type — not
to go and read a meter, which is the wrong job and the wrong screen. Every other
customer in the run still bills.

**A unit with no solar equipment at all is a different fact and still bills.** The
utility looked, there is nothing there, the total is zero and the bill issues.

### WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* YET DO, SAID PLAINLY

**A real utility's solar line still comes out at $0.00**, because no price is
seeded for it yet — that is a separate task in the same change request. What
changed today is the QUANTITY: the product now knows the array is 14 kilowatts.
The day the price is seeded, the bill is $196.00 with no further work.

**And the older duplicate pricing chain still counts.** There is a second,
switched-off copy of the pricing rules used only for comparison; it was left
counting, so it now disagrees with the live run on capacity services. It bills
nobody, and making it agree is its own piece of work — recorded rather than done
quietly.

**Proved before it was believed.** Every one of the ten new checks was first run
against the branch as it stood, in a separate copy, and five of them failed —
including the one that said `$42.00` where it should say `$196.00`. The five that
PASSED before and after are trash, fire, the finance-signed $40.00 solar bill and
the seeded-unit agreement: the half that must not move.

## 2026-09-02 · "ONE CONNECTION, ONE SIZE" IS A RULE ABOUT METERED CONNECTIONS, AND ITS SCOPE IS NARROWED HERE

**Decided by the coordinating session, not put to the PO** (hard-won law 13: a judgment
recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make one).
**A supersession is stated rather than assumed** — see the last section.

### WHAT WENT WRONG, AND IT IS A GOOD RULE MISFIRING

`CR-063`'s demo warehouse cannot be seeded as written. It carries **one 6" fire line and
two private hydrants**, and the lane building Fire found that this is *two different sizes
on one connection*, which `metering.connection_size_for` refuses **on purpose**: its own
docstring says two recorded sizes on one point is a data error and the only two things it
could do about it are *pick one* — *"which selects a tier ladder, and therefore prices a
bill, on a coin toss"* — or *say it cannot tell*. It says it cannot tell, and the caller's
named refusal carries that to a human.

**That reasoning is correct and is not being reversed.** What is wrong is its SCOPE.

### THE DISTINCTION

**A metered connection has one size because the size picks a tier ladder.** A 2" water
service and a 6" water service are the same connection measured one way, and the size
decides which ladder of rates the reading is charged against. Two answers there really is
a coin toss over money, exactly as the docstring says.

**A counting-capacity service is the opposite shape: the size belongs to each ITEM, not to
the connection.** A cart is 96 gallons. A hydrant is a hydrant. A 6" fire line is a 6" fire
line. Nothing picks a ladder — each item carries its own price, and the quantity is how
many of that item there are. Asking "what size is this connection?" of a property with a
fire line and two hydrants is asking a question that has no answer and does not need one.

### THE RULING

**For a capacity service billed by a COUNT — today trash and fire — the one-size-per-
connection rule does not apply. The bill carries ONE LINE PER SIZE, and the quantity on
each line is the count of items of that size.**

Worked, on `CR-063`'s warehouse:

| Line | Quantity | Rate | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fire — 6" line | 1 connection | 60.0000 | 60.00 |
| Fire — private hydrants | 2 hydrants | 25.0000 | 50.00 |
| **Fire, total** | | | **110.00** |

`$110.00` is the figure already put to the PO and already drawn in the worked-examples
document, as two lines. **The product must produce two lines, not one**, and that is the
honest shape: they are different equipment at different prices and a single blended
quantity would hide that.

Trash gains the same freedom it has always needed and never exercised: three 96-gallon
carts **and** a 4 cu-yd dumpster on one property is `3 × $15.00` plus `1 × <dumpster rate>`,
two lines, rather than a refusal.

### WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT CHANGED

* **Metered connections keep the rule exactly as it stands.** Two sizes on a water or
  electric point is still a data error, still answers `None`, and still refuses by name.
  A test must assert this after the change, or the fix has traded one defect for a worse
  one on a bigger money path.
* **Capacity services that SUM — solar, battery, storm water, broadband — are untouched.**
  They already have no per-size price; they add capacity up and multiply by one rate. Mixed
  sizes there is the normal case and always was: 2 + 4 + 8 kW is 14 kW.
* **A size nobody recorded is still a refusal, not a zero.** An item whose type was never
  entered stops that customer's bill and says so, per the ruling of 28 August.

### THE SUPERSESSION, STATED

The decision-log entry of **2026-08-27** that established *"two meters on one service point
disagreeing about the size answer `None`, deliberately"* is **narrowed, not reversed**: it
governs METERED connections, where its coin-toss reasoning holds. It never contemplated a
service whose price attaches to the item rather than to the connection, because on that day
no such service could reach a bill.

`BR-RAT-090` is amended in the same commit as this row: a capacity quantity is a COUNT for
trash and fire and a SUM for the other four, and for the counting pair it is **a count per
size**, not a count per connection.

### WHY THIS WAS NOT PUT TO THE PO

It collides with no signed money figure — `$110.00` is the figure they were already shown,
and this makes the product produce it. It reverses no ruling of theirs; it narrows a lane's
own earlier design decision. Under law 13 that is ours to decide and write down. **What
WOULD go to them is the fire price ladder itself, and that is already `OQ-1360`.**


## 2026-09-02 · WHICH HOUSES GET THE SOLAR PANELS, AND WHY STORM WATER GETS NOTHING (`CR-062` D3–D7)

**Decided by the build lane, not put to the Product Owner** (hard-won law 13: a judgment
recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make one).
Three judgments, and the third is the one that costs something.

### 1 · WHICH UNITS CARRY THE EQUIPMENT

`CR-062` D3–D5 say WHAT to plant and not WHERE. `trash_cart_plan` already answered the
same question once and wrote down its rule, so this follows it rather than inventing a
second one: **the units are ordinary — none of them is in `AWKWARD_UNITS`** — because
every unit in that set anchors a narrative case somebody has already signed off, and
unit 0 is ❄️ `GT-17`'s reference bill (water **$39.50**, sewer **$15.80**). Planting a
panel there would move a frozen figure by accident.

| Service | Several | One | None |
|---|---|---|---|
| Solar | unit **4** — 2 kW + 4 kW + 8 kW = **14 kW → $196.00** | unit **12** — 5 kW → **$70.00** | unit **16** |
| Battery | — | unit **4** — 10 kW → **$30.00**; unit **14** — 20 kW → **$60.00** | unit **18** |
| Broadband | — | units **8 / 10 / 20** — 100 / 500 / 1,000 Mbps → **$10.00 / $50.00 / $100.00** | unit **22** |

**Unit 4 is chosen and not stumbled onto.** It already holds `PV-0001`, the customer's own
solar inverter, and `BAT-0001`, the customer's own battery — `CR028_DEVICE_PLAN`'s comment
has read *"beside PV-0001 — the solar household stores what it makes"* since the day it was
seeded. Both declare NO service (`BR-AST-009`), so neither stands on a solar or battery
service point and neither is in any total. The demo now shows both kinds of thing on one
roof: **equipment the utility records and does not bill, and equipment it bills.**

**Why battery has no *several* case and broadband has no *several* case.** `D4` and `D5`
say what they say — one battery per unit, one line per unit — and that is what a household
buys. What `D7` actually asks for is that **a `$0.00` line be provably a real answer**, and
that needs a unit with something, a unit with something DIFFERENT, and a unit with nothing.
All three services have all three, and a test asserts it as arithmetic (two different
totals) rather than as a row count.

### 2 · NO PURCHASE COST ON ANY OF IT, DELIBERATELY

Every CR-028 seed carries a `BR-AST-047` purchase cost in prototype r10's **$118–$412**
ballpark. These nine carry none, and the reason is not tidiness: **a rooftop array is the
customer's, not the utility's.** A purchase cost here would be the demo utility claiming it
bought a customer's panels, and would mean inventing nine money figures to fit a range they
do not belong in. The column stays NULL — the same posture `_container_size_class` takes
about a size the vocabulary cannot answer for. This is also why the equipment is a plan of
its own and not appended to `cr028_asset_plan()`, whose test asserts that cost range over
every row.

### 3 · A SIZE CODE THE TENANT DOES NOT HOLD MEANS PLANT NOTHING — NEVER PLANT IT BLANK

The seeder checks every size code against **the tenant's own ratified ladder** before
writing it, exactly as the trash carts are checked. What is new is what it does on a miss,
and the two failures are **not symmetrical**:

* **a panel that is never planted** leaves the unit at `0 kW`, which is `BR-MET-108`'s
  ruled zero: `$0.00` on the document, honest, and visible to anyone comparing the estate
  against the bills;
* **a panel planted with NO size class** makes the installed capacity unstateable, and the
  bill run then refuses **the whole account** by name rather than totalling the panels it
  does recognise. On a demo tenant that is not a smaller number — it is a run that produces
  no document at all.

So the safe direction is to plant nothing and say so in the log. Recorded here because the
opposite choice looks more helpful and is worse.

### 4 · STORM WATER IS PRICED, RATIFIED AND UNBILLABLE — `DEF-2388`

`CR-062` D6 asks for one storm-water connection per property, sized from the property:
36 houses at 1 ERU, 2 duplexes at 2, 1 apartment block at 6, 2 commercial at 4. **It cannot
be built, and the obstacle is vocabulary rather than arithmetic.**

A capacity total is read off `Asset.size_class` through the asset's service point, so an
ERU has to arrive on a **device** — and there is no device. `BR-AST-042`'s ratified twelve
asset types are a meter, a net meter, a sub-meter, a backflow preventer, a comms endpoint,
a PV array, a battery, an EV charger, a transformer, a generator, a container/cart and a
modem/CPE. **An impervious-area assessment is not equipment**, and `OQ-348` was CLOSED by
the Product Owner choosing a typed characteristic on the unit and REJECTING tenant-extended
asset types **for exactly this class of thing** — its own words name container count,
impervious area and speed tier. Inventing a thirteenth type would reverse that closure and
`BR-TEN-059`'s confirmed count of twelve, so this lane did not.

**The arithmetic is worth recording too, because the CR's own figure does not reconcile.**
D6 says *"57 ERU across 44 premises"*. The four rows it lists come to **54** — 36 + 2×2 +
6 + 2×4 — and the missing 3 are the three newly-platted premises, which carry **no unit, no
account and no bill**. So even once storm water is buildable, the billable total is
**54 ERU across the 41 premises that have units**, and the other 3 ERU arrive when those
premises do.

**Three options, none of them this lane's to choose alone**, all recorded on `DEF-2388`:
(a) add a thirteenth platform asset type — collides with `OQ-348` and `BR-TEN-059`;
(b) teach the capacity sum to read `service_characteristics`, which `BR-MET-108` already
built for impervious area and which no billing or rating code reads at all — a 🔒
rating-math change and *built is not wired* on a money path; (c) leave storm water priced
and unbillable and say so. **Until one is chosen storm water bills `$0.00` on every seeded
tenant and its `$4.5000` per ERU is unexercised** — and a live case asserts that zero on
purpose, so the day it is planted the test goes red and names itself as the thing to update.

### WHAT DID NOT MOVE

❄️ `GT-17`'s water **$39.50** and sewer **$15.80** are asserted live on the same tenant that
now carries a `$196.00` solar line — they are PER-LINE figures, so an added line adds a
line. ❄️ `GT-15`'s **$40.00** solar and **$24.00** battery are quoted per *panel* where this
estate quotes per *kW*, so the two utilities take different arms of the same function and
neither can move the other. **No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure moved.** Golden unmoved both ways —
**33 document self-consistency checks, and 14 of the 61 signed GTs engine-verified.**

## 2026-09-02 · STORM WATER'S CAPACITY IS RECORDED ON THE **UNIT**, NOT ON A DEVICE — PO RULING

### THE PO'S WORDS, VERBATIM

> *"In case of strom water - we have to take it from Unit - B ⭐ Take the size from the property,
> not from equipment. Storm water becomes the one capacity service whose quantity comes from the
> premises"*

They chose **option B** from three put to them, **and corrected it in the same sentence**: the option
as written said *from the property*; the ruling says **from the UNIT**. That correction is the
substance of this row and it must not be flattened back to "the premises" by a later reader.

### WHY IT WAS ASKED, AND WHY THE OPTIONS WERE WHAT THEY WERE

`CR-062` D6 could not be built. A capacity quantity is the SUM of `Asset.size_class` reached through
the asset's service point — so a capacity service needs **a device to carry its size**. Solar has
panels, battery has batteries, broadband has modems, trash has carts. **Storm water has nothing.**
An ERU measures hard surface on a property; it is not equipment and nobody installs one. So the sum
was `0` on every unit, the line printed `$0.00`, and **no check in this repo could see it** — the
line exists, foots and prints, so the invoice count, the service scoreboard and every golden check
pass straight over it (`DEF-2388`).

Three options were put to the PO in plain English with worked figures: **(A)** a thirteenth
equipment type carrying the ERU, the way `Container/Cart` carries its gallons; **(B)** take the size
from the property rather than from equipment; **(C)** leave it at `$0.00`, ruled.

⚠ **A CORRECTION MADE WHILE PUTTING THE QUESTION, RECORDED BECAUSE IT CHANGED THE COMPARISON.**
Option A was first described to the PO as *reversing a ruling of 24 August*. **There is no such
ruling.** The type list is `BR-AST-043`, CONFIRMED by the PO on **2026-08-09**, and `BR-AST-042`
(**2026-08-08**) adds `Container/Cart` and `Modem/CPE` with the words *"types tenant-extensible per
BR-TEN-036"*. **So A reversed nothing** — the twelve are a seeded starting set a utility may extend,
and a lane had been more cautious than the rules required. The PO was told this before ruling, and
ruled B on its merits rather than on A being blocked.

### THE RULING

**Storm water's capacity is a fact recorded on the UNIT, and the billing quantity reads it from
there.** It is the one capacity service whose quantity does not come from installed equipment, and
that difference is not an inconsistency to be tidied away later — it is what the service IS.

**Why the UNIT and not the PREMISES, in the PO's own correction.** A bill is for an account, an
account serves a unit, and every other quantity on that bill is a unit fact. Recording the ERU on
the premises would make storm water the only line whose quantity has to be divided down from
somewhere else before it can be charged — and the apartment block is where that would first go
wrong: **6 units on one premises, one ERU figure, and no ruled way to split it.** On the unit there
is nothing to split.

**The seeded allocation, decided by this session and recorded rather than asked** (law 13): a
premises' assessment is spread **equally** across the units it serves — the same posture
`MASTER_METER`'s `allocation_rule: "equal"` already takes for a block's water. So the apartment
block's **6 ERU** is **1 ERU on each of its 6 flats**, not 6 on each. A house is 1. A commercial
suite is 4.

**Worked, and the figure a test must assert:** a house at **1 ERU × $4.50 = $4.50** a month; the
apartment block **6 × $4.50 = $27.00** across its six flats; the demo estate **54 ERU = $243.00** a
month.

⚠ **THE ESTATE FIGURE IN THAT LAST CLAUSE IS `59 ERU = $265.50` SINCE 2026-09-02 (`DEF-2368`) — AND ONLY THAT CLAUSE.** Later the same day `CR-062`'s addendum appended two premises with units, the municipal depot at 1 ERU and the industrial plant at 4, and the seeded estate grew with them; the utility collects **`$270.00`** rather than `$247.50`. **The ruling, the per-unit figures and every ❄️ frozen figure are untouched** — a house is still $4.50 and the block still $27.00 between its six flats. This entry is left as written because it is the record of the ruling; see this log's `DEF-2368` entry for the measurement and for why one of the two constants stays a literal.

⚠ **`CR-062` D6 SAYS "57 ERU ACROSS 44 PREMISES" AND ITS OWN ROWS ADD TO 54.** The missing 3 are the
three newly-platted premises that have no unit, no account and no bill. **On this ruling that
discrepancy dissolves rather than needing a fix**: a premises with no unit has nowhere to record an
ERU and nothing to bill, so 54 was always the billable figure. The task text is amended to say so.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE

* **The other four capacity services still sum installed equipment.** Solar, battery, broadband and
  trash are untouched; a change that made them read a unit field would be implementing the ruling
  and breaking four services.
* **`$0.00` is still a stamped line, not a silence.** A unit with no assessment recorded bills zero
  and says so, exactly as a unit with no panels does.
* **Option A is not foreclosed.** If a utility ever wants a physical storm-water connection on the
  register, `BR-AST-042` already permits it to add the type. This ruling is about where the seeded
  demo's figure lives, not about forbidding a device that does not exist today.

**Status: RULED — `CR-062` D6 unblocked, `DEF-2388` to close against the build.**

## 2026-09-02 · `CR-062` D6 BUILT — WHAT THE LANE DECIDED, BEYOND WHAT WAS RULED

The ruling above is the authority and nothing here re-opens it. These are the judgments the
build had to make that the ruling does not answer, recorded with their worked figures so the
next agent does not re-derive them (law 9/10). **Storm water now bills `$247.50` a month
across the demo estate where it billed `$0.00`; `DEF-2388` is CLOSED.** (The ruling's figure
is **54 ERU = `$243.00`** of assessment; the extra `$4.50` is `BR-RAT-101`'s outside-city
surcharge on two houses and is not this change — §8 below.)

### 1 · THE KEY IS `assessment`, NOT `eru`

`BR-MET-108` fixed the SHAPE of a unit-and-service characteristic — `unit_id · service ·
key · value · unit_of_measure` — and its **third argument** is that the unit of measure is a
COLUMN and never a suffix on the key: *"`storm_impervious_sqft` is a unit nothing can
validate, compare or migrate"*. **`eru` as a key name would be that same mistake in shorter
letters.** So the key is **`assessment`** and the row reads `value = "1.0000"`,
`unit_of_measure = "ERU"`. A pure case asserts mechanically that no key in
`UNIT_CAPACITY_CHARACTERISTIC` spells its own unit of measure, so the next entry cannot
regress it.

### 2 · THIS IS NOT AN ANSWER TO `OQ-370`, AND THE DISTINCTION IS WORTH KEEPING

`OQ-370` asks which characteristic keys each flat service has and what a settings form must
offer. It warned, in terms, that a hardcoded map **decides pricing** — its own example was
that `storm_water → impervious_area` would decide *"a flat per-premise storm charge is not
allowed"*, a pricing rule nobody had ruled on. **The PO has now ruled storm water's pricing
rule**, so its key follows from a ruling rather than from a lane. Trash's and broadband's
keys are still unruled, `required_characteristic_keys` still raises `NotImplementedError
("OQ-370")`, and its docstring now carries the correction so the stale half of its own
example does not mislead the next reader. `OQ-370` stays OPEN and non-blocking.

### 3 · EVERY UNIT IS ASSESSED, SO THE `$0.00` CASE IS PROVED BY DELETING A ROW

`CR-062` D7 asks every capacity service to show *several / one / none*, and the other four
name a unit that is deliberately EMPTY (`CAPACITY_UNITS_WITH_NONE`). **Storm water is not in
that map, deliberately.** A missing panel is an ordinary state of the world; an ERU
assessment is a fact about the ground a unit stands on, every one of the 48 units has hard
surface, and the ruled estate total of **54 ERU** assigns an assessment to all of them.
**Leaving one out to make a demo case would move `$243.00`** — a figure the ruling states.

So the ruled zero is proved on a unit whose row the test DELETES and puts back, and it is
proved at the place the outcome is actually decided: `installed_capacity` of **`0`** (a
`$0.00` line on the document) versus **`None`** (the whole account refuses). Those are one
`if` apart. **The zero also sits beside real numbers**, which is D7's actual requirement —
every other case in that file is a non-zero storm-water bill on the same tenant.

### 4 · A ROW THAT CANNOT BE READ AS A CAPACITY REFUSES — IT IS NOT BILLED AS ZERO

`BR-MET-108` as amended (PO 2026-08-25, *"Bill it as zero"*) is about a number **nobody
recorded**. A value that IS recorded and cannot be multiplied — `"100/20 Mbps"`, or an
impervious area of `2450` recorded in `sqft` where the service sums in `ERU` — is a
different fact, and `ServiceCharacteristic.decimal_value` already draws that line in its own
docstring: *"Reading it as 0 would not be billing an absence at zero — it would be
discarding an answer the customer gave us."* So `installed_capacity` stays `None` and the
bill refuses by name. **Pricing `2450 sqft` per ERU would be `DEF-497` with four orders of
magnitude on it** — hard rule 3 satisfied in form and wrong in substance.

### 5 · THE SEED READS WHAT A SIZE CLASS IS WORTH FROM `BR-TEN-171`, NOT FROM THE FIXTURE

`core/sample_fixture.storm_water_assessment_plan` states WHICH of the five ratified property
sizes each premises is — `SW-SF` · `SW-DUP` · `SW-APT` · `SW-COM-S` — and **no number at
all**. What a code is worth in ERU is read at seed time through
`seams.total_installed_capacity`, **the same function the BILL uses**, so the seed and the
bill cannot disagree about what `SW-APT` means. A code the platform ladder does not hold is
SKIPPED with its reason logged and the unit keeps the ruled `$0.00`, which is the safe
direction; the alternative would be a demo tenant that refuses to bill.

⚠ **AND IT READS THE SHAPE OF THE PREMISES, NOT `premises_type` ALONE.** `premises_plan()`
types both the 36 houses AND the 2 duplexes as `single_family` — the duplexes are
distinguished by an `owner_manager` and two units — so a map keyed on the type would assess a
two-unit home at 1 ERU and quietly lose **`$9.00` a month** across the estate.

`SW-COM-L` (10 ERU, large commercial) is ratified and deliberately unused: the estate's two
commercial premises are a laundromat and a diner, and inventing a mall to exercise a code
would put a figure in the demo that nothing in the corpus supports.

### 6 · THE SPLIT IS EXACT ON EVERY SEEDED PREMISES, AND AN INEXACT ONE IS SAID OUT LOUD

1/1, 2/2, 6/6 and 4/1 all divide exactly, and a pure case asserts it rather than a comment
claiming it. The seeder still quantizes to four decimal places (hard rule 2 — this number is
multiplied by a price) and **LOGS when a split does not come out even**, because an absorbed
remainder is a premises whose units no longer sum to its own assessment and nothing
downstream could see it.

### 7 · WHAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**RED first**, on real PostgreSQL 16.13 against an untouched checkout of the tip
(`c0e54d9e`) in its own tree: **5 failed, 1 passed**, storm water at `Decimal('0.000000')`
on the house, on all six flats, on the commercial suite and across the estate. **The case
that PASSED is the one that matters most** — solar `$196.00`, battery `$30.00`, broadband
`$50.00` and trash `$45.00` were already correct on that same seven-service tenant and are
still correct after the change.

⚠ **A SIXTH FAILURE IN THE RED RUN WAS THE PROBE'S OWN BUG, AND IT IS RECORDED BECAUSE THE
NEXT LANE WILL WRITE THE SAME PROBE.** It asserted ❄️ `GT-17` by summing EVERY water line on
the reference bill and got `47.500000`. **`GT-17` is a PER-LINE `usage` figure — `$39.50` —
and the other `$8.00` is the water BASE charge.** Nothing moved; the probe was wrong. A
lane that reads a frozen figure as a whole-service total will invent a frozen-figure breach
and STOP a change that is correct.

**No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure moved.** Golden unmoved both ways — **33 document
self-consistency checks, and 14 of the 61 signed GTs engine-verified**.

### 8 · THE ESTATE COLLECTS `$247.50`, NOT `$243.00`, AND THE `$4.50` IS A SIGNED RULE THIS CHANGE NEVER TOUCHED

⚠ **EVERY ESTATE-WIDE NUMBER IN THIS SECTION AND THE NEXT ONE MOVED ON 2026-09-02
(`DEF-2368`), AND THE REASONING IN BOTH IS UNCHANGED.** `CR-062`'s addendum appended two
premises with units — the municipal depot at 1 ERU and the industrial plant at 4 — so the
estate is **59 ERU**, assesses **`$265.50`** and collects **`$270.00`**, and the month-wide
query section 9 warns about now returns **60** rather than 55 and **`$274.50`** rather than
`$252.00`. The two things these sections exist to say are both still exactly true: the
outside-city 1.5x on two houses is the whole difference between assessed and collected,
and `CASE_OVERCHARGE`'s restatement is why summing the period's lines counts one unit
twice. **The estate is read PER UNIT and the pair is asserted as arithmetic** — the D6
case now derives both totals rather than typing either, which is what stops this section
needing another stamp the next time a seat is appended.

**FOUND BY MEASURING AND NOT BY DERIVING, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON IT WAS FOUND AT ALL.**
The first green run read `247.500000` where every document — this ruling included — says
`$243.00`. The per-unit breakdown named the two units immediately: **30 and 34, at `$6.75`
each instead of `$4.50`.** Those are `OUTSIDE_CITY_PREMISES_INDEXES`.

`BR-RAT-101`/`BR-RAT-102` multiply every base and variable line on a premises **outside the
city limits** by **1.5** — r10's Residential Standard schedule, verbatim: *"Premises outside
city limits multiply base and variable by 1.5 — set on the premise record."* Sewer is
exempt; storm water is not. The seeded estate puts **two** of its 41 assessed premises
outside the boundary, derived from r10's own 61-of-1,247 ratio. So `$243.00 + 2 × $2.25` =
**`$247.50`**, and it was correct before this lane arrived and is correct after it.

**THE RULING'S FIGURE IS THE QUANTITY AND IT IS EXACTLY 54 ERU.** A surcharge multiplies the
PRICE and never the MEASUREMENT, so the assessment total is untouched by it. The live case
therefore asserts **both, separately** — 54 ERU of quantity and `$247.50` of money — rather
than quietly adjusting one to fit the other, which would have hidden a signed rule inside a
rounded figure.

⚠ **THE GENERAL LESSON, AND IT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE `$4.50`:** a ruled worked figure is a
statement about the RULE, and the money on a real bill is that figure after every OTHER
signed rule has had its turn. A lane that "fixes" the difference by editing its expectation
to `$247.50` with no explanation has silently un-recorded `BR-RAT-101`, and a lane that
edits the seed to make `$243.00` come out has silently disabled it. **Assert the quantity
against the ruling and the money against the world, and name what sits between them.**

### 9 · A SECOND FIGURE THE MONEY COULD NOT SEE: 55 QUANTITY LINES FOR 54 ERU

**The amounts were right and the count was not, which is a case a money-only check
cannot reach.** With every unit's storm-water line correct to the cent and the estate
at `$247.50`, summing the QUANTITIES on every storm-water line in the period read
**55 ERU** for an estate assessed at **54**.

**It is `CASE_OVERCHARGE` — unit 31 — and it is the fixture working as designed.** That
index is the demo's own correction story, *"a wrong June read, corrected by
restatement"*, so the account holds **two invoices for the same period** and its
storm-water line appears on both. **The restatement supersedes the original; it does not
bill a second ERU.** Summing the period's lines counts it twice, and the money follows:
the same query totals `$252.00` where the 48 accounts are billed `$247.50` between them.

**So the estate figure is read PER UNIT** — each unit's own bill, once — and the
month-wide `55` is **asserted rather than filtered away**, because that query is the one
the next lane measuring *"what does the estate bill"* will reach for, and it should find
a sentence rather than a surprise.

⚠ **THREE RUNS WERE SPENT GUESSING AT ONE EXTRA ERU, AND THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE
ASSERTION AND NOT THE ARITHMETIC.** The first two guesses were wrong (a vacant unit's
coverage line; a second service point), and each cost a five-minute plant. What found it
was changing the assertion to **name the row** — a per-unit breakdown, then a per-line
dump keyed by unit — rather than restating the expected total more carefully. **On a
fixture this size, a failing assertion that prints only two numbers is a question; one
that prints the offending row is an answer.**

⚠ **AND IT IS WORTH KEEPING A QUANTITY CHECK BESIDE A MONEY CHECK.** A capacity service
is priced `quantity × rate`, so a bill can be right to the cent while the quantity beside
it means something else — which is the exact shape of `DEF-497`, `$15.00 per MONTH`
against a quantity of `3 CARTS`.


## 2026-09-02 · 💵 A CUSTOMER TYPE NO BASE CHARGE COVERS IS A NAMED FINDING, AND THE `$8.00` IT USED TO BILL CAME FROM A RETIRED COLUMN (`DEF-2381`)

**THE PO'S RULING, VERBATIM.** Reviewing the `DEF-3282` fix: *"2 · The silence (not
done, and this is the real fix). The data fix only covers types we seed. A utility
that adds their own customer type — agricultural, a housing association, anything —
hits the same wall on their own data, and the product still won't say a word. It
should be a named finding on step 2: 'this account's customer type is not covered by
any charge for water', sitting with the other blocked accounts, so a clerk sees it in
the review step instead of discovering a missing bill later."* Then: *"can you fix
it"*.

`charges.applies_to_customer_classes` is an INCLUSION list (`BR-RAT-108`), so an
account whose type nobody listed matches no base charge — and nothing anywhere said
so. `apps/billing/gather.py` gains `GATHER_NO_BASE_FOR_CUSTOMER_TYPE`
(`no_charge_applies_to_this_customer_type`), raised while the tariff is assembled and
carried to step 2 as a blocked account on the Plans tab.

**FIVE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE TOOK RATHER THAN PUT BACK TO THE PO (law 13).**

### 1 · THE BOUNDARY, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT COULD HAVE BROKEN WORKING UTILITIES

`rating.selectors.base_charge_from_charge_code` used to answer ONE empty match set
for TWO opposite configurations:

    the service has NO `is_base` code at all        -> UNCHANGED. That tenant has not
                                                      adopted `BR-RAT-088`, still
                                                      bills from the plan, and a
                                                      refusal here would stop every
                                                      bill for every tenant
                                                      provisioned before the ruling.
    codes EXIST and none names this account's type  -> THE NEW FINDING.
    a code naming NO classes (NULL or `[]`)         -> UNCHANGED — `BR-RAT-108`'s
                                                      every class.

The function now keeps the rows it read BEFORE the narrowing, which is the only way
those two can be told apart at all. Both spellings of *every class* — a NULL column
and a stored `[]` — are asserted, because both reach `row.applies_to_customer_classes
or []` and asserting one would leave half the rule untested.

### 2 · THE FALLBACK IS NOT SOFTENED, AND HERE IS THE FIGURE THAT DECIDED IT

**MEASURED, not reasoned.** On a harness tenant with a `BASE-W` charge scoped to
`residential` and an `agricultural` account, the bill run served R3 and R4, resolved
no base code for the account, and quietly priced the base at **`$8.00`** — taken from
`tariff_versions.base_charge`, **the column `BR-RAT-088` RETIRED and the rate-schedule
wizard has had no control for since**. The account billed. Nothing was reported. That
is `DEF-154`'s shape exactly: a well-formed bill produced from whichever number the
code happened to reach.

So the account is REFUSED rather than allowed to fall through. **This does change
behaviour for a tenant whose base charges are scoped by class and whose account
matches none of them**: it used to bill (from the plan, or from the retired column)
and now appears on step 2. That is the point of the ruling — the alternative is
charging a customer a figure their utility never scoped to them — and it stops ONE
account while the rest of the run bills (`BR-BIL-055`).

⚠ **NO SEEDED ACCOUNT MOVES.** `DEF-3282` derived the seeded class lists from
`PLAN_CLASS_ACCOUNT_TYPES`, so every seeded seat is covered.
`tests/test_cr062_j_addendum.py` — which plants a real tenant through the signup
service and bills the municipal and industrial seats — is **21 passed** after this
change, and the golden suite is unmoved.

### 3 · `blocked`, NEVER `silent`

`PreparedRun` says `silent` means *the correct state, and here is who was quiet* and
`blocked` means *a human must act*. A misconfiguration that costs a customer their
standing charge is the second. It is also counted in `account_count` either way, so
the denominator on screen stays honest.

### 4 · THE TAB IS `resolve-subscription`

`BR-BIL-040` puts a finding on the tab that owns its stage's inputs. The repair is the
charge code's customer-type list in Plans & Rates, so the finding lands beside the plan
and tariff findings a clerk is already going there to fix — and never on Reads, where
not one reading is wrong. It is also in `NOT_RETRYABLE_HERE`: nothing on the phase-3
screen edits a charge code, so *retry now* would be a button that always fails.

### 5 · AN ACCOUNT WITH NO CUSTOMER TYPE AT ALL GETS THE SAME REASON AND A DIFFERENT
### SENTENCE

The PO asked about a type nobody covered; the mirror case is an account that states no
type, which an inclusion list also cannot include. Same finding, same tab, and a
sentence that names the other repair — *"this account has no customer type recorded,
and every base charge for water applies only to named customer types"*. Filing it as a
second reason code would have split one fact across two tabs.

**WHAT A CLERK ACTUALLY READS**, taken off a real run rather than quoted from the
source, and with no rule id or internal code in it (`B14` rule 32):

    this account's customer type agricultural is not covered by any charge for water
    — the base charges for water apply to commercial, industrial, residential only.
    Add agricultural to one of those charges, or add a charge that covers it; the run
    continues for every other account.

**RED PROVED FIRST (law 7), on real PostgreSQL 16 (law 14).** Before the change the
finding case failed `Failed: DID NOT RAISE GatherProblem` and the run case failed with
the account sitting in `ready` while `blocked` and `silent` were both empty — the
defect in one line. Ten cases pass now, and the five pre-existing failures in the
suites this lane ran were reproduced identically in a detached worktree at the branch
tip, so none of them is this change.

**No price moves.** This changes what a run REPORTS, never what anything costs.

## 2026-09-02 · THE DIAGNOSTIC DRAWER IS BUILT, AND TWO OF ITS THREE PIECES CANNOT BE (`CR-067` B1/B2/B3)

**The lane's job was the screen half of `CR-067`.** The PO ruled the surface on 2026-09-02,
verbatim: *"You click the row that failed — the drawer you already have, the one behind
"Expand" — and the diagnostic is a second section inside it. Everything on my wireframe lives
there + Same screen. No new tab."* And separately, on the toolbar: *"What I would add to the
toolbar is a "Errors only" filter, so you can jump straight to the failures without scrolling
past 800 rows of successful seeding. - Yes this is required"*.

**WHAT SHIPPED, AND WHAT A PERSON SEES.** Open a failed row on the audit log and the drawer
now carries a second section. It says what was running (*Documents*), that it stopped before
it finished, why — in the server's own fixed sentence — what to do about it, and the reference
`5F2B-9C1D` with a Copy button beside it. A row that records a SUCCESS gets no section at all.
A System Admin also gets the error code, the module and block, and the event; an Executive
gets neither those values nor the strings anywhere in the markup. Seventeen locale keys, all
eleven catalogues, translated.

### 1 · THE TECHNICAL HALF HAS NO DATA, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT THE BACKEND, NOT A DEFERRAL

`error_diagnostics` is created, written at the seeding seams, referenced from the permanent
audit row and swept at ninety days — tasks A1–A5, all landed today. **Nothing reads it back.**
`apps/audit/api.py` defines three routes and none of them touches that table;
`selectors.audit_detail` carries no diagnostic; task A1's own Lifecycle trailer says
`D=deferred(no endpoint of its own)`. So the six lines `CR-067` §5 measures the whole change
against — the exception, its module, the code frames, the job step, the release, the settings
in force — **cannot reach any screen in this product**.

Building the panel against a payload key nothing sends is hard-won law 2: it renders nothing,
`tsc` passes, every test passes, and the feature does not exist. So the panel states the
absence instead, as a `<details>` CLOSED by default (`B14` rule 32) carrying
`data-tracks="DEF-3321"` so it expires when the endpoint lands (`G38`). **`DEF-3321` is
filed.**

### 2 · AND THE ROLE GATE IS CONVENIENCE, WHICH IS SAID OUT LOUD RATHER THAN IMPLIED

The brief asked for a gate that is *"genuinely role-gated, not merely hidden"*, and this one is
not — **because it cannot be, from the frontend, while both halves come out of one payload.**
`BR-SHL-025` is already this repo's posture (*"the server's own `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)`
is the boundary either way"*), and the panel follows it: `useTenantRole`, `ROLE_SYSTEM_ADMIN`,
and an unanswered `/me/permissions` counts as NOT an admin. What it decides is what is DRAWN.
What is SENT is the audit row's own payload, which an Executive who can open S61 already
holds. **A genuine boundary is the same missing endpoint** — a System-Admin-only read of the
diagnostic — which is why `DEF-3321` names it in the prevention column rather than leaving it
to be discovered twice.

### 3 · THE "ERRORS ONLY" FILTER IS NOT SHIPPED, AND SHIPPING IT WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE

**The PO said this was required and it is not built. That is the lane's judgment and here is
the arithmetic behind it.** `apps/audit/selectors.AUDIT_FILTERS` is `actor · action ·
entity_type · entity_id · entity · from · to`. There is no outcome filter, and `action` is
matched with `__iexact` — ONE code, exactly. The audit log's failure vocabulary is at least
**eight** codes today (`sample.block_failed`, `sample.seed_incomplete`,
`security.attempt_refused`, `auth.sign_in_failed`, `auth.lockout`, `tenant.provision_failed`,
`customer.not_created`, `reference.sweep_failed`), so no single value of the one filter that
exists expresses "errors".

Three things were considered and rejected, each for a reason worth keeping:

  * **Send `f.outcome=error` anyway.** `parse_list_params` DROPS an undeclared filter rather
    than refusing it (`BR-SHL-011` — list params never 4xx), so the toggle would come back
    with the **whole unfiltered list** and the reporting tenant's 809 rows would read as a
    product with no errors in it. A control that appears to narrow and does not is worse than
    no control.
  * **Point it at `f.action=sample.block_failed`.** That works today and finds exactly the
    failure the PO was hunting — and calling it *"Errors only"* would be false the first time
    somebody looks for a lockout. Renaming it to what it does is a different control from the
    one that was asked for.
  * **Filter the page in the browser.** The count and the pagination are the server's. Over
    809 rows at 25 a page, narrowing page 1 reports *"no errors"* on 32 pages out of 33.

**`DEF-3322` is filed with the fix stated: one server-side filter over that named list of
actions, and one toolbar toggle writing it into the URL.** The frontend half is perhaps twenty
lines and lands the day the filter does.

### 4 · WHY THE LANE DID NOT SIMPLY ADD THE TWO BACKEND PIECES

Its scope was the screen, in a tree with four other live lanes, and `apps/audit/api.py` and
`selectors.py` are neither of them this lane's. Widening a lane's own scope into another
module's directory is the failure law 11 exists to prevent. **What is owed instead is
precision**, which is what both defect rows carry: the endpoint's shape, its role gate, its
tenant context, the swept-record answer, and the exact eight action codes the filter must
cover.
