## 2026-09-02 — A CHANGE REQUEST WHOSE COMPLETION LIVES ONLY IN PROSE READS AS 0% DONE, AND A LANE WAS DISPATCHED ON THAT READING

**Decided by the CR-062/CR-063 reconciliation lane rather than asked (law 13), and
recorded because the next lane needs the rule and not the story.**

### What happened

A lane was dispatched to *"finish CR-062 and CR-063"* on a parse that reported
**70 of CR-062's 71 rows unticked and 30 of CR-063's 34**. Both change requests
were in fact substantially complete: read from the code, **three rows** are
genuinely outstanding across the pair, and every one of them is a decision
somebody else has to make — the version (the integrator's, twice), `OQ-370`
(narrowed, not closed) and the demo estate's fire equipment (`OQ-1361`).

**The parse was not careless. Neither register has ever used a tick.** Their task
tables are `| # | Task | Notes |` with **no status column at all**, and completion
is recorded in prose paragraphs underneath — *"A1–A6 ARE DONE (2026-09-02, CR-062
group A lane)"*, *"C1–C9: DONE, 2026-09-02, commits `70879c9` and after"*. A reader
looking for a status found none and reported everything outstanding.

### Why this is worth a decision row and not just a correction

It is the `33/33` failure one register along: **a number that was right about what
it measured and wrong about what it was quoted for**, with nothing in between to
say so. And the cost is the expensive kind — a lane sent to rebuild work that is
finished, on a money path, where rebuilding is not neutral.

It is also the exact hazard r11 step 0 names in terms: *"nothing automated reads
prose for truth"*. That sentence is usually read as a warning about STALE prose.
This is the other half of it — **prose that is accurate and unreadable by anything
that is not a careful human is the same hazard**, because the fallback is a
machine guessing and being believed.

### The rule, from here

**A change request's task table carries a STATUS COLUMN from the day it is
written.** Three values are enough — done, part, open — and a row that is `part`
or `open` names the question or the defect that holds it. The prose stays: the
paragraphs are where the evidence and the worked figures live, and they are what
makes a `done` checkable. What the column adds is that the ANSWER is in one place
and can be read at a glance, by a person or by a script.

**Retrofitting is not owed.** `CR-062` and `CR-063` now carry a reconciliation
table because a lane went and read the code to build one; the other sixty-five
change requests do not, and asking a lane to backfill them would be exactly the
mass shared-file rewrite law 11 exists to prevent. **The next CR gets a status
column; the old ones get one when somebody has already read them for another
reason.**

### What was verified, so the claim above is checkable

Every row was read from the branch tip, and every figure was re-measured on real
PostgreSQL 16.13 rather than quoted from the register: fire's **`$12.00`** for a
2" line and **`$110.00`** for a 6" line with two hydrants, on **two** bill lines;
storm water's **`$4.50`** a house, **`$27.00`** across the six-flat block and
**54 ERU** on the estate; the size-class ladder at **60 rows across eleven
services**. **No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure moved** — `GT-17`'s water **$39.50** and
sewer **$15.80** and `GT-15`'s solar **$40.00** and battery **$24.00** are
untouched, and golden is unmoved both ways: **33 document self-consistency checks,
and 14 of the 61 signed GTs engine-verified**.

⚠ **THE `54 ERU` IN THAT SENTENCE WAS NOT RE-MEASURED AND WAS WRONG
— it is `59` (`DEF-2368`, corrected 2026-09-02).** It was re-derived from
`CR-062` D6's own row table rather than from the estate, which is the register
dressed as a measurement and the exact failure the section it sits in was
written to describe. The three per-unit figures beside it WERE measured and all
three hold. The estate assesses **59 ERU across 43 premises — `$265.50`**.

### The second finding, and it is the one with teeth

`DEF-3086` recorded that twelve billing tests were red *"because they still write
`tenant_services.metered` and the column is gone"*. That diagnosis was correct and
it was **one of four independent causes stacked behind each other**: the dropped
column, then `BR-CUS-1024`'s account identifier, then `BR-RAT-088`'s base charge
code, then `R3`'s per-size water schedule. **Each became visible only when the one
in front of it was fixed**, because a red test reports its FIRST exception and
nothing in this repository can see past it.

**So a defect row about a set of red tests is closed on the tests going GREEN,
measured — never on its stated cause being fixed.** Six of the twelve are green;
`DEF-3343` and `DEF-3344` are filed and fixed, and `DEF-3345` holds the remaining
six deliberately, because they turn on what a capacity service with nothing
installed should do — `BR-MET-108`'s ruled zero meeting `BR-RAT-090`'s absent
count — and that is a decision to record, not a helper to edit.

### Correction, same day — `DEF-3320`'s escape reason was itself wrong, and the correction is the useful part

That row reads: *"Every test asserts against `len(SAMPLE_MODULES)`, so the suite
is green and stays green."* **It is not true, and it mattered.** Nine assertions
in two files were LITERALS, and they were red:

* `06-backend/tests/test_cr064_seventeen_steps.py` — **eight** of them:
  `len(catalogue) == 17`, `range(1, 18)`, three more `len(steps) == 17`,
  `len(plant_body["steps"]) == 17`, `plant["total"] == 17`, and two POSITIONAL
  literals, `skipped["position"] == 17` and `broken["position"] == 6`;
* `07-frontend/src/features/tenancy/provisioningSteps.test.ts` —
  `expect(seeded).toHaveLength(17)`, which is the ONE check in the repository
  that parses `SAMPLE_MODULES` out of Python and compares it with the screen's
  hand-typed list. **It went red the moment the eighteenth block landed and it
  did exactly the job it was written for.**

⚠ **THE POSITIONAL PAIR IS THE SHARPER LESSON, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT COUNTING.**
`CR-062`'s Municipal-discount block was **INSERTED at position 6**, not appended
— an enrolment needs an account to grant to, so it has to run after customers.
**An insertion moves every step after it**, so `broken["position"] == 6` broke
for a step whose position is unchanged in every sense a reader cares about, and
`assert rows[5].key === "metering:seed_sample_reads"` in the front end broke the
same way. A count literal fails once and obviously; a POSITION literal fails
confusingly, and the file that held both said in its own docstring that it
asserted *"against `SAMPLE_MODULES` itself rather than against a list typed
here"*.

**So the general rule this lane leaves behind: a length and a position are both
ALLOCATION, never law.** The block's `key` is its identity — `step_catalogue()`
already says so — and every one of the nine now derives from
`len(SAMPLE_MODULES)` or from a `_position_of(key)` lookup. A nineteenth block,
appended or inserted, costs these files nothing.

**And the escape reason a register row carries is a claim like any other.**
`DEF-3320`'s was written from a grep that found the derived assertions and did
not find the literal ones. It is corrected here rather than edited in place,
because the register is append-only and because the row is the record of what
was believed at the time.


## 2026-09-02 · 📐 THREE CRs RECONCILED FROM THE CODE, NOT FROM THEIR TICKS — AND THE TICKS WERE WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (`CR-058`, `CR-064`, `CR-065`)

**THE PO ASKED FOR STATUS *"based on actual code"*, and this is what reading the code found.** Ten
task rows across `CR-058` were blank while the work they describe had shipped days earlier; one CR
carried eleven of its rows TWICE; and one CR that every row calls ✅ had **seven test cases sitting
red on the branch**. The direction of the error is the interesting part: **the record was BEHIND the
code on `CR-058` and AHEAD of it on `CR-064`**, and a status assembled by counting marks would have
been wrong about both.

### 1 · WHAT WAS ALREADY BUILT AND UNTICKED — `CR-058`, ten rows

Rows 1 to 9 and 20 read *"—"*. Every one is built: `resolve_customer_for_account` exists at
`apps/customers/services.py:2619` and all three counter doors call it (`:2381` regular, `:3033`
master, and move-in through `_open_account`); both wizards send the customer block and show the
outcome sentence; the browser spec has four cases. **Ten rows of finished work reading as not
started is how a lane gets sent to rebuild it**, which is the failure the `CR-051 … CR-057` tick
audit of the day before was written about — one CR later, in the same file.

### 2 · ELEVEN ROWS APPEARED TWICE, THE SECOND COPY BLANK — `DEF-3342`

`CR-058`'s rows 10 to 20 stood a second time below the *TASKS 3–9 — BUILT* section, **with no Status
column at all**, so eleven tasks each marked **DONE v2.118.0** were followed on the same page by
eleven identical rows reading as untouched. A lane reading down reaches the blank copy last. Removed,
with a stamp in their place saying what stood there — never silently, because a register that erases
what it used to say is a register nobody can audit.

### 3 · THE ONE THAT REACHED A RUNNING PRODUCT — `DEF-3340`

`CR-062`'s addendum inserted an eighteenth seeding block at position 6 (the Municipal discount) hours
after `CR-064` closed. **The sign-up screen's own list is typed by hand**, and it stayed at
seventeen — so the first frame, the frame that CR exists to draw, showed seventeen rows. **No locale
catalogue had a label for the new step**, so it rendered the server's English sentence in all eleven
languages, and nothing threw, because the screen falls back to the server's label by design.

⚠ **THE JUDGMENT WORTH RECORDING IS ABOUT THAT FALLBACK.** `step_catalogue()`'s docstring calls it
*"the one thing that keeps a newly added step visible on screen instead of silently absent"* — and it
is true, and it is **only half a mitigation**. A fallback promises VISIBILITY. It does not translate
the step, it does not put it in the first frame, and it does not tell anybody the step arrived.
**A mitigation that makes a gap survivable also makes it invisible**, which is why the eighteenth
step went a day without anyone noticing. The docstring now says so at its own sentence.

### 4 · THE CHECK THAT COULD NOT FAIL, AND THE THREE THAT MOVED UNDER THEIR OWN FEET

`provisioningSteps.test.ts` exists to defeat exactly this: it PARSES `SAMPLE_MODULES` out of the
Python and asserts the typed copy IS that list. Its length clause did go red. **Its LABEL clause
iterated the typed copy**, so a step missing from the copy could never be found to be missing a
label — the file's own argument, defeated by the one clause in it that did not follow it. It reads
the parsed list now.

**And three assertions were INDEXES into a list somebody else can insert into** — `broke = steps[5]`,
`steps[6:]`, `states.slice(6)`. Once the break moved from sixth to seventh, the first asserted the
database's own sentence **about the wrong step**, and the other two silently included the failed row,
so a check about *"everything after the break is Done"* was asserting that **the break was Done**.
None of the three could fail and all three were green. They select by key and slice from the break
now. **The general rule, and it is cheap: never index a shared ordered list by a typed number — name
the thing you mean.**

### 5 · A FIXTURE IS RE-CAPTURED, NEVER EDITED

`CR-064`'s screen is proved against a body captured from a live PostgreSQL failure, and its header
promises exactly that. When the estate went from seventeen blocks to eighteen the fixture became a
body the server no longer produces. **The honest repair is to run the break again and keep what comes
back** — eighteen steps, the break at position 7, the database's own sentence — not to edit the
number inside it. Editing it would have kept every test green and quietly turned the file into the
hand-written fixture its header says it is not.

### 6 · TWO LANES REACHED THE SAME FINDING WITHIN AN HOUR, AND THE FIRST TO PUSH KEPT IT

A sibling lane landed the locale key, the typed constant and the `sample_data.py` prose while this
lane was building the same fix. **Theirs stands** — this tree was re-derived from the pinned tip
before a line was written, so nothing of theirs is reverted by subtraction, and only the five items
their fix did not reach were re-applied. `14-id-reservations.md`'s own rule decided it: the earlier
citation keeps the id, and the same reasoning applies to a hunk. **The cost of the duplication was
about an hour of two lanes' work and the mechanism is `DEF-1787`'s** — a sibling in its own worktree
is invisible until it pushes.

### 7 · NO MONEY FIGURE MOVED, AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

Nothing in this work touches a rule, a rate or a posted line. `G61` **130 frozen figures unchanged**,
`golden-verify` **33 PASS / 0 FAIL**, `G64` **14 of 61 engine-verified** — all three identical before
and after. `GT-17`'s water **$39.50** and sewer **$15.80** and `GT-15`'s solar **$40.00** and battery
**$24.00** are untouched, as is every other ❄️ frozen figure.

## 2026-09-02 — `DEF-2368`: the seeded estate's storm-water total, and the thing the register said that was not so

**Three decisions, all this lane's and none put to the Product Owner** (law 13:
a judgment recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable). No ruling is
contradicted, no ❄️ FROZEN figure moves, and nothing a customer is charged
changes.

### 1 · The diagnosis in the defect row was wrong, and correcting it is the point

`DEF-2368`'s row says a third red case was *"recorded rather than diagnosed"*:
**"unit 49's `$18.00` of storm water does not reach a bill at all."** Measured
on real PostgreSQL 16.13 at commit `b253e242`, on a seven-service tenant, that
is not what is happening. The failure, verbatim::

    AssertionError: these units do not bill their assessment:
    {49: Decimal('18.000000')}
    assert {49: Decimal('18.000000')} != {49: Decimal('4.50')}

**The `$18.00` is on the bill.** Unit 49 is `603 Silver Creek Rd`, the industrial
plant appended by `CR-062`'s addendum; it holds a storm-water service point, a
`4.0000 ERU` assessment characteristic, an active account (`AC-2026-00050`) and
**two issued invoices**, `BL-2607-000050` for June and `BL-2608-000100` for July,
each carrying `('storm_water', 'usage', 4.000000, 'ERU', 18.000000)`. What was
stale was the **TEST's expectation**: it built its per-unit map from the literals
`COMMERCIAL_UNIT` and `COMMERCIAL_UNIT + 1`, i.e. `{46, 47}`, and the estate had
grown a THIRD `commercial_building`.

⚠ **THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIGURE IT CORRECTS.** A stale expectation and
unbilled money produce a diff that looks identical when it is skimmed — a
`Decimal` on the left, a smaller `Decimal` on the right — and a lane in a hurry
reads the smaller number as the bill. **The register said money was missing from
a customer's invoice and it was not.** So the D6 case now DERIVES its expectation
from the plan and `BR-TEN-171`'s ladder, which is the only version that cannot
make the claim again.

### 2 · One constant is derived and one stays a literal, and the reason is a boundary

* **`STORM_WATER_ASSESSED_PREMISES` is now `len(storm_water_assessment_plan())`.**
  Counting the plan's rows needs nothing but the plan, so there was never a
  reason for it to be a second statement.
* **`STORM_WATER_ESTATE_ERU` stays a literal, corrected from `54` to `59`.**
  Totalling ERU needs to know what each size CODE is worth, and that lives in
  `apps/tenancy/service_size_classes`. `core/sample_fixture` may not import it:
  it is *"a DECLARATION and nothing else: plain data, no Django import, no ORM,
  no service call"*, and `storm_water_size_class_for` already refuses to type
  those numbers for the same reason. Retyping a literal that has just gone stale
  only resets the clock, so **the drift is what gets the check** rather than the
  number.

**The worked figures**, measured and not derived from any register: the estate
assesses **59 ERU across 43 premises**, which at the seeded **`$4.5000` per ERU**
is **`$265.50`** of monthly assessment and **`$270.00`** collected once
`BR-RAT-101`'s outside-city 1.5x lands on two houses. It was `54` / `41` /
`$243.00` / `$247.50`. The difference is exactly the two seats `CR-062`'s
addendum appended: `601 Quarry Hill Ct`, the municipal depot, `SW-SF`, **1 ERU**,
and `603 Silver Creek Rd`, the industrial plant, `SW-COM-S`, **4 ERU**.

### 3 · The check moves off PostgreSQL, because its PRICE was the defect

The D6 suite already held this comparison and said so in its own docstring —
*"The stated constant and the ladder are two independent statements of one
figure, and this is what stops them drifting apart in silence."* **It worked.**
It took a day because running it costs six minutes of PostgreSQL and a lane
appending two premises had no reason to run it.

So `10-scripts/gates/g73_storm_water_estate.py` makes the same comparison with
**no database and no Django**, by loading the two pure modules by path. Proved
RED first (law 7) on the defect's own numbers — it reports both disagreements
against `54`/`41` — and on three more shapes: a unit assessed twice, a unit not
assessed at all, and a size code the ladder does not ratify. **The fourth of
those found a bug in the gate's first draft**: `total_capacity` RAISES on an
unratified code, so the finding written to name that code in a sentence could
never be reached. That is what proving a guard red is for.

⚠ **AND IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT READ PROSE, HAVING CONSIDERED IT.** Eleven
sentences across nine files quoted `54 ERU` / `$243.00` and were corrected by
hand in this commit. Most of the sentences that remain are RECORDS — *"it said
54 until 2026-09-02"*, a verbatim red-first failure message — and a gate
demanding those be rewritten would falsify the record to keep itself green
(`DEF-182`: a check that cannot separate a real finding from an exempt one is
worse than no check).

### 4 · One thing found underneath and FILED rather than changed

`storm_water_size_class_for` assesses the municipal depot at `601 Quarry Hill Ct`
as **`SW-SF`, a single-family home, 1 ERU, `$4.50`** — because
`government_building` is neither `commercial_building` nor `apartment_complex`
and falls through to the dwelling branch. In the same fixture, `premises_plan`
types that building's unit `commercial` because *"the depot is a non-dwelling
building"*. **Two statements about one building, disagreeing** — which is
`DEF-2368`'s own shape. Nothing bills wrongly: 1 ERU is a ratified size and the
line is real money on a real bill. Assessing it `SW-COM-S` instead would put the
estate at **62 ERU / `$283.50`**. It is filed as `DEF-3400` rather than changed
here, because moving a demo total inside the commit that fixes a stale demo
total would obscure both, and because the estate figure is quoted in a
review-ledger row that a person has not yet signed.

### 5 · The new defect was filed twice, and law 11's id clause is why

`file_defect.py` allocated **`DEF-3383`**, and it was right about the register:
the highest four-digit id pushed anywhere was `DEF-3382`. It was wrong about the
RESERVATIONS, and it could not have been otherwise — the finance lane's
`DEF-3380–3399` row reached `14-id-reservations.md` while this lane was working,
and that row claims the whole block while saying, inside its own claim, that
*"`DEF-3383–3399` remain UNUSED and free"*. **A block listed ACTIVE is not yours
even when `max + 1` lands inside it**, so the id was given back and this lane
opened `DEF-3400–3419` instead, renumbering every citation in the same commit —
the fixture docstring, the decision log, the register row and the reservation.

**This is law 11's id clause firing exactly as written** — *"at push time,
re-derive BOTH: the file content AND the ids"* — and it is worth recording
because the failure looked like success at every step before that: the allocator
printed a true sentence, the number was genuinely free in the register, and
nothing downstream would have objected to a duplicate claim in a 1,474-row file.

## 2026-09-02 · THE RECONCILIATION SCREEN DOES ONE SUBTRACTION, AND IT IS THE SERVER'S OWN (`CR-059` W8, task 48)

**Lane judgment, recorded because the rules ran out at exactly one point** — the
kind law 10 says belongs here with its worked figure, before it is reported to
anybody.

### What was built

`/finance/deposits/statement`. Four backends have been mounted, tested and
unreachable since 2026-09-01 — the period reconciliation statement, an
explanation hung off a single bank LINE, the many-to-one match SET, and the
differences report — and `apps/payments/api.py` said so above them in its own
words: *"NONE OF THESE HAS A SCREEN CONTROL YET … the endpoints are live and
unreachable from the product"*. **Nothing in this product could reconcile a bank
statement.** It can now.

### The judgment, and why it is not an invention

The body carries **no signs**. `sign` and `signed_amount` were deleted from
every reconciling item on 2026-09-02, deliberately, so that no screen could
render an item as an addend to a balance — the PO having ruled (`OQ-1310`)
*"we need to go on factual basis, if bank as report we count if bank did not
report we dont count, and if clark wants to balance the book they can always
make journal entries on their own - that is allowed"*.

So a screen that listed the items and stopped there would be **a report**, and
the person reading it would still be doing the sum by hand — which is what they
were doing before this screen existed. The screen therefore asks one question:
**do the listed items account for the whole difference?**

The identity it uses is **not this lane's**. It is written down twice already,
in `bankrec_read.reconciliation_statement`'s own docstring and in this CR's
task 43 row, in these words:

> the bank says 48,112.40, the books say 46,946.12, and the 1,166.28 between
> them is exactly the three items (1,122.78 − 44.50 + 88.00)

Deposits in transit, LESS outstanding refund cheques, PLUS unexplained lines.

**What the screen does with it is one sentence and nothing else.** Either *"the
items below account for the whole difference"*, or a named residual: move the
unexplained lines from **88.00** to **22.00** and the screen says **66.00** is
accounted for by nothing. **No item is ever drawn with a sign, no adjusted
balance appears anywhere, and no figure produced by this subtraction is ever
added to a balance.** The deleted signs stay deleted.

### The three things that keep it honest

* **It is `null`, never `0`, whenever any input is.** A statement imported
  before the balance columns existed has no bank figure; a chart with no
  designated cash account has no book figure. The residual is then unanswerable
  and says so — *"one of these figures is missing"* — rather than reading as
  fully explained. That is `DEF-127`'s exact shape aimed at a bank rec, and a
  test asserts it.
* **It is exact.** Scaled `BigInt` on the six-decimal grid, through
  `depositsShared.scaledDecimal`. `Number("1122.78") - Number("44.50")` is the
  shape of every money defect this repository has logged.
* **The words "not reconciled" appear nowhere on the screen.**
  `bank_equals_books` is a fact and not a verdict: a period with legitimate
  deposits in transit reads `false` and is properly reconciled.

### What is NOT on the screen, and why

* **No adjusted bank balance**, because there is none on the body.
* **No dissolve control for a match set.** `CS-17` rules the set in and rules
  nothing about undoing one; neither the service nor the database has a path, so
  a control would promise what no code could honour.
* **No general-ledger account number typed by hand.** The account is chosen from
  the tenant's own chart by code and name; the id is the option's value and
  never its visible text (B14 rule 31).
* **No match control on an outstanding refund cheque.** That is `CS-15`, task
  47, and it is not built — the item is listed and aged and nothing more.

## 2026-09-02 · THE DIAGNOSTIC REACHES A SCREEN, THE ROLE GATE BECOMES A BOUNDARY, AND "ERRORS ONLY" LANDS SERVER-FIRST (`CR-067` B2/B3, closing `DEF-3321` and `DEF-3322`)

**What a person can do now that they could not this morning.** A System Admin
opens a failed row on the audit log and reads, under *Technical detail*: the
exception and the module it came from, the line of code it broke on, which step
of which job was running, which build was deployed, the settings that were in
force one line each, and the names of the fields the request carried. That is
CR-067 §5's own bar — *"could somebody holding ONLY the diagnostic record write
a failing test?"* — and it is now answerable from the screen. And anybody
looking at the log can tick **Errors only** and go from 809 rows to the handful
that failed.

Everything below is a judgment this lane made rather than a question it asked
(law 13). Each is written down because the next agent would otherwise have to
make it again, differently.

### 1 · THE ENDPOINT IS ADDRESSED BY THE ROW AND JOINED BY THE REFERENCE, AND THAT MOVED IT ONE HOP FROM THE DEFECT ROW'S WORDING

`DEF-3321` asks for *"a read of one diagnostic by the reference the audit row
already carries, answering 'no longer held' for a swept record rather than 404
with no explanation"*, and separately that another tenant's record be **absent**
rather than forbidden — a plain 404, so existence does not leak.

**Both of those sentences are true only if the two absences are different HTTP
answers**, and they can only be different if the thing being addressed is the
audit ROW. So the route is `GET /audit-log/{id}/diagnostic`:

* the **row** is missing or belongs to another tenant → **404**, the same body
  `GET /audit-log/{id}` already gives for both (HR-1/G4);
* the row is here and the detail behind its reference is not → **200** with
  `held: false`, because an expired diagnostic is a normal state and a 404 would
  read as a fault.

Addressing the record by its reference instead would collapse those two into one
answer and lose whichever sentence it chose. Recorded rather than quietly
resolved, because the shape differs from the words the defect row used.

**Three reason codes, not two, and the third is the one that matters today.**
`held` · `not_held` (it expired, was refused for carrying a value, or was never
stored) · `no_reference` — the row predates task A4 and never had one. **That
last is the state the Product Owner meets first**, because every row already in
their log was written before this afternoon. Saying "the detail expired" there
would invent a record that never existed.

### 2 · THE ROLE GATE IS A BOUNDARY NOW, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHICH READ THE DATA CAME FROM

The lane before this one wrote, correctly, that the drawer's System-Admin check
was `BR-SHL-025` **convenience**: both halves came out of ONE payload the
browser already held, so `useTenantRole` decided what was DRAWN and an Executive
who can reach S61 had the bytes either way.

**A separate, role-gated read is what changes that**, and it is why the endpoint
carries `SystemAdminOnly` while every other route in the module carries
`AdminOrExecutive`. An Executive asking for the record is refused **403
AUTH-002** by the server, with the `BR-AUD-018` attempt row written by the BE-02
handler. The test that proves it puts the record in an Executive's cache **by
hand** — the one state a "the browser was never sent it" argument cannot cover.

**What is still convenience, and is said out loud:** the plain half and the four
summary rows above the record still come from the shared payload. That has not
changed and is not claimed to have.

**A narrower gate than the screen it sits on is not a contradiction.**
`BR-AUD-009` says who may read the TRAIL — what was attempted, by whom, when,
and the plain-words reason. This serves something else: frames, a release, a
deployment's configuration. CR-067 §3's approved table already reads *"a second
section in the same row's drawer, **System Admin only**"*, so the narrowing was
ratified with the change request and is not a choice made here. **Reported for
the `BR-AUD-009` amendment** alongside the new filter.

### 3 · A SUCCESSFUL READ WRITES NO AUDIT ROW; A REFUSED ONE ALREADY DID

Hard rule 7 attaches the trail to a **money action**, and no read on this screen
writes one — `GET /audit-log/{id}` does not either. The half that matters for a
System-Admin-only door is the REFUSAL, and that is audited already by the BE-02
handler's `BR-AUD-018` attempt row. Asserted rather than assumed.

### 4 · "ERRORS ONLY" IS EIGHT NAMED CODES, READ OFF THEIR WRITERS, AND ONE THAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT

`f.action` matches ONE code with `__iexact`, and "did this go wrong?" is eight
codes. The filter is therefore a named set, server-side, because the count and
the pagination are the server's — narrowing one 25-row page in a browser would
report "no errors" on 32 pages out of 33.

The eight: `sample.block_failed` · `sample.seed_incomplete` ·
`security.attempt_refused` · `auth.sign_in_failed` · `auth.lockout` ·
`tenant.provision_failed` · `customer.not_created` · `reference.sweep_failed`.

**Every one was checked against its writer rather than inherited from the defect
row, and a test now greps the backend for each.** That check earned itself
immediately: `customer.not_created` looks absent to the obvious grep, which
finds `customer_not_created` — a payload KEY in two other modules — and the real
writer is one line in `apps/customers/services.py`.

**`service_request.refused` is NOT in the list and the next lane to notice it
should leave it out too.** It is written when a member of staff turns an
application DOWN: a business decision that worked exactly as designed. The PO's
ask is about *"errors [that] will happen run time and it is very difficult to
reproduce those"*. Putting a correct refusal under "Errors only" would make the
control lie in the other direction — a clean log reading as full of faults. **The
test for anything added later: did the PRODUCT fail, or did a PERSON say no?**

An unrecognised `f.outcome` value falls back to the **whole** list rather than an
empty one — the same posture `wants_archive` takes, and for the same reason: an
empty result for a value nobody typed on purpose would read as "no errors".

### 5 · THE FILTER HAD TO BE DECLARED IN THREE PLACES, AND ALL THREE FAIL SILENTLY

`parseTableParams`/`serializeTableParams` walk `TableConfig.filters`;
`auditQuery` walks `AUDIT_FILTERS`; and the server DROPS an `f.<name>` it does
not declare rather than refusing it (`BR-SHL-011` — a list param never 4xx's).
**Three vocabularies, three silent drops, and the only symptom of any of them is
a count that did not move.** Measured on a 24-row fixture shaped like the
reporting tenant's log — 20 successful seeding rows against 4 failures under 4
different codes — the toggle takes it to **4**; with the filter left undeclared
it comes back **24**, status 200, looking healthy. That is why `DEF-3322` said
the filter lands before the control does, and it is the case that bites first if
either vocabulary drifts.

### 6 · THE RETENTION WINDOW IS A DATE ON THE SCREEN AND NEVER A NUMBER OF DAYS

`OQ-1390` is OPEN — is ninety right, and does a diagnostic fall under
`audit_log`'s regime or its own — so printing a figure would resolve an open
question by choosing a value, which the prime directive forbids. And
`DIAGNOSTIC_RETENTION_DAYS` is a per-deployment SETTING the screen cannot read,
so a utility that set thirty would be told ninety by its own product. The server
STAMPS `expires_at` on the record at write time, so the panel prints **that
deployment's own date** — the honest answer the missing endpoint made impossible
until today. The digit ban now covers all six absence sentences in all eleven
catalogues rather than the single one that existed when it was written.

### 7 · TWO SABOTAGES PROVED NOTHING ON THEIR FIRST DRAFT, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING

Hard-won law 7 says prove a guard RED before trusting it green. Doing it
properly caught two checks that would have been trusted for nothing.

* **The cross-tenant leak.** The first sabotage answered a *friendlier* 404 body
  and the suite stayed GREEN — correctly, because that body is served for an
  absent id and a foreign one alike, so nothing is disclosed. **The kernel had
  already made the tidy version of the mistake unwritable:**
  `errors.NotFoundError` takes no message parameter at all, *"keeping
  cross-tenant and plain-absent bodies byte-identical (no leak)"*. The leak is
  telling the two APART, and the natural way to write it is to be helpful about
  a row that exists — so the sabotage now probes and returns 403, and the check
  bites with `assert (403 == 404)`.

* **The toolbar alignment.** The first sabotage gave the toggle's row
  `className="contents"` — a CSS display value that moves no DOM node — so the
  checkbox stayed a child of the flex column and the check passed on it. **That
  is also how the check was found to be in the wrong file.** "Is the toggle
  inside the six-filter grid" is a question about NESTING, and a static string
  can only answer questions about ORDER. It moved to
  `AuditToolbarAlignment.dom.test.tsx`, where `closest()` decides it —
  DEF-182's *"a check that cannot tell the breach from the fix is worse than no
  check, because it is trusted"*, arriving for the third time.

**The general form, and it is cheap: a sabotage that does not do the thing it
names makes a check look proved when nothing was proved.** Read what the
sabotage actually changed, not what it was called.

### 8 · THE RAW TRACE ID CAME BACK OFF THE SCREEN, BECAUSE A RATCHET MAY FALL AND MAY NEVER RISE

The panel carried the full 32-hex trace id for an hour, as *"the value a server
log is grepped for"* — which is the use `apps/audit/diagnostic_models.py` claims
for it in as many words. `G44`'s untreated-value ratchet went **21 → 22** on it,
and that file's own rule is that the number *"may FALL and may never RISE"*.

**Reading the entry rather than banking it said the gate was right**, on three
grounds that were already in the rules:

* **B14 rule 31's REASON applies even where its letter does not.** The rule is
  *"no Databse ID on screen"*, and a trace id is not a database key — but the
  reason rule 31 exists, a value a person can neither read aloud nor type back,
  describes `5f2b9c1d3e7a41b8905c6d2e8f0a1b34` exactly. **The eight-character
  reference exists BECAUSE the 32-hex one is not for humans.**
* **Rule 32's budget** — one more row on a panel the Product Owner has already
  said carries too much.
* **Nothing is lost, and that is checkable rather than asserted:** the reference
  IS the first eight hex of the trace, so `grep 5f2b9c1d` finds the same log
  line the whole string would.

**The field is still SERVED.** The endpoint is a read of a record, not a feed
for one panel, and a support engineer at the API has the whole of it. What
changed is what a screen draws.

### 9 · A TEST COUNT IS ARITHMETIC, AND READING IT AS ONE SAVED SIX CASES

A scripted edit to the frontend test file sliced from one case to `});` before
the Lifecycle trailer — which is the close of the LAST describe, not the one
being edited — and took **six passing cases** out with it: the four "provable
without a browser" reader cases and both eleven-catalogue cases. **The suite
stayed green.** It surfaced only because the count went 90 → 85, which is law
11's *"read the numstat AS ARITHMETIC, not as a glance"* in test-count form. The
same discipline belongs on a test run: a green suite that shrank is not a green
suite.

## 2026-09-02 — CR-060 T7b · T7d · T7f: the three judgments the rules ran out on

The CR-060 T7b/T7d/T7f lane. Three postings a period end could not make before
today, and the calls this lane made where no signed rule reached. **Nothing here
was put to the Product Owner** — law 13's short list is a ruling that collides
with a signed rule, a ❄️ frozen figure, and a fact only they hold, and none of
these is one of those. Each is recorded with its worked number so the next agent
builds the same thing.

### Judgment 1 — WHAT "UNPAID AT A PERIOD END" MEANS, and it is the double-count guard

`BR-LED-792`'s third clause reads **`paid_on IS NULL` OR `paid_on > period_end`**
— *unsettled AS AT the period end*, which is not the same question as *unsettled
today*. C17 does not say which, and the two give different books.

**Worked, on LE-11's CI-1 — $1,240.00 of bulk water bought 6 July.**

* **Paid 4 August, closing July.** `paid_on` is after the period end, so it is
  accrued into July, reversed on 1 August by the existing sweep, and settled on 4
  August. July's `5110 Purchased water` carries **1,240.00** — the month the
  water was sold — and August's carries **0.00**. The cost is charged once.
* **Paid 28 July.** The settlement is already in July's books (CR-060 C1 posts
  `DR cost / CR cash` on `paid_on`), so accruing it too would charge the same
  water twice in the same month. It is EXCLUDED and COUNTED as
  `settled_within_the_period`, and July's accrual is **50,662.50** rather than
  51,902.50.

**Without the clause, July's purchased water reads 4,340.00 against 3,100.00
bought** — which is `DEF-3343`'s own arithmetic arriving from the other side of
the books, twelve hours after that defect was fixed on the export side. The
alternative reading (*unsettled today*) is defensible only for a close run the
same day and silently wrong for every close run after a payment was recorded.

### Judgment 2 — A CLOSED PERIOD IS REFUSED BY ALL THREE, NOT FORWARDED

`BR-TEN-038` forwards a late-dated event into the earliest open period. This lane
refuses instead, in `unpaid_cost_accrual` and `depreciation` both, and for the
reason the T7 lane already recorded for the revenue accrual: an accrual exists to
complete the period it names, and forwarded it would recognise July's cost in
August and reverse it in September — **two months wrong, in a signed book, to
avoid saying no**. For depreciation the reason is sharper still: forwarding would
charge the later month twice and this one never, **and unlike an accrual there is
no day-1 mirror to take it back out**. Both refusals name the reopen (System
Admin, `BR-LED-006`).

### Judgment 3 — DEPRECIATION IS THE PERIOD'S MOVEMENT, AND A FIRST RUN POSTS NO CATCH-UP

`BR-LED-793`. The charge is
`accumulated(period end) − accumulated(the day before period start)`, both from
`apps.assets.selectors.asset_book_value` — BR-AST-047's single implementation —
so the ledger computes no depreciation and cannot come to disagree with the S49
panel about the same meter.

**Worked:** a meter bought for **$164.00** on 12 March 2024 with a 20-year life
has accumulated **$19.8167** by 31 August 2026 and **$19.1333** by 31 July, so
August's charge is **$0.6834**. Across the four such meters of the sample estate
the August entry is **DR 5700 Depreciation expense 2.73 / CR 1730 Accumulated
depreciation 2.73**, rounded ONCE on the sum.

**The consequence, stated because a reader would otherwise assume the opposite:**
a utility whose plant has been depreciating for two years and who runs this for
the first time in September gets **September's slice, not two years of
catch-up**. Posting 29 months into one month on the first press would misstate
that month by everything it absorbed, in an entry hard rule 4 gives nobody a way
to edit; bringing a going-live utility's accumulated depreciation onto the books
is an OPENING BALANCE (`3000`, `apps/ledger/opening_balances.py`) and a decision
about that tenant's history rather than about this month.
`depreciation_before_the_first_posted_period_is_not_in_the_books` rides on every
answer so nobody reads 2.73 as the plant's whole accumulated depreciation.

**And the entry is `type='standard'`, never `accrual`.** One word, and it is the
most important one in the module: `accrual` is what
`manual_je.run_accrual_auto_reversals` sweeps, and a depreciation entry that
reversed itself on day 1 would leave the plant at its purchase cost forever —
CR-060 §5's **$40,000** truck error arriving from the other direction.

### Judgment 4 — WHERE THE THREE NEW DESIGNATIONS GO, AND THE ONE ACCOUNT THAT IS MINTED

`GL_DESIGNATIONS` goes from thirteen to sixteen (`ledger/0014`). Two of the three
are placed on accounts the tenant ALREADY HAS — `2100 Accrued expenses` and
`1730 Accumulated depreciation — meters`, both `UTILITY_BOOKS_CHART` rows the PO
ruled into existence on 2026-09-01/02 — because minting a second accrued-expenses
account beside `2100` would be CR-060 §4's own *"a live account nothing consumes"*
smell reproduced one row later. **Nothing about those two accounts changes: a
designation is a pointer AT an account.**

**One account IS minted: `5700 Depreciation expense`, `signed=False`.** The PO's
111-row reference chart carries four accumulated-depreciation accounts (rows
70-73) and **no expense to charge against them**, which is half of a double
entry, and C20 cannot be built without the other half. It is listed in
`chart.PENDING_FINANCE_RE_SIGN_MATCHING` and its re-sign route is named in
`chart.PERIOD_MATCHING_RE_SIGN_SOURCE` — the same route 4160/4170, 4180, 4300 and
the eight cost-of-service rows all took. **No amount is attached to it.**

`services.ensure_period_matching_accounts` is the top-up that places them, for
hard-won law 4's reason: `seed_chart_of_accounts` runs at PROVISIONING and
nowhere else, so every tenant that exists today would have got two new postings
and no account to put either side in. It **checks the NAME as well as the code**,
so a tenant who renumbered `2100` into something of their own keeps it and the
posting refuses by name rather than quietly crediting somebody else's account.

### Judgment 5 — BR-LED-794: how one bill's collected tax is split across its authorities

**The apportionment, and it is the only one in T7d.** Payments records what a
payment met as ONE class, `taxes`, because `BR-PAY-010`'s order is about kinds of
CHARGE; S41 reports per AUTHORITY, because `BR-BIL-069` gives each authority its
own 2200-nn account. So **a bill's collected tax is split across the authorities
THAT BILL charged, in proportion to what each was billed on that same bill.**

Three things make it the honest choice rather than a guess, and all three are
asserted in `tests/test_cr060_t7d_allocation_classes.py`:

* **It is per BILL and never across bills.** Each authority's credits are summed
  per invoice out of `journal_lines` — the same rows the billed column is summed
  from — so State's share of WE-1's collected tax is computed from WE-1's own
  **13.87** and nothing else.
* **It is EXACT whenever a bill's tax was met in full**, which is the ordinary
  case and LE-3's signed **20.97**: collected equals billed on that bill, every
  authority receives precisely what it was billed, and the apportionment is the
  identity.
* **It only ever divides money that came in**, so the four authority figures
  always sum to the recorded collected total. A rule that could not guarantee
  that would let a return be filed for more than was received.

⚠ **AND IT ADJUDICATES NOTHING ABOUT PARTIAL PAYMENTS.** `OQ-174` closed
2026-08-12 with *"a partial payment covers TAX FIRST"*; `BR-PAY-010` makes the
within-bill sequence a TENANT SETTING whose shipped default puts tax SECOND. **The
two disagree and this change does not pick a winner** — CR-060 C19's ruled
disposition is that recording the breakdown *"makes the question moot"*, and it
does: whatever order a tenant set is what their money walked, and
`allocation_classes` writes down what it met. **Measured on the signed WE-1
bill: a $150.00 payment collects 0.00 of tax under the shipped order and the
whole 20.97 under tax-first — the same 20.97 spread the question was raised over,
now readable either way instead of refused.**

### Judgment 6 — THE COLLECTED COLUMN IS A FLOOR, AND THE AMOUNT IT OMITS IS PUBLISHED

Three kinds of allocated money carry no class breakdown and are not in the
collected figure: **everything allocated before 2026-09-02** (the breakdown was
computed and kept only in the `audit_log` payload, which is pruned, so it cannot
be backfilled and never will be), and the **application** or **release** of an
account credit, neither of which runs the class walk at all. Computing a
breakdown for those in the ledger would be a second implementation of the class
walk sitting downstream of the first — CR-060 §13's third exclusion.

So the amount travels on the response as `allocated_without_breakdown` and
`collected_tax_omits_allocations_with_no_class_breakdown` names it. **A return
filed on this figure under-remits rather than over-remits**, which is the
direction to be wrong in.

**The old refusal is RETIRED, not reworded**, as C19 requires in as many words:
`tax_inside_a_cleared_payment_is_not_derivable` described a limit that no longer
holds, and a reworded version would leave a screen telling a finance officer the
figure cannot be produced beside the column that produced it.

### What none of this touched

**No ❄️ frozen figure moved and B4/B5 were not opened.** LE-1's signed **598.69**,
LE-3's **20.97** and **47.38**, LE-11's **51,902.50**, GT-17's water **39.50** and
sewer **15.80**, GT-15's solar **40.00** and battery **24.00** are all unmoved;
`G61` reads 130 frozen money figures unchanged, the golden harness reads **33
PASS / 0 FAIL** on both sides of this work, and the ENGINE-VERIFIED record is
**14 of 61 GTs** at both ends — both numbers, because they do different jobs
(`DEF-2846`). CR-060 task T20's per-change run for T7b, T7d and T7f is that
evidence.

## 2026-09-03 · THE BELL HAS ONE STORE AND THREE DEAD LINKS FEWER (`DEF-3422`)

**What the Product Owner reported, verbatim (2026-09-02):** *"this says - staff
notification - but we dont get any notification"*, with the bell reading **"You're
all caught up."** That sentence was accurate, and on 2026-09-02 it always would be.

**Three links were dead at once, and each one looked fine on its own.** That is
why nobody found it by reading code: every file in the chain was correct, tested
and honest about itself.

| link | what was there | what was missing |
|---|---|---|
| the alert | `apps/tenancy/sample_data.py` resolved `notifications.services.queue_staff_alert` by name on every short provisioning run | the function was never written, so the resolve returned `None` and the run's own audit row recorded *"support_alert: not delivered"* |
| the store | `bell_events`, with an index, and `core/bell.py::notify()` calling itself *"the only sanctioned writer"* | no registered sink, **no caller anywhere outside its own test**, and no reader |
| the delivery | a celery-beat schedule firing every five minutes | `NOTIFICATIONS_DISPATCH_TENANTS` is unset on every deployment, so every firing paced **nobody** and said so in a log nobody reads |

### Judgment 1 — the staff alert goes through the ONE path that already delivers

`apps.notifications.services.queue_staff_alert` is published, and it is a thin,
non-raising, savepointed wrapper over `bulk_summary.queue_bulk_summary` — the same
function a finished bill run and a reconciliation run already use. It gets the
ruled audience for free (BR-NOT-021: the person who started it, plus every active
System Admin, because an alert is a failure by definition), one message per run
(BR-NOT-020), the database's own idempotency on the run's id (rule 6), and the
ordinary dispatch cycle (BR-NOT-005 — nothing is sent inline).

**Worked figure, from the acceptance test on real PostgreSQL:** a tenant is
provisioned with its `assets` seeder unwired. Twelve of eighteen sample blocks
therefore come up short — with no meters the opening reads fail validation, so no
bill is raised and no payment matched. The tenant still opens (C-15 is SOFT), and
the System Admin's bell reads **"Sample data setup finished. 18 processed · 12
failed"**. It is ONE message in FOUR inboxes on the multi-admin case, from ONE
queue row.

**What the alert does NOT carry:** the names of the parts that did not load. They
are module keys and reason codes (`assets: seam_not_wired`), the setup screen
already lists every one of them in a clerk's words, and B14 rule 32 with DEF-2377
settled what a person should be reading. The bell says what happened and how many.

### Judgment 2 — `bell_events` and `core/bell.py` are REMOVED, not wired

**This overturns the lane's own opening diagnosis, and the reason is worth
keeping.** The plan was to register the in-app channel as `core.bell`'s missing
sink. Two things found in verification make that wrong:

* **`notify()` has no production caller.** `grep -rn "core.bell\|from core import
  bell" 06-backend --include=*.py` returns `06-backend/tests/` and nothing else.
  Registering a sink would have made `bell_events` a table something *could* write
  and nothing *does* — the same defect one step later, wearing a fix.
* **A sink could not have written the inbox anyway.** `InAppMessage.outbound_message`
  is a NOT NULL in-module foreign key to the queue row, and `in_app.py`'s own
  docstring forbids a second send path (BR-NOT-005). The only lawful door is
  `services.queue_document`, which is the door judgment 1 uses.

So the choice was a second feed or no second feed. The bell already HAS a store —
`outbound_messages` (what the platform undertook to send) and `in_app_messages`
(what a person received, and whether they have looked) — carrying tenant scoping,
read state, a ruled audience, a settings screen, an API and the screen that renders
it. A second table behind one bell is **two answers to "what is in my bell"**, and
the one with no writer, no reader and no caller is the one that went.
`g74_unread_tables_baseline.txt` loses its `BellEvent` line, which is how that
ratchet holds a gain: three tables nothing touches, now two.

**BR-SHL-026 is NOT repealed and nothing was renumbered.** Its five events —
billing run result, payment failure, approvals waiting, import results,
integration broken — say what the bell SHOWS, never where it is kept, and they
were never enforced by the deleted module in any case, because nothing called it.
Of the five, **one has a trigger in this product today** (billing run, wired by
CR-048); the other four have no trigger anywhere in this codebase. **The count is
stated here because it was not stated anywhere before**, and it belongs in
BR-SHL-026's own row, where it now is. ⚠ It is NOT covered by `OQ-262`: that
question is about three of CR-009's **SET-12** staff events (hi-usage alert, SLA
breach, daily digest), which are a different five from the bell's five. Same
shape, different list — and mistaking one for the other is the kind of citation
this repo has already been bitten by.

### Judgment 3 — an unconfigured deployment now paces every live utility

`apps/notifications/schedule.py` could not ask who the tenants were: B1 and
BR-TEN-013 forbid it reading `tenancy.Tenant`, and tenancy published no
*"every live tenant"* read. Its own exception note named the one function that
would change when one existed. `apps.tenancy.selectors.live_tenant_subdomains`
is that read — a platform read on the RLS-exempt `tenants` table, the same
posture as `tenant_id_for_subdomain`, resolved BY NAME at call time — and
`scheduled_subdomains()` falls back to it when the environment variable is unset.

**Hard-won law 3: the unsafe option must be the one you type.** Pacing nobody was
the default, and it failed silently. An operator who names a subset still gets
exactly that subset; nothing they configured changes.

⚠ **Hard-won law 4 applies to the other half of this and is stated rather than
implied:** no `.env` on any running host needs editing for this, because the fix
is what happens when the variable is ABSENT. A host that already sets
`NOTIFICATIONS_DISPATCH_TENANTS` keeps its list and is unaffected.

### What none of this touched

No money path, no ❄️ frozen figure, no rating rule, no ledger posting. The one 🔒
sensitive file is the migration that drops the table (migration ordering), flagged
`HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` with its row in `09-human-review-ledger.md`. No open
question was answered by choosing a value and none was minted: the recipient
question (`OQ-261`) was closed on 2026-08-17 and this work implements that ruling
rather than reopening it.

## 2026-09-03 · TD-16 AND THE BELL: A RENDERED BODY IS NOT PROSE LEAKING OUT OF THE SERVER (`DEF-3422`, follow-on)

**Written down because the next agent will read it as a breach and it is not.**
TD-16 is one of this repo's oldest contracts: *the server sends a message key and
its params, and the UI renders the language.* The bell writer deleted on
2026-09-03 was built to it, and its item carried `summary_key` + `params`. What
the bell actually shows is a **rendered subject and body**, and a lane arriving
at that fact cold would file a defect.

**The distinction is who wrote the words.**

* **Product copy is a KEY, always.** Everything the bell says in its own voice —
  its title, *"You're all caught up."*, *"Mark all read"* — is
  `shell.bell.*` in eleven catalogues, and this work did not move one of them.
* **A message's wording is the UTILITY'S**, edited by a System Admin on
  Settings → Templates, versioned, published and audited (`staff_bulk_summary`).
  It is tenant DATA. No locale catalogue could hold it, because it does not
  exist until a tenant writes it — and shipping a key for it would mean the
  platform choosing words a utility has already chosen for itself.

So the two mechanisms were never the same shape: `core.bell` composed a feed the
PRODUCT wrote, and the feed that exists is composed by the TENANT. That is a
second, independent reason the two could not have been merged — beyond the two
already recorded (nothing called `notify()`, and `InAppMessage.outbound_message`
is a NOT NULL key to a queue row).

**Worked example, from the acceptance test:** the body a System Admin reads is
`"Sample data setup finished.\n\n18 processed · 12 failed\n09/03/2026"`. Every
token in it — `{operation}`, `{total_count}`, `{failed_count}`, `{finished_at}`
— comes from the caller; the sentence around them is the tenant's, and a tenant
that rewrites it in Spanish gets it in Spanish without this repo shipping a key.
`{failed_count}` is the one they cannot remove (`mandatory_content`), which is
BR-NOT-020's binding half enforced at save rather than trusted to a comment.

**What this closes:** nothing was decided here that was not already true. The
value is that it is now written where a lane will look, instead of being
rediscovered as a suspected breach of a signed contract.

## 2026-09-03 · ONE FIXTURE DEFECT, FILED SEVEN TIMES: THE `BR-CUS-1024` SWEEP, AND THE SHAPE THAT ENDS IT

**Written down because the aggregate never existed anywhere, and the aggregate is
the finding.** `BR-CUS-1024` landed on 2026-09-01 — PO verbatim, *"Without
identifier we cannot create Customer ID or master account ot regular account"* —
and it is correct, signed, 🔒 and untouched by any of this. What it reversed is
what a TEST FIXTURE may build: a payload carrying `contact.full_name` and no
`customer` block opened an account until that morning and has raised
`BIZ-COMPLETENESS` ever since, **in SETUP, before a single assertion of the file
it takes down runs.**

### The pattern, which is worth more than any of the seven rows

| row | filed | counted | file |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEF-2585` | 2026-09-01 | 3 | the rule's own landing commit, two suites |
| `DEF-2398` | 2026-09-01 | 2 | the accounts import suite — 0 of 3 accounts created |
| `DEF-3157` | 2026-09-02 | 2 | two collection-ladder master-account cases |
| `DEF-3220` | 2026-09-02 | 17 | every close-out case, through a shared W7 fixture |
| `DEF-2392` | 2026-09-02 | 16 | a move-out file, one case `isolation`-marked |
| `DEF-3343` | 2026-09-02 | 12 | two billing suites, hidden under `DEF-3086`'s first cause |
| `DEF-2343` | 2026-09-03 | 17 | the deposit carry-forward suite |

**Five lanes, seven rows, one defect.** Every one was filed honestly: each lane
ran the file in front of it, measured what it saw, and wrote down a number that
was true of that file. **Nobody was in a position to add them up**, and nothing
in the repository would have done it for them — every row's `escape_reason` says
the same sentence in different words: *nothing on the branch runs the files that
share a fixture together.* `DEF-3220` says it most plainly, having already been
the second count of the same cause: *"the reason the count kept growing is that
nobody had."*

⚠ **THIS REPO HAS SEEN THIS EXACT SHAPE BEFORE AND WROTE IT DOWN, WHICH IS THE
REASON TO WRITE IT DOWN AGAIN.** `10-scripts/gates/surface_debt.txt` opens with
it, about a different subject: *"Every lane was honest; nothing added the honest
notes up."* That was `DEF-112` — stories deferred one at a time until a whole
month-close journey had nothing to click. Same mechanism, three weeks apart, in a
register instead of a trailer: **an aggregate nobody owns does not exist**, and
honesty per item is not a substitute for one number somewhere.

⚠ **THE COSTLIEST PART IS NOT THE RED TESTS — IT IS THAT EACH ROW LOOKED SMALL.**
Two tests is a tidy-up. Eighty is a blocked branch. Filed one file at a time, a
branch-blocking defect presented seven times as somebody else's small chore, and
`DEF-2343` and `DEF-2392` each say in writing that they are *filed, not fixed*
because the canonical shape belonged to another row. Two rows deferring to each
other is how a defect stays open for three days with five people knowing about it.

### What was measured, and by whom

**The number in the task that started this was 80 red tests across 24 files,
measured by another lane. It is measured again here and it is SIX TIMES that.**

Both runs are the same 58 suites — every test file that can reach an account
door, computed as the transitive closure of the fixtures that open one — on real
`pytest`, `JOBS_EAGER=false`:

| | tests | failed | of those, `BR-CUS-1024` | files with identity failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **before**, at tip `5da4c02c` | 969 | **497** | **471** | **47** |
| **after**, at `e1b0fa5d` | 978 | 90 | **0** | **0** |

**471, not 80, and across 47 files, not 24** — and the reason the earlier count
was low is the reason this row exists: it was taken from the files somebody had
run, and nobody had run them together. The largest single casualty,
`test_def_708_the_fee_is_a_real_charge.py` at **29 tests**, is named in none of
the seven rows.

⚠ **AND THE WALL WAS HIDING NINETY OTHER RED TESTS, WHICH IS THE SECOND FINDING
AND MAY BE THE MORE EXPENSIVE ONE.** A test that dies in setup reports the FIRST
exception and nothing else, so for three days 471 refusals stood in front of
whatever those cases would have said next. With the refusal gone, **90 failures
across 23 files** are visible, and they are not identity — they are ordinary
product breakage that had no way to be seen:

  * **15** `TypeError: deposit_interest_accrued() missing 1 required positional
    argument: 'as_of'` at `apps/customers/transfers.py:684`. The caller was
    written on 2026-09-01; the argument was added to
    `selectors.deposit_interest_accrued` on **2026-09-03, in `fbe971d1`, today**,
    and the property-sale path has been broken since. Fifteen tests would have
    caught it on the commit that caused it, and every one of them was already red.
  * **15** `core.errors.NotFoundError` — twelve of them at
    `apps/customers/discounts.py:864`, the whole deposit carry-forward family.
  * **9** `AttributeError: module 'apps.customers.transfers' has no attribute
    'set_target_unit'`.
  * **7** in `test_cr030_w0_customer_no.py`, and those are a THIRD kind again:
    the suite asserts that `link_customer` mints `C-00001` from a display name
    and a legacy reference, which is what `BR-CUS-1023` stopped being true.
    **That is a test asserting a superseded rule and it is filed rather than
    rewritten** — the rule is right and re-stating seven numbering cases is the
    rule owner's judgment, not a fixture repair.

All ninety are recorded in ONE register row (`DEF-3541`) rather than
twenty-three, which is the whole point of this entry. The aggregate itself is
`DEF-3540`.

### The shape, and it is copied rather than invented

`06-backend/tests/identity_fixtures.py` — one file, imported by every repaired
suite. A person is identified by a `555-` phone, a company by `99-0001234`, which
is **exactly what `apps/customers/sample_data._customer_block` already writes**
and was already ruled on 2026-09-01 (*THE DEMO FIXTURE'S PEOPLE KEEP THEIR
CUSTOMER NUMBERS, AND NOTHING WAS INVENTED TO DO IT*). One rule applied twice,
not two lanes each deciding for themselves — which is the whole content of the
question `DEF-2392` left open.

**WHY A PHONE AND NOT A SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER, because that choice is the
safety property.** `BR-CUS-1023` accepts a phone as enough to MINT a number.
`BR-CUS-1024` does **not** accept one as enough to REUSE somebody else's — its
matching test is the name plus a GOVERNMENT-grade identifier — and `BR-CUS-089`
does not accept one as enough to move MONEY. So twenty-nine suites can share one
constant and none of them can take another's customer number, record a tier, or
let **$0.00** of anybody's deposit follow it. `tests/test_identity_fixtures_shape.py`
asserts all three of those, so the day one stops being true the suite goes red
instead of quietly becoming a different test.

⚠ **A COMPANY IS THE OTHER CASE AND IT IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND.**
For a company the reuse test IS the name plus the Tax ID, and `tier_for` calls
that pair **strong**. Two company fixtures presenting the same display name in
one tenant therefore share a customer row — by the rule, not by accident. No
repaired file does that today; a lane adding a second must give it its own name
or its own `tax_id=`.

### The one file repaired the other way, and the prediction that was wrong

`test_cr030_w0_customer_no.py` is the customer-NUMBERING suite, and its fixture
now presents NO party — `BR-CUS-1024`'s own third row, the PO's, the one that
keeps *"a service request that opens an account for a party named elsewhere"*
working. Every case in the file names its party on the very next line with an
explicit `link_customer`, which is the thing the file tests, and nothing in it
ever read the contact that was dropped.

⚠ **THE REASON GIVEN FOR THAT CHOICE WAS RIGHT AND INCOMPLETE, AND THE
MEASUREMENT IS WHAT SHOWED IT.** The reasoning written into the file was: giving
the fixture an identity mints a customer at the door, so the `link_customer` on
the next line hands out **C-00002** and `test_w0_tc1`'s *"the first customer a
tenant ever creates is C-00001"* would have to be edited to stay green — and a
fixture may change while the figure it pins may not. That is still true. What it
missed is that **the file is stale on a second, deeper count**: `link_customer`
with a display name and a legacy reference no longer mints ANY number, because
`BR-CUS-1023` requires a kind and an identifier too. So all seven cases are red
either way, now reading `assert None == 'C-00001'` instead of a refusal in setup.

**That is a test asserting a superseded rule, and it is FILED rather than
rewritten.** Re-stating seven numbering cases against `BR-CUS-1023` is a judgment
about what the suite should assert, and it belongs to the lane that owns the
rule — not to a fixture sweep. The repair is kept anyway, because it removes the
first of two causes and leaves the failure pointing at the real one, which is
`DEF-3343`'s lesson applied in advance rather than after the fact.

### What was NOT touched, and why each one was left

* **`BR-CUS-1024` itself, and every rule it cites.** Not one character. A test
  that asserts the old behaviour is a wrong test, not a wrong rule.
* **No test was skipped, quarantined or marked, and no assertion was weakened.**
  The whole sweep is 306 insertions and 3 deletions across 30
  files; the 3 deletions are the contact line above and two lines of a CSV
  fixture re-emitted with two new columns.
* **`test_def2480_account_snapshot_budget.py`** opens its account with no party
  at all, so it was already lawful and is untouched — which is fortunate, because
  it carries `ACCOUNT_OPEN_QUERY_BUDGET = 50` and giving it an identity would have
  added the customer write to a measured per-row query budget. That is a figure
  question, not a fixture question.
* **The version literal.** No product code changed, and two lanes are mid-flight
  on `07-frontend/package.json` today — the same reason the CHANGELOG's unreleased
  entry gives for not moving it.

## 2026-09-03 · CR-069's design document may be renumbered, because its ids are already taken

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"You can change the numbers - And here is the problem. Its
identifiers are already taken:"* — said in reply to being shown that the Integration
Substrate design document numbers its own stories and rules from 1, and that the repo
already holds different, real rules and stories at those numbers.

**What was shown to the PO, in plain English with the figures.** The design document
drafts thirty-six business rules as `BR-INT-001`–`BR-INT-036` and thirty-four user
stories as `US-INT-001`–`US-INT-034`. This repository already holds `BR-INT-001`–`017`
and `US-INT-001`–`012`, describing **different things**, cited from
`04-docs/01-spec/11-api-contracts.md`, `01-screen-inventory.md`,
`04-docs/02-decisions/03-tenancy-and-security.md` and `12-engineering-plan.md`. So
**seventeen rule ids and twelve story ids in the new document point at rules and stories
that already exist and say something else.** On the integrations module that lands on
bank imports and payment webhooks — a rule citation pointing at the wrong rule, on a
money path. The PO was told this is the same shape as `DEF-2820`, where `OQ-1166` read as
`OQ-116` for two days from a rating-math file.

### The ruling, applied — the renumbering map

**The existing ids do not move. The document's do.** Nothing in the repository is
renumbered, so no citation anywhere breaks; the new material starts above the live
frontier.

| Family | The document says | It becomes | Live frontier verified 2026-09-03 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Business rules | `BR-INT-001`–`BR-INT-036` | **`BR-INT-018`–`BR-INT-053`** | `BR-INT-017` |
| User stories | `US-INT-001`–`US-INT-034` | **`US-INT-013`–`US-INT-046`** | `US-INT-012` |
| Epics | numbered from 1 in the document | **`EP-INT-05`** onward | `EP-INT-04` |

**The offset is +17 for rules, +12 for stories.** Both are simple addition and that is
deliberate — a mapping a reader can do in their head is one they will not get wrong, and
a table of thirty-six arbitrary reassignments is a table somebody transcribes badly.

⚠ **THE SPELLING DOES NOT CHANGE.** `BR-INT-` and `US-INT-` are zero-padded to three in
this repository already, and that series **carries citations**, so the padding stays —
`BR-INT-018`, never `BR-INT-18` and never `BR-INT-00018`. Law 11's ban is on re-padding a
series that already has citations, and the five-digit rule of 2026-08-31 is a **ceiling,
not a spelling**.

⚠ **AND THE DOCUMENT'S OWN `C1`–`C36` HANDLES ARE NOT AFFECTED AND ARE NOT MINTED.** They
stay exactly as written, the way `CR-068` keeps `CP-`, so every reference back into the
source document still resolves. `CR-069` §11 already says so.

### What is still owed on that document, and it is not a numbering question

The document could not be read in full. It is **32.8 MB**, and the Drive download path
refuses anything over **10 MB**, so the text-extraction route was the only one available
and it **stopped at about page 106, mid-sentence**, inside a per-connector questionnaire.
What was extracted — 222,353 characters, 37,423 words — does contain the thirty-four
stories, the thirty-six rules, five `CREATE TABLE` statements for the five tables, and
endpoint, screen and test-case material. **It is not the whole document.**

**Two of `CR-069`'s claims were verified against the code while reading it, and both
hold:** `06-backend/apps/integrations/` is **11 lines** across `models.py` and
`tests.py`, and none of `integration_connection`, `integration_credential`,
`integration_run`, `integration_target_reference` or `integration_consent` appears
anywhere in the backend or in the contracts. **There is no legacy to unpick.**

**The PO was asked to re-export the file under 10 MB** — it is mostly images — or to
split it. Until then no lane should treat the extracted text as the complete
specification, and this row is the record of why.
