## 2026-09-07 · CR-075 WAVES G AND H — THE COVERAGE GRID, AND THE WORK LIST THE ENGINE FILLS

**`US-RBS-005` · `US-RBS-006` · `RB-124` · `RBS-006-R24` · `RBS-007`. Version `2.217.0`.**

### WHAT A CLERK CAN NOW SEE, IN FIGURES OFF THE RUNNING PRODUCT

On the seeded utility, in Chromium, signed in as a billing clerk:

* the coverage grid reads **1 clean · 0 estimated · 2 refused over 3 cells**, and the sentence under it
  reads ***All 3 plan and cycle combinations were priced. Left out: 32 sample.***
* **pressing a cell opens that account's own test bill** — `…/runbooks/test_bill/runs/01a079fb-74dd-…`,
  a real frozen result, not a string that looks like an address;
* the work list holds **6 items** — three from *Can we bill?* that block billing, two from the coverage
  grid (the two accounts that refused), one before go-live — and **pressing Resolve takes a row out of
  the open list**.

⚠ **THREE CELLS AND NOT TWENTY-FIVE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE FIXTURE RATHER THAN THE RUNBOOK.**
`US-RBS-005`'s **21 clean · 2 estimated · 2 refused** is written against the six-service fixture its own
§4 describes — *Electric · Water · Gas · Trash · Storm water · Broadband, 40 accounts* — and **that
fixture does not exist in this repository**. The demo utility holds three plan-and-cycle combinations
among its accounts, so the grid draws three cells and says so. The number on the card is not wrong; it
is a claim about an estate nobody has seeded, and the grid's own sentence is what makes the difference
readable instead of invisible.

### THE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE, WHERE THE DOCUMENTS RAN OUT

**J1 · EACH CELL IS A REAL CHILD RUN OF RUNBOOK 23, WITH `parent_run` SET.** `RB-124`'s step 2 reads
*"Runbook 23 on each cell"* and this takes it literally: `open_run` → `execute` → `close_run`, once per
cell. Three things follow and each is why. The cell's refusal sentence **is** runbook 23's, lifted out
of the child's own frozen `sentence` block, so the words on a red cell and the words on the screen that
cell opens cannot differ — which is exactly what `TC-RBS-005.4` asks (*a refusal composed by this module
would not change when the rate did*). The cell has somewhere to open, and `RecordGrid` **cannot express
a cell without a destination**. And there is one implementation of pricing: runbook 23 already calls
`billing.runs.price_account`, so nothing here prices anything.
⚠ **THE COST, STATED: a grid of 25 writes 25 extra `runbook_runs` rows.** They carry `parent_run` —
the column that exists for exactly this and that wave `I4` uses for `requires` — and **run history
(`RBS-008`) does not filter on it yet**, so a tenant running the grid daily sees 25 test-bill rows a day
in that list. Recorded here rather than left for a reader to discover.

**J2 · THE PICK IS A PURE FUNCTION, SORTED BY THE PLAN'S NAME.** The three axes are the unit's rate
plan, the services it takes and the cycles that read it; the representative is the first account by
number; the reading order is by WORDS, because a reader who asks *why is that cell first* deserves an
answer and a uuid is not one. Two runs over an unchanged estate therefore produce the same cells in the
same order, which is what `runbook_runs.scope_fingerprint` digests.

**J3 · WHAT THE PICK LEFT OUT IS A SENTENCE, EVERY TIME.** Combinations found, cells drawn, and the
accounts excluded with their reason. A silent `LIMIT 25` is hard-won law 7's *reporting zero over a
scope it silently excludes*, and on the demo estate the sentence is the only thing that says **32
accounts were left out as sample data**.

**J4 · A MASTER ACCOUNT IS NOT A CELL AND IS COUNTED RATHER THAN DROPPED** (`BR-CUS-1010` — it names a
premises and no unit, so it has no plan, no service mix and no cycle to sit in).

**J5 · *ESTIMATED* IS THE GATHER'S OWN FLAG AND THE CARD'S *OR DEFAULTED* IS NOT BUILT.** Nothing in
`billing.contracts` records that a quantity was DEFAULTED rather than read or estimated, so a cell
claiming to detect one would report a fact this product does not hold.

**J6 · THE PERIOD DEFAULTS TO THE LAST WHOLE CALENDAR MONTH, WHERE `RB-124` SAYS *THE NEXT CYCLE*.** A
period that has not happened has no reads, so a grid over it would be 25 refusals and would prove
nothing about a utility's data — the opposite of what a go-live artefact is for.

**J7 · THE WORK-ITEM FINGERPRINT IS A READABLE STRING AND NOT A DIGEST** —
`<tenant>|<runbook>|<subject>|<kind>`, and **the run id is deliberately not in it**, because with it
every run mints a new row and thirty daily sweeps over one missing read become thirty items instead of
one item thirty days old. It is readable because the `<runbook>|` prefix is what finds *the items THIS
runbook raised* when the run closes the ones that stopped recurring; a digest would need a second
column, and a column is a migration.

**J8 · A RUNBOOK RETURNS FINDINGS AND THE ENGINE WRITES `work_items`** (`BR-RBS-022`, unchanged).
`RunbookDefinition` gains an OPTIONAL `findings()` beside `report()`, handed the same view; a runbook
that raises nothing declares nothing, and the run's `counts` carry `work_items_raised` and
`work_items_closed` so *raised nothing* is visible beside *walked 25* rather than being an absence
nobody can see.

**J9 · THE WORK LIST IS AT `/{tenant}/runbooks/work`, NOT AT THE SHEET'S `operations/work`.**
`/{tenant}/work` belongs to the WORK MODULE — crews, work orders, parts — which is a different thing
with a confusingly similar name, exactly as `models.py` already says of the two tables. So
`operations` → `runbooks`, the same translation the library routes carry. ⚠ **A tenant could name a
runbook *Work*, and this static route would win over `:key`**; nothing reserves the word today and the
failure would be silent, so it is written down.

**J10 · THE AGE COLUMN IS DAYS AND READS *Today* UNDER ONE DAY**, where the sheet's samples include
*3 hours*. Eleven languages' plural rules for an hour count is a translation surface this screen does
not need; the fact it exists to carry is *how many days*.

### FOUR DEFECTS, EACH FILED BEFORE ITS FIX

* **`DEF-RBS-4354`** — the `Records` block's GRID mode handed a cell's tenant-relative route straight to
  `<Link to>`. That is `DEF-RBS-4329` one display mode over, and it had never fired because no runbook
  emitted a grid until now. Every coverage-grid cell would have opened onto nothing.
* **`DEF-RBS-4363`** — one cell whose child run is refused took the **whole grid** down: `open_run`
  carries two deliberate refusals of its own and neither is a database error, so the executor's savepoint
  does not net them. Caught per cell now; the record row counts it and the grid does not draw a cell it
  cannot open.
* **`DEF-RBS-4369`** — the grid draws **zero cells on the demo utility**, because `seed_demo` marks all
  72 of its accounts sample and `BR-RBS-014` correctly excludes them. **The grid was right and the
  fixture was the problem**, and the grid's own refusal — *0 cells over an estate holding 0
  combinations* — is what said so on the first PostgreSQL run.
* **`DEF-RBS-4370`** — a runbook row written by hand carries no `template_key`, and that one absent
  column makes it permanently unrunnable the moment the definition document moves: `open_run` refuses
  over an offer `pending_template_update` cannot compute. Three walkthrough seeds write rows that way.

⚠ **AND ONE THIS LANE CAUSED AND A SIBLING FIXED FIRST — `DEF-RBS-4365`.** A helper named `_person`
added with the work-list selectors **shadowed the module's own `_person` 1,200 lines above it**, so
`GET /runbooks/runs/{id}` answered 500 on every unapproved run and `RBS-006` drew an error frame instead
of the grid. Python redefines a module-level name in silence: no error, no warning, no failing import,
and no linter here reports it. **Eighty-nine backend cases were green over it** — the 15 new ones call
the new helper, the 74 conformance and test-bill ones never touch `run_header` — and **only the browser
could see it**. That is hard-won law 6 word for word. A sibling lane met the same 500 on `RBS-004` and
fixed it as `_owner_name` minutes earlier; this lane's own rename was dropped in favour of theirs,
because two fixes for one defect is worse than either.

### VERSION

`2.217.0` — a change-level bump, allocated with `10-scripts/allocate.py version --bump change` and
re-verified at push time.

## 2026-09-07 · `CR-075` WAVE `M`, SECOND CYCLE — THE GO/NO-GO FOR THE LIVE HALF, RE-TAKEN, AND IT IS STILL `NO-GO`

**Why it was taken again rather than inherited.** Wave `M` ran on 2026-09-06 and returned `NO-GO` on six
findings. In the twenty hours that followed, a wave `N` lane fixed three of them. **A go/no-go is a
statement about the build in front of you**, so the one on the branch this morning was a statement about a
build nobody was shipping any more. The cycle was re-run in full against `642a3cee` — same scripts, same
tenant, a fresh clone of the template built from that commit — and this row is its verdict. The evidence
is `04-docs/05-modules/17-runbooks/15-wave-m-dry-cycle.md` §8; §1–§7 are left exactly as written, because
the value of the document is that the same measurement was taken twice on two different builds.

### WHAT IS BETTER, AND IT IS MOST OF THE FIRST CYCLE'S LIST

`L9`'s board still does not exist in the seed — a firing on a fresh clone before seeding **resolved 31
subjects and planned 0**, all of them guarded sample accounts — so it was rebuilt: **1,004 past-due
accounts** on the real `brazosbend` tenant on top of the **31** already there. Five firings, one per
Monday, 3 to 31 August 2026, started by hand. Firings 1–3 planned **812** notices — 300 reminder · 250
ten-day · 170 five-day · 92 certified final — and firings 4–5 planned **855**, the 43 payment-plan
accounts whose first instalment fell due on 23 August. **62 accounts were guarded and never walked.**
**The database diff was clean on all five**, with `audit_log` moving by exactly the number of acts each
run performed and nothing else outside the seven tables moving at all.

**Proved RED on a real live firing, with nothing patched but the trust ratchet.** The first cycle's proof
had to force the mode and hand the port a template; both patches are deleted rather than made optional, so
a regression would fail this proof instead of hiding in it. **All 812 acts came back `queued`**, not
`held`: `outbound_messages` 337 → **1,961**, `notice_history` 0 → **1,624**, `account_collection_state`
512 → **812**, `audit_log` **+2,948**. Every account climbed **exactly one rung**. A second live firing a
week later queued **720** — everyone but the 92 already at the end of the ladder — and **a third, on the
same business day, queued 0** with nothing written anywhere. So `DEF-RBS-4345`, `DEF-RBS-4347` and
`DEF-RBS-4352` are closed in fact, `DEF-RBS-4343` no longer bites runbook 8, and `L4`'s cap refuses
correctly: 400 against 973 walked gave a `failed` run carrying *planned 973 · cap 400 · pinned 1,035* and
zero records.

### WHY IT IS STILL `NO-GO`, IN ONE SENTENCE

**A clerk cannot read the plan and nobody can approve one.** Phase 2's promise is *a person approves a
plan of a known size*: the size is computed, stored and correct; it is not on the screen; and there is
nothing to press.

* **`DEF-RBS-4387` — `RBS-006` draws the five headline tiles as LABELS WITH NO NUMBERS.** Verbatim from
  the page: `TO SEND` · `SKIPPED` · `NEED A PERSON` · `NOT SET UP` · `FEES DRAFTED`, nothing under any of
  them, and `TOOK 16s` beside them drawing its value perfectly. **The number 812 appears nowhere on the
  screen.** The runbook builds each tile as a bare integer where the block has read a value cell since
  wave `C`. This is condition 1 of the first cycle's `GO` list — *the plan read on screen* — failing for
  the second cycle running, for a different reason.
* **`L3` is still not on the branch.** No approval endpoint, no screen that shows a plan and offers
  approval.
* **`DEF-RBS-4382` — the cap a clerk reads is not the cap that is enforced.** `RB-108` shows *Most per
  run · 400* as an input and it resolves on every run; **nothing reads it.** The engine compares against
  `runbook.cap`, a different field, null until an admin types one — so this cycle walked 973 subjects a
  week against a card that says 400 and nothing was refused. **A cap on the card that nothing enforces is
  worse than no cap, because it is believed.**
* **`DEF-RBS-4388` — 977 record rows in one page, no pager, and the paging endpoint never called.**
  `NFR-3`, on the first runbook with more than a handful of records; about 38,000 rows and 1.4 MB of
  `jsonb` at the 40,000-account ceiling.
* **`DEF-RBS-4386` — *Email, then post* queues BOTH.** One live firing wrote **1,624** queue rows and
  **1,624** notice-history rows for **812** accounts. Whichever reading of the card is right, the wrong
  one costs the postage on 812 letters and a second copy of a legal notice. **Ours to decide and write
  down (law 13), and it must be decided before a live run.**

### THREE THINGS THAT ARE NOT BLOCKERS AND ARE WORTH THE ROW

**`DEF-RBS-4380` — a run's per-record list is emptied by the NEXT run.** After five firings,
`GET /runbooks/runs/{id}/records` returns **0 rows for four of the five runs** while each of those runs'
own frozen report still says **973**. Re-pointing a resumable row at the run that resumed it is
deliberate and documented; that it empties the earlier run is not, and for a collections ladder that list
is the regulator's record. It does not show on screen today only because the screen reads the frozen
report and never asks the endpoint — which is the other half of `DEF-RBS-4388`.

**`DEF-RBS-4381` — the check could not read its own subject, and it is the wave's own tool.**
`DEF-RBS-4352`'s fix made a record row `{id, meta, cells}`; the database diff still read
`row["outcome"]`, concluded every firing had performed **zero acts**, and failed five clean runs against
812 real audit rows. **It failed loudly and that was luck** — the same blindness with the arithmetic
reversed is a green cycle over a blind check. It now reads both shapes and **counts the rows it cannot
read**, printing that number beside the verdict. The same wave's browser check had the mirror fault: it
asserted the tile LABEL, which fails on an upper-cased strip and **passes on a strip with no numbers at
all** — a test named after an assertion it does not make.

**The diff's one blind spot, with its number.** It compares ROW COUNTS, so an `UPDATE` in place is
invisible: the second live firing advanced the tier on **812 rows** of `account_collection_state` and the
count did not move. Stated in the script's docstring with that figure, because a declared blind spot with
no number is indistinguishable from an empty one.

### AND THE SCHEDULER STILL HAS NEVER RUN A RUNBOOK

`I2` and `I3` landed the same day. `scheduler.decide()` correctly makes the ladder due at **2026-09-07
12:00 UTC** for *Mondays 07:00 `America/Chicago`*, and `next_run_at` returns **2026-09-14 12:00 UTC** —
so the machinery is right. **Not one firing in either cycle went through `sweep()`**; a person pressed
Run, five times, twice over. **The plans are soaked and the scheduler is not**, and wave `I` still owes
its own soak. `M4`'s verdict is about the plans, so it is unaffected — but nobody may read either cycle
as evidence that a weekly schedule works.

### WHAT WAS NOT PUT TO THE PRODUCT OWNER, AND WHY

None of the above. Every judgment here is a measurement or a defect; none reverses a signed statement,
moves a ❄️ FROZEN figure, or needs a fact only they hold (hard-won law 13). The one thing that is a
genuine choice — what *Email, then post* means — is recorded as a defect with both readings and their
cost, for the lane that fixes it to settle and write down.

## 2026-09-07 · THE GATE SUITE, TRIAGED — THIRTY-SEVEN STANDING FAILURES, AND WHAT THEY WERE HIDING

The suite read **`82 PASS, 37 FAIL, 2 SKIP`** at the start of this lane, not the
`82 / 31 / 3` the decision log recorded on 2026-09-06. Nobody had moved the
number and nobody had noticed it move. That is the whole argument for this lane:
**thirty-seven standing failures are camouflage**, and hard-won law 7 names the
mechanism — *a true red acquires the protective colouring of a known one*.

### The three piles, and the one that matters

**Gates that were themselves wrong — four, and every one had been green or
comfortably red for weeks.**

`DEF-GOV-4384` is the expensive one. `common._OQ_STATE_RE` skipped asterisks and
whitespace and nothing else, and this register has written a ✅ in front of a
closed state since 2026-08-24. So `✅ **CLOSED 2026-09-06 — the default cap is
100**` parsed to the EMPTY state and **`oq_is_closed()` answered False for 25
questions the Product Owner had actually ruled.** G8's clause D *did* report the
unreadable cell — as one of 35 formatting lines inside a gate that had been red
for weeks — while clause A (*a stub citing a CLOSED question is a stale stub*)
and clause C (*a story still `blocked_by` a CLOSED question*) were switched off
for all 25 without saying so. **That is `DEF-WRK-4030`'s failure with a machine
cause instead of a human one**, and the lesson generalises past the regex: a
parser that returns `''` rather than raising turns every one of its callers into
a false negative at once, silently.

`DEF-GOV-4385` is what fixing it uncovered. G8's clause A skipped a line
beginning `#`, `//` or `*` and called that prose — but this repository's
docstrings QUOTE the stub they replaced, and such a line starts with a warning
sign or a back-tick. **20 of the 32 citations it reported were docstrings**, so
its PASS line overstated its own reach by 167%. It never turned anything red,
which is exactly why it survived, and it became load-bearing the moment the
parser was fixed: three of those docstrings say *the question CLOSED*, so fixing
`4384` alone would have produced three brand-new FALSE failures naming correct
code.

`DEF-INT-4400` — G77 ran `_code_only()`, which BLANKS every string literal, and
only then matched `provider_key ==`. **By the time the pattern ran, the thing
that tells a real branch from an innocent comparison was already gone.** It
refused `one["provider_key"] != provider_key`, which counts how many rows on a
page belong to a different connection.

`DEF-GOV-4405` — grep this repository for `4061` and you get `DEF-GOV-4061` (the
base-is-the-tip check, cited from `CLAUDE.md` itself) and `DEF-WRK-4061`. Two
real rows, one number. **Thirteen numbers are claimed twice and G17 had never
printed a line about any of them**, because it compares id STRINGS and the PO's
ruling of 2026-09-03 makes the NUMBER the running unique thing.

**Real defects the gates had been naming all along, in words that read like
tidying.** `DEF-CWP-4390`: eslint was red on eight files, seven cosmetic and one
a React hook called after an early return — a crash `tsc`, vitest and `vite
build` are all green over. `DEF-WRK-4393`: G43 said *"a searchable list with no
prompt (B14 rule 19)"*, which reads as a copy nit; underneath it was a live
search box over an endpoint that reads `period` and nothing else. **A gate whose
message describes the symptom it can see rather than the damage it implies is a
gate people learn to skim.**

**Stale counts, all in one direction.** G72's sixteen sentences said the
sample-data plant walks eighteen or twenty steps; it walks twenty-one. The same
number is an ASSERTION in `test_po_six_service_tenant_end_to_end.py`
(`EXPECTED_BLOCKS = 18`), and that case is `skipif vendor != postgresql`, so
every default run skips it and the skip reads as green (`DEF-TEN-4404`).

### Judgments this lane made, so the next one does not re-make them

* **A number a gate must not raise, versus a ratchet seeded at what is there.**
  G40's `0 → 3` and G67's `123 → 202` were left alone and filed, because raising
  them is the one move that turns a guard into decoration. G17's new
  number-collision ratchet is seeded at the thirteen shares that exist — that is
  a check being ADDED where there was none, not a bar being lowered, and it can
  only tighten because a carried entry that stops colliding fails the gate.
* **Fix the gate, or fix the code?** Where the code was misleading, the code
  moved: `required_secret` held a field NAME, not a key, so it became
  `required_field_name` — G94 reasons about the name of an interpolated
  expression because nothing can reason about it statically, and a local whose
  name lies to the gate lies to the next lane too.
* **Whose file is it?** Eight failures were left standing on purpose, each with
  a row, because a live lane had the file open. Editing a file another lane owns
  is how `DEF-165` lost a money fix.
* **`DEF-RBS-4284` was closed by this lane and is not this lane's row.** Commit
  `8a76aa6c` says *"DEF-RBS-4284 fixed"* and describes the fix at length while
  the row read `open`, so G55 was blocking on a claim nobody had finished
  recording. The status column is what every other lane reads.

### Two things that happened TO this lane, and both are the same class

The shared register was reset to the branch tip by another lane to keep
in-flight rows out of its own commit. That discarded **ten rows this lane had
filed and two closures**, and *nothing would have told me*: `push_paths.sh`
refuses a line vanishing *measured against the tip*, and an unpushed row is
invisible to that check by construction. I would have pushed a file that no
longer contained my rows, with a correct file count, my own other work intact,
and every check in law 11 passing. **It was found by grepping the register for
the ids I had allocated** — which is now a step worth taking before any push
that touches it.

Then my own repair did the mirror image. Re-deriving the register by splitting
on `\n` and keeping lines whose first field was not a known id appended **ten
continuation lines of rows that were already there**, because a CSV record in
this register is not a line — a quoted `escape_reason` runs to paragraphs. The
push was clean by every check law 11 prescribes: zero deletions, *"nothing
vanished"*, insertions only, my own row present. **All of those are true of a
file that has just been corrupted by ADDITION**, and none of them asks whether
the result still parses. G17 caught it inside a minute, which is the case for
having the ratchet at all. **Parse it, or append to it — never split it.**

### What is left, and why

Twenty-something gates are still red and each now has a dated cause. The largest
are legacy debts no lane can close in a session — G1, G3, G10 and G11 name
between 100 and 1,000 files of missing Lifecycle trailers, checklist letters and
TC-named tests — and the rest are filed against the module that owns them. **The
deliverable was never `37 → 0`; it was that a reader can trust what remains.**

## 2026-09-07 · 🌡 THE WEATHER MORATORIUM IS ASKED AT RUN TIME, FROM A DROPDOWN — `OQ-RBS-1757` CLOSED

**The question.** `RB-112`'s card asks disconnect eligibility to check *"the forecast for the service area today"* against **below 32°F · above 100°F**. Nothing in this product holds a forecast, a temperature, or a regulator's cold-weather calendar. What exists is `customers.AccountProtection` kind `weather_moratorium` — a date window a person enters **per account** — which is checked in step 5 and does remove people. So the area-wide half reported **Not checked** and never the card's green *No*, deliberately: *we looked at the weather and it is fine* and *nobody looked* send a crew to opposite places.

**The ruling, Product Owner, verbatim:** *"when you run this runbook, ask user to check temp range from ddropdown and use that details in logic"*.

**What that settles, and why it is a better answer than either option put to them.** The two options offered were a per-account record (what exists) or an automatic area-wide temperature check (which needs a weather feed this product does not have and a ruling on whose thermometer counts). The PO chose neither: **the person running the runbook states the conditions, from a fixed dropdown, and the logic uses their answer.** It needs no feed, no integration and no new setting; it puts the judgment where the accountability already is, because a named person presses Run and signs the list; and it is auditable — the band chosen is stored on the run with everything else, so *why was nobody disconnected on 7 September* is answerable from the run itself.

**Both halves now run.** The per-account window (step 5) is unchanged and still removes. The area-wide half (step 6) reads the clerk's answer and, when the band is a moratorium band, holds the whole run. The tile can now say a true *No* — because somebody looked.

**Three bands, from the card's own thresholds:** below 32°F · between 32°F and 100°F · above 100°F. The thresholds are the card's and are not invented here; what is new is only who supplies today's reading.

**Required, with no default.** This runbook is manual-trigger only, so there is always a person to ask, and a default would be a plausible wrong answer — the exact failure `TenantRegional` records, where an unset regional format silently became `MM/DD/YYYY` for weeks. A clerk who has not looked out of the window must say so rather than have the run assume a mild day.

## 2026-09-07 · 🔗 LINKS BY DEFAULT, DIRECT UPDATES BEHIND *APPROVE ALL* — `OQ-RBS-1760` CLOSED, AND IT IS A PATTERN RATHER THAN ONE RUNBOOK'S ANSWER

**The question.** Runbook 33, *Budget billing re-level*, finds that four of twelve enrolled accounts are drifting and their monthly level should move — and nothing in the product can move one. No port does it, so the runbook records the refusal with both figures and holds the customer's letter too, because telling somebody their payment is changing when nothing can change it is worse than saying nothing.

**The ruling, Product Owner, verbatim:** *"most fo the time we give links to Clark to change - or you can ask approve all button to clark - in such case you can make the direct udpates"*.

**What it settles.** Both, and in a stated order:

1. **The default is a LINK.** Each row carries a route to the screen where a person makes the change themselves. That is what most runbooks should do most of the time, and it needs no new port — `BR-RBS-011` already requires every finding to name its fix route, so the default costs nothing new.
2. **An *Approve all* button unlocks the direct update.** When the clerk presses it, the runbook may write. This is not a weakening of the second-person rule — **it IS the second person**, made once over a named list of known size rather than once per row.

⚠ **WHY THIS IS RECORDED AS A GENERAL PATTERN AND NOT AS RUNBOOK 33's ANSWER.** The question was asked about budget levels and the answer describes a shape every Action in this catalogue can take. It resolves the standing tension between *a runbook that only reports is safe but saves nobody any typing* and *a runbook that writes is useful but frightening*: the link is always there, the button is the consent, and the size of what is being consented to is on the screen before it is pressed. It also means a runbook whose port does not exist yet is still USEFUL on the day it ships — it links — rather than being held back until someone builds a writer.

**What it costs runbook 33 specifically:** the four rows gain their link to the budget-billing screen now, and the direct update stays refused until a budget-level port exists — which is a reviewed interface, not a line a lane writes on the way past. The hold on the customer's letter stands until then, for the reason already recorded.

⚠ **AND IT DOES NOT WIDEN THE MONEY RULE.** *Approve all* is the second person for the ACT; nothing here touches CLAUDE.md hard rule 4's immutability of issued invoices, payments and journal lines, and nothing here lets a runbook reach a writer it does not hold.

## 2026-09-07 · 🅿 SIX RUNBOOKS ARE PARKED BY THE PRODUCT OWNER, AND `CR-075`'s BUILDABLE SCOPE IS CLOSED AT 28 OF 34

**The ruling, verbatim:** *"Please park those runbook - we will handle them later … I will give you full list what needs to be done, they are not yet design"*.

**Which six:** runbook 29 *overdue field orders* · 30 *portal and autopay adoption* · 31 *revenue at risk and aging trend* · 32 *flight results landed* · 34 *storm mass send* · 35 *service request chase*. Each has a number, a home, and one sentence saying what done looks like. Scope, parameters, steps, guards, ports and both screens are undefined, and **nothing has been inferred to fill the gap**.

**Why this is a ruling worth writing down rather than a lull.** The six cards each carried the sentence *"A card like the ones above is the next act."* That is true, and it reads to a lane as an invitation. It is not one: the PO has said the list is coming from them. Three of the six would **send messages to customers** if they turned out to be Actions — who they write to, what they say and when they fire are facts only the utility holds. A lane inferring them would be writing the customer's requirement on the customer's behalf, which the change process names exactly: *when it is ambiguous it is a DEFECT, not a change, because filing our misunderstanding as a "change" quietly converts our error into the customer's new requirement.*

⚠ **THE PARKING IS THE ANSWER, SO NO OPEN QUESTION IS MINTED FOR THEM.** A lane landing on one of these cards should do NOTHING — not write the card, not mint a question, not build a stub. All six cards now carry that instruction inline, because the card is what a lane actually reads (`DEF-WRK-4030`: a register's STATUS is authoritative and its BODY is what misleads).

**What this closes.** `CR-075`'s buildable scope ends at **28 of 34 runbooks — 15 Checks and 13 Actions**, all registered, constructing and walked. The remaining six are not late, not blocked and not owed by engineering; they are un-specified by design and will arrive as a list.

**What it does NOT close.** Phase 2 still holds its own `NO-GO` from wave `M` — a clerk cannot read a plan or approve one — and wave `O` still has no trigger because integrations emits no *batch landed* event. Both are engineering's, both are recorded elsewhere, and neither is affected by this parking.

## 2026-09-07 — DEF-PAY-4409: A RECEIPT THAT SAID NOTHING, AND THE THREE JUDGMENTS BEHIND MAKING IT SAY SOMETHING

**What the Product Owner saw.** They opened a waiting receipt on Settings →
Notifications → Messages needing attention and read a complete, well-formed
email in which **every single value was an em-dash**:

    Hi ——,
    Thank you — we have received your payment.
    Amount ——   Date ——   Method ——   Confirmation ——   Applied to ——
    Balance before this payment ——
    Balance after this payment ——

Their words: *"email doe snot show the values they are not resolved"*.

**What was wrong, and it was not what it looked like.** Nothing was broken. The
seeded body is right; the renderer is right and is doing exactly what `OQ-117`
ratified — a catalogued token with no value prints a NAMED ABSENCE rather than
an invented figure, *"because the customer needs the rest of it"*. What was
missing was the caller's half: `apps/payments/receipts.py` never passed a
`render_context` and had no parameter for one, while two siblings calling the
same function pass one and work (`apps/billing/delivery_seam.py`,
`apps/payments/notices.py`). Every check in this repo was green over it,
truthfully.

**THREE JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT. Each is recorded because the next
lane cannot infer any of them from what is written elsewhere.**

**(1) THE DATE ON A RECEIPT IS THE POSTING DATE, NOT THE CLEARING DATE.** A
payment carries both (`BR-PAY-021`). A cheque handed over on the 31st and
cleared on the 3rd has two defensible dates and the receipt has one line. It
prints `posted_at`, because that column is NOT NULL, is entered by the person
who took the money (`BR-PAY-033`), is the date the transaction is judged
on-time by, and is the date the customer wrote on the cheque — the only one
they can check against their own record. `cleared_at` is a fact about the bank
and is nullable, so a processing payment would print an absence for a receipt
the customer is holding.

**(2) `{first_name}` IS THE FIRST WORD OF THE CONTACT'S ONE NAME FIELD.**
`customers.contacts` holds a single `full_name` and no given-name column, and
A13's greeting is `Hi {first_name},`. The alternative — printing the whole name
— is never wrong but reads as a form letter, which is the opposite of this
product's voice. **What this gets wrong, said out loud:** a contact recorded
surname-first is greeted by surname. That is a real cost, it is bounded to the
greeting line, and closing it properly means a second name column on
`contacts`, which is a customers-module change and not this lane's.

**(3) BOTH BALANCES COME FROM THE LEDGER, AND ONE OF THEM IS ARITHMETIC.**
`ledger.reporting.ar_positions` is read AFTER the payment posts and inside the
same transaction, so it IS the balance after. The balance before is
`after + what met a bill` — and that is exact rather than approximate, because
`ledger_seam.post_payment_cleared` credits AR with the applied figure ALONE
(credit carried and a deposit held go to their own accounts) and REFUSES a
posting whose legs do not foot to the payment. `accounts.balance` is not read:
`BR-CUS-015` says it is a cache nothing writes, and serving it once told a
customer owing $108.88 that their balance was zero (`DEF-127`).

**THE WORKED FIGURE, MEASURED IN A BROWSER ON THE SEEDED UTILITY.** Grace
Gagnon, account `AC-2026-00007`, owed **$157.50**. A $100.00 cheque, number
8842, recorded on Brazos Bend's own Record payments screen, met bill
`BL-2608-000058` in full. Her receipt now reads **Amount 100.00 USD · Date
09/07/2026 · Method Check · Confirmation 8842 · Applied to BL-2608-000058 ·
Balance before this payment 157.50 USD · Balance after this payment 57.50
USD**, and the SMS beside it reads *"Brazos Bend Utilities: thanks, we received
100.00 USD. Confirmation 8842. Your balance is now 57.50 USD."* Before this
change every one of those was `——`.

**A FOURTH DECISION, ABOUT THE GUARD RATHER THAN THE RECEIPT: A CALLER STATES
EVERY TOKEN ITS DOCUMENT CAN CARRY, INCLUDING THE ONES IT HAS NO VALUE FOR.**
`queue_document` now REPORTS the merge fields a caller never named. It cannot
tell a figure nobody had from a figure nobody remembered unless the caller says
which — so the convention is that a key present with no value MEANS *this
document genuinely has none* (a cash payment's confirmation number; a payment
that met no bill), and a key that is simply absent means the caller forgot. It
costs a caller one `None`.

**IT REPORTS AND IT NEVER REFUSES, AND THAT IS THE RULING.** A refusal would
fail the queue write, and a queue write is reached from inside a bill run
(`BR-BIL-055`), a money transaction and a committed move-out. Turning *this
letter will have a blank line on it* into *this bill run died* is a worse
defect than the one being fixed. **What it will find:** every seeded body in
this product declares caller-supplied tokens — `email_bill_ready` eleven,
`email_payment_receipt` eight, the three disconnect notices six or seven each —
so the report will name real gaps on other paths as they are queued. That is
the point, and each is somebody's story rather than this lane's to fix.

**AND ONE DEFECT THIS FIX EXPOSED, FILED AS `DEF-NOT-4413` AND FIXED HERE.**
Giving receipts a stored context put money and dates on the *Waiting to go out*
panel's fact list for the first time — a helper that had only ever been pointed
at a portal enrolment code, whose facts are all strings. It printed `Balance
0.000000` and `Date 2026-09-07 00:00:00-05:00` two inches under a letter
reading *your balance is now 0.00 USD*. It formats through
`rendering._rendered_value` now: two decimals beside the tenant's currency, and
the tenant's Regional date format. **The lesson generalises past this bug —
widening what a column carries changes every screen that reads it, and only
opening one of them found it.**

## 2026-09-07 · `DEF-INT-4410` — WE WERE BLOCKING OUR OWN BILLS, AND `frame-src` WAS THE SMALLER HALF

**What the Product Owner saw:** on `/{tenant}/billing/bills/{id}` the printable
page was an empty grey region reading *"This content is blocked. Contact the
site owner to fix the issue."* The same thing was true of the portal's
document viewer and nobody had opened it.

**What it was.** CR-069 wave M gave this deployment its first
Content-Security-Policy on 2026-09-06, and two of its directives refuse the
product's own documents:

* `frame-src 'none'` — the staff bill's Document tab is an `<iframe>` at
  `/api/{tenant}/invoices/{id}/document.pdf` (a frame and not `<embed>` on
  purpose: the browser's own PDF viewer carries print and save, which
  `BR-BIL-036` calls the floor).
* `object-src 'none'` — the portal's `DocumentPreview` is an `<object>` at the
  same kind of address (an `<object>` and not a frame on purpose: it is the only
  one of the three with a child fallback).

**AND A THIRD, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY DREW THAT MESSAGE, AND WHICH NO
AMOUNT OF READING THE STRING WOULD HAVE FOUND.** `frame-ancestors 'none'` was
in the same base policy, and `PagePolicyMiddleware` puts that policy on **every
API response — the PDF included**. `frame-src` governs what a page may frame;
`frame-ancestors` rides on the FRAMED RESOURCE and says who may frame it, and
`'none'` means *nobody*, our own same-origin page included. **Moving `frame-src`
and `object-src` to `'self'` changed nothing in a browser:** Chromium still
answered `net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_RESPONSE` and logged *"Refused to frame … because
an ancestor violates the following Content Security Policy directive:
frame-ancestors 'none'"*. Only opening the screen in Chromium showed it — the
same lesson as hard-won law 6, one release later.

**The decision: all three go to `'self'`, and none of them to `*`.** The SPA and
the API are ONE ORIGIN by construction (`07-frontend/server.mjs` is the join),
so `'self'` permits exactly this product to embed exactly its own documents and
refuses every other site — the whole of the clickjacking protection `'none'`
was there for. A connected provider still has to EARN a frame host through
`page_policy.granted()`; nothing was widened for third parties.

**Both copies moved, because there are two.** `page_policy.BASE_DIRECTIVES` and
`server.mjs`'s `BASE_POLICY` are kept byte-identical by `server.test.mjs`, which
a Node process cannot avoid by importing a Python module. A half-fix now fails
that check — proved by half-fixing a COPY of the two files and watching it go
red — and `test_tc5_a_directive_that_gains_a_host_loses_none` was amended rather
than deleted: its subject (a granted host must never render beside `'none'`)
still holds and is now asserted over the whole policy.

**Why every existing check passed over it, which is the part worth keeping.**
`server.test.mjs` asserted the two copies AGREE, that the webfont host is
permitted (`DEF-INT-4261`) and that nothing is wildcarded. All three were true
of a policy that blanked both screens, because **none of them asks whether the
policy permits the thing the product actually does.** There is now a test that
names the two screens by the elements they use, so a lane tightening either
directive back reads why before it ships two grey boxes.

**Verified in Chromium, both screens, after the change:** the staff Document tab
holds a child frame at the PDF address with Chromium's own viewer inside it
(page 1 of 2, zoom, print and save), and the portal's `<object>` holds a child
frame at its own address. No CSP violation on either page. The one console
error left on both is `fonts.googleapis.com` answering `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`,
which is this sandbox having no route to Google and not a refusal — the policy
names that host.

Shipped as **2.218.2**.


## 2026-09-07 · 🖨 `CR-076` — THE TEMPLATE DESIGNER'S THREE CHANGES, AND THE ONE THE PRODUCT OWNER TALKED THEMSELVES OUT OF

The Product Owner used Settings → Templates (`SET-10`) on the live product and asked for three
things. **Two of them arrived as a proposal the PO then corrected**, and those two corrections are
the reason this entry exists: the shipped answer is different from the request in both cases, and
the next lane reading only the request would build the wrong thing.

**1 · A SURFACE SWITCHER — AND THE PO RULED OUT THEIR OWN LIST.** They proposed a fixed bar of five
(`printable · email · sms · in_app · contract`). Shown what a hand-typed list has already cost this
repo — the service list typed out in `SignupWizard.tsx` and `ratingShared.tsx`, so an eleventh
service silently never appeared on the sign-up screen — they ruled, verbatim: ***"you are correct -
dont use hard coding"***.

**So the tabs are DERIVED, and the derivation is the deliverable rather than the tab bar.** The
detail payload carries a new field, `preview_surfaces`, built by `catalogs.designer_surfaces` out of
`CHANNELS_BY_KIND` — the map added by `DEF-2473` and the only place in this repo that says what a
`kind` string MEANS. **The worked figures, read off the seeded utility in a browser:**

    disconnect_notice_10_day   "Print + email"      -> Printed page · Email     (2 tabs)
    contract_payment_plan      "PDF + email"        -> Contract · Email         (2 tabs)
    sms_bill_ready             "SMS"                -> no tab strip at all
    staff_bulk_summary         "In-app message"     -> no tab strip at all

**`pdf_print` resolves through the class's own group**, which is the one place a channel does not
name a surface: a contract prints like a letter and is a different document to look at. **And 32 of
the 38 seeded classes have exactly one surface**, so on the overwhelming majority of this screen's
templates nothing changed at all — which is what a derived list buys and a constant one does not.

**THE JUDGMENT INSIDE IT, so nobody re-makes it: the COMPOSER does not follow the tab.** A template
class has ONE body, ONE merge-field whitelist and ONE save. Pressing *Email* on a printable notice
redraws the document and changes nothing a person is editing — summoning a subject box there would
be a field the renderer refuses, which is hard-won law 2's shape (a control whose value can never be
saved). The switcher is `preview`, not `mode`.

**AND ONE MORE, WHICH IS THE COST OF NOT HARDCODING: the client still writes the five DRAWABLE
surfaces once**, as the type guard that narrows a served string before `PreviewBody` can draw it. A
sixth surface added on the server would be filtered out in silence — the same failure one layer
down. It is guarded from the other side instead of promised: a backend case asserts the derivable
set is exactly those five and **fails naming `TemplateDetail.tsx`**. Choosing where to put the guard
was this lane's, not the PO's.

**2 · THE WORDING PANEL TAKES 60%, WHICH SUPERSEDES `CR-048` E1 FOR ONE CONSTANT.** E1 ratified *"a
quarter of the screen for the controls, three quarters for what the customer will actually hold"*,
on the argument that a regulated notice *"is not a preview of the work — it IS the work"*. **That
argument is still true of LOOKING at a notice and was never true of WRITING one**, which is what
this screen is for and what a 344px rail made painful. `DESIGNER_FRAME` is `3fr:2fr`, wording left.
**Measured in Chromium at 1440 wide: 662px of 1104px — 60.0%.**

The supersession is stated rather than assumed, and **the paragraph above the constant was amended
in the same commit as the number**. A comment describing the opposite of the code beneath it is
worse than no comment (hard-won law 1), and the ratio is quoted in three places in that file.

**A second thing rode with it, and it is a readability fix rather than a preference.** The new value
carries no comma — `[3fr_2fr]` with `min-w-0` already on both columns, which is exactly what the
`minmax(0,…)` was doing. `RULE_LAYOUT`'s own docstring records why: an arbitrary Tailwind value
containing a comma produces a class SELECTOR containing a comma, and every selector parser in this
repo splits a selector list on commas, so `.grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(0,3fr)]` was read as two
selectors matching nothing. It compiled perfectly and no check could see it.

**3 · PRINT THE REAL RENDERED DOCUMENT — AND THE PO RULED OUT THEIR OWN SNIPPET TOO.** The request
arrived as `window.open("")` plus `<pre>${preview.body}</pre>`; the ruling that followed is verbatim
***"you should print real rendered document"***.

**The difference is not cosmetic and it is worth writing down.** `preview.body` is the rendered
TEXT. Everything that makes the pane a document is drawn around it — the page and its margin, the
inbox lines, the phone bubble, the bell panel — and two things sit OUTSIDE the body entirely: the
**locked rights blocks** (`BR-NOT-015`) and the **sample-data notice**. A `<pre>` carries neither. So
a person checking a regulated notice would have printed a page with no rights footer on it and no
statement that it was a preview, and would have had no way to tell. That is `DEF-PAY-4409`'s shape
from the day before — a preview showing what the real document does not have — pointed the other
way, and worse, because paper leaves the building.

**WHY THE BROWSER DOES THE PRINTING, stated because it looks like a gap and is not one.** This
product renders no PDF for a notice class: `rendering.py` produces a `RenderedArtifact` whose `body`
is text, and the payload has said so all along in `can_download_pdf: false` beside *"the platform's
page writer is billing's and it writes bills"*. **That field is unchanged by this CR.** The rendered
document in this product IS the server's body inside this screen's per-surface drawing, so what goes
on paper is that node, copied into a window of its own with the page's own stylesheets.

**AND WHY A SEPARATE WINDOW RATHER THAN `window.print()`.** `RouteDetailPage` prints the route sheet
with `window.print()` and Tailwind `print:` variants, which is right there because the sheet is the
whole page's subject. Here the document is one column of a designer, so printing this page would
mean marking the shell, the rail, the merge-field table and the tabs `print:hidden` — in files this
lane does not own. **The cost is stated rather than hidden: a blocked pop-up means nothing prints**,
so the button says so instead of failing silently.

**WHAT THE WALKTHROUGH FOUND, AND IT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR HAVING WALKED IT (`DEF-NOT-4414`).**
The first version put the right nodes into the print window with **no CSS at all** — the whole
disconnect notice as one wall of serif text, no page, no preserved line breaks. The built page links
its stylesheet as `/assets/index-<hash>.css`, a ROOT-RELATIVE url, and the window opens at
`about:blank`, which has no base to resolve it against, so the sheet was never requested. **`tsc`,
thirteen DOM cases and every gate were green over it**, because jsdom loads no stylesheets: the case
proving the node travelled was TRUE and said nothing whatever about the printout. Hard-won law 6, in
one afternoon. Every copied `href` is absolutised now, the walkthrough reads `getComputedStyle` in
the print window rather than only its DOM, and it is committed at
`10-scripts/cr076_template_designer_walkthrough.mjs` rather than left in a scratchpad.

**AND THE GUARD'S COST, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED — `+1 QUERY PER QUEUED
DOCUMENT`.** A queue write ran **16** queries before it and **17** after
(`CaptureQueriesContext` over `queue_document` on the seeded utility, warm, the
guard stubbed out for the control). It is one indexed row fetch — the pinned
body — taken ONCE per document and not once per channel, so a receipt's three
writes cost three and a five-hundred-bill run costs five hundred against the
several thousand that run already makes. That is the price of the check and it
is written down because *"a check whose cost nobody measured"* is how the next
lane justifies deleting it.

## 2026-09-07 · 🧹 WE ARE IN BETA: FIX THE SEED, DO NOT MIGRATE THE DATA

**The ruling, Product Owner, verbatim:** *"We are still in beta - so when all changes start working _ will delete the DBa nd restart it"*.

**What it settles, and it is bigger than the question that prompted it.** The question was narrow — 84 receipts on the seeded utility were queued before `DEF-PAY-4409` and still carry no figures; should they be re-rendered or discarded? The answer makes the question disappear: the database is thrown away before go-live, so **rows written before a fix are not a migration problem and not a decision**.

**The general rule this sets for every lane, until the PO says otherwise:**

* **A change to seeded DATA is made in the seed and nowhere else.** No backfill migration, no repair command, no "existing tenants keep the old value" caveat. The next `seed_demo` is the migration.
* **A change to the SCHEMA still needs its migration** — that is not what this ruling touches. Django cannot reach a fresh database without the migration chain, and `G120` fails the moment `django.setup()` cannot build it.
* **Stale rows are not evidence of a live defect.** Counting them is still useful — 352 of 390 queued messages carry no merge values today, and that number is how we found out the receipt fault has siblings — but the fix belongs at the WRITE path, never in a repair of what is already queued.
* ⚠ **AND THE CLOCK ON THIS IS REAL.** It expires the day the first customer's data is live, and the cost of forgetting is a silent one: a lane that keeps applying it afterwards ships a fix that never reaches the rows a real utility already has. It is dated here for that reason.

**What it changed immediately:** the three seeded template names reading `· email` are corrected to `· Email` in the seed alone (`DEF-NOT-4416`), with no data migration written, where an hour earlier that fix would have carried one.

## 2026-09-07 · `DEF-CWP-4411` — A SIGN-IN CODE IS NOT A LETTER, AND `DEF-TEN-4412` — WHY EVERY LETTER SAYS *call ——*

Two of the three things the Product Owner reported on the live product this
morning. Neither turned out to be what the report guessed, so both diagnoses are
written down as well as both outcomes.

### `DEF-CWP-4411` · *"A letter from us · Letter · How: Text message"*

**The report guessed a wrong route in the seeded data or a wrong default in the
channel decision. It was neither, and both were ruled out by looking rather than
by reasoning.** `services.channel_decision` is SUBTRACTIVE — its own docstring
says *"a channel nobody asked for cannot be introduced by a rule"* — so no
setting and no seeded rule row can put a letter on SMS. Every live caller that
asks for `sms` was then enumerated, and only one produces a row in the LETTER
pile: `apps.portal.credentials.queue_code`, the portal's one-time enrolment
code.

**Reproduced end to end** by enrolling through the real endpoints on a seeded
tenant — `find-account`, `verify-code`, `set-password` — and opening
`/pine-hill/portal/documents` in Chromium. The row read, verbatim, *A letter
from us · No reference number · No copy kept · Letter · Text message · WAITING
TO GO*.

**The SMS route is correct and is not being changed.** `credentials.contact_for`
prefers a mobile where one is held (field map §1's `otp_channel` default), and
every seeded account has a primary contact with a phone — so on any seeded
tenant every enrolment code goes by text, exactly as designed.

**What was wrong is that the code was on the list at all, and the vocabulary had
already ruled on it.** `models.SOURCE_TYPES` gained `portal` on 2026-09-04 with
its reason written beside it: *"a code is not a document, there is no envelope
for it, and it is worthless within ten minutes"* — which is why `portal` is
deliberately absent from `CHANNEL_FLOOR_BY_SOURCE`. The same sentence decides
this: `account_correspondence` now excludes the kind, through a named
`NOT_A_DOCUMENT_SOURCE_TYPES`.

**Excluded by SOURCE KIND and not by template code**, so a second credential
class cannot be added and forgotten — the same reasoning `TC-5` already gives
for excluding staff rows by the shape of the query rather than by a list of
kinds somebody maintains.

**THE ROW IS STILL WRITTEN, and the test asserts that half FIRST.** *A message
that was never queued leaves no trace* is why the queue writes a row even when
nothing can be delivered, and `US-CWP-017` reads the code back off it. A fix
that stopped queueing would pass a test that only checked the list, and would be
a worse defect than the one being closed.

**Why nothing caught it:** `US-CWP-036` TC-5 excludes *a document the customer
may not see* and the read excludes staff rows by having no `account_id`. Nobody
asked the mirror question — whether everything that HAS an `account_id` is a
document. And the portal fixture never enrolled anybody (`portal_credential` is
empty on a freshly seeded tenant), so no test and no walkthrough has ever had a
credential row in that list.

**The receipt line in the same report is CORRECT and was left alone.** *Text
message · Email · Post — We could not send this by Text message* is
`apps/payments/receipts.py` writing all three channels on purpose, with the SMS
row carrying `recipient_not_resolvable` because no mobile is on file — A15's
rule made visible, and the honest answer rather than a tidier one. A lane
"fixing" that would be deleting a deliberate absence.

### `DEF-TEN-4412` · `{support_phone}` prints as `——`, and it is CONFIGURATION

**Not a token nothing populates.** `support_phone` is a real column on
`tenants`, edited on Settings → Company, merged by `rendering._identity_context`
and populated on every fixture tenant. What the Product Owner is looking at is a
**self-served tenant where nobody has typed one in**, and that is a ruled
behaviour, not a gap: `services.provision_tenant` seeds seven identity fields
from the signup and deliberately leaves five NULL — EIN, state utility id, both
addresses and the support phone — under the PO's own 2026-08-17 ruling, because
*"a fabricated tax id or remit-to address on a bill is a FALSE FACT, not a
default"*. The signup collects the OWNER's phone, which is not the utility's
support line, and using it would be exactly that fabrication.

The product already says so twice: `template_preview` reports *"Support phone
will print blank — add it under Settings → Company"*, and the S62 checklist
reports `company_profile` as not done, deep-linked to that screen.

**WHAT ELSE IS BLANK THE SAME WAY, measured rather than guessed.** A tenant was
provisioned locally through the real `POST /api/tenants`, and every one of the
41 template classes was previewed against it:

| token | absences | classes |
|---|---|---|
| `support_phone` | **45** | **28** of 41 |
| `utility_address` | **5** | 5 — the three disconnect notices, the door hanger, the write-off notice |

So the one field the Product Owner happened to see is 45 places, and there is a
second token nobody has mentioned. The disconnect notices carry
`{support_phone}` six or seven times EACH, including A19 §2 tier 3's *"Medical/
critical-care customers: call {support_phone}"* — which is the sentence where a
`——` matters most.

**AND ONE FINDING THAT IS NOT CONFIGURATION, FILED AS `DEF-TEN-4412` AND NOT
FIXED HERE.** `_checklist_item_state("company_profile")` is satisfied by legal
name + EIN + mailing address + remit-to, and **does not include
`support_phone`** — so a utility can fill four fields, watch the onboarding item
go green, and still print *call ——* on 28 template classes. Adding the field to
that predicate would change `US-TEN-003` TC-2, which names those four by name,
and would change when an onboarding item goes green on every live tenant. That
is a ruling rather than a lane's edit, so it is filed and raised and left alone.

Shipped as **2.218.3**.

## 2026-09-07 — WHO PICKS THE LANGUAGE IN THE CUSTOMER PORTAL, AND THE GUEST DROPDOWN

**The report, verbatim:** *"Language setting does not work in customer portal"*.
It did not work in the ordinary sense of the word: `changeLanguage` is called in
exactly one file in the whole front end — the staff shell — and `PortalApp.tsx`
contains no reference to i18n at all. The portal never asked what language to
speak, so the tenant's regional setting and a customer's own stored preference
were both simply unread. Filed as `DEF-CWP-4440`.

**The ruling, verbatim, PO 2026-09-07:**

> *"a signed-in customer will get their account's own preferred language -
> Signed customer should get their own references. you can also provdie language
> option for gurst customers on top menu as drop down"*

**What that settles, in two halves.**

* **Signed in — the customer's own preference wins.** The language comes from
  the account's own `preferred_language`, and the tenant's regional default does
  NOT override it. A customer who chose Spanish sees Spanish on a utility whose
  default is English, on every page, without touching anything.
* **Not signed in — the tenant's setting starts, and the guest can change it.**
  A guest opens in the tenant's own language, and the portal frame carries a
  **language dropdown in the top menu** so a stranger paying a bill can switch
  it themselves. That control is part of this fix, not a follow-up: a portal
  that picks a language and gives the reader no way to change it is only half
  the report.

**Why this needed a ruling at all, since it looks obvious.** The two halves
disagree in the one case that matters — a signed-in customer whose stored
preference differs from the utility's default — and the product could honestly
have gone either way: a utility that has decided to write to its town in English
might reasonably expect its own screens in English. The PO ruled for the person
reading the screen. That is a rule about whose convenience wins, which is not a
lane's judgement to make.

**A consequence worth writing down before someone re-derives it wrongly:** the
guest dropdown is a control, and hard-won law 2's mirror applies to it. A
dropdown that renders and does not change the page is a live screen behind a
dead control, which is the failure that cost the customer portal five of its
eight front-page doors on 2026-09-05.

## 2026-09-07 — EVERY LETTER NOW CARRIES ITS OWN FIGURES, AND TWO OF THEM COULD NOT BE PRODUCED AT ALL

**The ruling this executes, Product Owner, verbatim:** *"(a) Fix all of them now"* — after
`DEF-PAY-4409` fixed the receipt and reported that its siblings were unfixed.

**Measured before the work, on a freshly seeded Brazos Bend utility:** 353 queued
messages, of which **100 carried no merge values at all** — every one of them a bill.

### WHAT WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS FOUR DIFFERENT THINGS WEARING ONE COSTUME

**1 · THE BILL-READY EMAIL NAMED NOTHING (`DEF-BIL-4448`).** `queue_bill_delivery`
passed no `render_context`, so the eleven merge fields the seeded body declares —
the customer's name, the service address, the bill number, the bill date, both ends
of the period, and all four figures of A19 §1.3's summary box — printed `——`. Its
subject line, A19 r8's own *"Your Silver Creek Water bill is ready — $247.30 due Aug
25"*, came out *"…is ready — —— due ——"*.

**2 · THREE MORE CALLERS DID THE SAME (`DEF-NOT-4449`), AND ONE OF THEM IS THE
SHARPEST CASE IN THE FAMILY.** `notices.generate_disconnect_notice` and
`generate_reminder` BUILD a context, hand it to `_render` four lines above the queue
write, and then drop it — so the artifact returned to the caller carries the balance
and the cut date while the row a customer's letter is actually rendered from carries
nothing. The staff resend copied the source, the channel, the pin and the recipient
snapshot and dropped the one column holding what the letter SAYS. Both send-test
buttons queued the real wording with nothing in it, so a System Admin checking their
bill-ready email received *"…is ready — —— due ——"* and learned nothing.

**3 · THE COLLECTIONS LADDER'S LETTERS NAMED NOTHING (`DEF-PAY-4450`)** — on the
legal step before switching somebody's water off.

**4 · AND THE ONE THAT IS NOT ABOUT FIGURES AT ALL (`DEF-PAY-4451`): EVERY
DISCONNECT NOTICE THIS PRODUCT HAS EVER QUEUED IS PINNED TO A TEMPLATE CLASS THAT
DOES NOT EXIST.** `send_disconnect_notices` composed `f"{template_code}_{tier}"` —
`disconnect_notice` plus `first_10_day` — and the three seeded classes are
`disconnect_notice_10_day`, `_5_day` and `_48_hour`. **Not one of the three composed
codes has ever existed.** Sending a real 10-day notice to a real debtor queued a row,
reported `template_pin_unresolved`, wrote its `notice_history` row, **advanced the
account's tier** — and left a row `render_for_dispatch` refuses forever, because the
pin is stamped at queue time. The ladder records that a customer was warned, moves
them a step closer to disconnection, and produces no letter.
⚠ **`apps/notifications/notices.py` WROTE THIS WARNING DOWN ON 2026-08-17 AND ITS
SIBLING WENT ON DOING IT** — *"an explicit map, not a f-string on the tier name: a
name-derived class would silently invent `disconnect_notice_<anything>`"*. And
`CR-048` wave B task B10 found the identical disease in the same file for plan
notices (`plan_installment_missed`) and fixed only that branch.

### THE ONE SIGNED STATEMENT THIS REVERSES, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

`outbound_messages.render_context`'s own docstring read **"AN INVOICE'S FIGURES ARE
STILL NOT PUT HERE"** from 2026-08-17, reasoning that duplicating them would create
*"a second copy of a money figure free to disagree with the invoice"*. It is
superseded, and the chain matters because the next lane will reconstruct the old
reading from first principles:

* The 2026-08-17 docstring reads `BR-NOT-012`'s phrase *"the notification's own
  stored render context for **non-invoice** notices"* as governing platform tokens.
  **`BR-NOT-012` is a rule about tenant CUSTOM FIELDS** — `{{account.custom.…}}`,
  double-braced, a different grammar on purpose — and it is `PROPOSED`, not confirmed.
* **`BR-NOT-027` (PO, CONFIRMED 2026-08-30, `CR-049`) supersedes it.** Part (1) is
  *"Keep all the underlying data — we already do (`outbound_messages.render_context`)"*,
  and the rule says in its own words *"SO THE RULE'S REACH IS WIDER THAN IT WAS FIRST
  WRITTEN: BR-NOT-027 APPLIES TO THE BILL TOO."*
* **And the original worry is answered by construction rather than waived.** Every
  figure is copied out of `invoices.bill_payload` — the instance locked at issue,
  protected by `billing/0006`'s trigger, and the same instance `billing.documents`
  renders the printed bill FROM. It is not a second copy free to disagree with the
  invoice; it is the invoice's own stamped number, and for the two to disagree the
  payload would have to disagree with itself. A figure NOT in the payload is still
  not put there.

The docstring is amended in the same commit as the code. A comment describing the
opposite of the code beneath it is worse than no comment (hard-won law 1).

### FOUR JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT

**(1) `{total_due}` IS THE PAYLOAD'S FIGURE, NEVER `invoices.total`.** `invoices.total`
is THIS PERIOD's charges alone — `issue.py`'s own trailer says prior balance is not in
it — and A19 §1.3's total due is previous balance − payments + current charges. Putting
`invoices.total` in the subject line would understate what a customer owes by their
entire arrears, on the one line of the one email they read. Worked: **45.00 + 393.76 =
438.76**, and a test goes red on `393.76`.

**(2) NOTHING IS QUERIED, AND THAT IS A REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN AN OPTIMISATION.**
This runs inside `issue_invoice`'s transaction, once per bill, five hundred times a
morning. Every value is an attribute of a row the caller already holds; a query count
of **0** is asserted rather than described. The one read the function can make — the
original bill's total on a correction — is in its own SAVEPOINT (hard-won law 14),
because on PostgreSQL a statement that errors inside a transaction aborts it and
losing an issued bill over a figure on a covering email is a far worse defect.

**(3) `{pay_by_date}` AND `{cut_date}` ARE TWO SPELLINGS OF ONE STORED DATE.** Tier 1
asks *"pay by X (10 days)"* and carries no cut date; tiers 2 and 3 carry the cut date
and no pay-by. This product holds ONE date for that step — `ladder._send` computes
`as_of + 10 days` and hands it in — and the day service stops IS the day by which
paying avoids it. Both keys are stated with the same value. **The alternative was a
blank where the deadline goes on a legal notice**, which is worse than a defensible
reading. If a utility ever needs a grace day between the two, that is a second stored
date and a ruling; a test is what goes red.

**(4) A SEND TEST CARRIES THE PREVIEW SCREEN'S OWN SAMPLES, NOT NEW ONES.** There is
no document behind a test, so a figure there could only be fabricated or sampled.
`template_preview.sample_context` is the ratified set SET-10's pane already renders
from — `SAMPLE-ACCOUNT`, `Sample Customer`, `123.45`, a FIXED `2026-01-31` — so a test
message and a preview of the same class cannot disagree. The four identity tokens stay
unsampled, because a test is the one message where `——` for the support phone is
USEFUL: it tells the admin their real letters will print it blank (`DEF-TEN-4412`).

Signed in as Dana Whitfield, Settings → Notifications → **Messages needing attention**
→ *Show the message*, on rows queued through the product's own services:

Customer name `Grace Gagnon` · Due date `08/22/2026` · First name `Grace` · Payments

Grace, Your bill for 113 Willow Bend Dr … Total due 393.76 USD by 08/22/2026"*, with

**⚠ AND THE PANEL SAYS *"No wording is published yet. These are the details."* ABOVE
THAT LIST, WHICH IS `DEF-BIL-4452` AND IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED.** A bill's queue
rows are pinned to a **BILLING** template on EVERY channel — `bill_template_versions`,
which `template_service.load_pinned` cannot find, because it looks in
`notification_template_versions`. For `pdf_print` that is right: billing's own page
writer makes that document. For the EMAIL row it means **`email_bill_ready` is never
reached and the bill-ready email cannot be produced at all**, whatever figures it
carries. `rule_catalog.EVENTS["bill_ready"]` already names the wording per channel
(`email_bill_ready`, `sms_bill_ready`) and nothing reads it at queue time. Pinning per
channel is a change to the ONE write path inside a bill run with idempotency
consequences, so it is raised rather than taken here. **The figures are stamped and
correct; only the wording is missing, and the panel now shows exactly that.**

### THREE ABSENCES THAT ARE THE PRODUCT'S TRUTH AND NOT THIS LANE'S GAPS

* **`{state_puc_ref}`** — nothing in this product stores a commission reference;
  `rights_footer.py` records it and `notifications.notices` takes it as a caller
  argument for the same reason. A fabricated regulatory citation is the worst thing
  that could appear on a disconnection notice.
* **`{correction_reason}`** (`DEF-BIL-4454`) — this product holds only an internal
  code (`wrong_read`). `correction_reasons.MECHANISM_IN_WORDS` looks like the answer
  and is not: it describes the MECHANISM to a clerk, not the fault to a customer.
  B14 rule 32 forbids an internal code in clerk-facing copy; BR-NOT-015 makes the
  wording notifications' to own.
* **The friendly reminder's class** (`DEF-PAY-4453`) — `collections_reminder_<tone>`
  is catalogued nowhere either. Not fixed with the tier map because WHICH class it
  should pin is a real question (`dunning` per BR-NOT-008, or `email_past_due` per
  SET-12) and the tier map was not.

### AND THE 100 TEMPLATE-LESS BILL PDFs TURNED OUT TO BE TWO DIFFERENT FACTS

Asked as one question and it is two. **The NULL `template_code` is by design** —
`queue_bill_delivery`'s own docstring says the readable handle is optional and *"not
defaulted to a plausible string — a code nobody assigned would look like a resolved
template assignment"*. Every one of the 100 rows carries a real `template_id` and
`template_version`, so nothing is unpinned. **What is a live defect is which TABLE
that pin points at**, which is `DEF-BIL-4452` above. So: not seed-era noise, and not
the missing code either — the code being absent is correct and the pin being billing's
is the fault.

### PROOF

**20 cases, and FIVE guards driven RED first through `python3.12 -m pytest` — the
harness that runs them.** ⚠ **TWO OF THEM CAME BACK GREEN OVER THE SABOTAGE THE FIRST
TIME AND ARE RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED**, because they are hard-won law
7's fourth shape and both were found by RUNNING the sabotage rather than by reading the
test: the tier case asserted the MAP was right and never that the caller USED it, so
restoring `f"{template_code}_{tier}"` left all eighteen cases passing; and the
collections case called `_notice_context` directly, so deleting the context from
`send_disconnect_notices` entirely changed nothing. Both now send through the real
function and read the stored column off the row it wrote. The five reds, each quoted:
`438.760000` reaching the page where `438.76` belongs; `total_due` served as this
period's charges; *"tier 'first_10_day' queued a row pinned to
'disconnect_notice_first_10_day', which resolves to no published version"*; *"the
notice was queued with no merge values at all"*; *"the bill was queued for delivery
with no merge values at all"*.

Walked in Chromium end to end on the seeded utility; the walkthrough is committed at
`10-scripts/def4448_letters_walkthrough.mjs` rather than left in a scratchpad, and it
reads the DRAWER rather than the page — an em-dash count taken over `body` includes
the nav and every other row and says nothing about the letter.

## 2026-09-07 · SET-10 REBUILT TO THE DESIGN — AND EDITING BECAME A MODE

**What was asked.** The Product Owner compared the running template screen with
the design they supplied and reported that the two are *structurally* different —
not different copy, a different shape. The design was transcribed from their own
screenshots into the lane brief, and that transcription is the source of truth
for this work: the PO said explicitly not to work from `05-prototype/r10` for it.

**The ruling that decides the screen: EDITING IS A MODE.** The default view is
the rendered document with a narrow rail beside it; the wording form appears
when *Edit wording* is pressed.

⚠ **THIS DOES NOT REVERSE CR-076 ITEM 2 AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS.** On
2026-09-07 the PO ruled the Wording panel takes 60% and the document 40%
(*"the panel a person TYPES IN gets 60%"*). That ruling is about the screen a
person is WRITING on, and it stands: `DESIGNER_FRAME` still declares
`lg:grid-cols-[3fr_2fr]`, `templateDesigner.dom.test.tsx` still asserts it, and
the browser measured **0.600** after this change. What moved is which of the two
a person LANDS on. Both rulings are now true of the same screen, one per mode.

**The surface switcher stays.** CR-076 item 1's preview tabs are derived from
`preview_surfaces` and never hardcoded (*"you are correct - dont use hard
coding"*); that behaviour survived the rebuild unchanged and the walkthrough
re-measured it on `disconnect_notice_10_day` (two tabs: Printed page · Email).

### THE SCREEN ID WAS WRONG AND HAD BEEN SINCE THE MAP WAS WRITTEN

`SET-09` is the template CATALOGUE. Opening one template replaces that list at
the same address plus `?template=<code>`, and BOTH drew `SET-09` — so a fault
photographed on the designer was filed against the list. **r10's own id function
has made the distinction since the prototype was drawn** (line 9280:
`s.tplView ? 'SET-10.' + s.tplView : 'SET-09'`), so `SET-10` is a badge r10
DECLARES and no row in `g29_allocated_badges.txt` is needed — that register is
for ids no authority defines, and minting one here would put a second authority
behind one number. `DEF-NOT-4443`.

⚠ **THE DOTTED SUFFIX IS DELIBERATELY NOT COPIED.** r10 appends the template
key. One of ours is `bill:<uuid>` (CR-048 E9's other store), and B14 rule 31
forbids a database id as the visible value of anything — the PO's own words,
*"no Databse ID on screen - that is a rule"*. The badge is the parent alone.

### WHAT THE SERVER DOES NOT SERVE, AND WHAT THE SCREEN SAYS INSTEAD

The design's head reads *"last edited Jul 12 · Alex Reed"* and its history reads
*"Jul 12 · Alex Reed — reworded usage line"*. **Three of those five facts have no
field behind them**, and each is NAMED rather than faked (BR-SHL-020):

| The design shows | What is served | What the screen draws |
|---|---|---|
| last edited (date) | `versions[].updated_at` | the date |
| the author's NAME | `author_label`, a `UUIDField` | *"author not recorded"* |
| why an edit was made | `change_note`, null on every row | *"Who edited and why are not recorded."* |
| which wording moved | `changed_fields` (CR-049 task 8) | the field names |
| where it is used | `used_by` | the sentence |

`author_label`'s own docstring says it is *"the id, or the platform, never a
name"* — identity's display names are another module's table (B11 F-3), which is
`OQ-255` and is still open. Drawing it would put a uuid on a clerk's screen.

⚠ **AND IT IS ALREADY DRAWN ONE SCREEN ALONG.** The version-history page
(`?view=history`) prints `version.author_label` in its trail cell, which on any
real tenant is a raw uuid — B14 rule 31, live today. Not fixed here because that
table is pinned by three other suites and the fix is a judgment about what to
draw instead; **reported rather than silently left**, and it belongs with
whoever answers `OQ-255`.

### THE PAPER: WHY NO FIGURE FROM THE DESIGN'S SCREENSHOT IS IN THE CODE

The design's document reads *"Silver Creek Water"*, *"Jordan Alvarez"*,
*"$24.02"*. **Those are prototype r10's demo data and this product deliberately
does not reuse them** — `template_preview.py` records the reason: *"a sample that
reads like a real utility's real customer is a sample somebody screenshots into a
ticket"*. The preview renders `Sample Customer` and `$123.45` instead, and on a
real tenant it renders that tenant's own identity. A screen that printed `$24.02`
regardless of the template would be worse than the one we had.

**The server sends the document as ONE STRING** — there is no line-item array,
no letterhead object and no totals block, and there should not be: a template is
WORDING. So `templateDocument.ts` SETS the served text as a page rather than
assembling a document from fields nobody sends. Its one safety rule:

> A line is a label-and-value row **only when it ends with a string the server
> told us is a sample value** — never a currency symbol, a trailing number or a
> colon.

A `$` test would right-align a utility's prose the moment somebody wrote a price
into a sentence. This cannot: the strings it matches are the exact strings the
renderer just substituted. **With no samples in hand nothing aligns at all**,
which is the honest degradation for a class whose merge-field catalogue nobody
has written.

⚠ **ONE KNOWN DEPARTURE, STATED RATHER THAN GUESSED.** The seeded bill's most
important line is `Total due {total_due} by {due_date}`. The design draws a total
as a right-aligned figure; splitting this one would put the amount in the label
column and the DATE in the money column, which states something false about which
number is the amount. It stays a sentence.

### TWO MORE DEFECTS FOUND ON THE WAY

* **`DEF-NOT-4444` — a raw message key reached a clerk's screen.** The variant
  badge built its key by interpolation and `i18n/index.ts` sets `keySeparator:
  false`, so the state this code calls `not-live` looked for
  `templates.detail.state.not-live` while all eleven catalogues hold `notLive`.
  A variant with wording nobody published rendered the literal key. **G15 could
  not see it** — the key is missing from all eleven equally, so parity is perfect
  and the badge is still wrong. A literal key per state now, so the next
  mismatch is a compile error.
* **`DEF-NOT-4445` — the preview strip's *Default variant* badge was always
  true.** It asked whether the TEMPLATE has a default variant, which BR-NOT-001
  makes mandatory, so it drew over every variant including the ones it was
  denying. No lawful payload could make it absent, so no test could assert it
  away. It asks about the OPEN variant now, and offers *Set as default* when
  that one is not the default — which is the design's own second state and the
  thing that makes the two cases distinguishable at all.

### AND FOUR THINGS ONLY THE BROWSER COULD SEE (hard-won law 6)

`tsc` and 267 DOM cases were green over all four:

1. **the paper was DARKER than the page** — `bg-surface` is the card colour
   (#eae9e9) on a #f3f2f2 ground, so the "white document card" read as a hole;
2. **the letterhead was not recognised on the one document that matters** — the
   seeded disconnection notice opens `{utility_name}` then `{utility_address}`
   with no blank between, and the first rule asked for a single line;
3. **two page titles in one outline** — this header is drawn inside the Settings
   page, which had already written `Settings` as the `h1`;
4. **a token overprinted its value in the rail** by 36px — `KV_KEY` lets the
   slot shrink and a `<code>` with no break opportunity does not shrink with it.

`PageHeader` gained an optional `titleAs` for (3) — the kit answer (B14 rule 36),
additive, no existing call site or pixel moved.

**Measured at 1440 after the fixes:** reading view 776px document + 320px rail;
edit mode 662/442 = 0.600; one `h1`; no overlapping rows; the disconnection
notice draws its letterhead, its accent rule, its addressee block and
`Account … SAMPLE-ACCOUNT` right-aligned to the paper's edge.

rows) · `2a727e3e` (the four browser findings and the new suites).
