## 2026-09-07 — SHOW WHAT THE CUSTOMER GETS; EVERYTHING ELSE IS INFORMATION

**The ruling, verbatim, PO 2026-09-07:**

> *"user does not udnerstand so many option - you should show what customer is
> going to get - rest is only for information"*

Said while looking at `SET-10` on the running product, after three separate
messages about the same screen: *"why all this content - there is so much
repeat"*, *"same is the problem here - why so many time pre view, pre view word"*,
and *"it is not PDF preview it is text only preview"*.

**What it settles.** A template screen has ONE subject — the letter, email or
page the customer will actually receive — and that document is the screen. Every
other thing on it is secondary: which surface is being previewed, which variant
is open, whether this variant is chosen automatically, that the data is a
sample, that nothing is being sent. None of those are wrong to show; they are
wrong to show FIRST, and wrong to show three times.

**Measured, on the branch tip at 1440×1000, which is what provoked the ruling.**
On the Past-due reminder the document's top edge sits at **832 px** of a
1000 px window — 83% of the screen spent before a word of the letter appears.
The word *preview* appears 2–3 times per screen and the word *sample* 12–21
times. Three separate captions say the same caveat: *"Previewing as…"*,
*"Preview only — sample data, nothing is sent."*, and on Welcome a third,
*"Fields the preview deliberately does not sample"*.

**The rule this becomes, and it is not only about `SET-10`.** Where a screen
exists to show a person a THING — a document, a bill, a letter, a report — the
thing leads, at the size it will be read at, and the controls and the caveats
arrange themselves around it. A caveat is stated once. An option that is not
being exercised right now does not occupy space above the subject.

⚠ **THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THE SAME PO HAS RULED IN THIS DIRECTION AND THE
FIRST RULING DID NOT REACH THE SCREEN.** B14 rule 32 — a screen has a
description budget, one sentence per section, no rule id or internal code in
clerk-facing copy — was ratified on 2026-09-02 after the PO said *"too much
content - desctiption is too much for clark to read"* four times in twenty
minutes. `SET-10` was then rebuilt on 2026-09-06 carrying a caption that reads
*"first line of the body — this product has no preheader field"*, which is our
database schema explained to a clerk. **A ratified rule that no gate reads is a
rule that has to be re-ruled**, and this is what that costs: the same person
saying the same thing a month apart about a screen built in between.

**Consequences recorded here so they are not re-derived:** `DEF-NOT-4464` (the
first line of the wording prints twice, with that caption between the copies),
`DEF-NOT-4465` (an email previews as a text blob while a printed letter previews
as a rendered page). Both filed before either was fixed.

## 2026-09-07 — TWELVE NEW TEMPLATES RULED IN, AND THE TWO MODULES THAT NEED NONE

**The ruling, verbatim, PO 2026-09-07:** *"okay add all of them"* — in answer to a
table of twelve gaps put to them with a shape and a reason for each, and a
recommendation that the five marked High be built first.

**How the gaps were found, so the next lane does not re-derive it.** The
catalogue holds **41 template classes**. They were listed against what the newer
modules actually DO — work orders, the customer portal, meter reads, autopay,
payment plans — and the question asked of each journey was *where does a customer
hear nothing?* Twelve moments answered. Every one is a journey this product has
already built; none is speculative.

| # | Template | Shape | The silence it fills |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Technician on the way | Text message | We say an appointment is BOOKED and never that somebody is arriving today |
| 2 | We couldn't get access | Print + email | Technician attends, nobody home or the meter is locked; the job closes and the customer hears nothing |
| 3 | Portal sign-up confirmed | Email | The portal creates accounts and nothing welcomes them or confirms the address |
| 4 | Password reset | Email | The portal has a reset flow with no letter behind it |
| 5 | Paperless turned on / off | Email | A customer switching off paper gets no record — and it is the last paper letter they should receive |
| 6 | High usage / possible leak | SMS + email | Meter reads can detect it; catching a leak early is the message a utility gets thanked for |
| 7 | We estimated your read | Email | We estimate when a meter cannot be read; the bill says so in small print and nobody is told plainly |
| 8 | Card or bank details expiring | Email | Autopay fails silently on an expired card, then becomes a payment-failed letter and a late fee |
| 9 | Payment plan broken | Print + email | `plan_notice_missed` and `plan_notice_void` exist; nothing says *the plan has ENDED and the full balance is due* |
| 10 | Meter exchange scheduled | Printed page | A swap needs notice at the property; `service_door_hanger` covers disconnects, not exchanges |
| 11 | Work completed — chargeable | Email | `service_work_completed` exists; nothing says *this one costs you 120.00 USD and lands on your next bill* |
| 12 | Deposit refund due | Email | `email_refund_issued` exists; nothing tells a customer their deposit is coming back after good payment history |

**41 → 53 classes.** By shape the additions are **7 email · 2 print + email ·
1 printed page · 1 SMS · 1 SMS + email**, so the five renderers ruled the same
day cover all twelve and no sixth shape is introduced.

⚠ **AND TWO MODULES DELIBERATELY GET NONE, WHICH IS A DECISION AND NOT AN
OVERSIGHT.** **Runbooks** and **Integrations** are staff-facing end to end; no
customer is a party to a runbook run or a connector sync, and inventing letters
for them would be manufacturing work. This was put to the PO in the same breath
as the twelve and not contradicted. If a customer-facing moment ever appears in
either — a runbook that writes to an account, say — that is a new question, not
a gap in this row.

**What is NOT settled here and must not be assumed:** the wording of any of the
twelve. Each needs a draft, and drafts are subject to the same rule as every
existing template — a value the product does not hold is STATED, never filled in
with something plausible (`DEF-TEN-4412`'s lesson, and the reason 28 of 41
classes print a dash for the support phone rather than a made-up number). Two of
the twelve are already known to touch facts we may not store: #1 needs an arrival
window, and #6 needs a usage threshold somebody has to choose.

## 2026-09-07 — THE SAMPLE CUSTOMER GETS A NAME, AND THE SETTINGS FRAME STAYS

Two answers from the PO on the template screen, given together, and the second
one **caps a number this repo has been treating as a target all day**.

### ⓵ The sample customer becomes a person

**Ruled: a normal-looking invented customer replaces the word "Sample".** The
preview letter reads *"Hi Pat, your bill for 12 Oak Street is ready… Account
AC-000000 … Total due 123.45 USD by 22 Aug 2026"*.

**What it supersedes, stated rather than assumed.** `template_preview.py` records
an earlier ruling that this product deliberately does not use realistic demo
data — *"a sample that reads like a real utility's real customer is a sample
somebody screenshots into a ticket"*. That worry was put to the PO in the same
sentence as the change and they chose the change. **The worry is answered by the
account number rather than dismissed:** `AC-000000` cannot be mistaken for a live
account, so the preview reads like a letter while still being unmistakably a
sample.

**The measurement that provoked it:** the word *"sample"* appears **12 to 21
times on one template screen** — 21 on Welcome — because the demo customer is
literally `Sample Customer` at `1 Sample Street, Sample City`, account
`SAMPLE-ACCOUNT`, starting on `Sample service start date`. Tidying our own
captions could never have fixed that; most of the repetition was the data.

### ⓶ The Settings frame stays, so 240 px is not reachable — and that is the ruling

Three options were put to the PO, each with its cost:

| Option | Where the letter lands | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| Let a template take the full page, Settings tabs stepping aside | ~240 px | nothing on other screens |
| Trim the Settings heading, the description line and the tab wrap | ~240 px | the top of every Settings screen changes |
| **Leave the Settings frame exactly as it is** ← **CHOSEN** | **~500–550 px** | nothing changes anywhere |

⚠ **SO THE DESIGN'S `240 px` IS NOW A RELATIVE FIGURE, NOT AN ABSOLUTE ONE, AND
EVERY CHECK WRITTEN AGAINST IT MUST BE RE-BASED.** The six regions and their
order are unchanged and still ratified — breadcrumb, title, variant tabs, one
caption line, the document, the rail. What changed is that the whole block sits
BELOW the Settings furniture rather than replacing it, so the document's top edge
lands around 500 instead of 240. **A walkthrough asserting `document top ≤ 240`
would now fail forever on a screen built exactly as ruled** — which is this
repo's *incapable of passing* shape (hard-won law 7), and it would have been
written today had this not been asked.

**The honest arithmetic, measured at 1440×1000:** 832 px this morning → 715 px
after the first pass → ~500 px once the refusal line, Surfaces and the
Deactivate/Reactivate pair move into the rail. The remaining ~260 px is the
Settings frame itself, and the PO has ruled that it stays. **A reader still
scrolls to finish the letter, and the PO accepted that cost knowingly** rather
than change five other screens.

## 2026-09-07 — THE DOCUMENT SCROLLS INSIDE ITSELF, WHICH DISSOLVES THE 240 px PROBLEM

**The ruling, verbatim, PO 2026-09-07:** *"you give scroll option in PDF view
area"* — offered in answer to being told the honest cost of keeping the Settings
frame: *"it'll land around 500 … you'll still scroll to finish reading."*

**It is a better answer than any of the three options that were put to them, and
it came from the person the options were put TO.** All three of those traded one
thing against another — either the Settings frame changed, or five other screens
changed, or the reader kept scrolling. This trades nothing. The document pane
takes the height left on the screen and **scrolls its own contents**, the way a
PDF viewer does. The page itself stops scrolling; the letter scrolls inside its
frame.

**What it fixes, and why the 240 px argument simply stops mattering.** The whole
argument was about where the document's top edge falls, because everything above
it was pushing the READABLE AREA off the bottom. With an internally-scrolling
pane the top edge is no longer load-bearing: the header, the variant tabs, the
one caption line and the right rail all stay put and stay visible while a clerk
reads to the end of a three-page notice. **Nothing needs to be deleted from any
screen.**

**The cost, stated rather than glossed.** On a 1000 px window with the Settings
frame kept, the pane gets roughly **500 px of height** — about half a US Letter
page at readable size. That is a window onto the letter rather than the whole
letter. Two things follow and both are the lane's to build: the pane must show it
is scrollable (a real scrollbar, not a hidden one) so nobody thinks the letter
ends where the frame does, and the pane must never be the thing that scrolls the
PAGE as well, which is the classic nested-scroll trap.

**The recommended refinement, recorded as this lane's judgment and not the PO's:**
let the page scroll ONCE — far enough to take the Settings heading and tab rows
off the top — and then let the document pane stick and take the full remaining
height. A reader gets a near-full-page view after one scroll, no other screen
changes, and the frame is still there when they scroll back. If that proves
fiddly in practice, the plain fixed-height pane above is correct and sufficient.

⚠ **THIS SUPERSEDES THE `document top ≤ 560 px` ASSERTION ISSUED TO TWO LANES
EARLIER TODAY.** That check was re-based off the cancelled `≤ 240` and is now
measuring the wrong thing entirely. **What must be asserted instead is that the
DOCUMENT PANE IS SCROLLABLE AND ITS FULL CONTENT IS REACHABLE** — scroll the pane
to its end in a browser and read the last line of the letter — plus the relative
facts that were always the real design: the document is the largest element, the
rail is beside it, exactly one caption line, Edit wording first. A top-edge
number is no longer a criterion at all.

## 2026-09-07 — SET-10: WHERE EACH THING THAT WAS ABOVE THE DOCUMENT WENT

**The ruling this implements**, PO, verbatim: *"user does not udnerstand so many
option - you should show what customer is going to get - rest is only for
information"*, with *"thi si very importna to achieve - Preview-first: a big
paper showing the real document"* and *"here 60 is for A big paper showing real
docume nt"*.

**The measurement that made it a defect** (`DEF-NOT-4456`). At 1440×900 the
document's top edge was at **902 px** and the scroll viewport ends at 900: a
person opening any of the 28 notification templates saw **none** of the thing
they opened the screen for. Three blocks stood between the variant tabs and the
paper, each individually correct and each added by a different change — the
test-send refusal (43 px), the *Surfaces* switcher with its heading (88 px), and
a preview strip that was itself two rows (74 px). **It is one shared layout, so
this is one fix and not 28.**

**Where each piece went, and why — this is the part a later lane needs.**

| What | Where it is now | Why there |
|---|---|---|
| the test-send refusal | beside the button it refuses, in the header's action row | a refusal belongs with its control; it is also the only place it reads as an explanation rather than a page-level alarm |
| the *Surfaces* switcher (the other STAGES of this event) | the right rail, after the design's three panels | it is navigation to a sibling document, not a fact about this one |
| Deactivate / Reactivate + *"Not chosen automatically"* | the right rail | a destructive commit is reachable, in the danger tier, and not in front of the thing a person opened the screen to read |
| the surface picker and *Print* | inside the one caption line | the design draws ONE thin line there and this is what fills it |
| *"Preview only"* → *"Nothing here is sent"* | the paper's own caption, under the document | it said *preview* a second time in one screen, and the paper is where the claim belongs when the node is printed |
| the platform-default OFFER (contracts) | the MAIN column | on the four contract classes that block **is** the document — it followed the variant controls into a 320 px rail and had to come back |
| the back link | the shared header's own `backTo` | it was a row of its own costing 59 px on every template |

**What deliberately did NOT move: a refusal.** `RefusalNotice`, the read-only
strip and the *"nobody has written this letter"* strip all still render above the
document. The rule is one sentence — **only something that is absent on a healthy
template may stand between the tabs and the paper** — and a refusal costs zero
pixels when there is nothing to refuse, while a refusal that DOES fire has to be
read before the document it qualifies.

**The 60 belongs to the DOCUMENT (`DEF-NOT-4457`), and the chain is written out
because the number 60 appears in three readings.** E1 asked for a
quarter/three-quarters in the document's favour; CR-076 item 2 read the PO's
*"60"* as the WORDING panel's share on 2026-09-07 and reversed it; the PO settled
it the same day against the running screen. Measured before: wording 662 px,
document 442 px. After: 662 and 442 the other way round, **and the document is
the FIRST column**, so the paper does not jump across the screen when *Edit
wording* is pressed.

⚠ **THE CHECKS THAT GUARDED THE SPLIT COULD NOT TELL THE TWO APART.** The DOM
suite pinned `[3fr_2fr]` and the walkthrough measured *"the rail is 55–65 % of
the frame"*. Both were true of the screen with the wrong pane enlarged. **A ratio
check that does not name its panes passes on its own mirror image** — hard-won
law 7's second question, and the same fault was in
`10-scripts/render-checks/set10-design-conformance.mjs`, corrected in the same
commit.

**The Settings frame was NOT touched, and the options are recorded here so nobody
re-measures them.** At 1440×900 the frame above SET-10 costs 273 px: the
*Settings* H1 and its description (84 px), a nine-tab strip that WRAPS to two
lines (93 px, one line would be 48), the five-tab *Configure* strip (48 px) and
the gaps. The levers, with their measured savings, were: unwrap the nine-tab
strip **−45 px**; drop the H1 and description while a detail is open **−72 px**;
fold the back link into the header **−59 px**; render SET-10 outside the Settings
tab frame **−165 px**. The PO chose to leave the Settings furniture exactly as it
is, so only the back-link fold was taken — it is inside SET-10 and changes no
other screen.

**And then the PO dissolved the problem** (*"you give scroll option in PDF view
area"*): the document pane takes the height left on the screen and scrolls its
own contents. Measured at 1440×1000: the pane is **294 px tall over 1340 px of
letter**, draws a **17 px** scrollbar, reaches its end, and scrolling it does not
move the page.

⚠ **BOUNDING ONLY THE DOCUMENT WOULD HAVE ACHIEVED NOTHING, AND THE NUMBER THAT
PROVED IT CAME FROM A SIBLING LANE.** Measured over all 38 rows this tenant's
catalogue serves, the largest element on the screen was `reading-rail` on **33 of
them** — the rail was bigger than the letter, which is the design's central claim
exactly inverted. A rail left free to grow keeps the page scrolling and stays the
tallest thing on screen, so the rail carries the same measured height. The
document pane is now **229,696 px²** against the rail's **94,720 px²**.

**The height is MEASURED in the browser, not written in CSS.** *"The height left
on the screen"* is not a number a stylesheet can know: the pane's top moves when
the title wraps, when a refusal appears, when a meta line grows. A
`calc(100vh − …)` is right at exactly one viewport and one payload and silently
wrong everywhere else.

**Two top-edge targets were issued and cancelled the same day** — `≤ 240 px`,
then `≤ 560 px`. The walkthrough therefore **records** the top edge and asserts
none: what it asserts is the pane scrolls, its last line is reachable, it draws a
visible scrollbar, it does not scroll the page, and the document is larger than
the rail.

## 2026-09-07 — THE SAMPLE CUSTOMER BECOMES A PERSON, AND WHAT THAT SUPERSEDES

**PO ruling.** `Sample Customer / 1 Sample Street, Sample City / SAMPLE-ACCOUNT`
becomes **`Pat Rivera / 12 Oak Street / AC-000000 / 123.45 USD`**, so a preview
reads *"Hi Pat, your bill for 12 Oak Street is ready… Account AC-000000 … Total
due 123.45 USD"*.

**The signed sentence it supersedes**, from `template_preview.py`'s own header:

> *"a sample that reads like a real utility's real customer is a sample somebody
> screenshots into a ticket"*

**That worry is ANSWERED rather than dismissed, and the answer is `AC-000000`** —
an account number of the right SHAPE, so a System Admin sees what will print,
whose digits are all zero, so no live account can ever hold it. A screenshot of
the pane cannot be mistaken for a customer's record even by someone who has never
seen the product.

**The measurement behind the ruling.** The word *"sample"* appeared **12 times on
the Past-due reminder, 13 on the Payment receipt and 21 on Welcome**. Most of
those were the DATA and not the captions, so tidying captions — which was tried
first, and which took the word *"preview"* from 3 occurrences to 1 — could never
have fixed it.

**FOUR VALUES MOVED AND NO MORE.** `customer_name`, `first_name`,
`service_address` and `account`/`account_no` are what a rendered letter puts in
front of a reader. Every other `SAMPLE-…` identifier — `SAMPLE-BILL`,
`SAMPLE-CYCLE`, `SAMPLE-COMMISSION-REF` — is deliberately unchanged: they appear
in the merge-field rail rather than in the sentence a person reads, and extending
the ruling to them is a decision nobody has taken. **A lane that wants to move
them must put the list to the PO rather than infer it from the four that moved.**

**What did NOT change**: r10's demo utility is still not reused.
*"Required by PUC rule 25.29"* is a regulatory claim this platform has no
business asserting, and a made-up UTILITY name would sit beside the tenant's real
one (`{utility_name}` is stamped from Settings → Company at render, BR-TEN-017)
and read as a second company.

**Version 2.218.8.**

## 2026-09-07 — TAX JURISDICTIONS FOR ALL FIFTY STATES, NAMED BUT NOT PRICED

**The request, verbatim, PO 2026-09-07:** *"Can you have Tax jurisdictions - for
all states - atleast 1 - you seed based on customer selection - if they select
Iowa you seed in Iowa, but you ahve to ahve a list for all 50 states"*.

**And the ruling on the shape, verbatim, the same hour:** put to them as *"the
right jurisdictions and the right authority names for all 50 states, and the
rates left blank for the utility to fill in"*, answered *"yes this is good - you
can have 0 filled in"*.

**Why the shape mattered enough to put back to them.** The Texas set this grew
out of carries WORKED RATES — 6.25% state utility tax, 2.00% local, an $0.85
per-bill PUC fee, a 1.50% city franchise fee, a $0.25/kgal water surcharge — and
a named county, **Bexar**, none of which was ever checked against a real
utility's tax position. Fifty states of that is fifty states of invented tax on
customers' bills, wearing the authority of something the product shipped. The
support-phone precedent decides it: a value the product does not hold is STATED,
never filled with something plausible.

**⚠ BLANK IS NOT ZERO, AND THIS LANE HAS TAKEN *BLANK* — SAID HERE SO THE PO CAN
OVERRULE IT IN ONE WORD.** *"you can have 0 filled in"* reads most naturally as
*having zero rates filled in is fine*, and that is the reading taken. It matters
because the two are different facts and this product already turns on the
distinction (`DEF-127`): **a NULL rate means nobody has answered yet**, and the
screen can say so and refuse to bill on it; **a 0.00 rate means the answer is
none**, which is a real tax position and bills silently at nothing. A seeded
0.00 would look deliberate, compute correct-looking bills, and never once ask
anybody to check it. So every seeded jurisdiction carries its authority and its
level and NO rate, and the plan wizard asks for the figure.

**What each state gets, minimum:** its revenue authority and its utility
commission, correctly named, plus the universal County · City · Special district
scaffold. `ALL` remains the fallback for a tenant that named no state.

⚠ **AND THE `DEF-444` TRAP APPLIES FIFTY TIMES OVER NOW.** The sign-up form does
not require a state. A tenant that signs up without one gets the `ALL` scaffold,
gets a seed-run row at the current version, and could then never receive its own
state's jurisdictions — not from a re-run, not from a version bump. That was
already fixed for Texas by not latching this one list to its run row; the fix
must hold for all fifty and a test must name it, because the failure is silent
and its symptom is *"No tax jurisdictions exist yet"* at plan wizard step 5 with
no customer on any plan able to be taxed.

**A name this lane may not invent either.** Where a state's authority name is not
known with confidence it is left out and reported, not guessed — a wrong
authority on a remittance is a payment sent to the wrong government.

## 2026-09-07 — FOUR RULINGS ON THE SEEDED REFERENCE LISTS

Given together while reading the values of all 27 lists on screen.

### ⓵ Asset statuses lose their second halves
**Verbatim:** *"use only Inventory and Installed"*. `Inventory/Spare` becomes
**Inventory**; `Installed/Active` becomes **Installed**. The other three —
Needs repair, In repair, Retired — are untouched. A slash in a lookup name is
two words competing to be the label, and a clerk reads the first one anyway.
⚠ These are seeded rows a tenant may already hold, so this is a **rename of
existing rows**, not only a fixture edit: a tenant provisioned yesterday has
`Inventory/Spare` in its own table and nothing re-seeds a changed NAME. Whoever
takes this must decide and state whether live rows are migrated.

### ⓶ Account subtypes gain Government
**Verbatim:** *"please add Governtment in it"*. Twelve become thirteen. Note the
shape this sits in: `Government` already exists as an account TYPE (one of the
platform's eight) and now also as a SUBTYPE. That is not a duplicate — the
subtype is the tenant-editable level beneath the type, and a utility that bills
a federal depot differently from a city hall needs the distinction.

### ⓷ Fire size classes ratified
**Verbatim:** *"fire — 2″, 4″, 6″, 8″, 10″, 12″. - these are good"*. ⚠ **THIS
CLOSES `OQ-1360`**, open since the hydrant was removed on 2026-09-03. The
register has said all week that removing `HYD` *"did not close it — the PO took
a row out, they did not ratify the six that remain"*. They have now ratified
the six. The going-live customer's warehouse bills `$60.00` for one 6″ line, and
`$84.00` with two 2″ lines beside it.

### ⓸ Import starters for every import, including the reads
**Verbatim:** *"it is required for - Premises, Units, Meters, Sub meter,s Assets,
Parts, Accounts, Reading - including all readings - Flat, Demand based, Seasonal,
Peak , off peak, etc"*.

Today `IMPORT_TARGETS` names six and four have a starter. The ruling adds two
things that do not exist at all:

* **Parts.** `apps.work.models.Part` is a real table with no import target. A
  utility coming onto the platform with a parts inventory has no way in.
* **Readings, in their several shapes.** A reads import EXISTS
  (`apps.metering.read_import`, with its own `template_csv()`) but it is a
  SEPARATE mechanism from the mapping-template system, so it has no starter and
  cannot be recognised from a saved map. ⚠ **AND THE PO'S CLAUSE
  *"including all readings"* IS THE HARD PART: a flat read is one number, a
  demand read carries a peak kW beside it, and seasonal / peak / off-peak reads
  carry SEVERAL REGISTERS PER METER.** Those are different column shapes, so
  they are different starters — not one Readings template with optional columns,
  which would import a peak register into a flat account without complaint.

**The through-line for whoever builds it:** a starter is GENERATED from the same
target contract that generates the sample file (`BR-AST-048`, `CR-028`), so the
sample always round-trips with zero mapping work and the two cannot drift. Any
new target must be built that way or it is a second copy waiting to disagree.

## 2026-09-07 — WORK ORDER TYPES BECOME TWO LEVELS, AND THE PO SUPPLIED THE LIST

**The PO gave the list itself**, prefaced *"This are the work order types and subtypes"*, as eighteen type/sub-type pairs. Reproduced verbatim, grouped:

| Type | Sub-types |
|---|---|
| **Consumer Complaint** | Low Pressure · No Water Supply · Billing Issues |
| **Meter Maintenance** | Meter Change · Meter Dispose |
| **Preventive Maintenance** | Routine Inspection · Meter Replacement |
| **Connection** | Survey for New Connection · Residential Connection · Commercial Connection · Industrial Connection |
| **Corrective Maintenance** | Leak Repairs · Electrical Line |
| **Infrastructure Development** | Main Extension |
| **Water Quality Monitoring** | Water Pressure |
| **Consumer Services** | Disconnection/Reconnection · Water Truck Services |
| **Reading** | Re-read |

**Nine types, eighteen sub-types.** This SUPERSEDES the eight flat rows seeded
today (Reconnect after payment · Main repair · Disconnect — non-payment · Leak
investigation · Meter exchange · Backflow inspection · Read verification ·
Move-in activation), which the PO had already rejected: *"this is not correct -
you will ahve to think from all Utilty services point of view - and based on
selection you will ahve to add"*.

⚠ **THIS IS A SCHEMA CHANGE, NOT A FIXTURE EDIT, AND THAT IS THE PART A LANE
WILL MISS.** `work_order_types` is a FLAT list today. Two levels means a parent
column, a depth cap, and the refusals that go with them — **the shape `areas`
already has** (`BR-MET-066b`: a row with no parent IS a type, a row with a parent
IS a sub-type, depth enforced in the service and not by a constraint, because SQL
cannot express *"a parent must itself have no parent"* without a trigger and a
trigger would be a second place the rule lives). Follow that precedent rather
than inventing a second posture; `SettingsReferenceData.tsx` already renders a
hierarchical list through `hierarchical: true`.

⚠ **AND THE LIST IS WATER-SHAPED, WHICH IS NOT A CRITICISM — IT IS THE NEXT
QUESTION.** *Low Pressure*, *No Water Supply*, *Water Truck Services*, *Water
Quality Monitoring*, *Main Extension* and *Leak Repairs* are a water utility's
day. The platform bills **eleven** services. Of the other ten only electric
appears, once, as *Electrical Line*. The PO's own earlier ruling says the seeding
follows the services a utility selected at sign-up, so the reading taken here is:
**these nine types are the COMMON spine, and each service contributes its own
sub-types beneath them.** A gas utility gets *Gas leak call-out* under Consumer
Complaint, not a tenth type of its own. That reading is this lane's and is put to
the PO with the proposed per-service sub-types rather than built on silently.

**Two smaller things worth stating before someone re-derives them.** *Reading →
Re-read* means the Work module now has a job type that a meter read can raise,
which is a Work↔Meter Reads seam and must go through the read-only seam file per
`CR-070` §2(a) — Work reads meter reads and writes none of them. And
*Consumer Complaint → Billing Issues* puts a billing complaint in the field-work
module; that is a routing decision, deliberate on the PO's part, and it means a
work order can exist that no crew ever visits.

## 2026-09-07 — THE PER-SERVICE WORK ORDER SUB-TYPES, AND THE SEEDING RULE

**Ruled, verbatim: *"we are good with these"*** — of the twenty-four per-service
sub-types put to the PO — **and of the seeding rule, *"this is also correct"***:
*a utility that picks water and gas gets the eighteen plus the four gas ones; a
water-only utility gets exactly the eighteen and nothing else.*

**The twenty-four, and the type each hangs under:**

| Service | Sub-types | Under |
|---|---|---|
| Gas | Gas leak call-out · Odour complaint | Consumer Complaint |
| Gas | Pressure test · Line purge | Corrective Maintenance |
| Electric | Outage report · Voltage complaint | Consumer Complaint |
| Electric | Transformer fault | Corrective Maintenance |
| Trash | Missed collection · Damaged cart | Consumer Complaint |
| Trash | Container swap | Consumer Services |
| Storm water | Blocked inlet · Flooding | Consumer Complaint |
| Storm water | Inlet clearing | Preventive Maintenance |
| Solar | Inverter fault | Corrective Maintenance |
| Solar | Export config check | Preventive Maintenance |
| Battery | Battery inspection | Preventive Maintenance |
| Broadband | No service · Slow speed | Consumer Complaint |
| Broadband | Drop repair | Corrective Maintenance |
| Thermal | Heat exchanger service | Preventive Maintenance |
| Fire | Flow test · Backflow test | Preventive Maintenance |
| Sewer | Blockage · Backup | Consumer Complaint |

**No new TYPES.** All twenty-four hang under the PO's own nine, which is what
makes the spine-plus-service reading work: a gas utility gets a gas leak
call-out under Consumer Complaint, not a tenth type of its own. **Nine types ·
eighteen base sub-types · twenty-four service sub-types**, so a utility selling
every one of the eleven services sees **forty-two**, and a water-only utility
sees eighteen.

⚠ **ONE WRINKLE THE RULE AS WRITTEN DOES NOT RESOLVE, RECORDED RATHER THAN
QUIETLY FIXED.** The eighteen base sub-types are WATER-SHAPED — *No Water
Supply*, *Water Truck Services*, *Water Pressure* under *Water Quality
Monitoring*, and *Main Extension* and *Leak Repairs* which read as mains work.
Under the rule as ruled, a **gas-only** utility receives all eighteen, water
sub-types included, plus its four. That is what *"a water-only utility gets
exactly your eighteen"* implies read the other way, and it was not put to the PO
in those words.

**The reading taken, and the reason:** seed the eighteen as ruled and do NOT
carve them up by service on our own judgment. Splitting them would mean deciding
which of the PO's own list is water-specific, and *Low Pressure* and *Leak
Repairs* are as true of gas as of water while *Water Truck Services* plainly is
not. That is a judgment about their operations rather than about the software.
**A utility can retire a sub-type it does not want** — these are tenant-editable
rows, not platform constants — so the cost of over-seeding is a row somebody
switches off, while the cost of under-seeding is a job type a crew cannot raise.
Raise it with the PO as an observation when the build lands; do not act on it
first.

## 2026-09-07 — SEVEN ESTIMATION METHODS OFFERED, ONE SEEDED

**The ruling, verbatim, PO 2026-09-07:**

> *"out of 5 oor 7 menthod that we seed in only 3 month avg will be default ,
> system admin can make the changes if they want using remaining method - Im not
> asking you to provide 6 or 7 menthod as default those values need to be
> availabel to system admin"*

**Offered vs seeded is the whole point of the ruling and the distinction is
easy to lose.** The dropdown OFFERS seven. Provisioning SEEDS exactly one —
**Daily average of the last 3 periods** — and it stays selected on every existing
tenant and every new one. The other six exist so a System Admin can choose them;
none is ever applied by us.

**The seven** (the PO added #2 and #7 to five put to them; #6 was this lane's
proposal and is flagged where it stands):

1. **Daily average of the last 3 periods** — today's behaviour · **THE SEEDED DEFAULT**
2. Daily average of the last 6 months
3. Daily average of the last 12 periods
4. The same period last year
5. Repeat the last actual reading
6. Average of similar accounts on the same route — ⚠ *"similar"* is undefined
7. Use the average from the plan — ⚠ see below

**Why the default not moving is a rule and not a preference.** How a missing
reading is estimated decides what a customer is billed. Changing it for a live
tenant as a side effect of shipping a dropdown would alter bills nobody agreed to
alter. So the release adds CHOICE and changes NO BEHAVIOUR, and any tenant whose
estimates change did so because a System Admin chose it.

⚠ **METHOD 7 HAS NO FIGURE BEHIND IT AND THE READING TAKEN IS RECORDED HERE.**
Grepped before writing: `apps/rating/services.py` holds no plan-level average or
expected-usage field, and `budget_billing` in `settings_families.py` carries
`eligibility_months`, `level_rounding`, `relevel_drift_pct`,
`relevel_cadence_months` and `settle_up_month` — machinery for levelling an
ACCOUNT on its own history, not a figure stored on a rate plan. **So *"the
average from the plan"* is read as the levelised amount the account's
budget-billing plan is already running on**, which is the only average-from-a-plan
this product holds and is by construction the figure the utility already decided
that customer's usage averages. An account NOT on a budget plan has no such
average, and that absence must be STATED rather than silently falling through to
another method — an estimate produced by a rule that quietly became a different
rule reaches a customer's bill looking deliberate.

**And the copy this replaces was a rule-32 breach in its plainest form.** The
field's help text read: *"The only ratified method today — offering a second
would answer a question the Product Owner hasn't."* That is our internal decision
process, and our Product Owner, described to a clerk at a water utility. It also
becomes false the moment this ships. It goes regardless of anything else on the
page.

## 2026-09-07 — THE LATE FEE MOVES TO THE CHARGE CODE — RULED, AND **BLOCKED ON A FINANCE RE-SIGN**

**The ruling, verbatim, PO 2026-09-07:**

> *"this is wrong - you ahve to take late fees form charge code mentione din the
> plan - if plan doent provide you that charge code then you have to put zero on
> late payment. - Logic aplplied ot Minimum late fee $5- - you can link these
> defaults in Charge code - we have a charge code for late payment"*

and, on deposit interest:

> *"you ahve to link this to charge code for deposit and use this as default -
> and charge code will be use in billing ; not directly from here"*

Confirmed unchanged in the same message: grace period, grace days counted as,
overcharge guardrail, payment allocation order.

### ⚠ THIS IS NOT BUILDABLE YET AND NOTHING HAS BEEN DISPATCHED

**It changes a ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure, which CLAUDE.md's change process says
means STOP and re-sign via HUMAN-GUIDE §6 — a constraint on us, never a question
we chose to ask.** `GT-10` and `GT-11` both carry a late fee of **$8.13**:
*usage 82.08 + base 18.50 = 100.58 taxable; late fee 8.13 NOT taxable; tax 8.25%
× 100.58 = 8.30; total 117.01* — **re-signed 2026-08-10 by the Product Owner as
finance authority under HUMAN-GUIDE §6**, correcting an arithmetic error of
exactly $1.00.

`apps/billing/decisions.py` was written specifically to make this ruling
impossible by accident. Its own words: *"a charge code carrying an `amount` that
overrode 8.13 would change a frozen figure — a finance re-sign via HUMAN-GUIDE
§6, never an implementation choice. This module therefore reads `id` off the
resolved code and NOTHING ELSE … a function that cannot see `amount` cannot
spend it by accident."* The guard is doing exactly what it was built to do; what
is needed is the signature it is guarding, not a way round it.

### ⚠ AND A CORRECTION THIS LANE OWES: THE ANSWER GIVEN EARLIER TODAY WAS WRONG

Asked *"can I override these in charge codes?"*, this lane answered **No** for
late fee rate, minimum late fee, grace period and grace days counted as. **All
four are already overridable — per PLAN, not per charge code.**
`rating.models.PlanPenaltyRule` is one optional row per plan carrying
`late_fee_min`, `late_fee_pct`, `grace_days` and `grace_mode`, and its own
docstring states the resolution: *"every NULL falls back to the tenant default
(tenant_settings late-fee columns)"*. So the Billing-defaults screen is already
the fallback the PO assumed it should be, and the override already exists one
level up from where they asked for it. The answer was assembled from
`decisions.py`, which is the CHARGE-CODE path, without checking the PLAN path.

### THE OPERATIONAL RISK IN THE *"ZERO"* CLAUSE, STATED WITH ITS MECHANISM

*"if plan doent provide you that charge code then you have to put zero"* is
unambiguous and correct as a rule. Its danger is the migration: **no plan names a
late-fee charge code today, because no such field exists.** So on the day this
ships, every plan on every live tenant provides no charge code, and every late
fee becomes **zero** — silently, on real bills, with no error anywhere. A utility
would simply stop charging late fees and find out from its own revenue.

**So the sequence matters more than the change:** add the field, populate it on
every existing plan (defaulting to the `LATE` code every tenant already has),
prove no plan is unpopulated, and only then switch the engine over. That ordering
is this lane's recommendation, recorded so it is not re-derived under time
pressure.

**Status: RULED, NOT STARTED.** It goes back to the PO with the figure —
$8.13 becomes whatever the plan's charge code says, or zero — and waits for a
`HUMAN-GUIDE §6` re-sign naming that.

## 2026-09-07 — THE LATE-FEE RE-SIGN, GIVEN

**The ruling, verbatim:** *"you capturd it correctly - please apply them - raise
CR if required"* — answering the change put to them in three numbered points and
a stated risk (see the review-ledger row of the same date, which records exactly
what was shown).

**So `CR-078` is raised and the frozen figure is re-signed.** The late fee and
the deposit interest move to the charge code; the Billing-defaults screen becomes
the fallback; a plan naming no charge code charges zero.

⚠ **THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE FIGURE DID NOT MOVE, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT THE
DATA RATHER THAN A CONCESSION.** The seeded `LATE` charge code carries
`percent 1.5, min_amount 5` — **the same two values the Billing-defaults screen
holds** — so `GT-10`'s **$8.13** is $8.13 read from either place. This lane
checked the fixture before putting the change to the PO, and it turned a
frightening ask (*a signed figure changes*) into a small one (*which of two
identical copies the engine reads*). **The lesson is worth more than the
outcome: the size of a change is not knowable from the rule it touches — it is
knowable from the data.**

**And it exposes a duplication of exactly the shape the PO already ruled against.**
`1.5` and `5` are stored twice today: on `tenant_settings` and on the `LATE`
charge code, with the engine reading the first and the screen showing the second.
That is `BR-RAT-080`'s lesson — the base charge on two objects billed `$24.00`
instead of `$12.00`, **`$23,069.50` a month across 1,247 connections**, *"and no
test catches it, because both rows are individually correct and only the rule
makes the total wrong."* This change removes the second copy's ambiguity by
making the charge code the source.

⚠ **A CORRECTION THIS LANE OWES, REPEATED HERE BECAUSE IT SHAPED THE QUESTION.**
Asked earlier the same day whether these could be overridden, this lane answered
**No** for late fee rate, minimum, grace period and grace mode. **All four are
already overridable per PLAN** — `rating.models.PlanPenaltyRule`, one optional
row per plan, *"every NULL falls back to the tenant default"*. The answer was
assembled from `decisions.py`, the charge-code path, without checking the plan
path.

**Not built. The build order is part of the ruling** and is stated in `CR-078`:
add the field, populate every existing plan with `LATE`, prove none is
unpopulated, then switch the engine. Shipping the switch first zeroes every late
fee on every live tenant, silently, on real bills.

## 2026-09-07 — THE FIVE DOCUMENT SHAPES GET FIVE RENDERERS, AND THREE OF THEM DID NOT EXIST

The Product Owner ratified a set of wireframes and a written specification for
SET-10. The governing sentence is theirs, verbatim:

> *"user does not udnerstand so many option - you should show what customer is
> going to get - rest is only for information"*

**The document IS the screen; everything else is a caption.** That sentence is
what the shapes below are for, and it is why this row exists rather than a
comment in a component.

### What was actually true before this

41 template classes — 53 after the same day's ruling — take **five shapes**, and
the screen drew **two** of them as documents. `printable` and `contract` got a
rendered page; `email` got a framed page; **SMS and in-app shared one bordered
box with a desktop measure**. So on three of the five shapes the screen had no
answer to the only question it exists to answer, and a clerk comparing a text
message with a letter was comparing two views of the same box.

Measured in Chromium over **all 38 rows the catalogue serves for `brazosbend`**
at 1440×1000, before any of this landed:

| What was asked | What was found |
|---|---|
| Is the document the largest thing on the page? | **On 3 rows of 38.** On 33 the largest element was `reading-rail` |
| How often does the word *preview* appear outside the document? | **3 times on 30 rows**, twice on 3, once on 5. Never zero |
| Is any visible text printed twice inside the preview? | **Yes, on the 3 disconnect notices** |
| How wide is a text-message bubble? | **352px on all four** — `max-w-[22rem]`, a desktop measure |
| Does a text message say what it costs? | **No, on all four**, unless the editor is open |
| Does the in-app template offer *Send test to me*? | **Yes**, disabled, with nowhere to send it |
| Do the four contracts draw a document? | **No.** All four showed *"Type a body to see it render."* |

### The five shapes, and the rule each one is built on

* **Email — 20 classes.** Subject in bold, sender and recipient beneath a rule,
  then the wording **once**. The header is composed from FIELDS only: no
  expression in it reads a slice of `preview.body`. That is the property that
  makes `DEF-NOT-4464` structurally impossible rather than merely fixed, and it
  is checkable by a reviewer at a glance.
* **Printed page — 8 classes plus `payment_failed_letter`,** whose `group` is
  NULL and which falls back to the page rather than to a blank pane. Unchanged.
* **Text message — 4.** A bubble at **190px**, a phone's own measure, with the
  character count and the message count under it. 160 characters is one message;
  a wording that silently becomes three triples the cost of a send, and on a
  2,000-account run that is real money.
* **Document to sign — 4.** The printed page **plus a signature block where the
  author's own signature line falls** — not appended underneath, because an
  appended block prints the labels twice and puts OUR words for *Customer
  signature* on a document whose author chose their own.
* **In-app — 1.** The banner over a faint sketch of the screen it appears on,
  and one sentence saying its reader is a clerk.

### Three judgments this lane made, with their reasoning

**⓵ The signature line is PARSED, never matched against English.** The separator
is a run of two or more spaces and the label ends at the first colon; nothing in
the renderer knows the word *signature* in any language. The body is the
TENANT's text, so a utility that rewrites its agreement in Spanish still gets a
block — B14 rule 35's principle applied to the one place on this screen where
the words belong to the customer rather than to us. A line that does not parse
returns null and is drawn as the prose it is: **a contract whose signature line
we cannot read is a contract we draw exactly as its author typed it.**

**⓶ The SMS meter is ADDED to the document, not MOVED there.** The first plan
was to move it out of the composer, on the reasoning that two live counts can
disagree. That would have deleted a signed requirement: CR-048 E2 says in as
many words that the counter *"belong[s] BESIDE THE WORDS BEING TYPED, not in a
validation message after saving"*. Both now read the same served
`rendered_length`, and the document's count is drawn only when a preview exists
— so the two can never disagree, and the writer and the reader each get the fact
where they are.

**⓷ The in-app *Send test to me* is ABSENT, not disabled.** BR-SHL-025 says a
control renders disabled WITH its reason rather than being hidden, and that rule
is right for a control a person could otherwise expect to use — what stops it is
a fact they can act on. `staff_bulk_summary` is not that case: it is a banner
drawn inside this product, so there is no address, no inbox and no handset, and
no setting anybody could change would give it one. **A disabled button is still
an offer.** The whole wrapper goes, not just the button, or an empty flex column
and a stray note are left behind.

### And one finding about the checks themselves

`DEF-SHL-4477`. The only check in this repo that can tell a real Tailwind
utility from a dead one — `routeBUtilities.test.ts`, which loads the actual
compiler — reads class names from `className="…"` literals and from constants in
files named `*Kit.ts`. **A component that keeps its classes in module-level
constants and writes `className={CONSTANT}` is read by neither**, which is
ordinary React and is what the new renderer file did. Measured: `bg-red-500`
planted in one such constant and all ten tests passed, over a class this theme
deliberately deletes.

The constants moved to `templateSurfacesKit.ts` and the same planted class then
went RED naming the file. **That fixes one file.** The general widening was
attempted and is recorded as not shippable: reading every module-level constant
in all 221 migrated files reports 23 orphans that are not classes at all —
locale keys, enum values, a route — because a lowercase word meant for `t()` is
utility-shaped, and a false-positive flood is what gets a grammar switched off
(DEF-323). Scoping it to constants the same file hands to `className` cuts that
to 5, still all false. **The distinguishing signal is a value built only from
string literals**, and a lane taking this on should start there and must print
its false-positive count before trusting it.

## 2026-09-07 — THE ARCHIVER RUNS PER TENANT, AND THE PORTAL OFFERS TWO LANGUAGES

Two open questions closed in one message.

### ⓵ The audit archiver — option (b), ruled

**The problem, as put to the PO:** *"When we file away old audit records, the
counter reads them with nobody's identity attached — so it counts zero over
records that are really there, and writes a receipt saying nothing was
archived."* Three options were offered with their costs. **Ruled: (b) — run it
once per utility, so it reads inside each one's identity.** The PO's own words on
the cost: *"It's the only one that keeps your ruling intact. The cost is a slower
nightly job, which nobody watches."*

**This closes `OQ-AUD-1724` and unblocks `DEF-AUD-4080`.** Those two isolation
cases have been the ONLY red in the tenant-isolation suite since the commercial
tables were fixed this morning — `2 failed, 267 passed` — and they are red
because `core.archival._manifest` and `._tenants_in` read the partition on a bare
cursor with no `app.tenant_id`, so on the NOSUPERUSER role production actually
uses they see zero rows over a partition holding two.

⚠ **THE OPTION NOT TAKEN IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN EASIEST, AND THAT IS THE
POINT.** Option (a) — let the job read across all utilities — is one line, and it
breaks the PO's own ruling of 2026-08-24 against `BYPASSRLS` (`OQ-354`). The
tests that fail today were written to REFUSE that repair: their own comment says
*"These assertions are RIGHT and stay exactly as they are: adjusting them would
turn a live defect into a passing test."* They held for two weeks and the ruling
has now come the other way.

**What must be true when it is built:** the isolation suite reports **0 failed**,
and the archiver's receipt names a real row count and a checksum of real bytes
rather than the digest of the empty string. A green suite with a receipt still
reading zero is the same defect wearing a passing test.

### ⓶ The portal offers English and Spanish only

**Ruled, verbatim:** *"currently in drop down show only 2 elnglish and spanish"*.
This implements the PO's ruling of 2026-09-05 (*"Portal languages: English and
Spanish only"*), which `DEF-CWP-4442` has carried unbuilt because narrowing the
list had a customer-data question attached.

**The reading taken on that attached question, recorded because the PO ruled on
the OFFER and not on the stored value.** `PORTAL_LOCALES` offers eleven today and
some accounts already hold `de` or `hi`. **Nobody's stored choice is reset.** A
customer whose account says German keeps reading German until they change it —
resetting it would take a setting away from a person who chose it, to solve a
problem they do not have.

⚠ **BUT A PICKER THAT LISTS TWO OPTIONS OVER A STORED THIRD RENDERS BLANK, AND
THAT IS THE FAILURE THE ORIGINAL DEFECT WARNED ABOUT.** So both pickers — the
guest dropdown in the portal's top menu and the customer's own preference on
*My details* — list **English and Spanish, plus the reader's OWN current language
where it is neither**, shown as what it is rather than silently dropped. Choosing
away from it is one click and irreversible by design: once a customer moves to
English or Spanish, German stops being offered to them too.

**The seeded default is unaffected** — a tenant's regional setting still decides
what a guest sees first, and a tenant set to something outside the two is a
separate question nobody has raised.

## 2026-09-07 — THE FIFTY-STATE TAX CATALOGUE IS BUILT, AND FOUR JUDGMENTS IT NEEDED

`CR-077`. The ruling itself is two entries above; this is what was built, and the
four places the rules ran out and a decision had to be made and written down.

**WHAT A UTILITY GETS.** `tax_jurisdictions` goes from **2 keys to 53** — `TX`,
`ALL`, and every remaining code in `tenancy.selectors.US_STATES`. A tenant that
names Iowa holds five jurisdictions: **Iowa Department of Revenue · Iowa Utilities
Commission · County · City · Special district**. **Not one of the 102 new rows
carries a figure**, and that is structural rather than careful: an entry states no
`taxes` block at all, and `rating.services._seed_fixture_taxes` mints a tax row
only from a stated figure, so there is nothing to price from. Fixture V2.48.0.9.

### ⓵ FIFTY-TWO KEYS AND NOT FIFTY, BECAUSE THE PLATFORM'S OWN LIST SAYS SO
The PO said *"all 50 states"*. The sign-up form accepts **52** values —
`US_STATES` is the fifty plus **DC** and **Puerto Rico** — and a state a utility
can SELECT and cannot be SEEDED for is `DEF-444`'s shape one layer up. So the
catalogue is pinned to that vocabulary by a test rather than to a list typed into
a fixture, and no other territory is added: a key nobody can select would be a
list nobody reads. **Puerto Rico's regulator covers ENERGY** (the Puerto Rico
Energy Bureau), so an island water utility answers elsewhere and edits the row —
which is what an editable seeded name is for, and is stated rather than hidden.

### ⓶ IOWA'S REGULATOR IS THE IOWA UTILITIES *COMMISSION*, AND THE BRIEF SAID BOARD
The lane was told, in writing, that Iowa should produce *"Iowa Department of
Revenue and Iowa Utilities Board"*. **The Iowa Utilities Board was renamed the
Iowa Utilities Commission on 2024-07-01** after 38 years, under Senate File 2385;
board members became commissioners and the site moved to `iuc.iowa.gov`. Checked
against the agency's own announcement rather than recalled. **Seeding the name in
the brief would have shipped a body that no longer exists onto a remittance
screen**, which is the exact failure the *"never invent an authority name"*
instruction exists to prevent — so the current name is seeded and the correction
is recorded here in case anybody goes looking for the old one. **West Virginia**
is the same shape and was checked the same way: the body formerly styled the West
Virginia State Tax Department writes itself the **West Virginia Tax Division**
today (`tax.wv.gov`).

### ⓷ TEXAS IS NOT RESTYLED, ALTHOUGH IT NOW READS DIFFERENTLY FROM THE OTHER 51
Texas's five rows are named `Texas State`, `Local`, `Texas Public Utility
Commission`, `City` and `Texas Water Development Board` — a transcription of
prototype r10's own tax table, ruled by the PO on 2026-08-18 with its figures. The
fifty-one new sets name their authorities directly (*Iowa Department of Revenue*),
so the two conventions differ on screen. **The ruled transcription is left exactly
as signed**: restyling it would move rows on a shipped screen and edit a signed
figure's row for cosmetic reasons. A test asserts the Texas rates are still there,
beside the test that asserts nothing else has one — because *"no rate anywhere"*
is one careless edit away from *"the 2026-08-18 ruling was deleted"*.

### ⓸ A CHECK WAS WIDENED TWICE, AND BOTH TIMES AFTER CHECKING THE STATE
The test that asserts every state names a revenue body and a regulator does it by
the words those bodies use for themselves. It went red on **Arkansas** — whose
collector is the *Department of Finance and Administration*, with no "Department
of Revenue" to name — and on **Puerto Rico**, whose regulator calls itself a
*Bureau*. Both words were added to the list **after** confirming the body, not to
make a red go away, and both are recorded in the test beside the word they added.

**NO MONEY PATH TURNS AN ABSENT RATE INTO A ZERO — CHECKED, BECAUSE IT WAS THE
ONE THING THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THIS CHANGE DANGEROUS.** Three layers all refuse
rather than default: `rating.selectors.plan_tax_rules` produces **no rule** for a
jurisdiction with no percent rate (*"a zero rate says this authority charges
nothing, which is a claim"*), `pricing.stages.compute_tax._tax_amount` raises
`TaxRuleUnpriceable` for a rule carrying none of the three forms, and the seeder
skips a fixture tax with no figure. So a seeded jurisdiction with no rate produces
**no tax line**, which is the visible absence the plan wizard can report.

## 2026-09-07 — IMPORT STARTERS FOR PREMISES AND UNITS, AND WHAT IS NOT BUILT

`BR-AST-048` as amended. `premises` and `units` gain a generated default
(*Premises default*, *Units default*), so all six import TARGETS have a starter and
both samples round-trip through the real extract endpoint with **zero mapping
work** — asserted by uploading the generated sample and reading back
`recognised_template` and the full 1:1 detected mapping.

**THE ONE THING WORTH KNOWING FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE REST.** The four existing
starters read their columns from `EXPLICIT_COLUMNS_BY_TARGET`, a DECLARED map, and
premises and units DERIVE theirs from the model's own `_meta` (`BR-MET-088`). So
the generator raised `KeyError('premises')` and the fix was not to declare their
columns — it was to read **`sample_columns`**, which is the list `sample_csv`
itself writes and answers for a target by either route. That is what makes the
round trip true by construction rather than by coincidence, and it is the property
`BR-AST-048` was written to protect.

### WHAT THE 2026-09-07 RULING ASKED FOR AND THIS LANE DID NOT BUILD
Named here so neither is quietly dropped, and so the next lane starts from a
measurement rather than from the list of words in the request:

* **Parts** — `apps.work.models.Part` is a real table with **no import target at
  all**. It is also the `work` module's table, and metering's importer writing
  into it would be a cross-module write; so this is an architecture question
  (whose importer, and through which seam) before it is a build.
* **Readings, in their several shapes.** `apps.metering.read_import` is a
  SEPARATE importer with its own `template_csv()`, so it has no starter and
  cannot be recognised from a saved map. ⚠ **HOW MANY SHAPES, MEASURED FROM THE
  RATING SIDE RATHER THAN FROM THE PO'S WORD LIST — the answer is FOUR, and one
  of the five words in the request is not a read shape at all.** The engine
  registers **six** pricing models (flat · tiered · time_of_use · demand ·
  capacity · percent_of_service) and `meter_reads.channel` carries **seven**
  registers (total · tou_on · tou_mid · tou_off · export · demand · generation).
  Neither number is the answer, because the reads file already carries `channel`
  as a column — one row per register. What actually differs is **which rows must
  be present per meter per date**:
    1. **flat / tiered / percent-of-service** — one `total` row;
    2. **time of use** — three rows, one per TOU register; a file with one of
       them silently under-bills;
    3. **demand** — a `total` row and a `demand` row, and `demand_reset` is
       meaningful only on the second (`BR-MET-051`, which already has an error
       code for it on the wrong channel);
    4. **net metering / export** — a `total` row and an `export` row sharing a
       `read_at` (`BR-AST-029`).
  **Capacity bills on a size class and reads no meter at all**, and **SEASONAL IS
  NOT A READ SHAPE**: a season is a property of the tariff (`rate_seasons`,
  `rate_tiers.season_id`) resolved from the service DATE, so a seasonal read is a
  flat read on a date. Building a fifth starter for it would teach a file shape
  that does not exist.

⚠ **AND ONE THING FOUND WHILE MEASURING THAT, REPORTED NOT FIXED:** `seasonal` is
an accepted value of `TARIFF_MODELS` and has **no registered pricing plugin**, so
a tenant can save a rate schedule the engine cannot price. It fails CLOSED (the
registry raises, naming the model and listing what is registered), so it is not a
money defect — but it is a control offering something that does not exist, which
is hard-won law 2's shape. Not this lane's module.

## 2026-09-07 — READ VALIDATION & ESTIMATION: A PAGE THAT STOPPED IN SILENCE, TWO COLUMNS THAT NEVER LINED UP, AND A METHOD THAT BECAME A CHOICE

`DEF-MET-4480` · `DEF-MET-4479` · `DEF-MET-4489` · `CR-079` · `OQ-MET-1761` · `OQ-MET-1762` · `OQ-MET-1763`

### 1 · WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THE MISSING SECTIONS, AND HOW IT WAS PROVED

The Product Owner had two screenshots of one URL minutes apart: one carried Electric,
Water, Sewer, Trash and Storm water; the other ended after the integrity chips with a
truncated panel border and nothing else. Three explanations were possible and **two are
now ruled out by experiment in a browser rather than by argument**:

* **an exception thrown after the integrity block — DISPROVED.** Fed a null unit and a
  missing switch map, this screen does not lose its lower half: React Router's default
  error boundary replaces **the whole application** with *"Unexpected Application Error!"*
  and a stack trace. The navigation does not survive, let alone the chips. So whatever the
  Product Owner saw, it was not a render error.
* **the estate probe failing with nothing drawn — DISPROVED.** `GET /assets/metered-services`
  answering 500 changes not one section: `BR-TEN-162` clause 3's fail-toward-showing works.
* **`services: []` — REPRODUCED EXACTLY.** Switch the tenant's services off and the page
  draws its intro, its integrity panel and its seven chips, then maps an empty array and
  draws **nothing**, with the estimation panel's top border cut by the fold. That is the
  reported screenshot down to the truncated border. It is reachable in ordinary use: the
  Services & UoM tab is two clicks away and a service switched off between two loads
  empties this page with no explanation.

**THE FIX IS THE GENERAL FORM, NOT THE INSTANCE.** An empty list is a FACT about the
tenant, so it is stated — *"No services are switched on, so there is nothing to check yet
— switch one on under Services & UoM and it appears here."* And every service the server
sends now carries `data-service-listed`, metered or not, so a check can ask whether the
page is the whole picture without reading our source. `10-scripts/render-checks/def-met-4480-read-validation.mjs`
asks exactly that, against the server's own answer.

### 2 · WHY DEF-900's ALIGNMENT FIX COULD NEVER HAVE WORKED

**MEASURED at 1440px before the change:** `rv-electric-days_hard_min` at y=1450 against
`rv-electric-days_hard_max` at y=1398 — **52px apart in one row**. DEF-900 had reached for
`grid-rows-subgrid` so that labels, help lines and inputs each got a shared row.
**Subgrid assigns children to tracks IN SOURCE ORDER.** A field WITH help has three
children and a field WITHOUT help has two, so the second field's INPUT lands on the HELP
row. The rows whose two fields happened to have the same shape lined up perfectly, which
is why it looked as though the fix worked.

**The cure is structural: no field in this grid carries help at all**, so every `.field`
has the same children and the inputs cannot disagree. All five pairs now share a top edge
to the pixel. The floor's unit rides its LABEL — *"High-use floor (kWh)"* — which honours
hard rule 3 at no cost in lines, and the hard-window constraint is already stated by the
refusal that fires when it is broken, at the moment it matters, under the field that broke
it.

### 3 · B14 RULE 32 — 21 SENTENCES BECAME 8

Counted on the Product Owner's own page (five services, Electric open, three unmetered
sections closed): **21 descriptive sentences before, 8 after.** Four per-field help lines
are gone. The two-sentence page intro, the integrity paragraph, the per-service summary,
the checks hint and the locked reason are each one sentence now.

**A JUDGMENT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS OURS TO MAKE.** `DEF-901` gave every unmetered
service its own collapsed panel carrying two sentences — *"You have no Sewer meters, so no
Sewer reading is ever taken…"*. That was right about the ABSENCE and wrong about the
WEIGHT: a tenant selling eleven services and metering two got nine near-identical
paragraphs. They are now **one line naming every unmetered service**, with its badge, and
one sentence. `BR-TEN-162` clause 2 is not weakened — the clause exists because a silently
missing section is indistinguishable from a broken page, and every service is still named
on screen with the reason.

### 4 · THE SAVE BUTTON CANNOT LOSE AN EDIT, AND NOW IT SAYS SO

Every save on this page is **per service** — `PUT /settings/read-validation/{service}` —
so *"Save Water thresholds"* saves water and nothing else. **Clicked and confirmed in a
browser:** type into Electric, save Water, and Electric still holds what was typed with
its own Save button live. What the page did NOT do was say so: `Disclosure` unmounts a
closed body, so collapsing a panel with edits in it took the Save button away with the
edits and left no sign either existed. The header now carries **Unsaved changes** when the
panel is dirty, shown closed as well as open.

### 5 · `CR-079` — THE ESTIMATION METHOD BECOMES A CHOICE OF SEVEN

**PO verbatim, 2026-09-07:** *"this should be drop down options - give 4 to 5 options
here"*, then, after five were proposed: *"we are good with these + add last 6 month avg +
Use avg from plan"*.

Until that day `est_method` accepted exactly one value (`BR-MET-026`) and the field was a
read-only box carrying this sentence: *"The only ratified method today — offering a second
would answer a question the Product Owner hasn't."* **That sentence is deleted.** It told a
clerk about our Product Owner and our internal decision process, which is B14 rule 32's
clearest breach in the product, and it became false the moment the dropdown landed.

**THE SEVEN, and which are running:**

| method | what it does | runs? |
|---|---|---|
| `trailing_3_daily_avg` | the signed formula, three periods — **the DEFAULT, unmoved** | yes |
| `trailing_6_daily_avg` | the same formula, six periods | yes |
| `trailing_12_daily_avg` | the same formula, twelve periods | yes |
| `same_period_last_year` | the twelfth actual back, on its own | yes — see `OQ-MET-1763` |
| `repeat_last_actual` | the same formula, one period | yes |
| `route_peer_average` | — | **no** — `OQ-MET-1761` |
| `plan_average` | — | **no** — `OQ-MET-1762` |

**THE ARITHMETIC DID NOT MOVE AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHY THIS WAS SAFE TO BUILD.** Every
runnable method is Σ consumption ÷ Σ days × days in period over a different SELECTION of
the same actual reads. `GT-9` ❄️ reproduces byte-for-byte — 612 + 618 + 624 over 90 days →
20.600000/day → **618.000000** — and its branch is still `trailing_actuals[:3]`.

**NOTHING MIGRATES A STORED ROW.** Changing how a missing reading is estimated changes
what a customer is billed; it has to be a choice somebody makes, not a side effect of a
release.

**THE TWO THAT CANNOT RUN ARE OFFERED AND NOT SELECTABLE**, refused in three places — a
disabled `<option>` carrying its reason, the form, and the server — and `estimate()`
answers `estimation_method_not_implemented` rather than falling through to a different
rule. **A reading estimated by a rule that quietly became another rule bills a customer
under a rule nobody chose**, which is the worst outcome available on this screen.

**FIVE READINGS ARE OURS, NOT THE PO's, AND EACH CAN BE CORRECTED IN ONE WORD:**

1. **The five method names of the first proposal were ours.** The PO approved the list; the
   wording of options 2–6 came from us.
2. ***"last 6 month avg"* is built as SIX BILLING PERIODS**, not 180 days. On a monthly
   cycle they are the same thing, and expressing it as a period count means no date
   arithmetic and no invented threshold.
3. ***"The same period last year"* is the twelfth actual period counting back**, used on
   its own. `EstimationInput` carries day counts and no dates. `OQ-MET-1763`.
4. ***"Repeat the last actual reading"* is that period's daily rate × this period's days**,
   not its raw consumption — periods differ in length and the daily rate is the signed
   formula's own unit.
5. ***"Use the average from the plan"* is read as the levelised amount an account's
   budget-billing plan is already running on** — the only *"average from a plan"* this
   product holds. `OQ-MET-1762` puts it to the PO with the absence case, which is the
   harder half.

`route_peer_average`'s definition of *similar* was never put to anybody: same account
type, same size class, or the whole route are three different rules wearing one sentence,
and on a route carrying the industrial plant the three answers are not close. Stubbed and
raised (`OQ-MET-1761`) rather than picked — an estimate becomes a bill.

### 6 · `DEF-MET-4489`, FOUND WHILE WALKING THE PAGE

`row_key` and `unit_mismatch` rendered as raw internal codes among thirteen English rule
names. Two rules joined the engine's judgment list without their wording, and **a key
absent from all eleven catalogues is parity-perfect to G15** — the only check that reads
catalogues compares them with each other. Fixed; the new render-check refuses any bare
snake_case token in clerk-facing text.

### 7 · TWO REDS I DID NOT CAUSE, DATED

* **G15 is RED and was before this lane started:** *"184 NEW value(s) pasted in English
  rather than translated"*, naming `de :: integrations.keys.versionSuffix` among others.
  `git log -S "integrations.keys.versionSuffix" -- 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/de.json`
  dates it to `91efe69c`, **2026-09-06**, 1,326 commits before HEAD. This lane's wording
  moved the untranslated count DOWN, not up: 21 keys added and 9 retired, every one written
  in each of the eleven languages rather than pasted from English.
* **A defect id collided mid-push.** `allocate.py defect --verify 4487` said TAKEN, 4488
  was allocated and ALSO taken by a sibling between allocation and push — and the verify
  line was printed and not read, so the duplicate reached the branch for one commit before
  being renumbered to `DEF-MET-4489` by a byte splice. **The check fired and was not read**,
  which is hard-won law 7 in one line, on the lane that had just written a paragraph about
  it.

## 2026-09-07 — BUILDING THE PER-UTILITY ARCHIVER: FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULING DID NOT MAKE

The PO ruled the SHAPE earlier today — *"run it once per utility, so it reads
inside each one's identity"* — and closing `OQ-AUD-1724` / `DEF-AUD-4080`
required four decisions underneath it that the ruling does not settle and that
nobody should have to re-derive. Written down here rather than left in
`core/archival.py`'s docstring alone, because three of them change what a
recorded figure MEANS.

**The measurement, first, because it is what the whole thing was for.** On the
same two seeded rows that produced the defect, the run record went from
`row_count: 0`, `sha256: e3b0c44298fc…7852b855` — **the digest of the empty
string** — to `row_count: 2`, `sha256: ceabc86bb357…6b99c78f`, with both
per-utility self-audit rows written and each carrying its own tenant's id.

### ⓵ THE PARTITION DIGEST IS NOW A FOLD, AND OLD DIGESTS ARE NOT COMPARABLE

The manifest's `sha256` was `sha256(md5(every row's text, ctid order))` over the
whole partition. **No statement can see a whole partition any more** — that is
the entire point of the ruling — so that number cannot be computed at all. It is
now a FOLD: each utility's slice gets its own `sha256(md5(its rows))`, and the
partition's digest is `sha256` over `<tenant id>:<that digest>` lines sorted by
tenant id, one line per utility WITH ROWS.

Three consequences worth stating. It still moves if any column of any row moves
by one character, which is what the manifest exists for. **A digest recorded
before today is not comparable with one recorded after**, so a verifier reading
a 2026-08 run record has to be told which shape it is checking — the open
question raised exactly this cost and it is real, not hypothetical. And a
utility with no rows in the partition contributes NO line, so provisioning a new
customer does not move any digest.

### ⓶ WHAT A UTILITY IS TOLD ABOUT ITS OWN ARCHIVAL IS NOW ITS OWN FIGURES

The self-audit row each utility gets used to carry the PARTITION's row count —
every utility's rows added together. It now carries that utility's own count and
its own digest. This is not tidying: `apps/audit/services.write_archive_audit`
already promised in its own docstring that each tenant *"learns nothing about
anyone else's"*, and a partition-wide total tells every utility roughly how much
traffic its neighbours make. The platform record (`archive_job_runs`) keeps the
total, which is where an operator needs it.

### ⓷ A PARTITION THAT CANNOT BE FULLY ACCOUNTED FOR IS NOT TOUCHED

Reading N utilities instead of 1 introduces a failure mode that did not exist:
one utility's read failing part-way. Swallowing it and carrying on would produce
a manifest that UNDER-REPORTS — which is `DEF-AUD-4080` again in a quieter form,
data filed away under a receipt that does not describe it. Letting it raise
would stop the whole nightly job for one utility.

**Ruled: the partition is left exactly where it is, and the run says so.** The
run is recorded with status `partial` and a note naming the partition and how
many utilities of how many could not be read. `archive_status` already surfaces
`last_run_status` and `last_run_note` on S61, so this is visible with no new
screen and no new column. Archival is idempotent by construction, so a deferral
costs a month at worst and never a double detachment. `status` gains a third
value — `success | skipped | partial`.

⚠ **AND THE LOOP TAKES A SAVEPOINT PER UTILITY, WHICH IS HARD-WON LAW 14 AND NOT
A STYLE CHOICE.** On PostgreSQL a failed statement aborts the whole transaction
and every later query raises `InFailedSqlTransaction`, so `except: continue`
loses the run at COMMIT anyway. The default suite is in-memory SQLite, which has
no aborted-transaction state and **cannot show this**, so the case that proves it
(`tests/test_us_aud_007_tc_archival.py::…one_utility_failing_holds_the_partition…`)
injects a REAL database error, `SELECT 1 / 0`, and asserts the connection still
works afterwards. The savepoint sits INSIDE `tenant_context`, not outside it,
because clearing the tenant GUC on the way out is itself a statement and would
raise on an aborted transaction.

### ⓸ THE TENANT LIST IS READ DIRECTLY, NOT THROUGH A REGISTERED SEAM

Every other collaborator of `core/archival.py` is a seam — `set_run_recorder`,
`set_self_auditor`, `set_cold_store_shipper` — because core must not import an
app model (B8 layering). **A seam for the tenant list would be different in
kind: an unregistered one yields NOTHING, which is bit-for-bit the failure this
whole change exists to end.** A missing table raises. So the run reads `tenants`
by name in SQL, exactly as this module already reads `audit_log` and
`meter_reads` by name, and no model import happens.

`tenants` is a platform table — no `tenant_id`, no policy — which is what makes
that read lawful under hard rule 1. **That claim is CHECKED rather than
trusted:** the run asks `pg_class.relrowsecurity` first and REFUSES by name if
`tenants` ever gains a policy. Without it, a future migration would make the
enumeration return nobody, every partition would manifest as empty, and every
test in the repository would pass over it — no test can assert a row count it
does not already know. The guard was proved to fire by switching row-level
security on for `tenants` inside a test.

**Every row of the registry is walked, `deleted_at` included and no filter at
all.** A soft-deleted utility still has rows in a partition until BR-TEN-044's
day-91 purge takes them, and skipping it would under-report by exactly those
rows.

⚠ **WHAT THE SUM STILL CANNOT SEE, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** It is complete
only if every row's `tenant_id` names a row of the registry. `meter_reads.tenant_id`
is an FK to `tenants`, so there it is complete by constraint. `audit_log.tenant_id`
is deliberately NOT an FK (`BR-AUD-015` — the trail must survive a tenant purge),
so there it rests on `BR-TEN-044` instead: the PO ruled on 2026-08-10 that the
day-91 offboarding purge DELETES that tenant's audit rows, so a row whose tenant
has left the registry is not supposed to exist. The entry records `tenants_read`
— how many identities the run entered — so a reader can tell a genuinely empty
partition from an enumeration that found nobody.

### THE COST, MEASURED

The PO accepted *"a slower nightly job, which nobody watches"*. Measured on
PostgreSQL 16 rather than estimated: one partition holding **40,000 rows across
5 utilities, on a 40-utility deployment**, takes **414 ms** to account for. The
same partition took **1–2 ms** before — and that figure was fast because it was
reading nothing and returning `0`. A utility with no rows in the partition costs
about **4 ms** (an index probe on the `(tenant_id, created_at, id)` primary key
and a round trip), so the loop grows with the tenant count and with nothing else.
No cap is introduced anywhere (`NFR-5`): it walks whatever the registry holds.

One thing got CHEAPER and is worth noting for a large deployment: the old
`string_agg` materialised every row of the partition in one statement, and the
per-utility version materialises one utility's share.
