## 2026-09-07 — THE ONE-INVOCATION CURE FOR DEF-GOV-4485 DOES NOT WORK, AND THE WORKTREE DOES

`DEF-GOV-4485` was filed this session with a prescription in its `prevention`
column: *"re-derive the blob from the pinned tip and push in ONE shell
invocation, so no other lane can write between the two."* **That prescription is
wrong and this row exists to say so before anyone follows it**, because a wrong
prevention in the register is worse than an empty one — it reads as a solved
problem.

### What was tried, and what it cost

The mechanism: `push_paths.sh` hashes the WORKING-TREE bytes of each named path
at push time. In a shared tree a sibling can rewrite that file between the moment
you write your bytes and the moment the script reads them.

It happened **three times in one session**, and the one-invocation fix was in
place for the third:

| Attempt | What was measured | What was pushed |
|---|---|---|
| First | a 107-line decision-log append | a sibling's 45-line append; mine dropped |
| Second | (recovered by re-deriving and pushing in one command) | correct, 107/0 |
| Third | `git diff --numstat` reporting a correct **7/7** | **three rows belonging to another lane**, and none of the seven |

**The third attempt did everything the prescription asks.** Re-derived from the
pinned tip, seven closures applied, numstat read as arithmetic and correct, all
inside one shell invocation. The sibling's write landed between the numstat and
the hash — a window of milliseconds inside a single command, which the
prescription cannot close because the two operations are not atomic with respect
to another process's `write()`.

⚠ **AND THE COMMIT MESSAGE IS THE REAL DAMAGE, NOT THE DIFF.** `ecfeada3` states
that it closes seven named defects. It closes none of them. A wrong diff is
caught by the next reader; **a confident message describing work that was not
done tells every future reader those rows are closed and not to look.** That is
the same failure as calling a red *pre-existing* without dating it — a false
record that suppresses the next investigation. Nothing was lost either time: the
register's row count is unchanged at 2236 and no id is missing.

### What actually works

**Do not share the tree.** Every guard in hard-won law 11 and in
`push_paths.sh` asks whether a path moved ON THE BRANCH; none of them can ask
whether the file on disk is still the one you wrote, and in a shared tree that is
a different question. In a private `git worktree` the question does not arise,
because no other process can reach the bytes. The seven closures went in cleanly
at `1882d37f` from `/home/user/wt-set10-checks`, first attempt, 7/7.

**The generalisable half, and it is about a check rather than about git:**
`git diff --numstat` is law 11's own prescribed catch for revert-by-subtraction,
and it earned that place — it caught the first two occurrences here. But it
measures the file **as it was when the command ran**, and the push hashes the
file **as it is when the push runs**. In a shared tree those are two different
files, so the check is evidence about the past rather than about what shipped. In
a private worktree they are the same file. **Same command, different guarantee,
and the difference is the tree and not the command.**

⚠ **AND THE GUARANTEE IS NARROWER THAN IT FIRST READS — a worktree answers ONE
of the two threats.** The first draft of this row said a private worktree makes
`--numstat` *"a check on the actual state, because nobody else can touch the
bytes"*, and that is true of SIBLINGS and false in general. Law 11's last clause
already records the other threat (`DEF-CWP-3771`): the numstat measures against
the **pinned tip**, and the tip is by definition the world without your own
uncommitted work in it — so your committed-but-unpushed work sits in exactly that
blind spot. A lane inside a private worktree that re-derives a file it has
already committed to this session can still subtract its own earlier hunks, and
the numstat will read zero deletions, **correctly**.

So the honest formulation: **a private worktree turns `--numstat` from a check on
a past state into a check on the current state WITH RESPECT TO OTHER LANES, and
changes nothing about your own earlier self.** The second half still needs law
11's existing remedy — diff against **your own previous commit on that file**,
not against the tip. Written without that qualifier the clause reads *"worktree,
therefore safe"*, and sends the next lane straight into the one case a worktree
does not cover. (Caught in review by the sibling lane, not by this one.)

**Practical rule:** a lane that writes to any shared register — the defect log,
the decision log, the open questions, the review ledger — should dispatch itself
into its own `git worktree` first. CLAUDE.md law 12 already calls this *the
cheapest lesson here*; this row is the third demonstration in one session that it
is also the only one that works.


### The second finding, and it may be the more valuable one

**The commit MESSAGE was worse than the diff.** `ecfeada3`'s diff is wrong and a
wrong diff is caught by the next reader. Its message states that it closes seven
named defects, and *that* is what stops the next reader looking at all. **It is
the same shape hard-won law 7 already names in a different costume** — calling a
red *pre-existing* without dating it, where two confident reports in good faith
told every subsequent reader not to investigate a true failure.

Put beside each other the two stop being anecdotes and become one rule:
**a confident claim about work you did not verify is more expensive than the
work being wrong**, because the error is self-correcting and the claim is not.
The remedy in both cases is the same and it is cheap: state what you actually
checked, and date it.
## 2026-09-07 · THE CONNECTION HALF OF THE SAMPLE ESTATE — why nine services billed nothing, the fire line gets an asset type, and every meter stops being the smallest one (`DEF-MET-4496`, `DEF-AST-4493`, `DEF-AST-4494`, `DEF-AST-4495`, `OQ-1361`)

**The report that started it said the seeded tenant sells all eleven services and
that nothing connects a unit to nine of them. The first half was not true, and
finding that out changed the whole job.**

⚠ **THE ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT A BROKEN SEEDER. NINE OF THE ELEVEN SERVICES WERE
SWITCHED OFF ON THE TENANT.** `tenant_services` on Brazos Bend read
`electric = True`, `water = True` and **nine `False`**. `core.sample_fixture
.estate_plan` builds the estate from the tenant's ENABLED set, so it was correct
to create nothing for the other nine — `BR-MET-003` forbids a service point for a
service a tenant does not sell. Measured on a private clone: enabling all eleven
and re-running `load_sample_data` gave **51 service points for every one of them**
with no code change at all, gas taking 50 meters at `G-250` and thermal 50 at
`TH-CW-25`. **The wiring was never broken; the tenant was never asked to sell the
services.** The bases were already right on all eleven rows — metered for
electric/water/gas/thermal, `share` for sewer, `capacity` for the other six.

**SEWER NEEDED NO DECISION AND ONE WAS NEARLY TAKEN.** `BR-RAT-015` and
`tenancy.selectors.unmetered_service_codes` already settle it in writing: sewer is
a percentage of the water usage charge, it is deliberately excluded from the
unmetered set because routing it through `BR-RAT-090`'s asset count would price it
at **zero** (a sewer connection has no assets), and it takes a service point with
**no meter and no asset**. The PO's *"this % of service"* of 2026-09-07 matches
what is built. Nothing changed.

### ⓵ `fire_line` becomes the thirteenth asset type — `OQ-1361`'s open half, closed

`OQ-1361` records this as *"ours to decide … because it changes a PLATFORM
CATALOGUE — a row in `SEED_ASSET_TYPES`, its mirror in `lookup_defaults.json` and
a fixture serial, which belongs with the lane that owns those files"*. This is
that lane and this is that decision, taken and written down rather than asked
again (law 13).

**The state it closes:** fire had 51 service points, a ratified six-diameter
ladder, ratified prices — and **no asset type in the twelve-row catalogue**, so
nothing could ever stand on those points. A capacity service is priced by a COUNT
of the unit's assets, so a count of zero is a *lawful* billable answer of nothing:
the failure surfaced as a correct-looking bill with no fire line rather than as an
error. Fire is the service a real utility is being onboarded on.

**`fire_line` and not `backflow`**, which that question names as the nearest, for
three reasons and the third is money:
1. a backflow preventer is a device **on** a fire line, not the line being sold;
2. `FL-2 … FL-12` are pipe diameters of a fire service and would not fit a device
   type shared with water;
3. **it would misprice.** Backflow preventers already stand on WATER connections
   here, so sharing the type would let a water device be COUNTED as a fire line the
   moment one landed on a fire point — a silent overcharge, the exact direction
   `BR-RAT-090` refuses to guess in.

The hydrant stays out: the PO ruled 2026-09-03 that *"hydrants are assets not
utility service as of now"*, and a hydrant's own type is `BR-AST-042`'s question,
not this one's. The asset-number prefix is **`FS-` and not `FL-`**, because
`FL-6` is a size class and an asset numbered `FL-0001` beside it reads as one
vocabulary when it is two.

**THE COUNT IS THE NUMBER OF ASSET ROWS AND THERE IS NO `count` COLUMN ANYWHERE.**
`assets.selectors.billable_asset_size_classes` returns one entry per
`AssetAssignment`; `metering.selectors.billable_asset_size_counts` groups them. So
the ratified `$84.00` case is **three rows on one unit** — one `FL-6` and two
`FL-2` — exactly as `CART_UNIT_WITH_THREE`'s three carts are three rows. A
`quantity` column was proposed as option B when `BR-RAT-090` was ruled and was
**rejected in terms** (*"a typed number can disagree silently with the carts in the
street"*), so adding one would reverse a ruling rather than implement it. **No
schema change was needed and none was made.**

Seeded: `1 × $60.00 + 2 × $12.00 = $84.00` **on two bill lines**, plus a
residential sprinkler (`FL-4`), a government `FL-6` and an industrial `FL-8` —
because the PO ruled 2026-09-07 *"even provide it on residential units"* — and one
unit deliberately left with **none**, so `BR-MET-108`'s ruled `$0.00` stands beside
real fire money.

### ⓶ Storm water needed nothing, and that is the finding

The PO ruled 2026-09-07 that storm water's capacity goes **on the unit itself**
and not on a counted asset. **That is already what is built and it is already
seeded**: `service_characteristics` carries **50 rows keyed by unit and service,
totalling 59 ERU**, with `ERU` in its own `unit_of_measure` column (hard rule 3).
`CR-062` D6 built it that way on the PO's 2026-09-02 ruling, *"In case of strom
water - we have to take it from Unit"*. **So no storm-water asset type was added
and none should be** — a request to add one is a request to build a second,
competing home for the same fact. The five ratified property bands
(`SW-SF` 1 · `SW-DUP` 2 · `SW-COM-S` 4 · `SW-APT` 6 · `SW-COM-L` 10 ERU) are
untouched; the PO's *"1 or 2 or 5 or 10 or 100 ERU"* is read as an illustration of
the mechanism, and changing the ratified five would be a separate ruling.

### ⓷ Every seeded meter was the smallest band — `DEF-MET-4496`

`apps/assets/sample_data.py` read `seed_size_class = sizes[0] if sizes else None`.
Correct code for one meter, wrong for an estate: **50 electric meters all
`E-1P-100` against a six-size ladder and 51 water meters all `W-58` against a
nine-size one.** A per-size base curve would have been exercised at exactly ONE
point, so five of six electric prices could be wrong with every test green. The
block's own comment recorded why it was safe when written — *"no rate schedule in
the seed carries a per-size override"* — and that sentence went stale the day a
per-size curve was seeded, with nothing watching it.

The band is now a fact about the CONNECTION, resolved per unit by customer class
(`core.sample_fixture.meter_size_class_for`). After the change the estate reaches
**all six electric bands, six of nine water bands, all four gas and all three
thermal**.

⚠ **NO ❄️ FROZEN FIGURE CAN MOVE, BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY INSPECTION.**
Every signed B4/B5 figure hangs off a RESIDENTIAL demonstration unit —
`GT-17`'s water `$39.50` / sewer `$15.80` on `CASE_REFERENCE_BILL` above all — and
those units keep the band they already carry. **The pin is residential-awkward
only**, deliberately: the estate's two COMMERCIAL seats are also in
`AWKWARD_UNITS`, but for `CASE_LANDLORD`, a multi-property *cheque* — a payments
case carrying no signed per-size rating figure. Pinning them too would have left
the commercial bands unreachable by any unit in the fixture, which is the very
defect being fixed. **It moves no money today** (no seeded schedule carries a
per-size override, so `pricing_inputs` returns the same NULL every-size group
either way) **and is intended to move money tomorrow**, the moment the rating lane
seeds the curve.

### ⓸ What the thirty-six unclassed assets turned out to be

Three different things wearing one number, and only the first two are faults:
* **20 meters and sub-meters standing ON a service point with no size**
  (`DEF-AST-4494`) — 7 electric meters, 3 water meters, 1 electric sub-meter and 9
  water sub-meters. `connection_size_for` reports these as *"nobody recorded one"*,
  which is a real answer, so nothing raised at seed time; the refusal would have
  arrived later at billing as `connection_size_unresolved_for_sized_schedule`, and
  only once a schedule carried per-size overrides. **A sub-metered building was the
  first case that would have broken.** Now sized — and each sub-meter takes the
  SAME band as its own unit's meter, because `connection_size_for` answers `None`
  when two assets on one point disagree, so a different band would have made the
  connection unresolvable.
* **10 devices** — backflow ×3, battery ×2, comms, cart, ev_charger, net_meter, pv.
  These carry an `AssetAssignment` to a unit but **no service point**, which for a
  customer-owned inverter or an EV charger is `BR-AST-009` working as designed: a
  water-only tenant may hold a customer's solar inverter without selling solar, and
  such a device is deliberately outside every billing count. **The real gap in this
  group is that none carries a `certification_due`**, so the annual backflow test
  the Work module exists to raise has no date to find (`DEF-AST-4495`, narrowed
  from its filed wording).
* **6 spare meters in inventory**, with no unit and no point — `BR-AST-011`'s
  leave-in-inventory path, correct as it stands.

### ⓹ Sub-meters were never missing — the measurement was keyed on the wrong column

A report of *"sub-meters: 0, none seeded"* was put to the PO. The estate in fact
holds **ten**, every one with `parent_asset_id` set (`BR-AST-003`), every one on a
service point, across **three apartment-complex premises** with **9
`residential_submetered` units and a `commercial_master`**. The count read zero
because it was keyed on `size_class`, and every sub-meter's was NULL — which is
`DEF-AST-4494` above, seen from the other side. **No second apartment complex was
built**, because the shape asked for already exists.

⚠ **The estate's submetering is still not ideal and this is recorded rather than
quietly reshaped**, as `master_sub_meter_plan` already says in its own docstring:
three apartment units hold TWO sub-meters (one parented on the unit's own meter
from `CR-010`, one on the master from `CR-028`), and the master has three children
for a six-unit block. A real submetering estate is one master per building with one
sub per unit. Re-parenting changes what every already-seeded tenant holds and is a
data question, not a fixture edit.

**Who gets the bill in a sub-metered building, since it was asked:** each occupied
unit has its own account and its own bill priced from its own connection, and the
MASTER account receives the common areas and the base charges of the EMPTY units —
`BR-CUS-170` / `OQ-531`, PO 2026-08-27, verbatim: *"when bill is generated for A -
we should consider common areas and U6 to U10 base charges ; U1 to U5 bill be send
to Accounts assocaited with U1 to U5"*. The master-versus-sum-of-subs gap is
STORED and REPORTED per premises per period (`BR-MET-125`) and **billed to nobody**
— that file says so in terms, and billing it is a future ruling rather than a
lane's call.

### ⓺ Thermal was left alone on purpose

The PO confirmed on 2026-09-07 that thermal is capacity-billed on connected
tonnage, and `CR-080` is being written for it. **Nothing here builds that half.**
Thermal is still `metered` in the data today with 50 sized meters, so the size
spread above leaves it exactly as it found it; the mapping entry for it becomes
inert the moment `CR-080` moves the basis, because the spread runs only over the
plan's METERED services.

## 2026-09-07 — THE TWO-LEVEL WORK ORDER TYPES, BUILT: WHAT HAPPENS TO THE EIGHT, AND THE SECOND REFERENCE PASS

The two rulings of this morning are now code (`BR-WRK-058`, `work/0022`). Three
things were decided along the way that the rulings did not settle, and each is
written here rather than left to be inferred.

### 1 · THE EIGHT FLAT ROWS ARE DEACTIVATED — NOT DELETED, NOT REMAPPED

`work_order_types` shipped eight rows the Product Owner rejected outright
(*"this is not correct - you will ahve to think from all Utilty services point
of view"*). They are on live tenants, and `work_orders.type_id` points at them.
**`work/0022` sets `active = false` on each and changes nothing else.**

**Why not DELETE.** Three reasons, each sufficient on its own: a job somebody
actually did names the row, so deleting it either fails on the FK or orphans
the work; `BR-TEN-036` already rules that a seeded row is deactivatable and
never deletable, and this table's own handler enforces it, so a migration that
deleted what the API refuses to delete would be a second and contradictory
statement of the same rule; and a deactivated row costs a utility one click to
switch back on while a deleted one costs them a support call.

**Why not REMAP.** *Meter exchange* reads like *Meter Maintenance → Meter
Change*, *Read verification* like *Reading → Re-read*, and *Reconnect after
payment* and *Disconnect — non-payment* both like *Consumer Services →
Disconnection/Reconnection*. **But *Main repair* and *Move-in activation* map
onto nothing on the new list at all**, so a remap would have to invent a
destination for two of eight — and `US-WRK-007` TC-6 already refuses exactly
this move for the free-text column, in as many words: matching one name to
another *"would be a guess about a customer's data"*. Two rows that cannot be
mapped even by guessing settle it for all eight.

⚠ **ONE REFINEMENT, AND IT IS THE PART A LATER READER WILL WANT.** Only a row
still carrying its SEEDED NAME is retired. `is_system` stays true when a tenant
renames a row, so the name is the only evidence anybody has adopted it: a
utility that renamed *Main repair* to *Watermain break* has made that row
theirs, and the migration leaves it active and alone.

### 2 · THE SECOND REFERENCE PASS, AND THE ORDERING THAT MAKES IT NECESSARY

⚠ **`provision_tenant` SEEDS REFERENCE DATA BEFORE IT ENABLES ANY SERVICE, SO A
SEEDER THAT FILTERS ON ENABLEMENT SEES AN EMPTY SET.** `_seed_reference_data`
runs at line ~1159 and `_enable_signup_services` at ~1203, and the order cannot
simply be swapped: a `tenant_services` row points at the UoM rows the reference
pass plants, so reversing them leaves every unit pointer NULL.

**Nothing was broken by this before today.** `uoms` and `service_size_classes`
are service-SCOPED but seed every row for every tenant and let the pickers
filter — both say so in their own docstrings, and
`MeterSizeClass.service` states the posture outright: *"the seed is the one path
that tags without asking about enablement"*. `work_order_types` is the **first**
list where the Product Owner ruled that the ROWS THEMSELVES differ by service,
so it is the first that trips over the ordering.

**The fix is a named second pass**, `_seed_service_scoped_reference_data`, over
a named set of one list (`SERVICE_ENABLEMENT_REFERENCE_LISTS`). It runs
immediately after `_enable_signup_services` and again from
`_apply_service_toggle` when a clerk switches a service on months later. Every
seeder it reaches is insert-missing, so it writes nothing on a replay and takes
no `reference_seed_runs` row of its own — it is a top-up of the first pass, not
a second run of it.

⚠ **THE FAILURE THIS AVOIDS IS A SILENT ONE AND THAT IS WHY IT IS WRITTEN DOWN
RATHER THAN JUST FIXED.** Without the second pass every tenant would receive the
common twenty-seven rows and not one service row — eighteen sub-types where the
ruling says twenty-two — with `tsc`, the gates and every test green, because a
test that drove the seeder directly would assert eighteen and pass. The two
tests that pin the ruling therefore provision a tenant end to end through
`provision_tenant` and count what a real utility ends up with.

**And the toggle half is a ruling of our own**, made rather than asked
(hard-won law 13): a water-only co-op that adds Gas in March gets the four gas
job types the signup path would have given it. The alternative — a utility whose
crews cannot raise a gas leak call-out, with nothing anywhere saying why — is
`DEF-3502`'s shape (*"built, and not wired, for exactly one of the two paths"*)
applied to data instead of to a column.

### 3 · NO `service` COLUMN, AND NO SEEDED PRIORITIES

**`work_order_types` carries no `service` column.** What depends on the tenant's
services is which rows ARRIVE, not what a row then is — *"a utility that picks
water and gas gets the eighteen plus the four gas ones"*. The tag lives on the
seed constant and is read once, at seeding time; the row that lands is an
ordinary tenant row they may rename, retire or re-parent. `MeterSizeClass`
takes the opposite posture (every size tagged for every tenant, filtered at the
picker) because the PO ruled a different thing about that list — the two are not
an inconsistency to tidy, and both now say so in their own docstrings.

**And no seeded row carries a default priority, an estimated duration or a
customer-present flag.** The eight retired rows carried r10's; the PO's list
states NAMES and nothing else. Deciding that *a gas leak call-out is Urgent · 60
minutes* would put a promise to a customer into a seed file on a lane's
judgment. Every row is editable on the card, and `BR-WRK-018`'s due-date
derivation simply has nothing to apply until a utility sets one. **This is
raised with the Product Owner as an observation, not resolved here.**

### 4 · THE OBSERVATION THE RULING LEAVES OPEN, RESTATED BECAUSE THE BUILD
### CONFIRMS IT

The eighteen base sub-types are water-shaped — *No Water Supply*, *Water Truck
Services*, *Water Pressure* — and under the rule as ruled a **gas-only** utility
receives all eighteen plus its four. That is seeded as ruled and NOT carved up
on our own judgment, for the reason the morning's entry gives: *Low Pressure*
and *Leak Repairs* are as true of gas as of water while *Water Truck Services*
plainly is not, and deciding which is which is a judgment about a utility's
operations rather than about this software. **It is a row somebody switches off,
and it is raised with the PO as an observation.**

### WHAT A UTILITY ACTUALLY GETS, AS NUMBERS

| The utility sells | Types | Sub-types | Rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Water only | 9 | 18 | 27 |
| Water + gas | 9 | 22 | 31 |
| Electric + water | 9 | 21 | 30 |
| All eleven services | 9 | 42 | 51 |

## 2026-09-07 — THE PORTAL'S TWO LANGUAGES, BUILT (`DEF-CWP-4442` CLOSED)

**This is the ⓶ entry above with a mechanism under it and the numbers it
produced.** The ruling and the reading are recorded there and were not re-made
here; what follows is what the code now does, and the three things a lane would
get wrong if it read only the ruling.

**Eleven became two.** `apps.portal.selectors.PORTAL_LOCALES` is `("en", "es")`.
⚠ **AND THE GUEST DROPDOWN WAS NOT READING THAT CONSTANT AT ALL** — it drew the
front end's `LOCALE_CODES`, the CATALOGUE registry, which is the fold
`BR-CWP-105`'s last clause says never to make. So the offer now travels on
`GET portal/public/front` beside the tenant's own language, and there is ONE
answer to *what may the portal offer* rather than two that happened to agree.
**The nine that left the dropdown, named, because an absence is what this change
IS and nothing in this repository can see one:** *Español de México · Deutsch ·
हिन्दी · Français (France) · Indonesia (Indonesia) · Italiano (Italia) ·
日本語 (日本) · 한국어 (대한민국) · Português (Brasil)*.

**The eleven CATALOGUES did not move and no file was deleted.** That is the whole
of keeping the two registries apart: `LOCALE_CODES` still carries eleven,
`supportedLocale` still validates against it, and `BR-CWP-105`'s chain is
untouched — so **a customer whose account says German still reads German**,
asserted on the wire and then read off the glass rather than reasoned about. The
new rule is `BR-CWP-106`; `BR-CWP-105` gained a dated correction where its text
still said this was the next lane's work.

**The third option is ONE function, called by BOTH controls.**
`offeredLocales(offer, current)` in
`07-frontend/src/portal/components/language.ts`: the offer, plus the reader's own
current language when it is neither and this build can draw it, carried through
**exactly as stored** rather than normalised — answering `en` for a stored
`en-US` would leave the control blank over it, which is this same defect one code
along. Two controls for one setting building their lists in two places is how
they come to disagree (hard-won law 5), so there is one place and a test that

⚠ **A CASE NOBODY RULED ON TURNED OUT TO NEED NO NEW BEHAVIOUR, AND THAT IS
WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE THE INSTINCT IS TO INVENT ONE.** The ⓶ entry above says
a tenant set outside the two "is a separate question nobody has raised" — and
the seeded demo utility IS one: `pine-hill` runs on `es-MX`. **What happens
today, measured in a browser rather than predicted:** the guest reads Mexican
Spanish (`BR-CWP-105` step three, untouched) and their dropdown lists **three** —
*English · Español · Español de México*. The clause that covers a stored German
covers a tenant's `es-MX` unchanged, because *the reader's own current language*
does not care which of the four sources it came from. **No rule was written for

deferral of it.

⚠ **AND IT CLOSED NO GEOMETRY DEFECT, WHICH WAS THE EXPECTATION AND IS
RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS WRONG.** `DEF-CWP-4468` — the guest header wrapped to
two rows in English when this control was added — looked as though it would
fall out of the narrowing, since the widest option was *Indonesia (Indonesia)*.
**Measured at 1440px on the running product: the control shrank from 186px over
three options to 105px over two, and the header is still `1100×95` with the nav
at `848×79` — two rows.** That defect's own row already carried the reason and
this only confirms it: the nav was at **853 of about 860 available pixels
BEFORE the control existed**, so it was going to break on whatever came next
and taking 80px off a 105px control cannot give the row back. `DEF-CWP-4468`

⚠ **ONE DEFECT IN THIS CHANGE WAS FOUND BY LOOKING AT A SCREENSHOT AND BY
NOTHING ELSE (hard-won law 6, and it is the second time this file has recorded
it).** Every option assertion passed — three options, *Deutsch* among them, the

verfügbar.`** printed underneath a list of **three**. The caption was counting
the server's OFFER while the control drew the offer PLUS this reader's own

asking, and every one of them was telling the truth. Fixed by counting the
rendered list, asserted in `Preferences.dom.test.tsx` (proved red: *expected …

**What was deliberately NOT done, each because doing it would exceed the

catalogue can draw** is a real hole and is filed as `DEF-CWP-4491` rather than

ⓒ **No change to `SEED_LANGUAGES`, `LOCALE_CODES` or the staff app's own picker**

## 2026-09-07 — THE LAW-11 RE-DERIVATION HAS A TEXT-MODE TRAP, AND IT REWROTE FIVE ROWS

Found while filing `DEF-GOV-4499`, caught by the prescribed check, recorded because
the mechanism is new and the fix is one word.

**WHAT HAPPENED.** `file_defect.py` appended a row to a working-tree register that
turned out to be stale — the tool's own docstring warns about exactly this
(`DEF-3523`: it reaches the remote for the ID and never for the BYTES). So the row
was re-derived the way CLAUDE.md law 11 prescribes: take the pinned tip's bytes,
re-apply your own edit to THOSE, write that. Done in Python, the obvious way:

    tip = subprocess.run([...], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

⚠ **`text=True` TURNS ON UNIVERSAL NEWLINES, WHICH SILENTLY CONVERTS EVERY `\r\n`
AND BARE `\r` IN THE FILE TO `\n`.** The defect register has rows whose prose
contains embedded carriage returns. So the "re-derived" file was the tip's content
with **five rows rewritten** — `DEF-CWP-4178`, `4180`, `4181`, `4182`, `4183` and
`4185` — and nothing about them looked different, because nothing about them WAS
different except bytes no terminal prints.

**IT DEFEATS EVERY CHECK IN LAW 11 EXCEPT ONE.** The file count is right. The row
count is right. Your own row IS present. Nothing vanished, so
`push_register_guard.py` would have passed it. `git diff --numstat` reports
insertions and deletions **in equal number**, which is exactly what a legitimate
rewrite looks like. And `git show <commit>` would have printed six hunks whose
`-` and `+` lines are visually identical — the whole-file-write shape law 11
already names, arriving through a tool that is not a `csv` writer.

**THE ONE THING THAT CAUGHT IT** was the check the law prescribes and this lane
happened to run before pushing: `diff <(git show <tip>:<path>) <path>`, read as
arithmetic. It printed five changed lines beside the one added line, and five is
not one.

**THE FIX IS TO DROP `text=True`.** Re-derive a shared file as BYTES —
`capture_output=True` with no `text`, `read_bytes()`, `write_bytes()` — and
compare bytes. After that the same command printed exactly `2261a2262`, one added
line and nothing else.

**THE GENERAL FORM, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT WORTH A ROW:** law 11 says re-derive
from the tip and says nothing about the ENCODING you re-derive through, because
every occurrence so far has been about stale content rather than about a lossy
read. A text-mode read is not a copy of a file — it is a copy of an interpretation
of a file, and for any file the repository treats as bytes (a register, a fixture,
anything with a digest over it) the interpretation is the thing that gets lost.
The same trap is one line away in any helper that opens a shared file with
`open(path)` instead of `open(path, "rb")`.

## 2026-09-07 — THE BASE CHARGE LEARNS THE METER SIZE, AND WHAT EACH SIZE COSTS

**The ruling this implements, PO verbatim:** *"We need to add this data for water
- and all other services - base charge amounts"*, said while looking at the
measured water table with the note *"the table that prices a base by meter size
is empty"*. Everything else on the pricing side was marked *"rest is good"*.

**What was actually wrong, counted rather than described.** `charge_code_amounts`
held **0 rows on every tenant this product has ever created** — four seeded
utilities on the demo database plus a freshly provisioned eleven-service one.
`BR-RAT-088` has published the example that table exists for since 2026-08-20 (a
5/8" water base at **$8.00** and a 2" at **$34.00** on one code) and `BR-RAT-690`
built the writer on 2026-08-28. Neither reached `apps/rating/sample_data.py`,
which had always seeded ONE flat amount per base charge code. So a utility
opening CHG-02 step 2 met a blank table and every connection of every size was
billed the same standing charge. Filed as `DEF-4497`.

### The method, and it is read off the register rather than invented

**A base charge is paid for the capacity a connection reserves**, not for what
flows through it, which is why every North American schedule steps it by meter
size. The ladder is

    multiplier(size) = 0.5 + 0.5 x (rated capacity / smallest size's rated capacity)

— **half of the smallest size's base is a customer component every connection
pays whatever its size, and half scales with capacity.** The smallest size is
always `1.0000`, so the amount for it is exactly what the charge code charges
today.

⚠ **THAT FORMULA WAS NOT CHOSEN FOR ITS SHAPE — IT REPRODUCES TWO LADDERS THIS
REPO HAS ALREADY RATIFIED.** `BR-RAT-108` publishes `5/8" $8.00 · 1" $14.00 ·
2" $34.00`; at AWWA meter-equivalence ratios of 1 and 2.5 the formula gives
**$8.00 and $14.00, both exactly**. Independently, fire's six PO-ratified prices
(`$12 / $30 / $60 / $100 / $160 / $230`) sit at `1.00 / 2.50 / 5.00 / 8.33 /
13.33 / 19.17` against diameter-squared capacity where the formula gives
`1.00 / 2.50 / 5.00 / 8.50 / 13.00 / 18.50`. Two ratified ladders, one shape.

**One pinned exception, recorded rather than smoothed.** At an AWWA ratio of 8
the formula gives `$36.00` for a 2" water meter and the register publishes
**`$34.00`** in three separate rules. The published figure wins; the `$2.00`
divergence is stated in `apps/rating/base_size_amounts.py` so nobody rediscovers
it as a defect.

### What a base now costs, per size — the seeded sample

Water, anchored on `BASE-W` `$8.00` (`BASE-W-COM` `$15.00` takes the same ladder):

| 5/8" | 3/4" | 1" | 1½" | 2" | 3" | 4" | 5" | 6" |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $8.00 | $10.00 | $14.00 | $24.00 | $34.00 | $68.00 | $104.00 | $154.00 | $204.00 |

Electric, anchored on `BASE-E` `$12.00` (rated kVA — 1-phase at 240 V, 3-phase at
208 V; `BASE-E-COM` `$48.00` and `BASE-E-IND` `$180.00` take the same ladder):

| 1φ 100A | 1φ 200A | 3φ 200A | 1φ 400A | 3φ 400A | CT-metered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $12.00 | $18.00 | $24.00 | $30.00 | $42.00 | $114.00 |

Gas, anchored on `BASE-G` `$6.00` (rated CFH): `$6.00 · $8.10 · $10.56 · $15.00`.

⚠ **3-phase 200 A sits BETWEEN 1-phase 200 A and 1-phase 400 A and that is not a
mistake** — it is 72 kVA against 48 and 96. The ladder is ordered by capacity,
not by ampere number, which is the whole reason the basis is written down.

**Measured, on PostgreSQL 16 through the real seeder:** 40 `charge_code_amounts`
rows on an eleven-service tenant, and `rating.selectors.base_charge_from_charge_
code` — the function the live bill path calls — answers **$8.00 for a 5/8" and
$34.00 for a 2"**, i.e. **$26.00 a month per 2" connection** that no seeded
tenant could express before.

### Why no seeded bill moves, and why it HAD to not move

The ladder is anchored on the code's own current figure, so the smallest size
reproduces it to the cent. That is not tidiness: `apps/billing/gather._base_
charge_for` **REFUSES an account by name** when the charge code and
`plan_services.base_charge` state different bases (`BR-RAT-088`'s *"migration
artefact"* clause). A ladder that broke the anchor would not mis-bill — it would
stop every seeded account with a sentence naming both amounts.

### The eight services that did NOT get a ladder, and why

Water, electric and gas are the only services whose base is a **signed, non-zero**
figure (billing workbook `[W] §1`). The other eight state `$0.00`, and any
multiple of zero is zero — a table for them would be 44 rows of `$0.00`, the
flattest possible table, which is precisely what makes a size class stop meaning
anything. **The zeros were left alone for two different reasons and neither is
this lane's to overturn:**

* **trash is a PO ruling** — `OQ-317` option A retired its base to zero because
  trash bills per CART (`$15.00` each, `BR-RAT-090`);
* **sewer, storm water, solar, broadband, thermal, battery and fire are
  unsigned** — `core/sample_fixture.CAPACITY_BASE` carries the fixture's own
  standing law, *"a base nobody signed is a base this fixture does not invent"*.

⚠ **AND RAISING ONE IS A TWO-FILE CHANGE, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS NOT DONE QUIETLY.**
The charge code's amount and the plan's must agree to the cent or the bill
refuses, and the plan's figure comes from `core/sample_fixture.py` — a file
metering and assets also read. **The figure that would need signing is one
number per service**: what a customer pays each month for HAVING the connection,
before any usage. It is put to the PO rather than chosen here.

## 2026-09-07 · A PRECONDITION CAN BE SATISFIED BY A DEFECT — the gas price that was nearly seeded behind an unratified swap (`DEF-TEN-4504`, `OQ-1290`)

**Two lanes nearly priced `$8,061.50` a month of demo gas behind a change nobody
ruled, and the thing that stopped it was asking WHO made a precondition true.**

**What happened.** `core.sample_fixture.GAS_FLAT_PER_CCF` carries the signed
`$1.15` from billing workbook §1 and a note saying, in its own words, that it
*"becomes usable the day a gas tenant declares `ccf` as its primary UoM"*. The
rates lane read that note, measured a freshly provisioned tenant, correctly found
`gas primary_uom = ccf`, and concluded the blocker had expired — a one-line
change, a signed figure, a precondition met in writing. Every step of that is
sound reasoning.

**Why it was wrong.** `SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS["gas"]` reads `("ccf", "therm")`
today because **somebody performed the swap `OQ-1290` says must go to the PO**,
and did not take the ruling. That row names the change and the reason in terms:
*"THE ONE WAY TO APPLY `$1.15/ccf` AS SIGNED, PUT TO THE PO BECAUSE IT COLLIDES
WITH A RATIFIED STATEMENT AND NOT BECAUSE THE ANSWER IS UNCLEAR"*, citing law 13
— *a ruling that collides with a signed rule; the supersession must be stated,
never assumed*. What it collides with is `EP-TEN-06` `US-TEN-007` TC-1.

**The guard did its job and nobody read it.** `test_us_ten_007_tc1__enable_gas
_defaults_therm_ccf_from_seed` has been RED since **2026-09-03**, asserting
`primary_uom == "therm"` against a seed that produces `ccf`. It was dated rather
than dismissed, which is law 7's habit (1) applied properly: the swap landed in
`e4a02b37`, a commit titled *"test: all 38 journeys for the three change requests,
and the index regenerated"* — **a change to a ratified default rode inside a
commit about a journeys index**, so in the log it reads as scaffolding. The test's
own assertion last moved 2026-08-23.

⚠ **THE GENERAL LESSON, AND IT IS A VARIANT OF LAW 7 THAT HAD NO NAME: A
PRECONDITION CAN BE SATISFIED BY A DEFECT.** Law 7's dating habit — *was this red
before I started, and `git log -S` answers it* — is written for a FAILING check.
This is the mirror case: a condition that has silently become TRUE. A docstring
that states its own unblocking condition invites exactly one question, *is it true
now*, and never asks *who made it true and were they allowed to*. Between "the
blocker expired" and "somebody stepped over it" there is no difference the
measurement can see, and the second one is a defect wearing the costume of
progress.
**So when a stated precondition turns out to be met, date it before building on
it** — the same one command, pointed at the thing that CHANGED rather than at the
thing that failed.

⚠ **AND THE COST OF NOT ASKING IS ASYMMETRIC, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS WORTH A ROW.**
Pricing money behind the swap would not merely have inherited the error, it would
have **entrenched** it: an issued gas line at `$1.15/ccf` becomes evidence that
`ccf` was intended, and hard rule 4 makes an issued invoice immutable. The
alternative branch is no better and `OQ-1290` already measures it — reading
`$1.15/ccf` against a therm register is `OQ-303` option (B), a signed figure
quietly made to mean something else, and about **4% over on every gas line**.

**WHAT WAS AND WAS NOT DONE.** `DEF-TEN-4504` is filed and **no value was
changed** — reverting to `therm` is as much a ruling as keeping `ccf`, and
`OQ-1290` asks for the supersession to be STATED. Both units are already ratified
for gas and already offered on S8, so what is put to the PO invents no figure: it
is which of the tenant's own two gas units the register reads. The test moves only
with the ruling. Gas usage stays `$0.00` meanwhile, which is `OQ-670`'s ruled
behaviour and is honest on the document.

**A second row narrowed the same afternoon, recorded here because it runs the
other way.** `DEF-4503` reports that a `government` customer class resolves no
base charge — fifteen combinations, six electric bands and nine water sizes —
because `BR-RAT-108` made `applies_to_customer_classes` an INCLUSION list and the
seeded codes name residential, municipal, commercial and industrial only. Measured
on the eleven-service estate, **no seeded account is `government`**: 60
residential, 10 commercial, 1 industrial and 1 municipal. The civic customer — the
Public Works Depot — is `municipal`, which IS listed and bills correctly at
`$24.00` electric and `$16.00` water. **So the refusal is LATENT and not live, and
nothing on the demo stops today.** What stays true is that `government` is in the
platform account-type catalogue, so a real utility that picks it on a real account
gets a stopped bill.

## 2026-09-07 — `git log -S` CANNOT DATE A CHANGE ON THIS BRANCH, AND TWO LANES BUILT A WRONG CONCLUSION ON IT IN ONE AFTERNOON

**CLAUDE.md law 7 prescribes one command for the question *was this red before I
started* — `git log -S "<the failing symbol>" -- <file>` — and calls it "one
command" that "answers it". On this repository it answers a different question,
and its output reads exactly like evidence of misconduct.**

**What happened, because the shape matters more than the subject.** A lane found
the seeded gas unit of measure had changed from `therm` to `ccf`, ran the
prescribed command, and got:

    e4a02b37  2026-09-03  test: all 38 journeys for the three change requests,
                          and the index regenerated

and reported — carefully, dating it exactly as the law asks — that *"a change to
a ratified default rode inside a commit about a journeys index and reads in the
log as scaffolding"*. A second lane repeated that in a report without
re-deriving it. Both were wrong, and the conclusion was about to stop a signed
money path.

**`e4a02b37` is not a commit about journeys. It is `3,405 files changed,
1,490,794 insertions(+)`, zero deletions — a whole-tree snapshot** that also
carries `.editorconfig`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and `.claude/agents/`.
Dropping the pathspec names a second one, `91efe69c`, at **4,397 files,
1,818,224 insertions(+)**, zero deletions. This branch's history is a series of
squashed imports.

**And the authoring commits are not here at all.** `DEF-3230` records its fix as
`5205cdb`, `f7fc34b`, `6a5a0dc`; `git cat-file -e` reports all three **absent
from this repository** — not unreachable, absent. So the earliest reachable
commit containing any given line is whichever snapshot imported it, and that
snapshot's subject line is about whatever else was being written that day.

⚠ **THE FAILURE IS NOT THAT THE COMMAND IS WRONG — IT IS THAT IT IS CONFIDENTLY
IRRELEVANT.** `-S` reports where a string's occurrence count CHANGED in the
reachable history. That is a true answer to a question nobody asked. It never
returns nothing, never errors, and its output has the exact shape of the answer
you wanted — a sha, a date, a subject line — which is law 7's *"a check whose
output cannot distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check, because it is
trusted"* wearing a date stamp.

**THE TELL IS ONE COMMAND AND IT IS CHEAP:**

    git show --stat --format='' <the sha -S gave you> | tail -1

**`N files changed, M insertions(+)` with no deletions means a snapshot, and the
dating is worthless.** A real authored commit touches a handful of files and has
deletions in it.

**What was actually true in the case that found this**, recorded so the wrong
version does not outlive it: the gas swap was **authorised**. `DEF-3230` was
filed by the Product Owner in their own words — *"this is problem with every
Utility services - why dont you se the correct data in Seed data and fix it"* —
its body names this exact fault (*"gas is signed at 1.15 dollars per ccf while
the seeded gas meter reads therm"*), and its status is `fixed`. The seed
contradicted signed law and was brought into line with it, which is a defect fix
by definition and is why it was not a change request. What remains true is
narrower and still worth acting on: `test_us_ten_007_tc1` still asserts `therm`
and is RED, as one of the eight surfaces that row says were left unrepaired. The
action is to finish those eight, not to withhold a ruling that was already given.

⚠ **AND THE SECOND-ORDER LESSON IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING.** The first lane's
instinct was right and saved money — it refused to price gas behind a red guard.
The second lane then repeated its dating **as established fact without running
anything**, which is the same move it had criticised itself for one hour earlier
on a different premise. **Two lanes checking each other only works if the second
one actually checks**; otherwise the pair produces more confidence than either
alone, on the same evidence. It was the coordinator, holding neither lane's
context, who asked whether the premise was true.

## 2026-09-07 · CORRECTION — `git log -S` CANNOT DATE A CHANGE ON THIS BRANCH, AND THE GAS SWAP WAS RULED ALL ALONG (supersedes the framing of *"A precondition can be satisfied by a defect"* above)

⚠ **READ THIS BEFORE THE ROW ABOVE IT. That row's general lesson survives; its
central factual claim does not, and I am the lane that got it wrong.**

**WHAT I CLAIMED.** That `SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS["gas"]` was switched from `therm`
to `ccf` **without the ruling `OQ-1290` says it needs**, and that the change *"rode
inside a commit about a journeys index"* dated 2026-09-03.

**WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, on three checks anyone can repeat in a minute.**

1. **THE SWAP IS RULED, AND THIS VERY FILE RECORDS IT.** The decision log of
   **2026-09-02** — `BR-TEN-1180`, closing `DEF-2409` and `DEF-3230` — lists the
   ruled defaults and names it outright: *"gas metered **ccf/therm (SWAPPED)**"*,
   under a heading that reads **"WHY GAS SWAPS, so nobody tidies it back"**, with
   the reasoning spelled out: `$1.15` per ccf is signed while the seeded meter
   read `therm` with no conversion factor, which is the exact mismatch the
   bill-time unit gate refuses (`OQ-004`, *no silent conversion*), so making `ccf`
   primary makes the seed agree with the signed price. **The row anticipated my
   error by name and I made it anyway.**
2. **`DEF-3230` IS PO-FILED AND `fixed`.** Reporter `PO`, status `fixed`, quoting
   them verbatim — *"this is problem with every Utility services - why dont you se
   the correct data in Seed data and fix it"* — and naming this exact case.
   **`therm` was the DEFECT; `ccf` is the FIX.** That is why it was a defect and
   not a change request: nothing about the agreement moved, the seed simply
   contradicted signed law.
3. **THE COMMIT I DATED IT TO IS NOT A COMMIT ABOUT ANYTHING.** `e4a02b37` is
   **3,405 files changed, 1,490,794 insertions, ZERO deletions** — a whole-tree
   snapshot that also carries `.editorconfig` and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`. A
   second, `91efe69c`, is **4,397 files / 1,818,224 insertions / zero deletions**.
   `DEF-3230`'s own row names the real fix commits — `5205cdb`, `f7fc34b`,
   `6a5a0dc` — and **`git cat-file -e` reports all three ABSENT from this
   repository.**

⚠ **SO THE REAL LESSON IS ABOUT LAW 7's OWN PRESCRIBED COMMAND, AND IT IS WORTH
MORE THAN THE ONE I WROTE.** Law 7 says *"was it red before I started is a claim
about history, so check it like any other claim — `git log -S "<symbol>" -- <file>`
ANSWERS IT IN ONE COMMAND"*. **On this branch that command cannot answer it.** The
authoring history is not here; content arrived by squashed whole-tree import. So
`-S` returns the earliest *reachable* commit containing the line, which is
necessarily a snapshot, whose SUBJECT is about whatever that day's work happened to
be — and the output then reads exactly like *somebody slipped a change into an
unrelated commit*. **It is not a weaker answer. It is a confidently wrong one, in
the specific direction of accusing a colleague.**

**THE TELL IS ONE COMMAND AND IT IS CHEAP:**

    git show --stat --format='' <sha> | tail -1

**"N files changed, M insertions(+)" with NO deletions, at thousands of files, means
the dating is worthless** — you have found an import, not an author. When that
happens, date the change from the REGISTERS instead: grep the decision log and the
defect register for the fact itself, which is where a ruling actually lives and
which is the one place a snapshot cannot lie about.

⚠ **AND MY PROCESS ERROR IS THE PLAINER ONE: I CHECKED A COLLEAGUE'S PREMISE AND
NOT MY OWN.** The previous row congratulates this lane for testing the rates lane's
premise rather than their conclusion. Having found the `ccf`, I then reached
*"unratified"* without grepping the decision log or the defect register for the gas
case — which is law 13's standing instruction (*grep `02-decision-log.md` and
`01-open-questions.md` for the subject*) and would have returned `DEF-3230` and the
2026-09-02 ruling on the first try. **The check I was praised for is the check I
skipped one step later**, and it cost a colleague a false accusation of shipping an
unratified change.

**WHAT REMAINS REAL, and it is why a row still stands.** The guard IS red:
`test_us_ten_007_tc1__enable_gas_defaults_therm_ccf_from_seed` asserts
`primary_uom == "therm"` (assertion last moved 2026-08-23) against a seed that
correctly produces `ccf`. That is an **unfinished follow-up of a ruled change** —
the ruling moved the seed and nobody moved the test — and not an unauthorised
change. **So the action inverts.** It is not *"never price gas until a ruling
arrives"*; the ruling arrived on 2026-09-02. It is: finish the follow-up, get the
guard green, and then gas can be priced at the signed `$1.15/ccf`. `DEF-TEN-4504`
is marked **invalid** because its stated premise is false, and `DEF-TEN-4505`
carries the red guard under the correct framing.

**`OQ-1290`'s gas paragraph is itself now stale** and is flagged here rather than
silently left: it still reads as though making the register `ccf` were an open
proposal needing a PO ruling, and that ruling was taken on 2026-09-02. This is the
register-body rot CLAUDE.md warns about — *the status column decides and a body
that contradicts it is stale until proved otherwise* — met from the direction
nobody expects, where the stale BODY is what sends a lane to raise a false alarm.

## 2026-09-07 — THE TWO PO RULINGS, EXECUTED: WHAT MOVED, WHAT DID NOT, AND WHAT WENT BACK TO THEM

The rulings themselves are the row of the same day headed **"TWO PO RULINGS ON WORK
ORDER TYPES"** — verbatim there, cited here rather than copied. This row is what the
build lane did with them, and the three judgments it had to make on its own.

### 1 · THE EIGHTEEN ARE WATER'S, AND THE CODE DID NOT CHANGE

Every sub-type now names a service. **`WorkOrderTypeLookupHandler.seed` was not
touched**: the filter already read the tag, and eighteen more rows acquired one. That
is the property worth recording — the counts live in `models.SEED_TYPES` and not in a
function, which is why the tests assert them by provisioning a real tenant.

| The utility sells | Types | Sub-types |
|---|---|---|
| Water only | 9 | 18 |
| Water + gas | 9 | 22 |
| Electric + water | 9 | 21 |
| **Gas only** | **9** | **4** |
| All eleven services | 9 | 42 |

**The nine TYPES are never scoped.** They are the common spine and every utility has
all nine whatever it sells; only sub-types follow a service. Nothing in the ruling
asked for the types to be scoped and scoping them would leave a gas utility with no
heading to file a billing complaint under at all.

### 2 · THE JUDGMENT THE RULING DID NOT COVER, AND WHY IT WENT BACK RATHER THAN
### GETTING DECIDED

⚠ **ELEVEN OF THE EIGHTEEN NAME NO SERVICE.** *Billing Issues* · *Meter Change* ·
*Meter Dispose* · *Meter Replacement* · *Routine Inspection* ·
*Disconnection/Reconnection* · *Re-read* · and the four *Connection* rows. A gas
utility changes meters, re-reads them, connects customers and disconnects for
non-payment exactly as a water utility does — so scoping all eighteen to water takes
eleven job types a gas utility does daily.

**That was NOT decided here.** The PO was shown *No Water Supply* and *Water Truck
Services* and answered about those; the eleven were not put to them. Splitting the
list on this lane's judgment is the exact mistake the first ruling's entry exists to
avoid making — *"deciding which is which is a judgment about a utility's operations
rather than about this software"* — and doing it now, unasked, would be that mistake
with more confidence. **`OQ-WRK-1764` is OPEN with the eleven rows named and the two
counts worked (gas-only 9+4 today, 9+15 under option (a)).** What ships is the ruling
as given.

### 3 · THE DEFAULT PRIORITY IS RULED IN AND IS STILL NOT SEEDED

*"Yes"* answers WHETHER a type carries one. It does not answer WHICH, and in this
product a priority is not a label: it carries SLA hours (`BR-WRK-018`) and `due_at` is
stamped from it the moment an order is raised. **So naming *Consumer Complaint*
Urgent is a four-hour response time promised to a customer.** `default_priority` stays
NULL on every seeded row and `OQ-WRK-1765` carries the proposal, per type, with the
hours spelled out — High 8 h for Consumer Complaint, Corrective Maintenance and Water
Quality Monitoring; Normal 3 days for Meter Maintenance, Connection and Consumer
Services; Low 7 days for Preventive Maintenance, Infrastructure Development and
Reading — **plus the four sub-types that must beat their type**: *Gas leak call-out*,
*Odour complaint*, *No Water Supply* and *Outage report* at Urgent, 4 hours, because a
gas leak inheriting eight hours from Consumer Complaint is the wrong number arriving
by inheritance.

### 4 · THE TWO-HOUR WINDOW, AND WHY IT GOT A MIGRATION RATHER THAN A SENTENCE

⚠ **`work/0023` DELIVERED THE UNSCOPED EIGHTEEN THIS MORNING**, so any host that
migrated between the two rulings gave a gas-only utility exactly the rows the second
ruling forbids. **Nothing else would ever put that right**: the seeder is
insert-missing and has no retraction path, the reference sweep only adds, and a
version bump adds nothing here. Hard-won law 4 says a change that cannot reach a
deployed host must SAY SO; reaching them cost forty lines, so `work/0024` reaches them.

**It DEACTIVATES and never deletes** — jobs point at these rows and `BR-TEN-036`
already forbids deleting a seeded one. **It skips a row a utility has RENAMED**, the
same test the eight retired types got, because a renamed row is one they have adopted.
**And it is narrowed to water on tenants with no water**, deliberately: a tenant that
took gas's four and later switched gas off keeps them, because that is a different
question nobody has asked and widening the migration would turn a correction into a
new rule.

### WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE

**No `service` column was added.** What depends on the tenant's services is still
which rows ARRIVE. **No seeded priority.** **No re-carving of the PO's list.** And the
ordering trap the first entry recorded now bites HARDER rather than less: with every
sub-type scoped, a broken second pass leaves a tenant with nine types and **no
sub-types at all**, where before it left a plausible-looking eighteen. Both are
invisible to every check in this repo, which is why the counts are asserted end to end
from `provision_tenant` and never from the seeder.

## 2026-09-07 — GAS BILLS ITS GAS: THE SIGNED `$1.15/ccf` IS SEEDED, `OQ-1290` CLOSES, AND THE PRICE WAS IN THE PRODUCT ALL ALONG (`DEF-RAT-4516`)

**The Product Owner, verbatim:** *"please fix this gap - One real gap, and it is money.
Gas bills $0.00 usage"*.

**What it was.** A seeded gas utility carries 50 sized meters, 150 committed readings
and 7,010 ccf of consumption, every reading in `ccf`. The reference customer `G-5000`
draws **40 ccf a month** and its bill line read **qty 40 ccf @ `$0.0000`**, so the whole
bill was the signed `$6.00` base plus twelve cents of tax. Thermal on the same estate
billed `30,000 × $0.045` = `$1,350.00`. **Thermal was priced; gas was not.**

**Nothing had to be asked, and that is the whole shape of this one.** The billing
workbook `[W] §1` line 22 signs *"Gas add-on · Gas flat $1.15/ccf · $6"*, and the
product already HELD the figure: `core.sample_fixture.GAS_FLAT_PER_CCF = "1.15"`, whose
own note said it was *"RECORDED and READ BY NOTHING"*. That is hard-won law 2 — built
is not wired — in fixture form, on a money path.

### 1 · WHY IT WAS LEFT, AND THE EXACT DAY THAT REASON EXPIRED

`GAS_FLAT_PER_CCF`'s note stated its own release condition: *"it becomes usable the day
a gas tenant declares `ccf` as its primary UoM, or a therm→ccf factor is ruled"*. The
figure is per `ccf` and the seeded gas register read `therm`; `register_units.DIMENSION_OF`
declares `therm` **energy** and `ccf` **volume**, so `BR-MET-143`'s verdict for the pair
is `dimension` with `multiplier_can_reconcile: False` — **no conversion factor reconciles
them and none ever can**, because the conversion needs a heating value, which is a
physical fact about the gas and not a column on `tenant_services`. Pricing the read on
it would have been `OQ-004`'s forbidden silent conversion and about **4% over** on every
gas line. **The refusal was right.**

**That day was 2026-09-02.** `BR-TEN-1180` — the ruling closing `DEF-2409` and the
PO-filed `DEF-3230` (*"this is problem with every Utility services - why dont you se the
correct data in Seed data and fix it"*) — swapped `SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS["gas"]` from
`("therm", "ccf")` to `("ccf", "therm")` **for exactly this purpose**. The register was
MOVED rather than converted, which is also the physically ordinary shape: a gas meter's
register is volumetric and a therm is computed from it. So the seeded read, the register,
the tariff and the workbook all say `ccf`, and the signed figure applies **exactly as
signed**. Nothing was reinterpreted to get here.

⚠ **THE SWAP LANDED AND THE PRICE DID NOT, AND THE GAP WAS FIVE DAYS OF LIVE `$0.00`.**
This is `CR-062`'s scope boundary outliving its own purpose: seeding gas was group B's
business and `E1`–`E6` name six services without gas among them, so `METERED_USAGE_PRICES`
correctly omitted it — and then went on omitting it after the blocker was removed.

### 2 · THE PRECONDITION: EIGHT UNREPAIRED SURFACES, AND THE GUARD WAS GREEN BEFORE MONEY MOVED

`DEF-3096` recorded that the 2026-09-02 swap left twelve cases red across four files and
that four were repaired, leaving **eight for the lane that moved the seed**. Measured
here on a pristine detached worktree at the tip with zero edits: **nine**, not eight.

| file | red | cause |
|---|---|---|
| `test_br_met_1160_upload_unit_mismatch.py` | tc1, tc2, tc7 | `register_reads` omitted `alt_uom`, and an omitted key means *keep what is on file* — so `primary_uom: "therm"` collided with the `therm` the new seed left in the alternate slot and `BR-TEN-027`'s `alt_equals_primary` refused FIRST. Each case died on a **settings** refusal before reaching the unit-gate assertion it was written for. |
| `test_us_ten_007_008_services_uom.py` | US-TEN-007 TC-1 | asserted `primary_uom == "therm"` — `DEF-TEN-4505`, the superseded value. |
| `test_us_ten_007_008_services_uom.py` | US-TEN-008 TC-4 | same omitted-key collision: it got `VAL-002` where it asserts `VAL-005`, so the **deactivated-lookup refusal it exists to prove was never reached** and went untested for five days. |
| `test_def_184_uom_service_scope.py` | 3 cases | the DERIVED uom scope moved with the rest of `DEF-3230`'s ten-service rewrite: `kW` **widened** to *All services* (solar and battery are both priced per `kW`, so three services name it) and `kgal` **narrowed** to water (storm water moved to `ERU`). The map also never learned `connection → fire`, seeded since `CR-063` on the same day. |

**The ninth was not gas at all** and is filed rather than fixed — `DEF-TEN-4514`:
`update_tenant_service` enforces **no role**, so US-TEN-007 TC-4's server-side
`AuthError` has never fired. Probed across four services — gas, water, electric and
trash all raise nothing — so it is service-independent. **The product is not open:**
`api.service_update` returns **403** to a billing clerk and the read returns 200, so the
door is shut at the API and what is missing is the layer behind it. Fixing it would also
refuse provisioning and the sample seeders, which pass a system actor, so it is a
judgment for tenancy's owner and not a one-line repair by a lane pricing gas.

**Nine red → one red before a single money figure moved**, which is what licensed
touching the price at all.

### 3 · THE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE, WITH THEIR REASONING

1. **The stored spelling is `"1.1500"` and the workbook quote stays `"1.15"`.** CLAUDE.md
   hard rule 2 stores money to four decimals and `CR-062` E8 asserts that spelling on
   every seeded figure — `"1.15"` would have failed it. They are legitimately two
   different things (a quotation and a stored price), `$1.15` is exact at two decimals so
   no precision is at stake, and a **Decimal-equality assertion pins them together** so
   they cannot drift into two different prices.
2. **`BACKBONE_USAGE_UNPRICED` is KEPT, and its reason is now a different one.** With gas
   priced, all four services in `METERED_ESTATE_SERVICES` price their usage, so **no
   seeded service lands on the stored zero any more**. This file's own rule is that a
   constant with no live caller is retired — and it still HAS one, as the `.get()` default
   in `_backbone_schedule_payload`. What it is now is a **safety net**: a fifth metered
   service arriving unpriced finds a stored zero that prints `$0.00` and names its gap,
   rather than a blank that stops the bill (`CR-013` part 1 / `DEF-277`). Retiring it is a
   larger judgment than the defect that priced gas and is recorded here rather than taken
   quietly.
3. **Two tests that pinned the wrong answer were FLIPPED, not deleted**, each keeping the
   reasoning that made it right: `test_..._is_recorded_and_seeded_nowhere` (which
   *guaranteed* the seeded price was not the signed one) and `test_pure_gas_is_untouched`
   (a scope boundary, crossed by the person entitled to cross it).

### 4 · `OQ-1290` IS CLOSED, AND GAS WAS THE LAST OF ITS THREE

*"What does a demo electric, gas or storm-water tenant charge for usage?"* — **all three
answered, and not one needed a number invented.** **Electric**: `CR-062` E1, 2026-09-02, a
signed TIERED ladder; the reference 800 kWh line went `$0.00` → **`$95.50`**. **Storm
water**: 2026-09-01, a **ruled** zero rather than a missing figure — a CAPACITY service
whose impervious-area characteristic nobody records, which `BR-MET-108` bills as zero
(*"Bill it as zero"*), stamped and surfaced. **Gas**: today.

**Closing it was a fan-out and not a status edit**, per CLAUDE.md: the register row's
status AND its body (every gas paragraph in it dates from before the swap and is now
marked history), the epic `EP-TEN-06` TC-1, `apps/rating/sample_data`'s module docstring,
its `NOT_SEEDED` tuple — **the entry is REMOVED**, because a Sample-data panel still
reporting *"no usage price is seeded"* over a bill charging `$46.00` is worse than
silence — and the check that guarded it, which now asserts the opposite.

### 5 · NO FROZEN FIGURE MOVED, AND HERE IS HOW THAT WAS ESTABLISHED

**`B4` and `B5` name no gas figure at all** — `grep -n "gas\|1\.15\|ccf"` over
`04-money-math-rules.md` and `05-golden-tests.md` returns one line, `OQ-004`'s list of
billed WATER units. The sixteen engine-verified golden tests carry no gas case. **No
finance re-sign is owed and none was sought**: this makes the product AGREE with a signed
workbook figure, which is the opposite of reversing one.

### 6 · WHAT SHIPS

The reference gas customer's bill goes from **`$6.00`** (base only, plus twelve cents of
tax) to **`$52.00` before tax** — `40 ccf × $1.15` = **`$46.00`** usage plus the signed
`$6.00` base. Across the 48 seeded seats a gas demo now shows a utility its own business
instead of a base charge. 🔒 `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING`, row in
`12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md` with that worked figure.

### 7 · THE ID THAT WAS NEARLY A COLLISION

A previous lane had this brief and was killed mid-work; its untracked walkthrough named
`DEF-RAT-4511`. **That number is now `DEF-GOV-4511`.** `file_defect.py`'s own `max + 1`
offered **4512**, which is also taken — `DEF-MET-4512` is cited twice from
`core/sample_fixture.py` by a sibling whose register row is not pushed, so it is invisible
to every listing that tool can read. `10-scripts/allocate.py defect --verify 4512` is what
said so. **This is law 11's *an allocated id is a blob too*, caught at allocation instead
of after the push**, and it is the second time in a week that the broader remote-aware
allocator has caught what the register's own `max + 1` could not.

## 2026-09-07 · TWO ID COLLISIONS IN ONE LANE, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM WAS REAL (`DEF-GOV-4517`)

The gas-price lane (`DEF-RAT-4516`) hit CLAUDE.md law 11's *an allocated id is a blob
too* **three times in one afternoon**, and the three are worth separating because the
right response differed each time.

**1 · REAL, CAUGHT AT ALLOCATION.** `file_defect.py`'s own `max + 1` offered **4512**.
`DEF-MET-4512` was already cited twice from `06-backend/core/sample_fixture.py` by a
sibling whose register row was not pushed — **invisible to every listing `file_defect.py`
can read**, because that tool sees the register and the pushed world. `allocate.py defect
--verify 4512` reads code and commit messages too, and refused it. The lane reserved
`4513`–`4515` in `14-id-reservations.md` and filed into the block.

**2 · REAL, CAUGHT AT PUSH.** While the lane worked, a sibling pushed **`DEF-WRK-4513`**.
The re-derivation of every register blob from the pinned tip is what surfaced it: an
append onto the copy read hours earlier would have published a **duplicate id** into a
2,246-row register, where a duplicate reads as a register and not as an error. The gas row
moved `4513` → **`4516`** and its sixteen citations moved with it. **This is the clause
that says re-derive BOTH the bytes and the ids, unconditionally, on every push** — and it
is the second time in three days it has paid for itself.

**3 · NOT REAL, AND IT NEARLY COST A POINTLESS RENUMBER.** The same verify then reported
**`defect 4514: TAKEN — a sibling pushed it`** and the same for `4515`. No sibling had.
The "sibling" was **the lane's own first commit**, `e95ed973`, whose message ends *"Also
files DEF-TEN-4514 and DEF-RAT-4515"* — and `allocate.py` reads commit messages as an id
source. `git log --grep` over the branch shows the only commits naming either id are that
lane's own two, and the register carries exactly one row per id.

⚠ **THE LESSON IS NOT *"the allocator is wrong"* — IT IS THAT COLLISION 2 MADE COLLISION 3
CREDIBLE.** A lane that has just renumbered sixteen citations for a genuine collision will
believe the next refusal without checking, which is precisely when it should check. The
tool's wording does the damage: *"a sibling pushed it"* names a culprit, where the true
statement is *"this number appears somewhere I can see and I cannot tell whose it is"*.
That is law 11's `--stat` shape and law 7's *check whose output cannot distinguish pass
from fail* — a **good** check (source 1 above is exactly why the commit-message source
exists and it caught a real fault) reporting its finding with false certainty.

**Filed as `DEF-GOV-4517`, not fixed here**, with the two candidate repairs written down:
teach it the caller's identity, or — simpler and probably better — keep the finding and
change the words, so a hit from a COMMIT MESSAGE reads as a maybe while a hit from a
pushed REGISTER ROW keeps the flat refusal. The second needs no notion of identity and
removes the false certainty, which is the actual defect.

**Until then, the one-line check before renumbering anything is `git log --grep=<id>
--all`.** It takes a second and it is the difference between a real collision and your own
reflection.

## 2026-09-07 — THE BILL GETS A DESIGN, AND THE PREVIEW WAS NEVER THE BUG (`DEF-BIL-4524`)

**The Product Owner, on the bill-layout chooser for at least the fourth time:**
*"you still gen me like this - I want formated templated not like this; we agrred
like this"*, beside the wireframe we agreed. All three visible previews were raw
monospaced text — `UTILITY BILL / Utility  Water corp / Address  — / contact
john@gmail.com`, columns held apart by spaces.

**The preview was correct and was never the defect.** `layout_preview_api.py`
renders a REAL issued bill of the tenant's through `documents.render_invoice`'s
own serialiser, deliberately, because a drawing assembled there would be a second
renderer that agrees with the first until the day it does not. That decision
stands. What the frame was faithfully showing is what a customer receives:
`grep -c font-family 06-backend/apps/billing/documents.py` returned **0**, and so
did a search for any stylesheet in the whole app. **Every bill this product has
ever produced was unstyled.**

### 1 · THE CHOOSER SHOWS THE **PDF**, SO CSS ALONE WOULD HAVE FIXED NOTHING

The brief anticipated that the PDF might not honour a stylesheet and asked for it
to be said rather than worked around. It is worse than not honouring one: the
five frames are `<iframe src=".../preview.pdf">`, so **the artefact the PO was
looking at is the hand-written PDF and no CSS reaches it at all.** A lane that
styled only the HTML would have shipped a real improvement to the e-bill email
and left this screen byte-for-byte as it was — and would have reported it fixed.
So both serialisations were typeset, in one commit, from the same constants.

### 2 · HELVETICA NEEDED A METRIC TABLE, AND THE MODULE HAD ALREADY NAMED THE RISK

Courier was not a lazy choice: fixed pitch makes a column position integer
arithmetic on characters, and `documents.py`'s own docstring rejects ReportLab
partly for *"a font-metric table to transcribe and get subtly wrong"*. That
objection is correct, and a wrong advance for `1` would move every money column
on every bill by a hair with nothing in this repo able to see it (law 6).

**So the table was not transcribed — it was MEASURED**, from the same Base-14
metrics a reader uses, and the measurement is in the repo rather than in a
sentence claiming it happened (law 1). `10-scripts/measure_base14_widths.py`
draws eight copies of each WinAnsi character at 100pt, reads back the word boxes
a PDF text layer reports, divides, **prints exactly the two literals
`documents.py` holds**, and checks itself on four whole strings first. The worked
figures, all eight agreeing to the hundredth of a point:

| string | measured | computed from the table |
|---|---|---|
| `Brazos Bend Utilities` | 922.50 | 922.50 |
| `Total due 22 Aug 2026` | 1011.80 | 1011.80 |
| `1,234.56 USD` | 628.10 | 628.10 |
| `Service period 1 Jul 2026 – 31 Jul 2026` | 1756.50 | 1756.50 |

**No dependency was added and the deployment image does not change.** Still the
standard library, still unembedded Base-14, so `OQ-149` — a real HTML/CSS engine
for a tenant's OWN designed body — is untouched and still OPEN. Helvetica's
digits are all 556/1000, i.e. already tabular, so money needs no second face.

### 3 · THE MASTHEAD LOST ITS LABELS ON **BOTH** SERIALISATIONS, AND A TEST NOW PINS THAT

The three lines the PO quoted are the masthead band, rendered as
`<th>Utility</th><td>…</td>` like every other section. **Nobody labels their own
letterhead.** It is a letterhead now: the utility's name set large, its address
and contact small beneath, `UTILITY BILL` and the bill number opposite, and a red
rule under the block.

`test_us_bil_022_tc13` required every field's LABEL to reach both serialisations,
so it went red on exactly this. **It was amended the strong way rather than
relaxed**: the masthead's values must still reach both, and its labels must now
reach **NEITHER** — a layout that puts one back, on the page or in the markup,
fails. Both directions were proved red before the green was trusted (a label
re-added to the page; a letterhead line dropped from the HTML only).

### 4 · WHAT LOOKING AT THE RUNNING SCREEN FOUND THAT NO TEST DID

The first draft of the rewrite printed `group.absent.detail` under the charge
groups — and on a legible page that is **a paragraph of our own engineering prose,
citing A19 §1.6 and BR-BIL-069, on a customer's bill.** `_html` has never emitted
it, so it also broke the one property this pair exists to keep. Removed; the
absence still travels on `RenderedDocument.absent` and still reaches the run
report. It was found by opening the chooser in a browser and reading a preview,
which is hard-won law 6 earning its place twice in one lane.

The same look found three **existing** divergences and closed them: the page
printed a `MESSAGES` heading and an `AMOUNT DUE` heading the markup did not have,
and the two spelled the remittance stub differently. Five section names are now
constants both serialisations read.

### 5 · THE PAGE, AS A DECISION RATHER THAN AS TASTE

US Letter, 56pt margins. The product's own palette from `tokens.css` — ink
`#201e1d`, muted `#6b6664`, hairline `#d8d5d3`, accent `#ec3013` — **and not a
second design system**; the accent is used exactly once, on the rule under the
letterhead. Figures right-aligned to ONE edge so a bill reads down its money
column; hairlines between charge rows; `Total due` bold over a 1.1pt rule. The
HTML falls back to Helvetica/Arial, which is what the page sets, so the two look
like each other on a machine with no webfont.

**The stylesheet is INLINE, and that is a constraint rather than a preference:**
the document is emailed, printed, shown in a `sandbox=""` `srcDoc` iframe, and
**frozen at issue** (`frozen_bill.py`) — a bill reprinted in 2031 has to carry its
own appearance, and a stylesheet fetched from a URL is a bill whose look depends
on a deployment that may not exist. It costs ~3.4KB per stored bill.

**Two behaviours were added that the old row-counting flow could not express**:
`keep_with_next`, so a section heading is never stranded at the foot of a sheet,
and `anchor_bottom`, so the remittance stub is torn off the BOTTOM of its page
rather than left floating mid-sheet. On the demo tenant's own bill the tightened
rhythm took Standard from two pages to one.

### 6 · BILLS ALREADY ISSUED ARE NOT REPAPERED, AND NOTHING ABOUT THE PIN MOVED

`BR-BIL-026` and `frozen_bill.py` mean an issued bill reprints from the HTML and
PDF kept at issue. **So this changes bills issued from now on and no others** —
which is the same rule the banner removed in this commit was describing.

## 2026-09-07 · ADDENDUM — THE PROPOSAL FOR THE PANELS BELOW A TEMPLATE, PUT IN WRITING RATHER THAN LEFT IN A REPORT

Section C of the entry above said the proposal was with the lane report. That is
a context leak (hard-won law 10), so it is here.

**What the PO wrote:** *"in many templates surface areas is list at bottom of the
template - how to handle these changes"*.

**What is actually on the screen, read off the running app rather than guessed.**
The right-hand rail of a template stacks, in this order: *Merge fields* (about
twenty rows), *Where it's used*, *Version history*, and only then **Surfaces** —
the control that opens this notice's OTHER documents. So a System Admin editing
*Bill ready · e-bill email* discovers that the same notice also exists as an SMS
only after scrolling past three panels, and nothing beside that list says what
editing one does to the others.

⚠ **AND THE WORD IS DOING TWO JOBS ON ONE SCREEN, WHICH IS PROBABLY WHY THE
QUESTION AROSE.** `preview_surfaces` is the strip ABOVE the paper (one wording,
several channels) and `SurfaceSwitcher` is the list at the BOTTOM (several
separate templates of one event, each with its own body and its own versions).
`TemplateDetail.tsx` says in its own comment that the two *"were told apart by
reading the payload, because the word 'surface' was doing both jobs on screen"*.

**THE PROPOSAL, in two sentences, to put to the PO:** move that list to the TOP
of the rail, directly under the tabs, and say what it is rather than naming it —
*"This notice also goes out as: SMS · Printed letter"* — so it is found before a
person starts editing rather than after. And answer the question it raises in
one line beside it: **each surface is edited and published separately, so a
change here changes only the document you are looking at.**

**NOTHING WAS RESTRUCTURED ON THIS READING.** The rail's order was set
deliberately — `DEF-NOT-4456`'s comment records that the three panels come first
*"because that order is what they transcribed"* from the PO's own design — so
moving them reverses a decision that was made on purpose, and that needs the PO
rather than a lane.

## 2026-09-07 — THERMAL/HEAT BECOMES A CAPACITY SERVICE ON CONNECTED TONNAGE (`CR-080`): A DEBT PAID, A PO-APPROVED FIGURE RETIRED, AND FOUR LANE JUDGMENTS RECORDED

**PO verbatim, 2026-09-07:** *"it is capacity based - please make a note and figure
out the impact - if you ahve to write a CR to ahndle this please write"*, and, in the
same message, *"connected tonnage - it is capacity not metering; i will ahve 100 tonne
or 200 tonne etc"*. Confirmed the same day in their eleven-service walk: *"Thermal —
basis disputed - this si correct"*.

### 0 · THIS REVERSES A LANE JUDGMENT, NOT A PO DECISION — AND THE REPO SAID SO IN WRITING FOR SIX DAYS

The PO ruled on **2026-08-27**: *"(a) multiplier replaces bands for capacity services
(solar, battery, thermal); bands stay for pipe/amp/CFH - this si corect"*. **Thermal
was named in that sentence and was the one of the three never executed.** `CR-062`
withdrew solar's four inverter bands and gave battery a catalogue; thermal kept its
three `TH-CW-*` ranges and was seeded METERED at `ton-hr`, and
`apps/tenancy/service_size_classes.py` recorded the omission against itself in its own
words — *"THESE THREE ARE STILL SUPERSEDED BY THE 2026-08-27 SENTENCE AND ARE STILL
NOT WITHDRAWN — the debt solar just paid, thermal still owes"*. `BR-TEN-171` and the
decision rows of 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02 said the same thing.

**So nothing here reverses a PO decision.** What it reverses is a lane judgment made
because a ruling had not reached the code — which is the second time that exact debt
has been paid, and the first time it was paid on the same file.

⚠ **AND THE FILE'S OWN TWO REASONS FOR KEEPING THEM ARE BOTH ANSWERED, ONE OF THEM BY
ITSELF.** It gave: *(i)* CR-062 bills thermal as a METERED service on a register
reading, so it is not priced on installed capacity — the 2026-09-07 ruling reverses
exactly that; and *(ii)* each of the three rows is a RANGE (*"≤25 tons"*, *"25–100"*)
with no single value a capacity could be. **Reason (ii) was always the argument FOR
withdrawing them.** A capacity is a number you multiply; *"25–100"* is not one.

### 1 · WHAT MOVED

`SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS["thermal_heat"]` is `ServiceDefault("ton", "klb", capacity)`.
The basis and the unit moved in ONE edit, which that map's own comment requires:
*"they come from one map or they will disagree: a service cannot be capacity-based and
