## 2026-09-08 — Premises & Units, second round: eight more rulings from the screen review

The Product Owner reviewed the revised screens one at a time. Recorded the same
session, per law 9. The first of these reverses live server behaviour and changes
the fix for a defect filed hours earlier, so it is written first and at length.

### 1 · THE OWNER BECOMES OPTIONAL WHEN A PROPERTY IS CREATED

PO, verbatim: *"Owner = search ( it should be optional)"*.

⚠ **THIS REVERSES WHAT THE SERVER DOES TODAY.** `metering/services.py` refuses a
create without one — `metering.premises.owner_required` — and its own comment
explains the reasoning: the requirement is **CREATE-ONLY**, deliberately not on
PATCH, so that a ten-year-old address stays saveable, and it shipped behind the
bulk import so a utility's first upload could not be refused row by row
(`DEF-1088`, and the PO's own words then: *"we will need to careful what we do
when we upload presmies in the system first time"*).

**The reversal is coherent with what is already built and does not strand
anything.** A property saved with no owner joins the set `unmatched_premises_qs()`
already returns — the same list that holds every property predating typed owners —
and the owner-matching panel on the list is the route out of it. So the two ways to
have no owner become one way, with one place to fix it.

⚠ **`DEF-MET-4679`'s FIX CHANGES AND THE ROW IS NOW MISLEADING.** It was filed
this morning as *"the owner is required, the form never says so"*, with the implied
repair being an asterisk. The repair is now the opposite: **stop requiring it**,
mark nothing, and let the property fall into the unmatched list. The defect itself
is still real — a form that hides a requirement is a defect whichever way the
requirement then goes — but a lane picking that row up must read this ruling first.

### 2 · WHAT ELSE WAS RULED, EACH IN ONE LINE

| Ruled | The words | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **Owner search shows what they already own** | *"what if this owner has other properties in system - we shoudl give message"* | Choosing an owner shows *already owns 3 properties, master account A-10442*. That is how a clerk notices they are about to create a second record for a landlord already on the system — the duplicate-owner problem solved by saying something rather than by adding a check |
| **Utility services is a multi-select dropdown** | *"Services available = Utility services = drop down - multi select"* | One searchable control over all eleven, chosen ones as removable chips. B14 rule 9's shape, with rule 8's type-to-filter because there are more than five |
| **The premise number is shown before the save** | *"you did not show any premises number that will be genrted using numbering from settings"* | The review names the property number and the unit numbers the series is about to allocate. When the series is not set up the row says so and links to Settings — never an invented number, never a silent omission, which is what `core.numbering` already promises |
| **Common areas can be recorded while creating** | *"you did nt allow to add any Common areas when we were creating premises"* | A shared space with its own meter, billed to the owner. Every new building landed on a *Common areas* tab reading *None* because nothing ever asked |
| **A GIS-checked flag, on create and on view** | *"We will need GIS verfieid Flag or field"* | `premises.gis_unchecked` exists and is set on **none of the 673 properties** — a column that means something and has never been used. It becomes *Checked against GIS*, with who and when, and the list column gains a third state: Checked · Placed, unchecked · Not placed |
| **Sub-area belongs on create and view** | *"Sub-area - field apper only in edit , it should be ther ein create , view as well"* | It is on the real create form already; it was missing from the drawing, which is how a field quietly stops being asked for |
| **Route and cycle in the header, and settable at creation** | *"In header we are not shouding Route and Cycle information - if it is assign or if it nor assign both the thing"* | Both optional. When either is missing the header says *No route yet* rather than leaving a gap that reads as fine — a property with neither will never produce a bill |
| **Every tab of the property page gets drawn** | *"you need show pages for each tab within property page"* | Units, Common areas, Meters, Work orders and Audit log, each with its real columns taken from walking them |

### 3 · THE MAP IS OUT OF SCOPE FOR NOW

PO, verbatim: *"we dont need this right now - Drag the pin to correct it"*.

Coordinates and the parcel stay — they are shown and they are editable as plain
figures. **What is deferred is the map itself and the drag-to-correct interaction.**
⚠ This does NOT withdraw the earlier note that a unit's own point moves the
equipment map's pin: that consequence is unchanged and stands recorded, it simply
is not being drawn on these screens now.

### 4 · WHAT THIS SESSION GOT WRONG, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS INSTRUCTIVE

Three times while walking these screens a fault was nearly reported that did not
exist — the wrong search box was typed into, a page was read to a line short of the
control being looked for, and a results panel was missed because the wrong markup
was expected. Each time the product was right. Everything reported as missing was
confirmed a second way before it was written down. **The general lesson is that
these screens are easy to misread, which is itself worth knowing about them.**

## 2026-09-08 · CR-085 blueprint, wave 2 — a tile that could never render, and where the equipment screen's two missing facts come from

### 1 · `DEF-MET-4684` — *NEXT READING DUE* has never been shown to anybody

`portal_reads.open_read_window_for_unit` asks for a read window with
`read_on IS NULL`. **The only `ReadWindow.objects.create` in the entire
product** is inside `read_windows.close_read_window()`, which sets `read_on`
at creation — and `close_read_window` has **no callers anywhere**. So an OPEN
window is unreachable by construction, the table is empty on every tenant
including both demos, and `CWP-033`'s next-reading tile has been dead since it
was written.

**Why nothing caught it, and this is the part worth keeping:** `None` is ALSO
the correct answer on a day with no window open, so **the dead lookup and the
quiet day produce the same output**. The query is right, the tile is wired,
`G13` sees the prop passed, and every test that could exist passes. It is
`DEF-CWP-4510`'s shape one layer down — *"it could not fail a test either:
`None` is ALSO the right answer"* — and it was found the same way that one was,
by opening the screen and asking why a thing was not there.

**THE FIX IS A DERIVATION, NOT A ROW.** A route belongs to a cycle and a cycle
carries `frequency`, `start_day`, `days_to_complete` and `first_run_date`;
`period_engine.upcoming_windows` already walks exactly that for the bill-run
wizard. `portal_reads.scheduled_read_window` reads it, stores nothing, and
**cannot be empty by construction** — a cycle with no schedule answers `None`,
which is an absence to state rather than a date to invent.

**Measured on the live `pine-hill` demo, before and after:**
`next_reading: null` → `{"from": "2026-09-14", "days_until": 6, "open_now": false}`.

⚠ **THE STORED-WINDOW BRANCH IS KEPT AND NOT DELETED.** It is the RIGHT answer
the day a crew's own window is genuinely opened — real dates beat a calendar —
and deleting it would make that future feature silently wrong. It is now
documented as unreachable-today so the next lane does not read its presence as
evidence that it works.

### 2 · `CPB-09` — the countdown is a NUMBER on the wire, and `today` is an argument

The Readings screen asks for *"Next read: Sep 30 · in 22 days"*. The server
serves `days_until: 22`; the catalogue writes *in 22 days* (B14 rule 35 — Hindi
and Japanese put the number elsewhere in the sentence, and ten catalogues cannot
translate an English string a server sent). It never goes negative: a crew
already walking the route is not *"in −3 days"*, so `open_now` is the fact the
sentence turns on and the count is clamped at zero.

`today` is a parameter (`BR-TEN-043`), which is why `GET /readings` now passes
one — a countdown read off a clock inside a read model is a figure no test can
pin.

### 3 · `CPB-10` — whose it is: a column on the TYPE, seeded from the category, never read off it

Screen 52 asks *"what is installed at my address, whose is it, and what am I
paying for it?"* and answered one third of it. Two facts were missing and each
came from a different place.

**WHOSE.** `asset_types.maintained_by` — `utility` · `customer`, a CODE the
catalogue writes as **Ours** / **Yours** (B14 rule 35). Three judgments, all
recorded rather than asked (hard-won law 13):

* **On the TYPE, not on the asset.** Whose a thing is is a property of the KIND
  of thing: all the meters are the utility's. A column on `assets` asks a clerk
  the same question 40,000 times and gets it wrong once. `BR-AST-031` already
  puts a behaviour class on a lifecycle STAGE for the same reason.
* **Seeded from `category` ONCE, in the migration, and never read live.**
  `behind_the_meter` seeds `customer`; `meters` and `sub_meters` seed `utility`.
  Reading it live would be `DEF-CWP-3765`'s *"a shape that implies it is a rule
  in disguise, and rules move"* — a utility that owns the battery it installed
  would be told on the customer's own screen that it is the customer's.
* **NOT NULLABLE, defaulting to `utility`.** A NULL means *nobody has said*, and
  this screen exists to settle the repair-bill question. *We do not know whose
  this is* beside a leaking meter is worse than stating the ordinary case and
  letting a tenant correct it.

**WHAT IT COSTS — and NO PRICE COLUMN WAS ADDED ANYWHERE.** `BR-MET-067` is
explicit: a price on an equipment or size-class lookup is *"a second, unsigned
rating input beside the signed one"*, and size-based base charges are *"a Plans
& Rates change with a finance re-sign, never a column added here"*. So the
`Monthly` column is read off **the customer's own latest issued bill**, at that
bill's own rate.

Three consequences, worked:

| the thing | its service's basis | what the column says | where the figure comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| Electric meter `E-5000` | `metered` | **No charge** | nothing — the meter is not what you pay for, the electricity is |
| Water meter `W-5000` | `metered` | **No charge** | as above |
| a 96 gal cart, a 2" fire line | `capacity` | **`$12.00` a month** | the latest bill's line RATE for that service |

⚠ **THE PER-ITEM FIGURE IS THE BILL'S `unit_price`, NEVER `amount ÷ quantity`.**
`BR-RAT-090` bills two carts as `2 × $12.00 = $24.00`, so both readings give
`12.00` on that line — and they stop agreeing the moment a proration, a partial
month or a rounding step touches the amount. Dividing would be this screen doing
arithmetic **the bill has already done**, and it would eventually contradict the
paper it exists to explain.

⚠ **TWO ABSENCES, KEPT APART.** *This kind of thing carries no monthly charge*
is a FACT (`charge_basis: "usage_only"` — the drawing writes **No charge**);
*we cannot find what you were charged* is a GAP (`monthly_charge: null` on a
capacity service). Collapsing both to `null` would print **No charge** over a
cart the customer is in fact paying for.

### 4 · `CPB-08` — a usage month says what it cost, and prices nothing

The blueprint's gap is five words: *"Nothing joins a usage month to the bill line
it produced."* The join is the ISSUED bill whose service period contains the
month's **LAST** day — the same period match `CWP-034` already makes for a
reading. The last day and not the first: a bill issued mid-month covers the
START of August and not its end, so joining on 1 August would price a whole
month's usage from a fortnight's paper.

⚠ **`amount` IS NEVER `quantity × rate` COMPUTED ON THE SCREEN.** `800 × 0.1150`
is `92.00` on a flat line and stops being so the moment a tier, a minimum or a
proration is involved — and the customer's paper says the stored figure either
way. **This is also what keeps the whole specification off B4's ❄️ FROZEN
ground: nothing here prices anything.** The specification says so itself —
*"the figure is the bill's own line, not a re-calculation."*

⚠ **ONE MONTH, NOT TWELVE.** A cost on every chart point would be twelve bill
lookups per service per page load — forty-eight on Ana's four services — to fill
a chart with no room to print them. The question a person arrives with is *why
does THIS one cost that*.

⚠ **`None` IS THE COMMON ANSWER, NOT THE EDGE.** The latest stated month is
usually unbilled: Ana's August is read and not billed. The screen states the
absence rather than printing `$0.00`, which is a claim that the month was free.


### 5 · Three things the BROWSER found that no test could, and one of them is my own bug

**(a) `DEF-CWP-4685` — the tile that woke up broken.** Releasing `DEF-MET-4684`
made `CWP-033`'s *NEXT READING DUE* tile render **for the first time ever**, and
it printed `2026-09-14–2026-09-14` in the KPI big-number font, wrapping over
three lines. Two faults in one: raw ISO dates on a customer screen, and a
one-day window drawn as a range between two identical dates. Its DOM test was
green over both, because it asserted `toContain("09")` — which `2026-09-02`
satisfies whichever way it is rendered. **This is hard-won law 2's mirror in its
purest form: a dead control's rendering has never been looked at, so releasing it
ships whatever was written years ago, unread.** The general rule, written down
because it will recur: **when you release a hold or a dead path, LOOK at what it
draws before trusting the test that has been green over it.**

**(b) `CPB-08` WAS ANSWERING `None` ON EVERY ACCOUNT IN THE PRODUCT, AND EVERY
UNIT TEST PASSED.** Two key names were wrong: the group key is `service` and I
read `service_code`; the line's quantity is `quantity` and I read
`quantity_display`. **Both fixtures were written by me from the shape I expected
rather than from a bill this product produces**, so the tests proved my code
agreed with my assumption. It was found by running the join over live `pine-hill`
data and watching it answer nothing where a bill plainly existed. The cases now
carry Ana's real July lines, copied out of `bill_detail_for`, and one asserts the
key name against the function that mints it.

**(c) THE BLUEPRINT DRAWS ONE CHARGE LINE AND THE PRODUCT BILLS TWO.** Ana's July
electric is `500 kWh at $0.1100 = $55.00` **and** `300 kWh at $0.1350 = $40.50` —
a tiered tariff, which is what most utilities charge. `CPB-08`'s panel serves
every line the bill wrote plus the bill's own total, `$95.50`. Serving only the
first would have shown a customer `$55.00` for a month that cost `$95.50` and
called it an explanation. **The bill's shape decides the panel's shape.**

### 6 · The cost panel walks BACK to the last month that was billed

The newest month an account has a reading for is almost never billed yet: Ana's
August is read (800 kWh, from the reading of 14 August) and unbilled, while her
June and July each cost `$95.50`. A panel tied to the latest stated month alone
would therefore read *"Not billed yet."* on every account, forever — **which is
the same shape as `DEF-MET-4684` one panel along: a screen that can only ever say
*we cannot tell you*.**

So the read walks back to the most recent month that HAS a bill, carries that
month in its own answer, and marks `is_latest_month: false` — which is what lets
the screen say *"Your newest month is not billed yet, so this is the last one that
was."* above the figures rather than silently answering about a different month
than the big number above it.

⚠ **BOUNDED AT THREE LOOKUPS.** Each step is a bill read; an unbounded walk over
a twelve-month window would be twelve per service — forty-eight on Ana's four —
to fill one panel. Three covers *this month unbilled, last month unbilled, the one
before that billed*, which is the worst ordinary case.

### 7 · A probe run from `/tmp` read ANOTHER LANE'S WORKTREE

Recorded because it wasted twenty minutes and will do it again to somebody else.
A diagnostic script run as `python3.12 /tmp/probe.py` with `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE`
set resolved `apps.portal.seams.billing_seam` to
`/home/user/SMARTBillHub/.claude/worktrees/agent-a70b03aaa0c91e503/…` — a sibling's
tree — and reported `AttributeError: no attribute 'usage_cost_for_month'` for a
function that was plainly in the file being edited. `python3.12 -c` from the
backend directory answered correctly on the same machine in the same second.
**Run probes from the backend directory with `PYTHONPATH` pinned**, or a green
answer is about somebody else's code.

## 2026-09-08 · CR-085 blueprint wave 2 — `CPB-04` is NOT in this wave, and the reason is written down rather than discovered later

Wave 2 owned six specifications. **Five shipped** — `CPB-06`, `CPB-07`, `CPB-08`,
`CPB-09`, `CPB-10`. **`CPB-04` (*"A customer can send us a meter reading"*) did
not, deliberately.**

**It is not a specification, it is a WAVE.** Unlike the other five — every one of
them a READ, answering *what did I use, what did it cost, what is at my address* —
`CPB-04` is a **WRITE into the billing chain**, and everything it needs is
already scoped as its own story:

* `US-CWP-042`, marked **wave 3** in `10-execution-plan.md`, with its own screen
  `CWP-035` (*Send us your reading*) which has no route, no `screenIds` row and no
  component;
* `BR-CWP-074` (CONFIRMED, PO 2026-09-04): *"we accept the reading - and then run
  the validation and flag it if any issue; you will also ahve to flag that this
  reading is reacievd from Cosnumer"* — an accept-then-validate path with **two
  distinct flags**, and a **fourth value on `meter_source`**, which the rule
  itself records as a **supersession** of B2's signed three (`ami` · `manual` ·
  `import`);
* two **GAP columns** that no row in this product can hold today —
  `meter_read.review_state` and `source = 'portal'` — so a migration on the
  metering write path;
* `portal_settings.self_read_enabled`, **the one portal switch that is OFF for a
  new tenant** (`CR-068` R8).

**Building that at the end of a wave would be the worst version of it:** a write
that reaches a bill, authored fast, behind a switch nobody has turned on, on a
path where `apps/portal/api.py` already says in its own words that *"a WRITE with
no screen is worse [than dead surface]: it is a route into billing nobody
clicked."*

**Nothing was left rotting to make this true.** The *Send a reading* control on
`CWP-034` is held with its reason, and — checked rather than assumed — its
**hold-expiry test is real and asserts both halves**: that `SEND_A_READING_PATH`
answers no route AND that `CWP-035` is in `unbuiltScreens`. The day the screen
lands the suite goes red and names the control still refusing over it, which is
hard-won law 2's mirror done correctly. `G103` agrees: the hold has a row saying
what would release it.

**What wave 2 leaves for whoever takes `US-CWP-042`:** the Readings screen now
carries `next_read` and its countdown (`CPB-09`), so the *"send your own before
we call"* argument has a date on screen to sit beside — which is the half of that
story that did not need a write.

## 2026-09-08 · `DEF-GOV-4686` — I reverted a sibling with the flag that exists to be careful with

**Self-reported, and the mechanism is worth more than the apology.**

Commit `71d7c3f7` (CR-085 wave 2) named **20 paths** and was pushed with
`REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1`. That flag asserts one property of **every path on the
command line**: *this file is the tip's bytes plus my own hunks*. It was true of
13 of them and false of three, and **95 lines of wave 1's `CPB-18` and `CPB-21`
work left the branch by subtraction**:

| file | lines of a sibling's work lost |
|---|---|
| `07-frontend/src/portal/api/portalClient.ts` | 25 — `PortalLevelPay.missing_months`, `offered_by` |
| `06-backend/apps/portal/seams/billing_seam.py` | 41 — *which* month is missing, on budget billing |
| `06-backend/apps/portal/selectors.py` | 29 — who set a payment plan up |

### What I actually did wrong, which is narrower than "I was careless"

I **did** rebuild from the tip — the two shared registers and all eleven locale
catalogues, and I verified each by arithmetic before pushing. Then I passed the
flag. **The error was in WHICH files I thought the property needed checking on:
I checked the files a sibling was OBVIOUSLY going to touch and assumed the rest
were mine alone.** Three files I had been editing since my previous push had
moved under me too — a portal API client, a billing seam and a selectors module,
all of which two lanes building portal screens will inevitably share.

### Every check CLAUDE.md law 11 prescribes passed on it

* the **file count** was right — I named 20 paths and 20 changed;
* **my own hunks were all present** — `git show HEAD:<path> | grep <marker>`
  succeeds for every one of my markers;
* `git show <commit>` carried **only my work**, correctly, because the deleted
  lines are not in the diff at all — they are missing from the tree the diff is
  taken against;
* `git diff --numstat <tip> <commit>` **printed the deletions** — `25`, `41`,
  `29` — and I read them as my own rewrite of `usage_cost_view` **instead of
  counting them**. That is the check that could have caught it, and it failed at
  the point where a person looks at a number and decides it seems about right.

### What found it, two pushes later

**`G54` going red on a SIBLING'S test file** — `LevelPay.dom.test.tsx` naming a
`missing_months` field that no longer existed on the type. My own
`tsc --noEmit` had been clean minutes earlier, because at that moment my tree
still held the pre-revert content; the gate ran against the branch. **A red I did
not recognise, in a file I had never opened, was the only thing standing between
this and a merge** — which is hard-won law 7's habit (1) earning its place, and
the reason that habit says to read failures you did not cause rather than to
dismiss them.

### The rule, stated so the next lane can follow it

**`REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1` is not "I was careful", it is a claim about every path
on the line, and it turns OFF the one guard that checks it.** Before passing it,
walk the command line and run
`git rev-parse <base>:<path>` against `git rev-parse <tip>:<path>` **for every
path**, rebuilding each that differs. **Better still: do not pass it.** A base
that equals the tip means either nothing to push or a check you have decided to
skip.

**The repair, which is reusable:** `git show <tip>:<path> > <path>`, then
`patch -p1` with `git diff <your-base> <your-commit> -- <path>`, then
`diff <(git show <tip>:<path>) <path> | grep '^<'` and confirm **every remaining
deletion is a line one of your own hunks replaced**. On these three files that
left 2, 1 and 5 deletions, all of them a signature or an import my change
rewrote. The portal suite went from **892 to 902** — wave 1's ten cases coming
back is what proves the restore rather than my reading of a diff.

## 2026-09-08 — Premises & Units, third round: eight rulings about how a screen is put together

The Product Owner walked the revised screens a second time. Recorded the same
session, per law 9. None of these changes a rule or a number; every one of them
changes **what a clerk meets on the screen**, which is exactly the kind of thing
that evaporates if it stays in a chat window.

| Ruled | The words | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **The property number goes in the header** | *"you ahve to show P-00080 also in header"* | The property page's header read *Premise / 412 Cypress Row / Silver Creek, TX 78611 · Apartment complex · Active*, which is the right shape and was missing the one thing a clerk reads down the phone. `P-00080` now sits first in the sub-line, in the ink colour, ahead of the town — the address leads because that is what a person recognises, and the number is there because that is what they quote |
| **Create and edit are the same screen** | *"05 Edit a property PRM-02 and create property screen should match - please update - it will help user to have simialr experience"* | Same sections in the same order, same labels, same required marks. A clerk who has created one property has already learnt how to edit one. The only differences are the ones that must differ: edit has no draft, and edit says what a change will do to things already billed |
| **A unit gets its number from the series too** | *"When we are creating Units - we are not using Numbering we have from settings - we ssign the unique number that is not coming out in units"* | Properties already show the number the series is about to allocate before the save; units did not. The generator now shows the unit numbers it will take — `U-01144` to `U-01147` — beside the labels it will create, and says so when the series is not set up rather than inventing one |
| **The unit number is shown on the units table** | *"P5 Property → Units -> in table Unit IDs are not shown"* | ⚠ **This corrects a mistake of ours, and it is written down because the mistake is the instructive part.** An earlier draft called that column a database id and removed it on the grounds of B14 rule 31. It is `unit_no` — the number from the tenant's own series, a printed reference exactly as legitimate as a property number. Nothing is removed; the label leads, the number sits under it, and the default sort moves to the label |
| **The list does not wear one unit's tabs** | *"U1 The units list … whya re we showing these - Overview / Meters / Plan / Account / Occupancy / Audit log"* | Those six tabs belong to **one** unit. On a list of 1,109 there is no unit to hang them on. They had been copied onto the list, and the same six were sitting switched-off on *Edit a unit* and *Take a unit out of service*. Removed from all three. The opposite fault was on *Unit → Meters*, which had **no** tab row and a page header of its own — so it read as somewhere you had travelled to rather than a tab of the flat you were on. It now wears the unit's header, the unit's three buttons and the six tabs, and *+ Assign from inventory* moves down onto the tab it belongs to |
| **No preamble above a form that already has a review step** | *"You are creating ... - not required; we will any way have preview and save this is duplcaite"* | The create screen opened with a sentence explaining what was about to happen, and then a review step said the same thing with the real values in it. B14 rule 32's description budget, applied by the PO before the rule was cited at them |
| **The create screen is laid out for the job, not for the table** | *"please improve the layout of this screen, interactive design, user experience"* | Where the property is · what it is · what it takes · who owns it · where it sits on the map · when it is read. Six sections in the order a clerk collects them, not the order the columns are declared in |
| **The document says where the unit screens begin** | *"Im unable tiunderstand fromw here Unit related screen start Create Unit/ View Unit and edit units. I need to clearly see those screens"* | The walkthrough splits into two named parts — eleven screens for a property, ten for a unit — each screen numbered `P1`–`P11` and `U1`–`U10`, so a reference in a conversation lands on one screen and not on a description of one |

### What this round is really about, and it is worth naming

Not one of these eight is a rule change. Six of them are **consistency**: the same
header on every tab, the same form for create and edit, the same numbering
promise for units as for properties. That is B14's whole reason for existing —
*"I want to see UI consistency every where"* — and every one of these was found
by the Product Owner looking at a screen, not by a gate. **No check in this repo
reads rendered output**, so this is the only mechanism there is, and it costs the
PO their attention every time.

The two that were our own errors are recorded as errors on purpose: the unit
number called a database id, and a tab row copied onto a list. Both are the same
shape — **a thing correct in one place, carried to a place where it is wrong** —
which is the mirror of hard-won law 12's pointer problem and has no cure but
looking.

## 2026-09-08 — Premises & Units, fourth round: twelve rulings, and six defects a walk of the live screens found

The Product Owner walked the revised screens against the RUNNING product this
time, sending screenshots of `ottumwa-water-works`. Recorded the same session,
per law 9. **Two of these reverse proposals of ours, and both times the shipped
product was right and the drawing was wrong** — which is the useful part of the
round and is written first.

### 1 · THE TAB IS **ASSETS**, AND IT HOLDS EVERY KIND OF THING WE OWN

PO, verbatim: *"Property → Meters - this should be assets - it will ahve all
meter, sub meters, cart, ERu, fire - all kind of assets will be tagged here"*.

⚠ **AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THE WALKTHROUGH PROPOSED RENAMING THIS TAB FROM
`Assets` TO `Meters`**, on the argument that *asset* was inventory language and
*meter* was what sits on a property. **That was wrong.** Counted from
`asset_types` on the live database, a tenant's catalogue holds **thirteen types
in three families**:

| Family | Types |
|---|---|
| `meters` | Meter · Net meter |
| `sub_meters` | Sub-meter |
| `behind_the_meter` | Backflow preventer · Battery storage · Comms endpoint · Container / Cart · EV charger · **Fire service line** · Generator · Modem / CPE · PV / solar · Transformer |

**Only three of the thirteen are meters, so the rename would have hidden ten.**
`BR-MET-045` already names the tab `Assets` and the component's tab id is
literally `"assets"` — the product never had this wrong. The tab keeps its name
on the property and on the unit, and the drawing now groups its rows: *meters
and sub-meters — these are what bill*, then *behind the meter — we own them,
they are not read*, with a last-read column that can say **not read** and why.

### 2 · AREA AND SUB-AREA ARE TWO CONTROLS, WHICH THEY ALREADY WERE

PO, verbatim: *"these should be 2 input fileds - Area · sub-area - not 1"*.

⚠ **ALSO ALREADY TRUE IN THE PRODUCT, AND ALSO ALREADY RULED** — by this same PO
on 2026-08-17, in the words *"when we add premises you should allow to select
areas and sub areas on premises"*. `AddPremisesWizard.tsx` carries the comment
*"TWO controls, one stored column (BR-MET-071)"*, and `areaPayloadCode` sends the
sub-area when one is chosen and otherwise the area. The drawing had collapsed
them into a single box reading *North Silver Creek · Cypress Row*, **which is how
the answer reads once given, not how it is given.** Corrected on create, on edit
and on the review step.

**The lesson from 1 and 2 together, and it is worth more than either:** a
walkthrough drawn from the SPEC and from screenshots can propose a change the
shipped product has already got right, and it reads as an improvement because
nothing contradicts it. **Before proposing that a screen change, read the
component.** Both of these cost the PO a round to catch.

### 3 · THE REST, EACH IN ONE LINE

| Ruled | The words | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **Adding units is a wizard with a review** | *"this should be wizard and you should show preview and create"* | Two steps like adding a property: Details, then Review & create. The generator writes on the press today, so a mistyped count or a pattern producing *Apt 101* where *1* was wanted is found afterwards, on a list, one row at a time |
| **It starts by asking which building** | *"firs form should start with Search premises - there is no premsies and on search you should show premises details - summary"* | Two doors need opposite things: from a property the building arrives already chosen, from the units list there is none. One search field, and choosing shows the building's address, number, type, status, how many units it has today, its route, cycle, owner and services — enough to know it is the right building before three flats are created on the wrong one |
| **A plan is attached at creation and changed on edit** | *"we shuld attached plans and it should be options, when I edit it later you should allow to change the plan ot apply the plan"* | Optional, searchable, offering only plans the building's services can be billed on. **Nothing new is needed underneath:** `BR-MET-007` is signed and the create endpoint already accepts a nested plan block — the wizard simply never drew the panel, on the reasoning that a plan is assignable once the unit exists. That reasoning holds for one unit and fails for three |
| **The unit's Overview carries its number** | *"you are not showing unit ID here"* | `U-01145` ahead of the address. Every other tab of the unit had it; the Overview did not — the same drift that had the property number missing from the property page |
| **The Overview says Assets, not Meters** | *"Meter = assets"* | The tile counts everything tagged to the unit and splits it: what is read and bills, and what is ours and is not |
| **The move screen has to be in the document** | *"Youa re not showing Unit move - screen"* | It exists, it is the ONLY button the unit page offers, and it was missing from the walkthrough entirely |
| **The account tab is expanded** | *"what all other infrmation we can display about accounts here"* | Read from the schema: the accounts table has 33 columns and six tables hanging off it, and the tab renders five facts |
| **The KPIs belong to the page, not to a tab** | *"Kpis you ahve shown on Unit view - these KPis will be displayed across all views"* | **Assets · Owed · Plan · Open work** on all six unit tabs; **Units · Assets · Owed here · Open work orders** on all six property tabs. Exactly as the header and the tab strip already are. A number true of the whole page should not be lost by moving sideways |
| **An occupied unit shows its account** | *"please display account if occupied"* | The number, the holder, the status, what is owed and when, the deposit held and whether autopay will take it, with one link out. It was a name and a number on one line |

### 4 · SIX DEFECTS, FOUND BY LOOKING AT THE RUNNING PRODUCT

Every one of these was on screen in `v2.233.0` and no gate in this repo can see
any of them, for the same reason each time: **nothing reads rendered output.**

* **`DEF-MET-4689` (high) — the Unit → Plan tab writes one date FOUR ways, two of
  them opposite orders.** The tile says `06/01/2026`; the pricing panel says
  `2026-06-01` for the **same date**; the period boxes say `01/09/2026` and
  `30/09/2026`, which are day-first; the sentence above them says `2026-09-01 to
  2026-09-30`. **A clerk reading `06/01/2026` cannot tell 1 June from 6 January**,
  and the screen supplies evidence for both readings forty pixels apart. Each
  formatter is correct in isolation — a tenant format, a stored ISO string, and
  two native date inputs the browser renders in its own locale — which is exactly
  why nothing caught it.
* **`DEF-AST-4690` (high) — `Fire service line` is missing from three of ten
  tenants.** `brazosbend`, `oak-ridge` and `silver-creek-water2` hold nine
  behind-the-meter types where the other seven hold ten. Fire is a live service
  for a customer being onboarded, and a tenant without the type cannot tag a fire
  line at all. Every tenant's catalogue is valid on its own terms, so a missing
  row is indistinguishable from a tenant that does not sell fire.
* **`DEF-CUS-4691` (high) — an account protection is on no screen a clerk reaches
  from a unit.** `account_protections` holds three rows on the demo utility. A
  protection forbids disconnection. A supervisor standing on a unit arranging a
  shut-off cannot see it, and the tab's five facts are each correct.
* **`DEF-CUS-4692` (medium) — nine account columns are populated on ZERO rows
  across both demo utilities**: cash-only, bad address, bounced-payment count,
  tax exemption, paperless, SMS reminders, preferred language, credit tier and
  the old system's reference. Two of them change what a screen should say —
  **cash-only decides whether autopay will actually take money** (the portal had
  this exact fault and it cost a wave to find), and **bad address** is a fact
  about post on an account whose address is walked from the building.
* **`DEF-MET-4693` (low) — one sentence printed seven times, and our
  implementation explained to a clerk.** *"No floor is set on this plan."* appears
  once for the plan and once for each of six services. The eligibility row reads
  *"Nothing checks a plan's eligibility rules yet. The rules are stored as they
  were written and no code reads them, so there is no result to show here."* —
  true, and B14 rule 32 forbids exactly that in clerk-facing copy.
* **`DEF-MET-4694` (low) — the move screen asks for a date format in words** —
  *"Enter the date as YYYY-MM-DD"*, which is what a screen says when it has no
  picker — **and warns about `2 account(s)`**, a machine's plural on the one
  sentence asking a person to accept an irreversible consequence.

### 5 · ONE THING WORTH KEEPING FROM THE PLAN SCREEN

The six service base charges on the live plan — Water `$8.00`, Sewer `$9.00`,
Trash `$0.00`, Solar `$0.00`, Battery `$5.00`, Fire `$0.00` — **add to exactly
the `$22.00` the plan reports as its base charges.** That is the one sum on the
screen a person can check, so the screen now says it is a sum.

And **three of the six show `$0.00` with nothing to say why.** Fire is priced by
the size of the line times the count (`CR-063`), trash per cart, solar by
capacity — so a zero base is CORRECT on all three and reads as broken. The
revised screen carries a *Priced on* column beside the figure for that reason
alone.

## 2026-09-08 — Three rules the Premises & Units blueprint holds and the repository does not

Restructuring the Premises & Units walkthrough into a blueprint produced an
appendix of every rule, figure, decision, guarantee and unstated assumption in
it. **Thirty-two of its thirty-five decisions were already recorded here** — the
four dated sections above, plus `BR-MET-1161` to `BR-MET-1164`. That was checked
rather than assumed, and it is the good news.

**Three were not, and a rule with no home is lost the day its document is.** They
are written out here, in full, so they survive.

### 1 · A BASE CHARGE OF `0.00` IS NOT FREE

On the live plan screen for `SCW-U-001` at Ottumwa Water Works, three of six
services show a base charge of **`$0.00`** — Trash, Solar and **Fire** — and
nothing on the screen says whether that means the service costs nothing or is
priced some other way.

**All three are priced some other way, and correctly:** trash per cart, solar by
capacity, and fire by the size of the line multiplied by the count (`CR-063`).
So a fire customer's `$0.00` base is *right* and reads as *broken*.

**The rule: a screen showing a base charge of zero must say what the service is
priced on instead, on the same row.** Not in a footnote, not in a tooltip. The
figure and its explanation are one fact.

### 2 · A NUMBER A SERIES WILL ALLOCATE IS SHOWN BEFORE THE SAVE AND TAKEN ON THE PRESS

The PO ruled on 2026-09-08 that the property number and the unit numbers are
shown on the review step before anything is written. **That ruling does not say
what happens if two clerks are reviewing at the same time**, and the obvious
implementation — reserving the number when the review renders — is wrong twice
over: it burns numbers on abandoned drafts, and it puts a reservation on a read.

**The rule: the number is READ for the preview and TAKEN on the press.** The
preview is a forecast, and the screen says so in those words. Where the number
moved while a clerk was reading, the commit re-reads it, the preview updates and
the button says what it is about to take.

This is the same shape as `allocate.py --verify` on the id families: re-derive at
the only moment the answer can be final.

### 3 · A DATE IS WRITTEN ONE WAY ON A SCREEN, WITH A NAMED MONTH

`DEF-MET-4689` records that the Unit → Plan tab writes one date four ways —
`06/01/2026`, `2026-06-01`, `01/09/2026` and `2026-09-01` — two of them opposite
orders forty pixels apart. **The defect is filed and the rule that would prevent
the next one is not**, which is the difference between fixing an instance and
closing a class.

**The rule: every date on a screen uses one format, and that format names its
month.** `1 Jun 2026`. A named month cannot be read two ways, which is the whole
of the argument. Each of the four formatters on that screen is correct in
isolation — a tenant setting, a stored ISO string, and two native date inputs the
browser renders in its own locale — so the rule has to be about the SCREEN and
not about any one component. That is also why no gate can find it: nothing in
this repository reads rendered output.

### AND ONE ASSUMPTION NOBODY HAS WRITTEN DOWN, WHICH IS WORSE THAN A MISSING RULE

**The tenant in a URL is a PATH SEGMENT, and the column that stores it is called
`subdomain`.** The running product serves
`/ottumwa-water-works/premises/units/<id>?tab=plan` and
`07-frontend/src/routing/screenIds.ts` declares `/:tenant/premises` — verified by
reading the router, not inferred from the field name.

**A reader who trusts the column name builds for a hostname that does not
exist.** There are roughly seventy-five routes in that register and every one of
them would be wrong. Nothing in the repository states this in words; it is
visible only to somebody who reads the router, and invisible to anybody who
reads the schema.

### WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS AT ALL

The blueprint's Appendix A marks every rule INHERITED, EXTENDS or **NO HOME**.
Three came back NO HOME. That column is the useful part of the exercise: it turns
"here are some rules" into "here are the rules that will not survive this
document", and the answer is short enough to act on in one commit.

## 2026-09-08 — CR-089 wave D: taking a place out of service, and the five judgments the ruling did not make

`BR-MET-1164` is the PO's own sentence and it settles the hard part —
*"if you ahve units - active, assets or active accounts, you cannot shut down
building pr premises"*, and *"Allow user to cahnge Unit and Premsies status"*.
Building it raised five questions the ruling does not answer. Every one is a
build judgment recorded here rather than a re-ask (law 13), and each is written
with the thing it protects.

### 1 · THE REFUSAL NAMES THE FIRST STEP, NOT EVERYTHING THAT IS WRONG

A building can be held by four things at once. The dialog draws all four counts,
and the sentence under them names **one**: *"Close the accounts first."*

The order is the order the work is actually done in — **accounts, then balances,
then assets, then units** — because an account is closed before its unit can be
taken out, and a unit's meters come off before the building goes. Listing all
four would produce *"close the accounts, then clear the balances, then remove the
assets, then deactivate the units"*, which is a plan and not a refusal, and B14
rule 33 caps a refusal at six words in any case.

**The order the counts are DRAWN in is different and deliberately so:** the PO
was shown *"4 active units · 9 attached assets · 3 open accounts"* and that is
what the screen renders, top to bottom. Two orders, two questions, neither
derived from the other.

### 2 · A UNIT'S ATTACHED ASSETS ARE COUNTED AND DO NOT BLOCK

`BR-MET-1164` names three terms for a property and **one** for a unit: an open
account. It says nothing about a unit's meters.

**They do not block, and the reason is what the control is for.** The screen this
wave builds exists to retire a flat that has been knocked through — and a flat
that has been knocked through has a meter on it. Making a meter block would
refuse nearly every unit this product has and leave the button as decoration.

**They are still COUNTED, and drawn beside the account**, because the clerk is
about to strand them; that is CR-089's own *"what happens to the meters"*
consequence. The count links to the unit's Assets tab.

### 3 · THE WORD ON THAT COUNT IS **ASSETS**, NOT **METERS**

⚠ **THIS DEPARTS FROM A SENTENCE IN CR-089 §6, AND THE DEPARTURE IS THE PO's OWN
RULING.** §6 D2's done-when reads *"the refusal shows 1 open account · 2 attached
meters"*. On the same day, reviewing the running product, the PO ruled of the
unit's Overview tile: *"Meter = assets"* — and the tenant's catalogue holds
thirteen asset types in three families, only three of which are meters.

So the count reads **2 attached assets**, and the link goes to the unit's
**Assets** tab, which is what that tab has always been called (`BR-MET-045`, and
the component's tab id is literally `"assets"`). Naming it *meters* would have
sent a clerk looking for a tab that does not exist — which is the whole reason
every count is a link.

This is the same lesson CR-089 §1 already records against two of our own
proposals: **before proposing that a screen change, read the component.**

### 4 · A UNIT MAY NOT BE REACTIVATED ONTO AN INACTIVE PROPERTY

Nobody ruled this. It is **derived from BR-MET-1164's own first half**: a
property cannot be inactive while a unit on it is active. Allowing a unit to be
put back onto a building that is out of service would breach that invariant one
press later, leaving a live flat in a building the utility has stopped serving —
and the only way to reach that state is through the control this wave just built.

Refused by name: *"Put the property back first."*

⚠ **REACTIVATION IS OTHERWISE HELD BY NOTHING**, deliberately. Every dependency
the rule names is a reason not to STOP serving an address; none of them is a
reason not to start again. CR-089 §8 names reactivation as the one half of this
wave a rollback must keep, because reverting without it strands everything
already deactivated with no screen that can bring it back.

### 5 · TWO DOORS, ONE COMPUTATION — AND THE OLD DOOR'S BLOCKER SET WIDENED

`POST /premises/{id}/deactivate` is the premises list's row action and predates
this wave. It refused on `BR-MET-047` alone — an active account or an unpaid
balance on a member unit — so **a building with four live units could be shut
down by pressing the other button**, and a signed rule enforced at one door and
not the other is not enforced.

Both doors now ask the same `selectors.premises_status_dependencies`. The list
row records no date and no reason; the dialog's `POST /premises/{id}/status` is
the door that does. Keeping the old door rather than requiring a date and a
reason on it was the choice that breaks nothing: making them mandatory there
would have turned a live row action into a 400 on every press.

**`BR-MET-047` is not superseded.** Its money term is a different fact from an
open account — an account can be CLOSED with a balance behind it — so it is
enforced alongside the three and appears as a fourth count *"1 unit still owes"*
only when it has something to say. DEF-138's fail-closed posture (an unreadable
book BLOCKS) and DEF-099's rule (the figure travels with its `CHAR(3)`) moved
into the selector unchanged.

### AND ONE THING THE CONTROL IS GATED ON THAT THE A4 MATRIX CANNOT EXPRESS

CR-089 asks that *"a read-only role sees no button at all — absent, not
greyed"*. ⚠ **The case that actually matters is not the read-only one.** A
Billing Clerk holds **Full** on Premises/Accounts and may create and edit
properties; the status endpoint is `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)`. Gating the
button on the A4 CELL would have offered a clerk a button that can only 403 —
hard-won law 2's mirror, a dead control over a live screen, in the other
direction.

So it is gated on the ROLE, using the constant `US-MET-013`'s dispute control
already needed for exactly this reason: A4's nine rows grade a SURFACE, not one
act inside it. A `null` role — the permissions read has not landed — still
renders the button, because BR-SHL-025's honest default is never to guess a role
and the server's own 403 is the boundary either way.

**Measured in the browser on 2026-09-08** (`10-scripts/cr089_wave_d_status_walkthrough.mjs`):
signed in as the System Admin the property header reads
`Edit · Change status · + New unit`; signed in as the Billing Clerk it reads
`Edit · + New unit` and the unit header reads `Move` alone.

### WHAT THE WALK MEASURED, IN FIGURES

On `brazosbend`, property `P-00037 · 181 Willow Bend Dr`: **2 active units · 4
attached assets · 2 open accounts · 1 unit still owes**, every one a link, the
commit held on *"Close the accounts first"*, and the same transition posted
straight at the API answering **409** with `metering.premises.status.holdAccounts`
and those four counts in its params. Property `P-00052 · 3450 Oak Ridge Dr`, whose
blockers were already clear, was taken out of service for real: its unit went
first, then the property, the pill read **Inactive**, and the same button then
offered **Put back in service** with no counts drawn at all.

## 2026-09-08 · CR-085 blueprint, wave 3 — *"I need a copy of something"*, and the four ids this lane had to define before it could build them

### 0 · WHAT `CPB-14`, `CPB-15`, `CPB-19` AND `CPB-20` WERE TAKEN TO MEAN, AND ON WHAT EVIDENCE

The decision of earlier today (*"CR-085's remaining work, cut into waves"*) sets
four specifications aside as **documents (`CPB-14`, `15`, `19`, `20`)** and says
nothing else about them. The `CPB-` series is **proposed and never allocated**
(`CR-085` §4), the portal blueprint that defines them is not in this repository,
and a full-text search of the tree returns those four ids **once**, in that one
sentence. So the first act of this wave was to establish what it was building,
and this section is that record — **written before a line was changed**, so that
nobody later mistakes an invented requirement for a numbered one.

**They were derived by walking the screens**, and the derivation is stated here
with what it rests on:

| id | taken to mean | the evidence it was derived from |
|---|---|---|
| **`CPB-14`** | *A customer can take a copy of ANY document we sent them, not only a bill.* | `CWP-031` lists bills, receipts and letters, names each one, dates it and says which way it went — and its row control was refused on every non-bill row with the sentence *"We kept no copy of this."* |
| **`CPB-15`** | *A customer can take a year of them in one go.* | `CWP-031`'s drawn head action `Download a year ↓`, held with *"Downloads are not ready yet"* |
| **`CPB-19`** | *Pressing "view my bill" answers with the bill or with a sentence — never a server error, and never a promise the server then refuses.* | two **500s** measured on the live API (`GET …/bills/…/document.pdf?view=1`), and `CWP-029` rendering 53 words |
| **`CPB-20`** | *A customer can take a copy of a receipt from the screen they are already on.* | `CWP-041`'s one held button under the table, *"Receipts arrive later this year"* |

**Nothing was invented and attached to a number silently.** Where this lane
built something the four ids do not obviously cover — the SIGNED plan agreement
on `CWP-043` — it is recorded under `CPB-14` in §5 with the reason, because it
is the same document out of the same store behind the same permission and
leaving it would have been the exact fault `CPB-03` fixed one screen over.

---

### 1 · WHAT A CUSTOMER CAN DO NOW THAT THEY COULD NOT

Measured on the live demo (`pine-hill`, `ana@example.test`, five documents on
account `AC-2026-00004`):

* **Take a copy of a receipt.** `PMT-2608-W3KEPT` answers **62 bytes beginning
  `%PDF`**, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="PMT-2608-W3KEPT.pdf"`.
  Yesterday that row's control was disabled and said *"We kept no copy of
  this."* over a copy we had.
* **Take a year of everything at once.** `Download a year ↓` answers a **5,835
  byte** archive holding **4 of the 5** documents listed, one file per kept
  document, byte for byte. The fifth is the one we genuinely kept no copy of,
  and the count says so on the response rather than the archive quietly being
  short.
* **Get the receipt where they are looking for it.** `CWP-041`'s money list now
  carries the receipt on the ROW and on the phone card, addressed by the
  payment's own `PMT-` number.
* **Open a bill without meeting a server error.** The one input that made
  `GET …/document.pdf?view=1` answer **500** — a stored file whose bytes no
  longer hash to the record — is a refusal by name now.

---

### 2 · `CPB-19` — TWO FAULTS, AND BOTH ARE ABOUT TWO READS DISAGREEING

**(a) `DEF-CWP-4658`, CLOSED.** `GET …/bills/BL-2607-000003/document` answered
`{"available": true}` while `GET …/bills/BL-2607-000003/document.pdf?view=1`
answered **409** for the same bill in the same second. The screen believes
`available`: it draws the frame, the sentence *"Exactly as it was printed and
posted on 2 July"* and a download link — over a file the server cannot hand
over. The cause is that the two reads answered **different questions**:
`printed_bill_for` asked whether a document ROW exists and `bill_document_pdf`
asked whether the BYTES can be served.

**It was already filed, by the test written for `DEF-CWP-4657`**, and that test
asserted `available is True` *deliberately the wrong way round* with the note
*"the day that check lands this test goes RED and names the row to close"*. **It
did exactly that.** It is one of the two reds that told this wave the row was
ready, and it is the clearest example in this repository of hard-won law 2's
mirror clause working as designed. ⚠ **This lane filed a SECOND row for the
same fault before finding that one** — the register was searched for the SCREEN
and the SEAM and not for the test that already documented it — **and that row
never reached the branch, for a second reason worth recording: at push time the
re-derivation law 11 prescribes found that a sibling had taken the very number
it had been given.** the number `4695` had gone to
`DEF-GOV-4695`, a Confirm-dialog census filed by another lane while this wave
was being built. Both lanes computed
`max + 1` correctly and got the same answer, which is the collision
`10-scripts/allocate.py` exists for and the reason the re-derivation is
unconditional. The duplicate was dropped rather than renumbered: it carried no
information `DEF-CWP-4658` did not already carry.

The fix is not a new backend method. That test's own note said an honest answer
*"needs an existence check the storage backend does not have — `put`, `get`,
`temporary_read_url` and no `exists`"*. True, and not the only way:
`printed_bill_for` now asks `document_store.fetch` **the same question the
serving path asks** and throws the bytes away. **It costs one extra object read
per open of `CWP-029`** — one document, for one customer, who is about to fetch
the same object to look at it. ⚠ **The LIST (`CWP-031`) deliberately does NOT do
this**: forty rows would be forty object reads to draw a table, so there the flag
stays a statement about the ROW and the file route answers precisely. That
asymmetry is written down rather than discovered.

**(b) `DEF-CWP-4699`, NEW.** A bill whose stored bytes no longer hash to the
record reached the customer as a **raw Django error page**. And it was not an
oversight: `ContentHashMismatch` was left uncaught **on purpose**, in three
files, each saying so, to keep `BR-NOT-027`'s distinction between *we no longer
have it* and *what we have is not what you received*. **The distinction is
right. What nobody had measured is where the raise came out** — on the one route
whose own docstring says *"NOT A 500 AND NOT A RE-RENDER"*.

There is a **third verdict** now — `not_trusted` — and it is not a softer
spelling of *not kept*: it has its own sentence (*"We cannot vouch for this
copy."*), its own `br_ref` (`BR-NOT-027`), and a test asserting the two keys are
different in both directions. Nothing degrades into a re-render, which is all
the rule ever asked for; the stack trace was never part of it.

**Proved RED first, verbatim:**

    apps.tenancy.document_storage.ContentHashMismatch: document 01a08243-f761-…
    hashed to 53c7bd99… and the record says 2d7089b2… . The bytes in the store
    are NOT the bytes that were frozen.
    django.server "GET /api/pine-hill/portal/bills/BL-2607-000003/document.pdf
    ?view=1 HTTP/1.1" 500 149

and on the screen: `Unable to find an element with the text: We cannot vouch for
this copy.`

⚠ **THE TWO 500s THE WAVE WAS HANDED COULD NOT BE REPRODUCED AS REPORTED**, and
that is said plainly rather than quietly claimed. On a freshly seeded Pine Hill
both bills answer **200**. The only input that makes that route answer 500 is
the hash mismatch above, which was reproduced by appending one byte to a stored
bill; the far likelier cause of what the walk saw — a database cloned into a
worktree whose `var/documents` holds none of its files — answers **409**, and
that is `DEF-CWP-4658` seen from the other side. Both are fixed. Neither is
claimed to be *the* 500 that was seen.

---

### 3 · `CPB-14` — THE SENTENCE THAT WAS FALSE

`CWP-031` has listed every document since `US-CWP-036` and would open exactly
one kind of them. The row control's condition was **`group == "bill"` AND a
reference AND a kept copy**, and everything else got *"We kept no copy of
this."* — **which is a false statement about every receipt and every letter
whose copy we did keep**, printed beside the row that says the opposite.
`DEF-CWP-4697`.

**Nothing could see it.** The refusal is correct for the case it was written for
and was applied to a wider one; its own test asserted the control was HELD, so
the assertion agreed with the defect. No gate in this repository asks whether a
refusal is TRUE — only whether it is present, which is `G103`'s own stated blind
spot.

**Three states now, and each is answered by the data every time it draws:**

| the row | what it draws |
|---|---|
| a copy was kept and it has a number | the copy, at `/api/{tenant}/portal/documents/{number}/file` |
| a copy was kept and it has no number | held: *"Use Download a year instead"* |
| no copy was kept | held: *"We kept no copy of this."* — now true |

⚠ **ADDRESSED BY THE NUMBER ON THE PAPER, NEVER BY A ROW ID** (B14 rule 31, and
`bill_in_set`'s own note). That is why `documents()` still publishes no
`source_id`, and it is the honest limit of the per-row control: a letter that
minted no number cannot be fetched one at a time. **It still leaves in the
year's archive**, which is why `CPB-15` is not merely a convenience — one of the
five documents on the demo account is exactly that case.

⚠ **AND THE TWO PLACES A DOCUMENT CAN BE FROZEN ARE ASKED IN ONE FUNCTION NOW.**
A bill is sealed at ISSUE against its own source; everything else is sealed at
DISPATCH against the OUTBOUND MESSAGE. `_stored` has always asked both;
`plan_agreement_bytes` asked both in its own words from `CPB-03`; a receipt and
a letter needed the same answer. Two copies of a two-place lookup is the drift
that file's own docstring warns about, so it is `stored_document_service` and
the plan route delegates to it.

---

### 4 · `CPB-15` — WHY A ZIP, AND WHAT THE COUNT IS FOR

The artefacts are frozen legal documents of more than one media type
(`frozen_bill` keeps HTML **and** PDF), so **merging them would produce a new
document the customer was never sent** — the re-render `BR-CWP-045` forbids,
wearing a different name. The archive carries each file byte for byte and adds
no cover page and no index.

**The window is twelve calendar months including this one** — `2026-09-08` →
back to `2025-10-01` — and it is measured on the queue's own day (`queued_on`),
never on `sent_on`, which is the dispatcher's stamp and is **null on everything
this deployment has ever written**. A window on a column that is always null
would answer an empty archive on every account, green, for ever.

**`X-Documents-Kept: 4` of `X-Documents-Listed: 5`.** A year in which three
letters were never frozen is a SHORTER archive, and one that quietly dropped
them would be a check that cannot fail one layer up.

⚠ **`DOCUMENT_BUNDLE_MAX = 200` IS NOT AN `NFR-5` CAP.** It bounds ONE RESPONSE,
over one account's own mail. A T5 account gets about twelve bills, twelve
receipts and a handful of letters a year, so 200 is an order of magnitude clear
of an ordinary year and still a file a browser can hold. No table, index or code
path gains a maximum.

---

### 5 · `CPB-20`, AND THE THIRD STATE ONLY A BROWSER FOUND

`CWP-041` carried **one** held button under the table — *"Receipts arrive later
this year"* — over a document `notifications` freezes at dispatch and the store
has been keeping all along. Even had it worked, a single per-page control could
not have said WHICH receipt. It is a row icon now, on the desk table and on the
phone card, and the per-page control is gone.

⚠ **IT IS ADDRESSED BY THE `PMT-` NUMBER AND NOT BY `reference`, AND THAT IS A
REAL DISTINCTION.** `_customer_reference` prefers the CHEQUE number the customer
wrote, because that is what they can find in their own bank statement; the
receipt document is filed under the payment's own number. Serving it off
`reference` would work on card and bank-transfer rows and answer *not found* on
**every cheque** — the row a person most often wants a receipt for. Two facts,
two fields, neither of them an id.

⚠ **AND THE FIRST DRAFT DREW A LIVE DOWNLOAD OVER A RECEIPT THIS DEPLOYMENT HAD
NEVER FROZEN.** `payments` knows a payment has a number; only `notifications`
knows whether a copy was kept. **Every fixture that gave a payment a number also
gave it a kept copy**, so the two could not disagree in the suite — and on the
live deployment they disagree on **every one of the 68 receipt rows the
dispatcher held**. Found by clicking, in the wave whose whole subject is that a
promise and a serving path must agree. `receipt_available` is a third field now,
asked once for the whole list through the same correspondence read `CWP-031`
draws.

**AND THE SAME HOLD, A THIRD TIME.** `CWP-043`'s *↓ Agreement* read *"Downloads
arrive later this year"* — the twin of the one `CPB-03` released on `CWP-063` a
wave earlier, over the same document class, out of the same store, behind the
same permission. Releasing a control and releasing its twin are two acts and
only the first feels like the work; both rows were `unwatched`, which is the
kind `G103` says in as many words it cannot see. It is a download now,
addressed as *this account's live plan's agreement* so that no plan id travels
(B14 rule 31, and `current_plans` publishes none).

**Three `unwatched` holds retired in one wave** — `portal.documents.downloadHeld`,
`portal.money.receiptHeld`, `portal.yourPlan.agreementHeld` — and each was
replaced by a refusal of kind `fact`, answered by the store on every draw. **A
refusal about THIS ACCOUNT cannot rot; a refusal about the WORLD can.** That is
the difference, and it is the durable part of this wave.

---

### 6 · WHAT WAS NOT BUILT, AND WHY

* **`CWP-032`'s final bill was not touched.** The 41 words the audit measured
  are the EMPTY STATE — *"When your service ends, your last bill will be
  here."* — on an account that is not leaving. The screen behind it is 250 lines
  and already links to `/bills/{number}/document`, which `CPB-14` improves for
  free. Nothing was wrong with it, and saying so is cheaper than building
  something.
* **`CWP-004`'s guest receipt download** (`portal.quickPay.receiptHeld`) stays
  held. A guest payment freezes no document and `gateway.py` records that its
  typed receipt address goes nowhere; the receipt a guest gets is `CPB-01`, and
  `CPB-01` and `CPB-22` are **wave 1's** and did not land.
* **`portal.money.exportHeld`, the CSV, stays held and is honest.** Nothing in
  this product writes a customer CSV, and a zip of frozen documents is not one.
* **`CPB-16`/`CPB-17` are still in no wave**, for the reason this morning's
  decision gives: building either would settle `/ask` versus `/ask-a-question`
  by accident.

---

### 7 · WHAT THIS COSTS IF IT IS WRONG

Nothing is refunded and no issued bill changes: the whole wave is reads, on
documents this product already froze. **Every new route serves bytes the store
already holds and renders nothing** (`BR-CWP-045`, `BR-NOT-027`), and no ❄️
FROZEN B4/B5 figure is approached — checked rather than assumed:
`04-money-math-rules.md` and `05-golden-tests.md` carry no document vocabulary
and `GT-1`..`GT-61` price no download.

**The rollback is three commits and each reverts alone**: the seam and its
verdicts, the two routes, and the screens. The one thing that does not revert is
the wording — three catalogue keys retired across eleven languages — and a
reverted screen would then draw a key rather than a sentence. Named here so
nobody meets it as a surprise.
## 2026-09-08 · CR-089 WAVE A BUILT — a property can say where it is, and five judgments the rulings did not cover

Nine tasks, `A1`–`A9`. What a clerk can do now that they could not this morning:
**open a property and read its point, its parcel and whether anybody has ever
checked it against GIS** — on the one screen whose subject is a place, which
until today showed none of the three. **Find the properties with no point at
all**, which previously took opening them one at a time. **Correct a point that
is wrong.** And **give a single unit its own point**, so a cabin in a park stops
being drawn on top of its site office.

**The figure that says why it mattered:** on the demo utility, **73 of 79
properties carry a map point and 6 do not**, and *not one of those 73 points had
ever appeared on any screen*. (`CR-089` §4 measures the same thing across the
full estate: 657 of 673.)

### The five judgments, each made here rather than put to the PO (law 13)

**1 · *Checked against GIS · with who and when* needed TWO NEW COLUMNS, and
`CR-089` §5 says the only new columns in this CR are two on a unit.** That
sentence is a SIZING paragraph written before anybody asked where *who and when*
would live; the ruling it sizes asks for both. `premises.gis_checked_by` and
`premises.gis_checked_at` are added (`metering/0055`), and §5 is stamped in the
same commit.
⚠ **The alternative was reading `audit_log`, and it was rejected for a reason
worth keeping:** the audit trail does hold the row that flips the flag, and
`audit_log` **is pruned on a retention schedule** — CLAUDE.md hard rule 4 says so
in terms, and whether any row is exempt is `OQ-1340`, still OPEN. A screen taking
a person's name from a table that will be swept prints *Checked · D. Whitfield,
8 Sep 2026* today and *Checked · —* afterwards, with nothing anywhere saying a
fact had decayed. **A fact a screen must state is a fact the row must hold.**

**2 · THE FLAG ALONE COULD NOT ANSWER THE QUESTION, AND SERVING IT ALONE WOULD
HAVE BEEN WRONG ON EVERY PROPERTY IN THE PRODUCT.** `gis_unchecked` is `NOT NULL
DEFAULT false`. So *false* is what all 673 properties hold and what every create
that never mentions it gets — it means **nobody has looked**, not *somebody
checked*. A screen drawing *false* as **Checked** would have told a clerk the
whole estate had been verified by a person who does not exist. **A property is
Checked only where `gis_checked_at` records that somebody pressed the control**,
and everything else reads *Not checked yet* whichever way the boolean sits. The
stamp is written only when a caller NAMES the field, so renaming a property does
not claim somebody re-checked it.

**3 · `G85`'s ALLOW LIST IS NOW FIELD-SCOPED, WHICH IS A NARROWING OF THAT GUARD
AND NOT A LOOSENING OF IT.** `BR-MET-1162` narrows `BR-MET-1161`'s coordinate
clause and only that clause — *"The address half stands."* Before this commit a
`HOMES` entry was a whole CLASS, so putting `Unit` on the list would have
permitted `city`, `postal_code` and `address_line` on it too, and the next lane
that wanted a unit to print its own street would have met a green gate. **That is
a check that passes wrongly** (hard-won law 7, habit 2): the entry would have
been added for a real ruling, in good faith, and it would have opened the door the
ruling explicitly kept shut. `HOME_FIELDS` permits `lat`/`lng` on a unit and
nothing else, and a **third self-sabotage** — a unit declaring a `city` beside
its point — proves that half bites.

**4 · A UNIT'S OWN PARCEL IS NOT BUILT, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE
DISCOVERED.** `BR-MET-1162` gives a unit a parcel *and* a point; wave A's task
list names only `lat` and `lng` (`A1`, `A7`), and `CR-089` §5 counts two columns.
`units.external_ref` cannot double as a parcel: it is `BR-MET-404`'s LEGACY match
key under `uq_units_tenant_external_ref_ci`, and two units in one building share
one parcel — the index would refuse the second. So that half of the ruling is
**UNBUILT and owed**, recorded on `BR-MET-1162`'s own status line.

**5 · THE POINT IS SHOWN AS FIGURES AND NOT ON A MAP, AND A DATE IS SHOWN IN THE
TENANT'S OWN FORMAT.** The first is the PO's, verbatim: *"we dont need this right
now - Drag the pin to correct it"*. The second is a judgment: the GIS-check date
renders through the shared `DateCell` in the tenant's chosen format, which on the
demo utility is `09/08/2026` and not the `8 Sep 2026` `A3` writes. The blueprint's
*"a date names its month"* rule is a SCREEN-WIDE change (`DEF-MET-4689`, wave H)
and it collides with a signed tenant SETTING; **inventing a fifth date formatter
on this one fact would have been that defect rather than its fix.**

### What the browser showed that no test could

Walked in Chromium against a seeded clone. `P-00010` reads **Parcel ID
R-114-0010-010**, **On the map 30.266350, -97.742150**, **Checked against GIS ·
Checked · Dana Whitfield, 09/08/2026**. `P-00007` reads **Not checked yet**. The
list's filter panel names its dimensions *Property type, Status, Area, Location*
and the **Needs a location** chip returns **6 of 79**.

⚠ **AND IT FOUND A CHECK LOOKING AT THE WRONG THING, WHICH IS THE ONLY WAY IT
COULD HAVE BEEN FOUND.** `A5` renders the address lookup's refusal, and the first
draft recognised that refusal by reading `error.body.error.message_key` — a shape
this client never produces. `api.request` parses the envelope and throws an
`ApiError` whose key is `messageKey`, so the test was **always false**: the panel
drew nothing, exactly as it does in the ordinary no-City case, and `tsc` was
happy with the cast. Hard-won law 6 is in this repository for precisely this, and
law 7's *"ask what would make this check pass wrongly"* is what it looked like
from the inside.

### The fixture, and why it had to move

`CR-089` §3 says the demo fixture must be re-seeded or three waves cannot be
demonstrated. Two of wave A's nine were among them: `gis_unchecked` was set on
**none** of the 673 properties and `external_ref` was empty on all of them, so the
flag had no true case anywhere in the product and the field `BR-MET-1163`
relabels had nothing to show. `apply_premises_gis_states` now seeds the three
states the screens draw — on the demo utility **10 not checked, 15 checked with a
person and a date, 63 with a parcel** — deterministically, idempotently, and only
on `is_sample` rows, which is the fence `apply_premises_geo` already uses so a
REAL address a clerk typed is never given a fictional parcel. Backfilling the 673
real properties stays out of scope, as `CR-089` §4 rules.
