## 2026-09-08 · CR-085 wave 3, VERIFIED BY A SECOND LANE — what the restarted lane actually left, and the one control it never walked

The lane that built wave 3 pushed and then the container restarted before it
reported. Its work was on the branch and **nobody knew whether it worked**, so
this section is the verification, run against a database and a document store
built from nothing by the lane writing it. Everything below was measured; where
the previous lane's claim and the measurement differ, the measurement is given.

### 0 · ⚠ THE WAVE'S ENTIRE FRONT END LANDED INSIDE TWO OTHER LANES' COMMITS

This is the finding nobody had, and it is law 11 mechanism five — *a pathspec
commit publishes another lane's uncommitted work* — at a scale worth writing
down. The wave-3 lane made **two** commits, `dc37d79d` and `6bb87b00`, and
between them they contain **backend files only** (7 files, then 3).

Everything else it built was swept into siblings' commits while it worked:

| what | landed in | whose commit it says it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Documents.tsx`, `Payments.tsx`, `YourPlan.tsx`, `PrintedBill.tsx`, `holds.ts`, `portalClient.ts`, `listTable.tsx` + 4 `.dom.test.tsx` | **`85486fee`** | *CR-089 wave D — the control is the System Admin's* (a **metering** commit about premises status) |
| `cr085-w3-documents.mjs`, `cr085-w3-fixture.py`, the 276-line decision-log entry, the review-ledger row, `CR-085` §6 | **`84834a4a`** | *DEF-MET-4696 — two live sentences still say a unit never moves between premises* |

**Nothing was lost and that is exactly why it is dangerous.** Every check law 11
prescribes passes on both commits: the file counts are right, each author's own
hunks are present, and no diff shows a deletion. The damage is to the RECORD —
`git log --oneline -- 07-frontend/src/portal/documents/Documents.tsx` answers
*CR-089 wave D*, so a lane asking *when did the documents screen change and why*
is sent to a premises-status ruling. Wave 3's front end has therefore never been
reviewed under its own name, and its version bump (`2.234.0`) is recorded
against CR-089.

**No repair is proposed** — rewriting either commit would rewrite pushed history
under live lanes for a cosmetic gain. It is written here instead, which is what
the record is for, and it is the concrete argument for the habit CLAUDE.md law
12 already ends on: **dispatch every lane into its own `git worktree`.** Both
sweeping lanes were working in the shared tree.

### 1 · THE TWO 500s THE WAVE WAS HANDED — WHAT THEY ACTUALLY WERE

The brief named `GET …/portal/bills/BL-2608-000052/document.pdf?view=1` and
`…/BL-2607-000001/…` as **500s**. Both were re-run on a freshly built Pine Hill
signed in as `ana@example.test`:

    BL-2608-000052   document → 404 · document.pdf?view=1 → 404
    BL-2607-000001   document → 404 · document.pdf?view=1 → 404
    BL-2607-000003   document → 200 · document.pdf?view=1 → 200, 16,407 bytes

**Neither bill belongs to that login.** `BL-2608-000052` is on `AC-2026-00013`
and `BL-2607-000001` on `AC-2026-00001`; ana holds `AC-2026-00004`. **404 is the
correct answer** and `BR-CWP-010` is working. The previous lane's note that it
could not reproduce the two 500s as reported is CONFIRMED, and the reason is now
known rather than guessed: whoever audited them was not signed in as the account
that owns them, or was reading a store that did not hold their files.

⚠ **AND THE STORE IS WORKTREE-LOCAL, WHICH IS WHY A CLONED DATABASE LIES.**
`config/settings/local.py` sets `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_DIR = BASE_DIR/var/documents`,
and `var/` is untracked. So a `proof-db.sh clone` opened from a fresh worktree
has every document ROW and **not one of the files**, and every document route
answers *we kept no copy of this* over documents that exist. That is not a bug
and it is not obvious; it is written here because it will otherwise be
rediscovered as a broken screen by every lane that clones a database into a new
worktree.

### 2 · BOTH FAULTS ARE FIXED, MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER ON ONE DATABASE

A second backend was run at `dc37d79d~1` against the **same** database and the
**same** document store, so the only variable is the code.

**(a) `DEF-CWP-4658` — the two reads disagreeing.** Bill `BL-2607-000003`, its
stored file moved out of the store:

    BEFORE  …/document        200  {"available": true,  "unavailable_reason": null}
            …/document.pdf    409  portal.billDocument.notKept
    AFTER   …/document        200  {"available": false, "unavailable_reason": "document_not_stored"}
            …/document.pdf    409  portal.billDocument.notKept

Before, the screen drew the frame, the sentence *"Exactly as it was printed and
posted"* and a download link over a file the server would refuse. Now the two
answers agree.

**(b) `DEF-CWP-4699` — the raw 500.** Same bill, one byte appended to the stored
PDF so its hash no longer matches the record:

    BEFORE  …/document.pdf?view=1  500  {"code":"SYS-INTERNAL"}
            server: apps.tenancy.document_storage.ContentHashMismatch: document
            01a082ac-5e36-… hashed to 638c258d… and the record says ac5ceebb… .
            The bytes in the store are NOT the bytes that were frozen.
    AFTER   …/document.pdf?view=1  409  {"message_key":"portal.document.notTrusted",
                                         "br_ref":"BR-NOT-027"}
            …/document             200  {"available": false,
                                         "unavailable_reason":"document_bytes_do_not_match"}

`BR-NOT-027`'s distinction between *we no longer have it* and *what we have is
not what you received* survives, and the stack trace does not.

### 3 · THE FOUR HELD CONTROLS ON `CWP-031`, RE-READ IN A BROWSER

Every disabled control on the screen was enumerated with its `title`:

| the control | then | now |
|---|---|---|
| `Download a year ↓` | held, *"Downloads are not ready yet"* | **LIVE** at `/api/pine-hill/portal/accounts/{id}/documents/year.zip` |
| a row control with no visible label | *"We kept no copy of this."* | **still held, and now TRUE** — it is the one receipt this deployment never froze |
| the same shape on the LETTER row | (did not exist) | held, *"Use Download a year instead"* — honest: the row minted no number to be addressed by |
| **both pagination arrows** | held, **no reason given at all** | **unchanged, and this is CORRECT** — see below |

⚠ **THE PAGINATION ARROWS ARE NOT A ROTTED HOLD AND MUST NOT BE "FIXED".** They
are `ListPager`'s `disabled={page <= 1}` and `disabled={page >= pages}` on a list
of six documents that fits one page. That is a fact about this account's data,
answered on every draw — the category this wave itself calls *a refusal that
cannot rot* — and a pager arrow at page 1 of 1 needs no sentence. They carry
`aria-label` *Previous page* / *Next page* and are reached by the shared kit, not
by portal code. **Recorded so the next audit does not file them.**

### 4 · ⚠ THE ONE CONTROL THE WAVE RELEASED AND NEVER WALKED

`CPB-14` also released `CWP-043`'s *↓ Agreement* from
`portal.yourPlan.agreementHeld`. The walkthrough written to prove the wave
printed, on every run:

    – SKIPPED: this login holds no live plan, so CWP-043 draws no action row.

and then **GREEN**. `ana@example.test` holds no plan at all on the seeded estate
— `{"plans": []}`, measured — so **the skip could never stop being a skip**. The
wave's fourth released control reached the branch having never been drawn in a
browser, inside the file whose entire purpose is that no control ships unwalked.
That is hard-won law 7's *structurally incapable of failing*, in the harness
meant to catch exactly that, and it is the sharpest lesson of this verification:
**a skip is a green light with a footnote, and a skip whose condition no fixture
ever satisfies is a check that does not exist.**

Closed in this session's `c690d3f0`: the fixture plants a live plan with a frozen
agreement and step 8b **REFUSES** where it skipped, then follows the control
rather than counting it. Proved red on the state that used to pass:

    ── 8b · CPB-14 · the SIGNED plan agreement on CWP-043 ──
    RED — this login holds no live plan, so CWP-043's agreement control cannot
    be walked.                                                          EXIT=1

and green with the fixture: the control drawn once, addressed at
`…/accounts/{id}/plans/current/agreement`, **200 not 500**, **66 bytes beginning
`%PDF`**, and the plan named `current` and never by id (B14 rule 31).

⚠ **THE AGREEMENT IS FILED AGAINST THE OUTBOUND MESSAGE, NOT THE PLAN**, and a
fixture that did it the obvious way would prove nothing: `notifications` spells a
plan `plan` and `tenancy` spells it `payment_plan` with a CHECK constraint
permitting only the second, so the source lookup can never match
(`DEF-CWP-4688`, filed not fixed). Only the dispatch lookup can hit. ⚠ And the
store REFUSED `kind="plan_agreement"` **by name**, listing its 36 permitted
kinds — the correct one is `payment_plan_agreement`. A refusal that names the
permitted set turned a guess into a two-minute fix, which is the argument for
writing refusals that way.

### 5 · WHAT ELSE THE WALK FOUND, AND WHAT IT DID NOT

**`DEF-CWP-4705`, filed and fixed.** `CWP-041`'s *See what this paid* — which
opens the BILL a payment settled — was refused with *"No receipt for this
row."*, a sentence about a different document, printed beside a receipt icon
that on the same row is a live download. **Pre-existing and dated rather than
assumed** (law 7, habit 1): `git log -S "portal.money.noReceipt" --
Payments.tsx` returns `93356954` of 2026-09-05, three days before this wave, and
`85486fee` carries no line touching it. It is `portal.money.noSingleBill` —
*"No single bill to open."* — in all eleven catalogues now.

**The wave's own screens, all measured at 1280px and 390px:** `/documents`
(*Documents and letters*), `/payments` (*What you have paid*), `/final-bill`
(*Your final bill*), `/plan` (*Your payment plan*) and `/bills/{number}/document`
(*The bill we sent you*, drawing *"Exactly as it was printed and posted on
07/02/2026"* over a live *↓ Download the bill*). **Overflow 0px on every one at
both widths. No unresolved catalogue key rendered on any screen. No 5xx
response of any kind across the whole walk.**

**Backend suites:** `test_cr085_w3_document_copies.py` + `test_us_cwp_034_printed_bill.py`
= **30 passed**. `tsc --noEmit` clean. `Payments.dom.test.tsx` 19/19.

**Not touched, deliberately:** `/requests`, `/track`, `/requests/{reference}`,
`/bills/{ref}/dispute` and `/report` are wave 4's and landed on this branch while
this ran. **`portal.money.exportHeld`** (the CSV) and the two `quickPay` receipt
holds stay held and stay honest — nothing in this product writes a customer CSV,
and a guest payment freezes no document.

⚠ **AND ONE ORPHAN WAS LEFT ON PURPOSE — WHICH WAS WRONG, AND IS CORRECTED
HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO ROT (amended the same day, commit `c66b6b2a`).** This
paragraph first read that `portal.money.noReceipt`, made callerless by the fix
above, should stay: *"deleting a key from eleven shared catalogues to tidy an
orphan is a wider blast radius than the orphan costs"*. **`G18` disagrees by
name.** A key nothing calls is a line on its *renders to nobody* list — a real
finding, not tidiness — and this one was there because of my own change:

    before   403 dead (172 unparked, renders to nobody)
    after    394 dead (163 unparked)

It is retired from all eleven catalogues, one line each, prefix AND suffix proved
byte-identical. The `DEF-CUS-3653` habit still applies and was run again first —
grep the CONSUMERS before retiring a value — and it returned one hit, a comment.
⚠ **HOW THE WRONG CALL SURVIVED IS THE LESSON.** The gate output first read was a
TRUNCATED capture holding only the last twenty rows, and the five gates a
catalogue edit can break — `G15`, `G18`, `G27`, `G32`, `G33` — were all above the
cut. **A truncated log reads exactly like a clean one**, and the claim was made
and reported before anybody asked whether the author's own change was inside a
failing gate's count. Reading the failures you did not cause is only half of it;
the other half is checking whether one of them is now yours.

## 2026-09-08 · CR-089 WAVE I BUILT — the unit's Account tab, and a salvage from a lane the container killed

`PUJ-36`..`PUJ-41` (`I1`..`I6`), `DEF-CUS-4691`, `DEF-CUS-4692`. Version `2.234.2`.

### 0 · THE SALVAGE, BECAUSE IT IS THE PART A LATER READER WILL NOT GUESS

A lane building this wave was killed by a container restart with its work
**never pushed**. It survived only as local commit `551a476a` in one container's
`.git`, and CLAUDE.md law 12 is exact about what that means: only what was pushed
survives, and the next restart destroys the rest.

**Its tree could not be pushed.** Measured against the tip before anything was
taken from it, `git diff --numstat` showed it would have deleted **5,396 lines
that landed after it branched** — wave A's whole migration
(`metering/0055`, −147), wave A's tests (−318), CR-085 wave 3's tests (−571),
`metering/selectors.py` (−176), `metering/services.py` (−161),
`portal/seams/payments_seam.py` (−72) and more. That is revert by subtraction,
and **every check law 11 prescribes passes on it**: the file count is right, the
author's own hunks are all present, and the deleted work is not in the diff at
all because it was never in the tree the diff is taken against.

**So the rule applied was: its NEW files are additions and can revert nothing;
every file it MODIFIED is re-derived onto the tip's bytes as additive hunks.**
Seven new files were taken (`unit_account_facts.py`, `sample_account_flags.py`,
`metering/unit_account.py`, the backend test, and three front-end files). Six
modified files were re-derived by hand — `metering/api.py` (three hunks kept, the
fourth was wave A's `location` filter being removed), `endpoints.ts` (one hunk of
four), `UnitDetailPage.tsx` (five hunks of eight; the two discarded were wave A's
`UnitPointFact`), and the eleven locale catalogues, where the merge is
**insert-only and skips any key the tip already has** — three of the dead lane's
"added" lines were reverts of wave A's copy wearing an addition's costume.

**Three defect ids it cited had never been filed** (`DEF-CUS-4697/4698/4699`
existed on no branch), so they were re-allocated against the remote through
`file_defect.py` and every citation re-pointed: `DEF-CUS-4702`, `DEF-PAY-4703`,
`DEF-CUS-4704`.

### 1 · WHAT A CLERK CAN DO NOW THAT THEY COULD NOT

Open a unit, press **Account**, and see the account's standing rather than five
fields scraped off a list row. On `brazosbend`, unit `SCW-U-359`:

> **Do not disconnect.** Medical certificate, until 11/05/2026 · set by this
> utility, from 08/07/2026

That row has been in `account_protections` all along. **It was on no screen a
clerk reaches from a unit**, so a supervisor standing on the unit arranging a
shut-off could not see the one record that forbids it — `DEF-CUS-4691`. There
are three such rows on the demo utility and the tab had no reader for any of
them.

And on `SCW-U-201`, the sentence `I3` exists for:

> Autopay — **On — but the account went cash only after 2 bounced payments, so
> nothing will be drafted**

### 2 · THE JUDGMENTS MADE HERE RATHER THAN PUT TO THE PO (law 13)

**a · A PROTECTION'S AUTHOR IS RENDERED AS A ROLE, AND THE CR's WORKED EXAMPLE
NAMES A PERSON.** `CR-089` `I1` reads *"set by D. Whitfield, 4 Aug 2026"*.
`account_protections.set_by` holds `tenant` or `regulator` — a ROLE — and **no
column in this product holds a person for a protection**. Who typed it is in
`audit_log`, which is pruned. The screen says *set by this utility*. Inventing a
name would be a fabricated attribution on the record that stops a disconnection.
⚠ **And the browser settled where the CR's name came from:** the signed-in demo
user IS **Dana Whitfield**, printed by the app frame in the sidebar. The first
version of the walkthrough's check searched the whole page for that name and
FAILED over a correct screen — hard-won law 7's *looking at the wrong thing*.

**b · `credit_tier` IS SERVED AND DRAWN NOWHERE.** `BR-CUS-058` makes it a
COMPUTED cache and `credit_tier_rules` is unbuilt, so nothing in this product
computes it. It travels with `computed: false` and its reason so a future reader
meets the reason instead of the value; a letter on screen would read as a grade
this utility awarded, which nobody did.

**c · THREE OF THE NINE EMPTY COLUMNS ARE WRITTEN DIRECTLY, AND IT IS REPORTED
RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND.** `bad_address` (`BR-PAY-018` says returned-mail
handling sets it — `delivery_return_events` rows exist and **nothing flips the
account column**), `external_ref` (writable only inside an import) and
`credit_tier` have **no writing door anywhere in the product**. The other six go
through the product's own doors, and the cash-only sanction is deliberately NOT
stamped on: `services.record_nsf` is called N times and `BR-PAY-013` trips the
flag itself, so the fixture is also a proof the rule works.

**d · A NOTE'S UNNAMED AUTHOR SAYS WHAT IT IS.** `author_name` is null on
**every note in the product** (`DEF-CUS-4704`), so the "we hold an author and
cannot name them" state is not the rare case — it is the only case. It renders
as *author not on file* rather than a bare `—` between the body and the date,
and it must never say *System*, which would attribute a clerk's note to a
machine.

**e · THE SCREEN USES THE PRODUCT'S OWN WORDS OVER THE CR's PARAPHRASE.** `I5`'s
done-when writes *"visible to the customer"*; the screen draws *Marked
customer-visible*, which is what the account's own Notes tab says about the same
flag. B14 rule 34 — one pair of words everywhere.

### 3 · WHAT THE BROWSER SHOWED THAT NO TEST COULD

A 37-check walkthrough (`10-scripts/cr089_wave_i_account_tab_walkthrough.mjs`)
drives five real accounts on the seeded demo. It was proved RED first by pointing
`UNIT_PROTECTED` at a unit with no protection — 9 checks failed by name.

⚠ **AND IT FOUND A LIVE DEFECT IN THE SHARED KIT THAT NOTHING ELSE COULD SEE.**
The protection banner is `WarningBox` on its `now` tier — B14 rule 6's danger
tone, reserved for a state a person must ACT on. It drew **no colour at all**:
`getComputedStyle` reported `borderLeftColor: rgb(32, 30, 29)` (the text colour)
and a fully transparent background, because `WARNING_TONE.now` asked for
`border-danger` and `var(--color-danger)` and this theme declares
`--color-danger-100/500/700` and **no bare `--color-danger`**.

That is `DEF-SHL-4281`, **filed by another lane on 2026-09-06 and open** — read
before re-filing (law 7's *read the failures you did not cause*, checked against
history rather than assumed). It is now fixed: the tone reads
`border-danger-700` and tints with the same token, so it matches `soon`'s shape.
**And the guard that should have caught it now does:** `runbookKitClasses.test.ts`
compiles every string in every annotated tone map — but its `FILES` list covered
the eight components CR-075 wave C ADDED and **not `WarningBox.tsx`, the file its
own header names as the defect**. Adding it made the suite fail by name
(`WarningBox.tsx names "border-danger", which this theme does not compile`)
before the fix, and pass after.

### 4 · WHAT WAS NOT BUILT, AND WHY

* **`position["disconnect_blocked"]` IS NOT CARRIED ONTO THIS TAB**, and that is
  `DEF-PAY-4703`. `payments.dunning.disconnect_blocked` reads
  `collections_pause_for` and the plan's `suspend_disconnect` election and
  **never looks at `account_protections` at all** — measured on `brazosbend`:
  `A-11902` carries a medical certificate in force to 2026-11-05 and that
  function answers **False**. Carrying it as a cross-check on the protection
  banner would have shipped the exact misreading the banner exists to prevent.
* **`paused_reason` is not shown for an account that is not in collections.**
  Payments answers `no_live_plan` for an account nobody has ever chased — true
  in its own vocabulary, and read here it would say *collections is paused
  because there is no payment plan* about an account that is not in collections.
* **The protection banner is a READ.** Lifting or recording a protection stays
  the customers module's; this screen owns no door to it and none was invented.
* **The `identity.user_display_name` seam is not published** (`DEF-CUS-4704`).
  It is identity's file, not this wave's.

## 2026-09-08 · CR-085 blueprint, wave 4 — *"I asked you for something; what is happening with it?"*, and what its four ids were taken to mean

The decision log of this same day cut CR-085's remaining specifications into
waves and set four aside as **requests (`CPB-05`, `11`, `12`) and the dispute
(`CPB-13`)**. This wave built them, and the first job was working out what they
say.

### 1 · The derivation, and it is the same admission wave 3 had to make

The `CPB-` series is **proposed and never allocated** (`CR-085` §4), the
blueprint document is **not in this repository**, and a full-text search of the
tree returns `CPB-05`, `11`, `12` and `13` **once** — in the sentence that sets
them aside. So each was derived by walking the screen it belongs to, against
the open register rows that already describe those screens' faults, and **what
was taken to mean what is written here rather than left to be inferred.**

| Spec | What it was taken to mean | The evidence it was derived from |
|---|---|---|
| **`CPB-05`** | *A request is described to the customer in the customer's terms, not in the sentence a clerk reads.* | `DEF-CWP-4198`, whose own row says the remaining half is *"a design decision and not a formatting one"*, and `13-wireframe-delta.md` row 46.4 — *"the customer described to themselves in the third person"* |
| **`CPB-11`** | *A customer can reach every request they have raised, not only the ones still open.* | `DEF-CWP-4203` / delta row 46.1 — *"a customer whose panel lists what is open has no way to reach a closed or older request"*, and `08-screen-layouts.md`'s `+ All requests →` |
| **`CPB-12`** | *The tracking screen says what the request is, when it matters, and what we are waiting for.* | `DEF-CWP-4201` and delta rows 51.1–51.4, whose title is that sentence almost word for word |
| **`CPB-13`** | *A customer disputing a bill is shown the money they are disputing and what will and will not happen to it.* | `DEF-CWP-4202` and delta rows 55.1–55.4; row 55.1 is called *"the row that matters"* |

⚠ **THE ASSIGNMENT OF NUMBER TO OUTCOME IS THIS LANE'S AND THE OUTCOMES ARE THE
DELIVERABLE.** Nothing in the repository fixes which of `CPB-05`, `11` and `12`
is which; the three were assigned in the journey order a customer meets them —
what a request is called, where the finished ones are, what its own page says.
`CPB-13` is unambiguous: the decision that cut the waves calls it *"the
dispute"* by name and there is one dispute screen. **If the blueprint says
otherwise, the labels move and not one line of the work does.**

### 2 · What a customer can do now that they could not, on the live demo

Ana (`ana@example.test`, tenant `pine-hill`, account `AC-2026-00004`) queried
her July bill through the screen, then withdrew it, then queried her June bill.

* **Her requests list said, in the column headed WHAT:** *"Queried through the
  customer portal bill BL-2608-000044 (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31, 843.36 USD):
  The bill is higher than usual. Their reason: We were away for three weeks in
  July and the house was empty.. They read the meter themselves today: 41988."*
  **271 characters, two ISO dates, a doubled full stop, and herself in the third
  person.** It reads **"A bill you queried — BL-2608-000044"** now.
* **The withdrawn one vanished.** `open_requests` came back **empty** with the
  row still on file, and nothing anywhere linked to the reference we had handed
  her. There is a **Still open / All of them** switch now, and it is absent
  until something is behind it.
* **`CWP-051` was headed *"Track your request"* whichever request you opened.**
  It is headed by the request now, with the `SR-` number as the kicker and
  *Raised 09/08/2026* under it, and the ladder says *through this website* and
  *We are waiting for: …* rather than a date alone.
* **`CWP-055` never stated the money.** Walked at 1280 and at 390: not one
  figure on either step. It reads **"You are querying bill BL-2607-000003,
  $611.49."** now, and the check-and-send row is the number and the figure.

### 3 · Three judgments nothing signed covers, recorded rather than asked (law 13)

**(a) `All requests →` is a SWITCH and not the drawing's second screen.**
`08-screen-layouts.md` puts that control at the top right of the OPEN REQUESTS
panel and **allocates no `CWP-###` for the screen it would open**. `G82` refuses
a portal route whose id nobody issued — *"an invented id is an id nobody can
look up in a bug report"* — so building the drawing literally would have meant
minting a screen id this lane has no authority to mint. A switch delivers the
outcome (a customer can reach a request that is finished) at this screen's own
address and invents nothing. **If the blueprint later allocates that id, the
switch becomes a link and the read behind it does not change.**

**(b) The customer's own words are kept as a SECOND row rather than by rewriting
the clerk's sentence.** `what_they_said` is documented as the applicant's own
words and four of the six portal shapes compose a worklist sentence into it,
because `service_requests` carries no category column (`DEF-CWP-3881`). The
clerk's sentence is untouched — `open_query_on_bill` matches on it and the
worklist reads it — and `services._keep_their_own_words` writes what the
customer typed as a `customer_visible` note, which is what `note_from_portal`
was built for. **The alternative was a migration on another module's table to
add a title column, which is a larger change than this wave's own subject.**

**(c) The title is DERIVED from the marker the write already puts at the front
of that column.** That is not a new mechanism: `open_query_on_bill` has
classified a request by matching `DISPUTE_MARKER` since wave R. The four markers
that had no reader moved out of `services.py`'s note templates into
`customers_seam`, so the string a clerk reads and the string the portal matches
on are one constant. **Ordered longest-first mechanically** (`sorted(key=len)`),
because five of the six begin *"Asked through the customer portal"* and
declaration order would file a payment-plan ask and a stop-service ask alike.

### 4 · Three things the drawing asks for that the product cannot honestly say

Recorded rather than built, and each already has a ruling behind it:

* **Delta row 55.3** — the rail panel *"A disputed reading is marked on the
  reading itself, so the next bill knows about it too."* `OQ-CWP-1681` is
  **OPEN** and what ships is option (a): **a clerk raises `metering`'s marker
  after reading the request.** Printing the sentence at the moment a customer
  presses send would promise a thing that has not happened. **This is the same
  shape as row 55.5 one row down, which the delta file already marks as
  unbuildable — 55.3 was not marked and should have been.**
* **Delta row 51.4's third description** — *"Sarah at the office"*, the acting
  clerk. `customers_seam._customer_visible_events` drops the actor **by name**
  (`BR-CWP-052`): *"who inside the utility touched it is the utility's
  business"*. It is not served, so it is not drawn, and a test asserts its
  absence so nobody completes the ladder by inventing a name.
* **Delta row 51.2's fourth rail row** — *Last day of service `17 Sep 2026`*.
  A move-out fact that lives inside the composed sentence and has no column
  (`DEF-CWP-3881` again). Absent rather than guessed at (`BR-CWP-093`).

### 5 · `CPB-16` and `CPB-17` were not touched, and one control was left alone on purpose

`CR-085` §4 item 1 records that **`/ask` versus `/ask-a-question` is an OPEN
question the Product Owner has not ruled on**, and the wave cut puts those two
specifications in no wave for that reason. `DEF-CWP-4202` covers **two** screens
— `CWP-055` and `CWP-054` *Ask a question* — and **only the `CWP-055` half was
built.** Rows 54.1, 54.3 and 54.4 stay open, named here so they are not read as
missed. `TrackRequest.tsx`'s finished-request card still links `/ask-a-question`
exactly as it did; nothing was added, removed or repointed on either address.

### 6 · Four defects this wave found, none of which a gate could have

`DEF-CWP-4706` (the list's tone map held seven of eleven states, so a withdrawn
request would have read *With us* — unreachable until this wave widened the
read, which is hard-won law 7's *structurally incapable of failing* in its
quietest form) · `DEF-CWP-4707` (`CWP-051`'s own test mounted the screen with no
`/:tenant/portal` route) · `DEF-CWP-4708` (`CWP-051` printed the clerk's
sentence in the thread under **You** — `DEF-CWP-4198`'s second surface, which
that row's `surface` field does not name) · `DEF-CWP-4709` (the list and the
detail kept two catalogues for the same eleven states and they disagreed).

⚠ **`DEF-CWP-4708` WAS FOUND BY WALKING THIS WAVE'S OWN FIX**, and only because
the fix made it visible: the customer note `CPB-05` adds appeared BESIDE the
clerk sentence, the same claim twice, once in her words and once in ours. **The
general lesson is in its escape reason: when a defect names a surface, grep for
the FIELD, not for the screen.** `DEF-CWP-4198`'s `surface` names one file and
the fault was in two.

## 2026-09-08 · CR-085 wave 4, corrected the same session — *"an unused key renders nothing"* is true of a page and false of this repository

The wave-4 entry above, and `DEF-CWP-4709`'s prevention field, both argued for
**leaving** the eight catalogue keys the wave orphaned:

> *"an unused key renders nothing (`CR-085` §6) and an eleven-file deletion in a
> shared tree is a larger risk than the debt."*

**Both halves were wrong, and reading the gate suite is what said so.**

**`G18` counts every catalogue key with no call site, names them, and its own
docstring says why the count matters** — *"a dead key is either wording to
delete or a control nobody built, and you cannot tell which from a count"*.
There are **172 unparked dead keys** today and somebody will eventually have to
work through them one at a time deciding which of those two things each one is.
Eight more, each of which THIS lane could answer in a sentence and nobody else
could, makes that job harder rather than cheaper. `CR-085` §6's sentence was
written about **a screen that is reverted**, where the keys are the residue of
work that is gone; it is not a licence to leave residue behind work that landed.

And the second half — *an eleven-file deletion is a larger risk* — was answered
by the repository before the argument was made: **`10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py`'s
`retire` exists and does exactly this**, all-or-nothing across the eleven with a
parity check before a byte is written. That is CLAUDE.md law 11's last clause in
miniature: *"before you write ANYTHING that touches a shared file, read
`10-scripts/`'s listing first"* — the risk was real and the tool that removes it
was already on the branch.

**Retired:** the seven live states of `portal.requests.state.*`, orphaned when
`DEF-CWP-4709` moved `CWP-046` onto the complete eleven-state namespace, and
`portal.dispute.amountUnknown`, which this wave added and never called because
the no-amount branch falls back to the existing lead sentence instead. Each was
proved to have **zero** call sites in `07-frontend/src` and in `06-backend`
first. `portal.requests.state.withUs` **stays** — it is the fallback for a state
neither screen has a word for and it is still called.

⚠ **AND THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME READING: `G98` NAMED THREE FILES AND ONE WAS
THIS LANE'S.** `billFailed` in `DisputeBill.tsx` was assigned and never read.
The other two were dated rather than dismissed —
`git log -S "GL_MAPPING_ROUTE" -- TaxWizard.tsx` gives `97f537a8`, 2026-09-08,
CR-087 lane B, and `RunbookSetupPage.test.tsx` dates to 2026-09-05 — which is
`DEF-CWP-4187`'s rule: **calling a red pre-existing WITHOUT DATING IT does the
exact opposite of what the habit is for.** `git show db9b0ace:…` shows
`billFailed` absent at the commit this lane started from, so that one was dated
too, in the direction that made it mine.

## 2026-09-09 · CR-089 WAVE C — FOUR JUDGMENTS ON THE PROPERTY'S TABS

Six tasks (`C1`–`C6`) on the tabs of a property page. Four calls were ours to make
and are recorded here rather than put to anybody; one of them departs from the
change request's own worked line and says so in full.

### 1 · A VACANT UNIT SHOWS NO FIGURE — `CR-089` §6 `C1` DEPARTED FROM, DELIBERATELY

`C1`'s *done when* reads: *"Unit 1 · 61.40 and Unit 4 · 0.00 · Vacant — base
charges bill to the owner, right-aligned and tabular"*. **The `0.00` is not
built and will not be.**

The money on this column comes from `customers.selectors.owed_for_units`, which
resolves the **occupying** account (`BR-CUS-055`'s behaviour class). A vacant
unit has none, so **no ledger read happens at all** — and a unit whose tenant
moved out **still owing** has a CLOSED account that map deliberately excludes.
Printing `0.00` there would say *nothing is owed* over a real debt.

That is `DEF-138` word for word: the deactivation guard used to read the cached
`accounts.balance` column, which nothing writes, and answered *nothing owed* for
every unit in the estate including one whose account held an issued, unpaid
**108.88**. Its tests passed throughout. The seam's own docstring, written by
wave E the same day, states the same rule from the other side: *"The caller says
vacant, never `0.00`"*.

**What is built instead:** the sentence alone — *Vacant — base charges bill to
the owner* — which states two SIGNED facts and invents neither. `BR-MET-094` (PO
2026-08-21, *"Yes vacant units will be charged we will not option base charges
or full billing"*): a vacancy is billed AUTOMATICALLY and it is not a staff
choice. `BR-CUS-170` (PO 2026-08-27, closing `OQ-531`, *"when bill is generated
for A - we should consider common areas and U6 to U10 base charges"*): the
owner's master account carries the base charge of every unit with no occupying
account, and `billing.gather.base_charge_only_units` is the built path.

**A common area gets a DIFFERENT sentence** — *It is always billed to the
owner's account* — because `BR-MET-101` says the flag is *"what separates a
common area from a vacant unit billed to the owner"*, and telling a clerk a
hallway is *vacant* is the one place those two rows must not read alike.

### 2 · THIS LANE DELETED ITS OWN BACKEND AND USED WAVE E's

`C1` was first built as `metering.selectors.unit_owed()` — a per-unit read over
`money_block_state`. Wave `E1` landed `unit_list_rows` + `seams.owed_for_units`
the same afternoon: **one ledger read for the whole page**, forwarding
`customers._balance_cells`' own output, which is the same derivation the
accounts list, the S21 header and the unit's Account tab already show.

`unit_owed` was **removed rather than kept beside it**. `DEF-127`'s whole lesson
is that a money figure with two computations agrees on the day it is written and
disagrees the first time a posting is reversed. `push_paths.sh` is what caught
the collision — it refused the push because `metering/selectors.py` had moved
under this lane, which is the guard working exactly as law 11 describes.

### 3 · AN ENTITY-SCOPED AUDIT READ CARRIES ITS RECORDED VALUES

`C6` asks that an audit row show what a value WAS **without a press**. The rows
were already loaded with `before`/`after` — `summarize()` reads them to build the
summary string — so `audit_page(..., with_values=True)` serves the structured
pair on an **entity-scoped** query and costs **no query and no round trip**. The
alternative was a `GET /audit-log/{id}` per row from the browser: twenty-five
requests to open one tab.

**It is OFF for the unfiltered `GET /audit-log`.** `audit_row`'s key set is
pinned by `US-AUD-004` TC-1 as the ratified S61 column contract, and S61 pages a
whole tenant's log — 809 rows on the reporting tenant — where two JSON documents
per row is a payload nobody reads. `window` set the precedent for a conditional
key on this payload (archive queries only) and this follows it.

**No new exposure and the same role.** These are the exact bytes
`GET /audit-log/{id}` already serves, to the same `AdminOrExecutive` permission,
from the same columns. `BR-AUD-006` holds unchanged: values are served **as
stored**, masked ones included, and no unmask path exists.

### 4 · THE FIRE-LINE BACKFILL IS UNCONDITIONAL, NOT NARROWED TO TENANTS THAT SELL FIRE

`C5`'s task line reads *"seeded for every tenant that sells fire"*.
`assets/0013` gives the row to **every tenant that lacks it**.

The catalogue this is catching up to is not service-gated: every tenant already
holds `pv`, `ev_charger` and `container_cart` whether or not it sells solar, EV
or trash, because an asset TYPE is a vocabulary and not a product decision.
Gating on the enabled services would make the catalogue's size depend on the
service list, which no other type does, and would **re-open this very defect**
the first time a utility enables fire, since nothing would run again.

⚠ **AND THE DEFECT'S OWN EVIDENCE WAS ONE TENANT OUT OF DATE.** `DEF-AST-4690`
names `brazosbend`, `oak-ridge` and `silver-creek-water2`. Measured on the
development database on 2026-09-09, `brazosbend` **holds** the row — created
`2026-09-08 18:45`, two days after its twelve siblings. Nothing was fixed: the
row arrived as a side effect of unrelated traffic, because
`ensure_reference_catalogs()` is insert-if-absent by code and runs **lazily**,
off whatever request happens to touch it. **That is the more interesting shape
of this defect than the count in its title** — one fixture, three catalogues,
and no screen anywhere that says which. `oak-ridge` and `silver-creek-water2`
still hold nine behind-the-meter types where the other eight hold ten.

## 2026-09-09 — CR-089 wave E · A NUMBER A REVIEW SHOWS IS TAKEN ON THE PRESS (`BR-MET-1165`), AND THE FIRST IMPLEMENTATION OF IT WAS WRONG

**The rule had no home in the repository.** The *Premises & Units Blueprint*
states it, `B7` (the premise number on the property review) and `E6` (the unit
numbers on the add-units review) both depend on it, and neither wave would have
found it in any register. It is `BR-MET-1165` in
`04-docs/05-modules/04-metering/02-business-rules.md` as of today, written by
the wave E lane while building the second of those two screens.

**Half (a) — nothing is reserved by looking.** The allocation happens inside the
create's own transaction (the PO's own words for the timing, recorded on
`CR-046 D1`: *"just before updating teh record in the database"*), so two clerks
reviewing at the same moment are **both** shown `U-00421` and the second one to
press gets `U-00424`. The alternative — reserving on preview — burns a number
every time somebody opens a wizard and closes it, and needs a release path
nobody has designed. So the screen says the numbers are what the series will
issue NEXT and never says they are held; the sentence on the review is
*"These are the numbers the series will issue next. Nothing is held until you
press Create."*

**Half (b) — the preview must SIMULATE the allocator, and this is where it went
wrong (`DEF-MET-4719`).** The first implementation always caught the series
counter up past the highest number on file, reasoning from `DEF-577` that the
counter can stand behind the table. It can. But `_allocate_unused_number`
catches up **only on a collision**: it allocates, asks whether that exact value
is already in the column, and moves the counter only when the answer is yes.

Measured on the `brazosbend` demo database, 2026-09-09: the `unit` series read
`next_number = 1` with `U-00420` on file and `U-00001` free. **The review
printed `U-00421` to `U-00423`. The three units created were `U-00001`,
`U-00002`, `U-00003`.**

Every backend test passed, `tsc` passed, and the preview endpoint agreed with
itself — because a test that asks an endpoint whether it agrees with itself is
the test that cannot see this. What found it was
`10-scripts/cr089_wave_e_add_units_walkthrough.mjs`, which reads the numbers off
the RENDERED review, creates three units for real, and compares them with the
`unit_no` values the server hands back. That is hard-won law 6 doing the only
job it can do, and law 7's *"ask what would make this check pass wrongly"* is
the question the first draft never asked.

**The generalisation, and it is worth more than the fix: a preview of an
allocator is only true if it walks the allocator's own loop through the
allocator's own arithmetic.** Restating what the allocator is *for* is not the
same as predicting what it will *do*. `preview_unit_numbers` now shares
`_highest_number_in_use` with `_allocate_unused_number` and repeats its
collision test as a read, so the two cannot drift apart without one shared
change. Re-walked after the fix: the review named `U-00004` to `U-00006` and the
three units created were `U-00004`, `U-00005`, `U-00006`.

**What else this wave decided, each recorded because the next agent could not
infer it:**

* **The units list's second column is the ADDRESS, and nothing was removed.**
  The list opened `Select · Unit ID · Premise · Unit`, so the first sortable
  column was the series number and the street was the second half of a cell
  whose first half was a property code. The street leads its column now with
  `P-00043` beneath it and the label leads the identity column with `U-01144`
  beneath that. `unit_no` is **not** a database id — it is a printed reference
  off the tenant's own series, as legitimate on screen as a premise number — so
  B14 rule 31 is not in play and this is a change of weight, not of removal.
  The standalone `Unit` column joins `Occupancy` in the column chooser, both
  still sortable, because deleting a sortable column would be a capability cut
  this CR did not ask for.
* **A column labelled Address sorts by the address.** `UNIT_SORTS` gains
  `address` → `premises__address_line`. `premise` (the premise NUMBER) is kept
  on the server so an API client carrying it still works; the screen no longer
  declares it, so a saved `?sort=premise` URL falls back to the default sort,
  which is `BR-SHL-011`'s declared behaviour for a sort a screen does not offer.
* **`Owed` is `_balance_cells`' own figure, forwarded, never recomputed.** The
  accounts list, the S21 header, the unit's Account tab and this column are one
  derivation grouped four ways — `DEF-127` is what a second derivation of a
  balance costs. It is batched (`customers.selectors.owed_for_units`, three
  queries for a whole page) rather than asked per row, because the per-unit
  `unpaid_balance_state` is right for a deactivation guard and wrong for a list.
  Four states are kept apart and **only one of them is `0.00`**: a figure · *We
  could not read this.* · *Awaiting* · and a vacant unit's dash.
* **Two of those sentences are wave C's keys and not new ones.**
  `metering.units.owed.unreadable` and `.vacantOwnerBilled` landed on the branch
  while this was being written, saying exactly these facts about exactly this
  column on the property's Units tab. B14 rule 34 asks for one pair of words per
  fact, so this screen reads theirs. **The fan-in refusing a duplicate key is
  what found it** — which is an argument for `10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py` being
  the only door to the catalogues rather than a convenience.
* **The default label pattern moved from `Apt {floor}{seq:00}` to `{seq}`.**
  That default is why adding three flats produced `Apt 101, Apt 102, Apt 103`
  when the clerk wanted `1, 2, 3`. The token grammar is not deleted — a clerk
  numbering a block `Apt 101 … Apt 310` needs it — it is one line down, folded,
  and the fold shows the pattern it holds so it never hides the answer.
* **The add-units wizard is its own screen and `AddPremisesWizard` was not
  touched.** `UNITS_ADD_ROUTE` used to be `/premises/new?mode=units_pattern`, so
  `+ New unit` on a building landed on the S16 four-way chooser with an EMPTY
  premise box — a clerk standing on `P-00043` was asked to find it again out of
  seventy-nine addresses. It points at `/premises/units/new` now.
  `AddPremisesWizard`'s `units_pattern` mode is unchanged and still reachable
  from its own chooser; nothing was deleted from a wave-B file.
* **The wizard commits with `skip_errors: false`, against the bulk importer's
  own default.** A CSV of 9,881 rows should land the good ones; a clerk who has
  just READ three labels should get all three or none.
* **The generated units still get no service points, and that is left alone.**
  The address's own list governs what they may OFFER (`BR-MET-119`); creating a
  service point per service is a different act with different consequences and
  belongs on the unit's Assets tab, not smuggled into a generator.

**Two checks that were not checking, found on the way and filed rather than
fixed silently:**

* `DEF-MET-4718` — `expect(html).toContain("P-00101 · 1408 Bluestem Ln")` in
  `UnitsPage.test.tsx` was reading the **filter picker**, not the row.
  `premisesPickerOptions` builds that exact string from the same fixture, so the
  assertion passed off the toolbar and went on passing through this wave
  splitting that cell in two — the change it existed to catch. It is row-scoped
  now, through a `rowFor` helper, with `cellWith` beside it because a row also
  carries the unit number in its checkbox's accessible name.
* `DEF-CWP-4720` — `hover:bg-neutral-50` in `portal/plans/PlanOffer.tsx` is a
  class no stylesheet declares and Tailwind generates no rule for, so the hover
  state does not exist. `routeBUtilities.test.ts` has been red on it since
  `cf2de4ba` (2026-09-08); dated with `git log -S` and attributed rather than
  dismissed as *"a red I did not cause"*.

## 2026-09-09 · CR-089 wave J — the move screen says what a move does, and three of the seven sentences are about facts no screen in this product had ever shown

**The screen was already good at asking.** It asked where the unit is, where it
is going, when, and why; the reason was required and its help said plainly that
it is *"the only record of why this unit moved"*; a future date was refused with
*"this product cannot hold a move that has not happened yet"*, which is a true
statement about the product rather than a validation message. All of that is
kept, untouched.

**What it could not do was say what the move DOES.** `PUJ-46` rules seven
consequences, and two of them reach much further than the two sentences that
were there:

**1 · EVERY ASSET TAGGED TO THE UNIT CHANGES ADDRESS, AND NOTHING SAID SO.** An
address is stored on `premises` and nowhere else (hard rule 8 / `BR-MET-1161`);
an asset derives its own by walking unit → premises, which `apps/assets/
selectors.py` serves as `assigned_address`. So the meters, sub-meters and carts
on a unit are all re-addressed at the moment of the press. **Measured on
`brazosbend`, twice:** `SCW-U-002` carried `CART-0001`, `CART-0002`,
`CART-0003`, `E-5001` and `W-5001`, every one reading `103 Willow Bend Dr`;
after the move all five read `412 Cypress Row`. `U-00101-A` carried `M-7001` and
`W-7001` at `1408 Bluestem Ln`; both now read `901 Hillside Ave`. The screen
stated the count before the press in each case.

**2 · THE ROUTE AND THE CYCLE CHANGE, WHICH IS WHO READS THE METER AND WHEN IT
BILLS.** A unit takes its route from its building — `BR-MET-082` clause 2, and
`derivation._resolve_one` says so in its own comment. `derivation.routes_if_moved`
answers the second side EXACTLY rather than approximately: `Resolution` takes an
optional `premises_override` (absent means nothing changes, so `units_in_cycle`,
`members_of_route` and `route_for_unit` resolve byte-for-byte as before) and the
destination's own units are resolved alongside, so a route the destination is on
only by a sibling's live pick is a candidate. Reading the destination's units
INSTEAD would have been an approximation in the two cases the answer is most
read for: it cannot see the moving unit's service set, and it cannot see a pick
on that unit which survives the move.

**THE PREDICTION IS CHECKED AGAINST THE OUTCOME, WHICH IS THE ONLY HONEST TEST
OF A PREVIEW.** `test_the_route_it_predicts_is_the_route_the_move_produces`
makes the prediction, performs the move, and asserts the product's own answer is
the same one. Proved RED first by neutering the override:
`assert 'RT-N-P1' == 'RT-S-P1'`. And it was walked: `U-00101-A` was predicted to
leave `Route RT-002 · Cycle CY-002` and join no route at `901 Hillside Ave`
(the pick goes stale because `RT-002` is drawn over NORTH and the destination is
EAST, and the EAST routes hold live picks so their area claim does not fill in —
`_resolve_one`'s own rule). After the move `routes_for_unit` returns `{}`.
Exactly what the screen said.

### The tier, and the argument it overturns

This file carried a note saying B14 rule 6's danger tier was **not** used and
was not an oversight, because *"a move destroys nothing — it is a correction"*.
`CR-089` overrules it, and the reason is worth keeping rather than only the
ruling: a move re-attributes where the unit's NEXT bill lands, and **moving it
back is not an undo** — the second move is its own dated event with its own
reason, so afterwards the record says the unit moved twice and neither date is
wrong. `FormModal` grew `submitVariant`, the same OPTIONAL pass-through
`ConfirmDialog.confirmVariant` took for `DEF-718`; absent still means primary,
so not one other form in the product moved.

### Three judgments where the rules ran out (law 13 — recorded, not asked)

**(a) `PUJ-47`'s worked example reads *"two accounts"* and the screen prints
*"2 accounts"*.** The defect (`DEF-MET-4694`) is the `(s)`, and it is gone:
`_one`/`_other` in all eleven catalogues, with `move_unit` now sending `count`
beside `accounts` because that is the parameter i18next chooses a plural form
by. Spelling the numeral out is a rule about ENGLISH, and B14 rule 35 says a
catalogue is written in its own language rather than translated from one —
eleven number-word tables would be that rule broken eleven times to satisfy an
illustration. Wave A recorded the same departure on `A3` for the date format.

**(b) The service is named by the CLIENT and no name is served.** The first
draft served `service_name` from `seams.service_catalog()`; the browser showed
it printing `storm_water`, and the seam's own docstring asks callers not to use
it — it is the S8 SCREEN read, 41 queries on an empty tenant. `DEF-763` already
ruled `rating.service.<code>` the ONE service-name catalogue, read by
`ReadDetailPage`, `UnitDetailPage`, `ServicesAvailableField` and
`UploadReadsWizard`. So the wire carries the code and the screen names it.

**(c) `J3` is NOT DONE and is owed to billing, deliberately.** The count needs
one function — the `.count()` of the queryset `billing.selectors
.last_issued_bill_for_unit` already writes — in `apps/billing/selectors.py`,
which is another lane's this session. `seams.issued_bill_count_for_unit`
DECLARES that contract and resolves it at call time, parked in
`seam_known_gaps.txt` with the reason; `None` is served for *nobody could count
them* and never `0`, which would read as *this unit has never billed* and is the
fact that makes a move harmless. Both sides are asserted in two test files so
publishing half of it goes red.

### Two defects the walk found, both in this file, neither visible to any check

**`DEF-MET-4721` (high) — pressing *Move unit* on an empty form did nothing at
all.** No field error, no summary line, nothing focused. One thing had three
names: the zod schema keyed `premisesId`, the input carried
`id="move-premises"`, and the server files its refusal under `premises_id`.
`collectFormErrors` files by the zod path, `useFieldError` looks up by the id,
and `envelopeErrors` files by the server's field — so three errors were filed
under names no field could ever ask for, `FormErrorSummary` prints only ABOVE
three and there were exactly three, and `scrollToFirstError` focused nothing.
Measured in Chromium: `FIELD ERRORS RENDERED: []` · `FOCUSED: (none)` before;
three sentences under their own fields and `FOCUSED: premises_id` after. Every
sibling modal in the feature already names its inputs after the server's fields
(`QuickReadModal`'s `meter_no`/`read_date`); this one did not, and nothing
compares an id with a schema key.

**`DEF-MET-4722` (low) — the server's refusal printed twice, one line apart.**
The modal kept its own copy of the sentence AND returned the envelope to
`FormModal`, which renders `message_key` for every consumer. *"A move cannot be
dated in the future."*, then again. Both renderings were correct, which is why
nothing caught it and why `toContain` could not have.

### What the demo estate cannot show, measured rather than assumed

Two of `PUJ-46`/`PUJ-47`'s illustrations name data that does not exist, and this
was checked across **all nine seeded tenants** rather than one:

* **No unit anywhere has ever carried more than one account.** `"This unit has
  carried two accounts"* cannot be walked; the `_one` form is what the browser
  shows and `_other` is asserted in `MoveUnitModal.test.tsx`.
* **Almost every route claim in the estate is an explicit pick.** On
  `brazosbend`, 243 of 248 claims across all 138 units are `picked` and 5 are
  `premises`; an area-less picked route stays live wherever a unit goes, so most
  moves change no route at all and the screen truthfully says *"stays on Route
  RT-008 · Cycle CY-001"*. The change branch is reachable only where the pick
  goes STALE, which is the `U-00101-A` case above.

**The general point, and it is the same one wave K raised:** a *done when*
written from a blueprint's readings is an illustration until somebody looks it
up on one tenant. Three of this wave's four figures were.

## 2026-09-09 — CR-089 wave E, second record: the figures in `E6`'s *done when* were illustrative, and what was actually proved

`E6` asks a review to show `U-01145` to `U-01147`. **Those numbers exist on no
tenant** — CR-089 §6's correction of the same day names them among the
illustrations carried over from the blueprint's walkthrough and never looked up.
This is recorded here rather than left in the change request because the wave's
own acceptance evidence would otherwise read as though it had missed its target.

**What was proved, and it is the rule rather than the figures.** On
`brazosbend`, three separate runs on three different buildings, each one reading
the numbers off the RENDERED review before the press and comparing them with the
`unit_no` values the server handed back afterwards:

| Building | Shown on the review | Allocated on the press |
|---|---|---|
| `P-00067 · Kestrel Park ph. 2` | `U-00004` `U-00005` `U-00006` | `U-00004` `U-00005` `U-00006` |
| `P-00045 · 301 Mill Pond Ln` | `U-00007` `U-00008` `U-00009` | `U-00007` `U-00008` `U-00009` |
| the third run | `U-00010` `U-00011` `U-00012` | `U-00010` `U-00011` `U-00012` |

and, for the other half of `BR-MET-1165`, the preview asked twice in succession
answers the same three numbers and moves the counter by nothing — which is what
*two clerks reviewing at the same moment* reduces to in a single-session walk.

⚠ **The numbers are low because the `unit` series counter on `brazosbend` stands
at the bottom while `U-00420` is on file.** That is `DEF-577`'s live state, it is
lawful — the allocator's invariant is *never hand out a number that already
exists*, not *never go backwards* — and it is precisely the state that made
`DEF-MET-4719` look right. It is worth a provisioning decision at some point
(named in the review-ledger row as something for a person's eye) and it is not
blocking anything today.

**Two more things a walk found that a test would not have.**

* **The empty case is also a claim.** Typing `Zzyzx Mirage Parkway` into the
  units list returns nothing and says **"No results for 'Zzyzx Mirage
  Parkway'."** with **Clear filters** beside it — it echoes what was typed, so a
  clerk sees they mistyped rather than concluding the building has no units. The
  first version of this check looked for the words *"No units"* and failed over
  a screen behaving perfectly: a check looking at the wrong thing, and the
  assertion is stronger for having been corrected.
* **A building carried in on `?premises=` was held and not SHOWN.**
  `SearchSelectField` seeds its displayed text once, with
  `useState(selected?.label ?? "")`, and this picker's options arrive from a
  second request — so the wizard held the right building and drew its
  placeholder, which is `DEF-442`'s mechanism exactly (*two controls, one fact,
  and the one a clerk can see says the opposite*). Re-keying the control on
  whether the options have arrived remounts it once, when they do. Only a
  browser can see this, because the fault is in the ORDER two requests land in.

**The hold this wave leaves, stated with the test that will fire when it
expires.** `+ New unit` on a property's own page still calls the bare route:
`PremisesDetailPage.tsx` is wave C's file and this lane may not edit it. The
wizard reads `?premises=` already and `unitsAddPath(id)` builds the URL, so the
day that button is changed the journey closes with no further work.
`UnitsPage.test.tsx` asserts the destination and its shape — including that an
id with a `/` or a `?` in it survives — so nobody has to rediscover it.

## 2026-09-09 · CR-089 WAVE B — CREATING A PROPERTY (`2.234.7`, `2.234.12`)

**The ruling this wave carries out, verbatim (PO, 2026-09-08):** *"Owner =
search ( it should be optional) - what if this owner has other properties in
system - we shoudl give message"*. It SUPERSEDES decision 1 of 2026-08-27
(*"when presmies are created you have owner for it, without owner how you can
create premsies = owner = master account"*, `DEF-650`, `BR-MET-401`). The
supersession is create-only; PATCH never required an owner and still does not.

### The reversal is one change with two halves, and they shipped together

`B1` deletes the create-time refusal; `B2` adds the **Needs an owner** filter
that finds what the reversal now allows. CR-089 §2.1 says so in the same
sentence as the ruling, and both the selector and the chip carry that sentence
in their own comments. **Measured on `brazosbend` the day it landed:**

| | |
|---|---|
| properties | **84** |
| no typed owner (`needs_owner`) | **78** |
| with one (`has_owner`) | **6** |
| of the owner-less: hold a free-text NAME | **8** — already on PRM-04 |
| of the owner-less: hold **nothing at all** | **65** — on no list in this product before today |

That last row is why `unmatched_premises_qs()` was not enough: it reads *has a
name and no record*, so a property nobody has typed anything against is
invisible to it **by design**. The new filter asks the question a BILL asks —
*is there a party at all?*

**The rollback is still the only one in this CR that is not free (§8).**
Restoring the requirement makes every owner-less property created meanwhile
unsaveable on edit, so there is exactly ONE place that enforces it and this
wave deliberately added no second one — the **Find an owner** control on the
property page ATTACHES when asked and never refuses, blocks or gates a save.

### Three figures in the CR's own *done when* sentences do not exist here

The coordinator flagged this mid-wave and it is recorded so the next lane does
not chase them: **there is no *Creekside Holdings LP*, no `A-10442`, and no
*Route 12***. `brazosbend`'s owners are *Creekside Laundromat*, *Mill Pond
Apartments LP*, *Quarry Hill Diner*, *Ridge Property LLC* and *Silver Creek
Duplex Holdings*; its accounts are `AC-2026-#####`; its routes are `RT-001`..
`RT-006` on cycles `CY-001`..`CY-005`. **And 0 of those 5 owner records had any
master account at all**, so `B2`'s *"master account A-10442 as a link"* could
not be walked until one was linked through the product's own endpoint. The
shape of each sentence was honoured at an address that carries the data, and
every row of the wave's status table now names the address it was walked at.

### `DEF-MET-4719` WAS FOUND TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, THE SAME HOUR

Wave E hit it on the unit series; this lane hit it on the premises series. Both
drafts reasoned identically and identically wrongly: *`DEF-577` proved
`number_series.next_number` can stand behind the table, so catch it up*. **It
does not follow.** `_allocate_unused_number` catches up **only on a
collision** — it allocates, asks whether that exact value is in the column, and
moves the counter only when the answer is yes. On a tenant whose rows are
numbered in some other format the counter is behind AND the number it renders
to is free, so the allocator uses it. Measured through the shipped endpoint on
`brazosbend`: the preview said `U-00421` and the very next create issued
`U-00003`.

**The lesson is not about numbering.** Two careful lanes read the same defect
note and drew the same wrong conclusion from it, because the note describes the
PROBLEM (`DEF-577`: the counter stands behind) and the fix is a different shape
from the problem. `preview_premise_number` therefore follows wave E's loop
rather than being a second idea about one question, and says in its own
docstring that it is deliberately not independent.

**And the first test written for it PASSED against the bug.** Sabotaging the
preview back to the broken shape left all eight cases green, because none of
them built the one state where the two arithmetics differ. It now puts
`P-00050` on file with the counter at `1`, which is the only discriminating
case, and goes red against the shipped shape. *"Ask what would make this check
pass wrongly"* is what found that, and it is worth more here than the fix.

### `DEF-MET-4715` — a payload key that was accepted and dropped

`route` sat on `_validate_premises`' tolerated-key list beside `units`, `unit`
and `auto_create_unit`, **with no consumer anywhere**. Every other unknown key
on that payload is refused by name with `metering.unknown_field`; this one was
exempted from the check and nothing asked whether the exemption had a reader.
`POST /premises {"route": "COMPLETE NONSENSE, NOT A ROUTE"}` answered **201**,
allocated `P-00081`, and returned `routes_joined: []`.

That is hard-won law 2 — *built is not wired* — on a **server payload** rather
than a React prop, and `G13` cannot see it: it reads component props. **A
tolerated key with no reader is the server's version of a dead prop, and this
repo has no check for it.**

### A mixed working tree manufactures failures that belong to nobody

Two metering cases went red that this lane had not touched — the Units-tab
money case and a move warning. Neither was real. After the first push the
worktree held the tip **only for the files being pushed** and the old base for
everything else, so the suite was measuring a MIXTURE of two commits. Syncing
the whole tree to the tip took 48 files to green.

This is `DEF-2474`'s state seen from the other end: that defect is about what a
stale tree **publishes**, and this is about what it **reports**. Both come from
the same fact — `commit-tree` updates no file on disk — so the sync is not
optional tidiness after a push, it is what makes the next test run mean
anything.

### `B8`: the six headings are declared once, not agreed twice

Create and edit did not match, and not by a little: the create form asked for
the parcel and the two coordinates FOURTH, the edit form LAST, and **neither
had a section heading of any kind**. The order now lives in
`premisesFormSections.tsx` as an exported array both forms map, because a
comment asking two files to stay in step is a comment and an array both render
is the thing itself. Neither file is Route-B migrated, so the heading is an
unclassed `<h4>` — which adds no class to any stylesheet, and is what B14 rule
21 is actually asking for. `G31` passes at 0 undeclared classes.

### What is owed, stated rather than left to be discovered

* **`B6`'s *— bills on the 12th* is NOT built.** `premises_routes` serves
  `cycle_code` and `cycle_name`; it serves no due day, because none of
  `Cycle`'s columns is one this lane could name with confidence. The route and
  the cycle both render; the date does not.
* **The route is read-only on the edit form.** Changing one after creation is
  `BR-MET-074`'s MOVE, which CR-006 requires be confirmed on screen — *"a move
  triggered by a form field on a different screen is a move nobody agreed to"*.
  The section says so on screen rather than leaving an unexplained absence.
* **`Download error report` still renders on every wizard's failure card wired
  to a no-op.** It is `StateFrame.tsx`, shared by every flow in the product, so
  removing it is a change to eighteen screens and not to this one.
  `DEF-MET-4679` names it and is closed here for the half this wave owns — the
  refusal now lands on the field — with the dead button left named.

## 2026-09-09 · CR-089 WAVE F — THE UNIT'S PAGE (`2.234.14`)

Six tasks, `F1` to `F6`, on the six tabs of a unit. Everything below was walked
in Chromium on `brazosbend` before it was written down;
`10-scripts/cr089_wave_f_unit_page_walkthrough.mjs` is the walk and it reports
**43 checks, 0 failures**.

**Which addresses, and why each — because §6's correction block asks for it.**
The worked figures in the task table name `A-10517` (which exists on no tenant)
and `412 Cypress Row` (real, and carrying no accounts at all). Three real rows
carry the data instead:

| Address | Unit | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| `1408 Elm Street` | `SCW-U-201` | occupied, account `A-10432`, **autopay on** and a **$150.00 deposit taken 02/05/2024** — every fact `F2` names, on one screen |
| `301 Mill Pond Ln` | `SCW-U-042` | a tenancy that **CLOSED on 31 Jul 2026**, so `F4`'s vacancy is derived from rows a person put there |
| `Kestrel Park ph. 2` | `SCW-U-307` | one **planned** work order, so `F3`'s fourth tile has a non-zero figure |

---

### 1 · THE COST OF THE TILES, MEASURED — because §5 asked for it by name

`CR-089` §5 flags `F3` as *"the one ruling in this CR whose cost grows with
tenant size"*, so it was designed rather than discovered. **The answer is that
the tiles cost nothing per tab change and one extra query per page load.**

Counted in the browser, every `/api/**` request the page issues:

| What | Requests |
|---|---|
| first load of a unit page | **7** (`me`, `shell/display`, `in-app-messages`, `me/permissions`, `units/{id}`, `plans/{id}`, `units/{id}/account`) |
| tab change → Assets | 1 — the assets tab's own registry read |
| tab change → Plan | 1 — the pricing panel's own read |
| tab change → **Account** | **0** |
| tab change → Occupancy | 1 — the accounts-by-unit read |
| tab change → Audit log | 1 — the entity's own audit read |

**Not one of those is a tile.** All three new figures — `assets`, `owed`,
`open_work` — ride `GET /units/{id}`, the request the page already makes, so the
strip re-renders on a tab change and fetches nothing. What they cost is **three
extra queries on that one endpoint**: one ledger read through
`customers.owed_for_units`, one count through the work seam, and a split of the
asset list the payload was already carrying.

**And nothing else in the product pays them.** They are served by
`selectors.unit_page_dict`, a new function, and NOT by `unit_list_dict` — which
is what `update_unit` and `create_unit` write into `audit_log` as
`before`/`after`, what `customers.seams` hands the move-in and move-out flows,
and what `unit_list_rows` calls once per row of a 133-row page. Three figures
added there would have put a ledger read and a work-order count into an audit
write and into every row of the busiest list on this screen — `DEF-2723`'s
shape, which was six per-row reads and a 562 ms accounts list nobody had
measured. `test_the_units_list_row_is_untouched_by_the_tile_figures` is what
stops a later lane moving them for tidiness.

**The `Account` tab costing ZERO is `F2`'s doing and it is worth naming.** The
Overview's account block reads `GET /units/{id}/account` under
`unitAccountQueryKey` — **the key wave I's Account tab already uses** — so the
two surfaces are observers of one cache and cannot describe an account two ways.
The alternative was assembling the same seven facts from
`GET /accounts?f.unit_id=`, which is what the tab itself did before
`DEF-CUS-4691` and which can see neither a deposit nor an autopay reading,
because those are not columns on a list row.

---

### 2 · TWO DEPARTURES FROM `§6`'s WORKED LINES, EACH WITH ITS REASON

**(a) `F4`'s *"28 May to 1 Jun 2026 · 4 days"* is one day long, and the row
draws three.** `apps/customers/services` bills a leaver **through**
`moved_out_on` (`"bill_through": moved_out_on.isoformat()`) and writes that same
date to `closed_at`. So a tenancy closing on the 28th **occupied** the 28th, the
unit is empty on the 29th, 30th and 31st, and the next tenant holds the 1st.
The CR's figure is the difference between the two TENANCY dates; the row draws
the vacancy's own dates and its own length, which is the number a landlord asked
for. On the real data walked: `08/01/2026 · Current · 40 days`.

**(b) `F2`'s *"due 24 Sep"* is a STATED ABSENCE and no date is drawn.**
`BR-CUS-033` makes the due date the **oldest still-open** bill's, and *which
bill is still open* is a payments position nothing publishes —
`ledger.reporting.ar_positions` sums the AR account per customer and says
nothing per invoice. `AccountDetailPage`'s header already states exactly that
absence, and the Overview reuses **that key**
(`customers.account.awaits.dueDate`) rather than wording a second sentence about
one gap. `B14` rule 34's *one pair of words per concept* applies to an absence
as much as to a fact, and `CR-043` finding 11 is what an unlabelled *"Not known
yet"* under a figure costs: the PO read it as being about the balance.

---

### 3 · `F5` WAS ALREADY DONE, AND THE BRIEFING'S EVIDENCE WAS STALE

The task was written from a walk that found *"Nothing has been recorded against
this record in the window the log covers"* on a unit's Audit tab. **Nothing was
built for it, because the unit page mounts the SAME `AuditTab` component wave C
fixed on the property (`C6`)** — so the inline old→new values and the removal of
the expand controls arrived on this screen the moment that landed.

Measured on `brazosbend` on 2026-09-09: **every one of its 131 units carries
audit rows**, so the empty state the briefing quotes is not reachable there at
all. Walked: *09/08/2026 13:27 · Dana Whitfield · **Plan assigned to a unit** ·
Plan name **Not set → Sample — Residential***, with **zero** expand controls in
the table.

**The lesson is the briefing's own warning taken seriously** — *"a crawler that
presses nothing cannot tell a refusal from a form waiting for input"*, and the
same is true of a screen whose data has moved since it was looked at. The check
now lives in the walkthrough, so if the shared component regresses this screen
says so by name.

---

### 4 · WHERE THE PLAN GOES, AND THE SILENT DROP THAT WAS ALREADY THERE

`F6` asked for one form carrying the label, the floor, the floor area **and**
the plan. The obvious build is two calls on Save — `PATCH /units/{id}` for the
fields and `POST /units/{id}/plan` for the plan — and it is wrong for a reason
that only shows on the bad day: when the second is refused (an unpublished plan,
a locked unit) the clerk is left with a **renamed** unit, an error about a plan,
and no way to tell which half landed.

So the plan rides the PATCH as a nested `plan` block, applied **inside the same
transaction** by the same `services._apply_unit_plan` the create and the plan
modal call. `BR-MET-040`'s lock guard, `BR-RAT-030`'s unpublished refusal,
`BR-MET-042`'s occupied-unit warning and `BR-CUS-013`'s history row are that
function's and are not restated.

⚠ **AND `plan` WAS ALREADY ACCEPTED ON THAT ENDPOINT AND SILENTLY DROPPED.**
`_validate_unit`'s `ignored` set has carried `"plan"` since S16 so the CREATE
payload could be handed to it whole; on a PATCH nothing then read it. **A PATCH
carrying a plan answered `200`, changed the label, left the plan exactly where
it was and said nothing about it** — `DEF-836`'s silent-drop shape, on the field
that decides what a unit is billed. A form built on that endpoint would have
looked like it worked, on every screen, for every clerk, forever.

**`source="change_plan"` and not a sixth word.**
`rating.models.UnitPlanAssignment.source` documents its own vocabulary in the
column — `new_connection|move_in|change_plan|bulk_update|import` — and a plan
changed from the unit's edit form IS a change of plan. Minting `unit_edit` would
put a word nobody ruled into a signed history table.

---

### 5 · WHAT THE BROWSER FOUND THAT NO TEST COULD — `DEF-MET-4732`

**The edit form drew a BLANK plan picker on a unit that has a plan.**
`SearchSelectField` seeds the text it DISPLAYS exactly once, with
`useState(selected?.label ?? "")`, and the plan options arrive from a second
request that has not landed on first render. The `value` was correct throughout
— so every assertion about what the form holds, what it posts and what the
server stores passes — and the control a clerk can see said **nothing**, which
on that field reads as *no plan* on a unit that is on one.

**This is `DEF-442`'s mechanism for the third time** (*"two controls, one fact,
and the one a clerk can see says the opposite"*), and wave E hit it four hours
earlier on the add-units wizard's premises picker. The remedy is the same one:
re-key the control on whether the options have arrived, which remounts it
exactly once, on the 0 → N transition, before anybody has typed.

**Found by reopening the form after a save and reading the screen.** Nothing
else in this repository could have.

---

### 5b · IT CLOSED THREE DEFECTS SOMEBODY ELSE HAD FILED HOURS EARLIER

Wave H was reading the same screen and filed what it could not reach, because
the KPI strip was this wave's file region and was being rewritten as wave H
landed. All three are closed here:

* **`DEF-MET-4729` — *"the unit page calls the same things METERS in a tile and
  Assets in the tab beside it"*.** Half of it was already untrue: `unit.meters`

* **`DEF-MET-4725` — *"the `ON PLAN SINCE` tile keeps the tenant's numeric

  replaced that tile, so there is no second date shape left to reformat.

⚠ **AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE WORTH READING, BECAUSE IT IS HARD-WON LAW 2's
MIRROR WORKING END TO END — WHICH THIS REPOSITORY HAS NOT RECORDED BEFORE.**
Wave H could not touch that tile, so instead of an allowance nobody ever removes
it wrote **a second check that goes RED the day the hold expires**, naming what
to delete:

> `EXPIRY · the KPI tile is still the ONE numeric date (DEF-MET-4725) — when
> this fails wave F has fixed it and this exception must be DELETED`

Wave F expired the hold; the check fired on its own; and **the lane that expired

`cr089_wave_h_plan_tab_walkthrough.mjs`. The whole-page date claim there is

still refusing over screens shipped days earlier — is what the alternative looks

### 6 · WHAT WAS NOT BUILT, AND WHY

* **The PROPERTY's four tiles are still `Units · Occupied · Meters · Master
  account`** where `F3` names `Units · Assets · Owed here · Open work orders`.
  `PremisesDetailPage.tsx` is wave C's file and this wave may not restructure
  it. Filed as `DEF-MET-4733` with the fix written out, rather than left to be
  rediscovered. ⚠ Note the property's `Meters` tile ALREADY counts every asset
  (`metering.premises.kpi.metersDetail` reads *"Assets on this property"*), so
  the number is right and the word is wrong — the same thing that was true of
  the unit's tile before this wave.
* **The units list keeps its own private copy of the edit form**
  (`DEF-MET-4731`). `UnitsListPage.tsx` is wave E's. `UnitEditModal` is exported
  so that list can drop its copy in one line.
* **No LEADING vacancy row** — the stretch before a unit's first tenancy would
  have to start when the unit was created, and `UnitRow` carries no created-at.
  Inventing one from the first account's start date would draw a zero-day row on
  every unit in the product.
* **The `Open work` tile counts the unit's OWN anchor and not a job standing
  on one of its assets — a decision, not an oversight.**
  `orders_at_premises_queryset` already walks asset → service point → unit →
  premises for exactly that case, so the reach exists and is deliberately not
  taken here. A tile reading **3** over a list showing **2** is worse than a
  tile that is narrow and says so, and the wave that draws the unit's
  work-orders LIST is the one that can make a tile and a list count the same
  rows. ⚠ **The first draft cited an `OQ-MET-1520` it had not minted**, which
  `G106` refused by name — *"a citation is how a rule is looked up, so an id no
  register issued is a rule nobody can read"*. Law 13 is the answer rather than
  a new register row: the judgment is made and written down here.
* **The vacancy row's ACCOUNT cell is a dash, not the owner's number.** r10
  draws `MA-1408 · owner` there. `BR-CUS-170` does say the owner's master
  account carries the base charge and the Account tab NAMES it — but that
  account is resolved per unit, **today**, through
  `master_account_covering_unit`, and printing it against a date range that
  predates the coverage would assert that THIS account was billed for THAT
  stretch, which nothing recorded.
* **`OQ-316`'s remaining word is still open and the row does not answer it.**
  The absence NARROWED rather than went: half of it had rotted (who receives the
  bill is `BR-CUS-170`, built, and wave I already names the account), and what
  is still unruled is base-only versus full — with a running toilet through
  3 kgal that is **$8.00 against $20.00** on the owner's bill.

`UnitsPage.test.tsx` had two assertions naming `Showing what applies as of

**That is worth more than the defect was.** `push_paths.sh` refused this push
