## 2026-09-10 · PRM-02's THREE TABLE TABS GET THE TABLE THE BLUEPRINT NAMES (`DEF-4739` · `DEF-4740`, `2.234.16`)

**What was wrong, in one sentence.** The property's Units, Assets and Audit log
tabs each drew `PlainTable` — the small in-panel table for a few rows of figures
— where the blueprint names the shared `DataTable` with its `FilterBar`. So all
three had **no search box, no filter chips, no column chooser, no pagination
footer and no footer counts**, and nine drawn columns were missing although the
API already served every one of them. Two of those columns had a message key
sitting unread in all eleven catalogues, which is why a grep for them found them
and read as present.

**What was built.** All three tabs now draw `DataTable` + `FilterBar`, with the
drawn columns in the drawn order. **Units:** `Unit ID` and `Unit` become ONE
cell (label leading, number quiet beneath), `Floor` and `Occupant` arrive,
`Owed` moves before `Status`, the hint line goes (the frame says *"no prose"*).
**Assets:** `Service` and `Size` arrive, `Asset type` becomes `What it is`,
`Assigned to` becomes `Where` and says *the property itself* in words,
`Meter type` and `Read method` leave both families. **Audit:** `Actor` becomes
`Who`, and `What changed` / `From` / `To` become COLUMNS with no disclosure
anywhere in the table.

### THE FIGURE THAT MATTERS, AND IT IS NOT A COUNT OF COLUMNS

`None → Route 12`. On the audit tab an absent previous value rendered as
**nothing**, so a property that had never had a route and one whose route was
CHANGED read identically. The blueprint calls this out in its own words — *"an
absent previous value is drawn as an absence … which is a different fact from a
route being changed"* — and it is now three drawn forms rather than one:
`—` where the row is a creation and there was no previous value at all, the
value in the ABSENT style where the field previously held nothing, and the value
plainly where somebody had typed one. It is asserted as MARKUP and not as a
word, because *rendered as nothing* is exactly what a `toContain` cannot see.

### FIVE JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT

1. **A vacant unit's `Owed` still refuses to print `0.00`, and the PO ruled
   both halves in one sentence.** The blueprint draws `0.00` on the vacant row;
   the ruling of 2026-09-10 moves the vacancy SENTENCE to `Occupant` and keeps
   the protection — *"show 0.00 only when the balance really is zero, never
   manufactured over a real debt"*. `owed_for_units` resolves the OCCUPYING
   account, so an unlet unit produced no ledger read at all and a tenant who
   moved out **still owing 108.88** has a CLOSED account that map excludes.
   So a real zero prints `$0.00` and an unmeasured unit reads `Not measured`.
   `DEF-138` is the record of what the other answer costs.
2. **The Assets tab's two group heading rows are NOT built, and the three
   things they bought a clerk are.** `DataTable` has no group-row capability;
   growing the shared kit for one tab is a bigger act than this fix. The rows
   that BILL still LEAD, the two family names are the `+ Filter ▾` panel's
   options, and the two counts are the footer sentence. Recorded in the
   conformance file as OPEN rather than quietly dropped.
3. **The two standing chips become a declared filter — a ratified rule beating
   the frame.** `DEF-1700` removed permanent dimension chips from this product
   by PO ruling; re-drawing them here would re-open it.
4. **The row-action columns (`👁 ✎ …`) are not built on any of the three.** Each
   frame draws them and none says what `✎` or `…` commits — and the Assets and
   Audit specification tables both state the tab's primary action is *None*. A
   control invented to fill a drawn cell is dead UI (hard-won law 2).
5. **One row per EVENT on the audit tab, capped at three changed fields with
   `+N more`.** The frame draws four events that each moved one field, so *one
   row per event* and *one row per change* are indistinguishable in it. They are
   not the same on real data: `premises.created` records the whole
   `premises_detail_dict` — thirty-odd keys — and a cell stacking every one
   would set the height of its row. A creation therefore reads as the EVENT with
   `—` in `From`, which is what the frame's own `Property added` row draws.

### TWO THINGS KEPT BY PO RULING, AGAINST THE FRAME

The audit tab's `Open the audit log for this record →` link and its `Showing the
last 2 years` sentence. PO, verbatim: *"keep it as it is"*. The window is
bounded server-side (`BR-AUD-006`, `BR-AUD-013`) and an unstated absence reads
as *it never happened*, which is the one thing an audit log must never say. The
conformance file is amended to say so rather than the two being deleted.

### THE `Assets` TAB IS NOT RENAMED TO `Meters`

The blueprint proposes it twice and **reverses it on page 28 in writing**. The
product was already right and nothing moved.

### A GUARD THAT COULD NOT FAIL, FOUND BY PROVING IT RED FIRST

Law 7's *break it first* found that the whole-row render **cannot reach**
`AuditFromCell`'s `before === null` branch: the `From` column short-circuits a
creation to one dash before it gets there, so a fault planted in that branch
left the suite green. The branch stays — the cell is exported and a
create-snapshot field legitimately carries `before: null` — and its three forms
are now driven DIRECTLY, where a test can actually fail. Six breaks were planted
in all; five went red on the first run and this was the sixth.

### THE REDS THIS LANE DID NOT CAUSE, DATED

Six failures in `PremisesPage.test.tsx` and one in
`PremisesServicesNotRecorded.dom.test.tsx` were failing **at `f70a4954e`, the
tip this lane started from**, and `routeBUtilities.test.ts` reports the same two
orphan classes there (`rounded` in `UnitDetailPage.tsx`, `hover:bg-neutral-50`
in `portal/plans/PlanOffer.tsx`). Confirmed by running each file in a pristine
worktree at that sha rather than assumed — `DEF-CWP-4187` records two lanes
reporting *"a red I did not cause"* in good faith when one of them had caused
it. `ServiceTags` was also an eslint error in `PremisesDetailPage.tsx` at that
tip; it is removed with the two imports this change orphaned, so the file is at
zero rather than carrying one red line nobody owns.

### WHAT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED, STATED PLAINLY

There is no running stack in this container, so **nothing here was seen in a
browser**. The checks that were run prove PRESENCE, ORDER and the exact STRING
of every drawn label — three of the seven the UI skill's §4 comparison asks for.
**Alignment, spacing rhythm, weight and colour were not verified**, at 1280 or
at 1440 or at all, and the tabs were not clicked. That is the largest hole in
this record and it is what the next person with a browser should spend ten
minutes on.

Source: `04-docs/05-modules/04-metering/conformance/CR-089-p025-property-common-areas.md`

25–28 and 32–34, rendered and looked at rather than inferred from a task
sentence. This is the sibling half of the commit above: that one took Units,
Assets and Audit log; this one takes Common areas and Work orders.

### `Billed to` IS ANSWERABLE NOW, AND `DEF-560`'s REASONING EXPIRED ON 2026-09-01

The blueprint calls `Billed to` *"the only question this tab exists to answer"*
and the product drew no such column, on the authority of `DEF-560`: a master
account ANCHORED on the premises' first common area, `GET /accounts` filtered on
`accounts.unit_id`, and so the endpoint could say *is there a master here* and
could not say *does it cover THIS area*. Every clause of that was true when it
was written.

**`CR-056` W1 / `BR-CUS-1010` moved the master account onto the ADDRESS** — it
carries `premises_id` and names no unit at all — and `useMasterAccounts` has
asked by address since. The question the old note could not ask is the question
the endpoint now answers, and the column was never re-drawn. The file's own
header block still opened *"WHY THERE IS NO BILLED TO COLUMN"*; it is amended,
dated, with the supersession written out, rather than deleted.

**What survives of `DEF-560` is real and is stated on screen rather than
guessed.** `POST /accounts/master` still accepts `unit_ids` to narrow coverage,
so a premises carrying MORE THAN ONE master cannot say which of them pays for a
given area. That case renders three words — *Several owner accounts* — with the
sentence on the tooltip, and never names one of them. One master at an address,
which is the ordinary case and the one the blueprint draws, names it on every
row.

### THE DRAWN `OPEN` CHIP BEATS `US-WRK-004`'s COMMITMENT SENTENCE, AND NOTHING IS HIDDEN

`US-WRK-004` says *"every job here, finished ones included, newest first"* and
the blueprint draws the chip `OPEN` as the tab's default filter with a footer
counting *2 open · 7 done*. Under the PO's 2026-09-10 ruling the drawn frame
wins. **The list still HOLDS every job**: what changed is that a filter arrives
applied, it is visible as a chip, and one press of `All` clears it. The
commitment sentence moved into the tab's closed disclosure, where it is now more
useful than it was above the table.

⚠ **AND A DEFAULTED FILTER WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE DRAWN EMPTY STATE, WHICH IS
THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE BLUEPRINT ASKS.** `DataTable` draws a screen's own
empty state only when nothing is searched and nothing is filtered; otherwise it
draws *no results, clear filters*. So on a building nobody has ever raised work
on, the drawn chip would have replaced *"an empty list here is good news and
should read like it"* with a dead end. The tab therefore passes an unfiltered
state to the table when there is genuinely nothing to filter — the chip row goes
back to `All` and the empty state is its own. **Found by a test, not by
reasoning: `TC-2` went red on it.**

### FOUR COLUMNS COME OFF THE DEFAULT SET AND NONE IS DELETED

`Service`, `Mode` and `Outcome` are drawn nowhere on the property's Work orders
tab, and `Stands on` is not among the drawn seven either. All four stay declared
with `defaultVisible: false`, so the column chooser the shared table brings
still offers them — deleting them would be a capability cut `CR-089` did not
ask for, and it is the same reasoning `UnitsListPage` already records for its
own `label` and `occupancy` columns.

**`Stands on` is default-ON for the ACCOUNT host and off for the property.**
`US-WRK-004`'s reason is specific to that host: a person on an account sees the
move-out's final read (on the account), the meter exchange (on the asset) and
the build's install jobs (on the build) in one list, and a list that did not say
which is which would be claiming they are the same kind of thing. The property's
list has one anchor and the blueprint draws seven columns without it.

### `What it is` IS THE TYPE IN WORDS, AND THE BLUEPRINT'S VOCABULARY DOES NOT EXIST

The blueprint asks for *"shared room, shared lighting, car park — rather than a
type code"*. The only column that can answer is `units.unit_type`, whose
vocabulary is `BR-MET-084`'s five seeded types, so the cell reads **Common
area** on a seeded row and a dash on a row this tab's own modal created — that
modal captures a name and the flag and nothing else. The column is drawn from
the type through the catalogue every other screen reads it through, so a tenant
renaming a type renames it here; the gap is `DEF-MET-4750` and is **not filled
with a guess**, because minting *shared room* and *car park* as unit types is
new vocabulary and needs the PO.

### THE MASTER-ACCOUNT FACT BLOCK IS DELETED, AND THE CREATE CONTROL IS NOT

`p025` §12 draws the fact block, the payer row and the coverage row as ABSENT —
the payer belongs on every ROW, which is what `Billed to` now does. The
**Create master account** button is not in that list and stays, secondary, with
the drawn `+ Add a common area` as the tab's primary. It is **absent while
there are no common areas**, which is not the `BR-SHL-025` posture and is
deliberate: `create_master_account` refuses `no_common_area_units` outright, so
a control there could only ever be pressed and refused. That behaviour and its
test predate this change and are kept.

### `+ Add a common area` GAINS ITS `+`

B14's button grammar is `+ Noun` opens a creator, the blueprint draws
`+ Add a common area`, and the stored string carried no `+`. The drawing and the
system agreed and the product was on its own, so the string moves in all eleven
catalogues.

### `DEF-4742`: TEN KEYS IN ZERO CATALOGUES, AND THE THIRTEEN NOBODY HAD COUNTED

Each was written `t(key, { defaultValue: "English" })`, so nothing was ever
missing at runtime, no warning fired, and the parity gate — which compares the
ten catalogues against `en.json` — had nothing to compare, because a key in NONE
of the eleven is absent from `en.json` too. Every tenant read English on those
strings, permanently.

All ten are in all eleven now, **written in each language rather than translated
from English** (B14 rule 35), and thirteen more in the same two files had the
same fault and are fixed with them — 61 keys in total. **Every static
`defaultValue` in the three files is deleted**, so a future absence prints the
key instead of quietly printing English. The only fallbacks left are on DYNAMIC
keys, where the fallback is the deliberate last resort for a value the catalogue
has never heard of.

**The durable half is a test and not a gate** (PO 2026-09-10: a new gate is the
last resort and needs their agreement).
`07-frontend/src/features/metering/def4742EnglishOnlyKeys.test.ts` asks the
question at the RAISE SITE instead of at the catalogue: for every literal key in
the three files it guards, is it in all eleven? It was run RED against
`67da0e4f2` first — **34 English-only call sites and 374 catalogue gaps** in
those three files — and is green at 0 and 0.

⚠ **AND IT PRINTS THE SIZE OF ITS OWN BLIND SPOT, WHICH IS THE FINDING THAT
MATTERS MOST HERE.** Hard-won law 7: *a declared blind spot with no NUMBER
attached is indistinguishable from an empty one.* Measured on 2026-09-10:
**555 English-only `t()` call sites across 30 other front-end files** —
`DEF-SHL-4756`. A ratchet on that figure was considered and rejected, in
writing, in the test itself: three lanes are adding `t()` calls to this tree
right now and it would go red on work whose owner would have no idea why.

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND HOW

Every amended and new case was run RED first, in the harness that runs it, in a
pristine worktree at `67da0e4f2` — four columns, no search box, no chip, no
`⚡ Raise work here` — and quoted before being run green. The DOM test exists
because the static one **cannot** answer the question the drawn chip raises: a
`renderToStaticMarkup` render can only ever show the arrival state, so *does
`All` bring the finished job back* is asserted by a click or not at all.

### THE REDS THIS LANE DID NOT CAUSE, DATED

Six in `PremisesPage.test.tsx`, three in `JurisdictionField.dom.test.tsx`, three
in `PremisesServices.dom.test.tsx` and one in
`PremisesServicesNotRecorded.dom.test.tsx`. **All thirteen fail identically at
`f70a4954e`, the tip this lane started from**, confirmed by running each file in
a pristine worktree at that sha rather than assumed — `DEF-CWP-4187` records two
lanes reporting *"a red I did not cause"* in good faith when one of them had
caused it. The seven services and jurisdiction ones are a sibling's, filed by
them as `DEF-MET-4749`; the six in `PremisesPage.test.tsx` are the
`PremisesDetailPage` redesign's.

### WHAT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED, STATED PLAINLY

There is no running stack in this container, so **nothing here was seen in a
browser**. Presence, ORDER and the exact STRING of every drawn label are proved,
and on the Common areas tab the CELL CONTENTS of the first row are proved too —
that is four of the seven comparisons the UI skill's §4 asks for. **Alignment,
spacing rhythm, weight and colour were not verified**, at 1280 or 1440 or at
all. `CR-089` task `C6` records that **no work order exists on any sample
property**, and that still holds: the Work orders tab has never rendered a row
in a browser, so everything asserted about it is asserted against fixtures.

## 2026-09-10 — FOUR RULINGS ON THE UNITS CONFORMANCE PASS, AND TWO OF THEM ARE RULES

Twelve unit screens were read against `05-prototype/Premises & Units Blueprint 2.pdf`
and produced about 145 named differences. Four of them could not be settled from the
repo and went to the PO in one table; all four came back in one message. **Two are
answers about units. Two are general rules and are now `B14` 37 and 38.**

### 1 · A UNIT HAS NO SERVICES OF ITS OWN, AND INHERITANCE IS LIVE

**PO, verbatim:** *"Can a clerk add or remove services on a single unit? The drawing
shows removable service chips per unit. - no they will do it on Premises - if it is
change on premises all units will inherit it."*

The blueprint's `Edit a unit` frame draws removable per-unit service chips with the
sentence *"Removing one is refused while a meter for it is attached"* — which presumes
a unit-level list a clerk can subtract from. That collides with the ruling of
2026-08-26, taken after `CR-037` was withdrawn and recorded on `DEF-755`: **no
unit-level column, no override.**

**The ruling UPHOLDS 2026-08-26 and adds the half that was never written down.** The
old ruling said where the column is not; this one says how a unit gets its answer:
**by reading through to the building, LIVE.** A change on the premises is inherited by
every unit under it, at read time — not copied at creation, not synced by a job.

**What this decides in code:** the unit edit form gets NO services control. It shows
the building's services **read-only** with one sentence saying where they come from
(`B14` rule 32 — an absence is stated, not left blank). ⚠ **And the inheritance claim
is now a promise on screen, so it has to be true in the code rather than assumed** —
a screen that promises inheritance over a stored copy is hard-won law 1 exactly. The
lane building it was told to prove the read-through before writing the sentence, and
to file a defect if anything copies.

**The drawing is amended, not followed.**

### 2 · THE UNITS LIST IS HEADED `Units`, WHICH REVERSES A SIGNED RULE

**PO, verbatim:** *"Should the units list say Units or Premises at the top? The drawing
says Units with its own subtitle. - t should say Unit"*.

**THIS SUPERSEDES `CR-023` P0 / `B15` §3** — *"h1 reads Premises on all three tabs,
from r10 line 630"* — cited in `PremisesTabsPage.tsx` at lines 22 and 121. That was
signed, and it is now overturned rather than missed; the citing comments say so in
place instead of being deleted.

⚠ **THE READING CHOSEN, RECORDED BECAUSE THE RULING AND THE DRAWING DIFFER BY ONE
LETTER.** The PO wrote the singular; the frame draws the plural `Units` with the
subtitle *"Every unit that can take service, across every property."* **The plural is
built**, on the grounds that a list of many is titled in the plural everywhere else in
this product and that a heading is not a row label — and the substance of the ruling is
that the heading follows the TAB rather than staying on one word for all three, which
is the same either way. If that reading is wrong it is a one-word fix and this
paragraph is where to look.

**So the `h1` follows the active tab.** The Units tab reads the drawn heading and the
drawn subtitle; the other tabs keep theirs. The guard asserts all three by tab, because
a test covering only the tab that changed is how the other two drift.

### 3 · `B14` RULE 38 — THE UI RULES GOVERN HOW A FORM IS BUILT

**PO, verbatim,** asked whether the shared dialog should change to match six things the
blueprint draws (two fields side by side, help under its input, `Cancel` on the left, an
identity line under the title, a different kicker, a labelled close instead of `✕`):
*"if youa re doing a form - go as per our UI rules"*.

**Ratified as `B14` rule 38.** It carries rule 36's split one step on: the captured packs
give layout and detail, `r10` gives visual style, and **form CONSTRUCTION belongs to
`B14` and the kit.** The drawing loses, the divergence is recorded, nothing is built.
What the form CONTAINS — which fields, in what order, under which headings, saying
what — is still the drawing's, and the *frame wins* ruling of the same day still governs
there.

**Why it is a rule and not a case:** each of those six changes EVERY dialog in the
product at once, on one screen's authority, with no lane owning the blast radius. Rule
36 already says what to do when the kit genuinely lacks a piece — add it to the kit, as
an opt-in, so nothing existing moves.

### 4 · `B14` RULE 37 — A DRAWN FIGURE IS AN ILLUSTRATION

**PO, verbatim:** *"Treat every number drawn in a wireframe as an illustration, never a
fact to build to."*

**Ratified as `B14` rule 37**, and it settles a class the *frame wins* ruling cannot
touch. That ruling decides frame-versus-sentence. **These are frame-versus-frame:** one
blueprint draws a tenancy as one account and date on page 80 and a different account and
year on page 84, and draws a four-day vacancy as a row on the Account frame while the
Occupancy frame omits the row and counts it in its own footer. Read as facts they are
irreconcilable; read as illustrations they are not in conflict at all.

**Build the shape both frames agree on and ignore both sets of figures.** No test
asserts a drawn number; no fixture is seeded from one.

### WHAT WAS DONE WITH THEM, THE SAME TURN

All four reached the four running fix lanes before this entry was written — two of them
REVERSE instructions those lanes were given twenty minutes earlier, and a lane building
against a superseded instruction is the cost hard-won law 9 exists to prevent. `B14`
gained rules 37 and 38, and **`CLAUDE.md`'s rule count moved 36 → 38 in the same
commit** — the first time that pointer has been moved with the rule rather than five
commits later, which is the failure that line has recorded about itself five times.

## 2026-09-10 — THE THREE UNIT TABS ARE CUT ONTO THEIR DRAWN FRAMES, AND FOUR JUDGEMENTS WERE MADE ALONG THE WAY

`DEF-MET-4764` · `DEF-MET-4765` · `DEF-MET-4766` · maintenance track
(`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`), because a user can do all
three of these tasks in the product today.

The Account, Occupancy and Audit tabs of `S15 · PRM-03` were diffed against the
`CR-089` conformance files and rebuilt to them. Most of it needed no judgement —
a drawn row was missing and the value was on the payload. **Four places the
rules ran out, recorded here with what was chosen and why.**

### 1 · A REQUIRED PROP ON A SHARED COMPONENT MANUFACTURED A DEAD CONTROL

`EmptyList` declared `ctaLabel` and `onCta` REQUIRED. A record's audit history is
a list **nobody can fill** — a clerk cannot create an audit row — so the tab had
nothing honest to offer and passed `onCta: () => undefined` to satisfy the type.
`EmptyList` wired that to a live `<Button>`, so an empty audit tab drew *Open the
audit log for this record →* twice: once dead, once working.

**Chosen: make the pair OPTIONAL, additively.** The alternative was to give the
dead button a real handler, which leaves two identical buttons — B14 rule 4's
*"two + Add part buttons"* shape, which `EmptyList`'s own docstring already
records. A block with no label now draws no button.

**Why this counts as a kit change we were allowed to make:** it is the third
time this component has grown an optional prop for exactly this reason
(`ctaVariant`, `secondaryCtaLabel`), each one leaving all 27 call sites
byte-for-byte unchanged. B14 rule 38 forbids RESHAPING the kit to match a
drawing; this adds an opt-in, which is what rule 36 says to do when the kit
lacks a piece.

### 2 · THE OCCUPANCY STATUS COLUMN NOW SAYS THE TENANCY'S STATE, NOT THE ACCOUNT'S

The column printed `AccountRow.status_name` — the tenant's own renameable label
for the ACCOUNT (`Active`, `Pending activation`). The frame draws `CURRENT` ·
`CLOSED` · `VACANT PERIOD`, which are words about the TENANCY.

**Chosen: the frame's words, in a `StatusPill`.** This tab is a history of who
held the unit and when; every other cell on the row is about a stretch of time,
and an account-status word in the sixth column answers a question nobody asked
there. `BR-CUS-055`'s *always show the tenant's own label* still governs the
ACCOUNT's status, which is one click away on the Account tab and now draws it as
a pill too.

**It is a vocabulary change on a live screen and is recorded as one** rather
than left as a silent consequence of following a drawing.

### 3 · AN EXPLAINED ABSENCE WHOSE EXPLANATION EXPIRED

The Occupancy tab carried a paragraph explaining why r10's `Closing read` and
`Final bill` columns are missing (`DEF-509`). Correct while r10 was the drawing.
The blueprint has since **ratified a six-column table containing neither**, so
their absence is no longer something a clerk is owed a paragraph about — and
that frame's own budget is *"six columns, no prose"*.

**Chosen: the prose goes, the defect stays open.** `DEF-509` is a real gap —
nothing serves a closing read per unit — and closing it because the drawing
stopped asking would convert a live gap into an invisible one. The two catalogue
keys were retired with the sentence they worded.

**The general shape, worth more than the case:** an absence explained on screen
has TWO expiry conditions and only one of them is obvious. It expires when the
thing arrives, and it also expires when the DRAWING STOPS ASKING FOR IT. The
second leaves a true sentence on screen answering a question nobody is asking.

### 4 · THE READ LANE SAID `Last payment` WAS ON THE PAYLOAD. IT IS NOT.

The U7 diff lists `Last payment` among rows that are *"already on the payload or
already derived in the same file"*. **There is no `last_payment` on `AccountRow`
or on `UnitAccountFacts` anywhere in this product.** Serving it means a new read
in `apps/customers/seams.py` into `apps.payments` — the pattern exists, and
`apps/portal/seams/payments_seam.last_payment` does exactly this for the
customer portal.

**Chosen: NOT BUILT, and the reason is hard-won law 7 rather than scope.** This
container has no Django and no pytest, so a backend test for a new seam could
not be proved RED through the harness that would actually run it. A guard proved
through a path nobody uses is no proof of the thing that matters
(`DEF-GOV-3733`). It is recorded in the U7 conformance file with the shape the
read needs, for whichever lane has a stack.

### AND ONE THING THE FRAME ASKED FOR THAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DELETED

The U7 frame draws no bad-address row. `facts.reach.bad_address` is a live flag a
clerk acts on before posting a bill, and the row that carried it went when the
third group was folded into one `Reach them by` row as drawn. **It rides the
`Post` row instead** — it is a fact about that address. Deleting a working signal
because a drawing omits it is a loss the drawing did not ask for, which is hard
rule 8's own lesson (`DEF-CUS-3653`) running in the other direction.

## 2026-09-10 · THE THREE UNIT DIALOGS — TWO SECOND DOORS, AND SIX JUDGMENTS THE RULES RAN OUT ON

**Lane:** the `U10` / `U11` / `U12` conformance pass (`DEF-MET-4761`, `DEF-MET-4762`,
`DEF-MET-4763`, and `DEF-MET-4731` closed). **Nothing here was put to the PO** — hard-won
law 13: a judgment recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable, a question is the
failure to make one. Each of the six is written into its conformance file beside the
frame it departs from.

### 1 · THE UNIT'S SECOND DOOR IS THE PROPERTY'S, SO THE PROPERTY'S RULING APPLIES

The units list drew a `Deactivate` row action posting `POST /units/{id}/deactivate` with
**no date, no reason and no dependency list**, beside a dialog that demands all three.
That is `DEF-4743` exactly, one level down, and the PO ruled `DEF-4743` on 2026-09-10 —
**option (b): keep the shortcut, point it at the real dialog.** It was applied rather
than re-asked.

**The worked figure, because it is what makes the defect real:** both doors always
refused on `BR-MET-1164` off one computation, so **nothing unsafe ever got through
either**. What differed is what was WRITTEN DOWN. `change_unit_status` puts the effective
date and the reason into `audit_log`; `deactivate_unit` wrote `{"active": False}` and
nothing else. Those two facts live in `audit_log` and in **NO column**, so a clerk who
took a flat out of service from the list left no recoverable record of when it took
effect or why — and **no check in this repository reads what an audit row CONTAINS**,
which is why 119 passing unit-list cases could not see it.

**Two behaviour changes at the API, stated rather than discovered:** the payload is now
required (a bare call is a field error, not a silent success), and the call is no longer
idempotent (deactivating something already inactive is refused by name). Both are what
`deactivate_premises` did on the same ruling.

### 2 · THE `New status` FIELD OFFERS EXACTLY ONE OPTION

The `U12` and `P11` frames draw `New status *` as a select. A live place can only go
inactive and an inactive one can only come back — the server computes which in
`status_change_dict.target_status` and refuses the other by name. **So the select carries
one option and no second choice**, because a control whose alternative can only fail is
worse than no control. What it earns its place with is the SENTENCE: *Inactive — no
longer takes service* is the one place on the dialog that says, in words rather than by
inference from a button, what state the record ends in.

### 3 · THE ZERO ROWS GO, AND `DEF-127`'s POSTURE MOVES WITH THEM

`visibleDependencies` drew a zero for every count the rule names, so that *"no open
accounts"* could not be mistaken for *"nobody looked"*. The frames draw the panel as
`NOT WHILE THIS IS LIVE` — **one row per blocker** — and draw it **only in the blocked
state**, where a nought is a line saying nothing is wrong inside a panel whose heading
says something is. The reassurance is not lost, it changes form: the clear state draws
the consequence instead, which states in words what happens to the meters and the
billing.

### 4 · THE `U12` TITLE KEEPS THE UNIT'S NAME, AND THIS IS THE ONE PLACE TWO RULES COLLIDE

The frame draws the neutral title `Change status` with the unit identified on a
**sub-line**. `B14` rule 38 forbids adding a sub-line slot to `ModalShell`. Obeying both
would leave the dialog naming nothing at all, so **identity won**: the title still reads
`Take {{name}} out of service?`. Recorded because it is the only divergence on these
three screens where following the drawing and following the UI rules cannot both be done.

### 5 · `Floor` STAYS A TEXT FIELD THOUGH THE FRAME DRAWS A SELECT

`units.floor_label` is free text in the model and already holds `Ground`, `G`,
`Mezzanine`, `PH`. A closed list needs a vocabulary nobody has ratified, and shipping one
would make every existing value **unselectable on the form that edits it**. The
divergence is stamped; the vocabulary is a change, not a copy fix.

### 6 · TWO SENTENCES THE FRAMES DRAW ARE NOT BUILT, BECAUSE THEY WOULD BE FALSE

Hard-won law 1 — a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee — applies to screen
copy exactly as it does to a docstring:

* the `U10` plan help says *"only plans this unit's services can be billed on are
  offered"*. `getUnitPlanOptions` is called with `{per: 500}` and no unit, so it does
  **not** filter. The filtering is worth having and it is a change.
* the `U12` refusal helper says *"Close the account and remove the meters first"*.
  `BR-MET-1164` names ONE term for a unit and the meters do **not** block. It is also two
  sentences of 13 and 16 words, over `B14` rule 32's budget and over `G33`'s twelve-word
  cap. The four-word hold sentence stands in its place.

### AND ONE PROMISE THAT WAS VERIFIED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN

`BR-MET-118`'s own amendment says the inheritance sentence *"is now a promise, so it has
to be true rather than assumed"*. It was checked in the code before the sentence was
written: **`selectors.unit_detail_dict` reads `unit.premises.services_available` at READ
TIME**, `units` carries no services column in the model or in any migration, and
`_validate_unit` never writes one. **Inheritance is live. There is no stored copy.** The
unit edit form shows the building's list read-only with one sentence saying where it
comes from, and offers no control.

## 2026-09-10 · CR-089 `U1`/`U2`/`U3` — THE THREE UNITS SCREENS AGAINST THEIR FRAMES

Maintenance, not build (`22-product-maintenance-process.md`): all three screens
exist and beta users are on them. Six judgments were made where the rules ran
out, and each is here rather than only in the code.

### 1 · THE UNITS LIST OPENS `Unit · Address`, WHICH REVERSES A CHANGE SHIPPED THE DAY BEFORE

`CR-089` wave E read `E1`'s task sentence — *"the units list is scanned by
address"* — and shipped `Address` as column one on 2026-09-09. The blueprint's
frame (page 51) draws `Unit ⇅` first. `CR-089-p050`'s own preamble rules the
tie — *"Where the teal block or a commitment sentence disagrees with the frame,
the frame wins"* (PO 2026-09-10) — so the frame won and the pair swapped back.
**What wave E actually fixed is untouched:** the series number no longer LEADS
either column. Recorded because reversing a shipped, PO-visible change on the
authority of a preamble is the kind of thing the next reader is owed.

### 2 · `Owed` ON A VACANT UNIT IS `Not measured`, DERIVED AND NOT DECIDED

The frame draws `0.00`. The PO ruled the same cell on the property's Units tab
on 2026-09-10: the vacancy sentence moves to `Occupant`, and `0.00` shows *"only
when the balance really is zero, never manufactured over a real debt."* A unit
with no occupying account produced no ledger read at all, so both lists of units
now say `Not measured` in the same words from the same key. **This is that
ruling applied to the second screen, not a second decision.**

### 3 · THE `Select` COLUMN AND THE BULK BAR STAY, AND THAT IS THE PO's CALL

`CR-089-p050` §12 lists both among the drawn absences. `BR-MET-041` is a signed
rule requiring bulk plan assignment and the checkbox is the only control that
reaches it. Removing a ratified capability to match a drawing is not a
maintenance fix; the divergence is stamped and **it goes back to the PO**.

### 4 · THE ADD-UNITS FORM STACKS, THOUGH THE FRAME DRAWS IT IN COLUMNS

`B14` rule 38, ratified the same day: *"a drawing telling you that two fields
sit side by side … is not layout, it is FORM CONSTRUCTION."* The frame lays §4
out three across then two. Multi-column field rows change every form in the
product and no lane owns that blast radius, so the fields stack and the
divergence is recorded. **Which fields, in which order, under which headings is
still the drawing's, and all of it is built.**

### 5 · `Floor` IS A TEXT FIELD ON THE CREATE FORM BECAUSE IT IS ONE ON THE EDIT FORM

Item 5 of this file's 2026-09-10 entry already ruled it for the form that EDITS
`floor_label`: the column is free text and holds `Ground`, `G`, `Mezzanine`,
`PH`, so a closed list needs an unratified vocabulary and would make existing
values unselectable. The frame draws a select on the CREATE form too. **A create
form offering a list the edit form cannot show back is one fact wearing two
shapes**, so the earlier ruling governs both and the frame loses on this control.

### 6 · TWO DRAWN WORDS ARE NOT PRINTED, BECAUSE THEY WOULD BE PROMISES NOTHING KEEPS

Hard-won law 1 applied to screen copy:

* `Starts`' drawn help ends *"Never mid-cycle."* No rule in this repository
  states that constraint and nothing enforces it — `CR-089-p053`'s own
  contradiction 3 says so. The first sentence is printed and the second is not.
  **Whether a unit plan may start mid-cycle is an open question for the PO.**
* the search help's second sentence describes when the box arrives filled, which
  the clerk can see. `B14` rule 32's one-sentence budget wins.

### AND ONE RETIREMENT, STATED SO NOBODY READS IT AS A REVERT

`metering.addUnits.howMany` moves from *"Units on each floor"* to **"How many
units"** and `metering.addUnits.howManyHelp` is RETIRED from all eleven
catalogues with its caller. Both are deliberate: `CR-089-p053` §4 row 1 draws
`How many units` with no help beneath it, and §13 removes the floors-times-units
multiplier the old label described from the form altogether. `Floors` is not
deleted — it moved into the naming fold, beside the `{floor}` token it is only
meaningful next to.

## 2026-09-10 — CITY LIMITS IS THE BUILDING'S FACT, AND THE RULING IS ABOUT THE DOOR NEXT TO IT

**PO, verbatim:** *"City limits - on Unit will be inherited from Premises only -
please note"*.

**Nothing in the code changes.** `inside_city_limits` lives on `premises` and
nowhere else — migration `0013_br_rat_101_inside_city_limits` declares
`model_name="premises"`, the `Unit` model has no such field, no unit screen
renders one, and no unit frame in the blueprint draws one. That was **checked
before this was written**, not assumed, because a ruling recorded as
"confirming current behaviour" is worthless if the behaviour is not what we
think.

**So why write it down at all.** Because of what sits beside it. On 2026-09-08
`BR-MET-1162` let a unit carry **its own `lat`/`lng`** — *"GIS data for unit
might change"* — a cabin or a pad being somewhere its site office is not. That
is the ONLY thing about a unit's location that may differ from its building's,
and a lane reasoning by analogy could easily conclude that any address-shaped
fact is now refinable per unit. **It is not.** City limits is an ADDRESS fact,
not a map fact: a flat cannot be outside the city its building is inside.

**And it decides money.** `BR-RAT-101`/`BR-RAT-102` multiply an address's bills
by the outside-city surcharge, so a unit-level override would let two flats in
one building price differently on a fact that cannot differ between them — and
would give a clerk a second place to answer it, where `DEF-507`'s lesson
applies: `null` is *unrecorded* and `Outside` is an ANSWER that charges someone.
One place to ask, one place to be wrong, one place to correct.

**What a unit screen may do:** show the building's answer, read-only, saying
where it comes from — the same shape `BR-MET-118` took for services under the
PO's other ruling of this same day. **What it may not do is offer a control.**

Recorded as `BR-MET-1170`. The four units lanes were told the same turn, because
one of them is building unit screens right now and a `City limits` row added in
good faith from a neighbouring screen is exactly how this would have arrived.

## 2026-09-10 — THE FOUR UNITS QUESTIONS, ANSWERED

Put to the PO after the twelve unit screens landed. All four came back in one
message; two confirm what was built, one changes what gets built, and one was
not understood and is restated below in plainer words.

### 1 · THE ASSETS COLUMN STAYS `Asset`

**PO, verbatim:** *"Asset — that table holds carts and fire lines too - Asset is
correct"*. The blueprint's frame draws `Meter`. **The frame loses**, and on
evidence rather than preference: the table holds non-meters, so `Meter` would be
a heading that lies about a third of its own rows. Recorded as a divergence in
`CR-089-p067`; no change.

### 2 · THE PLAN PICKER SHOWS EVERY PLAN, AND GAINS A SEARCH BOX

**PO, verbatim:** *"Yes, but it's a real change, not a fix - not required; you
should show all plan or allow user to do in-line search it and choose."*

**The frame claims the list is filtered to the unit's services. It is not, and
now deliberately never will be.** `getUnitPlanOptions` is not premises-scoped
and the ruling makes that the intended behaviour rather than an unbuilt half.

⚠ **THE RULING HAS TWO HALVES AND ONLY ONE WAS ALREADY TRUE.** *Show all plans*
was; *or let them search it* was not. The unit EDIT form has used
`SearchSelectField` for this field all along and the ADD form used a plain
`SelectField` — **one product asking one question two ways**, and the longer a
tenant's plan list grows the worse the add form gets. Changed, with
`UnitPlanPickerIsSearchable.test.ts` proved red on the old control first
(`expected 'SelectField' to be 'SearchSelectField'`).

⚠ **AND THE TEST GUARDS THE *NOT FILTERING* HALF TOO**, because a lane reading
the frame later would see an unfiltered list as a bug and "fix" it — which would
reverse this ruling. The case says so in as many words.

### 3 · THE UNIT EDIT TITLE — RESTATED, BECAUSE THE ANSWER SAID IT WAS NOT CLEAR

**PO:** *"I did not understand"*. Fair; the original note was written from the
lane's report rather than from scratch. The plain version:

The blueprint draws the dialog title as **`Edit Unit 2`** — the word *Unit* plus
the number. That works only if a unit's label is a bare number. **In this product
labels already carry the noun**: `Unit A`, `Suite 200`, `Apt 101`, `Master`. So
the drawn form produced **`Edit Unit Unit B`** on the first real screen, which is
what the browser walk photographed. The title is now just the label — **`Edit
Unit B`**, `Edit Suite 200`. Nothing is pending; this records why the drawing was
not followed, and the only way to have the drawn form back is to change what
labels contain.

### 4 · THE VACANCY NOTE STAYS WHERE IT IS

**PO, verbatim:** *"Thats correct"*, on leaving `OQ-316`'s note in place until
they say otherwise. No change.

## 2026-09-10 — FOUR OF THE `CR-087` DECISIONS, ANSWERED

### 1 · CHARGE CODES → CREATE → STEP 2 · THE FOUR TICKS STAY STACKED

**PO, verbatim:** *"Stacks them down the page"*. The blueprint draws the four
behaviour ticks on one row. **The drawing loses**, and it loses on the PO's own
earlier evidence: `DEF-2356` is the PO reporting the one-row version as broken
alignment on this exact screen. **The drawing is asking for the defect back.**
No change; recorded so no later lane "fixes" the stack.

### 2 · MONEY SHOWS TWO DECIMALS, EVERYWHERE IN PLANS & RATES

**PO, verbatim:** *"Keep two decimals"*. The blueprint draws `$45.0000` on
frame after frame. This re-affirms the re-sign of 2026-08-22 (hard rule 2:
stored to four, displayed to two) and the drawing appears to have drawn the raw
API response rather than the screen. **No change; the divergence is recorded in
every conformance file that met it.**

### 3 · DISCOUNTS → OVERVIEW → THE SECOND TILE COUNTS **ACCOUNTS**

**PO, verbatim:** *"it should be on accounts; discount is given to accounts"*.

⚠ **THIS REVERSES THE BLUEPRINT, WHICH RULES *"UNITS, NOT ACCOUNTS"* ON PAGE
78.** The reversal is the right way round and the code already said so in
writing: the discounts lane found `definitionDetail.tsx` arguing the
counter-case — enrolment carries a foreign key to **`Account`**, so a tile
reading *"31 of 86"* was spanning two different populations. **The PO's ruling
makes the count and the label agree**, and it agrees with the thing the data
actually holds.

**What it decides:** tile 2 is an ACCOUNT count and says `accounts`; the
adjacent `ELIGIBLE UNITS` column on the Plans tab is the one that must now be
re-read, because eligible-vs-enrolled must count the same kind of thing or the
fraction is meaningless.

### 4 · PLANS → CREATE → CHARGES / TAXES / DISCOUNTS & BILLING — THE ADD SHAPE

**PO, verbatim:** *"I want search from drop down, multi select and then set the
price - my aug rule was right"*, referring to their own ruling of 2026-08-21
(`DEF-447`): *"its search and add ; not select kind of UI"*.

⚠ **AND IT IS NOT SIMPLY *KEEP WHAT IS BUILT*, WHICH IS WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS.**
Three shapes are in play, not two:

| | what it is |
|---|---|
| the **September drawing** | one attached table with a single `+ Add` button |
| what is **built today** | r10's TWO PANES — the whole catalogue on the left, the plan's list on the right, `+ Add` per catalogue row |
| what the PO has now **asked for** | **one searchable dropdown → multi-select → then price each one** |

**The drawing loses. The two panes ALSO lose.** The ruling keeps the *"search
and add"* principle of August and replaces the two-pane realisation of it: a
clerk types into one box, picks several, and prices them in the list that
results — no second pane holding a catalogue.

**Confirmation is being taken visually before anything is built**, because a
sentence about an interaction is the thing most easily agreed and differently
imagined; a working mock was put to the PO the same turn.

### 5 · PLANS → A PLAN'S PAGE → AUDIT TAB · ONE DATE, NOT A RANGE

**PO, verbatim:** *"we need to display when it was changed - one date is good
enough"*.

⚠ **THIS UNBLOCKS AN ITEM THAT LOOKED LIKE IT NEEDED A SCHEMA CHANGE, AND THE
RULING IS WHY IT DOES NOT.** The blueprint draws each version with an
**EFFECTIVE RANGE** — a start and an end — and asserts it *"needed no new
column"*. It does: a range needs the NEXT version's start date, `plan_versions`
carries no `effective_from`, and `OQ-324` records that omission as
**deliberate** — *"adding one would make the dated reading storable before it is
ruled"*.

**One date is a different fact and it is already stored.** Every change writes
its own timestamp, so *when it was changed* can be read today. **So: build one
date, add no column, and the open question stays open rather than being settled
by a screen that needed it.** The drawn range is a divergence and is recorded as
one.

### 6 · DISCOUNTS → CREATE → STEP 4 · THE APPROVAL FIGURE COMES FROM THE SERVER

**PO, verbatim:** *"it should come from server"*.

The drawn second-approval sentence names a **monthly** subsidy figure. Nothing
computes it, and the client may not derive it: `DEF-364` is the standing refusal
to format or divide money in the browser, and `DiscountWizard.tsx` already
declines to do exactly this arithmetic in a comment. **The ruling puts the
figure on the server**, which is the same posture `RateChangesTab` takes for the
same reason.

⚠ **IT DOES NOT SETTLE *WHICH* SECOND-APPROVAL POLICY GOVERNS** — `PRB-13` and
`OQ-290` are both signed and disagree on the threshold. That half stays open;
this ruling decides only where the number is worked out. Whichever policy wins,
the figure is served, not divided on screen.

### 7 · DISCOUNTS → CREATE · THE SCOPE GAINS A PAIR, IT DOES NOT WIDEN

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-10:** *"Add a new choice. - one or more services from
drop down; All services or sepecific services; this is correct"*.

Answers `CR-091-BRC01` §5 question 1. **A clerk is offered `All services` or
`Specific services`; choosing the second opens a dropdown that takes one or
more.** The existing `one_service` scope is NOT widened — every discount already
saved keeps the meaning it had, and no migration has to reinterpret stored rows.

⚠ **AND IT SETTLES QUESTION 2 BETTER THAN THE ANSWER PROPOSED FOR IT.** The
recommendation put to the PO was *"an empty list means every service"*, copied
from how a **tax** behaves. **That reading is now wrong here.** With `All
services` on screen as its own choice, an empty list stops being an expression
of intent and becomes an **unfinished form**: a clerk who means every service
says so. So `Specific services` with nothing chosen is a **REFUSAL**.

**The general lesson, worth more than the case:** an absence only carries
meaning while there is no way to state the thing explicitly. Add the explicit
choice and the same empty value must change from *a synonym* to *a mistake* —
and a screen that kept the old reading would silently apply a discount to every
service on a form the clerk had not finished.

### 8 · THE AUDIT TAB IS RENAMED AND ITS ADDRESS DOES NOT MOVE

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-10:** *"Change the label, keep the address"*.

The blueprint renames the tab from `Versions` to `Audit` **and** changes its web
address from `?tab=versions` to `?tab=audit`. **The label changes; the address
stays.** Links already sent to people keep working, and the label is the half a
clerk reads.

⚠ **HALF OF THIS IS ALREADY DONE AND THAT IS WHY IT WAS WORTH ASKING.** The
charge code's tab ALREADY reads `Audit` in all eleven catalogues while its
address is still `versions` — so the drawn `?tab=audit` link in the blueprint
opens the Overview instead, silently, because `versions` is what the tab list
holds. **The ruling makes that state correct rather than half-finished:** the
label is the target, the address is not, and the drawn address is a divergence.

### 9 · THE FOUR EMPTY TAB BODIES GET BUILT

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-10:** *"build"* — asked whether the `Plans` and `Audit`
tabs on the **Taxes & fees** and **Charge codes** detail pages should exist at
all, given the blueprint specifies them across four pages and marks them **NO
COMMITMENT**.

**All four are built.** Today each renders ONE SENTENCE saying it cannot do its
job, and two of those sentences are the exact text the blueprint quotes back as
the defect.

⚠ **THIS IS NOT A SCREEN JOB AND THE SIZING MUST SAY SO.** Three of the four
need a server read that does not exist:

| tab | what is missing |
|---|---|
| charge code → Plans | no endpoint at all — `api.py`'s charge surface is three lines |
| charge code → Audit | **no version object exists** — no model, no table, no rows. A migration and a write path before any screen |
| tax → Plans | the reach list needs one `values_list` off an existing query — the cheapest of the four |
| tax → Audit | three of four columns are stored per row; a chain read and the actor are missing |

⚠ **AND THE CHARGE CODE'S AUDIT TAB CARRIES A DEPENDENCY THE BLUEPRINT ITSELF
NAMES.** Its create wizard is specified to require a *reason* for a change, and
there is nowhere to store one — the blueprint says the two "only work together".
So that tab and that wizard field are one piece of work, not two.

### 10 · THE PLAN WIZARD'S ADD-SHAPE, CONFIRMED FROM A WORKING MOCK

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-10:** *"Attaching charges to a plan - they way you ahve
show is correct; interction is also correct."*

**The agreed shape, on all three steps — `Charges`, `Taxes`, `Discounts &
billing`:**

1. **one search box** — a dropdown over every charge code / authority / discount
   the tenant owns, matched on the code, the name **and** the service;
2. **multi-select** — pick several; each becomes a removable chip;
3. **then price them** — the chosen rows become a list with an amount against
   each, **priced in the same step where they were picked**.

⚠ **THIS IS A THIRD SHAPE, NOT EITHER OF THE TWO IN THE TABLE, AND THAT IS THE
POINT OF THE ENTRY.** The September drawing has one attached table, one `+ Add`
and **no search**. What is built is `r10`'s TWO PANES — the whole catalogue
parked on the left, `+ Add` per row, pricing done elsewhere. The PO's August
ruling (*"its search and add ; not select kind of UI"*, `DEF-447`) was read as
the two panes, and this confirms the PRINCIPLE while replacing that
realisation: **the second pane goes, and pricing comes into the step.**

⚠ **CONFIRMATION WAS TAKEN VISUALLY, ON PURPOSE.** An interaction is the thing
most easily agreed in words and differently imagined — *"search and add"* has
now produced two different screens from one sentence. A working mock was put to
the PO in the same turn and they used it before answering:
`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/b3b41fb1-d68b-4f0f-88e6-548600b902f3`.
**Whoever builds this looks at that before reading this paragraph.**

⚠ **AND IT REVISES A RECOMMENDATION THIS LOG ALREADY CARRIES.** The entry of
earlier today recommended *"keep the two-pane"* on the strength of the August
ruling. That recommendation was wrong — it preserved a realisation the PO had
not actually asked for. Recorded rather than quietly replaced, because the next
lane reading both entries needs to know which one governs: **this one.**

### 11 · THE OUTSIDE-CITY SURCHARGE — THE SCREEN INVERTS, THE DATA DOES NOT

**PO, 2026-09-10, confirming a table put to them:** *"this si correct"*, over
**How much** stays on the plan · **Which services it hits** becomes one dropdown
meaning *apply it to these* · **What's stored — unchanged** · **What the billing
engine does — unchanged**.

⚠ **THIS SUPERSEDES THE PO'S OWN EARLIER SENTENCE IN THE SAME SESSION** —
*"no per service exemption as of now; its on entire plan and all services or no
services"* — and the supersession is the point of the entry. That first reading
would have **deleted `BR-RAT-102` and the worked case in design §A4 S2**: a plan
that surcharges water and electric outside the city while **sewer's base stays
$8.00 flat**. It was held rather than recorded, the collision was put to the PO
with that figure, and the answer that came back keeps the capability and changes
only how it is asked for. **Nothing was built against the first reading.**

**What changes:** the wizard stops drawing a yes/no *"spare this one"* on every
service line and draws **one dropdown of the services the surcharge APPLIES to**
— the same shape as the discount scope ruled two entries above, so a clerk
learns one control and not two.

**What does not change:** `PlanService.outside_city_exempt`, its migration, the
catalogue read `_outside_city_exempt_services`, and `resolution.py`'s
`if service in catalogue.outside_city_exempt_services`. **No schema work, no
engine work, no migration.**

⚠ **THE CLERK'S CHOICE IS THE EXACT NEGATION OF THE STORED FLAG, AND THAT IS
THE RISK.** Picked = surcharged = `outside_city_exempt` **false**. Unpicked =
spared = **true**. That is the same shape as the tax `discountTreatment` labels
a lane examined this same day and found correct only after checking — a control
reading the opposite way round from the value behind it is invisible to every
check that asserts the value.

**So the guard asserts MONEY, never the flag:** *sewer stays `$8.00` and water
rises 15% on a premises outside the city*. A later inversion then fails as a
wrong bill instead of passing as a correct boolean.

**One open detail, defaulted rather than asked twice:** a factor set with no
service picked mirrors the discount ruling — `All services` or `Specific
services`, with an empty specific list REFUSED as unfinished.

### 12 · THE SURCHARGE DROPDOWN OPENS WITH EVERY SERVICE PICKED

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-10**, asked what a 15% factor with no service picked
should mean: *"this will not happen - we will have all services as default
ooption"*.

**So the control is ONE dropdown that opens with every service already
selected**, and a clerk removes the ones to spare. There is no `All services` /
`Specific services` pair here — that pair was the recommendation put to the PO
and this answer replaces it.

⚠ **AND THE DEFAULT ON SCREEN IS THE DEFAULT IN THE DATABASE, WHICH IS WHY THIS
IS THE RIGHT ANSWER AND NOT MERELY A TIDY ONE.** `PlanService.outside_city_exempt`
is `models.BooleanField(default=False)` — *nothing is spared* is already what a
new row means. A screen that opens with everything picked WRITES what the column
already held, so the untouched path stores nothing surprising and the two
defaults cannot drift apart.

⚠ **IT ALSO REMOVES THE AMBIGUITY WITHOUT A REFUSAL.** The question was whether
an empty selection means *no surcharge anywhere* or *the form is unfinished*.
Pre-filling makes empty a deliberate act — a clerk who unpicks every service has
said *"spare all of them"*, which stores `exempt` on each and yields no surcharge.
That is coherent, so it is ALLOWED rather than refused, and nothing has to guess.

⚠ **THIS DIFFERS FROM THE DISCOUNT SCOPE TWO ENTRIES ABOVE, DELIBERATELY — DO
NOT HARMONISE THEM.** A discount offers `All services` or `Specific services`
with an empty specific list REFUSED; the surcharge offers one pre-filled
dropdown with empty ALLOWED. The difference follows the data: a discount's
service list starts as **nothing chosen** and an empty list there is genuinely
an unfinished form, while the surcharge's column starts as **nothing spared**
and an empty picking is a statement. Same-looking screens, opposite starting
points; a lane that unified them would silently change what a blank form means
on one of the two.

### 13 · A RATE SCHEDULE IS THE ONE PLACE A SERVICE'S FIGURES ARE SET; A PLAN SHOWS THEM

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-10:** *"Even if per service rate schedule has it per
service - base rate, Rates and Minim rates - you just need to attache dit ti
plan, lets not override that at plan level again. it complciated for user"*,
then: *"set it in rates and use it in plans - thats it - this is rule - when you
do the final review on plan you show all values - coming from rate schedule; and
when we view plan details you show the details again coming from rate schedule"*.

**THE RULE: one place to SET, everywhere else SHOWS.** A rate schedule carries a
service's base charge, its rates and its minimum. A plan ATTACHES a schedule and
**displays** those figures; it does not restate them.

⚠ **THE SCOPE IS TWO COLUMNS, NOT ONE — the question put to the PO was about the
minimum alone and their answer names the base charge too.** Measured:

| the schedule holds | the plan ALSO holds today | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `TariffVersion.base_charge` | `PlanService.base_charge` | duplicate — **goes from the plan** |
| `TariffVersion.minimum_bill` | `PlanService.minimum_amount` | duplicate — **goes from the plan** |

**And two display obligations come with it**, both named by the PO: the plan
wizard's **review step** shows the figures *coming from the rate schedule*, and
the **plan detail view** shows them again from the same source. So the values do
not disappear from those screens — they stop being editable there and start
being read through.

⚠ **`RatePlan.minimum_bill_amount` IS NOT IN SCOPE, AND THE REASONING IS
RECORDED RATHER THAN RE-ASKED.** The rule is *do not restate what the schedule
carries*. A schedule carries no whole-bill floor — it prices ONE service, and a
floor on the WHOLE BILL is a different fact that no schedule could hold. It is
therefore untouched by this ruling by construction, along with
`outside_city_factor` and `late_fee_charge`, which are likewise the plan's own.

⚠ **BUT `BR-RAT-028` CANNOT SIMPLY BE AMENDED, AND THIS IS THE STOP.** Its text
is *"both modes built — (A) per-service minimum and (B) plan-level floor … when
both set: per-service minimums apply first, then the plan floor tops up the
total"*, CONFIRMED, with `GT-13` behind it. **Removing mode A leaves that
combination clause with nothing to combine.** That is billing math on a signed
rule, so it needs a **re-sign via HUMAN-GUIDE §6, never an inline edit**, and
`GT-13` has to be re-read before anything is deleted.

**STILL OPEN — the live figure.** On the seeded utility, **one of four plan
service lines already carries a per-service minimum**. Removing the column
changes what that plan bills. Whether a migration carries the value onto the
schedule or drops it and lets the bill move has NOT been ruled and is not
assumed here.

### 14 · THE PER-SERVICE FIGURES MOVE TO THE SCHEDULE — AND NO BILL MOVES WITH THEM

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-10:** *"We are in beta - we can make these changes now -
we will not able to do it later- hence dont worry"*, and on the objection that
removing the column would move a bill: *"why it will impact bills - you ahve
value - you might have to change the formula"*, and *"rate schedule give you all
these - youa re only chaging the soruces within the plan thats it"*.

⚠ **THE PO IS RIGHT AND THE OBJECTION PUT TO THEM WAS OVERSTATED. RECORDED
BECAUSE THE MEASUREMENT IS WHAT SETTLED IT.** Read from the seeded utility:

| | |
|---|---|
| plan `RES-STD`, one service line | base `$8.00`, minimum `$15.00` |
| the rate schedule for that service | base **none**, minimum **none** |

**So the figures exist ONLY on the plan; the schedule is empty.** That makes
this a MOVE, not a recalculation: copy each plan service line's base and minimum
onto its attached schedule, then drop the plan's two columns. **The bill is
identical.** Delete without moving and the minimum vanishes and that plan
under-bills — which is the whole of the risk, and it is a migration step rather
than a ruling.

⚠ **AND THE RE-SIGN OBJECTION IS WITHDRAWN.** It was argued that removing mode A
of `BR-RAT-028` leaves its combination clause — *per-service minimums apply
first, then the plan floor tops up* — with nothing to combine, and therefore
needs a finance re-sign. **The PO's reading is better: the per-service minimum
still exists and still applies first; it is READ FROM THE SCHEDULE instead of
from the plan.** The arithmetic is untouched and `GT-13` still describes it. So
`BR-RAT-028` needs an AMENDMENT naming the new source, not a re-sign of math
that did not change.

**What gets built:** the migration above · the schedule's base drawn READ-ONLY
with its charge code named beside it (`BR-RAT-088` — the charge code owns the
base) · the plan wizard's review step and the plan detail view SHOWING both
figures read through from the schedule rather than setting them.

### 15 · SECOND APPROVAL ON A DISCOUNT: THE PLUMBING STAYS, THE DEFAULT GOES OFF

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-10:** *"lets do this - (b) Keep the plumbing, default it
off. The threshold setting stays but starts unset, so nothing ever requires a
second approval unless a utility deliberately turns it on."*

**This closes `PRB-13` / `OQ-290` without choosing between them.** Two approved
policies disagreed — one measuring projected monthly subsidy against `$500`, the
other measuring the budget cap against a `$10,000` setting — and the product said
so on screen in `rating.discountWizard.secondApprovalConflict`. **Neither now
runs by default. The conflict stops being live and stops being visible.**

⚠ **THE PO'S REASONING IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE PART THAT GENERALISES:**
*"we have cap also that one person get maixim X discount - that it - we dont
have to double check it again"*. **Verified before acting on it — there are
THREE per-customer caps already built and on the wizard**: `cap per bill`, `cap
per year`, `cap lifetime`, beside the programme's `budget cap` and a `floor`. So
exposure is bounded per customer three ways and in total once more, and a second
signature was checking something already bounded. **For a utility run by 10–20
staff, a mandatory second approver may not even exist.**

**What changes:** the threshold setting `discount_second_approval_threshold_amount`
**starts UNSET** rather than at `$10,000`; `second_approval_required` returns
false while it is unset; the conflict sentence is deleted.

⚠ **AND ONE CLAUSE MUST GO WITH IT OR THE FEATURE IS NOT ACTUALLY OFF.** Today a
**blank budget cap always forces** the second approval — *"unbounded always needs
a second approval"*. With the threshold unset that clause would still fire, so a
discount with no budget cap would demand an approver a small utility has not
got. **It is disabled with the rest.** The columns, the freeze-at-submit
behaviour and the setting all remain, so a larger utility can switch it on later
and get the whole mechanism back.

### 16 · THE PER-SERVICE MINIMUM IS BUILT ONTO THE SCHEDULE — AND THE BASE HALF IS STOPPED BY A SIGNED RULE

**Built 2026-09-10, Plans lane, against entries 13 and 14 above.**

**WHAT MOVED, AND THE ARITHMETIC DID NOT.** `plan_services.minimum_amount` is
gone. `rating/0030` copies every stated figure onto **every version** of the
tariff the plan attached for that service; `rating/0031` removes the column.
`gather._tariff_config_for` now reads `inputs["minimum_bill"]` — the rate
schedule version's own column, which `pricing_inputs` has published all along
and which `DEF-2446` deliberately left unread because *"nothing signed says what
a schedule that ALSO carries one means"*. **The PO's ruling is that missing
signature, and it removes the ambiguity rather than resolving it:** there is no
longer a plan column to disagree with, so no precedence exists to get wrong.
`DEF-2446` closes with it.

**THE MONEY, MEASURED AND PROVED RED FIRST.** `WE-3`/`GT-19` — `0.4 kgal`
residential water — prices `$1.60` usage + `$8.00` base = `$9.60`, topped to the
`$15.00` floor as `+$5.40`, tax `$1.42`, **total `$16.42`**. Without the floor
the same bill is **`$10.51`**. Both figures are asserted in
`test_cr090_minimum_reads_from_the_schedule.py`, which is written as DOLLARS on
purpose: a test asserting `minimum_amount == Decimal("15.000000")` passes on the
plan's column and passes on the schedule's, and a test asserting the column is
GONE passes on a product that has silently stopped charging the floor. **The
only assertion that can tell a successful move from a lost one is the amount on
the bill.**

⚠ **THE VERSION FAN-OUT IS THE PART A ONE-LINE MIGRATION WOULD HAVE GOT WRONG.**
The plan's column was VERSION-INDEPENDENT — whichever version `BR-RAT-007`
resolved, the plan's `$15.00` applied. The schedule's is version-DEPENDENT, so a
back-dated re-bill priced from last year's version would lose the floor unless
every version carries it. `0030` writes to all of them, leaves any that already
state a figure alone, and LOGS a disagreement by name rather than reconciling
it — that case is `OQ-238`'s shape and the plan's figure is about to be deleted,
so a silent preference would be undetectable afterwards.

⚠ **AND A SECOND FAN-OUT NOBODY WOULD HAVE SEEN: THE FLOOR IS CHARGED ONCE, NOT
ONCE PER SIZE LINE.** `_tariff_configs_for_sizes` passed the plan's figure on
the FIRST size group only — *"the standing charge and the minimum ride on a
group whose size is known"*. The schedule's figure is read INSIDE
`_tariff_config_for`, where `inputs` is built per size group, so an
unconditional read would top a warehouse's 6" and two 2" fire lines up three
times. The parameter is therefore **renamed** `minimum_amount` →
`carries_service_minimum`, not repointed: a caller still passing the old name
now fails loudly instead of having its figure silently ignored.

**`BR-RAT-028` IS AMENDED, NOT RE-SIGNED.** `GT-13` and `GT-19` were both
re-read first: **neither states a SOURCE**, both state the arithmetic, and the
arithmetic is untouched. HUMAN-GUIDE §6 was not entered.

---

⚠ **AND THE BASE HALF OF ENTRY 14 IS NOT BUILT, BECAUSE IT COLLIDES WITH A
CONFIRMED RULE THAT WAS RE-READ AND WHOSE SUPERSESSION WAS NEVER STATED.**

Entry 13's table names two duplicates and says both *"go from the plan"*. The
minimum is above. **The base cannot follow it, and this is reported rather than
decided** — hard-won law 13 puts a ruling that collides with a signed rule in
the short list of things that legitimately reach the PO, with the supersession
stated rather than assumed. Three reasons, in order of how much they cost:

1. **`tariff_versions.base_charge` IS RETIRED.** `BR-RAT-088` (CONFIRMED,
   2026-08-20) makes the CHARGE CODE the base's one source and says of the
   schedule's column, verbatim: *"A schedule version that still carries a base
   is a migration artefact and must be refused once the charge code owns it."*
   Copying the plan's base there would manufacture, on every plan in the
   product, exactly the artefact the rule says must be refused.
2. **`plan_services.base_charge` IS DELIBERATELY NOT RETIRED, AND THE RULE SAYS
   WHEN IT MAY BE.** `BR-RAT-088`'s amendment of 2026-09-01 (`CR-057`):
   *"THE PRECONDITION THIS RULE NAMES FOR RETIRING `plan_services.base_charge`
   IS NOW MET, AND THE COLUMN IS STILL NOT RETIRED — DELIBERATELY … the OFF path
   is the documented one-line rollback"*, and *"its precondition is not R4 has a
   caller but **the rollback has been withdrawn**"*. It has not been withdrawn:
   `SBH_BILLING_RESOLUTION_STEPS=` still falls back to
   `gather._base_charge_for`, which reads that column, and
   `test_br_rat_120_size_refusal.py::test_TC6b` prices a real bill through it.
3. **THE COST IF IT IS DONE ANYWAY IS `DEF-154`'s EXACT SHAPE.** A deployment
   that rolls back after the column is dropped bills **`$0.00` for base on every
   line of every bill** — which is the defect that ran for days on this product
   with the whole test suite green.

**WHAT IS BUILT FOR THE BASE INSTEAD, AND IT HONOURS THE RULING'S DISPLAY
HALF.** Entry 14's own *"what gets built"* already names the resolution — *"the
schedule's base drawn READ-ONLY with its charge code named beside it
(`BR-RAT-088` — the charge code owns the base)"* — and that is what the price
card does today: Band 1's `BASE` cell prints the `is_base` charge code's own
amount with `from BASE-W` as the row's footnote. The plan sets nothing;
`DEF-422` removed the control long ago and only the stored value is
round-tripped. **So the ruling's user-visible half — *one place to SET,
everywhere else SHOWS* — is already true of the base. What is not done is the
COLUMN DROP, and that is the part the signed rule reserves.**

**ONE SENTENCE FROM THE PO SETTLES IT, and the question is not *may we do it*
but *is the rollback withdrawn*:** if the R3/R4 chain is now trusted enough that
`SBH_BILLING_RESOLUTION_STEPS=` will never be typed again, `BR-RAT-088`'s own
precondition is met and `plan_services.base_charge` can be dropped in its own
change. Until then it is a column nobody sets, nobody shows and one deployment
switch still reads.

### 17 · THE PLANS TAB'S SCREEN WORK — THREE JUDGMENTS, AND ONE OF THEM CHANGED THE KIT

**Built 2026-09-10, Plans lane, second wave.**

**1 · THE SERVICE LIST BECOMES THE KIT'S CHIP MULTI-SELECT, AND THE KIT GAINED A
FIELD RATHER THAN THE SCREEN KEEPING ITS GRID.** Step 2 drew an eleven-cell
checkbox grid. B14 rule 9 forbids a wall of checkboxes **by name**, rule 36's own
breach (e) names one on another screen, and `CR-087-p087` §2 draws one select
plus removable chips and lists `MultiSelectField` + `ChipList` in its COMPONENTS
row. **This is not a rule-38 divergence** — the drawing and the UI rules said the
same thing and only the code differed.

⚠ **THE STRAIGHT SWAP WOULD HAVE DELETED A RATIFIED BEHAVIOUR, WHICH IS THE
JUDGMENT WORTH RECORDING.** `ChipMultiSelect` could only list CHOOSABLE options,
and this screen must name the services the utility has switched OFF — greyed,
inside the list, with where to switch them on. That is `BR-RAT-024`'s restored
clause and the PO's own words of 2026-09-08. So `ChipOption` gained **optional**
`disabled` and `reason`, which is rule 36's instruction (*"where the kit lacks a
piece, ADD IT TO THE KIT"*) with rule 38's caveat honoured: absent on every
existing call site, so nothing else in the product moves. **The reason renders as
visible TEXT beside the label, never on `title`** — an `<option title>` is
mouse-only, and B14 says colour, or its absence, is never the only signal.

**2 · STEP 7 NOW REFUSES A BLANK START DATE, AND THE DRAWING SAID IT ALREADY
DID.** `CR-087-p099` §3 records the fix as landed — *"It is checked here"* — and
the step declared **no `validate` at all**. Only steps 1, 2 and 3 ever had one.
Hard-won law 1: a document claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. It refuses
`Continue` and never `Save draft` (`BR-RAT-031`), and **step 8's own refusal
stays**, because it is the server's rule restated at the commit and it is what a
resumed draft jumping straight to step 8 still meets.

**3 · THE AUDIT TAB SHOWS ONE DATE — AND THE DRAWING'S OWN FIX COULD NOT BE
BUILT.** The frame draws `EFFECTIVE` carrying a RANGE, and says it *"needed no
new column"* because it is *"taken from the next version's start"*. **On the data
as stored there is no next version's start to take:** `plan_versions` carries no
`effective_from` and `OQ-324` records that omission as DELIBERATE, so building it
means option (B) of an open question the PO reserves. Put to them that way, the
ruling was **"one date is good enough"**. The column is now `Changed` and prints
the version row's own `created_at` — already stored, and already printed four
inches away under the version number while the column beside it showed an
em-dash and a sentence explaining the em-dash, on every row but one. **No column,
no migration, no ruling on `OQ-324`.**

⚠ **AND THE TEST NOW ASSERTS THE DATE RATHER THAN THE ABSENCE.** The previous one
asserted `noVersionWindow` was present, which is an assertion that passes over a
column showing nothing at all — hard-won law 7's *looking at the wrong thing*. It
asserts the year, the new column label, and the **absence of** the old sentence,
because a half-landed rename only shows as red when something refuses the string
that was supposed to go.

**WHAT IS NOT DONE, NAMED SO THE NEXT LANE DOES NOT HAVE TO REDISCOVER IT:** the
add-shape confirmed from the working mock — one search box, multi-select chips,
priced in the same step — is **not built on steps 4, 5 or 6**. It is one change
across three steps and shipping one of the three would leave two shapes in one
wizard. **One question comes with it and it is worth answering before a line is
written:** the mock's third panel is *"then price them"*, with an editable amount
against each row, and `BR-RAT-088` says a plan **displays** an amount and never
defines one — the step's own drawn sentence is *"A plan composes; it does not
price."* So on the Charges step the list that appears is priced READ-ONLY and the
only editable cell is `APPLIED`; on Taxes the rate is read-only; on Discounts the
editable cells are the two dates. That reading follows the signed rule and the
mock's figures are `B14` rule 37 illustrations, but it is the PO's sentence to
give, because *"then set the price"* were their words.
