## 2026-09-10 — THE TAXES & FEES SCREENS, AGAINST THEIR DRAWING (CR-087, maintenance)

**Track: MAINTENANCE, and the classification is ours to make** — a clerk can
already create, read and edit a tax on these screens, so `22-product-maintenance-process.md`
governs and not `r11`. Three defects filed by ROOT CAUSE, not by symptom:
`DEF-RAT-4820` (built-not-wired), `DEF-RAT-4821` (wrong-logic),
`DEF-RAT-4822` (design-divergence).

### 1 · THE PRIMARY ACTION ON THIS SCREEN DID NOT WORK, AND THE REFUSAL SAID SO IN WORDS THAT WERE NO LONGER TRUE

`POST /taxes/{id}/corrections` has been implemented, routed and typed since
`DEF-384`. **No component called it.** Meanwhile `Edit` was live on a tax in
force, opened `TaxWizard`, and the wizard refused every field with *"A mistake is
corrected by a new version carrying a written reason, and that route has not been
built, so nothing here can be saved."* That sentence was true the day it was
written and false from the day the endpoint landed.

**Every check passed over it for two weeks.** `G13` asks whether a prop is
passed; nothing asks whether a REFUSAL is still true, and a refusal renders
perfectly well however false it is. 578 rating cases, `tsc`, every gate — green.
This is hard-won law 2 in both directions at once, and it is the second time this
exact file has produced it (`DEF-RAT-4647` was `Edit` disabled over a wizard that
was live).

**The rule did not move.** A tax in force is still never edited in place: hard
rule 4 and `BR-RAT-104` are untouched, and the server still refuses the PATCH.
What changed is that the alternative the refusal NAMED is wired to the door that
serves it. **Three judgments were needed and are recorded rather than assumed:**

* **The body is `{reason, …only the keys that MOVED}`.** `correct_tax` merges the
  changes over the stored row, so sending the whole payload every time is legal
  — and it makes the server's own `rating.taxes.correction_empty` refusal
  (*"a correction that corrects nothing would mint an identical row and supersede
  a live rate for no reason"*) **unreachable for ever**. The diff is the shape the
  endpoint was written for.
* **The statutory window is shown and disabled.** `correct_tax` copies both dates
  off the row being corrected and ignores the payload, so a live box would take
  typing the server discards. `DatePickerField` gained an opt-in
  `disabled?: boolean` — the same prop `TextField` has always had — so nothing
  existing moves (B14 rule 38).
* **The save lands on the NEW row.** A correction returns a different id; sending
  the clerk back to the row they just superseded would show them the figure they
  came to fix.

**The reason's BOUND stays the server's.** The module's money law forbids a
second, drifting rulebook, so a reason that is too short comes back as
`rating.taxes.correction_reason` on the box.

### 2 · ONE COMPONENT, TWO ARGUMENT SETS — THE LAST SCREEN BEFORE A COMMIT SHOWED A REACH LARGER THAN THE TRUTH

The blueprint's guarantee is *"drawn by the same component as step 1, so the two
counts cannot disagree. One reader, one number."* The COMPONENT was the same and
the ARGUMENTS were not: step 1 passed the boundary, the classes and the services;
step 3 passed the boundary alone, and `MatchedPremisesNote` defaults the two
missing lists to `[]`. So a tax restricted to Commercial water read its true reach
on step 1 and the boundary's WHOLE count on the last screen before the commit —
**larger than the truth, which is the one direction this safeguard must never be
wrong in**, and exactly the failure `PRB-05` was written to remove one step
earlier.

**Nothing could see it.** Both steps render a well-formed sentence; the difference
is in the REQUEST and no test read one. **The guard that catches it compares the
two URLs WHOLE** — a substring check cannot see what is missing, and what was
missing was the narrowing (`DEF-182`'s shape, one axis over).

⚠ **AND IT FOUND A SEAM GAP WHILE BEING WRITTEN.** `MatchedPremisesNote` was the
one query in that file reaching for the module-level `api` instead of the
screen's injected client, which is why the arguments it sent had never been
observable. It takes the seam now.

### 3 · HALF THE TAX'S KPI STRIP WAS FURNITURE — THE DISCOUNT'S OWN FIX, ARRIVING TWO DAYS LATE

`Taxable base per month` and `Collected per month` were an em-dash on every tax
that has ever existed (`PRB-06`, two reads over invoice tax lines that do not
exist). `definitionDetail.tsx`'s comment on the DISCOUNT kind — written by
`CR-087 C2` two days earlier — names the shape exactly: *"the tile was a
permanently blank quarter of the strip — furniture, not a stated absence"*. The
tax had **two** such quarters and the same change request never reached it.

**Tiles 2 and 3 are now `Premises in scope` and `Status`, the two remaining facts
the drawing draws**, and both had a read all along —
`GET /taxes/matched-premises` has existed since `DEF-380` and this page never
called it. **The absences are not deleted in silence:** they are stated with their
reasons in a `NOT WORKED OUT YET` bar under the strip, which is the drawing's own
bar and its own rules line — *"A figure that does not exist is stated with its
reason and never drawn at the weight of one that does."*

**Two divergences recorded rather than built**, both under B14 rule 38: the
drawing's TILE ORDER (it puts `RATE` first, where `09-screen-inventory.md` §2
makes tile 1 the reach and tile 4 the defining characteristic on all five
details), and its split of tile 4 into a figure plus a caption (which would put a
second copy of half a money sentence into three more keys × eleven catalogues —
`DEF-364`'s own shape).

### 4 · THE `Plans` AND `Audit` TAB BODIES ARE BUILT, AND THE ACTOR IS A COLUMN

PO ruling of this date, verbatim: **"build"**. Both tabs rendered ONE sentence
saying they could not do their job and the blueprint quotes both back as the
defect.

* **`GET /taxes/{id}/plans`** names the plans the tile already counted, and says
  HOW each one gets the tax. ⚠ **A plan can hold BOTH mechanisms** — the model's
  check constraint bounds a ROW, not a PLAN — and the **binding is reported**,
  because `BR-RAT-113` makes a jurisdiction-mandated tax stay on the bill
  *"whether or not anyone ticked it"*. Naming the attachment would offer a clerk a
  detach that does not exist. Proved RED with the naive *last row wins*:
  `assert 'attached' == 'jurisdiction'`.
* ⚠ **`CR-087-p034` §9's SENTENCE WAS STALE, NOT WRONG.** It says the unit count
  *"is a join nothing in the rating module owns today"* and calls it the part
  needing a PO ruling. `discount_offered_unit_count` landed with `CR-087 C2`, in
  this module, over the same rating-owned table. **No ruling was needed and none
  was taken**; the file is corrected.
* **`GET /taxes/{id}/versions`** walks the correction chain both ways from
  whichever row was asked for, fenced against a cycle.
* ⚠ **`taxes.corrected_by` (rating 0032) IS THE `BY` COLUMN, AND IT IS A COLUMN
  BECAUSE `audit_log` IS PRUNED.** `correct_tax` already writes two audit rows
  naming the same person, so the cheaper-looking answer is a filtered audit
  query. Two existing guards forbid it — `DefinitionDetailPage.tsx`'s §10 note and
  the source-as-text check in `DefinitionDetail.test.tsx` — and hard rule 4's
  2026-09-02 narrowing gives the sharper reason: a rate history sourced from
  `audit_log` **loses its authors on the retention run, silently**, on the one
  screen whose job is to say who changed a statutory rate. NULL on every row
  written before today, and the screen renders a dash: *"History is never filled
  in backwards."* A test asserts that ABSENCE so a later lane that back-fills it
  goes red rather than shipping invented authorship.

### 5 · THE REMITTANCE BLOCK WAS DRAWN ONCE AND BUILT TWICE

Nine filing facts appeared as read-only rows in `Remittance & filings` **and
again as inputs below**, under a `Filing details` heading the drawing does not
have. B14 rule 32: *a row never repeats what its own control offers*. The drawing
has ONE block that both reads and writes, so the read-only copies are gone and
the form's own panels carry the drawn headings, the drawn `EDITABLE` kickers and
the drawn notes. `TAX TYPE` moved to `Remittance & filings`, where it is drawn.

### 6 · TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE

* **The step-2 discount-treatment labels were NOT re-worded.** Page 25 says the
  two options are labelled the opposite way round from the values they store. **At
  `2.234.19` they are not** — `before` reads *"Taxed after discounts (discount
  applies first)"*, which is what `selectors.taxable_subtotal_for` documents
  `before` to mean. A lane nearly "corrected" a money-adjacent label that was
  already right; the decision log of 2026-09-08 recorded the same finding.
* **`ROUNDING REQUIRED BY THE AUTHORITY` still says on screen that it is recorded
  and not honoured** (`OQ-309`, B4 ❄️ FROZEN). The drawing shows the control with
  no caveat. **The product is the more honest of the two and stays.** No signed
  figure was touched and none is proposed.

### 7 · THE COPY IS SHORTENED AGAINST THE DRAWING, ON B14 RULE 33

Three drawn sentences run to nine, fifteen and twenty-one words. Rule 33 caps a
fact at six and a consequence at six per sentence, at most two, *"never cut below
clarity"*. Where a drawing and a ratified B14 rule disagree about LENGTH, B14
wins on rule 38's own principle and each divergence is recorded in the
conformance file. **The eleven catalogues moved together and the new lines are
`NATIVE-REVIEW-OWED`** (rule 35) — one author, not eleven fluent ones.

## 2026-09-10 — `CR-087` · THE CHARGE CODES TAB AGAINST ITS DRAWN BLUEPRINT

Maintenance, not build (`22-product-maintenance-process.md`): a clerk can create,
edit and read a charge code today, so every finding here is a defect against a
screen people already use. Three root-cause rows: `DEF-RAT-4830`,
`DEF-RAT-4831`, `DEF-RAT-4832`.

### 1 · THE CUSTOMER-CLASS CONTROL GOES ON **STEP 2**, AND THE REFUSAL IS DELETED

**`charges.applies_to_customer_classes` has existed since 2026-08-21** —
`BR-RAT-108`, a model column, a validator (`_customer_class_list`), a writable
field and a served value — and step 1 said *"A charge code carries no
customer-class column, so it cannot be limited to one."* for twenty days.
`ChargeDraft` never gained the key, so the API could READ a code's class scope
and nothing a clerk could reach could SET it.

**The judgement this lane made, because it is ours to make (hard-won law 13):
the control goes on STEP 2, beside the amount it narrows.** The p003 conformance
file names the placement as *"a design call, not a lane's"*; it is settled by two
things already ruled rather than by a new question. B14 rule 38 (PO 2026-09-10)
governs form CONSTRUCTION and leaves *"which fields, in which order, under which
headings"* to the drawing, and the drawing is explicit: *"Customer class narrows
the AMOUNT, so it belongs beside the amount… This step is identity only."* So the
frame wins and the note on step 1 goes rather than being re-worded.

**It is a `ChipMultiSelect`** — B14 rule 9, removable chips plus an add control,
never a wall of checkboxes — and it sits directly ABOVE the class × size price
grid, because those two are the pair a clerk confuses: one says WHO the code
reaches, the other what each of them PAYS. The grid's own help line said *"Who
the charge reaches is set on the previous step"* and pointed at a control that
did not exist; it now reads *"…is set above"* and is true.

**An empty list is a real answer and the field says so.** `[]` means EVERY class
(`DEF-273`'s inclusion list), so the empty state reads `Every customer type`
rather than looking blank — a blank box would send a clerk hunting for eight
boxes to tick.

### 2 · THE TYPE IS A SELECT, AND `What the type decides` IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED

The drawing asks for one select plus a three-column comparison table; the product
shipped five radio cards in a `grid-cols-4`, so **`Adjustment` wrapped onto a
second row on its own** from the day `OQ-287` added the fifth type. B14 rule 8
governs a select's chevron and settles nothing about which control a field should
be, so the drawing wins here and the divergence register in `CR-087-p003` records
that reading.

**Every cell of the table is derived.** The rows are `CHARGE_TYPES` (the same
list the select offers) and the third column is `sectionsForType`, extracted from
`stepTwoSections` so step 1's promise and step 2's behaviour are ONE mapping.
Typing that table into a component or a catalogue would be the second list
`CLAUDE.md`'s hand-typed-list law exists to prevent — a sixth type would appear
in the picker and never in the table, silently.

⚠ **THE DRAWN `Adjustment` SENTENCE IS SHORTENED.** The frame writes *"Nothing
type-specific: an adjustment has no recurrence, no deposit and no trigger."* —
thirteen words for a FACT, where B14 rule 33 caps one at six. **The cap wins**
(rule 38's own principle, and the same call the tax lane made today); the
reasoning it drops is in the component's docstring. The frame's `NOT DRIVEN BY
TYPE` note is likewise two short sentences rather than one of twenty-five.

### 3 · B14 RULE 10 WAS **UNMEETABLE**, SO THE FIX IS IN THE KIT

The frame marks `TYPE*`, `HOW THE AMOUNT IS WORKED OUT*` and `AMOUNT*`. None
carried an asterisk, and only one of the three was a screen-level miss:

* `TYPE` spelled its label as a bare `<span>` instead of the kit's `FieldLabel`,
  so **no asterisk and no `aria-required` could be emitted at all**. Becoming a
  `SelectField` fixes it as a side effect of item 2.
* `AMOUNT` could not be marked **by any caller anywhere in Plans & Rates**:
  `MoneyTextField` declared no `required` prop and never passed one to the
  `TextField` underneath. That is B14's own `DEF-712` shape — *"a rule that
  cannot be obeyed renders into the same green as a rule nobody has got to
  yet"* — one component along.

**So the prop is ADDED TO THE KIT (B14 rule 36's own remedy), OPTIONAL**, and
the four call sites that do not pass it render byte-for-byte what they rendered
before. The amount **drops** the marker when the per-size table owns the figure:
`resolve_charge_codes` refuses a code stating both, so an asterisk over the
read-only box would ask for something the server would then refuse.

### 4 · THE `Plans` TAB IS BUILT, AND IT COUNTS **BOTH** ROUTES

PO ruling of today: *"build"*. `GET /charges/{id}/plans` is the read that did not
exist, and it serves the four drawn columns — `PLAN · PLAN CODE · REACHED BY ·
UNITS`.

⚠ **THE SECOND ROUTE IS THE FINDING, NOT THE FEATURE.** `charge_used_by` counts
`plan_charge_rules` and nothing else. `BR-RAT-088` gave the charge code the base
amount, so a code that DECLARES itself its service's base is read by every plan
carrying a rate schedule for that service **and named by none of them** — the
tile therefore reads `0` over a code that prices every connection on its service.
`charge_reach_plan_ids` returns both sets and each row names its own route as a
WORD; a screen that read the route off the blank code cell would decide a fact
the server already knows.

**`charge_used_by` is deliberately untouched.** It feeds the DELETE lock
(`services.delete_charge`), and widening a lock is a different decision from
widening a screen count.

⚠ **B14 RULE 16 WINS OVER THE DRAWING ON THE FOOTER; THE DRAWING WINS ON WHAT
THE COUNT MEANS.** The frame draws no pagination at all. `NFR-3` is a
`CLAUDE.md` requirement rather than a preference and the selector returns a
QUERYSET, so the envelope's `count` is a SQL `COUNT` over the whole set. What the
drawing DOES decide is the denominator — *"how many were checked out of how many
CARRYING THIS CODE, never out of every plan in the utility"* — which is exactly
what the served count is.

⚠ **AND THE `CODE` COLUMN IS HEADED `Plan code`.** The frame heads it `CODE` on a
screen whose every other surface uses `CODE` for the CHARGE code; the p016 file
already records the collision. One word, and it stops a clerk reading a plan's
code as the charge's.

### 5 · `?tab=audit` NOW OPENS THE AUDIT TAB, AND THE ADDRESS STILL DOES NOT MOVE

PO ruling of today: *"Change the label, keep the address"*. Half of it was already
done and that is why it was worth asking — the charge's tab has READ `Audit` in
all eleven catalogues since the rename while its address is `versions`, so every
document, drawing and person naturally writes `?tab=audit` **and that landed on
the Overview, silently**. `definitionTabFrom` cannot tell a mistyped tab from a
synonym.

**A history spelling the kind does not use now resolves to the one it does, in
BOTH directions** — a `?tab=versions` link to a DISCOUNT, written before that
kind was renamed on 2026-09-08, lands on its Overview for the identical reason.
`selectTab` still writes the kind's OWN id back, so the address a clerk copies
out of the bar is unchanged. Only what is ACCEPTED widened.

### 6 · WHAT THIS LANE DID **NOT** BUILD, AND WHY EACH ONE IS DELIBERATE

* **The four behaviour ticks stay STACKED.** The drawing puts them on one row and
  the PO reported that exact layout as broken alignment on this exact screen
  (`DEF-2356`). **The drawing is asking for the defect back.** No change.
* **Money shows TWO decimals.** The blueprint draws `$45.0000` frame after frame;
  hard rule 2 and the PO's ruling of today both say two. No figure moved.
* **The `WHAT THIS COSTS` note is NOT built.** It tells a utility to keep
  `CONN-RES` / `CONN-IND` as a workaround for a column that landed on 2026-09-08.
  Building it would re-publish a solved problem as a live instruction.
* **The `Audit` tab body is NOT built and is NOT stubbed** — see the sizing
  below. There is nowhere to store a reason and no version object to hang one on,
  so a stub would be a screen promising a record the product does not keep.
* **The step-3 comparison table and the `WHY THIS CHANGED` box are NOT built**,
  for the same reason and one more: the drawn `SAVING` column must render a money
  value the browser has been given no display string for, and choosing one in a
  component is client-side money arithmetic on a value the server owns — which is
  what `DEF-364` was.

### 7 · THE `Audit` TAB, SIZED HONESTLY RATHER THAN STUBBED

**It is a migration and a write path before it is a screen**, and it is the same
piece of work as step 3's `WHY THIS CHANGED` box — the blueprint says so in its
own words: *"the two changes only work together"*.

**There is no version object for a charge code anywhere in this product.**
`apps/rating/models.py` declares `TariffVersion` and `PlanVersion` and nothing for
a charge; `Charge` carries no `effective_from`; the migration folder holds nothing
for one; `api.py` has no `charges/{id}/versions` beside the two that do exist.

**What it needs, in order:**

1. a `ChargeVersion` model + migration — `charge`, `effective_from`, the priced
   state, `change_reason` and the actor as `{id, name}` on the row (`DEF-367`, so
   the `BY` column survives the `audit_log` retention prune);
2. a write path: `update_charge` files a version rather than only mutating the
   row, which is where the reason box's value lands;
3. `GET /charges/{id}/versions`, paged (`NFR-3` — a code repriced monthly for ten
   years is 120 rows);
4. the screen, which is then the smallest part of it.

⚠ **AND ONE THING THE PO SHOULD SEE BEFORE ANY OF IT IS BUILT.** The drawn table
puts an `AMOUNT` column against each version. A charge code that prices per size
and per class has **no single amount** — that is what `CR-087` A1 shipped — so a
one-figure history column would be honest for a scalar code and wrong for every
sized one. The question is one sentence: *when a charge code prices eight
different amounts, what should the history column show?*

### 8 · THE ELEVEN CATALOGUES

27 keys added, 3 retired (`customerClassPending`, `customerClassLabel`,
`typeSetPending`), 1 re-worded, all through `10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py` so parity
holds or nothing is written. **Every new line is `NATIVE-REVIEW-OWED`** (B14 rule
35) — one author, not eleven fluent ones.

## 2026-09-10 — THE DISCOUNTS FIX WAVE: TWO JUDGMENTS THE RULES RAN OUT ON, AND TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT

Written while cutting the Discounts tab onto blueprint pages 65–84 and building
`CR-091-BRC01` inside it. Neither judgment below was put to the PO: hard-won law
13 puts a judgment call squarely in the set of things we decide and write down,
and re-asking a question the PO has already answered once is how the repo
acquires two genuine rulings that contradict each other.

### 1 · `All services` IS A SCOPE VALUE OF ITS OWN, AND IT IS NOT A SPELLING OF `Subtotal before taxes`

**The ruling being built** is decision §7 of earlier today: *"Add a new choice. -
one or more services from drop down; All services or sepecific services; this is
correct"*, with `one_service` NOT widened.

⚠ **THE PAIR HAS TO GO SOMEWHERE, AND EVERY PLACE IT COULD GO HAD A COST.** The
discount already had a five-value scope (`whole_bill · one_service · usage_only ·
base_only · named_codes`). Two readings were open and they are not equivalent:

| reading | what it costs |
|---|---|
| the pair is a SECOND control, composed with the scope | fifteen scope × service states, each with its own money meaning, none of them ruled — and `one_service` becomes redundant with `whole_bill` + one service |
| the pair is TWO MORE SCOPE VALUES | `All services` sits on one dropdown beside `Subtotal before taxes`, and a reader has to be told how they differ |

**The second was chosen**, and the deciding argument is that the brief for this
wave states the engine change as *"`line.service == rule.applies_to_service`
BECOMES a membership test"* — a change INSIDE `_scoped_base`'s scope branches,
which is only true of the second reading. A composed second dimension would have
had to narrow every branch, `whole_bill`'s running-subtotal shortcut included,
which is a money change nobody ruled.

⚠ **AND `all_services` ADDS NO ARITHMETIC AT ALL, WHICH IS WHY IT IS SAFE.** It
is `_scoped_base`'s existing fall-through — `selected = list(lines)` — given a
name a clerk can choose. **The difference from `whole_bill` is real, is already
documented in that function, and is worth exactly one worked figure:**

> On the design's own §A4 S1 bill (electric `$121.10` · water `$60.80` · sewer
> `$8.00`, subtotal **`$189.90`**), after a `$10.00` fixed reduction has run
> first, a 10% discount takes **`$17.99`** on `whole_bill` (10% of the reduced
> `$179.90`) and **`$18.99`** on `all_services` (10% of the undiscounted
> `$189.90`). **One dollar, on one bill, decided by which of the two a clerk
> picks.** With one discount on the bill they are identical to the cent, which
> is what makes the addition safe.

`whole_bill` is the ONE scope the engine runs against the reducing subtotal;
every other scope takes the undiscounted sum of the lines it selects. That was
true before today and is asserted in `test_cr091_discount_names_its_services.py`
in both directions.

⚠ **WHAT IS FOR THE PO, AND IT IS A COPY CALL RATHER THAN A RULING:** the scope
dropdown now offers seven options, two of which — *Subtotal before taxes* and
*All services* — read similarly and differ only when discounts stack. If those
two words are wrong for a clerk, that is a one-line change to two catalogue
entries and nothing behind them moves.

### 2 · AN EMPTY SPECIFIC LIST IS REFUSED BY THE SERVER, NOT HIDDEN BY THE SCREEN

The PO ruled the empty list an unfinished form. **Where the refusal LIVES was not
ruled**, and the two choices are not equivalent: a client-side block is a refusal
one caller honours, and `PRB-14` plus `DEF-384` already say in this module that
*a client that cannot express a state is not a server that refuses it*. So
`_validate_version` GATE 3 refuses it for every caller and the wizard renders the
field error against the chip control. `BR-RAT-963` is the rule id.

### 3 · TWO THINGS THE BLUEPRINT DRAWS THAT WERE DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT

Both are named here so the next lane does not read the absence as an oversight.

**(a) The four Overview KPI tiles were NOT re-cut.** Three of the four built
tiles differ from the drawn four, and `CR-087-p076` records why the drawing
cannot simply be followed: its own CONTRADICTIONS §1 shows **three of the drawn
four repeat a fact drawn again below on the same frame**, and the drawn tile-2
denominator `of 86 eligible` is `PRB-20`, whose own card says the figure cannot
be stated until an eligibility read exists. The PO ruled the *units-vs-accounts*
half today (*"it should be on accounts; discount is given to accounts"*) and
tile 2 already counts accounts and says so. **Which four tiles is a question
p076 puts to the PO and nobody has answered**, and a tile set is a number a
finance lead reads. Left as it is, and raised.

⚠ **THE ADJACENT HALF OF THAT RULING IS NOT DONE AND CANNOT BE DONE HERE.** The
PO also said the `ELIGIBLE UNITS` column must be re-read *"because eligible and
enrolled must count the same kind of thing or the fraction is meaningless"*. The
Plans-tab table that column belongs to **is not built at all** (`CR-087-p079`
§1 — the tab renders one sentence about its own absence, and three of its four
columns need reads no route answers). The only live surface is Overview tile 3,
`Offered to · 86 units on a plan carrying it`, which counts UNITS beside a tile
counting ACCOUNTS. Making it count accounts needs a server read that does not
exist. **Recorded, not guessed.**

**(b) The absence bar and the consequence panels were NOT unified.** `CR-087-p074`
§4 names one idea with four hand-rolled spellings; this wave deleted one of the
four outright (step 4's second-approval panel, above) and left the rest.
**The reason is a collision, not a disagreement:** the kit piece they need —
`AccentBand`, a legend over one sentence behind a left accent rule — was added to
`components/TextBits.tsx` by a sibling lane **this afternoon and is not on the
branch**, and `DefinitionDetailPage.tsx`, where two of the remaining three live,
carries `+284/−9` of that lane's uncommitted work. Composing a symbol that is not
on the branch is hard-won law 2 wearing a fix's clothes, and editing that file
would revert a lane mid-rewrite. **It is one commit's work once `AccentBand`
lands.**

### 8 · POSTSCRIPT, FOUND BY CLICKING — THE CLIENT AND THE SERVER MEANT DIFFERENT THINGS BY *IN FORCE* (`DEF-RAT-4838`)

**Everything above was green — 656 front-end cases, 42 backend cases, `tsc`,
eslint, the gates — and the browser found this in one PATCH.**

`TaxWizard`'s `taxIsInForce` is a DATE test: active, started, not ended. Its
docstring argues for it carefully and the argument was right *when there was no
correction route*: reading `status === "active"` would have made the five seeded
Texas rates uneditable, and they carry no `effective_from` at all.

`update_tax`'s refusal is **`if blocked and not tax.is_draft`** — every non-draft
tax, window open or not.

**So the screen offered `Save changes` on exactly the taxes the server refuses.**
Measured on the built product: `PATCH /taxes/{id}` with `{"effective_from":
"2026-01-01"}` on *Local · Bexar County* came back
**`409 BIZ-IMMUTABLE · rating.taxes.in_force_edit_refused`** while the wizard
rendered an ordinary edit with no correction panel and no reason box. A clerk
meets a refusal nothing on the page could have predicted.

**THE SERVER'S LINE GOVERNS, AND THIS FILE'S OWN SENTENCE SAYS WHY:** *"a
client-side refusal is not a refusal"*. The wizard's correction mode is now
`status !== "draft"`, which is what `tax_row` already serves.

⚠ **AND THE OBJECTION `taxIsInForce`'s DOCSTRING RAISES NO LONGER APPLIES.** It
feared making those five rates *uneditable*. They are not uneditable — they are
**CORRECTABLE**, through the documented route the server accepts, which is the
door this same day's work wired. `taxIsInForce` is unchanged and still true of
what it says; it is simply not the question this screen asks.

⚠ **NOTHING BUT A BROWSER COULD HAVE FOUND IT.** Two layers each held a correct,
carefully reasoned expression of one rule and neither could see the other; a test
on either side alone passes. That is hard-won law 6 with a live server attached
— the walk is `10-scripts/cr087_tax_tabs_walkthrough.mjs`.

## 2026-09-10 — `CR-087` · THE CHARGE CODES TAB AGAINST ITS DRAWN BLUEPRINT

Maintenance, not build (`22-product-maintenance-process.md`): a clerk can create,
edit and read a charge code today, so every finding here is a defect against a
screen people already use. Three root-cause rows: `DEF-RAT-4830`,
`DEF-RAT-4831`, `DEF-RAT-4832`.

### 1 · THE CUSTOMER-CLASS CONTROL GOES ON **STEP 2**, AND THE REFUSAL IS DELETED

**`charges.applies_to_customer_classes` has existed since 2026-08-21** —
`BR-RAT-108`, a model column, a validator (`_customer_class_list`), a writable
field and a served value — and step 1 said *"A charge code carries no
customer-class column, so it cannot be limited to one."* for twenty days.
`ChargeDraft` never gained the key, so the API could READ a code's class scope
and nothing a clerk could reach could SET it.

**The judgement this lane made, because it is ours to make (hard-won law 13):
the control goes on STEP 2, beside the amount it narrows.** The p003 conformance
file names the placement as *"a design call, not a lane's"*; it is settled by two
things already ruled rather than by a new question. B14 rule 38 (PO 2026-09-10)
governs form CONSTRUCTION and leaves *"which fields, in which order, under which
headings"* to the drawing, and the drawing is explicit: *"Customer class narrows
the AMOUNT, so it belongs beside the amount… This step is identity only."* So the
frame wins and the note on step 1 goes rather than being re-worded.

**It is a `ChipMultiSelect`** — B14 rule 9, removable chips plus an add control,
never a wall of checkboxes — and it sits directly ABOVE the class × size price
grid, because those two are the pair a clerk confuses: one says WHO the code
reaches, the other what each of them PAYS. The grid's own help line said *"Who
the charge reaches is set on the previous step"* and pointed at a control that
did not exist; it now reads *"…is set above"* and is true.

**An empty list is a real answer and the field says so.** `[]` means EVERY class
(`DEF-273`'s inclusion list), so the empty state reads `Every customer type`
rather than looking blank — a blank box would send a clerk hunting for eight
boxes to tick.

### 2 · THE TYPE IS A SELECT, AND `What the type decides` IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED

The drawing asks for one select plus a three-column comparison table; the product
shipped five radio cards in a `grid-cols-4`, so **`Adjustment` wrapped onto a
second row on its own** from the day `OQ-287` added the fifth type. B14 rule 8
governs a select's chevron and settles nothing about which control a field should
be, so the drawing wins here and the divergence register in `CR-087-p003` records
that reading.

**Every cell of the table is derived.** The rows are `CHARGE_TYPES` (the same
list the select offers) and the third column is `sectionsForType`, extracted from
`stepTwoSections` so step 1's promise and step 2's behaviour are ONE mapping.
Typing that table into a component or a catalogue would be the second list
`CLAUDE.md`'s hand-typed-list law exists to prevent — a sixth type would appear
in the picker and never in the table, silently.

⚠ **THE DRAWN `Adjustment` SENTENCE IS SHORTENED.** The frame writes *"Nothing
type-specific: an adjustment has no recurrence, no deposit and no trigger."* —
thirteen words for a FACT, where B14 rule 33 caps one at six. **The cap wins**
(rule 38's own principle, and the same call the tax lane made today); the
reasoning it drops is in the component's docstring. The frame's `NOT DRIVEN BY
TYPE` note is likewise two short sentences rather than one of twenty-five.

### 3 · B14 RULE 10 WAS **UNMEETABLE**, SO THE FIX IS IN THE KIT

The frame marks `TYPE*`, `HOW THE AMOUNT IS WORKED OUT*` and `AMOUNT*`. None
carried an asterisk, and only one of the three was a screen-level miss:

* `TYPE` spelled its label as a bare `<span>` instead of the kit's `FieldLabel`,
  so **no asterisk and no `aria-required` could be emitted at all**. Becoming a
  `SelectField` fixes it as a side effect of item 2.
* `AMOUNT` could not be marked **by any caller anywhere in Plans & Rates**:
  `MoneyTextField` declared no `required` prop and never passed one to the
  `TextField` underneath. That is B14's own `DEF-712` shape — *"a rule that
  cannot be obeyed renders into the same green as a rule nobody has got to
  yet"* — one component along.

**So the prop is ADDED TO THE KIT (B14 rule 36's own remedy), OPTIONAL**, and
the four call sites that do not pass it render byte-for-byte what they rendered
before. The amount **drops** the marker when the per-size table owns the figure:
`resolve_charge_codes` refuses a code stating both, so an asterisk over the
read-only box would ask for something the server would then refuse.

### 4 · THE `Plans` TAB IS BUILT, AND IT COUNTS **BOTH** ROUTES

PO ruling of today: *"build"*. `GET /charges/{id}/plans` is the read that did not
exist, and it serves the four drawn columns — `PLAN · PLAN CODE · REACHED BY ·
UNITS`.

⚠ **THE SECOND ROUTE IS THE FINDING, NOT THE FEATURE.** `charge_used_by` counts
`plan_charge_rules` and nothing else. `BR-RAT-088` gave the charge code the base
amount, so a code that DECLARES itself its service's base is read by every plan
carrying a rate schedule for that service **and named by none of them** — the
tile therefore reads `0` over a code that prices every connection on its service.
`charge_reach_plan_ids` returns both sets and each row names its own route as a
WORD; a screen that read the route off the blank code cell would decide a fact
the server already knows.

**`charge_used_by` is deliberately untouched.** It feeds the DELETE lock
(`services.delete_charge`), and widening a lock is a different decision from
widening a screen count.

⚠ **B14 RULE 16 WINS OVER THE DRAWING ON THE FOOTER; THE DRAWING WINS ON WHAT
THE COUNT MEANS.** The frame draws no pagination at all. `NFR-3` is a
`CLAUDE.md` requirement rather than a preference and the selector returns a
QUERYSET, so the envelope's `count` is a SQL `COUNT` over the whole set. What the
drawing DOES decide is the denominator — *"how many were checked out of how many
CARRYING THIS CODE, never out of every plan in the utility"* — which is exactly
what the served count is.

⚠ **AND THE `CODE` COLUMN IS HEADED `Plan code`.** The frame heads it `CODE` on a
screen whose every other surface uses `CODE` for the CHARGE code; the p016 file
already records the collision. One word, and it stops a clerk reading a plan's
code as the charge's.

### 5 · `?tab=audit` NOW OPENS THE AUDIT TAB, AND THE ADDRESS STILL DOES NOT MOVE

PO ruling of today: *"Change the label, keep the address"*. Half of it was already
done and that is why it was worth asking — the charge's tab has READ `Audit` in
all eleven catalogues since the rename while its address is `versions`, so every
document, drawing and person naturally writes `?tab=audit` **and that landed on

**A history spelling the kind does not use now resolves to the one it does, in

kind was renamed on 2026-09-08, lands on its Overview for the identical reason.
`selectTab` still writes the kind's OWN id back, so the address a clerk copies
out of the bar is unchanged. Only what is ACCEPTED widened.
