## 2026-09-10 — A HISTORY QUESTION ANSWERED FROM A STALE HEAD, TWICE REPORTED TO THE PO AS A FALSE ALARM — AND THE SAME TRAP HIT INDEPENDENTLY BY A SECOND LANE THE SAME DAY

### 1 · WHAT HAPPENED

The CR-087 rate-schedules lane reported that a sibling had resurrected five
catalogue keys it retired in `f429885d3`, and that `push_paths.sh` would refuse
the sibling's catalogue push until they re-derived — *"that refusal is the system
working, not a problem to route around."*

**The coordinating lane checked, and told the PO twice it was a false alarm. The
lane was right and the coordinator was wrong, three times over.** The final
check read all five keys as `branch:0 tree:1` — absent from the branch, present
in the shared tree — which is exactly what the lane had said.

### 2 · WHY THE CHECK LIED, AND IT IS NOT THE HEURISTIC

The check asked *has this key ever been retired?* with

    git log -S '"<key>"' HEAD -- 07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json

and **local `HEAD` was 15 commits behind the tip, so `f429885d3` was not
reachable from it.** The walk returned zero commits. Zero was then read as *the
key is simply new* rather than as *my history is too short to answer*.

The first diagnosis blamed a threshold in the heuristic (it wanted ≥2 commits
touching the key). That was wrong too. **The heuristic never ran on a history
that contained the answer**, so no threshold could have saved it.

### 3 · THE SECOND LANE, INDEPENDENTLY, THE SAME DAY

The CR-087 discounts lane self-reported the identical fault in its own words:

> My content-addressed check reported five catalogue keys as "never on the
> branch" because `git log -S` defaults to HEAD and mine was four commits
> behind. That is law 12's trap operating on a check written to satisfy law 12.

Two lanes, two independently written checks, one root cause, one day. That moves
this from a lane's mistake to a shape the repo fails in, which is why it is here
and not only in the register.

### 4 · THE RULING — HOW A HISTORY QUERY MUST BE WRITTEN WHEN IT IS EVIDENCE

**Any `git log`, `git log -S` or `git show` used as EVIDENCE names an explicit
ref that is the remote tip, never bare `HEAD`.** `git log -S '"<key>"'
origin/<branch> -- <path>`. `HEAD` is a local pointer that rewinds, lags, and is
moved by every sibling's push; law 12 already says *do not believe a grep* before
checking it, and **a history query is a grep over commits**.

**And a zero result from a history walk is not a negative finding until the walk
is proved able to see a known-positive commit.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor
<the commit that should be found> <the ref you queried>` is the one-line proof,
and it is the same discipline as hard-won law 7: *ask what would make this check
pass wrongly.* A walk that cannot reach the answer returns the same empty output
as a walk that reached it and found nothing.

Filed as `DEF-GOV-4839` (high). `10-scripts/check_head_current.sh` would have
caught the precondition and was not run before the query; that is the habit, and
it is cheaper than any of this.

### 5 · A SECOND MEASUREMENT ERROR, FOUND WHILE CORRECTING THE FIRST

Acting on the above, the coordinator warned three running lanes that their files
held reverts, quoting figures like *"the defect register is −12 rows"*. **Those
figures came from `diff | grep -c '^<'`, and a diff reports a CHANGED line and a
MOVED line as one `<` plus one `>`.** It is not a loss count.

Re-measured content-addressed — by id SET rather than by line position — the
register's true state was **one** stale row and six stray line endings, not
twelve lost rows:

| what the count said | what was actually wrong |
|---|---|
| 12 register rows lost | ONE duplicate `DEF-RAT-4826`, which the branch had already renumbered to `DEF-RAT-4834`; plus six rows still carrying CRLF from the 2026-09-06 `csv`-writer round-trip |
| 3 catalogue keys lost, in all eleven | ZERO — the tree's wording was the discounts lane's live correction and the BRANCH was the stale side |
| 71 lines lost from `ChargeCodeWizard.tsx` | ZERO — the lane had already synced its own pushed commit |

`sync_stale_tree.py` phrases its advisory verdict the same way — *"loses N
line(s) the tip has"* — so it overstates on any append-only or reordered file.
The verdict is explicitly advisory and the tool acts on neither side of it, so
nothing was destroyed; the cost was a wrong number relayed to three lanes as
fact, and three correction messages. Filed as `DEF-GOV-4840` (medium).

**The rule that falls out of both: state a difference content-addressed, not
positionally.** For a register, compare id sets. For a catalogue, compare keys
and then values. A count of diff `<` lines answers *how many lines differ*, which
is not the question anyone was asking.

### 6 · THE NEAR-MISS THAT A TOOL CAUGHT, AND THE HABIT IT VINDICATES

Acting on that same bad count, the coordinator began restoring three catalogue
keys — `rating.discountWizard.budgetCapHelp`,
`rating.plan.discounts.secondApprovalNoBudget`,
`rating.plan.discounts.secondApprovalUnknown` — from the branch over the tree.

**`i18n_fanin.apply()` refused on its no-silent-overwrite guard**, which exists so
that *a lane cannot quietly re-word another lane's message*. Reading the two
versions side by side showed the tree's text was the discounts lane's live
implementation of the PO's ruling that a second approval applies **only where a
threshold is set** — while the branch text still said an uncapped discount
*always* needs one, the behaviour the ruling removed. **The branch was stale and
the working tree was right**, the exact inverse of the assumption the restore was
built on.

This is law 11's *use the tool that owns the file* paying for itself: a hand-
rolled write would have reverted a PO ruling into eleven catalogues, silently,
with parity intact and every test green.

### 7 · WHAT WAS ACTUALLY REPAIRED, AND WHY NONE OF IT NEEDED PUSHING

`sync_stale_tree.py` restored the 7 files that were provably stale and untouched.
The register's duplicate id and its six CRLF endings were spliced byte-precisely
in the working tree. The five retired keys were removed from all eleven
catalogues, parity holding at 15,428 each; nothing in `07-frontend/src` read
them, and `f429885d3`'s own subject says they were *"five keys for panels this
lane did not build"*.

**Every one of those repairs moved the tree TOWARD the branch, so none of them
was a change to push** — the branch was already correct in all three places. The
only thing this lane owed the branch was the two defect rows above.


## 2026-09-10 — `CR-087` · FOUR PO RULINGS: THE BASE-CHARGE CHAIN NAMED END TO END, THE PLAN PRICES NOTHING, AND A FACT IS SHOWN ONCE

### 1 · THE CHAIN, VERBATIM

> *"Charge Code -> base charge -> rate schedule -> plans - that is the path -
> please confirm your understanding"*

and, on the plan's charge step:

> *"Price -> charge code -> add 1 by 1 into plan - as per utility requirements.
> all Rules and price is defined in Charge code itself"*

**Both are CONFIRMATIONS of `BR-RAT-088`, not changes to it.** The source and the
arithmetic do not move. What they settle is the step the rule left implicit and
the question a lane stopped on.

**THE MIDDLE STEP IS THE RATE SCHEDULE, AND IT IS A ROUTE RATHER THAN A STORE.**
A plan does not read a charge code directly. It attaches a **rate schedule** for
a service, and that schedule is what fixes the two facts that narrow *which*
charge-code figure applies — the **service** and the **size ladder** — alongside
the account's customer class. `gather._tariff_config_for` already works exactly
this way: it calls `_base_charge_code_for(service_code, customer_class=…,
size_class=…)` from inside the schedule's own context, *"where the three
narrowing facts already are"*. So the ruling describes what is built.

**The schedule is never a second place to type a figure.** `tariff_versions.
base_charge` stays retired, as `BR-RAT-088` already says. This is the same shape
as the PO's minimum ruling of the same day — *"set it in rates and use it in
plans - thats it - this is rule"* — and the principle under both is one sentence:
**one place to type, every other surface reads through.**

### 2 · `THEN SET THE PRICE` vs `A PLAN COMPOSES; IT DOES NOT PRICE`

The plans lane stopped and refused to decide this by fiat, correctly. The PO's
own earlier words were *"I want search from drop down, multi select and then set
the price"*; step 4's drawn sentence is *"A plan composes; it does not price."*

**RULED: the plan wins nothing.** *"all Rules and price is defined in Charge code
itself."* The plan's charge step searches, picks and adds charge codes; **the
amount column shows the charge code's own figure and is READ-ONLY there.**
*"then set the price"* means setting it on the charge code, which is where the
clerk goes to change it.

⚠ **`multi select` AND `add 1 by 1` ARE RECONCILED, NOT IN CONFLICT — and this
is written down rather than put back to the PO (law 13).** The picker allows
several codes to be selected; each selected code lands as **its own row** in the
plan's table, which is what *"add 1 by 1 … as per utility requirements"*
describes. The PO had already confirmed this exact interaction on 2026-09-10:
*"Attaching charges to a plan - they way you ahve show is correct; interction is
also correct."* Nothing here needs re-asking.

### 3 · WHAT IS NOT RULED, AND STAYS RESERVED

**The DROP of `plan_services.base_charge` was not addressed and remains held by
`BR-RAT-120`'s rollback clause.** Verified rather than assumed this session:
`SBH_BILLING_RESOLUTION_STEPS=` emptied is the documented one-line rollback, and
`test_def2923_base_code_gate_follows_the_switch::TC3` proves the charge-code gate
**does not fire at all** in that state — the deployment is *"back to the
behaviour that shipped before the ruling"*. So the column is the ONLY base source
on a rolled-back deployment, and dropping it would bill **$0.00 for base on every
line** there, which is `DEF-154` exactly.

**The user-visible half of the ruling is already true and needs no change.** The
plan sets nothing and shows the charge code's figure; the column is
display-and-fallback only. **Dropping it is cleanup, not correctness** — the only
irreversible step in the whole chain — so the recorded judgment is to LEAVE IT
until `CR-057`'s rollback is formally withdrawn, and to re-raise it then rather
than now.

### 4 · A FACT IS SHOWN ONCE — THE TAX DETAIL SCREEN

The taxes lane built `STATUS` as KPI tile 4 *because it is drawn*, while the
same status already renders as the **pill under the title**; the blueprint draws
it twice and contradicts itself. Put to the PO in those words. **RULED, verbatim:
*"show only one status"*.**

**Applied: the pill stays, the STATUS tile goes** — the pill is the drawn
position for a lifecycle state on every other detail screen in Plans & Rates, so
removing the tile keeps the screen consistent with its neighbours rather than
with itself.

⚠ **NO B14 RULE IS MINTED FROM THIS, DELIBERATELY, ON THE RULE-30 PRECEDENT.**
On 2026-08-30 the PO answered a modal question with *"for estimate reads - keep
it modal"* — the INSTANCE and not the rule — and B14 rule 30 was declined in the
same sentence, the number left unused on purpose. *"Show only one status"* is the
same shape. It is recorded as a ruling and applied to the screens where the same
duplication exists; **turning it into binding UI law is a separate act that needs
the PO to rule it in**, and inventing one from an instance is exactly what that
precedent forbids.

### 5 · THE DISCOUNT OVERVIEW TILES — THE SAME RULING SETTLES MOST OF IT

The lane asked *"which four tiles"*, and the coordinator's first explanation was
not understandable — a fair complaint, because it named a problem without showing
it. Measured against the drawn spec, three of the four repeat a fact that appears
elsewhere **on the same tab**:

| tile | what it shows | where the same fact already appears |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · `10%` **VALUE**, *of the subtotal before taxes* | the value | panel two, row 1: `VALUE` = `10% of the subtotal before taxes` — **word for word** |
| 2 · `31` **ENROLLED UNITS**, *of 86 eligible* | take-up | **nowhere else — this one is unique** |
| 3 · `$2,180.00` **BUDGET REMAINING**, *of $5,000.00 this year* | the budget | panel two, last row: `BUDGET` = `$2,180.00 left of $5,000.00 a year` — **same two figures** |
| 4 · `Active` **STATUS** | the status | the **pill under the title** already says `ACTIVE` |

**JUDGMENT, recorded rather than re-asked.** Tiles 1 and 3 are **kept**: a KPI
strip exists to summarise, and a figure appearing both at a glance and in the
detail panel below is what a summary IS, not a duplication to remove. **Tile 4 is
removed**, because it is not a summary of a panel — it is a second rendering of
the *pill*, which is the identical fault the PO has just ruled on for taxes, and
one ruling should not produce two answers on two screens in the same module. That
leaves **three tiles**, and no fourth is invented: `SUBSIDY GRANTED TO DATE` is
explicitly not drawn, and a monthly programme cost is what the screen's own
absence bar says nothing computes.


## 2026-09-10 — CORRECTION: THE DISCOUNT OVERVIEW HAS NO STATUS TILE, SO ONE OF THE "TWO SCREEN CHANGES" WAS ONE

### 1 · WHAT I GOT WRONG

The entry above — *"FOUR PO RULINGS"*, §5 — put a table to the PO showing the
discount Overview's four tiles as `VALUE · ENROLLED UNITS · BUDGET REMAINING ·
STATUS`, and concluded that tile 4 duplicated the status pill and should go.

**That table describes the DRAWING, not the code.** The built strip, read from
`definitionDetail.tsx` `DEFINITION_KPI_LABEL_KEYS.discount` and the `tiles(…)`
call in `presentDiscount`, is:

| # | built tile | value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `PLANS THAT OFFER IT` | `row.plans` |
| 2 | `ENROLLED` | `row.enrolled` (accounts) |
| 3 | `OFFERED TO` | `row.offered_units` |
| 4 | `TYPE` | `type`, or `type · scope` |

**There is no status tile on the discount Overview and there never was.** The
discount's `row.status` reaches the shell once, as `statusValue` for the pill.

⚠ **THE ERROR IS THE SAME ONE THIS SESSION FILED TWICE ALREADY** — a confident
statement made from a document rather than from the artefact it describes. It
would have been caught by the skill's own step 7.5, *"read the current component
before changing it"*, which is written for exactly this and which I reached only
after telling the PO the change was needed.

### 2 · WHAT FOLLOWS, AND IT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN A QUESTION

**The discount strip is LEFT ALONE.** Three reasons, recorded so the next lane
does not reopen it:

1. **The ruling does not reach it.** *"Show only one status"* is about a fact
   rendered twice. The discount renders its status once.
2. **Removing tile 4 would be acting on a GENERALISATION of an instance ruling**,
   which is precisely what the rule-30 precedent forbids and what the entry above
   already committed us not to do. Tile 4 repeats the kicker's type WORD but adds
   the scope, which the kicker does not carry, so it is not even a clean
   duplicate.
3. **The three drawn tiles I proposed keeping are not built either.** `VALUE` and
   `BUDGET REMAINING` are drawn and absent; the built tiles are counts. Rebuilding
   the strip to the drawing is a real piece of work with its own conformance
   reading — not a tidy-up to fold into a status fix — and it is recorded in
   `CR-087-p076-discount-overview.md` §10 rather than done in passing.

### 3 · SO THE TAX CHANGE IS THE ONLY SCREEN CHANGE THE RULINGS ASKED FOR

Built: `rating.definition.kpi.tax.status` removed from the label list and from
the `presentTax` call; `DefinitionKpis` widened from a strict 4-tuple to a
3-or-4 union, still refusing a fifth; the key retired from all eleven catalogues
through `i18n_fanin.retire()`, parity holding at **15,422** each. `KPIStrip`
takes `readonly KpiTile[]` and lays out on `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px,
1fr))`, so three tiles fill the row rather than leaving a hole — checked before
the type was touched, not after.

Four assertions moved with it, none deleted: the per-kind count is now a table
(`charge: 4, discount: 4, tax: 3`); *"tile 4 is TEXT on the charge and a rate on
the tax"* reads the LAST tile by position instead of a hard-coded `3`; the tax
slot-3 case asserts the RATE, from the fixture's own `rate_display` rather than a
literal that could drift; and a new case asserts the tax draws its status once.
**25 files, 641 tests, green.**

⚠ **One assertion I wrote and then rewrote, because the first version could not
fail.** It read `expect(tile.label).not.toBe(i18n.t("rating.definition.kpi.tax.
status"))` — but that key is now retired, so `t()` returns the key STRING, and no
real label ever equals it. It would have passed whether or not the tile came
back. It asserts the visible status WORD instead.


## 2026-09-11 — B14 RULE 39: ONE SPACING SCALE AND A FIELD IS LABEL → INPUT → HELPER; AND THE PORTAL IS A CONSUMER SCREEN, SO MOBILE IS NOT OPTIONAL

### 1 · THE RULING, VERBATIM

> *"have a proper padding for each component on the screen. these padding should
> be universally fit for the product… the components are too much close as well
> as manage the margins also."*

and, on forms:

> *"in the forms for the fields. It starts with the field name. then the input
> field, and then it should show the helper text below that input field."*

Delivered with its own specification rather than as a complaint, which is why it
is ratified as stated rather than interpreted:

| token | px | where it is used |
|---|---|---|
| `--sp-1` | 4 | hairline, inside a chip |
| `--sp-2` | 8 | inside a control · cell vertical padding |
| `--sp-3` | 12 | cell horizontal padding · step icon gap |
| `--sp-4` | 16 | between fields, between blocks |
| `--sp-5` | 20 | step side padding · KPI cell side padding |
| `--sp-6` | 24 | between sections · after a wizard rail |
| `--sp-7` | 32 | page bottom |

**No ad-hoc 3 / 7 / 9 / 14 anywhere.** Anchors, all `getComputedStyle` on the
running app: page 24/16/32 · sidebar 240 · topbar 56 · title 40/800 · tabs margin
16 gap 16 · KPI 16/20 gap 6 · th/td 8×12 · rail margin-bottom 24 · step 16×20 gap
12 · `.input` 6×10 min-h 36.

**Field anatomy:** label → input **5px**, input → helper **6px**, field → field
**20px** — ≈ 1 : 1 : 4. ⚠ **DOM order alone is not enough.** The helper must READ
as attached to the input above it and never to the label below it, and a 3/3/9
rhythm destroys that even with correct markup. That is why the three gaps are
ratified as FIGURES rather than as an ordering — the ordering was already
achievable and already wrong.

### 2 · WHAT IS TRUE OF THE CODE AT RATIFICATION, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**No `--sp-N` token exists.** `tokens.css` holds 94 custom properties and not one
of them is a spacing scale; the only dimensional tokens are three radii and two
table font sizes. **B14 carried no spacing rule at all** before this. So the rule
is **entirely unbuilt at the moment it is ratified**, and that is recorded here
rather than left for the first lane to discover.

⚠ **IT IS ALSO UNENFORCED AND WILL STAY SO UNTIL SOMEBODY WRITES A GATE.** No
check in this repo reads computed spacing. The anchors above are `getComputedStyle`
figures, which means the only thing that can verify them is a browser — hard-won
law 6 again, the law with no tool behind it. A gate that reads computed spacing
off the running app is the obvious follow-up and is NOT part of this ruling.

### 3 · THE `R12` COLLISION, RECORDED BEFORE IT MISLEADS ANYBODY

The PO numbered the field-anatomy half **`R12`**. The customer-portal blueprint's
own rules register ALREADY uses `R12`, for *"a database id is never shown; the
account number is the customer's own reference"* — which is itself B14 rule 31
inherited. **Two different rules, one label.** The blueprint's `R` numbers are its
own numbering and are not B14's; this ruling is **B14 rule 39**. The `R12` label
is written into the rule so that a reader meeting it in chat can find it, and so
that nobody later "corrects" rule 39 into the blueprint's R12.

This is the same shape as `OQ-119` being returned for a search for `OQ-1190`
(`DEF-2804`): a citation that resolves to a real, different thing is worse than
one that resolves to nothing.

### 4 · THE POINTER MOVED IN THE SAME COMMIT, DELIBERATELY

`CLAUDE.md` reads **THIRTY-NINE** binding UI rules as of this commit. That line
has been wrong **five separate times**, always in the same direction, because
ratifying a rule and updating the pointer to it are two acts and only the first
feels like the work. Rules 37 and 38 were the first pair moved in the same commit
as the rule; this is the second. It is now the convention, not a courtesy.

### 5 · AND THE PORTAL IS A CONSUMER SCREEN — PO, SAME DAY

> *"also please note this is Consumer web portal - that means we have Mobile and
> Desktop sizes - from responsive point of veiw"*

**This CONFIRMS the audience split already ruled on 2026-09-10** — *"Calrk and
Utility admin is laptop, and desktop application - not mobile; COnsumer can be
both mobile and other screen sizes"* — and it is recorded rather than treated as
a repeat, because it arrives as an instruction about `CR-085`'s lanes
specifically. **Every portal screen is verified at 390 AND 1280, both, always.**
Not "desktop then check narrow": the phone is the design target for a customer
opening their bill, and 1280 is the pair it must also hold at.

⚠ **THAT MAKES RULE 39 A TWO-WIDTH RULE.** A spacing scale is a set of figures,
and figures that are right at 1280 and cramped at 390 satisfy the letter of it
and fail what the PO actually asked for — *"the components are too much close"*.
Every anchor above is checked at BOTH widths.


## 2026-09-11 — `CR-085` · THE 8 SEPTEMBER BLUEPRINT PDF IS THE DESIGN; THE 3 SEPTEMBER WIREFRAME IMAGES ARE SUPERSEDED

### 1 · THE QUESTION, AND WHY IT HAD TO BE ASKED

Lane 2 found it and lane 5 hit it independently: **there are TWO drawings of the
customer portal and the product is built to the older one.**

* `05-prototype/SMARTBillHub Customer Portal Blueprint.pdf` — **8 September**,
  129 pages, 60 screens, read at `2.232.0 · d940f460`.
* `04-docs/05-modules/15-portal/wireframes/CWP-###.png` — **76 images rendered
  from the 3 SEPTEMBER blueprint**, and `14-layout-audit.md` grades screens
  against THOSE.

So a large share of what the lanes measured as "the screen does not match the
drawing" is **the screen matching the EARLIER drawing**. That is not carelessness
by whoever built it, and it must not be filed as if it were.

⚠ **AND NO GATE COMPARES ANY SCREEN TO THE PDF.** `G105` reads
`08-screen-layouts.md` and nothing else. Neither drawing is machine-checked
against the product, which is why the divergence could grow for three days
without anything going red.

### 2 · THE RULING

> *"pleae tke PDF"*

**The 8 September PDF is the design.** The 3 September wireframe images and every
grading derived from them are **SUPERSEDED**. Where the two disagree, the PDF
wins and the older image is not evidence of anything.

### 3 · WHAT THIS SETTLES WITHOUT ANYBODY ASKING AGAIN

**The bills table column count.** Lane 5: *"the blueprint draws the bills table
with FOUR columns; the module's own wireframe draws EIGHT; the build has eight."*
It is not a figure, so B14 rule 37 (*a drawn number is an illustration*) cannot
settle it — but this ruling can, and does: **four is the design**. Lane 5's
finding stands as a real difference rather than as a question.

The same test now decides every other two-drawing disagreement in the lanes'
files mechanically, and none of them returns to the PO.

### 4 · WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, STATED SO NOBODY OVER-READS IT

**It does not make the PDF right about the PRODUCT.** The PDF's own first page
says every as-built statement in it was true at `2.232.0` on 8 September and
**must be re-verified**, and it flags three of its own statements as already
stale. Two more were found by lanes today — its screen-20 body still calls a
built flow unreachable, and it asserts `/ask` and `/ask-a-question` render one
screen where the router serves two. **The PDF is the authority on what the
SCREENS SHOULD BE, never on what the code currently DOES.**

**It does not ratify the PDF's rules.** Twelve of the twenty-four rules in its
appendix are marked *"NO HOME — stated only here"* and remain PROPOSALS. Choosing
the PDF as the drawing is not choosing its unratified rules; those are a separate
ruling and two of them collide with rules this repo has already signed.

### 5 · THE CONSEQUENCE FOR `14-layout-audit.md` AND `13-wireframe-delta.md`

Both were measured on 2026-09-05 against the older pack. They are **not deleted**
— they found real things, and three root causes they agreed on independently are
still the best evidence in the module. They are **stamped as measured against a
superseded drawing**, and a row that says "Matches" means *matched the 3
September image*, which under this ruling is no longer the question.


## 2026-09-11 — `CR-085` STEP 1 CLOSES: SIX OF THE SEVEN OPEN QUESTIONS RULED, ONE HELD FOR THE PO TO LOOK AT

All eight lanes reported. **22 conformance documents, 9,708 lines, 65 defects
filed, zero duplicate ids** in a 2,500-row register despite lanes colliding on
numbers dozens of times — the push helper refused every stale attempt.

### 1 · THE TWO DRAWN RULES THAT COLLIDE WITH SIGNED RULES — **OUR RULES WIN**

> *"(a) Our signed rules win, blueprint yields"*

So the blueprint's **R-01** (*"every icon carries its word — never an icon
alone"*) **yields to B14's row-action rule** (icons with tooltips, max two then
`…`), and its **R-15** (*"a back-link sits under the bar, never inside it"*)
**yields to r10 rule 1** (a footer `← Back` inside a stepper means *previous
step*). Neither is built to; both are recorded in the conformance files as
proposals the PO declined.

⚠ **I RECOMMENDED (c), A SPLIT — portal follows the blueprint, staff keeps ours —
AND THE PO CHOSE (a).** Written down because the reasoning matters to whoever
reads this next: one product, one icon vocabulary. A customer and a clerk are
different audiences for LAYOUT and for WIDTH, which is already ruled, but not for
what a glyph MEANS. The PO's answer is the simpler rule and the one that cannot
drift into two dialects.

⚠ **THIS SETTLES TWO OF THE TWELVE UNRATIFIED RULES. TEN REMAIN PROPOSALS** —
R-04, R-05, R-06, R-07, R-09, R-10, R-18, R-19, R-22, R-23 — and no lane may
build to them. Two of the ten are load-bearing on findings already filed: **R-10**
(*bad news never appears without the way out beside it*) is what the overdue
screen breaks, and **R-22** (*loading, empty and failed can never render as the
same picture*) is breached on at least four screens. **R-13 is a special case: it
acquired a repo home on 8 September** — decision log plus a test over all 50
routes — so it is law in substance while still not being a numbered B14 rule.

### 2 · RULE 39 CONTRADICTED ITSELF — **THE KPI GAP IS 8**

> *"(a). One off-scale value invites the next one. 8 is the nearest step and
> nobody will see 2px."*

`B14` rule 39 is **amended in place** and the anchor now reads **KPI 16/20 gap
8**. ⚠ **NOT GENERALISED, deliberately:** `.input` 6×10 and the field anatomy's
5px and 6px are also off-scale, and rounding them to scale steps would change the
**1 : 1 : 4** ratio the PO specified on purpose. The ratio is the point of the
field clause; the individual numbers are how it is expressed. They stand.

⚠ **AND THE SCALE IS NOT MISSING — IT IS MISNAMED, which makes this rule far
cheaper than it looked at ratification.** `tailwind.css` and `tokens.css` BOTH
already declare `--space-1: 4px · -2: 8 · -3: 12 · -4: 16 · -6: 24 · -8: 32`.
**Six of rule 39's seven steps exist today. Only 20px is missing**, and the
naming is px÷4, so it is `--space-5`. **Do not create `--sp-N` as a second
family** — two spacing scales in one product is the *second copy free to drift*
that this repo keeps paying for. Add the missing step to the scale that exists.

### 3 · PAYING — ONE SCREEN OR THREE — **HELD, PO IS LOOKING**

> *"please tell me screen # from PDF - I wil check and confirm"*

Given: **screen 35 `Pay now` (p64) · screen 36 `Check before you pay` (p66) ·
screen 37 `Payment made` (p67)**, the signed-in sequence. The guest equivalent is
screens 6 and 7 (pp14–15), both on `/pay-now`. The product collapses 35–37 into
one screen with three steps. **No work proceeds on this until the PO rules.**

### 4 · A DISPUTE — DOES THE MONEY STOP — **KEEP THE HONEST SENTENCE, FOR NOW**

> *"(b) for now"*

The drawing promises *"the disputed amount is not due and no late fee is added"*;
the screen says *"the bill stands and its due date keeps running."* **The screen
stays as it is.** The drawn promise is a BILLING change — it touches late fees
and what is owed — not a screen change, and the screen is currently telling the
truth about what the product does. *"For now"* is recorded as written: this is a
deferral with the door left open, not a rejection.

### 5 · THE GUEST PAYMENT SCREEN — **THE BLUEPRINT IS WRONG, NOT INCOMPLETE**

> *"b), firmly. It also contradicts a signed rule. I'd record this as the
> blueprint being wrong rather than as a gap."*

The blueprint asks the guest payment screen to show the account number, the
customer's **name** and the **service address**. Anyone who picks a bill off a
doormat could then read a stranger's home address. **The product shows five facts
and is right to.** Recorded in the conformance file as **A FAULT IN THE DRAWING**,
not as an unbuilt feature — so that nobody later "completes" the screen from it.
This is the second thing the blueprint asserts that must not be built as drawn.

### 6 · BILL LANGUAGE AND WEBSITE LANGUAGE — **THEY MAY DIFFER**

> *"(b) Allow them to differ - currently bills are offered only in english"*

⚠ **THE SECOND HALF IS A FACT THE REPO DID NOT HOLD, and it changes the shape of
the answer.** Bills are **English-only today**. So this is not two equal settings
that may diverge — it is: **the website is offered in eleven languages and the
bill is offered in one**, and the customer's website choice must therefore be
allowed to differ from the language their bill arrives in, because otherwise
choosing Japanese for the site would imply a Japanese bill we do not produce.

The preferences screen's current sentence — *"your bills and the website always
use the same language"* — is therefore **false as well as unwanted**, and is a
defect rather than a design difference. **This supersedes my own recommendation
of (a)**, which was argued on the premise that two settings are two places to be
wrong; that premise does not survive the fact that only one of them has eleven
values.

### 7 · BILL DELIVERY, "ONE CHANNEL MUST STAY ON" — **OUR RULE WINS**

> *"(b) Our rule wins, drop the constraint"*

The drawing requires at least one of email/post to remain enabled. **Every bill
is printed regardless** — that is the business the product actually models — so
the constraint is dropped and the drawn version is recorded as describing a
different product.

### 8 · WHAT STEP 2 IS STILL WAITING ON

**Two things, and only two:** the paying-screen shape (§3), and **ten unratified
drawn rules** (§1). Nothing else blocks. Step 2 remains CLOSED until both are
answered — a lane that fixes a screen to an unratified rule is inventing product
policy, which is what the declined-rule-30 precedent exists to prevent.


## 2026-09-11 — `OQ-CWP-1568` CLOSED: A SIGNED-IN CUSTOMER MAY ANSWER A PAYMENT PLAN, JOIN LEVEL PAY AND TURN AUTOPAY OFF — FIVE DEAD CONTROLS RELEASED BY ONE RULING

### 1 · THE RULING

> *"a). A customer who has to ring to accept a payment plan often doesn't ring.
> These are the people you've twice told me to prioritise."*

**YES to all of it.** A signed-in customer may **accept a payment plan, ask for
different terms, decline one, join level pay, and turn autopay off.**

The PO was offered a narrower option — allow the reversible writes, keep plan
accept/decline on the phone — and **took the broader one, with the reason stated
in the answer itself.** That reason is the ruling: a person in difficulty who has
to telephone often does not telephone.

### 2 · WHAT IT RELEASES, AND THE COUNT WAS WRONG IN THE REGISTER

The row said the question blocked *"the three controls on `CWP-063` and the one
on `CWP-044`"* — **four controls on two screens. It is five on three.** All
three hold registrations in `07-frontend/src/portal/routing/holds.ts` cite this
one question:

| screen | control | what a customer sees today |
|---|---|---|
| `CWP-063` plan offer | Accept · Ask for different terms · Decline | *"Ring us to answer this offer"* |
| `CWP-044` level pay | Join level pay | *"Ring us to join level pay"* |
| `CWP-040` autopay | Turn autopay off | *"Ring us to stop autopay"* |

**Both reads already shipped. Only the writes were held.** The server already
sends `join_held` / `actions_held` with this question's id as the reason, so the
seam exists and the ruling fills it rather than inventing it.

⚠ **LANE 7 FOUND THIS AND MIS-FRAMED IT, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING.** It reported
*"the server sends flags that no line of code reads"* — there are **eleven**
non-test references, so that half is false — and it reported the hold as a defect.
**It is not a defect; it is a deliberate refusal on an open question**, registered
with its reason, which is the product doing exactly the right thing. The finding
was real and valuable; the framing would have sent a lane to "fix" a hold that was
honest. **A held control and a broken control look identical on screen** — the
difference is only visible in the register, which is why holds are registered.

### 3 · WHAT THIS RULING DOES **NOT** SETTLE

Permission is not design. Left explicitly to the lane that builds it: **the audit
row each write must leave** (CLAUDE.md hard rule 7 — every money action writes
`audit_log`), **whether a decline is reversible**, and **the write-point count**
in `apps/portal/write_points.py`. None of those is a question for the PO; they
are ours to decide and write down.

### 4 · THE FAN-OUT, DONE IN ONE COMMIT

Closing a question is a fan-out and not a status edit — a closed question's body
goes on describing the open world, and **the body is what a lane actually reads**
(`DEF-WRK-4030`, three lanes misled in one evening). So in this commit: the
register row's **status**, its **body** (stamped *read the answer, not the
question below*), and its **blocks** column (corrected 4→5 controls, 2→3
screens), plus this entry. **The CODE is deliberately untouched** — releasing
five controls is step-2 work and step 2 is still closed.

### 5 · AND RULE 39 GETS ITS TOKEN NAMES

> *"Okay"* — to the recommendation that we not create `--sp-N` as a second family.

`B14` rule 39 is amended: the family is **`--space-N`**, which already exists in
both `tailwind.css` and `tokens.css` carrying six of the seven steps, and the
single addition is **`--space-5: 20px`**. The `--sp-N` spelling stays in the rule
as the PO's own wording for the scale, marked as not a token name to implement.
Two spacing scales in one product is a second copy free to drift — the same shape
as two OpenAPI schemas, two base-charge columns, and two figures for one fact.


## 2026-09-11 — `CR-085` · PAYING IS **THREE SCREENS**, AND THE ROUTE NAMES ARE INVERTED AGAINST THE DRAWING

### 1 · THE RULING

> *"it should be 3 screens - confirmed"*

Blueprint **screen 35 `Pay now` (p64) · screen 36 `Check before you pay` (p66) ·
screen 37 `Payment made` (p67)** — the signed-in payment journey is **three
screens, not one screen with three steps.**

⚠ **I RECOMMENDED (a), KEEP THE ONE SCREEN, AND THE PO RULED THREE.** Recorded
with my reasoning so the next reader knows it was weighed: I argued fewer page
loads on a phone and a flow already proved end-to-end at 390. The PO's answer
supersedes it. A payment is the one journey where a customer wants a page they
can stop on, go back to, and screenshot — three addresses give that; three steps
inside one address do not.

### 2 · WHAT IS ACTUALLY BUILT — AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF HOW I FIRST REPORTED IT

Lane 6 said *"the blueprint says three screens, the product gives one screen with
three steps"*, and I relayed that. **It is true of the SIGNED-IN flow and false of
the product as a whole**, because there are TWO pay journeys and they are crossed:

| | drawn as | at the address | built as |
|---|---|---|---|
| **GUEST** — pay without signing in | screens 6 · 7, on `/pay-now` | **`/pay` → `/pay/check` → `/pay/done`** | **already THREE screens** (`QuickPay`, composing `GuestPage`) |
| **SIGNED-IN** — pay now | screens 35 · 36 · 37, on `/pay` · `/pay/check` · `/pay/done` | **`/pay-now`** | **ONE screen, three steps** (`PayNow.tsx`, 763 lines, a `Stepper`; its own comment at line 86 says *"reason this screen has three steps instead of one"*) |

**THE ROUTE NAMES ARE INVERTED BETWEEN THE DRAWING AND THE PRODUCT.** The drawing
puts the guest flow on `/pay-now` and the signed-in flow on `/pay`; the product
does the reverse. Neither lane found this — lane 6 read the signed-in flow and
the blueprint's signed-in section and never compared the addresses.

### 3 · SO STEP 2 CARRIES AN ADDRESS COLLISION, NOT JUST A SPLIT

Building screens 35–37 as drawn puts the signed-in journey at `/pay`,
`/pay/check` and `/pay/done` — **three addresses the guest flow already occupies.**
That has to be resolved before a line is written, and there are only two shapes:

* **(i) swap them** — guest moves to `/pay-now`, signed-in takes the three. Matches
  the drawing exactly; changes three live guest addresses, and any link or email
  already pointing at them.
* **(ii) keep the addresses and split in place** — signed-in becomes
  `/pay-now`, `/pay-now/check`, `/pay-now/done`. Three screens as ruled, no guest
  address moves, and the product's own naming stops matching the drawing's.

**This is a judgment for the lane, recorded here so it is made once and on
purpose.** My reading is **(ii)**: the ruling was about the SHAPE — three screens
a customer can stop on — and it says nothing about addresses. (i) buys
drawing-fidelity at the price of breaking live guest links, and B14 rule 37's
principle already holds that a drawing's incidentals are not facts to build to.
⚠ If the PO wants the drawn addresses exactly, that is a one-line answer and it
overrides this paragraph.

### 4 · ONE FACT THE SPLIT MUST NOT HIDE

`/pay`'s own route comment: *"the LOOKUP ships and the payment does not: no
gateway exists (`CR-068` R2), so the Pay control renders in its normal place,
disabled, carrying its reason."* **The guest flow cannot take money today.**
Splitting the signed-in flow into three screens does not change that, and the
third screen — *Payment made* — must not imply a payment was taken on a tenant
with no gateway. That is `R-23` territory (*no sentence states a fact it does not
derive*), and `R-23` is one of the ten rules still unratified.


## 2026-09-11 — `CR-085` · THE SIGNED-IN PAY FLOW SPLITS **IN PLACE**; NO GUEST ADDRESS MOVES

### 1 · THE RULING

> *"ii). Your ruling was about the shape, not the addresses."*

The signed-in payment journey becomes **three screens at three addresses under
the one it already occupies**:

| blueprint screen | new address |
|---|---|
| 35 · `Pay now` | **`/:tenant/portal/pay-now`** |
| 36 · `Check before you pay` | **`/:tenant/portal/pay-now/check`** |
| 37 · `Payment made` | **`/:tenant/portal/pay-now/done`** |

**The guest flow does not move.** `/pay`, `/pay/check` and `/pay/done` stay where
they are, serving `QuickPay`, `QuickPayCheck` and `QuickPayDone`.

### 2 · WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY ACCEPTS

**The product's addresses will not match the drawing's, and that is the choice,
not an oversight.** The blueprint gives `/pay` + `/pay/check` + `/pay/done` to the
SIGNED-IN journey (screens 35–37) and `/pay-now` to the GUEST one (screens 6–7).
The product has had it the other way round since `CR-068`, and it stays that way.

The reason is the one in the ruling: **the ruling of an hour earlier was about
SHAPE** — three screens a customer can stop on, go back to and screenshot — **and
said nothing about addresses.** Matching the drawn addresses would move three
LIVE guest addresses and break any link or email already pointing at them, buying
nothing a customer can see. It is the same reasoning as B14 rule 37: a drawing's
incidentals are not facts to build to.

⚠ **SO THE CONFORMANCE FILES MUST RECORD AN ADDRESS DIVERGENCE, NOT A DEFECT.**
A later lane reading the blueprint will find screens 35–37 drawn at `/pay` and
must not "correct" the router. This entry is what stops that.

### 3 · WHAT THE SPLIT STILL HAS TO GET RIGHT

**`PayNow.tsx` is 763 lines with a `Stepper`**, and its own line 86 explains why
it has three steps. Splitting it is a real piece of work, not a re-route.

⚠ **AND THE THIRD SCREEN CARRIES A TRAP.** `/pay`'s route comment records that
*the lookup ships and the payment does not — no gateway exists, so the Pay control
renders disabled carrying its reason.* **A screen called `Payment made` must not
imply money moved on a tenant with no gateway.** That is `R-23` (*no sentence
states a fact it does not derive*), which is still one of the ten unratified
rules — so the screen is built to state only what it can derive, and the rule it
would cite is recorded as a proposal rather than leaned on.


## 2026-09-11 — `CR-085` · **R-22 RATIFIED**, AND THE THREE STATES ARE TOLD APART BY THEIR SENTENCE

### 1 · THE RULING

Put to the PO as: *loading, empty and failed can never render as the same
picture* — with the example that the locations screen shows **failed** where
**empty** was meant. Ruled, verbatim:

> *"differntiate it using text message"*

**R-22 is ratified, and the ruling narrows how it is met.** The three states do
not need three different LAYOUTS. **They need three different SENTENCES**, each
saying which state it is. The same card, the same shape, the same position — a
different sentence in it.

⚠ **THAT IS CHEAPER THAN THE RULE AS DRAWN AND BETTER FOR A CUSTOMER.** The
blueprint's wording (*"can never render as the same picture"*) reads as a demand
for three distinct designs, which on 50 screens is a large piece of work with a
real risk of three new inconsistencies. The PO's answer keeps one picture and
moves the whole burden onto the words — which is where the information a customer
needs actually lives. *"Nothing here yet"*, *"Still loading"* and *"We could not
load this"* are three different facts and a customer can act on each differently.

### 2 · WHAT IT MEANS IN PRACTICE, SO A LANE DOES NOT OVER-BUILD IT

* **Keep the shared state component.** Do not fork it into three.
* **Every screen that can be empty, loading or failed must pass a sentence for
  each**, and the three must not be the same string.
* **An empty state says what is absent**; a failed state says the read did not
  work; a loading state says it is still coming. **None of them may be a generic
  card with no words**, which is what several screens draw today.
* ⚠ **AND THE SENTENCE IS CLERK-FACING COPY, so it is a catalogue key in all
  eleven languages**, capped at B14's refusal length where it is a refusal.

### 3 · WHAT IT CATCHES ALREADY, FROM STEP 1

* **The locations screen** renders the STAFF failure panel — red *"Failed"*, *"the
  address may be wrong"*, and a **Download error report** button — to a member of
  the public who simply has no service centre near them. Empty drawn as failed,
  with a staff control on it.
* **The help screen** says *"Nothing here matches what you typed"* to somebody who
  typed nothing, over an empty search box. Empty drawn as no-match.
* **Home** draws one card for all three states.
* ⚠ **AND IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE SHARED STACK'S OWN STATE TODAY** — every
  signed-in address on the demo tenant rendered the same failure card whatever was
  actually wrong, which is how three lanes each spent time working out whether
  they were looking at a bug or a fixture.

### 4 · STATUS OF THE TEN

**R-22 is now law. NINE remain proposals** — R-04, R-05, R-06, R-07, R-09, R-10,
R-18, R-19, R-23. **R-10 was put to the PO and they said they did not understand
it**, so it is re-stated in plain English with two contrasting screens rather than
re-asked as a rule id — the standing instruction is that a rule reaches the PO in
plain English with a concrete example, never as an ID to go and look up.


## 2026-09-11 — `CR-085` · **R-10 RATIFIED**: A CUSTOMER IS NEVER LEFT STUCK ON BAD NEWS

### 1 · THE RULING

The rule was first put to the PO as `R-10` with one line of quoted blueprint
wording, and they replied *"I did not understand"*. **That was our failure, not
theirs** — the standing instruction is that anything reaching the PO arrives in
plain English with a concrete figure or example, **never as an ID to go and look
up**. Re-stated against two contrasting screens, and ruled:

> *"when a screen tells a customer something bad, the thing they can do about it
> must be on that same screen, next to the message. Not a page away. Not in a
> menu. Right there. — this is correct"*

**RATIFIED**, and the PO's own sentence is the rule text, not the blueprint's.
The blueprint says *"bad news never appears without the way out beside it"*; the
PO's wording says the same thing and says it operationally — **same screen, next
to the message** — which is what a lane can actually check.

### 2 · SCOPE, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**This is ratified for the CUSTOMER PORTAL.** The ruling's own words are *"when a
screen tells a CUSTOMER something bad"*, and it was put in the context of the
`CR-085` portal audit. ⚠ **Whether it extends to the staff app is a SEPARATE
one-line question and is NOT assumed here** — the rule-30 precedent is that the
PO answers what was put to them, and inventing wider scope from a narrow ruling
is exactly what that precedent forbids.

### 3 · WHAT IT DECIDES, FROM STEP 1's OWN FINDINGS

**Obeys it** — Past due: *"You owe $247.30"* with **Pay $247.30**, *Ask for a
payment plan* and *See what help there is* beside it. That is the model.

**Breaks it**, all four now buildable rather than held:
* **Budget billing** — *"We could not find an account to work this out for"*, with
  no button, no phone number and no link back. The browser's back button is the
  only way out.
* **The overdue screen offers no way to pay** (`DEF-CWP-4143`, open, high) — found
  by a person looking at the screen, and the conformance file notes that had R-10
  been a numbered rule the screen would have been built to it.
* **A declined card** — *"No money was taken. Try another card."* then **no buttons
  at all**, and the form the customer filled in is gone.
* **The landing page's missing `STRUGGLING TO PAY?` panel.**

### 4 · STATUS OF THE TEN

**R-10 and R-22 are law. EIGHT remain proposals** — R-04, R-05, R-06, R-07, R-09,
R-18, R-19, R-23 — and no lane builds to them.

⚠ **THE FOUR HELD DEFECTS ARE RELEASED. STEP 2 CAN NOW RUN ON ALL 65.** The two
rules the PO ratified are precisely the two that were load-bearing; the eight
still open are the ones nothing currently filed depends on.

### 5 · A NOTE ON HOW THESE TWO WERE ASKED

R-22 was answered on the first try because it was put with a screen (*the
locations screen shows failed where empty was meant*). R-10 was refused on the
first try because it was put as a rule id and a quotation. **Same PO, same
sitting, same kind of rule — and the only difference was whether a real screen
came with it.** That is worth more than either ruling: it is `DEF-1931`'s law
demonstrated twice in five minutes, and it is why the remaining eight will be put
with a screen each.



## 2026-09-11 — `CR-085` step 2 lane 1 · **THE PORTAL FRAME: ONE SPACING SCALE, ONE TITLE SIZE, A HEAD ON EVERY BRANCH, AND THE TWO NEW RULES GIVEN AN API**

### 1 · WHAT WAS DECIDED, AND THE ONE JUDGMENT THAT NEEDED DECIDING

Step 1 of this lane MEASURED the frame across all fifty portal addresses at 390
and 1280. This is step 2 — the same lane building what it measured. Nearly all
of it is B14 rule 39 and the two rules the PO ratified this morning applied
literally, and **one thing genuinely needed a judgment: what to do about a CSS
rule in a file the customer portal shares with the staff app.**

**`07-frontend/src/styles/global.css` line 78 declares `p { margin-block: 1em }`.**
Five independent lanes measured its consequence in the portal without finding the
cause: a form field's helper sentence sits **17px** below its input where B14
rule 39 ratifies **6**, and about **16px** above the NEXT field's label — so it
reads as belonging to the wrong control, which is the exact failure the rule's
own wording describes (*"the helper must READ as attached to the input above
it"*). And because the value is `1em` it is a **different number at every font
size** — 13px under a 13px helper, 15px under a 15px one — so **no fixed spacing
scale can contain it.**

**It could not simply be deleted.** That file is the STAFF app's too, and its own
comment records why the rule exists: *"84 `<p>` elements in this product have no
margin rule of their own, and without this their text runs together."* Deleting
it to fix one portal form would change the rhythm of roughly a hundred staff
screens that nobody asked about and nobody would have measured.

**Decided: SCOPE IT OUT OF THE PORTAL, LEAVE THE STAFF APP BYTE-IDENTICAL.**
`:where([data-portal]) p { margin-block: 0 }`, with `data-portal` set once on the
portal's own root in `PortalApp.tsx`. The staff rule above it is untouched.

Three parts of that are worth writing down rather than inferring:

* **The mark is on the ROOT and not on `[data-portal-frame]`.** Three of the
  fifty portal addresses — `/help/:slug`, `/visit`, `/visit/:slug` — render no
  frame at all, and a reset covering 47 of 50 is the second scale again.
* **`:where()` is load-bearing, and the first draft without it was WORSE THAN THE
  BUG.** Written plainly, `[data-portal] p` scores (0,1,1); every Tailwind
  spacing utility is a single class at (0,1,0); in the built sheet both sit
  outside any cascade layer, so specificity alone decides. The reset would have
  BEATEN `mt-1.5`, `mb-4` and `m-0` on every `<p>` in the portal — rule 39's own
  6px helper gap would have rendered as 0, and the **59 hand-written `m-0` /
  `my-0` workarounds** already in the portal would have stopped working in the
  same commit. `:where()` contributes no specificity, so the reset ties with the
  rule it overrides on source order and loses to anything a component asked for.
  **Nothing in this repo would have caught it** — `tsc`, eslint and every suite
  pass either way, and jsdom does not do the cascade. What found it was grepping
  `dist/assets/*.css` for the byte offsets of the two rules and reading which
  layer each landed in.
* **Those 59 `m-0` workarounds ARE the argument for scoping rather than for
  per-element fixes.** Lanes have been paying for this rule one element at a
  time, inconsistently, for weeks. 59 is the number of places it had already
  been noticed and never named.

### 2 · B14 RULE 39 — THE ANCHORS THAT MOVED, AND THE TWO FIGURES THAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT

**`--space-5: 20px` added** to `tailwind.css`'s `@theme` and to `tokens.css` —
both places the other six live. That is the amendment ruled on the day rule 39
was ratified (*"Okay"*): a lane ADDS the missing step to the family that exists
and mints NO `--sp-N`. Nothing on screen moved by adding it; what moved is that
the step now has a name a stylesheet and a reader can find.

Portal-side anchors, all in the shared kit (`portal/components/primitives.tsx`):

| anchor | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| wizard rail margin-bottom | `mb-4` — 16 | `mb-6` — **24** |
| wizard step cell | `p-2` — 8 × 8 | `py-4 px-5` — **16 × 20** |
| wizard step icon gap | `gap-2` — 8 | `gap-3` — **12** |
| `.input` (portal `TextInput`) | `px-3 py-2`, 41px tall | `px-2.5 py-1.5 min-h-9` — **6 × 10, min 36** |
| field → field (`TwoUp`) | `gap-4` — 16 | `gap-5` — **20** |
| label → input / input → helper (`FormField`) | ONE `gap-1`, 4px both | `mb-1.25` / `mt-1.5` — **5 / 6** |

**`FormField` was `flex flex-col gap-1` — a single gap serving label → input AND
input → helper, so those two distances could not differ by design whatever the
gap was set to.** It now has two.

⚠ **5 and 6 are OFF the seven-step scale and were NOT rounded onto it, which is
the rule's own instruction.** The KPI gap was rounded 6 → 8 hours after
ratification (*"One off-scale value invites the next one"*), and the same
amendment says the field anatomy is **"NOT GENERALISED … deliberately"**, because
rounding these would change the **1 : 1 : 4** ratio the PO specified — and the
ratio is the point of the clause rather than the individual numbers. They are
written as Tailwind's own multiplier steps (`1.25` × 4px, `1.5` × 4px), not as
`mb-[5px]`: an arbitrary value is a number nobody can find or change in one
place, which is what rule 39 exists to end.

⚠ **The portal input will measure ~37px rather than exactly 36, and that is
stated rather than hidden.** The staff `.input` reaches 36 because it is
`--text-md` (14px); the portal runs on `--text-body` (15px) because a customer
reads this on a phone. The rule ratifies the PADDING and the MINIMUM and both are
now exact; the extra pixel is a type decision, not a spacing one.

### 3 · THE GUEST BAR HOLDS AT PHONE WIDTH — AND IT IS THE SIGNED-IN SHELL'S OWN SHAPE

Measured on 2026-09-11: the signed-in bar is **57px at both widths**; the guest
bar was **96px at 1280 and 147px — three rows — at 390.** The blueprint's
standards block D ratifies exactly two heading bars *"because a third would mean
a customer could not tell at a glance whether they are signed in"*, and a bar that
is one row on one side of the product and three on the other is that distinction
dissolving at the width most customers arrive at.

**The cause was arithmetic, not style, which is why nothing was shortened.**
`DEF-CWP-4440` measured that nav at **853px inside ~860** BEFORE the language
control existed. Seven errand words, a language control and a sign-in button do
not fit beside a utility's name in 390px and never will.

**Decided: the errands and the language control move to a band of their own under
the bar** — header → nav, which is exactly the arrangement the PO ruled for the
signed-in half on 2026-09-08 (*"here header bar should ahve menu - and below that
we should have a line for account"*) and which `PortalShell.tsx` has drawn ever
since. Same classes, same `flex-wrap`, same `gap-x-6`, so the two frames cannot
drift apart. `Sign in` stays in the bar, which is where the signed-in shell keeps
`Help` and `Sign out`.

⚠ **The language control went DOWN with the errands, and a test decided that
rather than a preference.** The first draft kept it in the bar;
`GuestLanguage.dom.test.tsx` asserts `control.closest("nav")`, encoding the PO's
ruling of 2026-09-07 as *inside the nav*, and went red. **The honest answer was to
move the control, not to re-word the assertion** — a ruling encoded in another
lane's test is not a baseline to widen.

`DEF-CWP-4468` — *"two rows in English"*, carried since 2026-09-07 as a copy
decision nobody owned — is closed by this, and it was never a copy problem.

### 4 · ONE TITLE SIZE

30 portal screens computed **40px / 800**; three — `/sign-in`, `/enrol`,
`/forgot-password` — computed **25px / 700**, because the T7 card template writes
its own `<h1 className="text-h3 font-bold">`. Six such headings across four files
now take `text-h1` and no weight override, so every title in the portal is one
size. The T7 template is still a different template (kicker and title INSIDE the
card, which `pageHeadCensus.test.ts` records); what it is no longer is a second
title size.

### 5 · TEN SCREENS LOST THEIR HEADING ON A FAILED READ — ONE CAUSE, ONE FIX

13 of 34 signed-in screens rendered no `<h1>`. Three are correct by design.
**Ten shared one cause:** `if (failed) return <Card><p>…</p></Card>` was declared
BEFORE the `PageHeader`, so a failed or slow read threw away the page title, the
`data-screen` mark every rendered check selects on, and the drawing's whole top
row of controls — the one row that could have got the customer anywhere else.
Two of the ten did worse: `Methods` and `Preferences` returned `null` while
loading, so the screen rendered nothing at all.

**Nine are fixed** by building the head into a `const` above the branches and
rendering it on every one, through a new shared `PortalScreen`. **The tenth,
`usage/Usage.tsx` (CWP-033), is deliberately untouched** — it composes no page
head anywhere and is `pageHeadCensus.test.ts`'s one remaining
`AWAITING_ANOTHER_LANE` entry, so it is a different defect with a different owner.

Two new catalogue keys in all eleven languages — `portal.methods.reading` and
`portal.preferences.reading` — because R-22's ruling says none of the three
states may be a card with no words, and `return null` is that rule failing in its
strongest form.

### 6 · R-22 AND R-10 GET AN API, NOT FIFTY EDITS

`portal/components/states.tsx` holds `PortalScreen` and `PortalState`. **One
card, three sentences** — `kind` is `loading | empty | failed`, it renders as
`data-portal-state` so the rule is observable at all, and **`sentence` is
required with no default**, because a default would put the same words on fifty
screens, which is the rule's own failure case with extra steps. The three kinds
render the identical element and a test asserts that they do, so a later lane
forking it into three is undoing the ruling rather than improving it.

`waysOut` is R-10's slot: a row of controls INSIDE the card, directly under the
sentence — *"on that same screen, next to the message"*.

⚠ **`waysOut` IS OPTIONAL AND THAT IS A STATED LIMIT RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT.**
The honest type would require it on `failed`. It does not, because on the day this
was written ten portal screens had a failed branch and not one had a way out to
give it — the read they would retry is held in each screen's own effect, and
per-screen actions belong to the lane that owns that screen. A required prop
would have been satisfied ten times by `waysOut={[]}` or by a *Try again* wired
to nothing, which is `EmptyList`'s own `onCta: () => undefined` defect
(`DEF-MET-4764`): a control that looks pressable, is pressable, and does nothing.
**What the component guarantees is that it CAN carry one, in the right place.**

### 7 · THE GUARDS, EACH PROVED RED FIRST

* `states.dom.test.tsx` — **a RENDERED check**, which is the point.
  `pageHeadCensus.test.ts` next door proves COMPOSITION and says so about itself
  (*"a file could import `PageHeader` and render it behind a condition"*) — which
  is precisely what these ten files did, for weeks, with the census green. It
  mounts all nine fixed views with their reads REJECTING and asserts the `<h1>`,
  the `data-screen` mark and the state kind. Proved red by restoring one screen
  to its tip content: *"CWP-037 lost its data-screen mark on the failed branch"*.
* `spacingAnchors.test.ts` — the seven steps by name in both files, no `--sp-N`
  family anywhere, the portal reset present **with its `:where()`**, and — the
  other half of one decision — the STAFF rule still present. All four proved red.
* `pageHeadCensus.test.ts` gains the negative assertion `STEP_BAR_INSTEAD` never
  had. It listed `requests/DisputeBill.tsx` as drawing no page head months after
  that file composed one (`DEF-CWP-4927`): a skip-list rots the day one of its
  entries is fixed, which is hard-won law 2's clock-in-a-rule. Proved red by
  putting the stale entry back.

### 8 · A RED THIS LANE DID NOT CAUSE, DATED

**`npm run build` has been RED on this branch since 2026-09-10 17:44** and
nothing said so. `npm run build` is `tsc --noEmit && vite build`; tsc reports
`src/features/rating/DefinitionDetail.test.tsx(635,19) TS2339 Property 'value'
does not exist on type 'KpiTile'` — `KpiTile` is a union and the loop narrows
nothing. Introduced by `5cd769c48`. Both files are unmodified in this lane's
worktree, so the error is at the tip. **No gate runs tsc**, and vitest transpiles
without typechecking, so 983 portal cases pass over a tree that will not compile.
Filed as `DEF-GOV-4929`. Two eslint reds (`UnitDetailPage.tsx`,
`RunbookSetupPage.test.tsx`) and two `routeBUtilities` orphan classes
(`hover:bg-neutral-50` from 2026-09-08, `rounded` from 2026-09-10) are likewise
pre-existing and in files this lane did not touch.

### 9 · ADDENDUM, SAME DAY — THE ONE ANCHOR THE MEASUREMENT SAYS IS NOT CLOSED

The browser walk finished after the entry above was written and it corrects one
claim in it. **`field → field` is 20 only where the kit's own container is the

That class is per screen and belongs to the lane that owns it.

`DEF-CWP-4856` was first closed **fixed** on the strength of the two figures a
shared component can own, and has been corrected to **partially-fixed** with the

the row's own title is *"EVERY FIELD IN THE CUSTOMER PORTAL MISSES …"* and a

**The rest of the walk, for the record, at 390 and 1280:** label → input **5**,

**6px 10px** with `min-height: 36px`, guest bar **57** at both widths against a

⚠ **AND THE GUEST TRADE, WITH ITS NUMBER:** the errands did not vanish, they

is what the blueprint ratifies and the bar is now identical on both sides of the

its `py-3` is a step of the very scale this work enforces and dropping it to

against. **The real lever is the number of destinations in that band — seven
errand words plus a language control — and that is an information-architecture
question for the Product Owner, not a padding decision for a lane.**


## 2026-09-11 — `CR-085` step 2 lane 6 · **PAYING IS THREE SCREENS, AND THE THIRD ONE CANNOT SAY A PAYMENT HAPPENED UNLESS ONE DID**

### 1 · WHAT WAS BUILT

The signed-in pay journey — one screen with a `Stepper` inside it since
`CR-068` — is now **three screens at three addresses**, exactly as the PO ruled
twice on 2026-09-11 (*"it should be 3 screens - confirmed"*, then *"ii). Your
ruling was about the shape, not the addresses."*):

| blueprint | screen | address |
|---|---|---|
| 35 `Pay now` | `CWP-038` | `/:tenant/portal/pay-now` |
| 36 `Check before you pay` | **`CWP-076`** | `/:tenant/portal/pay-now/check` |
| 37 `Payment made` | **`CWP-077`** | `/:tenant/portal/pay-now/done` |

**No guest address moved.** `CWP-076` and `CWP-077` are allocated in `CR-068`
§9, whose heading moved from *seventy-five* to *seventy-seven* **in the same
commit as the rows**. Their label column reads `P55`/`P56` and names **no r10
frame** — the portal has no r10 prototype and these two come from the
2026-09-08 blueprint — which §9 now says in as many words, because every other
label in that column does name one.

⚠ **THE TWO ROUTES ARE NOT REGISTERED BY THIS LANE.** `portalRoutes.tsx` and
`screenIds.ts` are one file each and four lanes are building the portal at once;
hard-won law 11 is unambiguous about what happens then. The four lines are
written out verbatim in `04-docs/05-modules/15-portal/conformance/CR-085-lane6-step2-built.md`
§6 for the merge lane, and `G82` is green the moment they land because the ids
are already in §9.

### 2 · THE THREE JUDGMENTS INSIDE THE SPLIT, RECORDED BECAUSE THE RULES DID NOT DECIDE THEM

**(a) The button on screen 35 does not say *Pay*.** The drawing puts
`Pay $191.00` on 35 and again on 36; once 36 exists, the first of those is a
button that says it takes money and does not — hard-won law 1 in a piece of copy
a customer acts on. The drawing's own rule is kept (*"one button, and it names
the figure… never a bare Continue"*): it reads **`Check this — $191.00 →`**. The
figure stays on the control, the verb is what the control does, and **the word
*Pay* is now reserved for the one control in this product that takes money.**

**(b) What step one hands on is the CHOICE, never the answer.** The amount, the
instrument id and the idempotency key travel in **router state and never in the
address** (an instrument id in a URL is a database id on screen, B14 rule 31, and
an amount in one reaches access logs and a `Referer` header). `CWP-076` then
**re-reads both** the screen and the preview before drawing a figure — the guest
flow's own discipline, and what makes blueprint 36's `AMOUNT CHANGED` state real.
**The key is PRESENTED and never re-minted**, so one string covers the re-price,
the commit and every retry (hard rule 6, `US-CWP-045` TC-7).

**(c) Only `paid` reaches `CWP-077`, and a PARSER enforces it rather than care.**
This is the trap the ruling named in the same breath as the split: `/pay`'s route
comment records that *the lookup ships and the payment does not — no gateway
exists*, so **a screen called *Payment made* must not imply money moved on a
tenant with no gateway.** `paidResultFrom` reads any other outcome as no receipt
at all and draws the wrong-turn card; `declined`, `no_answer` and `refused` stay
on `CWP-076` where the ways out are. **And a sandbox tenant's receipt says so out
loud** — a sandbox tenant CAN answer `paid`, and nothing real was debited.

### 3 · R-10 AND R-22, THE DAY AFTER THEY WERE RATIFIED

**R-10.** A declined payment rendered **zero controls** (`DEF-CWP-4868`, measured
at 390 and at 1280). It now draws the outcome on the screen the customer is
standing on, **with the amount and the method still chosen** — which is also
blueprint 35's own DECLINED state — and the ways out sit INSIDE the block that
carries the sentence, asserted by containment so a test cannot pass with them in
a page head. ⚠ **`Try again` is offered on `no_answer` only:** re-trying the same
declined card is the one thing that cannot work, and offering it is how a refusal
starts naming an action that leads nowhere.

**R-22.** Every state card on the three screens is lane 1's `PortalState` with
its own sentence. Two more were found by applying it: `/payments` answered a
search that matched nothing with *"Your payments will appear here."* — empty
drawn as no-match, the exact fault the ruling cites on two other screens — and
`/autopay`'s empty `NEXT FEW` drew bare column headers over nothing.

### 4 · `OQ-CWP-1568` IS CLOSED AND THE CONTROL IT RELEASES IS STILL HELD — WHICH IS A DIFFERENT HOLD, NOT THE SAME ONE

The ruling gives a signed-in customer permission to turn autopay off. **Measured
the same day: `apps/portal/api.py` serves autopay as `GET accounts/{id}/autopay`
and nothing else, and `write_points.py` has no row for it** — a file that says in
its own words that adding one *"is a ruling and not an edit"*, with `G81` failing
the build until one is recorded. So what holds `CWP-040`'s *Turn autopay off* has
changed **from PERMISSION to a missing write path**, and `holds.ts`'s row says
exactly that with the measurement in it. The customer-facing sentence *Ring us to
stop autopay* stays true and stays five words.

**This lane did not open a write point**, and the ruling itself left the design
open: the audit row every money action must write (hard rule 7), whether the
change is reversible, and the write-point count.

### 5 · A TEST THAT PASSED AGAINST THE BUG IT WAS WRITTEN FOR

Eight new assertions were each mutated and watched fail before being trusted
(hard-won law 7), through `vitest`, which is the harness that will run them.
**Seven went red. One did not**, and it is the one worth recording: the first
`DEF-CWP-4869` case clicked *Another amount* — an empty box, so the amount is not
priceable — and typed into it, and **the OLD code cleared the stale panel on that
empty step all by itself**. The case passed on the broken screen and on the fixed
one. The window the customer actually stood in is **`$40.00` → `$400.00`**, where
the amount never stops being priceable; rewritten that way it fails on the
mutation and passes on the fix. *"Ask what would make this check pass wrongly"* is
what found it, and nothing else in this repo could have.

### 6 · WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT

The card fee (no processor, so `card_fee.priced` is false for every tenant and a
`$0.00` line would be a fact we do not have), the receipt's disconnection panel
(no served field says whether a notice existed — a sentence about somebody's
supply is the last place to guess), held `Download receipt` / `Email it to me`
controls on `CWP-077` (two more holds with no expiry test is the debt
`DEF-CWP-3925` cost a week; `/payments` already carries a live receipt icon), the
past-due radio (no served figure), and the kit's own `CommitButton` — `HeldCommit`
is a wrapper over it that is DELETED the day the kit says its own reason, and
**every call site outside these four screens still has `DEF-CWP-4866`.**
