## 2026-09-11 · CR-085 STEP 2 LANE 5 — THE FOUR-COLUMN RULING, AND THE SIGNED RULE IT COLLIDES WITH

**The ruling, applied.** PO 2026-09-11: **the 8 September blueprint PDF is the design;
the 3 September wireframe images are superseded.** That decides every
drawing-versus-drawing disagreement on this lane's six screens mechanically, without
coming back to the PO. `CWP-027`'s table goes from **nine columns to four** —
`BILL · COVERS · AMOUNT · STATUS` plus the row's two icons — `PERIOD` is renamed
`COVERS`, and `CWP-031` goes from **six to four** (`DOCUMENT · KIND · SENT · HOW`) and
is titled **`Your documents`** rather than *Documents and letters*.

### ⚠ THE JUDGMENT CALL, WITH ITS FIGURE — `BR-CWP-043` CANNOT SURVIVE FOUR COLUMNS INTACT

`BR-CWP-043` is signed law in `05-modules/15-portal/02-business-rules.md`:

> **Owing is a separate column from amount.** A $142.18 bill with $40.00 paid against
> it is neither a paid bill nor an unpaid one. — CONFIRMED, blueprint `P13`

**Its own citation is the document that just won.** `P13` and section 05 (pages 55–64)
are the same PDF, and section 05 draws four columns with no `OWING` among them. So this
is not the ruling overturning the rule — **it is the winning document contradicting
itself**, and CLAUDE.md law 13 says the supersession of a signed rule must be *stated*,
never assumed. A lane may not state it.

**What was built, and the worked figure.** The four drawn columns, with the rule's
SUBSTANCE kept inside them. A bill that charged **`$176.20`** and still owes **`$40.00`**
draws `$176.20` in the `AMOUNT` cell and **`$40.00 still owing`** on a second line beneath
it, with the `Part paid` chip in `STATUS`. The second line is drawn **only where what is
owed differs from what was charged** — a wholly-due or wholly-paid bill draws none,
because repeating the amount under itself, or printing `$0.00 still owing`, is noise on
the column a customer scans fastest. Both figures are still the server's; nothing on the
screen subtracts. The phone card draws the same second line from the same two strings, so
the two renderings cannot disagree about one bill.

**So no customer loses a figure. What is lost is the rule's letter — the separate
column.** Verified in a real browser at 1280: the header row reads
`Bill · Covers · Amount · Status · Actions` and the part-paid cell reads
`$40.00 still owing`.

**This needs one sentence from the PO and it is a genuine fork, not a clarification:**
either `BR-CWP-043` is amended to *"owing is shown wherever it differs from the amount"*,
or the bills table takes a fifth column and section 05 of the blueprint is stamped as
having been drawn without that rule in view. **Recorded here rather than asked, because
law 13 says a judgment recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable and a question is
the failure to make one — but this one collides with signed law, which is the short list
of things that legitimately reach the PO.** It is written up in full, with the collision
and both options, in
`04-docs/05-modules/15-portal/conformance/CR-085-lane5-04-step2-after.md` §1.

### The retention sentence was NOT built, and that is also a judgment

The drawing's `CWP-031` sub-line is **`6 documents · kept for seven years`** and its
`CWP-027` footer is **`Bills are kept for seven years`**. The COUNT is built. **The
retention period is not, and deliberately:** it is a per-deployment setting — the staff
catalogue's `audit.retention.law` interpolates `{{years}}` — and nothing serves it to the
portal. Printing *seven years* would be a screen making a promise about how long a utility
keeps its records, from a constant typed into a catalogue. That is the same family as the
defect fixed in the same commit (`DEF-CWP-4860`, a sentence claiming a letter bounced with
no date behind it) and a worse one, because a customer would act on it. `CPB-15`'s
retention half stays open and says why.

## 2026-09-11 — `BR-CWP-043` AMENDED: OWING IS SHOWN WHEREVER IT DIFFERS, NOT IN A COLUMN OF ITS OWN

### 1 · A DOCUMENT CONTRADICTING ITSELF, WHICH NO LANE MAY RESOLVE

Lane 5 applied the PO's ruling that **the 8 September PDF is the design** and cut
the bills table from nine columns to the four it draws — and hit a signed rule
going the other way:

> `BR-CWP-043` — *"Owing is a separate column from amount. A $142.18 bill with
> $40.00 paid against it is neither a paid bill nor an unpaid one."*
> **CONFIRMED — blueprint `P13`.**

⚠ **THE RULE'S OWN CITATION IS THE DOCUMENT THAT CONTRADICTS IT.** `BR-CWP-043`
cites blueprint page 13; the same PDF's section 05 draws the bills table with
**four columns and no owing among them**. So *"the PDF wins"* could not settle
it — the PDF is on both sides.

**Lane 5 refused to decide and that was right.** It built the four drawn columns,
kept the figure as a second line — `$176.20` with **`$40.00 still owing`**
beneath it and a *Part paid* chip — and put both options up with worked figures
rather than picking one and calling it conformance.

### 2 · THE RULING

> *"A. The information is on screen either way; four columns is what a customer
> can read on a phone."*

**AMENDED, not superseded.** The rule now reads: **owing is shown wherever it
DIFFERS from the amount.** A part-paid bill still shows both figures and no
customer loses anything. **What is dropped is the LAYOUT clause** — *a separate
column* — which was never what the rule was protecting. The alternative, a fifth
column, was declined on the ground a phone cannot read it.

### 3 · THE CODE ALREADY MATCHES, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD

Lane 5 shipped the second-line form in `448776e5a` **before** this ruling, as its
own recorded judgment while flagging the conflict. **So this amendment blesses
what is built rather than commissioning a change.** That is the right order: the
lane picked the reading that loses no information, shipped it, and named the
decision it could not make. Had it guessed the other way, a fifth column would
now need removing.

### 4 · WHAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE AMENDING

**21 files cite `BR-CWP-043`** — the rule table, the epic, the execution plan,
three conformance files, four backend files, five front-end files, two journeys
and a fixture. **None of them encodes the COLUMN clause as behaviour**; they cite
the rule for the *substance* — that a part-paid bill is neither paid nor unpaid —
which is unchanged. So the amendment is a wording change in one row and **no code
follows from it**, which is why this entry says so explicitly rather than leaving
a lane to re-derive that later.

### 5 · THE SHAPE, FOR NEXT TIME

**A drawing being made authoritative does not settle a rule that cites that same
drawing.** This is the second time this week a document has been found asserting
something its own other half contradicts — the portal blueprint also draws the tax
status twice, and the Plans & Rates blueprint cited an appendix it does not
contain. **Where a rule and its own source disagree, it goes to the PO**, because
picking either side is inventing product policy from a typesetting accident.


## 2026-09-11 — `CR-085` step 2 lane 2 · **THE GUEST ENTRANCE: A PORTAL THAT IS OFF IS OFF ON ALL TEN ROUTES, AND A REFUSED PUBLIC PAGE IS NOT A STAFF ERROR PANEL**

Ten routes — the landing page · `/sign-in` · `/enrol` · `/forgot-password` ·
`/track` · `/report` · `/visit` · `/visit/:slug` · `/help` · `/help/:slug`.
Every figure below was read off a browser at **390 and 1280, both**, against a
bundle built from this lane's own tree, on **two** tenants on purpose:
`pine-hill` (help answers, service centres, an emergency number and office hours
all published) and `brazosbend` (**none** of them), because every empty state in
this lane can be seen nowhere else. The walk is a file —
`10-scripts/cr085_lane2_guest_walkthrough.mjs`.

⚠ **WHAT IS MEASURED AND WHAT IS NOT, STATED BEFORE ANY FIGURE IS QUOTED
(hard-won law 1).** That walkthrough was run in full **BEFORE** these fixes and
every check below was seen RED on the code as it stood — those are the figures
quoted throughout. It had **not** been re-run green at the moment this entry was
written: the shared box was running six lanes and the bundle build was
OOM-killed twice, so the AFTER pass is the next thing this lane owes and the
walkthrough is in the repo so that anybody can run it. `npx tsc --noEmit` IS
green over the whole front end. **No sentence below claims an after-figure.**

### 1 · NINE OF THE TEN ROUTES IGNORED THE PORTAL'S OWN ON/OFF SWITCH, AND THE CAUSE WAS A COPY OF ONE FILE WITH ONE LINE MISSING

With `is_live:false` on the wire, only the landing page held. `/sign-in` served a
live sign-in box, `/enrol` the whole three-step enrolment wizard,
`/forgot-password` a live password-reset mailer, and `/track`, `/report`,
`/help`, `/visit` and the two detail screens their full screens — at a utility
that had not opened its portal, on the open internet.

`guest/GuestPage.tsx` has read the switch since wave C and says so in its own
docstring. `signin/SignInPages.tsx` held a private `GuestPageFrame` that was
**that component byte for byte minus the `is_live` line**, and five other pages
composed `GuestFrame` directly. **The duplicate read as diligence**: it is
short, it is correct about everything it does do, and the missing line is
invisible unless you diff it against the file it was copied from. So the fix is
a **deletion** — the copy is gone and all nine compose `GuestPage` (B14 rule 36).

⚠ **AND A SECOND HALF THAT IS ABOUT THE WIRE RATHER THAN THE SCREEN.** The four
content reads now carry `enabled: live`, so a switched-off portal draws the
holding notice **and asks the server for nothing**. Those are two different
statements and only the first is about what a visitor sees. It matters most on
`/help/:slug`, where opening an answer is an EVENT the back office counts
(`CP-34`) — a switched-off portal would have been logging *read this month*
against a utility whose customers cannot reach the page at all. The walkthrough
counts the content requests a real browser issues while the portal is off and
fails on anything but zero; that count is the AFTER pass's to report.

⚠ **THE SERVER HALF IS NOT FIXED AND IS NOT IMPLIED FIXED.**
`apps/portal/guest_api.py` reads `is_live` in **exactly two places**, so six
guest endpoints still answer on a switched-off tenant. **`DEF-CWP-4938`**, filed,
and the new test file names it in its own header rather than letting a passing
client suite imply the server is covered.

**Why nothing caught it:** 71 test files and 960 cases were green that morning.
Every one of the ten screens was tested — at its own address, against a fixture
whose `is_live` is true, because that is the state a screen is interesting in.
The question *does this screen respect the switch* belonged to no suite.
`guestOffSwitch.test.tsx` now walks the whole set in one table, and carries the
mirror case, because every assertion in it also passes on a guest surface that
renders nothing at all.

### 2 · A MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC WITH NO COUNTER NEAR THEM WAS SHOWN A STAFF ERROR PANEL WITH A *DOWNLOAD ERROR REPORT* BUTTON

`GET portal/public/service-centres` answers **404 on purpose** when the utility
shows no counter (`BR-CWP-093`): the server refuses the page rather than serving
a heading with nothing under it. Correct on the wire, and three screens handed it
to the STAFF panel — a red *Failed* chip, *"It may have been removed, or the
address may be wrong"* (blaming a visitor who typed nothing) and a control
offering a customer an error report they have nowhere to send — **rendered
outside the frame**, so with no utility name, no phone number and no way back.

**The ruling this lane made, and it is one line: a 404 is an EMPTY and
everything else is a FAILURE.** Both are `PortalState`, the same card, different
sentences — R-22 as the PO ruled it that morning. **Empty** says what is absent
and carries the utility's own phone as a `tel:` beside the message, which is the
drawing's `NONE CONFIGURED` state in one sentence (*"Falls back to the phone
number rather than an empty page"*) and R-10 literally. **Failed** says the read
did not work and offers the retry an empty state must not.

⚠ **READING EVERY REFUSAL AS *nothing here* WOULD BE THE SAME COLLAPSE IN THE
OTHER DIRECTION** — telling a customer the utility has no offices when the truth
is that the page did not load. Both directions are asserted.

### 3 · THREE FACTS, THREE SENTENCES: THE HELP SCREEN SAID *Nothing here matches what you typed* TO SOMEBODY WHO HAD TYPED NOTHING

On a tenant with nothing published, a customer got an empty search box, a
chooser with one option, and the no-match sentence — all three clauses of the
blueprint's `NO ARTICLES` state broken at once (*"Falls back to the phone number
and email — **never an empty search box**"*).

*Nothing is published* and *your search matched none of what is* are different
facts and now read as different sentences. **The test that decides which is
`narrowed`** — a typed word or a chosen chip is the visitor having asked for
less. Without one, an empty list is the UTILITY's absence and no control on the
screen could undo it, so the box and the chips do not render at all; with one,
they stay and the state carries the single press that undoes them.

And the rail. `Still stuck?` promised a call and named nothing to call on a
tenant that had published neither a number nor hours. The sentence now follows
the facts: with a number, the call is offered, the number is bold under it and
the hours are under that — the drawing's own reason being that *"a number
without hours produces a call to a closed office and a second call tomorrow"*.
With none, it says where the number actually is: on the paper bill. **The email
address the drawing also asks for is still absent, deliberately** — no endpoint
serves one, and a line naming an inbox would be a sentence stating a fact the
product does not hold.

### 4 · `CPB-24` WAS NARROWED BEFORE IT WAS EXECUTED, AND EXECUTING IT AS WRITTEN WOULD HAVE PRINTED A CATALOGUE KEY TO CUSTOMERS IN ELEVEN LANGUAGES

The specification says of **both** `portal.held.card` and `portal.held.signIn`
that they *"are rendered by no source file at all"*, and that done looks like
*"the two keys are gone from all eleven catalogues and no screen changes,
because nothing rendered them."*

* `portal.held.signIn` — **true**, and retired.
* `portal.held.card` — **false**. `FrontPageView.tsx:237` draws it under *What
  things cost*, whose `CR-068` R3 hold is still correct because the public
  prices screen is genuinely unbuilt. The live landing page reads *"Opens with
  the next release."* under that card right now.

`t()` answers a missing key **with the key**. **One key retired; the other stays
until its screen lands.**

### 5 · THE WORD A NORTH AMERICAN READS — AND THE SAME NARROWING IN THE OTHER DIRECTION

The blueprint's conventions block C names the vocabulary a North American
utility customer expects and *ZIP code* is in the list; the portal asked for a
**Postcode**. Changed in **`en.json` only**, four guest keys —
`portal.enrol.postcode`, `portal.postcodeHelper`, `portal.track.secondFact`,
`portal.quickPay.postcode`.

⚠ **THE OTHER TEN CATALOGUES WERE NOT TOUCHED AND THAT IS THE RULING RATHER THAN
AN OMISSION.** They already carry their own language's right word —
*Postleitzahl*, *código postal*, *CAP*, *CEP*, *पिन कोड*, *郵便番号* — and B14
rule 35 says a catalogue is written in its own language, not translated from
English. Pushing an English acronym into ten of them would break a ratified rule
to fix a defect that exists in one. **A change stated as "everywhere" that is
only correct in one place is `CPB-24`'s shape in the other direction, and it is
worth naming as a pattern: before executing a sweep, check each surface it
names.**

`portal.quickPay.postcode` is `/pay`, another lane's screen, and was changed on
purpose: `portal.postcodeHelper` is shared, so moving it alone would have left
`/pay` reading *"Postcode of the service address"* over the helper *"Just the
ZIP code…"* — one screen contradicting itself, which is worse than the defect.
Copy only, no layout moved, no source file of that lane's touched. Two
signed-in keys and one staff key remain and the row stays **partially-fixed**.

### 6 · TWO EMERGENCY BANDS, STACKED, ON THE MOST DANGEROUS SCREEN IN THE PRODUCT

`GuestFrame` gained an `EmergencyBand` in the same CR — above the children on
every signed-out screen, which is what the drawing asks for and what `/report`
alone used to provide. Measured at both widths on a tenant with a number
published: **two identical red panels**. The screen's own band is now the
FALLBACK for the one case the frame deliberately leaves empty (`BR-CWP-093` —
no phone, no band), where *ring the number on your bill* and *Do not use this
form* are the half only this screen can say.

⚠ **WHAT THAT COSTS, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND:** on a tenant WITH a
number the sentence *"Do not use this form."* no longer reaches `/report` at
all. The frame's band ends at `portal.emergency.anyHour`, correctly, because
that tail is wrong on `/sign-in` where *this form* is the sign-in box.
**`DEF-CWP-4937`**, open, and it is a frame decision rather than a screen one.

⚠ **AND `DEF-CWP-4852` WAS CLOSED WITHOUT THIS LANE AUTHORING THE FIX.** Step 1
measured the landing page on a tenant that has published **no emergency number
at all** and reported *"no band, no phone number and no danger tier anywhere"*.
The observation was true and the diagnosis was not: `BR-CWP-093`'s *no phone, no
band* is the correct answer to that tenant. **Measuring an absence on a tenant
that has nothing published cannot tell a missing FEATURE from a missing FACT** —
which is why both tenants were walked this time, and why the second one is now
written into the walkthrough rather than left to the next lane to think of.

### 7 · THE ENROLMENT WIZARD'S *Continue* WAS LIVE OVER THREE EMPTY REQUIRED FIELDS, ON THE ONE GUEST FORM THAT LOCKS AFTER THREE WRONG TRIES

`BR-CWP-036` gives this form three attempts and then fifteen minutes in the

## 2026-09-11 — THE BRANCH DID NOT COMPILE FOR FORTY-FIVE MINUTES, AND VITEST WAS RED OVER IT THE WHOLE TIME

**What happened.** `0c85f58ce` (CR-085 step 2, lane 7) put `return QUOTE;` into
`07-frontend/src/portal/payments/Fees.dom.test.tsx`. There is no `QUOTE` in that
file — the fixture is `BODY` — so `npx tsc --noEmit` exited 2 on the whole front
end, and `npm run build` is `tsc && vite build`, so **nobody could build the
branch**. Lane 5 found it, dated it with
`git log -S "QUOTE" origin/claude/hi-0jmv62 -- <file>`, did not cross into
another lane's surface to fix it, and filed `DEF-CWP-4934`. Lane 7 fixed it in
`c0157aa4c` by removing a duplicated test block, not by renaming the word.

**⚠ THE REGISTER ROW'S ESCAPE REASON IS INCOMPLETE, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS
MORE THAN THE FIX.** `DEF-CWP-4934` says the break escaped because *vitest
transpiles and does not typecheck*. That sentence is true in general and it is
**not what happened here**. Reading an undeclared identifier throws
`ReferenceError` at run time, so the second read rejected, the screen stayed on
its failure card, and the case that presses **Try again** could not find
`SR-26-0061`.

**Measured, not reasoned:** the pushed version of that file, run in an idle
worktree at `10e7cc7fd`, gives

    Tests  1 failed | 12 passed (13)
    × CWP-050 · fees to pay (US-CWP-050) > R-10 — a failed read still offers
      the question route, and really re-reads

**So vitest WOULD have caught it, in under nine seconds, on the file the lane
had just edited.** The escape is not a blind check. Lane 7 names it in its own
commit message: a background job was killed mid-run, the case was appended
twice, the duplicate was removed LOCALLY, `tsc` and the suite were re-run green
on the deduplicated tree — **and that tree was never pushed.** The commit had
already been hashed.

**The habit, and it is law 11's, unchanged:** after pushing, re-read each file
**from the pushed commit** and confirm your own change is in it —
`git show <commit>:<path> | grep <marker>` — **on every path in the commit, not
the ones that felt like the work.** Lane 7 ran exactly that check, on the source
files, and not on the tests.

**The general form, which is new and is why this is written down:** every guard
in law 11 answers *"is my change in the commit?"*. **None of them answers
*"is the commit the tree I tested?"*** — and a green check on an unpushed tree
is indistinguishable, from the outside, from a green check on the pushed one.

**Verified at the tip rather than asserted:** `npx tsc --noEmit` exits **0** on
`0909447ca`. That is the first typecheck this branch has been shown to pass
since the break, and no gate in this repository runs one (`DEF-GOV-4844`).

**Left open on purpose.** `DEF-CWP-4934`'s `escape_reason` column is not edited.
`close_defect.py` moves a status and a commit, by byte-splice, and nothing in
`10-scripts/` rewrites a free-text field of a 2,567-row register that four lanes
are writing — and reaching for a `csv` writer to do it is the exact move law 11
forbids. The correction lives here, where the row's citation leads.

## 2026-09-11 — I LOWERED A RATCHET TO SEVEN WHEN THE TRUTH WAS EIGHT, AND IT PASSED BECAUSE THE CHECK COULD NOT SEE THE EIGHTH

**The correction, first.** `3d5b2fc2c` lowered `pageHeadCensus.test.ts`'s ceiling
from 19 to 7 and its own message said *"Seven is what the filter above actually
returns"*. **That was true of the filter and false of the tree. The honest number
was EIGHT.** `home/Home.tsx` declared the screen mark nowhere in its code and was
counted compliant on the strength of ONE comment, at line 163 of that commit:

    // the loading branch carried no `data-screen="CWP-022"` at all — every

Measured against that commit's own bytes: raw grep finds 1 match, comment-stripped
finds **0**. Found by `CR-085` step 2 lane 4, which went to check the ceiling
after a sibling's correction rather than accepting it, and filed `DEF-CWP-4945`.

**What makes this worth a decision-log entry rather than a defect row alone is the
shape, and it has three turns:**

**(1) The two guards disagreed about what they were counting.** The census exists
to protect `g100_every_screen_has_a_door.py`, and **`g100` strips comments before
it matches while the census's ceiling filter did not.** Every OTHER assertion in
that same file goes through a comment-stripping helper; that one line did not. A
guard that measures something narrower than the guard it protects has a hole
exactly the width of the difference — and every reading of it is true. It was not
lying; it answered a question one character-class away from the one that mattered.

**(2) It is SELF-CONCEALING, which is the part nobody would predict.** The more
carefully a lane documents *why* the screen mark matters, the more likely its file
is to quote the mark in a comment and vanish from the ratchet. **Home was the most
heavily commented screen in the portal on exactly that subject, and it is the one
that disappeared.** A check that is defeated by good documentation of itself will
lose its best-documented subjects first.

**(3) THE BAD CEILING WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT.** Had the filter been honest at
`3d5b2fc2c`, 8 > 7 and the census would have gone RED naming `home/Home.tsx`. So
the ratchet was set correctly by intent and passed by accident, on the same defect
it would have caught. That is the uncomfortable half: **a number arrived at
carefully, from a measurement taken carefully, against a filter nobody thought to
question.**

**Where it stands.** `ae89fea9b` strips comments in the ceiling filter, proved by
planting the exact shape that fooled it — a comment-only `data-screen="CWP-030"`
in a file genuinely on the list — and measuring both ways: raw source 6, stripped
7. `f58a55735` (lane 4) gave Home a real literal. So filter and truth now agree at
**7 of a ceiling of 7**, tight, with no slack. `DEF-CWP-4945` closed against
`ae89fea9b`.

**The general form, for the next person setting a ratchet:** a ceiling is a claim
about a NUMBER, and a number is only as good as the filter that produced it. Before
lowering one, ask what the filter would count that it should not — not only what it
might miss. Both failures are silent and the first one reads as success.

## 2026-09-12 — FIVE RULINGS ON THE ASSETS MENU, AND TWO OF THEM SETTLE CONTRADICTIONS IN OUR OWN SIGNED RULES

`CR-092-BRC01` step 1 put eight questions to the PO. **Five are answered and are
recorded here verbatim before any of them is built** (law 9). Three remain open
and are named at the end so no lane builds them.

### 1 · SCOPE — all thirty-five

> ***"c) All 35"***

Every finding from step 1 is in scope: **7 high, 16 medium, 12 low**, of which 30
are Assets, 4 are the shared table and 1 is governance. **My recommendation was
(b), high and medium only, and it was declined** — recorded because a recommendation
that loses is the one worth keeping, and the reason is sound: the twelve "low" rows
are wrong labels and stale comments, which is exactly the class this repository has
learned to stop deferring.

### 2 · THE TWO WORDLESS TABS — D9 STANDS, AND THE FIGURES ARE THE WORK

> ***"a) Fix the figures"***

The PO's ruling of **2026-08-22** — *"drop the prose, draw the KPI grids"* — **is
not reversed.** The two tabs stay wordless. What was wrong is the premise: the
grids draw **four em-dashes** until every row is loaded, so the thing that was
meant to carry the meaning carries nothing. **Fixing the figures makes an existing
ruling true rather than replacing it**, and a test asserts the absence of the prose
by name, so the other reading would have meant undoing that too.

⚠ **This is the shape to remember: a ruling can go wrong without being wrong.**
D9 was correct when made and its premise decayed underneath it. Nothing in this
repository watches for that.

### 3 · FIELD SPACING — 20px, THE ANATOMY WINS

> ***"a) 20 everywhere — the anatomy wins"***

**B14 rule 39 stated both numbers**: its SCALE said `--sp-4` 16px *between fields*,
its FIELD ANATOMY said field → field **20px**. Both from the day it was written, so
any form could cite the rule and be wrong either way. **None was right** —
`CR-092` measured **zero of eleven** adjacent pairs at 20 (14px in dialogs, 16px on
full-page forms).

**Field → field is 20px everywhere. The 16px step governs blocks and sections,
never two fields.** The anatomy wins because the PO gave that clause as a RATIO —
5 : 6 : 20, ≈ 1 : 1 : 4 — and 16 collapses it to 1 : 1 : 3.2, which is what the
clause exists to prevent. B14 rule 39 is amended in the same commit as this entry.

⚠ **SECOND CONTRADICTION FOUND INSIDE RULE 39 IN TWO DAYS** (the KPI gap of 6 was
the first). **A rule that ratifies a SCALE and a set of ANCHORS in one breath will
keep producing them** — an anchor is a measurement, a scale is a policy, and
nothing checks one against the other. Both were found by measuring the running app.

### 4 · THE TECHNICIAN PICKER — A CREW READ, NAME AND EMAIL ONLY (`BR-AST-533`)

> ***"a) Let a clerk read the crew list (name + email only)"***

Two signed rules collided and neither could yield: `BR-AST-038` writes the
log-repair screen **for** a Billing Clerk, and B14 rule 31 forbids a database id as
a field's visible value — while that role is handed a text box and the help *"Your
role can't list users, so enter the technician's ID."*

**`GET /users` stays `SystemAdminOnly`.** What is created is a **new role-safe read
serving name and email only**. The id still travels as the chosen value; what is
forbidden is a person reading or typing it.

### 5 · RAISE WORK ORDER ON A RETIRED ASSET — DISABLED, WITH THE REASON (`BR-AST-534`)

> ***"a) Show it disabled, with the reason"***

An instance of `BR-SHL-025` extended from ROLE to STATE, which is the half nobody
had ruled. **A hidden control teaches a clerk the product cannot do the thing; a
disabled one with its reason teaches them why not** — and the two are
indistinguishable to every check this repository owns. The server side
(`row_actions()` serves no raise verb) is deliberately NOT settled by the ruling.

### STILL OPEN — NO LANE MAY BUILD THESE

**One asset, one cost** (which cost an asset shows and where the arithmetic lives —
note the "740 invisible costed jobs" is really **zero**, so this is about the future
not a live gap) · **the shared table's sort and pager** (four rows, 54 lists, my
recommendation was to size it separately) · **the sub-meter's allocation share**
(the four allocation methods have **no list anywhere in the product**, so somebody
must name them first).

## 2026-09-12 — CR-092's FINAL SCOPE: FORTY ITEMS, AND THE RECOMMENDATION TO DEFER THE TEN IS WITHDRAWN

Three further rulings close the eight questions step 1 raised.

**6 · ONE ASSET, ONE COST** — ***"a) One lifetime figure, both halves named
beneath"***. A clerk asking *what has this cost us* means both halves. Worth
recording beside it: the blueprint says **740 costed jobs are invisible from the
asset**; the real number is **zero** — 8 cost lines exist and **none is anchored to
an asset** — so this builds the plumbing before the data arrives rather than
recovering a live loss.

**7 · THE SHARED TABLE — ITS OWN CHANGE REQUEST** — ***"(b). It's the right fix and
it touches 54 lists at once. That risk doesn't belong inside an Assets pass"***.
Four rows leave `CR-092`: the sort's missing third click, first/last page, the two
title sizes, the KPI gap. **Two of the four were already filed weeks ago**
(2026-08-21 and 2026-08-30), which is itself the argument — they are not an Assets
discovery.

**8 · THE SUB-METER'S ALLOCATION SHARE — BUILD IT** — ***"(a)"***, with the caveat
about naming the four methods carried over from the recommendation. **What the four
methods actually are, measured rather than assumed:**
`allocation_rule = models.TextField(null=True, blank=True)  # rubs | sqft | equal | absorb`
— a **code comment on a plain text column**. No `choices`, no lookup table, no
constraint, and **no words in any of the eleven catalogues**. They are real
industry terms (RUBS is the standard ratio method), so **naming them on screen is
copy work rather than product policy**, and it is taken as ours to draft and put to
the PO for wording — not handed back as a blocking question.

### AND THE SCOPE DOUBLES, RULED THE SAME HOUR

> ***"Build 7 the task cannot be done at all today - yoou ahve to implment these also"***
> ***"please add 10 new capabilities also - implment them"***

**Step 2 builds everything: 23 maintenance + 17 build = 40 items.** My
recommendation was to take the ten capabilities as a later CR and it is

declined today, both in the same direction — **I proposed a narrower scope twice
and was widened twice**, and the pattern is worth more than either instance.

### THE UI SKILL IS MANDATORY AND THERE IS EXACTLY ONE

## 2026-09-12 — `CR-092` STEP 2 WAVE A · THE FIELD ANATOMY IS BUILT, AND THE ONE TOKEN I WAS SENT TO ADD WAS ALREADY THERE

**What this wave was for:** the shared form kit, landed alone and first, because
five screen lanes start on top of it and two lanes editing `FormModal.tsx` at once
is hard-won law 11's eighth occurrence waiting to happen.

**The readings, before and after, from the SAME instrument** —
`10-scripts/render-checks/cr092-lane3-field-anatomy.mjs`, 29 fields across five
asset screens, Chromium, 1280 **and** 1440, run against the deployed join
(`vite build` → `server.mjs` → `/api`):

| B14 rule 39 ratifies | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| helper **below** the input | **0** of 18 helper fields | **18 of 18** |
| label → input **5px** | 28.59px (one-line helper) / 47.19px (two-line) | **5px on 18 of 18** |
| input → helper **6px** | *the gap did not exist* — the helper was above | **6px on 18 of 18** |
| field → field **20px** | 14px in the dialog, 16px on the four full-page forms — **0 of 11 pairs** | **20px on 11 of 11 pairs** |

The 11 helperless fields measured 5px before and after; they were already right and
nothing moved them. Every figure above is identical at both widths.

### 1 · THE JOB I WAS SENT TO DO THAT WAS ALREADY DONE — `--space-5`

My briefing's first job was to add `--space-5: 20px`. **It has been in the tree
since `CR-085` step 2 lane 1 (`01cfb545a`, 2026-09-11)** — `tailwind.css:664` and
`tokens.css:286` — and B14 rule 39's own status cell says so. I added nothing and
created no `--sp-N` family. Recorded because a lane acting on that instruction
without reading the rule first would have minted a second spacing scale, which is
precisely the outcome the PO's *"Okay"* was given to prevent.

### 2 · `.field-help` IS TWO ROLES, SO THE 6px IS NOT ON THE CLASS

The obvious fix — change `.field-help { margin: 0 0 5px }` to a top margin — is
**wrong, and invisibly so**. Counted at this tip: `.field-help` has **44 render
sites in 22 non-test files**, and only **6** are a field's helper inside `.field`
(`FormModal.tsx`'s five variants and `CustomFields.tsx`'s multi-select). The other
~38 are standalone muted notes with no input above them at all — `RateScheduleWizard`'s
season, TOU and proration notes, `paymentsShared`'s `<summary>`, the three reports
parameter hints. **Re-spacing the class would have silently moved a fifth of the
product's forms to satisfy a rule about six elements.**

So the ratified 6px is written on the six kit sites as `mt-1.5 mb-0` — Tailwind's
own multiplier, 1.5 × 4px = 6px, emitted as `.mt-1\.5{margin-top:calc(var(--spacing)
* 1.5)}` and confirmed in the built sheet. Both files are on `route-b-migrated.txt`,
so the utilities are real rather than class names no stylesheet declares. `6px` is
off-scale on purpose: rule 39 says its 5px and 6px stand *because* rounding them to
scale steps destroys the 1 : 1 : 4 ratio that is the point of the clause.

### 3 · A FLEX `gap` CANNOT EXPRESS RULE 39, SO FIELD STACKS AND BLOCK STACKS ARE SPLIT

Rule 39 gives **two** values to two different adjacencies — 20px between two fields,
16px between blocks — and a container's single `gap` applies one value to both. The
four full-page asset forms stack **mixed** children: a lede `<p>`, fields, a `Note`,
a nested two-column grid.

The tempting general fix, `.field + .field { margin-top: 4px }`, is **wrong and would
have shipped a new misalignment**: in `AssetAddWizard`'s `grid grid-cols-2` rows the
two `SelectField`s are adjacent siblings in *different columns*, so it would push the
right-hand field 4px below the left-hand one — the exact defect step 1 was measuring.

So the split is by container: **a container whose children are fields carries 20px;
a container whose children are blocks keeps 16px.** Changed to `gap-5`: `.modal-body`
(the kit), `AssetFlowPages.tsx:197` (Reassign and Log repair share it), the five
`AssetAddWizard` step bodies, `AssetRetireWizard.tsx:310`. **Deliberately left at
`gap-4`:** `AssetRetireWizard.tsx` 236, 399 and 409, which hold a notice box, a
`Note` and a `MoneyCell` and contain no field at all.

⚠ **THIS IS THE HALF WITH NO GUARD AND THE NEXT FORM WILL GET IT WRONG.** Nothing
reads computed spacing, so a sixth wizard step written with `gap-4` is 16px and
every check in the repository passes over it. The durable answer is a kit-owned form
body, and it is **not** built here — it would have to be adopted by the five screen
lanes' containers in the same act, which is a wave of its own.

### 4 · WHERE THE HELPER GOES ON A DATE FIELD, WHICH RULE 39 DOES NOT CONTEMPLATE

`DatePickerField` renders a third element the anatomy has no slot for: the
`aria-hidden` regional echo (`field-date-display`), which redraws the typed value in
the tenant's format and renders **only** when the field has a value AND that format
differs from the browser's. Order chosen: **label → input → helper → echo.**

The reason is that rule 39 ratifies input → helper as a **figure**, 6px, and that is
only satisfiable when the helper is the element directly under the control; the echo
between them makes the gap the echo's height instead. The cost is that on a field
that *has* a value the regional rendering sits one line below its own box. Taken as
the lesser harm because the echo is decoration AT never sees, and because on every
fresh form — which is what a clerk meets — the echo is absent and the two orders are
identical. **Recorded rather than inferred, because it is a judgment and the next
lane will otherwise re-litigate it.**

### 5 · `DEF-MET-4974` IS **PARTIALLY-FIXED**, NOT CLOSED, AND MY BRIEFING SAID CLOSE IT

`DatePickerField` now takes optional `min` and `max` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, absent means
unbounded, so no existing date field moved). That is the half B14 rule 7 needed to
become *expressible*: before this, product-wide, there was exactly **one** `min=` on
any date input (`FilterBar.tsx:328`) and no screen could bound a date even where the
rule bounding it was already written.

**But the row names two things and rule 7 names three** — *"calendar affordance,
keyed entry, **Today shortcut**"* — and the Today affordance is not built. Building
it is a new control on **every** date field in the product plus a key in eleven
catalogues, which is a product-wide visual change no ruling has authorised. So the
row goes to `partially-fixed` with what remains written into it, rather than closed.
**No bound was set on any screen**; that is the screen lanes' work and setting one
here would have been this lane guessing at business rules it cannot see.

### 6 · THE INSTRUMENT EXITS 0 WHETHER THE RULE IS MET OR NOT

Worth one line because it is hard-won law 7's *"a check's output must distinguish
pass from fail to a reader"*. `cr092-lane3-field-anatomy.mjs` is a **measurement**,
and its exit code asserts only that every screen yielded fields — it returned **0 on
the fully-broken tree**. The pass/fail lives in the VERDICT block it prints. A lane
that runs it and reads `$?` will report success over 18 wrong fields.

## 2026-09-12 — SERVER PAGING APPROVED, AND "YOU CAN DO ACTUAL FIGURES" UNBLOCKS EVERY FINDING THAT NEEDED DATA

> ***"Okay - you can do actual figures"***

### THE RULING ON THE SCREEN (`AST-B-19` + `AST-B-24`)

The reads table pages on the server: **1–50 of 1,460**, rows-per-page, and
first / previous / next / last. Today **every read a meter has ever taken arrives
in one response**, and both endpoints fold the whole history in Python.

### THE RULING UNDERNEATH IT, WHICH IS WORTH MORE

**A lane may SEED the data a finding needs in order to reproduce it.** That is a
general permission and it closes a hole step 1 hit in three separate lanes:

| finding | why it could not be reproduced |
|---|---|
| the reads pager | the largest meter on any tenant holds **26 reads** |
| assignment history paging | **max 1 assignment** per asset |
| the work-order list | **all 65 work orders have `asset_id` null** |
| the maintenance table | **0 rows**, on all three tenants |
| the behind-the-meter export | **0 of 24** devices carry a `parent_asset_id` |
| the map's geo read | **0 geocoded premises** |

⚠ **THIS MATTERS BECAUSE THE MAINTENANCE PROCESS OPENS WITH *REPRODUCE — NEVER FIX
WHAT YOU HAVE NOT SEEN*, AND AN UNSEEABLE DEFECT IS THEREFORE UNFIXABLE UNDER OUR
OWN PROCESS.** Step 1 lane 2 put it exactly: these are *"structurally real and
unfalsifiable on this data — a step-2 lane following REPRODUCE will fail and must
not conclude otherwise."* Before this ruling the only lawful outcomes were *build
it blind* or *leave it*. **Now there is a third and it is the right one: make the
data, see the defect, fix it, see it gone.**

**The discipline that comes with it, so seeding does not become a new hazard:**
* **Seed into your OWN database on your own port.** Nothing is shared — there is no
  stack on 8401 and no seed to protect.
* **Say in the report WHAT was seeded and HOW MANY**, because a proof over 1,460
  rows a lane created is a different claim from one over rows that were always
  there, and the next reader must be able to tell.
* **Never seed the demo tenant to make a screenshot look better.** The data exists
  to make a defect visible, not to make a result presentable.

**Eight of the ten capabilities are now approved.** Only `AST-B-14`, the opening
read, is outstanding — and it carries a placement question rather than a
yes-or-no: the drawing puts it on **step 3 beside Install date**, away from the
register digits and unit a meter reading needs.

## 2026-09-12 — THE OPENING READ MOVES TO STEP 2, AND ALL TEN CAPABILITIES ARE NOW APPROVED

> ***"a) Build it as drawn — move it to step 2, beside the multiplier, register
> digits and the warning"***

**`AST-B-14` is the last of the ten.** The field becomes fillable **and moves**, out
of `AssignmentStep` and into step 2 beside the numbers that scale it.

### THE ARGUMENT IS THE PRODUCT'S OWN, WHICH IS WHY IT WON

Step 2 asks what the meter IS — `multiplier` (line 753), `register_digits` (761),
`unit` — and carries this, verbatim from `en.json`:

> *"A ×10 meter reading 4,286 means 42,860 units. Confirm against the meter face
> before saving."*

**Today `opening_read` sits on step 3**, with destination, premises, unit and
install date. **So the number the multiplier multiplies is typed one screen away
from the only warning that explains why it matters** — a clerk reads *"×10 means
42,860, check the meter face"*, presses Continue, and is asked for the reading
after the warning has gone. The blueprint calls that warning *"the best warning in
the module, and it is on the right screen"*; it is the FIELD that is on the wrong one.

### THE PRECISION THE CODE FORCES, AND IT IS NOT IN THE RULING

Step 2 is **two components, not one**:

| component | fields |
|---|---|
| `MeasuringSpecStep` | manufacturer, model, **multiplier, register_digits, unit**, serial_no, firmware_version, meter_type, size_class, net_metering |
| `DeviceSpecStep` | parent_asset_no, export_capacity_kw, test_interval_months, size_class, serial_no, manufacturer |

**The opening read belongs in `MeasuringSpecStep` ONLY.** A behind-the-meter device
has no register and takes no reading, and `DeviceSpecStep` has no multiplier for the
warning to describe. Putting it on "step 2" without that distinction would draw a
reading field on a solar inverter.

⚠ **AND THE RULING IS A MOVE, NOT AN ADDITION, WHICH CHANGES ITS RISK.** The spec's
own words are *"the column exists and the service takes it"* — true, but the field
also already exists on a step that submits it. **So this is a field changing
component, and `AssetAddWizard.tsx` is one file with a live lane in it.** It is wave
C work and cannot start until wave B lane 5 lands.

### HOW THIS QUESTION WENT WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT WENT RIGHT

**I put a false question to the PO**, asking whether to leave the field on step 3
*"where the drawing puts it"* — the drawing puts it on step 2. I had read a step 1
lane's report about **the code** as a statement about **the drawing**. Then, checking
that, my own screen-to-page index put step 3 at page 116 — **page 116's text reads
*"Continue from step 1"* and carries the multiplier warning, so it is step 2's.**
The index is right to within a page; anything that turns on WHICH page needs the page
read rather than the index trusted.

**All ten capabilities are now approved.** `AST-B-12`, `14`, `16`, `19`, `21`, `22`,
`24`, `25`, `27`, `28`.

**Version `2.237.2`.** Two rows, `DEF-MET-4971` and `DEF-MET-4972`. One is closed,

Tenant **`brazosbend`**, which holds **14 assets** (not the blueprint's 126;

FAIL DEF-MET-4971 — the saved type reached the database

* **`KPIStrip`** — one declaration at `gap: 6px`, 33 non-test mounts.
* **The pager** — and this one changed the sizing. `table.pager.pageOf` =
  *"Page {{page}} of {{pages}}"* **already exists in all eleven catalogues** and **is**
  rendered, by `components/ListPager.tsx`, which 9 files mount. `DataTable`'s inline
  pager, which 54 files mount, does not use it. **The two pagers in this product
  disagree and the smaller one is correct**, so the fix needs no new copy and no
  translation round.

### THE SEQUENCING THAT MATTERS

**The row-action work starts after `CR-092-BRC01` wave B lane 1 lands.** The worst
instance of the cap — six controls in one cell — is `AssetRegistryPage.tsx:663`, and
that file has a live lane in it. Two lanes on one file is law 11's mechanism two,
which reverts by subtraction and passes every check in law 11.

### AND A CORRECTION TO THE RECORD I MADE AND HAD TO UNMAKE

While raising this CR I "corrected" `CR-092-BRC01`'s scope line, which reads
*"first/last page"*, to say the row-action cap instead — on the reasoning that the
four `DEF-SHL-494x` rows were the four the ruling moved. **That was wrong, and the
way it was wrong is the pattern this CR keeps hitting: I took the four ids a prefix
grep returned and treated them as the measurement of what the ruling moved.** The
pager row is real, is `DEF-449`, and has been open since 2026-08-21; it simply does
not carry the `SHL` prefix because it was filed before the module-tagged scheme
existed. The edit was replaced with the five-row table above before anything was
pushed. **A prefix is not a scope.**

## 2026-09-12 — `CR-092` STEP 2 WAVE B LANE 4 · THE FOUR ACTIONS: A CLERK NAMES THE TECHNICIAN, AND THE RULING'S OWN PREMISE TURNED OUT TO BE HALF TRUE

Five rows built — `DEF-MET-4973` `4974` `4975` `4977` `4978` — and one new one
found by the work (`DEF-MET-4991`). Four judgments were made where the rules ran
out; each is written here with what it cost, because a judgment recorded is the
deliverable and a question would have been the failure to make one (law 13).

### 1 · `BR-AST-533` SAYS "A NEW READ", AND ONE THAT SERVES A CLERK ALREADY EXISTED

The PO ruled *"a) Let a clerk read the crew list (name + email only)"* and the
rule says, in as many words, that this is **a NEW read and not a widening of
`GET /users`**. Both halves are right, and the premise underneath the first one
was not quite what we thought.

**Measured, with a real Billing Clerk session on `pine-hill`:**

| read | a Billing Clerk gets |
|---|---|
| `GET /users` | **403 `BR-IDN-009`** — `SystemAdminOnly`, unchanged |
| `GET /work/technicians` | **200 · 7 rows** — and it already did |

`GET /work/technicians` is `CR-070` wave F's *add a technician* picker and carries
`WorkOrdersReadAnyWriteAdminOrClerk`, which admits all three office roles. So the
step-1 finding *"there is NO screen in the product where a Billing Clerk can look
a technician's uuid up"* was true **of screens** and not of the API.

**It was still not the read the rule describes, and the reason is the deciding
one.** That route serves `role_code`, `status` and `has_profile` beside the name —
exactly the three things `BR-AST-533` names as not-served — and they cannot be
dropped from it, because `Work-023` marks who already has a profile. **So the
choice was between narrowing a route another screen depends on, projecting in the
front end, or a second narrow read.**

**Chosen: a second narrow read, `GET /work/crew-directory`, serving `id`, `name`,
`email` and nothing else.** A front-end projection was rejected on one argument
and it is worth keeping: **`role_code` would still have crossed the wire into the
clerk's browser, and *role-safe* is a statement about what LEAVES the server**, not
about what a component chooses to render. Both reads share one query
(`identity_seam.staff_user_choices`), so *who works here* still has one answer and
two projections of it.

⚠ **THE TEST HOLDS BOTH HALVES AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** *A clerk may read the
crew directory* is worth nothing unless *a clerk still may not read `GET /users`*
stays true beside it — the second is the half that goes green by doing nothing,
and is therefore the half that quietly stops being true. Widening `UsersView` was
tried as a sabotage and the suite went red on it.

### 2 · THE DEGRADE THE RULING DOES NOT CURE — A CONTROL MAY NOT CHANGE TYPE

`BR-AST-533`'s own ⚠ names a second fault and leaves it: the fallback fires on
`techQuery.isSuccess` with `retry: false`, so a 500, a timeout or an offline
browser degraded exactly as a 403 did, and a **System Admin** was told *"Your role
can't list users"* — a statement about their own permissions that was false.

**Ruled here: the technician field is ONE control on every role and in every
state.** When the list cannot load it stays a picker and is **disabled with its
reason** (`BR-SHL-025`, and `BR-AST-534` extending it from role to state), and the
sentence says what happened rather than guessing why — *"The crew list didn't
load. Save without it, or reload."* The field is optional, which is what makes
disabling it honest rather than obstructive: the repair still saves.

**The reasoning generalises past this screen: a control that changes TYPE under
failure teaches a person the product is two different products.** The old fallback
swapped a picker for a text box, and the text box asked for a uuid — B14 rule 31
broken for precisely the role `BR-AST-038` wrote the screen for.

### 3 · WHICH DATE BOUNDS ARE OURS TO SET, AND TWO THAT ARE NOT

`DEF-MET-4974` asked for B14 rule 7's bounds on five date inputs. **Three are set
and two are deliberately not, and the rule applied is the same in both
directions: mirror a bound the product already states, and invent none.**

| input | bound | where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| log repair `date` | `max` = today | `services.py:1376` refuses a future date, and the help has said so since the screen shipped |
| retire `retire_date` | `min` = install date | `services.py:1516`, `assets.retire_before_install` |
| reassign `effective_date` | `min` = the current assignment's `from_date` | `services.py:1760`, `BR-AST-017` |
| **both `final_read_date`s** | **none** | **nothing states one** |

⚠ **`max = today` ON A FINAL READ IS THE TEMPTING ONE AND IT IS WRONG.** Left
blank, that field already resolves to the effective (or retire) date, which may
lawfully be in the future for a planned move — so capping it at today would make
the field **stricter than the path its own blank value takes**. Choosing a bound
anyway would be inventing a rule. The absence is written into the code beside the
field rather than left to be re-derived.

⚠ **AND `install_date` WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WRONG BOUND FOR THE REASSIGN DATE**,
which is worth recording because it is the one on the payload and therefore the
easy one to reach for. An assignment can start well after installation, so it
would accept dates the server refuses. **A wrong bound is worse than no bound:
it promises the server will accept what it will not.** The right date needed one
extra read (`GET /assets/{id}/assignments`, `AnyTenantRole`), and it degrades to
unbounded on any failure.

**Every bound ships with the sentence that explains it.** A greyed-out calendar
with no words is `DEF-MET-4973`'s greyed-out submit wearing a different control:
a refusal a person can see and cannot account for.

### 4 · WHERE A CLERK WITH NO TEMPLATE SHOULD GO — ANSWERED IN COPY, NOT IN A CONTROL

`AST-B-10`'s done-test asks for *"a control that goes somewhere"*. The three
candidates were the Work templates screen (**admin-only, so a clerk meets a second
refusal**), a template-less work order (**the form derives the order's `type` from
the template's name, so there is nothing to send**), and back to the asset (**which
the `Cancel` button and the `← Asset` link already do** — step 1 counted only
`<a>` elements and so counted neither).

**So the forward step is stated in words and no control was invented:** the
refusal now reads *"No template applies to this kind of asset. Ask an admin to add
one."* — two sentences of six words or fewer, which is B14 rule 33's own shape.
**`DEF-MET-4973` is therefore `partially-fixed` and not closed**: the reason is
carried, and a navigating control remains unbuilt because both destinations that
would work are unruled.

### 5 · THE ONE THAT WAS FOUND RATHER THAN ASSIGNED — `DEF-MET-4991`

Adding `max={today}` to the log-repair date turned its unit test green and
**changed nothing in the browser**. `App.tsx` mounts all three action screens with
**no props at all**, and `today` comes from one — so `prefill` was `undefined` too
and all three date fields had been rendering `value=""` in the shipped product
against `BR-PAY-033`'s *"the UI ALWAYS proposes a pre-filled default date"*.

⚠ **EVERY UNIT TEST ON THESE SCREENS PASSES `today="2026-08-16"` EXPLICITLY.** The
fixture supplied what the router does not, so it could not tell a wired screen
from an unwired one — hard-won law 2's fixture clause, one layer up from the
`MemoryRouter` case it was written for. The guard added beside the fix asserts the
bound **and** the prefill on a page rendered **without** the prop, which is the way
`App.tsx` mounts it.

`components/DateCell.tsx` gains `todayInZone(timeZone)`. **The tenant's zone and
not UTC**, on purpose: `billingOpsShared.todayIso()` slices an ISO instant, which
is right for the write it stamps and wrong for a `max` of *not in the future*,
where a tenant behind UTC would be refused their own today for several hours every
evening.

### 6 · TWO DRAWINGS THAT DRAW WHAT THE PRODUCT DOES NOT HAVE — NEITHER BUILT

* **Figure 35 draws a `Cancel` on retire step 1.** Measured footer at 1440 and
  1280: `["Continue"]` alone. The redrawn figure 36 replaces it with `Save as
  draft` marked **NEW**, which is `AST-B-28` and not this lane's. **Step 1's
  finding is confirmed against the running product.**
* **Figure 42 draws the raise form's footer as `Cancel · Raise work order ✓`**;
  the product draws the commit first. **B14 rule 38 names this case
  exactly** — *"that the footer puts Cancel on the left … is not layout, it is FORM
  CONSTRUCTION"* — so **the drawing loses, the divergence is recorded, and nothing
  is built for it.**

### WHAT THIS LANE DID NOT DO, STATED

**The Today shortcut** (B14 rule 7's other half) is a new control on every date
field in the product plus a key in eleven catalogues and **no ruling authorises
it** — wave A left it for the same reason. **`BR-AST-534`'s retired-asset
instance** is the detail page's door (`AST-B-02`, lane 2): the raise form's own
payload carries no status, so building it here would have meant a server change
under a row that is not this lane's. **The four shared-table rows** are
`CR-093-BRC01`'s.

## 2026-09-12 — `CR-092` STEP 2 WAVE B LANE 1 · THE REGISTRY: FOUR FIGURES SERVED, 319 QUERIES BECOME 2, AND A BASELINE I RAISED ON PURPOSE

**Lane:** CR-092-BRC01 step 2, the Assets registry (screens 01–06). **Ten rows.**
**Version `2.237.5`.** Built at `ce623f444`. Full record:
`04-docs/05-modules/05-assets/conformance/CR-092-lane1-registry-step2.md`.

### 1 · THE KPI FIGURES ARE SERVED, AND THE CARDS COUNT THE TAB RATHER THAN THE QUERY

`DEF-MET-4953`, and it is PO ruling 2 of 2026-09-12 (*"a) Fix the figures"*)
being kept rather than a new decision. Reproduced on **pine-hill** at 1440:
`?tab=meters` drew **four em-dashes** over a list reading *1–50 of 110*; so did
page two; so did a filtered view with its whole six-row result on screen.

**The judgment worth recording is WHAT the four cards count.** `GET /assets` now
carries `kpis`, and those figures are the **tab's whole population** — not the
filtered query. Two reasons, and the first is decisive: the client only ever
rendered these numbers when there was no search and no filter (`kpiRowsComplete`),
so the tab's population **is** what the four cards have always meant; serving
them keeps the meaning and drops the condition. Second, narrowing them with the
filter would make *In inventory* and *Meters in service* mutually exclusive and
at most one card non-zero, which is not a strip anybody drew.

It rides the LIST answer rather than its own route, for the reason `api.py`
already gives about `?terms=`: two routes could draw one tab's figures over
another tab's list and nothing would go red.

**Proved to be the same arithmetic, not a re-definition:** the served values were
compared with `metersKpis`'s own predicates row by row, and the browser's count
at `per=200` before the change read the same four numbers — *104 · 7 · 9 · 1%*.

### 2 · `asset_list` RETURNS A QUERYSET, AND THE FOUR PYTHON FILTERS BECOME SQL

`DEF-MET-4951` + `DEF-MET-4962`. Measured on **pine-hill**, 110 meters:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `f.assigned=true` | **111 queries** | **2** |
| `f.service=water` | **209** | **2** |
| both, returning 53 rows | **319** | **2** |
| `GET /assets/geo` | **241** | **8** |

`LIMIT`/`OFFSET` now appear in the generated SQL — asserted on the SQL string,
not inferred.

⚠ **`test_due` IS THE DECISION HERE, BECAUSE IT IS NOT A JOIN.** It is
`add_months(last_test_date, n) <= today`, and `add_months` CLAMPS the day to the
target month's length. No portable ORM expression does that — a 30-day
`timedelta` is a different answer and `INTERVAL` is spelled differently on
Postgres and on the SQLite the suite runs. **That is hard-won law 14's shape
exactly**: the obvious version is green on every machine and wrong on the one
that matters. So the predicate compares WHOLE MONTHS, which both databases can
do, and the day-clamp collapses to a constant the caller already knows because
`today.day >= days_in(today)` is only true on the last day of a month.

**It is not assumed to agree with `test_due()` — it is compared with it**, row by
row, over seven cadences (31 Jan + 1 month, a leap day, a 0-month cadence) across
66 simulated `today`s spanning fourteen months.

### 3 · I RAISED A GATE BASELINE, AND HERE IS WHY THAT WAS NOT THE FORBIDDEN MOVE

`G14` pins `assets.explainer.sub_meters` to r10's own sentence; `DEF-527` adopted
it on **2026-08-22**. **B14 rule 32 was ratified on 2026-08-31** (*"too much
content - desctiption is too much for clark to read"*) and rule 33 before it, and
both are LATER law: one sentence per section, six words per sentence. r10's is
24 words in two, and its second sentence names the four row actions visible three
inches below it.

`CLAUDE.md` settles which authority wins and it is not the gate's: r10's
`UI-RULES.md` *"is its SOURCE, not its authority — B14 wins and every divergence
is stamped there."* So `EXPLAINERS_NOT_IN_R10` moves **2 → 3**, with the key, both
rules, the dates and the reasoning written onto the constant in the same commit.
A fourth stale explainer still goes red.

**Raising a baseline is normally the single most damaging move available** — it
turns a true finding into a permanently invisible one — so the bar is a named key,
a named rule that outranks the one being relaxed, and the wording landing in the
same commit. The alternative was leaving a ratified copy rule broken because an
older gate encoded an older decision, and that is how a gate stops being a check
and becomes a veto.

### 4 · TWO CARRY-OVER QUESTIONS ON SCREEN 05c, DECIDED RATHER THAN ASKED

The blueprint's own arithmetic for 05c does not close: it counts ten as-built
elements and lists eleven dispositions. Step 1 recorded it and said *"whoever
builds 05c must decide where those two go"*. Decided, both toward preservation:

* **The Programme total survives**, beneath the table rather than inside it — a
  real served pair with no other home, and a total row inside a `DataTable` would
  mean a second table, which is the very rule-36 breach the rebuild ends.
* **The Turn into work panel survives** on the forecast section. Neither is listed
  as removed; the ONE field-bearing removal the document instructs is the Asset
  value panel, and that one IS removed (*"remove this - Asset value"*, PO
  2026-09-11) with its stated cost: `buy_value` and `present_value` are computed
  nowhere else in the product.

### 5 · WHERE I DISAGREE WITH ONE OF MY OWN ROWS

`DEF-MET-4950` names three controls that ignore `writeBlockedReason`. **Two are
gated** — the Lifecycle wrench and *Set up an exchange rule*, both of which open
a write. **`Parts in Work →` is deliberately NOT gated**: it navigates to the
parts REGISTER, a read screen a read-only role may open, and BR-SHL-025 gates
*forbidden actions*. Gating it would hide a capability the role has. Step 1 §5.3
reached the same reading independently. The row is `partially-fixed` with the
disagreement written into it rather than quietly skipped.

### 6 · `DEF-MET-4963`: THE ROW SAID THREE OFF-SCALE ANCHORS. IT IS FIVE. NOTHING IS SWEPT.

Re-measured at 1920, 1440 and 1280. Beside the rail item (`9px 12px`, gap 10) and
the status pill (`2px 9px`, gap 5), `main.view` is `24/24/56` at ≤1440 **and
`28px 32px 64px` above it** — two more off-scale values the row does not name
because it measured at one width — and `.card` carries `padding: 28px`.

**All five are in the shell and reach every screen in the product**, so this is
the same shape as the four shared-table rows the PO ruled out of scope the same
day. The row's own prevention says a sweep without a decision is how a product
acquires a fourth — and re-measuring found the fourth and fifth before anyone
swept. **Stated, not made.**

### 7 · A DEFECT MY OWN TESTS CAUGHT THAT THE BROWSER COULD NOT

The rebuilt Lifecycle tables were handed `loading={view.isFetching}`, which drew
**eight skeleton bars over a populated table** on every background refetch. `tsc`,
eslint and a browser walk at 1440 all passed over it — **in a browser the fetch
has settled before anybody looks.** The server-rendered test is what saw it.
Worth recording because the usual lesson runs the other way: here the suite
caught what the walk could not, and both were needed.

### 8 · ONE MORE READING NOBODY HAD: `geo_view` WAS 241 QUERIES AND STEP 1 COULD NOT SEE IT

Step 1 measured `GET /assets/geo` at **1 query** and said, correctly, that the
number was worthless: `brazosbend` has no geocoded premises, so the function
returned at its first branch. On **pine-hill** it costs **241** — a service lookup
and a tenant-today seam call per marker. It is **8** now. **A measurement over a
population that cannot exercise the code path is not a small measurement, it is
no measurement**, and step 1 was right to label it rather than report it.

## 2026-09-12 — B14 RULE 40: THE PAGE-HEAD TITLE IS 32px, AND THE TOKEN SHEET HAD BEEN ASSERTING IT FOR THREE WEEKS WITHOUT IT BEING TRUE

**What was shown to the PO, in plain English with the figure**, after they asked
what the line *"Page titles render at the wizard size on 136 of 137 screens"*
meant: that every screen has a big heading at the top; that we have two sizes —
**40px** for a step-by-step wizard and **32px** for an ordinary screen; that the
heading was drawing at **40 on 136 of the 137 screens**, so the size we called
the default was the one almost nothing used; and a rendered picture of the two
side by side.

**The ruling, verbatim:** ***"The heading is drawing at 40 on 136 of the 137
screens. - use 32 pixels — for every ordinary screen. if that is our rule"***,
then, unprompted and in the same words: ***"Please use 32 pixels"***.

### ⚠ IT WAS NOT OUR RULE, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY

The PO's *"if that is our rule"* was a fair challenge to the premise and the
honest answer was **no**. B14 held **no ratified rule about title size at all** —
it has rule 2 (*one page header*), rule 5 (*two button sizes*) and rule 20 (*one
table type size*), and nothing about the page-head title.

What existed was a **comment beside a token**: `tokens.css` line 203 reads
`--text-h2: 32px; /* page-head title — THE APP DEFAULT, every screen head */`,
with `--text-h1: 40px; /* full-page wizard title */` above it, both since the
type scale was ruled on 2026-08-19. **The note asserted an app default and
nothing in the product made it true.** That is hard-won law 1 in its purest
form — *a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee* — and it is worth
recording that the law's own example list now has a fourth member.

**The PO's instruction is what makes it a rule**, so it is ratified as **B14 rule
40** and `CLAUDE.md`'s pointer moved from THIRTY to **THIRTY-ONE (1–21 and
31–40)** ⚠ **IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE RULE** — the sixth-time-lucky application
of the lesson that file has recorded against itself five times. Counted from
B14's own status table rather than trusted from a pointer: **31 rows carry a
lifecycle cell, 22–30 absent** as designed.

### THE MECHANISM, AND WHY ALMOST NOBODY ESCAPED IT

`PageHeader` rendered a bare `<h1>`; `global.css` sizes a bare `h1` at
`--text-h1` = 40px. The **only** way to get 32px was `titleAs="h2"`, which
**demotes the heading level** — so a screen wanting the right size had to give up
its `<h1>` and leave the document outline with no page title.

**That is why exactly ONE caller in 137 ever used it**, and that caller turns out
to be right for a different reason entirely: `TemplateDetail` is drawn inside
Settings, which has already written *"Settings"* as the document's `h1`, and two
`h1`s is two page titles in one outline. **It was not opting into a size; it was
protecting an outline.** Left alone, deliberately.

**So the fix decouples the two:** the size is now set on the element
(`className="text-h2"`) on **both** branches, and the level answers to the
document outline and nothing else.

### NO WIZARD EXCEPTION — RULE 2 ALREADY SETTLED IT

The token sheet reserves 40px for a *"full-page wizard title"*, which reads like
a case for keeping two sizes. It is not, and the reason is a rule we already
ratified: **rule 2 says *"One page header. EVERY screen, including task pages and
workflows"*** — and **15 wizards mount this very component**. A second size for
them would re-create the exact defect being closed, whose title is *two
page-title sizes and nothing splits them by kind*. `--text-h1` stays a token; it
is simply not a page head.

### MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED — 40px → 32px

Through the **built** stylesheet at 1280 and 1440, via
`10-scripts/render-checks/cr093-page-title-size.mjs`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| size | **40px** | **32px** |
| weight | 800 | 800 (unchanged) |
| line-height | 44.8px | 35.84px |

⚠ **THE INSTRUMENT READS `getComputedStyle` AGAINST `dist/`, AND THAT IS THE
WHOLE REASON IT EXISTS.** A `toContain("text-h2")` assertion passes whether or
not any stylesheet declares the class — a Tailwind utility written in a file
absent from `route-b-migrated.txt` sits in the DOM and styles **nothing**, with
`tsc`, eslint and every assertion green (the UI skill's §7.1). Only a computed
style against what actually ships can tell those two apart. `PageHeader.tsx` is
on the ledger, and the compiled stylesheet came back **byte-identical** —
161,403 bytes, same content hash — because `text-h2` was already declared. **No
class was added to any stylesheet**, which is rule 21 satisfied rather than
argued.

The instrument has a `--before` mode that renders the pre-rule markup and **must
fail at 40px**; it was run first and did (law 7's red proof, through the same
entry point as the green run).

### ⚠ THE BLAST RADIUS WAS IN THE TESTS, AND ONE OF THEM WAS MADE INCAPABLE OF FAILING

Putting a class on the element broke **18 assertions across 12 test files** that
matched the literal string `"<h1>"`. Two shapes, and the second is the one worth
recording:

* **`indexOf("<h1>")` for ORDER** (page header, assets registry, premises): it
  now answers **-1**, and **a negative index compares as less-than everything**,
  so the assertion reports the order as correct over a page that has lost its
  title entirely. Rewritten to find `"<h1"` and to assert the index is
  **non-negative first**.
* **`expect(html).not.toContain("<h1>")`** in `AccountDetailPage.test.tsx:958`:
  after the change that string can never occur, so **the check would have passed
  forever regardless of what the page rendered** — law 7's *structurally
  incapable of failing*, manufactured by a change three modules away. Rewritten
  to `not.toMatch(/<h1[\s>]/)`.

**The general lesson: a matcher keyed to a literal tag is keyed to markup that is
not its subject.** None of these 18 assertions was about the tag; they were about
order, presence and text. Every one of them now matches the thing it is actually
asserting.

`AssetDetail.test.tsx` carries two of the same shape and was **NOT touched** — a
wave C lane is live in it, and two lanes in one file is law 11's mechanism two.
The exact replacement was sent to that lane to land in its own commit.

### WHAT WAS MEASURED AND HOW, GIVEN A TREE FULL OF OTHER LANES' WORK

The shared working tree currently holds three lanes' uncommitted edits —
including an `AssetDetailPage.tsx` that imports a module not yet on disk — so
`tsc` and the suite are **unmeasurable in it**, and any number taken there would
be someone else's. Both baselines were therefore taken in **private
`git worktree`s at the tip `404ae10c0`**: one clean, one holding only the 14
files of this change. That is law 12's own recommendation used as a measuring
instrument rather than as a recovery.

Two `UnitsPage.test.tsx` failures met along the way (`the premises picker is a
SEARCHABLE combobox`, `the destination picker never offers the premise the unit
is already on`) **reproduce at the clean tip with none of this change present** —
dated rather than dismissed, per law 7's habit (1). They are neighbours of
`DEF-MET-4718`, which is open.

## 2026-09-12 — CR-092 WAVE C LANE 3: PAGING INSIDE AN ASSET, AND WHY THERE ARE TWO SHAPES RATHER THAN ONE

`AST-B-24` (PO-approved 2026-09-12) · `DEF-MET-4995` (filed by this lane before
it was fixed) · `DEF-MET-4962`'s remainder · `NFR-3` · `NFR-5`.

Six reads in this module answered without a page parameter. They do not now.
Everything below is a judgment the rules did not settle, recorded with the figure
that settled it.

### 1 · THE PROCESS QUESTION, ANSWERED PER ITEM RATHER THAN ONCE

*Can a user do this task in the product today?* For the three lists inside an
asset the honest answer is **no** — nobody can page through a meter's read
history, because there is nothing to page with — so `AST-B-19`/`AST-B-24` sit in
`CR-092` §6b's **BUILD** column and were built through r11. For
`/assets/stock`, `/assets/lifecycle` and `/assets/geo` the answer is **yes**: the
three tabs load and are wrong about how much they load, which is
**MAINTENANCE**, and `DEF-MET-4962` is the row they were reproduced against.
Different processes on one branch, and saying which is which is cheaper than
arguing about it later.

### 2 · TWO SHAPES, AND THE REASON IS NOT TASTE

**A plain list answers `{count, next, previous, results}`** — the envelope
`StandardPagination` builds, the one `07-frontend/src/api/paginated.ts` declares
and `G114` polices. Three endpoints take it.

**A composite payload carries `<key>_window: {total, page, per, pages}` beside
its list, and keeps every existing key.** Three endpoints take that.

The alternative was one shape everywhere, and it does not exist: `/assets/stock`
answers a list **beside** KPI figures and `/assets/lifecycle` answers **three**
lists beside a value panel. There is no way for one of those lists to take
`count`/`results` without stealing the four names from the others, and inventing
`certifications_count` beside a real `count` is exactly the second description of
one idea that `paginated.ts` exists to prevent. The window is not invented here
either — `GET /imports/{id}` has served `rejects_window` since `DEF-766`, for
this reason.

**The test for which shape: is the payload the list, or does the payload
CONTAIN a list?** That is checkable by a reader, which a taste argument is not.

### 3 · THE READS TAB PAGES BY DATE, NOT BY ROW, AND `count` SAYS SO

`asset_reads` folds `BR-AST-029`'s typed pair into ONE row per read date. A
single-register meter therefore serves one row per date and a three-register TOU
meter serves three. Paging the ROWS would put half a meter's registers on page 1
and half on page 2 — a reading event cut in half by an implementation detail.

So the paging unit is the **read date**, `count` is the number of dates, and a
page's LENGTH varies. The cost of that choice is real and is stated in A11
Addendum r7 rather than left for a client to infer from a page that is sometimes
50 rows and sometimes 150: a pager drawing *"144 reads"* over a table of 150 rows
is off by the register count. The alternative was worse and nothing else was
available, because the fold cannot be expressed in SQL.

### 4 · A BREAKING SHAPE CHANGE, TAKEN DELIBERATELY, WITH ITS BLAST RADIUS COUNTED

`/reads` and `/assignments` answered a **bare array** and `/maintenance` an
object keyed `rows`. They now answer the envelope. **That breaks four shipped
front-end consumers**, and they are named rather than discovered:
`AssetDetailPage.tsx` (twice), `AssetFlowPages.tsx`, `ReadDetailPage.tsx` and
`accountDetailTabs.tsx` — three feature areas across two modules, all of them
reached through three wrappers in `07-frontend/src/api/endpoints.ts`.

**This lane edited none of them and that was the instruction**, so the break is a
sequenced handoff and not a surprise. What is recorded here is that the count was
taken BEFORE the change rather than after: the blast-radius step of the
maintenance process is what turned *"lane 1 owns the asset detail page"* into
*"two of the four consumers belong to no lane in this wave"*, which is a fact the
coordinator needs and the code cannot state.

**The rejected alternative, and why:** serving the envelope AND keeping `rows` as
an alias would have broken nothing. It was refused because two names for one list
on one endpoint is the `DEF-WRK-4098` shape with our fingerprints on it — a
client reads whichever it finds, and the day one of them stops being written the
screen renders `no results` in perfect silence.

### 5 · THE MONEY PATH IS NOT NARROWED TO PAGE A SCREEN

`apps.metering.selectors.typed_reads_for_asset` is the read **rating** consumes
(`US-AST-012` TC-3). The cheap way to page the Reads tab is a `limit=` on it.
`DEF-MET-4101` had already refused that move in those words — *narrowing a shared
money-path contract to fix a display is how a money path acquires a defect* — so
the display got its own two functions and the money path kept the one it had.
The row shape both answer with is built by one private function, so they cannot
drift. Written up as `BR-AST-536`.

### 6 · WHAT THE SEEDED DATA FOUND THAT NO FIXTURE COULD

PO 2026-09-12, verbatim: ***"Okay - you can do actual figures"***. 240 rows were
seeded on ONE asset of ONE tenant (`10-scripts/cr092_lane3_seed.sql`, pine-hill
water meter `M-88402`) because **the largest list inside any asset on any tenant
was 26 rows** and the page-size floor is 50 — so page 1 was the whole list
everywhere and a missing pager had no symptom anywhere.

**It immediately found a defect nobody had filed:** `assignments` called the unit
seam inside its row loop and cost **64 queries for 61 seats**. That is
`DEF-MET-4951`'s shape, inside the asset, and it had never executed twice in this
product's life because every asset on every seeded tenant has exactly ONE seat.
`stock_view` was paying a metering seam call per spare for the same reason.

**Measured against real PostgreSQL, before → after:**

| read | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Reads tab, 144 dates | 40,853 B, growing one row at a time | **14,199 B a page, flat** |
| Assignment history, 61 seats | **64 queries** | **4** |
| Maintenance, 60 entries | 20,562 B | 17,134 B a page, flat |
| Map, 123 markers | 66,104 B in one shot | **26,961 B and `total: 123`** |

**And every composite payload was diffed field by field against the old one**:
`stock.kpis`, `stock.rows`, all three lifecycle lists and the asset-value panel
come back **byte-identical**, including the `aged_over_12_months` count now
computed in SQL and the `value_at_cost` now summed in SQL. The only difference
anywhere is that the map answers 50 of its 123 markers. That comparison is the
check that a performance change did not quietly become a behaviour change, and it
is cheap enough that it should be the habit.

### 7 · A CLAMPED-MONTH COMPARISON, FOR THE SECOND TIME IN THIS CR

The Inventory tab's *aged over 12 months* KPI was a Python loop over the estate.
Moving it into SQL runs straight into the problem lane 1 hit with `test_due`:
`add_months` clamps the day to the target month's length and no portable ORM
expression does — `timedelta(365)` is a different answer and `INTERVAL` differs
between PostgreSQL and the SQLite this suite runs on, which is hard-won law 14's
exact shape, green on every machine and wrong on the one that matters.

`_aged_q` is spelled the way `test_due_q` is, in whole months, and it is **not
assumed to agree with the derivation — it is walked against it**, 30 purchase
dates × 30 simulated observation days. A correct approximation with an exhaustive
test beats a wrong exact one, and this is the exhaustive test.

### 8 · WHAT WAS LEFT, AND WHY, RATHER THAN LEFT SILENTLY

* **`GET /assets/geo` is a PAGE and is still not a VIEWPORT. `DEF-MET-4301`
  stays OPEN.** That row is right that a map of page 1 of 3 is a map of the wrong
  day; a viewport read is a change to what the map screen DOES and belongs with
  the screen. Bounding the payload is not that change and does not claim to be —
  and `assets_window.total` is exactly the figure an *"and 38,400 more, zoom
  in"* line needs.
* **`lifecycle`'s certifications are filtered in SQL and SORTED IN PYTHON.** The
  filter — *has a computable due date* — is exactly expressible; the ORDER BY is
  the clamped-month problem again, and an ORDER BY that disagreed with
  `next_test_date` would put a row on the wrong PAGE, where it would be missing
  from one page and duplicated on another, invisibly. That is worse than a slow
  sort. The residue is bounded by the CADENCED population and closing it needs
  the clamped due date as a stored column — a schema change, not this lane's.
* **`stock`'s per-type roll-up still walks the whole available set in Python.**
  It walks a seven-column `values_list` now rather than building a model instance
  per asset, and its seam call is batched; the grouping pass itself wants a
  stored roll-up, which is again a schema decision.
* **`warranty_groups` and `age_forecast.rows` are served WHOLE, deliberately** —
  both key off the type catalogue, so they are bounded by how many kinds of thing
  a utility buys rather than by how many it owns. A page over a four-row roll-up
  is furniture.
* **The front half (`AST-B-19`) is not built and is not this lane's.** The
  handoff is in the lane report and in A11 Addendum r7.
