## 2026-09-12 — THE ASSET WIZARDS: A READING THAT CAN BE TYPED IN, A SHARE THAT CAN BE SET, AND A WAY OUT THAT IS NOT *BACK* (`CR-092-BRC01` step 2 wave C lane 2, `2.237.8`)

Three PO-approved capabilities, built onto `404ae10c0`. Each is recorded here with
the judgment it needed, because in each case the rules ran out somewhere.

### 1 · `AST-B-14` — THE OPENING READ. **A DOCUMENTED REFUSAL WAS OVERTURNED, AND THE OVERTURNED REASONING IS KEPT**

> PO, verbatim: ***"Build it as drawn — move it to step 2, beside the multiplier,
> register digits and the warning"***

The add wizard drew *Opening read* on step 3 as a **disabled** box whose helper said a
reading *"cannot be captured here"*, and the file's own exceptions footer gave the
reason: *"no published seam lets assets write a `meter_reads` row at create"*.

**That reasoning was correct and the conclusion was wrong, and the difference is worth
naming: the seam was not missing, it was UNWRITTEN.** `metering.capture_final_read`
has committed a manual read inside the CALLER's transaction since the CR-028 debt
sweep (`BR-AST-022`, D5), refusing the whole operation when it cannot. An opening read
is that same act at the other end of an asset's life. *"No seam exists"* had quietly
become *"nobody has written the second door"*, and nothing re-reads a stated absence.

**The judgment: ONE BODY, TWO DOORS.** `_capture_manual_read` is extracted, and
`capture_final_read` and `capture_opening_read` both call it. Everything that varies
between them is a **string** — which field a refusal names, which sentence a clerk
reads, the row's `source_detail`, the audit action. Nothing about the arithmetic, the
lineage law or the BR-MET-020/022 validation set varies at all. A second implementation
would have been a second place to decide what a typed reading means, on a path where
being wrong makes every bill from that meter wrong (hard-won law 5's shape).
`capture_final_read`'s seven existing tests pass unchanged, which is the proof the
extraction is behaviour-preserving.

**The failure rule is the contract, and it is the strict one.** The capture runs inside
`create_asset`'s own `transaction.atomic()`, so **a refused reading takes the asset with
it**. The alternative — create the meter, drop the reading, tell nobody — puts a meter
into service reading from a baseline nobody knows, found on the first bill. B14 rule 11
says so on screen before the commit: *"Saved to Meter Reads first. If it fails, nothing
is created."* Proved by sabotage: moving the capture outside the `atomic()` fails the
case with `assert 1 == 0` on the asset count.

**The read date defaults SERVER-SIDE, and that is a judgment rather than a detail.** The
drawing's helper is *"Defaults to the install date"* — and the install date is chosen on
the NEXT step, so a client-side default would have to guess forward or rewrite itself
when step 3 is answered. `_capture_opening_read` applies it, so the wizard and a direct
API call cannot disagree about what a dateless reading means. A reading with neither a
date nor an install date is REFUSED rather than dated today.

**Worked figure:** a water meter created on `brazosbend` with `Opening read 12481`, no
read date and `install_date 2026-09-01` leaves ONE committed `meter_reads` row —
`current_value 12481.000000`, `prior_value null`, `unit kgal`, `source manual/opening_read`,
`read_at 2026-09-01`.

⚠ **AND THE CONTROL WAS DELETED FROM STEP 3, NOT UN-DISABLED THERE.** Wave B lane 5 left
that instruction at the control and it is hard-won law 2's mirror: a refusal is a hold,
and the day a hold expires the thing that was holding goes with it. The dead catalogue
key `assets.add.openingReadUnavailable` went in the same commit, in all eleven.

### 2 · `AST-B-27` — THE ALLOCATION SHARE, WIZARD HALF. **A COLUMN WITH A READER AND NO WRITER, FOR THREE WEEKS**

> PO, verbatim: ***"this is correct - build it"***, and the four words ratified:
> `rubs` → **Share of the building's total** · `sqft` → **By floor area** ·
> `equal` → **Split equally** · `absorb` → **Owner absorbs**

Every sub-meter this product has ever created came out *metered, not allocated*,
**permanently**. `allocation_share_pct` and `allocation_rule` are columns, `POST /assets`
and `PATCH /assets/{id}` have accepted both since CR-028 AST-W3, and
`submeter_reconciliation` reads them — and **no screen could put a value in either.**
No schema change and no endpoint change was needed; the whole of the fix is a control.

**The method is CHOSEN, never typed**, borrowing `BR-AST-530` judgment 1's reason one
column across: `allocation_rule` is a bare `TextField` whose four codes live in a code
comment and nowhere else — no `choices`, no lookup, no constraint — so free text puts a
fifth value into the reconciliation engine by typo and nothing downstream refuses it.

**The list is declared ONCE and exported** (`ALLOCATION_RULES`), because the drawing puts
allocation on the add wizard AND on `Edit · Measurement`, so there are two writers from
the first day. A second hand-typed copy is exactly how `fire` — the eleventh service —
*"does not appear on screen on its own and it fails SILENTLY"*.

**Loss tolerance is deliberately NOT on the add wizard.** Screen 17 draws it beside these
two because it is a fact about a MASTER's shortfall against its children, which a
sub-meter being created has no view of. Screens 28–32 do not draw it.

### 3 · `AST-B-28` — SAVE AS DRAFT. **HALF BUILT, ON PURPOSE, AND THE OTHER HALF IS A TESTED HOLD**

> PO, verbatim: ***"Can you fix this"***

**The specification's premise is wrong and saying so is most of the finding.** *"The
button was drawn and saved nothing"* is true of the five CUSTOMER wizards. Here there was
**no button at all**: neither asset wizard passed `WizardFrame`'s optional `exit` prop, so
none of the four add steps and none of the three retire steps drew either of B19 §12.2's
controls. A System Admin three steps into retiring the wrong meter had `← Back` and
nothing that said *leave this*; a clerk half way through a move-in had both.

**Nothing could have caught it, and that is the interesting part.** An unset optional prop
is what optional means: `tsc` is happy, `G13` asks whether a DECLARED prop is passed and
these two declared none, and every suite in the feature asserts what the steps CONTAIN
rather than what the footer OFFERS.

✅ **`Save & exit` is wired on both wizards and is the whole of what B19 §12.2 promises** —
*"leaves quietly and writes nothing of its own"*, which is honest here because neither
wizard writes anything before its final commit.

⛔ **`Park` renders DISABLED CARRYING ITS REASON, and the judgment is to stop there.** Two
blockers, both facts about the STORE rather than about these screens:

1. `wizard_parks.flow` is a **database CHECK constraint** over five values, so `add_asset`
   and `retire_asset` are a migration and not a client change (this log already said so
   earlier today);
2. `CR-035` AMENDMENT 1 puts a parked draft *"directly on each request"* tab — and the
   Assets registry has **no Drafts home**. Screen 33 is drawn and unbuilt, and
   `AssetRegistryPage.tsx` is outside this lane's files.

**A draft nothing lists is a write nobody can read, which is worse than no button:** it is
precisely *"a promise the product does not keep"*, which is the sentence the specification
uses against the old state. Shipping the write without the list would have converted a
missing control into a silent data sink. This is `BillRunWizard`'s own posture and its
reasoning (`DEF-1043`), and the remaining half is `DEF-MET-5003`.

⚠ **THE HOLD CANNOT ROT.** `AssetWizardExit.dom.test.tsx` asserts that neither asset flow
is in `WIZARD_PARK_FLOWS` and goes RED the day one is added, naming the two `exit` objects
that must then stop refusing — hard-won law 2's mirror, in the same commit as the hold.

### 4 · TWO PLACES THE DRAWING LOSES, AND BOTH ARE B14 RULE 38

**The drawing says `Save as draft`; the kit says `Save & exit` and `Park`.** A footer's
button labels are FORM CONSTRUCTION, the shared frame carries them for **twenty-nine**
files, and renaming them on one screen's authority is the blast radius rule 38 exists to
refuse. **Recorded, not built.** Wave B lane 4 hit the same rule on figure 42's footer
order and made the same call.

**The drawing's helper sentences run past B14 rule 33's caps.** Figure 55 draws *"The
reading on the dial the day it goes in. Leave it blank and the first bill measures from
zero."* (10 + 10 words) and a consequence of 25 + 13. Rule 33 caps an instruction and a
consequence at **six words per sentence**, and *"two sentences of six beat one sentence of
twelve"*. Figure 45's own shorter helper — *"The reading on the dial today."* — is six
words and was taken instead, with the blank-consequence as a second short sentence.
**The drawing decides WHAT the field says; rule 33 decides how long it may be.**

## 2026-09-12 — THE CONTAINER RESTARTED AND KILLED THREE LANES, AND THE UNSAVED TREE THEY LEFT HELD THREE LOADED REVERTS

**What happened:** the container was restarted while `CR-092-BRC01` wave C lanes
1, 2 and 3 were running. **The filesystem survived — only the processes died**,
which is the opposite of the 2026-08-25 rewinds where `.git` itself was restored
from a snapshot. Local HEAD was still the tip (`4078d7b7b`) and
`check_head_current.sh` passed.

**What was lost: nothing.** Lanes 1 and 3 had pushed. Lane 2 had not, and its
whole wave — the opening read moved to step 2, the sub-meter's allocation share,
`Save & exit` on both wizards — was sitting unsaved. It is now `2.237.10`.

### ⚠ THE FINDING IS NOT THE OUTAGE — IT IS WHAT THE UNSAVED TREE WAS HOLDING

**Three separate loaded reverts, none of them caused by the restart.** Every one
was already true while the lanes were running, and the restart merely stopped
somebody walking into it. Each is law 11 mechanism two — *a blob read before a
sibling pushed* — and each would have passed every check in law 11 on the way
out, because the destroyed content is not in the diff at all.

**Only one command sees any of them, and it must be read as arithmetic:**

```
git diff --numstat HEAD | awk '$2>0'      # any non-zero deletion count
```

| what | the arithmetic | what it would have destroyed |
|---|---|---|
| `12-governance/02-decision-log.md` | `+138 −157` | **wave C lane 3's entire entry**, pushed while lane 2 wrote |
| the **eleven** locale catalogues | `+1 −4` each | **the four PO-ratified allocation words × 11 languages = 44 keys** |
| `05-assets/02-business-rules.md` | `+3 −2` | **lane 3's `BR-AST-535` and `BR-AST-536`**, overwritten by different rules wearing the same numbers |

⚠ **THE CATALOGUE ONE IS THE ONE TO REMEMBER.** The four words —
*Share of the building's total · By floor area · Split equally · Owner absorbs* —
were **ratified by the PO the same day** and are the first customer-facing words
those values have ever had. They would have gone from all eleven languages at
once, silently: `tsc` green, every suite green, `G15` parity green (because
parity is preserved when a key leaves EVERY catalogue together), and the only
symptom a clerk would ever see is a blank where a word should be.

⚠ **AND THE RULE-NUMBER ONE IS LAW 11's *"AN ALLOCATED ID IS A BLOB TOO"*,
EXACTLY.** Both lanes computed `max + 1` correctly, from two worlds neither of
which contained the other. Lane 3 pushed `BR-AST-535`/`536`; lane 2 held
`535`/`536`/`537` for different rules. **`allocate.py` covers defects, gates and
versions and does NOT cover `BR-` ids**, so nothing could have caught it at push
time. Lane 2's three are renumbered **537 / 538 / 539**; its ids appear in no
code, so the renumber is complete rather than partial.

### HOW EACH WAS REPAIRED — REBUILD FROM THE TIP, NEVER HAND-MERGE

Every repair was *the tip's bytes plus the dead lane's own addition*, proved by
subtraction afterwards — `git diff --numstat HEAD` showing **deletions: 0** on
all thirteen files.

* **The decision log** — the tip's bytes, then lane 2's entry appended, with the
  prefix proved byte-identical to the tip.
* **The catalogues** — lane 2's new key rescued from all eleven working copies
  FIRST (its translations are genuinely written per language, rule 35, and would
  have been lost by a naive restore), all eleven restored to the tip, then the
  key fanned back in with **`10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py`** — the tool that owns
  that file, whose own docstring records being written from scratch three times
  because it kept being left in a scratchpad. Parity: 15,646 keys.
* **The rules file** — the tip's rows, then lane 2's three appended renumbered.

### WHAT WAS NOT REPAIRED, AND WHY THAT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER

Two suites fail. **Both reproduce at the clean tip in a private worktree with
none of the unsaved work present**, so neither is lane 2's and neither is the
restart's — and **both already have open rows**, which is the only reason they
are not being fixed here:

* `ConfirmDialogTier.dom.test.tsx` — 32 call sites against a 29-entry audited
  list; the three unlisted are `integrations/MachineKeysPage.tsx`,
  `work/OrderDetailPage.tsx`, `work/OrderEditPage.tsx`. **`DEF-GOV-4695` is
  open and its title is *"The ConfirmDialog tier census has been red for two days
  and nobody read it"*** — which is now considerably longer than two days, and is
  its own comment on law 7's habit (1).
* `regionalReachesTheScreen.dom.test.tsx` — one offender, `DEF-SHL-4994`, open,
  red since 2026-09-07.

### THE LESSON, AND IT IS ABOUT WHEN THE DANGER EXISTS RATHER THAN ABOUT OUTAGES

**The reverts were not created by the restart and would not have been prevented
by a cleaner shutdown.** They were manufactured the moment each lane read a
shared file, and they sat armed for as long as that lane held them unsaved. The
restart is incidental — what it did was hand the tree to somebody who checked.

**So the check belongs at a rhythm, not at an event.** `git diff --numstat HEAD`
over every uncommitted shared file, read as arithmetic, costs one command and is
the only thing that sees any of this. `push_paths.sh` performs it at push time —
which is correct and was never reached here, because **the danger window opens
when a lane READS a shared file and closes when it pushes**, and all three lanes
died inside that window.

## 2026-09-12 — A PO RULING OF 2026-09-10 IS RECORDED TWO DAYS LATE: A LIST OPENS ON WHAT WAS JUST CREATED, NOT ON THE ALPHABET

⚠ **THIS RULING WAS MADE ON 2026-09-10 AND WAS IN NO FILE OF THIS REPOSITORY
UNTIL TODAY.** It survived only in the chat that produced it and in
`05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf`, whose own §10 card says so in as
many words: *"This ruling is not in the repository… Law 9 wants it in
`12-governance/02-decision-log.md` and in the customers module's business rules
**the turn it was made**. Until it is there, the next agent will not find it."*
**The document was right, and it stayed right for two days.** Recorded now, on
the PO's instruction *"record the ruling first"*.

### THE RULING, VERBATIM (PO, 2026-09-10)

> *"Whenever any account is created or any entry is created in the system, it
> automatically sorts it by the alphabetical order. It should always sort it by
> the creation order. The new newly created entries should always show on the
> top."*

### ⚠ IT SUPERSEDES A SIGNED RULE, AND THAT IS WHY IT COULD NOT BE FILED QUIETLY

`BR-CUS-053` carries the clause **`default sort name A→Z`**, and the code says
the same thing in the same words — `selectors.py:111`:

```python
ACCOUNT_DEFAULT_SORT = "name"  # BR-CUS-053: customer name A→Z
```

**That clause is now SUPERSEDED.** The default becomes **`created_at`
descending**. Everything else `BR-CUS-053` says — the five search terms, the
filters, the columns — is untouched; this moves one clause of it and nothing
else. The new rule is **`BR-CUS-1046`**.

### THE WORKED FIGURE THE PO WAS SHOWN

Opening `/accounts` with nothing chosen sends `?sort=name&dir=asc` **before the
clerk touches a control**. On the seeded tenant that puts *Ana Alvarez* first and
**an account created a minute ago wherever its customer's surname happens to
fall — for half the alphabet, that is page 2.** A clerk who has just created an
account and wants to look at it has to search for the thing they made a moment
ago.

### ⚠ IT IS NOT ONE LIST, AND THE RULING SAYS SO ITSELF

The sentence says ***any entry***. Read literally — and it should be read
literally, because the PO wrote *any* rather than naming the accounts list — the
same default is owed by **the seven sibling tabs on that screen** (Requests, New
connects, Move-ins, Move-outs, Transfers, Disconnects, Imports) **and by every
list in the product that opens on a name.**

**The Accounts work can only speak for the Accounts menu.** Applying it to the
rest of the product is a separate walk and a separate piece of work — that is a
SCOPING judgment recorded here, **not a re-ask**: the ruling is ruled, and law 13
forbids putting it back to the PO for a tidier restatement.

### ⚠ AND THE FIX HAS A TRAP THAT MAKES A BREACH WORSE IF TAKEN ALONE

**The sort happens in Python, not in SQL.** `account_list` materialises every
matching row — `accounts = list(qs.order_by("id"))` at `selectors.py:2747` — and
then sorts that list in memory at `selectors.py:2803-2814`. So a new default is
**one more branch in the same in-memory sort**, not an `ORDER BY`.

It works at 72 accounts. It is the **fifth `NFR-3` breach** of the shape
`CLAUDE.md` already names four of, and `NFR-3` is not housekeeping — it is the
T4/T5 flexibility the PO ruled load-bearing. **So the default and the ordering
are fixed TOGETHER, or the fix makes the breach slightly worse and hides it
behind a feature.**

### ROUTING — A DEFECT, NOT A CHANGE

Ambiguous between the two, and `13-change-process.md` §1 settles ambiguity the
same way every time: **it is a DEFECT**, because *"filing our misunderstanding as
a 'change' quietly converts our error into the customer's new requirement"*. The
product does not do what the PO expected; that is the beta definition of a
defect.

### THE LESSON, AND IT IS LAW 9's OWN

Law 9 says write the ruling down **when it is made**, and law 10 gives the test:
*would the next agent, with only the repo, build the same thing?* For two days
the answer was **no** — a lane touching the accounts list would have read
`BR-CUS-053`, found *"default sort name A→Z"* ratified, and built exactly the
behaviour the PO had already rejected. **A ruling that lives in a chat and a PDF
is a ruling nobody is keeping.** It took a 242-page document, read for an
unrelated reason, to surface it.

## 2026-09-12 · FOUR MORE PO RULINGS OF 2026-09-10 WERE IN NO FILE OF THIS REPOSITORY — RECORDED VERBATIM, WITH THEIR SOURCE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED AS RULES

**`CR-094-BRC01` step 1 lane 2 · `DEF-GOV-5006`**

`CR-094-BRC01` §0 found ONE ruling of 2026-09-10 that had reached no file in this
repository — the creation-order sort, landed as `BR-CUS-1046` / `DEF-CUS-4996` two
days late. **It did not look for the others. There are four more, they are on pages
57–59 of `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf`, and they are the rules the
whole Account-detail redesign is drawn to.**

**Measured rather than asserted:** every sentence below was grepped against every
`.md`, `.tsx` and `.py` in the tree. **Zero hits for each.**

### The four, verbatim, as the blueprint prints them

> **Rule 1 — PO ruling 2026-09-10:** *"keep all buttons on screen"* and *"keep all
> icon only disable them"*.
>
> **Rule 3 — PO ruling 2026-09-10:** *"i will keep all header info and manage it"*.
>
> **Rule 4 — PO ruling 2026-09-10:** *"we should have all these details captured on
> screen"*.
>
> **Rule 5 — PO ruling 2026-09-10:** *"when we do information architecture, we have
> to logically group the information, give group a heading so that it is easy for
> user to understand"*.

**Rule 2 is a measurement, not a ruling**, and **rule 6 is already repo law** — B14
rules 31 and 32.

### What each one is asking for, in plain words

**Rule 1** says nothing is hidden by state: a control this deployment cannot honour
stays on the screen, disabled, carrying its reason. **That does not supersede
anything** — it is `BR-SHL-025` restated by the PO, and the blueprint says so: *"No
supersession was needed and none is claimed."* Its cost is accepted out loud: on a
`pending_activation` account **nine of the thirteen controls are disabled at once**.

**Rule 3** keeps every fact in the header. What it needs is a rule for the one part
that grows without a ceiling — **a tenant may enable eleven services and each renders
a chip**. Measured on the running header by the blueprint: `256px` at two services,
`302px` by six, a chip row `739px` wide and a real chip about `130px`, so eleven need
about `1,430px` — **three rows**, pushing the tabs and the whole money band toward the
fold. The reporter's own production tenant already wraps at six.

**Rule 4** says everything the API serves is on the screen. The account endpoint
serves **69 fields** and **eleven were served and drawn nowhere**: `ageing_segment`,
`ageing_days_past_due`, `ageing_source`, `last_bill_at`, `autopay`,
`status_behavior_class`, `kind`, `master_account`, `balance_basis`, `balance_source`,
`unit_plan_code`, `service_agreements[].started_on`. **Ageing is the one that matters
and this lane re-measured it: the accounts LIST shows an Ageing column, and the words
*past due* appear nowhere on the account detail at `2.237.10`.** A clerk drills in and
loses the single fact that says how overdue the customer is.

**Rule 5** says every fact sits under a named group, and gives the test: a new field's
group can be named without asking. The blueprint's seven are **Money · Service ·
History · Customer · Billing preferences · Account setup · Portal access**. What
grouping removes is counted: the name appeared **three times** on the old screen, the
account number twice, the deposit twice. **And the dangerous one is the address** —
the service address and the mailing address are two different facts that were
identical on the sample account and drawn twice with nothing to tell them apart, so a
clerk learns to skip the second and misses it on the landlord account.

### THE JUDGMENT THIS LANE MADE, AND WHY IT STOPPED WHERE IT DID

**These are RECORDED here and are NOT minted as `BR-` ids.** A step 1 lane classifies;
minting a business rule from a quote in a PDF, with the PO not in the room, is a step
further than classifying. **The precedent on this branch cuts both ways and is worth
stating honestly:** `BR-CUS-1046` WAS minted from a blueprint quote on 2026-09-12 —
and it was minted *"on the PO's instruction, 'record the ruling first'"*, with the PO
present. No such instruction covers these four.

**So the deliverable is this entry**: verbatim, dated, sourced to the page, with the
figures each ruling implies worked out, so that **the next agent, with only the repo,
builds the same thing** (law 10's own test). Minting the ids and stamping the citing
documents is step 2's, or the PO's.

### WHAT IT COST, AND WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A NOTE

**`DEF-GOV-5006`.** The blueprint IS committed — at
`05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` — so these rulings are technically in
the repository. **But 101 of its 242 pages extract under 150 characters and every
digit extracts as `&`, so a grep for a ruling in this repo cannot see them.** A
document nobody can grep is a document the next agent does not have. That is the
whole mechanism, and it is the same one that cost two days on the sort ruling.

**The prevention is timing, not tooling:** when a prototype artefact carrying a PO
ruling lands, the ruling goes into this file **in the same commit as the artefact** —
law 9's timing rule, *before the thing that depends on it*.

## 2026-09-12 · THE ACCOUNTS REGISTER, WALKED — SIX OF ITS EIGHT LISTS OPEN ON THE WRONG THING, AND FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT SETTLE

**`CR-094-BRC01` step 1 lane 1 · `DEF-CUS-5060` `DEF-CUS-5061` `DEF-SHL-5062`
`DEF-CUS-5063` · `OQ-CUS-1790` · conformance
`04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/conformance/CR-094-lane1-register-step1.md`**

**THE THING THAT MADE THIS LANE DIFFERENT FROM THE DOCUMENT IT READS.** The
blueprint's own entry for screen 01 says ***"Not walked. The app could not be booted
here (no docker daemon, no systemd, no PostgreSQL, no node_modules). Every statement
in this entry is read from source."*** This lane booted the stack — Django on 8570,
the built SPA on 8571, the seeded `brazosbend` tenant, Chromium at 1440 — and walked
all eight tabs. Everything below is a measurement.

### The measurement `BR-CUS-1046` was owed

`BR-CUS-1046` (PO 2026-09-10) says a list opens on **creation order, newest first**,
and says ***any entry***, naming the seven sibling tabs. Nobody had counted what that
costs. **Measured: six of the eight lists on this one screen open on something else,
and two already comply.**

| tab | opens on | |
|---|---|---|
| accounts | `?sort=name&dir=asc` — name A→Z, sorted in Python | ✗ |
| requests | `received_at` ascending — *"Sorted by age, oldest first"* | ✗ |
| new connects | `target_activation` ascending — *"Sorted by target date, soonest first"* | ✗ |
| move-ins | `opened_at` ascending | ✗ |
| move-outs | `closed_at` ascending | ✗ |
| transfers | `-created_at, -id` — *"Newest job first"* | **✓** |
| disconnects | `account_no` — alphabetical | ✗ |
| imports | `-created_at` | **✓** |

**The worked figure:** opening `/brazosbend/accounts` sends
`?sort=name&dir=asc&page=1&per=50` before the clerk touches a control, and the most
recently created account — `AC-2026-00052`, *Ridge Property LLC* — comes back at
**position 58 of 73**. At the page size the screen uses that is **page 2**.

**And the `NFR-3` half, measured rather than reasoned:** `GET /accounts?per=1` costs
**0.107 s** and `?per=50` costs **0.102 s**. Asking for ONE row costs the same as
asking for fifty, because `account_list` materialises every matching row
(`selectors.py:2747`) and sorts it in memory (`:2803-2814`). At 73 accounts that is
0.107 s; T5's ceiling is 40,000, about **548×** the rows built to render the same
fifty.

### Judgment 1 — the six lists are a DEFECT, not a change, and they are ONE row

`13-change-process.md` §1 settles ambiguity the same way every time, and this was
not even ambiguous: `BR-CUS-1046` is a ruled rule that names the seven tabs, so the
product not doing it is a defect. **One row and not six**, because six rows for one
ruling reads as six decisions and there is only one — `DEF-CUS-5060`, with the
per-tab table in it so the size is visible.

### Judgment 2 — one thing here legitimately reaches the PO, and it is narrow

`BR-CUS-1046`'s second clause is *"a clerk's chosen sort must still win"*. **Measured:
on six of the eight lists there is nothing for a clerk's choice to win with** — only
the accounts tab declares sortable columns; the other six servers accept no `sort`
parameter at all. So on those six, *newest first* does not become a default, it
**replaces** the ordering — and four of them are ordered by urgency and print the
reason on screen (*"the oldest thing waiting is the thing to look at"*, *"the next
thing due is at the top"*). Putting a collections ladder into creation order changes
what a collections clerk can do on Monday morning and no clerk can put it back,
which is `22-product-maintenance-process.md`'s own test for what returns to the PO.
**`OQ-CUS-1790`, three answers with their costs, none chosen** (prime directive).
⚠ **The accounts tab is NOT blocked by it** — it has a sort control, so the ruling
applies to it literally and `DEF-CUS-4996` can be fixed without the answer.

### Judgment 3 — two controls the drawing shows and the product lacks are NOT findings, and B14 settles both

The drawn toolbar carries `Columns ▾` and `⇩ Export`; the product has neither as
drawn. **Neither is filed.** `⇩ Export` is a **registered refusal** — `DataTable`
exposes `downloadSlot`, `AccountsListPage` does not pass it, and the screen's own
header records why (*"`/exports` has no `accounts` resource registered, and
BR-SHL-010 says an undeclared capability does not render"*). `Columns ▾` **exists**,
icon-only, as `aria-label="Show or hide columns"` — and **B14 rule 12 is RATIFIED and
spells the toolbar out as `[Search…] [All | filter chips ×] [+ Filter ▾] … [▦ Columns]`,
so the product IS the rule and the drawing loses.** That is rules 36 and 38 applied:
a toolbar's control set is construction, the divergence is recorded and nothing is
built for it. ⚠ **This is the trap `CR-094` §5(b) names — a held control and a broken
control look identical on screen, and the difference is only visible in the register.**

### Judgment 4 — a fifth shared-table finding is filed against `CR-093`'s family rather than built here

`DEF-SHL-5062`: B14 rule 13 reads *"Headers show ⇅; click cycles asc → desc →
clear"*, and `DataTable.tsx:846-851` draws the glyph only for the column currently
sorted. **Measured:** the live `ACCOUNT` header is
`<button class="table-sort">Account</button>` with no child at all. So four sortable
columns and four unsortable ones are indistinguishable on screen. **The drawing and
the rule agree with each other and the screen matches neither.** The two rule-13
defects already filed are both about the THIRD CLICK — a rule with two clauses, one
of them filed, reads to the next lane as a rule already covered. It is a shared
component reaching 54 lists, which is precisely the blast radius PO ruling 7 of
2026-09-12 moved out of a blueprint pass, so it is **stated and not built**.

### One correction owed to a sibling lane, recorded rather than argued

Step 1 lane 2 settled `CR-094` §3b the same hour and reached the same figure this
lane did independently — **§12 lists seventeen rows, ids running to `ACC-S21`**. Its
one wrong clause is that ***"`ACC-S19` appears nowhere in the document"***. It does:
it is the tag beside remedy `R9`'s heading on **page 198**, read off the rendered
page. So all four numbers absent from the register have a home in §10 — `S11` `S12`
`S13` are finding ids and `S19` is a remedy tag — which is a tidier rule than *three
findings plus one that does not exist*, and it matters because a lane sent looking
for `ACC-S19` and told it is not there stops looking. `08-screen-layouts.md` is
corrected in the same commit; `DEF-GOV-5007` keeps the settlement.

### And two more places the blueprint contradicts itself, both read off rendered pages

**The tab count is given as both eight and ten.** p4 says *"**Eight**, all in the URL
as `?tab=`"* and draws eight; **p149 §09** says *"All **ten** tabs render a real list"*
and **p209 `ACC-S20`** says *"the register's **ten** tabs"* — while `ACC-S20`'s own
body then lists **seven** worklists, which with `accounts` is eight. **The product
has eight**, measured in the DOM. **Eight is right.**

**§09 grades `UI-RULES 16` PASS over a defect open since 2026-08-21.** Its evidence
is *"On the response"* — but rule 16 is about what the FOOTER renders, and the footer
renders no `Showing`, no `⇤`/`⇥` and no `Page x of y` (`DEF-449`, re-found as
`DEF-MET-4958`, both `CR-093`'s). A lane reading §09 would conclude the footer is fine.

## 2026-09-12 — A REFUSAL THAT WAS IMPLEMENTED THREE WEEKS AGO IS STILL ASSERTED BY EIGHT SURFACES, TWO OF THEM ROWS OF THIS LOG

`OQ-373` is **CLOSED 2026-08-25 → `BR-MET-116`**. `create_owner_account()` is
implemented at `apps/metering/connections.py:3181` and **called from
`commit_connection` at `:3059–3060`**. `grep 'NotImplementedError("OQ-373")'`
over `06-backend/apps` returns comments and nothing else. The running product
agrees: `/brazosbend/connections/new?step=7` reads, on screen, *"Billed to — The
owner's account, created at step 9. The owner captured at step 1 is given an
account number and the whole quote is tagged to it."*

### The stated reason is false twice over, measured on the running database

```
accounts.unit_id      is_nullable = YES
ck_accounts_anchored          CHECK (unit_id IS NOT NULL OR premises_id IS NOT NULL)
ck_accounts_regular_has_unit  CHECK (kind <> 'regular' OR unit_id IS NOT NULL)
```

So *"an account must name a UNIT"* — the whole premise of the refusal — is not
true of a `master` account, which is exactly what `BR-MET-116` makes an owner's
build account.

### ⚠ TWO ROWS OF THIS LOG USE THE FALSE SENTENCE AS PROOF, AND THEY ARE NOT EDITED

The rows of **2026-09-04** (`CR-070` wave O, and the Work execution plan's
re-hosting) both read *"PROVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `create_owner_account()`
raises `NotImplementedError("OQ-373")`"*, and both used it to justify hosting a
build on the premises rather than the account. **That judgment is not disturbed
and those rows are left exactly as written** — a decision log records what was
believed when a decision was made, and rewriting it would destroy the only
evidence of how the mistake propagated. **This row is the correction.**

The judgment itself survives on its own merits: the premises is still the host
that always exists for a build with no common area, which `BR-MET-116` itself
calls *"a boundary, not an omission"*. What does not survive is the sentence
used as its proof.

### The other six surfaces

`connections.py:701` (the `owner_account` field docstring — *"NOTHING FILLS IT
AUTOMATICALLY YET … `create_owner_account()` refuses"*, **2,480 lines above the
implementation, in the same file**) · `connections.py:1698` ·
`metering/migrations/0029_br_met_113_owner_account.py:28` and `:34` ·
`work/api.py:229` · `work/seams/metering_seam.py:318` ·
`tests/test_us_wrk_002_one_destination.py:92` ·
`16-work/10-execution-plan.md:211` · `16-work/08-screen-layouts.md:224`.

### ⚠ THE COST IS ALREADY OUTSIDE THIS REPOSITORY

The Accounts Menu Blueprint read these comments and **drew a clerk-facing refusal
on pages 90 and 92** — *"THE PRODUCT WILL NOT TAG THIS ACCOUNT YET"* — over a
screen that says the opposite. It flagged the smell itself (*"That reason
expired on 2026-09-01 and the refusal did not"*) and drew the refusal anyway,
because the code said so. **A stale comment did not merely mislead a lane; it
reached a design document a human will read.** → `DEF-MET-5081`.

### The lesson, and it is CLAUDE.md's own, one level down

The prime directive already says *a closed question's body goes on describing the
open world, and the body is what a lane actually reads.* This is that shape in
**code comments, a migration, a test, two module documents and this log** — none
of which has a status column at all, so nothing marks them stale. **Closing a
question means grepping its ID across the whole tree in the closing commit.** A
closing commit that leaves the OQ id sitting in a docstring has not finished.

Page 2 defines it: *"A screen no specification covers carries NO COMMITMENT —
that absence is the finding, not an oversight."* Read off the rendered pages:

  01 · 02 · 03 · 04 · 08 · 10 · 11 · 12 · 13 · 14 · 15.

## 2026-09-12 — TWO RULINGS CLOSE `OQ-CUS-1790` AND `OQ-CUS-1769`: EVERY LIST OPENS NEWEST-FIRST **AND** GAINS A SORT, AND AN ACCOUNT MAY BE RE-POINTED AT ANOTHER UNIT AS A CORRECTION

Both were put to the PO with their worked figures and their costs, both were
answered in one message, and both are recorded here the turn they were made.

---

### 1 · `OQ-CUS-1790` CLOSED — OPTION (c). ALL EIGHT LISTS OPEN NEWEST-FIRST, AND THE SIX WITHOUT A SORT CONTROL GAIN ONE

**PO verbatim:** ***"(c) All eight open newest-first and the six gain a sort
control. Largest job: six server-side sorts."***

**The PO took the largest of the three options and named its cost in the same
sentence.** They were offered a cheaper one — registers newest-first, work queues
left on urgency — and did not take it.

**Why this is the faithful reading rather than merely the thorough one.**
`BR-CUS-1046`'s own second clause is *"a clerk's chosen sort must still win and
still survive a refresh"*. **Measured 2026-09-12: on six of the eight lists a
clerk has no sort to choose** — `requests`, `new-connects`, `move-ins`,
`move-outs`, `transfers` and `disconnects` declare no sortable columns, because
each server accepts no `sort` parameter and fixes one `.order_by(...)`. On those
six, *newest first* would not be a DEFAULT a clerk could override; it would
**replace** the only ordering they had. **Option (c) is the only one of the three
under which the ruling's second clause is true of all eight lists.**

**What it costs, stated because the PO stated it:** six server-side sorts and six
sets of sortable columns.

**WHAT THE FOUR URGENCY QUEUES LOSE, AND WHY THAT IS NOW ACCEPTABLE.** Four of
the six are ordered by urgency and say so on screen today — Requests *"Sorted by
age, oldest first — the oldest thing waiting is the thing to look at."* · New
connects *"Sorted by target date, soonest first"* · Move-ins and Move-outs
*"soonest first"*. Under (a) a collections clerk would have lost that ordering
with no way back. **Under (c) they keep it as a CHOICE** — the list opens on the
newest and one click returns it to urgency, and that click survives a refresh.
**The four on-screen sentences must be rewritten** from a statement of fact
(*"Sorted by age"*) into whatever is true once the default moves; leaving them is
hard-won law 1, a comment claiming a guarantee.

**Two lists already comply and need no work:** `transfers` (`-created_at, -id`)
and `imports` (`-created_at`).

⚠ **AND THE ORDERING HALF IS NOT OPTIONAL, WHICH THE PO'S ANSWER MAKES EASIER
RATHER THAN HARDER.** `account_list` materialises every matching row
(`list(qs.order_by("id"))`, `selectors.py:2747`) and sorts in Python
(`:2803-2814`). Measured: **asking the server for one row costs the same as
asking for fifty** (0.107s vs 0.102s) because the whole tenant is built either
way. At 73 accounts that is a tenth of a second; **at 40,000 — the top of our
own ICP — it is about 548 times the rows built to draw the same fifty.** Six new
server-side sorts are the natural moment to put the `ORDER BY` where it belongs.
**The fifth `NFR-3` breach is fixed by this ruling rather than deepened by it.**

---

### 2 · `OQ-CUS-1769` CLOSED — OPTION (a). AN ACCOUNT MAY BE RE-POINTED AT ANOTHER UNIT AS A CORRECTION

**PO verbatim:** ***"(a) Narrow the rule to allow exactly this correction: a
reason from a fixed list, a supervisor's approval, effective today, never
backdated, issued bills untouched."***

⚠ **THIS SUPERSEDES PART OF A SIGNED RULE AND THE SUPERSESSION IS STATED, NEVER
ASSUMED** (law 13). `BR-CUS-017` is CONFIRMED (PO closure batch, 2026-08-08) and
reads *one account ↔ one unit; never premises-attached; at most ONE active
account per unit*. `apps/customers/services.py:3223` refuses the field by name:
`if field in ("unit", "account_type"):  # create-only, never patched`.

**WHAT MOVES AND WHAT DOES NOT.** The rule is **narrowed, not reversed**. Still
one account to one unit. Still at most one active account per unit. Still no
premises attachment. **A genuine MOVE still goes through move-out and move-in** —
because the bills, the meters and the reads belong to the unit and must not
follow a person. **What opens is a CORRECTION path for a record that named the
WRONG unit from the start**, where nobody moved and the account has simply been
billing against the wrong meters since it was opened.

**The four conditions are the ruling, not decoration:**
1. **a reason from a fixed list** — not free text;
2. **a supervisor's approval**;
3. **effective today, NEVER backdated**;
4. **every issued bill left exactly as it is** — hard rule 4 is untouched; a bill
   that was wrong is credited and replaced, which is its own flow.

**WORKED, on the blueprint's own fixture (`ACC-E07`, p185):** `A-11812 · Bramble
Bakery` moves `Suite 1 · U-000417` → `Suite 2 · U-000418` at the same address.
Plan `SCW-RES v1 → SCM-COM v2`; base charge **`$20.00` → `$63.00` a month**, so
**`$43.00` more**; meters `E-4417/W-4417 → E-4418/W-4418`; **the reading history
stays with Suite 1 and does not follow**; billing cycle unchanged; route changes.
**Five bills have already been issued against Suite 1 and they stay exactly as
they are.** **The ADDRESS does not move** — it belongs to the building and both
suites are in it (hard rule 8).

**What this unblocks:** `R5`'s sixth edit dialog (`ACC-E07`) and nothing else.
The other five `R5` surfaces, `R4`, `R6` and `R7` never needed a ruling.

**Why it reached the PO at all:** it collided with a signed rule. It was not a
gap we noticed and asked about — the PO raised the case themselves, in the words
*"from the edit perspective, I cannot see the unit edit where I want to change
unit a to unit b."* Without this ruling the only way to fix a typo was to close
the account and open another, **losing its whole history**.

## 2026-09-12 — EIGHTEEN MORE PO RULINGS FROM THE ACCOUNTS BLUEPRINT, RECORDED VERBATIM ON THE PO'S INSTRUCTION

**PO instruction, 2026-09-12:** *"record all 23 once the lanes land"*, and before
that *"record the ruling first"*.

⚠ **THE COUNT MOVED WHILE THE LANES RAN, AND THE HONEST NUMBER IS EIGHTEEN.** When
this was first measured the answer was **23 of 24 quoted rulings absent**. Step 1
lanes 2 and 3 then recorded five of them in their own write-back, correctly and
without being told to. **Re-measured at push time: 24 quoted rulings in the
document, 6 recorded, 18 absent.** These are the 18. Counting again rather than
re-using the first number is the whole discipline — *a description is not a
measurement*, and *23* had become one the moment those lanes pushed.

### HOW THEY WERE FOUND, SO THE NEXT READER CAN REPEAT IT

A ruling in this document is introduced by `Ruled:`, by *"ruling, verbatim"*, or
by `PO <date>:`, and is followed by a quotation. Every match was taken, then
tested against the whole of `12-governance/` and `04-docs/` by its first 45
characters. **A miss means no file in this repository contains that sentence.**

⚠ **THIS IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING.** It finds rulings that are QUOTED. A ruling
the document paraphrased rather than quoted is not in this list, and step 1 lane
2 found four such by reading rather than grepping. **Nobody should treat 24 as
the number of rulings in that document.**

### WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS

**These are not observations about the product. They are the specification the
whole redesign was drawn to** — every remedy in §10 is built to one of them. A
lane reading only the repository would build the drawing's shape and miss its
reason, which is exactly how `CR-092` produced *"four pencils, not six"*.

And the second cost is the one the PO named themselves: a ruling that lives only
in a chat and a PDF **gets re-asked**. Law 13, in the PO's own words — *"i try to
be consisitence but as human i might make a mistake in my response"*. Re-asking
does not merely cost their time; it manufactures two genuine contradictory
rulings and then blames the human for it.

### THE EIGHTEEN, VERBATIM, WITH THE PAGE THAT CARRIES EACH

⚠ **RECORDED, NOT RATIFIED.** Each is the PO's sentence and its location. **None
is turned into a numbered business rule here**, because several name screens
outside the Accounts menu and several will need a worked figure put back to the
PO before they can be built. **A build lane may not treat this section as a
specification** — it is the evidence that the specification exists.

**1.** (p219) *"A complaint form should be of a staple form and on new page it should open up. Same for the services"*

**2.** (p212) *"Make it as account preferences in that user can also select paperless billing. that should also be available."*

**3.** (p216) *"Please add everything that is captured in the new connect form. Each and everything should be visible … Also on that actions, what will happen? That wireframes should also be available below that screens only."*

**4.** (p210) *"So only one table. That is the meters of this unit. Don't show any other tables. And for the read log, just put an action there to view the read log for the particular meter. Build the search and filters for the meter table."*

**5.** (p221) *"What can be done with the deposit is given. but there are no actions that can be done on the deposit … After the final bill and deposit step, move the short fall step after that."*

**6.** (p189) *"change the premises tab to accounts tab. And in that, show only one table with all the accounts that are associated with this master account and with their account status."*

**7.** (p212) *"each and every details properly from each and every step. The deposit details also show properly. The payment of deposits also show properly … and move the save as actions, draft and activate at the bottom."*

### WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE HERE

## 2026-09-12 — THE MASTER ACCOUNT'S ACCOUNTS TAB IS CONFIRMED, AND THE PO NAMED THE DERIVATION RATHER THAN THE OUTCOME

**PO verbatim, 2026-09-12**, confirming the blueprint's ruling *"if the account
is of master account, then after the overview tab, it should show the accounts
that are connected to that master account"*:

> ***"this is correct - you can see the premises -> units -> regular accounts
> assocaited with it"***

⚠ **THE SECOND HALF IS THE VALUABLE HALF AND IT IS A MECHANISM, NOT A RESTATEMENT.**
The blueprint says the accounts on that tab are *"related by ADDRESS, not by a
link"* — true, and it does not say how the product gets from one to the other.
The PO named the walk: **premises → units → regular accounts.**

### IT IS ALREADY BUILT, AND THAT WAS VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

Measured 2026-09-12 against the running code:

* `customers.selectors.premises_id_for_account()` — *"The ADDRESS this account
  hangs off — the stored column first, the unit's…"*
* `customers.selectors._premises_id_for_unit()` reads metering's own unit row
  through the seam (B1: customers touches no other module's ORM) and returns its
  `premises_id`. **`None` is a real answer** — an account with no `unit_id` has no
  premises, therefore no master and no children, *which is every standalone
  account in the product.*
* `accounts.premises_id` exists as a **backfilled finder** (migration `0037`,
  `BR-CUS-1010`), indexed `ix_accounts_tenant_premises`, and `f.premises_id` is
  already a supported filter on the accounts list.
* `Unit.premises` is a real `ForeignKey(Premises, on_delete=PROTECT)`.

**The selector's own comment states the design and it agrees with the PO
exactly:** storing the relationship would be *"a second place for it to be wrong,
and it would need a clerk to maintain it through every move-in and move-out. The
link is READ."*

### ⚠ SO THE GAP IS THE TAB, AND HAS ALWAYS BEEN THE TAB

The same comment records that this was already understood once: *"CR-040's 'the
master has no children' was a REPORTING gap rather than a data gap — `500 Main
Street`'s five accounts have been children of `AC-2026-00052` since the day both
were seeded."* The blueprint reached the same conclusion independently:
*"Nothing here needs a new table and none of it needs a new relationship… What is
missing is the tab."*

**Three sources, arrived at separately, agreeing.** That is the strongest form of
confirmation available here and it is why no ruling is needed on the data model.

### A REAL WORKED CASE EXISTS AND SHOULD BE PREFERRED TO THE DRAWING'S

⚠ **The blueprint's six-row table is SAMPLE DATA and says so** — *"The rows are
invented to show the layout working; what the product can and cannot link is
not."* **`500 Main St` is real, seeded, and already returns five accounts under
`AC-2026-00052`.** A build lane should prove the tab against that, not against
the invented rows. **`BR-CUS-1010`'s own measurement is the warning attached to
it:** searching `500 Main St` returned **five of the six accounts standing there**
and left out `AC-2026-00051`, *the account that owns the building* — because the
owner's Master Account names **no unit** and hangs off the ADDRESS. **So the walk
the PO describes must start from the premises, not from the master's unit, or it
loses the master itself.**

### WHAT IS STILL NOT RULED, AND IS NOT BEING DECIDED HERE

The blueprint draws **no total under the balance column** and gives its reason:
the six rows sum to `$810.95`, which means nothing — two are `$0.00`, one is the
owner's own `$69.60`, and the rest is `$741.35` owed by three unrelated tenants.
**That is the drawing's judgment, not a PO ruling**, and it stays a drawing
decision until somebody puts it to the PO. It is recorded here so a build lane
does not add a total believing it was merely forgotten.

## 2026-09-12 — THREE CONFIRMATIONS AND ONE DESIGN QUESTION PUT BACK TO US, ON THE ACCOUNTS BLUEPRINT'S RULINGS

Recorded the turn they were made. **Each is the PO confirming a ruling already
recorded verbatim in this log** — nothing new is being ratified here, and where a
ruling's SCOPE is still open it is said so rather than assumed.

### 1 · THE COMPLAINT AND SERVICE FORMS — CONFIRMED

**PO verbatim:** ***"Yes that is correct"***, on *"A complaint form should be of a
staple form and on new page it should open up. Same for the services."*

**So both are FULL PAGES, not dialogs.** That is the B14 modal-or-screen test
answering itself: a form with an address a person can send, that must survive a
refresh, and that someone will want to come back to. **`ACC-S21`'s shape applies —
each queued record opens onto its own page.**

### 2 · THE MASTER ACCOUNT'S TAB — CONFIRMED, WITH ITS DERIVATION (recorded above)

### 3 · ⚠ THE PO ASKED US A DESIGN QUESTION RATHER THAN ANSWERING ONE, AND THAT IS THE RIGHT WAY ROUND

**PO verbatim:** ***"can we combine them with Service request - you can tell me
how you wna tot handle this"***, on *"in the main tab list, add complaints and
services. These two tabs. build their ad form and detail view. and tables."*

⚠ **THIS IS OURS TO DECIDE AND WRITE DOWN, NOT TO PUT BACK** (law 13 — *a
judgment call recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the
failure to make one*). What was MEASURED before recommending:

`customers.models.ServiceRequest` already carries **three** kind columns, and the
comment on the third states the design: `applicant_kind` (person or business) ·
`problem_kind` · `outcome_kind` (*"what sort of child the decision opened"*).
⚠ **`problem_kind`'s vocabulary is NOT the customers module's** — it is
`metering.interruptions.STORABLE_KINDS`, **imported and not copied**, because
*"the operational record is metering's (B2 §2) and two spellings of one list is
how they drift."* And `ACC-S21` describes the record's five outcomes as *"the link
between"* a request and the job it becomes.

**So a service request is ALREADY the intake record whose outcomes are jobs.** A
complaint and a service ask the same five questions — who asked, what about, when,
what we did, what it became — and the machinery for all five exists once.

**THE RECOMMENDATION, RECORDED AS A JUDGMENT:** one record, one table, one detail
page; **Complaints and Services become two FILTERED TABS over it**, each with its
own full-page capture form per confirmation 1. What must stay distinct is a
**class** column and **not** a new table — because a complaint carries two things
a service request does not: a regulatory response clock, and an outcome
vocabulary of *upheld / not upheld* rather than a job.

⚠ **AND THE REASON IS THE DEPOSIT LESSON IN MINIATURE:** three parallel record
types give three behaviours, three sets of filters and three places for the same
bug. **This is put to the PO as a recommendation with its cost, not built on our
own authority** — the tab list is theirs.

## 2026-09-12 — ⚠ THE PO CORRECTED THE CONTEXT OF THE EIGHTEEN RULINGS: SEVERAL WERE INSTRUCTIONS FOR PREPARING THE BLUEPRINT, NOT REQUIREMENTS FOR THE PRODUCT

**PO verbatim, 2026-09-12:**

> ***"see some of these ruling where given when we were prepating the artifact
> document - it was for that document - so you ahve to take these in those
> context - not necessary you ahve to apply - bascially we have resolved everyt
> item in wireframes and detaisl are captured beow them - that should be
> enough"***

⚠ **THIS CORRECTS HOW THE EIGHTEEN RECORDED RULINGS MUST BE READ, AND IT CORRECTS
THIS SESSION.** They were recorded verbatim, correctly, and presented to the PO as
*"the specification the whole redesign was drawn to"*. **Some of them are not.**
They were directions to whoever was DRAWING the blueprint — *make this table
consistent*, *reduce this content* — and the blueprint **has already carried them
out**. The drawing IS the resolution; the notes beneath each drawing are the
detail.

**TWO ARE EXPLICITLY CLOSED BY THE PO IN THIS MESSAGE:**

| ruling | PO |
|---|---|
| *"where you ahve use tables - ensure you ahve toolkit above it = { search bar, filter, colume silector, download button } - I see inconsistency at many places"* | ***"these ar eresolved"*** |
| *"look for internal data references, content sizes - it should be reduce and meaningful"* | ***"it is resolved"*** |

⚠ **SO `OQ` #3 OF THE STEP-1 QUESTION SET — *how far does the table-toolbar ruling
travel?* — IS WITHDRAWN, NOT ANSWERED.** It was a question about a product-wide
rollout of an instruction that was never about the product. **Asking it cost the
PO a decision they should never have been offered**, and the recommendation
attached to it (*fix the shared component so every list inherits it*) is
withdrawn with it. ⚠ **This does NOT touch the sort-indicator finding measured on
the shared table by step 1 lane 1** — that is a real, measured defect with its own
row, and it stands on its own evidence rather than on this ruling.

### WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT HOW STEP 2 READS THE BLUEPRINT

**The drawing and the notes beneath it are sufficient. A lane does not need to
re-derive a ruling's intent from the ruling.** PO: *"we have resolved every item
in wireframes and details are captured below them - that should be enough."*

⚠ **AND THE GENERAL LESSON IS ABOUT PROVENANCE, NOT ABOUT THESE TWO ROWS.** The
extraction that found the eighteen could see that a sentence was a ruling; it
could not see **who it was addressed to**. Every one was filed as though it were
addressed to the product. **A quotation carries its words and loses its audience**,
and nothing in the document distinguishes *"change the premises tab to accounts
tab"* (the product) from *"look for internal data references"* (the document)
except knowing which conversation it came from.

**So the record keeps all eighteen — they are real sentences the PO said and the
repository should hold them — and this entry is the one that says they are not
uniformly a backlog.** The care taken not to mint rule numbers for them, and to
stamp them **RECORDED, NOT RATIFIED**, is what made this correction cheap: no
business rule, no story and no lane was built on the misreading.

## 2026-09-12 — THREE SCOPING RULINGS, AND A QUESTION I NEARLY ASKED THAT THE REPOSITORY HAD ALREADY ANSWERED

### THE THREE RULINGS

| # | PO verbatim | what it settles |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | ***"(a) Accounts only now; the rest when each menu is audited."*** | the table-toolbar consistency work is **scoped to the Accounts menu**; every other menu gets it when that menu is audited |
| 4 | ***"(a) It is one concept — money held against an account — and building it four times would give four behaviours."*** | **ONE deposit capability, designed once, appearing in each wizard** — not four per-wizard builds |
| 5 | ***"(a) Fold into this CR as build items."*** | **Complaints and Services are built inside `CR-094-BRC01`**, not given their own change request |

⚠ **RULING 3 ANSWERS A QUESTION THAT HAD BEEN WITHDRAWN AN HOUR EARLIER, AND THE
ANSWER IS KEPT.** The PO had just explained that the toolbar sentence was an
instruction for preparing the blueprint rather than a product requirement, and
the question was withdrawn on that basis. **They ruled on the scope anyway, and
(a) costs nothing and removes an ambiguity**, so it stands as the scope for the
toolbar work the Accounts audit found on its own evidence. **It is not a
re-opening of the withdrawn question and must not be cited as one.**

⚠ **RULING 5 REVERSES THIS SESSION'S OWN RECOMMENDATION, WHICH WAS (b) — THEIR OWN
CR.** The reasoning offered was the `CR-092` lesson: *four new screens inside a
repair pass is how a fix pass becomes a build project and neither finishes*. **The
PO chose (a) and that is the decision.** ⚠ **What the recommendation was protecting
against is now a real risk on this CR and must be managed inside it rather than
argued again:** `CR-094-BRC01` now carries both a 17-screen repair pass AND roughly
four genuinely new screens. **Step 2 sequences them as separate waves with
separate versions, so the repair work can land without waiting on the build.**

### ⚠ AND A QUESTION I PUT TO THE PO AS *"THIS ONE GENUINELY NEEDS YOU"* — WHICH THE REPOSITORY HAD ANSWERED ON 2026-08-12

I told the PO that ruling 4 *"needs you, because whether a deposit is a liability
we owe back changes the books, not just the UI."* **That was wrong. It is ruled,
signed, and built.**

* **`BR-CUS-025`** — *"Deposit is a liability, never revenue; at move-out it (+
  accrued interest, `BR-CUS-057`) applies to EVERYTHING OUTSTANDING, remainder
  refunds via payments `refunds`"*, amended 2026-08-12 when the PO closed
  `OQ-158`.
* **The chart of accounts already names it**: `deposit_liability` **2300**, one of
  the eleven the PO named account by account — and `deposit_interest_expense`
  **6950** beside it.
* **`deposit_interest.py` cites `BR-CUS-025` in its own header.**

**One `grep` found all three.** Law 13 exists for exactly this and says so in the
PO's own words — *"this is very exzuating and taxing as a human… i try to be
consisitence but as human i might make a mistake in my response"*. **Had the PO
answered from memory, the repo could now hold two genuine rulings on deposit
accounting, and no way to tell which was current.**

**What IS still open about deposits is a different question entirely** and neither
is about accounting treatment: `OQ-CWP-1767` (*where does a leaving customer's
deposit go back to?*) and `OQ-CWP-1600` (*what does a new deposit cost to get

## 2026-09-12 — ⚠ THE GENERAL RULE, SAID BY THE PO THREE TIMES BEFORE IT WAS GENERALISED: THE BLUEPRINT'S RULINGS WERE INSTRUCTIONS FOR DRAWING IT, AND THE DRAWING IS THE ANSWER

**PO verbatim, on the master-account tab ruling:**

> ***"this was when we were prepaing the wireframe it is resolved now in the
> document - you dont have to resolve it again"***

**That is the THIRD row the PO has had to say this about**, after *"where you ahve
use tables - ensure you ahve toolkit above it"* (*"these ar eresolved"*) and
*"look for internal data references, content sizes"* (*"it is resolved"*), and
after the general statement that preceded both: *"we have resolved everyt item in
wireframes and detaisl are captured beow them - that should be enough."*

### THE RULE, STATED ONCE SO IT IS NOT RE-LEARNED ROW BY ROW

**A quoted ruling inside `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` is, by
default, an instruction to whoever was DRAWING that document — and the drawing
that follows it IS the resolution.** It is not an open item, not a backlog row,
and not a design question to re-answer. **Build to the drawing and the notes
beneath it.**

⚠ **I EXTRACTED EIGHTEEN OF THEM AND PRESENTED THEM AS A SPECIFICATION.** The
extraction could read the words and could not read the **audience**. Three
separate PO corrections were needed before the pattern was generalised rather
than patched one row at a time — **which is itself the failure**: the first
correction contained the general rule (*"we have resolved every item in
wireframes"*) and it was applied only to the two rows the PO named.

### WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE

**DOES NOT change the record.** All eighteen stay, verbatim, as sentences the PO
said. They were stamped **RECORDED, NOT RATIFIED** with no rule numbers minted,
and that caution is the reason three corrections cost nothing to absorb.

**DOES change how step 2 reads them.** A lane does not work from the ruling; it
works from the drawing the ruling produced. **The ruling is provenance, the
drawing is the specification.**

⚠ **AND ONE DISTINCTION MUST NOT BE LOST IN ABSORBING THIS**, because dropping it
silently would be the opposite error: **the DESIGN of the master-account Accounts
tab is resolved; the TAB ITSELF IS STILL ABSENT FROM THE PRODUCT.** The blueprint
says so in its own words — R7 carries `NO COMMITMENT`, and its closing sentence is
*"Nothing here needs a new table and none of it needs a new relationship… **What
is missing is the tab.**"* **So it stays a build item in `CR-094-BRC01` with its
design already settled.** Nothing further is asked of the PO about it; this
paragraph exists so that *"resolved in the document"* is never read as *"already
in the product"*.

## 2026-09-12 — `OQ-CUS-1810` CLOSED: THE DISCONNECTION CUT DATE IS RULED, AND THE PO CORRECTED A FACT THE STEP-1 LANE GOT WRONG

**Four answers in one message, closing the blueprint's only `BLOCKED` screen.**

| # | PO verbatim | what it settles |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | ***"(b) A per-tenant setting, seeded with our three, that each utility sets to its own regulator's number."*** | the notice period is **a per-tenant setting**, seeded with our existing 10-day / 5-day / 48-hour |
| 7 | ***"Business days"*** | the clock counts **business days** |
| 8 | ***"we ahve holidays in settings you can check it out it is per tenant"*** | the roll uses **the tenant's own holiday calendar, which already exists** |
| 9 | ***"(b) Floor it at the notice date itself now… - give a message but allow it"*** | a date before the notice **warns; it does not block** |

### ⚠ THE PO CORRECTED A FACT, AND THE STEP-1 LANE WAS WRONG

`OQ-CUS-1810`'s body — written by `CR-094-BRC01` step 1 wave 4 and repeated by me
to the PO — says *"this product holds no holiday calendar for any tenant"* and
that where one comes from *"is part of the answer rather than a detail of it."*

**Both clauses are false, and one `grep` disproved them:**

* **`tenancy.HolidayCalendar`** — `db_table = "holiday_calendars"`, columns
  `tenant`, `holiday_date`, `label`, unique on `(tenant, holiday_date)`. **Per
  tenant, exactly as the PO said.**
* **`BR-TEN-039` is CONFIRMED** — *"Four new Reference-data cards approved:
  Holiday calendar (S63)…"* — so it has a ratified rule **and a screen**.
* **`us_holidays.py` seeds it at provisioning** (`services._seed_us_holidays`),
  under `US-TEN-011`, with `BR-TEN-043`'s event-time law (*the year is an
  argument, never a clock*).
* ⚠ **AND THE EXACT PATTERN THE PO JUST CHOSE IS ALREADY RATIFIED AND BUILT
  ELSEWHERE:** **`BR-BIL-002`, PO 2026-08-11** — *"business-day grace excludes
  the tenant's public holidays"*. **Billing has been counting business days
  against this very calendar for a month.**

**So question 8 was never an open question. It was a lane's unchecked assertion
carried into a question and put to the PO as fact.** The PO answered it from
their own knowledge of their product, which is the failure law 13 exists to
prevent — *asking again is a bug in us*. **The one command that would have caught
it is the one the law prescribes before anything reaches the PO: grep the repo
for the subject first.**

### WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE BUILD — FOLLOW THE PRECEDENT, DO NOT INVENT ONE

The cut-date calculation is **`BR-BIL-002`'s shape applied to a different date**:
notice date **+ N business days**, where `N` is the tenant's setting, skipping
weekends **and the tenant's own `holiday_calendars` rows**. `BR-TEN-043` governs
the year handling — *the year is an argument, never a clock*.

⚠ **THE TRAP `B18`'s FIXTURE CARRIES IS NOW AVOIDABLE AND MUST BE TESTED FOR.**
Adding 48 hours implements *"+2 days"*, which agrees with that fixture **by
luck** — 22 Aug 2026 is a Saturday, so the drawn case needs no roll at all and a
wrong implementation passes it. **A business-day test must include a case where
the roll actually fires**, and the obvious one is a tenant holiday: notice
Thursday **21 May 2026**, five business days, **Monday 25 May 2026 is Memorial
Day**, so the answer is **Friday 29 May** and not Thursday 28 May.

### ⚠ RULING 9 IS A WARNING, NOT A BLOCK, AND THE WORDING MATTERS

**PO: *"give a message but allow it"*.** So a cut date before the notice date
**must not be refused** — no `min` attribute, which would silently prevent typing
it. **The clerk sees a message and may proceed.** That is deliberate: a floor that
blocks would be this product asserting a legal rule it does not yet hold, and the
PO chose to inform rather than to prevent. **The statutory period goes on top once
the per-tenant setting exists; until then the message is the only guard.**

## 2026-09-12 — PO STANDING INSTRUCTION: **BUILD FROM THE ACTUAL CODE, AND DO NOT CREATE DUPLICATE CODE**

> ***"Do all changes bsed on actual code - also dont create duplcate code"***

**Said in the same hour the PO had to correct a lane that asserted a table did not
exist when it does**, and while a lane was being briefed to build a business-day
calculation that billing has performed for a month. **It is not a general
sentiment; it names the two failures that were live on the branch at that
moment.**

### THE FIRST HALF — *based on actual code*

**A claim about this product is a MEASUREMENT, not a reading.** `OQ-CUS-1810`'s
body asserted *"this product holds no holiday calendar for any tenant"*; the
calendar is `tenancy.HolidayCalendar`, per tenant, ratified as `BR-TEN-039`, with
a screen (`S63`) and a provisioning seed. **One grep disproved it, and that grep
was never run before the sentence reached the PO.**

This is the same fault the Assets pass recorded against itself repeatedly — *a
description is not a measurement* — and the remedy is the same one word: **open
the thing.** Before any lane writes *"there is no…"*, *"nothing does…"*, or
*"this does not exist"*, it greps for it and quotes what it found.

### THE SECOND HALF — *do not create duplicate code*

⚠ **THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN HISTORY IS THE ARGUMENT.** `CLAUDE.md` law 11 records
three separate occurrences in one night of *a careful operator reaching for the
obvious general-purpose tool instead of asking whether this repo already owns
that job* — a `csv` writer over a register that has `file_defect.py`, a
hand-rolled push script when `push_paths.sh` already existed **and was stricter**.
Its conclusion: **the cause was not a missing guard; it was an existing guard
nobody looked for.**

**So the rule in practice, and it costs one command:**

| before you write | look for |
|---|---|
| a script that touches a shared file | `ls 10-scripts/` — the tool that owns that file probably exists and says why in its own docstring |
| a component | `ls 07-frontend/src/components/` — 45 of them. *A second table, a third button size or a bespoke dialog is a defect, not a contribution* (the UI skill's §7.2) |
| a calculation | grep for the rule id. **Business days already exist** — `BR-BIL-002`, *"business-day grace excludes the tenant's public holidays"*, shipped 2026-08-11 |
| a message to a clerk | the eleven catalogues, via `i18n_fanin.py`. A second spelling of one sentence is how they drift |
| a lookup or vocabulary | the owning module. `problem_kind`'s values are `metering.interruptions.STORABLE_KINDS`, **imported and not copied**, and the model comment says why: *"two spellings of one list is how they drift"* |

⚠ **AND WHERE REUSE WOULD CROSS A MODULE BOUNDARY, THAT IS A SEAM QUESTION, NOT
PERMISSION TO COPY.** `B1` forbids customers touching another module's ORM;
`B2 §2` makes cross-module FKs a reviewed set. **A lane that cannot reach a
helper states the seam and stops** — it does not reimplement the helper on its
own side, which is duplication wearing a boundary as an excuse.

**This instruction is now in every step 2 briefing and was sent to the three
lanes already running.**

## 2026-09-12 · `BR-CUS-1046` BUILT ON ALL EIGHT LISTS — and the ordering moved into SQL with it

**`CR-094-BRC01` step 2 wave C.** Closes `DEF-CUS-4996`, `DEF-CUS-5060` and
`DEF-CUS-5061`. Version **2.238.0**.

### What was ruled, and what it cost

The PO's ruling of 2026-09-10, verbatim: ***"Whenever any account is created or
any entry is created in the system, it automatically sorts it by the alphabetical
order. It should always sort it by the creation order. The new newly created
entries should always show on the top."*** Extended 2026-09-12, answering
`OQ-CUS-1790`: ***"(c) All eight open newest-first and the six gain a sort
control. Largest job: six server-side sorts."***

**The PO took the largest of three options and named its cost in the same
sentence.** Option (a) — registers newest-first, work queues left alone — was
cheaper and was not taken, and the reason is the ruling's own second clause: *a
clerk's chosen sort must still win and still survive a refresh*. On six of the
eight lists a clerk had no sort to choose, so under (a) *newest first* would have
REPLACED the only ordering four urgency queues had, with no way back.

### The worked figure, measured rather than estimated

**Before:** opening `/brazosbend/accounts` untouched sent
`?sort=name&dir=asc`, and the newest account on the utility —
`AC-2026-00052`, *Ridge Property LLC*, created that morning — came back at
**position 58 of 73**, which is **page 2** at the page size the screen uses.
**After: position 1 of 73, page 1.** Read off the rendered table in Chromium at
1440 and again at 1280 by `10-scripts/cr094c_sort_walkthrough.mjs`.

### The ordering was fixed WITH the default, because the rule said to

`BR-CUS-1046`'s own words: *"it must be fixed WITH the ordering, not before it …
or the fix makes the breach worse and hides it behind a feature."*
`account_list` materialised **every matching row** (`list(qs.order_by("id"))`)
and sorted that list in Python, so the fifth `NFR-3` breach of the shape
`CLAUDE.md` names four of was on the product's busiest screen.

**Measured, by counting ROWS BUILT rather than by a clock —
`10-scripts/cr094c_accounts_page_cost.py`:**

| request | rows returned | rows BUILT before | rows BUILT after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `?per=1` | 1 | **73** | **1** |
| `?per=10` | 10 | **73** | **10** |
| `?per=50` | 50 | **73** | **50** |

⚠ **NEITHER OF THIS REPO'S USUAL INSTRUMENTS COULD SEE THIS, AND THAT IS WORTH
MORE THAN THE FIGURE.** The **wall clock** cannot: at 73 accounts both requests
are dominated by fixed overhead, so `per=1` measured 0.107 s and `per=50` 0.102 s
before, and 0.156 s / 0.157 s after — unchanged, and meaningless. The
**statement count** cannot either: `DEF-2723` made this list cost a constant
number of statements whatever the page holds, and that guarantee held throughout
while the rows those same statements BUILT grew with the tenant.
`test_def2723_accounts_list_statement_count.py` was green before and is green
after. **Two different properties, two different instruments, and only one of
them could ever see `NFR-3`.**

### Four judgments made in the lane, each recorded rather than raised

1. **THE DERIVED SORTS STAY IN PYTHON, AND THE EXPENSIVE PATH IS NOW THE
   EXCEPTION RATHER THAN THE DEFAULT.** `balance` and `last_bill` are figures
   that live in the LEDGER and in BILLING, not in a column (`BR-CUS-016`, and
   `DEF-127`'s note that the cached `accounts.balance` is written by nothing), as
   are the `f.ageing` and `f.balance_gt` filters. An `ORDER BY` or `WHERE` over
   either would be a SECOND implementation of a figure that already has one,
   free to disagree with the cell the same response renders — the trade
   `DEF-127` deliberately made. So `account_page` takes the page in SQL for
   `created`, `account_no`, `name` and `status`, and falls back to the whole-tenant
   build for the four derived cases, which `ACCOUNT_DERIVED_SORTS` names out
   loud. **Every request a clerk makes by OPENING the screen is now `O(page)`;
   only one they make deliberately is `O(tenant)`.**
2. **NO `Created` COLUMN WAS ADDED TO ANY OF THE EIGHT TABS.** Neither the
   blueprint nor B18 draws one, and the UI skill's §2.5 is explicit that an
   absence is a decision — *say so, do not add it*. The consequence is stated
   rather than hidden: while a list is on its default no header carries the sort
   glyph, and the sentence under the pager is what states the ordering, which is
   the mechanism six of these tabs already used for exactly that job.
3. **THE SORT NAMES ARE THE SCREENS' EXISTING COLUMN KEYS, NOT TIDIER ONES.**
   `DataTable` stores a clerk's show/hide/reorder preference keyed by `screenId`
   + column key (`BR-SHL-013`, `DEF-647`), so renaming a column to match a
   cleaner server name would have silently discarded every saved column set on
   this screen. The server name moved instead — `received` → `received_at`,
   `target` → `target_activation`, `account_no` → `account` on the two move tabs.
4. **`transfers` KEEPS ITS DEFAULT AND STILL COUNTED AS ONE OF THE SIX.** It
   already opened `-created_at, -id`, so the ruling's first clause asked nothing
   of it; it is in the six because it had no sort to CHOOSE, which is the second
   clause. `imports` likewise already opened newest-first and needed only its cap
   removed.

### The bug this pass shipped and caught by MEASURING, recorded because the lesson is general

The first draft stored `("-created_at", "-id")` in all seven sort maps **and**
declared `DEFAULT_DIR = "desc"`. `core.pagination.order_terms` did exactly what
it says and flipped the term for `desc`, the two minuses cancelled, and **all
eight lists opened on the OLDEST row** — `BR-CUS-1046` inverted, shipped as a
working feature. Every unit test was green, because the unit test had been
written to the same wrong convention as the code.

**Nothing mechanical found it.** It was found by `curl`-ing the endpoint and
reading the first three account numbers — build-process step **2d**, *prove it by
clicking*, earning its place. The test now asserts the CONVENTION (a term is
stored ascending; *newest first* is `desc` over it) rather than the mechanics,
and says in its own docstring that it once did the opposite.

**The same shape twice more, both times a false FINDING rather than a false
pass**, and both worth naming because a walkthrough that manufactures findings is
worse than none: a stale `runserver` process served the previous module for two
measurements (answering 200 and drawing a real screen the whole time), and two
drafts of one assertion named a specific seeded row where the demo data already
held an older one. The walkthrough now reads the served sort vocabulary — which
catches the stale process — and asserts a PROPERTY (did the order change; does
the screen render what the server ordered) instead of a row name.

### What was NOT fixed, and why it is filed

**`DEF-CUS-5091` — a chosen sort does not survive a refresh on seven of the eight
tabs.** It WINS everywhere: the parameter reaches the server, the `ORDER BY`
changes and the rows move. It SURVIVES a refresh only on the accounts tab, the
only one of the eight that keeps its table state in the query string. The other
seven hold it in `useState` by a DELIBERATE earlier design — `DEF-664` gave the
embedded Requests list `urlState={false}` because all eight tabs share ONE query
string and each one's `?sort=` would overwrite the others'. Namespacing the
parameters per tab changes all eight at once and re-opens what `DEF-664` settled,
so it is a decision rather than a line of code. **The walkthrough asserts the
current truth and names the row, so the day it is fixed the check goes red and
says which defect it belongs to** — law 2's rule for a hold, applied.

**`DEF-SHL-5062` — no sort glyph on an unsorted column** (B14 rule 13's first
clause) is `CR-093-BRC01`'s, stated here and not built. It is now visible on
sixteen more headers than it was this morning, which raises its value and does
not change its owner.

**The three Imports tabs still page in the browser, and the server fix alone
would have been a REGRESSION rather than a fix.** With the cap gone
`GET /imports` pages like every other list, so its default page is 50 — and all
three tabs (accounts, assets, premises) slice `rows` themselves AND compute
`totalLoaded` / `totalRejected` / `lastRun` by summing the whole array. Shipping
only the server half would have shown a tenant with 120 runs fifty of them and
reported the first page's totals as the totals of everything: a WRONG FIGURE
where there had been a truncated list. `getImportRuns` therefore asks for the top
IS-2 page size, which keeps all three exactly as they were and lifts the ceiling
from 200 to 1,000. Converting them properly needs the server to publish those two
sums over the whole filtered set, and two of the three tabs are other modules'
screens.
