## 2026-09-12 — `CR-094-BRC01` STEP 2 WAVE 4: SIX JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT, ON THE FOUR ENDING-SERVICE SCREENS

**Six defects fixed, `OQ-CUS-1810` built, and three new rows filed. These are the
calls that were not already ruled, each with the figure or the sentence it turned
on. Version `2.238.1`.**

### 1 · `BR-PAY-017` IS STORED IN HOURS AND THE PO RULED THE CLOCK IN BUSINESS DAYS, SO THE UNIT HAD TO BE RECONCILED

The final notice tier is `final_notice_hours = 48`; the two tiers above it are
`notice_tier_days = [10, 5]`. Answer 7 of the ruling is *"Business days"*.
**Converting 48 hours into business days is therefore forced, and it is done by
dividing by 24 and rounding UP** — 48 → 2, and a utility that sets 36 gets 2
rather than 1, **because a period is a MINIMUM the regulator grants the customer
and rounding it down shortens their protection.**

That is a unit conversion rather than a business decision — it is what the
stored number already means — and it is recorded because it is exactly the kind
of step that looks like arithmetic and behaves like a rule. **If a regulator
genuinely counts the final period in clock hours rather than in business days,
this reading is wrong for them and `BR-PAY-017` needs a unit beside the number.**
Nothing was guessed further than the ruling reaches.

### 2 · TWO OF THE FOUR ANSWERS ASKED FOR THINGS THAT ALREADY EXISTED, AND NOTHING NEW WAS BUILT FOR EITHER

Answer 6 — *"(b) A per-tenant setting, seeded with our three, that each utility
sets to its own regulator's number"* — **describes something shipped weeks ago**:
`settings_families.COLLECTIONS` carries `notice_tier_days` and
`final_notice_hours` under `BR-PAY-017`, per tenant, on screen `S70`, with our
three seeded. Answer 8's calendar is `tenancy.HolidayCalendar` (`BR-TEN-039`,
screen `S63`), which `OQ-CUS-1810`'s own body said did not exist. Measured on
`brazosbend`: **22 holiday rows, one of them 2026-05-25.**

So `cut_date.py` reads both through seams and **builds no second home for
either.** Building one would have given this product two places a regulator's
number lives — the duplication the PO's standing instruction of the same day
refuses in as many words (*build from the actual code, and do not create
duplicate code*). Recorded as law 13's cost: the question put a lane's unchecked
assertion to the Product Owner as fact.

### 3 · A REUSED RULE CAME WITH COPY THAT NAMED THE WRONG ACT

The transfer wizard's buyer block reuses `accountIdentityShortfall` — right, it
is `BR-CUS-1023`'s client half and the same function two other wizards use, so
none of the three can disagree with the server. **Its four catalogue sentences
came with it and all four say *"before opening the account"*.** A sale opens
nothing, so a clerk selling a property was told in a red strip that an account
could not be opened.

**Judgment: keep the rule, remap the KEY, and write the sale's own four
sentences.** Not a second implementation of the rule — that is what would drift.
Found by walking the screen; `tsc`, twenty cases and every gate passed over it,
because **reusing a rule and inheriting its copy is indistinguishable from
reusing both to every check that exists.**

### 4 · `Split into two` WAS REMOVED RATHER THAN LEFT DISABLED

It was drawn on the frame of the replaced job, where a transfer was a move-out
plus a move-in and splitting it back was at least coherent. Under `BR-CUS-1030`
one account changes hands and nothing closes, **so there is nothing to split
into.** A greyed control for an incoherent act is hard-won law 2's mirror — a
dead door teaching a clerk the product might one day do something it never will
— and the drawn step 1 at p113 carries only `Save & exit`. **The header's action
slot is now empty, and a test asserts that rather than asserting a disabled
button.**

### 5 · THE CLOSE-OUT SCREEN'S BALANCE GOES THROUGH `MoneyCell`, WHICH CHANGES A DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION IN ITS OWN FILE

That file's exception list said the balance renders the server's `display`
string and never a re-rounding of `stored`. It printed `8240.00` — **no
currency, while `currency` sat unused in the same payload**, and the drawing
shows `$318.40`. `MoneyCell` is the kit's one formatter and is what closed
`DEF-088`; it reads the 4 dp `stored` figure and displays 2, which is hard rule
2 rather than a re-rounding. **The null case is untouched and stays a sentence**:
a balance that could not be read is never `$0.00` (`DEF-127` / `DEF-628`).

### 6 · THE PROTECTIONS SPLIT IS ON WHETHER THE SERVER CAN *ANSWER*, NOT ON WHETHER IT SENT A ROW

`protection_check` sends four rows and the fourth — the open dispute — answers
`unavailable`, because nothing in this product stores a disputed AMOUNT. Splitting
on *did a row arrive* would file that under **Checked by the product**, which is
the fabricated clearance the whole step exists to refuse. **So `pass` and `fail`
are CHECKED and everything else stays under *Not checked by anything*.** Today
that is 3 checked against 7, derived from the payload rather than from the
hand-typed flag that rotted — and the day a fourth check lands, the screen moves
it across on its own and a test goes red naming it.

### ⚠ WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY — TWO THINGS, BOTH DELIBERATE

**The eleven locale catalogues were not written.**
`10-scripts/i18n_extract_defaults.py`'s own header says lanes are banned from
editing them and names the sanctioned handover: the English lives at the call
site as `defaultValue` and the translation lane fans it in. **A sibling lane was
holding all eleven uncommitted in the shared tree at the time.** Every new string
carries its `defaultValue`, and **24 keys are recoverable where a first draft
left only 14** — the draft resolved these sentences by interpolating a server
code into the key, which works, type-checks, renders correctly in English and is
**invisible to the extractor**, so ten of the sentences a clerk reads most would
have stayed English for ever with every check green.

**The Transfers TAB was not fixed** (`DEF-CUS-5092`). It still describes the
replaced job — five KPI tiles about deposits carrying and arrears following, two
date columns showing the same date, and a `FROM → TO` cell now reading
`AC-2026-00022 → AC-2026-00022`. It is lane 1's file in this CR. Two lanes in one
file is the revert every check in law 11 passes over.

## 2026-09-12 — `CR-094-BRC01` STEP 2 WAVE E · THE STARTING-SERVICE WIZARDS: A REFUSAL THAT EXPIRED IN TEN PLACES, A REFUSAL THAT POINTED AT NOTHING, AND TWELVE PAIRS OF FIELDS THAT TOUCHED

**WHICH PROCESS THIS WAS, decided and not asked.** A clerk can open all five of
these wizards in the product today, so every one of these rows is
**MAINTENANCE** (`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`) and not
Build — reproduce, locate, blast radius, minimal fix, prove against the
reproduction, regression-walk the neighbours. ⚠ **AND THE THINGS THIS WAVE DID
NOT DO ARE THE BUILD HALF, NAMED SO NOBODY READS THEM AS MISSED:** the three
ruled step-count changes (new account loses its plan step, move-in gains a
deposit step, new connect merges its first two) and the ONE deposit capability
are **BUILD**, and the scoping ruling of this same day says step 2 *"sequences
them as separate waves with separate versions, so the repair work can land
without waiting on the build"*. Nothing here touches a step count.

### WHAT A PERSON CAN NOW DO, in plain words

A clerk taking a service request at the counter is told **which field is
missing**. Pressing *Continue* on step 1 with the name typed used to say *"Fill
in what's marked above"* over a screen with **one** mark on it, and that mark on
the field they had just filled; the customer category the step actually refuses
on carried no asterisk at all. It carries one now.

A link to any step of that wizard **opens on that step**. Six addresses are
drawn for it and all six landed the clerk on step 1: `?step=2` painted `Step 1
of 6`, and so did `?step=3` through `?step=6`. Out of range still clamps — `?
step=7` opens step 6, `?step=banana` opens step 1 — rather than erroring.

**The fields on these forms are no longer touching.** On the new account
wizard's step 1 — the door every counter sign-up goes through — eight adjacent
pairs of fields sat **0px** apart. They are **20px** apart now. On the new
connect wizard they were **12px**.

And ten places in the product stopped saying that the owner of a new building
cannot be given an account, three weeks after the product started being able to
give them one.

### THE MEASUREMENTS, so every figure here can be re-taken

| what | how |
|---|---|
| the drawings | rendered as IMAGES at scale 2 from the PDF pinned at `033981d4f`, `sha256` verified to begin `c8d596bb505f5020ce4b9474`. **No figure came from the text layer, in which every digit extracts as `&`** |
| the step counts | read off the RAIL the browser painted, never off the URL — four of these five wizards clamp `?step=` silently |
| the spacing | `getComputedStyle` + `getBoundingClientRect` in Chromium at **1280 AND 1440**, `10-scripts/cr094_wave_e_walkthrough.mjs` |
| the schema and the data | `information_schema`, `pg_constraint` and SQL on the running PostgreSQL with `app.tenant_id` SET |
| `create_owner_account` | CALLED, four payload shapes, inside a transaction that was ROLLED BACK |

### `DEF-MET-5081` — TEN SURFACES, AND THE COST HAD ALREADY LEFT THE REPOSITORY

`OQ-373` closed **2026-08-25 → `BR-MET-116`**. `create_owner_account()` is
implemented at `connections.py:3181` and `commit_connection` calls it at step 4
whenever the payload asks; `NewConnectWizard.tsx:345` sends that flag for any
build whose owner is named. **Ten live surfaces still said it raises
`NotImplementedError("OQ-373")`** — the field's own docstring **2,480 lines
above the implementation in the same file**, `home_of_connection`, migration
`0029`, `work/api.py` twice, `work/seams/metering_seam.py` twice, a **passing
test**, the committed OpenAPI document twice, three front-end comments and two
Work documents.

**The stated reason was false twice over.** Measured on the running database:
`accounts.unit_id` is **nullable**, `ck_accounts_regular_has_unit` binds only
`kind='regular'`, and `ck_accounts_anchored` accepts a premises anchor. And
`brazosbend` holds exactly one account with a null `unit_id`: **`AC-2026-00052`,
`kind='master'`, active, anchored on `CON-26-0117`'s own premises** — the build
the comments said could have no owner account **already has a master account at
its address.**

**Called rather than reasoned about.** Four payload shapes were driven through
the real function on `CON-26-0117`, all rolled back: no `NotImplementedError` on
any of them, and with a full `contact` + `customer.identity` block it ran to
`BIZ-STATE customers.account.unit_already_occupied` — its own logic, all the way
through.

⚠ **THE COST WAS ALREADY OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY, WHICH IS WHY THIS ONE MATTERS
MORE THAN A TIDY-UP.** The Accounts blueprint read these comments and drew a
clerk-facing refusal on pages 90 and 92 — *"THE PRODUCT WILL NOT TAG THIS
ACCOUNT YET"* — over a screen that says the opposite; the product's own step 7
reads *"The owner's account, created at step 9."* **A stale comment did not
merely mislead a lane; it reached a design document a person will build from.**

**THE JUDGMENT THOSE COMMENTS SUPPORTED IS UNCHANGED AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT
DISTURBED.** The premises is still the host to build on. Only its PROOF moved:
from *"the writer is missing"* to *"the column is optional"* — a build carries no
owner account until one is asked for, and `BR-MET-116` refuses one outright on a
build with no common area. Measured: **8 `brazosbend` connections, 0 with an
owner account**, because this fixture seeds connection rows directly rather than
committing them through step 4. **And the two decision-log rows of 2026-09-04
that cite the false sentence as evidence are NOT edited** — a decision log
records what was believed when a decision was made.

⚠ **THE OLD SENTENCE IS KEPT AT EVERY SITE AS A DATED STAMP** (*"this said X
until 2026-09-12"*), so a grep for it returns only corrections. That is
deliberate: deleting it would destroy the only evidence of how it propagated,
which is the whole lesson.

⚠ **ONE SURFACE WAS PATCHED AND NOT REGENERATED, SAID OUT LOUD.**
`06-backend/openapi/schema.json` is a COMMITTED generated file. Its two
descriptions were edited as raw bytes and the document re-validated as JSON,
because `manage.py spectacular` at this tip emits **1,295,700 bytes against the
committed 784,953** — the committed copy is not reproducible from the current
generator, and regenerating would have been a 500KB unrelated diff inside a
repair wave. That gap is hard-won law 5 pointing at itself and is reported
rather than fixed here.

### `DEF-CUS-5082` — A GATED FIELD WITH NO MARK MAKES THE FRAME LIE

`ServiceRequestCapturePage`'s step 1 gates `Continue` on
`account_type_code !== ""`, unconditionally, on every channel. The group carried
**no asterisk, no `required` and no `aria-required`**, so the frame fell back to
its generic sentence. Measured before the fix: `[aria-invalid=true]` count **0**,
error-class count **0**, and the words on screen *"This step isn't finished.
Fill in what's marked above, then press Continue again."*

**That is the exact case `WizardFrame` warns about in its own comment** — *"the
generic one is the FALLBACK — true whenever the unmet condition is a marked
field, and **a lie whenever it is not**"* — and B14 rule 10.

**THE JUDGMENT: `SegmentedField` GAINS THE `required` PROP THE OTHER FIVE
VARIANTS ALREADY HAVE, rather than the screen growing its own mark.** It
hard-coded `required={false}` with no way to say otherwise. Threading the same
prop to the same `FieldLabel` keeps rule 10 as one rule with one implementation;
a second marking mechanism at one call site is how four screens acquire four
asterisks. `aria-required` goes on the **radiogroup** and not on each radio,
because the GROUP is what must be answered — a required radio input tells a
screen reader every option is separately obligatory. **Absent means `false`,
which is what all eighteen existing call sites render**, so nothing outside this
screen moved.

⚠ **AND `channel` IS DELIBERATELY NOT MARKED, THOUGH THE DRAWING MARKS IT.**
Blueprint page 76 draws `Channel *`. `emptyCaptureForm` seeds
`CAPTURE_CHANNELS[0]`, so the control can never be empty and nothing gates on
it. **An asterisk on a field that cannot be unanswered teaches a clerk that the
mark means nothing — which is this defect running the other way.** The test
asserts both directions, because a one-directional assertion is
`DEF-CUS-4298`'s recorded shape.

### `DEF-CUS-5083` — THE ONE WIZARD OF FIVE WHOSE STEP WAS NOT URL STATE

`EP-SHL-03-forms-wizards.md` is a rule and not a habit: *"Wizard step | **all
wizards** | A9 routing model (`?step=`) | none (URL state) | int |
system-derived | clamped to reached steps (BR-SHL-018)"*. `MoveInWizard` and
`MoveOutWizard` both cite it verbatim. The capture held its step in component
state and read `useSearchParams` for `?request=` only.

**THE JUDGMENT: IT COPIES THE FOUR SIBLINGS RATHER THAN INVENTING A FIFTH
BEHAVIOUR.** `NewAccountWizard:477`, `MoveInWizard:411` and `NewConnectWizard:439`
all derive `{ step, reached: step }` from the URL and say why in the same words —
*"The forward fence is the step itself: a user can always go BACK to a step they
have been on, and forward only through Continue (BR-SHL-018)."* The alternative,
keeping a `reached` fence (which `NewOrderWizard` does and which is BR-SHL-018's
more literal reading), would have left the six DRAWN addresses still not
resolving on a cold link, and would have given this menu **two step models
across five screens**. The defect is that one of five differs; the repair is to
make it the same, and the codebase had already taken and documented that
judgment in three files.

It reuses `clampStepToReached` — `WizardFrame`'s own clamp, which the frame's
header tells consumers to restore through — rather than writing a fourth copy of
`Math.min(Math.max(1, n), count)`.

### `DEF-CUS-5098` — TWELVE ADJACENT PAIRS OF FIELDS, AND NOT ONE AT 20px

B14 rule 39 as amended this day ratifies **field → field 20px** (*"a) 20
everywhere — the anatomy wins"*), and the PO's own words for why the rule exists
are *"have a proper padding for each component on the screen… the components are
too much close"*.

**Measured in Chromium at 1280 AND 1440, before:** the new account wizard's step
1 reported **eight adjacent pairs at 0px** (one at −0.01px) — a run of `.field`s
dropped straight into a `Panel`, which is `display: block` with `gap: normal`, so
they touch — and the new connect wizard's step 1 reported **12px** on four pairs.
**Zero of twelve adjacent pairs across these five wizards were at 20px**, the
same shape `CR-092` step 1 measured as *"zero of eleven"* on the asset screens.
`label → input 5px`, `input → helper 6px` and the painted order were already
correct everywhere, from `CR-092` step 2 wave A.

**THREE JUDGMENTS, and the scoping one is the one that matters.**

**(1) The rhythm is `[data-panel] > .field + .field`, and the descendant
restriction is the whole safety of it.** It matches only a field that is a DIRECT
child of a `Panel`. Where a container already supplies the rhythm as a flex or
grid `gap` — `.modal-body`, `FieldStack`, `FieldGrid` — the field is a child of
THAT, so the margin cannot reach it. **A bare `.field + .field` would have added
to every one of those gaps and taken every dialog in the product to 40px.** And
`+` means *the next field*, which is the only distance rule 39 governs: a field
followed by an `<h4>` subhead, a `RefusalStrip` or a `<Note>` — three cases
inside the very panel this was written for — is untouched.

**(2) It is a RULE in `FormModal.css`, where rule 39's other two figures already
live, and NOT a class on `Panel`.** A panel holds headings, prose, tables, KPI
rows and figures across 149 call sites; 20px between a heading and its own hint
is not rule 39 and would move every one of them. A `stack` prop on `Panel` was
written first and deleted for exactly that reason — it would have re-spaced the
`<h3>` and the hint line above the fields.

⚠ **AND THIS REACHES EVERY PANEL-HOSTED FORM IN THE PRODUCT, NOT ONLY THESE
FIVE SCREENS. SAID PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE RISK IN THIS WAVE.** That is what
rule 39 asks for in the PO's own words — *"universally fit for the product"* —
and it follows the precedent `CR-092` step 2 wave A set when it put the other
two figures in this same stylesheet. **707 tests across 38 files** (all of
`features/customers`, the shared kit, the premises detail) pass unchanged, and
the five wizards were re-measured in a browser at both widths; no other screen
was measured, and that is stated rather than implied.

**(3) `FieldGrid`'s missing ROW gap was a second, separate bug in the same
figure.** `gap-x-6` sets `column-gap` alone, so `row-gap` stayed at `normal` —
**0** — and below 1024px, where `max-lg:grid-cols-1` collapses the grid to one
column, every field in it touched the next. `gap-y-5` is added; the 24px COLUMN
gap is untouched, because rule 39's 20 is the vertical rhythm between two fields
and `--space-6` 24 is what separates side-by-side blocks.

**`FieldStack` is named ONCE in the kit** (`FormModal.tsx`) and replaces three
hand-written `flex flex-col gap-3` wrappers in `NewConnectWizard`. It is the
same string the four asset full-page forms already carry from `CR-092` step 2
wave A (`d9fbffde4`); naming it stops a fifth screen spelling it differently.

⚠ **AND `route-b-migrated.txt` IS NOT WHAT CLAUDE.md's SUMMARY SAYS IT IS —
MEASURED, AND REPORTED RATHER THAN REWRITTEN.** CLAUDE.md states that *"a
Tailwind utility is emitted ONLY for a file listed in
`07-frontend/src/styles/route-b-migrated.txt`"* and that a utility in an unlisted
file *"renders as nothing at all"*. `07-frontend/src/styles/tailwind.css:133` is
`@source "../"`, so the v4 compiler scans the whole of `src/` and emits a utility
for **any** file. What the ledger actually gates is the CHECKS: `G31` skips the
listed files and demands that every class in an UNLISTED file be declared by a
stylesheet, and `routeBUtilities.test.ts` owns the listed ones. **The consequence
of writing a utility in an unlisted file is therefore a RED GATE, not an
invisible class** — which is a different hazard needing a different reflex.
⚠ **This wave did not act on that difference and did not need to:** the utility
strings were put in `FormModal.tsx` and `FormModal.css`, both of which are
lawful under either reading, so `NewAccountWizard.tsx` and `MoveInWizard.tsx` —
the two unlisted files — add no class of their own. The correction to that
CLAUDE.md paragraph is left for a deliberate edit with its own evidence rather
than taken in passing inside a repair wave.

### `DEF-CUS-5084` and `DEF-CUS-5085` — TWO DOCUMENT DEFECTS, CORRECTED IN THE RECORD AND NOT BUILT

**The `NO COMMITMENT` chip is applied exactly backwards across these screens.**
Screen **03**, the new account wizard, carries the chip and is named by **three**
register rows — `ACC-S4`, `ACC-S6` and `ACC-S18`, whose entire subject is that
wizard's own review step, drawn across six pages as remedy `R8`. Screens **05,
06 and 07** carry no chip and are named by **no row at all**. So the door every
counter sign-up goes through reads as uncommitted while three rows commit to it,
and the three screens with a genuine absence of commitment say nothing. **A step
2 lane must read §12's Screens column and ignore the chips.** Rows 09 and 10 are
deliberately untouched — they are wave A's screens.

**And the capture's step-1 drawing claims to be the as-built and is wrong four
ways.** Page 75 says *"real field labels in the order the component renders
them"*. It **omits the seven-radio customer-category group entirely** — a control
the PO asked for on 2026-08-25 and which the product renders first and gates the
step on, so a lane building the drawing DELETES it; it draws **Date of birth and
Driver's licence as filled inputs** where both are stated absences because
`_clean_capture` refuses those keys by name, so building it rebuilds the dead UI
two code comments exist to prevent; it puts **`Channel` first** where the product
puts the category first; and it marks **`Channel *`** while leaving the category
unmarked, which is the opposite of what the code refuses on.

⚠ **SO FOR THIS ONE PAGE THE DRAWING IS THE STALE RECORD AND THE SCREEN IS THE
CURRENT ONE — AND THAT IS NOT THE GENERAL RULE.** `CR-094` and B14 rule 37 both
hold that the drawing is the answer, and the blueprint's own screen-03 section
says *"every drawing below is the wizard as it should be, not as it is"*. The
exception is narrow and is this page's own doing: it alone claims to be a
TRANSCRIPTION of the as-built. Where the blueprint PRESCRIBES it still wins.

### EVERY NEW ASSERTION WAS SHOWN RED FIRST, IN THE HARNESS THAT WILL RUN IT

`10-scripts/cr094_wave_e_walkthrough.mjs`, against the pre-fix build on the same
stack: **13 FAIL** — `?step=2` … `?step=7` each painting `Step 1 of 6`, the
category label with no asterisk and no `aria-required`, and the refusal quoted
verbatim beside `markedCategory: false`. The two unit test files were shown red
by undoing exactly the two product hunks and re-running `vitest`: **6 failed**,
and `?step=1`, `?step=0` and `?step=banana` correctly still PASSED, which is how
a reader can tell those cases are measuring the step and not the mount.

The probe itself was **extracted, not copied** (PO: *"dont create duplcate
code"*): the `PROBE` and `RULE` that were a `const` inside
`10-scripts/render-checks/cr092-lane3-field-anatomy.mjs` now live in
`10-scripts/render-checks/lib/fieldAnatomy.mjs` — the directory's own existing
home for shared probe code — and both scripts import them. The corrections that
made that probe trustworthy (measure to the VISIBLE control box, never to a radio
inside a `.seg`; refuse to call a distance across an intervening row a
field-to-field gap) were each paid for once with a wrong number in a published
table, and a copy would have had to pay for them again.

⚠ **THE SPACING ASSERTION CARRIES A NAMED HALF-PIXEL TOLERANCE, AND WHY IS
WRITTEN BESIDE IT.** `getBoundingClientRect` returns fractional coordinates, so
an exact 20px margin reads **19.99** where the field above ends on a fractional
pixel — the same field read **−0.01** before the fix. Exact equality would fail
on the browser's sub-pixel layout rather than on a spacing decision. **What would
make it pass wrongly?** Nothing this defect is about: the readings it was written
for were 0px and 12px, and half a pixel cannot hide either.

### ⚠ `DEF-CUS-5099` — MY OWN FIX BROKE THE PATH IT WAS ON, AND ONLY THE WHOLE-PATH WALK COULD SEE IT

Moving the step into the URL turned the **first draft save into a reset to step
1.** The save mutation wrote `setSearch({ request: id })` — the WHOLE query
string set to one key — which was harmless for as long as the step lived in
component state. The first save happens on a FORWARD MOVE, so a clerk pressing
Continue on step 3 landed back on **step 1** with the draft loaded and the
address reading `?request=…` with no step at all.

⚠ **EVERY PER-STEP CHECK PASSED OVER IT.** `?step=1` through `?step=6` each
painted its own step, correctly, because each step IS right at its own address —
the fault is only in the TRANSITION, and only after a write. `tsc`, eslint and
**707 vitest cases** all passed, because no test drives this wizard through a
save. **It was found by `CR-094`'s own PROVE IT rule — *a wizard needs its whole
path walked, not one step* — and by nothing else.**

The write now MERGES into the query string rather than replacing it, so
whatever else is in the bar survives: today `step`, tomorrow anything the screen
adds. **The general rule worth keeping: when a value moves into the URL, grep
every other writer of that URL before believing the move is done.**

⚠ **AND THE CHECK THAT WAS MEANT TO CATCH IT REPORTED `ok` OVER IT FIRST.** The
walk's advance assertion read *"an enabled Continue exists and I clicked it"*,
which is a different question from *"did the wizard advance"* — so it printed
`ok  Continue was offered on step 4` on a click that moved nothing. That is
hard-won law 7's second shape written by the same hand that was hunting it. The
corrected check reads the caption AFTER the click, compares it, and prints the
wizard's own refusal sentence when the step has not moved; the mistake is kept
in a comment beside it.

⚠ **TWO MORE FAULTS IN THIS LANE'S OWN INSTRUMENTS, both recorded rather than
quietly fixed.** The step-1 lane's `cr094_lane3_walk_and_measure.mjs` fills
**four field ids that do not exist** on the capture's step 3
(`#service_address_line1`, `#service_city`, `#service_postal_code`,
`#unit_count`; the real field is `#address_as_given`) and its `fill()` helper
returns false in silence — and because that script never got past step 1 either,
nothing exposed it. And this script's first draft asserted `fields > 0` on the
standalone move-in's step 2, which **deliberately** renders one sentence —
*"Choose the unit above first — the rest of the move-in is about it."* — with the
rail keeping all five cells on purpose (`BR-SHL-046`: the step number is an
INDEX, so a vanishing step would misaddress every step after it). Asserting
fields on a screen designed to have none is `CR-094` §5(b) exactly: *a held
control and a broken control look identical on screen.* It now asserts the
refusal instead.

**Three draft service requests on `brazosbend`: `SR-26-0009`, `SR-26-0010` and
`SR-26-0011`** — one per run of the instrument, because the capture wizard's six

**Nothing else was written.** The four `create_owner_account` calls were each

## 2026-09-12 · `CR-094-BRC01` STEP 2 WAVE D — THE REQUEST QUEUE, THE IMPORT AND THE TWO WIZARDS WITH NO STEP RAIL (`2.239.4`)

Four rows repaired, three more found on the way, and every fault reproduced in
a browser before a line was changed. The instrument is
`10-scripts/cr094_wave_d_walkthrough.mjs`, run at **1280 and 1440**: `26 checks,
0 failed` after, on `brazosbend`.

### THE FOUR, WITH THE FIGURE EACH TURNED ON

**1 · `DEF-CUS-5010` — a clerk was reading our internal code as the reason a
button was greyed out.** On `SR-26-0006` the Decision tab printed
`customers.serviceRequest.verdict.newConnection.premiseExists`,
`…moveOut.noAccountHere` and `…transfer.noLiveAccount` as literal text, each
one in the disabled button's tooltip AND beside it as the note a clerk reads,
plus `…lookup.servedAndVacant` on two tabs. **Eight keys, declared in 0 of the
11 catalogues.** Now `8` of `8` resolve, in all eleven.

⚠ **IT WAS TWO FAULTS AND THE CATALOGUE LINES ALONE WOULD HAVE FIXED ONE.**
`service_requests.lookup_found` **stores a key, not English** — deliberately,
so a screen's words come from the catalogue (the ruling of 2026-08-19) — and
three screens handed that value to `TextOrNotSupplied`, which prints a string
as it stands. Read from the live API to be sure rather than inferred:
`GET /api/brazosbend/service-requests/{id}` answers
`"lookup_found": "customers.serviceRequest.lookup.noPremiseRecord"`. A new
`CatalogueSentence` resolves it. **The third site is another wave's file**
(`ServiceRequestCapturePage.tsx:1289`) and is left with the component built and
one line to wire.

**THE JUDGEMENT: the copy is capped at six words per sentence even though no
gate can see it.** `G32` reads `message_key=` keyword arguments with `ast`;
these keys are f-strings returned in a tuple, so it reports **0 unresolved**
truthfully over everything it can see — `CLAUDE.md` law 7's *reporting zero
over a scope it silently excludes*. `G33` walks G32's key set by construction,
so the six-word cap could not reach them either. The eight English lines are
one sentence each, six words or fewer, and a backend test asserts that where
`G33` cannot.

**2 · `DEF-CUS-5009` — the held control was on the wrong rows.**
`RUN-2814` (1,251 in / 1,247 loaded / **4 rejected** / Loaded) and `RUN-2822`
(312 / 310 / **2** / Loaded) were offered only *Roll back this run*;
`IMP-260912-02` (3 / 0 / **0 rejected** / File read) was offered *Fix the
rejected rows*, disabled. **THE JUDGEMENT: each action asks its own question of
its own field** — roll back where something LOADED, the fix where something was
REJECTED, and a run where both are true is offered both. A run still in flight
with nothing rejected is offered neither, because there is nothing to do to it.
The old code was one ternary on `status`, and the `rejected` count — the only
thing the fix is about — played no part.

**The hold stays and its expiry test ships with it.** Reopening a finished run
is `ACC-S9`, a specification no ruling defers, so *Fix the rejected rows*
renders disabled with its reason; the case that fires the day it is built is in
the same commit (law 2's mirror half).

**3 · `DEF-CUS-5011` — the chip said `All` over a filtered list.**
Chip `All`, `aria-pressed="true"`, footer `1–18 of 18`, and the one network
call `?segment=open&…` on a tenant holding **20** requests. Two defaults, each
written correctly, that nothing ever compared.

**THE JUDGEMENT: `All` means all, and the drawn default becomes an APPLIED
filter.** B19 §12.1 draws the strip with **Open** selected, so `open` is the
default and the chip now says `Show: Open`; an absent segment means `all`,
which is what the shared `FilterBar`'s chip has always claimed. The alternative
— teaching `FilterBar` that one screen's *no filter* is not *all* — would move
twenty-odd lists on one screen's authority.

⚠ **SEEDING THE URL ON MOUNT WAS TRIED AND ABANDONED**, and it is worth
recording because it looks like the obvious fix: it works, and it makes
`DEF-664`'s own case false — that case asserts the standalone screen's address
starts EMPTY and gains parameters only when a clerk acts. **THE PRICE, stated
rather than hidden:** a cleared segment is not shareable, because a bare URL is
the default. Nothing on screen lies while that happens, which is the whole of
this defect; it is the same class as `DEF-CUS-5091` and belongs to that row.

**4 · `DEF-CUS-5071` — the step rail, and it was a WIRING job.**
Zero rail nodes on change-plan at step 1 **and at step 2 after a plan was
picked**, zero on payment-plan. Both now mount `components/WizardFrame`, which
the other nine customers wizards already use, so **10 of 11**. The rail is
built by `.map()` over the declared const, which is the half that matters: a
fourth step appears on it, and a step with no label key is a typecheck error.

Measured after: the rail renders with all three names, step 1 `active` and step
3 `upcoming`, and **B14 rule 39's own anchors — 24px below the rail, 16×20 per
step, gap 12, badge 26×26** — read with `getComputedStyle`, not off a
stylesheet. Rule 40's 32px title holds. It also MOVES: picking a plan and
pressing Continue advances it, step 1 becomes navigable and step 3 does not.

**TWO DIVERGENCES FROM THE DRAWING, both deliberate and both recorded in the
code.** The drawing inks a greyed-out Continue; the frame renders it live and
prints the refusal at the button that refused it (`DEF-178`, `DEF-936`).
**B14 rule 38 settles that** — where a drawing and our UI rules disagree about
how a form is BUILT, the UI rules win — and changing the frame instead would
move eleven wizards at once. **And the RBAC refusal moved to a page-level
strip**, because a read-only role must learn it cannot act BEFORE pressing
anything; that is what the nine siblings do (`MoveOutWizard.tsx:816`), so it is
reused rather than re-invented.

## 2026-09-12 — ⚠ A COMPLAINT IS A WORK ORDER, NOT A SERVICE REQUEST — AND THIS REVERSES THIS SESSION'S OWN RECOMMENDATION OF THE SAME DAY

**`CR-094-BRC01` step 2 wave G, built.** The PO ruled the WHAT and asked us the
HOW: *"in the main tab list, add complaints and services. These two tabs. build
their ad form and detail view. and tables."*, then *"can we combine them with
Service request - you can tell me how you wna tot handle this"*. Under
`CLAUDE.md` law 13 that second sentence is ours to answer and write down, so
this is the answer with its evidence.

### THE JUDGMENT

**A complaint is a WORK ORDER of type `Consumer Complaint`, and a service is a
work order of type `Consumer Services`. No new table, no new write path, no
`class` column.** The two tabs are two filtered views of `GET /work-orders`, one
per heading, and both intake forms commit through `POST /work-orders` — the
route `07-endpoints.md` §1 row 14 already calls *"the ONE raise every door
uses"*.

### ⚠ IT SUPERSEDES THE RECOMMENDATION RECORDED IN THIS LOG EARLIER TODAY

The entry *"THREE CONFIRMATIONS AND ONE DESIGN QUESTION PUT BACK TO US"* recorded
this recommendation: *"one record, one table, one detail page; Complaints and
Services become two FILTERED TABS over [`ServiceRequest`], each with its own
full-page capture form … What must stay distinct is a **class** column and
**not** a new table."*

**It was never put to the PO as a decision and it is withdrawn.** It was written
from `customers.models.ServiceRequest`'s three `kind` columns without reading the
blueprint's §10 drawings — and those drawings answer the question in their own
words on page 39:

> *"This tab does not exist, and everything behind it does. There is no
> complaints list, no complaint form and no complaint record anywhere in the
> front end — but a complaint is already a **work order**: `Consumer Complaint`
> is one of the nine job types the Product Owner listed themselves, it carries
> fifteen kinds beneath it, and a job can already stand on an account. **What is
> missing is the screen, not the record.**"*

And the PO's general ruling of the same day makes that drawing the
specification: *"we have resolved everyt item in wireframes and detaisl are
captured beow them - that should be enough"*, with *"The ruling is provenance,
the drawing is the specification."*

### WHY THE WORK-ORDER MODEL WINS ON THE EVIDENCE, MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING

| what the two forms need | where it already is |
|---|---|
| the two kinds of record | `work.models.SEED_TYPE_SPINE` — `COMPLAINT` / *Consumer Complaint* (High) and `CONSUMER_SVC` / *Consumer Services* (Normal), seeded for every tenant |
| the fifteen kinds beneath each | `SEED_BASE_SUB_TYPES` + the per-service groups, a tenant's own two-level catalogue (`BR-WRK-058`) |
| standing on an account | `work_orders.account_id`, `BR-WRK-006`'s third anchor, with `ck_work_orders_has_anchor` under it |
| the response-time promise | `BR-WRK-018` — the priority stamps `due_at` from the utility's own `sla_hours` |
| the one write | `POST /work-orders` |
| the detail view | the work order's own page, which the blueprint itself draws at `/…/work/wo/…` |

**Against `ServiceRequest`, whose own vocabulary is a MOVE** — its `type` is
`move_in` / `move_out` / `disconnect` — and which carries no priority, no due
time and no job. Building there would have meant a `class` column, a second
intake write, a second queue and a second place for the response-time rule to be
read differently. **That is the PO's own deposit reasoning applied one table
over**, from the same day: *"It is one concept … and building it four times
would give four behaviours."*

### TWO TABS RATHER THAN ONE FILTER, AND THE REASON IS THE DRAWING'S

Page 46: *"`Consumer Services` is what a customer ASKED FOR; `Consumer
Complaint` is what went wrong. A container swap answered in three days is a good
service and a missed collection answered in three days is not, which is why they
carry different response times and why they are two tabs rather than one
filter."* The two headings carry different seeded SLAs — **8 hours against 72** —
so the two queues answer different questions about lateness.

### ⚠ AND THE TABS ARE ON THE REGISTER, NOT ON THE ACCOUNT DETAIL

*"The main tab list"* names neither screen and both draw a strip, so it was read
off the drawing rather than guessed: page 39's address is
`/:tenant/accounts?tab=complaints` and page 47's is
`/:tenant/accounts?tab=services`, and the drawn header reads *"10 tabs"*. The
register went from eight to **ten**, `Complaints` and `Services` sitting after
the six flow queues and before `Imports`. **The account detail's twelve tabs are
untouched.**

### WHAT THE FORMS DO NOT COLLECT, AND WHY EACH ONE IS AN ABSENCE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT

`work_orders` has no column for any of these, and a field with nowhere to store
its value is dead UI (hard-won law 2):

* **the reporter's name and phone** (page 41's *Who told us*) — the complainant
  may not be the account holder and there is no reporter column;
* **the complaint's own words, and an attachment** — there is no description
  column; `technician_notes` is what a crew writes afterwards, a different fact.
  The drawing states this gap itself: *"A job closes with a sentence somebody
  typed and nothing else — no cause, no outcome category, no complaints
  register."*;
* **a cause or an outcome category** — page 42's own dashed block says *"There is
  no vocabulary to offer"*;
* **the service form's drawn fifth step, `Service fees`** — page 219 calls it *"a
  proposal"* on *"a model that already exists rather than a new one"*, meaning
  the SERVICE REQUEST's fee model. `work_orders` carries no quoted, collected or
  outstanding column, and `work.costing` computes what a finished job COST from
  labour and parts, which is not what a customer was quoted. **So the service
  form is FOUR steps and not five**, and nothing on either screen mentions a
  fee.

Also absent with their reasons: the drawn `CUSTOMER` column (the row serves
`{id, account_no}` and nothing else — a dash in every cell would assert *"this
job has no customer"* on every row), the four KPI tiles (each is a figure over
the whole queue and A11's envelope carries no aggregate), and the `Resolved` /
`All` segment chips (`GET /work-orders` serves the OPEN window only).

### TWO DEFECTS THE BUILD FOUND, BOTH ON THE CRITICAL PATH, BOTH FIXED HERE

**`DEF-WRK-5106` — the type filter matched a heading and nothing beneath it.**
`dispatch._apply_filters` matched `type_ref_id` and the free-typed words only,
which was right while the catalogue was flat and stopped being right on
2026-09-07 when `BR-WRK-058` made it two-level. **Every row the blueprint draws
is a sub-type**, so a queue pinned to *Consumer Complaint* returned NOTHING on a
utility full of complaints — and an empty list is indistinguishable from having
none. Fixed one level deep (`type_ref__parent_id`), never as a prefix, so picking
a kind still narrows to that kind. `BR-WRK-026`'s six filters do not move.

**`DEF-WRK-5109` — a job filed under a kind with no response time of its own got
NO priority and NO due date at all.** Three documents said otherwise:
`work/models.py`'s own comment (*"which hangs under Consumer Complaint, would
inherit **8 hours**"*), `OQ-WRK-1765`'s closure, and the name
`URGENT_BEATS_ITS_PARENT`, which only means something if there is an inheritance
to beat. **`_resolve_priority` walked no parent.** Twelve of the seeded sub-types
carry no default — `Billing Issues`, `Low Pressure`, `Missed collection`,
`Voltage complaint` among them — so the queue's *Respond by* column would have
been empty on nearly every row, reading exactly like a utility that had not
seeded priorities. **Hard-won law 1 in its purest form.** Fixed as a FALLBACK and
never an override, so a gas leak call-out keeps its own 4 hours rather than
inheriting its heading's 8 — which is the figure `OQ-WRK-1765` exists to prevent.

**Worked, on the seeded water utility:** a complaint filed as *Billing Issues* at
09:14 now carries **High · 8 hours**, so its *Respond by* reads **17:14 the same
day**. Before the fix that cell was a dash.

### AND A THIRD RED, NOT MINE, DATED RATHER THAN DISMISSED

`test_us_wrk_026_tc4_each_of_the_five_chips_narrows_the_list` has been red since
**2026-09-07**: its fixture raises jobs of *Leak investigation* and *Read
verification*, both of which `work/0023` DEACTIVATED under `BR-WRK-058`, so
`_resolve_order_type` (which filters `active=True`) resolves neither and the
priority chip returns zero. `DEF-WRK-5108`, filed and **not** fixed here — it is
another lane's suite and fixing it inside a commit about complaints is the silent
side-fix the UI skill forbids.

## 2026-09-12 — `CR-094-BRC01` STEP 2 WAVE H · THE ONE DEPOSIT CAPABILITY, AND AN ENGINE THAT HAD BEEN FINISHED FOR SIXTEEN DAYS BEHIND NO DOOR

**WHICH PROCESS THIS WAS, decided and not asked.** A clerk **cannot** take a
deposit in the product today, on any of the four wizards that draw one — so
this is **BUILD** (`r11`), not maintenance. The one question of
`22-product-maintenance-process.md` answers itself: *can a user do this task in
the product today?* No.

### WHAT A CLERK CAN NOW DO, in plain words

Take the deposit, in the same flow as the move-in, and have it land in the right
three places at once.

A clerk doing a move-in now meets a **Deposit** step. They say whether the
account needs one, type the amount and pick why, set when it is due, and — if
the customer is paying at the counter — record how the money arrived, the
reference, the posting day and the day it cleared. Pressing *Complete move-in*
writes the account, the opening readings and the payment **in one go**, and if
the payment is refused nothing is written at all and every field is still on
screen.

**Worked, on `brazosbend`:** a move-in that takes **$150.00** by card with the
clearing date filled in leaves one cleared payment marked as a deposit,
**$150.00** credited to the deposit-liability account in the books, and
**$150.00** against the account as money held. Leave the clearing date empty and
the same commit records the payment, leaves the account at **$0.00** of deposit,
and says so before the clerk commits — because the money has not arrived, and
the books wait on the same day.

### ⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT THING THIS WAVE FOUND, AND IT WAS FOUND BY GREPPING RATHER THAN BY BUILDING

**Everything except the door already existed, and had since 2026-08-27.** One
call does all of it:

    payments.services.record_payment(purpose="deposit", cleared_at=…)
      → ledger_seam.post_payment_cleared          DR undeposited / CR 2300
      → customers.services.record_deposit_movement  BR-CUS-670, the REGISTER
      → notifications                             the customer's receipt

`record_deposit_movement` is itself a **customers** function, published for
payments and resolved there by name, and it already locks the account, refuses a
movement of zero, refuses a release that would take the register below zero
rather than clamping it, stamps the receipt date **only when the account has
none** (`BR-CUS-050`, so a second deposit cannot restart the interest clock) and
writes its own audit row.

**So `DEF-177` — *"nothing writes `accounts.deposit_on_file`"* — was already
CLOSED, and the first draft of this wave re-opened it.** That draft wrote the
column itself, which would have been **two paths to one money column**:
`DEF-154`'s shape, and the thing `DEF-177` was filed about from the other side.
It was caught by reading the payments dataclass — `deposit_held_after` and
`BR-CUS-670` are fields on `RecordedPayment` — and the writer was deleted. The
figure is now read back off the payment and nothing on the customers side
writes it.

⚠ **AND THE ABSENCE IS NOW GUARDED RATHER THAN REMEMBERED.**
`test_cr094_wh__customers_is_not_a_second_writer_of_the_register` makes the
register writer unreachable and asserts the column does **not** move. A second
writer in `apps/customers/deposit.py` passes every other case in that file and
fails only that one.

**What was ACTUALLY missing was the entry point**, measured at 2.239.4:
`POST /accounts` and `POST /accounts/{id}/move-in` refused a `deposit` block
with `customers.account.unknown_field` on field `deposit`. That is hard-won
law 2's mirror at feature scale — a finished engine behind no door — and it is
`DEF-CUS-5112`.

### THE FOUR RULINGS THIS BUILT, AND THE ONE THAT DECIDED THE SHAPE

| PO verbatim | what it settled |
|---|---|
| ***"(a) It is one concept — money held against an account — and building it four times would give four behaviours."*** | **ONE capability**, mounted per flow |
| ***"if there are deposits, then there should be a proper flow to accept those deposit also … you figure it out where … but it should be in the same flow"*** | it is a STEP of the wizard, not a separate errand |
| ***"on the plans and deposit step, change the plans and deposit step to account preferences … and add one more step of deposit into the move in stepper and copy the deposit step also. from the new account."*** | move-in 5 steps → **6** |
| ***"Make it as account preferences in that user can also select paperless billing. that should also be available."*** | the renamed step carries the delivery elections |

**ONE OF EACH, which is the whole of the shape ruling:** one customers-side
module (`apps/customers/deposit.py`), one `deposit` key in
`services.CREATE_FIELDS` — so `MOVE_IN_FIELDS`, which is `CREATE_FIELDS` minus
`unit_id`, gains it **in the same line** and S18 and S19 cannot drift apart —
one React component (`depositCapability.tsx`) whose only per-flow difference is
a `carryForward` prop, and **no** second writer of the register.

### ⚠ A QUESTION I DID NOT ASK, BECAUSE THE REPOSITORY HAD ALREADY ANSWERED IT

The brief warned that a previous lane told the PO the deposit's accounting
*"genuinely needs you"* and was wrong. It is ruled: **`BR-CUS-025`, 2026-08-12 —
a deposit is a LIABILITY, never revenue**, with `deposit_liability` **2300** in
the chart of accounts. **Nothing in this wave decides anything about the
books**, and hard rule 5 keeps the ledger posting service the sole writer of
journal lines. Law 13, applied rather than restated.

### WHERE THE DEPOSIT AMOUNT COMES FROM — ASKED OF THE CODE, AND RECORDED

**B14 rule 37: the `$150.00` on blueprint page 70 is an ILLUSTRATION and is
stated nowhere in the product.** What the product holds:

* **`rating.plan_deposit_rules`** — rate_plan × account_type → one fixed amount
  **and its `CHAR(3)`** (`BR-RAT-020/023`, r5 #8). Editable on Plans & Rates, so
  it **is a tenant setting**, not a constant.
* `rating.selectors.deposit_rule_for(rate_plan_id, account_type_id)` reads it,
  and has since billing needed it for `BR-BIL-012`'s first-bill line.
* **Nothing published a per-ACCOUNT read of it.** `apps/payments/purposes.py`
  names that contract (`DEPOSIT_REQUIREMENT_READ =
  "deposit_requirement_for_account"`), resolves it at call time, finds nothing,
  and reports `deposit_requirement_not_checked` on every deposit-purpose
  payment. **That is still true** — this wave publishes a CUSTOMERS-side read,
  which is not what payments resolves, and says so rather than half-serving it.

**So the clerk TYPES the figure, which is the drawing's own ruling** — its
helper reads *"Typed by hand today."* beside a dashed *"A credit tier would size
this, and nothing works one out"* (`BR-CUS-058`: the tier is COMPUTED from
payment history and has no input path). What this wave adds is that the server
**resolves the plan's standard and reports it beside what was typed**, so two
figures for one fact cannot pass silently — and **never overrides it**, because
sizing a deposit is a judgement and a server refusing a clerk's figure because a
reference table disagreed would be inventing a rule nobody signed.

**Worked:** where the plan's rule says **$120.00** and the clerk types
**$150.00**, the answer carries `deposit_amount_differs_from_plan_standard` and
**$150.00** is what is taken. Where the plan names no rule at all the answer
carries `deposit_plan_standard_not_configured` — **which is not a standard of
zero**, and rating's own read warns about exactly that collapse.

### THREE ANSWERS AND NOT TWO

`required` · `not_required` (none was assessed) · `waived` (one WAS assessed and
somebody decided not to collect it). **Collapsing the last two would lose a
decision with a person behind it**, and it is the same distinction
`rating.deposit_rule_for` draws one layer down about `None` versus `0.00`.

### WHAT I DECIDED RATHER THAN ASKED

**1 · The deposit's own step is added and the plan step is RENAMED, not split.**
The step never chose a plan — the plan lives once on the unit and the account
derives it (PO 2026-08-11) — so an id reading `plan` named the one thing the
step cannot do. Both the id and the label moved, because `MOVE_IN_STEPS` is what
the rail **and** the Move-ins tab's STEP column are derived from (`BR-SHL-046`);
moving one without the other paints `4 of 5` over a six-step flow, which is
`DEF-648`'s exact shape.

**2 · A stale step number clamps DOWNWARD and that is the safe direction.** The
numbers are INDEXES and a parked draft or a Move-ins row reopens the wizard AT
one. Inserting `deposit` at 5 moves `review` to 6, so a draft parked on the old
step 5 now opens on `deposit` — one step short of where it was rather than past
the end. `stepFromParam` clamps, so no stale number errors.

**3 · Carry-forward stays a STATED ABSENCE rather than becoming a control.**
`OQ-510` is now **answered for the collection half** — the wizards do offer a
deposit election — and **not for carry-forward**: `BR-CUS-024`'s mechanics are
unsigned, nothing can read a prior position, and a control that saved nowhere
would be a decision the customer believes was recorded. The drawing agrees: page
71 draws it dashed.

**4 · The tenders are a TYPED list and it is filed as a defect.** `BR-PAY-026`
makes payment methods a tenant lookup and no endpoint serves them to a wizard
step, so the blueprint's seven are typed out — hard-won law 12's shape, one list
over. The honest mitigation is that the **server** decides: `record_payment`
refuses an unknown code by name. `DEF-CUS-5115`.

**5 · A `null` currency renders a SENTENCE, never `USD`.** The move-in reads the
currency off the outgoing account (`BR-TEN-042`'s lock); the new-account wizard
has no account yet and there is **no front-end reader of the tenant's own
currency at all** — `TenantRegional` publishes a timezone and a date format and
nothing else. So its footer states the absence, which is
`UnitPricingPanel.money`'s own precedent in this family. `DEF-CUS-5114`, with
the one-line ask written down; **not** fixed here, because `TenantRegional.tsx`
is the shell's and reaches every money screen in the product.

### ⚠ WHERE THIS LEAVES THE DRAWING — RECORDED, NOT DONE QUIETLY (B14 rule 38)

**Every one of the drawing's ten controls is present, in its order, with its
options and its stated absences. What changed is LENGTH.** The drawing's section
heads are questions — *"Does this account need a deposit?"* — and **rule 33 caps
a heading at three words with no sentence**; its *Due* helper is one twelve-word
sentence where the rule allows six per sentence and says *two sentences of six
beat one of twelve*. The dashed boxes each carry a fact **and then a paragraph
explaining why the product works that way**, and rule 33's fifth cap gives
rationale **zero words on screen**.

So the headings read *The deposit.* · *Carried over.* · *Paid today.* — the
short noun phrases this wizard family already uses (*Plan & deposit.*,
*Deposit & credit.*) — the helpers are split into two short sentences, and the
rationale lives in the component's docstring and in `BR-CUS-1050`. Rule 38's
last clause leaves WHAT a form contains to the drawing and **nothing was
dropped**; rule 33 governs how long it may be.

⚠ **`04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/08-screen-layouts.md` IS A SIBLING LANE'S
IN-FLIGHT FILE** (the master-accounts tab, uncommitted in this shared tree), so
this divergence is recorded HERE and in the component's docstring rather than
appended to that file — writing into it would have published another lane's
unfinished rows (`DEF-168`'s mechanism). **It is owed there**, and this
paragraph is the handover.

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND HOW

**RED FIRST, in the harness that runs it, at the tip.** A private
`git worktree` was pinned at `c9d4a1bea` and the new backend file run there:

    ImportError: cannot import name 'deposit' from 'apps.customers'

…which only proves the module is new, so a second probe called the **existing**
door at the tip and printed what a clerk would have met:

    REFUSED: customers.account.unknown_field ['deposit']

That is the defect in one line: the counter door refused a deposit **by field
name**. Green afterwards: **21 backend cases** and **21 front-end cases**, plus
the four touched wizard suites (**100 passed**).

**READ THE FAILURES I DID NOT CAUSE, AND DATED THEM.** Two `tsc` errors stand
that are **not** mine and **not** at the tip either — they are a sibling lane's
uncommitted work in this shared tree: `AccountsCreateEntry.test.tsx` missing the
`services` and `complaints` tab keys (the `jobIntakeShared.tsx` wave, untracked)
and two `AssetFormModal` imports against a modified `assetsShared.tsx`. Neither
is in `git log` because neither is committed. **Reported, not touched.**

### THE FILES, AND THE LANE SPLIT IN A SHARED TREE

**Mine:** `apps/customers/deposit.py` (new) · `apps/customers/seams.py` (two
resolves) · `apps/customers/services.py` · `tests/test_cr094_wh_deposit.py`
(new) · `features/customers/depositCapability.tsx` (+ its test, both new) ·

### VERSION AND ROLLBACK

## 2026-09-12 — `CR-092-BRC01` `AST-B-12` · AN ASSET IS CORRECTED AT AN ADDRESS, AND THE THREE PANELS THAT COULD NOT TURN THEIR OWN PAGES (`2.239.9`)

**The capability, in the specification's own words:** *"A clerk can correct an
asset from the asset, at an address they can come back to."* PO instruction of
2026-09-11, verbatim: *"this should be form and not modal."* Approved
2026-09-12 with the other nine.

**What changed is the container and the route, and nothing else.** The form,
its schema and its write already existed and are unchanged: `AssetFormModal`
moved out of `AssetRegistryPage.tsx` into `AssetEditPage.tsx` with its
`FormModal` frame removed, which is the drawing's own instruction (*"the dialog
frame itself — REMOVED … it is the container, not a field"*) and the same
conversion `CR-028 AST-W4` made for reassign, log-repair and retire on
2026-08-22. **There is no second copy of that form anywhere**, and the registry
pencil now navigates instead of setting a piece of local state.

### THE JUDGMENTS, WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT

**1 · THE FIELD SET IS THE AS-BUILT NINE, AND THE DRAWING NAMES A TENTH.**
Screen 14's field table lists `location_note` where the built form carries
`manufacturer_model`, while its own note says the field set *"is read from
`AssetRegistryPage.tsx`'s `AssetFormModal`"*. It was read wrongly. Neither
field was moved on the strength of it: `location_note` **is** editable, on the
Lifecycle panel dialog (`AST-B-25`, shipped in this same pass), so adding it
here would be a second way to write one field rather than a new capability, and
removing `manufacturer_model` would delete one a clerk has today. Filed as
`DEF-AST-5107` and noted on the screen's own row in `08-screen-layouts.md`,
which is where a lane looks before opening the drawing. ⚠ **The reconciliation
table beside it (as-built 11 = unchanged 10 + moved 1 − removed 1 + new 1)
cannot see a SWAP, because a swap leaves the count right** — which is why the
arithmetic passed over it.

**2 · THE LEAD SENTENCE IS FOUR WORDS, NOT THE DRAWN NINE.** The drawing writes
*"Correct what was recorded when this meter went in."* B14 rule 33 caps an
instruction at **six words per sentence**, and B14 rule 38 says the UI rules
win where a drawing and our rules disagree about how a form is built. The
screen ships *"Correct what was recorded."* The clause that was dropped — *when
this meter went in* — is also wrong for an asset still in inventory, which has
never been installed at all.

**3 · SAVING RETURNS THE CLERK TO THE ASSET, NOT TO THE LIST THEY CAME FROM.**
The dialog returned to whatever was behind it. A page cannot, and the four
lifecycle flows converted in 2026-08-22 all land on the asset's own screen —
which is also the screen that shows the corrected value. So the two doors lead
to one place. The toast still names the asset.

**4 · `AST-09` IS A MINTED BADGE AND A1 MINTS NOTHING.** r10 draws `AST-01`..
`AST-08` and draws no edit screen, because in r10 editing WAS a dialog and a
dialog carries no badge; the badge is registered in
`10-scripts/gates/g29_allocated_badges.txt`, which is the third authority `G29`
reads. A1's `S49`–`S60` addendum names add, reassign, log-repair and retire and
no edit screen, so the route carries `a1: null` with its reason and the G29
ratchet moves from 53 to 55 — **two**, because one of them is not ours (below).

### WHAT BUILDING IT FOUND, AND IT IS THE LARGER HALF

**⚠ `AST-B-19` — THIS MORNING'S SERVER PAGING — GAVE FOUR PANELS PAGE STATE AND
ONLY ONE OF THEM A PAGER (`DEF-AST-5117`, fixed here).** `Export` and
`Assignment history` each held `page`/`per` that nothing could set, and `Work &
maintenance` passed no page at all and discarded the `total` beside its rows.
So three lists inside every asset showed their first fifty rows and offered no
way to reach the rest — **the exact fault `AST-B-19` was written to remove**,
shipped inside the change that removed it. Every check passed over it: a page of
rows renders correctly whether or not a second page is reachable, and no gate in
this repo reads rendered output. **`eslint --max-warnings 0` named it at the
raise site** (*"setExportPage is assigned a value but never used"*) from the
moment it landed, and this lane found it by running eslint on a file it was
touching for another reason. The lesson is not new and it is worth writing
again: **a pager is the CONTROL half of server paging, and a panel holding page
state with no footer is dead UI by construction.**

**⚠ `G29` HAD BEEN RED FOR FIVE DAYS WITH NO OWNER (`DEF-RBS-5110`, fixed
here).** `/:tenant/runbooks/work` claimed `RBS-007`, a badge no authority
defined, from `df1ade52e` on 2026-09-07 — dated with `git log -S`, not assumed.
The badge is real (`17-runbooks/01-overview.md` line 445 names it) and the
registration was simply skipped, so the fix is the transcription that was
missed. It is fixed rather than merely filed because the gate is merge-blocking
and a lane meeting a red it did not cause is how a true failure acquires the
protective colouring of a known one.

**⚠ AND THE SCREEN-ID MAP IS FIVE ROUTES BEHIND THE ROUTER (`DEF-SHL-5116`,
filed and NOT fixed).** `routing/screenIds.test.tsx` compares the whole map
against `App.tsx`'s flattened routes; five are missing — `/:tenant/runbooks`
(2026-09-06), `/:tenant/premises/units/new` (2026-09-09),
`/:tenant/work/parts/import`, and `/:tenant/complaints/new` and
`/:tenant/services/new` (both today). **Not this lane's to answer:** each needs
an id decision in its own module, and taking five of them inside a commit about
an edit screen is exactly the smuggling the process forbids. ⚠ **`G29` reports
PASS over the same map**, because it reads the map against the two id
authorities and never against the router — a check measuring a scope that
excludes the thing that is wrong.

### PROVED RED BEFORE TRUSTED GREEN — AND THE FIRST PROOF FAILED

Each fault planted, each restored byte-identical, transcripts in the lane's
scratch report. Removing the header's Edit control turns `TC-A1` red; leaving
the registry pencil as it was turns `TC-A3` red; removing either `ListPager`
turns its own panel's case red on the footer being absent.

⚠ **BUT DELETING THE ROUTE FROM `App.tsx` LEFT ALL FIVE NEW CASES GREEN**, because
the suite mounts its own `<Routes>` and therefore says nothing about where the
application mounts the screen — law 7's *check that cannot fail*, in the shape
the CWP audit already records. The real mount is asserted by
`routing/screenIds.test.tsx`, and the test file now says so instead of claiming
a proof it does not have.

### VERSION AND ROLLBACK

**`2.239.9`.** No migration, no column, no recorded figure moves. Rollback is
the revert of these commits: the page and its route leave, `AssetFormModal`
returns to the registry with its dialog, the header loses its Edit button, and
the three pagers go with it — which puts those panels back on their first page,
so a rollback is a return to `DEF-AST-5117` and not to a clean state.

## 2026-09-12 — `CR-094-BRC01` wave J · `ACC-S14` · A QUICK ACTION IS A FORM OVER THE ACCOUNT, AND THE ENDPOINT DECIDES WHAT IT MAY ASK (`2.240.0`)

**The commitment, in the blueprint's own card (`ACC-S14`, p208):** *"Every quick
action on an account opens as a form over the account, with all of its fields and
a recap before it commits."* Its acceptance sentence: *"A clerk on the phone
presses any of the thirteen, fills the form **without losing sight of the balance
behind it**, reads back a recap, and commits — or reads why it cannot be
committed, on the button itself."*

### THE JUDGMENTS, WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT

**1 · MODAL OR PAGE IS SETTLED BY THE COMMITMENT CARD, NOT BY THE DRAWING, AND
NO RULE WAS INVENTED.** B14 rule 30 was DECLINED on 2026-08-30 and the skill's §5
says a case that does not resemble the estimate precedent must be stated rather
than decided quietly. **Several of the thirteen do not resemble it** — six are
multi-step, four hold a table of their own, and losing a twenty-field move-in on
a refresh costs real work. What resolves it is not a new rule but the card: *"without
losing sight of the balance behind it"*. **A page replaces the balance; a dialog
does not.** The specific beats the general.

⚠ **`AST-B-12` OF THE SAME DAY — *"this should be form and not modal"* — DOES NOT
REACH THESE THIRTEEN.** That ruling is about **correcting an asset** *"at an
address they can come back to"*: its value is the bookmarkable address, and there
is no context behind the dialog worth keeping because the clerk came from a
registry row. Here the requirement is the opposite and is written down — what is
behind the form is half of what the clerk is being asked about. **Two instances,
two answers, one principle: what is BEHIND the form decides.** Neither is
generalised; neither was re-raised with the PO (law 13).

**2 · THE ENDPOINT IS THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT, AND THE DRAWING DOES NOT KNOW IT
(`DEF-CUS-5121`).** `apps/customers/services.activate_account` opens with
`_reject_unknown(data, frozenset({"opened_at", "status"}))`, and `_reject_unknown`
**raises a field error on a stranger rather than ignoring it**. R4's `ACC-Q03`
draws **ten** fields — an opening-read choice, a start date per service, a base
charge, a deposit choice, a deposit amount, a deposit due date, a billing cycle
and two notification checkboxes. **Nine of the ten cannot be sent.**

**WORKED, on the blueprint's own fixture:** activating `A-12048 · Kwan, Michael`
through the drawn form would post ten fields; the server would refuse the first
stranger it met and the activation would fail — while a form that silently
dropped them would collect a clerk's deposit decision and throw it away. **So the
built form asks for the ONE writable field (`opened_at`), shows the two facts it
can read, and states the other three as absences on screen.** Two of those three
are R4's own caveat box; the third — the opening read — the drawing draws as a
live picker.

⚠ **`Base charge` and `Billing cycle` are not drawn even as read-only facts**,
because `AccountUnitPlan` is `{name, code, version, since}` and `AccountDetail`
carries no cycle. There is nothing to put in those boxes.

**3 · ONE COMPONENT, THIRTEEN CONFIGURATIONS — AND ELEVEN OF THEM ARE NOT
RE-AUTHORED.** PO standing instruction: *"Do all changes based on actual code —
also don't create duplicate code."* The other twelve quick actions already open a
complete, live, tested surface — six wizards, a page and two modals totalling
**~7,300 lines** with park-and-resume behind them. **Re-authoring those as dialogs
is the duplicate code that instruction forbids**, and it would throw away their
tests and their server wiring. `accountQuickActions.ts` declares all thirteen with
their figure id and destination, so the wave that moves a CONTAINER changes a
destination and re-types no form.

**4 · WHERE THE DRAWING LOSES, IT IS B14 RULE 38 BY NAME.** Rule 38 lists
**verbatim** the disagreements this drawing has with the kit: *"two fields sit
side by side"* and *"the footer puts Cancel on the left"* are **form
CONSTRUCTION**, where the UI rules win and *"nothing is built for it"*. R4 draws
every section as two columns and puts `Save & exit` on the left of two of them.
Built as one column through `FieldStack`, with the kit's footer. **What the form
CONTAINS is still the drawing's** — which fields, in which order, under which
headings, with which helper sentence.

**5 · THE KIT GAINED TWO OPT-INS RATHER THAN THIRTEEN SCREENS GAINING COPIES.**
`RecapBox` (this repo already held THREE private answers to that one shape —
`DEF-SHL-5123`) and `FormModal.commitBlocked`, so a form with no write behind it
refuses on its own commit instead of at the server. **Absent means unchanged, so
no existing caller moves**; `FormModal`'s own 28 cases and `AccountActions`' 29
were run and are unchanged.

### WHAT BUILDING IT FOUND

**⚠ THE ACTIVATE BUTTON COMMITTED ON THE CLICK.** No dialog, no date, no recap and
no way back, on an act that starts billing — `activate.mutate()` straight off
`onClick`. That is what R4's caption for `ACC-Q03` names (*"the confirmation the
product is missing"*). It now opens its form, and `opened_at` can be set at all
for the first time.

**⚠ THE `Adjust` BUTTON'S `onClick` IS `() => undefined` (`DEF-CUS-5125`).** G13
asks whether a prop is PASSED, and `() => undefined` is a passed handler — so a
control that opens nothing passes every check this repo has. Declared `held` with
its reason; its form is the next wave.

**⚠ A RED NOBODY CAUSED, DATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED (`DEF-CUS-5124`).** The Meters
tab shows no last read. It fails at this wave's PARENT too — proved in a
`git worktree` pinned at `fa2298b11`, not assumed — and `formatQuantity("43148")`
was **measured** returning `"43,148"`, so the formatter is not at fault. Which of
the screen and the fixture is stale is left to the metering seam's owner.

**⚠ AND THE DRAWING THIS WAS BUILT FROM IS ON NO BRANCH (`DEF-CUS-5122`).**
`05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` is cited by path by five step-1
documents and every wave brief, and `git ls-files` does not list it. Recovered by
blob hash and verified against the `sha256` step 1 recorded, so this wave and that
audit read the same 242 pages.

### PROVED RED BEFORE TRUSTED GREEN

Each fault planted against the PRODUCT code, each restored byte-identical: the
recap made to ignore live form state turns *"the recap MOVES when the date does"*
red; `commitBlocked` made not to disable turns two `BR-SHL-025` cases red; a field
the endpoint refuses added to the configuration turns *"asks ONLY for fields the
endpoint accepts"* red. **38 new cases, all green.**

⚠ **`tsc` WAS ITSELF PROVED.** `npx tsc --noEmit` printed nothing, which is
indistinguishable from hard-won law 7's false pass; a type error was injected and
the LOCAL binary (5.5.4) named it at its line.

⚠ **NOT DONE, AND SAID RATHER THAN IMPLIED:** no pixel is asserted (jsdom computes
no layout, so rule 39's 5/6/20 have no check here or anywhere), and **the running
product was not driven in a browser** — hard-won law 6's diff against the
prototype is this wave's gap.

**`2.240.0`.** No migration, no column, no money figure moves. Rollback is the
revert of these commits: the Activate button returns to committing on the click,
`RecapBox` and `commitBlocked` leave the kit unused by anything else, and the
thirteen-action census goes with them.
