## 2026-09-12 · `CR-094-BRC01` step 2 wave K — `ACC-S16`, writing to the customer from the account

**What was asked for**, from the blueprint's own commitment card: *"A clerk can
write to the customer from the account, and see what has already been sent."*
Step 1 lane 2's finding F11, verbatim: *"There is no way to write to the customer
from this screen. Seven icons and six buttons and not one sends a word."*
Drawing `R6`, pages 186–188, read as rendered images through
`10-scripts/pdf/pdf_render.py` because that PDF's text layer prints every digit
as `&`.

### THE JUDGMENT THAT DECIDED THE WHOLE WAVE, WITH ITS MEASUREMENT

**Nothing in this product sends anything, and the screen had to say so.**
`BR-NOT-013` is CONFIRMED (PO 2026-08-15): *"DELIVERY IS OUT OF THIS RELEASE …
No provider adapter exists or is coming on ANY channel, print included."*
**Measured rather than trusted** (hard-won law 1 — and the docstring that asserts
it is itself stale in the safe direction): `provider_seam` resolves the vendor
adapter as `apps.integrations.services.dispatch_outbound_batch`; that function
exists **nowhere** in `apps/integrations`, whose **11** occurrences across
`06-backend/` are **all tests monkeypatching it with `raising=False`**. Meanwhile
`apps/integrations` has grown to **14,722 lines** since the seam's docstring
called it *"three docstrings and no code"* — so the docstring's REASON is stale
and its CONCLUSION is exactly right.

**So the commit reads `Queue the message`**, the recap keeps the drawing's own
words *"It is queued, not sent"*, and every channel row carries `delivers`,
served from the same `channel_route` the dispatcher branches on. On this
deployment that is **false for email, text and post** and true only for the
customer portal (`BR-NOT-1031`). ⚠ **This is a BUILD to a signed rule, not a
value chosen for an open question** — no question was minted, because
`BR-NOT-013` already answers it.

### FOUR OF THE DRAWING'S FIVE KINDS ARE REFUSED HERE, BY NAME

A payment reminder and a disconnection notice are the collections LADDER's acts:
`BR-PAY-035` maps a reminder's tone onto a dunning TIER template and says
*"free-text tones do not exist"*; `BR-NOT-008` renders the disconnect class
whatever tone was picked. A ladder step composed on this dialog would carry no
tier and write no `NoticeHistory` row — the regulatory trail would hold a letter
no ladder knows about, which is the opposite of the drawing's own *"what a
customer was told has to be provable later"*. A bill copy is billing's reprint
and a balance statement is the statement path. **Each is OFFERED and refused
with the owner named**, `BR-SHL-025`'s shape, served from
`customer_events.message_kinds()` so one list governs both sides.

### A THIRTEENTH SOURCE KIND, AND FILING IT UNDER `account` WOULD HAVE COST REAL MONEY

`models.SOURCE_TYPES` gains **`message`**. The nearest existing kind is
`account`, and `account` carries the `BR-NOT-024` PRINT FLOOR — so a clerk
emailing *"I am looking into your balance and will call Friday"* would **also
have posted a letter**, every time, on a message whose whole point is that it is
quick. `message` gets no floor entry and is classified `NOT_A_DOCUMENT_KINDS` in
the floor test — the second edit `models.py` warns gets forgotten, made in the
same commit. **Proved by breaking it:** filing it under `account` turns the suite
red with `assert {'email', 'pdf_print'} == {'email'}`.

### THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY IS MINTED BY THE SCREEN, AND THAT NEEDED ITS OWN GUARD

There is no job row to key on — the occasion IS the composing — so the dialog
mints a UUID when it opens and a double-clicked *Queue the message* meets its own
row (CLAUDE.md rule 6). **The hazard a client-minted key brings is an id spent on
a DIFFERENT account**, which would dedupe the second message into the first and
tell the clerk it was queued while nothing was written. Refused by name;
the guard was proved red (`assert False is True`).

### NO SET-12 EVENT, DELIBERATELY

`account_message` joins `rule_catalog.WRITER_REACHED_CLASSES` as **the first
entry whose writer is a person**. A SET-12 rule lets a utility switch off a CLASS
of automatic message; a clerk pressing a button is not that. A rule that swallowed
it would leave the clerk believing they had written to somebody, and would put a
switch on the settings screen whose real effect is to break a button.

### THREE CONTROLS THE DRAWING SHOWS AND THIS WAVE DID NOT BUILD

Hard-won law 2 both ways: a control that does nothing is dead UI, and a refusal
that outlives its reason costs more. So none of the three is shipped disabled.
**Template** — there is ONE class for a clerk's own words and the other three the
drawing names have no wording; inventing the body of a customer-facing document
is what `CLASSES_WITHOUT_CATALOG` exists to refuse. **Attach the balance as a
statement** — `catalogs.LISTINGS` says of that class, in its own words, *"the
wording is ready; nothing produces a statement yet"*. **Save as a draft** —
nothing stores a draft, and `ACC-S16` commits to writing and to reading, not to
drafting. ⚠ **None of the three absences is explained on screen** (B14 rule 33:
rationale is ZERO words on screen); it is explained here and in the file.

### WHAT WAS REUSED RATHER THAN REBUILT — the PO's standing instruction

*"Do all changes based on actual code — also don't create duplicate code."*
**The history half added ZERO server code.** *What has already gone out* is
`GET /outbound` with `f.account_id` — notifications' own S8 queue list, which
already carries the capability row's search and filters, the ratified *failed and
bounced first* sort, `Resend`, `Requeue` and server pagination. The write goes
through `services.queue_document`, the one writer of `outbound_messages`, reached
by the seam `apps/customers/notifications_seam.py` that already existed; the form
uses the kit's own `FormModal` fields, so B14 rule 39's 5 / 6 / 20 anatomy is
inherited rather than re-measured; the eighth glyph reuses `MessageIcon`.

### THE EIGHTH GLYPH, AND WHY IT IS NOT A QUIET ADDITION

`BR-SHL-045` ruled SEVEN — against a proposal to REDUCE them to
two-plus-a-menu. It ruled on the PRESENTATION of the actions that existed, not
that no action could ever join them, and `ACC-S16` is a commitment card in the
blueprint's §12. The rail's `actions` prop is a `Record` over the ids, so the
eighth **did not compile** until the page wired it, and the case literally named
*"and no eighth"* went red and was amended with this reasoning rather than
loosened. **It is LIVE from its first commit** — the endpoint is mounted and the
write is served.

### TWO REDS THIS LANE DID NOT CAUSE, BOTH DATED

**`DEF-NOT-5120` (filed).** `test_def_210__every_seeded_class_has_a_catalogue_and_a_listing`
has failed on three template names since **2026-09-07**: `DEF-NOT-4416`
capitalised the seeder's `Statement · Email` and left the catalogue's
`Statement · email`. Proved not-mine by reading both names out of the tip's bytes
and re-running the file in a clean worktree at `bd1833183` — **3 failed, 31
passed**. Filed rather than fixed: `DEF-NOT-4416`'s own ruling says *"the
lowercase one is data"*, so which side is right is ambiguous, and
`13-change-process` §1 says an ambiguity is filed.

**The Meters tab red — ALREADY FILED BY A SIBLING AS `DEF-CUS-5124`.** This lane
allocated `DEF-CUS-5126` for it and **did not publish the row**: wave J had filed
the same finding minutes earlier, from the same commit `798d63028` and by the
same worktree method. The duplicate was removed from the working copy by a
BYTE-SPLICE, prefix proved byte-identical, never through a `csv` round-trip.
**The id is abandoned rather than reused**, which the register's own guard calls
legitimate.

### THE GATE SUITE, READ RATHER THAN GLANCED AT

`run_gates.py --changed`: **8 FAIL, 10 PASS**, and the runner's own ratchet says
**0 newly failing, 0 newly fixed, 18 unchanged**. None of the eight names a file
this wave touched.

### PROVED RED BEFORE TRUSTED GREEN — five guards, each quoted

`{'email','pdf_print'} == {'email'}` (the print floor) · `'queued' == 'sent'` (a
screen claiming delivery) · `assert False is True` (the cross-account id) ·
*"Unable to find … Waits in the queue"* (a channel row claiming it delivers) ·
`expected true to be false` (a channel with no address left tickable). **13
backend cases and 5 DOM cases, all green.** ⚠ `tsc` was run through the LOCAL
binary (5.5.4), not `npx`, for hard-won law 7's reason.

⚠ **THE INVISIBLE-CLASS TRAP CAUGHT THIS WAVE AND IT IS WORTH RECORDING:**
`text-muted` and `hover:text-fg` are not theme keys, so they compiled to
**nothing** — `tsc` passed, every DOM assertion passed, and the text would have
rendered at the default colour. `routeBUtilities.test.ts` named both, on the
listed file, which is exactly what skill §7.1 says that ledger is for.

⚠ **NOT DONE, AND SAID RATHER THAN IMPLIED:** the running product was **not
driven in a browser**, so hard-won law 6's diff against the prototype is this
wave's gap; no pixel is asserted anywhere; and the compose dialog's submit path
is covered by the server's 13 cases rather than by a DOM round trip.

**`2.241.0`.** One migration-free change: `SOURCE_TYPES` grows by a value and one
template class is seeded. No money figure moves and no ❄️ FROZEN figure is
touched. **Rollback is the revert of these commits** — the rail returns to seven
glyphs, `POST /accounts/{id}/communication` 404s, and the `account_message`
template stays seeded and unreachable, which is the state twenty-six other
classes were in before `CR-048`.

## 2026-09-13 — TWO PO RULINGS ON `CR-094`'s ACCOUNT SCREEN, AND A QUESTION ABOUT MALWARE SCANNING THAT IS NOT ONE

Both rulings arrived in reply to wave J's and wave I's reports of the previous
evening, and both are recorded here **before** the reply that answers them
(law 9) and in `03-customers/02-business-rules.md` as `BR-CUS-1051` and
`BR-CUS-1052` (law 10's table: a rule the PO states lands in the module's own
rules, not only here).

### 1 · THE EIGHT QUICK ACTIONS MOVE OVER THE ACCOUNT

**PO, verbatim: *"Yes move the eight quick actions over the account"*** — and,
in the same message, *"what are these 8 actions - and why they need to move"*,
which is a request for the list and the reason rather than a second question.

**The eight, read off `accountQuickActions.ts` at `b92c3defa`** (their
`route` destinations, with the screen each one owns today):

| # | the control a clerk presses | where it takes them today |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Move-out** | `MoveOutWizard` — six steps |
| 2 | **Move-in** | `MoveInWizard` — five steps |
| 3 | **Close out** | `CloseOutPage` |
| 4 | **Print bill** | billing's bill-document route |
| 5 | **Issue credit** | billing's fix-a-bill screen |
| 6 | **Change plan** | `ChangePlanWizard` — three steps |
| 7 | **Disconnect notice** | `DisconnectWizard` — five steps |
| 8 | **Payment plan** | `PaymentPlanWizard` |

**Three already open over the account** (Activate — built by wave J — plus
Record payment and Add note) and **two are held with their reason** (Adjust:
no adjustment writer exists in billing; Send statement: nothing renders a
statement). 3 + 8 + 2 = 13.

**Why they move, in the commitment's own words:** `ACC-S14` asks that a clerk
act *"without losing sight of the balance behind it"*, and finding `F12`
measured that **nine of the thirteen take the clerk off the account**. A clerk
pressing *Payment plan* is answering a question about arrears they are reading
on that screen; replacing the screen takes the arrears away at the moment they
are needed.

⚠ **THE RULING IS ABOUT THE CONTAINER, NOT THE FORM, AND WAVE J'S REASONING IS
NOT OVERTURNED — IT IS COMPLETED.** Wave J left the eight because each owns a
complete, tested, multi-step form with park-and-resume, about **7,300 lines**,
and re-typing them as dialogs is the duplicate code the PO's standing
instruction forbids. That was right. What it missed is that MOUNTING is not
COPYING: the existing wizard renders inside a dialog over the account, and
`accountQuickActions.ts` changes a destination from `route` to `form`. No form
is re-authored.

⚠ **IT OVERRIDES THE *estimate precedent* FOR THESE EIGHT AND FOR NOTHING
ELSE.** B14 rule 30 was DECLINED on 2026-08-30 so that the PO could answer
instances, and its test — *a handful of fields, one outcome* — points the other
way for a six-step move-out. **The PO answered the instance. No rule is minted;
rule 30 stays declined.** A lane meeting a different form asks the estimate
test again rather than citing this.

### 2 · A FILED DOCUMENT CAN BE REMOVED

**PO, verbatim: *"We should have this functionality"***, on wave I's report
that *"a clerk who files the wrong scan cannot take it back"*.

⚠ **THIS COLLIDES WITH A CONFIRMED RULE, SO THE SUPERSESSION IS STATED RATHER
THAN ASSUMED (law 13).** `BR-SHL-031` makes the legal class **write-once for
seven years** and `stored_documents` enforces it with a database trigger;
`NFR-35` says the same. **Neither is reversed by this ruling.** The control
WITHDRAWS the filing: the document leaves the account's list, cannot be opened
or counted there, and the withdrawal writes an audit row naming who and when —
while the stored object stays under its retention lock. The clerk's misfiled
scan stops being part of that customer's file, which is what was asked for, and
no signed retention promise is broken to deliver it. `BR-CUS-036`'s audit-locked
classes (system, contract) still refuse a withdrawal BY NAME, with the reason on
screen: a clerk may take back a scan they filed, never a contract the system
attached.

### 3 · MALWARE SCANNING — A QUESTION, AND WHY NO RULING IS RECORDED HERE

**PO: *"can you implment this? and how in tbale format?"*** — a request for
options, so nothing is ruled and nothing is built on it yet. The facts the
options were measured against, all read from the code rather than assumed:

* **`NFR-34` and `BR-SHL-031` both say *malware scan on every upload BEFORE
  acceptance*** — "pre-acceptance" is the signed wording, and it is what
  separates the options below.
* **There is no scanner and no seam for one.** Nothing in `document_store.py`
  or `document_storage.py` calls out to one.
* **There are SEVEN upload doors, not one** — `apps/tenancy/api.py`,
  `apps/customers/api.py`, `apps/integrations/api.py`, `apps/work/api.py`,
  `apps/work/sync.py`, `apps/payments/api.py`,
  `apps/payments/payment_import_api.py`. **So a scan bolted onto the Documents
  tab would leave six doors open**, which is the single most important fact in
  the choice: it belongs at the kernel boundary every door already calls.
* **Storage is S3 by default** (`DOCUMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND` defaults to
  `"aws_s3"`; the filesystem backend is tests and local dev only), and **a
  Celery worker exists** (`config/celery.py`, `celery_routes.py`,
  `apps/tenancy/tasks.py`), so both an in-line and a queued design are
  reachable without new infrastructure beyond the scanner itself.
* **Hard-won law 3 decides the failure mode**: the unsafe option must be the one
  you type, so a scanner that is unreachable REFUSES the upload rather than
  waving it through.

The options table as put to the PO is in the session reply; when they choose,
the choice lands here as a ruling and in `00-platform-shell/02-business-rules.md`
beside `BR-SHL-031`, because it is a shell capability and not a customers one.

## 2026-09-13 — FOUR MORE INSTRUCTIONS IN ONE EXCHANGE: THE ACCOUNT EDIT SURFACES, THE MALWARE SCANNER, AND THE TWO HELD ACTIONS

All four arrived within minutes of the `CR-094` status table being put to the PO.
Recorded here before the reply that answers them (law 9); the two that state a
rule are also in their module's own rules (law 10's table), as `BR-CUS-1053` and
`BR-SHL-253`.

### 1 · BUILD THE ACCOUNT EDIT SURFACES — `ACC-S1` + `ACC-S15`

**PO, verbatim: *"Build the account edit screen"***, and in the next message,
listing what to start: *"Correcting an account's details from the account …
Every group on the Overview carrying its own edit control"*. Recorded as
**`BR-CUS-1053`**.

**The measurement that prompted it:** `PATCH /accounts/{id}` has been mounted,
handled, audited and tested since August, and **`grep` finds no caller in the
whole front end** — `updateAccountNote` is the only account write a screen makes.
So a clerk cannot correct a misspelt name or a wrong telephone number from
anywhere in the product.

⚠ **THE SCOPE IS WHAT THE SERVER ACCEPTS, WHICH IS NARROWER THAN THE SCREEN
SUGGESTS, AND IT IS WRITTEN INTO THE RULE SO NO LANE HAS TO RE-DERIVE IT.** Seven
fields are writable; **eleven are refused by name with their own rule id**; and
**`unit` and `account_type` are skipped SILENTLY** — `update_account` does
`if field in ("unit", "account_type"): continue`, so a form offering either
returns success and changes nothing. That is `DEF-MET-4971`'s shape (a control
that validates, submits, toasts and writes nothing) on a money-adjacent record,
and it is a defect to file rather than a thing to design around.

⚠ **THE UNIT CORRECTION IS NOT FOLDED IN.** `OQ-CUS-1769` closed 2026-09-12 on
option (a) — `BR-CUS-1047`, a correction with a reason from a fixed list, a
supervisor's approval, effective today, never backdated — **and the code still
refuses it.** A ruling that reached the register and not the code is exactly what
step 0 exists to catch; it is named here so the next lane finds it rather than
discovering it as a stale comment.

### 2 · THE MALWARE SCANNER — OPTION A, EXECUTE

**PO, verbatim: *"please execute this"***, choosing from four options put to them
in plain English. Recorded as **`BR-SHL-253`**.

**Nothing about the requirement changed** — `BR-SHL-031` and `NFR-34` have said
*scan before acceptance* since 2026-08-08 and it has been unbuilt for thirty-six
days. What the PO ruled is the MECHANISM: a scanner running beside the
application, given the bytes before they are stored.

**Why the other three were rejected, in their own terms:** a scanning VENDOR
sends a utility's identity documents outside our boundary; **storage-side
scanning** (GuardDuty, Defender) and **accept-then-quarantine** both let the file
exist before the verdict, which the signed wording does not allow. Those two
remain the honest fallbacks if the in-line scan ever proves too slow, and
adopting one would be a change to the signed wording rather than an
implementation detail.

⚠ **IT GOES AT THE KERNEL BOUNDARY BECAUSE THERE ARE SEVEN UPLOAD DOORS**, listed
in the rule. A scan on the account-documents screen alone would leave six open
and would look, to every check this repo has, exactly like a scan that happened.
**It fails closed** (hard-won law 3): an unreachable, slow or stale scanner
refuses the upload rather than accepting unscanned bytes.

### 3 · START *Adjust* AND *Send statement* — AND BOTH ARE LARGER THAN A CONTROL

**PO, verbatim: *"start these one also"***, listing both alongside the two above.
No rule is minted for either: the blueprint already commits to both controls
(`R4`'s `ACC-Q01` and `ACC-Q07`) and what was missing is the capability beneath
them. Two findings from reading the code before dispatching, because both change
what the waves are:

* **AN `adjustments` TABLE ALREADY EXISTS** — `apps/billing/models.py:1241`,
  `db_table = "adjustments"`, indexed by account and by invoice — **and nothing
  writes it.** `grep "Adjustment.objects.create"` over the whole backend returns
  one hit and it is a COMMENT in the portal seam saying so. There is no endpoint.
  So *Adjust* is the deposit pattern again: a structure finished and standing
  behind no door. ⚠ **It is a 🔒 money path** — hard rule 4 (an issued invoice
  never changes; corrections are new rows), hard rule 5 (only the ledger posting
  service writes journal lines), hard rule 7 (audit) — and billing already owns a
  full corrections capability (`BR-BIL-004`/`014`/`041`–`048`: reason → scope →
  impact preview → approval → staged execution). **Whether an account adjustment
  is a new thing or a shape of that correction flow is the first question the
  wave answers, from the code, not from the drawing.**
* **A `statement` TEMPLATE CLASS ALREADY EXISTS** —
  `apps/notifications/catalogs.py:268`, and `S91`–`S93` are named there as
  *bill residential / bill commercial / statement*, owned by BILLING. What is not
  established is whether anything GATHERS a period's activity and renders one.
  **The wave establishes that before it designs anything**, because "nothing
  renders a statement" was this session's own claim and the adjustments table
  above shows how that kind of claim goes wrong.

**Neither wave may guess a money rule.** Where the arithmetic or the GL treatment
is unruled, the lane builds to the boundary, mints the question and stubs it with
the id in the code — the prime directive, unchanged.

## 2026-09-13 · `CR-094-BRC01` wave M — **SEND STATEMENT: THE MEASUREMENT, BEFORE ANY DESIGN**

**The wave was briefed on a sentence this session wrote itself** — *"nothing
renders a statement"* — and the brief said to establish it rather than repeat it,
because the same session had already said nothing writes an adjustment and an
`adjustments` table turned out to have existed all along. So the first act was a
measurement of the three parts a statement needs, and **it came back the opposite
way round from the briefing.**

### (a) A statement TEMPLATE — **EXISTS, twice, and one of the two has no wording**

* **`email_statement` is SEEDED AND LIVE** — `apps/notifications/seed_templates.py:1314`,
  with a real subject (*"Your {utility_name} statement, {period_start} to
  {period_end}"*) and a real body that already carries A19 rule 1's disclaimer
  **verbatim**: *"This is a summary of what has happened on your account. It is
  not a bill, and nothing is due from this statement."* Nobody had to write that
  sentence; it has been in the repo and in eleven catalogues' reach the whole time.
* **`statement` (the PRINTED one) is a declared class with NO BODY ANYWHERE.**
  `apps/notifications/catalogs.py:268` declares the class, its channel (`print`)
  and its ten tokens, and `mandatory_content=("nothing is due",)`. But
  `seed_templates.py:2000` **excludes** `statement` from the notifications
  seeder, on the ground that *"Bills and statements are BILLING's registry (B2
  r10 #4) and are seeded by `apps.billing.services.seed_bill_templates`"* — and
  that name resolves (`billing/services.py:84`) to
  `templates_service.seed_platform_default`, which seeds **the bill layout** and
  plants no statement body at all. **So the printed statement is a class with a
  token palette, a mandatory sentence, an owner named in two places, and no
  wording on any deployment.** That is `DEF-123`'s shape exactly — the defect
  where `resolve_for` refused for every tenant because the only rows that ever
  existed were ones the tests created — one document to the left.

### (b) Something that GATHERS a period's activity — **EXISTS, and has since 2026-08-11**

`apps.ledger.reporting.account_ledger(account_id, start=, end=)` — dated, and it
returns the statement **row for row**: `opening_balance`, then per row
`entry_date` / `type` / `reference` / `description` / `charge` / `payment` /
`running_balance`, then `totals.charges`, `totals.payments`,
`totals.closing_balance`. Put A19 §1's statement definition beside it — *"a
running ledger over a date range — date / description / reference / charges /
payments / balance. No rates, no meter reads, no due date"* — and the two are the
same list in the same order. It is the read behind `S59`, it is live, and it was
dated with `git log -S "def account_ledger"`: **commit `dea0d6f0b`, 2026-08-11.**

### (c) Something that RENDERS and DELIVERS — **EXISTS**

`apps/notifications/services.queue_document` is the only writer of
`outbound_messages` (B1), `rendering.py` renders, and
`payments/receipts.py::queue_receipt_for_recorded_payment` is a working
precedent for a non-bill document being built, queued on three channels and
reported on. **Nothing SENDS** — no provider is connected on email, text or post
and none is this release (PO, 15 August 2026) — so the word is **Queued**.

### THE VERDICT, AND IT CHANGES WHAT THE WAVE IS

**All three parts exist. Not one of them is joined to the next.** Nobody calls
(b), fills (a)'s tokens with it, and hands it to (c). This wave is therefore
**WIRING, not building** — hard-won law 2, *built is not wired*, in its purest
form, and the reason no check caught it is that each of the three parts is
correct, tested and live **on its own**.

### THE REFUSAL'S OWN REASON IS STALE, AND IT IS A LAW-1 MISS

`accountRailReadiness.ts` holds the sentence that kept this control dark:

> *"`apps/billing/documents.py` renders INVOICES and nothing else, and **the
> account-ledger derived view a statement would read does not exist**."*

**The second half has been false since 2026-08-11** — four days before that
comment's own module was written. It is hard-won law 1: a comment claiming a
gap, which nothing re-checks, outliving the gap. **The first half is TRUE and
stays true**, and so does the comment's warning that
`GET /reports/customer-statement` is not this document.

### WHY `GET /reports/customer-statement` (CR-060 C16) CANNOT SERVE THIS

It was read end to end (`customers/api.py:1331`, `customers/selectors.py:2527`)
before anything was designed, because the standing instruction is not to build a
second copy of something. **It is a different document and it is not close.** It
is *one customer, their accounts, each balance, and a total across them* —
keyed on a CUSTOMER, and `Send statement` is on an ACCOUNT. Set its payload
against the ten tokens the `statement` class declares: it supplies a per-account
closing balance and **none** of `period_start`, `period_end`, `opening_balance`,
`ledger_date`, `description`, `reference`, `charges`, `payments`,
`running_balance`. It takes **no date range at all** — the one thing A19 says a
statement is over. It has no ledger lines, no disclaimer and no queue write.
**Pointing ✉ at it would ship a button that produces the wrong document, which
is worse than one that refuses** — and that is not a fresh conclusion either:
`accountRailReadiness.ts` had already reasoned it out and written it down. The
measurement confirms it rather than overturning it.

**What this wave reuses rather than rebuilds:** `account_ledger` for every
figure (it recomputes no money — hard rule 2 and B4 are untouched), the seeded
`email_statement` wording, `queue_document` for the queue row and its
idempotency, and `receipts.py`'s problem/outcome reporting shape.

**`GET /reports/customer-statement` is left exactly as it is.** It is a good
report, it has a screen, and nothing here changes it.

## 2026-09-13 — START THE CUSTOMER EDIT: THE GAP BEHIND THE GAP

**PO, verbatim: *"Start the customer edit one also - we will need this"***, in reply
to being told — as a correction to this session's own earlier wording — that the
account edit screen would NOT fix a misspelt name or a wrong telephone number,
because those are the CUSTOMER's fields and **`GET /customers/{id}` is read-only
with no PATCH anywhere in the product.** Recorded as **`BR-CUS-1054`**.

**Why it is not a second copy of the account edit:** the two touch different
tables and only one of them is PII. Measured before dispatching:

* `customers` holds `display_name`, `kind`, `customer_no`, `external_ref`,
  `date_of_birth`, and **`ssn`, `driving_licence`, `phone` and `tax_id` as
  `EncryptedTextField`s, each with a `_bidx` blind-index column beside it**.
* `Contact` holds the `email` (citext).
* `customers.addresses` `kind='mailing'` is hard rule 8's named exception — the
  only address a customer owns, and where the bill goes.

⚠ **THE FAILURE THIS WAVE IS MOST LIKELY TO SHIP IS A STALE BLIND INDEX.** Write a
corrected phone without recomputing `phone_bidx` and the value is right while
search stops finding the customer by it — **and every test that reads the field
back passes**, because the field IS correct. It is hard rule 8's closing lesson in
another costume: an absence is invisible to every check this repo has.

⚠ **AND THE PORTAL SIGN-IN IS A SEPARATE COLUMN.** `apps/portal` holds its own
`email` and it **is the sign-in identifier, unique per tenant**. Correcting a
contact email may not re-point a credential — it is another module's table
(B2 §2), and doing it silently either locks a customer out or hands their account
to a new address. **Whether the two should follow each other is unruled**; the
wave states the absence and it returns to the PO as a question rather than being
chosen by a lane.

**Issued bills do not restate.** A bill's customer name is locked into its
snapshot at issue (hard rule 4), so a correction changes the next bill and
nothing already sent — which is the sentence the screen needs to say, in six
words or fewer (B14 rule 33).

## 2026-09-13 — `CR-094-BRC01` WAVE L: THE EIGHT QUICK ACTIONS MOVE OVER THE ACCOUNT, MOUNTED AND NOT RE-TYPED

Builds `BR-CUS-1051` (PO 2026-09-13, verbatim: ***"Yes move the eight quick
actions over the account"***). The ruling and its reasoning were written down
the same morning, above; this row records **how it was built and the judgments
the ruling did not settle**, which is what step W asks for.

### 1 · WHAT A CLERK CAN DO NOW, AND THE FIGURE

**Eleven of the thirteen quick actions on an account now open OVER it.** Before
this wave it was three — Activate, Record payment, Add note — and **nine of the
thirteen replaced the screen the clerk was reading** (finding `F12`). The eight
that moved are Move-out, Move-in, Close out, Print bill, Issue credit, Change
plan, Disconnect notice and Payment plan. The two that did not are `Adjust` and
`Send statement`, which stay refused with their reason (`BR-SHL-025`), because a
dialog over a control that cannot act opens onto nothing.

**Nothing was re-typed.** The eight own **8,838 lines** between them, counted
rather than estimated — `MoveInWizard` 1,827 · `DisconnectWizard` 1,723 ·
`MoveOutWizard` 1,546 · `PaymentPlanWizard` 913 · `ChangePlanWizard` 895 ·
`FixABillTab` 759 · `BillDocumentPage` 740 · `CloseOutPage` 435. (`BR-CUS-1051`
says *"about 7,300"*; that was wave J's estimate of the six wizards and this is
the measured total of all eight. The rule is not amended — an estimate and a
measurement disagreeing by 20% is not a contradiction, and the figure the rule
uses is doing rhetorical work rather than arithmetic.) **Not one field, step,
schema or endpoint call was copied.** The whole of this wave's new code is
**one 290-line container**, two optional props on the shared dialog shell, a
three-line fallback in one wizard, and the route table.

### 2 · THE JUDGMENT THE RULING LEFT TO US: **THE CONTAINER IS A ROUTE**

The ruling says *over the account*. It does not say how, and the obvious answer —
a `useState` flag on `AccountDetailPage` that renders the wizard in a dialog —
**would have broken three things and needed eight screens edited to fix them.**
So the eight are **CHILD ROUTES of `/accounts/:accountId`**, and
`AccountDetailPage` renders whichever one the URL names through an `<Outlet/>`
inside the shared `ModalShell`. Four properties come out of that for free:

| what a state-flag dialog would have cost | what the nesting keeps |
|---|---|
| `useParams().accountId` | five of the eight read their subject that way; **none needed a prop** |
| `?step=` on a reload | three park a half-finished job there — **park-and-resume is untouched** |
| the exit | every one of the eight already leaves by `navigate(accountDetailPath(accountId))`, which **un-matches the child and closes the dialog**; no exit was rewired |
| the address | every path is the string it already was — a nesting, not a re-addressing |

⚠ **AND IT IS WHY THIS DOES NOT COLLIDE WITH THE *estimate precedent*.** The
skill's §5 table reserves *"needs an address a person can send"*, *"must survive
a refresh"* and *"more than one step"* for a SCREEN rather than a modal. **A
ROUTED dialog has all three.** B14 rule 30 stays declined and nothing here is a
rule: a lane meeting a different form asks the estimate test again.

### 3 · THREE OF THE EIGHT WERE NEVER ACCOUNT-SCOPED, AND KEEP THEIR OWN DOOR

`Print bill`, `Issue credit` and `Disconnect notice` pointed at screens that live
somewhere else in the product. Each **gains a second, account-scoped address and
keeps its first**, which is the `/move-ins/new` precedent read again: two routes,
one screen, one id, and no debt count moves.

| control | its own address, untouched | the new one |
|---|---|---|
| Print bill | `/billing/bills/{id}/document` | `/accounts/{id}/bills/{invoiceId}/document` |
| Issue credit | `/billing/fix?bill={id}` | `/accounts/{id}/issue-credit?bill={id}` |
| Disconnect notice | `/disconnects/new?account={id}` | `/accounts/{id}/disconnect` |

**`Print bill` is the only one of the eight whose segment carries a parameter**,
because it is the only one whose subject is a BILL: `BillDocumentPage` reads
`useParams().invoiceId` and there is nothing account-shaped for it to read.
WHICH bill is still the rail's derivation (the newest ISSUED one) and did not
move. **`Issue credit` mounts the TAB and not `BillsListPage`** — a clerk who
pressed *Issue credit* on one account did not ask for every bill in the utility.

### 4 · THE ONE SCREEN THAT NEEDED A LINE CHANGED, AND WHY

`DisconnectWizard` took its subject from `?account=` and from nothing else.
Mounted at `/accounts/{id}/disconnect` it would have opened **the account finder,
over the very account it was launched from** — a search for something the URL
already names. It now falls back to `useParams().accountId`.
`/disconnects/new` and `/disconnects/new?account=` behave exactly as before.

### 5 · THE DIALOG HEAD IS BARE, AND THAT IS A B14 RULE 32 DECISION

**Seven of the eight draw their own `PageHeader`** — kicker, 32px title (rule
40), roll-up sentence, and a back arrow that already points at this account. A
dialog head carrying the action's name as well is **two headings on one surface**
and spends the description budget rule 32 caps at one sentence per section. So
`ModalShell` gained `titleHidden`: the ✕ alone, with the action's name as the
dialog's `aria-label`, so a screen reader is handed the same words either way.

**`Issue credit` is the exception and it is DECLARED rather than judged per
screen.** `FixABillTab` is a TAB — `BillsListPage` draws the head at its own
address — so there the dialog supplies the title, or the surface has no heading
at all. The flag is `ownsItsHeading` on the overlay row, and **a test reads each
source file and fails when the flag stops being true of it**: a claim about
another file that nothing re-checks is this repo's own most-repeated lesson.

`ModalShell` also gained `size="wide"` (`w-[min(1120px,100%)]!`). **Both props
are optional and absent means exactly what it always did**, so every existing
caller renders byte-for-byte as before.

### 6 · WHAT THIS WAVE DID **NOT** DO

* **The two held actions were not swept in.** The ruling names eight.
* **No wizard's post-commit navigation was changed.** `DisconnectWizard` still
  finishes at the Disconnects tab and `MoveOutWizard` still parks to the parked
  list; that is each screen's own contract **at both doors**, and changing it
  here would change it at the other door for callers who never asked.
* **Documents, the communication section and the account-edit surfaces**
  (`ACC-S1`/`ACC-S15`) are other work and were not touched.

### 7 · HOW IT WAS PROVED — TEN SABOTAGES, TEN REDS

Step 2d, and each guard was shown to fail on the defect it was written for
**through the harness that runs it** (`npx vitest run`, not `__main__`), before
being trusted green:

| what was broken | what went red |
|---|---|
| a child route deleted from `App.tsx` | *the account route owns children, and they are exactly the eight overlays* |
| a child pointed at the wrong screen (`issue-credit` → `BillsListPage`) | *each child opens the screen the overlay table names, BY COMPONENT* |
| an address re-spelled (`move-out` → `moveout`) | *does not re-spell the five addresses the product already had*, plus 6 more |
| the other door removed (`/disconnects/new` → the wrong screen) | *the disconnect wizard is still at /disconnects/new* |
| the dialog made to open unasked | *renders nothing at all on the bare account* |
| a half-resolved `:invoiceId` link built instead of thrown | *throws rather than putting :invoiceId in the URL bar* |
| `ownsItsHeading` flipped on `CloseOutPage` | *says a screen draws its own PageHeader only where it does* |
| `size="wide"` dropped | *is WIDE — a six-step wizard is not a 560px card* |
| the title hidden on the screen that has none | *draws a visible title for the one screen that has no heading of its own* |
| an overlay left declared and unreached | *every mounted action names an overlay the container actually declares* |

**42 cases across the two files, all green afterwards.** The container cases
mount a STUB child rather than the real wizards on purpose: what is under test
is **what the container hands its screen** — the path param, the query, the host
still rendering — and each wizard's own suite already owns its behaviour at its
own address.

### 8 · A RED THIS WAVE DID NOT CAUSE, DATED

`routing/screenIds.test.tsx` is red and was **before this wave started**:
`DEF-SHL-5116`, filed 2026-09-12, *"the screen-id map is five routes behind the
router"*, oldest missing row `19e446875` of **2026-09-06**. The five it is
missing are `/runbooks`, `/premises/units/new`, `/complaints/new`,
`/services/new` and `/work/parts/import`. **This wave added eight rows to that
map and the failure diff is still exactly those five** — nothing was added to
the pile and nothing of ours is in it.

## 2026-09-13 — `BR-SHL-253` BUILT: THE MALWARE SCAN IS ON THE WIRE, AND FIVE JUDGMENTS THE RULING DID NOT DECIDE

The PO ruled the MECHANISM on 2026-09-13 (*"please execute this"*, option A of
four). Everything below is what building it required deciding, recorded with
its worked figure so the next lane does not re-derive it — and so that what was
NOT put to the PO is visible.

### 1 · IT IS MIDDLEWARE, NOT A CALL IN SEVEN PLACES

**Measured first, then decided.** `grep -rln "request.FILES\|multipart"
06-backend/apps` returns **seven modules** and the same seven the rule names:
`tenancy/api.py`, `customers/api.py`, `integrations/api.py`, `work/api.py`,
`work/sync.py`, `payments/api.py`, `payments/payment_import_api.py`.

Seven call sites is seven chances to forget and an eighth door next month with
no chance at all. `core/malware_scan.MalwareScanMiddleware` reads every part of
every `multipart/…` POST, PUT or PATCH before any view is entered, so **six of
the seven doors are covered without knowing the module exists.**

**The seventh is called by hand and that is unavoidable.**
`integrations/api.py::_file_bytes` accepts a RAW REQUEST BODY as well as a
multipart part, and a raw body never populates `request.FILES`. It calls
`require_clean()` at the one line where those bytes come into existence. The
test `test_the_one_raw_body_door_scans_by_hand` reads that function's source and
fails if the call leaves it; `test_no_eighth_upload_door_appears_without_being_considered`
fails when the inventory of seven moves at all.

### 2 · `document_store.store()` IS **NOT** THE BOUNDARY

The obvious place looked like the store — it is where bytes are accepted. **It
is the wrong place**, and the figure says why: `document_models.py` already
models a large tenant at **532,000 stored documents**, nearly all of them bills
this product RENDERED. `NFR-34` says *every upload*, and a bill we typeset
ourselves is not one. Scanning generated documents would cost hours per bill run
to answer a question nobody asked. The wire sees uploads and nothing else, which
is exactly the rule's scope.

### 3 · THE FRESHNESS CEILING IS **72 HOURS**, AND IT IS A REFUSAL

A reachable scanner running on an old signature database answers *OK* to
everything it has never heard of — hard-won law 7's *structurally incapable of
failing*, wearing a green tick. So the adapter reads clamd's own `zVERSION`
reply (`ClamAV 1.0.7/27456/Fri Sep 12 09:21:33 2026` — engine, database
revision, build date) and refuses the upload when the database is too old.

**72 hours, and the arithmetic is freshclam's own default of 24 checks a day:**
72 hours is **three consecutive days of every check failing**. Shorter and one
missed update refuses a customer's document; longer and a scanner nobody is
feeding survives a week unnoticed. `MALWARE_SIGNATURE_MAX_AGE_HOURS` moves it.

**A version reply with NO date is treated as stale, not as fresh.** The safe
reading of *"I cannot tell you when I last learned anything"* is *"too long
ago"*. This is not hypothetical — a `clamd` with no `.cvd` loaded answers
exactly `ClamAV 1.5.3`, which is what the proof run against a real daemon
showed.

### 4 · THE CATALOG HAS NO MALWARE CODE, SO NONE WAS INVENTED

B12 §3's code set is AUTH/VAL/BIZ/SYS and `ApiError` refuses anything outside it
by construction (G1: *"no endpoint invents a code"*). So:

* an infected file is **`VAL-002`, 422** — the content is not acceptable;
* an unreachable, timing-out, stale or unparseable scanner is **`SYS-PROVIDER`,
  503** — *we cannot check this right now*, which is a different sentence and a
  different HTTP contract from *your file is bad*.

**A catalog gap is REPORTED rather than filled**, the same posture `core/errors.py`
already takes for the 413/415 transport rows. A `VAL-MALWARE` code would be a PR
to B12 §3.

### 5 · THE TEST DOUBLE IS GATED BY A SETTING, NOT BY `DEBUG` — AND THE FIRST DRAFT WAS WRONG

`PatternScanner` detects the EICAR test string and nothing else, so the suite's
infected cases are real refusals rather than a mock agreeing with itself. It
must never reach a customer.

**The first draft gated it on `DEBUG` and that was wrong in a way worth
recording: `config/settings/test.py` runs with `DEBUG` False**, so the gate
locked the suite out of its own double while never asking the question that
matters — *did a person type the second key?* It is now
`MALWARE_SCANNER_ALLOW_TEST_DOUBLE`, False in `base.py`, True only in `local.py`
and `test.py`, and **never read from the environment**, so no deployment can
switch the scanner off by editing a `.env`. That is the same two-key shape
`DOCUMENT_STORAGE_ALLOW_FILESYSTEM` uses eight lines above it in the same file.

### 6 · WHAT A 10 MB SCAN ACTUALLY COSTS — MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED

`10-scripts/br_shl_253_clamav_proof.py`, against a real `clamd` 1.5.3 over TCP
INSTREAM, five runs on a 10,485,760-byte file:

| run | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | median |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ms | 350.5 | 463.2 | 331.3 | 129.5 | 74.7 | **331.3** |

⚠ **THAT FIGURE IS A FLOOR AND THE REASON IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED.** This
container's egress proxy refuses `database.clamav.net`, so `freshclam` could not
fetch `daily.cvd` and the daemon was loaded with **ONE hand-written EICAR
signature** instead of ClamAV's full set. A production scanner matches against
millions of signatures and will be slower. The measurement proves the TRANSPORT
and the framing cost, not the matching cost, and it is quoted that way
everywhere it appears. A 10 MB upload already spends longer than this crossing
the network.

### 7 · A CHECK OF MINE THAT COULD NOT FAIL, FOUND BY BREAKING IT (law 7)

Three guards were broken and each failure quoted:

| what was broken | what went red |
|---|---|
| the `part.seek(0)` rewind removed | `assert b'' == b'%PDF-1.7\np...ve-the-scan\n'` |
| the middleware unregistered from `MIDDLEWARE` | `assert 'core.malware_scan.MalwareScanMiddleware' in [...5 others]` |
| `_read_reply` reduced to a single `recv` | **31 passed — GREEN** |

**The third one is the finding.** `test_a_reply_split_across_two_tcp_segments_is_still_infected`
exists because a reply read in one `recv` can arrive truncated, and
`"stream: Eicar-Test-Signature FO"` does not contain `FOUND` — an infected file
becomes a clean one. **The test could not fail**, because two `sendall` calls
back to back are coalesced by the kernel into ONE segment and the client gets
the whole reply regardless. The fake now waits **250 ms** between the two
chunks, and the same sabotage turns the verdict into
`upload.refusal.scanner_unavailable`, which is the failure the test is for.

**The general shape, which is law 7's habit (2) — *ask what would make this
check pass wrongly*:** a test that stages a race by doing two things quickly is
not staging a race.

### 8 · TWO DOCSTRINGS THAT CLAIMED AN ABSENCE NOW FILLED

Hard-won law 1 runs in both directions. `apps/tenancy/logo.py` has said since
2026-08-11 that *"there is no image re-encode and no malware scan —
BR-SHL-031's scanner seam does not exist yet"*, and
`apps/customers/account_documents.py` quoted it on 2026-09-12 and added *"and it
is still true"*. **Both were right when written and both stopped being right the
day this landed.** They are corrected in the same commit as the change that made
them wrong, rather than left for the next lane to build around — which is the
same discipline B14's rule-count line has now failed at six times.

### 9 · THE REGRESSION WALK, AND THE TWO ASSERTIONS THIS WAVE REALLY DID BREAK

**75 files, 1,340 cases: 1,289 pass, 5 fail, and every one of the five was RED
BEFORE THIS WAVE.** That last clause is measured rather than remembered — a
throwaway `git worktree` at `feed3007f`, the commit before this wave's first, with

THE WIZARD — and scoped to the dialog they are STRONGER than they were, because

and *"no unit picker"* halves stay unscoped on purpose: *"nowhere on this screen
is there a second way to choose the account"* is a claim about the whole document,
and narrowing it would quietly stop checking the thing it was written for.

**A third case joins them and it CLICKS**, which is the nearest this suite gets
to hard-won law 6: start on the account, press *Move-out*, and assert the whole
chain — the button on S21, the URL, the real route table, the dialog, the
wizard's own H1, and the account STILL RENDERED behind it. A case that navigates
straight to the child address proves the route and not the control; one that
mounts the container over a stub proves the container and not the page.

## 2026-09-13 — THE CUSTOMER EDIT, BUILT: WHAT MOVED, WHAT DID NOT, AND THE ONE FAILURE IT WAS WRITTEN TO AVOID

`BR-CUS-1054` is built. PO, verbatim: ***"Start the customer edit one also - we will
need this"***. Wave `CR-094-BRC01` R, version **2.247.0**.

**WHAT A CLERK CAN DO NOW THAT THEY COULD NOT DO YESTERDAY.** Open the customers list,
press the pencil on somebody's row, and correct their name, the number the old system
knew them by, their date of birth, their telephone number and their email address. Until
today none of those could be changed anywhere in the product: `GET /customers/{id}` was
read-only and there was no PATCH on any door. The account edit screen does not reach them
— those are the account's columns, and a person's name is not one of them.

**THE FAILURE THIS WAVE WAS MOST LIKELY TO SHIP, AND HOW IT WAS PROVED AWAY.** Four of
these columns are encrypted, and beside each one sits a separate search token that is the
only way the row can be found by that value. Write a corrected telephone number without
rebuilding that token and the number on the record is right while the search box stops
finding the customer by it — and **every test that reads the field back passes**, because
the field IS correct. So nothing in this file writes one of those columns directly: it
calls the helper that already existed for exactly this (`identity_match.set_identifier`),
which writes the value and its token in one act. **The test does not read the number
back; it SEARCHES for it.** Corrected `512-555-0142` to `512-555-0199`, then ran the
clerk's own search: the new number finds her, the old one finds nobody.

**WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT MOVE, EACH WITH ITS REASON.**

* **The portal sign-in.** A customer signs in to the online portal with an email address
  held in another module's table, unique per utility. Correcting the billing email does
  not touch it. Whether it SHOULD follow is genuinely unruled and both answers do harm,
  so it is `OQ-CUS-12350` and the screen says *"Portal sign-in does not move."* out loud.
* **Bills already sent.** A bill locks the customer's name into its own snapshot when it
  is issued (hard rule 4), so a correction changes the next bill and nothing already
  posted. The dialog says so in five words.
* **The person-or-company flag.** Refused by name. Flipping it would strand every piece
  of identity already on file in a column the matching rules for the new kind never read
  — the record would look corrected and quietly stop recognising a returning customer,
  which is what carries a **$150.00** deposit across. `OQ-CUS-12351`.
* **The customer number.** Refused: it is allocated from the utility's own series inside
  the transaction that creates the row, and it is printed on letters already sent.
* **The mailing address.** Refused here, and see the measured gap below.

**A JUDGMENT THIS LANE MADE RATHER THAN ASKED ABOUT (law 13).** The audit trail masks the
three government identifiers — a Social Security number reaches `audit_log` as
`•••••6789` — because `BR-CUS-092(c)` says the full value never enters an audit blob. It
does **not** mask the telephone number, and that is deliberate: a phone is not one of the
two identifiers that rule names, the product already shows it in full on the customers
list and searches on it, and masking it only in the audit would leave the one record that
exists to answer *"what was the old number"* unable to answer it — on the single most
common correction this door will ever take.

**A GAP MEASURED ON THE WAY PAST, RECORDED RATHER THAN CLOSED.** `contacts` and
`addresses` are created when an account is opened and are thereafter written by **one
caller in the whole product: the customer PORTAL**. No clerk door has ever been able to
change a contact or a mailing address. This wave opens the first clerk door onto a
contact and it moves the EMAIL only; the telephone number on the contact row and the six
parts of the mailing address are untouched, and the mailing address carries the
returned-post clearing rule (`BR-CWP-086`) with it. That is its own wave, not a line of
code on the way past. The account-edit lane running beside this one independently
measured the same absence and put *"The mailing address is not editable yet."* on its
own screen.

**ONE HOLD EXPIRES WITH THIS COMMIT AND IT IS ANOTHER LANE'S FILE TO RELEASE.**
`AccountPanelEdits.tsx` (in flight beside this wave) refuses its *Edit customer* pencil
with *"Customer details are not editable yet."* and names `BR-CUS-1054` in a comment as
the wave that will make that false. It is false as of this commit. That lane owns the
file and its expiry test, so it is told rather than edited from here — which is hard-won
law 2's own instruction: when you land a screen, grep for the control that was holding
it.

**WHAT WAS REUSED RATHER THAN INVENTED:** `identity_match.set_identifier` (the
ciphertext and its search token, together), `portal_self_service`'s reach rule for an
email (one save touches every account the customer holds, because the contact row hangs
off the account), `service_request_service`'s masking-at-the-boundary shape for the
audit, `update_account`'s refused-field shape, and the shared form kit's dialog. No new
table, no migration, no money figure.

### 10 · THE GATES, AND A CROSS-LANE FACT THE NEXT AGENT NEEDS

**Seven gates were run BY NAME rather than as the 123-gate suite** — that suite
runs the golden pytest suite and takes 40+ minutes on a box carrying eight
lanes — **and each was run twice: once in the shared tree, once in a private
`git worktree` at the pinned tip.** The shared tree holds four other lanes'
uncommitted work, so a gate run there measures them as much as us, and the
difference between the two runs is the whole answer to *"is this one mine?"*.

`G31` PASSES at the clean tip (0 undeclared classes) — the four it reports in the
shared tree are a sibling's. `G13`, `G27`, `G07` and `G17` each fail on files and
ids this wave never touched. `G15` fails with **the identical 292 values at
`feed3007f`**, before this wave began.

⚠ **`G29` IS THE ONE THIS WAVE MOVED, AND IT WENT RED FIRST.** It read PASS at
131 screens / 142 routes before this wave, and this wave's three new addresses
took it to 134 / 145 — the rise it exists to catch. `screen_id_baseline.txt` now
carries the block explaining it: three routes, **no new screen and no new id**,
each row carrying the ids of the screen it MOUNTS (the `/move-ins/new`
precedent), and `screens_without_a1` rising by **two, not three**, because A1
numbers neither the rendered bill document nor the disconnect wizard at their
EXISTING addresses either — a second address cannot be where an A1 id is
invented.

⚠ **CORRECTED THE SAME HOUR — THE PARAGRAPH BELOW SAID THOSE TWO ROWS *"NEED
RE-FILING"* AND THAT WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. DO NOT ACT ON IT.** Both
authors carried their own finding forward within minutes, and the two ids are
**not free to reuse**:

* **The printed-statement finding was RE-FILED BY ITS OWN AUTHOR as
  `DEF-BIL-5133`**, committed `2544d531f` at 04:25 — eighteen minutes after the
  lost row was last seen — and `06-backend/apps/billing/statement.py` cites that
  number in its own docstring. **Filing it again would publish a duplicate of a
  row that is already on the branch.**
* **The `external_ref` finding is CLOSED BY THE WORK OF THE LANE THAT FILED IT.**
  `customers.external_ref` could be set at create and at import and nowhere
  else; `BR-CUS-1054` landed the service at `64e6e40ac` (04:18) and the screen at
  `1f13d7102` (04:31), so an admin edits it on `CustomerEditDialog.tsx` today
  through `customer_edit.update_customer`. ⚠ **Only that author can say whether
  the clause this lane never saw — the row's title was read from a 130-character
  diff fragment — was the same gap.**
* ⚠ **AND THE TWO NUMBERS ARE TAKEN.** `allocate.py defect --verify 5129` and
  `--verify 5130` both answer *"TAKEN — a sibling pushed it"*: they are held on
  ANOTHER BRANCH's register, because the allocator asks every remote ref and not
  only ours. **Re-using either would publish one id meaning two things on two
  branches**, which is the collision `allocate.py` exists to prevent.

**The lesson survives the correction and is the only part of the paragraph below
that was right:** a row that is not pushed is a row any lane can erase, and
`file_defect.py` appending it is only half the job. What saved both findings was
their authors pushing within twenty minutes, not anything this lane did.

⚠ **THE ORIGINAL PARAGRAPH, KEPT SO THE CORRECTION CAN BE CHECKED RATHER THAN
TAKEN ON TRUST — SUPERSEDED, DO NOT FOLLOW:**

⚠ **AND A FACT FOR WHOEVER FILED `DEF-BIL-5129` AND `DEF-CUS-5130`: THOSE TWO
ROWS ARE GONE FROM THE SHARED TREE AND FROM EVERY REF, AND THEY NEED RE-FILING.**
Both were in `12-governance/10-defect-log.csv` in the working tree this morning
(*"The PRINTED statement template class has no wording seeded on any
deployment…"* and *"The utility's own legacy account id (`external_ref`) can be
set at create and at import…"*). They were never committed, `git log --all -S`
finds neither, and no remote ref holds them. **They were already absent when
`push_paths.sh`'s sync step reported `restored` on that file**, and that verdict
is the evidence rather than a guess: `sync_stale_tree.py` restores ONLY on a
content-addressed HIT — *this exact blob is an older version of this path* —
which a file still carrying two uncommitted rows cannot produce. So the loss
happened upstream of that sync, in a tree seven lanes are writing to.
**The lesson is rule 11's last line and nothing cleverer: a row that is not
pushed is a row any lane can erase, and `file_defect.py` appending it is only
half the job.**

### 10 · THE DOOR COUNT IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND MY OWN GUARD FOUND IT

`BR-SHL-253` names **seven** modules. Building the guard that keeps that list
honest showed the list is a list of modules that TALK about uploads, not one of
modules that TAKE them.

**Two of the seven are not doors at all.** `work/sync.py` mentions multipart in
two COMMENTS — it documents the attachment endpoint, which lives in
`work/api.py`. `payments/api.py`'s single mention says a multipart branch there
*"would be a second request shape for one operation"*, which is a statement that
it deliberately has none.

**FIVE modules actually read uploaded bytes:** `tenancy/api.py` (the company
logo), `customers/api.py` (account documents), `integrations/api.py` (bank and
meter files), `work/api.py` (field evidence, two endpoints) and
`payments/payment_import_api.py` (remittance and lockbox files).

⚠ **AND THERE IS AN EIGHTH SHAPE NOBODY COUNTED, WHICH IS THE FINDING THAT
MATTERS.** `payments/payment_import_api.py::_uploaded_bytes` takes a remittance
file **either as a multipart part or as base64 inside a JSON body** — its own
docstring says why: *"the S35 modal posts a file and an integration posts JSON,
and a second endpoint for the second shape would be a second place for the hash
to be computed differently"*. **The base64 shape never populates
`request.FILES`**, so the middleware had nothing to look at, and **a bank
posting a lockbox file through the integration path would have had it stored
unscanned** while every check in this repo reported a scan. It now calls
`require_clean()` at the line those bytes come into existence.

**So there are TWO hand-scanned doors and not one** — `integrations::_file_bytes`
(a raw body) and `payments::_uploaded_bytes` (a base64 field) — and
`test_a_door_the_wire_cannot_see_scans_by_hand` is parametrised over both. Proved
red by removing the new call: *"payments/payment_import_api.py::_uploaded_bytes
accepts a base64 field in a JSON body, which never reaches MalwareScanMiddleware,
and does not scan it"*.

**How it was found is worth more than what was found.** The first draft of the
inventory guard grepped for `request.FILES` OR the word `multipart`, so it went
red on **its own author's docstring** — the sentence added to `logo.py` saying
the scan now happens. A guard that matched prose was wrong; being wrong is what
made it read the seven modules one at a time. **A check that can only be
satisfied by looking is worth more than one that can be satisfied by agreeing.**

## 2026-09-13 — `CR-094-BRC01` WAVE M: A FILING CAN BE TAKEN BACK, AND THE BYTES STAY WHERE THE LAW PUT THEM

Builds `BR-CUS-1052` (PO 2026-09-13, verbatim: ***"We should have this
functionality"***). The ruling and its supersession chain were written down the
same morning, above; this row records **how it was built and the three judgments
the ruling did not settle**, which is what step W asks for. Shipped `2.245.0`.

### 1 · WHAT A CLERK CAN DO NOW, AND THE FIGURES

Every row of an account's Documents tab carries a bin. Press it on a scan
somebody filed by mistake and **the document leaves that account**: it is not
listed, **not counted** and not openable, and the download link answers the same
404 as a document that never existed.

* **A list of three documents becomes two, and the footer says two.** The filter
  is on the queryset, not on the slice, so the `COUNT(*)` that draws the
  pagination footer runs over it too. A tab that hid a row and still said
  *"3 documents"* would be the withdrawal failing in the only place a clerk
  could see it.
* **Three of the five types can be taken back; two refuse by name.** `kyc`,
  `payment` and `correspondence` are withdrawable. `system` and `contract` are
  `BR-CUS-036`'s audit-locked pair and answer **409 `BIZ-LOCKED`**, with the
  same sentence on the disabled bin before the clerk presses it.
* **13 backend cases, 21 front-end cases, and wave I's own 18 re-run green.**
  Eight guards were broken first and quoted red; the list is in the
  review-ledger row.

### 2 · THE JUDGMENT THE RULING LEFT TO US: **NOTHING PUTS IT BACK**

`BR-CUS-1052` says what a withdrawal DOES. It says nothing about whether a
withdrawn document is reachable again, and the wave needed an answer to build.
**Law 13 says that is ours to decide and write down, not to ask.**

**Decided: there is no restore, and the row is a tombstone rather than a
deletion.** `withdrawn_at` and `withdrawn_by` are stamped on the filing card;
the card stays, the `document_id` stays, the stored object stays under its
seven-year lock. Nothing in the product lists it, counts it, opens it or brings
it back — **recovery is a job for somebody holding the audit trail**, which is a
database read and a decision by a person, not a second button.

**Why the narrower thing rather than an Undo:** the ruling was asked for so a
misfiled scan stops being part of a customer's file. An Undo control is a second
decision with its own questions — who may press it, for how long, and does a
restored document reappear under its original filing date or today's — and none
of them was put to the PO. Building it would be answering four unasked questions
to satisfy one asked one. **It is one ruling away if this is wrong**, and the
tombstone is what makes that cheap: the row and the bytes are both still there.

### 3 · THE SECOND JUDGMENT: **`DELETE`, AND THE HONESTY IS AT THE RIGHT LAYER**

The obvious objection to `DELETE /accounts/{id}/documents/{docId}` is that
nothing is deleted, and it was weighed rather than waved past. The alternative
considered was hard rule 4's own precedent — `POST /payments/{id}/correct-
reference`, a named endpoint for a narrow act on an immutable row.

**`DELETE` won because the address names the FILING, and the filing is exactly
what stops existing.** `/accounts/{id}/documents/{docId}` is *this account's
filing of that document*; the very next `GET` of that address answers 404. The
verb describes the resource the caller addressed, not a table two joins away.
The payments precedent differs in the way that matters: there the ROW survives
in every read and only three columns move, so `DELETE` would have been a lie to
the caller. Here it is not.

**And the honesty a clerk needs is on the screen, where they are:** *"This
leaves the account permanently. The stored file is kept."* Two sentences of five
words — B14 rule 33's cap for a consequence before an irreversible act — and the
second exists because a clerk who believed they had shredded a customer's
passport scan would have been told the opposite of what happened.

### 4 · THE THIRD: **A SECOND PRESS ANSWERS 404, NOT "ALREADY REMOVED"**

A stale tab can press the bin twice. The options were a named refusal
(*"already taken back"*) or the ordinary not-found.

**Decided: 404, the same answer another utility gets.** After the first press
the account does not hold that document, so *"there is no such document on this
account"* is the literal truth, and `BR-TEN-003` (HR-1 — existence must not
leak) already requires a stranger and a non-existent row to be
indistinguishable. A third answer would have made the withdrawn case
distinguishable from the stranger case by any client that asked twice — a small
leak bought for a message nobody needed.

⚠ **THE RACE IS CLOSED IN THE `UPDATE` AS WELL AS IN THE READ, AND THE RED PROOF
SHOWED WHY THAT IS NOT BELT-AND-BRACES.** The `UPDATE` is scoped
`withdrawn_at__isnull=True` a second time, so two clerks pressing in the same
second write it once and the loser is told 404. When the READ's filter was
removed to prove it red, `test_a_second_withdrawal_answers_not_found` **still
passed** — the `UPDATE`'s own scope caught it. Two guards, two different
failures; neither is the other's spare, and only breaking them separately showed
that.

### 5 · WHAT WAS NOT BUILT, EACH NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE NOTICED

* **No malware scan on this door.** `BR-SHL-253` landed on this branch today and
  covers the integrations upload; the customers upload door is not wired to it.
  Not this wave's file and not silently ignored — REPORTED.
  ⚠ **THE THREE SENTENCES ABOVE ARE FALSE AND ARE LEFT STANDING SO THE
  CORRECTION IS READ WHERE THE CLAIM IS (corrected 2026-09-13, hours after they
  were written).** **The customers upload door IS scanned.**
  `core.malware_scan.MalwareScanMiddleware` is registered in
  `config/settings/base.py`'s `MIDDLEWARE` — the GLOBAL chain, not an app's —
  and its own docstring reads *"Every multipart part, scanned before any view
  sees it."* `apps/customers/api.py` reads `request.FILES`, so the
  account-documents upload passes through it exactly like every other multipart
  door. **The wave looked for an explicit call inside its own module and read
  the absence of one as an absence of cover** — which is precisely what putting
  a rule ON THE WIRE means, and precisely the reading `BR-SHL-253` was written
  to make impossible.
  ⚠ **THE CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE ERROR.** A recorded gap that does not
  exist is an instruction to the next lane to build a SECOND scanner on a door
  that already has one — hard-won law 1 with its sign flipped. **A claim that
  something is NOT covered is a claim like any other**, and it is checked the
  same way: read the middleware list, not the module.
* **No `withdrawn_by_process` column.** No automation withdraws anything, and a
  column nothing ever writes is dead schema every test passes over (law 2).
  `ck_account_documents_withdrawal` refuses a withdrawal that names nobody.
* **`GET /accounts/{id}/documents/{docId}` still has no caller on screen.**
  `customers.account.documents.open` has sat in all eleven catalogues, unused,
  since wave I. An Open row action beside the bin is the obvious next thing and
  it is not this wave's ruling — REPORTED, not slipped in.
* **`OQ-1340` is OPEN and it binds this wave's copy.** `audit_log` is pruned on
  a retention schedule, so nothing here — screen, docstring or rule row —
  describes the withdrawal row as a permanent record of what the account used to
  hold.

### 6 · A RED THIS WAVE DID NOT CAUSE, READ RATHER THAN STEPPED OVER

`DEF-SHL-5101` — the B14 rule-6 call-site census — had been **red since
2026-09-12**, and reading it found the census wrong in **both** directions. Four
`ConfirmDialog` call sites had arrived unaudited (`MachineKeysPage`,
`OrderDetailPage`, `OrderEditPage`, and this wave's own); **two had LEFT and
nobody moved the record** — the deactivate confirms `CR-089` P1/P10 deliberately
removed on 2026-09-10 under `DEF-4743`, so the audit went on asserting that two
destructive controls existed and were classified when neither existed at all.
That second half is filed as **`DEF-SHL-5137`**.

**It is the half nobody goes looking for.** A census is wrong in both directions
or it is not a census, and 34 + 4 − 2 = **36 call sites, 27 pinned danger**. Each
of the four new rows was read by a person before it was written, which is that
defect's own remedy in its own words: *"the number in the audit must never be
raised to match the code without a reader looking at each new call site."*

⚠ **`DEF-SHL-5101` IS MARKED `partially-fixed`, NOT CLOSED.** It names four red
suites and this wave fixed one. The other three — `regionalReachesTheScreen.dom`
(1) and `UnitsPage` (2) — were re-measured on 2026-09-13 and are still red, and
they belong to metering and the shell rather than to this wave.

### 7 · THE VERSION WAS TAKEN TWICE WHILE THIS WAVE WORKED, AND THE VERIFY CAUGHT IT

Worth one line because it is `DEF-GOV-3756`'s exact shape and it cost nothing
this time. This wave computed `2.243.0` correctly from the remote, wrote it into
five documents, and `allocate.py version --verify 2.243.0` then answered
***"TAKEN — origin/claude/hi-0jmv62 carries it"***: a sibling had pushed it in
the meantime. `2.245.0` was re-derived and every document re-written from the new
tip. **The defect id went the same way** — `DEF-SHL-5129` was gone by the time
the row was filed and the allocator issued `5137`. Law 11's clause is right and
it is worth restating in its strongest form: **re-derive the ids in the same
breath as the blobs, every push, unconditionally.**

## 2026-09-13 — `BR-CUS-1047` BUILT: THE RULING THAT REACHED FOUR DOCUMENTS AND NO LINE OF CODE

**What a clerk can do this morning that they could not do last night:** put an
account back on the right unit. Until now an account opened against the wrong
unit had no way back — the only fix was to close it and open another, which
loses its number, its notes, its payment record and its whole history, to
correct a typo.

⚠ **THE RULING WAS A DAY OLD AND NOTHING WAS WRONG ANYWHERE.** `OQ-CUS-1769`
closed on 2026-09-12 on option (a). It was written into this log, into
`BR-CUS-1047`, into `BR-CUS-017`'s own row and into the open-questions register
— **and into no line of code.** `apps/customers/services.py` went on refusing
the field, citing the un-narrowed rule, and every gate in this repository was
green over it. **Nothing here can see that gap:** a gate reads code against
code, and a ruling that never arrives leaves nothing to disagree with. The only
check that finds one is a person reading the register against the product, which
is what `r11` step 0 asks for and why it is step 0.

### WHAT WAS BUILT

`POST /accounts/{id}/correct-unit` (`apps/customers/unit_correction.py`), with
an append-only record in `account_unit_corrections` (`customers 0045`, RLS in
`0046`) and 14 cases in `tests/test_br_cus_1047_unit_correction.py`.

The four conditions, one for one — PO 2026-09-12, verbatim: ***"(a) Narrow the
rule to allow exactly this correction: a reason from a fixed list, a
supervisor's approval, effective today, never backdated, issued bills
untouched."***

### TWO JUDGMENTS THE RULING DID NOT DECIDE, RECORDED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**1 · WHO IS A SUPERVISOR — AND IT WAS NOT PUT BACK TO THE PO, BECAUSE THEY HAVE
ANSWERED IT TWICE ALREADY (law 13).** This product has no role called
supervisor, and two independent places already say who counts as one:

  * **`OQ-042`'s closure**, verbatim — *"optional toggle default ON; supervisor
    = SysAdmin/Executive; blocks when enabled (PO R6)"*. `metering.services.
    cosign_read_batch` has been built on it since `CR-038` W7.
  * **A4's signed grid** (`identity.models.A4_MATRIX`, transcribed verbatim
    under `BR-IDN-014`), row `adjustment_approval` — **System Admin `Approve` ·
    Executive `Approve` · Billing Clerk `Request`**. `core.permissions.
    AdminOrExecutive`'s own docstring reads *"+ approvals"*.

So the door is `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN, EXECUTIVE)` and a Billing Clerk is
refused. That is not a stricter guess; it is the only reading both sources
support. **A correction a clerk can give themselves is not an approval.**

**2 · WHAT THE FIXED LIST IS.** The ruling requires one and enumerates none, so
it was DERIVED rather than invented: **the three doors in this product that
write `accounts.unit_id` are the three ways a record can come to name the wrong
one** — `create_account` → `opened_on_wrong_unit`, `create_from_import` →
`imported_onto_wrong_unit`, `move_in` → `moved_in_to_wrong_unit`. The list is a
`CHECK` constraint, not a tenant lookup, because the ruling says *fixed* and a
list a tenant may extend is not fixed.

⚠ **NOT ONE OF THEM SAYS A CUSTOMER MOVED, AND THAT IS WHAT KEEPS `BR-CUS-017`
INTACT.** A genuine move still goes through move-out and move-in, because the
bills, meters and reads belong to the unit and must not follow a person. A test
asserts the absence, so a lane adding `customer_moved` has to delete it first.

### THE BOUNDARY, DRAWN RATHER THAN STUBBED — `OQ-CUS-12355`

A4 gives a Billing Clerk `Request` on that same row, so the signed grid does
contemplate *clerk raises it, supervisor approves it* as two acts by two people.
**Nothing in this product implements a request that waits for an approval, on
any table** — not even adjustments, where `ACTION_UNAVAILABLE["adjust"]` says
the write path is absent. Building the pending row, the queue, the notification
and the supervisor's inbox would have resolved an open decision by picking a
value, which the prime directive forbids.

So a supervisor performs the correction and their performance IS the approval,
recorded on `approved_by`. A clerk is refused by name and the screen will show
the control disabled with that reason (`BR-SHL-025`) — a true product behaviour
they can act on (*ask a supervisor*), not a `NotImplementedError` standing where
a feature should be. **`OQ-CUS-12355` asks the PO whether a clerk should be able
to raise one**, and it matters at our size: the ICP is a utility run by 10–20
staff and at `T7` by one or two, which is the exact ground `OQ-WRK-1492` was
ruled on — *"clark can do it sicne it s a day to day work"*, because *"a
two-person utility has no supervisor sitting by the screen"*.

### WHY THE RECORD IS A TABLE AND NOT ONLY AN AUDIT ROW

Hard rule 7's audit row is written, and it is not enough on its own: **`audit_log`
is pruned on a retention schedule** (hard rule 4's own text says so, and whether
a correction's row is exempt is `OQ-1340`, OPEN). The question *"why is this
account on Suite 2 when five bills say Suite 1?"* outlives any retention window,
because the five bills do. So the audit row is the EVENT and
`account_unit_corrections` is the RECORD.

### WHAT MOVES AND WHAT STAYS — the ruling's own worked case (`ACC-E07`, p185)

`A-11812 · Bramble Bakery`, `Suite 1 · U-000417` → `Suite 2 · U-000418`.

  * **The service agreements move** — the old ones end TODAY, the new ones start
    TODAY. That is what actually re-points the plan, the meters, the route and
    the cycle, none of which has a column on the account (`BR-CUS-029`).
  * **The plan changes because the unit's does** — `SCW-RES v1` → `SCM-COM v2`,
    base **`$20.00` → `$63.00` a month, `$43.00` more**. No plan is written here.
  * **The reading history stays with Suite 1.** Reads belong to meters and
    meters belong to the unit.
  * **The five issued bills stay** — hard rule 4, proved by reading every
    invoice row of the account before and after and comparing them field by
    field. A bill that was wrong is credited and replaced, which is its own flow.
  * **The address does not move** — hard rule 8. No address column is declared
    on the correction and none is read.

### THE SECOND FINDING: A REFUSAL THAT NAMED NO RULE (`DEF-CUS-5127`)

`PATCH /accounts/{id}` answered *"unknown field"* for `unit`, `unit_id` and
`account_type` — real columns told a caller they do not exist, against
`_reject_unknown`'s own promise that *"a field that names a real column or a
real rule gets that rule back"*. Both now refuse BY NAME:

  * `unit` and `unit_id` cite `BR-CUS-017 · BR-CUS-1047` and **point at the new
    door**. The old reason said re-homing is *"the move-out → move-in pair"* full
    stop, which stopped being the whole truth on 2026-09-12 — a refusal whose
    reason has expired is hard-won law 1 in its second form, and it is why
    `paperless` and `sms_reminders` were removed from that map rather than
    reworded.
  * `account_type` cites `BR-CUS-012` **and says plainly that no rule states how
    a category may be changed** (`OQ-CUS-12356`). Inventing a rule id to make
    that entry read like its neighbours would have been the purest form of law 1
    — a refusal citing a guarantee nobody signed.

### A THIRD THING, FOUND WHILE LOOKING: `DEF-CUS-5135`

`account_subtype` IS patchable and `_resolve_account_subtype` never checks that
the chosen sub-type's `parent_account_type_id` matches the account's own type.
So a clerk can already put a commercial sub-type on a residential account, and
nothing objects. It is filed rather than fixed here — it belongs to whoever owns
the sub-type picker — and `OQ-CUS-12356` names it, because whatever is ruled
about changing a category has to settle that pair too.
