## 2026-09-13 — `BR-CUS-1047`: WHAT IS STILL OWED, AND THE SURVEY THAT LOOKED FOR MORE OF THE SAME

### THE SCREEN IS NOT BUILT, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT

`r11` step 2b numbers the front end so that skipping it is VISIBLE. **It was
skipped, deliberately, and here is the boundary and the reason.**

`POST /accounts/{id}/correct-unit` and `GET` of an account's corrections both
work and are proved. **No screen calls either.** `R5`'s sixth edit dialog
(`ACC-E07`) is not drawn, so today the capability is reachable by API only —
which is hard-won law 2's *built is not wired*, stated rather than hidden.

**Why it was left:** the account Overview and its six edit surfaces belong to
`BR-CUS-1053`'s wave, which was editing those files while this ran, and this
correction **must not sit among the Overview's edit pencils** — it is a
supervisor's act and a Billing Clerk is refused, so it is a different control
with a different door. Adding it would have meant editing the account screen's
routing and its dialog set in the same hour as the lane that owns them; the
shared-tree cost of that is `DEF-GOV-5138`, which this lane had already paid
once today on a business-rules file.

**What the screen must do when it is built**, so the next lane does not have to
re-derive it: one control, on the account, VISIBLE and DISABLED with its reason
for a Billing Clerk (`BR-SHL-025`, never hidden); a `ConfirmDialog` at the
**danger tier**, because a correction re-points a live billing record and is not
undoable by the same door (B14 rule 6); a reason picked from the three, never
typed; **no date field at all**; and a sentence in the product's own words
saying which act is which — *a move is not a correction* — at six words per
sentence (B14 rule 33). The eleven catalogues already hold the five refusal
sentences this path raises.

### THE SURVEY: WAS THIS THE ONLY RULING THAT NEVER REACHED THE CODE?

**Asked because a ruling that never arrives is invisible to every gate here**,
so the only way to find one is to read the register against the product. Every
customers rule CONFIRMED or AMENDED on 2026-09-10 or later was checked against
the code, and every customers question closed in that window:

| ruling | in the code? |
|---|---|
| `BR-CUS-1046` — a list opens on what was just created | **yes** — `ACCOUNT_DEFAULT_SORT = "created"`, `dir = "desc"` |
| `BR-CUS-1047` — the unit correction | **NO — this was the one.** Built 2026-09-13 |
| `BR-CUS-1048` — a master account's `Accounts` tab | **yes** — `MasterAccountsTab.tsx` |
| `BR-CUS-1049` — `Complaints` and `Services` tabs | **yes** — `AccountsListPage.tsx`'s ten-tab strip |
| `BR-CUS-1050` — one deposit capability, mounted | **yes** — `apps/customers/deposit.py`, and the move-in wizard's step |
| `BR-CUS-1052` — a filed document can be withdrawn | **yes** — `customers/0044`, same day it was ruled |
| `BR-CUS-1053` — the account edit surfaces | **yes** — in flight as this was written |
| `OQ-CUS-1790` — all eight lists newest-first | **yes** — built the day it closed, `2.238.0` |
| `OQ-CUS-1810` — closed 2026-09-12 | **yes** — built in `2.238.1` |

**So `BR-CUS-1047` was the only one, and the honest reading is that the repo is
good at this and missed once.** What made it miss is worth naming: every other
ruling in that list arrived attached to a wave that was already running, and
this one closed a question whose own row said *"NOTHING IS BLOCKED AND NOTHING
IS STUBBED"* — true, and therefore nothing anywhere went red or amber when it
was answered. **A ruling that blocks nothing has no owner by default.**

### A DIFFERENT SHAPE, FOUND ON THE WAY, AND IT IS THE MIRROR

`BR-CUS-1053`'s own row carried **two clauses that were false about the code**:
that `unit` and `account_type` were *"skipped SILENTLY"* so a form offering
either *"gets a SUCCESS and changes nothing"* (measured: both were refused at
the door, and the branch that reads as their handling is unreachable), and that
`BR-CUS-1047` *"is unbuilt"* (true when written, false hours later). Both are
corrected in the row.

**That is the mirror of a ruling that never reached the code: a rule that
describes code that is not there.** Neither is visible to a gate, and both are
found the same way — by reading one against the other.

### AND `DEF-CUS-5135`, WHICH IS NEITHER

`account_subtype` is patchable and `_resolve_account_subtype` never checks that
the chosen sub-type's `parent_account_type_id` matches the account's own type,
so a commercial sub-type can sit on a residential account today and nothing
objects. **No rule was broken and none was ignored — nobody ever asked whether
two fields of one row agree**, which is why every test is green over it: a
fixture author picks a sensible pair. Filed rather than fixed, because it
belongs to the sub-type picker's owner, and named in `OQ-CUS-12356` because
whatever is ruled about changing a category has to settle the pair too.


## 2026-09-13 — `CR-094-BRC01` wave N · `ACC-S1` + `ACC-S15`: AN ACCOUNT IS CORRECTED FROM THE ACCOUNT, AND THE RULE THAT COMMISSIONED IT HAD THE SCOPE WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

`BR-CUS-1053`, PO 2026-09-13: *"Build the account edit screen"*, and
*"Correcting an account's details from the account … Every group on the Overview
carrying its own edit control"*. Built at `2.249.0`.

**WHAT A CLERK CAN DO THAT THEY COULD NOT DO THIS MORNING.** Open an account,
press the pencil on the Account group, and correct its sub-type, whether it is
tax exempt, the exemption certificate number, the date that exemption runs out,
the preferred language, paperless, text reminders and autopay — eight fields, in
a dialog over the group they belong to, with one audit row. **`PATCH
/accounts/{id}` has been mounted, handled, audited and tested since August and
had no caller anywhere in the front end**, so until today a misspelt sub-type or
a wrong exemption date could not be fixed from anywhere in the product.

### 1 · ⚠ THE RULE'S OWN SCOPE SENTENCE WAS WRONG, MEASURED, AND IT WOULD HAVE COST THREE FIELDS

`BR-CUS-1053` and this log's entry of the same morning both say `PATCH
/accounts/{id}` takes **SEVEN** fields and refuses **ELEVEN** by name. Measured
against `apps/customers/services.py` on the day the wave started:

| | the rule says | the code holds |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH_FIELDS` | 7 | **11** |
| `REFUSED_FIELDS` | 11 | **34** |

**The three the rule omits are `tax_exempt_ref`, `tax_exempt_expires` and
`preferred_language` — and all three are fields `R5`'s own dialog DRAWS.** A lane
that trusted the rule rather than the code would have shipped a form with no
certificate number, no expiry and no language, and every test would have passed,
because nothing in this repository compares a prose scope with the set the server
enforces. Both figures are amended in the rule, dated, and **pinned by
`test_cr094_n_account_edit_scope.py::…tc6`** — the tool the lesson asks for:
*where a rule restates what a tool does, name the tool and let a reader run it.*
The eleven the rule lists BY NAME are a real subset — the columns owned by
another path — and each is asserted one by one against the rule id the screen
will print.

### 2 · ⚠ THE "SILENT SKIP" IS NOT A SILENT SKIP, AND THE REAL DEFECT IS BIGGER

The rule warns that `unit` and `account_type` are *"skipped SILENTLY"* — that
`update_account` does `if field in ("unit", "account_type"): continue`, so a form
offering either returns success and changes nothing. **Measured, that is not what
happens.** Both are refused at the door with `VAL-002` before that branch can
run, because `_reject_unknown` checks the payload against `PATCH_FIELDS` first
and neither name is in it. **The branch is dead code**: `_validate_account`
populates those two keys only under `if not partial:`, and `update_account`
always passes `partial=True`.

**What IS wrong is the reason given.** `_reject_unknown`'s own docstring promises
*"a field that names a real column or a real rule gets that rule back, so the
caller learns WHY rather than being told the field does not exist"* — and
`account_type` is a real column. A clerk correcting a miscategorised account
would be told the field does not exist. **`DEF-CUS-5127`.**

**And walking every concrete column of `accounts` through the door made it seven
columns wide rather than two.** The five nobody had looked at are `premises_id`,
`cash_only_no_autopay`, `final_read_state`, `is_sample` and — the one with a
clerk-facing cost — **`external_ref`, the utility's own legacy account id.**
`_validate_account` HAS a branch cleaning it and both `CREATE_FIELDS` and the
bulk import accept it; it is simply absent from `PATCH_FIELDS`, so **a number
typed wrong at cutover can never be corrected from anywhere. `DEF-CUS-5141`.** ⚠ **RE-FILED: this row was first allocated `DEF-CUS-5130` and its register line was lost to a sibling's whole-file write before it reached the branch — law 11, mechanism two, on this wave's own record. `DEF-CUS-5130` is left UNUSED rather than re-used, because re-using it would publish one id meaning two things.**
Neither is fixed here: deciding who may write those columns is a ruling, not a
lane's pick. The set is PINNED so it can only shrink deliberately.

### 3 · EIGHT CONTROLS, ONE LIVE — and the count is a judgment, recorded rather than assumed

`R5` draws **twelve** groups with a control each. **The built Overview renders
SEVEN**, plus the mailing-address sub-head. The five the drawing has that this
product has no group for — `Money`, `Service`, `Plan`, `Unit` and a free-standing
`Mailing address` panel — are KPI tiles, another tab, or nothing at all.

**The judgment: put a control on the eight headings that exist, and do not create
five new panels.** Creating them is restructuring the Overview, which is not what
`ACC-S15` asks for, and a pencil cannot be put on a heading that does not exist.
Of the eight, **exactly one is live** — `Account`, the only group whose endpoint
exists — which is `R5`'s own finding in its own words: *"Two of the twelve need no
new server work at all."* The other seven are **disabled WITH their reason**
(`BR-SHL-025`), each decided by one function so no panel can acquire its own
answer, and each within B14 rule 33's six-word cap for a refusal.

### 4 · THREE FIELDS ARE WRITABLE AND DELIBERATELY NOT OFFERED

Recorded rather than dropped in silence, because a writable field absent from a
form is invisible to every check this repo has:

* **`status`** — the drawing refuses it ON the form, in its own words: *"closing
  an account is the move-out flow, not an edit"* (`BR-CUS-030`). A status select
  on a correction form is a second door onto the move-out flow. Pinned by
  `…tc4`, which asserts BOTH halves — that the server accepts it and that the
  form does not offer it — so anyone adding one has to come and change a
  sentence explaining why they should not.
* **`opened_at`** — drawn nowhere in `R5`. Backdating when service began moves
  what a bill run picks up; that is not a typo fix.
* **`custom_data`** — the tenant's own fields, already rendered READ-ONLY by
  `CustomFieldsView` in another panel. An input for them belongs to the group
  that displays them.

### 5 · THREE DIVERGENCES FROM THE DRAWING, FILED AND NOT FOLLOWED (B14 rule 38)

Rule 38: where a drawing and our UI rules disagree about how a FORM IS BUILT, the
UI rules win; what the form CONTAINS is still the drawing's.

1. **The section headings are shortened.** `R5` writes *"WHAT KIND OF ACCOUNT
   THIS IS"* and *"DELIVERY AND CONTACT PREFERENCES"*; rule 33 caps a heading at
   THREE WORDS and forbids it being a sentence. They read *Account kind* and
   *Delivery preferences*.
2. **`Preferred language` is a text field, not the drawn select.** No endpoint
   lists the tenant's `BR-TEN-042` language set, so a select could only be
   hand-typed — which hard-won law 12 forbids by name — or empty. A text field is
   also what `NewAccountWizard` and `MoveInWizard` already render for this same
   column, and a second construction for one field is the drift B14 rule 36
   exists to stop.
3. **The *not editable here* list carries LABELS, not the drawing's reasons.**
   *"Unit — an account never moves between units; a new occupant is a move-in"* is
   RATIONALE, which rule 33 puts at **zero words on screen**. The five names stay
   and the reasons live in the code — the same resolution the asset module's
   `NotOnThisForm` reached for the same rule.

### 6 · ⚠ A HOLD THAT WAS RE-CHECKED MID-WAVE AND CHANGED WHAT IT SAYS

The Customer group was written as *held, pending an endpoint*. **A sibling lane
landed `BR-CUS-1054` while this wave was being built**, so `updateCustomer` and
`CustomerEditDialog` now exist — and re-reading the code rather than trusting the
morning's note showed **they are not this panel**. `updateCustomer` writes the
`customers` row and is mounted on the customer's OWN screen; this panel renders
the ACCOUNT'S CONTACT (`account_contacts`), a different table, and **nothing in
the product writes a contact.** `R5` says the same: *"GET /customers/{id} is
read-only and there is no contacts route at all."*

So the refusal stands and the **expiry test asserts the thing that is actually
missing** — that `endpoints.ts` wraps no contact write. ⚠ **And the detector is
proved before it is trusted** (`TC-N7a`), over names it must catch and names it
must not, because an expiry test whose pattern matches nothing reports *"still
held"* forever while the hold quietly expires — hard-won law 7's *structurally
incapable of failing* shape.

**A separate gap found in that re-check, recorded and not built:** the account
carries `detail.customer` and **there is no link from the account to its customer
record anywhere on this screen**, so a clerk who needs to fix a name must leave
and search for the customer by hand.

### 7 · WHAT WAS REUSED RATHER THAN BUILT

Every one of these was looked for before anything was written, which is B14 rule
36 and the PO's standing instruction of 2026-09-12 (*"BUILD FROM THE ACTUAL CODE,
AND DO NOT CREATE DUPLICATE CODE"*):

* `features/assets/AssetPanelEdits.tsx` — the built precedent for a pencil per
  panel (`AST-B-25`). This follows its shape rather than inventing a second one.
* `components/Panel.tsx` already carries `title` + `trailing`, so **no new
  component was written** for a heading with a control on its row.
* `components/RowActions.tsx` already makes `reason` and `disabled` ONE prop, so
  a caller *cannot* disable a control without saying why — `BR-SHL-025`
  implemented in the kit rather than in this screen.
* `FormModal`'s five help-bearing field variants already render **label → input →
  helper** (B14 rule 39), so the field anatomy needed nothing.
* The Payment method panel keeps the disabled `→ Update method` it has shipped
  since `CR-030` W3 rather than gaining a second control beside it — two refusals
  for one fact.
* `NewAccountWizard`'s existing construction for the same four tax/language
  fields, so the product has one answer for them and not two.

### 8 · ⚠ AND THIS WAVE'S OWN WORK WAS SILENTLY REVERTED FOUR TIMES IN ONE SESSION

Recorded because it is hard-won law 11 happening to a lane that had read it.
Uncommitted edits to `07-frontend/src/api/endpoints.ts`, to all eleven locale
catalogues, to `09-human-review-ledger.md` and to this file were each reverted by
siblings' whole-file writes, and **nothing announced any of them.** The first was
caught only because `tsc` then said `updateAccount` was not exported; the second
only because a `--numstat` against the tip printed nothing where 35 keys should
have been; the third and fourth only because the content was looked for again
before pushing. Two of those pieces later reached the branch anyway, swept in by
a sibling's pathspec commit (mechanism five).
**The practical lesson is law 11's own last line, and it is the one that costs:
commit small and commit often.** After the second, every block of this wave's
prose was written to a file in the scratchpad and the screen wiring kept as an
idempotent re-apply script, so the third and fourth cost seconds rather than
minutes. **A lane holding twenty minutes of uncommitted work in this tree should
expect to lose it.**

## 2026-09-13 · `CR-094-BRC01` wave M — **SEND STATEMENT: WHAT WAS BUILT, AND THE FOUR JUDGMENTS TAKEN RATHER THAN ASKED**

The measurement above found all three parts of a statement already in the repo
and none of them joined to the next. This is what joining them cost and what had
to be decided along the way. **Version `2.249.0`. `BR-BIL-1033` is the rule.**

⚠ **THAT NUMBER WAS `2.248.0` FOR AN HOUR AND THE CHANGELOG CARRIED THIS ENTRY
TWICE — `DEF-GOV-5139`'s shape, walked into by a lane that had already filed
`DEF-GOV-5134` about the neighbouring one.** `allocate.py version --verify`
answered *"still free on every branch"* about `2.248.0`, truthfully, and it was
already taken **in the shared working tree** — a version is claimed by editing
three tracked files, and a lane holds those edits for as long as it takes to
write a changelog entry before anything is pushed. So the entry landed under one
number, the version files were renumbered to the next, and **the first block
stayed behind**: two headings, one body, word for word identical.

⚠ **AND THE GATE PROPOSED FOR `DEF-GOV-5139` WOULD HAVE PASSED STRAIGHT OVER
IT.** That gate refuses a REPEATED `## [x.y.z]` heading. These two headings were
DIFFERENT — `2.248.0` and `2.249.0` — and the four hundred words beneath them
were the same. **The check that catches both shapes is a duplicate BODY, not a
duplicate heading**, because the failure is always a renumber that left its draft
behind, and a renumber changes precisely the heading the gate is looking at.
Cheapest form: hash each entry's body with its version string masked out, and
refuse two entries that hash alike.

⚠ **AND THE REMOVAL ITSELF WAS REVERTED ONCE BEFORE IT LANDED**, by a sibling's
whole-file write in the seconds between the edit and the push — `DEF-GOV-5134`
again, in the same session that filed it. The fix that worked was to rebuild the
file from the pinned tip and push **in the same command**, with no gap for
anything to write into.

**THE WORKED FIGURE, which is already signed in two other places:** account
`ACC-1042` over **1–31 July 2026** opens at **45.00** (a cutover balance dated
2026-06-30, before the window), is charged **247.87** on the 15th, pays
**292.87** on the 25th, and closes at **0.00**. `account_ledger`'s own docstring
states the same three movements, and US-LED-009 §7's `r_n = r_{n−1} + charge_n −
payment_n` is what makes them foot. The statement copies all four and computes
none of them.

### Four judgments taken here rather than put to the PO (law 13)

**1 · THE PERIOD HAS NO DEFAULT.** `BR-TEN-043` forbids a clock in a service
module, so the two dates had to come from somewhere. A server-side default
("last three months") was rejected: a statement covering the wrong period is
wrong in a way nobody notices, and a default is a product decision taken in the
quietest possible place. The endpoint requires both dates and answers 422 naming
which one is missing; the FORM proposes today in both boxes — the shared
quick-form's own behaviour for a date field — which the clerk can see and change.
**A visible proposal is not a hidden default.**

**2 · `bill_no`, `cycle` AND `bill_date` ARE LEFT UNFILLED.** `catalogs.py`
builds the statement class's palette from `_BILL_META`, which drags three
bill-shaped tokens along with it. A statement has no bill number, no cycle and
no bill date — `BR-CUS-040`, *statement ≠ bill*, CONFIRMED 2026-08-08 — so
supplying one would invent a fact. **This is an application of signed law, not a
judgment gap, so no question was minted.** What IS reported: the Templates
screen will count three merge fields for this class that no statement can fill.
Narrowing an A19-derived palette belongs to whoever owns A19.

**3 · THE RUNNING-LEDGER BAND IS NOT PUT IN THE RENDER CONTEXT, AND THIS ONE WAS
FOUND BY THE CODE REFUSING.** `rendering.encode_context` is **TOP-LEVEL ONLY** —
it tags a `Decimal`, a `datetime` or a `date` directly under a key and lets
anything nested fall through — so an array of dated rows reached Django's
JSONField as raw Python and died on `json.dumps` with *"Object of type date is
not JSON serializable"*. Pre-formatting the rows into strings would have been
worse: it moves money's display rounding out of `format_money`, which rule 2
keeps in exactly one place. **And nothing would have read them** — the only
statement body that exists names six tokens and no row token. The row COUNT
travels on the result instead. Written into the code at the point where the next
lane would reach for it.

**4 · THE PRINTED STATEMENT'S WORDING IS NOT AUTHORED HERE.** `DEF-BIL-5133`.
The class is declared with its ten tokens and `mandatory_content=("nothing is
due",)`, and no deployment has a body for it: the notifications seeder excludes
it to `apps.billing.services.seed_bill_templates`, which resolves to
`templates_service.seed_platform_default` — the BILL LAYOUT seeder, which plants
no statement. Authoring that wording is a document-registry act with an owner
named in two files, and this wave declined to quietly become that owner. The
absence is **reported on every result** (`statement_print_wording_absent`) rather
than papered over, and the print row is still queued because `BR-NOT-024`'s
floor is right that a customer document goes on paper.

### What was reused rather than rebuilt

`ledger.reporting.account_ledger` for every figure · the seeded `email_statement`
wording, which already carried A19 rule 1's disclaimer · `queue_document` for the
row and its idempotency · `receipts.py`'s problem/outcome shape AND its
per-channel filter — the print floor means the email call also touches the print
row, and without that filter a clerk is told three copies were queued when two
were · the `QuickForm` mechanism wave L had just built, so the screen half is a
declaration and not a new dialog.

### What is NOT done, stated rather than implied

**The ✉ glyph on the account still refuses.** The server is live and `ACC-Q07`
declares its form, but the one hunk that mounts the dialog lives in
`AccountDetailPage.tsx`, which is mid-wave under another lane with an untracked
import in it. Publishing that file would have published their unfinished work —
which is exactly what `DEF-GOV-5134` records this lane doing **by accident**
earlier the same day, so doing it deliberately an hour later was not defensible.
The refusal string was rewritten in all eleven languages instead, because
*"Statements are not built yet"* had stopped being true.

⚠ **AND THE REFUSAL THAT HELD THIS CONTROL FOR A MONTH WAS WRONG ON THE DAY IT
WAS WRITTEN.** `accountRailReadiness.ts` said *"the account-ledger derived view a
statement would read does not exist"*; `account_ledger` landed **2026-08-11**
(`dea0d6f0b`), four days BEFORE that module. Not stale — wrong at birth, and
nothing ever re-read it. That is hard-won law 1, and its cost here was a feature
that already existed sitting behind a closed door for a month.

### The option the blueprint raises and this wave did NOT take

Folding *Send statement* into the communication door (`accounts/{id}/communication`)
is explicitly the PO's to decide and is left alone. Stated here so the next lane
knows it was seen and deliberately not taken.

## 2026-09-13 — THE VERSION NUMBER NAMED TWO BUILDS THREE TIMES IN ONE AFTERNOON, AND THE ALLOCATOR WAS RIGHT EVERY TIME (`2.249.1`)

**PO, verbatim: *"in last few release - we are making mistake in allocating
Version # - can you identify what is the issue and fix it"***.

⚠ **THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN ONCE AND LOST BEFORE IT REACHED THE BRANCH, WHICH IS
RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME CLASS OF FAULT AS THE ONE IT DESCRIBES.**
It was appended to the shared tree, verified as a superset of the tip minutes
before pushing, and was **absent from the tree by push time** — overwritten by a
whole-file write from one of eight concurrent lanes. The push that followed
carried the file anyway and published a sibling's in-flight register line
(`DEF-CUS-5141`'s re-filing note) while carrying none of this. `git diff
--numstat` said `1 1`, which is what an 80-line loss looks like when the thing
that replaced it is the same size as the file. **Law 11's closing line is the
only defence and it is not a check: commit small and commit often.**

### WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG — NOT THE ARITHMETIC

* **`allocate.py version --bump` was already correct**, taking the maximum over
  the working tree AND every remote branch (`DEF-GOV-3756`, `DEF-GOV-4023`).
* **`--verify` deliberately does NOT read this tree, and that is also correct** —
  `DEF-GOV-3843` records what happened when it did: at push time a lane's own
  number is already in `package.json`, so counting this tree answered *TAKEN*
  for every number a lane could ask about and *free* for one a sibling had
  shipped, **both exactly backwards**.
* ⚠ **THE COST OF THAT CORRECT EXCLUSION IS THE BLIND SPOT WHERE EVERY COLLISION
  LIVES: A VERSION IS CLAIMED BY EDITING THREE TRACKED FILES IN A SHARED TREE,
  LONG BEFORE ANYBODY PUSHES.** With one lane, a rare race. **With eight, the
  ordinary case** — and the tool kept answering *"still free on every branch"*
  about a number already taken an arm's length away.

**Three occurrences in one afternoon, and a fourth the new gate found:**
`2.246.0` twice for two changes (`DEF-GOV-5139`); `2.248.0` and `2.249.0` for
ONE change, a draft renumbered and the draft published by a sibling's whole-file
commit; and **`2.174.0`, published twice since 2026-09-05 — eight days, nothing
looking.**

### THE FIX, IN TWO HALVES THAT COVER DIFFERENT THINGS

**1 · `allocate.py` says what the tree holds, beside its verdict.**
`tree_claim()` prints ⚠ *THIS TREE ALREADY READS …* when an authoritative
literal is at or past the number being verified, and **does not change the
verdict** — that is what `DEF-GOV-3843` cost, and the tool cannot know whether
the literal is the asker's own bump or a sibling's. **The person asking does.**
`claims_at_or_above()` is pure and held by `selftest`, comparing tuples of
integers and never text: `"2.9.0" > "2.10.0"` is true as strings and false as
versions, and that error would leave the tool silent on exactly the collisions
it exists to catch.

**2 · `G123 one-change-one-version` refuses the damage however it arose** — a
tool a lane forgets to run protects nothing. It asserts **both shapes**: no
heading twice, **and no two entries with the same body**.
⚠ **THE PREVENTION PROPOSED WHEN `DEF-GOV-5139` WAS FILED WAS THE HEADING CHECK
ALONE, AND IT WOULD HAVE REPORTED PASS ON THE VERY NEXT OCCURRENCE** —
`2.248.0`/`2.249.0` are two headings over one body. Two lanes reached that
conclusion independently within the hour. Bodies are compared with whitespace
collapsed, so a duplicate surviving a re-wrap is caught too; a parse finding
fewer than 50 entries is refused (`DEF-057`'s shape); and the count scanned is
printed beside the verdict.

### PROVED RED FIRST, ON REAL DAMAGE, THROUGH THE RUNNER'S OWN PATH

`G123` was not proved on a planted fault: **it went red on the real
`CHANGELOG.md`, naming `2.174.0`**, exercised through `_assert_registry_sane()`
→ the registry entry → `module.run()` exactly as `run_gates` line 2573 calls it,
never through `__main__` (`DEF-GOV-3733`). The allocator's sentence was proved on
real state: with the files at `2.249.1`, `--verify 2.249.1` printed *"still free
on every branch"* **and** the tree warning — what a colliding lane would have
seen and did not.

### WHAT WAS REPAIRED

`2.174.0`'s second copy is removed, the two blocks compared byte for byte first
(1,259 bytes each, identical) and the bytes either side proved byte-identical to
the tip. The deletion was declared with `ALLOW_REGISTER_DELETIONS=1` rather than
slipped past the guard. `G35` and `G123` both PASS at `2.249.1`.

## 2026-09-13 · A CLERK STARTS FROM THE UTILITY'S OWN WORDING, NOT A BLANK BOX

The Product Owner opened the Communication dialog on the live product and said,
verbatim:

> *"it should also have ready to use messages from our Notification rules - user
> will not write it every time"*

**RULED: the dialog offers the tenant's published templates as a starting
point.** It is not a new store and not a second catalogue — Settings →
Templates already holds them, and this tenant had **thirty-four published
versions** the dialog simply could not see. A class published, re-worded or
archived there changes the picker with no release on the account screen.

### WHAT DECIDES WHICH ONES ARE OFFERED, AND WHY IT IS A CATEGORY LIST

The dialog already refuses four message KINDS by name, for two reasons:
collections is the dunning **ladder** (`BR-PAY-035`, `BR-NOT-008` — a step
composed by hand would carry no tier and write no `NoticeHistory` row), and
billing's classes are **documents that already have a writer** (a bill copy is
billing's reprint, a statement is the statement path). **The same two reasons
decide the templates**, one layer down: `payments`, `service_field` and
`account_lifecycle` are offered; `collections` and `billing` are not.

It is a list of CATEGORIES and not of codes on purpose. A class filed under
`payments` appears the day it is seeded, where a hand-kept list of codes is the
shape `used_by` failed in — 23 sentences of 38 true the day they were typed and
wrong within weeks (`DEF-NOT-4531`).

### THE TOKEN RULE — WHAT MAKES IT SAFE RATHER THAN A TRAP

**A clerk's message is queued as ONE class, `account_message`, and rendered
against ITS palette.** A receipt's body carries `{amount}`, `{confirmation}`,
`{balance_after}` — facts only the payment that caused it holds, which this
screen cannot supply and which `rendering.validate_body` refuses **by name**. So
every token is sorted before the wording is offered:

* **inside the palette** (`{first_name}`, `{account_no}`, `{utility_name}`,
  `{service_address}` …) — LEFT STANDING, because dispatch fills them from the
  real account and a clerk should not be retyping a customer's own name;
* **outside it** — replaced with a blank line the clerk types over.

**So nothing offered can be queued into a refusal, and nothing reaches a
customer with a token printed in it.** Measured on the seeded tenant: 17
templates offered, **0 tokens outside the palette**. With the blanking removed
the test names all 16 that would have been refused — it was proved red that way,
not on a planted fault.

### WHAT ELSE THE SAME SCREENSHOT SHOWED

Two rendering faults on the same dialog, both filed:

* **`DEF-CUS-5155`** — three raw locale keys printed to the clerk
  (`common.close` and the two *Queue it* options). ⚠ **`G27` HAD BEEN RED SINCE
  THE DIALOG WAS BUILT**, naming the file and all three keys with the sentence
  *"Each renders its own key name to a user"*, and the work was pushed past it.
  Proved by running the gate in a worktree at `HEAD`. Hard-won law 7 shape 1.
  *Close* now reuses the existing shared `forms.close`; no twelfth spelling of
  one word was minted.
* **`DEF-CUS-5156`** — the footer buttons rendered as bare text. The class IS
  in the DOM, so `tsc`, eslint and any `toContain("btn")` pass over an unstyled
  element; it uses the kit's `Button` now, as `AuditLogPage` already did.

  ⚠ **THE CAUSE RECORDED HERE ON THE DAY WAS WRONG, AND IS CORRECTED THE NEXT
  MORNING BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BUILT ON IT.** It read: *"`.btn` is declared by
  `components/StateFrame.css`, imported by `StateFrame.tsx` alone — so the rule
  exists only on a page that mounts a StateFrame."* **`.btn` is loaded on every
  page.** Vite emits ONE stylesheet for the whole application — a single 164K
  `index-*.css` — so which module imports a CSS file decides nothing about
  whether its rules are live. The claim was an inference from the import graph
  that nobody checked against the build, which is the same fault CLAUDE.md
  already records against its own Tailwind paragraph: *a rule that restates what
  a tool does is a claim nothing re-checks.*

  **The true cause is narrower and more useful.** `.btn`'s base rule is
  deliberately invisible — `background: transparent`, `border: 1px solid
  transparent` — and **`CR-018` Phase 4a (2026-08-20) deleted the six variant
  rules** that painted it. Since that day the look lives only in `buttonKit`'s
  Tailwind classes, applied by the kit's `Button`. So a bare `className="btn"`
  is a **ghost button by design**, and the fault is reaching past the kit —
  B14 rule 36's clause, not rule 21's.

  **The correction changes the blast radius, which is why it mattered enough to
  chase.** The wrong cause implies a whole class of pages where a stylesheet is
  absent; the right one implies a grep. The grep was run product-wide:
  **exactly one bare-`btn` site existed**, the one the PO photographed. Two
  `btn btn-icon` sites remain and are correct — `.btn-icon` supplies the 36px
  square and the kit's own close ✕ is one of them.

## 2026-09-13 · THE THREE ACTIONS THAT END AND START A TENANCY, BUILT TO THEIR DRAWINGS (lane A, `CR-094-BRC01`, v2.260.0)

**Scope: move-out (S20), move-in (S19) and close out.** Walked in a browser at
1280 and 1440 against `04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/blueprint/` pages 66–74,
98–106 and 107–111. The step-1 record is
`04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/conformance/CR-094-laneA-ending-and-starting-service-step1.md`.

### THE JUDGMENT THAT MATTERS MOST: THE DRAWN COMMIT LABEL WAS NOT USED

The blueprint draws close-out as **two** screens. The first ends with
*"Record the close-out"* and opens `?confirm=1`; the second ends with *"Yes —
close it out"* and does it. **The second screen does not exist** (`DEF-CUS-5162`),
so one press on the first closes the account irreversibly — and closing is the
one act in this product that no correction can un-say (hard rule 4).

*"Record the close-out"* over that mechanism promises a step that is not there.
The button therefore reads **"Close out this account"**, in the danger tier.
**B14 rule 41 says the product matches the blueprint exactly; this is the case
where obeying the label would have made the screen lie**, because the label
belongs to a two-screen flow and only one screen was built. It is recorded here
rather than decided silently, and the missing screen is filed.

### AND THE SECOND: THE DRAWN `Status it takes` SELECT IS A FACT

The drawing puts a dropdown reading `Closed ▼` under *"A terminal status."*
`CloseOutRequest` does carry an optional `status`, so the control is buildable —
and `BR-CUS-055`'s statuses are **tenant-extensible** and the server already
picks that tenant's own seeded terminal one. A select here would offer this
product's guess at a tenant's vocabulary, which is the same reasoning
`MoveOutWizard` recorded when it omitted `status` from its payload. The row
keeps its drawn LABEL and states what will happen instead of pretending to
choose it.

### AND THE THIRD: FOUR DRAWN SENTENCES BREACH A SIGNED RULE, SO THEY WERE NOT COPIED

Of the six refusals the blueprint draws, four run past B14 rule 33's six-word
cap — *"Enter the date you are closing this account out."* is nine. The drawn
`IF` column is used word for word; the answer column is this product's own
wording, which `DEF-CUS-5087` wrote to that cap the day before, **and the three
live blockers read from the very same map the refusal strip uses**, so a clerk
cannot be told one thing in the reference table and another in the refusal.
Rule 41 sends a drawing that contradicts a signed rule to the PO; this one does
not need to go, because the rule already has an answer on this screen and the
answer is a day old.

### WHAT WAS SERVED ALL ALONG, AND WHAT WAS NOT

| the drawn row | where it came from |
|---|---|
| customer, customer number, category, status, address, unit, services, opened | **already served** by `GET /accounts/{id}` — the screen simply never asked (hard-won law 2) |
| case, cut date, balance | already served by the close-out preview |
| cut reason, services cut, what was owed at the cut | **on `DisconnectCase` and not on the wire.** Served now, read-only, from the case `eligibility()` had already resolved — no second query, because a second reader is a second answer to *which case is open* |
| final metered bill, base charges since | **nothing exists.** Billing has no invoices table. Stated on screen; no column invented, no dash, no `$0.00` |

### A CHECK THAT NEARLY STOPPED CHECKING, CAUGHT IN THE WRITING

Adding the drawn *When it refuses* reference table put all six refusal sentences
on the screen **whatever the server says**. The existing case asserting the live
refusal read `document.body.textContent`, so it began passing BEFORE the server
answered — and would have gone on passing if the live refusal strip stopped
rendering altogether. It asserts `[data-refusal]` now, which only the live strip
carries. **A reference list of every refusal is a hazard to every test that
looks for one**, and it is worth knowing before the next screen grows one.

### AND A SENTENCE OF MINE THAT BROKE THE RULE I WAS ENFORCING

The new rule-33 case reads each sentence off the **rendered** screen and counts
its words. It failed on its first run, on copy written in the same hour:
*"No. The meter was read at the cut."* is seven words in its second sentence. It
reads *"No. It was read at the cut."* The case asserts PRESENCE first and the cap
second, so it goes red both when a sentence leaves the screen and when one grows
— a cap asserted over a literal list is a check that cannot fail.

### THE MOVE-IN WIZARD SAID FIVE STEPS OVER A SIX-STEP RAIL

`MOVE_IN_STEPS` grew a deposit step on 2026-09-12 by PO ruling; the roll-up
quoting the count did not move with it, in all eleven languages. That is
`DEF-648`'s exact shape — the defect `BR-SHL-046` was ruled to stop — and the
sibling move-out wizard had already fixed **its own copy** of it and left this
one. Both counts are derived from the declared list now. The same commit adds
the step's NAME to the line the blueprint draws on all twelve wizard screens.

### WHAT THIS LANE DID NOT DO, AND WHY

* `DEF-CUS-5160` — both wizards put the FLOW's sentence at 32px where the
  blueprint puts the STEP's name. Five assertions in another lane's
  `MoveEntryPoints.dom.test.tsx` pin those two strings by exact text, and the
  same divergence is on **all eight** blueprint wizards, so it is a family
  decision and not two screens.
* `DEF-CUS-5161` — the shared field-visit panel tells a clerk about a MOVE-OUT
  on the move-in, the transfer and the service-request screens. It is a
  `defaultValue` in `components/`, outside this lane's files.
* `DEF-CUS-5162` — the close-out's second and third drawn screens.
* The drawn `Save & exit` in the close-out head: the act is one step with no park
  store behind it, so the control would save nothing (hard-won law 2).

## 2026-09-13 · RECORD PAYMENT ORDERS ITS FIELDS THE SAME WAY ON BOTH SCREENS

**PO ruling, put as a collision and answered: the BLUEPRINT order, on BOTH
screens.** The question shown to them, verbatim in substance: *Record payment
exists on two screens and they now order the fields differently. On 3 September
you walked the Payments screen's version and said the inputs weren't in a
logical order; that fix put "What this money is for" at the foot, next to "Apply
to". The Accounts blueprint draws it second, right under the amount — and rule 41
says the drawing decides order. Seven of eight fields match; this one doesn't.*
Answer: **second, under the amount, and change the Payments screen to match.**

### WHY IT REACHED THE PO AT ALL

Law 13's list is short, and this is its first item: **a ruling that collides with
a signed rule — the supersession must be stated, never assumed.** `DEF-3507` is
the PO's own ruling of 2026-09-03, made walking the deployed form — *"too much
text on the form and Im not sure whether inputs are arranged in logical order"* —
and B14 rule 41 is the signed rule of 2026-09-13. Deciding it in a lane would
have silently overridden one of the two.

### THE FAULT UNDERNEATH, AND IT IS LAW 2's SHAPE

⚠ **`DEF-3507`'s FIX NAMED `S22` IN ITS OWN TRACE HEADER AND NEVER REACHED
`S22`.** The account screen's twin of this form kept the shape the PO had
rejected **for ten days**, and the reason is exact: **`S35` had a field-order
test and `S22` had none.** Every check passed over the gap, because a test that
does not exist cannot fail. The fix landed, the other half of it did not — which
is hard-won law 2 running in the direction nothing watches.

### WHAT MOVED

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `S22` account screen | purpose LAST (rejected shape, ten days) | amount · **purpose** · posted · cleared · method · confirmation · apply_to · memo |
| `S35` payments screen | purpose ninth, beside apply_to at the foot | account · amount · **purpose** · posted · cleared · type · method · confirmation · apply_to · memo |

**The eight fields the two forms share are now in identical relative order.**
`S35`'s two extras — the account search at the front and the tender kind leading
the group it governs — are this screen's alone.

`DEF-3507`'s coarse/fine reasoning (purpose is *which position*, apply_to is
*which bills*, so keep them adjacent) is **deliberately given up**: a clerk
answers *what is this money for* while the amount is still under their hand, and
`apply_to` moves up beside the bills it names.

### PROOF

The `S35` edit is a **pure reorder — 0 lines lost, 0 added**, verified as a
multiset of lines against the tip rather than by reading a diff. The file was
**re-derived from the pinned tip** and both moves re-applied, because a
hand-splice had left a `<SelectField` opening tag behind and produced JSX that
did not parse. `recordFormOrder.dom.test.tsx` — the file that pinned the
September order — now pins this one, with the supersession written into it, and
was **proved red against the tip in a worktree** before being trusted green.
**336 payments cases pass.**

⚠ **NO VERSION IS TAKEN HERE.** Two lanes were mid-bump on `package.json` when
this landed (tip `2.260.0`, working tree `2.261.0`), and writing a third number
into a contested file is the collision law 11 exists to prevent. The next version
to ship carries this change.

## 2026-09-13 · THE DIALOG CHECK WALKED A LIST IT HAD TYPED ITSELF

`10-scripts/render-checks/account-dialog-fit.mjs` was written this morning to
catch a dialog taller than its window. It did — three of them. **It also spent
the rest of the day reporting a pass over a scope it silently excluded**, and
the lane that found it was not its author.

Lane D added a ninth dialog (`Change unit`) and reported, in its own words:
*"it walks a hardcoded list and my new dialog is not in it, so that zero says
nothing about it"*. The check printed **`0 findings over 14 frames`** while never
opening the new dialog at all — and it printed that sentence directly beneath a
header quoting hard-won law 7 at length. **A file citing the law committed the
thing the law names.**

### THE FIX IS THE CAUSE, NOT THE SYMPTOM

Adding a tenth row to the list would have bought one day. The controls are now
**DISCOVERED FROM THE RENDERED PAGE** — the page head's action row, the icon
rail, and every pencil on an Overview group — so a dialog added tomorrow is
measured tomorrow with nobody remembering to edit this file. Measured coverage
went from **14 frames to 25**, and `Change unit` came in at **683px**, matching
the figure Lane D had taken by hand.

**A DISABLED control is reported as SKIPPED with the reason it carries**, never
counted as a pass: a greyed pencil and an unchecked dialog must not look the same
in the output. The run now prints 25 measured and 37 skipped, each skip naming
its own refusal — *"Meters are changed in Assets."*, *"A credit needs an issued
bill."* — which is the difference between a check that is quiet and a check that
is empty.

### THREE FAULTS IN THE CHECK ITSELF, EACH FOUND BY RUNNING IT

1. **It enumerated the controls on the LIST page**, because `firstAccountPath`
   leaves the browser on `/accounts` and the discovery ran before the navigation.
   It found three buttons and reported *"2 frames, 0 findings"* — a pass over
   almost nothing, exactly the shape it was being rewritten to cure.
2. **Tabs are `<button>` too.** Clicking one moves the screen instead of opening
   a dialog, and the next measurement would have been of the wrong page. Excluded
   by `role="tab"`.
3. The selector `.page-header-actions` is a **stylesheet class, not a data
   hook**, because that is what the shared page header actually draws. If it is
   renamed this check finds nothing and **says so** — the zero-guard added on the
   first version (*"NOTHING WAS MEASURED — this is not a pass"*) fired on run one
   and is what stopped a false green.

### WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT THE REST

⚠ **THE CENSUS COVERS ONE SCREEN OF NINETEEN.** `drawn/*.json` holds twelve
files and all twelve are TABS OF THE ACCOUNT DETAIL. **No wizard has a
drawn-as-data spec**, so for eighteen of the nineteen Accounts screens *"matches
the blueprint"* means a lane quoted the drawing and looked at a browser. That is
discipline, not a gate — and B14 rule 41's own status cell says RATIFIED and
UNENFORCED for exactly this reason. It is why the move-in wizard could say *five
steps* over a six-step rail, in eleven languages, for a day.

## 2026-09-13 · A SCREEN IS BUILT FROM THE PICTURE, NOT FROM THE TEXT (B14 RULE 42)

**PO ruling, verbatim:**

> *"When you use images to create screens your accuracy is higher; hence dont
> create screens using only Text"*

and, put to them as *should this be a law*:

> *"so we should have a law screen should be done using images only"*

**RATIFIED as B14 rule 42.** It is **rule 41's METHOD**: 41 says the product
matches the blueprint, 42 says how a lane is permitted to read the blueprint.
Render the pages and LOOK at them; the extracted markdown under a module's
`blueprint/` folder is an INDEX — find your page, check a spelling — and is
never the specification.

### THE REPO PROVED IT BEFORE THE RULING EXISTED

`CR-094`'s own step-1 record reads *"54 pages read as IMAGES at scale 2, never
from the text layer"*, and a second says *"prose quoted from the text layer"* is
the unreliable half. **The wireframes are VECTOR ART**, so an extractor returns
the labels and silently drops everything DRAWN rather than written: which fields
sit side by side versus stacked, what is a table and what is a list of facts,
column widths, alignment, grouping, emphasis, which column a block is in, where a
control sits inside its heading.

⚠ **AND IT LOSES SCREEN BOUNDARIES.** In the Accounts blueprint the extractor
gives screens **09 and 10 the same starting page**, and **16 and 17 the same** —
it could not tell where one screen ends and the next begins. A lane reading only
text cannot know that. A lane looking at the page sees it in a second.

### WHERE IT LANDED, AND WHY NOT IN CLAUDE.md AS PROSE

**Three places, one commit**, each doing a different job:

| where | why |
|---|---|
| **B14 rule 42** | this is where binding UI law lives; a "law" in this repo means a numbered B14 rule with a status cell |
| **`react-tailwind-css-ui-generator` §1.1** | the file a lane actually opens at build time, with the exact commands |
| **CLAUDE.md's B14 pointer** | moved from THIRTY-TWO to THIRTY-THREE **in the same commit as the rule** |

⚠ **THE POINTER MOVED WITH THE RULE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF RECORDING IT
HERE.** That line has been wrong **six times**, always in the same direction,
because ratifying a rule and updating the pointer are two acts and only the
first feels like the work. This is the third consecutive time it has moved in
the same commit. ⚠ **AND THE COUNT WAS RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE TABLE RATHER
THAN INCREMENTED:** a first count returned **41 rows** and looked like a
mismatch; B14 holds **33 DISTINCT rules** (1–21, 31–42) and four of them appear
three times each, as rows in other tables further down the file. *Count the
table, never trust a number in a pointer, including this one.*

**It is NOT written into CLAUDE.md as a paragraph, deliberately.** That file's
own instruction says *"where a rule restates what a tool does, name the tool and
let a reader run it"* — a prose description of how to render a PDF is a claim
nothing re-checks, and it outlives the behaviour it describes.

### HOW, IN THIS CONTAINER

```bash
git show "origin/<default-branch>:05-prototype/<name>.pdf" > /tmp/x.pdf
mkdir -p <out>                                          # the script does NOT create it
python3 10-scripts/pdf/pdf_render.py /tmp/x.pdf <out> 2 60,61,62
```
Scale 2 is 2448x1584; scale 4 for a dense table. Then open each PNG with the Read
tool. `pdftoppm`, `PIL` and `pypdf` all fail in this container and
`10-scripts/pdf/README.md` says why — which is why those two scripts exist.

⚠ **THE BLUEPRINT PDFs LIVE ON THE DEFAULT BRANCH, NOT ON A WORKING BRANCH.**
Six of them, including an Assets blueprint nobody had counted. **A lane reporting
"the drawing is not in the repo" has looked at one branch** — said on 2026-09-13,
corrected by the PO the same hour.

### APPLIED IMMEDIATELY, NOT ONLY WRITTEN DOWN

Three lanes were building screens from extracted text when this was ruled. Each
was stopped mid-flight, given the rendered PDF, its own page span, and the
instruction to re-check work already done against the images and treat any
difference as the image being right.

### THE GAP THIS EXPOSES

Rule 42 is **UNENFORCED and deliberately so — no check can tell whether a person
looked at a picture.** What is mechanical is rule 41's conformance census, and
**it covers twelve tabs of ONE screen. No wizard has a drawn-as-data spec.** So
for eighteen of the nineteen Accounts screens, "matches the blueprint" rests on a
lane's discipline and on nothing that re-runs afterwards.

## 2026-09-13 · THE TEN ASSETS CAPABILITIES, RULED ONE BY ONE — AND TWO OF THE TEN CHANGED SHAPE

**PO ruling, verbatim, answering a numbered list of the ten capabilities `CR-092-BRC01`
§6b put into scope:**

> ***"1. Inherit from Unit, premises, 2. Yes - create an entry in read resgiter 3. Bult
> it, 4 bulit it, 5. Built it 6. But it, 7. buit it, 8 buil ti 9 built it; 10 buit it"***

The list they were answering, in order: `AST-B-12` · `AST-B-14` · `AST-B-16` ·
`AST-B-19` · `AST-B-24` · `AST-B-21` · `AST-B-22` · `AST-B-25` · `AST-B-27` ·
`AST-B-28`. **Items 3–10 are "build it" and carry no change of shape.** Items 1 and 2
do, and they are the reason this entry exists rather than a line in a status report.

### 1 · `AST-B-12` — AN ASSET INHERITS ITS ADDRESS. IT NEVER HOLDS ONE.

The capability was written down as *"an edit address for an asset"*, and **that phrasing
invited exactly the change hard rule 8 forbids.** The ruling settles it: the address is
**inherited from the Unit and the Premises**, so the edit surface SHOWS a place by
walking `asset → assignment.unit → premises` and **writes nothing of its own**.

**This CONFIRMS `BR-MET-1161` (PO 2026-09-04) rather than bending it** — *"we are having
addresses at one place now - Premises and Units -> then they flow to {Meters, Sub meter,
assets} + {accounts}"*. Assets was already named in that ruling as a place addresses
*flow to*; this says the same thing again from the Assets side, after a capability
description made it look optional.

**Measured on this branch before the ruling was written down, so it is a confirmation
and not a hope:** `06-backend/apps/assets/models.py::Asset` declares **no** `city`,
`address`, `postal`, `state` or `street` column. It reaches a place two ways, both
cross-module FKs in the reviewed set — `service_point` (→ metering) and
`AssetAssignment.unit` (→ metering units). `location_note` (`models.TextField`, ≤280) is
a note about where to find the device, **not an address**, and the blueprint's own
screen 30 says so in its Words row: *"Location note, not address — the address lives on
the premises and is walked to (hard rule 8)."*

⚠ **AND THE BLUEPRINT ITSELF NAMED THIS DOOR AS UNGUARDED.** Its appendix F (assumptions
the document makes and never states, p192) records that an `assets.city` *"would break
it and nothing here would object"*. **`G85` is what objects** — its `HOMES` map carries
exactly three homes and fails a fourth. The ruling closes the door by name; the gate is
what keeps it closed.

**So the work in `AST-B-12` is a READ and a route, never a column.** A lane that adds an
address field to the asset edit page has reversed a ruling, not implemented one.

### 2 · `AST-B-14` — THE OPENING READ IS A REAL READ, NOT A REMEMBERED NUMBER

> ***"Yes - create an entry in read resgiter"***

The opening read captured on Add-an-asset step 2 **writes a row into the read register**.
It is not a value stored on the asset and displayed back, and it is not a draft note.

**This is the shape the product already has at the other end of the asset's life**, which
is why it is buildable without a new interface: the retire flow's *Final read + date*
is written to `meter_reads` on commit, and the blueprint records that path as owned
`assets → metering ⇄`. Its section on that flow says as much — *"already commits a manual
read inside the caller's transaction and refuses the whole operation when it cannot; this
is that, at the other end of the asset's life."*

⚠ **IT IS A CROSS-MODULE WRITE, WHICH CLAUDE.md FORBIDS OUTRIGHT — SO IT GOES THROUGH THE
SEAM THAT ALREADY CARRIES THE FINAL READ, AND A LANE DOES NOT OPEN A SECOND ONE.** The
rule is *"Cross-module writes are forbidden; cross-module FKs are the reviewed interface
set (B2 §2)"*. The retire path is the reviewed precedent; the opening read joins it.
**If the read cannot be committed, the whole create is refused** — the same
all-or-nothing the retire path already applies, because an asset that exists with a
missing opening read is worse than one that was never created.

⚠ **AND IT IS A MOVE, NOT AN ADDITION.** The PO's earlier ruling on this same capability
(2026-09-12) was *"Build it as drawn — move it to step 2"*, and it applies to
`MeasuringSpecStep` **only**, never `DeviceSpecStep`: a device has no register and no
multiplier, so there is nothing for an opening read to mean.

### WHAT THIS ENTRY IS FOR

Both rulings arrived as a single line of chat answering a numbered list. Neither would
survive the session. **Item 1 in particular reads as a small clarification and is not
one** — it is the difference between deriving an address and storing a second copy of
one, which is the failure `BR-MET-1161` was ruled to end and which `G85` exists to
refuse. Written down before any lane builds against it, per step W and hard-won law 9.

⚠ **AND IT MUST NOT BE ASKED AGAIN (law 13).** All ten of these were already approved on
2026-09-12 and re-put to the PO on 2026-09-13 as a table. That re-ask is the bug law 13
names; it cost the PO an answer they had already given. What it bought — two changes of
shape that the 2026-09-12 approval did not carry — does not make the re-ask correct, and
the rulings above are now the record so it cannot happen a third time.
## 2026-09-14 · METER READS — THE NINE STEP-1 QUESTIONS, RULED

**All nine were put to the PO in one table with both sides quoted and a recommendation
each, and all nine came back in one reply.** They are written here before any of them is
built on, per step W and hard-won law 9 — and because `CR-096-BRC02` exists precisely
because nineteen earlier Meter Reads rulings were left inside a PDF and reached no file.

### Q1 · `BR-MET-011` is NARROWED, not broken

> ***"Narrow it. Sound distinction — but stated by the document, not by you"***

`BR-MET-011` reads *"S26/S27 are read-only operational views; **all CRUD in Settings**"*. It
now means **all CRUD of a cycle's DEFINITION** — its frequency, start day and window length
stay in Settings. **The reading WORK is writable on the operational screen.**

⚠ **THE PO'S OWN WORDS CARRY THE REASON THIS IS RECORDED AND NOT JUST APPLIED:** the
narrowing had been *"stated by the document, not by you"*. A specification that quietly
reinterprets a CONFIRMED rule is a rule change wearing a drawing's clothes; it is a ruling
now, with this date on it.

### Q2 · The cross-module write is DEFERRED, and the trigger is named

> ***"we will create work mobile app and then these reads are push to mobile app - until
> then defer in case you have a seam just update it and write in table"***

**`Send someone out` on the cycle detail is NOT built.** The work reaches a technician
through a **Work mobile app** that does not exist yet; reads are pushed to it when it does.

**What was done about the seam, stated because the PO asked to be told:** the seam
MECHANISM exists and metering already uses it — `apps/metering/seams.py` reaches Work
through `resolve("work", …)` for `CR-077`'s three parts doors, and Assets raises its own
work through `apps.work.asset_door`. **What does not exist is a door for raising a visit
from a read or a cycle, and one was NOT added.** Adding a door is building the
cross-module write, not deferring it.

⚠ **AND NO DISABLED CONTROL WAS SHIPPED EITHER, DELIBERATELY.** Hard-won law 2's mirror is
a live screen behind a dead control, and a hold with a clock in it rots silently — on
2026-09-05 the customer portal had two working doors out of eight for exactly this reason.
A button reading *"opens with the mobile app"* would be that, with no test to fire when the
app lands. **The control is absent until the mobile app is real**, and this row is the
record of why.

### Q3 · A walk is reordered in Settings only

> ***"Settings only"***

`BR-MET-011` holds for route configuration. **This costs nothing to honour**: Settings'
own `RouteDetailPage.tsx:214` already writes the order through `saveRoutePremisesOrder`, so
read-only-in-Reads is today's behaviour. The blueprint's entry 21 draws it read-only with
`Manage in Settings →`, which is now ruled rather than assumed.

### Q4 · The window fork is settled BEFORE anything is built on it

> ***"Settle first."***

Two derivations of *"the current window"* give different answers — measured on one day, the
cycle row printed **August** while the completeness engine answered **September**. Entry
15's ④ and ⑤ are **not built** until that is one answer.

⚠ **THE DRAWING CALLS IT *"a filed backend disagreement"* AND THE FILED ROW DOES NOT
EXIST.** Searched the defect register for *two derivations*, *current window*, *window
disagree* and every chase/completeness row, and the open-question register for *window*
narrowed to cycle/completeness. The only *two derivations* row is `DEF-139`, which is the
ledger's balance against payments'. **A blocker nobody can name is a blocker nobody will
honour**, so it is being filed rather than cited.

### Q5 · `MR-17` — what it is, and the PO asked

> ***"What is it?"***

**A read-batch supervisor co-sign.** When a tenant switches it on, committing a read batch
blocks until a second person — System Admin or Executive — co-signs. `OQ-042` is **CLOSED**
and rules it verbatim: *"optional toggle default ON; supervisor = SysAdmin/Executive;
blocks when enabled (PO R6)"*. **The writer is already built** (`services.py:7994`,
`@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN, EXECUTIVE)`); its own comment records that the BLOCKING half
was deferred to a screen lane. What remains is the block and the screen.

⚠ **AND ITS DEFECT ROW IS CLOSED THE OTHER WAY:** `DEF-815` reads **`wontfix`**, so
building it reverses that row. **Left unbuilt pending the PO's answer** — the question was
put back to them and is not decided here.

⚠ **ONE FACT THE PO SHOULD HAVE WITH IT, BECAUSE IT IS THE ICP's OWN:** this product is run
by **10–20 staff, and at the bottom tier by one or two**. `OQ-WRK-1492` was ruled on exactly
that ground — *"clark can do it sicne it s a day to day work"*, because *"a two-person
utility has no supervisor sitting by the screen"*. **A co-sign nobody present can give is a
commit that does not happen.**

### Q6 · A control is removed only when its refusal is PERMANENT

> ***"Narrow it — but write it down, because today's product obeys the ruling that is in
> the repo"***

The ruling of **2026-09-10** — *"keep all buttons on screen"*, *"keep all icon only disable
them"* — stands, and is **narrowed**: a control whose refusal is a **STATE** is disabled
with its reason; a control whose refusal is **PERMANENT** is removed. The Estimate button
on a committed reading is the second kind.

⚠ **THE PO'S OWN CLAUSE IS THE IMPORTANT HALF:** *"today's product obeys the ruling that is
in the repo"*. The as-built is correct against the older rule, so this narrowing is a
CHANGE to working behaviour and not a defect fix — and it had to be written down before a
lane could act on it, which is the whole of why this entry exists.

### Q7 · The wrong-register trap is FIRST

> ***"Put this first. DEF-797 already cost 412 kW billed as 14 kWh — $154 against
> $4,532. Money path, so I'm not classifying it"***

A reading recorded against the wrong register is **permanent**: `supersede_read` takes only
a value and a reason, and migration `0007`'s trigger freezes the channel. On a demand plan
the units differ, which is how `DEF-797` happened.

**The PO declined to classify it and said so — that is the correct move and it binds the
build.** B4/B5 are ❄️ FROZEN and move only by a finance re-sign (HUMAN-GUIDE §6), never by
an inline edit. **Nothing here may choose a rounding, a unit or an estimate.** The four
shapes the blueprint puts on the table remain unchosen; what is ruled is the ORDER — this
is the first thing the module does.

### Q8 · A completed wizard step shows its NUMBER

> ***"numbers"***

B14 rule 3's numbered rail wins over the drawn ✓. **Seven wizards move either way**, so
this is a product-wide answer and not a Reads one.

### Q9 · A reading displays AS DRAWN

> ***"as drawn"***

`45910`, not `45910.000000`. No signed rule covered it — hard rule 2's *display 2* governs
**money and percentages**, not consumption, and hard rule 3 is already satisfied because
the unit is always present or its absence is stated. ⚠ **This is a DISPLAY ruling only.**
The stored value is untouched; nothing about what is written to `meter_reads` changes.

### What this entry is for

Nine rulings arrived in one reply to one table. **Six of them change what gets built, two
narrow a CONFIRMED rule, and one (Q7) is a money path the PO deliberately declined to
classify.** None of them would have survived the session. The module they belong to already
has nineteen rulings trapped inside a PDF and reaching no file — which is the defect
`CR-096-BRC02` exists to stop repeating, and repeating it in the same session would have
been the worst possible answer to it.

## 2026-09-14 · A BLUEPRINT'S OWN `R` INSTRUCTIONS ARE DISCHARGED BY THE DRAWING

> **PO, verbatim:** ***"these instructions were to create the blueprint documents those are
> resolved"***

Asked whether `R4` — *"in detail section use Panel to information groups"* — should be
ratified into **B14** (product-wide) or kept scoped to Meter Reads, the PO answered neither.
**The `R` rows are instructions the PO gave WHILE THE BLUEPRINT WAS BEING DRAWN, and the
blueprint is what discharged them.**

### What this settles, and it is a general rule for every blueprint

**`R1`–`R9` are NOT transcribed into B14 or into a module's business rules as new rows.**
They are already in the drawing — which, under **B14 rule 41**, IS the specification, and
under **rule 42** is read as an image. A screen built to the drawing implements `R3`, `R4`,
`R5` and `R8` **by construction**, because the drawing is what they changed.

⚠ **AND COPYING THEM OUT WOULD BREAK HARD-WON LAW 5 — one source, never a second copy free
to drift.** A B14 rule reading *"detail sections use `Panel`"* and a drawing showing a Panel
are two statements of one fact, and the day they disagree nothing can say which is current.
**The drawing wins because the drawing is the source.**

### The residue, which is NOT discharged and is the reason this entry is long

**An instruction that only changed the DRAWING is resolved. An instruction that REVERSED A
SIGNED RULE left that rule sitting in the repo still saying the opposite** — and a lane
reads the repo, not the PDF. Two rows were stamped in the same commit as this entry:

| Rule | Was | Now | Why it could not be left |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`BR-MET-060`** | **CONFIRMED** — *"Reads screen opens on **Needs attention**"* | **SUPERSEDED 2026-09-12** by `R1` (*"Need Attention — does not add any value"*) | The drawing opens Reads on the readings. **A CONFIRMED rule saying the opposite is how a later lane rebuilds the tab** — and `ReadsListPage.tsx:24` already states the superseded rule in its own words |
| **`BR-MET-011`** | **CONFIRMED** — *"all CRUD in Settings"* | **CONFIRMED-AS-NARROWED 2026-09-14** (step-1 Q1) | *"All CRUD"* now means all CRUD of a cycle's DEFINITION; the reading WORK is writable on the operational screen |

`R2`'s collision with `BR-MET-011`'s S26/S27 split, and `R1`'s retirement of `US-MET-019`,
are carried by **`CR-096-BRC02`**, which already held those chains before this ruling.

### The test this leaves behind

**Ask of every `R` row: did it change the DRAWING, or did it change a RULE THE REPO STILL
STATES?** The first is resolved by the blueprint existing. **The second is a supersession
that must be stamped before the screen is built, or the product and the repo will contradict
each other with both sides signed.** That is step W's timing rule — before the thing that
depends on it — and it is the whole of what this ruling leaves for us to do.

## 2026-09-14 · NO SECOND SIGNATURE — `MR-17` IS WITHDRAWN, AND `OQ-042`'s CLOSURE IS REVERSED

> **PO, verbatim:** ***"we do not need confirmation or sign off from another person"***

Said of **`MR-17`**, the read-batch supervisor co-sign, after it was reported as not-built with
its reasoning. **It is a statement about second signatures, not about reads**, and it reaches
further than the one specification.

### ⚠ THIS REVERSES A CLOSED QUESTION, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WRITTEN OUT IN FULL

`OQ-042` was **CLOSED** with the opposite answer — *"optional toggle default ON; supervisor =
SysAdmin/Executive; blocks when enabled (PO R6)"*. That closure said the co-sign **EXISTS and
BLOCKS**. It does not. The row is now stamped **SUPERSEDED 2026-09-14**.

**`DEF-815`'s `wontfix` is therefore correct BY RULING rather than by default** — and the
difference matters, because the earlier reasoning for leaving it alone was *"building it
reverses a closed row"*, which is a procedural objection anyone could have argued past. This
is a decision.

### What was found in the code, and what was done about it

| | |
|---|---|
| `cosign_read_batch` | **Built** at `06-backend/apps/metering/services.py:7994`, `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN, EXECUTIVE)` |
| Callers | **NONE — it has never had one.** Migration `0037`'s own docstring says so: *"A signature with no [caller]…"* |
| The blocking half | **Never built.** `DEF-815` carried it |
| Columns | `cosigned_by` (migration `0003`), `cosigned_at` (migration `0037`) |

**The writer is left in place and annotated, not deleted.** Its columns stay as lawful empty
containers; dropping them is a migration on a live table and is not this ruling's scope.
⚠ **What WAS changed is the comment block above it**, which told the next reader the blocking
half was *deferred* — a body that contradicts its own status is exactly the rot that sent
three lanes wrong on 2026-09-05 (`DEF-WRK-4030`). It now says the door is closed by ruling.

### The reasoning is the ICP's own, and it was already on the record

`OQ-WRK-1492` was ruled on precisely this ground — *"clark can do it sicne it s a day to day
work"*, because *"a two-person utility has no supervisor sitting by the screen"*. This product
is run by **10–20 staff, and at the bottom tier by one or two**. **A co-sign nobody present
can give is a commit that does not happen.**

### ⚠ THE KNOCK-ON, WHICH IS THE PART A LANE WOULD HAVE MISSED

**`OQ-042`'s closure is CITED AS PRECEDENT by an open question in another module.**
`OQ-CUS-12355` — may a billing clerk RAISE a unit correction for a supervisor to approve —
quotes it verbatim for *"supervisor = SysAdmin/Executive"* and offers three options.

**This ruling forecloses option (b)** — *clerk raises it, a supervisor approves it later* —
because a pending row waiting for a second person's approval is exactly what *"we do not need
confirmation or sign off from another person"* rules out. **The question is now (a) against
(c) and it is LEFT OPEN**: choosing between them is picking a value on something the PO has
not been asked, which the prime directive forbids. The row carries that note now, and it also
carries the warning not to quote the superseded half again.

**A4's signed grid (`BR-IDN-014`) is untouched** — it still gives `Approve` to System Admin
and Executive. What is ruled out is a SECOND person having to act, not who may act.

## 2026-09-14 · `Q2` REVERSED THE SAME DAY — THE READS→WORK DOOR IS BUILT, NOT DEFERRED

> **PO, verbatim:** ***"please build this"***, quoting back the paragraph that reported
> the door as deliberately not built.

**This overturns the `Q2` row recorded earlier today**, which read *"The cross-module write
is DEFERRED to a Work mobile app"* and *"no door for raising a visit from a read was added,
and one was NOT added"*. **A clerk can now send someone out from a reading.** The mobile app
is no longer the precondition; the door goes in ahead of it.

⚠ **BOTH ENTRIES STAND, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** The earlier row is not edited away. A
reader who finds only the reversal cannot tell whether the deferral was ever considered, and
the whole reason `CR-096-BRC02` exists is that a chain of rulings went unrecorded. The
supersession is stated here, in the later row, where the convention already puts it.

### What this does NOT change, and it is most of the reasoning

The earlier row gave two reasons for not shipping a control. **The second one survives
untouched:** no greyed-out *"opens with the mobile app"* button was shipped, and none will
be — that is a hold with a clock in it, which on 2026-09-05 left the customer portal with
**two working doors out of eight**. What changed is that the control is now LIVE rather than
absent. **At no point does a disabled button pointing at an unbuilt thing become the answer.**

### The architecture was already decided; this ruling does not get to choose one

`06-backend/apps/work/from_flows.py` is **ONE RAISE SERVICE, FIVE CALLERS** — service
request, move out, move in, transfer, reconnect. **A reading is the sixth caller**, not a
sixth mechanism. Its three standing rules bind this build:

1. **THE RAISE IS OFFERED, NEVER AUTOMATIC.** `propose()` writes nothing; `raise_for()`
   writes only what a person ticked. ⚠ **A flagged reading must never raise a visit by
   itself** — the file's own words: *"a flow that raised jobs on its own would put a crew in
   a van because somebody pressed Close account."*
2. **A FAILED RAISE NEVER FAILS THE FLOW** (`BR-WRK-055`). **A reading stays recordable when
   no visit can be booked.** The alternative is a field module able to block a meter read.
3. **NO NEW ANCHOR COLUMN AND NO NEW CROSS-MODULE FK.** A reading walks meter → connection
   → premises, and `create_work_order` already takes that anchor. The link back is
   `source_ref`, free text.

**The boundary is kept the sanctioned way, not bypassed:** `apps/work/seams/metering_seam.py`
already carries `raise_work_order(actor, payload)`, which calls metering's own
`create_work_order` **by name**, so the owning module applies its numbering, its audit row
and its refusals. `G78` fails a foreign write.

### ⚠ One trap, named here because the code already paid for it once

`BR-WRK-024` says every order carries its source, and `WORK_ORDER_SOURCES` is a **closed
vocabulary** that `ck_work_orders_source` enforces **in the database**. A token the tuple
does not hold is accepted by Python and **refused by PostgreSQL inside the transaction**.

`connections.py:544-568` warns, in bold, **"IT IS NOT `dispatcher`"** — the nearest existing
token is what a lane in a hurry reaches for, and a visit filed as *raised by a dispatcher*
**vanishes from `EP-WRK-10`'s first-time-fix report, the one report that measures failures.**
If no existing token means *a reading needs a visit*, one is ADDED, following `metering/0052`:
the CHECK is dropped and rebuilt, because **adding a token refuses nothing that worked
yesterday** whereas a constraint disagreeing with the tuple is *"the one outcome nobody could
debug."*

### And no approval step

Ruled the same day: *"we do not need confirmation or sign off from another person."* Nothing
in this door waits for a second signature.

| **No BACKEND caller** | **TRUE** — `commit_read_batch` does not consult it |
| **No FRONT-END caller** | ⛔ **FALSE.** `<CosignPanel …>` is **MOUNTED IN PRODUCTION CODE** at `UploadReadsWizard.tsx:2319`, and `cosignReadBatch(batch.id, client)` is **called** at `:3264` |
| The component | `readsImportRail.tsx:542` |
| What a clerk SEES | A panel headed **"Supervisor co-sign"** with a button **"Co-sign this batch"** |

**It is OPTIONAL and does not hold the post today** — the server answers
`cosign_blocks_post: false` and the panel says so: *"Optional. A co-sign records a second
review; it does not hold the post."* **A `required` string also exists** — *"This batch must
be co-signed before it can be posted."* — and renders if that flag ever turns true.

### ⚠ HOW THE ERROR WAS MADE, BECAUSE THE METHOD IS THE LESSON

The check was `grep -rn "cosign\|supervisor" 07-frontend/src … | head -8`. **`head -8`
truncated the result before it reached `readsImportRail.tsx` and `UploadReadsWizard.tsx`**,
which sort after `api/` and `components/`. The command returned three irrelevant hits and I
read that as "the front end does not call it."

**This is hard-won law 7's *reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes*, committed by
the person auditing others for it in the same session.** A truncated search is not a search.
**When the question is "does ANYTHING call this", never pipe the answer through `head`** —
use `-l` for the file list, or count.

### What it means for the ruling

The PO ruled *"we do not need confirmation or sign off from another person"* **believing
nothing was built.** The ruling's INTENT is unambiguous, but removing a live, working,
clerk-facing panel is a different act from declining to build one, and the PO has not been
asked that question. **NOTHING WAS REMOVED ON THIS ROW'S AUTHORITY.** The discrepancy is
being put back to them with the facts corrected. `MR-17` — the BLOCKING half — remains
withdrawn either way; that half was never built and this changes nothing about it.

### A second, smaller correction in the same breath

The step-2 lane brief told five lanes that **B14 rule 3 forbids hardcoding a step count.**
**Rule 3 contains no such clause.** Counted and read: *"Steppers. Any flow with 2+ stages
uses the numbered step rail (clickable when complete) + a wizard-actions footer. Single
forms never fake a stepper."* The derive-the-count practice is sound engineering and it is
**NOT SIGNED LAW**, and citing it as such is inventing a rule. Found by the upload-wizard
lane, which counted B14's status table itself — **33 rules** — rather than trusting the
brief, which is exactly what the brief had by then been corrected to tell it to do.

## 2026-09-14 · METER READS ENTRY 02 — THREE JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT DECIDE

The reads list was rebuilt to the blueprint's entry 02 (`MR-26` · `MR-27` · `MR-31`,
and `MR-04`'s screen half). Most of it was ruled: `BR-MET-060` is SUPERSEDED and
the drawing settles the rest. **Three things it did not settle are recorded here
rather than left in a diff**, because each one reaches beyond the screen that
raised it.

### 1 · `Channel` → `Register` was relabelled EVERYWHERE, not only on S25

The blueprint relabels the reads list's column and its filter. **The same
catalogue key is also read by the upload wizard's staged-rows table and by the
unit's assets panel**, so relabelling only S25 would have left one product
calling one thing by two names — the drift `B14 rule 34` exists to stop, and the
blueprint's own reason for the change (*"one word for one thing, and Register is
the clerk's"*) argues against a per-screen fix more strongly than for one.

So the **value** moved in all eleven catalogues and the **key** did not:
`metering.reads.col.channel` still names `meter_reads.channel`, which is the fact
a developer needs, and `Register` is what a clerk reads. Two screens outside
entry 02 change one word as a consequence; nothing else about them moves.

**Why it is worth a row:** a lane auditing the upload wizard against its own
blueprint will find a word it did not change, and this is where it finds out who
changed it and why.

### 2 · The `Read cycles` tab mounts the screen that already existed

Entry 02 draws a second tab; **entry 15 redraws what is inside it**, and entry 15
is a separate piece of work with its own commitments and one blocked on
`DEF-MET-5206`. The tab was still built, pointing at `CyclesOpsPage` exactly as
it stands today.

**The reasoning is hard-won law 2's mirror.** `/:tenant/reads/cycles` has been
routed and built since `CR-006` with nothing in the product linking to it — a
live screen behind no control at all, which is the shape that left the customer
portal with two working doors out of eight. A tab pointing at a real screen is
the defect closed; a half-built table is not an improvement on a whole one, and
a tab held back until entry 15 lands would be a hold with a clock in it.

### 3 · The column picker still lists `Select`, and the drawing does not

The drawn Columns panel holds exactly fifteen entries — the fifteen data columns —
and **no `Select` row**, while the shared picker lists every declared column and
therefore lists the selection checkbox. It does so on **every bulk-select list in
the product**, not only here.

**Not changed, deliberately.** `B14 rule 14` says only *"▦ opens show/hide with
reorder and Reset"* and names no contents, so this is HOW the control is built
rather than what the screen contains — `rule 38`'s split, where the UI rules win
and a drawing does not get to change every list in the product on one screen's
authority. It is a one-line kit change if somebody wants it, and it should be
made as its own decision rather than as a side effect of this screen.

### And one thing was NOT built, with its row

**`MR-27`'s `Plan` column is not built** — `DEF-MET-5209`. It is specified to read
*"the stored `plan_registers` outcome"* and the commitment says it waits on
nothing, but that outcome carries only `plan_id` — a uuid — and `plan_model`, and
no served field names the plan. Drawing it would breach **`B14 rule 31`**, the
rule this same entry invokes for the `Batch` column two lines earlier. That is
`rule 41`'s own carve-out — a drawing contradicting a signed rule — so it is
filed and put to the PO rather than resolved by choosing what the column means.
