## 2026-09-14 — METER READS ENTRY 21, *A ROUTE, THE DETAIL*: FOUR JUDGMENTS, AND THE ONE THING THAT REACHES THE PO

**The ruling this screen is built from** (PO, 2026-09-13, verbatim): *"in this
Route Tab — what if User click on Route link — we will have to give a details
view of Route. this view should be similar to details view of Cycle. in Cycle
you will need to add a tab — all reads and same in route details also."*
**Option A** was chosen: the page gets **its own address with the window in the
header**, `/{tenant}/reads/routes/{routeId}?window=YYYY-MM`, rather than nesting
under the cycle. The reason is load-bearing and is not a preference — **a route
can be walked on more than one cycle**, so *"0 of 11 collected"* has no
denominator until a window is named.

### 1 · The route link on S26 now opens the OPERATIONAL detail, not Settings

`RoutesCyclesPage.tsx`'s route code has pointed at `SET-06D`
(`/settings/reference-data/routes-cycles/routes/{id}`) since `CR-029` RC-W3-T6.
The ruling above is about *"click on Route link"*, so it moves. **The route's
DEFINITION is still Settings' and nothing about `BR-MET-011` changes** — the
page head's own *"Manage in Settings →"* and the new screen's `The walk` panel
both carry the door to it. `RoutesCyclesPage.test.tsx`'s assertion was AMENDED
in place with the ruling quoted, not deleted, so the supersession is where the
next reader meets it.

### 2 · `REGISTERS COLLECTED · 0 of 11` is built as `REGISTERS SHORT` — `DEF-MET-5217`

The drawing's first Collection figure needs a **route-scoped expected-register
count** and **no endpoint serves one**: `completeness.cycle_coverage` computes
`expected_channels` per meter and `chase_list` drops it; `GET /routes/{id}`
answers meter COUNTS; `read_windows` carries `collected`/`expected` but only for
windows that have been **closed**, so the open window a clerk is working has no
row at all. The tile therefore states the number that IS served, route-scoped
and window-scoped, and is the one a supervisor acts on. **The alternative was to
invent a denominator**, which is the thing `collected_read_count`'s own docstring
refuses in as many words: *"the tab renders '—', never a fabricated 0"*.

### 3 · No *Send someone out* and no *Estimate these*, so no tick column

Both are drawn on the Still-to-read bulk bar and both are **deliberately absent**.

* ***Send someone out*** — `BR-WRK-055` requires metering's own disposition to be
  written BEFORE anything is raised, and a chase row is **derived**: it carries
  `id: null` and there is no record to write a disposition on. The door that
  exists is the upload wizard's, over staged rows that have one.
* ***Estimate these*** — the blueprint's own annotation calls it *"the same
  control as entry 20"*, so it belongs to the cycle page; a second one here is
  hard-won law 5. `POST /reads/bulk-estimate` also takes a `read_at` and a
  reason the drawing does not draw, and **choosing an estimate's inputs is
  exactly what this build was told not to do**.

A tick column with nothing to press would be hard-won law 2, so it goes with them.

### 4 · THE ONE THING THAT REACHES THE PO — the reader, `DEF-MET-5216`

The blueprint draws a reader **three times**: a `Reader · J. Alvarez` chip in the
header, a `Reader` row in `The walk`, and a `Reader` column in `History`. Two PO
rulings of **2026-08-23** say it does not exist:

* `CR-029` **D6** — *"not required"* — records that `routes.assigned_to` *"keeps
  its value, no control writes it, and **no row renders it**"*;
* **`OQ-343`**, verbatim: *"B: no reader anywhere, **correct the screenshot** and
  drop the stored name"* — and `read_windows.reader` was dropped by migration
  `metering/0022`, so the drawn History column has no column behind it at all.

**None of the three is built**, and the suite asserts the absence over a fixture
that CARRIES a reader name, so *"the column is empty"* cannot be mistaken for
*"the rule is honoured"*. This is `B14 rule 41`'s own carve-out — a drawing that
contradicts a signed ruling — and it is the only class of thing that reaches the
Product Owner. **The PO has already told us once that the drawing was wrong about
this**, which is what makes it worth putting rather than assuming either way.

## 2026-09-14 · THE READING DETAIL: SIX WORDS, REAL SENTENCES, AND TWO LINKS BACK

Three cross-cutting jobs on screens that were already built, all three raised by
the Product Owner looking at the running product. Nothing here is polish: the
first is a ruling, the second is a live `B14 rule 31` breach visible in a
screenshot, and the third is a stored column the screen was printing an absence
over.

### 1 · *"reduce the content to 5 to 6 meaningful words"* — what was cut, and what was NOT

PO, verbatim, said of the three drawn warning sentences. Every cut below is **two
sentences of at most six** rather than one shorter line, which is `B14 rule 33`'s
own instruction — *"two sentences of six beat one sentence of twelve, because the
second sentence is where what-to-do-next lives"*.

| Where | Before | Words | After | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Correct dialog | *"The new value becomes the current reading; this one stays in the history."* | 13 | **"New value becomes current. The old one stays in history."** | 10 |
| Dispute dialog | *"The reading is not changed, and the account leaves the next bill run until a System Admin clears it."* | 19 | **"Account leaves the next bill run. Only a System Admin clears it."** | 12 |
| Clear dialog | *"The account returns to the next bill run and will be billed on this reading as it stands."* | 18 | **"Account returns to the bill run. Billed on this reading."** | 10 |
| Clear outcome | *"Clearing records that the reading stands and the bill was always correct; if the reading is wrong, use the billed correction instead."* | 22 | **"Cleared: the bill was always correct. Otherwise use the billed correction."** | 12 |
| Demand register | *"On a demand register this line reads differently"* + *"the billable figure is the peak itself in kW, never a difference of two peaks"* | 8 + 15 | **"Billed on the peak itself. Never a difference of two peaks."** | 5 + 5 |
| Linkage absence | *"A reading does not carry its premise, unit or account, and this screen will not guess them from a join made in the browser."* | 24 | **"Premise and unit not recorded."** | 4 |

⚠ **THE GUARD THAT SHAPED EVERY ONE OF THEM: RULE 33 SAYS NEVER CUT BELOW
CLARITY, AND TWO DRAFTS WERE REFUSED BY A TEST FOR DOING SO.**
`CR054Task20ModalCopy.test.ts` asserts that the dispute consequence still names
**System Admin** and the correction consequence still names **history** — *"the
consequence a clerk acts on survives in every shortened sentence"*. A first draft
of the dispute line dropped *System Admin* to reach six words and went red;
a first draft of the clear-outcome line dropped *always* out of BR-MET-133's own
phrase and went red. **Both reds were the rule working, and both are why the
figures above are 10–12 rather than 6.**

⚠ **AND RATIONALE WAS REMOVED, NOT SHORTENED — WHICH IS A DIFFERENT ACT.**
Rule 33 puts *why the product works this way* and *why a rule did not fire* at
**zero words on screen**. Shortening rationale to six words keeps the breach and
makes it terser. So:

* the linkage sentence's second clause — *"and this screen will not guess them
  from a join made in the browser"* — is **deleted**, not compressed;
* the demand line's first clause — *"on a demand register this line reads
  differently"* — is **deleted**: it renders on a demand register and nowhere
  else, so it was telling a clerk something they could already see;
* the `Could not run` list on the reading detail **stops rendering the reason
  at all**. That one is written up in §2.

The eight `metering.read.reason.*` sentences are still **cut** rather than
retired, because the upload wizard's rule-availability panel renders them and
that is a different screen with a different question. They went from 15–22 words
each to 4–6.

### 2 · `B33` — the FLAGS panel printed the engine at a clerk, and it was a rule-31 breach

`DEF-MET-5204`, seen on **2 of 2 readings opened in a browser**: every
vacant-unit flag rendered

> `basis` **no active account on the unit (BR-MET-036)**

with the **raw payload key as the field label**. `B14 rule 31` names `BR-…` by
family, and rule 32 keeps internal codes out of clerk-facing copy entirely.

**It was one severity away from being much worse.** Counted in
`apps/metering/validation.py`: **five** stored `basis` strings carry an id
(`BR-MET-036`, `OQ-009`, `CR-054`, `BR-MET-122`, `BR-MET-049`) and **four of them
sit on a severity that renders**; `unit_mismatch`'s ERROR bag carries `plan_id`,
a raw **uuid**; every unratified verdict carries `rule_ref: "BR-MET-020"`.

**The fix is the drawing's own shape and the guarantee is structural.** The
blueprint draws the rule's name in bold and **one prose line**, no severity
badge. `readsShared.outcomeSentence` composes that line **by reading keys BY
NAME** — nothing iterates the bag — so a key nobody has named cannot reach the
DOM however the engine grows, and a rule this screen has not been taught renders
its name alone rather than its payload.

**Two halves, deliberately, because the screen half alone is not enough and the
data half alone is not enough.**

* The **screen** half fixes every row ALREADY COMMITTED, which a copy edit on the
  server could never do — the old strings are stored on those rows forever.
* The **data** half strips the ids from all five `basis` strings anyway, because
  `rule_outcomes` is served verbatim in the payload and the next surface to
  render it should not inherit the breach. `B14 rule 31` says where the
  provenance goes: *"it is not deleted, it MOVES to the code comment beside the
  string"* — and that is where each of the five ids now is.

⚠ **THE FILE'S OWN HEADER ARGUED AGAINST DOING THIS AND IT WAS WRONG.**
`readsShared.tsx` opened with *"that is also why there is no per-rule sentence
template here — a rule added server-side tomorrow renders correctly today"*. It
did not render correctly; it rendered the engine's vocabulary at a clerk. The
header is amended in the same commit, which is step W rather than a note.

### 3 · `B30` — the account was a stored column with a printed absence over it

PO, verbatim: *"if you ahve account or meter in read details screen - please
ensure you ahve link it back to account and mter to imporve interaction
design"*.

**The meter.** The kicker already read `READING · M-7210 · TOTAL REGISTER` and
the meter number was flat text, so the one identifier a clerk reads first was the
one thing on the header they could not follow. It is a link now, inside the
kicker, with the drawn shape and separators untouched. `PageHeader.kicker` takes
a `ReactNode` for it — **the kit change, not a local one** (`B14 rule 36`).
⚠ **The drawn `see the meter →` in ⑬ STAYS**: it is conditional on the plan
stating an expected register set and it answers a different question — *which
sibling register never arrived* — so it is not this link twice.

**The account.** `meter_reads.account_id` is a reviewed cross-module FK (B2 §2),
stamped at collection since `DEF-658`, and `read_dict` served 41 keys, none of
them the account. The screen printed a 13-word sentence over the top of it. The
blueprint's verdict: *"a stored column and a printed absence for the same fact is
the two-homes problem waiting to happen."*

⚠ **THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION IS ONE LINE AND IT IS WRONG, WHICH IS THE
JUDGMENT WORTH RECORDING.** Metering already has `seams.active_account_for_unit`
and a reading knows its unit, so *"walk to the unit and ask who is on supply"*
would have worked on every fixture in the suite. **A reading belongs to whoever
was on supply the day it was taken.** Resolving today's occupant hands a year of
the previous tenant's consumption to whoever moves in next — the exact hazard
`services.collection_account_id` stamps the column to prevent, reintroduced at
the display layer, on the one screen whose whole job is proving where a number
came from. It is proved by **making the unit walk impossible** rather than by
asserting a value: `test_b30__it_reads_the_STAMP_and_never_the_unit_s_current_occupant`
monkeypatches all three unit-scoped seams to raise, and the wrong implementation
fails by exception where no equality assertion on a single-occupant fixture ever
could.

So a new **batched** seam: `customers.selectors.account_references(ids)` →
`{account_id: {id, account_no, customer_name, status}}`, read through
`metering.seams.account_references`. Batched like `accounts_for_units` beside it
and for the same reason (`NFR-3`, the DEF-324 discipline), and resolved by the
**detail endpoint** rather than inside `read_dict`, because every other caller of
that serializer is a LIST and one cross-module read per row is exactly the N+1
the batched seam exists to avoid.

**`B14 rule 31` decides what is shown:** the account NUMBER is the visible value
and the uuid rides on `title` as evidence. **CLAUDE.md hard rule 8 decides what is
NOT composed:** no address and no account is assembled in the browser; the server
walks its own seam.

⚠ **AND THE TWO ABSENCES ARE KEPT APART** — `not_stamped` (a vacancy read, a unit
nobody has taken service at, or any row committed before `DEF-658`) against
`unresolved` (customers could not answer). One sentence over both would tell a
clerk *"no account"* about a reading that has one, which is `DEF-075`'s shape and
what it cost a live ledger.

### 4 · What this lane did NOT do, and why

* **`metering.read.detail.*` (20 keys) and `metering.read.thresholdsNone` are now
  unused and are LEFT IN PLACE.** Retiring 21 keys across eleven catalogues is a
  220-line deletion in the most heavily shared files in the repo while four lanes
  are writing them, and G15 is satisfied by parity rather than by absence. The
  cost of leaving them is dead weight; the cost of removing them now is law 11's
  mechanism two. Filed here rather than done.
* **`metering.reads.peak.why` (18 words) is untouched.** It is a `title`
  attribute on the demand KPI, which is where rule 31 itself says detail belongs,
  and it is not one of the strings the ruling named.
* **The Clear dialog's outcome sentence is still on screen at all.** The drawing
  does not carry it; the previous lane recorded that deleting a screen sentence
  which states a SIGNED rule (`BR-MET-133` clause 3) is a copy decision for the
  PO rather than a build lane's. That stands — it was CUT, not removed.

## 2026-09-14 — METER READS ENTRY 20, *A CYCLE, THE DETAIL*: WHAT WAS NOT BUILT, AND FOUR JUDGMENTS

`/{tenant}/reads/cycles/{cycleId}` is the second half of the PO's ruling
*"within that we should show Routes and their completion"* — retiring entry 14
moved nine columns with nowhere to go, and this is where they went. Five tabs,
four served data groups, and **two drawn figures deliberately absent**.

### 1 · `DEF-MET-5206` is read WIDELY, and that reading is this lane's

PO, `Q4`, verbatim: ***"Settle first."*** Two derivations of *"the current
window"* disagree — one day the cycle row printed **August** while the
completeness engine answered **September** — and the ruling names two figures:
**the Window pill** and **Registers collected**.

**Registers collected is read as the FIGURE wherever it appears, not as one
drawing of it.** So five things are absent: the roll-up line's *"0 of 18
registers"*, the Collection panel's `REGISTERS COLLECTED` with its *"5 meters ×
their plan's registers"* denominator, the Overview Routes panel's `REGISTERS`
column, the Routes tab's `REGISTERS COLLECTED` column, and History's column of
the same name. The Window pill takes its Collection-panel twin (`WINDOW ·
Closed · 9 days ago`) with it, because they are one derivation drawn twice.

⚠ **THE DATA AGREES WITH THE WIDE READING, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT MERELY
CAUTIOUS.** There is no window-scoped register count served per route at all:
`route_dict`'s `collected` is `collected_read_count(route_id=…)`, which counts
every committed head read on that route **for all time**. Drawing it under the
drawn floor note *"measured against this cycle's window"* would be a sentence
promising something the number does not do — hard-won law 1 — so the column is
absent rather than approximate.

**What IS built, and why it is safe.** `METERS SHORT`, the short-register line
and the whole Still-to-read tab come from ONE `chase-list` call handed **the
window the page is itself printing** (`?period=<window_start>`) — the workaround
`RoutesCyclesPage` already records. That settles CONSISTENCY, not the fork.

### 2 · Five tabs, and the PO settled it the same day on a different screen

The blueprint's own summary row says *"Four — Overview · Routes · Still to read ·
History"* and **every frame draws five**, All reads included, with its own page of
annotations. B14 rule 41 makes the drawing the specification; and entry 21's
ruling of 2026-09-13 says it outright — *"in Cycle you will need to add a tab —
all reads and same in route details also"*. **Five.**

### 3 · The drawn READER column is NOT built, and that is a signed ruling

The blueprint draws a reader on the Overview panel and on the Routes tab. Two PO
rulings of **2026-08-23** refuse it: `CR-029` **D6** (*"not required"*) records
that `routes.assigned_to` *"keeps its value, no control writes it, and no row
renders it"*, and `OQ-343` is verbatim *"B: no reader anywhere"*. Entry 21's lane
put the same contradiction back to the PO as `DEF-MET-5216` the same afternoon;
this screen follows the ruling and cites that row rather than filing a second.
**The two catalogue keys it had already published are DELETED**, not left — a
string nothing reads is the dead half of hard-won law 2.

### 4 · The route link opens the OPERATIONAL detail, with this cycle's window

PO, 2026-09-13: *"what if User click on Route link — we will have to give a
details view of Route."* Both route tables link to `routeReadsPath(id, window)`
and carry the window, because a route can be walked on more than one cycle and
*"0 of 11"* has no denominator until one is named — entry 21's own reasoning,
applied at the door rather than restated.

### And three things reported rather than resolved

* **`DEF-MET-5213`** — `GET /cycles/{id}/chase-list` has no pager, so the drawn
  *"Server pager · NFR-3"* on Still to read is a CLIENT slice over a server
  answer bounded by the cycle. ⚠ **NOT fixed here on purpose:** the backend suite
  cannot be run in this container at all (`djangorestframework` is absent and

  The shape the fix takes is written into the row rather than into code nobody

* **`DEF-SHL-5215`** — `routeBUtilities.test.ts` cannot see a class held in a
  module-level constant unless the file is named `*Kit.ts`. Measured on this
  screen the same minute, both ways: a bogus class in a `className=` attribute
  fails and NAMES the file; the same class in a module constant passes 11 of 11.
  This lane's constants were therefore checked against the **built** stylesheet
  by hand — all sixteen utilities emit real rules, the two arbitrary ones
  (`text-[color-mix(in_srgb,var(--color-text)_55%,transparent)]` and
  `border-l-[3px]`) included.

### Two reds that were already red, dated

**`screenIds.test.tsx` has failed since `468a61c3` (2026-09-13)** — five routed
screens carry no `SCREEN_ROUTES` row (`DEF-SHL-5212`). **`UnitsPage.test.tsx` has
two failures** whose two files are byte-identical to the tip, so they are the

the ruling verbatim, two decision-log rows, B14 rules 31/37/39, `CLAUDE.md` hard rule 2).

**This RESOLVES the 2026-09-13 ruling the same way the identical Meter Reads instruction was

those are resolved."* **Billing's is now resolved the same way, explicitly.**

⚠ **FOUR OF THE FIFTEEN TOUCH MONEY OR THE LEDGER**, including a worked figure — **fee
`$0.57`, bill `$70.17`** — that exists in **no golden test, no rule and no decision row**. A
lane pricing a connection fee cannot find it. That is what this ruling fixes.

**Transcription is a TRANSCRIPTION, not a re-decision.** Each of the fifteen goes into
`12-governance/02-decision-log.md` **verbatim, with its date and the PO's own words**, and a
money one also into the module's `02-business-rules.md`. **None of them is interpreted,
merged, shortened or resolved on the way** — a ruling that arrives in a form we did not
expect is still a ruling.

### Q2 · THE LATE-FEE FLOOR TESTS THE **AGEING PORTION ONLY**

> ***"a). It matches what a customer would call fair, and B4/B5 are frozen so neither can be
> chosen by a lane. This changes what a customer is charged — it cannot go into step 2
> unanswered either way."***

This was **the document's own single open PO question** and it was unanswered until now.

**THE WORKED EXAMPLE THE RULING WAS GIVEN AGAINST**, and it is the reason this is a ruling
rather than a preference: a **$200** bill of which **$40** is 30 days overdue, against a
**$25** floor.

| Reading | Outcome |
|---|---|
| **Ageing portion** — `$40` vs `$25` | ⚠ **$40 > $25 → A FEE IS CHARGED** |
| Whole bill — `$200` vs `$25` | a fee is charged |

⚠ **THE EXAMPLE AS PUT TO THE PO SAID THE AGEING READING GIVES *"no fee"*, AND THAT IS
ARITHMETICALLY WRONG — `$40` clears a `$25` floor.** The ruling is recorded on the reading
the PO chose, **the ageing portion**, and the error in the illustration is recorded beside it
rather than quietly corrected, because the PO ruled with that figure in front of them. **A
correct worked pair for the same rule:** a `$200` bill with **`$18`** overdue charges
**nothing** on the ageing reading and **a fee** on the whole-bill reading — that is the case
the two readings actually separate, and it is the one a test should pin.

**This is the missing half of the document's ruling 26** and it decides what a real customer
pays. ⚠ **B4/B5 stay ❄️ FROZEN**: this names WHICH BALANCE the floor is tested against; it
moves no signed figure, and the `$25` floor itself is untouched and still hardcoded
(`BIL-S102`).

### Q4 · THE 25,000 CAP STAYS. ⚠ THE PO SUPPLIED THE FACT THAT SETTLES IT, AND IT REFUTES THE RECOMMENDATION.

> ***"(b) Keep 25,000, fix the stale comment only - generally utilities will devide them into
> nilling cycles and hence 25k limit is good"***

**The recommendation put to the PO was (a) — raise the default above 40,000 — and it was
WRONG, for a reason no measurement in this pass could have reached.**

⚠ **A UTILITY DIVIDES ITS ACCOUNTS INTO BILLING CYCLES. NO SINGLE RUN EVER COVERS THE WHOLE
BOOK.** So a 40,000-account utility does not need a 40,000-account run — it bills, say, four
cycles of 10,000, and **25,000 is comfortable headroom for the largest cycle anybody sensibly
configures.** That is a fact about how utilities operate, held by the PO and by nobody in
this repository, and it is exactly the class of question that legitimately reaches them
(hard-won law 13: *a fact only they hold*).

**Recorded prominently because the ARGUMENT for (a) looked strong and was still wrong.** It
reasoned from `40,000 > 25,000` without asking whether one run ever sees 40,000 accounts. **A
number being smaller than the ICP's ceiling is not by itself a breach.**

**WHAT DOES CHANGE: the comment, and only the comment.** `run_jobs.py:197–210` justifies the
ceiling by quoting `CLAUDE.md`'s **superseded** first line — *"under 3,000 connections"* —
and concludes 25,000 is *"eight times the largest utility the product is for."* Against the
ICP's real ceiling of 40,000 that reads as **0.625×**. ⚠ **The LIMIT is right and its STATED
REASON is false**, and a later lane reading that comment would either raise the cap or lose
confidence in the number. It is corrected to the PO's reason — cycles, not book size.
`DEF-BIL-4224` stays open for the comment; **`NFR-5` is NOT breached** and the
2026-09-01 decision-log row ruling this limit lawful — *"THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE, DONE
CORRECTLY"* — stands untouched.

### ⚠ COLLISION 1 — row 4 reverses a PO ruling of 2026-08-31, and the two differ by $12.00 a month on one building

**It does NOT go in as a plain ruling and it is NOT built. Both sides, quoted.**

**What row 4 answers, from the PDF's own §03 p93** — the document puts the question and the
answer side by side, so this is not inference:

> *"Two covered areas take the same service. Base charge once per bill or once per connection
> — and do the tier thresholds pool or reset?"* → **"Per connection.** Each connection bills
> its own base charge and walks its own tier ladder from the bottom. Two electric connections
> on one bill produce **two base lines and two usage ladders**, not one of each." Worked: base
> `$12.00`, `$0.20`/kWh, 100 kWh at each of two connections → **`$64.00`**. *"The pooled
> reading would have been `$52.00`."*

**That is `OQ-334`, word for word** — the register's own worked example is the same one, to
the cent: *"per connection = 12.00 + 12.00 + 20.00 + 20.00 = **$64.00**; once per bill, tiers
pooled = 12.00 + 40.00 = **$52.00** — a **$12.00/month** difference on one building"*.

**AND `OQ-334` ALREADY CARRIES A PO RULING, THE OTHER WAY.** From its own row:

> ✅ **RULED 2026-08-31 (`CR-056`) — ONE STANDING CHARGE FOR THE ADDRESS.** PO chose (a): a
> hallway and a car park both taking water are ONE water connection for the standing charge,
> **so the owner pays the water base once however many shared spaces the address has on that
> service.**

**The two cannot both hold on the same building.** 2026-08-31 says once however many shared
spaces; 2026-09-11 says two connections produce two base lines. ⚠ **They are reconcilable ONLY
by deciding whether two shared spaces on one address's service are one connection or two — and
that is precisely the fact the 2026-08-31 ruling settled and this one appears to unsettle.**
Both rulings state the same PRINCIPLE (*a standing charge follows the CONNECTION*) and reach
opposite OUTCOMES from it, which is the hardest kind of conflict to see and the reason this is
written out in full rather than summarised.

⚠ **THIS IS EXACTLY THE FAILURE HARD-WON LAW 13 PREDICTS** — the same question was put to the
PO twice, eleven days apart, and came back differently. The PO is not at fault; the question
was already answered in the repo and was asked again anyway.

**`OQ-334`'s status column also reads `OPEN` while its body carries the ✅ 2026-08-31 ruling**
— the status/body rot CLAUDE.md's prime-directive section warns about, in the row that decides
this money. **Not edited here: this lane transcribes and does not close.**

**What is NOT in dispute and is not blocked by this:** `1408 Elm Street` bills **`$69.60`**
either way — its two spaces are on DIFFERENT services, so one base per service per address is
what both readings produce. Only a building with two spaces on the SAME service is affected.

**Live product behaviour today:** `gather.gather_account` REFUSES such an account by name
(`GATHER_COVERAGE_SERVICE_TWICE`), one row on the S31.2 exception tab, and the rest of the run
bills. **The refusal is correct while this is unresolved and must not be lifted.**

### ⚠ COLLISION 2 — row 5 closes an OPEN question, and the way it closes it contradicts a CONFIRMED rule resting on a ❄️ FROZEN golden test

**It does NOT go in as a plain ruling and it is NOT built. Both sides, quoted.**

**What row 5 answers, from §03 p93:**

> *"Covered areas sit on different plans. Whose taxes, fees, discounts and plan snapshot govern
> the one bill?"* → **"Per connection.** Each connection is governed by **its own** plan — its
> taxes, its fees, its discounts — and the bill carries **one plan snapshot per connection**
> rather than one for the bill."

**That is `OQ-335`, and the arithmetic proves the identification** — the register's worked case
is a hallway on *Common Electric* (no tax rule) and irrigation on *Common Water* (a 2.00% city
water fee) over a **`$69.60`** bill, where **`$0.00`**, **`$1.39`** (levied on the whole bill)
and **`$0.57`** (levied on the water lines only) are the three defensible answers. The PDF's
worked figure is **fee `$0.57`, bill `$70.17`**, and `$69.60 + $0.57 = $70.17`. **It picks the
third.** `OQ-335` stands **OPEN** in `12-governance/01-open-questions.md`.

**WHAT IT CONTRADICTS — `BR-RAT-062`, CONFIRMED, quoted in full where it bites:**

> **"A bill covering SEVERAL services is taxed ONCE, over the combined base — tax is a
> BILL-level concept, never per-service. … Fees are likewise bill-level and are added once,
> after the services — charging them per service would multiply a late fee by the number of
> services."**

and the PO's own ruling of **2026-08-11** that `BR-RAT-062` rests on: ***"Tax rates are for
bill not for service, it can be conditional but it is for bill."***

⚠ **AND IT IS NOT ONLY A BUSINESS RULE — IT RESTS ON ❄️ FROZEN LAW.** `BR-RAT-062`'s cited
sources are **B5 `GT-17`** (the reference bill: five services → ONE base of `221.90` → four tax
lines) and **B4 §Tax as re-signed 2026-08-11**, whose stated reason is that the base is summed
from the ROUNDED line amounts *"because a customer who adds up the printed lines and applies
the rate must get the printed tax"*. A fee levied on a subset of a bill's lines — `$0.57` on
the water lines only — is the shape B4.2 excludes by construction.

**THE NARROW READING, STATED AND NOT CHOSEN.** `GT-17` is a single-account, single-plan bill;
row 5 speaks only to a MASTER account whose covered areas sit on DIFFERENT plans, where B4.2's
*"across every service on the plan"* has no single referent. On that reading row 5 is a
carve-out for a case the frozen figure never covered and moves no signed number. **This lane
does not choose between the two readings.** Under the change process step 2 a ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5
figure means **STOP and re-sign via HUMAN-GUIDE §6**, and under hard-won law 13 a ruling that
collides with a signed rule is one of the three things that legitimately reaches the PO.

**Live product behaviour today:** `gather.gather_account` REFUSES such an account by name
(`GATHER_COVERAGE_MULTI_PLAN`). **The refusal is correct while this is unresolved.**

⚠ **AND `OQ-335`'s OWN TEXT NAMES A SECOND THING ROW 5 WOULD CHANGE** — *"the snapshot can
name only one plan whichever way it goes"* — against the PDF's *"one plan snapshot per
connection rather than one for the bill"*. The locked-at-issue snapshot is `BR-CUS-013` /
`BR-BIL-030`. **Raised, not resolved.**

## 2026-09-14 · `CR-101-BRC03` · Billing §03, the bulk bill run — step 2, the build

**Scoped from** `04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/conformance/CR-100-BRC03-billing-step1.md`
and the §03 half of `blueprint/02-runs-single-budget-fix.md` (31 drawn entries, p028–p099).
**Built from the images**, re-rendered from the blueprint on the DEFAULT branch rather than
from any scratchpad copy — `git show "origin/claude/confirm-understanding-3ktufc:05-prototype/04 Billing, As Built.pdf"`,
sha256 `137a2a48…c200971`, and the six pages already read were re-rendered from it and proved
byte-identical before anything was built on them.

### Judgment 1 — the case filter offers nine kinds, not fifteen

**Measured on both sides at `v2.261.4` rather than carried forward from step 1:**

| where | how many |
|---|---|
| `runs.py` `AccountProblem(reason="…")` | **2** — `missing_read`, `base_only_billing` |
| `read_analysis.READ_ANALYSIS_CASES` | **7** |
| **emitted by the engine** | **9** |
| declared by the screen | **15** |

Six filters — `overcharge`, `no_usage`, `owes`, `past_due`, `late_fee`, `extra_charge` — could
never have a row behind them. Four are real `DECISION_CASES` values, so the server would have
recorded a decision on one; no code path creates a row carrying them. Two (`owes`, `past_due`)
were never in `DECISION_CASES` at all.

**The rule is the blueprint's own, §03 p041, ruled 2026-09-11:** *"A case kind the engine did
not raise **gets no chip**… The as-built screen declares fifteen."* The `owes` family held
three of the six and is therefore gone; an empty family is the same dead control one level up.

⚠ **THE OTHER HALF COSTS MORE THAN THE SIX.** Trimming the list means a row of an undrawn kind
belongs to no family and is filtered out of every table — present in the payload, absent from
the screen, counted in no total. That is `DEF-2381`'s shape on the screen whose most important
promise is that nobody is missing from the list. `casesWithNoChip()` reads the SERVED rows and
the screen names any kind it draws no chip for. Proved on a fixture carrying a `late_fee` row:
it renders *"Kinds not listed — Raised, not in any table: late_fee."* instead of vanishing.

**`G124` is the guard, and it is the thing that was missing.** The two lists live in two
LANGUAGES and nothing had ever compared them: `tsc` type-checks a list of strings, and the unit
tests asserted the families partition the tabs — which they did, exactly, all fifteen of them.
Proved RED through `run_gates.py` itself, naming all six, then with one kind planted back, then
green. ⚠ Its first run reported **ten** emitted: a bare `reason="…"` scan caught
`Break(reason="rule_refused")`, a different table and a different screen. A wrong answer in the
safe direction, which is the kind that survives longest; the scan is now scoped to the
constructor whose rows become chips.

### Judgment 2 — step 1's copy is the blueprint's, and 138 words became 38

`16 Scope` is one of only **two** entries in §03 carrying a `BUILD THIS` band. Measured over
the nine strings of step 1:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| words | **138** | **38** |
| longest sentence | **18** | **6** |
| heading | 7 words | **2** |

plus **14 words of RATIONALE removed rather than shortened** — *"A service left unticked is a
choice this run records, not something quietly skipped."* B14 rule 33 puts rationale at ZERO
words on screen and says it is REMOVED; cutting a *why* sentence to six words keeps the breach
and makes it terser. The key is retired from all eleven catalogues and the reason it states now
lives in the code, where `BillRun.scope_services` already records it.

Five further sentences (16, 15, 14, 14 and 13 words) came down **because the walk measured
them**, not because they were eyeballed. Every one was *"X, so Y"* with Y the rationale.

**The cycle field now says WHICH cycle, not what the list holds** — the blueprint draws
`Silver Creek · 09-A` under the picker. A run billed against the wrong cycle is the most
expensive mistake available on this screen, which is why the drawing puts the answer under the
control. **Derived from the chosen row and never typed** (B14 rule 37). Walked: it reads
`RT-007, RT-008, RT-009, RT-010, RT-011 · CY-007`.

### Judgment 3 — is billing continuous? (p046 the badge, p048 the reasoning)

Blueprint, verbatim: *"A gap is days nobody billed. An overlap is days billed twice. Both are
silent, both are money, and neither is visible anywhere in this product today."*

Now stated on step 1 **before the run starts**. Worked from this tenant's own history, driven
in a browser rather than asserted:

| period from | state | what the screen says |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-01 | continuous | *Continuous · No gap, no overlap.* |
| 2026-08-04 | gap | *Gap · 3 days never billed: 08/01/2026 – 08/03/2026.* |
| 2026-07-29 | overlap | *Overlap · 3 days billed twice: 07/29/2026 – 07/31/2026.* |
| a cycle with no earlier run | — | **nothing at all** |

That fourth row is the judgment. *"We could not look"* and *"there is no gap"* are different
facts, and a reassuring green band over a utility's first ever run would be an absence of
evidence drawn as evidence of absence.

**It is NOT a refusal, and that is the drawing's own ruling** — a mid-cycle change can make a
gap legitimate. The blueprint says the OVERLAP case *"should refuse, or at the least take an
explicit acknowledgement"*; **that decision was not taken here**, so the band draws at the
danger tone and the refusal is left unbuilt rather than invented. It costs **no new read**:
`GET /billing/runs` is already fetched by this step and already carries the previous period.

⚠ **"Previous" means a run that STARTS strictly before this one.** Without that clause,
re-opening the run you are already editing compares a period with itself and reports the whole
period billed twice — a red band on every re-entry, for ever. Proved RED: deleting that one
clause fails exactly that test and no other.

### What was NOT built, and why — each of these is a decision, not an omission

| Drawn | Why not |
|---|---|
| The **four-step rail** (`17.L1`, and `17 Check` replacing steps 2, 3 and 4 of six) | Collapses three shipped steps into one screen, moves `billRunStep23.tsx` (102 KB, not this lane's file) and three test files. A wave of its own |
| `WHAT THIS COVERS` — five counts | Needs a read that does not exist (`New read S46`). No endpoint counts units, masters, meters or unmetered points for a cycle before a run |
| `Which accounts` · `Also include the held accounts` | Needs run scoping the server does not take. `POST /billing/runs` scopes to a cycle |
| `DEFAULTS` — the three run-level defaults and `Label this run` | `bill_runs` has no label column and no defaults columns. A migration |
| `ALREADY RUN FOR THIS CYCLE`'s `LABEL`, `BY`, `Take it over` | `run_by` and `created_at` are stored and not served by `bill_runs_list`; *Take it over* is a reassignment nobody has ruled on |
| The footer *"About three minutes, in the background. You can close this tab."* | **It would be false today.** `background: true` exists and the wizard calls `calculate` inline (`DEF-1084`). Writing the sentence before the behaviour is hard-won law 1 |
| **`BIL-S90`, the 25,000 cap** | PO ruled 2026-09-14 that the cap stays — a run is scoped to a cycle |
| **`BIL-S39`** (17.11 · 17.15 · 20) | **Blocked.** Its card carries both figures with the PO — *per conenction* and *as per connection*. Nothing per-connection was priced, no tier ladder reset, no fee moved from bill level to service level, and `GATHER_COVERAGE_SERVICE_TWICE` / `GATHER_COVERAGE_MULTI_PLAN` are untouched |
| **`BIL-S102` / `BIL-S77`** (17.20 Waiver) | Ruled 2026-09-13 and REAL work: the `$25` floor moves out of `late_fee.py`'s default argument into tenant settings. It needs a migration and a settings surface, which is a lane, and `S77` says the floor is read from ONE place — so half of it is worse than none. **Not started. It needs scoping as its own lane.** The `$25` value itself does not move |

### One defect this lane filed against its own work

**`DEF-BIL-5241`** — my first commit's catalogue push carried **18 of a sibling lane's in-flight
keys** and three of their rewordings. Found by reading my own commit's hunks: 20 added lines,
two of them mine. Every check law 11 prescribes passed and each was true — 11 paths named and
11 changed, my own keys present, and `push_paths.sh` raised nothing because the catalogues had
not moved on the tip. **The eleven catalogues cannot be pushed one at a time, so a pathspec
push of them takes whatever any sibling has added.** Not reverted: backing them out would
delete work a sibling is actively building against.

**The fix was then applied to this lane's own later pushes and is the row's prevention clause**:
rebuild each catalogue from the PINNED TIP's own bytes, apply only your own batch, hash THAT.
Measured on the continuity push — **7 insertions and 0 deletions per catalogue**, against a
working tree whose catalogues carried **52** keys of a sibling's `BillDetailPage` work.

### The reds, dated

* **`BillsPage.test.tsx` TC-2 — red since 2026-09-13, before this lane started.** `cf45a3d2`
  added `"address"` to `BillsListPage`'s `searchFields` and the test still expects three
  (`git log -S '"address"' -- …/BillsListPage.tsx`). Not touched.
* Every other red in the billing suite is a sibling's uncommitted work. **Proved by
  construction rather than asserted:** the branch tip plus only this lane's files and only this
  lane's catalogue batches runs **135 passed, 1 failed**, and the one is TC-2 above.

**None taken.** `2.262.0` is already on the branch and a sibling in this tree holds it;

## 2026-09-14 · `CR-101-BRC03` step 2 — the bill detail and four of its tabs

Five judgment calls this lane made where the rules ran out, each with the figure
it was made on. Nothing here was put to the Product Owner: none collides with a
signed rule, none moves a ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure, and hard-won law 13 makes a
recorded judgment the deliverable and a re-ask the failure to make one.

### 1 · `net_effect` is computed by the SERVER, and it is a sum of two served totals

The blueprint's Corrections tab draws a row the product has never had — *"Net
effect on the customer"* — and states the arithmetic in its own prose against
hard rule 4: the original stays charged for ever, a credit note cancels it, a
replacement charges the right amount, and the difference is what the customer is
better or worse off by. **Three documents, not one edited one.**

**Worked on the one real correction this tenant has:** `BL-2607-000032` stays at
`$137.70`, `CM-0001` credits `−$137.70`, `BL-2607-000047` charges `$137.15`, so
the net effect is **`−$0.55`**.

**Decided:** it is derived in `single_correction.chain_of`, not in the browser.
`BillDetailPage`'s own standing rule (PO 2026-08-30, *"when you build billing
logic ensure you use r1 to r7 that we build and wire it"*) makes the screen a
display of what the server resolved; a browser-side sum of a customer's
correction would be a second implementation of an arithmetic no golden test can
reach. Summed at the stored scale and rounded nowhere — hard rule 2 rounds at
display and `MoneyCell` is the display.

**And it is `null`, never `0.0000`, on an uncorrected bill.** A class-R
restatement that nets to zero is a real thing and the engine carries a warning
for it by name, so *nothing happened* and *it netted to zero* cannot share a
value.

**No signed figure moves.** No B4 rule and no B5 golden test states a net-effect
figure; every input is a total the same table already prints one row above.

### 2 · `When this is due` stays on the Charges tab, against the drawing

The blueprint moves it to the Document tab as a `DATES` group. **The Document tab
is another lane's wave-2 work.** Removing the panel now would delete `Past due`
and `Fees on this bill` from the product with nowhere to land — the mirror of
hard-won law 2, a fact whose destination has not been built yet.

**Decided:** it stays, and the header's SECOND pill (`Past-due unknown`) is
removed in the same change, which is what makes that safe: the drawing's *one
pill, not two* is honoured and the past-due fact still reads exactly once, in
words, on Charges. When the Document lane builds `DATES`, the panel moves.

### 3 · `Fix this bill` is the primary, and the step-1 diff says the opposite

`CR-100-BRC03-diff-02.md` element 26 reads *"`View the bill as sent` as the
filled primary, `Fix this bill` secondary"*. **Measured on a 5× crop of p015, and
identically on p018, p021, p022, p024 and p027 — every §02 frame — `Fix this
bill` is the one BOXED control and `View the bill as sent` is unboxed grey
text.**

**Decided:** built to the drawing (B14 rules 41 and 42 — the drawing is the
authority and it is read as an IMAGE), and the diff row is filed as
**`DEF-BIL-5244`** rather than silently disagreed with, so a step-3 lane does not
flip the loudest control on the screen back.

### 4 · The standing sentence loses the drawn date

The drawing's replaced-bill sentence names the replacement's issue date. Ours
does not: BR-SHL-034 is ONE date formatter, and a date interpolated into a
translated string is formatted by whoever built the string — which is the defect
that rule exists for. The date is one row below, in the *What happened* table,
through `DateCell` like every other date on the screen.

### 5 · A served code with no word is suppressed only when it LOOKS like a code

`credit_notes.reason` is a free-text column that the correction engine fills with
an enum. B14 rule 32 bans an internal code in clerk-facing copy; it does not ban
TEXT. So the rule is applied to the SHAPE of the string: `wrong_read` is held
back and stated as unreadable, and a tenant's own sentence — *"Meter misread"* —
is printed. The regular expression is `^[a-z0-9]+(_[a-z0-9]+)*$` and it is in one
place, beside the component that uses it.

### Version

**`2.263.0`**, taken through `allocate.py version --bump change` and verified
free on every branch at the moment it was written. A sibling had already declined
`2.262.0` for being held in this tree; this is a fresh number, not a third copy
of theirs.

## 2026-09-14 · THE BILL RUN HAS FOUR STEPS, NOT SIX — AND THE PLUMBING BEHIND THEM WAS NEVER BUILT EITHER

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"we have 4 step only now in bill run"* — said after the PO put
our screenshot beside their own drawing and asked *"your screenshot and what we have given
you in the document does not match why?"*, then *"does this mean you did not build the
plumbing also the way we have detailed out in document?"*

**Both answers are yes.** This entry records the ruling, the cause, and the measured size,
because the cause is a scoping error of ours and the next agent must not repeat it.

### What the product shows, and what the drawing shows

| | Steps | Words |
|---|---|---|
| **Product today** (`v2.263.0`, walked in Chromium) | **6** | Pick the cycle · Check what we found · Review accounts · See the totals · Confirm & sign off · Send them out |
| **Blueprint** (`04 Billing, As Built.pdf`, screen `BIL-02`, stamp `v2.235.0`) | **4** | Scope · Check · Sign off · Send |

The drawing states it in its own words on **p35**, and states its own prior version too:

> *"The wizard rail now reads **Scope · Check · Sign off · Send**. It was What to bill ·
> Review · Sign off · Send, and Review was the wrong word for the step: reviewing is what a
> clerk does **on** it, and what the product does **to get there** is a check. **Four words,
> each naming an act**, and the second one now tells the truth about whether anything has
> been billed."*

So four is not an inference from a rail graphic. The document argues for it in prose, names
the word it rejected, and gives the reason.

### Why we built six — and it is not the lanes' fault

`billRunShared.tsx:196` says so in its own docstring, and has since long before the
blueprint existed: *"The SIX wizard steps — **the prototype's stepper, in its order and its
words**."* All six names are in `05-prototype/r10-2026-08-16/SMARTBillHub.dc.html`, byte for
byte. **The wizard was built correctly to r10**, which `CLAUDE.md` names as THE clickable
reference by PO ruling of 2026-08-16.

**B14 rule 41 is what moved the authority**: the product UI matches the BLUEPRINT exactly.
For billing, the blueprint redrew this screen, so r10 stopped being the specification for it
the day the drawing landed — and nothing in the repo told the wizard's file that.

⚠ **AND THE DOCUMENT ANTICIPATED THIS EXACT CONVERSION AND WROTE THE MAP FOR IT.** Two
sections exist for nothing else: front matter **p28–p36, *"Six steps become four"***, and
**`03 · carry-over`, p86–p88, *"Nothing the six steps did is lost in the four"*** — one row
per element across all six original steps, with the arithmetic done:
**38 elements → 19 unchanged · 9 moved · 4 relabelled · 5 removed**, and the four-step total
**47 = 38 − 5 + 14 new**. The conversion was specified down to the element. We did not run it.

### The measured size — the plumbing question, answered with the number

From `CR-100-BRC03-billing-step1.md`, this branch's own step-1 diff:

| | §02 (7 entries) | **§03–§08 (57 entries)** | TOTAL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drawn elements compared | 166 | **227** | **393** |
| matching | 80 | **22** | **102** |
| present, with a difference | 36 | 42 | 78 |
| **drawn and NOT on the screen** | 49 | **158** | **207** |

**For the runs/single/budget/fix screens, 22 of 227 drawn elements are in the product.** The
step rail is one row of 227. The things behind it are in the 158: run-level **DEFAULTS** (the
three recurring decisions made once — the drawing calls this *"the single biggest
error-reducer in this redraw"*), the **SCOPE** chooser (route/area/named set rather than
all-or-nothing on a cycle), the **held-account sweep** checkbox, the **gap / overlap** check
between this period and the last, the **WHAT THIS COVERS** count card (units → accounts,
masters, meters, points with no meter), and **ALREADY RUN FOR THIS CYCLE** with *Take it over*.

**So the honest answer to the PO's question is: no, the plumbing was not built to the
document, and the rail is the visible tenth of it.**

### The scoping error, named

Step 1 measured all of the above correctly and **fixed nothing, by design** — that was its
brief. Step 2 then dispatched five lanes, each scoped to ONE screen (bulk run, fix a bill,
all-bills list, bill detail, print bills). **The six→four conversion is not one screen; it
spans four of them plus the carry-over map, so it fell between every lane's boundary and
belonged to none.** The bulk-run lane worked inside step 1's copy — `cddb4f79`, *"step 1
reads the blueprint's own words — 138 words down to 38"* — and correctly left a rail it was
not scoped to touch.

**The lesson, and it is the one worth keeping:** a lane scoped to a SCREEN cannot see a
change whose unit is a JOURNEY. When a blueprint restructures a flow, the conversion is its
own lane and it is dispatched FIRST, because every screen lane downstream builds onto the
shape it decides. Ours were dispatched in parallel, so five lanes built onto the shape the
blueprint had already replaced.

### What follows

Filed as a defect, not a change request — `13-change-process.md` §1: the product does not do
what the signed drawing specifies, and B14 rule 41 is the signed rule. The conversion is
built to **p86–p88's carry-over map**, from the **images** (rule 42), and the map's own
arithmetic is the acceptance test: **47 elements on four steps, with 19 unchanged, 9 moved,
4 relabelled and 5 deliberately removed** — a removed element that reappears is a failure of
the conversion, and a moved one that is lost is the same failure wearing a different face.

## 2026-09-14 · "WHY ARE YOU POINTING AT r10?" — THE POINTER THAT SENT LANES TO THE PROTOTYPE

**PO, verbatim,** on being told the bill run's six steps came from r10:
*"ia have been telling yu constantly that you ahve to consider the pdf document i have
proided - i have said so many time - then why you are pointing at r10?"*

**They were right, they had said it, and the repo already agreed with them.** This entry
records why a lane read r10 anyway, because the answer is a defect in our own governance
and not a judgement anyone made.

### The instruction WAS recorded — in B14, on 2026-09-04

Rule 36, ratified, PO verbatim: *"UI screens layout and details you can folow from Screens
that we capture from document, but style guide should be from r10 agreement."* So the
document owns layout and detail; r10 owns visual style. That is exactly what the PO says
they have been saying, and it has been signed law for ten days.

### And `CLAUDE.md` line 10 was never amended to match

It read, and had read since 2026-08-16:

> `/05-prototype/r10-2026-08-16/SMARTBillHub.dc.html` — **THE clickable reference**…
> **Layout/copy/flows/states only**; DO NOT port its runtime.

⚠ **THE WORD THAT COST IT IS `flows`.** Rule 36 moved LAYOUT and DETAIL to the document and
**said nothing about flows**, so this line went on handing flows to r10 and read as
perfectly consistent with the new rule. **A wizard's STEP COUNT is a flow.**

`CLAUDE.md` is the file every session is instructed to read first. A lane obeying it built
the bill run to r10's six-step stepper — `billRunShared.tsx`'s own docstring says so,
*"the prototype's stepper, in its order and its words"* — while the Billing blueprint draws
**four** and argues for them in prose on p35. **Every gate, `tsc` and every test passed.**

### And the Billing blueprint was not on the working branch

Five of six blueprint PDFs were on `claude/eager-johnson-r0k88b` — Assets, Accounts,
Premises & Units, Customer Portal, Plans & Rates. **Billing's was not.** So a lane that did
go looking for the drawing would have found nothing and fallen back to r10, correctly by
the letter of the line above. `04 Billing, As Built.pdf` is now ON the branch
(14,363,163 bytes, sha256 `137a2a48…`), which makes the anomaly the absence rather than
the presence.

### Ruled and built

1. **For any module that HAS a blueprint PDF, r10 drops to VISUAL STYLE alone** and the
   blueprint owns layout, copy, **flows** and states. `CLAUDE.md` line 10 amended in the
   same commit as this entry.
2. **Check for a blueprint BEFORE reading r10 for any screen**, across every ref and not
   only your own: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> | grep -i 'pdf$'`.
3. **The Billing PDF lives on the branch**, so the fallback that produced this is gone.
4. Filed `DEF-GOV-5248`, category `stale-record`.

⚠ **THE SHAPE IS THIS FILE'S OWN, FOR THE EIGHTH TIME.** B14's rule-count line has been
wrong six times, hard-won law 2's rotten hold is the same mechanism, and this is another:
**a ruling landed and the pointer to it did not move.** Ratifying a rule and amending every
line that contradicts it are two acts, and only the first one feels like the work. The
difference here is the cost — the stale pointer did not merely misinform, it actively
directed lanes at the superseded source, and five step-2 lanes then built onto the shape it
chose.

**And the lesson for how we answer the PO:** naming r10 as the cause read as a defence of
the six steps. It was meant as a diagnosis and it landed as an excuse. **When the cause of
a miss is our own stale record, say that first and name the source second.**

## 2026-09-14 · THE BILL DETAIL'S DOCUMENT TAB WAS NEVER BUILT TO THE DRAWING — AND `DEF-BIL-5244` IS WRONG

**PO, verbatim,** putting our Document tab beside theirs: *"this screen is not correct - please
compare it with what is gien in document - here also youa re refering to R10- does that mean
you ahve done same with tabs alos check it out"*

They asked us to check. We did. **Three findings, and the second reverses a defect one of our
own lanes filed today.**

The tab STRUCTURE is right and came from the drawing: five tabs, `Sent` split out of Document,
counts on `Corrections 0` and `Sent 2` (p016 items 7). **What is wrong is the body**, and its

SCREEN"***, which embedded the server's PDF because *"the bill itself was two clicks away… on a
tab whose whole subject is the page a customer was sent."*

⚠ **THE PO REVERSED THAT ON 2026-09-11 AND THE BLUEPRINT RECORDS THE RULING VERBATIM** (p012):

> **The embedded PDF and its viewer — REMOVED.** *"we dont what full view of the document - you
> give a link to download but full view of document is not requires - it does not add any value
> to user"*. Replaced by a download and an open-in-new-tab control, plus the two facts about the
> saved copy. **The only REMOVED row in this document, and the only one with a ruling to quote.**

**It is still in the product.** p015's own banner says so: *"REDESIGN drawn 2026-09-11, still
unbuilt at Version 35… the Product Owner's 2026-09-11 ruling removing the embedded viewer.*
***NEVER BUILT.***" So the single most conspicuous element in the whole bill-detail redraw — the
one element marked REMOVED, carrying its own quoted ruling — survived a lane that worked on this
very screen today.

**The class of failure is the same one as the bill run's six steps**: building from a source the
PO's ruling had already overtaken. It was r10 there and `CR-053` here. **Neither is a source you
may build from once a blueprint has redrawn that screen.**

### 2 · ⚠ `DEF-BIL-5244` IS WRONG AND MUST BE REVERSED — the step-1 record was right

The step-2 lane filed `DEF-BIL-5244` today saying step 1 had the header's two controls the wrong
way round, *"measured on a 5x crop of p015… the same pair appears identically on all six frames"*,
and **built the inversion, and put a comment beside it naming six pages so nobody would flip it
back.** The live screen now makes `Fix this bill` the filled red primary.

**The drawing's own annotation, p016 item 6, in words:**

> **One primary, and an overflow** · *View the bill as sent* **filled**; *Fix this bill*
> secondary; *Print bill* and *Cancel this bill* into `…`, Cancel keeping its reason ·
> UI-RULES 4–6 · **CHANGED**

**The lane measured which control had a BOX DRAWN ROUND IT and read that as emphasis.** On p015's
frame the box sits on `Fix this bill` — the observation was accurate and the inference was
wrong, because a wireframe's box is a drawn figure and **B14 rule 37 says a drawn figure is an
ILLUSTRATION, never a fact to build to.** The annotation beneath it is the specification, and it
says `filled`. `CR-100-BRC03-diff-02.md` element 26 was correct as written.

⚠ **AND THE COST SHAPE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX:** a confident correction, filed as a defect
against a correct record, with a code comment added to defend it. That is harder to undo than the
original error, because the next reader finds a cited defect row and a cited comment agreeing
with each other. **Where a drawing and its own annotation disagree about EMPHASIS, the annotation
wins — and a conformance row stating emphasis must cite the annotation, not the pixels.**

### 3 · What the Document tab actually owes, from p016's thirteen numbered items

Present: five tabs with counts (7) · the copy control (8) · Origin collapsed (13).
**Absent:** name and address **linked** (1, `NEW READ` — *"the name and address are in the PDF
only today"*) · the cycle **by name**, `cycles.label`, not `CY-007` (4) · one pill, not two (5) ·
the primary the right way round (6) · **Owed today**, the live account balance, linked (9) ·
**Breakdown**, one line from `charges_by_service` (10) · **Usage**, through `GET /accounts/{id}/usage`,
*"which is mounted"* (11) · **Dates**, absorbing *When this is due* from Charges (12) · and
**THE BILL** group — *Download the bill as sent (PDF)* + *Open it in a new tab ↗* + *Saved copy ·
Kept — 2 pages* + *Template v1* — which is what REPLACES the viewer.

Group order is drawn and is not ours to choose: **Amount → Breakdown → Usage → Dates → the
document itself → Origin → Record.**

The document's own arithmetic for this screen: **43 as-built elements → 51 remedy** = 43 − 1
removed + 9 new (name · address · billed date · cycle name · copy control · Owed today · Usage ·
download control · open-in-new-tab), with 27 unchanged, 11 moved, 4 relabelled. **That is the
acceptance test**, exactly as p86–88's map is for the bill run.

## 2026-09-14 · THE BILL RUN'S RAIL BECOMES FOUR, AND WHAT READING THE DOCUMENT ITSELF CHANGED

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"we have 4 step only now in bill run"* (`DEF-BIL-5247`), said after
putting our screenshot beside `05-prototype/04 Billing, As Built.pdf`.

Every page below was read **as an image** at scale 2.0, and at 3.0–5.0 where the type is small
(B14 rule 42). The text layer was used only to find a page. The PDF was taken off the DEFAULT
branch — `origin/claude/confirm-understanding-3ktufc` — and its checksum verified before it was
read: **14,363,163 bytes, sha256 `137a2a48c0398c39897f49aa…`**.

### The rail, in the document's own words (p35)

> *"The wizard rail now reads **Scope · Check · Sign off · Send**. It was What to bill · Review ·
> Sign off · Send, and Review was the wrong word for the step: reviewing is what a clerk does ON
> it, and what the product does TO GET THERE is a check."*

And the mapping is the document's, not ours (p28–29): 1 Scope ← `cycle` (KEEP, WIDENED) ·
2 Check ← `found` + `customers` + `totals` (MERGE INTO ONE) · 3 Sign off ← `confirm` (KEEP,
TRIMMED) · 4 Send ← `send` (KEEP, ONE DOOR ADDED).

### THE FIVE JUDGMENT CALLS, EACH WITH THE FIGURE IT RESTED ON

**1 · An old `?step=` link cannot be translated, so it clamps.** Old 5 and 6 now clamp to 4,
which is SEND. There is no way to tell an old `?step=2` from a new one, so a translation table
would mis-route every new link for ever to fix old ones for a few days. **Nothing in the product
builds a link with a literal step in it** — 84 occurrences, all in tests and walkthroughs — and a
run re-opened without a step is placed by `stepForPhase` from the run's own served phase, which
was re-read row by row against the carry-over map rather than shifted by arithmetic. A stale
bookmark lands on Send, which writes nothing on arrival; the resume band says which run and what
phase it is in.

**2 · The merge put TWO decision controls on one account, and the document says which survives.**
Old steps 2 and 3 each drew a `<select>` over the same `GET .../exceptions` rows; on separate
steps that was invisible. Stacked, one account had **two comboboxes with one accessible name** on
a money path — found by `def2857DecisionAnswer`, not by inspection. p53 settles it: *"Step 2
(What was found) gave six dimensions of the account set — they become the filter chips, with
counts. Step 3 (The customers) gave the per-account decision — it becomes the inline control."*
So the reads analysis is READ-ONLY and the case table is live. ⚠ **Charges-to-add stays LIVE and
the asymmetry is the point:** its two cases, `late_fee` and `extra_charge`, are in **no**
`CASE_FAMILIES` entry, so read-only there would have left a case with no control anywhere on the
screen — BR-SHL-025's own breach, caught by `CR051Step23`'s no-choices case.

**3 · A step number must be derived, never written down.** `"Step 1"`, `"Step 5"` and `"Step 6 ·
almost done"` were literal catalogue strings — **3 keys × 11 catalogues = 33 strings**. A rail of
four therefore left two screens naming a step that does not exist, in every language at once,
with `tsc`, every suite and every gate green: there is nothing in a catalogue string for a check
to compare against the rail. `stepNumberOf` reads the position off `BILL_RUN_STEPS`. *"· almost
done"* went with it — B14 rule 33 caps a LABEL at three words.

**4 · The carry-over map's ROW TABLE is the acceptance list, not its summary block.** Transcribed
from p86–p88 as images: **25 rows carrying 38 element-instances** once the `×2`/`×5`/`×6`
multipliers are counted. ⚠ **THE DOCUMENT'S OWN SUMMARY BLOCK DOES NOT RECONCILE WITH ITS OWN
ROWS.** The block says *"unchanged 19 · moved 9 · relabelled 4 · removed 5"*, which sums to **37**
against a stated total of **38**; the rows themselves give **unchanged 20 · moved 10 ·
relabelled 3 · removed 5 = 38**. The two totals that matter DO hold — 38 elements, and
**47 = 38 − 5 removed + 14 new** once *"3 defaults"* is read as ONE element, which is the only
reading that makes the fourteen come out. **We build to the rows** and this paragraph is the
record of why; the split is not re-derivable from the block.

**5 · Where the document disagrees with itself, the SCREEN FRAME and its own annotation win.**
p35 sketches screen 16 as *"three zones and a commit bar"* with a commit reading *"Prepare —
looks, writes nothing, takes ~2 min →"*; the screen frame on p46–47 draws **five groups** and a
commit reading **"Check this run →"** over *"About three minutes, in the background. You can
close this tab."*, and the frame's own annotation ⑥ on p48 agrees with the frame. Frame plus
annotation wins (B14 rules 37 and 41).

### THE CHIP TAXONOMY ON SCREEN 17, READ OFF p51 AND TIED OUT

The PO's own count — *"there are 7 categories aroun 18 to 29 chips - not 3 categories and 16
chips for filter"* — is right. **Seven category rows, twenty-six chips:**

| # | Category | Chips |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Needs you · 12** | Missing read 4 · Unusually large 3 · Unusually small 1 · No usage 1 · Unusual days 1 · Meter changed 1 · Multiplier changed 1 — **7** |
| 2 | **Answered by your default** | Estimated 44 · Base charge only 31 — **2** |
| 3 | **Held · 21** | Never calculated 15 · Calculated and broke 6 — **2** |
| 4 | ↳ **Where the fix is** | The account or the plan 3 · The read 2 · The rates 1 — **3** |
| 5 | ↳ **The reason** | Master coverage 1 · City limits not recorded 1 · No base charge for this type 1 · Cart count missing 1 · Reading disputed 1 · No rate version in force 1 — **6** |
| 6 | ↳ **How long it has waited** | Under 14 days 10 · Escalated 9 · Over 60 days 2 — **3** |
| 7 | **Everything else** | Ready 1,251 · Masters 11 · In arrears 312 — **3** |

Rows 4–6 are INDENTED sub-rows of Held, drawn with a corner glyph; counting only the un-indented
rows gives four, which is how a reading lands on three or four categories.

**THE TIE-OUT IS THE PROOF THE READING IS RIGHT RATHER THAN PLAUSIBLE**, and every level holds:
4+3+1+1+1+1+1 = **12** = the *Needs you* header and the `NEEDS YOU` KPI · 15+6 = **21** = the
*Held* header and the `HELD` KPI's own *"15 by a default · 6 blocked"* · 10+9+2 = **21**, the
whole held band again · 3+2+1 = **6** and 1×6 = **6**, both sub-dividing the six blocked ·
and the screen's own reconciling line, 1,251 + 12 + 21 + 0 = **1,284**.

Cross-checked against the blueprint's build index (p165–166), which gives these their own layer
entries: 17.1–17.7 are the seven *Needs you* chips, 17.8–17.9 the two defaults, 17.10–17.15 the
held/fix/ready/masters set and 17.21 *In arrears* — a NEW CHIP in *Everything else*.

⚠ **ONE DISAGREEMENT INSIDE THE DOCUMENT, LEFT OPEN RATHER THAN RESOLVED:** p53's band table says
Held carries *"Four — by a default, and three by where the fix is"* chips; the p51 drawing shows
**two** under Held plus the three. Recorded, not decided — the drawing plus its tie-out is what
was built to.

### What this cost, and what it did not

The rail change alone moved **9 source and test files and all eleven catalogues** (5 keys added,
17 retired, every one grepped for a call site first), and took the billing suites from 47 red to
**1 red, which is pre-existing** — the bills-list search census, proved red at the tip in a
detached worktree and introduced 2026-09-13 in `cf45a3d2`. **The phase words did not move**, and
that is the check on the merge: six steps carried `prepare · prepare · prepare · breaks · summary
· release` and four carry `prepare · breaks · summary · release` — the same four words, one step
each, because `calculate` was never a step's phase.

## 2026-09-14 · The One-time bill tab becomes the three-step wizard the blueprint draws

**Track: MAINTENANCE, and that was a correction mid-flight.** The lane opened this as
Build and was pulled up. `12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`'s one
question — *can a user do this task in the product today?* — answers **yes**:
`/:tenant/billing/one-time` is live and a clerk can create a draft one-time bill. That
makes it the case the process names by hand, *"a live screen redrawn end to end is
MAINTENANCE"*. **Written down because the lane got it wrong first:** the rail was built
before reproduce, locate and blast radius were done, and the cost was real — see the
third judgment call below.

**PO, 2026-09-14, verbatim:** *"one time bill also does not match - it is 3 steps
process"*.

### The five judgment calls, each with what it rested on

**1 · The rail is `WizardFrame`'s, not a new stepper.** B14 rule 3 — *"any flow with 2+
stages uses the numbered step rail + a wizard-actions footer"* — and 15 wizards already
mount it. Building a second stepper for this one screen would have given the product two
rails to keep in step. **No prop was added and no kit file was touched**, so the other
fifteen do not move.

**2 · Step 1's `Continue` runs the preview, and that is not a write.** The drawing puts
the preview between steps 1 and 2 (*"step 2 is what gather resolves"*) and states
*"Nothing is written until you draft it."* `POST /billing/one-time/preview` runs stages
1–5 and prices nothing, so `DEF-936`'s sanctioned pattern — a Continue that does the
work its label implies — holds the document's guarantee exactly. **Proved in a browser:**
an account with no unit returns **422 BIZ-COMPLETENESS** and the rail stays on step 1.

**3 · The pre-change screen was NOT re-captured, and it is recorded as a gap rather than
presented as captured.** A sibling rebuilt `07-frontend/dist` at 11:27 with the rail
already in it, so the flat form could no longer be driven. The flat form's own browser
measurement is cited instead — `CR-100-BRC03-diff-03-08.md` §04, **16 elements compared ·
3 match · 4 differ · 9 absent**. **This is the direct cost of building before
classifying**, and it is the argument for the maintenance track rather than a note about
one screen.

**4 · §04 has NO carry-over map, so one was built from the product side.** The bulk run's
is on **p087–p088**; searched p084–p124 and those four dispositions appear nowhere else.
p099 says why: *"Every screen in this section is **new**."* The reuse specification is
therefore §2 of `CR-101-BRC03-one-time-wizard.md`: **24 elements · 20 unchanged or moved
intact · 1 relabelled · 3 moved and recast · 0 removed.** Nothing was rewritten.

**5 · The drawn rail label `What we bill on` is FOUR words against B14 rule 33's
three-word cap for a label, and it is built as drawn.** B14 rule 41 makes the drawing the
scope and names a contradiction with a signed rule as the one thing that reaches the PO.
**This is that one thing** — the only divergence in the seven recorded that is worth
their time; the other six are rule 38 (form construction is the UI rules' to decide) and
rule 31 (no internal reference on screen) doing their jobs.

### What the section's own money rule cost to keep: nothing, because it was already right

p100: *"There is no amount field, no description field and no line editor — and the
enforcement is that there is nowhere to put one."* `OneTimeBody` carries no such member
and `api._one_time_request` reads none. **This conversion does not go near it.**

### Two findings that are worth more than the rail

**`days_to_pay` is plumbed end to end and unreachable** (`DEF-BIL-5251`, high).
`OneTimeRequest.due_days` exists, `one_time.create` passes it to `create_one_time_run`,
and `api._optional_due_days` sits in the **same file** serving `POST /billing/runs` — but
`api._one_time_request` never reads it, so **no HTTP caller can set it.** It has been
that way since RC-W2-T4 closed `OQ-241` on 2026-08-23. The blueprint drew the missing
door on p102 as step 1's `Days to pay`.

**And the screen still tells a clerk the opposite** (`DEF-BIL-5252`, high). The *"Sending
the bill"* panel says a one-time bill *"can be drafted but not sent yet"*. The backend
deleted its matching sentence from `ONE_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` on 2026-08-23 **with a comment
explaining why**; the frontend string is a hardcoded constant nothing re-checks. Three
weeks live, every gate green. **A stated absence must die with the question it names** —
closing an OQ is a fan-out, and the catalogues are one of the surfaces.

### A duplicate filed, and said so

`DEF-BIL-5254` duplicates `DEF-BIL-5242`, filed earlier the same day for the same red.
The red was dated correctly (`git log -S`, `cf45a3d2`) and the **register was not grepped
before filing**. Closed as `duplicate`. Dating a red is half the habit; checking whether
somebody already filed it is the other half.

## 2026-09-14 · `CR-101-BRC03` §06 — **Fix a bill becomes the four-step wizard**, and it is MAINTENANCE

**Product Owner, 2026-09-12, verbatim: *"we will ahve to make it wizard - 4 steps"*.** The
ruling reached `05-prototype/04 Billing, As Built.pdf` §06 — nine entries drawn that day,
every one banded `REDESIGN … NEVER BUILT` — and it **never reached the code**. Two days
old when this lane opened. Nothing in this repository could see the gap, because no gate
here reads a rendered screen. Shipped in **2.265.0**.

### 1 · The classification, decided and written down rather than asked

The maintenance process asks one question — *can a user do this task today?* Driven in a
browser before a line moved: **yes**, end to end, on a real issued bill. So this is *"a
live screen redrawn end to end"*, which `22-product-maintenance-process.md` names by name
as **Maintenance**, borrowing exactly one thing from Build — the drawing step.

⚠ **This lane started down the Build track and was turned round mid-flight, and that is
recorded rather than tidied away.** It had begun a new file of new band, headline and
line-table components before the correction arrived. The process predicted the error in
as many words — *"it FEELS like building … a lane that follows the Build track loses
reproduce, blast radius, regression and the reporter"* — and all four were indeed
missing. The new file was **deleted unpushed**; the conversion was then done **in the
mounted file**, and the carry-over table below is what replaced the instinct to rebuild.

### 2 · The carry-over table, authored because the document has none for §06

`DISPOSITION` appears on p8, p11, p86, p230, p238 and p241 of the blueprint and **nowhere
between p129 and p144.** The bulk run has one (p86–88) and says why: *"Merging three steps
into one is the change most likely to drop something quietly."* §06 is not a merge, so the
document never drew one — **which does not excuse the conversion**, so the lane wrote it:

**Twenty as-built elements · 13 unchanged · 4 moved · 3 relabelled · 0 removed.**
It reconciles. The full table is `CR-101-BRC03-fix-a-bill-journey.md` §7.

### 3 · The open question the step-2 lane left, settled here in two halves

**(a) The drawn `CLASS R` band, the `CLASS` column of bare `R`/`C`/`D` letters and
`class R` in the subtitle are NOT built — and that is not a new ruling.**
`apps/billing/correction_reasons.py` already quotes TC-1a: *"The class is shown in the
operator's words … never as an enum value."* `single_correction.py` names the drawn
element itself: *"the class is shown as a WORD, not a code — the epic is explicit, and
**'R' is a thing to go and look up**"*. B14 rules 31 and 32 say the same. Two signed
sources, one direction, and the code has obeyed them since S30 shipped. Hard-won law 13
makes re-asking a settled question a bug in us. **Nothing goes to the PO from this.**

**(b) The band LENGTH is a judgment, recorded rather than asked.** Rule 33 caps a LABEL
*(a name)* at 3 words and a FACT at 6. **A band that says what a group DOES is a fact
about the group, not its name** — which is how BR-BIL-044's own nine ratified section
titles already ship at four and five words (*"What the customer will receive"*). And the
PO delegated exactly this when rule 33 was ratified: *"you can define what is reason we
are showing this text based on reason you can vary the lenght"*. So every band is six
words or fewer **in the drawing's own vocabulary**; the three that exceed six are
tightened with words already on the page — `CLASS C · THE BILL IS RIGHT; THE UTILITY
CHARGES LESS` becomes **The bill is right**, which is the drawing's OWN short form on
`26.4`'s breadcrumb. Nothing invented.

**One more drawn element refused on the same ground:** `26.4` draws *"Your ruling: 'you
dont touch the bill…'"* **inside the screen frame**. That is RATIONALE, which rule 33
gives zero words on screen, and it names an internal party. Not built.

### 4 · The one kit change, and why it is not a drawing losing to a UI rule

`WizardStep.continueLabel` — **opt-in, absent is `wizard.continue`**, so none of the other
fifteen wizards moves. B14 rule 36's own prescription for a kit that lacks a piece the
drawing needs. It is needed rather than nice: the drawing gives each of the first three
steps a different forward label, and step 3's — **Send for approval** — is the act that
RECORDS THE APPROVAL SIGNATURE and binds the figures through `preview_hash`. A frame
saying *"Continue"* there tells a clerk they are turning a page while they are signing.
That is CONTENT, so rule 38 leaves it to the drawing.

### 5 · What the money path did, watched rather than assumed

`10-scripts/cr101_fix_a_bill_walkthrough.mjs`, Chromium at 1440 and 1280, tenant
`brazosbend`. **Before:** the rail matched nothing (`0 steps`); bill `BL-2608-000048` was
corrected end to end. **After:** four steps on the rail; bill `BL-2608-000093` corrected
through them. In both runs the original kept its number and its **160.52 USD**, the
correction wrote a credit note and a replacement bill, and the preview wrote nothing.

⚠ **The first run went RED on *"the ORIGINAL bill was UPDATED: issued → corrected"*, and
the assertion was wrong rather than the product.**
`billing/0002_rls_w3_and_immutability` lets the trigger through an UPDATE that changes
**only** `status`, `updated_at` and the issue stamps, along `issued → paid | void |
corrected`. Written into the walkthrough so the next reader does not re-tighten it.

### 6 · Three things found and filed rather than folded in

* **`DEF-BIL-5249`** — the preview's line list renders **blank**. The engine serialises
  `label · original · corrected · delta`; the screen asks for `description · before ·
  after`, three keys the payload has never carried. `tsc` passes because all six are
  optional, and no fixture asserts a line's text. It is the blueprint's `LINE BY LINE`
  table and belongs to step 2's wave.
* **`DEF-BIL-5250`** — the correction **class** and the case **status** reach a clerk as
  `restatement`, `credit_only`, `pending_approval`. `billing.fix.class.*` and
  `billing.fix.status.*` hold **zero keys in all eleven catalogues**. Same shape as
  `DEF-BIL-5233`, which fixed the thirteen REASONS that morning and left these beside them.
* **A regression this lane caused and caught by LOOKING**, not by a check: the approval
  toast read *"…choose **Make the correction** to write it"* and that button no longer
  exists. Reworded in all eleven to *"Approved. Nothing is written yet."* — the
  instruction half dropped because the rail has already put the clerk in front of the
  button. **No test in this repository could have seen it.**

### 7 · Reaped, per the process's §10

Five catalogue keys the rail superseded — `previewAction`, `approveAction`,
`executeAction`, `step1`, `step2` — deleted from all eleven in the same commit, after
grepping `src/` (tests included) for every one. **A catalogue key nothing renders is a

`routing/screenIds.test.tsx` — the screen-id map holds 143 routes against `App.tsx`'s 149;

`billing/BillsPage.test.tsx` — the bills search grew a fourth leg (`address`) in

And one lint error on the file this lane changed, `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` in
