## 2026-09-14 · p050, "THE CHECK, IN FLIGHT" — THE ARCHITECTURE THE PO POINTED US AT, AND WHAT IT CORRECTS

The PO pasted the whole of screen 17's step-2 body — the seven chip rows at ~9,400 accounts,
the toolbar, the bulk bar, the six table columns and the footer — and said *"these are all on
step 2"*. Every figure they quoted is **p050** of `04 Billing, As Built.pdf`, captioned
`1440 × desktop · the check, in flight`, read here as an image at scale 2.0.

⚠ **THERE ARE TWO FRAMES OF SCREEN 17 AND WE HAD ONLY READ ONE.** p051 is the **settled**
frame (1,284 accounts, `Ready 1,251 · Needs you 12 · Held 21`). p050 is the **in-flight**
frame (`9,412 of 25,000`, `Ready 9,184 · Needs you 87 so far · Held 141 so far`). The chip
taxonomy is identical in both — seven categories, twenty-six chips — but **the in-flight frame
is where the product's hardest requirement lives**, and a lane reading only p051 would build a
screen that cannot exist at scale.

### The page's own verdict, in red: ⚠ "This screen does not exist"

> *"**At 25,000 accounts it is the difference between a usable product and an unusable one.**
> Today the clerk presses Prepare and **waits on one request**. Measured on real PostgreSQL, a
> run costs **137 ms per account** — so 25,000 accounts is **about 57 minutes**, and the
> request wall is about **60 seconds**. **There is no version of this where the clerk waits.**"*

### The four rules it states, verbatim

| Heading | What it says |
|---|---|
| **It opens immediately and fills in** | *"Prepare hands the pass to the worker and **Check opens at once**, populated as the pass proceeds. The progress figures are the job's own `done` and `total` — **already served, already polled. Nothing here needs new plumbing.**"* |
| **The clerk works while it runs** | *"Decisions on the accounts that have arrived are recorded immediately. **Eighty-seven decisions are waiting before the pass is half done**, and an hour spent clearing them is an hour the clerk did not spend waiting."* |
| **Every count says *so far*** | *"A count that will grow must say so, or a clerk reads *Needs you 87* as the final answer and plans their morning around it."* |
| **Six words carry the whole screen** | *"Nothing is being billed yet. You can close this page — it keeps going."* Two sentences, down from four, *"because the long version explained OUR mechanism rather than answering the clerk's question."* The two facts a clerk needs: **no bill exists**, and **leaving is allowed**. |

⚠ **AND THE HEADER CARRIES NO COUNT, DELIBERATELY** — *"`9,412 of 25,000` is already the first
KPI cell, and a figure shown twice is a figure a clerk has to reconcile. What is left on the
header is the one fact that appears nowhere else: **how long**."* That is B14 rule 33's
discipline applied to a number rather than a word.

### ⚠ TWO REQUIREMENTS THE DOCUMENT SAYS CANNOT BE DRAWN, AND BOTH ARE REAL WORK

1. **Refuse rather than run inline above the bar.** *"A deployment with no worker runs the
   check inline today and the request dies long before its own `ran inline` answer can be
   read."* `JOBS_REQUIRE_LIVE_WORKER` (`DEF-2487`) exists for exactly this and asks Celery
   whether any worker is alive before handing work to a queue in front of a waiting person.
   **Whether it is wired on this path is unverified and must be checked, not assumed.**
2. **Resume without re-walking.** *"A worker killed at 9,000 of 10,000 pays **22 minutes**
   again unless the checkpoint is used."*

### What this CORRECTS in our own record

`DEF-BIL-5258` (filed today) diagnosed the right problem — 26 chip counts computed in the
browser from an unpaginated payload — and proposed `GROUP BY` aggregates computed after the
pass. **The document's answer is better and cheaper:** the counts are the job's own `done` and
`total`, *"already served, already polled"*, and the screen opens at once rather than waiting
for any aggregate at all. The defect stands; its `prevention` column is superseded by this row.

⚠ **AND IT SETTLES THE PO'S CELERY QUESTION WITHOUT AMBIGUITY.** Not "Celery or online" —
**Celery, and the clerk never waits for it.** The earlier reading in `DEF-BIL-5258`, that
nothing in the front end asks for background mode, **was wrong** and was corrected by the
six-to-four lane: `billRunEndpoints.ts` posts `{"background": true}` and
`BillRunWizard.tsx:898` calls it through `calculateBillRunMaybeBackground`, polls the 202 and
distinguishes the inline 201. **What is unbuilt is the TIMING** — the blueprint fires the pass
from step 1's commit bar so Check opens already filling, while today the button sits inside
Check. ⚠ **THE ERROR WAS A GREP ARTIFACT AND IT IS THE THIRD OF THE DAY:** the search looked
for a literal `background: true` and the call is wrapped in a helper whose NAME carries the
word. Also today: `head -8` truncated a search into a false "no caller" claim, and `\>` in an
ERE was read as a literal `>` when it is a word boundary. **An absence found by grep is not an
absence** — confirm it by reading the call site, not by the silence of a pattern.

## 2026-09-14 · THE BILL RUN'S SCREENS ARE WRITTEN AGAIN — THE UI IS NOT REFITTED

**PO ruling, verbatim,** asked what should happen to the live six-step wizard while the
redrawn bill run is built:

> *"i dont think you will able to refit the Ui - keep them seperate - you will have to write
> screens again and plumbing if required - or reuse some fo the backend work"*

Said after: *"please undetstand we have rewroye the entire design for bill run - im not sure
whether you previous design will work or not - still you have made maany issues in Bill run -
how can we resolve this"*.

### What this rules

1. **THE SCREENS ARE WRITTEN AGAIN.** Not converted, not refitted, not diffed against what is
   there. New screens at their own place, built to the drawn frames.
2. **THE TWO ARE KEPT SEPARATE.** The live six-step wizard is not progressively mutated into
   the four-step one. A half-converted product — a correct rail over bodies built to nothing —
   is the state that produced *"many issues"*, and it is what this ruling ends.
3. **PLUMBING IS WRITTEN WHERE REQUIRED**, and **BACKEND WORK IS REUSED WHERE IT FITS.** The
   reuse is on the server, not on the screen.

### ⚠ THIS SUPERSEDES THE CLASSIFICATION THIS SESSION GAVE FOUR LANES

Earlier today all four billing journey lanes were told: *"MAINTENANCE, reuse the code, do not
rewrite."* That was derived correctly from `CLAUDE.md`'s test — *can a user do this task in the
product today?* — and from its clause *"a live screen redrawn end to end is MAINTENANCE"*.
**For the JOURNEY it still holds**: reproduce before fixing, locate the mounted file, blast
radius both ways, tell the reporter which build to look in. **For the SCREENS it is now
wrong**, by PO ruling.

⚠ **AND THE BLUEPRINT SAID SO ALL ALONG, IN ITS OWN CHIPS, WHICH NOBODY READ AS A
CLASSIFICATION.** Screen `17 Check` is chipped **`New build S27 S83 S90 S91 S92 S96`**; entry
`17.0 Checking` is **`New build S96`**; §04's front matter states *"Every screen in this
section is **new**: the tab exists and can draft, but no kind has ever had a screen of its
own"*; and every frame in §03–§08 carries the red banner `REDESIGN … NEVER BUILT`. **The
document classified these as NEW BUILDS on every page, and we classified them as maintenance
from a rule in `CLAUDE.md`.** Where the drawing states what a thing IS, that beats a rule we
applied to it from outside.

### Why refitting could not work, stated with the measurements

Screen 17 alone, product against drawing: the rail was **6 steps against 4**; the KPI strip is
**7 tiles carrying no money against 5, two of which carry money** (`WOULD BILL $2,361,904`,
`NEEDS YOU 87 · $31,204 at stake`); the filter is **6 sub-tabs grouped by DATA SOURCE against
7 categories and 26 chips grouped by WHAT NEEDS A DECISION**; the table columns differ; and
the entire in-flight behaviour — opens at once, fills as the pass proceeds, *"about 35 minutes
left"*, *"Nothing is being billed yet. You can close this page — it keeps going"* — does not
exist in any form. **Nothing of the old body is load-bearing for the new one.**

### What IS reused, and it is the expensive half

**The engine.** `run_calculate_job`'s own docstring: *"Phase 2 in a worker — the SAME
`runs.calculate_run` a request calls. That sameness is the point: the transport changed and the
work did not"* — `BR-BIL-052`'s per-account transaction, `BR-BIL-023`'s draft replacement,
`BR-BIL-055`'s a-break-never-stops-the-run. `p048` agrees from the other side: *"idempotent by
construction, not by a flag"*, stages 1–5 pure, stage 6 replaces rather than adds. And `p050`:
the progress figures are the job's own `done` and `total` — ***"already served, already polled.
Nothing here needs new plumbing."***

**So: keep the engine and the job transport. Write the screens and the read endpoints.**

### The root cause of the "many issues", named

**Every brief this session was written from PART of §03.** `p035` and `p046`–`p048` produced
the six-to-four dispatch; `p051` — the **settled** frame — produced a chip taxonomy that was
correct but incomplete; `p049` and `p050`, the **in-flight** frames where the whole
architecture lives, were never read until the PO pasted their contents back. Every lane
inherited whichever slice its coordinator had happened to open.

**The fix is a reading order, not a process change: read the WHOLE of a section as images and
build one element inventory for the journey BEFORE any lane is briefed.** §03 is `p028`–`p099`,
seventy-two pages. A brief assembled from fewer pages than the section contains is a brief that
will be corrected by the PO, and it was, four times today.

## 2026-09-14 · WHAT ACTUALLY RUNS BEHIND THE BILL RUN'S FOUR STEPS — AND THE STAGE NUMBERS ARE OFF BY ONE

The PO asked the engineering question the redesign rests on: *"tehre is whole data processing
behind the screen - in backend - it cannot be done online - im not sure how are you designing
that part … i dont know how you are enginering this - **our bill generation process work but we
need to run it from screen and that what we redesigned**"*.

**That last clause is the finding.** The engine is not being redesigned. Every phase already has
an endpoint. What the redraw changes is WHEN each is fired and WHAT the clerk sees while it runs.

### The eight stages, from `pipeline.py`'s `SEQUENCE` — named once in code, deliberately

| # | Stage | Owner | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `resolve-subscription` | billing | no |
| 2 | `measure-consumption` | billing | no |
| 3 | `price-usage` | rating | no |
| 4 | `apply-charges` | rating | no |
| 5 | `apply-discounts` | rating | no |
| 6 | `compute-tax` | rating | no |
| 7 | `assemble-document` | billing | **yes — the draft** |
| 8 | `post-to-ledger` | billing | **yes** |

`TERMINAL_STAGES = (7, 8)`; stages 1–6 are the pure front. **`137 ms per account` is these eight
stages, once.**

### ⚠ THE DRAWING'S STAGE NUMBERS ARE ONE BEHIND THE CODE — `DEF-BIL-5269`

Entry `17.0` on p049 reads *"stages 1–**5**, pure, nothing written"*. `pipeline.py` reads
*"Stages 1–**6** are the pure front."* **Both are correct for their own date.**
`apply-discounts` was INSERTED as stage 5 on **2026-08-22** (`DEF-502`) and everything after it
renumbered — `pipeline.py` says so itself: *"older prose citing stage 6/7 reads as 7/8"*. The
drawing was made on 2026-09-11 against `BR-BIL-037`'s original seven.

⚠ **WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: a break NAMES THE STAGE THAT FAILED (`BR-BIL-040`/`053`), and the
stage decides WHICH TAB THE FIX ROUTES TO.** A missing base charge is `resolve-subscription`, so
it routes to Plans & Rates — *"never on Reads: not one reading is wrong."* **A lane building the
Check screen's *What is wrong* column to the drawn numbers mislabels every break and sends
clerks to the wrong screen.** Build from `SEQUENCE`, never from a number printed on a page.

⚠ **AND WHY STAGE 5 EXISTS AT ALL IS THE BEST ARGUMENT IN THIS REPO FOR READING A LIST ALOUD.**
`BR-BIL-037`'s seven stages had **no discount stage**, so `apps/rating/discount_pricing.py` was
priced by nothing on the bill path and *"an enrolled customer's reduction never reached an
invoice."* **No per-function test could catch it, because the gap was a missing STAGE rather
than a wrong one — and the PO found it by reading the list aloud.**

### The five phases mapped to the four drawn steps

| Step | Endpoint | Runs | Online or batch |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 Scope** | reads only | the counts card | online |
| **1 → commit bar** | `POST .../calculate` `{"background": true}` | phase 1 gather (writes nothing) then phase 2 draft | **batch · Celery · 202 + poll** |
| **17.0 Checking** | polls the job | `calculate_run(…, on_progress, already_done)` over all eight stages per account | batch |
| **2 Check** | `POST .../exceptions/{case}/resolve` | one recorded decision carrying who made it; `case_ids` is `BR-BIL-060`'s bulk — N rows sharing **one `bulk_action_id` minted by the SERVER**, because only the server can share an id across rows | **online** |
| **2, after a decision** | scoped `calculate` | re-prices THAT account, **replacing its draft rather than adding one** | micro-batch, 1 account |
| **3 Sign off** | `POST .../release` | **not generation — the drafts already exist.** A gate: `BR-BIL-053`, *"the run cannot enter phase 4 with an unresolved break"* | online check |
| **4 Send** | `POST .../issue` → `enqueue_issue` | phase 5, with issue date, release date and the **pinned template id + version** | **batch · Celery** |

**Two background passes, not four.** Prepare-and-draft at 1→2, issue-and-dispatch at 3→4;
everything between is online row writes.

`run_calculate_job`: *"Phase 2 in a worker — the **SAME** `runs.calculate_run` a request calls.
That sameness is the point: the transport changed and the work did not."*

### What is genuinely missing, and it is small next to what exists

The screen consuming progress PROGRESSIVELY (the counts exist; the screen waits for the whole
payload) · `already_done` **persisted** so a killed worker resumes — **the parameter exists;
whether it is checkpointed is UNVERIFIED and must be checked, not assumed** · the refusal when
no worker is alive (`JOBS_REQUIRE_LIVE_WORKER` exists, wiring unverified) · the scope resolver
(route / area / named set) · three run-level default columns and their migration · and
`DEF-BIL-5258`, the counts computed in the browser.

**No new billing logic, no money math, nothing near ❄️ B4/B5.**

## 2026-09-14 · FOUR ENGINE QUESTIONS FROM THE PO, AND TWO OF MY ANSWERS WERE WRONG

The PO read the eight-stage table back and asked four things of it. Two corrected a claim I
had made; two found gaps. All four are worth the next agent's time.

### ⚠ 1 · `post-to-ledger` DOES NOT RUN DURING CHECKING, AND IT DOES NOT WRITE

**I stated both wrongly.** PO: *"you will ahve to run this ste when invoice/bills are approved
without that you will end up creating worng entries"*. **They are right as a principle and the
code already honours it — my table did not.**

`pipeline.py`, verbatim: ***"STAGE 7 — post-to-ledger. EMITS. WRITES NOTHING. EVER."*** Billing
emits `{invoice id, account, service_date, per-GL bucket sums, AR total, currency}` and
**the ledger is the sole writer** — `CLAUDE.md` hard rule 5 and `BR-BIL-011`; `ledger/0004`'s
trigger is the fence and `posting_seam.post_bill_issue` is the one door. And `issue.py`'s header
says it is ***EMITTED THERE since 2026-08-11*** — at issue, after sign-off.

`runs.py` imports `assemble_document`, `measure_consumption` and `resolve_subscription` and
**does not import `post_to_ledger` at all.** So **Checking runs stages 1–7**; stage 8 is not
reached until issue. The corrected table: **stage 7 `assemble-document` writes the DRAFT; stage
8 emits at issue and writes nothing, ever.**

### 2 · The account set is not a stage — it is resolved before them

The eight stages run PER ACCOUNT. Membership is resolved in the prepare pass (`prepared_for` →
`PreparedRun`) and shown on Scope's counts card *before* anything runs — `Units in the cycle
1,502 → Accounts to bill 1,284`, which the drawing annotates *"Two numbers, not one … The gap
between them is where every master-account failure lives."*

### 3 · The header facts are frozen at DRAFT, from what gather captured

`assemble_document`: *"THE SNAPSHOT (PO ruling 2026-08-11: 'you have to keep lock data for that
bill and save the instance'). The payload is assembled HERE, at draft time, from what the
gather step captured — **not at issue, and never by re-reading live rows** … Sarah marries
between the run and the release, and the bill goes out in her new name for a period billed
under her old one. **The draft carries what was TRUE WHEN IT WAS PRICED.**"* Issue adds the due
date, stamps the GL account and the template, and freezes it.

### ⚠ 4 · NO CYCLE RUN CHECKS THAT AN ACCOUNT STARTS WHERE ITS LAST BILL ENDED — `DEF-BIL-5270`

PO: *"where is the check that last bill of any specific account you will ahve to check last read
from that invocie/bill otherwise you will ahve probelm"*.

Billing does not compute the delta. `runs._readings_for` asks metering through
`billing_reads_for_unit(unit_id, period_start, period_end, service_codes)`, and metering answers
with a figure it **stored when the read was taken**: *"`consumption` is metering's stored figure
— `(current − prior) × multiplier`, unrounded (B4.4)"*. **The anchor is the previous READ, not
the read the last ISSUED bill closed on.**

⚠ **AND THE FINAL-BILL PATH HAS THE CHECK THE CYCLE PATH LACKS.** `cut_bill.py`: *"unbilled day
is the day AFTER the last issued period end"*. Nothing equivalent exists on the cycle run.
Scope's `Continuous — no gap, no overlap` compares run PERIODS, so it passes over this
entirely. A skipped read, a re-read, a meter exchange, or a draft that was never issued puts
them out of step — **and the failure is money in both directions: a gap bills nobody for real
consumption, an overlap bills a customer twice.**

## AND THE RE-PRICE QUESTION, WHICH IS THE ARCHITECTURAL ONE

PO: *"you calculate bill in step 2 and saved them as draft - but due to changes suggested by
user - you will ahve to reculate many bills - how are you going to ahndle that"*.

| Case | What exists | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| One account, one fix | `POST .../breaks/{account}/retry` — *"ONE ACCOUNT, STAGES 1–6, AND NOTHING ELSE IS TOUCHED"*, and a retry that still fails is a REFUSAL not a 201 | ~137 ms |
| A bulk decision on N accounts | `resolve_cases(case_ids=[…])` records N decisions under one server-minted `bulk_action_id` — **and stops there** | N retries, or a full re-run |
| **A shared fix** — a tariff, rate version or plan corrected in Plans & Rates | **NOTHING.** No way to say *"re-price everyone on this plan"* | full re-run ≈ **21 minutes at 9,412** |

**Why this is cost and not corruption:** *"Re-running [assemble-document] for an account already
drafted in this run REPLACES that draft rather than adding a second one"*, and stages 1–6 are
pure, so a re-run always converges. A full re-run is always RIGHT; it is only expensive.

⚠ **BUT THERE IS A CORRECTNESS RISK INSIDE CASE 2, AND IT REACHES SIGN-OFF.** A decision is
recorded and the draft is NOT re-priced. `BR-BIL-053` gates phase 4 on *unresolved* breaks — a
**resolved but un-re-priced** case passes that gate. So a clerk can bulk-decide 44 estimates,
see `WOULD BILL` unchanged, and sign off on stale numbers. **The drawn strip's own sub-line is
*"updates as you decide"*, which is exactly the behaviour that does not exist.**

**What is needed, and it is not new billing logic:** a scoped re-price taking a SET of accounts
— the ones a decision touched, or the ones a changed plan covers — run through `calculate_run`
with a narrowed list, in the same worker, on the same progress channel. Per-account
transactions and draft replacement already work. The drawing marks it **NEW** on p052 item 7
and says why it is safe: *"it is safe because the engine already guarantees it."*

**Added to the build scope:** scoped re-price by account set · bulk decision wired to re-price
the set it touched · sign-off gate extended to *decided but not re-priced* · and `DEF-BIL-5270`.
**Three are wiring. The fourth is a correctness gap the PO predicted before we found it.**

## 2026-09-14 · THE BILL TEMPLATE IS DECIDED AT STEP 1 SCOPE, NOT AT ISSUE

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"in this step 1 scope - you will ahve to also decide on billing
template"*.

### What this reverses, stated rather than assumed (law 13)

**The blueprint does NOT draw a template picker, deliberately.** Its `DEFAULTS` group on p047
holds four controls — *when there is no reading · when a bill looks unusually large · unusual
days · label this run* — and no template. Two pages address the absence and **neither
re-argues it**: p087 and p099 record that a panel headed *"What this step no longer asks you"*,
which existed on screen to explain *"why a template picker and a typed due date are absent"*,
is **REMOVED** — *"a note about a design decision taken long ago, printed to a clerk on every
run. Its content belongs in this document."*

**So the exclusion is an OLD decision the drawing inherited, and this repo has no decision-log
row for it.** That is why this ruling is recorded with its reasoning rather than as a one-line
change: the next agent will find a drawing with no picker and must know why the product has one.

### Where the template is decided TODAY, and why that is the wrong moment

The run-level pin **already exists** — `template_pin_explicit` on `issue_run`, and `issue.py`
describes it in its own words: *"an EXPLICIT pin typed by the clerk deliberately governs the
whole pass."* The run carries two counters, `template_resolved_per_account` against
`template_pinned_by_run`, and *"a run where both are non-zero is NORMAL, not an error"* — a
tenant with one template resolves the same fallback for everybody.

⚠ **BUT IT FIRES AT ISSUE, WHICH IS STEP 4.** And `issue.py` also carries
**`template_problems`** — *"distinct reasons a bill could not resolve its own template, with the
number of bills each affected"*. **A bill CAN fail to find a template**, and today that failure
is discovered AFTER Scope, AFTER Check and AFTER sign-off — at the moment of issue, with the
clerk's approval already given.

**That is the same failure shape the whole redraw exists to remove.** p048's argument for moving
pricing into step 1 is *"step 2 opens with money on every row"*, and the argument here is its
twin: **a template that cannot resolve should be a count on step 1's card, not a surprise on
step 4.**

### What is built

1. **Step 1 Scope gains a template decision**, alongside the four drawn defaults. It sets the
   run's explicit pin — the `template_pin_explicit` path that already exists — rather than
   inventing a second mechanism.
2. **The counts card reports template resolution** the way it reports everything else: how many
   accounts resolve their own, how many take the run's pin, and **how many resolve NEITHER**,
   with `template_problems`' reasons behind the count.
3. **Step 4's specimen renders with the pinned template**, so what the clerk approves and what
   the customer receives are the same artifact.
4. **The per-account fallback is untouched.** `template_resolved_per_account` stays legitimate;
   the run pin governs where a clerk has deliberately set one, exactly as `issue.py` already
   describes.

⚠ **THIS DOES NOT MOVE THE FREEZE.** `assemble_document` stamps the template AT ISSUE and that
is unchanged — *"Issue is a separate act (US-BIL-005) that sets the due date, stamps the GL
account and the template, and freezes it."* **Deciding is not stamping.** Step 1 records the
clerk's CHOICE; issue still pins the version onto each invoice, so a template edited between
scope and release cannot silently change a bill a clerk already approved.

### The divergence from the drawing, recorded

B14 rule 41 says the product matches the blueprint exactly, and this adds a control the
blueprint does not draw. **A PO ruling outranks a drawing** — the drawing's own note calls the
absence an inherited decision rather than a finding of the redraw — so the control is BUILT and
the divergence is recorded here and in the conformance file. **The drawing is not amended by
us**; if the PO wants the picker drawn, that is a change to their document, not ours.

### ⚠ AND STAGE 2 IS ASSETS AS WELL AS READS — MY TABLE SAID ONLY READS

**PO, same exchange:** *"in this stage you also need to find out all assets"*. **Correct, and
the code already does it; the summary given in chat was what was incomplete.**

`measure-consumption` resolves a unit's billable quantity from **two different sources**, and
which one applies is decided by the SERVICE's own declaration (`tenant_services.metered`,
`BR-RAT-081`), never by what happens to be installed:

* **METERED** → the read. `consumption` arrives as metering's stored
  `(current − prior) × multiplier`, already post-multiplier, always with its unit.
* **UNMETERED** → the ASSETS. `BR-RAT-090` (`DEF-1813`): *"an UNMETERED service's billable
  quantity is a COUNT of its assets on the unit"*, and metering publishes that count on the same
  row — `asset_count`, **observed at the service-period end date** — carried UNPRICED and
  **WITHOUT A UNIT**, because *"three carts is three things, not three of any measure"*.
* **CAPACITY-BASED** → the asset's size. Metering publishes `installed_capacity` and
  `capacity_uom` beside the count.

**Two separate absence reasons exist and they are deliberately not one:**
`ABSENT_ASSET_COUNT_UNAVAILABLE` (the count itself cannot be had) and the capacity/size-class
absence (*"an asset records no size class"*). Collapsing them would hide which fix is needed.

**Why this matters beyond tidiness:** fire is trash's arithmetic — the size class picks the
price and the COUNT multiplies it, so one 6" line with two 2" lines is `$60.00 + 2 × $12.00` on
two bill lines. **That number comes out of stage 2, not stage 3.** A stage-2 summary that says
only *"the reads"* invites a lane to build a screen that cannot explain why a trash-only or
fire-only account has a quantity at all.

**The corrected row:** *Stage 2 `measure-consumption` — reads AND assets: the metered quantity
from the read, the unmetered quantity from `asset_count`, and `installed_capacity` +
`capacity_uom` for capacity-priced services. A missing read is a decision, never a zero; an
unavailable asset count and an unstated size class are two different decisions.*

## 2026-09-14 · A CHIP IS AN ACTION — AN ACCOUNT NEEDING TWO ACTIONS APPEARS IN TWO CHIPS

**PO ruling, verbatim,** on whether the Check screen's tags sum to their band or exceed it:

> *"if we have to take 2 actions on it to bill it then it should come in two chips"*

Put to them as account **100263, M. Okonkwo** — no reading was taken **and** its multiplier
changed this cycle. **One account, two cases.** The ruling: it appears under **both**
*Missing read* and *Multiplier changed*.

### What this settles, and it was a real collision

The document disagrees with itself. **Its prose says so twice** — p041 and p046: *"Twelve
accounts raise nineteen case rows … so the tags under Needs you · 12 sum to more than twelve,
**on purpose**."* **Its pictures say otherwise** — both drawn frames sum to exactly the band
(`4+3+1+1+1+1+1 = 12`, and `31+22+9+12+6+4+3 = 87`).

**The prose wins, and B14 rule 37 is why rather than anyone's judgement:** *"a figure drawn in a
wireframe is an ILLUSTRATION, never a fact to build to."* The drawn sums are figures; the
sentence on p041 is a rule. Rule 37 exists for exactly this collision.

⚠ **THE PO'S REASONING IS BETTER THAN THE ONE PUT TO THEM AND IS THE ONE TO BUILD FROM.** The
argument offered was work-list completeness — a clerk filtering *Multiplier changed* must not
miss 100263. **The PO named the unit instead: A CHIP IS AN ACTION.** A tag does not count
accounts, and it does not really count "cases" either — it counts **things a clerk must do
before this account can be billed**. Two actions, two chips. One action, one chip. That
definition decides every future chip without another ruling, which the completeness argument
would not have done.

### The three consequences, all forced by the ruling

1. **Tags sum to MORE than their band**, and the gap is the number of accounts needing more than
   one action. `Needs you · 12` over tags summing to 19 means twelve accounts and nineteen jobs.
2. **The band stays ACCOUNTS.** This is not optional: *"Nobody is missing"* — `1,251 + 12 + 21 =
   1,284` — is account arithmetic tied to the cycle's 1,284 accounts. Making the band count
   cases would break the one line on the screen the document calls *"the most important thing"*.
3. **The screen must say the tags count actions**, in **≤6 words** (rule 33 — a fact), or the
   strip reads as broken arithmetic. **Rationale is ZERO words on screen**, so the sentence
   states the fact and explains nothing.

### ⚠ AND THIS REVERSES THE TIE-OUT TEST THIS SESSION GAVE A LANE, TWICE

The wave-1 brief told its lane that `4+3+1+1+1+1+1 = 12` was **the proof a chip list had been
read correctly**. It is the opposite: **a tag row that sums exactly to its band has been
misread, or is drawn from an illustration.** The lane caught it by reading p041 and filed
`DEF-BIL-5273`. **Any future check on this strip asserts `sum(tags) ≥ band`, never equality**,
and the tie-out that remains valid is the ACCOUNT arithmetic — `ready + needs you + held =
accounts in the cycle`.

**Question 2 — whether `Over 60 days` is a disjoint bucket or a subset — is NOT settled by this
ruling and remains open.** It is a different question: there the document states no rule at all
and only two drawings disagree.

## 2026-09-14 · THE WAITING BANDS ARE DERIVED FROM THE CYCLE'S FREQUENCY AND SET AT CYCLE LEVEL

**PO ruling, verbatim,** asked whether `Over 60 days` is a disjoint band or a subset:

> *"it depends on cycle frquency i fcycle is for 15 days then 12 to 18 days become a band if 30
> days then 25 to 35 days become a band , so on and so forth - we should capture this at value
> at cycle level so that we can control it and user can set it - while we provide a defualt
> value"*

### ⚠ THE QUESTION AS PUT WAS THE WRONG QUESTION, AND BOTH OFFERED OPTIONS WERE WRONG

It was put as *disjoint bucket or subset*, on the evidence that Check draws `10 + 9 + 2 = 21`
(clean) while screen 20 draws `38 + 9 + 2 = 49` over a band of `47` (an excess of exactly 2).
Two options were offered — three disjoint buckets, or two buckets plus a severity flag — and a
recommendation given for the first.

**The PO rejected the frame.** `14 days` and `60 days` are not thresholds at all: **they are
MONTHLY-CYCLE ASSUMPTIONS HARDCODED AS DAYS**, and on any other frequency they mean nothing. A
fortnightly utility's *"Under 14 days"* is an entire billing cycle of lateness; a quarterly
one's *"Over 60 days"* has not yet reached its next bill.

⚠ **AND B14 RULE 37 ALREADY COVERED THIS AND NOBODY APPLIED IT.** *"Every number drawn in a
wireframe is an ILLUSTRATION, never a fact to build to."* **`14` and `60` are drawn numbers.**
Both options offered to the PO treated them as the specification and argued only about set
membership. The rule that would have caught it was quoted in the same session, to three
different lanes, about other numbers.

### What is ruled

1. **The waiting bands are DERIVED FROM THE CYCLE'S FREQUENCY**, not fixed in days. The PO's own
   worked figures: a **15-day** cycle bands at roughly **12–18 days**; a **30-day** cycle bands
   at roughly **25–35 days**; *"and so on and so forth"*.
2. **The value is CAPTURED AT CYCLE LEVEL so a tenant can set it.** It is configuration, not a
   constant, and it belongs on the cycle because the cycle is what defines the frequency.
3. **WE SUPPLY A DEFAULT** so no tenant has to configure it before billing works.
4. **The bands are therefore DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION** — they are ranges, and an account cannot
   sit in two ranges. That settles the original question as a consequence rather than as a
   choice: **screen 20's drawn `38` is an illustration that does not tie, and Check's clean
   `10 + 9 + 2 = 21` is the shape to build.**

### What this forces, and some of it is new scope

* **The chip LABEL is computed, not literal.** *"Under 14 days"* is a monthly tenant's rendering
  of *within this cycle*. A fortnightly tenant sees different words from the same component, so
  the label is derived from the cycle's setting and the catalogue string is a pattern.
* **A cycle-level setting and its migration**, plus a surface for a tenant to set it. Neither is
  in the bill-run rebuild's scope as tabled; both are added.
* **A default that is defensible without configuration** — expressed against the cycle's own
  length rather than in absolute days.

### ⚠ ONE QUESTION THIS RULING DOES NOT ANSWER, AND IT IS NOT BEING GUESSED

**The held queue spans cycles.** An account held in September and still held in November has
waited across more than one cycle, and possibly across a change of frequency. **Which cycle's
bands apply — the one it was held FROM, or the one being run NOW?** The ruling settles where
the value lives and does not say which value applies to a queue that outlives its cycle. It is
recorded here as OPEN and will be put to the PO with a worked figure rather than decided by a
lane.

**Both Check frames and screen 20 draw the queue, so the answer changes what two screens count.**

## 2026-09-14 · "NO HARDCODING" — SWEPT ACROSS BILLING, AND THE RESULT IS BETTER THAN EXPECTED

**PO, verbatim,** on being told that `14` and `60` were monthly-cycle assumptions hardcoded as
days: ***"no hardcoiding"***.

Taken as a general rule rather than a note about two numbers, so the module was swept rather
than the sentence merely agreed with.

### What the sweep found

**Billing does not hardcode its thresholds, and it avoids doing so deliberately.**

* **`Unusually large` / `Unusually small`** — the two chips most at risk — are **already
  tenant-configurable and billing does not own the value.** `read_analysis.py` states the
  reasoning in its own words: the ratio and the threshold are *"all read off"* the analysis
  rather than recomputed, because a local copy *"would be a second implementation that drifts
  the day a threshold changes"*, and the `days_threshold` verdict is *"a WARNING judged against
  **TENANT BOUNDS**"*.
* **`budget.py`'s `> 20%`** cites `US-BIL-020 §7` — a signed figure, not an invented one.
* Every `timedelta(days=1)` in the module is **arithmetic, not policy** — *the day after the
  last issued period end*, *the day before a rate version starts*. A day is a day.

### ⚠ SO WHY DID THE WAITING BANDS ESCAPE? BECAUSE THEY WERE NEVER BUILT

`Under 14 days · Escalated · Over 60 days` exist **only as drawn chips**. No code holds them, so
no lane ever had to decide where the value lived, and the numbers sat unchallenged on a page
until the PO read them against a fortnightly cycle.

**That is the generalisable lesson and it is not about hardcoding at all:** a constant inside
code gets reviewed the first time someone edits the file. **A constant inside a DRAWING is
reviewed by nobody**, and it arrives at the lane that builds the screen looking exactly like a
specification. B14 rule 37 is the rule that catches it — *"every number drawn in a wireframe is
an ILLUSTRATION"* — and this session quoted rule 37 to three lanes about other numbers while
putting `14` and `60` to the PO as though they were thresholds to choose between.

### The standing instruction for the rebuild

**Every number the Check screen shows a clerk is either DERIVED (from the cycle, the run, or the
account) or CONFIGURED (tenant or cycle level, with a default we supply). None is a literal in
the component.** Where a drawn number has no home yet — as the waiting bands did — **the home is
part of the build, not a follow-up.**

## 2026-09-14 · THE BILL RUN'S CHECKPOINT WAS REACHABLE BY NOTHING, AND THE BAR ABOVE WHICH A RUN IS REFUSED RATHER THAN RUN INLINE (CR-105-BRC03)

Blueprint p050, the panel headed *"What it must also do, but cannot be drawn"*, verbatim:

> **Refuse rather than run inline above the bar** — a deployment with no worker runs the check
> inline today and the request dies long before its own *ran inline* answer can be read. And
> **resume without re-walking**: a worker killed at 9,000 of 10,000 pays **22 minutes** again
> unless the checkpoint is used.

Two requirements. **The first was built and unreachable; the second was not built at all.**

### 1 · THE RESUME — BUILT, TESTED, DOCUMENTED, AND DEAD (`DEF-BIL-5284`)

Everything the resume needs already existed and is good work. `apps/billing/run_resume.py`
writes a cursor. `core.jobs.record_progress` persists it. The `jobs` table has a `checkpoint`
column. `core.jobs.start` allows `failed → running` and says *"checkpoint SURVIVES"*.
`CELERY_TASK_ACKS_LATE` is on so a dead worker's message comes back.

**One hop was missing and it made all of it dead weight.** A worker killed by `SIGKILL` writes
nothing — `run_job` catches `Exception`, and a process that dies raises none — so the record is
left saying `running`. The redelivery then reached `start()`, which refuses a `running` record,
and raised

    JobsError: job … is running — cannot start (resume is failed→running)

So the run did not pay 22 minutes again. **It never finished at all**, and the record said
`running` for ever with nobody working on it.

**Why nothing saw it, and this is the part worth keeping.** `tests/test_cr051_run_scale.py`
proves the resume with a job record it builds itself — a dict whose `id` is the BILL RUN's
primary key, never saved to `jobs`, never passed through a status transition — and calls
`run_jobs.run_calculate_job(record)` directly. Ten cases, all green, all skipping the one hop
that refused. And `10-scripts/cr051_kill_and_resume.py`, the script tc11 calls *the real proof*,
got to the checkpoint only by hand-writing `core_jobs.fail(job_id, "worker killed (SIGKILL)")`
first — **supplying the missing hop itself**, and then passing honestly.

**Built:** `core.jobs.reclaim` (`running → failed`, checkpoint untouched) and `core.jobs.resume`,
which `apps/tenancy/tasks.run_pending_job` now calls instead of `run_pending`.
`tests/test_cr105_run_transport.py` drives every case through that task.

**The judgment call, and its worked figure.** A reclaim is only safe if a redelivery proves the
previous attempt is dead, and nothing in the record can say so — there is no owner column and no
heartbeat, and adding either is a migration onto a table five modules share. What makes it true
is the broker: kombu re-delivers an unacked Redis message after `visibility_timeout`, **whose
default is 3,600 s while the hard task limit is 8,520 s** — so a legitimate 71-minute bill run
was already being re-delivered while it was still running (`DEF-BIL-5285`), and nothing had gone
wrong only because `start()` was refusing the second delivery. `visibility_timeout` is now
`CELERY_TASK_TIME_LIMIT + 300` = **8,820 s**, set in one expression with the limit it depends on,
so a redelivery cannot arrive until after the hard limit has killed whatever was running.

**The clerk's own re-press is deliberately NOT a resume.** It mints a new record with no
checkpoint and re-prices every account, which is what `test_cr051_run_scale.py` tc6 has always
asserted and what a clerk who has just fixed a plan needs.

### 2 · THE BAR — 300 ACCOUNTS, AND IT IS ARITHMETIC OVER TWO PUBLISHED FIGURES

`api.run_calculate` and `api.run_findings` asked `would_run()` and, on a `False`, **logged a line
nobody reads and ran the whole pass inline anyway**. On a 25,000-account run that is a dead
connection at 60 seconds over a server still working 57 minutes later, and the `background:
false` member that would have explained it travels in a body nobody receives.

**Where 300 comes from.** p050 publishes both inputs: *"a run costs 137 ms per account"* and
*"the request wall is about 60 seconds"*. The figure in the code is **0.17 s**, which is the same
measurement re-taken with row-level security ENFORCED (`DEF-2717`; p050's 137 ms was measured
with RLS bypassed — reported, not corrected in the drawing). So the largest run that can finish
inside the wall is **60 ÷ 0.17 = 352 accounts**, and the bar is **300** — 51 seconds of billing,
leaving about 9 seconds for everything a request does that is not billing.

**This is not a decision about whether work goes to a worker.** That is still the caller's
`background` flag, and `run_jobs.py`'s standing reason for having no row bar — *"there is no
equivalent figure for a bill run anywhere in this repository"* — has expired, because CR-051
task 21 measured it. This is the narrower question of what to do when the caller asked for a
worker and there is not one.

**Below the bar nothing changes.** A small utility with no broker at all keeps the inline
fallback it has today; that is why this file chose an inline fallback over the import's flat
refusal in the first place, and `tests/test_cr105_run_transport.py` tc7 is what stops the fix
quietly taking it away. `BILLING_INLINE_ACCOUNT_BAR` is a declared setting and `0` switches it
off.

The refusal is `billing.run.noWorker`, written in all eleven catalogues. English: *"Billing
cannot run right now. Nothing has changed."* — two sentences, five words and three, which is
B14 rule 33 for a consequence, and no rationale on screen.

### ⚠ WHAT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN BUILT

**A job that FAILED is still re-delivered by nothing** (`DEF-BIL-5287`). A worker KILLED mid-pass
now resumes; a soft time limit or a raised body leaves a `failed` record with a perfectly usable
checkpoint and no retry policy, no reaper, and no `manage.py run_pending_jobs` — a command
`apps/tenancy/tasks.py` has named in a docstring and in an operator-facing error message since
2026-08-19 and which has never existed. How many times a money job may re-attempt itself, and
after how long, is a product decision rather than a lane's. `core.jobs.resume` is the entry point
either answer would call.

## 2026-09-14 · "MY APPEND" IS A STATEMENT ABOUT POSITION, NOT AUTHORSHIP — AND IT DUPLICATED NINE AND A HALF THOUSAND BYTES

**A lane found this in its own push and named the mechanism exactly; the coordinator then found
the same fault in ITS OWN pushes, by looking only because the lane said so.**

The lane's words: *"I computed 'my append' as the working copy minus my base, which is a
statement about **position, not authorship**, so a sibling's row inside that window got replayed
onto a tip that already had it."* It caught the instance in `10-defect-log.csv` — a duplicated
`DEF-BIL-5283` — filed it as `DEF-BIL-5289`, and rebuilt that register **by id**.

⚠ **IT DID NOT CATCH THE SAME FAULT IN `02-decision-log.md`, AND THERE IT REPLAYED 9,571 BYTES.**
Three coordinator entries — *A CHIP IS AN ACTION*, *THE WAITING BANDS ARE DERIVED FROM THE
CYCLE'S FREQUENCY*, and *"NO HARDCODING"* — appear TWICE on the branch, as one contiguous block,
byte-identical. They sat inside the lane's window and were replayed onto a tip that already held
them.

### The technique that did it, which the coordinator had been using all session

    MARK=$(wc -c < file)      # before appending
    cat >> file <<'EOF' ... EOF
    tail -c +$((MARK+1)) file > my-block
    cat <tip's file> my-block > new

**Every step is defensible and the whole is wrong.** `tail -c +MARK` means *"the bytes after
this offset"*, and on a file any lane may append to, that is **whatever arrived after that
offset — not what I wrote.** The prefix proof does not catch it: the result IS a superset of the
tip, so `diff <(head -c N new) tip` passes, `--numstat` shows insertions and **zero deletions**,
and every check law 11 prescribes comes back clean. **A duplicate is not a revert, and nothing in
this repo was looking for one.**

### ⚠ AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THE FIX WOULD HAVE DESTROYED A LANE'S WORK

Excising *"from the second copy to end of file"* looked obviously right and removed **15,843
bytes where the duplicate is 9,571** — because a lane had appended its own entry after the
replayed block. **The size mismatch is the only thing that revealed it**, and it was noticed only
because the script printed both lengths and compared them instead of assuming. The correct
excision runs from the separator before the duplicate to the separator before the NEXT genuine
entry, and is proved by `dup == orig` byte-for-byte before anything is written.

*"Verify before you remediate"* is already law 11's clause, written after a false alarm led to a
`git checkout` over six shared files. **This is that clause's second life: the alarm was real
this time and the remedy was still wrong.**

### What to do instead

**Derive an append by AUTHORSHIP, never by position.** Keep the exact bytes you are adding in
their own file from the moment you compose them — write the heredoc to `my-block` and
`cat my-block >> file`, rather than appending first and recovering the block by offset
afterwards. Then `cat <tip's file> my-block > new` is true by construction.

**And add the check that would have caught it**, because the prefix proof cannot: after building
`new`, assert that **no heading, id or row it contains occurs more than once**. For
`10-defect-log.csv` that is the id column, which is why rebuilding **by id** was the right repair.
For `02-decision-log.md` it is the `## ` headings. A one-line `sort | uniq -d` over either would
have failed loudly on both instances.

## 2026-09-14 · THE BILL DETAIL IS THE SEVEN DRAWN GROUPS, THE EMBEDDED VIEWER IS GONE ON A RULING, AND THE HEADER'S EMPHASIS WAS BUILT BACKWARDS (CR-105-BRC03)

**Screen S30 · BIL-05, `/:tenant/billing/bills/:invoiceId`.** Built from the Billing blueprint's
entry 02.1 — `05-prototype/04 Billing, As Built.pdf` p011–p018, sha256 `137a2a48…0971`, read AS
IMAGES at scale 2 and cropped to 5–6× for the header and the annotations (B14 rule 42). Routed as
**MAINTENANCE**: a user can do this task in the product today, so it is the redesign case
`22-product-maintenance-process.md` names on purpose, and it reproduced in a browser before any
code was read.

### 1 · THE ONE THING REMOVED, AND IT IS THE ONLY ROW IN THE DOCUMENT PERMITTED TO GO

Product Owner, **2026-09-11**, verbatim: *"we dont what full view of the document - you give a
link to download but full view of document is not requires - it does not add any value to user"*.

The Document tab's body was a **760px `<iframe>`** pointed at
`/api/{tenant}/invoices/{id}/document.pdf`, under a banner reading **CR-053 TASK 3 — THE OUTPUT
IS THE SCREEN**. Three days after the ruling it was still in the product, on a screen whose own
drawing is banner-marked *"REDESIGN drawn 2026-09-11, still unbuilt at Version 35 … NEVER
BUILT."*

**The banner is deleted with the frame.** CR-053 task 3's argument is superseded, and a comment
carrying a reversed decision's reasoning is exactly what a later lane restores the thing from —
hard-won law 1 with the argument still attached. The three test cases that pinned the frame were
**rewritten rather than deleted**, so a case goes RED if it comes back; a removed case proves
nothing.

**What replaced it answers more than it did.** The two things a clerk actually needed from a
rendered page — *does a saved copy exist* and *can I send it to someone* — are now stated:
`↓ Download the bill as sent (PDF)`, `Open it in a new tab ↗`, and `Saved copy — Kept — 2 pages`
off the server's own `pdf_page_count`.

⚠ **SCREEN 03 IS NOT TOUCHED, DELIBERATELY.** p017 asks whether the ruling reaches
`/billing/bills/:id/document`, whose only purpose is the full view, and answers itself: *"I have
not assumed either way."* Neither does this lane. The same page raises whether the tab should
stop being called *Document* now that it holds Amount, Breakdown, Usage and Dates — also left.

### 2 · `DEF-BIL-5244` CLOSED AS **invalid** — THE ANNOTATION DECIDES EMPHASIS, NOT THE BOX

A sibling lane filed `DEF-BIL-5244` against a **correct** step-1 record, built the inversion, and
wrote a comment into the code naming six pages to defend it: *"on p015, p018, p021, p022, p024
and p027 — every §02 frame — `Fix this bill` is the boxed control and `View the bill as sent` is
unboxed grey."*

**Every word of that is a true reading of the pixels, and it is the wrong instrument.** p016
legend 6, verbatim: *"One primary, and an overflow · View the bill as sent FILLED; Fix this bill
secondary; Print bill and Cancel this bill into `…`, Cancel keeping its reason · UI-RULES 4–6 ·
CHANGED"*. **Neither control is drawn FILLED anywhere in the document**, so the drawing could not
have settled this in either direction. B14 rule 37 says which instrument does: *a figure drawn in
a wireframe is an ILLUSTRATION, never a fact to build to.*

The drawn ORDER corroborates it — `View the bill as sent` is LEFTMOST, which is where
`PageHeader.leadingAction` exists to put a primary (US-SHL-020).

**And the refusal changed with it, which closes p014's own finding:** *"Print disables with a
reason; View vanishes. A clerk cannot learn one rule from the pair."* `View the bill as sent` no
longer disappears on a bill with no saved copy; it disables with the same reason the print
control carries, read off the same fact in the same order (`DEF-116`). BR-SHL-044's *exactly one
primary* now holds on every bill rather than on bills that happen to have a document.

### 3 · THE CYCLE BY NAME — A NEW FIELD, NOT A CHANGE OF MEANING

The header printed **`CY-007`** while the PRINTED BILL for the same bill said **"Silver Creek —
monthly"**, because `issue._cycle_label_for` has stamped the name into `bill_payload["cycle"]`
since `DEF-2865` and `GET /invoices/{id}` served `run.cycle.code`. One cycle, two words for it,
on two surfaces a clerk reads side by side.

`invoices.cycle_label` is read by **four** screens, so changing what it means would move all four
on one screen's authority. The NAME arrives as its own field, `cycle_name`, with the same
fallback the payload already uses — name, else code, else null — and the CODE keeps its place
under Origin, which is what legend 4 asks for in as many words: *"the id CY-001 stays under
Origin"*.

⚠ **The annotation names `cycles.label` and there is no such column.** `metering.Cycle` has
`code`, `name` and `frequency`, and the drawn value is verbatim the `name` of `CY-007` in this
deployment. Built as the schema has it; recorded rather than followed literally.

### 4 · THE TWO LIVE READS, AND THE ONE COLUMN THAT IS AN ABSENCE

§09 of the document counts the new reads itself: *"Only 'Owed today', the usage AVERAGE and the
paperless election need a read this module does not have today"* — and the paperless election is
the Sent tab's, already made. Neither of the other two is a new endpoint:
`GET /accounts/{id}/open-bills` has served the account's whole open position since 2026-09-01
(CR-059 CS-4) and `GET /accounts/{id}/usage` is the ACC-01 Usage tab's read. Both are asked
through the SAME query keys those screens use, so opening the account afterwards costs neither
again.

**Worked, on `BL-2608-000094` in the running product:** Total due **$321.04** — the figure frozen
on the bill at issue — against Owed today **$158.10**, the account's live open position. Two
different questions, two different figures, on one panel, with the caveat saying which is which.
That difference is the whole argument for the row.

⚠ **THE `READ` COLUMN OF THE USAGE TABLE IS DRAWN AND CANNOT BE FILLED.** The drawing shows
`M-8841 · 08/01`. `GET /invoices/{id}/document` answers, in the server's own words,
`absent: [{field: "meter_no · prior_read · current_read", why: "…stage 6 keeps only whether the
service was measured, so the document can say WHETHER a meter was read and never WHAT it read"}]`,
and `GET /accounts/{id}` serves `meters` with **no service tag** — so a meter cannot be matched to
a service row without guessing. **The column is kept and each cell carries the server's sentence.**
A guessed meter number on a bill is a screen telling a clerk a reading came off the wrong meter,
which is worse than an absence and looks better.

**THIS PERIOD is the bill's own arithmetic and needs no read at all:** Σ of this bill's `usage`
lines per service, and **only where the unit agrees** — hard rule 3. A tiered water charge is
three lines of one quantity in one unit and they sum to the consumption; two units inside one
service is not a quantity, it is two, and that renders as a named absence rather than a number.

### 5 · THE JUDGMENT CALLS, EACH WITH WHAT IT RESTS ON

| Call | Rests on |
|---|---|
| The seven groups are the kit's `Panel` — a box — where the drawing rules them off with a rule | **B14 rule 36**: the packs give layout and detail, `r10` gives VISUAL STYLE, the kit is how you comply. `Panel` is the information group on a detail screen in 145 files. Order, grouping and rows are the drawing's and are built exactly |
| The AMOUNT caveat is two six-word sentences, not the drawn 17 + 9 | **B14 rule 33** — *two sentences of six beat one sentence of twelve* — and the PO's 2026-09-14 target, *"reduce the content to 5 to 6 meaningful words"*. Both facts survive. This is a drawn element disagreeing with a signed rule, which rule 41 makes the one thing that legitimately reaches the PO; recorded rather than asked because the shorter copy carries the drawing's whole meaning |
| The caveat renders on Document and NOT on Charges | p018 draws no sentence under the Charges AMOUNT. The same 17 words printed on both tabs is B14 rule 32's description budget, twice |
| The customer's name is a LINK though the drawing inks it in the body colour | Legend 1 says *"both linked"*. Rule 37 again: where a drawing and its own annotation disagree, the words are the specification |
| `↓ Download the bill as sent (PDF)` keeps its 6 drawn words against rule 33's 3-word label cap | The product's precedent on this very header is `View the bill as sent` — 5 words, drawn and shipped. Rule 41's default. Recorded, not silently followed |

### 6 · WHAT IS OWED, AND IT IS NAMED RATHER THAN SKIPPED

**The version bump.** `allocate.py version --bump change` offers **2.267.0** and this lane did not

⚠ **AND THE CR NUMBER ON THIS WORK IS NOT ITS OWN.** `CR-105-BRC03` already names a different
change — *"in this step 1 scope - you will ahve to also decide on billing template"*, a template

That is `DEF-2804`'s shape — a real id read for a different real id — and `DEF-GOV-5229`'s lesson
is that a finding recorded only in the file you happen to be in is a finding nobody can count.

## 2026-09-14 · A PERIOD OPENS AT THE LAST BILLED READ — NOT AT A CHOICE, AND NOT AT WHATEVER THE METER SAYS

**PO ruling, verbatim,** on the register-continuity case built for `DEF-BIL-5270`:

> *"there is no sign off issue - you ahve to raje start reading as 13,500 - we cannot create
> wrong conusmption that is loss"*

### The case, with its figures

May's issued bill closed the meter at **13,500**. June's read opens at **13,800**. Every period
tied out perfectly — no gap in the calendar, no overlap — and **300 kWh sat on no issued bill**.

**What was built:** a decision named `billing_continuity` with two choices, *bill as it stands*
or *hold and investigate*, on the reasoning that a gap is sometimes lawful.

**What is ruled:** ⚠ **THERE IS NO CHOICE. THE PERIOD OPENS AT 13,500.** The 300 kWh is
consumption that physically happened and a customer physically used. Opening the period at
13,800 does not "skip a decision" — **it bills 300 kWh to nobody, for ever, and that is
revenue lost rather than deferred.**

### Why the decision was the wrong instrument, stated so it is not rebuilt

A decision asks a clerk to choose between outcomes that are each defensible. **Here one outcome
is simply wrong.** Nobody should be able to choose to lose 300 kWh, and a screen that offers it
will eventually have it chosen — on a busy day, in bulk, across a whole run, by someone clearing
a work list. **The right instrument for a fact that is never acceptable is not a decision; it is
the anchor itself.**

⚠ **AND THE CALENDAR ANCHOR AND THE REGISTER ANCHOR ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING, WHICH IS
WHAT THE BUILD CONFLATED.** The calendar case — *billed through 30 April, run opens 1 June, 31
days nobody billed* — **can** be lawful: a service was off, an account was closed and reopened,
a cycle moved. That one may legitimately raise a decision. **The register case cannot be
lawful**: a meter that read 13,500 and now reads 13,800 recorded 300 units of real use, and no
circumstance makes billing them optional.

### What is built

1. **A billing period's OPENING READ IS THE CLOSING READ OF THE LAST ISSUED BILL** for that
   meter, always. Not the previous read on the meter, not the earliest read in the window.
2. **No decision, no chip, no clerk choice** for the register case. `billing_continuity`'s
   register branch is removed as a decision kind and becomes the anchor's own behaviour.
3. **The calendar case keeps its decision** — that one is genuinely ambiguous and this ruling
   does not touch it.

### ⚠ WHAT MUST NOT BE SWALLOWED BY THIS RULE, AND MUST BE RAISED INSTEAD

**A meter exchange and a register rollover both break the arithmetic**, and neither may be
silently anchored at the old number:

* **exchange** — the old meter left at 13,500 and a NEW meter starts at 0, so 13,800 is a
  different device's register and `13,800 − 13,500` is meaningless;
* **rollover** — a 5-digit register passing 99,999 returns to 0, and the subtraction goes
  catastrophically negative.

**Anchoring blindly on the last billed read would bill a fiction in both cases** — the mirror of
the loss this ruling exists to prevent. Each must be detected and raised, and `DEF-BIL-5269`'s
lesson applies: the fix is to read what metering already publishes about the asset rather than
to infer an exchange from the numbers.

**So: anchor on the last billed read; raise only when the anchor cannot be trusted, never when
it merely produces a number somebody might dislike.**

## 2026-09-14 · A BILL RUN MAY BE SHOWN A SCOPE AND MAY NOT BE COMMITTED TO ONE — AND THE WAITING-TIME BANDS COME OFF THE CYCLE'S OWN CLOCK

Three reads were built for blueprint §03 screens 16 and 17 (`DEF-BIL-5255`, `DEF-BIL-5258`).
Six judgments were taken where the rules ran out. Each is recorded with the figure it rested
on, because every one of them is invisible on a screen that looks finished.

### 1 · A NARROWED SCOPE IS SHOWN AND IS **NOT COMMITTABLE**, AND THAT IS A REFUSAL RATHER THAN A TODO

The blueprint's step 1 draws *Which accounts — every account in the cycle, or a route, an area,
or a named set*. `DEF-BIL-5283` is that `runs.create_run` composes its idempotency key from
**cycle + period and nothing else**, while a service scope is already accepted, stored and
honoured.

**Worked, on a real cycle:** a clerk runs **Water only** for September. That run consumes the
key `cycle|2026-09-01|2026-09-30`. The **Sewer** run for the same September is then refused as
a duplicate — and because it is REFUSED rather than EXCLUDED, **zero exclusion rows are
written**, so those accounts never reach the held queue, and a catch-up run bills only what the
held queue holds. **Nothing ever bills them.**

**The choice taken:** the resolver serves the scope and its counts, and answers
`committable: false` for every scope narrower than the whole cycle — a route, an area, a named
set, or any service subset — with the limit stated in a clerk's own words and no rule id in it.
**The alternative was to ship the chooser and fix the key later, which is a dropdown over a
revenue hole.** The key itself lives on the run-creation path, which was another lane's file
for the whole of this work, so the refusal is the half that could ship honestly today.

### 2 · THE WAITING-TIME BANDS ARE MULTIPLES OF THE CYCLE'S OWN PERIOD — ONE AND TWO

The PO ruled that the *how long it has waited* bands DERIVE FROM THE CYCLE'S FREQUENCY and are
settable at cycle level with a default we supply. The blueprint draws *Under 14 days* and
*Over 60 days*; B14 rule 37 makes a drawn figure an illustration, never a fact to build to.

**The default chosen: escalate after ONE cycle period, long wait after TWO.** Worked, through
`metering.cycle_expected_span_days`, which answers the calendar distance rather than a constant:

```
Monthly, period opening 1 Jun 2026    30 days  →  escalate 30 · long wait 60
Monthly, period opening 1 Aug 2026    31 days  →  escalate 31 · long wait 62
Fortnightly                           14 days  →  escalate 14 · long wait 28
Quarterly, period opening 1 Jun 2026  92 days  →  escalate 92 · long wait 184
a cycle carrying no frequency          —       →  NO age tags at all, absence stated
```

**Why one and two rather than the drawn fourteen and sixty.** One period is the point at which
an account has missed a whole bill of its own, which is what the escalation is about; two is
the point at which it has missed two. A fixed **14** escalates a quarterly cycle's entire queue
**before its first bill is due**, and a fixed **60** never escalates a fortnightly one at all.
On the monthly cycle the drawing was made for, one and two reproduce the drawn pair to within a
day (31 and 62 against 14 and 60 — the long wait lands, the escalation is the half the drawing
set tighter).

**The cycle-level override is asked for BY NAME and is not built** (`DEF-BIL-5298`): the read
calls a metering seam `cycle_waiting_bands` before falling back, so the day the column lands no
billing code changes.

### 3 · AN ACCOUNT HELD ACROSS CYCLES IS COUNTED AND IS NOT BANDED — `OQ-BIL-12358`, OPEN

An account held on **2 May** from a monthly cycle and swept into a run over a quarterly cycle is
**74 days old on 15 July**. Banded on the RUN's cycle (92 → escalate at 92) it reads *under
escalation* and nobody looks at it. Banded on the cycle it was HELD from (30 → escalate at 30,
long wait at 60) it reads *long wait* and is the oldest thing on the screen. **Same account,
same day, same 74 days, opposite urgency.**

`finding_counts` takes `age_bands_from` as a parameter **with no default**. While it is unset a
cross-cycle hold is counted as `cross_cycle_unsettled`, kept out of all three age tags, and the
absence is stated. **Choosing either clock silently would answer an open question in a place
nobody would ever find it.**

### 4 · THREE COUNTS ON THE SCOPE CARD ARE NULL, AND A ZERO WOULD HAVE BEEN A CLAIM

The card draws *meters this cycle*, *+ sub-meters* and *points with no meter*. The assets seam
answers meters **one service point at a time**, so a 1,502-unit cycle would pay roughly **1,600
round trips to draw three numbers on a header** — on a card whose own note says every figure is
a COUNT precisely because resolving scope for real is the expensive thing (137 ms per account;
40,000 accounts ≈ 91 minutes). **A zero would claim the cycle has no meters.** Served null with
the reason beside them; `DEF-BIL-5297` asks assets for the bulk read.

### 5 · `In arrears` IS NOT FOLDED INTO THE FINDINGS PASS

It is a fact about an ACCOUNT — what it owed before this bill, at a date the clerk chooses —
not about this run. Folding it in would make a balance read part of the billing pass and give
the run a number **that changes when somebody pays**. Served as a named absence; `DEF-BIL-5299`.

### 6 · THE COUNTS GET THEIR OWN ADDRESS AND PAGING STAYS OPT-IN

`GET /billing/runs/{id}/findings` is unpaginated **by declared design**, because its lists are
the denominator the twenty-six chips count — one argument holding up both halves, at a measured
**66,053 SQL statements and the whole population on the wire at 1,000 accounts, per refresh**.
Serving the counts separately dissolves it.

**Paging is opt-in and not the default**, and that is deliberate rather than timid: the live
screen still computes its chips from `.length`, so making the page the default today would turn
`ready.length` into a page size and the screen would confidently report **fifty accounts in a
run of ten thousand** — the exact failure the endpoint's own docstring warns about. The day the
screen reads its numbers from the counts address, the page becomes the default and the
parameter goes away.

⛔ **Nothing here is cached.** `OQ-843` is closed on the PO's ruling that the pass is dynamic —
a clerk who fixes a plan and comes back must see the fix — and it ends *"A lane may not reopen
this by proposing a cache."* What was saved is the wire and the browser's arithmetic.

### ⚠ AND ONE THING WAS FOUND BY LAW 7 RATHER THAN BY A TEST

The new invariant `sum(tags) >= band` found a real bug before it was written: *where the fix is*
counted **every** blocked account, while a block whose reason carries **no stage** produces no
stage tag, so the band claimed an account its own chips did not show — the direction that HIDES
work from a clerk. **Its first version could not fail.** Reverting the fix in a worktree pinned
at the tip left the case GREEN, because the fixture held only a block that did carry a stage
and `len(staged_ids)` and `len(blocked_ids)` were the same number. A third account was added
that breaks with no stage, and the proof re-run: `AssertionError: ('where_the_fix_is', 1, 2)`
red, then green with the fix restored. **A guard proved red on the wrong fixture is no proof of
the thing that matters.**

### ⚠ AND ONE THING MOVED UNDER THIS LANE WHILE IT WORKED

`bill_runs` had **no `label` column** when these reads were written, so the runs table served
`label: null` under its contracted name with a defect row against it. `BR-BIL-1041` landed the
column in **`2.267.0`** from the schema lane, in the same afternoon. **Re-reading the four
places the repo changes under you — r11 step 0 — before closing the record is what caught it**,
and the read now serves the real column. `DEF-BIL-5300` is closed against that commit rather
than left standing as a true-sounding claim about a column that exists.

**PO ruling, verbatim**, on being shown §04 p101–p102 beside the built screen:

> *"Billed from is fixed, not typed. The drawing shows it as text — 01 Sep 2026, "The last bill
> ended here" — with only Billed to editable, annotated "9 days of a 30-day cycle." The product
> offers two free date fields. we can take this input field"*

**What is ruled.** The blueprint draws *Billed from* as DERIVED TEXT — the last bill's end date,
with the sentence *"The last bill ended here"* under it — and leaves only *Billed to* editable.
The product ships two free date inputs. **The PO accepts the product's shape: `Billed from` stays
an editable input.** The drawing is not followed on this field.

⚠ **THIS IS A DIVERGENCE THE PO HAS ACCEPTED, NOT ONE THE DOCUMENT LOST.** B14 rule 41 says the
product matches the blueprint exactly and that a drawing contradicting a signed rule is what
reaches the PO. That is what happened here and the PO ruled for the product, so the divergence is
now DELIBERATE and must be stamped where it would otherwise read as a defect — nobody may "fix"
this field back to derived text on the strength of the drawing.

what was shown):**

* **`Days to pay` is still REQUIRED and is still absent from the built screen.** p101: *"A bill
  with no cycle has no days to pay of its own — your ruling was that they are captured at billing
  time — so an empty field means the bill **drafts and cannot be issued**."* The backend already
  takes `due_days`; the screen never asks for it.
* **The annotation `9 days of a 30-day cycle`** under *Billed to* is a separate element and is
  still owed. `cycle_days` is already in the preview payload, so it is derivable today.
* **The sixth kind, `Fee`**, is absent from the screen AND from `ONE_TIME_KINDS` in
  `06-backend/apps/billing/one_time.py`, which carries five.

**Where a reader goes next.** §04 runs p099–p117 of `05-prototype/04 Billing, As Built.pdf`, read

one frame per kind, p103–p113) · **23 Confirm and send** (step 3, p114–p115). Every frame is

## 2026-09-15 · ONE-TIME BILL STEP 2 GAINS A **WHO** GROUP, BEFORE **WHERE**

**PO instruction, verbatim**, given against the §04 step-2 spine:

> *"can you also add who in this — [the step-2 group table] — before where — give me updated version"*

**What is ruled.** §04 p101 draws step 2 with a fixed lettered spine — **A** where, **B** what,
**C** readings, **D** how it prices — *"the same lettered spine on all six kinds"*. The account is
chosen on step 1 and the drawing never restates it on step 2. **The PO adds a WHO group and places

then the kind's own group, then the ⚠ block.

⚠ **THIS ADDS A GROUP TO A DRAWN SCREEN, so it is not a conformance gap and must not be filed as
one.** A later lane reading p101 will count four lettered groups and find five built; this row is
why. The drawing's own rule still governs the rest — a group a kind does not need is KEPT AND
GREYED WITH ITS REASON, never dropped, because *"a step that changes shape between kinds teaches
nothing, and a group that vanishes looks like a bug"*.

**What WHO carries, and the plumbing that already exists.** The account number, the customer, and
the account's billability class are the three facts that identify who is being billed:

  `selectors.primary_contact_name` / `customer_for_account`, surfaced as `customer_name` on the

⚠ **AND A NAMELESS ACCOUNT IS A REAL STATE, NOT AN ERROR.** An account with no customer link

and was first mis-read as a product defect; it is the correct answer for an account nobody has
linked a customer to, and the WHO group must keep saying so rather than drawing a blank.

## 2026-09-15 · SCREEN 21 *WHO AND WHEN* — THE SIX PLACES §04's DRAWING AND A SIGNED UI RULE DISAGREED, AND WHAT WON

**Not a PO ruling.** These are lane judgments made while building §04 entry 21 (p101–p102), written
down because B14 rule 41 makes the drawing the scope by default — *"it is expected that Product UI
will match extactly the way it is given in Blueprint document"* — so **every place the built screen
departs from the drawing is a claim that needs its reason on the record.** A later lane holding the
PDF beside the screen will count six differences; this row is why, and each is also stamped at its
own call site in `07-frontend/src/features/billing/OneTimeWhoStep.tsx`.

**The rule that settles most of them is B14 rule 38** — *"where a drawing and our UI rules disagree
about how a FORM IS BUILT, the UI rules win … and the drawing is still right about what the form
CONTAINS"* — and **rule 33**, whose hardest clause is that RATIONALE is **zero words on screen**.

| # | The drawing | What was built | What decided it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | *"Shown so a clerk picking the kind knows what they will need to hand."* under the six-row table | **Not rendered** | Rule 33 — it explains why the table is there. Rule 33's own test settles it: a clerk cannot ACT on it. Quoted in the docstring instead. |
| 2 | *"A bill outside a cycle has none of its own, so an empty field drafts and cannot be issued."* under *Days to pay* | **Not rendered**; the field carries the kit's required mark | Same clause. The bold *"Days to pay is required"* half survives AS the required mark (BR-SHL-017); the sentence after it is rationale. |
| 3 | *"The last bill ended here."* under *Billed from* | **Not rendered** | It is a claim about a DERIVED value, and the PO ruled the same day that the field is typed. Over a box a clerk may type into, the sentence becomes false the moment they do — worse than absent. |
| 4 | *"The kind decides what step 2 asks for."* (8 words), under the GROUP | **"The kind decides step 2."** (5 words), under its own INPUT | Rule 33 caps a fact at six. The move from group to input is rule 38 — help under its input is construction, and the kit's. |
| 5 | *"Nothing is written until you draft it."* (7 words) | **"Nothing is written until you draft."** (6) | Rule 33 caps a consequence at six per sentence. The dropped word is the only one carrying nothing. |
| 6 | ONE account combobox reading `100377 · Ridge Coffee Co. — 12 Foundry Ln ▾` | **TWO controls** — a search box that queries the server, and a select of what came back | **`NFR-3`.** The kit's `SearchSelectField` filters a list it is HANDED, client-side; being right here would mean loading a tenant's whole account list, and a T5 tenant has **40,000**. This is the pair every account picker in the product already uses. |

⚠ **AND ONE THING WAS DELIBERATELY *NOT* SHORTENED, WHICH IS THE SAME RULE POINTING THE OTHER WAY.**
The six sentences in the *what each kind will ask you next* table run **7 to 9 words** against rule
33's six-word cap for a fact, and they stand verbatim. Rule 33's own priority says why: ***"shorten
by deleting RATIONALE, never INSTRUCTION"***, and these are the instruction — cutting *"A list of
periods, and a reading for each"* to six words destroys exactly what the PO asked the table for
(*"a fee needs no reading, a back-bill needs one per period"*). **Three group headings are likewise
over the three-word LABEL cap** — *Who, and which kind* (4) and *What each kind will ask you next*
(7) — and stand, because for a module with a blueprint the blueprint owns COPY (`DEF-GOV-5248`).
**These four are the row on this page most likely to be "fixed" by a later sweep; they are a
decision, not an oversight.**

⚠ **A SEVENTH DIFFERENCE IS AN ABSENCE RATHER THAN A WORDING.** p101 draws a **`Past one-time
bills`** button at the top right and **it is not rendered**. Nothing serves *past one-time runs*:
the bills list filters on `bill_type`, and a one-time INTERIM bill is written as a **`cycle`**-typed
document (`one_time.py` — *"an interim bill is an ordinary bill over an unusual window"*), so no
filter value can mean it. A button pointing at `/billing?bill_type=final` would be a lie in the
shape of a link, which is hard-won law 2's mirror (`DEF-CWP-3925`). It is recorded with an OWNER —
`ONE_TIME_WIZARD_NOT_BUILT` in `oneTimeWizardContract.ts` — and a test asserts the entry is still
true, because *"has the door started pointing at it"* belonging to nobody is how that defect
happened.

**What would reopen any of this:** a PO ruling, or a kit that grows a server-search combobox (rule
36's own remedy — *"ADD IT TO THE KIT as an opt-in, so nothing existing moves"*), which would close
