## 2026-09-15 · §05 ENTRY 25.1 `ENROL` — WHAT THE SCREEN DRAWS THAT NOTHING SERVES, AND WHY NONE OF IT WAS INVENTED

**Nobody was asked anything.** Every judgment below was ours to make under law 13, and each is
recorded here because the next agent would otherwise re-decide it differently.

**1 · THE FRONT END DOES NO MONEY ARITHMETIC, SO TWO DRAWN FIGURES ARE ABSENCES.** The drawing's
level section reads `Trailing twelve months, billed | 12 bills | $936.00` and
`The band you may override within | ±30% | $54.60 – $101.40`. Neither AMOUNT is served:
`GET /budget-billing/{id}/eligibility` gives the twelve per-period actuals and no sum, and
`budget.override_bounds` has no caller outside `validate_override`. **Both could have been computed
in the browser and both would have been wrong to compute.** The band needs `money.finalize`, which
is a 🔒 money-rounding path with no TypeScript twin; and the total is worse than it looks —
`compute_level` divides by the tenant's `eligibility_months`, which need not equal the number of
actuals read, **so a browser-side `total ÷ 12` could disagree with the computed level drawn two rows
below it on the same screen**. The PERCENTAGE is served and is drawn (the tenant's own
`override_bound_pct`, BR-BIL-021, never the seeded 30). `DEF-BIL-5312`, `DEF-BIL-5313`.

**2 · ENROL-AT-AN-OVERRIDDEN-LEVEL IS DRAWN AND CANNOT BE DONE IN ONE ACT.** The drawing puts an
override box in the form and labels the button `Enrol at $85.00`.
`POST /budget-billing/enrollments` carries `{account_id, plan_offers_budget, on_date}` and nothing
else; `enroll` computes the level itself; an override is a SECOND write and `validate_override`
**refuses a reason-less one**, which the drawing gives no field for. Doing it as two calls would
leave a customer enrolled at $78.00 when the second call fails — a partial write on a money path
with no rule for the half-done state. **So the box is drawn and greyed WITH its reason, which is the
blueprint's own doctrine one page earlier** (p121: *"Greyed-with-a-reason tells a clerk to enrol one
at a time; a missing control tells them the product forgot"*), and **the button names the COMPUTED
figure, because that is what the request will write.** A button naming a number the request does not
carry is a customer paying something nobody agreed. `DEF-BIL-5315`.

**3 · TEN FACT ROWS ARE DRAWN AND THE DOCUMENT SAYS NINE, TWICE** — p123 *"Nine facts"* and p124
*"Nine facts, in three bands"*, over `WHO, AND WHERE` 3 + `CAN IT BE LEVELLED` 4 + `WHAT CHANGES FOR
THEM` 3 = **10**. B14 rule 42 makes the image the specification and the prose an index, so ten are
built. Two lanes counted the page independently — `CR-103-BRC03` step 1 at scale 4, this lane at
scale 2 — and got ten both times.

**4 · THE AUTOPAY WARNING IS WORDED TO WHAT THE PRODUCT DOES, AND THIS IS NOT A COPY-LENGTH CUT.**
The drawing says *"From 30 Nov the amount taken becomes the level, not the bill."* **Nothing is
taken.** `DEF-644` already ruled this once — *"autopay in this version is 'a promise recorded, never
a charge'… a clerk can switch it on and reasonably expect the next bill to be taken. It will not
be"* — and grew `StatusPill.title` for it. Printing the drawn sentence would tell a clerk money will
leave a customer's account when nothing collects. The row carries the established qualifier and the
warning says the true, useful half: **tell them the amount changes**. Law 13: this was ruled, so it
is built, not re-asked.

**5 · THE CHOSEN ACCOUNT LIVES IN THE ADDRESS (`?account=`), NOT IN COMPONENT STATE.** The drawn
breadcrumb gives the screen two entrances — `+ Enrol an account`, with nobody picked, and *"an ask on
screen 25.3"*, which arrives knowing the account. **An address is the only way the second entrance
can hand it over**, and it makes a half-filled screen a link a clerk can be sent. `/billing/fix?bill=`
is the same shape one tab along. B14 rule 31 is not engaged: the rule governs the visible value of a
FIELD, and the id is never rendered — the picker's label is the account number, the name and the
address, and the id rides only on `<option value>`.

**6 · THE VERSION WAS NOT BUMPED, DELIBERATELY.** The scheme is four literals in lockstep and one is
`06-backend/pyproject.toml`; this lane was scoped frontend-only with the backend owned by another
lane in the same hour. **Bumping three of four makes `G35` red**, so the choice was between crossing
a lane boundary on a money-free one-line literal and leaving step 7 owed. Step 7 is owed, stated in
the conformance record and in this lane's report rather than quietly skipped — which is the thing
step 7 exists to prevent.

## 2026-09-15 · ONE-TIME BILL — *DAYS TO PAY* IS REQUIRED ON STEP 1 FOR `fee`, AND FOR NO OTHER KIND

**Not a PO ruling, and deliberately not put to them:** the rule it applies is already signed, and the
server's own record decides where it lands. Recorded because a later lane will find one kind behaving
unlike the other five on the same field and needs the reason without re-deriving it.

**The signed rule, unchanged.** §04 p101: *"A bill with no cycle has no days to pay of its own — your
ruling was that they are captured at billing time — so an empty field means the bill **drafts and
cannot be issued**. That is the rule refusing, not a guessed due date starting a late-fee clock."*
For `interim`, `first`, `final`, `backbill` and `penalty` that is exactly what happens and step 1
lets an empty field through.

**Why `fee` cannot follow it.** `apps/billing/fee_bill.raise_charge_fee` declares **`due_days: int`
with no default**, so a fee bill with no terms never drafts at all — the sentence *"drafts and cannot
be issued"* describes a state it cannot reach. `apps/billing/one_time.py`'s fee path refuses first,
with a `BillingRuleError`, and **its own docstring already says where that refusal belongs**:

> *"`due_days` IS REQUIRED AND IS NOT CHOSEN HERE. A cycle-less bill has no cycle to take its terms
> from (CR-029 D8③), and `issue` refuses a bill whose due date cannot be derived rather than guessing
> one — so **an absent value is refused at step 1** rather than becoming a late-fee clock nobody
> started."*

**What was built.** `dueDaysIsRequiredFor(kind)` in `oneTimeWizardContract.ts` returns true for `fee`
alone; `requestIsComplete` refuses an empty field only for that kind, and step 1's commit bar says
**"Enter days to pay."** The field keeps its required mark for every kind (BR-SHL-017) because it is
expected for every kind — what changes is only *where the product stops you*.

⚠ **THIS IS NOT A SECOND RULE COMPETING WITH THE PO's — IT IS THE PO's RULE APPLIED TO A KIND THAT
CANNOT DRAFT.** The alternative considered and rejected was letting step 3 expect the refusal by
name: it spends a round trip to tell a clerk something step 1 already knew, and it puts the sentence
two screens away from the field it is about. **The half most easily broken by a later sweep is the
NEGATIVE one** — widening this to all six kinds would move the PO's refusal upstream and change the
flow — so it is asserted directly: `oneTimeWizardContract.test.ts` requires the other five to accept
an empty field, by name, one case per kind.

**What would reopen it:** `raise_charge_fee` growing a default, or the PO ruling that a fee bill may
draft without terms. Either makes `dueDaysIsRequiredFor` return false for everything, and it is one
line.

## 2026-09-15 · STEP TWO'S LETTERS, AND THE DRAWN COPY AGAINST B14 RULE 33

Two judgments taken while building §04 screens 22.1–22.6. Both are recorded here
rather than put to the Product Owner, because hard-won law 13 says a judgment
call recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable and a question is the failure
to make one — **except** for the second, which is rule 41's one legitimate
question and is therefore ALSO on the agenda, with both sides quoted.

### 1 · WHO TAKES THE LETTER **A**, AND THE DRAWN GROUPS SHIFT ONE

The ruling of this date adds a WHO group and places it FIRST, ahead of WHERE. It
says nothing about the letters, and the drawing letters its four groups
**A** where · **B** what · **C** readings · **D** how it prices.

So something had to give. Either WHO is the only unlettered group on a lettered
screen, or the drawn groups shift a letter and five pages of blueprint prose that
say *"group E"* name a group this screen letters **F**.

**Chosen: WHO is A and the rest shift.** The ruling's own words decide it — it
warns that *"a reader counting four lettered groups on p101 will find five
built"*, which only makes sense if WHO takes a letter. So: who **A** · where
**B** · what **C** · readings **D** · how it prices **E** · the kind's own group
**F**, and **G** for the second group a final bill has.

⚠ **THE LETTER IS DERIVED FROM POSITION AND IS NEVER STORED**
(`oneTimeWhatLetter`), so a group inserted or removed later re-letters every
sibling in the same act. A stored letter is a fact that can disagree with the
screen it is printed on; a derived one cannot.

### 2 · THE DRAWN COPY EXCEEDS B14 RULE 33, SYSTEMATICALLY — BUILT, AND RAISED

**Rule 33** caps a LABEL or heading at **3 words** and puts RATIONALE — *"why the
product works this way, why a control is absent"* — at **ZERO words on screen**.

**The drawing exceeds both on every one of the six frames:**

* ten group headings run 4–7 words — *"WHAT — SERVICE POINTS AND THEIR ASSETS"*,
  *"THE PERIODS, AND WHAT THE GROUPING COSTS"*;
* every group carries a caption that is rationale by rule 33's own definition —
  *"The address is walked to from the premises, never stored on the account."*;
* the greyed-group sentence IS a stated reason for an absent control. p101
  requires it in terms — a kind that does not need a group *"keeps it and greys
  it with the reason on its face"* — and rule 33 puts exactly that at zero words.

**What was built, and why.** B14 **rule 41** (ratified 2026-09-13, the later of
the two) says *"Everything else — layout, grouping, order, labels, which facts
appear — is the drawing's and is built"*, and that a drawn element contradicting
a signed rule *"goes to the PO with both sides quoted"*. So **the drawing is
built and the contradiction is raised**, which is rule 41 followed literally
rather than a lane choosing between two signed rules.

Two things make that safe to do:

* Rule 33's own status column records it as **NOT ENFORCED** for these five
  kinds — `G33` reads only the refusal half, over keys a backend raise site
  resolves — so none of this copy was ever inside a gate's reach and nothing is
  being silenced.
* **Every drawn sentence sits behind its own catalogue key**, so a ruling either
  way moves keys in eleven catalogues and touches no screen code.

⚠ **AND WHERE THIS LANE AUTHORED COPY RATHER THAN COPYING IT, IT OBEYED RULE
33.** The WHO group is not drawn, so its caption is four words — *"Chosen on step
one."* — and its heading follows the drawn siblings' shape rather than inventing
a seventh idiom on one screen.

**What is put to the PO, in plain English:** the blueprint's own step-two frames
write group headings of up to seven words and put one explaining sentence under
every group, and our UI rule says a heading is at most three words and that an
explanation belongs in the code rather than on screen. The screen is built the
way the blueprint draws it. Which of the two should win here?

## 2026-09-15 · §05 SCREEN 25 · WHERE AN OVERRIDE IS ASKED FOR, WHEN THE DRAWING DOES NOT SAY

**Lane:** `claude/eager-johnson-r0k88b`, Budget Bills table walked against §05
entry 25 (p121–p122, read as images per B14 rule 42). **Defect:** `DEF-BIL-5262`,
filed 2026-09-14, medium. **Record:**
`04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/conformance/CR-103-BRC03-entry-25-table-walk.md`.

**The judgment, and it is a judgment because the drawing is SILENT rather than
contradictory.** p121 draws the Budget Bills table and **no override anywhere on
the screen** — not the two boxes that were shipped, and not a dialog either. It
draws no actions column at all. Entry 25.1 answers only the ENROLMENT moment, and
its own override box is greyed because an enrolment request carries no override
(`DEF-BIL-5315`). **So nothing drawn says where a clerk overrides the level of an
account that is already enrolled**, and the product has done it since 2026-08-16.

**Two readings, and the cost of each:**

* *Build the silence* — delete the override from this screen. It takes a live
  money write off the product to satisfy a drawing that simply does not cover the
  case, and nothing else in the product can do it.
* *Keep it where it was* — two inputs under the table, attached to no row. That
  is the defect: **a clerk typed an amount and a reason, and only the pencil they
  pressed afterwards decided whose bill it changed.** An override fixes what a
  customer pays for a year.

**Chosen: the CONTROL is the drawing's and the FORM is ours.** The pencil row
action stays where the product already had it; pressing it opens a dialog scoped
to that account. **That is B14 rule 38's split applied to a silence rather than to
a disagreement** — *"where a drawing and our UI rules disagree about how a FORM is
built, the UI rules win … what the form CONTAINS is still the drawing's to
decide."* What it contains is the drawing's: p122's own rule row requires the
computed figure to stay visible — *"The ±30% bound is measured against the
computed figure, so hiding it is how an override gets typed blind"* — so the
dialog carries it beside the box.

**The worked figure shown:** an account whose computed level is **$88.00** and
whose override is typed as **`96.50`**. The dialog heads itself `A-40001 ·
Navarro, P.`, prints `$88.00` under `Computed`, and posts `"96.50"` — a decimal
STRING, never `Number("96.50")`, which is `96.5` and does not survive
`NUMERIC(18,6)` (CLAUDE.md rule 2). `TC-D4` asserts the type and the value;
`TC-D5` opens a SECOND row and asserts the post goes to the SECOND account, which
is the only case that distinguishes "a dialog names an account" from "a dialog
names THE account".

⚠ **NOTHING HERE IS PUT TO THE PRODUCT OWNER, DELIBERATELY.** Hard-won law 13's
short list is a ruling colliding with a signed rule, a ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure, or
a fact only they hold. This is none of the three: no signed statement is reversed,
no money figure moves, and the ±30% bound, the audit row and the write path are
exactly what they were. **A judgment call recorded with its reasoning is the
deliverable; a question would have been the failure to make one.** The one thing
on this screen that IS a PO question — grey-with-a-reason versus remove, for the
bulk controls — was already raised by the 2026-09-14 lane and is not re-asked.

**⚠ AND THE REASON THIS NEEDED A LANE AT ALL:** the 2026-09-14 record deferred
`DEF-BIL-5262` to *"entry 25.1's wave"*. **Entry 25.1 landed and did not take
it** — what it built was the enrolment-time override, a different act — so the
hold expired with nobody holding it. That is hard-won law 2's mirror, and the
countermeasure is now on this screen: the one remaining drawn-but-absent control,
`Settle up the year →`, has a test (`TC-B10`) that goes RED on the day entry
25.2's route is declared and says in its own words what is then owed.

## 2026-09-15 · THE FIRST BILL COULD NOT DRAFT, AND WHY THE SMALLER FIX WAS THE DANGEROUS ONE (DEF-BIL-5318)

The FIRST-BILL kind of S30's one-time tab had never produced a bill, on any
account, since 2026-08-16. `apps/billing/one_time._account_type_id` read
`account_type_id` off customers' `account_detail` seam, that seam has never
published that key, `.get()` turned the absence into `None`, and
`first_bill.deposit_line_for` refused: *"account E11-0006 names no consumer
category, so the deposit rule for its first bill cannot be resolved"*.

**Reproduced before anything was read or changed**, on the live demo tenant
(Brazos Bend Utilities), account `E11-0006`, window 1 → 15 September 2026:
`account.account_type_id` is a real uuid, `account_detail_dict` returns **64
keys** and `account_type_id` is not one of them, and `one_time.create` refuses
with the sentence above.

### THE JUDGMENT: PUBLISH THE ID FROM THE SEAM, NOT READ THE CODE IN BILLING

Two repairs were available and they are not equivalent.

**(1) Publish `account_type_id` from customers' detail seam.** Widens a
published read. **(2) Have billing read `account_type`, the key the seam already
serves.** Smaller, one line, no seam change.

**Chosen: (1).** Option 2 is not merely smaller — it is an under-bill that no
check in this repo would catch, and the reason is three signed facts in a row:

  * `rating.models.PlanDepositRule.account_type_id` is a **`UUIDField`** — the
    table is keyed on the id, not the code (BR-RAT-020/023). `rating/models.py`
    says so about itself, in the note above `charge_code_amounts.customer_class`:
    *"`plan_deposit_rules` keys its class with `account_type_id`, so that
    precedent exists and this deliberately does not follow it."*
  * `rating.selectors.deposit_rule_for` opens with
    `if not (_valid_uuid(rate_plan_id) and _valid_uuid(account_type_id)): return None`.
    Handed the code `"residential"` it returns `None` — it does not raise.
  * `None` from that read is **signed to mean *this plan asks this category for
    no deposit***, and `deposit_line_for` then emits **no line at all**, on
    purpose, because a `$0.00` line would state a deposit was assessed and
    waived.

So option 2 produces a first bill that drafts, foots perfectly, and is missing
the deposit. **The worked figure is WE-6's own: $150.00**, absent from a
document that is immutable at issue, with `tsc`, every gate and the whole suite
green. Option 1 costs one additive key on a read whose consumers were walked
(below); option 2 costs $150.00 a customer, silently. That is the whole of the
decision.

**Resolving the code to an id inside billing was never on the table**: the
lookup table is `customers.account_types`, billing may not query another
module's tables (B2 §2), and no seam publishes that mapping. The fix belongs on
the customers side, in customers' own file, which is where it was made.

### BLAST RADIUS, BOTH WAYS

**What else reads this payload:** `GET /accounts/{id}` (the S18 screen), and
~20 audit before/after snapshots inside customers itself (`services.py`,
`close_out.py`, `unit_correction.py`). The key is **additive** and was checked
against each hazard: no exact-key-set assertion exists over the ACCOUNT detail
(the one in the repo, `test_w6_connection_detail.py`, is the CONNECTION
payload); the OpenAPI entry for `/api/{tenant}/accounts/{account_id}` declares
**"No response body"**, so no generated contract moves; `AccountDetail` is a
TypeScript interface and extra JSON fields do not break one; and no snapshot
DIFF helper exists that a new key could confuse. `accounts.account_type_id` is
**NOT NULL**, so the key is never absent on a real account.

**What USED what changed:** nothing is removed. The refusal *"names no consumer
category"* is asserted by no test, and it survives — it is now reachable only
when an account genuinely has no category, which is what it always said.

### THE SECOND HALF, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL PREVENTION

`_account_type_id` now **asserts the key** instead of `.get()`-ing it. A missing
KEY and a missing CATEGORY are different facts and only one of them is the
customer's:

  * key absent ⇒ our seam is wrong; refused here, naming the seam and the field;
  * key present, value `None` ⇒ this account has no category; travels on, and
    `deposit_line_for` refuses in the customer's own language, unchanged.

`.get()` flattened the two into the second. That is why a seam defect read for
three weeks as a statement about somebody's data, three frames away from the
thing that was actually wrong — which is the defect register's own `prevention`
column for this row, built rather than merely written down.

### ⚠ A CORRECTION TO THE REGISTER ROW, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THE TOOL CANNOT MAKE IT

`DEF-BIL-5318`'s `escape_reason` says *"account_detail_dict serves twelve keys
and account_type_id is not one of them - the CODE is served by account_row, the
LIST serializer, and the detail serializer serves neither code nor id."* **Two
clauses of that are wrong and the second one matters.** The detail serves **64**
keys, not twelve; and it **does** serve the code, because `account_detail_dict`
opens `{**account_row(account), …}`. A reader who believed the detail served
neither would conclude the code has to be fetched from somewhere — and the
nearest somewhere is the LIST serializer, which is the option-2 path this entry
exists to refuse. `10-scripts/close_defect.py` changes a row's STATUS and
nothing else, by design (it rewrites one line's bytes and never re-serialises
the register), so the correction lands here and in both changed files'
docstrings rather than in the row.

### RESULT, MEASURED

Same tenant, same account, same window, after the fix: the first bill **drafts**
— invoice `BL-2609-000106`, status `draft`, bill_type `first`, **25 lines**,
subtotal **$573.33**, tax **$0.00**, total **$618.33**, carrying the
first-bill-only `Connection fee` of **$45.00**. No deposit line, correctly: this
tenant has **zero** `plan_deposit_rules` rows, which is the signed meaning of
*this plan asks this category for no deposit*. The draft was rolled back; no
demo data was written.

⚠ **NOTHING HERE IS PUT TO THE PRODUCT OWNER.** Hard-won law 13's short list is a
ruling colliding with a signed rule, a ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure, or a fact only
they hold. This is none of the three: no signed statement is reversed, and
WE-6's **$150.00** is QUOTED — asserted in the new test so drift goes red —
never moved.

## 2026-09-15 · §05 ENTRY 25.3 `ASKS` — WHOSE TABLE A CUSTOMER'S ASK LIVES IN, AND THE CONTRACT 25.4's JOIN BUTTON CAN NOW POST TO

**Not a PO ruling and deliberately not put to them for the part that is ours** (law 13). The
decision log of 2026-09-11/12, closing `OQ-CWP-1568`, said so in as many words: the write
point, the audit row and reversibility *"are design, not permission, and they belong to the
lane that builds it"*. What IS the PO's is minted as **`OQ-BIL-12359`** below rather than
decided here.

### 1 · THE PATH, AND WHICH MODULE OWNS EACH TABLE IT TOUCHES

| Step | Who runs it | Which table | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25.4 *Ask to join level pay* | `portal` calls `customers.service_request_service.create_from_portal` | **`customers.service_requests`** (+ `service_request_events`, `audit_log`) | WRITE — through customers' own door |
| 25.3 the queue | `billing` resolves a read by NAME through `apps/billing/customers_seam.py` | **`customers.service_requests`** | READ ONLY |
| 25.1 `Enrol →` | `billing` | **`billing.account_budget_status`** | WRITE |

**Billing owns no ask table and must not grow one.** That is the whole shape decision, and it
is `BR-CWP-066` applied rather than invented: *"a portal ask raises an ordinary service
request, **never a request of a new kind**"*. A `billing.budget_ask` model would be exactly
that new kind, in the module that prices the customer's water. `test_s253_budget_asks.py::
test_billing_owns_no_ask_table_and_imports_no_customers_module` asserts both halves — no
`apps.customers` import in the seam (parsed from the AST, not grepped) and no `Ask`-shaped
model in `billing.models` — so a later lane cannot drift it back.

**Three modules, two boundaries, zero cross-module writes.** `G78`'s subject is `work`, but the
same rule is what shaped this: the portal never touches `account_budget_status` and billing
never writes a service request.

### 2 · THE CONTRACT 25.4's JOIN BUTTON CAN POST TO — IT ALREADY EXISTS

`POST /api/<tenant>/portal/accounts/{account_id}/help-paying/ask`, body `{"route":
"level_pay", "note": "<optional>"}`, `201` with `{reference, protection_created: false,
granted_by: "clerk", bring_the_document: …}`.

**Refusals, by name:** no session → `IsPortalCustomer` · account outside the session's set →
`_account_in_set` (`BR-CWP-010`, intersected IN THE QUERY) · the account's customer has no
telephone number → `VAL_REQUIRED` on `phone`, `message_key` `portal.helpPaying.phoneNeeded`
(`BR-CWP-089` — *"we ring you only if we need to"*, and somebody who cannot pay is the one a
clerk will certainly ring) · an unknown `route` → `VAL_UNKNOWN_LOOKUP`, `message_key`
`portal.helpPaying.routeUnknown`.

⚠ **WHAT THE CONTRACT CANNOT CARRY, AND IT IS THE FIGURE THE SCREEN IS ABOUT.** There is no
field for **the level the customer was shown**. `create_from_portal` accepts only
`PORTAL_CAPTURE_FIELDS` and refuses every other by name, so the amount has nowhere to go but
into the free-text `note`, where it is prose rather than money. That is `OQ-BIL-12359`.

⚠ **AND `bring_the_document: true` COMES BACK FOR A LEVEL-PAY ASK, WHICH IS WRONG** —
`DEF-CWP-5330`. There is no document in a request to level next year's payments, and the
clerk's worklist sentence tells them the customer *"has been told to bring it to the office"*.
Filed, not fixed here: it is `portal`'s file and its own test.

### 3 · THE JUDGMENT THAT NEEDED MAKING — *ASK* OR *ENROL*, GIVEN THAT THE PO SAID YES

The blueprint draws 25.4's Join as an **ask**, and argues it from *"an open question against
it"*. **That question, `OQ-CWP-1568`, was CLOSED by the PO on 2026-09-11 — the day before the
drawing is dated** — verbatim: *"a). A customer who has to ring to accept a payment plan often
doesn't ring."* So the drawing argues from a premise that had stopped being true. `DEF-BIL-5332`.

**What was built: the ask, and here is why that is not a narrowing of the ruling.**

* **Permission is not a write path**, which is the repo's own settled reading from that same
  ruling, reached independently by two lanes. `BR-CWP-001` allows the portal rows of a declared
  set of kinds and budget enrolment is not one; `write_points.py` says adding one *"is a ruling
  and not an edit"* and `G81` fails the build until one is recorded. Nothing here opened one.
* **A direct portal enrolment cannot be built honestly today even with permission.** `POST
  /budget-billing/enrollments` takes `plan_offers_budget` as a REQUIRED argument because
  `BR-RAT-043` puts the flag on the rate plan and nothing publishes it (`OQ-237`). A portal
  caller would have to assert a rule it cannot read — and the consequence is a year of what a
  customer pays.
* **The ask is not the telephone call the PO ruled against.** Their reason was *a customer who
  has to ring often doesn't ring*. An ask raises a worklist row without a telephone call; what
  it costs is a wait, not a call.
* **It is reversible.** If the PO wants the direct write, 25.3 keeps its job — the not-eligible
  rows, the ones the drawing says need *Tell them why* — and only 25.4 changes.

**`OQ-CWP-1568` IS NOT REOPENED AND WAS NOT RE-ASKED** (law 13). `OQ-BIL-12359` asks a
different question — *where does the ask keep its facts* — and says in its own body that the
permission half is already ruled, so the next lane cannot mistake one for the other.

### 4 · THE FOUR TILES, AND THE ONE FIGURE THAT IS REAL

Measured on the seeded utility with three status rows written for the test: two enrolled this
month and one on the last day of last month → **`enrolled_this_month` = 2**. That tile is
billing's own row and billing's own `enrolled_on` date, so it is counted.

The other three — `WAITING`, `ELIGIBLE NOW`, `NOT ELIGIBLE` — are all downstream of one
missing fact, so they carry **one shared sentence** rather than three wordings a clerk would
read as three problems. And `count` is served **`null`, never `0`**: a zero on this table says
*six people asked and none of them qualifies*, which is a claim about customers, where a null
is a claim about us. The drawing's own note is what that costs — *"a customer who asked online
and heard nothing asks again by telephone."*

The drawn detail line *"3 from the portal"* is not served. Nothing on `account_budget_status`
records where an enrolment came from, and B14 rule 37 makes a drawn figure an illustration.

### 5 · WHERE THE DRAWING AND B14 DISAGREED — RECORDED, NOT BUILT

Numbered D1–D7 in `04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/conformance/CR-103-BRC03-entry-25-3-asks.md`.
The largest is **D1: group 1, `WHY AN ASK AND NOT AN ENROLMENT`, is not rendered at all** —
four rows, every one of them answering *why does the product work this way*, which B14 rule 33
gives **zero words on screen**: removed, not shortened. The reasoning is in this row, in
`budget_api.py`'s own header and in the conformance record, which is where rule 33 puts it.

⚠ **AND THE TABLE ITSELF IS NOT DRAWN WHILE THE ROWS ARE WITHHELD.** Headers, a search box and
two filter chips over rows that cannot arrive is furniture a clerk would type into —
`DEF-CWP-3925`'s lesson that a control over nothing costs more than a missing one. The COLUMNS
are declared in code regardless, so the day `customers` publishes its read the screen is wiring
and not a rewrite, and **`test_hold_expires_when_customers_publishes_the_read` goes RED that
day and names what to do.**

### 6 · WHAT A CLERK GETS TODAY, BECAUSE A DEAD END IS NOT AN ANSWER

The asks are **already on a worklist** — the requests queue, channel *Customer portal*, with
the customer's own sentence on the row. They are not filterable and not actionable from
billing, which is `OQ-BIL-12359`; they are not invisible. So the screen carries one six-word
sentence and a door: *"These asks reach the requests queue."* → `Open requests →`.

## 2026-09-15 · `DEF-BIL-5326` and `DEF-BIL-5317` — two second opinions on the sub-period bill path

**Both are MAINTENANCE** (`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`): a
user can raise a back-bill and a penalty bill in the product today, so the
question is *why does it do the wrong thing*, not *how do we build it*. They were
fixed by one lane because they touch the same code — `SUB_PERIOD_KINDS` — and
two lanes in one file is how this project has lost work repeatedly (law 11).

⚠ **NOTHING HERE WAS PUT TO THE PRODUCT OWNER, AND HARD-WON LAW 13 IS THE
REASON.** Its short list is a ruling that collides with a signed rule, a ❄️
FROZEN B4/B5 figure, or a fact only they hold. This is none of the three: no
signed statement is reversed, **no frozen figure moves**, and WE-11's
`TAMPER $500.00` is deliberately NOT written anywhere — see below.

### THE SHAPE THEY SHARE, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER FIX

**Neither defect is a rule being wrong. Both are a file holding a SECOND OPINION
about something another file already decided**, and each file stayed internally
consistent, so every suite was green over both.

  * `backbill.py` kept its own copy of *which absent-read reasons are exempt from
    BR-BIL-015*. The interim path's list had grown from two reasons to four
    (`DEF-161`, `DEF-990`/`DEF-1060`); the sub-period copy stayed at one.
  * `penalty.py` kept its own opinion about *whether rating publishes a
    charge-code read*, as the module constant `CHARGE_CODE_READ = "charge_ref"`.
    Rating published `charge_by_code` on 2026-08-27 and three siblings read it;
    this one went on refusing for nineteen days.

**The generalisation, and it is the durable part: where two files must agree
about a money rule, one of them must ASK rather than RESTATE.** A restated list
drifts silently and a restated seam name cannot go stale loudly. `backbill` now
reads `measure_consumption.EXEMPT_FROM_MISSING_READ`; `penalty` now calls
`fee_bill.charge_code_line`, which asks `gather._resolve` at call time.

### `DEF-BIL-5326` — a percent-of-service utility could not be back-billed

**Reproduced first, on the demo tenant, before any code was read.** Account
`E11-0001`, window 2026-08-16 → 2026-09-15, one tenant, one account, three kinds:

| kind | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `interim` | **24 lines, $573.33** — incl. *sewer usage — 60.00% of water volume* **$28.35** and *sewer base charge* **$22.50** | unchanged: **24 lines, $573.33** |
| `backbill` | REFUSED `missing_read_undecided_at_calculate` naming sewer | **24 lines, $573.33**, both sewer lines present |
| `penalty` | REFUSED `missing_read_undecided_at_calculate` naming sewer | **24 lines, $573.33**, both sewer lines present |

Sewer prices a percentage of water (BR-RAT-015), so it has **no reading of its
own to be missing**. `measure_consumption` says so in both paths — measured, it
derives `absent_reason = tariff_prices_no_consumption` for sewer identically for
interim and for back-bill. Only the sub-period path refused. Sewer as a
percentage of water is the ordinary North American arrangement, so **two of the
six one-time bill kinds were unusable by an ordinary tenant**.

⚠ **BR-BIL-015 IS NOT WEAKENED AND THAT HALF IS THE DELIVERABLE.** Proved live
on the same account over three windows with no reads in them (2026-09-01→09-14,
2026-08-21→09-05, 2026-06-01→06-20): all three kinds still refuse
`missing_read_undecided_at_calculate`, naming **battery, electric, gas, solar,
thermal_heat, water** — every metered service — and **not sewer**. A metered
service with no read still stops the bill in every path.

⚠ **A SECOND SITE, AND IT NEEDED A DIFFERENT ANSWER — THE PART THAT COST A
CYCLE.** `_estimate_read_less_segments` decides which services to go and
estimate when a tariff CUTS a sub-period, and it filtered on the READING's
`absent_reason`. **The reading and the service carry different vocabularies for
one service**: measured on `E11-0001`, sewer's READING says `no_meter` —
metering's honest answer, there is no sewer meter — while the SERVICE says
`tariff_prices_no_consumption`. Filtering that set by the shared exempt list
would have exempted trash and left sewer exactly where it was. Whether a read
was ever OWED is a fact about the TARIFF's pricing model, which metering cannot
know, so that set now asks `data.tariffs` through `prices_no_consumption` /
`bills_base_only`.

### `DEF-BIL-5317` — the penalty bill's tamper fee refused over a read that exists

`penalty_charge_line` raised for **every** code in **every** tenant. Its
docstring said *"rating publishes no read that resolves one"*; that was true when
written and false from 2026-08-27, when `DEF-708` pointed
`fee_bill.charge_code_line` at `apps.rating.selectors.charge_by_code`.
`first_bill`'s connection charge and `decisions`' late fee read the same seam.
**Its own tests asserted the refusal**, so the suite was green over a capability
that existed, and a theft bill restated the stolen usage and carried no penalty.

**Measured, same account and window, after the fix:** a penalty bill with
charge code `TAMPER` prices **25 lines**, subtotal **$573.33**, tax **$0.00**,
total **$823.33** — the 24 usage and base lines plus *Tamper fee* **$250.00** as
a non-taxable fee line. With no code it is **24 lines / $573.33**, which stays
legal: a penalty bill may be restated usage and nothing else.

⚠ **THE $250.00 IS THE TENANT'S ROW AND IS NEVER TYPED.** WE-11 and the Billing
blueprint both draw **$500.00**. B14 rule 37 makes a figure drawn in a wireframe
an ILLUSTRATION and never a fact to build to; BR-BIL-019 forbids a hand-typed
amount outright; and $500 would be wrong for every tenant but one. `Decimal("500")`
appears nowhere, and the amended test asserts no fee line contains `500`.

⚠ **THE NEGATIVE HALF IS KEPT AND PROVED.** `charge_by_code` returns
`amount: None` for a `percent` or `percent_with_minimum` rule because it has no
basis to apply, and for a code with no flat amount at all. Measured live in this
tenant: `TAMPER` → **$250.0000** and `CONN` → **$45.0000** build lines;
`DAMAGE` and `TAP` — real codes with no flat amount — and `NOPE` — not a code —
all **REFUSE**. Nothing defaults, because a fee that quietly prices at nothing is
a fee nobody notices was never charged, and it lands on a document hard rule 4
makes immutable.

### WHAT USED WHAT WAS CHANGED (blast radius, both directions)

  * `runs.calculate_account` and `midperiod._measured_segment` spelled the four
    reasons out and now read the shared tuple. **Pure extraction, identical
    membership** — proved by the interim bill above still pricing 24 lines and
    **$573.33** to the cent.
  * `ONE_TIME_UNAVAILABLE`'s `penalty_charge_code_line_cannot_be_priced` row is
    **DELETED WITH ITS REASON**, not reworded, and so is `one_time.py`'s trailer
    exception (5). A live capability behind a sentence saying it does not exist
    is the mirror of dead UI (law 2's other direction, `DEF-CWP-3925`), and it
    keeps a clerk from trying the thing that now works.
  * `penalty.CHARGE_CODE_READ` is **removed**. The wrong string was not the
    defect — holding a string for a seam at all was.
  * Four further files quote `penalty_charge_line` as evidence that the seam is
    missing: `apps/payments/reversal.py` (twice), `apps/payments/ledger_seam.py`
    and `tests/test_us_pay_009_nsf.py`. **They are NOT changed by this lane** —
    each is a different module's stated absence with its own reproduce and its
    own reporter — and they are FILED as `DEF-PAY-5333` rather than edited in
    passing. Measured the same day: `charge_by_code('NSF')` returns
    **30.000000** flat with a GL account, so PE-7's **322.87** balance IS
    producible end to end while `reversal.py` still tells a clerk it is not.

### WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, AND IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED

  * `backbill._measured` still raises BR-BIL-015's refusal for an absent asset
    COUNT (BR-RAT-090) and an unstatable installed CAPACITY (CR-062), where
    `runs` and `midperiod` refuse by their own names. Behaviour is unchanged by
    this lane — those reasons refused before and refuse now — but the sentence a
    clerk reads sends them to the Reads tab when the work is to count the carts.
    Filed as `DEF-BIL-5334`.
  * `midperiod._estimate_missing_segments`' own `short` set has the identical
    reading-vocabulary flaw. It is the MID-PERIOD path, not this one, with its
    own reproduce and blast radius. Filed as `DEF-BIL-5335`.
  * **`apps/billing/penalty.py` and `apps/billing/stages/measure_consumption.py`
    join `DEF-BIL-5329`'s blind spot.** That row — filed by the `DEF-BIL-5318`
    lane hours earlier, for `final_bill.py` — says it exactly: `G7` enforces the
    marker only WITHIN a glob list, so a money path matching no glob is not
    unmarked-and-caught, it is INVISIBLE. These two files now decide money and
    match no glob. **The markers are written into both; NO GLOB IS ADDED**,
    because widening that list is a process event and the PO's call, not a
    lane's (`DEF-1841` is the fourth time that deadlock recurred). No second row
    is filed: `DEF-BIL-5329` is the same finding and a near-duplicate in a
    2,800-row register reads as a register rather than as a finding.

### ⚠ AN ID COLLISION CAUGHT AT PUSH TIME, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS LAW 11 WORKING

The three rows above were first allocated as `DEF-PAY-5330`, `DEF-BIL-5331` and
`DEF-BIL-5333`. While this lane worked, a sibling pushed `DEF-CWP-5330`,
`DEF-BIL-5331` and `DEF-BIL-5332` — so **`DEF-BIL-5331` would have been a
duplicate NUMBER**, which `G17` refuses and which reads, in a 2,900-row
register, as a register rather than as an error. Both lanes' arithmetic was
right; what differed was *which world the maximum came from*, because
`file_defect.py` reads the pushed world plus this checkout and a sibling's rows
are in neither until it pushes.

**What caught it was the unconditional step and nothing else:** re-derive the
register from the pinned tip AT PUSH TIME and re-run
`allocate.py defect --verify`. The register was rebuilt as the tip's bytes plus
three appends, the prefix proved byte-identical, and the rows re-filed as
`DEF-PAY-5333`, `DEF-BIL-5334`, `DEF-BIL-5335`.

⚠ **AND THE MAIN WORKING TREE WAS HOLDING A THREE-ROW REVERT WHILE THIS
HAPPENED.** `file_defect.py` resolves the repo from its OWN location, so rows
filed from a private `git worktree` land in the SHARED tree's register, not the
worktree's. That register was three rows behind the tip, so an ordinary pathspec
commit naming it would have published the subtraction of three sibling rows with
a correct file count and every hunk its author's own — mechanism two exactly. It
was restored to the tip's bytes before anything was pushed.

### RESULT, MEASURED, ON THE BRANCH

## 2026-09-15 · §05 ENTRY 25.2 `SETTLE-UP FORECAST` — THE ONE BUDGET SCREEN WITH NO ENDPOINT, AND THE TWO SIGNS THAT LOOK LIKE A CONTRADICTION

**The wave.** `CR-103-BRC03` continued: the forecast read (`GET
/budget-billing/settle-up-forecast`) and the screen at `/:tenant/billing/budget/settle-up`.
Record: `04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/conformance/CR-103-BRC03-entry-25-2-settle-up-forecast.md`.

**`OQ-142` was read by its STATUS COLUMN and the read is lawful.** The status says
**ANSWERED 2026-08-15** — the PO chose a separate budget-variance account
(*"Create seperate account"*) — and what remains is a **finance re-signature of B5 line
74 ❄️, not a decision**. `posting_seam.budget_variance_account_id` already refuses by
name and says so in its own docstring. **So no `NotImplementedError("OQ-142")` was
added, and adding one would have recorded as open a question the PO closed.** Nothing
this lane built posts anything: the forecast is a read of figures
`account_budget_status` and the append-only `account_budget_events` already hold, which
is exactly where `budget.py` drew the boundary — *"the billing-side arithmetic below is
complete and tested; only the posting is blocked."*

**THE JUDGMENT THE RULES DID NOT COVER: two screens show the same money with opposite
signs, and neither is flipping one.** `BudgetBillsTab` records *"nothing here flips a
sign"* and prints ❄️ WE-8's July as **−50.87**. This screen prints **+50.87 → Collect**,
which is what the drawing draws. They are different FACTS: screen 25 shows the POSITION
an account is in (`variance_balance`), and 25.2 shows the TRANSACTION that is coming.
The engine already published the second one — `budget.SettleUp.amount` is always
positive, `direction` carries the sign, and `SettleUp.signed`'s own docstring reads
*"+ collects, − credits"*, which IS the drawn column. So `balance_signed` is served off
the ❄️ frozen dataclass and **no figure is negated in the API or in the browser.** This
is written down because the next reader will otherwise see two screens disagreeing about
a customer's money and "fix" one of them.

**The three money columns tie out by construction, which is why the browser adds
nothing.** A `billed` event's movement IS `level − actual`, so over one settle-up period
`Σlevel − Σactual` is the balance. Worked on the frozen chain: **paid 3 × 242 = 726.00**,
**actual 292.87 + 231.40 + 198.75 = 723.02**, **balance −2.98 → CREDIT 2.98**. The
period starts at the LAST SETTLE-UP and not at enrolment, or the two sums would report a
year the balance no longer covers.

**`DEF-BIL-5327`, found on the way in and filed before it was fixed.**
`selectors.budget_actuals_to_date` — the Budget Bills tab's shipped `ACTUAL TO DATE`
column — summed every event carrying an `actual`, and a settle-up month writes TWO such
rows for one bill. Measured on the frozen chain driven through its settle-up: **$921.77
over 4 months served where $723.02 over 3 is true**, overstated by **$198.75**, and the
month count inflated with it so the row looked internally consistent. Fixed by filtering
on `event = billed`. **The lesson is the shape: the event KIND is the fact being asked
for, and "has an actual" was a proxy for it that stopped being true the moment a second
event kind carried one.**

**`DEF-BIL-5328`** — the drawn `Export` has no export resource behind it
(`EXPORT_RESOURCES` is a closed eleven and `BR-SHL-010` makes the server's capability row
the config), so it ships **disabled with its reason**, which is the blueprint's own p121
doctrine — and **the hold carries the test that fires when it expires**.

⚠ **TWO GUARDS PASSED THEIR FIRST SABOTAGE, AND THAT IS THE REUSABLE PART.** Both were
written to law 7 and both were checks that do not check. `toContain("disabled")` is
satisfied by the kit's `disabled:opacity-45` CLASS on every Button, disabled or not. And
`toContain("$212.80")` is satisfied by `-$212.80`, so **a sign check built only from
`toContain` cannot see a flipped sign at all** — on the one column a clerk reads out to a
customer. Neither was visible by reading the test; both were found by breaking the
component and watching the suite stay green.

⚠ **NOTHING HERE IS PUT TO THE PRODUCT OWNER.** Hard-won law 13's short list is a ruling
colliding with a signed rule, a ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure, or a fact only they hold. This is
none of the three: no signed statement is reversed, and WE-8's chain is QUOTED and
asserted so drift goes red, never moved. The copy divergences are B14 rule 33 winning
over drawn prose, which is the precedent entry 25.1 already set on the sibling screen.

## 2026-09-15 · `CR-101-BRC03` §06 · Fix a bill step 1 (`26 · What and why`) is built as drawn, and the shape of the holds on steps 2–4 is decided here, BEFORE the code

**Lane A of a two-lane wave. Branch `claude/gifted-johnson-top7zn`.** The blueprint's
sixteen pages (p129–p144 of `05-prototype/04 Billing, As Built.pdf`) were read **as images**
at scale 1.5 (B14 rule 42); the page map is in
`04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/conformance/CR-101-BRC03-step2-06-lane-A-step1.md`. Five
judgments where the written rules ran out, each recorded with its reasoning so nobody re-asks
them (hard-won law 13). **Nothing here reaches the Product Owner** — no signed statement is
reversed, no ❄️ figure moves, and no fact only they hold is missing.

### 1 · Steps 2, 3 and 4 keep what a clerk can do today UNDER the stated absence — a hold is not a regression

The brief for this lane asks that steps 2–4 *"render a stated-absence body for now"* while
lanes C–F build the drawn bodies. The mounted file already renders real bodies on those steps
(`BR-BIL-044`'s nine sections dealt 3 · 3 · 3, the approval signature on step 3, the commit on
step 4), and a clerk corrected a real bill through them in a browser on 2026-09-14. **The
maintenance process is explicit that a fix must not take away a task a user can do today**,
so the absence stated on each step is the absence of the DRAWN shape (26.1–26.5's variants,
26.6/26.7's four panels, 26.8's two groups) and the carried body stays live beneath it. The
test that fires when the hold expires watches the CONTRACT rather than a filename, exactly as
`oneTimeWizardSteps.test.tsx` does: any file in the folder whose code names
`FixABillStepBodyProps` and is not wired by `fixABillSteps.tsx` turns the suite red and names
the file.

### 2 · What the resolve table (group 2, `THE BILLS THAT ANSWERS TO`) reads from TODAY, and what it states as absent

⚠ **AMENDED THE SAME AFTERNOON, BEFORE THIS WAS PUSHED.** As first written this section
said there was **no scope-resolve endpoint** and drew the table from `GET /invoices` with
PAID, STATE and the totals as stated absences, behind a hold test that would fire when lane
B's read landed. **Lane B landed it while this lane was proving its build** (`5f426eb4`,
`GET /corrections/resolve` — `BILL · PERIOD · AMOUNT · PAID · STATE`, paged, with a totals
row computed in SQL over the whole scope and `correctable_statuses`). The hold fired exactly
as designed — *"bulk_corrections.py now serves "paid" — lane B's read has landed. Wire it"* —
and the table was rewired to that read before the push, so no stated absence shipped over a
server that answers. What remains stated: a **`paid`/`state` served as `null`** (payments
unreachable — the seam never answers zero) renders *Not read yet*, and a totals `currency`
of `null` (a scope spanning two currencies, a problem names it) renders *Not totalled yet*.
The rows are the SERVER's resolution — one filter, `resolve_scope_queryset`, shared with
`open_case` — so what a clerk sees in step 1 is what the case pins in step 2. The browser
still sums nothing.

### 3 · The `Or:` row — which chips switch and which narrow is read off the server, not off the drawing

`bulk_corrections.resolve_scope` narrows a scope by exactly two things: a **service** and a
**plan** (*"a second selector NARROWS: run 07-A · service Water · plan Residential Standard is
three predicates, not three cases"*). It has no run-or-cycle narrowing on another kind. So of
the five drawn chips, **`A plan ▾` and `A service ▾` narrow** the chosen scope, and **`One
bill`, `A bill run ▾` and `A cycle ▾` switch** it — they are the *Or* the row is named for.
The drawn sentence *"A second choice narrows rather than widens."* is kept, word for word,
because it is true of the two that narrow. A chip that the server ignored would be dead UI
(hard-won law 2).

### 4 · `Several months on one account` — drawn, selectable, and its Continue is HELD (`DEF-BIL-5348`)

The server's `date_range` scope takes `period_start`/`period_end` and **no account**; sending
it with an account chosen would sweep every bill in the window across the utility. The option
is drawn and choosable (a group that vanishes looks like a bug — the drawing's own rule), the
resolve table shows the account's bills in the window, and Continue is refused in plain words
until the server accepts the narrowing. The hold test reads the accepted scope-key tuple in
`corrections_api.py` and goes red when `account_id` joins it. A date range with NO account is
the bulk case the drawing's own table on p131 names (*"Many accounts at once … a date range"*)
and is opened as before.

### 5 · Multi-select, and the derived sentence

The thirteen reasons are **checkboxes** (the drawing's `WHY — PICK ONE OR MORE`; the API has
taken `reason_codes` as an array since S30). Group 4's sentence names every chosen reason and
the mechanism of the **strongest class present**, in the order the catalogue serves its
`classes` (the server's own `R > C > D` precedence) — the screen derives nothing of its own.
The five *not a correction* rows are drawn as disabled checkboxes with their destination in
the second column, as drawn. The `CLASS` header is kept as drawn; the letters are NOT built
(settled 2026-09-14, entry *"Fix a bill becomes the four-step wizard"* §3a) and the thirteen
cells are left to the band that names the class — nothing is invented to fill them.

**A drawing inconsistency, noted rather than fixed (B14 rule 37):** p131's table sends *"One
account, several months"* to screen **26.4** and *"Many accounts at once"* to **26.5**, while
the entries themselves are `26.2 Several months` and `26.3 A batch`, with `26.4` Goodwill and
`26.5` The page only. The entries win; the table's screen numbers are illustrations.

## 2026-09-15 · FIX A BILL STEP TWO, THE TWO SINGLE-BILL SHAPES — SEVEN JUDGMENTS WHERE THE DRAWING RAN OUT

`CR-101-BRC03` step 2, lane C. Screens **26.1 `One bill`** (class R) and **26.5 `The page
only`** (class D), built to `05-prototype/04 Billing, As Built.pdf` pages **p129, p130, p134,
p135, p139 and p140**, every one read **as an image** at scale 1.5 and again at scale 4 (B14
rules 41 and 42). None of the seven below was put to the Product Owner: none reverses a signed
rule, none moves a frozen figure, and none needs a fact only they hold (hard-won law 13).

### 1 · The drawn heading *"THEIR DISCOUNT IS SAFE"* is used for the case it was drawn for, and for no other

p135 draws group 2 of 26.1 as `2 THEIR DISCOUNT IS SAFE` over the sentence *"Their $8.40
low-income discount is on both bills"*. Lane B's panel has **seven outcomes**, and one of them
— `on_the_original_only` — is a recomputation that DROPPED the reduction, which is money
leaving the customer's pocket. A heading reading *safe* over that row would be false on the
approval surface.

**Decided:** the drawn heading renders when the outcome is `on_both_bills`, which is the case
the drawing draws; every other outcome takes **`Their discount`**. Two catalogue keys, one
conditional, and a jsdom case proves the *safe* heading is absent on a dropped reduction — the
sabotage that makes the heading unconditional turns that case red.

### 2 · 26.5 draws a THIRD absent panel, for the discounts

p140 draws two absences on 26.5 — `— NO PAYMENTS TO MOVE` and `— NO TAX CHANGES` — which are
exactly the two cells p129's case table marks **Absent** for that row. Its DISCOUNTS cell reads
**Unchanged**, and the screen drawing has no group for it, so the fact would have appeared
nowhere.

**Decided:** it is drawn, in the same shape as the other two — `— NO DISCOUNT CHANGES` over
*"Nothing is re-priced, so it stays."* The blueprint's own rule on p129/p130 is the reason:
*"A clerk who sees no payments panel on a goodwill credit should read why there isn't one, not
wonder whether the screen forgot"*, and p135's annotation calls *"Am I losing my discount?"*
**the question a clerk is actually asked**. Lane B already serves the answer as
`outcome: "unchanged"`, so nothing is invented — a served fact was simply going to be dropped.

### 3 · Step 2 is ONE registry slot and FIVE drawn screens, so the slot dispatches

`FIX_A_BILL_BODIES` has one entry per STEP and `HELD_FIX_A_BILL_STEPS` one hold per step, while
p129 gives step 2 five variants built by three different lanes at the same time.

**Decided:** `fixABillSteps.tsx` gains `STEP2_DRAWN_BODIES`, a map from blueprint entry to the
drawn body, and the slot's body dispatches on `step2VariantFor`. A lane landing `26.2`, `26.3`
or `26.4` adds **one line** to that map and takes its entry out of the hold's `entries` string;
nothing else in the file moves, which is what four lanes editing one file at once needs. The
step stays `carried: true` and stays on the hold list until all five have landed, because
`carried` is a fact about the STEP and three of the five still render yesterday's body — and
because lane F's flipped assertion now reads `carried` off the hold list. **The stated absence
never appears over a drawn variant:** the drawn body renders INSTEAD of the carried one, not
beneath it, which is hard-won law 2's mirror (`DEF-CWP-3925` — a live screen behind a dead
control).

### 4 · The group rules take the divider, not the accent, because the frames disagree

p134 draws an ACCENT rule above `1 LINE BY LINE` and p135 a GREY one above `2 THEIR DISCOUNT IS
SAFE`; p140 does the opposite way round — grey above group 1, accent above group 2. Two frames
of one drawing, disagreeing about the same thing, which is B14 rule 37's situation.

**Decided:** build the shape they agree on — a horizontal rule between groups — and take it
from `OneTimeWizardZone`, the numbered accent group lane A already mounts for step 1 of this
same wizard. One screen, one chrome.

### 5 · The answer sentence is composed from the payload's own two figures, never from the server's prose

p134 draws *"This bill drops by $99.24. They have already paid it, so they will be $99.24 in
credit."* The server has a sentence that says almost this — `sections.the_customers_balance.
in_plain_language` — and it reads *"…it is payments' fact and was not supplied
(`balance_before`). BR-BIL-044 §6 requires it…"*. That is `DEF-BIL-5267` and `DEF-BIL-5344`'s
shape, and B14 rules 32 and 33 forbid it on screen.

**Decided:** two catalogue sentences, interpolating two figures the payload already carries —
`the_money.delta` for the first and the settlement's `returns_to_credit` for the second — each
through `formatMoney`, the same function `MoneyCell` calls (BR-SHL-023, one money path). **The
screen performs no arithmetic:** a leading `-` and a run of zeroes pick the VERB (*drops* /
*rises* / *does not move*) and the sign is then stripped from the figure the verb already
describes. Nothing is added, subtracted, or parsed as a number; a screen that did would be a
second definition of the correction's arithmetic, which is what `preview_hash` exists to make
impossible.

### 6 · *"Payments already made, and applied"* comes to step 2 as the settlement panel's four figures

The Product Owner's action table marks row 18 — *"Show payments already made in the period, and
applied"* — **"Built but in step 3, not step 2"**. Section 6 carries exactly those four figures
(`paid_to_date`, `rebill_takes`, `returns_to_credit`, `still_owed`), computed by
`corrections.settlement_preview`.

**Decided:** 26.1 draws them in a third group, `WHAT THEY HAVE PAID`, reusing the four labels

Rule 33 caps a FACT at six words and a heading at three. Lane A's step 1 kept the drawn group
headings at their drawn length (*"The bills that answers to"*, *"So this is what will happen"*),
and changing that convention is a screen-wide act rather than one step's, so the headings here
are drawn verbatim. The sentences are shortened, as lane A shortened four of step 1's:

| Drawn | Built |
|---|---|
| *"The old bill is credited in full and a replacement issued — nothing is edited."* (13) | **The old bill is credited. A replacement is issued.** (5 + 4) — the third clause is already step 1's `noEditNote` |
| *"A document correction whose money delta is not zero is refused."* (11) | **A money change here is refused.** (6) |
| *"Read from the account as it stands now."* (8) | **Read from the account now.** (5) |
| *"Fix a name now and an address in November and both survive."* (12) | **Two fixes months apart both survive.** (6) |
| *"$0.00 moves, so the money that met this bill is untouched."* (11) | **Nothing moves. What they paid stays.** (3 + 3) |
| *"Still exists, and is still what was first sent"* (9) | **Still what was first sent** (5) |
| *"A second fix later"* (4, a label) | **Another fix later** (3) |

**And two things the drawing draws that this lane did NOT build, because nothing serves them:**

## 2026-09-15 · FIX A BILL STEP FOUR (`26.8 Generate and send`) — FIVE JUDGMENTS, AND THE ONE THE PRODUCT OWNER MAY WANT BACK

Lane F of the §06 wave, built to p144 and the upper third of p145 read as images. ⚠ **Written
after the code rather than before it, which step W forbids** — said plainly rather than
back-dated. The screen it describes is on the branch and every figure below was read off the
running product at `http://127.0.0.1:8084` on the demo tenant.

### 1 · The step body DRAWS and the frame WRITES — the lane brief and the contract disagreed, and the contract won

The brief for this lane said to *"move that behaviour into your step body"* for approve and
execute. `fixABillContract.ts` says the opposite in terms: *"A body READS; it never opens,
approves, executes or abandons… a body drawing its own button would lose that guard
(DEF-712)."*

**Decided: the contract.** It is not deference — it is what `DEF-712` already cost. The frame
single-flights the one transactional commit (BR-SHL-019), renders A18 §3's working state and
A18 §4's failure-with-entered-state-preserved, and a second button beside it keeps none of the
three. So approve stays step 3's Continue, execute stays the frame's commit, they stay TWO acts,
and **the step-4 body renders no button at all** — asserted by a case that goes red the moment
one appears. Nothing was re-implemented and nothing was moved.

**What that costs, stated rather than hidden:** p145 draws `Create 12 documents & post` and the
frame passes the uncounted `billing.fix.commit.createAndPost`. The count is one line in lane A's
file and eleven plural strings; the exact hunk is in the lane record's §10, and it was not taken
here because four lanes were editing that file the same hour.

### 2 · Group 2 draws ONE "Other channels" row where the drawing draws two named ones

p145 draws `Email · Not available · Needs a channel election we do not publish` and
`Text · In-app · Portal · Not available · Not named in billing's delivery seam`.

**Decided: the served channels get a row each, and everything else gets one row —
`Other channels · Not offered here · Print is the only route.`** Two reasons at once. Both drawn
WHY cells are RATIONALE, which B14 rule 33 puts at zero words on screen; and both CHANNEL cells
are a **hand-typed channel list that billing's own delivery seam does not name** —
`what_the_customer_will_receive` serves `{"channels": ["print"]}` and nothing else. Typing the
rest into the screen is the eleventh-service mistake in miniature: it reads correctly today and
rots silently the day a channel arrives, with every check green.

⚠ **This is the largest visible difference between the built screen and the drawing, so it is
the one to put in front of the Product Owner.** If they want `Email` named, the honest route is
for the server to serve every channel it knows about with a state each — which is what the bill
run's own send step already does (`billing.run.sending.channel.*`, three states: *Goes out*,

### 3 · The counts come off the BILLS, and the kinds come off the class

p145's annotation: *"R — a credit note and a replacement, per bill. C — a credit note only.
D — a reissued document only. Only group 1's counts change with the class."*

**Decided:** the KINDS are the class's (three lists, from `corrections.py`'s own per-class
`documents` tuples) and every COUNT is the number of bills that really carry a document at that

panel already records as one of two readings in the corpus. The drawing's prose is an
illustration (B14 rule 37); the engine is what actually writes. The screen says **Account
credit · Comes off a future bill**.

`_case_detail` serves BR-BIL-044's nine sections for a SINGLE-bill case and the aggregate panel,

shapes."* The drawn screen is a six-month case, which is a bulk case — so on the very shape it

**Decided: the drawn row is still drawn, and its count reads _Not counted_** (BR-SHL-020 — the

`the_gate.standing_statement` cites `BR-BIL-044` inside its own text,
`what_the_customer_will_receive.detail` names an unbuilt schema field in backticks, and
