## 2026-09-15 · `CR-101-BRC03` §07 · Past billing runs (screen 27) is built as drawn, and the four judgments the drawing could not settle are decided here, BEFORE the code

Read as images per B14 rule 42: `05-prototype/04 Billing, As Built.pdf` **p145 and p146
at scale 2**, p146 again **cropped at scale 4** (the head-and-toolbar band and the table
band) and its notes at 2.5, plus **p007 at scale 3** for the page head. Nothing below was
taken from the text layer.

The screen is the `history` tab of the Billing page — `/:tenant/billing/history` — and it
shipped a grey panel reading *"Past billing runs list every run with what it produced and
who signed it off. It arrives with the billing run work."* over a read that has answered
since `CR-029`. That is `DEF-BIL-5351`, and the blueprint says so about itself on p145:
the blocker the screen names is *"false in both halves that matter"*.

### 1 · The page head stays as it is on this tab, because the blueprint draws it two ways

p007 draws this page titled **Billing**, with *Bills lifetime 7240 · Out this cycle
$342,180.00 · Unresolved from the last run 3 →* beneath it and the three buttons
`Pending queue` · `Print bills` · `Start a billing run →`. p146 draws **the same page**
titled **Past billing runs**, with *34 runs · 11,842 bills issued this year* beneath it
and two actions, `Export` and `Start a run →`. Both are frames of one page, so *the frame
wins* cannot settle it — this is B14 rule 37's third clause exactly, and the portal's own
`+ Add an account` entry of 2026-09-12 is the precedent: **what the two frames agree on is
the SHAPE** — title, one rollup line, right-aligned actions, then the seven-tab strip —
and the shipped head already is that shape.

So the head does not re-title per tab. Re-titling would have put `Past billing runs` over
a page whose other six tabs the blueprint titles `Billing`, on the authority of one frame,
and the head is shared by all seven. The drawn `Start a run →` is the shipped
`Start a billing run →`, same action and same destination; the drawn `Export` is built
where p146 ALSO draws it, as the toolbar's `↓` (`DataTable`'s IS-9 download slot), rather
than twice.

### 2 · The drawn `Open` link is built as B14 rule 15's icon, and the row itself opens the run

p146's last column is an unlabelled `Open` in link red on every row, and its note is the
point of the screen: *"Every row opens the run it names — its exceptions, its totals and
its sign-off. A table you cannot drill into is a report, and this is a workspace."*

**B14 rule 15 is RATIFIED and G37-ENFORCED: row actions are ICONS with tooltips, never text
links.** So the drawing loses on CONSTRUCTION and wins on CONTENT, which is rule 38's split
carried to a table: the drill-in is built THREE ways and all three are the drawn one —
the `RUN` cell is the identity link (which is how `All bills` builds its bill number), the
whole row carries `rowHref` to the same address, and the actions column holds the 👁
`RowAction`. Nothing is invented and no text link ships. Recorded, not raised.

### 3 · The VALUE column is absent because nothing serves it — NOT because a rule forbids money here

`apps/billing/api.py`'s exception (3) and `selectors.bill_runs_list`'s own header both keep
money off this row citing **`BR-MET-078` as hardened by CR-029**, *"Money never touches
these surfaces"*. Measured against the rule's own wording, that citation is out of scope:
`BR-MET-078` is the PO's *"you dont need late fees in this. so dont have anything related
to money when you create route and cycles"*, and its subject is r10 `SET-07.3` — the route
and cycle **creation** screens. A billing run's history row is neither.

**So the drawn `VALUE` column is not blocked by a signed rule.** It is absent from this
build for the only reason that is true: no endpoint serves a run's value or its currency
today. It is drawn as a stated absence and a test goes red the day the field arrives. This
is written down rather than relied on quietly, because a lane reading the two docstrings
would conclude the opposite and build nothing.

### 4 · What the server cannot answer yet is stated once and tested, never faked

Measured against the live demo tenant at `GET /billing/runs`, three runs, not the 34 the
drawing illustrates (B14 rule 37): `run_no`, `period_start`/`period_end`, `bills_issued`,
`ran_by_name` and `cycle_id` are all served — so **RUN, PERIOD, BILLS, RUN BY and CYCLE are
built today**, the cycle by its `code` through the tenant's own cycle list, never by its id
(B14 rule 31). `VALUE`, the four tiles, the `Status`/`Year` filters, the search box and a
page total are **not served**, so none of them is drawn: a filter the server ignores and a
search box that searches nothing are both a screen lying about what it did.

They are named ONCE, in the disclosure the module already uses (`RunGap`, structurally a
`<details>` closed by default — B14 rule 32), and each one carries a test that fires the
day it lands. `STATUS` is the fifth: `bill_runs.status` is written `"draft"` at creation
and no writer advances it (`DEF-BIL-5352`), so the pill composes from evidence through
`runStatusLabel`, which `Cycle detail` and the run wizard already share — three screens,
one composer. The blueprint's three status words (`Issued`, `Corrected`, `Abandoned`)
arrive when the column does.

## 2026-09-15 · `CR-101-BRC03` §06 · Fix a bill step 2 for a case with MANY BILLS — `26.2 Several months` and `26.3 A batch` (lane D)

**Lane D of a four-lane wave.** Five judgments where the written rules ran out, each
recorded with what was measured so nobody re-asks them (hard-won law 13). **Nothing here
reaches the Product Owner** — no signed statement is reversed, no ❄️ figure moves, and no
fact only they hold is missing. p129 and p135–p138 were read **as images** at scale 1.5 and
again as crops at scale 4 (B14 rule 42); the full record, with the pictures, is
`04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/conformance/CR-101-BRC03-step2-06-lane-D-bulk.md`.

### 1 · THE ANSWER BAND IS THREE SHORT FACTS, NOT THE DRAWN SENTENCE — AND IT LOSES NOTHING

p137 draws *"412 bills are affected. 389 go up and 23 go down, for a net of +$4,593.80."*
That is 21 words where B14 rule 33 caps a FACT at six. Rule 33's own clause is that **two
sentences of six beat one sentence of twelve**, so the band is three facts of three or four
words: `24 bills change. · 23 up, 1 down. · Net $689.37`. **Both directions are still on
the face of it**, which is what BR-BIL-046 and p138's own annotation insist on (*"↑ and ↓
are not optional, and a test proves it"*), and the money goes through `MoneyCell` rather
than into an interpolated string, because a figure inside a sentence cannot carry its
currency (rule 2).

### 2 · THE DRAWN PER-BILL CHECKBOX IS NOT BUILT, BECAUSE THE SERVER REFUSES THE WHOLE CASE

p136 draws seven bills with six ticked and the seventh disabled — *"Cannot be increased —
13 months old"* — under the sentence *"Each bill is judged on its own age, so a window can
be partly allowed."* **Measured: it cannot.** `corrections.refuse_upward_beyond_window`
RAISES, and `bulk_corrections.open_case` calls it inside the per-bill loop, so one bill past
the cap with an upward delta refuses the WHOLE case at step 1. No case ever HOLDS such a
bill, so the checkbox could never be pressed and p137's *Beyond the 12-month cap · Removed
from the set* row could never be anything but zero. A control nobody can press is a status
(B14, `DEF-1083`) and a row that is structurally always zero teaches a clerk something
false, so neither is built. **Which of the two moves — the server allowing a partial set, or
the drawing losing the checkbox — is a product question and is `DEF-BIL-5360`**, not an
engineering one: a clerk who asked for seven months and got six needs to know which one.

### 3 · FOUR FIGURES THE SERVER CANNOT ANSWER ARE DRAWN AS ABSENCES, EACH WITH THE TEST THAT FIRES WHEN IT IS SERVED

A **PERIOD** on a pinned row (`DEF-BIL-5358`), a **paid total across a batch**
(`DEF-BIL-5359`), the partial window above, and a **`Narrowed by` row** — the case's scope
carries `plan_id`/`service_code` as ids, and a uuid may not be rendered (B14 rule 31) nor a
raw service code (`DEF-BIL-5336`). The first two are drawn as stated absences with a guard
that reads the SERVER's source and goes red the day the field lands; the second two are
recorded rather than invented. **Nothing is guessed** — in particular the month is never
derived from a bill number, which only looks like one.

### 4 · THE SCREEN WINDOWS WHAT THE SERVER SENT WHOLE, AND SAYS SO

`corrections_api._case_detail` builds `bills_detail` from `case_bills(case)` with no
envelope, no `page` and no `per`, so a T5 run of 40,000 bills is 40,000 impact objects in
one GET (`DEF-BIL-5361`). The screen adds **no cap** (`NFR-5` forbids one) and cannot page
what arrived whole; it windows the set it was already given, and a case names the screen
that must follow the day the endpoint pages its rows.

### 5 · ⚠ THE PRODUCT OWNER'S ROW 18 IS ANSWERED FROM `impact.settlement`, WHICH ALREADY EXISTED

*"Show payments already made in the period, and applied"* was marked *"Built but in step 3,
not step 2"*. CS-36's four figures — paid to date, what the replacement takes, what returns
to credit, what is still owed — are on **every** per-bill impact of a restatement already
(`corrections.settlement_preview`), so step 2 needed no server change: four columns read
them. Where payments could not be asked the seam answers `null` and the cell reads *Not read
yet*; **it never reads `$0.00` on a guess**.

### ⚠ AND THE WALK FOUND THAT THIS TENANT CANNOT OPEN A CLASS-R BULK CASE AT ALL — `DEF-BIL-5377`

`POST /corrections` with any bulk scope and a class-R reason returns **422**: *"account
'AC-2026-00042' is not in the billable set for its unit (BR-CUS-055)"*. That account is
CLOSED and holds two issued bills. **Six scopes were tried and six refused** — the June run,
a June date range, four rate plans, cycle CY-001, and both service scopes that match
anything at all (`electric` and `water` each resolve all 79 correctable bills, and both of
the closed account's bills are in both). A class-**D** case over the same cycle opens fine,
79 bills, which places the refusal in the re-pricing path rather than in the scope.
**At 40,000 accounts a utility always has closed ones, so bulk corrections do not work at T5
as it stands**, and the refusal a clerk reads is an account number and a customers rule id.
The probe case was abandoned with a reason; no live case was left.

### ⚠ THREE FAULTS CAME OUT OF THE PICTURES AND NOT ONE COULD HAVE FAILED A TEST

A column of whole warning SENTENCES set the height of its whole ROW and made seven bills a
wall three times their drawn height — `TableColumnConfig.cell`'s own docstring is written
against exactly that, and the cell holds three or four words now with the sentence on
`title`. Ten columns measured **1,073px inside a 960px step at 1280** with every wrapper
computing `overflow-x: visible`, so the last column was not cramped but UNREACHABLE
(`DEF-SHL-5378` is the kit gap; this screen wraps its own table meanwhile). And the four
payment headers took p143's shorter words, because step 3's panel vocabulary is what ran the
table off the edge. **All three passed `tsc`, eslint, 22 DOM cases and every gate while the
screen was wrong**: jsdom performs no layout, and the instrument was a person looking at a
capture.

### ⚠ THE SHARED STEP-2 REGISTRY: THIS LANE THREW ITS OWN DESIGN AWAY, ON PURPOSE

Lane D built a variant registry and, before it could push, **lane C landed the same idea
under different names** with a comment saying what a sibling's edit should be. Lane D
adopted lane C's and deleted its own, so the final hunk in `fixABillSteps.tsx` is three
lines rather than two registries doing one job. **That is what re-reading the tip before
re-applying a blob is FOR** (law 11), and it is worth recording because the cheaper move —
pushing the version already written — would have been invisible to every check.

## 2026-09-15 · `CR-101-BRC03` §08 · Print bills (screen 28) is built as drawn, and the nine judgments the drawing could not settle are decided here

Lane J, building blueprint screen 28 from p147–p150 read as images (B14 rule 42).
Closes `DEF-BIL-5354`. Nothing here was put to the Product Owner: none of it moves a
frozen figure, none of it collides with a signed rule without the rule winning, and
none of it is a fact only they hold (law 13).

### 1 · A bill is TWO pages, not the six the wireframe draws

The PAGES tile is what a print shop quotes against, so the number had to be real. The
drawing shows *"~2,424 · 6 a bill, measured"*. **Measured instead, on 2026-09-15:
every one of the demo utility's 79 printable bills was drawn through `_page_for` — the
same call the archive makes — and every single one came back at 2 pages**, at 0.0047
seconds a bill. `MEASURED_PAGES_PER_BILL = 2`.

So the tile reads **~158 pages for 79 bills** where the drawing's figures would have
said 474. B14 rule 37 is what decides it: a figure drawn in a wireframe is an
illustration, never a fact to build to.

⚠ **A test bill is not a real bill, and the test says so out loud.** A fixture bill
with a two-field payload draws in ONE page, so the test holds the constant against the
renderer **within one page** rather than exactly. That tolerance cannot catch the
layout gaining exactly one page; only re-measuring on real bills can, and the
constant's own note says to do it when the layout changes.

### 2 · Three of the eight hold reasons can be forecast, and five cannot

The screen has to say *"8 held back, each with a reason"* BEFORE a clerk commits a
worker to an archive. The archive decides it a bill at a time, cheapest check first:
the bill number, then a filename collision, then the address, and only then does it
draw the page.

**Everything above the draw is forecastable and everything at or below it is not.** No
bill number, a bill number no filename can carry, and an incomplete mailing address
are two columns and a seam read. A refused document, a kept original that will not
read back and a page count that cannot be taken are only knowable by drawing the page
— and forecasting those would mean rendering every bill in the period to paint a
screen. `held-back.csv` inside the finished archive stays the record of all eight.

`duplicate_filename` is left out for a different reason: `uq_invoices_no` is a UNIQUE
index over (tenant, bill number), so two bills cannot share one and the check in the
archive guards a constraint that would have to have failed first.

**The counts are four COUNTs over the archive's own selection — measured at 4
statements and 0.026 seconds on the demo tenant**, and a page of fifty rows is judged
in ONE more. The alternative, asking the address seam a bill at a time, is two
statements a bill: 158 on this tenant and 80,000 at the top of the ICP, which is the
shape `NFR-3` exists to forbid.

### 3 · Where a drawn control would have promised something the server refuses

Four controls are drawn on p148 that this build does not offer, and in each case
offering it would have been a screen lying about what it did:

* **Status** — a print set is issued and paid bills always, and the server drops a
  status filter deliberately.
* **Route and service** — neither is in any list's filter vocabulary, so there is
  nothing to send. This one is a HOLD, and it carries the test that fires when it
  expires: the day either filter is accepted, `test_route_and_service_are_drawn_
  filters_that_no_list_serves` goes red and names the screen that owes them a control.
* **Manifest format** — one format is registered, so a picker is a control with a
  single option (B14 rule 32). The FIELD is still shown with the drawing's own warning
  line, because what the vendor receives is worth knowing before it is handed over.
* **Bill layout** — a reprint renders the version PINNED at issue for ever
  (`BR-BIL-026`), so there is no layout to choose. It reads **"Each bill's pinned
  layout"** rather than the drawn *"Default — your live template"*, which would have
  been false.

### 4 · The period picker filters the ISSUE date, and its labels say so

Drawn as *Period from / Period to*. The server's window is `issued_from`/`issued_to`,
the day the bill was ISSUED; a bill's service period is a different pair of dates and
nothing filters on them. **A control labelled *Period* that narrows by issue date
answers the one question this screen exists to answer — is this customer's bill in the
set — wrongly**, so the label follows the filter: **Issued from / Issued to**.

### 5 · Two doors that would have opened onto nothing are not drawn as doors

**`Past print sets`** (top right, p148): nothing records a print set after it is handed
over — the archive is a job artefact fetched by job id, and no table says which cycle
it covered or who made it. The button is not drawn; the absence is stated where a
clerk would look for it, as *"Past sets · Not recorded after hand-over."*
(`DEF-BIL-5374` carries what recording one would take.)

**`See the 8 held back →`**: screen 28.1, with its eight named reasons and whose job
each one is, is not built (`DEF-BIL-5375`). The control is live instead of dead — it
narrows this table to the held rows and becomes *"Show all bills"*, so it is not a
one-way door — and it loses the arrow, because B14's button grammar gives `→` to
something that navigates.

### 6 · Three headings shortened, and two drawn sentences removed

*"THE BILLS IN THIS PERIOD"* → **Bills this period**, *"WHAT THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT
CLAIM"* → **Not claimed here**: B14 rule 33 caps a heading at three words, and the
repo's own precedent is a sibling lane doing exactly this on the budget-asks screen
four days ago.

Two sentences drawn inside the screen frame are rationale — *why* the product works
this way — which rule 33 gives **zero words on screen**. They are in the code's own
header instead. A third keeps its instruction and loses its reason: *"Search it before
you generate."*

### 7 · What the browser found that no check could

Two layout faults, found by putting the 1440px capture beside p148 and p149: **the
tiles were built below the form and the drawing puts them above it**, and **the account
cell was a stacked pair where the drawing draws `100377 · Ridge Coffee Co.` on one
line** — which also halves the height of every row in a fifty-row table. Both fixed.

And one copy fault no test could have caught: the tile read **"about 1 seconds"**.
`{{seconds}}` is not i18next's `count`, so nothing was ever going to pluralise it. One
now has its own sentence, *"about a second"*, in all eleven languages.

### 8 · The demo tenant has no held bill, and that is information

**79 printable bills, all in cycle `CY-001`, every one with a complete mailing
address**, so the drawn *"8 held back"* has no real row to stand on. The held state was
seeded through the product as a clerk would — an account's mailing address with its
city cleared, through `PATCH /accounts/{id}/mailing-address` — which held that
account's two bills, and the city was put back in the same pass. The tiles then read
**77 + 2 = 79**, which is the arithmetic the blueprint asks for in capitals.

Three rulings in one message, while the PO was reading the field-level

because `BR-MET-112` holds every write to the final commit: eight of its steps

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT: THE PREMISE STEP ALSO DECIDES SERVICES AND THE PLAN

The PO walked the field-level measurement of the new connect wizard step by
step and confirmed three of them as correct — step 1 (Owner & scope), step 2
(Premise) and step 3 (Units), each with its built/not-built column. **Those
three measurements are now signed and are the build target.** On step 3 they
confirmed specifically that the disabled *Upload a unit schedule* button is
right as it stands.

On step 2 they added two requirements, verbatim:

> *"you also need select utility services - one or more from drop down - multi
> selct drop down - only utlity services activated by teantn/utility. you also
> need to select Plan at this stage not at step 5; once plan is slected show the
> details of plan as summary"*

### WHAT MOVES, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE SAME AS THE STEP THAT LOSES IT

**Services** are chosen on the PREMISE step as a multi-select of the tenant's
own enabled services. The Map services step keeps the per-unit grid: **the
premise decides which services are in play, the grid decides which UNIT gets
which.** The availability constraint that already exists — a unit may only take
a service the premise offers — becomes the join between the two.

**The plan** is chosen on the premise step and its details are summarised there.
Plans & work orders keeps the work-order template and the target activation date
(which arrives there from step 2 in the same wave, per the drawing on p089).

⚠ **THE COVERAGE CHECK MOVES WITH THEM AND MUST NOT BE LOST.** `PlansStep`
computes real plan-coverage gaps against the plan's own service list —
*"WON'T COVER — the plan chosen does not cover {{services}}"* — and never
blocks. It is one of the few checks on this wizard computed for real rather than
drawn, and it now has to run when either services or plan change.

⚠ **AND THE MONTHLY FIGURE STAYS ABSENT.** The drawing prints
`$30.50/month × 25 = $762.50`. A plan summary is not permission to multiply that
up in a browser: hard rule 2 rounds money once, on the server, and no endpoint
publishes a plan's base charge per unit to this screen. `PlansStep` already
carries that refusal with its reasoning; the summary carries it forward.

### THE TRAP THIS RULING WALKS INTO, NAMED IN ADVANCE

A multi-select of *"only utility services activated by this tenant"* is the
third place the front end would be tempted to type the service list out by
hand. **The first two are why hard-won law 2 exists** — `SignupWizard.tsx`'s
tick-list and `ratingShared.tsx`'s badge map, where an eleventh service does not
appear on screen and fails SILENTLY: the row exists, the API serves it, `tsc`
and every test pass, and the screen simply never offers it. The list is read
from the tenant's enabled set or it is not built.

### WHERE THIS IS GOING

This is the PO's own simplification arriving one step at a time. They put it
plainly on 2026-09-15: *"when we dedice premises we also dei=cide utilities
services and plans that will be required so i will ask or input all those
detials and then just on sepearet ppage ask for Units and thats it … show create
grid directly"*. The eight-step shape is being collapsed toward three by moving
decisions onto the page where they are already being made, rather than by
deleting any of them.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT: A UNIT INHERITS THE PREMISE'S SERVICES, SO THE GRID SHOWS RATHER THAN ASKS

The PO confirmed the step 4 (Map services) measurement as correct, and then
answered what the grid's cells should be. Verbatim:

> *"units inherit all utility services from premises - hence we have to show all
> utility services"*

and, on the same step:

> *"you move how many services to premises itself - the grid part - instead of
> tick can you make them drop down"*

### WHAT THIS SETTLES, AND IT IS LARGER THAN A CONTROL

**The per-unit service choice is not a choice.** Services are decided once, on
the premise step, as the multi-select ruled earlier the same day; a unit
**inherits** them. So:

* **the drawn *"Apply to all units / Choose per unit"* pair is unnecessary** —
  the answer is always *all*, and a radio whose second option nothing will pick
  is a control that teaches a clerk the wrong model;
* **the grid SHOWS the inheritance** — every unit, every service the premise
  takes — rather than asking a question per cell;
* **the dropdown the PO asked for is the PREMISE-level one**, not eighteen
  dropdowns in a grid. *"the grid part — instead of tick can you make them drop
  down"* reads as the tick-list becoming the premise multi-select, which is the
  same instruction arriving twice.

The three running counts under the grid — service points, meters to fit, work
orders — **stay visible**, ruled in the same exchange. They change as the grid
changes and they are the only feedback that it is right.

### THE ONE PLACE INHERITANCE COLLIDES WITH THE DRAWING, AND THE READING TAKEN

⚠ **The blueprint's whole argument for this grid is the common area.** p089, in
red: *"The common area is why this grid exists. It takes electric and water and
no sewer — there is nothing to drain from a hallway and a car park."* The drawn
grid ticks electric and water on the common-area row and leaves sewer **empty**.

Pure inheritance gives the car park a sewer connection.

**Reading taken, and it is a judgment rather than a ruling:** inheritance is the
**DEFAULT, not a lock.** Every unit opens with every premise service already
set, so a clerk who does nothing gets the PO's rule exactly; the cell stays
editable so the common area can drop the one it does not take. That satisfies
the ruling as stated and keeps the one case the drawing exists to argue, and it
is the only reading that loses neither. **If the PO wants inheritance to be
absolute, the common-area exception has to move somewhere else and this row is
where to start from.**

### WHAT A CELL IS NOT

The four shapes offered and not chosen are recorded because the next lane will
wonder: a cell is **not** a plan picker (the plan is the premise's, ruled the
same day), **not** a meter size or type (that is an asset decision, and
`sub_meter_links` on this same screen already answers *"cannot be made from
here"*), and **not** a three-way including a shared-meter case. It is the
inherited service, shown.

   few more work order"*. Today the list is remove-only: the proposal is the
   server's and the draft carries only `removedWorkOrderTemplateIds`. Adding
   means a picker over the utility's published templates and a second list the
   draft has to carry.

**The target activation date stays here** — it arrives from step 2 in the same
wave, because the blueprint draws it on this step beside the work-order template
it dates, and that is still true when the plan leaves.

⚠ **THE COVERAGE WARNING HAS NOWHERE LEFT TO LIVE ON THIS STEP.** *"WON'T COVER
— the plan chosen does not cover {{services}}"* is computed for real against the
plan's own service list and never blocks. With the plan gone from here it moves
to the premise step with it, which the earlier ruling already required; this
row records that the move is now forced rather than optional.

⚠ **AND `DEF-MET-5428` GETS BIGGER, NOT SMALLER.** The wizard already sends its
chosen work orders and `commit_connection` never reads them, so a clerk told
*"nine orders will be written"* gets none. **Letting the clerk ADD orders makes
that silent loss worse** — a hand-picked order would vanish the same way as a
proposed one. The add control must not ship before the commit reads the list.

### STEP 6 · CHARGES IS REQUIRED

> *"this step is required"*

The PO confirmed the measurement — **every drawn element is Not built on the
front end**, and the back end has no door for most of them — and ruled the step
in. That closes the question of whether the money conversation could be dropped
to reach a shorter wizard: it cannot.

**The blocker is unchanged and it is not this screen.** Billing's one-time
charge door takes ONE `connection_charge_code` with **no amount, no description
and no lines** (`BR-BIL-020` — an absent field rather than a removable
validation), and the quote is four coded lines with quantities. So today
`commit_connection` records the total on the connection and **posts it nowhere**,
with its own stated absence saying so (`quote_recorded_not_posted`).

**Requiring the step therefore requires widening that door.** It is the same
hole the application fee was in until 2026-09-16, when `CC-REQFEE` was given a
charge row and a revenue account — that fix proved the counter path end to end
($25.00 cash: `DR 1010 Undeposited funds / CR 2400 Customer credit balances`,
then on approval `DR 2400 / CR 4600 Connection & new-service fees`) and it
covers ONE code with ONE amount. A build's quote needs lines.

⚠ **AND THE DRAWING'S OWN EXPLANATION ON THIS PAGE IS STALE, WHICH IS A TRAP FOR
WHOEVER BUILDS IT.** p090 prints, in orange: *"The create-a-payer path refuses,
and the stated reason is that an account must name a unit."* **That reason
expired on 2026-09-01** — `accounts.unit_id` is nullable and `ck_accounts_anchored`
allows premises-only anchoring. The drawing even carries its own correction
beside it. The refusal is real; the reason printed next to it is not, and

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT: STEP 7 IS THREE MESSAGES, NOT SIX, AND STEP 8 OWES TWO BLOCKS

The last two steps of the same walk. The PO confirmed step 8's measurement twice,
in two shapes, including both of the rows I had reported wrong and corrected.

### STEP 7 · THREE DEFAULTS, AND THE SIX-ROW TABLE GOES

> *"in this step we have to do the communication with owner that request is
> created - may be we ahve to send contract , maybe we have to send cost and ask
> them to pay it - all this communciation will be required here and we have to
> make it 3 or 3 communciiton default thats - all these 6-8 line items are not
> required"*

**Three messages go out when the build is created:**

| # | What | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The build request has been created | the drawing's *Build confirmed*; not built |
| 2 | **The contract** | ⚠ **new — nothing in the product or the drawing has one** |
| 3 | What it costs, and please pay it | the drawing's *Quote and what is owed*; blocked with step 6 |

**The drawn six-row table is out.** *Schedule of works*, *Inspection booked* and
*Welcome pack* are not built and are no longer wanted at creation. The PO's
words are plain: *"all these 6-8 line items are not required"*.

⚠ **THE STATUS MESSAGE IS NOT DROPPED AND THIS IS NOT A REVERSAL.** Earlier the
same day the PO ruled *"we need to send mesage that request is created and what
is the status of request"*. A STATUS message fires **on a state change**, not at
creation, so it was never one of this step's defaults — it belongs with the
completion letter, which their 2026-08-25 ruling already moved to the work-order
screen (*"sent it whnr utility user mar that job complete traigger it tat that
time"*). **Recorded explicitly because CLAUDE.md law 13 exists for exactly this
shape:** two genuine rulings that look contradictory until the trigger is named,
and a lane that re-asks manufactures the inconsistency it was trying to avoid.

⚠ **THE CONTRACT IS A NEW OBJECT AND NOBODY HAS SAID WHAT IS IN IT.** The
template library exists and a contract could be one more template, but *"maybe
we have to send contract"* does not say whether it is a document we render, an
agreement the owner signs and returns, or a quote under another name — and a
lane that picks one will build the wrong thing confidently. **This is an open
question to mint, not a value to choose** (prime directive: never resolve an
open question by choosing a value). Everything else on the step is buildable
around it.

**What stays from the drawing:** *Who we are telling* — contact, email, phone,
preferred language — and the template picker with its search, its group /
channel / variant / version columns and its drafts listed but not selectable.
Those three are the parts the back end already has.

**What does not change:** everything here is **queued, and nothing is sent**.
This product writes a row per message and no sender picks it up.

### STEP 8 · CONFIRMED, AND TWO DRAWN BLOCKS ARE OWED

Every element measured as built is confirmed built: the seven counts, the
contract sentence, the occupancy choice, *Sub-meter links* answering *"cannot be
made from here"* rather than `0`, the services tag list we added that the drawing
does not have, *Outstanding work*, and *"Nothing before this button has written
anything"*.

**Two drawn blocks are not built and are now owed:**

1. **"From each step" — every field read back.** The drawing lists owner,

2. **"What happens next" — SEVEN rows**, not six: the build is created across

⚠ **ROW 2 OF THAT TABLE IS ABOUT TO BECOME WRONG, AND IT IS THE STEP-7 RULING
THAT DOES IT.** The drawing says *"Three messages are queued to the owner"* —

## 2026-09-16 · THE NEW CONNECTS LIST GETS ITS TOOLBAR, AND THE BLUEPRINT'S FOUR CHIPS DO NOT ANSWER OQ-371

**What the PO asked for, verbatim:**

> *"now lets start working on New Connect - we have 3 cases here  list view, new
> connect request and view, act and approve - on List view - can you imporve the
> interaction design, you also dont have filter and toolkit - elements search,
> filter, colum selecot, description etc"*

Built from `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` — **p086–p097 read as
images at scale 2, and p094's toolbar band again at scale 4** (B14 rule 42; a
full scale-4 page is 4896×3168 and the reader downsamples away the detail, so
`10-scripts/pdf/crop_render.py` was written to crop before assembling the PNG).

### WHY THE DRAWN CHIPS ARE A FILTER DIMENSION AND NOT A SEGMENT STRIP

p094 draws `[Open] [Partly activated] [Activated] [All]` beside a `[Filter ▾]`.
**`OQ-371` is OPEN and blocks a segment strip on this screen**, so the first
question was whether building these chips answers it. It does not, and the
reason is in the drawing's own arithmetic: the tile above reads **`OPEN BUILDS
2`** while **`PARTLY ACTIVATED 1`** — so `Open` CONTAINS the partly-activated
build rather than competing with it. OQ-371 asks which of two EXCLUSIVE tabs
holds a build that is `partly_activated` AND waiting; nested scopes have no such
question, and `connection_reads.CONNECTION_FILTERS` already records the same
distinction in the opposite direction: *"`f.state=partly_activated` returns the
builds in that state and claims nothing about which tab owns them."*

**So no precedence was decided, nothing is hidden, `?segment=` still raises, and
the two deliberately negative tests that keep OQ-371 open are untouched.**

### AND THEY RENDER THROUGH THE KIT, NOT AS A NEW ROW OF BUTTONS

The Requests tab — the other tab of the same register — already renders its five
segments as **one declared filter dimension**, reading `All · Show: Open × ·
+ Filter ▾`. `DataTable` has no `dimensionsSlot` and its absence is a ruling
(`DEF-1700`): *"a screen that wants a new dimension declares it in
`TableConfig.filters` and passes `filterBarSlot`. It does not grow a row."* So
New connects declares `state` with the drawn values, the kit renders B14 rule
12's grammar, and **the two tabs of one register now ask one question in one
voice.** Worked, on the live demo tenant: `Show: Open ×` gives **8 of 10** rows,
`Show: Partly activated ×` gives **2**, `Show: Activated ×` gives **2**.

The panel offers the drawn three FIRST and then the five remaining states, so
nothing a row can be in became unreachable by gaining a chip in front of it. The
drawing does not draw the inside of its own `Filter ▾` panel, so this adds to an
absence rather than contradicting a drawn one.

### TWO DEFECTS WERE UNDERNEATH THE PO'S SENTENCE, AND NEITHER WAS A MISSING CONTROL

**`DEF-CUS-5432` — the tab has had no filter control at all since 2026-08-27.**
`list_connections` has returned `filters`, `states`, `sorts`, `sort` and `dir`
since CR-045 wave D. `_connections_envelope` forwards its keys BY NAME and was
never amended, so `GET /connections` answered with no `states` on it, the filter
group had no options, `offerableFilters` dropped it, and `FilterBar` returned
`null`. **Every layer behaved exactly as written over a capability nobody could
reach.** Three kinds of check passed: the frontend cases build their own payload
WITH `states` in it (they prove the fixture), `ConnectionList` declares both
fields so `tsc` is satisfied by the type rather than by the server, and the
backend cases call the selector directly. Nobody asked what the ROUTE answers.

**`DEF-CUS-5431` — the `Activated` chip could never have worked.** `f.state`
accepted only `OPEN_STATES` and mapped everything else to an empty queryset, on
a written belief that *"this list is the OPEN worklist, so `activated` and
`cancelled` are already outside it (see `_connections`' window)"*. **There is no
window** — `_connections` is `Connection.objects.filter(tenant_id=…)` and
nothing else — so activated builds have always been in the list, the blueprint
draws one, and the demo tenant holds two. Hard-won law 1: a comment claiming a
guarantee is not the guarantee.

⚠ **The test aimed at that value passed for the wrong reason.** It seeded ONE
`requested` build, asked for `state=activated` and asserted zero — and zero was
the right answer to that fixture whether the filter worked or not. Replaced by a
case holding one activated build and one that is not.

### `Open` IS THE TILE'S OWN SET, RESOLVED IN SQL

`open` is the one chip that is not a stored state. It is `OPEN_STATES`, which is
what the `OPEN BUILDS` tile counts, so a clerk can ask for the set the number
above the toolbar already names. It leaves the browser as `f.state=open` and is
expanded to `state IN (…)` on the server — never in the screen. A case reads the
statement the server actually sent and requires the predicate in the `WHERE` and
the page in a `LIMIT`, because **no assertion about the ANSWER can tell SQL
narrowing from Python narrowing** (`NFR-3`; `CLAUDE.md` names four existing
breaches and says not to add a fifth).

### THE DESCRIPTION IS ONE SENTENCE, AND THE DRAWING'S OWN PARAGRAPHS STAY OFF SCREEN

p093 states this list's whole brief: *"Onto the New connects tab, either raised
directly or created by approving a request — and the list says which."* On
screen that is **"Raised here, or from a request."** — a FACT at rule 33's
six-word cap, at rule 18's `--desc-measure`.

p094 also prints two grey paragraphs under its pager — *"a list that answered
only activated: yes or no would call that whole building unfinished or finished,
and both would be wrong"* and *"The From request column is the spine"*. **Those
are RATIONALE, which rule 33 puts at ZERO words on screen.** They are not
shortened, they are removed, and the drawing's argument reaches the product the
way it was always meant to: as the `Partly activated` state and as the **FROM
REQUEST column, now visible by default** instead of declared and off. A test
asserts both sentences are ABSENT, so a later lane "completing" the screen by
pasting them in goes red. **This is rule 41's named case — a drawing that
contradicts a signed rule — and it is reported rather than taken silently.**

### THE ROW'S OWN DOOR

The only way into a build was an eye icon at the far right of a nine-column row.
**The connection number is a link now**, to the same destination, decided by the
same function (`buildHomePath`). The eye stays — it is B14 rule 15's row action.
Rule 31 holds: the visible value is `CON-26-0130`, never the row id. At 1280 the
table scrolls inside its own container to reach the eye, and the number does not
— which is the point.

### WHAT WAS FOUND AND NOT FIXED, EACH WITH ITS REASON

* **`DEF-MET-5430` — three cases in `test_w6_connection_list.py` have been red
  since 2026-09-13 and nobody read them.** They still assert the list opens on
  target date, soonest first, which `BR-CUS-1046` superseded. Measured at the
  pinned tip `894a0896` with nothing modified: **3 failed, 20 deselected.**
  Correcting them means re-deriving `DRAWN_ROWS`' expected order, which is B18
  fixture work and not this wave.
* **The KPI tiles read `OPEN · WAITING ON INSPECTION · PARTLY ACTIVATED · UNITS
  AWAITING ACTIVATION · OLDEST`; p094 draws `OPEN BUILDS · PARTLY ACTIVATED ·
  UNITS AWAITING · WAITING ON INSPECTION · OLDEST OPEN`** — different words and
  a different order. Pre-existing, and the tiles are not what the PO asked about.
* **Three column headers differ from the drawing**: `CONNECTION` for `CONNECTION
  #`, `ORDERS` for `WORK ORDERS`, `TARGET` for `TARGET ACTIVATION`. Each is a
  catalogue key in eleven languages and none was raised.
* **`⇩ Export` is drawn and absent** — `POST /exports` registers no
  `connections` resource; tracked as `DEF-1005` since 2026-08-27.

### `DEF-GOV-5433` — THE SHARED SCRATCHPAD IS A SHARED FILE

Two lanes wrote `scratchpad/msg1.txt`. The sibling's write landed at 03:41:27
and this lane's `push_paths.sh` read the file at 03:42:15, so `acff5d07` carries
the New connects toolbar under the title *"Approving a move-in now raises a
pending job on the Move-ins tab"*. **No code was lost in either direction** —
every change is on the tip, verified marker by marker, and the move-in lane's
own code is in `80bb7f6c`. What was lost is the record.

**Every post-push check in law 11 passed**, and for the reason that law keeps
teaching: they all read the commit's CONTENT, and the content was right. None of
them reads a commit's own message against what the commit does. `push_paths.sh`
could hash the message file and re-read it immediately before `commit-tree` —
the same staleness check it already runs on every named path, applied to the one
input it currently trusts.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT: THE ORDER THE COMMIT CREATES THINGS IN, AND THREE COLLISIONS THIS RULING CREATES

Closing the step-by-step walk, the PO ruled on what the final button does.
Verbatim:

> *"in this step first premises are created, then units are created, then assets
> are created, then master account is created , then Customer ID is created or
> mapped if it is existing one; itms 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 not rrequired"*

### THE ORDER, AND WHAT IS NEW IN IT

| # | Act | Today |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The premises is created** | ⚠ **not done by the commit at all.** `commit_connection` receives `premises: {id: null, …}` and its own comment says the address *"is created at step 1–2 by `create_connection`"*. The wizard writes nothing until the last button, so on this path the premise arrives by another door or not at all |
| 2 | Units are created | ✅ built, and it is the commit's first act today |
| 3 | Assets (a meter per service point) | ✅ built, through the assets seam |
| 4 | The master account is created | ⚠ built and **refused** — the wizard's owner block and the account door use different field names, so the owner's NAME never arrives (`DEF-MET-5093`) |
| 5 | **The customer id is created OR MAPPED if it already exists** | ⚠ **the mapping half does not exist.** The wizard always creates; nothing looks for a customer already on file |

⚠ **THE PLAN ASSIGNMENT IS NOT IN THE PO'S LIST AND IS IN THE CODE, BETWEEN 3 AND
4.** `commit_connection`'s own docstring says the ordering *"was discovered by
building it rather than by reading the screen"*: plans are assigned **before**
the owner's account, because `create_master_account` creates the account ACTIVE
and an active account on an unpriced unit is an invoice waiting to be wrong.
**A lane reimplementing the list above in the order given would move the plan
assignment after the account and reintroduce that.** Recorded here because the
reason is not visible from the screen and was learnt the expensive way once.

⚠ **AND "MAPPED IF IT IS EXISTING ONE" IS A RULING WE ALREADY HAVE, FROM ANOTHER
DOCUMENT.** 2026-09-12, item 5 of the Accounts-blueprint rulings: *"the system
should flag if the details were already attached to any of the accounts in the
system and should show the details of the customer account with the proper
customer details. This is very important scenario."* Same requirement, different
wizard. It is one behaviour and should be built once.

### THE THREE COLLISIONS, NAMED RATHER THAN RESOLVED

*"items 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 not required"* refers to the numbered table the
PO was reading. Taken literally it collides three ways, and CLAUDE.md law 13 is
explicit that a supersession must be **stated, never assumed** — so none of these
is decided here.

1. **Items 7 and 8 are the AUDIT ROWS, and hard rule 7 is signed law:** *every
   money action writes `audit_log`*. The commit stamps `connection.submitted` and
   writes a `connection.committed` row carrying all seven counts. Both are built,
   both work, and removing them is not a scope cut — it is a change to a hard
   rule, which needs its supersession written down. **They stay until it is.**
2. **Item 10 is the WORK ORDERS, and the PO required them at step 5 the same
   day:** *"show work order already selected from allow user to add few more work
   order"*. A clerk who picks orders and sees none raised is the exact failure
   `DEF-MET-5428` already describes. Read as *not required in this wave* rather
   than *never* — but the ADD control must then not ship either, or the wizard
   collects a deliberate choice and discards it.
3. **Item 11 is *Build confirmed*, which the PO required at step 7 the same
   day:** *"we have to do the communication with owner that request is
   created"*. It is the first of the three defaults ruled minutes earlier.

**Items 5, 6, 9 and 12 carry no such collision.** Item 5 (the quote, recorded and
posted nowhere) is superseded by the step-6 ruling, which requires the money path
rather than dropping it. Item 6 (sub-meter links) is already an honest stated
absence. Item 9 (the state recompute) is a cache refresh with no observable
alternative — a build with a stale state would show under the wrong segment of
the New connects tab. Item 12 (*Unit energised*) fires on a state change and is
not a creation act at all.

**What goes back to the PO, in plain English and without ids:** whether the build
should still write its audit trail, whether the work orders a clerk picks should
still be raised, and whether the owner should still be told the build exists —
because all three were required by them today and this ruling reads as removing
them.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT STEP 3: THE UNITS TABLE ARRIVES FILLED IN

The PO confirmed the step 3 measurement again, and added one instruction:

> *"please provide default values to Table · Unit · Kind, Table · Occupancy"*

**The table is not a blank grid the clerk fills; every row arrives with an answer
already in it.** Three columns, three defaults, and two of the three are values
this repo has already signed.

| Column | Default | Where the default comes from |
|---|---|---|
| **Unit** | the generated label — `<Prefix> 1`, `<Prefix> 2` … and `CA` for the common area | the pattern on this step plus the Prefix, which moves to step 1 in the same wave. With no prefix the label is the bare number, which is what the blueprint draws (`1`, `2`, `CA`) |
| **Kind** | `Dwelling` on every numbered row · `Common area` on the CA row | derived today from `isCommonArea` and never shown as a changeable default; the blueprint draws exactly these two words |
| **Occupancy** | **`Vacant · service off, billing nobody`** · `—` on the common-area row | `OCCUPANCY_DEFAULT` already, and its own copy says *"The default. Nothing is billed on a unit until somebody moves in."* The blueprint draws `Vacant` on the dwellings and `—` on the common area |

### THE REAL CHANGE IS THAT OCCUPANCY BECOMES PER UNIT

Today occupancy is **one choice for the whole build**, asked on the review step
as a four-way: *vacant · service off* · *vacant · base charges only* ·
*landlord-billed between tenants* · *open an account now*. The blueprint draws it
as a **column on the units table**, and the PO has now asked for a default in
that column — which only means anything if the column exists.

So this step gains the column, each row defaulted, and the review step's single
choice becomes the thing that SETS them all rather than a separate answer. **A
build where unit 4 already has a tenant moving in and the other five do not is
the case that cannot be expressed today**, and it is an ordinary one.

⚠ **THE DEFAULT IS NOT A NEW DECISION AND MUST NOT BE RE-ASKED.** `BR-MET-116`,
PO 2026-08-25, closing `OQ-373`: *"unit will be all vacant right now, if there is
common area you can add that in premises"*. That is why `commit_connection` can
create the owner's master account at all — at confirm **no unit is occupied**, so
`BR-CUS-017`'s one-occupying-account guard cannot bite. **A per-unit occupancy
that defaults to anything other than vacant would put that guard back in play on
the commit path**, and the reason is two modules away from the screen.

⚠ **`open_account_now` IS THE ONE VALUE WITH A CONSEQUENCE ON THIS SCREEN.** Its
own copy says it *"Creates an account per unit immediately"*. As a whole-build
choice it is rare and deliberate; as a per-row default it would open six accounts
on an empty building. It stays selectable and it is never a default.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT STEP 4: THE GRID CARRIES THE ASSET, NOT A TICK

The largest of the day's rulings, and it changes what step 4 IS. PO, verbatim:

> *"bascailly we are saying how many units to be build, utility services, plans
> are already confirm , how many meters , meter sizes to be build - you will ahve
> to ass meter size, or asset sizes, so you will hae t allow utility service,
> asset type its size, install date, work order here, i can raise solar or meter
> or cart - we ahve 11 services, but based on what utility servcies we ahve
> selected at premises level - accrdongly we wil have to choose plus any other
> imprtant details that we need to ap for units"*

### WHAT A ROW IS NOW

One row per **unit × service**, which is what the back end already stores — the
blueprint says so on p088: *"One row per unit per service is what the product
stores, each with its own state and its own activation date."* The cell stops
being a tick and the row carries:

| Column | Source | Exists? |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | the pattern on step 3 | ✅ |
| Utility service | **only those chosen at premise level**, out of the eleven | ✅ |
| **Asset type** | `asset_types` — 13 rows, platform-seeded | ✅ catalogue exists |
| **Size** | `RATIFIED_SERVICE_SIZE_CLASSES` — **all eleven services have ratified classes** | ✅ |
| **Install date** | new on this screen | ❌ not collected |
| **Work order** | raised for this asset | ❌ and see below |

**The PO's three examples are three real catalogue rows**: *"i can raise solar or
meter or cart"* → `pv` (PV / solar), `meter`, `container_cart` (Container / Cart).
Nothing here needs inventing; it needs wiring.

### WHAT THE COMMIT SENDS TODAY, AND IT IS THIN

`commitPlanOf` emits `meters.push({unit_label, service, asset_no: null})` — a
unit, a service and a **null asset number**. No type, no size, no install date.
The asset number is deliberately null (*"a meter serial invented here would be a
meter serial nobody has"*) and that stays true; type, size and install date are
choices a clerk can actually make and are simply not asked.

### THE ONE THING THAT DOES NOT EXIST: WHICH ASSET TYPES A SERVICE OFFERS

There is **no service → asset-type mapping anywhere in the repo**. `asset_types`
carries a `category` (`meters` · `sub_meters` · `behind_the_meter`) and that is
the S49 tab partition, not a service filter. So *"accrdongly we wil have to
choose"* has nothing to drive it.

**Judgment made rather than asked**, from the catalogue's own names, recorded so
it can be overturned against a row instead of rediscovered:

| Service | Offered |
|---|---|
| electric | meter · net meter · sub-meter · battery · EV charger · PV · transformer · generator |
| water | meter · sub-meter · backflow preventer |
| gas · thermal/heat | meter · sub-meter |
| sewer | meter · sub-meter — commonly none, since sewer is usually billed off water |
| trash | container / cart |
| storm water | commonly none — it is area-based, not measured |
| solar | PV · net meter · battery |
| broadband | modem / CPE |
| battery | battery · net meter |
| **fire** | ⚠ **NOT DECIDED HERE — it is already an open question** |

⚠ **FIRE IS LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE.** CLAUDE.md records that `OQ-1361` is HALF
answered — the hydrant is an asset, and **the fire-LINE asset type is still
`BR-AST-042`'s question**. `fire_line` exists in the catalogue; whether it is
what a fire service point takes is the open half. Deciding it here would answer a
question the PO has not been asked, which the prime directive forbids.

### TWO HAZARDS THIS RULING WALKS INTO

⚠ **"WORK ORDER HERE" MEETS A COMMIT THAT DROPS WORK ORDERS.** `DEF-MET-5428` is
open and high: the wizard already sends its chosen orders and `commit_connection`
never reads them, so a clerk promised *"nine orders will be written"* gets none.
**Raising an order per asset from this grid multiplies that silent loss by every
row.** The grid's work-order column must not ship before the commit reads the
list — a lane is fixing that side now.

⚠ **AND THE SERVICE LIST IS THE THIRD HAND-TYPED COPY WAITING TO HAPPEN.** The
front end types the eleven services out by hand in `SignupWizard.tsx` and
`ratingShared.tsx`, which is why `fire` — the eleventh — never appeared on the
sign-up screen while the row existed, the API served it, `tsc` passed and every
test passed. A grid that hardcodes its columns is that defect a third time, on a
screen where the missing service would mean a meter nobody fits.

## 2026-09-16 · THE CONNECT WIZARD'S COMMIT: THREE JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT COVER

`DEF-MET-5428` and `DEF-MET-5093` half (a), built in `commit_connection` and
`create_owner_account` (`06-backend/apps/metering/connections.py`). Each of the
three below was DECIDED rather than put to the PO, per hard-won law 13 — none
collides with a signed rule, none moves a ❄️ FROZEN figure, and none is a fact
only the PO holds. Recorded here with its worked case so it can be overturned
against a number instead of rediscovered.

### 1 · A TEMPLATE REPUBLISHED MID-WIZARD: RAISE FROM WHAT WAS COPIED, AND SAY SO

Step 6 proposes work orders from published templates and the payload carries
`{template_id, template_version}` for each. **The version the browser holds can
be stale by the time step 9 is pressed** — two clerks, one afternoon, one
republish. Three ways out, and the rules name none of them:

* stamp the number the payload sent — **rejected.** `order_copies` takes its
  copies from the template's rows AT THE RAISE, so the order would say `v1`
  over a checklist copied from `v2`. That is `BR-WRK-008` broken by a VALUE
  instead of by a join, which is the exact failure `create_work_order` already
  refuses a DRAFT template to avoid;
* refuse the whole commit — **rejected.** `BR-MET-112` is both or neither, so a
  developer's 26-unit build would be lost to somebody editing a checklist;
* **CHOSEN: raise from the version actually copied, and report the divergence.**

**Worked:** a *Backflow test* template is proposed at **version 1**; it is
published again before the clerk presses **Create connection ✓**. The order is
written stamped **version 2** — the version its six copies came from — the build
completes, and the commit returns an `unavailable` row
`template_republished_since_proposal` naming the template, `proposed_version 1`
and `raised_version 2`. The manifest still reports the order. Nothing is
silently different; the screen is told.

### 2 · THE OWNER'S PHONE IS AN IDENTITY CLAIM, FOR A PERSON ONLY

`BR-CUS-1024` refuses an account for a party nobody can identify, and
`BR-CUS-1023`'s creation minimum accepts, for a **person**, an SSN **or** a
driving licence **or** a **phone** — and for a **company**, its Tax ID alone.
**Step 1 of the connect wizard has collected a phone all along**, as a contact
detail.

**Decided: that phone travels into `customer.identity.phone`.** It is the
owner's own number, not a borrowed field, and it is the difference between a
door that opens and a door that refuses a clerk who has typed everything the
screen asked for.

**Worked, both sides:**

* *Marisol Ibarra*, landlord, phone `555-0182`, no other identifier → **the
  master account opens** and `connections.owner_account_id` is set.
* *Brazos Bend Developments LLC*, builder/developer, the **same** phone and no
  Tax ID → **still refused**, because a phone does not mint a number for a
  company.

⚠ **It changes nothing about REUSING a number already on file.** `BR-CUS-1024`'s
matching test is a name plus a GOVERNMENT-grade identifier, and a phone is not
one — the repo says so in four places. A phone MINTS and may not MATCH, and that
asymmetry is untouched.

### 3 · THE OWNER'S CLASSIFICATION IS NOT THE PARTY KIND, AND IS NOT DERIVED FROM IT

`DEF-MET-5093`'s own prescription said *"`kind` → `customer.kind`"*. **That
mapping is wrong and would have failed on every value.** `OWNER_KINDS` is a
CLASSIFICATION — *builder or developer · property owner · landlord · occupier* —
and `customer.kind` is `person` or `company`. **All FOUR classifications are
refused by `customers._validate_customer_kind`**, so the mapping would have
traded a missing-kind refusal for an unknown-lookup one: the same closed door
with a worse sentence on it.

Deriving *company* from *builder or developer* was rejected outright.
`BR-MET-112` is that a wizard does not mint a money object because a field was
filled in, and `identity_match.normalise_kind` already **refuses to pick** a
kind for a sole trader for exactly this reason — *"choosing here would resolve
an open question by writing a value into a customer's row"*. A landlord is
routinely a person and routinely a company; nothing on step 1 says which.

**So the party kind is a NEW FIELD, asked by name.** The payload carries
`owner.party_kind` (`person` | `company`) and `owner.identity`, the server reads
both, and the classification is mapped nowhere. **The PO confirmed on 2026-09-16
that the owner's identifier belongs on step 1** — shown a table listing it as
*"nowhere / Not built / Door refuses without it"*, they replied *"this is
correct"*. Filed as `DEF-MET-5438`, because the register row that prescribed the
wrong mapping is what a later lane would have read.

⚠ **The identity block travels ONLY when a party kind is stated**, which is
`BR-CUS-1022` rather than caution: evidence presented against an unstated kind
*cannot be assessed at all*. Sending it regardless would turn one refusal that
names the missing dropdown into a field error about the evidence — two sentences
where a clerk needs one.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT: THE CUSTOMER SEARCH, THE PREMISES NAME, THE CHARGE CATEGORIES, AND THE DEFAULT STATUSES

The PO confirmed all eight steps and the commit order, and added four things.

### 1 · STEP 1 MUST SEARCH FOR THE CUSTOMER

> *"how you will search Customer ID here if foudn what and if not found then what
> - you will ahve to add this here"*

**This is the same requirement as the 2026-09-12 Accounts ruling, arriving on a
second wizard:** *"the system should flag if the details were already attached to
any of the accounts in the system and should show the details of the customer
account with the proper customer details. This is very important scenario."*
**One behaviour, built once**, and it closes the *"created OR MAPPED if it is
existing one"* half of the commit-order ruling, which has no implementation at
all today — this wizard always creates.

### 2 · STEP 2 TAKES THE PREMISES NAME

> *"also take premises name here"*

⚠ **THE COLUMN ALREADY EXISTS AND IS SIMPLY NOT ASKED.** `premises.name`, B2
base, nullable. So do **three** of this wizard's gaps: `premises.external_ref`
is the external system reference the PO moved to step 1, and
`premises.services_available` is where step 2's new multi-select belongs.
**Nothing here needs a migration.**

### 3 · STEP 6 — THE CHARGE CATEGORIES AND THE DEPOSIT PAYER

> *"you will select connection fees, deposites, work order fees, based on plan
> you will devicde how many charges to calculate for this premises - charges will
> be per unit - we will ahve to allow whether deposite will be given by owner or
> it should be charge to person who move in in to this units. if it is owner and
> we charge all, if it is occupant then we dont charge"*

**Three categories:** connection fees · **deposits** · work order fees. **The
plan decides how many of each** and **the charges are per unit**, which matches
the blueprint's own note that *"every quantity is counted from the services grid,
not typed"*.

**The deposit payer is a two-way choice with a consequence, not a preference:**

| Chosen | What happens at commit |
|---|---|
| **The owner** | every unit's deposit is charged now, to the owner's account |
| **The occupant** | **nothing is charged now** — the deposit is taken from whoever moves in, at move-in |

⚠ **A DEPOSIT AGAINST A QUOTE IS NOT A DEPOSIT AGAINST AN ACCOUNT, AND THE
DRAWING SAYS SO ON THIS PAGE:** *"This money settles one-time charges on a build;
it is not the security deposit a tenant pays when they move in, and the two never
meet."* The ruling above is about the SECURITY deposit and therefore crosses that
line deliberately — **the owner option makes the build charge a tenant deposit
per unit up front**, which is a new money path, not a rename of the existing one.
The move-in wizard already has a deposit step (`BR-SHL-046` era); **the occupant
option is that step doing its existing job and must not duplicate it.**

### 4 · THE COMMIT CREATES THE REQUEST ROW FIRST, AND SENDS THE MESSAGES

> *"you will also have to create thsi new request in table first; send
> communcaition"*

So the order is: **the request row · the premises · the units · the assets ·
(the plan) · the master account · the customer, created or matched · then the
messages go out.**

### THE DEFAULT STATUSES, MEASURED RATHER THAN RECALLED

| Object | What it is created as TODAY | Vocabulary |
|---|---|---|
| **Connection / request** | `draft`, then the commit stamps `submitted_at` | draft · requested · in progress · partly activated · on hold · activated · cancelled |
| **Premises** | **`active`** | draft · pending · active · inactive |
| **Unit** | ⚠ **no status column, and no occupancy column either** | — `BR-MET-036`: both are DERIVED from the active account |
| **Asset** | ⚠ **`active` — "Installed"** — `stage_code = "active" if unit_id else "inventory"` | Inventory · Installed · Needs repair · In repair · Retired |
| **Master account** | **`active`** (`BR-CUS-068`) | Pending activation · Active · Marked disconnect · Vacation hold · Closed · Disconnected |
| **Customer** | created with the account | — |

⚠ **THREE OF THESE LOOK WRONG FOR A BUILD AND ARE NOT MINE TO CHANGE.**

1. **An asset is `Installed` the instant it is created against a unit.** On a new
   connect **nothing has been fitted** — fitting it is what the work orders are
   for, and the review step's own words are *"it opens no accounts, sends
   nothing, and energises nothing"*. `Inventory` exists and means exactly
   *"available, not in service"*. A meter marked Installed before anyone visits
   is a reading route with 20 meters nobody can read.
2. **The premises is `active`** on a property that is a hole in the ground.
   `draft` and `pending` are both in the vocabulary and neither is used here.
3. **The master account is `Active`** on an empty building, which is why plans
   must be assigned before it — *"an active account on an unpriced unit is an
   invoice waiting to be wrong"*. `pending_activation` exists and is
   `non_billable`.

**Each is a default with a money or field-work consequence, so each is the PO's
to rule rather than a lane's to pick.** Recorded together so they are asked once.

### AND THE UNIT-LEVEL OCCUPANCY COLUMN HAS NOWHERE TO BE STORED

⚠ **`units` HAS NO `occupancy` COLUMN AND THAT IS DELIBERATE** — `BR-MET-036`,
and `models.py`'s own module note says so: *"units.occupancy/status deliberately
absent (BR-MET-036 derived; US-MET-002 §5 display-only)"*. So the per-unit
occupancy ruled onto step 3 earlier today is an **instruction to the commit**
about which units get an account opened, **not a column to write**. A lane that
reads the ruling and reaches for a migration will be refused by the model's own
docstring, and a lane that adds the column anyway breaks the derivation every
other screen reads.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT STEP 1 IS BUILT AS DRAWN: NINE STEPS BECOME EIGHT, FOUR ELEMENTS COME HOME, AND THE RAIL FITS AT LAST (`v2.278.0`)

`DEF-CUS-5186` · `DEF-CUS-5198` · `DEF-CUS-5435` · `DEF-CUS-5436`. Built from
pages 86 and 87 of `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` **rendered as
images and looked at** (B14 rule 42), never from the extracted text.

**This closes a ruling the PO had to make twice** — 2026-09-12, *"merge the
first and second step"*, and 2026-09-16, *"please biring them on step 1 if
darwing is aksing it … it shoyld be as per drawing from document"*. The drawing
has said eight since it was drawn, and argues the merge in its own words:
*"Two steps, merged, because they are one question. Who is asking and what they
are building were never separable."*

### 1 · What a clerk can do now that they could not

The whole of step 1 is on one page: who the owner is, what is being built, how
the work is done, what the units will be called, and the owner's id in whatever
system the utility ran before. **Two fields had no page at all** — the external
system reference, and the prefix, which was asked three screens later on the
step that counts units rather than the step that names the build.

### 2 · The rail measurement, and it is the part that was assumed

`DEF-CUS-5198` was filed as *"244px outside the rail at 1280 and 84px at 1440"*.
Re-measured in a browser at `v2.277.0`, before any change:

| width | cells | content | box | hanging outside |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1280 | 9 | 1236px | 992px | **244px** |
| 1440 | 9 | 1236px | 1152px | **84px** |

**The merge alone did not fix it, and this is why the number was measured rather
than assumed.** Eight cells at 1280 still needed 1113px in a 992px box —
**121px outside**, half the fault and not none. 1440 fitted exactly.

The cause is one missing token: a flex item's `min-width` is `auto`, so a rail
cell **refuses to shrink below its own label** and the row overflows instead of
wrapping. `min-w-0` on `WIZ.step` lets the label wrap, which is what the
blueprint draws — p086 sets *Plans & work orders* on three lines and splits
*Communication*. After it, every rail reports `scrollWidth == clientWidth`:

| width | new connect | move-in | move-out | transfer | disconnect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1280 | 992/992 ✅ | 960/960 | 960/960 | 992/992 | 992/992 |
| 1440 | 1152/1152 ✅ | 1120/1120 | 1120/1120 | 1152/1152 | 1152/1152 |

**The other four wizards are pixel-identical before and after** — same
scrollWidth, same clientWidth, same rail height — because a rail that already
fits has no shrink pressure and nothing to shrink. That is the blast-radius
check for a change to a component all five share, and it was measured in a
browser rather than reasoned about, because **jsdom computes no layout: every
element is 0×0 there, so the vitest suite that renders this rail could never
have seen this defect in either direction** (hard-won law 6).

### 3 · Three judgments made rather than asked

**(a) The drawn warning is two sentences, not the one drawn.** p087 prints
*"This build has no home yet — the premise arrives on the next step"*, thirteen
words in one sentence. B14 rule 33 caps a FACT at six words and an INSTRUCTION
at six PER SENTENCE, and says in terms that *two sentences of six beat one
sentence of twelve*, because the second sentence is where *what to do next*
lives. Built as **"This build has no home yet. The premise arrives next step."**
— 6 words and 5. Both halves survive; neither breaches the cap.

**(b) Two drawn section headings were shortened and three help sentences were
removed outright.** *"What is being built"* (4) → **What is built**;
*"How is the work being done?"* (6, and a sentence) → **How it's done**. Rule 33
caps a heading at three words, and the precedent is one day old and in this same
log: the bill-run lane shortened *"THE BILLS IN THIS PERIOD"* → *Bills this
period* on the same rule. The three help sentences were RATIONALE — *why* the
owner becomes billable, *why* the sub-lines are definitions, *why* mode can
change later — which rule 33 gives **zero words on screen**. ⚠ **Rationale is
REMOVED, not shortened**: cutting a *why* sentence to six words keeps the breach
and makes it terser. All three are in `OwnerScopeStep`'s own comment. The
blueprint draws no help text inside this form either — the grey prose beside it
on p086–p087 is the document talking to a reader, not the screen talking to a
clerk.

**(c) The page H1 keeps the drawn sentence and is longer than three words.**
*"Who is asking, and what for?"* is six. Rule 41 says the product UI matches the
blueprint, and **every one of this flow's eight drawn H1s is a question or a
phrase**, so reading rule 33's heading cap onto the page title would discard all
eight. The cap is applied to the section headings and labels below it, where it
is obeyed.

### 4 · What the server does and does not read, stated rather than implied

`scope`, `units_prefix` and the owner's `external_ref` now travel in
`CommitPlan`. **Nothing reads any of them, and that is a property of the DOOR
rather than of these three fields:** `POST /connections/commit` with no id — the
wizard's own commit, because `BR-MET-112` means no connection row exists before
the last step — is still unserved, so no member of that payload is read today.
Measured on the tree: `connections` has **no column** for a scope or a unit
prefix; `customers.external_ref` **does** exist, nullable and unique per tenant,
described in the model as *"the LEGACY system's identifier"*, and is the home
the external reference is written for.

⚠ **The prefix's EFFECT already travelled and its VALUE did not.**
`expandUnitPattern` builds `Apt 1 … Apt 26`, so `units[].label` carries the
prefix twenty-six times over and a committed build holds no record of what it
WAS. Sending it once means a unit added to the same building next year can be
named the same way without a person re-reading a label and guessing.

### 5 · A test had been red for three days and three lanes ran past it

`DEF-CUS-5436`. `NewConnectWizard.test.tsx` asserted the lowercase, mid-sentence
form of a string that commit `c107eaae` **split in two and capitalised on
2026-09-13**. `toContain` is case-sensitive, so it has failed on every run since
— measured at the tip `6d060621` in a clean worktree: 1 failed, 18 passed.
**Nothing forced anyone to read it**: the failure names a SENTENCE rather than a
behaviour, so it reads like copy drift rather than a broken guard, and it sat
inside a suite that is red in 23 places for other reasons. That is hard-won law
7's *proved red, then never read* in its ordinary clothes.

**How the 23 were separated from the one that was mine**, since "was this red
before I started" is a claim about history: the customers suite was run at the
tip in a `git worktree` and diffed against the same suite on this tree. Tip:
**23 failed, 1041 passed**. Here: **23 failed, 1052 passed** — the same 23 files
and names, minus the one above that is now fixed, plus exactly one the merge
broke and this commit repairs (`parkedDrafts.dom.test.tsx` asserted a new
connect counts against **nine**).

### 6 · What a parked draft does, because the merge moved every step number

A new-connect draft parked BEFORE this commit stored a nine-step number, and
nothing versions it. The waiting list therefore prints its `Step N of 8` **one
step late** for those rows, and the clamp keeps an old step 9 honest as
`Step 8 of 8`. **It is a label, not a destination**: `resumePath` carries
`?parked=<id>` and no `?step=`, so a resumed draft reopens at step 1 with
everything typed hydrated whole. Nothing is lost and no migration is owed.

### 7 · One thing deliberately not built

⛔ The drawn **Owner's identifier (Tax ID / SSN)** is a hole in `OwnerScopeStep`
with a comment where it goes. `create_owner_account` refuses the master-account
door without one (`BR-CUS-1024`, PO 2026-09-01) and `DEF-MET-5093` is that
mapping, owned by another lane. A half-built identifier field would be worse
than none: it would look like the thing that unblocks the door and would not.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT: THE DEFAULT STATUSES ARE RULED, AND THE COMMIT GAINS FOUR ACTS

The PO answered the three status questions and added to the commit. Verbatim,
in the order given:

> *"it means you will ahve unit, utility service, asset type, Size,
> installatiion date, work order, occupany - default - also all these values
> shoudl come as default"* · *"this is pending"* (the premises) · *"based on
> premises pending assign some default staus to units"* · *"assets are not yet
> installed - we need differnt status here"* · *"account is not yet actiavted"* ·
> *"plus crte all work orders"* · *"yes we need this"* (service points, service
> agreements, the premise's service list) · *"new service fees ; applcition fees
> not requried"*

### THE THREE STATUS RULINGS

| Object | Was | **Ruled** |
|---|---|---|
| **Premises** | `active` | **`pending`** — the vocabulary already holds it |
| **Asset** | `active` / Installed | **not installed** — see the caveat below |
| **Master account** | `active` | **not activated** → `pending_activation`, which is `non_billable` |

⚠ **THE ACCOUNT RULING REMOVES THE REASON FOR AN ORDERING NOBODY SHOULD NOW
UNDO.** `commit_connection` assigns plans **before** the account because
`create_master_account` opened it ACTIVE and *"an active account on an unpriced
unit is an invoice waiting to be wrong"*. A `pending_activation` account is
`non_billable`, so that hazard is gone — **but the ordering stays**, because it
costs nothing and the next person to reverse it will not know why it was there.

⚠ **AND THE ASSET RULING MAY NEED A VALUE THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** The five seeded
statuses are `inventory` (Inventory, *available*) · `active` (Installed) ·
`needs_repair` · `in_repair` · `retired`. **`inventory` is the only one that
means "not in service" and it is the right answer if "on the shelf" is close
enough.** If the PO means a distinct *awaiting installation on a known unit*,
that is a **new lookup row**, not a default change — and lookup values are
platform-seeded reference data (`BR-AST-031`), so adding one is a change to what
every tenant receives. Recorded as the fork rather than resolved.

⚠ **THE ASSET DOOR REFUSES WITHOUT AN INSTALL DATE WHEN A UNIT IS NAMED, AND THE
BUILD ALWAYS NAMES ONE** (`DEF-AST-5443`). So a build commits **50 meters as
Installed, on a date, before anyone has visited**. The rule is right for its own
door — a clerk assigning an existing meter IS installing it — and the fault is
that a BUILD borrows that door. **Changing the default is not enough; the date
requirement has to move with it**, or the build supplies an installation date
for equipment nobody has fitted.

### THE UNIT STATUS COLLIDES WITH A SIGNED DESIGN RULE

> *"based on premises pending assign some default staus to units"*

⚠ **`units` HAS NO STATUS COLUMN AND NO OCCUPANCY COLUMN, DELIBERATELY.**
`BR-MET-036` and `models.py`'s own note: *"units.occupancy/status deliberately
absent (BR-MET-036 derived; US-MET-002 §5 display-only)"*. A unit's status is
COMPUTED from its account.

**Two readings, and the difference is a migration:**

* **(a) The derivation answers it.** With the premises `pending` and no account
  on any unit, the computed status reads *not in service* on every unit — which
  is a default status, arrived at without storing one. **Costs nothing and
  breaks nothing.**
* **(b) A stored column.** Every screen that reads the derivation would have two
  sources that can disagree, which is the fault `BR-MET-036` exists to prevent.

**Reading (a) is taken** and is flagged here so the PO can overturn it against a
row. Nobody adds the column without that ruling.

### THE COMMIT GAINS FOUR ACTS

> *"plus crte all work orders"* and *"yes we need this"*

1. **All the work orders are raised.** This settles the earlier *"items … 10 …
   not required"*: they ARE required. The commit already reads them as of today
   (`DEF-MET-5428` closed — two templates named, two rows written).
2. **Service points** — one per unit per service, the thing a meter hangs off.
   **Unverified: I could not confirm the commit creates them** and it must be
   measured before it is built on.
3. **Service agreements** — how a master account covers its units
   (`BR-CUS-068`). Without them the account exists and covers nothing.
4. **The premise's service list** — `premises.services_available`, the column
   step 2's multi-select belongs in. Without it a premise does not know what it
   offers.

### THE FEE ACCOUNT, AND WHAT "NOT REQUIRED" MEANS

> *"new service fees ; applcition fees not requried"*

**Read as two statements.** The revenue account is confirmed: one-time build
charges earn into **4600 Connection & new-service fees**. And **the application
fee is not part of a new connect's charges** — step 6 takes connection fees,
deposits and work-order fees, and the `$25.00` application fee belongs to the
service REQUEST, which is where it is already collected and earned.

⚠ **THIS IS NOT READ AS RETIRING THE APPLICATION FEE.** `CC-REQFEE` was seeded
at `$25.00` against `4600` on 2026-09-16 and its counter path is proved end to
end (`DR 1010 Undeposited funds / CR 2400 Customer credit balances`, then on
approval `DR 2400 / CR 4600`). Retiring it would contradict the PO's own ruling
that the fee is non-refundable and stays in the books on a refusal. **Stated
because the sentence admits both readings and only one of them is cheap to
reverse.**

### STILL UNANSWERED AFTER THIS EXCHANGE

**The audit trail** — whether the build still writes it — and **the contract**.
Both were put and neither was answered, so both stay open.
