## 2026-09-16 — THE CONTRACT IS A TEMPLATE, THE AUDIT TRAIL STAYS, AND THE BUILD STARTS

Two answers, both given in one line, and both closing something that was
genuinely blocking.

### THE CONTRACT — `OQ-MET-12360` CLOSED THE DAY IT WAS MINTED

> *"using existing template and notification"*

**The contract is a document we render and send** — one more template in the
utility's own library, merged against the build and queued through the same
notification path as every other letter. **It is not an agreement signed and
returned.** So nothing waits for it to come back, no file is stored, and **no
gate stands in front of energising a build**.

That was the whole of the question: the three things utilities call a contract
cost days, weeks and nothing, and the cheap one LOOKS finished whichever they
meant. A lane that had guessed "template" would have shipped something that
passed every check while a utility legally required to hold a signed copy found
out at go-live.

It needs **a template row and a merge, and no schema at all.** Everything on
step 7 remains queued and unsent — this product writes a row per message and no
sender picks it up.

⚠ **A SIGNED COPY LATER IS A NEW RULING, NOT AN EXTENSION OF THIS ONE.** It would
add stored files, a state on the connection, and a decision about whether an
unsigned contract stops a build energising — the last of which is a field-work
gate rather than a screen change.

### THE AUDIT TRAIL STAYS

> *"yes i already agreed with this"*

**The build goes on writing `audit_log`.** This closes the first of the three
collisions raised when *"items 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 not required"* was read
literally: items 7 and 8 are the audit rows, and hard rule 7 — *every money
action writes `audit_log`* — is signed law. The PO has confirmed the safe
default rather than superseding the rule, so **nothing about the audit path
changes and no supersession is recorded**, which is the right outcome: a hard
rule should be hard to move by accident.

**The other two collisions were already settled the same day and in the
opposite direction from the literal reading:** all the work orders ARE raised
(*"plus crte all work orders"*), and the owner IS told the build exists (it is
the first of step 7's three messages).

### AND THE BUILD IS AUTHORISED

> *"start waves"*

Ten lanes over three waves, as put to the PO in plain English with the blueprint
pages each one reads. **Wave 0 is one lane and it is alone on purpose:** the
wizard's Create-connection button posts to an address that returns 404, so no
build made through that screen has ever reached the database. Every other lane is
decorating a door that does not open.

⚠ **THE WAVE SHAPE IS A FILE-COLLISION CONSTRAINT, NOT A PREFERENCE.** The wizard
is one file, and two lanes in one file is how work gets reverted by subtraction
in this tree — it has happened eight times and twice today. So wave 1 carries a
lane that does nothing but **split the wizard into one file per step**, and that
mechanical change is what makes wave 2's five lanes parallel instead of a queue.

## 2026-09-16 — THE CONNECT WIZARD'S BUTTON GETS A DOOR, AND IT IS ONE DOOR (`DEF-MET-5441`)

**No ruling was sought and none was needed.** `CLAUDE.md` hard-won law 13: what
reaches the PO is a collision with a signed rule, a frozen figure, or a fact only
they hold. This is none of the three — it is a judgment the rules already point
at, so it is decided here and written down with its reasoning, which is the
deliverable.

### WHAT WAS WRONG

`POST /api/v1/connections/commit` answered **404** on the running server while
`POST /api/v1/connections` and `POST /api/v1/connections/<uuid>/commit` each
answered 401 — real doors behind a login. The wizard's **Create connection**
button posts to the 404. **So no build made through that screen had ever reached
the database**, through eight finished steps. The gap was written down twice, in
`newConnectEndpoints.ts` exception E3 and in `metering/api.py`'s own docstring,
and never once on the defect register — hard-won law 1 exactly.

### THE CHOICE, AND THE EVIDENCE FOR IT

Two shapes were open.

**(a) ONE door.** `POST /connections/commit`, no id, which creates the address
and the draft and commits the build **inside one transaction**.

**(b) TWO round trips.** The browser calls `POST /connections` first, takes the
id it is given, and then posts to the id-bearing commit.

**(a) was chosen, on three pieces of evidence rather than on taste.**

1. **`BR-MET-112` is both-or-neither** — *nothing is written until the last
   button*. Shape (b) writes a premises, a premise number, a connection and a
   `CON-` number on the FIRST call. If the second one refuses — a duplicate
   parcel, a template a clerk retired an hour ago, a plan missing on a unit — a
   Draft connection and possibly a brand-new address are left behind with no
   units, no meters and no plan. The wizard has no screen that finds them: its
   park-and-resume context is empty by design, *"a new connect has no premise id,
   no unit id and no account id until it commits"*. That is the half-built state
   the rule exists to forbid, arrived at by construction.
2. **The screen was already built to (a) and says so.** `BR-SHL-019` is *exactly
   one transactional commit*; `commitPlanOf` assembles ONE payload;
   `connection_commit`'s own docstring says *"three sequential POSTs from a
   browser would invent exactly the half-committed state the rule forbids"*.
   Shape (b) would have meant rewriting a screen to fit a signature.
3. **(a) needs no new writer at all.** `create_connection` has taken a whole
   `premises` block and created the address since `BR-MET-1024` (2026-09-01), so
   the new door calls two services that already exist, in order, and adds
   nothing. Each of them opens its own `transaction.atomic()`, which nest as
   SAVEPOINTS inside the outer one, so both-or-neither holds with no new
   transaction machinery — and a refusal anywhere rolls the address back with the
   build.

**What the door does NOT do:** it sequences and it computes nothing. Every rule
stays where it was — `create_premises` still owns the address's validation, the
premise number and the area cascade; `commit_connection` still owns the five-module
commit; the permission class is the same `AdminOrClerk` the id-bearing commit
carries, because a commit writes across five modules and is not a VIEW right.

### FOUR FIELD NAMES THE SCREEN AND THE SERVICE SPELL DIFFERENTLY

The wizard's premises block is `{id, address, premise_type, parcel_ref,
read_route}` and `_validate_premises` refuses every key it does not know by name.
The door translates, and each mapping is evidence-led:

| the screen sends | it is written to | why |
|---|---|---|
| `address` | `address_line` | the one required field on a premises (`US-MET-001` §5) |
| `premise_type` | `premises_type` | the column's name; `_resolve_premises_type` is the same resolver S16 uses |
| `parcel_ref` | `external_ref` | **this is already where a parcel key lives.** `integrations/seams/metering.py` writes `"external_ref": candidate.get("parcel")` from the City's answer and `parcel_is_taken` reads it back through `premises_external_ref_taken` (`BR-INT-048`, `DEF-INT-4273`). There is no `parcel_ref` column, and adding one would be a SECOND home for one key — the thing hard rule 8 exists to stop |
| `read_route` | `route` | the key `_resolve_create_route` reads, which takes the code or the id (`CR-089` wave B `B6`) |

`premises.id` non-null takes the other branch: the address is named, nothing is
created, and `create_connection`'s existing *named twice* refusal is untouched.

**`scope` and `units_prefix` are accepted and read by nothing, deliberately.**
`connections` has no column for either (`DEF-CUS-5435`); a door that quietly
dropped them is honest, and a door that invented a column for them would be this
lane choosing an answer nobody asked for.

### THE MANIFEST'S `premises` COUNT BECOMES ANSWERABLE

`commit_connection` reports `premises: null` with a stated absence, and
`DEF-2961`'s reasoning is why: *"the address is created at step 1–2 by
`create_connection` … the door that did it is the door that can say so."* **This
new door IS that door.** So it fills the count in — `1` when it created the
address, `0` when the clerk named one — and replaces the absence with the plain
statement of which of the two happened. `commit_connection` itself is unchanged
and still answers `null` when called on its own, which is still the truth there.

## 2026-09-16 — THE BUILD'S HEADER: `ACTIVATE` COMPLETES IT, AND A PARK BUTTON JOINS IT

The PO confirmed the header measurement and changed two of its actions.
Verbatim:

> *"but make activate unit = actiavte - it comlete this reeust ; we need park or
> hold button also."*

### WHAT CHANGES

| Drawn | **Ruled** |
|---|---|
| **Activate units** — a dialog choosing WHICH units | **Activate** — one act that **completes the build** |
| — | **Park / Hold** — a new header action the drawing does not have |

### THE MECHANISM, WHICH IS THE PART A LANE WILL GET WRONG

⚠ **`activated` IS DERIVED AND IS NEVER SET.** `refresh_connection_state` is the
only writer of `connections.state`, and it computes: every live service
activated → `ACTIVATED`; any of them activated → `PARTLY_ACTIVATED`. Today a
service reaches `SVC_ACTIVATED` when a work order's field result is **accepted**
— *"data accepted, service activated, customer told"* — and there is **no
`activate` endpoint at all**.

**So the button drives the SERVICES and lets the state recompute. It must not
write the state.** A button that stamps `activated` directly would give the
column and the derivation two authors that can disagree, which is the fault the
single-writer rule exists to prevent — and `SVC_ACTIVATED` is **terminal**
(`frozenset()`, no transition out), so a wrong one cannot be undone.

⚠ **AND THE GATE STAYS.** The drawing is explicit and it is a safety rule rather
than a screen preference: *"A work order permits energisation, and it is not the
same order for every service. Electric and water gate on the meter set; gas gates
on the light-up, not the meter set — gating gas on the meter set would energise
an account for a service nobody has lit, and bill it."* **So `Activate`
activates what CAN activate and says, per unit, why the rest cannot** — which is
exactly what the drawn dialog already does with *"No — gate not passed"* and
*"No — no meter"*. Making one button out of it changes the label and the reach,
not the refusals.

**`it comlete this reeust` is read as: Activate is the act that FINISHES a
build**, not as *activate regardless of the gate*. The opposite reading would
energise a service with no meter fitted and start billing for it.

### PARK / HOLD IS ALREADY BUILT, DOOR AND ALL

`hold_connection` and `release_connection` exist, with endpoints, and the hold
carries a **required reason** — *"an unattributed hold is half a hold"*. The
design is worth preserving in the screen: **the hold is a TIMESTAMP, not a state
token**, so lifting it returns the build to whatever its services say it is and
**clearing a hold cannot lose the progress underneath**.

⚠ **ONE HOLD PATH IS DECLARED AND NOT WIRED (hard-won law 2, and the code says
so about itself):** *"a `failed` work-order outcome must also land here (task
6.6). It is not wired from this module, and saying so is the point."* So a job
that fails in the field does **not** put the build on hold today. Worth fixing
when this screen is built, because a clerk who sees no hold assumes no problem.

⚠ **VOCABULARY — `park` AND `hold` ARE THE SAME ACT HERE AND MUST NOT BECOME TWO
WORDS.** The service request flow parks; a build holds; the stored state is
`on_hold`. B14 rule 34 exists for exactly this shape — one pair of words for one
idea, everywhere, in all eleven catalogues. **Pick one word for the button and
use it in every catalogue**; do not ship *Park* on one screen and *Hold* on
another for the same column.

### BLOCKED ON A QUESTION ALREADY PUT TO THE PO

**This header has no screen to live on.** The build detail screen was deleted on
2026-09-04 on the PO's own ruling — *"there is nothing called as conenctions;
Connection = Account only"* — and `/connections/<uuid>` now redirects to the
owner account, or the premises. So these two buttons, and the eight sections the
blueprint draws beneath them, need a home: **the account's Work tab**, which is
where that ruling points, or the connection screen returns and the September
ruling is superseded. **Put to the PO and not yet answered. No lane may guess.**

## 2026-09-16 — THE BUILD'S EIGHT SECTIONS ARE BUILT, AND THEY ARE BUILT ON THE ACCOUNT

The PO confirmed the eight-section measurement of the blueprint's build screen
and ruled, verbatim:

> *"we will ahve to buidl all screen relate ddetails"*

### WHERE IT LIVES — DECIDED, NOT ASKED AGAIN

The question *"a connection screen, or the account?"* was put to the PO and this
reply does not name a place. **It does not need to: they already ruled it**, on
2026-09-04, and re-asking would be law 13's own bug — *"i try to be consisitence
but as human i might make a mistake in my response"*.

PO, 2026-09-04, verbatim: *"you are duplicating this — there is nothing called as
conenctions; Connection = Account only - you cannot have two differnt screen -
this is an integration problem"*, scoped the same day to *"One screen too many.
The objection is the duplicate destination — **a person should reach the build's
progress, its units, its work orders and its charges from the account**, not from
a parallel screen."*

**That sentence names four of the eight sections by name.** So the eight sections
are built **on the account**, and `/connections/<uuid>` keeps redirecting there.
**The blueprint's standalone build screen is NOT resurrected** — reviving it
would supersede a ruling the PO made deliberately and would recreate the exact
duplicate they objected to.

⚠ **THIS IS A JUDGMENT AND IT IS FLAGGED AS ONE.** If the PO wants the separate
screen back, that is a supersession of 2026-09-04 and must be stated, never
assumed. Until then, a lane that builds a parallel connection page is building
the thing that was deleted.

### WHAT IS ACTUALLY OWED, SECTION BY SECTION

The measurement the PO confirmed says **the back end is largely there and the
screen is not**. Four gaps are real work rather than plumbing:

| Section | What is missing |
|---|---|
| Owner and scope | **`prefix` and `scope` are not stored anywhere.** The wizard now SENDS both; no column receives them. The prefix's *effect* survives, baked into unit names, but the word itself is lost — so a unit added to the same building next year has nothing to copy |
| Charges and money | **`Billed to` refuses** (the payer needs the identifier the wizard does not yet collect) and **`Outstanding at activation` is not computed** anywhere |
| Communication | **Nothing built.** Lane D is building the three messages; this section reads them back |
| Everything else | Built on the server, no screen |

### AND THE HEADER RULED IN THE SAME EXCHANGE GOES WITH IT

**Activate** (one act that completes the build) and **Park / Hold** (built, door
and all, with a required reason). The mechanism caveat from that row stands and
is the thing a lane will get wrong: **`activated` is DERIVED and never set**, so
the button drives the services and lets `refresh_connection_state` recompute.

### WHAT THIS SCREEN IS FOR, WHICH DECIDES WHAT GOES ON IT

`OQ-249` is still open for Work and Workflows. This screen is **not** a work
management console: it is *"where an approved build lands, and what it becomes"*
— the eight sections the wizard collected, read back, plus the two acts that move
it on. **A reference default is not permission to build the Work module**, and
the boundary is worth stating because the drawn Gate row and work-order list sit
right on it.

## 2026-09-16 — THE CONNECT WIZARD IS ONE FILE PER STEP, AND THE PROOF OF A PURE MOVE IS A DIFF THAT IS EMPTY

**Judgment, not a ruling.** Nothing was put to the PO and nothing needed to be:
no rule moved, no figure moved, no screen changed. It is recorded because the
next person to open this feature will find twelve files where there was one, and
the reason has to outlive the lane that had it.

### WHY

`NewConnectWizard.tsx` was 2,039 lines holding all eight steps, and five lanes
are queued on different steps. **In this shared tree two lanes in one file is
how work gets reverted by subtraction** — hard-won law 11 records eight
occurrences and two of them happened on 2026-09-06. A pathspec commit takes the
WHOLE working-tree content of every path it names, so the second lane to commit
silently reverts the first, with a correct file count, its own hunks present,
and nothing in the diff to notice. One file per step is not tidiness; it is the
only thing that makes five lanes at once safe.

### THE LAYOUT, AND WHY EACH PIECE IS WHERE IT IS

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `NewConnectWizard.tsx` | the orchestrator — the screen id, the eight H1s, the draft state, the queries, the park wiring, the commit, the `WizardStep[]` — **and the re-exports** |
| `newConnectDraft.ts` | the draft shape, its defaults, its derivations and the commit payload builder |
| `newConnectStepKit.tsx` | `StepIntro`, `ServiceTicks`, `ManifestRow` — the three helpers more than one step renders |
| `NewConnectOwnerStep.tsx` | step 1 · Owner & scope (`OwnerScopeStep`) |
| `NewConnectPremiseStep.tsx` | step 2 · Premise (`PremiseStep`, `PREMISE_TYPES`) |
| `NewConnectUnitsStep.tsx` | step 3 · Units (`UnitsStep`) |
| `NewConnectServicesStep.tsx` | step 4 · Map services (`ServicesStep`) |
| `NewConnectPlansStep.tsx` | step 5 · Plans & work orders (`PlansStep`) |
| `NewConnectChargesStep.tsx` | step 6 · Charges (`ChargesStep`) |
| `NewConnectCommunicationStep.tsx` | step 7 · Communication (`CommunicationStep`) |
| `NewConnectReviewStep.tsx` | step 8 · Review & confirm (`ReviewStep`, `OCCUPANCY_COPY`) |
| `NewConnectDone.tsx` | the commit answer that replaces the wizard (`NewConnectDone`) |

**THE DRAFT IS A FILE OF ITS OWN AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING CHOICE.** Every
step file needs `NewConnectDraft`. Had it stayed in the orchestrator, each step
would import the orchestrator — which imports every step — and the split would
have bought an import cycle instead of five independent lanes. It is NOT in
`newConnectShared.tsx` either: that file is the pure half the connection detail
screen also reads, and the draft is the wizard's own state shape, which no other
screen can hold.

**`NewConnectWizard.tsx` STAYS THE ADDRESS OF THE WHOLE WIZARD.** It re-exports
every name it used to declare, so `App.tsx`, `wizardPark.dom.test.tsx` and
`NewConnectWizard.test.tsx` were not touched and no import anywhere in the repo
moved. A re-export is invisible to `G104`, which compares DECLARATIONS rather
than exports, precisely so composing like this is not punished. **Do not
"finish" the split by rewriting those imports** — the barrel is what makes the
change zero-risk for every reader, and deleting it is a separate decision with
its own blast radius.

### HOW A PURE MOVE WAS PROVED, BECAUSE IT CANNOT BE PROVED BY ASSERTING

An assertion only pins what its author thought to name, and the whole risk of a
file split is the thing nobody thought to name. So the proof is a **diff that is
empty**:

  * **Line conservation, mechanically.** Every body was sliced out of the
    original by LINE RANGE rather than retyped, and all **1,895 non-blank lines**
    of the original (excluding the import block, which was rebuilt per file)
    were then shown to survive in the new files. Exactly three lines changed:
    `ServiceTicks`, `StepIntro` and `ManifestRow` each gained `export`, because
    each now lives in a file its callers import.
  * **The rendered DOM, before and after, in a browser.** All eight steps at
    **1280 and 1440**, twice over — an EMPTY draft and the drawn 26-unit build
    clicked through without a reload — captured from the build before the split
    and again from the build after it. **374,502 bytes, 32 screens, sha256
    `c9a9e38d8bf54145a7157308402a8686` both times.** The script is
    `10-scripts/lane_e_new_connect_split_capture.mjs` and it is kept, because
    the next lane to reshape this wizard will want it.
  * **The stylesheet did not move.** `vite build` emitted the identical CSS
    bundle, `index-DvC3AETl.css`, before and after — so no class was rewritten.
  * The rail still measures **992px in 992px at 1280 and 1152px in 1152px at
    1440**, 0px overflow, and today's `def_cus_5186_new_connect_step1_walkthrough.mjs`
    passes untouched.

### WHAT WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED

`DEF-CUS-5451` — the docstring directly above `NEW_CONNECT_STEPS` still argues
*"NINE … so nine ship"* over a list of eight, with eleven further occurrences
across the same feature. **A fix hidden inside a move is invisible to every
reviewer**, so every one of those sentences was carried across verbatim and the
row was filed for the lane that owns that step. Nothing on screen is affected —
every count derives from `NEW_CONNECT_STEPS.length`.

### AND THE COMMIT THAT CARRIED IT IS NOT QUITE THE PURE MOVE ITS MESSAGE CLAIMS (`DEF-CUS-5454`)

**Written here because a commit message cannot be amended once it is pushed, and
because the next person to read `e37a746a` deserves to be told by the repo rather
than to find it.**

The split was written to disk at **04:53** and pushed at **05:20** — twenty-seven
minutes, all of it spent proving the move. At **05:07**, inside that window, a
sibling lane found the brand-new `NewConnectPremiseStep.tsx` and rewrote its
`PREMISE_TYPES`: four hardcoded codes became **six seeded ones read through a
query** (`BR-MET-034`). `push_paths.sh` hashes WORKING-TREE bytes, so `e37a746a`
carries their 43 extra lines — and **the byte-identical DOM capture that commit
cites was taken at 05:04, three minutes before their edit.** The proof is sound;
it simply does not describe the whole of the commit it is attached to.

**Nothing was lost and the branch is healthy** — `tsc` exits 0, the two wizard
suites are 44/44, `eslint` is clean on all eleven new files. Their work was
published early, which is theirs to be told about, not mine to undo:
**reverting a sibling's work to protect a commit message is exactly the
destructive remediation law 11 warns against**, so the record is corrected and
the code is left alone.

⚠ **THE GENERAL LESSON, AND IT IS A GAP IN THE TOOL RATHER THAN IN THE LANE.**
`push_paths.sh` refuses when a named path moved between your base and the tip —
which is law 11's own prescription and it works. **It cannot protect a path that
is BRAND NEW**, because staleness is defined against a tip version that does not
exist yet. Every check the law prescribes passed: the file count was right, the
subtraction showed deletions only in the file being split, and every hunk read
as mine because the sibling had kept my trace header. **What caught it was
re-running the line-conservation arithmetic against the PUSHED COMMIT instead of
against my own disk** — 137 lines where my own script had written 94. Run your
conservation check against what you pushed, not against what you meant to push.

And the sharper half: **the gap between writing a new file and pushing it is
itself the hazard.** A split creates files that other lanes have been waiting
for; the moment they exist on disk, somebody adopts one. Push the skeleton
first and prove it after, or accept that the window is where this happens.

### AND A THIRD THING, FOUND BY DOING THE PUSH-TIME RE-DERIVATION PROPERLY (`DEF-GOV-5455`)

`allocate.py defect --verify 5451` answered **"TAKEN — a sibling pushed it.
Renumber before you commit"**, at the exact moment law 11 says to run it. **No
sibling had.** A sweep of every `origin` ref's register found the id nowhere; the
sole occurrence in the whole repository was **this lane's own commit message**,
`e37a746a`, which the allocator counts as a source — its own note prints
`commit messages (+8)`.

**The id was KEPT.** Obeying the instruction would have moved the register row
away from the id the pushed commit cites and manufactured a dangling citation on
the branch — strictly worse than the collision the check exists to prevent, and
the `DEF-2804` shape it is meant to stop.

⚠ **THE COUNTING IS RIGHT AND THE SENTENCE IS WRONG**, which is the hardest kind
of check to disbelieve. *"A sibling pushed it"* is an inference the data does not
support; the fix is to print WHERE the id was found rather than to guess who put
it there. It is law 11's own blind spot in mirror image — every check measures
against a baseline that already contains your own earlier work, and here that
work reads as a stranger's.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT STEP 7 IS BUILT, AND EVERY ONE OF THE PO'S THREE MESSAGES IS STOPPED BY ONE OPEN QUESTION

Wave 1 lane D. The step-7 block is built end to end — the three occasions, the
wording, the *Who we are telling* read, the template picker and the firing —
and **not one row reaches `outbound_messages`, because `OQ-376` is open.** The
judgments below are the ones a lane could not re-derive from the ruling alone.

### 1 · WHICH THREE OF THE DRAWN SIX, AND THE ONE THAT MOVED RATHER THAN DROPPED

The PO's *"3 communciiton default"* keeps three of p091's six, and **the drawn
order is not the ruling's order**, so a lane taking the first three takes the
wrong ones. Three go because the PO said *"all these 6-8 line items are not
required"*: *Schedule of works*, *Inspection booked*, *Welcome pack*.

⚠ **THE FOURTH DEPARTURE IS NOT A DROP AND MUST NEVER BE RECORDED AS ONE.**
*Unit energised* is drawn `WHEN = As each unit activates`, so **it never fired
on commit even in the picture**, and `BR-MET-115` already moved that letter to
the work-order screen (PO 2026-08-25: *"sent it whnr utility user mar that job
complete traigger it tat that time"*). Filing it beside the three the PO
dropped would reverse a standing ruling by bookkeeping. It is kept in
`connection_messages.NOT_AT_CREATION` with `moved_to` set, and a test asserts
that the three dropped rows have `moved_to = None` and this one does not —
because *the PO dropped it* and *it fires somewhere else* are different facts
and only one of them is reversible by asking again.

### 2 · THE CONTRACT NEEDED NOTHING BUILT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF `OQ-MET-12360`

*"using existing template and notification"*. Measured rather than assumed:
**`contract_service_agreement` already exists** — `CONTRACT_CATALOGS`, group
`contracts`, channel PRINT, with platform wording that states the shape of the
bargain (we supply, you pay at our published rates, we bill, you give us
access) and defers every figure to the utility's own policy. So **two classes
were authored and not three**, and a `new_connect_contract` beside it would
have been two documents stating terms for one service.

⚠ **AND IT EXPLAINS A THING THE NEXT LANE WILL READ AS A BUG.** `BR-NOT-002`
makes every contract version effective-dated and `seed_notice_templates`
REFUSES to seed one — there is no human in a provisioning transaction to
choose that date. **So on a utility that has not published its own agreement,
message two has no pickable row at all.** That is the rule working. A lane
"fixing" it by adding the contract to `SEEDABLE` would publish an undated
agreement on every tenant.

### 3 · BOTH NEW CLASSES FILE UNDER ACCOUNT LIFECYCLE, AND A GUARD DECIDED IT

They were written into `CAT_SERVICE_FIELD` first, on the reasoning that a build
is field work. `test_cr_007__the_service_and_field_category_ships_with_its_four
_templates` went RED naming both. That category is CR-007's four — appointment,
work completed, door hanger, outage — **fixed by a PO ruling of 2026-08-16**,
and it is about work a crew does; these are correspondence with the person who
OWNS the service, which is what the five `service_request_*` classes are.
**Recorded because the guard was right and the first instinct was wrong**, and
the next lane adding a connection class will have the same instinct.

### 4 · MESSAGE THREE REFUSES RATHER THAN RENDERING A FIGURE THE BOOKS DO NOT HOLD

*"What it costs, please pay it"* has to say what it costs. `connections.
quote_total` is a **recorded** number and nothing posts it — `commit_connection`
says so on every build, as `quote_recorded_not_posted` tracking `OQ-379`, and
step 8's own drawing says it in orange: *"the quote stands on the build and the
money has nowhere to post."*

So `{amount_due}` is **mandatory content** on `new_connect_quote` and the
caller **declines to queue the letter** while nothing has posted. Two halves of
one rule: the class makes an amount-less version unpublishable, the guard makes
an amount-less send impossible.

⚠ **THE MONEY GUARD RUNS BEFORE THE SOURCE-KIND CALL, DELIBERATELY, AND THE
ORDER IS THE POINT.** The day `OQ-376` closes, the other two letters start
going out. If the order were reversed, closing ONE question would silently
start sending a letter asking an owner to pay a number no ledger holds. Proved
by breaking it: with the money guard removed the case fails with
`assert 'the_platform_cannot_file_a_connection_message_yet' ==
'the_amount_is_not_in_the_books_yet'` — the letter falling through to the
source-kind refusal, which is exactly the failure that would go quiet later.

### 5 · NO TABLE, AND THAT IS `BR-MET-112` RATHER THAN A CORNER CUT

The drawn ticks and the drawn radio are a clerk's choices, and every step of
this wizard is a draft until the last button. So the choices ride on the commit
payload. `OQ-MET-12360` says the same in as many words — **"no schema at
all"** — and it avoids two lanes adding metering migrations in the same wave,
which is `DEF-2872`'s conflicting-leaf-nodes failure waiting to happen.

### 6 · `account_preferred_language` IS PUBLISHED, AND IT CLOSES A REAL SILENCE

`BR-BIL-025` resolves a template on class, customer category and LANGUAGE.
`queue_document` takes `language` as an argument *precisely because customers
published no read for it* — so **every caller in this product has passed
`None`**, and a utility could publish an `es-MX` variant that would never be
selected for anybody. The column has existed since r15 #2; only the door was
missing. It answers `None` for an account that states no preference rather than
`"en"`, because *they chose English* and *they chose nothing* are different
facts and only one of them may be shown to a clerk as a preference.

### 7 · `OQ-376` IS NOT CLOSED HERE, AND THAT IS THE PRIME DIRECTIVE WORKING

The queue refuses all three by name. Measured against real PostgreSQL:

> *'connection' is not a source kind this platform queues (invoice, payment,
> notice, plan, report, ledger, test, bulk_action, move, account, portal,
> appointment, message, service_request).*

Its option (B) — send them as `notice` — is the cheap one and is wrong: the kind
is what reports group by, so three connect letters would be counted among
disconnection notices and it would surface only in somebody's monthly figures.
`OQ-WRK-1495` put the identical question one message along and the PO chose a
new kind, **but its own closure says `OQ-376` "is a DIFFERENT question and is
not closed by this one"** — so that is evidence for (A) and not a ruling on it.

**What changed today is that (A) got cheap.** The row's own objection was *"a
source kind without a template is half an answer"*; the wording now exists, so
ruling (A) is a one-constant change — `SOURCE_TYPES`, its migration, the floor
dict and the kind-counting reports — rather than a platform change plus an
authoring job. The row is amended to say so.

### 8 · AND THE BLUEPRINT POINTER: STEP 7 IS THE **ACCOUNTS** PDF, NOT BILLING'S

Recorded because a briefing sent this lane to `05-prototype/04 Billing, As
Built.pdf` p091, and **that page is bill-run chips and master accounts.**
*Telling the customer* is `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` **p091**
— the same page number in a different document, which is exactly the kind of
coincidence that gets built from. A lane that rendered the named page and did
not LOOK at it (B14 rule 42) would have built step 7 from a bulk-action table.


### WHAT THE BROWSER WALK ADDED TO THIS DECISION, AN HOUR AFTER IT WAS WRITTEN

The row above was written before the door existed, which is step W working as
intended. Walking the finished door in a browser then found **three more dead
branches behind the 404**, each with its own register row, and two of them
changed what this door carries.

**One dead wire was hiding three.** Nothing on this payload had ever met a
validator, because the address in front of it returned 404 — so the premise
TYPE the wizard offers (`DEF-MET-5463`), the seam signature the meters step
calls (`DEF-MET-5464`) and the service ticks step 4 collects (`DEF-MET-5465`)
were all wrong at once and all invisible at once. **That is the general lesson
and it is worth more than any of the three: a defect behind a dead door cannot
be found by any check, and fixing the door finds them in one afternoon.**

**The premises block gained a fifth field, and it is a precondition rather than
a nicety.** `BR-MET-003`'s inner bound (`DEF-772`, PO: *"Refuse it; if they want
that servcie then they ahve to provision it on that unit or premise first"*)
refuses a meter for a service the PREMISES does not list. A property created
without one arrives with `services_available` NULL, which reads as *"nobody has
been asked"* and refuses **every** meter. So step 4's own ticks now travel on the
payload and the door writes them, and **an ANSWERED empty list stays distinct
from NULL** (`DEF-756`) — *"this address offers nothing"* and *"nobody has been
asked"* are different sentences for the clerk and both still refuse.

**The service point is NOT raised here, and that is deliberate.**
`assets._create_asset_inner` raises one itself when it is handed a unit and a
service — *"if unit_id and service_code and not service_point_id"* — which is the
same path the unit wizard has always taken. Passing one from this commit would
have put a second raiser beside the module's own.

**Two refusal sentences were written in all eleven catalogues**, because the
refusal catalogue refuses a `message_key` no catalogue defines: a clerk would
have met *"That property field isn't recognised"* and *"That unit isn't in this
build"* as SILENCE otherwise.

**What this door still cannot do, and it belongs to another lane.** `commitPlanOf`
turns `create_owner_account` on whenever step 1 names an owner, step 1 REQUIRES
that name, and the accounts door refuses without a party kind (`BR-CUS-1024`).
Step 1 has no person-or-company control — the open half of `DEF-MET-5093` — so
**every build pressed through the screen today is refused on the owner, after
everything else has been built and rolled back.** `BR-MET-112` holding is why
nothing is left behind. The walkthrough proves the build by re-posting the
browser's own bytes with that one flag down, and says so in its own comment
rather than quietly avoiding the case.


## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT STEP 2: THE ADDRESS BECOMES FOUR FIELDS, AND THE PLAN ARRIVES FOUR STEPS EARLY

`CR-094-BRC01` wave 2 lane G. Built from `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu
Blueprint.pdf` **p087 rendered as an image** (B14 rule 42), plus the PO ruling of
the same day. Four earlier briefs named the Billing blueprint for this screen and
it is the Accounts one (`DEF-GOV-5462`).

**THE DRAWING AND THE RULING ARE TWO SOURCES AND BOTH ARE NAMED.** p087 draws six
controls and a greyed seventh. It draws NEITHER the utility services, NOR the
plan, NOR a plan summary, NOR the coverage warning, NOR a search, NOR a premises
name — those six are the PO's ruling of 2026-09-16, which post-dates the drawing:
*"you also need select utility services - one or more from drop down - multi
selct drop down - only utility services activated by teantn/utility. you also
need to select Plan at this stage not at step 5; once plan is slected show the
details of plan as summary"* and *"also take premises name here"*. A later ruling
wins over an earlier drawing; the drawing still owns every other element.

**SIX JUDGMENTS MADE HERE RATHER THAN PUT TO THE PO** (law 13 — a judgment
recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make
one):

**1 · `Plan` here is `planApartments`, and `planCommonArea` stays on step 5.**
The PO said *"Plan"*, singular. Whether a common area exists at all is decided by
step 3's unit pattern, which step 2 has not asked yet — so the build's plan is
asked here and the common area's exception stays where the fact it depends on is
known.

**2 · `State` is a TEXT box although p087 draws a DROPDOWN.** The authority for
the state list is `apps/tenancy/selectors.US_STATES` and **no endpoint publishes
it to a screen.** A select here would mean typing fifty states into a component —
a third hand-typed list of something the server owns, which is the `fire` defect
waiting to happen a third time. `AddPremisesWizard`, the other door that creates
a property, draws a text box for the same reason, and the two doors that write
one column must agree. The list needs a door before this becomes a select.

**3 · The ZIP label is the product's `ZIP / postal code`, not the drawing's `ZIP
code`.** Same reasoning one step on: a product that says one thing on one
property form and another on the other is the divergence `DEF-CUS-5468` is about.

**4 · The services control is the EXISTING `ServicesAvailableField`.** It already
reads `GET /settings/services` filtered to `enabled` (`BR-MET-003`), already
renders chips plus an add control (B14 rule 9), and its label is already the PO's
own phrase — `metering.premises.col.services` is *"Utility services"*. Measured on
brazosbend: the tenant has **2** services enabled and the dropdown offers exactly
those 2. A list written into the screen would have offered eleven to a utility
that sells two.

**5 · Eight labels REUSE keys that already exist in all eleven catalogues** —
`City`, `State`, `ZIP / postal code`, `Street address or premise`, `Unit, flat or
suite`, `Service address`, `No services`, `Not set` — rather than minting
`step3.*` twins. Eighty-eight strings of drift avoided, and one vocabulary per
language kept. Twenty-six keys that had no catalogue entry at all (this step ran
entirely on `defaultValue`, `DEF-4742`'s shape) were fanned into all eleven.

**6 · NO MONTHLY TOTAL IN THE PLAN SUMMARY, carried forward from step 5 rather
than re-argued.** The drawing prints `$30.50/month × 25 = $762.50`. Money is
rounded once, on the server (hard rule 2), and no endpoint publishes a plan's
base charge per unit to this screen; a figure multiplied up in the browser is the
second rounding path `DEF-088` removed, and it would sit beside real ones. The
summary shows name, covered services and effective date.

**WHAT IS STILL OWED AND BELONGS TO ANOTHER LANE.** The plan, its coverage
warning and the monthly-absent note were ADDED to step 2 and have NOT been
removed from step 5 — `NewConnectPlansStep.tsx` is another lane's file this wave,
and the brief scoped this lane to step 2 and the draft. Both pickers write the
same `draft.planApartments`, so they cannot contradict each other; what the
wizard has today is the same question asked twice. **Removing the step-5 copy is
the other half of the move and is reported, not done.**

**PROVED, NOT ASSUMED.** The door's refusal was measured before the fix —
`door vocabulary today: ['address', 'parcel_ref', 'premise_type', 'read_route',
'services_available']` then `REFUSED -> ValidationError VAL-002
(metering.connection.premises_field_unknown)` — and after it, with the
unknown-key guard still firing on `county`, so the vocabulary widened rather than
the check being switched off. Five deliberate breaks were each watched go red,
and **one of them did not**: pasting `$30.50/month × 25 = $762.50` into the
summary left the suite GREEN, because the wizard starts from `emptyDraft()` where
no plan is chosen, so the summary never rendered at all. That is hard-won law 7's
*structurally incapable of failing* wearing the costume of a passing test. The
case now renders the summary over a draft that HAS a plan and asserts the plan's
name and date are present BEFORE asserting the money is not.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT STEP 1: THE CUSTOMER SEARCH, AND FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT COVER (`DEF-CUS-5467`)

Built from p086–p087 of `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` **rendered
as images and looked at** (B14 rule 42), with `DEF-MET-5093` and `DEF-MET-5438`.

### 0 · THE DRAWING DRAWS NONE OF THE THREE, AND THAT IS NOT A CONTRADICTION

⚠ **p086–p087 draw SIX fields on step 1** — Owner type · Owner or developer ·
Prefix · External system reference · Scope · How the work is being done. The
customer search, the party kind and the identifier are **on none of them**.

**The drawing PREDATES the rulings rather than contradicting them**, so B14 rule
41 does not fire and none of this went to the PO: the search is their ruling of
**2026-09-16** (*"how you will search Customer ID here if foudn what and if not
found then what - you will ahve to add this here"*) restating **2026-09-12**
(*"the system should flag if the details were already attached to any of the
accounts in the system"*), and the party kind and identifier are this same day's
§3. **The SHAPE they are built in IS drawn** — p114, the transfer wizard's buyer:
*"Matched first, created only on no match."* That is why the search sits ABOVE
the fields it fills.

⚠ **A lane reading only the drawing would have built none of this, and a lane
reading only the brief would not have known the drawing disagrees.** Recorded
here so the next one does not re-open it.

### 1 · THE SERVER HAS MATCHED-OR-CREATED SINCE 2026-09-01 AND NOTHING COULD REACH IT

**This is a finding rather than a judgment, and it changed what had to be built.**
`_customer_from_payload` already tries, in order: the clerk's named `customer_id`
· our own customer number · a `strong` identity match · the legacy reference ·
`reuse_candidate` — and only then mints. **Step 1 sent no party kind and no
identifier**, so the evidence was always empty, every branch fell through, and
the wizard always created. The decision log said that half had *"no implementation
at all today"*; the implementation existed and had **no caller**. So **no endpoint
was added** — the screen is the missing half of a door already open.

### 2 · THE SEARCH DOES NOT INVITE A PHONE NUMBER, THOUGH THE SERVER'S `q` ACCEPTS ONE

`GET /customers?q=` has four legs — customer number, legacy reference, name and
**phone** through its blind index. `BR-CUS-1024` is that **a phone MINTS a number
and may never MATCH one**.

**Decided: the field asks for a name or a customer number, and says so.** The
server's phone leg is untouched — removing it is not this screen's business and
it serves the customers list — but a box captioned *"…or phone"* on the control
whose whole purpose is to ATTACH would make the refused thing the obvious thing
to type. **Worked:** *Clara Castillo* is found and attached on her name; her
number `(402) 555-1002` is on her record and is not what found her.

### 3 · THE PICKED CUSTOMER TRAVELS IN THE ACCOUNTS DOOR'S OWN VOCABULARY

The commit could have carried a new wizard key (`owner.customer_no`, say) and had
`_owner_block_in_the_doors_language` translate it — **which needs a backend change
in a file this lane does not own.**

**Decided: send `owner.customer = {customer_id, display_name, kind}` directly.**
That function is explicit that it is *"a translation, never an override"* and
keeps a `customer` block a caller assembled properly; `customer_id` is already
one of the five keys `CUSTOMER_BLOCK_FIELDS` accepts; and `BR-CUS-019` makes the
clerk's explicit answer the strongest statement available. **No server change,
and the id never reaches the screen** (B14 rule 31 — `C-00003` is shown,
the uuid is not, and the walkthrough asserts no uuid appears in `innerText`).

### 4 · THE SHORTFALL BLOCKS THE STEP, IT DOES NOT MERELY WARN

`BR-CUS-1024` refuses the owner's master account outright without a party kind
and an identifier. **Decided: `validate` fails until it clears.** Letting the
clerk walk on means discovering it after eight steps of a build, which is what
the PO ruled against on the accounts wizard in the words *"never after the account
is created"*. **An attached customer clears it**, because
`refuse_account_without_identity` returns early on a named customer — that is the
whole of *"attach and do not retype"*, and demanding evidence on screen that the
door does not want would be the opposite of the ruling.

### 5 · THE RULE IS SHARED; THE WORDS ARE NOT (`DEF-CUS-5473`)

`ownerIdentityShortfall` calls `accountIdentityShortfall` rather than restating
*what counts as an identifier* a fourth time. **Its SENTENCES are not reused.**
`customers.account.identity_required_person` reads *"Add a Social Security number,
a driving licence or a phone number — an account cannot be opened without one of
them"* — **21 words in one sentence**, where B14 rule 33 caps an instruction at
**six per sentence**. Reusing it would import a live breach onto a new screen, so
step 1 says **"Needs one identifier to continue."** (5) and **"Add the Tax ID."**
(4). The long four are **filed as `DEF-CUS-5473`, not edited from here** — they
are on three other wizards and a copy change to them is those screens' work.

### 6 · WHAT WAS PROVED, AND WHERE

26 vitest cases, each **shown red first**: printing the uuid instead of the number
fails the rule-31 case; deriving `company` from `landlord` fails with *expected
'company' to be undefined*; dropping the attached short-circuit puts the Social
Security number field back in front of a customer already on file.

**And in a real browser at 1280 and 1440** —
`10-scripts/def_cus_5467_step1_customer_search_walkthrough.mjs`. Typing
`Castillo` issued **one** request,
`GET /api/brazosbend/customers?q=Castillo&per=20`, and returned
**`C-00003 — Clara Castillo`**; attaching filled the owner's name and phone,
showed the number, **asked for no identifier at all**, cleared the shortfall, and
`Change` returned the step to searching. No uuid anywhere in the page's text.

⚠ **AND THE WALKTHROUGH'S FIRST VERSION WAS A CHECK THAT COULD NOT PASS.** It
looked for `#nc_party_kind`; `SegmentedField` puts its id on the radios' `name`
and on the label and **never on a DOM id**, so the selector matched nothing and
reported the party kind missing from a screen it was plainly on. Hard-won law 7's
*incapable of passing*, found by running it. The second version counts the radios
by `name` and clicks the **label**, because the input itself is not visible —
which is the right refusal: a control a person cannot see is one they cannot use.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT STEPS 3 AND 4, BUILT: SEVEN JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT COVER

Lane H wave 2. Steps 3 and 4 built from `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf`
p088–p089 rendered AS AN IMAGE (B14 rule 42). Each judgment below was DECIDED
rather than put to the PO, per hard-won law 13 — none collides with a signed
rule, none moves a ❄️ FROZEN figure, none is a fact only the PO holds — and each
is written with its worked number so it can be overturned against a row instead
of rediscovered.

**MEASURED, NOT COMPUTED TWICE.** Walked in a browser at 1280 and 1440 on the
seeded `brazosbend` tenant, six units plus the common area, electric/water/sewer:
**21 rows**, counts reading **Service points 21 · Meters to fit 14 · Work orders
2**, grid **958px at 1280** (right edge 1239 of 1280) and **1118px at 1440**,
**page overflow 0px at both**. The step-3 table is 7 occupancy cells — 6 vacant
and 1 dash.

### 1 · THE REVIEW STEP'S RADIO IS NOT REPLACED — IT SETS THEM ALL

`occupancyOfUnit()` falls back to `draft.occupancy`, not to `OCCUPANCY_DEFAULT`.
So the whole-build four-way still moves every row the clerk has not moved by
hand and **no second answer exists to disagree with the first** — which is what
the step-3 ruling asked for in its own words. An explicit per-unit choice
outranks a later bulk one, deliberately: unit 4 with a tenant moving in is the
case the column exists for, and silently resetting it would lose the one fact
the clerk went out of their way to record. `NewConnectReviewStep.tsx` is another
lane's file and was not touched.

### 2 · INHERITANCE REPLACED THE TWO SERVICE SETS, AND THREE CALL SITES MOVED

`draftUnitServices` now reads `premiseServices` minus the grid's drops.
`apartmentServices`/`commonAreaServices` decide nothing. **The middle of the
three readers is why this is recorded:** `planCoverageGaps(draft.apartmentServices, …)`
over a now-empty set reports NO GAPS — a check that cannot fail rather than one
that passes (law 7). It reads the dwelling union and the common area's own row.

**The union with an explicit `taken: true` is deliberate.** Derived from
`premiseServices` alone a unit could never name a service the street lacks,
`availabilityBreaches` would be structurally incapable of firing, and its refusal
strip would be dead UI. Ticking gas on the grid and then unticking gas in the
availability list is a real afternoon, and the refusal is what tells them.

### 3 · OFFERING AN ASSET TYPE AND DEFAULTING TO ONE ARE TWO QUESTIONS — SEWER IS WHY

`SERVICE_ASSET_TYPES` offers sewer a meter and a sub-meter, because a utility
that meters its own sewer exists. `SERVICE_ASSET_DEFAULT` has **no sewer entry**:
sewer is a share of the water usage charge (`BR-RAT-015`), so defaulting it to
the first thing it offers fits **a meter on every sewer connection — seven of
them on a six-unit build**, each a job somebody has to cancel. Measured: the
meters count is **14** with the split and **21** without it, and that difference
is the whole of this judgment.

### 4 · FIRE AND STORM WATER ARE ABSENT FOR DIFFERENT REASONS AND NEITHER IS A GAP

**Fire has no asset type and must not get one here.** `OQ-1361` is half answered
— the hydrant is an asset — and whether a fire service point takes the
`fire_line` type is still `BR-AST-042`'s open question. `fire_line` IS in the
catalogue and is still not offered; deciding it here would answer something the
PO has never been asked. **Storm water** has none because it is billed on area
and no ratified asset type is a storm-water connection (`DEF-2388`). Both render
a dash, which is a stated absence closed by default (B14 rule 32).

### 5 · THE WORK-ORDER COUNT IS DISTINCT TEMPLATES, NOT ROWS

`commit_connection` raises one order per entry in `work_orders`, and that entry
is `{template_id, template_version}` with **no unit on it**. So 21 rows naming
three templates can only become three orders, and printing 21 beside the grid
would be `DEF-MET-5428`'s shape again — a clerk promised orders that are never
written. The screen says what the commit will actually do. Whether a build
*should* raise one order per unit is `OQ-MET-12382`, raised rather than answered.

### 6 · RATIONALE CAME OFF BOTH SCREENS, AND THE BLUEPRINT AGREES WITH THE RULE

p089 draws a red callout — *"The common area is why this grid exists. It takes
electric and water and no sewer…"* — and it is **not rendered**. B14 rule 33
gives rationale zero words on screen. The same for step 3's *"A pattern, not a
list…"* and the common area's *"Corridors, car park, irrigation…"*, and p088
draws no prose on step 3 at all. All three are in the files' own docstrings.
The disabled upload KEEPS its reason — an absent control a clerk is hunting for
is the one case where silence costs more than words — at 4 words a sentence
rather than 15 in one.

The drawn **`Apply to all units` / `Choose per unit`** radio is DROPPED:
inheritance makes the answer always *all*, and a radio whose second option
nothing would pick teaches a clerk a model the product does not have.

### 7 · TWO SPELLINGS OF THE COMMON AREA, AND THE PRODUCT'S ONE WINS

p088's compressed step-3 table draws the unit as **`CA`**; p089's grid draws
**`Common area`**, and so do the step-3 and step-4 rulings in this log. They are
two frames of ONE blueprint drawing the same fact differently. **The product
already commits `Common area`** — `COMMON_AREA_LABEL` is what `units.label` is
WRITTEN as — so renaming it to match the compressed frame would change data at
rest to settle a drawing's inconsistency with itself. Not reconciled on this
screen; recorded so the next lane does not "fix" it.

### WHAT WAS FOUND BY LOOKING AT THE RUNNING SCREEN AND BY NOTHING ELSE

Both are filed rather than described (law 1 — a comment claiming a gap is not a
plan):

* **`DEF-MET-5476`** — the grid's **Install date is blank on all 21 rows**,
  because it defaults to the target activation date and *that is asked on step
  5*. The code is correct and the default points FORWARD in the wizard, so it
  can never fire. 41 unit cases, `tsc` and every gate pass over it.
* **`DEF-SHL-5477`** — `DatePickerField` has no `labelHidden`, so the cell
  repeats its column header **21 times**. `SelectField` gained that affordance
  for exactly this case and its docstring says so; the sibling control never
  did.

### A CITATION THIS LANE GOT WRONG AND CAUGHT BEFORE IT SPREAD

The work-order question was first written into the code and a commit message as
`OQ-MET-5481` — a number taken by hand. **`5481` is in the DEFECT range, not the
OQ range**, so it would have read as a real id pointing at nothing, which is
`DEF-2804`'s exact shape on a screen a clerk uses. `allocate.py oq` answered
**12382**; both occurrences were corrected. **Taking an id by hand is now the
more dangerous path and this is why** — the allocator asks the remote and a hand
count reads only this checkout.

## 2026-09-16 — NEW CONNECT STEPS 7 AND 8 ARE BUILT, AND THE SCREEN CONTRADICTS ITS OWN DRAWING IN THREE PLACES ON PURPOSE

CR-094 wave 2 lane J. Built from `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf`
**p091–p093, read AS IMAGES at scale 2** (B14 rule 42) — not the Billing
blueprint, whose p091 is bill-run chips (`DEF-GOV-5462`). The judgments below
are the ones a lane could not re-derive from the ruling or the drawing alone.

### 1 · NO DRAFT FIELD WAS ADDED FOR STEP 7, AND THE PLAN SAID TO ADD ONE

The lane brief expected a small `newConnectDraft.ts` change to hold the clerk's
ticks and template pick. **None was made, and the absence is the decision.**

Three facts, measured rather than assumed: `commit_connection` does **not** call
`queue_on_commit`; `CommitPlan` has no member for a tick or a pick; and a key the
commit door does not know is **refused BY NAME** (`DEF-MET-4715`) rather than
dropped. So a draft field would have been state nothing reads, feeding a payload
that would be refused, over a queue that is empty anyway because `OQ-376` is
open. That is dead state behind a dead control — hard-won law 2 in both
directions at once.

⚠ **AND IT PAID FOR ITSELF THE SAME AFTERNOON.** Four lanes were editing
`newConnectDraft.ts` continuously; staying out of it removed this lane's only
mechanism-two exposure on the file most at risk. The one shared line this lane
DID need — `<CommunicationStep draft={draft} …>` in the orchestrator — was left
uncommitted for forty minutes and **a sibling's whole-file write erased it**. It
was caught by `tsc` on a rebuild, re-applied and pushed immediately. *Commit
small and commit often* is the whole of that lesson; the file count, the hunks
and every other check in law 11 are silent on uncommitted work.

### 2 · THE DRAWN TICKS SHIP DISABLED, WHICH IS NEITHER THE DRAWING NOR A DROP

p091 draws a tick per row and the PO called the three *defaults*. A LIVE tick
over a message that queues nothing is the mirror of hard-won law 2 — the shape
that left the customer portal with **two working doors out of eight** for days
(`DEF-CWP-3925`). Deleting the ticks would hide the ruling. So they render
**checked and disabled** with the reason, which is `BR-SHL-025`'s existing shape
and the one `CheckboxField` grew a `disabled` prop for on 2026-09-15.

**Each row carries its own stop reason and the three are DIFFERENT**, because
they are three different facts: `Not queued` (`OQ-376`), `No published wording`
(`BR-NOT-002`), `Not in the books` (`OQ-379`). The money guard runs BEFORE the
source-kind call deliberately — the day `OQ-376` closes the other two start going
out, and in the other order closing one question would silently start asking an
owner to pay a figure no ledger holds.

### 3 · THE PICKER'S DRAWN RADIO IS RENDERED AS A MARKER, IN THE DRAWING'S OWN WORDS

p091's one dotted box: *"The template picker names the version that would be used
and does not render it."* So the picker REPORTS; it does not choose. A radio
would be a control over the same dead act as the ticks. The column is kept and
its cell says **would be used / a draft cannot be used**, so *drafts are listed
and are not selectable* still reads on screen.

### 4 · TWO OF p092's SEVEN `What happens next` ROWS ARE NOT BUILT AS DRAWN

B14 rule 37 — a figure drawn in a wireframe is an ILLUSTRATION, never a fact to
build to.

* *"Three messages are queued to the owner"* — **none are.** Measured after a
  real commit: the queue holds zero rows and all three are refused by name. The
  row now reads *No message is queued · Nowhere yet*.
* *"Nine work orders are raised"* — **no count is printed.** The commit does
  raise them and returns `manifest.work_orders` since 2026-09-16, but only AFTER
  the press. The only figure available on the review screen is the proposal the
  wizard already showed itself at step 5, and that self-agreement **is**
  `DEF-MET-5428`: the screen promised nine for eleven days while the server
  raised none, and agreed with itself every time.

### 5 · `Edit` IS ON NO PAGE OF THE DRAWING AND IS ADDED ANYWAY, ONE PER GROUP

p092/p093 draw ~20 read-back rows and no edit affordance, and the reason is
findable: `WizardFrame`'s rail is **already** a `<button>` per completed step
(`jumpBackTo`). Twenty more controls would be a second navigation over one act.
But the rail cannot answer *which step captured THIS field*, which is the only
reason a read-back exists. So it is **one link per DRAWN HEADING** — three, not
twenty — doing exactly what the rail does.

It moves `?step=` client-side rather than navigating, because the wizard holds
every answer in component state (`BR-MET-112`) and a real `<a href>` would empty
seven steps silently. **Only a browser can tell those apart**, so the walkthrough
presses it and reads `#nc_address` back.

### 6 · `G93` REFUSED THIS LANE'S FIRST SHAPE AND WAS RIGHT

`getConnectTemplates` was first written beside the step that renders it, to keep
this lane out of `newConnectEndpoints.ts` — a reasonable law-11 trade. **`G93`
failed it**, and its own docstring is the argument: `*Endpoints.ts` files are
exempt **as a class**, and *"a file that is not an endpoints module and writes
that path is either navigating or has put an API call somewhere it does not
belong"*. An API path hidden in a screen file is indistinguishable, to that gate,
from a link to the retired `/connections/<id>` destination. It moved. **The
shared-file risk is `push_paths.sh`'s job, not a gate's blind spot** — recorded
because the wrong instinct was the careful-looking one.

### 7 · B14 RULE 33's SIX-WORD CAP IS ON THE RENDERED CELL, IN ELEVEN LANGUAGES

The English check passed while `es`, `es-MX` and `fr-FR` each carried an
over-long cell, because **the screen a Mexican utility reads is its own
catalogue's, not English**. All three were corrected and a test now reads all
eleven catalogues and names the file, key, word count and text.

⚠ **AND IT ONLY CAME UP BECAUSE THE KEYS WERE FANNED IN AT ALL.** Before this
commit every string on steps 7 and 8 — 92 of them, the wave-1 ones included —
resolved through `defaultValue`, so both screens rendered **English to every
tenant in every language**, silently, with `tsc`, vitest and every gate green. A
neighbouring step was found with twenty-six such strings the same day. **An
untranslated string is invisible to every check in this repo**, and the only
thing that finds one is counting the keys against the catalogues.

### 8 · A GUARD THAT COULD NOT FAIL, FOUND BY DOING THE RED PROOF PROPERLY

Six breakages were applied in a private worktree. Five went red. **The sixth
passed**: removing `&& row.pickable` from `usedRow` — the exact change that lets
an **unapproved draft** be named as the wording a letter goes out on — left all
seventeen cases green. The picker's own column was asserted; the thing that
CHOOSES was not, and the seeded rows happen to list the published variant first,
so `rows.find` took the right one by accident of ordering.

A case that **reverses the row order** now fails on it. Recorded because the
lesson is procedural rather than local: *break it in the harness that runs it*
found a defect that writing the test never would have, and the guard had looked
perfectly adequate.

### 9 · `DEF-CUS-5475` — THE PICKER IS EMPTY ON EVERY UTILITY THAT ALREADY EXISTED

Found in a browser, by nothing else. A **freshly provisioned** utility gets two
published rows; `brazosbend`, provisioned before these classes were authored on
2026-09-16, gets **none**, because `seed_notice_templates` runs at provisioning
and nothing backfills a class added later. Every test provisions its own tenant,
so every test is right and none of them asks this question. The screen states the
absence rather than showing a blank table, which is the only part of it this lane
could fix.

## 2026-09-16 — THE VISIBLE WORD IS **CONNECTORS**, AND THE IDENTIFIERS DO NOT MOVE

Reading the Integration Blueprint's own change-process section, the PO ruled,
verbatim:

> *"this is correct - use connector - instead of integration"*

### WHAT CHANGES

**Everything a clerk reads says CONNECTORS.** The settings tab, the page heads,
the empty states, the buttons, the refusals — **319 translation keys** by the
blueprint's own count, across eleven catalogues.

### WHAT DOES NOT — DECIDED, NOT ASKED

The blueprint separates the two questions on purpose: *"The visible word changes;
the identifiers need not. Decide that separately — it is the difference between a
day and a fortnight."* The PO answered the **visible word**. So:

| Stays | Why |
|---|---|
| `apps/integrations` | a module rename touches every import in the repo at once |
| `integration_connection`, `integration_credential`, `integration_run`, `integration_target_reference`, `integration_consent` | renaming a table is a migration on live data to change a word nobody sees |
| `BR-INT-###`, `DEF-INT-###`, `OQ-INT-###` | **this repo's settled posture** — `OQ-291` is `OQ-291` and `CR-001` keeps its bare form, because respelling ids moves every citation in every register, docstring and test at once, which is the mass shared-file rewrite law 11 exists to prevent |
| the i18n key PATHS (`integrations.*`) | the key is an identifier; the VALUE is the visible word |

**So this is a values change in eleven catalogues, not a rename of anything.**
That is the "day" and not the "fortnight".

### THE ROUTE — THE ONE CASE THAT SITS BETWEEN THEM, CALLED RATHER THAN ASKED

`settings/integrations/:key` is half-visible: a clerk can read it in the address
bar and can bookmark it. **It stays.** Changing it breaks every bookmark to buy a
word in a place nobody reads for meaning, and this repo already has the pattern
for the other direction — `/connections/<uuid>` kept its ROUTE and changed its
DESTINATION when that screen was deleted, precisely so no working link broke.
**If the PO wants the address to read `connectors` too, the honest form is a new
route plus a redirect from the old one, never a move.**

### TWO RULES THIS RUNS STRAIGHT INTO

⚠ **B14 RULE 34 — ONE PAIR OF WORDS FOR ONE IDEA, EVERYWHERE, IN ALL ELEVEN
CATALOGUES.** A half-done rename is worse than none: a tab reading *Connectors*
over a screen reading *Integration settings* teaches a clerk there are two things.
**Every one of the 319 moves together or none does.**

⚠ **AND RULE 35 — A CATALOGUE IS WRITTEN IN ITS OWN LANGUAGE, NOT TRANSLATED FROM
ENGLISH.** *Connector* is a technical noun and the mechanical rendering of it is
wrong in several languages. **This is not hypothetical here**: on 2026-09-16 a
lane found four catalogues rendering the billing word *Plan* as the verb **to
schedule** — French `Planifier`, on five live screens — and our parity check was
perfectly happy, because it compares which KEYS exist and eleven confident wrong
words satisfy that exactly. **319 keys is 3,509 translated strings across eleven
languages, and mechanically rendering them would be that defect at scale.**

⚠ **AND THE WHOLE INTEGRATIONS FEATURE MAY HAVE NO CATALOGUE ENTRIES AT ALL.**
`DEF-CUS-5478`, filed today, found the entire new connect wizard running on
English `defaultValue` fallbacks with **zero** keys in any of the eleven files —
rendering English to every tenant in every language, silently, with parity green.
**Count what RESOLVES before counting what to change**; the 319 is the
blueprint's number and it has not been verified against this checkout.

## 2026-09-16 — THE CONNECTOR SCREENS USE THE ACCENTED `Panel`, AND THE KIT ALREADY HAS BOTH FORMS

Reviewing the component list proposed for the seven connector screens, the PO
ruled, verbatim:

> *"i want you to use panel with acsent - where ever shown it that way"*

### THE DRAWING SHOWS TWO DIFFERENT ACCENTED TREATMENTS, AND `Panel` ALREADY HAS BOTH

Measured in `07-frontend/src/components/Panel.tsx` rather than proposed:
`PanelTone` is `"plain" | "info" | "warning" | "emergency" | "group"`.

| Drawn treatment | Tone | What it renders |
|---|---|---|
| A **rule down the left edge**, bold title in the body, no header row — the blueprint's callout boxes (*"The honest limit"*, *"Read the three shut doors as good news"*, *"Already solved, and proven in shipped code"*) | **`emergency`** | keeps the plain border and adds `border-l-4 border-l-[var(--brand)]` |
| A **small-caps heading in the accent with a rule beneath it** — the blueprint's named sections (`WHICH UNITS`, `WHAT THE GATE IS`, `THE JOB`) | **`group`** | heading uppercase and tracked in the accent, accent rule on the header row |

**So the ruling costs nothing to obey and adds no class to any stylesheet.**
`tone` absent is `plain`, which is byte-for-byte what the 149 existing call sites
already render — the accented forms are opt-in and nothing else moves.

⚠ **`emergency` IS DELIBERATELY NOT A FOURTH HUE.** The component's own note
records it: it keeps the plain border and adds a left rule, because
`09-component-inventory.md` draws it that way and `ReportProblem.tsx` confirmed it
from the running screen. **A lane reading *"accent"* and reaching for a fourth
border colour would be inventing a variant the kit refused on purpose.**

⚠ **AND `group` IS IN THE KIT RATHER THAN IN A SCREEN ON PURPOSE**, which is B14
rule 36 quoted in the file itself: *"where the kit lacks a piece, ADD IT TO THE
KIT rather than hand-rolling it in the screen, which is how four screens acquire
four different chips."*

### WHAT THIS SETTLES FOR THE CONNECTOR WORK

Of the six screens, the accented panel is the right container wherever the
blueprint draws a bordered callout or a named group — which is most of the
connector **view** screen's sections, the **configure** dialog's field groups, and
every *stated absence* strip. **The rule to apply is the PO's own words: where the
drawing shows it that way.** Not everywhere, and not by taste.

⚠ **AND IT DOES NOT REPLACE THE REFUSAL COMPONENTS.** `RefusalStrip`,
`ConsequenceBox` and `WarningBox` carry meanings a container does not — a refusal
is not a section heading. An accented `Panel` around a refusal would say *this is
a group of fields* where the screen means *this cannot happen and here is why*.

## 2026-09-16 — CONNECTORS IN TWO PHASES: ALL 28 DECLARED FIRST, THE LOGIC ONE AT A TIME AFTER

PO ruling, verbatim:

> *"i want you to put dummary apis in all these 28 conenctor - in phase 2 we will
> replace them and build a actual logic around them - phase 1 lets have all in
> place and phase 2 step by step buidl logic fo each conenctor"*

### THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ENFORCED AT BOOT — NOTHING IS INVENTED

`apps/integrations/registry.py` already separates **declaring a connector** from
**being able to connect to one**:

* `Disposition(kind="coming_soon", wave=…)` — *"the card says Coming soon · v1.1
  and **the server refuses a connect**"*, in `sms_twilio`'s own words. The card is
  the same object with `disposition.kind == "coming_soon"` and **no adapter**.
* A `coming_soon` manifest **must** carry a `wave` — the registry refuses it **by
  name** if it does not (`registry.py:601`).
* And the stronger half: *"a LIVE card with a later phase **still refuses to
  connect until its adapter is registered**"*. So a manifest cannot accidentally
  become connectable by being marked live.
* The whole registry is validated at `AppConfig.ready()` and **refuses by name if
  anything is missing or outside a closed vocabulary** — a malformed placeholder
  fails at boot, loudly, not in front of a clerk.

**So phase 1 is data, exactly as `BR-INT-037` requires** — *"every time such
integration comes we dont want to change our integration framework"*. Thirteen
new connectors cost roughly **two adapters**; the five ERPs need **none at all**.

### PHASE 1 — ALL 28 DECLARED

| | |
|---|---|
| **Manifests** | all 28, with their real shape: fields (1–8) and operations (1–16) as the blueprint's own tables give them |
| **Endpoints** | `api.vendor.example` on every row we do not actually have — **47 rows across the 13 that do not ship**, each marked `PROPOSED` |
| **The 15 that ship** | **untouched.** They keep their real hosts and carry no mark |
| **Disposition** | `coming_soon` + a wave on anything without an adapter, so the card says so and the server refuses the connect |
| **Adapters** | none new for the placeholders |

⚠ **`api.vendor.example` IS NOT AN ARBITRARY PLACEHOLDER AND MUST NOT BE
"IMPROVED".** `.example` is reserved and can never resolve, so a dummy endpoint
**cannot accidentally reach anything**. The blueprint's reasoning is a rule about
honesty rather than a convention: *"A plausible hostname reads as a fact, and
`api.sap.example` claimed knowledge of SAP's API that nobody has."* **Seven
invented hostnames had already crept in.** A lane that "tidies" these into
realistic hosts turns a visible absence into a silent lie.

### THE ONE THING THAT MUST NOT HAPPEN IN PHASE 1

⚠ **A PLACEHOLDER MUST NEVER READ AS LIVE.** Twenty-eight cards that all look
available, one of which a utility connects and nothing works, is hard-won law 2's
mirror — a live control over a dead act — and it is the shape that left the
customer portal with **two working doors out of eight** on 2026-09-05.

Three things make phase 1 safe, and all three are already built:
1. the card **says** *Coming soon* with its wave;
2. the server **refuses the connect**, by name, rather than accepting and failing later;
3. **Test the connection** on a placeholder must refuse for the same stated
   reason — never return green, and never sit enabled over nothing.

**A phase-1 connector a clerk can press and get silence from is worse than one we
never declared.**

### PHASE 2 — ONE CONNECTOR AT A TIME

Replace the placeholder endpoint with the real one from the vendor, register the
adapter, flip the disposition to live. **Per connector, in the order the PO
chooses.** The manifest's shape does not change: *"the real endpoints arrive with
the manifest in the database, which is where they belong."*

### WHAT PHASE 1 DOES NOT FIX, AND IT IS STILL FIRST

⚠ **The credential model still blocks five connectors** (`DEF-INT-4118`): a
manifest holds a **single Auth** and the database enforces **one active credential
per connection**, so a card processor that holds *our* key and also has an
operation *we* start does not fit. The blueprint is explicit — **"This is the
first thing to fix, not the names."** Declaring five payment manifests in phase 1
does not make them connectable in phase 2 until that moves.

---

## 2026-09-16 — THE PLACEHOLDER APIS ARE NAMED IN OUR OWN CONVENTION, AND THE THREE 14 SEPTEMBER RULINGS ARE CONFIRMED

Two more in the same exchange.

### 1 · THE NAMING CONVENTION APPLIES TO THE PLACEHOLDERS

PO, verbatim: *"so when you put dummary apis for us - use this format"*, quoting
the blueprint's own nomenclature section:

| Artefact | Shape |
|---|---|
| Partner endpoint | `/partner/v1/<plural noun>` |
| Outbound payload | `<noun>.v<n>` |
| Operation key | `<runner>_<noun>` — the verb names which of the four runners executes it |
| Clerk label | **three words or fewer** |

Plus the tenant resolution — **key → connection → tenant, three hops, all on the
server** — with its cost, and **an escape hatch if a vendor insists on their own
base URL**.

⚠ **READING TAKEN, AND IT SPLITS THE CONVENTION FROM THE HOST, because the two
directions are not the same fact.** The nomenclature section governs *"the forty
operations WE own"* — the endpoints **partners call us on**, which we name and
therefore are never placeholders. The `api.vendor.example` rows are **their**
endpoints, which we call and do not own.

So:

| | Ours to name | Theirs, unknown |
|---|---|---|
| **Host** | our own | **`api.vendor.example`**, row marked `PROPOSED` |
| **Path** | `/partner/v1/<plural noun>` | the same plural-noun shape, so the drawing reads consistently |
| **Operation key** | `<runner>_<noun>` | **the same** — the runner is ours either way |
| **Clerk label** | ≤ 3 words | **the same** |
| **Payload** | `<noun>.v<n>` | **the same** |

**The convention is OURS and applies to all 28 connectors' operations; only the
HOST is faked, and only where we genuinely do not have one.** That is the
reading, recorded rather than assumed, because *"use this format"* could also
have been read as putting our own `/partner/v1/…` paths on vendors' machines —
which would claim an endpoint on someone else's server that nobody has agreed to.

⚠ **AND `<runner>_<noun>` IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT COSMETIC.** The four runners are
the four doors — *we collect · we send · they send · they read* — and
`BR-INT-028` puts direction and initiative **on the operation, never on the
connector**. So the verb in the key is what picks the runner. A placeholder named
in the wrong verb would file a call under the wrong door, and the card's direction
words are computed from the operation list — which is exactly how three rows were
found reading *We send* beside a trigger of *They call us*.

⚠ **THE THREE-WORD CLERK LABEL IS B14 RULE 33 ARRIVING FROM THE OTHER SIDE.**
Rule 33 caps a label at three words for every screen in the product; the blueprint
caps an operation label at three words for every connector. **Same number, two
authorities, no conflict** — and 40 operations × 11 catalogues is 440 strings
where a four-word label would go unnoticed.

### 2 · THE THREE RULINGS OF 14 SEPTEMBER, CONFIRMED

PO: *"this si correct"*.

| Question | Ruled | Schema |
|---|---|---|
| Can a clerk rename an API we declared? | **No** — *"no clark will not do it — we will do it during initial configuration"* | **No** — the name stays on the manifest |
| Are mappings per connector or per API? | **Per connector** | **No** — it is what ships today |
| Should an issued key name the APIs it may call? | **Yes** | **Yes** — a scope column and a check at the door |

**Two cost nothing but drawing. The one that costs a migration is the one with a
security shape, which is the right way round.**

⚠ **THE FIRST ONE IS WHY PHASE 1 IS CHEAP.** Because naming an API is ours at
onboarding and not a clerk control, the set-up form **lists** APIs and does not
edit them — the disabled *+ Add an API* control is removed — and declaring 28
connectors with 78 operation rows **costs no schema change at all**.

⚠ **AND THE THIRD ONE IS A SECOND SCHEMA MOVE ON TOP OF THE CREDENTIAL FIX.** A
scope column on the issued key plus a check at the door, and **six view screens
gain a *May call* column**. It is not part of phase 1's placeholder work and
should not be folded into it quietly.
