## 2026-09-16 — TWO TOKENS, PROD AND SANDBOX: ALREADY BUILT, AND IT IS NOT THE THING THAT BLOCKS FIVE CONNECTORS

PO ruling, verbatim, on the thirteen *We send* connectors' one-token-per-connection
shape:

> *"youa re correct - so there will be two token 1 for prod and 1 for sandbox"*

### THIS COSTS NOTHING — IT IS `BR-INT-026` AND IT SHIPPED

Measured in `06-backend/apps/integrations/models.py` rather than proposed. The
connection model's own docstring:

> *"One provider, one environment, one tenant — and NO secret material. … live
> and sandbox environments are **two rows** (`BR-INT-026`): the UNIQUE below is
> the sandbox / live split."*

`integration_connection` carries an `environment` column and a unique constraint
on **`(tenant, provider_key, environment)`**. So a utility already holds **two
connections** for one vendor — live and sandbox — and **each carries its own
credential**. Two tokens is what the product already does; it is reached by two
connection ROWS rather than two credentials on one row.

**So the ruling needs no migration, no new column and no change to the token
shape.** *"One token per connection"* and *"two tokens, prod and sandbox"* are the
same sentence once you know a connection is per environment.

⚠ **AND THE GRID ALREADY FILTERS ON IT.** The blueprint records that *"every
dimension + Filter ▾ opens — direction, state, **environment** — is already in
the grid payload"*. So the screen half exists too.

### ⚠ THIS DOES NOT FIX `DEF-INT-4118`, AND THE TWO MUST NOT BE CONFLATED

The environment split is a **second row per vendor**. The thing blocking the five
card processors is **two credentials in the SAME row**: a manifest holds a single
`Auth`, and the database enforces **one active credential per connection** — while
a processor **holds our key** *and* has an operation **we start**, so it needs both
directions at once in one environment.

**Different axis, different fix.** Doubling the environments doubles the problem
rather than solving it: after this ruling a card processor needs two credentials
in *live* and two more in *sandbox*. The blueprint's order stands — **"This is the
first thing to fix, not the names."**

### THE THREE EDGES THIS RULING MEETS, AND NONE OF THEM MOVES

| Case | What two environments means |
|---|---|
| **The two that cannot hold a token** — SMTP (username and password) and the file drop (no token at all) | **unchanged.** Two of nothing is nothing; their stated refusal is the same in both environments |
| **The two already on OAuth** | two connections means **two authorisations** — a vendor's sandbox app is a different app. The token's state is shown, not generated by us |
| **`payments_sandbox`, the standalone *Test payments* connector** | **not the same thing and it stays.** A fake processor for demonstrations is a different object from the sandbox environment of a real one — and it is one of the three connectors that legitimately spans two doors |

### THE LESSON THIS ROW COST, AND IT IS THE LAW'S OWN

⚠ **THE FIRST ATTEMPT TO WRITE THIS ROW WAS ERASED BEFORE IT COULD BE PUSHED.**
It was appended to the shared tree's copy of this file, and a sibling lane's
whole-file write landed on top of it seconds later — law 11 mechanism two, on the
file the law names, happening to the lane that had been warning others about it
all afternoon. Nothing was published and nothing else was lost, because the
push-time check compares the working tree against the pinned tip and the row
simply was not there.

**The fix is the one the law already prescribes and this session had not been
applying to itself: build a shared-file append in a PRIVATE `git worktree` at the
pinned tip and push from there.** The shared tree is then never the place the
content lives, so nobody can write over it and it can write over nobody.

## 2026-09-16 — THE CHARGES STEP CALCULATES. IT DOES NOT RENDER A QUOTE SOMEBODY ELSE MADE

The PO, looking at step 6 of the running wizard, asked why it says what it says:

> *"why youa re giving this messge - if charges are calculated you will ahve
> details"*

quoting the screen's own refusal — *"There is no quote on this build. A quote
arrives with an approved service request."* — and then ruled:

> *"so with chagres in - we have to fix this"*

### THE FAULT IS THE PREMISE, NOT THE WORDING

`NewConnectChargesStep.tsx` was built as a **renderer**. Its docstring says so —
*"the quote is the request's, and this screen prices nothing"* — and the premise
reaches the clerk in three places: *"These lines come from the request's quote and
are not re-priced here"*, *"This wizard was opened without a request, so there is
no quote to show"*, and the refusal above.

⚠ **SO A BUILD RAISED DIRECTLY CAN NEVER BE CHARGED. EVER.** That is not an edge
case. The New connects list carries a **From request** column that shows a **dash**
for directly-raised builds, and the blueprint's own caption reads *"either raised
directly or created by approving a request — and the list says which."* **Half the
doors into this wizard produce a build the charges step cannot price**, and the
screen calls that a normal state.

### THE DRAWING SAYS COUNTED, NOT ARRIVED

p090, in red, on the Charges page itself:

> *"Every quantity is counted from the services grid, not typed. Six units, twenty
> service points, one premise — change a tick on step 4 and these move with it."*

**The services grid is step 4 and exists on every build.** So a quote is computable
on any of them: **quantities from the grid, prices from the tenant's own charge
codes.** That is what makes it a calculation rather than a copy, and it is why the
step can show a figure with no application behind it.

### THE TWO PATHS, AND BOTH END IN THE SAME TABLE

| The build | What step 6 does |
|---|---|
| **Raised directly** | **counts** the quote from the grid and prices it from the utility's charge codes |
| **From an approved request** | **shows** the request's quote and does **not** re-price it — the drawing is explicit that *"changing a quantity would put the request and the build out of step"* |

### THE GUARD, AND IT IS HARD RULE 2

⚠ **IF THE SERVER CANNOT PRICE FROM THE GRID TODAY, THAT IS REPORTED AS A
MEASURED FACT — NOT SOLVED BY A CALCULATOR IN THE BROWSER.** Money is rounded
**once, on the server**. A total multiplied up in a screen is the second rounding
path `DEF-088` already removed, and here it would sit beside real figures on a
money screen. A lane that cannot find the pricing door **names it and stops**.

⚠ **AND THE PRICE IS NEVER TYPED.** A signed rule forbids a hand-typed amount
reaching a bill. Where a stored quote and the utility's price list disagree, the
path **refuses and shows both figures** rather than quietly choosing one.

### WHY THIS SURVIVED REVIEW, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING

**The refusal is honest, specific, and correct about its own premise** — which is
exactly what made it invisible. It reads as a well-built stated absence rather
than a missing capability, and it was approved as one. Nothing in this repo
compares a screen's stated precondition against the blueprint's sentence for the
same screen; the two live in different documents and no check reads either.
`DEF-CUS-5483`.

**The durable check is a walk that enters by EVERY DOOR the product says exists** —
here, a build raised directly and a build from an approved request. A screen that
works on one door and refuses on the other passes every test written from the
working one.

## 2026-09-16 — THE DEPOSIT IS THE OWNER'S OR THE TENANT'S, DECIDED ONCE, AND IT NEVER MOVES BETWEEN THEM

`OQ-BIL-12381` closed by the PO the day it was minted. Verbatim:

> *"we can go with b - but we need to give clark an option all or none - it means
> either we will charge ensite diposte ot inwer at the time of request or we will
> hcharge it to tenant later - we cannot do the transfer f depsotes later"*

### THE RULE

**One choice, for the whole build, made once:**

| The clerk chooses | At the build | At move-in |
|---|---|---|
| **The owner pays** | **every unit's deposit** is charged to the owner, all of it | **the tenant is asked for nothing** |
| **The tenant pays** | **nothing is charged** | each tenant pays their own deposit, as today |

⚠ **ALL OR NONE — THERE IS NO PER-UNIT MIX.** A build where units 1–3 are the
owner's and 4–6 are the tenants' is not offerable. The PO's words are *"all or
none"*, and it is the whole of what makes this cheap: one flag on the build
rather than a deposit state per unit.

⚠ **AND THERE IS NO TRANSFER, EVER.** This is the clause that narrows option (B)
as it was put to the PO — that version said the owner's deposit would be
*"released or transferred as each tenant arrives"*. **The PO refused the transfer
outright.** A deposit taken from the owner **stays the owner's**; it is never
moved to a tenant's account when they move in, and a tenant never inherits one.
**Money held for one party does not become money held for another because
somebody moved in.**

### WHERE IT SITS, AND IT IS NOT REVENUE

A deposit is **money we owe back** — a **liability at `2300`**, never revenue at
`4600`. Taking it from the owner changes **who** we owe it to and nothing else
about its shape. `BR-RAT-020` and `BR-RAT-023` keep the AMOUNT on the plan's
deposit rules, and those rules *"explicitly supersede a flat deposit charge"* —
so **the owner path may not become a charge code on the quote.** It reads the same
per-unit policy the tenant path reads, and totals it.

### ⚠ THE ONE CONSEQUENCE A LANE WILL MISS, AND IT COLLECTS TWICE

**Move-in must know the deposit was already taken and must not ask again.** A unit
whose deposit the owner paid at the build has a satisfied deposit requirement; the
move-in wizard's deposit step reads the per-unit policy and would ask the tenant
for it as a matter of course. **Nothing today tells it otherwise**, so the
straightforward build of this ruling collects the same deposit twice — once from
the developer and once from the first tenant — and the second one is a real
customer paying real money for something already held.

**So the owner path is not finished when the charge posts.** It is finished when
the move-in step can see that a unit's deposit is already held and says so.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT ANSWER, AND IS NOT BEING ASSUMED

**When the owner gets their money back.** With no transfer, the deposit sits
against the owner's account until something releases it — the unit closing, the
building being sold, a refund somebody asks for. The PO ruled how it is COLLECTED
and said nothing about how it is RETURNED, and a liability with no stated release
is a balance that grows for ever. **Not invented here; raised when the path is
built.**

## 2026-09-16 — STEP 5 LOSES THE PLAN AND GAINS AN ADD; STEP 6 COUNTS WHAT IT CANNOT YET PRICE

**Built by** the New Connect step 5/6 lane · **Version** `2.278.1` · **Commit** `746f8764`
· **Closes** `DEF-CUS-5482`, `DEF-CUS-5483` · **Files** `DEF-CUS-5485`, `DEF-BIL-5486`,
`OQ-CUS-12391`

### What the PO said, and what was built

> *"now on this step we should show work order already selected from allow user to add
> few more work order - plans are not required here"*
> *"on charges - nothing is calcualted - i dont know how you cloed this"*

Step 5 no longer asks for the plan — step 2 does, and step 2's coverage warning was
**read in that file before this one dropped its copies** rather than assumed to have
survived. The step, its page head and its rail label read *Work orders* in all eleven
catalogues. A clerk can now ADD a work order from the utility's own published templates;
until today the list was remove-only and the draft carried only
`removedWorkOrderTemplateIds`.

Step 6 counts. `per unit`, `per meter` and `per premise` come off step 4's grid and move
with it — walked in a browser at 1280 and 1440, a six-dwelling build on electric, water
and sewer reads **6 · 14 · 1**, and the same build reads **0 · 0 · 1** before a service is
ticked. That is p090's own red sentence made real: *"Every quantity is counted from the
services grid, not typed."*

### Three judgments, recorded because the rules ran out

**1 · THE SCREEN PRINTS NO MONEY, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.**
p090 draws a CHARGE, DESCRIPTION, UNIT and AMOUNT column and a `Quoted` total, and every
one of those is money. `charge_code_line` forbids a caller computing it, in its own words:
*"A caller that multiplied first and handed in a product would be the second rounding path
this comment exists to prevent, which is why there is no amount parameter for it to arrive
through."* The function that WOULD serve this screen exists and says so —
`price_quote_bill`, *"the screen shows a clerk the lines and the total BEFORE the button
that writes"* — but it takes an `account_id`, and `BR-MET-112` says a draft build has no
account until step 8. **Measured, not assumed:** `POST /billing/one-time/preview` is the
only priced preview served over HTTP, needs the same account, and takes ONE charge code
with no quantity; `rating.Charge` has no basis column and no new-connection role, so
nothing declares WHICH code is counted per unit. The gap is a missing DOOR and is filed as
`DEF-BIL-5486`, not papered over with a browser multiply. The drawn `$3,030.00` is an
illustration (B14 rule 37) and is not printed; a browser check asserts no currency symbol
reaches the screen at all.

**2 · THE DRAWN PAYMENT CAPTURE IS REFUSED BY NAME RATHER THAN DRAWN DEAD.**
`POST /connections/commit` accepts exactly four quote fields — `quote_payer`,
`quote_due_days`, `quote_posting_date`, `quote_total` — and none of them is a payment. So
*Take payment · Method · Reference · Amount taken · Clearing date* and the whole *Payment
summary* would each be a box whose value is discarded at commit. Hard-won law 2, and this
repo paid for eight such controls on one portal page in one day.

**3 · THE COMMON AREA'S PLAN IS AN OPEN QUESTION, NOT A FALLBACK.** Removing step 5's
second picker leaves `planCommonArea` unset, so a common area commits with
`tariff_id: null`. The tempting fix — inherit the dwellings' plan — is a money decision: a
common area takes electric and water and **no sewer**, so a dwelling tariff would price a
hallway on a plan nobody chose. Nothing was chosen; `OQ-CUS-12391` states the three
answers with their costs.

### And the thing that turns the whole money path on

`DEF-CUS-5485`. The commit has accepted `quote_due_days` since `CR-109` and **no caller in
the product sent it** — `fee_bill.raise_quote_bill` says so in its own docstring — so
every real commit took the `quote_payment_terms_not_captured` branch and raised no charge,
over a path proved on real PostgreSQL (10 passed: invoice `BL-2609-000082` at `$800.00`,
`DR 1200 800.0000` against `CR 4600 270.0000` and `CR 4630 530.0000`). Step 6 asks for the
terms and the posting date now, and `commitPlanOf` sends all three. **There is no default
and there must not be:** `BR-BIL-024` derives a due date from a cycle's days, a build's
bill has no cycle, and the PO ruled on 2026-08-23 that a clerk captures the terms and
nobody guesses them — a guessed number starts a late-fee clock on a real invoice.

### Two lane collisions caught at push time, both by guards rather than by care

`DEF-CUS-5484` was allocated for the charges divergence and **a sibling pushed
`DEF-INT-5484` while this lane worked**; `allocate.py defect --verify` caught it in the
same breath as the blob re-derivation. Re-reading the tip's register then showed
`DEF-CUS-5483` already held this lane's exact defect, filed by another lane the same hour,
so the duplicate row was dropped and every citation re-pointed rather than a second row
filed. Separately, `push_paths.sh` REFUSED the first push because the defect register had
moved between this lane's editing base and the tip — the guard working, and the reason
nothing of four siblings' rows was subtracted.

## 2026-09-16 · `BR-INT-002`'s `Connect` half is superseded: the card opens a SCREEN, not the modal (`DEF-INT-5513`, `CR-110-BRC04`, `2.283.1`)

**The PO, from the deployed product, verbatim:**

> *"we have mereged and deployed new version. it is still saying integration only and it
> is still showing modal - i think routing issue - it is not reolsved"*

**They were right and their diagnosis was right.** `CR-110-BRC04` wave A built, routed
and tested the connector set-up screen — **S147 · INT-07**, at
`/:tenant/settings/connectors/:providerKey/configure` — and **nothing in the product
linked to it.** It was reachable only by typing the address, on all 28 connectors. The
card's primary control went on calling `onOpen(card, "connect")` and mounting
`ConnectModal`.

**What was ruled, and by what.** `BR-INT-002` is CONFIRMED law from 2026-08-07 and says
*"Every integration card opens the connect modal"*. Its **`Connect` half is superseded**
by the Integration Blueprint and by the report above; the rest stands. This was not put
back to the PO (hard-won law 13): they had already ruled it, in the sentence above, and
the drawing they supplied settles the shape.

**The drawing, read as an IMAGE (B14 rule 42), not inferred.** CON-01's own legend row
for the control reads *"New — the form has an address now, so a connected card can
reopen it"*, and every CFG frame is drawn as a **PAGE** carrying that connector's own
configure address in its header — `CFG-01` at
`/:tenant/settings/connectors/email_microsoft/configure` (p021) and `CFG-02` at
`…/email_google/configure` (p023) — each with a `← Connectors` back link, the accent
*Connection details* panel, the connector's full field set, an *API on this connector*
table and a *Save and test* footer.

**The worked figure, in plain English:** on the deployed build, pressing **Connect** on
Microsoft 365 opened a dialog and the address bar never changed. On `2.283.1` it opens
`/brazosbend/settings/connectors/email_microsoft/configure`, headed *Microsoft 365*,
with *Sign in with Microsoft 365* and its one API listed. Four connectors of four
different auth shapes were walked in a browser and each landed on **its own** page;
**28 of 28** now have a door, where **0 of 28** did.

**What did NOT move, deliberately.** The modal is not retired — it still serves
**Manage**, **Fix it**, **Disconnect** and the test that needs a typed recipient
(`BR-INT-026`), whose screens do not exist yet. A *coming soon* card and a card with no
adapter keep their **disabled** buttons and their reasons: turning a ruled refusal into
a link would send a clerk to a form for a connector that cannot be set up. A read-only
role keeps a disabled `<Button>` rather than a link, because a `<Link>` cannot be
disabled and `BR-SHL-025` requires the role's reason to be on the control.

**Nothing was renamed.** *"it is still saying integration only"* is the **rename wave**
and stays held — 319 catalogue entries and the routes must move in one act or every
existing link breaks. The set-up screen's back link says *Connectors* and the grid says
*Integrations*; both were left.

**Where it is written:** `04-docs/05-modules/13-integrations/02-business-rules.md`
(`BR-INT-002`, now CONFIRMED-AS-AMENDED 2026-09-16, with the PO's words and the date in
the source column) · `CR-110-BRC04-connectors.md`, the `DEF-INT-5513` maintenance
section · the defect register (`DEF-INT-5513` fixed; `DEF-INT-5521` opened for the
modal's now-orphaned connect mode) · and the code's own header.

**The durable part, and it is not about connectors.** The two halves of this were each
tested at their OWN address — wave A's route test asserts the screen is REGISTERED, the
grid's suite asserts the control FIRES ITS HANDLER — and *"does the button open the
screen we built"* belonged to neither file. The new assertion is made **from the card's
side** and pins the **address AND the screen id it resolves to**, so a later lane moving
the screen turns the grid's own suite red. **When you land a screen something was
waiting for, grep for the control that was holding its place** — the blueprint had even
named the symptom, *"Set up has no door"*, and the door was built without moving the
handle.

## 2026-09-16 · `CR-110-BRC04` phase 2 waves 0 and 1 — the fourth operation, the reference endpoint, and the ninth check (`2.284.0`)

**Ruled by the PO on 2026-09-16, and built here.** Four of the ten rulings in the
CR's PHASE 2 section reach code in this wave; six belong to the three lanes that
follow.

### The judgment calls the rules did not make, each with its worked figure

**1 · THE ADDRESS IS `/api/{utility}/partner/v1/…` AND THE CR'S OWN SHORTHAND
SAYS `/api/partner/v1/…`. THE UTILITY SEGMENT STAYS.** The PO's ruling was
*"why aclarian in it - we cna make it generic - saying partner - so that we can
give it to anyone who needs bills for any csutomer if autherised"*, and that is
honoured exactly: no vendor name appears in any of the five addresses, and SAP,
Workday, Infor, MSGP and Aclarian all dial the same four. What is NOT dropped is
the utility slug, because `BR-TEN-003` reads the tenant from the PATH and from
nothing else, and with no tenant context RLS `FORCE` returns **zero rows for
every key including a valid one** — the door would be incapable of passing
(hard-won law 7's third shape), and the only way to make it pass would be to
read the tenant from a parameter, which is the rule. The 2026-09-06 decision-log
row already settled this for `v1/payments`; this extends it rather than
reopening it, and the divergence is recorded in the CR's own table.

**2 · `company_id` IS COMPARED AND THROWN AWAY.** PO: *"company_id = tenant
id"*. It is required on **every** partner route, not only `reference`; a
mismatch is `403` with `COMPANY_MISMATCH` and **echoes neither id**, because a
`403` that printed *you sent X, we are Y* would be a probe for real utility ids
on the one route a partner calls with one in hand. It is distinguishable from
the one refusal, and that is safe for a single stated reason and no other: it is
reachable only by a caller that has already passed checks 1–6, so it holds a
live key for a live utility. The same argument the two `429` codes rest on, and
no wider.

**3 · `CODE_UTILITY_INACTIVE` IS THE NINTH REFUSAL CODE AND IT EXTENDS THE PO'S
TABLE RATHER THAN SUPERSEDING IT.** The eight were the PO's 2026-09-16 ruling
*"go with your recommendation - implment all these code"*, taken over the causes
that existed that morning. Their OTHER ruling of the same day — *"you have to
also check whether connector is activae whether tenant is active"* — adds a
CAUSE, and a cause with no code is the thing that ruling was about. It falls on
the RECORD-ONLY side of the split the recommendation already set, because a
distinct code on the wire would answer *does this utility exist and is it
switched on* to anyone holding any key: `BR-INT-044`'s enumeration oracle
pointed at the tenant instead of at the credential.

**4 · *ACTIVE* MEANS `deleted_at IS NULL AND provisioned_at IS NOT NULL`, AND
TENANCY OWNS THE SENTENCE.** It is the same predicate `live_tenant_subdomains`
already uses, published as `tenancy.selectors.tenant_is_live` and reached
through `integrations/seams/tenancy.py` — a second copy in the door would part
company with the first the moment either moved (`DEF-094`'s shape). **The
`provisioned_at` half is what this check actually adds:** the path resolver
filters `deleted_at` and nothing else, so a signup that stopped half-way
resolves, sets a tenant context, and would have served a partner key issued
against it.

**5 · THE SEAM ANSWERS `False` WHERE ITS TWO NEIGHBOURS ANSWER `None`.**
`today()` and `job()` in that file return the honest third answer and let their
callers decide. This one is a GUARD on a door an outside company presents a key
at, so its third answer is **no** — a read that raised, a tenancy that published
nothing, a malformed id. Same reasoning as `rate_limit_store` having no
`allow_on_error`.

**6 · FOUR OPERATIONS AT SIXTY IS 240 A MINUTE AGAINST A STOLEN KEY, AND THE
FIGURE IS WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE NOTICED.** The window is per
connection AND per operation (blueprint p017), so adding the fourth read raised
the aggregate from 180 to 240. Sixty is kept uniform because the ledger is the
largest set and is the one the arithmetic was computed for: a 200,000-row ledger
month is **200 pages at 1,000 a page, three and a half minutes at sixty a
minute**. A per-operation ceiling reads like a total and is not one.

**7 · THE REFERENCE ENDPOINT IS NOT AN OPERATION, SO IT IS NOT A FIFTH SCREEN
ROW.** The PO ruled FOUR API rows and *no scope tick*. A fifth operation would
put a fifth tick beside *What they may read* for a document that carries no
utility's records. It is metered under its own window (100 a minute, the product
default, for a document a partner pulls once and caches) and recorded like every
other partner read. The scope GUARD still bites — a key that may call nothing
may not read the description of what it may call.

**8 · AN UNBUILT ADDRESS ANSWERS `501` AND NAMES ITS WAVE.** Not `404`, which is
this surface's refusal and reads as *your key is bad*; and above all not
`{"records": [], "total_records": 0}`, which reads to a finance system as **this
utility issued no bills** and would be posted as such. **A missed bill is a
missed GL entry and nothing on either side would raise.** All eight checks run
first, so a declared-but-unbuilt address is not a hole in the door.

**9 · `LINE_KINDS` WAS MINTED BECAUSE THE VOCABULARY ONLY EXISTED AS A
COMMENT.** `# usage | base | fee | tax | adjustment | minimum` on
`InvoiceLine.kind` — six words after a `#`, which nothing can read and nothing
can check. Retyping it into the reference endpoint would have been a seventh
place for the set to drift (hard-won law 1). It is a tuple in
`apps/billing/models.py` now and the column's comment points at it.

### Two defects the drawn columns already had, found by building on them

`DEF-INT-5524` — the connection screen showed **100** where the door enforces
**60**, because `_operation_row` called `rate_limit_for(connection)` with no
operation and the manifest's declared default is that function's third source,
reachable only when the operation is passed. The PO ruled this limit uneditable
from the product, which makes that one screen the only place a wrong number can
be noticed, and it was wrong there.

`DEF-INT-5522` — the ENDPOINT column could never show anything for the whole
`they_hold_ours` quadrant, because a partner connector has no vendor host: the
address on the row is ours. `DEF-INT-5502`'s fix made the column work for
connectors we DIAL and left the ones that dial US exactly as they were.

### A red that outlived both its owners

`DEF-INT-5523` (fixed) — `Operation.rate_limit_per_minute` was declared **twice** in one
dataclass and the `< 1` validation was written **twice** in one validator, by
waves C and D, each unaware of the other. The duplicate field was harmless
(same type, same default, the second silently wins) and its two comment blocks
said two different things. The duplicate CHECK was not harmless:
`test_cr110__a_ceiling_of_nothing_is_refused_by_name` had been **RED and unread
since wave D**, on a message mismatch and never on the rule — a zero-ceiling
manifest was refused correctly the whole time. Dated with
`git log -S "is a door that is shut, not a limit"`, which names `346d4c47`
(wave D) against `72868434` (wave C, which wrote the test). Fixed here on this
CR's own principle: *a red that outlives its owner belongs to whoever is still
here*.

**Two further reds are pre-existing and are NOT fixed here**, dated by running
`tests/test_be_default_authentication.py` against the pinned tip `c800881f` in a
clean worktree with no lane's work in it: both cases fail there, on 58 portal
routes carrying a third authenticator class and 83 routes declaring `AllowAny`.
`CLAUDE.md` already records this test as red since 2026-09-04. The five new
partner addresses appear in neither list — they are named in `PUBLIC_ROUTES`,
which is what `partner_api.py`'s own docstring instructs.

## 2026-09-16 · `CR-110-BRC04` phase 2 wave 2 — the Customer API serves ACCOUNTS, and its address is the building's (`2.285.0`)

**The ruling being built** — PO 2026-09-16, verbatim, two of the ten on this CR:
*"Customers = accounts"* and *"send service address"*.

**What was decided here, because the rules ran out and nothing was put back to
the PO** (hard-won law 13 — a judgment recorded with its reasoning is the
deliverable; a question is the failure to make one):

**1 · `id` is the ACCOUNT NUMBER and the supplied document says otherwise.**
Aclarian's reference prints `"id": 1001`. We serve `"id": "A-10432"`, which is
`consumer_no` repeated. `seams/billing.as_record` already states the rule for
this whole surface — *"a partner keyed on our uuid is coupled to our storage
forever"* — and B14 rule 31 says the same one layer out. The worked figure a
person can check: on the live demo tenant the first record reads
`{"id": "A-10432", "consumer_no": "A-10432", "customer_name": "Miller, Sarah"}`
where the document would have had us print `01a0aa4a-0f7f-7618-b669-…`. **This
is a recorded divergence and not a silent choice**; if the PO wants their
vendor's shape, the change is one line and this row is what it supersedes.

**2 · One `address` per ACCOUNT, and it is the BUILDING's — so two accounts in
one building read the same line.** Hard rule 8 says an address lives on
`premises` and *a unit refines a premises by LABEL, not by address*. So the
partner's `address` is the premises' street line plus its locality and carries
no unit label. **The worked figure: 84 accounts on the live demo tenant resolve
to 71 distinct addresses — thirteen share a building with another account**,
because they are units of it. That is the truth about the building rather than a
collision: the partner matches on `consumer_no`, which is unique per tenant, and
**no other surface in this product puts a unit label inside a service address**
either — `billing/statement.py`'s `{service_address}` token and `ACC-02` R5's
Service address row both compose without one. Composing `"1408 Elm Street ·
Unit B"` here would have been this product's only place that treats a label as
part of an address, on the one surface where somebody else's books depend on it.

**3 · The Customer API takes no `since`/`until`, where bills, payments and the
ledger all do.** This CR records the paging trap — paging by page number over a
moving table skips rows — and it is a rule about a set sorted NEWEST FIRST,
where an arriving row pushes later rows across a page boundary. Accounts are
ordered by `account_no` ASCENDING; it is unique within a tenant
(`ux_accounts_no`) and allocated from the tenant's monotonic series
(`BR-TEN-035`), so a new account lands AFTER any cursor a partner has passed,
and no account number is reused or deleted (every FK onto `accounts` is
`PROTECT`). A date window could therefore only HIDE a row, never save one. **The
one case that can still insert mid-order is named rather than waved away** — an
import that supplies its own account numbers — **and `total_records` in the
envelope is the answer to it**: the partner's job compares what it pulled with
what we said existed rather than trusting it reached the end. Measured live:
`{"total_records": 84, "page": 28, "page_size": 3, "total_pages": 28}`.

**4 · An account whose premises will not resolve is SERVED with
`address: null`.** Three ordinary states produce it, and the `customers 0036`
column comment names one of them itself. Dropping the record would move
`total_records` and leave the partner reconciling a shortfall it cannot explain;
fabricating an address would have it reconcile consumption against the wrong
property, which is worse. Zero such accounts exist on the live demo tenant
today, which is exactly why the case is in the fixture rather than left to be
met by a customer.

**5 · The status label is read from the ACCOUNT'S OWN joined lookup row, not
from the reference endpoint's list.** Both are `account_statuses` and both apply
`str(name or code)`, and a test asserts they agree code-for-code for every
active status. The difference is one real case: the reference endpoint filters
`active=True`, and an account may still hold a status a clerk has since
deactivated — built from the list, that account's label would be missing. Read
from the row it is right, and because the PO ruled every coded field ships
inline as `{code, label}`, the partner resolves it anyway.

**What was NOT decided here and is somebody's:** `DEF-INT-5539` — the published
specification offers `from`/`to` on this route, which it does not read. The
parameter loop is one block shared by four routes with three lanes live in that
file within the hour (law 11), so it is filed rather than fixed in passing.

## 2026-09-16 · `CR-110-BRC04` phase 2 waves 3 and 4 — the nested bill, the payment, and the phase-1 pair retired (`2.287.0`)

**The rulings built here are the PO's own, quoted in the CR section.** What
follows is the seven judgments this lane made where the rulings ran out, each
with the figure that decided it, so the next agent builds the same thing.

**1 · `replaces` is on EVERY bill record, `null` when it replaces nothing.** The
supplied document annotates it *present only on a bill that replaces one*. A
finance system pairing a correction cannot tell a key we OMITTED from a bill
that replaces nothing — the same *missing versus empty* confusion this surface
already answers `501` to rather than an empty list. **How it is derived was not
invented:** `invoices.corrects_invoice` is a self-FK that lives on the
REPLACEMENT and points back, by the PO's ruling of 2026-08-12 closing `OQ-120`
(*"Nod to add the link on the new bill"*), UNIQUE per original so the chain is a
chain and never a tree. Proved live: `BL-2607-000041` carries
`replaces: "BL-2607-000029"` and that bill comes back in the same page as
`corrected`.

**2 · A bill line carries `unit` beside `quantity`, and the document has no such
field.** CLAUDE.md hard rule 3 — consumption is always stated with an explicit
unit. The live payload carries `kWh` and `kgal`; a partner reading gallons where
we meant thousands of gallons is wrong by a factor of a thousand.

**3 · The payment's four coded fields map onto our four payment vocabularies —
`type`→`payments.type`, `projectType`→`payments.purpose`,
`tenderType`→`payment_methods`, `paymentPayType`→`payments.status`.** ⚠ **THE
VENDOR'S DOCUMENT IS NOT IN THIS REPO**, so what each name MEANS in Aclarian's
world is written nowhere we hold and this mapping is OURS. It is recorded rather
than inferred because each is a one-line change in one place if the partner's
engineer says otherwise. It does NOT reopen `BR-INT-054`: what Runbooks owns is
the TRANSLATION — our *Bank transfer* into their `ACHCHECK` — and
`serve.partner_fields()` is still empty, with the case that asserts so kept.

**4 · `reference.py` grows three vocabularies, seven keys to TEN.** Without
`paymentType`, `projectType` and `paymentPayType` a partner that cached the
document meets `paymentPayType: cleared` with nothing to resolve it against,
which is the exact failure the PO commissioned the endpoint to prevent.

**5 · The phase-1 flat pair is RETIRED with `410`, not upgraded in place, and
one measured fact decided it: `amount` CHANGED MEANING.** On the flat record it
was THE BILL'S OWN TOTAL; on the nested record it is THE ACCOUNT'S BALANCE NOW,
and the bill's total is `bill_amount`. One key, two meanings, and a finance
system cannot see the difference — it would go on posting a receivable from a
field that had quietly started answering a different question. `410` rather than
`404` because a `404` here is the REFUSAL and a partner would go looking at its
credentials for an address that is finished; the body names the replacement, and
it authenticates FIRST so a retirement notice is not an *this utility exists*
oracle. **The two suites that drove those routes moved onto the phase-2
addresses rather than being deleted with them** — every case in them is about
the door or the key, not the payload.

**6 · `accountString` on a PAYMENT is the tender's `clearing_gl_account_id`, and
`null` when the tender is unmapped.** The receipt leg falls back to the
`undeposited_funds` designation in that case, and publishing that fallback here
would be this seam stating a posting decision it did not make, free to disagree
with the ledger the day either moves. All seven of the demo tenant's tenders map
to `1010`, so the live payload carries a code on every row.

**7 · The three balance clocks are read from three different places, and
`before` is READ FROM THE BILL'S OWN STAMP rather than recomputed.**
`balance_forward` is written at issue (`BR-BIL-035`) into `bill_payload`, which
the immutability trigger freezes — so the figure a partner is given is the
figure PRINTED on the document the customer holds. A recomputation would drift
from it the moment anything else moved, and the partner and the customer would
be holding two different bills. An unreachable figure is `null`, never `0.00`.

**Measured, not asserted:** 81 collectable bills on the demo tenant, all 81
reconciling (Σ lines == `bill_amount`); **0 of 640 served lines carry a null GL
account** — the seven that do are all on the one DRAFT, which never leaves; five
bills with all three clocks different; 66 payments; the page answering in 0.35s.

**Three defects filed with their arithmetic:** `DEF-INT-5545` (four ERP
manifests declare no `served_path`, so their specification now advertises the
retired pair), `DEF-INT-5542` (`open_balances_for_accounts` costs one
`SUM(allocations)` per invoice — 17 statements for one bill, 21 for five,
~4s extrapolated for a 1,000-row page), `DEF-INT-5543`
(`COLLECTABLE_STATUSES` names two payment statuses that do not exist).

## 2026-09-16 · The utility leaves the partner URL, and the key resolves it (`DEF-INT-5546`, `CR-110-BRC04` phase 2)

**The PO, having been shown the five partner addresses as built, verbatim:**
*"thi si wromg - we agreed not to use utility names in partner apis that was our
rule - so these urls are not corect - we will resolve utility name using keys...
please confirm your understanding"*.

They were right, and the repo already agreed with them. Blueprint p159 is titled
**WHY NOT PUT IT IN THE PATH** and carries the diagram in four arrows:

    key ──► connection ──► tenant ──► app.tenant_id set ──► RLS does the isolating

### What was built, and the reasoning that built it

The five addresses were mounted inside the tenant include as
`/api/{utility}/partner/v1/…`. The lane that built them **deviated from the
drawing deliberately and recorded the deviation**, on this argument:
`BR-TEN-003` reads the tenant from the path; with no tenant context RLS `FORCE`
returns zero rows for the credential lookup — for a valid key exactly as for an
invented one — so the door would be *incapable of passing* (hard-won law 7's
third shape).

**Every clause of that is true, and the conclusion does not follow.** It is true
of a TENANT table, and it only forces the utility into the URL if the FIRST
lookup has to be against one. The drawing's first arrow says it does not.

I then repeated that justification to the PO as settled, which is how a lane's
reasoning becomes the product's rule. The defect row carries the durable lesson:
**when a lane records a deviation from a drawing, the review question is not
whether its reasoning is sound but whether the drawing already answers it.**

### What is built now

`integration_key_directory` (migration `integrations/0011`) — one row per issued
key, holding the key's one-way fingerprint, the utility it was issued by, and
the two ids that name its rows. **It is not a tenant table and carries no RLS
policy**, which is the whole of why it works: a partner request arrives with a
key and nothing else, and this is the one table readable at that moment.
`key_directory.open_utility_for` reads it and opens the utility; the five views
then run unchanged.

**THE EXEMPTION IS NOT A NEW IDEA — `sessions` HAS BEEN ON B2 §3's NO-RLS LIST
SINCE W0 FOR THE IDENTICAL REASON.** `/api/jobs/{id}` and `/api/exports` carry
no utility either; `core.tenancy.adopt_session_tenant` reads the session row and
opens the utility it names, and its own docstring states the principle: *"the
cookie selects a row, the row states the tenant. Adopting it is not client
input."* A bearer key is the same shape.

**AND `sessions` QUIETLY DISPROVED B2 §3's OWN TEST, WHICH NOBODY HAD SAID.**
The brief states *"a table belongs here when it has NO `tenant_id`"* — and
`identity.Session` has carried a `tenant_id` since W0 and has been exempt just
as long. §3 now records **two** tests instead of one: no `tenant_id` at all, or
*its whole job is to resolve the tenant, so a policy on it could only ever be
checked against an answer it has not given yet*. Class two is exactly two
tables. `DEF-TEN-4446`'s mistake — a table that merely SOUNDED platform-ish —
is a different thing and is not widened by this.

### BR-TEN-003 is CLARIFIED, not superseded — and the clarification is that it
### never said what the code said it said

The rule's own words are **"never client input."** Three places paraphrased that
as *"the tenant is read from the PATH and from nothing else"* — the middleware,
`runners/serve.py` and `partner_api.py` — and the paraphrase is narrower than
the rule in the one direction that matters. Nothing was reversed here; a rule was
read through a code comment's summary of it instead of being read. That is the
same failure shape as B14's rule-count pointer, in a different family.

Three resolvers are lawful and the product has always had two: the path's slug
against `tenants`; the session row on the platform paths; and now an issued key
against `integration_key_directory`. All three read something WE wrote. None
reads a tenant id a caller sent. **A fourth is a decision, not a convenience.**

### What did NOT change, which is most of the argument

Nothing in `runners/serve.py`'s door. By the time `resolve_caller` runs,
`app.tenant_id` is set exactly as it would be on a path-resolved route; the
credential lookup is scoped by RLS exactly as before; and TC-5 and TC-7 remain
properties of the database rather than lines of code. **The directory decides
which door to open and nothing else** — a row naming the wrong utility buys an
attacker nothing, because the credential lookup under that utility would not
find the key and the caller is refused in the ordinary way.

`company_id` stays accepted and stays VERIFIED, never used to select. With the
segment gone it is the last value on a partner request that names a utility,
which is why `test_a_key_cannot_claim_the_other_utility` exists.

One hunk in the locked file, and it gates a RECORDED CAUSE rather than the
refusal: an unknown key now resolves no utility, so `utility_is_live(None)` is
correctly `False` — and writing `UTILITY_INACTIVE` down for it would tell a
manager their utility is switched off when the truth is that we never worked out
which utility the caller meant.

### The phase-1 pair did not move

`/api/{utility}/v1/payments` and `/v1/billing` still serve the flat
`US-INT-041` payload from inside the tenant include. Different address,
different payload shape, their own retirement schedule; moving them in the same
commit would have made one change look like two.

### Timing, because this surface is measured in milliseconds

`open_utility_for` spends **two statements on every path, hit or miss** — it
runs before `resolve_caller` starts the clock `REFUSAL_FLOOR_S` pads against, so
whatever it costs is added on TOP of the floor rather than absorbed by it. A hit
that set the GUC while a miss set nothing would be one `set_config` round trip of
difference, measurable, and it would mean *your key is at least one we issued*.
So a miss CLEARS the context instead of leaving it alone — the same two
statements, and fail-closed in its own right.

## 2026-09-16 — the access-log panel keeps its WATCH note and does NOT grow a second Revoke button (`CR-110-BRC04`, `ACC-01`)

The *Who has been reading* panel was rebuilt to the Integration Blueprint's
`ACC-01` drawing (p99–p101) in `2.287.3`. Four of the drawing's elements moved
and are simply built. Three judgments are recorded here because the rules ran
out or collided, and law 13 says a judgment written down with its reasoning is
the deliverable.

### 1 · The three read states, and why this was never a design choice

**The panel said the same eleven words in three different situations.**
Measured in a browser on 2026-09-16, signed in as a System Admin on
`brazosbend`, against a build of this branch: while the read was in flight,
after a forced 500, and on `erp_workday` — a connected connector with genuinely
zero reads — the panel's text was **byte-identical**:

> Who has been reading / An access log, not a run history / **Nobody has
> collected anything yet.**

It now reads three different things: loading bars while the read is in flight,
*"The access log did not load / We cannot say whether anybody has read
anything."* with **Retry** when it failed, and *"Nobody has read anything /
This partner has a key and has not used it."* only when the read came back and
came back empty. No new endpoint and no new field — `isPending` and `isError`
were on the query object and unread. `DEF-INT-5484`, closed.

### 2 · The WATCH note stays on the screen, and the collision is asked

At the foot of the panel is a note saying *why the screen exists* — that
nothing else in the product would show a partner taking two years of history at
two in the morning. **B14 rule 33 says rationale is zero words on screen.**
`ACC-01` draws it, on a page stamped DRAWN TO THE RULES, and **B14 rule 41 says
the product matches the blueprint.**

**Decision: it ships as drawn**, in the quieter shape the drawing gives it — a
quote with a grey left rule, replacing the filled amber `ConsequenceBox` that
shipped. Taking a block the blueprint draws off the screen on this lane's own
reading of rule 33 would settle a collision between two of the PO's own
instructions silently, in the direction no drawing supports. **The collision is
`OQ-INT-12394`**, which is rule 41's own named case — *"the only thing that
reaches the PO is a drawing that contradicts a signed rule"*. Two lines at the
foot of one panel; reversible in five minutes either way.

### 3 · `Revoke the key` is NOT drawn here, because this page already has that door

`ACC-01` draws two buttons at the foot of the panel. Neither is built, and the
reason has CHANGED — which is why this is a decision and not an inherited note.

* **`Revoke the key`** is built, and it is on this same page. `ConnectionDetailPage`'s
  `ManagePanel` draws the keys table and a **Keys** link a few hundred pixels
  above this panel, and revoke lives behind a `ConfirmDialog` that spells out
  the consequence and lets a clerk choose **which** key — which a single button
  on a per-connection panel cannot do. A danger-tier control here would be two
  destructive doors onto one act on one screen, against B14 rule 4. **So it is
  not drawn, and the absence is stated in the panel's header** (B14 rule 32).
  Not filed as a defect: nothing is missing from the product.
* **`Allowed addresses`** has no endpoint, no screen and no field anywhere —
  the blueprint's own legend says so, *"the revoke endpoint exists; the
  allowlist one does not"*. A button here would open onto nothing, which is
  hard-won law 2's mirror. **Filed as `DEF-INT-5564`**, because unlike revoke
  this one IS a real product gap: a System Admin cannot see or change the
  addresses a partner key may call from.

### 4 · The failed block is composed in the panel, not taken from the kit

`ACC-01` draws **one** button on the failed state. The kit's `FailedWithRetry`
draws three, and its `onDownloadReport` and `onCancel` are **required** — so
**98 of its 102 call sites pass `() => undefined`** to the first, a live
*Download error report* button that downloads nothing. On a panel inside a page
*Cancel* cancels nothing either. Shipping three buttons where the drawing draws
one, two of them inert, on the one screen whose job is to raise an alarm, is
the defect this repo keeps refiling. **So the BLOCK is the drawing's and the
BUTTON is the kit's** (`Button`, `states.failed.retry`), which is what B14
rule 36 asks for. **The kit gap is `DEF-INT-5562`** — not worked around
silently, and not fixed here: `StateFrame.tsx` has 102 callers and two sibling
lanes are live on this branch.

## 2026-09-16 · `DEF-INT-5560` — VIEW-17 rebuilt from the drawing, and the ONE thing in it that was NOT changed

The Product Owner opened `/{tenant}/settings/integrations/erp_aclarian` on
`2.287.2`, put it beside the Integration Blueprint and said, verbatim: *"this
screen does not match with images in document - why?"*, then, after a
comparison chart: *"please fix all view screen in that case"*. The 28 connection
views are one component, so this is one file.

Built from `05-prototype/05 Integration Blueprint.pdf` p066–p067 (VIEW-17) and
p047–p048 (VIEW-10) **as images**, B14 rule 42 — the PDF text layer holds only
the frame captions, so there was never a shortcut here. Both VIEW frames are
`PROPOSED`, not signed, so under rule 41 nothing reached the PO.

**What moved:** the footer row to the bottom of the page, under a divider, with
the append-only footnote right-aligned beside the buttons · *Recent activity*
from a hand-written `<h2>` in 12px grey capitals to `<Panel>`'s own `<h3>` at
16px dark, which also puts the toolbar, the table and the pagination footer
inside the drawn box · the credential panel into the slot p047 draws it in ·
and two description sentences plus a dead `Test it now` button off the screen.

### The judgment: the EMPTY run history keeps the framework's block, with no toolbar and no column headers

This is the one place the rebuild deliberately does not follow the shape of the
drawing, and it is worth writing down because the opposite is the obvious move.

`BR-SHL-012` is **CONFIRMED** and says the framework owns the empty state, the
screen supplies only the empty-list copy, and there is **no empty table header
ever**; `DataTable` implements it by replacing the WHOLE table region — toolbar
included — when a list has nothing in it. Every `VIEW-` frame in the blueprint
is drawn POPULATED: there is no drawn empty state anywhere in the pack. So the
drawing and the signed rule do not disagree; the drawing is **silent**, and
where a drawing is silent the signed rule decides. Drawing a toolbar and four
column headers over nothing would make this the only screen in the product that
does, which is the drift B14 rule 36 exists to stop, and it would have to be
done by reaching past `DataTable` rather than through it.

**What DID change in the empty state** is the part no rule protected: the
`Test it now` button was wired to `onCta: () => undefined` — pressable, and
pressing it did nothing — with *"Test it from the card"* under it as its reason.
`EmptyList` has taken an optional `ctaLabel` since `DEF-MET-4764` precisely so
that an empty state with nothing honest to offer can draw no control at all,
and that is now what this one does. Nothing could have seen it: the prop HAD a
caller, so `G13` passed, and the words WERE in the DOM, so every text assertion
passed.

### What was left behind, on purpose

Three catalogue keys — `integrations.runs.intro`, `integrations.runs.empty.cta`
and `integrations.runs.empty.ctaReason` — now render to nobody. They are **not**
retired in this commit: retiring a key rewrites all eleven catalogues, and a
sibling lane holds eight uncommitted `integrations.*` keys in exactly those
files. Rewriting them would either destroy that lane's work on disk or publish
it in a pathspec commit — hard-won law 11, `DEF-168`'s mechanism five. Filed as
`DEF-INT-5561` with the tool and the moment to do it (`i18n_fanin.retire()`,
when the catalogues are quiet). `G18` already reports 435 unparked dead keys, so
three more would have vanished into a count nobody reads; the row names them.


## 2026-09-16 · A connector card counts its APIs instead of listing them (`DEF-INT-5528`, `CR-110-BRC04`, `2.287.5`)

### The ruling, verbatim

The Product Owner, looking at the connector grid:

> "on nepture - don show all apis on screen - it is breaking the size of the box
> - you canjust mention the number"

and again, having been sent a build that still listed them:

> "neptune list of all apis also not removed"

### The worked number

`meters_neptune360` declares **sixteen** operations, and the card drew one line
per operation, so Neptune's card stood sixteen lines tall beside neighbours four
lines tall. **This was the grid's default and not one bad card:** counted off the
registry, **10 of the 28 connectors declare more than three operations, 87
operations in total**. Neptune's card now reads ONE line, and on the seeded
utility that line is **`16 APIs · 0 working`** — the connector is refusing, so
every one of its sixteen operations is in a `not_working` state. Measured in the
browser across the whole grid: **87 operation lines before, 28 count lines
after**, and **zero `<li>` inside any card**.

### The drawing decided it, not us

Integration Blueprint **CON-01 p013** draws no per-API list on any card: every
card carries its state word, then one line of the form `3 APIs · 2 working`, and
a card nobody has tested carries a bare `2 APIs`. p014 gives the reason in its
own words — *"Neptune's card is sixteen operation lines tall beside neighbours
four lines tall (S8-1), and hiding the per-API lines is the one thing that makes
the grid scannable again"*. Read as an image, per B14 rule 42.

### `BR-INT-028` is NARROWED, not contradicted

`BR-INT-028` says each operation reports its own state *"not one word averaging
them"*, which had been read to forbid a state word on a multi-API card — the
code carried `card.operations.length > 1 ? null : <StateWord/>` on exactly that
reading. **The drawing shows the opposite**: p013's `Esri ArcGIS` has three APIs
and carries *● Not working*; p012's `Aclarian` has three under *● Reading from
us*. **`BR-INT-028` is PROPOSED and was never signed**, and B14 rule 41
(RATIFIED) says the product matches the blueprint exactly, so the drawing wins
and the narrowing is written into the rule's own row with its date. Had the rule
been signed this would have been a re-sign under HUMAN-GUIDE §6 and not an
amendment. The rest of the rule is untouched: each operation still HAS its own
state, and the connection view still draws every one of them as a table.

### The one judgment the drawing did not make

**When does the `· N working` half appear?** Two readings fit every card the
blueprint draws, and they part on a card it does not draw.

Counting alone — *show it when at least one API is working* — reproduces all
nine drawn cards, because `selectors.operation_state` cascades a connection's own
word onto every operation: a turned-off, not-set-up or never-tested connector has
nothing in a `working` state, so both readings print the bare `2 APIs` the
drawing shows.

They differ on **a tested connector whose APIs are ALL failing**. Counting prints
`3 APIs`, which is byte-identical to what an untested card says — the one
connector a clerk most needs to tell from *not tested yet* would look exactly
like it. So the rule shipped is **has this been tested**: the clause appears when
any operation is in a state a RUN produced (`working` or `not_working`), and that
card reads `3 APIs · 0 working`. The other direction is why the clause is omitted
at all — `· 0 working` on a connector nobody has tried reads as a failure, which
is the opposite of *not tested*.

### What was wrong with the test that was there

The old `TC-3` asserted `toContain("Account lookup")` — it **required** the
per-API list, so this defect could not be fixed without that test going red. It
is the shape this same file already records at `DEF-INT-3721`: a test holding a
wireframe artefact in place. Its one surviving assertion, `data-operations="3"`,
sat on the old `<ul>` and sits on the new `<p>`, so it is true either way and
could never have caught this.

### Not done, and filed rather than left

p013 draws a **coming-soon** card carrying `1 API` (`Single sign-on`, under
*Coming soon · v2*); the code still suppresses the line on those cards.
**Measured in the browser on the seeded utility: 12 of the 28 cards are
coming-soon and show no API line, and all 16 live cards show one.** That is a
line ADDED to cards the Product Owner did not complain about, so it is filed as
**`DEF-INT-5566`** rather than folded into this fix.

## 2026-09-17 · `CON-01` BECOMES A TABLE — the grid is overridden, and the actions cell is four icons (`CR-110-BRC04`)

**Three rulings, all from the Product Owner on 2026-09-17, recorded together
because they are one screen and the second two only make sense once the first
has landed.** Written BEFORE a line of TSX, per the build process step W.

### 1 · Grid → table, and there is no toggle

> *"we are overriding the deciion and converting it form Grid -> Table - table only"*

**"Table only" is the load-bearing half.** It is not a table view added beside
the cards; the cards GO. No grid/table toggle is built, and nothing keeps a
per-viewer memory of which one a clerk last had, because there is only one.

### ⚠ WHAT THIS SUPERSEDES, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED (law 13)

**B14 rule 41 (RATIFIED) says the product matches the blueprint EXACTLY**, and
the Integration Blueprint draws `CON-01` as a card grid on p011–p013. It did not
merely omit a table — **it considered one and declined to draw it**, on p014, in
its own words, read as an image per B14 rule 42:

> *"If you would rather have a real table view behind a grid/table toggle, that
> is a different and larger change. Say so and I will draw it."*

The PO has now said so. **A PO ruling overrides a blueprint**, and under law 13
the supersession is STATED and never left to be inferred, so it is written here,
in the CON-01 conformance record, and in `IntegrationsTab.tsx`'s own header.

⚠ **The blueprint's `S8-1` reasoning is not refuted — it is answered.** p014
argues the column selector matters *"because Neptune's card is sixteen operation
lines tall beside neighbours four lines tall … hiding the per-API lines is the
one thing that makes the grid scannable again"*. A table makes every row one
line tall by construction, so the problem p014 solves with a control, the table
solves with its shape. `DEF-INT-5528` had already collapsed Neptune's sixteen
lines to one `16 APIs · 14 working`; this ruling finishes the same thought.

⚠ **AND ONE THING THE BLUEPRINT DRAWS CANNOT SURVIVE THE MOVE.** A card carries
a per-connector SUMMARY SENTENCE (*"Collect readings and keep the meter list in
step."*), and a sentence in a cell sets the height of its whole row — which is
the failure `tableTypes.ts` documents at length and which the PO found ten times
in one sitting on 2026-08-30. The sentence is NOT given a column. It is kept in
the DOM on the Connector cell's `title`, so it is still reachable by a pointer
and by a screen reader, and it is still the first thing on the connector's own
screen. The provenance flags (`NEW CONNECTOR` · `RENAMED`) were never built and
are not built now.

### 2 · The actions cell is FOUR icons, fixed, and the STATUS changes which are live

> *"Action im looking for - Connect, View, Edit, Keys- based on this status will chnage"*

**and, having read the matrix below back in full:**

> *"this is good - please add it"*

**Both sentences are here because they did different jobs.** The first is the
ruling; the second is the RATIFICATION of the worked detail, and what was shown
to the PO was the seven-row table below **with the greyed reasons in it**, not
the four words alone. That is what HUMAN-GUIDE §6 means by *write down what was
shown* — a signature covers only what was put in front of the signer, and the
reason strings were.

**Connect · View · Edit · Keys**, in that order, in every row, always all four
present. What a status changes is which are ENABLED — never which are drawn —
so the actions cell is the same shape on every row and the eye is not asked to
re-read it. Every disabled icon carries its reason, which `RowActions` makes
unavoidable: `disabled` and `reason` are ONE prop, so a greyed icon with no
explanation does not compile (`BR-SHL-025`).

| Status | Connect | View | Edit | Keys | The reason on the disabled ones |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Not set up | ✔ | — | — | — | *Not connected yet* |
| Not tested | — | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | *Already connected* |
| Working | — | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | *Already connected* |
| Not working | — | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | *Already connected* |
| Turned off | — | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | *Already connected* |
| Reading from us | — | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | *Already connected* |
| Coming soon | — | — | — | — | *Not built yet* — on all four |

Read as: **Connect is live only where there is nothing to connect to yet; the
other three are live the moment a connection exists, in every state it can be
in.** Icons `BoltIcon` · `EyeIcon` · `PencilIcon` · `KeyIcon`, each with its one
word as `aria-label` and tooltip (B14 rule 33 — a label is at most three words).

**The reason strings are EXACTLY the two the PO read** — *"Not connected yet"*,
*"Already connected"* and, on a coming-soon row, *"Not built yet"* — and they
are not to be reworded, because those are the words that were shown.

### Three points the PO agreed explicitly, so they are decisions and not taste

They go in `connectorActions`' own docstring as well as here, because the next
lane will otherwise tidy them away and every check will pass while they do it.

1. **FOUR ICONS ON EVERY ROW, ALWAYS, IN THIS ORDER. An action never
   disappears; it greys.** The PO's own reason: *"A row where the icons move
   around is a row people have to re-read"*. A later lane hiding a disabled
   icon to make the cell tidier is undoing a ratified decision, not tightening
   one.
2. **EVERY GREYED ICON CARRIES ITS REASON.** `RowActions` already makes
   `disabled` and `reason` ONE prop, so this cannot be skipped by accident —
   and that is said out loud rather than left for the next reader to discover
   from the prop shape.
3. **The tooltip on an ENABLED icon is the action word alone** — Connect, View,
   Edit, Keys. One word, B14 rule 33. The reason strings appear on greyed icons
   and nowhere else.

**Three things this supersedes in what the card did**, and each is a real loss
of a verb rather than a rename:

* **`Set up` and `Fix it` both become `Edit`.** Same destination — `S147` — at
  two different points in a connector's life. The card gave them different
  words; the row gives them one icon.
* **`Turn on` / `Turn off` LEAVE the row entirely.** Enabling and disabling a
  connector is a control on the connector's own screen. It was the only
  destructive-tier thing in the cell, so **the danger tier leaves with it** and
  no icon in this table is red.
* **`Keys` is on every connected row**, not only on the *Reading from us* one.
  The grid drew it only where the manifest issues a key AND a connection
  existed — 0 of 28 rows in the demo tenant, a door that was live, routed and
  reachable only by typing its address.

⚠ **`Disconnect` IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE ROW, AND NOTHING ABOVE CHANGES
THAT.** Disconnecting destroys every key on a connector and a partner stops
working mid-morning. It stays behind the connector page's confirm dialog, where
the consequence can be read before it is taken. An absence with a reason is a
different fact from an absence without one, which is why it is written here.

⚠ **AND THIS RULING RETIRES A JUDGMENT THIS LANE WAS ABOUT TO MAKE.** The
briefed recommendation was to keep each row's PRIMARY act as a small BUTTON —
*Connect* · *Test it now* · *Turn on* · *Fix it* are four different verbs and an
icon carries a verb badly — with icons for the rest. **The PO has ruled the
other way and it is a better answer**: four verbs in one column position was the
problem, and a fixed set of four with the status moving the ENABLEMENT removes
it rather than dressing it. B14 rule 15 wants icons in an actions cell, and this
is the version that obeys it without going ragged.

### 3 · The ten columns

> *"Im good with these columes - please implment it"*

| # | Column | What it reads | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Connector | `display_name` | the identity column, links to the connector. The catalogue line wins; `display_name` is the English fallback. |
| 2 | Category | `category` | the chips' own vocabulary, unchanged. |
| 3 | Direction | `kicker.direction` + `.initiative` | **four words out of two fields** — `out`+`us` = *We send*, `in`+`us` = *We collect*, `in`+`them` = *They send*, `out`+`them` = *They read*. The enum never reaches the screen. |
| 4 | State | `display_state` | dot + word, through the existing `StateWord`. Not a second one. |
| 5 | APIs | `operations` | `16 · 14 working`. |
| 6 | Environment | `connection.environment` | *Production* · *Sandbox*. |
| 7 | Where | `connection.describe` | the masked host, **masked by the server** (`BR-INT-003`). Never composed here — `DEF-INT-5555` was exactly that. |
| 8 | Last run | newest `operations[].last_run_at` | **the sortable one.** |
| 9 | Why | `connection.last_test_text` | only when the state is *Not working*. |
| 10 | — | — | the four icons above. |

**No new endpoint and no new field: all ten are already on the wire**, checked
against `integrationsEndpoints.ts` rather than assumed.

⚠ **COLUMNS 6, 7 AND 9 ALL READ `connection`, WHICH IS `null` ON EVERY *Not set
up* AND *Coming soon* ROW** — 12 of 28 in the demo tenant. They draw an empty
cell. Not a dash, not a fabricated value, not a crash.

⚠ **COLUMN 9 IS THE ONE STRUCTURALLY AT RISK OF BEING INCAPABLE OF SHOWING
ANYTHING** (hard-won law 7's third shape). Its cell is populated from a field
that is `null` on every row except the failing ones, so a fixture with no
failing connector in it would let a column that can never render pass every
check. It is proved by finding a real *Not working* connector in the demo tenant
and READING the sentence in a browser, and by a unit fixture that carries all
seven states rather than one.

### The one thing we decided, because the rules ran out: the paging

**The table pages CLIENT-SIDE, on rows already fetched, and that is a deliberate
`NFR-3` deviation with the same reasoning the blueprint already accepted for
this screen's search.** `NFR-3` requires server pagination everywhere, and the
reason is `T5` — a tenant list that grows with the utility's data. **This list
does not.** Its length is the number of MANIFESTS WE SHIP — 28 today — and it is
bounded by our own code rather than by tenant data. It is the same number at a
3,000-connection utility and a 40,000-connection one, and `GET /integrations`
has never taken a `page` param. The blueprint says exactly this about the search
on p014 — *"At 28 manifests that is defensible, because the list is bounded by
our code rather than by tenant data — and it is the same shape NFR-3 forbids, so
it should be written down rather than tidied out of sight."* **So it is written
down here rather than tidied out of sight.** The line it must not cross: the day
a connector list becomes per-tenant data, this becomes a server page.

### 1 · ⚠ SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY BY RULING 5 BELOW — `company_id` — the KEY guarantees the tenant; `company_id` only has to MAP to it

> ⚠ **SUPERSEDED 2026-09-17 by ruling 5 of this same entry** (*"you will ahve to remove company ID
> filter from all Apis"*). **This ruling was made and is recorded as made; it was never built.**
> Everything below describes a comparison that no longer exists in the agreement. **`BR-INT-070`
> carries the current law and the whole chain.** Kept, not deleted, because `serve.py`'s docstring
> still quotes the 2026-09-16 sentence this section supersedes, and a reader tracing that quotation
> needs the middle link.

**The question as put:** *"`company_id` = 393, or our own id?"* — Invoice Cloud's document sends
`company_id=393`, an integer of their own numbering, while `runners/serve.py:company_id_matches()`
requires a UUID and refuses anything else.

> *"company_id = Keys will esnure it map to tenant ID"*

**THE READING CHOSEN.** The partner may send **THEIR OWN number** — `393` — and we compare it
against a value stored on the connection. We do **not** demand our uuid. The key is what
guarantees the tenant; `company_id` is a cross-check that the partner is pointed at the utility
they think they are.

⚠ **`BR-TEN-003` IS UNTOUCHED, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT OF THIS PARAGRAPH.** *"The ONLY input
consulted is the request path; `tenant_id` in a header/param/body is never read"* — as narrowed
2026-09-16, a key is proof and not a claim. The tenant still comes from the key, through
`key_directory.open_utility_for` in `partner_urls.py`, and RLS `FORCE` still does the isolating.
`company_id` is still **VERIFIED AND NEVER USED TO SELECT**. Whoever can send one utility's id can
send another's, so a `company_id` that SELECTED would be a door onto every utility in the product.
**What moves is only the set of values that compare equal.**

⚠ **THIS SUPERSEDES A READING OF NINE DAYS' STANDING, NOT A RULE.** PO ruling 2026-09-16 was
*"company_id = tenant id"*, and it was read as *the partner sends OUR uuid*.
`company_id_matches()` was built to that reading — it parses the presented value as a `uuid.UUID`
and returns `False` for anything that is not one — and the docstring at `serve.py:793` quotes it.
Under law 13 the supersession is STATED and never assumed, so it is stated here, in
`BR-INT-070`, and in the CR.

⚠ **WHAT STAYS EXACTLY AS IT IS:** the parameter is **REQUIRED on every route**; a **missing value
is a NO** (hard-won law 3 — treating absent as *the caller meant their own* would remove the one
honest use of the check, a partner configured against the wrong utility discovering it on the
first call rather than after a month of empty pulls); the comparison is **case-folded after
stripping**; and the refusal is `403` with code `COMPANY_MISMATCH`, in check 7's existing position
in `partner_api._admit`, writing the same `S142` access-log row it writes today.

⚠ **`BR-INT-044` IS NOT AMENDED, AND IT IS THE THING THIS CHANGE CAN MOST EASILY BREAK.** The six
auth refusals are ONE refusal in words AND in timing — the same 41 bytes, the same `404`, padded to
a floor, proved side by side on bytes, status and elapsed time (wave E, 2026-09-16). Check 7 is not
one of those six: it is the one place a partner IS told something specific, and it runs after the
key has already been admitted. **The danger is a new database read.** Today the check reads
`caller.tenant_id`, already in hand, and issues no query; a value stored on the connection must
come from the row `resolve_caller` already loaded and **not from a second lookup**, or a mismatched
`company_id` becomes measurably slower than a matched one — which is `BR-INT-044`'s own enumeration
oracle wearing the fix, the same shape wave E met when it had to move the run-row write inside the
40ms padding. **And a connection with no stored number is a NO, not a pass.**

### 2 · A partner does NOT post a payment. The feed arrives as a BATCH, on a schedule

**The question as put:** *"Can a partner post a payment at all?"* — their document specifies
`POST /api/partner/v1/make-payment/`. Everything our partner surface serves today is a READ.

> *"Can a partner post a payment at all? - I want to use batch run  to take payment feed from Them
> - not online updates"*

**THE READING CHOSEN.** `POST /api/partner/v1/make-payment/` is **NOT BUILT**. The payment feed
arrives as a **BATCH on a schedule**, not as live calls. **This is the single biggest scope
decision in the Invoice Cloud integration, and it REMOVES a partner's ability to write money to us
live.**

**NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY PROMISED IT, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.**
`partner_urls.py` mounts five addresses — `reference`, `customers`, `bills`, `payments`, `ledger` —
and all five are `GET`. `ROUTE_WAVE` is empty. No manifest, epic, business rule or endpoint table
commits us to a partner payment POST, and no lane is building one. **So nothing is discarded: the
collision was with a partner's document, not with our code.**

⚠ **AND IT AGREES WITH THE SHAPE THE PRODUCT OWNER ALREADY DESCRIBED ON 2026-09-06**, which is why
this is a scope decision and not a reversal. That day, verbatim: *"In integration - for invoicecloud
we have both. Cases together they hold ours and we hold theirs. **They will call our invoice and
account APIs and we will call their payment APIs for payment records**."* Their side READS from us;
our side CALLS THEM for payment records. **The 2026-09-17 ruling names the cadence of that second
half — a batch, not online updates — and refuses the third shape their API reference introduced.**
`pay_invoicecloud`'s manifest already declares exactly that shape: `fetch_settlement`,
`direction="in"`, `trigger="scheduled"`, *"We collect what they settled, once a settlement is
cut."*

⚠ **WHAT THIS RULING DOES **NOT** RETIRE, STATED BECAUSE A LANE WILL OTHERWISE OVER-READ IT.** The
kiosk network's inbound door is a **different relationship, ruled separately and already built**:
`BR-INT-058` (*they push: the door and the work are two separate acts*), `OQ-INT-1729` option (a),
2026-09-06, live at `POST /api/{utility}/integrations/inbound/{key}/{operation}` since `2.202.0`.
**A signature covers only what was shown** — the Product Owner was shown Invoice Cloud's
`make-payment`, and was not asked again about a door they ruled on eleven days earlier. The
Integration Blueprint's naming table draws `POST /partner/v1/payments` for the kiosk, and that
record is a measurement of a drawing; it is annotated with this boundary rather than corrected,
because correcting a measurement is falsifying it.

### ⚠ AND HARD RULE 6 ON THIS PATH IS NOW AN OPEN GAP — `OQ-INT-12396`, FILED, OPEN

⚠ **READ THIS BEFORE THE VERIFICATION THAT FOLLOWS IT.** The `payment_import_batches` paragraph
below was written when *"batch run"* was read as a file arriving. **It is KEPT as a record of WHAT
EXISTS and it is no longer this feed's idempotency**, because **every part of that key is derived

**A re-run, a collection that times out half way, or a window re-run over an overlapping date range
can present the same payment twice — and nothing in this product would currently refuse the second
one.** What their API gives us to key on — their own payment id, a **composite** (`BR-INT-058`'s
shape, where *"id alone is not a sufficient key: a reversal carries the same one as the payment it
reverses"*), or a settlement identifier bracketing a set — **is a fact only Invoice Cloud can
supply**, so it is routed to them on `OQ-INT-1476`'s precedent rather than put to the Product
Owner, and **it is not guessed: a guess here is a customer paying twice.**

**The collection may be built and may be scheduled. Nothing may WRITE a payment from
`fetch_payment` until `OQ-INT-12396` is answered.**

#### The verification itself, kept for the record — it describes the FILE families

⚠ **HARD RULE 6 STILL APPLIES TO THE BATCH PATH, AND THE EXISTING MACHINERY ALREADY CARRIES IT —
VERIFIED AGAINST THE CODE, NOT ASSUMED.** `payment_import_batches` carries
`UniqueConstraint(["tenant", "file_hash", "tag_fingerprint"], condition=Q(status=IMPORT_COMMITTED,
file_hash__isnull=False))` (`apps/payments/models.py:1165`), scoped to COMMITTED batches on purpose
so re-opening a modal on the same file is free and only a second COMMIT is refused; `file_hash` is
a server-computed SHA-256 of the exact bytes, never accepted from a client. `apps/payments/lockbox.py`
is the one parser — `parse_remittance_file` has exactly one production caller
(`payment_import.py:371`) and `parse_bank_statement` exactly one (`reconciliation.py:1162`), and
the hash and the tag fingerprint come from the same module. ⚠ **One correction worth carrying:
`lockbox.py` serves TWO families in opposite directions of money.** Its trace header names
`bankrec_models.BankStatementImport` — that is the **bank statement** half (`US-PAY-021`, S38). A
partner payment feed is the **remittance** half (`US-PAY-003`, `BR-PAY-023`), which stamps
`payment_import_batches` and is the one that CREATES payments. A lane reading only the header will
reach for the wrong table.
