## 2026-09-17 · Plans & Rates · A TYPO IN A LIVE RATE IS NOW FIXED AS A CORRECTION, NOT FILED AS A RATE CHANGE

**`DEF-RAT-5715` · builds `BR-RAT-104` for the second object it was always about**

### The report, verbatim

The PO, in the beta: *"if user make an error while creating the rate schedule and
they want to rectify that error using edit - how are they going to do it; it is
not a new rate or it is not a change in rate - it is just an error handling"*.

### Why this is a DEFECT and not a change request

`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`'s test is *can a user do this
task today?* — and the answer is no, which points at BUILD. **It is still a
defect, and the reason is that the rule was already signed.** `BR-RAT-104` is
RATIFIED, and the words it quotes from CR-013 part 4's **shared rules** name no
object at all:

> *"in-place edits of an active version are refused outright, even for
> Owner/Admin, because rate history is an audit artefact; a historic typo is
> fixed by a documented correction version with a reason."*

The 2026-08-21 build satisfied that on the TAX and not on the TARIFF VERSION —
the two objects in this module that have rate history. So this is `not-built`:
**something signed was never built, and the absence is the defect.** Filing it as
a change would have converted our own half-build into the customer's new
requirement, which is exactly what `13-change-process.md` §1 exists to prevent.

### The distinction, because it is the whole design

A rate **CHANGE** is a new row with a **NEW** window: the price moves on a date
and every bill before it was right. That is `BR-RAT-037` and it is untouched.

A **CORRECTION** restates the **SAME** window: the figure recorded for that period
was wrong.

**That single property is what the code enforces**, and it enforces it in the one
place it can be enforced: `correct_rate_schedule_version` copies the window from
the row being corrected and **never reads a date from the payload**. It goes one
step further than `correct_tax`, which overrides a posted date silently — here a
date in a correction payload is **refused by name**, because a caller that sent
one believed it would be used and would otherwise never learn it was not.

### ⚠ THE LOAD-BEARING LINE, AND IT IS ONE LINE

After a correction there are **two activated rows whose window contains the same
day**. `in_force_version` now carries `.filter(superseded_by__isnull=True)`.

**Without it the order-by decides which one prices — by `effective_from`, which
is IDENTICAL on both rows.** That is not a tie-break, it is a coin toss on a
money path, and it would resolve differently on different runs with nothing on
any screen looking wrong. The test that asserts it is named in the suite as the
one that matters.

**`activated_versions` deliberately does NOT filter.** A superseded row is still
history: a regulator asking what this schedule has ever said must still see it,
and `BR-RAT-017`'s seven-year reproducibility reads out of that list. The two are
different questions and only one of them is about pricing.

### The dependency the brief said to verify, verified — and the answer was good

2.5 needs *"has this version priced any bills?"*. `billing/backbill.py` claims the
engine stamps `tariff_version_id` on every priced line — **and that is a
docstring, and hard-won law 1 says a comment claiming a guarantee is not the
guarantee.** `DEF-079` is this exact shape: a counter that answered 0 over live
bills.

**So it was read back off a running tenant before anything was built on it.**
Sample data loaded, then measured:

| | |
|---|---|
| issued invoices | **92** |
| invoice lines | **732** |
| `usage` lines carrying a version id | **456 / 456** |
| `base` lines carrying one | **184 / 184** |
| `tax` lines carrying one | **0 / 92** — correct; a tax line is priced by a tax |
| stamped ids that resolve to a real `TariffVersion` | **3 / 3**, **0 orphans** |
| the per-version count 2.5 needs | Residential water from 2026-06-01 → **47 issued bills**; from 2026-08-01 → **45**; from 2027-01-01 → **0** |

**So the PRECISE test was built and not the conservative one.** The conservative
fallback — any issued invoice overlapping the window — refuses more often than it
needs to, and it was not needed.

⚠ **AND `None` IS KEPT DISTINCT FROM `0` ON BOTH SIDES OF THE WIRE.** *"Nobody has
been billed on this"* and *"we could not work this out"* send an operator to two
different places, and flattening the second into the first is what DEF-079 cost.
The screen draws three different sentences and a test asserts they differ.

### What the screen does, and one place the blueprint had to be read past

The blueprint (p033) rules the button set `Duplicate · Edit · Retire` everywhere
and says *"what editing does still differs — and that belongs in a sentence, not
in a fourth name for the same button"*; on a tax in force, `Edit` opens the
correction flow.

**That works for a tax because a tax in force is only ever corrected. A rate
schedule is the object where both answers are real** — a utility files a new
price every year AND occasionally types one wrongly — so the sentence had to
become a question. **It is still not a fourth button:** the button is `Edit`, and
the question is the first thing inside it, drawn with the kit's `SegmentedField`.
Default `Change the rate`, so no existing habit breaks on the day it ships.

In correction mode the two date fields are **absent, not disabled**: a greyed box
invites *"why can I not change this"* and answering that on screen is rationale,
which B14 rule 33 caps at zero words. The dates are shown as the fact they now
are, read off the version being corrected.

### ⚠ THE WALKTHROUGH PRINTED "ALL CHECKS PASSED" OVER A 404, AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS ENTRY

The first draft of `def_rat_5709_correct_a_version_walkthrough.mjs` committed the
correction and then asserted **that the window had not moved**. It had not — and
it had not because the POST came back **404** from a stale server process. The
window does not move when the commit is refused either.

**A walkthrough written to obey hard-won law 6 had law 7's flaw inside it**: a
check whose pass and whose no-op are indistinguishable. It now watches the
correction call itself, fails on any 4xx, and reads the correction chain back off
the schedule — so *"nothing happened"* can no longer satisfy it. Both halves were
re-proved: red on the 404, green once the route was live.

### What was NOT done, and why each is a row rather than a silence

* **2.5's "point at the rebill path" is a SENTENCE, not a link** — *"Fix those in
  Billing."* Wiring a deep link into billing's correction flow needs the case id
  that flow opens from, which nothing here holds; a link that lands on the wrong
  screen is worse than a sentence that names the right one. Not filed as a
  defect because nothing is broken — it is the honest size of what this lane
  could verify.
* **Whether a correction must also restate the bills already issued under it is
  STILL UNRULED.** `correct_tax` raised it as `OQ-310` and it is open. This path
  reports the count and does nothing automatic, and the review-ledger row says so
  rather than letting a signature imply it.
* **The version bump is the INTEGRATOR's** (§7 as amended 2026-08-26).

### Rollback

Code plus **one migration**. ⚠ **A revert of the code alone leaves the four columns
in place, which is harmless — they are nullable and nothing else reads them — but
a revert of the MIGRATION drops any correction row's link to what it corrected.**
Stated before shipping, per the maintenance process §7: this is one of the fixes
that is not purely undoable, and the undoable half is the code.

### Three more reds found and filed, not fixed

* **`DEF-RAT-5716`** — all six `BR-RAT-114` mid-period-split TCs went red on
  **2026-09-16** (`8c8adfb03`), on a size-axis refusal the fixture does not
  satisfy. That is B4 money math with no live engine check since.
* **`DEF-RAT-5714`** — all eight `BR-RAT-091` rate-change-impact TCs are red and
  `worst_case_pct` answers `None` where `6.00%` is the ratified figure. The
  second-approval gate reads that number, so it currently fails CLOSED and looks
  fine from a screen.
* (`DEF-RAT-5696` and `DEF-RAT-5708`, filed in the previous entry, are the other
  fourteen.)

### ⚠ AND THE TIP MOVED UNDER THIS WORK IN THREE FAMILIES AT ONCE — WHICH IS WHY IT IS RECORDED

While this was being built, a sibling lane landed `BR-RAT-1016` under a PO ruling
made the **same day** — *"please fix all these"*, said over a table of what each
of the five priced objects in Plans & Rates does. Re-deriving from the pinned tip
at push time (law 11) found **three collisions, in three different families, in
one push**:

* **A MIGRATION NUMBER.** `rating/0034` was taken by
  `0034_br_rat_1016_discount_corrections`. Renumbered to `0035`, and its
  `dependencies` moved to name that migration rather than `0033`.
* **A DEFECT ID.** `DEF-RAT-5709` was allocated here and taken there, minutes
  apart, for **different defects** — mine the rate schedule, theirs the discount.
  `file_defect.py` asks the remote and both answers were right when they were
  given; the sibling had not pushed. This is law 11's own worked example, third
  family, and it renumbered to `DEF-RAT-5715` before anything was committed.
* **A RULE THAT DID NOT EXIST WHEN THIS STARTED.** `BR-RAT-104` was the governing
  rule at the beginning of this work and `BR-RAT-1016` is the governing rule at
  the end of it. **This build is now the fifth and last of its five objects** —
  the charge code (`2.297.0`) and the discount (`2.301.0`) shipped, the plan
  stopped deliberately at `OQ-RAT-12409`, and the rate schedule is this.

⚠ **AND THE SHAPE WAS RE-ALIGNED RATHER THAN LEFT MERELY COMPATIBLE.** The route
was `POST …/versions/{vid}/correct`; the module's other two corrections are
`POST /taxes/{id}/corrections` and
`POST /discounts/{id}/versions/{vid}/corrections`. It is
`POST /rate-schedules/{id}/versions/{vid}/corrections` now, because the finding
the PO was shown was **five objects answering one question five ways**, and
shipping a sixth spelling on the day that was ruled would have made this build its
own counter-example.

**Two independent lanes reached the same design for the screen**, which is worth
recording as evidence rather than coincidence: the discount lane's judgment (2)
reads *"THE CORRECTION IS A SEPARATE DOOR, NOT A MODE OF `Edit`… the operator must
say which — a new price from a date and that figure was always wrong produce
different history, and a screen that guessed would mint corrections over ordinary
rises."* That is exactly what the intent picker here does, arrived at from the
blueprint's own p033 reasoning.

## 2026-09-17 · Plans & Rates · THE TIER LADDER NOW SAYS WHICH TIER AND WHICH NUMBER — AND THE RULE DID NOT MOVE

**`DEF-RAT-5717` · closes a tension `CR-087-p045`'s conformance file recorded for the PO and did not resolve**

### The report, verbatim

The PO, in the beta: *"in tied rates - if tier 1 start from 0 to 100 and tier 2
start from 101 to 300 ; then it give error - tier 2 should start from 100"*.

### ⚠ THE PRODUCT WAS RIGHT AND THE MESSAGE WAS AT FAULT — THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING

`BR-RAT-032` is **CONFIRMED (PO R5-5)**: tiers are contiguous, tier *n+1*'s
`From` **is** tier *n*'s `To`. The boundaries are half-open — tier 1 is 0 up to
but **not including** 100 — so `101` genuinely leaves a gap and `100` is the
answer. **No rule changed here and none should have.**

**The server had ALREADY COMPUTED the number.** `services.py` has passed
`expected=str(previous_to)` since it was written. The catalogue sentence was
*"Tiers must run on from one another with no gap: each tier starts where the one
before it ends."* — **it has no placeholder for `expected`, so i18next dropped it
in silence.** The clerk was told a rule and left to work out which tier and which
number.

⚠ **NOTHING WENT RED, AND THAT IS THE ESCAPE.** `G32` asks whether a message key
RESOLVES. `G15` asks whether the eleven catalogues hold the same keys. **Neither
asks whether a sentence renders the params its raiser sends**, so a server that
computes the right answer and a sentence that discards it are each individually
correct. The prevention column on the defect row names the check that would see
it.

### The second half: it fired on the wrong step

The blueprint p047 names it exactly: *"Contiguity, inverted tiers and an open
middle tier are checked here, where the numbers are typed. **All three were
server refusals discovered on the last step.**"* A clerk typed three tiers,
walked four steps, and was then told a number on the first one was wrong.

### THE TENSION THIS CLOSES, AND WHO CLOSED IT

`04-docs/05-modules/06-rating/conformance/CR-087-p045-create-step3-rates.md`
recorded this in as many words and **deliberately built nothing**:

> *"THIS IS A REAL TENSION AND IT NEEDS A DECISION, NOT A LANE'S PREFERENCE …
> either (a) surface its field error on this step instead of at commit, or
> (b) send tier indices and quantities as params so the sentence can name them.
> **Recorded for the PO; nothing built.**"*

**The PO answered it without being asked it**, in the beta, by reporting the
symptom — *"tier 2 should start from 100"* is **(b)** in their own words, and the
blueprint asks for **(a)**. Both are built. That is the conformance file working
as designed: a lane declined to pick, wrote down the two options, and the ruling
arrived.

### ⚠ THE SERVER STILL OWNS THE RULE, AND THE SHAPE IS WHAT MAKES THAT TRUE

The conformance file's other quote is the one that could have been broken here:
*"The server owns every rule … This file therefore performs NO money validation
of its own."* **It still does not.** `tierGapAt` is a PREVIEW of the server's
refusal, not a second copy of it:

* it renders **the server's own catalogue key**, so the two sentences cannot
  drift apart — there is only one sentence;
* the server still refuses, unchanged, and a ladder this preview is silent about
  is still refused if it is wrong;
* it returns `null` on any blank or unparseable row, because **a half-typed
  ladder is not a broken one** and shouting mid-keystroke is its own defect.

### ⚠ ONE DIVERGENCE FROM THE DRAWING, FILED RATHER THAN FOLLOWED

p046 draws the sentence as *"Tier 2 starts at 2 and tier 1 ends at 3. Tiers must
run on from one another with no gap and no overlap."* — **10 words then 13.**
B14 rule 33 caps an instruction at **six words per sentence** and puts the RULE
itself (*why* blocks must run on) at **zero words on screen**, because that is
rationale.

**The UI rules win where they and a drawing disagree about construction, and the
divergence is written into the conformance file rather than followed silently.**
Built: `Start tier {{tier}} at {{expected}}. Tier {{previous}} ends there.` —
five words then four, naming the same two tiers and the same two numbers the
drawing names. **The drawing is right about WHAT to say and over the cap in HOW.**
A test asserts both sentences stay inside six words, so the next lane cannot
quietly restore the longer one.

### The brief's own instruction, and why it was not followed

This lane was briefed to make tier *n+1*'s `From` **read-only and auto-filled**,
so the error becomes unreachable. **It is auto-filled and it is NOT read-only**,
and the reason is the drawing: p046 draws `FROM` as an ordinary editable input
with a `Remove` beside it, and `DEF-GOV-5248` gives the blueprint layout, copy,
flows and states. A read-only field would also make an INVERTED ladder
(`100 → 90`) unexpressible in a wizard whose own server still checks for one.
**The pre-fill gives the briefed benefit — a clerk who presses `+ Add tier` gets
`100` already typed — without contradicting the drawing or removing a control it
shows.**

### What was NOT built from the brief, and why

* **3.2 — the ladder reading `0 – 100 · 100 – 300 · 300 and above`.** The
  blueprint draws the last row's `To` **blank**, with the help line *"Blank on
  the last row means no upper limit."* Rendering `300 and above` somewhere else
  would be a second way of saying the same thing on one screen.
* **3.3 — stating the half-open convention once.** The drawing does not carry it,
  and *"From is included, To is not"* is the RULE rather than a fact about this
  screen — rule 33 puts that at zero words. It is in `tierGapAt`'s docstring and
  in `BR-RAT-032`, which is where the rule says to put it.
* ⚠ **One thing seen and left alone, because it is already recorded:** the *"Leave
  blank on the last row for no upper limit"* help renders on **every** row, not
  only the last. That is the same conformance file's **D4**, already written down,
  and widening this fix to it is the tidying the maintenance process §3 forbids.

## 2026-09-17 · Plans & Rates · THE DATE A CLERK PICKS NOW SAYS WHAT IT CLOSES — AND WAVE 4's REDESIGN IS STOPPED FOR A DRAWING

**`DEF-RAT-5718` built · `OQ-RAT-12410` minted · the TOU/season nesting NOT built, on purpose**

### The report, verbatim

The PO, in the beta: *"i want to change the rate from tomorrow - eisting rates
say it is valid until 31 dec"*.

### What it is

`create_rate_schedule_version` closes the previous window **the day before** the
new one opens. That is correct and `BR-RAT-037` requires it — windows never
overlap. **Nothing on any screen said so.** A rate whose own detail page reads
*valid until 31 December* stops in September, and the clerk finds out afterwards.

⚠ **THE ESCAPE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX.** The auto-close is asserted by tests
that all pass, because they assert the BEHAVIOUR. **No check in this repository
can see a sentence that is absent**, and the only copy anywhere near it —
`effectiveToHelp`, *"Leave blank to run until the next version starts."* —
describes the NEW version's own end, not the rewriting of the OLD one's. A
consequence that is correct and unstated is indistinguishable, to every gate
here, from one that is stated.

### ⚠ IT MIRRORS THE SERVER'S CONDITION AND DOES NOT APPROXIMATE IT

The server closes only when `effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to >= new_from`.
A screen saying *"the current rate ends"* over a version that has **already**
ended would announce a change that is not going to happen — a true-looking
sentence about the wrong row, which is worse than silence. `currentRateEndsOn`
reads the same two values and applies the same test, and it is silent on every
case the server leaves alone.

⚠ **AND IT IS `latest_version`, NOT `current_version`.** They are the same row on
most schedules and they are **not** the same when a future-dated version is
already filed: `current_version` is then the one in force today and
`latest_version` is the future one — and `latest_version` is the row the server
actually closes. Serving the wrong one would print a real date belonging to a
different row. Two scalars are served rather than the row, because the screen
needs exactly the two the server's condition reads.

The date is rendered through `DateCell` (`BR-SHL-034`), so it is the tenant's
own format and never a string interpolated into a sentence.

### ⚠ A SILENT NO-OP IN THIS LANE'S OWN EDIT, CAUGHT BY THE BROWSER AND NOTHING ELSE

The review-step half (4.7) was written, `tsc` passed, 74 unit cases passed — and
**it was not on the screen.** The edit's anchor string named `DEF-RAT-5709`,
which this lane had renumbered to `DEF-RAT-5715` an hour earlier, so the
replacement matched nothing and did nothing. **A string replace that finds no
match is a no-op that looks exactly like a success.**

It was found by the walkthrough (hard-won law 6) and by nothing else, and the
repair carries an `assert` on the anchor **and** on its uniqueness, which is the
habit rather than the fix.

### ⛔ 4.1 – 4.5 ARE NOT BUILT, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION

The brief asked for the TOU and seasonal editors to be **redesigned**: windows
nested inside their season, the per-window season dropdown removed, month names
instead of bare numbers, the range echoed back, gaps and overlaps checked as you
type.

**There is no drawn specification for it.** The Plans & Rates blueprint draws the
TIERED editor (p046) in full and mentions seasonal and time-of-use only as
STATES on p047 — *"A red banner first… Each window must name the meter register
it bills from"*. It draws neither editor. Searched: three mentions of *season* in
126 pages, none of them a layout.

The UI skill's §1 is explicit about what to do next, and it is a PO ruling of
2026-09-10: **draw it, show it to the PO in plain English, get a yes, then
build** — *"the middle step is not optional"*. Building five specifications of
layout from a task sentence is precisely how the property Overview shipped with
three rows missing, which is the example that ruling was written from.

**So this lane stopped at the boundary and minted `OQ-RAT-12410`** carrying what
it would have drawn, so the next lane starts from a question rather than from a
blank page.

⚠ **AND ONE THING IN THAT LIST IS ALREADY DECIDED AND SHOULD NOT BE RE-ASKED:**
the brief called `TouEditor` rendering `SeasonEditor` with `withPrice={false}`
*"correct, not a bug"*, and it is — a TOU window is per (season × day type). The
question is the LAYOUT that makes that legible, not the model.

### The corrected steer about `DatePickerField`, checked against the source

This lane was told there is no date-picker component in the kit. **There is** —
`DatePickerField` in `FormModal.tsx`, made mandatory for every date field by
`BR-SHL-033`, and `RateScheduleWizard` **already imports and uses it** for both
effective dates. `LONG_LIST_THRESHOLD = 10` and `SearchSelectField` exist too.

On 4.4 specifically, read from the component rather than from either sentence:
**`DatePickerField` takes a `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date and a season boundary is
a month-and-day with NO year**, so the control genuinely does not express it.
That is recorded in `OQ-RAT-12410` as a stated divergence from `BR-SHL-033` for
the next lane to build against, rather than decided here on a screen nobody has
drawn.

### Rollback

Code only: revert the commit. The two served scalars are additive and read by
one component.

## 2026-09-17 · Plans & Rates · "TOO MUCH TEXT" — THE IMPACT PANEL REDRAWN TO ITS BLUEPRINT, AND THE REST MEASURED RATHER THAN SWEPT

**`DEF-RAT-5719` built · the remaining four items of the text sweep MEASURED and NOT built**

### The report, verbatim

The PO, said of steps 2, 3, 4 and 5: ***"too much text"***.

### What was built, and it is the blueprint's own shape

`ImpactAnalysisPanel` rendered every figure in one grid, and **each unmeasured
figure carried its own copy of a sixteen-word sentence** — *"Not calculated.
Nothing works this figure out yet, and it is left blank rather than guessed."*
With three of the four unmeasured, a clerk read **forty-eight words of identical
text to learn one thing.**

⚠ **THE REPETITION WAS A PROPERTY OF THE DATA, NOT OF THE CODE.** With ONE
unmeasured figure it read perfectly. That is why no review caught it, and why no
check could: B14 rule 33 is RATIFIED AND UNENFORCED, because **nothing in this
repository reads rendered output.**

**The blueprint p048 already draws the answer** and it was not invented here: the
measured figures stay in the grid, and beneath them a single
`NOT WORKED OUT YET` heading lists the ones nothing computes, **one short line
each**. Measured on the running product: `48 → 4` words plus three labels.

⚠ **AND THE PROPERTY `DEF-434` FOUGHT FOR IS UNCHANGED.** A figure blank because
nothing computes it must never read as a figure blank because it is zero, and
`second_approval_required(None)` still returns `null` rather than `false` on both
sides of the wire. What moved is that the explanation is said **once for the
group** rather than once per row. `DEF-434`'s own test case is amended in place,
with that reasoning in its body, so nobody reads the change as a weakening.

### The three verdicts, inside rule 33

`secondApprovalRequired` (17 words), `secondApprovalClear` (17) and
`secondApprovalUnknown` (27) are now two sentences of five or fewer:
*"Second approval required. Worst case 11.4%, over 10%."*

⚠ **AND THE FIGURES SURVIVED THE SHORTENING, WHICH IS ITS OWN TEST.** Cutting
copy is exactly how a sentence loses the number a filer acts on — that is
`DEF-RAT-5717` in reverse, where a sentence silently dropped the param its raiser
sent. A case asserts both measured verdicts still carry `pct`. The UNKNOWN one
deliberately drops `{{threshold}}`: a bar is meaningless when nothing was
measured against it.

### ⚠ A DEFECT IN THIS LANE'S OWN TEST, WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX

The rule-33 cap checks written in three earlier waves counted sentences with
`text.split(".")`. **The first string carrying a figure broke it**: *"Second
approval required. Worst case 11.4%, over 10%."* is two sentences and
`split(".")` makes it four.

Those earlier checks had all passed — on strings with no decimal point in them.
**A check that is correct only for the data it has seen is the shape hard-won law
7 names**, and it was in a check written to enforce a rule about words. There is
one `sentencesOf` now, used by all five cap checks, and it splits on terminal
punctuation rather than on every full stop.

### ⛔ FOUR OF THE SIX BRIEFED ITEMS ARE MEASURED AND NOT BUILT

Not because they are wrong — they are right — but because each needs something
this lane could not honestly supply. **The measurement is recorded so the next
lane starts from numbers:** `38` of the `rating.rate.*` strings are over twelve
words; the longest are `sizes.legacyBase`, `filing.captureOnly` and
`baseOnlyGap` at **29 words each**.

* **6.1 · step 2's header (≈38 words → ≈9)** and **6.2 · step 3's two
  paragraphs** and **6.5 · step 5's ≈110 words** — every one of these is a
  judgment about **what a clerk still needs on a screen the blueprint does not
  draw in that state.** Cutting an explanation that turns out to be load-bearing
  is a defect that reads as tidiness, and `rating.rate.sizes.noBaseCode` (28
  words) is precisely the kind that tells a clerk where to go next. This wants
  one pass with the PO over the measured list, not a lane's preference applied
  38 times across eleven catalogues.
* **6.6 · "Activating stores this pricing…" onto the confirm — NOT A COPY
  CHANGE.** `WizardFrame` has `commitLabel` and `commitFailedTitle` and **no
  consequence slot at all**. Adding one changes every wizard in the product on
  one screen's authority, which is exactly what B14 rule 38 exists to stop a lane
  doing by itself. It is a kit change with its own justification, and it is named
  here rather than done in passing.

## 2026-09-17 · `DEF-RAT-5724` IS MISATTRIBUTED — THE PO NEVER SAW A UUID ON A SCREEN

**The row records the reporter as "Product Owner" and the fault as _"The plan
wizard shows a GL account as a raw uuid"_. Neither is what happened, and the
lane that inherited it has been sent looking for a screen that cannot exist.**

**What actually happened, from the working session.** The PO asked for the plan
wizard's steps 4, 5 and 6 to add a GL column — verbatim: *"you shoudl displat
the name and charges an d gl code for that"*. Checking the code before
answering, the coordinating session found that `charge_row`, `tax_row` and
`discount_row` served **only `gl_account_id`**, a uuid, and told the PO that
showing it was therefore blocked by B14 rule 31 and needed server work first.
The PO replied to **that statement**, not to a screen: *"dont show uuiD- shoe
actual 3 of gL code 4000 , 4010 something liek this and its name - you might
have to pull it from GL code mapping we have it - if GL code is not map then
dont show it"*.

So the uuid was a description of **what the API served**, never of what any
screen drew. **The GL column did not exist yet** — that is the whole reason the
request was made. The `partially-fixed` lane was right that it could not
reproduce it: it walked the three catalogue tabs and all eight wizard steps and
found no uuid rendering, because there was none to find.

⚠ **THIS IS THE CHANGE PROCESS'S OWN NAMED HAZARD, ONE STEP EARLIER.**
`13-change-process.md` §1 warns that filing our misunderstanding as a *change*
converts our error into the customer's new requirement. This is the mirror:
filing our own **description** as the customer's **defect report** converts our
reading of an API into a sighting they never had — and it is worse, because a
defect row names a reporter and no gate reads prose for truth. A row attributed
to the PO is the one kind a later lane will not second-guess.

**Standing correction.** The requirement is unchanged and was correctly built:
resolve the id through the ledger seam and serve `gl_account_code` /
`gl_account_name`, showing nothing when unmapped. That half is live and proved —
`AFTER-HRS` renders `4630 · Field-service & meter fees`. What remains is the
three screens (`ChargesStep`, `TaxesStep`, `DiscountsStep`, ~1,042 lines), which
were deliberately left whole rather than half-started.

**And the question the row raises must NOT be put to the PO.** *"Which screen
did you see the uuid on?"* has an answer in this record: none. Asking would be
CLAUDE.md law 13 exactly — the repo holds the answer, and a re-ask manufactures
an inconsistency the human is then blamed for. Whoever closes the row should
close it on this entry, not on a reply.

**How it happened, stated plainly so it is not repeated.** The coordinating
session — mine — described an API limitation in a message; the request that
followed was briefed to a lane as a defect; and the lane filed the row from the
brief. Nobody invented anything. The row is simply a paraphrase that acquired a
reporter on the way through.

## 2026-09-18 · `OQ-RAT-12408` CLOSED — A CHARGE CODE GETS AN EFFECTIVE START AND END DATE

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"yes there should be effective stat date and end date
for charge code also"* — in answer to the question put in plain English with its
figure: a price typed today prices the CURRENT open cycle, there is no way to
schedule a rise for the 1st, and `BR-RAT-088`'s own worked cost of a wrong base
is **`$23,069.50` a month across 1,247 connections**.

This closes the question the uniform-verbs lane stopped at rather than guessed.
**Option (C) — *neither, and the product says so* — was what shipped, and it is
now superseded.** The charge code stops being the one priced object of five that
cannot say WHEN.

### What the PO ruled, and what they did not

They ruled the **requirement**: effective dating, start and end. They did not
choose between the two storage shapes the question offered, and that choice is
ours to make and record rather than to ask again (CLAUDE.md law 13 — *"a
judgment call recorded in the decision log with its reasoning is the
deliverable; a question is the failure to make one"*).

**WE CHOOSE OPTION (A), A `charge_versions` TABLE — NOT (B), DATES ON THE ROW.**
Four reasons, and the second is decisive on its own:

1. **(B) breaks `charges.code` uniqueness**, which `BR-RAT-035` states as signed
   law and which every screen, every import path and the plan builder's picker
   assume. A price change under (B) is a NEW ROW with the same code, so a
   lookup by code stops having one answer. Reversing a signed uniqueness rule to
   get a date column is a much larger change than the one being asked for, and
   it would be discovered by an importer rather than by this decision.
2. **`BR-RAT-1016` was ruled by the same PO the day before** — *"please fix all
   these"* — giving all five priced objects the same three verbs. The other four
   already carry their dates in a versions table or on a row with a correction
   chain. (A) is that uniformity; (B) would make the charge code the odd one out
   again, in a new way, one day after the ruling that stopped it being odd.
3. **(A) carries `corrects`/`superseded_by`, so verb 2 arrives with it.** The PO
   asked for *"effective start date and end date"* and for corrections in the
   same breath of work; (A) answers both, (B) answers only the first.
4. It is the shape `tariff_versions` already proves, including the per-size
   table (`BR-RAT-690`) that any version row must carry — the fire customer's
   `$60.00` 6" line lives entirely in it, and guarding the five scalars alone
   would guard one of two routes to the same money.

### The sub-question the ruling does not settle, and the constraint on it

The existing rows carry `created_at` and nothing else. **A backfill that reads it
would claim a price was in force from the day the CODE was created, which is
false for every code whose amount was ever edited — and until `DEF-RAT-5712`
landed, nothing recorded that an amount had been edited at all.**

**THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, decided here: THE MIGRATION MANUFACTURES NO DATE.** An
initial version row may not assert a start it cannot know. What it may assert is
that the price was in force *before this product recorded dates*, which is true
and is exactly today's behaviour — so the migration must change no bill, and a
test must prove that on the seeded estate before and after.

⚠ **AND THE OBVIOUS SPELLING IS TAKEN.** On `tariff_versions` a NULL
`effective_from` means **DRAFT** (`BR-RAT-031`). Copying that spelling onto a
charge version would give one column two meanings inside one module, which is
how a resolver comes to price a draft. The lane building this decides the
spelling and states it, with the collision named — a sentinel, a separate flag,
or a different column — and whatever it picks, `in_force_version`'s equivalent
must never select a row that has not started.

### Standing
🔒 **rating math AND migration ordering.** Every reader of `charges.amount` moves
— `resolution.py`, `resolution_catalogue.py`, `gather.py`, `selectors.py` and the
shadow — so this is a re-sign question as well as an engineering one, and the
files carry `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` with a review-ledger row stating the shape and
its worked figure in plain English.

## 2026-09-18 · A PLAN MUST SURFACE CHANGES TO WHAT IT BINDS (PO ruling)

**PO, verbatim:** *"yes we should build this. It measn every time Rate, taxes,
Charge code, Discounts are changed, at apporval we need to take action to inform
Plan about it - Fix this"*.

**The gap, as put to them.** A plan shows WHICH schedule it binds and never that
the bound schedule's PRICE moved. A clerk looking at `Sample — Residential`
cannot see that its water rate went from `15.00` to `18.00` last Tuesday. This
follows directly from the PO's own correction of the same day — *"plan will not
do any edits to Rates … plan only binds it"* — which is `BR-RAT-088` restated:
*"the CHARGE CODE owns the base amount; a plan displays it, never defines it."*
Once money lives entirely on the bound objects, **the plan's whole job is to show
what it is bound to, and it was showing only half of that.**

### The design, and the one judgment inside it

**TWO HALVES, and they are deliberately not the same mechanism.**

**(1) THE DISPLAY IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED.** The plan detail reads
`rate_change_log` — which already carries `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `before`,
`after`, `reason`, `actor_user_id` and `created_at`, and already holds live rows
for `schedule` and `charge` — for the entity ids this plan binds. **No new
storage, and it cannot drift**: a derived view is right by construction, where a
copied one is right only until something fails to copy.

**(2) THE NOTIFICATION AT APPROVAL IS AN ALERT, NOT THE RECORD.** The PO asked
for *"at approval we need to take action to inform Plan"*, and that is built —
but it is built ON TOP of (1) rather than instead of it. ⚠ **A push that fails
to fire is invisible for ever, which is hard-won law 2's exact shape**: the
plan would sit there looking untouched while its rate had moved. With the
display derived, a missed notification costs an alert and never costs the truth.

**⚠ THE FAN-OUT IS THE PART TO GET RIGHT, AND IT IS A TIER PROBLEM.** A change to
a charge code or a tax reaches EVERY plan that binds it — one tax can touch all
of them. On this estate that is 6 plans; `NFR-3`/`NFR-5` forbid an unpaginated
list or an unbounded loop anywhere, and T5 is 40,000 accounts. So the affected-
plan set is resolved as a bounded query, never a loop per plan, and the screen
paginates.

### What it is NOT
It is not a plan version. A bound object changing is not a change to the PLAN —
that is the whole point of the PO's ruling — so `plans.version` must not move and
no `plan_versions` row is written. A lane that "fixes" this by minting a version
has inverted the ruling.

### Standing
Read-only over an existing money-path log. Not 🔒 itself, but it renders signed
figures, so every amount is shown to 2 places from the stored 4 (hard rule 2) and
no figure is recomputed on the way to the screen.

## 2026-09-18 · INVOICE CLOUD POSTS PAYMENTS TO US — THE DIRECTION REVERSES

**PO ruling, verbatim, 2026-09-18:** *"they post to us daily"*.

### What this supersedes, quoted, one day old

**PO ruling 2026-09-17, verbatim:** *"no this is not there - we will call htheir
APis - we will ahnel those APis seperately - rember Invoice Cloud is both
direction"* — which settled that **a partner does not post a payment to us** and
that we call their APIs on a schedule and COLLECT.

**That is now reversed.** The direction is PUSH: Invoice Cloud posts, daily. The
2026-09-17 ruling stands only for the half it also covered — Invoice Cloud is
both directions, and the outbound half (they READ our accounts, bills, payments
and ledger through `/partner/v1/…`) is untouched by this.

### What this does to `OQ-INT-12396`

`OQ-INT-12396` asks *"what does Invoice Cloud's payment API give us to key on, so
that a scheduled pull re-run does not post the same payment twice?"* — **and it
exists only because of the pull model.** Under a push its premise is gone: the
inbound path already carries TWO independent idempotency guards, and neither
needs a key derived from a file or a window.

⚠ **IT IS NARROWED, NOT CLOSED.** If we ever pull from them for reconciliation
the question returns unchanged, and the 2026-09-17 ruling's *"Invoice Cloud is
both direction"* is exactly the case where we might. Left OPEN and re-scoped.

### What already exists — measured, not assumed

**The inbound path is built, routed and fails closed.** `apps/payments/webhooks.py`
(HUMAN-OWNED · HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING, authored 2026-09-03), routed at
`portal/webhooks/payments/<str:provider>` (`apps/portal/api.py:3213`):

* **Two independent idempotency guards catching two different facts**, each
  asserted on its own so neither can silently stand in for the other:
  `uq_payment_webhook_events_event` on `(tenant, provider, event_id)` — *has this
  DELIVERY been seen?* — recognises a redelivery BEFORE any money path runs; and
  `uq_payments_webhook_key` on `webhook|<provider>:<event_id>` — *has this
  PAYMENT been recorded?* — catching a race that slipped past the first.
* **HMAC-SHA256 over the RAW BODY BYTES**, never a re-serialised dict, compared
  with `hmac.compare_digest`.
* **No secret configured ⇒ REFUSE** (hard-won law 3). The default mapping is
  empty, so a deployment that has not set a secret takes no callbacks at all.

**So this is a WIRING job, not a build.** What Invoice Cloud specifically needs:
the inbound dialect for THEIR callback shape (`shapes.py`'s `INVOICE_CLOUD`
covers the outbound direction only), the account match (`consumer_no` is our
account number, already ruled), and the two facts below.

### The two facts that are not ours to choose

1. **THEIR SIGNATURE SCHEME.** We verify HMAC-SHA256 over the raw bytes. If
   Invoice Cloud signs any other way — or does not sign — **every delivery
   refuses, correctly, and the feed is silently dead.** This is the same shape as
   the open SendGrid question (`DEF-INT-5630`, HMAC vs ECDSA) and it is a fact
   from their documentation, not a decision.
2. **THE SHARED SECRET MUST BE SET ON THE DEPLOYED HOST.** ⚠ Editing
   `.env.example` fixes nothing already running (hard-won law 4), and this is the
   one endpoint where getting that wrong means an unauthenticated path that
   creates payments — so it fails closed by design and stays that way.

## 2026-09-18 · `OQ-RAT-12409` CLOSED — A PLAN CORRECTION IS OPTION A

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"The plan correction — A, B or C - option A pls"*.

So `plan_versions` gains `corrects` / `superseded_by` / `correction_reason`, the
unique key becomes PARTIAL (`WHERE corrects IS NULL`), a correction is a NEW ROW
carrying the SAME `version_no`, the corrected row keeps its snapshot for ever,
and `plans.version` never moves.

### What was put to them, so the record shows what the yes covers

The question was put twice. The FIRST framing was **WRONG and was withdrawn**: it
used *"minimum bill $12.00 → $15.00 on the plan"*, and that figure does not live
on a plan — `plan_minimum_moves_to_the_schedule` and
`plan_service_minimum_removed` moved it. The PO corrected the premise themselves:
*"plan will not do any edits to Rates … plan only binds it"*, which is
`BR-RAT-088` restated.

**The framing they actually ruled on** used a real case on real data: `Sample —
Residential` (`SCW-RES`), v1, **75 units assigned, every one recorded against
`plan_version = 1`**. A clerk points the water service at `Sample — Commercial
water (flat)` instead of `Sample — Residential water (inclining tiers)` and puts
it back an hour later — **three versions today, two of which are a slip and its
undo**, and any unit assigned in that hour stamped with a version number that
exists only because of a mis-click.

⚠ **AND ONE ARGUMENT AGAINST B WAS WITHDRAWN BEFORE THEY CHOSE, WHICH IS WHY
THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SUMMARISED.** B was first described as destroying
the evidence. **It does not.** `update_plan` already writes a `RateChangeLog` row
with `entity_type="plan"` and BOTH `before` and `after`, permanently, beside the
audit row — so under B the wrong binding survives in the change log and only the
FILING RECORD is restated. B's real and only cost is narrower: a version number
that `unit_plan_assignments.plan_version` points at stops meaning what it meant
when those rows pointed at it. That correction was given to the PO before they
answered.

### Why A, with B's cost correctly stated

Not because B loses the record — it does not. Because **A is the shape taxes and
discounts already use**, both built this week under `BR-RAT-1016`'s uniformity
ruling, and a third mechanism for the third object is a cost paid by every future
reader of this module. B's one breakage is also **contingent on `OQ-323`**, which
is unruled: if an assignment's version drives pricing, B is a money problem; if
it is historical, B is cosmetic. A does not depend on that answer either way.

### Standing and scope
🔒 **migration ordering** — it changes a unique constraint on a filing table, so
it carries `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` and a review-ledger row. No data moves: every
existing row is a non-correction, so the partial key covers them unchanged.
**Severity is MEDIUM, not high** — with money off the plan a wrong binding is
caught by the next bill run rather than by a customer overpaying.

## 2026-09-18 · `OQ-323` ANSWERED — A BILL IS PRICED BY THE VERSION IN FORCE FOR THE SERVICE PERIOD, NOT TODAY'S

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"rate on 1 Jan 2026 was R1 athen in 30 Jun 2026 it
Change to R2 - Today is 17 Sep 2026 - if we generate bill for 1 feb, it will take
R1 rate and if we generate bill for july it ill take r2; you hv to manage boundry
correctly when it transtion that is 30 Jun"*.

### What it settles

**The SERVICE DATE decides, never the wall clock.** A bill run executed today for
a February period prices at R1. This is `BR-RAT-007` restated by the PO in their
own worked case, and it is what `selectors.in_force_version(tariff, service_date)`
already implements — *"the version whose window contains the SERVICE date, never
the current one"*.

**AND IT ANSWERS `OQ-323` BY REMOVING ITS PREMISE.** `OQ-323` asked which version
prices an account assigned at an OLDER PLAN version. Under this ruling and the
PO's correction of the same day — *"plan will not do any edits to Rates … plan
only binds it"* — **a plan version prices nothing at all.** Pricing follows the
RATE version in force at the service date; `unit_plan_assignments.plan_version`
is a historical record of what was bound when, and never an input to a price.

That also settles, retrospectively, the cost of option B in `OQ-RAT-12409`: B's
one breakage — a version number meaning something different from what it meant
when an assignment pointed at it — is **cosmetic rather than a money problem**,
because nothing prices from it. The PO chose A anyway, on the uniformity ground,
and A does not depend on this answer either way.

### ⚠ THE BOUNDARY IS RULED, IS BUILT, AND HAS NO WORKING PROOF

The PO's *"you hv to manage boundry correctly"* is **`BR-RAT-114`, their own
ruling of 2026-08-22**, with a signed figure: *"Water at $2.00/kgal until the
15th, then $2.20, 10 kgal spread evenly: split = $21.00"* — one bill, priced per
sub-period, each sub-period at the version in force, never the single-version
$20.00 or $22.00.

**ALL SIX OF ITS TEST CASES FAIL. Run directly on 2026-09-18 rather than taken
from a report:**

    FAILED tc1__the_pin__ten_kgal_across_a_midpoint_reprice_is_21_00
    FAILED tc2__no_boundary_means_no_split_and_the_untouched_path
    FAILED tc3__a_read_dating_the_boundary_wins_over_the_day_weight
    FAILED tc4__a_plan_change_on_the_16th_splits_the_same_way
    FAILED tc5__the_ordinary_run_and_the_back_bill_give_one_answer
    FAILED tc6__the_split_bill_is_taxed_once_over_the_whole_bill

Red since **2026-09-16** (`DEF-RAT-5716`, filed by the rate lane and independently
confirmed here). **tc1 is named after the PO's own figure**, so the signed
contract for a mid-period split has been unverified for two days — on the exact
transition the PO has now asked, in writing, to be managed correctly.

⚠ **THIS IS THE FOURTH RED-AND-UNREAD FINDING IN TWO DAYS** — after
`DEF-SHL-5695`, `DEF-RAT-5713` and `DEF-GOV-5732` — and it is the one on a money
path. The pattern is not the individual gates: it is that this repo runs no CI,
so a red exists only while somebody is looking at it.

## 2026-09-18 — the BR-RAT-114 mid-period pin is green again, and both causes were fixture drift behind ruled changes

`DEF-RAT-5716` is **fixed** in `bbf593891`. All six TCs pass. **The signed figure
did not move, and on a signed figure it never may** — the rule is that the engine
moves, never the expectation. What moved was where a utility writes two facts.

**Cause 1 · R3, the size axis.** `configured_sizes_for` reads a banded service's
axis off `rate_size_rows`. The fixture declared none, so water's axis was `()` and
every account refused with *"connection size `'W-58'` has no row on the rate
schedule version …"* before a single tier was priced. `DEF-2799` is the identical
failure on the demo fixture, seeded there for the same reason.

**Cause 2 · R4, where a zero is stated.** The fixture stated its base as the
schedule version's `base_charge=0`. Two rulings retired that reading in turn:
`BR-RAT-088` moved the base AMOUNT to the charge code, and `DEF-2830`
(2026-08-31) then settled that a schedule's stored `0.00` reads as **NOT STATED**
rather than as *the charge is nothing* — *"the opposite reading would give the
standing charge away because somebody left a box alone"*. So R4 refused with
*"Nobody has stated this service's base charge"*. The zero is now declared where
the product reads it: a `water` charge code marked `is_base`, stating `$0.00`.
`test_br_rat_120_size_refusal` already does exactly this, in its own words *"so
that the refusal it is actually testing … cannot be R4's missing-base refusal
wearing the same exception."*

**The size is `BR-TEN-171`'s own**, read through `_smallest_ratified_band` — the
SAME resolver `a_meter` uses for its own default — so the meter these fixtures
fit and the schedule they bind cannot drift apart when the ratified list moves.
`minimum_bill` is NULL and not zero (*"Absent is not zero"*), so no money is
added. Both facts are lifted into two named helpers called from all three
version-building sites, so a fourth site cannot quietly omit them.

**PROVED RED BEFORE TRUSTED GREEN (law 7).** With the reprice moved outside the
period, tc1 fails with a single usage line of **$22.00** — the exact figure its
own docstring says it must never be. The pin therefore still measures the SPLIT:
5 kgal × $2.00 + 5 kgal × $2.20 = **$21.00**.

⚠ **THE GENERAL SHAPE, AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING.** Neither cause was a
bug in the engine and neither was a bug in the arithmetic. **Both were a ruling
landing correctly in the product while a fixture went on stating the same fact
the old way** — which is this repo's own commonest failure (B14's rule count, the
module-segment caveat, r10 vs the blueprints) in a new place. A test that states
a fact the product no longer reads does not fail loudly at the moment of the
ruling; it fails weeks later, at a step BEFORE the thing it exists to prove, and
reads as a broken test rather than as a stale statement.

## 2026-09-18 — three PO rulings, recorded the turn they were made (law 9)

### 1 · A platform provider's credentials live in the environment, never in a table

PO, verbatim: *"we will keep them in nv or save thm as platform secreate and not
in table"*.

**The case.** A platform-level provider connection (the one the PLATFORM holds,
not a tenant's own) needed somewhere to keep its auth mode and secret. The
options put were a column on the connection row versus an environment variable /
platform secret. **Ruled: the environment or a platform secret.** No table
column holds it.

**What follows, so a lane does not have to re-derive it.** A secret that is not
in the database is not in a backup, not in an export, not readable by RLS and not
visible to a tenant admin on any screen — which is the point. A screen that needs
to say whether one is configured shows PRESENT or ABSENT, never the value, and
reads it from the environment at request time. Hard-won law 3 applies with full
force: the unsafe option must be the one you type, so an ABSENT secret refuses
rather than falling back to an unauthenticated call.

### 2 · The mapping-editor test is narrowed to the connectors it was written about

PO, verbatim: *"this is correct"*, to: *"The test was right for its wave and is
now too broad — narrow it to the connectors it was written about, keep the ban
for those."*

**The collision.** Two of the PO's own rulings disagreed once a later wave
widened the connector set: an earlier ruling banned a mapping editor for the
connectors of its wave, and a test enforced that ban across EVERY connector,
including ones the later ruling says should have an editor. **Ruled: the ban
stands for the connectors it was written about, and the test is narrowed to
those.** It is not deleted — a ban that is still correct keeps its guard.

### 3 · Any tenant admin may retire any account type from new business — `OQ-CUS-12407`, option (a)

PO, verbatim: *"go with option a"*.

**Option (a) as it was put:** *"Yes, on any row. It is the tenant's list;
retiring a code from new business without disturbing existing accounts is exactly
what a growing utility needs, and `active=false` — the only control they have
today — is the blunter instrument: it removes the code from filters and reports
as well."*

**The worked case that was put with it:** a utility stops offering `Marina berth`
on new accounts and goes on billing the eleven boats that already have it. Under
`active=false` those eleven vanish from filters and reports; under `legacy=true`
they bill and report exactly as before and the code simply stops being offered.

**What this settles and what it does NOT.** It settles WHO may write `legacy` —
any tenant admin, on any row, seeded rows included — so `government`'s flag is
now clearable by a tenant. That was option (b)'s stated objection and the PO
overruled it. It does not touch `BR-CUS-094`'s own ruling about `government`'s
MEANING, and it does not answer `OQ-CUS-12356` (may an account's category be
CHANGED after it is opened), which stays **OPEN** and is a different question.
`DEF-CUS-5135`'s consistency hole — `account_subtype` is patchable and is never
validated against the account's type — is also untouched and still needs settling
with whatever answers `OQ-CUS-12356`.

## 2026-09-18 — `OQ-RAT-12410` CLOSED: the seasonal / time-of-use editor was drawn, shown and approved, and one signed rule is deliberately diverged from

**PO, verbatim, approving the drawing:** *"this is good - Wave 4 — the seasonal /
time-of-use editor"*. **Unblocking the work in the first place:** *"please design
it - as per ui rules we have - fix these alos"*. **And on the shape itself:** *"so
first select the season and within season select time of use within a given day"*.

**Why this question existed at all.** The Plans & Rates blueprint draws the TIERED
editor in full on p046 and draws neither of the other two — three mentions of
*season* in 126 pages, none of them a layout. B14 rules 41 and 42 say a screen is
built from its drawing, so a lane with no drawing may not invent one from a task
sentence. `OQ-RAT-12410` was minted on 2026-09-17 for exactly that reason and the
previous lane stopped at it rather than guessing. The PO ruling above is the
drawing being commissioned, shown and accepted — the *draw it, show it, get a yes,
then build* sequence, with the middle step taken.

### The five decisions, as they were put and approved

1. **ONE panel — *Seasons and their windows* — instead of two.** `TouEditor` was
   rendering a `SeasonEditor` beside itself, so a clerk who picked *Time-of-use*
   was also shown a *Seasons* panel and could not tell whether they had chosen
   wrongly. The PO reported it as *"when time of use is slected it show time of
   use and also seasonal"*.
2. **A window NESTS under the season it belongs to** and is added from inside
   that season, never from a shared button at the bottom.
3. **The per-window Season dropdown is removed.** This is the point of the
   design rather than a tidy-up: a window nested under Summer already is in
   Summer, so *forgot to pick a season* becomes UNREACHABLE rather than refused.
   That is the move `DEF-RAT-5717` made for tiers, and unreachable beats refused.
4. **Month chosen by NAME, day bounded by the month chosen**, so 31 April cannot
   be typed.
5. **The range echoed back** — *1 Apr – 30 Sep* — with gaps and overlaps named as
   the clerk types instead of at activation.

⚠ **THE MODEL UNDERNEATH WAS ALREADY RIGHT AND WAS NOT TOUCHED.** A TOU window is
per (season × day type), so a time-of-use schedule genuinely HAS seasons, and the
nested editor carrying no price was correct too. Only the DRAWING was at fault.
The seasonal structure now uses the same panel in a second mode, so the two
structures cannot drift apart.

### The stated divergence from `BR-SHL-033`, which is the part that needed a ruling

`BR-SHL-033` (PO, 2026-08-09) makes EVERY date field a `DatePickerField`. **That
control's value is a `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date, read off the component rather
than assumed. A season boundary is a month and a day with NO year** — it recurs
every year — so the control cannot express it, and two `SelectField`s are used
instead.

**This is a divergence from a signed rule, so it was put to the PO with the
alternative offered explicitly rather than decided by a lane**, and it is covered
by the same approval. It was named in `OQ-RAT-12410` when the question was minted
precisely so it would be decided WITH the drawing instead of discovered in review.
**The divergence is narrow and is the whole of it:** every other date field in
this wizard — effective from, effective to, the filing dates — is still a
`DatePickerField`, and `BR-SHL-033` is otherwise untouched. The dropdown half of
the same rule is obeyed rather than diverged from: the size picker measures
`LONG_LIST_THRESHOLD` against the list actually offered and switches to
`SearchSelectField` past it.

### What was built, and the four defects it answers

`SeasonsAndWindows` replaces `SeasonEditor` and `TouEditor` with one component in
two modes (`seasonal` | `tou`). The draft now carries a minted `season_key` rather
than the season's LABEL, because the label is the one field a clerk retypes —
renaming *Summer* to *Peak* used to turn every window pointing at it into
`rating.tou.unknown_season` at activation, and two unnamed seasons were worse
still, both being `""`. **The server contract did not move:** `structurePayload`
resolves the key back to the label the API expects, through a single bridge
(`seasonKeyForLabel` / `seasonLabelForKey`) so the two ends cannot disagree.

The coverage check walks the same 2001 reference year `_season_intervals` uses —
2001 because it is NOT a leap year, so 29 February never participates and
`date(2001, 2, 29)` raises. The screen and the server therefore cannot disagree
about whether a year is covered; what the screen ADDS is WHICH of gap or overlap
it is and WHERE, because the server sends one message for both.

Month names come from `Intl` through `DateCell`'s newly exported `monthLabel`,
never from a catalogue: **B14 rule 35 says a catalogue is written in its own
language, and twelve hand-written month names in eleven files would breach it the
day a twelfth language is added.**

`DEF-RAT-5736` (the two panels) · `DEF-RAT-5733` (the season boundary) ·
`DEF-RAT-5734` (pick, price, then Add) · `DEF-RAT-5735` (the rule 33 sweep).

⚠ **`DEF-RAT-5736` WAS FILED AS `DEF-RAT-5732` AND RENUMBERED BEFORE IT WAS
PUSHED.** A sibling lane took 5732 for `DEF-GOV-5732` while this lane was working,
and both lanes computed *the register maximum plus one* correctly — the numbers
came from different worlds, which is law 11's allocated-id clause exactly.
`allocate.py defect --verify 5732` is what said so, at push time, which is the
only moment the answer can be final.

### What this does NOT settle

`DEF-RAT-5735` is closed as **partially fixed** and the residue is stated rather
than left to be discovered. Measured on `en.json`: of the `rating.rate.*` keys,
**35 ran past twelve words before this wave and 0 live strings do now** — the
three at 29 words (`sizes.legacyBase`, `filing.captureOnly`, `baseOnlyGap`) are
gone, and the rationale they carried moved into the code beside the string, which
is what rule 33 requires of rationale and what a docstring is for.

**Twelve words is not the whole of rule 33 and this is the honest gap:** the rule
caps by KIND — a fact at six words, an instruction at six words PER SENTENCE — and
roughly **28 strings that still render exceed six words in their worst sentence**
while being under twelve. They were NOT cut in this wave, deliberately: cutting a
load-bearing explanation is a defect that reads as tidiness, and a silent cut is
the failure mode this row was written to avoid. **Six catalogue keys are now
orphans** — `sizes.tierOverrideGap`, `impact.notComputed`, `review.notSavedYet`,
`baseChargeHelp`, `baseChargeLabel`, `sizes.setAllHelp` — held in all eleven
catalogues and referenced by no non-test source. They are left in place rather
than deleted, because an absence is invisible to every check this repo has
(`DEF-CUS-3653`) and a computed key family can name one without naming it
literally; removing them is catalogue hygiene and wants its own measured pass.


## 2026-09-18 · `OQ-RAT-12409` OPTION A IS BUILT — AND THE PLAN'S INVARIANT IS THE COUNTER, NOT A WINDOW

Shipped in `c58b4e7ec` at `2.305.0`, closing `DEF-RAT-5710`. The ruling itself is
recorded above; this is what was JUDGED while building it, because four of these
were decisions and not transcription.

### ⚠ THE ONE THAT MATTERS: A PLAN HAS NO WINDOW, SO WHAT DOES A CORRECTION HOLD FIXED?

`BR-RAT-104` and `BR-RAT-1016` both define a correction by the WINDOW: it is
copied from the row being corrected and never read from the payload, and without
that property a "correction" is a backdated change wearing a correction's
clothes. `correct_tax` and `correct_rate_schedule_version` are both built on it.

**A plan version has no window at all** — `OQ-324` records that omission as
deliberate, and `plan_versions` has no `effective_from` to copy. So the rule as
written has nothing to bite on here, and copying it literally would have produced
a verb with no defining property at all.

**The judgment: the equivalent invariant is the COUNTER.** `version_no` is copied
from the row being corrected, `rate_plans.version` does not move, and a payload
naming `version` or `version_no` is refused **BY NAME** rather than ignored in
silence — `correct_rate_schedule_version`'s posture for a date, for its stated
reason: a caller that sent one believed it would be honoured.

**Why the counter and not something else:** it is the only thing about a plan
version that anything outside rating reads. `unit_plan_assignments.plan_version`
snapshots it at assignment (`BR-CUS-013`) and those rows outlive the plan — **75
of them on `SCW-RES`, every one at `plan_version = 1`**. A version minted for a
typo is a number they point at for ever, which is the whole of `DEF-RAT-5710`.

### THE SCREEN SHOWS NO COUNT OF ISSUED BILLS, AND THAT IS A DECISION

`correct_tax` and `correct_rate_schedule_version` both answer with a count of
bills already issued, because an invoice line stamps `tariff_version_id`
(`DEF-276`) and the count is exact. **There is no equivalent for a plan.**
`BR-BIL-030` locks what a bill priced into the bill, so nothing on `invoices` or
`invoice_lines` points back at a plan; the only link is `plan → plan_rate_schedules
→ tariff_versions → invoice_lines`, which `billing.selectors.plan_invoice_count`
walks — and it counts **LINES, not bills**, and over-counts when two plans share
a tariff, which its own docstring says and `OQ-185` records.

**Measured rather than reasoned about: it answers 640 for `SCW-RES` where that
tenant holds 135 issued invoices.** Printing 640 beside the word *bills* would
overstate a money consequence roughly fivefold, so the screen states the
consequence in words and states no figure, and a test asserts the absence so a
later lane has to delete a line to add an approximate count.

### THE AUDIT TAB BROKE IN THREE PLACES AT ONCE, SILENTLY, AND NONE OF THEM IS THE FEATURE

`version_no` stopped being unique the moment the partial key landed, and PLN-02's
Versions tab was built on the assumption that it was. Every one of these passed
`tsc` and every existing test:

* **THE STATUS PILL.** `versionNo === detail.version` was the whole test, so both
  rows at v1 wore the plan's own `Published` pill — the screen would say the plan
  is published twice over, once on the filing that was just declared wrong. It
  reads `superseded_by` now, which is set on exactly the row that no longer
  states what the plan says.
* **THE REACT KEY.** Two `<tr>` under one key is a silent rendering fault, and it
  would have landed on the exact pair a correction exists to make readable.
* **THE AUTHORED SENTENCE.** `change_reason` TRAVELS to the correction unchanged,
  because the filing did not change — only what it says did. Printing it on the
  correction would repeat the old sentence under the new one and say nothing
  about the fix, which is `DEF-RAT-5710` wearing a screen.

**And the selector's sort gained a second key for the same root cause.**
`plan_versions` reads `rows[index + 1]` as "the previous row", so `-version_no`
alone would not merely reorder the table — it would invert the arithmetic under
it and print a correction's own fix backwards. `-created_at` puts the correction
directly above the row it corrects, which is what makes the same subtraction go
on meaning *what did this row change*.

⚠ **THE GENERAL LESSON, AND IT IS THIS REPO'S OWN:** making a unique key partial
is a one-line migration whose blast radius is every screen that ever treated the
key as an identity. Nothing greps for that. **When a uniqueness guarantee is
weakened, grep for the CONSUMERS of the thing that was unique** — it is hard rule
8's *"before retiring a value, grep for its consumers"* with the value still
present and only its uniqueness gone, which is harder to see and fails the same
way.

### ⚠ A FINDING FILED RATHER THAN LEFT IN PROSE — `DEF-RAT-5738`

The bound-change view ruled the same day derives from `rate_change_log`. Scoping
it turned up that **only three entity types are ever written to that table from
anywhere in rating — `schedule`, `charge` and `plan`** (plus `rate_change_batch`
and `unit_plan_assignment` for other purposes). **No tax path and no discount path
writes one**, not `update_tax`, not `correct_tax`, not any discount service; the
literal set in the module is exhaustive. So a view derived from that log can
answer for two of the four object kinds the PO named — *"Rate, taxes, Charge
code, Discounts"* — and is structurally blind to the other two. It would report
ZERO for a tax that moved yesterday, truthfully, over a scope it silently
excludes (hard-won law 7).

It is filed as `DEF-RAT-5738` rather than written only here, because CLAUDE.md
hard rule 4's own lesson is that a finding recorded in the file you happen to be
in is a finding nobody can count — two lanes wrote `OQ-1330` in prose and it
spread to 54 citations. **The bound-change view is NOT built in this commit**,
and building it before this gap is closed would ship a screen that is blind by
construction and says so nowhere.

## 2026-09-18 · THE BOUND-CHANGE VIEW IS BUILT, AND IT STATES ITS OWN BLIND SPOT

Shipped in `f9481bcb4` at `2.306.0`, against the PO ruling of the same day —
*"every time Rate, taxes, Charge code, Discounts are changed, at apporval we need
to take action to inform Plan about it - Fix this"*. `GET /plans/{id}/bound-changes`,
paged from the server, drawn on PLN-02's Audit tab beside the versions table.

The design was already recorded above and is unchanged: **derived from
`rate_change_log`, never stored**, so a missed notification costs an alert and
never costs the truth. What follows is what was JUDGED while building it.

### ⚠ IT ANSWERS FOR TWO OF THE FOUR KINDS THE PO NAMED, AND SAYS SO ON SCREEN

**Only three `entity_type` values are ever written to `rate_change_log` from
anywhere in rating — `schedule`, `charge` and `plan`.** No tax path and no
discount path writes one: not `update_tax`, not `correct_tax`, not any discount
service. The literal set in the module is exhaustive and was read rather than
assumed. That is `DEF-RAT-5738`.

**The judgment: build it, and print what was skipped beside what was checked.**
The alternative considered and rejected was to wait for `DEF-RAT-5738` — which
would have left the rate-schedule case, the first thing the PO named and the one
that actually moves money, unbuilt for the sake of tidiness. The other
alternative, shipping it silent, is the one hard-won law 7 names outright: **a
declared blind spot with no number attached is indistinguishable from an empty
one**, and `G32` reported *0 unresolved* truthfully over 21 live refusals for
exactly that reason.

**So the coverage is served as DATA and not as a sentence.** The server answers
with `covered`, `uncovered` and `uncovered_defect`; the screen renders one
six-word line from `uncovered` and draws nothing when it is empty. The day a tax
change writes a log row, the apology deletes itself — and a test asserts both
halves, so whoever fixes the defect has to delete `"tax"` from an assertion,
which is the moment the screen should stop apologising. **A hold with no test
that fires when it expires is a promise nobody is keeping** (hard-won law 2's
second clause); this is that test, written in the same commit as the hold.

### ⚠ THE FALSE PASS THIS FEATURE HAD TO BE WRITTEN AGAINST

Law 7's second habit — *ask what would make this check pass wrongly* — found a
real one before it shipped. The filter is built from the ids a plan binds, and a
plan that binds **nothing** yields an empty id list. Assembling the predicate
from an empty list without an explicit match-nothing term produces a bare `Q()`,
**which matches EVERY row** — so a plan binding nothing would have been told
about the whole tenant's change log, and it would have looked like a working
feature with data in it. `plan_bound_changes_queryset` starts from `Q(pk__in=[])`
and `test_a_plan_that_binds_nothing_returns_nothing_not_everything` is the case.

### THE `NFR-3` TEST ASSERTS THE TWO THINGS THAT ACTUALLY DIFFER

A list paginated in Python and a queryset paginated in SQL produce the **same**
`count` and the **same** `results`, so neither alone can tell them apart. The
test asserts that the selector returns a `QuerySet` **and** that a set larger
than one page reports the whole count over one page of rows. ⚠ **And the obvious
version of that second half is a false pass:** `per=2` reads like a page of two
and `clamp_page_size` silently raises it to 50 — the floor of `PAGE_SIZES` — so
a five-row fixture returns all five and a Python-paginated list would have passed.
The set has to cross fifty for the cut to be observable at all.

### IT IS NOT A PLAN VERSION, AND IT EXCLUDES THE PLAN'S OWN CHANGES

`rate_plans.version` does not move and no `plan_versions` row is written — a
bound object changing is not a change to the PLAN, which is the whole point of
the ruling. The queryset also excludes `entity_type='plan'`: that is the Audit
tab's own subject, drawn in full in the panel directly above, and folding the two
together would let a plan's own edits drown the one signal this was built to
carry.

### A READ THAT HAS NOT ANSWERED IS NOT AN EMPTY LIST

On this screen the two would say opposite things, and *"nothing has changed
underneath you"* is exactly the reassurance a read that failed must never give.
Three states are drawn apart and asserted apart.

## 2026-09-18 — law 14 gets a mechanism: `config/settings/pgtest.py`, and the proof that it can see what the default suite cannot (`DEF-GOV-5740`)

**The gap, stated plainly.** Hard-won law 14 says *"any code that catches a
database error and continues MUST be proved on PostgreSQL, not on the default
suite."* It has said so since 2026-08-29, written from two lanes finding the
same trap independently, in different modules, weeks apart. **The repo provided
no way to do it.** `config/settings/test.py` replaces `DATABASES` wholesale with
SQLite and ignores `DATABASE_URL` — it says so in its own line 6 — so obeying
the law meant hand-rolling a settings file, every time, from memory.

⚠ **AND THE HAND-ROLLED ONE WRITTEN TODAY WAS ALREADY WRONG.** It hardcoded a
single shared test-database name, which walks straight back into `DEF-054`: two
lanes against one PostgreSQL, one dropping the database under the other, fifty
minutes lost and `assert not self._finalizers` surfacing as a defect in whatever
file happened to be executing. `base.py` had already solved that — it derives
`test_sbh_<checkout>_<hash>` per checkout precisely because *"a `git worktree`
isolates the FILES and shares the DATABASE, which is one level worse"* — and its
own comment says that name matters *"only when a lane runs against real
PostgreSQL, which is the one place it is needed."* **The need was anticipated in
writing and the way in was never built.** A workaround everybody reinvents is a
gap in the repo, and reinventing it badly is what gaps cost.

**What landed.** `config/settings/pgtest.py` changes the DATABASE and nothing
else: `from .test import *`, then `DATABASES` re-imported from `base.py` so it
carries the repo's own `env.db()` parsing AND the per-checkout `TEST["NAME"]`.
Everything else — fixtures, eager jobs, the malware test double — is `test.py`'s,
unchanged, so a difference in outcome between the two runs is attributable to one
variable.

**IT FAILS CLOSED, AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART.** A settings module that
silently left SQLite in place would report a green run over the exact class of
bug it exists to catch — law 7's *incapable of failing* shape, wearing the name
of the fix. It raises instead, and the message names the law. **Proved by
pointing it at a SQLite URL and watching it refuse**, not by reading the code.

**THE DIFFERENCE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED** —
`tests/test_law14_postgres_transaction_shape.py`, same file, same command, one
variable different:

    default settings (SQLite)        1 passed, 2 skipped
    --ds=config.settings.pgtest      3 passed

The two that skip are the two that matter: a failed statement poisoning the rest
of the transaction, and a `SAVEPOINT` being what makes carrying on work. **A SKIP
on SQLite is the law being true, not the test being unavailable**, and the skip
reason says so.

⚠ **A MISTAKE OF MINE, RECORDED BECAUSE THE NEXT LANE WILL MAKE IT.** The first
"SQLite" run reported **3 passed** and I nearly reported that as the baseline. It
was not SQLite at all: `.env.example` sets
`DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.production`, so `set -a; . ./.env` exports
it and **pytest silently runs under production settings against the real
database**. The environment variable beats `pytest.ini`. Export only
`DATABASE_URL` and `SBH_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` for a test run, never the whole
file. **What caught it was the count, not the outcome**: three passes where two
skips were expected. An unexpected PASS deserves the same suspicion as a failure,
which is law 7's habit (2) — *ask what would make this check pass wrongly* —
arriving from the other direction.

**What this does NOT change.** `pytest` still defaults to SQLite and should: it
is faster and catches everything that is not transaction-shaped. This is for code
that CATCHES a database error and carries on, depends on a SAVEPOINT, asserts a
constraint fires, or has row-level security as its subject — RLS being untestable
on SQLite is recorded at `test.py` line 3 and is the same gap seen from another
angle.

**Already used in anger, the same hour.** The plan-correction verb
(`OQ-RAT-12409` option A) shipped with its `IntegrityError` path proved only on
SQLite; the lane said so honestly and could not close it. Run through this module:
**13 of 13 pass on real PostgreSQL**, the duplicate-filing refusal inside its
savepoint included.

## 2026-09-18 — the add control moves ABOVE the list on a plan's three binding steps (2.307.1)

**The ruling, verbatim**, on seeing the rebuilt screens in a browser: *"is it
possible to move add - dropdown search = add button above the table istead below
the table on all 3 screens"*. Charges, taxes and discounts.

**The reason it is right, stated so the next lane does not undo it.** On those
three steps the add control is the PRIMARY act — a clerk opens them in order to
attach something, and the table is the record of what they have attached so far.
A control reached for first should not sit under a list that grows.

**ONE OPT-IN PROP, NOT A GLOBAL FLIP — and that is the whole judgment here.**
`EditableTable` is shared. The work template builder passes `addRow` **five
times** and asked for none of this; `RateScheduleWizard` uses the component and
passes no add row at all. Moving it unconditionally would have rearranged a
module nobody was looking at, on one screen's authority. `addRowPosition`
therefore defaults to `"below"`, so **nothing that exists moves**, and the three
plan wizard call sites opt in. Same shape and the same reasoning as
`rowRemoveBlocked` one commit earlier, and B14 rule 36's: extend the kit, never
copy it into a screen.

The divider follows the position — `border-b` above, `border-t` below. Not
cosmetic: a divider on the wrong side reads as the add row belonging to whatever
lies beyond it.

⚠ **THE EXISTING TESTS COULD NOT SEE THIS CHANGE AT ALL, AND THAT IS THE PART
WORTH KEEPING.** All **50** cases across `EditableTable.dom.test.tsx` and
`planWizardTables.dom.test.tsx` passed BEFORE the move and after it — not one of
them asserts where the add row sits, so they would have been just as green had
nothing been done. That is law 7's *incapable of failing* shape sitting quietly
inside a suite that looks thorough, on a screen that had just been rebuilt and
reviewed.

**The three new cases assert DOCUMENT ORDER, not a class and not an attribute**,
because order is the actual requirement: a test reading `data-editable-addrow`
would pass over a block carrying the right marker in the wrong place — law 7's
*looking at the wrong thing*.

**PROVED RED BOTH WAYS BEFORE TRUSTED GREEN.** Forcing `addAbove = false` failed
the "above" case; forcing `addAbove = true` failed **both** "below" cases.
Restored: **53 passed**, `tsc --noEmit` clean. **The default case is the
load-bearing one** — if `"above"` ever becomes the default, the work template
builder rearranges silently, and that test now goes red first and names it.

**Seen rendered, not only tested (hard-won law 6).** Rebuilt and re-walked in
Chromium against the live backend, on the real `Residential Standard` plan of
brazosbend, all six wizard steps, **zero page errors and zero failed requests**.
No gate in this repo reads rendered output, so this is the only check that could
have confirmed the control actually moved.
