## 2026-09-19 — `DEF-MET-5802` · `DEF-MET-5803` — THE IMPORT TEMPLATES ARE CURATED, AND ONE OF THE TWO DEFECTS WAS NOT REAL

**PO, 2026-09-19, having read the generated premises and units import
templates:** *"okay I want updated CSV file"*. The corrected files are committed
at `12-governance/24-import-templates/` and the header rows are quoted in its
README, so they can be read without running anything.

### 1 · WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG: NOBODY HAD CHOSEN THESE COLUMNS

Premises and units DERIVED their offered columns from the model's own `_meta`
(`BR-MET-088`) while the other five targets DECLARE theirs. Derivation was the
right call and its own docstring says why — *"the picker cannot offer a target
with no column behind it and cannot omit one that exists"* — but it cannot judge
whether a column is a **utility's to supply**. So every field added to the
premises table was published to every customer's template the next day, wearing
a heading generated from its field name. That is how **"Gis parcel id was"** and
**"Gis verified at"** became things a utility was asked to fill in.

**Removed — premises (9):** `gis_unchecked`, `gis_checked_by`, `gis_checked_at`,
`gis_parcel_id_was`, `gis_key_changed_at`, `gis_status`, `gis_verified`,
`gis_verified_at`, `owner_manager`.
**Removed — units (5):** `gis_point_id_was`, `gis_key_changed_at`, `gis_status`,
`gis_verified`, `gis_verified_at`.

⚠ **FOURTEEN, NOT TWELVE.** The defect row's own title says *"12 columns nobody
chose"* and its body then names nine and five. The lists are what was approved
and the lists are what was removed; the headline number was never right. Counted
as distinct NAMES across the two targets it is ten, which is probably where
twelve came from, and none of the three numbers is the one that matters.

**Kept, and this is the dividing line the whole defect turns on:**
`gis_parcel_id` and `gis_point_id` are what a **CITY GIVES A UTILITY** and are
in the file being migrated. Everything else in that block is written by our own
address-matching process. Both kept keys were also relabelled — `GIS parcel ID`,
`GIS point ID` — because a kept column still wearing a heading generated from
its field name is the same complaint one size smaller.

Measured: premises **31 → 23** offered columns, units **20 → 15**.

### 2 · CURATE, NOT FILTER — AND THE REVERSAL IS THE POINT

The first recommendation was to keep deriving and FILTER out the machine-written
fields. The PO's own question is what refused it: **a filter removes the noise
and can never surface a column that is MISSING**, because no filter finds
something that was never there. So the two targets now DECLARE their columns
like the other five.

⚠ **A DECLARATION LOSES HALF OF `BR-MET-088` AND HAS TO BUY IT BACK.** Derivation
guaranteed both *cannot offer a column that does not exist* AND *cannot omit one
that does*. Declaring keeps the first for free and loses the second. It is
bought back by `NOT_OFFERED_COLUMNS_BY_TARGET` — every withheld column named
**with its reason** — and by `tests/test_def_met_5802_declared_columns.py::
test_every_model_column_is_classified`, which fails, naming the field, when a
model column appears in neither table. **Add a field to `premises` and somebody
now has to decide whether a utility supplies it.** The previous mechanism made
that decision silently, every time, and always answered yes.

### 3 · `DEF-MET-5803` WAS NOT REAL AS FILED, AND THE MIS-DIAGNOSIS IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX

It was filed saying the premises template carries *"no name field"* and that the
only name-shaped column was `owner_manager`. **Both halves are false.**

`Premises.owner` is a real column, offered, labelled `Owner`, and it is the one
`owner_account_verdict` reads as the owner's NAME through `mapped["owner_ref"]`.
Printed, not inferred — a row carrying a company, a Tax ID and an account type
but no `owner_ref` answers `no_owner`, and the same row with a name answers
`eligible`. **An owner could never be created without a name.** The opposite of
what the row said.

The report came from reading `PREMISES_OWNER_COLUMNS` — the six VIRTUAL identity
columns — where the name is legitimately absent, **because it was being supplied
by the derived set this very change replaces.** Reading a definition answered
one question; running the function answered a different one, and only the second
was the product.

**WHAT WAS REAL, and it explains the report:** the template offered **two
name-shaped columns and only one of them created anybody** — `Owner` and `Owner
name (legacy)`. A utility filling in the more explicit-sounding of the two got
an address and no owner account, with nothing saying so. Retiring the legacy box
(§1) removes the decoy, and the survivor is relabelled **`Owner name`**.

⚠ The label could only move to a string already in that column's alias tuple, or
the sample stops auto-detecting its own header (`DEF-1077`). `owner name` was
already one of `owner`'s four aliases, which is what made the rename safe rather
than merely nicer; the test asserts that constraint rather than trusting it.

**So the two rows land together, but for the OPPOSITE reason to the one filed.**
The filed reason was *"or the template loses its last name-shaped field"*. The
real one is that removing the decoy is what makes the remaining name column
unambiguous.

### 4 · THE OWNER EMAIL — THE JUDGMENT, AND WHAT IT TURNED ON

**Decided: YES, an owner email belongs, and it is CONTACT and never IDENTITY.**

* An owner master account is created **ACTIVE and it bills**. Six identity
  columns and no contact column means a utility can load 5,000 owners who can be
  billed and not reached — no emailed bill, no portal invitation. For a landlord
  with 200 units, which is the master-account case, that is the whole point of
  the portal.
* **The other door already has it.** The Accounts import — the other way a
  customer is created here — has carried `Email` and `Phone` all along. Two
  doors to one act should not disagree about what may be supplied, which is
  `CR-058`'s own reasoning.
* **It cost no new contract.** `create_master_account` already validates a
  `contact` block and `ensure_master_account_for_premises` already forwards one
  verbatim; the import simply never sent one. Nothing in `customers` moved.
* An import is a **one-time bulk act**. A column absent from it means 5,000
  emails typed in by hand afterwards, one screen at a time, or never.

⚠ **THE RISK, AND THE GUARD ON IT.** The PO ruled on 2026-09-01 that a party is
created from *"DL, SSN, Phone or Tax ID"*. Adding `owner_email` to
`OWNER_IDENTIFIER_COLUMNS` is a one-line edit that would look like a tidy-up and
would let a name-and-email row mint a Customer #, reversing a signed ruling. A
test asserts a name-plus-email row is still `awaiting_identity`.

⚠ **IT IS WIRED, NOT JUST OFFERED** (hard-won law 2). `owner_contact_block`
builds the block the load hands to the account door, and a test asserts the
email reaches it. **With no email it answers `{}`**, `_validate_contact` reads
`{}` as `None`, and the door falls back to the premises' own `owner_manager` —
which `_resolve_owner_ref` has already written from the same `Owner name` cell.
A file with no email therefore behaves exactly as it did before, down to the
contact's name.

### 5 · THE STOP-CONDITION ON RETIRING `owner_manager`, CHECKED BY RUNNING IT

`customers.create_master_account` falls back to `premises.owner_manager` for the
contact's name and **refuses by name** without it. If retiring the column had
stopped that field being written, every imported owner account would have lost
its name — an absence, which CLAUDE.md records as invisible to every check this
repo has.

It does not. `_resolve_owner_ref` writes `owner_manager` from the `Owner name`
cell regardless of whether the column is mapped. **Run, not read**, on the
first-migration branch where no party is on file: in `{"owner_ref": "Balcones
Development LLC"}` → out `{"owner_manager": "Balcones Development LLC",
"owner_id": None}`. Pinned by a test, on that branch.

### 6 · WHAT REMOVING A COLUMN DOES TO A SAVED MAPPING — IT USED TO CRASH THE RUN

A tenant's saved `ImportMapping` is a row written months ago; retiring a column
does not go back and edit it. `_detected_mapping` returned a recognised
template's map **verbatim**, so a template naming `owner_manager` would pre-fill
the picker with a column that no longer exists, the operator would confirm it,
and `_transform_locked` would refuse the whole run with
`metering.import.unknown_mapping_target`. **A run that cannot be mapped at all
is not an honest degradation — it is a crash with a message key.**

A retired target is now DROPPED, so its source column arrives UNMAPPED and the
operator is asked to decide about it; the rest of their map survives, including
an explicit `— ignore —`, which is a mapping choice and not a column.
`_auto_map` has always done exactly this — *"the model lost the column —
BR-MET-088 wins over the alias"* — and only this branch was missing it. The
asymmetry was invisible while the set was derived, because a column could then
only vanish by being dropped from the table.

The two **system** defaults are generated from `sample_columns` and follow by
construction. Existing tenants' rows were written at provisioning; they are
refreshed by a reference-data replay (`import_mappings` is in
`RERUN_REFERENCE_LISTS` and the handler updates an existing system row's
mapping). Until that replay runs, the drop above is what keeps a stale default
from refusing a run.

### 7 · FOUR SAMPLE CELLS THAT WERE ASKING A UTILITY TO ACCEPT AN INVENTED VALUE

Reading the generated file — the thing the PO asked for — showed `Lat` reading
**`Sample lat`**, `Lng` **`Sample lng`**, `GIS parcel ID` **`Sample gis parcel
id`** and `GIS point ID` **`Sample gis point id`**. `DEF-962`'s ruling already
covers this and these four were simply never enumerated, so they fell through to
the generic fallback. All four ship BLANK now. A latitude whose worked cell is
the words *"Sample lat"* is not an example, it is a parse failure with a
friendly name.

Found by reading the output, by nothing else: no check in this repo compares a
sample cell with the column it sits under.

### 8 · WHAT IS STILL MISSING AND IS NOT OURS TO ADD — FILED, NOT BUILT

**There is no owner CATEGORY column.** Reproduced end to end on real PostgreSQL:
a row naming an owner **not already on file** gets a master account with **no
owner party attached** — `premises.owner_id` `None`, no `premises_owners` row,
the name in the legacy free-text box only. The same file with the owner already
on file works perfectly. **On a first migration nobody is on file, so every row
takes that branch.**

`ensure_master_account_for_premises` declines to create the party deliberately:
`premises_owners.category_id` is NOT NULL and `BR-MET-151` clause 3 forbids
reading a category off a name. That reasoning is sound and was not worked
around. The five categories are an editable Settings lookup and the import
offers no column for them — verified by printing the offered set, where neither
`owner_category` nor `category` appears.

**It changes the shipped CSV template, so it is the PO's to decide.** Filed and
left OPEN; nothing built.

### 9 · HOW IT WAS PROVED

Law 7 asks for a guard shown failing on the defect it was written for, in the
harness that runs it. These are pytest tests, so pytest is that harness.

A run against the pristine tip errored at COLLECTION —
`AttributeError: module 'apps.metering.import_runs' has no attribute
'DECLARED_COLUMNS_BY_TARGET'` — which proves the symbols are new and **proves
nothing about whether the assertions bite**. So each check was then shown red by
MUTATING the finished code in a separate worktree, one defect per check: a
machine-written GIS column put back on the template, `owner` dropped from the
premises contract, a model field classified nowhere, the email un-wired from the
account door, and the saved-template filter removed.

⚠ **ONE CHECK OF MINE WAS WRONG AND WENT RED ON THE CORRECT BUILD.** It asserted
no heading starts with `"gis "` — which `GIS parcel ID`, a KEPT column with a
deliberately curated heading, does. It is a check that could not pass. It now
asserts the kept key's heading BY VALUE and that it differs from the one
generated from its field name. Law 7's *"ask what would make this pass wrongly"*
would have caught it; the comment recording that is left in the test.

⚠ **EVERY ASSERTION NAMES COLUMNS, NEVER COUNTS.** *"The premises template has
23 columns"* passes on the wrong 23 — it would pass on a template that had lost
`owner` and kept a GIS field. `test_the_premises_contract_still_names_the_owner`
exists for exactly the mis-diagnosis in §3, and is the one check every other
test in the file would have stayed green without.

### 10 · ONE EXISTING TEST CHANGED ITS ANSWER, AND WAS AMENDED RATHER THAN DELETED

`test_def650_owner_is_the_master_account.py::test_def1247__the_Owner_header_maps_
to_the_TYPED_owner_not_the_free_text` asserted
`{"Owner": "owner", "Owner / manager": "owner_manager"}` — *"both headers must be
claimed, one each"* — which was right while both columns were offered. It now
asserts `{"Owner": "owner"}`.

**What `DEF-1247` was protecting is unchanged and is still asserted first**: the
free-text column must never claim the `owner` header. The test also now asserts
the alias is still INTACT and the COLUMN withheld, because a header can go
unclaimed by deleting the alias — a different and much worse change that would
take the `owner` header's own protection with it.

### 11 · THE OWNER CATEGORY — BUILT, UNDER THE RULING OF THE SAME DAY

**PO, verbatim: *"Yes add owner category column in csv template"*.** §8 above was
written when this was still `OPEN`; it was ruled the same afternoon and is built
here. The reasoning that made it safe is in the decision entry of 2026-09-19
(*"THE PREMISES IMPORT MAKES AN ACCOUNT NOBODY OWNS"*) and is not repeated.

**What it does:** a premises row that STATES a category has its owner party
created and linked, so the address ends with an owner and the account ends with
an owner record — `premises_owners.master_account_id` written, which is the
declared link `DEF-2902`/`DEF-2903` report missing from every master account.

⚠ **IT IS NOT A THIRD CREATION PATH.** The party is created through
`match_premises_owner` — the same door a person uses on `PRM-04`, which takes
the CALLER's category, links `premises.owner_id`, audits both writes and leaves
`owner_manager` alone as `BR-MET-151` clause 4 provenance. The premises then HAS
a typed owner, so `ensure_master_account_for_premises` takes its existing
already-on-file branch **unchanged**. Nothing reaches around `customers`' door.

⚠ **A BLANK CELL IS NOT AN ERROR AND DOES NOT BECOME ONE.** No default, no
guess: the address loads, the owner account is still created, the party waits
for a person — today's behaviour exactly — and `PRM.OWNER_CATEGORY_MISSING`
says so at rehearsal as a WARNING + FLAG_ONLY. An ERROR would refuse the first
upload a utility ever sends, which is `DEF-1088`'s lesson in as many words.

⚠ **AND ONLY ON THE ELIGIBLE PATH.** A name and a category with NO identifier
still creates nothing, exactly as ruled on 2026-09-01. This ruling is about the
master account not being generated; it does not widen what earns one.

**`BR-MET-402` clause 5 is NARROWED, not reversed**, and stamped at its own
sentence: *no party from a NAME ALONE*. `premises_owners.category_id` is still
NOT NULL and `BR-MET-151` clause 3 still forbids reading a category off a name.
**Being TOLD a category was never the same act as reading one off a name** —
which is why the ruling sits inside clause 3 rather than against it. The new
rule is `BR-MET-1175`.

### 12 · THE FIFTH VERDICT NOW HAS A COUNTER

`owner_account_verdict` answers five ways and the loader's chain had a branch
for four. A row whose Owner cell names nobody was warned at rehearsal — *"This
row names no owner."* — and then counted nowhere, so `premises_owner_blank` and
`premises_with_no_owner` both read 0 over it. **PO: *"this is correct"*.**

That is law 7's *reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes*, in a receipt
rather than a gate: four owner figures printed and a fifth could not, so four
zeroes read as a clean run. It has a branch, a receipt key
(`premises_owner_no_owner_named`) and a tile field now, matching the four
already there. **The guard is a test that reads the chain's SOURCE and asserts
every verdict constant appears in it**, deliberately a source check: reaching
that branch through a real load needs a row several other rules also fire on.

### 13 · TWO BUGS THIS CHANGE INTRODUCED, BOTH CAUGHT BY ITS OWN TESTS

Recorded because the escape route matters more than the bug, and both were the
same species: **a column that exists everywhere except where it is read.**

**(a) `TypeError: Premises() got unexpected keyword arguments:
'owner_category_raw'`** — on every row that filled the column in. A
`KIND_LOOKUP` column writes `<target>_raw` beside the resolved code, and
`_NOT_A_COLUMN` spread the owner column NAMES from one declaration while
hand-typing `"owner_account_type_raw"` as a single literal.
⚠ **THE COMMENT FOUR LINES ABOVE THAT LITERAL HAD PREDICTED IT** — *"a seventh
owner column added above and forgotten below would be a 500 on every row of
somebody's migration"*. It was right, it was read, and it was **not a guard**
(hard-won law 1). Both halves are derived now, and a test pins it.

**(b) THE COLUMN RESOLVED TO NOTHING AND SAID `Matched`.** `LOOKUP_INDEX_
BUILDERS` had no `owner_category` entry, and the lookup branch reads
`lookup_indexes.get(target) or {}` — so every cell resolved to `None`. The
column shipped, mapped cleanly, showed **Matched**, and created no party.
**Nothing errored anywhere.** That is `DEF-771`'s exact shape (*"9,881 rows said
`city customer plan`, mapped clean, showed Matched, and loaded 9,881 units with
no plan"*), and **no check that reads the column contract could have seen it** —
which is most of this file's other tests. The index exists, and a test now
asserts every lookup column on a target HAS one and that it is not empty.

**Both were found by the end-to-end test asserting the DATABASE**, not by the
contract tests. That is the same lesson the defect itself carries: a receipt
count, a column list and a green picker were all true while the feature did
nothing.

### 14 · TWO CHECKS OF MINE WERE WRONG, IN THE SAME DIRECTION, AND BOTH WENT RED ON THE CORRECT BUILD

Worth recording together because they are one habit, not two slips.

* A header check asserted no label starts with `"gis "` — which `GIS parcel ID`,
  a KEPT column with a deliberately curated heading, does. **It could not pass.**
* A hardcoding check grepped `import_runs.py` for `owner_occupier` — which is
  there, in the comment explaining why the five must NOT be hardcoded. **A check
  that cannot tell a value from a sentence about a value could not pass either.**

Both now assert by VALUE: the kept key's heading is compared with the one that
would be generated from its field name, and the category check reads the
module's own constants rather than its text. **Law 7's *ask what would make this
pass wrongly* has a mirror nobody writes down — *ask what would make it fail
rightly* — and a check written from a description rather than from the thing
fails it every time.**

### 15 · WHAT WAS NOT BUILT, AND THE FIGURE THAT SIZES IT

**The beta holds 1 master account and it is already orphaned**: `AC-2026-00051`
on `P-00059`, 500 Main St, whose owner `Ridge Property LLC` exists while
`premises_owners.master_account_id` is NULL. **0 of 5 owners on the tenant carry
that link.** That is the existing `DEF-2902`/`DEF-2903` and it is not fixed
here; this change stops NEW imports adding to it. **One row is the whole blast
radius**, which is the only reason that is an acceptable place to stop — and it
was measured before any of this was written, which is what the maintenance
process's REPRODUCE → LOCATE → BLAST RADIUS step is for.

### 16 · A THIRD FINDING, AND ONLY THE WALK COULD HAVE MADE IT

With the column built and every unit test green, the walkthrough's case 8 — a
category of `not_a_real_category` — came back counted as **"no category
stated"**. That is the receipt telling an operator the opposite of what their
file says, and it happens because the lookup has already resolved the typo to
`None` by the time the loader reads it: *said nothing* and *said something we do
not recognise* arrive as the same value.

They are different facts with different next actions — one is a decision nobody
has taken, the other is a typo or a list that needs a new entry — so they are
told apart now, by reading the operator's own text out of `owner_category_raw`,
which `_map_row` has always kept for exactly this. An unrecognised category is
counted as a REFUSAL carrying the tenant's own lookup's reason, and
`PRM.OWNER_CATEGORY_IN_LOOKUP` says so at rehearsal — `PRM.TYPE_IN_LOOKUP`'s
shape, on the column added today, WARNING + FLAG_ONLY because rejecting the row
would throw away an address over a spelling. `PRM.OWNER_CATEGORY_MISSING` now
stands down on those rows, so only one of the two can ever hit a row.

⚠ **NO UNIT TEST WOULD HAVE FOUND IT**, and it is worth being precise about why:
every contract test asserts what the column IS, and this is about what a COUNT
MEANS. The figure was present, non-zero and wrong. **Both numbers are asserted
now** — a typo counts as one refusal AND as zero unstated categories — because
asserting either alone passes on the bug.

### 17 · THE WALK, AND WHAT IT PROVES THAT THE SUITE CANNOT

`10-scripts/premises_owner_import_walkthrough.py` — eight scenarios through
`extract → transform → validate → load` on **real PostgreSQL**, against the beta
tenant, inside one transaction that ends in a deliberate rollback. Verified
either side: **79 premises and 5 owners before and after.**

⚠ **EVERY CASE ASSERTS THREE FACTS OUT OF THE DATABASE** — `premises.owner_id`,
whether the address has an account, and `premises_owners.master_account_id` —
**never a receipt count.** That is the whole point: the receipt count is what
hid this for weeks, because `premises_owner_accounts_created = 1` was true the
entire time.

Green, exit 0: a stated category creates and links the party; a blank one leaves
today's behaviour exactly as it was; no account type, no owner kind and a
name-only row all create nothing; a name only in the legacy box creates nothing
and is now counted; **an owner already on file is LINKED and no second party is
minted** — `BR-MET-150`'s reuse, which the per-case checks cannot see and a
count of parties created does; and an unrecognised category refuses the party,
keeps the address and its account, and says which it was.

⚠ **AND IT FOUND A BUG IN ITSELF FIRST**, which is worth recording: it was
copied from the reproduction written that morning and still mapped a header at
`owner_manager`, the column retired four hours earlier. Stage 2 refused it by
name. That is the retirement working, met from the outside.

## 2026-09-19 (LATER) — RETIRING A COLUMN BROKE 51 TESTS, AND THE TESTS WERE RIGHT

### 1 · WHAT HAPPENED, AND IT WAS PUSHED BEFORE IT WAS KNOWN

`DEF-MET-5802` retired `owner_manager` and thirteen GIS fields from the premises
and units templates. Measured against a PRISTINE tip on the same eleven files
with the same flags:

    pristine tip   17 failed · 129 passed · 1 skipped · 46 errors
    with the change 68 failed ·  78 passed · 1 skipped · 46 errors

Same 46 errors — those are a **Redis outage in this container**, proved by
running one of the files on both trees and getting identical results. The **51**
is mine.

⚠ **AND IT WAS PUSHED FIRST.** The comparison run was still queued on a loaded
box when `8649f6459` went out, on the reasoning that every targeted suite was
green and that work is only durable once pushed. **The targeted suites were the
wrong evidence**: each one I chose exercises the columns I changed, and the
break was in files that merely USE the premises mapping in passing. Choosing
what to verify is itself a judgment, and mine excluded the failure.

### 2 · THE CAUSE IS A PRODUCT DEFECT, NOT A FIXTURE PROBLEM

`test_cr023_import_stages.py`'s shared premises `MAPPING` contains
`"OWNER": "owner_manager"`. `_transform_locked` looks a confirmed target up in
the offered set and, finding none, refuses the WHOLE RUN with
`metering.import.unknown_mapping_target`.

**That fixture is doing exactly what a tenant's saved `ImportMapping` does.** A
saved template the UI loaded, a script, a retry, a spreadsheet built from last
year's sample — every one of them names a column that was on this template for
months, and every one of them now fails the entire import. **The operator
cannot map their way out of it, because the target they are refused for is one
we removed.** Fifty-one tests failing was the product telling me that, in the
only voice it has.

⚠ **I HAD ALREADY FIXED THE OTHER HALF AND CALLED IT DONE.**
`_detected_mapping` drops a retired target from the SUGGESTION, which protects
an operator who clicks through the picker. It does nothing for the mapping a
client actually POSTs — and the brief asked for exactly this: *"a stored map
pointing at a column no longer offered must degrade honestly, not crash a run"*.
Half the path was honest and the half that a real migration takes was not.

⚠ **AND MY OWN WALKTHROUGH HIT IT AND I READ IT AS CORRECT.** The script was
copied from a reproduction written that morning, still mapped `owner_manager`,
and was refused by name. I recorded that as *"the retirement working, met from
the outside"* and pointed the header at `— ignore —`. It was the defect
reporting itself and I filed it as a feature.

### 3 · THE FIX: A RETIRED COLUMN IS NOT AN UNKNOWN ONE

`_transform_locked` now resolves a target named in
`NOT_OFFERED_COLUMNS_BY_TARGET` to an explicit `— ignore —` and reports it on
the answer as `retired_columns`. Nothing of the operator's is written, and
nothing is silently dropped either: they are told, by column, which ones this
product no longer takes.

⚠ **A TARGET THAT NEVER EXISTED STILL REFUSES, BY NAME.** The forgiveness is
scoped to a DECLARED list of columns withdrawn on purpose, each with its
reason. Widening it to *"anything unrecognised"* would turn every misspelled
target into silently unloaded data — `DEF-632`'s shape, and the opposite of
what this is for. The two sets are asserted as different answers, because a
test naming only the retired one passes on a build that forgives everything.

**So all three stages now agree about a retired column** — `_auto_map` skips it,
`_detected_mapping` drops it, `_transform_locked` ignores it and says so. They
did not before, and the one that disagreed is the one a customer's own saved
mapping goes through.

### 4 · THE LESSON, AND IT IS ABOUT EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ABOUT COLUMNS

**A baseline on a loaded box is slow, and skipping it is how a change ships on
the strength of the tests its author thought to run.** Every suite I chose was
green and every one of them was about the columns. The breakage was in files
that use those columns incidentally — which is precisely where a retirement
does its damage, in the product as much as in a suite.

⚠ **THE COUNT WAS THE SIGNAL AND I NEARLY DISMISSED IT.** 46 errors were
genuinely environmental and proved so; sitting in the same summary line was a
51-test difference that was not. CLAUDE.md's habit — *read the failures you did
not cause, and date them* — has a second half this is the case for: **a run
whose failures you HAVE explained can still contain ones you have not, and only
a number compared against a baseline separates them.**

## 2026-09-19 (LATER STILL) — THE SHIPPED SAMPLE DEMONSTRATED THE DEFECT IT WAS FIXING

### 1 · WHAT THE FILE ACTUALLY SAID

Printed from running code rather than read off the committed evidence:

    Owner name                       sample=None
    Owner is a person or a company   sample='person'
    Owner Social Security number     sample=''
    Owner driving licence            sample=''
    Owner phone                      sample=''
    Owner Tax ID                     sample=''
    Owner account type               sample=''
    Owner category                   sample=''
    Owner email                      sample=''

**The sample said the owner is a person and then named nobody.** Run through the
loader it answers `no_owner` — no party, no master account, nothing. That is
*"we import premises, provide owner details, and no Master Account is
generated"*, the complaint that started this work, **shipped as the worked
example a utility is handed to copy.**

⚠ **A BLANK CELL IN A SAMPLE IS NOT NEUTRAL, IT IS INSTRUCTION.** An operator
opens it to learn what goes in each column. Nine owner columns with one
committing value and eight empty teaches that the rest are decorative — and the
lone `person` made it **worse than all-blank**, because the section looked
demonstrated.

### 2 · THE ROW NOW EARNS AN ACCOUNT, AND `DEF-962`'s REASON IS KEPT

    Owner name   Sample Owner (or this tenant's own first owner)
    kind         person
    phone        555-0142
    SSN / DL     BLANK
    Tax ID       BLANK
    account type residential   ← this tenant's own lookup
    category     owner_occupier ← this tenant's own lookup
    email        sample.owner@example.test

**`DEF-962`'s rule was a blanket over a reason, and the reason is what survives.**
It read *"a worked cell here would put an invented Social Security number in the
file a utility hands its staff"* — exactly right, and it does not reach all six
columns. A **GOVERNMENT IDENTIFIER** ships blank, always, and is now asserted
for its own sake. The **PHONE** carries a `555-01xx` number, the range reserved
for fiction, which cannot be anybody's and is enough on its own to create a
person. The two **LOOKUPS** carry the tenant's own code, which is not an
invention by any reading — it is what `premises_type` has always done with
`apartment_complex`.

### 3 · THE BUG UNDERNEATH, AND IT IS A THIRD STATE NOBODY HAD

`sample_csv`'s `cell()` tests `if "sample" in entry` **before** its kind-aware
branches, and `_premises_owner_column` always set that key. So a declared `""`
**shadowed** the tenant's own `seed_codes` answer: `Owner account type` and
`Owner category` shipped EMPTY while the indexes behind them held eight codes
and five. Two states were not enough — *declared value*, *declared blank* and
*declares nothing* are three different things, and the blank is what `DEF-962`
wants for `owner_ssn` while the absence is what a lookup needs.

⚠ **THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS FIX SHIPPED THE EMPTY CELLS ANYWAY** and the test
caught it, which is the only reason the three-state distinction got written
down. Asserting the VERDICT rather than the nine cells is what made that
possible: a test listing expected values would have passed on a row that is
self-consistent and still earns nothing.

### 4 · A CORRECTION TO MY OWN MEASUREMENT, AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE SAMPLE

I reported *"8 failed, 44 passed — and the pristine tip produces the same five
named failures, so the residue is pre-existing."* **The baseline was wrong.**
Pristine produces SEVEN, not five: my `tail -6` had truncated the list and I
read the truncation as the whole. Eight failures with five explained leaves
three unaccounted for, and the report read as though all of it were explained.

⚠ **AN UNDER-COUNTED BASELINE TURNS YOUR OWN REGRESSIONS INTO SOMEBODY ELSE'S**,
and it does it silently, in the direction that flatters you. The habit CLAUDE.md
already states — *read the failures you did not cause, and date them* — needs
the half this cost: **name every failure, or name the count you cannot explain.**
A comparison is only as good as its baseline.

### 5 · THE TWO THAT WERE MINE

**`test_tc4__maps_to_offers_the_real_columns_and_nothing_else`** asserted
`from_model - {"custom_data"} <= offered` — every concrete field must be offered,
which is **the half of `BR-MET-088` that moving premises to a declaration
removes**, and its own docstring says it exists to catch exactly the drift a
hand-written list introduces. It is rewritten to assert the NEW contract rather
than deleted: every concrete field is either offered or listed as not-offered
WITH A REASON, and nothing is in neither. It still fails, by name, on a new
field — which is the job it was written for, against the new mechanism.

**`test_tier_1_stops_the_row_before_tier_2_is_asked`** is STATE-DEPENDENT and
not mine. It passes in isolation on this branch (`1 passed`), and the two runs
that disagreed about it differed in the `--reuse-db` flag, which changes how
many premises are already on file when `PRM.ADDRESS_ON_FILE` counts. Run with
IDENTICAL flags on both trees, the only difference in the whole file is `tc4`.
**Stated as a finding rather than acted on:** the test's own subject is that a
row with no address is not also counted as a duplicate address, and it deserves
its own isolation fix from somebody who owns that file.

## 2026-09-19 (FINAL) — THE SAMPLE NAMED A REAL CUSTOMER, AND A NAME IS NOT A LOOKUP

### 1 · WHAT THE SERVED FILE SAID

    Owner name                      = 'Creekside Laundromat'
    Owner is a person or a company  = 'person'
    Owner category                  = 'owner_occupier'
    Owner phone                     = '555-0142'

`Creekside Laundromat` is a **live `premises_owners` row on the beta tenant**.
Two separate faults in one cell.

**IT CONTRADICTED ITSELF.** A laundromat filed as a `person` and an
`owner_occupier`. It answered `eligible` only because a phone is a valid
identifier for a person — **the same row with a Tax ID answers
`identity_mismatch`.** So the file a utility is handed to copy demonstrated a
business filed as an individual, which is the exact mistake
`PRM.OWNER_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` exists to catch.

**AND IT WAS SOMEBODY'S REAL DATA.** A downloadable template carried one of a
customer's actual owner names, and an operator loading the sample unmodified
would attach a property to a real party — beside `Sample Building`, `12 Sample
Street`, `555-0142` and `sample.owner@example.test`, which are fiction.

### 2 · WHERE MY OWN REASONING STOPPED APPLYING

I made the account type and the category read from the tenant's own lookups
**because I had just found the resolve-to-nothing bug**, and that was right:
those are LOOKUPS, and a sample naming a value the tenant does not hold ships
that bug as an instruction. I then applied the same reasoning to the NAME, on
`KIND_PREMISE_REF`'s pattern — the tenant's own first owner.

⚠ **THE TEST IS WHETHER ANYTHING HAS TO RESOLVE.** A unit ref, a premise number
and a parent asset must name a row that EXISTS or the sample cannot load.
`owner_account_verdict` reads the owner as **free text**; a name not already on
file is the ordinary first-migration case, and with the category beside it the
party is created. **Nothing resolves, so nothing needs to be real** — and the
name is fiction now, like every other invented cell.

### 3 · TWO CHECKS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT

`eligible` is a weaker statement than it looks, so the sample test now also
asserts the row is **internally coherent** — the identifier present belongs to
the stated kind — and that the owner name is **not a party on this tenant**.
The second is three lines and it is the whole defect.

### 4 · TWO ARTEFACTS CLAIMING TO BE ONE FILE — HARD-WON LAW 5

The committed evidence said `Sample Owner` while the product served `Creekside
Laundromat`. **Neither was wrong about itself; nothing compared them.**

⚠ **AND THE SAMPLE IS PER-TENANT BY DESIGN**, so a committed copy can only ever
be *"what this file looks like for ONE utility"* — the services are the tenant's
enablement, the account type and category its own lookups, a units row its own
first premises. A test now regenerates both for the fixture tenant and refuses
any difference, so the next drift is a red build rather than a surprise, and the
README says plainly that a reader's own download will differ in those cells.

### 5 · THE LESSON, WHICH IS ABOUT A CORRECT RULE APPLIED ONE STEP TOO FAR

Nothing here was careless. *Read it from the tenant* was the right answer to the
bug in front of me, and I carried it to a cell where the premise did not hold.
**A rule learned from one defect will happily be applied to a case it does not
fit, and it arrives wearing the authority of the defect that taught it.** The
guard against that is not more care; it is asking what the rule DEPENDS on — here,
that something must resolve — and checking the new case has it.


## 2026-09-19 · 📐 DEF-MET-5844 — THE ADD PREMISES FORM OPENS THE OWNER'S ACCOUNT, AND THE TWO CALLS THE RULINGS DID NOT MAKE (maintenance lane, 2.310.3)

**The PO's report, verbatim, from the live product:** *"when user add propery from
add new premise form - user provides owner type, name, managed by input but system
does not create master account"*.

**They were right and it was not a data problem — the code was absent.** Three doors
should produce an owner's Master Account. New Connect
(`metering/connections.py:3797`) calls `ensure_owner_master_account`. The premises
import (`import_runs.py:7706`) calls `ensure_master_account_for_premises`.
`create_premises` called **neither**: it wrote the premises, its units and its route
memberships and never mentioned an owner. Measured on `brazosbend`, real PostgreSQL,
rolled back: a property created with **Ridge Property LLC** attached left master
accounts at **1 → 1**, no account on the property, and
`premises_owners.master_account_id` NULL.

**A fourth door was found while fixing it and it is worse:** `CommonAreasTab.tsx`'s
*Create master account* modal — the manual one on the property page — posts to the
same endpoint and is refused too (`DEF-CUS-5846`). **So on this tenant no screen in
the product can open an owner's Master Account.** Only the import can, because a
spreadsheet has columns for the owner's kind and identifier.

### 1 · A BLANK ACCOUNT TYPE DECLINES THE ACCOUNT AND NEVER BLOCKS THE SAVE

`customers.create_master_account` refuses a missing `account_type` by name, and the
form never asked for one — so the server could not have supplied it and the door
could never have been called usefully. **The account type is now a box on the form,
optional, and its absence means no owner account.**

**Why not required, and why not defaulted.** Not required, because *an address is a
real address whether or not anybody can be billed for it* — the PO's ruling of
2026-08-27, and blocking a property save on a money question would be this form
deciding that an address without a payer is not worth recording. Not defaulted,
because the account type is the consumer category the bill is priced and reported
by: guessing `residential` for a builder's site is a money decision taken by a
shrug. The premises row's own `premises_type` is a PROPERTY type, and deriving one
from the other would be inventing a money-bearing default and calling it a mapping.
**This is the same call `CR-058` W3 judgment 1 made for the import's sixth column
on 2026-09-01, taken deliberately rather than re-argued** — one fact, one rule, two
doors.

**And the clerk is told BEFORE they save, which is the half that is easy to drop.**
The field's own line reads **`Blank creates no owner account.`** — five words — and
the review step's row reads **`No owner account will be created.`** — six words,
counted on the rendered screen and not in the catalogue. B14 rule 33 caps a
consequence at six words per sentence.

### 2 · A NAME TYPED IN `Managed by` WITH NO OWNER RECORD PICKED CREATES NOTHING

The picker is the only thing that names a party. A string in the free-text box is a
NAME, and turning it into one would need a CATEGORY — which `BR-MET-151` clause 3
forbids reading off a name in as many words, and which `BR-MET-402` clause 5 already
stops the import doing for the same reason. `BR-MET-112` is the other half: a wizard
does not mint an account because a field was filled in. **So the address saves, no
party is invented, and the response says `no_typed_owner`** rather than being silent
about it.

### 3 · WHAT THIS LANE DID NOT DECIDE, AND WHY THAT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER

With both gates passed the door is called and, on this tenant, it refuses:
`BR-CUS-1024`, PO 2026-09-01 — *"Without identifier we cannot create Customer ID or
master account ot regular account"*. **That collides head-on with `CR-056`'s ruling
of 2026-08-31 that every address gets its owner a Master Account**, and the
collision is mechanical rather than interpretive: `premises_owners` carries a
category, a name and contact details and holds no person/company kind and no
identifier (`BR-MET-150` — *"category is okay, no richer text"*), while
`premises_owners.customer_id` is ruled out as the path by `BR-MET-1020`.

**Two signed rulings, and stating which supersedes is the PO's act and not ours**
(CLAUDE.md hard-won law 13's first named category). It is `OQ-MET-12472`, OPEN,
with four options and their costs written out. **Nothing was guessed to get past
it** — no kind read off a category, no identifier read off a phone number, and the
`require_identity=False` escape hatch deliberately not taken. Hand the same door a
kind and a Tax ID and it creates **AC-2026-00058** and writes the declared link, so
the plumbing is complete and the evidence is what is missing.

### 4 · THE SAVEPOINT IS THE FIX, NOT THE TIDINESS — AND IT WAS PROVED THE HARD WAY

`create_premises` is ONE transaction, so a refused account would take the address
with it. The nested `transaction.atomic()` is CLAUDE.md law 14, and the first
attempt to prove it red **proved nothing**: `BR-CUS-1024` is raised in Python
*before* the door opens a transaction, so no statement failed, nothing was poisoned,
and BOTH versions passed. That is law 7's *"what would make this check pass
wrongly"* answered by the check itself. Re-run with a refusal raised AFTER a failed
statement — the shape every catch-the-`IntegrityError`-and-name-it refusal in this
repo takes:

    WITH savepoint    -> the address SURVIVED the refusal: True
    WITHOUT savepoint -> InternalError: current transaction is aborted,
                         commands ignored until end of transaction block

**The suite cannot see this and the test file says so in its own docstring:**
`config/settings/test.py` hardcodes in-memory SQLite, which has no aborted-
transaction state, so the broken version is green everywhere.

### 5 · A CHECK OF THIS LANE'S OWN THAT PASSED WRONGLY, CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED

The first draft reported `owner_account_created` from the door's return value.
**`ensure_owner_master_account` is *ensure*: an owner already linked gets that
account back, writes nothing, audits nothing — and returns THE SAME SHAPE.** So a
caller reading only the return value cannot tell a creation from a lookup, and the
form would have announced *account created* over an account created last month, on a
money object. The owner row is now asked BEFORE the call, and
`OWNER_ACCOUNT_ALREADY_LINKED` exists so the two can never be confused again.

### 6 · AN EIGHTEENTH REVIEW ROW, RECORDED RATHER THAN ABSORBED

`conformance/CR-089-p015` specifies **seventeen** fact rows *"in this exact order"*.
`Account type` makes eighteen. B14 rule 41 says the frame wins, so the divergence is
written into that file as row 17a with its reason — the blueprint could not draw
this row because the form it drew never asked the question — and it rides with
`OQ-MET-12472` to be put back to the PO with the drawing rather than living as a
permanent exception.

## 2026-09-19 · NO SCREEN IN THE PRODUCT CAN OPEN AN OWNER'S MASTER ACCOUNT — `OQ-MET-12472` CLOSED, AND TWO SMALLER RULINGS

### 1 · WHAT WAS PUT TO THE PO, AND WHY IT HAD TO BE

**Two signed rulings meet on this path and only one can hold.** This is the
narrow case CLAUDE.md hard-won law 13 says legitimately reaches the PO — *"a
ruling that collides with a signed rule — the supersession must be stated,
never assumed"* — and not a judgment we ducked.

* **2026-08-31 (`CR-056`):** *every address gets its owner a Master Account,
  whether or not anything is shared, and whether or not the owner lives there.*
* **2026-09-01:** *"Without identifier we cannot create Customer ID or master
  account ot regular account"*.

`premises_owners` carries a **category, a name and contact details** and
**no person/company kind and no identifier** (`BR-MET-150`). So the account
door cannot be satisfied from what any screen collects.

⚠ **AND IT IS NOT ONE FORM — IT IS EVERY FORM, WHICH IS WHAT MADE IT WORTH A
RULING RATHER THAN A FIX.** Measured on the beta, both by direct call:

| Door | Result |
|---|---|
| Premises import (CSV) | **works** — the file has columns for kind and identifier |
| New Connect | works |
| Add Premises form | `customers.contact.name_required`, then the identity gate |
| *Create master account* on the property page | `customers.account.identity_kind_required` |

**So on Brazos Bend today only a spreadsheet can open an owner's master
account.** A coordinating report had earlier told the PO the property page's
button *"works"* and that *"nobody is completely stuck"*; that was **wrong**,
found by calling `customers.create_master_account` with the Common Areas
payload shape on a fresh premises, and corrected to the PO in the same session.

### 2 · THE RULING (PO, 2026-09-19)

Four options were put in plain English with their costs. The PO chose, verbatim
against the option as worded:

> *"The Add Premises form must collect an identifier — it gains the same kind +
> identifier fields the import already has, and no account exists until they're
> supplied."* — **"this is correct"**

**So the 2026-09-01 rule STANDS and the 2026-08-31 rule YIELDS on this path.**
The form asks. The three options NOT taken are recorded because a later reader
will reach for them: *the account opens without an identifier* · *the owner
record carries identity* · *the August rule gives*.

⚠ **THE RULING GOVERNS WHAT THE FORM ASKS, NOT WHERE THE ANSWER IS STORED.**
An owner with ten buildings being asked ten times is a real cost and
`premises_owners` has nowhere to put it today, so whether identity lands on the
owner is left to the building lane to decide and record — with the storage
question filed at its cost if it needs a schema change.

### 3 · THE SECOND RULING — AND IT WAS ALREADY RULED, WHICH IS THE POINT

On the option that would have opened an account without an identifier, the PO
added: *"it should create account number based numbering set in settings"*.

**That is `OQ-790`, closed by the PO on 2026-08-27, and it is already built.**
`customers._allocate_account_no` calls `core_numbering.next_number(ACCOUNT_SERIES, …)`
under `BR-TEN-035` and refuses by name with
`customers.account.numbering_unavailable` rather than inventing a number; the
beta's `AC-2026-00051` is a series number. **Nothing was built for it and the
PO was told so** — law 13: *"before putting anything to the PO, grep the
decision log and the open questions for the subject"*, and the same discipline
applies to a requirement they restate. It is asserted in the walk so it can
never be raised a third time.

### 4 · THE THIRD RULING — `DEF-MET-5845`, THE DOUBLE ADDRESS BLOCK

The Add Premises form draws **two headings and two address blocks**: *"Where is
it?"* then *"Where is this property?"*, an `Address` box above `Street
address`, and both `Zip (optional)` and `ZIP / postal code`. The
address-lookup panel renders its own heading and its own fields inside a
section that already has both.

PO, shown the confirmed reproduction: **"yes one is optional"**.

**Read as:** the lookup is an optional convenience and the manual fields are the
real answer — one section, one heading, the lookup as an aid inside it, no
duplicate Unit or postcode boxes. **The reading is recorded as a reading**, and
the lane was told to stop and re-ask if its reproduction contradicts it, rather
than build to a guess and have the PO answer twice.

⚠ **IT IS INVISIBLE ON THE DEMO TENANT AND THAT IS WHY IT SURVIVED.** Brazos
Bend's City lookup is switched off, so the panel collapses to one grey line.
Every walk this repo has ever run has run against that tenant. **A defect that
only exists in a configuration nobody walks is not caught by walking harder —
it is caught by walking the OTHER configuration**, which is now required of the
fix: with the lookup on AND off.

### 5 · WHY NO CHECK CAUGHT ANY OF THIS

The account was never created, and **an absence is invisible to every check
this repo has** — the lesson `DEF-CUS-3653` already recorded once. Worse, the
one suite that covers this path, `test_def_met_5844_add_premises_owner_account.py`,
has **seven cases and every one asserts that nothing is created**: no owner →
nothing, no account type → nothing, *"the door is reached and its own refusal
is reported"*. There is no case asserting an account IS opened, because on that
path one never is. **A suite can be green, honest, and pin the defect** — the
same shape as `test_cr058_w3`'s *"the import still creates no PARTY"*, found
the same day.


## 2026-09-19 · 📐 `OQ-MET-12472` CLOSED · `DEF-MET-5845` · `DEF-MET-5847` — THE FORM ASKS WHO THE OWNER IS, AND THE STEP STOPS DRAWING TWO ADDRESSES (maintenance lane, 2.310.4)

### 1 · THE RULING, VERBATIM, AND WHICH SIGNED RULE YIELDS

Two signed rulings met on the Add Premises form and only one could hold:

* **2026-08-31 (`CR-056`):** *every address gets its owner a Master Account, whether
  or not anything is shared, and whether or not the owner lives there.*
* **2026-09-01 (`BR-CUS-1024`):** *"Without identifier we cannot create Customer ID
  or master account ot regular account"*.

Four options were put to the PO in plain English with the cost of each. **They chose
the one that keeps the September rule**, against the option as worded:

> *"The Add Premises form must collect an identifier — it gains the same kind +
> identifier fields the import already has, and no account exists until they're
> supplied."* — **"this is correct"**

**So: the September rule stands. The August rule yields ON THIS PATH. The form asks.**
`CR-056`'s sentence is not deleted and does not need to be — it is now true of every
address whose owner somebody has identified, and an unidentified owner is a stated,
reported state rather than a silence.

### 2 · THE PO'S ONE ADDITION WAS NOT NEW WORK, AND IT IS VERIFIED RATHER THAN BUILT

> *"it should create account number based numbering set in settings"*

**That is `OQ-790`, closed by the PO on 2026-08-27, and it was already built.**
`customers._allocate_account_no` calls `core_numbering.next_number(ACCOUNT_SERIES, …)`
under `BR-TEN-035` and refuses BY NAME with `customers.account.numbering_unavailable`
rather than inventing a number. **Measured in the browser walk rather than asserted
from memory:** the tenant's own `account` series was read from Settings → prefix
`AC-`, the account the walk opened came back `AC-2026-00058`, and the assertion
compares the two. CLAUDE.md hard-won law 13: a re-ask manufactures inconsistency, so
this is written down here and asserted in the walk so nobody has to raise it again.

### 3 · WHERE THE IDENTITY LIVES — PASSED THROUGH, NOT STORED ON THE OWNER

The PO's ruling governs what the FORM does; it does not say where what the form
collects is kept. That was this lane's to decide, and it is **passed straight to the
account door**. `premises_owners` gains no kind column and no identifier column.

**Four reasons, and the last one is the measurement that decided it:**

1. **Identity has one home and it is `customers`.** A second copy on a metering
   table is the shape hard rule 8 reasons about for addresses, and `BR-MET-1020`
   already rules the metering→customer shortcut out by name.
2. **`customers` is the module with the machinery.** Field encryption, the four
   blind indexes (`ssn_bidx`, `driving_licence_bidx`, `phone_bidx`, `tax_id_bidx`)
   and `identity_match` live there. `premises_owners` has no encryption story at
   all, so an SSN written to it would be a government identifier in plaintext.
3. **It is a schema change, which is bigger than the PO sized.** They agreed to *the
   form asks*, not *the owner record changes*.
4. **THE COST IT WOULD HAVE BOUGHT IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS, AND THIS IS THE WORKED
   EXAMPLE.** The objection to passing through is *an owner with ten buildings is
   asked ten times*. **They are not: they are asked ONCE.**
   `ensure_owner_master_account` returns at its first line when
   `master_account_id is not None` — before it reads the payload at all. Measured on
   `brazosbend`, real PostgreSQL, rolled back:

       Ridge Property LLC, building 1 · company + Tax ID 74-3182640
         -> masters 1 -> 2, account AC-2026-00058, premises_owners.master_account_id WRITTEN
       Ridge Property LLC, building 2 · NO kind, NO identifier, account type only
         -> masters 2 -> 2, the SAME account handed back, warning `owner_account_already_linked`

   So the identity is asked **once per OWNER, not once per ADDRESS**, and buildings
   2..10 need nothing typed. Storing it would have bought one screenful of typing on
   one building and cost a second home for a government identifier.

**The storage question is filed rather than taken:** `OQ-MET-12482` asks whether
`premises_owners` should carry a kind and an identifier so `PRM-04` can settle a
party's identity once, away from a property form. Its cost is stated there: a
migration, `BR-CUS-092` field encryption on a metering table, and a widening of
`BR-MET-150`, whose whole point was *"category is okay, no richer text"*.

### 4 · ONE FUNCTION DECIDES WHAT THE ANSWERS EARN — IT IS CALLED, NOT COPIED

`import_runs.owner_account_verdict` is the one function that judges the six owner
cells, and the form now calls it. It was the spreadsheet's judge; it is now both
doors'. **A second copy on this side would eventually tell one clerk that a name
plus a phone earns an account and another that it does not**, and on this path both
answers reach the SAME person — one on the review step and one on the receipt.

It cost one visible behaviour change and it is the right one. A property saved with
an owner, no account type and no identifier used to report `no_account_type`; it now
reports `awaiting_identity`, because the verdict asks for the identifier FIRST. That
is the order the import receipt has always used, and the screen now names the same
missing fact the spreadsheet would.

**What the five verdicts do, measured on real PostgreSQL, every one rolled back:**

    person + SSN / licence / phone + account type -> masters 1->2, AC-2026-00058, link SET
    company + Tax ID + account type              -> masters 1->2, AC-2026-00058, link SET
    company + phone only                         -> identity_mismatch / identifier_belongs_to_the_other_kind
    kind, no identifier                          -> awaiting_identity
    identifier, no kind                          -> identity_mismatch / kind_not_stated
    no account type                              -> no_account_type
    no owner at all                              -> no_typed_owner

**The address saved in every one of the last five.** PO 2026-08-27, untouched: an
address is a real address whether or not anybody can be billed for it.

### 5 · THE WRONG KIND'S IDENTIFIER IS UNREACHABLE ON SCREEN, NOT REFUSED LATE

`BR-CUS-1022`: a person is identified by SSN, driving licence or phone; a company by
its Tax ID. **Offering a company a phone box files a business under a telephone
number, where the company matcher never looks.** The verdict refuses that pairing by
name — and *a screen that can reach a named refusal is a screen that should not have
offered it*. So no identifier box is drawn until a kind is picked, then only that
kind's boxes exist, and the payload builder sends only that kind's value (a clerk who
types a phone as a person and then switches to Company does not silently post it).
The server still refuses it, for the seam and for every caller that is not the form.

### 6 · `DEF-MET-5847` — THE BLOCKAGE NOBODY WAS LOOKING AT, AND IT WAS NOT THE IDENTITY GATE

Measured on `brazosbend`, real PostgreSQL, before anything was changed:

    owner picked, Managed by BLANK  -> refused: customers.contact.name_required
    owner picked, Managed by FILLED -> refused: customers.account.identity_kind_required

**The first one is not the famous gate, and it would have survived the identity fix.**
`create_master_account` falls back to the premises' free-text `owner_manager` when no
contact block arrives — and after `CR-089` `p008` split the owner PICKER from
`Managed by`, that box is ordinarily empty. So the door refused every owner picked
properly, and only a clerk who ALSO retyped the name into the free-text box got past
it. The owner row has carried `contact_name`, `email` and `phone` since `BR-MET-150`
and this door forwarded none of them. It forwards them now, in the shape the door
accepts — `{full_name, email, phone, is_primary}`, because `{"name": …}` is refused
as `customers.account.unknown_field`.

### 7 · `DEF-MET-5845` — THE STEP DREW TWO ADDRESS BLOCKS, AND THE BLUEPRINT SETTLED IT

The PO saw a screenshot and asked about it; shown the confirmed reproduction they
ruled **"yes one is optional"**. What a clerk met, with a City lookup that works:

    Where is it?
    Where is this property?          <- the lookup panel's OWN heading
      Address            [ ]         <- and its own address box
      Unit (optional) [ ]  Zip (optional) [ ]
      Street address *   [ ]         <- the form's
      City / State / ZIP-postal code [ ]

Two headings, two address boxes, two postcode boxes, and nothing saying which counted.

**The blueprint decides the shape and it is not a judgment call.** `05-prototype/
Premises & Units Blueprint 2.pdf` p9 (S16·PRM-07, frame P2) draws ONE block —
`Street address *` with the help line *"Start typing and we will look it up."*, then
`Town / city` · `State` · `ZIP`, then the *Found on the city map* panel — and
`PUJ-03`'s own acceptance sentence puts the lookup's refusal *"in a grey line under
the box"*, singular. CLAUDE.md's blueprint ruling of 2026-09-14 gives a module with a
blueprint its layout, copy, flows and states.

So the panel is now **headless and fieldless**: it reads the form's own `Street
address` and `ZIP` and renders only the City's answer. The help line under `Street
address` was already *"Start typing. We look it up."* — it is now literally true; it
used to describe a box somewhere else.

⚠ **IT WAS INVISIBLE ON EVERY DEMO TENANT AND THAT IS WHY IT SURVIVED REVIEW.**
`brazosbend` has no City connection, so the panel collapses to `absent` and draws
nothing. **The defect exists only where the lookup WORKS** — the one state no
walkthrough had ever been run in. The walk now runs both: the City's answers are
intercepted at the network for the ON case (connecting a real connector would write
rows into a beta this lane must leave untouched, for a screen state that is a pure
function of two API answers), and the OFF case runs against the real server with
nothing intercepted.

⚠ **AND THE TEST THAT GUARDED IT ASSERTED THE DEFECT.** `FindTheAddress.dom.test.tsx`
read *"draws Unit and Zip, which the frame does and the first build did not"* — a
true statement about frame 66.1 read **in isolation**. The panel was checked against
its own frame and never against the section it renders into. The assertions are
inverted rather than deleted, so a lane that puts a box back meets a red test naming
the ruling.

### 8 · A CHECK OF THIS LANE'S OWN THAT WOULD HAVE PASSED WRONGLY

`create_premises` returns `owner_master_account` and it is **not an id** — it is
`owner_detail_dict(...)`, the whole party. The first draft of the saved-twice proof
compared two of those dicts for equality, and they differ on `premises_count`, which
moves between the two saves and has nothing to do with whether a second account was
opened. It went red, which is what a red proof is for. Both the test and the
walkthrough now compare `master_account_id`.

**And the saved-twice case could prove nothing at all until today**, which the
previous lane recorded rather than claimed: with no identity both saves refused, so
*the second opened no second account* was true of two nulls. It now asserts that the
FIRST save really opened one before asserting the second did not.

### 9 · A PRE-EXISTING RED, DATED RATHER THAN CALLED PRE-EXISTING

`tests/test_br_met_1032_staged_identity.py` fails seven cases with
`sqlite3.OperationalError: unrecognized token: ":"`. It issues raw SQL containing
`raw::text` — a PostgreSQL-only cast — and the suite runs on in-memory SQLite, so
those seven are **structurally incapable of passing** (CLAUDE.md hard-won law 7's
third shape). `git log -S "raw::text"` dates it to `c7485bebc`, 2026-09-08, and the
file is byte-identical to the pinned tip. Filed as `DEF-MET-5848`; not this lane's
to fix and not silently stepped over.

## 2026-09-19 · 🔒 `DEF-RAT-5823` — THREE PLANS POINT AT A CUSTOMER CLASS THAT WAS DELETED BY ANOTHER MODULE, AND THE CLASS IS RECOVERABLE BUT NOT BY A MIGRATION (maintenance lane, 2.310.5)

### 1 · WHAT WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS NEVER `rating/0039`

Three plans on the beta — `SCW-RES`, `SCW-COM`, `SCW-IND` — each named one
customer class, and **not one of the three ids resolved against anything.**
Measured inside a tenant context on 2026-09-19: the stored ids all carry the
prefix `01a0afa2-`; all nine `account_types` rows brazosbend has carry
`01a0b026-` (8) or `01a0b7cc-` (1). **Zero of nine match.**

`rating/0039` was blamed for this and `rating/0039` is the messenger. It read
`plan_versions.snapshot`, found exactly the three plans that had stated a
class, and wrote exactly those three values. Its arithmetic and its docstring's
count are both correct. **The values were already dead before it ran.**

**The cause is `customers/0054`, on 2026-09-17 at 16:15:26.** It turned
`account_types` from a platform table into a per-tenant one: it cloned every
platform row once per tenant keyed on `code`, repointed every referencing row
to its own tenant's clone, and deleted the platform rows. Its referencing list
is three tables —

    REFERENCING = ("Account", "AccountSubtype", "ServiceRequest")

— and **`rate_plans` is not in it.** `rate_plans.account_type_id` was a bare
`models.UUIDField(null=True)` with **no foreign key at all**, so deleting the
rows out from under it raised nothing and `0054`'s own "stranded" refusal could
not see it. `rating/0038` then moved the already-dead value into
`account_type_ids` and `0039` restored it from the snapshots. **Three
migrations carried a corpse forward and every one of them was internally
correct.**

**The blast radius was measured in both directions and is exactly one column.**
`accounts` 0 dangling, `account_subtypes` 0, `service_requests` 0,
`plan_deposit_rules` 0, `tariffs` 0 of 54 rows. `rate_plans.account_type_ids`
is the only survivor of the miss.

### 2 · THE RULING WE MADE, AND WHY IT IS OURS RATHER THAN THE PO'S

**A dangling id is not written, and nothing is invented to replace it.**
`rating/0041` drops any `account_type_ids` entry that does not resolve for that
tenant and leaves the rest alone. Writing a dangling id is strictly worse than
writing nothing: it is invented data, it puts a raw database id on screen
against B14 rule 31, and every consumer already reads it as *names none*, so it
switches the narrowing off anyway — invisibly.

⚠ **`[]` IS ALSO WRONG AND IS NOT PRETENDED OTHERWISE.** Under `DEF-RAT-5768`
an empty list means EVERY class, and those three plans named ONE. It is not a
REGRESSION — `PlanWizard.addableCharges` already dropped the unresolved id and
`classCodes.size === 0` already turned narrowing off — so behaviour does not
move; what changes is that the wrongness becomes honest, visible and legal on
screen. **The three plans go back to a human to re-state, by name**, which is
`OQ-RAT-12473`.

### 3 · THE CLASS IS RECOVERABLE, AND WE DID NOT AUTOMATE IT — THIS IS THE JUDGMENT

The obvious reading is that nothing can resolve the id, and that reading was
checked key by key and is right **about the snapshot**: all 8 `plan_versions`
rows carry only `account_type_id` and a NULL `account_subtype_id`, with
`eligibility` `{}`. No code, no name. And the plan CODE is not evidence —
`SCW-RES` reading like *residential* is exactly the inference `BR-MET-151`
clause 3 forbids, *"Whitfield Rentals LLC is not proof of a landlord"*.

**But a route does exist, and it is a proof rather than a guess.** Because
`0054`'s repoint is code-preserving by construction (it clones with
`code=row.code` and remaps `old.id -> clone.id`), what an old platform id MEANT
can be read back out of the rows it repointed:

| the dead id | what it became | accounts agreeing |
|---|---|---|
| `01a0afa2-8ba0-7452-b43e-9d5154a8eedd` | **residential** | 63 |
| `01a0afa2-8ba2-7dee-9ddb-313f91788323` | **commercial** | 12 |
| `01a0afa2-8ba3-747c-bab6-2197d9d64126` | **industrial** | 1 |

76 accounts, **unanimous** — every one of the three old ids maps to exactly one
current type, never two. All 76 were created between 15:25:48 and 16:09:02,
**entirely before `0054` ran at 16:15:26**, and **no account's
`account_type_id` was ever changed afterwards** (0 type-changing
`account.updated` rows). The order corroborates it independently:
`customers/0003` seeded the platform rows `residential, commercial, industrial,
government` in that order, and the three uuid7 ids sort in that same order.

⚠ **AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE MIGRATION, FOR TWO REASONS THAT BOTH
MATTER.** It rests on `audit_log`, which is **pruned on a retention schedule**,
so a migration built on it would silently do nothing — or something different —
on the next host, which is hard-won law 7's *incapable of failing* wearing a
data dependency. And restoring a customer class changes which charge codes a
clerk is offered, which is a judgment the PO makes once rather than one a
migration makes quietly on every estate. **So the finding is written down here
and put to the PO in plain English as `OQ-RAT-12473`, where confirming it is
one word.**

### 4 · `rating/0039` IS NOT EDITED, AND THE SECOND REASON IS THE INTERESTING ONE

The first reason is its own: committed migrations are append-only and repairing
forward is the honest record. **The second is that `0039` HAS ALREADY RUN ON
THE BETA — under a different name.** `django_migrations` carries
`0039_def_rat_5800_class_backfill_under_rls`, applied 2026-09-19 04:59:17,
while the file on disk is `0039_def_rat_5799_…`. The authoring lane had taken
`DEF-RAT-5800`, ran the migration, and renumbered at push time because a
sibling had taken 5800 for an unrelated front-end row — **hard-won law 11's id
collision, caught exactly where the law says it is caught, with the database
keeping the name it ran under.** Django therefore still reports `0039` as
pending and re-running it is a no-op here (it only ever fills an empty list,
and the three plans are not empty). Editing a migration that has already
executed is how history stops being a record.

### 5 · `0039`'s *"FULL RECOVERY THERE"* IS NOW FALSE, AND A SNAPSHOT IS WHY

`0039` names ONE unrecoverable case — a draft plan that named a class and never
filed a version — and says of the snapshot route *"Full recovery there."*
**There is a SECOND case it did not anticipate, and it is the one this estate
has: a filed snapshot whose `account_type_id` no longer resolves.** The
snapshot is intact, append-only and exactly as `BR-RAT-111` promises, and it is
still unrecoverable — **a snapshot preserves a VALUE; it cannot preserve the
world the value referred to.** That is the durable lesson and it generalises
past this column: any snapshot holding a foreign id has this hole, and nothing
in this repo checks for it.

### 6 · WHY NO CHECK CAUGHT IT, AND THE ONE THAT NOW WOULD

`account_type_ids` is a JSON list with **no referential integrity at all**, by
design (a deferred FK, B11 F-3), so the database could not refuse it. The
default suite is sqlite, where `account_types` is not RLS-scoped and every
fixture id resolves, so the case cannot arise there at all — hard-won law 14
again, the same wall `DEF-RAT-5799` hit. And downstream **every reader treats
an unresolved id as absent, which fails open**: a picker offering MORE rows
reads as a healthy catalogue rather than as a rule that stopped running.

⚠ **THE REGISTER ROW'S OWN REMEDY WAS WRONG AND IS SUPERSEDED HERE.**
`DEF-RAT-5823` recommends *"fall back to matching the account type by CODE,
which is stable across re-seeds where the id is not"*. **There is no code to
match on** — the snapshot carries none, and the platform row that held one was
deleted. The register's measurement stands; its recommendation does not, and
`BR-RAT-1026` is where the rule now lives.

⚠ **AND THE GENERAL LESSON IS `customers/0054`'s, not `rating`'s: a migration
that deletes rows other modules point at must enumerate its referencing
tables, and a column with no foreign key is invisible to that enumeration.**
`0054` listed three of the five columns in this schema that hold an
`account_type_id`. The two it missed were the two with no FK — `rate_plans`
(dangling) and `tariffs` (clean only because no row uses it). **A refusal
keyed on "what does the ORM say points at me" cannot see a bare `UUIDField`,
and this repo has those by design.**

## 2026-09-19 · THE CHARGE-CODE SCREENS, FIVE DEFECTS FROM ONE CLERK WALK — AND THE FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT MAKE FOR US

**Maintenance track** (`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`), not
build: a clerk can add and edit a charge code in the product today, these five
things simply went wrong while they did it. Reproduced first, in a browser, on
`brazosbend`, against a `dist` built the same hour —
`10-scripts/po20260919_charge_code_clerk_walk.mjs` reported **9 pass / 8 fail**
before a line was changed, which is the number the walk's own header records.

`DEF-RAT-5819` · `DEF-RAT-5820` · `DEF-RAT-5821` · `DEF-RAT-5824` ·
`DEF-RAT-5825` are the five. **Nothing here needed the PO** — each is us not
doing what we said we would — so under hard-won law 13 the judgments are ours to
make and to write down, and these are the four where the rules genuinely ran
out.

### 1 · THE CONTRADICTION IS MADE UNREACHABLE BY DISABLING THE TICK, NOT BY REMOVING IT

`DEF-RAT-5820`: `Apply automatically` was offered identically on all five charge
types, and `BR-RAT-730` makes the engine REFUSE `auto_apply` on a non-recurring
one — *"Auto-apply means every bill; that type means an event."* So a clerk
could save a Penalty code scoped to Commercial and it would then refuse the bill
of every Commercial account and leave Residential and Industrial untouched.

**Three shapes were available and the drawing decided between two of them.**

| | why not |
|---|---|
| **warn and let them save** | it is the state the defect was already in — the engine's refusal existed the whole time and simply arrived weeks later, at a bill run. A sentence a clerk can click past changes when they find out, not whether |
| **remove the tick on four types** | `CR-087-p006` §2 draws **four ticks on one row**, and a control the drawing shows may not silently vanish |
| **present, disabled, with its reason** | **chosen.** `BR-SHL-025` is the rule this repo already has for a control that must not be used, `CheckboxField.disabled` exists for exactly it, and the drawn four ticks are all still there |

**And the box is ENABLED again the moment it is already ticked**, which is not a
loophole but the only way out of the state. A row saved before this fix — or a
draft ticked lawfully on `recurring` whose type was then changed — carries the
pair already, and a screen that refuses a configuration while offering no
control that could fix it is `DEF-384`'s *refusal with nowhere to go*. Step 2's
`validate` holds Continue until the tick comes off.

⚠ **THE ENGINE'S REFUSAL IS UNTOUCHED AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** `BR-RAT-730`
stays exactly where it is. What was missing was never the refusal; it was that
**no layer owned the PAIR** — the wizard offered two independent fields, the
serializer validated each against its own enum, and only the engine knew they
could not both be honoured.

### 2 · `chargeApplication` WAS WIDENED RATHER THAN COPIED — A FOURTH STATEMENT OF ONE RULE WAS THE REAL RISK

`BR-RAT-730` is already stated three times: `resolution.rides_a_periodic_bill`,
`selectors._rides_a_periodic_bill`, and `PlanWizard.chargeApplication`. The
first two deliberately do not call each other, because *"a comparison whose two
sides are the same function is a check that cannot fail"*.

The charge-code wizard needed the same answer about a DRAFT, which has no `id`,
no `*_display` strings and no `used_by_*` counts. **Writing `is_base ||
charge_type === "recurring"` into the wizard would have been a fourth copy — on
the very screen where the rule is authored** — correct today and silently stale
the first time the engine's disposition moves.

So `chargeApplication`'s parameter became `Pick<ChargeRow, "is_base" |
"auto_apply" | "charge_type">`, which is the truth it always had, and the wizard
asks it a **counterfactual**: `chargeCanAutoApply` is *"would ticking this box
produce the conflict?"*. Every existing caller passes a whole `ChargeRow` and is
unaffected.

### 3 · THE REVIEW ECHOES THE TYPED STRING; THE DRAWN COMPARISON TABLE IS NOT BUILT HERE

`DEF-RAT-5819`: on an EDIT the review read back the SERVER's stored display
string and never consulted what the clerk had typed. Walked: amount `3.50`,
typed `4.25`, step 3 printed `AMOUNT 3.50` and `Paper bill fee 3.50`. **The save
was correct** — `4.25` went in — which is the dangerous direction, because the
screen shows a well-formed, server-formatted, plausible number that happens to
be the wrong one.

The blueprint draws a `NOW / SAVING / CHANGE` comparison table for this screen
and it does not exist; `CR-087-p011`'s own diff says so. **We did not build it**
— that is a screen, not a defect fix — and its conformance file already
prescribes the interim in its own words: *"a served preview or the typed string
shown verbatim, not a client-side format."*

So the `AMOUNT` row prefers the DRAFT whenever any money field differs from the
stored row, and `rating.charges.amount.flat` is `{{amount}}`, a passthrough, so
**no format is invented**. Echoing is not arithmetic — nothing is scaled,
rounded or re-based, which is what `DEF-364` actually forbade — and it is
exactly what the sample bill line one panel below has done since 2026-09-19.

**Two cases are deliberately unchanged.** A CREATE still reads *As typed above*:
it is honest, it shipped, and the defect was reported against the edit path
alone. A retyped **percent** also reads *As typed above*, because the column
holds a FRACTION (`0.015` is 1.50%) — echoing it is `DEF-364` reproduced and
scaling it is the arithmetic that rule forbids.

### 4 · THE EDIT DOOR STOPS CLAIMING A VERSION; IT DOES NOT ACQUIRE ONE

`DEF-RAT-5824`: the charge-code header read *"…references the version in force,
so an issued bill never changes."* **There is no version in force.** `charges`
has no `effective_from`, no `effective_to` and no version table, and its own
Audit tab says so.

⚠ **THE WALK'S OWN ASSERTION ASKED FOR THE WRONG REMEDY AND WAS CORRECTED.** It
read `/Fix an error/i` — the rate schedule's *Change the rate / Fix an error*
question — over a screen whose whole finding is that it is **not versioned**.
**Passing that test would have meant inventing versioning to satisfy it.**
Effective-dated charge amounts are `OQ-RAT-12408` and are the PO's to size. The
case now asserts what the edit door actually owes a clerk: the change prices the
next bill.

This is `DEF-RAT-5711`'s mirror — that row corrected the identical false promise
on the rate-schedule review on 2026-09-17 and never reached this object — and
its own closing advice is what found this one: **grep the catalogues for the
CLAIM, not for the key.** Doing so turned up a third surface, filed below.

### 5 · WHAT WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED — both filed, neither silent

* **A customer-class FILTER on the charge-codes list.** The COLUMN is built and
  is what answers *which codes are class-scoped*. The filter is not:
  `charge_list_queryset` filters in SQL (`NFR-3`) and
  `applies_to_customer_classes` is a JSON column whose `__contains` lookup
  PostgreSQL supports and **SQLite does not** — and SQLite is what the whole
  test suite runs on (hard-won law 14). Half-building it would have shipped a
  filter that works in production and cannot be tested, or one tested on a
  database where the guarantee cannot exist.
* **The `Dated` banner on the charge code's Audit tab** still reads *"Bills
  always use the version in force on the usage date"* — the same false claim,
  on the same object. **It is the DRAWN specification** (`CR-087-p018` §4), so
  changing what a drawing says is the PO's call and not a maintenance lane's.

### 6 · WHY NO CHECK CAUGHT ANY OF THE FIVE

Two distinct shapes, and both are already in this repository's own lessons.

**Three of the five are an ABSENCE, which is invisible to every check we have.**
The Applicability tab rendered, every field it listed was correct, all eleven
catalogues held every key, `tsc` and every suite were green — and **nothing
compares the fields a detail tab SHOWS against the columns the row CARRIES.**
That is `DEF-CUS-3653`'s shape exactly.

**The other two are a screen stating something untrue of the object beneath it**,
and no gate reads a sentence against a schema. `G33` counts the words in
*"references the version in force"* and passes. `G15` confirms all eleven
catalogues hold the key and passes. The DOM tests assert the sub-line is SHOWN —
**the defect asserted as the feature.**

⚠ **AND ONE OF OUR OWN RED PROOFS DID NOT GO RED, WHICH IS THE LESSON WORTH
BANKING.** Six guards were broken in turn before being trusted green. Five
failed on exactly the case they were written for. The sixth — `DEF-RAT-5819` —
**passed**, because the revert was written as an early assignment in front of an
`if/else` chain that then ran anyway and overwrote it. The GUARD was fine; the
PROOF was the thing that could not fail. It was redone against the real pre-fix
expression and then failed correctly on two cases. **A red proof is a claim about
the revert as much as about the check, and the only thing that catches a bad one
is reading the line instead of the exit code.**

A second instance the same hour, in the browser walk: case `5b` compared the
page text before and after ticking the box. Correct against the OLD screen,
where ticking was the event. On the fixed screen the reason is drawn the moment
the step opens, so before and after are identical and **the case failed over a
screen doing the right thing.** Both were found by reading the output.
