## 2026-09-19 · BUILD THE MOVE-OUT WIZARD TO ITS DRAWING — STEPS 3, 4 AND 5, AND THE PLAN NAME ON STEP 1

**PO ruling, verbatim**, given step by step against a mapped table of all six
steps of the move-out wizard (blueprint p109–p116, read as images):

| Step | PO's words | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Find account | *"you should have plan name also in this - all other correct"* | ADD the plan name. Everything else on step 1 is signed off as built. |
| 2 · Date & final reads | *"this si correct"* | Signed off. No change. |
| 3 · Final bill & deposit | *"we need to do it"* | **BUILD IT** to the drawing. |
| 4 · The shortfall | *"this is correct"* | The drawing is right; build to it. |
| 5 · What happens next | *"we should build this"* | **BUILD IT** — the eight consequences. |
| 6 · Review & close | *"this si correct"* | Signed off. Built. |

**And the process rule, verbatim:** *"now only thing is clark can process and do
save and exit due to any reason - then it is available in the list - othersiwe
clsoed request is available for view in list view"*. Then: *"Can you build this
using the drawing and match the screena nd process"*.

### ⚠ THE KEYSTONE IS A FINAL-BILL PREVIEW, AND EVERYTHING ELSE DEPENDS ON IT

Steps 3, 4 and 5 are not three independent builds. **They are one blocked
chain**, established from code the same day with file:line evidence:

1. `move_out_settlement.settlement_for` takes a final-bill figure **the caller
   states**. Its own docstring says the wizard is *"already showing"* it.
2. **It is not.** Step 3 renders an `ArrivesWith` panel and five `NotRecorded`
   facts — no number, no input. *"There is no preview route and no invoice to
   price from — an amount here would be invented money."*
3. So **no caller in the product ever states one.** All three production reads of
   `close-impact` send none.
4. So the settlement returns `landing: null`, `gaps: ["final_bill_not_stated"]`,
   **every total null, on every account**.
5. So step 4's four shortfall radios render **ENABLED** (the skip test is false
   under a null landing) and `POST /accounts/{id}/settle-shortfall` refuses with
   `no_shortfall` **every single time** — a live control that can never succeed,
   hard-won law 2's mirror.
6. So step 5's money panels have nothing to state.

**The engine that makes a final bill EXISTS, is golden-tested, and works** —
`06-backend/apps/billing/final_bill.py`, BR-BIL-013. It is reachable **only**
from Billing → One-time bill, kind `final`, with **no link from any move-out
screen**, and `final_bill.py` refuses an account whose behaviour class is no
longer billable — *"The final bill therefore has to be produced BEFORE the
move-out writes the close"*. A clerk who commits the move-out first **cannot
raise the final bill at all**.

**So the ruled build order is: the preview first, then 3, then 4, then 5.**
Building step 3's panels before a figure exists would ship the same inert screen
with better typography.

### What the preview must and must not do
The drawing settles this itself, on p112, in a dashed panel: **"NO BILL IS ISSUED
BY THIS SCREEN. Billing raises the final bill; this wizard prices what it will
contain and posts nothing. The figures above are a settlement position, not an
invoice, and the account closes owing what the invoice will say."**

So: **PRICE, do not POST.** The preview reads assets, readings and plan/rates and
returns the lines and the net. It writes no invoice, no journal line and no
payment. That is what makes it safe to run inside a wizard a clerk may abandon.

### The save-and-exit rule is already served by two rulings made hours earlier
*"clark can process and do save and exit… then it is available in the list"* is
`ParkedDraftsPanel` (PO 2026-08-26) plus today's ruling that unfinished move-outs
become ROWS, plus today's ruling that the record page gains an action that
finishes the move. **Nothing new is needed for it**; it needs those three to land
and be walked in a browser together.

### Two things this ruling does NOT decide
* **Whether step 3 raises the bill itself or links out to the one-time bill
  screen.** The drawing says price-don't-post, so the preview is the answer for
  the FIGURE — but a clerk still needs a path to the real invoice, and the order
  trap above (bill before close, or it is refused forever) means that path cannot
  simply be "afterwards". Flagged to the PO; not settled here.
* **Deposit interest.** The signed arithmetic includes it and the product does
  not track it, and **the error runs against the customer** — a $150.00 deposit
  held fourteen months at 2% earns $3.50, so applying $150.00 where the rule says
  $153.50 makes the shortfall $3.50 too big. That is a ❄️ FROZEN figure question
  and needs a finance re-sign, not a lane.

## 2026-09-19 · THE CLERK CHOOSES WHAT THE UNIT BECOMES; NOTHING DERIVES IT

**PO ruling, verbatim: *"give option to clark to chose from - using drop down -
let him make the decision"***, answering whether the move-out record's drawn row
**`Unit now — Vacant · standby off`** should be served or dropped.

### ⚠ THE RULING DISSOLVES THE OBJECTION THAT BLOCKED THE ROW, RATHER THAN OVERRIDING IT
`MoveRecordPage.tsx`'s `UNIT_NOW_NOT_SERVED` refused to fill this row, and its
reasoning was sound: *"A unit standing empty and a unit whose standby charge was
switched off are two different facts; deriving either from occupancy would state
a measurement nobody took."* **Three options were put to the PO — serve it by
derivation, drop the row, or leave it stating the absence — and the PO answered
with a fourth nobody had offered: let the clerk state it.** Then nothing is
derived, no measurement is invented, and the objection simply does not arise.

### What is actually being decided, and it is MONEY
`metering.Unit.vacant_standby_auto` is a boolean, and `BR-MET-094` is the rule it
serves: **a vacant unit billed to the owner.** So the choice a clerk makes at
move-out is *when this unit stands empty, does the owner pay the base charge or
does nobody?* On the blueprint's own example that is `$20.00 a month` (p110,
drawn as an illustration under B14 rule 37 — the SHAPE, never the figure).

That is why a dropdown is right and a derivation was wrong: **nobody can infer
from an empty unit whether its owner agreed to be billed for it.**

### Where the choice is made, and where it is shown
**The clerk chooses on the WIZARD — step 5, `What happens next`**, which is where
the blueprint already draws `The unit · Vacant standby · Off — nobody is billed
for it` as a consequence. A consequence a clerk can change is a control, so the
drawn fact becomes the drawn choice.

**The RECORD page then SHOWS what was chosen**, as a fact. It does not offer the
dropdown: `/moves/{ref}` is the record of an act already taken, and putting the
choice on both surfaces is how two surfaces drift — which this product already
pays for once in `DEF-CUS-5901`, one state called two things on two screens.

### What this ruling does NOT decide
* **The option list itself.** Two are certain from the data — vacant with the
  owner billed, and vacant with nobody billed. Whether a third is needed for a
  unit going straight to a new tenant is the builder's to establish from the
  model and the drawing, not the PO's to enumerate.
* **Whether the choice may be changed after the move-out commits.** The record
  page shows it; changing it afterwards is a unit edit on another screen and is
  not in scope here.
* **What happens when a clerk parks mid-wizard without choosing.** It must not
  default silently — a blank consequence and a harmless one look identical once a
  screen guesses, which is p115's own warning about the six consequences the
  product cannot state.

## 2026-09-19 · DEPOSIT INTEREST IS COMPUTED AT SETTLEMENT — AND THIS IS IMPLEMENTING SIGNED LAW, NOT CHANGING IT

**PO ruling: option **B**, *"Compute at settlement only — from the deposit, its
date and the rate. Correct figure, no ongoing tracking."***

### The defect it answers
The signed arithmetic is `applied = deposit held + deposit interest`. The product
computes no interest, so it applies the deposit ALONE — and
`move_out_settlement.py` says what that costs in its own words: *"interest
understates `applied`, biasing the answer toward `short`."* **The error always
runs against the customer**, because applying less makes the shortfall bigger.

Worked, on the blueprint's own example (p112, an ILLUSTRATION under B14 rule 37 —
the shape, never the figures): a **$150.00** deposit held **fourteen months** at
**2%** simple earns **$3.50**. The rule applies **$153.50**; the product applies
**$150.00**; the departing customer is asked for **$3.50 more than they owe**.

### ⚠ NO FINANCE RE-SIGN IS NEEDED, AND THE REASON MATTERS
This was put to the PO as a ❄️ FROZEN-figure question. **On reading the code it
is not one.** The frozen arithmetic ALREADY includes the interest term;
`Settlement.deposit_interest` already exists as a field and already registers
`GAP_DEPOSIT_INTEREST` when absent. **Nothing signed is being changed — a signed
rule is being implemented for the first time.** Had this been recorded as a
re-sign it would have waited on finance for no reason, which is the opposite
failure to the one HUMAN-GUIDE §6 exists to prevent.

### What to build
`apps.customers.selectors.deposit_interest_accrued` is **published by nothing**
(US-CUS-023 §7). Compute at settlement from the deposit, the date it was taken
and the tenant's rate. **No accrual engine, no ongoing tracking** — option A
stays available later for a correct LEDGER; this gets the correct FIGURE at the
only moment it changes what a customer is asked for.

Money to **4 decimals stored**, percentages to **6**, **both display 2** (hard
rule 2). 🔒 sensitive path: `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` plus a review-ledger row
stating the worked figure in plain English.

### ⚠ ONE QUESTION THIS DOES NOT ANSWER, AND THE CODE ALREADY FLAGS IT
`GAP_DEPOSIT_INTEREST`'s own detail reads *"the accrued interest could not be
worked out. Either the day to accrue TO…"* — **interest to WHICH day?** The
move-out date, or the day the settlement is worked. It is a day or two of
interest, pennies on the example above, and it must be decided ONCE rather than
per lane, because two lanes choosing differently is two customers charged
differently for the same tenancy. Not settled here; raise it with the figure
attached when the builder reaches it.

## 2026-09-19 · THE RESUME DOOR IS BUILT, AND THE WORD IS `Resume` — NOT `Continue`, NOT `Complete`

Built from the ruling headed *"THE MOVE RECORD GETS AN ACTION THAT FINISHES THE
MOVE"* above. That ruling left exactly one thing to the builder, and this is it
recorded before it was reported to anybody (hard-won law 10).

### The judgment the ruling handed us

The ruling's own words: *"**Whether the action reads `Continue` or `Complete`.**
A move at step 2 of 6 is continued; one at step 6 is completed. That is the
builder's to resolve against the drawing and B14 rule 33's three-word cap on a
label — not a question for the PO."*

**Neither word was used. The action reads `Resume`,** and the reasoning is the
deliverable rather than the choice.

### Why not `Complete`

**It is true only at step 6.** The door opens the wizard at whatever step the
draft was parked at, so on the blueprint's own drawn example — `MVO-26-0087 ·
2 of 6 · In progress`, p117 — a button reading `Complete` promises four steps
it does not perform.

⚠ **AND ON A MOVE-OUT IT PROMISES SOMETHING THE PRODUCT CANNOT PRESENTLY DO AT
ALL.** Established with file:line evidence the same day: no final bill is
produced anywhere in the move-out flow, the settlement engine works off a
final-bill figure the caller states and no caller in the product ever states
one, so `close-impact` returns `landing: null` with
`gaps: ["final_bill_not_stated"]` on every account, and step 4's shortfall
POST is refused every time. **A button that says `Complete` over that is a
promise the screen cannot keep**, and it is the kind of promise a clerk only
discovers four steps in.

### Why not `Continue` either

`Continue` is TRUE at every step, so it clears the bar `Complete` fails. It was
rejected for a different reason: **it mints a SECOND word for an act this
product already names.**

`customers.waitingOn.action.resume` is **`Resume`**, and it is the word on the
parked-drafts panel — **the very surface this door replaces a trip to.** It
already exists in **all eleven catalogues**, written in each language rather
than machine-translated from English (B14 rule 35): `Fortsetzen` · `Reanudar` ·
`Reprendre` · `Riprendi` · `Lanjutkan` · `Retomar` · `फिर शुरू करें` ·
`再開する` · `재개`.

**One act, one word.** That is B14 rule 34's principle — *"one pair of words for
*held here* and *in the books*"* — applied to the act this pair of surfaces
shares, and it is the exact failure `DEF-CUS-5901` records: **one state called
two things on two screens.** The ruling cites that defect itself as the cost of
letting two surfaces drift.

### And the key is SHARED, not copied

The page reads `customers.waitingOn.action.resume` directly rather than minting
`customers.moveRecord.action.resume`. A new key would be **eleven new strings
free to drift from the eleven that already say the same thing**; sharing the key
makes drift impossible instead of merely discouraged. A test asserts both
surfaces resolve the same word, so anyone re-wording the panel is told they are
re-wording this door too.

**Rule 33 is satisfied either way and more tightly than asked:** a LABEL caps at
three words, and this is **one**.

### What the ruling did NOT have to decide, because the data decided it

**Where the action sits.** The brief asked whether finishing a move outranks
`Open the account` on an unfinished record. **It cannot contend with it at all**
— `_in_flight()` serves the account door as `NO_ACCOUNT_UNTIL_IT_COMPLETES` on
**every** unfinished move, because an account is what completing one PRODUCES.
So the primary slot was **already empty** on exactly the records this action
appears on. That emptiness is what a clerk experienced as the dead end, and no
drawn control is displaced to fill it.

### The one field the backend had to grow, and why it is not a join

⚠ **THE RECORD IS ADDRESSED BY REFERENCE AND THE WIZARD IS RESUMED BY ID**, so
the payload could NAME the draft and could not OPEN it. `GET /moves/{ref}` is
keyed on `MVI-26-0114` because that is the number a clerk quotes (B14 rule 31),
while `resumePath()` builds `/move-ins/new?parked=<id>`.

`_in_flight()` is handed the `WizardPark` row that `_park_by_reference()` has
already resolved, so **`park_id` is a projection of the object in hand — no
query, no join.** Matching a draft to a record by address and date, which is the
shape a join would have taken, picks the wrong draft the first time one unit has
two. It is `str(park.id)`, the same expression `wizard_parks.row_dict` uses, so
the two doors onto one act hand the wizard a byte-identical handle.

**It is served for `in_flight` and for nothing else**, and that absence is a
guard rather than an omission: a completed move has no draft to go back into, so
a completed record cannot grow this door even by accident.

### What was NOT built, and is not implied

* **`Tie the shortfall back`** — p118's second head action. A money path: it
  moves money between accounts and needs the ledger posting service, hard rule
  7's `audit_log` write and a 🔒 human-review row. **The write path
  `POST /accounts/{id}/settle-shortfall` EXISTS and is live** — what is missing
  is the consent dialog. Held, with a test that goes red the day it lands.
* **The money spine.** This door gives the journey its door; a move-IN can
  complete, and a move-OUT lands the clerk in a wizard whose money step is
  inert. **Nothing in the UI, the docstrings or the report says otherwise.**


## 2026-09-19 · THE FINAL-BILL PREVIEW — THE KEYSTONE BUILT, AND THE FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULES RAN OUT ON

Built to the ruling of the same day (*"BUILD THE MOVE-OUT WIZARD TO ITS DRAWING
— STEPS 3, 4 AND 5"*), whose own words put this first: *"the ruled build order
is: the preview first, then 3, then 4, then 5."*

**WHAT WAS BUILT, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT.** `final_bill.
preview_final_bill` prices the closing period and returns the LINES and the
net. It is **not a new engine and not even a new preview**: the price-only path
already existed end to end and nobody had noticed — `one_time.preview(kind=
'final')` has called `prepare_final_bill` + `runs.price_account` since
`CR-108` wave 1, and `POST /billing/one-time/preview` serves it. What was
missing was a door the WIZARD could open, because that route needs a
`period_start` the wizard does not have and must not guess. So the new function
is the composition and nothing else: derive the window, call the two existing
calls, serialise. **`runs.price_account` is stages 1–5 of the run's own
`calculate_account`, so the figure a clerk approves and the figure Billing
raises cannot differ by construction.**

### Judgment 1 — THE PREVIEW RETURNS THE CHARGES, AND `close-impact` APPLIES THE REST
p112 draws *Unbanked export credit* as a row of the final-bill table with
*Final bill, net* beneath it, and a lane reading only the drawing would
subtract it in the preview. **It must not.** `BR-MET-107`'s credit is
metering's fact applied by the SETTLEMENT: `move_out_settlement` reads it and
computes `final_bill_net = final_bill − export_credit` itself, and serves both
on `close-impact`. Measured the same day: **`export_credit` occurs ZERO times
anywhere in `apps/billing/`** — the engine prices no such line. So the
preview's `total` is the CHARGES, it is exactly what `?final_bill=` wants, and
a subtraction in both places would credit the customer **twice for the same
exported kWh on an account nobody re-reads**. The deposit is split the same
way and for the same reason: `BR-BIL-013` applies it FIRST and the remainder
selects the path, and that arithmetic is `settle_closing_position`'s.
**So the drawn table is assembled from the two calls together** — priced rows
from the preview, the export-credit row and the net from `close-impact`. It is
written into both docstrings, because the next lane to read only the drawing
will reach for the subtraction again.

### Judgment 2 — THE SEAM RETURNS `None`; ITS NEIGHBOUR RAISES
`customers.seams.preview_final_bill` answers `None` when billing has not
published, which is **the opposite posture to `raise_and_issue_cut_bill`
directly above it**. That one raises, because it is a WRITE and a caller
reading `None` as *"no bill then"* would close an account whose last days were
billed to nobody. This one is a READ on a screen that already knows how to say
*"this could not be worked out"*. Refusing the whole wizard because a preview
could not be produced would block a move-out the product can otherwise
complete.

### Judgment 3 — NO `audit_log` ROW, AND IT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION
Hard rule 7 is about money ACTIONS. The preview moves no money, records no
decision and changes no row. Auditing it would fill the log a clerk uses to
reconstruct a money path with **one row per keystroke of a wizard they may
abandon**, and make the genuine rows — the shortfall decision, the refund, the
issue — harder to find rather than easier. It takes the posture
`account_close_impact` already states for the same screen (*"A READ — no
`audit_log` row, because nothing moved"*).

### Judgment 4 — AN EXISTING MESSAGE KEY, NOT A TWELFTH ONE
The route refuses an absent `moved_out_on` with
`customers.account.move_out_date_required` — *"Enter the move-out date."* —
which already exists in **all eleven catalogues**. B14 rule 35 makes a
catalogue its own language rather than a translation of English, so minting a
new key would have meant ten machine translations or ten missing entries, and
a refusal that reaches a clerk as **silence** (`DEF-CWP-3925`'s shape, and the
21 live refusals `G32` could not see).

### WHAT IT UNBLOCKED, MEASURED ON 2026-09-19
**The worked case, run rather than predicted.** A closing electric account read
on the move day prices **300 kWh @ $0.120000 = $36.00** plus an **$18.50** base
charge, **$54.50 in all, no tax**, over a window of **2026-06-01 → 2026-06-12**
that was DERIVED rather than stated (12 service days).

⚠ **THE BASE CHARGE IS WHOLE, NOT PRORATED, AND THAT IS `OQ-242`'s WITHDRAWAL
RATHER THAN A DEFECT.** B4.3 ❄️ divides by `service_days / cycle_days`; a
one-time run has no cycle, so every engine defaults the denominator to the
WINDOW's own length, the factor is 1, and a partial window carries a full base.
The PO was shown that consequence in those words and closed it on 2026-08-23 —
*"its proration denominator (the current guess OVER-CHARGES while it stands). -
this is not required"*. **The preview therefore shows $18.50 deliberately**,
because the DRAFT path (`one_time._draft_for` → `prepare_final_bill(cycle_days=
_cycle_days(request))`, which is always `None`) will raise exactly that. Cut to
twelve days it would be **$7.40**, a difference of **$11.10** on this account —
restated in the review-ledger row because it is real money and the reviewer's to
change, not a lane's. **`tc12` pins the ruled figure so nobody "fixes" it into
new arithmetic on a ❄️ FROZEN rule.**

`settlement_for` WITHOUT a figure: `gaps: ["final_bill_not_stated"]`,
`complete: false`, **`landing: None`**, `step_4_live: false`.
WITH `final_bill=54.50` on an account carrying **$500.00** of arrears:
outstanding **$554.50**, applied **$153.50** (deposit $150.00 + $3.50 interest,
first, per BR-BIL-013), **shortfall $401.00**, `gaps: []`,
**`landing: "short"`, `step_4_live: TRUE`** — and `shortfall_paths` offers
collect, payment_plan and write_off, with transfer correctly disabled carrying
its reason (no owner account on this premises, BR-MET-105a).
**That is `step_4_live` becoming a measurement instead of a constant** — step
4's four shortfall radios had rendered ENABLED over a `POST` that refused with
`no_shortfall` on every account in the product, hard-won law 2's mirror.

⚠ **AND IT DOES NOT UNBLOCK EVERY LANDING.** The SAME $54.50 on an account with
no arrears lands **$99.00 in CREDIT**, and there `landing` is STILL `None`
because `gaps` carries `open_disputes_not_readable`. `BR-CUS-096` holds a refund
while a dispute is open and **nothing in this repository stores a disputed
AMOUNT**, so the settlement fails closed, correctly. The refund direction stays
blocked on `BR-CUS-096`; `tc10` pins it so the next lane meets it as a test
rather than as an empty screen.

### IT IS THE EXISTING FLOW, AND THAT IS PROVED RATHER THAN CLAIMED
**PO instruction, verbatim:** *"i hope you will use existing code to generate
single bill - we have this flow build in billing"*. `POST /billing/one-time/
preview` with `kind: "final"` has been mounted and price-only since `CR-108`
wave 1 and IS that flow. `preview_final_bill` does not replace it: it calls the
SAME `prepare_final_bill` then `runs.price_account`, and serialises each line
with the SAME `one_time._line_body`. **`tc11` drives both doors over one account
and requires them to agree line for line and on the net**, so a second
arithmetic behind either one goes red naming the figure.

**What the mounted route could NOT do is open its own window**, and that is the
whole of what was added. Measured: `one_time.preview` with no `period_start`
refuses by name — *"a 'final' bill needs both ends of its period. Every
proration in B4.3 divides by this window and no end of it is defaulted."* The
wizard knows ONE date, the move-out day; the other end is `cut_bill.
first_unbilled_day` — the day after the last ISSUED bill (BR-BIL-004), or the
account's move-in date, and a REFUSAL when it is neither. **That derivation is a
money decision and was never the front end's to make**, which is why it is
served rather than asked for.

### ⚠ THE CONTRACT STEP 3 BUILDS AGAINST — PUBLISHED FOR THE FRONT-END LANE

**Call:** `GET /accounts/{id}/final-bill-preview?moved_out_on=YYYY-MM-DD`
(`&period_start=` OPTIONAL, only to re-price a window a clerk corrected).
`moved_out_on` is the day stated on step 2. Absent, it refuses with
`customers.account.move_out_date_required`.
The identical body is available from `POST /billing/one-time/preview`
`{account_id, kind:"final", period_start, period_end}` when the caller already
holds BOTH ends of the window — `tc11` proves the two agree line for line.

**Body on success:**

```
{ "priced": true,
  "account_id", "account_no",
  "period_start": "2026-06-01", "period_end": "2026-06-12",
  "period_start_derived": true,      // false when the clerk stated it
  "service_days": 12, "cycle_days": 12,
  "lines": [ { "kind": "usage"|"base"|"tax"|"fee",
               "description": "electric usage",
               "amount": "36.00",          // 4dp text, DISPLAY at 2 (rule 2)
               "quantity": "300.000000", "unit": "kWh",   // rule 3: never bare
               "unit_price": "0.120000",   // on a TAX line this IS the rate
               "taxable": true, "service": "electric",
               "estimated": false,         // BR-MET-029 — p112's "· estimated"
               "tax_id", "tariff_version_id", "charge_id" } ],
  "subtotal": "54.50", "tax_total": "0.00", "total": "54.50", "currency": "USD",
  "split": false,
  "issues_nothing": true, "writes": [] }
```

**Body on refusal** — `priced: false`, `lines: []`, **NO `total` KEY AT ALL**
(a `0.00` is a money claim), plus
`priced_unavailable: {reason, detail}`. The four reasons a screen must group on:
`final_bill_period_start_not_derivable` (no issued bill and no move-in date) ·
`account_already_closed_for_billing` (the move-out was committed first) ·
`deposit_interest_not_accrued` · `final_bill_preview_seam_unpublished`.

**HOW STEP 3'S DRAWN TABLE IS ASSEMBLED — IT IS TWO CALLS, NOT ONE.**
p112 draws `LINE · PERIOD · AMOUNT` then *Unbanked export credit* then
*Final bill, net*. The priced rows and the PERIOD come from **this** call; the
**export-credit row and `Final bill, net` come from `close-impact`**
(`everything_outstanding.export_credit` and `.final_bill_net`), which applies
`BR-MET-107`. **Do not subtract the export credit on the client** — billing
prices no such line and the settlement already nets it; doing both credits the
customer twice.

**THEN:** pass `total` VERBATIM to
`GET /accounts/{id}/close-impact?final_bill=<total>&as_of=<moved_out_on>` — as
TEXT, never a JSON number (rule 2). That is what makes `landing`, `step_4_live`
and `shortfall_paths` real. Every money figure there arrives as
`{"stored": "401.0000", "display": "401.00"}`: **render `display`.**

⚠ **`landing` CAN STILL BE `null` AFTER ALL THIS, AND THE SCREEN MUST HANDLE
IT.** A close that lands in CREDIT gaps on `open_disputes_not_readable`
(`BR-CUS-096`, no dispute store exists). Only the SHORT direction currently
produces a landing, and `step_4_live` is true in that one alone.

### TWO THINGS REPORTED RATHER THAN TAKEN
* ⚠ **`06-backend/apps/billing/final_bill.py` IS NOT ON
  `10-scripts/gates/human_owned.txt`.** It implements `BR-BIL-013`'s entire
  settlement matrix — 🔒 rating math — while BOTH its callers, `one_time.py`
  and `cut_bill.py`, are on the list. A lane may not add itself (that file's
  own header calls changing it a process event), so the glob is ASKED FOR in
  the review-ledger row, exactly as `cut_bill.py` asked for its own. **This is
  the seventh time this escape has hit a money path.**
* ⚠ **❄️ GT-23 — WE-7, the final-bill settlement — HAS NO ENGINE-VERIFIED
  GOLDEN TEST.** `06-backend/tests/golden/` holds 14 of the 61 signed GTs
  (GT-1..11, 16, 24, 47) and GT-23 is not among them, so **nothing in that
  directory runs the engine over a final bill**; what guards those frozen
  figures is `test_us_bil_011_final_bill.py`. (`10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py`
  reports 33 DOCUMENT self-consistency checks and imports no application code,
  so it cannot cover this either.) Filed, not fixed — writing a golden test for
  a ❄️ FROZEN figure is a separate, deliberate act.

**The two questions the ruling left open are untouched**: whether step 3 links
out to the real invoice, and deposit interest (a ❄️ FROZEN figure question
needing a finance re-sign, not a lane).

## 2026-09-19 · THE MOVE-OUT WIZARD'S STEPS 3, 4 AND 5, BUILT — AND THE THREE
## PLACES THE DRAWING ASKS FOR A CONTROL NOTHING ACCEPTS

Built under the ruling recorded above (*"we need to do it"* · *"this is
correct"* · *"we should build this"* · *"you should have plan name also in
this"*), from **p110–p115 of `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` read
as IMAGES** (B14 rule 42; the PO's standing instruction of the same day —
*"product screesn to be created using impages and UI genetor skills"*). Each
drawn screen spans two PDF pages, which the text layer cannot show: step 3 is
the bottom of p112 plus the top of p113.

### What is on each step now

* **Step 1** gains ONE row, the plan, written `SCW-RES · Residential · v1` as
  p110 draws it. It is the UNIT's plan (`unit_plan`, through
  `accounts.unit_id → units.rate_plan_id`) and never `detail.plan`, which is
  the account snapshot that has no table — `DEF-2419` is the defect that came
  from reading one as the other. No plan id is served or shown (B14 rule 31).
  Nothing else on step 1 changed; the PO signed the rest off.
* **Step 3** is the drawing's three left sections — *The final bill* (LINE ·
  PERIOD · AMOUNT), *What to do with the deposit*, *Everything outstanding* —
  and its two right ones, *The five landings, one arithmetic* and *What the
  other three would ask for*.
* **Step 4** is *What happens to $X*, the four paths, *What each one would ask
  for* (with the drawing's third column, **WHO CAN**) and *What the chosen path
  will do*.
* **Step 5** is *The account* · *The unit* · *The meters* · *The money* · *What
  we will send* · *What this close does NOT do*, plus the six p115 names.

### ⚠ THE KEYSTONE IS WIRED, AND THE CHAIN IS CLOSED IN ONE DIRECTION

`GET /accounts/{id}/final-bill-preview?moved_out_on=` is read on step 3 and its
`total` is stated to `GET /accounts/{id}/close-impact?final_bill=`, which is the
term `settlement_for` has always required and **no caller in this product ever
supplied**. The read also states `as_of` — the move-out day — which is what
BR-CUS-057's interest accrues to. Until the preview route lands on this branch
the read fails and **every figure states its own absence**; nothing is
defaulted and no figure is drawn that the server did not send.

### ⚠ THREE PLACES THE DRAWING DRAWS A CONTROL AND NOTHING ACCEPTS THE FIELD

Recorded rather than taken quietly, because each is a judgment where the rules
ran out and the next lane will otherwise read the drawing and put the control
back.

1. **p112's four deposit radios are built as four STATED options.** The drawing's
   own caption is the reason: *"Which of the four is available is decided by the
   subtraction below, NOT BY THE CLERK."* `POST /accounts/{id}/move-out` refuses
   `deposit_disposition` outright (BR-CUS-025, `services.REFUSED_FIELDS`), so
   four radios would be hard-won law 2's mirror — a live control that can never
   succeed, which is the defect this same lane fixed one step along. All four
   are named, one is marked as the applied rule, and the three unavailable ones
   each say why in ≤ 6 words.
2. **p112's *Amount to apply* and *Applied on* are built as FACTS, not inputs.**
   The settlement applies the WHOLE deposit (`derive(deposit_held=…)`) and has
   no partial-apply parameter; the date it accrues to is the move-out day the
   clerk already stated at step 2. The deposit figure falls back to the
   account's own `deposit_on_file`, which is **the same column** the settlement
   reads as `deposit_held` — one number, one step earlier, not a second figure.
   **The prior balance gets no such fallback**: `detail.balance` is a cache
   nothing writes (DEF-127) where the settlement reads the LEDGER.
3. **p113's *Forwarding address* input under `Collect it` is not drawn as an
   input.** `shortfall_decision` accepts `path`, `final_bill` and `as_of` and
   nothing else. The field is NAMED in *What each one would ask for*, which is
   the drawing's own table and says exactly this.

### ⚠ AND ONE PLACE THE DRAWING'S ANNOTATION BECAME SCREEN STRUCTURE

p115's dashed panel — *"SIX CONSEQUENCES THE PRODUCT CANNOT YET STATE … Each is
named rather than defaulted, because a blank consequence and a harmless one
look identical once a screen guesses"* — is rendered as **six visible named
rows**, not behind a closed disclosure. B14 rule 32 puts a stated absence in a
closed `<details>`; that governs a screen's DESCRIPTION BUDGET, and **a
consequence folded away is the same blank the sentence warns about**, which is
B19 §15.7's own rule (the headline fact cannot be folded) and the reason the
nine panels this replaced kept their `CHECK`/`BLOCKED` advisories outside the
disclosure body. Each label is ≤ 3 words (rule 33's LABEL cap).

### What was REMOVED, and it was ~900 words of rationale

Step 5's nine `Disclosure` panels (Premises · Unit · Assets · Plans · Deposit ·
Payments · Open items · Sub-accounts · Collections) are gone. They were
assembled on 2026-08-24 from the UNION of B18 row 5.7's seven and B19 §15.10's
six, before the blueprint existed, and they explained themselves at length —
which B14 rule 33 puts at **ZERO words on screen**. One sentence they carried
was a live rule-33 breach of thirty words (*"While the unit is empty its
standing charge is billed to the owner's account AC-… and it comes off that
account again the day the next tenant takes the unit"*); it is now two sentences
of six, and the PO's 2026-08-31 ruling it serves — which account, that the
charge continues, and the reverse edge — is still stated in full.

### The defect this build found and fixed

`DEF-CUS-5920` — step 4's four shortfall radios rendered **ENABLED on every
account in the product** over a `POST` that refused `no_shortfall` every time.
The skip test read `landing !== null && landing !== "short"`, which is false
under a null landing, and the landing was null everywhere because nothing ever
stated a final bill. It now reads the SERVER's own `step_4_live`. Two cases pin
it, and both were **proved RED against the original two-branch code** — the
first attempt at that proof reverted one line, the guard stayed green, and only
restoring the whole original shape showed the defect. A red proof that does not
reproduce the defect is not a proof.

### Two things this does NOT decide

* **Whether a clerk can reach the real invoice from here.** The preview prices
  and posts nothing, by the drawing's own instruction; `final_bill.py` still
  refuses an account whose behaviour class has left the billable set, so the
  bill must be raised BEFORE the close. No link is added on a guess.
* **Deposit interest.** Unchanged and still a ❄️ FROZEN-figure question needing

  and the error runs against the customer. The screen prints *Not recorded*

## 2026-09-19 · THE UNFINISHED MOVE-OUTS ARE ON THE LIST, AND THE FOUR CALLS THAT WERE OURS

The ruling itself is the entry above — *"THE MOVE-OUTS LIST SHOWS THE UNFINISHED
ONES, AND ONE WORD IS `Completed`"*, PO verbatim **`yes`**. This records what was
BUILT for it and, more usefully, the four judgments the ruling did not settle.
Each is written down because the next agent reads the repo and not this session.

### What a clerk sees now

The Move-outs tab holds **two kinds of row**. A move-out that HAPPENED is the
row it always was, and its state word is now **`Completed`** rather than
`Closed`. A move-out a clerk STARTED and put down is a new row beside it,
carrying the step they actually reached — `2 of 6` — and the word **`In
progress`**, or **`Waiting`** when they recorded what they are waiting for. On
the seeded `brazosbend` tenant the list went from **1 row to 2** with one parked
move-out planted, and back to 1 when it was removed.

It is one ordered page over both kinds in SQL, not two lists merged in Python —
`NFR-3`, the same shape `BR-CUS-1077` gave the Move-ins tab. `f.closed` is a
window on `accounts.closed_at` and a draft has closed nothing, so that filter
returns **1 of the 2** and never both.

### Call 1 · THE THREE KPI TILES STILL COUNT THE CLOSED ROWS ONLY

`OPEN` reads **`1`** over a list of **2**, and its caption says exactly what it
counts: *"closed, not yet finally billed"*. The drawing captions that tile
*"not yet closed"*, which is the opposite, and until today our code said the
drawn caption was unbuildable because *"a move-out in flight is not recorded
anywhere"* — the sentence this ruling proved false.

**So the drawn caption IS buildable now, and it was deliberately not built.**
The ruling is one sentence about which ROWS the list holds. Redefining what a
tile COUNTS would move a number the PO read on this screen the same morning,
silently, and would make `OPEN` mean the opposite of the five words printed
under it. `open_means` is served precisely so a caption cannot redefine a
figure, and it still reads `closed_and_not_yet_finally_billed`.

**If the tile should count the unfinished ones instead, that is a one-line
change to `move_out_kpis` and a caption — and it is a decision, not a
consequence.**

### Call 2 · THE PANEL ABOVE THE TABLE IS STILL MOUNTED, AND IT IS THE PO'S TO REMOVE

`AccountsListPage.tsx` renders `<ParkedDraftsPanel flow="move_out" />` above this
table under a PO ruling of 2026-08-26. The same parked move-out is now on that
screen **twice**. That is worse than either alone and it is not ours to fix:
removing the panel reverses a ruling given in the PO's own words, which hard-won
law 13 puts on the short list of things that legitimately reach them.

**What makes it recommendable is the panel's own argument.** `parkedDrafts.tsx`
§1 rejected merging drafts into these tables because *"a `MoveInRow` and a
`WizardParkRow` share not one field"*. **True of a move-IN draft, false of a
move-OUT one:** the move-out wizard starts from an account a clerk has already
picked, so the draft carries `account_id` and the row fills ACCOUNT, CUSTOMER,
UNIT and STEP from it — four of ten columns, including the table's identity
column. `OQ-CUS-12488` carries it with the cost of each option, including the
one real loss: the panel's `Discard` control has no equivalent on a row.

### Call 3 · A ROW'S `↗ Open` HAS TWO DESTINATIONS, AND THE ROW DECIDES

A FINISHED move-out opens its record at `/moves/{ref}` — the page that says what
happened. An UNFINISHED one has **no record and no reference to address one
with**, and what a clerk wants from it is to carry on; so it opens the wizard at
the step it was left on, `/move-outs/new?parked=<id>`, through `resumePath` —
**the same builder the parked panel's Resume uses**, so two surfaces cannot
drift apart on the handle. The button says `↗ Open` either way, because the verb
a clerk reads is *open this move-out* in both cases.

⚠ **A SIBLING LANE WIDENED `resumePath` TO `Pick<WizardParkRow, "id" | "flow">`
THE SAME AFTERNOON, FOR THE MOVE RECORD'S OWN RESUME DOOR, WITH THE SAME
REASONING IN ALMOST THE SAME WORDS.** This lane had made the identical edit and
DROPPED it at push time in favour of theirs. Worth recording because it is law
11's mechanism two caught working: the tip moved, the rebase was against the
pinned tip, and the duplicate edit was found by re-deriving rather than by a
test.

### Call 4 · THE STEP HAS TWO ANSWERS AND BOTH ARE RIGHT

A parked row prints `2 of 6`. A closed row prints *"Step not recorded"*, and
**must**: four code paths write `accounts.closed_at` and only one is the wizard
(`services.move_out`, against the disconnect close-out at `close_out.py`, the
account import and the import rollback). `6 of 6` on the other three would claim
a clerk walked six steps they never saw. The two are asserted on ONE page, in
one case, in both suites.

### The absences an unfinished row states rather than invents

| Cell | What it says | Why |
|---|---|---|
| REFERENCE | *"This move-out has not finished, so it has no number yet."* | only a move-IN draft is numbered while it is in hand (`CR-122-BRC06`, ruled the same day) — `OQ-CUS-12489` |
| SETTLEMENT | *"Not settled until it closes"* | nothing is settled until the account closes, and there is not even a gap to name |
| MOVE-OUT DATE | *"No move-out date yet."* | the step that asks for one has not been reached |
| ACCOUNT | one of two sentences | nobody has picked an account yet · or the one this draft named has gone |

⚠ **THE SETTLEMENT CELL HARDCODED THE CLOSED ROW'S REASON AND WAS FOUND BY
BUILDING THE NEW ONE.** It printed *"the final bill is not readable"* on every
row, which is true of a closed one and states a GAP where an unfinished one has
a LIFECYCLE. The label follows the absence's code now.

### What was stale and is amended, dated, in the same commit

`MOVE_OUT_NOT_YET_CLOSED_HAS_NO_STORE`'s sentence (kept under its own code and
narrowed to the one state still unholdable — `scheduled`, a move-out nobody has
started) · `STEP_HAS_NO_STORE`'s claim that a parked step *"is the parked-drafts
panel above this table, not a row in it"* · `MoveStepCell.reached`'s
*"⛔ ALWAYS `null`"* · `MoveStepBar`'s *"nothing is filled because nothing is
known"* · `move_reads.py` §2's title *"A MOVE-OUT HAS NO BEGINNING IN THIS
SCHEMA"* · the `GET /move-outs` handler's *"ONLY A MOVE-OUT THAT HAS ALREADY
HAPPENED IS SERVABLE"* · `ABSENCE_COPY`'s clerk-facing sentence, **which was the
false one actually on screen**.

`DEF-CUS-5919` is the row for all of it, and its escape reason is the durable
part: **the absence was asserted as a guarantee by its own test**, so the code
and its guard agreed with each other and neither agreed with the schema. Nothing
in this repo re-reads a stated absence to ask whether it is still true.

### Version

**`2.313.1`** — `<release>.<change>.<fix>`, a fix bump on the tip's `2.313.0`.
Maintenance, not Build: the list is live, this was reproduced in a browser
before any code was read, and `DEF-CUS-5901` and `DEF-CUS-5919` are the rows it
closes.

⚠ **THIS LINE SAID `2.312.1` FOR ONE COMMIT, AND THE MECHANISM IS WORTH MORE
THAN THE TYPO.** The branch took six commits from three lanes while this one was
being written, so every shared file was re-derived from a freshly pinned tip at
push time — correctly. **The version step ran AFTER the append step in the same
script**, so it rewrote the decision-log FRAGMENT that the append had already
consumed: the file on disk kept the figure from the previous attempt while
`package.json`, `pyproject.toml` and `CHANGELOG.md` all carried the new one.
`allocate.py version --verify` would not have caught it either — the number
shipped was right, and the only thing wrong was a sentence describing it.
**The general form: a re-derivation that writes a fragment must run BEFORE
anything reads that fragment, and the check is to diff the figure against the
artefact rather than to re-read the script.**

## 2026-09-19 · WHAT THE BROWSER FOUND THAT THE SUITE COULD NOT — FIVE THINGS,
## ON THE MOVE-OUT WIZARD, ALL GREEN

The steps above were built, typechecked, linted and unit-green at 52 passing
cases. They were then **booted and clicked** — a Django runserver on the
worktree's own code, `vite build` + `server.mjs`, Playwright at 1440 — because
hard-won law 6 says that is the only check in this repository that reads
rendered output, and `renderToStaticMarkup` never performs the second render a
crash needs (`DEF-CUS-5911`).

**Five findings, none of them visible to any check this repo has:**

1. ⚠ **`Short by $0.00` — `DEF-CUS-5926`, and it is the serious one.**
   `MoveOutSettlement` fails closed on the LANDING and the TOTALS and says so
   in its own docstring, but `shortfall`, `excess`, `settled_amount` and
   `refund_amount` are typed `-> Decimal` and return `ZERO` when `net` is None.
   So the payload carries `verdict.shortfall = "0.0000"` under a gap, and the
   screen printed **the claim that this customer owes nothing** three rows
   under its own sentence *"The subtraction has not run yet"* — and again on
   step 4's headline, step 5's money group and step 6's recap. **A zero the
   arithmetic never reached is not a measurement.** Guarded client-side (the
   four verdict figures are readable only with a landing; the prior balance and
   the deposit held are real reads and survive). The SERVER half — those four
   properties should be `Decimal | None`, like `net` already is — is filed and
   is a money-path lane's own work.
2. **The five landings rendered in the SERVER's order, not the drawing's.**
   `MONEY_LANDINGS` ends `refused_other_debt, refused_excess`; p112 draws Held
   before To a sibling. Order is part of the design. Still derived — anything
   the server adds that the drawn list does not name is appended rather than
   dropped.
3. **Three enum codes reached the clerk**: *"Method — ach · mailed cheque ·
   carry to new account"*. `method.replace(/_/g, " ")` looks like a formatter
   and is a raw code with its underscores combed (B14 rule 32).
4. ⚠ **A catalogue sentence that went false three weeks ago.**
   `customers.moveOut.impact.notServed` is in all eleven catalogues reading
   *"This arrives with the close-impact read, which is NOT BUILT YET"*. The
   read was mounted on 2026-08-25 (`DEF-669`). **A catalogue entry beats a
   `defaultValue`**, so the correct sentence written in the code rendered
   nowhere — the `DEF-731` shape, and hard-won law 1 running in the direction
   nothing looks at. A new key states the fact; the old one is retired.
5. **Two labels welded to an absence**: *"Vacant, from Set the move-out date
   first."* and *"2 end"* — a sentence with its object missing. Each now reads
   as one thing or the other.

**The generalisable part:** every one of the five is a STRING or a FIGURE that
is correct in the code and wrong on the page. `tsc`, eslint, 55 unit cases and
every gate passed over all five. Two of them (3 and 4) exist *because* a
catalogue and an enum are resolved at render time, which is precisely the layer
a `toContain` assertion on markup cannot judge and a person reading the screen
judges in a second.

## 2026-09-19 · The move-out scenario suite — twenty-seven rows, two columns, and what the billing keystone actually bought

**What was asked, verbatim.** *"ensure you run end to end walk withmuitle
scenarios - deposites, settlement, bill creation etc - update all premises,
unit, plans , asset and acunt status etc move the pending money to master
account - create variosu cases and scenarios and do end to end walk to ensure
clark is able to perform all these task from screen"*.

Built as `06-backend/tests/test_move_out_scenarios.py`, run by
`./10-scripts/move_out_scenarios.sh`, recorded as `J-MVO-TWENTYSEVEN`. It
follows the move-in suite's shape deliberately — ONE TABLE a runner iterates,
every row declaring a verdict for all THIRTEEN dimensions, `declares()`
refusing an incomplete row at IMPORT time — for the PO's own reason: *"otherwise
scenario twelve gets a check that scenario three doesn't, and nobody notices."*

### THE NUMBER WORTH QUOTING: 1 of 27, and 16 of 27

Every scenario runs TWICE, in two independent transactions, because
`settlement_for` takes the final bill **from its caller** and a settlement with
a bill and one without are two different settlements about one customer's money.

| column | what it asks | complete |
|---|---|---|
| **NO BILL** | `settlement_for(actor, id)` | **1 of 27** |
| **WITH BILL** | `settlement_for(..., final_bill=…, as_of=…)` | **16 of 27** |

**That pair is the clearest statement anyone has of what the final-bill preview
bought.** Fifteen scenarios move from incomplete to complete on one keystone.
The single row that is complete without a bill is `E2` — the BR-BIL-004 refusal,
which never reaches the money at all.

**COMPLETE means no failure AND nothing left unasserted**, and that definition
is the judgment. A row whose landing could not be asserted in a pass is not
complete in it, however many of its other checks passed: counting it green would
report a scenario as working on the strength of the dimensions that are not what
it is about, which is hard-won law 7's *reporting zero over a scope it silently
excludes*, in a scoreboard. Scored the looser way the first column would have
read **20 of 24** and meant nothing.

### THE KEYSTONE LANDED MID-BUILD, AND STEP 0 IS WHAT CAUGHT IT

This suite was written against a brief that said the wizard states no final
bill, so `landing` is `null` on every account in the product. **That stopped
being true at 18:47, while the suite was being written**, when `1c69a87ab`
landed `preview_final_bill`. It was found by the build process's step 0 — *check
the packet is current* — an hour after the fact, not by any check.

Two things changed because of it. The ORDER group was **re-pointed at the
product's own door**: it calls `preview_final_bill` and asserts what the product
prices, rather than a figure the suite states for itself. And the columns were
renamed from `TODAY`/`ONCE WIRED` to `NO BILL`/`WITH BILL`, because the first
pair had become a claim about the calendar and the second is a claim about the
call.

### FIVE JUDGMENTS, written down because the rules did not reach them

**1 · THE SUITE ASKS THE PRODUCT FOR THE BILL RATHER THAN STATING ONE.** The
ORDER group drives `preview_final_bill`; every other row states a figure only so
that ONE term of the subtraction varies and the arithmetic stays checkable by
hand. No figure is invented to make a landing come out, and the deposit interest
is ❄️ WE-7's `$3.50` **quoted**, never recomputed from the engine under test — a
golden figure a test derives from the code it is checking can never disagree
with it.

**2 · A ROW DECLARED FOR ONE PASS IS BLOCKED IN THE OTHER, NOT FAILED.** A
landing cannot be asserted with no bill stated. Scoring that as a failure would
put a real defect and a known keystone in the same bucket, which is the thing
two columns exist to keep apart.

**3 · p115's SIX CONSEQUENCES ARE CHECKED AS *NEVER DEFAULTED*, NOT AS
*EMPTY*.** The drawing says all six arrive empty; four now answer. Asserting
*empty* would make the suite go RED when the product got BETTER — a check
pointed at the wrong thing. What holds either way is the rule underneath the
sentence: each of the six is a real measurement or an explicit absence, and a
`0`, a `false` or a blank standing in for a fact nobody took is the failure.
**Measured: four SERVED** — premises occupancy afterwards, the owner on record,
the vacant-charge position, the master-account effect — **two stated ABSENT**,
none defaulted on any row.

**4 · THE THROWAWAY UTILITY IS A DATABASE, NOT A TENANT.** A move-out closes an
account, ends its agreements, writes readings and writes a permanent record;
readings are append-only and thirteen triggers refuse a DELETE. So the run is on
`config.settings.pgtest` and the beta is opened only to be COUNTED, before and
after: **78 accounts · 2 move records · 74 payments · 751 journal lines · 92
invoices · 1 parked draft**, identical both times.

**5 · ONE SEAM IS STOOD UP AND IT IS DECLARED.** `E2` drives
`last_issued_invoice_period_end` directly rather than issuing a real invoice,
because issuing one needs a template pin, a number series, a cycle with due
terms and a GL map — which would put the bill-issue pipeline under test in a
suite about move-outs. The deviation is printed on the row, and the patch is
restored in a `finally` so a leak cannot make every LATER scenario refuse a
move-out.

### WHAT IT FOUND — five real gaps, filed

| | What a clerk would see |
|---|---|
| **`DEF-CUS-5930`** · E1 | A master account with two open sub-accounts **moves out**. `settlement_for` SERVES `open_sub_accounts` for BR-CUS-171 (*"a parent with open children cannot be moved out"*) and `services.move_out` never reads it: the account closes, its agreements end, and a numbered move record is written for a move the signed rule forbids |
| **`DEF-CUS-5931`** · O1 | Step 3 prices the last month from reads step 6 has not written. p111 says it in its own words — *"the reads are committed with the close, not before it"* — so `MeterMultiplierUnstated` refuses, because BR-MET-056 stores the factor USED and an absent factor is NOT 1 |
| **`DEF-CUS-5932`** · O2 | The sentence that explains that order is unreachable: `prepare_final_bill` gathers before reading `behavior_class`, so a clerk who closed first is told about tariff versions instead of about the close |
| **`DEF-CUS-5933`** · R2 | An estimated final read is COMMITTED and the record files it under nought. `posted_reads` counts `len(posted)` while `accounts.final_read_state` reads `estimated`. One move-out, two answers about one row |
| **`DEF-CUS-5922`** · P1 | A parked move-out cannot be opened from its own record. **Filed by a sibling the same evening and CITED rather than re-filed** — two ids for one fault is how a register stops being countable. What this run adds: `_in_flight` reads `moved_in_on`/`effective_on` and never `moved_out_on`, so the date does not show; and `move_outs_list`'s window is CLOSED ACCOUNTS, so an unfinished move-out is in no list at all |

**Deliberately NOT filed as new rows.** `SH4`'s missing supervisor gate is
`DEF-CUS-5908`'s shape on the way out and cites it. The dispute-blocked group —
`L2`, `L4`, `L5`, `D3` — is a **stated absence and not a defect**: nothing stores
a disputed AMOUNT, so `_open_dispute_total` answers None, every credit-direction
close states no landing, and three of p112's five landings are unreachable.
`E3`'s missing `service_request_id` on the wizard payload is already known.

### ⚠ A CORRECTION TO THIS LANE'S OWN FIRST REPORT

It described `DEF-CUS-5927` as *"the mirror"* of this suite's `SH` group. It is
worse than a mirror: the **read** learns the figure and the **write** is never
given it, so step 4 renders three live radios over a `409
customers.move_out.no_shortfall` and prints *"there is no shortfall to decide"*
directly beneath its own `SHORT BY $1,591.85`. `e00b5dca6` settled which half is
at fault — `shortfall_decision` already reads `final_bill` off the payload and
`api._settlement_payload` already parses it, so **no backend change is needed**
and what reaches the endpoint is `{path}` alone. **SH1–SH3 are green here only
because this suite passes the figure**, and the journey now says so above those
rows, because a reader of three green rows would otherwise conclude a clerk can
do it.

### PROVING IT CAN FAIL

`MOVE_OUT_BREAK=<id>:<dimension>` damages what the runner **observed** for one
dimension before the checkers see it — not what the row declared — so what it
proves is that the checker really reads PostgreSQL's answer and compares it,
which inverting a verdict would not. Proved on **two different checkers**:
`C1:unit_after` through `_subset`, and `R1:move_record` through its own logic.
Each went red on exactly its own row and dimension — 2 failed, 2 passed, the
neighbour untouched — and the same four rows are 8 passed restored.

### ⚠ AND THE FILING ITSELF HIT LAW 11's OWN COLLISION, WHICH IS WORTH THE LINE

The five rows were allocated against the tip, written, and the tip then moved
before the push. The re-derivation law 11 requires — **content AND ids, in the
same breath, unconditionally** — found that a sibling had taken **`DEF-CUS-5929`
minutes earlier**: both lanes computed the next free number correctly, and
neither could see the other's unpushed row. The four rows were renumbered to
`5930`–`5933` by re-running the allocator against the new tip rather than by
hand, and the citations in the suite, the journey and this entry were moved in
ONE simultaneous substitution — a sequential `5929→5930` then `5930→5931` would
have cascaded every id onto the next one's number.

**Nothing downstream would have caught it.** A duplicate id in a 3,400-row
register reads as a register. What caught it is that the check is
unconditional: the register had moved, so it was re-derived, and the id check
rides the same command. The `--reuse-db`-shaped lesson applies — a step that
only runs when something looks wrong is a step that does not run.

### WHEN IT RUNS AGAIN

**Whenever the move-out wizard, the final-bill preview, the settlement engine,
the deposit-interest accrual or the move record changes.** The difference
between two runs is the report.

## 2026-09-19 · THE MOVE-OUT SHORTFALL DECISION CAN BE RECORDED — THE SCREEN NOW
## STATES THE FIGURE ON THE WRITE, AND `DEF-CUS-5927`'s OWN CAUSE WAS WRONG

**`DEF-CUS-5927` (critical) · `DEF-CUS-5928` (medium) · shipped `v2.313.2` ·
MAINTENANCE, not build — step 4 is a live screen on a live money path.**

### WHAT A CLERK COULD NOT DO

Step 4 of the move-out wizard is where a clerk says what happens to money the
customer still owes after the deposit is applied: collect it, put it on a
payment plan, write it off, or move it to the landlord. **Pressing that button
failed on every account in the product.** The screen drew `Short by $1,591.85`,
drew three live radios and an enabled `Record this decision`, and then answered
***"Nothing is left unrecovered here, so there is no shortfall to decide"*** —
printed directly beneath its own figure.

### THE REPRODUCTION, BEFORE ANY CODE WAS READ

Account `AC-2026-00031`, move-out 2026-09-30, on the live stack:

    GET  /accounts/{id}/final-bill-preview?moved_out_on=2026-09-30
         -> priced True, total 789.42
    GET  /accounts/{id}/close-impact?final_bill=789.42&as_of=2026-09-30
         -> landing "short", gaps [], shortfall {stored 1591.8500, display 1591.85}
    GET  /accounts/{id}/close-impact                       (no figure)
         -> landing null, gaps ["final_bill_not_stated"]
    POST /accounts/{id}/settle-shortfall {"path":"collect"}
         -> 409 BIZ-STATE customers.move_out.no_shortfall
            params {landing: null, gaps: ["final_bill_not_stated"]}

### ⚠ THE FILED CAUSE WAS WRONG, AND BELIEVING IT WOULD HAVE COST A BACKEND WAVE

`DEF-CUS-5927`'s row says *"POST /settle-shortfall takes no final-bill figure
while GET /close-impact does"*. **It takes it.** `move_out_settlement.
shortfall_decision` reads `final_bill` off the payload and hands it to
`settlement_for`, and `api._settlement_payload` parses **both** `final_bill`
and `as_of` out of the POST body. The browser evidence on that row is exact and
its diagnosis is not — which is `DEF-CUS-5929`, filed by the preview lane
against the wrong diagnosis rather than by editing another lane's row, and
**still OPEN**: the row's prose is unchanged, because the tool that owns the
register (`close_defect.py`) edits a status and nothing else, and hand-editing a
3,400-row CSV is what law 11 forbids. Its closed status and this entry are what
stop it misleading the next lane. `tests/test_br_bil_013_final_bill_preview.py::
tc16` proves both halves against one account and is the greppable proof.

**So the whole fix is one change in the front end, and no backend file moved.**

### WHAT WAS CHANGED, AND THE ONE JUDGMENT IN IT

The judgment was **where the two terms come from**, and it is the difference
between a fix and a second version of the same bug. The obvious repair is to
build a body in `settleShortfall` — read the preview, take its total, send it.
That is a **second computation of one customer's closing money**, three hundred
lines away from the first, and the entire defect is two halves disagreeing
about one figure. So instead:

    const statedTerms: CloseImpactTerms = {
      finalBill: preview?.total ?? null,
      asOf: movedOutOn === "" ? null : movedOutOn,
    };

is declared **once**, in `MoveOutWizard`, and the same object is handed to
`closeImpactPort.read` (the query key is built from it too) and down to
`ShortfallStep`, which hands it to `settleShortfall`. **One object, both call
sites.** There is no expression anywhere that could produce a different figure
for the write than for the read, because there is only one expression.
`CloseImpactTerms` is the read's own type, reused rather than re-declared for
the same reason.

An unstated term is **absent from the body, never empty**: `""` would be a
stated figure of nothing, and the service's `_stated_final_bill` refuses a
non-decimal by name.

### THE CONTRADICTORY SENTENCE — VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED

*"Nothing is left unrecovered here, so there is no shortfall to decide"* is the
catalogue text for `customers.move_out.no_shortfall`, rendered by
`ShortfallPathChoices`' `refusal` slot **only while the mutation is in error**.
It was never keyed off the landing, so nothing about it was changed. It is gone
because the POST no longer fails — **checked in a browser rather than reasoned
about**: the same walk was run against a build of the pre-fix code and a build
of the fixed code, and the sentence is present in the first and absent in the
second.

### `DEF-CUS-5928`, THE SAME SCREEN, ONE LINE UP

The heading read **`What happens to 1591.85`** — no symbol, no separator —
above a cell reading **`$1,591.85`**. It interpolated the served `display`
string raw while every cell beneath it went through `MoneyCell`. A heading is a
string and cannot hold a `<span>`, so the **formatter** underneath that
component is used instead: `formatMoney(shortfall.stored, money.currency)` —
same function, same default locale, same 4dp→2dp `halfExpand` — and the two can
no longer disagree. It now reads `What happens to $1,591.85`. Hard rule 2:
money displays to two decimals, with the currency that rides with it.

### HOW IT WAS PROVED, AND WHAT THE PROOF CANNOT COVER

Two guards were added to `MoveOutWizard.test.tsx` and **each was shown RED on
the exact defect first**, in `vitest`, the harness that runs them (law 7, and
its *prove it in the harness that will run it* half): the write's body coming
back `{path: "collect"}` against the expected three keys, and the heading
missing its currency. 57 passed / 4 todo, up from 55. `tsc --noEmit` and
`eslint --max-warnings 0` both clean.

⚠ **WHAT THOSE GUARDS CANNOT SEE, STATED RATHER THAN ROUNDED UP.** They assert
the body `settleShortfall` builds **from terms it is handed**. Nothing in this
repository checks that the wizard hands it the same terms the read used — the
suite renders the screen statically and cannot click it. **A unit test could
not have found this defect and cannot protect against its return**: both halves
were individually correct the whole time. The browser walk is the evidence, and
it is the only evidence. `10-scripts/def_cus_5927_shortfall_write_walkthrough.mjs`
is that walk, kept, and it takes a `WALK_EXPECT_OK=0` mode that asserts the OLD
behaviour so the before-and-after is reproducible rather than remembered.

### READ BACK OUT OF POSTGRESQL, NOT OFF THE SCREEN

`audit_log` row `01a0bb37-ef1e-7728-80b3-2d91d7203a52`, written by the click:
action `account.move_out.shortfall_decided`, entity `account 01a0aff9-6140-
7e09-be9e-a3d983503041`, `after.path = "collect"`, `after.amount = {"stored":
"1591.8500", "display": "1591.85"}`, `before` null. Hard rule 7 satisfied;
hard rule 4 satisfied, because it is a new row and not an edit. **No money
moved and none could** — there is no `final_settlements` table, `persisted` is
`false` on the wire, and customers writes no invoice, payment or journal line.
The beta's counts are unchanged across the whole session: **78 accounts, 2 move
records, 74 payments, 751 journal lines, 92 invoices, 1 parked draft.**

### THE SCENARIO SUITE'S OWN FRICTION LIST WAS AMENDED IN THE SAME COMMIT

`test_move_out_scenarios.py` printed *"the SERVICE takes a final bill … and the
SCREEN does not send one"* against all four shortfall rows. That sentence went

### ROLLBACK

## 2026-09-20 · THE FINAL BILL IS PRICED FROM WHAT THE CLERK KEYED; THE READS COMMIT WITH THE CLOSE

**PO ruling: option B — *"price from what's keyed, commit at the close"*, verbatim
*"option b is correct"*.** It answers `DEF-CUS-5931`, whose prevention field asked
for a **ruling and not a fix**, because both orders were written down as law and
they contradicted.

### The question as it was put
Step 3 prices the final bill from the closing meter reading. Step 6 is where
readings are committed. **So at the moment step 3 prices, the closing reading
does not exist yet.** Two orders were available and each was already written:

| | What happens to the meter |
|---|---|
| **A** · commit the reads at step 2 | pricing works at once, and **an abandoned move-out leaves a committed final reading on a live meter** |
| **B** · price from what is keyed, commit at the close | **nothing is written** until the clerk commits the whole move-out |

**The worked case shown to the PO:** Sam keys a closing electric read of
**52,410** at step 2 on the 28th, reaches step 4, is called away and never
finishes. Under A that reading is now committed, the next bill run uses it, and
the move-out never happened. Under B the move is parked and the meter is
untouched.

### ⚠ THE RULING AGREES WITH THE DRAWING, WHICH IS WHY IT IS THE CHEAPER ANSWER
Blueprint p111 already states it: ***"The reads are committed with the close, not
before it. The whole move-out is one transaction, so a refused reading rolls the
close back with it and everything stays on screen."*** Option A would have broken
that guarantee — and with it the property the wizard already has, that a clerk
may walk away from a move-out at any step without consequence. `Save & exit` is
on every step of this flow by the PO's own ruling of the same week, so
abandonment is not an edge case, it is a designed path.

### What this requires
Step 3 prices from the reads **keyed on step 2 and not yet committed**, and
**says so on its face** — a figure priced from an uncommitted reading is not the
same claim as one priced from a committed one, and B14 rule 33 caps how that is
said, not whether. The commit order at step 6 does not move: reads commit with
the close, inside the one transaction.

### What this ruling does NOT decide
* **The words step 3 uses to say so.** That is the builder's, against the drawing
  and rule 33's six-word cap on a fact — not a question for the PO.
* **Whether the final bill must be RE-priced at the close** if a read changed
  between step 3 and step 6. The suite's `O1` row is the evidence either way and
  this is the next question underneath, not settled here.
* **`DEF-CUS-5932`**, the unreachable sentence about this very order
  (`prepare_final_bill` gathers before reading `behavior_class`, so a clerk is
  told about tariff versions instead of about the close). Still open, still a
  fix rather than a ruling.

## 2026-09-20 · TEN MOVE-OUT RULINGS IN ONE SITTING

**PO ruling, verbatim: `1. b; 2 c. 3a. 4a 5a 6 a 7b 8a 9a 10 a`** — answering ten
questions put as a table of question, worked example, options and a
recommendation. **All ten took the recommendation**, which is worth recording
precisely because it means the reasoning is now load-bearing: nobody re-derived
it, so it has to be findable here.

### The three that change what a customer pays

**1 · A MOVE-OUT'S FINAL BILL PRORATES. Option B.** A closing customer served
**12 days** is billed the whole month's base charge — **$18.50 where proration
gives $7.40, so $11.10 too much**, and they are leaving.

⚠ **THIS NARROWS `OQ-242`'s WITHDRAWAL RATHER THAN REVERSING IT.** On 2026-08-23
the PO was shown the over-charge and answered *"its proration denominator (the
current guess OVER-CHARGES while it stands). - this is not required"*. That
withdrawal was about **cycle-less one-time bills**, which have no cycle to read a
denominator from. **A move-out closes a CYCLED account, which has one.** So the
scope moves and the earlier ruling stands where it was aimed.

⚠ **THE BUILDER MUST ESTABLISH WHETHER THIS IS IMPLEMENTATION OR A RE-SIGN,
BEFORE WRITING ARITHMETIC.** `one_time._cycle_days` returns `None` always and
`TC12` pins that ruled figure. B4.3 is ❄️ FROZEN and the refusal names it —
*"every proration in B4.3 divides by this window"*. **If B4.3 already gives the
denominator for a cycled account's final bill, this is implementing signed law
and needs no re-sign** — exactly as the deposit-interest ruling turned out to be
on 2026-09-19, where an escalation was avoided by reading the rule instead of
assuming. **If B4.3 does not, it is a finance re-sign via HUMAN-GUIDE §6 and
stops there.** Do not guess which.

**2 · RE-PRICE ONLY IF A READ CHANGED. Option C.** Step 3 prices; a clerk may
correct a reading before step 6 commits. Always re-pricing is right and costs a
pass nobody needs; never re-pricing ships a figure the reads no longer support.
**Re-price when, and only when, a read moved between the two.** This is the
question left deliberately open by the same morning's ruling that the bill is
priced from what the clerk keyed.

**3 · THE MOVE-OUT REASON GETS A COLUMN. Option A.** Five options are drawn on
step 1 and **none is stored** — `accounts.close_reason` is PROPOSED-SCHEMA and
`reason` is a REFUSED field (`BR-CUS-030`). The blueprint's own dashed panel says
it: *"the wizard asks and forgets - which is worse than not asking."* A utility
that cannot say why forty accounts closed last quarter cannot answer its own
board.

### The five screen answers — and three of them are DO NOTHING

| # | Ruling | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **4** | **A** — drop the panel **on Move-outs only** | An unfinished move-out shows twice on one screen. The panel's own stated reason — a draft *"shares not one field"* with the rows — is TRUE of a move-in and FALSE of a move-out, which starts from an account already picked. It stays on the other four flows, so the PO's ruling of 2026-08-26 is untouched where its reasoning holds. `OQ-CUS-12488` closes. |
| **5** | **A** — leave the `OPEN` tile | It reads 1 over a list of 2, captioned *"closed, not yet finally billed"*. **Changing the count would make the tile contradict its own caption.** NO CHANGE. |
| **6** | **A** — step 3 is titled **`Final bill & deposit`** | The product says *"Settle the money"*. The drawn title names what the step CONTAINS; a clerk hunting for the bill should read the word "bill". |
| **7** | **B** — keep the progress bar | The drawing has `2 of 6` as plain text. The bar is drawn by a component shared with the Move-ins tab, so removing it changes a screen nobody asked about. NO CHANGE. |
| **8** | **A** — the wizard stays an overlay | The drawing gives each step a full page. Steps 1, 2 and 6 are signed off in overlay form, and this would change all six at once on no clerk-visible benefit. NO CHANGE — revisit when the money work is closed. |

### The two process answers

**9 · A PARKED MOVE-OUT IS ALLOCATED A REFERENCE, as a move-in already is.
Option A.** `_allocate_draft_reference` returns `None` for every flow but
`move_in`, deliberately — and that decision predates the move-out having a
screen. ⚠ **IT IS NOT COSMETIC: `/moves/{ref}` is keyed on a reference and
`_park_by_reference` filters `reference__iexact`, which NULL never matches, so a
parked move-out cannot be opened from its own record AT ALL** and the `Resume`
door built on 2026-09-19 is unreachable for it (`DEF-CUS-5922`). A clerk also
gains a number to quote on the phone. `OQ-CUS-12489` closes.

**10 · STEP 3 LINKS OUT TO THE REAL INVOICE. Option A.** The wizard PRICES and
does not post — p112, *"NO BILL IS ISSUED BY THIS SCREEN."* ⚠ **And the order is
a trap: `final_bill.py` refuses an account whose behaviour class is no longer
billable, so the invoice must be raised BEFORE the close or it cannot be raised
at all.** Option B — step 3 raising it — was declined because it would put bill
creation in two places, and hard rule 4 means a wrong one cannot be taken back.

### What none of these ten decides
* the WORDS of any new control or link (B14 rule 33's caps, the builder's);
* whether the reason list is the five drawn or tenant-editable;
* what happens to move-outs already closed with no reason recorded — **no
  migration may write one, hard rule 4**; report the count and leave them.

   *"Not available yet."* until the backend lane serves them — the ROW is
   untouched, only the reason it gives for being empty.
3. **`OQ-680` is no longer stated on screen.** The payment-plan paragraph was
   the only place the product said it had not checked for a running plan, an
   open dispute or an unbilled cycle. The question is unchanged and still OPEN;
   B14 rule 32 puts a stated absence closed by default and rule 33 puts
   rationale at zero words on screen, so it belongs in the register and not in
   front of a clerk. **A lane closing `OQ-680` must therefore look for its
   refusal at the door rather than for this paragraph.**

### STEP 5: THE SEND TABLE IS NOT BUILT, AND HERE ARE THE FOUR COUNTS THAT DECIDED IT

The PO asked for communication options. **The blueprint draws them** (p130,
`What goes out to the buyer and the seller` — a SEND tick, a recipient, a
channel, a template and a when) **and it also states, in its own words, the
reason they cannot be honest yet**: *"Everything here is queued, and nothing is
sent. This product writes a row per message and no sender picks it up — no
email, no text, no print file."*

Measured on `brazosbend`, 2026-09-20, because the screen's own sentence —
*"Nothing is sent by this screen. No channel exists yet"* — was **half false**:

* `outbound_messages`: **420 rows, every one `queued`, `sent_at` null on all
  420**, across five channels (pdf_print 168, portal 91, email 85, sms 74,
  in_app 2). The channels exist; the delivery has never once run.
* `notification_templates`: **41 rows on this tenant and not one** matches
  ownership, transfer or changeover. The two the drawing names —
  `Change of ownership — buyer v2` and `— seller v2` — **do not exist**.
* `apps/notifications/api.py` mounts `requeue`, `resend` and `unsent`.
  **Nothing CREATES an outbound message**, so no screen can queue one.
* `TransferCommitPlan` carries three keys and `transfer_commit` reads exactly
  those three.

**So a tick in that table would be dead four ways at once** — naming a template
that is not there, putting a key on the wire the door does not read, queueing
through a route nobody mounted, and promising a delivery this product has never
made. That is hard-won law 2's mirror, and this surface has already produced
that defect once (`DEF-CWP-3925`). **The panel now states the fact and what the
clerk does about it** — *"Nobody is told about this sale."* and *"Tell the buyer
and seller yourself."* — and the build is filed as **`DEF-CUS-5949`**: a
template, an event on the commit, and a door, in that order.

### THE ELEVEN CATALOGUES WERE LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE — `DEF-CUS-5973`

**Measured after the change: 7 new call sites are in no catalogue and 9 catalogue
keys have no call site left.** The seven render correctly in English through their
`defaultValue` and fall back to English in the other ten languages. `G15` still
reports **0 missing, 0 extra** — parity is catalogue-to-catalogue and this is the
code-to-catalogue direction `G18` owns, which is the asymmetry `DEF-036` says must
be kept.

**Why they were not edited here, stated rather than glossed:** two lanes were
writing those files at the time, a 16-key edit across eleven of them is 176 line
splices into hot shared files, and **B14 rule 35** says a catalogue is written in
its own language rather than translated from English — which this lane cannot do
for ten languages. So the debt is FILED with its exact key list rather than left
as a note in a docstring, which is hard rule 4's last paragraph applied to the
lane's own shortfall.

### TWO LIVE BREAKS FOUND BY WALKING, NEITHER OF THEM THE ONE THAT WAS REPORTED

* **`DEF-CUS-5948` — every way OUT of the transfer wizard landed on an error.**
  `TRANSFERS_TAB_PATH` was `/accounts/transfers`, and the accounts router
  carries `accounts/:accountId`, so that address is read as *the account whose
  id is the word "transfers"*. The `← Transfers` head link, `Save & exit` on all
  five steps and `TransferDone`'s *Back to transfers* all rendered **"Accounts ·
  Failed · This account could not be opened."** ⚠ **The finding already existed
  and had never been filed**: `moveShared.tsx`'s own docstring names both
  constants and says they *"are written the path way and hit exactly that; they
  are another lane's file and are REPORTED, not edited here."* No register row
  was ever written, so nothing counted it — CLAUDE.md hard rule 4's last
  paragraph, in a second family. `PARKED_HOME_PATHS` has always held the query
  form, which is why PARKING out of the wizard worked and LEAVING it did not.
  Both constants now carry `?tab=`.

* **`DEF-CUS-5934` — THE REPORTED BREAK DID NOT REPRODUCE, and that is recorded
  as a finding rather than as a closure.** The row stays OPEN. Walked in
  Chromium against the live stack on `brazosbend` at build 2.313.2, whose
  `TransferWizard.tsx` and `FormModal.tsx` are **byte-identical to v2.310.3**
  (the build the PO reported on — verified by `git log`, the file has not moved
  since 2026-09-13). Pressing `I have shown this to the buyer` records the tick
  and leaves the step standing in **every** state the component has: at 1440,
  1280, 1024 and 390px; with the account loaded, with a null balance, a null
  deposit, a null currency and with no account at all; before and after the sale
  date is set; arriving forward, by the rail, by `Back` from step 5 and by a
  reload; with the park panel open; ticked, unticked and ticked again; and after
  96 seconds of idling with six window blur/focus cycles. Also pressed in jsdom
  through the repo's own harness. **Zero page errors, zero error boundaries in
  all of it.** Every other enabled control on step 4 was pressed too, one fresh
  session each — and two of them, `Save & exit` and `← Transfers`, were broken:
  that is `DEF-CUS-5948` above, it is on step 4, and it is the only thing on
  that step that does break the screen. Whether it is what the PO hit is **not
  claimed** — the defect row's *"the 'I have shown this to the buyer' checkbox"*
  is the filer's inference from reading the code, not something the PO said, and
  the only fact in their words is *"step 4 when last tick is press - uI breaks"*.
  **What the PO should be asked for is the tenant and what the screen looked
  like**, because `ann-arbor-seu` is not a tenant this tree holds and the data
  is the one axis that could not be varied.

### ⚠ WHY THE COPY IS WRONG AND NOT MERELY LONG
The Transfers TAB, ruled in the same sitting, carries **six statements that are
false** under `BR-CUS-1030` — two KPI tiles counting an election nobody makes, and
an empty state describing a transfer as *"the same customer to a new address"*,
which is the exact case the wizard's own red warning says **is not a transfer**.
The commit that made a transfer a reassignment rewrote the backend by **916
lines** and touched `TransfersTab.tsx` by **38** — all one sentence and a link.
**A clerk learning the flow from that tab learns it backwards.**
