## 2026-09-20 · THE TRANSFER'S BUYER CARRIES A MAILING ADDRESS

**PO ruling, verbatim: *"please add it at buyer"***, on the finding that the
transfer's buyer step has no mailing address — so **a landlord's bill has nowhere
to go but the property they have just bought.**

### Why this is lawful and needs no new column
⚠ **Hard rule 8 says an address lives on `premises` and NOWHERE else.** This is
not an exception being carved: `customers.addresses` with `kind='mailing'` is one
of the **three named exceptions already in the rule**, and it is described there
as exactly this case — *"where the BILL goes, which for a landlord is another
building."*

**So the buyer's mailing address uses that existing home.** No address column is
added to any entity, and the service address continues to be derived by walking
to the premises.

⚠ **AND `kind='service'` IS RETIRED AND REFUSED BY NAME** — `G85` fails a fourth
home. A lane reaching for a second kind here would be refused by a gate, which is
the outcome the rule intends.

### What it is part of
This rides the same change as the PO's earlier ruling that the buyer must carry
what an account needs — *"step 2 dont allow to take kYC documents - DOB, all
detaisl we need to create account - Similar to Move in request we will need all
details for account"*, and then *"we have it - we have created it for service
request move in - use it"*. **The reuse instruction governs here too:** the
service request's own mailing-address handling is the thing to reuse, not a
second implementation beside it.

### Why it matters beyond tidiness
A transfer hands a **live ledger** to a new owner. If the bill can only go to the
property, then every landlord, every company buying a rental, and every
out-of-area purchaser is billed at an address they do not read — and the first
anyone learns of it is a dunning ladder running against somebody who never saw a
bill.

## 2026-09-20 · A CUSTOMER ID IS NEVER OVERWRITTEN — THE SELLER'S LINK IS ENDED, NOT DELETED

**PO ruling, verbatim: *"we cannot override customer id - seller and buyer cstmer
id are unique those does not change"***, answering the finding that after a sale
the seller survives only in `audit_log`, which is pruned.

### What the product does today, measured
1. `transfers.py:1451` — `models.CustomerAccount.objects.filter(…).exclude(customer_id=buyer_id)` and **the seller's link row is REMOVED.**
2. `accounts.customer_id` is overwritten with the buyer's.
3. **So the only surviving trace of who sold the property is an `audit_log` row**, and `audit_log` is pruned on a retention schedule.

**The consequence, plainly: this product forgets who sold a property.** The
drawn transfer record's own title is `Tan, Wei → Ferraro, L.` and its
*What happened* panel has a **`Sold by`** row — neither can be rendered from a
log that ages out.

### ⚠ THE RULING IS ABOUT IDENTITY, AND IT IS RIGHT ON ITS OWN TERMS
A customer id is a **permanent identity**, not a slot on an account. `C-00344`
is the seller for ever and `C-00877` is the buyer for ever; the ACCOUNT moves
between them. Overwriting the field treats an identity as a property of the
account, which is what produced the data loss.

### The shape that follows — PROPOSED by this lane, not ruled
**`customer_accounts` is already an N:M link and its own docstring says so:**
*"the uniqueness is on the PAIR, not on the account, so nothing here forbids a
jointly-held account."* It therefore already permits both customers to be linked
to one account — **what it lacks is a PERIOD.** It carries `created_at` and
nothing that says a link ENDED.

So the proposal is: **a sale ENDS the seller's link and OPENS the buyer's, and
neither row is deleted.** Ownership history becomes a query rather than a log
scrape, `Sold by` is durable, and hard rule 4's principle — *corrections are new
rows* — is honoured rather than worked around.

⚠ **This needs its own decision before it is built**, because it changes a link
table three modules read and it interacts with `BR-CUS-054`, `BR-CUS-089`'s
stored match tier and the discounts path that reads it. **A lane must not simply
add a column and move on.**

### What this ruling does NOT decide
* whether the period is a nullable `ended_on` on the link or a separate history row;
* what happens to the **existing** links already destroyed by past sales —
  ⚠ **no migration may invent a seller for a historical transfer**, hard rule 4;
  report the count and leave them;
* whether `accounts.customer_id` remains as a denormalised pointer to the
  CURRENT customer, or is derived from the open link. **That is the larger of the
  two questions** and it reaches every reader of that column.

## 2026-09-20 · TWO OF THE TEN MOVE-OUT RULINGS, BUILT — ITEMS 9 AND 3 (`v2.314.0`)

Building the PO ruling of 2026-09-20 recorded above (*"TEN MOVE-OUT RULINGS IN
ONE SITTING"*), **item 9** (a parked move-out is allocated a reference, option
A) and **item 3** (the move-out reason gets a column, option A). MAINTENANCE,
not Build: both surfaces are live and a clerk can do both tasks in the product
today — `12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`.

### Item 9 · the number, and the question the ruling told us to establish first

**THE RULING SAID *"Do not mint a second numbering scheme if one exists."* One
exists, and nothing new was minted.** `core.numbering.MOVE_OUT` has carried
`MVO-{YY}-{0000}` since `CR-039` wave D, seeded on every tenant; on the beta it
stands at `next_number = 2` because the one completed move-out took
`MVO-26-0001`. **A parked move-out now draws from that same series**, so the
next draft is `MVO-26-0002` — the number a clerk quotes on the phone.

**WHAT HAPPENS TO IT WHEN THE PARK COMPLETES: the record ADOPTS it, and the
counter is spent once per job.** `services.move_out` takes `wizard_park_id`,
`_adopt_wizard_draft` reads the draft's reference and deletes the draft, and
`moves.record_move(reserved_move_no=…)` files the finished move-out under that
string — all inside the close's own transaction, so a refused reading rolls both
back and the clerk still has their draft with the same number. **This is
`move_in`'s mechanism unchanged**; the only thing that moved is that
`_adopt_move_in_draft` became `_adopt_wizard_draft(…, flow=…)`, because a
move-out must not be able to consume a move-in's number.

⚠ **THE REASON THE OLD BEHAVIOUR WAS RIGHT IS THE REASON IT STOPPED BEING
RIGHT.** `_allocate_draft_reference`'s docstring said *"minting numbers for four
other flows THAT NOTHING DISPLAYS would be a series burning through its counter
with no screen to show for it"* — exact on 2026-09-19, and the condition it
rests on was removed the same week when the Move-outs tab began listing
unfinished move-outs. **`transfer`, `disconnect` and `new_connect` still take
no number**, because that original reasoning still holds for them: their drafts
appear only in the parked-drafts panel, which draws no reference column.

**IT WAS NOT COSMETIC, AND `DEF-CUS-5922` CLOSES.** `/moves/{ref}` is keyed on
the reference and `_park_by_reference` filters `reference__iexact`, which **NULL
never matches** — so a parked move-out could not be opened from its own record
AT ALL, and the `Resume` door built on 2026-09-19 was unreachable for it. A
live screen behind a dead door: hard-won law 2's mirror.

**TWO MORE FAULTS FELL OUT OF THE SAME CAUSE AND ARE FIXED WITH IT, because
fixing only the allocator would have left the ruling half-built:**
* `move_record_reads._in_flight` read `moved_in_on` / `effective_on` and never
  `moved_out_on`. The day a parked move-out became openable it would have opened
  saying *"not chosen yet"* about a date the clerk had typed themselves.
* `move_reads` hardcoded `move_no: None` plus the *"no number yet"* absence on
  every unfinished row. The draft would have been numbered, the record page
  would have opened on it, and **the list — the one screen a clerk reads a
  number off — would still have said it had none.**

⚠ **AND ONE OF `P1`'s THREE RED ASSERTIONS WAS NEVER A PRODUCT GAP AT ALL
(`DEF-CUS-5938`).** `draft_in_move_outs_list` was red because the scenario's
park call sent only `values` and no `subject_ref`, while `move_reads` resolves
an unfinished row's account from `subject_ref` exactly as `MoveOutWizard` writes
it. The row was in the list all along under a null account. The suite was
reporting a gap that had been closed the day before — **a fixture that does not
build what the screen builds is a check that does not check**, and the scenario
row's prose is left as written with the correction beside it rather than
silently amended.

### Item 3 · the column, and the two things the ruling left to us

**BUILT:** `accounts.close_reason`, one nullable TEXT column (migration
`customers/0058`, 🔒 HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING) with `ck_accounts_close_reason`
permitting NULL or one of five codes. `reason` is an accepted field on
`POST /accounts/{id}/move-out` **and on no other door**; it is served on the
account, on the move-out response and on the move record's *What happened* list,
because a value a clerk types that no screen returns is the shape that produced
three defects on this surface in one day.

**JUDGMENT 1 — THE LIST IS THE FIVE DRAWN, AS FIXED CODES, NOT A TENANT
LOOKUP.** The ruling named this as undecided. Three reasons, recorded here so
nobody re-derives them: a fixed list can be counted ACROSS the product and a
per-tenant one only within one utility, which is half of what `OQ-830` asks for;
`disconnects.CUT_REASONS` is the established shape for the same question one
table over, and a second differently-shaped answer on the same screen family is
how one product grows two vocabularies; and a tenant-editable list is a Settings
screen, a lookup table, a seed and a migration — more than the ruling asked for,
and it would decide `OQ-830` by building its answer first. **Widening stays
cheap and is `OQ-CUS-12512`:** these are CODES, never display strings, so a
lookup table can adopt them as seeded rows without moving one stored value.

**JUDGMENT 2 — NULL MEANS *NOBODY WAS ASKED* AND IS NEVER FOLDED INTO
`other`.** Two different facts about a utility's own record, and a report that
merged them would over-count `other` by every close made before today. The move
record therefore serves **two** absences: `close_reason_was_not_asked` for a
close dated before the column shipped, `close_reason_not_given` for one made
since and skipped. The date constant that tells them apart is an approximation
and says so in its own docstring — a backdated `moved_out_on` sits on the wrong
side of it.

**JUDGMENT 3 — AN UNKNOWN CODE IS REFUSED BY NAME, NEVER COERCED.** Silently
mapping a typo onto `other` is how a count becomes a lie: the bucket would grow
by every client bug and nobody reading the report could tell.

**JUDGMENT 4 — REQUIRED ON THE SCREEN, OPTIONAL AT THE DOOR.** The wizard marks
the select required and blocks `Continue` without it, which is what *"stop
asking and forgetting"* means for a clerk. `services.move_out` still accepts a
move-out with no reason, because an import, a script or the scenario suite has
no clerk in front of it — and turning a ruling about COLLECTING a fact into a
new refusal on a closing path would have been a larger change than the one
ruled.

### MOVE-OUTS ALREADY CLOSED WITH NO REASON — THE COUNT, AND THEY ARE LEFT

⚠ **NO MIGRATION WRITES ONE — hard rule 4, and the ruling said so.** Measured on
the beta after `customers/0058` applied: **78 accounts, of which 1 is closed,
and that 1 carries no reason.** One move-out record, one terminal-class account,
and `select count(*) from accounts where close_reason is not null` is **0**.
Inventing a reason for a historical close would be falsifying a record. The
account's record page says the product never asked, which is the truth.

### What this does NOT decide
* whether the five become tenant-extensible — `OQ-CUS-12512`, OPEN;
* whether a mistyped reason may be corrected after the close — `OQ-CUS-12513`,
  OPEN. Today it cannot be: `close_reason` is refused on every door but the
  move-out, so a clerk who picks *deceased* meaning *lease ended* has no way
  back. The nearest precedent runs the other way (`OQ-1322` widened the
  immutability trigger for three columns of `payments`), and the cost of any
  correction is the same one `OQ-1340` is still open about — the replaced value
  would live only in `audit_log`, which is pruned;
* anything about the move-out REASON in the scenario suite's thirteen
  dimensions. `U4` is marked closed there and the suite still asserts nothing
  about it, deliberately: adding a fourteenth dimension makes all twenty-seven
  rows incomplete for a fact its own file already covers.

## 2026-09-20 · THE TRANSFER'S BUYER CARRIES WHAT AN ACCOUNT NEEDS — `BR-CUS-1081`

**PO ruling, verbatim**, having walked the wizard in the live product:

> *"step 2 dont allow to take kYC documents - DOB, all detaisl we need to create
> account - Similar to Move in request we will need all details for account"*

and, when told a backend lane would be needed:

> *"we have it - we have created it for service request move in - use it"*

**The second sentence is a requirement about HOW and it is the harder half.**
The buyer's set is not eleven names typed into `transfers.py`; it is
`service_request_service.CAPTURE_FIELDS` filtered to what a buyer is about, and
`transfers._capture_vocabulary()` **raises** if any of them has left that set.
An intersection would have been the obvious spelling and is the wrong one — it
shrinks silently, and a capture set that quietly stops carrying a date of birth
is a match that quietly stops being strong.

### WHAT IS REQUIRED — THREE, AND THE RULING ADDED NONE

A NAME, a stated KIND, and ONE identifier belonging to that kind. Unchanged.

**Everything the ruling added is OPTIONAL, and that is a lane judgment with a
reason rather than a default.** The PO named the move-in request as the
benchmark, and on that form a date of birth, an email, a telephone number, a
preferred language, a co-applicant and a mailing address are every one of them
optional. **Making a SALE stricter than the application the PO pointed at would
refuse a buyer at the counter for a field the benchmark does not ask for.**
`BR-CUS-1023` is the signed minimum — *"Customer ID - minimum name and one ID -
minimum"* — and a minimum is not a maximum. It sits WITH `BR-CUS-1030`'s note in
`transfers.py` rather than against it: that note is about nobody being
identifiable behind a live ledger, and one identifier answers it.

**THE COST OF THE DATE OF BIRTH BEING OPTIONAL, SAID OUT LOUD:** `BR-CUS-089`
needs **name + date of birth + one government identifier** for a `strong` match,
and `discounts.carry_forward_offer` moves money only on `strong`. A returning
customer whose deposit is **$150.00** therefore carries **$0.00** of it and is
minted a SECOND customer number beside the one they already have — `DEF-2587`
measured that shape on a landlord and found three rows over one Social Security
number. **So it is optional and it is not silent:** the step-2 response reports a
candidate that could not be matched strongly AND names the missing fact, so a
clerk is told what one more question would buy. Requiring it would refuse a
genuine first-time buyer who has nothing on file to match against at all.

### WHERE EACH PIECE LANDS — AND `transfers` GAINS NO COLUMN

| what | table | the door, which already existed |
|---|---|---|
| name · kind · SSN · licence · **date of birth** | `customers` | `services.link_customer` |
| email · phone · date of birth | `contacts` | `services.update_account_contact` |
| preferred language | `accounts` | `services.update_account` |
| **mailing address** | `customers.addresses` `kind='mailing'` | `services.update_account_mailing_address` |
| KYC documents | `account_documents` `doc_type='kyc'` | `POST /accounts/{id}/documents` |
| a co-applicant | **nowhere** | `OQ-CUS-12514`, raised |

**The mailing address is CLAUDE.md hard rule 8's first named exception and no
address column is declared anywhere.** The conformance walk of the same day found
it missing in one sentence — *"there is no `Mailing address` for the buyer, so a
landlord's bill has nowhere else to go"* — and **the PO ruled it while this lane
was building: *"please add it at buyer"*** (`08e5de63c`, the same day). So this
is the BUILD of that ruling rather than a lane's own reading of a conformance
finding, and that entry's instruction governs it too: *"reuse the service
request's own mailing-address handling rather than writing a second one beside
it."* `G85` fails a fourth home and this path
gives it nothing to find.

⚠ **AND THE ACCOUNT'S CONTACT WAS THE SELLER'S, WITH NOTHING CHANGING IT.**
`TransferWizard.tsx` says so on its own review step — *"Autopay and the bill
email stay the seller's. Change them next."* — which is an accurate description
of a product that hands over a house and goes on emailing the bill to the person
who sold it. The buyer's email has been on the wire since the step was built and
the validator dropped it (`DEF-CUS-5941`).

### KYC DOCUMENTS RIDE THE ACCOUNT'S CABINET, NOT THE REQUEST'S

**`service_request_documents.request_id` is a non-null `PROTECT` foreign key to
`service_requests`.** A transfer has no request row, and minting an empty one to
hold a file would be the second weaker home for a person's evidence that
`BR-CUS-1020` exists to stop. `account_documents` already carries `BR-CUS-036`'s
`kyc` type, is uploadable and withdrawable, and the account exists before step 1
— so the wizard points at a door that is already built and needs no new endpoint,
table or migration. **Two limits of that cabinet are named rather than
discovered:** it has no `what_it_proves` column (`DEF-CUS-5943`) and
`uq_stored_documents_filed` allows one artefact per content type per account, so
two PDF scans cannot both be filed (`DEF-CUS-5944`).

### THE CLERK IS TOLD ABOUT A MATCH BEFORE THE COMMIT

`POST /transfers/buyer-preview` — validates a buyer, **writes absolutely
nothing**, and answers whether they are already on file. It is the drawn feedback
line on p126 and the step's own premise, *"Matched first, created only on no
match"*, stated back about the buyer being typed.

It is a POST that writes nothing **deliberately**: a `GET` would put a government
identifier in a URL, and a URL is logged by every proxy, sits in browser history
and lands in the next request's referer header — the class of leak
`BR-CUS-092`(c) is about. It creates no transfer row, which matters more than it
looks: `uq_transfers_open_from` allows one open transfer per account and no
screen lists one in flight, so a preview that started a job would leave an
account nobody could ever sell again and nobody could find to cancel.

### TWO THINGS FOUND ON THE WAY IN, AND THE FIRST IS NOT A DOCUMENTATION BUG

⚠ **`DEF-CUS-5940` — A PROPERTY WITH A DEPOSIT ON IT COULD NOT BE SOLD, AND HAD
NOT BEEN SELLABLE SINCE 2026-09-08.** `transfers._deposit_interest` called the
seam as `read(account.id)` while `selectors.deposit_interest_accrued(account_id,
as_of)` has required two arguments since `c7485bebc` gave it a body. Before that
commit the seam resolved to `None` and the line never ran; after it, every
account carrying a non-zero `deposit_on_file` raised `TypeError` on
`POST /transfers/commit` and on `GET /transfers/{id}/money`. `move_out_settlement`
was moved in the same commit; this call site was not. **Fourteen of the nineteen
cases in `test_cr058_w4_transfer_reassigns.py` had been erroring for twelve
days** — hard-won law 7's first shape, proved red at birth and then never read.
Fixed by forwarding `seams.tenant_today()`, and all fourteen are green.

⚠ **`DEF-CUS-5945` — THREE PLACES IN `transfers.py` SAID A TRANSFER HAS NO
REFERENCE NUMBER, AND `OQ-426` CLOSED ON 2026-08-27.** Every provisioned tenant
has held the `transfer` series at `TRF-{YY}-{0000}` since that ruling, and
`test_cr039_wd_transfer_and_case_numbers` asserts a new tenant's first transfer
renders **`TRF-26-0001`**. **The cost landed outside this file:** the Accounts
blueprint's transfer-record page draws a dashed panel reading *"No transfer
numbering series exists, so this sale carries no reference in the database
today"* — a drawing written from a comment that had been false for twenty-four
days, telling a screen lane to build the absence instead of the number. It is
CLAUDE.md's own warning exactly: a closed question's STATUS is edited and its
BODY goes on describing the open world, and the body is what a lane reads.

### WHAT IS NOT BUILT, AND IT IS NAMED SO NOBODY BUILDS AGAINST A PROMISE

**The transfer RECORD page's backend is not in this commit**, and the reason
sharpened while this one was being written.

**Four of the drawn record's facts have no durable home today** — the SELLER,
the balance as it stood, the deposit as it stood, and whether the buyer was
matched or created. All four exist only in `audit_log`, which is pruned.

⚠ **THE SELLER HALF IS NOT OURS AND WAS RULED WHILE THIS LANE WAS BUILDING —
`2c8a9a8e8`, THE SAME DAY.** PO verbatim: *"we cannot override customer id -
seller and buyer cstmer id are unique those does not change"*. **A `sold_by`
column on `transfers` is therefore the WRONG answer** and an earlier draft of
this entry proposed one. The shape that follows is a PERIOD on
`customer_accounts` — a sale ENDS the seller's link and OPENS the buyer's,
deleting neither — and that entry says in terms that it **needs its own decision
before it is built** because it changes a link table three modules read, and
that *"a lane must not simply add a column and move on."* **This lane has not.**
⚠ `reassign_account` still deletes the seller's link at the line that ruling
measures; **that is deliberate restraint and not an oversight**, and nothing in
this commit makes it worse.

**The two MONEY snapshots are still ours**, and nothing ruled today touches
them. `reassign_account`'s own docstring claims the row records *"the balance and
deposit AS THEY STOOD at the moment of sale"* — **it records neither**, which is
hard-won law 1: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. Two nullable
`NUMERIC(18,4)` columns settle it, on a table that is none of hard rule 4's four,
written ONCE at commit as new facts rather than as corrections.

⚠ **AND THE NUMBER IS ALREADY THERE, WHICH THE DRAWING DENIES** — see
`DEF-CUS-5945` above. The record page needs no numbering lane at all.

## 2026-09-20 · THE FINAL BILL IS PRICED FROM KEYED READS — BUILT, AND THE THREE THINGS IT LEFT OPEN

**`DEF-CUS-5931` and `DEF-CUS-5932` are FIXED, `v2.314.3`.** This records what was
built for the ruling of the same morning (*"option b is correct"*), the WORDS the
ruling deliberately left to the builder, and — most importantly for the next lane
— the ESTABLISHMENT the proration ruling demanded before anyone writes arithmetic.

### What was built, in one sentence each
* **Step 3 prices the reads keyed on step 2 and not yet committed.**
  `metering.provisional_reads_for_unit` lays the clerk's capture over
  `billing_reads_for_unit`'s rows and **writes nothing** — no `meter_reads` row,
  no staged batch, no estimate, no lock. The arithmetic is metering's own
  (`validation.compute_consumption`), the factor is the meter's own
  (`asset.multiplier`, which is exactly what the commit stamps), and a
  **committed read always wins**, so an account whose closing read was taken in
  the field prices exactly as it did before.
* **The commit order did not move.** `services.move_out` is untouched. Blueprint
  p111 stands: *"The reads are committed with the close, not before it."*
* **`DEF-CUS-5932`:** `prepare_final_bill` now reads the behaviour class off the
  account row BEFORE the gather, so a clerk who closed first is told the final
  bill had to come first — rather than being told about tariff versions.

### The words, which the ruling left to the builder
**`Priced from reads not yet committed.`** — six words, B14 rule 33's cap on a
FACT, using the drawing's own verb. It is not a warning and carries no tone:
nothing is wrong, and a clerk should learn where the number came from rather than
that they have made a mistake. The RATIONALE — why it is not committed yet, what
happens at step 6 — is **zero words on screen** (rule 33) and lives in the code
and here. It appears only when the engine actually priced a provisional row, and
a test proves it ABSENT on a committed read, because a sentence that is always on
screen tells a clerk nothing.

### ⚠ THE PRORATION RULING IS IMPLEMENTATION, NOT A RE-SIGN — ESTABLISHED, NOT GUESSED
The ruling of the same day (*"1. b"*) requires the builder to establish, **before
writing arithmetic**, whether B4.3 already gives the denominator for a cycled
account's final bill. **IT DOES, and the evidence is a ❄️ FROZEN worked figure.**

* B4.3, CONFIRMED: *"proration is by **calendar days**. The **base charge is
  always prorated**."*
* **GT-3, ❄️ FROZEN 2026-08-08**, states the denominator outright: *"move-in day
  16 of 30; base $30.50. Base proration **15/30** × 30.50 = **15.25**"*. The
  numerator is the days served and the denominator is the **cycle's own calendar
  length**. A mid-cycle move-OUT is the mirror of that mid-cycle move-IN.

**So it needs no finance re-sign: the frozen arithmetic already carries the term
and only the computation is missing** — the identical shape as the
deposit-interest question of 2026-09-19. ⚠ **AND `OQ-242`'s WITHDRAWAL IS NOT
TOUCHED BY IT**: that answered a CYCLE-LESS one-time bill, which has no cycle to
read a denominator from, and `TC12` must go on pinning `one_time._cycle_days`
returning `None`.

⚠ **AND THE PO HAS SINCE GIVEN THE GO-AHEAD, verbatim: *"okay we have to buld
it there will ebe code to reuse"*.** Read against the establishment above that is
an instruction to BUILD, not a request for a re-sign — the frozen arithmetic
already carries the term and only the computation is missing. **It would be the
opposite if B4.3 had not given the denominator: a PO saying *build it* is then
the REQUEST for a re-sign and never a substitute for one.** It gave it.

### ⚠ THE CODE TO REUSE — FOUND, AND THE PO WAS RIGHT THAT IT EXISTS
Nobody needs to write a proration routine. The chain is already built, already
🔒 review-pending, and already carries this exact defect's scar tissue:

* **`metering.period_engine.billing_period(frequency, start_day, first_run,
  as_of)`** — its own docstring opens *"**B4.3's DENOMINATOR, LOCATED ON A
  CALENDAR**"*. Pure, no ORM, no clock. It handles `OQ-339`'s month-end clamp
  and `OQ-340`'s anchor, and argues why the end is the next anchor rather than
  `expected_span_days`.
* **`metering.selectors.billing_period_for_unit(unit_id, as_of=…)`** — the seam,
  published for `DEF-2708`.
* **`customers.seams.billing_period_for_unit`** — customers' side of it.
* **`customers.disconnects._cycle_days_for(account, as_of=cut_on)`** — **the
  function to reuse, and it is four lines long.** It is the DISCONNECTION's cut
  bill doing precisely this, and it already carries the worked case: `A-11488`
  cut 18 August on a **$40.00** monthly base was charged **$40.00** where 18
  days of 31 is **$23.23** — **$16.77 too much on a real customer's final bill**
  — until the seam was published on 2026-08-31. A move-out's final bill is the
  same shape as a disconnection's cut bill.
* **`None` IS PART OF THE REUSE AND MUST TRAVEL.** A pre-CR-029 cycle carries no
  frequency and no first run, and a unit on two cycles has no single period.
  `cut_bill.CUT_BILL_DENOMINATOR_ABSENT` states that consequence on the result
  rather than inventing a 30-day month. **Nothing may assume 30.**

**IT IS NOT IN THIS COMMIT, and the reason is neither doubt nor the arithmetic.**
It is that **the preview and the RAISED bill have to move together or the preview
lies** — `TC5` requires the previewed total to equal the drafted invoice's total,
and `TC11` requires this door and the mounted one-time preview to agree line for
line. The raised final bill goes through `one_time._draft_for`, whose
`_cycle_days(request)` is **shared by every one-time kind** and is the very thing
`TC12` pins as RULED for a CYCLE-LESS bill. So the change must be scoped to
`kind='final'` inside `one_time`, leave `TC12` pinning what it pins, and carry
its own red proofs on all three cases and its own review-ledger row with its own
worked figure. That is a money commit, and it is this one's sibling rather than
its passenger. **The next lane starts here and re-derives none of it.** Measured
today, unchanged: a closing account is billed the whole **$20.00** plan charge
for a part-month window, and the PO's own case is **$18.50 where proration gives
$7.40 — $11.10 too much on a customer who is leaving.**

### Two fixture gaps the suite had, which were hiding the subject
`O1` could not have gone green on the fixture alone, and both gaps were the
fixture being BEHIND the product rather than the product being wrong:
* **the plan had no start date.** `plan_version_facts` says it in as many words —
  a published plan with no `effective_from` *"bills forever on the live path and
  refuses at R1 on this one"* — and `rating/0024` (DEF-494) back-fills one onto
  every published plan a real tenant holds. The fixture built a plan the product
  no longer builds.
* **the rate schedule stated no size axis.** `DEF-2799` is this exact gap one
  layer up, where it refused **47 of 47** accounts of a seeded utility, and
  `rating.sample_data.sample_size_rows` is the shape copied: the PLATFORM's
  ratified ladder for the service, every row with a NULL `minimum_bill`.

### What this commit deliberately did not take
* **`DEF-CUS-5935`** — `resolution_shadow._multiplier_for` asks the seam for the
  LATEST billable head rather than preferring the factor on the row being priced,
  which `billing_reads_for_unit`'s own docstring already calls the authoritative
  answer. Preferring the row everywhere is the better rule and **moves the factor
  on live bills**, so this commit takes the row's factor only where the row is
  PROVISIONAL and the seam cannot answer — which can unblock and can never change
  an existing figure.
* **`DEF-AST-5936`** — found by clicking, and by nothing else: **27 of the beta's
  133 assets record no connection size**, so the move-out wizard refuses to price
  a final bill on every account they stand on (`A-10432` was the one walked). It
  is a DATA state a human fixes on the asset screen; **no migration may write
  one.** Every fixture in this repository gives its meter a size class, so the
  one population nobody tests against is the customer's own.

Move-outs, **p131** Transfers, **p41** Complaints, **p48** Services — read AS IMAGES at
scale 6 (B14 rule 42, and its own point: the sub-lines are vector art and the text layer
carries none of the four). **Four frames of one head is what makes this generalise
rather than fit one tab**, which is why they were all opened.

⚠ **IT WAS REPORTED TWICE IN PROSE AND NEVER FILED AS A ROW.** `MoveOutsTab.tsx`'s own

2026-09-19 and deferred in its words — *"retitling it from a Move-outs lane would rename
the page under nine siblings"* — and the Transfers lane deferred the same way. Both were
right to defer and neither filed a row, so nothing counted it and it did not appear on
any list. **That is hard rule 4's own lesson in a different family: a finding recorded
only in the file you happen to be in is a finding nobody can count.** `DEF-CUS-5939` is
that row, filed BEFORE the fix (step W).

**THREE JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT, EACH WITH ITS FIGURE.**

**1 · THE THIRD SUB-LINE FRAGMENT IS OMITTED ON ALL TEN TABS, NOT ZEROED.** The drawings
read `10 tabs · Move-outs · 1 still open` (p117, p131), `… · 3 open` (p48) and
`… · 4 open, 1 past due` (p41). The figures are ILLUSTRATIONS under B14 rule 37 and the
shape all four agree on is `N open`. **No tab can hand the head that number honestly
today.** Every tab body owns its own query and its `OPEN` tile rides INSIDE that query's
envelope, keyed by table state the tab holds in its own `useState` —
`MoveOutsTab`'s `moveOutsQueryKey(state)` is the shape, and `move_out_kpis` is computed
over `move_outs_queryset()` rather than over the rows on screen. A count read from the
head would therefore be a SECOND DEFINITION of *open* on one screen. **That is exactly
the hazard the PO ruled on for the Move-outs tile on 2026-09-19 — option A, LEAVE IT,
because a figure that contradicts its own caption is worse than a missing one.** And a
`0` is a claim, not an absence: `0 open` says *nothing is open*, which nothing here
knows. So the head renders **two** fragments — `10 tabs · Move-outs` — and
`DEF-CUS-5953` carries the third with what it needs: each tab publishing its SERVED
`kpis.open` up to the head, one number and one definition, the way this screen now
publishes its breadcrumb leaf.

**2 · THE ONE HEADER ACTION DROPS FROM THE FILLED `primary` TIER TO THE KIT'S QUIET
`ghost`, AND THAT BREAKS NO RULE.** All four frames draw it as plain words top right:
`+ New move-out`, `+ New transfer`, `+ Log a complaint`, `+ Request a service` — no fill,
no border, no underline. BR-SHL-044 orders the row *status → secondaries → ONE primary*
and its clause **(c)** says in terms that *"a tab may legitimately have NO header
action"*, so the law is a CAP of one and not a requirement of one. It stays per-tab and
it stays the only action in the row. ⚠ **`ghost` AND NOT `link`, WHICH IS THE ONE PLACE
THE DRAWING AND THE KIT DISAGREE**: `link` underlines and none of the four frames does,
so the quiet borderless accent tier is what composing the kit means here (B14 rule 36 —
compose the kit, never hand-roll a fifth button style in a screen). Measured on the
built stylesheet rather than asserted from a class name: background
`rgba(0,0,0,0)`, border colour transparent, `text-decoration: none`, on all ten tabs at
both widths.

**3 · THE HEAD TAKES A NEW TITLE KEY RATHER THAN RENAMING `customers.accounts.title`.**
That key's VALUE is *Accounts* and **five other screens read it as their `← back`
label** — `AccountDetailPage`, `NewAccountWizard`, `NewConnectWizard`, `MoveInWizard`,
`MoveOutWizard`. p117's second figure draws that control as `← The register`, so
changing the one value would have been RIGHT and would have renamed a control on five
screens at once, four of them under a live lane, on this lane's authority, with

does not own. **So the head took `customers.accounts.head.title` and the back links were

or forgotten.

**AND THE STRIP COUNT IS GONE, WITH A MEASURED REASON THAT IS NOT THE DRAWING'S.** One
tab out of ten rendered `Accounts 78`, and the file's own docstring called it *"the one

was `listQuery.data.count` — the number of rows matching the CURRENT FILTERS — so typing
in the search box moved the number beside the tab's own word. None of the four frames

from all eleven catalogues in the same commit, because a string nothing renders is the
next lane's false lead. The figure is not lost: the pager under the table states

**THE BREADCRUMB NEEDED A SHELL CAPABILITY THAT DID NOT EXIST, AND `DEF-374` HAS SAID SO
SINCE 2026-08-21.** `breadcrumbFor` resolves crumbs from `SHELL_NAV` and the PATHNAME
alone and is right to — US-SHL-002 TC-3 says query params never move the breadcrumb, and
this tab rides in `?tab=` — so a screen whose sub-context is not in the path had no way

FILE BECAUSE `AppShell.tsx` CANNOT BE PUT ON `styles/route-b-migrated.txt`** — the

**ONE SOURCE FOR THE TAB'S WORD, WHICH IS THE THING THAT KEEPS THE HEAD HONEST.** Three

## 2026-09-20 · THE TRANSFERS TAB IS REBUILT TO THE SALE IT ACTUALLY PERFORMS (`DEF-CUS-5092`)

**PO approval, verbatim: *"this is correct - please fix it"***, on a change list
put to them in plain English with the counts: **drop 3 tiles · add 1 · rewrite 1
· add 2 columns · change 3 · remove 1 · delete ~70 words · rewrite the empty
state.** Shipped in `v2.315.1`.

### WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN A COPY FIX

`BR-CUS-1030` (PO 2026-09-01) made a transfer a **reassignment** — *"dont create
new account - we reassing that account - bascailly I have sold my property."*
That commit (`d1066469e`) rewrote `transfers.py` by **916 lines** and touched
`TransfersTab.tsx` by **38**, all of which were one added sentence and a link.
**So for nineteen days the list beside the rebuilt wizard drew the deleted job,
and six of its statements were not stale but FALSE.** The PO, looking at it
live: *"too much text"*. It was worse than that — **a clerk learning the flow
from this tab learned it backwards**:

| On screen | Why it was wrong |
|---|---|
| `Open` — *"same customer, new address"* | a sale is a **different** customer at the **same** address: the exact inverse |
| `Moving this week` | nobody moves; it is a sale date |
| `Deposits carrying` — *"not refunded and re-collected"* | counted an election `OQ-1252` removed the same day |
| `Arrears following` — *"a debt moving to a new account"* | **there is no new account** |
| the empty state — *"moves the same customer to a new address as one job"* | the exact case the wizard's own red warning says is **not** a transfer |
| `ONE JOB — its two halves are deliberately kept out of Move-ins and Move-outs` | **there are no halves**, and it published an internal counting decision, which B14 rule 33 puts at zero words on screen |

### WHAT IT IS NOW — blueprint p131, read AS AN IMAGE (B14 rule 42)

**Three tiles** — `Open` (*"a sale part-way through"*) · `Selling this week`
(*"sale date within 7 days"* — the word moved, the arithmetic did not) · `Owed
on accounts being sold`.

**Eight columns** — `Reference · Address · Account · Sold to · Sale date · Step
· Taken on · State`. The property's address is drawn for the first time; the
two-line `A-10650 → A-11940` cell is one account number, because
`reassign_account` sets `to_account_id` to the SAME account and that cell read
`A-11455 → A-11455` on every completed sale; `Out date` and `In date`, written
to the same day by construction, are one `Sale date`; and `Money`'s two stacked
sentences are one `Taken on` figure.

### FOUR JUDGEMENTS THE RULES DID NOT MAKE FOR US

**1 · `Sold to` is empty until the sale commits, and says so.** One served name
does two jobs: `start_transfer` sets `transfer.customer` to the **seller**, and
`reassign_account` overwrites it with the **buyer** at commit. A column labelled
`Sold to` that simply printed it would name the SELLER on every open row — the
same class of falsehood being removed. It renders the buyer only once
`committed_at` is set and states the absence before that: *"Recorded when the
sale completes."*

**2 · `Sold by` and `↗ Open` are NOT built, and that is the ruling rather than a
shortfall.** PO, 2026-09-20: *"Two held deliberately: Sold by and ↗ Open. Both
would need faking — one from a pruned audit log, one pointing at a page that
doesn't exist. That's the defect we spent yesterday removing."* `DEF-CUS-5980`
and `DEF-CUS-5979`. **The expiry tests are in the same commit** (hard-won law
2's mirror): one runs `matchRoutes` over the real `APP_ROUTES` and requires that
nothing matches `/transfers/:id`, the other asserts `sold_by` is absent from the
row shape. Either becoming possible turns the suite red and names the column.

**3 · The money tile states its absence rather than showing a zero.**
`kpi_strip` serves five counts and no money, so `Owed on accounts being sold`
has nothing to show. **`$0.00` would be a claim that nothing is owed** —
DEF-127's *"looks exactly like a settled account"* at strip scale.
`DEF-CUS-5979`.

**4 · `Sale date` is not sortable, and that is a refusal.**
`transfer_reads.SORTS["out_date"]` orders by `from_account__closed_at` — correct
while a transfer CLOSED the outgoing account, **NULL on every live row since the
ruling removed the closure**. A date header that reorders rows by nothing is a
control telling a clerk something untrue. `DEF-CUS-5979`; the column gains it
back when the server's term names `transfers.out_date`.

### ⚠ NOTHING SERVED WAS RETIRED — `DEF-CUS-3653`'s LESSON, APPLIED

`kpi_strip` still returns `deposits_carrying`, `arrears_following` and
`completed_this_month`; `money.lines` still carries the `deposit_carried` line;
`from_cell`, `from_to`, `in_date` and `exclusion.callout` are all still sent and
still typed. **Three tiles and two columns stopped being DRAWN; nothing stopped
being SERVED**, and two backend suites still assert every one of those counts.
Every consumer was grepped first, which is the whole of `DEF-CUS-3653`: an
account header lost `Austin, TX 78704` on every account, silently, because a
value was retired without that grep.

### ONE DIVERGENCE FROM THE DRAWING, STAMPED

p131 draws `TAKEN ON $64.20` in plain ink; the figure renders **amber**, because
`line.tone` arrives as data and B18 §5.7.2 decided that for the arrear. Kept,
for two written reasons: B14 rule 37 makes a drawn figure an illustration, and
dropping it would make the screen a second place deciding a tone the payload
carries on purpose. Verified in a browser at 1440 and 1280. A ruling either way
is one expression to change.

### WHAT FOUND WHAT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING

**The unit suite found the copy.** Three assertions went red on the real strings
and stayed red until the **catalogues** were corrected — because **a catalogue
entry beats a code `defaultValue`**, so changing only the fallback would have
shipped `same customer, new address` to every English user with a green suite.
Fifteen keys corrected or added and sixteen retired, through
`10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py`, which owns those eleven files: **34 changed lines
per catalogue and nothing else moved.**

**The browser found the rest**, at 1440 and 1280, against a stack booted on this
branch's own build: `10-scripts/po20260920_transfers_tab_walkthrough.mjs`, **43
checks, all passing**, with `po20260920_transfers_tab_seed.py` and its purge
either side. `DEF-CUS-5934`'s prevention column asked for exactly this — *"this
flow has no walkthrough script while move-in, move-out and the clerk request
walk all have one"*.

⚠ **AND THE SEED CARRIES ONE INDEBTED ACCOUNT ON PURPOSE.** The first run put
`—` in every `Taken on` cell, truthfully, because every demo account it could
sell sits at a zero balance — **a column of dashes cannot tell a working money
cell from a broken one.** The seed now makes its own seller for an account
carrying a balance, and the walk asserts a real `$30.50` at two decimals.

⚠ **AND THE PURGE WRITTEN FOR THAT WALK DELETED A REAL CUSTOMER'S ACCOUNT LINKS
— `DEF-CUS-5980`, self-reported.** It read `row.customer` as *"the buyer"*,
which on an OPEN transfer is the **seller**: the same one-name-two-jobs mechanic
this whole rebuild exists to remove, in the tool written to check the rebuild,
within the hour. It removed every `customer_accounts` row for Ana Alvarez
(`C-00001`) and was stopped from deleting her only by a `PROTECT` edge. The link
was restored and the beta verified back to 55 customers, 57 links, 0 transfers
and no orphans. **The durable point: a cleanup script is a write path on live
data and deserves a gate's question — *what would make this pass wrongly?*** It
now refuses any row whose name does not carry its own marker.

### ⚠ AND THE SIX DEFECT IDS THIS ROW CITES ARE THE SECOND SET

The first six were allocated correctly against the remote, and **all six were
taken by sibling lanes while this work was being done** — twenty-one commits
landed on the branch in the interval, including a `2.314.1` this lane had also
reserved. `10-scripts/allocate.py <family> --verify` reported every one as TAKEN
at push time and nothing else would have: the arithmetic was right both times,
and what was wrong was *which world the maximum came from*. Every blob was then
re-derived from the new tip — the eleven catalogues re-fanned onto the new
bytes, both registers restored and re-appended, the version re-allocated — which
is CLAUDE.md law 11's unconditional push-time re-derivation performed rather
than described. **The register merged cleanly at every point**, which is the
part worth remembering: a clean merge says nothing whatever about whether two
lanes took the same number.

## 2026-09-20 · A LANDLORD WITH OPEN TENANTS IS WARNED, NOT REFUSED — `OQ-CUS-12515` CLOSED, OPTION B

**PO ruling, verbatim: *"option B - give a warning and allow it; if owner has sold
the property to new owner then we are transfering all libalities and ownership to
new owner"***.

**This REVERSES `BR-CUS-1082`, which was built hours earlier as a hard refusal
failing closed.** It was minted as a LANE JUDGMENT precisely because the rule it
enforces was never signed (`B19 §15.8`: *"THIS IS NOT IN ANY SIGNED RULE … It
needs ratifying before W5 builds step 1"*), and `OQ-CUS-12515` was opened for
exactly this ratification. **The question was asked correctly and the answer is
no.** `BR-CUS-1082` becomes a WARNING and its row says so with this date.

### ⚠ THE PO'S REASON IS THE PART THAT MATTERS, AND THE LANE DID NOT HAVE IT
The build argued from asymmetry: refusing wrongly costs a support call, permitting
wrongly writes a numbered record hard rule 4 forbids deleting. **That reasoning is
sound and it is answered by a fact about the product rather than about risk.**

**A landlord leaving is not a landlord abandoning their tenants.** Where the
property has been SOLD, the act is a TRANSFER — and a transfer moves the whole
account, its liabilities and its ownership to the new owner, with the tenants
untouched beneath it. So the case the refusal was protecting against **already has
its own flow**, and blocking the move-out blocks the legitimate remainder: an
owner who is leaving for some other reason entirely.

**A product that refuses a lawful act to prevent a mistake the adjacent flow
already prevents is not failing closed; it is failing shut.**

### What changes
* `services.move_out`'s refusal becomes a **warning carried on the response**, not
  a raise. It still reads the ONE count `selectors.sub_accounts_for_master`
  answers, so the screen and the commit cannot disagree.
* Step 1's strip stays, **reworded from an instruction to a fact** — a clerk may
  now continue. B14 rule 33 caps it: a fact ≤ 6 words, and **no rationale on
  screen** (the *why* lives here and in `br_ref`, never in the copy).
* `E1` of the move-out suite **must be rewritten, not deleted**: it currently
  asserts the refusal. The contract it guards is still real — *a clerk is told* —
  and a row that simply vanishes takes the coverage with it.

### What this ruling does NOT decide
* **the words of the warning** — the builder's, against rule 33;
* whether the clerk must acknowledge it or may walk past it silently;
* anything about the TRANSFER path, which is where the sold-property case belongs
  and is being built separately.

### BUILT — `v2.317.0`, the same day

**The reversal is in the product.** `services.move_out`'s raise became a
`warnings.append` **in the place the raise stood** — above `_commit_event_reads`,
before any write — carrying `code: master_closed_over_open_sub_accounts`,
`br_ref: BR-CUS-1082`, the same `message_key` step 1 draws, and the count. It
still reads the ONE call `selectors.sub_accounts_for_master` answers, which is
the same call `settlement_for` makes, so the screen and the commit cannot
disagree; **that clause survived the reversal untouched, because it guarantees
one definition of an open child whether the answer refuses or warns.**

**The three the ruling left open, decided here and written down rather than
asked back:**

* **The words: `2 sub-accounts are still open.`** — a FACT of five words
  (B14 rule 33) and nothing else. The instruction *"Close or reassign them
  first."* was removed from **all eleven catalogues**, in each language, by
  dropping the second sentence rather than re-translating the first (rule 35).
  It had to go: it told a clerk to do something the product no longer requires.
  No rule id and no reason on screen (rules 31/32).
* **No acknowledgement.** The clerk may walk straight past it. A tick-to-continue
  would be the refusal again with one more click, which is the thing the PO
  removed, and five further steps plus a named commit button already stand
  between reading the warning and closing anything.
* **Nothing about the TRANSFER path**, which is another lane's and was left
  alone. ⚠ **The screen is asserted NOT to mention it** — after this ruling the
  tempting rationale is *"a sale is a transfer"*, and rationale is zero words on
  screen.

⚠ **THE TIER MOVED WITH THE WORDS, AND THAT IS NOT DECORATION.** Step 1's strip
was a `RefusalStrip` — danger, `role="alert"`, `data-refusal` in the markup. A
warning left in that wrapper still reads as a refusal to a clerk and still
announces itself as one to a screen reader, whatever the sentence says. It is
the kit's `WarningBox` now (`tone="soon"`, `role="status"`,
`data-warning="customers-open-sub-accounts"`), which is B14 rule 36 — and which
also keeps `MoveOutWizard.tsx` free of Tailwind utilities, because that file is
NOT on `route-b-migrated.txt` and G31 still owns every class in it.

⚠ **PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE BOTH FALSE PASSES ARE REAL HERE (law 7).**
A warning that never fires passes a test that only checks the commit succeeded —
every move-out commits now — and a warning that fires on EVERY account passes a
test of the master case exactly as a correct one does. **Four mutations in two
pairs, each run on `config.settings.pgtest` and reverted:** the warning DELETED →
`tc1`+`tc4` red, `tc2`+`tc3` green · WIDENED to every account → `tc2`+`tc3` red,
`tc1`+`tc4` green · the COUNT hard-coded to 1 → `tc1`+`tc4` red on the number
while the code still fires · the `if` INVERTED → all four red. **And the close is
asserted as well as the warning**: `E1` now declares `outcome=committed`,
`account_status=CLOSED` and a real `move_record` where it declared a refusal and
`move_record=None` a day earlier.

⚠ **THE OLD BROWSER WALKTHROUGH WOULD HAVE CLOSED A REAL BETA ACCOUNT, AND THIS
IS THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING.** `def_cus_5930_master_move_out_walkthrough.mjs`
stated in its own header that it *"NEVER COMMITS ANYTHING, AND THE BETA IS SAFE
BY CONSTRUCTION … the request that would write is the request that cannot"* — a
safety property that rested entirely on the move-out being REFUSED. This ruling
removed the refusal, so the script's POST would have permanently closed
`AC-2026-00051` (*Ridge Property LLC*), ended its agreements and allocated a move
record hard rule 4 forbids deleting — **and every check in the file would have
gone on passing, for the opposite reason.** The POST is replaced by a read-only
close-impact GET; the write half is proved on a throwaway tenant instead.
**The general form: a safety guarantee that rests on something being refused
expires on the day the refusal does, and nothing announces it.**

⚠ **THE SUITE SCORE WAS RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN CARRIED FORWARD.** The brief
quoted *18 of 27*; a run at the tip measured **20 of 27** complete with the bill
stated and **5 of 27** with none. Other lanes had landed work in between — a
score quoted from a document is a claim about the past.

**Registers walked in the same commit (closing a question is a fan-out):** the
`OQ-CUS-12515` row's STATUS *and its BODY* · `BR-CUS-1082`'s row · `B19 §15.8`
(item 1 superseded; items 2–3 stand, and the section's own *"this is not in any
signed rule"* disclaimer is kept verbatim, because it is what sent the question
to the PO and it was right to) · the `J-MVO` journey · the human-review ledger
(the `v2.314.2` row's statement (1) is now ANSWERED; its statements (2) and (3)
never were and return to the agenda) · `CHANGELOG.md` and the three version
files.

## 2026-09-20 · THE TRANSFER RECORD IS BUILT, AND FOUR OF ITS ROWS ARE THE RULE RATHER THAN A READING

**PO ruling, verbatim: *"buildit - use drawing images. screens hosuld match
exactly to drawing"***, on blueprint **p132** — *"The transfer, opened ·
TRF-26-0021 · /brazosbend/transfers/trf-26-0021"*. The conformance lane had
measured the gap the same week and called it the sharpest on the surface:
**a clerk could make a sale and had no way to read it back.** No route, no
component, no endpoint.

Built to the page READ AS AN IMAGE (B14 rule 42) — one 2x whole-page render and
three crops at 3x and 3.5x — never from the text layer.
`07-frontend/src/features/customers/TransferRecordPage.tsx`, mounted at
`/:tenant/transfers/:ref`, **after** the static `/transfers/new` so `new` can
never be read as a reference.

### ⚠ THE DRAWING'S OWN DASHED PANEL IS STALE, AND A LANE FOLLOWING IT WOULD HAVE BUILT A REFUSAL THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE
p132 draws a dashed block reading *"No transfer numbering series exists, so this
sale carries no reference in the database today."* **`OQ-426` reads CLOSED in
the register's status column**, ruled **2026-08-27**, PO verbatim: *"Transfer
TRF-26-0001 … follow same logic that we are following for other numbers we have
did in settings."* `core/numbering.py` carries the series, `transfers.py`
allocates inside `start_transfer`'s transaction, and `_serialize` already emits
`transfer_no` **and** `TRANSFER_NUMBER_UNAVAILABLE` for a row that predates it.

So the screen renders BOTH arms — the number when there is one, the server's own
absence sentence when there is not — which is what the dashed panel asked for,
in four words instead of forty-five. **This is the prime directive's own lesson
in a drawing rather than a register row: the status column decides, and a body
that contradicts it is stale until proved otherwise.** A sibling lane reached
the same finding independently the same day and wrote it up in
`conformance/transfer-record-what-is-durable.md`; `DEF-CUS-5945` records how the
drawing came to say otherwise.

### FOUR ROWS ARE A PROHIBITION, NOT A MEASUREMENT — AND THAT IS THE ONE PLACE THIS SCREEN DRAWS A FIGURE THE SERVER DID NOT SEND
`BR-CUS-085`, verbatim: *"This customer is not leaving. Their deposit, their
discounts and their history move with them — nothing is refunded and
re-collected."* The register states what the rule BINDS — `deposit_on_file` is
not touched, no refund is raised, `transfers.py` commits `"refund_raised":
False` and a test asserts it.

**So `Refunded to seller` and `Re-collected from buyer` read `$0.00` from the
RULE.** Rendering them as an absence would say *"we did not check"* about the
single fact this screen exists to prove. `Fees charged · None` is the same one
step weaker — the word *fee* does not appear anywhere in
`apps/customers/transfers.py` — and `Unit and meters`, `Plan` and
`Service agreements` read `Unchanged` for the same reason: `BR-CUS-1030` forbids
the sale touching any of them, so a server READ would be asking whether a thing
the code cannot do had happened. **The sibling's measurement agrees in its own
words: those two rows are *"CONSTANTS of the rule"*.**

**Everything else is served or stated as an absence, and three absences are
named with their reasons:** the seller (`reassign_account` deletes the link and
`audit_log` is pruned — the PO ruled on 2026-09-20 that this must stop, and the
shape that follows is proposed, not built), deposit interest (*computed at
settlement*, PO 2026-09-19 — a `$0.00` here is **$3.50 wrong against the
customer** on a $150.00 deposit held fourteen months), and the ledger's length
(nothing in this product counts unbroken months, so p132's `38 months` is B14
rule 37's illustration and nothing more).

⛔ **AND THE SCREEN MAY NEVER READ TODAY'S BALANCE AND LABEL IT AS THE SALE'S.**
The drawing says every figure is *"as it stood on the day, not as it stands
now"*, and the two snapshots are computed at commit and never stored. This page
renders only what the server sends, so the wrong-by-what-has-moved-since defect
cannot happen here.

### THE COPY IS OURS AND THE SHAPE IS THE DRAWING'S — SIX CUTS, EACH RECORDED
PO, 2026-09-19: *"even if drawing sshow too much content ons creen - dont apply
that we have to use our rules to show content on screen"*. Cut as RATIONALE
(B14 rule 33, zero words on screen): the banner's 24-word second sentence (every
clause of it is a ROW of *Nothing changed* below), *"Nothing moved, and that is
why this is cheap…"*, *"A bill is a record of what was sent…"*, the 48-word red
contact-details box (the row *Contact details · Still the seller's* survives),
the dashed reference panel, and the `Account` row's second clause (`Status` is a
row six lines down). All six live in the file's own §3.

### ⚠ ONE DRAWN ROW IS KEPT UNDER PROTEST AND IS PUT TO THE PO
*Buyer told · Not decided* is `OQ-1253`, OPEN. **On 2026-09-20 the PO struck the
wizard's own *Who gets told this figure* panel** — *"why we are showing this"* —
because it shows a clerk an undecided internal question. That ruling is about
STEP 4, where a clerk is deciding; this row sits in a section whose whole job is
to name what the record cannot tell you, and the brief for the screen lists it.
**Kept, in two words, and reported.** One word from the PO removes it.

### TWO JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT MAKE FOR US
* **The door VARIANTS.** p132 draws `Open the customer` as an OUTLINED button
  and `Open the account` as quiet text: **no filled button appears on this
  screen at all**, which is *"this record has no actions"* said in ink. This
  kit's `primary` is `bg-accent` — filled, the colour a commit wears — so the
  two doors are the kit's `secondary` and `ghost`. Picking from the kit rather
  than inventing a grey is B14 rule 36.
* **Their ORDER.** p132 puts the customer door on the LEFT; `PageHeader` renders
  `secondaryActions` before `primaryAction` on ~137 screens, so the emphasised
  door is rightmost. **B14 rule 38 settles it** — a header's button order is
  CONSTRUCTION, and following the drawing would make this the one screen in the
  product whose action bar reads the other way round. What the bar CONTAINS is
  still the drawing's.

### WHAT IS OWED, AND IT IS FILED RATHER THAN LEFT
* **No door points here yet** (`DEF-CUS-5982`). `TransfersTab.tsx` states
  in its own §4 that it draws no row action because *"There is no transfer
  detail screen, so a 👁 icon would link onto nothing"* — a refusal that stops
  being true at this commit, and hard-won law 2's mirror exactly. That file is
  held by another lane today, so the door is OWED and filed, never silently
  left.
* **The breadcrumb's leaf** (`DEF-SHL-5983`). p132 draws
  `Accounts / Transfers / TRF-26-0021`; `AppShell.breadcrumbFor` derives crumbs
  from the nav config and its own comment says the record's leaf is *"the
  consuming detail screen's to supply when it lands"* — and no prop exists to
  supply it. `/moves/:ref` has the same gap. It is a shell change, so it is
  filed rather than taken.
* **`GET /transfers/{ref}` is not mounted.** Until it is, the address renders
  one sentence saying the reference names no transfer. Deliberate: a screen that
  draws its own furniture over no data looks like a working page, which is worse
  than a 404.
* **The walkthrough that did not exist.** Transfer was the only one of these
  flows with no browser walk — which is why the PO found a live step-4 break in
  one pass while 39 tests were green.
  `10-scripts/po20260920_transfer_record_walkthrough.mjs` is that walk: 33
  assertions, and it says in its own report every time it runs that two of its
  three walks answer the unmounted endpoint from a browser-side stub.

## 2026-09-20 · THE TRANSFERS TAB IS REBUILT TO THE SALE IT ACTUALLY PERFORMS (`DEF-CUS-5092`)

**PO approval, verbatim: *"this is correct - please fix it"***, on a change list
put to them in plain English with the counts: **drop 3 tiles · add 1 · rewrite 1
· add 2 columns · change 3 · remove 1 · delete ~70 words · rewrite the empty
state.** Shipped in `v2.315.1`.

### WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN A COPY FIX

`BR-CUS-1030` (PO 2026-09-01) made a transfer a **reassignment** — *"dont create
new account - we reassing that account - bascailly I have sold my property."*
That commit (`d1066469e`) rewrote `transfers.py` by **916 lines** and touched
`TransfersTab.tsx` by **38**, all of which were one added sentence and a link.
**So for nineteen days the list beside the rebuilt wizard drew the deleted job,
and six of its statements were not stale but FALSE.** The PO, looking at it
live: *"too much text"*. It was worse than that — **a clerk learning the flow
from this tab learned it backwards**:

| On screen | Why it was wrong |
|---|---|
| `Open` — *"same customer, new address"* | a sale is a **different** customer at the **same** address: the exact inverse |
| `Moving this week` | nobody moves; it is a sale date |
| `Deposits carrying` — *"not refunded and re-collected"* | counted an election `OQ-1252` removed the same day |
| `Arrears following` — *"a debt moving to a new account"* | **there is no new account** |
| the empty state — *"moves the same customer to a new address as one job"* | the exact case the wizard's own red warning says is **not** a transfer |
| `ONE JOB — its two halves are deliberately kept out of Move-ins and Move-outs` | **there are no halves**, and it published an internal counting decision, which B14 rule 33 puts at zero words on screen |

### WHAT IT IS NOW — blueprint p131, read AS AN IMAGE (B14 rule 42)

**Three tiles** — `Open` (*"a sale part-way through"*) · `Selling this week`
(*"sale date within 7 days"* — the word moved, the arithmetic did not) · `Owed
on accounts being sold`.

**Eight columns** — `Reference · Address · Account · Sold to · Sale date · Step
· Taken on · State`. The property's address is drawn for the first time; the
two-line `A-10650 → A-11940` cell is one account number, because
`reassign_account` sets `to_account_id` to the SAME account and that cell read
`A-11455 → A-11455` on every completed sale; `Out date` and `In date`, written
to the same day by construction, are one `Sale date`; and `Money`'s two stacked
sentences are one `Taken on` figure.

### FOUR JUDGEMENTS THE RULES DID NOT MAKE FOR US

**1 · `Sold to` is empty until the sale commits, and says so.** One served name
does two jobs: `start_transfer` sets `transfer.customer` to the **seller**, and
`reassign_account` overwrites it with the **buyer** at commit. A column labelled
`Sold to` that simply printed it would name the SELLER on every open row — the
same class of falsehood being removed. It renders the buyer only once
`committed_at` is set and states the absence before that: *"Recorded when the
sale completes."*

**2 · `Sold by` and `↗ Open` are NOT built, and that is the ruling rather than a
shortfall.** PO, 2026-09-20: *"Two held deliberately: Sold by and ↗ Open. Both
would need faking — one from a pruned audit log, one pointing at a page that
doesn't exist. That's the defect we spent yesterday removing."* the `Sold by` row
and the transfer-record-page row. **The expiry tests are in the same commit** (hard-won law
2's mirror): one runs `matchRoutes` over the real `APP_ROUTES` and requires that
nothing matches `/transfers/:id`, the other asserts `sold_by` is absent from the
row shape. Either becoming possible turns the suite red and names the column.

**3 · The money tile states its absence rather than showing a zero.**
`kpi_strip` serves five counts and no money, so `Owed on accounts being sold`
has nothing to show. **`$0.00` would be a claim that nothing is owed** —
DEF-127's *"looks exactly like a settled account"* at strip scale.
the money-tile row.

**4 · `Sale date` is not sortable, and that is a refusal.**
`transfer_reads.SORTS["out_date"]` orders by `from_account__closed_at` — correct
while a transfer CLOSED the outgoing account, **NULL on every live row since the
ruling removed the closure**. A date header that reorders rows by nothing is a
control telling a clerk something untrue. the sale-date sort row; the column gains it
back when the server's term names `transfers.out_date`.

### ⚠ NOTHING SERVED WAS RETIRED — `DEF-CUS-3653`'s LESSON, APPLIED

`kpi_strip` still returns `deposits_carrying`, `arrears_following` and
`completed_this_month`; `money.lines` still carries the `deposit_carried` line;
`from_cell`, `from_to`, `in_date` and `exclusion.callout` are all still sent and
still typed. **Three tiles and two columns stopped being DRAWN; nothing stopped
being SERVED**, and two backend suites still assert every one of those counts.
Every consumer was grepped first, which is the whole of `DEF-CUS-3653`: an
account header lost `Austin, TX 78704` on every account, silently, because a
value was retired without that grep.

### ONE DIVERGENCE FROM THE DRAWING, STAMPED

p131 draws `TAKEN ON $64.20` in plain ink; the figure renders **amber**, because
`line.tone` arrives as data and B18 §5.7.2 decided that for the arrear. Kept,
for two written reasons: B14 rule 37 makes a drawn figure an illustration, and
dropping it would make the screen a second place deciding a tone the payload
carries on purpose. Verified in a browser at 1440 and 1280. A ruling either way
is one expression to change.

### WHAT FOUND WHAT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING

**The unit suite found the copy.** Three assertions went red on the real strings
and stayed red until the **catalogues** were corrected — because **a catalogue
entry beats a code `defaultValue`**, so changing only the fallback would have
shipped `same customer, new address` to every English user with a green suite.
Fifteen keys corrected or added and sixteen retired, through
`10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py`, which owns those eleven files: **34 changed lines
per catalogue and nothing else moved.**

**The browser found the rest**, at 1440 and 1280, against a stack booted on this
branch's own build: `10-scripts/po20260920_transfers_tab_walkthrough.mjs`, **43
checks, all passing**, with `po20260920_transfers_tab_seed.py` and its purge
either side. `DEF-CUS-5934`'s prevention column asked for exactly this — *"this
flow has no walkthrough script while move-in, move-out and the clerk request
walk all have one"*.

⚠ **AND THE SEED CARRIES ONE INDEBTED ACCOUNT ON PURPOSE.** The first run put
`—` in every `Taken on` cell, truthfully, because every demo account it could
sell sits at a zero balance — **a column of dashes cannot tell a working money
cell from a broken one.** The seed now makes its own seller for an account
carrying a balance, and the walk asserts a real `$30.50` at two decimals.

⚠ **AND THE PURGE WRITTEN FOR THAT WALK DELETED A REAL CUSTOMER'S ACCOUNT LINKS
— the purge row, self-reported.** It read `row.customer` as *"the buyer"*,
which on an OPEN transfer is the **seller**: the same one-name-two-jobs mechanic
this whole rebuild exists to remove, in the tool written to check the rebuild,
within the hour. It removed every `customer_accounts` row for Ana Alvarez
(`C-00001`) and was stopped from deleting her only by a `PROTECT` edge. The link
was restored and the beta verified back to 55 customers, 57 links, 0 transfers
and no orphans. **The durable point: a cleanup script is a write path on live
data and deserves a gate's question — *what would make this pass wrongly?*** It
now refuses any row whose name does not carry its own marker.

### ⚠ AND THE SIX DEFECT IDS THIS ROW CITES ARE THE SECOND SET

The first six were allocated correctly against the remote, and **all six were
taken by sibling lanes while this work was being done** — twenty-one commits
landed on the branch in the interval, including a `2.314.1` this lane had also
reserved. `10-scripts/allocate.py <family> --verify` reported every one as TAKEN
at push time and nothing else would have: the arithmetic was right both times,
and what was wrong was *which world the maximum came from*. Every blob was then
re-derived from the new tip — the eleven catalogues re-fanned onto the new
bytes, both registers restored and re-appended, the version re-allocated — which
is CLAUDE.md law 11's unconditional push-time re-derivation performed rather
than described. **The register merged cleanly at every point**, which is the
part worth remembering: a clean merge says nothing whatever about whether two
lanes took the same number.

### ⚠⚠ AND THE RENUMBER THAT FIXED THAT CASCADED — `DEF-CUS-5984`, AND IT IS PUBLISHED

The helper written to renumber on every pass replaced the six ids **one pair at
a time**, so `5973 → 5975` and then `5975 → 5977` rewrote the id it had just
created: the six collapsed onto the last two — **three rows are published as
`DEF-CUS-5979` and three as `DEF-CUS-5980`** — and fifteen citations point at
whichever of the pair they became. That is why the rows above are named by
SUBJECT rather than by id: the mapping no longer exists.

**Every check passed and each was true** — the new ids were free at the tip,
both registers were byte-identical prefixes of it, the numstat showed additions
only, and every hunk was this lane's. **None of them asks whether six ids are
still six.** What found it was law 11's last step done literally: reading each
marker back out of `HEAD`, where one cited id returned a count of **zero**.

⚠ **THE REPAIR IS PREPARED AND DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED.** Correcting an id
makes the old line VANISH, and `push_register_guard.py` refuses that by design —
its allowance is per-ID and the id is the one field that must change. The splice
was built and proved (same file length, exactly six lines differing, **all 3,482
other rows byte-identical**) and it needs `ALLOW_REGISTER_DELETIONS=1`, which
this lane could not run. It is `DEF-CUS-5984` and it is open.

**The durable lesson is law 7's second habit asked of a helper rather than a
gate:** *what would make this check pass wrongly?* — *"the new ids are free"* is
a true statement that says nothing about whether they are still DISTINCT.
Renumber through one single-pass mapping, and assert the invariant
(**distinct ids == rows**). `G17` fails a duplicate id and would have caught it.

### ⚠ AND THE `↗ Open` HOLD EXPIRED THE SAME DAY — THE TEST SAID SO, BY NAME

`TransfersTab.test.tsx` landed asserting, by ADDRESS against the real route
table, that **nothing** matches `/transfers/:id`. A sibling lane mounted
`TRANSFER_RECORD_ROUTE` hours later and the case went red naming the column:
*"expected true to be false"*. **That is hard-won law 2's mirror working rather
than being described** — `CR-068` R3's holds rotted for days because nobody ever
wrote one, and the portal shipped a front page with two working doors out of
eight. The hold is **re-pointed, not deleted**: `GET /transfers/{ref}` is still
unmounted, so the record page draws its own not-found sentence and a row action
would send a clerk to it. The sibling's own route comment says the same and
files the door as `DEF-CUS-5982`.
