**`v2.315.2`.** This is the sibling commit the keyed-read entry above asked for
and it re-derives none of it: that entry had already established, before any
arithmetic was written, that **B4.3 ❄️ already gives the denominator** and that
the PO's *"okay we have to buld it there will ebe code to reuse"* is therefore
an instruction to BUILD rather than a request for a finance re-sign.

### THE FIGURE, BOTH WAYS, ON ONE ACCOUNT
A closing customer served **12 days** of a **30-day** monthly cycle:

| | base charge |
|---|---|
| before | **$18.50** — the whole month |
| after | **$7.40** — 12/30 × 18.50 |

**$11.10 too much, on the last bill anybody will ever read**, on a customer who
is leaving and will never query it because the bill foots either way.

### WHY NO RE-SIGN, RESTATED SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT RE-OPEN IT
B4.3 CONFIRMED: *"proration is by **calendar days**. The **base charge is always
prorated**."* **GT-3, ❄️ B5 FROZEN 2026-08-08**, states the denominator
outright: *"move-in day 16 of 30; base $30.50. Base proration **15/30** × 30.50
= **15.25**"* — numerator the days served, denominator the **cycle's own
calendar length**. A mid-cycle move-OUT is the mirror of that mid-cycle move-IN.
**No frozen figure moved and none was re-read**; only the computation was
missing. ⚠ **The inverse is the rule that matters for next time:** had B4.3 NOT
carried the term, a PO saying *build it* would be the REQUEST for a re-sign
through HUMAN-GUIDE §6 and never a substitute for one.

### WHAT WAS REUSED — NO THIRD IMPLEMENTATION
* the calendar is **`metering.period_engine.billing_period`** (*"B4.3's
  DENOMINATOR, LOCATED ON A CALENDAR"*), served through
  **`metering.selectors.billing_period_for_unit`** — `OQ-339`'s month-end clamp
  and `OQ-340`'s anchor come free;
* the factor is **`rating.proration.proration_factor`**, *"the only proration
  number in the engine"*;
* the **four-line read** is `customers.disconnects._cycle_days_for`'s, written
  again in billing only because **B1 / gate G6 forbid billing importing a
  customers module**. It carries the same scar: `A-11488`, cut 18 August on a
  $40.00 monthly base, charged **$40.00** where 18 of 31 days is **$23.23** —
  **$16.77** — until that seam was published on 2026-08-31.
* **`None` TRAVELS.** A unit on no cycle, on TWO cycles, or on a pre-`CR-029`
  cycle with no frequency or first run answers `None`, and **nothing assumes a
  30-day month**. The fallback is the window's own length, which is exactly what
  every final bill did before, so an unreadable cycle can never make a bill
  WORSE than it already was.

### THE SCOPING, WHICH WAS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY
**`final_bill.prepare_final_bill` is the ONE function that reads the cycle, and
the only bill that reaches it is the final one.** That is the scoping — not a
`kind ==` test in `one_time` that a later lane could widen by one line. Three
doors call it: the move-out wizard's preview (`preview_final_bill`), the
One-time tab's preview (`one_time.preview(kind='final')`) and the DRAFTED
invoice (`one_time._draft_for(kind='final')`), **so they move together by
construction** — the property `runs.price_account` was extracted to guarantee.
A stated `cycle_days` still wins, which is why the 27-scenario move-out suite
(it passes `cycle_days=31` explicitly) does not move.

⚠ **`OQ-242`'s WITHDRAWAL IS UNTOUCHED.** *"its proration denominator (the
current guess OVER-CHARGES while it stands). - this is not required"* (PO
2026-08-23) answered a **CYCLE-LESS** bill: an interim, catch-up, penalty or fee
run has no cycle to divide by, still charges its base whole, and
`one_time._cycle_days` still answers `None` for **every** kind including
`final`. The screen sentence was narrowed to name those four kinds and to say
the final bill is the exception, because a live capability behind a sentence
saying it does not exist is hard-won law 2's other direction
(`DEF-CWP-3925`).

### PROVED RED FIRST, IN THE HARNESS THAT RUNS IT (law 7), AND BOTH WAYS
On `config.settings.pgtest`, `JOBS_EAGER=false --reuse-db`:
* **the derivation removed** → `test_preview_tc12` (preview), `tc12c` (the
  drafted invoice) and `tc12b` (the scoping pair) all red, each on
  `assert 12 == 30`; `tc12d` stayed green, correctly, because that mutation is
  the fallback made universal.
* **the denominator widened to EVERY one-time kind** → `tc12b` red on
  `assert 30 is None`, **and `tc12` STAYED GREEN** — which is exactly the false
  pass the brief named, demonstrated rather than argued. The cycle-less guard
  `tests/test_cr029_rcw2_due_from_the_run.py::test_w2_t4__no_proration_
  denominator_is_invented_for_a_cycle_less_run` went red on the same mutation.
* ⚠ **AND THE PARITY CASES CANNOT SEE EITHER MUTATION.** `tc5` (preview total =
  drafted total) and `tc11` (the two preview doors agree line for line) stayed
  **green through both**, because both sides move together by construction.
  They guard DRIFT and they can never guard a FIGURE; `tc12`/`tc12c` are what
  guard the figure. Anyone citing the parity cases as proof of this change has
  cited the wrong ones.
* the fixture had to be moved first, and that is law 7's second shape: `a_cycle`
  builds a cycle with **no frequency and no first run**, so the denominator was
  never readable and `tc12` would have printed a full base charge whatever the
  engine did — **a check incapable of failing.** `_a_scheduled_cycle` changes
  exactly the two fields the derivation needs and nothing else.

### THREE THINGS FOUND AND FILED RATHER THAN WRITTEN IN PROSE HERE
* **`DEF-BIL-5988` — a RED nobody read, at the tip, for a day.** `tc5`, the
  parity case, counted `invoice.lines.count()` **outside** `tenant_ctx`, which
  CLEARS on exit — so it answered **0** against a preview holding 2 lines, on
  both harnesses, since `1c69a87ab` (2026-09-19). `invoice.total` is a loaded
  attribute needing no query, so the equality above it passed and hid it. Dated
  with `git log -S` and confirmed on a pristine checkout of the tip before a
  line was changed (`DEF-CWP-4187`'s habit). **Fixed here**, because the surface
  this commit had to prove could not be proved while it was red.
* **`DEF-GOV-5989` — `TC12` is THREE different tests on this one path.** The
  entry above says *"`TC12` must go on pinning `one_time._cycle_days` returning
  `None`"* (true, and it is `test_cr029_rcw2_due_from_the_run.py`'s case), while
  `preview_final_bill`'s own docstring said *"`tc12` pins it"* about
  `test_preview_tc12` — **the case this ruling required to change.** A lane
  reading the entry alone and grepping `tc12` finds the preview case first and
  is told to leave alone the very thing it was sent to build. `DEF-GOV-5229`'s
  shape in another family: every id-existence check passes because both exist.
  Both citations now name FILE and FUNCTION.
* **`DEF-BIL-5987` — the fallback is silent.** When the cycle cannot be read the
  base charge is charged whole and **nothing on the payload says why**;
  `cut_bill.CUT_BILL_DENOMINATOR_ABSENT` says exactly that one bill type along.
  Not fixed here on purpose: a second `billing_period_for_unit` read inside one
  payload is how two figures about one customer's money come to disagree on one
  screen, and the alternative widens `AccountBillingData`, a FROZEN contract
  every billing stage consumes.

### THE SCREEN NEEDED NO EDIT, AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED
`rating/pricing/stages/price_usage.py` already appends **`" (prorated)"`** to a
base line whose period is partial, and `moveShared.FinalBillLines` renders
`line.description` verbatim. So step 3 now reads **`electric base charge
(prorated) · $7.40`** with no front-end change, and a test asserts the word is
PRESENT on the final bill and ABSENT on the interim one over the same window.

### CLICKED — AND THE BETA CANNOT SHOW THE CHANGE, WHICH IS THE FINDING
Driven through the REAL route on the live beta with a logged-in session,
`GET /api/brazosbend/accounts/{id}/final-bill-preview?moved_out_on=2026-09-12`:
`AC-2026-00001` prices, and the denominator it now reports is the **CYCLE's 31
days** where before it was the **WINDOW's 43**. **The money does not move**, and
`gather._service_days` is why — it ends `return max(0, min(cycle_days, days))`,
so the days served are CLAMPED to the cycle and B4.3's factor can never exceed
1. `electric base charge $12.00` and `water base charge $8.00` before and after,
total `$160.52` both ways, on `AC-2026-00001`, `00002` and `00003`.
**Every `brazosbend` account's closing window today is that same 43-day stretch
(1 Aug – 12 Sep), so not one beta account changes price under this commit** —
which is also why nobody found the over-charge by clicking, and why the PO's
case came from a constructed scenario rather than from the beta. `tc12e` pins
the unchanged direction so a later lane removing the clamp finds out in a test
rather than on somebody's bill. ⚠ **The clamp itself is a separate, older
question and is filed as `DEF-BIL-5986`:** forty-three days of service carrying
ONE month's base charge is an under-charge of about four tenths of one, exactly
as true before this commit as after, and no signed rule covers an over-long
window either way.

Scoped to `kind='final'` BY CONSTRUCTION — `prepare_final_bill` is the only reader and the only bill that reaches it — so `OQ-242`'s withdrawal for cycle-less bills is untouched and `one_time._cycle_days` still answers `None` for every kind. ## 2026-09-20 · A PUSH TOOK ANOTHER LANE'S DEFECT ROW BY TAKING ITS NUMBER — `DEF-GOV-5990`, RESTORED

**`v2.316.3`.** Ten minutes after `3a8692a42` landed the final bill's proration,
its own post-push check found that the commit had **replaced the
transfer-record lane's `DEF-GOV-5985` with a different row carrying the same
id**. The sibling's row is back, byte-for-byte from `e0eab74ca`; this lane's is
renumbered **`DEF-GOV-5989`**, and its three citations moved with it.

### WHY EVERY CHECK IN LAW 11 PASSED OVER IT, AND THE ONE THAT DID NOT
Two lanes took `DEF-GOV-5985` minutes apart and **both were right**:
`allocate.py` asks the REMOTE, and the other lane's row was not pushed when
this one read the maximum. Law 11 already says that can happen. What it does
not say is that **`push_register_guard.py` cannot see it.** The guard refuses
when a LINE VANISHES from a shared register, and its rule is that a row's bytes
may change **as long as the ID SURVIVES** — deliberately, so that
`close_defect.py` marking a row fixed is not read as a deletion. A replacing row
carrying the same id therefore walks straight through. **So the one guard
standing between a shared register and a silent revert is blind to precisely the
collision the allocator can only warn about.**
Every other check passed too, and each was true: the file count was right, this
lane's own rows WERE present, `git show`'s hunks were all its own.
**What found it was `git diff --numstat <tip> <commit>` READ AS ARITHMETIC** —
`4 insertions, 1 deletion` on a register nobody deletes from. That is DEF-1706's
sentence (*"on a two-row append, `2 insertions, 1 deletion` is not noise — it is
a destroyed row"*) doing its job on the sixth occurrence, and it is the only
check in the whole law that could have.

### THE FIX ASKED FOR, AND WHY IT IS CHEAP
One more rule beside the id-survives allowance: **if a row's id survives but its
SECOND field — the reporter — or its DATE changes, that is not an edit to a row,
it is a different row wearing its number.** Refuse and name both. It cannot fire
on `close_defect.py`, which rewrites `status` and `fixed_commit` and never the
reporter, and it converts a warning into a refusal at the only moment the answer
is final.

| date | decision | by | refs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-20 | 🐛 **FOUND AND REPAIRED: a pathspec push replaced a sibling's defect row with one carrying the same id, and the register guard passed because the id survived.** Restored from `e0eab74ca`; this lane's row renumbered `DEF-GOV-5989` with its three citations. The guard is asked for one more rule — an id that survives while the REPORTER changes is a different row, not an edit. Found by `git diff --numstat` read as arithmetic and by nothing else. | AI (the final-bill proration lane, 2026-09-20) | `DEF-GOV-5990` · `DEF-GOV-5989` · `10-scripts/push_register_guard.py` · commit `3a8692a42` |

## 2026-09-20 · SEVEN PO RATIFICATIONS FROM ONE SITTING, WRITTEN DOWN AFTER THEIR LANES DIED

⚠ **THIS ENTRY EXISTS BECAUSE THE CONTAINER RESTARTED AND TOOK SEVEN LANES WITH
IT.** Each ruling below was put to the PO in the working session, ratified in
their own words, and handed to a lane that was told to record it *before*
building on it (step W). Every one of those lanes was killed mid-flight. Only
`d54a7f7d7` — the landlord warning — had pushed. **So all seven ratifications
existed nowhere but in a chat transcript**, which is hard-won law 9's exact
failure: *the conversation does not survive; the repo does.* They are written
here by the session that took them, rather than re-put to the PO, because
re-asking is law 13's bug and a person answering twice from memory eventually
answers differently.

**The durable lesson, and it is not "the container restarted":** a ruling
delegated to a lane is a ruling that exists only in that lane's context until
it pushes. Where a sitting produces several rulings at once, the session that
heard them writes them down FIRST and the lanes read them from here.

### 1 · THE SERVICE REQUEST ACTION BAR IS DRIVEN BY STATE

PO, verbatim: *"this is correct - fix it"*, quoting the table back in full.
This ratifies what `service_request.TRANSITIONS` already enforces and makes it
the SCREEN's contract, which it was not.

| State | Submit | Approve | Ask for more | Refuse | Park |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | ✅ the only lawful action | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Submitted | ✗ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (→ Under review) |
| Under review | ✗ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✗ |
| More info needed | ✗ | ✅ | ✅ (can ask again) | ✅ | ✗ |
| Approved | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Refused | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

**What was wrong when the PO found it:** a DRAFT offered Refuse, Ask for more,
Park and Approve — all four unlawful from `draft` — and had **no Submit control
at all**, which is the one action the table allows. The PO's words: *"this is
draft version of request - it does not allow me to submit"*. A second fault in
the same block: every disabled control gave one reason,
`customers.serviceRequest.park.terminalNoPark` — *this request is closed* — over
a draft, which is false.

⚠ **PARK IS IN THE RATIFIED TABLE AND IS NOT IN `TRANSITIONS`.** It is
deliberately absent from that table (see the comment at
`service_request_service.py:2823` — *"Putting it in the table would make it
appear in `actions_available`"*), and the screen gates it on `can_park`, which is
`not is_terminal(state)` and therefore offers it on draft, under_review and
more_info. The ratified table says **submitted only**, which is also the only
state park can act from. The screen is wrong, not the table.

### 2 · THE APPROVE DIALOG'S OUTCOMES ARE GATED BY THE EVIDENCE

PO, verbatim: *"this is correct"*. The verdicts already exist server-side in
`service_request._verdict_for`; the dialog was not reading them, so all five
outcomes were offered flat on every request.

| Outcome | Refused when | What the clerk sees |
|---|---|---|
| New connection | a premise record already exists at the address | disabled — *service exists here* |
| New connection | resolver found no premise record | **suggested** — fits the evidence |
| Move-in | never refused | offered; **suggested** when the unit is served and vacant |
| Move-out | applicant holds no live account at this address | disabled — *nothing to close* |
| Transfer | applicant holds no live account anywhere | disabled — *no live account* |
| Disconnect | never refused | offered, never suggested |

⚠ **THE PO ASKED WHETHER THE THREE REFUSED OUTCOMES SHOULD BE REMOVED FROM THE
LIST ENTIRELY, AND THE ANSWER GIVEN WAS NO, ON TWO GROUNDS.** `BR-SHL-025` is
signed: a control this state cannot honour is DISABLED WITH ITS REASON, never
hidden (the assets design states the reasoning at
`04-docs/02-decisions/16-cr028-assets-design.md:646` — *"hiding them would
misrepresent r10, disabling them tells the truth"*). And the verdicts are
**per-REQUEST, not per-outcome**: move-out is refused for THIS applicant because
they hold no account here, while for a customer actually moving out it is the
option they need. A hidden option cannot be chosen, so hiding would make
move-out and transfer requests unclassifiable.

⚠ **DISCONNECT'S "never refused" IS KNOWINGLY INCOMPLETE AND WAS NOT RESOLVED.**
It is inside `OQ-356`, which is OPEN, and `_verdict_for`'s own disconnect branch
says so by name. A recommendation was put to the PO — grey it using the same
test transfer uses, no live account anywhere — and **no ruling was given before
the restart. It stays `possible` as the server returns it.**

### 3 · A DRAFT REQUEST IS CREATED FROM THE MINIMUM, AND SAYS SO WHEN IT CANNOT BE

PO, verbatim: *"this is correct"* on the table, plus *"we should show a message
in short to user when this happens"*.

| Gate | Required before | Required now |
|---|---|---|
| Save as draft, steps 1–2 | applicant name **+ address** → *impossible* | **applicant name alone** |
| Save as draft, step 3+ | applicant name + address | unchanged |
| Staff-raised (collections) | address only → *impossible on step 1* | **nothing** |
| Submit | — | applicant name + address |
| Approve as move-in | outcome chosen; arrears clear | unchanged |

**The defect this answers:** `canCreateDraft` (`ServiceRequestCapturePage.tsx:434`)
requires `address_as_given`, and the address is captured on **step 3** while
`Save as draft` is a header action on **every** step. So the control was
permanently disabled on steps 1 and 2 for every request type in the product.
`create_request`'s own docstring says the opposite — *"a row has to exist before
step 2"* — so intent and validation contradicted each other and validation won.

**The address requirement MOVES to submit; it does not disappear.** `BR-CUS-070`
is untouched: the address is still stored verbatim, the resolver still writes
beside it, and it is still immutable after capture.

⚠ **THE TRAP THAT MUST BE PROVED BEFORE THIS SHIPS.** `BR-CUS-070` makes
`address_as_given` immutable after capture. If a draft is now created with no
address, a blank MUST NOT count as captured, or the clerk reaches step 3 and the
field is locked empty forever — a worse bug than the one being fixed, and one
that passes every unit test and fails in a browser.

**The short message** obeys B14 rule 33: an INSTRUCTION caps at six words per
sentence and RATIONALE is zero words on screen. *"Enter the name first."* It
must be VISIBLE TEXT, not the current `title` attribute, which a touch or
keyboard user never sees.

⚠ **`EP-CUS-09-service-requests.md` line 139 says the address is "required to
create". That is FALSE the moment this lands and moves in the same commit.**

### 4 · CAPTURED DETAIL REACHES THE MOVE-IN BY REFERENCE, DOCUMENTS INCLUDED

PO, verbatim: *"this is correct + Document links or details"*.

`move_in_jobs` stores `request_id` and copies no fields — its own docstring, line
~70: *"all on the request already, and this row names the request"*. So name,
kind, contact, language, DOB, driver's licence, SSN, co-applicant, address, unit,
picked premises/unit, requested start, property type, units on site and the fee
columns all reach the move-in by reference, and nothing goes stale.

Documents hang off the request by FK (`ix_sr_documents_request`) and
`outstanding_documents(request)` at `move_in_jobs.py:329` reads the condition
back through that link, so the OUTSTANDING count travels the same way.

⚠ **WHAT WAS NOT VERIFIED, AND MUST NOT BE WRITTEN UP AS WORKING:** whether the
document LINKS AND DETAIL — the files themselves — are VISIBLE on a move-in
surface. `MoveInWizard.tsx` and `moveInRequestBlocks.tsx` both mention documents;
mentioning is not rendering. The check was assigned and died with its lane.

⚠ **DONE 2026-09-20, BY RENDERING THE SCREEN — AND THE ANSWER IS HALF AND HALF
(`DEF-CUS-6002`).** Mounted at `/:tenant/accounts/:accountId/move-in?request=…`
on step 2 with two documents served carrying `file_present: true`, the
`Documents` block DOES render on the Customer step: **two rows, each with its
file name, what it proves and where it stands** — *Driving licence.pdf · Who
they are · Verified* and *Lease.pdf · Where they live · Not checked*. So the
DETAIL half of *"Document links or details"* is real and is now locked by
`MoveInWizardDocuments.dom.test.tsx`, which mounts the whole wizard at that
address and was proved capable of failing by deleting the mount at
`MoveInWizard.tsx:1569` — three of its four cases go red.

**The LINKS half is not there.** That block contains **zero anchors and zero
buttons** over two rows that have files behind them, while the server has had
`GET /service-requests/{id}/documents/{docId}/download` all along and the
request's own Documents tab uses it. A clerk on the move-in can see that a
licence was attached and cannot open it. **And the OUTSTANDING COUNT is the
same shape one layer out:** `move_reads.py:2058` serves `documents_outstanding`
on every move-in row, `MoveInsTab.tsx:354` declares it in the row type, and no
JSX in the product reads it — a field that travels and is seen by nobody, which
is `DEF-CUS-5995`'s fault in a second family on the same day.

⚠ **NOT BUILT HERE, DELIBERATELY, AND THE REASON IS A QUESTION FOR THE PO
RATHER THAN AN ESTIMATE.** The ratified words are *"Document links or
**details**"*, so details may be exactly what was meant and the absent link may
be no promise at all. Confirm which before building — and note that a download
control on this screen is a second door onto stored documents whose
authorisation and bearer-token lifetime belong to the request's own screens
(`document_store.download_url` mints a token; `service_request_documents.py:532`
calls the link *"a link that dies"*).

⚠ **THE METHOD IS THE DURABLE PART: THIS WAS MEASURED BY RENDERING, NOT BY
GREPPING.** A grep for *document* across those two files returns dozens of hits
and would have reported this working — which is how *"Export is present"*
reached a conformance document twice over a product with no export path.

### 5 · THE PARKED-DRAFTS PANEL IS REMOVED; DRAFTS BELONG IN THE LIST

PO, verbatim: *"remove it - it is anyway in the list so we dont need it
sepretely - if it is not in list add it"*.

This **AMENDS `CR-035` amendment 1** (PO 2026-08-26, *"We dont need seperate tab
for this - this will be directly on each request Request, Connect, Move IN move
Out, Trasnfr, Disconnect - seperate queue not reequired"*), which put parked work
on each tab and said nothing about a separate panel. Today's ruling settles the
placement that one left open.

**It extends a ruling the PO already made.** On 2026-09-19 they ruled (*"yes"*)
that unfinished move-outs belong on the Move-outs list, and it was built:
`move_reads.py:159` shows the window as `… ∪ wizard_parks WHERE flow='move_out'`.
So **Move-outs already does this and its panel is pure duplication**, while
**Move-ins does not** — `move_reads.py:223` says outright that a parked draft
*"is not a ROW OF THIS LIST … and it lives on the panel above this table"*.
Transfers, disconnects and new connects are unchecked.

⚠ **THE OLD OBJECTION IS OVERTAKEN, NOT IGNORED.** `parkedDrafts.tsx` §1 rejected
table rows because *"a `MoveInRow` and a `WizardParkRow` share not one field"*.
Two facts answer it: the Move-ins list ALREADY renders a service-request draft
row with em-dashes in those cells (`SR-26-0012`, account *"— draft"*, unit *"—"*,
*"Step not recorded"*), and the Move-outs list already unions parked drafts and
works. **The one constraint that survives: do not fold drafts into `totalRows`,
and do not client-side splice into a server-paged list.**

**✅ BUILT AND PUSHED THE SAME DAY — `DEF-CUS-5994`, version `2.319.0`.** The
ruling is recorded as `CR-035` **AMENDMENT 2** in `11-change-requests.md`, with
its supersession chain written out; this entry is the decision and that one is
the change record.

**WHAT THE FIVE LISTS DID AND WHAT EACH NEEDED, measured rather than assumed:**

| Flow | Before | What it took |
|---|---|---|
| **Move-outs** | already unioned `wizard_parks` (2026-09-19) — **the panel above it was pure duplication from that morning** | the mount removed; `parked_by_name` ADDED to the row; Discard re-homed |
| **Move-ins** | `move_reads.py` said outright a parked draft *"is not a ROW OF THIS LIST … and it lives on the panel above this table"* | a THIRD union arm beside draft accounts and `BR-CUS-1077` pending jobs |
| **Transfers** | no drafts at all | a two-arm union (`_page_keys` / `_fetch_page`) |
| **Disconnects** | no drafts at all | a two-arm union; a `DISCONNECT_STEP_COUNT` constant |
| **New connects** | no drafts at all | a two-arm union; metering gains its OWN `wizard_parks` seam, because it may not reach tenancy through customers |

⚠ **TWO THINGS LIVED ON THAT PANEL AND ONLY ONE OF THEM EXISTED ANYWHERE ELSE.**
`Parked by` is what amendment 1 put in place of the mine/everyone's toggle it
dissolved, and **DISCARD existed nowhere else at all** — the Move-outs row had a
Resume and no way to throw a draft away. Removing the panel without re-homing it
would have deleted a live capability from the product **with nothing to notice**,
because no gate, test or type reads a control that is no longer there
(`DEF-CUS-3653`). **That is the general trap in a *"remove the surface"* ruling
and it is worth more than this instance: before deleting a surface, list what is
ON it and find each one a home.**

⚠ **AND THE COUNT REQUIREMENT INVERTED RATHER THAN LAPSED.** Amendment 1's
requirement 2 was *"the count must not lie"*, honoured by keeping drafts OUT of
`total`. They are rows now, so `total` must COUNT them — and every list unions in
SQL, so the figure is the server's over ONE window rather than a sum computed in
two places. `NFR-3` and `NFR-5` are why it could not be a client-side splice.

⚠ **ONE DEFECT WAS FOUND ON THE WAY AND FIXED IN PASSING — `DEF-CUS-6004`.**
`transfer_reads.SORTS` published a sort named `reference` and `Transfer` has no
such field (the column is `transfer_no`), so `GET /transfers?sort=reference` had
raised `FieldError` since 2026-09-13 on a name the endpoint offers in its own
`sorts` list. **Nothing caught it because no test asks for a sort by name and a
list that opens on its default never reaches the line** — a published vocabulary
checked in one direction only.

PO, verbatim: *"fix it"*, and separately *"we will not make changes to drawing"*.
So the blueprint stands as drawn and the PRODUCT changes; where the drawing
contradicts a signed rule, the signed rule wins (B14 rule 38) and the deviation
is recorded rather than silently taken either way.

### 7 · WHAT A CLERK CAN DO TO A MOVE-OUT RECORD, BY STATE

PO, verbatim: *"this si correct"*. The record has exactly two states —
`STATE_IN_FLIGHT` and `STATE_COMPLETED` (`move_record_reads.py:317`) — and the
second axis is whether money is still unplaced.

| State | Shortfall | Actions and tier |
|---|---|---|
| In flight (parked draft) | n/a, nothing settled | `Resume →` **primary** · `Discard draft` **danger** · `Open the account →` ghost |
| Completed | settled or refunded | `Open the account →` secondary · `Open the customer →` ghost · `Open the request →` ghost |
| Completed | short, **undecided** | the three above **plus** `Tie the shortfall back ✓` **primary** · `Follow the customer ✓` secondary · `+ Payment plan` secondary · `Write it off ✓` **danger** |
| Completed | short, **decided** | the three doors, and the outcome stated as a FACT — not four live buttons |

**Three things this settles.** The four options are not permanent furniture —
they belong to one situation, money short and nobody has said whose it is, and
once decided they become a sentence. **`Write it off` is the only danger action
on a completed record and `Discard draft` the only one on an in-flight record**,
because B14 rule 6 names write-off by word and nothing else here destroys
anything; `Tie the shortfall back` moves money but is not destructive, so it is
primary. And `Open the request →` appears ONLY where the move-out came from a
service request — where it did not, it is ABSENT rather than greyed, which is a
different thing from `BR-SHL-025`'s disabled-with-reason.

⚠ **TWO FINDINGS THE TABLES DID NOT COVER.** **(a) One act, two names** — the
header reads *Tie the shortfall back* and the options row reads *Tie back to the
master*. Same act; one verb must win, in all eleven catalogues, the discipline
B14 rule 34 applies to *Recorded* / *In the books*. **(b) A money commit needs a
consequence preview** — B14 rule 11. That is the honest home for the deleted
rationale paragraph: it appears AT THE MOMENT OF THE ACT, capped by rule 33 at
two sentences of six words, rather than standing permanently on screen.

### 8 · "THE REGISTER" NAMES FOUR DIFFERENT PLACES

Found when the PO pressed the back control on an approved MOVE-IN request and
landed on the requests list: *"when i lick on register - it shoudl take me to
movein list page - instead it takes me to request list page"*. Then again on a
move-out record: *"Same problem with MOve out also - it takes you to move in list
page"*.

Four catalogue keys render the identical string `The register` and go to four
destinations — `customers.accounts.head.title` (the Accounts page, which owns
the Move-ins tab), `customers.moveRecord.back`,
`customers.serviceRequest.detail.backToRegister` (→ `/requests`) and
`customers.transferRecord.back`. **B14 rule 1 decides it: a page header's `←`
NAMES WHERE IT EXITS TO.** A control that names its destination cannot send a
clerk to the wrong tab.

**The move-out case is a plain bug, not an ambiguity:** `MoveRecordPage.tsx`
serves BOTH kinds and hardcodes `tab=move-ins` at lines 495 and 661, while the
page already reads `record.kind` at 480 and 557 and a note at 618 records that
`kind` is served and always was — *measured, not assumed*. The destination simply
ignored a fact it already held. `TransferRecordPage.tsx` hardcodes
`tab=transfers` and is CORRECT, because it only ever serves transfers.

For a service request the destination follows the OUTCOME, and
`request_jobs.py:~284` already maps each outcome to its queue
(`QUEUE_MOVE_INS = "move_ins"` and siblings) — that map is the single source; a
second one is how two screens come to disagree.

### 9 · WHAT WAS PUT TO THE PO AND IS STILL UNANSWERED

**A final bill covering 43 days charges ONE month's base charge.** Measured on
the beta 2026-09-20: every brazosbend account's closing window is 1 Aug – 12 Sep,
43 days against a 31-day cycle, and each is charged one month's standing charge.
`gather._service_days` ends `return max(0, min(cycle_days, days))`, so the
factor can never exceed 1. B4.3 is written for a PARTIAL period and says nothing
about an over-long one, so **no signed rule covers it either way**. It is filed
as `DEF-BIL-5986` with the figures; **the QUESTION — one base charge, or 1.4? —
is not on the open-questions register and must be put there.** It may well be
deliberate: a bill covering more than a cycle is arguably a back-bill's job, and
`backbill.price_day_weighted` already weights day by day for exactly that reason.

## 2026-09-20 · THE MOVE-OUT RECORD, AUDITED AGAINST ITS DRAWING AND THEN REBUILT

**The audit is `04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/conformance/move-out-record-against-its-blueprint.md`.**
Every blueprint page in it was rendered and read AS AN IMAGE (B14 rule 42), and
so was the product — the live screen was opened in a browser, which corrected
one row of the audit table and added two more. The PO's standing instruction
held throughout: *"we will not make changes to drawing"*.

### WHERE THE MOVE-OUT RECORD IS DRAWN, AND THE CITATION THAT WAS NOT

`MoveRecordPage.tsx` cited **p074** twelve times, including its Trace and
Lifecycle blocks. p074 is the **move-in WIZARD**. The move-IN record is
**p077**; the MOVE-OUT record is **p117's lower frame running onto p118**, and
its commit dialog is **p118's lower frame running onto p119**. The citation
never dangled — p074 is a real page of the same blueprint about the same flow —
which is why no id check and no reviewer caught it. `DEF-2804`'s shape, filed as
`DEF-CUS-6000`. The same file already cited p118 correctly seventeen times, so
right and wrong page numbers sat side by side and the two a next lane reads
FIRST were the wrong ones.

### THREE RATIFIED ROWS WERE ALREADY DONE, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO

§6's table read the screen as it was before the waves of 2026-09-19/20 landed.
Measured on 2026-09-20: the option meanings are **already ≤ 6 words**
(`The debt stays theirs.` is four), the ~60-word rationale paragraph is **not
rendered** — it is a code comment, correctly — and the three-line settlement is
**built and served**. Those three rows are recorded as NO WORK rather than
rebuilt. The Money row's *"neutral border, not accent"* is half done: the border
is already `border-neutral-300` and only the `Short by` figure's accent remains.

### ⚠ THE DRAWING PROMISES A CONSEQUENCE THE PRODUCT CANNOT HONOUR

p118 draws the commit dialog saying, as the first thing that happens **Now**:
*"$186.40 moves to A-10001 and A-10432 settles at zero"*.

**It does not.** `move_out_settlement.shortfall_decision` records the decision,
its resolved target, its actor and its amount, writes the `audit_log` row, and
writes **no journal line at all** — `posting: {posted: false, oq: "OQ-1250"}`.
`OQ-1250` is OPEN. An account balance is the ledger's own sum over posted
journal lines (`DEF-127`), so **a transfer nobody posts is a transfer that did
not happen** and neither balance moves.

So the consequence preview says what the act ACTUALLY does, inside B14 rule
33's two sentences of six words: **`A-10001 is chased from now. The books do not
move yet.`** Building the drawn sentence would have been hard-won law 1 — *a
comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee* — on a money path, with the
clerk as the person who found out. The drawing is unchanged; the deviation is
recorded in the conformance file and asserted by a test that fails if anyone
reinstates *"settles at zero"*.

### ONE ACT, ONE NAME — SETTLED STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN BY A SWEEP

§7 finding (a) is that one act had four spellings: the header's *Tie the
shortfall back*, the options row's *Tie back to the master*, the dialog
footer's *Tie it back to A-10001* and the catalogue's *Tie to master*. **The PO
ruled that one verb must win and did not say which**, so under hard-won law 13
that was ours to decide and write down rather than ask.

**B14 rule 33 decides it: a LABEL caps at THREE WORDS.** *Tie the shortfall
back* is four and *Tie back to the master* is five. **`Tie to master` is three,
and eleven catalogues already carry it idiomatically** — `Auf Hauptkonto`,
`Pasar a la matriz`, `親契約へ付替` — which rule 35 asks for and a fresh
English-shaped translation would have thrown away.

**And the fix is structural.** The header control and the options row now read
the SAME catalogue key, so they cannot drift; a rename moves both in one edit.
A sweep that matched four strings would have left four strings free to drift
again tomorrow, which is how the defect was born. It is proved by a mounted
case that could not have been written before it landed: the trigger and the
confirm button now share one accessible name, so an unscoped selector finds two
elements and refuses.

### ⚠ `Open the request →` CANNOT APPEAR ON ANY MOVE-OUT TODAY

§7 makes it ABSENT rather than greyed where a move-out came from no request —
a ratified exception to `BR-SHL-025`, because a counter-raised move-out has no
request to open and never will, so there is nothing to wait for and nothing to
grey. Measured: `move_records.request_id` exists and is indexed, the move-out
wizard **never writes it**, and `move_record_reads.py` contains the string
`request` **zero times**. The scenario suite has said so since before this lane
started — `E3 · raised from a SERVICE REQUEST — and the wizard never sends the
link`, red in both columns. Filed as `DEF-CUS-6001`. **A control correctly
absent on 100% of records is indistinguishable from one nobody built**, so it is
written down rather than left to be inferred.

### A BROWSER FOUND WHAT SEVENTY GREEN TESTS DID NOT

The dialog title rendered **`Tie 186.40 back?`** — a money figure with no
currency, on a money commit. Every other figure on the screen goes through
`MoneyCell`, which adds the symbol; a dialog TITLE is a plain string, so the
server's `display` (2 dp, symbol-less by design) went straight into it. `tsc`
cannot see it and no gate reads rendered output. It now goes through
`formatMoney` — the same formatter, not a second one — and a case that fails on
the bare number was proved red first. Hard-won law 6, again.

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND WHERE IT WAS PROVED

`10-scripts/move_out_scenarios.sh` before and after: **5 of 27 and 20 of 27,
identical**, the same nine rows red in the same columns — correct, because no
backend code changed. The beta is untouched, counted by the script itself in
both runs: 78 accounts, 2 move records, 74 payments, 751 journal lines, 92
invoices, 1 parked draft. Front end: 70 green across three suites, every
mutation shown red under `vitest run` first. In a browser at 1440: six controls
at the ratified tiers, and **B14 rule 6 measured on the rendered output** —
`Write it off ✓` has a transparent background at rest and fills to
`rgb(168, 22, 0)` on hover, which is the outlined-fills-on-hover danger tier
doing what the rule says rather than a class name asserted in a test.

## 2026-09-20 · `Waive it (needs a supervisor)` IS ENFORCED — THE PARENTHESIS WAS THE RULE (`DEF-CUS-5908`, `v2.319.1`)

**Found by running the move-in nineteen-scenario suite end to end against real
PostgreSQL** — `4 failed, 17 passed in 87s` at branch tip `0e7b4afd2`. Scenario
**M6** asks the PO's own question: *"Waive it — does it REFUSE a clerk who is
not a supervisor?"* It did not. A **Billing Clerk waived a `$150.00` deposit and
the entire move-in committed**: an account, one `move_in` reading, an occupied
unit, move record `MVI-26-0001` and customer `C-00002`. Five red assertions,
**one cause**.

### THE AUTHORITY, AND WHY NOTHING WAS PUT TO THE PO

Blueprint **p073** draws the deposit dropdown's help line as *"Yes — take one ·
No · **Waive it (needs a supervisor)**"*, over a screen whose actor block reads
`Sam Ortiz · Billing Clerk`. **A control whose own label names an authority is
stating a requirement, not a caption.** `DEF-CUS-5908`'s escape reason says why
it was never built: *"The authority lives only in the drawing … No rule id was
minted for it, so no gate, test or docstring names a role."*

**Who counts as a supervisor was NOT asked, because the repo has answered it
twice (hard-won law 13 — asking again manufactures inconsistency).** This
product's roles are exactly `system_admin`, `billing_clerk`, `executive`; none
is called *supervisor*. Both answers already on file:

* **`OQ-042`'s closure**, PO verbatim — *"optional toggle default ON;
  **supervisor = SysAdmin/Executive**; blocks when enabled (PO R6)"*, which
  `metering.services.cosign_read_batch` has been built on since `CR-038` W7;
* **A4's signed grid** (`identity.models.A4_MATRIX`, `BR-IDN-014`), row
  `adjustment_approval` — System Admin **Approve** · Executive **Approve** ·
  Billing Clerk **Request**.

`BR-CUS-1047` already applied that exact reading to a second control in
`apps/customers/unit_correction.py` (*"a supervisor's approval"* →
`@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN, EXECUTIVE)`, a Billing Clerk refused). **So this is
the same reading on a third control, not a new decision.**

### THREE JUDGMENTS THAT WERE OURS, RECORDED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**1 · A PER-DECISION GATE, NEVER `@require_role` ON `take()`.** A whole-function
decorator would refuse a Billing Clerk **taking an ordinary deposit** — their
daily work, and the very thing p073 draws them doing. Only the THIRD answer
names an authority, so only the third answer is gated.

**2 · `BizError(BIZ-APPROVAL)` AND NOT `AuthError(AUTH-002)`.** This is not *you
may not use this door*; a clerk may take, defer and decline a deposit on this
same step. It is *this ANSWER needs a second person*, which is what
`BIZ-APPROVAL` names. It also keeps the refusal inside the set `move_in` and
`create_account` already roll back as ONE commit (`BR-SHL-019`): the account,
the reads and the payment all go, and the clerk fixes one field with everything
else still on screen.

**3 · THE REFUSAL CARRIES A WAY OUT.** `params.accepts` names the two roles that
count, so a refused clerk is told **who to ask** instead of clicking the same
option again. The English sentence is **"Only a supervisor may waive this. Ask
one to approve it."** — two sentences, six words and six words, inside B14 rule
33 / G33's cap, and written natively into all eleven catalogues (rule 35).

### WORKED, THE FIGURE THIS MOVES

A move-in assessing **`$150.00`** and choosing *Waive it*, keyed by a **Billing
Clerk**, now refuses with `customers.deposit.waiveNeedsSupervisor` citing
`BR-CUS-025 · BR-CUS-1050`, and **writes nothing at all** — no account, no
reading, no move record, no customer link. The identical move-in keyed by a
**System Admin** commits exactly as before. `M6` reads **9/9 GREEN**.

### AND ONE THING THE ROW ITSELF HAD WRONG — `DEF-CUS-6013`

M6 could not reach green on the product fix alone: its own
`deposit_register=Expect(Decimal("0"))` **contradicts its own
`outcome=refused`** — a zero asserts an account EXISTS holding nothing. Every
other refusal row of the nineteen (`R1`–`R4`) declares `Expect(None)`, *"no
account exists to carry a register"*. The contradiction was unreachable while
M6 was red on its first dimension. Corrected to `None`, which is **stricter**:
it fails if an account exists holding anything, zero included.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO

* **It does not mint a `supervisor` role.** The move-out suite's `SH4` waits on
  `KEY_SUPERVISOR` for the write-off path and **still does**; that path is
  `shortfall_decision`, a different door, and p113's WHO CAN column is its own
  work. What this ruling establishes is that the *role question* is not what
  blocks either of them.
* **It does not change the screen.** `depositCapability.tsx` still offers
  *Waive it* to a clerk and the server refuses on commit with its sentence.
  Greying the option for a non-supervisor (`BR-SHL-025` — visible and disabled
  with its reason, never hidden) is filed, not built.

## 2026-09-20 · `Still to collect` WAS MEASURED AGAINST THE WRONG PAIR — THE ASSESSED DEPOSIT NOW HAS A COLUMN (`DEF-CUS-5909`, `v2.319.2`)

**Found by the move-in nineteen-scenario suite, scenario `M4`** — *"amount taken
LESS than the deposit — a lawful shortfall"* (`BR-CUS-090`: a shortfall is a
lawful state). It read **`95.0000`** where blueprint **p075**'s review block
computes **`125.00`**.

### THE ARITHMETIC WAS RIGHT AND THE PAIR WAS WRONG

`accounts` held **one** of the two sides. `deposit_on_file` is what ARRIVED
(`BR-CUS-670`, written when the payment clears). **Nothing at all held what the
clerk ASSESSED**, so `move_record_reads._money_taken` reached for
`plan_deposit_rules` — which `BR-CUS-1050` is explicit is a reference figure
*"reported beside what was typed"* and **never enforced**.

**Worked, on `DEF-CUS-5909`'s own case:** `$150.00` assessed · `$25.00` handed
over · `$120.00` plan standard.

    what it did      120.00 − 25.00  =  $95.00      (plan standard − taken)
    what p075 draws  150.00 − 25.00  =  $125.00     (assessed − taken)

**So the utility would have chased this customer for `$30.00` LESS than they
owe** — and a customer assessed BELOW the standard would have been chased for
more. `p075` settles it in its own three drawn lines: `Amount $150.00` ·
`Amount taken $150.00` · `Still to collect $0.00`. **The drawing requires both
sides to be readable afterwards**, which is why this is a column and not a
formula change. Read as an IMAGE, B14 rule 42.

**Why nothing caught it:** every existing test asserted the deposit REGISTER,
and the register was right all along. **None asserted the difference** —
`DEF-CUS-5909`'s own prevention line: *"Where a screen shows a difference,
assert the difference and not only its two ends."*

### THE COLUMN, AND THE THREE JUDGMENTS IT NEEDED

`accounts.deposit_assessed`, `NUMERIC(18,4)`, nullable — `customers 0059`,
HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING with its row in `09-human-review-ledger.md` (migration
ordering is 🔒).

**1 · NO BACKFILL, AND THAT IS HARD RULE 4 RATHER THAN LAZINESS.** Deriving a
figure for existing rows from `plan_deposit_rules` would write **the very
number this defect exists because we read**, into thousands of rows, where no
test would ever go red again. Every existing account reads NULL, and NULL means
*no deposit is owed* — never *nobody typed one*. The move record states the
absence.

**2 · NULL ON A WAIVED DEPOSIT, NOT THE AMOUNT WAIVED.** `BR-CUS-1050` defines
`waived` as *"one WAS assessed and somebody decided not to collect it"*. Writing
the assessed figure would make the record demand money the utility chose to
forgive — `Still to collect $150.00` on a deposit a supervisor waived that
morning. The amount and the person ride the commit's answer and the audit row,
which is where a decision with somebody behind it belongs. Written ONLY on the
`required` decision.

**3 · NO `>= 0` CHECK CONSTRAINT.** `deposit.clean()` is the one writer's gate
and already refuses a negative or non-decimal amount BY NAME with its own field
error. A constraint whose only reachable violation is a bug in that one writer
buys nothing and makes every future correction migration heavier. Declined
deliberately, stated in the migration.

**Four decimals and not six**, per hard rule 2 as re-signed 2026-08-22 — what a
NEW money column declares. `deposit_on_file` beside it stays `18,6`; the same
rule calls an existing `18,6` column a lawful container.

### AND TWO THINGS FOUND WHILE FIXING IT

**`DEF-CUS-6015` — the row asserted a SCREEN format against a WIRE payload.** It
expected `"125.00"`, so once the arithmetic was right it still read *"Still to
collect reads 125.0000, wanted 125.00"* — **a red row over the correct figure**.
Money travels this API as a string at FOUR decimals and the screen renders two:
hard rule 2 (*"round only at finalization/display"*), `BR-TEN-080` (*"exactly 2
dp on screen"*) and `MoneyCell.formatMoney`, which trims `8.2985` to `$8.30`
for exactly this reason. Corrected to `"125.0000"` — **the same number, the
serialiser's format**; the arithmetic assertion the row exists for is untouched.
B14 rule 37 again: a wireframe figure is an illustration, and so is its number
of decimal places.

**`DEF-CUS-6016` — and the screen really does print `125.0000`.** The move
record's three money facts render `value` verbatim instead of going through
`MoneyCell`, so a clerk reads four decimals and no currency symbol. **Filed, not
fixed**: it is four facts, a nullable currency and the page's own tests, and it
predates this work. It is the display half of the same rule.

### ONE MORE FIELD FOUND A HOME

`deposit.amount` — p075's `Amount` — was reported **homeless on every money
row** by the suite's field-by-field walk, because nothing served it. It is now
`money_taken.assessed`, and `MOVE_RECORD_HOMES` names it.

## 2026-09-20 · THE MOVE RECORD WAS SHOWING THE USAGE IN A COLUMN HEADED `READING`, SO A REGISTER A CLERK READ COUNTED AS UNREAD (`DEF-CUS-5910`, `v2.319.3`)

**Found by the move-in nineteen-scenario suite, scenario `S5`** — *"a DEMAND
register that cannot be read AND cannot be estimated"*. It reported
`unread_registers` = **2** over an estate with **one** unread register.

### MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — THE TWO ROWS, PRINTED

The estate stands two meters: `M-9101` electric kWh **total**, which the clerk
READ, and `M-9301` electric kW **demand**, which was left out because
`BR-MET-062` forbids estimating a demand peak. A probe against real PostgreSQL
printed what the page was actually looking at:

    meter M-9101  {'channel': 'total', 'consumption': None, 'unit': 'kWh', …}
    raw row       {'prior_value': None, 'current_value': 41680.000000,
                   'consumption': None, 'event_context': 'move_in'}
    meter M-9301  registers: 0

**`41680` is the blueprint's own drawn figure on p072/p075.** The reading was
there all along and the seam did not publish it.

### THE CAUSE, AND IT IS NOT A DOUBLE COUNT

The count was not counting one register twice. **It was counting the RIGHT
register and one that had no business being in the list.** `consumption` is the
DELTA between two reads, so an OPENING read — which has nothing before it to
subtract from — carries `None` there **however carefully the dial was read**.
`_opening_reads` took `consumption` as its `reading`, found `None`, wrote `How:
Not estimated`, and `unread` counts exactly the rows that say `Not estimated`.

So the two were the unread demand register (**correct**) and the register the
clerk had actually read (**wrong**). The move record also showed every opening
read in the product as *Not estimated* — `DEF-CUS-5910`'s headline — because the
two are the same line of code.

### THE FIX IS A PRECEDENT, NOT A NEW DECISION

**`DEF-MET-5862`, PO ruling 2026-09-19, verbatim *"fix it"*** — one selector
over, on `latest_read_for_asset`, for this exact fault. Its reasoning is
transcribed rather than re-derived: *"`consumption` is the wrong number to put
in a column headed previous reading"*, and the register's own figure *"is what
a clerk compares against the dial"*. `metering.selectors.reads_for_unit` now
publishes **`current_value` beside `consumption`**, in that shape, with the
same field name.

**Both are independently null and BOTH DIRECTIONS HAPPEN**, which is why
neither is derived from the other: a first read has a **reading and no usage**;
an ESTIMATE has a **usage and no reading** — nobody read the dial (`BR-MET-028`).
So `How` now asks whether EITHER figure arrived, and the `READING` column
carries the index alone. `Not estimated` goes back to meaning what the
blueprint says it means: **no figure of any kind**.

### WHAT ELSE MOVED, AND IT IS THE SAME LINE

`initial_reads` — the reads a clerk KEYS on step 3 — was reported **with NO HOME
on the move record for thirteen of the nineteen scenarios**. Its finder looks
for `opening_reads.rows[].reading`, which was `None` on every row for the reason
above. It is housed on all thirteen now. **Nothing was added for it**; the field
had a home and the home was empty.

`consumption` is served beside the reading rather than folded into it, so a
screen can draw an estimate (usage, no reading) and an opening read (reading, no
usage) without either pretending to be the other.

### THE SUITE

`S5` 8/9 → **9/9**. The whole nineteen: **4 failed / 17 passed** at the session's
start, **1 failed / 18 passed** after this.

## 2026-09-20 · A MOVE-IN THAT LINKED A RETURNING CUSTOMER STOPPED WARNING THAT IT COULD NOT (`DEF-CUS-5912`, `v2.319.4`) — AND THE SUITE IS 19/19

**Found by the move-in nineteen-scenario suite, scenario `S7`** — *"a returning
customer · STRONG match"*. The commit **linked `C-00001`**, stored a `strong`
match tier, kept ONE customer number across two tenancies — **and still
answered `customer_not_linked`**.

### THE REASON EXPIRED ON 2026-08-11 AND THE ENTRY RODE ON FOR FORTY DAYS

`MOVE_IN_UNAVAILABLE`'s entry read, verbatim: *"the first-class `customers`
entity has no table, so a RETURNING customer cannot be recognised — this
move-in writes a fresh contact row"*. **`customers` and `customer_accounts`
were both built on 2026-08-11** by the `US-CUS-019` lane. So on `S7` every
clause of that sentence is false: the table exists, the returning customer WAS
recognised, and no fresh contact row was written. Hard-won law 1's second form
— **a stated reason that outlived the thing it described**.

`services.REFUSED_FIELDS` was corrected for exactly this on the same day. This
tuple was not, and `MoveInWizard.tsx`'s own header has carried a note since
2026-08-25 saying so: *"FOUR user-visible sentences elsewhere still carry the
old false reason and are REPORTED, not edited."* **Reporting it is what let it
live another twenty-six days.**

### THE MECHANISM IS WORTH MORE THAN THE BUG

The list is assembled **before** the transaction, and `move_in` filtered
**exactly one** member out of it — `initial_reads_not_committed`. That single
conditional **made the whole tuple look conditional**, and the other two passed
straight through on every move-in. `DEF-CUS-5912`'s own words: *"A warning list
filtered for one member is a list nobody re-read."*

**And nothing could see it, because nothing asserted an ABSENCE.** Every test
named the codes it expected and compared them as a set — which goes red if one
DISAPPEARS and stays green forever over one that should have. The outcome is
only knowable after the commit, which is why the filter now sits there and not
beside the tuple.

### WHAT CHANGED

`move_in` drops `customer_not_linked` whenever the commit **linked OR created**
a customer. On a committed move-in that is always: `require_identity=True`
means `BR-CUS-1024` refuses an account whose customer identifies nobody (`R3`
proves it), so the un-linked case never reaches a commit.

**The entry is KEPT rather than deleted**, with its reason rewritten to
something true — *"no `customers` record was linked to this account, so nothing
ties it to the person's other tenancies"* — because it is the right thing to
say if a door ever does open an account without one. `customer_not_created`
(`BR-CUS-1023`) remains the separate, live fact for a customer number that
could not be minted.

**The eleven catalogues carried the false sentence to a clerk**, so they were
corrected too: *"No customer record was linked. This account joins no others."*
— five words and five, inside B14 rule 33's cap, written natively in each
(rule 35).

### THE TEST THAT LET IT RIDE NOW ASSERTS THE ABSENCE BY NAME

`test_us_cus_004_tc1__move_in_names_what_it_cannot_carry_over` asserted the old
set and was green throughout. Its docstring claimed *"All three need tables
that do not exist"* — false since 2026-08-11. It now asserts
`"customer_not_linked" not in codes` **by name**, so a lane putting it back has
to delete that line and read the reason first. `DEF-CUS-5912`'s prevention, in
its own words: *"Where a stated absence can close, assert that it stops being
served on the day it closes — the same discipline a hold needs."*

### WHAT IS FILED AND NOT FIXED — `DEF-CUS-6017`

**`deposit_carry_forward_unavailable` rides the same way, on the same kind of
expired reason** (*"with no customer entity there is no 'same customer' to
carry from"* — there is, and `discounts.carry_forward_offer` really answers;
`R5` drives it and gets a named refusal on a weak tier, which is the door
working). It was **not** corrected with its sibling because
`test_w5_move_in_out_cases` TC-MVI-2 asserts it present on a returning-customer
move-in, and **that test's own docstring already records the reason as stale and
out of its lane**. The assertion and the entry now hold each other up, which is
a bigger unpick than this row and deserves its own.

### THE SUITE

**`4 failed · 17 passed` at `0e7b4afd2` → `19 GREEN · 0 RED`, 21 passed, in
71s.** Four scenarios, four defects, and two more found underneath them.


## 2026-09-20 · THE TRANSFER NOW TRANSFERS THE NAME — `DEF-CUS-5971` AND `DEF-CUS-5972` (`v2.319.5`)

**The PO, walking a property sale in the live product:** *"after transfer is
completed units, assets, plans are get atatched to account of buyer"*, and
*"account number you can assign to new buyer, but in that case are you checking
account - name change to new buyer - and customer id we cannnot trsnfer to new
buyer"*.

**In plain English, with the figures.** Mrs Delgado sells 1408 Elm Street to Mr
Vasquez. The account number does not change — `BR-CUS-1030`, the account changes
HANDS rather than moving — and the **$318.40** she owed goes with the property.
Until today **every screen in the product went on calling that account Mrs
Delgado's after the sale**: the Accounts list's Name cell, the unit's Occupant
column, and the customer shown against every meter on the property. The buyer's
Customer # sat on the same row as the seller's name — one product, two answers
to *whose account is this*. **It now reads Mr Vasquez on all three.**

### THE MEASUREMENT, BOTH NUMBERS, EITHER SIDE

`./10-scripts/transfer_scenarios.sh`, on real PostgreSQL, at `fe00d24f7`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| pytest | **19 failed · 9 passed** | **2 failed · 26 passed** |
| NO FAILURE TODAY | **6 of 25** | **23 of 25** |
| COMPLETE TODAY | **0 of 25** | **0 of 25** |

**Quote both.** `0 of 25` is unchanged and that is honest: a row is COMPLETE
only when nothing is left unasserted, and every row is still waiting on the
three keystones this lane did not build — the seller's link, the message and
the record read.

### WHAT WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS ONE CONDITION

`reassign_account` rewrites `customer_accounts` and never touches `contacts`.
Every display name in the product is `primary_contact_name`, which reads
`contacts.full_name`. The account changed hands in one table and went on
announcing the seller from another.

`_carry_buyer_onto_account` already intended to fix this and said so in its own
words — *"THE NAME GOES LAST AND ALWAYS, BECAUSE THE ROW IS THE SELLER'S"* —
but the write sat under `if contact_changes:`, which is true only when the
buyer presented an **email, a telephone number or a date of birth**. All three
are OPTIONAL under `BR-CUS-1081` (*"REQUIRED: three, and the ruling added
none"*). **So a lawful sale to a buyer identified by a phone and nothing else
wrote nothing at all**, and the name that appeared afterwards depended on which
optional box a clerk happened to fill in. That is hard-won law 1 — a comment
claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee — inside the function that states it.

### THE JUDGMENT: THIS FIXES THE TRANSFER, IT DOES NOT RE-HOME `contacts`

`DEF-CUS-5971` offers three readings and its own prevention column calls option
(b) — every name-bearing selector reading the LINKED CUSTOMER and falling back
to the contact — the one that costs nothing a clerk can see. **It is also B2 r9
#1's Eng-Lead disposition, it touches 42 call sites in four modules, and it is
not one lane's to take.** What was done instead is narrower and is already
signed: `BR-CUS-1081` puts the buyer's details on `contacts` through this exact
door, and the only thing that changed is that the buyer's NAME lands whether or
not they also gave an optional field. **The seam is still there.** Option (b)
remains the right long answer and `DEF-CUS-5971` stays open against it.

**AND THE HALF THAT DOES NOT MOVE IS NOW SAID OUT LOUD.** A buyer who gave no
email and no telephone number leaves the account's contact details reading the
SELLER's, so the bill email still goes to the person who sold the house. That
was true before today and silent; the commit now returns
`contact_details_still_the_sellers` beside the mailing-address absence that was
already there.

### `DEF-CUS-5972` — A GUARD THAT COULD NOT FIRE, IN PRODUCTION CODE

Selling to the person who **already owns it** was not refused. The guard
compared the customer id `link_customer` RETURNED against the seller's — and a
phone cannot reuse a customer (`identity_match.REUSE_ID_FIELDS` is `(ssn,
driving_licence)` for a person), so a phone-identified buyer always got a NEW
number, the ids always differed, and the guard always passed. The sale went
through, the seller's link was deleted, and **one person ended up holding two
Customer #s for one property — with their history hanging off the number that
had just been unlinked.** Hard-won law 7's *structurally incapable of failing*,
outside a test, for nineteen days.

**The question is now asked BEFORE anything is resolved, against this account's
own customers, and the criterion is a judgment recorded here rather than
inferred:** the presented buyer is refused when the **name AND at least one
other comparable fact** agree with a customer this account is already linked
to.

* A name alone is never enough — *"A. Kulkarni and Ajinkya Kulkarni are two
  landlords and nothing objects"* (`CR-056` §4), and refusing a sale over a
  shared surname would be telling somebody they may not buy a house.
* An identifier alone is never enough — a household shares a telephone line.
* **It is deliberately weaker than `BR-CUS-089`'s `strong`, and that is the
  point.** `strong` needs name + date of birth + one government ID and decides
  whether MONEY MAY FOLLOW somebody. This decides whether to refuse an ACT,
  which a clerk recovers from in thirty seconds because the refusal names the
  Customer # that matched and what it matched on. Requiring `strong` would have
  left the guard exactly as unfireable as it was.
* The id-equality guard is KEPT beside it. It catches a different case — a
  buyer whose government identifier matches a customer this account has no link
  to — and removing it would trade one unfireable guard for another.

### THE PO'S TWO OTHER SENTENCES, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**1 · The plan.** *"plans are get atatched to account of buyer"*. **It was
already right and nothing was testing it from the account's side.** Under
`BR-CUS-1030` the account does not move, so the plan does not change BECAUSE
the account does not change: `accounts.unit_id` → `units.rate_plan_id` →
rating's `plan_ref` is a walk along foreign keys that **reads no name at all**.
That is exactly why this dimension never broke while its two neighbours broke
36 times between them — they resolve a NAME and it does not. The fix here was a
TEST, not code: `the_accounts_plan_changed` now asserts what
`GET /accounts/{id}` actually serves as `unit_plan`, beside the
`plan_on_unit_changed` that already watched the unit. Green on all 25.

**2 · Two people, two numbers.** *"customer id we cannnot trsnfer to new
buyer"*. **The cheapest way to make every name assertion go green at once is to
write the buyer's details onto the `customers` row the account already points
at** — it works instantly on every surface, and it MERGES TWO PEOPLE INTO ONE
and destroys the seller's identity with no error anywhere. Nothing asserted
against it before today. Two new checks do:
`the_seller_and_the_buyer_are_two_numbers` (two Customer #s, both on file, both
different) and `the_sellers_own_record_still_names_the_seller`. **Both were
proved RED by writing that merge into `reassign_account` and watching it
fail**, then restored.

### PROVED RED FIRST, IN THE HARNESS THAT RUNS IT

`06-backend/.venv/bin/python` under `config.settings.pgtest` — never
`python3 <file>`, and never SQLite (law 14).

* With the name write put back under its old condition, `SL1` goes red
  verbatim: `✗ GAP identity: … the_account_name_is_the_buyers: want True, saw
  False`, beside the two original signatures `assets_and_account:
  names_the_buyer: want True, saw False · names_the_seller: want False, saw
  True` and the same pair on `occupancy_at_unit`.
* With the merge written in, `SL1` goes red on
  `the_sellers_own_record_still_names_the_seller`.
* Restored: `SL1` green, `1 passed` in 8.06s.

### THE BETA WAS NOT OPENED, COUNTED BOTH SIDES

`accounts 78 · transfers 0 · customer links 57 · customers 55 · payments 74 ·
journal lines 751 · invoices 92 · queued messages 420 · parked drafts 1` —
identical before and after every run.

### FILED AND NOT FIXED

* **`DEF-SHL-6019`** — `test_both_the_transfer_and_the_disconnect_series_are_catalogued`
  has been RED since **2026-09-16**: the number-series catalogue holds 30 names
  and the test pins 29. Dated with `git log -S`, not called pre-existing. It is
  a canary doing its job and nobody read it for four days.
* **`DEF-CUS-6020`** — `RF2` declares that the occupant is NOT the buyer, and
  in `RF2` the buyer's name IS the seller's name, so the row asserts a
  distinction its own fixture removed. Red identically before and after.
* **`DEF-CUS-6021`** — `PR2` sells a unit with no meter and asserts every asset
  names the buyer; with no assets that can never be true. Red identically
  before and after.

**Those two are the whole of the remaining `2 failed`, and neither is a product
fault.** They were not weakened to make the number look better — the suite's own
instruction, and the reason `23 of 25` rather than `25 of 25` is the honest
figure to quote.

## 2026-09-21 · THE DISCONNECT WIZARD KEEPS TWO ACTIONS — PARK AND COMPLETE

**`CR-125-BRC07` · `BR-CUS-1030` is untouched; this is the disconnect wizard
(`S90`), blueprint p135–141.**

### THE RULING, VERBATIM

Put to the PO against a measured table of every control on the five-step
disconnect wizard, the PO ruled:

> *"we need to keep only park, complete - two action only"*

The reading was then put back to them in plain English as a five-row table —
what each control becomes, not which id it carries — and the PO confirmed it in
their own words:

> *"this si correct"*

⚠ **THAT IS A COMPLETE ANSWER AND IS RECORDED AS ONE.** `CLAUDE.md` law 13 names
this exact form — *"a ruling that arrives in a form we did not expect is still a
ruling … `this si corerct` … are all complete answers"* — and asking for a tidier
restatement of a decision already made is the same bug wearing better manners.

### WHAT WAS SHOWN, AND WHAT IT MEANS

| Control | Ruled | What it becomes |
|---|---|---|
| **Park** | KEPT | The one way to put a half-finished disconnect down. **`Save & exit` merges into it** — they were two names for one act |
| **Complete** | KEPT | The danger-tier commit. Creates the case with its date, services, deposit election **and now the proof of service** |
| `Save & exit` | REMOVED | folded into Park |
| `Record the proof` | REMOVED as a separate act | proof becomes data the wizard carries to Complete, not its own immediate write |
| `Back` / `Continue` | KEPT | navigation, not actions |

**Five action controls become two.** Nothing signed ever gave this wizard five;
it grew them, which is why this is a CHANGE and not a correction.

### THE CONSEQUENCE THAT WAS SHOWN BEFORE THE CONFIRMATION, NOT AFTER

⚠ **`Record the proof` writes IMMEDIATELY today, and folding it into Complete
moves a legal record.** This was put to the PO in the same breath as the table,
because a signature covers only what was shown (HUMAN-GUIDE §6):

*"No proof, no cut" is NOT weakened* — `assert_service_proved` still demands the
same facts in the same call, server-side. **What changes is that a clerk who
abandons the wizard halfway no longer leaves a proof row behind.** The PO
confirmed with that stated.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE

Neither of the two figures blocking this screen was put to the PO here and
neither may be chosen by a lane (law 13 — a fact only they hold):

* **A reconnection costs `$75.00`** in the drawing and in the signed worked
  figure, and **`$45.00`** in the seeded catalogue under a different code name —
  the completion path looks up `CC-RECON`, the seed spells it `RECON`. **Three
  sources, two disagreements, and every cut refuses today.**
* **`Case raised by`** and **`oldest debt in days past due`** are both drawn and
  have **no source at all**. Two columns would be needed; neither is invented.

### WHY THIS IS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE REPLY THAT ANSWERS IT

Law 10's test is not *"was a decision made"* but *"would the next agent, with
only the repo, build the same thing?"* A lane is building this wizard right now
in its own worktree; the ruling reached it as a message, which exists only in
that lane until it pushes. This row is the copy that survives.

## 2026-09-20 · THE DOCUMENT CAPTURE IS A COMPONENT — B14 RULE 43'S SECOND EXTRACTION

PO, verbatim: *"document sotrage - we need to make it compoentn so thatw e cna
use it in other palces also"* and *"make them coponents - dont write stand alone
code , engineer it"*. `applicantCapture.tsx` was the first extraction; this is
the second, and it was the same shape one screen over.

**WHAT SHAPE IT WAS FOUND IN — measured, not assumed.** Not a component. The
document capture was **~330 lines of JSX plus eight `useState` hooks and an
`addDocument` function written inline** inside
`07-frontend/src/features/customers/ServiceRequestCapturePage.tsx`, a 4,324-line
file, importable by nothing. Rule 43's test is ADDRESSABILITY rather than line
count, and a sibling screen needing the block had exactly two options: copy it,
or ask for a backend it already had.

**THE BACKEND WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM AND NOTHING WAS ADDED TO IT.**
`apps/tenancy/document_storage.py` already had `store`, `for_source` and
`download_url` with object-lock retention, and two callers to copy the posture
from. No bucket call, no presigner, no endpoint was written by this lane.

| Date | Decision | Source | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-20 | ✅ **BUILT: `07-frontend/src/components/documents/` — the drawn table, the four chips, the `Attaching one` form and its two buttons, the field set and the filter**, each exported on its own so a host that draws it differently takes the form without forking the block (rule 43 clause 3). `ServiceRequestCapturePage.tsx` renders it and is **−327 lines** | PO 2026-09-20, *"make them coponents"* | B14 rule 43 · `components/documents/index.ts` |
| 2026-09-20 | 📐 **JUDGMENT: the catalogue keys stay `customers.serviceRequest.*` and no second namespace is minted.** They are the product's DOCUMENT vocabulary — `Attach a file`, `Nothing attached`, `What it proves` — answered in all eleven catalogues and already read by three screens. A second namespace is two spellings of one sentence, which rule 34 refuses; renaming the existing ones moves every citation in eleven catalogues at once and belongs to whoever rules on the namespace | the session; recorded rather than asked (law 13) | B14 rules 34 · 35 · `documentCapture.ts` header |
| 2026-09-20 | 📐 **JUDGMENT: `SERVICE_REQUEST_DOCUMENT_ACCEPT` becomes the kit's `DOCUMENT_ACCEPT`, and `ACCOUNT_DOCUMENT_ACCEPT` is left alone.** The old docstring refused to import the ACCOUNT door's constant, which still stands — it was never an objection to a SHARED one. The account door is another lane's file and is named in the handover | the session | `BR-SHL-031` · `documentCapture.ts` |
| 2026-09-20 | 📐 **JUDGMENT: a document with a file can now be OPENED from the capture table, reversing a stated choice on that screen — and the reason it gave is the part that changed.** The inline block said *"there is no open control, which is the drawing's choice and not an omission"*: p078 draws the file as TEXT, and *"the dev storage backend mints `file://` URLs a browser cannot follow, so a link here would be dead in every local walkthrough and alive only in production — the worst of both"*. The first half is rule 37's territory (a drawing shows a cell; it does not forbid a control). **The second was a real objection and is ANSWERED rather than ignored** — `openStoredDocument` checks the scheme and refuses an unfollowable link BY NAME, so the control is never silently dead. It is drawn only over `file_present`, never over the six seeded rows of `DEF-CUS-5872` | the session | `openStoredDocument.ts` · `DEF-CUS-6022` |
| 2026-09-20 | 🐛 **FOUND: `GET /service-requests/{id}/documents/{docId}/download` has been live since 2026-09-19 and was called by NOTHING.** Three front-end surfaces draw these rows and not one could open a file — including the request detail's Documents tab, which offers **Verify and Reject on a document it gives no way to read**. That is hard-won law 2's mirror with the control missing rather than dead, and no check in this repo asks whether a live endpoint has a caller | the session | `DEF-CUS-6022` |
| 2026-09-20 | 📐 **JUDGMENT: `formatBytes` is spelt twice today, it is STATED rather than hidden, and a drift guard holds the two together.** The kit is where a formatter every document screen needs belongs, but it lives in `AccountDocumentsTab.tsx`, another lane's file; and a kit component importing a whole account TAB to borrow one function is a worse coupling than the one it cures. The guard compares both on a table of byte values and is deleted WITH the duplicate, not before | the session; the same idiom `applicantCapture.dom.test.tsx` uses | `DocumentCapture.dom.test.tsx` |

**TWO OF THIS LANE'S OWN CHECKS COULD NOT FAIL, AND THE LAW 7 PROOF IS WHAT
FOUND THEM.** Both were written carefully and both passed green over the exact
fault they existed to catch:

* The formatter drift guard held nine byte values and **not one distinguishes
  `Math.round` from `Math.ceil` in the KB branch**, so a real change to the
  rounding passed. `1_100` and `2_100` are in the table now because they do.
* `expect(page).toContain("<DocumentCapture")` **passed over a page renamed to
  `<DocumentCaptureXX`** — the substring survives the very mutation that proves
  a host stopped rendering the component. It is matched to its own boundary now.

The habit that found both is the second of law 7's three: *ask what would make
this check pass wrongly*, not only what makes it fail.

**THE ADOPTION RECORD, BECAUSE A HOLD NEEDS A TEST THAT FIRES WHEN IT EXPIRES.**
Four more surfaces draw documents and none uses the kit yet; two are other
lanes' files. `DocumentCapture.dom.test.tsx` names every host that imports it
and goes **RED, naming the file**, the day one more does — so *has the second
host arrived* belongs to somebody instead of nobody, which is the question that
cost the customer portal six working doors.

## 2026-09-20 — A LADDER STOPPED BY HAND GETS ITS OWN SENTENCE, AND TWO CHEAPER HOMES WERE REFUSED

**`CR-125-BRC07`, the disconnect wizard built to blueprint pages 135–141.
Ours to decide, recorded rather than asked** — hard-won law 13: it collides with
no signed rule, moves no ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure and is not a fact only the PO
holds, so a question here would have been the failure to make a decision.

### WHAT WAS WRONG

Blueprint p137 draws step 2's *"Or stop the ladder without a protection"* as
three radio reasons **and a free-text line under them labelled `What happened`**,
holding *"Customer disputes INV-26-0411 on a meter reading"*, captioned
*"Recorded with the act and with who did it."*

**There was no parameter and no column.** `disconnects.stop_by_hand` took
`reason` — one of three CODES — and nothing else. The wizard asked for the
sentence and dropped it, which is worse than not asking for it.

### THE DECISION — A COLUMN OF ITS OWN (`disconnect_cases.stopped_note`)

**Option (a), `audit_log` alone — REFUSED.** The actor and the act are already
audited, so this looks like the free option. `audit_log` is **pruned on a
retention schedule** (CLAUDE.md hard rule 4's own note; whether such a row may be
EXEMPT is `OQ-1340`, still OPEN). The sentence explaining why a utility stopped
chasing a real debt is exactly what a regulator or an auditor asks for a year
later, and a home that ages out is not a home.

**Option (b), reuse `stopped_reason` — REFUSED, and it is the one that looks
cheapest.** That column holds a CODE from a closed set of three, and
`stop_by_hand` refuses anything outside it BY NAME so that *"a fourth way to stop
chasing a real debt needs a ruling"*. Letting prose into the same column would
**delete that guard in the act of reusing it** — the day somebody writes a
sentence into it, the check that refuses a fourth reason stops working. A closed
vocabulary and a free-text field cannot be the same column.

**Option (c), a column of its own — TAKEN.** It is the shape this module already
uses one class over: `AccountProtection.note` is the same fact about the same
kind of act, so it adds no new idea to the schema.

### THE WORKED EXAMPLE THAT WAS WRITTEN DOWN

A clerk stops case `DSC-26-0003` on 11 May 2026, picks **Disputed**, and types
*"Customer disputes INV-26-0411 on a meter reading."* The case records the date
(`stopped_on`), the reason code (`stopped_reason`) and the sentence
(`stopped_note`); the audit row separately names who did it. The caption's *"with
the act and with who did it"* is satisfied by the three together.

### NULLABLE, AND NOT MADE REQUIRED — THAT IS PART OF THE DECISION

Every case stopped before today has no note, and a backfill would be fiction
(hard rule 4: no migration may write one). **Requiring a note would REFUSE a
stop**, and on this ladder a refused stop means a disconnection carries on
because a clerk had nothing to type. The note is evidence; it is never a gate.
An empty or whitespace note stores as NULL rather than `""`, because *nobody
wrote a note* and *somebody wrote nothing* are one fact and two spellings of one
fact is how a screen renders a blank line where it meant an absence.

**Migration:** `customers/0061_cr125_brc07_disconnect_stopped_note` — one
nullable `TEXT` column, no index, no default, no check, no backfill. 🔒
HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING, row in `12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md`.

### AND WHAT THIS DECISION DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SETTLE

The same drawing's `Case raised by` row has the same shape of problem — a fact
the screen wants, living only in a pruned log — and it was **NOT** decided the
same way. It is `OQ-CUS-12517` and is OPEN, because *who raised a case* is a
statement the regulator-facing record makes about itself, and whether it may live
only in an activity log is a product judgment about durability rather than a
storage choice. The difference between the two: this note is a NEW fact that has
nowhere else to go, and that one is an EXISTING fact whose only home is being
questioned.
