## 2026-09-20 · A TRANSFER MESSAGE NAMES ITS PARTY IN THE SNAPSHOT, NOT IN A NEW COLUMN

**The judgment:** a property sale now queues three messages on commit — two to
the buyer, one to the seller — and **the seller's message is told apart from
the buyer's by `outbound_messages.recipient_snapshot`, not by a new recipient
column.** `DEF-CUS-5949`, built by the transfer backend lane.

**Nothing was put to the PO.** This is ours to decide and write down (hard-won
law 13): no signed rule is reversed, no ❄️ FROZEN figure moves, and nobody but
us holds the fact. The PO's own two words on this wizard — *"no commucation
options"* — asked for the messages; how a row says who it is for is engineering.

### THE PROBLEM, IN ONE SENTENCE

`outbound_messages` addresses an **account**, and `BR-CUS-1030` makes a sale a
reassignment — the account stays and its **customer** changes. So from the
instant a sale commits, *the account* means *the buyer*, and a letter telling
the **seller** they no longer hold it cannot be told apart from the buyer's by
`account_id`. There is no customer column on that table and never has been.

### THE TWO OPTIONS, AND WHY THE CHEAPER ONE IS ALSO THE HONEST ONE

**(a) — CHOSEN. The seller's row carries `account_id` NULL and names its party
in `recipient_snapshot`.** Three fields: `party` (`seller` or `buyer`), `name`,
and `customer_id`. `BR-TEN-017` already makes that payload the record of who a
message was addressed to as it stood at queue time, which is exactly the
question being asked, and `service_request_events` already does it one kind
over for the same reason — an applicant has no account either. No migration, no
new index, and every existing dashboard can read it.

**(b) — REJECTED. A `recipient_customer_id` column on `outbound_messages`.** It
would be a 🔒 migration with a review-ledger row, on a table eleven writers
share, to record a fact the JSON payload was built to record — and it would
still answer nothing for the 373 rows already queued, because nobody could
back-fill who they were for.

**⚠ WHAT WOULD MAKE (b) RIGHT LATER, STATED NOW SO NOBODY REDISCOVERS IT:** a
screen that LISTS *every message ever addressed to this customer*. A JSONB read
is the wrong index for that, and a column becomes right. That is a new ruling
with a migration; it is named in `transfer_events.py` so the next lane inherits
the trade instead of re-deriving it.

### THE THREE MESSAGES, AND WHY THE KEY IS DERIVED

Buyer: a change-of-ownership **email** and a meter-visit **SMS** (the buyer is
the one who has to let a technician in). Seller: a change-of-ownership
**email**.

The queue's idempotency key is `(tenant, source_type, source_id, channel,
copy_no)`. **A sale has exactly one occasion row and three messages come off
it**, two of them on the same channel — so keying all three on `transfer.id`
would meet the unique index and **silently dedupe the seller's letter into the
buyer's**, reporting `created=False` while the clerk is told it was queued.
That is `move`'s own documented trap one kind over.

So `source_id` is `uuid5(transfer.id, party + channel)` — **derived, not
minted**. A replayed commit computes the same three keys and writes nothing
(CLAUDE.md rule 6), three messages off one sale cannot collide, and the real
transfer id travels in `render_context["transfer_id"]` so nothing is lost.

### ⚠ QUEUED IS NOT SENT, AND THE FIGURE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN QUOTED

Counted on the beta (`brazosbend`) on 2026-09-20, before this work:
**373 messages are queued in this product and not one has ever been sent** —
`sent_at` is null on every row, and `BR-NOT-013` is why: there is no provider
adapter on email, SMS or print. These three join that number; they do not
change it. Every sentence in the seam, the module, the catalogue card and the
response says *queued*. The scenario suite asserts `sent: 0` on purpose.

### WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE

* **No `rule_catalog.EVENTS` row, so no `event_key`.** A tenant toggle for a
  class of message is a SET-12 row, and minting one here would put a switch on
  a Settings screen that no ruling asked for.
* **No entry in `CHANNEL_FLOOR_BY_SOURCE`.** `BR-NOT-024` names six source
  kinds print is the floor on and a transfer is none of them. A lane may not
  widen a signed rule by editing a dictionary — the `move` precedent, where the
  merge lane put it to the PO instead. **The consequence is stated rather than
  hidden: a utility gets an email and a text and no posted letter.**
* **No wording was claimed as ratified.** The three bodies are seeded defaults
  a tenant edits, carrying their own `_LANE_AUTHORED` source string rather than
  borrowing the PO's 2026-08-17 ruling. `OQ-CUS-12524` is where the PO settles
  the words.
* **No figure in any of the three bodies, and the palettes cannot express one.**
  A balance written into a row queued today and delivered whenever an adapter
  lands is wrong by exactly the amount the account has moved since.

### THE TWO CHECKS THAT COULD NOT PASS, AND WHAT FIXED THEM

Both are hard-won law 7's third shape, in the scenario suite rather than in a
gate, and **both were written honestly and were true the day they were
written** — which is what makes them worth recording.

1. `queued_to_the_seller` was a hardcoded `0` under a comment reading *"always
   zero, and it is a measurement rather than an assumption"*. Against a
   declared `1` it reads WAITING for ever and becomes a permanent FAIL the
   moment the keystone lands. **It now counts rows whose snapshot names the
   SELLER'S OWN CUSTOMER ID** — the id and not the word `seller`, so a row
   whose writer merely typed the word cannot satisfy it.
2. `_a_transfer_message_kind_exists()` enumerated five seam constants **by
   hand** and asked whether any contained `transfer`, so a sixth name could
   never reach it. **It now enumerates the seam's `WRITE_*` constants and then
   RESOLVES them**, which is the harder half: a published constant whose
   function does not exist is hard-won law 2, and a check reading only the
   constant would go green over silence.

**Both were proved RED in the harness that runs them**, not through a direct
module call: addressing the seller's letter to the buyer's customer id sent
`queued_to_the_seller` back to 0, and renaming the notifications function while
leaving the seam constant in place sent `queued_by_the_commit` 3 → 2 and
`a_transfer_message_kind_exists` True → False in the same run.

## 2026-09-20 · A COMMITTED SALE CAN BE READ BACK — `GET /transfers/{ref}`, AND WHY IT IS ITS OWN URL MODULE

**The judgment:** the transfer record read is mounted in a module of its own,
`apps/customers/transfer_record_api.py`, included in `config/urls.py` **after**
`transfer_disconnect_api`. Built by the transfer backend lane. Nothing was put
to the PO: no signed rule moves and nobody but us holds the fact.

**The gap it closes** was ranked first of everything the transfer surface still
needed, in the conformance file's own words: *"a clerk can make a sale and then
has no way to read it back."* `TransferRecordPage.tsx` has existed for days and
has drawn its NOT-FOUND branch at every address, because nothing answered.

### ⛔ WHY NOT ONE LINE IN `api.py` — IT IS AN ORDERING FACT, NOT A PREFERENCE

`config/urls.py` includes `apps.customers.api` **before**
`apps.customers.transfer_disconnect_api`, and Django matches by PATH and not by
method — *"a duplicate path SHADOWS rather than merges"*, which that file says
in its own words. `transfers/commit` and `transfers/buyer-preview` are
two-segment paths and so is `transfers/<str:ref>`.

**So declaring the route in `api.py` would have swallowed `POST
/transfers/commit`**: every property sale in the product answering 405 from a
GET-only view. `transfer_disconnect_api.py` predicted it exactly, in a comment
above its own list — *"the next lane to add `transfers/<id>` would create that
collision silently"* — which is why that file is worth reading before adding a
route to this resource and why this one is included last.

### THE ADDRESS IS THE REFERENCE (B14 rule 31), AND THE ID IS A WAY IN

`TRF-26-0001` is what a clerk quotes down a phone (`OQ-426`, PO 2026-08-27).
The layer below accepts a uuid as a FALLBACK because a tenant provisioned
before the `transfer` series was seeded has sales with `transfer_no = NULL`,
which would otherwise be unreadable for ever — `transfer-record-what-is-
durable.md` §1 asks for exactly that. **It is a way IN and never a way to
DISPLAY one:** `reference` still serves the server's own stated absence.

### WHAT THE RECORD CAN ANSWER TODAY, AND WHAT IT STATES AS ABSENT

The durability measurement of this morning named FOUR drawn facts with no
durable home. **One of the four closed the same day:**

* ✅ **`Sold by` IS SERVABLE.** That file called the seller this page's
  blocker, because the commit deleted the seller's link and overwrote
  `transfers.customer_id`. Both halves were reversed by `customers/0060`
  hours later: the link ENDS rather than being deleted, `customer_id` keeps
  naming the seller permanently, and the buyer got a column of its own. Its
  instruction to put `Sold by` under *What this record does not say* is
  **SUPERSEDED**, and its warning *do not add `transfers.sold_by_customer_id`*
  was honoured — the column that arrived names the BUYER.
* ⛔ **the balance and the deposit as they stood, `Buyer matched or created`,
  `Committed by` and the ledger's unbroken span** are STATED ABSENCES, each
  with its own code and its own sentence.

**The drawing forbids the obvious workaround and the read obeys it.** Every
figure is *"as it stood on the day, not as it stands now"*, so reading today's
`accounts.balance` and labelling it the sale's figure would be wrong by exactly
the amount the account has moved since — a wrong number on a money path, worse
than a blank.

**`Committed by` is the one absence worth arguing separately:** the name IS in
`audit_log`, and `audit_log` is pruned on a retention schedule. CLAUDE.md hard
rule 4 forbids any document, screen or docstring describing that as a permanent
record, so the record states the absence rather than scraping a log that will
one day answer differently.

### THE TWO `$0.00` ROWS ARE A PROHIBITION, NOT A MEASUREMENT

`BR-CUS-085`: *nothing is refunded and re-collected*. `Refunded to the seller`
and `Re-collected from the buyer` are served as `0.0000` **from the rule**, and
a non-zero there would mean the rule had been broken and the screen must show
it. Rendering them as an absence would say *"we did not check"* about the one
fact this page exists to prove. `taken_on` is **not** added up — two absences
do not make a total, and doing that arithmetic on a read is what hard rule 2
and B4 put on the other side of the wire.

### THE THIRD AND FOURTH CHECKS THAT COULD NOT PASS

`_a_transfer_read_door_exists()` read **one module's** `urlpatterns` and
demanded a pattern spelled `transfers/<str:transfer_id>`. Both of the things
that actually shipped were outside what it could see, and for reasons it could
not have known — the route had to be in another module because of the ordering
above, and B14 rule 31 makes the parameter a reference rather than an id.
**It now asks the ROUTER** (`django.urls.resolve`), so no module is excluded,
the include order is exercised rather than assumed, it resolves **the row's own
reference** rather than a literal, it compares the view by identity, **and it
CALLS the read and requires p133's four sections** — because a door that opens
onto a 500 is not a door.

And `queued_by_the_commit` counted *everything queued between the two counts*,
so `CT1` — whose road is `sell_then_move_out` — reported **5** against a
declared 3: the sale's three plus a move-out's own final-bill letter and its
print-floor copy, four months later. It now scopes to the SOURCE KIND, read off
the module that owns the vocabulary rather than typed as a literal.

**Both proved RED in the harness that runs them:** removing the include from
`config/urls.py` and renaming one drawn section each sent
`readable_back_through_a_door` back to False.

### WHAT IS OWED NEXT, NAMED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED

`transfer-record-what-is-durable.md` §4's two nullable `NUMERIC(18,4)` columns
(`balance_at_sale`, `deposit_at_sale`) and a nullable `buyer_was_matched`, all
written ONCE at commit as new facts. `transfers` is none of hard rule 4's four
tables. **No back-fill for any of the three** — nothing in this database can
say what a past sale's balance was, and a migration that guessed would put an
invented figure on a record a regulator may read.

## 2026-09-21 · FOUR NEW CONNECT RULINGS FROM ONE SITTING

**All four were put to the PO in plain English with a real case and options, and all
four came back as a choice.** They are written here before anything is built on them —
law 9, and law 10's test: *would the next agent, with only the repo, build the same
thing?*

---

### 1 · THE BUILD RECORD IS **ONE DESTINATION, MADE COMPLETE** — `OQ-MET-12520` CLOSED

**The question.** The PO ruled on 2026-09-04, verbatim: *"you are duplicating this —
there is nothing called as connections; Connection = Account only — you cannot have two
different screen — this is an integration problem."* A separate New Connect detail
screen was deleted under it. **Blueprint pages 100–104, published 2026-09-17 —
thirteen days LATER — draw a six-tab build record anyway.** Two live authorities
pointing opposite ways, and `B14` rule 41 makes the blueprint the specification.

**Three options were put, with a real case** — *a developer finishes a 7-unit apartment
block; today a clerk reads its facts and eight actions on the property's Build tab, the
nine jobs on its Work orders tab, and the money on the account: three places.*

**THE PO CHOSE C.** Their words, quoting the option back: *"C. Your ruling's words were
'you cannot have two different screen' — that's about duplication, not about the
content. The drawing isn't asking for a duplicate; it's asking for completeness we
don't have. C gives you both: nothing duplicated, and the clerk stops hopping three
places."*

**SO:** ⛔ **NO SECOND SCREEN AT ITS OWN `/connections/…` ADDRESS.** The property's
**Build tab** gains what the six drawn tabs carry, **as sections**. The 2026-09-04
ruling stands and is NOT superseded; what changes is that one destination becomes
complete.

⚠ **AND THE DRAWING IS NOT STAMPED "WRONG" — IT IS STAMPED "ONE DESTINATION".** Pages
100–107 are the **content** contract for those sections; only their ADDRESS and their
tab strip are superseded. A lane building from them takes what each tab shows and not
where it lives.

⚠ **THIS DOES NOT UNBLOCK BUILDING, AND THE PO WAS TOLD SO BEFORE THEY ANSWERED.** Four
measured things still stop a real build (`12-governance/28-new-connect-measured-2026-09-21.md`
§2): nothing can be ACTIVATED at all, the completion path has **never once run**, no
build made through the wizard can **ever** raise a charge, and a single house cannot be
built. Everything those pages draw is a picture of what a completed build leaves
behind.

---

### 2 · A CONNECTION LETTER GETS **ITS OWN MESSAGE KIND** — `OQ-NOT-12521` CLOSED

**The question.** `connection` is not one of the fourteen things a message may be about,
so all three commit letters are refused **by name** and the commit honestly reports it
queued none. Measured 2026-09-21: **373 queued messages product-wide — 200 payments,
159 invoices, 9 service requests, 3 bulk actions, 2 moves, and ZERO connections.**

**THE PO CHOSE A**, quoting the option back: *"A · A new connection kind — Its own
retention, its own template group, and a clerk sees connection letters grouped as
connection letters."*

**SO:** a new `connection` source kind, with its own template group and retention.
**Reusing `notice` was explicitly the rejected option**, and the reason is recorded
because it is the one a future lane will be tempted by: it would put a **welcome letter
among disconnection notices**, where retention, template group and a clerk's
expectations all differ.

⚠ **ANSWERING THIS DELIVERS NOTHING ON ITS OWN — QUEUED IS NOT SENT.** There is no
provider adapter for email, SMS or print anywhere in this product, so a queued row is
still the finished state. **No document, screen or docstring may describe this as
telling anybody anything.**

---

### 3 · THE WORD IS **ACTIVATE**, AND THIS IS THE SECOND TIME OF ASKING

**PO, verbatim, twice in one sitting:** *"we ahe to say activate"*, then *"3 · Energise
or activated? activated"*.

⚠ **AND IT WAS ALREADY RULED ON 2026-08-25 — `CR-032`, verbatim: *"instead of energise
can we use activated"*, SHIPPED IN `2.46.0`.** `connections.py`'s tokens are `ACTIVATED`
/ `PARTLY_ACTIVATED` and the old names are gone, not aliased.

**So this is not a new ruling; it is a MISSED INSTANCE of an old one**, and recording it
that way is the point. `NewConnectReviewStep.tsx`'s *"what happens next"* row kept the
old word while the rest of the product moved — **and the very same row already reads
`Partly activated` beside it.** One row, both words, for four weeks.

⚠ **LAW 13 IS WHY THIS IS WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN JUST FIXED:** the PO should not have
been asked a question the repo had already answered. The repair is the grep, not the
apology — before putting a wording question to the PO, search the decision log for the
word.

⚠ **FOUR OF THE ELEVEN CATALOGUES SAID IT AND SEVEN DID NOT.** English, German
(*"ans Netz gehen"* — onto the grid), Japanese (*通電* — energise) and Indonesian
(*menyala* — lights up) are all ELECTRIC-ONLY and wrong for water, gas and sewer.
Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi and Korean already avoid it and are **LEFT
ALONE** — `B14` rule 35: a catalogue is written in its own language, never translated
from English.

---

### 4 · THE BUILT STEP NAMES ARE CORRECT — THE DRAWING IS STALE ON STEP 5

**PO, verbatim, against the eight-step table:** *"build names are correct here"*.

The one divergence was step 5: drawn **Plans & work orders**, built **Work orders**.
**The built name stands.** It is not a divergence at all but the PO's OWN ruling of
2026-09-16 already applied — the plan is chosen earlier and moved to step 2, and the
step's name moved with it. **The drawing has not caught up**, and p95 is stamped rather
than rewritten.

**So the wizard is eight steps and seven of eight names were never in question:**
Owner & scope · Premise · Units · Map services · **Work orders** · Charges ·
Communication · Review & confirm.

## 2026-09-21 · THE NEW CONNECT WIZARD, STEP BY STEP — PO CONFIRMATIONS AND THREE CHANGES

The eight steps, every data element and every action were put to the PO as measured
tables. **Steps 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 and the action list came back confirmed as
measured** — *"this is correct"* against each. Three things changed, and two questions
were asked back and are OPEN.

### 1 · STEP 1 MUST TAKE DOCUMENTS — a new requirement

**PO, verbatim:** *"Step 1 — Owner & scope (p92) + you ahve to take documents - rest is
all good"*.

So **Owner & scope gains a document capture**. ⚠ **AND THE COMPONENT ALREADY EXISTS** —
`07-frontend/src/components/documents/` landed 2026-09-21 under `B14` rule 43, with the
backend store (`apps/tenancy/document_storage.py`), the `POST /accounts/{id}/documents`
door and two existing callers. **A lane writing a bucket call or a presigner here has
missed it.**

⚠ **AND THE TRANSFER WIZARD'S OWN DOCUMENT QUESTION DOES NOT APPLY HERE.**
`OQ-CUS-12522` asks where a BUYER's papers go before a sale commits, because during a
sale the account still belongs to the SELLER. **A new connect has no such problem:**
nothing is owned by anybody else, so the owner's documents may be captured at step 1
and filed against what the commit creates. Stated so the open question is not read
across.

### 2 · STEP 4 OFFERS ONLY THE TENANT'S ACTIVE SERVICES

**PO, verbatim:** *"here filter only active Utility services for that Tenant"*.

**What was wrong:** step 4's tick list is a HAND-TYPED constant —
`newConnectShared.TEN_SERVICES` — holding all ELEVEN platform services, with the line
*"N of 11 available at this address"* above it. The demo utility sells **two**, so
**nine of eleven tick boxes could not commit**; the server refuses *"gas isn't one of
the services this utility bills"*.

⚠ **THIS IS THE THIRD HAND-TYPED COPY OF THE SERVICE LIST IN THE FRONT END, AND
`CLAUDE.md` ALREADY NAMES THE OTHER TWO** — `SignupWizard.tsx`'s tick-list and
`ratingShared.tsx`'s badge map — as hard-won law 2, *"an eleventh service does NOT
appear on screen on its own and it fails SILENTLY"*. **The ruling kills the whole class
here rather than renumbering a constant:** read the tenant's enabled set instead.

**The source exists on the server** — `apps/tenancy/services.py` resolves through
`tenant_services` with `enabled=True`.

⚠ **AND `TENANT-ENABLED` IS NOT `AVAILABLE AT THIS ADDRESS` — THEY ARE TWO DIFFERENT
FILTERS AND BOTH ARE REAL.** A utility may sell gas (tenant-enabled) at an address that
has no gas main (`premises.services_available`). This ruling names the TENANT one;
the address one is question 1 below and is still open. **A lane must not collapse them.**

### 3 · THE CONTRACT LETTER COMES FROM THE PLAN, LATER

**PO, verbatim:** *"we dont have contract yet- we wil create it later and attach to plan
so you can take the contract from plan itself"*.

**Context:** step 7 keeps three letters — the build confirmed, **the contract**, and the
quote with what is owed — and the CONTRACT is **not on the drawing at all**, so a lane
building from p97 alone would build the wrong three.

**Ruled:** the contract is **not authored by this wizard**. A contract will be created
later and **attached to a PLAN**, and the wizard takes it from the plan. ⚠ **So the
letter is a DELIVERY of a plan attachment, not a template this step owns** — and until
plans carry one, the row states its absence rather than inventing a document.

### 4 · TWO QUESTIONS WERE ASKED BACK AND ARE OPEN

Both were put with a real case, three options and a recommendation, and **neither has
been answered**:

* **The picked address loses its service list.** Choosing an address already on file
  copies street, town, state and ZIP and **not** the premise type, parcel, route, name
  or **what services that address offers** — so the clerk's step-4 ticks are a local
  fiction and every meter is refused at the last press, after eight steps.
  **Recommended: the picker fetches the whole premise.**
* **No build made through this wizard can ever raise a charge.** The payload always
  sends the application reference EMPTY and the server's first pricing test asks for
  one. **Zero of nine connections have a quote total**, and `CON-26-0129` — a real
  Draft build at 500 Main St — **can be finished by no screen in the product.**
  **Recommended: open the wizard from the application first, then allow pricing
  without one.**

⛔ **NEITHER IS BUILT UNTIL RULED.** The second is a billing precondition and the first
changes what picking an address means.

## 2026-09-21 · THE APPLICATION AND THE NEW CONNECT ARE SEPARATE — AND THE RECORD PAGE IS CONFIRMED, SECTION BY SECTION

**Raised as `CR-126-BRC07`.** Four rulings, and the first supersedes code that is already
shipped. The two questions this log's previous section left OPEN are both answered here.

---

### 1 · AN APPLICATION IS NOT A DEPENDENCY. IT IS PROVENANCE.

**PO, verbatim:**

> *"no - we are keeping application process and new connect process seperate - applciation
> is submitted - reviewed and approved or rejected - once that is doen application life is
> completed. then approve applciation may create a new conenct request - as draft request -
> this request is new work and recognized seperately from applcaition and hence we should
> not make it dependent on applciation #"*

**THIS CLOSES THE SECOND OF THE TWO OPEN QUESTIONS** — *"No build made through this wizard
can ever raise a charge"* — and it closes it **against the recommendation that was put.**
The lane recommended *open the wizard from the application first, then allow pricing
without one*; the PO ruled the dependency out entirely rather than sequencing it. That
reversal is recorded because the recommendation is what a future lane will find first.

**What it means, concretely:**

* `request_id` is **carried and displayed** — *where this came from* — and is **never
  required**, never a foreign-key dependency, never a precondition of pricing.
* A build raised directly, with no application behind it, **prices itself and raises its
  own charges.**
* An approved application **may** create a new-connect request **as a DRAFT**, and the
  application's life ends at that moment.

**THE WORKED CASE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS URGENT AND NOT TIDY:** today the wizard's payload
always sends the application reference EMPTY and the server's first pricing test asks for
one, so **zero of nine connections have a quote total**, and `CON-26-0129` — a real Draft
build at 500 Main St — **can be finished by no screen in the product.** Under this ruling
it can be priced and finished with no application at all.

⚠ **THIS REVERSES A BUILT DESIGN, SO IT IS A CHANGE AND NOT A DEFECT**, and the business
rule in the customers module is marked SUPERSEDED with its date in the commit that builds
it — not after.

---

### 2 · ASSET NUMBERS ARE GENERATED AT COMMIT. ONLY INSTALL AND ACTIVATION WAIT.

**PO, verbatim:** *"you can generate meter, sub meter or asset # and assigned it -
buttheya re not yet installed or actiavted"*, and then, asked where the install date comes
from: *"install date on work order completion - yes, start the work"*.

The lane had proposed that a meter created at commit is a placeholder. **The PO corrected
it:** the NUMBER is real and assigned from day one; what is not yet true is that anything
is installed or activated. A new connect exists precisely to provision the field work, and
the meter, the asset and the first reading only become real when that work completes.

**So: `install_date` is written on WORK ORDER COMPLETION.** ⚠ **Today it was measured
DEFAULTING TO TODAY AT CREATION** — so every build made through the wizard has been
recording an installation that has not happened. That is the defect this ruling exposes,
and it is fixed under `CR-126-BRC07`.

⚠ **AND THE ASSET'S LIFECYCLE STATUS HAS NOT BEEN READ.** Nobody has checked whether a
meter created at commit lands in a status that says *not yet installed*. Stated here as an
absence rather than assumed either way; the lane that checks it files what it finds.

### 4 · BUILD FROM THE DRAWING AS AN IMAGE, AND USE THE UI GENERATION SKILL

**PO, verbatim:** *"build new connect request creet and detial view using images of
drawing not text; use UI genration skills - this is important"*.

That is **`B14` rule 42 restated by the person who ratified it** — *"When you use images to
create screens your accuracy is higher; hence dont create screens using only Text"* — and

with `10-scripts/pdf/pdf_render.py` from `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` and

in this log's previous section as the step-4 ruling, and it settles the step-2 question by
the same principle: **the picker fetches the whole premise**, and what a premises offers is
the premises' own fact, not a local fiction assembled in the wizard.

⛔ **SO NEITHER QUESTION IS OPEN ANY LONGER.** The paragraph at the end of the previous
section that says *"NEITHER IS BUILT UNTIL RULED"* was true when written and is now
superseded by this section. It is left in place rather than edited, and this line is the
supersession — a closed question's BODY goes on describing the open world, and the body is
what a lane actually reads (`DEF-WRK-4030`).

## 2026-09-20 · THE BUILD RECORD IS THE BUILD TAB, CONFIRMED — THE PO'S OWN TWO STATEMENTS, 37 MINUTES APART, RESOLVED

**`OQ-MET-12520` stays CLOSED on option C. Nothing is superseded. This section exists
because for about twenty minutes the repo held two PO statements pointing different ways,
and the resolution is worth more than the answer.**

**THE TWO STATEMENTS.**

* **18:25:47 UTC**, closing `OQ-MET-12520` (commit `5495a5978`), the PO chose option C:
  *"Your ruling's words were 'you cannot have two different screen' — that's about
  duplication, not about the content. The drawing isn't asking for a duplicate; it's
  asking for completeness we don't have. C gives you both: nothing duplicated, and the
  clerk stops hopping three places."*
* **19:02 UTC — thirty-seven minutes LATER** — the PO clicked `CON-26-0128` on the New
  connects tab in a browser, landed on the premises record titled *240 Sable Court*, and
  said: *"it show premsies - it should show new connect detail page"*.

⚠ **THE TIMELINE WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, AND THE FIRST READING OF IT WAS WRONG.** A
lane reported the complaint as the ruling's INPUT. It is not: the commit clocks are
`18:25:47` and `19:03:32 +0000`, and the PO's own taskbar read `3:02 PM` in the minute they
wrote — so they are on UTC−4 and the click was `19:02`. **A claim about what happened first
is a claim like any other and is checked like one.**

**WHY IT WAS PUT BACK TO THE PO AT ALL, GIVEN LAW 13 FORBIDS RE-ASKING.** Because it is the
one category law 13 names as legitimately reaching them: *a ruling that collides with a
signed rule — the supersession must be stated, never assumed*. The collision here is
between two statements by the SAME person, which is exactly the failure law 13 predicts
when we make someone answer from memory — and the honest response is to show them both,
not to pick one.

**HOW IT WAS PUT.** Both statements quoted back with their times, the real case, two
options in plain sentences with what each costs, and a recommendation. **The PO chose:
MAKE THE BUILD TAB COMPLETE.**

**SO, AND THIS IS NOW SETTLED TWICE:**

* ⛔ **No second screen at its own `/connections/…` address.** No route, no `SCREEN_ROUTES`
  row, no `NCT-02` badge, and `BuildRedirect` is not touched. That address is a deliberate
  doorway from when `ConnectionDetailPage.tsx` was DELETED under the 2026-09-04 ruling, and
  it is kept alive for bookmarks.
* ✅ **The property's Build tab becomes the complete build record** — the drawn header
  facts, the five tiles, the blocking banner, Live state, Owner & scope, The premise and
  Where it came from, plus what the other five drawn tabs carry, **all as sections**.
* ✅ **Blueprint p100–p107 remain the CONTENT contract in full.** Only the ADDRESS and the
  TAB STRIP are superseded.
* ✅ **`buildHomePath` is CORRECT and is not repointed**, and the three tests in
  `NewConnectsTab.test.tsx` that assert the premises destination stay. **`DEF-CUS-6049`
  was filed on the wrong diagnosis and is corrected rather than withdrawn: the defect is
  that the Build tab is not the build record.**

**AND IT IS BUILT AS COMPONENTS, WHICH IS WHY THE TWENTY MINUTES OF DOUBT COST NOTHING.**
`B14` rule 43, ratified the same day — *a piece of UI is built as a COMPONENT; standalone
code inside a page is not reuse*. The header facts, tiles, banner and four sections take
their data as props and know nothing about where they are mounted. Had the answer gone the
other way, a route, a registry row, a `g29` baseline and three tests would have moved and
**nothing would have been rebuilt.** That is the general lesson: **when a question is open
about WHERE something lives, build it so the answer only moves a mount point.**
## 2026-09-21 — THE FIRST DISCONNECTION THIS PRODUCT HAS EVER COMPLETED, AND THE FOUR THINGS IT DID NOT DO

**Asked, verbatim:** *"can you do end to end web walk for diconnect - all screens -
create disocnenct request, view it, list view filter, search etc, and then complete the
request and see it does what it says - disocnnect mean account status mter, assets
status etc. anything else what we have to do"*

**Walked in a browser** on `a3a572501`, the commit that respelled the reconnection
charge code to `RECON` and moved it to **$75.00**. Until that commit landed **every cut
in this product refused, on every tenant**, because the completion path looked up
`CC-RECON` and no tenant has ever had a row by that name. The walk and the row counts
are `10-scripts/po20260921_disconnect_web_walk.mjs` and
`10-scripts/po20260921_disconnect_walk_readback.py`.

### THE CUT ITSELF — `A-11340` · `DSC-26-0001` · cut on 2026-09-20

Counted before and after, with the tenant set, on the live database:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the case | `scheduled`, no cut date, no fee | **`cut`**, `cut_on 2026-09-20`, fee `75.0000`, code `RECON`, deposit `held`, `outstanding_at_cut 8315.0000` |
| invoices | none | **one** — `BL-2609-000081`, type `fee`, **issued**, **$75.00**, due the day of the cut |
| invoice lines | none | one — *Reconnection fee* $75.00 |
| journal entries / lines | 168 / 663 | 169 / **665** — a **balanced pair**, debit `1200` $75.00, credit `4610` $75.00 |
| `audit_log` for the account | 12 | 13 — one `disconnect.cut.committed` |
| outbound messages | 373 queued, **0 sent** | 375 queued, **0 sent** |

**It is one transaction.** The bill, the fee, the status decision and the settlement are
inside one `atomic()`, and the audit row is inside it too.

### ⚠ FOUR THINGS THE CUT DID NOT DO, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS A BUG

**1 · THE ACCOUNT STATUS DID NOT MOVE, AND THAT IS CORRECT.** It still reads
`Marked disconnect`. The product **held it deliberately**, and said so on the wire:
billing refused the final bill because *"base charge code `BASE-E-COM` prices per
connection size and states no amount for size None"*. Writing `Disconnected` would drop
the account out of the bill run with days still unbilled — the `$23.23` of `OQ-1170`.
**The supply is recorded off and the account keeps billing until the size is priced.**

**2 · NO FINAL METERED BILL WAS RAISED**, for the same reason. The only invoice the cut
produced is the fee.

**3 · NOTHING HAPPENED TO ANY METER, ASSET, SERVICE POINT, CONNECTION, ROUTE, CYCLE OR
WORK ORDER, AND NO METER READ WAS WRITTEN.** `commit_cut` accepts `final_reads` and
**no screen passes one** — the path is built and unreachable. The deposit was `$0.00`,
elected `held`, and no money moved.

**4 · NOTHING ANNOUNCES THE DISCONNECTION.** The two messages the cut produced are both
`bill_ready` — about the **fee bill** — and both are **queued**, like all 375 in the
product, **none of which has ever been sent**.

### THE DEFECT THE FIRST CUT EXPOSED — `DEF-CUS-6050`, money

**`To clear first` double-counts the fee the moment the cut commits.** The PO's own
signed figure (`BR-CUS-104`, 2026-08-25, on this same account) is
**$8,240.00 arrears + $75.00 = $8,315.00**. After the cut the arrears ARE $8,315.00,
because the fee is now a real receivable — and `_to_clear` adds the fee again and shows
**$8,390.00**, on the number that gates a customer back into service.
**It could not have been found before today**, because before today no cut committed.

## 2026-09-20 · ALL TEN DISCONNECT FINDINGS APPROVED, IN THE ORDER PUT, AND THE WALK IS RE-RUN AFTERWARDS

**The first end-to-end disconnect walk happened this day** and produced a verdict put to
the PO in one sentence: *a clerk can do one straightforward non-payment cut today; they
cannot run disconnections as a job.* Ten findings were then put as a table — issue, the
fix, the screen, what it solves — split into **six one-file fixes** and **four that are
real work, not fixes**, each labelled as such so the cost was visible before approval.

**THE PO APPROVED ALL TEN AND ASKED FOR THE WALK AGAIN.** Their words, in order:
*"okay do it"* · *"okay"* · *"fix these as well"* · *"please fix these as well - The four
that are real work, not fixes"* · **"fix all these and again run the web walk"**.

⚠ **THE FOUR WERE APPROVED WITH THEIR COST STATED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS RECORDED AS AN
APPROVAL AND NOT AN INSTRUCTION.** They were headed *"real work, not fixes"* in the table
the PO read, and approved anyway. Nobody may later describe them as a misunderstanding of
scope.

**THE ORDER IS THE PO'S OWN AND IS NOT A LANE'S CHOICE:**

1. **The money one, today** — *"It's wrong on every cut, and it's the number that decides
   whether someone gets their power back."*
2. **The other five small ones together** — *"they turn the screens from honest but rough
   into something a clerk reads without stumbling."*
3. **Connection sizes** — *"it's not code and it blocks the whole event completing."*
4. **The three builds, restore service first** — *"a utility that can cut and can't
   reconnect isn't finished."*

**WHY THIS COULD NOT HAVE BEEN FOUND EARLIER, AND IT IS THE USEFUL PART.** Until this day
**every cut refused on every tenant**, because the completion code looked for a
reconnection charge code `CC-RECON` that no utility has ever had. So **no cut had ever
committed**, and every one of these ten is a defect that only exists *after* a commit —
a figure that double-counts a fee the moment the fee becomes real debt, a consequences
panel that was a list of intentions until something ran, a tile whose window meant *when
it will* and started matching *when it did*. **A guarantee nothing has ever executed is
not a guarantee**, and a green suite said nothing about any of them.

**THE TEN, AND WHERE EACH LANDS.** Six fixes: the reconnection figure that says
`$8,390.00` where the signed figure is `$8,315.00` (`DEF-CUS-6050`) · two of five cut
reasons that can never commit, two misspelled strings (`DEF-CUS-6023`) · the *due to cut*
tile that counts cases already cut and opens an empty list (`DEF-CUS-6055`) · a cut dialog
promising a status the server deliberately held (`DEF-CUS-6051`) · raw server codes
reaching a clerk on two screens (`DEF-CUS-6053`) · a *Case reference* row rendering the
word `service` (`DEF-CUS-6052`). Four builds: **restore service** and the five other write
paths with no door · **something that watches a cut date**, since the completion code has
exactly one caller and it is a person pressing a button · **visit outcomes** for a crew
that attends and does not cut · **connection sizes priced**, which is what held the
account status on both real cuts and which will hit the customer being taken live.

⛔ **ONE BOUNDARY IS RULED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO A LANE: NOTHING CUTS SUPPLY
AUTOMATICALLY.** The PO asked for due work to be **surfaced**, not executed — *"the clerk
stops being the scheduler"*, not *the scheduler stops being a person*. Nothing in this
product has ever cut a supply without somebody pressing a button, and turning a date into
an automatic disconnection is a new ruling, not this one.

**AND THE ACCEPTANCE IS THE WALK, NOT THE SUITE.** *"again run the web walk"* — the same
end-to-end browser walk, re-run over all five screens once the ten land.
`10-scripts/po20260921_disconnect_web_walk.mjs` and
`10-scripts/po20260921_disconnect_walk_readback.py` exist so it is re-run rather than
re-done by hand. **No gate in this repo reads rendered output**, and all ten of these
passed every test in it.

## 2026-09-21 · A BUILD PRICES ITSELF — THE APPLICATION IS PROVENANCE, NOT A DEPENDENCY

**PO ruling, verbatim:**

> *"we are keeping application process and new connect process seperate - applciation is
> submitted - reviewed and approved or rejected - once that is doen application life is
> completed. then approve applciation may create a new conenct request - as draft request
> - this request is new work and recognized seperately from applcaition and hence we
> should not make it dependent on applciation #"*

### WHAT IT SUPERSEDES, AND IT IS A SENTENCE RATHER THAN A NUMBERED RULE

Nothing in any `02-business-rules.md` said the quote comes from the application. **The
dependency lived in code and on a screen**, which is why it needed finding rather than
looking up:

* `apps/metering/connections._post_connection_quote`, the first branch of a 🔒 money
  path: *"This build has no service request, so there is no quote to raise. **A quote
  arrives with an approved application; a build a developer starts without one is priced
  by nobody and charges nothing.**"*
* the wizard's step 6: *"No priced lines yet. Charges are raised from an application."*

**Both are SUPERSEDED 2026-09-21** and the rule that replaces them is **`BR-MET-1178`**,
written into `04-docs/05-modules/04-metering/02-business-rules.md` before a line of code
moved.

### THE FIGURE THAT MADE IT URGENT

**Not one of the nine connections in the demo tenant carries a quote total, and not one
has an owner account.** `newConnectDraft.ts` sent `service_request_id` EMPTY on every
commit and the server's first pricing test asks for one, so **no build made through this
wizard could ever raise a charge** — and the payer, the payment terms and the posting
date step 6 collects were read by nothing at all.

### WHAT A BUILD'S OWN LINE IS, AND THE DRAWING ALREADY DREW IT

Accounts blueprint p094, in red: *"Every quantity is counted from the services grid, not
typed. Six units, twenty service points, one premise — change a tick on step 4 and these
move with it."*

So a line is **a CHARGE CODE the clerk picks out of the tenant's own catalogue** plus a
**BASIS** — `per_unit` · `per_meter` · `per_premise` — and the **QUANTITY is counted**
from step 4. **What crosses the wire is a count, never a figure** (`CLAUDE.md` hard rule
2, `BR-BIL-007`, `BR-BIL-020`): billing reads the price off the tenant's charge row and
multiplies, and nothing is rounded before finalization.

⚠ **THE CHARGE CODE IS PICKED, NEVER GUESSED, AND THAT IS THIS LANE'S JUDGMENT
RECORDED RATHER THAN A QUESTION ASKED (law 13).** The drawing names `CC-CONN`,
`CC-METERSET` and `CC-CASVC`. **Nothing in this product declares which charge code is
counted per unit, per meter or per premise** — `rating.Charge` has no basis column and
no new-connection role — so hard-coding those three would be a vocabulary this screen
invented, and `Charge.is_base`'s own docstring records what that costs: *"it breaks the
moment a tenant names theirs `SERVICE-CHG`, and it breaks silently"*. The clerk picks
from `GET /charges`, exactly as a clerk already picks the charge code on a service
request's fee line. **Whether a tenant should be able to DECLARE a default code per
basis in Settings is a real improvement and is not built** — it would be a new Settings
surface and a new column, and the picked-code path is correct without it.

### THREE THINGS THIS RULING DOES NOT DO, STATED SO THEY ARE NOT READ INTO IT

1. **A build that HAS a request still takes the request's quote.** The ruling removes a
   REQUIREMENT, not a source. Those lines are what the customer was shown, `BR-CUS-090`'s
   waivers apply to them, and `_refuse_quote_price_drift` still refuses a catalogue that
   has moved. **The finance-proved posting of 2026-09-16 is untouched** —
   `BL-2609-000082`, `DR 1200 800.000000 · CR 4600 270.000000 · CR 4630 530.000000`.
2. **The price-drift refusal is not run on a build's own line, and that is not a gap.**
   It exists because a request's fee line stores the `unit_amount` a customer was QUOTED;
   a build's own line stores no price, so the catalogue IS the price and there are not
   two figures to disagree. `OQ-BIL-12376` stays open and is about the request path.
3. **No deposit.** A deposit is a liability at `2300`, `BR-RAT-020`/`BR-RAT-023` put its
   amount on the plan's deposit rules, and `OQ-BIL-12381` is open with its `$900.00`
   figure. Connection fees and work-order fees only.

### NOTHING IS CHARGED TWICE, AND THE GUARANTEE IS STRUCTURAL

The request path stamps `service_request_fees` so a second commit cannot re-raise it. A
build's own lines have no such row **and do not need one**: `commit_connection` refuses
any connection that is not `DRAFT` with `metering.connection_already_committed`, so a
second commit cannot happen at all. The bill a build raised is found again through
`connections.quote_invoice_id`, the column a sibling lane added under this same ruling.

### NO TOTAL BEFORE THE PRESS, AND THE ABSENCE IS STATED RATHER THAN FILLED

`billing.fee_bill.price_quote_bill` prices counted lines and takes an `account_id`; a
draft build has no account until step 8 writes one (`BR-MET-112`). So step 6 shows the
CODE, the BASIS and the QTY and **no money at all**. That is `DEF-BIL-5486` — a missing
door, not a missing screen — and the drawn `$3,030.00` is an illustration (`B14` rule
37), printed nowhere.

## 2026-09-20 · THE OTHER HALF OF THE JOB — A UTILITY CAN PUT SOMEBODY BACK ON, AND A FAILED VISIT LEAVES A MARK

**Lane DBLD-2.** Two PO-approved items from the disconnect walk, built together because
they are the same gap seen from two ends: the product could take supply away and had no
way to record anything that happened afterwards.

PO, verbatim, on the first: *"The other half of the job. Today a utility can cut supply
and cannot restore it from the product."*
PO, verbatim, on the second: *"The register reflects reality. Today a failed visit is
invisible and the case looks untouched."*

### 1 · RESTORING SERVICE HAD NO BUTTON ANYWHERE, AND THE ENGINE WAS FINISHED

`disconnects.mark_reconnecting` and `disconnects.restore_service` were both written on
2026-08-25, both role-gated, both tested, and **both reachable only from Python**. Their
HTTP routes existed too — `POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/reconnecting` and
`.../restore` — and **nothing in the product called either.** They are two of the six
disconnect write paths with no door: open a case, advance a tier, record a notice, lift
a protection, mark reconnecting, restore service.

That is hard-won law 2 read from the engine end, and it is R2's central failure in
miniature — a finished engine, an honest deferral, and no screen.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** `disconnects.reconnection_readiness()` (read-only) ·
`disconnect_record.reconnect_panel()` on `GET /disconnects/{ref}` ·
`ReconnectDialog.tsx` on the case record, as the header's commit.

⚠ **THE THREE REFUSAL SENTENCES MOVED AND NOT ONE WORD CHANGED.**
`reconnect_blockers` and `restore_blockers` now hold them, and `mark_reconnecting`
raises the first of them rather than carrying its own copy. A screen that paraphrased a
server refusal would be a second answer to a question the writer already answers, and it
drifts the moment either side is edited.

⚠ **THE HEADER STILL SHOWS THREE CONTROLS, WHICH IS WHY THIS DOES NOT REOPEN *"too many
actions"*.** The commits are STATE-EXCLUSIVE: a case is `scheduled` **or** `cut` **or**
`reconnecting`, never two, so exactly one is ever offered. `Mark as cut` on a case cut
last Tuesday can never become pressable again — `cut_readiness` answers `already_cut` for
ever — and a permanently dead control over a live screen is the mirror of law 2 that cost
the customer portal six of its eight doors.

### 2 · A CREW ATTENDS AND DOES NOT CUT — `OQ-383` CLOSED, RULE `BR-CUS-1083`

`OQ-383` has been open since 2026-08-25. The PO named the four outcomes: **locked gate ·
paid at the door · disputed · access refused**, and ruled that *"each must move the case
somewhere, not merely annotate it"*.

**WHICH somewhere was ours to decide and is recorded here rather than put back to them**
(hard-won law 13 — a judgment with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the
failure to make one). Two destinations, four outcomes:

| Outcome | Where the case goes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `locked_gate` | cut date **cleared**, state → `notice_sent` | The cut is still lawful and still owed; what failed was the visit. The case must stop advertising a date that has passed, and must be re-schedulable. |
| `access_refused` | the same move | Same position, different FACT — a padlock is an obstacle and a person in the doorway is a refusal, and that is the distinction the record is kept for. |
| `paid_at_door` | the same move | A crew holding a cheque is **not a posted payment**, and `apps/customers` writes no financial table (`BR-CUS-037`). Clearing the date is the most this may honestly claim. When the money posts, `halt_reason` answers `nothing_owed` by itself and `schedule_cut` refuses — the ladder stops itself, which is `BR-PAY-036`'s design. |
| `disputed` | **`stopped`**, reason `dispute` | This one already had a ruled home: blueprint p137 draws `Disputed · The customer is contesting the bill` as one of the three reasons a ladder is stopped by hand, and `disconnects.STOP_REASONS` carries it. A doorstep dispute is that dispute. |

**REFUSED: a fifth state.** An `attended_not_cut` state would need a migration to
`ck_disconnect_case_state`, a register segment, a chip in eleven catalogues and a rule
about what may leave it — for a position `notice_sent` already describes exactly (*the
ladder has served notice and no cut is on the calendar*). The TIER is untouched, so a
re-schedule resumes rather than restarts.

**REFUSED: stopping on `paid_at_door`.** `STOP_REASONS` is closed at three and widening
it is explicitly *"a fourth way to stop chasing a real debt"*, which needs a ruling. And
a stop on an unposted payment is a claim this product cannot back: if the cheque bounces
the case has been closed on a crew's word.

**REFUSED: an amount on `paid_at_door`.** `PAID_AT_DOOR_TAKES_NO_MONEY` — an amount typed
on a case would be a receivable nobody posted, sitting beside a ledger that never
received it.

### 3 · SET A STATE, OR DERIVE IT? — SET, AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE ANSWER TO `on_hold`

`STATE_ON_HOLD` is declared by the schema and **assigned by nothing**: a protection
writes its own row and the register works `On hold` out on every read. That is right
there and wrong here, and the difference is **whether the fact has a clock in it.**

A protection EXPIRES — a certificate runs out, a window closes, a plan is missed — so
*is this case held* changes while nobody is looking, and a stored state would be stale
with nothing to re-read it. **A visit has no clock.** A crew attended on a day and found
a padlock; that never stops being true and never becomes true later. Deriving it would
mean asking *what is the latest visit and what did it imply* on every read, which is a
computation over history rather than a fact about now — and it gives the WRONG answer the
moment a clerk re-schedules the cut, because the visit is still the latest one and the
case is no longer where it sent it.

**So the outcome is an immutable row (`disconnect_visits`) and the move is an explicit
write on the case, both in one transaction.** The reasoning is in the file's own docstring,
§2, with a named warning to the next lane that `on_hold` is not a precedent for it.

### 4 · WHAT THE FIRST RECORDED VISIT WROTE — AND WHY THE RECONNECTION DID NOT

Measured, on the live development tenant, not asserted. ⚠ **THIS HEADING SAID *“THE FIRST RECONNECTION”* AND THERE HAS NOT BEEN ONE** — see the correction below.

⚠⚠ **CORRECTED THE SAME EVENING, BY THE LANE THAT WROTE IT. THE PARAGRAPH THIS
REPLACES DESCRIBED A RECONNECTION THAT DID NOT HAPPEN**, and it is quoted rather than
deleted because the way it got here is the lesson. It read:

> *"`DSC-26-0002` on `A-11721` — cut 20 Sep, reconnected 20 Sep. A payment of $1,279.50
> was taken first, which is what the gate requires; the ladder stopped itself on
> `nothing_owed` the moment it posted. Then `Mark reconnecting` → state `reconnecting`
> … Then `Restore service` → state `restored` … and the row left the register."*

**None of that happened.** It was written from the plan, before the walk, under step W's
*write back before the thing that depends on it* — and step W means write down what was
RULED and what was DECIDED before building on it, never what a measurement is expected to
say. **A figure belongs in this log AFTER it is measured.** Reading the old paragraph, a
later lane would have believed this product had completed a reconnection. It has not.

**WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED ON `A-11721`, MEASURED THREE WAYS.** The payment posted — twice,
in fact, $1,279.50 then $1,204.50, both cleared — and **the gate never opened.**

| | figure |
|---|---|
| the migrated opening balance (`account_opening_buckets`, `d90_plus`, `BR-CUS-048`) | **$1,204.50** |
| the ledger receivable `disconnects._balance_for` reads | **$1,204.50** |
| the account's CREDIT POSITION — money taken that met no invoice | **$2,409.00** |

**The customer has paid twice what they owe and the case record still reads *Money is
still owed.*** `BR-BIL-160` (PO 2026-08-27, closing `OQ-530`) already rules that those
two numbers travel together — billing's `previous_balance` includes the migrated opening
balance and its `payments_credits` includes the settled part of it, read from
`billing/payments_seam.credit_position_for_account`. **The disconnect gate reads the
first and not the second.** That is `DEF-PAY-6074`, and it is ONE READ rather than the
allocation engine: the seed is right (56 opening-bucket rows on this tenant, each with
its balanced opening entry), the buckets are right, and billing already weighs them.
`OQ-570` already owns the separate question of the settlement being inferred rather than
recorded as a row.

**So the reconnection is proved everywhere except the last mile**, and the distinction is
worth keeping rather than blurring: the two doors, their dialogs, their refusals and their
money figures were walked in a browser; the two POSTs and their bodies are asserted in
`vitest` with four cases proved RED first; and the whole `cut → reconnecting → restored`
transition, its two audit rows and the status absence are proved by 21 cases under real
PostgreSQL with RLS on (`config.settings.pgtest`). What has never run on live data is the
pair of button presses, and `DEF-PAY-6074` is why.

⚠ **AND IT LEFT A MARK ON THE FIXTURE.** `A-11721` now carries three recorded payments
— one $1,279.50 `processing` (the first walk omitted `cleared_at`, so it never reached
AR) and two cleared, $1,279.50 and $1,204.50 — against a $75.00 fee invoice and a
$1,204.50 opening bucket. **Hard rule 4 forbids deleting any of them**, so they stay: the
case is still `cut`, the ledger receivable is still $1,204.50 and the credit position is
$2,409.00. A lane walking that account next should expect those numbers and not read them
as a second defect.

⚠ **THE FIRST WALK ASSERTED THE HTTP 201 AND NOT THE BALANCE**, so it reported *"the
payment posted"* — true, and useless, because the thing under test was the number. That
is law 7's *ask what would make this check pass wrongly*, and the walk now asserts the
figure the gate itself reads.

**The account-status half of the original paragraph WAS right and stands:**
`status_before_cut` is NULL on both completed cuts, so a restoration would leave the
account status untouched and `status_before_cut_not_resolvable` says so on screen before
the button is pressed — restoring a customer to `active` who was on `vacation_hold`
would write a status nobody decided.

**`DSC-26-0003` on `A-11812` — a locked gate.** `Record visit` → one `disconnect_visits`
row (`locked_gate`, 2026-09-20), the cut date **cleared**, state back to `notice_sent`,
one `disconnect.visit.recorded` audit row. **No money moved, no invoice, no journal
line** — a visit outcome is not a money action.

### 5 · WHAT THE DRAWING COVERED, AND WHAT IT DID NOT

`05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` p135–p144, rendered at 2.0× and **read as
images** (B14 rule 42). It draws the five wizard steps, the register, the case record and
its two dialogs — **and no reconnection screen and no visit screen at all.** Its own
`Why Blocked` note says so in as many words: *"what happens when a crew attends and does
not cut … those are rulings, not code."*

**Reported rather than claimed as drawn.** What the drawing DOES commit to is the SHAPE:
the register draws a `CUT, AWAITING RECONNECT` KPI, a `RECONNECTIONS` KPI and a
`Reconnections` filter chip, so the states are the drawing's even though the acts are not.
Both new dialogs are built to the neighbouring `HoldCaseDialog` and `MarkAsCutDialog`,
which were built to p144 and p145 this month, and to the shared kit (B14 rule 36).

## 2026-09-21 · THE RECONNECTION FIGURE IS READ ONCE AFTER THE CUT — `DEF-CUS-6050`, AND WHY THE OTHER SHAPE WAS REFUSED

**The number.** `BR-CUS-104` is signed over `A-11340` (PO 2026-08-25, verbatim:
*"does reconnection need $8,315.00 - this is correct"*): **$8,240.00 arrears +
$75.00 reconnection fee = $8,315.00 to clear**. After the cut of 2026-09-20 the
record page read **`To clear first $8,390.00`** beside its own **`Owed
$8,315.00`**, with nothing paid in between — **one fee too much, on the figure
that decides whether a household gets its supply back.**

**Why it was right until the day it ran.** `commit_cut` raises and ISSUES the
fee bill inside the cut's own transaction (DEF-708, PO 2026-08-27). Before the
cut the fee is a QUOTE and the ledger position does not contain it, so *arrears
+ fee* is the answer. From the instant the cut commits the position already
contains it. `_to_clear` was written before any cut had ever completed — every
cut in this product refused on an unresolvable charge code until 2026-09-20 —
**so the only state the figure was ever read in is the one where it is right,
and every existing test quotes it pre-cut.**

**THE JUDGMENT, because the rules did not settle it.** The filed row offered two
shapes: **(a)** read the position once after the cut and stop adding, or **(b)**
keep the sum and state its basis on the payload so the overlap is visible.
**(a) was taken.** A figure built by ADDING two sources has to know whether they
overlap, and here the overlap is *created by the very act the figure describes*
— so the sum has no stable meaning and no label can give it one. (b) would have
left a clerk and a customer reading `$8,390.00` with a footnote. The basis is
carried **as well** (`to_clear.basis`, with `fee_in_arrears`), so a later reader
can see which question was answered; it explains the figure, it does not repair
it.

**What decides which side of the cut we are on: `case.cut_on`.** It is written
in the same transaction that issues the fee bill and nothing else writes it, so
it is exactly the fact *has this fee reached AR*. **Not a list of states** —
`service_off_windows` in the same module already records why a state list is
wrong here: `restored` and `stopped` cases also hold a `cut_on` and would be
dropped silently.

**Both readers, and they now agree by construction.** The record panel
(`disconnect_record._what_a_cut_would_do`) had its OWN copy of `Owed + fee`;
that copy is deleted and it quotes the module. `mark_reconnecting` already read
the position once and needed no arithmetic change — its refusal sentence now
says the fee is *already inside* the figure rather than *added to* it, and
prints the amount at 2 dp as a string (rule 2) instead of the raw six-decimal
`Decimal` it used to print.

**Proved in a browser, on the real case, both sides of the commit:**

| screen | before the fix | after the fix |
|---|---|---|
| `DSC-26-0001` · `A-11340`, **cut** | `Owed $8,315.00` · **`To clear first $8,390.00`** | `Owed $8,315.00` · **`To clear first $8,315.00`** |
| `DSC-26-0003` · `A-11812`, **not cut** | `Owed $2,410.00` · `To clear first $2,485.00` | unchanged — `$2,410.00 + $75.00 = $2,485.00` |

**The general lesson, and it is worth more than the fix:** when an act moves
money INTO the balance, every quote built as *balance plus that money* changes
meaning the instant the act commits — and the only thing that finds it is
running the act.

⚠ **AND THE SAME ADDITION EXISTS ON THE CUSTOMER'S OWN SCREEN, IN ANOTHER
MODULE, AND IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE.** `apps/portal/selectors
._if_it_goes_that_far` (CWP-057, *What it would cost*) adds the open-bill
position to the same quoted fee. Measured on `A-11340` after the cut: owed
**$75.00** + reconnection fee **$75.00** = subtotal **$150.00**, where the
$75.00 owed IS the fee bill the cut issued. It did not render on that account
because `overdue` was false, so it is latent rather than live. It is a different
module, a different balance read and a different screen, so it is its own row:
**`DEF-CWP-6072`**.

⚠ **AND THE ENDPOINT THAT SERVES THIS FIGURE STILL DESCRIBED `DEF-700` AND
`DEF-708` AS OPEN** — *"the fee reaches AR through nothing today … the
reconnection gate reads AR alone and lets a customer through short by exactly
the fee"* — three weeks and a day after both closed, in
`transfer_disconnect_api.py` and in the copy of it inside `openapi/schema.json`.
Filed as **`DEF-CUS-6071`** and amended in the same commit as the fix.
**Closing a defect and amending every sentence that describes it as open are two
acts, and only the first one feels like the work** — the identical shape this
file already records for a closed open question. `openapi/schema.json` still
carries the old sentence: it is generated, nothing regenerates it today
(`.github/workflows/ci-backend.yml` is `.disabled`), and re-deriving it is not
this lane's to do — it is stated on `DEF-CUS-6071` rather than left implied.

## 2026-09-20 — SOMETHING READS CUT DATES DAILY, AND IT DOES NOT CUT ANYTHING

**PO, verbatim:** *"Something has to read cut dates daily and surface what's
due… A case due last week stops looking identical to one due next month. The
clerk stops being the scheduler."* Screen: **the register — a *due today* view;
plus a scheduled job.**

### What it was, measured in a browser rather than argued

`disconnect_cases.cut_scheduled_for` carried its own note in the model —
*"A STORED DATE THAT NOTHING WATCHES"* — and `disconnects.NO_SCHEDULER` rode on
every ladder answer the product has ever served: *"no runner, job, queue or
timer in this product reads a date and acts on it."* The Accounts blueprint
prints the same sentence in red on p139. `commit_cut` had exactly one caller:
a person.

**The worked case, on `brazosbend`, 2026-09-20.** `DSC-26-0001` on `A-11340`
was scheduled through the wizard for **2026-09-14** and never cut — six days
late, supply still on:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the row's cut date | `09/14/2026`, plain text | `09/14/2026` · **OVERDUE** · **6 days late** |
| the accent (§5.8.2, *this week*) | on `DSC-26-0002` (Sep 20) | unchanged — it is the SERVER's |
| a view that finds it | none | `Due now`, **1 row**, counted in SQL |
| anything reading the date daily | nothing | the watch, reporting `1 overdue, 0 due today` |

⚠ **THE ONLY EMPHASIS THIS COLUMN HAD RAN THE WRONG WAY ROUND**, and that is
sharper than *"there was no emphasis"*. `_within_the_week` is forward-looking by
its own docstring, so the accent lands on a cut booked for next Thursday —
which nobody has to do anything about — and leaves one that was due last Monday
in plain text.

### The judgment: ONE predicate, three readers

`apps/customers/disconnect_due.py` answers five things about a date — `overdue`
· `due_today` · `ahead` · `no_date` · `done` — and it takes the case's STATE as
well as its date. The row, the new `f.due` filter and the nightly watch all read
that one function, so a tile, a list and a job cannot drift.

**That is `DEF-CUS-6055`'s own remedy applied rather than restated.** Its filed
row names the shape: *"a date that records WHEN something happened keeps
matching a window that was meant to mean WHEN IT WILL."* A cut does not clear
`cut_scheduled_for` — correctly, it is the record of when the supply went off —
so a pure date test reads a cut case as late for ever.

### ⛔ WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, AND WHY EACH IS A QUESTION

**1 · Nothing cuts automatically. `OQ-CUS-12525`, OPEN.** The word in the
ruling is **surface**. Every other schedule in this product WRITES — the
collections ladder advances a debt, the work sweep raises orders — so there is
a precedent for an unattended act, and reading the precedent as permission
would be a lane deciding that a household's water may be turned off by a timer.
`BR-CUS-039` needs tier 3 *with proof of service*, and this product cannot
serve a certified notice at all, so *proof recorded* is a clerk's typed
reference rather than a delivery we made. An automatic cut would act on that.

**2 · No bell message. `OQ-CUS-12526`, OPEN.** `queue_staff_alert` is the only
staff entry point; it refuses a `failed_count` below 1 and addresses every
System Admin under `BR-NOT-021` because it treats every alert as a FAILURE.
*"Three cuts are due today"* is not a failure, and putting it through that door
would print `total 3 · failed 3` in an inbox. Which event class a due cut is,
and who should be told, is a product vocabulary decision.

**3 · The `DUE TO CUT` tile was not moved.** A sibling lane fixed it forty
minutes earlier (`DEF-CUS-6055`) and its caption still reads *within 7 days of
today*, which is what the figure IS. Widening a tile to include the past would
make it disagree with its own printed caption — `DEF-716`'s shape on this same
strip.

### `NO_SCHEDULER` is AMENDED, not deleted, and it is now two keys

Half of that sentence stopped being true today and half did not, so joining
them would have made the whole thing a lie either way it moved:

* `reads_cut_dates_on_a_schedule: true` — new, and it is what closed;
* `advances_on_a_schedule: false` — unchanged. No tier advances, no notice is
  written, no supply is cut on a timer;
* `watches_next_step_due: false` — the watch reads `cut_scheduled_for` **alone**,
  so a reader who sees *a scheduler exists now* cannot conclude the ladder runs.

The superseded sentence is quoted beside the new one, dated, rather than
deleted (hard-won law 1).

### How it was proved

**RED first, through pytest — the harness that runs it, not a bare `python3`:**
with the STATE test removed from `due_status` (the pure date test the module
exists to refuse) the extended check failed `assert 'ahead' == 'done'` on the
cut row; with the `f.due` narrowing removed it failed `assert 6 == 1` on
`due_now`. Green after both were reverted; no `# BREAK:` marker survives.

**THE CHECK IS THE SIBLING'S, EXTENDED — NOT A SECOND ONE.**
`test_dsc_every_kpi_tile_equals_the_rows_of_its_own_segment` landed with
`DEF-CUS-6055`; this adds ONE overdue account to ITS fixture and asserts `f.due`
and the watch's own register against the same rows. Two checks over one subject
that disagree are worse than one.

**Walked in a browser at 1440 and 1280** —
`10-scripts/po20260921_cut_date_watch_walkthrough.mjs`, 20 passed · 0 failed.

### ⚠ THE DRAWING DOES NOT COVER THIS, AND IT IS SAID RATHER THAN IMPLIED

Accounts blueprint p140 draws the register's five quick views — `Due to cut ·
At notice · On hold · Reconnections · All` — and **every one of them is a case
STATE**. `CUT DATE` is drawn as a plain date. There is no overdue state anywhere
on the register, the case record (p141–p143) or the wizard. The two new pieces
are built to their siblings in `disconnect/list/` and to the shared kit, and the
addition is REPORTED rather than claimed as drawn (B14 rules 41, 42).

## 2026-09-20 · THE BUILD RECORD IS WIRED — SIX JUDGMENTS MADE WHILE JOINING A READ TO A SCREEN

`CR-126-BRC07`, lane NCD-7. The backend read (`GET /connections/{id}/record`) and the
eight drawn panels landed in two different lanes **and nothing passed a value from one to
the other**. Every section rendered its stated absence, `tsc` and every test passed, and
the feature did not exist — CLAUDE.md hard-won law 2 in its exact words. This row records
the six judgments the join required, because none of them is in a signed rule and the
next agent would otherwise have to re-make them.

**No question went to the PO.** Law 13: every one of these is ours to decide and write
down, and a question here would have been the failure to make a decision.

### 1 · WHERE BOTH READS ANSWER, THE BUILD READ WINS

`state`, `waiting_on`, `target_activation` and `mode` are on BOTH payloads and are the
same derivation over the same row. The build read is what **gates the eight acts**, so a
screen that took the pill from one read and the buttons from the other would be two
sources for one fact — which is the thing `DEF-127` is about, one screen down. The record
fills only what the build read cannot answer: the two counted pairs, `activated_at`, step
1's five answers, the whole premise block, the provenance and the service tags.

### 2 · THE BILL'S FIGURE BEATS THE COMMIT'S, AND FALLS BACK TO IT

`connection_record._money` serves `quoted` (off the bill) beside `quote_total_recorded`
(the figure the commit wrote down) so a reader can SEE a disagreement. A tile has one
slot, so the screen has to pick: **the bill wins**, because that is what the customer was
actually asked for and `invoices.total` is immutable once issued (hard rule 4). Where
there is NO bill, `quoted` is `{null, null}` and the recorded figure is all there is —
which is exactly the figure this tile has shown since wave O. Falling back to it is what
keeps a tile a clerk reads today from vanishing tomorrow.

### 3 · THE GATE BANNER READS PAGE ONE, AND `unitsHeld` STAYS NULL

The banner names the ONE open work order the build marks as its gate, chosen from
`sections.work_orders.results` — **the first page, fifty rows**, which covers every build
in this product and would miss a gate on a build with more than fifty orders. That bound
is stated rather than guessed at: the alternative is a second round trip to fill a
banner, which is the hopping `OQ-MET-12520` exists to stop. A `completed` or `cancelled`
gate draws no banner at all, because a passed inspection blocks nobody.

**`unitsHeld` is null and stays null.** The drawing's *"four units cannot activate until
it passes"* needs a figure nothing in this product derives — no read counts the units one
order holds — so the banner says its shorter sentence rather than inventing the number.

⚠ **AND THE BANNER REPORTS A GATE; NOTHING ENFORCES ONE.** `work_orders.is_gate` is
written, stored, printed and read by nothing that refuses anything.

### 4 · A STORED CODE IS LABELLED BEFORE IT REACHES A PANEL

`owner_type` and `scope` are stored as CODES (`builder_developer`, `new_premise`) and the
panels print the string they are handed. So the join resolves both through the catalogue
families the WIZARD already uses — `customers.newConnect.ownerKind.*` and
`customers.newConnect.scope.*` — **adding no string to eleven catalogues**, and it
imports `OWNER_KINDS` and `CONNECT_SCOPES` rather than re-typing them so a fifth owner
kind appears on its own (law 2's hand-typed-list lesson).

`scope` is FREE TEXT on the server by `metering/0058`'s deliberate choice, so an
unrecognised value falls through to ITSELF: what a clerk typed is a truer answer than a
missing translation.

### 5 · THE SERVICE TAGS RESOLVED A CATALOGUE FAMILY THAT DOES NOT EXIST — `DEF-MET-6080`

`BuildRecordHeader` asked for `enums.service.<code>`. **There is no `enums.service`
family in any of the eleven catalogues**; en.json holds four complete eleven-service
families and that is not one of them. Every tag therefore fell back to the raw stored
code.

It hid twice over. The list was **DEAD** until this lane joined the read — `services` was
the empty array, so the map never ran — and `Kicker` uppercases, so `electric` renders
`ELECTRIC` and reads perfectly correct while `storm_water` renders `STORM_WATER` and
`thermal_heat` renders `THERMAL_HEAT`. Fixed to `work.orders.service.<code>`, the family
this module already owns, which carries all eleven services including `fire`.

⚠ **THE GENERAL SHAPE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX: a lane that lights up a dead control
inherits every bug behind it.** Nothing was wrong with this code while nothing reached it.

### 6 · NINE FILES CITED A TEST THAT DID NOT EXIST — AND `G116` WAS ALREADY SAYING SO

`buildRecordPanels.test.tsx` was named on the `Tests:` line of nine files in
`features/work/buildRecord/` and had never been written, so the eight drawn panels had no
test at all (`DEF-MET-6070`, now fixed — 14 cases).

⚠ **AND THE ESCAPE REASON FIRST FILED FOR IT WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL FINDING
(`DEF-GOV-6081`).** That row said no gate reads a Trace `Tests:` line. **`G116` does
exactly that, is registered in `run_gates.py`, and was RED on those eight** — red since
2026-09-17 on four other citations and eight worse since `38d5ce65a` on 2026-09-20.
Measured: **18 failures before this lane, 10 after.** That is CLAUDE.md law 7's first
shape — *proved red, then never read* — and a suite with other failures in it is where a
true red goes to hide.

### WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO

**It adds no screen and no route.** `/connections/:connectionId` is still a redirect,
there is no `SCREEN_ROUTES` row and no `NCT-02` badge: `OQ-MET-12520` closed on option C
and was confirmed a second time when the collision was put to the PO. **No markup
changed** — the panels are as lane NCD-2 built them.

**Both holds are still held.** `Edit details` has no endpoint anywhere and nothing in the
product can activate anything, so both stay greyed with the reason as visible text, and
`buildRecordHolds.test.ts` still fires the day either stops being true.
