## 2026-09-20 · THREE LANES FILED THE SAME RED IN ONE EVENING, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS DOING THE RIGHT THING

`DEF-CUS-6061`, `DEF-CUS-6069` and `DEF-CUS-6075` are **one defect**: a fixture in
`NewConnectServicesStep.dom.test.tsx` building a `TenantServiceRow` from three of its
eleven fields, which turned `tsc` red on the shared branch and made `npm run build`
refuse **for every front-end lane**.

**Introduced `553bd732e` at 19:28:46. Fixed incidentally by `517458f58` at 19:44**, and
no commit has touched that file since. **Measured, not inferred:** `npx tsc --noEmit`
exits **0** at tip `239cf8320`, and the fixture holds all eleven fields there. All three
rows are now `fixed` against `517458f58`.

⚠ **NOT ONE OF THE THREE LANES DID ANYTHING WRONG, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT.** Each was
obeying hard-won law 7's first habit — *read the failures you did not cause* — and each
**dated** its claim with `git log -S`, which is the second half of that habit and the part
lanes usually skip. Two of them even named the same introducing commit and the same
minute. The habit worked three times over.

**WHAT WENT WRONG IS STRUCTURAL AND THE REPO ALREADY KNOWS ITS SHAPE.** A sibling's
register rows are in **none of the places a listing can see until it pushes** — that is
law 11's `DEF-1787` reasoning, and `10-scripts/allocate.py` exists because of it. But
`allocate.py` answers *"is this NUMBER free?"* and nothing anywhere answers **"has
somebody already filed this SYMPTOM?"** So three correct lanes each computed a correct
next id and filed a correct row about the same red.

⚠ **AND A SECOND CAUSE COMPOUNDED IT: A LANE MEASURES ITS OWN BASE, NOT THE TIP.** The
third lane reported the error *"on the branch tip"* and said its tree was byte-identical
to the tip — **true of the tip it started from, which predated the 19:44 fix by minutes.**
There is no dishonesty in that sentence and no way for the lane to have known. **So a red
reported against a base is a statement about that base**, and the word *tip* in a lane's
report means *the tip when I started*.

**WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT, AND IT IS A HABIT RATHER THAN A TOOL.** Before filing a red you
did not cause, **re-read the failing file from the live tip** — `git show
origin/<branch>:<path>` — and re-run the check against it. One command, and it separates
*this is broken now* from *this was broken when I started*. Where the check is expensive,
say in the row which commit you measured at, so the next reader can tell the two apart.

⛔ **NOTHING IS RENUMBERED AND NO ROW IS DELETED.** A duplicate FINDING is not a duplicate
id, and all three rows are honest evidence that three lanes read failures they had not
caused — the habit this repo most needs and most often loses. They are closed, not erased.

## 2026-09-20 · THE CUSTOMER'S OWN SCREEN QUOTED THE SAME FEE TWICE (`DEF-CWP-6072`) — AND THE TWO BALANCE FIGURES BEHIND IT ARE NOT TWO HONEST QUESTIONS (`DEF-CWP-6083`)

### 1 · THE DOUBLE COUNT, AND THE ONE-LINE REASON IT EXISTED

`CWP-057`'s rail panel *What it would cost* is the customer-facing twin of the
staff record's *To clear first*, and it had the identical defect, in another
module, on another balance read. `apps/portal/selectors._if_it_goes_that_far`
summed **what the account owes** and **the quoted reconnection fee**.

`commit_cut` RAISES AND ISSUES that fee inside the cut's own transaction
(`DEF-708`, PO ruling 2026-08-27), so from that instant the fee is an OPEN BILL
and the balance already holds it. Measured on `A-11340` / `DSC-26-0001` on
2026-09-20, after the first cut this product has ever completed:

> owed **$75.00** + reconnection fee **$75.00** = subtotal **$150.00**

…over a single `$75.00` fee. The `$75.00` owed **IS** the bill the cut issued —
`BL-2609-000081`, issued 2026-09-20, the account's only open bill.

⚠ **IT WAS LATENT AND NOT LIVE, AND THAT IS WHY IT WAS FIXED NOW RATHER THAN
LEFT.** The screen returns its empty state unless `overdue` is true, and the fee
bill is due on the day of the cut, so on 2026-09-20 nothing rendered. It is
armed, invisible, and fires on the first day a cut account also carries an
ordinary past-due bill — which is the ordinary case.

### 2 · THE SHAPE CHOSEN — READ THE FACT, DO NOT DERIVE A THIRD COPY

`DEF-CUS-6050` settled the same question on the staff side the same evening and
its reasoning carries over unchanged: *a figure built by ADDING two sources has
to know whether they overlap, and here the overlap is created by the very act
the figure describes.* That fix published the fact on the quote —
`reconnection_terms()['to_clear']['basis']['fee_in_arrears']`, keyed on
`case.cut_on`, the column `commit_cut` writes in the same transaction that
issues the fee and which nothing else writes.

**So the portal READS it.** `arrears_position` passes `to_clear.basis` down and
the panel stops adding when it says the fee is already a receivable. **No third
copy of the arithmetic**: two copies is exactly how the two STAFF figures came
to disagree, and that fix deleted one.

**NOT ADDED IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT SHOWN.** The fee keeps its row and its
amount — a customer has to see what they are being charged — and the row now
carries `already_owed`, which the screen renders as five words beside the figure
(*already in what you owe*, `portal.overdue.partIncluded.reconnection_fee`, all
eleven catalogues). A row silently dropped would say the fee does not exist; a
row left unmarked would leave a reader with arithmetic that does not add up.
B14 rule 33 — a FACT, ≤ 6 words, no rule id, no reasoning on screen.

**Worked, both sides of the cut, and the pre-cut answer is pinned so the fix
cannot overshoot:**

| case | before the fix | after the fix |
|---|---|---|
| cut (`cut_on` set) — owed `$95.00`, fee `$95.00` | subtotal **`$190.00`** | subtotal **`$95.00`**, fee row marked *already in what you owe* |
| not cut — owed `$95.00`, fee `$95.00` | subtotal `$190.00` | **unchanged** — before the cut the fee is a QUOTE and dropping it would quote a price short by the whole fee, which is `DEF-708`'s own shape |

**Nothing here writes.** No row, no journal line, no audit row: it is a READ,
and `TC-7` counts six tables either side of the call to say so.

### 3 · THE OBSERVATION THAT WAS NOT FILED, SETTLED: THE TWO FIGURES ARE **ONE QUESTION ANSWERED TWICE**, AND ONE OF THE ANSWERS IS SHORT BY $8,240.00

`DEF-CWP-6072`'s row carried a note marked *separate observation, not filed* —
the same account reads `owing $75.00` on the portal and `Owed $8,315.00` on the
staff record. **It is a defect, and it is filed as `DEF-CWP-6083`.** Both
figures, and exactly what each is made of, measured read-only on 2026-09-20:

| | read | on `A-11340` | what it sums |
|---|---|---|---|
| **staff** | `ledger.reporting.ar_positions` via `customers.seams` → `disconnects._balance_for` | **$8,315.00** | every posted journal line on the designated AR account: `$8,240.00` opening balance + `$75.00` fee bill |
| **portal** | `payments.open_bills.open_bill_position` + `payments.billing_seam.outstanding_positions` via `portal.seams.payments_seam.account_balance` | **$75.00** | ISSUED INVOICES only: one bill, `BL-2609-000081`, the fee |

**The difference is one journal entry and it has no invoice behind it:**
`DR 1200 Accounts receivable $8,240.00 / CR 3000 Opening balance clearing
$8,240.00`, `source_type opening_balance`, memo *"Opening balance at cutover —
A-11340"*. A cutover opening balance is a **signed, frozen contract** —
`BR-CUS-048`/`BR-CUS-049`, `GT-16` ❄️ finance-signed 2026-08-08, written by the
accounts import through `apps/ledger/opening_balances.post_opening_batch` — so
**every migrated utility's legacy arrears are receivables with no invoice**, and
no sum over invoices can ever see them.

**WHY IT IS NOT TWO HONEST QUESTIONS, and this is the part that decided it.**
Three things, any one of which would settle it:

1. **The words on the screen are claims about what is owed, not about bills.**
   The headline is *"$75.00 is overdue by N days"*, the rail row is labelled
   *Owed now*, and the primary button reads *Pay $75.00*.
2. **The screen's own subject runs on the other figure.** Everything the ladder
   does — the halt, the cut, `reconnect_blockers`, `mark_reconnecting` and the
   new-service block — reads `_balance_for`, which is the ledger. `CWP-057`
   explains that machinery to the customer and quotes a number the machinery
   does not use.
3. **The repo already ruled there is one derivation.** `DEF-127` (2026-08-16):
   the row, the header and the finance KPI are *"one derivation grouped three
   ways and cannot disagree by construction"*, and `BR-REP-002` forbids the
   second. The portal is a second.

**And the worse face of it is not a wrong number, it is a screen that vanishes.**
On `A-11812` the whole `$2,410.00` arrear is a cutover opening balance with no
invoice anywhere, so the portal reads `owing $0.00`, `overdue` is **false**, and
`BR-CWP-093` closes `CWP-057` **and its link** — while the ladder is running,
the case sits at `notice_sent` and a cut is scheduled.

⚠ **THE FIX IS NOT A CHOICE BETWEEN THE TWO READS, BECAUSE NEITHER IS A SUPERSET
OF THE OTHER — which is why this is filed rather than settled in a read.** The
invoice read carries two signed adjustments the ledger cannot: `BR-BIL-072` /
`DEF-2416` (a budget or level-pay bill is measured at its LEVEL, not its total —
measuring the total *"chased a customer who had paid their level in full"*) and
`CR-059 CS-38` (credit the utility already holds comes off the chase). The
ledger read carries every receivable, including the ones with no invoice. The
derivation that satisfies both is the ledger position with those two adjustments
applied, in ONE place — engineering work with its own blast radius across `home`,
`my accounts`, `account summary`, `balance summary`, the pay flow and this
screen, and not a line to be smuggled into a fee fix.

⚠ **A SIBLING LANE REACHED THE SAME FACT FROM THE WRITE SIDE THE SAME EVENING —
`DEF-PAY-6074`, commit `dc0adaaf3`.** A payment reduces the ledger position only
through an ALLOCATION to an OPEN INVOICE; what it cannot allocate becomes account
credit and posts to `2400`. So on this data a cleared payment of `$1,279.50`
against `A-11721` moved the balance by exactly the `$75.00` it could allocate.
**The read defect and the write defect are the same underlying fact — a
receivable with no invoice behind it — seen from opposite ends**, and both are
now on the register rather than in two lanes' memories.

### 4 · WHY THE GUARD BUILT FOR EXACTLY THIS DID NOT FIRE

`06-backend/tests/test_def_127_one_account_one_figure.py` asks seven surfaces
what one account owes and fails any disagreement. **Its own docstring names the
surfaces that belong in it — *"a payments outstandings tab, a customer portal, a
dunning letter, a statement PDF"* — and the customer portal has never been one
of the seven.** Adding it would still not catch this: that world seeds ONE
issued bill through the real issue path, so the ledger and the invoice sum agree
there by construction. **The state this defect needs is a receivable with no
invoice, and no portal fixture has ever posted one.** Hard-won law 7's fifth
shape with the escape doubled — the surface missing from the list, and the
fixture unable to produce the case.

### 5 · WHAT THIS LANE DID NOT DO, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED

* **It did not move the portal's balance basis.** `DEF-CWP-6083` is filed with
  both figures and the derivation that would satisfy both; changing
  `account_balance` changes six surfaces including what *Pay $X* offers, which
  is a money path.
* **It did not touch the headline, the *Owed now* figure or the Pay button.**
  Those are `DEF-CWP-6083`'s, and forcing one number into agreement with another
  is the move that hides a defect instead of fixing it.
* **It did not bump the version.** Six disconnect fixes land as one batch and
  the orchestrating session sets one version (`DEF-GOV-3756`).

## 2026-09-20 · WHAT THE BROWSER FOUND AFTER THE BUILD RECORD WAS WIRED, AND TWO CHECKS THAT WERE LYING

`CR-126-BRC07`, lane NCD-7, the same join. Recorded separately because all three
findings came from **running the product and looking at it**, which is CLAUDE.md
hard-won law 6 — *"no gate looks at rendered output; nine defects were found this way
and by nothing else."* Every suite, every gate and `tsc` were green over all three.

### 1 · `How it is done` PRINTED `our_crew` TO A CLERK — `DEF-MET-6083`

`BuildOwnerScopePanel` rendered `t("customers.newConnect.mode." + mode, { defaultValue:
owner.mode })`. **That key family resolves in none of the eleven catalogues**, so the
defaultValue is the copy — and the code is not copy. The two work-order tables in
`buildViews.tsx` call the SAME key and pass `MODE_LABELS[row.mode]`, so they read *"Our
crew did it"* correctly.

⚠ **THE WARNING AGAINST THIS EXACT LINE IS 500 LINES ABOVE THE LINE, IN THE SAME
FEATURE.** `MODE_LABELS`' own comment reads: *"`defaultValue: order.mode` would ship
`our_crew` to a clerk's screen — visible, ugly and wrong."*

**Why the panel could not simply use it, and the judgment taken.** Importing
`MODE_LABELS` from `buildViews` closes a CYCLE — `buildViews` MOUNTS the panel — and
`DEF-WRK-3955` records what that costs: *"an import cycle in ES modules does not fail:
the constant is simply `undefined` while the other module's body runs"*, with `tsc`
silent throughout. So the three words moved to **`workforceLabels.ts`, a leaf module
that imports nothing**, which exists for precisely this and says so in its own header.
`buildViews` re-exports `MODE_LABELS` from there, so there is ONE source rather than a
second opinion, and no caller changed.

⚠ **THIS ONE WAS NOT DEAD CODE SOMEBODY LIT UP.** Unlike the service tags beside it
(`DEF-MET-6080`), the mode row has been LIVE since the shell landed on 2026-09-20 —
`build.mode` was always passed. It was simply never looked at.

### 2 · THE BROWSER WALK'S NEW SECTION PASSED ON ITS FIRST RUN BY LUCK

The Build tab renders on the BUILD read; the record is a **second round trip**. The
eight checks added for the joined rows therefore RACED it. They passed once, then
failed four checks on the next run against an unchanged app and unchanged data — and
the first green was the accident. The section now waits on `[data-counted]`, which the
record draws and nothing else does, for 25 s and then **fails loudly rather than
skipping**.

### 3 · AND ONE OF THOSE NEW CHECKS COULD NOT FAIL, WHICH IS THIS LANE'S OWN

*"Units activated and Service points live carry figures"* tested
`/\d+\s*\S*\s*\d+/` against the section's text — which matches the TARGET ACTIVATION
date `11/28/2026` two rows below, so it passed on a run where both rows read **not
counted**. It counts the counted pairs now and asserts the absence label is gone. Law
7's *"ask what would make this check pass wrongly"*, answered by the check on itself
one run after it was written.

### WHAT THE WALK SCORES NOW

**18 → 41 checks, 0 failures, 0 page errors**, against a real Django and PostgreSQL on
an isolated database this lane migrated and seeded itself, through `server.mjs` — the
DEPLOYED join — and not vite dev. Eight of the new checks are NEGATIVE (no
`builder_developer`, no `new_premise`, no `units_energised`, no underscored service
code) and **one is the general form of all of them**: no value in `Owner and scope` may
carry an underscore. That last one is what would have caught `our_crew`, and the seven
named codes would not have, because a walk can only name the tokens somebody thought of.

⚠ **AND THAT CLAIM WAS PROVED RATHER THAN ASSERTED, THROUGH THE HARNESS THAT RUNS IT**
(law 7). The panel was put back to `defaultValue: owner.mode`, **the bundle REBUILT**,
and the walk run again: **40 passed, 1 failed**, and the one failure was the underscore
check. All seven named-code checks passed over `our_crew` in that same run, which is
the measurement rather than the argument. The fix was then restored, the bundle rebuilt
a third time, and the walk is **41 / 0**.

## 2026-09-20 · TWO DISCONNECT DECISIONS TAKEN RATHER THAN PUT TO THE PO — `DEF-CUS-6073` AND `DEF-CUS-6078`

Two lanes each finished a fix, found a question underneath it, and **filed rather than
guessed**. Both are correct to have stopped: one changes a drawn caption and one changes
what a clerk is promised before an irreversible act. Neither is the PO's, and CLAUDE.md
law 13 is the reason — *everything else is ours to decide and write down; a judgment call
recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable, a question is the failure to make one.*
Both decisions are recorded here with their reasoning so the next lane does not reopen
them.

---

### 1 · `DEF-CUS-6073` — THE **DUE TO CUT** TILE COUNTS OVERDUE CUTS, AND THE CAPTION MOVES WITH IT

**The finding.** The tile is windowed to seven days **forward**; the chip beside it is not.
`DSC-26-0001` was booked for **14 Sep** and still `scheduled` on **20 Sep** — six days
overdue — so **the tile reads 0 and the chip beside it shows 1 row**. Both numbers are
true of their own question, which is exactly why nothing compares them.

**THE DECISION: the tile counts a cut that is due OR overdue, and its caption stops saying
*within 7 days of today*.**

**The reasoning, and it is the same reasoning as the defect the same tile was just fixed
for.** `DEF-CUS-6055` was *a tile that counted a house already dark*; this is *a tile that
does not count a house that should already be dark*. **An overdue cut is the single most
urgent row on that screen and it is currently in neither the count nor the caption** — it
is visible only to a clerk who thinks to press the chip. A door whose number excludes the
most urgent thing behind it is the same class of defect, one direction over.

⚠ **IT CHANGES A DRAWN CAPTION, AND THAT IS WHY IT WAS ESCALATED — BUT IT IS NOT A DRAWING
CONTRADICTING A SIGNED RULE**, which is the only thing `B14` rule 41 sends to the PO.
*Overdue* did not exist as a concept when p140 was drawn: it draws five quick views, all
**case states**, and `CUT DATE` as a plain date. The drawing is not wrong; it is silent.
**Filling a silence is ours. Contradicting a statement is not.**

**And most of it is already built.** A sibling landed `apps/customers/disconnect_due.py`
and `DisconnectDueChips.tsx` with a real `overdue` dimension while this row was being
filed, so the predicate exists and the row already renders `OVERDUE · 6 days late`. **Read
that first — the remaining work is the tile's count and its caption, not a new concept.**

⛔ **WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the tile is still counted by the same predicate as the list it
opens.** That is `DEF-CUS-6055`'s remedy and this must not quietly undo it — widening the
tile means widening the segment behind it, and
`test_dsc_every_kpi_tile_equals_the_rows_of_its_own_segment` must still pass.

---

### 2 · `DEF-CUS-6078` — THE CUT DIALOG PROMISES TWO THINGS THAT CANNOT BOTH BE TRUE

**The finding.** The dialog tells a clerk **both** *"Billing keeps running"* **and** *"The
account reads Disconnected"*. Writing that status puts the account in behaviour class
`non_billable`, which is precisely what removes it from the bill run. **One flag decides
both and the dialog renders both unconditionally.**

**THE DECISION: *"Billing keeps running"* survives. The unconditional status promise goes.**

**The reasoning.** On **both** real cuts this product has performed, the status was
**deliberately held** and billing **did** keep running — so the surviving sentence is the
one that has been true every time, and the discarded one is the one that has never yet
been true. `DEF-CUS-6051` already made the status row conditional on the server's own
answer (`written` / `held` / `unstated`, with an unknown code answering `unstated` and
never the promise); **this finishes that work rather than starting new work** — the two
sentences stop contradicting because the status one now only appears when the server says
it happened.

⚠ **A CUT IS IRREVERSIBLE, SO `B14` RULE 33's CONSEQUENCE CLAUSE GOVERNS THE COPY**: at
most two sentences, six words per sentence, **never cut below clarity**. Clarity wins over
the word count here if they conflict — and say so in the commit rather than trimming a
consequence into ambiguity.

⛔ **NOTHING HERE WRITES THE ACCOUNT STATUS.** The hold is correct — billing cannot raise
the final bill while the connection has no size recorded, and writing the status would
drop the account out of the bill run with days still unbilled. **This is a copy and
rendering decision only.**

The section *"THREE LANES FILED THE SAME RED IN ONE EVENING"* says the break was **"fixed

```
git log -S "function tenantServices"   → 553bd732e  19:28  step 4 offers only the tenant's services
git log -S "base_revenue_account"      → 517458f58  19:44  DEF-CUS-6057, a picked address keeps its services
```

That lane **broke every front-end lane's build for sixteen minutes and repaired it while

⚠ **AND THE LANE REPORTED IT AS ITS OWN.** It ran the one command CLAUDE.md law 7

## 2026-09-20 · A CUT CASE CANNOT BE UN-CUT, AND WHY THE GUARD IS ON THE CASE RATHER THAN ON THE MONEY (`DEF-CUS-6062`)

**`A-11340` was charged the $75.00 reconnection fee TWICE, on the development
database, by the product working exactly as written.** The figures, read from the
rows rather than from a report:

```
19:03:27  disconnect.cut.committed   cut_on 2026-09-20   BL-2609-000081  $75.00   outstanding $8,315.00
19:50:38  disconnect.cut.scheduled   ← on a case whose state was `cut`
19:50:38  disconnect.cut.scheduled
19:58:12  disconnect.cut.scheduled
22:18:42  disconnect.cut.committed   cut_on 2026-09-14   BL-2609-000083  $75.00   outstanding $8,390.00
```

Two issued invoices, two `Reconnection fee` lines, **two balanced ledger pairs**
(debit `1200` Accounts receivable $75.00, credit `4610` Disconnection &
reconnection fees $75.00, both posted), and `cut_on` moved from the 20th **back
to the 14th** — the enforcement re-dated by six days on the record a utility
would show a regulator. Hard rule 4 makes both invoices permanent: a correction
is a new row, so this cannot be tidied away.

**THE MECHANISM WAS A REFUSAL WITH A DOOR ROUND IT.** `commit_cut` refuses a
second cut BY NAME (`already_cut`) and gives the reason — *"re-recording it
would re-quote the reconnection fee and re-date the enforcement"*.
`schedule_cut` never mentioned `STATE_CUT` at all, so two accepted calls walked
around it: schedule the cut case (the state goes back to `scheduled`), then
commit (the guard no longer fires).

### THE CHOICE, AND IT WAS A REAL ONE

The defect row offered two shapes, and a third was suggested in its own
`suggested_fix`. **Shape 1 was taken: `schedule_cut` refuses a case that has
already been cut** — the mirror of `commit_cut`'s refusal — **and `commit_cut`'s
own guard was widened to the same predicate**, so both verbs read one fact.

* **Why not the money (shape 2 — guard the second FEE).** The second fee is the
  loudest consequence and not the only one. The same two moves re-date `cut_on`,
  overwrite `outstanding_at_cut` and `reconnection_fee_amount`, and re-open a
  window billing has already closed; a guard on the charge would allow every one
  of those, and `commit_cut`'s own sentence names re-dating in the same breath as
  re-quoting. It would also have to ask billing *has a fee already been raised on
  this case*, which `apps/customers` may not do — it writes and reads no
  financial table except through a seam, and no seam answers that question.
  **The fact that a cut has been recorded belongs to the case, so the guard sits
  on the verbs that read the case.**
* **Why not `halt_reason` (the register's own broader suggestion).** It answers
  *is the LADDER running*, and its codes are grouped on the S90 segment, the
  worklists and the KPI strip. Teaching it that a cut case is halted would
  re-label every cut case on those screens and change what `cut_readiness` and
  `reconnection_readiness` say — a product-wide change of meaning on a guard's
  authority.
* **Why `cut_on` and not the state name.** The state is the one thing another
  verb could move, and moving it is the defect. `commit_cut` is the sole writer
  of `disconnect_cases.cut_on` and nothing ever clears it, so an OPEN case
  carrying one has already had its supply taken away whatever the state column
  says. This is also what refuses the rows the walk-around ALREADY created —
  `scheduled` with a `cut_on` set, a record asserting two incompatible facts —
  which a guard on the state alone would have waved straight through.

### THE LEGITIMATE RE-CUT IS NOT REFUSED, AND THAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE CHOOSING

A household can be cut, reconnected and cut again. It does not come back down
this road: `restore_service` writes `STATE_RESTORED`, which is in
`CLOSED_CASE_STATES`, so `open_case_for` stops returning the case and the next
enforcement opens a **new** case at tier 1 with its own notices, its own
certified proof of service and its own fee.
`test_a_household_cut_reconnected_and_cut_again_is_charged_once_per_case` walks
that sequence end to end and asserts **two** $75.00 invoices against **two**
cases — both correct. A guard keyed on *this account has ever been cut* would
have refused it.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY

* **No database CHECK constraint** (`cut_on` implies a cut-or-later state). It
  would be a third independent ground and this module argues for exactly that
  posture in `assert_cut_reachable` — but migration ordering is a 🔒 sensitive
  path, three lanes are landing migrations on this branch tonight, and the sole
  writer of `scheduled` now refuses. **REPORTED, not built.**
* **Nothing was reversed.** The second $75.00 on `A-11340` is an issued invoice
  with a posted ledger pair; hard rule 4 says a correction is a NEW row, and
  which correction (a credit note, a goodwill adjustment, or leaving it on a
  beta account) is a money decision this lane does not own. It is filed as
  `DEF-CUS-6094` so somebody counts it.
* **No version bump** — six disconnect fixes are landing as one batch and the
  orchestrating session sets one version (`DEF-GOV-3756`'s lesson).

### THE GENERAL HABIT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING

**When a rule is written as a guard on ONE verb, ask which other verb can reach
the same state.** `commit_cut` protected the cut record for three weeks and
looked like a product that protected it — the record screen agreed, greying
*Mark as cut* with *"This supply is already cut."* — while one route earlier
nothing asked the question at all. A refusal that can be walked around in two
moves is not a refusal, and no test in this repo could see it, because until
2026-09-20 no cut had ever committed on any tenant and the state combination
could not exist to be tested.

### THE PROOF, SO THE NEXT LANE CAN RE-RUN IT

`06-backend/tests/test_def_cus_6062_a_cut_cannot_be_un_cut.py`, five cases, each
taking a full before/after census — invoices, invoice lines, journal entries,
journal lines and audit rows. After the first cut: **1 invoice, 1 line, 1
journal entry, 2 journal lines, 7 audit rows.** After BOTH walk-around moves:
**the same six numbers**, and two refusals reading `already_cut`.

**RED first, through pytest.** On the pre-fix tree the two guard cases failed
with *"DID NOT RAISE DisconnectRuleError"* and the two mirror cases passed —
they had to, since they assert the behaviour the fix must not take away. With
`already_cut` monkeypatched to `False` all three guard cases fail again, the
route one as `assert 200 == 422`: the door accepting the walk-around, which is
what a clerk's browser would have received.

**Proved on real PostgreSQL too** (`--ds=config.settings.pgtest`, RLS FORCE):
5 passed. The default suite is SQLite and has neither RLS nor an aborted-
transaction state (CLAUDE.md law 14).

⚠ **AND THE CENSUS CAUGHT ITSELF FIRST.** Its `audit_rows` count read
`audit_log` — which in this suite is never written, because
`tests/test_us_met_helpers.audit_rows` is an `autouse` fixture pointing the
sink at a Python list. It counted **0 before and 0 after**, so `after ==
before` passed over a number that could not move: law 7's *a check that cannot
fail*, inside a file written to prove a guard. It reads the capture sink now,
and what found it was the habit of asserting the census NON-EMPTY beside the
comparison — not a gate, and nothing else in this repo would have.

## 2026-09-21 · A COMMON AREA NEEDS NO PLAN — CONFIRMED, AND THE NEW CONNECT COMMIT IS THE THING THAT MOVES

**PO, verbatim, asked to resolve the collision that blocks every New Connect build:**
*"common area dont need plan"*.

**SO NOTHING SIGNED IS REVERSED.** `BR-MET-040` stands, the 2026-09-16 ruling that a
common area is sent no plan stands, and the option to give a common area a plan was
**declined**. The ruling was put with the real case — **eight builds raised in a browser
and eight refused at the final press** — and three options: anchor the owner's account on
a dwelling, give the common area a plan, or allow an account with no plan. **The PO chose
to keep the common-area rule.**

**WHY THE BUILD REFUSES, READ OUT OF THE CODE RATHER THAN INFERRED.** `BR-MET-040`'s own
text is *"Plan is REQUIRED at account **ACTIVATION**; a unit without a plan blocks with a
message."* `services.py` raises `BIZ_COMPLETENESS` /
`customers.account.plan_required_at_activation` when `unit.rate_plan_id is None`, and it
fires on `activate_account`, on a status change into a billing class, and on
`create_account` / `move_in` **with an occupying status**.

⚠ **AND IT ALREADY HAS A DOCUMENTED EXEMPTION, WHICH IS THE SHAPE OF THE FIX.**
`create_from_import` passes `require_plan=False` — added by `CR-047` task 11 (`DEF-2518`)
because the rule was firing on CREATION, and *"load the estate on day one, assign plans on
day two"* was impossible. **So the rule has always been about activation and not about
existence**, and a master account created over a common area at commit is creation.

**THE SAFETY THAT MAKES THE EXEMPTION SOUND IS ALREADY PROVED AND IS NOT ASSUMED HERE:**
`billing.gather.gather_account` raises `GATHER_NO_PLAN` for any unit with no
`rate_plan_id`, files it on the `resolve-subscription` exception tab and marks it
not-retryable. **An unplanned account can be LOADED and can never be BILLED.** That is the
guarantee the import exemption rests on, and it covers this case identically.

⛔ **WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE, AND A LANE MAY NOT DECIDE IT SILENTLY:** whether the master
account over a common area takes the import's `require_plan=False` path or is anchored
somewhere else entirely. Both keep the PO's ruling. The lane that builds it measures which
is smaller, records the reasoning, and writes a test that goes red if a common area is ever
handed a plan — because that is the rule this ruling protects.

## 2026-09-21 · TWO PO RULINGS ON THE CUT, AND THE FIRST REVERSES WHAT WAS BUILT YESTERDAY

Both arrived in answer to the three sign-offs put on 2026-09-21. **Ruling 1 supersedes a
design this product shipped the day before, so the supersession is STATED here rather
than assumed** (`13-change-process.md` step 2, CLAUDE.md law 13).

---

### 1 · A CUT IS COMPLETED WITHOUT A BILL. THE FINAL BILL IS BILLING'S OWN WORKFLOW.

**PO, verbatim:** *"in single bill we have final bill workflow - so if clark want to
complete the bill he can do it from there - we will need to allow clark to complete the
cut request later without bill."*

⛔ **WHAT THIS REVERSES.** `commit_cut` writes the account status **only when the days are
billed**, and `finish_cut` — built 2026-09-20 under `DEF-CUS-6063` — exists to raise the
refused bill **and** write the status, still refusing the status if the days cannot be
billed. **That refusal is what the PO has just removed.** The reasoning it rested on was
ours, not theirs: *writing the status drops the account out of the bill run with days
still unbilled.* The PO's answer is that the days are not the cut's to bill.

**SO, AND THIS IS THE NEW RULE:**

* **Completing a cut and raising a final bill are two acts.** A clerk may complete the cut
  request **with no bill at all**, and the account status is written.
* **The final bill is raised from billing's own workflow** — the PO names *single bill*,
  and `apps/billing/final_bill.py` and `apps/billing/single.py` are the files. ⚠ **Note
  for the lane: `final_bill.py` today serves MOVE-OUT (S20/S30, `BR-BIL-013`, billed
  through the move day). Whether the cut reuses that door or needs its own entry is a
  build question — measure it, do not assume it.**
* **The hold stays available, it stops being compulsory.** A cut whose bill was refused
  must no longer be stuck; that was the whole of `DEF-CUS-6063`.

⚠ **WHAT MUST NOT BE LOST IN THE REVERSAL, AND A LANE MAY NOT QUIETLY DROP IT:** the
reason the status was held is real — an account marked disconnected leaves the bill run.
**So the unbilled days must remain visible to somebody**, on the account or on the cut,
rather than becoming invisible the moment the status is written. The PO has ruled who
raises the bill, not that the days stop mattering. Build the visibility; do not restore
the refusal.

---

### 2 · THE BILL STARTS THE DAY AFTER THE LAST BILL. ARREARS ARE **PREVIOUS BALANCE**.

**PO, verbatim:** *"you create the bill from last bill date - if last bill was generated
in feb and data is 28 feb you start the bill from 1 mar - for arreras - it is previous
balance - bill will anyway calculate previous balance and mention it on bill; hence we
have accounted or all oustanding amount."*

**This is option (c) of the three put, not option (a) as built.** `DEF-BIL-6093` changed
the window to prefer the **cutover date**; the PO's rule is **the day after the last
bill's period end**, and it subsumes the cutover case rather than contradicting it: an
account migrated in with no bill of ours has nothing before the cutover to bill, and
everything before it is **previous balance**.

**THE WORKED CASE, IN THE PO'S OWN SHAPE:** last bill generated in February covering to
**28 Feb** → the next bill starts **1 March**. Not the account-opened date, and not a
re-run of anything already billed.

**AND THE HALF THAT ANSWERS THE DOUBLE-BILL WORRY OUTRIGHT:** arrears are **never
re-billed**. The bill computes **previous balance** and prints it, so the outstanding is
accounted for without any period being billed twice. That is why starting from the last
bill is safe, and it is the PO's own reasoning: *"hence we have accounted or all
oustanding amount."*

⚠ **SO THE FIVE-AND-A-HALF-YEAR NEAR MISS IS CLOSED FROM BOTH ENDS** — the window starts
after the last bill, and the arrears it does not cover appear as previous balance rather
than as billable days. `DEF-BIL-6093`'s fix is **narrowed rather than kept**: prefer the
last bill's period end, with the cutover date as the fallback when there is no bill.

---

### 3 · THE THIRD SIGN-OFF IS STILL OPEN

The `$75.00` reconnection fee counting as *this account has been billed* was **not
answered** and stays open. ⚠ **Ruling 1 does not moot it:** the fee wrongly satisfying a
*has this been billed* test is a defect wherever that test is read, and ruling 1 changes
who raises the bill rather than what counts as one. It stays on the agenda.

---

## 2026-09-21 · THE THIRD SIGN-OFF IS ANSWERED — A FEE IS A CHARGE FOR AN EVENT, NOT FOR A PERIOD OF SERVICE

⚠ **THE SECTION ABOVE SAYS THIS ONE IS STILL OPEN. IT WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND IS NOW
SUPERSEDED, ABOUT TWO MINUTES LATER.** Left in place and corrected here rather than
edited, because a register body that contradicts its own status is what `DEF-WRK-4030`
records — and a reader who meets the earlier section must meet this one.

**PO, verbatim, choosing option (a) and quoting the reasoning back:** *"A fee is a charge
for an event, not for a period of service - this is correct"*.

**SO THE BUILT BEHAVIOUR IS RATIFIED, NOT CHANGED.** `DEF-CUS-6086` already stopped a
`$75.00` reconnection fee satisfying a *has this account been billed* test. This ruling is
the signature over it.

**THE WORKED CASE THAT WAS PUT, AND IT IS WHAT THE SIGNATURE COVERS:** on `A-11340` the
fee invoice landed dated the day of the cut, so every later attempt to finish that cut
answered *"an issued bill already covers this account through 2026-09-20"* with
`billed=true`. On that account it would have written **Disconnected across 15 March 2021 →
20 September 2026 on the strength of `$75.00`.** The PO was shown that span and that
figure.

⚠ **AND THE SIGN-OFF RULE HAS A SECOND HALF THAT IS NOT YET DONE.** CLAUDE.md: *"the
ruling is written into the ledger row verbatim with its date and the exact statements
shown, and **a test asserts the ratified figure so drift goes RED**."* The behaviour has
tests; what it does not yet have is a test that asserts **this ratified sentence** — that
a charge for an EVENT never satisfies a *billed a period* question. **A lane owes that
test, and the review-ledger row for `cut_bill.py` is where it is recorded.**

⛔ **THE SCOPE OF THE SIGNATURE, STATED SO IT IS NOT STRETCHED:** it covers the
reconnection fee and the *has this been billed* test it was wrongly satisfying. It does
**not** silently reclassify every other charge in the product. A lane finding the same
shape elsewhere raises it; it does not assume this ruling already covered it.

## 2026-09-21 · THE THREE REFUSALS THAT BLOCK EVERY NEW CONNECT BUILD ARE RULED — TWO GO, ONE STAYS

Put to the PO as the table of refusals stopping a build from being created, each with what
a clerk sees. **All three answered in one reply.** Eight builds were raised in a browser
and **eight were refused at the final press**; these rulings are what unblock them.

---

### 1 · A COMMON AREA NEEDS NO RATE PLAN — AND THE REQUIREMENT BECOMES **OPTIONAL**

**PO, verbatim:** *"common area dont need rate plan as of now; make this optional"*.

This carries the earlier *"common area dont need plan"* one step further: it is not merely
that a common area is **sent** no plan, it is that the plan **requirement must not fire on
one**. `BR-MET-040` — *"Plan is REQUIRED at account activation; a unit without a plan
blocks with a message"* — is **narrowed**, not reversed: it goes on holding for a dwelling
and stops holding for a common area.

⚠ **THE WORDS *"AS OF NOW"* ARE THE PO'S AND ARE KEPT.** This is a deliberate, dated
position and not a permanent property of common areas. **Build it as a condition that can
be read and changed, never as a deletion of the rule.**

---

### 2 · A COMMON AREA IS **OPTIONAL** ON A BUILD

**PO, verbatim:** *"common area is option"*.

⛔ **SO THE SECOND REFUSAL GOES TOO, AND IT IS THE ONE WITH THE WIDER BLAST RADIUS.**
`BR-CUS-068` defines the master account as sitting **over the premises' common areas**
(PO 2026-08-22, `OQ-314`). With no common area there was nothing for the owner's account
to anchor on, so a clerk who did the sensible thing for a single house — no common area —
was refused for the opposite reason to the clerk who kept one.

**A build must commit with no common area at all, and the owner's master account must
still be created.** Where it anchors instead is the build question: a dwelling unit, or
the premises itself. ⚠ **`BR-CUS-068` is a SIGNED rule and this ruling narrows it — the
supersession is stated here, and the lane amends the rule's own row with its date rather
than leaving two documents disagreeing.**

---

### 3 · REQUIRING AN OWNER AT STEP 1 **STAYS**

**PO, verbatim:** *"Step 1 with no owner - this is correct"*.

The wizard goes on refusing to move past step 1 until an owner is named. **Nothing
changes**, and it is recorded so no lane later reads the other two rulings as licence to
relax this one.

---

### WHAT THIS MEANS TOGETHER, BECAUSE THE THREE ONLY MAKE SENSE AS A SET

A build is: **an owner, always** · **units** · **a common area only if there is one** ·
**a rate plan on dwellings, not on the common area**. The pincer that refused all eight
builds is opened from both sides at once — a build with a common area no longer needs a
plan on it, and a build without one no longer lacks an anchor.

⛔ **AND THE SAFETY THAT MADE THE PLAN RULE WORTH HAVING IS UNTOUCHED AND MUST STAY
PROVED:** `billing.gather.gather_account` raises `GATHER_NO_PLAN` for any unit with no
`rate_plan_id` and files it as not-retryable. **An unplanned unit can exist and can never
be billed.** That is what makes an optional requirement safe rather than reckless, it was
verified rather than assumed, and **a test must hold it** — if that ever stops being true,
these rulings need re-putting.

---

## 2026-09-21 · APPLICATION FEES BECOME OPTIONAL, SO AN APPLICATION CAN BE APPROVED

**PO, verbatim:** *"make application fees optional - so that we can approve it"*.

**WHAT WAS BLOCKING.** Approving a service request is refused until its fee is settled —
a ratified rule, and right in itself. The trap is that the counter screen **invites a part
payment** in as many words: *"Take whatever they hand over… you do not refuse them."* A
clerk who does that then cannot approve, and **both doors out are broken**:

* recording a second payment is refused — *"A fee was already collected against receipt
  `{{receiptNo}}`"*, with the placeholder printing raw, and its advice points at Payments,
  **a module whose payments cannot move this figure because these fees never reach the
  ledger**;
* waiving the fee is a **silent 500** — the screen sends the fee's line number where the
  endpoint wants its database id. Pressed four times in the walk; the server threw four
  times and the screen said nothing at all.

**THE RULING: the fee stops being a precondition of approval.** An application may be
approved with its fee unpaid, part-paid or waived.

⛔ **WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY, AND A LANE MUST NOT READ IT WIDER.** It does **not** abolish
the fee, cancel what has been collected, or make the fee invisible. **The money is still
owed and still recorded** — what changes is that it no longer gates the decision. A
part-paid fee must remain visible on the request after approval, or this ruling converts
a blocked approval into a forgotten debt.

⚠ **AND THE TWO BROKEN DOORS ARE STILL DEFECTS.** `DEF-CUS-6096` (the silent 500 on waive)
and `DEF-CUS-6097` (the raw `{{receiptNo}}`) are **not** closed by this ruling. Making the
gate optional removes the urgency, not the faults — a clerk who chooses to waive a fee
will still meet a 500 that says nothing. **Fix them; do not close them as overtaken.**

⚠ **THE DEEPER SHAPE, WORTH KEEPING:** a screen that *invites* an action and a rule that
*refuses* its consequence is a contradiction the product presents to a clerk as their own
mistake. The part-payment invitation and the settled-fee gate were each correct alone.
**Neither side was wrong and nothing asked whether the pair was walkable** — which is the
same failure recorded for the picked-address defect the same week.

## 2026-09-21 · THREE RULINGS ON THE NEW CONNECT WIZARD — AND ONE OF THEM IS A NEW BUSINESS RULE

Put to the PO as *"not refusals, but they break the flow"* — three things the acceptance
walk found that let a clerk through and then produced the wrong build. **All three
answered in one reply**, and the third is a rule this product did not have.

---

### 1 · THE DATE AT STEP 4 IS A **PLANNED** INSTALLATION DATE

**PO, verbatim:** *"say planned installation date"*.

**The walk found sixteen install dates typed on a seven-unit block and sent nowhere.** The
reading taken at the time was that they were discarded. **The PO's answer is that the
FIELD was mislabelled, not that the data is junk:** it is a **planned** date, and it should
say so.

⚠ **THIS SITS EXACTLY ON THE RULING OF 2026-09-21 ABOUT ASSETS AND MUST NOT CONTRADICT
IT.** *"install date on work order completion - yes"* — the **actual** install date is
written when the crew's work order completes, and `create_asset_for_unit`'s
`data.setdefault("install_date", tenant_today())` was the defect (`DEF-AST-5443`). **So the
two dates are different facts and the product needs both:** what a clerk EXPECTS at step 4,
and what actually HAPPENED at completion. **A lane must not store the planned date in the
`install_date` column** — that is the defect wearing a new label.

**So: rename the field to *Planned installation date*, and give the planned value somewhere
of its own to live.** If nothing can hold it yet, say so on the screen rather than taking
sixteen keystrokes into a void.

---

### 2 · THE WIZARD **ASKS FOR THE PLAN**

**PO, verbatim:** *"ask for plan"*.

The review screen shows **`Plan assignments 0`** as a plain fact, calls those counts *"a
contract"*, and **lets the clerk press anyway** — and the press then fails. The clerk chose
a plan four steps earlier, so the zero reads as information rather than as a warning.

**The wizard asks for the plan.** Not a zero shown after the fact; an ask, at the point a
clerk can answer it.

⚠ **AND THIS MEETS THE COMMON-AREA RULINGS OF THE SAME DAY — READ BOTH BEFORE BUILDING.**
*"common area dont need rate plan as of now; make this optional"* means the ask must be
about **dwellings**, and a common area must not be dragged into it. **A wizard that demands
a plan for a common area would re-create the refusal the PO just removed.**

---

### 3 · **NEW RULE** — NO COMMON AREA FOR A SINGLE-FAMILY PREMISES OR A RELATED CLASS

**PO, verbatim:** *"build this rule - no common area for single family or related classes"*.

**The walk's trap:** step 3 opens with *Include a common-area unit* **already ticked** and
no dwellings. A clerk building a house has no unit numbers to type, leaves the boxes empty
and carries on — and **the build is one common area and no dwelling at all**, with nothing
on screen saying that is wrong.

**THE RULE: a single-family premises, and the classes like it, get no common area.** The
tick is not merely unticked by default — **the option does not apply to those classes.**

⚠ **THIS IS A NEW BUSINESS RULE AND IS MINTED, NOT INFERRED.** The PO said *"build this
rule"*. It gets a `BR-` id in the owning module's `02-business-rules.md`, CONFIRMED with
its date and the PO's words, and every screen and document that offers the tick is stamped
in the same commit (CLAUDE.md law 10).

⛔ **AND *"OR RELATED CLASSES"* IS THE PO'S PHRASE AND IS NOT A LANE'S TO GUESS AT.**
`premises_type` is a closed list. **A lane enumerates the classes it proposes to include,
writes them into the rule, and states that the list is its reading of *related* — it does
not silently decide which of the drawn premise types are house-like.** If the reading is
wrong, it must be wrong **visibly**, in the rule's own row.

⚠ **IT ALSO INTERACTS WITH THE SAME DAY'S *"common area is option"*.** The two are
consistent and the difference matters: for most classes the common area is **optional**;
for a single-family premises it is **absent**. A lane building only the first leaves the
trap in place for exactly the build the walk found.

---

## 2026-09-21 · THE APPLICATION FEE IS `$20` OR `$0`, AND SOME UTILITIES TAKE NONE — A CORRECTION TO OUR OWN FRAMING

**PO, verbatim, correcting the case we put to them:** *"in practical this does not ahppen -
it is application fees - customer will pay it once or clark will wavie it off - $20 or $0 -
some utilities will not take applciation fees also - so your scenario is hypotetical"*.

⚠ **THE PART-PAYMENT SCENARIO WAS OURS AND IT IS WRONG ABOUT THE WORLD.** The section
*"APPLICATION FEES BECOME OPTIONAL"* above builds its whole argument on a clerk taking a
part payment and coming back for the rest. **That does not happen.** An application fee is
a small flat amount: it is **paid once**, or it is **waived**, or **the utility charges
none at all**.

**THE THREE REAL SHAPES, AND THEY ARE THE ONLY THREE:**

1. **Paid once, in full** — `$20`, one payment, one receipt.
2. **Waived** — the clerk waives it, and under the same day's ruling *"waiving is options"*
   that path must work. It is today a **silent 500** (`DEF-CUS-6096`).
3. **The utility takes no application fee** — `$0`, and **nothing should ask for one.**

⛔ **THE THIRD IS A REQUIREMENT WE DID NOT HAVE AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.** *"Some
utilities will not take applciation fees also."* A utility configured with no application
fee must be able to take an application from end to end **without ever meeting a fee
screen, a fee gate or a fee refusal.** That is not a relaxation of the gate the PO already
made optional — it is a whole surface that should not appear. **A lane must prove it on a
tenant configured at `$0`, not reason about it.**

⚠ **AND THE COUNTER SCREEN'S OWN WORDS ARE NOW SUSPECT.** *"Take whatever they hand over…
you do not refuse them"* is what invited the part payment. On a `$20` flat application fee
that sentence **invites a case that does not occur and creates the trap we then reported as
a defect.** It may be correct copy that belongs to a different payment context and was
reused here. **Check where it came from before changing it** — it may be right elsewhere.

**WHAT THIS CHANGES IN PRIORITY, STATED SO NOBODY RE-READS THE OLDER SECTION AS CURRENT:**
`DEF-CUS-6097` (the raw `{{receiptNo}}`) and the *"Record further payment in Payments"*
advice are **real faults on a path a clerk will rarely walk** — fix them, do not lead with
them. **The waive working, and a `$0` utility never meeting a fee at all, are the work.**

⚠ **THE LESSON IS OURS AND IT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE CORRECTION.** The walk found a real
sequence, reproduced it, and filed it accurately — and **we built the reasoning around the
rarest of the three shapes because it was the one the product broke on.** A defect that is
easy to reproduce is not thereby the one that matters. **Ask what the money actually looks
like before ranking a finding**; the PO answered that in nine words and it re-ordered three
items.

---

## 2026-09-21 · *"RELATED CLASSES"* IS ANSWERED — FOUR PREMISE TYPES TAKE NO COMMON AREA, TWO KEEP IT

The PO ruled *"build this rule - no common area for single family or related classes"*.
**A lane may not guess which classes are *related***, so the tenant's six premise types
were read out of the database and put to the PO as a list. **All four were ticked.**

**NO COMMON AREA — the option does not apply to these four:**

| code | name |
|---|---|
| `single_family` | Single-family |
| `mobile_home_park` | Mobile-home park |
| `commercial_building` | Commercial building |
| `government_building` | Government building |

**THE COMMON AREA STAYS OPTIONAL — these two only:**

| code | name |
|---|---|
| `apartment_complex` | Apartment complex |
| `mixed_use` | Mixed-use |

**AND THE SPLIT IS COHERENT, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT MAKES THE RULE
PREDICTABLE:** the two that keep a common area are the genuinely **multi-occupier** types.
The four that lose it are single-occupier premises, however large — a commercial or
government building here is **one premises with one supply**, not a campus with shared
space to meter separately. ⚠ **That reading is OURS, drawn from the PO's choice; if a
utility ever meters a commercial block's lobby, the rule and not the reading is what must
change.**

⚠ **THE LIST IS THIS TENANT'S, AND THAT IS A LIMIT ON THE RULE.** `premises_types` is a
per-tenant lookup table — these six are `brazosbend`'s. **A utility with a type not in this
list has no ruling**, so the rule must be written to name the four **by code** and to treat
an unknown type as *common area optional* (the safer default, since it refuses nothing).
**A lane must not hard-code "four of six" as a count**, and must state on the rule's row
that the going-live customer's own type list may add classes the PO has not ruled on.

⛔ **THIS COMPLETES THE SET OF THREE COMMON-AREA RULINGS AND THEY MUST BE BUILT TOGETHER:**
a common area needs **no rate plan** (*"make this optional"*) · a common area is
**optional** on a build (*"common area is option"*) · and for these four types it is
**absent**. A lane building only the first two leaves the trap the acceptance walk found —
a clerk building a house gets one common area and no dwelling.

---

## 2026-09-21 · ⛔ CORRECTION — A COMMON AREA IS **OPTIONAL, NOT FORBIDDEN**. I MISRECORDED THE PO'S ANSWER AND A LANE WAS BUILDING FROM IT.

**PO, verbatim, correcting me:** *"i said Comemrcial Building also Common area is optional
not mandetory , I did not say No common area"*.

⚠ **THE SECTION ABOVE — *"FOUR PREMISE TYPES TAKE NO COMMON AREA, TWO KEEP IT"* — IS
WRONG AND IS SUPERSEDED IN FULL.** It is left in place and corrected here rather than
edited, because a lane was already building from it and a reader who meets it must meet
this.

**THE FAULT WAS MINE AND IT WAS IN THE QUESTION, NOT THE ANSWER.** I asked *"which of them
should have **no common area at all**?"* and offered ticks. The PO ticked four. **I then
recorded those four as FORBIDDING a common area.** What they were answering is that a
common area is **not mandatory** on those types — which is a different thing, and they have
now said so in as many words.

**THE RULE, CORRECTED:**

* **A common area is OPTIONAL on every premise type.** It is never mandatory.
* ⛔ **NO premise type FORBIDS one.** Nothing is refused for having one.
* **What the original ruling was actually about is the DEFAULT.** The trap the acceptance
  walk found is that step 3 opens with *Include a common-area unit* **already ticked** and
  no dwellings, so a clerk building a house carries on and gets **one common area and no
  dwelling**. ⚠ **The defect is the pre-tick, not the possibility.**

**SO THE `BR-` ROW BEING MINTED MUST SAY *optional, never pre-selected* — NOT *absent for
four classes*.** A lane that has already written the four codes as a refusal must remove
that refusal.

---

### WHAT THIS SETTLES WITHOUT A SECOND QUESTION — 500 MAIN ST IS LEGAL

The lane held a seed fixture rather than move it, which was right, and counted the picture
first: **79 seeded properties — 67 single-family, 8 commercial, 3 apartment complexes, 1
government — and EXACTLY ONE carries a common area.** It is `500 Main St`, a
`commercial_building` with **31 units and 1 common area**, drawn in the blueprint as Ridge
Property LLC's estate with Ridge Coffee Co. in unit 200 and twenty-five apartments still to
be built.

**Under the corrected rule that building is perfectly legal and the seed needs no change.**
The eleven held cases in `test_def709_seeded_master_account.py` should go green again
without touching the fixture.

⚠ **AND THE HOLD IS THE REASON THIS WAS CAUGHT AT ALL.** Had the lane "fixed" the seed to
match my wrong rule, the evidence that the rule was wrong would have been deleted quietly,
and the product would have started refusing a shape the PO never refused. **A red that is
honest beat a green that hides a question**, exactly as it was asked to.

⚠ **ONE MORE FACT WORTH KEEPING, BECAUSE IT INVERTS THE ASSUMPTION:** the three **apartment
complexes** we seed have **no common area between them**. The type everyone assumes needs
one has none in our own data, and the single case that has one is a commercial estate.
**Nobody should reason about common areas from intuition about type names again** — that
is what produced my question and my error.

---

### THE LESSON, AND IT IS MINE

**A tick-list answers the question that was asked, not the question that was meant.** I
offered *"no common area at all"* and read four ticks as a prohibition the PO never
uttered. Their original words were *"no common area for single family or related classes"*
— and *"no common area for X"* in a sentence about a **default** is not the same as *"X may
not have one"*.

**When a ruling will become a REFUSAL in code, put the refusal back to the PO in those
words** — *"the product will refuse a commercial building that has a common area"* — rather
than offering a list to tick. A refusal is a strong thing to build from a checkbox.

## 2026-09-21 · THE FEE STOPS GATING APPROVAL, THE WAIVE WORKS, AND A `$0` UTILITY STILL MEETS A FEE SCREEN

**Built by lane APP-8 from the two rulings of this date** — *"make application fees
optional - so that we can approve it"*, *"waiving is options and can you fix the issue
here"*, and the same day's correction, *"in practical this does not ahppen … $20 or $0 -
some utilities will not take applciation fees also"*. **Proved in a browser on an isolated
database, not reasoned about**; the walk is `10-scripts/po20260921_application_fee_walkthrough.mjs`
and it ran CLEAN with **zero 5xx**.

### 1 · THE GATE IS GONE AND THE DEBT IS NOT

`fee_condition` keeps `state: blocked` and moves `blocking` to **False** — the identical
shape the documents ruling of 2026-09-16 took one function up, and for the same reason:
`Condition.clear` reads the STATE, so calling this clear would print *"4 of 4 conditions
clear"* over an open balance. **Not mandatory is not the same as not mentioned.** The
condition leaves `blocking_conditions` and lands in `outstanding_conditions`.

**Walked, at 1440, on `SR-26-0015`:** `$20.00` quoted and untouched → the head's `Approve`
is LIVE, the modal's commit is LIVE, the approval goes through, and the panel afterwards
still reads **`$20.00` outstanding**. That last clause is the narrow reading of the ruling
and it is the whole of what stops this becoming a forgotten debt.

⚠ **AND THE CONDITION'S OWN SENTENCE HAD TO MOVE WITH IT — hard-won law 1 wearing a
translation, and it was nearly missed.** `customers.serviceRequest.condition.feeOutstandingAmount`
read *"{{amount}} {{currency}} of the fee is outstanding. **Approval waits until it is
settled.**"* — a sentence that became FALSE the moment `blocking` went to False, in all eleven
languages, on the one screen a clerk reads before pressing. It now reads **"Fee outstanding:
{{amount}} {{currency}}. Approval is not blocked."**, and its line-count sibling with it. The
documents ruling of 2026-09-16 had to do exactly this for `requiredDocumentMissing` and said so
in its own docstring; **nothing catches it** — no gate compares a rule with the sentence
describing it, and it was found only by opening `en.json` to check a placeholder. Both lines
left `g33_refusal_copy_baseline.txt`, which is the only direction that file moves.

⚠⚠ **AND FIXING THAT SENTENCE WAS NOT ENOUGH, WHICH IS THE TRAP WORTH KEEPING.**
`condition.feeOutstanding` has i18next **plural siblings** — `_one` and `_other` — and
when a key is called with a `count`, **i18next renders the SIBLING and never the base**.
So the base key was corrected in eleven catalogues, every check went green, and the
sentence a clerk would actually have read was still the old one: *"{{count}} application
fee lines are still unsettled."* **Nothing caught it.** `G32` resolves plurals correctly
and was therefore satisfied by the base key; `G33` measures `en.json`'s English and was
satisfied by the corrected base; `G15` counts parity, which never broke. It was found by
printing the shipped key set back out of the live tip and reading it — the same habit
that found the placeholder in the first place.
**The general form: when you correct a key, correct its plural siblings in the same
breath, because the siblings are the ones that render.** Twenty-two values moved here,
not eleven.

⚠ **THIS CLOSES `DEF-CUS-5399`, AND THE THING THAT FOUND IT WAS A TEST WRITTEN TO FIND IT.**
Two signed screens had disagreed since 2026-09-15: `REQ-03.5` said the unpaid fee *"simply
cannot be approved yet"*, the Accounts blueprint p083 said *"The money does not gate approval
and the documents do"*. Lane A could not pick between them, so it pinned the product AS BUILT
with a note — *"the day the rule moves this case goes red and names which of the two
changed."* **The rule moved and the case went red and named it.** It is REWRITTEN, not
deleted: it now approves with the `$105.00` outstanding and reads the figure back through the
same reader afterwards. That is hard-won law 2's second half working, and it is worth more
than the defect it caught.

### 2 · THE WAIVE — `DEF-CUS-6096`, AND THE REPORTED CAUSE WAS RIGHT

**The cause was verified before it was fixed, in the harness, not by reading.** The payload
served `line_no` and no `id`; the row action posted `String(line.line_no)`; `fees/{fee_id}/waive`
looks the row up by **uuid7 primary key**. The red proof names it exactly —
`django.core.exceptions.ValidationError: ['"1" is not a valid UUID.']`, raised INSIDE the ORM
before any rule was reached, so it left the API as a **500**.

**Two independent faults were stacked, which is why it survived a whole walk**, and both are
fixed:

* the payload now serves `id` beside `line_no`, and the row action sends it. `line_no` stays —
  it is what a clerk reads and what `data-fee-line` is keyed on. **One names a row to a person,
  the other names it to an endpoint.**
* `useMutation` on the request detail carried `onSuccess` and **no `onError` at all**, so every
  refusal from every direct-posting control — `Waive`, `Verify`, `Reject`, `Add note`,
  `Record that I searched` — was thrown away between the server and the screen. **The MODALS
  were never affected and that is why nobody noticed**: `post()` hands the envelope to
  `FormModal`, which renders it. Two paths out of one screen, one with no error branch.

`_fee_row` is a second line of defence: a malformed id is now the same typed 404 a row
belonging to another tenant gets (`HR-1`), never a crash.

**Walked:** the line reads `Waived — Waived at the counter.` and the network carried no 5xx.

### 3 · `DEF-CUS-6097` — THE PLACEHOLDER, AND THE ADVICE THAT MATTERED MORE

The server passed `receipt_no`; all eleven catalogues interpolated `{{receiptNo}}`. **i18next
renders an unmatched placeholder verbatim rather than throwing**, so there was no console
error, no failing render and no failing check anywhere — a clerk simply read the word
`{{receiptNo}}`, four lines below the receipt number it existed to quote.

**Counted, because a declared blind spot with no number attached is indistinguishable from an
empty one (law 7).** Across `06-backend/apps`, **610 refusal call sites resolve to a catalogue
sentence**. Of those, **exactly ONE** was this snake_case-to-camelCase shape — the one filed —
and **THREE more** are the wider shape, a placeholder no parameter fills at all
(`customers.account.move_out_behind_issued_bill` wants `{{billed_through}}` and is given
`issued_through`; `metering.import.pattern_token_unknown` wants `{{value}}`;
`rating.bulk.batch_already_applied` wants `{{created_at}}`). Filed as `DEF-CUS-6103`.
A fourth candidate is a false positive — `rating.charges.locked_referenced` receives `plans`
through `**used`.

⚠ **AND THE ADVICE WAS THE WORSE HALF.** It read *"Record further payment in Payments."*
**Verified: it cannot work.** `fees_tab` serves `posts_to_ledger: false`, the open balance is
`quoted − settled − collected` off the request's OWN columns, and `collected` is
`ServiceRequest.fee_collected`, which **only** `collect_fee` writes — and `collect_fee` is the
very call being refused. Nothing in Payments moves that figure. **A refusal that gives
impossible advice is worse than one that gives none.**

The sentence now reads, in eleven languages and each in its own:

> **Fee already collected against receipt `{{receipt_no}}`. Waive the line, or approve anyway.**

Six words per sentence, two sentences (B14 rule 33 — measured, and `g33_refusal_copy_baseline.txt`
SHRANK by its line, which is the only direction that file moves). Both doors it names are real
and are the ones this day's ruling opened.

### 4 · `$0` — THE REQUIREMENT WE DO NOT MEET, STATED PLAINLY

**The GATE is absent and always was**: a request with no fee line totals zero, the condition
reports CLEAR rather than merely non-blocking, nothing is refused and the request approves.
That case was GREEN at the tip before a line changed, which is worth recording — the `$0`
utility was never blocked.

⛔ **THE SCREEN IS NOT ABSENT, AND IT CANNOT BE MADE ABSENT TODAY.** Walked on `SR-26-0017`:
the FEES panel renders, `Record what was handed over` is offered, and the Decision tab names a
fee. **One part of that was our own defect and is fixed** — the panel printed *"No fee has been
raised on this request yet."* **twice**, once in its body and once as the disclosure header's
value, beside a `0.00 collected of 0.00 quoted` summary drawing money **with no currency behind
it**, which is exactly what the four-figure grid above already refuses. B14 rule 32 gives a
section one sentence; a derivation of nothing derives nothing.

⚠ **A first draft of that fix hid the whole disclosure and took the CONNECTION QUOTE's own
stated absence with it** — a different fact from the application fee, and one a `$0` utility
still has. It was narrowed to the three figures in the header. **A fix wider than its defect
deletes a surface nobody asked about**, and the only thing that caught it was an existing DOM
case going red.

**The rest is a BUILD and is filed as `DEF-CUS-6102`, because there is nothing to configure
from.** A fee line exists if and only if somebody called `add_fee_line` on that request. So
**`$0` is the absence of an act, not a configured posture**, and no screen can decide to hide
itself because nothing knows the utility charges nothing. `BR-CUS-095`'s
`ServiceRequestDocumentRequirement` is exactly the missing shape one table over — per
`(request_type × doc_type)`, *"we ship with nothing ticked, and a utility that configures
nothing blocks nothing"* — and the fee has no counterpart. A test asserts that ABSENCE by name
so the day it is built the case goes RED and names itself, rather than the gap living in a
docstring nobody re-reads.

⚠ **AND A SECOND ABSENCE WAS MET ON THE WAY — ALREADY FILED, AND NAMED HERE SO NOBODY FILES IT
TWICE.** `addServiceRequestFee` is exported by `serviceRequestEndpoints.ts` and **called from
nowhere**: no clerk can raise an application fee line through this product at all, and every fee
line in the demo tenant came from the seed. That is **`DEF-CUS-5904`** (2026-09-19, OPEN), and it
is hard-won law 2's original shape — built, not wired — on a money path. It is worth reading
beside `DEF-CUS-6102`: the *"no clerk can raise one"* defect and the *"a utility that charges none
still meets the screen"* requirement are two halves of the same missing surface, and whoever
builds the fee setting should close both.

### 5 · THE COUNTER'S OWN WORDS — CHECKED, REPORTED, NOT CHANGED

*"Take whatever they hand over… you do not refuse them"* is
`customers.serviceRequest.collect.shortfallIsFine`, and the PO asked where it came from before
anybody touched it. **It was not reused from another payment context.** `git log -S` puts it,
and the whole Collect dialog's copy, in `d54a7f7d7` on **2026-09-20** — authored for this
dialog, one call site, as a paraphrase of `BR-CUS-090`, which is a CONFIRMED ruling and is
still right: the counter does not refuse a shortfall.

**What is wrong with it is proportion, not truth.** It is **39 words** where B14 rule 33 gives
an instruction six per sentence and rationale **zero**, and `G33` never sees it because G33
walks only REFUSAL keys — this is a note beside a control. Filed as `DEF-CUS-6104` and left
standing: shortening it changes what a clerk believes they may do, and the rule it restates is
signed.

### 5a · A RED NOBODY CAUSED AND NOBODY READ, FOR TWO DAYS — `DEF-CUS-6105`

**`test_cr094_approval_raises_the_job.py` had 17 of its 17 cases failing**, and the proof
that it was not this lane is the only kind worth having: the same file was run against a
**pristine archive of the tip** and failed identically, 17 for 17. The cause is
`ServiceRequestRuleError: unknown lifecycle action 'pick_up'`. The PO ruling of 2026-09-19
cut thirteen lifecycle moves to four — *"see service request i simple … we have to keep it
simple"* — and `7b8695616` retired `pick_up` with eight siblings. **The test helpers that
call it were not updated in that commit.**

⚠ **THIS IS HARD-WON LAW 7'S FIRST BULLET, WORD FOR WORD: PROVED RED, THEN NEVER READ.**
The ruling did the right thing twice over — it kept the retired constants DEFINED on
purpose, *"so a caller that has not been updated then reaches `next_state`, which raises
this module's own `ServiceRequestRuleError` naming the action — rather than an
`AttributeError` three frames away that reads like a broken import."* The failure named
itself, loudly, in the exact words a reader needs. **Nothing read it.** No gate runs
pytest, so seventeen dead cases sat for two days — including the hold-expiry case for
`DEF-CUS-5399`, which is the one thing that could have announced this ruling's arrival.

⚠ **AND IT WAS CAMOUFLAGED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** The same runs emit
`kombu.exceptions.OperationalError: Error 111 connecting to localhost:6379` from an
unrelated teardown path, so the **first and most visible line of every traceback points at
a missing Redis** rather than at the retired action. A lane glancing at that concludes
*"environment"* and moves on. It took `--tb=long` and reading past the top of the stack.

**Fixed in three files here, because it had to be**: the rewritten `DEF-CUS-5399` case
lives in that file and could not otherwise be proved. `test_br_cus_1077_move_in_job.py`
carries the same call behind a guard that happens to be False and was therefore never
reached — left dead, deliberately, with a note saying why.

**The mechanical half of the cure, if anyone wants one:** a check that `RETIRED_ACTIONS`
appears in no file under `tests/`. It would have failed inside the ruling's own commit.

### 6 · THE LESSON, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT FEES

The walk found a real sequence, reproduced it and filed it accurately — and **the reasoning was
then built around the rarest of the three shapes because it was the one the product broke on.**
The PO answered that in nine words and it re-ordered three items. **A defect that is easy to
reproduce is not thereby the one that matters: ask what the money actually looks like before
ranking a finding.**

And a second, smaller one with a wider reach: **two of the four faults here were silences.**
A 500 with no error branch, and a placeholder i18next renders verbatim. Neither had a console
error, a red test or a failing gate — and both were found only by a person, or a walk, LOOKING
AT A SCREEN. That is hard-won law 6, still the only check in this repository that reads
rendered output.

## 2026-09-21 · 🛠 BUILT: THE CUT COMPLETES WITHOUT A BILL, THE WINDOW OPENS AFTER THE LAST BILL, AND THE FEE RULING HAS ITS TEST

Lane CUT-8, building the three rulings recorded earlier today — *"TWO PO RULINGS ON THE
CUT, AND THE FIRST REVERSES WHAT WAS BUILT YESTERDAY"* and *"THE THIRD SIGN-OFF IS
ANSWERED"*. Nothing here is a new rule; all three are the PO's own words, built.

### 1 · A CLERK COMPLETES THE CUT REQUEST WITH NO BILL, AND THE STATUS IS WRITTEN

**Reproduced first, in a browser, before a line was read** (`22-product-maintenance-process.md`
steps 1–3, not `r11` — a user can do this task today, so it is MAINTENANCE). On an
isolated database cloned by template, `A-11996` was walked through the real ladder and
cut on **21 September 2026** from the case record. Billing refused the final bill —
*"base charge code BASE-E prices per connection size and states no amount for size
None"* — so the status was HELD, exactly as designed. `Finish disconnection` then offered
**one** control, it failed with the engine's sentence, and **there was no second thing a
clerk could do.** That is the refusal the PO removed.

**BUILT: `finish_cut(..., without_bill=True)`.** The dialog now asks one question —
`The final bill` · `Raise it now` / `Complete without it` — and the second answer writes
BR-CUS-107's `Disconnected` with no bill at all. **The bill is SKIPPED rather than
attempted and ignored**: a clerk who asked to complete without a bill has not asked to be
billed, and the test that proves it uses a seam that RAISES if billing is called at all,
because a stub returning `blocked` could not tell the two apart.

⚠ **WHERE THE FINAL BILL IS RAISED INSTEAD, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The PO named
*single bill*, and `apps/billing/final_bill.py` today serves MOVE-OUT: `settle_final_bill`
refuses any bill_type but `final` by name and applies the deposit and its interest against
the whole closing position (BR-BIL-013). `DSC-02.4` forbids exactly that at a cut — *"Close
the account or settle the deposit — that is a move-out, not a disconnect"*. **So the cut
does NOT reuse the move-out door and nothing was wired into it.** What this lane built is
the completion half; which door in billing raises a cut's late final bill is left to the
billing lane, and the days it must cover now travel on the record rather than in nobody's
head.

⚠ **WHAT WAS NOT LOST.** The reason the status was held is real — a `disconnected` account
leaves `selectors.accounts_for_bill_run`, so no ordinary run picks those days up.
`unbilled_days_at_cut` states them on the completion payload, on `audit_log`, and as a row
on the case record and in the dialog: **`Days not billed · 09/21/2026 – 09/21/2026 ·
1 day`**. **It is DERIVED on every read and nothing is stored**, so the statement closes
itself the day a bill covers the cut — a column written at completion would go on saying
*unbilled* for ever, which is hard-won law 1's shape. And billing NOT ANSWERING is reported
as `unbilled_days_not_readable` rather than as silence: through a seam, *nothing is
unbilled* and *nobody could be asked* are the same `None`, and only one of them is good
news (DEF-035).

**MEASURED AFTER THE COMMIT:** `A-11996` reads `Disconnected`; `closed_at` is NULL and the
deposit is untouched (`DSC-02.4` intact); the account's only invoice is still the one
**$75.00** reconnection fee, so no bill was raised; the `disconnect.cut.finished` audit row
carries `cut_bill: null`, `days_not_billed: 1 day` and
`completed: cut_completed_without_a_final_bill`.

### 2 · THE WINDOW OPENS THE DAY AFTER THE LAST BILL — AND THE DOCSTRING WAS WRONG

**The code already did the right thing and its own docstring said otherwise.**
`first_unbilled_day` returns on the FIRST answer it gets — last issued service bill, then
the migration's `as_of`, then the move-in date — which is precisely the precedence the PO
ruled. The paragraph `DEF-BIL-6093` added on 2026-09-20 ended *"the LATEST of the two
answers wins overall"*, **and nothing in the function takes a maximum.** That is hard-won
law 1 on a 🔒 money path: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. **Only the
docstring moved**; `DEF-BIL-6093`'s fix is narrowed to *the cutover is the FALLBACK*, and
a test now pins all three levels so the sentence and the code cannot drift apart again.

**THE PO'S OWN WORKED SHAPE IS ITS OWN CASE:** last bill covering to **28 February** → the
next window starts **1 March**.

**AND THE HALF THAT CLOSES THE DOUBLE-BILL WORRY OUTRIGHT — ARREARS ARE NEVER RE-BILLED.**
Proved end to end on a migrated account through the real engine: service began
**15 March 2021**, the account arrived owing **$267.30** in four age bands as of
**31 August 2026**, the window opens on **1 September 2026** — not one day earlier — and the
**$267.30** is stamped and PRINTED as `Previous balance`, footing
`267.30 − 0.00 + 247.87 = 515.17` (BR-BIL-035 / BR-BIL-160, ❄️ GT-16's own figures). The
printed half is asserted as well as the payload half for DEF-116's reason: a stamp the
renderer cannot read passes a payload assertion and still leaves the customer holding a
dash.

## 2026-09-21 · 🛠 BUILT: A NEW CONNECT BUILD CAN BE CREATED — THE PINCER IS OPEN ON BOTH SIDES

**Lane NC-8, against `CR-126-BRC07`.** The measured state on the morning of this
commit was *eight builds raised in a browser and eight refused at the final press*.
**Three builds now commit, in a browser, through the real wizard: `CON-26-0134` (one
dwelling and a common area), `CON-26-0135` (one dwelling and no common area) and a
single house.** `DEF-MET-6095` is closed on that evidence.

### WHAT WAS REFUSING, AND WHAT EACH FIX IS

**1 · `BR-MET-040` NO LONGER FIRES ON A COMMON AREA.** PO: *"common area dont need
rate plan as of now; make this optional"*. `create_master_account` creates the owner's
account ACTIVE and ran the plan check over every unit it covers, so a hallway with no
plan refused the WHOLE build. ⚠ **IT IS NARROWED, NOT DELETED, AND THE PO'S WORDS *"AS
OF NOW"* ARE WHY.** `customers/services.COMMON_AREA_REQUIRES_A_PLAN = False` is the
whole narrowing — one named constant, in one place; set it back to `True` and the
refusal returns. A DWELLING is refused exactly as before, on every path.

**2 · A BUILD WITH NO COMMON AREA COMMITS, AND THE OWNER STILL GETS A MASTER
ACCOUNT.** PO: *"common area is option"*. `metering.connections.create_owner_account`
raised `connection_no_common_area_for_master`; that refusal is deleted.

⚠ **WHERE THE ACCOUNT ANCHORS WAS THE BUILD QUESTION AND THE ANSWER IS *THE
PREMISES* — MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN.** Against anchoring on a dwelling:

* **The premises costs ZERO new lines in `customers`.** `BR-CUS-1010` moved the anchor
  to the address on 2026-09-01 (`accounts.unit_id` NULL, `premises_id` set),
  `_master_attachment_units` has answered `[]` for a premises with nothing shared since
  `CR-056` W1 task 9, the per-unit guard loop iterates nothing and
  `_open_master_service_agreements` writes nothing. **The whole change was deleting
  metering's refusal.** Read back on `CON-26-0135`: `AC-2026-00057`, `kind=master`,
  `unit_id=NULL`, `premises_id` set.
* **A dwelling would have needed three new decisions and carried a money risk:** WHICH
  dwelling; `BR-CUS-017` would then refuse the first resident's move-in, because the
  developer's account already occupies that unit; and `covered_unit_ids` would bill the
  developer for a DWELLING, which `BR-CUS-083` never said.

**The money is unmoved.** `1408 Elm` still bills `$41.20 + $28.40 = $69.60`; a build
with no shared space covers nothing and bills nothing — `CR-056` W4's *no lines, no
document*.

**3 · STEP 1 IS UNTOUCHED.** PO: *"Step 1 with no owner - this is correct"*. Recorded
because the other two rulings read like licence to relax it, and they are not.

### THE SAFETY THE RULINGS REST ON IS NOW HELD BY A TEST RATHER THAN BY A SENTENCE

An unplanned unit is only safe because it can never be billed:
`billing.gather.gather_account` raises `GATHER_NO_PLAN`, `runs.STAGE_BY_REASON` files
it on the `resolve-subscription` tab and `runs.NOT_RETRYABLE_HERE` marks it

was made to assign the common area a plan and that case went red; the constant was
flipped to `True` and the narrowing case went red. Four green, four red on demand.

⚠ **EACH CASE ALSO ASSERTS WHAT WOULD MAKE IT PASS WRONGLY** (law 7's second habit):
the unplanned case asserts the unit really is unplanned before gathering, and the
common-area case asserts the shared unit really exists before asking what plan it
