## 2026-09-21 · THE APPLICATION FEE BECOMES A CHARGE CODE — WHICH ANSWERS BOTH HALVES OF THE MISSING FEE SURFACE

**PO, verbatim:** *"we wil add charge code for it"*, said of the two open rows about the
application fee — `DEF-CUS-5904` (a clerk cannot raise one anywhere) and `DEF-CUS-6102`
(a utility that takes none still meets the fee surface, and cannot be configured as `$0`).

⚠ **THIS IS A DESIGN DIRECTION, NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, AND IT IS ELEGANT BECAUSE IT DELETES
TWO PROBLEMS RATHER THAN SOLVING THEM.** A charge code is already a **per-tenant row a
utility edits on Settings** — that is what `rating.selectors.charge_by_code` says in its
own words, *"the amount is a SEED the tenant edits, never a constant"*, and it is how the
`$75.00` reconnection fee and fire's six diameters already work.

**So both open rows dissolve into the path this product already has:**

* **`DEF-CUS-6102` — the `$0` utility.** A utility that charges no application fee simply
  **does not configure the code.** No new setting, no `is_fee_charged` flag, no second
  concept. The absence of a charge code is already how this product says *we do not charge
  for this*.
* **`DEF-CUS-5904` — no clerk can raise one.** Raising a fee stops being a bespoke door
  (`addServiceRequestFee`, exported and called by nothing) and becomes **the ordinary
  charge path**, which has screens, rules and a ledger behind it.

⚠ **AND IT FIXES THE THING NOBODY ASKED ABOUT: THESE FEES NEVER REACH THE LEDGER.** That
is why *"Record further payment in Payments"* was impossible advice — the figure lives on
`ServiceRequest.fee_collected` and only `collect_fee` writes it. **A charge code posts.**
So the money becomes visible to finance, reportable, and payable through the same door as
every other charge.

⛔ **WHAT A LANE MUST NOT ASSUME FROM SIX WORDS, AND MUST PUT BACK RATHER THAN DECIDE:**

1. **Whether the existing `ServiceRequest.fee_*` columns are migrated or left.** Fees have
   already been collected against them in the beta. **Hard rule 4 — corrections are new
   rows, never edits** — so a migration that rewrites collected money is not available.
2. **Whether the charge is raised at capture, at approval, or when a clerk asks.** The PO
   has ruled the fee no longer gates approval, so the timing is genuinely open.
3. **What the code is called and what it seeds at.** A figure nobody has ruled is an open
   question, not a lane's choice — the same rule that stopped fire's six diameters being
   invented.

**Measure first, then put those three back to the PO in plain English with a figure.** The
ruling is the direction; the shape is ours to propose and theirs to confirm.

## 2026-09-21 · ⛔ THE REASON GIVEN FOR REFUSING TO RAISE A BUILD FROM AN APPLICATION IS FALSE — MEASURED AGAINST THE SCHEMA

**PO, verbatim, challenging it:** *"why youa re saying request dont have owner - we take
details on customer when service request is created - that mean you ahve both customer
details and premises details ... i still notunderstand what is mandetory that is stopping
you"*.

**THEY WERE RIGHT.** The orchestrating session relayed a code comment to the PO as fact.
Checked against the live database rather than read, **both of its claims fail**.

**The comment** (`request_jobs.py::_raise_connection`): *"creating the premise here would
need the mandatory owner `BR-MET-1010` requires and the application does not carry."*

### WHAT IS ACTUALLY MANDATORY

| To raise a build you need | Mandatory? | Does the request carry it? |
|---|---|---|
| `connections.premises_id` | **YES — NOT NULL** | only if the address resolved — **the one real blocker** |
| …and to create that premises: `address_line` | **YES — the only NOT NULL business column** | **yes**, `address_as_given` |
| an owner on the premises | **NO — `premises.owner_id` is NULLABLE** | yes anyway: `applicant_*` + `matched_customer_id` |
| the owner's master account | **NO** | — |
| `premises_type_id` | **NO — nullable** | yes, `property_type` |
| `city`, `postal_code` | **NO — nullable** | yes, in the address |

**AND THE SECOND CLAIM IS REFUTED BY THE CODE IT CITES.** `metering/services.py:1748`
creates the owner's master account **LAST, in its own savepoint**, and its own comment
says: *"a refused account leaves the address standing"* and *"**SERVED EVEN WHEN IT IS
`None`, AND THAT IS THE POINT** — a key that appears only on success is a key a screen
cannot ask about."* **A premises is deliberately creatable with no owner account.**

⛔ **SO THE REFUSAL IS A CHOICE, NOT A DATA GAP.** Nothing is missing. One row must exist
first, and everything needed to create it is already on the request. **`DEF-CUS-6109` is
the build; `DEF-MET-6117` is the false comment, filed separately so that fixing the
behaviour does not leave a false reason standing under it.**

⚠ **AND THE SERVICE REQUEST CARRIES MORE THAN ANYONE CREDITED IT WITH** — the PO's point,
verified: `applicant_kind`, `applicant_name`, `applicant_email`, `applicant_phone`,
**`matched_customer_id`**, `address_as_given`, `address_unit_as_given`, `plot_or_parcel`,
`property_type`, `what_is_being_built`, `units_on_property`. **A draft build has every
fact it needs.**

### THE LESSON, AND IT IS HARD-WON LAW 1 CATCHING THE ORCHESTRATOR

*A comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee.* This one was **persuasive** — it
cited a rule id, named a mandatory field and gave a reason — and it was relayed to the PO
as a finding. ⚠ **A comment that supplies a REASON FOR A REFUSAL is the most dangerous
kind**, because a lane meeting it stops measuring: the explanation feels like the
investigation. **It took one query against `information_schema` to refute it, and the
person who asked for that query was the PO.**

## 2026-09-21 · A RULE REFUSAL REACHES THE CLERK ON THE STEP THEY CHOSE IT — APPROVED, WITH THE STEP NAMED

**PO, verbatim:** *"this fix is correct - you ahve to show the error at step you
mentioned"*.

**WHAT WAS PUT, AND WHAT IS APPROVED.** Two crashes found by the acceptance walk are one
fault: **a business rule reaching a clerk as a raw HTTP 500.**

* **`DEF-MET-6110`** — step 6, pick `TAP` **from the product's own picker**. Commit →
  *"Something went wrong on our side."* **Thirty-three presses gone.** The code is not a
  flat amount; pricing raises `BillingRuleError`; nothing catches it.
* **`DEF-MET-6111`** — pick an existing address that already holds units 1–3, add units
  labelled 1–3. Commit → the same raw 500 on `uq_units_tenant_premises_label`. **The
  database is right to refuse; nothing asked first.**

**THE APPROVED FIX IS TWO LAYERS, AND THE PO'S SENTENCE IS THE SECOND ONE:**

1. **Ask before the clerk works.** Step 6 offers only charge codes a build can actually
   price. Step 3 reads the picked premises' existing labels and says *"Unit 1 already
   exists here"* **before a word is typed.**
2. ⛔ **AND THE REFUSAL LANDS ON THE STEP THE CLERK CHOSE IT** — *"you ahve to show the
   error at step you mentioned"*. Not on the done panel, not as a 500, not on step 8. The
   charge refusal appears on **step 6**; the label refusal on **step 3**. **With the work
   intact**, so the clerk corrects one field rather than losing a build.

⚠ **THE SECOND LAYER IS NOT A NICETY AND IS WHY LAYER 1 ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH.** A charge
code priced today can stop being priceable tomorrow — a tenant edits it on Settings, which
`rating.selectors.charge_by_code` says is exactly what a charge code is for. A picker
filtered at step 6 cannot know that. **So the commit must still catch the rule error and
answer with words on the step that owns the field, rather than letting it leave as a 500.**

⚠ **AND THE SHAPE GENERALISES — SAY IT RATHER THAN FIX TWO CASES.** *A business rule that
reaches a clerk as a 500 tells them the product is broken when they have simply chosen
something the product refuses.* The clerk is told it is our fault, cannot act on it, and
the work is gone. **Any `RuleError` escaping the New Connect commit is this defect, not a
new one** — a lane fixing these two looks for the others rather than waiting for a walk to
find each in turn.

⚠ **ONE THING NOT TO CONFUSE IT WITH:** a refusal that is ALREADY named and lands on the
right step is correct behaviour and is not in scope. Step 2's *"Choose a plan for the
units."* and step 3's *"Add at least one unit."* are the shape being asked for, not
examples of the fault.

## 2026-09-21 · BUILT — THE REFUSAL NOW LANDS ON THE STEP, AND FOUR THINGS THE RULING DID NOT DECIDE

`DEF-MET-6110` and `DEF-MET-6111` are FIXED (lane NC-9, batch `2.322.0`). The ruling above
is the requirement; these are the judgments made where it ran out, written down because
the next lane reads the repo and not this session.

**BEFORE, in a browser, on an isolated clone of the demo tenant:**

* **`DEF-MET-6110`** — `x6110` of `10-scripts/cr126_s9_acceptance_walk.mjs`: a single house,
  `TAP` picked at step 6. `POST /connections/commit` → **HTTP 500
  `{"code":"SYS-INTERNAL", …}"`**, the screen read *"Failed. The connection was not
  created. Something went wrong on our side. Nothing was saved."*, the clerk was left on
  **step 8**, and **33 clerk acts** were gone. Server log:
  `apps.billing.exceptions.BillingRuleError: charge code 'TAP' is priced as 'flat', which
  needs a BASIS …`.
* **`DEF-MET-6111`** — `x6111`: `2200 Riverbend Ct`, which already holds `Apt 101–103`,
  with `Apt 101–103` typed at step 3. Same raw **HTTP 500**, same sentence, 25 acts gone.
  Server log: `django.db.utils.IntegrityError: duplicate key value violates unique
  constraint "uq_units_tenant_premises_label"`.

**AFTER, same walk, same clone:**

* the charge case answers **HTTP 422 `metering.connection_charge_refused`**, the clerk is
  left on **step 6**, the strip reads *"A charge here cannot be billed. Check the
  charges."*, the footer still carries **Back · Continue**, and `Payment terms` still
  holds `30`;
* the label case answers **HTTP 422 `metering.connection_unit_label_taken`**, the clerk is
  left on **step 3**, the strip reads *"A unit number here is taken. Change the unit
  numbers."*, the footer is intact, and `From 101 / To 103` are still in the boxes.
  Before the press, step 3 now says *"Apt 101 already exists here. Change the unit
  numbers."* and marks all three rows *"Already exists here."*

### FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULING DID NOT MAKE

**1 · THE REFUSAL CARRIES THE STEP'S ID, NEVER ITS NUMBER.** `params: {"step": "charges"}`,
and the browser resolves that against its own `NEW_CONNECT_STEPS`. A number would have
been the obvious choice and it rots silently: `owner` and `scope` merged into one screen on
2026-09-16 and every later step moved down one, so a refusal carrying `6` would have meant
*Charges* before that day and *Communication* after it, with nothing going red. A step id
is a stable code, which is what `BillingRuleError`'s own docstring permits in `params`
(*"figures and stable codes"*, never prose).

**2 · A ROUTED REFUSAL DOES NOT TAKE THE FOOTER.** `WizardFrame`'s `FailedWithRetry`
REPLACES the whole action row, which is right for a commit that failed on the review step
and wrong for a rule the clerk can fix four steps back — it leaves them on the owning step
with no `Continue` and no `Back`, so correcting one field costs a `Cancel` first. So
`WizardCommitOutcome` gained an OPTIONAL `refusedOnStep`, and the controller skips the
failure card when a consumer sets it. **Additive: no other wizard sets it and all 20+ are
behaviourally unchanged.** The shape it produces is the one the ruling pointed at — step
2's *"Choose a plan for the units."* and step 3's *"Add at least one unit."*

**3 · ONE UNIQUE CONSTRAINT ON THIS PATH IS A CLERK'S CHOICE, AND THE OTHER FOUR STAY
LOUD.** `uq_units_tenant_premises_label` is a value the clerk typed.
`uq_premises_tenant_premise_no`, `uq_units_tenant_unit_no`, `ux_accounts_no` and
`uq_assets_tenant_no` are numbers the SERVER allocates, so a collision on one is a
numbering defect. Translating those would tell a clerk to change something they never
typed and would bury the defect behind a polite sentence. **Only the named constraint is
recognised; every other integrity error is re-raised with its own traceback and still
answers `SYS-INTERNAL` with a trace id.** The same discipline covers the charge half: the
`except` names billing's OWN rule-error class, resolved through a seam, and anything else
leaves untouched.

**4 · NO LABEL TRAVELS IN THE SERVER'S REFUSAL.** The pre-check knows which label clashed
and the race cannot, so naming it would have needed two near-identical catalogue entries
for one rule. **Step 3 names every clashing label ON THE SCREEN instead**, beside the row
it belongs to, which is where a list is legible and a one-line strip is not. One sentence
for the rule; the table says which.

### WHAT WAS **NOT** TURNED INTO A POLITE MESSAGE, AND WHY

A census of the commit path's call graph — `commit_new_connect` resolved through each
module's own imports, **278 functions at `560c77f94`** — finds **120 raise sites of 11
non-catalogue exception classes** that can leave this door as an HTTP 500 today. (The
function count was 271 when this fix was written and 278 an hour later, which is the whole
reason the method is spelled out below rather than the figure being left to be quoted. The
raise-site count did not move. A name-based classifier also counts this fix's own three
`_refused_on_the_step_that_chose_it` calls among them; they raise `BizError` and are not
in the 120.) **83 of them are
`BillingRuleError` and its subclasses** (`BillingRuleError` 72 · `PostingRefused` 6 ·
`GatherProblem` 3 · `DuplicateRun` 2) and ALL 83 are now answered on **step 6**, because
step 6 is where the clerk chooses the charge code, the basis, the payer, the terms and the
posting date. The remaining **37 are left loud, deliberately**:

| class | sites | why it stays a 500 |
|---|---|---|
| `AuditWriteError` | 5 | hard rule 7 — the money action's audit row could not be written. Not a choice a clerk made, and not a thing they can fix. |
| `NumberingError` | 8 | a `CON-`/`U-`/`P-` series is exhausted or misconfigured (`BR-TEN-035`). A numbering fault told as *"check the charges"* would never be reported. |
| `StorageNotConfigured` · `DocumentStoreError` | 15 | the document store is not set up. `CR-049` says the product must REFUSE loudly rather than fall back to container disk. |
| `BillingConfigError` | 3 | a tenant registry/service map is missing — setup, not a build. |
| `IdempotencyKeyError` | 2 | a programming error in a key's shape. |
| `NotFrozen` | 1 | a frozen-document invariant. |
| `NotImplementedError` | 1 | `_check_mode`'s `OQ-249` stub — an open question, and the prime directive says a stub stays a stub. |
| `TypeError` · `ValueError` (`require_role`) | 2 | a caller passed the wrong shape. |

⚠ **THE COUNT IS A CENSUS AND NOT A GUARANTEE, AND THE METHOD IS WRITTEN OUT HERE SO IT
CAN BE REDONE RATHER THAN QUOTED.** It walks the AST from
`metering.connections.commit_new_connect`, resolving each call through the calling module's
OWN import table — `mod.func()` through the alias, bare `func()` within the file — so a
call lands on ONE definition or on none. **A first pass matched by bare NAME and reached
942 functions**, because every module in this repo has a `_tenant_id`; that number is
meaningless and is recorded here so nobody re-derives it and believes it.

It **UNDER-collects** where a door is resolved by STRING, which this path does six times,
so those six are seeded by hand: `rating.selectors.charge_by_code` (through
`billing.gather._resolve`) and `billing.fee_bill`'s `raise_and_issue_quote_bill`,
`price_quote_bill`, `charge_code_line`, `_unit_for_basis` and `_account_facts` (through
`metering.seams.quote_bill_door` / `quoted_charge_shape`). **Re-measure before quoting the
number again** — it moves whenever billing's quote path does.

### PROOF

* **RED FIRST, THROUGH THE HARNESS THAT RUNS IT** (hard-won law 7). With the two handlers
  and the pre-check removed, `tests/test_def_met_6110_6111_refusal_on_its_step.py` reports
  **5 failed / 4 passed** — the charge cases on `BillingRuleError` and the label cases on
  `UNIQUE constraint failed: units.tenant_id, units.premises_id, units.label`. Restored:
  **9 passed**. With the two front-end filters removed,
  `NewConnectStepRefusal.dom.test.tsx` reports **4 failed / 8 passed**; restored, **12
  passed**. The four that stay green either way are the cases asserting what must NOT
  change, which is why they are in the file.
* **IN A BROWSER** (law 6), `cr126_s9_acceptance_walk.mjs` variations `x6110`, `x6110b`
  and `x6111`. `x6110b` is the one that matters most: it puts a PRICEABLE code on the
  quote at step 6 and then **edits that code on Settings through
  `PATCH /charges/{id}` before the last press** — the case layer 1 structurally cannot
  cover, because *"the amount is a SEED the tenant edits, never a constant"*.

## 2026-09-21 · AN APPROVED APPLICATION BECOMES A DRAFT BUILD — BOTH SHAPES, WALKED IN A BROWSER

**`DEF-CUS-6109` built; `DEF-MET-6117` — the false reason under it — corrected in the same
commit.** This is the section above (*"THE REASON GIVEN FOR REFUSING TO RAISE A BUILD FROM
AN APPLICATION IS FALSE"*) executed, and nothing here re-argues it.

### WHAT A CLERK CAN DO NOW THAT THEY COULD NOT THIS MORNING

Walked in Chromium at `2.322.0` on a private clone, **twenty-two presses, both shapes**:

| The application | What approving did before | What it does now |
|---|---|---|
| `SR-26-0004` · 14 Willow Bend · **address matched nothing** | approved with outcome `new_connection` and **created no build**; `outcome_ref` empty | raises **`CON-26-0130`** as a DRAFT and opens its wizard; the clerk finishes it and the property `P-00080` is created **at the last button** |
| `SR-26-0008` · 88 Pine Vista · **address matched `P-00057`** | *"A new connection"* was **greyed** — *"A premise record already exists here."* | the option is **offered**; approving raises **`CON-26-0131`** against `P-00057`, and the wizard creates **no second property** |

Both requests now read `approved` and name their own build in `outcome_ref`; both builds
carry their application in `connections.request_id`; both opened the owner's master account
(`AC-2026-00052`, `AC-2026-00053`).

### THE ONE SCHEMA MOVE, AND WHY IT IS THE ONLY ONE

`connections.premises_id` was `NOT NULL`, so the only way to raise the draft on the
unresolved shape was to create the address first — **which is exactly what `BR-MET-112`
forbids**: a clerk who abandons the wizard would leave a brand-new property standing with
no units, no meters and no plan, and `commit_new_connect`'s own docstring says no screen in
this product can find that wreckage.

So `metering/0059` drops `NOT NULL` **and puts the guarantee back where it is actually
true**: `ck_connections_premises_once_submitted` — *a build that has been SUBMITTED has an
address*. ⚠ **Keyed on `submitted_at` and never on `state`**, because `state` is a cache
`refresh_connection_state()` rewrites and a cancel outranks, so a constraint on it could be
defeated by cancelling. Every existing row satisfies it; nothing is backfilled.

### THE DRAWING SETTLED THE INVERSION, AND IT TOOK ONE PAGE

**Accounts blueprint p089, read AS AN IMAGE at scale 2.4 (`B14` rule 42).** `SR-26-0001`'s
own detail on p088 reads `Matched premises · PR-0731 · exact` and `Matched unit · U-001884
· exact` — and the approve modal on p089 draws **`A new connection` selected and enabled**,
over a red callout that answers the whole question in one sentence:

> *"Nothing is preselected, deliberately. The resolver matched this address to PR-0731
> exactly, and that is EVIDENCE — not the decision."*

So `_verdict_for`'s `premise_exists → NOT_POSSIBLE` branch is **WITHDRAWN**. An existing
property with no service is an ordinary new connection; the wizard simply has no address to
create. The option is `POSSIBLE` and **not** `fits_the_evidence` — no screen draws that
badge for a matched address, and awarding one would be authoring the rule `OQ-356` exists
to ask for.

⚠ **AND THE SAME PAGE SAYS WHAT HAPPENS NEXT**, which is why approving now OPENS the
wizard rather than printing a note about it. p089's `WHAT APPROVING WILL DO` table, fourth
row: *"Next · The build's own wizard asks for units, services, plans and charges."*

### WHAT THE DRAFT WRITES, AND WHAT IT DEFERS

**At approval** — one `connections` row: the `CON-` number, `state=draft`,
`service_request_id`, `target_activation`, and `premises_id` **only where the application's
address already resolved to one**. One `connection.created` audit row. Nothing else.

**At the last button** — the premises (on the unresolved shape), the units, the meters, the
plans, the owner's account, the work orders and the charges, in ONE transaction, through
`commit_connection`, exactly as for a build raised directly. `BR-MET-112` is untouched.

⚠ **THE COMMIT FINISHES THE DRAFT; IT DOES NOT CREATE A SECOND BUILD BESIDE IT.**
`commit_new_connect` takes `connection_id`, attaches or creates the address on **that** row
and commits it. A commit that ignored the id would satisfy every other check — the address
would exist, the units would exist, the manifest would read `premises: 1` — and leave an
abandoned draft on the New connects tab for ever. That is the assertion the tests are built
around.

⛔ **`request_id` STAYS PROVENANCE** (`BR-MET-1178`). `/connections/new` with no `?build=`
reads nothing, sends `connection_id: null`, and behaves exactly as it always has.

### WHAT THE APPLICATION HANDS THE WIZARD, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

The PO's challenge was that the facts are already there — *"we take details on customer when
service request is created - that mean you ahve both customer details and premises
details"*. `GET /connections/{id}` now serves them as `prefill`, and step 1 opened on
**"Okonkwo, David"** and step 2 on **"14 Willow Bend, Springfield"** in the walk above.

⚠ **THEY ARE OFFERED, NEVER DECIDED WITH.** The owner is still REQUIRED at step 1 and
`ownerIdentityShortfall` still blocks it: an applicant is who ASKED and an owner is who the
property and the money belong to. ⚠ **AND THE UNIT PATTERN IS NOT PREFILLED** although the
request carries `units_on_property`. That number is a COUNT; a pattern is prefix, from and
to, and turning six into `1 … 6` would invent six LABELS nobody typed — labels that then
reach `uq_units_tenant_premises_label` and every bill after it.

### TWO THINGS THE WALK ITSELF GOT WRONG FIRST, RECORDED BECAUSE BOTH READ AS THE DEFECT

`cr126_s9_request_to_record_walk.mjs` was extended rather than replaced, and its first two
runs lied in the same shape the defect it was walking for has:

1. It filtered the two shapes off `resolution_kind` on the **list row**, which does not
   carry it — every row read `undefined`, both `find`s returned nothing, and the walk
   reported *"this seed offers none"* over a database holding both. The resolution is on
   the DETAIL.
2. It read `outcome_ref` off `header`, where it is not, and printed **`(none)`** over two
   requests that named their builds correctly.

Both are hard-won law 7's *looking at the wrong thing*, and both printed a sentence
indistinguishable from a real failure. The walk now asks the detail, and **compares**
`outcome_ref` with the build rather than merely printing it — a non-empty reference pointing
at the wrong build would pass a check that only asked whether it was set.

Nine builds raised in Chromium on an isolated clone at `v2.322.0`, **23–38 presses and

and the nine-noun part-3 readback are in `CR-126-BRC07` §9.2 rather than here, because that
is where §9.1 already put them and two homes for one table is two things to keep in step.

a clerk presses and the product discards. Ten rows were filed instead: `DEF-CUS-6122`,
`DEF-MET-6123`, `DEF-BIL-6124`, `DEF-MET-6125`, `DEF-MET-6126`, `DEF-CUS-6127`,
`DEF-CUS-6128`, `DEF-CUS-6129`, `DEF-CUS-6130`, `DEF-CUS-6131`.

unpriced."* **and the Continue button is not refused.** Five of the nine builds raised on

is the PO's; it is written into `DEF-CUS-6131`'s prevention rather than answered here, and
no lane may settle it by picking one. **What is ours, and is filed as the defect, is that

part 4, which WALK-B is walking at the same time. It was filed anyway and says so in its

word for it, while a finding held back for a sibling to maybe find is a finding nobody
counts. **It arrived with yesterday's fix for `DEF-CUS-6098`**, which correctly stopped the
panel printing a raw code and gave `in_progress_draft` the word `draft` already carried —
the completeness test that fix added passes, because nothing asked whether the map was

`cr126_s9_acceptance_walk.mjs` counted step 4's grid and pressed Continue, in every one of
its fourteen variations. So sixteen asset-type pickers and sixteen size pickers were walked

200. **A control a walk never presses is a control a walk cannot report on**, which is

Two other things it could not do and now can: `PART=record CONNO=<n>` runs parts 3 and 3b
against a NAMED build, so two lanes can walk §9 at once without one of them spending a

speak for — the premise register's Owner line, the asset register's status words, and the
bill behind `money.invoice_no`. Each of the three found a defect the build read is silent
about, `DEF-MET-6123` and `DEF-BIL-6124` among them.

### A FALSE ABSENCE THIS WALK REPORTED FIRST, KEPT BECAUSE IT READ EXACTLY LIKE THE DEFECT

The walk's money detector matches `$` followed by digits, and it reported **"the Build tab
shows 0 money figures"** over a tab showing `QUOTED 315.00` and `OUTSTANDING 315.00`. Both
are real and neither carries a currency mark: `BuildRecordTiles` prints the server's
`display` string and says in its own comment that passing the money variant *"would mean
INVENTING a currency on the client"*, because `BuildMoney` is `{stored, display}` and
carries no `CHAR(3)`. **The tiles are right and the detector was wrong**, and the line it
printed is indistinguishable from the tab having no money on it at all. It is not filed as
a defect — the choice is deliberate and documented — and it is recorded here because the
next lane reading that sentence in a walk log would file it.

  is now measured.
* **Finishing the resumed draft finishes THAT draft.** The build count did **not** move
  across the last press — **11 before, 11 after** — while premises went 79 → 80 and units
  131 → 132. `POST /connections/commit` answered `200` carrying **the same id it was given**,
  `CON-26-0130` went `draft → requested`, `P-00080` and its unit were created at the commit,
  and the owner's master account `AC-2026-00052` opened. Exactly **one** build names
  `SR-26-0004`. A second build beside the first would have shown as 12.
* **The request reads `approved` and names its own build.** Compared rather than checked for
  emptiness: `outcome_ref` = `CON-26-0130` on `SR-26-0004` and `CON-26-0131` on `SR-26-0008`.
* **A rule refusal on the RESUMED path reaches the clerk as words on the step they chose.**
  Two rules were broken on purpose, on the two shapes:
  * a **duplicate unit label** (`Unit 1`/`Unit 2` on a property that already has both) —
    `422 BIZ-COMPLETENESS metering.connection_unit_label_taken params.step=units`, the clerk
    **left on step 3** reading *"A unit number here is taken. Change the unit numbers."*;
  * an **uncountable charge** — `422 metering.connection_charge_refused`, the clerk **left on
    step 6** reading *"A charge here cannot be billed. Check the charges."*
  Both keep the footer (`Save & exit · Park · Back · Continue`), and both wrote **0 builds,
  0 properties, 0 units**. `DEF-MET-6110`/`6111` hold on a door nothing had ever driven.
* **The wizard opens prefilled.** Step 1 arrives with **7 of its 21 controls already
  answered** — the applicant's name, email and phone, the party kind, the scope and the
  mode — and step 2 on the address the applicant gave.

### WHAT DID NOT — AND IT IS THE THING A BUILD-AND-REPORT CYCLE CANNOT SEE

**`DEF-CUS-6132` — an abandoned draft cannot be resumed.** The row is on the New connects
tab, reading `Draft`, naming its request. Where the address had resolved, its number and its
eye both go to `/premises/<id>?tab=build`, where **`Edit details` is disabled reading *"No
edit path exists yet."*** Where the address had **not** resolved, the row carries **no link
at all** and the eye is disabled. The wizard is at `/connections/new?build=<id>` and
**nothing in the product points there**. The rest of this walk reached it by typing the
address, which is not a clerk's path and is said so out loud in the script.

**`DEF-CUS-6133` — the filter offers the word `Draft` twice.** Read off the rendered panel:
`Open · Partly activated · Activated · Draft · Requested · In progress · On hold · Cancelled
· Draft · Parked`. `DEF-CUS-6098` correctly stopped `in_progress_draft` and `parked` reaching
a clerk as codes, and gave `in_progress_draft` the word `Draft`, which `draft` already had.
The raw-code detector tests **case**, so two capitalised English words both pass it; no check
asks whether two options read the SAME.

### §9 PART 4 · `NFR-3` IS REAL ON THIS LIST, AND THIS IS THE FIRST TIME IT WAS PROVED

The sibling walk reported *"the list read slices in SQL … so `NFR-3`'s server pagination is
real on this list; with 11 rows on file a second page cannot be walked in a browser today"* —
true about the SOURCE, and an assertion about the product. It is now driven: **45 empty draft
builds were raised through the product's own `POST /connections`**, taking the list to **54**,
and then:

| what was asked | what came back |
|---|---|
| opening the tab | `?page=1&per=50&sort=created&dir=desc` · **50 rows**, first `CON-26-0174` |
| pressing `Next page` | `?page=2&per=50&sort=created&dir=desc` · **4 rows**, first `CON-26-0121` |

**No row appears on both pages**, so the server sliced and the browser did not.

⚠ **AND THE PROBE THAT NEARLY FILED A DEFECT AGAINST A CORRECT LIST IS THE PART WORTH
KEEPING.** `GET /connections?per=1` answers **nine rows** with `next: null`, and
`?per=2&page=2` answers the same nine with `previous: null`. Read alone that is an
unpaginated list and an `NFR-3` breach of the `DEF-PAY-4221` family. It is neither:
`core.pagination.clamp_page_size`'s vocabulary is **50/100/200/500/1000**, so **`per` clamps
UP**, one page of fifty holds all nine, and `_connections_envelope` correctly derives
`next` from `page < last`. **A check you cannot describe a false pass for is a check you do
not understand — and this one had a false FAIL in it.** The comment is now in the walk.

### THE FIVE SEARCHES §9 NAMES, TYPED INTO THE BOX

Every one reached the server as `?q=…` and returned the row it names: `CON-26-0129` → 1 row ·
`P-00059` → 2 rows · `500 Main St` → 2 rows · `Ridge Property LLC` → 1 row · `SR-26-0002` → 1
row. The filter narrowed 9 rows to 1, reached the address, and survived a reload. The column
selector took `Actions` out — 10 columns to 9 — and that choice survived a reload too.

**JUDGMENT, because the rules ran out here: two of the five searches return a row that does
not say why it matched, and that is REPORTED rather than filed.** `P-00059` and
`Ridge Property LLC` appear nowhere on screen: the PREMISE column draws the ADDRESS, and the
APPLICANT column is `defaultVisible: false`. `NewConnectsTab` states that trade-off in its
own words — *"drawing it by default would add a column the blueprint does not draw; dropping
it would leave a search leg whose results look arbitrary"* — and the column chooser is the
remedy it names. So it is a deliberate, reasoned absence with a way out, not a defect. **A
clerk meets it as: search an applicant, get one row, and nothing on it is the name you
typed.** There is no premise-number column at all, so for that leg the chooser is no remedy.

### B14, READ OFF THE RENDERED TABLE

Rule 31 holds — **no database id among the 450 cell values on screen**. Rule 33 holds on the
headers — 10 labels, the longest **2 words**. No cell value reads as a raw server code. The
one word that fails is the duplicated `Draft` above, which is `DEF-CUS-6133`.

### TWO NEAR MISSES IN THE WALK ITSELF, RECORDED BECAUSE BOTH READ AS THE DEFECT

1. **The first search assertions checked that the TERM appeared in the returned row**, and
   reported *"AND NOT THE ONE SEARCHED FOR"* on two correct searches — the same trap this
   file's own header already records one field over: reading a field off a list row that the
   list row does not carry. They assert the row's **connection number** now, and report the
   invisible match separately.
2. **The charge probe reported `POST /connections/commit` *(never called)*** on its first
   run, over a door it had not reached: the wizard refused to leave step 6 with *"Say when
   this charge is due."*, a client-side gate. A commit that was never called reads exactly
   like a commit that fell over silently.

### AND ONE THAT WAS CAUGHT AT PUSH TIME — `DEF-CUS-6122` WAS TAKEN TWICE

Both lanes walking §9 allocated **`DEF-CUS-6122`** within the same hour, and `6123` after it.
Every arithmetic was right; `file_defect.py` reads the working tree, `HEAD` and the pushed
remotes, and a sibling in its own worktree has its rows in none of them until it pushes —
`DEF-1787`'s shape exactly. It cost nothing because law 11's push-time re-derivation was run:
the register was restored to the tip's bytes, both rows re-filed as **`DEF-CUS-6132`** and
**`DEF-CUS-6133`**, the citations inside the two walk scripts renumbered with them, and the
register's first **7,275,017 bytes** proved byte-identical to the tip. **The unconditional
re-derivation is what caught it, not a conflict** — the register merged cleanly, as an
append-only file almost always does.

### WHAT A CLERK ACTUALLY SEES ON THE TILE `DEF-CUS-6121` ASKS ABOUT — READ, NOT RESOLVED

`DEF-CUS-6121` is open and unruled: the register's *"approved, not started"* tile counts
approved applications with **no build attached**, and approving now always attaches one. This
walk did not choose a value for it; it read the screen with the condition in front of it.

On `sbh_clone_walkb` after this walk, **three** approved applications each carry a DRAFT
build nobody has finished — `SR-26-0002 → CON-26-0129`, `SR-26-0004 → CON-26-0130`,
`SR-26-0008 → CON-26-0131`. The Requests tab's tile reads:

> **APPROVED, NOT STARTED** · **0** · *No job opened yet*

So the tile is one step worse than the question states. It does not only *stop counting new
connections*: it reads **0** over exactly the set a clerk would open that tile to find — work
that was approved and has not been done — and its supporting sentence, *"No job opened yet"*,
is now false of every row it is silent about. **A job HAS been opened; it has not been
finished.** Whether the tile should count unfinished builds, count nothing, or be replaced is
`DEF-CUS-6121`'s to settle and is not settled here.

### ⛔ THE SANCTIONED WAY OUT OF THE WIZARD MAKES A SECOND BUILD — `DEF-CUS-6135`

The finding above — *an abandoned draft has no door back* — sent this walk looking for the
door the product DOES intend, and the answer changes the shape of the whole thing. There are
three ways to leave the New Connect wizard and they behave differently:

* **Walking away** leaves the draft build on the list with no door (`DEF-CUS-6132`).
* **`Save & exit`** discards everything typed, silently — **and that is correct.** `B19 §12.2`
  is explicit: *"`Save & exit` leaves quietly and writes nothing of its own."* Measured:
  typed a marker into the owner name, pressed it, re-opened the wizard, and the field was
  back to the application's prefill. **Not a defect, and it is written down here because it
  looks exactly like one.**
* **`Park`** is the one that keeps the work, and its panel says so in its own words:
  *"Parked at step 1 of 8. Reopening this from your Waiting on list brings you back to this
  step with everything you have typed. Nothing is created or changed until you finish the
  wizard."*

**Every clause of that sentence is true of the TYPING and none of it is true of the BUILD.**
Walked end to end on `CON-26-0131`, raised by approving `SR-26-0008`:

| step | what happened |
|---|---|
| parked it at step 1 | a `wizard_parks` row with `flow=new_connect` and **`reference` EMPTY** — the move-in park beside it carries `MVI-26-0002` |
| looked at the list | a new row whose **CONNECTION cell is BLANK**, opening `/connections/new?parked=<park-id>` — **no `build=`** |
| reopened it | the marker came back; the address carried `?parked=…&step=1` and **no build at all** |
| pressed through to the commit | the commit answered `200` with **`CON-26-0132` and a NEW id**, on the same property `P-00057`, reading `from = —`; units went 131 → 132. **`CON-26-0131` is still `draft`, still naming `SR-26-0008`.** |

So one piece of work now has **three rows** on the New connects tab: the orphaned draft, the
parked row with no number, and the real build — and the real build has lost its application.

⚠ **THIS IS THE EXACT FAILURE THIS LOG ALREADY SAYS THE TESTS ARE BUILT AROUND**, one door
over: *"A commit that ignored the id would satisfy every other check — the address would
exist, the units would exist, the manifest would read `premises: 1` — and leave an abandoned
draft on the New connects tab for ever."* That assertion is TRUE of `?build=` and was never
asked of `?parked=`. The commit answers `200`, the manifest is right, the property and the
unit appear, `tsc` is clean, and the only symptom is a row nobody looks at.

**The cause is one line of history rather than a bug in either piece.** `BR-SHL-048(c)` —
*"a parked wizard holds nothing"* — was ruled when a New Connect wizard genuinely held
nothing until its last button. `DEF-CUS-6109` made a build exist BEFORE the wizard finishes,
and the park was never told. **A rule that was true of the world when it was written, and
stopped being true when something else changed** — which is the shape this repo keeps paying
for, and is why `PHASE=park` now drives it in `cr126_s9_request_to_record_walk.mjs`.

⚠ **AND THE PROBE THAT FOUND IT LOOKED FOR A `[role="dialog"]` FIRST AND REPORTED
*"(no dialog)"*** over a park panel that was on the screen. The panel is INLINE. That read as
a dead control and nearly became a wrong defect; it is law 7's *looking at the wrong thing*
for the third time in this walk, and each time the false sentence was indistinguishable from
a real failure.

⚠ **AND THE FOURTH TIME WAS IN THE CHECK WRITTEN TO CATCH THIS ONE, WHICH IS WHY THE VERDICT
IS NOW AN ID AND NOT A COUNT.** `PHASE=park`'s first version counted the envelope of
`GET /connections` — **and that is the LIST's count, which includes parked wizards as rows**,
because the tab draws them. So parking twice moved it by two and the walk announced *"a
SECOND build was created"* over a run in which **nothing committed at all**: a false sentence
in the exact shape of the defect it was written for. The verdict is now `commit.id` against
the draft's id, which needs no denominator — the same id means the draft was finished, a
different one means a second build is standing beside it — and the run says so out loud when
the commit was never called. **Any figure quoted from that endpoint is ROWS ON THE LIST, not
builds**, and this section's own first draft said *"builds 12 → 13"* when it meant rows.

## 2026-09-21 — ONE PIECE OF WORK IS ONE BUILD: A PARKED WIZARD FINISHES THE BUILD IT WAS WORKING ON

**PO ruling, verbatim, on being shown the park defect above:**

> *"this is big problem - we cannot create two build - you can update the existing build"*

**THE RULE: where a wizard is working on a build THAT ALREADY EXISTS, parking it and coming
back must finish THAT build. It may never create a second one beside it.**

### The worked case, which is the one that was walked

`SR-26-0008` is approved. That raises **`CON-26-0131`** as a draft against `P-00057` — the
application's life ends there (`BR-MET-1180`, ruled 2026-09-21) and the build is separate
work that prices itself. A clerk opens the build's wizard, types for ten minutes, and
**parks** it because they are waiting on something.

**What happens today:** the park stores `flow=new_connect` with its `reference` **EMPTY**,
the list draws a row whose connection cell is **BLANK**, reopening it carries `?parked=<id>`
and **no build at all**, and the last press answers `200` with **`CON-26-0132` — a new build,
on the same property, naming no application.** `CON-26-0131` is still sitting there as a
draft, still the one `SR-26-0008` points at. **One piece of work, three rows on the tab, and
the real build has lost its application.**

**What must happen:** the last press finishes **`CON-26-0131`**. The tab shows **one** row for
it. `SR-26-0008` still names it. No `CON-26-0132` is ever minted.

### WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE IN `BR-SHL-048`

⚠ **IT IS A NARROWING, NOT A REVERSAL, AND THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING** — a lane
reading this as "the park may now write things" would undo a signed ruling.

* **`BR-SHL-048`'s headline stands: a parked wizard still changes nothing until it is
  executed.** The build in the worked case was **not created by the park** — it was created
  at **approval**, by a different act, on a ruling of its own. The park's only fault is that
  it **forgot** it.
* **Clause (a) stands and is in fact the fix.** A parked draft carries no foreign key and
  stores ids as **COPIED VALUES** — and `wizard_parks` already has the field: the move-in
  park beside this one carries `MVI-26-0002` in `reference`, and the New Connect park leaves
  it blank. **The mechanism was already built and already correct; New Connect simply never
  filled it in.**
* **Clause (b) stands without qualification.** A resumed draft is **re-validated at
  execution, never trusted from the park.** Everything typed may have gone stale — the unit
  may be taken, the plan may have a new version, a charge code may have been retired. Resume
  restores the typing and re-runs every check before it commits. **Finishing the existing
  build is not the same as trusting what was parked.**
* **A New Connect started from SCRATCH and parked is untouched by this ruling.** No build
  exists in that case, the park holds nothing, and the last press creates exactly **one**
  build. `BR-MET-112` — nothing is written until the last button — is unchanged.

### WHY IT BROKE, AND IT IS THIS REPO'S OWN RECURRING SHAPE

`BR-SHL-048(c)` was ruled on **2026-08-26**, when a New Connect wizard genuinely held nothing
until its last button. **`DEF-CUS-6109` made a build exist BEFORE the wizard finishes — on
2026-09-20 — and the park was never told.** A rule that was true of the world when it was
written, and stopped being true when something else changed.

⚠ **EVERY CHECK PASSED OVER IT.** The commit answers `200`. The manifest is right. The
property and the unit appear. `tsc` is clean. The only symptom is a row nobody looks at. The
assertion that WOULD have caught it already exists for the other door — *"a commit that
ignored the id would leave an abandoned draft on the New connects tab for ever"* — and was
**never asked of `?parked=`**.

### THE SECOND HALF, WHICH THE RULING MAKES UNAVOIDABLE

*"You can update the existing build"* requires a clerk to be able to **reach** it.
`DEF-CUS-6132` says they cannot: an abandoned draft's row leads to the property page where
every action is greyed out, or — where the address matched nothing — **has no link at all.**
The lane that found it could only continue by typing the address in by hand.

**So the door and the park are one piece of work.** A ruling that says *update the existing
build* is not satisfied by code that updates it correctly down a path no clerk can walk.

**Filed:** `DEF-CUS-6135` (the second build) and `DEF-CUS-6132` (no way back in).

## 2026-09-22 — THE BASIS SERVICE LIST IS DERIVED, NEVER A HARD-CODED PAIR (`CR-127`, percent-of-another-service)

**PO ruling, verbatim**, answering the question *"do you want the charge basis available on every
service pair, or only where it makes sense?"*:

> *"youa re correct — however dont hard code anything - use logic to derive it so that it is
> flexible and handle any scenario. that the objective."*

**THE RULE: nothing in the percent-of-another-service structure may name a service.** Not `water`,
not `sewer`, not a pair, not a list of "sensible" combinations. What a schedule may take a
percentage of is **derived from what the tenant has switched on and from what the chosen basis can
actually supply**, and it is derived at read time so a utility that enables an eleventh service gets
it for nothing.

**The two derivations, stated so a later lane cannot "tidy" them into a table:**

| basis kind | what the logic requires of the basis service | why |
|---|---|---|
| **% of the usage** | the basis service is **enabled** on this tenant, is **not this service**, and **produces a metered quantity** | the derived figure is a QUANTITY in the basis service's own unit, so a service that meters nothing has no quantity to take a percentage of (hard rule 3 — the unit travels and is never assumed) |
| **% of the charge** | the basis service is **enabled** and is **not this service** | the derived figure is MONEY, and any service that can put a usage charge on the bill can supply it |

**So *"electric as a percentage of gas"* is not forbidden — it is simply never configured**, and the
product does not spend a line of code preventing a utility from doing something we have not thought
of. ⚠ **THE HARD-CODED VERSION IS THE ONE THAT BREAKS**, and this repo has the receipts: the front
end types the service list out by hand in two places, so an eleventh service *"does NOT appear on
screen on its own and it fails SILENTLY"* (hard-won law 2); and a build's only *Add service* control
was a literal `"water"` (`DEF-MET-6118`), correct for the demo tenant and structurally incapable of
being right for another.

### THE TAXABLE HALF — RAISED BY THE PO, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT IT ALREADY EXISTS ONE LEVEL UP

PO, same message: *"you may want to provide a check for tableble or non tablebale in this"* — i.e. a
taxable / non-taxable switch on this structure. **It is not being built on the rate schedule, for two
independent reasons, and either one alone would be enough.**

**(1) The product already has it, on the TAX.** `taxes.applies_to_services` is a per-tax list of the
services a tax reaches; `resolution.py` reads it and its own note says the field *"also NARROWS THE
BASE"*. A utility whose state does not tax sewer leaves sewer off that list, once, and every sewer
line on every schedule is untaxed. **A second switch on the rate schedule would be a second place
that can disagree with the first about one fact** — which is this repo's own `$12.00` failure, where
plan, schedule and charge code each held it and the bill charged `$24.00`, *"and no test catches it,
because both rows are individually correct."*

**(2) It would move signed money law, not add a field.** Every pricing plugin in the product emits
its usage line with `taxable=True`, each citing **B4.2**, which is ❄️ FROZEN and reads: *"tax base =
usage + base charge only (fees and late charges are NOT taxed)"*. Taxability is decided by what KIND
of line it is, deliberately. A per-schedule override makes it a property of the SCHEDULE instead, and
that is a re-sign under HUMAN-GUIDE §6 — never an inline edit.

**What is done instead, and it is one sentence of screen copy rather than a feature:** the
percent-of-another-service card says where taxability is decided, so a clerk looking for the switch
is sent to Settings rather than concluding there isn't one. ⚠ **If the PO wants taxability ON the
schedule after reading this, that is a legitimate ruling and it reopens B4.2 — put it to them with a
worked figure, never decide it here.**

## 2026-09-22 — A PREMISES NAMES ITS MASTER ACCOUNT DIRECTLY (`CR-130-BRC07` PART THREE, amended)

**PO ruling, verbatim**, on reading why all three owner screens find nothing:

> *"why you are point is at owner id - why not directly at master accoutn Id - it will solev the
> problem … master Account do not have any Owner ID - please confirm ; we are not using it - owner
> IDs are not required hence no screens or fucntionality for it"*

and, on the three consequences put back to them: *"yes - im okay with this"*.

**THE RULE: `premises` names its MASTER ACCOUNT. The owner record is not in the chain a screen
walks, and no screen creates, picks or searches one.**

### CONFIRMED, BECAUSE THEY ASKED US TO CONFIRM IT

Read off the models by two readers independently, rather than asserted:

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| does `customers.Account` carry an owner id? | **NO.** All 35 fields listed; nothing points back at `premises_owners` in any spelling |
| does an account already know its property? | **YES** — `accounts.premises_id`, `BR-CUS-1010`, plus `unit` as a real cross-module FK |
| what does `premises_owners` hold? | category · name · contact_name · email · phone · customer · source_owner_manager · master_account · active — **thirteen fields and NOT ONE IDENTITY FIELD** |
| where do the ids the Add Premises form collects belong? | **`customers.Customer`** — `kind`, `ssn_bidx`, `driving_licence_bidx`, `phone_bidx`, `tax_id_bidx`, with their blind indexes |

**So the owner record duplicates a party's name and phone, carries none of the identity being
collected, and stands between the property and the account for no benefit.**

### ⚠ THIS IS NOT A NEW RULING. IT IS `OQ-790`'s OWN RULING, FINALLY BUILT.

`OQ-790` has read **✅ CLOSED 2026-08-27 — option (c), MASTER IMMEDIATELY** for almost a month, and
the PO named the mechanism in that ruling, verbatim:

> *"you ahev to call master account creation logic by passing the details and generate account
> number using Setting -> numbering and use this number to write premsies"*

**That sentence is today's ruling, word for word, written twenty-six days earlier.** What stopped it
being built is the owner-record gate: `_ensure_owner_master_account` reads `row.owner_id` FIRST, and
when it is empty it appends `no_typed_owner` and **returns before it ever looks at the identity
payload** — so a clerk types a name, a kind and a tax id and the code discards all three because
they did not also pick a row from a table nothing fills.

⚠ **AND `OQ-790`'s BODY STILL DESCRIBES THE OPEN WORLD, WHICH IS `DEF-WRK-4030` EXACTLY.** Its
status column says CLOSED; its body still says *"`ensure_owner_master_account` raises
`NotImplementedError("OQ-790")`"* and that master-ness is *"derived from whether anyone else
occupies the premises, not chosen at creation"*. **Both are false and the second is the reading the
PO REVERSED.** The body is what a lane reads, and this one misled the brief written from it: an
instruction to have the screen ASK whether the account is master or regular went out, which would
have resolved a closed question against the PO's own answer. **The body is corrected in this
commit.**

Two rules settle it and they agree: `OQ-790` option (c) — MASTER IMMEDIATELY — and `CR-056`
(PO 2026-08-31) — *every address gets its owner a Master Account, whether or not anything is shared
and whether or not the owner lives there*. And a screen could not ask it anyway: `kind` is a
**refused input** on every account door except `POST /accounts/master` (`BR-CUS-068`).

**What the screen genuinely asks is a different question and is already built:** `OQ-MET-12472`,
closed 2026-09-19 (`BR-MET-1176`, shipped `2.310.4`) — the form asks the owner's **kind, person or
company, and one identifier**, and no account exists until they are supplied.

### ⚠ THREE COLUMNS WOULD BE ABLE TO ANSWER ONE QUESTION, SO THE ORDER IS RULED HERE

`premises.master_account_id` (new) · `premises_owners.master_account_id` (existing) ·
`accounts.premises_id` (existing, `BR-CUS-1010`, already read by `sub_accounts_for_master` where
nothing declares an account as an owner).

**Three answers that can disagree about who gets billed is the hazard `BR-MET-400` retired the
hallway inference for**, and it must not come back by the side door. **The precedence is DECLARED
here rather than left to the reading order of a function:**

1. **`premises.master_account_id`** — the declaration. It wins whenever it is set.
2. **`premises_owners.master_account_id`** — the pre-ruling declaration, for rows that predate this.
3. **`accounts.premises_id`** — *which premises this account covers*, never *who owns this
   premises*. It answers a different question and is never promoted to answer this one.

⚠ **AND IT IS CHEAP, WHICH IS WHY IT IS SAFE.** The whole money path joins through **two seam
functions** — `owner_master_account_for_premises` and `premises_ids_owned_by_account`, both in
`apps/metering/premises_owners.py` — with **four call sites in the entire backend**:
`customers/selectors.py:884`, `:917`, `:1056`, and `customers/move_out_settlement.py:1470`. Change
what those two read and the empty-unit base charge, the move-out shortfall, the sub-account list and
the account header all follow, with no consumer touched. **`BR-MET-400`'s *declared, never inferred*
survives intact**, because both functions stay reads of a declared column — a shorter chain, not a
guess.

### WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, AND THE PO AGREED TO EACH

* **No owner-record screens are built.** `createPremisesOwner` is defined in `endpoints.ts:6799` and
  `metering/api.py:478` and called by nothing. ⚠ **That stops being hard-won law 2's dead door and
  becomes a DELIBERATE ABSENCE**, recorded here so the next lane does not "fix" it by wiring a
  screen the PO has said they do not want.
* **`premises_owners` is NOT deleted.** 19 backend files read it, and two do real work: `BR-MET-151`
  matches the import's free text against it, and the move-out shortfall stands on it. Retiring it is
  separate work and is nobody's job today.
* **`BR-MET-112` is not weakened.** Nothing is written until the last button; what changes is what
  that one press writes.

### THE FIVE WORDS, COUNTED

*Owner* · *Owner (record)* · *Owner / manager* · *master account {{n}}* · *Needs an owner*, live on
screen today across `metering.premises.field.ownerRecord`, `field.owner`, `col.owner`,
`owner.masterAccountPrefix` and `owner.needs_owner`. The PO's *"we ahve to use one volcabory"* is a
**measurement, not an impression**. One word reaches a clerk — **Owner** — with the account number
beside it; *owner record* and *master account* become internal words nobody reads.

⚠ **GREP FOR A RETIRED WORDING'S CONSUMERS BEFORE RETIRING IT.** Closing one such door cost a live
account-header line that would have returned null for ever with `tsc` and every test green
(`DEF-CUS-3653`). An absence is invisible to every check this repo has.

### ONE CORRECTION TO THE RECORD

The diagnosis put to the PO called Edit premise's owner control *a plain dropdown*. **It is a
`SearchSelectField` and has been since `CR-089` wave B**, and it is the **same component**
(`OwnerField.tsx`) the Add wizard renders — one file, two screens. The substance held (it lists
owner records, and there are none) but the shape did not, and whatever replaces it replaces both at
once. Recorded because a wrong detail in a diagnosis the PO has read is a wrong detail the next lane
inherits.

## 2026-09-22 — A ROUTE IS NOT A SNAPSHOT. IT NAMES PREMISES AND DERIVES EVERYTHING INSIDE THEM (`CR-131-BRC07`)

**PO ruling, verbatim:**

> *"thi sis correct - The routes design — storing 726 unit rows instead of 6 premises, and the
> route going stale the moment anything changes. and route should not be status - it is
> dynamicallyderive the details of units, assets meter acocount swithin it"*

⚠ **THE READING CHOSEN FOR `"should not be status"` IS *SHOULD NOT BE **STATIC***, and it is
recorded rather than assumed** (the same discipline the log applied to *"register max"* on
2026-09-03). The rest of the sentence settles it — *"it is dynamically derive the details of units,
assets meter acocount swithin it"* — and the PO had argued the point in full the message before:
*"deriving the units, assets and accounts is a danalmic process - it is not status - user wil keep
upaiting units, its status, add, remove assets, changes status of assets, move in move out
accounts - in such cases when we need details of route or cycle - it should be deived at that
time"*. **It is NOT about `routes.status` (draft | active), which is untouched.**

**THE RULE: a route stores WHICH PREMISES ARE ON IT. Its units, its meters and its accounts are
DERIVED every time they are asked for, and are never stored.**

### WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND WHY THE PO FOUND IT BEFORE WE DID

A clerk editing `RT-006` at **Ottumwa Water Works** picked **6 premises** carrying **726 units**.
Step 3 drew *"No meters yet"*; step 4 sat on *"Working…"* for ever with no error.

**Five symptoms, ONE cause — the route materialises what it could ask for:**

| symptom | cause |
|---|---|
| step 3 shows no meters | `getRouteMeterPicker` sends **one `unit_id` query parameter per unit** — 726 × ~45 chars ≈ a **33,000-character URL** against a 4–8 KB server limit. The request never arrives |
| step 3 would crawl anyway | `selectors.route_meter_picker` loops **one unit at a time**: a `Unit…first()` then `assets_on_unit()` — **~1,450 sequential round trips** |
| step 4 hangs, silently | `_set_route_members` loops `RouteMembership.objects.update_or_create` per unit — **~1,450 statements in one transaction** holding the route row locked. The front end DOES catch errors; *"Working…"* for ever means the request never returned at all |
| the clerk is told nothing | a FAILED meter fetch renders the **empty state** — *"No meters yet… Or none have meters fitted"*. **A rejected request and a meterless route look identical** (hard-won law 7's false absence) |
| the route goes stale | **and this is the one that matters.** The membership is a photograph. Add a unit, fit a meter, move a tenant in — none of it reaches the route until somebody re-opens the wizard and saves. Nobody will |

⚠ **THE STALENESS IS A CORRECTNESS BUG AND THE REST IS ITS SHADOW.** Patching the URL to a `POST`
would have made step 3 load and left a route that is wrong a week later — which is why the PO's
question (*"why at this stage youa re saving or dealing with so many units"*) is worth more than the
five fixes it replaces.

### WHAT MAY BE STORED, AND IT IS A SHORT LIST

| fact | stored? | why |
|---|---|---|
| **which premises the clerk ticked** | **YES — 6 rows** | an arbitrary SET, not a rule. `routes.area` cannot express *these 6 of the area's 40* |
| **excluded meters, with the reason** | **YES, unchanged** | `BR-MET-075` — *"read elsewhere"* is a human judgment and is not derivable |
| units · meters · accounts | **NO** | every one is a query from the premises |
| **walk order** | **YES — but on the UNIT** | see below |

### WALK ORDER MOVES TO THE UNIT — PO ruling, same exchange

> *"i will update the walk order on units directly or asset - one of these palces - not keep them
> in routes - becuase keeping the walk order in route is wrong since derive the units is dynamic"*

**Of the two places the PO offered, it is the UNIT, and the reason is the ruling's own logic one
level down:** a meter is **equipment that gets replaced**, so an order stored on it is lost at every
swap — the same staleness, one layer lower. **A unit is a PLACE**; the doorway does not change when
the meter inside it does. Neither model carries a position today, so it is a new column either way
and the right place wins.

**And the split is already half-built:** `assets.location_note` (≤280 chars — *"basement, rear"*)
holds **where in the stop**, which genuinely belongs to the meter. The unit holds **the order of the
stops**.

⚠ **ONE ORDER PER UNIT, NOT ONE PER ROUTE, AND THE TRADE-OFF IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.** A
physical position is stored once — which is this ruling's own principle — so a drive-by route and a
walking route covering one street share the sequence. That is accepted. **If a utility ever
genuinely needs two, a per-route override is added THEN, for the routes that use it**, rather than
paying for it everywhere now. `uq_route_memberships_walk_order` goes with the column.

### ⚠ THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE PROVED FIRST, BEFORE ANY OF IT IS BUILT

**`BR-MET-081` — *"Changes take effect next read window. Collected reads keep their route."*** The
wizard says it on screen and `update_route`'s docstring says *"touches no `meter_reads` row at
all"*.

**Derivation is the one change that could quietly rewrite that.** A read taken in September must
still report against September's route, and last month's reader sheet must reproduce **as issued**,
not as the world is today. **This is a money-adjacent record and it is step 1, not step 6** — if it
cannot be proved, the ruling needs re-opening with that fact in front of the PO, not working around.

### BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED

**Five backend files** touch `RouteMembership`, all inside metering: `walk_order.py`,
`services.py`, `selectors.py`, `derivation.py`, `models.py`. **This is contained** — unusual for
something this structural, and worth saying, because it means the design can be fixed rather than
the symptoms patched.

### AND IT IS A SCALE DEFECT, NOT A ROUTE DEFECT

726 units is **T7/T6** scale. `NFR-3` (universal server pagination), `NFR-5` (no hard caps) and B6's
*"no table, index, or code path may enforce a maximum account count per tenant"* are the flexibility
the PO ruled load-bearing for T4/T3. **A per-row loop that dies at 726 dies sooner at 40,000**, and
the meter list must be paginated whatever else changes.

## 2026-09-22 — NEW WORLD / LOGOS: A SEPARATE ENDPOINT FOR THE RECEIPT, THE LEDGER REUSED UNCHANGED (`CR-132-BRC07`)

**PO ruling, verbatim**, after the spec was read and the options put:

> *"i think we shoudl create seperate enpoint - you can se the same components that you use , dont
> write completely new code - what way we can keep it sepearet"*

and, settling which of the two:

> *"we need seperate endpoint if we deicde only for payemnt and not for ledge"*

**THE RULE: the PAYMENT side gets its own partner endpoint. The LEDGER side is
`GET /api/partner/v1/ledger`, reused unchanged. Everything beneath both is shared code.**

### WHY A SEPARATE ENDPOINT IS RIGHT, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT FORMAT

**The first answer offered was *parameterise it* and that was wrong** — the reasoning was that XML is
already a supported codec (`json · xml · csv · mime`, each fixture-backed) and `codecs.py`'s own
docstring names this exact case: *"a payment as JSON to one finance system and as XML to another"*.
**Reading the specification changed the answer**, and the distinction is worth keeping:

| our Payment | New World's Receipt |
|---|---|
| one row, one tender | a **header** · one or more **transactions** · one or more **GL distributions** per transaction · up to **four payment nodes** |
| flat | four levels |
| a record | an **aggregation with a balancing rule** — distributions must sum EXACTLY to the transaction amount |

**So this is not the same resource in another format. It is a different projection of the same
facts**, and bending `/api/partner/v1/payments` into it would change a contract other partners
already consume. **XML being available is what made *parameterise* look sufficient; the four-level
hierarchy is what makes it insufficient.**

### WHAT IS NEW AND WHAT IS REUSED — the PO's *"dont write completely new code"*

| layer | new? |
|---|---|
| the receipt endpoint | **NEW — one view** |
| the connector manifest `erp_newworld`, beside `erp_aclarian` | **NEW — one file** |
| tender → their five payment types · our bill type → their bill type | **NEW CONFIG, not new code** — `mappings.py` |
| the GL mapping tables | **REUSED** — the same ones Aclarian resolves against |
| the XML codec | **REUSED** — already supported, already fixture-tested |
| key auth · tenant-from-key · access log · rate limits | **REUSED — nothing written** |
| `GET /api/partner/v1/ledger` | **REUSED UNCHANGED** |

**The separation is the PROJECTION, not a second stack.** A GL rule changes in one place.

### THE ORIGIN COLUMN — ruled in the same exchange

PO: *"we need to filter it based on origin - webhooks only … or we might have to save the source
seprately - and make it available to import and entry also - what do you think"*, and the answer put
back — **store it properly, for all three** — was accepted.

**Today a payment's origin lives ONLY as a prefix inside the idempotency key string**
(`entry` · `webhook` · `import`, from `apps/payments/idempotency.py`). It is not a column, not
indexed, and not queryable. **Three reasons it becomes one:**

1. **The key's job is preventing duplicates, not reporting.** Reading it as an origin gives one
   field two meanings, and the next person to change the key shape breaks a report nobody connected
   to it.
2. **There are already TWO half-answers** — the key prefix and `payment_import_batches.source_kind`
   — which is the *two places that can disagree* shape this log has recorded twice today already.
3. **Counter and lockbox need it as much as online does.** Every reconciliation question starts
   with *where did this money come from*.

⚠ **THE BACKFILL IS A DERIVATION AND MUST BE MARKED AS ONE.** Existing rows take their value from
the key prefix where one exists and `entry` otherwise — and a derived value is not an observed fact.
Hard rule 4 makes this write-once at creation; nothing updates it afterwards.

### TWO THINGS PUT BACK TO NEW WORLD, AND THE SAFE DEFAULT IS BUILT MEANWHILE

**1 · WE DO NOT SEND CARD NUMBERS, AND THE CAPABILITY IS NOT BUILT.** Their spec carries
`ReceiptPaymentCreditCardNumber`, `…Type`, `…ExpirationDate` and `…ValidationNumber`. Populating
them pulls cardholder data into a file and **destroys the PCI scoping that keeps card data out of
this product entirely**. `ReceiptPaymentType = Charge` with no card number. ⚠ **Not built and then
left switched off — NOT BUILT**, so there is no switch for a later lane to turn on.

**2 · ONLINE-ONLY IS A RISK TO THE CITY'S BOOKS AND IS FLAGGED ONCE, NOT ASSUMED AWAY.** New World
is the official record for **all** municipal revenue. If SmartBillHub sends only the online
receipts, counter and lockbox money must reach it another way or the GL is short. That is probably
already true — a cashier system and a bank lockbox usually post directly — **but being wrong means
the City's books do not balance and we are the obvious suspect.** One question, not an assumption.

**Neither blocks the build:** the card fields are simply absent, and online-only is what was asked.

### STILL WITH NEW WORLD, NOT WITH US

Whether they call these APIs on their own schedule or we generate a file and deliver it another way
— and at what frequency — is a strategy decision with their team. **The APIs are built so that
either works**, which is the whole point of the approach and is why no schedule is being chosen
here.

## 2026-09-22 — STEP 1 OF `CR-131-BRC07` IS A GATE, AND IT DID NOT PASS: THE READ HISTORY IS SAFE, THE SCREENS THAT REPORT IT ARE NOT

**Lane R, `CR-131-BRC07` step 1.** The CR's own §4 makes this the one thing proved before
anything is built: *"Prove a collected read keeps its route under derivation … If it cannot be
proved, STOP and re-open the ruling with that fact — never work around it."* **It could not be
proved. This row is that fact, with its measurement, and NOTHING WAS BUILT.**

### WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND HOW

A seeded PostgreSQL clone (`sbh_clone_laner`) of the pinned tip `cb2757596`: 79 premises, 131
units, 11 routes, **516 collected reads, every one of them carrying a route stamp**. RT-009
*"Cedar Ridge — monthly walk"* holds 8 premises, 9 member units and 100 stamped reads.

Its 8 premises were moved onto RT-001 **through the product's own `services.update_route`** — not
by touching a table — and every surface that answers *"which reads belong to this route"* was
asked before and after. The transaction was rolled back, so the fixture did not move.

| what was asked | before | after the move | reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meter_reads.route_id` — the BR-MET-079 stamp | 100 | **100** | **the stamp** |
| the delete guard (`route_read_history_count`) | 100 | **100** | the stamp |
| S25's reads list, filtered by route | 100 | **0** | the live join |
| read progress (`BR-MET-011`) | 100 | **0** | the live join |
| the printed route sheet | 18 meters | **0** | the live join |
| last read completion | 2026-08-12 | **None** | the live join |
| RT-001's delete guard | 8 | **108** | it inherited RT-009's history |

### THE THREE FINDINGS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT STOPS THE LANE

**1 · THE STAMP IS SAFE, AND DERIVATION CANNOT REACH IT.** `meter_reads.route_id` is written once
by `collection_route_id` at the moment of collection and **nothing in the codebase updates it** —
grepped in both directions, and proved by the move above leaving all 100 in place. Hard rule 4
holds here without help.

⚠ **BUT IT HOLDS BY CODE AND NOT BY THE DATABASE, WHICH THE NEXT LANE MUST KNOW.** The
`meter_reads_value_immutable` trigger (`metering/0007`) refuses an UPDATE that moves `asset_id`,
`read_at`, `channel`, `prior_value`, `current_value`, `multiplier`, `consumption` or `unit` —
**`route_id` is not in that list.** So nothing in PostgreSQL would stop a future "refresh the
stamp from the current membership" statement; the only thing protecting it is that no such
statement exists. `metering/0012` itself ran three `UPDATE meter_reads` backfills when the column
landed, so the path is demonstrably open. **A guarantee that rests on nobody having written the
code yet is hard-won law 1's shape**, and if derivation is built, the cheapest hardening is to add
`route_id` to that trigger in the same commit.

**2 · BUT `BR-MET-081` IS ALREADY BROKEN ON EVERY SCREEN A CLERK READS, AT THE PINNED TIP, BEFORE
ANY OF THIS CR'S WORK (`DEF-MET-6143`).** *"Collected reads keep their route"* is printed in the
wizard and asserted in `update_route`'s docstring — *"touches no `meter_reads` row at all"* —
which is **TRUE and answers a different question than the one it is read as answering.** Four of
the five surfaces resolve the route through `asset__service_point__route_id`, the LIVE membership
projection. A hundred reads collected on RT-009 left its reads list, its progress count, its route
sheet and its last-read date the instant its premises moved, and RT-001 acquired them. **The
history did not move; everything that reports it did.** This is hard-won law 1 in its purest
form, and it is a pre-existing defect rather than anything derivation introduces.

**3 · "LAST MONTH'S SHEET REPRODUCES AS ISSUED" IS NOT SOMETHING THE PRODUCT CAN DO AT ALL
(`DEF-MET-6144`).** The route sheet is print-ready HTML rendered on demand from CURRENT membership;
`api.route_sheet_view` carries the comment *"a clerk PRINTS the sheet; nothing writes"*. **There is
no issued artifact to reproduce** — not a wrong one, none. The same move took RT-009's sheet from
18 meters to 0. This is an ABSENCE, and CR-131's own ruling forbids inventing a snapshot table to
make the promise true, so it is the PO's to rule on.

### AND THE FORWARD HAZARD, WHICH IS THE ONE THE GATE WAS ACTUALLY WRITTEN TO CATCH

**The stamp's ONLY source is `service_points.route_id`.** A derivation design that stops
maintaining that stored projection stops stamping new reads — proved by emptying the column and
calling the real function:

```
collection_route_id WITH the point stamped    : …8913  (RT-009)
collection_route_id WITHOUT any point stamp   : None
-> a read collected now would be stamped route_id=None
```

**Nothing would go red.** `meter_reads.route_id` is nullable and its own docstring calls NULL
*"honest"*, so the read history would simply stop being recorded, silently, from the day
derivation shipped. **Any design that lands must keep a route resolvable at collection time** —
through derivation itself rather than through a stored projection — and that requirement is now
written down rather than left to be rediscovered.

### WHAT THIS LANE IS ASKING FOR, IN PLAIN ENGLISH

Two questions, and the first is the one that decides whether the rest of `CR-131` is safe:

**(a) When a clerk opens a route and asks what was read on it, should the answer be the reads
COLLECTED on that route, or the reads on the meters that are on it TODAY?** Today it is the
second, and the product promises the first. Making it the first is four query changes and it makes
a signed rule true; but it CHANGES WHAT FOUR LIVE SCREENS SHOW, which is why it is not ours to
choose. ⚠ **It also has a cost that must be stated: on a database where older reads carry no
stamp, switching to the stamp makes them vanish from the route filter.** On this fixture that cost
is **zero — all 516 reads are stamped** — but it is not zero on a tenant that predates
`metering/0012`.

**(b) Must a reader's sheet be reproducible as issued?** If yes, that is a stored record and a
story of its own, and it should be ruled BEFORE `CR-131` builds anything, because the CR's own
ruling says a route stores almost nothing.

⚠ **AND A THIRD, WHICH IS A COLLISION RATHER THAN A CHOICE — `OQ-MET-12572`.** The walk order the
2026-09-22 ruling moves to `units` was ruled ***"Per premises"*** by the same PO on 2026-08-23, and
that ruling is the one that is BUILT: `route_premises_orders`, two constraints, an audited writer,
and the printed sheet's stops come from it. The column the September ruling was reasoning
about — `route_memberships.walk_order` — is superseded, has no writer and holds 0 rows. Steps 2
and 8 of the CR cannot start until the grain is settled.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY

**No code was changed.** Not the four surfaces, not the picker, not the save path, not the walk
order. The CR makes step 1 a gate and names *"this cannot be done safely"* as a complete outcome;
designing around a failed gate is the one thing it forbids. The N+1 picker, the 33 KB URL and the
~1,450-statement save are all confirmed by reading and are untouched — they are real, they are
`DEF-PAY-4221`'s shape, and they are not worth fixing underneath a membership model the PO may
restate once these three answers are in front of them.

## 2026-09-22 — AN UNBALANCED RECEIPT IS SENT, FLAGGED AND NEVER PLUGGED (`CR-132-BRC07`, amending the same day)

**PO ruling, verbatim:**

> *"please send receipt even if it is not balance"*

**This REVERSES a design decision made by the orchestrating session hours earlier** and written into
the lane brief as: *"Refuse to emit a receipt that does not balance — never emit one that is short
and never round to make it fit."* **The PO's call stands and mine was wrong.**

⚠ **THE REASONING IS WORTH MORE THAN THE RULING, BECAUSE IT IS A PRINCIPLE THIS REPO ALREADY HOLDS
AND I APPLIED BACKWARDS.** A refused receipt is money that **silently never reaches the City's
books** — invisible on both sides, discovered when someone reconciles a quarter later. An unbalanced
receipt is money that **arrives wrong and can be found.** That is exactly `BR-BIL-015`'s shape (a
refused line goes to the exception list rather than being silently forgiven) and exactly the seam
rule's (*"an unwired seam REPORTS that it cannot answer, never answers 0"* — and *"90% of an
unavailable number is not $0.00"*). **I reached for a refusal because their spec states a rule, and
enforcing someone else's control on our side turns their rejection into our silence.**

### WHAT *SEND IT* MEANS, IN FOUR CLAUSES

| clause | |
|---|---|
| **SEND IT** | no refusal, no exception that blocks emission, no holding it back |
| **NEVER SILENTLY** | the receipt is FLAGGED, the difference is stated **as a figure**, and the run reports how many were short and by how much. **A wrong receipt nobody knows about is worse than a refused one** |
| **NEVER PLUG IT** | no balancing line, no invented distribution, no adjusting a real one to make the arithmetic work. **Send what is true** |
| **LET THEM REJECT IT** | their importer enforces their rule. A rejection we can see beats a receipt we never sent. **Do not pre-empt their control with ours** |

### ⚠ WHAT IS BEING MEASURED RATHER THAN DECIDED

**Almost every imbalance is expected to be a ROUNDING RESIDUE OF ONE CENT, not a mis-mapping.**
Money is stored to 4 decimals (hard rule 2) and `DistributionAmount` is `9,2`, so a transaction of
`100.0000` split three ways emits `33.33 × 3 = 99.99`.

**That difference matters because the two have different answers.** A systematic one-cent residue
has a standard one — **assign the remainder to the largest distribution, which PLACES A REAL CENT
rather than inventing one** — and a genuine mis-mapping does not; plugging that would hide a broken
GL mapping behind correct-looking arithmetic.

**The lane is measuring how often each occurs on real data and reporting a figure. It is NOT
implementing the residue assignment.** Today's ruling is *send it*; the residue question goes back
to the PO **with the number attached**, which is what `CLAUDE.md`'s standing instruction means by
putting a rule to them in plain English with a concrete figure.

⚠ **AND THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN THE TWO IS EXACTLY THE ONE A LATER LANE WILL BLUR.** Assigning a
residue is placing money that exists. A plug line is inventing money that does not. **They look
identical in a diff and they are opposite acts** — which is why this section exists rather than a
line in a docstring.

## 2026-09-22 — ONLINE-ONLY IS NEW WORLD'S OWN REQUIREMENT, NOT OUR ASSUMPTION (`CR-132-BRC07`)

**PO ruling, verbatim**, answering the one question this integration was carrying:

> *"this requirement came from them - so build it this way"*

**THE QUESTION IS CLOSED. The New World payment feed carries `webhook`-origin payments ONLY, and
that is the CUSTOMER'S SPECIFICATION rather than a choice we made.**

The concern put to them, in full: *New World is the City's official record for all municipal
revenue. If SmartBillHub sends only the online receipts, the counter and lockbox money must reach it
another way or the City's ledger is short, and we are the obvious suspect.* **It was raised as ONE
QUESTION and not as an assumption in either direction**, because both readings were plausible — a
cashier system and a bank lockbox usually post to the ERP directly, which would make online-only
exactly right, and if they do not, a silent gap in the City's books is the worst failure this
integration could have. **New World asked for it**, so the other channels reach their books by
arrangements that are theirs to run and not ours to model.

⚠ **RECORDED WITH ITS REASONING BECAUSE THE FILTER WILL LOOK LIKE A BUG LATER.** A lane meeting
`origin = webhook` on a money feed to a general ledger will reasonably ask why three quarters of the
receipts are missing, and *"the customer asked for it"* only survives if it is written where they
will look.

⚠ **AND IT IS WHY THE ORIGIN COLUMN IS BUILT FOR ALL THREE VALUES RATHER THAN AS A WEBHOOK FLAG.**
Had online-only been our own narrowing, a boolean would have done. Because it is a customer's
*current* requirement, the filter must widen without a migration on a money path the day they ask
for counter receipts too — `NFR-5`'s reasoning applied to a value set instead of a row count.
