## 2026-09-22 — THE THREE NEW WORLD FIELD ANSWERS: GL ACCOUNT ALWAYS, PROJECT CODES NEVER, DUE-TO EMPTY (`CR-132-BRC07`)

Three fields were raised as questions rather than guessed. The PO answered all three. **Two are
taken as given; one carries a single word this session is changing, with the reason stated.**

### 1 · `GLAccountNumber` — ALWAYS SENT. The conditional is CLOSED.

**PO verbatim:** *"we are mapping gL code to various utility services and all cahrge codes so we
will ahve a gl code"*.

Their spec marks it **C — required UNLESS New World derives it from the payment-code mapping**. The
PO's answer closes that condition in our favour: our accounting settings map **every service's usage
and base charges, and every charge code**, to a GL account, so **a GL account is always resolvable
and is always sent.** New World never has to derive one.

### 2 · `ProjectCode1/2/3` — EMPTY, BOTH SETS.

**PO verbatim:** *"curerntly you send our GL codes as Project codes … if it changes we will figure
it out"*.

⚠ **THE SESSION PUT BACK THAT THEIR OWN SPEC FORBIDS IT, AND THE PO DID NOT REAFFIRM**, so empty
stands. Their sheet, quoted: *"Only used when GL distribution isn't specified separately — **not
expected to be needed since SmartBillHub supplies GL Distribution nodes**"*. **The transaction-level
project codes are an ALTERNATIVE to a GL breakdown, not a second place to put one.** We supply the
breakdown, so sending the GL code there states one fact in two fields that mean different things —
ignored at best, double-posted or rejected at worst.

**There are TWO sets and they do different jobs:** transaction level *replaces* a GL breakdown;
distribution level sits *alongside* one as an extra reporting dimension. **The second set is the
real gap** — a City tracking revenue against a grant would use it and we have nothing to put in it —
and it is deferred on the PO's own terms: *if it changes we will figure it out*.

### 3 · `DueToDueFromFund` — EMPTY, NOT ZERO.

**PO verbatim:** *"no we are mapping gL code to various utility services and all cahrge codes so we
will ahve a gl code - you can pick it up or say zero"*.

**The substance is accepted:** we do not state the inter-fund entry. Because a GL account always
travels, New World derives the fund from it exactly as most municipal charts intend.

⚠ **THE ONE WORD BEING CHANGED IS `zero`, AND IT IS THIS DAY'S OWN RULING APPLIED ONE FIELD OVER.**
`DueToDueFromFund` is **64 alphanumeric and OPTIONAL (N)**. An empty optional field cannot corrupt
their posting; **`0` is an invented fund identifier** and their importer is free to read it as fund
zero. The PO offered *"pick it up or say zero"* as two options and did not instruct zero, so the
third — **empty** — is taken, and recorded here so the choice is visible rather than assumed.

⚠ **AND THE SAME ANSWER COVERS THE CASE `zero` WAS OFFERED FOR.** If a GL account is ever NOT
resolvable — a tenant that has not finished its mapping — the receipt is **sent and FLAGGED, never
filled with a placeholder.** That is the PO's own ruling of this morning, verbatim in its own
section: *SEND IT · NEVER SILENTLY · NEVER PLUG IT · LET THEM REJECT IT*. A zero GL account and a
plug distribution line are the same act.

**THE PATTERN ACROSS ALL THREE, WORTH MORE THAN ANY OF THEM:** every one was a field we could have
filled with something plausible — a GL code in a project slot, a zero in a fund slot, a rounded cent
in a distribution. **An empty optional field is a fact. A plausible value is a lie that reconciles.**

## 2026-09-22 — BOTH PERCENT BASES SHIP, THE ENGINE CARRIES THE BASIS, AND NOT ONE FROZEN FIGURE MOVES (`CR-130-BRC07` wave A, rating backend, 🔒)

**What was built, in one sentence:** a rate schedule priced as a percentage of another service now
says **what it is a percentage OF** — that service's metered QUANTITY or that service's usage-charge
DOLLARS — and the engine prices both.

### THE TWO WORKED FIGURES, WHICH ARE THE ACCEPTANCE TEST

The Product Owner gave one for each basis, verbatim:

> *"if water charge is $100, and %age is 80% then sewer cahrge will be $80"*

> *"if Water usage will be 100 gallan %age is 80% then sewer uage will be 80 gallan = sewer charge
> will be 80 X { flat rate or tiered rate}"*

Both are asserted against the real engine in `06-backend/tests/test_cr130_percent_basis.py`:

| basis | what is on the bill | what sewer bills |
|---|---|---|
| **charge** | water usage **$100.00** (plus a **$25.00** water base, which is NOT in the basis) | **$80.00** |
| **usage** | water **100 gallons**, sewer's own flat rate **$0.50** | 80 gallons → **$40.00** |
| **usage, through a ladder** | the same 80 gallons through 0–30 at `$1.00` · 30–60 at `$2.00` · 60+ at `$3.00` | `30.00 + 60.00 + 60.00` = **$150.00**, on three lines |

**The base charge is excluded and it is on the bill so the exclusion is exercised rather than
assumed:** 80% of `$125.00` would be `$100.00`. `engine._usage_dollars` filters by line KIND, which
is `BR-RAT-015`'s own three exclusions — base out, tax out, fee out — restored together with the
arithmetic they belonged to.

### NOTHING SIGNED MOVES, AND HERE IS THE NUMBER THAT PROVES THE RISK WAS REAL

❄️ `GT-17` **$36.00** · `GT-20` **$54.00** · `GT-25` **$27.00** · `GT-26` **$27.00**, all re-signed
by the PO on 2026-09-08 under HUMAN-GUIDE §6, are **unchanged**, and all four are now asserted
against the ENGINE rather than only against the document harness.

⚠ **On GT-17's own bill the wrong basis costs 45 cents a month.** Water bills `$20.00 + $19.50 =
$39.50` of usage, so 90% of the MONEY is **$35.55** where 90% of the VOLUME is **$36.00**. Both foot
against themselves; nothing on the document says which one it is. That figure is why
`rating/0043_cr130_percent_basis.py` writes `'usage'` onto every existing row **by name** in a
separate backfill and only then makes the column `NOT NULL` — the `SET NOT NULL` is the assertion,
and a row the backfill could not reach stops the deploy instead of quietly acquiring the right
answer.

### THE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE, WITH THEIR REASONING — NONE OF THESE WAS PUT TO THE PO

1. **A missing basis REFUSES; it does not default to `usage`.** Every stored row names one of the
   two, so a `None` at the plugin means a seam dropped the column across four hops (column →
   `pricing_inputs` → `gather` → `normalize` → plugin). Defaulting would hide that hop and be
   indistinguishable from a tenant's choice, at a cost of 45 cents a month per sewer account on the
   signed bill.
2. **A rate stated on the `charge` basis is REFUSED BY NAME, at both layers.** A percentage of money
   has no price per gallon. Accepting and ignoring one is a number the tenant types, the screen
   shows and the engine drops — the same class of fault as the `tiers[0]` discard below.
3. **`basis_amount` is the Σ of the basis service's FINALIZED (printed, 2dp) usage lines.**
   `OQ-232` asks exactly this and is **OPEN — non-blocking**, with the printed reading already
   recorded in the register together with its reasoning (`03-golden-verify.py` computes GT-17's old
   basis from the rounded tier lines; B4.2's re-sign of 2026-08-11 settled the identical question
   for the tax base because *"a customer who adds up the four printed lines and applies the rate"*
   must reach the printed figure). **The PO's own figure, `$100.00` at 80% → `$80.00`, is exact at
   both readings and does not distinguish them.** Nothing new was decided; a disposition already in
   the register was implemented and stated in the code.
4. **The ladder is walked by `tiered.price`, not by a second implementation.** `BR-RAT-026`'s *every
   unit bills through a tier* refusal, `BR-RAT-002`'s threshold proration and the block wording then
   exist once in the product, and only the line's DESCRIPTION is rewritten afterwards so the
   customer can see where the quantity came from.
5. **A schedule may not be a percentage of ITSELF**, refused at the screen's own validator rather
   than only at bill time — the engine already refuses it structurally (the basis record is written
   in pass A only), but a refusal a clerk can see beats a bill nobody gets.

### THE `tiers[0]` DISCARD — FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE THAT OPENS THE DOOR

`selectors.pricing_inputs` read `tiers[0].unit_price` for a percent schedule and **silently
discarded every block after the first**. It was correct while nothing in the product could create a
second block. The moment the ladder exists, a five-block sewer ladder would have billed every gallon
at block one's price — on the figures above, **$80.00 where the answer is $150.00**, with no error
anywhere and a document that foots against itself. A one-block schedule still publishes `unit_price`
and an EMPTY tier list, which is exactly what keeps ❄️ GT-17 at `$36.00`; both directions are
asserted.

### THE BASIS LIST IS DERIVED — NO SERVICE CODE IN ANY CONDITION

Per the PO's ruling of this date (*"dont hard code anything - use logic to derive it so that it is
flexible and handle any scenario"*), `selectors.percent_basis_options` offers, on **charge**, every
service the tenant has switched on except this one, and on **usage**, those of them the utility
declares it METERS — read from `tenant_services.billing_basis` through
`seams.service_bills_from_a_register`, never from a list this module keeps. The test asserts it
against the function's **source**, not only its output, because a list that happens to be right
today can still be built from a hard-coded pair and the eleventh service is when anybody finds out.

### WHAT IS OWED AND IS NOT CLAIMED DONE

* **The charge basis has no ❄️ frozen golden test behind it.** `$80.00` is the PO's own figure and
  is asserted against the engine, but it is not B5-signed. The review-ledger row puts it to them in
  plain English with the number.
* **Three backend refusals need a sentence in eleven catalogues, and wave B owns those files.**
  `rating.percent.basis_is_itself`, `rating.percent.basis_meters_nothing` and
  `rating.percent.rate_not_on_charge_basis`. Until they land, `G32` counts three more unresolved
  keys (8 → 11 against a baseline of 0) and those three refusals reach a clerk as silence. Named
  here rather than left in a lane's own file, because a finding recorded only where its author
  happened to be is a finding nobody can count.

## 2026-09-22 — A PRINTED READER SHEET IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE ABSENCE (`CR-131-BRC07` question 2)

**PO ruling, verbatim:**

> *"not required, you dont have to reproduce it . option a"*

**A reader's sheet is a WORKING DOCUMENT, not a record.** Nothing stores that a sheet was printed,
nothing will, and `DEF-MET-6144` closes as **not a defect — a deliberate absence**, recorded here so
the next lane meeting it does not "fix" it.

**What answers the question a sheet would have answered:** the READINGS. What was read, when, by
which meter, and — once question 1 is settled — on which route.

### ⚠ OPTION (c) IS RULED OUT WHATEVER ELSE CHANGES, AND THIS IS THE HALF WORTH KEEPING

A sheet could be *rebuilt* from the readings collected that day, cheaply, and it would look like an
answer. **It is not one.** It shows what **was read** and never what was **asked for** — so the one
thing anybody opens an old sheet to find, **a stop the reader missed**, is exactly the thing such a
reconstruction cannot show. It is invisible by construction.

**So: no stored sheet, and no reconstruction presented as one.** If the City ever acquires an
obligation to prove what a reader was instructed to do, that is a **stored artifact and a story of
its own** — not a query dressed up as one.

⚠ **THE SHAPE IS THIS REPO'S OWN AND IT IS WHY THE RULING IS WRITTEN OUT RATHER THAN TICKED:** a
cheap answer that is confidently wrong about the one case it exists for is the *check that does not
check*, one layer up — `CLAUDE.md` law 7's fourth shape, *looking at the wrong thing*, arriving as a
feature instead of a test.

## 2026-09-22 — `CR-131-BRC07`, THE STEP 1 GATE ANSWERED: RT-009 SHOWS 100, AND THE WALK ORDER STAYS PER PROPERTY

The gate stopped the lane with three questions. **The PO answered all three.**

### QUESTION 1 · WHAT *READ ON THIS ROUTE* MEANS — **the readings COLLECTED on it**

**PO verbatim**, asked whether RT-009 shows 100 or 0: **`"100"`**, and, on how:

> *"you will build it in dynamic way not static. when you query or search for 100 meter and its
> reading they are property of meters. when units are moved to another route, and that route search
> meters and its reading you wil find what was there - if you hard code it - you will not find it ,
> if you use logical code you will find it"*

A route walked in August reports its August readings **after** its properties move; the route that
acquired them reports only its own. Four queries change — the readings list, the progress count, the
sheet and *last read on* — which is `DEF-MET-6143`.

⚠ **THE STAMP IS NOT THE HARD-CODING THE PO IS WARNING AGAINST, AND THAT WAS PUT TO THEM IN THOSE
WORDS BEFORE THEY ANSWERED.** `meter_reads.route_id` is **a recording of which route covered that
meter at the moment the reader stood in front of it** — written by the product from the LIVE
membership at collection time. It is the already-computed answer to *which route was this meter on
when it was read*. **Re-deriving it from the change history is the fragile option, not the flexible
one**: it would reconstruct a fact about August from records of what changed since, using an audit
trail never designed to be replayed. **Build from the stamp.** All 516 reads on the fixture carry
one.

⚠ **THE COST IS STATED WHERE A TENANT WILL MEET IT:** readings older than the stamp have **no route
and drop out of the route filter**. Zero on this fixture, **not zero on an old tenant** — so it goes
in the release note rather than surprising a clerk, because *an absence a clerk cannot explain is
worse than a number they can*.

### QUESTION 3 · WALK ORDER — **PER PROPERTY**, and this SUPERSEDES the morning's ruling

**PO verbatim:** *"a is okay"*.

⚠ **THIS REVERSES THE PO's OWN RULING OF THE SAME MORNING** — *"i will update the walk order on
units directly or asset"* — **and the supersession is STATED here rather than assumed** (law 13). The
**2026-08-23** ruling stands: *"a reader walks to an address and reads everything there"*, and it is
the one that is BUILT — `route_premises_orders`, an audited writer, both uniqueness rules,
drag-to-reorder on screen, and the printed sheet's stops.

**`CR-131` steps 2 and 8 are CANCELLED.** No column on `units`, nothing migrated, the reorder screen
untouched. `OQ-MET-12572` closes. **The cancelled steps are REMOVED from the CR rather than left to
rot** — a cancelled step in a live plan is the stale body this repo keeps paying for.

⚠ **AND WHY IT NEEDED NO CHANGE AT ALL, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING:** a per-property order is
**6 rows attached to the 6 premises we are keeping** — declared, not derived — so **it cannot go
stale**, which is the whole of the morning ruling's reasoning already satisfied. The morning ruling
was aimed at `route_memberships.walk_order`: a **dead column, never written to, zero rows**. **The
thing the PO objected to was real; it was simply not the thing in use** — and that is why the gate
asked instead of relocating a rule on top of a working one.

## 2026-09-22 — THE THREE ANSWERS THAT RE-OPEN `CR-131-BRC07`: A ROUTE REPORTS WHAT WAS COLLECTED ON IT, A PRINTED SHEET IS NOT KEPT, AND THE WALK ORDER STAYS PER PROPERTY

**Step 1 of `CR-131-BRC07` was a gate and it did not pass** (the section above, *"STEP 1 OF
`CR-131-BRC07` IS A GATE"*). It asked the PO three things and built nothing. **All three are now
answered. This row is the answers, verbatim, before a line of the build.**

### 1 · *WHAT DOES "READ ON THIS ROUTE" MEAN?* — **PO: *"100"***

The question put to them, in plain English with its figure: *when a clerk opens RT-009 and asks what
was read on it, should the answer be the **100** readings COLLECTED on that route, or the readings on
the meters that are on it TODAY — which is **0** the moment its eight properties move to another
route?*

**PO ruling, verbatim: *"100"***.

**THE RULE: A ROUTE REPORTS THE READINGS COLLECTED ON IT.** A route walked in August reports its
August readings even after its properties move; the route that acquired those properties reports
only its own. `BR-MET-081` — *"Collected reads keep their route"* — becomes TRUE on the screens a
clerk reads, and not only in a docstring.

**The PO's reasoning, verbatim:**

> *"you will build it in dynamic way not static. when you query or search for 100 meter and its
> reading they are property of meters … if you hard code it - you will not find it, if you use
> logical code you will find it"*

⚠ **THE STAMP IS NOT THE HARD-CODING THEY ARE WARNING ABOUT, AND THIS WAS PUT TO THEM IN THOSE WORDS
BEFORE THEY ANSWERED — so the reading is recorded rather than assumed**, the same discipline this
log applied to *"register max"* on 2026-09-03 and to *"should not be status"* this morning.
`meter_reads.route_id` (`BR-MET-079`, `metering/0012`) is **a recording of which route covered that
meter at the moment the reader stood in front of it**, written by the product from the live
membership by `services.collection_route_id`. It is the already-computed answer to *which route was
this meter on when it was read*. **Re-deriving that from the change history would be the fragile
option, not the flexible one** — it would need a temporal record of every membership change that
this product does not keep and that the same ruling forbids inventing.

**So it is built FROM THE STAMP: four query changes**, and the earlier lane measured that all
**516** reads on the seeded fixture carry one.

⚠ **THE COST IS STATED WHERE A TENANT WILL MEET IT, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE A CLERK CANNOT EXPLAIN IS
WORSE THAN A NUMBER THEY CAN.** On a tenant holding readings older than the stamp — anything
collected before `metering/0012` — **those readings have no route and vanish from the route
filter.** On this fixture that cost is **zero: 516 of 516 are stamped.** It is not zero on an old
tenant, so the release note and the screen say so rather than letting a clerk discover a silent gap.

### 2 · *MUST A PRINTED SHEET BE REPRODUCIBLE AS ISSUED?* — **PO: *"not required, you dont have to reproduce it . option a"***

**`DEF-MET-6144` CLOSES AS NOT A DEFECT — A DELIBERATE ABSENCE.** Nothing stores that a reader's
sheet was printed and nothing will. The product renders a sheet on demand from current membership,
and that is the whole of the capability.

⚠ **AND OPTION (c) IS RULED OUT WHATEVER ELSE CHANGES.** A sheet could be rebuilt cheaply from the
readings collected that day, and it would look like an answer. **It is not one:** it shows what was
**read**, never what was **asked for** — so **a stop the reader MISSED, which is the one thing
anybody ever opens an old sheet to find, is invisible by construction.** No stored sheet, and no
reconstruction presented as one. A reconstruction that cannot show an omission is worse than the
honest absence, because it answers confidently and wrongly.

### 3 · *WALK ORDER — PER PROPERTY OR PER UNIT?* — **PO: *"a is okay"* — PER PROPERTY**

`OQ-MET-12572` offered three options in plain English. **The PO chose (a): leave the walk order
where it is, per premises, in the table that already holds it.**

⚠ **THIS SUPERSEDES THE PO's OWN RULING OF THIS MORNING, AND THE SUPERSESSION IS STATED RATHER THAN
ASSUMED** (`13-change-process.md` step 2). The superseded sentence, verbatim, from the
2026-09-22 *"A ROUTE IS NOT A SNAPSHOT"* exchange:

> *"i will update the walk order on units directly or asset - one of these palces - not keep them in
> routes - becuase keeping the walk order in route is wrong since derive the units is dynamic"*

**It is superseded because it was reasoning about a dead column.** `route_memberships.walk_order` is
superseded, has no writer and holds **0 rows**. The 2026-08-23 ruling — *"Per premises"*, with its
reasoning *"a reader walks to an ADDRESS and reads everything there"* — **is the one that is BUILT**:
`route_premises_orders` with both uniqueness rules (one stop one position, one position one stop),
`walk_order.save_premises_order` as its audited writer behind a `SYSTEM_ADMIN` guard,
`walk_order.premises_order_for_route` as its reader, drag-to-reorder live on `RouteDetailPage.tsx`,
and the printed sheet's stops read from it. That ruling **stands and is what is built.**

**AND NOTE WHY IT NEEDED NO CHANGE AT ALL, because this is the part that makes both rulings agree:**
a per-property order is **6 rows attached to the 6 premises we are keeping — declared, not
derived — so it cannot go stale.** The September ruling's own principle (an order must not depend on
a derived set) is *satisfied* by the August grain, because premises membership is the one thing
`CR-131` stores. Only the September sentence disagreed, and only because of what it was told about.

**`CR-131-BRC07` STEPS 2 AND 8 ARE CANCELLED.** No column is added to `units`, nothing is migrated,
the reorder screen is untouched. `OQ-MET-12572` closes. ⚠ **The per-unit instruction is REMOVED from
the CR rather than left to rot** — a cancelled step left in a plan is exactly the stale body
`CLAUDE.md`'s prime directive records three lanes being misled by in one evening.

### WHAT THIS LEAVES THE LANE TO BUILD, AND THE ONE CONSTRAINT THAT BINDS ALL OF IT

The stamp's **only** source is `service_points.route_id`. The gate proved that emptying that column
makes `services.collection_route_id` return `None`, that `meter_reads.route_id` is nullable, and
that **nothing goes red** — the read history would simply stop being recorded from the day a
derivation design shipped. **So whatever lands must keep a route resolvable at collection time**,
and that is proved by emptying the projection and calling the real collection function, not by
reading the code.


## 2026-09-22 — BUILT: A PREMISES NAMES ITS MASTER ACCOUNT DIRECTLY (`CR-130-BRC07` part three, lane C1, backend)

The ruling is the section above; this is what was built from it, the five judgments the ruling
did not settle, and one near-miss worth more than any of them.

**MEASURED FIRST, ON REAL POSTGRESQL, BEFORE A LINE WAS CHANGED** — a clone of the `brazosbend`
beta, `22-product-maintenance-process.md` step 1, which no gate in this repo can ask for:

| what a clerk did | what happened |
|---|---|
| name `Harriet Vane`, kind **person**, an **SSN**, account type **residential** | master accounts **1 → 1** · no account on the address · one warning, `no_typed_owner` |
| name `Ridge Property LLC`, kind **company**, a **Tax ID**, account type **commercial** | identical |
| the whole beta | **0 of 79 properties** had an owner account the money path could find |

That third line is the one that matters. `BR-MET-105`'s empty-unit base charge — worked at
**$30.50 a month** — and the move-out shortfall both post to *the owner*, and on that database
there was nobody to post to at any address. Filed as **`DEF-MET-6139`**, before it was fixed.

### JUDGMENT 1 · THE PRECEDENCE HAS ONE IMPLEMENTATION, AND THE SERIALISER'S COPY IS ASSERTED AGAINST IT

The ruling declares the order; it does not say where it lives. It lives in
`premises_owners.premises_master_account_link`, and `owner_master_account_for_premises` is now the
one-value form of that function rather than a second reading of the same two columns.

**There is a SECOND reading and it is deliberate:** `selectors.premises_master_account_from_row`
reads a row already in memory, because a list holding 200 rows must not issue 200 queries. Two
implementations of one order is exactly how `BR-CUS-171`'s geometric derivation came to disagree
with the declared owner — so **a test asserts the two agree**, on both shapes, and says in as many
words that if they ever differ the money path is right and the serialiser is wrong. A comment
claiming they agree would have been hard-won law 1.

### JUDGMENT 2 · EVERY READ SAYS WHICH DECLARATION ANSWERED

`master_account_source` is `premises` or `owner_record`, served on every premises read.

It is not tidiness. **It is `BR-MET-1162`'s shape**: a unit may carry its own point or fall back to
its building's, and that rule makes every screen showing a point say which of the two it is showing.
Two declarations that can disagree owe a reader the same sentence — and here the sentence decides
who is billed. It costs no query, because both columns are already read.

### JUDGMENT 3 · THE NUMBER RIDES FREE ON THE LIST; THE ACCOUNT DOES NOT

**B14 rule 31 is signed law: no database id is ever the visible value of a field.** A list column
holding only `master_account_id` therefore had nothing it was allowed to draw — and `DEF-324`
forbids the obvious fix, having measured one-account-read-plus-one-ledger-derivation per row at
*47 of 118 profiled seconds answering one question 304 times*.

So the page's ids are asked **once**: `customers.selectors.master_account_numbers` is a single
`SELECT account_no, kind, status … WHERE id IN (…)`, with **no balance and no ledger** — because
`DEF-127`'s shape (the ledger's Σ, with a REASON where the books cannot be asked, never `0.00`
substituted for *we could not tell*) cannot be served cheaply in bulk, and a figure on a list is a
figure somebody quotes.

⚠ **AND THE PER-ROW FALLBACK IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, WHICH IS THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE BITTEN.**
`exports.PREMISES` serialises **every** premises the tenant has, one row at a time, with no page to
batch over. A serialiser that quietly asked per row when nobody handed it a page would have put one
statement per property into that file — `DEF-324` re-created in the one place `NFR-3` cares about
most, and invisible until a utility with 40,000 addresses pressed Export. The batch is **opt-in**,
the export gets `master_account_no: null`, and `master_account_expanded: false` says nobody asked.

### JUDGMENT 4 · `no_typed_owner` IS RENAMED, AND THE OLD NAME IS KEPT AS AN ALIAS

There is no typed owner in the chain any more, so the reason a clerk is given had to change:
**`owner_not_named`**. The old constant stays, assigned to the new value, because tests and
walkthroughs written for `DEF-MET-5844` import it by name — and a rename that breaks a sibling's
file at the same moment as a behaviour change is two failures wearing one commit.

**The five verdicts now each carry their own `message_key` and exactly one wording of it.** Before
today the server computed a distinct answer every time and **a whole-front-end grep found zero
occurrences of any of them outside the import receipt** — the wizard fired one toast, *"Premise
created"*, and threw the array away. `refused` deliberately has **no** entry in that map: the door
that refused carries its own key, and a second wording here is how two doors start explaining one
refusal differently.

### JUDGMENT 5 · WHAT USING THE TYPED NAME DOES AND DOES NOT CROSS

The party an account is opened FOR is now the name on the form. Two rules were checked against that,
one at a time, rather than waved at:

* **`BR-MET-151` clause 3 — never read a party's CATEGORY off a NAME.** Not crossed. **No
  `premises_owners` row is created by this path at all**, so there is no category to read. The name
  is used as a NAME, which is the same string `create_master_account` has always fallen back to out
  of `owner_manager` for the contact and the customer. A test counts the owner table before and
  after, because the cheapest wrong fix is to invent a party with a guessed category.
* **`BR-MET-112` — a wizard does not mint an account because a field was filled in.** Not crossed.
  It takes a name AND a kind AND an identifier of that kind AND an account type — four deliberate
  answers, which is `owner_account_verdict`'s ELIGIBLE and is `OQ-MET-12472`'s ruling in as many
  words. One door, one press, one transaction.

### THE COST TO A CLERK, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED — `OQ-MET-12573`, OPEN

The identity ask used to be **once per OWNER**: the owner RECORD carried the link, so a landlord's
second address reused the first one's account. The declaration is on the PREMISES now and owner
records are out of the screens, so for a party with no owner record the ask is **once per ADDRESS**.

For a landlord with twelve buildings that is eleven extra identifier entries. It is raised and not
decided, because every route to an answer either reverses the PO's ruling of the same day or crosses
`BR-MET-151` clause 3 — matching a party by a string somebody typed is precisely what that clause
forbids. **Nothing stubs on it and nothing guesses at it**; the shipped behaviour is complete, and
`customers` resolves the party by the IDENTIFIER, so twelve accounts still belong to one customer.

### ⚠ THE NEAR-MISS, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE CHEAPEST LESSON HERE

This lane wrote the whole change against **`BR-MET-401`** — and `BR-MET-401` **has existed since
2026-08-27** and says something else: *at premises creation the owner is required, and an existing
party is reused rather than duplicated*. The number was chosen by reading the rules that surround
`BR-MET-400`, which is exactly the wrong place to look: **this family's maximum is `BR-MET-1180`,
four hundred rules further on.**

Nothing would have caught it. `G106` asks whether a cited id was ever ISSUED, and this one was;
`G17` refuses a duplicate CR number and not a duplicate BR. The result would have been **two rules
with one id on a money path**, which is `DEF-2804`'s shape — a real id read for a different real id
— and CLAUDE.md names that family as 37 ids from the same cliff.

It was found by grepping the rules file before appending, not by a tool. **So: allocate a `BR-` id
the way a defect id is allocated — from the family's MAXIMUM, asked of the remote — never from the
neighbourhood of the rule you are amending.** The new rule is **`BR-MET-1181`** and the rename
touched 45 occurrences across eight files.

## 2026-09-22 · THE CHART OF ACCOUNTS' REFUSAL WAS NEVER MISSING — IT WAS 14,428 PIXELS AWAY (`DEF-LED-6140`)

**PO, verbatim:** *"one more bug in charts of account in setting - you ahve given action at bottom,
add and edit; make both actions a modal. and second give add button on top, not at bottom - remove
the bottom forms. on edit if youa re unable to save , then show the reason why youa re unable to
save to user, currently it is not showing"*, and on the plan: *"go ahead and start it - ensure
rufuse messages are for human short and concise and meaningful"*.

**Classified MAINTENANCE, not a change** (`22-product-maintenance-process.md`): a clerk can add and
edit chart accounts in the product today, and the product did not do what was expected. We
classified it; it did not go back to the PO, because nothing here changes what a user can DO.

### THE FINDING, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A DIAGNOSIS

*"Currently it is not showing"* is what the PO SAW, and the code said the opposite — the panel
rendered `{failure !== null && <p role="alert">}` and every test asserting that sentence was in the
document passed. **Both were true.** Driven in Chromium at 1440x900 against the demo tenant's
**129-row** chart:

| what | where |
|---|---|
| the scroll viewport (`main.view`) | **844px** tall, content **15,354px** |
| the `Save ✓` button the clerk presses | y = **15,126** — on screen |
| the refusal sentence | y = **698** — `inViewport: false` |
| **distance** | **14,428px · about seventeen screenfuls** |

**So the defect is not a missing sentence, it is a sentence with no relationship to the button that
produced it** — and no gate in this repository can see that, because none of them reads a pixel.
The inline Add form began at y=14,770 and the Edit form at y=14,999, so *both* the PO's complaints
are one fault: a form at the bottom of an unbounded list, and the one refusal strip at the top.

### WHAT WAS DECIDED, WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT

**1 · `FormModal`, not a seventh dialog.** B14 rule 43. The six sibling dialogs on this same screen
already use it, and it already owned every part of the fix — the refusal between the fields and the
buttons, `envelopeErrors` routing each `field_error` under its own input, focus to the first bad
field. **Nothing had to be extended; it only lacked a caller.**

**2 · SIX BACKEND REFUSALS NOW NAME A FIELD, AND NOTHING ELSE MOVED.** `code_taken`,
`tax_series_reserved` and `designation_taken` carried no `field_errors`, so even a dialog had
nowhere to put them; five `_clean_*` field errors carried no `message_key`, which resolves to
nothing and paints a box red with no words beside it. **What is refused is exactly what was refused
before.** The house precedent is `metering.premises.external_ref_taken`, which carries the same key
in both halves.

**3 · ONE SENTENCE, ONCE — a change to the SHARED `FormModal`, deliberately.** That envelope shape
carries a field-naming refusal twice, so a dialog rendering both puts identical words under the
input and above the buttons. `FormModal` now drops the form-level line **only** when a field is
already showing that exact sentence. Every existing caller renders as before; a whole-payload
refusal that names no field still renders in the form slot.

**4 · THE COPY — three refusals came OFF the `G33` baseline, 578 over-cap messages down to 575.**

| before | after |
|---|---|
| *"You already have an account numbered 1200."* (7 words) | **"That number is already used. Use a different one."** (5 + 4) |
| *"Another live account already holds the cash role. Clear it there first."* (8 + 4) | **"Another account already holds this role. Clear it there first."** (6 + 4) |
| *"Numbers in the 2200 range are reserved for tax authorities."* (10) | **"Tax authorities own the 2200 range. Pick another number."** (6 + 3) |

⚠ **THE SECOND ONE WAS ALSO PRINTING A RAW ENUM.** `{{designation}}` interpolated the database value
`cash`, so a clerk read *"the cash role"* — B14 rule 31's shape on a settings screen. The role picker
is beside the sentence, so the role does not need naming at all, and the shortening removed the
breach as a side effect rather than by a separate fix.

The frozen note moved into the edit dialog and lost its RATIONALE rather than being compressed
(rule 33: *rationale is removed, not shortened*) — *"— history is never restated"* now lives only in
`update_account`'s docstring. *"The number and type cannot change. To renumber, add a new account."*

### TWO THINGS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED

* **`DEF-LED-6147`** — Retire, Bring back and Delete are row commands with no form, so their refusal
  still renders in the strip at the top. Same distance fault, different control family. Redesigning
  three row actions the PO did not report is what maintenance step 3 forbids.
* **`DEF-LED-6146`** — **the panel has no `readOnly` concept at all.** `SettingsAccountingTab`
  threads `readOnly` into the Import button only, and `GeneralLedgerPage` mounts the panel with no
  read-only handling whatever, under a page whose own subtitle says *"Read-only trial balance"*.
  **So the Finance surface is NOT read-only today and never was** — it already carried a live Add
  form and live row actions before this change, which is why moving them into a dialog makes nothing
  editable that was not editable this morning.

**Shipped in `2.324.1`. Rollback is a revert of the commit; nothing was migrated and nothing was
sent.**

## 2026-09-22 — THE NINE UNSCOPED SEED UNITS CANNOT BE SCOPED, AND THE UNIT PICKER IS FIXED A LAYER ABOVE THEM (`CR-130-BRC07` part two, lane B)

**What was asked.** `CR-130-BRC07` §8.3 item 4: *"the nine unscoped seed units get the scopes they
should always have had"*, in `lookup_defaults.json` plus a migration for existing tenants. It was
written while sizing the Product Owner's report — *"when you show the unit of measure while setting
the rates, please use unit of measurement set in the settings for that utility"* — and it is the
one item of part two that **cannot be built as written without taking a legitimate unit away from a
service that needs it.** This row records the judgment, the figures it rests on and what shipped
instead, so the next lane does not reach for it again.

### THE FIGURES, MEASURED RATHER THAN READ

| measured | where |
|---|---|
| **28** units in the seed | `apps/tenancy/fixtures/lookup_defaults.json` |
| **9** of them state no service IN THE FIXTURE | `kWh · kW · kgal · ccf · therm · month · MMBtu · kW-DC · day` |
| **7** of them are unscoped **in a provisioned database** | PostgreSQL 16.13, `sbh_clone_laneb`: `kWh` resolves to `electric` and `therm` to `gas` before the row is ever written |
| **8** units offered on a Sewer schedule | walked in Chromium: `EDU · MMBtu · ccf · day · kW · kW-DC · kgal · month`, all eight selectable, none preselected |
| **1** unit this utility actually declared | `tenant_services.primary_uom` for sewer = `kgal` |

**The fixture's nine and the database's seven are two different numbers and both are true.**
`_seed_uoms` resolves a new row as `stated or SEEDED_UOM_SERVICE_SCOPE.get(code)`, so a fixture
entry that states nothing is decided by `_derive_uom_service_scope` — which is why the report showed
eight and not ten.

### WHY THE SEVEN CANNOT BE NARROWED

`tenancy.services._derive_uom_service_scope` NULLs any unit that **more than one service claims**,
and its own docstring argues the rule: *"One nullable column cannot say 'water or gas', and
inventing a join table to say it would be resolving a question nobody asked. NULL already means
'All services' … which is the SAFE direction: the failure this closes is a picker offering TOO
MUCH, never too little."*

Every one of the seven is in one of three buckets, and none of them is a mistake:

| unit | claimed by | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `kgal` | water **and sewer** | scoping it to water **refuses the very sewer schedule this change request is about** — `CR-081` gave sewer a quantity in water's unit on 2026-09-08 and this scope was deliberately WIDENED back that day |
| `ccf` | water, gas **and sewer** | three claimants; one column, one answer |
| `kW` | electric, battery **and solar** | three claimants, stated in that function as a warning against exactly this edit |
| `month`, `day` | nobody | *Month (flat)* and *Day (prorated flat)* are how ANY service bills a flat or prorated charge. Scoping them would break every service that does |
| `MMBtu` | nobody | ambiguous between gas and thermal/heat — scoping it to one takes it from the other |
| `kW-DC` | nobody | *Kilowatt DC* is solar's rating **and battery's**; same ambiguity, same cost |

⚠ **AND NARROWING IS THE RISKY DIRECTION, WHICH THAT FUNCTION ALSO ALREADY SAYS** — *"narrowing is
the RISKY direction and was accepted deliberately, since the seed governs NEW rows only and no
stored unit is rewritten."* A seed narrowed here reaches new tenants; a MIGRATION narrowing existing
tenants, which item 4 also asks for, would make `resolve_uom` start refusing units those tenants are
currently using.

**So item 4 would have moved the unit list by at most one entry (8 → 7 on Sewer) and would have cost
a refusal on a live sewer schedule to do it.** `lookup_defaults.json` and the tenancy migration are
therefore NOT changed, and nothing about the seed moves.

### WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD, AND WHY IT IS THE BETTER ANSWER TO WHAT WAS REPORTED

Items 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 — the layer the Product Owner actually described. **The picker reads
`tenant_services.billed_uom`, else `primary_uom`** — this utility's own declaration, which is
per-tenant and per-service where a seed scope is neither — preselects it when the service is chosen,
and leaves every other unit **present and unselectable with its reason**. On the reported screen that
is **8 offered → 1 selectable, `kgal`, chosen before the clerk arrives.** A utility that has declared
nothing keeps today's list exactly, because there is nothing to narrow and inventing a narrowing
would be choosing a unit on their behalf.

⚠ **AND IT IS THE ONLY PLACE THAT CAN CATCH IT FOR A SHARE SERVICE.** `CR-130-BRC07` §8.2 says the
product *"checks them only at SAVE, as `BR-RAT-038`'s notice"*. **That is not true of sewer.**
`uom_gate_for` answers `no_register` — satisfied, no notice — before either unit is read, whenever
`tenant_services.billing_basis` is `share` or `capacity`, and sewer is `share`. So on the exact
service reported, **nothing anywhere told a clerk the unit was wrong: not at entry, and not at
save.** The save-time notice stays as the backstop it is (a script or a replay never opens this
screen); it was never the safety net §8.2 assumed. Filed as `DEF-RAT-6143`.

### THE OTHER THREE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE, WITH THEIR REASONS

1. **`usage` is the default basis and is listed first.** It is what every percent schedule in the
   product bills today and what six ❄️ FROZEN figures were re-signed onto on 2026-09-08
   (`GT-17`: 8 kgal → 7.2 kgal × `$5.0000` = **`$36.00`**). A control defaulting the other way would
   offer to change a live sewer bill by being opened, and §2 requires every stored schedule to be
   migrated to `usage` **by name**.
2. **A single-block percent schedule posts `unit_price` ALONGSIDE `tiers`; a multi-block one does
   not.** §3 keeps `unit_price` *"accepted for one block, as today"*. Wave A's server takes the
   `tiers` branch first and ignores `unit_price` when both arrive, so for ONE block the two agree
   by construction — they carry the same number — and the schedule saves against the server as it
   stood before wave A landed as well as against the one that accepts the ladder. Sending
   `tiers[0]`'s price for a THREE-block ladder would have been the same defect `selectors.py:5244`
   is being fixed for: one price silently standing in for three. A multi-block ladder posts `tiers`
   alone, so an older server refuses it by name instead, which is the right failure.
3. **THE `Based on` LIST IS THE SERVER'S ANSWER, NOT THE SCREEN'S — AND THIS LANE DELETED ITS OWN
   WORKING COPY TO MAKE THAT TRUE.** Wave B built `basisServiceOptions()` in `ratingShared.tsx`
   before wave A landed: the same three clauses, in TSX, with seven passing cases. Wave A then
   shipped `GET /rate-schedules/percent-basis-options` and an appendix asking for it to be used —
   *"It exists so the derivation is not written a second time in TSX … hard-won law 2 is precisely
   about the front end keeping its own copy of that list."* **The function and its seven tests are
   deleted rather than kept as a fallback.** The two agreed clause for clause, which is the reason
   to remove one rather than a reason to keep both: two derivations that agree today are two that
   can disagree tomorrow, and the copy on the SCREEN is the one no gate in this repo can watch go
   wrong. A fallback is the same hazard with a smaller name, so there is none — the card says the
   list has not arrived yet, which is this step's own house pattern.

4. **The taxability sentence names WHERE and never WHY.** B14 rule 33 puts rationale at **zero words
   on screen** and says it is REMOVED rather than shortened. The card reads *"Tax is set in
   Settings. Each tax lists its services."* — six words and five. The two reasons it is not a
   control here are in this log's own entry of 2026-09-22 and in `CR-130-BRC07` §5, which is where
   a reason belongs.

## 2026-09-22 — ❄️ FINANCE SIGN-OFF: THE CHARGE BASIS BILLS `$80.00`, AND THE STANDING CHARGE IS OUT

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"a is correct"*, answering a question put with its worked figure.

### WHAT WAS SHOWN, BECAUSE A SIGNATURE COVERS ONLY WHAT WAS SHOWN (PO ruling 2026-08-11)

A bill carrying a **$100.00 water usage charge** and a **$25.00 water standing charge**, with sewer
set to **80% of water on the CHARGE basis**:

| option shown | sewer bills | |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) the usage charge only** | **`$80.00`** | **SIGNED** |
| (b) include the standing charge | $100.00 | declined |
| (c) do not sign yet | $80.00, unsigned | declined |

**`$80.00` — eighty per cent of the $100.00, NOT of the $125.00.**

**Why the exclusion is the right half of the answer, and it is the PO's own earlier reasoning:** the
VOLUME basis they re-signed on 2026-09-08 excludes a standing charge and tax **by construction** —
the basis there is a metered quantity, so a base charge was never in it. Including it here would
make the two bases disagree about what *"the water"* means on one screen.

### ⚠ WHAT THIS SIGNATURE DOES **NOT** COVER

**The tiered usage figure `$150.00` and the flat usage figure `$40.00` are ENGINE-PROVED AND REMAIN
UNSIGNED.** They were reported to the PO as results; they were **not put for signature** and are not
carried in on this one. **The ladder is a NEW money path** — `GT-17`'s signed `$36.00` is the FLAT
usage basis, and pricing a derived quantity through blocks is arithmetic no frozen figure covers.
**They go to the agenda as their own question with their own worked numbers**, not as a footnote to
this row.

⚠ **THIS IS THE CLAUSE THAT GETS LOST.** A card with one signed figure on it reads, six weeks later,
as a signed card. **It is not.** The row in `09-human-review-ledger.md` now says so on its own first
line, so a reader meeting the row cannot take the signature wider than it goes.

### THE SECOND HALF OF A SIGN-OFF: A TEST ASSERTS THE RATIFIED FIGURE

`CLAUDE.md`'s sensitive-paths rule requires both parts — the plain-English ruling **and** a test that
goes RED on drift. The `$80.00` is asserted **against the engine** by lane A's wave-A suite, not
against a document that recomputes itself. **Confirm that assertion names this figure before this
row is treated as complete**; a signature with no test behind it is half a sign-off, and the half
that rots.

## 2026-09-22 — THE THREE PREMISES OWNER SCREENS, BUILT (`CR-130-BRC07` PART THREE, LANE C2)

Lane C2's judgment calls, with their figures. The RULING is the section above; this is
what building it decided.

### 1 · THE REPRODUCTION — AND THE ONE FACT NOBODY HAD PREDICTED

The whole diagnosis the PO read was **read from code**; the CR says so in as many
words (§9.4). It was clicked for the first time on 2026-09-22, on `brazosbend`, on a
real PostgreSQL clone, through `server.mjs`. Three of the four findings confirmed the
diagnosis. The fourth did not, and it is the one that explains the report:

| what was clicked | what happened |
|---|---|
| Add premise · the owner picker | **0 options.** The cupboard is empty |
| Edit premise · the same control | **0 options**, under *"Not listed? Type the name below"* |
| Premises detail · `Find an owner` + `AC` | `GET /premises-owners?q=AC` → **nothing**, on a tenant holding `AC-2026-00051` |
| the save | **HTTP 201**, body `[{"code":"owner_account_not_created","reason":"no_typed_owner"}]` |

⚠ **THE SAVE SUCCEEDS. IT IS NOT AN ERROR NOBODY SURFACED — IT IS A SUCCESS NOBODY
QUALIFIED.** Nothing failed, nothing was retried, no red appeared anywhere; the
address really was created, and the half of the act that did not happen was simply
never mentioned. The wizard fired one toast — *"Premise created"* — and dropped the
`warnings` array. **A whole-front-end grep for those verdict strings finds zero
occurrences outside the import receipt.** That is precisely why the report reads *"it
does not create the master account and also not linking that account to premsies -
why"*: the server had always said why, and no screen had ever asked.

Filed as `DEF-MET-6155` **before** anything was changed.

### 2 · ONE CORRECTION TO OUR OWN RECORD, MADE RATHER THAN LEFT

`DEF-MET-6155`'s `escape_reason` says the three screens *"read a table no screen can
fill"*. **That is one word too strong and the correction belongs here rather than in a
rewritten register row** (the register is append-only; `close_defect.py` rewrites one
line's bytes and nothing else).

`createPremisesOwner` is indeed called by no screen — that is the CR's own measured
claim and it holds. **But `POST /premises/{id}/match-owner` CAN create an owner
record**, from a free-text name, through `OwnerMatchingPanel` on the premises list.
So the cupboard has a door: type a name in `Managed by`, save, go to the list, find
the matching panel, choose a category, create. **Five steps, on a different screen,
and it still opens no master account** — which is why the PO experienced it as no door
at all. The distinction matters for a second reason: **Owner matching stays**, because
`BR-MET-151` matches the import's free text against it, and this lane did not touch it.

### 3 · WHAT THE BLUEPRINT ALREADY SAID, AND IT AGREED WITH THE RULING

`05-prototype/Premises & Units Blueprint 2.pdf` was read as **images** (B14 rule 42),
pages 9-11 and 36-41, via `10-scripts/pdf/pdf_render.py`. The drawn `WHO LOOKS AFTER
IT?` group on BOTH forms is:

> `Owner` · a search box · a confirmation card carrying the name, the account number
> and a `Change` control · then `Managed by`, helper `Only if different.`

**The drawing already labels the row `Owner` and already calls the second box `Managed
by`.** It draws a SEARCH, which is the shape the product already had; what was wrong
was only what it searched. So the drawing and the PO's ruling of 2026-09-22 agreed
with each other and not with the product — the screens were built to neither.

**Three divergences from the drawing are STATED, not absorbed** (B14 rule 41):

* the drawn line 1 is `Creekside Holdings LP · Landlord` — that category is the OWNER
  RECORD's, and there is no owner record under the ruling. Line 1 is the account's
  name alone.
* the drawn line 2 says `master account A-10442`. **Two of those words are retired by
  a later ruling** — *"we ahve to use one volcabory"* — so the number stays and the
  words go. A drawing dated 2026-09-10 does not outrank a ruling dated 2026-09-22.
* `Already owns 3 properties` is drawn and **is not on the wire yet**. Rendering zero
  would say the opposite of what it means, so the line draws only when a count
  arrives; `MasterAccountSearch.dom.test.tsx` proves that branch today, so the day
  C1's `premises_ids_owned_by_account` reaches the wire it appears with no further
  change. That is hard-won law 2's *write the test that fires when the hold expires*.

### 4 · THE VOCABULARY — FIVE WORDINGS, COUNTED OUT TO ONE NOUN

| wording | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `Owner` | the list column, the review, the property fact | **KEPT — the one word** |
| `Owner (record)` | the control on both forms | **retired**, 0 consumers |
| `Owner / manager` | the edit form's free-text box | **`Managed by`** — the drawing's own word, and the review step ALREADY used it |
| `master account {{n}}` | under the chosen owner | **retired** — the number alone |
| `Needs an owner` | the list chip, the filter, the property page | **KEPT, deliberately** |

⚠ **`Managed by` COST NOTHING TO ADOPT:** `metering.premises.field.managedBy` already
existed in all eleven catalogues, because the review step had been using it since
`CR-089`. **The edit form was the last screen in the product still saying *Owner /
manager*.**

⚠ **`Needs an owner` IS KEPT AND THE REASONING IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT LOOKS LIKE A
MISS.** It is the surviving noun naming its own absence, not a fifth name for the
thing — a clerk meets exactly one noun, `Owner`, and its negative. The blueprint names
that list twice (`CR-089-p036`: *"Clearing it is allowed and puts the property on the
Needs an owner list"*), and `needs_owner` is also the LIST FILTER's server-side value
(`PremisesListPage.tsx`, `f.owner=needs_owner`). Retiring the phrase would have
renamed a filter the drawing specifies. **Grepped for consumers before deciding** —
which is `DEF-CUS-3653`'s lesson, and it changed the answer.

### 5 · `Kind` LEFT THE PROPERTY PAGE'S FACT LIST, AND A RULING IS WHY

The owner block rendered `Account · Kind · Billed to · Outstanding`. Under `OQ-790`
option (c) — MASTER IMMEDIATELY — plus `CR-056`'s *every address gets its owner a
Master Account*, `kind` is **`master` on every account this block can ever show**. A
fact row whose value cannot vary is furniture. Removed, not hidden, and recorded here
because it is a ruling's consequence rather than a tidy-up.

### 6 · WHAT THIS LANE DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO

* **The property page's fact grid was not re-cut to the drawn two lines.** That grid is
  PO 2026-08-27's *"you ahve to showall details form account"*, and re-laying it out in
  the same commit that changes what it READS would bury the change nobody could then
  review. It is `CR-089-p019`'s own conformance work.
* **`OwnerMatchingPanel` was not touched.** It is the import's matching surface and
  `premises_owners` keeps doing real work there.
* **No owner-record screen was built.** `createPremisesOwner` stays uncalled, which the
  ruling above records as a deliberate absence the PO agreed to.

### 7 · FOUR CONTROLS RETIRED, AND ONE OF THEM WAS DOING A REAL JOB

`useOwnerNameCheck` · `OwnerNameCheck` · `OwnerAccountLink` · `OwnerOwnsLine` are gone
from `OwnerAccount.tsx`. Three were plumbing. **The fourth was `BR-MET-401`'s check** —
PO 2026-08-27, *"it can be existing master account also so at the time of premises
creation we should check"* — which resolved the typed free-text name against owner
records and offered to pick one. Under the ruling no screen may search those, so its
offer could only ever name a row nothing fills; on the day it was measured it rendered
*"No party by that name yet. The address saves and appears on Owner matching."* — **a
second dead instruction on the same screen as the first.**

**The PO's check is not lost, it moved up one control.** `Owner` is now a live search
over the tenant's master accounts, so a clerk adding a landlord's twelfth address
finds the account the first eleven used, by name or by number, at the moment of
creating. That is what *"it can be existing master account also"* asked for and what
the empty picker could never deliver.

### 8 · A TEST NAMED FOR THE DRAWING WAS ASSERTING THE DIVERGENCE

`AddPremisesWizard.test.tsx`'s *"every field, in the drawn order"* expected
`"Owner (record)"`. **The blueprint never drew that**, on either form. The test passed
for as long as the divergence lived, because it had been written from the screen rather
than from the drawing. Corrected to `"Owner"`.

A second stale premise went with it: that list's comment justified `Account type`
breaking a drawn adjacency on the ground that *"`OwnerNameCheck` already renders between
the picker and `Managed by`, so the drawn adjacency was not intact to break."* That
control is now retired, **so the adjacency IS intact and `Account type` is the only
thing breaking it.** Stated rather than left resting on a premise that stopped being
true.

### 9 · A FALSE PASS THIS LANE PAID FOR, KEPT AS A TEST

The first draft of `cr130_c2_premises_owner_walkthrough.mjs` asked `/created/.test(…)`
of the verdict and **reported the broken screen as FIXED** — because
`owner_account_not_created` contains the word `created`. CLAUDE.md hard-won law 7,
habit 2: *ask what would make this check pass wrongly.* Every comparison in
`premisesOwnerContract.ts` is now against a WHOLE constant, and
`premisesOwnerContract.test.ts` carries the case; reintroducing the substring match
turns it red, which was proved before it was trusted.

### 10 · MEASURED, AND WHAT AWAITS C1

The walk runs in two modes and **both were run against the same live stack**. `before`
was 11/11 against the pinned tip and now fails on four rows — which is the proof it was
measuring the real thing. `after` is **26 PASS · 3 PENDING · 0 FAIL**.

The three PENDING rows are C1's half and are reported as PENDING rather than FAIL, so a
sibling's unlanded work does not acquire the colouring of a real red:

* `POST /premises` refuses `master_account_id` — `metering.unknown_field`, field
  `master_account_id`. **That is the door working, and it proves the screen sends the
  agreed key.**
* no master account is opened yet.
* the verdicts carry no `message_key` yet, so `verdictSentences` renders none. C1 owns
  the eight wordings and their eleven catalogue rows; this lane renders
  `t(warning.message_key)` and writes no sentence of its own.

**Pre-existing reds, DATED rather than asserted** (CLAUDE.md hard-won law 7, habit 1):
the same four files were run at the pinned tip in a separate worktree and **2 of the 7
failures were already there** — `UnitsPage.test.tsx` (`03/12/2024`, last moved
2026-09-18 by the `DEF-MET-5743` lane) and `PremisesServices.dom.test.tsx`
(`services_available` assertion, 2026-09-11). The other 5 were this lane's and are
fixed.

### 11 · THE ID THIS LANE ALLOCATED WAS GONE BY PUSH TIME, AND THE LAW CAUGHT IT

Filed as `DEF-MET-6140` when the reproduction finished. By push time **`DEF-LED-6140`
held that number** — the chart-of-accounts lane took it while this one was building.
The ids are one running number across the whole register, so two module prefixes on
one number is a collision, and *"a duplicate id in a 957-row register reads as a
register, not as an error"*.

**Nothing downstream would have caught it.** It was found by doing what CLAUDE.md law
11 prescribes and nothing else: re-deriving **both the file content and the ids** from
the pinned tip at push time, unconditionally, rather than only when git reports a
conflict. `allocate.py defect` asks the REMOTE — it read 3,734 numbers across six refs
including four this checkout had never seen — and answered `6155`. Re-filed as
**`DEF-MET-6155`** and renumbered across eleven files in the same act.

⚠ **AND SIXTEEN OF THIS LANE'S PATHS HAD MOVED UNDER IT** — all eleven catalogues, the
three version files, the decision log and the register — because lanes A, B and C1 all
landed while this one was in a browser. Pushing the blobs read at the start would have
reverted every one of them by subtraction, with a correct file count, correct hunks and
a clean `git status`. The catalogues were re-fanned onto the tip's bytes, the version
re-verified free (`2.325.1`, after B took `2.325.0`), and the entry above appended to
the tip's file rather than to the copy this lane had been holding.

## 2026-09-22 — `CR-131-BRC07` STEPS 2–7 ARE BUILT: THE ROUTE REPORTS WHAT IT COLLECTED, AND STORES SIX BUILDINGS INSTEAD OF 726 UNITS

**Lane R2, following the three answers recorded above.** Version **2.326.0**.

### WHAT RT-009 NOW SAYS, WHICH IS THE HEADLINE

**A route reports the readings COLLECTED on it.** Move a route's properties to another route
and its reads list, its progress count and its last-read date do not move with them — they stay
with the route whose reader took them, and the receiving route reports only its own. Before this,
a hundred readings left RT-009 and arrived at RT-001 the instant the premises moved, and the
product printed *"changes take effect next read window"* on the screen while doing it.

**The route COLUMN on the readings list moved with the filter**, which is `DEF-045`'s own
requirement rather than a new one: its test is named *"the route filter and the route column
agree"*, and leaving the column on the service point would have had a clerk narrow to `RT-009`
and read `RT-001` in the rows that came back.

⚠ **THE ROUTE SHEET IS DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED, AND THIS IS A JUDGMENT WITH ITS REASONING RATHER
THAN AN OMISSION.** The gate's measurement listed four surfaces that resolve a route through the
live membership, and the sheet is one of them. **It stays live because it is the walk a reader is
about to make.** Asked of the collection stamp, a meter fitted last week — which has no readings
at all — would never print, and a meter that moved to another route last month would send
somebody to the wrong door. `CR-131-BRC07` §5 items 3 and 4 (*"add a unit … it is on the route"*,
*"fit a meter. It is on the route"*) are **unsatisfiable under a stamped sheet**. The sheet's fix
is derivation, which is step 3, and it is fixed there.

### THE COST OF THE STAMP, STATED WHERE A TENANT WILL MEET IT

A reading collected before `metering/0012` carries no stamp, so it belongs to no route: it is
absent from the route filter and its Route cell is blank. **0 of 516 readings on the seeded
fixture; not zero on a utility that predates the column.** It is in the release note for 2.326.0
in plain words, in `BR-MET-081`, and — the part that matters — **asserted by a test**, so a later
lane cannot quietly "repair" it by falling back to the live join, which is the defect.

### STEPS 3–7, AND THE NUMBERS ARE MEASURED ON A REAL 726-UNIT PROPERTY

A property carrying **726 units and 725 meters** was seeded, because `CR-131-BRC07` §5 says in as
many words that *a fix proved on six units proves nothing here* — the whole defect is arithmetic
on the unit count.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| step 3's URL | **32,781 characters** (one `unit_id` per unit) against a 4–8 KB limit | **113 characters** — `premises_id` and nothing else |
| step 3's cost | 5.1 queries per unit → 3,711 round trips | **6 queries**, 0.1 s |
| step 4's save | **4,420 queries, 10.4 seconds** | **68 queries, 0.5 seconds** |
| what a route stores | 726 rows | **1 row** |
| a unit added afterwards | never reaches the route | **on it immediately** — 728 → 729 members, no wizard |

**Proved in a real browser on the deployed join** (`10-scripts/cr131_route_wizard_walkthrough.mjs`,
16 checks, all passing): step 3 draws *"1 Premises · 728 Units · 725 of 725 Meters"* instead of
*"No meters yet"*; the review states `BR-MET-074`'s move — *"1 premises move from TWRB977B · No
bills change. Only the reader."* — before the press; the save lands and reports 725 meters on 1
premises.

### THE FORWARD HAZARD THE GATE PROVED IS CLOSED, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN SILENT

`services.collection_route_id` resolved a route ONLY through `service_points.route_id`. The gate
showed that emptying that column makes it return `None`, that `meter_reads.route_id` is nullable,
and that **nothing goes red** — the read history would simply have stopped being recorded from the
day derivation shipped. It now has a **third hop that asks the derivation**, which needs no stored
projection at all. Proved red through the real path first: with the hop switched off the test
fails with *"a read collected now would be stamped route_id=None"*.

### THREE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE, WITH THEIR REASONING — NONE WAS PUT TO THE PO

1. **A `unit_id` in a save payload is PROMOTED to its building, not refused.** The derivation has
   treated a unit pick as a building pick since `CR-029` RC-W4 (`BR-MET-082` clause 2), so every
   ANSWER the product gave was already premises-grained; only the stored rows pretended otherwise.
   Refusing would break callers over a distinction the product does not make.
2. **`route_memberships` is still written alongside the new table.** A table is retired after its
   readers move, never in the change that supersedes it — the discipline `RoutePremisesOrder`
   already records about the column it replaced. Step 8 owns the retirement.
3. **The `basis` a unit reports changes from `"premises"` to `"picked"` for a building's siblings.**
   It is the truer word — a human picked the building — and it is called out because
   `move_preview` publishes `basis` in its payload. No screen renders it; checked, not assumed.

### AND A MIGRATION BACKFILL THAT WROTE ZERO ROWS AND SAID SO

⚠ **A MIGRATION DOES NOT RUN WITH RLS OFF, AND THE FIRST DRAFT'S COMMENT SAID IT DID.**
`route_memberships` carries `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and the migration role is neither superuser
nor `BYPASSRLS`, so with `app.tenant_id` unset the policy resolves to `tenant_id = NULL`, every
read matches nothing, and **the migration completes successfully having seen no data.** Nothing
would have gone red; the table would simply have been empty and every route would have lost its
membership the moment the readers moved onto it.

**The only reason it was caught is the print at the bottom of the backfill** — `0 unit rows -> 0
premises rows` on a fixture known to hold nine memberships is a sentence somebody can be wrong
about out loud, and *"Applying … OK"* is not. That is hard-won law 7's third habit doing the work
it was written for. It is tenant-scoped explicitly now, and it prints the tenant count beside the
row counts, because **a zero with no scope attached is indistinguishable from an empty one.**
