## 2026-09-22 — THE RECEIPT, BUILT: WHAT EACH LEVEL IS MADE OF, AND THE RESIDUE MEASURED AT ZERO (`CR-132-BRC07`)

The ruling of this morning said a separate endpoint and shared components beneath it. **This
records the judgments the build had to make that no ruling covered**, because each one would
otherwise have to be re-derived from the code by whoever meets it next.

### 1 · THE GL DISTRIBUTIONS ARE OUR JOURNAL ENTRY'S CREDIT LEGS — arithmetic, not a judgment

`payments/ledger_seam.post_payment_cleared` writes **exactly one debit** — the tender's clearing
account, or undeposited funds — and **one to three credits**: accounts receivable for what went
against bills, customer credit for what was carried, deposit liability for what is held. The debit
IS the payment amount, so by hard rule 5 the credits sum to it too.

**So the distributions are the credits, and their balancing rule is satisfied by our own.**

Their `ReceiptPaymentLevel` already carries the cash side, and their `GLAccountNumber` is
documented as derivable from the payment-code mapping — **the cash leg is the one thing they do not
need from us.** Emitting both sides would double the total and fail their own rule by construction,
which is what makes this arithmetic rather than a choice.

⚠ **AND IT IS WHY A GL RULE STILL CHANGES IN ONE PLACE.** The account code comes from
`seams/ledger.account_code` — the same resolution `/partner/v1/ledger` puts Aclarian's rows through,
promoted from a private name to a public one for this and nothing else. **Nothing in the receipt
projection reads the chart of accounts**, and a test asserts that by reading the module's code with
its comments and docstrings stripped.

### 2 · ONE PAYMENT IS ONE RECEIPT WITH ONE TRANSACTION, and a bill number that is often blank

Their model allows several transactions per receipt. Our payment is one row with one tender and one
purpose, so a second transaction would mean **inventing the split between them**.

`ReceiptTransactionARBillNumber` holds ONE bill number, and a payment may be allocated across
several. **It is left BLANK whenever it is not exactly one bill.** Naming the first of three would
tell a City's books that a $300 receipt paid one $100 bill; splitting the receipt into three
transactions would mean splitting the GL credit across them, which is an allocation rule nobody has
agreed — the same thing `seams/ledger.as_record` already refuses to invent when it meets three
debits against four credits. **A blank field is a partner looking the payment up by customer
number; a wrong one is a partner reconciling against a bill that was never paid.**

### 3 · `ReceiptNumber` IS SENT BLANK, AND OUR NUMBER TRAVELS IN `ReceiptDescription`

Their field is **13 characters and optional — they assign one if it is blank.** Ours is
`PMT-2609-0187`, which is **15**. It does not fit, and truncating it would hand their books a
reference that matches no payment of ours and cannot be looked up from either side.

**A wrong 13-character number is worse than an absent one, because it looks like an answer.** So
the field goes blank, they assign, and our number goes in `ReceiptDescription` (256) where both
sides can find it.

### 4 · `ReceiptCashier` IS `SMARTBILLHUB`, SET EXPLICITLY

Their field defaults to the IMPORTING USER. Left alone, **every online receipt would look as though
a named person at the City had taken it at a counter** — which is precisely the fact this feed
exists to distinguish.

### 5 · `VoidedFlag` IS ALWAYS `false`, AND THE TWO RULES AGREE

Their platform forbids altering a voided receipt. Our hard rule 4 forbids updating an issued
payment; a bounced payment is a **new row with a negative amount**. **These say the same thing, so
there is ONE mechanism and not two** — we have never voided a receipt we sent, because we have no
way to alter one. A reversal becomes its own receipt.

### 6 · THE RESIDUE, MEASURED — AND THE ANSWER IS THAT IT CANNOT HAPPEN ON THIS PATH

The PO's ruling of this morning — *"please send receipt even if it is not balance"* — raised the
question of how often an imbalance is a **one-cent rounding residue** rather than a real error,
because the two have the same symptom and opposite fixes.

**Measured on the real path** — payments recorded through `record_payment`, posted by
`post_payment_cleared`, read back through the seams and projected —
`tests/test_cr132_newworld_endpoint.py`:

> **7 receipts · 7 balanced · 0 residue · 0 material · largest difference `0.00`.**

The spread was chosen to make it go wrong: thirds of a dollar (`33.33`, `66.67`), an odd cent
(`33.34`), **a one-penny bill**, and three overpayments — which are the only shape that produces
TWO credit legs and therefore the only shape in which a residue could arise at all.

⚠ **AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN LUCKY, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE FIGURE WORTH
ANYTHING.** `post_payment_cleared` refuses to post unless `applied_to_bills + credit_carried +
deposit_held` equals the payment **exactly**, and each of those three is already a two-decimal
figure: a payment amount is what somebody actually paid, and an invoice total is quantised once
when the bill is formed (B4 — *round only at finalisation*). **Rounding a set of two-decimal
numbers changes none of them**, so Σ round(leg) = round(Σ leg). A residue needs a sub-cent leg and
the posting path does not make one.

**So the remainder-assignment fix has nothing to fix today, and it is deliberately not built.** The
worked `33.33 × 3 = 99.99` case is real arithmetic and is kept as a unit case and in the recorded
fixture — it is what the code does IF a sub-cent leg ever arrives — but it does not arise from any
path this product has. The measurement is written to **report rather than assert a zero**, so the
day something produces one it prints the figure instead of going quietly green.

### 7 · WHAT WENT WRONG IN THE BUILD, AND IT IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF

**`DEF-INT-6162` — the balance tests proved a COPY of the emitter.** The test file carried its own
six-line helper that rebuilt the serialisation loop, so seventeen cases graded the test file and
**the path the endpoint calls had no coverage at all.** Every ordinary signal said otherwise: all
seventeen passed and the fixture matched byte for byte. It was found only by the red proof law 7
requires — **a refusal was inserted into `emit()`, reinstating the exact rule the PO reversed, and
every case stayed GREEN.** `newworld.render()` was split out so there is one implementation and the
helper calls it. **A test helper that reimplements its subject grades the copy, not the product.**

**`DEF-INT-6161` — the guard this lane was told to rely on cannot fire.**
`tests/test_be_default_authentication.py` asserts `unclassified == []` and then
`public == PUBLIC_ROUTES`. The first has been red since 2026-09-04 on portal routes, **so the
second has never run since.** Measured by running the sweep's own classification past the first
assertion: **58 unclassified, every one of them portal, and 25 public routes nobody has had to
declare** — 24 portal plus `api/{tenant}/integrations/page-policy`, whose `AllowAny` is itself
deliberate and argued but whose DECLARATION is missing. So the new address was verified by hand
instead: `api/partner/v1/receipts` is in the public surface and the declared set matches on the
partner half. **A breach sheltering behind an older breach is `DEF-INT-4256`'s own phrase; what was
not recorded is that it makes a second assertion unreachable.**

## 2026-09-22 — THE TIER LADDER: THREE REPORTED FAULTS, TWO CAUSES, AND ONE OF THEM WAS A PROP (`DEF-RAT-6164`, maintenance)

**The Product Owner, on the deployed build `v2.325.1`, in two messages:**

> *"version Deployed for tiered rate align all input field in one row and UI breaking at bottom"*

> *"'Leave blank on the last row for no upper limit.' This text is reapeted"*

**Screen: `RAT-03` step 3 — Plans & Rates → a rate schedule → Percent of another
service, on the Usage basis, with a tier ladder open.** The same ladder is drawn by
the `Tiered` structure and carried every fault there too.

**Track: MAINTENANCE, not Build** (`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`).
A user can do this task in the product today, so it is Maintenance by the one
question that file asks — and the beta default is DEFECT, not change.

### 1 · WHAT WAS MEASURED, BEFORE ANY CODE WAS READ

Reproduced in Chromium at 1440×900 against `server.mjs` — the deployed join, not a
dev server — on an isolated seeded clone. **Three tier blocks open, document
coordinates of the four controls in one row:**

| | `From` | `To` | `Rate` | `Remove tier` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| input top | 642 | **599** | 642 | 644 |

**A 45px spread across four controls the blueprint draws on one line**, with `To`
sitting **43px above** its neighbours. The mechanism is in the box heights: the `To`
field measured **103px** where `From` and `Rate` measured **60px**.

### 2 · TWO OF THE THREE FAULTS WERE ONE PROP

`help={t("rating.tier.toHelp")}` sat inside `tiers.map(...)`.

* `help` renders INSIDE the field's box, so that box was 43px taller.
* `.rating-tier-row` is a grid on `align-items: end`, which bottom-aligns the
  **boxes** — so a taller box carries its input upward, on **every** row.
* And because it was per-row, the sentence printed **once per block**: three blocks
  printed it three times, six printed it six. **It says *"on the LAST row"*, so it
  was false on five rows out of six** (B14 rule 32 clause 3).

**The PO reported those as two separate faults and they were one line of code.** That
is the finding worth keeping: a repeated sentence and a broken baseline look like two
problems and a `help` prop inside a `map` produces both.

### 3 · THE THIRD FAULT — *"UI breaking at bottom"*

`+ Add tier` measured **1088px wide**, the full width of its panel, against **69px**
for `Back` and **102px** for `Continue`. `Panel` is `display:flex;
flex-direction:column`, so a `Button` that is its DIRECT child becomes a flex item and
stretches across the cross axis. On screen it reads as an empty input, not a button,
and it is the last thing in the ladder — which is where the PO was looking. Wrapped in
a block div, the same button is `inline-flex` again and measures **111px**, which is
what blueprint p046 draws.

⚠ **AND A FALSE LEAD WORTH RECORDING, BECAUSE IT COST HALF AN HOUR AND WOULD COST THE
NEXT LANE THE SAME.** The first full-page screenshot showed the page slicing through
`+ Add tier` with everything below it blank, which reads exactly like a screen
breaking at the bottom. **It is an artefact of the capture, not the product.**
`.app-shell` is `height:100vh; overflow:hidden` and the real scroller is `main.view`,
while `document.documentElement.scrollHeight` still reports the content's height — so
Playwright's `fullPage: true` captures a tall image whose bottom is empty. **On this
app, scroll `main.view` and capture the VIEWPORT.** The walkthrough says so in its own
header.

### 4 · THE JUDGMENT — WHERE THE SENTENCE GOES, AND WHY NOT WHERE THE DRAWING PUTS IT

**Blueprint p046 draws the sentence once, INSIDE the last row, under that `To` box.**
It was built once **after** the last row instead, and pointed at from the last row's
`To` through a new opt-in `describedBy` on the kit's `TextField`.

Two reasons, and the first is the ruling:

1. **That placement is the thing that makes the box taller.** Following it literally
   reproduces the misalignment on the last row — which is the fault the PO reported.
   B14 rule 38 hands FORM CONSTRUCTION to the UI rules where a drawing disagrees, and
   *help under an input* is named in `CLAUDE.md` as construction. **The PO's own
   instruction to align the row is the ruling here; the drawing is not being
   overruled on what to say or where it belongs, only on how it is built.**
2. **At 390 the row's `auto-fit` grid collapses to one column**, so a sentence offset
   to the `To` column would start an implicit column and scroll the page sideways.

**Checked at one block as well as six**, because one is the commonest case: the
`Tiered` structure draws one row and the sentence reads correctly under it (the only
row IS the last row). The percent card's flat case passes an **empty** ladder and
draws its price above, so there is no `To` box and **no sentence is printed at all** —
which is right, and is asserted.

### 5 · THE WORDING — D3's FINDING FOR THE SECOND TIME

The drawing words it `Blank on the last row means no upper limit.` — **nine words in
one sentence**, where B14 rule 33 caps an INSTRUCTION at **six per sentence** and says
two sentences of six beat one of twelve. Built as:

> **Leave the last To blank. That block has no upper limit.**

Five words and six. **The drawing is right about WHAT to say and over the cap in
HOW** — which is exactly what this screen's conformance file already recorded for the
contiguity message (D3), and it is the second time on one screen.

⚠ **NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY READS THAT CAP FOR THIS STRING.** `G33` walks only the
REFUSAL key set (it shares `G32`'s), and `G129` walks only
`metering.premises*`/`metering.units*`. **The old ten-word sentence was on no
baseline and breached no gate** — so the brief's instruction to *"take the line off
`G33`'s baseline"* had nothing to take off, and the cap is now asserted in the
module's own test instead.

**All eleven catalogues moved together**, through `10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py` — the
tool that owns those files — never by hand. B14 rule 35: each is written in its own
language, and the ten non-English ones deliberately do **not** name the column by its
label, for the reason in §7.

### 6 · THE CHECK THAT SHOULD HAVE EXISTED

**This was already written down and nobody could count it.** Divergence **D4** in
`04-docs/05-modules/06-rating/conformance/CR-087-p045-create-step3-rates.md` recorded
the repeated sentence on the day that file was written, and the screen went on
printing it until a beta user saw it. A finding recorded only in prose is a finding
nothing re-checks.

Two checks now exist, and they split on what each CAN see:

* `07-frontend/src/features/rating/tierLadderOneSentence.dom.test.tsx` — 10 cases,
  **7 shown RED against the pre-fix source** before being trusted green. It counts the
  sentence (3 over 3 blocks, 6 over 6 — the PO's report as a number), proves no
  `tier-to-N-help` element exists, proves only the LAST row points at it, and asserts
  rule 33's cap on the string.
  ⚠ **Its `+ Add tier` case PASSED against the pre-fix code on the first draft** — it
  asserted `parentElement.tagName === "DIV"`, which is true either way because
  Testing Library mounts into a `<div>`. That is hard-won law 7's second habit (*ask
  what would make this check pass wrongly*) catching a check at birth. Rewritten to
  assert the wrapper holds the button ALONE; then red, then green.
* `10-scripts/def_rat_6164_tier_row_walkthrough.mjs` — the measurement, in a browser,
  `MODE=before`/`MODE=after`, at **1440 and 390**, on **1, 3 and 6** blocks, for
  **both** structures that draw a ladder. **jsdom has no layout — `getBoundingClientRect`
  is all zeroes — so a unit test claiming the row is aligned would be law 7's fourth
  shape, a check looking at the wrong thing.** The file says so in its own header.

**After: the spread is 1px** (`FROM 737 · TO 737 · RATE 737 · REMOVE 738` at six
blocks), the sentence appears **once** over six blocks, and `+ Add tier` is **111px in
a 1120px panel**.

### 7 · A SECOND THING FOUND IN PASSING, FILED AND NOT FIXED — `DEF-RAT-6163`

Reading all eleven catalogues for §5 turned up that **`rating.tier.to` is the EMAIL
sense of the word in four languages**: `받는 사람` in ko-KR means *recipient*, `Untuk`
in id-ID means *for*, `Para` in pt-BR is the recipient sense, and ja-JP has the
particle `に` where a numeric range wants `まで`. The other seven are correct range
words in their own language (de `Ab`/`Bis`, es `Desde`/`Hasta`, fr `De`/`À`, hi
`से`/`तक`, it `Da`/`A`).

**Filed, not fixed** — the maintenance process says a second problem found on the way
past is filed, and the fix order decides when it is worked. It is also why the ten
non-English versions of the sentence above do not name the column by its label: doing
so would have spread a wrong label into a second string.

### 8 · SCOPE, AND WHAT DID NOT MOVE

Nothing about what is refused or what is billed. The percent card's arithmetic, its
two bases, the derived service list and every refusal are untouched — lanes A and B
shipped those today and they are proved. **`.rating-tier-row`'s stylesheet rule was
NOT edited**, deliberately: its selector is shared with `.rating-season-row` and
`.rating-window-row`, so changing it would have re-spaced the seasons and time-of-use
editors on this same screen. The fix needed no CSS at all — taking the help out of the
box made every cell the same height, and `align-items: end` then does the right thing
on its own. **No class was added to any stylesheet** (B14 rule 21), and
`RateScheduleWizard.tsx` and `FormModal.tsx` were both already on
`route-b-migrated.txt`, so the ledger did not move and `routeBUtilities.test.ts` —
the stricter of the two checkers — was run and is green (11/11).

### 9 · THE KIT GAINED ONE OPT-IN PROP

`TextField` now takes `describedBy?: string`, appended to the field's own help and
error ids and never replacing them. Absent, every existing call site renders
byte-for-byte what it rendered before. It is the same opt-in shape and the same
reasoning as `labelHidden` (`DEF-RAT-5734`, B14 rule 38: *where the kit lacks a piece
a screen needs, add it to the kit as an opt-in, so nothing existing moves*). It exists
so that detaching a sentence from a box did not detach it from the field — the last
row's `To` still announces it.

**Rollback: code only — revert the commit.** Nothing was migrated, no data was
repaired and nothing was sent.

### 10 · AND THE ID COLLIDED, CAUGHT BY THE ONE CHECK THAT CAN CATCH IT

Filed as `DEF-RAT-6161` when the reproduction finished. At push time
`allocate.py defect --verify 6161` answered **TAKEN** — the `CR-132-BRC07` New World
lane had pushed **`DEF-INT-6161`** while this one was in a browser, and `DEF-INT-6162`
with it. Renumbered to **`DEF-RAT-6164`** across the register row, the two source
files, the test, the walkthrough (and its filename), the conformance file and this
entry, in one act.

**`file_defect.py` was not wrong and neither was its arithmetic.** It reads the
working tree, `HEAD` and the `origin` refs — which is the PUSHED world plus this
checkout — and at the moment it ran, this checkout was at `34376e38c`, three commits
behind, where `6160` genuinely was the maximum. **What was wrong was WHICH WORLD the
maximum came from**, which is the exact mechanism `DEF-1787` records.

⚠ **AND THE HALF THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED SILENTLY:** the ids are one running number
across the whole register, so `DEF-INT-6161` and `DEF-RAT-6161` are a COLLISION even
though the strings differ — the same shape `CLAUDE.md` records for CR numbers, where
*"the STRING is unique and the NUMBER is not"*. Nothing downstream would have caught
it: **a duplicate id in a 3,658-row register reads as a register, not as an error.**
Two such pairs are on the branch right now (`DEF-CUS-5979` and `DEF-CUS-5980`, three
rows each), and they are at the tip rather than from this lane.

⚠ **THE VERSION HAD MOVED TOO.** This lane started against `2.326.0` and would have
bumped to `2.326.1`; `allocate.py version --bump fix` read the REMOTE and answered
**`2.327.1`**, because `CR-132-BRC07` had shipped `2.327.0` in between. Both answers
came from the same command run at the same moment as the blob re-derivation, which is
the only moment either can be final.

**Sixteen further paths had moved under this lane** — all eleven catalogues, the three
version files, the decision log and the register — because siblings landed while it was
measuring. Every one was rebuilt from the pinned tip rather than written back from the
copy this lane had been holding, and each register append proved its PREFIX
byte-identical to the tip's file before it was kept. `10-scripts/sync_stale_tree.py`
moved the other 21 stale files and correctly LEFT all 26 of this lane's own.

## 2026-09-22 — THE NEW REQUEST REVIEW TABLE IS THREE COLUMNS, AND THE THREE I PROPOSED ARE REFUSED

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"dont add these"*, quoting back the whole table of three
columns this lane had proposed for the step 6 review — **Size / meter size**,
**Charge**, and **Waiting on / status** — together with the reasoning offered for
each.

**So the review table on step 6 of the New request wizard is exactly what the PO
asked for on 2026-09-21 and nothing more:**

| Column | |
|---|---|
| Service | the utility service requested |
| Requested start | the date the applicant asked for |
| Connection date | the date we will connect |

One row per utility service requested. **Three columns. No fourth.**

⚠ **THE RULING IS A REFUSAL OF ADDITIONS, NOT A REFUSAL OF THOSE THREE FACTS.** The
meter size, the charge and a per-service block are all real and may already appear
elsewhere on the wizard or on the request's own screen; what is ruled is that they do
NOT go in this table. A later lane reading *"size is refused"* and removing it from
step 4 would be reading this row backwards.

**WHY IT WENT THIS WAY, RECORDED BECAUSE THE LANE WAS WRONG AND THE REASONING IS THE
USEFUL PART.** The argument offered for each column was a good one on its own terms —
the size is what prices the service, an empty money column is worse than none, a
blocked service should say so. **Each was an argument for that column in isolation and
none of them was an argument against the screen getting longer**, which is the thing
the PO has been telling us about all month. B14 rule 32 gives a screen a DESCRIPTION
BUDGET and the PO ruled it on 2026-08-30 after saying *"too much content - desctiption
is too much for clark to read"* four times in twenty minutes; the same lane quoted that
history back in its own proposal and then proposed three columns anyway. **A budget
that is cited and not applied is not a budget.**

⚠ **AND THE ASK ITSELF CARRIED THE LICENCE, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS EASY TO GET WRONG.**
The PO's 2026-09-21 message ended *"if you awant to add anything else in it tell me"* —
an invitation to propose, answered here with a refusal. **An invitation to propose is
not a prediction that the proposal will be taken**, and a lane treating a polite
opening as a mandate produces exactly this: three extra columns nobody asked for,
argued for at length, on a screen already too full.

**Nothing is superseded.** No signed rule named these columns; the proposal was a
lane's and it is withdrawn. B14 rule 43 still governs HOW the table is built — the
shared table component, never markup inside the page.

**Consequence for the lane building it (Requests wizard batch):** build the three
columns and stop. Do not leave a placeholder column, a hidden column or a commented-out
one — a column that exists and is empty is the thing this ruling is against, and a
commented-out column is a promise nobody is keeping (hard-won law 1).

---

## 2026-09-22 — A REQUEST TAKES THE ADDRESS IN PARTS SO IT CAN FIND THE PREMISES; THE PREMISES IS STILL THE ONE ADDRESS

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"correct address will be on presmies but first time you will ahve to take the details to match it"*.

**Said in answer to this lane refusing to capture the parts at all.** The lane had
written, in a list put to the PO: *"I am not adding city, state and ZIP as new columns
on the request. An address lives on the property and nowhere else — that is your own
ruling from 4 September."* **The rule was quoted correctly and applied to the wrong
act.** `BR-MET-1161` governs where an address is STORED as the truth. It says nothing
about what a clerk may TYPE, and a request that cannot take a city and a ZIP cannot
find the premises it is about — which is the one thing step 3 exists to do.

**WHAT IS RULED**

| | |
|---|---|
| The New request wizard captures | Address line · Unit, flat or suite · City · State · ZIP |
| What those parts are FOR | Matching the application to a premises (and to a unit) |
| Where the address of record lives | `premises`, unchanged, exactly as `BR-MET-1161` says |
| What the request keeps | **what the applicant said** — the same posture `address_as_given` has carried since it was written, and the same posture as `interruptions.location_text` |

**SO `BR-MET-1161` IS NOT NARROWED AND NOTHING IS SUPERSEDED.** Its three exceptions
stand as they are and no fourth is created. A request is not a home for an address: it
is a record of a statement made by a member of the public, which is why the column has
always been called `as_given`. The distinction is the same one the rule already draws
for `interruptions.location_text` — *"what a stranger typed — a report, not a record"*.

⚠ **AND THE PARTS MUST GO ON READING AS A STATEMENT, NOT AS AN ADDRESS.** Whatever
their storage shape, every one of them is *as given*: nothing downstream may read them
as the service address, no screen may present them as the property's address once a
premises is matched, and once `premises_id` is set **the premises is what every screen
shows**. `G85` fails a fourth home and must go on being able to — so if these land as
columns they are named so that they cannot be mistaken for the real thing, and the
matched premises is what the review step and the detail screen display.

**THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS WRITTEN OUT RATHER THAN FILED AS A LINE.**
A hard rule about STORAGE was read as a rule about CAPTURE, by a lane that had the rule
in front of it and quoted it accurately. **A rule stating where a fact is kept says
nothing about who may say it**, and the two are easy to conflate precisely when the
rule is being obeyed carefully. The cost here was one refusal the PO had to overturn;
the same conflation applied to a meter reading or a payment reference would refuse a
clerk the ability to type what a customer told them.

## 2026-09-22 — THE "RECORD WHAT WAS HANDED OVER" MODAL MUST OFFER WAIVE, AND ITS OWN HELP TEXT SAID IT MUST NOT

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"on modal you ahve to give Waive off button"*, then *"button
or options"*. Said with `REQ-02`'s fee modal open on `SR-26-0011`.

**WHAT THE MODAL DOES TODAY.** *Record what was handed over* asks three required
fields — **Amount taken**, **How it was paid**, **Receipt number** — and ends with this
paragraph:

> *"Take whatever they hand over. If it is less than the quote, the difference stays as
> an open balance on this request and finance reconciles it — you do not refuse them
> and you do not write it off here."*

**SO THE RULING REVERSES A SENTENCE THE PRODUCT ALREADY SHOWS A CLERK**, which is why
it is written out rather than filed as a line: *"you do not write it off here"* is a
statement of policy on screen, and the PO has now said the opposite. The supersession
is stated, never assumed.

**WHAT IS RULED:** the fee modal offers a waive. Nothing else about the modal's money
handling moves — a short payment is still an open balance and is still not a write-off,
because **a waiver and a shortfall are different acts** and conflating them is what the
old sentence was guarding against. What changes is that the clerk can now perform the
first one from here.

**HOW IT IS BUILT — a lane judgment, recorded because the PO offered the choice
(*"button or options"*) and a judgment call is ours to make and write down.** Two
options at the head of the modal, not a third footer button:

| Option | What the modal then asks |
|---|---|
| **Taken** (default) | Amount taken · How it was paid · Receipt number — exactly as today |
| **Waived** | **Reason** (required). The three money fields are not shown |

**The reasoning, in one sentence: a waive has no amount, no tender and no receipt, so a
footer button would leave three required money fields on screen that a waive must never
fill** — and a modal whose title says *what was handed over* cannot be submitted by
somebody stating that nothing was. The title moves with the choice.

⚠ **IT IS REUSE, NOT NEW CODE, AND THE BACKEND IS ALREADY THERE.**
`waive_fee_line(actor, fee_id, *, reason)` exists in
`apps/customers/service_request_service.py` and `waiveServiceRequestFee(id, feeId,
reason)` is already imported by `ServiceRequestDetailPage.tsx` — there is a per-line
waive today, **buried inside the fee disclosure behind `Expand`**, which is why the PO
could not find it. B14 rule 43: lift the existing control, do not write a second one.
⚠ And `DEF-CUS-6096` is the lesson attached to it: the waive is addressed by the fee
row's **uuid**, never by `line_no` — sending `"1"` was a 500 the screen swallowed on
every press until 2026-09-21.

⚠ **AND THE PARAGRAPH THAT CARRIED THE OLD POLICY BREACHES B14 RULE 33 THREE TIMES
OVER, SO IT DOES NOT SURVIVE THE EDIT UNCHANGED.** It is three sentences where the cap
is two; its sentences run to 21, 19 and 14 words where an instruction caps at six per
sentence; and *"finance reconciles it"* is RATIONALE, which rule 33 puts at **zero
words on screen**. The replacement states the act and stops.

## 2026-09-22 — TWO PO ANSWERS: THE APPROVE MODAL LOSES THREE OUTCOMES, AND AN IDENTIFIER ON A LIST IS MASKED

Both were put to the PO as questions with a worked example and lettered options, in
plain English with no ids — the standing instruction, and HUMAN-GUIDE §6's shape.

### 1 · THE APPROVE MODAL OFFERS TWO OUTCOMES, NOT FIVE — `BR-CUS-091` SUPERSEDED IN PART

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"Option (b) — remove all three permanently"*, answering a
table that set out (a) *hide an outcome that cannot apply to this request* against
(b) *remove move-out, transfer and disconnect from the modal for good*.

**So REQ-02's *What kind* list is: A new connection · A move-in.** Move-out, transfer
and disconnect are gone from it, on every request, not merely greyed.

⚠ **WHAT THIS REVERSES, QUOTED, BECAUSE A SUPERSESSION IS STATED AND NEVER ASSUMED.**
`BR-CUS-091` is CONFIRMED and was ruled by this same PO on **2026-08-24**, verbatim
*"Yes customer can request it"*. It says a customer MAY request a disconnect, that the
service request is therefore the front door for collections-initiated as well as
customer-initiated work, and — about **this exact control** — that the panel's old
reason for disabling Disconnect *"is withdrawn and the control is enabled."* That
sentence is now itself withdrawn.

**THE COST WAS PUT TO THE PO BEFORE THEY ANSWERED, WITH A WORKED CASE**, so the
signature covers it: shown two requests side by side — John Doe at 77 Foundry Row
Unit 1 (empty unit, no live account, three outcomes already greyed) and Ridge Coffee
Co. at 500 Main St (live account, 90 days in arrears, collections wanting it cut) —
and told that under (b) **collections can no longer start a disconnect from a request
and a clerk can no longer close an account as a move-out from here**, and that we did
not yet know whether another door exists for either. They chose (b) anyway.

⚠ **SO THE OPEN OBLIGATION IS OURS, NOT THEIRS: FIND OR BUILD THE OTHER DOOR.**
`BR-CUS-091` also records — and this half is NOT reversed — that a move-out and a
disconnect are **different outcomes**: a move-out closes the account and settles the
deposit (`BR-CUS-030`), a disconnect leaves it open and accruing (`BR-MET-105`'s base
charge keeps running), and *"the capture form must not quietly convert one into the
other."* Removing the place where that choice was made does not remove the need to
make it. The lane building this must NAME where each of the three now starts, in this
log, and **where no door exists it says so out loud rather than shipping over the
hole.** A screen that quietly loses a capability is the shape hard-won law 2 is about.

### 2 · AN IDENTIFIER ON A LIST SHOWS ITS LAST FOUR DIGITS

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"Yes, last four only"*.

**The worked case shown:** a driving licence offered as proof of identity, where the
Documents tab's `WHAT IT PROVES` cell on `SR-26-0011` was printing **`865554556`** —
a licence number in plain text on a list screen, because the form asks *what does this
document prove* and gives the clerk nowhere else to put a number.

**So:** wherever a document identifier reaches a list or a table cell, it is masked to
its last four — `••••4556` — which is `BR-CUS-092`'s posture everywhere else in the
product, now applied here.

**AND THE FIELD QUESTION IS A LANE JUDGMENT, TAKEN RATHER THAN RE-ASKED (law 13).**
Three options were offered: (a) add a separate *Document number* field and keep *What
it proves* for words, (b) rename the question to *Document number*, (c) drop the
column. The PO answered the masking question and not the lettered one. **(a) is taken**
— masking the number presupposes the number is CAPTURED and KEPT, which rules out (c);
and (b) would throw away the fact of what the document is for, which is the one thing
the column was minted to carry. (a) is also the only reading under which both facts
survive: *What it proves* = **Identity**, *Document number* = **`••••4556`**. If this
reading is wrong the cost is one field, and the PO can say so; re-asking them a
question they have already half-answered is the bug law 13 exists to prevent.

## 2026-09-22 — WHERE A MOVE-OUT, A TRANSFER AND A DISCONNECT START, NOW THAT THE APPROVE MODAL NO LONGER OFFERS THEM

**This is the second half of the ruling recorded above as *TWO PO ANSWERS*.** That
entry carries the PO's words — *"Option (b) — remove all three permanently"* — and
ends with an obligation on us rather than on them:

> ⚠ **SO THE OPEN OBLIGATION IS OURS, NOT THEIRS: FIND OR BUILD THE OTHER DOOR.**
> … The lane building this must NAME where each of the three now starts, in this
> log, and **where no door exists it says so out loud rather than shipping over the
> hole.**

**This entry is that naming, and it is written from a walk of the running product
rather than from a grep.** Nothing below is an inference from a route constant: each
door was opened in Chromium on `brazosbend`, at the build this ruling ships in.

### WHAT WAS REMOVED, EXACTLY

`REQ-02`'s **Approve** dialog asks *What kind* and offered five radios. It now offers
**two** — `A new connection` and `A move-in` — and the other three are not greyed,
not hidden behind a condition and not commented out. They are not there.

### WHERE EACH OF THE THREE STARTS INSTEAD

| | Where it starts | What carries a clerk to it |
|---|---|---|
| **A transfer** | `/{tenant}/transfers/new` — `TransferWizard`, screen `TRF-02` | Accounts → **Transfers** tab. `+ New transfer` is that tab's one primary action (`AccountsListPage.tabPrimary`), and the tab's empty state carries the same act. |
| **A disconnect** | `/{tenant}/disconnects/new` — `DisconnectWizard`, screen `DSC-02` | Accounts → **Disconnects** tab, same shape: `+ New disconnect` as the tab's primary, and on the empty state. The wizard also takes an account in its query string, which is how the account's own rail reaches it. |
| **A move-out** | `/{tenant}/accounts/{id}/move-out` — `MoveOutWizard`, screen `S20` | **The account's own page.** There is also a standalone `/{tenant}/move-outs/new` mounted, which the Move-outs tab's empty state uses. |

**SO ALL THREE HAVE A DOOR AND NONE OF THEM IS ORPHANED.** That is the answer to the
question the ruling left open, and it is the reason the removal costs no capability.

⚠ **ONE DOOR IS NOT LIKE THE OTHER TWO AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WORTH WRITING DOWN.**
A transfer and a disconnect can be started from the Accounts page's header, with no
row chosen, because their wizards ask which account they are about. **A move-out
cannot**, and this is recorded rather than filed as a gap: the move-out endpoints are
**account-scoped**, so a header button with nothing selected would have to guess which
account a clerk meant. `AccountsListPage`'s own note has said so since 2026-08-11 —
*"both endpoints act on ONE account and this header has no row selected, so a live
button would have to guess which one you meant"* — and it renders the control disabled
with that reason rather than hiding it (`BR-SHL-025`). **The live control is on the
account.**

### WHAT HAPPENS TO THE CHOICE `BR-CUS-091` PROTECTS

`BR-CUS-091` records — and this half is **NOT** reversed — that a move-out and a
disconnect are **different outcomes**: a move-out CLOSES the account and settles the
deposit (`BR-CUS-030`), a disconnect leaves it OPEN AND ACCRUING (`BR-MET-105`'s base
charge keeps running), and *"the capture form must not quietly convert one into the
other; where an applicant describes ending service, the clerk picks the outcome."*

**THE CHOICE SURVIVES AND IT MOVES EARLIER.** It used to be made at APPROVAL, on a
request already in the queue, by whoever reviewed it. It is now made at the DOOR, by
whoever starts the work: a clerk who opens `/disconnects/new` has chosen a disconnect,
and a clerk who opens the account's `Move-out` has chosen a move-out. **Nothing
converts one into the other**, because there is no longer any screen on which both are
options and one can be picked by mistake.

⚠ **WHAT IS GENUINELY LOST, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE THE PO PAID FOR IT KNOWINGLY:**
a request that ARRIVES describing one of these three — a customer writing in to say
they are leaving — can no longer be turned into that piece of work by approving it.
The clerk reads the request, starts the right wizard at its own door, and the request
is closed against it by hand. **That is a real extra step and it is not a defect**;
it is the shape the PO chose, having been shown both requests and told what (b) costs.

### WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO

**The five-value vocabulary is untouched.** `SERVICE_REQUEST_OUTCOMES` still holds all
five, `decide_outcome` still accepts all five, every request already carrying one of
the three still renders its type, and the tenant's document checklist
(`ServiceRequestDocumentSettingsPage`, `BR-CUS-095`) still carries **a column per
request type**.

⚠ **THAT LAST ONE IS THE BLAST-RADIUS FINDING AND IT IS WHY A SECOND CONSTANT EXISTS.**
The obvious implementation — delete three entries from `SERVICE_REQUEST_OUTCOMES` —
would have silently deleted three columns of that settings grid, and a utility that
had ticked *proof of identity* against a move-out would have lost the tick with no
ruling behind it. The PO removed three options from **one modal**. So the modal reads
`APPROVE_OUTCOMES`, a constant of its own, and the shared list is not touched. This is
`CLAUDE.md` hard rule 8's own lesson in another module: *before retiring a value, grep
for its CONSUMERS, because an absence is invisible to every check this repo has.*

## 2026-09-22 — THE ADDRESS PARTS ARE BUILT, AND `BR-CUS-1055`'s REFUSAL IS WITHDRAWN

**This is the ruling recorded above as *A REQUEST TAKES THE ADDRESS IN PARTS SO IT
CAN FIND THE PREMISES* carried into code.** That entry says what was ruled; this
one says what it cost, what was NOT changed, and the two things a later lane will
otherwise get wrong.

### WHAT IS BUILT

`service_requests` gains three columns (`customers/0065`) — **`address_city_as_given`,
`address_state_as_given`, `address_postal_code_as_given`** — `CAPTURE_FIELDS` accepts
them, `location_and_services` serves them, and capture step 3 asks for them as typed
boxes **until a premises is picked**. The moment one is, those boxes disappear and the
register's own city, state and ZIP take their place, read-only — which is the ruling's
second half in as many words: *once `premises_id` is set, the premises is what every
screen shows*.

**Not required.** `Continue` asks for the street line and nothing else, exactly as it
did. A new connection at a field with nothing on record is the job this wizard exists
for, and an asterisk here would refuse a clerk who has a street and no town.

### WHAT WAS NOT CHANGED, AND WHY THE REVERSAL IS THIS NARROW

**`BR-MET-1161` is not narrowed. No fourth home is created.** The rule governs where
an address is **stored as the truth**; these three are a record of **what a member of
the public said** — which is why every one of them is spelled `_as_given`, the same
posture `address_as_given` has carried since it was written and the same posture
`interruptions.location_text` carries (*"what a stranger typed — a report, not a
record"*).

⚠ **THE BARE SPELLINGS ARE STILL REFUSED, AND THAT IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.**
A `city` on this table is the fourth home `G85` catches by name, and it is what the
2026-09-15 near-miss actually was. The backend case asserts all three bare names are
REFUSED in the same breath as the three `_as_given` names are stored — because an
implementation that accepted a bare `city` would satisfy *the parts are captured* and
would be exactly the thing the rule forbids (hard-won law 7: ask what would make the
check pass wrongly).

### TWO THINGS A LATER LANE WILL OTHERWISE GET WRONG

**1 · `CAPTURE_FIELDS` SAID *"Do not re-add them"* UNTIL TODAY, AND IT WAS RIGHT.**
Three columns of these exact names were added on 2026-09-15 and removed the same hour,
under the PO's ruling of that day — *"if we have unit or street address then we should
take it from premises/Unit - it means its a search"*. `BR-CUS-1055` records that
near-miss in four files. **The comment is AMENDED rather than deleted**, with the whole
chain written out, because a lane that finds these columns and then finds a warning
against them has no way to tell which came first.

**2 · `G85`'s DECLARED BLIND SPOT MOVES FROM 3 TO 6, IN THE SAME COMMIT.**
That gate matches by NAME, so an `_as_given` spelling is invisible to it — and it is
**deliberately not taught that spelling**, because teaching it would make it refuse
`address_as_given` itself, which `BR-CUS-070` requires. What keeps the door shut is the
name: a bare `city` is still caught, because `city` IS in `ADDRESS_SHAPED`.

⚠ **So the NUMBER is what does the work here, and that is the general lesson.** Hard-won
law 7's fifth shape is *a declared blind spot with no NUMBER attached is
indistinguishable from an empty one* — and a **stale** number is indistinguishable from
a current one. `UNSEEN_AS_GIVEN_SPELLINGS` moves with the columns, every time, or the
gate goes back to reporting a clean zero over a scope it cannot see.

### AND THE OTHER HALF OF `BR-CUS-1055` WENT THE OTHER WAY THE SAME DAY

Row 12 of the same PO report removes **`How many units are on this property?`** — the
question on step 3, the `Units on site` row on the request's screen, and the evidence
table's third line, which weighed the applicant's claim against the register and is the
half of that rule the blueprint argues hardest for. **The column, the payload key and
every row already holding a number are untouched.** It was built on the PO's own
instruction of 2026-09-15 and taken off a week later; both directions are in
`BR-CUS-1055`'s own row now, dated, so neither reads as an oversight.

## 2026-09-22 — THE APPLICATION FEE GETS A DOOR, AND `Collect later` LOSES ONE

**PO report of this date, row 11**, second half: the Application fee amount comes
from a dropdown reading the CHARGE CODES, and `Collect later` goes. This entry
records the four judgments made where that instruction ran out, and — more
importantly — **the three things it deliberately does NOT do**, because the
ruling it carries forward has three open items that are the PO's and not ours.

### WHAT WAS BUILT

`ApplicationFeeAdder` — one component, mounted twice (B14 rule 43): on capture
step 5 and inside the request's own Fees panel. Pick a fee, see what it costs,
add it to the list. And `Collect later`, the two-button control it lived in, and
the `Due by` date it opened are all off `REQ-03` step 5.

### THE JUDGMENTS, AND WHY EACH IS PRECEDENT RATHER THAN TASTE

**1 · IT IS ON BOTH SCREENS, NOT ONLY THE ONE THE PO WAS LOOKING AT.** The PO
named the wizard. But the door being missing is `DEF-CUS-5904`, filed on
2026-09-19 out of the PO's own clerk walk, and that defect is about the PRODUCT:
*"a clerk cannot raise an application fee anywhere"*. A request whose fee was not
raised at capture would still have had no way to be given one. Building it on the
wizard alone would have closed the sentence and left the defect.

**2 · ONLY `one_time`, PRICEABLE CODES ARE OFFERED — 15 of the 19 on the seeded
utility.** The priceability half is **the PO's own ruling of 2026-09-21**
(`DEF-MET-6110`): *"Step 6 offers only charge codes a build can actually price"*,
after a clerk picked `TAP`, which states no amount, and lost thirty-three acts to
*"Something went wrong on our side."* `canBeRaisedOnItsOwn` is **imported** from
`NewConnectChargesStep`, not re-written, because two copies of *can this be
priced* drift apart. The `one_time` half is ours: a recurring base charge or a
penalty is something that happens to an ACCOUNT over time, and an application fee
is taken once, at a counter, against a request that has no account yet.

**Measured on `brazosbend`, with `app.tenant_id` set:** 29 charge codes · 19
one-time · 15 of those priced · the four left out are `BULK-WATER`, `DAMAGE`,
`IMPACT` and `TAP`, each of which states **no amount AND no amount rule**. Every
charge on that tenant carries a GL account, so the GL clause of the predicate
changes nothing there — it is carried because the 2026-09-21 direction is that
this fee eventually POSTS, and a list built without it would stop working on the
day that lands.

⚠ **WHAT AN AMOUNT-LESS CODE DOES, ASKED AND ANSWERED: IT IS LEFT OUT, NOT SHOWN
DISABLED.** `BR-SHL-025` says a control that cannot act is disabled with its
reason — and that governs a CONTROL, not one option among sixteen. Fifteen
options in this dropdown can act; greying a sixteenth teaches a clerk that the
product is broken rather than that a code is unfinished, and rule 33 gives the
reason nowhere to live (rationale is zero words on screen). **Where the whole
catalogue has nothing raisable there IS a stated absence**, one sentence, because
an empty picker with no words is a screen a clerk cannot tell from a broken one.

**3 · `fee_timing` IS DERIVED FROM THE TENDER, NOT FORCED.** With one option left
there was no control to read. Writing `collect_now` on to every request would
tell the customer portal *before we start* about money nobody intends to take at
the counter — so: a METHOD chosen means `collect_now`, and no method means **no
answer rather than a guess**. That is not invented here; it is what
`apps/portal/paying.py::_fee_when` already does with a null, in its own words:
*"a screen saying before we start over a request nobody set a timing on would be
inventing a deadline."*

**4 · THE CONTROL WENT, NOT JUST THE OPTION.** A choice of one is not a choice.
Leaving `Collect now` alone in a two-button control is the dead control hard-won
law 2's mirror describes — a thing that looks like a decision and cannot be
decided.

### WHAT WAS NOT CHANGED, AND THE FIGURE THAT MADE IT SAFE

**No stored value is retired and no row is rewritten** (hard rule 4).
`ServiceRequest.fee_timing` still accepts `collect_later`, `fee_due_by` still
exists and is still served, and the customer portal still reads that spelling and
answers *later* to a customer. **What went is the QUESTION, not the spelling** —
row 12's unit count in the other direction, on the same day.

**Measured before the cut, with `app.tenant_id` set: 22 service requests on the
seeded utility, every one of them with `fee_timing` NULL and not one with a
due-by date.** The control had never produced a value there at all. And
`fee_due_by` is read by NOTHING — no dunning, no reminder, no refusal — so the
date a clerk typed was a promise the product could not keep.

### ⛔ WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, AND IT IS THE PART A LATER LANE WILL ASSUME

The ruling of 2026-09-21 that this carries forward — *"we wil add charge code for
it"* — **named three things a lane must not assume and must put back to the PO**,
and all three are still open:

1. whether the existing `ServiceRequest.fee_*` columns are migrated or left
   (money has already been collected against them in the beta, and hard rule 4
   means a migration that rewrites collected money is not available);
2. whether the charge is raised at capture, at approval, or when a clerk asks;
3. what the code is called and what it seeds at.

⚠ **AND THE HALF THAT RULING CARED ABOUT MOST IS UNTOUCHED: THESE LINES STILL DO
NOT REACH THE LEDGER.** `service_request_fees` posts no journal line and issues no
invoice (B18 §4.6, hard rules 4 and 5). **This work moves the SCREEN, not the
posting.** A lane reading *"the application fee is a charge code now"* and
concluding that finance can see it would be wrong, which is why it is written out
here rather than left to be inferred.

**`DEF-CUS-6102` — the utility that charges NO application fee — is also still
open.** Not configuring a code is how that utility says so, and this dropdown
respects it by offering nothing; but the PANEL and `Record what was handed over`
still appear on a `$0` request, and hiding a live money-taking control changes
what a clerk can DO.

## 2026-09-22 — THE BETA'S COLLECTED FEES STAY WHERE THEY ARE, AND A FEE LINE MUST RECORD WHO TOOK THE MONEY AND WHEN

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"(a) Leave them — Old requests keep their record as it
is. New ones use the charge code - we alsoneed to record who took it and when"*.

Answering a table that set out three options for the application fees already
collected during the beta, each with its cost named, against a worked case: a
request where a clerk took **$25.00 in cash, receipt 1041, on 12 September**,
recorded on the request row and never seen by finance.

### 1 · NOTHING IS MIGRATED

The beta's collected fees stay in the columns they were written to —
`service_requests.fee_timing`, `fee_due_by`, `fee_method`, `fee_currency`,
`fee_receipt_no`, `fee_collected_at`, `fee_collected_by`. No backfill, no
conversion, no rewrite. New requests raise a **fee line** against a charge code.

**THE COST THE PO ACCEPTED, STATED BECAUSE A SIGNATURE COVERS ONLY WHAT WAS
SHOWN:** two ways of holding one fact will exist side by side for the life of
this data, and **finance will only ever see the new ones**. That was put to them
in those words before they chose. Every report, screen and export that totals
application fees must therefore say which population it is counting, or it will
silently answer for one and be read as answering for both.

⚠ **AND NOTHING MAY DELETE OR REWRITE THOSE COLUMNS ON THAT BASIS.** "Leave
them" is an instruction to leave them, not permission to retire them later
because the new path exists. `DEF-CUS-3653` is this repository's own lesson:
retiring a value whose consumers were never grepped returned null on every
account for ever, with `tsc` and every test green.

### 2 · A FEE LINE RECORDS WHO TOOK THE MONEY AND WHEN — AND TODAY IT DOES NOT

The second clause is a REQUIREMENT, not a restatement, and the gap is real.
Measured against `apps/customers/models.ServiceRequestFee` as it stands:

| Fact | On the fee line today |
|---|---|
| Who WAIVED it, and when | ✅ `waived_by`, `waived_at`, `waive_reason` |
| When the line was raised | ✅ `created_at` |
| **Who RAISED it** | ❌ nothing |
| **Who TOOK the money, and when** | ❌ nothing |
| **How it was paid, and the receipt number** | ❌ nothing |

**The collection details live on the REQUEST row instead** — one set per
request, written by the *Record what was handed over* modal. So the moment a
request carries MORE THAN ONE fee line, the product cannot say which line the
money was against. A waive is fully attributed and a payment is not, which is
exactly backwards: the waive takes no money.

⚠ **AND `audit_log` IS NOT THE ANSWER, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A COLUMN AND NOT A
SHRUG.** Hard rule 7 means the act already writes an audit row, and a lane could
reasonably argue the fact is therefore recorded. It is not recorded DURABLY:
`audit_log` is pruned on a retention schedule, and whether a money row is exempt
from that pruning is **`OQ-1340` and is OPEN**. CLAUDE.md states the consequence
in terms — no document, screen or docstring may describe such a path as a
permanent record. So *who took it and when* belongs on the row.

**WHAT IS TO BE BUILT:** the fee line carries who raised it, and — when money is
taken against it — who took it, when, how it was paid and the receipt number.
The *Record what was handed over* modal writes them to the LINE. ⚠ The old
columns on the request are NOT the place to put them and are not extended;
clause 1 freezes them as the beta's record.

⚠ **THIS IS MONEY AND IT IS THEREFORE APPEND-ONLY BY DEFAULT.** Hard rule 4
governs what may be updated on a money row. A collection stamp is a
`NULL -> set` write-once, the same shape as a payment's `deposit_batch_id`, and
a correction is a new act rather than an edit. A lane building this decides
nothing about immutability on its own.

### 3 · QUESTIONS 2 AND 3 REMAIN OPEN

The other two of 2026-09-21's three are NOT answered by this ruling and no lane
may take them: **when the charge is raised** (at capture, at approval, or when a
clerk asks — today it is when a clerk asks) and **what the charge code is called
and what it starts at**. Until they are answered the application fee reaches the
SCREEN and not the BOOKS, and nothing in this repository may say otherwise.

---

## 2026-09-22 — THE APPLICATION FEE IS RAISED AT APPROVAL, NOT AT CAPTURE

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"(b) At approval — 24 Sep — A clerk who took $25 cash at
the counter on the 22nd has held money the books knew nothing about for two days"*.

They quoted the option back **together with its stated cost**, which is the clearest
form a ruling takes here: the cost was on the table and they took it.

**The worked case they were answering:** John Doe walks in on **22 September** and
applies for water, sewer and trash; the request is approved on **24 September**;
connection is **14 October**. The three options were (a) raise it at capture, (b) at
approval, (c) when the clerk raises it — which is what is built today.

**SO: approving a request raises its application fee.** The driver is the one (a)
fails on — an abandoned or refused application must not leave a charge behind to be
reversed — and (b) buys that at the price of a two-day gap when money is taken early.

⚠ **THIS SUPERSEDES WHAT SHIPPED THIS MORNING.** `2.328.4` built (c): a clerk raises
the fee by pressing **Add** on the fee panel, on either screen. That is now the
exception rather than the rule, and the lane that built it recorded (c) as the
behaviour — that record is superseded by this row and must be amended wherever it is
cited, in the same commit as the code.

### THE CONSEQUENCE THE RULING DOES NOT SETTLE, DECIDED HERE RATHER THAN RE-ASKED

(b) says when the charge is RAISED. It does not say what happens when a clerk **takes
money before approval**, which the product allows today — *Record what was handed
over* sits on a request from the moment it exists. Under a literal (b) there would be
no fee line to take the money against for two days.

**Decided (CLAUDE.md law 13 — a judgment call is ours to make and write down):**

> **A fee line is raised at approval, OR EARLIER IF A CLERK TAKES MONEY AGAINST IT.**

Three reasons, and the third is the one that decides it:

  1. **Money taken is a fact and a paid fee certainly exists.** A charge that has been
     settled cannot sensibly be said not to have been raised yet.
  2. **It preserves what the ruling is actually for.** (a) was refused because an
     application nobody approved must not leave a charge behind — and an application
     somebody PAID FOR is not that case.
  3. **The alternative removes something a clerk can do today**, which needs a ruling
     of its own and did not get one. Hard-won law 2's mirror is a live screen behind a
     dead control; silently refusing the counter collection would be exactly that.

**If that reading is wrong the PO can say so in one word, and the cost of being wrong
is one condition.** Re-asking them a question they have just answered is the bug law
13 exists to prevent — *"i try to be consisitence but as human i might make a mistake
in my response"*.

### WHAT MUST BE TRUE WHEN THIS IS BUILT

* **Idempotency — hard rule 6.** Approving twice raises ONE fee line. `BR-CUS-093`
  clause (e) is the shape: the idempotency key is the request itself.
* **A refused, withdrawn or abandoned request raises nothing**, which is the whole
  point of refusing (a).
* **A re-approval after a reopen must not raise a second line** where one already
  exists — and if the rules genuinely require a second charge, that is a new ruling,
  not a lane's call.
* **A utility with no application-fee charge code configured raises nothing, and
  that is lawful, not an error.** Not configuring the code is how a utility says it
  does not charge one.
* **Question 3 is still open and this ruling does not close it** — what the code is
  called and what it starts at. Until it is answered there is nothing for approval to
  raise on a fresh utility, so this lands inert until the PO names the code.

## 2026-09-22 — THE APPLICATION FEE IS CALLED "Application fees", COSTS $10.00, AND IS CHARGED ONCE PER APPLICATION

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"Applciation fees, we wil charge $10 and per applciation"*,
answering the third and last of 2026-09-21's three open questions with all three parts
in one sentence.

| | The answer |
|---|---|
| What the charge code is called | **Application fees** |
| What it costs | **$10.00** |
| Charged per service, or per application? | **Per application** — one charge however many services are asked for |

**WORKED, BECAUSE A RULING IS PUT AND RECORDED WITH A CONCRETE FIGURE.** John Doe
applies on 22 September for **water, sewer AND trash**. The request is approved on 24
September. **One fee line is raised, for `$10.00`** — not three, and not `$30.00`.
That is what *per application* means and it is the whole content of the third part.

**SO THE THREE QUESTIONS OF 2026-09-21 ARE ALL CLOSED**, and the application fee can
now reach the books rather than only the screen:
  1. the beta's collected fees stay where they are (a), and a fee line must record who
     took the money and when;
  2. the charge is raised **at approval** (b), or earlier if a clerk takes money
     against it;
  3. **`Application fees`, `$10.00`, per application.**

### HOW THE FIGURE IS HELD, WHICH IS NOT THE PO'S TO SPECIFY AND IS STATED HERE

⚠ **`$10.00` IS A SEEDED DEFAULT ON A TENANT'S OWN CHARGE CODE, NOT A CONSTANT IN
CODE.** Every price in this product belongs to the utility that charges it, and this
one is no different: it is a charge code a tenant edits on Settings, exactly like
fire's six sizes. A utility that charges nothing configures no code, and that is how
they say so — `2.328.4` already leaves an unpriced code out of the picker rather than
greying it.

⚠ **CLAUDE.md HARD RULE 2 GOVERNS THE STORED FIGURE.** Money is stored to **4
decimals** and DISPLAYED to 2. So the code carries `10.0000` and a clerk reads
`$10.00`; the screen sends the stored four-decimal amount and never the rounded one,
which `2.328.4` already asserts with a test proved red by sending the rounded figure.

⚠ **IT IS NOT A ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 FIGURE AND MUST NOT BE WRITTEN INTO ONE.** B4's money
math and B5's golden tests are finance-signed and move only by a re-sign through
HUMAN-GUIDE §6. A tenant's application fee is a configured price, in a different class
entirely, and no golden test may come to depend on `$10.00`.

## 2026-09-22 — PAYMENTS BLUEPRINT PHASE 0: ONE SOURCE COLUMN, THE TIMEZONE FIX GOES FORWARD ONLY, AND EVERY TASK IS RE-READ AGAINST TODAY'S CODE

`05-prototype/06 Payments Page Blueprint.pdf` — 109 pages, on the DEFAULT branch
(`claude/confirm-understanding-3ktufc`), not on any working branch. ⚠ **A LANE
LOOKING FOR IT ON `main` OR `master` FINDS NOTHING: THIS REPOSITORY'S DEFAULT BRANCH
IS A `claude/…` BRANCH.** That is how this one was nearly reported missing, and it is
the same absence that cost the Billing wizard its step count. `git ls-remote --symref
origin HEAD` answers it in one command; CLAUDE.md's *"across the refs, not just
yours"* means that command, not a guess at a name.

Phase 0 is **Foundations, 17 tasks, `P0.1`–`P0.17`**, and the document's own summary
is *"Nothing a clerk can see, and everything else waits on it … the only phase with no
user value."* Three of its four open decisions were put to the PO with worked cases
and options; these are the answers.

### 1 · ONE COLUMN, NOT TWO — `P0.1`/`P0.2` EXTEND WHAT SHIPPED THIS MORNING

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"(a) One column — extend what we shipped — Rename or map the
three values, add the check the blueprint wants."*

⚠ **THE COLLISION, STATED BECAUSE IT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE BEEN BUILT TWICE.** `P0.1`
asks for `payments.source`, a text column with a CHECK over `counter | digital |
post`, and **names `payments/0029` as its reference**. `CR-132-BRC07` shipped
`payments.origin` **this morning** — values `entry | webhook | import` — **as
migration `payments/0029`**. The blueprint was read at `2.322.0` on 2026-09-21 and
says of itself that every as-built statement *"must be re-verified before it is
trusted"*; this is that warning coming true within a day.

| The blueprint's value | What shipped | |
|---|---|---|
| `counter` | `entry` | money handed over at the counter |
| `digital` | `webhook` | a payment that arrived over a wire |
| `post` | `import` | a batch keyed or loaded from a file |

**So: no second column.** The existing column takes the blueprint's vocabulary and its
CHECK. ⚠ **AND THE TWO DERIVATIONS ARE NOT THE SAME, WHICH IS THE PART THAT WILL BITE
A LANE THAT READS ONLY THE TABLE ABOVE.** `P0.2` derives `post` from a row in
`payment_import_rows` naming the payment; the shipped backfill derives `import` from
the idempotency key's `import|` prefix. `P0.2` also demands **no nulls and a row
matching none of the three FAILS LOUDLY**, where the shipped column is deliberately
NULLable and documents why. Reconciling those two is real work and is not a rename.
⚠ And `origin_is_derived` must survive it: the backfilled value is an INFERENCE, the
PO ruled it must be marked as one, and a CHECK that makes the column NOT NULL must not
quietly turn an inference into an observation.

### 2 · THE TIMEZONE FIX APPLIES GOING FORWARD ONLY — `P0.7`

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"Going forward only"*.

`isoToday()` (`PaymentsPage.tsx:677`) returns `new Date().toISOString()` — the UTC day
— while the tenant timezone setting exists and the date component already honours it.
The blueprint's worked case: **a 17:30 shift in UTC−7 stamps its payments into
tomorrow.**

**So the fix changes what is stamped from now on and NOTHING ALREADY RECORDED.** That
is also the only lawful answer: a payment's posting date is frozen by CLAUDE.md hard
rule 4 and by `payments/0014`'s trigger, which names `posted_at` among the columns
frozen from the moment the row exists. **Correcting a past payment's day would be a
new row, never an edit** — so "going forward only" is the PO agreeing with a
constraint rather than choosing between two open options, and it is recorded as such.

### 3 · EVERY TASK IS RE-READ AGAINST TODAY'S CODE BEFORE IT IS BUILT

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"do all cahnges based on most updated code"*.

This is a standing instruction for the whole phase, not a remark about one task, and
it matches the document's own warning about itself. What it means in practice: **a
`P0.x` row is a hypothesis about the code until a lane checks it.** Four have already
been checked and two of those had moved:

| Task | The blueprint says | Today |
|---|---|---|
| `P0.1` | *"The row has no such field today"* | **FALSE since this morning** — `payments.origin` exists |
| `P0.7` | `isoToday()` returns the UTC day | **TRUE**, `PaymentsPage.tsx:677` |
| `P0.8` | four tabs, seven drawn | **TRUE**, `PAYMENTS_TABS` holds four |
| `P0.12` | *"52 call sites … and zero times in staff payments"* | **TRUE to the number**, measured today |

**So each task is verified before it is written, and where the document is out of date
the CODE wins and the row is struck with what is true instead.** A task that turns out
to be already done is reported as done, never re-built.

### 4 · TWO DECISIONS REMAIN OPEN AND NO LANE MAY TAKE THEM

**`P0.6`, the deposit-batch re-key**, and **whether the ledger change it depends on is
in scope for phase 0.** Both were put to the PO with worked cases; neither is answered
yet. `P0.6` is the document's own most-gating item — *"It is the first thing to do,
and it is not in payments"* — and it carries its own ⚠ in the task table: *"a dropped
unique key with no replacement lets two batches collide silently."* Real money has
been banked against the existing batches and `BR-PAY-004` locks a reconciled one, so
nothing here is a lane's to improvise.

## 2026-09-22 — PHASE 0'S LAST THREE ANSWERS: SEVEN TABS AS DRAWN, `STL-26-0001`, AND A SUPERVISOR MAY FORCE A TILL CLOSED

Three more of the payments blueprint's phase 0 decisions, each put to the PO with a
worked case and lettered options.

### 1 · THE SEVEN TABS SHIP IN PHASE 0, AS THE DOCUMENT DRAWS THEM — `P0.8`/`P0.9`

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"go as per phase 0 ; we are going to implement all phases
one by one so fcus on current one."*

**The question was what a clerk sees when they click a tab with nothing behind it.**
Phase 0 makes Counter, Imports and Settlements reachable and builds no screens, so
three doors open onto nothing until later phases. Three options were offered: (a) add
each tab when its screen lands, (b) all seven with the three saying plainly that they
are not built, (c) all seven with three greyed out.

**So: all seven render and all seven are reachable**, which is `P0.8`'s outcome
(*"Seven tabs render on every payments screen"*) and `P0.9`'s (*"Every new tab is
reachable. Three screens in this audit were built and unreachable; this is how that is
avoided by design"*). The three without screens say so plainly.

⚠ **AND EACH OF THE THREE SHIPS WITH THE TEST THAT FIRES WHEN ITS HOLD EXPIRES,
WHICH IS NOT AN EXTRA AND IS NOT THE PO'S TO ASK FOR.** CLAUDE.md hard-won law 2's
mirror is this exact situation and cost a whole front page: on 2026-09-05 the customer
portal had **two working doors out of eight**, five cards and three nav words still
refusing over screens that had shipped days earlier. The law's instruction is in
terms — *"WHEN YOU WRITE A HOLD, WRITE THE TEST THAT FIRES WHEN THE HOLD EXPIRES, in
the same commit — assert the destination by ADDRESS and by the screen id it opens."*
A "not built yet" with no such test is a promise nobody is keeping.

**The second half of the ruling is a standing instruction for the whole plan:** phases
are implemented one at a time and a lane works the phase it is in. A phase 0 task is
not enlarged because a phase 2 screen will want more.

### 2 · THE SETTLEMENT SERIES IS `STL-26-0001` — `P0.13`

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"(a) STL-26-0001"*.

So the new series' default format is **`STL-{YY}-{0000}`**, matching `DEP-`, `MVI-`
and `MVO-` exactly. Counter batches reuse `deposit_batch` and imports reuse
`import_run`; this is the ONE series phase 0 adds, and `P0.13` calls it *"the entire
Settings change for all 35 screens."*

⚠ **A SEEDED DEFAULT A TENANT EDITS, NEVER A CONSTANT.** Like every series in this
product it is configurable on Settings → Numbering; thirty already exist. What is
ruled is what it starts as.

### 3 · A SYSTEM ADMIN MAY CLOSE SOMEBODY ELSE'S TILL, AND THE RECORD SAYS SO — `P0.3`

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"(b) A System Admin can close it, recorded as a forced
close"*.

**The worked case put to them:** Dana opens a till on Monday at 08:00, takes **$1,240
in cheques**, goes home at 17:00 without closing it, and is off sick on Tuesday. Under
(a) — only Dana may close it — the one-open-till-per-person index means **Dana cannot
work when they return**. Under (c) the till closes itself overnight with no count,
which was put to them as a hole in the money trail and which this lane said it would
not build.

**So `counter_sessions.close_kind` has at least two values** — a normal close by the
owner, and a **forced close** by a System Admin — and `closed_by` records who actually
did it, which on a forced close is not the owner. That is the one field in `P0.3`'s
column list the drawing did not spell out, and this ruling is what fills it.

⚠ **THE MONEY CONSEQUENCE, STATED BECAUSE THE PO ACCEPTED IT:** on a forced close,
somebody other than the owner counts a drawer the owner is accountable for. The record
must therefore make the two people distinguishable for ever — which is why this is a
`close_kind` and a `closed_by`, not a quiet close in the owner's name. A forced close
is also a money action, so CLAUDE.md hard rule 7 applies: it writes `audit_log`.

⚠ **AND WHO MAY DO IT IS A ROLE CHECK AT THE SERVICE, NOT ON A SCREEN.** `BR-SHL-025`:
server-side enforcement is THE enforcement. A button hidden from a Billing Clerk is
not a guarantee; `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)` on the close is.

## 2026-09-22 — THE BATCHES ALREADY BANKED ARE TOLD APART BY WHAT THEY LACK, NOT BY ANYTHING WRITTEN TO THEM (`P0.6`)

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"d) Tell them apart by what they lack — Nothing at all. A
batch with no session is one banked the old way — Yes — Recommended"*.

**THE QUESTION.** `P0.6` re-keys the deposit batch: today a batch is *one day, one
payment method* for the whole utility; after phase 0 it is *one person's till
session*. **The batches already banked have no session to attach to, because tills did
not exist.** Worked case put to the PO: Tuesday 22 September at a two-counter office,
Dana takes 6 cheques and Sam takes 4 — today that is one batch, `DEP-26-0922-CHK`,
holding all ten; afterwards it is two.

**WHAT IS RULED: NOTHING IS WRITTEN TO AN EXISTING BATCH. A BATCH WITH NO SESSION
*IS* ONE BANKED THE OLD WAY.** The absence is the fact.

### WHY THIS WAS THE RIGHT ANSWER AND NOT MERELY THE CHEAPEST

Four options were offered and **two of them were impossible**, which is the part worth
recording because it is not obvious from the outside:

| Option | Why it fell |
|---|---|
| (b) give each old batch a session | **A reconciled batch is LOCKED (`BR-PAY-004`)**, so the write is refused — and the session would be INVENTED, recording that somebody ran a till that never existed |
| (c) stamp each one *"banked the old way"* | Same wall. **A marker is still an UPDATE**, and a locked batch refuses it |
| (a) leave them and say nothing | Lawful, but every report that groups by session silently answers for one population and is read as answering for both |
| **(d) tell them apart by what they lack** | **Writes nothing, touches no locked row, needs no data migration, and cannot get it wrong** |

⚠ **THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH IS THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN AND WORTH MORE THAN THE
RULING:** the first three options all assumed the distinction had to be WRITTEN
somewhere. It did not — the schema already carried it, as an absence. **Before
migrating data to record a fact, ask whether the fact is already implied by a column
being empty.** The same shape appears in `payments.origin_is_derived` and in
`ArPositions`' unavailable codes: an absent answer is never spelled the same way as a
real one.

### THE ONE THING (d) REQUIRES, AND IT IS A GUARD RATHER THAN A MIGRATION

**After the re-key, nothing may create a batch without a session**, or the two
populations stop being cleanly separable and the ruling quietly becomes false.

* The replacement unique key is **partial**: one batch per session, `WHERE session IS
  NOT NULL`. ⚠ `P0.6`'s own warning in the drawing is *"a dropped unique key with no
  replacement lets two batches collide silently"* — a partial index that ignores the
  legacy rows is NOT a missing replacement, because no new row may join that
  population. **That must be enforced, not assumed.**
* So the guard is: a batch created after this change **requires** a session. Prove it
  at the database, not only in the service — `BR-SHL-025`, and `payments/0014`'s own
  reasoning: a Python check is not a guarantee against a repair script with a cursor.
* ⚠ **PROVE THE GUARD RED FIRST, ON POSTGRESQL** (hard-won law 7). The suite defaults
  to in-memory SQLite where neither the partial index nor RLS behaves as it will in
  production, and that asymmetry has already shipped two defects to a live deploy
  today (`DEF-PAY-6165`, `DEF-PAY-6166`).

### WHAT IS STILL OPEN

**Whether the LEDGER change `P0.6` depends on is in scope for phase 0** is NOT
answered by this ruling and no lane may take it. The drawing is explicit that it gates
everything and is not in payments: *"It is the first thing to do, and it is not in
payments."* `P0.6` does not start until that is answered, because the answer decides
whether it is one piece of work or two.

---

## 2026-09-22 — PHASE 0 INCLUDES THE LEDGER CHANGE, SO `P0.6` IS ONE PIECE OF WORK ACROSS TWO MODULES

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"(a) Payments and ledger together — The re-key, and the
ledger accepting two deposits where it expected one — Phase 0 takes longer —
Recommended"*.

**THE LAST OF PHASE 0'S OPEN DECISIONS.** All seventeen tasks are now unblocked.

**The worked case put to them:** Dana's Tuesday session holds **$1,240** of cheques
and Sam's holds **$880**. Today the ledger sees **one** deposit of **$2,120** for 22
September, cheques. Afterwards it must see **two** — and **the day must still tie to
$2,120 exactly.**

**The three options and their costs, as shown:** (a) both together, phase 0 takes
longer; (b) payments side only — *the till table exists but nothing can bank from it,
and phase 2's counter screens stall on arrival*; (c) skip the re-key — phase 0
finishes soonest and **the counter cannot be built at all**, which is the biggest gap
in the product. The drawing's own verdict on this task: *"It is the first thing to do,
and it is not in payments."*

### WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT LICENCE

⚠ **IT IS NOT PERMISSION FOR A CROSS-MODULE WRITE.** CLAUDE.md is unconditional:
cross-module writes are forbidden and cross-module FKs are the reviewed interface set
(B2 §2). *"Payments and ledger together"* means **one piece of work spanning two
modules, each writing its own tables** — not payments reaching into the ledger's.

⚠ **AND HARD RULE 5 IS UNTOUCHED: only the ledger posting service writes journal
lines.** A deposit becoming two deposits changes WHAT that service is asked to post;
it does not change WHO posts it. Any lane that finds itself writing a journal line
from payments has taken a wrong turn.

⚠ **BALANCED PAIRS AND THE DAY'S TOTAL ARE THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, NOT A NICETY.**
Splitting one deposit into two must leave every pair balanced (hard rule 5) and the
day's cash total unchanged. **$1,240 + $880 = $2,120** is the figure this ruling was
signed on and it is what a test must assert.

### THE SIGNED RULE THIS CHANGES, QUOTED

**`BR-PAY-025`** (payments module, CONFIRMED): *"Deposit batches group day × method
(day = POSTING date per RQ-5/BR-REP-013), numbered from tenant series (DEP-…)"*,
amended 2026-08-12 by PO ruling so the code carries the year. **Re-keying on the
session supersedes the grouping half of that rule and must be stamped as such, in the
same commit as the code**, with the amendment of 2026-08-12 left standing — it is
about the CODE FORMAT, not the grouping, and this does not touch it.
⚠ `BR-PAY-004` — **a reconciled batch is LOCKED** — is NOT changed and is what makes
yesterday's ruling (d) the only workable answer for the legacy rows.
⚠ `payments/0014`'s trigger refuses a change of `deposit_batch_id` on a payment that
already has one, calling batch membership WRITE-ONCE, *"because a batch total is the
sum of its members, so moving a payment between batches would rewrite two signed-off
day totals at once."* **Nothing in this work may move an existing payment between
batches.**

### HOW IT LANDS

It is **one change request across two modules**, executed through the build process,
with the ledger side written by whoever owns the ledger's tables. Migration ordering
is a 🔒 sensitive path in both modules, so both migrations carry
`HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` and a row in the human-review ledger stating what would be put
to the PO in plain English with the `$1,240 / $880 / $2,120` figure.

---

**PO instruction, verbatim:** *"start all 19 immediately"*, answering a message that

**Phase 1 is "Make what exists reachable", 23 tasks**: *"Four finished engines get a

⚠ **THEY ARE HELD FOR A MECHANICAL REASON, NOT A PLANNING ONE: THEY ARE THE SAME
FILES THREE PHASE 0 LANES ARE EDITING RIGHT NOW.** CLAUDE.md law 11 is this
repository's most expensive lesson and it cost three id collisions, a duplicated
version and a duplicated migration number **today**. Two lanes in one file is how a
commit publishes or reverts work nobody meant to touch.

### `P1.9` — RETIRED, AND RETIRED **LAST**

**What it is, in the drawing's words:** *"Retire `payment_import.py` — six endpoints
and two staging tables doing four of the runner's five stages, with **no Transform**.
Or amend the rule."* Outcome: *"One import pipeline. **A PO call** — assets' staged
path was retired for exactly this."*

**MEASURED BEFORE PUTTING IT TO THE PO, because the whole question turns on it:** the
six endpoints are `payment-imports` plus `/validate`, `/commit`, `/discard`,
`/rows/{id}/account` and the detail route (`payment_import_api.py:269-274`), and
**NOTHING IN THE ENTIRE FRONT END CALLS ANY OF THEM.** Zero non-test references. So
the old pipeline is server code with no user, and has never been reachable by a clerk.
Retiring it is invisible to a clerk by construction; what it changes is what the next
person to work on payments finds — one way of importing, or two with the second dead.

**HOW THE ANSWER ARRIVED, AND WHY IT IS READ AS (a).** The PO did not type the letter;
they asked *"cant we use the import runner here - i did not understand what does this
mean"*, were given the plain-English version, and answered *"start all 19
immediately"* to a message ending *"So: (a)? One word and all 19 start."* CLAUDE.md
law 13 is explicit that **a ruling arriving in a form we did not expect is still a
ruling** — *"okay dont link it"* and *"a for now, c if it bites"* are named as
complete answers. This is that shape.

⚠ **BUT THE 19 EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED `P1.9`, SO THE INSTRUCTION HAS TWO HONEST
READINGS**, and the sequencing settles both without anyone being asked again:

> **The 19 start now. The retirement is the LAST act of phase 1, and the deletion is
> confirmed with the PO before it lands.**

That is also the only correct engineering order: **you do not remove the old machine
before the new one is proved working.** `P1.1`'s dict entry, `P1.11`'s end-to-end on
PostgreSQL and `P1.14`'s journey all have to be green first. A lane that deletes the
old path early has removed the fallback it might need.

**WHAT STAYS EITHER WAY:** `P1.4` is its own task and says so — **the two staging
tables are KEPT.** `payment_import_batches` and `payment_import_rows` *"hold the
provenance of every payment they created"*, and phase 0's source backfill still reads
them. **Retiring the pipeline is not deleting the history**, and any lane that reads
`P1.9` as licence to drop those tables has misread it.
