## 2026-09-22 — THE NOTES UNDER A DRAWING ARE PART OF THE DRAWING, AND THE OLD PAYMENTS IMPORT PIPELINE IS DELETED

**PO instruction, verbatim:** *"i want you to use drawing images exactly to build
screen; dont use text ; below each drawing threr are instructions and details you
should use them and also use ui skills from repo"* — and, on `P1.9`: *"we should not
use second machine - (a) Delete it if possible"*.

### 1 · B14 RULE 42 IS SHARPENED, NOT RESTATED — AND THE SHARPENING MATTERS

Rule 42 says a screen is built from the drawing AS AN IMAGE and that *"extracted text
is an index, never the specification."* **That is exactly right and it is one word
away from being read backwards.** A lane can read *"never the specification"* as
*"ignore the words"*, and the blueprint's pages carry, under every wireframe,
**annotations, callouts and a task table that ARE the specification.** The PO has now
said so in terms: *"below each drawing there are instructions and details you should
use them."*

**So the line is between two different things, and it is worth stating precisely:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **The rendered PAGE — the wireframe AND the notes under it** | **IS the specification.** Read it by looking at it |
| **The text stream `pdf_text.py` pulls out of the PDF** | An INDEX for finding which page to render. Never built from |

⚠ **THIS IS NOT PEDANTRY: THE TEXT STREAM IS LOSSY IN WAYS THAT LOOK LIKE CONTENT.**
Measured on this very document — the task ids come out of `pdf_text.py` as a bare
`P` on every row, so all seventeen of phase 0's tasks read as the same id; figures and
column boundaries are shuffled; `NUMERIC(18,6)` survives but the column it belongs to
does not. **A lane briefing itself from that stream builds seventeen tasks it cannot
tell apart.** The images were rendered at scale 2.0 and every task id, reference and
outcome read cleanly.

**And the repo's own UI skills are part of the method**, per the same instruction:
`.claude/skills/react-tailwind-css-ui-generator`, `.claude/skills/measure-before-you-
build` and `.claude/skills/build-one-commitment-end-to-end` are present in every
worktree. A lane building a screen loads them; they are not optional background.

### 2 · `P1.9` IS RULED — THE OLD PAYMENTS IMPORT PIPELINE IS DELETED

**PO, verbatim:** *"we should not use second machine - (a) Delete it if possible"*.

So `payment_import.py` and its **six endpoints** go: `payment-imports` plus
`/validate`, `/commit`, `/discard`, `/rows/{id}/account` and the detail route
(`payment_import_api.py:269-274`). **Measured before this was put to the PO: nothing
in the entire front end calls any of them — zero non-test references.** It is server
code with no user and has never been reachable by a clerk, so the deletion is
invisible to a clerk by construction.

⚠ **"IF POSSIBLE" IS PART OF THE RULING AND IS NOT A HEDGE.** If something reaches
that pipeline which this measurement did not see — a job, a management command, an
integration, a partner API, a test that is the only caller — **the lane reports it
rather than deleting around it.** The measurement covered the front end; it did not
cover every caller in the backend, and saying so is the difference between a check and
a claim (hard-won law 7: a check that cannot cover its whole subject prints what it
skipped beside what it checked).

⚠ **THE ORDER STANDS AND IS NOT CAUTION FOR ITS OWN SAKE: THE NEW PATH IS PROVED
FIRST.** `P1.1`'s dict entry, `P1.11`'s end-to-end on PostgreSQL with one bad row in
four hundred, and `P1.14`'s lockbox journey all go green before the old path is
removed. **You do not remove the old machine before the new one is proved working** —
and `P1.14` is itself blocked on phase 0, so the deletion is genuinely the last act of
phase 1.

⚠ **AND `P1.4` IS UNTOUCHED BY THIS: THE TWO STAGING TABLES ARE KEPT.**
`payment_import_batches` and `payment_import_rows` hold the provenance of every
payment they created and phase 0's source backfill still reads them. **Deleting the
pipeline is not deleting the history**, and a lane reading `P1.9` as licence to drop
those tables has misread it. `P1.4` is a task to NOT do something and it stays that
way.

## 2026-09-22 — `P0.6` VERIFIED BEFORE BUILDING: THE LEDGER NEEDS NO CHANGE, AND THE THING THAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS THE RE-KEY IS THE BATCH *CODE*

**Nothing was built.** This row records a measurement taken before writing a line,
under the standing PO instruction *"do all cahnges based on most updated code"* and
the Payments blueprint's own warning that every as-built statement in it *"must be
re-verified before it is trusted"*. The document was read at **2.322.0**; this was
run at **2.328.4**, on a seeded PostgreSQL 16 clone, and **two of its statements did
not survive.**

### 1 · THE LEDGER HALF IS ALREADY DONE, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE

The PO ruled on 2026-09-22 that phase 0 includes *"the ledger accepting two deposits
where it expected one"*, on this worked case: **Dana's Tuesday session holds $1,240 of
cheques and Sam's holds $880; today the ledger sees one deposit of $2,120 for 22
September and afterwards it must see two — and the day must still tie to $2,120
exactly.**

**It already does. Measured, through the real posting service, on PostgreSQL:**

| what was asked | answer |
|---|---|
| deposits the ledger holds for 22 September | **2** |
| Dana's entry | debits `1240.000000` = credits `1240.000000` |
| Sam's entry | debits `880.000000` = credits `880.000000` |
| the day's cash debits | **`2120.000000`** |
| entries left behind (the run rolls back) | 0 |

**Why it already works, in one sentence:** a deposit's journal entry is keyed
`deposit_batch|<batch uuid>|reconciled` — on the BATCH, never on the day or the tender
— so two batches are two keys, `uq_journal_entries_posting_key` has no quarrel with
them, and every ledger report sums journal lines by `source_type`, which is additive.
**There is no day-level or method-level assumption anywhere in `apps/ledger/`.**

⚠ **PROVED RED FIRST, IN THE HARNESS THAT WILL RUN IT (law 7).** The mutation is the
ledger this task feared: both deposits keyed on the DAY rather than the batch. It fails
**5 checks and exits 1** — Sam's deposit replays instead of posting, the day holds one
entry, and the cash reads **`2480.000000`** because Dana is counted twice and Sam's
$880 has vanished. That is what a ledger keyed on the day would actually do to a
utility's books, and it is the shape this check exists to refuse.

The proof is `10-scripts/p06_ledger_two_deposits_readback.py`. It writes nothing.

⚠ **AND HARD RULE 5 IS ENFORCED IN THE DATABASE, WHICH CAUGHT THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS
PROOF.** A hand-written `INSERT` into `journal_entries` raises
`ledger_sole_writer_guard()`: *"journal_entries is written ONLY by the ledger posting
service … This INSERT did not come through post()"*. The guard was right and the draft
was wrong; the proof goes through `apps.ledger.posting.post()` and nothing else.

### 2 · THE DRAWING'S `P0.6` ROW IS INCOMPLETE, AND THE MISSING HALF IS THE ONE THAT BITES

`P0.6` says *"Drop `uq_deposit_batches_day_method` and key on the session"*. **That is
necessary and it is not sufficient, and the row does not mention the reason.**
`deposit_batches` carries a SECOND unique key — `uq_deposit_batches_code`,
`UNIQUE (tenant_id, code)` — and `apps/payments/reconciliation.batch_code(day,
method_code)` is a pure function of the day and the tender. **So both of Dana's and
Sam's Tuesday cheque sessions render `DEP-260922-CHK`.**

**Run with the drawing's DDL applied and nothing else changed:** Dana's $1,240 batch
inserts; Sam's $880 batch dies on

    ERROR:  duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_deposit_batches_code"

**So the drawing's own warning lands one step further along than it says.** *"A dropped
unique key with no replacement lets two batches collide silently"* is the hazard it
names; the hazard that is actually there is that **the second session cannot bank at
all**, loudly, on a constraint the row never mentions. A lane following `P0.6` as
written would ship the migration, watch every test pass, and discover it the first time
two people worked a counter on one day.

⚠ **AND `batch_code`'s OWN DOCSTRING SAYS WHY:** *"a batch code is not a COUNTER (there
is exactly one batch per day per method)"*. **The re-key destroys that premise.**
Meanwhile `core/numbering.py` already seeds the `deposit_batch` series as
`DEP-{YY}{MM}{DD}-{00}` — with a SEQUENCE token — so the shipped Settings screen and
the shipped code have disagreed since the series was written, and `P0.13` walks into
the same gap.

### 3 · WHAT WAS NOT BUILT, AND WHY — THREE THINGS, NONE OF THEM OURS TO DECIDE

**The DDL half is blocked on `counter_sessions`**, which is `P0.3`–`P0.5`
(LANE P0-DB, `payments/0030`). It does not exist on the branch at `ca6557b16`: there is
no `session` column to key on and no table to point a foreign key at.

**And three questions were found that a lane cannot answer for itself**, because each
collides with a signed statement (law 13's first category). They are minted rather than
guessed:

* **`OQ-PAY-12575` — what number does the second till of the day bank under?** It
  collides with the PO's own code-format ruling of 2026-08-12 (*"Add the year + Date is
  important"*).
* **`OQ-PAY-12576` — what banks the ACH, card and wire money after the re-key?**
  Yesterday's ruling requires that *nothing may create a batch without a session*, and
  `cut_deposit_batches` has to go on cutting session-less batches for four of the seven
  seeded tenders — money that never saw a till and never will. Building the guard as
  stated would stop a utility banking its electronic takings.
* **`OQ-PAY-12577` — is a batch one session, or one session and one tender?** The ruling
  says the first; `deposit_batches.method_id` is NOT NULL and `P0.3` draws *"counted
  totals per method"*, which says the second. The answer decides the wording of
  `payments/0014`'s tender refusal, which cites `BR-PAY-025`'s grouping half by name.

### 4 · `BR-PAY-025` IS **NOT** STAMPED SUPERSEDED, DELIBERATELY

The ruling requires the grouping half to be stamped SUPERSEDED-IN-PART *"in the same
commit as the code"*. **No code shipped, so no stamp.** Marking a rule superseded before
the thing that supersedes it exists is this repository's own worst habit run backwards
— a pointer moving ahead of its rule instead of behind it — and a lane reading a
superseded `BR-PAY-025` would stop building day × method grouping that is still, today,
exactly what the product does and must do. A dated forward note naming the three open
questions is added to the rule instead, which is true now and stops being needed the day
the re-key lands.

### 5 · THE LESSON, WHICH IS THE ONE THE BLUEPRINT ITSELF ASKS FOR

Both corrections came from **running the thing on a real PostgreSQL rather than reading
it**. The ledger half looked like work and was already done; the payments half looked
like one line of DDL and has a second unique key behind it. **A task table is a claim
about code, and a claim about code is re-verified by executing it** — which is exactly
what the document says about itself, and it was right.

**Nothing was built · nothing was written to any database · `P0.6` is blocked on
`counter_sessions` and on `OQ-PAY-12575` / `OQ-PAY-12576` / `OQ-PAY-12577`.**

### ⚠ AMENDED THE SAME HOUR — `counter_sessions` LANDED WHILE THIS WAS BEING WRITTEN, AND ONE SENTENCE ABOVE IS ALREADY STALE

The section above says *"`P0.6`'s DDL half is blocked on `counter_sessions`… It does
not exist on the branch at `ca6557b16`"*. **It exists now.** LANE P0-DB pushed
`76c24705f` — `payments/0030` (the source check), **`payments/0031` (`counter_sessions`)**
and `payments/0032` (its RLS) — between this lane's first push attempt and its second,
and `10-scripts/push_paths.sh` refused the first attempt on exactly that staleness.
**The table is no longer the blocker. The three questions are.**

**AND THE TABLE THAT LANDED IS EVIDENCE ON ONE OF THEM.** `counter_sessions.counted_totals`
is `{payment_method_id: "1240.0000"}` — **a till is counted PER TENDER**, so one session
holds cash and cheques at once. `deposit_batches.method_id` is NOT NULL. **So the
ruling's *"one batch per session"* and the schema cannot both be satisfied**: under a
strict `(tenant, session)` key Dana cannot bank her cheques and her cash on the two
slips a bank actually takes. That is `OQ-PAY-12577`, and the landed table makes the
case for `(tenant, session, method)` stronger without answering it — the PO said *"one
batch per session"* in those words, and narrowing a ruling is theirs, not ours.

⚠ **NOTHING ELSE ABOVE MOVES.** The ledger measurement was taken against
`apps/ledger/`, which those three migrations do not touch; none of them touches
`deposit_batches` at all; and `uq_deposit_batches_code` is exactly as it was. **Only the
blocker changed, and it is recorded here rather than by editing the sentence above**,
so the record still shows what was true when the measurement was taken.

⚠ **AND THE LESSON IS THE FILE'S OWN, EARNED RATHER THAN QUOTED:** this row named a
blocker that stopped being true **within the hour**, and the only reason it did not rot
is that the push helper refused a stale base and forced a re-read. **A blocker is a
claim about another lane's work, and it is the shortest-lived kind of claim this
repository writes down.**

## 2026-09-22 — `P0.7` BUILT: THE POSTING DAY A PAYMENTS SCREEN PROPOSES IS NOW THE UTILITY'S OWN DAY

The payments blueprint's phase-0 row `P0.7` is built on `claude/laughing-thompson-kpmwih`.

**What was wrong, in one sentence with the figure:** the Record-payment form filled in
today's date from the clock in **UTC**, so a clerk finishing a shift at **17:30 in
UTC−7** was offered **tomorrow's date** — 23 September while it was still the 22nd where
they were standing — and every payment they took in the last six and a half hours of
that shift went into the books under the wrong day.

**What changed:** five date fields across two screens now read the day from the utility's
own timezone, which is the one already set on Settings → Company → Regional and the one
every date on screen is already displayed in.

⚠ **NOTHING ALREADY RECORDED MOVES — PO ruling 2026-09-22, verbatim: *"Going forward
only"*.** That is also the only lawful answer available: a payment's posting date is
frozen by CLAUDE.md hard rule 4 and is not one of the three columns `payments/0014`
lets a correction touch, so restamping an old payment would have to be a new row and
could never be an edit. **No backfill was written and none may be.**

### THE LANE JUDGMENT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WENT THE OTHER WAY FROM THE TASK'S WORDING

`P0.7` is written as *"`isoToday()` reads the tenant timezone"*, which reads as an
instruction to give that function an argument. **It was DELETED instead**, and its
callers now use `todayInZone(timeZone)` from the shared kit (`components/DateCell.tsx`).

**Why:** that function already existed and already did exactly this job. It was written
on 2026-09-04 for `DEF-MET-4991`, when three asset date fields proposed no date at all,
and its own docstring names this bug in the abstract — *"`todayIso()` in
`billingOpsShared` slices an ISO instant, which is UTC … wrong for a bound where a
tenant behind UTC would be refused their own today for several hours each evening."*
Two functions answering *what day is it here* is how two screens come to disagree about
a utility's business day, which is what B14 rule 43 is for.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND IT IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME BUG

**The WRITE half is untouched and is still wrong.** `apps/payments/api._moment` anchors
a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` at **midnight UTC** and says so in its own docstring; that is
`DEF-094`, it is backend, and it belongs to another lane. `OQ-153` was CLOSED on
2026-08-12 in favour of *midnight in the utility's own timezone*, so the rule is settled
and only the code is behind.

**`billingOpsShared.todayIso()` is the same UTC slice one module over** and was
deliberately left alone: its callers stamp a write rather than propose a bound, and it
is not this lane's file.

### THE STALE SENTENCES THIS FIX HAD TO CORRECT FIRST (step W)

`PaymentsPage.tsx` carried, in a comment beside the code, *"the tenant timezone cannot be
chosen yet, so nobody may claim to know the utility's business day"*, citing `OQ-153` and
`DEF-082` as open. **Both were closed five weeks ago** — the ruling on 2026-08-12 and the
Settings control on 2026-08-15 — and the comment was the reason the UTC slice looked
defensible to every reader since. It is rewritten rather than deleted, so the next reader
can see what was believed and when it stopped being true.

### THE PROOF, AND WHY IT IS TWO ZONES AND NOT ONE

`07-frontend/src/features/payments/postingDayInTenantZone.dom.test.tsx` pins ONE instant
— `2026-09-23T00:30:00Z` — and renders the screen twice, once for a utility in UTC−7 and
once for one in UTC+10, asserting they are offered **different days**: 22 September and
23 September. A single-zone assertion would pass on any machine whose own clock agreed,
and would go on passing forever if someone reinstated the UTC slice while the suite ran
in UTC. **RED PROVED FIRST, in vitest, the harness that runs it:** against the pre-fix
code the UTC−7 case failed with `expected '2026-09-23' to be '2026-09-22'`.

⚠ **THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT TEST'S FOURTH CASE WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT AND IS RECORDED
BECAUSE IT IS LAW 7's OWN SHAPE.** It grepped the page's SOURCE for the UTC expression —
and matched the comment that explains why the expression is gone, so it went red over a
file that was already correct. A text scan cannot tell code from prose about code. It
asks the module's exported shape instead.

## 2026-09-22 — THE DEPOSIT BATCH GETS A UNIQUENESS MECHANISM, EVERY BATCH HAS A TILL INCLUDING A SYSTEM ONE, AND A BATCH IS ONE TILL × ONE TENDER

Three PO answers that unblock `P0.6`, each put with a worked case and lettered
options. They close the three questions `LANE P0-BATCH` minted rather than guessed
(`OQ-PAY-12575`, `OQ-PAY-12576`, `OQ-PAY-12577`).

### 1 · A MECHANISM, NOT A LONGER STRING — `OQ-PAY-12575`

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"we need to build mecanism to get unique number"*.

**THE PROBLEM, MEASURED ON A LIVE POSTGRESQL 16 BY `LANE P0-BATCH`:** `deposit_batches`
carries a SECOND unique key nobody had named — `uq_deposit_batches_code` on
`(tenant, code)` — and the code is composed from the day and the tender ALONE. With
the drawing's change applied and nothing else, Dana's **$1,240** cheque session banked
and Sam's **$880** cheque session **died** on `duplicate key value violates unique
constraint "uq_deposit_batches_code"`. **So the drawn hazard is not the real one:**
`P0.6` warns that a dropped key with no replacement lets two batches collide
*silently*, and what actually happens is that **the second person to work a counter
that day cannot bank at all, loudly**, on a constraint the task row never mentions.

⚠ **THE CODE DOES NOT COME FROM SETTINGS, AND THE SETTINGS SCREEN IMPLIES THAT IT
DOES.** `reconciliation.py`'s own docstring: *"BR-TEN-035's format grammar has no
method token and REQUIRES a sequence token, so the composed code cannot be stored in a
`number_series` row at all."* A `DEP-` series exists on Settings → Numbering and the
banking code ignores it. **That divergence is a finding in its own right** and is
recorded here so the next reader does not spend an hour looking for the format in the
wrong place.

⚠ **THIS EXACT FAULT HAS HAPPENED ONCE AND THE PO ALREADY RULED ON IT, WHICH IS WHY
THE FIX IS THE SAME SHAPE.** `DEP-{MMDD}-{METHOD}` carried no year, so 8 Aug 2026 and
8 Aug 2027 rendered identically and *"no tenant could bank money on its go-live
anniversary"*. PO ruling 2026-08-12, verbatim *"Add the year + Date is important"*
(`OQ-162`, `DEF-066`). **The code was missing a dimension and the dimension was
added.** It is missing one again — WHICH TILL — and the same answer applies.

**WHAT IS TO BE BUILT — and the word the PO used is `mechanism`, deliberately:** a
per-`(tenant, day, tender)` counter rendering `DEP-260922-CHK-01`, `-02`, so the code
reads *"the second cheque banking of the 22nd"*. ⚠ **A COUNTER COMPUTED BY COUNTING
EXISTING ROWS IS A RACE, AND THE MECHANISM IS WHAT MAKES IT SAFE, NOT THE
ARITHMETIC:** two clerks closing tills in the same second both read the same maximum.
`uq_deposit_batches_code` is the GUARANTEE — allocate inside the transaction, let the
unique key refuse a duplicate, and retry. The index is not a safety net behind the
mechanism; **it is the mechanism**, exactly as `payments/0014`'s reasoning has it (a
Python check is not a guarantee against a second caller). Prove it with two concurrent
closes on PostgreSQL, not with a unit test on SQLite, which has neither the index's
behaviour nor real concurrency.

### 2 · EVERY BATCH HAS A TILL, AND ELECTRONIC MONEY GETS A SYSTEM ONE — `OQ-PAY-12576`

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"we have to make process uniform for all hence we should
geneate system generated till"*, choosing **(b)**.

**The question:** yesterday's ruling says every new batch must have a session, but the
job that cuts batches handles SEVEN tenders and four of them — **ACH, card, wire,
lockbox** — never touch a counter. The worked case: a utility takes **$14,280 of ACH**
on a Tuesday, with no clerk, no drawer and no till. Built exactly as ruled, a utility
**could not bank its electronic takings at all.**

**So: a SYSTEM-GENERATED till.** Every batch has a session, the guard stays one
sentence — *a batch has a session* — with no tender-by-tender exception, and the
uniqueness mechanism above works the same way for all seven tenders. **That uniformity
is the PO's stated reason and it is the right one:** an exception list is a thing that
rots, and four tenders' worth of special case would have had to be remembered by every
future lane.

⚠ **A SYSTEM TILL MUST BE VISIBLY A SYSTEM TILL, AND THIS IS THIS LANE'S JUDGMENT
RATHER THAN THE PO'S INSTRUCTION.** Phase 2's own *done when* is *"a clerk opens a
counter at 08:55, takes seventeen payments, closes it at 17:30 with a counted drawer,
**and a supervisor can see the three tills nobody counted**."* If electronic money
opens sessions, **those sessions would appear in that list and a supervisor would
chase four tills that no human was ever at.** So a system session is marked as one,
and every screen that asks *who has not counted their drawer* excludes them. It also
never carries an opening float, is never force-closed by a System Admin (there is
nobody to close for), and its `close_kind` is its own value — the forced-close ruling
of today is about a person's till and does not reach these.

### 3 · A BATCH IS ONE TILL × ONE TENDER — `OQ-PAY-12577`

**PO answer:** **(a)**, together with a question back — *"whta is till and what is
tender?"* — which is answered to them in plain words and is recorded here because
**the vocabulary is the thing the three questions turned on**:

| Word | What it means here |
|---|---|
| **Till** | One person's session at one counter — Dana, counter 2, 08:00 to 17:00. Opened, taken money into, counted, closed |
| **Tender** | HOW the money arrived — cash, cheque, money order, ACH, card, wire, lockbox. Seven of them |

**So one till holds several tenders**, and Dana's Tuesday shift taking **$600 cash and
$640 cheques** is **one till and two tenders, $1,240 in total**.

**A batch is ONE TILL × ONE TENDER**, so that shift produces **TWO batches** — $600 and
$640. **The reason is the bank, not the product:** a bank credits cash and cheques
separately and they clear on different days, so a single $1,240 line could never be
reconciled against a statement.

⚠ **THIS REFINES YESTERDAY'S *"one batch per session"* AND DOES NOT REVERSE IT.** One
session is still one clerk's shift; what is settled is that the bank sees it as one
deposit per tender. ⚠ **AND `counter_sessions` IS EVIDENCE FOR IT RATHER THAN AGAINST
IT** — `LANE P0-DB` built it storing **counted totals keyed by tender**, which is the
shape of a till that holds cash and cheques at once. The table does not change.

## 2026-09-22 — THE SOURCE COLUMN KEEPS THE WORDS IT WAS BORN WITH, THE BLUEPRINT'S FIRST DERIVATION IS WRONG ABOUT 74 OF 74 ROWS, AND A TILL CAN NOW BE WRITTEN

`CR-135-BRC07`, phase 0 tasks `P0.1`–`P0.5` and `P0.14`–`P0.17` of
`05-prototype/06 Payments Page Blueprint.pdf`. Version `2.329.0`. Phase 0 ships
no screen, no endpoint and no service — PO ruling of this date, *"go as per
phase 0 ; we are going to implement all phases one by one so fcus on current
one."*

Three judgments were ours to make under CLAUDE.md hard-won law 13. Each is
recorded here with what was measured, because the rules ran out and a question
would have been the failure to decide.

### 1 · THE STORED VALUES DO NOT MOVE — `entry · webhook · import` KEEP THEIR WORDS

**The ruling being applied**, PO, this morning: *"(a) One column — extend what
we shipped — Rename or map the three values, add the check the blueprint
wants."* **Both halves were offered and this is the MAP.** What follows is why,
because the PO delegated the choice and a delegated choice that is not written
down is a coin toss the next lane cannot audit.

**The correctness argument, which is the one that decided it.** The blueprint's
three words describe the three CHANNELS money arrives by. The shipped three
describe HOW THE ROW WAS CREATED, which is a wider set that includes rows where
no money arrived at all:

  * `apps/payments/transfer.py` writes `entry` for **both legs of an internal
    transfer** — money moving between two accounts we already hold.
  * `apps/payments/reversal.py` writes `entry` for a **bounce**.
  * `record_payment` writes it for a **goodwill credit**.

Renaming `entry → counter` would make the database state, of every one of
those, *this was taken at a service desk*. That is false. `entry` says *a
person keyed this row*, which is true of all of them.

**Three supporting reasons, each measured.**

  * **The values are the idempotency key's own three, deliberately.**
    `apps/payments/idempotency.py` composes `"<source>|<reference>"` with
    exactly `entry · webhook · import`, and **four creation sites pass that
    segment straight through** as `origin=idempotency_source`
    (`services.py:1136`, `transfer.py:966` and `:987`, `reversal.py:1369`).
    Renaming the column without renaming the key prefixes — which are a UNIQUE
    key and 🔒 Eng-Lead delegated mechanics under `BR-PAY-028` — would put two
    vocabularies for one fact inside the money module, which is the *two places
    that can disagree* shape `payments/0029` was written to close.
  * **A rename is an UPDATE on 74 cleared payments** and therefore a second
    unnecessary visit to `trg_payment_immutable`, on a table that blocked the
    Product Owner's release this morning for exactly that reason
    (`DEF-PAY-6165`).
  * **Nobody would see the difference.** B14 rule 31 — no database value is the
    visible value of a field. `payments.reversal_reason` already stores
    `bank_chargeback` and the screen says *Bank chargeback*. The blueprint's own
    §03 tab 2 sets the Source filter's class to `SIGNED` and sources it from
    *"`payments.source`'s CHECK — three values"*; the CHECK supplies the three
    values and the CATALOGUE supplies the three words, which is how every other
    picker in this product already works.

**The map, written down once** (`apps/payments/models.PAYMENT_ORIGINS`):

| stored | the blueprint's word | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| `entry` | Counter | a person keyed it |
| `webhook` | Digital | it arrived over a wire |
| `import` | Post | it came in a file or a batch |

⚠ **THE RIGHT-HAND COLUMN IS NOT BUILT AND IS NOT THIS LANE'S.** It is a label
and belongs in the i18n catalogue, which is `07-frontend/` — LANE P0-FE's
territory this phase, and the Source column itself is phase 2 (`2·1`). It is
written here so the lane that builds it does not re-derive it.

### 2 · THE BLUEPRINT'S FIRST DERIVATION MISCLASSIFIES 74 OF 74 ROWS, AND THE SECOND IS BETTER THAN WHAT SHIPPED

`P0.2`, verbatim: *"Derive it: non-null `webhook_key` → digital · named by a
`payment_import_rows.payment_id` → post · otherwise counter."*

**MEASURED**, not reasoned — on a PostgreSQL 16 clone of the demo database
(`sbh_clone_p0db`, template stamp `bc23a826`), inside the tenant context,
because `payments` carries RLS **FORCE** and an unscoped count answers 0:

| | |
|---|---|
| payments in the tenant | **74** |
| with a non-null `webhook_key` | **74** |
| whose key prefix is `entry|` | **74** |
| named by a row in `payment_import_rows` | **0** |
| rows in `payment_import_rows` at all | **0** |

**So *non-null `webhook_key` → digital* would stamp all 74 as `digital`, and
every one of them is a keyed entry.** The reason is a column NAME: `webhook_key`
is the generic idempotency key and holds a key for all three sources. The
blueprint read the name; `payments/0029`'s shipped derivation reads the
contents and gets **74 of 74 right**. It stands unchanged.

**The SECOND clause is a genuine improvement and `payments/0030` applies it.** A
row in `payment_import_rows` naming the payment is an OBSERVED fact; a string
prefix is a label the importer chose. Where they disagree the link wins — but
**only where the origin was DERIVED or absent**, because an inference must never
overrule an observation. Rows it moves stay `origin_is_derived = TRUE`: derived
from a link rather than from a prefix, and still derived. That is the PO's
ruling of this morning held intact.

⚠ **ON TODAY'S DATA THAT PASS MOVES 0 ROWS OF 74, AND THE MIGRATION SAYS SO
RATHER THAN PRINTING `OK`.** It prints `74 visible, 0 re-derived` per tenant,
which is the pair CLAUDE.md hard-won law 7 asks for — *a declared blind spot
with no NUMBER attached is indistinguishable from an empty one*. `0 visible, 0
re-derived` is `DEF-PAY-6166`'s signature and is now a different line of output.
It is written anyway because the Product Owner's live deployment is demonstrably
not this database: it RAISED on `payments/0029` where this clone silently did
nothing.

### 3 · `NOT NULL` IS NOT ADDED, AND THE REASON IS A SIXTH CREATION SITE NOBODY HAD COUNTED

`P0.2`'s outcome asks for *"No nulls"*. `payments/0029` argued the column must
stay nullable because *"a fifth creation site added by a lane that has not read
this file would fail its INSERT"*.

**That site already exists and predates the argument.**
`apps/integrations/management/commands/seed_partner_morning.py:232`
bulk-creates `Payment` rows and passes **no origin at all** — a SIXTH site,
where `payments/0029`'s own `Impacts:` line counts four. Filed as
`DEF-PAY-6196`. A `NOT NULL` would have failed that command on the day it was
added, and CLAUDE.md hard-won law 3 says the unsafe option must be the one you
type.

**What `P0.2` actually buys is served instead: the FOURTH VALUE.**
`ck_payments_origin` refuses `'lockbox'` by name, from every path — *"fails
loudly rather than defaulting"*, delivered. And the *"no nulls"* half is
enforced **at merge rather than at 2am**, by an inventory test that fails
naming any seventh creation site.

A second CHECK, `ck_payments_origin_derived_needs_a_value`, refuses
`origin IS NULL AND origin_is_derived` — a row claiming to have inferred
nothing. That is the PO's *mark it as a derivation* ruling given teeth in the
one direction it could otherwise have rotted.

### 4 · THE TILL TABLE, AND THE ONE PLACE THE DRAWING IS NOT FOLLOWED

`counter_sessions` — `payments/0031`, with RLS in `payments/0032`. Six phase 2
screens wait on it. `close_kind` holds `counted` or `forced` and `closed_by`
records who actually sealed it, which on a forced close is not the owner: PO
ruling of this date, *"(b) A System Admin can close it, recorded as a forced
close"*.

⚠ **THE OPENING FLOAT IS `NUMERIC(18,4)` WHERE `P0.3` DRAWS `NUMERIC(18,6)`.**
CLAUDE.md hard rule 2, PO re-sign 2026-08-22, verbatim: *"We already confirmed
this - MOney 4 decimal, percentage 6 decimal , display both 2 decimal"*.
Existing `18,6` columns stay lawful containers; the rule governs what a NEW
column declares, and this one is new. It is `core.money_fields.money_field()`,
the single place that number is written down. Put to the Product Owner and
answered before this lane started, so it is NOT re-asked (hard-won law 13); it
is recorded here so a reader comparing the drawing with the schema finds the
answer rather than a discrepancy. In B14's terms it is rule 38's shape: where a
drawing and a signed rule disagree about CONSTRUCTION, the rule wins, because
the alternative changes a money column on one screen's authority.

**Three further constraints are this lane's own judgment**, each cheap and each
refusing a state that would otherwise have to be ignored by every reader:

  * `ck_counter_sessions_closed_together` — `closed_at`, `closed_by` and
    `close_kind` are all set or all null. **A till sealed with no record of HOW
    is a forced close that has become indistinguishable from a normal one**,
    which is the exact outcome the PO's ruling exists to prevent.
  * `ck_counter_sessions_close_kind` — `counted` or `forced`, and **`auto` is
    absent BY NAME**. The overnight self-close was put to the PO as a hole in
    the money trail and was not chosen; a value the column can hold is a value
    some path can write.
  * `ck_counter_sessions_float_not_negative` — a drawer that starts owing money.

`counted_totals` is a JSON map keyed by payment method, **holding STRINGS**:
hard rule 2 says never float, and a JSON number is a double in every serialiser
in this stack. `DjangoJSONEncoder` writes a `Decimal` as a string and the column
declares it. A method absent from the map was NOT COUNTED, which is p056's
*"you cannot count a card total in a drawer so the screen does not pretend"*
expressed in the shape rather than in a comment.

**No freeze trigger, and that is a judgment rather than an omission.**
`counter_receipts` has one because a receipt is evidence of money handed over. A
counter session is **designed to be updated once** — it opens with a float and
later takes five closing columns — and phase 2 adds a third write when a
supervisor-closed till is DECLARED after the fact (`3·3d`). Writing a freeze now
would be guessing which columns phase 2 may move, and a freeze that has to be
widened later is worse than one written when the write paths exist. It is
`BR-PAY-1160`'s open half and is named in the review-ledger row.

### 5 · WHAT WAS PROVED, AND ON WHAT

All on `sbh_clone_p0db`, PostgreSQL 16, role `smartbillhub`
(`rolsuper=f rolbypassrls=f`), because SQLite has no RLS and no triggers:

  * **forwards, backwards, forwards again** — `payments/0030`–`0032` applied,
    reversed to `0029`, re-applied. `trg_payment_immutable` read `'O'` at every
    stage and the 74 rows were unchanged throughout.

⚠ **THAT IS NOT `P0.16` CLEARED, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE OF IT.**
`P0.16`'s task line is *"migration forwards and backwards"* and its OUTCOME is
*"The deposit re-key is reversible"* — which is `P0.6`'s migration, and `P0.6`
is not built, is blocked on two PO decisions and is not this lane's. **So
`P0.16` stays OPEN.** What is proved is that the three migrations that EXIST
reverse. Writing a test that proved a migration nobody has written reverses
would be a check that cannot fail, which is the shape CLAUDE.md hard-won law 7
names; it was not written.
  * **every new constraint shown RED on the case it was written for and GREEN
    on the neighbouring lawful one** — a second OPEN till refused, a second
    CLOSED till permitted (`P0.15`'s easy-to-miss half), a half-closed till
    refused, `auto` refused, a negative float refused, `'lockbox'` refused, a
    lawful `import` accepted, `NULL` + `FALSE` accepted, `NULL` + `TRUE`
    refused.
  * **the claim `payments/0030` makes about RLS and DDL**, because a comment
    claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee (law 1). With `app.tenant_id`
    unset: `SELECT count(*) FROM payments` → **0**, and
    `ALTER TABLE payments ADD CONSTRAINT tmp CHECK (origin = 'nonsense')` →
    **`ERROR: check constraint "tmp" of relation "payments" is violated by some
    row`**. The tenant loop can be fooled by a bad scope; the constraint cannot.
    ⚠ And PostgreSQL says *"some row"* — never a count, never an id — so the
    constraint is a reliable refusal and a useless diagnosis.

### 6 · WHAT THIS LANE DID NOT DO, AND WHY

**`P0.6`, the deposit-batch re-key, was not started.** It waits on two PO
decisions that are still open — what happens to the batches already banked in

**The blueprint's migration numbers are all one lower than the files.** `P0.1`

## 2026-09-22 — THE DEPOSIT BATCH CODE COMES FROM SETTINGS → NUMBERING, AND THE SERIES IS ALREADY THERE

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"(b) Put it in Settings today — DEP-260922-0001 — Settings →
Numbering, like every other number"*, choosing between keeping the tender in the label
with the code composed in application code, and having the code configurable like
every other number in the product.

**THIS SUPERSEDES THE ANSWER THEY GAVE MINUTES EARLIER** — *"a) Add a counter —
DEP-260922-CHK-01"* — and the supersession is stated rather than assumed, because the
earlier one is also in this log. **What changed between the two was a measurement**,
not a preference: the format grammar allows four tokens (`{YYYY}` `{MM}` `{DD}` `{YY}`)
plus one counter and caps a format string at **24 characters**, and
`DEP-{YY}{MM}{DD}-{TENDER}-{00}` is **30** — even a one-letter token gives 25. So (a)
could never have lived in Settings without moving two signed rules, and the PO was
shown that and chose the shape that fits.

### ⚠ THE SERIES ALREADY EXISTS, ALREADY HAS A COUNTER, AND IS ALREADY SEEDED

Measured on a seeded PostgreSQL 16 tenant:

| series | format | restart |
|---|---|---|
| `deposit_batch` | **`DEP-{YY}{MM}{DD}-{00}`** | `never` |

**So (b) needs NO new series, NO seeding, and NO rule change.** The row is on the
tenant, configured, with exactly the shape the PO chose. **The banking code simply
ignores it and composes its own string.** That is the whole of the work: make the
banking path ALLOCATE from the series it already has.

⚠ **AND THE COMMENT THAT SENT US THE OTHER WAY WAS TRUE AND IS NOW OBSOLETE.**
`reconciliation.py` says *"BR-TEN-035's format grammar has no method token and REQUIRES
a sequence token, so the composed code cannot be stored in a `number_series` row at
all."* Every clause of that is correct **about a code containing the tender** — and it
reads as *the batch code cannot come from Settings*, which is now false, because the
tender is leaving the code. **Strike it in the same commit as the change** or it will
send the next lane straight back to composing a string by hand. This is CLAUDE.md's
most repeated failure — eight recorded occasions of a ruling landing while the
pointers to it did not move.

### TWO THINGS TO SET RIGHT WHILE THE PATH IS BEING CHANGED — THIS LANE'S JUDGMENT

⚠⚠ **BOTH OF THE TWO BELOW WERE WRONG, AND THEY ARE STRUCK RATHER THAN DELETED.
CORRECTED THE SAME DAY BY `LANE P0-BATCH-3`, WHICH MEASURED THEM INSTEAD OF
BELIEVING THEM — the full correction is the entry headed "P0.6 AS BUILT" below, and
what follows here is kept only so a reader who met the claim can find out that it
moved.** One was a false statement of fact; the other was a recommendation whose
stated reason was that same falsehood and which would have put a REFUSAL ON THE
BANKING PATH. ⚠ **AND THE SHAPE IS THIS FILE'S OWN, THREE LINES ABOVE ITS OWN
WARNING ABOUT IT** — this entry tells the next lane that a ruling landing while the
pointer to it does not move is *"CLAUDE.md's most repeated failure — eight recorded
occasions"*, and then left its own two claims unstamped for a reader to hit first.

**1 · ~~THE PAD IS TWO DIGITS AND THE COUNTER NEVER RESTARTS, SO IT RUNS OUT AT 99
BATCHES FOR THE LIFE OF THE TENANT.~~ FALSE.** It read: *"`{00}` with `restart: never`
is a counter that reaches `DEP-260922-99` and then cannot allocate."* **`core.numbering
.render` NEVER TRUNCATES — its own docstring says so — and `will_overflow` is read by
exactly one caller, a Settings screen field whose docstring says *"never a refusal"*.
Measured: `{00}` at 100 renders `DEP-260922-100`.** The pad is a MINIMUM WIDTH, not a
ceiling. ⚠ The conclusion happens to survive its own reasoning — the seeded default IS
`{0000}` — but **for a different and better reason: `DEP-260922-0001` is the number the
PO wrote.** A right answer reached by a wrong argument is not a right answer; the next
person to lean on the argument gets a wrong one.

**2 · ~~RESTART YEARLY, NOT NEVER.~~ DECLINED, AND THE DECLINE IS THE IMPORTANT
HALF.** It read: *"Four digits and no restart gives 9,999 batches for ever; a utility
banking four batches a day exhausts that in about ten years."* That arithmetic rests
on the same untruth as (1), **and it carried a cost this row never weighed:
`_allocate` refuses a BACKDATED issuance under a restart policy, by name,
`numbering_restart_backdated`.** So a utility cutting **last December's batch in
January** would have been **refused on the banking path** — a clerk stopped from
banking real money, to buy a cosmetic tidiness. **A live refusal on a money path is
never worth a cosmetic gain**, and the restart stays `never`.
⚠ **Neither is the PO's instruction and both are stated here as judgments** so they can
be overturned in one word. ⚠ And **existing tenants hold `{00}`/`never` in a row they
own** — a seeded default governs a NEW tenant, and changing what an existing tenant has
configured is a different act that nobody has ruled on. Report it; do not migrate it
silently.

### WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE

⚠ **EVERY BATCH ALREADY BANKED KEEPS ITS CODE.** `DEP-260808-CHK` is on a financial
record that CLAUDE.md hard rule 4 freezes, and `BR-PAY-004` locks a reconciled batch
outright. Old codes read one way and new ones read another, **which is the same
two-populations answer the PO gave for the legacy sessions** and is consistent with it.
⚠ **`BR-PAY-025` IS AMENDED, NOT REVERSED, AND THE 2026-08-12 RULING SURVIVES INTACT.**
That ruling was *"Add the year + Date is important"* — the year and the date are both
still in `DEP-{YY}{MM}{DD}-{0000}`. **Only the method token leaves.** Say so in the
amendment, because a reader seeing the format change will otherwise assume the August
ruling went with it.
⚠ **AND THE UNIQUENESS PROBLEM DISSOLVES RATHER THAN BEING SOLVED.** The counter is
allocated by the series, which is already race-safe and already used by thirty other
numbers; there is no per-day-per-tender counter to build and no retry loop to get
right. `OQ-PAY-12575` closes with this row.

## 2026-09-22 — BUILT: A DEPOSIT BATCH IS ONE TILL AND ONE TENDER, EVERY BATCH HAS A SESSION INCLUDING A SYSTEM ONE, AND THE CODE COMES FROM SETTINGS (`P0.6`, LANE P0-BATCH-3)

`CR-135-BRC07`, payments blueprint phase 0 task `P0.6`. Version **`2.330.0`**.
Migrations `payments/0033`. The four PO rulings of this date are built; the three
questions the earlier lane minted rather than guessed — `OQ-PAY-12575`,
`OQ-PAY-12576`, `OQ-PAY-12577` — are all CLOSED, status **and** body, in the same
commit as the code.

**WHAT A UTILITY CAN DO NOW THAT IT COULD NOT BEFORE.** At a two-counter office on
22 September, Dana takes **$1,240** of cheques and Sam takes **$880**. Until today
that was **one** deposit batch for the whole utility, which neither clerk could be
held to. It is now **two**, and the day still ties to **$2,120** exactly.

### WHAT WAS BUILT

| | |
|---|---|
| the key | `uq_deposit_batches_day_method` **dropped**; `UNIQUE (tenant, session, method) WHERE session_id IS NOT NULL` in its place |
| the guard | `trg_deposit_batch_needs_session` — a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger refusing a session-less batch, **at the database** |
| the system till | `counter_sessions` with no owner, no centre, no closer, no float, `close_kind = 'system'`, **born closed**, one per tenant per banking day |
| the code | ALLOCATED from the tenant's `deposit_batch` series — seeded `DEP-{YY}{MM}{DD}-{0000}`, rendering **`DEP-260922-0001`** |
| the ledger | **nothing changed**, and that is the finding rather than an omission |

### 1 · THE LEDGER HALF NEEDED NO CHANGE, AND IT WAS RUN RATHER THAN READ

The PO ruled *"(a) Payments and ledger together"* on the understanding that the
ledger would have to accept two deposits where it expected one. **It already
does.** A deposit's journal entry is keyed on the BATCH —
`deposit_batch|<uuid>|reconciled` — never on the day or the tender, so splitting
one deposit into two posts two entries with no code change anywhere in
`apps/ledger/`.

Proved on PostgreSQL 16 by `10-scripts/p06_ledger_two_deposits_readback.py`, which
posts through `apps.ledger.posting.post()` and nothing else and rolls back:
**Dana 1,240.00 debits = 1,240.00 credits · Sam 880.00 = 880.00 · the day
2,120.00 · zero rows left behind.** Hard rule 5 is enforced in the database by
`ledger_sole_writer_guard()`, which threw out the first draft of that proof for
writing a journal INSERT by hand; the guard was right and the draft was wrong.

**So this work writes not one journal line**, which is what *"payments and ledger
together, each writing its own tables"* means in practice.

### 2 · THE GUARD IS A TRIGGER AND NOT A `NOT NULL`, AND THE REASON IS THE PO'S OWN RULING

Ruling (d) — *"Tell them apart by what they lack"* — forbids touching a batch
already banked, and those batches have no session. **A `NOT NULL` is validated
against every existing row, so it would refuse to apply at all on any live
tenant**; forcing it through would mean inventing a session for money nobody took
at a counter, which is the option the PO rejected. A `BEFORE INSERT` trigger asks
the question only of rows being born, which is exactly what the ruling describes:
the legacy population is closed and nothing may join it.

It is at the database rather than in the service under `BR-SHL-025` and
`payments/0014`'s own reasoning — *a Python check is not a guarantee against a
repair script with a cursor*.

### 3 · THE SYSTEM TILL IS OPENLY NOBODY'S, AND THAT IS THE PO'S OWN SHAPE ONE STEP ON

`counter_sessions.owner` and `service_centre` were NOT NULL. A system till has
neither, and **pointing one at a real user would record that that person ran a
till they never sat at** — the invention the PO rejected as option (b) for the
legacy batches, four hours earlier. So `owner IS NULL` means *nobody sat here*,
which is the vocabulary `deposit_batch_events.actor` has used since W5 (NULL = a
job did this).

**It is born CLOSED, and that is what keeps it off the supervisor's screen.**
Phase 2's *done when* is *"a supervisor can see the three tills nobody counted"*,
and that list asks `closed_at IS NULL`. A till closed from its first moment never
answers it — so the screen needs no knowledge of system tills and cannot drift out
of step with this rule. There is nothing to force-close either.

`ck_counter_sessions_system_is_nobodys` makes it two-way: a `system` till may name
no person and carry no float, **and a till that is not `system` must have an
owner** — so nothing can write an ownerless `counted` session and lose who is
accountable for a drawer. It is spelled as a membership test rather than
`NOT (close_kind = 'system')`, because `close_kind` is NULL on an open till,
`NOT (NULL = 'system')` is NULL, and **a CHECK evaluating to NULL passes** — the
negation would have been a check that cannot fail on the one row it was written
for.

⚠ **THIS CHANGED LANE P0-DB's TABLE, WHICH THIS LANE WAS TOLD NOT TO DO, AND IT
COULD NOT BE AVOIDED.** `deposit_batches.session_id` must point at ONE table, so a
system till has to be a `counter_sessions` row; the ruling's guard is one sentence
with no exception. The changes are additive and the table ships EMPTY and unwritten
(*"Written by nothing yet — phase 0 ships no service"*), so no data is at risk:
`owner` and `service_centre` nullable, a `system_day` column, a third `close_kind`,
and `ck_counter_sessions_closed_together` **widened by one branch** to permit a
NULL `closed_by` when and only when the close kind is `system`. Its intent is
unchanged — *a sealed till always records HOW it was sealed* — and a forced close
still names a person. `counted_totals`, `difference`, `note` and the
one-open-till-per-person index are untouched.

### 4 · TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT CORRECT THE CLOSING ROW'S OWN JUDGMENTS

The row that closed `OQ-PAY-12575` carried two judgments, both flagged as
overturnable in one word. **One is taken and one is not, and both because the same
claim was measured.**

That row says `{00}` with `restart: never` *"reaches `DEP-260922-99` and then
cannot allocate at all"*. ⚠ **IT DOES NOT.** `core.numbering.render`'s own
docstring says *"a counter that outgrows its pad keeps all its digits (never
truncated)"*, and `will_overflow` — the only thing that notices — is read by one
caller, a Settings **screen field**, with the docstring *"this is a WARNING the
screen raises, never a refusal: refusing would stop a bill run over cosmetics"*.
Measured: `{00}` at 100 renders **`DEP-260922-100`**, unique and lawful.

| judgment | taken? | why |
|---|---|---|
| pad `{00}` → `{0000}` | **YES** | not because `{00}` runs out — it does not — but because **`DEP-260922-0001` is the number the PO wrote in their own ruling.** Measured: renders `DEP-260922-0001` at 1 and `DEP-260922-10000` at ten thousand |
| restart `never` → `yearly` | **NO** | its stated reason (*"9,999 batches for ever"*) is the same untruth. And it has a cost the row did not weigh: `_allocate` refuses a **backdated** issuance under a restart policy with `numbering_restart_backdated`, so a utility cutting last December's batch in January would be **refused by name on the banking path**. A cosmetic gain is not worth a live refusal on a money path |

⚠ **EXISTING TENANTS HOLD `{00}`/`never` IN A ROW THEY OWN AND ARE NOT MIGRATED.**
`_seed_number_series` is `get_or_create` per series, so a configured row keeps ITS
format and ITS counter; a seeded default governs a NEW tenant. They still bank
correctly, for the reason above. **Reported, not rewritten** — changing what a
utility has configured is a different act and nobody has ruled on it.

### 5 · THE 2026-08-12 RULING SURVIVES INTACT, AND ONLY THE METHOD TOKEN LEFT

*"Add the year + Date is important"* (`OQ-162`, `DEF-066`). **The year and the date
are both still in `DEP-{YY}{MM}{DD}-{0000}`** — measured, `DEP-260808-0005` in 2026
against `DEP-270808-0006` in 2027, so the anniversary defect stays fixed. What left
is the TENDER, because two tills banking cheques on one day both rendered
`DEP-260922-CHK` and `uq_deposit_batches_code` refused the second. The tender lives
in the `method` column it always had — the PO's own *"a code is a label, never a
data store"*.

**The comment that said this was impossible is struck in the same commit**, in both
places it appeared (`reconciliation.py`'s module docstring and its lifecycle
exception 8): *"BR-TEN-035's format grammar has no method token and REQUIRES a
sequence token, so the composed code cannot be stored in a `number_series` row at
all."* Every clause was true **of a code containing the tender** and it read as
*the batch code cannot come from Settings*, which is now false. `batch_code` and
`method_token` are deleted rather than left to be found by the next lane.

### 6 · `payments/0014`'s TENDER REFUSAL STANDS; ONLY ITS REASON MOVED

Ruling (a) on `OQ-PAY-12577` keeps a batch at ONE tender, so the refusal *"the
tender cannot be corrected while it is banked"* is still TRUE and still fires. Its
stated reason was *"deposits are grouped by day AND tender"*, which was about to
become false, so both triggers are re-emitted in `payments/0033` with **one
sentence corrected** — *grouped by TILL and tender* — and
`payments_deposit_batch_lock`'s identity sentence now names the till.

⚠ **HARD RULE 4's ALLOW LIST DID NOT MOVE.** `mutable` and `stamps` are
byte-identical to `payments/0014`'s; the bodies were extracted from the deployed
files programmatically rather than retyped, and the reverse of `payments/0033`
restores `payments/0005`'s and `payments/0014`'s wording verbatim. CLAUDE.md is
explicit that `payments/0014` is the only place that list moves, and it has not.

### 7 · WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY

* **No data migration, which the drawing asks for.** `P0.6` says *"⚠ A data
  migration, not just DDL — existing batches ARE day × method."* The drawing was
  written before the question reached the PO, and their ruling (d) is that nothing
  is written to those rows. The absence is the fact.
* **No screen, no endpoint, no service.** Phase 0 ships none — PO, *"go as per
  phase 0"*. The Counter screens are phase 2.
* **`payments.counter_session_id` is NOT added.** It is phase 2's, arriving with
  the screens that open and close a till. Until then `reconciliation._session_for`
  answers *the day's system till* for **every** tender, not just the four
  electronic ones — which is honest rather than a stand-in, because no drawer has
  ever been counted in this product and a system till records exactly that. It is
  the one function phase 2 changes.
* **`P0.16` is not closed by this lane** — *"the deposit re-key is reversible"* is
  LANE P0-DB's, and `payments/0033` is the migration it was waiting for.

### 2 · `DEF-PAY-6202` — A DOCSTRING ON THE MONEY PATH NAMED A TABLE THAT DOES NOT EXIST

`import_runs.py`'s eighth-target block said *"`WRITE_MODES_BY_TARGET` offers this
target ONE mode"*. **There is no such table.** `WRITE_MODES` is a flat tuple of two
modes with no target in it, and the narrowing is a FUNCTION,
`_refuse_payments_write_mode`, which refuses `upsert` for this target by name from the
one helper both entry points already call.

**The behaviour was right and tested the whole time** — what was false was the
mechanism a reader was sent to look for. That is hard-won law 1 exactly, and the cure
is CLAUDE.md's own, twice recorded: **where a rule restates what a tool does, name the
tool and let a reader run it.** Nothing in this repository checks that an identifier
named in a docstring exists, which is why it was found by reading the module's
by-target tables one at a time rather than by any gate.

### 3 · `DEF-MET-6203` — A GUARD HAD BEEN RED FOR FOUR DAYS AND NOBODY HAD READ IT

`test_the_accounts_load_bar_is_100_rows_and_the_default_is_untouched` asserted
`async_row_bar(TARGET_PREMISES, "load") == 5_000`. That was true when it was written on
**2026-09-11** (`28dee3b8b`); `DEF-MET-5756` gave premises its own measured bar of
**500** on **2026-09-18** (`3d37b2ce4`) and moved the table without moving the
assertion. Both dates are `git log -S` on the symbol rather than recollection, which is
the habit CLAUDE.md added after two lanes called the same red pre-existing in good
faith and the second was the lane that caused it.

It has failed on every run since — in a file whose other fourteen cases pass and which
takes **four minutes forty-seven seconds**. That is law 7's commonest shape, *proved
red then never read*, and a long suite is where a true red goes to hide.

### 4 · `DEF-PAY-6204` — THE BAR GUARD COULD ONLY SEE ONE TARGET OUT OF EIGHT

`DEF-2487` added `test_every_bar_divides_into_the_web_worker_timeout_with_margin` so
that no load bar would ever again be applied to a per-row cost nobody had measured. It
read **one** bar — accounts — against **one** constant, and passed truthfully over
everything else. That is law 7's hardest shape: *a declared blind spot with no NUMBER
attached is indistinguishable from an empty one.*

**So the eighth target reached the branch with a bar and no figure, and this is that
figure.** Measured on a PostgreSQL 16 clone migrated to the tip, `app.tenant_id` set,
and **every row confirmed WRITTEN** — a load that rejects is fast and means nothing,
so the benchmark refuses rather than quoting a cost when `created != rows`:

| rows | load | ms/row | created |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 4.51s | 90.2 | 50 |
| 100 | 8.87s | 88.7 | 100 |
| 200 | 17.81s | **89.0** | 200 |
| 400 | 36.61s | 91.5 | 400 |

**Flat across an eightfold range, so it is a per-row cost and not a fixed overhead** —
and it is **accounts-shaped (94 ms/row), not premises-shaped (2.03)**, which is what a
row that walks the match ladder, creates a payment through payments' own writer and
writes an audit row was always going to be.

⚠ **THE BAR IS NOT MOVED, AND THE REASON MATTERS: THE STAGE DEFAULT'S OWN REASONING IS
CONFIRMED RATHER THAN REFUTED.** `ASYNC_ROW_BAR_BY_STAGE["load"] = 200` was chosen
deliberately to fail closed — its comment says *"200 is the worst measured load's bar,
not the best"* and works 200 × 94 ms = 18.8s against the 20.0s a third of the request
allows. Payments came out at **17.8s at the bar**. The default did its job, on a target
that did not exist when it was written.

⚠ **BUT 1.1x IS THE TIGHTEST MARGIN IN THE TABLE** — accounts has 2.1x, premises 19.7x
— **and the figure was taken on a box running four other lanes' suites against the same
PostgreSQL.** The premises entry already states the rule that applies: *a contended
figure is not a per-row cost.* So the honest position is that 1.1x is now written down
rather than inferred, and `10-scripts/pay_p1_1_load_bar_benchmark.py` on a quiet box is
what would settle it. **If the true cost is above 100 ms/row the bar belongs at 100,
beside accounts.**

**WHAT CHANGED, AND IT CHANGES NO BEHAVIOUR.** `(TARGET_PAYMENTS, "load"): 200` is now
an explicit row carrying the measurement — 200 is what the stage default already
resolved to — and the guard walks **every** target that declares a bar, refuses one
with no measured figure **by name**, and PRINTS what it skipped beside what it checked:

    load bars checked against a measured per-row cost:
      accounts: 100 rows x 94 ms = 9.4s (2.1x inside 20.0s)
      payments: 200 rows x 89.0 ms = 17.8s (1.1x inside 20.0s)
      premises: 500 rows x 2.03 ms = 1.0s (19.7x inside 20.0s)
    NOT checked — no bar of their own, inheriting the stage default of 200 rows,
    none of them ever timed: ['assets_devices', 'assets_meters',
    'assets_submeters', 'parts', 'units']

**Five targets still have a bar nobody has timed. That is now a printed number instead
of an absence**, which is the whole of what law 7 asks for.

**PROVED RED FIRST, IN PYTEST, BOTH WAYS**, then the proof was deleted rather than left
lying in the suite: a target with a bar and no figure fails naming `units`, and the
payments bar raised to 500 fails with *"500 payments rows at 89.0 ms/row is 44.5s

is NULL.** With `close_kind` NULL that branch reads `NULL = 'system'` → NULL,
so the whole chain is `FALSE OR FALSE OR NULL` = NULL and **the row is
accepted**. Measured both ways on 2026-09-22 rather than reasoned: PostgreSQL
16.13 accepted an INSERT with `closed_at` set and `close_kind` and `closed_by`
NULL, and a hand-built SQLite probe of the same expression accepted it too.

**So a till can once again be sealed with no record of how — which is the exact
outcome the PO's forced-close ruling of this morning exists to prevent**, and
the constraint that gave it teeth is off on the real database.

The only thing that asks the question is
`test_cr135_p0_foundations.py::test_p0_3_a_till_cannot_be_sealed_with_no_record_of_how`,
which went red when `P0.6` landed and was pushed red — law 7's
*proved-red-then-never-read*, one more time, on a constraint rather than a
gate. **The case is deliberately NOT weakened to make the suite green**; it
carries the defect id and the measurement in its own docstring.

**The cure is one clause** — begin the system branch `close_kind IS NOT NULL
AND close_kind = 'system'`, so a NULL makes the branch FALSE rather than NULL.
It is not applied here because `payments/0033` is another lane's migration and
was landing while this was measured; changing an in-flight money migration from
a second lane is how two lanes revert each other (law 11).

**The general lesson is worth more than the fix, and it is new to this repo:
adding a branch to an OR'd CHECK can only ever make it WEAKER, and a branch
that compares a NULLABLE column to a literal weakens it to nothing for every
row where that column is NULL.** The three-value logic does the damage
silently: no error, no warning, and a constraint that still reads correctly to
a person.

### 5 · REDS THAT WERE NOT THIS LANE'S, DATED

Gate suite in this worktree: **73 PASS, 53 FAIL, 5 SKIP**. It differs from the
74/55/2 quoted at hand-over because a worktree has no `.gate-record`, so
`run_gates` printed *"NOTHING TO COMPARE — no record existed before this
run"* and three gates skipped where they had failed.

  were CR-135's and are fixed here. 10 remain and are other modules'; the

### 8 · AMENDED THE SAME DAY — `G44` NAMED A FILE OF MINE AFTER I HAD REPORTED THAT NONE OF THE RED GATES WAS

The report this entry closes said, of the failing gates, that **none was newly

```
07-frontend/src/components/SelectionToolbar.tsx:134  [money] props.total

```

a NEW entry above a banked ratchet of 20.

**The finding is genuine and was not argued with.** `G44` classifies an

across `OutstandingsTab.test.tsx` and `ageingCards.dom.test.tsx`.

**This is not a classifier dodged.** The test applied was whether the rename
would be worth making if the gate did not exist, and it is: the docstring
already said *already rendered* while the name said *total*, and the name is
what a caller reads. `G44` now reports **37** untreated where it reported 38,

**The durable part is the scope of the claim, not the rename.** *"None of the

say none of them is yours**, and if the answer is a tier, say the number.

## 2026-09-22 — `DEF-PAY-6207` FIXED, AND THERE WERE **TWO** CONSTRAINTS RATHER THAN THE ONE THAT WAS FILED (`payments/0034`, LANE P0-BATCH-3)

Version **`2.331.1`** — the FIX digit. Filed by LANE P0-DB, who measured it and
**deliberately did not fix it**, because `payments/0033` belongs to this lane and
*"changing another lane's in-flight money migration from this lane is how two
lanes revert each other."* That restraint is why this was a defect row and a red
test rather than a collision, and it is worth recording as the right call.

### THE RULE, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX AND IS NEW TO THIS REPO

> **A CHECK constraint refuses a row only when its expression is FALSE, and
> PASSES when the expression is NULL.**
>
> So **adding a branch to an OR'd CHECK can only ever make it WEAKER**, and a
> branch that compares a **NULLABLE** column to a literal **weakens it to
> nothing** for every row where that column is NULL.

`FALSE OR FALSE OR NULL` is NULL, and NULL is accepted. `payments/0033` added
exactly that branch — `close_kind = 'system'` — to make the system till
storable, and switched the constraint off for every row with a NULL
`close_kind`.

### ⚠ THE FILED ROW NAMES ONE CONSTRAINT. CHECKING THE OTHERS FOUND A SECOND

The coordinator's instruction was *"check the other two branches for the same
shape while you are in there"*, and it paid:
**`ck_counter_sessions_system_is_nobodys` had the identical fault** and is not
in the defect row. Both are fixed in `payments/0034`, together, so neither can
come back alone.

| | what the hole accepted | what it costs |
|---|---|---|
| `ck_counter_sessions_closed_together` | `closed_at` set · `close_kind` NULL · `closed_by` NULL | **a till sealed with no record of how or by whom** — the exact outcome the PO's ruling of today exists to prevent |
| `ck_counter_sessions_system_is_nobodys` | `system_day` set · `close_kind` NULL · no owner | **an OPEN system till** — `closed_at` NULL, so it answers `ix_counter_sessions_open` and appears on the *"which tills are open"* screen: a drawer a supervisor would chase that nobody ever sat at |

The second is this lane's own design being broken by this lane's own migration.
A system till is **born closed** precisely so that screen never sees one, and
the NULL branch let an open one through.

### THE CURE, AND WHY IT IS A NEW MIGRATION

One clause each: `close_kind IS NOT NULL AND close_kind = 'system'`, so a NULL
makes the branch **FALSE** rather than NULL.

⚠ **`payments/0033` IS NOT EDITED, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** It is already
APPLIED — the proof templates carry it and other lanes have cloned them.
Editing an applied migration leaves `django_migrations` saying it ran while the
broken constraint stays in the database **for ever, on exactly the hosts that
already have it**. A forward migration is the only shape that reaches them.

### PROVED RED FIRST, IN THE ORDER LAW 7 ASKS FOR

`10-scripts/def_pay_6207_null_branch_readback.py`, PostgreSQL 16, writing
nothing:

* **at `0033`** — both rows **ACCEPTED**, each reported against the constraint
  that should have refused it. That is the RED.
* **at `0034`** — both **refused BY NAME**, and **all three lawful shapes still
  accepted**: a normal counted close, a closed system till, and an open till
  belonging to a person. A fix that refuses everything is not a fix.
* **`test_p0_3_a_till_cannot_be_sealed_with_no_record_of_how`**, left red on the
  branch on purpose by the lane that filed it, **was not touched** — `git diff`
  against the tip for that file is empty — and goes green on the constraint.

⚠ **THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE PROOF HAD A FLAW OF ITS OWN AND IT IS RECORDED
RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED.** Each case ran in a savepoint that was rolled back
only when the row was REFUSED, so an ACCEPTED red row survived inside the outer
transaction and collided with a later case: the lawful *closed system till* was
refused by `uq_counter_sessions_system_day` — by the row the previous case had
just left behind — and the script printed *"the fix is too strong"*. **That was
a statement about the probe, not about the schema.** Every case now rolls back
whether it was accepted or refused. A check whose earlier case changes the
answer to its later one is not measuring what it says it measures.

### WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, AND IT IS LAW 7'S OWN SHAPE

**SQLite cannot show this and the suite runs there** (law 14). The one thing
that asks the question is that single test, and it **went red when `0033`
landed and was pushed red** — proved-red-then-never-read, on the constraint
that gives a PO ruling its teeth. This lane ran the payments suites and read
`1 failed, 97 passed`, dated the one failure correctly, and **never looked at a
file it had not changed**. The defect register's `escape_reason` says the same.

**The habit that would have caught it:** *read the failures you did not cause*
means the whole suite, not only the files your diff names.

| Who | Link |
|---|---|
| LANE P0-DB (measured and filed, correctly did not fix) · LANE P0-BATCH-3 (the fix, and the second constraint) | `DEF-PAY-6207` · `apps/payments/migrations/0034_def_pay_6207_null_safe_check_branches.py` · `apps/payments/counter_session_models.py` · `10-scripts/def_pay_6207_null_branch_readback.py` · `tests/test_cr135_p0_foundations.py` |

*"the extraction is REPORTED rather than taken here, because PremisesImportsTab
is another story's file"*. `AccountImportsTab`'s: *"this IS the third consumer
AST-04 named as its extraction trigger, and that is REPORTED rather than taken
here"*. **Every author was right about their own scope, and that is exactly how
a repo ends up with three answers to one question.** A fourth report would have
been the cheapest thing to write and the thing the blueprint explicitly asked us
not to do.

**So `components/workflow/ImportRunsList.tsx` is the run list now**, exported
through the kit's one import path, and it has **two callers on its first
commit**: `AccountImportsTab` (515 lines → 100 of configuration, its 15 existing
cases green and unedited) and the new `PaymentsImportsTab`.

⚠ **AND PRM-04 AND AST-04 ARE DELIBERATELY NOT MIGRATED, WHICH IS THE JUDGMENT
RATHER THAN THE WORK.** The three copies are not three copies of one decision;
they have DIVERGED on purpose. `DEF-CUS-5009` split the accounts tab's row
actions — a run that LOADED something can be rolled back, a run with REJECTED
rows can be fixed — and the other two still make them mutually exclusive on a
field the clerk does not read, so a premises run that lost four rows offers no
path to those four. `DEF-CUS-5061` scoped the accounts list on the SERVER; PRM-04
sends no scope at all and AST-04 filters in the browser. **Folding all three now
would either carry three behaviours as three flags — three implementations
inside one file, which is no better — or change two live screens inside a task
whose subject is payments.** The accounts copy moved because it is the one whose
two known defects are fixed; the other two are named as follow-up here.

⚠ **NO ROLLBACK ON A PAYMENTS RUN, AND IT IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE SERVER.**
`import_runs.rollback` refuses this target BY NAME and `_load_payments_rows`
creates no rollback point, because a posted payment cannot be unwritten (hard
rule 4). The list asks the KIT's own per-target rule — `rollbackControlIsOffered`,
which `P1.22` put there so the row action and the runner's stage-5 panel cannot
disagree — rather than answering it itself. A `↺` on a payments run would be a
live danger-tier button over a door the server keeps shut.

⚠ **THE FOUR KPI TILES AND THE THREE EXTRA COLUMNS 4·1 DRAWS ARE NOT BUILT, AND
THAT IS THE REGISTER'S INSTRUCTION RATHER THAN A CUT.** The wireframe draws
*Waiting · Applied today · Needs a person · Refused* over figures `GET /imports`
does not serve, and SOURCE / LABEL / AMOUNT columns `ImportRunRow` has no fields
for. B14 rule 37 makes a drawn figure an illustration; §05 says *Reuse*. **Four
tiles reading `—` would be worse than four tiles that are not there.**

⚠ **THE HEAD CHANGES ON THIS TAB AND ONLY THIS TAB.** 4·1 draws `PAYMENTS ›
IMPORTS` over **Imports**, where 2·1, 2·1b and 7·1 all draw plain **Payments**
with no kicker. Read off the rendered page at 2.0 (B14 rule 42), and it is not a
head a clerk has seen say something else, because the tab had no screen at all
until this commit.

⚠ **AND THE DOOR'S LABEL IS `↑ Import` WHERE THE DRAWING DRAWS `Import →`.** B14
rule 4 names `↑` for an import and three sibling screens already say `↑ Import
premises` / `↑ Import meters` / `↑ New import`; the `→` is dropped because the
glyph already says *this opens the importer* and two direction marks on a
two-word button is noise. **The word is the drawing's; the glyph is the rule's.**

### 2 · `P1.8` — THE BUTTON'S FIGURE COMES FROM THE RUN'S OWN PREDICATE

§03 frame 2·1b files the gap itself: *"`bulkActionRefusal` returns 'allowed' if
ANY selected row can be acted on … The confirm that follows takes **only a
count** — it asks 'Reverse 5 payments?' when it is about to reverse one and
silently refuse four. You find out afterwards, per row."* And it names the fix:
*"The product already knows which four … **The fix is not new logic; it is
showing what is already computed.**"*

**So `splitSelection` takes the caller's own `refusalFor` and adds no rule.** A
second rule in the bar would be a screen that says one thing before the button
and does another after it, over money — the one place that cannot be allowed to
drift. What changed is only WHEN the clerk is told.

**The worked figure, and it is the drawing's own:** three payments ticked,
`$1,080.53` on the bar. One of them is already a reversal. The bar reads
**Reverse 2**; the confirm says **2 of 3 will be reversed, 1 skipped**, draws all
three rows with `Skipped — already a reversal` against the third, and its
consequence box reads **$278.10 goes back to 2 accounts** over **2 bills
re-open**. `158.10 + 120.00 = 278.10`, summed with `sumDecimalStrings` on the
storage grid, never a float (hard rule 2).

⚠ **THE TWO MONEY FIGURES ON THAT SCREEN DIFFER ON PURPOSE AND IT IS WORTH
WRITING DOWN.** The bar's `$1,080.53` is `POST /payments/selection-total`, which
applies CS-35's signed rule that the figure is the day's CASH — *"or it will not
tie to the drawer"*. The consequence's `$278.10` answers a different question:
how much money is about to move back to customers, over the rows the run will
actually touch. They are not two answers to one question, and the drawing shows
both.

⚠ **THE REFUND CONFIRM GETS THE SAME SHAPE AND THE DRAWING DRAWS ONLY THE
REVERSAL'S — recorded here so it can be overturned in one word.** The GAP box's
sentence (*"a bulk reversal writes money across several accounts and shows no
'what this will do' box at all"*) is true of a bulk refund word for word, and
`bulkRefundRefusal` already computes a per-row reason that the refund form was
throwing away exactly as the reversal's was. **Two forms one step apart, one
asking per row and one asking for a count, teaches a clerk two habits.**

⚠ **AND ONE CATALOGUE STRING LEFT THE SCREEN.** The Why field's help was *"A
payment needing approval is reversed on its own row"*; the drawing's note ⑥ puts
*"One reason for all of them. Split the selection if they differ."* there, and
B14 rule 32 gives a section one sentence. The drawn one wins (rule 41 — the
product UI matches the blueprint). **`payments.bulk.reverseNoApproval` is KEPT in
all eleven catalogues**: it is a true fact about a path that still exists, and
retiring a string from eleven catalogues is the expensive half of putting it
back.

### 3 · `P1.14` — TWO HALVES OF THE OUTCOME SENTENCE ARE NOT BUILT, AND THEY ARE FILED RATHER THAN ASSERTED

`P1.14`'s outcome is *"The payments appear on the one list with their run and
Source · Post."* Measured at `67cb9e0c7`, with `app.tenant_id` set:

| half | verdict |
|---|---|
| **the one list** | TRUE — every created payment is an ordinary `payments` row on S33, and there is no second list anywhere |
| **Source · Post** | **TRUE IN THE DATABASE, INVISIBLE ON THE SCREEN.** `payments.origin` holds `import`, the stored spelling of the blueprint's *Post* under the PO's 2026-09-22 ruling *"One column — extend what we shipped"*, and `import_writer` sets it on every row under `ck_payments_origin`. `selectors.py`'s list row does not carry it, `PaymentRow` does not declare it, and S33 draws no Source column — `DEF-PAY-6212` |
| **their run** | **NOT SERVABLE AT ALL.** Nothing links a payment to the run that created it; the run and the row live only inside the idempotency key — `DEF-PAY-6213` |

⚠ **THE SECOND ONE MATTERS BEYOND THIS JOURNEY.** `P1.4` keeps
`payment_import_batches` and `payment_import_rows` precisely because they *"hold
the provenance of every payment they created"* — on the OLD path. The NEW path
has no such link, so **deleting the old pipeline under `P1.9` would delete the
only provenance this product has** unless `DEF-PAY-6213` lands first. That is a
sequencing fact `P1.9`'s own decision rows do not yet name.

**The journey is written and NOT activated**, the same posture `JPAYWRONGACCT`
took eight hours earlier and for a sharper reason: two of its checks cannot pass
today, and a journey first seen green is a journey nobody has proved.

⚠ **AND `J-PAY-lockbox-morning` COULD NOT HAVE BEEN THE ID.**
`g12_journeys.VALID_JOURNEY_ID_RE` is `^[JT][A-Za-z0-9]*(?:-\d+)?$` and takes no
interior hyphen, so the task table's name is a TITLE. The id is `JPAYLOCKBOX`,
the file is named for it — `DEF-QAE-6208`'s lesson applied rather than repeated —
and both names are in the heading so a reader searching for either finds it.

### 4 · TWO REDS THAT WERE NOT MINE, DATED

**`G31` had been RED since 2026-09-19** (`DEF-RAT-6211`).
`features/rating/discountDetailTabs.tsx` landed in `c656deea1` written entirely

**`G12` is still RED on seven journey files** — the remainder of

### 5 · A STALE PARAGRAPH CORRECTED ON THE WAY PAST

`paymentsBulk.tsx`'s header stated the **superseded** rule-21 mechanism: *"the
Tailwind compiler emits nothing for a utility written here … it renders as
NOTHING AT ALL"*. `DEF-GOV-5102` corrected that on 2026-09-12 by PO ruling
(*"Yes correct it"*) — `tailwind.css` declares `@source "../"` and the compiler

lane reading it hand-writes a stylesheet class, which is what rule 21 forbids.
