## 2026-09-23 — FIVE PO RULINGS IN ONE SITTING, ON THE COUNTER, THE WRITE-OFF QUEUE, THE "WHAT IS MISSING" PANEL AND THE BARCODE

All five were put to the PO in plain English with a worked figure, per the
standing instruction, and all five are recorded here with their words verbatim
and the case that was shown. **Two of them overturn a position this repo held
deliberately**, which is why the reasoning is written out rather than inferred.

### 1 · A CLERK MAY BACKDATE THE OPENING TIME WITHIN THE SAME BUSINESS DAY

**Shown:** *Dana opens the counter at 09:00, forgets to start it, notices at
11:00 and sets it back to 09:00 — which moves the takings into a different
business day.* Options put: (a) today only, no backdating · (b) backdate within
the same day · (c) any date.

**Ruled, verbatim:** *"(b) Backdate within the same day"*

**So:** `opened_at` may move BACKWARD within the same business day and no
further — not to yesterday, not to a future moment. ⚠ **"The same day" is the
TENANT'S business day in the TENANT'S timezone**, the same regional source the
picker renders in; computing the day boundary a second way is how the two
disagree. ⚠ **The refusal belongs at the ENDPOINT, not only in the form** — a
form-only check is a suggestion, not a rule, and this one decides which business
day's takings a payment lands in.

### 2 · THE PICKER APPLIES TO ALL FOUR COUNTER WRITES, NOT ONLY TO OPENING

**Shown:** *Dana closes the till at 17:05 but counts the cash at 17:20 — which
is the closing time?* Options put: (a) a picker on all four · (b) a picker on
open only.

**Ruled, verbatim:** *"(a) Picker on all four, same as opening"*

**So:** close, force-close and declare each get the same date-and-time picker as
open. This closes `DEF-PAY-6315` as a BUILD rather than as the report it was
filed as: the lane found, on its own blast-radius check, that all three siblings
omit the required moment their endpoint reads — **so a clerk could not have
CLOSED a till either, not merely opened one.**

### 3 · A WRITE-OFF MAY BE APPROVED BY THE PERSON WHO ASKED FOR IT (`BR-PAY-037` STANDS)

**Shown:** *today an Admin who asks for a `$1,202.40` write-off can approve it
themselves, and both acts are recorded separately. The drawing says they should
not be able to.* Options put: (a) keep v1 as signed and redraw the two
sentences · (b) move enforced separation-of-duties forward from v2.

**Ruled, verbatim:** *"allow it - we are dealing with smaller utilites they dont
have too many people"*

**So option (a). `BR-PAY-037` is re-affirmed as signed** — the same user holding
the approver role MAY initiate AND approve in v1, both acts recorded distinctly;
enforced separation-of-duties stays v2. **The REASON is an ICP argument and is
worth keeping:** a utility run by 10–20 staff may not HAVE a second approver, so
a control requiring one would stop the work rather than protect it.

**WHAT IS NOW WRONG IS THE DRAWING.** Blueprint p086 draws *"A second person
decides."* and *"You cannot approve one you asked for."* and a third row reading
*"Yours — someone else decides"*. Those are SUPERSEDED. The screen's existing
behaviour — *your request* drawn as a WARNING beside a row the viewer raised,
never a block — is now the ratified shape rather than a stopgap. **This was B14
rule 41's one escalation clause working as designed:** a drawing that
contradicts a signed rule reached the PO by being written up, not by being
built.

### 4 · THE "WHAT IS MISSING" PANEL KEEPS ITS FACTS AND LOSES ITS REASONS

**Shown:** the PO asked, of the Payments Summary screen, *"on this screen youa
re showing these details why - What is missing * Finance owns this formula. It
is not worked out here. * Medical protections cannot be shown here."*
**Measured for them:** the `payments.problem.*` family is **40 strings**, of
which **29 have a sentence over B14 rule 33's six-word cap**, the worst at **30
words**. Options put: (a) delete all 40 · (b) keep the facts, shorten to six
words, delete the reasons · (c) leave as is.

**Ruled, verbatim:** *"(b) Keep the facts, shorten to six words, delete the
reasons"*

**So:** each of the 40 is classified as a FACT a clerk can act on (keep, shorten
to the cap) or RATIONALE (delete outright — rule 33 removes rationale, never
shortens it). *"Recorded, not in the books…"* is a fact. *"Finance owns this
formula"* is not. ⚠ Deleting a string is not deleting a fact from the PRODUCT:
rule 32's closed `<details>` is the home for anything useful but not
actionable, and `ProblemList` is where that half was always owed.

### 5 · BILLS WILL PRINT BARCODE BARS, AND THE SCAN CARD IS RELEASED BEHIND THEM

**Shown:** the scan card is held because *a wedge scanner reads bars* and our
bills print only the human-readable line `ACC-1042$BL-2608-0117$14218%`;
releasing it as-is means a clerk scans one of our own bills and gets nothing.
Options put: (a) build the bars, then release · (b) leave held · (c) release now.

**Ruled, verbatim:** *"please enable it and also start putting bar code on bills
- we are still in beta and uat - we ahve to make these changes now"*, and on
being shown the option table again, *"My recommendation is (a) - yes do it"*.

**So option (a), and THE ORDER IS THE RULING.** Bars first; the card is released
only once a DECODE ROUND TRIP proves a scanner would read them — the drawn
rectangles extracted from a real PDF and decoded back to the line that went in.
*"It looks like a barcode"* is law 7's *looking at the wrong thing*. If only one
half lands it is the BARS, never the card.

**THIS OVERTURNS A MEASURED HOLD, AND THE HOLD WAS RIGHT WHEN IT WAS MADE.**
`remittance.bars()` specifies the symbol in full; what was missing is a
filled-rectangle primitive in the PDF writer, and `documents.py`'s only mention
of `bars(` is a COMMENT at line 1677, not a call — verified rather than assumed.
`scanSourceIsReachableAndHeld.dom.test.tsx` holds the card shut with a failure
message naming the exact reopening condition; **it is updated deliberately, not
deleted**, because a sibling lane wrote it so this moment would be a decision
rather than an accident.

**AND THE HOLD AUDIT THAT CAME WITH IT.** All four Extract sources — scan,
sftp, api, manual — are drawn PRESENT AND REFUSED with their reason
(`BR-SHL-025`), each with a test that fires when its reason stops being true.
None was found rotten. That is the opposite result from the Record-payment
button and the write-off way-in reported the same morning, both of which were
holds with a clock in them and no test.

## 2026-09-23 · `DEF-PAY-6319` — THE ACCOUNT PICKER IS ONE CONTROL NOW, AND THE FIVE STATES ARE WHAT HAD TO SURVIVE (lane ACCOUNT-COMBO)

**Reported, verbatim.** The Product Owner, looking at the Raise-a-refund form:
*"why to button - why cannot we have dropdown search drectly for this - user has
to do two clicks"*. They were then told why it was built as two fields, and
ruled: *"fix it"*.

**What they were looking at.** `AccountPickerFields` drew a *Find account* text
box and, once something matched, a separate *Account* select underneath it. Two
gestures to choose one account, on four screens: Record a payment, Raise a
refund, Issue credit, and Move / reapply.

**THE SPLIT EXISTED FOR A REAL REASON AND THE REASON IS NOT THE SECOND
CONTROL.** `DEF-3506` (PO, 2026-09-03: *"On this payment record form unable to
search account"*) was filed because a clerk could not tell FIVE situations
apart — typed too little · searching · **the search itself failed** · the search
ran and nothing matched · here are your matches. A select holding one
placeholder draws four of those five identically. The 2026-09-03 repair made
them distinguishable by ADDING a field, and that addition is what the PO has now
reported. **So the deliverable was: keep all five, lose the second gesture.**

**The pair that a naive dropdown destroys, and why it is not cosmetic.** *The
search could not run* is a fact about the PLATFORM (`BR-SHL-020`) and support
can act on it; *no account matches that* is a fact about the TERM and the clerk
can act on it by typing. In an ordinary combobox both are one empty list. They
are kept apart three ways: a different sentence, a different surface — the
failure is a `RefusalStrip` with `role="alert"`, the other three are `Note`s —
and a `data-panel-state` attribute naming which of six the panel is in. The
state machine is a PURE FUNCTION, `remoteSearchPanel`, on `popoverAnchor.ts`'s
precedent, and **the ORDER of its tests is the rule**: `failed` is asked first,
so no combination of a stale `searched` flag, a cached row or a retry in flight
can bury it.

**THE MONEY RULE, AND IT IS THE PART THAT GOT HARDER RATHER THAN EASIER.** The
two-field picker cleared the chosen account id on every keystroke, with the
reason written beside it: *"Leaving a stale id behind a changed box is how a
clerk posts money to the account they were looking at a moment ago."* One
control makes that easier to get wrong, because the box now holds the chosen
account's OWN NAME — so the obvious implementation leaves the id attached while
the text changes over it. **The worked case:** a clerk picks
`AC-2026-00050 — Miller, Sarah`, then types `AC-2026-99999` and submits. What
must post is NOTHING — `raiseRefundSchema` refuses an empty `account_id`, and
the request is addressed `/accounts/{id}/refunds`, so a stale id would have been
the whole address. It is asserted twice: at the control's own seam (the spy sees
`""`) and on the real Raise-a-refund form (no POST, and `acc-0050` in no call).

**WHY IT IS IN THE KIT AND NOT IN PAYMENTS (B14 rules 43 and 36).** The kit
already had a combobox — `SearchSelectField` — and it filters a list the browser
already holds, so it can only say *here are the options* or *No matching
options*. It cannot say *the search could not run*. That gap is why three
features (payments, `customers/accountFinder.tsx`, `metering/OwnerAccount.tsx`)
each hand-rolled the two-field pattern. `components/RemoteSearchSelectField.tsx`
is the missing piece, added to the kit rather than to the screen.

**`AccountPickerFields` KEPT ITS EXPORTED NAME AND ITS PROPS, DELIBERATELY.**
Four screens compose it and a sibling lane was building a fifth host while this
was written; only the internals moved, so **no call site needed an edit**. The
one control's id stays `account_id` because that is the name every zod schema
and every server refusal uses; `account_query` was a second id for one question
and is gone with the second control.

**A judgment this lane made rather than asked about:** with one control there is
one label, so the field's NAME (`accountLabel`, e.g. *Account*) is the label and
the search's invitation (`searchLabel`, e.g. *Find account*) is the placeholder.
Both strings every host already passed are still on screen and **not one
catalogue key moved** — the kit takes its four sentences from the host, which is
B14 rule 35 (a catalogue is written in its own language) applied to a shared
component.

**AND ONE DEFECT FOUND BY READING THE FOUR CALL SITES — `DEF-PAY-6320`.** The
Move-a-payment modal passed `accountLabel={t("payments.move.destination")}` and
**that key exists in none of the eleven catalogues**, so the field was named with
its own raw key. G15 could not see it, because a key missing from ALL eleven is
parity-perfect; it reached the screen only after a search matched, which is a
state a lane rarely walks to. It mattered more after this change, because the
label is now always visible. Fanned into all eleven as *Destination account* and
its ten siblings, each written in its own language rather than translated.

⚠ **AND G18 IS NOT THE ANSWER TO "WHY DID NOTHING CATCH IT" — IT SAW IT AND
NOBODY READ IT.** G18's direction B is exactly this check, and it PASSES today
while reporting `22 missing (19 unparked, renders raw to a user)` in one line,
naming three of them and `(+16 more)`. That is hard-won law 7's fourth shape
with a number on it: the count is true, it is printed on every run, and a key
inside `(+16 more)` is not distinguishable from one that does not exist. The
honest reading is that the gate did its job and the reporting surface is where
this was lost.
`payments.form.accountPlaceholder` — the old select's *Choose an account* — has
no reader any more and is retired in the same commit, so G18 does not inherit a
dead key.

**Version 2.346.5.** The reporter looks in that build.

⚠ **THAT VERSION SENTENCE IS SUPERSEDED: THE BUILD IS 2.346.14.** It was
written when the branch stood at `2.346.4`, and eight further numbers were
taken by sibling lanes while this change was being proved — the tip moved
under it six times and every shared blob was re-derived from the new one
each time (law 11). **The reporter looks in 2.346.14.** The line above is left
standing rather than corrected in place, because a register is amended and
not rewritten, and because deleting it is the revert-by-subtraction
`push_register_guard.py` exists to refuse.

**THE BLAST RADIUS, AND THE SWEEP THAT MISSED IT FIRST.** Removing a field id
is a deletion, and an absence is invisible to every check this repo has — the
`kind='service'` lesson in `CLAUDE.md` hard rule 8, one layer down. Three
further test files and six Playwright specs drove `#account_query` and then
`selectOption`-ed the `#account_id` SELECT: `consequenceOnMoneyForms.dom.test`
(green at the clean tip, red under this change), `recordFormOrder.dom.test`'s
field-ORDER census, and `W4-payment-write`, `CR-009-notifications`, `J2`,
`J19`, `T5-09` and `CR-008-accounting`. All nine are updated here.

⚠ **THE FIRST SWEEP FOUND NONE OF THEM, AND THE REASON IS THIS FILE'S OWN LAW
7.** It was `grep -rn "account_query\|AccountPickerFields\|…" --include=*.test.tsx
… | head -30` — and the `head -30` cut the output before the payments hits,
so the command reported truthfully about everything it could see and the lane
read that as *nothing else uses it*. **A limit on a search that underpins a
conclusion is a blind spot with no number beside it**, which is `G32`'s shape
and the `grep -i 'pdf$'` shape, self-inflicted in one line. What found them was
running the neighbours' suite; what fixed the method was re-running the sweep
with no limit at all. `#account_query` now appears nowhere but in comments
recording that it used to exist.


## 2026-09-23 · `DEF-PAY-6335` — THE `Figures for` BAND, AND THE JUDGMENT THAT THE DATE UNDER IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE (lane FIGURES-FOR)

**Reported by the PO, walking S32, verbatim:** *"these detailsa re not aligned on
ui - Figures for*"*. They were looking at the top strip of Payments → Summary.

**Routed as MAINTENANCE** (`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`): a
clerk can open this screen and use this band today, so the one question that
decides the track answers *yes*.

### What was actually wrong, measured rather than described

`.pay-toolbar` is `align-items: flex-end`, and the date field has carried FOUR
lines since the help sentence was added — label, input, the help sentence, and
the IS-8 tenant-format echo. Flex-end aligns to the bottom of all four. Measured
in Chromium at 1440 on the unfixed bundle:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the two counters' centre line | **y = 314** | y = 268 |
| the *Mark returned post* button | **y = 316** | y = 268 |
| the business-day input's centre line | y = 268 | y = 268 |
| top of the highest control to bottom of the lowest | **83px** | **36px** |

**This is the SECOND report of the same band.** On 2026-09-03 the PO said *"why
Figures for ... and Automatic payments lined up ... Mark returned post - why
these are in two differnt lines - again layout issue"*, and that fix — moving
the chips inside the toolbar — was right for the field as it then was. It rotted
when the field grew two lines underneath its input, and the CSS comment written
at the time went on asserting the guarantee it no longer had: *"`align-items:
flex-end` lines the chips up with the bottom of the date input rather than its
label"*. Hard-won law 1, three weeks in the open, reading as documentation that
the band was fine.

### THE JUDGMENT THIS LANE MADE RATHER THAN ASKED ABOUT: the doubled date stays

`09/23/2026` in the control and `23-Sep-26` under it look like one fact said
twice, and the brief that dispatched this lane asked whether one of them should
go. **Neither should.** A native `<input type="date">` renders in the BROWSER's
locale and never the tenant's, so `DatePickerField` draws the IS-8 line beneath
it — and `regionalDateEcho` returns **null** when the two would read the same
(CR-043 finding 15, `components/DateCell.tsx`). On a tenant whose `date_format`
is `DD-MMM-YY` that line is the only place their own format reaches this screen;
on a `MM/DD/YYYY` tenant it does not render at all. Deleting it would take the
tenant's format off the screen for the tenants who set one, which is the single
thing it exists to do.

**What it needed was not a caption but a column.** Adrift in a wrap-flex band it
was a stray date; inside the field's own 240px column, under the input it
belongs to, it is that field in the tenant's format. **No words were added
saying so, deliberately** — B14 rule 33 puts RATIONALE at ZERO WORDS ON SCREEN,
so a caption explaining the echo would have broken one rule while trying to obey
another. The reason lives in the component's docstring and in this row.

### The second judgment: the counters lost their chip boxes

The two counts were `.pay-chip` — an inline label-and-value in a bordered box
with an accent top-rule, three of them in a 1120px strip that already has one.
They are a label above a figure now, which is what `components/AgeingCards.tsx`
— the kit piece minted from this same blueprint — draws for a labelled figure,
and what the blueprint's own TODAY tiles draw. **It is also what makes the
alignment structural rather than measured:** every column in the band is now the
same two boxes, a label and a 36px control row, so the figures land on the
input's row by construction. A second help sentence tomorrow cannot move them.

`.pay-chips`, `.pay-chip` and `.pay-chip-value` are deleted from `payments.css`.
**`.pay-chip-label` stays and that is not an oversight** — `ReconciliationStatementPage.tsx`
draws it standalone on the residual line. Grepping for a class's CONSUMERS
before retiring it is `DEF-CUS-3653`'s lesson from the other side.

### What was deliberately NOT done, and why it is a defect row rather than a diff

**The payments blueprint redraws this whole screen and nothing was ever scoped
to it — `DEF-PAY-6336`, filed, severity high.** §03 frame 1·1 (p027–p029, read
as images at 2.0 and 6.0 per B14 rule 42) is headed *"REDRAWN AS A WORKLIST"*
and draws a counter band, a five-row *Needs you* list and four TODAY tiles.
**It draws no business-day field, no counters and no *Mark returned post*
button anywhere.**

Building it as drawn — which B14 rule 41 makes the default — would delete the
only control that types `as_of`, and **BR-TEN-043 makes `as_of` REQUIRED on the
wire and forbids reading a clock**; it would also delete the only door to
US-PAY-016's bulk mark, the queue that spent five days counting a chore nobody
could do. A drawn element that contradicts a signed business rule is precisely
rule 41's one narrow exception, and it goes to the PO with both sides quoted
rather than being decided by a lane fixing an alignment. It is filed so it is a
row somebody can count, which is the whole lesson of rule 41's own history:
`DEF-GOV-5006` captured the ACC-02 rulings and captured is not built.

### What is now checked, and what is honestly not

`10-scripts/render-checks/def-pay-6335-summary-band.mjs` measures the band in
Chromium — 19 checks, and three of them are the geometry no source check can
see. It carries a `--before` mode that rebuilds the pre-fix band in the page and
**must fail**; it was run in both modes and the `--before` numbers were compared
against the real unfixed bundle before it was trusted, because a reconstruction
that is *nearly* the old screen is exactly the thing that quietly stops
reproducing anything.

`summaryFiguresBar.dom.test.tsx` holds the nine claims jsdom CAN decide and says
in its own header that it cannot see the defect — every one of its assertions
would have passed at the broken commit, which is what `SummaryTab.test.tsx` did
for three weeks.

**Version 2.346.9.** The reporter looks in that build.

## 2026-09-23 · `DEF-BIL-6325` — OUR BILLS PRINT A BARCODE A SCANNER CAN READ, AND THE SCAN CARD WAS RELEASED BY REMOVING ITS REASON (lane BARCODE, `c531d6823`, `2.346.15`)

Recorded by the coordinator, who holds this file; the three judgments are the
lane's and are written down here because the lane was fenced out of it.

### 1 · A DEFECT, NOT A CHANGE REQUEST

The PO's words read like a new requirement — *"please enable it and also start
putting bar code on bills"*. It was filed as a **defect** under
`13-change-process.md` §1's beta clause, and the reason is on the record: the
phase-5 board's `P5.10` row is titled *"Billing: the remittance barcode"* with the
outcome *"Without it a scanner reads nothing. Which is why it ships in this
phase."* **We shipped the human-readable LINE and not the BARS.** That is our
miss against our own promise. Filing it as a change would have converted our
error into the customer's new requirement, which is precisely the move §1 exists
to prevent.

### 2 · THE GEOMETRY, WITH THE REASON FOR EACH NUMBER

Measured off the rendered page, not read back from constants.

| | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|
| X-dimension (narrow bar) | **1.0 pt = 13.9 mil** | Above Code 39's 7.5-mil floor; inside the 10–20 mil band an office printer renders without merging bars |
| Wide : narrow | **2.5** | 2.0 is out of spec below 20 mil — ink spread eats a larger share of a narrow bar |
| Quiet zone | **18 pt (0.25 in) each side, held inside the row** | The page margin satisfies it today and would stop silently the first time a cell is added to that row |
| Bar height | **36 pt (0.5 in)** | |
| Ink | **pure black**, not the page's ~88% `INK` | The only marks on the sheet a machine must read get full contrast |
| Too long to fit | **below 0.72 pt (10 mil) → no bars at all**; the line still prints | A symbol nobody can decode is worse than none, because a clerk cannot tell the two apart. Cliff measured at 43 characters; realistic lines land at 11–14 mil |

**The worked figure, from a real issued bill:** `BL-2607-000101`, account
`A-10432`, total due `$100.58`. The page prints `A-10432$BL-2607-000101$10058B`;
155 rectangles were read back out of the PDF's own content stream, spaces
recovered by subtraction as a decoder does, and decoded with a Code 39 table
**written independently of `remittance._PATTERNS`** — a decoder sharing the
encoder's table would round-trip perfectly through a mistyped pattern. Result:
**byte-identical to the line that went in.** Five deliberate corruptions are
refused. *"It looks like a barcode"* was never accepted as proof.

### 3 · THE GENERAL RULE: RELEASE A HOLD BY REMOVING ITS REASON, NEVER BY OVERRULING IT

The PO's instruction read card-first. Built in that order, a clerk selects *Scan
paper*, points a scanner at one of our own bills and gets nothing — a live
control over a door onto nothing, hard-won law 2's mirror. So the order was the
ruling: **bars built → decoded → only then the card released**, and at no moment
was there a live card over blank paper.

**This is worth keeping as the rule for every hold, not only this one.** A hold
carries a reason. The legitimate way to release it is to make the reason false
and prove it false; the illegitimate way is to flip the flag because someone
asked. The hold's own test is how the difference is kept: both hold tests were
**inverted, not deleted**, so they now assert the property that ever mattered —
*the card is live if and only if our own paper can be scanned* — rather than
merely *the card is on*.

It is the same lesson as the day's other holds, seen from the other side. The
Record-payment button and the write-off way-in were holds whose reason had
**expired unnoticed**; the scan card was a hold whose reason was **still true**,
and the right move was to change the world rather than the flag.

**Filed, not fixed:** `DEF-BIL-6340` (the HTML serialisation of a bill still
draws no bars) and `DEF-BIL-6341` (`test_us_bil_022_tc11` red since
`955f1d64c`, because issue now fills a tenth field and the case's substitution
list knows nine).

## 2026-09-23 — RECORD A PAYMENT BECOMES A PAGE, AND THE TWO THINGS THE DRAWING DID NOT DECIDE (`DEF-PAY-6317`, lane RECORD-PAGE)

**The PO, on the deployed build with the blueprint open beside the product:**
***"record payment is form - not modal"***. Classified a DEFECT, not a change:
a user can record a payment today, so it is MAINTENANCE
(`22-product-maintenance-process.md`), and in the beta a report is a defect by
default. Nothing about it went back to the PO — it was agreed in writing
already, in the frame header of §03 frame 2·3a: *"today: a modal · agreed:
`/:tenant/payments/record/new` — a page, not a modal"*.

**THE FINDING IS NOT THE FIX, IT IS HOW THE WORK STAYED INVISIBLE.** The move
was known and written down **three times on 2026-09-23** — `CR-136-BRC07` row
`P2.9`, the `P2.6` conformance file's *"what is NOT done"* list, and
`CounterDoors.tsx`'s lifecycle `exceptions:` line — in the same words each
time: *"a SEPARATE change and was not made"*. **None of the three is a queue.**
It never became a CR row, an open question, a task or a defect, so nothing
counted it, and no gate could: an `exceptions:` line is a docstring, and no
check in this repository reads one for work still owed. The PO found it
instead. **A deferral recorded only where the code is is a deferral nobody can
count** — the same mechanism as the two lanes who wrote `OQ-1330` in prose and
filed no row, and it cost the same thing. All three now say DONE and say why
they were not enough.

### Two judgments the drawing does NOT settle, ruled here rather than asked

**1 · THE TWO-COLUMN GRID IS OURS (B14 rule 38).** p037 draws the fields two to
a row, and the page is built that way — but the AUTHORITY is **B14 rule 39**
(*"TWO FIELDS TO A ROW, 20px between fields in both directions"*), not the
picture. Rule 38 puts side-by-side fields, help under an input and the footer's
button order in the FORM CONSTRUCTION bucket, where B14 and the kit decide:
*"if youa re doing a form - go as per our UI rules"*. They agree here, so
nothing was given up — **but the reason matters for the next form, where they
may not.** What the form CONTAINS stays the drawing's: which nine fields, their
order, their labels, the counter banner and the open-bill picker.

**2 · THE FIELD ORDER DOES NOT MOVE, THOUGH THE DRAWN PAIRING DIFFERS.** p037
pairs **Method | Reference** on one row and **Kind | Apply to** on the next.
The JSX emits `type` (Kind) BEFORE `method`, so in a two-column grid the pairs
come out **Kind | Method** and **Reference | Apply to**. The order is left
alone, for three reasons that agree: the drawing says TWICE that the order is
the JSX's and is UNCHANGED (*"NINE FIELDS IN THE ORDER THE JSX EMITS THEM"*,
and *"nine fields, their order, labels, helpers and the open-bill picker ·
UNCHANGED from §02 screen 03"*); `recordFormOrder.dom.test.tsx` pins it, and
what it pins is a **PO ruling of 2026-09-13** — *the blueprint order, on BOTH
screens* — which put `purpose` under the amount here and on `S22`; and B14 rule
37 makes a drawn arrangement an illustration where it contradicts its own
stated rule. **Recorded rather than silently followed either way**, which is
what the UI skill asks when a drawing and the system disagree.

### Three things that were NOT taken from the drawing, each for a stated reason

* **② stays a searchable select, not a segmented control.** The frame asks for
  *Cheque · Cash · Tap and pay* as buttons; **p039's own GAP box reverses it,
  dated 2026-09-22** — *"that was a rule 8 breach wearing a nicer coat"*, since
  a list of five or more options is searchable and a tenant is seeded six
  methods. p037's wireframe draws the select, so the drawing agrees with itself.
* **`/payments/record` is NOT redirected to the new page.** It is the payments
  LIST (p030 frame 2·1), the sidebar's own entry and a `sidebarDestinations`
  row. Redirecting it would delete the list of every payment from an address a
  clerk may have bookmarked. The two are siblings.
* **The posting-date echo under the date fields stays.** It is the shared
  `DatePickerField`'s IS-8 behaviour (`BR-SHL-023`) and it renders only when the
  tenant's format differs from the browser's — so it is a FACT (rule 33, ≤ 6
  words), not rationale, and removing it is a kit change affecting every date
  field in the product.

### And the modal is GONE rather than kept beside the page

p036 states the discipline for the same move one frame up: *"leaving both would
give the product two answers to one question, which is how a figure starts to
drift"*. `RecordPaymentModal` left `PaymentsPage.tsx` whole; its body is now the
exported COMPONENT `RecordPaymentForm` (B14 rule 43 — the drawing names three
further callers on p053, p062 and p084, so addressability is the point).
**Four doors were repointed in the same commit** — the list's head button, its
empty-state prompt, the Summary tile and the till's own button — three of which
had been landing the clerk on the table rather than the form. Each is an
ADDRESS and not a handler (`DEF-CWP-3925`).

## 2026-09-23 — THE VIRUS SCAN COMES OUT, AND WHY IT DID NOT COME OUT THE FIRST TIME; AND FIVE RULINGS ON `New request`

### 1 · NO MALWARE SCAN ON UPLOAD — `BR-SHL-031`, `NFR-34` AND `BR-SHL-253` ARE SUPERSEDED

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-23:** *"please remove virus scan chek user don't wan't it. we
have ask remove it before why you did not remove it?"*

**The earlier instruction, verbatim, 2026-09-22** (already recorded in that day's row
on `New request`): *"once you remove the virus check - you will ahveonly two cases
verified or rejected in case of rejected show the reason in short to user why it is
rejected."*

**THIS IS A SUPERSESSION OF SIGNED RULES, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `BR-SHL-031` and
`NFR-34` (*scan every upload before acceptance*, signed 2026-08-08) and `BR-SHL-253` (the
PO's own 2026-09-13 ruling, *"please execute this"*, choosing an in-line ClamAV scanner)
all said uploads are scanned. **The PO has now ruled the opposite twice**, so under
hard-won law 13 it is not put to them a third time: an upload is accepted with no
malware scan, and nothing on screen mentions scanning.

**WHY IT DID NOT COME OUT ON 2026-09-22 — the finding worth keeping.** The lane read
*"remove the virus check"* as **the sentence on screen** (*"Every attachment lands Not
checked."*), removed that sentence, and wrote down *"nothing about how a file is handled
moved"* — recording the narrow reading as though it answered the request. The PO's
second clause, *"you will have only two cases verified or rejected"*, is only coherent if
the scan itself is gone. **A PO instruction names a THING, not the words that describe
it on screen**; when the two readings differ, the larger one is almost always meant,
and a lane that takes the smaller must say so to the PO rather than record it as done.

**THE COST WHILE IT STAYED:** the deployed host runs no scanner, so New Request step 4
refused every upload with *"The virus scanner is unreachable. Try again shortly."*, no
file ever attached, and the review showed *No file* for every document.

Lane NO-SCAN removes the scan from every upload path, retires every scan string, and
stamps the three rules superseded where they live.

### 2 · `New request` STEP 3 — THE BILLING ADDRESS IS A US ADDRESS, AND IT IS OPTIONAL

**PO, verbatim:** *"on step 3 if customer want put billing address then it should full
address line, unit, city, zip it shoould be match how address taken in USA ;do'nt make
it mandatory"*.

Today one free-text box (`billing_address_as_given`). **Ruled:** street line, apt/suite/
unit, city, **state**, ZIP (5 or ZIP+4), none required. **State is the coordinator's
addition**, stated rather than slipped in: a US envelope needs it and a ZIP alone does
not make one. It lands as a STRUCTURED `customers.addresses` `kind='mailing'` row — the
permitted home under hard rule 8, and the exact fields lane BAD-ADDRESS now builds
envelopes from, so a new customer's bills can actually be addressed.

### 3 · STEP 5 — FEES ARE CHOSEN IN THE KIT'S `EditableTable`

**PO, verbatim:** *"on step 5 - for selecting fees can you use table array component"*.
Today a dropdown plus an *Add to the list* button. **Ruled:** the kit's `EditableTable`
(inline add row, one row per fee, a Total) — extended in the KIT if it lacks money
cells or a total, never forked (B14 rule 43). Money stays decimal (hard rule 2).

### 4 · THE REVIEW SCREEN — THE REQUESTED DATE, AND THE FEES AS A TABLE

**PO, verbatim:** *"On review screen requested date is not display. fee should be in
table format"*. REQUESTED START read `—` on every service beside a CONNECTION DATE of
`15-Oct-26`; the lane finds where the value is lost rather than papering over the
column. The fee card becomes the same fee table, read-only, with its currency.

### 5 · *Capture another* STARTS A BLANK REQUEST AT STEP 1

**PO, verbatim:** *"when user click on cappture another button user should redirect on
new request wizard on step ."* — read as step 1 of a fresh wizard. The button navigates
to `/requests/new`, which is where the confirmation already renders, so on the
coordinator's reading it never resets the wizard; the lane reproduces before fixing, and
a new request must never carry the finished one's draft number.

### 6 · THE ENGLISH CATALOGUE IS AMERICAN ENGLISH

**PO, verbatim:** *"cheque should american english check"*. Read — and recorded — as the
general rule it implies for a North American product whose only English catalogue is
`en.json`: **US spelling and US vocabulary**. Measured before the sweep: *cheque* 28
strings, *cancelled* 34, *centre* 10, *catalogue* 8, *licence* 7, *colour* 5,
*behaviour* 4, *organisation* 1, plus *flat* meaning a dwelling (while *a flat amount*
stays), and *acknowledgement*. **Values change, keys never do; a stored method CODE of
`cheque` is data and stays.** ⚠ If the fee-method label comes from SEEDED reference data
rather than the catalogue, the deployed tenant keeps the word already written into its
database (hard-won law 4) until it is edited or migrated — the lane reports which.
**A Canadian utility would need its own `en-CA` catalogue**, where *cheque*, *centre* and
*cancelled* are correct; not built, recorded so nobody reverts the sweep for it.

### 7 · THREE QUESTIONS NOW IN THE REGISTER RATHER THAN ONLY IN A CHAT

`OQ-PAY-12611` (keep the Summary's past-day picker and returned-post button),
`OQ-PAY-12612` (delete the medical-protections sentence) and `OQ-PAY-12613` (a
*Write-offs* door on Debtors) were put to the PO this afternoon and existed nowhere in
the repository. That is the `DEF-GOV-5229` lesson: a question held only in a
conversation is one nothing counts.

## 2026-09-23 — THE PO ASKS FOR *EDIT* ON A SERVICE REQUEST, AND WHY IT CANNOT BE THE NEXT THING WIRED

**PO, verbatim:** *"if user makes mistake while filling t new request form then system should
allow to correct it using edit , there is no edit available on list view as wellas detail view"*.

**THE ASK IS RIGHT AND IS RECORDED AS RULED** — a clerk corrects a request's mistakes
through Edit, reachable from the requests list and from the request's own page. It is
not put back to the PO.

**WHY IT IS NOT WIRED IMMEDIATELY — a data-loss guard, not a missing feature.**
`serviceRequestResumeHold.test.ts` (2026-09-19, `DEF-CUS-5880` + `DEF-CUS-5881`) fails
the build if anything links to the wizard for an EXISTING request, because:
* reopening a saved request shows an **EMPTY** wizard — the fetched request is never
  loaded into the form (`DEF-CUS-5880`); and
* every step PUTs the **whole** form, so a clerk who retypes one field over the empty
  boxes sends blank `email`, `phone` and `ssn` over the stored values.
The missing door is the only thing between that and destroyed customer data. **The
order is therefore the rule:** load the saved request into the wizard FIRST, then add
Edit/Resume doors, then delete the hold test in the same commit that wires them — which
is what the test's own header instructs.

**TWO TRAPS THE BUILD MUST CLOSE, stated so the lane does not rediscover them:**
1. **MASKED FIELDS.** The request shows the SSN as `••• •• • 5236` and the driver's
   license as `•••••9566`. Loading the MASK into the form and saving it back would
   overwrite the real value with the mask. A masked field is sent as *unchanged* unless
   the clerk types a new value — never round-tripped.
2. **THE FORM IS CHANGING SHAPE TODAY.** Lane REQ-FIX is splitting the billing address
   into structured fields and rebuilding the fee step. Loading-into-the-wizard must be
   built against the NEW shape, so Edit is sequenced **after REQ-FIX lands**, not beside it.

**WHICH REQUESTS ARE EDITABLE — the coordinator's call under law 13, recorded rather
than asked:** while the request is still being worked — *Draft*, *Submitted*, *Under
review*, *More info needed*. **Not** once *Approved* or *Refused*: those are decisions,
and an approved request has already become an account and a job, so correcting it is a
correction to THOSE records, not to the request. Every edit writes `audit_log`
(hard rule 7) with the before and after. Draft rows get a *Resume* door as well.

Also registered: `OQ-PAY-12614` — whether a refund's check number, now write-once, may
be corrected the way the PO allowed for payments on 2026-09-02.

## 2026-09-23 — SIGNED: A REFUND'S CHECK NUMBER MAY BE CORRECTED, THE WAY A PAYMENT'S CAN (`OQ-PAY-12614`)

**PO, verbatim:** *"One thing needs your sign-off, because it is a money record: (b) Allow
a correction, the same way you allowed it for payments on 2 September"*.

**WHAT WAS SHOWN, SO THE SIGNATURE IS NOT READ WIDER THAN IT IS** (the 2026-08-11 sign-off
rule): *Dana sends a refund of **$91.60** by check **#10241** but types **#10214**; as built
(`payments/0041`, write-once) it can never be changed.* Options: (a) leave it write-once ·
(b) allow a correction the same way as payments. **(b) chosen.**

**SO:** `refunds.reference` — the check number — becomes correctable through **one named,
audited path**, the refund's twin of `POST /payments/{id}/correct-reference` (`OQ-1322`,
PO 2026-09-02, *"(a) Allow those fields to change"*; `payments/0014`). **Only the check
number.** The payment rule also covers a memo and the tender; those were **not** put to
the PO for refunds and are **not** signed here — a refund's money has already left by the
method it left by. The amount and the account stay frozen, as does every other column.

**THE SAME CAVEAT CARRIES OVER VERBATIM IN SPIRIT:** the replaced number then lives only in
`audit_log`, and `audit_log` has one retention rule with no exempt row type (`OQ-1340`,
CLOSED 2026-09-23, *"when audit log is delete - it is deleted thats okay"*). No screen,
document or docstring may describe the correction path as a permanent record of the old
number — and under B14 rule 33 the screen says nothing about retention at all.

**WHY THIS IS THE CONSISTENT ANSWER:** money in and money out now share one rule for a
mistyped check number. Leaving refunds write-once would have made the rarer, riskier
direction the stricter one with no reason given.

**This is the human sign-off** for the *write-once rather than amendable* judgment named
unsigned in `payments/0041`'s review-ledger row; lane REFUND-CORRECT records it there.

## 2026-09-23 — THE FEE TABLE'S COLUMNS, `OQ-357` CLOSED, THE SERVER PRICES A FEE, AND *APPROVE* CHECKS THE UNIT BEFORE IT IS PRESSED

### 1 · THE STEP-5 FEE TABLE — COLUMNS CONFIRMED BY THE PO

Put to the PO as a table of candidate columns, each backed by a real field on
`service_request_fees`, with a recommendation. **PO, verbatim:** *"i like this please use
this"*, quoting: **Fee · Charged per · Qty · Unit price · Amount · Waive · (remove)**, an
*Add a fee* row, and a **Total**. **Code is not a column** (recommended out — clerks work by
name). Read-only on review, detail and confirmation, with a **Paid** column (the receipt) on
the detail page only — nothing is paid at step 5. Built on the kit's `EditableTable`.

### 2 · THE SERVER PRICES A FEE LINE — AND *WAIVE THE FEE* WAIVED NOTHING

Both found by lane REQ-FIX while checking a column; **PO, verbatim:** *"youa re correct -
fix it"*.
* `POST /service-requests/{id}/fees` stored whatever `unit_amount` the caller sent, so a
  direct API call could record the **$70.00** application fee as **$0.01**. **Ruled:** the
  server prices the line from the charge code at the moment of the Add, and **refuses** a
  mismatched amount rather than silently correcting it. The price stays locked on the line
  (`unit_amount`, `amount`, NUMERIC(18,4)) — a later price change does not move a quote
  already given.
* *Waive the fee* on step 5 stored the word `waive` in `fee_method` and marked no line
  waived, so the request went on owing the full amount. **Ruled:** it leaves the
  payment-method picker and becomes the per-line **Waive** column, backed by the existing
  `POST …/fees/{feeId}/waive` with its required reason.
* **Correction recorded, because it was said to the PO:** the coordinator first told the PO
  a fee line stores no price. It does — `money_field()` declares `unit_amount` and `amount`,
  and a grep for `models.` never matched them. Law 7's fifth shape, in the coordinator's own
  search.

### 3 · `OQ-357` CLOSED — BOTH: REMOVE ON A DRAFT, WAIVE ONCE SUBMITTED

The approved layout carries both controls on step 5 only, which is the question's own
third reading. Recorded in the register row with the worked case and the rule.

### 4 · *APPROVE* CHECKS THE PROPERTY AND UNIT FIRST — AND SAYS WHAT IT FOUND

**PO, verbatim, first:** *"on this screen when user select move-in , also check whether
premise available and unit without this check move-in not work , This check is not required
in newconnection ; In case of New connect duplicate premise and unit should not be created
… also infomation layout in side modal is not effectieve for user how can we make it
effective amd improve readability"* — asking for the plan in a table **before any change**.
The plan was put; then, verbatim: *"but we are not showing all this issues to user when
they are processing ehnce they dont understand what is hapening"*. **Read as go, with a
requirement added**, and recorded as that reading so it can be overturned in one word.

**WHAT WAS FOUND, measured:** approval checks only arrears, documents (reporting since
2026-09-16), eligibility and the fee — **nothing about the property or the unit.** A move-in
approval queues a `move_in_jobs` row; the unit is checked only when the account opens
(`_refuse_if_unit_occupied`, locked with `FOR UPDATE OF accounts`) — **on move day**.
**The PO's own list is the case:** `SR-26-0016` (Tim David) and `SR-26-0013` (District
Court) both ask for **U-00003** at highland park; both could be approved today, and the
second fails only when its account is opened.

**RULED — MOVE-IN, at Approve, blocking, and each refusal NAMED on screen:**
(1) the address resolved to a premises on the register · (2) a unit is chosen where the
premises has units · (3) **the unit is free** — no live account occupies it, read through
the ONE existing `occupying_accounts_for_unit`, so a vacant unit billed to a MASTER account
counts as FREE (master and owner accounts name no unit) · (4) no other move-in is already
waiting for that unit. The move-day lock stays as the backstop for a unit taken between
approval and move day.

**RULED — NEW CONNECTION:** no availability check (the PO's words). **No duplicate premises
and no duplicate unit:** a resolved address reuses its premises (already true); a NEAR match
is offered before anything is created (*"Looks like Highland Park, 58502. Use this?"*), the
clerk deciding, as the owner match already works (PO decision 3); the same unit label twice
on one premises is refused; a second open build for the same address is refused.

**THE REQUIREMENT THE PO ADDED — and it is the larger half:** *every problem found while a
request is processed reaches the clerk in plain words, on the screen they are looking at* —
at Approve, on the Move-ins tab when the account opens, and wherever a job is refused
(`raise_job`'s `not_raised`). A refusal that exists only as a code, a log line or a toast
that vanishes is the defect the PO is describing.

**THE MODAL:** checks first as ✓ / ✗ / ! rows; the five-row *Now / Next / Not now* table
becomes two lines in the kit's `ConsequenceBox`; the two kinds side by side; **Approve
disabled with its reason while any ✗ remains**; no scrolling at laptop size. This departs
from blueprint p083–p084's construction, not its content (B14 rule 38) — which is why it
was put to the PO rather than done.

**SEQUENCED after lane REQ-FIX lands**, because `ServiceRequestDetailPage.tsx` is live under
two lanes.

**PO, verbatim, on the Move-in sketch:** *"this is good - please please ensure you follow ui
styleguide and correct tailwind components"* — and asked to see the New connection view.
Then, verbatim: *"start it"*. Lane APPROVE-CHECKS dispatched the same hour. This records
what was APPROVED, so a lane that has to rebuild it builds the same thing.

**MOVE-IN (approved):**
```
Approve SR-26-0016 · Tim David
What kind    (●) Move-in      ( ) New connection
Checks
 ✓  Property    highland park, Ottumwa
 ✓  Unit        U-00003 · 1
 ✗  Unit free   Occupied · AC-2026-00012      (red — the blocker)
 !  Documents   2 not checked                  (amber — noted, not blocking)
```

**NEW CONNECTION (shown to the PO the same turn):** no *Unit free* row. Rows —

address` · documents · fee; consequence *"Raises a build on New connects. / Service starts
when the build finishes."*; button *Approve and raise the build*. A NEAR address match reads

premises is ever created by default. A second open build reads `✗ Open build · NC-26-0004

rows on `components/Chain.tsx` (`ok` / `bad`, with the amber *noted, not blocking* tone
ADDED TO THE KIT), the consequence on `ConsequenceBox`, the fee read-back on `RecapBox`;

`route-b-migrated.txt`; rule 33's caps; rule 31 (account and unit NUMBERS, never ids); US
English; no scrolling at 1440×900; usable at phone width. **The lane returns screenshots of
both variants**, because the PO is judging the look and no gate reads rendered output
(hard-won law 6).

**⚠ AMENDED THE SAME HOUR — "THE REGISTER" IS NOT A WORD A CLERK READS.** The PO read the
New connection sketch above and asked, verbatim: *"what does this mean - Address · on the
register?"* "The register" is our internal name for the premises list; the clerk knows it
as **Premises**, the sidebar word. So on screen: `✓ Address · Found in Premises`, and a new
address reads `New · the build adds it`. **"Register" appears in no clerk-facing string**,

matched"* is renamed the same way. Code and documents may keep the word.

## 2026-09-23 — ⛔ SUPERSEDED BY THE PO: THE NEW-CONNECTION RULE IN THE TWO ENTRIES ABOVE IS WRONG

**The two entries above headed *"… *APPROVE* CHECKS THE PROPERTY AND UNIT BEFORE IT IS PRESSED"*
(§4, *"RULED — NEW CONNECTION"*) and *"THE *APPROVE* WINDOW'S TWO LAYOUTS, APPROVED"* state
that a new connection at an address found in Premises REUSES that premises and goes ahead.
The PO has overruled that. Do not build it.** The MOVE-IN half of both entries stands.

**PO, verbatim:** *"no this is wrong - we should allow only if address is not available in
register. if addrss is available then we need to check its status - on active presmies we
cannot do new conenct - sicne it is physical address and service conenctions build process
- youa re not applying the correct logic - please confirm your understand in this chat"*.

**THE RULE, AS UNDERSTOOD:** a new connection BUILDS a physical service connection, so it
is refused at a property that is already connected. **The coordinator's first restatement
read "active" from `premises.status` — and that is the wrong signal, found by lane
APPROVE-CHECKS before anything was built:**
* `premises.status` is a stored column, `draft | pending | active | inactive`
  (`metering/models.py:463`, `services.py:170`), and **every premises is written `active`
  at creation** unless the caller says otherwise (`services.py:2002`, `create_premises`) —
  including every premises the New connect build itself creates. The only screen door moves
  it `active ↔ inactive` (`services.py:2187`); `draft` and `pending` have no screen door.
* So refusing a new connection on status `active` would refuse it at almost every address
  on file, including one created yesterday with nothing built on it.

**PUT TO THE PO FOR CONFIRMATION (`OQ-CUS-12615`), recommended:** a premises is **already
connected** if it has ANY of — an installed meter on it or its units · a live account on it
or its units (which covers trash and fire, which have no meter) · an `activated` build
(`connections.state`). All three because the utility's existing premises arrived by IMPORT,
not through a build, so *activated build* alone would miss nearly all of them. Then:
**not in Premises → allowed, the build creates it · in Premises and NOT connected → allowed,
the build uses that record (no duplicate) · in Premises and connected → refused, "Already
connected. Use a move-in." · near match → the clerk confirms it is the same place, then the
above.** This makes the status column irrelevant to the decision, which also settles
`draft`/`pending`/`inactive`.

**Lane APPROVE-CHECKS holds all new-connection code unpushed** until the PO answers.

**The lesson, since it cost a round trip:** the coordinator restated a PO rule in terms of a
column it had not read, and the first thing the column's own definition said contradicted
the restatement. Read the field before naming it as the test.

## 2026-09-23 — RULED: A NEW CONNECTION ONLY WHERE THE ADDRESS IS NOT IN PREMISES — IN ANY STATUS (`OQ-CUS-12615` CLOSED)

**PO, verbatim, confirming:** *"this si correct understanding"* — against: **not in Premises →
allowed, the build creates the property · in Premises and active → refused, "Use a move-in"
· close to an existing address → the clerk first confirms whether it is the same property,
then one of the two applies.** And on the other three statuses, verbatim: *"we dont allow
these status - dont create new request even if property is in draft, pending or inactive"*.

**THE RULE, FINAL:** **presence in Premises refuses a new connection, whatever
`premises.status` says.** Nothing reads the status column for this decision — which makes
the lane's finding (every premises is written `active` at creation, so the column cannot
mean *connected*) irrelevant to it. The *already connected* test the coordinator proposed an
hour earlier (meter · live account · activated build) is **not adopted.**

**WHAT THE LANE BUILDS:**
* not in Premises → allowed; the build creates the premises (it is always new, so no
  duplicate premises can arise from a new connection);
* in Premises, any status → refused, naming the property:
  *"Highland Park is in Premises. Use a move-in."* (rule 33: two sentences, each ≤6 words);
* a NEAR match → the clerk confirms same-or-new before Approve is enabled; *same* → refused
  as above; *new* → allowed;
* two OPEN new-connection requests for the same new address → the second is refused, since
  both would create a premises for it (the one duplicate this rule still leaves open).

**Stated consequence, recorded once and not re-asked:** a property keyed into Premises ahead
of its connection (a lot entered as draft or pending) cannot take a new connection; its first
connection has to be the build that creates it.

## 2026-09-23 — RULED: NO APPLICATION FEE IS EVER CARRIED TO AN ACCOUNT — IT IS PAID OR WAIVED. ONE COLLISION PUT BACK (`OQ-CUS-12617`), AND THE MOVE-IN WIZARD'S FIRST-OCCUPANT DEAD END (`DEF-CUS-6353`)

**PO, verbatim:** *"there are no unpaid fees either applcition fee is paid or it is waived -
so this is not applicable anymore"* — said of step 4 of the move-in approval flow ruled an
hour earlier (`OQ-CUS-12616`), which read *"fee PAID → recorded as revenue; fee UNPAID →
carried to the customer's account"*.

### 1 · WHAT IT WITHDRAWS, AND WHAT WAS STOPPED

The UNPAID half of step 4 is gone. **Lane FEE-ATTACH, dispatched to build it, was stopped
before it wrote anything** — nothing on the branch, confirmed against the tip. Step 4 now
reads: **paid → recorded as revenue (already built, `_release_counter_fee`) · waived →
nothing owed.** `OQ-CUS-12616`'s body is amended in the same commit, not only its status.

⚠ **AND THE GAP IT WAS ANSWERING WAS MISDESCRIBED — BY ME, TO THE PO.** I told the PO the
unwired piece was *"unpaid fee carried to the account"* and cited `DEF-PAY-5394`. That
defect is the opposite case: `attach_to_account` (`apps/payments/counter_receipts.py` §3)
is the RECORD-KEEPING half of a PAID fee — the $25.00 taken at the counter appearing in
the new account's payment history — under the 2026-09-15 ruling *"when it is approved you
can attached it to account"*, which is about money already TAKEN. The books are right
without it. **So `DEF-PAY-5394` stays open, unchanged by this ruling**, and the PO was told
so in one line. The ruling itself does not depend on the misreading: an unpaid fee has
nowhere to go either way.

### 2 · THE COLLISION THIS OPENS — PUT BACK, NOT ASSUMED (`OQ-CUS-12617`)

On **2026-09-21** the PO said *"make application fees optional - so that we can approve
it"*, and lane APP-8 built it as `fee_condition` → `blocking: False`: **Approve goes through
over an unpaid fee** (walked on `SR-26-0015`, `$20.00` outstanding after approval). Today's
statement says an unpaid fee does not exist at approval. Both are genuine; they cannot both
hold, and law 13 puts exactly this kind back to the PO with the supersession stated.
**Worked:** SR-26-0014 quotes **$45.00**, collected **$0.00** — (a) Approve stays off until
paid or waived, or (b) it goes through and the $45.00 sits on the request, where nothing now
collects it. **Recommended (a).** **Until answered, `fee_condition` is left exactly as the
tip has it**, and lane APPROVE-CHECKS draws the Fee row from the server's `blocking` flag
with no *"unpaid fee moves to …"* sentence for either kind — so the answer moves one flag.

### 3 · THE MOVE-IN WIZARD REFUSES A UNIT NOBODY HAS LIVED IN — `DEF-CUS-6353`

The PO sent a screenshot of Accounts → Move-ins → New, step 1, **highland park · U-00003**,
and asked *"why are you showing this message tell me in table"*. The message:
*"This unit has no finished tenancy to follow, so there is no closing account for a move-in
to succeed. Open it as a new account instead — it takes the same checks. + New account"*.

**Why it shows:** the wizard was built as the continuation of a move-OUT — its own header
says *"the start date is the day after that account's move-out"* — and its endpoint is
account-scoped, so it needs a closed previous account at the unit. U-00003 has never had an
account. **The list offers it anyway**, because the unit list reads `occupancy=vacant`,
and a unit nobody has ever lived in is vacant. So the screen offers what it then refuses,
in 26 words of rationale (B14 rule 33 puts rationale at zero).

**Why it cannot stay:** `OQ-CUS-12616`, ruled today, sends the clerk from an approved
move-in straight to the move-in *"to set the move-in date and the first meter reading"*, and
the Approve checks require only that the property and unit exist and the unit is free —
which U-00003 passes. **So a real approved request for a new unit would land on this
refusal.** The ruled flow already requires the wizard to take it.

**DECIDED, NOT ASKED (law 13 — the PO's ruled flow settles it):** the move-in wizard serves
a first-occupant unit. Step 1 names it as the first occupant instead of a previous account;
the clerk picks the start date (there is no move-out to follow) and enters the first
reading; the server opens the account under the SAME guards `POST /accounts` already takes
(`BR-CUS-017` unit free, `BR-CUS-056`), and a linked move-in job closes as it does today.
The refusal key is retired, not reworded. **Worked:** highland park U-00003, no account
ever → today: the red strip and a link out; after: *First occupant*, a start date, a first
read, an account opened. **One condition sends it back to the PO:** if the Accounts
blueprint DRAWS the move-in as predecessor-only or draws this refusal, the drawing
contradicts the ruled flow and the lane reports that instead of building (B14 rule 41).

## 2026-09-23 — RULED: THE DEPOSIT IS THE PLAN'S FIGURE FOR THE CUSTOMER'S CATEGORY, WITH NO OVERRIDE (`BR-RAT-020`/`023` made the default; `OQ-CUS-12620` opened)

**PO, verbatim, on the move-in Deposit step (ACC-05 step 5):** *"you need to take deposit
amount as per plan ; plan will have deposite chanrge code as per customer categoris ;so that
value should be atken as by default no override is required"*.

**WHAT IT SUPERSEDES — A DESIGN, NOT A SIGNED RULE.** `depositCapability.tsx` §*"THE AMOUNT IS
TYPED, AND THAT IS THE DRAWING'S OWN RULING"*: the Amount box was empty and typed by hand, the
blueprint's own helper read *"Typed by hand today"*, and the server resolved the plan figure
(`plan_deposit_rules`, rate plan × account type) only to REPORT it beside what was typed
(`deposit.take` → `plan_standard`, *"reported and never enforced"*). **The signed rules already
agreed with the PO** — `BR-RAT-020` (*"fixed $ amounts per consumer category"*) and `BR-RAT-023`
(*"Deposit schedule is PLAN-level"*) — so this collides with nothing signed; it makes the signed
figure the one the screen uses. **The figure now comes from the plan on the unit, for the
category picked on the Customer step, and the clerk cannot change it; the server takes it from
the plan and does not trust a figure sent from the screen.**

**What follows from it, decided here (law 13) rather than asked:**
* **"Why this amount" goes.** Its four reasons (standard · no credit history · previous arrears ·
  returning customer) are the grounds for a *typed* judgement; a fixed figure has no judgement to
  justify. Deleted from the screen, not reworded (B14 rule 33).
* **No plan figure for this category → no deposit is asked**, and the step says so in a few
  words; nothing can be typed in its place. `BR-RAT-020` has no fallback figure and inventing one
  would be the override the PO just ruled out.
* **A waive now leaves a mark on the ACCOUNT.** Asked what *Waive* does, the honest answer was:
  a supervisor forgives the figure, no money is taken, nothing reaches the first bill — and **the
  only record is the account-opening row in `audit_log`**, which is pruned (`OQ-1340`, closed
  2026-09-23: no row is exempt). So a year later a $150.00 waive and a *No* look identical on the
  account. That is a defect, not a question: a waive is a money decision with a person behind it
  (`deposit.py`: *"not_required and waived are different facts and must never collapse"*), and it
  had collapsed at rest. The account keeps who waived it, when, the figure, and a short reason.

**Put back, not assumed — `OQ-CUS-12620`:** with no override, *No* on a plan that asks a deposit
is an override by another name, and it needs no supervisor where *Waive* does. **Worked:** Rosa
Pemberton, Residential, plan asks **$150.00** — a billing clerk's *No* opens the account owing no
deposit with nobody's approval. Recommended (a): *No* only where the plan asks none.

**Worked, end to end after the fix:** the unit's plan asks Residential **$150.00** · Rosa is
Residential · the step shows **Deposit $150.00**, not editable · *Taken today* → a $150.00
deposit payment (`DR` undeposited · `CR` 2300 deposit liability, `BR-CUS-025`) · not taken →
it falls on the first bill · *Waive* (supervisor) → nothing taken, the account reads *Deposit
waived · $150.00*.

## 2026-09-23 — THE TRANSFER WIZARD (TRF-02): THE PO'S REPORT, HELD FOR THEIR CONFIRMATION; ONE VOCABULARY RULE; ONE FIELD-VISIT COMPONENT

**The PO reported the sale-transfer wizard on the sample tenant** (A-11512, Hollis, Marcus, 61
Larkspur Way · Unit 1; buyer *tim Aiden*; sale 24-Sep-26) and then said, verbatim: *"please list
down all fixed and solution in table format … dont start the lane yet for transfer bugs"*.
⚠ **A lane had already been dispatched minutes earlier; it was STOPPED on that sentence and had
pushed nothing** (its worktree held no change). The list below went to the PO; **no transfer
fix is built until they confirm it.** Every item is a DEFECT by default in the beta.

**Measured before the reply, so the PO was told causes and not guesses:**
* **The sale failed at the very end** — *"A-11512 is not linked to a customer. Link it to one
  first."* (`transfers.py` `REFUSAL_NO_CUSTOMER`). The sample account has no linked customer,
  which is also why step 1 printed *Customer number —* and *Customer kind —*. The wizard let the
  clerk walk five steps before refusing. What a sale of an unlinked account should DO is put to
  the PO (`OQ` below).
* **Base charge, Billing cycle, Current period, Next bill, Ledger** read *"Not available yet"*
  because `TransferWizard.tsx` HARD-CODES them (`unserved("DEF-CUS-5182")`). The screen never asks.
* **Sub-category is never rendered**, and its justifying comment (*"`account_subtypes` holds ZERO
  rows — measured"*) is stale: the seed carries 13. Hard-won law 1.
* **Nobody is told about the sale; autopay and the bill email stay the seller's; the property's
  owner record is not updated; a co-applicant is captured and not stored** — each is a named gap
  in `transfers.py` (`CONTACT_DETAILS_UNCHANGED`, `PREMISES_OWNER_NOT_UPDATED`,
  `CO_APPLICANT_NOT_STORED` → `OQ-CUS-12514`), rendered to the clerk as rationale.

**RULED — ONE WORD FOR WHERE THE BILL GOES.** PO, verbatim: *"Bill goes elsewhere - it should
mailing address , we should use same vocablory in everywhere; take USA Address specific
fields"*. **Mailing address** on every screen (the stored kind is already `kind='mailing'`,
hard rule 8's permitted exception), entered through the one US-address component
(`components/UsAddressFields.tsx`) with a *Same as service address* tick. Any screen still saying
*Bill goes elsewhere* or a synonym is a defect against this row.

**DECIDED (B14 rule 38 — construction is ours): ONE FIELD-VISIT COMPONENT, INLINE ADD, FOR EVERY
FLOW.** PO on the transfer: *"it should be dropdown please use table array component with add
option; also have no visit required option"*. The move-in design approved an hour earlier added
rows through a modal on the PO's permissive *"you can use modal"*; two constructions for one
thing is what rule 43 forbids. Lane MOVEIN-WIZ builds ONE component — a kit table-array with
*+ Add work order*, the approved columns (Job type · Priority · Due · Assigned to · Status · Note
· 🗑) and a *No visit needed* tick — which move-in mounts now and transfer mounts once confirmed.
The PO was told the modal step is gone.

## 2026-09-23 — CORRECTED BY THE PO: T1's SEARCH IS FOR THE BUYER, ON STEP 2 — AND WHAT THAT LEAVES FOR THE SELLER; THE LIST RELEASED; *DOWNLOAD ERROR REPORT* DOES NOTHING ON 99 SCREENS

**PO, verbatim:** *"my bad search custoemr id should be on step 2 - not on step 1"*, then
*"no we have to search custoemr id for buyer hence on step 2"*. **The two entries above that
place the search on step 1 for the SELLER are SUPERSEDED.** The *Search customer* finder
(one match → details, several → a table, none → *Create customer*) belongs to **step 2, The
buyer**: find the buyer's existing customer number and link it, or create a new one. It is
New Connect's finder, extracted into one component.

**WHAT IT LEAVES, DECIDED RATHER THAN ASKED (law 13):** the seller-side refusal that started T1
— A-11512 has no linked customer, so the sale was refused after five steps — is not answered by
a buyer search. **The sale goes ahead and the seller is recorded by the name on the account**
(*Hollis, Marcus*). This is the posture `transfers.py` already takes one row over for a missing
contact — *"a buyer must not lose a property because a row nobody ever created is missing"* —
and refusing would leave this sale impossible to complete from the wizard at all. The PO was
told this reading in the same reply.

**THE LIST IS RELEASED:** *"these are all good fix it … please address them before you start
the lane"*. Addressed in the reply, then the lane started. The three points:
* **#9 documents** — *"you have to take buyer documents - as we have taken document in move in
  or new connect or new request"*: the buyer step uses the SAME document capture those three
  screens use (`components/documents` `DocumentCapture`), not a variant.
* **#10 why remove *"A phone identifies a person here"*** — answered: only the sentence, never
  the Phone field; B14 rule 33 keeps an explanation off screen. **But the sentence carries a fact
  the clerk needs** — on this step a phone is enough to identify the buyer (it may CREATE a
  person; `BR-CUS-1024` still refuses ATTACHING on a phone) — so it becomes a six-word
  INSTRUCTION beside the identifiers, *"Give one ID or a phone."*, not a deletion.

  screens (`onDownloadReport={() => undefined}`, and `WizardFrame` passes `noop`). Hard-won law

## 2026-09-23 — BUILT: THE DEPOSIT IS THE PLAN'S FIGURE; *NO* ONLY WHERE THE PLAN ASKS NONE; A WAIVE IS KEPT ON THE ACCOUNT (lane DEPOSIT, `DEF-CUS-6369`/`6370`/`6371`, `OQ-CUS-12620` (a))

Built to the two rulings of this date (*THE DEPOSIT IS THE PLAN'S FIGURE…* and `OQ-CUS-12620`
(a)). **Worked, proved in a browser and on PostgreSQL:** the unit's plan asks Residential
**$150.00** (Commercial $400.00, Industrial nothing); Rosa Pemberton is Residential → the
Deposit step shows **150.00**, not editable, with *Yes — take one* / *Waive it* and no *No*;
taken today → ONE $150.00 deposit payment, `DR 1010 Undeposited funds / CR 2300 Customer
deposit liability`; not taken → assessed $150.00, falls on the first bill; a Billing Clerk's
waive → *"Only a supervisor may waive this. Ask one to approve it."*; a System Admin's waive
with *Hardship* → nothing taken and the Deposit tile reads **Waived · $150.00** with who and
when. Change the category to Commercial → **400.00**; to Industrial → *No deposit on this
plan.* and nothing to pick or type.

**Judgments made here, not asked (law 13):**
* **The server REFUSES a figure that is not the plan's rather than silently using the plan's.**
  The block may omit `amount` (the plan's is used). If it sends one, it is the figure the clerk
  saw and quoted; if the plan was edited in between, substituting would charge a customer an
  amount nobody at the counter saw. So `customers.deposit.amountNotPlan` — *"Deposit must match
  the plan."* — and the clerk steps back to read the new figure. Either way no override exists.
* **A request with NO `deposit` block is *No*, on the two doors that ask the question**
  (`POST /accounts`, `POST /accounts/{id}/move-in`) — so a hand-built request cannot skip a
  deposit the plan asks by leaving the block off. `create_account(require_deposit_answer=…)`
  defaults ON (the `require_identity` shape); no caller passes it off in the product. Other
  creators (import, transfer, `_open_account` direct) are untouched.
* **A plan rule of 0.00 is "asks none"**, not "asks zero" — a zero deposit cannot be taken
  (`record_deposit_movement` refuses a zero movement) or forgiven.
* **The one condition `OQ-CUS-12620` moved is `deposit.plan_asks_deposit()` + the single
  `not_required` refusal in `take()`.** Option (b) would have deleted that one line.
* **The credit-tier note went with *Why this amount*** — both existed to justify a TYPED
  figure (rule 33: rationale removed, not shortened). The server stays tolerant of a `reason`.
* **`deposit_not_applied` is dropped from the answer on these two doors** — its sentence says
  the plan lookup *"is not built"*, and on S18/S19 it has just run. Every other door keeps it.
* **The step reads the figure by `GET /accounts/deposit-standard?unit_id=&account_type=`** —
  the same walk the commit takes (`deposit.standard_for_unit` → `seams.deposit_rule_for_account`
  → `rating.deposit_rule_for`), so screen and commit cannot disagree.

**Found and NOT fixed — needs the PO (`DEF-CUS-6372`):** `BR-CUS-1050` names System Admin OR
Executive as the supervisor who may waive, but A4 (signed) makes an Executive *View* on
Accounts — so the New account and Move-in doors refuse an Executive before the deposit is ever
asked (*"Your role can view accounts but not change them."*, measured signed in as Avery Cole).
**In practice only a System Admin can waive today.** Letting an Executive waive means either a
second-person approval (clerk asks, supervisor approves) or widening A4 — a signed grid, so it
is the PO's. Pinned by `test_cr094_wh__an_executive_cannot_reach_the_waive_today`.

## 2026-09-23 — JUDGMENT (lane LANG-MSG): *THE UTILITY'S DEFAULT LANGUAGE* IS ASKED FOR AS ITS REGIONAL CODE, NOT AS "NO LANGUAGE"

**The ruling being built:** `OQ-CUS-12619` (a) — *"Portal only; emails in English."* A message
takes the utility's default language, never `accounts.preferred_language`; the variant model is
untouched (`BR-NOT-006` amended). **Where the rules ran out:** the variant model has TWO ways to
say "the utility's language" — the `default` sentinel variant (by the model's own definition *"the
tenant's own default-language variant"*) and a variant tagged with the utility's own Regional
code (`es-MX`). A writer that passes no language gets only the first; a writer that passes the
Regional code gets the second where one is published and falls back to the first.

**Chosen: the six writers that read the customer's preference now pass the utility's Regional
code** (Settings → Regional, through `seams.tenant_default_language` in customers and in
metering — one read per module over `tenancy.selectors.regional_settings`, no second way to read
it). **Why not "no language":** the OQ row says *"a utility with a Spanish default still sends
Spanish"*. A Spanish-default utility whose Spanish wording is a published `es-MX` variant keeps
sending it this way; passing nothing would silently switch every one of its customers to the
English platform wording. **Worked:** Rosa, Spanish, at Brazos Bend (Regional `en-US`, an `es`
variant published) → acknowledgement pinned to the default English wording; the same request at
a utility whose Regional language is `es` → pinned to the `es` variant; her portal answers `es`
either way.

**What this leaves, filed rather than fixed (`DEF-NOT-6379`):** the writers that never passed a
language — bill emails, receipts, reminders, the welcome, move-out and account-closed letters —
still ask for nothing and always get the `default` wording. The two agree unless a utility
publishes a variant under exactly its own Regional code, which no utility has today. Making them
one is a single decision for whoever takes `DEF-NOT-6379`. The Settings → Notifications language
choice per channel is saved and read by nothing (`DEF-NOT-6355`); its label now says *"Utility's
default language"* because that is what every message gets. Built under `DEF-NOT-6354`, version `2.348.2`.

## 2026-09-23 — DECIDED (lane ERROR-REPORT, `DEF-SHL-6377`): WHAT THE ERROR REPORT CARRIES, AND WHAT IT WITHHOLDS

The ruling above (*"Fixed once, in the shared failure panel"*) is built. Pressing *Download error
report* on any failure panel now saves `<screen>-error-<yyyymmdd-hhmm>.txt`. **The worked case,
the PO's own:** selling `A-11512` (no linked customer) on the demo utility and pressing the button
saved `TRF-02-error-20260923-1555.txt`, which reads, below a header saying what it leaves out:
`Screen: TRF-02` · `Page: /brazosbend/transfers/new?step=5` · `Time: 2026-09-23 15:55:03
America/Chicago` · `Version: 2.347.2` (the proof build; the fix ships as `2.350.2`) · the panel's two sentences as shown · `Method: POST` ·
`Path: /transfers/commit` · `Status: 409` · `Code: BIZ-STATE` · `Message key:
customers.transfer.from_account_has_no_customer` · `Reference: D2D8-A591`. The buyer's typed name
and Social Security number were on the form and are not in the file.

**Four judgments where no rule reached, decided rather than asked (law 13):**
* **The request is noted by the transport, not threaded through the screens.** The panel is
  handed two sentences and never the error, and threading the error would edit 101 call sites
  under other lanes (law 11). `api/client.ts` notes every refusal it throws — method, contract
  path with the query cut off, status, `code`, `message_key`, the short reference; never a body,
  never `params` — and the report takes the newest one that arrived no more than a minute before
  its panel appeared. With none, the file says so rather than guessing.
* **Record ids and links in addresses are withheld, UUIDs included.** The portal's draft link
  `/start-service/:draft` is a capability and it is a UUID (`portal/draftToken.ts`), so a rule
  keeping UUIDs as "just ids" would put a working link in a file somebody emails. Kept: route words
  and printed references (`A-11512`, `SR-26-0001`). Query VALUES are withheld except `step`, `tab`,
  `view`, `page`, `per`, `sort`. The support reference finds the refused attempt's audit row.
* **The file's labels are English in every language**; the clerk's two sentences travel verbatim.
  Support reads one format, the same reasoning `ScreenIdTag` records for the screen id.
* **A caller's own handler still runs, after the download.** `PaymentDetailPage` passes one that
  navigates back to the payments list, which is wrong for a button labelled *Download* — it now
  downloads and then navigates. Reported, not changed here.

**Left for the lanes that own them:** the 99 `onDownloadReport={() => undefined}` props are dead
and harmless (the prop is optional now), and `WizardFrame`'s `?? noop` likewise. `DEF-INT-5562`
(2026-09-16) proposed hiding the button instead; its download half is answered by this ruling,
its `onCancel` half (about forty `onCancel={() => undefined}`, measured 2026-09-23) is not, so it stays open.

## 2026-09-24 — DECIDED (lane SMALL-PAY, `DEF-PAY-6323`): THE DEMO STATES WHERE ITS MONEY CAME FROM, AND THE REPLAY GUARD IS A SECOND READ IN THE SEEDER

**The judgment, ours (law 13):** the sample set's card and ACH payments are recorded with the
`webhook` origin (*Digital*) and its cash and cheques with `entry` (*Counter*), decided by the
same `counters.HAND_TENDERS` question the till block asks, so the SOURCE and BATCH columns can
never disagree about a row. **Worked figure:** a fresh demo had **38** card/ACH payments reading
*Counter* (measured on the unchanged tip: `PY-260808-0001` card `entry` …); after the change it
has **0**. **The hazard the defect row named is closed by a READ, not by rewriting rows:** the
origin is the first segment of the idempotency key, so on a tenant seeded before today
`record_payment`'s replay read would miss and record a SECOND permanent payment per card/ACH
bill. The seeder now asks for the payment under the old `entry|…` key first and, on a hit,
answers exactly as `record_payment` answers a replay (`created=False`, nothing written).
`record_payment`, the key function and every other caller are untouched. **What stays as it
is:** a demo tenant loaded before today keeps *Counter* on its old card/ACH rows — `origin` is
not on `payments/0014`'s allow list and no row is rewritten. Proof:
`06-backend/tests/test_def_pay_6323_seeded_payment_source.py`.

## 2026-09-24 — EDIT ON A SERVICE REQUEST (lane REQ-EDIT, `DEF-CUS-6427`): THE JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULING RAN OUT

The ruling of 2026-09-23 (*"THE PO ASKS FOR *EDIT* ON A SERVICE REQUEST…"*) set the order and the
editable states. These are the calls the build had to make beyond it, recorded before they are
reported (law 9), none of them put back to the PO (law 13):

1. **A PATCH carries only what changed.** The wizard keeps the form as last saved (or as loaded)
   and sends the difference — `changedCapturePayload`. Worked: Dana Whitfield's request
   `SR-26-0048`, submitted with SSN `•••••5236`, email and phone; the clerk corrects the phone
   `512-555-0100` → `512-555-0199` and the PATCH is `{"applicant_phone": "512-555-0199"}` —
   one key, one audit row whose before/after is that one field. Before this, every step sent
   the whole form. A key that went from a value to empty is sent as `null` (JSON drops
   `undefined`, so clearing the job date would otherwise never arrive). A premises pick travels
   as a PAIR, because the server reads *both null* as *undo*.
2. **A masked value is a PLACEHOLDER, never a value.** The SSN box opens empty showing
   `••• ••• • 5236`; the licence `•••••9566`. Typed → sent; untouched → the key is absent
   (the server's *unchanged*); switching the applicant to a business → sent as `""`, which
   clears it (`BR-CUS-1022` refuses an SSN on a company). There is no code path that can send
   the mask.
3. **The server gate covers the wizard's three writes, not only the PATCH.** `update_request`
   refused only the TERMINAL states, so `approved`, `in_fulfilment` and `on_hold` took a PATCH
   silently. Now `update_request`, `set_customer_category` and `set_services` all refuse outside
   Draft · Submitted · Under review · More info — `approvedNoEdit` (*"Approved already. It
   can't be edited."*) or the existing `terminalNoEdit`. The resolver, documents and fees keep
   their own rules (fees: remove while Draft, waive after — `OQ-357`).
4. **On a request that has left Draft, the service address line is read-only** (`BR-CUS-070`
   already refuses it), the header button is *Save changes* and returns to the request, and the
   last step commits *Save changes ✓* — a submitted request is never re-submitted. The kicker
   reads *EDIT SR-26-0048*; the *Saved as draft* footer is not drawn (it would be false).
5. **The doors.** The requests list: the ✎ pencil (B14 rule 15's own glyph), labelled *Resume* on
   a Draft and *Edit* while Submitted, Under review or More info — beside the eye, which is rule
   15's maximum of two. The request's own page: a WORD button, *Edit* / *Resume*, secondary —
   an ordinary button says a word (PO 2026-08-20, *"this only for table actions ; not for
   buttons"*). **A decided request shows NO door, not a greyed one:** an approval cannot be
   undone, so the control could never be pressed again — the reasoning `PremisesDetailPage`
   records for its status control. A typed address onto a decided request gets the refusal
   sentence and no form.

SECURITY` a migration role with no tenant set counts zero rows (filed `DEF-TEN-6432`); the database's
