## 2026-09-24 — RULED: SEVEN ANSWERS IN ONE REPLY (P1–P7), ONE OF THEM A CORRECTION OF MY OWN READING, AND ONE A QUESTION I SHOULD NOT HAVE ASKED

**PO, verbatim, the whole reply:** *"p1 a, p2 a, p3 - clark and sysem admin can do it; p4 - i
already calrified this - all or waived - why you ask again and again - are we missing something
erhe? p5 yes all correct - Confirm all five as they are; p6 b) Keep a short version: "Medical
protections apply. Not shown here."; p7 (b) — nothing is lost, and the payment-row lock stays
exactly as it is"*.

| # | Register | Ruling | What is built |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `OQ-PAY-12621` | (a) | a cash application fee joins its counter's EXPECTED cash; the close balances; booked once |
| P2 | `OQ-PAY-12622` | (a) | the Debtors row shows *Write-off pending / approved / declined*; no Finance access moves |
| P3 | `OQ-CUS-12623` | a fourth answer | **a Billing Clerk or a System Admin waives a deposit** (`BR-CUS-1050` amended) |
| P4 | `OQ-CUS-12624` | already answered | **the counter takes the WHOLE application fee or it is waived; a short payment is refused** (`BR-CUS-090` stamped) |
| P5 | review ledger `CR-141` | confirmed | the five refund-correction defaults are signed |
| P6 | `OQ-PAY-12612` | (b) | *"Medical protections apply. Not shown here."* |
| P7 | `OQ-PAY-12608` | (b) | `payments.settlement_id` is dropped; `settlement_members` stays the one record |

⚠ **P3 CORRECTS ME.** On 2026-09-23 the PO wrote *"clark can waive it off"*; I recorded it as *"the
waive is the way out, not a widening of who may press it"* and kept the set at System Admin or
Executive. The PO meant the clerk. `OQ-CUS-12620`'s body is stamped CORRECTED in this commit.
**The lesson is a sharper form of law 13's own:** when a ruling's words name a person and the
option text names a different one, the PO's own words win — I chose the option text because it
was tidier.
⚠ **P4 WAS A QUESTION I SHOULD NOT HAVE ASKED, AND THE PO SAID SO.** `OQ-CUS-12617` had already
ruled *"either fee is paid or waived - no other condition"*. **What we were missing** — the answer
to the PO's own question — is the PO's 24 August rule (`BR-CUS-090`): the counter accepts LESS
than the fee and finance reconciles. That is the only road to a part-paid fee. Read by date, the
later ruling supersedes it for application fees. I put the collision back as a question instead
of stating the supersession and building it, which is exactly what my own note of 2026-09-23 says
not to do. Worked: $130.00 quoted, $25.00 offered → refused, *"Take the full $130.00, or waive
it."*; requests already part-paid keep what was taken and waive the rest.

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane RULINGS-0924, `DEF-CUS-6455`): P4 — THE WHOLE FEE OR WAIVED, AND FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULING DID NOT MAKE

`OQ-CUS-12624` (PO: *"all or waived"*) is built at the desk. `collect_fee` refuses any amount
that is not the fee still owing (quote less what an invoice settled), BEFORE a row is written:
quoted **$130.00**, **$25.00** offered → 422 `BIZ-COMPLETENESS`
`customers.serviceRequest.feeTakeInFull`, params `amount 130.0000 · currency USD`. The idempotent
replay of a receipt already taken still runs FIRST, so a double-click of a full payment returns
rather than being refused against an owing of $0.00. Proved on PostgreSQL 16 inside an enclosing
transaction (`10-scripts/def_cus_6455_whole_fee_pg_proof.py`, ALL PASS): $25.00 refused, the same
transaction then answers a query and holds no receipt, $150.00 refused, $130.00 taken in that same
transaction — one receipt, one balanced `130.0000` pair, one audit row — and the outer block commits.

**Four judgments, each ours to make (law 13), recorded here rather than asked:**

1. **More than the fee is refused too.** *"All"* is the fee, not more than it; the brief said the
   amount must EQUAL the fee owing. $150.00 against $130.00 gets the same sentence. The only
   remaining roads to more cash than quote are a line waived after collection and rows written
   before today, and the release still holds the excess in `2400` for both.
2. **The sentence is two sentences.** The worked words *"Take the full $130.00, or waive it."* are
   SEVEN tokens and G33 caps a sentence at six (B14 rule 33). Every word is kept and the comma
   becomes a stop: *"Take the full $130.00. Or waive it."* (4 + 3). The server sends the figure as
   stored; the modal formats that one refusal's `amount` through `formatMoney`.
3. **`feeAlreadyCollected` is reworded**, because it is the refusal a part-paid request now meets
   and it ended *"Waive the line, or approve anyway"* — false since `OQ-CUS-12617` put the fee back
   in front of Approve. It now states the fact only: *"Already taken on receipt {{receipt_no}}."*,
   in all eleven catalogues.
4. **The Okonkwo sample request (`SR-26-0042`) takes nothing.** It seeded $25.00 of $130.00 through
   `collect_fee`, which would now be refused, and its park note described a state the product can
   no longer reach. It waits on the whole $130.00, which is what its drawn `WAITING ON payment`
   always said. Tests that need a part-paid request write the columns as the pre-ruling code left
   them (*"requests already part-paid keep what was taken"*); two ledger-release tests reach their
   states by the roads that remain (a line waived, or a line added, after collection).

APPROVE-CHECKS' strict xfail (*"take the $105.00"*) is flipped to assert the refusal: the second
collection is refused naming `RCP-26-4471` and the waiver approves.
## 2026-09-24 — DECIDED (lane TRANSFER-2, `DEF-CUS-6431`): A PROPERTY CAN BE SOLD AGAIN — THE ONCE-EVER INDEX IS NARROWED, NOT DROPPED

**What was wrong, walked on a private copy of the sample utility:** A-11512 sold by *Hollis,
Marcus* to *Aiden, Tim* (`TRF-26-0001`), then resold by Tim to *Reyes, Carla* — refused at the
commit with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_transfers_to_account"`, which
reached the clerk as *"Something went wrong on our side."* `customers/0021` wrote that index for
the transfer as it was on 2026-08-25 — a customer MOVING, which opened a new account — so *"an
account is the incoming half of one transfer, ever"* was right. `BR-CUS-1030` (2026-09-01) made a
transfer a SALE that writes `to_account_id = from_account_id`, and the same index then meant
*"an account can be sold once, ever"*.

**JUDGMENT, OURS (law 13) — NARROW, DON'T DROP.** `customers/0069` replaces it with
`uq_transfers_opened_account`, the same columns `WHERE to_account_id IS NOT NULL AND
to_account_id <> from_account_id`. *One open sale per account at a time* was never this index's
job — it is `uq_transfers_open_from` (0021), untouched, and `transfers.sale_refusal` asks it by
name first (`from_account_already_being_sold`). Dropping the index outright would lose a guard
that still means something on rows of the moving shape (2026-08-25 → 2026-09-01); keeping it
whole makes every property sellable once. **Renamed** so an error names the rule that refused.

**THE ROLLBACK CAUTION, STATED:** the reverse re-creates the once-ever index and PostgreSQL
refuses it the moment any account has been sold twice; satisfying it would mean deleting a real
sale. Once a resale exists, roll forward. Ledger row: *"A property can be sold more than once"*.

**Proved, by the lane that wrote it (2026-09-24, worktree since removed):** red on SQLite and on
a PostgreSQL clone before the migration; after it, both sales `done` with the same account on both
sides and a second OPEN sale still refused by name; forward/back/forward on PostgreSQL; the wizard
sold A-11512 twice in a browser.

⚠ **RE-PROVED BEFORE THE PUSH, IN A DIFFERENT CONTAINER, BY THE LANE THAT LANDED IT** — the
original lane's container and its screenshots are gone, and a proof nobody can re-run is a claim
(hard-won law 1). On PostgreSQL 16, provisioned fresh: `tests/test_def_cus_6431_resale.py`,
`test_def_cus_6429_transfer_record_committed_by.py` and `test_def_cus_6462_transfers_sold_to.py`
— **10 passed** under `--ds=config.settings.pgtest`. The two read tests were shown RED first
against the tip's own `transfer_reads.py` (`v2.351.20`).

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane RULINGS-0924, `OQ-CUS-12623`): P3 — A BILLING CLERK WAIVES A DEPOSIT, AND FIVE JUDGMENTS THE RULING DID NOT MAKE

PO, verbatim: *"p3 - clark and sysem admin can do it"*. `deposit.WAIVE_ROLES` is now
`{billing_clerk, system_admin}`; it read `{system_admin, executive}` since the 2026-09-20 amendment
of `BR-CUS-1050`. **Worked, and it is the test's own figure:** a Billing Clerk (Marcus) opens Rosa
Alvarez's account on a plan asking **$150.00**, answers *Waive* with the reason *Hardship*, and the
move-in commits — no payment row, `deposit_waived_amount = 150.0000`, `deposit_waived_by` = the
clerk, and the account detail reads **Waived · $150.00** with who and why on the ROW (`audit_log`
is pruned with no row exempt, `OQ-1340`, so the commit's answer was never enough).

**Proved red, then green, in the harness that runs it** (hard-won law 7). Against the tip's code
`tests/test_cr094_wh_deposit.py` reported **2 failed, 30 passed** —
*"AssertionError: Extra items in the left set: 'executive' · Extra items in the right set:
'billing_clerk'"* — and **32 passed** after. Also proved on **PostgreSQL 16** (`--ds=config.
settings.pgtest`), because the waive WRITES three columns inside the move-in's one transaction
(hard-won law 14: `config/settings/test.py` hardcodes in-memory SQLite).

**Five judgments, each ours to make (law 13), recorded here rather than asked:**

1. **The refusal key is RENAMED, not reworded.** `customers.deposit.waiveNeedsSupervisor` →
   `customers.deposit.waiveNotYourRole`, in all eleven catalogues. A key naming a supervisor for a
   set that holds a clerk is this repo's most-filed rot (`amendment_history_is_not_a_permanent_
   record` is the precedent, `P3.18`). The sentence is *"Your role cannot waive a deposit. Ask a
   Billing Clerk."* — **6 words then 4**, B14 rule 33's instruction cap, two sentences of six
   beating one of twelve.
2. **An Executive is now refused BY NAME, and `DEF-CUS-6372` is CLOSED rather than pinned.** That
   defect was *the rule names two roles and the screens admit one*: `BR-CUS-1050` let an Executive
   waive while A4's signed grid gives them View on Accounts, so the door turned them away before
   the deposit step. The ruling takes the Executive out of the SET, so **the rule moved to meet the
   door** and the two now say the same thing. No permission moves. The test that pinned the old
   behaviour asserts the set instead, on the gate itself, because no screen lets an Executive reach
   it.
3. **The gate stays per-DECISION and never `@require_role` on the door.** A Billing Clerk may take,
   defer and decline a deposit all day — blueprint p073 draws them doing it — and only the third
   answer named an authority. Widening the set did not change that shape, so `_refuse_unless_
   may_waive` is still called from one line of `take()` and the refusal is still `BIZ-APPROVAL`
   inside `BR-SHL-019`'s one transaction: a refused waive rolls the account, the reads and the
   payment back together and the clerk fixes one field with everything still on screen.
4. **M6 of the nineteen move-in scenarios FLIPS from a refusal to a commit, and the actor stays a
   Billing Clerk on purpose.** The row existed to ask whether the product enforced p073's
   *"(needs a supervisor)"* parenthesis; it now proves the clerk CAN waive. Nine of its declared
   dimensions move with it — `deposit_register` from *no account exists* to **`Decimal("0")`**
   (*forgiven: nothing held*), `readings.move_in` 0 → 1, `unit_occupied` false → true,
   `move_record` none → `MVI-`, `customer_link` none → created — and `payment_rows` stays
   **0**, which is what waiving IS.
5. **`EXECUTIVE` leaves the import and stays in the docstring.** The 2026-09-20 reasoning is kept
   under a `⛔ SUPERSEDED` banner rather than deleted, so a reader who meets p073's parenthesis in
   the blueprint finds out why the code no longer enforces it. Blueprint p073 is NOT amended: B14
   rule 41 sends a drawing that contradicts a signed rule to the PO, and they have already ruled on
   this one.

**Already done before this lane started, and verified rather than repeated:** the register row
(`OQ-CUS-12623` CLOSED, `OQ-CUS-12620`'s body stamped CORRECTED) and `BR-CUS-1050`'s
`⛔ AMENDED 2026-09-24` clause were both landed by the coordinator. Closing a question is a fan-out;
this commit carries the code, the tests, the eleven catalogues and the two docstrings that still
described the old set.

## 2026-09-24 — RULED BY THE PO: THE MOVE-OUT'S STEP COUNT IS SETTLED IN THE WORKING CHAT, NOT READ OFF THE ACCOUNTS DRAWING

**PO, verbatim**, asked how many steps a move-out (ACC-06) should have and told that the answer
belongs to the drawn specification: *"lets do it ourself - you show me here and then we agree"*.

**WHAT THIS SUPERSEDES, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** B14 rule 41 says the product UI matches the
blueprint exactly and a screen is built to its drawn specification; `DEF-GOV-5248` (PO ruling
2026-09-14) hands LAYOUT, COPY, **FLOWS** and STATES to the blueprint for any module that has one,
and a wizard's STEP COUNT is a flow — that is the whole lesson of the bill run, built with six
steps from r10's stepper while its blueprint drew four and argued for them in prose, with four
further lanes building onto the wrong shape. **For the move-out wizard, and for nothing else, the
PO has chosen to settle the flow in the chat instead.** The Accounts blueprint remains the
specification for this screen's layout, copy and states; only the step count and what sits on each
step are being agreed here. A later lane finding the drawing and this entry in disagreement must
follow THIS entry for the step count, and must not "correct" the wizard back to the drawn number.

**WHAT PROVOKED IT.** Six reports from the PO in one hour, walking all six steps of the live
wizard at `v2.351.19`, every one of them naming the same fault in different words — *"too much
text on this screen please reduce it"*, *"too much inforation - reduce it"*, *"why this
information is required - it does not add any value to user"*, and finally the structural one:
*"also user expeirinceing rpeating of infrmaion on step 4 , 5 and 6 - can we reduce the steps"*.
The repetition is real and measured from their own screenshots: the subtraction is drawn on steps
3, 4 and 6; *What we'll send* on 5 and 6; *the unit falls vacant* and *the meters stay fitted* on
5 and 6.

**THE PROPOSAL PUT TO THEM — SIX INTO FOUR.** Step 1 *Find account* and step 2 *Date & reads*
stand. Steps 3 and 4 merge into one money step, because the shortfall is the bottom line of the
same subtraction the deposit is applied to, not a separate fact. Steps 5 and 6 merge into one
review, because **step 5 carries no input anywhere on it** — it was already a review page sitting
one click before the review page. Nothing is deleted by the merge itself; what goes is the
duplication and the rationale, under B14 rule 33.

**NOT AGREED AT THE TIME OF WRITING.** This row records the RULING ABOUT WHO DECIDES and the
proposal as put. The agreed shape is written here when the PO answers, and the wizard is not
rebuilt before that.

## 2026-09-24 — RULED BY THE PO: THE MOVE-OUT RAISES A **DRAFT** FINAL BILL AS THE CLERK WORKS, AND MARKS IT FINAL ON COMPLETION

**PO, verbatim**, asked whether a move-out should raise a draft final bill, having seen ACC-06
step 3 show *"Final bill, net — Not worked out yet"* with every deposit option greyed out:
*"it should generate draft bill during the process and mark it final once user complete the
process"*.

**WHAT THIS SETTLES.** The move-out flow is no longer a pure record that waits for billing's own
cycle. It RAISES a bill in draft while the wizard is being worked — so the subtraction has real
figures, the deposit can be settled against something, and the shortfall is a number rather than
*"Not worked out yet"* — and that same bill is marked FINAL when the clerk completes the flow.
The two letters that read *Not queued here* on step 5 (the deposit refund notice and the
shortfall demand letter) exist to follow that settlement, so they are downstream of this ruling.

⚠ **WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO, AND NOBODY MAY READ INTO IT.** It does not touch a ❄️ FROZEN
B4/B5 figure, it does not change how a bill is CALCULATED, and it does not make the move-out the
owner of billing's arithmetic — the draft is raised THROUGH billing, by billing's own rules, from
the move-out flow. Hard rule 4 is untouched: a draft that becomes final is a bill reaching its
issued state for the first time, never an UPDATE of an issued invoice. If building it turns out to
require a frozen figure to move, that STOPS and returns for a finance re-sign (HUMAN-GUIDE §6);
it is not covered by this ruling.

**STATUS: RULED, NOT YET SIZED.** A read-only investigation was already running when this ruling
arrived — what step 3 does today, why each deposit option is disabled, whether a draft or
off-cycle bill can be produced at all today, and what already stands ruled about it. The ruling
is recorded here first (law 9: write it down when it is made, not at the end), and the build is
scoped from what that investigation establishes, because whether this is *wire up something that
exists* or *build a final-bill path that does not* changes the shape of the work entirely.

## 2026-09-24 — FOUR ANSWERS ON THE MOVE-OUT, AND ONE OF THEM SUPERSEDES B14 RULE 33

Four questions were put to the PO in plain English with a worked figure each, in one table. Their
answers, **verbatim**, in the order asked:

| Question as put | PO's answer |
|---|---|
| The empty unit's charges — keep them on screen? | *"(a) Keep, as one line in 'The unit'"* |
| *"field visit is options hence no field visit options hould be available"* — which way? | *"(a) Keep 'No visit needed'"* |
| Shorten the four shortfall path names? | *"b) Leave as drawn"* |
| Two account-number formats | *"(b) They're different tenants and both are correct"* |

**1 · THE VACANT CHARGES STAY, AS ONE LINE.** The *Not stated here* panel on the review is deleted
(rationale, B14 rule 33) and this one row is NOT deleted with it: it carries real money —
Water `$8.00` · Sewer `$9.00` · Trash `$0.00` · Solar `$0.00` · Battery `$5.00` · Fire `$0.00`,
**`$22.00` a month** once the unit stands empty. It moves into *The unit* as ONE line naming the
monthly total with the services behind it, exactly as put to them. A clerk closing an account can
see what the empty unit will be charged; nothing explains why.

**2 · *NO VISIT NEEDED* STAYS.** The PO's sentence was ambiguous — it reads equally as *"a visit
is optional, so offer a no-visit choice"* and as *"remove the no-visit choice"*. It was put to
them both ways rather than guessed, and they kept it. This also keeps the move-out consistent with
the transfer, where the PO asked for exactly that option on 2026-09-23 (*"also have no visit
required option"*), and with `FieldVisitOrders.tsx`, the one component all three flows mount.

**3 ⚠ THE FOUR PATH NAMES STAY LONG, AND THAT SUPERSEDES B14 RULE 33 FOR THESE FOUR LABELS.** The
names on the drawing are *Pursue it* · *Put it on a payment plan* · *Write it off* · *Tie it back
to the master account*. Rule 33 caps a LABEL at **three words and no sentence**, so three of the
four breach it (5, 3 and 7 words). The PO was shown the shortened set — *Pursue · Payment plan ·
Write off · To master account* — and ruled *"Leave as drawn"*. **So the drawing wins for these
four strings and rule 33 is not applied to them.** This is recorded rather than quietly obeyed
because the next lane to run a copy audit will find four labels over the cap and "fix" them; it
must not. The supersession is NARROW: four labels on ACC-06 step 4, nothing else on the screen,
and no change to rule 33 anywhere else in the product.

**4 · TWO ACCOUNT-NUMBER FORMATS ARE BOTH CORRECT — THEY ARE DIFFERENT TENANTS.** `A-10650` and
`AC-2026-00025` are not a defect and nothing is unified; `seed_demo` mints the `AC-2026-#####`
form, and the utility the PO is walking uses `A-#####`. **The live consequence is one string:**
ACC-06 step 1's help text told a clerk to *"type the account number as your lists show it
(AC-2026-00025)"* — a format that tenant's lists never show. That text is being deleted anyway as
over-budget copy, and the ruling means **no example is put back in its place**: a per-tenant format
cannot be hardcoded in a shared string. No defect is filed for the two schemes.

## 2026-09-24 — RULED: THE MOVE-OUT IS **FOUR** STEPS, AND THE LAYOUTS ARE SHOWN BEFORE ANYTHING IS BUILT

**PO, verbatim**, on the six-into-four proposal put to them step by step: *"i okay with these
steps"* — then, in the same breath: *"can you show me all 4 screen layout here - before you build
it"*.

**THE AGREED SHAPE.** ACC-06 goes from six steps to four:

| Step | What is on it | What the clerk does |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · Find account** | One searchable dropdown; the account panel beneath it | Picks the account |
| **2 · Date & reads** | Move-out date, reason, the reading table, the field-visit table | Types the date and the closing readings; adds a visit or says none is needed |
| **3 · Bill & deposit** | The draft bill's subtraction, what to do with the deposit, and — ONLY when there is a shortfall — the four paths | Settles the money |
| **4 · Review & close** | Account, unit, date, the subtraction, the choices made, the unit's vacancy and charges, the meters, what we will send | Reads it, confirms, and the draft becomes final |

**WHY THESE TWO MERGES AND NOT SOME OTHER PAIR**, recorded because a later lane will ask:
* Old steps **3 and 4 are ONE subtraction.** The shortfall is that subtraction's bottom line
  (*Short by*), not a separate fact, so drawing it on its own step guaranteed the repetition the
  PO reported. The four shortfall paths appear on the money step only when there IS a shortfall.
* Old step **5 carried no input anywhere on it.** Every panel was read-only, which makes it a
  review page sitting one click before the review page. Merging it into step 6 removes a step
  without removing a single fact.

**⚠ NOTHING IS REBUILT UNTIL THE LAYOUTS ARE APPROVED.** The PO asked to SEE all four screens
first, and that is a gate on the build, not a formality — B14 rule 41 is that the product matches
the drawing, and here WE are the ones drawing (entry above: the PO ruled the flow is settled in
the chat rather than from the Accounts blueprint). The layouts are put to them as a rendered page
they can look at, not as extracted text, because rule 42's whole point is that a screen agreed as
a picture is a screen agreed, and one agreed as prose is not.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE.** Every approved remedy from the 23-row list still stands and lands
in whichever of the four steps now owns it; the approved tables are unchanged; and the draft-bill
ruling is what makes step 3 capable of showing figures at all.

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane RULINGS-0924, `OQ-PAY-12608`): P7 — `payments.settlement_id` IS DROPPED, AND THE ONE JUDGMENT THAT CHANGED MID-BUILD

PO, verbatim: *"p7 (b) — nothing is lost, and the payment-row lock stays exactly as it is"*.
`payments/0044` removes the column `payments/0038` added one day earlier on the blueprint's
`P5.6` (p024, *"nullable. Null is Awaiting settlement."*). `settlement_members` stays the one
record of which payments a payout holds.

**WHY A COLUMN ONE DAY OLD WAS REMOVED.** It was never writable. `payments_payment_immutable()`
compares a payment's whole row minus a short allow list and `payments/0005`'s own comment says
*"a column added later is frozen the day it is created"* — and the `processing` branch names its
mutable set explicitly too, so the column was settable **only at INSERT** and a payout by
definition arrives after the row exists. There was no window at any point in a payment's life.
Hard rule 4 narrows itself in terms (*"widening it anywhere else is a new ruling"*), so the lane
that found it asked rather than guessed.

**WHAT IT COSTS, WITH THE FIGURE PUT TO THE PO:** at the top of tier T5 a utility holds about
**40,000 accounts**; the payments list filtered to *Awaiting settlement* reads through
`settlement_members` instead of a column — one extra join on a paged query (`NFR-3`), not a scan.
And it already did: `awaiting_settlement_filter()` never read the pointer, because the pointer was
never readable. **No read in this product changed behaviour on the day the column went**, which is
what makes *"nothing is lost"* a fact rather than a reassurance.

**FIVE JUDGMENTS, OURS TO MAKE (law 13):**

1. **The trigger is not touched, and that is deliberate rather than convenient.**
   `payments_payment_immutable()` is written as `to_jsonb(OLD) - locked_columns`, so it enumerates
   no column and a column leaving the table leaves the comparison exactly as it was. `payments/0044`
   is a one-line `RemoveField` with no `RunPython`. **`payments/0014` is still the only place the
   database's allow list has ever moved**, which is the other half of what the PO ruled.
2. **THE JUDGMENT THAT CHANGED MID-BUILD — the measurement script is INVERTED, not deleted.**
   `10-scripts/cr139_p5_6_pointer_freeze_proof.py` printed `FAIL: payments.settlement_id does not
   exist` when it could not find the column, which after the drop is the only line it could ever
   print: law 7's *incapable of passing* shape, which that script's own docstring warns about. The
   first plan was to delete it. **A grep changed that:** it is cited from six live places, and one
   of them is a row in `12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md`, **which may not be edited** — the
   register guard reads a changed line as a deletion. Deleting the file would have left six
   citations pointing at nothing and no lawful way to repair one of them. So its VERDICT is turned
   round — absence is the pass and exit 0, presence means the database predates `payments/0044` and
   the three original probes still run and still report the finding — and it can still fail, on the
   thing that would matter: the pointer coming back.
3. **The declared absence keeps its CODE and loses its reason.**
   `no_payment_row_is_stamped_with_its_payout` in `SETTLEMENT_UNAVAILABLE` is still exactly true
   and is what a caller groups on, so renaming it would break every consumer for no gain — unlike
   `amendment_history_is_not_a_permanent_record`, whose old name asserted a question was open. Only
   the detail moved, from *a column exists that nothing can write* to *the PO ruled it away*. A
   test now asserts the OLD wording is absent, because a stated absence whose stated reason has
   stopped being true is `DEF-PAY-6330`'s shape and passes every parity check.
4. **Three test cases are REWRITTEN rather than deleted, because two of them would RAISE.**
   `…_the_pointer_is_nullable_and_a_plain_uuid` becomes
   `…_the_pointer_column_is_gone_and_stays_gone` (the standing guard, and it runs on SQLite like
   everything else — a column's absence is a schema fact and needs no trigger to observe, which is
   exactly why the ORIGINAL finding needed PostgreSQL and this one does not).
   `…_pointer_and_member_agree` — written to *"matter on the day `OQ-PAY-12608` closes"* — becomes
   `…_the_membership_is_the_only_place_the_payout_is_held`: the question closed the other way, so
   the check being kept warm can never be needed. And `P5.12`'s case, which read
   `row.settlement_id is None` on four payments, now asserts the WIDER thing it was really
   guarding — **an ingest writes no payment row at all** — against `updated_at` and `status`.
5. **The reverse is exact, and it is worth stating because most 🔒 reverses are not.** The column
   held NULL on every row in every tenant, because it had no writer, so re-creating it as
   `uuid NULL` restores byte-for-byte the state that was dropped and no data can be lost either
   way. `customers/0069`, three days old, cannot say that: its reverse fails the moment any
   property has been sold twice. What a rollback does NOT restore is the ruling.

## 2026-09-24 · THE MOVE-IN REVIEW SHOWS THE CUSTOMER'S MESSAGES, AND THE TWO PARAGRAPHS IT SHOWED INSTEAD ARE DELETED (`DEF-CUS-6365`, item 7 of twenty, `v2.351.24`)

**The PO, verbatim, on their own screenshot of `ACC-05` step 6:** *"reduce this text; As per
drawing you are not showing consumer communication related items email, contract, text , inapp
message taht will be sent to cutomer once move-in is approve"* — confirmed with the whole
twenty-item list the same day, *"all these issues are correct - fix it"*.

**What was there, measured before anything was built:** a two-row definition list headed *What
we'll send*, both rows typed into `MoveInWizard.tsx`; a **60-word** paragraph, *What this move-in
will not write*; and a **57-word** block, *Nothing is delivered to the customer*. Both prose blocks
are RATIONALE, which B14 rule 33 puts at **zero words on screen**, and both had clauses that had
become false while nobody re-read them — *"It does not … commit an opening meter reading"* predates
step 3's reading table (`DEF-CUS-6362`, the day before), and *"neither of the two above is sent,
queued or mailed"* predates notifications gaining in-app, a mailbox and sender configuration.

**What is built:** blueprint **p077** (`05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf`, read AS AN
IMAGE at scale 5 — B14 rule 42), the section headed *What goes out to the customer*, six columns
**SEND · WHAT IT SAYS · TO · CHANNEL · TEMPLATE · WHEN**. It is a COMPONENT and not a section of
the page (B14 rule 43): `07-frontend/src/features/customers/MoveInMessages.tsx`, drawing through
`MoveMatrix` — the same table the move-out's own *What we will send* uses, so the two move screens
cannot acquire two table styles. Every cell but the heading is the server's answer, read from
`GET /move-ins/messages` and decided by **the same calls the save makes** (`channel_decision` per
event, `template_service.resolve` per class), so the review and the queue cannot disagree. Worked:
a residential move-in taking a $150.00 deposit that does not clear on the day draws p077's three
ticked rows in p077's order — *The new account and its number* (Email · Printed letter, Welcome —
move-in v5), *A receipt for the deposit* (Email, Deposit receipt v3), *The service agreement*
(— , —).

**FIVE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE AND THE RULING DID NOT. Each is recorded rather than asked
(law 13); the full reasoning is
`04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/conformance/DEF-CUS-6365-move-in-review-what-goes-out.md`.**

1. **THE SEND TICK IS A FACT, NOT A CHOICE.** p077 draws a tick per row.
   `POST /accounts/{id}/move-in` has **no parameter for which messages to queue** —
   `services.MOVE_IN_FIELDS` is the account create set and a key it does not know is REFUSED BY
   NAME. A live checkbox over a door that would refuse it is hard-won law 2's mirror, the shape
   that left five refusing cards on the portal's front page for days (`DEF-CWP-3925`). The box is
   **disabled** (`BR-SHL-025`) and ticked from `channels.length > 0`, so it reports whether the
   save really queues the row. New-connect step 7 renders p091's ticks the same way for the same
   reason. **The hold carries its expiry test**: `MoveInMessages.dom.test.tsx` asserts every box is
   disabled, so the day a *which messages* parameter is ruled the suite goes red and names the file.
2. **TWO OF p077's FIVE ROWS ARE NOT DRAWN, AND THE SERVER — NOT THE SCREEN — IS WHERE THEY WILL
   ARRIVE.** *The readings this account opened on* and *That a meter still has to be read* are drawn
   UNTICKED and **neither names a template class this product holds anywhere** — no code in
   `notifications.catalogs.LISTINGS`, no event key, no rule; the second's own TEMPLATE cell reads
   *— none chosen* in the drawing. Two rows of pure `—` on the screen the PO asked to carry LESS
   text would be the defect being fixed, one row over. Because every row comes from the server's
   plan rather than a list in the component, **authoring either class grows the row and the table
   draws it with no change to the screen.**
3. **THE CONTRACT IS LISTED, AND LISTED AS GOING OUT ON NOTHING.** The PO named *contract*, p077
   draws it third, so `move_in_message_plan` grew a fourth row. `services._move_in` **writes** a
   `service_agreements` row per service at the unit and **queues nothing**: there is no event key,
   so no rule can switch it on and no channel decision is taken. `channels` is `[]` **by
   construction rather than by a switch somebody could turn on**, and the template resolves through
   `contract_service_agreement`, which is absent on a fresh utility because `BR-NOT-002` makes a
   contract version effective-dated and `seed_notice_templates` refuses a date nobody chose. A dash
   in both cells and **no sentence** — why a row has no channel is rationale, which rule 33 gives
   zero words.
4. **THE HEADING IS *What goes out*, NOT p077's *What goes out to the customer*.** Rule 33 caps a
   heading at three words, and rule 34 wants one pair of words for one thing: new-connect step 7
   and transfer step 5 already say *What goes out*. The longer form would have been a third wording
   for one idea. ⚠ **AND THE PRODUCT NOW HAS TWO WORDINGS FOR THIS ONE PANEL, WHICH IS WORTH
   SAYING OUT LOUD.** Hours before this landed, the PO approved the MOVE-OUT's panel unchanged —
   *"this is corret use it"* — and that one is headed ***What we'll send*** (decision log, *"THE
   MONEY TABLE AND THE MESSAGES TABLE, APPROVED (ACC-06 STEPS 4 AND 6)"*). That was an approval of
   an existing panel and not a vocabulary ruling, and the move-in is built to its OWN drawing
   (rule 41), so it keeps *What goes out* — **three screens say that and one says the other.**
   Unifying them is one string in eleven catalogues and is the PO's to call; it is recorded here
   so the next copy audit finds the split already known rather than filing it twice.
5. **p078's *Choosing a template* PICKER AND ITS FOUR NOTES ARE NOT BUILT — RECORDED, NOT DECIDED
   QUIETLY** (B14 rule 38's instruction). The four paragraphs are rationale (*"Everything here is
   queued, and nothing is sent"*, *"Print is the floor"*, *"A template resolves on three axes"*,
   *"The draft version is listed and cannot be picked"*) and the PO's instruction in this very
   defect is *"reduce this text"*. The picker is informational in the drawing's own caption — *"The
   template picker names the version that would be used and does not render it"* — and that
   information is already in the TEMPLATE column of the table above it, per row, resolved by the
   dispatcher's own call; a second table with a radio column over a commit that accepts no template
   choice would be a dead control. **If the PO wants the picker on the review it is a follow-up,
   and nothing on the screen claims it exists.**

**ONE LAW-1 REPAIR MADE ON THE WAY.** `customer_events.RECEIPT_CHANNEL_TEMPLATES` carried a comment
saying *"`test_def_cus_6365` asserts they equal `receipts.RECEIPT_TEMPLATE_CODE` and its two
siblings, so the two lists cannot drift apart silently."* **No such test existed.** The list is
duplicated on purpose (B1 forbids notifications importing payments) and a duplicate with nothing
holding it together is a second opinion waiting to happen. `06-backend/tests/
test_def_cus_6365_move_in_messages.py` is now that test, and it is the file's first case.

**Twelve catalogue keys retired in all eleven languages** — `customers.moveIn.review.notWritten`
and its title, and the ten `customers.moveIn.send.*` — and fourteen added, through
`10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py` so parity cannot break. Every call site was in `MoveInWizard.tsx`,

## 2026-09-24 — DECIDED (lane SMALL-CUS): FIVE JUDGMENTS MADE WHILE CLEARING SIX UNOWNED REDS, AND ONE RED THAT WAS HIDING A SECOND DEFECT

Six suites had been red with nobody's name on them (`DEF-CWP-6424`, `DEF-BIL-6456`,
`DEF-RBS-6457`, `DEF-CUS-6458`, `DEF-CUS-6433`, `DEF-PAY-6463`). Clearing them needed five
calls no ruling had made. They are written here rather than put to the PO (law 13).

**(a) A red that was hiding a defect, and the defect is the bigger one — `DEF-RBS-6467`.**
Fixing `DEF-RBS-6457` (the move-outs test handed the runbook the string `"t"` as its tenant)
left two cases still failing on ARITHMETIC: `assert '0.00' == '20.01'`. `move_outs.report()`
re-derived every closing with `_closing(one, None)` — **no settlement** — so `amount_stored`
came back `None` and `currency` came back the `"USD"` default, on every row. **The Move-outs
checklist's "Deposit money" tile therefore read `$0.00` on every run since 7 September, and a
run whose accounts are in two currencies showed one.** Filed before fixing. **The judgment is
WHERE the figures now come from:** the RECORDS (`closing.as_row()` carries `amount_stored` at
four decimals and the account's own currency) rather than a second derivation, so the tile and
the table under it cannot disagree about one customer's deposit. The alternative — writing the
settlement back onto the plan row — would have put the same number in two places, which is what
`B4` forbids by name.

**(b) The move-outs suite gets a BARE `tenants` row, not a provisioned utility.** The file's own
header says its cases prove *"the runbook's reasoning and NOTHING about the seams"*, and every
seam in it is monkeypatched; the only reason a tenant is needed at all is that `acts.plan` writes
a `runbook_run_records` row before anything is acted on (`BR-RBS-004`). `tenants` is RLS-exempt
(a platform table, `db/rls_tenancy_w0.sql`), so one `Tenant.objects.create` satisfies the foreign
key in milliseconds where `provisioned_tenant` would seed a whole utility 34 times. The RECORD
table is NOT exempt, so the execute runs inside `tenant_context` — invisible on SQLite and
refused on PostgreSQL (hard rule 1, law 14). Measured: the file still runs in **2.5 seconds**.

**(c) `list_row` takes the tenant's zone as an argument, and the list endpoint resolves it once.**
`DEF-CUS-6433`'s fix needs `tenant_timezone()`, which is a query with no cache. A page of 50
requests would have asked the same question 50 times, which is an N+1 nobody would have noticed
and `NFR` would rightly refuse at T5. Left out, the row still asks for itself, so the single-row
read (`GET /service-requests/{id}`) is unchanged and both paths are exercised.

**(d) `DEF-CUS-6426` is CLOSED as already fixed, not re-fixed.** `b7144d236` (2.350.7) moved the
sub-category pickers onto the customers-side `GET /accounts/subcategories` and left the Settings
door as signed; nobody closed the row. Re-proved rather than assumed — the backend case and the
14 cases of `AccountSubtypePicker.test.tsx`. Closing a row against somebody else's commit is the
honest record; re-fixing it would have been a second answer to a question already answered.

**(e) `DEF-CUS-6468` is FILED and NOT fixed, deliberately.** `BR-CUS-070` freezes *the address as
the applicant gave it* once a request is submitted, and `update_request` names exactly one field
in that refusal — so since `BR-CUS-1091` put the city, state and ZIP back on the table
(2026-09-22), those three can still be edited after submission while the street line cannot.
Whether the parts are covered by that rule is a question about the rule, and the lane that owns
Edit on a service request should answer it in one place rather than this lane guessing in
passing. The row records both halves so it cannot be lost.

**And the shape worth keeping, which is law 7's:** every one of these six reds had been read past
by at least one lane as *"pre-existing, not mine"*. `DEF-BIL-6456` was seventeen days old,
`DEF-RBS-6457` seventeen, `DEF-CUS-6458` two. **A red nobody owns is a red nobody reads**, and the
second defect above — a money tile reading zero on a live checklist — was sitting behind one of
them where no check could ever have reached it.

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane RULINGS-0924, `OQ-PAY-12621` / `DEF-PAY-6375`): P1 — A COUNTER FEE JOINS ITS TILL'S EXPECTED CASH, AND FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULING DID NOT MAKE

PO, verbatim: *"p1 a"* — *the fee counts toward the counter's expected cash; the drawer balances;
the books are unchanged.* `payments/0045` adds `counter_receipts.counter_session_id`,
`record_counter_receipt` writes it, and `running_split` reads a SECOND source.

**WHAT WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS TWO CORRECT RULINGS MEETING.** A2 (2026-09-19) posts a service
request's application fee at collection and writes **no payment row** — the PO accepted the stated
cost, *"the counter clerk's drawer doesn't balance on the day"*. The ruling of 2026-09-23 then made
a drawer difference at close **reach the books**. Together the cash was in the drawer, the expected
count was not, the close read OVER by exactly the fee, and **that over posted: one fee booked
twice.** Lane REQ-FEE measured it as `DEF-PAY-6375` and built nothing against it; the code comment
in `counter_receipts.till_refusal` said so in as many words.

**WORKED, AND IT IS THE RULING'S OWN FIGURE:** Dana's counter holds **$400.00**; she takes Sarah
Miller's **$70.00** application fee in cash (`DR 1010 · CR 2400` at collection, unchanged) and
counts **$470.00** at close. Before: expected **$400.00**, difference **+$70.00**, posted. Now:
expected **$470.00**, difference **$0.00**.

**FOUR JUDGMENTS, OURS TO MAKE (law 13):**

1. **ONLY A HAND TENDER JOINS A TILL, which is what `assert_till_open_for_tender` already does for
   a payment row.** `open_counter_for(actor)` returns the clerk's till whatever the tender, so the
   obvious build would have attached a CARD fee to the drawer too. `payments.counter_session_id` is
   deliberately left null for `card`, `ach`, `wire` and `lockbox` — *you cannot count a card total
   in a drawer* (p056 ③) — and a receipt and a payment of the same tender disagreeing about which
   till they belong to, on the same screen, is the kind of difference a clerk reads as meaning
   something. So the tender is translated (`cheque` → `check`) and checked against `HAND_TENDERS`
   first.
2. **THE COUNT BESIDE THE FIGURE MOVES WITH IT.** `MyCounterPage` prints each tender's
   `payment_count` directly under its total. A receipt is not a `payments` row — that is A2's
   design and this build does not touch it — but a count that excluded a line the total includes
   is a number a clerk cannot reconcile with the one next to it. So a receipt moves `system_total`,
   `countable_expected`, `taken` AND the count. The distinction between a receipt and a payment
   belongs to the payments LIST, not to the drawer figure.
3. **THE TWO SOURCES ARE MERGED BEFORE THE LOOP, NEVER ADDED AFTER IT.** `_merge_sources` folds
   payments and receipts into one row per tender first, so the float rule (*the float sits inside
   the cash line*), the countable rule and the currency set are each applied in exactly one place.
   Adding a fee to a finished `system_total` would have meant re-deciding *is this the cash row?* a
   second time, and a rule stated twice is a rule that drifts.
4. **ALL THREE RECEIPT STATES COUNT, AND THE QUERY IS GROUPED IN SQL.** `held`, `applied` and
   `earned` differ only in what the BOOKS have since done with the money; none of them is the cash
   leaving the drawer. And the aggregate is a `GROUP BY` with `ix_counter_receipts_session` behind
   it, not a Python fold — `NFR-3`, the same rule `running_split`'s own docstring cites against
   copying `counter_receipts.list_totals`.

**WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT DONE, because the ruling says so:** no payment row is invented, no posting
changes, no deposit batch changes, and hard rule 4's allow list does not move. A test asserts the
`payments` row count is unchanged, because writing one would make the drawer balance too — and
book the fee twice in the LEDGER instead, which is the same defect moved one table along.

## 2026-09-24 — NOT BUILT (lane RULINGS-0924): P2 IS THE ONE OF THE SEVEN THIS LANE DID NOT REACH, AND THIS IS WHAT THE NEXT LANE NEEDS

`OQ-PAY-12622` (PO: *"p2 a"* — the Debtors row shows *Write-off pending / approved / declined*;
no Finance access moves) is **CLOSED and UNBUILT**. Recorded here because a closed question with
nothing built behind it is exactly the shape a later reader mistakes for done — the register row
says CLOSED and the product does not do it.

**What was measured before the lane ran out of time**, so the next one does not repeat it:

* The row is `apps/payments/outstandings.OutstandingRow`; `as_dict()` is the wire. Every per-account
  fact on it is already batched over the PAGE (`accounts`, `names`, `last_payments`, `states`,
  `plans`, `notice_counts`) — **add one more dict keyed by `account_id` over `ids`, never a query
  per row** (`NFR-3`, and `DEF-PAY-4221` is what that rule is for).
* The model is `apps/payments/collections_models.WriteOff`, statuses
  `requested · approved · rejected · reversed` (`WRITE_OFF_STATUSES`). The PO named three words and
  the table has four values, so **a judgment is needed and it is not a lane's to duck**: a
  reversal is a NEW row carrying `reversed` with `reverses_write_off_id` set, and the original
  stays `approved` (`writeoffs.py` issues no UPDATE). The reading this lane would have taken, for
  the next one to accept or overturn: take the account's most recent row; map
  `requested → pending`, `approved → approved`, `rejected → declined`; and show **nothing** for
  `reversed`, because the three words describe a REQUEST's progress and an account whose write-off
  was reversed is an ordinary debtor again with no live request.
* **No permission moves** — that is half of what the PO ruled. The cell is read from the row the
  clerk already has; `BR-SHL-003` and A4's grid are untouched, and the *Write-offs* link on Debtors
  still opens Finance for the roles that have it.
* B14 rule 33 caps the column head at **3 words** and each value is one word.
* Eleven catalogues, as always.

## 2026-09-24 — RULED BY THE PO: A MASTER ACCOUNT LISTS ITS SUB-ACCOUNTS AND **CANNOT BE CLOSED** WHILE IT HAS ANY — WHICH REVERSES `BR-CUS-1082`

**PO, verbatim**, asked what differs between a master-account move-out and a regular one and shown
a four-step comparison: *"in case of master account we will need a panel or table for all sub
accounts associated with it and we should tell user that master account cannot be closed until all
these child acocunts are move to another master account."* — then, against the step-1 row of that
chart: *"no 2 step"*.

**⚠ WHAT THIS REVERSES, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED (change process step 2).** `BR-CUS-1082` says a
master with open children is **WARNED, not refused**, and that is itself a PO ruling (2026-08-24,
closing `OQ-CUS-12515`, recorded at `move_out_settlement.py:1080-1096` and drawn in
`MoveOutWizard.tsx:652`). The blueprint draws the warning, the backend serves
`open_sub_accounts` for it, and the front end renders it. **That is now superseded: the count
becomes a REFUSAL.** One selector answers both the screen and the commit
(`selectors.sub_accounts_for_master`, `BR-CUS-171`), so the refusal has exactly one definition of
an open child and the screen cannot disagree with the save — the thing `DEF-CUS-5901` exists to
prevent. `BR-CUS-1082` is to be marked SUPERSEDED with this date and these words, in the module's
business rules, in the same commit as the build.

**WHAT IS BUILT, on step 1 and on no new step.** *"no 2 step"* is read as **this belongs on step 1
and does not become a step of its own** — the sub-account table sits in the *What is open on this
account* panel where the count already lives, and the wizard stays FOUR steps as ruled this
morning. A master with children shows the table and cannot continue; a regular account shows what
it shows today. ⚠ **The reading was put back to the PO in one line for correction**, because the
same three words could mean *not on step 2*, which would be the same answer by a different route.

**⚠ THE REMEDY THE REFUSAL NAMES DOES NOT EXIST AS AN ACT, AND THIS IS THE FINDING THAT MATTERS.**
*"until all these child accounts are moved to another master account"* describes setting a link.
**There is no such link.** `sub_accounts_for_master` (`selectors.py:927`) derives the children:
*"every OCCUPYING account on this master's premises"*, keyed off the status's behaviour class and
the DECLARED OWNERSHIP of the premises (`DEF-650`, PO 2026-08-27). No column on a tenant's account
names its master. **So a tenant cannot be moved to another master one at a time; children follow
the BUILDING.** In today's model the only acts that move them are (a) the premises' declared owner
changing — every child moves at once — or (b) each tenant physically moving to another property.
**A refusal that instructs a clerk to do something the product offers no way to do is hard-won law
2's mirror** — a live screen behind a dead instruction — so the refusal's SENTENCE must name the
act that exists. Put to the PO with the worked case: *Elm Street Holdings LLC closes while six of
eight flats are occupied; the building is sold to Marten Row Holdings, whose master account then
covers all six, and only then can the old master close.*

**STATUS: RULED ON THE REFUSAL, OPEN ON ITS SENTENCE.** The refusal and the table are ruled and are
to be built. What the refusal SAYS — and therefore which act a clerk is sent to — waits on the PO's
answer to the paragraph above. The move-out lane stays HELD until it lands (PO, the same hour:
*"please hold line for move out"*).

## 2026-09-24 — THE MASTER-ACCOUNT MOVE-OUT, STEP BY STEP: THREE MORE RULINGS AND ONE THING STILL OWED

Answering the four-step master-versus-regular chart put to them, the PO ruled on three of the four
steps in three messages. **Verbatim, in order:**

| Step | PO's words |
|---|---|
| 1 · Find account | *"if master account dont have any active child acounts in that case - go to next step"* |
| 2 · Date & reads | *"but you will ahve to show all units that are tagged to master account - we have unit states to be used for it"* |
| 3 · Bill & deposit | *"billing process for master account will be differnt"* |
| 4 · Review & close | *"this will remain same"* |

**STEP 1 — THE REFUSAL IS CONDITIONAL, AND THE CONDITION IS *ACTIVE* CHILDREN.** Taken with the
ruling above it (the table, and *cannot be closed until*), step 1 for a master is: list the
sub-accounts, refuse while any is ACTIVE, and **continue normally when there are none**. That last
clause matters more than it reads — it means a master move-out is not a special flow, it is the
ordinary flow with one gate at the front. *"Active"* is already defined and must not be
re-defined here: `selectors.sub_accounts_for_master` keys off the status's BEHAVIOUR CLASS, never
its label (`BR-CUS-055`, `BR-CUS-171`), so a closed tenant drops out on the day they close and a
pending one never appears. The same selector answers the screen and the commit, so the gate cannot
disagree with the save.

**STEP 2 — A MASTER ALSO SHOWS ITS UNITS, BY STATE.** The meters panel stands; beside it, for a
master only, a table of **every unit tagged to that master** with its state. *"We have unit states
to be used for it"* names what already exists rather than asking for something new: the Units list
serves **Occupied · Vacant · Sub-metered** as its occupancy filter (`units_list`, and
`UnitsPage.test.tsx`'s own options), so the column is a read of a state the product already keeps.
⚠ **This is the answer to a question the chart raised and could not settle:** a master hangs off
the ADDRESS, not a unit (`BR-CUS-1010`), so *"the meters on that unit"* was never quite the right
frame for it — the building's units are what a clerk closing the owner's account needs to see, and
now they see them, with the state each one is in.

**STEP 4 — UNCHANGED, AND THAT IS A RULING, NOT AN OMISSION.** *"this will remain same"* closes the
second gap the chart named. The review is one screen for both kinds: the unit falls vacant, the
standing charge moves to the owner's account, the notice to the owner is queued. **The blueprint's
drawn *Close a sub-account* action is therefore NOT built** — step 1's gate means a master reaching
step 4 has no active children left to close, so a control for it would be a control that can never
act (hard-won law 2's mirror). Its absence is deliberate and is recorded here so nobody adds it
back from the drawing.

**⚠ STEP 3 IS RULED IN PRINCIPLE AND NOT YET IN SUBSTANCE — THIS IS WHAT IS STILL OWED.**
*"billing process for master account will be differnt"* states that it differs; it does not say
how, and **we must not guess on a money path.** What the repo already establishes, and what a
worked question to the PO is built from: a master's bill is not a tenant's — `base_charge_only_
coverage` puts every unit with **no occupying account** onto the owner's bill (*"the exclusion test
is the ACCOUNT, never a flag"*), which is why one unit emptying moved a worked example from
`$69.60` to `$81.60`. So a master's closing bill is common areas plus the base charge of every
empty unit, for the closing window. Separately, the fourth shortfall path — *Tie it back to the
master account* — is meaningless on a master and must go or be replaced. **Both go back to the PO
with figures. The lane stays HELD.**

## 2026-09-24 — THE MASTER'S REFUSAL, SETTLED: **CLOSE THE TENANTS FIRST**, NOT "MOVE THEM TO ANOTHER MASTER"

**PO, verbatim**, answering the worked question *"a master closes with tenants still in place —
Elm Street Holdings closes while 6 of 8 flats are occupied"* against three options:
***"(b) Refuse until they're closed"***.

**THIS CLOSES THE ONE THING THE EARLIER RULING LEFT OPEN**, and it closes it the safe way. That
ruling said a master *"cannot be closed until all these child acocunts are move to another master
account"*, and the finding filed against it was that **moving a child to another master is not an
act this product has**: `sub_accounts_for_master` derives the children from the premises' DECLARED
OWNERSHIP (`selectors.py:927`, `DEF-650`), so no column links a tenant to a master and children
follow the BUILDING. A refusal instructing a clerk to do something the product cannot do is
hard-won law 2's mirror. **Option (b) names an act that exists in the product today: close the
tenant's account, which is this very wizard, once per tenant.**

**SO THE REFUSAL AND ITS SENTENCE ARE NOW BOTH RULED.** A master with any ACTIVE sub-account cannot
continue past step 1; the screen lists them and says to close them first. With none active, the
flow continues exactly as a regular account's (ruling above).

⚠ **ONE CONSEQUENCE, STATED SO NOBODY DISCOVERS IT LATER.** Under (b) a landlord SELLING a building
with tenants in place cannot be handled by the move-out at all — the tenants have not left, so
their accounts are active, so the master cannot close. **That case is the TRANSFER flow, not this
one**, and the transfer already exists and already keeps the deposit and the history where they
are (blueprint `08-move-out-wizard.md:288-291`). The two flows now divide cleanly: a building
EMPTYING closes through the move-out, a building CHANGING HANDS goes through the transfer. Nothing
about the transfer changes here; what changes is that the move-out stops half-accepting a case it
cannot finish.

**NOT DECIDED AND NOT ASSUMED:** whether the refusal should offer a link that opens each listed
tenant's own move-out (a convenience) or merely name them. The table lists them either way; a lane
may add the link only if it is proved to reach a screen that exists, with the hold-expiry
discipline hard-won law 2 requires.

## 2026-09-24 — AND THE VACANT UNITS REFUSE IT TOO: A MASTER CANNOT CLOSE WHILE ANY UNIT STILL BILLS TO IT

**PO, verbatim**, on the worked case *"2 empty flats bill $22.00 a month each to Elm Street
Holdings. It closes"*: ***"its not allowed - refule the move out"***.

**SO THE GATE ON STEP 1 HAS TWO CONDITIONS, NOT ONE.** A master's move-out is refused while EITHER
* any **active sub-account** exists (ruling above — *"(b) Refuse until they're closed"*), or
* any **unit still bills vacant charges to it**.

The second is the one this row adds. `selectors.base_charge_only_coverage` puts every unit with no
occupying account onto the owner's bill — *"the exclusion test is the ACCOUNT, never a flag"* — so
an empty flat is not a neutral thing a closing master can leave behind: it is a live monthly charge
with nowhere to go. `$22.00` a month each on the PO's own example, `$44.00` the building.

**WHAT THIS MEANS IN PRACTICE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS A BIG CONSEQUENCE.** Taken with the
first condition, a master can close only when **no unit on its premises bills to it at all** —
neither occupied nor empty. In the ordinary life of a building that is rare: a building being sold
goes through the TRANSFER flow (ruling above), and a building still standing always has units. The
master move-out therefore becomes the narrow case it should always have been — a premises that has
genuinely ended: demolished, taken off supply, or otherwise carrying no units that bill. **This is
recorded, not queried:** the PO has now ruled *refuse* twice on this screen, in two different
worked cases, and law 13 says a ruling is not re-asked. What a lane MAY NOT do is soften it into a
warning because the refusal seems strict.

**THE SCREEN ALREADY HAS WHAT THE REFUSAL NEEDS TO SAY.** Step 2's new units-by-state table (ruled
above) is exactly the evidence: the units tagged to the master and the state each is in. The step-1
refusal names the two counts — how many tenants are active, how many empty units still bill — and
the table below shows which. No new read is invented for it: the sub-accounts come from
`sub_accounts_for_master`, and the units and their states from the same occupancy the Units list
already serves.

## 2026-09-24 — THE MASTER'S FOURTH SHORTFALL PATH: **TIE IT TO THE CUSTOMER**, NOT TO AN ACCOUNT

**PO, verbatim**, on the last gap the master-versus-regular chart named — *"the shortfall on a
master: there is no master above a master, so the fourth path is meaningless"*: ***"we have to tie
to customer id"***.

**WHAT IS RULED.** On a REGULAR account the fourth path is *Tie it back to the master account*, and
the target is resolved by the server, never typed (`BR-CUS-097`, `TRANSFER_TARGET_MASTER`). On a
MASTER account that target does not exist, and the residue attaches to the **CUSTOMER** the master
account belongs to — the legal entity, *Elm Street Holdings LLC* on the worked example — so the
debt follows the customer rather than dying with the account. The other three paths (pursue, a
payment plan, write it off) are unchanged on both kinds.

**WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND NOT A SPECIAL CASE.** `move_out_settlement` already knows two
transfer targets — `TRANSFER_TARGET_MASTER` and `TRANSFER_TARGET_OWNER` (`:375-377`) — so a target
that is neither an account nor a premises is the new part, and it is the customer. A customer
outlives every account they hold, which is exactly the property a residue needs; tying it to a
closed account is what makes a debt unreachable. ⚠ **What this does NOT do:** it does not move
money, it does not write a journal line, and it does not make the customer's other accounts liable
by arithmetic. It records WHO the residue belongs to. Collections then has a customer to chase
rather than a closed account, which is the whole point of the path.

**WHAT A LANE MUST ESTABLISH BEFORE BUILDING IT** (recorded so it is not invented at the keyboard):
whether `settle_shortfall` can carry a customer-shaped target at all today, what
`TRANSFER_TARGETS` accepts, and what the collections ladder does with a customer that has no open
account. If the answer is that nothing downstream reads a customer target, the path is built with
a hold and a test that fires when collections can read it — never shipped as a control that
records something nobody acts on (hard-won law 2).

**⚠ STILL OWED AFTER THIS: STEP 3'S BILLING ITSELF.** *"billing process for master account will be
differnt"* remains ruled in principle only. This row settles the SHORTFALL's destination, not how a
master's closing bill is composed — common areas plus the base charge of every empty unit, for the
closing window, is what the code does today and what a worked figure must be built from before it
is put to the PO.

## 2026-09-24 — LANDED (lane MOVEOUT-BUILD, `v2.351.33`): THE HELD LANE'S COPY CUTS AND COMBOBOX, AND THE EIGHT IDS THAT WERE TAKEN WHILE IT WAS HELD

The move-out lane was put on hold by the PO mid-morning (*"please hold line for move
out"*) and released in the afternoon (*"please start the lane for move out — use images
to build the screen"*). **The held lane had finished two of the scope's items and pushed
none of them** — 18 files, unpushed, in a worktree a container restart would have taken.
This push is that work, carried onto the tip and re-proved, before any new building.

**WHAT WAS ADOPTED RATHER THAN REDONE**, because redoing proved work is its own defect:
the 16 retired copy keys (495 words off the screen, 11 back, all eleven catalogues at
19,852 keys each), and `AccountFinder`'s move onto the kit's `RemoteSearchSelectField`.
Neither needed a new component — `RemoteSearchSelectField` named `accountFinder.tsx` in
its own Impacts header as the hand-roll that belonged there, which is B14 rule 43's
*look for the component first* answered by the repo itself.

**⚠ THE FINDING THAT MATTERS, AND IT IS HARD-WON LAW 11's ID CLAUSE ON A REAL LANE.**
The held lane had filed its eight defect rows as `DEF-CUS-6466`–`6473`, correctly, from
the register's maximum at the time. **By the time this lane came to push them, SIX of
those eight numbers had been taken by four other lanes** — `6466` (MOVEIN-WIZ), `6467`
(SMALL-CUS, a runbooks row), `6468` (SMALL-CUS), `6469` (RULINGS-0924, a payments row),
`6470` and `6471` (MASTERQ, the two master-account findings this lane's own scope cites).
The rows were re-filed against the remote through `10-scripts/file_defect.py`, landing at
`6472`–`6479`.

**⚠ AND THEN IT HAPPENED A SECOND TIME, BETWEEN THE RE-FILING AND THE PUSH.** A fifth
lane pushed `DEF-CWP-6472` and `DEF-CWP-6473` in the twenty minutes the re-filing took,
and `10-scripts/allocate.py defect --verify` caught both at the only moment the answer
can be final. ⚠ **`G17` fails a duplicate NUMBER even where the module segments differ**,
so `DEF-CUS-6472` beside `DEF-CWP-6472` is a collision and not a near miss. The two rows
moved again, and the final set is **`DEF-CUS-6474`–`6479` plus `6480` and `6481`** — not
contiguous, deliberately, because renumbering the six that were still free would have
moved citations for nothing.

**Nothing downstream would have caught it.** A duplicate id in a 3,957-row register reads
as a register, not as an error — law 11 says exactly that — and every allocation in this
story was arithmetically right when it was made. What was wrong was *which world the
maximum came from*.

**THE VARIANT WORTH NAMING: A HELD LANE MANUFACTURES THIS COLLISION BY EXISTING.** Law 11
prescribes re-deriving ids at PUSH time, which assumes allocation and push are minutes
apart. **A lane that is paused keeps its allocated ids only in its own tree, and every
hour it is paused is an hour siblings go on allocating past it** — six numbers in one
morning here. So: **re-derive the ids when a lane RESUMES as well as when it pushes**, and
treat a long gap between the two as the same hazard as a stale blob.

**A SECOND JUDGMENT, RECORDED BECAUSE THE GUARD IS THE HERO.** Retiring
`customers.moveOut.date.metersHint` turned `i18n/retiredWords.test.ts` RED — its allow
list named the key as a legitimate use of the word *register* (the meter's dial), and
that list is itself asserted to contain only keys that still exist. **That second
assertion is the whole reason the retirement did not leave a dead entry behind**, and it
is the shape law 7 asks for: a guard that also guards its own allow list. The entry was
removed with the key, in the same commit, and why is written where the entry was.

**ONE RED LEFT ON THE BRANCH, DATED RATHER THAN DISMISSED (law 7, habit 1).**
