## 2026-09-24 — THE INVOICE CLOUD *MAKE PAYMENT* API, CONFIRMED BEFORE A LINE IS WRITTEN

The PO brought a partner-written specification (*Smart360 Next ↔ Invoice Cloud, Make Payment API
Specification v1.0*) and asked, verbatim: *"tell me how to handle this - dont start the work tell
me what you will do"*, then *"tell me the steps you will run … including what codes you will handle
in table format"*, then *"please confirm in table before you start this APIs"*. **Nothing is built.
This row is what was confirmed, so the build starts from the repo rather than from a chat.**

**THE HEADLINE: MOST OF IT EXISTS.** `payments.services.record_payment` already takes the account,
amount, currency, method, posting date, allocation targets, `purpose`, `payment_type`,
`idempotency_source` and `idempotency_reference`, and already does creation → allocation → ledger →
audit inside ONE transaction. The partner door already exists at `/api/partner/v1/…` with five
key-authenticated READS. **So Make Payment is the first WRITE on an existing door, not a payments
build.**

### The eight authorisation checks are already written, and they are one function

`integrations/partner_api._admit` runs them for every partner route: **1** key real and active ·
**2** connector enabled · **3** utility active · **4** address on the allowlist · **5** key holds
this scope · **6** the tenant context (opened by the KEY, `key ─► credential ─► connection ─►
tenant ─► app.tenant_id ─► RLS FORCE`) · **7** GONE by ruling · **8** the rate limit.

⚠ **CHECKS 1–5 ANSWER ONE IDENTICAL `404`, NOT A `401` OR A `403`, AND THAT IS THE SECURITY
ARGUMENT RATHER THAN AN ACCIDENT.** All five are computed together with no early return, the body is
`SHARED_REFUSAL_CODE` and `REFUSAL_SENTENCE` whichever fired, and the response is padded to
`REFUSAL_FLOOR_S`. A guessed key answering `KEY_UNKNOWN` says *keep guessing*; a stolen key
answering `ADDRESS_NOT_ALLOWED` says *the key is real, now find a proxy*. The six real causes live
in the RUN ROW, where a manager reads them on S142 and an attacker cannot. **An earlier draft of
this plan said `401 AUTH-KEY` / `403 AUTH-SCOPE` and was WRONG; it is corrected here.**

⚠ **`tenant_id` IN THE BODY IS ACCEPTED, IGNORED AND RECORDED — NOT REFUSED.** That is the PO's own
ruling of 2026-09-17 (*"you will ahve to remove company ID filter from all Apis - we cannot tell
tenant ID outside our system"*), and an earlier draft of this plan proposed refusing on a mismatch,
which would have contradicted it. What they named goes on the run row's window text. **The partner's
document sends it on every call, so refusing an unrecognised parameter would break a live partner
on the day we told them to stop sending it.**

### The three dates — there are TWO columns, not three

| The partner's word | Our column | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| payment date **and** posting date | `posted_at` (datetime, NOT NULL) | *The record entered the system.* **User-entered, never a clock** (`BR-PAY-033`). Billing consumes exactly this column, the payment NUMBER is minted against its date, and the batch cut groups by it |
| clearing date | `cleared_at` (datetime, nullable) | *The money actually arrived.* NULL while `processing` |

`paymentDate "20-06-2026"` (day-month-year) becomes 20 June 2026 at **midnight in the utility's own
timezone** — `OQ-153`, PO 2026-08-12, *a typed posting date is midnight in the utility's own
timezone*. ⚠ `cheque_date` and `bankable_from` exist and are NOT these: both are NULL on every
tender that is not a paper cheque.

### Status — the partner's spec asks for one we cannot produce

`record_payment` writes **`cleared` when `cleared_at` is given and `processing` when it is not.**
`PAYMENT_POSTED` is a real constant that this service **never writes**. The PO was shown that table
and answered *"this is okay"*, so the correction is accepted.

⚠ **WHAT IS NOT YET RULED, AND IT DECIDES WHETHER THE MONEY REACHES THE BOOKS:** whether an Invoice
Cloud payment is recorded as `cleared` (pass the payment date as the clearing date — it joins the
day's reconciliation) or `processing` (it is **excluded from the batch cut, which takes cleared
money only**, and today nothing would ever clear it). Recommended: `cleared`, because Invoice Cloud
reports money it has already taken. **Put to the PO; not assumed.**

### Till and batch — an Invoice Cloud payment never touches a drawer

`counter_session_id` is **NULL** and stays nullable by PO ruling 2026-09-23: only the three tenders
that pass through a person's hands — `cash`, `check`, `money_order` — are refused without an open
till; ACH, card, wire and lockbox never touch a counter. So an Invoice Cloud payment carries no
till, is **not** stamped with a `deposit_batch_id` at insert, and is therefore a candidate for
`cut_deposit_batches`, which groups the day's CLEARED money *"that nobody's hands touched"* under
the day's **system till** (`_session_for`, PO: *"all hence we should geneate system generated
till"*). **One record at a time changes nothing** — the cut runs per day, so ten payments on 20 June
become one batch per tender, and a second cut cuts nothing (hard rule 6).

### Created by, updated by, audit

**The payment row carries NO `created_by` and NO `updated_at`, deliberately** — a payment is never
updated (three columns aside, `payments/0014`), and an `updated_at` would invite the belief that it
can be. **Who did it lives in `audit_log`, every time** (hard rule 7). For a partner payment the
actor is not a user: `actor_user_id` is NULL and `actor_kind`/`actor_label` name the caller.
⚠ **WHAT THE ACTOR SHOULD SAY IS NOT RULED.** Recommended: the CONNECTOR — *"Invoice Cloud"* — so a
manager reading the trail sees the partner rather than a blank or a meaningless system user; the KEY
used is already on the integration's run row, and the two together answer *which partner, which key,
which call*. **Put to the PO.**

### Five mismatches between the partner's document and this product

1. `tenant_id` in the body — accepted, ignored, recorded (above), never a refusal.
2. `consumer_id: 69843` and `bill_id: 452615` are **integers**; our identifiers are account and bill
   NUMBERS (`A-10650`, `AC-2026-00025`) over UUIDs. Take the numbers the existing partner reads
   already return.
3. `idempotency_source = invoice_cloud` — the sources are `entry`, `webhook`, `import` and
   `inbound_payment_key` **refuses an unknown one BY NAME**, because *"a typo'd namespace is a key
   that will never match the row it was meant to dedupe against"*. Adding `invoice_cloud` is a
   deliberate act, recommended over reusing `import` so every partner payment is identifiable by its
   key alone.
4. `currency` validated against tenant configuration — **there is no currency table yet**; Finance
   P0.6 is building one, started this day. Sequence behind it or accept USD only and say so.
5. **Which Invoice Cloud field is immutable — `id` or `FeeEntryId`.** Their own document flags it.
   It is the idempotency key. **Hold the build on it rather than guess.**

### The duplicate path, and why it is two layers

The key is `invoice_cloud|TID161007`, checked BEFORE any work so a retry costs nothing, and backed
by the database's own unique constraint so two simultaneous copies cannot both pass. A replay
returns `RecordedPayment(created=False)` — **never an exception** — and the response says
`duplicate: true` with the original payment. `PAYMENT_ALREADY_EXISTS` is therefore **not an error**:
it is a `200`.

## 2026-09-24 — THE *MAKE PAYMENT* API IS BUILT: FIVE JUDGMENTS NO RULING MADE, AND ONE REGRESSION THE EXISTING TESTS CAUGHT

The Product Owner walked the whole design with the coordinator and said ***"please do"***.
The specification is the entry above — *"THE INVOICE CLOUD *MAKE PAYMENT* API, CONFIRMED
BEFORE A LINE IS WRITTEN"* — and it is not restated here. **This row is only what the
build had to decide that the confirmation did not cover**, per hard-won law 13: a judgment
recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable and a question is the failure to make one.

### 1 · THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY IS `webhook|invoice_cloud:<payment_reference>` — WHICH SUPERSEDES THE PLAN'S OWN MISMATCH 3

The confirmed plan says, of `idempotency_source`: *"Adding `invoice_cloud` is a deliberate
act, recommended over reusing `import` so every partner payment is identifiable by its key
alone."* **That recommendation is superseded, and the reason is load-bearing rather than
stylistic.**

`payments.settlements._payment_for` finds a payout's members by **re-composing the string
`webhook|<provider>:<reference>` literally** — the prefix is typed into that function, not
derived from anything:

    key = f"webhook|{provider}:{reference}"

So a payment recorded under `invoice_cloud|TID161007` would be **invisible to the
settlement that later names it**: `ingest_payout` would file it under
`MEMBER_PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND`, the payout would still be written, and a real bank credit would
sit in this product against a payment it holds and cannot find. **Nothing would go red.**
`OQ-PAY-12625`'s own row states the same join from the other side, and that function's
docstring says why it re-composes rather than matching on `confirmation`: *"a join that a
correction can break is a join that will silently stop matching one day."*

**So the SOURCE is `webhook` — the namespace for a payment rail's own event id, which is
exactly what Invoice Cloud is sending — and the PROVIDER travels in the reference.** A
second property comes free and is worth naming: `payments.webhooks._record` composes the
identical string for a signed callback from the same provider, so if Invoice Cloud ever
both POSTs a payment here and re-delivers it through the webhook door, the second is
recognised as the replay it is instead of taking the money twice.

⚠ **THE GENERAL LESSON IS THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN:** a namespace is not a label, it is a
JOIN, and the other end of this one was a literal in a function nobody would have thought
to read. The plan's recommendation was sound on the facts it had.

### 2 · `cash`, `check` AND `money_order` ARE REFUSED ON THIS DOOR — a judgment, not a ruling

PO ruling 2026-09-23 §3.4 refuses the three hand tenders without an open till, *"It is the
only option where every cash dollar belongs to somebody"*. **A partner door has no clerk,
no session and therefore no till to name.** So a partner `cash` payment would be recorded
with `counter_session_id` NULL and bank under the day's SYSTEM till as money *"nobody's
hands touched"* — **the exact outcome that ruling exists to prevent, arriving through a
door the ruling was not shown.**

**The worked case:** Invoice Cloud reports a $60.00 cash payment taken at an agent's
counter on 20 June. Accepted, it lands in the day's system-till batch with no drawer and no
count behind it, and the first person to notice is whoever is footing a deposit that does
not tie. Refused, Invoice Cloud's integration gets `METHOD_NEEDS_A_TILL` on its first such
call and somebody asks the question.

**Nothing is lost by refusing:** Invoice Cloud is a card and bank-transfer portal, and ACH,
card, wire and lockbox all pass. If they ever genuinely need to report cash, that is a
ruling to take and not a default to assume. `counters.HAND_TENDERS` is READ rather than
re-spelled, so there is one list. `BR-PAY-1197`.

### 3 · A NOT-FOUND REFUSAL DOES NOT ECHO THE NUMBER THAT WAS SENT

The first draft answered *"bill_id 'INV-2026-09999' is not a bill of this account"*. It is
the caller's own input, so it leaks nothing — **and it made the property unassertable.**
Four different facts have to be ONE answer here (no such bill · another utility's bill ·
another account's bill · a void bill) or a partner can walk our invoice numbers, and with
the value in the sentence the bytes differ and the case can only *reason* that it is safe.
With the value out, `test_another_utilitys_bill_is_the_same_answer_as_no_such_bill` compares
the whole body byte for byte.

⚠ **A PROPERTY YOU CAN ONLY REASON ABOUT IS ONE THAT ROTS** — which is `partner_bill_
download`'s own posture (*"it is not a comparison we make and then hide; it is
structural"*), reached here from the opposite direction.

### 4 · THE ACTOR IS THE CONNECTION'S LABEL, NOT THE MANIFEST'S NAME

`actor_kind` is `integration` and `actor_user_id` is NULL — that much the plan confirmed.
**Which words go in `actor_label` was not put to anybody.** The connection's own
clerk-given label wins, the manifest's display name is the fallback and the provider key is
the floor, because a utility with two Invoice Cloud connections named them for a reason and
the trail should use the word they chose. It can never be empty: `AutomationActor` refuses
a blank name at construction, and a refusal there would lose the audit row and take the
payment with it (hard rule 7).

### 5 · THE STATUS IS `processing`, AND THE BILL TARGET IS CARRIED RATHER THAN APPLIED

`OQ-PAY-12627` is OPEN, so no clearing date is passed and `record_payment` writes
`processing`. ⚠ **THE CONSEQUENCE IS BIGGER THAN THE STATUS AND IS WRITTEN AT THE WRITE
SITE:** `record_payment` returns BEFORE the allocator when `cleared_at is None`, so the
bill this payment names is **resolved, checked, passed — and not met.** No allocation row,
no journal entry, and `cut_deposit_batches` never sees it because that takes cleared money
only.

The bill is passed anyway, as `order="specific"` with the invoice number as the target, so
that the day the question is answered `cleared` the allocation is already wired and
correct. **Wiring it then is the second act that never feels like the work** — hard-won law
2's shape, and the reason the code comment and `BR-PAY-1197` both name the consequence
rather than leaving it to be found.

**What the response says about it, and why it says anything at all:** every successful
response carries an `unavailable[]` entry, `recorded_as_processing_not_cleared`, naming
`OQ-PAY-12627`. A `200` carrying a payment number would otherwise read to a partner as *the
bill's balance moved*, and it has not. That is hard-won law 1's mirror — not a comment
claiming a guarantee, but a **silence a reader fills in optimistically.**

### ⚠ AND ONE REGRESSION THE EXISTING TESTS CAUGHT BEFORE IT LEFT THE WORKTREE

`partner_api.partner_provider_keys()` — the set of connectors whose keys may open the
partner door — required that **EVERY** operation on a manifest be `direction="out" and
initiative="them"`. Declaring `record_payment` (`in · them`) therefore dropped
`pay_invoicecloud_partner` out of that set entirely, and **all six of its LIVE READ
addresses would have refused its own customer's key with the five words, on the day a real
utility is being onboarded.**

Its own comment had predicted the shape of it — *"it would go quietly wrong the day a
second partner manifest is registered"* — and it did not go quietly either time:
`test_the_partner_connector_resolves_to_its_own_dialect` names the connector and went RED.

**The predicate now asks the question it was always for:** *does this connector publish an
address on THIS surface* — `any(op.served_path.startswith("/partner/v1/"))`. The kiosk is
still excluded, by the fact that decides it (it declares no `served_path` at all and is
reached at a different door with a different authenticator) rather than by a quadrant that
was a proxy for it. Nothing else moves.

**Two sibling facts, both recorded:** `registry._validate_operation` refused a
`served_path` on an inbound operation for the same conflation — `direction` where it meant
`initiative` — and that IS filed, as `DEF-INT-6485`, because it had a live victim: the
three `payments_kiosk` inbound operations carry no address and therefore draw no row on
S142, which is `DEF-INT-5622` sitting unreported in the inbound quadrant the whole time.
The predicate is now `op.they_call_us`, which is what `Manifest.we_never_dial` had already
written down and given its reasons for.

⚠ **THE `partner_provider_keys` HALF IS NOT FILED AS A DEFECT, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS
STATED SO IT IS A CHOICE RATHER THAN AN OMISSION:** it was correct for every manifest that
existed, it was caught by an existing test in the same hour it was created, and it never
reached the branch. The registry half IS filed, because its victim is live today.

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane MOVEOUT-BUILD, `v2.351.41`): ACC-06 STEP 2 TO ITS DRAWING, AND THE DOOR THAT WOULD HAVE THROWN THE TABLE AWAY

Step 2 of the move-out is now `02-date-and-reads.png`: the date and reason as two
pickers, the PO-approved nine-column reading table, and the PO-approved
seven-column field-visit table. **Neither table is new** — `MoveInReadingsTable`
and `FieldVisitOrders` both existed and both were ratified for this flow on
2026-09-24 (*"this si correct use it"*, *"this si correct - use it"*). The move-out
was the flow that never mounted them.

**⚠ THE FINDING THAT CHANGED THE SHAPE OF THE WORK — `DEF-CUS-6487`.**
`POST /accounts/{id}/move-out` called `_field_visit_templates()`, which returns
`template_ids` and nothing else. `FieldVisitOrders` emits `{none, orders}`. **So
mounting the approved table as instructed would have given a clerk seven columns
and an *Add work order* button over a door that threw every row away** — and the
move-out would have reported success, closed the account, and sent nobody.

**That is hard-won law 2's mirror, and it is worse than a dead prop.** A dead prop
renders nothing and is at least visible. This one renders, accepts input,
succeeds, and there is no error anywhere for anybody to read. `RaiseFieldWork`,
the panel that stood there, offered only the utility's PUBLISHED TEMPLATES — none
at a utility that has written none, which is most of them — so the panel a clerk
saw was usually empty and the door's narrowness had never cost anything.

**WHY NO TEST COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, WHICH IS THE GENERALISABLE PART.** The
move-out is the one flow of three that never mounted the table, so **no caller had
ever sent it `orders`. A door that ignores a key nobody sends is
indistinguishable from a door that handles it.** `DEF-CUS-6363` taught `_move_in`
and the transfer to read the whole election in `2.351.0` and did not re-read the
third door; nothing in this repo counts the flows that share a COMPONENT but not
its CONTRACT. **The habit: when a shared front-end component is approved for a
further flow, diff that flow's DOOR against what the component emits, not only
its screen against the drawing.**

The fix mirrors `_move_in` and invents nothing: `_field_visit()` already parses
all three parts, `_raise_flow_work()` has accepted `orders=` since
`DEF-CUS-6363`, and `field_visit_declined` is already the answer's own key. It is
**additive** — `{"template_ids": [...]}` parses exactly as before, which is
asserted rather than assumed. Five cases, RED first, then green, and green again
on real PostgreSQL because it is a write path that validates before its
transaction opens (law 14).

**FOUR JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULINGS RAN OUT (law 13):**

1. **`OQ-394`'s PREFILL IS NOT A PROP ON THE TABLE, AND THAT WAS THE SECOND
   DRAFT.** The obvious build is `openWith="lastReading"` on the shared
   component. It was written that way and then **deleted**, because
   `moveReadsCapture.effectiveReadsDraft` already does it — and its own docstring
   records that an EFFECT-seeded version was tried and is wrong: an effect runs
   after paint, so for one frame the box shows a figure while the state the
   payload is built from is still empty, and a submit in that frame posts nothing
   over a screen showing a number. The prefill lives in the DRAFT, derived; the
   table renders `props.draft` and has no opinion, so the move-out opens with the
   register's last reading and the move-in opens empty **without the table
   knowing which flow it is on**. The skill's own §7.2 and law 11's *look for the
   tool that owns the job first*, paid for a second time.
2. **THREE PROPS WERE ADDED, AND EACH ONE IS A FACT THE TABLE CANNOT DERIVE:**
   its HEADING (a master has no unit and reads *Meters on the common areas*), its
   DOM-id PREFIX (two wizards addressing `moveIn-read-<id>` is a collision
   waiting for the first screen that mounts both), and the READING COLUMN's
   label. **The third was found by an assertion, not by reading:** the column and
   the hidden label a screen reader announces both said *Move-in reading* on a
   screen closing an account. It typechecked and passed every suite. The
   move-in's own header is PO-approved as built, so it keeps it as the default
   and only the move-out passes its own.
3. **THE TEMPLATE-OFFER QUERY WENT WITH THE PANEL IT FED.**
   `GET /field-work/offer?flow=move_out` is untouched and still serves the
   disconnect; the move-out stopped calling it, because `FieldVisitOrders` reads
   Work's own job types and crews, which every tenant has.
4. **A FIELD-VISIT ROW WITH NO JOB TYPE STOPS *Continue* ON STEP 2.** The server
   refuses it before the transaction opens either way; refusing it here keeps the
   refusal beside the row that caused it rather than on the commit two steps
   later. `visitTried` is set on the press, never on blur, so nothing is red while
   a clerk is still filling the row in.

**PROOF, AND THE BASELINES IT WAS MEASURED AGAINST.** `tsc` clean; eslint clean.
The customers + work front-end suites were run at the TIP and on this tree:
**25 failing cases on both sides, and the two sets are IDENTICAL** — zero
regressions caused, zero fixed. The gate suite likewise: **50 FAIL on both sides,
same set**, and `run_gates`' own comparison prints *0 newly failing, 0 newly
fixed, 132 unchanged*.

**TWO UNOWNED REDS FILED RATHER THAN DISMISSED (`DEF-WRK-6486`).**
`test_us_wrk_039_from_flows.py` TC9 asserts `WORK_ORDER_SOURCES` is 14 and it is
16; TC4's service request does not close on its third job acceptance. Both were
dated by running them in a throwaway worktree at the tip, where both are red.
TC9 is the shape worth naming: **a hardcoded COUNT over an extensible vocabulary
must be edited every time the thing it guards legitimately grows, which is
exactly how a reader learns to dismiss it** — it should assert that the tokens
the case needs are PRESENT. TC4 is a live behaviour claim and is the more serious.

**⚠ AND THE IDS COLLIDED AGAIN, FOR THE THIRD TIME IN ONE DAY.** `6482` and
`6483` were allocated against the remote, and both were taken by siblings
(`DEF-SHL-6482`, `DEF-LED-6483`) before this push ran. They are now `6485` and
`6486`; twelve citations and a test FILENAME moved with them. **The filename is
the part a `sed` over source files misses**, and it is worth writing down: an id
in a path is a citation too.

## 2026-09-24 — ADDENDUM TO THE MAKE PAYMENT BUILD: THREE THINGS BROKE THE SAME WAY, AND THE PATTERN IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIXES

The entry above records five judgments and one near-miss. **By the end of the day there
were FOUR, one of which reached the branch, all created by the same act — declaring one operation — and all
found by reading rather than by any check.** They are written together because separately
each reads as a small bug and together they name a mechanism this repository will meet
again the next time somebody adds an operation of a new KIND.

| What broke | What it would have cost |
|---|---|
| `partner_api.partner_provider_keys()` required EVERY operation to be `out · them` | Invoice Cloud's SIX LIVE READ addresses would have refused their own customer's key, on the day a real utility is being onboarded. Caught by an existing test in the same hour; never left the worktree |
| ⚠ **the FIX for that one, which asked for a `/partner/v1/` address instead** (`DEF-INT-6490`) | **The same failure, moved onto four other partners — and this one WAS PUSHED.** `erp_workday`, `erp_sap`, `erp_infor` and `erp_msgp` declare no `served_path`, so every Workday, SAP, Infor and MSGP key on the branch was refused with the five words for two hours |
| `ConnectionDetailPage`'s default key scope was EVERY operation (`DEF-INT-6488`) | The FIRST key a clerk issued could take money, with nobody ticking it and nothing on the screen saying so |
| `partner_openapi` emitted a `get` with paging parameters for EVERY served address (`DEF-INT-6489`) | The published document told a partner to send `GET /partner/v1/make-payment/?page=1`. They build their client from that document, meet our five-word refusal, and go looking at their key |

### The mechanism, stated once

**All three were DERIVED, and derivation is exactly what made them break.** Deriving the
set of partner connectors, the default scope and the published method from the manifest is
what makes a sixth ERP cost one file and no line of code — that is `BR-INT-037` working,
and none of the three should be replaced with a list.

⚠ **BUT A DERIVED VALUE CARRIES AN UNWRITTEN ASSUMPTION ABOUT WHAT IT IS DERIVING FROM,
AND ADDING A MEMBER OF A NEW KIND CHANGES WHAT THE VALUE MEANS WITHOUT TOUCHING THE LINE
THAT COMPUTES IT.** Every one of the three said *every operation* and meant *every read*,
because until 2026-09-24 those were the same sentence. **Not one of them had a test, and
not one could have had a useful one**, because there was nothing yet to tell apart: a case
asserting *the default scope is every operation* would have been green before and after,
and would have been wrong afterwards.

⚠ **AND NONE OF THEM IS A ROUTE, A RULE OR A PAYLOAD — WHICH IS WHY THE CHECKLIST MISSED
THEM.** The endpoint's own 35 cases were green throughout. What broke was the FURNITURE
around an operation: who may hold a key for this connector, what a new key reaches by
default, and what the published document says the address is. **That is the list to walk
when an operation is added**, and it is written here so the next lane does not have to
find it three times.

### ⚠ THE THIRD ONE WAS THE FIX FOR THE FIRST, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL OF THE THREE

`DEF-INT-6490` is not a fourth instance of the pattern above — it is what happens when
somebody corrects a derived predicate **by describing the case in front of them** instead
of asking what the predicate is for. *Invoice Cloud declares `/partner/v1/make-payment/`,
so let the predicate look for a `/partner/v1/` address* is true of Invoice Cloud, true of
Aclarian, true of New World, and **false of the four ERPs that inherit the phase-1 pair
and declare no address at all**. The fix was shaped to the symptom.

**The question the predicate is actually for is *does THIS DOOR serve anything this
connector declares*, and `SERVED_ROUTES` is that list already** — it is the same table
`_admit` reads to decide which operation a key's scope is checked against. Asking it
directly covers all four kinds of manifest with no branch and no list to maintain.

⚠ **AND THE ESCAPE IS NOT A MISSING CHECK, WHICH IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART.** The suite
DID catch it: 17 partner cases went red naming `erp_workday`. **The lane pushed before
reading that run**, because the previous run of the same set had been green and the grep
used to read the new one matched celery connection noise instead of the summary line. That
is CLAUDE.md law 7 habit 1 running backwards — not *a red I did not cause*, but **a red I
did cause and had not yet looked at** — and law 7's third habit naming the mechanism
exactly: *a check's output must distinguish pass from fail TO A READER*. A grep that can
match a stack trace is not reading a result.

### What is owed, and it is not more tests

`payments_kiosk` declares three inbound operations today and draws **no address** on its
own connector screen, because `registry._validate_operation` refused a `served_path` on
anything inbound until this build corrected the predicate (`DEF-INT-6485`). **That defect
existed the whole time and had a live victim**, and it was invisible for the same reason
the three above were: a guard written when every door was a read cannot distinguish *a
door we publish* from *a door data leaves through* until somebody builds the other kind.
The kiosk's manifest may now declare its addresses; **doing so is a separate change with a
clerk-facing effect and is NOT done here**, because a lane passing through should not
alter what a connector's screen shows for a relationship it is not building.

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane MOVEOUT-BUILD, `v2.351.44`): ACC-06 STEP 1's PANEL, AND THE TWO CLASSES THAT RENDERED NOTHING

Step 1's *This account* panel is now `01-find-account.png`: two columns, twelve
rows, in the drawn order. **Four of those rows were absent and every one was
already on the wire** — `addresses`, `account_type`, `account_subtype_name` and
`kind` have all been served by `account_detail_dict` the whole time. Nothing was
added to the payload; the screen simply never drew them (`DEF-CUS-6476`).

**THAT IS HARD RULE 8's OWN LESSON IN A SECOND PLACE:** *an absence is invisible
to every check this repo has*. `tsc`, eslint, 68 unit cases and 132 gates were all
green over a panel missing a third of its drawn rows, because nothing compares a
panel to its drawing. The only thing that finds one is reading the image row by
row — which is why the guard written here asserts the drawn list **in order**,
not merely that each label appears somewhere.

**THREE JUDGMENTS (law 13):**

1. **IT IS A NEW FILE, AND THE KIT IS WHY.** The drawing puts the facts in TWO
   COLUMNS of label-and-value; the kit's `FactList` is `.met-facts`, a two-column
   grid holding ONE pair per row, so it cannot draw the panel as drawn. The
   alternatives were a four-column class in a stylesheet — which B14 rule 21
   forbids for new UI — or a listed file in Tailwind. `MoveOutWizard.tsx` is NOT
   on `route-b-migrated.txt`, so a utility written there fails `G31` at merge;
   **the fix for an unlisted file is to list a FILE, never to reach for a
   stylesheet class.** `moveOutAccountPanel.tsx` is listed, and it is also where
   the master variant and step 4's review will reuse it (B14 rule 43).
2. **⚠ THE LEDGER'S STRICTER TEST EARNED ITS PLACE ON THE FIRST RUN, AND THIS IS
   THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING.** The panel was written with `text-lg` and
   `text-white`. Both read as perfectly ordinary Tailwind and **this theme
   defines neither**: the size scale runs `xs · sm · base · md · lead · …` with
   no `lg`, and the palette runs `neutral-100..900` with no `white`. Both compile
   to **nothing**, and *every* check that could plausibly have caught it passed —
   `tsc`, eslint, all 68 unit cases — and so would
   `expect(el.className).toContain("text-white")`, because the class genuinely IS
   in the DOM and simply renders no rule. `routeBUtilities.test.ts` named both in
   one line. **This is the concrete argument for LISTING a file rather than
   leaving it to `G31`**, which asks only whether a stylesheet declares each
   class and would have said nothing about either.
3. **THE PANEL'S THREE RIGHT-HAND LABELS DIVERGE FROM THE REST OF THE PRODUCT,
   AND BOTH SIDES ARE RULED (`DEF-CUS-6491`).** The account detail page calls the
   same three columns *Category*, *Sub-category* and *Account kind*; the drawing
   says *Type*, *Sub-type*, *Kind*, and the PO ratified it **after** the panel
   gained exactly those words (*"okay we are good with all changes agreed for
   move out"*). So the product now calls one field two things on two screens.
   **It is FILED rather than resolved either way**: choosing silently is how a
   ruling gets quietly reversed by the next copy audit, and which pair of words
   the product uses is the PO's to settle — B14 rule 34's shape. **A lane running
   a copy audit must not "fix" either screen.**

**PROVED RED BEFORE GREEN, TWICE, ON THE GUARD ITSELF (law 7).** The drawn-row
assertion was shown to bite in both of its halves: deleting the mailing-address
row gave *"Mailing address is missing from the panel, or is out of drawn order"*,
and swapping *Type* with *Sub-type* — a change that leaves every label present —
gave the same failure naming *Sub-type*. A presence-only check would have passed
the second sabotage, which is why the order is asserted.

**REGRESSION:** the customers + work front-end suites report **25 failing cases
here and 25 at the tip, the same set**.

## 2026-09-24 — THE BROWSER WALK OF ACC-06 STEPS 1 AND 2 (lane MOVEOUT-BUILD, `v2.351.45`), AND THE ONE THING IT FOUND THAT NOTHING ELSE COULD

`10-scripts/po20260924_move_out_steps_1_2_walkthrough.mjs` drives the two rebuilt
steps against a booted stack on the seeded `brazosbend` tenant, at **1440 and
1280** — the two staff widths, and nothing narrower, because the staff app is not
a mobile product (PO 2026-09-10). It is READ-ONLY and says so: a move-out commits
and there is no undo (hard rule 4), so the walk opens the screens, reads them and
photographs them, and submits nothing.

**WHAT IT PROVED, IN A BROWSER, THAT NO UNIT TEST IN THIS REPO CAN:**

* step 1's panel draws **all twelve rows in the drawn order** —
  `Account · Name · Service address · Mailing address · Services · Plan` then
  `Type · Sub-type · Kind · Status · Since · Balance`;
* the account finder is **ONE control**, not a box plus a second select, and it
  shows no database id (B14 rule 31);
* step 2's dates are real pickers — **five of them** on a unit with four
  registers (the move-out date and one Read date per row);
* the reading table renders the **nine approved columns**, headed
  `Asset # · Type · Service · Register · Last reading · Last read on · Reading ·
  Read date · Estimate` — and **not** *Move-in reading*, which is what a shared
  table hands you for free;
* **`OQ-394`'s prefill works on a real tenant**: `E-5043` opens with `7891`
  against a last reading of `7,891 kWh` and `W-5043` with `2642` against
  `2,642 kgal`, while two sub-meters with no prior read open EMPTY. Signed law,
  both halves, visible in a photograph;
* every struck sentence is **gone from the rendered page**, and no rule id, OQ or
  DEF reaches a clerk.

**⚠ AND IT FOUND `DEF-CUS-6492`, WHICH IS HARD-WON LAW 6 EARNING ITS KEEP.** On a
MASTER account the meter area of step 2 rendered **nothing at all** — no heading,
no table, no sentence. `MoveInReadingsTable` returns `null` on an empty `unitId`,
which is **correct** for the move-in (it mounts the table before a unit has been
chosen and must draw nothing there) and wrong the moment a second host inherits
it; a master's `unit_id` is NULL by `BR-CUS-1010`.

**Nothing else could have seen it.** Every jsdom case seeds unit assets, so the
table is always present in the suite; `tsc`, eslint and 132 gates were green. The
failure is SILENT — the panel is simply not there, which is indistinguishable
from a panel nobody ever drew. **The guard went in the HOST and not the
component**, because the decision is the host's: the move-in genuinely wants
nothing, and a flag on the shared table would be two answers to one question.

⚠ **THE GENERAL HABIT:** a shared component's early return is a BEHAVIOUR, and a
second host inherits it unasked. When mounting one, exercise the state the FIRST
host could never reach — here, an account with no unit, which only a master can
be.

**⚠ AND THE WALK'S OWN FIRST VERSION DID NOT CHECK (law 7, turned on itself).**
It asked *is there a `<table>`*, and `MoveInReadingsTable` renders FOUR states of
which only one is a table — `loading` is a skeleton, `failed` is a Note, and a
unit with no registers is an empty-text box reading *No meters at this unit*. It
reported "nothing" over a panel plainly on the screen. It now asks for the
COMPONENT and reports which state it is in, which is the difference between a
check and a decoration.

**WHAT THE WALK ALSO SHOWED, AND IS NOT YET BUILT — reported, not quietly left:**
the rail still draws **six** steps, because the four-step merge is the next wave;
the move-out date and the reason are STACKED where `02-date-and-reads.png` draws
them SIDE BY SIDE; the drawing gives the date and reason their own panel above
the meters and the build has all three in one; and the audit sentence at the foot
of the frame (*"Closing an account is recorded in the audit log by the server,
with who, when, and everything that changed."*, 16 words) is RATIONALE on screen
under B14 rule 33 — it was not on the PO's 23-row list, so it is **named here
rather than cut on this lane's own authority**.

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane MOVEOUT-BUILD, `DEF-CUS-6465`, `v2.351.46`): WHAT A MOVE-OUT SAYS IT DID NOT DO IS TRUE AGAIN

`MOVE_OUT_UNAVAILABLE` is the ONE place a caller learns what a move-out did not
do, **so a lie there is worse than a silence.** Three of its five entries had gone
false, and its own comment is why they were never revisited: the list is
unconditional *"because none of these is conditional"* — true the day it was
written, and the sentence that kept anyone from re-reading it.

**MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE SCHEMA RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM THE DEFECT ROW**, which
is why a fourth was found:

| claim | checked | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| billing *"has no tables"* | `invoices` | **exists** — false |
| payments *"has no tables"* | `refunds`, `payments` | **exist** — false |
| the accrual *"is not built"* | `selectors.deposit_interest_accrued` | **answers** — false |
| *"billing has no `invoices` table"* (the issued-bill check) | its seam, wired by `DEF-035` | **wired** — false |
| collections *"has no tables"* | `dunning_cases` | absent — **still true** |
| notifications *"has no tables"* | `notification_messages` | absent — **still true** |

**THE CODES DO NOT MOVE, AND THAT IS THE JUDGMENT.** `final_bill_not_issued` is
still accurate — a move-out PRICES the closing window and does not RAISE the
invoice (blueprint p112, PO ruling 10 of 2026-09-20) — and `deposit_not_settled`
is still accurate because settling needs that invoice. **What was false in both
was the REASON.** Renaming a code that is still true would move a wire contract
to fix a sentence, and the codes are what other surfaces match on.

**THE ACCRUAL ENTRY BECAME CONDITIONAL, WHICH IS THE REAL FIX.** It now takes
`final_reads_not_committed`'s shape, the only other conditional row here: **an
unconditional entry is a claim about the PRODUCT; a conditional one is a claim
about THIS move-out.** The accrual stopped being a product-level absence the day
it shipped (2026-09-03, `CR-059` CS-20), and until today every clerk was told no
interest was worked out — including on the accounts where it had been.

⚠ **THE READ IS WRAPPED, AND NOT OUT OF TIDINESS.** It runs after the transaction
has committed the close, so an accrual that raises must not take the move-out
down with it — `BR-WRK-055`'s posture applied to a read: the account is closed
either way, and a figure we could not reach is reported as exactly that.

**⚠ THE JUDGMENT WHERE THIS LANE DEPARTED FROM THE DEFECT ROW'S OWN PREVENTION,
STATED RATHER THAN QUIETLY TAKEN.** The row says to *"retire the stale catalogue
keys through `i18n_fanin.py` rather than rewording them in place"*. **That would
have been wrong here.** The key IS the code (`customers.account.warning.<code>`)
and every one of these codes is still emitted, so a retired key reaches a clerk
as **silence** — which is the 21-live-refusals hazard `G32` was written for, and
strictly worse than a wrong sentence. Retirement is right when a key stops being
rendered; here the sentence changed and the key did not. The four were corrected
in place across all eleven catalogues through the tool's own `allow_overwrite`,
which exists for exactly this and records that the overwrite was deliberate.

**AND THEY WERE SHORTENED WHILE BEING CORRECTED (B14 rule 33).** The old sentences
carried their RATIONALE — *"Billing owns invoices and has no tables"* — which rule
33 puts at ZERO words on screen. The new ones are a fact and, where a clerk can
act, a second short sentence: *"No final bill was raised. Billing raises it on its
run."*

**PROVED RED FIRST (law 7).** Seven cases, three red and four green at the start —
the four that were already green are the ones guarding what must NOT change: the
two still-true sentences, the accrual selector's existence, and the completeness of
the list. The clerk-facing guard was shown to bite by putting the old sentence
back. **A regression in the OTHER direction is the real risk here** — a lane
sweeping stale claims is one keystroke from "correcting" collections and
notifications, which are exact — so that is asserted by name.

**TWO EXISTING ASSERTIONS HAD TO BE ARGUED WITH, WHICH IS THE ASSERTION WORKING.**
`test_us_cus_005_tc1__move_out_names_every_downstream_it_cannot_perform` pins the
warning set with `==` and its docstring said *"NONE of those modules has a
table"*. Both were corrected with the reasoning in place; a `<=` would have let
the change pass in silence.

**PROOF:** 12 cases green on SQLite and again on real PostgreSQL (law 14 — the
change adds a read after the commit). The two suites that neighbour it report the
same 2 failures and 1 error here as at the tip, both pre-existing move-IN cases.

⚠ **ONE MORE FOUND AND NOT TAKEN:** `customers.account.warning.deposit_not_applied`
still says the plan's deposit lookup *"is not built"*, and the deposit landed on
2026-09-23 (`DEF-CUS-6369`/`6370`). It is the MOVE-IN's warning, it is already
conditional, and it belongs to that flow's lane — **named here rather than swept
into a move-out commit.**

## 2026-09-24 — B14 RULE 44 APPLIED TO THIS LANE'S OWN WORK (`v2.351.47`), AND THE GATE-DIFF HABIT THAT LET IT THROUGH

Rule 44 was ratified while this lane was building — *"please use our ui,
styleguide, spacing specifications. all the time , drawing is for how screen will
look like you ahve to build it sing our ui standard"*. **Counted from B14's own
status table, it now holds THIRTY-FIVE rules, numbered 1–21 and 31–44**; 22–30
were never minted and 30 was declined.

The lane audited its own wave 3 against it and found a breach.

**⚠ `DEF-CUS-6496` — SIX MIN-WIDTH VARIANTS SHIPPED INTO A DESKTOP-FIRST STAFF
SCREEN**, plus `py-2.5` (10px) and `gap-x-10` (40px), neither on the
4·8·12·16·20·24·32 scale. `md:flex-row`, `md:items-baseline`, `md:gap-4`,
`md:w-40`, `md:shrink-0`, `lg:grid-cols-2`.

**THE METHOD FAILURE IS THE FINDING, NOT THE CLASSES.** This lane ran the gate
suite before and after its change and diffed the results — and **diffed each
gate's PASS/FAIL VERDICT.** `G107` was ALREADY FAILING on 39 pre-existing sites,
so six new sites inside it changed nothing about its verdict: the diff printed
*no new gate failures*, truthfully, and the breach went through. `G107` also
truncates its own output at eight findings with `(+31 more)`, so the six were
never printed either.

**That is hard-won law 7's *a true red acquires the protective colouring of a
known one*, one level up: not a red nobody read, but a red whose CONTENTS nobody
compared.** The habit this adds: **when a gate is already failing, diff its
FINDING COUNT, not only its verdict** — a gate going from 39 to 45 findings has
been made worse while still reporting FAIL. The number was available the whole
time, printed as `(+31 more)`, and unread.

**THE REPAIR IS THE KIT, WHICH IS RULE 44's OWN ANSWER.** The panel was
hand-laying label/value rows in Tailwind; `FactList`/`Fact` already own that —
the label column's width, the row rhythm and the type sizes. The file now decides
**one** thing, which is the two-column arrangement the drawing shows, and a
`<span className="font-semibold">` for the two values the drawing sets heavier.
`grid-cols-2` is the BASE rule with no variant: the staff app is laptop and
desktop only, verified at 1280 and 1440 and nothing narrower (PO 2026-09-10), so
widening from a phone breakpoint is construction for a case the product does not
have.

**⚠ AND THE EARLIER FINDING IN THE SAME FILE IS RULE 44's OTHER HALF, FOUND
BEFORE THE RULE EXISTED.** The first draft used `text-lg` and `text-white`; this
theme defines neither, so both compiled to NOTHING while `tsc`, eslint and every
unit case passed — and `toContain("text-white")` would have passed too, because
the class genuinely is in the DOM. `routeBUtilities.test.ts` named both in one
line. **A file on the migration ledger is asked the strict question; an unlisted
one is not**, which is the argument for listing.

**`DEF-CUS-6497` — TWO HEADINGS, ONE LINE APART.** Extracting the panel moved
the drawing's heading into it and left the step's question in the wizard, so step
1 printed *"Which account is moving out?"* twice. **Both are well-formed keys
resolving in all eleven languages**, so every gate and every unit case was green;
the step-1 case asserted the heading with `toContain`, which passes on one
occurrence and on two. Found on the browser walk. The panel now reads *This
account*, as `01-find-account.png` heads it, and **the assertion counts
occurrences rather than testing presence** — after an extraction, the duplicate
is the likelier defect.

**PROOF:** `tsc` and eslint clean; 69 unit cases green; `routeBUtilities.test.ts`
green; the browser walk re-run at 1440 and 1280 against the seeded tenant, still
drawing all twelve rows in the drawn order.

## 2026-09-24 — THE DEPLOY THAT DIED ON `rating/0044` (lane FIX-0044, `v2.351.46`): EIGHT CONSTRAINTS BECOME `NOT VALID`, AND NOT ONE ROW OF MONEY DATA IS TOUCHED

**WHAT HAPPENED.** `rating/0044_p0_4_p0_5_deferred_fks` landed on the morning of
2026-09-24 with Finance `P0.4`/`P0.5`, adding eight `FOREIGN KEY` constraints.
A deploy running `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.production` died
applying it, on the eighth and last:

    django.db.utils.IntegrityError: insert or update on table "plan_deposit_rules"
    violates foreign key constraint "fk_plan_deposit_rules_account_type"
    DETAIL:  Key (account_type_id)=(01a07f66-1139-79aa-a657-0afb2f867087) is not
             present in table "account_types".

The container could not start. `DEF-RAT-6494`.

**WHERE THE ROW CAME FROM, AND IT IS NOT A BUG IN ANY WRITER.** That id is a
uuid7; its first 48 bits decode to **2026-09-08 05:03:10.649 UTC**. It is a
PLATFORM-era `account_types` row — from before `customers/0054` (PO ruling of
2026-09-17, *"utility can get their own account types"*) turned that table from
a platform table into a per-tenant one. `0054` clones every platform row per
tenant, repoints the referencing rows, then deletes the platform rows. **Its
repoint list is `REFERENCING = ("Account", "AccountSubtype", "ServiceRequest")`
and `plan_deposit_rules` is not in it.** `plan_deposit_rules.account_type_id` is
a bare `UUIDField` — a `B11 F-3` deferred FK with no foreign key at all — so
nothing refused, `0054`'s own "stranded" guard could not see it, and the value
was left naming a row that no longer exists. **It is exactly `DEF-RAT-5823`'s
root cause one table further on**; `rating/0041` repaired `rate_plans
.account_type_ids` and measured `plan_deposit_rules` as `0 dangling` **on the
beta**, which was true of that database.

**THE DECISION, AND WHY.** The three options were weighed and only one of them
touches no row:

| Option | Why not / why |
|---|---|
| Delete or NULL the orphaned rows | ⛔ **REFUSED.** A deposit rule is the figure a new customer is actually charged (`BR-RAT-020/023`). Deleting one silently changes that figure — a rule reading `$150.00` becomes `$0.00` for that class with nobody told. And the column is `NOT NULL`, so NULLing is not even available. This is a PO question, minted as `OQ-RAT-12633`. |
| Skip the constraint | ⛔ **REFUSED.** It reopens the door `P0.4` exists to shut while the outcome sentence claims it is closed. |
| **`ADD CONSTRAINT … NOT VALID`** | ✅ **CHOSEN.** The deploy proceeds, every future write is refused correctly from the moment it lands, and the rows already at rest are honestly recorded as unexamined. |

**THE WORKED FIGURES, AND WHICH DATABASE EACH IS FROM.**

| Measured on | Deposit rules | Orphans | What happened |
|---|---|---|---|
| The deploy database (from its traceback, 2026-09-24) | ≥ 1 | ≥ 1 | migrate died on the 8th constraint |
| The seeded dev database `smartbillhub`, PostgreSQL 16.13 | **0** | **0** | 8 account types, 31 charges; `0044` applied clean — which is what the docstring measured |
| The beta, via `rating/0041`, 2026-09-19 | not stated | **0** | true of that database, and of no other |
| The throwaway reproduction `sbh_fix0044` built for this fix | **1** | **1** | old text died, new text applied |

**AND A SECOND FINDING THAT IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST.** `rating/0044`'s docstring
claimed *"THE CONSTRAINT IS ITS OWN PROOF: ADD CONSTRAINT … FOREIGN KEY
validates every existing row and PostgreSQL refuses the migration if one id
names nothing."* **That is false under `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, which every
one of these eight tables carries.** PostgreSQL validates a new foreign key with
an ordinary scan, and that scan is evaluated against the `B2 §3` policy like any
other read. The migration role carries `app.tenant_id =
00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` — the NO-TENANT sentinel — in its own
`rolconfig`, which overrides the database default, so the scan matches no row of
any tenant. **Measured on PostgreSQL 16.13 on 2026-09-24, one real orphan
present: `manage.py migrate` exited 0, the constraint came out `convalidated =
t`, and the orphan was still there.** The same database, read as the app role,
reports `charges = 0` where the truth is `charges = 31`.

So the file both **dies** on a role that can see the rows and **silently
certifies nothing** on the role that actually runs migrations. `NOT VALID` is
the honest form of what was already happening, and it is now recorded as such:
`convalidated = f` on all eight.

**ALL EIGHT, NOT JUST THE ONE THAT FAILED.** The other seven validated against
one database's rows on one day. That is evidence about that database and about
nothing else — which is this defect's entire lesson, and converting only the
eighth would leave seven doors to the identical failure open on the next deploy.

**WHAT IS OWED AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN.** A `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`
migration, which examines the rows already there. It is **not** written now,
because on the deploy database it would fail on the same row and block the same
deploy again. It waits on `OQ-RAT-12633`.

**A LIVE SECOND EXPOSURE, FOUND IN BLAST RADIUS AND FILED — `DEF-CUS-6495`.**
`customers.lookups.AccountTypeLookupHandler.used_by` counts `accounts`,
`account_subtypes` and `service_requests` — **the same three tables `0054`
repointed, from the same wrong source: the set of tables holding a real Django
`ForeignKey`.** A deferred pointer is by construction not one. So a tenant admin
could delete a consumer category a deposit rule prices against, and make a fresh
orphan, through the S8 reference-data card. **After this migration the database
refuses that delete** — proved on PostgreSQL, `NOT VALID` refuses parent deletes
just as a validated constraint does — **but it reaches the clerk as a 500 with
no sentence in it, which is the exact outcome `used_by`'s own docstring says it
exists to prevent.** Filed rather than fixed here: it is a different module and
a different screen, and this lane's job was the deploy.

**THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH IS THIS REPO'S OWN LAW 7 IN A NEW PLACE.** *"A check
reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes."* Two of them in one file: a
row count measured on one database and published as a fact about all databases,
and a constraint-validation scan that obeys row-level security and therefore
certifies only what the migration role can see. **A migration that adds a
constraint over existing rows must say which database and which date its counts
came from, in those words** — the docstring now does — **and must never call
`ADD CONSTRAINT` a proof.**

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane FINANCE-P1, `v2.351.50`): THE JOURNAL PAGES IN SQL, THE BATCH POSTS IN FULL OR NOT AT ALL, AND SIX JUDGMENTS NO RULING MADE

**`P1.8` · `P1.10` · `P1.18` · `P1.22`, with `DEF-LED-6493`, `DEF-LED-6521`,
`DEF-LED-6523` and `DEF-LED-6522` filed.**

**MEASURED FIRST, AND THE FIGURE IS WHY THIS PHASE EXISTS.** `GET
/ledger/journal-entries` handed DRF a built LIST, so the wire response was
bounded — which is what 11b G5 checks — and the QUERY was not. Measured on the
branch's own code before the fix: **67 database statements over 60 journal
entries and 307 over 300**, one per entry, because `entry.reversed_by.first()`
sat inside the row loop. At the top of T5 that is 40,000 entries built to draw
fifty. After: **twelve statements at 60 entries, twelve at 20,000** — flat, and
the page is a `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` with the count in a `COUNT(*)`.

### The six judgments, each where a rule ran out

**1 · `core.pagination.prepaged` EXISTS BECAUSE THE CODE ASKED FOR IT BY NAME,
AND THE THREE EXISTING COPIES ARE NOT CONVERTED.** `apps/rating/api._prepaged`'s
own docstring reads *"THIS IS A SECOND COPY OF `customers._prepaged` AND THAT IS
DELIBERATE BUT NOT DESIRABLE. Its home is `core/pagination.py` … a third copy
should trigger it instead of being written."* The ledger is that third caller,
so the move was taken. **The three existing copies stay**, and that is a
decision rather than an omission: they carry THREE different signatures —
customers `(request, rows, total, params, extra, refetch)`, metering `(request,
rows, total, params, refetch, extra)`, rating `(request, params, fetch, extra)`
— so converting them is a change to three other modules' endpoints with three
other modules' suites to re-prove, inside a phase whose own plan says *"one team
does not silently do another's migration"* (`P1.13`). The pointer is in the new
function's docstring, where the next lane reads it.

**2 · THREE FACTS ON THE JOURNAL RESPONSE ARE ABOUT THE FILTERED SET AND NOT
ABOUT THE PAGE, AND EACH WOULD HAVE BROKEN SILENTLY.** `total`, `currencies`
(DEF-081's mixed-book banner) and the `posted_entries_without_a_je_number` gap
were all derived from the built `rows`. Sliced to a page they become statements
about fifty arbitrary entries: the banner goes quiet on page 2 and the gap
reports fifty on page 1 and ten on page 4 of one book. All three are now SQL
over the whole set, and two cases pin it.

**3 · THE GAP'S ID LIST IS BOUNDED AT FIFTY AND THE WIRE CARRIES THE COUNT
INSTEAD.** An unbounded id list inside a bounded page is `NFR-3` breached inside
its own fix — 40,000 UUIDs beside fifty rows. ⚠ **AND THE IDS HAD NEVER REACHED
A CLIENT AT ALL (`DEF-LED-6521`, found by the case written for this):**
`wire.gap` serialises four NAMED keys while its docstring promised *"nothing
else changes, and no field is dropped"*, so `entry_ids` has been on the read
model's gap since the gap was written and on no response ever. Hard-won law 1.
The COUNT is now carried — a screen can say *"168 carry no number"* in six words
(B14 rule 33) — and the ids deliberately are not, because nothing renders them
(law 2).

**4 · `?sort=number` ORDERS BY `entry_date`, AND THAT IS THE RULE RATHER THAN A
SHORTCUT (`P1.18`).** The drawing (p020 item 6) puts a `⇅` on ENTRY NO. and on
DATE. `JE-{MM}{DD}{YY}-{0000}` does not sort chronologically as text —
`JE-011526-0001` precedes `JE-020325-0001` and is eleven months older — and the
PO ruled that format knowing so. The blueprint calls it *"one consequence to
build around rather than to ask about"*. Both sort names map to the same date
terms, and a case asserts the DESCENDING order of exactly those two numbers, so
a later lane "simplifying" it to `order_by("number")` goes red instead of
silently reordering the journal. **Every sort tuple ends in `id`**, because
`created_at` is not unique under a bulk insert and a page over a non-total order
shows one row twice and another never.

**5 · `P1.22`'s PRE-CHECK IS A SEPARATE, NAMED, CALLABLE FUNCTION.** The PO's
option (c) and the rejected (a) both leave the books untouched on a failure;
(c) was chosen for exactly one reason — *"Priya is told about the missing memo
before anything is attempted"*. A build that posts, fails and rolls back has
implemented (a) and would pass every all-or-nothing case. So
`precheck_manual_je_batch` stands on its own and is asserted on its own.
**Proved by deliberate break:** with the pre-check removed,
`test_the_batch_is_refused_before_anything_is_attempted` and
`test_the_pre_check_reports_every_bad_entry_not_only_the_first` go RED and the
six all-or-nothing cases stay GREEN — which is what makes them a discriminator
rather than a restatement.

**6 · THE PERIOD IS NOT PRE-CHECKED AND ACCOUNT STATE IS NOT EITHER, BOTH FOR
STATED REASONS.** `BR-TEN-038` AUTO-FORWARDS a date in a closed period rather
than refusing it, so there is nothing for a pre-check to refuse. A GL account
switched off BETWEEN the check and the post is the case `BR-LED-798` itself
records as **UNSPECIFIED** — *"naming which entry and why in that rarer case is a
screen question nobody has put"* — so the transaction rolls the batch back,
which is the ruling applied, and nothing is invented about what the officer is
told.

### Three reds read, dated, and filed rather than dismissed

CLAUDE.md law 7 habit 1, and habit 1's own amendment: *calling a red
pre-existing WITHOUT DATING IT does the exact opposite of what the habit is
for.*

* **Four `test_def_081_mixed_currency_book.py` cases** fail on their own SETUP:
  the fixture posts a CAD entry to build a mixed book and `P0.7` made that
  refusal correct. Dated with `git log -S "keeps its books in"` to
  **`5022fab70`, 2026-09-24**, lane FINANCE-P0. `DEF-LED-6523`.
* **Two `tc2b` cases** assert `posted_entries_without_a_je_number` is REPORTED.
  `P0.3` seeded the series, so every posted entry now carries a number and the
  gap is correctly absent. Dated to **`b813394a6`, 2026-09-24**, the same lane.
  A probe printed nine posted entries, every one numbered `JE-063026-0001`
  onward — which also proves the OLD code would fail these identically, so they
  are not this lane's. `DEF-LED-6522`.
* **This lane's own two**, found and fixed before pushing: `.distinct()` after
  `.order_by()` does not collapse, because Django puts the ordering columns in
  the SELECT — the first draft returned nine `'USD'`s for a nine-entry
  single-currency book and **would have fired the mixed-currency banner on every
  screen in the product**; and `exclude(number__in=("", None))` never matches
  NULL in SQL, so a case meant to prove no number was allocated passed over five
  clean drafts.

### And the volume fixture could not run on the only database that matters

⚠ **HARD-WON LAW 14, IN A FIXTURE RATHER THAN IN THE CODE.** `plant_entries`
bulk-creates journal rows, which is fine on SQLite and is REFUSED outright on
PostgreSQL by `ledger/0004`'s sole-writer trigger —
`psycopg.errors.RaiseException: CLAUDE.md rule 5: journal_entries is written
ONLY by the ledger posting service`. The first version of the whole file was
green on the default suite and **incapable of passing** on the tier where the
guarantee exists. Found by running it under `--ds=config.settings.pgtest` and by
nothing else. The fixture now opens the transaction-local write window
explicitly and says in its own docstring why that is not a bypass: it seeds
read-path volume and asserts no money figure.


## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane MOVEOUT-BUILD, `DEF-CUS-6464`, `v2.351.51`): STEP 3 ANSWERS THE PO'S OWN QUESTION

**PO, 2026-09-24, looking at the running product:** *"no bill is generated here
... why are we unable to generate the bill here?"*

**THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY ON THE WIRE.** `preview_final_bill` returns
`priced: false` with `priced_unavailable{reason, detail}`, and the `detail` is
the engine's own actionable sentence. Two things kept it off the screen:

1. **The port threw half of it away.** `finalBillPreviewPort` kept the `reason`
   — a CODE, which B14 rule 32 forbids showing a clerk — and dropped the
   `detail`, so there was nothing left that could legally be rendered.
2. **The one place that read it was unreachable.** `FinalBillLines` read
   `preview.unavailable` inside a `rows.length === 0` branch, and that branch
   stopped being reachable on **2026-09-19**, when the export-credit and *Final
   bill, net* rows were added: `settlementMoneyOf` never returns null once
   close-impact answers, so `money` is non-null on every account and the two
   rows it pushes make the empty branch dead.

**Measured on the seeded tenant: 30 of 75 open accounts refuse to price**, and on
every one the panel drew two rows and **no sentence at all**.

**THREE JUDGMENTS (law 13):**

1. **KEYED ON `priced === false`, NOT ON `rows.length`.** The old condition was a
   proxy that stopped tracking the thing it stood for. The new one asks the
   server's own question.
2. **RENDERED BESIDE THE TABLE, NOT INSTEAD OF IT.** The export credit and the
   net are real figures even when the priced lines are missing; hiding them to
   show a refusal trades one silence for another.
3. **⚠ THE ENGINE'S WORDS, VERBATIM — AND THIS IS A DELIBERATE TENSION WITH B14
   RULE 33.** The sentence runs to about sixty words and carries its own
   reasoning (*"An unpriced size is REFUSED and never substituted (PO ruling
   2026-08-28) — charging this connection another size's rate is not charging it
   for the connection it has"*). Rule 33 caps a FACT at six words and puts
   RATIONALE at zero. **It is quoted anyway, for the reason
   `oneTimeConfirmShared.ts` already quotes it one flow over: a paraphrase
   behind a catalogue key would be a SECOND COPY of an engine message, free to
   drift from the engine** — and the engine is the only thing that knows which
   charge code and which size. Shortening it would take the actionable half out.
   **This is REPORTED rather than taken quietly:** if the PO wants engine
   messages inside rule 33's caps, that is a change to the ENGINE's messages, in
   one place, not a paraphrase on this screen.

**PROVED RED, THEN GREEN, THEN IN A BROWSER.** Two cases: the refusal renders
with `role="alert"` and its code stays on `data-` only; and a PRICED preview
draws no refusal even when a stale detail rides along — the mirror case, without
which the sentence could have been hardcoded onto a healthy screen. The fix was
sabotaged back to an unreachable branch and the first case went red naming the
missing sentence.

⚠ **AND ONE ASSERTION WAS WRONG BEFORE THE CODE WAS.** `visible()` in this suite
strips `title="…"` and nothing else, so `expect(visible(html)).not.toContain(code)`
fails on the test's own `data-final-bill-unavailable` — which is exactly where
the code is SUPPOSED to be. Rule 32 is about what a clerk READS, so the check is
against text content with the tags stripped. **A helper named `visible` is not a
text extractor, and reading its name instead of its body is how a true assertion
gets written backwards.**

**THE BROWSER WALK IS WHERE IT WAS REALLY PROVED** (hard-won law 6). Walking to
`?step=3` directly proves NOTHING: the preview query is disabled until a
move-out date exists — correctly, since there is no window to price without one
— so the walk now types the date on step 2 and presses *Continue*, which is
in-page only and writes nothing. On account `A-10432` at 1440 and 1280 the
sentence renders in the accent colour above the bill and the code
(`plan_has_no_tariff_for_service`) is absent from `document.body.innerText`.
**The walk stays read-only: nothing is submitted and nothing is parked**, because
a move-out commits and there is no undo (hard rule 4).

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane FINANCE-P1, `v2.351.52`): 1·1 JOURNAL IS A VIEW OF ITS OWN AND THE LANDING VIEW, AND FIVE JUDGMENTS NO RULING MADE

**`P1.1` · `P1.9` · `P1.15` · `P1.17`, built from the RENDERED IMAGES of
`05-prototype/07 Finance Blueprint.pdf` p020, p021 and p022** (B14 rule 42, and
the PO restated it in their own words: *"when you use images to create screens
your accuracy is higher; hence dont create screens using only Text"*). The text
layer of that PDF is scrambled — screen headings land against the wrong titles
and the reading order is not the page order — so nothing here was built from it.
**B14 rule 44, ratified the same day, decided HOW it was built**: the spacing,
the type scale and the tokens are `tokens.css`'s, not the drawing's pixel
values.

**WHAT A CLERK CAN DO THAT THEY COULD NOT.** The journal was a `PlainTable`
rendered *inside* `?view=balance`, as a panel below the trial balance: no
search, no filter chips, no column chooser, no pager and no sortable headers,
over a list that grows with transaction volume. p022's TABLE CONTROLS row said
so in the blueprint's own words — *"All six, none of which exists today."* A
clerk reached fifty entries and no more. They can now search the memo and the
entry number, filter by type, state and source, choose and reorder columns, sort
by number or by date, page through the whole book, and **send a colleague the
filtered view as a link** — which is this phase's own *"A clerk can newly"*
line, and the half that had never worked.

### The five judgments

**1 · `journal` IS A NEW URL VALUE AND `balance` KEEPS ITS OLD ONE.** p023
records the split — *"Balance · was 'Trial balance & journal'; the journal moved
out to 1·1"* — so the WORD on screen changed. The VALUE did not: every existing
bookmark, ticket link and test carries `?view=balance`, and renaming it would
break each of them to no purpose. `journal` is FIRST and is what an absent or
unknown `?view=` falls back to, because p020 marks it *"the landing view"* and
p022's DOORS line reads *"It is the landing view, so every door to `/finance` is
a door to this screen"*. **One existing case pinned the old fallback**
(`ledgerAdmin.test.tsx`) and is AMENDED with the ruling written beside it rather
than quietly made green — what it actually asserts, that an unknown value
resolves to something and never 404s, is unchanged.

**2 · THE VIEW SWITCH NO LONGER WIPES THE QUERY STRING (`P1.9`).** It did
`setSearchParams({ view })`, which REPLACES the whole string — so `q`, `sort`,
`page` and every `f.*` were thrown away by changing section, and a browser Back
could not bring them home. Only `view` moves now.

**3 · THE JOURNAL PARSES `?sort=` WITH ITS OWN CONFIG, NOT THE TRIAL
BALANCE'S.** `parseTableParams` validates `sort` against the columns it is
handed, so reading `?sort=entry_date` through `trialBalanceConfig` falls back to
`code` — **a shared URL that opens on a different order than the one that was
copied**, which is the exact promise `P1.9` exists to make good. One view is on
screen at a time, so the two states never both drive a table.

**4 · THE 👁 VIEW ACTION IS DISABLED WITH ITS REASON, AND THAT IS THE HONEST
BUILD RATHER THAN A GAP.** p020 note 7 draws three controls — *"👁 view · ↺
reverse, then `…`"* — and p022's WRITE SURFACES line says *"Detail NOTHING —
`GET /ledger/journal-entries/{id}` is mounted DELETE-only"*. There is no entry
detail to open. A live 👁 onto nothing is `DEF-007`'s family and hard-won law
2's mirror — **a dead control over a screen that does not exist** — so the
control stays VISIBLE, disabled, and says *"No detail view"* (`BR-SHL-025`, four
words, B14 rule 33). The day the read lands, the reason goes and the handler
arrives with it.

**5 · THE CAP LIVES IN THE CALLER AND NOT IN `RowActions` (`P1.17`).** B14 rule
15 wants *"max 2 visible, then `…`"* and the drawing's own note says *"the cap
`RowActions` does not enforce"*. Making the container enforce it would change
every table in the product at once on one screen's authority — the class of
change rule 38 refuses. The journal's Actions cell draws 👁 · ↺ · `…`, exactly
as p020 draws it, with *Delete draft* in the overflow because a draft is not in
the books (`BR-LED-003`) and a posted entry can never be deleted (hard rule 4).

### Two things the checks found that a reading would not

⚠ **`text-muted` COMPILES TO NOTHING IN THIS THEME**, and `tsc`, eslint and
`toContain("text-muted")` all pass over it. The first draft of `JournalView.tsx`
used it four times; `routeBUtilities.test.ts` named the file and the token.
`RateScheduleWizard.tsx:1694` already carried this warning in its own comment
from `DEF-RAT-6447`, one screen over. **Proved capable of failing on THIS file**
before it was trusted green: a planted `text-muted` produced *"text-muted (asked
for by features/ledger/JournalView.tsx)"*, and its removal turned the check
green again.

⚠ **G15 WAS RED BEFORE THIS LANE STARTED AND IS NOT ONE VALUE WORSE FOR IT.**
Dated rather than assumed (law 7 habit 1, and its amendment: *calling a red
pre-existing WITHOUT DATING IT does the exact opposite of what the habit is
for*): the gate was run in a throwaway `git worktree` at `a5242414a`, this
lane's own base, where it reports **546 NEW untranslated values**. The first
draft of the new keys took it to 551, because five were HOMOGRAPHS —
*"Journal"* in German and French, *"Balance"* in Spanish and French — and the
gate cannot tell a homograph from an untranslated paste, correctly. **The
baseline was NOT widened**, which is the one move that converts a true finding
into a permanently invisible one. Each was re-worded to the term that language's
own bookkeepers use — *Buchungsjournal*, *Journal comptable*, *Libro diario*,
*Sumas y saldos*, *Balance générale* — which is both distinct AND better copy
under B14 rule 35. The gate is back at **546**, exactly the base's figure.

### AND THIS LANE REPRODUCED LAW 11's OWN NAMED TRAP, TWICE, IN ONE SCRIPT

Worth a paragraph because the law already describes it exactly and it was
written anyway. CLAUDE.md law 11: *"the script written to apply the paragraph
above did `open(dst,"w")` and only then read its input — so when the read
failed, the output file had ALREADY been truncated … never let a re-derivation
script open its destination before it has the bytes to put in it."*

The push helper for this commit contained `open(p, "w").write(open(p).read()
.replace(...))` in two places. Python evaluates the outer call's object first,
so `open(p, "w")` truncates before the read runs and the read returns an empty
string.

**`10-scripts/push_register_guard.py` refused the push**, naming the exact
damage: *"81387 line(s) present in `e767a2bb:12-governance/02-decision-log.md`
are ABSENT from the version about to be pushed. That is a revert BY SUBTRACTION
and every other law-11 check passes on it."* It was right, and **nothing reached
the branch** — the working copy was the only casualty, and it was rebuilt from
the pinned tip on the next run.

⚠ **THE SECOND OCCURRENCE IS THE INSTRUCTIVE ONE, BECAUSE THE GUARD COULD NOT
SEE IT.** The same statement had already truncated `decision_section.md` — a
SCRATCHPAD file, which no guard watches — so the corrected run appended an empty
section and pushed a decision-log change of **one line, not 178**. The
`--numstat` said `1 1` and reading it AS ARITHMETIC is what caught it; a glance
would have called that the placeholder fix and moved on. This section is that
work, rewritten and pushed separately.

⚠ **AND THE PLACEHOLDER ITSELF WAS THE FIRST SYMPTOM.** `a5242414a` shipped its
decision heading reading `v__VERSION__`, because that script substituted the
version into the COMMIT MESSAGE and not into the section. Corrected in
`7ec79ef36`, declared out loud through `ALLOW_REGISTER_DELETIONS=1` because it
is genuinely one line changing rather than work being lost. **The durable lesson
is smaller than the law and sits beside it: a template that reaches more than
one file needs the substitution to happen ONCE, before anything is written —
not per file, afterwards, by the step most likely to be edited in a hurry.**
