## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane FINANCE-P1): `P1.21` — THE BATCH SCREEN, WHICH IS THE DOOR `P1.22` DID NOT HAVE

**Built from the RENDERED IMAGES of p029 and p030** (B14 rule 42), under rule
44's standard: the kit's spacing, type scale and tokens decide how it is built,
and the drawing decides what is on it.

⚠ **IT IS FILED HERE AS A LAW-2 REPAIR AS WELL AS A TASK.** This lane shipped
`POST /ledger/journal-entries/post-batch` in `a5242414a` with **nothing in the
product able to call it** — an endpoint, tested and proved on PostgreSQL, that
no human could reach. That is hard-won law 2 exactly, committed by the lane that
has the law quoted at the top of its own brief. The gap existed for three
commits.

**WHAT A CLERK CAN NOW DO.** A finance officer closing a month types five
entries into one screen and posts them in one act. Before, each was a separate
trip through a modal with no address, no batch and no draft to return to — p030
records that state in the blueprint's own words.

### The judgments

**1 · `PageHeader`, NOT `WizardFrame`, AND THE DRAWING SAYS WHY.** p030's
components table: *"Replaces the modal's header and footer. **Not
`WizardFrame`** — composing is a loop, not a sequence of steps."* A numbered
rail over something done three times in any order would misdescribe the work.

**2 · TWO ACCOUNT PICKERS AND ONE AMOUNT, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES A ROW AN ENTRY.**
p029 note 3: *"Two accounts and one figure cannot be unbalanced, so `BR-LED-003`
holds **by construction rather than by validation**."* So this screen has no
"must balance" footer, because there is nothing it could ever say. The composer
refuses one account on BOTH sides — the FIELDS table's own *"Refused if equal to
the debit account"* — because such an entry moves nothing and would post
cleanly: a balanced, numbered, immutable no-op in the books.

**3 · A MEMO IS REQUIRED TO POST AND NOT TO ADD**, which is the FIELDS table's
own `Required: To post`. `BR-LED-003` needs it because a posted entry is
immutable, so the memo is the only place the WHY can be written — but a clerk
should be able to get five sets of figures down first. **The screen refuses the
BATCH for a missing memo before the one irreversible button**, which is the half
of the PO's option (c) that lives on the screen rather than in the service.

**4 · *Post all N ✓* IS N+1 CALLS AND THE GUARANTEE IS UNHARMED.** The batch
endpoint takes ENTRY IDS, so a composed entry must exist as a draft first: the
button saves every unsaved entry and then makes **one** batch call.
`BR-LED-798`'s promise is about POSTING — *"no journal entry, no journal line
and no allocated number"* — and the posting is the one transaction. A save that
fails half way leaves DRAFTS, which are freely editable and deletable and carry
no number (`BR-LED-003`), so nothing a reader of the books would ever have to
explain. **A loop over `postManualJournalEntry` would be the option the PO
rejected**, and the client wrapper's docstring says so where the next lane will
read it.

**5 · THE COUNT IS IN THE BUTTON AND IN THE CONFIRM.** p029 note 8: *"the count
is in the button, so nobody posts three thinking it is one"*. The confirm is the
one thing that stays a modal (p030) and names the count and that it cannot be
undone — two sentences, six words each, B14 rule 33.

**6 · TAGS ARE ABSENT AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN SILENT.** p029 note 4 draws
*"Tags · the five dimensions, optional · P1.16"* and the FIELDS table marks them
`Required: No`. `P1.16`'s backend is not built — `ManualJournalLine` is *"an
account, a side, an amount"* and carries none of the five — so a Tags control
here would be a form field with nowhere to send its value, which is `DEF-007`'s
family. **Not drawn, and recorded as owed.**

### And two things about method, both this lane's own errors

⚠ **`tsc` WAS REPORTED CLEAN OVER FIVE REAL TYPE ERRORS, BECAUSE A 0-BYTE
OUTPUT FILE WAS READ AS A CLEAN RUN.** The typecheck had not finished writing.
It later reported, on the same tree: `apiErrorText` imported from the wrong
module, `useRegional` and `RegionalProps` from the wrong module, and two
implicit `any`s — and a sixth, a module that does not exist at all
(`@/features/shell/useTenantPath`), which **vitest** caught first because its
real module resolution runs the import. **A check's OUTPUT is not its RESULT:
only a completed process and its exit code are.** Reading an in-progress
artefact as a verdict is law 7's *looking at the wrong thing*, in the reader
rather than in the check.

⚠ **AND THE WAIT WRITTEN TO AVOID THAT PROBLEM COULD NEVER FINISH.**
`until ! pgrep -f "tsc --noEmit"; do sleep; done` matches **its own command
line**, so the loop waits for itself — seven of them accumulated, each spinning
for ever. A guard that cannot pass is the mirror of one that cannot fail, and
both are law 7's subject. The working form is a SENTINEL the job itself writes
when it is done, which is what the run that finally reported `136 passed (136)`
used.

## 2026-09-24 — `DEF-LED-6526` (lane FINANCE-P1): I REVERTED ANOTHER LANE'S WORK, AND THE FLAG THAT LET ME DO IT WAS ONE I SET TRUTHFULLY

**What was lost, for eleven minutes, in `af8956920`:** the P2 lane's `P2.3`
premises filter on the General ledger (its control, its `usePremisesSearch`
hook and the premises in the trial balance's CACHE KEY) and `DEF-LED-6524`'s
three-valued `balanced` — the fix that renders a filtered table's `null`
verdict as *"the question does not apply"* rather than as a red **UNBALANCED**
pill with a difference beside it. Restored in `513f39089`, rebuilt from
`4ecf5b9cb` with exactly one hunk of this lane's re-applied; `diff` against
their version shows that hunk and nothing else.

### The cause, and it is not the one law 11 warns about

`10-scripts/push_paths.sh` **refuses a named path that moved between the base
and the tip**. That is the single guard written for exactly this, and
`REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1` turns it off.

**I set that flag truthfully.** The push carried eleven locale catalogues, the
decision log, the changelog and three version files, and every one of them HAD
been rebuilt from the pinned tip seconds earlier — because those are the files
this repository loses work in most often, and re-deriving them is what the law
asks for. The flag then applied to the other six paths too, which came straight
from a working tree last synced three commits earlier.

⚠ **THE FLAG IS ALL-OR-NOTHING AND THE ASSERTION IT MAKES IS ABOUT EVERY NAMED
PATH.** A lane that re-derives the *dangerous* files and reaches for the flag to
say so is, without noticing, also vouching for the ordinary ones. That is the
shape: **the more carefully you handle the shared registers, the more likely
you are to disable the guard protecting the source files.**

### Every other check in law 11 passed, exactly as the law says they would

The file count was right. My own change WAS in `HEAD`. `git show` showed my
hunks. `git status` was clean. **The deleted work is not in the diff at all** —
it is missing from the tree the diff is taken against.

**What caught it was reading `git diff --numstat` AS ARITHMETIC**, which is the
one thing law 11 prescribes that no tool does for you: `56 121` on a file I had
added twelve lines to. A glance would have read "56 and 121, looks like a
refactor" and moved on.

### What to do instead, and it is a change to the helper rather than a habit

**A push that re-derives SOME paths must re-derive ALL of them, or the helper
must take the re-derived SET rather than a global assertion.** `REDERIVED_FROM_TIP=1`
should name paths — `REDERIVED_PATHS="a b c"` — so the staleness check still
runs over everything else. Until it does, the honest options are two: re-derive
every named path, or split the push in two, the re-derived files in one commit
and the ordinary ones in another where the guard is live.

**This lane used the flag five times today and this is the one that bit.** The
other four named only files that had genuinely been rebuilt.

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane FINANCE-P1): `P1.6` — THE EXPORT TARGETS ARE SERVED ONCE

The four accounting-export formats `BR-LED-004` names — QuickBooks Online,
Xero, CSV and IIF — were typed out in `07-frontend/src/api/endpoints.ts` as
`EXPORT_TARGETS = ["qbo","xero","csv","iif"]`, under a comment reading
***"`apps.ledger.models.EXPORT_TARGETS` verbatim"***.

⚠ **THAT COMMENT IS A CLAIM ABOUT ANOTHER FILE AND NOTHING RE-CHECKED IT**
(hard-won law 1). A fifth target added on the server would have left the format
picker offering four **for ever**, with `tsc`, eslint and every test passing —
which is the service-list failure CLAUDE.md law 12 names, one module over:
*"the service list is typed by hand in TWO places, so an eleventh service does
not appear on screen on its own and it fails silently."*

**`GET /finance/export/batches` now serves `targets`**, and `CloseExportPage`
draws the picker from the response.

### Two judgments

**1 · IT RIDES ON AN EXISTING RESPONSE RATHER THAN ON A NEW ENDPOINT.** This is
the read the Close & export screen already makes, and the screen that draws the
picker is the screen that draws this history. A `GET /lookups/export_targets`
would have been the wrong shape as well as a new route: `/lookups/{list}` is
TENANT REFERENCE DATA a tenant edits on Settings, and the export formats are a
PLATFORM constant — what this product can write, not what a utility has chosen.

**2 · THE CONSTANT STAYS, AS THE TYPE AND AS THE FIRST-RENDER FALLBACK.**
`ExportTarget` is a union the whole screen is typed on, and the picker has to
draw something before the first response arrives. What changed is which one the
CLERK sees: the list on screen is the server's. The constant is no longer the
source of truth and its docstring now says so, which is the difference between
a fallback and a second copy.

⚠ **AND THE GATE AGAINST DRIFT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A TEST**: the picker
renders the response. A fifth target appears the moment the server has one.

### AND THE CONTRACT SNAPSHOT: A RED THAT WAS NOT MINE, AND A REGENERATION THAT CARRIES THREE LANES

`tests/test_be11_openapi.py` refuses when `06-backend/openapi/schema.json` no
longer matches the routes the code mounts. It was **already red at this lane's
base** — dated, not assumed: the first line of its diff names
`/api/partner/v1/make-payment`, which `git log -S` puts at **`dd7915c6d`,
2026-09-24, the Invoice Cloud lane**, and which is absent from the snapshot
committed at `a09c62259`. This lane's own `POST
/ledger/journal-entries/post-batch` (`P1.22`) then made it stale a second time.

⚠ **THE SNAPSHOT IS ONE GENERATED FILE, SO REGENERATING IT PUBLISHES EVERY
LANE'S ROUTES AT ONCE.** `manage.py export_openapi` adds exactly three groups:
`/api/partner/v1/make-payment` (Invoice Cloud's),
`/api/{tenant}/ledger/journal-entries/post-batch` (this lane's) and
`/api/{tenant}/move-ins/messages` (the move-in lane's). **There is no way to add
one without the others**, which is `DEF-168`'s mechanism — a commit publishing
another lane's work — arriving through a generated file rather than through a
pathspec.

**Taken deliberately, and said out loud rather than left to a reader of the
diff.** A contract snapshot that is wrong about a partner route which WRITES
MONEY is worse than a tidy commit boundary, and the alternative — leaving it —
means the next lane inherits a gate that has been red since yesterday for
reasons belonging to three different people. The commit message names all
three.

⚠ **AND FIXING ONE RED EXPOSED ANOTHER THAT HAD BEEN BEHIND IT — `DEF-INT-6529`.**
With `tc05` green, `tc02` now runs to completion and fails: it asserts an EXACT
allowlist of operations the contract publishes as PUBLIC, and **fifty
`/api/partner/v1/…` operations are in it.** The partner surface authenticates by
API KEY, which declares no `sessionCookie` requirement, so drf-spectacular emits
`security: [{}]` — the same shape as a genuinely public route. The contract
therefore tells a client generator that fifty partner operations, one of which
WRITES A PAYMENT, need no credential.

**It is not this lane's and it is not new**: the partner routes predate this
lane's base. It was simply unreachable while `tc05` failed first. **A red behind
a red is a red nobody has read**, which is law 7's own subject — and the honest
fix is to declare the partner key scheme beside its authenticator, as
`apps/identity/auth.py` already does for the session cookie, rather than to
widen `tc02`'s allowlist. Filed rather than fixed, because it is another
module's surface.

### AND TWO MORE REDS THIS LANE DID NOT CAUSE, BOTH DATED AND FILED

`DEF-LED-6530` — `test_us_led_016_finance_api.py`'s `tc1` and `tc2` fail on
`assert 'complete' == 'unknown'`: `ITEM_RUNS_ISSUED` now answers **complete**
where the case expects **unknown**. Dated to **`a6dff5057`, 2026-09-24**, the
close role-gate commit, which rewrote 106 lines of `close.py`. Whichever answer
is right, the lane that changed the state machine is the one that knows.

⚠ **BOTH OF TODAY'S "not mine" REDS WERE FILED RATHER THAN MENTIONED**, which
is `OQ-1330`'s lesson taken literally: *"a finding recorded only in the file you
happen to be in is a finding nobody can count, and it goes on spreading while
two lanes both believe it is written down."* Two lanes wrote that one in prose
and neither filed a row, and it spread to 54 citations.

## 2026-09-24 — RULED + BUILT (lane ROW-OPEN, `DEF-CUS-6532`, `v2.351.62`): A RECORD IS VIEWABLE IN EVERY STATE, AND A HOLD RE-POINTED ACROSS A TIER HAS NO EXPIRY TEST

**The Product Owner, verbatim**, looking at the Transfers tab of Ottumwa Water
Works at `v2.351.46` — one row, `TRF-26-0001`, sold to `kyle spade`, state
**Done**, with no row action and no link on the reference:

> *"also this done request - we are unabel to open - view should be available -
> all the time"*

### THE RULING, STATED GENERALLY BECAUSE THAT IS HOW IT WAS MEANT

**A record can be viewed in EVERY state — done, in progress, scheduled, parked,
cancelled, whatever exists. Opening is never gated on state.** What a clerk
cannot *do* with a record is disabled **on the record page**, carrying its own
reason. **Removing the door is never how a product says "there is nothing left
to decide here."**

The two words that decide it are *all the time*, and they are the same two
words that carried B14 rule 44 on the same day. A rule scoped to one state is
read as permission for every other (`DEF-1931`'s shape).

**The worked figure put to the PO:** on Ottumwa the Transfers tab drew **one
row and zero doors**. On the demo tenant, reproduced before anything was
changed, it drew **five rows and zero doors** — no `<a>` and no `<button>` in
any row, in any state. It now draws **five rows and five doors**, and the
`Done` row the PO named opens onto a record page that has been live since
2026-09-20.

### THE DOOR WAS NOT MISSING FOR WANT OF A SCREEN — IT WAS MISSING FOR FOUR DAYS BEHIND AN EXPIRED HOLD

`TransferRecordPage.tsx` is routed at `/transfers/:ref`, tested, and richly
populated. `transfer_record_api.py` serves `GET /transfers/{ref}` and landed
**2026-09-20 in `86a28f23d`**. Both halves were live. Only the door was absent.

**And this file had written the expiry test hard-won law 2's mirror asks for.**
That is why this entry exists rather than a one-line defect row.

* **Hold 1** — *"no transfer record page exists at any address"*. True when
  written. Its test asserted by ADDRESS that nothing matched `/transfers/:id`.
  A sibling mounted `TRANSFER_RECORD_ROUTE` hours later and the case went RED
  by name, *"expected true to be false"*. **The mechanism worked exactly as the
  law describes.**
* **Hold 2 is where it broke, and it broke BECAUSE the hold was re-pointed.**
  The reason became *"`GET /transfers/{ref}` is not mounted"* — a **backend**
  fact — while every assertion the test kept is a **frontend** one: the route
  matches, `transfers/new` is not swallowed, no `/transfers/` href is rendered.
  **No vitest case can observe a Django urlpattern.** The condition expired on
  2026-09-20 and, measured at the tip on 2026-09-24, the case still passed
  GREEN.

### THE JUDGMENT THIS LANE MAKES, BECAUSE NO RULE COVERED IT

**A hold re-pointed ACROSS A TIER BOUNDARY has no expiry test — only something
shaped like one.** Law 2's mirror says *write the test that fires when the hold
expires*; it does not say the test must be able to SEE the new condition, and
here it could not. That is law 7's *incapable of failing* wearing law 2's
mirror as a costume, which is the worst combination available: the guard is
present, documented and trusted.

**So, going forward: when a hold's reason changes, either assert the new
condition where it lives, or release the hold and file the remainder as its own
row.** Re-pointing is the move to be suspicious of. It is cheap, it feels like
diligence, and it silently converts a live guard into a comment.

### A SECOND MISS, AND IT IS THE ONE A READER WOULD HAVE TRUSTED

The hold's reason was written in **three** places in `TransfersTab.tsx` — the
top comment, the `Lifecycle` exceptions block, and the test's own docstring —
and **only one of them was amended when the reason changed on 2026-09-20**. A
lane reading the exceptions block on 2026-09-24 was told *"No transfer record
page exists at any address"*, which had been false for four days. Both are
corrected in this commit. **A hold belongs in ONE place that the test cites.**

### HOW IT IS BUILT, AND WHERE THE DRAWING LOST

Accounts blueprint **p133, read as an IMAGE** (B14 rule 42) draws `↗ Open` on
**both** rows it shows — the `Completed` one and the `In progress` one. **The
drawing agreed with the PO a fortnight before they said it.**

* **B14 rule 44 (ratified today) and rule 15 decide HOW, not whether.** p133
  draws a bordered, labelled `↗ Open`; rule 15 makes a row action an
  **unlabelled icon with a tooltip**. The drawing says what is on the screen;
  our UI standard says how it is built and wins every time. `DisconnectsTab`
  stamped the identical divergence against p142, and following it here keeps
  one grammar across the product instead of two.
* **B14 rule 43** — the door is `RowActions` + `RowActionLink` from the kit,
  not a hand-rolled link. The test asserts `data-variant="ghost"` and
  `data-size="row"`, which are `Button`'s own stated contract, so a hand-rolled
  `<Link>` wearing the same classes still fails.
* **B14 rule 31** — the address is built by the record lane's own
  `transferRecordPath` from the transfer NUMBER. **No uuid reaches the screen
  or the href.** The reader accepts one as a way IN for a tenant whose sales
  predate the numbering series; that is never a way to write one into a link.
* **B14 rule 33** — nothing is explained beside the control. Why the record has
  no verbs is rationale, and rationale is zero words on screen.

### ONE JUDGMENT INSIDE THE RULING, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR A STATE GATE

**A row with no reference is disabled with its reason** (BR-SHL-025), because
the record is addressed by its number and such a row cannot be addressed at
all. That is the **tenant's numbering series**, never the sale's progress, and
it is the same absence the first column already draws. `DisconnectsTab` reached
the same answer independently for the same reason.

### A SHAPE CHANGE MADE ON PURPOSE, WORTH ONE PARAGRAPH

`transfersTableConfig` now takes the **path builder as a required argument**
rather than accepting the door as a caller-supplied cell. `DisconnectsTab`
builds its `↗ Open` at the call site as `cells.actions`, which works and leaves
the door **optional** — a caller can hand in a cell that renders nothing and
every check stays green, which is this very defect with a shorter fuse. Taking
the path builder makes the column, its address and its refusal all the config's
own: **there is no way to construct this table without the door in it.**

### PROPOSED FOR B14, NOT MINTED HERE

**A door to a record is never gated on the record's state.** This lane believes
that is a UI rule rather than a defect — it is general, it is about every list
in the product, and it would have caught this one at review. **It is NOT minted
here on purpose:** B14's count and the pointer to it must move in the same
commit, and that is a coordinator-level act (`CLAUDE.md`'s rule-count line has
been wrong six times for exactly the want of it). ⚠ **And it is already stale
again:** B14's own status table holds **35** rules — 1–21 and **31–44** — while
`CLAUDE.md` still says *thirty-four*, numbered *1–21 and 31–43*. Rule 44 landed
today and the pointer did not move with it. **That is the seventh time.**

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND IN WHICH HARNESS

* **Reproduced first**, in a browser, before a line was changed: five rows,
  zero links, zero buttons (`before-transfers-list.png`).
* **RED before green, twice, in `vitest` — the harness that runs them.**
  Removing the actions column fails all six new cases; gating the door on
  `state === "done"` fails **only the `done` case**, by name, which is the
  assertion doing precisely the job the ruling asks of it.
* **Pressed in a browser at 1440**: every row has a door, every href matches
  `/brazosbend/transfers/TRF-nn-nnnn`, no uuid anywhere, the `Done` row opens
  onto its record, and a keyboard alone can focus the control. No horizontal
  scroll at 1280, 1440 or 1920.
* `10-scripts/def_cus_6532_transfer_door_walkthrough.mjs` re-runs all of it.

### ⚠ A POSTSCRIPT THAT IS THIS LANE'S OWN LAW 11, AND IT IS WORTH THE LINES

**This defect was filed as `DEF-CUS-6529` and is `DEF-CUS-6532`.** The
allocator was right when it ran; between filing and pushing, an integrations
lane pushed `DEF-INT-6529`. **The module segment is PROVENANCE and the NUMBER
is what must be unique**, so a differing prefix does not save you — `6529` was
taken and `DEF-CUS-6529` would have been a duplicate number in a 3,950-row
register, which reads as a register rather than as an error.

**`allocate.py defect --verify 6529` caught it, run in the same breath as the
blob re-derivation, exactly where law 11 says to put it.** Nothing downstream
would have.

**The cost is real and is recorded here rather than hidden:** the first commit
`76bf00efe` had already been pushed and its message cites `6529`. A pushed
message cannot be amended, so the source citations are corrected in the
follow-up commit and this paragraph is the pointer for anyone who greps the log
for `6529` and finds a customers commit under an integrations id.

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane MO-COPY, `DEF-CUS-6550`, `v2.351.66`): THE ENGINE'S BASE-CHARGE REFUSALS ARE CUT AT THE SOURCE, AND THE AUDIT LINE IS DELETED

**THE DECISION THIS ROW EXISTS TO RECORD IS *WHERE*, NOT *WHAT*.** ACC-06 step 3's *The
draft bill* panel prints the engine's refusal **verbatim** — deliberately, `DEF-CUS-6464`,
because *"a paraphrase behind a catalogue key would be a second copy of an engine message,
free to drift from the engine."* That reasoning is sound and it survives this change. It is
also exactly why the LENGTH could not be fixed on the screen.

**TWO OPTIONS WERE PUT AND THE FIRST WAS TAKEN — SHORTEN AT THE SOURCE.**

| Option | What it would have been | Why not / why yes |
|---|---|---|
| **(1) Shorten at the source** ✅ | One sentence, in the two functions that compose it | **TAKEN.** Every renderer of this string is clerk-facing, so there is no audience that needs the long form on screen |
| (2) Keep the long text and serve a short `message_key` beside it | A key in eleven catalogues, the long text kept for logs/support | **DECLINED.** It forks one string into two that can disagree — the exact thing `DEF-CUS-6464` chose verbatim quoting to prevent — and it is only justified when two audiences need two lengths |

**WHO RENDERS THIS SENTENCE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED — THREE PLACES, ALL
CLERK-FACING.** `moveOutTables.DraftBill` (ACC-06 step 3) · `moveShared`'s final-bill panel
(the same flow's other mounting) · and **`billRunResume`'s break table, under the column
*Why***, because `runs.record_break` stores `str(refusal)` in `bill_run_breaks.detail` and
`GET /billing/runs/{id}/breaks` serves it. There is no log-only or support-only reader: the
string's other homes are an API field and a database column that exist to feed those three
screens. **So option (2) had nothing to be for**, and B14 rules 32 and 33 bind the bill-run
screen exactly as they bind the move-out one.

⚠ **THE BRIEF NAMED ONE SENTENCE AND THE SCREEN WAS SHOWING A DIFFERENT ONE, WHICH IS THE
REPRODUCE STEP EARNING ITS PLACE.** The task quoted `gather._base_charge_for`'s 100-word
*"the base charge is stated in more than one place and they disagree"* — which is what the
CODE says. Walked in a browser on `brazosbend` `A-10432`, what a clerk was actually reading
came from `rating.selectors.base_charge_from_charge_code` and was 63 words:

    service electric: base charge code BASE-E prices per connection size and states no
    amount for size None. An unpriced size is REFUSED and never substituted (PO ruling
    2026-08-28) — charging this connection another size's rate is not charging it for
    the connection it has. Price that size on the charge code, or record the
    connection's size. The run continues for every other account.

**Measured on that database the same day: 74 open accounts · 36 price · 30 refuse with this
family · 4 have no unit · 3 wait on a read decision · 1 is already closed.** Fixing only the
sentence in the brief would have left thirty accounts in eight. So the unit of work is **the
BASE-CHARGE FAMILY — all eight refusals** the two functions compose, which is one subject,
one panel and one defect.

**WHAT NOW REACHES A CLERK.** Every one is a FACT then an INSTRUCTION, **two sentences, six
words or fewer each** (B14 rule 33; `G33`'s own reading of the same ruling adds *at most two
sentences*). The live one went **63 words → 10**:

> **This connection's size is not recorded. Record the connection's size.**

**THREE JUDGMENTS, OURS TO MAKE (hard-won law 13), each reported rather than hidden:**

**① THE AUDIT LINE IS DELETED, NOT SHORTENED — AND RULE 33 DOES NOT COMPEL THAT.** *"Closing
an account is recorded in the audit log by the server, with who, when, and everything that
changed."* was 19 words under the footer of **all four steps**. ⚠ **Rule 33 names *an audit
line* among its six-word FACTS**, so trimming it to six would have been lawful and deletion
is a CALL. The call: the kinds are told apart by what a sentence is FOR, and a FACT says
something about THIS record — who closed it, when — where this one says nothing about this
account at all. It is a promise about the system, which is RATIONALE, and a clerk cannot act
on it. The repo's precedent is deletion (`CorrectionRetentionNote`; the transfer wizard's six
sentences, `DEF-CUS-6385`), and the PO's own approved remedy list for this very screen deletes
*What confirming writes* and *What confirming does not do* on the same ground.
**The guarantee is untouched**: hard rule 7 still writes `audit_log` on the close, and
`test_move_out_scenarios.py` is what holds that — never this sentence.
**Its four siblings are LEFT ALONE and filed as `DEF-CUS-6551`** — move-in, New account,
Assets and Meter Reads carry the same line on screens nobody reviewed with the PO today.

**② ONE FACT IS GENUINELY LOST RATHER THAN MOVED, AND IT IS THE COVERED-CLASS LIST.** Where
an account's customer type is covered by no base charge, the old sentence listed the types
that ARE covered — *"so the edit is obvious without opening the charge code first"*, which
`test_def_2381` asserted. The new sentence names the TYPE and the SERVICE (the two facts the
PO's own words name) and sends the clerk to **Charge codes**, where that list is on screen
beside the repair. The test now asserts the list is **absent**, so a lane putting it back
goes red and reads why.

**③ ONE MESSAGE WAS COVERING TWO DIFFERENT PROBLEMS, AND SPLITTING IT IS WHAT MADE SIX WORDS
POSSIBLE.** *"states no amount for size None"* is the branch where a connection's SIZE WAS
NEVER RECORDED, and the same branch also serves a size the code does not price. Two states,
two repairs, in two different modules — which is why the old sentence needed 63 words and
offered both at once, **and why it printed a Python `None` to a clerk.** They are now two
sentences, each saying the one true thing. The branch condition and the answer are unchanged;
only which sentence it carries is decided there.

**ALSO FIXED, AND IT IS A HARD-RULE-2 BREACH THAT NOBODY HAD COUNTED:** the disagreement
message printed the stored `48.000000` and `120.0000`. Money DISPLAYS to two decimals. It now
goes through `core.money.finalize` — the same call `billing/selectors._display_money` makes —
rather than a local `quantize`, because the rounding constants are HUMAN-OWNED.

**AND ONE PARAMETER IS GONE.** `_base_charge_for(…, code_label=)` existed only to print
*"charge code BASE-E-COM says 120.0000"* inside that sentence. With the sentence cut it read
nothing, and a parameter nothing reads is hard-won law 1 in miniature.

**PROVED — and the red proofs were run in the harness that runs the check (law 7), not through
a `__main__`:**
* `tests/test_def_cus_6550_base_refusals_are_short.py`, **16 cases**, builds all eight
  sentences through the functions that compose them, counts words per sentence against six,
  caps sentences at two, and refuses any `BR-`/`DEF-`/`OQ-`/`CR-`/`GT-`/`S<digit>` id **or a
  ruling date**. Shown RED three ways first: the old 63-word sentence restored in
  `rating/selectors.py` (*"unpriced size: 4 sentences, cap is 2"*), `BR-RAT-088` put back into
  `gather.py` (*"charge code vs plan: 3 sentences, cap is 2"*), and `S9` put into a message
  that is still short (*"charge code vs plan: names S9 to a clerk"*). It also asserts the
  counter does NOT fire on `BASE-E-COM` or `W-58` — a pattern that refused the utility's own
  catalogue codes would push the repair out of the sentence.
* `MoveOutWizard.test.tsx` — a new case walks **all four steps** (the line was rendered by the
  wizard SHELL, so a step-3-only test would have passed over three surviving copies) and
  asserts on the WORDS and the class, never the retired key. Shown RED by restoring the line:
  *"expected … not to contain 'audit log'"*. 72 cases green after.
* `10-scripts/def_cus_6550_move_out_copy_walkthrough.mjs` — the browser, at 1440 and 1280,
  which is the only check in this repository that reads rendered output. It **counts words
  rather than matching the new string**, because a walk asserting the sentence verbatim would
  pass on the next 60-word one. It SKIPS loudly with a number when the account priced, rather
  than reporting a silent pass over a scope it could not see.
* `tsc` clean and shown to have COMPLETED, on the pinned local 5.5.4, not a fetched one.

**NOT FIXED HERE, AND COUNTED SO THE ABSENCE IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR AN EMPTY SET:** the other
three refusal families reaching this same panel — *account has no unit* (17 words, names
`BR-CUS-017`), *no usable read and no decision* (~40 words, names `BR-BIL-015`) and *already
non-billable* (~100 words, which prints `apps/billing/stages/resolve_subscription.py` to a
clerk) — and the ~20 sentences of the R1–R7 chain in `resolution.py`, which reach here through
`RuledPathRefused` when R3/R4 are served. They are other modules' stage refusals on money
paths, none of them is what the PO is looking at today, and each needs its own reproduction.

## 2026-09-24 · THE TRANSFER WIZARD'S PAGE HEAD, AND A GROUP HEADING THAT OUTLIVED ITS GROUP

**Lane TRF-TITLES · `DEF-CUS-6542`, `DEF-CUS-6543` · `2.351.67` · maintenance, not build**
(a clerk can open this wizard today, so it is the maintenance process:
`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`).

Two faults the PO is looking at right now, on the screen that landed at `2.351.65`.
**Both were reproduced in a browser before a line was read** — shots in the lane's
scratchpad, `before/` and `after/`, at 1440.

### 1 · THE TITLE IS THE STEP'S, AND THE FIVE ARE THE DRAWING'S

The head was ONE constant key for five screens. It was therefore right on step 1
and wrong on the other four: a clerk on the buyer step read *"Find the account,
and who is selling"* with `Step 2 of 5 · The buyer` printed immediately below it.

**The five titles were read off `05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` (the
281-page edition) AS IMAGES at scale 2 — B14 rule 42 — PDF pages 127–131**, one
screen per page. They are not the rail labels: four of the five differ.

| Step | Rail label (unchanged) | Drawn `<h1>` | Words |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Find the account | **Find the account, and who is selling** | 7 |
| 2 | The buyer | **Who is buying it** | 4 |
| 3 | Date of sale | **The date of sale** | 4 |
| 4 | What they take on | **What the buyer takes on** | 5 |
| 5 | Review & confirm | **Review — one account, one new owner** | 6 |

They live on `TRANSFER_STEPS` beside the rail labels, as `titleKey`/`titleEn` —
`BR-SHL-046`'s *"ONE declared step list"*, which already answers the count, the
rail and the step line. A sixth step needs no edit in the wizard. Five keys in
eleven catalogues through `10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py`; no hardcoded English on
screen.

### ⚠ 1a · ALL FIVE BREAK B14 RULE 33's THREE-WORD HEADING CAP, AND ALL FIVE STAND — FOR THE PO

Rule 33 caps a LABEL or heading at **three words** and forbids it being a
sentence. **Every drawn title above exceeds it** (7 · 4 · 4 · 5 · 6), and step
1's carries a clause.

**They are built as drawn, and the reasoning is the precedent set this morning on
the move-out's four shortfall path names**: put to the PO in plain English,
answered ***"b) Leave as drawn"***. A heading's WORDS are the drawing's to decide
(rule 41). Rule 44, ratified today, gives our UI standard the CONSTRUCTION — the
32px size, the kicker, the step line — and that is where it wins; it does not
hand us the wording. **Inventing five shorter strings for a screen the PO is
reviewing would be this lane writing copy nobody agreed.**

**WHAT TO PUT TO THE PO, in one sentence with the figure:** *the five headings on
the transfer wizard are the ones you drew, and they run from four to seven words
where our own rule says three — leave them as drawn, as you did with the
move-out's shortfall names, or shall we shorten them?* Until they answer, the
drawing stands.

⚠ **ANSWERED THE SAME DAY — THEY RULED (b), SHORTEN.** PO, verbatim: ***"4 · The
five transfer headings - b  Shorten all five to the cap"***. The five are now
*Account & seller* · *The buyer* · *The date* · *The money* · *Review & confirm*,
built by lane TRF-CAP at `2.351.69`. **Everything above stands as the record of
what was put to them and why the drawing was held meanwhile**; only the last
sentence is overtaken. The entry that carries the ruling, the five before-and-
after strings and why the move-out's *"Leave as drawn"* is untouched by it is
**"RULED: THE FIVE TRANSFER HEADINGS ARE SHORTENED TO THE CAP — AND THE
MOVE-OUT'S FOUR ARE NOT"**, at the foot of this log.

### 2 · THE ROLLUP PARAGRAPH IS DELETED, NOT SHORTENED

The head also carried *"5 steps · the account changes hands, nothing else
moves."* on every step. **p127–p131 draw exactly three lines above the rail —
kicker, 32px title, `Step N of 5 · <rail label>` — and no paragraph**, so the
sentence was ours rather than the agreement's.

**This is not this lane's judgment call; it is the PO's own ruling of this
morning, applied one wizard over.** `DEF-CUS-6480` is the identical sentence on
the move-out — PO, verbatim, *"too much text reduce it"* — deleted rather than
trimmed, with `customers.moveOut.subSteps` retired from all eleven catalogues.
The transfer carried the same shape and the fix did not travel with it.

It also broke two rules it was standing next to: its COUNT is a third statement
of what the line below and the rail already say (**rule 32** — a row never
repeats what its own control offers), and *"nothing else moves"* is RATIONALE,
which **rule 33** puts at zero words on screen and says is REMOVED rather than
shortened.

⚠ **NOTHING FACTUAL IS LOST, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON IT COULD GO.** *What this
sale will not touch* is drawn as a panel of its own on step 1 (p127) and is
rendered there in full — issued bills, payments taken, journal entries, the
account number, the unit and meters, the service agreements. A clerk who wants
the assurance gets it itemised, on the step where it belongs, instead of nine
words repeated over four screens where it answers nothing they are asking.
`customers.transfer.subSteps` is retired from the eleven catalogues in the same
commit. **Its consumers were grepped first** (hard rule 8's lesson: an absence is
invisible to every check this repo has) — there were none but the head itself and
one test assertion, which now asserts the absence.

### 3 · A GROUP HEADING BELONGS TO ITS GROUP — THE CHOICE, AND WHY

`ApplicantCaptureFields` drew *"One identifier"* and *"Give one ID or a phone."*
on `headings === true && identity !== false`, asking nothing about whether any
field followed. An unstated customer kind correctly yields NO identifier field
(`BR-CUS-1022`), so a clerk opening step 2 read a label and an instruction over
**nothing at all**.

**Two options were on the table. The one taken: the heading and its instruction
are drawn from the same answer that decides whether the group has any members** —
`asked.size === 0` now gates both.

**The one rejected: an empty-state line such as *"State the kind first."*** It is
inside rule 33's six-word instruction cap, so the cap is not what rules it out.
**Every host draws the Person/Company control immediately above this group**, so
the sentence would tell a clerk what the adjacent control already offers — rule
32 — on a screen the PO has four times called *"too much content"*. A group
heading belongs to its group; when the group has no members there is nothing to
head.

⚠ **THE FAULT WAS A STATE NOBODY ARRIVED IN, NOT A STATE NOBODY TESTED.** Every
existing case for this block states a kind first — that is what the cases are
about — and until `DEF-CUS-6549` a clerk reached these fields only after pressing
a button. Opening step 2 straight onto the form is what put it first on screen.

### ⚠ 3a · THE BLAST RADIUS IS ONE SCREEN, NOT THREE — AND THE DEFECT ROW SAYS THREE

`DEF-CUS-6543`'s own row reads *"it affects every host that passes headings: the
transfer's step 2, the move-in request capture and new connect"*. **Walked, both
ways, before the change: `ApplicantCaptureFields` has exactly ONE importer.**

* **Move-in capture** (`ServiceRequestCapturePage.tsx`) keeps its own
  `identityFieldsFor`, which returns the person's three for any kind that is not
  `business` — **it can never return an empty list** — and it draws no group
  heading at all.
* **New connect** (`NewConnectOwnerStep.tsx`) draws its identifier fields inline,
  with no heading over them.

So the fix is right on all three screens because two of them never had the fault.
**That is recorded rather than assumed**: the new test file pins all three
findings, including a guard that the identifier heading is rendered from exactly
ONE file — a second host writing its own copy is how rule 43 says two screens
drift, and it would reopen this defect somewhere nothing mentions it.

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND IN WHICH HARNESS

* **Reproduced first, in a browser**, on the unfixed bundle: the walkthrough's
  own checks were **7 red of 18**, naming each wrong title and both stray lines.
  **18 of 18 green** after. `10-scripts/def_cus_6542_6543_transfer_head_walkthrough.mjs`
  re-runs all of it, including a `getComputedStyle` reading of the title at
  **32px** against the built stylesheet (B14 rule 40 — unchanged by this work).
* **RED before green, twice, in `vitest` — the harness that runs them.** Pinning
  step 2's `titleKey` to step 1's fails `step 2's head is its own title (p128)`
  BY NAME, quoting both strings, and independently fails
  `the five heads are five different strings` with *expected 4 to be 5*.
  Reverting the `asked.size === 0` guard fails
  `no kind stated: no heading, no instruction, and no boxes`.
* **`npx tsc` was proved CAPABLE OF FAILING before it was trusted** — a deliberate
  type error was planted, seen to fail at `applicantCapture.tsx(374,7)`, and
  removed. The real run then COMPLETED with zero errors, through the pinned local
  `typescript@5.5.4`, never a fetched one.

### ⚠ A REGRESSION THAT IS THE DRAWING'S OWN DOING, AND WORTH THE PARAGRAPH

Giving the head its own title broke three cases in
`TransferWizardPress.dom.test.tsx` — the ones guarding the crash the PO reported
on step 4. **p130 puts the words *"What the buyer takes on"* on the screen
TWICE**: the page title and the left column's section heading. So
`getByText(...)` began matching two nodes and threw.

**Resolving it the lazy way would have gutted the case.** Those three assertions
mean *the step is still the step*, and their own comment says why: *"a boundary
replaces the CONTENT and leaves the frame, so the frame being there proves
nothing."* **The `<h1>` is the frame.** A selector that quietly settled on it
would have gone on passing over the exact crash it exists to catch — law 7's
*looking at the wrong thing*, one heading level up. They now address the section
heading by role and level, which is what they always meant and could not say
while only one node carried the words.

### FILED, NOT FIXED

**`DEF-CUS-6552` — the move-out wizard has the identical fault.**
`MoveOutWizard.tsx:1259` renders *"Close an account and free the unit."* on every
step, while the blueprint titles each one (read as images at p113: step 2 is
*Date & final reads*, step 3 is *Final bill & deposit*). **Deliberately not fixed
here:** this lane's brief is the transfer, and the move-out is mid-redesign —
`DEF-CUS-6537` cut it from six steps to four this morning, so the drawn titles
for the two MERGED steps must be re-read against the new shape before any are
written. The mechanism is already shared and waiting: `FlowStepDef` now carries
optional `titleKey`/`titleEn`, so the move-out needs its four drawn titles and one
line in its head.

### THE REDS THIS LANE DID NOT CAUSE, DATED

`vitest run src/features/customers/` reports **27 failures across 10 files**, and
**every one of them is the tip's.** Dated conclusively rather than by assertion:
the identical command was run in a second worktree pinned to
`1b10b714759f1b33df3fe78d0dce2e348a6b339e`, the base this lane started from, and
it produced **the same 27** — the set difference of the two failure-name lists is
**empty in both directions**. This lane's work takes the passing count from
**1,757 to 1,772** and moves the failing count **not at all**.

Two of the 27 have a named cause from today: `e45a8e034` cut the move-out from
SIX steps to FOUR under `DEF-CUS-6537`, and the two `BR-SHL-046` cases asserting
six (`stepOf …counts to 6, not 5` and `the rail still addresses SIX steps`) were
not moved with it.

`run_gates.py` (133 gates) reports **54 FAIL on this tree and the SAME 54 on the
tip**, the same set. **No gate's finding COUNT was raised** — checked line by
line, not by verdict. Two worth naming: **G15 reports 546 new-untranslated values
on BOTH trees**, so five keys across eleven languages added none — the
translations are translations; and **G1 would have risen by one** for the new test
file, which now carries the Lifecycle trailer it was missing, putting it back at
the tip's 1,669.

### ⚠ A POSTSCRIPT ON LAW 11, BECAUSE THIS PUSH COLLIDED TWICE IN ONE MINUTE

`push_paths.sh` **REFUSED the first attempt**, naming fifteen paths that had
moved between this lane's base and the live tip — the three version literals,
all eleven catalogues and `CHANGELOG.md`. It was right to: a sibling had landed
`2b5c1b4c6` in the meantime, and pushing tip-plus-my-hunks from a stale read of
eleven catalogues is the revert-by-subtraction every other check in law 11 passes
over.

**Re-deriving from the newly pinned tip surfaced TWO collisions, and
`--verify` had said both were free only minutes earlier:**

* **the version.** This lane wrote `2.351.66`; the sibling published `2.351.66`.
  Re-bumped to **`2.351.67`**.
* **the defect id.** This lane filed `DEF-CUS-6550`; the sibling's commit message
  closes `DEF-CUS-6550` and `DEF-CUS-6551`. Re-filed as **`DEF-CUS-6552`**.

**Neither was an arithmetic error and neither was caught by a grep.** The
allocator asks the remote, and the remote did not yet hold either number when it
was asked — which is exactly what `allocate.py`'s own docstring says it cannot
fix: *"it CANNOT reserve… it removes the STALE read, which is the common case,
and catches the rare one at the only moment the answer can be final."* **That
moment is push time**, and the only reason both were caught is that the
re-verification was run there rather than at allocation time. The register
arithmetic after re-derivation reads `3 insertions, 2 deletions` — one appended
row and two rewritten status lines — which is what it should be and is the check
read as arithmetic rather than glanced at.

## 2026-09-24 · RULED: THE FIVE TRANSFER HEADINGS ARE SHORTENED TO THE CAP — AND THE MOVE-OUT'S FOUR ARE NOT

**Lane TRF-CAP · `2.351.69` · maintenance, not build** (a clerk can open this wizard
today, so it is `12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`). It answers the
question the entry *"THE TRANSFER WIZARD'S PAGE HEAD, AND A GROUP HEADING THAT
OUTLIVED ITS GROUP"* left open under its heading **1a**, earlier the same day.

**THE QUESTION, AS IT WAS PUT:** *the five headings on the transfer wizard are the
ones you drew, and they run from four to seven words where our own rule says three —
leave them as drawn, as you did with the move-out's shortfall names, or shall we
shorten them?*

**THE PO'S ANSWER, VERBATIM:**

> **"4 · The five transfer headings - b  Shorten all five to the cap"**

### THE FIVE, BEFORE AND AFTER

| step | as drawn (p127–p131) | words | ruled | words | = its rail label? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Find the account, and who is selling | 7 | **Account & seller** | 3 | no — rail is *Find the account* |
| 2 | Who is buying it | 4 | **The buyer** | 2 | **yes** |
| 3 | The date of sale | 4 | **The date** | 2 | no — rail is *Date of sale* |
| 4 | What the buyer takes on | 5 | **The money** | 2 | no — rail is *What they take on* |
| 5 | Review — one account, one new owner | 6 | **Review & confirm** | 3 | **yes** |

Words are whitespace-separated tokens, so `&` counts as one — the stricter reading,
which is why *Account & seller* and *Review & confirm* are AT the cap rather than
under it. On the same count step 5's drawn title is **seven**, not the six recorded
this morning: the em dash is a token of its own. The figure that was put to the PO
(*"four to seven words"*) is right either way.

### ⚠ WHERE THE SHORT WORDS COME FROM, BECAUSE THEY ARE MOSTLY NOT OURS

**Three of the five are the blueprint's own short names for the same content.** p131
— the review screen — heads its sections **The buyer**, **The date** and **The
money**, each with a `↖ Step N` flag back to the step it summarises. So steps 2, 3
and 4 are renamed in the drawing's own vocabulary rather than in ours, which is as
close to rule 41 as a ruling to shorten can get. Step 5 takes the drawn step strip's
own name for step 5 (*Review & confirm*). **Step 1 is the only one that is a
construction**, and it keeps both halves the drawn title made a point of — the
account, and who is selling — in three words.

**Nothing factual is lost.** Every long title's full wording is still on its own
screen, as the section heading directly beneath the head: *The account being sold* ·
*Who is buying it* · *The date of sale* · *What the buyer takes on* · *One account,
one new owner*. The head is now a NAME and the section says what the step does,
which is the split rule 33 is describing.

### ⚠ TWO OF THE FIVE NOW EQUAL THEIR RAIL LABEL, AND THAT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN DISGUISED

*The buyer* and *Review & confirm* are the shortest true name for their step and the
rail already had it. **Forcing a difference would be inventing a second name for one
thing**, so they are left equal and it is written down here. Steps 1, 3 and 4 still
differ, which is why `titleKey` remains a field of its own on `FlowStepDef` and is
NOT derivable from `labelKey` — a test now pins the figure at exactly two, so the day
it reaches five somebody is told the field can go.

The visible cost is on step 5, where the head and the line under it both read *Review
& confirm*. It was looked at in a browser before it was accepted: the line under the
head is small grey progress text and the repetition reads as quiet rather than as
noise. **Screenshots of all five steps, before and after, at 1440, are in the lane's
scratchpad** — the PO chose the shorter set without seeing it, so the shots are how
they check we read them right.

### ⚠ THIS RULING AND THE MOVE-OUT'S SIT SIDE BY SIDE. NEITHER OVERTURNS THE OTHER

**This morning**, on the move-out's four shortfall path names — *Pursue it* · *Put it
on a payment plan* · *Write it off* · *Tie it back to the master account*, three of
which breach the same cap — the PO was shown the shortened set and ruled ***"b) Leave
as drawn"***. **This afternoon**, on the transfer's five page heads, the same question
got ***"Shorten all five to the cap"***.

**Both are live. Neither is a general rule.** A lane running a copy audit over ACC-06
step 4 will find four labels over the cap and must NOT shorten them; a lane looking at
TRF-02 will find five headings that differ from the drawing and must NOT restore them.

**Why they differ is worth writing down, because guessing it wrong is what a future
lane will do.** The four move-out strings are the NAMES OF FOUR CHOICES a clerk picks
between — *Pursue it* and *Write it off* are different acts with different money
consequences, and a name that is shortened until the acts read alike costs a wrong
decision on somebody's debt. The five transfer strings are the NAME OF THE SCREEN YOU
ARE STANDING ON, and the step line, the rail and the section heading underneath each
say it again. **Rule 33's cap bites hardest where the words are most redundant and
least where they carry a decision** — which is the reading that makes both answers
consistent, and it is OURS rather than the PO's: they ruled two instances, not a
principle. It is recorded as our reasoning so that the next lane reopens the question
if it does not hold, rather than applying one ruling to the other screen.

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND IN WHICH HARNESS

* **Reproduced first, in a browser, at 1440**, on a bundle built from the live tip
  (`c548f4921`): `10-scripts/def_cus_6542_6543_transfer_head_walkthrough.mjs`
  reported **16 passed · 12 failed**, naming every long head and its word count.
  **28 of 28 green** on this lane's bundle. The same run measures the title at
  **32px** through `getComputedStyle` against the BUILT stylesheet (B14 rule 40,
  unchanged by this work).
* **RED BEFORE GREEN IN `vitest`, THE HARNESS THAT RUNS IT** (hard-won law 7).
  Restoring step 1's drawn title in `en.json` — the catalogue, because a catalogue
  entry BEATS a code `defaultValue`, so a check over the declared constant would have
  gone green on a screen printing seven words — fails four cases by name:
  `step 1's head is within rule 33's heading cap (p127)` with *"step 1 head "Find the
  account, and who is selling" is 7 words: expected 7 to be less than or equal to 3"*,
  `no head is a sentence — rule 33's other half` on the comma,
  `what is declared is what renders…`, and the pre-existing
  `step 1's head is its own title (p127)`. `en.json` was restored byte-identically
  (`cmp` clean) afterwards.
* **Rule 33 has TWO halves for a label and both are checked** — ≤ 3 words AND not a
  sentence. A cap alone passes *"Sold. Now who?"*: three words, two sentences.
* **`npx tsc` was proved CAPABLE OF FAILING before it was trusted.** A deliberate type
  error was planted in `transferDisconnectShared.tsx`, the pinned local
  `typescript@5.5.4` was seen to fail at `(862,7) TS2322` and to print
  `tsc COMPLETED exit=2`; the probe was removed and the real run **COMPLETED** with
  `exit=0`.
* `TransferWizardHead.dom.test.tsx` **15 → 24 cases**, all green. The four other
  transfer suites — `TransferWizard`, `TransferWizardPress`, `TransferBuyerCapture`,
  `TransfersTab`, `TransferRecordPage` — **100 passed, 0 failed**, so the shortened
  set did not collapse two steps onto one string or break the press cases that guard
  the step-4 crash.

### FILED, NOT FIXED

* **`DEF-CUS-6556` — the same screen's OTHER over-cap strings.** Shortening the five
  heads put their neighbours on screen beside them: the rail reads *What they take on*
  (4 words) and the five section headings run 4 · 4 · 4 · 5 · 5. Every one is a LABEL
  under rule 33 and every one is over the cap. **The PO ruled on the five page-head
  titles and on nothing else**, and the move-out precedent proves the answer cannot be
  assumed, so they are filed to be put to the PO as one table rather than shortened on
  this lane's reading.
* **`DEF-GOV-6557` — B14 rule 33's row records neither ruling.** The move-out's
  supersession lives in this log and in the move-out's code comments and NOWHERE in
  B14, so rule 33 reads as an unqualified cap and the next copy audit will "fix" four
  labels the PO ruled. A narrow supersession of a B14 rule is a fan-out — the log, the
  rule's own row, and the comment beside the strings — the same discipline closing an
  open question already has.

**No open question is closed by this ruling, because none was minted:** heading 1a of
this morning's entry put the question in the decision log and in the code comment
beside the strings, and the register was never given a row. That is the gap hard-won
law 10 names — a thing recorded only where you happen to be standing is a thing
nobody can count — and it is why this entry names the question it answers in full
rather than by id.

The five short strings, the reasoning that reconciles this ruling with the move-out's, and the choice not to force a difference where a title equals its rail label are AI judgment under hard-won law 13, recorded here rather than re-asked | `DEF-CUS-6542` · `DEF-CUS-6556` · `DEF-GOV-6557` · B14 rule 33 · `BR-SHL-046` · `07-frontend/src/features/customers/transferDisconnectShared.tsx` · `moveShared.tsx` · `TransferWizardHead.dom.test.tsx` · `10-scripts/def_cus_6542_6543_transfer_head_walkthrough.mjs` · the eleven catalogues via `10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py` · `2.351.69` |


## 2026-09-24 · BUILT (lane FIN-P4, `P4.1` · `P4.2` · `P4.7` · `P4.10` · `P4.13`, `v2.351.71`): FINANCE WRITES FILES, AND A SENT ONE CANNOT MOVE

**The phase's own sentence for why this matters, from the Finance blueprint p017:**
*"Hand the accountant an actual file — today the handover is recorded and nothing
is written or emailed."*

### What was judged, where the rules ran out

**1 · A hand-over's file is RE-DERIVED, never stored.** `J19` step 7 asks that
*"the export file re-generated from the batch is identical (hash-stable)"*. The
obvious build writes the file at send time and keeps it; that satisfies the rule
only as long as the copy and the payload stay in step, and nothing re-checks
that. The build instead makes the file a **pure function of the frozen payload**,
so hash-stability holds **by construction** rather than by a copy nobody
re-reads. It also settles `US-LED-006` TC-4 for free: `4100`'s QBO ref moving
from 79 to 101 after July's batch cannot reach July's file, because the ref in
the file is the one written into the payload at send (`BR-TEN-020`). A renderer
that went back to the chart would break CLAUDE.md hard rule 4 **through a report
rather than through an UPDATE**, which no gate in this repo would see.
*Proved on real PostgreSQL* — `test_p4_7__a_later_ref_edit_does_not_move_a_sent_file`,
7 passed under `--ds=config.settings.pgtest`.

**2 · The three vendor import sheets carry the JOURNAL rows only; the plain CSV
carries everything.** A stored payload holds two kinds of row — the journal
summary and `BR-LED-039`'s cost-of-service extract — and `US-LED-021` TC-7 is
explicit that the cost total is **never added** to the debits and credits. An
accounting import file is by definition a set of lines that must foot, so
putting an unbalanced register extract into one either fails the import or, far
worse, imports and double-books payables the tenant's own AP already holds.
**The omission is never silent:** `export_files.omitted_cost_rows()` reports the
count, and it rides on the download as `X-Cost-Rows-Omitted`. *"Seven rows"* and
*"seven of nine rows"* must not read the same — that is `DEF-2345`'s shape, a
true statement about part of the data presented as a statement about all of it.

**3 · `remittance`'s file names NO basis, and that is `BR-REP-001` honoured
rather than skipped.** Every other Finance export is `posting`. `BR-LED-013`
lets each authority remit on its own basis — `LE-3` has State on collected and
County on billed **in the same month** — so a file stamped with either label
would be false about half its own contents. The `{basis}` segment reads
`per-authority` and every row carries its own `remitting_basis` column.

**4 · A report that needs a subject REFUSES rather than widening.**
`account_ledger` without `account_id`, `customer_statement` without
`customer_id`: both raise `VAL-001` naming the field. `BR-SHL-011`'s *"fall
back, never 4xx"* governs a SORT OR FILTER term the list does not honour; it is
not a licence to change the SUBJECT of a report. The alternative is a file
called *one account's ledger* holding every customer's money.

**5 · IS-9's second half is implemented and the kernel's docstring is amended
in place.** `apps/tenancy/exports.py` had said since 2026-08-10 that *"current
filters AND VISIBLE COLUMNS"* was half built. **RULED, PO 2026-09-24:** *"all
selected columns will go in downloaded file"*. `columns_for` resolves the ticked
set ONCE and it is used for the header **and** for the cells, so a reordered
header can never arrive over unreordered values — a file where every column is
mislabelled and every value is real. `BR-SHL-013` is untouched: the server
stores no preference, the client now sends one.

### What is NOT decided and is with the PO

`OQ-LED-12635` — **the QuickBooks Online and Xero column layouts have never been
round-tripped against the real products.** Written from each vendor's published
import template, plausible, and untried. It is a fact only a customer holds, so
it is a question rather than a judgment, and it blocks nothing: the CSV and IIF
targets are unaffected and any of the four opens in a spreadsheet.

`DEF-LED-6608` — **`qbo` names two unrelated things in two registries**, an OFX
bank statement coming in and an accounting hand-over going out. Found by reading
`10-scripts/`'s and `codecs.py`'s existing registry before writing a new one,
which is the habit CLAUDE.md law 11's last clause prescribes and is also what
stopped a bank-statement encoder being pointed at an accountant.

| Ruled by | Surfaces |
|---|---|
| **PO, 2026-09-24**, verbatim *"all selected columns will go in downloaded file"* (`P4.13`). Items 1–4 above are AI judgment under hard-won law 13, recorded here rather than re-asked | `05-prototype/07 Finance Blueprint.pdf` p017 · p069 · p070 · `apps/tenancy/exports.py` · `apps/tenancy/services.py` · `apps/tenancy/api.py` · `apps/ledger/finance_exports.py` · `apps/ledger/export_files.py` · `apps/ledger/apps.py` · `apps/ledger/finance_api.py` · `BR-LED-004/013/014/017/020/039` · `BR-TEN-020/031` · `BR-SHL-011/013/016` · `BR-REP-001/018` · `US-LED-006` TC-4 · `US-LED-021` TC-7 · `J19` step 7 · `OQ-LED-12635` · `DEF-LED-6608` · `DEF-SHL-6554` · `DEF-SHL-6555` · the eleven catalogues via `10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py` · `2.351.68` · `2.351.71` |

## 2026-09-24 — BUILT (lane FIN-P3, Finance blueprint `P3.1`–`P3.9`, `v2.351.72`): FOUR SCREENS OVER BACKENDS THAT WERE FINISHED, TESTED AND UNREACHABLE

Finance blueprint phase 3, *The missing doors*. Every task in it is hard-won
law 2's MIRROR as a work package: a live, tested capability behind a door
nobody built. **~145 KB of tested Python across four accrual engines, eight
routes, had zero front-end callers.** `POST /finance/periods/reopen` and its
typed wrapper had both existed since 2026-08-16 and no component called either.
`GET /refunds/{id}` and three reads beside it were built and called by nobody,
which is why the approve modal apologised in the product's own words: *"The
account is not shown here. No account served."*

### THE PHASE'S OWN ARITHMETIC, BECAUSE IT UNDERCOUNTS ITSELF

p016's header reads **Task mix … = 9** and the table holds **TWELVE** rows,
`P3.1`–`P3.12`. The header is right for `P3.1`–`P3.9` and was never moved when
`P3.10`–`P3.12` were appended. **Every phase in that document undercounts itself
the same way.** Both numbers are in this lane's report; the rows are what was
worked from.

### THE JUDGMENTS NO RULING MADE, EACH WITH ITS FIGURE

**1 · A ROW IS A LINE AND AN ACT IS AN ENGINE (`P3.1`).** p027 note 5 splits
unbilled revenue by service — *"Four engines, with unbilled revenue split by
service"* — and the drawing puts `👁 ✓ …` on all five lines. **A post is per
ENGINE**: `accrue_unbilled_revenue` writes ONE entry covering every service in
the window, which p028's WRITE SURFACES row states (*"Post per engine — preview
and post, four times"*). On the seeded tenant that is **Electric $10,367.30 and
Water $4,711.37 in one $15,078.67 entry**, so a `✓` on the Water line that also
posted Electric would be a control lying about what it does, on a money path.

**Ruled here:** the acts render **once per engine, on its first line**; a
continuation service line carries none. The confirm dialog names the engine and
its whole total. This is the one place the screen differs from the drawing and
it is deliberate.

**2 · `entry_type` AND `reverses_on` ARE SERVED, NOT DECIDED IN A BROWSER.**
`accruals_api._posting_shape` puts both on every one of the four previews.
A browser holding its own table of *which engine reverses* is p019's own *"a
literal outlives its list"*, one step worse because this literal is a claim
about money: `depreciation.py`'s own docstring measures the error at **$40,000
on one truck**. The date comes from `manual_je.accrual_reversal_due_on`, which
asks `close.period_window` — never `end + 1 day`, because a tenant closing
QUARTERLY accrues into a quarter (BR-TEN-022).

**3 · NO `RFD-` NUMBER IS INVENTED (`P3.3`).** The drawing's head reads *"REFUND
RFD-2609-0004 · CHEQUE"*. **`refunds` has no number series in this product** —
grep `RFD` across `06-backend` and nothing answers — so that string is an
ILLUSTRATION (B14 rule 37). The identity shown is the CHEQUE NUMBER, with a
stated absence where there is none, and **there is no `?? row.id` fallback**
(`DEF-2580` printed a raw uuid to a finance user with exactly that shape).

**4 · NO *Other accounts in arrear* ROW, AND THAT IS A REPORTED GAP RATHER THAN
AN OMISSION.** The drawing has the row. `customers.selectors.arrears_on_other_
accounts` is resolved BY NAME inside `refunds.offset_before_refund` and **has no
endpoint**, so nothing in this product answers the question about a refund that
already exists. Drawing it as *None* would be a claim about another account's
balance that nothing here checked. The screen says nothing.

**5 · THE SERVICE HALF OF THE GL MAP IS EDITABLE; THE ROLE HALF STAYS ONE
ACCOUNT AT A TIME (`P3.4`).** `save_gl_mappings` REFUSES a cleared designation
by name — *"a bulk page must not be able to unmap the books in one press"* — and
re-pointing a role is already reachable through the map's own account link. The
service half is the half that had no screen at all.

**6 · THE *Settings → Services* SENTENCE IS DELETED, NOT REWORDED.** It read
*"Set on Settings → Services. It is kept with the service itself, so a change
here would be a second place to look."* The first clause stopped being true in
this commit; the second is RATIONALE, which B14 rule 33 puts at **zero words on
screen**. Retired from all eleven catalogues.

**7 · TWO DRAWN SENTENCES ARE REWRITTEN BY B14 RULE 44.** 6·1b's consequence is
drawn as *"Reopening does not recall that handover — post the difference by
hand"* (thirteen words, where rule 33 allows six per sentence); it reads
**"Handed over {date}. That handover stands. Post the difference."** And the
drawn title *"Reopen September 2026?"* became **"Reopen this period?"** with the
window in the kicker — this product's period is a WINDOW and not a month name,
so interpolating it produced *"Reopen 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31?"*, eight tokens
where a heading allows three. **The FACT is the drawing's in both cases and the
construction is ours**, which is rule 44 as ratified today.

### `P3.8` IS AN ABSENCE WITH AN ANSWER BEHIND IT, AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE

The PO ruled on 2026-09-24: **closing a month is `system_admin` + `billing_clerk`;
REOPENING is `system_admin` ONLY, reason required, audited.** `BR-LED-006` is
amended and `apps/ledger/close.reopen_period` already gates it. So `P3.8` stays
*Settings: none* — **not a gap, a settled question.** The screen offers or
withholds the control (BR-SHL-025) and the service is the boundary either way; a
null role OFFERS it, because `/me/permissions` not having answered is not a
refusal.

### `P3.9` — THE SEAM IS DECLARED

Refund detail is **payments' record at a `/finance` address**. Every read and
the one write are `apps/payments/refunds_api.py`'s, through the typed client.
**No endpoint, table or rule is added in payments.** The refunds LIST stays at
`/payments/refunds` where `P4.10` moved it on 2026-09-23; what a Finance
approver opens is the one refund they are about to agree to.

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND HOW

**`P3.6` on real PostgreSQL 16, watched** —
`10-scripts/fin_p3_6_accrual_reversal_pg_proof.py`, against a private clone, all
rolled back. The accrual posts `type='accrual'` dated the period end and
balances **15078.670000 = 15078.670000**; a replay answers `created: false` with
the same id; the day-1 mirror lands **2026-10-01** and the pair is linked both
ways (`auto_reverse_entry` forward, `reversal_of` back); **the unbilled-AR
account nets 0.000000 across the pair**, which is LE-4's figure; a second sweep
leaves exactly one mirror; and depreciation posts `type='standard'` and the
sweep does not touch it.

⚠ **TWO OF THIS LANE'S OWN CHECKS COULD NOT FAIL, AND BOTH WERE FOUND BY ASKING
WHAT WOULD MAKE THEM PASS WRONGLY.** §7 first read `all(row.created is False for
row in repeated)` over a list that is EMPTY on the second sweep — vacuously true
whatever the engine did. It counts mirrors in the database now. And §8 asserted
`uq_journal_entries_reversal` by name and went RED, correctly: **a raw INSERT
into `journal_entries` never reaches that index, because a database TRIGGER
refuses any write that did not come through `apps/ledger/posting.py`** — hard
rule 5, enforced in the database rather than by convention. The check was
rewritten to say what is true rather than softened to pass, and the index's
existence is now asked of `pg_indexes` instead of inferred from an error.

**`P3.5` — every door asserted by ADDRESS and by the SCREEN it opens**, in
`financeP3Doors.dom.test.tsx` (10 cases) and again in a real browser. Both
harnesses mount under the real `/:tenant/…` pattern.

**`P3.7`** — `J19-month-end-close.md` gains step 8: reopen, and the trial balance
must be **byte-identical** either side. The seven steps and the signed
**598.69 / 553.69** figures are untouched.

**THE BROWSER, AT 1440 AND 1280** —
`10-scripts/fin_p3_screens_walkthrough.mjs`, on the deployed join
(`server.mjs`), against a seeded clone. Every check passes and every screen was
opened and looked at beside the page it was built from.

### ⚠ THREE FAULTS FOUND BY LOOKING, AND NOTHING ELSE COULD HAVE FOUND THEM

* **`DEF-LED-6609`** — 2·5d printed *"163 Willow Bend Dr · Unit 1 · Unit 1"*.
  `customers.selectors._premise_cell` ALREADY composes `premise` as
  `"<address> · <label>"`; appending `unit_label` beside it duplicates. Fixed.
* **`DEF-LED-6614`** — 6·1's close checklist prints the raw code
  `unpaid_cost_accrual` to a clerk. Not this lane's screen; filed.
* **`DEF-LED-6612` / `DEF-LED-6613`** — four GL roles render their raw code, and
  the unsigned-account note is glued to the account name with no separator —
  `DEF-LED-6170`'s exact complaint, one panel over. Filed, not fixed here.

And **two of this lane's own checks were filed as defects** rather than quietly
corrected: `DEF-GOV-6610` (the walk waited on a button that renders beside the
table, so it reported six columns MISSING over a correct screen) and
`DEF-GOV-6611` (the 1280 overflow check read `documentElement`, which in this
shell can never overflow — a green that means nothing).

### AN ID COLLISION, CAUGHT WHERE THE LAW SAYS IT WILL BE

`DEF-LED-6608` was taken by this lane **and** by a sibling, minutes apart. Both
arithmetics were right; the remote held neither row when either allocator asked.
It surfaced on the rebase, as a duplicate in the register, and was renumbered to
**`DEF-LED-6614`** with every one of this lane's six ids re-verified against the
remote in the same breath as the push.
