## 2026-09-24 — HANDED BACK (lane FIN-P3): `P3.10`, `P3.11` AND `P3.12` ARE PAYMENTS' CODE, MEASURED SO THE NEXT LANE DOES NOT RE-MEASURE

The Finance blueprint's phase 3 table holds twelve rows and three of them touch
**another module's shipped screens**. p083's own ruling on the eleven
re-attributed tasks: *"They stay in the plan, but they are raised, scheduled and
reviewed with the module that owns them."* p083 also names the reason —
*"**This is the single largest duplication risk in the plan**: a Finance lane
that 'builds' one of them rebuilds something that already exists and is already
tested, in a module it does not own."*

**So they are handed back rather than half-built.** What follows is the
measurement, so the Payments lane starts from a fact rather than from a task
sentence.

### `P3.11` NEEDS NO BACKEND CHANGE AT ALL — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED

*"Say when a locked batch no longer sums. A reversal inside a locked batch is
lawful, so the frozen `recorded_total` can drift from the live payments."*

`GET /deposit-batches/{id}` **already serves both sides of that comparison**:
`DepositBatchDetail.batch.recorded_total` is the frozen figure and
`DepositBatchDetail.members[]` each carry `amount`, `currency` and `status`.
The drift is Σ(members) − `recorded_total`, computed over data the screen is
already holding.

⚠ **THE SUM MUST BE EXACT, NOT `Number()`.** `paymentsShared.sumDecimalStrings`
already adds decimal strings on the `NUMERIC(18,6)` grid with `BigInt` and is
the function to use; a `parseFloat` here is the shape of every money defect this
repository has logged. **Show the difference; change no rule** — p016 says so in
terms, and `_refuse_if_batch_locked` stays exactly as it is.

### `P3.10` — TWO OF THE THREE ROW ACTIONS ALREADY HAVE ENDPOINTS

*"Row actions on the batch lines. Three `PlainTable`s with no row control
anywhere, on the screen where a wrong cheque number is found."*

`DepositBatchPage.tsx` renders three `PlainTable`s (lines 163, 250, 343) and not
one `RowActions` among them. The three acts p016 names are **open the payment**,
**correct the reference** and **carry a reverse**; `POST /payments/{id}/correct-
reference` is served and gated `AdminOrClerk` (hard rule 4's three-column
narrowing, PO 2026-09-02), and the payment detail is routed. Each member row
already carries `payment_id`, `payment_no`, `confirmation` and `account_no`, so
nothing new is needed on the wire.

⚠ **B14 rule 15's cap is the CALLER's**: two visible icons then `…`.

### `P3.12` IS THE LARGEST OF THE THREE, AND THE SERVICE IS READY

*"Multi-line resolve. A repeating row (reason · GL · amount · note) and a
running residual that must reach $0.00 before Reconcile enables."*

`reconciliation.py:2301` already takes a LIST and already refuses a sum that
does not match the difference — p055's own TODAY row: *"The server refuses the
reconcile until the resolutions sum to the difference — **a service rule, not a
convention**."* What is missing is the pop-up, which draws ONE row. The drawing
(p055) is a `FormModal` with a repeating row, a `+ Add explanation`, a
Difference / Explained / **Residual** trio, and `Record ✓` enabled only at a
residual of `$0.00`. Its worked case is a card day short by **$172.50**: a
`$147.50` processor fee AND a `$25.00` chargeback, and **one forced reason files
the chargeback as a fee and defeats CS-18**.

### WHAT THIS LANE DID PUSH IN PAYMENTS, STATED

Three files, and each is the minimum the Finance screen needed:

* `RefundsQueuePanel.tsx` — the cheque number becomes the door to 2·5d. **No
  act is added**; the panel's own `E1` (no second copy of five role-gated
  controls) is untouched.
* `RefundsPage.test.tsx` and `refundCorrectCheck.dom.test.tsx` — one field each
  in a fixture, because `RefundRow` gained `account_id`, which the server has
  served since `CR-059` CS-7 and the type omitted.

**No payments endpoint, table, rule or service changed.**
## 2026-09-24 — DECIDED (lane FIN-PAY, Finance blueprint `P1.3`): THE REFUND APPROVAL QUEUE IS PAGED, AND THE ARGUMENT AGAINST PAGING IT IS ANSWERED RATHER THAN OVERRULED

**This is a judgment call, not a build.** The Finance blueprint's Phase 1 plan
(PDF p012, task `P1.3`) says so in its own OUTCOME column: *"Either a pager, or
a recorded decision that this one list is exempt."* This row is the decision.

### WHAT THE CODE ARGUED, IN ITS OWN WORDS

`apps/payments/selectors.py::refund_queue` carried this, and it is quoted here
rather than paraphrased because it is a good argument and the next lane should
meet it whole:

> *"Unpaginated, deliberately, for the reason `write_off_queue` and
> `/outstandings` are: a utility under 3,000 connections has a queue a person
> reads in one screen, and **a page of an approval queue is a queue that lies
> about what is pending.**"*

Both halves matter. The first is a CAPACITY claim. The second is a claim about
what a screen MEANS — an approver looking at a queue is asking *"what is waiting
for me?"*, and fifty rows of nine hundred answers a different question while
looking identical.

### THE DECISION: PAGE IT, AND SERVE THE TRUE TOTAL ON EVERY PAGE

**The capacity half is simply false now.** The PO ruled the ICP ceiling from
3,000 to 40,000 accounts on 2026-09-06, and `NFR-3` (universal server
pagination) carves out no exception for a queue. The same excuse appears
verbatim on `/outstandings`, which was measured this week at **61.5 seconds
against a 60-second worker timeout** at 40,046 debtors — at the top of the range
it was not slow, it was **killed before it answered**. An approval queue that
cannot answer is worse than one that answers a page at a time.

**The meaning half is answered, and the answer is a number.** The blueprint
settles it on p040, and the wording is worth keeping: *"The answer to 'a page
lies about what is pending' is the count in the view label: `Refunds · 1` states
the true total on every page, so paging can no longer hide anything."* A
paginated queue that also states *"120 waiting"* answers the approver's actual
question better than an unpaginated one did, because the unpaginated one made
them scroll to find out.

**So the pager and the count are ONE change and neither ships without the
other.** `refund_queue` returns `total` as a required key rather than an
optional one, `GET /refunds` serves it as `count`, and `RefundsQueuePanel`
renders it beside its heading. A caller that draws the rows and drops the count
re-opens `DEF-PAY-6555`, and that sentence is in three docstrings so a later
lane meets it where it would make the mistake.

### WHAT WAS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED

**(a) Exempt this one list, as the OUTCOME column permits.** Declined. The
exemption would have to be written as a rule — *"an approval queue may be
unpaginated"* — and `write_off_queue` and `/outstandings` carry the same
sentence, so the rule would cover three lists and then a fourth. `NFR-5` (no
hard caps anywhere) and B6's design rule exist precisely to stop a ceiling being
designed in, and *"this list is small"* is a ceiling with no number on it.

**(b) Keep it unbounded and cap the RENDER instead** — serve everything, draw
fifty. Declined, and it is the tempting one because it needs no backend change.
It fixes the screen and leaves the cost: the query still builds every row, which
is the 61.5 seconds. It also makes the lie worse rather than better — the client
would know the true total and the server would still be the thing that fell
over.

### WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS CHANGE

* **The write-off queue.** `write_off_queue` carries the identical sentence and
  is `P2.19`'s, which the blueprint narrowed on its own page 7: *"P2.19 was also
  narrowed: its paging duplicated P1.8, which already pages both queues."* This
  lane did not touch it, and the narrowing note is worth re-reading by whoever
  does — `P1.8` paged the JOURNAL and not these two.
* **Search on `GET /refunds`.** `P2.19`'s, explicitly (*"Paging, search and a
  pending count on both queues"*). The queue takes `f.status` and no `q`.
* **The count BADGE in the view-strip label.** `P2.15`/`P2.18`'s. What landed
  here is the count on the wire and on the panel that reads it; the badge is the
  view strip's, and the number it will show is this one.

### THE WORKED CASE, AS IT WOULD BE PUT TO A PERSON

A utility with 900 refunds waiting. Before: the screen asked for all 900 and
drew all 900 inside a Revenue & AR panel. After: it asks for fifty, draws five,
and says **900 waiting** beside the heading. The approver learns the true number
faster than they did by scrolling, and the request no longer grows with the
utility.

## 2026-09-24 — MEASURED AND BUILT (lane FIN-SEED, `v2.351.75`): THE DEMO TENANT'S FINANCE DATA WAS NEVER MISSING — IT WAS IN THE WRONG MONTH, AND A COUNT WITH NO TENANT SET IS WHY WE THOUGHT OTHERWISE

The brief this lane was given opened with a measurement: *"The demo database has
no finance data at all — `journal_entries = 0 · journal_lines = 0 · invoices =
0 · payments = 0`."* It had reached a lane README as fact (*"THE TENANT HAS NO
FINANCE DATA, AND IT IS THE SEED"*) and from there into the task.

**It is false, and the four figures are false in the same way.** Counted on the
shared `smartbillhub` database with `app.tenant_id` set:

| | with no tenant set | with the tenant set |
|---|---|---|
| `invoices` | 0 | **80** |
| `invoice_lines` | 0 | **637** |
| `payments` | 0 | **66** |
| `journal_entries` | 0 | **167** |
| `journal_lines` | 0 | **661** |
| `accounts` | 0 | **75** |

RLS `FORCE` is on (hard rule 1), so a session that has not said which tenant it
is asking about sees **nothing in every tenant table** — and says so truthfully.
That is hard-won law 7's fifth shape exactly: *a check reporting zero over a
scope it silently excludes*, where the excluded scope was the whole tenant.
Filed as **`DEF-GOV-6641`**.

### THE SCREENS REALLY DID READ `$0.00`, AND THE REASON IS THE CALENDAR

The symptom was real; only the diagnosis was wrong. `useFinancePeriod` serves
**the current accounting period** (`BR-TEN-022`, computed never stored) and the
Finance tabs have **no period picker** — a clerk cannot look at another month.
On 2026-09-24 that period is **FY2026 Period 12, 09/01–09/30**.

`core/sample_fixture.py`'s `PERIODS` holds its calendar as `date()` CONSTANTS:
June 2026 billed, July 2026 billed, August read-and-unbilled. Correct when it
was written in August. **So every period-scoped Finance figure went to `$0.00`
on 1 September, on a full database, and nothing went red** — every row count is
non-zero, every gate is green, and no gate in this repo reads rendered output.

Filed as **`DEF-LED-6640`**. It is hard-won law 2's *"a rule with a clock in
it"* in a fixture: it rots on the day the clock passes it, not on the day it is
written, and the honest general lesson is that **a demo fixture pinned to fixed
months has an expiry date nobody wrote down.**

### WHAT WAS BUILT, AND WHY IT IS NOT A SECOND SEEDER

`10-scripts/seed_finance_current_period.py`. It seeds no tenant, creates no
account, premises, plan or bill, and shares no code with a fixture —
`load_sample_data`'s own docstring rules that *"it is not a second seeder"* and
this stays on the right side of that line. It does the one thing a fixture of
constants cannot: **put money in whatever month is open when it runs.**

Three blocks, every one through the service the clerk's own button calls:

* **38 payments** across the open period, mixed tenders — `record_payment`.
  Most are full or half; the last four waves take **a tenth or so from a lot of
  accounts**, which buys journal rows *without* emptying the ageing buckets.
  That mattered: the journal's rows-per-page chooser starts at **50**, so its
  pager cannot come alive under 51 entries in the period, and paging that list
  was the whole of `P1.8`. Buying those rows with full payments would have
  collected the arrears the Aging view exists to show.
* **3 overpayments and the 3 refunds they make possible** — `record_payment`
  then `request_refund`. An overpayment is the ONLY honest route to a refund:
  `request_refund` refuses an account that owes money (*"the credit is offset
  against it FIRST"*, PO 2026-08-12), so a refund needs a real credit behind it.
  `core/sample_fixture.py` already names this as case 11.
* **3 write-offs, 2 left waiting and 1 approved** — `request_write_off`, then
  `approve_write_off` on one. The two waiting are what make the *Write-offs*
  view and its badge visible at all; the approved one is where money moves.
  All three are in `payments/sample_data.py`'s own `NOT_SEEDED` list, so this
  fills a gap the repo had already named rather than inventing one.

**Figures read back out of the database afterwards**, on a `proof-db.sh` clone:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `payments` | 74 | **115** |
| `journal_entries` | 187 | **229** |
| `journal_lines` | 749 | **836** |
| `refunds` | 1 | **4** |
| `write_offs` | 0 | **3** (2 requested, 1 approved) |
| journal entries dated in September | 18 | **60** |
| **trial balance** | $68,328.16 = $68,328.16 | **$75,240.21 = $75,240.21** |
| unbalanced entries | 0 | **0** |

**The books foot after seeding**, which is the condition that decides whether
the seed is right: if the trial balance did not foot the Finance screens would
correctly shout that the books are broken, and the PO would read a true red
banner as a real problem. The script checks it itself and exits 1 if it fails.

### TWO REFUSALS, PROVED BEFORE THE FIRST WRITE

A money row written through a real service **can never be deleted** (hard rule
4) — which is how twelve phantom `$84.00` refunds came to be permanent in the
shared demo tenant this same day, seeded by a sibling lane so a screenshot had
something to count. The database refused every attempt to remove them, by name,
and that refusal is correct.

So this script refuses **before it opens a database**, and both refusals were
run and watched, not asserted:

* no `--database` at all → `error: the following arguments are required:
  --database`, **exit 2**. There is no default, because a default would be the
  shared demo.
* `--database smartbillhub` → a named refusal naming the six lanes reading it,
  **exit 2**, overridable only by `--yes-the-shared-demo`.

**It is idempotent**, and that was proved by running it a fourth time: `0
recorded, 36 already there (replayed)`, every count identical, trial balance
identical. Each payment carries an `idempotency_reference`, each refund an
`idempotency_key`, and each write-off is found by a marker in its note.

⚠ **ONE IDEMPOTENCY BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS LANE, AND IT IS WORTH THE
LINE.** The first version `continue`d as soon as a write-off's marker was found
— so a run that requested a write-off and then failed to approve it left the row
`requested` for good, and **every later run skipped the step that had never
happened**. An idempotency check that also skips the unfinished work is not
idempotent, it is stuck. The marker now says whether the REQUEST is done and the
status says whether the APPROVAL is.

### WHAT SEEDING CANNOT FIX, STATED SO NOBODY SEEDS AT IT

* **Billed this month stays `$0.00`.** There is no September bill run and there
  must not be: `PERIODS` leaves a month unbilled because that is the PO's own
  acceptance test — *"everything done leaves nothing to evaluate"*. Billing it
  here would have deleted it.
* **Aging shows no buckets.** The report loads every open bill into memory and
  cannot be paged or filtered; `P2.21` was handed back rather than half-built
  (`DEF-REP-6607`). The bills that would fill it are in the database — 39 at
  31–60 days and 41 at 61–90.
* **Costs is empty** because the demo utility has never captured a supplier
  invoice, and **bank reconciliation** is empty because no statement was ever
  imported. Both are a person's act, not a seeding gap.
* **Written off YTD still reads *Not available*** although a write-off is now
  approved and the Bad debt panel on the same screen shows it as `$75.99` —
  the figure is unserved (`DEF-LED-6606`), not unseeded.

### THREE THINGS FOUND BY OPENING A SCREEN, WHICH NOTHING ELSE COULD SEE

Hard-won law 6 earning its place. All three were filed, none fixed here:

* **`DEF-LED-6643`** — General ledger prints *"The books will not state this.
  The reason has no wording yet."* twice, on the Journal and the Trial balance.
  The served gap code `posted_by_is_in_audit_log_not_on_the_entry` has no
  `finance.gap.*` catalogue key, so `gapSentence` falls through to
  `finance.gap.unknown` — **a grammatical English sentence, so nothing throws,
  nothing logs and `tsc` is green.** `CloseExportPage.tsx` records this exact
  mechanism being fixed once already for a different code; the fix was made for
  that code and no check was added for the family.
* **`DEF-LED-6642`** — Finance → Costs prints `BR-LED-028:` and 38 words of
  reasoning at a clerk, against B14 rule 32 (no rule id in clerk-facing copy)
  and rule 33 (rationale is zero words on screen). It is a SERVED string, so no
  front-end copy check reads it, and the code comment above it presents it as
  deliberate.
* **`fullPage: true` does not work on this product**, which is why every shot
  in this gallery before today is exactly 900 pixels tall. The shell scrolls an
  inner `main.view` (`scrollHeight` 2,166 against a `document.scrollHeight` of
  900), so Playwright is told the page is one screen tall, believes it, and
  returns a crop **with no error and no warning** — a truncation that reads as
  deliberate framing. `10-scripts/fin_seed_gallery_walkthrough.mjs` measures the
  scroller and grows the viewport, and prints each shot's height so a short
  screen can be told from a cropped one.

### THE GALLERY

`WITH-DATA/` and `BEFORE-NO-CURRENT-MONTH/` — all thirteen Finance surfaces, the
same build (`2.351.72`) on the same database, with and without the seeder, so
any two files of the same name compare directly. Both were taken on a
`proof-db.sh` clone, which is built by migrating an empty database rather than
copying the shared one — **checked, not assumed: 0 `WALK-` rows against the
shared demo's 12 of 13 refunds.** Nothing in this work wrote a row into the
tenant six other lanes are using.

## 2026-09-24 · lane FIN-P3 · two lanes found one broken queue within an hour, and what the second one threw away

**Found by looking at a screenshot**, which is the only check in this repo that
reads rendered output. Phase 3's shots were being re-taken for the PO when the
Revenue & AR refunds panel came back reading **"Nothing is waiting here."** with
a badge beside it reading **1**, over a refund that was genuinely waiting.

**What had happened.** `GET /refunds` began paging in SQL (`965ed8fed`, payments
`P1.3`, `DEF-PAY-6555`) and moved to the DRF `{count, results}` envelope. The
client's `RefundQueueResponse` still declared `rows`, so `results` arrived
unread, `rows` came back `undefined`, and the panel drew its empty state. **The
badge went on working**, because it reads `pending`, which still arrived — so
the screen contradicted itself rather than breaking. Measured against the live
API: `?f.status=requested` answered `count=1`, one result, `pending=1`. Filed as
`DEF-PAY-6644`, with the measurement, because the escape was never written down.

**Nothing could have gone red.** `tsc` is satisfied — the type says `rows` and
nothing checks a type against a wire. Every front-end fixture for this endpoint
was written FROM that type, so all of them described a body the server had
stopped sending and all of them passed: the sibling's
`revenueArViews.dom.test.tsx`, and **this lane's own `financeP3Doors.dom.test.tsx`**,
which asserted the new door over the old shape.

**THE DECISION, AND IT IS ABOUT WHAT NOT TO PUSH.** This lane fixed it in the
client wrapper — `getRefunds` mapping `results` back to `rows` — proved it red,
proved it green, and proved it in a browser. While that was happening, **lane
FIN-PAY fixed the same defect properly and pushed first**: `RefundQueueResponse`
now declares the server's own `{count, next, previous, results}` and the panel
reads `results`. **Theirs is the better fix** — a wrapper that translates one
endpoint's envelope back into a private shape makes the next paged list a coin
toss — so **this lane's fix was DELETED rather than merged**, along with its
fixture correction to `financeP3Doors.dom.test.tsx`, which the same commit had
already made.

**What survived of it, deliberately:** the defect row, because the escape reason
is the durable part; **a test of `getRefunds` against a RECORDED response**
(`07-frontend/src/api/refundsQueueEnvelope.test.ts`), because the wrapper had no
test at all and that is how the wire change reached a screen unseen; and the
correction to `revenueArViews.dom.test.tsx`, whose stub still described the old
shape on the tip.

**The rule this leaves behind:** a fixture written from a TYPE tests the type.
Record the response.


## 2026-09-24 · BUILT (lane FIN-P4, `P4.5` · `P4.6`, `v2.351.77`): SIX DOWNLOAD CONTROLS WORK, AND FOUR REFUSAL SENTENCES ARE DELETED

**The phase's DONE WHEN, from the Finance blueprint p017:** *"Every download
control in Finance either works or is disabled for a reason that is true."*
**Measured in a browser at 1440 and 1280 against a booted stack on real seeded
data: six work, two are disabled until a subject is chosen, and both of those
were proved true by choosing one and watching the control come alive.**

### The judgment: a refusal sentence is DELETED, never shortened

B14 rule 33 puts RATIONALE at **zero words on screen**, and the rule is
explicit that rationale is REMOVED rather than cut — a *why* sentence trimmed
to six words keeps the breach and makes it terser. So four keys are retired
from all eleven catalogues rather than reworded:

* `reports.export.reason` · `finance.gl.exportUnavailable` ·
  `finance.taxes.reportUnavailable` · `payments.deposits.slipUnavailable`

and with them the server-side gap `no_deposit_slip_export`, whose whole text
was a reason that stopped being one.

⚠ **THE SHAPE IS WORTH RECORDING: TWO OF THESE SENTENCES WERE CORRECTED HOURS
BEFORE THEY WERE DELETED.** `P2.5` fixed them on the MORNING of 2026-09-24
because they blamed a service that was running; `P4.1` registered the resources
that afternoon and the corrected sentences became false in turn. **A hold with
a clock in it rots on the day the thing it waits for arrives**, and correcting
a hold makes it look maintained while leaving it in place. That is hard-won law
2's mirror, and the answer the law already gives is the one taken: the tests
that asserted the holds are INVERTED rather than deleted, in the same files, so
a lane putting a refusal back goes red. `p45DownloadsWork.dom.test.tsx` and
`depositsSurface.test.tsx`'s deposit-slip case are those tests.

### A component, not three copies (B14 rule 43)

`ReportDownloads` stays one component taking a resource and its filters, so the
next change to how a Finance report downloads is one edit and not three.
`P2.10`'s *"one change, three screens"* is what makes that worth saying.

⚠ **IT ALSO CAUGHT A REAL BUG, WHICH IS WHY THE TEST ASSERTS THE CALL AND NOT
THE BUTTON.** The first draft called `requestListExport` without the page's
client, so it would have reached the real network from inside any test and any
seam-mounted screen. A case that only asked *is the button pressable* would
have passed. The same omission was present in both ledger pages and is fixed in
all four.

### Three faults found by OPENING the screens, which no check could see

* **`DEF-REP-6648` — S59, the account ledger, had never run for anybody.** The
  screen asked for `f.account_id` and the server reads a bare `account`.
  Measured: `422 VAL-001 reports.account_ledger.account_required` with
  `field_errors [{field: account}]`, over a correctly filled-in box. **It is the
  SAME defect `endpoints.ts`'s own docstring records for `from`/`to`, one param
  over** — and that docstring asks in as many words that *"the next param added
  here has to be classified deliberately"*. `account_id` never was. **FIXED**,
  with an explicit `SERVER_PARAM_NAMES` map rather than a rule about names.
* **`DEF-REP-6649` — the same box asks for the wrong thing and crashes on it.**
  Its helper text says *"as the accounts list shows it"*, the list shows
  `AC-2026-00001`, the read model wants a UUID, and a non-UUID is a **500**
  rather than a refusal. **NOT FIXED**: which identifier that field takes is a
  product decision, and B14 rule 31 (no database id is ever the visible value of
  a field) points at a picker rather than a text box. The 500 half needs no
  decision and should be fixed on its own.
* **`DEF-LED-6647` — an intermittent failure in a neighbouring lane's file**,
  seen once in four runs and not reproduced. Recorded rather than dismissed,
  because an intermittent red teaches every later reader to scroll past a
  failure in that file.

**`DEF-SHL-6555` is also CLOSED here.** The *"nine registered lists"* guard was
an equality over a process-global registry, so its verdict depended on which
other test files shared the pytest process. Eight new resources would have made
it deterministically red. It is now a subset check — *nothing NAMED is missing*
— and the half it dropped (*"nothing more is exported by accident"*) was never
true of the registry, only of whatever happened to be imported.

## 2026-09-24 — `P3.10` · `P3.11` · `P3.12` BUILT (lane PAY-BATCH), AND THE HAND-BACK'S ONE MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG

The three Finance-blueprint phase-3 rows that live in PAYMENTS' code are built.
Two judgments below were nobody's ruling and are recorded with their figures;
one correction is a defect against the hand-back itself.

### THE CORRECTION: `P3.11` DOES NEED A BACKEND CHANGE (`DEF-PAY-6651`)

The hand-back of 2026-09-24 states, in capitals, *"`P3.11` NEEDS NO BACKEND
CHANGE AT ALL — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED"*, and prescribes the drift as
**Σ`members[].amount` − `recorded_total`**, *"computed over data the screen is
already holding"*.

**That figure is identically zero, for ever, on every batch.** Measured on real
PostgreSQL before any code was written:

| | |
|---|---|
| batch | `DEP-260808-0002`, reconciled and LOCKED |
| `recorded_total` | **2,388.84** |
| Σ `members[].amount` | **2,388.84** |
| Σ reversed | **501.33** |
| what it still stands for | **1,887.51** |

So the prescribed arithmetic answers **0.00** on a batch that is **501.33**
short — a tile added to say *this no longer sums* would have affirmed that
nothing was wrong.

**The mechanism is two rules working exactly as written.** `reversal._write_reversal`
creates the reversing row with **no `deposit_batch_id`**, so it is not a member;
and hard rule 4 forbids updating the original's `amount` or `status`, so no
member row moves either. Both are correct. What is not available is the drift.

**Nothing would have caught it.** The arithmetic is right, `sumDecimalStrings`
is exact, `tsc` and every test pass, and no gate reads a rendered figure. The
measurement was taken from the served payload's FIELD LIST rather than from the
write path that produces the drift.

**So `live_total` is SERVED** — Σ(`amount` − `reversed_so_far`) in `Decimal` on
the `NUMERIC(18,6)` grid — and each member carries its own `reversed_amount`, so
the gap is attributable to a LINE rather than only to a total. It is computed in
`batch_detail` and deliberately NOT in `batch_row`, which the list and the
dashboard share and where one aggregate per row is the round trip
`DEF-PAY-6554` had just removed.

**The durable lesson:** a claim that a figure *can be computed from what the
screen already holds* is a claim about the WRITE path, not the read path. It is
settled by constructing the state and reading the figure out — one service call
here — not by reading the payload.

### JUDGMENT 1 — THE `Status` KPI TILE IS REMOVED, AND THE STRIP IS THE DRAWN FOUR

`P3.11` adds a *Live payments* tile. The batch strip already held four, so it
would have held five, and the blueprint (p050) draws **four**.

Measured on the running screen at 1440 before deciding: `.kpi-grid` is
`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr))` over ~1,160px of content, so five tiles
wrap and `Status` lands alone on a row of its own. Photographed, not predicted.

`Status` was also the one tile that said what the screen already said twice over:
`PageHeader` renders the batch's `StatusPill` two inches above it, so
*Reconciled* appeared twice, and the lock is stated by which control the head
offers — `Unreconcile` when locked, `Resolve difference` when not.

**Removed.** The strip is now `We recorded · Live payments · Bank shows ·
Difference`, which is the drawn count and fits without wrapping. No fact left
the screen.

### JUDGMENT 2 — `Record ✓` IS NOW GATED ON THE RESIDUAL, REVERSING THIS FILE'S OWN EXCEPTION (5)

`DepositBatchPage.tsx` has carried, since 2026-08-16, exception (5): *"the
client-side tie-out is advisory only and never gates submit — the server's is
the enforcement"*, on the reasoning that a client which thought it knew better
would be a second implementation of a signed rule.

p055 rules otherwise and draws `Record ✓ · enabled only at a residual of $0.00`.

**Both can be true, and the blueprint is right.** Disabling a commit is not a
second implementation of the tie-out: `reconcile_batch` still decides, and the
screen merely stops offering a press that must fail. That is `BR-SHL-025` in its
own words, and `FormModal.commitBlocked` renders the reason as announced text
rather than as a tooltip.

**`residual === null` BLOCKS.** The bank has not spoken, or an amount will not
parse — *we do not know what is left* is the one state where a plausible zero
must not open a money commit.

### JUDGMENT 3 — TWO FIELDS PER LINE IN THE RESOLVE MODAL, NOT THE DRAWING'S FIVE

B14 rule 38: *"where a drawing and our UI rules disagree about how a FORM IS
BUILT, the UI rules win"* — side-by-side fields are CONSTRUCTION, and one
screen's drawing does not get to change how every dialog in the product is
built.

It is also measured. The 560px card leaves ~512px of body, so the drawing's five
across gives each input about **90px**. Built that way first and photographed:
the inputs read `proce`, `bank_`, `returnec`, and the help text wrapped into
columns one word wide. **What the row CONTAINS is still the drawing's** — the
same four fields (reason · GL · amount · note), repeating, with the same ✕ and
the same `+ Add explanation`.

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND HOW

* **The worked case, driven in a browser and watched.** A card day short by
  **$172.50** is a **$147.50** processor fee AND a **$25.00** chargeback — two
  reasons, two GL accounts. Residual −$172.50 → −$25.00 after the fee → **$0.00**
  after the chargeback, with the commit refused at every step until then.
* **Four backend tests on real PostgreSQL**, not the default SQLite suite
  (hard-won law 14): the reversal moves no member row, `live_total` and
  `reversed_amount` are served, an untouched batch reads live == recorded, and
  the bulk reversal read agrees with its single-row sibling.
* **Every guard shown RED first, in the harness that runs it** — and two of them
  could not fail on the first attempt, which is the finding worth keeping. A
  residual rewritten to go through a float left all sixteen tests GREEN (at
  ordinary money magnitudes `toFixed(6)` rounds the error away), and sending only
  `drafts.slice(0, 1)` — the exact defect `P3.12` repairs — left all forty deposit
  tests GREEN, because every case exercised `residualOf` DIRECTLY and none drove
  the screen. Both were rewritten and both sabotages re-run against them.

### AND A WORKED FIGURE THREE MONEY FILES CITE DOES NOT REPRODUCE (`DEF-PAY-6650`)

`DepositBatchPage.tsx`, `depositsShared.tsx` and `depositsSurface.test.tsx` each
justify their BigInt arithmetic with *"`Number("5120.40") - Number("4972.90")` is
`147.50000000000045`"*. On this engine it is **exactly 147.5**, and so is the
card day's own pair. The conclusion is right and the exact arithmetic stays —
`9758.11 - 8154.50` really does give `1603.6100000000005821` — but the evidence
cited for it is not reproducible, which is hard-won law 1 in a code comment: a
worked number nothing re-runs. All three now cite a pair that IS inexact, and the
claim is asserted in a test rather than restated in a comment.

## 2026-09-25 — BUILT (lane FIN-DATA, `DEF-LED-6640`, `v2.351.85`): THE DEMO CALENDAR TRAVELS WITH THE REAL ONE, AND THE UNBILLED MONTH SURVIVES IT

**The defect, restated because the fix is only interesting against it.**
`core/sample_fixture.py` held its calendar as `date()` CONSTANTS — June 2026
billed, July 2026 billed, August 2026 read-and-unbilled. Correct the day it was
typed. The Finance screens show the **CURRENT accounting period**
(`useFinancePeriod` → `GET /shell/display`, computed per `BR-TEN-022`) and there
is **no period picker** to move off it, so from 1 September every period-scoped
Finance figure read **`$0.00`** on a database holding 80 invoices, 66 payments
and 167 journal entries. Nothing was broken and nothing was lying: the money was
in a month the screen cannot show.

⚠ **A SCREEN READING `$0.00` AND A SCREEN WITH NO DATA BEHIND IT ARE
INDISTINGUISHABLE TO EVERYONE WHO LOOKS AT THEM.** That is what made this cost
more than a demo blemish, and it had already produced one false report to the
Product Owner (`DEF-GOV-6641`, a count taken with no `app.tenant_id` set on a
`FORCE` RLS database). A demo that shows a zero teaches everyone who sees it
either to distrust the figures or — worse — to trust that zero.

### ⚠ THIS WAS NOT A NEW JUDGMENT — THE PO RULED IT IN AUGUST AND IT NEVER REACHED THIS FILE

**Found while measuring the blast radius, and it is the most useful thing in
this entry.** `apps/metering/sample_data.py` solved this identical problem for
the work-order exhibit months ago, under a ruling from the Product Owner
themselves, quoted verbatim in that file:

> *"whenever you do the migration cant you devcide the date at that time"*
> — PO, `DEF-629`

Its block header states the posture in full: *"every date below is an OFFSET
from the tenant's own today and the drawn date rides beside it"*, and
*"`BR-TEN-043` is satisfied for `DEF-629`'s own reason: the clock is read ONCE,
at the moment the fixture is planted, and the answer is STAMPED into the rows."*
The route cycle went further and already anchors on
`fixture.PERIODS[-1]["read_on"]`, so it travelled the moment the periods did.

**So the accounting calendar was the ONE part of the fixture that never got the
ruling**, and it is the part where a stale date is money. That is this file's
own most-repeated shape — a ruling lands in one place and the siblings that
needed it are never amended — and it is why `DEF-LED-6640` reads as a fresh
discovery six weeks after the answer was given. **Nothing counted the modules
the ruling should have reached, so nobody could see that one was missing.**

### THE DECISION: THE MONTHS BECOME A SHAPE

The three periods are kept exactly as signed and are now read as a shape stated
**relative to the fixture's own "today"**, which the spec has always put in
mid-month. The whole table is shifted by a WHOLE NUMBER OF MONTHS at seed time:

| position | canonically | what it is | on a tenant seeded 2026-09-25 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **M-2** | June | billed, ~95% collected, closed | **July 2026** |
| **M-1** | July | billed, uncollected | **August 2026** |
| **M** | August | **READ AND UNBILLED — OPEN** | **September 2026** |

`OPENING_READ_ON` and `BUSY_DAY` travel with it — the busy day's mixed takings
land on the **8th of the open month**, which is what puts cash in the accounting
period Finance actually shows.

⚠⚠ **THE UNBILLED MONTH SURVIVES, AND IT WAS THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPED THE
FIX.** `PERIODS` leaves a month unbilled because it is the Product Owner's own
acceptance test — *"everything done leaves nothing to evaluate"* (CR-010
Part-10.4, and CR-040 task C9 when the count of finished cycles rose from one to
two). **Travelling the calendar bills NOTHING new.** The last entry is still
`billed: False`; **BILLED THIS MONTH is still `$0.00`, deliberately**; and
acceptance item 4 is still *"run the August billing run"*, now meaning *this
month's*. The seeder that preceded this work reached the same conclusion from
the other side and the note it left — *"Billing it here would have deleted
it"* — is why this fix moves dates and never a `billed` flag.

### WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH "JUST SHIFT THE DATES", AND IT IS ARITHMETIC

**Month-end stickiness is load-bearing and the first draft did not have it.**
The billed periods are WHOLE CALENDAR MONTHS. A day-preserving shift turns
**30 June into 30 July** — a 31-day month ending a day early — while the next
period still starts on the 1st. That is a **one-day hole of consumption that no
bill covers, on a money path**, and it would have been invisible: every row
count stays the same and no total moves. A date that is the last day of ITS
month now lands on the last day of the target month, and
`test_the_periods_are_contiguous_with_no_hole` is the assertion that says so.

**And nothing may be dated in the future.** Run on the **3rd** of a month, the
shifted busy day (the 8th) and the open period's read (the 14th) would both be
next week — a demo containing a payment banked in the future and a meter read
nobody has taken. Everything that must already have happened is clamped to
today, so the open period is simply SHORT, which is what a month in progress
looks like. `apps/payments/sample_data._collection_day` is clamped the same way,
against `fixture.TODAY` — **a DECLARED figure on the fixture, never a clock of
its own**, which is the distinction `BR-TEN-043` and `G6` are about.

### DETERMINISM, AND SAYING OUT LOUD WHAT THE SUITE DOES NOT PROVE

The wall clock is read **once**, in `core/`, and every other date is derived
from it. `SBH_FIXTURE_TODAY` overrides it, and `config/settings/test.py` pins it
to the anchor day — **where the offset is zero and the fixture reproduces the
2026 constants byte for byte**, so all sixteen test files that assert on
June/July/August are unaffected and **none was rewritten**.

⚠ **THAT PIN MEANS THE SUITE PROVES NOTHING ABOUT THE TRAVELLING, AND THE PIN
SAYS SO IN ITS OWN COMMENT**, because it is exactly hard-won law 7's *check that
cannot fail* shape. The travelling is proved instead by one file,
`tests/test_def_led_6640_the_calendar_travels.py`, which **states the day it
means** for ten simulated dates (the anchor, both ends of a month, a year
boundary, a February, a leap day, four years out) and reads the REAL clock in
exactly one test, on purpose — the defect register's own prevention column made
executable.

**PROVED RED BEFORE TRUSTED GREEN, in the harness that runs it** (law 7's other
half):

| what was broken | what the suite said |
|---|---|
| offset forced to `0` — the defect restored | 9 failures, `assert datetime.date(2026, 8, 1) == datetime.date(2026, 9, 1)` |
| month-end stickiness removed | `AssertionError: june ends 2026-07-30 and july starts 2026-08-01` |
| both restored | **65 passed** |

### WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SEEDED, AND WHY — ASKED SCREEN BY SCREEN

Three Finance surfaces are still empty. **Each was classified rather than
assumed, and none of them is seeded here.**

* **Reconcile a bank statement** — empty because nobody ever imported a
  statement. ⚠ **THIS IS THE SAME DESIGNED ABSENCE AS THE UNBILLED MONTH, NOT A
  GAP.** The demo-tenant spec's acceptance walk names it as **step 6** —
  *"deposit batches, statement import, the card fee, reconcile"* — exactly as it
  names the bill run as step 4. Seeding it would delete an acceptance step, the
  identical mistake the unbilled month exists to prevent. `apps/payments/sample_data.NOT_SEEDED`
  already names it.
* **Costs → Captured purchases** — empty because no supplier invoice was ever
  captured. This one is a genuine gap rather than a designed absence, and it is
  still not seeded, for two measured reasons. **It cannot be part of THIS fix:**
  `OQ-200` closed on 2026-08-16 with option (b) — *capture posts NOTHING to the
  books today* — so a captured purchase moves no period-scoped Finance figure at
  all. **And it is partly blocked:** `OQ-201` (the purchase-side unit vocabulary
  per service) is **OPEN**, and guessing a unit on a money-adjacent path is what
  the prime directive forbids. Water and electric would compute; gas would not.
* **Bought vs billed** cannot produce a loss percentage — it needs purchase
  volumes, so it follows the row above and for the same reasons.

⚠ **THE GENERAL JUDGMENT, WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE THE NEXT LANE WILL FACE IT:** a
demo where every screen is full teaches a different lie from one where some are
empty. The three above are each **a person's act that the product is waiting
for**, and a demo that has already done the visitor's work for them is a demo
with nothing left to demonstrate.

### WHAT THIS FIX CANNOT DO, STATED SO NOBODY EXPECTS IT

**An already-seeded tenant does not move and cannot.** Hard rule 4 makes issued
invoices, payments and journal entries append-only, so the calendar travels for
a tenant seeded **from now on**; an existing one is re-dated by seeding a FRESH
tenant, never by mutation. `10-scripts/seed_finance_current_period.py` remains
the only tool for putting cash into the open period of a tenant that already
exists, and its docstring now says which of the two to reach for — it was
written against the diagnosis this entry supersedes and would otherwise read as
the whole answer.

### THE KEYS ARE STILL `june` / `july` / `august`, AND THAT IS ON PURPOSE

They are stable IDENTIFIERS, not month names: **37 files ask the fixture for
`august` meaning *the open one***. Renaming them would move every citation at
once for no gain — the same reasoning that leaves `OQ-291` as `OQ-291`. A reader
meeting `august` in code on a tenant seeded in February is looking at February,
and `test_only_the_dates_move` pins the keys so a future lane cannot quietly
re-point them.

### ⚠ CORRECTED THE SAME HOUR: `BILLED THIS MONTH STAYS $0.00` WAS NEVER THE INVARIANT

**Everything above was written before the screens were opened, and opening them
corrected it.** Three places in this lane's own work — this entry, the fixture's
comment and the demo spec's banner — said *"BILLED THIS MONTH is still `$0.00`,
deliberately"*. **It is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that would have
cost the most**: the next lane reading it would have gone to "fix" a screen that
is now correct.

**Measured in a browser at 1440 on the first tenant seeded with a travelling
calendar** (2026-09-25, build `2.351.86`, a `proof-db.sh` clone nobody else was
seeding):

| Finance → Revenue & AR | reads |
|---|---|
| **BILLED THIS MONTH** | **`$15,734.17`** — *"Posted between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-30"* |
| **COLLECTED** | **`$22,312.81`** — *"in cash and $0.00 from applied deposits"* |
| **STILL OWED** | **`$24,988.71`**, 44 accounts owing |
| Revenue by service | **two rows** — electric `$9,963.29`, water `$5,462.36`, footing to `$15,734.17` |

The panel that read *"Nothing to export"* yesterday now has both services in it.

**THE TILE COUNTS BY POSTING DATE; THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS ABOUT THE SERVICE
PERIOD. They are different questions and the sentence conflated them.** Read
back off the same database with `app.tenant_id` set:

| | |
|---|---|
| bills covering a September **service period** | **0** |
| bills **posted** in September | **45**, every one covering `2026-08-01`–`2026-08-31` |
| September reads, committed, awaiting a run | **117** |
| trial balance | **`$72,374.01` = `$72,374.01`**, difference `.0000` |

That is **bill run 2 going out on the 2nd**, exactly as this fixture has always
issued it. **So the Product Owner's acceptance test is untouched** — no bill
covers the open month, and their own run is still the third cycle, with 117
committed reads waiting for it.

⚠ **AND ON THE OLD CONSTANTS THE SAME TILE WAS NEVER `$0.00` EITHER.** At the
fixture's own mid-August "today", July's bill had posted on 2 August and the
tile showed it. **The `$0.00` was a SYMPTOM of the defect** — a tenant whose
newest bill had posted six weeks earlier — and it was recorded, in good faith,
as a property of the design. **A sentence describing a symptom, carried forward
as a rule, is this repo's most-filed rot**, and it took one hour and one
screenshot to produce a fresh instance of it.

**The invariant, stated correctly so it can be quoted:** *no bill covers the
OPEN SERVICE PERIOD.* That is what `billed: False` on the last entry means, it
is what `test_exactly_one_period_is_unbilled_and_it_is_the_last` asserts in
every month it is asked about, and it says nothing at all about what a
posting-date tile shows.

### THE WALK: TWELVE OF THIRTEEN FINANCE SURFACES HAVE DATA

`10-scripts/fin_seed_gallery_walkthrough.mjs`, both widths, same build and
database. It counts rows and non-zero money cells per screen, so an empty one
says so with a number beside it:

| screen | rows | non-zero money |
|---|---|---|
| General ledger · Journal | 50 | 100 |
| General ledger · Trial balance | 61 | 133 |
| General ledger · Chart of accounts | 282 | 0 (a chart carries no money) |
| General ledger · Accruals | 5 | 3 |

| Revenue & AR · Write-offs | 0 | 4 |
| Revenue & AR · Refunds | 0 | 4 |

**Costs is the one empty screen and it is the deliberate one**, for the reasons

## 2026-09-25 — FIXED (lane FIN-COPY, fifteen Finance copy defects): THE SCREENS STOP EXPLAINING THEMSELVES, AND THE GUARD THAT COUNTS THEM CANNOT SEE MOST OF THEM

Fifteen open Finance defects about **what a clerk reads**. Two turned out to be
already fixed, one a duplicate, twelve were real. Every judgment below is written
here because the rules ran out somewhere in it.

### THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THE FIFTEEN: FOUR OF THEM WERE NEVER COUNTABLE

`financeCopyRule33.test.ts` reports **144 Finance strings over B14 rule 33's
cap**, and it is the number this repo quotes. It counts `en.json`.

**Four of these defects were prose composed in a Python read model and printed
verbatim** — a 90-word basis paragraph quoting `OQ-202` and a PO ruling, a
`Formula: (bought_volume - billed_volume) / bought_volume` line of our own field
names, a 55-word note weighing up which download pipeline we have not chosen, and
38 words with `BR-LED-028:` in front of them. **Removing all four moved the
guard's number by ZERO**, because none of them was ever a key. The number moved
144 → **141** on the three CATALOGUE strings alone.

That is hard-won law 7's fifth shape — *a check reporting a number over a scope
it silently excludes* — and the guard is not lying: it names its scope in its own
docstring. **But 144 reads as "the number of over-long strings a Finance clerk can
meet", and the worst four were outside it.** Filed as `DEF-LED-6698`. It is also
`TD-16`/`B8` broken in four places: a server sending English to a product with
eleven catalogues shows ten of them English.

### JUDGMENT 1 — `DEF-LED-6620`: THE BASIS LABEL COMES OFF TWELVE CELLS, AND BR-REP-001 IS NOT BEING REVERSED

Every money cell in the tie-out printed **POSTING DATE** beside its figure. The
register row says sixteen; **the real number on that data is FIFTEEN and the row
is corrected** — four subledgers × three money columns = **12 in the table**,
plus **3 live KPI tiles**. Sixteen is the maximum: the fourth tile, *Written off
YTD*, reads *Not available* on that tenant (`DEF-LED-6606`), so it carried no
money and therefore no label.

**This did not go to the PO, and the reason is that the signed rule already says
it.** `BR-REP-001`, verbatim: *"every KPI/report **header** labels its basis — no
unlabeled money number anywhere"*. It asks for a label on the HEADER, once. The
code passed it to every CELL. And `tie_out.BASIS` is a module CONSTANT
(`BASIS_POSTING`) — the same value on every row of every tenant — so there was
never a per-row fact to tell. The Finance blueprint p036 draws this table with
clean figures and puts the basis caption on the KPI strip above it, which is the
same reading. **The strip is untouched** and still labels every money tile
(`revenueArKpis` makes it un-omittable), so no money number on this screen is
unlabelled. Twelve repetitions of one report-level fact is also B14 rule 32's
description budget.

### JUDGMENT 2 — WHERE THE BLUEPRINT NAMES THE WORDS, THE WORDS ARE THE BLUEPRINT'S

`DEF-LED-6603`'s undismissable tie-out note was 19 words of rationale. The
Finance blueprint **p036, read as an image** (B14 rule 42), draws it and names its
length in the same breath — *"The undismissable note · **three words**"* — and
the drawn screen reads **"Clears when explained."** That is what the eleven
catalogues now hold. Nothing was invented.

Same page settles `DEF-LED-6670`: p063's table draws **Water** and **Electric**,
so the raw keys go through `serviceLabel` — `rating.service.*`, the single
product-wide label `DEF-763` already settled.

### JUDGMENT 3 — WHERE IT DOES NOT, A RAW CODE TAKES THE NAME THE PRODUCT ALREADY USES

* `DEF-LED-6612` — four GL roles rendered their code. `accumulated_depreciation`
  took `finance.gl.category.accumulated_depreciation` **verbatim in all eleven
  languages**: the product's own name for the same thing, printed as the section
  heading on the same screen. The other three took their SEEDED ACCOUNT NAMES
  from `chart.py` — *Accrued expenses*, *Allowance for doubtful accounts*, *Cash
  over and short*, the last being the PO's own words of 2026-09-23 — translated
  into each language's standard accounting term rather than from the English
  (B14 rule 35).
* `DEF-LED-6613` — the unsigned-account note was a bare `<span>` of twelve words
  with no whitespace before it, so it rendered glued to the account name. It is
  now `<StatusPill tone="warning">` with `finance.coa.unsigned` — **Proposed** —
  **the control and the word line 351 of the same file already uses for the
  identical state**. `ChartOfAccountsPanel.tsx` is deliberately OFF
  `route-b-migrated.txt` and B14 rule 21 forbids adding a stylesheet class, so
  reusing the kit was the only lawful fix and also the right one. The 12-word key
  is retired.
* `DEF-LED-6661` — a write-off's uuid7 in the Journal memo. A write-off has no
  number of its own and minting one would be a schema change dressed as a copy
  fix, so the memo names the **account** (`accounts.account_no`, `A-10432`), which
  is the shape every other memo in that seam already uses. **The provenance is not
  deleted, it leaves the SENTENCE**: `source_type`, `source_id` and the posting
  key are untouched.

### JUDGMENT 4 — A GAP SENTENCE WITH NO WORDING IS SOMETIMES NOT A MISSING SENTENCE

`posted_by_is_in_audit_log_not_on_the_entry` was appended to **every** journal
read unconditionally, with no catalogue key, so **every Journal and every Trial
balance printed *"The books will not state this. The reason has no wording
yet."*** It is **REMOVED rather than worded**: it described a *Posted by* column
**no screen in this product offers** (`grep -rn 'posted_by'
07-frontend/src/features/ledger` returns nothing), which makes it rationale, not
an absence a clerk meets. The day a screen offers that column it comes back —
with a key, which it never had.

`finance.gap.unknown` itself lost its second sentence. *"The reason has no
wording yet"* is our own unfinished work told to a utility user; rationale is
removed, not shortened.

The two that ARE actionable absences got words cut from the product's own
existing sentences for the same facts, under the six-word cap, in all eleven
catalogues.

### WHAT WAS NOT FIXED, AND WHY — three rows filed rather than guessed

* `DEF-LED-6676` — **twenty more gap codes in `apps/ledger` have no
  `finance.gap.*` key**, found only once a scan existed. They are baselined in
  the new guard rather than left red (*a red nobody can act on is a red nobody
  reads*), and every NEW code now fails on its first commit.
* `DEF-LED-6677` — the **sixteen cost CATEGORIES** still render raw on Costs.
  `serviceLabel` covers the eleven SERVICES. Their names already exist in
  `chart.COST_CATEGORY_SPECS` and must be fanned in, never coined here.
* `DEF-LED-6698` — the scope blind spot above.

### A RED THAT WAS ALREADY RED, DATED RATHER THAN DISMISSED

`test_the_reconciliation_download_is_refused_by_name_not_by_404` asserted
`"has not been ruled" in …["reason"]`. `233472ac1` (`P2.5`, 2026-09-24) reworded
that sentence to *"has not been decided"* and did not move the test, so it had
been failing for a day on a screen whose copy was actively being fixed. **Dated
with `git log -S "has not been ruled" -- apps/ledger/cost_api.py`, not from
memory** (hard-won law 7). Repaired in the same commit that turned the field into
a key.

## 2026-09-25 · FOUR PO RULINGS, RECORDED BY LANE RULE

All four were given by the Product Owner on 2026-09-25 in the working chat
session. Each row carries the PO's verbatim words, the worked figure that was
put to them, and — separately — **what the signature does not cover**, because a
signature covers only what was shown.

### RULING 1 — SEWER'S BASE CHARGE IS MAPPED TO THE WRONG ACCOUNT, AND IT IS WRONG

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-25:** *"a — It's wrong — point it at 4120 · Sewer"*.

**What was shown to them.** On tenant Ottumwa Water Works, Finance → Chart →
*Where each service's revenue goes*, **Sewer's base-charge revenue points at
`3010 · Operating grants`** while its usage revenue correctly points at
`4120 · Sewer`. Every other service points both halves at its own account —
Water→Water, Trash→Trash, Solar→Solar, Battery→Battery, Fire→Fire. So sewer
standing charges have been reported as **grant income**.

**THE BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED — `DEF-LED-6716`.**

* **IT IS NOT SEEDED THAT WAY, AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.**
  `apps/ledger/chart.py`'s `SERVICE_REVENUE_ACCOUNTS` maps `sewer` to
  `("4120", None)`. The `None` is the BASE half, and `BR-BIL-010` makes a `None`
  base fall back to the usage account — so a freshly provisioned tenant's sewer
  base charge lands in `4120 · Sewer` by construction and cannot land in `3010`.
  Read live on the only tenant present in all thirteen local databases (Brazos
  Bend Utilities): `sewer | 4120 Sewer | <base NULL>`, correct, as are all
  eleven services. **So it is ONE TENANT'S STORED CONFIGURATION, not a default
  every utility we provision carries.**
* **NOTHING IN THE PRODUCT COULD HAVE OBJECTED, AND THAT IS THE REAL DEFECT.**
  `tenancy.services._apply_service_gl_accounts` validates exactly one thing —
  `seams.ledger_account_is_live`, which asks whether the account exists, is this
  tenant's, and is not deactivated. It asks nothing about what KIND of revenue
  account it is. And the screen's own picker, `GlServiceMapEditor.
  revenueAccountOptions`, offers **every ACTIVE REVENUE account**; `3010
  Operating grants` is seeded `type="revenue"`, `category=CAT_GRANTS`, so it is
  in the list. The picker's own test asserts it offers active revenue accounts
  and nothing else — which it does, correctly. **The guard, the picker and the
  test are all working exactly as written and the wrong answer passes all
  three.** A clerk can point any service's revenue at grant income on any
  tenant and nothing anywhere says a word.
* **HOW LONG IT HAS BEEN LIVE — NOT ESTABLISHED, AND SAID SO PLAINLY.** Ottumwa
  Water Works is the PO's DEPLOYED tenant and is **in none of the thirteen local
  databases** (every one holds Brazos Bend Utilities and nothing else), so the
  stored row, the date it was written and the `audit_log` entry behind it cannot
  be read from this checkout. `git log -S` answers nothing either, because the
  value is DATA and not code — the seed never wrote it. **The date it was
  mis-pointed is a question for the deployment, not for the repository.**
* ⚠ **WHETHER PAST MONTHS ARE MISSTATED IS THEREFORE UNANSWERED AND MUST NOT BE
  ASSUMED EITHER WAY.** If sewer base-charge lines have posted while the map
  pointed at `3010`, every one of them credited Operating grants and those
  months' revenue reports are wrong by exactly that amount. `audit_log` on the
  deployment carries `settings.service.gl_updated` with its before/after and its
  timestamp, and that one row dates the exposure; the journal lines credited to
  `3010` with `source_type='bill_line'` measure it. **Both reads are on the
  deployment and neither was run.**

⚠ **WHAT THE FIX CAN AND CANNOT DO — HARD RULE 4.** No UPDATE or DELETE on
issued invoices, invoice lines, payments or journal entries; corrections are new
rows. **So re-pointing the map fixes the FUTURE only.** Every sewer base-charge
line already posted stays credited to `3010` and no map change moves it.
**NOTHING WAS RE-POSTED AND NO CORRECTING ENTRY WAS WRITTEN** — a correcting
entry is a balanced pair in the current open period, debiting `3010 · Operating
grants` and crediting `4120 · Sewer` for the total of the sewer base-charge
lines that landed in `3010`, dated the day it is posted and never backdated into
a closed period. **That is described here and deliberately not built**: it moves
money between two accounts on a real utility's books and it is the PO's to rule
on, not this lane's.

⚠ **WHAT THIS SIGNATURE DOES NOT COVER.** The PO was shown one tenant's screen
and ruled where sewer's base charge belongs. They were **NOT** asked and have
**NOT** ruled: whether a correcting entry should be posted for the months
already reported as grant income; how far back the exposure goes; or whether the
mapping screen should stop offering non-operating revenue accounts at all. The
last of those is `DEF-LED-6716`'s second half and is a product change, not this
ruling.

### RULING 2 — HAND-TYPED JOURNAL ENTRIES GET THE FIVE TAGS, OPTIONAL — `OQ-LED-12629` CLOSED

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-25:** *"a — Add the five tags, keep them optional"*.

**Option (a) of three, and (a) is not what was recommended.** The lane putting
the question recommended **(c)**; the PO chose **(a)**. The three as they were
put: **(a)** `P1.16` adds the five tag pickers and they stay OPTIONAL · **(b)**
the pickers are added and a revenue or cost line is REFUSED without a service,
the way `BR-LED-001` already requires `source_type`+`source_id` · **(c)**
optional, plus a stated absence on each report naming what it could not place.
**The choice is recorded, not the preference.**

**The worked case shown to them:** a finance officer reclassifies **$400.00** of
power cost by hand on 23 September; the by-service report for September shows
every other cost and not that one, and there is no cell anywhere that reads
*"and $400.00 we cannot place."* **Measured on the seeded database: 661 of 661
live journal lines carry an `account_id`** — every one written by the machine
paths — and a hand-typed entry carries nothing.

⚠ **WHAT THIS SIGNATURE COVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.** It covers **that the five
pickers are added — service · account · premises · unit · tax authority — and
that they stay OPTIONAL**. It does **NOT** rule that reports must name what they
could not place: that was option (c) and it was **not chosen**. **So the
catch-all row stays, and nothing here licenses adding a "we could not place
this" line to any report.** A lane that builds one is building an option the PO
declined.

⚠ **`BR-LED-001` SAYS EACH DIMENSION IS REQUIRED *"WHERE IT APPLIES"* AND THAT
PHRASE STILL HAS NO RULE. THIS RULING DOES NOT GIVE IT ONE.** Choosing (a) makes
all five optional on the hand-typed path, which is a different statement from
saying which of the five *apply* to a hand-typed reclassification. **A lane
whose work needs that answer mints a new question and stubs it; it does not
decide it.**

**`P1.16` IS UNBLOCKED BY THIS RULING** — the tags on the manual entry — and the
build is a separate piece of work that this lane deliberately did not start.

### RULING 3 — REFUNDS GET THEIR OWN NUMBER SERIES, AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE SENTENCE IS NOT TRUE OF THE PRODUCT

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-25:** *"b — Give refunds their own number series - it is
already there in setting -> configure numbering"*.

**The worked case:** the account ledger prints a document number on **147 of
167** lines; **19 are opening balances and correctly blank; 1 is a refund, and a
refund has no number anywhere.** That empty cell is what prompted the question.

⚠ **THE SECOND HALF OF THE PO'S SENTENCE IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE PRODUCT AND IT WAS
CHECKED. IT IS NOT TRUE TODAY — THERE IS NO REFUND SERIES ON THE NUMBERING
SCREEN.** Three independent reads, because a single grep in a single folder is
how this was got wrong once already:

1. **The server's catalogue.** `core/numbering.py`'s `SERIES_CATALOG` holds
   **THIRTY-ONE** series and **none of them is a refund**: account, premises,
   unit, service_request, customer, bill, payment, receipt, adjustment,
   credit_memo, write_off, bill_run, deposit_batch, journal_entry,
   collections_notice, export_batch, connection, work_order, service_template,
   dispatch_batch, asset, read_batch, route, cycle, import_run, transfer,
   disconnect_case, move_in, move_out, interruption_report, settlement. The
   whole file contains no `REFUND` constant and no case-insensitive match for
   *refund* at all.
2. **The live data the screen renders.** `SettingsNumberingTab.tsx` composes no
   list of its own — its own docstring says so, *"`row.options` arrives from the
   server's `SERIES_CATALOG`"* — and the rows come from `number_series`. Read on
   the live database inside a transaction with `app.tenant_id` set:
   **31 rows, and `WHERE series ILIKE '%refund%'` returns none.**
3. **The product already says it in its own words.**
   `apps/payments/refunds_and_credits.py` states it verbatim: *"REFUNDS HAD NO
   SERIES AND STILL HAVE NO NUMBER COLUMN. There is no `REFUND` constant in
   `core/numbering.py` … and no `refund_no` on `payments.models.Refund`."*

⚠⚠ **AND THE RULING ITSELF IS NOT NEW — IT WAS ALREADY MADE TWO DAYS EARLIER AND
THE PO HAS NOW BEEN ASKED THE SAME THING TWICE. THAT IS HARD-WON LAW 13, AND IT
IS OURS, NOT THEIRS.** `OQ-PAY-12605` was **CLOSED on 2026-09-23** on the PO's
words *"(a) Its own series, RFD-26-0001"* — the same question, the same answer,
with the seeded default already ruled as **`RFD-{YY}-{0000}`, day one
`RFD-26-0001`**. **The two answers agree**, which is luck rather than process:
law 13's whole warning is that a human answering twice from memory will
eventually answer differently, and then the repo holds two genuine rulings that
contradict each other. **The PO's *"it is already there"* is them remembering
their own ruling of 2026-09-23, not describing a screen** — and they are right
that it was settled. What is missing is the BUILD.

**SO THE RECORD IS: the series is RULED and NOT BUILT.** The ruled default
`RFD-{YY}-{0000}` from `OQ-PAY-12605` stands and today's ruling re-confirms it;
nothing is re-decided here. The owed build is cited in three live places —
`refunds_and_credits.py`, `test_cr138_p4_4_p4_25_refund_reads.py` and
`refundsAndCreditsShared.tsx` — and **until today no register row tracked it**,
which is why it was invisible enough to be asked again.

⚠ **NOTHING IS BACKFILLED — HARD RULE 4.** Once a document number is issued it
can never be withdrawn, and a number never issued cannot be invented after the
fact. **Refunds already issued carry no number and keep none**; the series
applies to refunds issued from now on.

⚠ **WHAT THIS SIGNATURE DOES NOT COVER.** It covers that refunds get their own
series. It does **not** cover the format — that came from `OQ-PAY-12605` on
2026-09-23 — and it does **not** rule on backfilling, which hard rule 4 settles
without asking. **The PO was not told that the series does not yet exist on
their screen, because the ruling arrived with that belief already in it; they
should be told.**

### RULING 4 — NO QUICKBOOKS OR XERO FILE IS AVAILABLE — `OQ-LED-12635` CLOSED AS ACCEPTED RISK

**PO, verbatim, 2026-09-25:** *"no"* — answering whether they can give us a
sandbox account or one real exported file.

⚠ **THIS IS NOT A RESOLUTION AND MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS ONE. THE PO DECLINED TO
SUPPLY THE INPUT, SO THE QUESTION IS CLOSED AND THE RISK IS ACCEPTED, NOT
ABSENT.**

**The consequence, written plainly because this is exactly the sentence that
gets lost:** *we generate the hand-over file and it has never been imported into
QuickBooks or Xero. The first person to find out whether it works will be a
customer at month end.*

**The worked case as it was put:** July's hand-over is **$15,066.00 across ten
accounts**. If Xero reads our *Amount* column as all-positive, the ten lines do
not cancel and Xero refuses the file — noisy and safe. If it reads our account
code column as a NAME instead, it may create ten new accounts called *79*, *80*,
*84* and so on, post the money into them, and report a balanced month — which
looks right on every screen either side. **Two of the four files are
unaffected**: the plain spreadsheet is our own columns and the QuickBooks Desktop
IIF file uses a format this product already writes and already tests. **The
QuickBooks Online and Xero column layouts are the two written from each
company's published import template and never tried against the real thing.**

⚠ **WHAT THIS SIGNATURE DOES NOT COVER.** The PO ruled only that they cannot
supply a sandbox or a real exported file. They did **not** rule that the two
layouts are correct, that the feature should ship as it is, or that no warning
belongs anywhere — and **the risk does not expire**. It is closed as accepted
and it re-opens the moment anyone gets hold of a real file or a real login.

## 2026-09-25 — **WHAT A UTILITY STILL OWES A TAX AUTHORITY IS A BALANCE, NOT THE WINDOW'S DELTA** (lane TAX, `DEF-LED-6705`)

**What the Product Owner saw**, on deployed **v2.351.84**, tenant *Ottumwa Water
Works*, Finance → Taxes & Remittance, period 01-Sep to 30-Sep: the *By authority*
table footed to **Still owed −$65.00**, and eight lines below it on the same
screen *Ties out to the books → Tax payable in the ledger* said **$266.75**.
Their words were *"in taxes no taxes are shown."*

**Both figures were computed honestly and they were answering different
questions.** `rows[].outstanding_billed` was `billed − remitted` over the
**requested window**; `tie_out.tax_payable_gl` was `gl_totals(end=end)` with
`start` left `None`, so **inception-to-date**. The code beside the tie-out
asserted they could not disagree — *"both are summed from the same rows here,
which is the point — one derivation cannot drift from itself"* — and that is
hard-won law 1 exactly: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee.

**THE RULING, AND IT IS OURS TO MAKE RATHER THAN THE PO'S (hard-won law 13):
the BALANCE is the true number and the delta was the wrong one.** `BR-LED-007`
is already signed — *"tax payable = remittance outstanding"* — and a July bill
does not stop being owed because the report window starts in September. The
delta also could not see two movements the books carry and no column of that
table names: a **credit note** debiting the liability, and a **remittance
settling tax billed before the window**, which is what drove *Still owed*
negative (`DEF-LED-6708`). Nothing here overturns a signed figure, so it did not
go to the PO; it makes the code obey a rule it was already contradicting.

**Measured, on the seeded tenant (`sbh_clone_taxlane`, template
`sbh_tpl_finwire`), before and after:**

| window | rows sum to | tie-out says | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-01 → 30 (no postings in it) | **$0.00** | **$600.26** | both **$600.26** |
| 2026-07-01 → 31 (holds the postings) | **$262.06** | **$259.36** | both **$259.36** |

The **$2.70** July gap is a credit note — proof that the disagreement was never
only about the window.

**Both figures are now taken from one `balance_to_date` dict**, so the screen
cannot print two answers to one question again, and
`06-backend/tests/test_def_led_6705_tie_out_foots.py` pins **both** the equality
and the **absolute** figure (LE-3's signed **20.97**), because a tie-out
assertion with no absolute number beside it is true by construction and is the
*check that cannot fail* shape this repo files one defect in eight for.

⚠ **WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, STATED SO THE NEXT LANE DOES NOT ASSUME IT DID.**
`outstanding_collected` is **still a window figure**, deliberately. A
collected-basis balance is *collected to date − remitted to date*, and
collected-to-date means apportioning every payment the utility has ever cleared
across every bill it has ever issued —
`payments_seam.collected_tax_by_invoice` takes the invoice ids as a **tuple**,
so at the top of the ICP that is one call carrying every bill of every month,
which is `NFR-3`'s shape. **Nothing renders it**: the *Still owed* column and its
footer both draw the billed basis, the one `BR-LED-007` ties to the books. It
needs a seam that takes a **window** rather than a bill list.

⚠ **AND A SIGN DISAGREEMENT IS LEFT OPEN AND UNTOUCHED.** The PO also reported
the General ledger → Balance trial balance closing `2200-01` at **−$266.75**
while this screen states the same liability as **+$266.75**. The tie-out shows a
liability as a positive net credit; the trial balance shows it negative. That is
the **General ledger** tab, which lane **BAL** holds, so this lane did not touch
it — but the two screens state one account's balance with opposite signs and
somebody must rule which convention the product uses.

## 2026-09-25 — **A PROTECTION WARNS THE CLERK; IT NEVER STOPS THEM** (lane PROT, closes `OQ-680`, mints `BR-CUS-1096`)

⚠ **THIS IS ONE OF FIVE RULINGS OF ONE PRINCIPLE, NOT A LOCAL EXCEPTION — AMENDED 2026-09-25 (lane RECON).**
The principle: **the product tells the clerk what is true and does not stop them acting.** The other
four were ruled the same day and are recorded in the section *"FOUR MORE RULINGS OF ONE PRINCIPLE"*
at the end of this file: **`BR-CUS-1097`** (reconnection shows what is still owed and never requires
it clear) · **`BR-CUS-1098`** (an occupant's protection does not block a cut of the master account) ·
**`BR-CUS-1099`** (no recorded proof of certified service warns, it does not refuse the schedule) ·
**`BR-CUS-1100`** (the block on new service marks the ACCOUNT and the CUSTOMER, never the address).
**A sixth case of this shape is the principle applying again, not a new question to raise**
(hard-won law 13), and **friction before proceeding has now been declined FOUR times** — option C
below, and again on each of the three protection/reconnect rulings.

⚠ **THIS IS ONE OF FOUR RULINGS OF ONE PRINCIPLE, NOT A LOCAL EXCEPTION — AMENDED 2026-09-25 (lane RECON).** The
principle: **the product tells the clerk what is true and does not stop them acting.** The other
three were ruled the same day and are recorded in the section *"THREE MORE RULINGS OF ONE
PRINCIPLE"* at the end of this file: **`BR-CUS-1097`** (reconnection shows what is still owed and
never requires it clear) · **`BR-CUS-1098`** (an occupant's protection does not block a cut of the
master account) · **`BR-CUS-1099`** (no recorded proof of certified service warns, it does not
refuse the schedule). **A fifth case of this shape is the principle applying again, not a new
question to raise** (hard-won law 13), and **friction before proceeding has now been declined FOUR
times** — option C below, and again on each of the other three.




**THE RULING, VERBATIM.** Product Owner, 2026-09-25:

> *"so please show the warining - but dont stop clark from doing his work; we
> have to tell there is an issue but we ant stop them"*

**THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS.** On the disconnect wizard, when a protection is in
force on an account — a **medical certificate**, a **weather moratorium**, an
**active payment plan** — does the product **stop** the clerk scheduling a cut,
or only **warn** them? That is `OQ-680` (*"which conditions must BLOCK a
transfer or a disconnect, and which merely warn?"*), raised 2026-08-27 from
`DEF-744` and open for 29 days.

**THE ANSWER: WARN, NEVER BLOCK.** A protection in force is **shown** to the
clerk and the clerk may proceed. Nothing about a protection prevents a clerk
from doing their work.

### WHAT WAS PUT TO THEM, AND WHAT THEY DECLINED

A signature covers only what was shown (PO 2026-08-11), so what was shown is
written out here rather than left to be inferred.

| | Option | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **The product REFUSES the schedule while a protection is in force** — what the code does today | **DECLINED** |
| **B** | **The product WARNS and the clerk proceeds** | ✅ **CHOSEN** |
| **C** | A middle path — the clerk may override, but must **type a reason** first | **DECLINED** |

**THE CONCERN WAS SHOWN EXPLICITLY AND THE RULING WAS MADE OVER IT.** The PO was
told, in plain English, that in much of North America a **medical certificate or
a weather moratorium is LAW, not process**, and that a recorded protection is a
different kind of fact from a ticked checklist — a household on a doctor's
certificate is one a regulator says may not be cut, and the product would be
letting a clerk cut it. They ruled against blocking anyway, and they ruled
against option **C** as well: *"we ant stop them"* rules out anything the clerk
must supply before proceeding, so **a typed reason is NOT a requirement and must
not be built as one.**

### THE CONSEQUENCE — THE PART THAT WILL BE FORGOTTEN

This is not a second decision. It is what makes *"warn but do not stop"* a
defensible position six months later at a hearing, and it follows from the
ruling rather than qualifying it.

**If nothing blocks, the RECORD OF THE OVERRIDE is the only protection that
exists** — for the customer and for the utility. So the product must capture,
**automatically and without asking the clerk for anything**:

1. **which protections were in force** at the moment of the act, by kind, with
   their dates;
2. **that the clerk was shown the warning**;
3. **who proceeded**;
4. **when**.

All four are captured by the product, not supplied by the person. Hard rule 7
already puts a money act in `audit_log`; this is the same shape for an act that
takes away a household's supply.

⚠ **AND THE HONEST BUILD IS SILENCE ON SCREEN ABOUT THE RECORD-KEEPING.** B14
rule 33 puts RATIONALE at **zero words on screen**. The warning states the fact
— which protection, and its dates — and says nothing about being recorded, and
nothing about why the product permits this.

### WHAT THE CODE DOES TODAY, MEASURED — IT BLOCKS, AND THAT IS NOW THE GAP

Measured on the pinned tip, `06-backend/apps/customers/disconnects.py`:

* `schedule_cut` calls `_require_running(..., for_cut=True)`;
* `_require_running` calls `halt_reason`, which calls `protection_check` and
  returns `HALT_PROTECTED` — *"the ladder is FROZEN by a protection in force"* —
  the moment any of the three is in force;
* `_require_running` raises `DisconnectRuleError`, so **the schedule is refused.**

So today the product does option **A**, which the PO has just declined. **This
lane records and does not build** — the wiring is a separate commitment and is
named in the report to the coordinator. Nothing here changes behaviour.

⚠ **AND `schedule_cut`'s DOCSTRING CLAIMED THE REFUSAL CAME FROM THE WRONG
GUARD** — *"Calls `assert_cut_reachable` first … so a protected account and a
closed account are each refused"*. `assert_cut_reachable` checks a **closed
account** and a **collections sequence** and reads no protection at all; the
refusal is `_require_running`'s. Hard-won law 1 — a comment claiming a guarantee
is not the guarantee. Corrected in this commit.

### WHAT THIS RULING DOES **NOT** TOUCH, STATED SO NOBODY ASSUMES IT DID

* **The automatic ladder is untouched.** `HALT_PROTECTED` freezing the *unattended*
  dunning ladder — reminders, notices, the certified final letter — is a machine
  declining to act, not a clerk being stopped. The PO's words are about a person
  (*"dont stop clark from doing his work"*). **The ladder halt stands as signed**
  and needs its own ruling to move.
* **`BR-CWP-091`** (*"a hold stops a disconnection, not the debt"*) is a portal
  rule about what a hold does to the DEBT and is not re-opened here, but its
  first clause now reads against this ruling and **must be re-stated by whoever
  owns it** — reported, not edited by this lane.
* **Recording a protection is unchanged.** `record_protection`'s three lifetimes,
  its refusal of a fourth kind, and every date rule on it stand exactly as signed.
