## 2026-09-25 — A TABLE'S TOTAL IS SUMMED FROM THE TABLE, NEVER BORROWED FROM A NEIGHBOURING KPI (lane REV, `DEF-LED-6717`)

The Product Owner, walking deployed **v2.351.84** on *Finance → Revenue & AR →
Services*, photographed one row reading **Total billed $50.00** above a **Total**
line reading **$0.00**, beside a *Billed this month* tile also reading **$0.00**.

**Neither figure was wrong, which is the whole lesson.** The rows sum movement on
the tenant's REVENUE accounts (`reporting.revenue_by_service`); the Total line
printed `kpis.billed`, which sums **AR DEBITS from invoice-sourced entries**. On
books written entirely by the bill run those are one sum seen from two sides, so
every fixture in the repo agreed with itself by accident and every test passed.
They part the moment money is posted by hand.

**Reproduced on real PostgreSQL before any code was read** (`10-scripts`-free,
a clone of `sbh_tpl_finwire`): one manual entry through `posting.post` crediting
revenue `50.0000` and debiting AR `50.0000` with `source_type='manual'` gives
`revenue_by_service` one row of `50.00` and `kpis.billed` of `0` — the PO's own
photograph, to the cent.

**THE RULING TAKEN, and it is ours to take rather than the PO's** (hard-won law
13 — a judgment recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is
the failure to make one): **the ROWS are right and the TOTAL LINE was wrong.** A
total under a table is a statement about the rows a person is being shown, so it
is summed from them — over the whole FILTERED set, with the page windowing only
what is drawn. That is CLAUDE.md's own `NFR-3` resolution of this shape, already
applied to the Aging view, and the Billed TILE is left saying exactly what it
always said.

**WORKED, both ways, so the difference is on the record rather than inferable.**
Moving the same screen to August 2026 through its new period filter:

| | figure | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| Billed this month (tile) | **$17,385.30** | Σ AR debits on invoice-sourced entries |
| Revenue by service (rows) | **$17,044.40** | Σ movement on revenue accounts |
| difference | **$340.90** | tax — credited to a tax-payable account, never to revenue |

Measured in the clone: `asset debit 17385.30 = revenue credit 17044.40 +
liability credit 340.90`. **Both numbers are correct and they are still not the
same number**, because the table's Tax column is a stated absence
(`per_service_tax_and_collected_columns`: a tax line carries no `service`
dimension). **This is reported and NOT reconciled** — nothing on the screen
connects the tile to the table, so a reader can still read the two as
disagreeing, and closing that is a copy decision with the PO rather than a sum.

**Money arithmetic on the client needed a decision too.** Hard rule 2 gives a
subtotal no exemption from *never float*, so `components/moneyMath.ts` adds in
`BigInt` at the scale it is handed. Its first draft refused anything past four
decimals and threw on the first real response it met — the wire serves six, out
of `NUMERIC(18,6)` — which is hard-won law 7's *incapable of passing* wearing
the costume of strictness, and is recorded here because the next lane reaching
for a money sum will reach for `Number()`.

**What is NOT decided here:** whether a revenue line must carry its dimensions at
all, and whether the manual entry should refuse one that does not, is
`OQ-LED-12629` — OPEN and with the Product Owner. The catch-all row is now a
deliberate, labelled absence rather than what grouping happened to leave behind,
and nothing in this commit picks one of its three options.
⚠ **PAIRED WITH THE RECONNECTION RULING OF THE SAME DAY, DIRECTLY BELOW
(`BR-CUS-1097`).** Two independent decisions, **one principle**. Read them
together: whoever finds only one of them cannot tell a local exception from a
pattern, and will guess.

## 2026-09-25 — **THE BALANCE NEED NOT BE CLEAR TO RECONNECT — SHOW WHAT IS OWED AND LET THE CLERK PROCEED** (lane PROT, mints `BR-CUS-1097`, SUPERSEDES half of `BR-CUS-104`)

**THE RULING, VERBATIM.** Product Owner, 2026-09-25, choosing option **(a)** of
two put to them:

> *"Show what's still owed and let the clerk proceed"*

**THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS.** On reconnection, **must the balance be clear before
a clerk can restore service?**

**THE ANSWER: NO.** The screen shows what is still owed — **the arrears plus the
reconnection fee, and what has been paid against them** — and the clerk proceeds
anyway. Nothing blocks.

### THE WORKED CASE PUT TO THEM

**Brett Calloway owes $1,204.50 plus the reconnection fee. He pays $400.00 and
agrees a plan for the rest. The clerk restores water the same day.**

### THE ALTERNATIVE, DECLINED

| | Option | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| **a** | **Show what is still owed and let the clerk proceed** | ✅ **CHOSEN** |
| **b** | **Require the balance to be clear before reconnecting** — what the code does today | **DECLINED** |

⚠ **AND NO FRICTION IS TO BE ADDED IN ITS PLACE.** No typed reason, no
tick-to-acknowledge, no supervisor. **The PO has now declined that twice in one
day** — here, and on the protections ruling above.

### ⚠ IT SUPERSEDES A SIGNED RULE, AND THE SUPERSESSION IS STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**`BR-CUS-104` is CONFIRMED (PO 2026-08-25, closing `OQ-381`)** and says, in as
many words: *"a customer must clear the arrears PLUS the fee before
`mark_reconnecting` will accept them"*, worked as `A-11340` clearing
**$8,315.00**.

**SPLIT IT IN TWO, BECAUSE ONLY ONE HALF MOVES:**

* **THE FEE'S TIMING IS UNTOUCHED.** The reconnection fee still lands **AT THE
  CUT**, it is still a real receivable raised by `commit_cut`, and `A-11340`'s
  position is still **$8,315.00** and not $8,240.00. `BR-CUS-105` (a cut
  account's balance is static) is unaffected.
* **THE GATE IS GONE.** *"must clear … before `mark_reconnecting` will accept
  them"* is **SUPERSEDED**. $8,315.00 is now what the clerk is **SHOWN**, not
  what they must collect first.

`DSC-02.4`'s drawn line *"Block new service elsewhere until it is settled"* is
the drawing, and B14 rule 41 sends a drawing that contradicts a signed rule to
the PO. **It went, and this is the answer.**

### ⚠ AND IT PULLS A DERIVATION OUT FROM UNDER `OQ-1170`

`OQ-1170`'s closing note settles *what status a restored account returns to* by
**deriving** it: *"`mark_reconnecting` refuses with `not_settled` while the
account owes … so a case reaches RECONNECTING → RESTORED only once the balance
is clear; the debt that would justify `Marked disconnect` cannot exist at that
point."* **That premise is now false** — a restored account CAN owe money. The
CONCLUSION (a restored account returns to the billable status it held before the
cut) is not reversed here and is not re-opened; what is gone is the argument
that made it safe. **Whoever next touches restored status must re-argue it on
its own facts and not on this derivation** — a justification by reference
outlives the justification.

### THE CONSEQUENCE — THE SAME ONE, AND IT FOLLOWS FROM THE RULING

**If nothing blocks, the record is the only protection there is.** At reconnect
the product must capture **automatically, without asking the clerk for
anything**:

1. **what was still owed** at the moment service was restored;
2. **what had been paid** against it;
3. **who restored it**;
4. **when**.

**Reconnecting on a payment plan is normal practice; reconnecting with no record
of what was outstanding is how a dispute six months later has no answer.**

⚠ **AND NONE OF THIS IS EXPLAINED ON SCREEN** (B14 rule 33 — rationale is zero
words). The screen states the figures; it says nothing about why it lets the
clerk through.

### WHY THE TWO RULINGS OF 2026-09-25 BELONG TOGETHER

**One principle: the product TELLS THE CLERK WHAT IS TRUE AND DOES NOT STOP THEM
ACTING** — and, because nothing stops them, **the product records what was true
at the moment they acted.** A protection warns and never blocks (`BR-CUS-1096`);
an unpaid balance is shown and never blocks (`BR-CUS-1097`). They were ruled
independently, hours apart, on unrelated screens. **A lane that finds one of them
alone will read it as a local exception.** Cross-referenced both ways here, in
both business rules, and in the code.

### WHAT THE CODE DOES TODAY, MEASURED — IT BLOCKS

`disconnects.reconnect_blockers` returns a **`not_settled`** refusal whenever
`balance > 0`, quoting `DSC-02.4`; `reconnection_readiness` reports
`ready: False`; and `mark_reconnecting` refuses. So the product does option
**(b)**, which the PO has just declined. **This lane records and does not build**
— the reconnect design is PAUSED at the PO's instruction until they have seen the
current screens.

## 2026-09-25 — **THE CLOSE & EXPORT FILTER BAR, AND TWO THINGS THAT LOOK BROKEN AND ARE NOT** (lane CLOSE, `DEF-LED-6728`, `DEF-LED-6730`, `DEF-LED-6733`)

**The Product Owner, on deployed `v2.351.84`, tenant Ottumwa Water Works:**
*"on close and export screen - filter is not align - it is not in 1 line."*

### The judgment, and it is about WHERE the fix goes rather than what it is

Twenty screens in this product hand-roll `flex flex-wrap items-end gap-N` around
a few kit fields. `items-end` aligns the BOTTOM of each field's box, so the
moment ONE field in a row carries a sentence under its control — a help line, or
the IS-8 regional date echo — that field's label and control are pushed up by the
height of the sentence and the row becomes two rows. Measured in Chromium at
1440px: date label top **334** / input **357**; select label **356** / input
**380**; `Apply` **377**. Three heights in one row.

**The choice was between fixing this bar and fixing this SHAPE.** B14 rule 43
settles it — a piece of UI is a component, and a bar aligned by hand on one
screen is not reuse — so the fix is `07-frontend/src/components/FilterRow.tsx`,
the one place a horizontal band of filter controls and its trailing action is
laid out, and the Export band is its first caller. Every other screen carrying
this latent defect can now adopt it instead of each discovering it.

**The mechanism is top alignment, not a margin.** The row aligns from the TOP, so
the baseline a control sits on no longer depends on anything BELOW it: a required
marker is inline in the label, a help or echo line is under the control, and
neither is in the flow that decides where the control sits. Whether a field has
them stops being a layout question. The action reserves an empty `.field-label`
slot rather than taking an offset — the first draft used a `<span>` and measured
**1px** high, because the kit states the label's bottom margin twice
(`.field-label` 4px, `.field > label` 5px, the second winning on specificity), so
the slot is a real `<label>` inside a `.field` and its height is the kit's.

### Why nothing in this repo could see it, which is the part worth keeping

`brazosbend` seeds `MM/DD/YYYY` — **exactly what a headless Chromium draws inside
a native date input** — so `regionalDateEcho` returns `null`, the echo never
renders, and the bar measures perfectly aligned in every test and in every
screenshot this repo has ever taken of this screen. Six of the seven formats show
it. Hard-won law 6 says to look; this says **looking is necessary and not
sufficient — you have to look at the tenant who complained.** The defect
reproduced only after setting the fixture's `date_format` to `DD-MMM-YY`.

### TWO THINGS ON THE SAME SCREEN THAT LOOK BROKEN AND ARE NOT — RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-INVESTIGATES

**1 · *CODE IN YOUR PACKAGE* reading `Not available` on every row is HONEST.**
The API serves `target_ref: null` on every row — **served and empty, not
unserved.** Every `ledger_accounts.qbo_ref` and `.xero_ref` in the tenant is
blank, which is what the Chart tab shows too, and that is precisely what blocks
the hand-over (`BR-LED-014`). The screen proves itself: the **Codes set** gate
goes ✗ for QuickBooks Online and Xero and ✓ for the two file formats, because
`REF_FIELD_BY_TARGET` maps `csv` and `iif` to `None`. **Nothing to fix, and
inventing codes would defeat the gate that exists to stop a half-mapped export.**
What IS wrong is narrow and is filed as `DEF-LED-6733`: under `csv` and `iif` the
cell still says *"no code set"* although no code could ever be set there, so the
column and the gate disagree on one screen.

**2 · The Close button's two refusals are now DISTINCT, and both are true.**
Proved in all four combinations rather than the one that was reported:

| Who | Month | Close button | Reason shown |
|---|---|---|---|
| System Admin | closed | disabled | *The month is closed.* |
| System Admin | open | **enabled** | — |
| Executive | closed | disabled | *The month is closed.* |
| Executive | open | disabled | *Your role cannot close an accounting period.* |

The STATE is asked first and the ROLE second, which is the order a clerk meets
them. The role sentence is still there and is still TRUE when it appears — which
was the whole of `DEF-LED-6668`, where a System Admin who had just closed
September was told their role was at fault.

### And a mistake this lane made, recorded because the shape generalises

`DEF-LED-6730`: this lane's own push helper re-stamps its OWN register row with
the version it has just allocated, and selected that row with an id prefix **AND
a phrase from the prose** — `b"params band" in ln`. `DEF-LED-6701` contains the
words *params band* entirely legitimately (the Finance blueprint p023 lists the
Balance screen's sections and one of them is a params band), so the helper
rewrote **another lane's row**, changing which build the PO had reported it on.
Repaired by splicing one line's bytes. **A shared register is addressed BY ID and
never by a phrase out of its prose — prose is another lane's to write, and it
will one day contain your search string.** Found by law 11's arithmetic: the
numstat said *2 insertions, 1 deletion* where a pure append is 1 and 0.

## 2026-09-25 — **FOUR MORE RULINGS OF ONE PRINCIPLE: THE PRODUCT TELLS THE CLERK WHAT IS TRUE AND DOES NOT STOP THEM ACTING** (lane RECON, mints `BR-CUS-1098`, `BR-CUS-1099`, `BR-CUS-1100`; `BR-CUS-1097` was minted for the same day's reconnect ruling by lane PROT and is cited, not duplicated)

⚠ **READ THIS FIRST: THERE ARE NOW FIVE RULINGS AND THEY ARE ONE PRINCIPLE, NOT
FIVE EXCEPTIONS — PLUS ONE OPEN RECOMMENDATION THAT IS NOT A RULING AND IS MARKED AS SUCH.** A lane that finds one of them alone must be able to tell
which it is, so each names the other three:

| | Ruling | Rule | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | A **protection** warns the clerk and never refuses the act | `BR-CUS-1096` | decision log 2026-09-25 (lane PROT), `OQ-680` CLOSED |
| **2** | **Reconnection** shows what is still owed and never requires it clear | `BR-CUS-1097` | **lane PROT's own section in this file** — cited here, not duplicated |
| **3** | An **occupant's** protection does not block a cut of the **master** account | `BR-CUS-1098` | this section |
| **4** | **No recorded proof of certified service** warns; it does not refuse the schedule | `BR-CUS-1099` | this section |
| **5** | The block on new service marks the **ACCOUNT and the CUSTOMER**, never the address | `BR-CUS-1100` | this section |
| **—** | ⚠ **NOT A RULING.** What applying the deposit should do — **a recommendation PUT TO THE PO AND AWAITING THEIR ANSWER** | *none — no rule may be minted for it* | this section |

**The principle, stated once:** *the product tells the clerk what is true and
does not stop them acting.* Four separate questions, four separate PO answers on
one day, all the same shape. **A sixth case of this shape is the principle
applying again, not a new question to raise** (hard-won law 13).

**AND THE SAME CONSEQUENCE FOLLOWS FROM ALL FOUR, ONCE:** if nothing blocks,
**the RECORD is the only protection there is.** The product captures it
**automatically and asks the clerk for nothing** — no typed reason, no
tick-to-acknowledge, no supervisor. ⚠ **THE PO HAS NOW DECLINED FRICTION-BEFORE-
PROCEEDING FOUR TIMES** (option C on `BR-CUS-1096`, and again on each of the
three below). **A pattern declined four times is not to be re-proposed.** And
none of this reasoning appears on screen (B14 rule 33 — rationale is zero words).

---

### RULING 2 · **RECONNECTION SHOWS WHAT IS STILL OWED AND THE CLERK PROCEEDS** (`BR-CUS-1097` — **recorded by lane PROT; see its own section in this file**)

⚠ **TWO LANES RECORDED THIS RULING INDEPENDENTLY WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THAT IS
WORTH ONE LINE OF ITS OWN.** Lane PROT minted **`BR-CUS-1097`** and wrote the
full section *"THE BALANCE NEED NOT BE CLEAR TO RECONNECT"* above; lane RECON was
given the same ruling by the coordinator and had drafted the same rule. **`BR-CUS-1097`
is the id and PROT's section is the record** — this lane deleted its duplicate
rather than publish a second rule for one decision, which is how a register
acquires two genuine answers to one question (hard-won law 13).

**The ruling, for a reader arriving here:** PO 2026-09-25, option (a) of two —
*"Show what's still owed and let the clerk proceed"*. Option (b), **require the
balance clear before reconnecting**, was put to them and **DECLINED**. Worked
case: **Brett Calloway owes $1,204.50 plus the reconnection fee, pays $400.00,
agrees a plan for the rest, and the clerk restores water the same day.** The
consequence is the one shared by all five rulings below. **What the code does
today is the opposite** — `reconnect_blockers` appends `not_settled` whenever
`balance > ZERO` and `mark_reconnecting` raises it, so Brett is refused;
**`DEF-CUS-6735`**.

### RULING 3 · **AN OCCUPANT'S PROTECTION DOES NOT BLOCK A CUT OF THE MASTER ACCOUNT** (`BR-CUS-1098`)

**TWO THINGS ARRIVED TOGETHER AND THEY ARE RECORDED SEPARATELY**, because one is
a confirmation of a table and the other is an answer to a direct question.

#### 3a · The table, confirmed in full

**PO, 2026-09-25, verbatim:** *"this si correct you should ocnsider these while
building"* — confirming, as a whole, the table below of **how a master account
differs from a regular one in disconnect and reconnect**.

The three rules this rests on are **cited, not restated**: a master account is
the owner's account at an address and need not name a unit (**`BR-CUS-1010`**);
an occupying account is its child (**`BR-CUS-171`**); a sub-account's unpayable
residue transfers up to it (**`BR-CUS-097`**).

| | Regular account | Master account |
|---|---|---|
| **What gets cut** | One unit's services | **A building.** A cut hits common supply and can affect occupants who owe nothing |
| **Who is affected** | The account holder | **The owner and every occupying account under them** |
| **Protections** | Checked against one household | **Checked against EVERY OCCUPANT** |
| **The debt** | What that account owes | **Their own plus residue transferred up from sub-accounts** (`BR-CUS-097`) |
| **Reconnect** | One visit, one address | **May need several** — common supply plus each affected unit |
| **The work order** | One | **One per affected SERVICE POINT** |

**AND WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE FOUR STEPS, confirmed in the same message:**

* **Step 1** carries **one line** — *"Master account · 25 occupying accounts"*.
  **That single line is the whole warning.**
* **Step 2**'s protections table gets **a row per occupying account that has a
  protection**, not only the master's own.
* **Step 3**'s field-work table gets **a row per affected SERVICE POINT** rather
  than per service — which may be twenty-five.
* **Step 4** names **WHO LOSES SUPPLY** rather than only what the account owes,
  and shows **transferred residue separately** from the owner's own debt.

#### 3b · The question, asked separately and ANSWERED separately

The confirmed table contained the words *"one medical certificate downstairs
protects the whole building"*. **Those were our words in the question, not the
PO's**, and they are ambiguous between two very different things — that the
protection is **SHOWN** for the whole building, or that it **BLOCKS** a cut of
the whole building. So it was put to the PO directly.

**THE QUESTION:** *Can a clerk cut a master account while an occupant is
protected?* **THE ANSWER — option (a), verbatim:**

> *"Warn and let them proceed — consistent with your two rulings"*

**THE RULING: a protection held by an OCCUPANT does not block a cut of the
MASTER account. It is SHOWN to the clerk, who proceeds or does not.**

**THE WORKED CASE PUT TO THEM: 500 Main Street.** The owner owes **$14,390.00**
across **25 units**, and one tenant in **unit 12** holds a **medical
certificate**. **The clerk may cut.**

⚠ **WHAT MAKES THIS ONE DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHERS, AND IT WAS PUT TO THE PO IN
THESE TERMS BEFORE THEY RULED.** `BR-CUS-1096` and `BR-CUS-1097` are both about
**the person who owes the money**. **This one is about cutting off someone WHO
OWES NOTHING and has a certificate on file.** That distinction was shown
explicitly — that it is materially different from the other two — and the PO
ruled anyway. **A signature covers only what was shown (PO 2026-08-11), and what
was shown here includes the distinction.** It is written down because it is the
reason somebody will want to reverse this one day.

⚠ **AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS SHARPER HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE: FOR A MASTER
ACCOUNT, THE PEOPLE AFFECTED ARE NOT THE PEOPLE THE RECORD IS ABOUT.** So what
is captured at the moment of the cut must name **EVERY OCCUPYING ACCOUNT THAT
HELD A PROTECTION, by kind and by date** — not merely that the master's own
checks were seen. **The owner's case file is the only place a protected tenant
downstairs will ever appear.** That is not a new decision; it is the same
*capture automatically, ask the clerk for nothing* consequence as the other
three, applied to the case where it matters most.

---

### RULING 4 · **NO RECORDED PROOF OF CERTIFIED SERVICE WARNS; IT DOES NOT REFUSE THE SCHEDULE** (`BR-CUS-1099`)

**THE RULING, VERBATIM.** Product Owner, 2026-09-25:

> *"So we warn user , but we dont stop user - We can't send a certified notice —
> a final-tier cut isn't lawful without one"*

**WHAT IT RULES.** The disconnect wizard's step 3 today carries *"No proof, no
cut"* — a cut cannot be scheduled until proof of certified service is recorded.
**Under this ruling that becomes a WARNING, not a gate.** A clerk may schedule a
cut with **no proof of certified service recorded**. **The screen still asks for
it; it no longer refuses.**

⛔ **AND THIS ONE WAS VERIFIED IN THE CODE BEFORE IT WAS RECORDED, BECAUSE WHAT A
SCREEN SAYS AND WHAT THE CODE DOES ARE TWO FACTS** (hard-won law 1; the same
sentence pattern hid a real refusal twice on this branch today). **Measured on
the pinned tip**, `06-backend/apps/customers/disconnects.py`:

* `schedule_cut` calls **`assert_service_proved(case)`** (line ~3597); so does
  `commit_cut` (line ~4456);
* `assert_service_proved` reads `service_proof_for(case, tier=TIER_3)` and, when
  `proof["recorded"]` is false, **raises `DisconnectRuleError`** with code
  **`cut_on_unrecorded_service`** (`BR-CUS-100`);
* it raises a **second** refusal, **`tier_3_proof_not_certified`**
  (`BR-CUS-039`), when the recorded channel is not certified mail.

**So the product REALLY REFUSES — this is not a screen sentence over a permissive
service.** Both refusals are now against the ruling. The first is what the
ruling names; **the second is reported beside it rather than assumed**, because
the PO's words are about the ABSENCE of proof and say nothing about a notice
served by another channel. `assert_service_proved` does not read `signed_for_on`
and that question stays open exactly as it was. **The gap is filed as
`DEF-CUS-6736`.**

⚠ **WHAT MAKES THIS ONE DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHER THREE — IT REVERSES WHO THE
RECORD PROTECTS.** The first three are about **protections**: the record exists
to show the utility considered a **CUSTOMER'S** circumstances. **This one is a
legal precondition on the utility's OWN act.** A final-tier cut without proved
certified service is not merely unwise — it is a cut **the utility may not
lawfully have made**. So here **the record protects the UTILITY**, and its
absence is **the utility's own exposure** rather than the customer's. That
distinction was **not** put to the PO in those words; it is recorded as the
consequence of their ruling and **not as a caveat on it** — they have applied
this principle four times and the pattern is deliberate.

**WHAT MUST BE CAPTURED**, on the same *automatically, ask the clerk for nothing*
rule: **that no proof of certified service was recorded at the moment the cut was
scheduled**, **who** scheduled it, and **when**. For the other three the record
names what the clerk was told; **for this one it names what the utility could not
show.**

⚠ **AND THE PRODUCT GAP IS A SEPARATE FACT FROM THE RULING — STATE BOTH OR A
READER WILL THINK THE RULING FIXED IT.** **We cannot SEND a certified notice at
all.** The notice is served outside the product and its proof is typed in by a
person (`cut_date.py`, and `assert_service_proved`'s own docstring: *"a cut
authorised by this product's own claim to have delivered something would be
authorised by a column that is NULL on every row"*). **That limitation exists
today, is already filed, and is NOT what this ruling changes.** The ruling is
only about whether the **absence of proof blocks**.

---

### WHAT NONE OF THESE THREE TOUCH, STATED SO NOBODY ASSUMES THEY DID

* **Nothing was built.** The **disconnect rebuild and the reconnect panel are
  PAUSED at the PO's instruction** until they have seen the current screens.

### RULING 5 · **THE BLOCK ON NEW SERVICE MARKS THE ACCOUNT AND THE CUSTOMER — NEVER THE ADDRESS** (`BR-CUS-1100`, closes `OQ-384`)

**THE RULING, VERBATIM.** Product Owner, 2026-09-25:

> *"you ahve to mark account and Customer ID also"*

**THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS** is `OQ-384`, open since 2026-08-25 and never
answered: after a cut, the screen promises the account is *"blocked from taking
new service until settled"* — **but nobody had decided whether that means THIS
ACCOUNT, EVERY ACCOUNT THE CUSTOMER HOLDS, or EVERYBODY AT THE ADDRESS. Those
are three different products.**

**THE ANSWER: mark the ACCOUNT and mark the CUSTOMER. NOT the address.**

⚠ **THE SPLIT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, AND IT IS WHY THE PO CHOSE IT.**

* **Marking the CUSTOMER catches them applying for service at a DIFFERENT
  address.** The debt follows the debtor.
* **NOT marking the ADDRESS means a new tenant moving into that same unit is not
  punished for the previous occupant's debt.**

**That is the difference between CHASING A DEBTOR and BLACKLISTING A PROPERTY,
and the PO chose the first.** A lane that "helpfully" adds a premises-level mark
reverses a ruling.

⛔ **AND THE HOLE IT CLOSES IS LIVE TODAY: THE SCREEN PROMISES A BLOCK AND
NOTHING ENFORCES IT.** This was **verified in the code, not inferred from a
failed search.** Measured on the pinned tip:

* `disconnects.new_service_block_for(account_id)` **computes** the block and is
  deliberately **three-valued** (`None` when AR is unreadable, because a failed
  reading is not a clearance);
* the module names its own gap in a constant —
  **`NEW_SERVICE_BLOCK_UNCONSUMED`**: *"the block is COMPUTED here and read by
  nothing … so a customer cut at one address can take service at another
  today"*;
* **the only callers are `tests/test_w7_cut_reconnect.py` and one API docstring
  in `transfer_disconnect_api.py`.** No move-in, service-request or
  account-creation path calls it. A grep test in that file asserts the absence
  on purpose.

**So a customer cut for non-payment can sign up again immediately and nobody
would know.** That is **not a design gap — it is a promise the product makes and
does not keep** (hard-won law 2).

⚠ **TWO CONSEQUENCES RECORDED AS OUR READING, OPEN TO CHEAP REVERSAL — THE PO
HAS BEEN TOLD WE WILL BUILD THESE UNLESS THEY SAY OTHERWISE. THEY ARE NOT
RULINGS.**

1. **The mark WARNS; it does not refuse.** A new-service request from a marked
   customer **shows the clerk what is outstanding and the clerk decides.** That
   is **the fifth application of the same principle** and follows automatically
   from the other four.
2. **"Settled" includes an AGREED PAYMENT PLAN, not only a zero balance.** The
   PO has already ruled (`BR-CUS-1097`) that a clerk may reconnect on a plan; if
   a plan did not clear the mark, **the two rules would contradict each other.**
   They have been asked to correct this if it is wrong.

---

### ⚠ NOT A RULING · **WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A CLERK APPLIES THE DEPOSIT — A RECOMMENDATION PUT TO THE PO AND AWAITING THEIR ANSWER**

⚠ ⚠ **THIS IS NOT A DECISION AND NO RULE ID IS MINTED FOR IT.** The PO asked
*"What we should do when clark chose it"*, we answered, and **they have not
replied.** It is recorded here so the reasoning survives (hard-won law 10) and
**kept visibly distinct from the five rulings above, because a recommendation
recorded as a ruling is how a decision nobody made becomes law.**

**WHAT WAS PUT TO THEM — applying the deposit should MOVE THE MONEY.** The
deposit is **the customer's money held as a liability**; applying it against
arrears **debits the deposit liability and credits what they owe, through the
ledger posting service** (hard rule 5 — only that service writes journal lines).

* **Worked:** a **$65.00** deposit against **Brett Calloway's $1,204.50** leaves
  **$1,139.50**, shown on screen **BEFORE the clerk commits**.
* **It posts AT THE CUT, not at restoration**, because that is when the
  reconnection figure is quoted — **and if the money has not moved, that figure
  is wrong.**
* **It cannot be undone.** A reversal is **a new correcting entry** (hard rule 4).

**ALSO PUT TO THEM AND ALSO UNANSWERED: what happens when the deposit EXCEEDS the
debt.** Recommended **(a)** apply only what the debt needs and keep the rest
held, over **(b)** apply all of it and leave the customer in credit.

**AND THE ALTERNATIVE OFFERED IF THEY DO NOT WANT THE MONEY TO MOVE: rename the
button** — because the choice genuinely does only one thing today: it decides
whether a **new deposit is required to reconnect**.

⛔ **THE CURRENT STATE IS A DEFECT, AND IT IS ALREADY FILED — CITED HERE RATHER
THAN FILED A SECOND TIME.** The button says ***"Apply it against the arrear"***,
the clerk reasonably tells the customer it has come off what they owe, and
**nothing moves — not then, not later, not ever.** That is **hard-won law 2 on a
money path**.

## 2026-09-25 — **THE CHART TAB IS ONE TABLE, AND AN ABSENCE THAT HAD NO ROW SURVIVED THE MERGE** (lane CHART, `DEF-LED-6715`)

**The PO, reading Finance → General ledger → Chart in build 2.351.90**, verbatim:
*"i will have 1 table only and i will use columns to manage rest of the table"*,
and of the four panels beneath the chart: *"cant we merge it in charts - first
table itself"*. Of the service→revenue map specifically: *"we are doing it in
settings -> accounting -> Charts of Accounts -> GL code mapping - it is already
available user will do it there"*.

**THE DRAWING ALREADY AGREED AND NOBODY HAD BUILT IT.** Finance blueprint p025
note 1 is marked **CHANGED**: *"Chart · was 'Chart of accounts & mapping'; the
mapping is columns ④, not a second name"*, and p024 draws ONE panel whose FIELDS
are `Code · Name · Type · Designation · Category · QuickBooks · Xero · State ·
Actions`. So there is no disagreement between the ruling and the drawing to
record — this row exists because the two AGREED and the product did neither.

### WHAT EACH PANEL BECAME

| Panel | Became | Why that is not a loss |
|---|---|---|
| What each kind of money lands in | the **Role in the books** column, which was already there | it printed `role → account`; the table carried the same fact per row |
| Tax authorities | a **Role filter** value | `2200-01`/`2200-02` are rows in the chart; p025: *"Designation is how 4·1 finds the tax accounts"* |
| Codes your accounting package knows | the **QuickBooks** and **Xero** columns, off by default, edited from the pencil | two values against the same rows; `PATCH /ledger/accounts/{id}` already took both |
| Where each service's revenue goes | nothing here — **Settings → Accounting → Mapping** | VERIFIED before deleting: `SettingsAccountingTab`'s `MappingPanel` draws every enabled service with its usage and base-charge accounts and a pencil per row |

### THE JUDGMENT THIS LANE HAD TO MAKE, AND IT IS THE REASON FOR THE ROW

**A column cannot carry an absence.** Three GL roles on the demo tenant have no
live account — `accrued_expenses`, `accumulated_depreciation`,
`allowance_doubtful_accounts` — and a posting that needs one refuses by name
(`BR-LED-796`). The deleted panel was the only surface that said so. **An
unfilled role has no account row**, so merging the panel into the table as asked
would have removed a true operational warning with every test still green —
hard-won law 2's mirror, an absence that stops being visible because the thing
that showed it was tidied away.

> ⚠ **CORRECTION, 2026-09-25, LANE CHARTFIX — ONE CLAUSE OF THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE
> IS FALSE AND IS LEFT STANDING SO THE RECORD SHOWS WHAT WAS BELIEVED.** *"a
> posting that needs one refuses by name (`BR-LED-796`)"* was never measured;
> it was inherited from the lane's brief and propagated to six surfaces.
> **Measured in `06-backend/apps/ledger/selectors.py`:
> `gl_account_for_designation` returns `None` for a recognised designation whose
> role has no live account, and raises `ValueError` ONLY for a designation NAME
> it does not recognise** — a distinction its own docstring argues for, because
> *"no account is designated accounts receivable"* and *"you asked for
> `accounts_recievable`"* are different problems. Both halves are already pinned
> by tests (`tests/test_us_led_005_chart_api.py` for the `None`,
> `tests/test_us_led_005_gl_designations.py` for the raise), so the claim was
> checkable the whole time and nobody checked it. `BR-LED-796` is the worked
> case of ONE caller that must refuse an unfilled role rather than substitute;
> it is not a fence across every designation.
>
> **THE DECISION THIS PARAGRAPH RECORDS IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOW BETTER
> FOUNDED.** The reason to keep the warning on screen was never that a posting
> would refuse loudly — it is that, since nothing central refuses, this screen
> is the only place the gap surfaces before month end. The false clause made the
> product sound SAFER than it is, which is the direction that costs most.
> Corrected in the wire contract, the panel, both test files and the browser
> walkthrough in the same commit; the prevention column of `DEF-LED-6715` moved
> with them.

**Decided here, not asked:** the absence becomes a **served count** beside the
Role filter and a **filter value** that lists the roles themselves. B14 rule 32
keeps the list CLOSED by default; rule 33 keeps the reason at zero words on
screen. Nothing was put to the PO, because nothing here contradicts a signed
rule — law 13.

**The count is SERVED and never derived.** `roles_needing_account` comes from
`selectors.designation_map()`. A screen deriving it from its own rows would
always find none, and would report all-clear over a real gap.

**It was four when the PO reported it and is three today** — `cash_over_short`
has an account now — which is exactly why nothing hardcodes the list.

### WHAT THIS COST, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE LESSON

Three faults reached the branch and **every one was found by looking at the
running product, none by a test** (hard-won law 6):

1. **The chart SEARCH was deleted by accident.** The commit adding the Role
   filter replaced a text anchor that happened to contain
   `chart_of_accounts`'s four search lines. `tsc`, 214 front-end cases and every
   ledger test passed, **because no case had ever asked this endpoint to find a
   row by name** — and a search returning everything looks exactly like a search
   with nothing excluded. Found by typing *cash* and counting: 130 rows where
   there should be 4.
2. **Choosing *Needs an account* blanked the whole panel, the count included.**
   The value went into the served query, so it changed the react-query key, so
   the panel fell to its skeleton for a round trip whose answer it did not need.
3. **The count badge pushed its own filter 20px out of line**, because
   `.fin-params-field` is a column flex and the badge was a second child. The
   DOM was correct; only the image showed it (B14 rule 44).

**And the walkthrough written to prove all this had the same disease three
times over** — it waited on a clock, then on a condition that was already true,
then for a button reading *Columns* over an icon disclosure — reporting a
working screen broken each time.

### WHAT WAS LEFT ALONE, STATED SO NOBODY ASSUMES IT WAS DONE

* **`GlServiceMapEditor.tsx` is on disk and now has no mount.** A sibling lane
  was editing it as this landed; taking the file out from under a live fix
  trades one defect for another. Filed, not done.
* **The `sections` prop is accepted and ignored.** Both values draw the same
  screen now. Its two callers lose it in their own commits.
* **`GET /ledger/accounts` is still unpaginated** and its docstring still argues
  why. That argument is the chart being bounded by the tenant's own chart rather
  than by transaction volume, which is a different claim from `/outstandings`'s
  withdrawn one — and p024 draws a pager this lane did not build. Not widened
  here: the maintenance process's step 3 is about not turning a reported fault
  into a redesign nobody asked for.
* **`GET /ledger/gl-mappings` is still served** and still read by Settings.

## 2026-09-25 · `DEF-LED-6723` — a journal entry opens (lane JE)

**CLASSIFIED AS A DEFECT AND NOT A CHANGE, AND THE REASON IS THE DRAWING.** The
maintenance process routes on one question — *can a user do this task in the
product today?* — and the answer was no, which on its face is BUILD. But
`04-docs/01-spec/11b-api-audit.md` line 436 has called S56 **"Journal list +
detail"** with two routes and *"lines expand to dimensions"* since the API
audit, and the Finance blueprint p020 item 7 draws the control in terms:
*"Row actions as icons · 👁 view · ↺ reverse"*. **Something specified and never
built is our miss**, and `13-change-process.md` §1 is explicit that filing our
misunderstanding as a change quietly converts our error into the customer's new
requirement. Filed as a defect.

**WHAT THE PRODUCT OWNER SAW**, on v2.351.84, tenant Ottumwa Water Works:
*"on this screen user is unable to see detail screen of Journal entry - we
cannot click on eye."*

**THE REFUSAL WAS TRUE, WHICH IS WHY THIS WAS NOT A WIRING FIX.** The eye was
VISIBLE AND DISABLED WITH ITS REASON under `BR-SHL-025` — the correct build of
a true refusal — because `ledger/journal-entries/<uuid>` was registered
DELETE-only, and **Django resolves by URL and not by method**, so the GET could
not be added anywhere without shadowing one of the two views. The gap was
written down in FOUR places and scheduled in none: `apps/ledger/api.py`'s
exception (1), which even named the read to write; the S56 spec row; the
screen's own comment; and the blueprint's gap register as **G3, ⛔, "no read —
journal_api.py is DELETE-only — no task — reported, not scheduled"**.

**THE JUDGMENT, WITH ITS WORKED FIGURE.** The lines READ is paged and the
entry's `debit`, `credit` and `balanced` are computed over the WHOLE entry in
SQL before the page is cut. That is `journal_entry_list`'s own `P1.8` lesson one
level in: derived from a page, a 120-line entry would report a different verdict
depending on where a clerk stopped scrolling, and it would still look right on
every fixture we have. **Measured on real PostgreSQL 16, demo books:** a 2 July
bill of **six lines** — Electric usage 95.50, Electric base 12.00, Water usage
39.50, Water base 8.00, Bexar County tax 3.10, all credit, against one debit to
1200 Accounts receivable of **158.10**; the five sum to 158.10 exactly.

**AN ENTRY WITH NO NUMBER SHOWS NO NUMBER.** An opening balance is not a
document and has none; a draft has none by `BR-LED-021`'s ruling; a posted entry
whose tenant has no series row has none for ever, because hard rule 4 freezes
the column at post. All three render as `—` and **nothing composes a number**,
because an invented one could never be withdrawn. Proved in a browser on a real
opening balance: two lines, **$402.15 against $402.15**, entry no. `—`.

**ONE ROLE DECISION, RECORDED BECAUSE IT COULD HAVE MOVED A RULING BY
ACCIDENT.** One path now carries two verbs with two different role answers
(`core.permissions.JournalEntryReadAnyDeleteAdminOrClerk`, the
`ConnectionsReadAnyWriteAdminOrClerk` shape). The READ is every tenant role,
which is what all four existing ledger reads already are — a detail an Executive
may not open, of a list they may read, would be an odd book. **The DELETE's role
set is copied UNCHANGED** from the `AdminOrClerk` it replaces on that verb: it
is the PO's closure of `OQ-175` on 2026-08-12 and is not this lane's to widen. A
case pins the two frozen together so a later widening of the read cannot move it.

**WHAT LOOKING FOUND THAT NO TEST DID.** The first build rendered *"NO ENTRY
NUMBER"* in the page eyebrow over a facts panel whose `Entry no.` row already
showed a `—` — the same absence stated twice, six lines apart, which is B14 rule
32's budget broken and the identical fault `RefundDetailPage` records against
its own kicker. Every test passed over it. It was found by reading the
screenshot, which is hard-won law 6, and the eyebrow is now empty where there is
no number.

## 2026-09-25 — **RECONNECTION BECOMES A SCREEN, AND TWO DESIGN CHOICES ARE OURS RATHER THAN THE PO's** (lane RECONNECT, `S148` · `US-CUS-032`; mints NO rule and NO question)

**WHAT WAS RULED ALREADY, AND IS BUILT TO RATHER THAN RE-ASKED** (hard-won law
13): `BR-CUS-1097` (the balance is shown and never blocks) and `BR-CUS-1098` (a
master's units come back together, residue transferred up is its own line, one
work order per affected service point). Both were signed by the PO earlier the
same day. **Nothing on this screen needed a ruling that had not been given**, so
no `BR` and no `OQ` was minted, which is the whole of law 13's instruction.

### What was reproduced first, before any code was read

Maintenance process, step 1. **Case `DSC-26-0005` on `A-11996`, owing $139.80**
— $64.80 of arrears plus the $75.00 reconnection fee. On the case record the
`Mark reconnecting` button renders **GREYED**, under the sentence *"Money is
still owed."* `disconnects.reconnect_blockers` appends `not_settled` whenever
`balance > ZERO` and `mark_reconnecting` raises the first blocker it is handed.
**`/brazosbend/reconnects` renders the app frame over nothing** — there is no
reconnect route anywhere. Both filed before anything was touched:
`DEF-CUS-6742` (the gate) and `DEF-CUS-6743` (the screen).

### The judgment that cost the most to get right, and it is arithmetic

**`outstanding_at_cut` ALREADY CONTAINS THE RECONNECTION FEE.** The column's own
docstring says so — *"the final metered bill raised at the cut, the reconnection
fee, and everything that was already outstanding"* — and `DEF-708` made the cut
raise the fee as a real charge precisely so the gate and the quote would be one
read. The first draft of the money table added the fee to it again to work out
what had been paid, and **reported $75.00 PAID on an account nobody had paid a
cent against**: a receipt for a payment that never happened, on the screen whose
entire job is to state what is owed.

It was found by reading the live payload rather than by a test, which is the
uncomfortable part. Corrected, on the same case:

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| Arrears at the cut | **$64.80** (the recorded position LESS the fee) |
| Reconnection fee | **$75.00** |
| Paid since | **− $0.00** |
| **Still owed** | **$139.80** — the LEDGER's figure, read once, never a sum of the rows |

It foots by construction now, and the total is still `_balance_for` rather than
arithmetic done on a screen — `DEF-CUS-6050`'s rule, that the figure a clerk
states and the figure that admits the customer back cannot differ.

### Two choices that are OURS, recorded so they are cheap to reverse

The coordinator drew both and handed them over **as proposals, not law**. Nothing
signed contradicts either, so both are built and both are written down here:

1. **`Remote` as a third way a service can go back on**, for a service point that
   needs nobody to attend. `BR-WRK-055` already makes *No visit needed* a
   RECORDED CHOICE rather than an absence, so this extends a shape the product
   has rather than inventing one. **Reversing it is deleting one entry from
   `HOW_OPTIONS`.**
2. **The new deposit is a LINE THE CLERK SEES** rather than something that
   happens silently. `DSC-02.4` says a new deposit is required after an applied
   one and says nothing about how much; **nothing in this product collects or
   prices one.** So the figure shown is the OLD amount, labelled as the old
   amount, and the row says *due before service returns* rather than quoting a
   price nobody set. A FIELD would have been dead UI (hard-won law 2), which is
   the posture `ReconnectDialog` already took; this is the same fact with its
   amount beside it.

### Where the drawing lost to our own UI standard, and where it won

**B14 rule 44.** The drawings show the two steps as a full-width two-cell bar;
**`WizardFrame`'s numbered rail is what is built**, because the UI standard wins
on the frame too. What the drawing DECIDES is the content — that there are two
steps, that they are *Choose* and *Confirm*, and what is on each — and every one
of those is built exactly as drawn. Rule 37 says the same from the other side.

**And the table array is `EditableTable` from the kit, reused** (rule 43). Lane
WIZARD needs the same shape for the disconnect steps; nothing new was written for
either of us to keep in step.

### What the Accounts blueprint draws about reconnection: NOTHING, measured

`05-prototype/02 Accounts Menu Blueprint.pdf` is **283 pages**. The word
*reconnect* appears on **five**: 143, 146, 248, 249 and 250, every one a FEE, a
JOB TYPE or prose. **p143 was rendered and read AS AN IMAGE** (B14 rule 42) — it
draws the case record with three actions, `Hold the case`, `Open the account`,
`Mark as cut`, and no reconnection screen at all. So the four PNGs of 2026-09-25
are this screen's only drawn specification, and that is stated as a measurement
rather than as an assumption.

### What is NOT built, stated plainly

**The commit.** `mark_reconnecting` refuses over `not_settled` against
`BR-CUS-1097`, and the write that records the rule's four facts — what was owed,
what had been paid, who restored it, when — does not exist. `disconnects.py`
belongs to another lane. **The screen therefore renders its commit DISABLED WITH
THE SERVER'S OWN REASON AS VISIBLE TEXT** (`BR-SHL-025`) and asks the server what
it would refuse rather than restating it, so the day that clause goes the screen
starts working with nothing on this side edited (hard-won law 1).

## 2026-09-25 · THE DISCONNECTS LIST, REDRAWN — AND FOUR JUDGMENTS THE RULES DID NOT COVER

**Lane LIST, maintenance track** (`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md`).
Ten findings from the Product Owner's walk of Accounts → Disconnects. Six were
defects (`DEF-CUS-6744` … `DEF-CUS-6749`), filed **before** they were fixed;
three were the redesign; one was a duplicate of another. Every one was
reproduced in Chromium at 1440 and 1280 first, and **measured rather than
eyeballed** — which is how two of the six turned out to be worse than reported.

**WHAT THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED ABOUT THE REPORT ITSELF, and it is the part worth
keeping.** The walk said *"five of eight state filters return zero rows"*. It is
**six of eight**, and the sixth is a different KIND of fault: `f.state=on_hold`
returned zero **by construction** — `STATE_ON_HOLD` is declared in `CASE_STATES`,
is in the migration's CHECK vocabulary, and is assigned **nowhere in this
repository** — while two rows on the same screen had a State cell reading *On
hold*. The other five were true zeroes. A report that lumps them together gets
the remedy wrong for both halves: one needed code, five needed a number.

---

### JUDGMENT 1 — THE EYE ON A ROW WITH NO CASE OPENS THE ACCOUNT

**The question was put to the Product Owner and has not been answered.** Both
options are open: either the protection-only rows leave this list, or the eye
opens something. **The lane took the second, as the less destructive of the
two**, and it is recorded here so it can be reversed cheaply — it is one
conditional in `DisconnectsTab.tsx`'s actions cell.

**Why that way round.** Dropping the rows would take a held account off the one
screen that says a utility may not cut it, and would silently change what the
`HELD` tile counts against the list beneath it — a tile of 2 over a list that
cannot show either of them. Adding a door removes nothing. If the PO rules the
other way, the rows leave and the door goes with them; nothing else moves.

**What it was.** Two of six rows offered the clerk **nothing at all**: the eye
was disabled, reading *"This row has no case reference."* — which is TRUE, which
is `BR-SHL-025` satisfied to the letter, and which is exactly what hid it. The
rule asks whether a refusal is STATED. **Nothing asked whether the row had any
working door**, and that question belonged to nobody. Hard-won law 2's mirror.

### JUDGMENT 2 — `Last notice` COMES OFF THE DEFAULT COLUMNS AND STAYS IN THE CHOOSER

**The blueprint and the new drawing disagree, and neither is overruled.** p142 of
the Accounts blueprint draws a `LAST NOTICE` column; the redesign drawing does
not, and draws a column chooser instead.

**Measured:** ten columns came to **1453px** inside a viewport with **no
horizontal scroll container** — so the Actions column, and the only row action
on the screen, were **clipped**: by 13px at 1440 and by **173px at 1280**, where
a clerk could not reach it at all. `LAST NOTICE` alone was 242px of that.

Deleting the column would overrule the blueprint on its own layout; leaving it
on keeps the table off the screen. `defaultVisible: false` does neither — the
column exists, it is listed in the `▦` panel, and one click brings it back. A
case in the drawing suite **turns it on through the chooser** to assert its
contents, so *off by default* cannot rot into *deleted* with nothing going red.

### JUDGMENT 3 — SIX CLERK WORDS, AND A SEVENTH STATE THE SIX DO NOT COVER

`Notified · Scheduled · Off · Paid · Restored · Held`, in all eleven catalogues,
on the State column and on the five tiles alike — **one vocabulary, so a clerk
who reads a tile can find its rows by their badge.** The stored codes did not
move and no server value changed.

⚠ **`closed_out` IS A SEVENTH STATE AND WAS GIVEN NO WORD.** It is real
(`BR-CUS-430`), it is offered as a filter, and a case can hold it on this list.
It reads **`Closed`** rather than being folded into one of the six: mapping it
onto *Restored* would tell a clerk the supply is back on when the case was
merely finished. **This is the one to put back to the PO** — if the six are meant
to be exhaustive, then a closed-out case should leave this list, and that is a
ruling rather than a lane's choice.

### JUDGMENT 4 — A STATE FILTER THAT ANSWERS ZERO CARRIES ITS COUNT RATHER THAN BEING WITHDRAWN

The brief offered two remedies for the empty filters: *either they return rows,
or states that cannot exist yet are not offered.* **`on_hold` was fixed** — it
now resolves the way the list and the `HELD` tile already resolve it, an account
carrying a protection in force, so it returns the two rows whose cell says
*Held* (**0 → 2**, measured on PostgreSQL 16).

**The other five are true zeroes and they are KEPT, each carrying its count.**
Withdrawing them would make the filter list change shape as a tenant's data
changes — a clerk who completes their first cut would find a new option appear —
and it would hide from a utility that *Off* is a thing this product tracks. A
control that answers *nothing* is indistinguishable from a broken one **until
the number is beside it**, which is the whole of the remedy: nothing is hidden
and no option is removed. **A case asserts the count and the filter AGREE for
every offered value** — the exact shape `on_hold` failed in, where a count
computed one way and a filter resolved another would have gone unnoticed.

⚠ **The reason three of those five are zero is `DEF-CUS-6750`'s neighbourhood and
is lane CUTPATH's, not this one's:** nobody can record a cut today, so no case
reaches `cut`, `reconnecting` or `closed_out`. The list's job in the meantime is
to be honest about it, and that is what the counts do.

---

### WHAT NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY COULD HAVE CAUGHT, AND WHY

**`DEF-CUS-6749` — a crew's visit reached no screen.**
`apps/customers/disconnect_visits.py` has carried four outcomes, a CHECK
constraint and its own test file since `BR-CUS-1083`. `disconnect_reads.py`
contained **zero references to it**. Three of the four outcomes CLEAR the cut
date and return the case to `notice_sent` — **a real and correct state** — so a
case a crew drove to on Tuesday and could not cut rendered **identically** to a
case nobody has ever visited: same word, same empty Cut date. No null, no dash,
no gap anywhere for a check to notice. The write side was fully tested and the
read side did not know the table existed; *"can anybody see this happened"*
belonged to neither.

Proved end to end before it was written up: recording a `locked_gate` visit on
`DSC-26-0001` moved it from `scheduled` to `notice_sent` and cleared its cut
date, and the row then read `Notified · Visited · Locked gate · 09/24/2026`.

**The three geometry defects are unmeasurable by the entire unit suite, and not
by oversight.** `vitest` runs under jsdom, which has **no layout engine** —
`getBoundingClientRect` returns zeroes there. So a 277px row, a column 173px
past the viewport and a table with no scroll container cannot be seen by any
case in `DisconnectsTab.test.tsx`, and `innerText` is returned for a clipped
element exactly as for a visible one. `10-scripts/def_cus_6744_6749_disconnects_list_walkthrough.mjs`
is the durable form of that check: it asserts **geometry as numbers** at both
widths, and it was proved RED on the pre-fix tree first — **23 of 26 assertions
failed**.

⚠ **ONE OF ITS ASSERTIONS CANNOT FAIL AND IS KEPT, LABELLED.** *"no horizontal
page scroll"* passed before and after, because the overflow was CLIPPED rather
than scrollable — which IS the defect. Naming an always-green assertion beats
deleting it, and beats leaving it unlabelled for the next reader to trust.

### WHAT REACHED ANOTHER LANE'S SCREEN, SAID OUT LOUD

The six clerk words live in the shared catalogues, which is the right place for
them — one vocabulary, not two. **`DisconnectRecordPage` reads the same keys**,
so lane CUTPATH's case record now says `Notified` where it said `At notice`.
Walked and correct, and reported rather than left to be discovered.

**Two things this lane did NOT fix and does not own:** the same 22-word
paragraph is still in the Case # cell on **Transfers** and **Move-outs**
(`transferDisconnectShared.RecordNumberCell`, mounted by four screens — changing
it would have redrawn three other lanes' tables in this commit), and the five
KPI tiles **wrap 4+1** at 1440 against a drawing that shows five across, which
is the shared `kpi-grid` class on **55 screens** and not one screen's to move.

## 2026-09-25 — **THE FIVE 2026-09-25 RULINGS REACH THE CODE: A CLERK CAN RECORD A CUT, AND CAN RESTORE SERVICE TO SOMEBODY WHO STILL OWES** (lane CUTPATH, wires `BR-CUS-1097` and `BR-CUS-1099`, closes `DEF-CUS-6735`, `DEF-CUS-6736`, `DEF-CUS-6744`, `DEF-CUS-6750`, `DEF-CUS-6751`, `DEF-CUS-6752`)

**WHAT WAS REPORTED, AND THE FIRST THING THIS LANE DID WAS CHECK IT.** A walking
lane reported, in its own words, that *"nobody can record a cut in the product
today"* and that `Mark as cut` was *"greyed on every case"*. **That is not what
the product does, and the correction matters more than the fixes below.**

**MEASURED, in Chromium at 1440 against a private clone, 2026-09-25:** on case
`DSC-26-0006` — a case scheduled through the wizard with its services named —
`Mark as cut` is **LIVE**, the dialog opens, and pressing it **records the cut**:
`disconnect_cases` row `DSC-26-0007` now reads `state=cut`, `cut_on=2026-09-24`,
`reconnection_fee_amount=75.0000`, `outstanding_at_cut=223.9000`, with the fee
raised and issued as a real invoice. **The cut path works end to end from the
case record page.**

⚠ **THE FIRST READING OF THE DATABASE SAID THERE WERE NO CASES AT ALL, AND THAT
READING WAS WRONG — IT IS WORTH ONE LINE BECAUSE IT IS THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN
LAW 7.** `select … from disconnect_cases` as the application user returns **0
rows** with no error and no warning when `app.tenant_id` is not set, because RLS
`FORCE` is on (hard rule 1). Eight rows were there the whole time. **A query
that answers truthfully about everything it can see is indistinguishable from an
empty one**, and the conclusion drawn from it — *"the seeded cases do not
exist"* — would have been reported as a finding. `set app.tenant_id` first, every
time, or count what you found against what should be there.

**SO WHAT THE TWO REPORTED SENTENCES ACTUALLY ARE:**

| What a clerk saw | What it is |
|---|---|
| *"No cut is scheduled yet."* at notice | **CORRECT.** A cut is scheduled before it is recorded — the wizard's five steps — and `commit_cut` refuses a case with no schedule behind it because *"a cut with no schedule behind it is a cut nobody was told about"* |
| *"No service is chosen."* once scheduled | **CORRECT, and `DSC-02.1` requires it** — *"One decision per service, not all or nothing"*. It is true of the SEEDED cases (`DSC-26-0001` and `DSC-26-0002` carry `services_cut = []`) and of nothing a clerk creates: the wizard passes `{service_code: treatment}` on every schedule, and `scheduleCutPlanOf` is where it does it |

⚠ **AND `schedule_cut` IS SAFELY REPEATABLE, MEASURED.** A case scheduled
without its services is **not** a dead end — re-scheduling `A-11803` with
`{electric: full_disconnection, water: full_disconnection}` was ACCEPTED and the
services landed. The seeder header in `10-scripts/cr094_wave_b_seed_cut_account.py`
says the opposite (*"once a case is scheduled, `_require_running` refuses …
a dead end by design"*) and **that sentence is stale**. Nothing was built for
this: what is owed is a door from the case record back into the wizard for a
case in that shape, and it is `lane WIZARD`'s surface rather than this one's.

### RULING 1 · `BR-CUS-1097` — THE BALANCE NEED NOT BE CLEAR TO RECONNECT

PO, verbatim, 2026-09-25, choosing option (a) of two: *"Show what's still owed
and let the clerk proceed"*.

**THE WORKED CASE, AND IT IS THE ONE PUT TO THE PO.** Brett Calloway owes
**$1,204.50** plus the reconnection fee. He pays **$400.00** and agrees a plan
for the rest. **The clerk restores water the same day.** Under the code as it
stood he was refused `not_settled` and the button was grey.

**WHAT MOVED.** `reconnect_blockers` no longer returns `not_settled`;
`reconnect_warnings` returns `money_still_owed` with the same figure, from the
same read, and `ready` does not look at it. **Proved on the running product:**
`DSC-26-0007` owes **$223.90**, `Mark reconnecting` is live, and the screen says
*"Money is still owed."* above the panels.

**AND THE HALF THAT IS NOT ABOUT BLOCKING.** *"With nothing blocking, the record
is the only protection there is."* `mark_reconnecting` now writes **what was
still owed**, **when**, and **who** (the `audit_log` row, hard rule 7). **What
had been PAID is NOT recorded and is NOT invented** — nothing on the disconnect
path reads it, `DEF-PAY-6074` is the open row for the credit-position read that
would answer it, and a number made up here would be a second, wrong answer to a
question `BR-BIL-160` answers exactly. It travels as a named absence,
`paid_against_arrears_not_read`.

⚠ **ONE REFUSAL WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SWEPT UP.** An **unreadable** balance still
refuses. `BR-CUS-1097` is about a balance that is KNOWN and not clear; a reading
that FAILED is a different fact, and moving a case to *"paid, awaiting a visit"*
on it would put that sentence on screen with nothing behind it.

### RULING 2 · `BR-CUS-1099` — NO RECORDED PROOF OF CERTIFIED SERVICE WARNS

PO, verbatim: *"So we warn user , but we dont stop user - We can't send a
certified notice — a final-tier cut isn't lawful without one"*.

`assert_service_proved` no longer raises `cut_on_unrecorded_service`;
`service_proof_warnings` carries it, and `schedule_cut` and `commit_cut` put it
on the payload they audit — **so `audit_log` records that no proof was there,
who acted and when.** This is the one ruling of the five where **the record
protects the UTILITY**: a final-tier cut without proved certified service is one
it may not lawfully have made.

⚠ **`tier_3_proof_not_certified` WAS NOT REMOVED WITH IT**, and a test now
exists whose only job is to go red if a later lane removes it. The PO's words
are about the ABSENCE of proof and say nothing about a notice served by another
channel. Reading a ruling wider than it was given is how a refusal on a
household's water supply disappears by accident.

### `DEF-CUS-6744` · A CASE READ `At notice` AND `On hold` AT ONCE

Blueprint p144 promises three immediate effects and this product kept **one**.
`disconnects.displayed_state` now derives `on_hold` from the protections in
force, so **two of the three** are kept and the record stops contradicting its
own protections panel.

⚠ **DERIVED, NOT STORED, AND THAT IS THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN EARLIER DECISION
RATHER THAN A SHORTCUT.** `_ladder_restarts` rejects a stored `on_hold` by name
and `disconnect_reads.py` §1 opens with *"`On hold` cannot be a stored state"*.
The reason is the reason nothing stores *"the ladder is running"*: **a hold
cached on a row outlives the thing that caused it**, and a payment plan's
protection has no expiry at all (`BR-CUS-043`), so a written `on_hold` would need
a nightly job that does not exist. Computed, it is right every time it is asked.
The drawn word is **segment**, which is what a derivation reads. The third
promise — clearing the cut date — is **still not kept** and is still stated as
its own consequence, because a clerk holding a scheduled case must not discover
the date afterwards.

### `DEF-CUS-6752` · EVERY REQUIRED-FIELD MESSAGE ON THIS SCREEN RENDERED NOWHERE

**The reported symptom was one dialog; the cause is five.** `FormModal` DOES
validate on submit and DOES block the post. The message is then looked up with
`useFieldError(props.id)` — keyed by the input's **id** — while
`collectFormErrors` keys its map by the **zod path**. Not one pair matched in any
of the five case-record dialogs. So a clerk pressing `Hold the case` with
`Review on` empty got **nothing at all**, which is worse than a refusal.

**Four are fixed by making the schema key BE the field id** (Hold, Mark as cut,
Record visit; Finish cut has no field to key). **`ReconnectDialog.tsx` is NOT
fixed here** — it is lane RECONNECT's file and the change is one line: key its
schema `"disconnect-reconnect-on"` instead of `on_date`.

### A DEVIATION FROM THE DRAWING, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIET (`DEF-CUS-6751`)

p144 draws FOUR hold reasons. The fourth, *A bill is disputed*, was built drawn
DISABLED with its refusal underneath, on `BR-SHL-025`'s authority. **That rule
was the wrong rule for this control.** `BR-SHL-025` is about something *this
deployment* cannot honour — a thing some tenant could switch on, which a clerk
deserves to see and be told about. **There is no deployment, tenant setting or
future flag that makes this radio pressable**: `record_protection` refuses a
fourth kind by name and nothing in the repository stores a disputed amount. A
permanent impossibility offered beside its own refusal is the mirror of hard-won
law 2 — a dead control over a live screen — and on a dialog with three real
choices it costs a clerk a decision every time they open it. **It is removed and
its two catalogue keys are retired.** The FACT is not hidden: p143's drawn
question *"Disputed bill open?"* is still answered on the protections panel,
where it is a read rather than an offer to act. **What a disputed bill SHOULD do
is `OQ-CUS-12737`**, minted here and put to the PO.

⚠⚠ **AND THE RE-DERIVATION ITSELF ALMOST CORRUPTED ANOTHER LANE'S ROW — CAUGHT BY
ARITHMETIC AND BY NOTHING ELSE, WHICH IS THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING.** Fanning the
new version number out was done with `sed -i 's/2.351.99/2.351.100/g'` over the
WHOLE decision log — and the Disconnects-list lane had shipped **in 2.351.99**,
so its own closing row was silently rewritten to a version that never contained
it. **Every check in law 11 passes on that**: the file count is right, this
lane's block IS present, and `git show` shows the block. What found it was
`git diff --numstat <tip>` reading **174 insertions / 1 DELETION** on what must
be a pure append. **On an append-only file the deletion count is not noise, it is
the whole check**, and one is as bad as a thousand. The file was rebuilt as the
tip's bytes plus this block — `173 / 0` — and the other lane's row is byte-
identical to what they pushed. **A blunt `sed` over a shared register is the
`csv`-writer mistake wearing a different tool**; append, then prove the prefix.

## 2026-09-25 — **THE DISCONNECT WIZARD IS FOUR STEPS, AND FIVE RULINGS REACH A SCREEN FOR THE FIRST TIME** (lane WIZARD, `v2.351.99`, `DEF-CUS-6750`…`DEF-CUS-6765`)

**MAINTENANCE, NOT BUILD, AND THE ROUTING IS THE FIRST DECISION.**
`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md` names this case in as many
words: *a live screen redrawn end to end is MAINTENANCE*, borrowing exactly one
thing from Build — the drawing step. A clerk can do this task in the product
today, so the one question the process asks answers itself. It has already gone
wrong once, on the property Overview, and what a lane following Build loses is
reproduce, blast radius, regression and the reporter.

### THE SHAPE, AND WHY THE PROTOTYPE'S STEPPER WAS NOT INHERITED

`Choose · Check · Schedule · Confirm` — **four words, each naming an act.** B18
§5.8.7 and blueprint p136–p141 both draw FIVE, and the old 4 and 5 were the same
screen twice: *Fees & consequences* then *Review*, with the fees, the deposit and
the consequences on both.

**The argument is the Billing blueprint's and it is borrowed deliberately** (p35,
*"Four words, each naming an act"*). It is worth restating why: `billRunShared.
tsx` was built to r10's SIX-step stepper — its own docstring says so, *"the
prototype's stepper, in its order and its words"* — while the Billing blueprint
draws four and carries a carry-over map on p86–p88. **A lane obeying the pointer
built the wrong shape and passed every check**, and four further lanes then built
onto it. The four here come from this rebuild's own drawings, read AS IMAGES
(B14 rule 42).

**The carry-over, written out so nothing is lost by subtraction:**

| was | is |
|---|---|
| 1 Account & reason | **1 Choose** — the account, the reason, the services |
| 2 Protections | **2 Check** — and the ladder check is HERE ONLY |
| 3 Notice & date | **3 Schedule** — the notice, the date, who goes |
| 4 Fees & consequences | **4 Confirm** |
| 5 Review | **4 Confirm** |

### FIVE RULINGS OF ONE PRINCIPLE REACH A SCREEN

All five were recorded on 2026-09-25 by lanes PROT and RECON and **none of them
had been built.** The principle: *the product tells the clerk what is true and
does not stop them acting.*

| rule | what the screen now does |
|---|---|
| `BR-CUS-1096` | a live protection WARNS — *"A protection is in force. You may continue."* The drawn sentence *"Recording one stops the cut"* is DELETED |
| `BR-CUS-1097` | supersedes `BR-CUS-104`'s gate clause. The wizard's own header restated that gate as current for a day; amended (`DEF-CUS-6751`) |
| `BR-CUS-1098` | the master variant — one banner line, the owner's debt split from residue transferred up, a row per service point |
| `BR-CUS-1099` | a missing proof WARNS. *"No proof, no cut"* is gone |
| `BR-CUS-1100` | step 4 names the ACCOUNT and the CUSTOMER as marked, **and says the address is not** |

⚠ **FRICTION WAS DECLINED FOUR TIMES AND NOTHING WAS ADDED BACK.** No typed
reason, no tick-to-acknowledge, no supervisor, on any of the five. **A sixth case
of this shape is the principle applying again rather than a question to raise**
(hard-won law 13).

⛔ **AND THE SERVER STILL REFUSES ALL THREE.** `halt_reason` → `HALT_PROTECTED`,
`assert_service_proved` → `cut_on_unrecorded_service` and `reconnect_blockers` →
`not_settled`. **The SCREEN no longer blocks, which is this lane's half**; a
server refusal reaches the clerk through the frame's commit failure with every
entered value preserved. Reported to lane CUTPATH rather than worked around —
a screen that pretended the schedule would succeed is hard-won law 1.

### TWO JUDGMENTS WHERE THE DRAWING AND THE PRODUCT DISAGREED, AND THEY WENT OPPOSITE WAYS

**(1) THE DEPOSIT SUBTRACTION IS NOT DRAWN — `DEF-CUS-6753`.** Both drawings put
`Deposit applied − $65.00` above `To clear before reconnection`.
`disconnects._to_clear` is **`arrears + fee` and subtracts nothing**, and it
cannot: applying a deposit against an arrear is a balance-sheet posting and hard
rule 5 leaves every journal line to the ledger posting service.
`DEPOSIT_APPLICATION_NOT_POSTED` has said so since W7. **Drawing the subtraction
would have quoted a customer a figure nothing computes, two inches from the
figure `mark_reconnecting` actually reads.**

**THE SPLIT IS THE DECISION, AND IT IS NOT *remove the control*.** The brief's
own instruction was *it moves the money, or the control goes*. **The CONTROL
stays and the CLAIM goes**, because the election is real and stored:
`schedule_cut` takes `deposit`, `commit_cut` records it, and `reconnection_terms`
reads it back to answer whether a new deposit is needed. It is not a dead
control — **what was dead was the arithmetic beside it.**

**(2) THE RESTRICTOR OPTION IS REMOVED — item 3.14.** The old screen offered
*Restrictor / limiter* DISABLED beside a paragraph explaining that this product
cannot record one. That is two breaches at once — a control nobody may press, and
rationale on screen — **and deleting the option answers both**. The server's
refusal, `RESTRICTOR_UNBUILDABLE` and `SERVICE_TREATMENTS`' third value are all
untouched, so `OQ-385` is exactly as open as it was and the option comes back
from the shared list the day a schema can hold a restricted supply.

### WHAT WAS FOUND WHILE BUILDING, AND FILED RATHER THAN FIXED IN PASSING

* **`DEF-CUS-6750`** — the branch did not type-check. `SegmentedControl.onSelect`
  hands back a `string` into a `Record` of three literals, so `npm run build`
  (`tsc --noEmit && vite build`) exited 2 and the container image could not be
  produced. **Pushed on its own, ahead of this work**, at the coordinator's
  instruction. Narrowed rather than cast: a cast silences the compiler and keeps
  the hole, because `schedule_cut` refuses an unknown treatment by name and the
  clerk would meet that refusal four steps later.
  **Escape: nothing in this repo type-checks the front end at merge** — the
  vitest suites transpile without checking, so 66 green tests ran over a real
  type error, and 55 of 56 walk scripts run `vite build` alone, which strips
  types without checking them.
* **`DEF-CUS-6752`** — the three fees are priced from the TENANT's one charge
  catalogue, not from the account's plan by category, so a residential and a
  commercial account are quoted the same figure. The drawing labels the panel
  *Residential · Standard plan* and gives every row a `FROM`. **The screen names
  the account's own plan and category as a fact about the ACCOUNT**, and says
  where the figure really came from — nothing on screen claims a plan priced a
  fee that plan did not price. Backend half: lane CUTPATH.
* **`DEF-CUS-6764`** — `schedule_cut` has five keyword arguments and none is a
  note, so the clerk's `What happened` is KEPT on the draft, survives a park, and
  **does not yet reach the case.** Half of the reported defect fixed, and the
  half that is not is stated rather than quietly dropped.
* **`DEF-CUS-6765`** — the shared `AccountFinder` prints the raw account id in
  its search box and as a pickable option whenever a wizard arrives
  pre-selected. **B14 rule 31, live on three screens.** Found by dumping the
  markup while writing the rule-31 case — the assertion that could see it, where
  every existing assertion asks whether the id TRAVELLED, which is the opposite
  question and passes exactly when the id is on screen. **Not fixed here:** that
  file is shared by three wizards and two other lanes are in this tree today.

### TWO THINGS THE SCREEN NOW SAYS IT CANNOT DO, WHERE IT USED TO SAY NOTHING

**Continue on an empty cut date now names the field.** It returned a bare `false`
before, so the frame printed its generic *"fill in what's marked above"* over a
screen with nothing marked — `DEF-936` exactly. **This is also what produced a
sibling lane's byte-identical screenshots of two different steps**, and the
walkthrough md5s its shots for that reason.

**`+ Raise work order` is disabled with its reason.** `from_flows.FLOW_KINDS`
holds six kinds and `propose()` refuses anything else by name; a cut is not one
of them. The row's VISIT choice is still real and recorded; the raise is what is
not built.

### WHAT A GREEN SUITE HERE IS AND IS NOT WORTH

42 cases, and **six of them were shown RED first against the exact mutation they
exist to catch** — the step count, the step labels, the rail's buttons, the
restrictor, `BR-CUS-1096`'s withdrawn sentence, `BR-CUS-1099`'s, and the deposit
subtraction. They read STRINGS and ATTRIBUTES. **They cannot see layout,
spacing, alignment, hierarchy or colour** — nearly half of everything that goes
wrong on a screen — and they cannot tell a screen that matches its drawing from
one that merely contains the same words. That is
`10-scripts/def_cus_6750_four_step_disconnect_walkthrough.mjs` and a person, and
it is the only check in this repository that reads rendered output.
