## 2026-09-25 — THE PO'S OWN 2026-09-19 RULING ON THE MOVE-OUTS ROW ACTION IS SUPERSEDED, AND THREE COLUMNS STOP EXPLAINING THEMSELVES

**Lane MOVEOUT · `v2.351.102` · maintenance, not build** — a user can do all of
this in the product today, so it went through
`12-governance/22-product-maintenance-process.md` and not through r11.

### The reversal, stated rather than assumed

**PO, verbatim, looking at `v2.351.98` on `ottumwa-water-works`:** *"few bugs on
Move out - list screen action it should be icons not buttons"*.

**That supersedes the PO's own ruling of 2026-09-19**, recorded that day as
*"this si all good - please update it"*, which accepted the Accounts blueprint
p117's drawn bordered `↗ Open` on this list and on the Move-ins list. The
supersession is written here because a ruling that collides with a signed one
must state what it overturns; the old ruling was **not** re-put to the PO, which
is hard-won law 13's bug.

**It also lands where B14 rule 15 always stood** — *row actions are ICONS with
tooltips, never text links* — and where the Disconnects list already is: p142
draws a bordered `↗ Open` there too and that lane built an icon, on rule 44's
reasoning (*our UI standard says how it is built, and it wins every time*).
`components/RowActions.tsx` is mounted; nothing new was written (rule 43).

### The judgment calls, each with the figure it was made on

**1 · The SETTLEMENT column's absence is an em dash.** It printed *"No
settlement yet — the final bill is not readable"* on **5 of 5 rows** measured in
Chromium at 1440. The second clause is RATIONALE, which B14 rule 33 puts at zero
words on screen and says is REMOVED rather than shortened. **The blueprint
agrees from the other side:** p119 draws this column as `Short by $186.40` ·
**`—`** · `Refund $42.15`. Both branches collapse, not one — the parked row's
*"Not settled until it closes"* is the same kind of sentence and p119 draws the
in-flight row's cell as a dash too. Its key is retired from all eleven
catalogues. The engine's reason still rides on the cell's `title` and the two
money terms are still `data-deposit-held-display` / `data-outstanding-display`.

**2 · The STEP cell draws no bar where there is no step.** Every closed row drew
**4 empty segments** above the words *"Step not recorded"* — one absence stated
twice, the top half placeholder furniture. p119 draws **no bar at all** in this
column: its cells are `6 of 6` · `2 of 6` in plain text. The filled bar is kept
where the server sends a `reached`. **This is in `MoveStepBar`, which both tabs
mount, so the Move-ins tab is fixed by the same change** — walked in a browser
and confirmed: its one row with a real step still draws `1 of 6` with its bar.

**3 · The first KPI tile is labelled for what it counts.** The PO saw `OPEN 5`
standing over five rows each reading `Completed`. **Both were true and no logic
moved:** `move_out_kpis` counts *move-outs that have closed and are not yet
finally billed*, and the rows are right that the move-out completed. p119 heads
the same tile `OPEN` under the caption *"not yet closed"* — **the opposite
sense** — and this product cannot count those at all, because a move-out before
it closes is not a row anywhere. So the tile carried the drawn WORD over an
undrawn MEANING, with a caption underneath to stop it being read backwards.
**A label that needs a caption to stop it being read backwards is the wrong
label**, so the label now reads **Awaiting final bill** (three words, rule 33's
cap) and the caption comes off (rule 32, one statement per section). The
server's `open_means` is still carried as data — the same shape `FINAL READS
DUE` directly below it already uses.

### The wizard's step 2, measured rather than eyeballed

**PO:** *"spacing problem reason and table start"*. Measured in Chromium at
1440, `getComputedStyle` and bounding boxes, before and after:

| gap | before | after | the rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reason select → `Meters on this unit` | **0px** | **24px** | B14 rule 39, `--space-6`, between sections |
| meters table → `Field visit` | **20px** | **24px** | the same step |
| `Move-out date` label → its input | 5px | 5px | rule 39's ratified field anatomy |
| `Reason` label → its select | 5px | 5px | the same |
| field → field | 20px | 20px | rule 39, `FieldStack` |

⚠ **THE PO'S FIRST OBSERVATION IS NOT BORNE OUT AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY.**
They reported that *Reason* sits on its select with no gap while *Move-out date*
has normal spacing, i.e. two fields built differently. **Both are 5px, the
ratified figure, and they are the same control code.** What makes *Reason* look
cramped is the **0px section boundary directly underneath it** — the heading of
the next section reading as a caption on the field above. One fault, not two.

**`WizardSectionStack` is where the utilities live, and that is deliberate.**
`MoveOutWizard.tsx` is NOT on `styles/route-b-migrated.txt`, so `G31` owns it
and a Tailwind utility written there is a red gate at merge; every utility these
two wizards need has lived in `moveShared.tsx` since `CR-030` W5 and this
follows that posture. **`MoveInReadingsTable`'s own `mb-5` is neutralised by the
host rather than deleted from the component** — the move-in wizard mounts the
same table and was not reported or walked today, so stripping its margin there
would leave the move-in's own step at 0px, which is this defect running
backwards. `DEF-CUS-6772` carries the move-in half.

### Two things reported and NOT defects, verified in a browser

**The second line under the move-out date is not a repeat.** *"Charges run
through this day."* is the field's helper, already cut from 30 words to 5 by
`DEF-CUS-6477` on the PO's own ruling. The `30-Sep-26` beneath it is
`regionalDateEcho`, which renders **only when the tenant's date format differs
from what the browser's native date input shows** — it is the same date in a
DIFFERENT format, and it is the only place a tenant on `DD-MMM-YY` ever sees
theirs. On `brazosbend` (MM/DD/YYYY) it correctly renders nothing at all, which
is why it took reading `DateCell.regionalDateEcho` to explain the screenshot.

**`+ Add work order` is a live door.** Pressed in Chromium: it adds an inline
order row with job type (28 options), priority, due date, assignee, *Not raised
yet* and a note, plus a remove control. `POST /accounts/{id}/move-out` reads
`field_visit` as `{none, orders}` since `DEF-CUS-6487`, so the rows reach Work.

## 2026-09-25 — **A SHIPPED SCREEN'S STORY WAS WRITTEN AND INVISIBLE, AND TWO "KNOWN LIMITS" HANDED TO THIS LANE WERE ALREADY BUILT** (lane SMALLFIX, `S148` · `US-CUS-032` · `DEF-CUS-6775` · `DEF-CUS-6776`; mints NO rule and NO question)

**The judgment: the story was NOT rewritten.** This lane was briefed to author
`US-CUS-032` from scratch on the grounds that it had *"zero hits in
`04-docs/06-epics/`"*. **That directory does not exist** — epics live in
`04-docs/05-modules/*/06-epics/` — so the search was hard-won law 7's fifth
shape, a check reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes. The story was
there, written the same morning by lane RECONNECT, with sections 1, 2, 3 and 8
in its neighbours' own numbering. **What was missing was the YAML frontmatter
block, which is the half both gates read**: `G2` resolves a cited `US-ID`
against `^id: US-` and `G25` asks which story's `screens:` list names the
screen. Prose satisfies neither. So the fix is twelve lines of frontmatter, not
a second story — authoring one over the top would have duplicated an accurate
record and buried its author's reasoning.

**Two limits this lane was told to carry into the story are STALE, and writing
them down would have been the mirror-image defect** — a stated absence that is
not absent, which this repo files as `stale-stated-absence`. Checked against the
code rather than taken on trust:

| Briefed as a limit | What the code does |
|---|---|
| *"nothing raises the work order yet"* | `POST /disconnects/{ref}/reconnect/work-orders` exists (`reconnect_read.py:602`), goes through `services._raise_flow_work`, and the row's control calls it (`ReconnectPage.tsx:230`). Live since `b8e7a6c9a`, the shipping commit itself |
| *"the master-account facts are on no wire"* — occupant count, transferred-up debt | `_master_panel` serves `units` and `unit_accounts`; `_owed` serves `transferred_up`. The REAL limit is narrower and the story already states it exactly: the residue cannot be **split** from the owner's own debt (`transferred_up_not_separable`) |

**The lesson is the one this file keeps paying for:** a briefing is a claim about
the repo like any other, and *"grep found nothing"* is only as good as the path
it searched. Both the absent directory and the two stale limits would have
produced confident, green, wrong work.

## 2026-09-25 — G134 IS ADDED, AND FIVE CHECKS ARE TIGHTENED TO WHAT THE TREE HOLDS (lane GATEFIX, `DEF-GOV-6777`, `DEF-GOV-6778`, 2.352.2)

**No product behaviour changed.** Every edit here is to a check, to a check's
data file, or to a register that describes the tree. No screen, rule, figure,
endpoint or migration was touched.

### The judgment, and it was an Eng-Lead-class one: a new merge-blocking gate

`G31` refuses a component naming a class no stylesheet declares. For a file on
`07-frontend/src/styles/route-b-migrated.txt` that rule is FALSE — a Tailwind
utility is declared by the COMPILER — so `G31` skips those **559** files by
design and hands them to `07-frontend/src/styles/routeBUtilities.test.ts`,
which asks the real compiler. **Nothing ran that check.** `run_gates` is Python
and runs no vitest, and `.github/workflows/ci-frontend.yml` — the workflow that
did `npm test` — has been `.disabled` since 2026-09-04 with every other
workflow. `g31_declared_classes.route_b_migrated()`'s own docstring said *"Run
it by hand"*, which is hard-won law 1 exactly.

**What it cost, in one sentence a person can check:** `moveOutTables.tsx` asked
for `border-danger` and `bg-danger-50` from 2026-09-24; neither compiles and no
stylesheet declares either, so that panel drew with **no border and no
background** on a live screen, with `tsc`, eslint, `toHaveClass()` and all 134
gates green over it. A sibling lane fixed the panel at `6291bd3df`
(`DEF-CUS-6775`, 2.352.1) while this gate was being written — which is what
gave `G134` the proof below.

**Both honest routes were taken rather than one**, because they answer
different questions and the cheap one does not replace the real one:

* **`G134 route-b-utilities-compile`** shells that one vitest file from
  `run_gates` and reports its orphan list. **Proved RED at birth on the two
  REAL orphans and GREEN when the REAL fix landed** — no planted orphan was
  needed — both times through `run_gates`' own registry and `module.run()`,
  never through `python3 g134_….py`, which `DEF-GOV-3733` showed proves nothing
  about the path the suite uses. Its **SKIP** branch was proved too: with
  vitest absent it returns `SKIP … 559 Route B file(s) … were checked by NOBODY
  this run`.
* **`G31` now carries the skipped count in its RETURNED detail.** It had the
  number and `print`ed it, so the runner's row read *"0 undeclared class(es),
  at the baseline of 0"* over 559 files the gate had not looked at. Hard-won
  law 7, fifth shape: **a declared blind spot with no NUMBER attached is
  indistinguishable from an empty one** — `G32`'s `0 unresolved` over 21 live
  refusals, again.

### Five checks lowered to the measurement, none of the gains this lane's

Each of the five was **asking in its own failure text** to be tightened. A
ratchet fails on an IMPROVEMENT, so a good day and a bad day print the same
red, and in a suite carrying 57 of them that is where a true red hides.

| Check | Was | Now | What earned it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `G38` `UNTRACKED_BASELINE` | 47 | **44** | move-out wizard 2 → 0 at `2b5c1b4c6` (`DEF-CUS-6550`/`6551`); Taxes & Remittance 2 → 1 at `7f6cbae0a` (Finance `P4.12`/`P4.11`/`P4.8`) |

| `G20` `seam_known_gaps.txt` | park on line 44 | **deleted** | `apps.rating.selectors.tax_authority_id_for_tax` is published at `rating/selectors.py:3645`, landed `b813394a6`. The seam was NOT widened — it had asked by name since 2026-08-11 |

| `G23` `surface_debt.txt` payments | 1 | **line deleted** | same story; a module at zero needs no line, which is that file's own rule |

Both ratchet comments now **say that a fall is red and that the only lawful
response is to lower the integer**, so the next reader cannot mistake a gain
for a rise and "fix" it by raising the number.

## 2026-09-25 · THE GATE THAT GUARDS THE FROZEN BILLING FIGURES WAS NOT RUNNING, AND THE SUITE UNDERNEATH IT WAS GREEN THE WHOLE TIME (`DEF-GOV-6781`, 2.352.3)

**`G4`'s pytest leg reported 1,186 errors at the tip. Not one of them was a
billing fault.** An ERROR is a case that never ran, so the number said nothing
about what any of them prove — and it was read, reasonably, as the money path
being broken.

**Root cause: environment, in two layers, both of them law 7's *incapable of
passing*.**

1. **It ran `sys.executable`.** On this machine bare `python3` has pytest 9.1.1
   and **no Django**, so every one of the backend's test modules failed to
   import and pytest aborted collection. `06-backend/.venv/bin/python` has
   pytest **and** Django 5.2.17 and was never a candidate. This is the same
   cause `DEF-GOV-6698` recorded for five gates earlier the same day; it left
   `G4` standing as its open item **(b)**, and `G4` was the worst of the set
   because it does not SKIP — it FINDS pytest in a Django-less interpreter and
   returns **FAIL**, which reads like a defect in the bills.
2. **It named no path.** `pytest -m golden` with no path collected all
   **16,894** backend tests to deselect 16,871 of them, so **any unrelated
   broken import anywhere in the backend turned the FROZEN-figure gate red.**

**What the suite actually says, measured at tip `3a572853d` through
`module.run()` — the path `run_gates` uses, never `__main__`:**

> `G4 golden` **PASS** — harness (documents, not the engine): 33 PASS, 0 FAIL;
> engine golden suite (`06-backend/.venv/bin/python`): **23 passed, 1 xfailed**
> in 353.75s.

**That is the identical figure the GT-24/GT-47 lane recorded on 2026-08-11**
(`23 passed, 1913 deselected, 1 xfailed`, written into
`test_gt24_budget_chain.py`'s own gates line). So the answer to *has it ever
been green* is **yes, and it has not moved in six weeks** — what changed is that
for some part of that time nothing was running it.

**THE TWO NUMBERS, BOTH QUOTED, NEITHER ALONE (`DEF-2846`).**
**33 document self-consistency checks** — `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py`
recomputes B4/B5's own figures and imports no application code, so it cannot go
red when the engine drifts. **14 of the 61 signed GTs are ENGINE-VERIFIED** —
GT-1..11, 16, 24, 47, named in `g64_engine_verified_gts.txt`. **47 of the 61
signed billing figures still have no test that runs the engine**, and that is
unchanged by this work.

⚠ **AND THE ENGINE NUMBER HAS A SMALLER NUMBER INSIDE IT: OF THE 14, ONLY 13
ASSERT.** `GT-6` (credit note) is `xfail` — *"rating engine not implemented
(HUMAN-OWNED, B4) — lands W3"* — because billing has not published
`issue_credit_note`. It is a written contract that does not yet execute, and
`G64` counts it as engine-verified because the FILE exists. That is not an
error in `G64`, whose job is the identity of the set, but it means the sentence
*"14 of 61 are engine-verified"* is one case optimistic until billing publishes
that seam. Recorded here rather than fixed: moving `G64`'s arithmetic is a
change to the record `DEF-2846` created, and this lane did not have a ruling
for it. **Filed as `DEF-GOV-6782`** so it is counted rather than left in prose —
CLAUDE.md hard rule 4's own lesson, that a finding recorded only in the file you
happen to be in is a finding nobody can count.

**NOTHING SIGNED WAS TOUCHED.** No B4 or B5 figure moved, no golden expectation
was edited, no baseline was lowered. The engine and the frozen figures agree
today.

**What was changed, and why each is not a smoothing:**
* `gates/common.py` gains **one** `interpreter_with(*modules)` helper — which
  is `DEF-GOV-6698`'s open item **(c)**, verbatim: *"the candidate list belongs
  in gates/common.py as ONE helper — a paragraph in two files is the shape that
  produced this."* It also searches **the MAIN worktree's venv** via
  `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, because law 12 tells every lane to work in a
  private `git worktree`, `.venv/` is gitignored, and `git worktree add`
  therefore produces a checkout with no virtualenv in it at all. A probe that
  looks only at its own tree finds nothing in exactly the place the process
  tells lanes to stand.
* `G4` runs the golden suite **through that helper**, names `tests/golden` as
  its path, and **reports SKIP — never PASS — when no interpreter on the machine
  can run it**, saying what it looked for. `run_gates` already flags a
  FAIL→SKIP transition as *"stopped being checked"*.
* `G4` gains a clause that **FAILS if a `pytest.mark.golden` is written outside
  `06-backend/tests/golden`**. That is the price of naming a path: scoping a
  check must not be able to silently shrink it.
* One word in `04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/conformance/CR-100-BRC03-billing-step1.md`.
  `G64` was **FAIL at the tip** over that file — it states both numbers
  correctly and never uses the repo's agreed term, so the table row now reads
  **Golden — ENGINE-VERIFIED**. No figure in it moved.

**PROVED RED BEFORE TRUSTED GREEN, THROUGH `run()` AND NOT `__main__` (law 7,
`DEF-GOV-3733`):** a stray golden marker outside the directory → **FAIL** naming
the file · no capable interpreter → **SKIP** naming the candidates it tried ·
the pytest leg returning non-zero → **FAIL** carrying the failure line. `G64`'s
own self-test reports `stripping the vocabulary surfaces 12 again, so the check
bites`.

⚠ **AND ONE END-TO-END RED, BECAUSE THE THREE ABOVE PROVE THE GATE AND NOT THE
MONEY.** `core/money.py`'s `finalize` was flipped from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to
`ROUND_DOWN` — one line, in a private worktree, reverted and never committed
(`git hash-object` back to `8a805ccc1` against the tip's own blob) — and the
golden suite went **4 failed, 19 passed, 1 xfailed**. So the 23 green cases are
green because the engine agrees with B5, not because they assert nothing.

**STILL OPEN AND NOT FINISHED HERE:** `g05_isolation.py` and
`g120_the_application_starts.py` still hold their own literal copies of the
candidate list — folding them into the shared helper is the rest of
`DEF-GOV-6698` item (c) and was left alone because both files are live under
another lane this same day (law 11). The money gate costs **≈6 minutes**
(353.75s measured), and the cost is the test database being rebuilt from 278
migrations on every run — **not** collection and **not** the eager job runner:
`JOBS_EAGER=false` was measured at **403.77s**, i.e. no help, and is therefore
not set. `--reuse-db` takes the same 24 cases to **5.36s** and was deliberately
NOT added: the SQLite test database is one digest-named file, two lanes' gate
runs would share it, and a **flaky** money gate is worse than a slow one. If
that six minutes is what stops people running it, the fix is a per-run database
name the way `G5` does it (`SBH_TEST_DB_NAME`), which is a separate piece of
work and is named here rather than half-done.

The isolation proof of 2026-09-25 10:51 UTC recorded **287 passed · 8 failed ·
1 skipped · 2 errors** on real PostgreSQL 16 as `smartbillhub`
(`rolsuper = f`, `rolbypassrls = f`). **An error is a case that never ran**, so

## 2026-09-25 — **A UNIT INHERITS ITS ADDRESS'S SERVICES BY DEFAULT, AND THE SHORTFALL BECOMES COUNTABLE** (lane METER, `DEF-MET-6796`, `BR-MET-119` amended, `2.353.1`)

**The ruling, verbatim.** PO, 2026-09-25: *"the premises' list is what a unit
takes, the tick-list stays, and a clerk may untick"*.

**Why it is a DEFECT and not a change request.** `BR-MET-119` has said since
2026-08-26, in signed words, that *a unit INHERITS that list*. The create path
never implemented it: `_create_unit_inner` looped `data.get("services")` and
created one service point per ticked code. So this is the product failing to do
what a signed rule already said — the routing table's own test
(`13-change-process.md` §1) and the beta default. Filed `DEF-MET-6796`,
category `not-built`.

**What moved, in one word.** `INHERITS` becomes `INHERITS BY DEFAULT`. A unit's
set is now *within* the premises' set rather than equal to it. Nothing else in
the rule moves: a premises still DECLARES, a unit still has no list of its own,
a meter may still only attach against one of the unit's services, and
`_refuse_service_not_at_premises` is untouched — a unit may never take a service
the address does not offer, and the default is a subset of the offer by
construction.

**THE FIGURE THAT MAKES IT CONCRETE, worked for the PO.** A four-service address
— electric, water, sewer, trash — with three flats added through the Add units
wizard. Before: **twelve service points that should exist, and zero that do.**
After: twelve. Under `BR-BIL-300` service points decide what a bill charges, so
those twelve were four services the address advertises at three flats, on which
nothing was ever billed.

**ABSENT IS NOT EMPTY, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE FIX.** Three states, not two:
no `services` key means nobody was asked and the ADDRESS answers; `services: []`
is a clerk unticking everything and is honoured; a partial list is honoured.
`data.get("services") or []` cannot tell the first from the second, and that is
the shape the defect had in TWO places — in `_create_unit_inner`, and again in
`importers._stage_pattern`, which set the key **unconditionally**, so every unit
the add-units wizard has ever generated arrived at the create carrying an
explicit empty list. A service-layer default alone would have been overruled by
a key the clerk never sent, on the one door that makes units in bulk.

**A PREMISES HOLDING `NULL` INHERITS NOTHING, and the create still succeeds.**
`NULL` is *nobody has ever been asked* (`DEF-756`/`DEF-762`), and an address
nobody has been asked about has provisioned nothing — `BR-MET-119`'s own words.
Defaulting from it would have made the create die on a service nobody typed.

**NO MIGRATION, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `service_points` already carries
`tenant · unit · service` and nothing else was needed. The PO accepted that an
absent service point cannot be distinguished from a deliberate untick, and no
column was added to record the difference.

---

### The judgments this lane took, where the rules ran out

| # | Judgment | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The default is intersected with the tenant's ENABLED services, and the dropped codes are NAMED in a warning.** | An address that offered gas before the utility stopped selling it would otherwise make every new unit at that address refuse, on a create that had nothing to do with gas. A silent drop would be hard-won law 1 — a create quietly giving a unit fewer services than its address advertises is the defect this fix exists to close. |
| 2 | **The gap report draws NOTHING when nothing is short.** | A panel reading *Nothing missing* every day is furniture on a screen a utility opens all day (B14 rule 32's description budget). **The cost is stated rather than hidden: a clerk cannot confirm a zero from this panel.** The units list's own Services column answers that. |
| 3 | **The gap report is a SECOND table, not a chip on the first.** | Its rows carry two facts the units list has no column for — what the address OFFERS and what is MISSING. Folding them into `DataTable`'s `UnitRow` would give one table two row shapes. `PlainTable` + `ListPager` is the kit's own answer for a list that is not the shared table. |
| 4 | **The tick-list is CHIPS, not checkboxes.** | B14 rule 9 is binding and says a multi-select is removable chips. The ruling's *"a clerk may untick"* is satisfied either way — a chip's ✕ is how this product unticks. |
| 5 | **`_link_asset` now reads the unit's OWN service points instead of the request's `services`.** | It read `data.get("services") or []`, which is `[]` for every row that INHERITS — so a meter on such a row would have been attached with no service point at all. What the unit ended up holding is a fact only the create knows, and it is the fact a meter has to be fitted into. |
| 6 | **`test_tc5_the_premises_read_is_tenant_scoped` now creates its unit with an explicit `services=[]`.** | The test asserts `count() == 0` after a REFUSED call. Under the amendment the unit arrives already holding the water point, so the zero would have failed over a point that has nothing to do with the foreign read. An explicit untick is the ruling's own vocabulary and leaves the assertion about the tenant filter, which is what it was written for. |

---

### How the shortfall is made countable — `S4`/`A3`

`GET /units/service-gaps` → `selectors.units_short_of_offer_page`. A unit is
short when it holds fewer live service points than its address offers.

⚠ **`held < offered` IS SOUND ONLY BECAUSE THE OTHER SIDE IS GUARDED.**
`_refuse_service_not_at_premises` makes a unit's points a SUBSET of the offer, so
comparing two counts is the same question as comparing two sets — and comparing
counts is a thing SQL can do. **The subset guard is load-bearing for this read:
if it is ever relaxed, this comparison becomes wrong before it becomes slow.**
The PAGE still computes the SETS, so each row names its missing services, and a
row naming none would be the assumption breaking in public.

**HOW IT IS ANSWERED IN SQL WITH NO MIGRATION.** `services_available` is a JSON
list, so there is no portable `length(column)` to compare against. There does not
need to be: the number of DISTINCT offers in a utility is a handful, so their
lengths go into a `CASE` and the comparison happens in the database. The held
count is a **correlated subquery** rather than `Count(...)`, because
`units_queryset` carries `select_related("premises")` and an aggregate annotation
would put every premises column into the `GROUP BY` — which PostgreSQL refuses
and SQLite silently permits, i.e. a query that passes the whole suite and fails
on the only database this product runs on.

⚠ **A UNIT WITH ZERO SERVICE POINTS IS IN THAT SET, AND IT IS THE ROW THE OBVIOUS
IMPLEMENTATION LOSES.** Counting from the service-point table and grouping by
unit answers only about units that HAVE a point — so the units that are worst
off, which is every unit the Add units wizard has ever made, are exactly the ones
such a read cannot see, and the total reads low and plausible. The subquery is
coalesced to `0` for that reason and `T4` asserts it by name.

---

### A second door, NOT changed, and flagged rather than fixed

`apps/metering/connections.py::_commit_build` creates units directly
(`metering_models.Unit.objects.create`) and does not go through
`_create_unit_inner`, so it inherits nothing. It is the move-in / new-connect
build commit, which provisions through `connection_services` instead, and lane
MOVEIN owns that flow. **Those units DO appear in the gap report**, so the
shortfall is visible rather than silent — but whether that door should inherit is
a question for the lane that owns it.

## 2026-09-26 — **A REPORT CARD OPENED SETTINGS → COMPANY FOR SIX WEEKS, AND THE OBVIOUS GUARD WOULD HAVE PASSED OVER IT** (lane REP-P1, Reports Phase 1 · `P1.4` · `P1.6` · `DEF-REP-6812`, 2.354.1)

The report library's **User activity audit** card pointed at `/settings/audit-log`.
Walked in a browser at 1440 before a line was read: the card opens
**Settings → Company**. The audit log has had its own address, `/{tenant}/audit-log`,
since `OQ-029` closed; `/settings/audit-log` was the address it was reached from
when the card was written on 2026-08-16.

**Why nothing caught it, and it is hard-won law 2's mirror rather than a dead link.**
`/settings/audit-log` matches `settings/:tab` perfectly well. `SettingsPage`
resolves an unknown tab with `tabs.find(…) ?? tabs[0]`, so the wrong address
renders a **real screen** with no error anywhere — `tsc`, eslint, 14 report cases
and every gate green over it. `reportCentre.test.tsx` asserted what `ROUTE_TARGETS`
does **not** contain and never that what it does contain resolves.

### The judgment: a route check that only asks "does it match?" passes on this defect

The obvious guard is `matchRoutes(APP_ROUTES, address) !== null`. **It is green on
the defect**, because the router matched it; the SCREEN threw the value away. So
`routeTargetsResolve.dom.test.tsx` checks two things that fail independently:

1. the address is routed at all — against `APP_ROUTES`, which `screenIds.test.tsx`
   already ties to `SCREEN_ROUTES`, so there is one table here and not two;
2. every `:param` the address fills carries a value the receiving screen declares,
   read from that screen's **own** table (`SETTINGS_TABS`, `RATING_TABS`).

**A parameter with no registered vocabulary FAILS rather than being skipped.**
That is deliberate and it is hard-won law 7's fifth shape: `G32` reported
`0 unresolved` truthfully, of everything it could see, over 21 live refusals. A
skip here would make this file's green mean less than it says. The cost is one
line in `PARAM_VOCABULARIES` for the next lane that adds a parameterised target.

### Measured, on the running product at 1440

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| card `href` | `/brazosbend/settings/audit-log` | `/brazosbend/audit-log` |
| page it opens | `H1` **Settings**, tag `SET-01.profile` | `H1` **Audit log**, tag `SET-16 · S61` |

The other five targets were re-walked in the same browser run and each still
opens its own screen: `/finance/taxes`, `/finance/gl`, `/reports/account-ledger`,
`/reports/by-premises`, `/plans-rates/history`. **`S11 → /plans-rates/history`
passes the new check and must** — `history` is in `RATING_TABS`, so the guard does
not go red on a door that works.

**Rollback:** revert the two files; `ROUTE_TARGETS.S61` returns to the literal and
the guard goes red on it again, by name, which is the shape that made it findable.

## 2026-09-26 — **THE TWO NEW SCREENS WERE OPENED IN A BROWSER, AND THE BROWSER FOUND A DEFECT NOTHING ELSE COULD** (lane METER, `DEF-MET-6815`)

**Hard-won law 6, done properly.** Chromium 141 against a private clone
(`sbh_clone_metershots`, cloned from `sbh_tpl_6812b2e0`, migrated to the tip),
Django on `127.0.0.1:8791`, the built SPA served through
`07-frontend/server.mjs` on `:5791` with `/api` passed through — the same-origin
join `10-scripts/11-smoke-stack.sh` prescribes. Signed in as Dana Whitfield.
Screenshots at **1440 and 1280**, the two widths the staff app must work at.

### THE NUMBER THE PRODUCT OWNER ASKED FOR, MEASURED AT LAST

**44 of 131 units on the seeded utility are short of their address's offer — 88
missing service points.** Every address offers electric and water; **all 44 hold
ZERO service points**, not one or the other. That is why the report's *Offered
here* and *Missing* columns show the same two badges on every row on this data:
it is the truth, not a rendering fault, and the two columns differ the moment a
unit holds one of the two (`T4` asserts exactly that case).

### WHAT THE BROWSER FOUND — `DEF-MET-6815`

**The gap report was drawn inline, and it pushed the units list off the screen.**
Measured at 1440: the panel was **2,650px tall** — 44 rows at a 50-row page —
and **the units table began at y=3054**. A clerk opening Units to find a flat
met a whole exception report first.

⚠ **EVERY TEST PASSED ON IT, AND NOT ONE OF THEM COULD HAVE FAILED.** The jsdom
cases assert the count, the columns, the row text and the absence at zero. **A
count is a count whether it is drawn in 40px or in 2,650.** This is the exact
thing law 6 exists for — *"no gate looks at rendered output; nine defects were
found this way and by nothing else"* — and it was found in the first minute of
actually looking.

**THE FIX:** the report is a `Disclosure`, **closed by default**, which costs
one line — `Missing services … 44 units  Expand ▾` — and unmounts its body, so
the 44 rows are not built either. The read still runs, because the heading needs
the count. Opened, the full paged table is there; closed again, it goes.
B14 rule 32's *"a stated absence CLOSED by default"* is the same posture.

⚠ **AND THE HEADING WAS FOUR WORDS.** *"Short of the address (44)"* against
B14 rule 33's cap of THREE for a heading. It is `Missing services` now, with
the count in `Disclosure`'s own `value` slot — which is what that slot is for.

### A SECOND FINDING, SMALLER, AND ALSO ONLY VISIBLE IN A BROWSER

**The services tick-list sat at `margin-top: 0` and read as part of the sentence
above it.** `[data-panel] > .field + .field` gives every field in that wizard
`var(--space-5)` (B14 rule 39, PO 2026-09-11: *"the components are too much
close"*), and that rule deliberately does not reach a field following a
`<Note>` — its own comment says so. Measured: the note ended at **y=566** and
the `Services` label began at **y=583**, against **20px** between every other
pair of fields on the form. It now carries `mt-[var(--space-5)]` — **the
product's own token and not the number 20**, because two figures for one
distance is the drift rule 39's comment warns about. Re-measured after the fix:
`margin-top: 20px`, level with every sibling.

### The two questions this lane had named, answered

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| does the chip row wrap sanely at 1280 | **Yes.** `Electric ×` `Water ×` and the add-back select sit on ONE line at both widths; the row is 1086px at 1440 and 926px at 1280 inside a panel that is wider than both. Horizontal page overflow measured **0px** at both widths. |
| does the gap panel sit correctly above the units table | **It did NOT — that is `DEF-MET-6815` above.** It does now: the band sits between the bulk bar and the table's toolbar, and the units table's first row is on screen at both widths without scrolling. |

### 2026-09-26 · A POSTSCRIPT WORTH MORE THAN EITHER BUG: **TWICE IN ONE LANE, A NEW FINDING HID INSIDE AN ALREADY-RED GATE**

This lane classified its gate run correctly — 50 FAIL, every one of them named in
`12-governance/23-gate-suite-baseline-2026-09-25.md`, set difference EMPTY — and
that classification was TRUE and nearly cost two defects.

**`G86 house-style-controls`** was red for other files and its finding also read
*"features/metering/UnitServicesField.tsx hand-rolls a button"*. **`G35
version-lockstep`** was red for other reasons and its finding also read
*"VERSION 2.356.1 HAS NO CHANGELOG ENTRY — CHANGELOG.md's newest heading is
2.356.0"* — because both of this lane's changelog entries had been appended to
the FOOT of a file that is newest-first, 23,500 lines below where a reader
looks (`DEF-MET-6818`).

⚠ **THE SET-DIFFERENCE CHECK CANNOT SEE EITHER OF THEM, BY CONSTRUCTION.** It
asks *is this gate newly red* and the answer is legitimately no. The question
that finds them is a different one: **does this gate's FINDING name a file I
touched?** One command answers it —
`grep -oE "[^ ;|]*(<my files>)[^ ;|]*" <the gate log>` — and it is the check
this lane will carry forward.

**The general shape is hard-won law 7's *guard red and unread*, one turn of the
screw tighter:** a guard nobody reads is bad, and a guard everybody reads as a
KNOWN red is worse, because the known-ness is what stops the reading. A red
gate is not one fact. It is a list.

## 2026-09-26 — **THE REPORT CATALOGUE STOPS BEING A PYTHON TUPLE, AND THE THREE JUDGMENTS THAT COST** (lane REP-P1, Reports Phase 1 · `P1.1` · `P1.2` · `P1.3` · `P1.5` · `P1.7` · `P1.8`, 2.357.1)

`GET /reports` served `apps/reports/catalog.py`'s frozen tuple of **23 cards in
3 groups** until today, and the screen named every one of them through
`t("reports.card.<key>.name")`. It now serves **45 cards in 6 groups and 19
sub-groups** out of `report_definitions`, with search and two filters read
server-side. Walked in Chromium at 1440 and 1280: 45 cards, six group headings,
a search for *ageing* returning one, a Finance filter leaving eight, `Custom ·
0`, no horizontal scroll and no page errors.

### 1 · The name comes out of the row, and the nine translations are lost

The brief, p5: *"Until a report's name comes out of a row, no utility can ever
author one"* — because a utility cannot edit our locale catalogues. So the
server resolves `name_override` → `name_i18n[locale]` → `name`.

**A catalogue preference was built and deleted the same hour, and that is the
judgment worth recording.** Nine of the 23 old keys survive into the 46 and
`reports.card.<key>.name` holds an authored translation for each in all eleven
catalogues, so preferring that copy for a platform card looked like a free way
to keep ten languages. **Its own test found what it actually did:**
`reports/0003` renames `ar_aging` from *"AR aging summary"* to **"AR Ageing"**,
the drawing's own word, and the preference rendered the OLD name and ignored the
row. That is `P1.1` defeated — a locale catalogue a utility cannot edit quietly
outranking the row that exists so it can.

**So the retired mechanism is retired.** The cost is stated rather than hidden:
a non-English clerk now reads English report names. **`DEF-REP-6822`**, with
the count: 46 names + 6 groups + 19 sub-groups × 11 languages = **506 strings**,
of which **99 were authored and 9 are in use today**. B14 rule 35 — a catalogue
is written in its own language, never translated from English — so they are not
a lane's to author, and `name_i18n` is the slot they land in.

### 2 · A live screen lost its catalogue door, and it is filed rather than invented

The 23-card tuple routed a **By-premises summary** card to `S60`. The 46 seeded
rows hold no `by_premises` row, so the catalogue stops being a door to a screen
that is live, routed and tested. It is **not orphaned** — `AppShell.tsx:317`
lists `/reports/by-premises` as a nav child, so the sidebar still opens it — and
a forty-seventh platform row is the seed's to add, not this read's to invent.
**`DEF-REP-6821`**. Counted rather than papered over, because hard-won law 2's
mirror is a door that stopped pointing at a live screen and nobody noticed.

### 3 · Three drawn figures where our standard won, and one drawn control not built

* **The default page is 50, not the drawn 20.** B14 rule 37 makes every number
  in a wireframe an illustration, and 50 is one of rule 16's five ratified
  sizes — so the pager is real, `NFR-3` is satisfied, and all 45 cards fit one
  page. The drawn *"1–20 of 45 · Page 1 of 3"* is the shape, not the numbers.
* **`SubTabs` pads `px-4` where `.settings-tabs` pads 18px.** 18px is not on the
  scale; rule 44 says the scale wins and there is nothing to escalate. A
  2px-per-side difference from the three shipped Settings strips, deliberate.
* **The card has NO fill.** The 23-card grid carried `bg-surface`, which drew a
  grey panel behind every card; p20 draws a top rule and three lines of text on
  the page's own ground. Found by putting the running screen beside the drawing
  (hard-won law 6), not by a test.
* **The drawn `▦` is not built.** It is `DataTable`'s column chooser and the
  document's own TABLE CONTROLS row for this screen says *"Columns n/a, a card
  grid"*. A control onto nothing is law 2's mirror; the drawing and the
  document's prose disagree and the prose settles it.

### 4 · Two things the browser found that no test would have

**`0 sub-groups` on the Custom sub-tab.** The sub-line counted sub-groups from
the groups the PAGE draws, and Custom draws none — so it read *"45 reports · 6
groups · 0 sub-groups"* over a catalogue that has nineteen. p20 callout ① says
the sub-line states the shape of the CATALOGUE, so the two totals are now served
as their own numbers.

**A bare `Custom` beside `Standard · 45`.** Only the active sub-tab's count was
served, so the zero — *"Custom reads 0 on day one and that is the point"*,
callout ④ — was invisible until you clicked the thing that would teach you.
Both counts are served now, and both follow the other filters: counting them
before the search left the strip promising 45 over a grid holding one.

## 2026-09-26 — **THE 46 REPORT DRAWINGS STOP BEING A PDF, AND NOT ONE OF THEIR 53 WARNINGS NEEDED THE PO** (lane REP-REGISTER, brief p49–p73, `DEF-REP-6824`…`6829`)

**WHAT WAS DONE.** Pages **49–73** of `05-prototype/09 Reports Build Brief.pdf` — §03 *"The 46,
drawn"* — were read **as images at scale 4** (B14 rule 42) and transcribed into
`04-docs/05-modules/12-reports/02-business-rules.md` §R1–R46: per report, its group,
sub-group, dataset, date basis, **the drawn column list in the drawn order**, and its warning
**verbatim**. Those 53 warnings were in a PDF and in nothing else, and **a PDF is the one place
no check in this repo can read**. No other lane was pointed at these pages.

**THE JUDGMENT THAT COST MOST THOUGHT: NO OPEN QUESTION WAS MINTED.** 53 warnings, zero OQs. It
looks like an omission and it is the finding. **34 restate signed law** — hard rules 3, 4, 5, 6,
8, `BR-REP-001`/`003`/`004`/`005`/`009`/`016`/`021`/`023`/`024`/`030`/`034`, hard-won law 14 —
and **28 of the 34 carry an id**, so the honest act is to cite them. **13 are checkable and
unchecked**, of which **11 describe reports with no query behind them** — six of the nine
datasets have none — so their tests belong to the phase that builds the query and are named per
row rather than written as stubs that assert nothing. **6 contradict the product today** and are
defect rows. **Nothing was left that a person had to decide.** CLAUDE.md law 13 is explicit that
a judgment recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable and a question is the failure to make
one; this row is that record.

⚠ **AND LAW 13 EARNED ITS KEEP ON THE ONE CANDIDATE THAT LOOKED LIKE A RULING COLLISION.** R37's
warning reads *"Rates show four decimals and percentages six, displayed at the precision the rule
stores — hard rule 2"*, which reads as a head-on challenge to hard rule 2's *both DISPLAY 2* and
looked like a STOP-and-re-sign. **It is not.** `OQ-620(a)` was **CLOSED on 2026-08-27** with the
PO's own words — *"What does a tariff rate show? Four ($0.1420). A rate is not money and not a
quantity - 4 decimal places"* — built as `formatRate` and `BR-SHL-250`'s sixth row, with hard
rule 2 explicitly **not** changed. **A rate is a third kind, and the three live in
`06-backend/core/money_fields.py`: AMOUNT 4 · PERCENT 6 · RATE 6 stored; amounts and percentages
DISPLAY 2, rates display 4.** So the rate half of the sentence is law. **The percent half is
simply wrong** — `BR-RAT-087`, PO ruling 2026-08-20, CONFIRMED and built as `DEF-364`, says
percentages display two — and the sentence **cites hard rule 2 as its authority while stating the
opposite of it**. Filed as `DEF-REP-6829` **against the document**, not asked again: the PO has
now answered the decimal question three times (`OQ-285`, `OQ-286`, `OQ-620`) and a fourth ask
manufactures precisely the inconsistency law 13 exists to prevent.

**THE COLUMN-SET GAP, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED — AND NOTHING WAS SEEDED.** Phase 0
deliberately seeded **no `columns` on any of the 46**, because the drawn sets are *"a screen's
four-of-seven choice rather than a ratified list"*, `BR-REP-021` already names five reports as
column-unratified, and inventing 46 lists would be the seeder choosing (spec rule 7). **That
reasoning stands and this lane overturns none of it.** What it adds is the size of the gap, in
`10-scripts/rep_r1r46_drawn.py --report`, so the ratification question can be put to the PO with
figures: **48 of 51 drawings** show a different column count from the dataset their definition
names (only **R17**, **R18**, **R43** agree); the widest is **R1 Payments, 5 drawn against 19
declared**, then **R2**, **R14** and **R19** at 6 against 19.

⚠ **THE COUNT UNDERSTATES IT, AND THE SECOND NUMBER IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.** An empty `columns`
means *"every column the dataset declares"*, so the generic viewer does not show a **wider**
version of the drawn table — on **sixteen** of the 51 it shows a **different** one. `R28 Read
Completeness` heads ROUTE · READER · EXPECTED · ACTUAL · ESTIMATED · SKIPPED · MISSING ·
COMPLETE and `meter_reads` publishes one row per **read**: **not one heading corresponds**. Those
sixteen are reports whose rows are AGGREGATES, and **no column list can reconcile them — they
need a query.** A lane measuring only the counts would have reported a tidy superset problem and
missed that.

**WHY THE MEASUREMENT IS A SCRIPT AND NOT A PARAGRAPH.** CLAUDE.md: *"where a rule restates what a
tool does, name the tool and let a reader run it."* Every figure above moves the day a dataset
gains a column, so a sentence quoting one is wrong by the next commit.

**THE TRANSCRIPTION IS GUARDED, BECAUSE AN UNGUARDED ONE IS WORSE THAN THE PDF** — it rots and
still looks current. `06-backend/tests/test_rep_r1r46_drawn_register.py` compares the drawn record
against the seed **in both directions** and over the **symmetric difference**, not over two
counts, which can agree while naming different reports. Its sibling asserts **R17's footer carries
no cross-service quantity total** — hard rule 3, *"gallons plus kilowatt-hours is not a number"*.
**Both were proved RED first through pytest** (deleting R41's drawn record; adding a `usage` key to
the footer) and the code restored byte-identical. ⚠ **The second passes today for a reason that is
itself a defect** — `DEF-REP-6828`, the built query serves no usage column at all — **which is
exactly why it exists before the column does**, hard-won law 2's mirror applied forwards.

**SIX DEFECTS, AND THREE OF THEM SHARE ONE BLIND SPOT WORTH NAMING.**

| id | what |
|---|---|
| `DEF-REP-6824` | R5 draws **Cycle** as a parameter; `billing_register` accepts a date window and no cycle. The brief says so in its own warning. |
| `DEF-REP-6825` | R1 draws **Group by** = method · teller · purpose · day and a TELLER column; `payments_by_method` groups by method only. Three of the four reports do not exist. |
| `DEF-REP-6826` | The brief's R10 warning states the debtor read is *"unpaginated on purpose"* — **withdrawn by `CR-138` `P4` on 2026-09-23**; it pages and sorts in SQL. A justification-by-reference outliving its justification, **one document out** — the third carrier of that same withdrawn sentence. |
| `DEF-REP-6827` | **A FIFTH unpaginated read** — `/reports/by-premises` — outside the four `DEF-PAY-4221` names. |
| `DEF-REP-6828` | R17 is drawn with a USAGE column; the built query serves **seven of the eight cells** and no usage at all. |
| `DEF-REP-6829` | R37's percent-display sentence contradicts `BR-RAT-087`. |

⚠ **THE BLIND SPOT BEHIND 6824, 6825 AND 6828 IS ONE THING: A DRAWN PARAMETER BAR AND A DRAWN
COLUMN SET HAVE NO REPRESENTATION IN THE REPO.** The seeded row carries a register, a key, a name,
a group, a sub-group, a dataset and a basis — and **no parameters and no columns** — so there is
no data structure for any check to compare a query against. Each query is correct about everything
it does do, every test passes, and the gap is a column of a drawing nobody had opened. The
prevention is the shape `P2.12` already used for paging: **make it a FIELD a test can read rather
than a paragraph somebody remembers.**

⚠ **AND `DEF-REP-6827` IS HARD-WON LAW 7'S FIFTH SHAPE ONE REGISTER ALONG.** `DEF-PAY-4221`
**enumerates** its four places, truthfully, over a scope it never declared it was excluding — and
a defect that lists its instances goes stale the moment a fifth exists. Nothing counts the class.
The row deliberately does **not** extend `DEF-PAY-4221` in place, because rewriting its four would
destroy the evidence that **the enumeration was the mistake**.

**THE DATASET CROSS-CHECK CONFIRMS AN EXISTING GUARD RATHER THAN ADDING ONE.** All 46 resolve to
one of the nine, and `test_p0_6__every_definition_names_one_of_the_nine_datasets` already asserts
it. ⚠ **But the DRAWINGS name a composite source in twelve places** — R4 *"bills + reads"*, R32
*"jobs + meter reads"*, R36 *"identity + audit"*, R39 *"journal lines + accounts + reads"* — while
a definition holds exactly one dataset, **and two drawn source words are not datasets at all**:
`jobs` (the export pipeline's table, which §05 says is deliberately not one) and `identity` (a set
of attributes **on** the audit dataset). That is `DEF-REP-6797` seen from the drawings' end and
**no new row was filed for it**.

## 2026-09-26 — **AN ACCOUNT THAT BOUGHT THREE SERVICES WAS BILLED FOR SIX, AND THE FIX HAD TO NOT UNDO YESTERDAY'S RULING** (lane BILLNARROW, `DEF-BIL-6823` · `BR-BIL-1048`, 2.357.2)

**WHAT WAS WRONG, IN PLAIN WORDS.** On 25 September a clerk gained the ability
to say which of a property's services an account actually takes — six offered,
three bought (`BR-CUS-1101`). The bill never learned. It went on charging for
every service the PROPERTY is connected for, so a customer who took electric,
gas and fire was invoiced for water, sewer and trash as well.

**MEASURED BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN**, on a seeded six-service utility on real
PostgreSQL 16 (`10-scripts/br_bil_1048_account_subset_measure.py`). Account
`AC-2026-00003` was left holding three of its unit's six agreements and its
September bill came back **byte-identical at `$475.68` over fifteen lines**:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| electric | `$230.50` | `$230.50` |
| gas | `$46.25` | `$46.25` |
| fire | `$0.00` | `$0.00` |
| **water** | **`$98.10`** | **not on the bill** |
| **sewer** | **`$76.50`** | **not on the bill** |
| **trash** | **`$15.00`** | **not on the bill** |
| tax | `$9.33` | `$5.54` |
| **total** | **`$475.68`** | **`$282.29`** |

**`−$193.39` a month on one account** — `$189.60` of charges and the `$3.79` of
tax that was riding on them. Nine lines where there were fifteen.

**THE JUDGMENT THAT COST THE MOST THOUGHT, AND IT IS WHY THIS ROW EXISTS.**
There are two ways a service can be on a plan and not on a bill, they look
identical from inside the code, and they have OPPOSITE ruled answers:

* the property **has no connection** for it — `BR-BIL-301`, ruled by the PO the
  previous day, option (b): **a line at `$0.00`, marked *not connected***;
* the account **did not buy** it — this work: **no line of any kind**.

A service with no connection cannot have an agreement, so the naive narrowing
sweeps it up with the rest and reverses a one-day-old ruling in silence. So
`BR-BIL-301`'s list is computed FIRST and handed to the narrowing to exclude by
name, and `tc2` is the case that fails if anybody merges them later.

**AND IT COMES BACK WEARING A DIFFERENT SENTENCE IF YOU STOP ONE FUNCTION
SHORT.** Removing a service from the tariffs makes it *a service the unit has
that nothing prices*, which is `OQ-670`'s case — a `$0.00` line reading *(not
priced on this plan)*. A fix that stopped at the tariff list would still have
printed water, sewer and trash on the customer's bill, at zero, blaming the
plan. `tc6` is the only case that can see that.

**THE READ IS DATED, AND THE ALTERNATIVE WOULD HAVE BROKEN EVERY FINAL BILL.**
The obvious implementation asks *is this agreement still open* — which is what
the account screen's chips ask. But move-out stamps an end date on every
agreement (`BR-CUS-030`) and the FINAL bill is prepared afterwards, for a month
the customer plainly did have their services. An open/closed read would have
narrowed every closing customer's last bill to nothing and refused it. The
naive form was installed deliberately and the suite run: **one case went red,
`s2`, and the other three passed** — which is exactly the false pass it was
written for.

**IT CAN ONLY SUBTRACT, NEVER EMPTY.** When the read cannot tell — customers
has not published it, or the account holds no agreement overlapping the period
— it answers *nobody can tell* and the bill prices exactly as it did before.
An absence of rows is not a clerk's decision to buy nothing, and narrowing a
bill to zero on an absence would be a worse defect than the one being fixed.

**NO SIGNED FIGURE MOVES.** Narrowing removes whole services and touches no
per-service arithmetic. Asserted rather than asserted-about: on the engine
fixture the total goes `$124.00 → $55.00`, and the `$69.00` difference is
exactly the three refused services at `$23.00` each and nothing else.

**REGRESSION, MEASURED THE SAME WAY.** All **75** accounts of the seeded
utility were gathered and priced at the tip and again after the change: **73
byte-identical, 2 moved, and both were meant to.** One is `AC-2026-00003`
above. The other is the account this lane had narrowed to fire, sewer and
trash while reproducing — and it is the finding below.

**ONE NEW QUESTION, OPEN, NOTHING GUESSED — `OQ-BIL-12739`.** Sewer is priced
at 90% of the water the customer used (`BR-RAT-1030`). A clerk may now untick
water and keep sewer, and that account produces **no bill at all**: the engine
refuses by name and the account waits on the run's exception list with a
sentence a person can read. That refusal is `BR-RAT-1030`'s and predates this
work, so nothing has been chosen. Put to the PO as three answers, with (a) —
refuse the combination at the move-in door — recommended.

### 2026-09-26 — THE `journal_lines` DATASET QUERY, AND THE TWO THINGS IT REFUSES TO SAY (lane DS-LEDGER)

**The decision.** `apps/reports/datasets.py` has declared a dataset called
`journal_lines` since Phase 0 — grain *one journal line*, eight columns, ten
seeded definitions naming it — and nothing implemented it, so `runner.run()`
raised `DatasetNotExecutable` for all ten. `apps/ledger/reporting.py` holds nine
aggregates over journal lines and **not one of them returns a LINE**, so the
gap was a missing primitive rather than a tenth summary. The query is
`06-backend/apps/ledger/journal_lines_dataset.py`, it reads only, and it pages,
sorts and filters in SQL (`NFR-3`, brief §7.5). It reuses `reporting.py`'s
`_posted_lines` and `_one_currency` rather than re-deriving *whose books* and
*in what currency* — one derivation, per `BR-REP-002`.

**Judgment 1 — a narrowed set states NO verdict about the books.** `balanced`
is `None`, never `False`, the moment a filter narrows WITHIN an entry
(`account_from`/`account_to`, `service`, `account`, `premises`,
`tax_authority`). Worked: the fixture posts three balanced entries, six lines,
Σ 390.00 each side, difference 0.00, `balanced=True`. Narrowed to GL codes
4000–4999 it serves **three lines, Σ credits 390.00, Σ debits 0.00, difference
390.00, `balanced=None`** — the difference is still published because it is a
real figure about the rows in front of the reader, and it is explicitly NOT
evidence about the posting service. `False` there would fire `BR-LED-007`'s
release blocker on every chip a clerk clicks, and a warning that cries wolf is
not believed when it is real. This extends `CR-060` C24's identical ruling for
`trial_balance`'s property filter one level down, rather than re-arguing it.

**Judgment 2 — the declared `balance` column is served NULL on every row, with
a reason.** A running balance is cumulative over an ORDER, so it is a property
of a sequence rather than of a line, and §7.2.2 makes it SEMI-ADDITIVE — a
footer summing it is the canonical wrong answer the brief names first.
`apps.ledger.reporting.account_ledger` computes it for one account with a
carry-forward that survives a page; this dataset does not, and says so in
`problems` rather than serving a plausible number (`BR-REP-024`).

**Judgment 3 — `paginates` moved to `True` and its old value is filed as a
defect** (`DEF-REP-6830`). It read `False` with `DEF-PAY-4221` and
`ledger/reporting.py` cited beside it: a precise, sourced, checkable statement
about a read model **that had never been written**. `P2.12` asserts that field
and went green on it. A field recording a limitation of something ABSENT cannot
be told from one recording a limitation of something PRESENT — hard-won law 7's
*reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes*, in a data structure.

**What was NOT decided, and went to the register instead.** R17 Revenue Analysis
is seeded against `journal_lines` and its live query reads BILLING's invoice-line
read model; the drawing on p056 heads it *"journal lines"* and its RATE SCHEDULE
column is not a journal dimension, so the two readings genuinely disagree about
which book the report is struck from. Filed as `DEF-REP-6831` and left alone —
two derivations of one revenue figure is precisely what `BR-REP-002` forbids,
and choosing between them is a product question.

**Reports turned on:** 4 of the 10 on this dataset — R15 Trial Balance, R16
Journal Export, R18 Tax Remittance, R21 Close Pack. Six are reported unbuilt
with their reasons in the lane report; none of them is stubbed and none opens
onto a plausible number.

## 2026-09-27 · A total that cannot be trusted is refused rather than printed (`CR-142-BRC07` `P2.22`, lane REP-P2-MODEL, `2.362.0`)

**JUDGMENT, not a ruling put to the PO** — it implements §7.2.2 of the Reports
brief, which is already signed. Recorded here with its worked figures because
three of them were measured against the code rather than taken from the
document, and two of those measurements contradict the document.

**WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND HOW.** Ran
`10-scripts/cr142_p2_22_wrong_totals.py` against the code at `43366f956`:

| Measured | Figure |
|---|---|
| `totals={…}` maps built in `apps/reports/queries.py` | **9** |
| references to `assert_summable` or additivity on the render path | **0** |
| application-code callers of `runner.validate()` | **0** (tests only) |
| seeded definitions that group by anything | **0** |

So §7.2.2's *"nothing stops you today"* is **literally true and was still true
after `P0.16` shipped**: `P0.16` built the RULE and put it behind a SAVE-time
guard, and there is no save path yet (`P5.2` is Phase 5). The rule is right and
complete; what was missing was a caller on the render path.

**WHERE THE CALLER WENT, AND WHY THERE.** `runner.run()` — the one path the
viewer and the export both take (`P0.5`). Wiring the nine `totals=` maps in
`queries.py` instead would have been nine chances to miss one, and `queries.py`
is a file three lanes are editing this week.

**THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES THIS CORRECT RATHER THAN CAUTIOUS.** A SUBTOTAL
and a FOOTER ask different questions. Group the receivables by month: each
month's subtotal holds time FIXED and is a balance summed across households,
which is lawful and must stay a number; the grand total spans every month and
is not a receivable. Two functions, `subtotal_across` and `footer_across`. A
single shared one would be wrong for one of them whichever way it was written,
and a version that refused both would pass every refusal test in the suite and
make grouping useless.

**A FOOTER SPANS THREE THINGS, EACH A MEASURED CASE.** Every grouped dimension;
`service`, unless a filter pins it to one — which is how the two-units case is
caught with no grouping involved at all; and `time`, when the report covers a
range rather than an instant — which is why the ageing *as at a date* keeps its
total.

**TWO DECLARATIONS FOUND FALSE, BOTH FILED.** `DEF-REP-6846`: the shared `time`
dimension's hierarchy matches **none** of the nine datasets' declared calendars
and offers a calendar level on the one dataset that declares the billing
calendar. `DEF-REP-6847`: of **71** declared dimensions, **14** resolve to a
column their own dataset produces and **37** to a filter it accepts — so
deriving slicers from the declaration alone gives **34 dead controls**. AR
Ageing therefore gains **9** slicers and not the **13** p12 promises.

**ONE SIGNED-RULE COLLISION, NOT RESOLVED HERE.** `IS-11`/`BR-REP-018` says a
CSV carries no metadata rows; `P2.22` says the refusal appears in the CSV. Put
to the PO as `OQ-REP-12740` (hard-won law 13). What ships is the narrow
reading: the row is written only when a total refused itself, so every lawful
file is byte-identical to yesterday's.

### 2026-09-27 — THE `payments` DATASET QUERY, AND A GRAIN THAT WOULD HAVE DROPPED EVERY DEPOSIT (lane DS-PAYMENTS)

**Ten report definitions are seeded onto the `payments` dataset and TWO of them
produce a report today** — R1 Payments and R9 AR Ageing. **The other eight are
refused by name rather than served**, and the reason is the same one the two
sibling dataset lanes found before this one: **brief §7.2 says a dataset states
ONE GRAIN, and `payments` is being used as a bucket for "anything Receivables".**

**The ten, and what each one's DRAWING actually says its row is** — read as
images per B14 rule 42, p051–p058:

| id | report | the row its drawing draws | the source that owns it |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Payments | one GROUP of payments — method × teller | `payments` ✅ |
| R2 | Deposit Batches | **one deposit batch** | `payments.deposit_batches` |
| R3 | Payment Exceptions | **one exception EVENT about a payment** | reversals + transfers + `audit_log` |
| R9 | AR Ageing | one ACCOUNT's position as at a date | invoices − allocations ✅ |
| R10 | Debtor List | one ACCOUNT's position as at a date | invoices − allocations |
| R11 | Cut-Off List | one ACCOUNT's position + eligibility | + `account_collection_state` |
| R12 | Collections Activity | **one collections EVENT** | `notice_history` + `payment_plans` |
| R14 | Closed Account Balances | **one CLOSED ACCOUNT** | `customers.accounts` + final bill |
| R19 | Cash Reconciliation | **one RECONCILING ITEM** | `bank_lines` + `deposit_batches` |
| R20 | Deposits | **one ACCOUNT's security-deposit position** | `customers.accounts.deposit_*` |

**Not one of the ten is "one payment allocation", which is what the registry
declared.** R19's own drawing settles the coordinator's flag in one row: the
bank-charge line of −18.40 exists at the bank and **has no system row at all**,
so it is not a payment and cannot be a row of a payments dataset. R20's HELD,
APPLIED and REFUNDED columns read `customers.accounts`; a payment with
`purpose='deposit'` is only the TAKING event.

**THE DECLARED GRAIN WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT DROPS MONEY** (`DEF-REP-6853`).
`apps/payments/services.py` branches on `if not linkage.allocates:` and writes
**no `allocations` row** for a deposit, a prepay or a plan-down. Measured on a
perf tenant on real PostgreSQL 16: **400 of 2,066 payments carry no allocation
at all**, so an allocation-grain query would have served 1,666 rows and a
smaller day. A smaller day does not read as wrong; it reads as a quieter
Tuesday. **The grain built is ONE PAYMENT**, and a test asserts the deposit is
a ROW and the total is 598.55 rather than 448.55 on a five-payment fixture.

**AND R1 — MARKED AS ALREADY HAVING A QUERY — DOES NOT PAGE, WHICH IS THE
FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE NEW QUERY** (`DEF-REP-6854`). `reporting.
payments_by_method` runs `for payment in cleared:` over every payment in the
window and builds one `PaymentDetailRow` each; neither it nor its viewer takes
`page`, `per` or `sort`. Measured side by side against the new query on the
same 2,066 rows:

| read | statements | rows | seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| dataset · page 1 | **6** | 50 | **0.031** |
| dataset · last page (42) | **5** | 16 | **0.023** |
| dataset · group by method | 3 | 4 | 0.018 |
| dataset · stream (the export) | 4 | 2,066 | 0.690 |
| **TODAY · `payments_by_method`** | **2,068** | 2,066 | **3.344** |

**2,068 statements for 2,066 payments is an N+1** — one round trip per row for
the customer name, which is the same defect `P2.21` closed on the ageing and
never closed here. **The last page costs 0.76× the first**, which is the
property `NFR-3` actually asks for; a Python slice cannot hold that.

**AND THE DRAWING ASKS FOR FOUR GROUPINGS AND THE CODE HAD ONE** (`DEF-REP-6849`).
p052, verbatim: *"Group by switches this between method, teller, purpose and
day. **Four reports, one row.**"* `teller` is a DECLARED COLUMN of this dataset
and the word appears nowhere in the report that is supposed to serve it. All
four are now grouped in SQL; `teller` reads `payments.counter_session_id` →
`counter_sessions.owner`, and where that is null — electronic money, and
anything banked before tills — the row serves a null teller **beside a named
reason**, never the word "Unknown".

**A MONEY-PATH FINDING REPORTED RATHER THAN RECONCILED** (`DEF-PAY-6848`).
Hard rule 4's banked-tender refusal was confirmed in the code at both layers —
`amendments.refuse_tender_change_once_batched` and the `RAISE EXCEPTION` in the
`payments/0014` trigger — and **it fires correctly**. But both messages still
tell a clerk that *"deposits are grouped by day AND tender"*, which `P0.6`
superseded on **2026-09-22**: a batch is one **TILL** and one tender
(`UNIQUE (tenant, session, method)`). The refusal survived the ruling; its
stated reason did not. `amendments.py` carries an inline note recording the
amendment at two separate lines — **so the code knew and the strings did not
move**, which is hard-won law 1 one indirection out. R2's drawn warning carries
the same superseded sentence, and its rows show a batch whose tender is *"Cash
& cheque"*, which the ratified key cannot produce. **Neither is reconciled here:
the drawing is what should be, the code is what is, and a trigger's exception
text is a migration on a money path.**

**NOTHING SEMI-ADDITIVE IS SERVED FROM THE NEW QUERY, AND THAT IS THE POINT.**
The eight balance columns the registry declares — `current`, `d1_30`, `d31_60`,
`d61_90`, `d90_plus`, `total`, `deposits_held`, `accounts_active` — are
positions AS AT a date whose grain is one ACCOUNT. They are left **absent** with
a named reason rather than served as `0.00`, because a zero would make a footer
appear and a balance summed down a list of payments is the canonical wrong
answer §7.2.2 opens with.

**Reports turned on:** the dataset now pages, sorts and streams, and R1 gains
the three groupings its drawing demands. **Eight of the ten remain unproducible
and every one is refused with the source and grain it really needs** — none is
stubbed and none opens onto a plausible number.

## 2026-09-27 — **A UTILITY CAN NOW WRITE ITS OWN REPORT, AND SIX THINGS WERE WRONG THAT ONLY A BROWSER COULD SEE** (lane REP-P5, Reports Phase 5 · `P5.1`–`P5.4` · `P5.6` · `P5.7` · `P5.10` · `P5.11`, **`2.366.0`**)

⚠ **THE COMMIT SUBJECT OF `b3699fb1f` SAYS `2.365.0` AND THE VERSION THIS LANE
SHIPPED IS `2.366.0`.** Corrected here rather than by a force-push, which this
repo does not do. The cause is worth one line, because it is the shape of
`DEF-GOV-3756`: `allocate.py version --bump change` was called TWICE — once
before the push guard refused the whole set as stale, and once after every blob
had been re-derived from the new tip — and the message file was written from the
first answer while `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `pyproject.toml`
carry the second. **`package.json` is the source of truth and it reads
`2.366.0`.** The lesson generalises past the typo: **a version is a blob like
any other and belongs in the re-derivation, not only in the allocation** — the
ids in this entry were re-derived (a sibling had taken `DEF-REP-6861` while this
lane worked, caught by `push_paths.sh` and renumbered to `6862`–`6867`) and the
version in the commit message was not.

**WHAT A CLERK CAN NEWLY DO.** Open one of the forty-five reports we ship, change
which columns it shows, and save it under their own name. It appears on a new
**Custom** list, runs at its own address, and a colleague sees it only once it is
shared. That is the phase's DONE WHEN — *"a utility saves a report we never
wrote, shares it, and it appears in the catalogue for their colleagues and nobody
else's"* — and it was walked end to end in a browser against real PostgreSQL 16.

**THE TASK TABLE SAYS TWELVE TASKS AND ITS OWN MIX ROW SAYS TEN.** Counted off
the rendered pages (p16–p17, read as images per B14 rule 42): `P5.1`…`P5.12`.
The row reads `0 DB · 2 Backend · 3 Front end · 1 Settings · 2 Test · 1 E2E ·
1 Other-module` = 10; the real mix is **5 Front end**, not 3. `P5.3`, `P5.4`,
`P5.10`, `P5.11` and `P5.12` are all front-end rows. **Eight of the twelve are
built** — `P5.1` `P5.2` `P5.3` `P5.4` `P5.6` `P5.7` `P5.10` `P5.11`. Four are
not, and each is named with its reason at the foot of this entry.

### THE RULING THIS PHASE RESTS ON, CITED AND NOT RE-DERIVED
The builder is a **PANEL, NOT A WIZARD** — PO 2026-09-26, answered *"panel"*,
recorded in this log's own index row 25. It breaks a 42-file `WizardFrame`
convention on purpose: *"A forward fence fights that, and commit-at-the-end means
you cannot see your report until you have finished describing it."* Screen `2·2`
is therefore an edit panel beside the live table, and **the preview IS the
viewer** rather than a second renderer that could disagree with it.

### THE SPATIAL FACTS NO SUMMARY CARRIED, READ OFF THE DRAWING
p31 was opened as an image because *"an edit panel beside the live table"* is a
sentence and not a specification. What it actually draws: the panel is a narrow
column on the **right**, the table keeps its own toolbar, pager and rows one
column narrower, and the panel has **seven sections** — Report · Attributes ·
Measures · Filters · Group & sort · Where it lives, with the unsaved marker in
the rollup. A summary of this screen called it *"two sections"*. Measured on the
running product at 1440: the panel's left edge is at **1160px** and the table's
right edge at **1144px**, so it is beside rather than over, and horizontal
overflow at 1280 is **0px**.

Screen `2·4` is the same story one page on. The task row says *"name, category,
visibility"* — three fields. p35's own FIELDS row says **Four**: Name · Group ·
Sub-group · Visible to. The drawing is the specification.

### SIX DEFECTS, AND NOT ONE OF THEM WAS VISIBLE TO A GREEN SUITE
Every one was found by running the product. `tsc` was clean, 15 DOM cases passed
and 74 backend cases passed over five of the six.

| id | what was wrong | why nothing saw it |
|---|---|---|
| `DEF-REP-6862` | **An unlawful total was not refused at save.** `P2.17` taught `validate()` that a group target may be a LEVEL (`accounting_period`) and did not change the line three below it, which still handed `assert_summable` the raw levels — and it compares DIMENSION names. So *group by `time`* was refused and *group by `accounting_period`*, the only way a clerk would ever express **by month**, was not. The render path was correct all along, because `_shaped` maps levels through `slicers.footer_across`. | Nothing compared the two paths, and no test asserted the refusal through a level name. This is the one that lets a clerk build a report showing $41,220.00 + $44,118.50 + $48,221.14 = **$133,559.64**, a figure nobody owes. |
| `DEF-REP-6863` | **Save as opened with an empty Group while its select drew *Billing*.** An HTML `select` whose value is `""` draws its first option, so the dialog looked filled and every first save was refused by the client schema with *"String must contain at least 1 character(s)"*. Found twice: the second time because `GET /reports` answers ONE sub-tab, so a report on **Custom** had no card to seed from at all. Closed by serving the report's own `group` on its payload. | Every test passes a group in explicitly. |
| `DEF-REP-6864` | **A private report was served to every colleague.** `catalogue_read.py` contained the string `visibility` **zero times**. The column landed in `P0.1`, the constraint with it, the control on `2·4` — and no read ever filtered on it. | RLS cannot catch it: the policy is scoped to the TENANT and both users are in one. Every test had one user. |
| `DEF-REP-6865` | **A refused save said nothing at all.** `onSubmit` let the `ApiError` propagate instead of returning `{ok:false, error}`, so the server refused correctly — right status, right key, right params — and the dialog sat there with no sentence. | The key resolves in all eleven catalogues, G32 passes, the backend case asserts the refusal. Only a browser shows that a click did nothing. |
| `DEF-REP-6866` | **Every tenant-authored report was drawn as a dead card** reading *"This report cannot be produced yet."* `_viewer_keys()` returns the per-REPORT viewers; `runner.queries_for` has TWO lookups and falls back to the DATASET's query, which is the brief's whole arithmetic. ⚠ **Its own docstring claimed it read `runner.queries_for` "so this file cannot drift from what the viewer will actually do"** — hard-won law 1, word for word. | Phase 1 had no tenant rows to test with. |
| `DEF-REP-6867` | **A saved report could be listed and never opened.** `_VIEWERS` is frozen at import, so `GET /reports/{key}` answered *"There is no report called overdue-60"* while the runner served it perfectly. The viewer also titled it `overdue-60` — a slug on screen, which is B14 rule 31. | The backend suite calls the runner; the DOM suite mounts components; nothing opens a saved report in a browser. |

**THE PATTERN IS WORTH MORE THAN THE SIX.** Five of them are the same shape:
**code that was correct while every row was one of ours, and wrong the first day
a utility wrote one.** A frozen dict of keys, a catalogue that reads one sub-tab,
an availability check that knows about shipped viewers, a title that comes from a
translation catalogue. None of it was careless; all of it was written before
there was such a thing as a tenant's own report. **When a phase turns data that
was ours into data a customer writes, grep for every place that enumerates the
old set.**

### THE JUDGMENTS THIS LANE MADE, RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-LITIGATES THEM
1. **`?edit=1` is a QUERY PARAMETER and not a new segment.** Ruling 3 signs the
   reserved list at FOUR. Every new segment under `/reports` is a word a utility
   may never name a report, so giving the builder its own segment would have
   widened a signed rule on this lane's authority. A parameter costs nothing.
2. **`/reports/custom` is the SAME screen on its second sub-tab**, not a second
   page — p23 calls the strip *"the whole argument for a sub-tab over a filter"*,
   and a second page is a second catalogue read, toolbar and empty state to keep
   in step. The segment **stays reserved** even though it now opens a screen,
   exactly as `history` did in `P3.2`.
3. **Visibility is filtered in the READ, not in the policy, and the reason is
   written down.** §8.1's *"row-level security does that work"* is about the
   TENANT boundary and it holds — proved three ways on real PostgreSQL. Privacy
   between two colleagues **inside** one tenant is a boundary the policy has no
   notion of; making it one means a second GUC (`app.user_id`) on every request
   and read by every policy. That is a platform decision, not a reports one, and
   it is recorded on `DEF-REP-6864` so it is made deliberately rather than
   inherited.
4. **`columns` became a RUN CONTROL**, exactly as `group_by` did in `P2.17` and
   for the same reason: the panel's ticks are a control a clerk turns, and a
   live preview is impossible while the only column list the runner reads is the
   one already stored. It is **not a hole in §8.1** — every name is checked
   against the dataset's declaration and an unknown one is dropped.
5. **B14 rule 9's multi-select is NOT used for the attribute list.** Rule 9's
   subject is a field picking values from a flat set; this is an ORDERED list
   whose rows carry show, move and rename, and `P5.11` requires the last two by
   name. The kit is still what it is BUILT from (rule 44).
6. **Reordering is two buttons, not a drag.** The drawing shows a drag handle; a
   drag with no keyboard path is a control half the readers cannot use.

### WHAT IS NOT BUILT, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED
* **`P5.5` · screen `E·2`, the Reports section of Settings → Configure →
  Reference data.** It needs a `/lookups` handler for `report_categories` and a
  new `reports` group in `referenceDataConfig.ts`; the grid pattern exists and
  the work is real but untouched. **A tenant can therefore add no catalogue
  category of its own yet**, and a saved report must be filed under one of the
  six we ship.
* **`P5.8` · the `J-REP-04` journey file.** The journey is WALKED — every step of
  it, in `10-scripts/rep_p5_builder_walkthrough.mjs` — and the markdown in
  `08-qa/01-e2e/journeys/` is not written.
* **`P5.9` · role gating on a definition (`min_role`).** `BR-REP-023` restricts
  the access-review report to System Admin and Executive and **nothing enforces
  it**; every card is served to any tenant role today. Untouched by this lane.
* **`P5.12` · the link from `5·1` History's retention line to `E·2`.** It points
  at a screen `P5.5` did not build.
* **Building a report FROM SCRATCH.** 1·2B draws one whose *Based on* reads
  *from scratch*. It needs a preview that runs a DATASET rather than a saved
  KEY, and `GET /reports/{key}` resolves a definition first — so there is no read
  path for a report that has never been saved. Inventing one is an interface
  decision beyond this lane. `+ Build your own` therefore opens the **Custom**
  list, whose empty state carries p22's own instruction — *"Open a standard
  report. Change it. Save it here."* — which callout ② itself calls *"the usual
  way a custom report gets made"*.

### A RED THIS LANE DID NOT CAUSE, DATED
`phaseHolds.dom.test.tsx` HOLD 1 — the four-tab strip — had been **red since
`007510e95`**, the Phase 3 commit that mounted `ReportRunsPage` at
`/reports/history`. Dated with `git log -S`, which is law 7 habit 1: *was this
red before I started?* is a claim about history. The hold expired the moment that
commit merged and its two cases had been naming the right thing to a reader
nobody sent. Both are retired here, in the same file as this lane's own expired
hold, and the first case now asserts the strip IS drawn — because a check that
only said *no Dashboard tab* would pass just as happily over a screen with no
strip at all.
