## 2026-09-27 — THE PATH SAYS WHICH TENANT; THE TOKEN ONLY SAYS WHO (`P2.20`), AND A GROUP ROW'S `path` IS NOT A FILTER SET (`P2.18`)

**Lane REP-P2-TAIL · `CR-142-BRC07` Phase 2 tail + the Phase 0 task that was
never met.** Four tasks: `P2.18`, `P2.20`, `P2.21`, `P0.7`. Three judgments here
that the rules did not decide, each with the figure it was decided on.

### 1 · A subtotal's `path` is what it IS, not what reproduces it (`DEF-REP-6869`)

`slicers.group_rows()` shipped with this in its own docstring: *"The path IS the
filter set, so the rows behind a subtotal cannot be a different query from the
one that produced it."* A sibling reported the drill-through data as already
built on the strength of it. **Measured on real PostgreSQL 16 against the seeded
demo tenant, it is wrong three separate ways and each is enough alone:** the
path names the dimension `consumer_class` where the `payments` dataset declares
the filter `class`; it carries the DISPLAY label `Commercial` where the filter's
vocabulary is the code `commercial`, which the row holds in a sibling column
`account_class_code`; and its `column` names the display column.

**Replaying a path verbatim returns 30 rows — THE WHOLE REPORT — for a group of
11 and for a group of 19 alike**, because `runner.bind` discards a parameter the
dataset does not declare and says nothing. On a tenant with one group that reads
as a perfect match, which is how it would have shipped.

**The judgment: the SERVER emits each group row's reproducing filters, derived
from the dataset's declared filter names and the member row's code column, and
emits `null` where it cannot.** A client assembling them would be a forty-seventh
place to keep a vocabulary in step. `null` draws NO control at all rather than a
disabled one, because a drill-through that opens the unfiltered report under a
chip naming one group is worse than an absent one — the clerk cannot tell.
Measured after: subtotal 11 rows → `{"class": "commercial"}` → 11 rows; 19 → 19.

**And the check that would have caught it is an EFFECT assertion, not a shape
one.** `tests/test_rep_p2_17_slicers.py` asserts the path has the keys
`dimension`, `column` and `value`, and a path with the right keys carrying the
wrong vocabulary satisfies every one of its cases.

### 2 · 44 of 71 subtotals cannot be opened, and that is a register (`DEF-REP-6871`)

`P2.17` gives every report its dataset's whole dimension set as slicers; `P2.18`
says every subtotal opens. **Nobody compared the two tuples.** Measured over
`datasets.DATASETS`: 71 dataset/dimension pairs, **44 with no declared filter
that can select them** — journal_lines 7 · accounts 7 · invoices 6 · payments 6 ·
meter_reads 6 · work_orders 5 · assets 3 · rate_schedules 2 · audit_log 2. Nine
of the 44 are `time` and are a different fault worth separating: the filter NAME
exists (`from`/`to`) and what is missing is the derivation from a time LEVEL and
VALUE to a pair of dates. **The number is asserted in the suite so it moves only
when somebody decides it should.**

### 3 · `P2.20` — the PATH chooses the tenant, and the RLS proof is what decided it

The first design resolved the tenant FROM the bearer token, looking the
credential up with no tenant context. **`10-scripts/rep_p2_20_service_account_rls_proof.py`
refused it on real PostgreSQL before it reached a test:** `FAIL 5 · brazosbend's
token resolves to brazosbend — resolved to nothing`. That failure is the policy
working — a read with `app.tenant_id` unset evaluates `tenant_id = NULL`, which
is not TRUE, so the table yields zero rows. **The only way to make the first
design work would have been to read the credential outside row-level security,
setting the tenant GUC from an unauthenticated header**, which is the hole the
table exists to keep shut.

**So the token is looked up inside the tenant context `TenantContextMiddleware`
has already set from the `/api/{tenant}/…` path segment**, exactly as a screen's
data is. Three consequences, all better than the rejected version: there is no
bypass anywhere; the cross-tenant refusal is the POLICY's rather than a slug
comparison somebody has to remember to write; and it is the same rule
`apps/identity/auth.py` applies to a session. **Proved with two tenants under a
NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role: a token is found on its own tenant's path,
INVISIBLE on the other's, and invisible with no context at all — ALL PASS.**

⚠ **CLAUDE.md hard-won law 14's exact shape:** the default suite is in-memory
SQLite, which has no row-level security of any kind, and would have passed the
broken design green on every machine.

**Two rulings read narrowly rather than generously, both stated rather than
assumed.** §7.8 p89: the PO wrote *"a · Administrators only … M. Okonkwo creates
it and hands Dana the token + clerk"*, and Dana is a billing clerk — so an
administrator ISSUES and any staff member HOLDS, and whether a clerk may also
CREATE one is *"one line"* that is NOT taken. And an EMPTY `report_keys` grant
denies everything: an empty list meaning *all* would turn a half-finished create
into a key to the building, silently.

### 4 · `P0.7` is still not met, and the residue is four with a reason each

Two of the six deleted — `CATALOG` (with `ReportCard` and `catalog_payload`,
which had no reader left after `P1.1`) and `VIEWER_SEGMENTS` (four rows, every
one of them `key.replace("_","-")`, over a catalogue of 46 — the other 42 were
already working through its fallback). **Four remain:** `VIEWERS` is in
`queries.py`, which lane REP-UNBLOCK owns this session; `MONEY_COLUMNS` and
`NUMERIC_COLUMNS` are blocked on `DEF-REP-6870`, measured — deriving them from
the dataset declaration matches the hand-typed map on `ar_aging` (6 of 6 money
columns) and on money for two others, and declares **none of
`revenue_by_service_rate`'s seven served columns**, because that definition
names the `journal_lines` dataset while serving a service-by-tariff aggregate;
`REPORT_FILTERS` is the per-report OFFERED set, narrower than the dataset's on
purpose, and deriving it would widen every report's bar onto filters its query
does not honour — *"13 slicers, free"* delivering 9.

**The count is asserted in `tests/test_rep_p07_maps_deleted.py` in both
directions**, so closing one is a deliberate act rather than drift — which is
the rot CLAUDE.md's own rule-count line has suffered six times.

## 2026-09-27 — lane DS-SMALL: the last three dataset queries, and two reports refused on grain

**The decision, in one sentence:** the `work_orders`, `assets` and
`rate_schedules` dataset queries are built at the grains their datasets declare,
which serves **R31 Meter Fleet** and **R33 Service Order Activity**, and **R34
Disconnect & Reconnect** and **R37 Rate Change History** are **refused by name**
because the grains their drawings state are not the grains their datasets do.

**Why, with the worked numbers.**

**R34** — the drawing (p065, read as an image per B14 rule 42) is dated
*"work orders + accounts"* and every drawn row is an ACCOUNT carrying the whole
five-state sequence: `100907 · Okafor, D. · 418.90 · notice 02/09 · disconnected
11/09 · paid 418.90 · reconnected 12/09 · Restored`. The `work_orders` dataset
states *one work order*. **An account cut and restored inside the window has TWO
orders**, so it appears twice and `Σ BALANCE` double-counts the debt. Its own
warning says a supervisor reads it to answer *"where is each account in the
sequence"*, which is one row per account by construction. Independently,
`BR-REP-021` (PO RP-3, 2026-08-08, CONFIRMED) holds its column set unratified,
so the catalogue card's present sentence stays true and **no column set is
invented**.

**R37** — the drawing (p066–p067) puts **one COMPONENT** on each row: *Usage
tier 1 · 0.0142 → 0.0154 · +8.5%*. The `rate_schedules` dataset states *one
rate-schedule version*, and a version owns MANY priced components — measured
against `apps/rating/models.py`: `base_charge` (one), `RateTier.unit_price` (one
per tier per season per size class), `RateSizeRow`, `CapacityRate`,
`TimeOfUseWindow`, `DemandRateConfig`. **A four-tier schedule whose tiers all
move on 1 October is four drawn rows and ONE row at this grain**, and the dataset
declares a single `unit_rate` column with nowhere to name which of the four it
holds. `WAS`/`NOW` are additionally a diff against the superseded version, for
which no column is declared.

**And R37's drawn second source is refused on a rule that already exists.** The
drawing dates it *"rating + audit"*. `apps/rating/models.py`'s comment on
`TariffVersion.corrected_by` rules it verbatim: *"NOT read back out of
`audit_log`: that table is pruned on a retention schedule … so a rate history
sourced from there would lose its `BY` column silently."* `OQ-1340` closed that
retention question on 2026-09-23 with **no row type exempt**. So `BY` comes from
rating's own `submitted_by` / `corrected_by` / `approved_by`. **Nothing was put
back to the PO** — hard-won law 13: it is ruled, in the module that owns it.

**What was NOT reconciled, deliberately.** R37's warning says *"percentages
six, displayed at the precision the rule stores"*. That is already split and
signed: the RATE half is law (`OQ-620(a)`, CLOSED 2026-08-27, PO verbatim *"Four
($0.1420). A rate is not money and not a quantity"*) and the PERCENT half is a
filed defect against the drawing (`DEF-REP-6829`; `BR-RAT-087` and hard rule 2
both say DISPLAY 2). **The query displays nothing and rounds nothing** — every
figure leaves as the stored `Decimal` — which is the only posture that keeps a
❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure safe.

**Measured on PostgreSQL 16** (`10-scripts/ds_small_datasets_cost.py`, median of
3 after a discarded warm-up, 40,025 work orders · 40,074 assets · 2,005 dated
versions in one tenant):

| read | statements | rows | seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `work_orders` page 1 (per=50) | 2 | 50 | 0.418 |
| `work_orders` page 801 (last) | 2 | 25 | 1.946 |
| `assets` page 1 (per=50) | 5 | 50 | 0.644 |
| `assets` page 802 (last) | 5 | 23 | 0.638 |
| `rate_schedules` page 1 (per=50) | 10 | 50 | 0.071 |
| `rate_schedules` page 41 (last) | 10 | 5 | 0.052 |
| `assets` stream (40,073 rows) | 44 | 40,073 | 24.649 |

**`work_orders`' last page costs 4.65× its first, and `EXPLAIN` says why it is
not the defect the threshold was written for.** The `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` IS applied
in SQL; underneath it a `Parallel Seq Scan` feeds a `Sort` with *"Sort Method:
external merge Disk: 3888kB"* on **every** page including page 1, because
`work_orders` carries four indexes and **none on `created_at`** — which is the
raise date, R33's declared basis and this dataset's default sort. Filed as
`DEF-MET-6881`; the index is metering's migration to add and not this lane's
(migration ordering is a sensitive path and three sibling lanes were running).

**Two further rows filed, both about declarations rather than about code.**
`DEF-REP-6879` — the two grain mismatches above, as a register row so they are
counted rather than living only in a docstring. `DEF-REP-6880` — `WORK_ORDERS`,
`ASSETS` and `RATE_SCHEDULES` declare fewer columns and measures than their own
drawn reports need (`average_days_to_close` is non-additive and undeclared;
`age_years`, `status_class`, `premises_address` and the two absence kinds are
served and undeclared). The declarations are **not edited from these lanes**:
`datasets.py` is shared and P0.16's owner declares a measure's additivity once.

## 2026-09-27 — **SIX REPORTS RIDE ON `meter_reads` AND THREE OF THEM ARE NOT ABOUT A READ** (lane DS-METER, `CR-142-BRC07`)

**JUDGMENT, not a ruling put to the PO.** It applies §7.2 of the Reports brief,
which is already signed: *a dataset states ONE GRAIN*. Recorded here because
three of the six seeded definitions are refused by name, and a refusal nobody
writes down is re-litigated by the next lane.

**HOW THE SIX WERE READ.** As IMAGES at scale 4 per B14 rule 42
(`10-scripts/pdf/pdf_render.py` over `05-prototype/09 Reports Build Brief.pdf`):
p061, p062, p063, p064, p065 for the drawings, p083–p087 for §7.2/§7.2.2
additivity, the read path and scale, p090–p092 for §08.

### 1 · Three serve, three do not

| id | report | what ONE ROW is, from the drawing | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| R45 | My Usage | one read, per period, per service | **served** |
| R29 | Consumption Exceptions | one read that tripped a rule | **served** |
| R30 | Usage & Ranking | one account, ranked | **grouped** — 7 of 8 columns |
| R28 | Read Completeness | one route | **refused** |
| R32 | Read Import Log | one import | **refused** |
| R46 | Bill Projection | one projected charge component | **refused** |

**R28 is refused because of its DENOMINATOR, and that is the durable reason.**
p063 heads EXPECTED, which is *a count of reads that did not happen* — and a
read that did not happen has no row in `meter_reads`. No filter, no group and no
join can produce it. The arithmetic already exists elsewhere:
`apps/metering/completeness.py::cycle_coverage`, whose denominator walks
`assets → service_points.cycle_id` through `PlanRegisterResolver` to read each
unit's RATE PLAN. None of those tables is in this dataset.

**R32 is refused because of REJECTED.** A rejected row never became a meter
read — it sits in `read_import_rows` with `meter_read_id` NULL. A read-grain
query counts the accepted and is structurally blind to the rejected, so the file
would not look wrong; it would look like a clean import. Its natural key is
`ReadImportBatch`. The brief names the source itself: *"jobs + meter reads"*.

**R46 is refused because two of its four drawn rows have no read behind them at
all** — `Water base` and `Sewer base`, both `Monthly`, quantity `1 month`. It is
a rating output with an error bar, and it carries money (`RATE 0.0142`,
`PROJECTED 59.64`) that this dataset publishes no column for.

### 2 · Hard rule 3 is a refusal in code, not a sentence in a docstring

§7.2.2 (p085): *"Consumption — additive **within one service** — gallons plus
kilowatt-hours is not a number."* `consumption_total()` counts the DISTINCT
UNITS in the **same aggregate call** as the sum, and where there is more than
one it returns `total=None`, `unit=None` and a reason. It does not sum and
label, pick the commonest unit, or convert.

**Measured on real PostgreSQL 16** (`10-scripts/ds_meter_reads_cost.py`, clone
`sbh_clone_ds_meter`), over a set holding `gal`, `kWh` and `kgal`: the total was
REFUSED with `consumption_spans_more_than_one_unit`, and the same set narrowed
to one unit returned **1,500 rows totalling 15,000.000000 gal**. Both halves are
asserted, because a refusal that is really *"always None"* is not a refusal.

### 3 · R30's warning is structural, not documented

p064: *"One service at a time, and the dropdown is not optional… The service
parameter is required, not defaulted."* `account_usage_ranking(service=…)` is
keyword-only **with no default**, so a caller that omits it raises `TypeError`
at the call site. A default of `None` meaning *all* would have had exactly the
bug the warning names.

### 4 · R28's warning read like a live defect and is not one — checked

p063: *"Route R-03 has no reader and still reads 100% complete — an unassigned
route is a scheduling gap, not a read gap."* `cycle_coverage` reports per CYCLE
with no route breakdown and no reader column, so no shipped surface conflates
them today. The fact an R28 lane needs exists: `metering.models.Route.
assigned_to`, whose own comment reads *"NULL = System (auto-pull)"* — render
that NULL as *Unassigned*, never as a gap.

### 5 · R32's savepoint warning is about the WRITE path, and it is obeyed

p065: *"A rejected row is skipped inside its own savepoint — hard-won law 14."*
Checked rather than repeated: `10-scripts/ds_meter_reads_cost.py
--savepoint-audit` finds `with transaction.atomic():` nested around the
`_post_row` call in `apps/metering/services.py` (line 8862 at `b6312ef47`), and
the module header at line 70 states the reason in full. **The audit was proved
RED first** by removing that one line — it printed the failure and exited 1.

### 6 · `select_related` on a partitioned table defeated the LIMIT, and cost 7×

**MEASURED, not inferred.** `meter_reads` is PARTITIONED MONTHLY on `read_at`
(DB-7/NFR-24, BR-MET-055) and the proof clone carries 28 partitions
(2024-09 → 2026-12). The first version of this query loaded its two labels with
`select_related("account", "asset")`. On PostgreSQL 16, 40,201 reads in one
tenant, page 1 of 50 with `ORDER BY read_at, id`, median of 5:

| what was run | seconds |
|---|---|
| page, `ORDER BY` **+ `select_related`** | **0.345** |
| page, `ORDER BY`, no `select_related` | 0.011 |
| page, no `ORDER BY`, no join | 0.011 |

**The join defeats the `LIMIT` pushdown** — the planner joins the whole
partitioned parent to `assets` and `accounts` before it cuts fifty rows, so the
work scales with the tenant's whole read history rather than with the page. At
T5 the brief puts that history at ~480,000 rows, twelve times what was measured.

The labels are now resolved AFTER the page, in two `IN (…)` reads bounded by
`per` — the shape `payments_dataset._teller_names` already uses. Whole-call
figures over the same 40,201 rows, median of 3:

| call | before | after | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| page 1 (per=50) | 0.604s | **0.054s** | 4 |
| page 805, the LAST page | 0.652s | **0.129s** | 4 |
| page 1 sorted by consumption | 0.613s | **0.114s** | 4 |
| R30 ranking, group by account | 0.547s | **0.286s** | 2 |
| R45 portal, one account | 0.072s | **0.022s** | 4 |
| export, whole set streamed | 13.588s | **3.791s** | 43 |

**The last page is not slower than the first** in any run, which is the property
that distinguishes a SQL `OFFSET` walk from a Python slice over everything.

⚠ **MEASURED TWICE, AND THE SECOND RUN IS QUOTED TOO BECAUSE THE MACHINE WAS
NOT QUIET.** A later run of the identical script, with eight sibling `pytest`
processes on the same box, gave page 1 **0.115s**, last page **0.123s**, ranking
**0.246s**, portal **0.050s** and the export **5.598s**. Same order of
magnitude, same verdict on every property, and the last page still not slower
than the first. The figures above are the quieter box; these are the loaded one.
Neither is averaged with the other, because a median across two different
machine states is a number describing no machine.
⚠ **The statement that still costs real time is the R30 ranking at 0.286s** — a
`GROUP BY account_id, unit` over the whole window is a full scan by nature, and
it is named here rather than averaged away.

**RLS proved on the same run**, under a role that is neither superuser nor
`BYPASSRLS` (`smartbillhub`, `rolsuper=f rolbypassrls=f`) against a table with
`relrowsecurity` and `relforcerowsecurity` both true: a second tenant holding
2,201 heads, and **none of its 2,202 row ids reachable by id** under the first
tenant's `app.tenant_id`; rows, stream and footer all 40,201.

⚠ **THE FIRST ISOLATION CHECK FAILED AND THE CHECK WAS WHAT WAS WRONG.** It
compared the dataset against `MeterRead.objects.count()` and printed
`40201 against 40202`, which reads exactly like a leak and was one superseded
read being correctly excluded (BR-MET-016/053). The baseline is now spelled the
way `_base()` spells it, and the count — which is the weak question, since two
tenants can hold the same number — now sits beside the strong one: are any of
the other tenant's specific ids reachable at all.

### 7 · Two judgments recorded so nobody re-litigates them

**The lineage-head filter takes no argument.** `superseded_by_id__isnull=True`
is unconditional and a caller cannot switch it off: a report counting a read and
its correction counts one meter twice, and the wrong answer is LARGER, so it
reads as a busier month rather than as an error.

**`ESTIMATED_Q` is a second spelling of `selectors.read_is_estimated` and is
allowed only because a test forbids it from drifting.** That helper is the one
derivation and takes two Python values, so it cannot be applied in a `WHERE`.
The test walks the full cross product of `READ_STATUSES` × `DISPOSITIONS` + None
— **one real row each, through the database, not through `Q.check()`** — and
fails naming any status and disposition where the two disagree.

### 8 · What is NOT built, named rather than left to be discovered

**R45's `NEIGHBOURHOOD AVERAGE` tile (p061, `152 gal`) is not served and must
not be bolted on without a ruling.** It necessarily reads other customers'
consumption on a customer-portal screen, and an average over a small enough
neighbourhood identifies a household. Nobody has decided what the floor is. It
is an open question, not an omission.

**R30's `BILLED` column is `None` with a stated reason, never `0`** (BR-REP-024).
A zero there reads as *"used 148,200 gal, billed nothing"*, which is a defect
report rather than a report.

## 2026-09-27 — lane DS-ACCOUNTS: the `accounts` and `audit_log` dataset queries, a TENTH dataset for `notifications`, and five of eight reports refused on grain (`2.370.0`)

**The decision, in one sentence:** the `accounts` and `audit_log` dataset
queries are built at the grains their datasets declare — which serves **R22
Account Census** and **R35 Audit Trail** — a **TENTH dataset query,
`notifications`, is built for **R8 Bill Delivery** rather than forcing it onto
`audit_log`, and **R23 Account Activity**, **R26 Data Quality**, **R27 Plans &
Discounts**, **R41 Migration Assurance** and **R36 Access Review** are **refused
by name** because the grains their drawings state are not the grains their
datasets do.

**Three of eight produce a report. Five do not, each with the source and grain
it actually needs.** That matches the three lanes before it: `journal_lines` 10
seeded → 4; `invoices` 8 → 1; `payments` 10 → 2. The premise of
`CR-142-BRC07` §8.2 — *"46 definitions sit on 9 datasets, so a dataset lights a
whole block at once"* — has now broken four times out of four.

**Why, with the worked numbers, drawings read as IMAGES (B14 rule 42): p051,
p059–p061, p066, p068–p069, p071, p083–p087, p090–p092.**

**R23 Account Activity** — `ACCOUNTS` states *one account*; the drawing (p060)
tiles `OPENED 38 · CLOSED 14 · TRANSFERRED 6 · NET +24` over a window, which are
four counts of EVENTS. One account can move in and out twice in a year and
would be one row. Measured: the two date columns the drawing's own warning
insists on — *"when the clerk did it, and when it takes effect"* — are
`performed_at` and `effective_on` on `apps/customers/moves.py::MoveRecord`, and
`moves.KINDS` is a two-tuple (`move_in`, `move_out`), so the drawn
*Transferred in* row is `apps/customers/transfers.py::Transfer`. **Two tables,
one grain, and neither of them is `accounts`.**

**R26 Data Quality** — the drawn row is a CHECK: `No mailing address and no
premises · Blocking · 4 · 100455 · Bill cannot be delivered · Accounts`. Four
rows cover 1,947 accounts. Three of the four checks span modules `accounts` does
not own, and **nothing in this repo enumerates the checks at all** — there is no
data-quality rule registry to read. Its warning is the clearest statement of the
grain: *"Every row names the screen that fixes it"*, and the *Fix in* column is
a property of the rule.

**R27 Plans & Discounts** — the drawn row is an ENROLMENT. Its own warning is
*"Three programmes in one table"*, and its tiles settle it arithmetically:
`LEVEL PAY 184 + PAYMENT PLANS 84 + ASSISTANCE 50 = ENROLLED 318`, which holds
only because those are sign-ups rather than accounts. Served at account grain
the four drawn columns `SINCE · TERMS · INSTALMENT · REMAINING` have no
account-level value: an account on two programmes has two instalments and two
remaining balances. The three live in three different modules (billing's budget,
payments' plan agreement, rating's assistance discount) and `accounts` carries
none of them — `Account.autopay` is the nearest column and is marked
CAPTURE-ONLY in v1 (`BR-CUS-059`).

**R41 Migration Assurance** — the drawn row is a reconciliation CHECK, and its
LEGACY column **is not in this database.** Measured: `AccountImportBatch` holds
`row_count`, `valid_count`, `cutover_date` and a `file_hash` and **no money
column**, so `Opening balance 44,118.02` and `Deposits held 18,400.00` have no
legacy side stored anywhere. Its warning — *"a money tolerance above zero would
make the report worthless, so it is fixed at zero and not configurable"* — is a
property of the check, with nowhere on an account row to live.

**R36 Access Review** — `AUDIT_LOG` states *one audit event*; the drawn row is a
PERSON and the tiles are `USERS 9 · ACTIVE 8 · NEVER SIGNED IN 1 · CAN APPROVE
MONEY 3`. ⚠ **A user who has never signed in has written NO audit events**, so
at this grain that tile reads `0` over a real dormant login, and `0` on a
security report reads as *nothing to look at*. The report exists to find exactly
the row this grain is blind to. Measured: `identity.TenantMembership` already
carries `status`, `invited_at`, `invited_by` and `last_active_at` — whose own
column comment reads *"null renders 'Never'"* — so four tiles and six of the
seven columns are answerable from **identity alone**, and the drawing's
*identity + audit* source line overstates what audit contributes. `CAN APPROVE
MONEY` is a permission on the row's role in `identity.RolePermission`.
⚠ **`BR-REP-023` restricts this report and NOTHING ENFORCES IT** (`P5.9`, left
untouched by a sibling lane, which said so). The identity-grain query is where
that check belongs; this lane did not silently add one.
⚠⚠ **AMENDED 2026-09-27 (lane REP-P5-REST): `P5.9` IS BUILT AND THE SENTENCE
ABOVE IS NO LONGER TRUE.** It is kept rather than edited because it is this
lane's own honest report of the world it found. Two corrections: the rule is
enforced now, by `apps/reports/role_gate.py` reading
`report_definitions.min_role`; and **the check is NOT in the identity-grain
query** — a dataset query answers WHAT the rows are, and a role floor is a
property of the DEFINITION, so putting it in the query would guard this one
report and leave the next restricted one open. It is asked at the two doors a
person uses: the catalogue leaves the card out, and `GET /reports/{key}`
refuses 403.

**THE TENTH DATASET — R8 BILL DELIVERY, AND WHY IT WAS BUILT RATHER THAN BENT.**

`R8` is seeded on `audit_log` and its drawing (p051) is dated
`Billing › Delivery · notifications · —`. The brief says *nine datasets* four
times and its own §05 table lists **ten owners**; ten is right, and this is the
tenth (`DEF-REP-6797`, `P6.10`).

**The deciding fact is not a preference.** `audit_log` could not have served one
column of R8: **no audit row is written when a provider bounces an email.**
`BR-NOT-013` states it — *"`delivered` and `bounced` can never be written by
anything in this repo"*, both are provider facts. A bounce is a provider's
answer ABOUT a message, not an act anybody performed. Forcing R8 onto the trail
would have rendered **an audit register under the title *Bill Delivery*** — real
rows, a footing total, and an answer to a question nobody asked.

Every column R8 draws is already on `notifications.outbound_messages`: `channel`,
`recipient_address`, `sent_at`, `status`, `last_error` / `unavailable_reason` /
`held_reason`, and `account_id`. Its grain — *"one row per document per
CHANNEL"* (`BR-BIL-016`) — is R8's grain exactly: a bill emailed **and** posted
is two delivery attempts, and the `SENT` tile counts attempts. A grain of *one
bill* would have counted it once and lost whichever channel sorted second, which
is the `payments` lane's dropped-deposit shape (`DEF-REP-6853`) met before it
shipped.

**⚠ REGISTRATION IS NOT DONE HERE AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.**
`apps/reports/datasets.py` and `queries.py` belong to lane REP-UNBLOCK this
session, and a sibling found that adding a key to `VIEWERS` can override a live
screen through the dict merge in `api._VIEWERS`. What needs registering is
reported: a `NOTIFICATIONS` `Dataset` entry, `R8`'s seeded `dataset` column moved
from `audit_log`, `ACCOUNTS.paginates` and `AUDIT_LOG.paginates`, and the six
`AUDIT_LOG` columns that belong to other grains (`DEF-REP-6888`).

**FOUR JUDGMENTS MADE HERE RATHER THAN ASKED, each with its worked figure
(hard-won law 13 — a judgment recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable).**

**① *As at* IS HALF-DERIVABLE, AND THE HALVES ARE NAMED.** R22's eyebrow says
*As at* and §7.2.4 (p085) ruled option (b) — one effective-dated table on
customers — which is **not built**. Re-measured against the code rather than
taken from the page: `grep -n "effective_from\|effective_to"
06-backend/apps/customers/models.py` returns **no match**. So the query answers
*as at* in two pieces and says which is which: **membership is real** (`opened_at
<= as_of` and not yet closed, two stored dates) and **class, type and status are
as-is today**, published as `GAP_ATTRIBUTES_ARE_AS_IS` on every call that passes
a past `as_of`. Beyond the audit retention window the previous value is
**unrecoverable**, which §7.2.4 says in its own words and hard rule 4's
retention ruling (PO 2026-09-23) confirms.

**② THE CENSUS TILES KEY OFF THE BEHAVIOUR CLASS, NEVER THE TENANT'S LABEL.**
`BR-CUS-055`: *"every status carries a behaviour class so billing keys off the
CLASS, never the tenant's label"*, and B14 rule 37 makes the drawn words
*Active* and *Final* illustrations. **This is Phase 5's lesson in its own
words** — *code that was correct while every row was ours, and wrong the first
day a utility wrote one.* A tile written `status__name == "Active"` is right on
the seeded tenant and returns **0** for a utility that calls the same status
*Open* or *En service* (B14 rule 35). The test fixture names all three statuses
in French on purpose, so a label-keyed tile measures **0 active over 3 live
accounts** and goes red. The measure is named `closed` rather than the drawn
*Final*, because `Account.final_read_state` is a real, different column about
the closing read.

**③ THE DELIVERY STATUS BUCKETS ARE A PARTITION OF `models.STATUSES`, CHECKED AT
IMPORT.** `notifications.STATUSES` holds **nine** values; it held five before
`DEF-NOT-5626` split a bounce into hard and soft and added `complained` and
`unsubscribed` on 2026-09-17, and `models.py` says in its own comment that
*"three hand-maintained copies of this tuple is how a new status becomes
invisible on the one screen that exists to show it."* A tile written
`status="bounced"` counts **zero** on this deployment — `bounced` is LEGACY and
nothing in this repo has ever written it — while hard and soft bounces sit
uncounted. `_assert_every_status_is_bucketed()` therefore runs at **import**,
not in a test: a test can be deselected by the lane that adds the tenth status;
an import-time refusal cannot, and it names the value. It refuses a value
counted twice as well, which is the mirror defect where the tiles add to more
than the sent count. Two further facts are COLUMNS rather than buckets because
`models.py` says why: a returned letter *"was genuinely SENT"* (`BR-NOT-005`
forward-only) and a held letter was *"written, marked held, never dispatched"*
(`BR-PAY-018`) — so held rows are outside the SENT denominator, or the delivered
percentage is struck against letters still in the building. Measured on the
fixture: **six of eight sent, not eight of eight.**

**④ R8's ADDRESS IS THE PINNED ENVELOPE, AND THAT IS HARD RULE 8 OBEYED RATHER
THAN BENT.** The drawn warning is *"The address column walks to `premises` …
Nothing here holds its own copy."* This dataset declares **no address column**
and composes none; it serves `outbound_messages.recipient_address`, *"the
address as it stood when the row was written"*, which for a postal row was
walked from `premises` at QUEUE time through metering's `envelope_addresses` —
the walk `DEF-PAY-6342` was filed to make real. Walking at READ time would show
where the letter **would** go now, so a letter returned *No such address* whose
address has since been corrected would render against the corrected address and
read as a live fault at a good address. `BR-TEN-017` pins the envelope for the
same reason. And two of R8's three drawn rows are email: an email address is not
an address in hard rule 8's sense at all.

**ONE THING PUT TO THE PO RATHER THAN DECIDED — `OQ-REP-12742`.** R35's
`MONEY EVENTS` tile is **not derivable**. Measured in the code: `core/audit.py`'s
`money_action` calls `write_row` with exactly the arguments a settings change
uses, and `AuditLog` carries no flag, class or catalog reference, so a money row
and a settings row are indistinguishable. The classification belongs to the
`US-AUD-002` event-code catalog, which `apps/audit/selectors.py`'s own docstring
states is **not built**: *"Classifying codes here would invent that catalog."* A
prefix match on `payment.` / `invoice.` would count a bill being printed and
miss a deposit being waived, and would print the guess to a compliance officer
as a fact. The tile is served as `None` beside a named reason (`BR-REP-024`),
the other three tiles are real, and the question — build the list, keep the
dash, or remove the tile — is the PO's because it changes what the drawing
promises (`DEF-REP-6887`).

**AND THE RETENTION TILE IS BUILT AS SILENCE, WHICH IS TWO RULES AGREEING.**
p066's warning: *"The retention tile is the honest part and it belongs here, not
on a form … ruled 23 Sep, no row type exempt. The Correct-reference screen says
nothing about it; this report shows the oldest date it holds."* The period is
READ from `core.archival.RETENTION_MONTHS` — **84** on this deployment — and the
drawing's `12 months` is an illustration (B14 rule 37); hard-coding 12 would have
shipped a compliance tile understating the trail's life by six years. The oldest
date is `MIN(created_at)`, `None` on an empty tenant, which is a real answer. And
the tile carries **no sentence explaining the policy**: hard rule 4's retention
ruling forbids describing this path as a permanent record of an old value, B14
rule 33 puts RATIONALE at ZERO WORDS ON SCREEN, and a tile that explained the
policy would break rule 33 while trying to obey the ruling.
`CorrectionRetentionNote` was deleted from eleven catalogues for exactly that.

**Defects filed:** `DEF-REP-6885` (four reports on `accounts` state grains it
does not) · `DEF-REP-6886` (R36 on `audit_log`, and the dormant login it cannot
see) · `DEF-REP-6887` (the money-events tile) · `DEF-REP-6888` (six `AUDIT_LOG`
columns belonging to other grains).

**A red this lane did not cause, DATED (hard-won law 7, habit 1).** The whole
backend suite refused to start on `b6312ef47` with *"Conflicting migrations
detected; multiple leaf nodes in the migration graph: (0004_p2_20_service_accounts,
0005_cr142_p4_schedules_rls in reports)"*. `git log --diff-filter=A` dates it:
`0004_cr142_p4_report_schedules` landed in `c7609569a` and
`0004_p2_20_service_accounts` in `24e12122a`, **both 2026-09-27** — two lanes
took `0004`. It was fixed by a sibling in `a47280585` (`DEF-REP-6877`) while this
lane was working, and this lane rebased onto that tip. Reported rather than
re-fixed.

**Proof.** `06-backend/tests/test_rep_accounts_dataset.py`,
`test_rep_audit_log_dataset.py`, `test_rep_notifications_dataset.py` on the
SQLite suite · `10-scripts/ds_accounts_audit_notifications_cost.py` for cost and
paging on real PostgreSQL 16 · `10-scripts/rep_ds_accounts_rls_proof.py` for
tenant isolation on real PostgreSQL 16, two tenants, three tables, with a
red-first control that exits if it is measuring an empty table.

## 2026-09-27 — AMENDMENT to the DS-ACCOUNTS row above: as-was history IS built, and the row said it was not (`DEF-REP-6889`, `2.371.0`)

**What this corrects, in one sentence:** the row above says *"§7.2.4 ruled
option (b), one effective-dated table on customers — which is **not built**"*
and cites a re-run of the brief's own grep as the evidence. **That is wrong.
The table exists and the census now reads it.**

**The fact.** `CR-142-BRC07` `P0.18` landed on 2026-09-26:
`06-backend/apps/customers/migrations/0072_cr142_p0_18_attribute_history.py`,
the model `apps/customers/attribute_history_models.py::AccountAttributeHistory`
with `effective_from` / `effective_to` over `account_type_id`,
`account_subtype_id` and `status_id`, and the reader
`apps/customers/attribute_history.as_was(account_id, on=...)`.

**Why the check passed over it, and this is the part worth keeping.** The
brief's §7.2.4 (p085) states a MEASUREMENT: *"`06-backend/apps/customers/
models.py` has no effective dating of any kind — no `effective_from`, no
history table."* The standing PO instruction is *"do all tasks based on actual
code"*, so this lane re-ran that exact grep against that exact file, got **no
match**, and treated the agreement as confirmation. **The grep was right and
the conclusion was wrong: the columns are in `attribute_history_models.py`, not
in `models.py`, so the brief's own command cannot see them.**

⚠ **RE-RUNNING A DOCUMENT'S OWN COMMAND REPRODUCES ITS BLIND SPOT.** That is
the durable lesson and it is a new shape of this repo's oldest one — a
measurement quoted in a document is a claim about a MOMENT, and checking it the
way the document checked it proves only that the document was internally
consistent. **Grep for the CONCEPT, not for the sentence.**

**What it would have cost, measured.** Every historical census would have
reported each account's class, type and status as they read TODAY. An account
moved from Residential to Commercial in September would appear as Commercial in
June's figures — which is the exact case §7.2.4 was ruled to prevent — **and it
would have travelled with a confident caveat explaining why it was
unavoidable.** A wrong number under an excuse is worse than a bare wrong
number, because the excuse stops the next reader looking.

**What is built now, and it is four things rather than one.**

**①** `_as_was_for()` reads the history periods for a whole PAGE in **ONE**
query. `attribute_history.as_was()` takes one account id, so a page of fifty is
fifty round trips and a 40,000-row export is forty thousand — the N+1
`DEF-2723` closed on the accounts list and `P2.21` closed on the ageing report.

**②** Every row carries `attribute_basis` — `"as_was"` or `"as_is"` — so a
mixed report is readable. That is the brief's NEXT sentence, obeyed verbatim:
*"Where it does not … it falls back to as-is and SAYS SO ON THE FACE OF THE
REPORT. One report will state both for the first year, and that is correct
rather than untidy."*

**③** The CLASS and STATUS **filters** and the ACTIVE and CLOSED **tiles**
resolve on the SAME basis the rows show, both in SQL. A filter on today's
column would serve a row under a *Residential* chip whose own class column
reads *Commercial*; a tile on today's column would not foot to the rows
beneath it. Neither is an error anybody would see.

**④** `GAP_SOME_ATTRIBUTES_FELL_BACK_TO_AS_IS` carries the **COUNT** — *"12 of
the 50 rows served"* — rather than a sentence true of every report forever. A
declared blind spot with no number beside it is indistinguishable from an empty
one, which is hard-won law 7's fifth clause.

**And the fallback never substitutes.** `attribute_history.as_was`'s own
docstring forbids it: *"`None` … is not the current row and a caller must not
substitute one."* This query falls back EXPLICITLY, marks the row, and counts
it.

**Nothing else in the repository repeats the stale claim** — grepped for *"no
effective dating"* across every `.md` and `.py`: the only two hits were this
lane's own file and they are both fixed.

**Proof:** `tests/test_rep_accounts_dataset.py::test_as_was_wins_where_a_history_period_covers_the_date`
(June says Résidentiel/Ouvert while today says Commercial/Soldé on the same
account, and June's ACTIVE tile is 3 where today's is 2) and
`::test_a_class_filter_on_an_as_at_read_matches_what_the_row_shows` (the as-was
chip returns 1 and today's returns 0).

## 2026-09-27 — THE NEIGHBOURHOOD AVERAGE TILE IS BUILT, WITH A FLOOR OF TEN HOMES AND NO EXPLANATION ON SCREEN

**Ruled by the PO, verbatim, in answer to the three options put to them:**

> *"(a) with a floor of at least ten homes, and the tile simply absent below
> that, saying nothing about why"*

**WHAT WAS PUT TO THEM, in the words they were shown.** The customer's own
usage page is drawn with a `NEIGHBOURHOOD AVERAGE` tile beside their own
figure — **152 gallons next to their 137** (brief p061, report `R45`). That
tile is an average over other people's accounts, shown on a **customer-portal**
screen. An average over a small enough group, plus one household somebody
already knows, identifies a specific home's usage. No floor had been decided.
Three answers were offered: **(a)** a floor, **(b)** compare against the whole
service area instead, **(c)** drop the tile. **(a) was recommended with a floor
of ten and (a) is what was ruled.**

**THE RULE, as it must be built.**

| | |
|---|---|
| The tile is shown | when the comparison group holds **at least 10 other homes** |
| Below 10 | the tile is **ABSENT** — not a dash, not a zero, not a placeholder |
| What the screen says about the absence | **NOTHING.** No sentence, no tooltip, no *"not enough homes nearby"* |
| The customer's own figure | unaffected — it is their own data and is always shown |

**THE SILENCE IS PART OF THE RULING AND IT AGREES WITH B14 RULE 33**, which
puts RATIONALE at **zero words on screen**. It is also the safer build: a
sentence reading *"too few homes nearby to compare"* is itself a fact about
the neighbourhood, and on a short street it tells the reader something about
their neighbours that the tile was withheld precisely to protect.

**THE WORKED CASE THE FLOOR EXISTS FOR.** A cul-de-sac of three houses. Alia
opens her usage page and sees her own **137 gal** beside a neighbourhood
average of **152 gal**. Two other homes are in that average, and she knows one
of them is away for the month at near zero — so the third home's usage falls
out of the arithmetic in one subtraction. At ten homes that subtraction stops
being possible from one known figure.

**WHAT THIS SUPERSEDES.** `04-docs/05-modules/12-reports/02-business-rules.md`
and `06-backend/apps/metering/meter_reads_dataset.py` both carried *"must not
be added without a ruling … no floor has been decided"*, written 2026-09-27 by
lane DS-METER. **There is now a ruling**, and both are amended in the same
commit as this row — a body that contradicts a decision is what CLAUDE.md's
prime-directive section calls stale, and it is what a lane actually reads.

**⚠ THE PROCESS LESSON, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY COST THE RULING.** This
question was raised **in prose, inside the file the lane happened to be
editing**, and never as a row in `12-governance/01-open-questions.md`. Nothing
counted it, no register listed it, and it reached the PO only because the
coordinator read a lane report and carried it up by hand. That is the exact
shape CLAUDE.md records under hard rule 4's citation lesson: *a finding
recorded only in the file you happen to be in is a finding nobody can count.*
**It is now ruled, so no question row is minted after the fact** — this row is
the record, and the two stale bodies are corrected here.

**NOT YET BUILT.** The tile does not exist in any form today: `portal_usage()`
serves no cross-account aggregate and the customer portal shows no such tile.
This row is the authority to build it; it is not a claim that it is built.

## 2026-09-27 — THE WORK-ORDER RAISE DATE IS INDEXED, AND THE SCREEN IS STILL NOT INSTANT (lane MET-IDX, `DEF-MET-6881`, `metering/0062`, `2.371.1`)

**THE JUDGMENT.** `work_orders` carried four indexes — `(tenant, connection)`,
`(tenant, state)`, `(tenant, dispatch_state)`, `(tenant, due_at)` — and none on
`created_at`, which is the RAISE date: `work_orders_dataset`'s DEFAULT sort
(`WORK_ORDER_DEFAULT_SORT = "raised_on"` → `("created_at", "id")`), R33 Service
Order Activity's declared basis, the `from`/`to` filter's column, and the
tiebreak of four of the other five sorts. `metering/0062` adds one:
**`ix_work_orders_raised (tenant_id, created_at, id)`**. No rule was reversed and
nothing was put to the PO — this is an index on an existing column, which
CLAUDE.md law 13 leaves ours to decide and write down.

**THE WORKED FIGURES.** Real PostgreSQL 16.13, one tenant at **40,025 work
orders** — the top of T5, which is the whole ICP — read through
`apps/work/work_orders_dataset.py` at its own default sort, `per=50`, median of
7 after a discarded warm-up, the index dropped and re-created inside one process
so the two halves differ in exactly one variable:

| read | before | after | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| the PAGE QUERY, page 1 | 0.0655s | 0.0034s | 19.3× |
| the PAGE QUERY, page 801 (last) | 0.0953s | 0.0259s | 3.7× |
| the whole dataset call, page 1 | 0.156s | 0.131s | 1.19× |
| the whole dataset call, page 801 | 0.876s | 0.694s | 1.26× |

Statements: **2 before and 2 after**, on every one of those reads. That is
precisely why nothing in this repo could see the defect — a statement count
finds an N+1 and is blind to a missing index.

**THE PLAN, WHICH IS THE EVIDENCE.** `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`, page 801
(`LIMIT 50 OFFSET 40000`), BEFORE:

```
Gather Merge  (actual time=46.705..72.711 rows=40025 loops=1)
  ->  Sort  (actual time=43.655..48.950 rows=20012 loops=2)
        Sort Key: created_at DESC, id DESC
        Sort Method: external merge  Disk: 4288kB
        Worker 0:  Sort Method: external merge  Disk: 2736kB
        ->  Parallel Seq Scan on work_orders (rows=20012 loops=2)
Execution Time: 74.646 ms
```

AFTER:

```
Limit  (actual time=23.419..23.438 rows=25 loops=1)
  ->  Index Scan Backward using ix_work_orders_raised on work_orders
        Index Cond: (tenant_id = (NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant_id'...
Execution Time: 23.468 ms
```

**There is no `Sort` node in the after-plan at all**, so the `external merge
Disk: 4288kB` and the `temp read=878 written=880` are not smaller, they are
absent. Page 1 went the same way: `Seq Scan` + `Sort (top-N heapsort, 38kB)` at
**63.089 ms** became `Index Scan Backward` at **0.082 ms**.

⚠ **THE DEEP PAGE READS MORE BUFFERS AFTER, NOT FEWER** — `shared hit=1654` →
`shared hit=17676` — and is three times faster. An `OFFSET 40000` walk touches
every heap tuple it skips; the index trades buffer hits for a sort it no longer
performs and a spill it no longer writes. A reader checking BUFFERS alone would
call this a regression.

**⚠ THE HALF OF THIS THAT THE INDEX DOES NOT FIX, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE
DISCOVERED.** The page query improved 19× and the dataset CALL improved 1.19×,
and the difference is the TILE AGGREGATES: `raised`, `completed`, `open`,
duration, average-days-to-close and on-time are SQL aggregates over the WHOLE
filtered set, deliberately, because that is what makes them foot to the report
rather than to the page (`work_orders_dataset.py`'s own *"TOTALS ARE A SQL
AGGREGATE OVER THE WHOLE FILTERED SET"* section, and the premise `/outstandings`
got backwards). An aggregate over 40,025 rows reads 40,025 rows whether this
index exists or not. **So the honest headline is 1.19×/1.26× on the screen, not
19×**, and a later lane measuring ~0.13s must not conclude the index is missing.
Whether those tiles should be capped, cached or computed differently is NOT
decided here and no question is minted for it — 0.694s on the worst page is
inside the 60s worker budget by two orders of magnitude, so there is nothing to
route yet.

**⚠ ONE CLAIM IN THE DEFECT ROW DID NOT REPRODUCE.** `DEF-MET-6881` says the
disk spill occurs *"on EVERY page including page 1"*. On this server page 1
sorted IN MEMORY — `Sort Method: top-N heapsort  Memory: 38kB` — because a
`LIMIT 50` top-N fits in `work_mem`; only the deep pages, which must order the
whole set, spilled. **Page 1 was still a full `Seq Scan` of 40,025 rows and 63 ms
of server time**, so the defect and its fix are unchanged; the wording is
corrected in `metering/0062`'s docstring because a later reader checking page 1,
seeing a heapsort and concluding the defect was imaginary is the expensive
mistake here. Likewise the row's headline figures (0.418s → 0.161s page 1,
4.65× last/first) did not reproduce on this machine — the lane DS-SMALL run and
this one are on different hardware — which is why this row quotes its own A/B
rather than repeating theirs.

**WHY ASCENDING, WITH NO `DESC`.** The probe index in the defect row was
`(tenant_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)`. This one declares no direction and is
not a weaker version of it: PostgreSQL serves the screen's default
`ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC` by scanning it **backward**
(`Index Scan Backward`, no Sort) and the ascending toggle by scanning it
**forward** (`Index Scan`, no Sort). Both were measured. A `DESC` index serves
the default and leaves the other toggle on a Seq Scan — one index doing half a
job. It also matches the four indexes already on this table, none of which
declares a direction.

**WHAT IT COSTS.** **2,320 kB** against a **13 MB** table at 40,025 orders —
17.4% — as a fifth index on a table with four. Paid on INSERT and on any UPDATE
of `created_at`, which is `auto_now_add` and therefore never updated after the
raise.

**`NFR-5` AND THE T4/T3 FLEXIBILITY CLAUSE ARE UNTOUCHED.** An index imposes no
cap, makes no row unreachable and adds no per-tenant maximum. The same index
serves 160,000 orders more usefully, not less.

**PROOF.** `06-backend/tests/test_def_met_6881_work_order_raise_index.py`, seven
cases, four proved RED through `pytest` against the tree without the index (the
failures are quoted verbatim in that file's header) and green with it, plus a
vendor-gated live-catalogue case that SKIPS on sqlite rather than passing over a
`pg_index` it cannot read. The sibling `tests/test_rep_small_datasets.py` passes
**25 of 25** with this change in (661.96s). The migration was applied forward,
reversed to `0061` and applied forward again against real PostgreSQL 16.13.
`makemigrations metering --check --dry-run` reports no changes, and Django's own
`detect_conflicts()` reported `none` both before the migration was written and
at push time.

**ROLLBACK.** `manage.py migrate metering 0061`, then delete the migration, the
five-line declaration in `WorkOrder.Meta.indexes` and the test file.

## 2026-09-27 — lane REP-P2-REST: a group row has a RESTING STATE and it is CLOSED (`P2.24`, `2.372.0`)

**THE JUDGMENT, AND IT IS OURS RATHER THAN THE PO's.** `P2.24` says *"A group
row expands to the next level **without leaving the report** — Area opens its
routes, a route its premises. Collapse restores it."* It does not say which
state a grouped report OPENS in, and 2·1E on p028 draws a mixed one: `North`
open, `R-01` open showing two accounts, `R-02` closed, `South` closed. B14 rule
37 makes a drawn figure an illustration, and a drawing showing both states
cannot be the answer to which is the default.

**RULED: CLOSED, showing the outermost level only.** Note ② draws *"▾ open · ▸
closed"* and the verb in the task is *expands* — so opening is the ACT and
closed is what the act starts from. A mixed drawn state is only reachable if
closed is where the screen rests.

**THE WORKED FIGURE.** `trend_pack`, grouped `year → accounting_period →
service` on the seeded `brazosbend` tenant, real PostgreSQL 16: the server
returns THREE group rows covering 36 journal lines. Before this change the
screen drew all three at once, indented, with no way to close any of them.
After it the screen opens showing **one** row — `2026-01-01 · 36 rows` — and
two clicks reach all three. Walked at 1440 and 1280, `2.372.0`.

**WHAT IT COSTS, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED.** On `ar_aging` grouped by
consumer class the server interleaves 26 FACT rows under one group row. Those
26 rows are on screen today and are behind one click after this change. That is
a visible change to a live screen and it is the reason this row exists.

**WHY IT IS NOT IN THE URL.** Every other control on 2·1 lives in the query
string (`BR-SHL-011`) so a bookmark reopens the same page, sort and search. A
disclosure changes NOTHING about the question asked of the server, and a
history entry per triangle is a page load in the only sense a clerk cares
about — against a task whose own words are *"no page load"*.

**THE CONTROL IS ABSENT WHERE IT WOULD DO NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING
HALF.** Measured before a line was written
(`10-scripts/rep_p2_24_grouping_depth.py`, real PostgreSQL 16, 2026-09-27): of
the **46** live report definitions, **1** groups three levels deep, **2** group
exactly one level, and **43** cannot group at all — 18 refusing with
`DatasetNotExecutable` and 17 with `DatasetCannotServe`. On the SQL path the
answer is `collapsed: true`, group rows and no facts, so the DEEPEST group row
opens nothing on 45 of the 46. Expandability is therefore derived from the
payload — *is the next row deeper?* — and a group with nothing beneath it draws
a spacer, never a disabled triangle. That is hard-won law 2's mirror applied
before it could bite rather than after.

**MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: ZERO REQUESTS.** `10-scripts/rep_p2_24_shots.mjs`
counts every `/api/{tenant}/reports/…` request the browser makes. Across open,
open and close on `trend_pack`: body rows `1 → 2 → 3 → 1`, report reads **0**.
A screenshot proves the tree; only the counter proves it was free.

## 2026-09-27 — CORRECTION: commit `f6d367a03` carries the WRONG SUBJECT over lane MET-IDX's work (`DEF-GOV-6892`)

**WHAT THE BRANCH LOOKS LIKE.** `f6d367a03`'s subject reads *"feat(reports): a
group row opens the next level in place… (P2.24, 2.372.0)"*. **Its diff is
`DEF-MET-6881` and nothing else** — `git diff --numstat 2b23c5fa0 f6d367a03`
prints exactly ten paths, all of them lane MET-IDX's: `metering/0062`, the
`WorkOrder.Meta.indexes` declaration, the new test, `2.371.1` in three files,
and the four register appends. The row above this one is that work's real
record; **read the diff, not the subject.**

**HOW.** `push_paths.sh` takes a MESSAGE FILE as an argument and passes it
straight to `git commit-tree -F`. This lane wrote that file to
`/tmp/claude-0/msg.txt` — **a scratch directory every lane in the container
shares**, already holding `.bak` files and `a1.txt`/`a2.txt` from several of
them — and a sibling lane wrote its own `msg.txt` over it in the minutes between
the write and the push. `commit-tree` read the sibling's bytes.

**NOTHING WAS LOST, IN EITHER DIRECTION, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN
ASSUMED.** The sibling's P2.24 commit was not on the branch at the time, so
nothing of theirs was reverted; the numstat above proves nothing of theirs rode
along either. The damage is a label.

**⚠ WHY NO CHECK CAUGHT IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** Every check
CLAUDE.md law 11 prescribes reads CONTENT, and on this push every one of them
passed **truthfully**: the closing numstat named exactly the ten intended paths,
all four register guards reported *nothing vanished*, and `git show` holds no
other lane's hunk. **Nothing anywhere reads a commit SUBJECT**, so a commit
describing work it does not contain is invisible to the whole toolchain — law
7's *reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes*, one level up from the
files. `push_paths.sh` asks the staleness question of every named path and does
not ask it of the message it is handed.

**NOT REWRITTEN, DELIBERATELY.** Two lanes are live on this branch. A force-push
to relabel one commit would move the tip under them, which is a real revert
risk traded for a cosmetic gain. This row is the record instead.

**WHAT THE NEXT LANE SHOULD DO.** Give `push_paths.sh` a message file inside
the session's OWN scratchpad directory, never a bare `/tmp/claude-0/<name>`. The
durable fix is in the script: copy the message to a private temp file at
argument time and `commit-tree` from that, or refuse when its bytes moved during
the run. `DEF-GOV-6892` carries both.

## 2026-09-27 — TWO AMENDMENTS by lane MET-IDX to its own two rows above (`DEF-MET-6881`, `DEF-GOV-6892`)

**1 · *"THE FIFTH INDEX ON THIS TABLE"* IS WRONG AS A PHYSICAL CLAIM. IT IS THE
TWENTY-FIFTH.** The `DEF-MET-6881` row above, `metering/0062`'s docstring and
`DEF-MET-6881`'s own defect row all say `work_orders` carried FOUR indexes.
That is true of `WorkOrder.Meta.indexes` and false of the TABLE: Django puts a
single-column index on every ForeignKey, and this model declares nineteen of
them. Counted in `pg_indexes` at 40,025 orders:

| | |
|---|---|
| indexes on `work_orders` before `0062` | **23** |
| their total size | **17 MB** on a **13 MB** table |
| `ix_work_orders_raised` | **2,320 kB**, the third largest |
| largest | `uq_work_orders_tenant_no` 3,904 kB, then `work_orders_pkey` 2,488 kB |
| the nineteen FK indexes | 416–448 kB each |

**The conclusion does not move and the framing does.** Not one of the
twenty-three covers `created_at`, so the defect and the fix are exactly as the
row above states, and a composite `(tenant, created_at, id)` is the only thing
that removes the sort. But *"a fifth index on a table with four"* reads as a
cheap addition to a lean table, and the honest sentence is *"a twenty-fourth
index on a table already carrying 17 MB of them, and the third largest of
those"* — which is a bigger write cost than the row implied and still worth it,
because a work order is raised a few hundred times a day and read on every
dispatcher's screen and every R33 run. **The lesson is `journal_lines`' own,
recorded in `tests/test_cr060_t8_dimension_indexes.py`: `Meta.indexes` is not
the index set. Count `pg_indexes`.**

**2 · THE PREVENTION IN `DEF-GOV-6892` IS TOO WEAK, AND THE ROW SAYS SO ITSELF
ONE LEVEL DOWN.** It prescribes *"a path inside the session's OWN scratchpad
directory, never a bare `/tmp/claude-0/<name>`"*. **That directory is shared
too** — the session scratchpad this lane was given holds `App.orig.tsx`,
`AgingView.keep.tsx`, a `DS-SMALL/` folder and files dated three days before
this session started, from lanes that are not this one. Moving one directory
down moves the collision, it does not remove it.

**The two things that actually remove it, in order:** (a) `mktemp` — a name no
sibling can guess — for every scratch file that another process will read back,
which is what this lane used after finding this; and (b) the durable half,
which belongs in `10-scripts/push_paths.sh` and is what `DEF-GOV-6892` should
be fixed with: **copy `MSG_FILE` to a private temp file at argument time and
`commit-tree` from THAT**, or refuse when its bytes moved during the run. The
script already asks the staleness question of every named path; the message is
the one input it takes on trust.

⚠ **THE GENERAL SHAPE IS THIS FILE'S OWN LAW 11: *before you write ANYTHING
that touches a shared file, ask whether it is shared.*** A lane picking a
scratch path asks *is this outside the repo* and stops there. The question that
matters is *can another process write this exact name*, and in a container
running six lanes the answer for any obvious name is yes.

|---|---|---|
| definitions resolving a query | 28 | **46** |
| definitions raising `DatasetNotExecutable` | **18** | 0 |
| definitions SERVED (a payload) | 11 | **18** |
| definitions REFUSED by name with a sentence | 17 | **28** |
| served + refused | 28 | **46** |

**The SEVEN reports a clerk can newly open** (11 → 18): R22 Account Census ·
R29 Consumption Exceptions · R30 Usage & Ranking · R31 Meter Fleet · R33
Service Order Activity · R35 Audit Trail · R45 My Usage. Proved on data rather than on an empty

and its own `refuse()` on `accounts` and `audit_log`, and the two

**⚠ ONE REGRESSION THIS LANE CAUSED AND CLOSED IN THE SAME COMMIT, AND IT IS
THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE.** `catalogue_read.catalogue_payload` decided whether
a card was available by asking `runner.queries_for` alone — correct while a
dataset with an engine served every definition on it. The moment the last six
datasets were registered, **all forty-six cards claimed to be producible** and
twenty-eight of them refused the instant they were clicked: *a viewer that opens
onto a reason is a screen pretending to be a report*, which is the posture
`apps/reports/catalog.py` ships and this lane briefly broke. Two existing
assertions caught it (`DEF-REP-6894`) — `test_rep_p1_catalogue.py`'s *"every card available would
mean the check cannot fail"* and `test_us_rep_canned_reports.py`'s *"the
catalogue claims every report is producible"* — which is a check written against
the false-pass case doing exactly its job.
**The fix:** `queries.definition_refusal(key, dataset)` answers *may this
dataset serve this definition* WITHOUT running the query, from the same
functions the viewer calls, so the card and the click cannot reach different
answers. A card is available only when the dataset has an engine AND that engine
does not decline the report. The catalogue now carries a **second reason code**,
`report_grain_is_not_this_dataset_grain`, because *the engine is not built* and
*the engine declines this report* wait on different people — a dataset lane, or
a ruling about which dataset the report belongs on. **No locale key was added:**
`ReportLibraryPage` renders `reports.library.reason.<code>` with
`reports.library.unavailableGeneric` as its `defaultValue`, so an unknown code
reads *"This report cannot be produced yet"* in all eleven languages — true of
both states, and a sentence naming the grain would be RATIONALE on screen, which
B14 rule 33 puts at zero words.

**THREE FURTHER REDS WERE FOUND AND NOT CAUSED HERE, EACH DATED WITH
`git log -S` RATHER THAN CALLED PRE-EXISTING** (hard-won law 7's first habit,
and `DEF-CWP-4187`'s lesson that an undated *not mine* tells every later reader
not to look). One is FIXED because it is a one-line stale assertion in this
lane's own blast radius; two are FILED and left, because fixing either is a

## 2026-09-27 — THE CUSTOMER STATEMENT IS BUILT ON THE LEDGER, LIKE A BANK STATEMENT

**Ruled by the PO, verbatim, choosing option (a) of three put to them:**

> *"it should be like bank statement. this si correct - Build it on the ledger —
> the account's running record, which holds both sides. Correct by
> construction; more work"*

**WHAT WAS PUT TO THEM, in the words they were shown.** A customer statement is
a list of what an account was charged and what they paid, over a period. Which
body of data should it be built on? **The worked case:** *"Dana opens Alia's
statement for September. It must show the September bill of `$84.20`, the
payment of `$84.20` on the 14th, and the balance carried forward. Today's
invoice data holds the charges and not the payments, so the statement would
show what she owed and never what she paid."* Options: **(a)** the ledger,
which holds both sides · **(b)** invoices with payments added alongside ·
**(c)** leave the old page and retire it later. **(a) was recommended and (a)
is ruled**, with the PO adding the shape in their own words: **like a bank
statement.**

**THE RULE — `BR-REP-038`.** A customer statement is an **account's running
record over a period**: an opening balance, every charge and every payment in
date order, and a closing balance that is the opening balance plus the
movements. It is built on the **ledger** (`journal_lines`), never on invoices.

| | |
|---|---|
| One row is | one posting against the account |
| Both sides present | charges AND payments, in date order |
| Opening and closing balance | required — it is what makes it a statement rather than a list |
| Source | the ledger, the same body `R25 Ledger` already reads |

**WHY THE INVOICE READING IS NOT MERELY HARDER BUT WRONG.** Invoices are
charges. A statement built on them is arithmetically incapable of showing a
payment, so its closing balance can only ever be the sum of what was billed —
which is the one number a customer already knows and the one they never query.

**WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS.** `CR-142-BRC07` `P2.8`, `P2.15` and `P2.16` — the last
three tasks of Phase 2 — retire three old report pages into new definitions,
and two of those definitions could not return a row: `statement` was refused
by the invoices dataset by name, and `DEF-REP-6859` records that the task rows
also name definitions that are not in the catalogue at all. This ruling settles
which dataset `statement` belongs on. **`reports/0003_seed_catalogue.py` seeds
`R24 statement` on `invoices` (line 237) and that seed is now WRONG** — moving
it is a migration, not an edit, and it lands with the work.

⚠ **ONE CONSEQUENCE TO MEASURE RATHER THAN ASSUME, AND IT IS NOT RULED HERE.**
`R44 My Bills & Payments` — the CUSTOMER-facing screen — is seeded on
`invoices` too (line 241) and its drawn name promises both sides in the same
way this statement does. **Nobody may quietly move it on the strength of this
row**: the ruling names the statement. The lane taking this work measures
whether `R44` can show a payment today and reports the answer; if it cannot,
that is a defect to file and a one-line question to the PO, not a value to
choose. `R25 account_ledger` is already seeded on `journal_lines` and is
untouched by this.

**NOT YET BUILT.** This row is the authority to build it, not a claim that it
is built.

## 2026-09-27 — lane REP-REFUSE: twenty-seven reports told a clerk the product had broken; they say what it actually knows (`DEF-REP-6898`, `2.373.1`)

**WHAT A CLERK SAW, PHOTOGRAPHED.** Opening **Read Completeness** — a METER
READS report — drew a red panel headed *"The finance figures could not be
loaded"* with *"Something went wrong on our side. Nothing was saved."* under it.
Nothing had gone wrong, nothing was being saved, and the word *finance* has no
business on a meter-reads screen. **Twenty-seven of the forty-six reports did
this**, measured by opening every one of them in Chromium at 1440.

**AND THE PRODUCT ALREADY KNEW THE ANSWER, TWO CLICKS EARLIER.** The catalogue
card for the same report said, calmly and correctly, *"This report cannot be
produced yet."* Two surfaces, one fact, opposite sentences.

**THE CAUSE, VERIFIED BY RUNNING IT.** `apps/reports/api.report` caught
`DefinitionNotFound` and `DatasetNotExecutable` **by name**.
`queries.DatasetCannotServe` is their SIBLING — all three subclass
`NotImplementedError`, and `tests/test_rep_ds_invoices.py` asserts none is a
subclass of another — so the one the dataset queries actually raise fell
straight through DRF's catch-all to `500 SYS-INTERNAL`. It is hard-won law 2
one layer out: the engine refused BY NAME and the wire threw the name away.
`7e22165ba`'s own commit message reports *"REFUSED by name with a sentence
28"*; that was true of the RUNNER and false of the wire.

**THE STATUS IS 422 `BIZ-COMPLETENESS`, AND THE THREE IT IS NOT ARE RECORDED
SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES THEM.** Not **500** — nothing broke and nothing was lost,
and a fault report sends a clerk to support for an answer the product holds.
Not **404** — the report is real and listed, and an absent address would make
it indistinguishable from a typo, which is the one thing `HR-1` reserves 404
for. Not **409** — there is no conflicting state to resolve and no retry that
would help. It is a semantic refusal of a well-formed request, which is the
B12 §3 row `BIZ-COMPLETENESS` occupies. `br_ref` is **`BR-REP-024`** — *a
stated absence, never a silent one*.

**IT ADDS NO CLERK-FACING STRING, DELIBERATELY.** The envelope's `message_key`
is `reports.library.unavailableGeneric` — the CARD's own key, already authored
in all eleven catalogues. A second sentence for the viewer is how the two
surfaces drifted apart in the first place, and a new key used on screen is
`DEF-REP-6900`'s fault (seven reports showing raw i18n keys today). **Zero
keys were added to any catalogue.**

**WHAT A CLERK NOW READS, EXACTLY:** the heading **"Report not available"**
(three words) and the sentence **"This report cannot be produced yet."** (six
words). The server's own prose — why the grain does not match, what the report
would need — travels in `params.detail`, which `refusalParams` drops before
i18next ever sees it (PO ruling 2026-08-19) and which B14 rule 33 puts at ZERO
WORDS ON SCREEN. It is in the log and in the code, which is where a paragraph
about datasets belongs.

**MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER, BY WALKING ALL FORTY-SIX AT 1440 AGAINST REAL
POSTGRESQL 16** (`10-scripts/rep_6898_refusal_walk.mjs`, seeded `brazosbend`):

      SERVED  (a payload and rows)            18  ->  18
      REFUSED (six words a clerk can read)     0  ->  27
      ASKS    (the screen wants a parameter)   1  ->   1
      BROKEN  ("something went wrong")        27  ->   0
      ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
                                              46      46

**ONE THING FIXED THAT WAS NOT ASKED FOR, AND WHY IT WAS UNAVOIDABLE.** A
refused report has no payload, so `ReportViewerPage`'s title fell back to
`reports.card.<key>.name`, which is authored for only nine of the forty-six
keys — so the refusal screen was headed **`read_completeness`**. That is B14
rule 31 (no database id is ever the visible value) reached through a fallback,
and shipping *"in words they can act on"* under a slug is not shipping the fix.
The title now prefers the CATALOGUE ROW's name — the same name on the card the
clerk just clicked. Filed as part of this defect rather than separately,
because it is only reachable on the screen this defect creates.

**THE FOURTH VERDICT IN THE WALK IS A FINDING, NOT A BUCKET FOR TIDINESS.**
`account_ledger` is S59, a route card with its own screen, and that screen asks
for an account before it fetches anything — **"Choose an account. This report
runs for one account at a time."** The first draft of both the test and the
walk called that BROKEN. It is a good answer, and counting it as a fault would
have put a working screen in the defect column. It is `ASKS`, and what is
asserted of that bucket is a PROPERTY — the refusal names the field it wants —
rather than a list of keys, which would be the count that rots.

**Pending propagation:** none. `12-governance/10-defect-log.csv`
(`DEF-REP-6898` → fixed), `CHANGELOG.md`, the three version files and this row
move in the same commit as the code.
