## 2026-09-27 — A STATEMENT IS SERVED FOR FIVE SUBJECTS, NOT ONE

**Ruled by the PO, verbatim, answering three questions at once:**

> *"we can do based on regualr account, master account, premises, units, customer
> id ; then it resoleves your questions"*

**WHAT WAS PUT TO THEM.** Three questions, each with a worked example: does a
statement exist for a PERSON as well as an ACCOUNT (Ridge Property LLC holding
four accounts in one building, wanting one total); does one exist for a UNIT
(apartment 3B with three tenants in a year, where a unit statement names both
occupants across a move-out and an account statement shows only the current
tenant); and should the two catalogue entries that do not exist be created.
**The PO answered by naming the whole set rather than picking from the
options.**

### `BR-REP-043` — THE STATEMENT'S SUBJECT

A statement is the account's running record — an opening balance, every charge
and every payment in date order, a closing balance, built on the ledger
(`BR-REP-038`, ruled earlier today). **What this ruling settles is WHOSE record
it is.** Five subjects, and the SUBJECT scopes the set of postings; the GRAIN of
a row does not change.

| subject | the set is | the worked case put to the PO |
|---|---|---|
| **regular account** | one account's postings | the statement built today |
| **master account** | the master and what it covers | an owner's account over common areas |
| **premises** | every account at that address | a building, however many units |
| **unit** | one unit, across tenancies | apartment 3B, three tenants in a year |
| **customer** | every account that customer holds | Ridge Property LLC, four units, one total |

⚠ **THE UNIT SUBJECT IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE AND IT IS NOW RULED IN.** The
coordinator recommended deferring it; the PO ruled otherwise. It needs a
running-record read model in `apps/ledger` that **no seam publishes today** —
`CR-142-BRC07` `P2.15` records this, filed as a Front-end task when it is a
ledger task. That is the build, not a screen change.

⚠ **AND A UNIT OUTLIVES ITS TENANTS, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE SUBJECT.** A
three-month unit statement spanning a move-out **names both occupants**; an
Occupant column appears on this subject and on no other. A unit declares no
address of its own (hard rule 8) — the head reads the premises address plus the
unit label.

⚠ **THE CUSTOMER SUBJECT CARRIES A GUARD THAT ALREADY EXISTS AND MUST SURVIVE.**
`CustomerStatementPage.tsx` — the screen `P2.16` was to delete — holds the
`held_with` guard that stops a stranger's arrears appearing on this person's
statement, and a server-reasoned absent-figure. **Those are the careful parts;
`P2.16`'s own text says to keep them.** The page is the CUSTOMER grain and the
statement built today is the ACCOUNT grain, which is why deleting it would have
removed a working screen — recorded 2026-09-27 by lane REP-P2-LAST.

### What this unblocks, and what it costs

**Phase 2's last three tasks all turn on this ruling.** `P2.8` retires three
screens into definitions and `P2.16` retires the third; both were blocked
because two of the definitions they retire into — *by premises* and *customer
statement* — **are not in the catalogue at all** (`DEF-REP-6859`, verified
against the code). **They are now ruled in**, as two of these five subjects.

⚠ **NOBODY MAY DELETE A SCREEN BEFORE ITS SUBJECT SERVES ROWS.** The addresses
are bookmarked and linked from Finance, `P2.8` says to keep them, and a redirect
to a subject that refuses is the dead-control failure this repo files most.
**Serve the subject, prove it in a browser, then retire the page and redirect.**

### What did NOT change

`BR-REP-038` stands: the statement is built on the **ledger**, never on
invoices, because invoices are charges and a statement must show a payment.
`runner.bind` carries `subject` and `subject_id` (`DEF-REP-6908`, fixed) — the
four-grain vocabulary `P2.14` built now has a fifth value and a ruling behind it.

## 2026-09-27 — TWO SMALL RULINGS: THE PLAN LIST'S BASE TOTAL, AND A BRAND NAME IN A TRANSLATED VALUE

Both put to the PO with a worked example and options. **Both answered (a).**

### 1 · `BR-RAT-1040` — the plan list shows the REAL base total and no longer sorts by it

PO verbatim: *"a is good"*.

**The problem, as shown to them:** `Monthly base total` reads **`$0.00` on every
plan**, because it sums `plan_services.base_charge` — the column `BR-RAT-088`
retired when the charge code took the base over. The same annotation is the
list's **SQL sort key** (`plan_list_queryset` maps the `base_charges` sort onto
it), and `NFR-3` requires the Plans list to page and sort in SQL. Resolving the
figure honestly means walking the charge codes narrowed by class and size — a
Python walk, not a subquery — so the figure and the sort cannot both stay in the
database.

**The worked case:** *"A clerk opens Plans & Rates, sees ten plans all reading
`$0.00`, and clicks the column to sort by base charge. Today it sorts by a
retired column — so the order is meaningless too, it just looks plausible."*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Ruled** | Show the **real** figure; **drop sorting by it** |
| Still sortable | name, service, status — every other column is untouched |
| Why it is safe | a plan list is ten or twenty rows at a utility of this size, so sorting by base charge is a convenience; a wrong number on a pricing screen is not |

⚠ **`NFR-3` IS NOT WEAKENED.** The LIST still pages and sorts in SQL; one sort
option is withdrawn because the value behind it cannot be computed there. Nobody
may read this as licence to sort a list in Python.

### 2 · `BR-REP-045` — a manufacturer is DATA, not vocabulary

PO verbatim: *"a"*.

**The problem:** two catalogue values read `AMI · Itron` and `AMI · Sensus`,
identical in all eleven languages — correctly, because *Itron* and *Sensus* are
company names. The translation check counts them as untranslated
(`DEF-REP-6931`). Option (b) was to add them to the check's hand-curated
exception list.

**Ruled: take the brand name OUT of the translated phrase.** Translate the part
that is words — the reading method — and render the manufacturer **beside it as
data**. ⚠ **The reason option (b) was refused is worth keeping:** an exception
list needs somebody to remember to edit it the day a utility buys from a third
manufacturer, and nothing would remind them. **A brand name never enters a
translatable value again.**

## 2026-09-27 — lane FIX-SMALL: four judgment calls behind four small fixes

Four unrelated defects, cleared together. None needed a PO ruling — law 13's
list is short and none of these is on it — so the judgments are written here
with their worked figures instead.

### 1 · `DEF-TEN-6935` — the rule id on a Settings field has NO replacement

Every field on every Settings rule page carried a help line reading
**"Set by BR-REP-018"**. Measured in a browser at 1440 on `brazosbend` before a
line was changed: **12 of those lines across two of the four rule cards, naming
four distinct rules** — `BR-BIL-017` on Budget billing, and `BR-PAY-016`,
`BR-PAY-013`, `BR-PAY-018` on Collections & notices.

**The judgment is that it is deleted rather than reworded.** B14 rule 32
clause 4 bans a rule id in clerk-facing copy, which settles the id; what it does
not settle is whether something shorter should take its place. Rule 33 does:
the line answers *who decided 200%?*, which is RATIONALE — why the product works
this way — and rationale is **zero words on screen**. A six-word replacement
would still be rationale. So the line goes and the help text keeps only what a
clerk types against: the unit, and whether the field may be left empty.

⚠ **It survived every check because the id is INTERPOLATED.** The catalogue
holds `Set by {{br}}` and the id arrives from `param.br` at render time, so no
grep of `en.json` for `BR-`-shaped text could ever see it. The three tests that
pinned it are now inverted and match by SHAPE (`/BR-[A-Z]{3}-\d{3,5}/`), not by
the one id — an assertion naming `BR-LED-002` would pass the day the line comes
back on a page whose parameters cite a different rule.

### 2 · `DEF-REP-6924` — a check reporting a token the page does not ask for

Two of the three reported tokens, `primary` and `default`, were **arguments to
`buttonClasses(...)` written inside a `className={…}` attribute**. Both
class-name readers in this repo take the quoted strings out of that expression,
because that is the only way to see a class in markup that builds one — so they
read the two arguments as two class names. The string the kit returns was always
the real one; nothing was ever mis-rendered.

**Fixed by hoisting the call to a module constant**, which is what every other
kit call site in the product already does (`FILTER_TRIGGER_KIT`,
`PANEL_TRIGGER_KIT`, `DOOR`, `COMMIT_DANGER`) — this was the last inline one.
The grammar is not touched: it is shared by two readers and a golden corpus, and
widening it to understand a function call would be a change to the one thing
keeping those two readers in step.

⚠ **AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE COMMENT EXPLAINING THE FIX RE-INTRODUCED THE
DEFECT.** The grammar reads source TEXT and does not know what a comment is, so
quoting the old markup verbatim in a docstring kept `G134` red — on a file whose
only remaining reference to those two tokens was the paragraph describing their
removal. Worth knowing before writing the next such note.

The third token, `border-border`, was real: `border` is not a colour this
product declares (the edge token is `--color-divider`), so three borders on the
report builder's edit panel drew at the browser's `currentColor` default.

### 3 · `DEF-GOV-6930` — the changelog check is ratcheted, not rewritten

`G35` clause 4 asks whether the version that is CURRENT has an entry. On a
branch where six lanes bump the fix digit, **a version is current for about
twenty minutes**, so one that ships unrecorded is never asked about again.

**Measured: 21 versions had been published with no entry** — three of them today
(`2.377.1`, `2.377.2`, `2.380.3`; the briefing named two and the third was found
by counting). `DEF-GOV-6813` recorded this same hole two days earlier, in a
`### Known` block of the changelog, where no gate reads.

New clause 5 asks the whole question: every version this branch's history has
written into `package.json` must carry a bracketed heading. **The eighteen older
gaps are named in `12-governance/changelog-gaps-baseline.txt` rather than
written up.** The judgment: entries invented three weeks late from commits whose
lanes are gone would be invention, and a gate born red on eighteen rows is a
gate somebody switches off. The baseline is a list with a count beside it, which
is law 7's fifth shape — a declared blind spot with no number is
indistinguishable from an empty one.

### 4 · `DEF-GOV-6962` — the durable copy goes OUTSIDE the repository

A 67-minute isolation run finished FAIL (9 failed, 11 errored, 301 passed) and
its receipt was destroyed minutes later by an ordinary restore-from-branch. The
counts survived in a lane's notes; **the names of the twenty cases did not**,
and naming them is the one thing the receipt exists for.

**The archive is `~/.smartbillhub/isolation-runs/`, not the session
scratchpad.** The scratchpad dies with the container, which is the same class of
loss one step along — `10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py`'s own docstring records being
lost there twice. One file per run, never overwritten, never pruned: a run costs
an hour and a receipt is 2 KB.

**And the archive is written FIRST, before any refusal can fire.** The in-repo
receipt is then declined where the new run is older than the recorded one, or
reports no cases at all. A guard that discarded the evidence it was guarding
would be worse than the defect.

⚠ `12-governance/isolation-reproof-2026-09-25.md` §4 proposed half of this two
days earlier — *"refuse to build a receipt when the run produced no counts"* —
and that half was built (`DEF-GOV-6704`). The other half was not, and this is it.

## 2026-09-27 — **THE REPORT EDITOR'S FOUR JUDGMENTS** (lane REP-EDITOR-A, the quick pass over screen `2·2` / `RPT-02`, `DEF-REP-7070`)

The Product Owner opened `/{tenant}/reports/statement?edit=1` on deployed
`v2.380.3` and reported, verbatim: *"report editor is not user friendly — as a
user I don't know what I'm doing and how fields are shown — no edit no adds"*.
Four things were fixed. **None of the four needed a ruling** and each is a
judgment recorded here with its worked number, per law 13.

### 1 · A required input is DECLARED BY THE SERVER, not inferred by the screen

**The judgment.** The editor had to ask for the account first, and the obvious
way to know it needs one is to look at the refusal the run already publishes
(`unavailable[a_statement_names_one_account]`). That was rejected: a refusal
arrives only AFTER a run that returned nothing, so a screen built on it can
only draw a chooser once it has already asked a question it knew would fail —
and mapping refusal codes to inputs is a hand-written table with one entry,
which is the shape `CLAUDE.md`'s *never hand-type a list* is about.

**What was built instead.** `apps/reports/statement.py` publishes
`controls.requires = [{"param": "subject_id", "finds": "account"}]` through
`queries._report`'s existing `controls` passthrough — **no change to
`queries.py` or `runner.py`, which four sibling lanes were live in.** `finds`
names the KIND of record, so `BR-REP-043`'s other four subjects become an entry
in the front end's `FINDERS` map rather than a rewrite.

**The figure that decides it:** **one** report of forty-six declares a required
input today. A screen that guessed would have added a step to the other
forty-five, and the billing-register shot in
`scratchpad/po-shots/report-editor-a/` is the proof that it does not.

**Why `controls` and not a new top-level key.** `controls` is *what this report's
table may offer*, and a required parameter is a control. A new key would have
been a line in `queries.py`, which is edited by a live lane. The statement
therefore also publishes `sorts: []` and `searchable: false` — both TRUE of it
today and both previously left to be inferred from an absent `controls`.

### 2 · A KIND WITH NO FINDER DRAWS NOTHING, AND THAT IS NOT A HIDDEN GAP

`BR-REP-043` (ruled the same day) gives the statement five subjects. The ledger
publishes a running record for **one**: `apps/reports/statement.py` refuses
`customer`, `premises` and `unit` BY NAME. So a chooser for those three would be
a live control in front of a query that will refuse whatever is typed into it —
hard-won law 2's mirror. `finderFor()` returns `null` and the server's own
refusal is what the clerk reads. A test asserts the three refused kinds have no
finder, so the day the ledger publishes a premises running record the pairing is
one entry and a red test, not a rediscovery.

### 3 · AN EXAMPLE THAT CONTAINS NO CHARACTERS

**The judgment.** The task asked for *"a few example rows so the shape is
visible"*, with the condition that a clerk must never mistake them for their own
utility's data. The repo's screen skill forbids the obvious implementation by
name — *"❌ Filling an empty state with placeholder or sample data"* — and this
product's posture elsewhere is `queries._report`'s own: *a confident wrong fact
is worse than having none*. An invented `AC-2026-00041 · 84.20` on a money
screen is a figure somebody eventually quotes.

**What was built.** `ReportShapePreview` draws the chosen columns as headings
and each cell as a **grey bar**, under the heading **Example** and a five-word
fact, *"Shape only. No data here."* It carries what a person building a report
needs — how many columns, in what order, how wide, which read right-aligned —
and **not one character in any language.** The guarantee is structural rather
than a disclaimer: the test asserts the example body's `textContent` is the
empty string, so a later lane that puts `84.20` in a bar to make it clearer
turns it red on the character it added. Drawn only under `?edit=1`: a clerk
READING an empty report is told *No rows match* and is shown no diagram.

**Why not the kit's `LoadingSkeleton`.** Bars with no heading over them state
the one thing that is false here — that rows are on their way.

### 4 · `ATTRIBUTES 7 of 5` — BOTH NUMBERS WERE TRUE OF A DIFFERENT SET

`draft.columns` is every column the report SERVES (attributes and measures);
`attributes.length` is the rows in that section. The numerator is now the
intersection with the rows it heads. **Worked, on the two reports photographed:**
the statement reads **`1 of 5`** (seven served columns, five listed attributes,
one name in both — `reference`); the billing register moves from **`8 of 12` to
`6 of 12`**, because two of those eight are measures counted in the section
below. The drawing's own form is `4 OF 7`, where shown ≤ total by construction.

### 5 · THE NAMING PATH WAS EXTRACTED, NOT WRITTEN TWICE

`reportTableConfig` named a column inline as
`t("reports.col.<name>", {defaultValue: name})`, so the editor could only have
had words by writing that expression a second time — which is how a heading and
its own checkbox come to disagree. `reportWord()` is that expression, moved into
`reportsShared.tsx`, and **both** callers use it. It falls through to
`reports.param.*` because a FILTER is not a column and `source_type` has never
had a `reports.col.*` entry. **33 keys in eleven catalogues.** A name neither
catalogue has authored still renders as itself, deliberately: a blank is a
silence a clerk cannot report, so a raw name on screen is now a MISSING
CATALOGUE ENTRY and never a design.

### 6 · WHAT WAS FOUND AND NOT TAKEN

`DEF-REP-7071` / `DEF-REP-7072` — **opening `?edit=1` on a MODULE VIEWER strips
the statement from SEVEN served columns to ONE.** The panel seeds its draft from
`report.columns` and sends the ticks as a `columns` run control;
`runner._requested_columns` keeps only names the DATASET declares, and the
statement's seven intersect `journal_lines` in exactly `reference`. **Measured
in a browser at 1440: 7 columns without `?edit=1`, 1 with it.** It is invisible
on the forty-five dataset-backed reports and invisible to every fixture, because
none opens the editor on a module viewer. It was NOT fixed here: the three
candidate fixes are wave-two design decisions on a screen the PO is about to
have redrawn, and a lane choosing one would settle the shape of a screen already
under redesign. It is also why the new Example draws one column on that report —
the shape reads the same config the table does, so it is telling the truth about
a table that is wrong.

### 7 · NO VERSION IS CLAIMED, AND THAT IS A DECISION

`package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `pyproject.toml` were holding a sibling
lane's **uncommitted** bump to `2.381.1` in the shared working tree, over a
CHANGELOG entry describing rating work that is not on the branch. Writing
`2.382.1` over that line reverts their bump (law 11, mechanism two); committing
the three files as they stood publishes a release note for a fix nobody has
pushed (`DEF-168`, mechanism five). The allocator answered **`2.382.1`** and it
was free at push time. This lane's work ships under whichever version the next
bump carries, and the CHANGELOG says so in its own entry rather than leaving a
reader to work it out.

## 2026-09-27 — BR-RAT-091's RATIFIED `$0.00` BASE AND THE SAMPLE UTILITY'S SIGNED `$8` CANNOT BOTH DESCRIBE ONE TENANT (`DEF-RAT-7140`, lane RAT-REDS-9)

**The judgment, so no lane re-asks it (law 13): the fixture states the zero in
BOTH places. Neither signed figure moved, and neither was put to the PO.**

`BR-RAT-091`'s worked example is finance-shown and is pinned by
`06-backend/tests/test_br_rat_091_rate_change_impact.py`: *"the water +6% filing
moves an 11 kgal household `$59.00 → $62.54`, `+$3.54`/month, `$38,826`/year
across 914 accounts — and it FLOWS, because 6% is under the bar."* `$59.00` is
`5 × $4.00 + 6 × $6.50` and a base of **`$0.00`**, stated on the PLAN — a
`DEF-277` *"stated, and free"* zero, not an absence.

`BR-RAT-088` (PO 2026-08-20) then made the CHARGE CODE the first question, and
`tests/test_us_rat_helpers` auto-declares every enabled service's base code at
`core.sample_fixture`'s signed figure — `[W] §1 "Base/mo … Water $8"`. So one
tenant had a plan saying `0.00` and a `BASE-W` code saying `8.0000`, and
`apps/billing/gather._base_charge_for` refused the pair by name:

    GatherProblem: Two base charges for water. Clear 0.00 on the plan.

**THE REFUSAL IS THE PRODUCT WORKING AND WAS NOT TOUCHED.** A bill produced from
whichever of two disagreeing figures the code reached first is `DEF-154`. What
was wrong is the FIXTURE: it asked for a utility that charges no water base and
then declared an `$8` one for it.

**WHAT WAS DECIDED, AND WHY IT IS OURS RATHER THAN THE PO'S.** The fixture now
declares `BASE-W` at **`$0.00`** before the schedule is built — the way a
utility would, on the Charge codes screen, through `create_charge` with
`is_base` set. **`$8` is the SAMPLE utility's figure and is untouched**;
`BASE_CHARGE_AMOUNTS` already seeds trash and sewer at `0` under the PO's own
`OQ-317` ruling, so a `$0.00` base is a lawful thing for a utility to have. No
signed figure is reinterpreted and no frozen figure moves, so this is a judgment
recorded here rather than a question — law 13's *"a judgment call recorded in the
decision log with its reasoning is the deliverable"*.

**MEASURED, BOTH WAYS, ON THE SAME TIP `5a75e6258`:**

| | result |
|---|---|
| before | **8 failed, 7 passed** in `1319.76s` |
| after | **15 passed** in `67.53s` |

The four ratified figures come back exactly: `worst_case_pct 6.000000`,
`average_change 3.540000`, `second_approval_required False`,
`second_approval_threshold_pct_display 10.00%`.

**`DEF-528`'s INVARIANT IS UNTOUCHED** — the service still HAS a base charge
code, and it states zero. Nothing weakens `_guard_base_charge_code`.

**AND THE PARK THAT HID IT IS THE DURABLE LESSON.** All nine reds were parked in
`backend_suite_known_reds.txt` under `DEF-RAT-7000`, whose fix (`bb62396d2`) is
an **ancestor of every commit they were measured at**, the parking commit
included. A park is a claim about a **CAUSE**, not merely about a node id, and
nothing in this repo re-asks whether a parked red is still red for the reason it
was parked for. The file is empty again, and its header now carries the measured
numbers instead of a sentence about six files that was already false when it was
written.

## 2026-09-28 · The report editor moves to its OWN PAGE — superseding the 2026-09-26 "panel" ruling

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"the report editor — panel or its own page - own page"*

⚠ **THIS REVERSES A RULING TWO DAYS OLD AND THE SUPERSESSION IS STATED RATHER
THAN ASSUMED (hard-won law 13).** On **2026-09-26** the same question was put and
answered **"panel"**: the builder sits beside the live table so the rows change
as a column is ticked, instead of the clerk having to finish describing a report
before seeing one. That ruling is stamped `RULED PANEL` on p31–p33 of
`05-prototype/09 Reports Build Brief.pdf`, is index row 25 of this log, and was
built — the panel measured at 1160px against a table ending at 1144px, 0px of
horizontal overflow at 1280.

**Why it was re-asked rather than simply obeyed.** On 2026-09-27 the PO said of
the shipped panel: *"report editor is not user friendly - as a user i dont know
what im doing and how field are shown - no edit no adds, can you use a page
instead of size panel?"* Lane REP-EDITOR-B checked the drawing before building,
found the panel ruling one day older than the complaint, and **stopped** rather
than guess which was current — which is what law 13 asks for when a new
instruction collides with a signed one.

**What was put to the PO before they chose, in plain English:**

  * **Renaming and moving a column already work** — the pencil renames a heading,
    the arrows move it (`ReportEditPanel.tsx:335-412`). So *"no edit no adds"* was
    partly a discoverability fault, not an absent feature.
  * **What genuinely cannot be done is inventing a column the dataset does not
    produce.** A column such as *Total = 61-90 plus 90+* is a change request of
    its own.
  * **The crowded filters are OUR miss and are drawn otherwise** — p31 §4 draws
    only the filters carrying a value, then `+ Add filter`, then
    `Show on the bar · 4 of 13`. `ReportEditPanel.tsx:466` maps the dataset's
    WHOLE filter list, so thirteen declared filters draw thirteen stacked rows
    (`DEF-REP-7080`).
  * **The cost of a page**, stated before the choice: the live preview the panel
    was chosen for. A page cannot show the rows changing as a column is ticked.

**The PO chose the page with that cost in front of them.** So the trade is
accepted, not overlooked, and nobody may re-open it by citing the 2026-09-26
ruling — that ruling is SUPERSEDED as of this date.

⚠ **WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO.** It does not make the drawing wrong about
anything else on p31-p33, and it does not cancel `DEF-REP-7080` (the thirteen
stacked filters), `DEF-REP-7072` (opening the editor on a statement strips the
report from seven columns to one) or `DEF-REP-7073` (fixed: any control closed
the editor). Those are faults of the editor whatever shape it takes, and a page
that carried all three forward would be the same complaint at a different
address.

⚠ **AND THE PREVIEW IS THE THING TO DESIGN FOR, NOT THE THING TO DROP.** The
panel's whole argument was *commit-at-the-end means you cannot see your report
until you have finished describing it* (Reports Build Brief p3). A page that
simply reproduces that failure is the wizard the PO already refused on
2026-09-26. Whoever builds it owes an answer to *what does the clerk see while
they are choosing* — the `ReportShapePreview` built on 2026-09-27 (column
headings and grey bars, no data, so no invented figure can be quoted) is the
starting point, not a page with nothing on it.

## 2026-09-28 · The Units screen's "Missing services" block becomes a FILTER on the list

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"the Units "Missing services" block — filter or leave
it. - filter"*, raised by them as *"why this is build - missing services - it
would ahve been a filer criteria and I can filter th units based on this"*

**WHAT WAS THERE.** `UnitServiceGaps.tsx` draws a second table above the units
list — 60 of 132 units on the seeded utility — with its own pager, its own
columns (`OFFERED HERE`, `MISSING`) and its own read (`GET /units/service-gaps`).
It was added 2026-09-25 for `DEF-MET-6796` (units created holding fewer service
points than their address offers, invisible to every screen, gate and test).

⚠ **IT WAS AN ADDITION TO A DRAWN SCREEN, NOT A DRAWN FEATURE.** The Premises &
Units blueprint's `U1` frame (pages 50-52) draws the units list with no gap
report on it. The lane recorded that departure in its own header rather than
leaving it to be found, which is why this question could be answered from the
repo in one read.

**WHY THE PO IS RIGHT, and the reason is not aesthetic.** A section cannot
compose. The 60 units are shown twice — once in the block, once in the list
below — and in the block a clerk cannot combine them with the search or the four
existing filters, cannot page them with the list, and **cannot select them for a
bulk action**. That last one is the strongest: the gap is a thing to FIX, and the
block is the one place in the product where those exact units cannot be acted on
together.

**WHAT REPLACES IT.** A *Missing services* filter on the ordinary units list,
carrying its count (`60`) the way the existing filters do. The two facts the
block carried become two columns of the units table, show/hide like any other.
The separate block is DELETED, not kept alongside — two doors onto one set is how
they drift apart, and `CR-068` R3's rotten holds are this repo's worked example.

⚠ **THE COUNT MUST SURVIVE THE MOVE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE ORIGINAL
DEFECT.** `DEF-MET-6796` exists because the shortfall was INVISIBLE. A filter
nobody switches on is invisible too, so the count belongs where the eye lands
whether or not the filter is engaged — that is the deliverable, not the filter
control.

⚠ **AND THE READ MUST STAY PAGED AND SORTED IN SQL (`NFR-3`, `NFR-5`).** The
block's read already pages; folding it into the list's read must not turn it
into an unpaginated scan, and no per-tenant cap may appear.

**FOUND WHILE ANSWERING, AND FIXED FIRST (`DEF-MET-7090`):** every unit name in
that block was a DEAD LINK. It built `/units/<id>` by hand while `App.tsx` mounts
`premises/units/:unitId`, so pressing a unit read *"This screen is not built
yet"*. `meteringShared` has owned `unitDetailPath` all along. The test asserted
the SAME literal the component built — a string compared with itself, which can
never ask whether the router mounts it.

### BUILT 2026-09-28 — and what the signature actually covered

**Lane `MET-GAPFILTER`, version `2.387.0`.** The ruling above was put back to
the PO as a change plan and they answered **"this is correct"**, so the seven
lines below are RATIFIED rather than this lane's judgment, and each is recorded
as what was shown:

| Shown to the PO | Built |
|---|---|
| the separate block is **deleted**, not hidden | `UnitServiceGaps.tsx` and its dom test are gone |
| its own pager goes | the units list's footer pages the filtered set; one pager on the screen |
| `GET /units/service-gaps` is **retired** | deleted, after its one consumer was walked; a test asserts the address is absent |
| a **Missing services** filter with the four already there | declared in `unitsTableConfig`, `f.missing_services` on the wire, a removable chip |
| **its count is visible whether or not the filter is on** | `service_gap_count` on the units envelope, drawn as a `ChipToggle` on the toolbar |
| an **Offered here** column | declared, hidden by default — see the one thing going back to them |
| a **Missing** column | declared, visible by default |

**MEASURED IN A BROWSER, 1440 AND 1280, `brazosbend`:** the toolbar reads
**`Missing services 43 units`** with nothing switched on; pressing it narrows
131 units to 43 and leaves a `Missing services: Yes ×` chip; adding the search
*Main* narrows it again to 25; and the bulk bar's `Select all 43` and
**Assign a plan to these** both reach the filtered set. Shots in the lane
report.

**MEASURED ON REAL POSTGRESQL 16** (`10-scripts/def_met_7220_units_gap_cost.py`,
median of 3 after a discarded warm-up), because the ceiling is 40,000 accounts
and `CR-138` `P4` is the worked precedent for a read that is correct at 3,000
and **killed** at 40,000:

| tenant size | list, filter off | list, filter on | the toolbar count | whole envelope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,000 units | 1.211s | 0.590s | 0.020s | 1.231s / 0.609s |
| **40,000 units** | 1.204s | 1.017s | 0.174s | **1.378s / 1.191s** |

**1.4 seconds against a sixty-second worker, and FLAT across a tenant twenty
times larger** — because the rows BUILT are fifty either way and only the two
`COUNT(*)`s grow. `NFR-3` and `NFR-5` both hold: `_short_of_offer` narrows
inside `units_queryset`'s own SQL and nothing caps anything.

⚠ **ONE THING GOES BACK TO THE PO AND IT IS NOT A DECISION THIS LANE TOOK.**
`Offered here` and the drawn `Services` column are the SAME fact — `row.services`
is what the address offers (`DEF-755`), which is what *Offered here* meant inside
the block. The ratified column is therefore DECLARED but **hidden by default**,
because a second default column would draw one fact twice on a row that already
carries ten (B14 rule 32) and would add a column the `U1` frame does not draw
(rule 41). The question put to them, in their own words: *the Services column
already shows what the address offers, so Offered here is the same list under a
second name — is one column enough?* Recorded in the conformance file beside the
frame it departs from.

⚠ **AND THE DELETED-UNIT EXCLUSION MOVED WITHOUT CHANGING ANY NUMBER.** The
retired report excluded deleted units — *"a unit taken out of service is not a
service the utility is failing to bill"* — while the units list shows them with
an `inactive` status. Both still hold: the exclusion rides INSIDE the filter's
branch, so the figure a clerk reads is the same figure the block printed.

## 2026-09-28 · R4's ROUTE column shows EVERY route as a short code — it does not pick one

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"just show multi or short code for routes - R-001,
R002 - somehing like this"*

**THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS (`OQ-REP-12768`, now CLOSED).** An account does not have
a route. A route belongs to ONE service, so a house taking water and gas is on
TWO routes — the route-membership table says so in its own words (*"a house on
water AND gas is on two routes"*) and carries two uniqueness constraints
precisely so it can. The Bill Run Readiness drawing (p49-p50) has one ROUTE cell,
which is only correct for a utility that sells one thing.

Four shapes were on the table. The coordinator recommended *the route belonging
to the cycle the clerk already picked* — single-valued for free, because the
clerk has already typed the cycle. **The PO rejected the premise rather than
choosing between the options: do not pick one, SHOW THEM ALL.**

**And they are right, for a reason worth writing down.** Every option that picks
one route answers a question the clerk did not ask, and answers it invisibly. A
clerk looking at a held account before a bill run needs to know where to send
somebody; *one of the two routes this account is on* is a worse answer than both,
and there is no way to tell from the screen which rule chose it.

**WHAT TO BUILD.** The cell lists the account's route codes, comma-separated, in
a stable order: `R-001, R-002`. One route draws one code. No route draws the
column's stated absence, never a blank. The code is the tenant's own short code
for the route — **B14 rule 31: never the database id**.

⚠ **THIS RULING COVERS ROUTE AND NOT USAGE.** The USAGE column fails for a
related but different reason — a two-service account's consumption is gallons
PLUS kilowatt-hours, and the Reports Build Brief says on p62 that quantities are
never added across services *"because gallons plus kilowatt-hours is not a
number"*. Listing route codes is lawful because a list of names is not an
addition; a single usage figure is. **USAGE stays served empty with its reason
until it is ruled separately.** Nobody may read this ruling as licence to sum it.

⚠ **AND THE FILTER FOLLOWS THE COLUMN, NOW THAT THE COLUMN CAN ANSWER.** Lane
REP-P6-W4 deliberately did not offer a Route filter, because a filter over a
column that is empty on every row is a control that cannot work. That reasoning
expires with this ruling: a filter matching an account that is ON a named route
is well-defined even when the account is on two. It is `BR-REP-060`'s clause to
amend, in the commit that fills the column — hard-won law 2's mirror says the
hold and the thing that releases it move together, or the hold rots.

## 2026-09-28 · The Billing Register's CSV export KEEPS the zeros the screen hides

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"whether the Billing Register's CSV export should hide
the same zeros the screen now hides - show them"*

**THE QUESTION (`DEF-REP-7015`, now CLOSED as ruled-and-correct).** On
2026-09-27 the register's USAGE cell stopped drawing *counted* zeros — `0 cart`,
`0 connection` — while still drawing *measured* ones, because `0 cart` means the
unit has no carts and `0 kgal` means a meter was read and read zero. Two facts,
the same `"0"` on the wire (`DEF-REP-7010`). The export was left alone, so the
same filters now give two answers.

**RULED: the file keeps them.** A file is the record; a screen is for reading.
The export is what a finance officer loads into a spreadsheet and reconciles
against, and a reconciliation that cannot see a zero cannot tell *no carts* from
*a column that was dropped*.

⚠ **THIS CONFIRMS CURRENT BEHAVIOUR RATHER THAN CHANGING IT, AND THAT IS WHY IT
IS WRITTEN DOWN.** `_usage_cell`'s drop is on the viewing path only; the export
already carries every figure. A ruling that changes nothing is still a ruling:
without it the divergence reads as an oversight and the next lane "fixes" it in
one line, exactly as `DEF-REP-7015` proposed. **Nobody may align the export to
the screen without a new ruling.**

⚠ **THE TWO READS ARE ALREADY TWO FUNCTIONS, NOT ONE FUNCTION WITH A FLAG, AND
THIS RULING IS WHY THAT MATTERS.** Viewing fetches a page; exporting streams
every row. Collapsing them so the drop could be shared would make this
divergence impossible to hold.

⚠ **AND THE SCREEN MUST NOT START CLAIMING COMPLETENESS.** B14 rule 33 puts
RATIONALE at zero words on screen, so the register says nothing about what the
export contains — it simply never claims the cell is the whole story. A note
explaining the difference would break rule 33 while trying to honour this
ruling; the honest build is silence.

## 2026-09-28 · SFTP delivery REQUIRES the customer's server fingerprint, given at setup

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"a — ask for the number (recommended)"*, answering
*"If the customer tells us their number in advance - this is correct"*.

**THE QUESTION (`OQ-REP-12767`, now CLOSED.)** `P4.14` ruled that a scheduled
file may leave the product to admin-set destinations. SFTP was refused **at
create**, not at send, for two reasons and only one was code: no SSH client is
installed here (`paramiko`, `pysftp`, `asyncssh` — all absent, checked rather
than assumed), and **nobody had decided what to do the first time our system
meets a host key.**

**WHY IT COULD NOT BE DECIDED BY A LANE.** *Accept whatever answers* is every
library's default and it is a man-in-the-middle **with no symptom**: the transfer
succeeds, the delivery is logged as sent, and `P4.15`'s own *"412 names,
addresses and balances"* are read by whoever answered. The safe alternative needs
the server's public-key fingerprint **in advance**, and that is a fact only the
customer holds — which is exactly the third bullet of hard-won law 13's short
list of what legitimately reaches the PO.

**WHAT WAS PUT TO THEM, IN PLAIN ENGLISH AND WITH NO JARGON:** every file server
has a permanent ID of its own, the same every time. If the customer tells us
theirs when the destination is set up, we check it every night and stop if it
does not match. If they do not, the first connection trusts whoever answers, and
that is the one connection an interceptor wants. **Cost to the customer: one line
of text their IT person reads off their own server in about thirty seconds, on a
form where they are already typing a host, a username and a folder.**

**RULED: (a) — the fingerprint is REQUIRED at setup.**

**What this means for the build, and the first clause is the load-bearing one:**

  * **The destination CANNOT BE SAVED without a fingerprint.** Not a warning, not
    a default, not a tick-box to skip it. Hard-won law 3: *the unsafe option must
    be the one you type* — and here there is no unsafe option to type at all.
  * **A mismatch at send time STOPS that delivery and says so.** It never falls
    back to sending anyway, and never silently retries against whatever answered.
    A refusal a clerk can read beats a file that went somewhere.
  * **The fingerprint is a per-destination secret-adjacent value.** It is not a
    password and does not need to be hidden from the clerk who typed it, but it
    is tenant data under hard rule 1 like everything else.
  * **Every delivery is logged (`P4.14`), and a refused one is logged too.** A
    delivery that did not happen is the one a utility most needs to see.
  * **Changing a fingerprint later is an ordinary edit of the destination**, and
    it is exactly what a customer does when they rebuild their server. It is not
    a corruption to be feared; it is a routine event that must not require us.

⚠ **THE CLIENT LIBRARY IS STILL ABSENT AND THAT IS NOW THE ONLY BLOCKER.**
Installing one is an environment change (`environment.dependencies`), not a
product decision. Until it lands, SFTP keeps refusing **at create** — which is
deliberate and is law 2's mirror: a destination a clerk could save and that then
failed silently every night is worse than one they cannot save.

⚠ **THIS RULING IS ABOUT SFTP AND NOTHING ELSE.** Signed download links
(`P4.14`, four hours, tenant-scoped, proved over real HTTP) and email delivery
are unchanged and need no fingerprint.

## 2026-09-28 · A STALE PLAN FIGURE MAY NOT STOP A BILL — the charge code bound to the plan is the only source

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"we ahve to take ot from Charge code - whya re you confuse about it - charge code binded in plan - unitl it is part of plan we cannot take amount from charge code - we will never take default value from plan $8.0 - that is retired"*

**TWO STATEMENTS, AND BOTH ARE LOAD-BEARING:**

  1. **The amount comes from the CHARGE CODE, and only where that code is BOUND TO THE PLAN.** An unbound `is_base` code prices nothing — being in the catalogue is not being in this customer's plan.
  2. **The plan's own base figure is RETIRED. It is never a source and never a fallback.** Not even when the charge code is silent.

⚠ **THIS SUPERSEDES ONE CLAUSE OF `BR-RAT-088`'s ENTRY, AND THE SUPERSESSION IS STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED (law 13).** That entry reads, of the 2026-08-31 switch (`DEF-2823`): *"The live path now asks the `is_base` CHARGE CODE first … and REFUSES a plan figure that disagrees with it, naming both amounts: a plan still carrying a different base is a migration artefact"*, and *"The plan's column is NOT retired and is still written and still shown; it is a DISPLAY"*.

**The DISPLAY half stands. The REFUSES half does not.** A display that can stop a bill is not a display — it is a second source wearing a different word. `apps/billing/gather._base_charge_for` reads `plan_base`, `schedule_base` and `code_base`, and where the code has an amount and either of the other two differs it raises `GatherProblem("Two base charges for {service}. Clear {amount} on the {object}.")`. **Under this ruling that is wrong: with a bound charge code stating an amount, the bill is produced from it and the stale figure is ignored.**

⚠ **THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE THE OLD BEHAVIOUR LOOK SAFE IS THE REASON IT WAS NOT.** `BR-RAT-088`'s entry records: *"all 47 ready accounts on the seeded tenant state the SAME figure on both objects, so no bill moved"*. True, and it means the refusal branch **was never exercised by a real account** — it was unreachable on the data it was measured against, so a check that could only fire on a tenant whose migration left a different number went out untested against the case it existed for. Law 7's *incapable of failing* shape, one step removed.

**WHAT THIS COSTS A REAL UTILITY, WHICH IS WHY IT IS A MONEY-PATH FIX AND NOT TIDYING.** Any tenant whose retired column still holds an old figure has **every bill for that service stopped**, with a message telling a clerk to go and clear a number on an object the product itself says does not define it. The PO met the same family of refusal on the live beta twice this week.

**THE DEMO DATA IS THE WORKED CASE.** `apps/portal/sample_data.py:551` writes `"base_charge": "8.0000"` into the plan for **every service in a loop**, while the charge codes at line 440 say water `$12.00`, sewer `$8.00`, trash `$9.00`. So water and trash disagree and sewer agrees by coincidence. That is not two opinions about trash; it is one retired column filled blindly. **Both halves get fixed: the code stops reading the plan figure, and the fixture stops writing it.**

⚠ **`apps/billing/gather.py` AND `apps/rating/selectors.py` ARE 🔒 SENSITIVE PATHS.** AI authors them under the strongest machine gates, each flagged `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` with a row in `12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md`, and the ruling above is the human signature for the RULE — the implementation still needs its own row stating, in plain English with a figure, what was built.

⚠ **NO ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 FIGURE MOVES, AND THE FIX MUST PROVE THAT RATHER THAN CLAIM IT.** The golden suites are the check: `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` (33 document checks) and `06-backend/tests/golden/` (the 14 engine-verified GTs). Quote both, and remember they answer different questions — the first imports no application code and can never go red when the engine drifts.

⚠ **WHAT IS NOT RULED HERE.** Whether the plan's retired column should stop being WRITTEN and SHOWN at all is a separate question — the PO ruled on what may be READ. Do not delete the column or its display on the strength of this entry; a screen that stops showing a figure a clerk has been reading for weeks is its own change.

## 2026-09-28 · The unit statement WORKS OUT a historic occupant from the service records

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"this si correct - a — work it out from the service records"*, choosing option (a) of three.

**THE PROBLEM.** `journal_lines.customer_id` — the holder AT POSTING — began being stamped on 2026-09-24. Hard rule 4 forbids a backfill of a financial row. Measured on the real database: **661 of 661 lines carry `unit_id` and ZERO carry `customer_id`**, so the unit statement's Occupant column is empty on every line this product has ever written (`DEF-REP-7051`).

**THE ANSWER: DERIVE IT, and the data is already there.** `customers.ServiceAgreement` is account ↔ service point over time, with `started_on` and `ended_on` (NULL = still in force). A service point belongs to a unit. So for any line's posting date and unit, the account holding service that day is a lookup, and from the account its holders.

**WORKED EXAMPLE PUT TO THE PO.** Unit 200, 500 Main St. Marisol Vega billed `$84.20` on 1 August, moves out on the 15th; Dwayne Okafor billed `$120.00` on the 20th. Today both rows print Occupant BLANK. After this, **Marisol's two rows say Marisol and Dwayne's one says Dwayne** — which is the assertion that separates a right implementation from one reading today's holder, and the unit statement's existing test already makes exactly that distinction.

⚠ **THE COST WAS STATED BEFORE THEY CHOSE AND IS ACCEPTED, NOT OVERLOOKED.** Where an account is **held jointly**, the derived line names **BOTH holders**, not the one person who was actually there — a joint account belongs in full to each holder, so there is no honest way to pick one. And it is a **derived** answer rather than what was recorded at the time.

⚠ **THE STAMPED VALUE WINS WHERE IT EXISTS.** From 2026-09-24 the line carries what was true when the money moved; that is a fact and the derivation is an inference. **Stamp first, derive only where the stamp is absent.** Nothing about the stamping changes and no financial row is written.

⚠ **AND THE SCREEN DOES NOT EXPLAIN THE DIFFERENCE.** Option (c) — marking each cell as stamped or derived — was put to the PO and NOT chosen. B14 rule 33 puts RATIONALE at ZERO WORDS on screen, so a cell saying *(derived)* is the rule being broken to excuse the product. The reasoning belongs in the read model's docstring and in this entry.

⚠ **WHERE NO AGREEMENT COVERS THE DATE, THE CELL STAYS A NAMED ABSENCE.** A line posted against a unit with no service agreement on that day is a real gap, and inventing a holder for it is precisely what this ruling does NOT license. Refuse by name; never fall back to today's occupant.

**THIS IS A READ.** Hard rule 4 is untouched: no journal line is created, updated or deleted. `NFR-3` — the statement pages and sorts in SQL, and the derivation must not become a per-row query; resolve the whole page's agreements in one read or it is a quadratic loop on a document a clerk prints.

## 2026-09-28 · A bill records WHEN IT WAS VOIDED, from now on — and no past figure is corrected

**PO ruling, verbatim:** *"a is okay; dont correct old ones - we are in beta and no customer data is affected yet"*

**THE PROBLEM (`DEF-PAY-7020`).** `invoices` carries `issued_at` — whose immutability trigger refuses any UPDATE once set — and **no `voided_at` and no `corrected_at`**. So a past-date AR Ageing cannot tell whether a bill that is void TODAY was live at the as-at date. A `$340` bill issued 5 August and voided 20 September belongs in the 31 August figure and cannot be put there. The read counts those bills and publishes `retired_bills_cannot_be_restored_to_a_past_date` with the count rather than understating in silence — 1 on the sample tenant.

**RULED: record the void date from now on.** Every month-end from the day it ships is exact; every earlier one keeps its stated caveat.

⚠ **AND THE SECOND HALF IS A RULING IN ITS OWN RIGHT: NO OLD FIGURE IS RECONSTRUCTED.** Option (c) — rebuilding void dates from the audit trail — was put to the PO and is NOT taken. `audit_log` is pruned on a retention schedule with **no row type exempt** (PO ruling 2026-09-23, `OQ-1340`), so a reconstruction would be complete today, less complete next quarter, and would promise an accuracy the product cannot keep. **The PO's reason is better than ours: *"we are in beta and no customer data is affected yet"*** — the history that cannot be recovered is demo history, so buying it with a source we delete on a schedule is a bad trade twice over.

⚠ **THE CAVEAT STAYS ON PAST DATES AND MUST NOT BE QUIETLY DROPPED WHEN THE COLUMN LANDS.** A date before the column exists is still inexact, and the count beside it is the only thing telling a finance officer so. **Whoever ships the column must make the read say WHICH dates it can answer exactly** — a screen that stops mentioning the gap the day the column arrives is claiming accuracy for August that it does not have. That is hard-won law 2's mirror: the hold and the thing that releases it move together, or the hold rots.

⚠ **A VOID DATE IS AN ADDITION, NOT AN EDIT — hard rule 4 is untouched.** Writing `voided_at` when a bill is voided is the same act as writing `issued_at` when it is issued: a column set once, at the moment the thing happens, never updated afterwards. It must carry the same immutability guarantee `issued_at` has, or it becomes a field somebody can move and the report's exactness evaporates.

⚠ **`corrected` IS RECONSTRUCTIBLE AND `void` IS NOT, AND THIS RULING COVERS THE COLUMN ONLY.** A rebill carries `corrects_invoice_id` and its own frozen `issued_at`, so a corrected bill's live window is in principle derivable without a new column — lane P4-LAST recorded that and deliberately did not build it. Nothing here licenses building it either; it needs its own decision, and until then a corrected bill counts in the same stated gap.

**This is the same shape as the Occupant ruling of the same day: right going forward, never backwards, and honest about which.**

## 2026-09-28 · A report served by its own viewer declares its own columns — one list, not two

**THE PROBLEM (`DEF-REP-7072`), and what makes it worth an entry rather than a commit message.** Opening `/reports/statement?edit=1` cut a SEVEN-column statement to ONE. Measured through the runner on real PostgreSQL 16 before a line was changed:

    runner.run("statement", {...})                    -> 7 columns
    runner.run("statement", {..., "columns": <the 7>}) -> ['reference']

**NEITHER HALF WAS WRONG ABOUT ITSELF.** The editor offers the columns a DATASET declares, because *"a definition chooses from what a dataset offers"* is the property the whole report framework rests on. The runner honours the columns a DATASET declares, for the same reason. The statement is served by a MODULE VIEWER with a vocabulary of its own: it serves seven names, `journal_lines` declares five, and **the two lists intersect in `reference` and in nothing else.** One word out of seven, and the only control that sends the list is the one nobody presses while reading.

**THREE CANDIDATE FIXES WERE PUT AND ONE WAS TAKEN.**

| | What it was | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) TAKEN** | a module viewer DECLARES its served columns, and the editor and the runner both read that one declaration | — |
| (b) | the editor stops sending a `columns` control for module-viewer reports | It deletes the feature rather than fixing it: the panel would draw a tick list that changes nothing, which is hard-won law 2's mirror — a live control in front of a dead query — on the screen a defect was just filed about for being unusable. |
| (c) | `_requested_columns` falls back to the served set instead of emptying | **It does not even fire here.** One name survived the filter, so the list was never empty; the collapse was a PARTIAL overlap, not an empty one. And as a rule it converts a wrong answer into a different wrong answer: on any partial overlap it would silently discard what the clerk asked for. |

**THE REASONING, and it is the part that generalises past this screen:** the failure was two vocabularies that each behaved correctly and shared one word. A fall-back papers over the symptom; a removal deletes the feature; **only a single shared declaration makes the fault unreachable.** `runner.served_columns()` is now the one function that answers *what may this report be asked for*, and the offer (`column_choices` on the wire), the render narrowing and `validate()` at save all read it.

⚠ **THE OFFER AND THE HONOUR ARE DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT SETS, AND THAT IS NOT AN INCONSISTENCY.** `served_columns` is the UNION across a report's subjects, so a bookmarked `columns` is not refused the moment a clerk switches grain. `column_choices` is what the panel DRAWS and is the RUN's own set — on an account statement the unit subject's `occupant` and `account` are not among them, because a tick box for a column this run cannot serve is a control over nothing. Measured in a browser at 1440: the section read **`7 of 9`** before that split and **`7 of 7`** after.

⚠ **§8.1 IS NOT WIDENED.** A clerk still cannot name a column no reviewed declaration offers; a module viewer is reviewed code exactly as a dataset is. `viewer_columns()` returns `()` for all forty-five dataset-backed reports, so every one of them is refused at save exactly as it was, measures included.

## 2026-09-28 · Every report subject names the record it is about, through one composition

**THE PROBLEM (`DEF-REP-7052`).** `Subject.head_from` has been published since `P2.14` — `("account_no", "customer_name")` for an account, `("premises_address", "unit_label")` for a unit — and **was read by nothing**, on the server or on the screen. `grep -rn "head_from" 07-frontend/src` returned nothing. So a clerk printed a page of somebody's money with the report's name above it and no indication whose, and the shipped account ledger page has never named its account either. The Reports Build Brief draws it twice (p69 `100244 · Ruiz, Marisol`) and states it in prose on p71: *"The head reads 1408 Elm Street · Unit 3."*

**RULED HERE, as a judgment the rules ran out on (law 13): the composition lives on the SERVER and the screen holds no table of which subject shows what.** `apps/reports/subject_head.py` walks the subject's own `head_from` and asks a registered resolver for the values; `ReportSubjectHead.tsx` joins what it is handed with ` · ` and names no subject anywhere.

**WHY, and this is the cost of the alternative:** a front end that composed the head would need a map from subject to fields, and lane REP-SUBJ-2 is building the customer and premises subjects in the same hour. A hand-typed map there is the seventh of the six `P0.7` deleted, and it fails the way the eleventh utility service fails — the row exists, the API serves it, `tsc` and every test pass, and the screen simply never shows it.

**SO A NEW SUBJECT PLUGS IN AT ONE PLACE: `HEAD_RESOLVERS` in `apps/reports/subject_head.py`.** Nothing on any screen changes.

⚠ **A PARTIAL HEAD IS PUBLISHED AND AN EMPTY ONE IS `None`.** A field that cannot be resolved is dropped, never guessed; a head with no parts at all is absent from the payload, so the screen draws nothing rather than a stray separator. **B14 rule 31:** every value is a word a clerk already reads — an account number, a person's name, an address, a unit label — and the id that selected the record travels only in the URL. A browser walk asserts the uuid is absent from the page's `textContent`.

⚠ **IT IS A ROLL-UP ITEM AND NOT A THIRD LINE.** `DEF-REP-7011` is the Product Owner counting four stacked lines above the register's first row and asking for two; the head goes FIRST in the line the window, the basis and the grain already share, because it is the SUBJECT of the sentence and the other three are facts about it.

## 2026-09-28 · The statement's export is registered — and a file carries every subject's columns

**THE PROBLEM (`DEF-REP-7053`).** `statement_stream` has been in `MODULE_STREAMS` since `P2.8`, measured yielding every row, and **no clerk could reach it**: the viewer draws Download only where `exportable` is true, `exportable` asks the export registry, and the registry had never heard of `statement`. Built and not wired — hard-won law 2 in its original direction, on the one report that is printed and posted more than any other.

**Proved over real HTTP rather than against a rendered button**, because a drawn control over a 404 is the defect one door along (`DEF-REP-6899`, on this same screen last week): `POST /api/exports` → **202**, `GET /api/exports/{job}/file` → **200**, 583 bytes, `content-disposition: attachment; filename="brazosbend_statement_20000101-20991231_posting_20260927T2306.csv"` — IS-11's basis segment included — and every money cell at **two decimals** in the file as on the screen.

⚠ **THE FILE CARRIES THE UNION OF BOTH SUBJECTS' COLUMNS, so `occupant` and `account` are EMPTY on an account statement.** One resource serves every subject because it is one report; a second registration keyed by a run parameter would be a second filename grammar and a second audit row for one file. R34's `paid`, R43's `target` and R4's `route` each already carry this reasoning: a column that is empty is one a reader can still tell apart from one that was never offered.

## 2026-09-28 · What the clerk sees while they choose: the builder's preview is FIVE REAL ROWS, and the shape where there are none

**This is the one decision the page ruling handed to whoever built it**, and it is recorded here rather than left in a docstring because the next lane will ask why the page does not simply show the whole table. The 2026-09-28 page ruling's own words: *"Whoever builds it owes an answer to what does the clerk see while they are choosing."*

**RULED, as a judgment the rules ran out on (law 13 — ours to decide and write down, not to ask):** screen 2·2 draws **the report's own first five rows**, run with the draft's columns, re-running on every tick — and, where the run returns nothing, **`ReportShapePreview`**: column headings over grey bars, carrying not one character that can be read as a figure.

**THE ARITHMETIC THAT DECIDED IT.** The panel bought a live table and paid for it in width: at 1440 the panel's left edge measured `1160px` against a table ending at `1144px`, and the controls got **240px**. On the page the controls get **384px** — one step up our own spacing scale — and the preview gets the rest. What that 144px buys is a filter's name and its value no longer competing for one line, which is the physical half of *"as a user i dont know what im doing and how field are shown"*.

**WHAT WAS GIVEN UP, NAMED.** The preview has no toolbar, no search, no sort, no pager, no KPI band, no export and no more than five rows. Every one of those belongs to the report a clerk is **reading**, which is 2·1 and is one click away; none of them is a decision being made on this screen.

**WHAT WAS GAINED, AND IT IS NOT A CONSOLATION PRIZE.** The preview is **sticky**. On the panel, scrolling to *Group & sort* scrolled the live table out of sight — the rows sat beside section ① and nowhere near section ⑤, so the thing the panel was chosen for was visible for one section out of seven. The preview now holds its position while the sections scroll under it. **That is the one respect in which the page is better than the panel it replaces.**

⚠ **REAL ROWS ARE NOT THE DECISION `ReportShapePreview` REVERSED.** That component draws bars because it fires where the query returned NOTHING, and the only alternative there is an invented figure on a money screen — the skill file forbids placeholder data by name and this product's posture is that *a confident wrong fact is worse than having none*. Here the server has answered with the tenant's own rows. There is nothing to invent, and the page picks between the two on `rows.length`, so a clerk always has a shape in front of them and never a made-up number.

⚠ **THE PREVIEW IS THE VIEWER'S OWN REQUEST AND ITS OWN CELL RENDERER.** Same endpoint, same query key, same `ReportCell`. A second preview endpoint or a second renderer would be two derivations of one fact, which is `7 of 5`'s mechanism one layer out.

## 2026-09-28 · The builder's address is a CHILD SEGMENT, so the signed reserved list does not move

**THE CONSTRAINT.** `/reports/:reportKey` is a catch-all over a name a **tenant** chooses, which is why `custom`, `dashboard`, `scheduled` and `history` each had to be RESERVED before they could be routed — four ordinary English words a utility might each name a report. That list is signed at FOUR, and `P5.3` chose `?edit=1` rather than widen it on a lane's own authority.

**RULED: `/reports/{key}/edit`.** A report key is `[a-z0-9_]` and never holds a slash (`apps/reports/models.py` validates the column; `reportKeyGrammar.test.ts` asserts the seeded vocabulary rather than trusting that sentence). So `/reports/edit` is still a report a utility may call *Edit*, `/reports/edit/edit` is that report's builder, and **the reserved list stays at four.** It is three segments against the viewer's two, so neither can swallow the other whatever the route order.

⚠ **AND IT CLOSES `DEF-REP-7073` STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN BY A FLAG.** That defect was `searchFrom` rebuilding the whole query string from the report's own parameters, so `edit` — which is not one of them — was DELETED by every control on the screen and the editor closed mid-keystroke. The fix at the time was one line re-setting it, which every future caller of `update()` has to remember. **A path is not rebuilt by `searchFrom` and cannot be dropped by it.**

⚠ **`?edit=1` STILL ANSWERS AND REDIRECTS, CARRYING THE REST OF THE QUERY.** It was the builder's address for two days and is in bookmarks, in two walkthrough scripts and in the Product Owner's own screenshots. An address that silently drops its meaning and renders the plain report is the worst of the three available behaviours: the clerk sees a screen that looks right and is not the one they asked for.

## 2026-09-28 · BUILT — the plan's retired base is off the money path, and the fixture that filled it blindly stops

**This entry RECORDS AN IMPLEMENTATION, not a new ruling.** The ruling is the
entry above it, *"A STALE PLAN FIGURE MAY NOT STOP A BILL"*. What is judged here
is what the rules did not say, and each judgment is written with its figure so
the next lane does not have to make it again.

**`DEF-BIL-7170` (critical) and `DEF-CWP-7001` are CLOSED at `2.387.1`.**
`DEF-BIL-7310` is OPEN and was filed by this lane.

### JUDGMENT 1 · The two retired parameters are DELETED, not left unread

`gather._base_charge_for(service_code, plan_base, schedule_base, code_base)`
became `_base_charge_for(service_code, *, code_base)`. Leaving the two in the
signature and ignoring them was the alternative and was rejected on this file's
own precedent: it deleted `code_label=` four days earlier saying *"a parameter
nothing reads is hard-won law 1 in miniature — so it is GONE rather than kept
'in case'"*. A retired source still sitting in a signature is an invitation to
read it again.

⚠ **AND `code_base` IS KEYWORD-ONLY, WHICH IS THE PART THAT IS NOT TIDINESS.**
Had the new function simply taken two positionals, every stale call would have
passed **the plan's figure where the charge code's belongs** — billing the
retired column under the ruling that retired it, with nothing anywhere going
red. That is `DEF-154`'s shape. Keyword-only turns each one into a `TypeError`
at the first line that runs it, and `test_the_two_retired_parameters_cannot_be_passed_BY_POSITION`
asserts exactly that.

**The deletion cascaded, and every hop was followed rather than left:**
`_tariff_config_for`'s own `plan_base=` (its only reader was that call),
`rating.seams.base_charge_for`'s `plan_base`/`schedule_base`, and the two
queries that existed only to fill them — one in the rate-change impact analysis
and one in the customer portal's standing charge. ⚠ **That seam is where
`DEF-RAT-7000` happened one week ago**: it wraps the call in `except Exception`
and reports a broken call as an ordinary refusal, so a caller left behind would
have failed silently for days. It is the reason the parameters had to go from
the seam too rather than merely stop being passed.

### JUDGMENT 2 · Where no bound charge code answers, it REFUSES — and the repair no longer names the plan

The sentence was *"No base charge for {service}. Type it on the plan's
services."* Under this ruling that sends a clerk to type a figure into the one
column the product has stopped reading: the bill would refuse again on the next
run and nothing on screen would say why. It is now **"No base charge for water.
Declare one on Charge codes."** — two sentences of six words, B14 rules 32 and
33, with the whole of the *why* in the function's docstring.

⚠ **THIS REFUSAL PRE-EMPTS THE RULED CHAIN'S OWN, AND THAT IS A REAL CHANGE OF
COPY ON A LIVE DEPLOYMENT.** With `R3,R4` served — the default — a tenant with
no base charge code was already refused, by R4, in **95 words** that name
`BR-RAT-088`, `DEF-154`, the schedule version's UUID and the connection size.
`gather` now refuses first, in twelve. The reason code on the exception screen
moves from `ruled_path_refused` to `plan_has_no_tariff_for_service`, which is
the more accurate of the two: it is a tariff configuration fault, not the ruled
path declining. **Measured, on PostgreSQL:** before, the clerk read the 95-word
paragraph; after, six words and a screen name.

### JUDGMENT 3 · Which fixtures stop writing the retired column, and which do not

The portal demo fixture wrote `base_charge: "8.0000"` into the plan **for every
service in a loop** while its charge codes said water `$12.00`, sewer `$8.00`
and trash `$9.00`. It stops writing it. **The alternative — writing the RIGHT
number — was rejected**: three services, two places, one figure each, and the
moment they can disagree something has to decide which wins, which is what the
ruling took away.

⚠ **`apps/rating/sample_data.py` AND `seed_demo.py` GO ON WRITING IT, DELIBERATELY.**
Both derive the plan's figure from the SAME expression that builds the
`is_base` charge code (`service_base_amounts.base_for`, `fixture.BACKBONE_BASE`),
so the two cannot drift; and the ruling explicitly does not touch the column's
being **written and shown**. What changes there is the REASON, which is stamped
in each file: agreement is now a DISPLAY requirement, not a condition of the
bill running.

### JUDGMENT 4 · A SECOND, OLDER FAULT THE FIX EXPOSED — `US-CWP-062`'s standing charge

Closing `DEF-CWP-7001` turned six red cases green and revealed that all of them
had been arithmetically wrong since **2026-09-06**, hidden behind the refusal.
`US-CWP-062` §4's `$18.50` is **water's** standing charge, and the demo account
has taken water, sewer AND trash since `CR-068` wave H — so the screen's real
figure was `$18.50 + $8.00 + $9.00 = $35.50`, and every derived figure in that
file was short.

**The fixture is what was changed, not the signed figures**, and the reason is a
guard: `test_us_cwp_062_twelve_months_still_says_stopping` exists to stop
`DEF-CWP-3608` being reverted, and it turns on `12 × $18.50 = $222.00` being
LESS than `$335.00`. At `$35.50` that becomes `$426.00`, the verdict flips to
*closing*, and the guard silently stops guarding. So the fixture prices the
other two services at an explicit **`$0.00`** — a stored zero is a PRICE and
bills `$0.00` (PO 2026-08-19, *"print $0.00"*), where removing the code would be
*nobody has stated this* and would refuse the whole read. It is also the honest
shape for this utility: sewer is billed as a share of water usage and trash per
cart, and neither needs a standing charge of its own.

### JUDGMENT 5 · One thing found and LEFT ALONE, with a row against it

`resolution_switch`'s R2-without-R3/R4 fork still compares
`tariff_versions.base_charge` between the two versions and refuses when they
differ. That column now decides nothing; what a version CAN still move is the
**binding**, `tariff_versions.base_charge_code` (`BR-RAT-1025`), which the
branch does not look at. It is `DEF-BIL-7310`, filed rather than fixed: the
branch runs on no deployment (`SERVED_BY_CHAIN_DEFAULT` is `R3,R4`), so the fix
could not be proved against a real configuration, and it fails CLOSED. **A
money-path change nobody can run a reproduction against is how the defect this
ruling fixes was shipped in the first place.**

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND HOW

**Reproduced first, on real PostgreSQL 16**, on the seeded `brazosbend` tenant —
the mismatched configuration the 2026-08-31 switch was never proved on, which is
the whole of `DEF-BIL-7170`'s escape reason.
`10-scripts/def_bil_7170_plan_base_retired_proof.py`, printed from
`gather.gather_account`:

    BEFORE  Two base charges for water. Clear 11.50 on the plan.
    AFTER   water base on the bill = 8.000000

**RED proved in the harness that runs it** (`pytest`, never `__main__`): eleven
cases across three files, each quoting its own sentence, on the pre-fix
`gather.py`. **No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure moved, and it was run rather than
claimed:** the document harness reports **33 checks, 33 PASS** and imports no
application code, so it can never go red when the engine drifts; the engine
suite — **14 of the 61 signed GTs engine-verified**, the number `G64` recomputes
— reports **23 passed, 1 xfailed**.

⚠ **TWO REDS THIS LANE DID NOT CAUSE, DATED AND RE-CHECKED AGAINST THE BRANCH
RATHER THAN DISMISSED.** `test_def_277_tc1` and `tc2` fail with
`rating.schedules.no_base_charge_code`, which is the schedule-activation guard
and not the billing read. They were re-run against the tip's own `gather.py` in
this same worktree and fail there identically, so they are pre-existing.

## 2026-09-28 · DEPLOYMENT: two hosts, `/api/health`, and per-environment frontend builds

**Three rulings, recorded BEFORE any code is written (hard-won laws 9, 10 and 13).**
The product moves off a single `docker-compose` to ECS Fargate behind an
Application Load Balancer, a static frontend on S3 behind a CDN, and three
environments — dev, sandbox, production.

### Ruling 1 — TWO SEPARATE HOSTS. The browser calls the API host directly.

**PO, verbatim:** *"I dont want to get locked in with the cdn from an cloud
provider later if I move out from this cloud I dont want this to be a blocker."*

So **no CDN path-routing of `/api/*`, and nothing CDN-specific in the code.**

| | frontend | API |
|---|---|---|
| dev | `https://app-dev.bynry.com` | `https://api-smart360-dev.bynry.com` |
| sandbox | `https://app-sandbox.bynry.com` | `https://api-smart360-sandbox.bynry.com` |
| production | `https://app.bynry.com` | `https://api-smart360.bynry.com` |

⚠ **THE SANDBOX PAIR FOLLOWS THE PATTERN AND WAS NOT SEPARATELY RULED.** It is
built as written; anything that DEPENDS on it goes back to the PO rather than
being assumed.

⚠ **THIS RULING IS WHY THE SECURITY POLICY MOVES INTO A `<meta>` TAG.** The
header was set by `07-frontend/server.mjs`, and **there is no Node server on S3**.
A CDN-specific header rule would be the lock-in the PO just refused, so the
policy is baked into `index.html` per build. **HSTS cannot go in a meta tag** —
the static host sends it, and that is an infrastructure note, not code.

### Ruling 2 — THE HEALTH PATH IS `/api/health`

**Not** `/api/smart360/health/`. **`/api/smart360/...` was REJECTED because every
`/api/<segment>/` is read as a customer (tenant) slug** — `core/tenancy.py`
resolves the tenant from that segment, so a health path shaped like one would ask
for a utility called `smart360`.

**It must need no sign-in**, so the load balancer's check passes.

⚠ **AND IT MUST BE ANSWERED BY MIDDLEWARE PLACED FIRST, WHICH IS NOT A STYLE
CHOICE.** The load balancer sends **the ECS task's private IP as the host name**.
`ALLOWED_HOSTS` does not list it, so **Django answers 400 before any view runs** —
a health VIEW can never be reached. The middleware therefore sits ahead of
`SecurityMiddleware` and `CommonMiddleware` in `config/settings/base.py`, and
**ahead of any HTTPS redirect added for HSTS**, or the check gets a 301 instead
of a 200. It is kept shallow on purpose: `200 {"status":"ok"}`, **no database, no
Redis** — a check that fails when the database is slow takes the whole service
down instead of reporting it.

**Verified in the code before recording:** `health` is ALREADY reserved as a
non-tenant segment in `core/tenancy.py:127` (`NON_TENANT_SEGMENTS`) and in
`apps/tenancy/selectors.py:102` (`RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS`), so no customer can ever
be named `health`. `core/tenancy.py:115` even carries the comment *"health — the
load-balancer probe (09-infra; no Django route yet)"*. The reservation was made
and the route never was.

### Ruling 3 — THREE BUILD COMMANDS, EACH BAKING ITS OWN API HOST

`npm run build:dev`, `npm run build:sandbox`, `npm run build:prod`. The pipeline
copies `dist/` to S3.

⚠ **THE BUILD MUST FAIL WHEN `VITE_API_BASE_URL` IS MISSING for sandbox or
production** — hard-won law 3, *defaults fail closed*. A build that silently
falls back to a relative URL produces a bundle that calls its own static host and
**every screen fails at once, in production, with nothing red anywhere in CI.**

⚠ **THE VALUES ARE BAKED IN AT BUILD TIME.** Changing an env file changes nothing
already on S3; it needs a rebuild. That is hard-won law 4's shape for the front
end, and it goes in the README rather than being left to be discovered.

The brief named `connect-src` and `img-src`. Built with **four**, and the extra

| **`frame-src`** | `BillDetailPage` and `BillLayoutTab` FRAME `/api/{tenant}/…/document.pdf` |
| **`object-src`** | the portal's `DocumentPreview` shows a kept document in an `<object>` |

`DEF-INT-4410` moved those two off `'none'` on 2026-09-07 for exactly this
reason, when the same-origin assumption still held. **The day the API stops
being the same origin, `'self'` is worth what `'none'` was worth then** — an
empty grey box saying the content is blocked, on the screen that puts a bill in
front of a person. Leaving them out would have reproduced that defect
identically, and no check in this repository would have said so.

`frame-ancestors` is deliberately NOT widened: it governs who may frame THIS
document, and nothing about that changed.

⚠ **THE BASE POLICY IS READ OUT OF `server.mjs`, NEVER COPIED.** It already
lives twice — `server.mjs` and `page_policy.py`, kept byte-identical by
`server.test.mjs` — because a Node process cannot import a Python module. A
third literal in the Vite config would have been the same drift one file
further along (hard-won law 5), so `scripts/deployConfig.mjs` parses
`server.mjs` exactly as that test does. `server.test.mjs` is green, 14 of 14,
with the identity case among them.

### ⚠ WHAT THE MOVE COSTS, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY ACCEPTED — `DEF-INT-7430`

`server.mjs` asked the API for a **per-tenant** policy and widened `img-src`
with that tenant's registered basemap tile host (`DEF-INT-4287`). **A document
baked once and served to every tenant cannot do that**, and a `<meta>` policy
**intersects** with any header the static host later adds rather than being
replaced by it — so the meta tag caps what a header can ever allow. The asset
map's tiles are therefore refused on the static host until that host is given a
tile origin of its own.

It is filed rather than fixed here because the fix is a choice between two
infrastructure shapes, and neither is this lane's to make: give the static host
the tile origin, or have it serve the whole policy as a header and drop the meta
tag. **Nothing in this repository could have caught it** — the tile host arrives
at runtime from `GET /integrations/page-policy`, so the build, `tsc`, eslint,
every unit test and the new bundle check all pass over it, and it is visible
only as a grey map in a browser.

The brief said the build must fail for **sandbox or production**. Built to fail
for **dev as well**, deliberately, and it is a strictly safer superset rather
than a disagreement: `app-dev.bynry.com` is a static host too, so a dev bundle
with a relative base URL fails every screen in exactly the same way, and
`.env.dev` supplies the value so nothing is inconvenienced. The dev SERVER
(`npm run dev`) and the test run are untouched and stay same-origin — those are
the two places an empty value is the right answer.

It also refuses a **trailing slash** and an origin **carrying a path**, rather
than trimming either: `client.ts` appends its own `/api/…`, so `https://host/`
would build a double slash, and a helpful trim is how the next reader comes to
believe the value is normalised somewhere it is not.

**Proved red in the harness that runs it** — `.env.production` emptied, then

```
Error: VITE_API_BASE_URL is empty or missing for mode "production".
A deployed bundle is served from a static host that answers no API, so a
relative base URL makes every screen in the product fail at once and nothing
in CI goes red. Set it in 07-frontend/.env.production — for example
  VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://api-smart360.bynry.com
```

## 2026-09-28 · A BUNDLE CHECK, AND THE ONE FAULT IT EXISTS FOR

`07-frontend/scripts/checkBundleHost.mjs` reads the BUILT files and asserts the
bundle names **this** environment's API host and **no other environment's**.

**The fault it exists for is not a typo.** A production deploy built from the
sandbox env file is a perfectly healthy-looking bundle, identical in shape, that
sends every production customer's data to the sandbox API. `tsc` cannot see it,
no unit test can (they never build), and the running page looks right until
somebody opens a network tab.

**Proved RED first, twice, in the harness that runs it:**

* pointed at the production bundle asking for sandbox —
  `FAIL — 3 problem(s)`, naming `dist-production/assets/index-Ctrn4c-Z.js` and
  `dist-production/index.html` as carrying the production host, and then
  `no file … contains this build's API host … (5 files read)`;
* pointed at an empty directory —
  `FAIL — no .js/.html/.css files under … — nothing was checked`.

The second is there on purpose: **a check reporting a clean zero over a scope it
cannot see is this repository's most-filed fault**, so an empty scope is a
failure and never a pass, and the pass line prints the number of files read
beside the verdict.

⚠ **ONE RED PROOF CAME BACK NULL AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH.** The origin-boundary
case — that `https://api-smart360.bynry.com` must not match inside
`https://api-smart360-dev.bynry.com` — could not be made to fire, because
`api-smart360` is followed by `-dev` rather than by `.bynry`, so these three
particular hosts do not collide. The boundary test is kept and is covered by a
unit case instead; **it is a guard against the next host name, not against these
three, and saying so is the difference between a proof and a claim.**
