## 2026-09-29 — `DEF-CUS-7910` AND `DEF-CUS-7911` · THE BRIDGE THAT OUTLIVED ITS CONDITION, AND WHAT A PHOTOGRAPH SAW THAT NO TEST COULD

**Lane NCT-01 (`CR-150-BRC09` tasks 11–14), version `2.410.6`.**

**WHAT WAS WRONG.** From `2.401.0` the last step of New Connect rendered *Who we
are telling* and *Messages* **twice** — two contact tables, two message tables,
two `+ Add template` buttons, and therefore the same element `id` twice in one
document. `NewConnectWizard.tsx` mounted the old Communication panel beneath the
review with a comment that said exactly when to remove it: *"until the REVIEW
lane draws it there, the step's own panel renders here so no message, channel or
template is lost."* The Review lane drew it there in the same release. **The
hold was correct the day it was written and wrong the day its condition was
met** — hard-won law 2's mirror, and CLAUDE.md's own instruction, *when you land
a screen, grep for the control that was holding it*, not followed by the lane
that landed the screen.

**WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** Every check this
repo had was a PRESENCE check, and **a presence check is satisfied by the first
copy and says nothing about the second**. `toContain` passed. The browser walk's
`page.$(sel)` passed. 22 DOM cases, `tsc`, eslint and every gate passed. The one
artefact that could have shown it is a picture of the whole screen — hard-won
law 6, the job no gate here does.

**AND THE PICTURE WAS CROPPED WITHOUT SAYING SO.** The walk shot with
`fullPage: true`, which grows the DOCUMENT; this app scrolls an INNER container,
so the document is always exactly one viewport tall and every capture came back
`1440x1400` for a screen **3,326px** long. No error, no warning, nothing in the
output to say two thirds of the screen was missing — **law 7's fifth shape, a
check reporting truthfully over a scope it silently excludes.** The duplicate sat
below the crop. Fixed: `shot()` now scrolls every scroller to the top, measures
the tallest, grows the viewport to fit and **prints the height beside the file**,
so a truncated capture is visible in the log rather than only in the pixels.
Review now captures at 2,633px, and the 693px difference IS the deleted
duplicate.

**THE CHECK THAT REPLACES THE ASSUMPTION.** Four cases in
`NewConnectRedesignSteps45.dom.test.tsx` mount **the assembled wizard** — not the
Review step alone, which cannot see a copy mounted around it — and **COUNT**:
`data-telling`, `data-array="messages"` and `data-array-action="add-template"`
must each appear exactly once on step 5 and not at all on step 4. Proved RED in
the harness that runs them, reporting `expected 2 to be 1` three times, before
the bridge was removed.

**TWO SMALLER CORRECTIONS IN THE SAME COMMIT.** The `data-tracks` handle on the
plan-assignment absences said `step-2` on both the Review glance cell and the
Charges context strip. **There is no plans step any more** — the five-step list
folds units, services and plans into step 3 — so both now say `step-3`. They are
`aria-hidden`, which is precisely why they rot unnoticed.

**WHAT WAS NOT TOUCHED.** `ConnectionDetail` is imported and unused in
`NewConnectWizard.tsx`; `git log -S` dates it to **2026-09-24** (`dbe98329a`) and
it is unused at the tip as well, so it is **not this lane's and is left for its
owner** rather than tidied inside another lane's file. The `frame-ancestors` CSP
console warning is the same: `c6caadf2f`, **2026-09-22**, from `server.mjs`. It
was being counted as a walk finding, which pinned that walk's exit code at 1
forever — a check that can never report success (law 7, habit 3) — so it is now
classified as not-ours **by its exact directive name**, narrowly, rather than by
widening the pattern to swallow a real policy error later.


**AND THE SAME DEFECT WAS FOUND TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, WHICH IS THE PART TO
KEEP.** Lane **NC5-PHOTOS** photographed all five built steps the same
afternoon and filed `DEF-CUS-7910` for this duplicate from its own picture,
minutes before this lane reached it from the other end. **Both routes were the
same route:** look at the whole screen. This lane had allocated `DEF-CUS-7920`
for it before seeing theirs and **withdrew that row rather than publish a
second id for one defect** — two rows for one fault is exactly the harm
`file_defect.py` exists to prevent, and the earlier id belongs to whoever
pushed first.

**`DEF-CUS-7911`, FIXED HERE AND FOUND BY THEM.** Their photograph showed the
review's charge table with three columns where `step5-review.png` draws five:
`Each` and `Amount` were simply absent, so the last screen before *Create*
summarised the charges and never said what one cost. ⚠ **The group's own
docstring two lines above already claimed both came from
`POST /connections/quote-preview` through this component's props** — hard-won
law 1 in its purest form, a comment claiming a guarantee that nothing
provided. Both columns now read the SAME cached preview step 4 reads, through
the same `QuoteMoney` cell, so the review cannot disagree with the step it
summarises; **an unpriced line draws a blank and never `$0.00`**, and the new
case asserts no `$` reaches an unpriced screen, so it goes red the day anyone
multiplies in the browser.

**WHAT THE TWO LANES TOGETHER SAY ABOUT THIS REPO'S BLIND SPOT.** Every check
on these screens asked *is it present* — of a panel, of a row. Neither axis of
this pair was covered: `7910` is a panel present TWICE, `7911` is a column
present ZERO times, and a presence check cannot see either. The cases added
here COUNT panels and name columns for that reason. **Law 6 is not a slogan
about diffing against the prototype; on this branch it was the only instrument
that worked.**

## 2026-09-29 · FOUR DATABASE IDS ON THE ONE-TIME BILL SCREEN, AND THE GUARD THAT COULD NOT SEE THEM (`DEF-RAT-7991`, `v2.410.9`)

**What a clerk was shown, word for word:**

> R2: 4 versions of schedule '01a0b366-61fa-7f50-8cc4-25fa070287cc' are in
> force for 'sewer' on 2026-10-29 (01a0b366-6200-75a1-b0ca-a47e7ba7f490,
> 01a0b388-86ba-726e-91c9-1ad57e082b3b, 01a0b424-e5ce-7b18-81b9-b696cbbfc1ff,
> 01a0e712-0c79-7c63-988e-e54d1173aa8e). Exactly one prices a service; there is
> no best match and this chain never picks.

B14 rule 31 — PO, verbatim: *"no Databse ID on screen - that is a rule"*.

**WHY EVERY EXISTING PROTECTION PASSED OVER IT, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH
KEEPING.** `BR-SHL-020 r2` (PO 2026-08-19, *"server detail text should not
reach customer screens"*) is enforced by `refusalParams` in
`07-frontend/src/api/client.ts:204`, which does `delete rest.detail`. That
strips `detail` from an **ApiError's params**. This `detail` is a field in a
**200-response body**, so the stripper is not anywhere near it and never was:
**the guard existed, was correct, and could not see the shape.** `G28` reads
source with `ast` and the id is an f-string's RUNTIME value — its own docstring
already conceded it (*"a uuid-shaped VALUE in a field is the one thing G28
cannot see"*) — and, worse, its part-3 baseline PARKS eleven `resolution.py`
sites on the measured argument that *"this prose reaches the audit row and the
server log and stops there"*. **That argument was true of an ApiError and false
of this path**, so a truthful baseline covered a live leak. `G69` reads
frontend source for a sliced or joined id; nothing here is sliced.

**THE JUDGMENT, AND IT IS NOT "REMOVE THE SENTENCE".** `DEF-CUS-6464` put the
sentence on screen on purpose, because a bare reason code breaks rule 32, and
`one_time.py`'s own docstring calls `detail` *"the ACTIONABLE half"*. **The
decision to show a sentence was right; nobody had asked what the sentence
contained.** So the sentence stays and its AUTHOR changes: nine raise sites now
state a `message_key`, its facts and an id-free English mirror beside the
engineer's text, which keeps its ids for the log, the audit row and the shadow
report. The vehicle is `DEF-BIL-5339`'s `GapNotes` key, reused rather than a
second one invented.

**THE WORKED FIGURE, WHICH IS WHAT WAS PUT TO THE REVIEWER:** the sentence
above now reads **"4 schedules price Sewer on 29 Oct 2026. Ask an administrator
to retire one."** — two sentences, six words each (B14 rule 33), in eleven
languages, with `sewer` resolved to the clerk's own word on the client so no
catalogue value carries a dotted identifier (rule 32).

**TWO THINGS DECIDED HERE BECAUSE THE RULES RAN OUT, BOTH RECORDED RATHER THAN
ASKED (law 13).** (1) **The date is written English-style inside a translated
sentence** — `29 Oct 2026` in all eleven — because the server holds no locale
and `Intl` lives in the browser; the alternative was an ISO key on screen,
which is worse for a clerk. It is named in the review-ledger row as the
reviewer's to overturn. (2) **No parameter is called `count`**: i18next reads
`count` as the plural selector and looks for `<key>_one`/`<key>_other` first, so
the keys interpolate `{{plans}}` and `{{schedules}}` instead — `DEF-323`'s shape
avoided before it could happen.

**THE GUARD, AND WHAT IT ADMITS.** `G139` **runs the chain** — `resolution.py`
is pure dataclasses, so each of the nine refusals can be raised in-process with
real uuids in the catalogue — and reads the CLERK payload rather than the
source. It was proved RED through `run()`, not `__main__` (`DEF-GOV-3733`):
`10-scripts/tests/g139_red_proof.py` reverts the fix in memory and the gate
reports `FAIL: 18 clerk-facing refusal problem(s)`, nine naming a uuid. **It
prints what it skips on every run — 28 of 37 raise sites and 4 render sites —
because `G32` once reported `0 unresolved` truthfully over 21 live refusals,
and a blind spot with no number beside it is indistinguishable from an empty
one.** It also fails if a tenth site starts stating a `message_key` without a
case being added, so the list cannot go stale in silence.

**TWO ID COLLISIONS INSIDE ONE LANE, BOTH CAUGHT, BOTH LAW 11.** `allocate.py
gate` answered `137` and a sibling lane on this same branch had already
registered `G137 declared-constraints-are-built`; `run_gates._assert_registry_
sane()` refused the duplicate NUMBER by name and the later gate renumbered to
`G139`. `file_defect.py` then re-derived `DEF-RAT-7980` — which this lane had
already written into seven files — to `DEF-RAT-7991`, because it asks the
REMOTE and the sibling's row was there. **Both were caught by a tool that reads
further than this checkout, and neither would have been caught by arithmetic.**

## 2026-09-29 — `DEF-RAT-8000` · THE NO-OVERLAP CONSTRAINT B2 §2 SIGNED AND NOBODY BUILT, AND THE THREE WAYS IT COULD NOT BE BUILT LITERALLY

**WHAT WAS WRONG.** `06-backend/db/000_extensions.sql` never installed
`btree_gist`, so migration `rating/0001` could not create B2 §2's
`EXCLUDE USING gist` no-overlap constraint on `tariff_versions` and created
nothing. `rating/0004`'s header reported that in 2026-08-19 and left it *"for
the human review of this row"*. **That review never happened, and nothing
counted it** — the review-ledger row it pointed at carried no such item. Six
weeks later `services._apply_batch_to_schedule` carried a comment saying *"two
open-ended windows would collide with the B2 EXCLUDE constraint on Postgres"*,
which is hard-won law 1 exactly: a comment claiming a guarantee that did not
exist, inside the function that depended on it. Ottumwa Water Works reached
**four versions of one sewer schedule in force on 2026-10-29**, and its
one-time bills and move-out final bills refuse with `AmbiguousSchedule`.

**THE JUDGMENT THAT NEEDED RECORDING, AND WHY IT IS OURS AND NOT THE PO's
(hard-won law 13).** B2 §2's literal expression **cannot be built** — it would
break shipped, PO-ruled behaviour on the day it landed. Three deviations, each
traceable to a rule ratified AFTER B2 was written, and each measured:

| B2 §2 says | What is built | Why, and what the literal version costs |
|---|---|---|
| `effective_from date NOT NULL`, no predicate | `WHERE effective_from IS NOT NULL` | `rating/0004` made the column NULLABLE because **a NULL `effective_from` IS the draft** (BR-RAT-031), and recorded that as a modification of B2. `daterange(NULL, …)` is unbounded BELOW. **Cost of the literal version: one saved draft overlaps every dated version of its schedule, so no tenant holding a draft can be migrated at all.** `uq_tariff_versions_one_draft` is already partial for this identical reason. |
| no `superseded_by` predicate | `AND superseded_by_version_id IS NULL` | A CORRECTION **restates the SAME window** — PO, 2026-09-17, *"it is not a new rate or it is not a change in rate - it is just an error handling"* (BR-RAT-104 / BR-RAT-1016 verb 2). A corrected schedule ALWAYS holds two rows with identical windows, deliberately. **Cost of the literal version: every correction on all five priced objects is refused by the database.** |
| `daterange(effective_from, coalesce(effective_to,'infinity'))` | `daterange(effective_from, COALESCE(effective_to + 1, 'infinity'))` | `effective_to` is **INCLUSIVE** everywhere here — `selectors.in_force_version` asks `effective_to >= service_date`, every writer closes with `next_from - 1 day` — and `daterange` is half-open. **Worked figure: a version ending `2026-03-31` and a version starting `2026-03-31` do NOT overlap by B2's expression, and BOTH are returned by `in_force_version` on `2026-03-31`.** One day of coin toss on a money path, per rate change, for ever. Proved on PostgreSQL 16: the built constraint refuses that pair, and the literal one does not. |

**It is not a re-sign question.** B2 is signed law, not a ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5
figure, and the three later rules are themselves PO-ruled and LATER. The
literal text and the later rulings cannot both be honoured; the predicate is
the only shape in which both are true, and B2's own stated intent — its inline
comment, *"no overlapping in-force windows per tariff"* — is what is built.
Recorded here rather than asked, per hard-won law 13.

**AND THE CONSTRAINT IS `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`, WHICH IS NOT A
PREFERENCE.** `services.correct_rate_schedule_version` writes the correction
row FIRST and stamps `superseded_by` on the original SECOND, inside one
`transaction.atomic()`. Between those two statements there are two live rows on
one window, so an IMMEDIATE constraint refuses the INSERT **even with predicate
2 in place**. Proved both ways on PostgreSQL 16.

**WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND WHAT WAS NOT.** On a throwaway clone of the demo
database (`sbh_ratovl_a`, PostgreSQL 16.13) the repair migration closed **2** of
3 open windows on a planted succession, left the newest open, left the planted
correction untouched, and **REFUSED the planted same-date tie by name**, rolling
the whole migration back — which is the intended outcome, not a failure.
⚠ **The demo database itself holds 4 `tariff_versions` rows in 1 tenant and
ZERO overlaps**, so the repair is proved to RUN and is proved to FIND a planted
overlap (`10-scripts/rat_schedule_overlap_census.py --plant-proof`), and it is
proved about production by **nothing at all**. The same command must be run
against the real database before anyone believes there was nothing to repair.

### THE PLAN-SIDE HALF OF THE PLAN WAS NOT BUILT, AND THIS IS WHY

The approved plan's step A5 read *"the same constraint on plan versions —
`resolve_plan` has the identical defect and refuses identically."* **It was
checked before it was built, and the premise does not hold.** Three facts, each
read out of the code rather than assumed:

1. **`resolve_plan`'s `AmbiguousSchedule` branch is unreachable from the live
   catalogue.** `resolution_catalogue.plan_version_facts` builds its candidates
   from `RatePlan.objects.filter(pk=plan_id, status="published").first()` and
   returns **a tuple of at most ONE**. `Catalogue(plan_versions=…)` is
   constructed in exactly one place in the whole backend — measured with
   `grep -rn "plan_versions=" 06-backend/` — and that is the place. `len(in_force) > 1`
   therefore cannot be true in production today.
2. **There is no dated plan-version table to put a constraint on.** The dates
   live on `rate_plans` itself, one row per plan, so an `EXCLUDE` grouped by
   tenant and plan id is grouped by the primary key and guarantees nothing.
3. **The table called `plan_versions` has no `effective_from`, deliberately,
   and adding one would answer an OPEN question by building it.** `OQ-324`
   reads **OPEN** in its status column and its body says so in as many words:
   *"adding one would make the dated reading storable before it is ruled"*.
   The prime directive forbids a lane resolving that by choosing a value.

**So nothing was built on the plan side, and B2 §2 signs nothing there either
— its only `EXCLUDE USING gist` is on `tariff_versions`.** This is recorded
rather than silently skipped, because *"the same constraint on plan versions"*
reads like an outstanding task to whoever picks this up next, and it is not
one until `OQ-324` is answered.

## 2026-09-29 — `DEF-RAT-8004` · THE LIVE RUN PICKS AND THE ONE-TIME BILL REFUSES. **FOR THE PO.**

⚠ **THIS IS NOT DECIDED. IT IS WRITTEN DOWN WITH ITS FIGURE AND LEFT FOR THE
PRODUCT OWNER**, because it is a money-path judgment and hard-won law 13's
short list puts it there: it is a ruling that collides with a signed rule.

**THE TWO ANSWERS, TODAY.** When more than one rate-schedule version is in
force on one service date, the product does two different things depending on
which door the clerk came through:

* **The nightly bill run** (`selectors.in_force_version`) **SILENTLY PICKS** —
  `.order_by("-effective_from").first()`. The newest wins, nothing is said, the
  bill prints, and the customer is charged.
* **The one-time bill and the move-out final bill** (`resolution.resolve_
  schedule`, R2) **REFUSE** with `AmbiguousSchedule` and name the count.

**THE WORKED FIGURE.** Ottumwa Water Works, sewer schedule, 2026-10-29: four
versions in force. Say the two live candidates are `$18.40` and `$21.60` a
month on a 5/8" residential connection. **A household billed by the nightly run
is charged `$21.60` and told nothing. The identical household closing their
account the same morning gets no bill at all** and a clerk sees a refusal
naming four version ids. One configuration, one date, two products.

**WHY NEITHER BEHAVIOUR WAS CHANGED HERE.** Both are defensible and the choice
is the PO's:
* **Refuse everywhere** stops a wrong bill before it reaches a customer, and
  stops the nightly run for every account on that schedule — at a utility of
  40,000 accounts that is a billing cycle missed while somebody is found.
* **Pick everywhere** keeps the cycle running and puts a price on a bill on the
  strength of an order-by, which is what `in_force_version`'s own comment calls
  *"not a tie-break … a coin toss on a money path"*.
* **Leave it split**, which is today, and is the only option nobody chose.

⚠ **`DEF-RAT-8000`'s constraint makes the question rarer, and does not answer
it.** From `rating/0047` onwards the database refuses a second in-force window
at COMMIT, so no NEW overlap can be created. Every overlap that exists today
was created before the constraint, and the same-date ties `rating/0046` refuses
to touch are still there waiting for a person.

**WHAT IS ASKED OF THE PO, in one sentence:** *when two rate schedules are in
force on the same day and neither has been marked as a correction, should the
bill run stop for that whole schedule, or should it bill on the newest one?*

## 2026-09-29 — `DEF-RAT-7980` IS THE CANONICAL ROW AND `DEF-RAT-8000` IS THIS LANE'S DUPLICATE OF IT

**TWO LANES FOUND THE MISSING NO-OVERLAP CONSTRAINT INDEPENDENTLY, HOURS
APART, THE SAME DAY — AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** The **wave-F gate
lane** found it by READING B2 §2's signed DDL against a migrated PostgreSQL
16.13 and asking which declarations the database actually has; it filed
`DEF-RAT-7980` and built `G137` — *"every constraint B2 signs is sorted into
MATCHED, DIVERGED or NOT BUILT, and there is deliberately no baseline for NOT
BUILT: it is the `tariff_versions` incident, and a file that could excuse it
would be the review that never happened, in another costume."* This lane
(`RAT-NO-OVERLAP`) came the other way, from a live tenant's refused bills, and
filed `DEF-RAT-8000` before seeing theirs.

**Two rows for one fault is the harm `file_defect.py` exists to prevent, and
the earlier id belongs to whoever pushed first** — the precedent is
`DEF-CUS-7910` / `DEF-CUS-7920`, ten days ago, same register, same reasoning.
So `DEF-RAT-7980` is **fixed** by `ed2fc3a70` and `DEF-RAT-8000` is **closed as
a duplicate of it**.

⚠ **THE CITATIONS IN THE CODE STILL READ `DEF-RAT-8000`, DELIBERATELY, AND
THIS IS WHY.** `rating/0045`, `0046` and `0047` carry that id in their
FILENAMES, and those three migrations are recorded in `django_migrations` on
every database they have been applied to. **Renaming an applied migration
makes it apply again** — which here would re-run a data repair and re-add a
constraint — so the cost of tidying the id is a broken deploy, and the cost of
leaving it is one hop through a register row that names its canonical id in
its own `fixed_commit` field. The row is the index; the filename is just a
name.

**AND THE TWO LANES DID DIFFERENT HALVES, WHICH IS WHY NEITHER IS WASTED.**
`G137` is the check that this class of gap cannot happen again — it reads
every constraint B2 signs and fails on one nothing builds. `rating/0045`–
`0047` are the constraint itself. **Measured, not assumed: `G137` was RED at
`0423d1e4` (the commit immediately before this one) —** *"1 of 2 EXCLUDE
constraint(s) signed by B2 are created by no migration and no db/*.sql file —
tariff_versions over (tenant_id, tariff_id, daterange(effective_from,
coalesce(effective_to,'infinity'::date)))"* **— and is GREEN at `ed2fc3a70`.**
So the gate found the fix, on the branch, the way a gate is supposed to.
**Neither lane's work makes the other's redundant: one is the fix and one is
the tripwire, and the gap survived eight weeks because there was neither.**

## 2026-09-29 — `BR-RAT-1044`: A CORRECTED RATE SCHEDULE VERSION RECORDS THE DAY IT STOPPED BEING USED

**THE RULING, IN THE PRODUCT OWNER'S OWN WORDS**, choosing option (a) of three
put to them:

> *"i will take this and use superseded_by in filter - so that it is always
> unique and even if we see in audit it is clear"*

**WHAT WAS WRONG WITH THE OLD BEHAVIOUR, IN PLAIN ENGLISH.** When a clerk fixes
a typo in a live rate — the board approved `$3.20`, somebody typed `$32.00` —
the product writes a second row over the SAME window and marks the first as
superseded (`BR-RAT-104` / `BR-RAT-1016` verb 2; PO 2026-09-17: *"it is not a
new rate or it is not a change in rate - it is just an error handling"*). The
wrong row carried **no end date at all**, so the schedule's own Versions &
filings table showed it as `02/01/2026 →` — this screen's way of writing *still
running* — for ever, on a row that had not priced a single bill since the day it
was corrected.

**THE RULE.** When `correct_rate_schedule_version` supersedes a version:

```
old.effective_to   = max(the correction date, old.effective_from)
old.superseded_by  = the new version
new.effective_from = the original's effective_from   (unchanged — this is what
                                                      makes it a correction)
new.effective_to   = open
```

**THE TWO WORKED CASES SHOWN, BOTH TESTED**
(`06-backend/tests/test_br_rat_1044_correction_closes_the_window.py`):

| Case | Version's window | Corrected on | Old row's `effective_to` | Reads as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Corrected **after** it started pricing | from 2026-02-01 | 2026-03-01 | **2026-03-01** | in use a month, then replaced |
| Corrected **before** it started (activated, FUTURE-dated) | from 2026-02-01 | 2026-01-15 | **2026-02-01** (the `max`) | replaced the day it would have started |

⚠ **THE `max` IS THE WHOLE EDGE CASE AND IT IS NOT "CORRECTED BEFORE
ACTIVATION".** A DRAFT has no dates and is edited in place — the service
refuses a correction of one by name (`rating.schedules.correct_draft`), no
version exists and there is nothing to supersede. The edge case is the OTHER
thing: a version **activated with a future date** and corrected before that date
arrives. Without the `max` its end lands 17 days before its start, which
`services.py` already refuses by name as `window_inverted`, and the correction
fails outright — so the naive rule does not merely produce an odd row, it takes
the clerk's only way of fixing a typo away. Proved: the second case was RED
against `caab7e774` with `assert None == datetime.date(2026, 2, 1)`.

**WHY IT IS SAFE, AND ALL THREE LEGS WERE PROVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The
corrected row carries `superseded_by`, and that is what excludes it from
pricing — not its window:
  1. `selectors.in_force_version` has filtered `superseded_by__isnull=True`
     since `DEF-RAT-5715` (the live bill run);
  2. `resolution_catalogue.schedule_version_facts` gained the same filter today
     under `DEF-RAT-8002` (the one-time and move-out final bills);
  3. `rating/0047`'s `ex_tariff_versions_no_overlap` carries the predicate
     `WHERE effective_from IS NOT NULL AND superseded_by_version_id IS NULL`,
     so the pair's overlapping windows do not violate it.
Each has a test: one per reader on SQLite, the constraint on real PostgreSQL 16
(`tests/test_br_rat_1044_correction_window_pg.py`, with
`SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE` where the answer is due — under `django_db` a
DEFERRED constraint is otherwise never checked and every case passes vacuously,
which is the trap the sibling `test_def_rat_8000_no_overlap_pg.py` fell into on
its first draft).

**HARD RULE 4 — NO ISSUED BILL'S BASIS MOVES, CHECKED THE ONLY WAY THAT SETTLES
IT.** The comparison is not *before the correction* against *after* — the
answering row moving from the original to the correction IS the correction
working. It is **this change against the old behaviour**: take the correction,
ask both readers for every day across the window and past the new end, then put
the corrected row's `effective_to` back to NULL and ask again. The two sets of
answers are identical, because both readers drop a superseded row before they
look at a window at all.

### THE JUDGMENT THE PO WAS NOT ASKED FOR, AND WHY WE TOOK IT

⚠ **A STATED END DATE IS NEVER MOVED. THIS CLAUSE IS OURS.** The ruling was put
and answered for the ordinary case: the CURRENT version, whose window is open. A
version that a later rate change already CLOSED stopped being used on the day
its successor started, not on the day somebody noticed the figure was wrong —
so writing the correction date over it would make the register say the row ran
a month longer than it did, which is the opposite of what the ruling is for.
**Worked:** a version running 2026-02-01 → 2026-03-31, superseded by a rate
change on 2026-04-01 and corrected on 2026-06-01, keeps **2026-03-31**; the
naive rule would write **2026-06-01** and claim it priced two months it never
priced. It is also `rating/0046`'s own rule for the same column, one writer
along: *"ONLY A NULL END IS FILLED. AN END DATE THAT ALREADY EXISTS IS NEVER
MOVED — somebody typed it, it is what a bill was reproduced against."* Law 13:
a judgment recorded with its reasoning is the deliverable; a re-ask is the
failure to make one.

**THE CORRECTION DATE IS THE UTILITY'S OWN DAY** — `seams.tenant_today()`,
which is `BR-TEN-081`'s clock read event-time under `BR-TEN-043`. A server-side
`date.today()` would put a Houston correction made at 19:00 on the 8th onto the
9th.

### FORWARD-ONLY, AND THE NUMBER THE NEXT RULING NEEDS

**Nothing is backfilled.** Rows corrected before today keep their open end.
Whether they should be given one is a SECOND ruling the PO has not taken, and it
needs a figure first: `10-scripts/rat_schedule_overlap_census.py
--corrected-open` counts corrected rows carrying a NULL `effective_to`, per
tenant. **Measured on every database reachable from this container — 8 of them,
41 `tariff_versions` rows in total, 0 superseded rows anywhere: the answer is
0 found, and this container has no production data.** The command has to be run
against the real estate before that ruling is worth putting.

### THE FOURTH READER, SETTLED IN PASSING

`selectors.latest_version` has NO `superseded_by` filter where its two siblings
do, and twelve call sites take its answer — `previous` for a rate change, the
base charge code carried forward, the window that gets closed. **It cannot
return a superseded row, and the reason is the ORDERING rather than the name:** a
correction copies the original's `effective_from`, so the pair always ties on
the first sort key and is always separated by the second, `-created_at`, which
is `auto_now_add` and therefore strictly later on the row written second.
Worked through for the three shapes that could break it — correcting the newest
version, correcting a correction (a chain), correcting a version that is not the
newest — and pinned by tests rather than left in this paragraph. **A blanket
filter was considered and NOT applied:** ten of the twelve call sites want the
newest LIVE row and would be unchanged, but **two ask a different question** —
`update_rate_schedule`'s `latest_version(tariff) is not None` guards ask *has
this schedule ever gone live*, which is a property of the SCHEDULE, and a
corrected row is a perfectly good answer to it. What is NOT guaranteed, stated
rather than left to be found: two rows written inside one microsecond would tie
on both keys and the answer would be whichever the database returned first.
Nothing in this repo can produce that.

## 2026-09-29 · `DEF-RAT-8050` — the discount version overlap, and the three judgments it needed (v2.410.14)

**LANE `RAT-DISC-OVERLAP`, branch `claude/brave-dijkstra-xgfsgz`.** The class of
fault `DEF-RAT-8000` found on `tariff_versions` — a signed no-overlap guarantee
that nothing built, plus writers that closed one predecessor window and readers
that settled a tie by `.first()` — asked of `discount_versions`. **Three
judgments were made here rather than put to the PO** (hard-won law 13: what
legitimately reaches them is a collision with a signed rule, a ❄️ FROZEN figure,
or a fact only they hold). Each is written out with its worked number.

### 1 · WHICH STATUSES THE CONSTRAINT BINDS — `active`, AND ONLY `active`

`discount_versions` has six statuses and **no `superseded_by` semantics of the
kind `tariff_versions` has**: `discounts.py` says *"`superseded` is what a
later version does to an earlier one"*, so supersession is a STATUS. The
constraint therefore keys off `status = 'active'` and **not** off
`superseded_by_version_id IS NULL`, because naming both would be a second
representation of one fact — which is precisely how the two readers of this
table came apart.

**`scheduled` looks like it belongs inside the predicate and does not**, and
the reason is measured rather than argued from the name.
`activate_discount_version` supersedes by STATUS and has never written an end
date, so a live discount's `effective_to` is NULL — an OPEN window — until its
successor is activated. **Put `scheduled` inside the constraint and approving
any successor to any live discount is refused**, because that open window
contains every future date. Same for `pending_approval`: a proposal is not a
price. The establishing facts are that the three readers which feed money or a
money screen — `discount_services.active_version`, `resolution_catalogue
._discount_facts` and `discount_enrolments_read` — all filter `active` and
there is no fourth.

### 2 · CLOSING EVERY OLDER WINDOW MOVES NO BILL, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS SAFE

`_close_open_windows_before` closes **every** older open window at activation,
not the most recent one. On rate schedules that act can move which version a
past date resolves to (hard rule 4). **On discounts it cannot**, and the reason
is specific: the rows it closes are the same rows `activate_discount_version`
flips to `superseded` one statement later, and a `superseded` row is already
excluded by every reader. The close makes the DATA say what the STATUS says; it
changes no answer. Measured rather than asserted — `rat_schedule_overlap_census
.py --discounts --reprice-check` found **0 grants on an issued invoice** on
every database available here, which checks nothing and says so in those words.

### 3 · THE WORKED FIGURE PUT IN THE REVIEW-LEDGER ROW

A senior discount whose version 1 says **15%** and whose version 2 says
**1.5%**, both live from 1 January, on a **`$196.37`** bill: one row takes off
**`$29.46`** and the other **`$2.95`** — **`$26.51` a month per household**,
chosen by whichever row sorted first. That is the cost of the coin toss, and it
is the sentence the PO is being asked to rule on.

### WHAT WAS MEASURED, WITH THE NUMBERS

PostgreSQL 16.13, a clone of a 449-migration database (`sbh_clone_d8041`):
* `discount_versions` carried **0** exclusion constraints; `discounts` and
  `discount_versions` held **6 and 6** rows, **one version per discount**, so
  **0 overlapping groups**. A zero on that estate says nothing about
  production and the census footer says so.
* the demo database `smartbillhub` holds **0 discounts and 0 discount_versions**.
* **8 write paths** touch a discount version (`create_discount`,
  `create_discount_version`, `update_discount_version`,
  `correct_discount_version`, `submit`, `approve`, `activate`, `discard`) and
  **0 of them closed a predecessor's window** before this commit —
  `effective_to` was written only on the row being created, never on a
  predecessor, anywhere in `discount_services.py`.
* `rating/0048` on a clone: `examined 6 dated version(s); filled 0 open
  window(s); left 1 non-active row(s) alone; 0 overlap(s) need a person`.
* `G137`: **2 signed constraints NOT BUILT** on a clone at `rating/0044`;
  **33 of 35 declarations compared, 33 built** with `rating/0045`–`0049`
  applied. It compared **32 of 34** before this commit.

### WHAT WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED

**`DEF-RAT-8051` — the taxes sibling, and it is NOT the same fault.** `taxes`
carries `effective_from`/`effective_to` and `superseded_by_tax_id`, and the
correction case IS handled (`tax_in_force` refuses a superseded row). But
**`selectors._authority_tax` chooses between two rows of one `(tenant,
jurisdiction, kind)` by `created_at` and never consults the date at all** —
`rows.filter(superseded_by__isnull=True).order_by("created_at").first()` — and
only then does `tax_in_force` apply the window. So a rate change filed the way
the model's own comment says to file it (*"r6.5; new row per change"*) yields
**no tax line**, not the new rate, because the oldest row wins the choice and
then fails the window. **A no-overlap constraint would not make that read
correct**, which is why it is a separate row and not part of this one.
Measured: `taxes` holds **2 rows, 0 of them dated, 0 overlapping pairs, 0
exclusion constraints** — the missing predicate is the identity on all existing
data, which is exactly what `DEF-483` recorded about the sibling half of the
same function.

**`DEF-RAT-8052` — `G137` could not read an `ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT`.**
B2 addendum r26 signs the discount constraint in that form on purpose
(restating forty ORM-owned columns would create a second source of truth for
all of them), and the gate parsed only `CREATE TABLE` and `CREATE [UNIQUE]
INDEX`. It would have read the addendum as saying nothing and gone on
reporting a clean verdict — law 7's fifth shape, in the gate written to stop
exactly that. Fixed in the same commit, with the synthetic `ALTER` in
`_selftest()` so it is re-proved on every invocation.

### A PROCESS TRAP WORTH MORE THAN THE DEFECT — RESERVE **AFTER** YOU FILE

`allocate.py defect` answered `8041`; this lane wrote a reservation block for
`DEF-RAT-8041–8049` and only then called `file_defect.py`, which **reads
`14-id-reservations.md`, steps over an active block, and takes `max + 1`
rather than the first free id** — so it allocated `8050` and `8041` became
permanently unreachable. Eight files and two migration filenames citing `8041`
had already been pushed; they were renumbered to `8050` in one pass rather
than left naming a number no register row will ever carry (`DEF-2804`'s
shape). **A reservation is a fence against OTHER lanes and the allocator
cannot tell you from them.** Recorded in `14-id-reservations.md` beside the

**2026-09-29 — THE TWO CRITICAL NEW CONNECT DEFECTS, THEIR CAUSE AND THEIR AGREED FIX.
`DEF-CUS-8020` · `DEF-CUS-8021`. WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE FIX, ON THE PO's INSTRUCTION:
*"also write in repo - if we have to change the chat we should able to start it another
chat"*.**

⚠ **THIS ROW EXISTS SO THE NEXT AGENT NEEDS ONLY THE REPO.** Hard-won law 10's test is
not *"was a decision made"* but *"would the next agent, with only the repo, build the
same thing?"* Everything below was established in a working session and would otherwise
have evaporated with it.

## `DEF-CUS-8020` — New Connect's **Create** has never worked

**Symptom.** A clerk fills all five steps and presses Create. The server answers **422**
and the clerk reads *"This app sent a field an account doesn't have. Nothing was saved."*
Every press, every clerk, every build. **Nothing has ever been created by this wizard.**

**Cause, verified three ways rather than inferred:**

| Fact | Where |
|---|---|
| `commitPlanOf` always sends four billing preferences on the owner block — `autopay`, `tax_exempt`, `tax_exempt_ref`, `tax_exempt_expires` | front end |
| `create_owner_account` passes them through, under a comment citing `customers.CREATE_FIELDS` | `customers/services.py` |
| That door builds a **MASTER** account, whose allow list is `MASTER_CREATE_FIELDS` | `customers/services.py:3463` → `_reject_unknown(data, MASTER_CREATE_FIELDS)` |
| `MASTER_CREATE_FIELDS` holds **nine** fields and **none of the four** — `premises_id · unit_ids · account_type · account_subtype · opened_at · contact · addresses · custom_data · customer` | `customers/services.py:1046` |
| The four columns **exist on the model** | `customers/models.py:608-611` |
| `CREATE_FIELDS`, the ORDINARY-account door, **permits all four** | `customers/services.py:801-804` |

**So this is not a missing capability. One door's allow list was written without them, and
New Connect builds a master account.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Fix** | Add the four to `MASTER_CREATE_FIELDS` |
| **Size** | Four lines |
| **Risk** | Low — the columns exist and the sibling door already writes them |
| **Test** | Press Create and assert an account row exists — **the test nobody had** |

⚠ **MUST BE CHECKED BEFORE WIDENING, AND THE ANSWER IS NOT OBVIOUS.** Is the omission
deliberate? A master account is the owner's account at an address (ruling 2026-08-31).
**If autopay or a tax exemption on a master account is meant to be REFUSED, then the
WIZARD should stop asking and the server should keep refusing — the opposite fix.**
`CR-056 W3 task 17` and the comment inside `MASTER_CREATE_FIELDS` itself (which explains
why `customer` was added to that set) are the places to settle it. **Do not widen the
list merely because widening makes the error go away.**

## `DEF-CUS-8021` — pressing Create twice creates two of everything

**Measured**: `CON-26-0130` and `CON-26-0131` from one identical payload — two accounts,
two customers, two properties at one address, and **two payments of $250.00, each posting
its own balanced ledger pair.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Fix** | A real idempotency key on `POST /connections/commit` — hard rule 6 |
| **Today** | With a parcel number, a *uniqueness constraint* refuses the second press. **With the box empty, nothing does** |
| **Why that is not idempotency** | It refuses by accident of a different rule, and returns 409 rather than the first result |
| **Right shape** | Same key → return the **first** connection; do not create a second and do not error |
| **Test** | Post the identical payload twice **with no parcel number**; assert one connection, one account, one payment |

⚠ **THE FIRST PASS OF THIS CHECK PASSED, FOR THE WRONG REASON** — the parcel box was
filled, so the uniqueness constraint refused and the check read as green. **That is how it
stayed hidden, and it is why the test must run with the box EMPTY.**

## They must land together

Fixing `8020` alone turns a button that does nothing into a button that **bills twice**,
with two balanced ledger entries that both look correct. **Neither ships without the
other.**

## The escape reason, which is the durable part

**Every earlier walk filled the five steps and stopped.** `nc5_five_step_photographs.mjs`
says so in its own last line. The screens photograph perfectly; nobody had pressed the
button. Five months of work, 95+ green tests, `tsc`, eslint and the gate suite all passed
over a wizard that could not create anything. **The process fix is that a wizard is not
verified until its commit is pressed and the rows are read back out of the database.**

## 2026-09-29 · `DEF-RAT-8051` — a filed tax rate change wrote NO tax line, and the two judgments the fix needed (`v2.410.15`)

**WHAT WAS WRONG, IN ONE SENTENCE.** `rating/selectors.py`'s `_authority_tax`
took no date: it picked the OLDEST non-superseded row for a
`(tenant, jurisdiction, kind)` by `created_at` and handed it back, and only
afterwards did the caller ask `tax_in_force(tax, service_date)`. So a rate
change filed the way the model's own comment instructs — *"r6.5; new row per
change"* — produced **no tax line at all**: the old row won the pick, failed
the gate, and the newer row was never considered.

**THE WORKED FIGURE THE PO ACCEPTED.** A state utility tax goes 6.25% → 7.00%
on 2027-01-01. Row A (Jan 2024, 6.25%, ends 2026-12-31), row B (Dec 2026,
7.00%, from 2027-01-01). A January 2027 bill of **$196.00** carried **$0.00**
of tax where it should carry **$13.72** — on a bill that looks completely
normal. After the fix it carries $13.72, and a December 2026 bill of the same
size carries **$12.25**, which is the old rate on the old month.

**THE FIX.** The date goes into the CHOICE as a new FIRST branch — the row
whose window contains the service date wins — and **the whole existing chain
is untouched beneath it**. That preserves the three things the function's own
docstring says are deliberate: `BR-BIL-069` still resolves a row when none is
in force, so a bill names the right authority and then writes no line;
`DEF-384`'s final unfiltered fallback still catches an authority all of whose
rows are superseded; and whether a DEACTIVATED tax should price a bill stays
**declined**, exactly as declined as it was. Each has a test.

**JUDGMENT 1 — TWO ROWS IN FORCE REFUSE RATHER THAN PICK, AND THE REFUSAL IS
NOT A `ResolutionError`.** `taxes` carries no uniqueness or exclusion
constraint on `(tenant, jurisdiction, kind)`, so the shape is possible and
nothing upstream prevents it. Picking is `in_force_version`'s *"not a
tie-break, a coin toss on a money path"*, and `AmbiguousDiscountVersion`
(`DEF-RAT-8050`, the same day) is the shape one object over — so
`AmbiguousAuthorityTax` is deliberately its twin rather than a third
invention. **It is NOT added to the `ResolutionError` hierarchy**, and that is
the judgment: R7 publishes no refusal class *by design* — a tax whose
condition excludes a bill produces no line and never an error (`DEF-273`) —
and `tests/test_cr052_task20_shadow_measure.py` asserts exactly that in one
line (*"R7 not in resolution.refusal_steps().values()"*). Widening the chain's
refusal signature inside a defect fix would move a designed invariant and
change `resolution_shadow`'s step map. `resolution.clerk_refusal()` reads
`message_key` / `clerk_detail` / `message_params` off ANY exception through
`getattr`, so `DEF-RAT-7991`'s clerk mechanism is reused whole without the
hierarchy moving at all.

**JUDGMENT 2 — THE FIX SHIPS AHEAD OF ITS CONTAINMENT, AND THAT IS FILED AS
`DEF-RAT-8060` RATHER THAN LEFT AS A COMMENT.** `gather._taxes_for` calls this
selector through the seam and the run loop catches `PricingRefused`,
`GatherProblem` and `BillingRuleError`; the new refusal is none of the three,
so a tenant holding two overlapping in-force rows would fail the RUN rather
than the ACCOUNT. **It is unreachable on any data that exists:** measured
2026-09-29 on PostgreSQL 16 (`smartbillhub` and `sbh_clone_d8041g`), `taxes`
holds **2 rows, 0 dated, 0 `(tenant, jurisdiction, kind)` groups with more
than one row**. The alternative — a new `GATHER_` reason, its two run maps and
a `billing.run.reason.<code>` key in eleven catalogues — is a billing change
this lane has not measured, and `gather.py:2028` already holds the pattern for
whoever takes it. Weighed against holding the money fix back: the defect being
fixed loses $13.72 a month on a correctly-configured utility, and the refusal
cannot fire on one.

**WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, AND WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE TESTS.** Every tax row in
this product is UNDATED, so every row is in force on every date, the window
gate never bites, and the old query and the fixed one return the same row on
all existing data — which is what makes the fix safe under hard rule 4 (no
issued bill re-prices) and what makes any test that does not CREATE dated rows
worthless. `tests/test_def_rat_8051_tax_rate_change.py` writes its own dated
rows in every case and says so in its docstring; `test_tc6` asserts the seeded
rows are still undated, so the argument goes red rather than quietly expiring.

**WHAT IS NOT COVERED, WITH ITS NUMBER.** `G139` re-raises the **nine**
refusals of `resolution.py` and ties each to `en.json`; this refusal is raised
from `selectors.py`, so the gate's count does not move and its tie never
reaches the new key — `test_tc2b` is that tie, and it is a pytest rather than
a gate. And **1 of the 1,295 backend test files was run**.

**FOUND IN PASSING AND FILED, NOT FIXED — `DEF-RAT-8061`.**
`services._detach_tax` loops over `("percent", "flat")` at two places, and
`"flat"` is not a tax kind: `services.TAX_KINDS` is
`("percent", "flat_per_bill", "per_unit", "per_meter")`. So a jurisdiction
whose only tax is a flat-per-bill fee counts as bringing nothing to
`BR-RAT-115`'s *at least one tax must be left standing* floor. The string
reads correct because the model's own docstring still carries r6.5's older
vocabulary.

## 2026-09-30 · `DEF-BIL-8283` — every bill names its customer, both addresses and its sender, and the four judgments the fix needed (`v2.411.6`)

**What was wrong.** The PO's one-time fee bill BL-2609-000081 (AC-2026-00058,
Ottumwa Water Works) printed no customer name, no service address, no mailing
address, and *"This bill did not record it"* under *Who sent it*. The one-time
kinds build their bill with an EMPTY gather snapshot (`fee_bill._fee_usage`,
`snapshot={}`), and nothing at draft asked customers who the bill was for. A
cycle bill carried the name and the service address from gather and the
mailing address on NONE — `documents._meta` had no mailing row at all.

**What is built.** Stage 6 (`stages/assemble_document.py`, the one path every
bill kind shares) stamps `customer_name`, `service_address`, `unit_label`,
`mailing_address`, `mailing_address_source` and the utility's three masthead
keys into `bill_payload`, frozen with the rest of the snapshot (BR-BIL-030).
Read through the owning modules only: `customers.selectors.
bill_addressee_for_account` (new) behind `billing.customers_seam.
bill_addressee`, and `tenancy.selectors.bill_masthead`.

**Judgments taken here (ours, per hard-won law 13; none moves money):**

1. **Gather's values win; stage 6 fills only what nobody stamped.** A cycle
   bill's name and service address are captured at gather from the same
   sources, and that is what the clerk reviewed — so an existing cycle bill's
   snapshot does not change shape. Worked: Sarah Chen's cycle bill keeps
   *"1901 Bluestem Ln, Katy, TX 77494"* from gather and gains *"18 Wapello St,
   Suite 2, Ottumwa, IA 52501"* as its mailing address.
2. **The service address is printed WITHOUT the unit; the mailing fallback
   WITH it.** The document already prints the unit on its own *Unit* line under
   the service address, and gather has always stamped the street that way. An
   envelope has no Unit line, so where the account has no mailing row the
   mailing address is the service address with the unit in it — *"1901
   Bluestem Ln, Unit A, Katy, TX 77494"* — the same answer the delivery queue
   already gives (B2 §2: no mailing row means *same as service*).
3. **The customer's name is the primary contact's, else the linked customer's
   display name.** The contact is what every billing screen already calls the
   account's name (`primary_contact_name`); an account opened with a customer
   record and no contact would otherwise print a dash. For a master account the
   bill's account IS the master, so its holder — the payer — is named.
4. **The utility's address falls back: company mailing address → remit-to
   address → the first service centre it SHOWS customers.** Each is an address
   the utility typed for the public; a hidden depot is never printed and
   nothing is composed from fragments. The contact falls back to that centre's
   phone. A utility with none of these still prints the named absence
   (`test_def_2865`'s case is unchanged). Stamped at draft AND re-stamped at
   issue by `issue._stamp_bill_header`, which is the value frozen.

**Already-issued bills are not touched** (hard rule 4; the database refuses
the UPDATE anyway). They keep printing the dash for whatever they lacked. How
many there are could not be counted from this session (no database reachable);
the count is one query per tenant:
`SELECT count(*) FROM invoices WHERE status <> 'draft' AND NOT (bill_payload ? 'mailing_address')`
— every bill issued before `2.411.6` lacks `mailing_address`, and one-time
bills also lack `customer_name`/`service_address`. **Proposed, not done:** a
bill that must go out again with a name and address is re-issued through the
existing correction path (a new document row), never by editing the old one.

## 2026-09-30 · Bulk bill run, the rest (plan B14, B18–B20, B23, A8–A10, F-screens) — nine judgments where the rules ran out (`v2.413.0`)

Lane: bulk-run-rest. Defects: `DEF-BIL-8286` · `8216` · `8217` · `8218` ·
`8220` · `8223` · `8224` · `8243` (one choice) · `8247` · `8248` · `8410`–`8415`.
None of these reverses a signed rule; each is recorded so the next lane builds
the same thing.

1. **The Check's categories run in ONE fixed order — account, services,
   decisions, warnings, payments — and a re-check re-runs the touched category
   plus everything downstream** (`check_engine.REGISTRY`, `DEF-BIL-8286`). A
   category upstream of the touched one runs as INPUT only and its saved
   findings are kept. Worked: a plan fixed on a unit re-checks `services`,
   `decisions`, `warnings` and `payments` for that ONE account; its `account`
   findings (say "no unit") are kept as saved, not re-derived. The staleness
   sweep maps a unit change → `account`, a plan change → `services`, a payment →
   `payments`. **B27/B28 (parallel batches of 500) are not built here**; nothing
   in this shape serialises the pass — each account's categories are
   independent of every other account's.
2. **A Check tag's category is the SCREEN's grouping, not an engine category**,
   so a tag pane's *Re-check N* re-checks its accounts IN FULL. Only a write the
   server itself knows the category of (an inline fix, the staleness sweep)
   re-checks partially. Sending `payments_balances` as a check category would be
   refused (`billing.check.unknownCategory`) — it is not one.
3. **An inline fix writes through the OWNING module by name and never through
   billing** (`check_fixes.FIXES`): plan → `metering.services.assign_unit_plan`,
   size → `assets.services.update_asset` on every asset of that connection,
   city limits → `metering.services.update_premises`. A missing size under the
   ruled path arrives as the generic `ruled_path_refused`, so the refusal now
   carries `{blocked, service_code}` in its params and `fix_for` maps that ONE
   cause to the size fix (`DEF-BIL-8411`); every other ruled-path refusal keeps
   its link.
4. **Every account the run does not bill is queued at Send** (`DEF-BIL-8410`),
   one row each, idempotent, reason prefix `check_` (`check_blocked`,
   `check_waiting_on_a_decision`), origin *prepare*. Left-out accounts carry
   `staff_left_out_by_clerk`. **A held month billed by the next cycle closes its
   own Pending row** (`DEF-BIL-8413`): a later bill whose period covers the held
   period resolves the row, so a catch-up cannot bill the held month twice
   (held on the June run → the next bill from 1 June closes the June row; a
   bill for July alone leaves it open).
5. **Paid after cut-off → *Apply to this bill* is an applied choice, not a
   hold** (`DEF-BIL-8243`, that ONE choice). The payment is counted once, through
   the ledger/payments read at issue: previous $200.00 − $120.00 paid = $80.00
   carried, and the account is billed. The other holding choices named in
   `DEF-BIL-8243` stay open; *Apply next bill* still bills like *Apply to this
   bill* (`DEF-BIL-8412`, open).
6. **A standing-charges-only account with no reading is not blocked by the
   missing-multiplier refusal** (`DEF-BIL-8247`): when usage is not billed for a
   service (a base-only tariff, or the account's class bills base only), no
   quantity is resolved for it and the multiplier refusal does not fire.
7. **The bill after a skipped instalment says "Payment plan — Now ends
   2027-02-15."** (`DEF-BIL-8248`; $270 on $45 × 6, September skipped). The
   notice is read at gather in a SAVEPOINT (law 14 — proved on PostgreSQL), so a
   failed read leaves the bill gathered with no notice rather than a poisoned
   transaction.
8. **The screen starts the Check itself on a run nobody has checked**, once
   per run, as a job; *Check again* does the same. *Price N accounts* prices
   the served `ready` tile (answered decisions move an account to ready).
9. **Two losses in the move to the paged served reads are FILED, not hidden**:
   the Ready list's services/plan/readings columns (`DEF-BIL-8414`) and the
   typed-reading estimate on a No-reading row (`DEF-BIL-8415`). The Sign-off
   *Fix & re-check N* selection button is dropped — each Not-in-this-run row's
   own *Fix in Check* goes to its tag and account, which is what the button did
   for the first selected row only.

13. ***Price N* counts what Calculate will price, read from the saved Check** (`DEF-BIL-8554`).

    holding answer, WAIVED by a waiver, UNDECIDED while a must-answer case (the Check's cases, an

    PRICED otherwise. The two must change together; the function says so. Worked figure (accuracy

    no-plan accounts left unanswered), waived 1.

17. **The check report shows each account's LIVE answers** (`DEF-BIL-8555`, check A6): its own (who,

18. **Send asks for the background issue pass and shows its *n of N*** (`DEF-BIL-8422`) — the pass

19. **The walk's figures are the SERVED taxonomy's.** On `seed_j72_bulk_run` the Check reads Blocked

## 2026-09-30 · Bulk bill run, the last clerk checks (U5, A5, F1–F4) — seven judgments where the rules ran out (`v2.417.0`)

The final bulk-run lane closed `DEF-BIL-8418`, `8420`, `8421`, `8510`, `8511`, `8512` and filed and
fixed `DEF-BIL-8580`, `8581`. None of the seven below was put to the PO: each is a build choice
inside an existing ruling (law 13), recorded here with its figure so the next lane builds the same
thing.

1. **Only the three S66-keyed answers are STORED at Check; every other decision tag opens on its
   first choice and stores nothing until the clerk applies it** (`DEF-BIL-8418`, BR-BIL-1040 as
   amended). BR-BIL-1040 says the answers are pre-selected from S66 and stored on the run; changes
   row 45 says a former automatic case stays *Need a decision* until accepted. Storing every first
   choice would have accepted *Accept the suggestion* on every rollover and unitless reading
   without a clerk — the automatic fix the PO ruled out. So a whole Check pass writes, once, the
   run's own `case_defaults` (resolved from S66 at create, else the tenant's current values) for
   *No reading*, *Unusually large* and *Unusual days*, never over a clerk's answer (any row for
   the case, live or superseded, counts as answered); the other tags show their default selected
   with **Apply to all N**. A stored *Estimate* still answers no account (decision 14 above): on the
   J72 seed `00003` stays *Need a decision* until its own figure is typed.
2. **Resume never runs the Check in the request; it hands the job back to the billing queue, and
   so does the Check screen's own poll when the worker is gone** (`DEF-BIL-8511`). A running job is
   "gone" when the workers answer `inspect().active()` and none lists it AND it has written no
   progress for **20 s** (`BILLING_JOB_STOPPED_FLOOR_SECONDS`), or — when nobody can tell — after
   **300 s** of silence (`BILLING_JOB_STALL_SECONDS`). The Check writes progress every 25 accounts
   (~12–17 s at the measured 0.5–0.7 s an account), so 20 s never takes a job off a live worker
   between two heartbeats. Before: the broker's `visibility_timeout`, **8,820 s**, or a Resume that
   ran the other 9,000 accounts inside a 60-second request. The run row is locked while the job is
   decided and the dispatch waits for the commit, so two presses put one message on the queue.
   The killed worker's own message still comes back at 8,820 s; by then the resumed pass is over
   (it started after the kill and the hard limit is 8,520 s), so `reclaim`'s promise holds.
3. **The Meter Reads outage switch is a FILE on the server's disk, never a setting, route or
   command** (`DEF-BIL-8510`). `SBH_WALK_SWITCHES_DIR=<dir>` at start-up, `<dir>/meter_reads.down`
   to take it down; `production.py` sets `WALK_SWITCHES_FORBIDDEN = True` and empties the directory.
   It is read in Meter Reads' own `units_in_cycle`, so billing's stop, its reference and the banner
   are the real path. It cannot be used to take Meter Reads down at Scope and walk Check: Scope
   refuses a run while Meter Reads is down (BR-BIL-1050), so the walk starts the run, then takes it
   down and presses *Check again*.
4. **The stop is served in the error envelope, and the banner's reference is the server's**
   (`DEF-BIL-8580`): `message_key billing.bulkRun.check.down.<module>`, `params {module, who, ref}`,
   trace id = the stop's own `SBH-` digits. The clerk reads *"Meter Reads is not answering. No
   account was checked. Support can fix this. Try again in a few minutes. The run is saved. Ref
   SBH-73FBC9D7."* — the same reference the log carries.
5. **A bill Send could not issue is a `bill_run_breaks` row at stage `send`, closed as `issued`
   when a retry sends it; *Retry failed* signs a NEW release row and sends the run's remaining
   drafts** (`DEF-BIL-8421`, `DEF-BIL-8581`). `release.py` already says a second authorised release
   is a second row; the press of **Retry failed** (danger tier, consequence *"Sends only these bills.
   Sent bills stay sent."*) is the confirmation, and the five confirmations are recorded again under
   that clerk's name. After a Send the remaining drafts ARE the failed bills, so nothing is named
   and nothing already issued can be reached. A bill a concurrent Send issued is never filed as not
   sent.
6. **`--send-failure` clears ELECTRIC's revenue account, so the one electric bill (`AC-2026-00008`)
   breaks at Send** (`DEF-BIL-8421`). The old flag pinned `00002` to an unpublished template, and a
   bulk run's required template (BR-BIL-1041) is an explicit pin that governs every bill, so the
   override was never read and all 8 bills went. The new break is found only at issue — Check,
   Calculate and Sign off never read the GL map — which is F3's point.
7. **"Who else is on this run" lives in the cache with a 90-second life, not in a table**
   (`DEF-BIL-8512`). The screen says so every 30 s; a closed tab falls out by itself; there is no
   migration, no clock in billing (G6) and no lock — the guarantee that two Sends cannot both issue
   is the per-bill row lock in `issue_invoice`, proved on PostgreSQL by two concurrent releases
   (`tests/test_bbr_f4_two_sends_pg.py`).

**And one seed fix that is not a judgment:** `--month-two` no longer plants `00003`'s Oct 31
reading; `--late-october-read` plants it through Meter Reads' own stage → validate → post after
September is sent, so the 7 kgal true-up is Meter Reads' (`DEF-BIL-8420`).
