## 2026-10-01 · A closed account's deposit interest is stated at its closing date (`DEF-CUS-8711`)

**The defect.** The deposit-position screen and the carry-forward offer at move-in raised a
`TypeError` (a 500) for every CLOSED account holding a deposit. `discounts._deposit_interest`
called the published accrual with no date, and the accrual has required one since `fbe971d14`
(2026-09-03). `transfers.py` had the same miss and was fixed as `DEF-CUS-5940`; this call site
was not.

**The judgment, ours to make (law 13), and it is the existing rule applied rather than a new
one.** `BR-CUS-057` (CONFIRMED) says deposit interest *"pays out at refund/closure"*;
`BR-CUS-030` makes `closed_at` the move-out date; and the move-out settlement already states
the interest at that day (`services.move_out` passes `moved_out_on`). So the day is the
account's **closing date** — the day service ended — which is the figure the final bill
settled on. Not today: a closed account takes no service and its deposit stops earning.

**Worked figure (❄️ WE-7's own numbers).** $150.00 received 15 June 2025, 2% a year, account
closed 15 August 2026: 14 completed months, 150.00 × 0.02 × 14 ÷ 12 = **$3.50**, so the screen
shows **$153.50** refundable. Stated at today, 1 October 2026, it would be 15 months and
**$3.75** — 25 cents a month more for every month the account has been closed.

**A closed account with no closing date** (a row predating the stamp) gaps — no figure, the
existing `deposit_interest_not_readable` absence — and never falls back to today's date, which
gate G6 keeps out of a money path.

Built in `06-backend/apps/customers/discounts.py` (🔒, ledger row added); proved by
`tests/test_w5_eligibility_and_deposit_carry.py` (three new cases, red first on the
`TypeError`, plus the four the triage lane left red).

## 2026-10-01 · The move-out wizard's preview refuses a final bill with no cycle (`DEF-BIL-8702`)

**The ruling being built, not a new one.** PO 2026-10-01: *"show warning and A · Refuse until
the account has a cycle (same as first bill)"*. The One-time tab already refused; the move-out
wizard's step-3 preview reached the same engine through `preview_final_bill` and priced the
base whole — ten days of a month charged the month's **$30.50**.

**Where it is refused, and why there.** In `final_bill.prepare_final_bill`, the one function the
wizard's preview, the One-time tab and the drafted invoice all share, through the same seam,
key and sentence as the first bill (`one_time.refuse_a_bill_with_no_cycle`). The window-length
fallback stays only for an account that IS on one cycle whose calendar cannot be read (`tc12d`).

**Two judgments of ours.** (1) The preview's `priced_unavailable` now carries the refusal's
`message_key` (and `message_params`) whenever the refusal has one, because the wizard already
reads them and shows the clerk sentence — *"No billing cycle. Assign one on the account."* —
and it was only ever being sent the engine's English. (2) The move-out scenario fixtures put
their unit on a cycle rather than being re-priced: every scenario states `cycle_days=31`, which
wins over any read of the cycle, so **no figure moved**. Measured: the only scenarios this
change turned red were `O2` (both variants), and the cycle puts them back; eleven others
(`L2`, `L4`, `L5`, `SH4`, `D3`, `R2`×2, `O1`×2, `E3`×2) are red identically on the tip before
this change (settlement and dispute reads) and are not touched here.

## 2026-10-01 · A utility that signs up for one capacity service gets sample bills again (`DEF-BIL-8725`)

**What was wrong, measured.** On the tip, a utility signing up for trash, storm water, solar,
broadband, thermal/heat, battery or fire ALONE got 75 sample accounts and **0 bills**; on the
all-services tenant storm water and thermal/heat reached no bill line. Two causes, both exposed
by the PO's ruling of 2026-09-30 that **a service with no asset is not in service**:

1. **The sample equipment was never planted for a capacity-only utility.** The assets block
   refused (*"no meters were seeded"*) before it reached the trash carts, fire lines, solar
   panels, batteries and broadband lines, so no unit carried any asset. Before 2026-09-30 a
   capacity service billed with nothing installed; after it, nothing billed. **Fixed in the
   seeder:** with no metered service, the block now plants that equipment and reports what it
   planted; it still refuses by name when there is nothing at all to plant.
2. **Storm water and thermal/heat can never have an asset — by ruling.** Their capacity lives
   on the unit (PO 2026-09-02, *"In case of strom water - we have to take it from Unit"*;
   thermal on connected tonnage, PO 2026-09-07), and no asset type exists for either. Read
   literally, the 2026-09-30 rule switched both services off on every tenant.

**The judgment, ours (law 13), and why it is not a new rule.** The 2026-09-30 ruling made ONE
exception, sewer, and gave the reason: *"sewer is exception because it is % of service"* — a
service that cannot carry an asset cannot be judged by whether it carries one. Storm water and
thermal/heat are that same case, by the PO's own earlier rulings. So a service whose capacity is
recorded on the unit is not asked the asset question (`gather._point_has_asset`, through
metering's new published `capacity_is_recorded_on_unit`). Every other service is exactly as
ruled on 2026-09-30. **Worked:** a house assessed at 1 ERU bills **1 × $4.50 = $4.50** a month of
storm water again; a unit connected at 5 tons bills **5 × $12.50 = $62.50** of thermal/heat.
Before this, both were $0 and off the bill entirely. Flagged in the review ledger as NOT shown to
the PO.

**What is not changed.** Sewer signed up alone is still refused by name — it is 90% of water's
volume (`CR-081`) and there is no water. The coverage test's sewer fragment moved from
`BR-RAT-015` to `CR-081`, which is what the fixture's sentence has said since the 2026-09-08
re-sign; that wording mismatch had kept the file red for three weeks and hid this defect.

**Proved** on PostgreSQL 16: `tests/test_service_billing_coverage.py`, 17 passed — the 16
recorded signup shapes and a new case per service signed up alone (ten services), each
asserting bills issue AND the service is on them. Red first on the tip: *"trash alone issued 0
bills. 13 of 28 seeding blocks failed"*.

## 2026-10-01 · The owner's bill with an empty unit's base prices $81.60 on the ruled path (`DEF-BIL-8724`)

**What was wrong, measured.** BR-CUS-170's own case — 1408 Elm, hallway **$41.20** + shared
irrigation **$28.40** = **$69.60**, plus empty Unit D's electric base **$12.00** = **$81.60** —
issued no bill at all. Through the run's own path (`prepare_run`) the owner was refused *"the
ruled path resolves one answer per service and this bill carries more than one tariff for
electric"*. The bill carries two electric tariffs on purpose (DEF-990, 2026-08-27): the hallway's
(usage and base, the owner's plan) and Unit D's (base only, **Unit D's own plan**). The R1–R7
chain resolves ONE plan with one answer per service, so it has no answer for a base that belongs
to another unit on another plan.

**The triage lane's sentence — *"R3: the unit has no meter for it"* — was a test-only effect.**
`br_cus_170` tc3/tc4 called `gather_account(...)` with no `readings`; the adapter builds its meters
from the reading rows, so EVERY metered service looked meterless — the hallway's electric first,
not Unit D's. The product never gathers that way; the two tests now hand the gather the run's own
readings (`runs.readings_for_account`). tc4 also declares the premises owner, because the
master link has been DECLARED since DEF-650 (2026-08-27) and named directly since BR-MET-1181
(2026-09-22) — its last assertion had rotted under that ruling.

**The judgment (ours, law 13).** The empty unit's base-only tariff now NAMES its unit
(`TariffConfig.covers_unit_id`, set only by `gather._unbilled_unit_tariffs`), and the ruled path
leaves THAT tariff exactly as the live path priced it — by name and logged, the shape it already
uses for a per-size line (CR-063) — while the hallway's and the irrigation's tariffs are still the
chain's. Rejected: running the chain a second time on Unit D's plan (a second invocation the
switch's own docstring calls the two-implementations defect), and refusing (the bill DEF-990
exists to issue). The adapter also stops reading that tariff as *"electric is base-only"*, which
had dropped the hallway's quantity and relaxed the multiplier guard for the hallway's meter.
**No ❄️ B4/B5 figure moves**: no arithmetic reads the field and no ordinary tariff carries it.

**Proof.** `tests/test_def_bil_8724_owner_bill_empty_unit_base.py` (red first on the refusal and
on the hallway's dropped quantity), `br_cus_170` 5 of 5, `br_cus_068` green; on PostgreSQL 16,
7 passed.

## 2026-10-01 · Changes row 44 "no multiplier" is built as a clerk decision (PO 2026-09-30)

**The ruling being built.** Row 44: *"no multiplier → **Hold** (default) / Bill with multiplier
1"*; row 45: no check fixes anything by itself; row 46: each case its own tag bucket. A meter
that has never been read has no multiplier (metering answers it from the latest read) and a
missing factor is never 1 (BR-MET-056). The ruled path's adapter refused it as **"ruled path
refused"** — a BLOCK in *Pricing refused* with no answer — so the clerk never reached the choice.

**What is built.** A new Check tag `meter_has_no_multiplier`, Meter history, named **"Meter
never read"** (*"It has no multiplier yet."*), opening on **Hold**. A clerk's *Bill with
multiplier 1* is a decision row with who and when (per row, selected, or *Answer for all*); the
next pass — Re-check or Calculate, both a Check pass — hands it to the adapter, which is the
only thing that ever puts a 1 there. Re-check keeps the answered decision on the account, so the
tag, the Check report and Calculate all still see it.

**Three judgments of ours.**
1. **Outside a Check pass nobody can answer**, so the adapter's refusal stays a refusal there —
   EXCEPT where the meter has no register difference this period. Then nothing on the bill is
   priced from a quantity on either path (the chain's own `billable_quantity` answers None for
   None, `DEF-2875`; the switch substitutes no quantity), so the refusal guarded no figure. That
   is what lets a first bill with no prior read reach its own rule, BR-BIL-062 (`us_bil_010` tc8
   green). A read WITH a difference and no factor is refused everywhere outside the Check exactly
   as before (`test_bbr_never_read_multiplier` tc4), and the adapter's DEFAULT is unchanged
   (refuse), so the shadow's numbers do not move.
2. **Its own tag, not a second code in "No multiplier"**: that tag is the anchored-period read's
   factor (`anchor_multiplier_unstated`), a different fact fixed in a different place; row 46
   gives each case its own bucket.
3. **Copy (B14 rule 33):** label *Meter never read* (3 words), fact *It has no multiplier yet.*
   (5). No rationale on screen.

**Worked case (J72 `--never-read`, walked at 1440 on PostgreSQL 16).** Rosa Delgado,
AC-2026-00012, water meter W-72116, never read: September's Check lists her under Meter history ›
Meter never read, pre-selected Hold, and not under Pricing refused; *Bill with multiplier 1* →
Re-check → the decision stays, answered *"For all: Bill with multiplier 1"* by Dana Whitfield, and
her next question, *No reading*, is asked. 9 of 9 checks PASS
(`10-scripts/chg44_never_read_walkthrough.mjs`, screens `08-qa/screens/chg44-never-read-2026-10-01/`).

## 2026-10-01 · A part-month kW line prints its days; a sample set lands whole on any sign-up day (`DEF-BIL-8744`, `DEF-MET-8693`, `DEF-BIL-8755`, `DEF-PAY-8756`, `DEF-RAT-8757`)

PO, of both, verbatim: *"fix it"*.

**`DEF-BIL-8744` — the line foots now, and no amount moved.** After `DEF-BIL-8743` (2.428.1) a
solar or battery kW charge is cut down by days while its kW and its rate stay whole, so Carla
Mendes's first bill printed *6 kW · $14.00 · $53.20*. It now prints *6 kW · $14.00 · 19/30 days ·
$53.20* (6 × 14 × 19/30 = 53.20). **Judgments of ours:** (1) the days are READ, never recomputed —
the saved line's `pricing_trace.service_days / cycle_days` (`billing/0039`), or the gathered
account on a preview not yet saved; (2) the share is printed ONLY where it explains the amount —
`quantity × rate` does not round to the amount and `quantity × rate × days ÷ cycle days` does — so a
whole month, a metered line, a base line and a counted service's joined line (whose rate is
already its share) print nothing, and a line that fails to foot for any other reason is never
labelled as prorated; (3) wording *19/30 days*, a fact of three tokens (B14 rule 33), one key in
all eleven catalogues, one component (`DayShareNote`, rule 43) under the Rate cell on the one-time
Review, the sent bill's Charges tab and the portal's bill detail; (4) on the PRINTED document it
rides on the description (*solar usage · 18/31 days*), because that Rate column is 74pt and
truncates. A bill issued before the fix keeps the document it kept at issue (BR-BIL-030).

**`DEF-MET-8693` and the three causes behind it — every sign-up day gets the whole sample set.**
Measured through the real sign-up with `SBH_FIXTURE_TODAY` set: on 1 October 2026, 16 seeding blocks
failed. Four causes, each filed before it was fixed:
1. **The cycle's start day (`DEF-MET-8693`)** — `read day − 4` was below 1 on the 1st–4th. **Clamped
   to the 1st, never wrapped**: a cycle is a day-of-month definition and BR-MET-077 compares the bill
   day with the window's close as days of one month, so a window starting 27 September closes
   (clamped) on the 31st and a bill day of the 2nd is refused. The open month's walk is clamped the
   same way (`route_read_on`: never before the month's 1st), so the window is the days the crew is out.
2. **The second cycle (`DEF-BIL-8755`)** — signed up on the 1st or 2nd, the busy day's payments sit
   between September's end and its bill date (BR-PAY-021's *Paid after cut-off* window) and 45 of 49
   accounts waited on a decision: 5 bills where mid-month issues 49. The fixture records **Apply next
   bill**, through the real decision service with its reason — what the anchor calendar already does
   (busy day the 8th, bill the 2nd: the money is next month's).
3. **The collections (`DEF-PAY-8756`)** — on the 1st–8th the collection day and the busy day are both
   today and the busy day's drawer is already sealed, so every cash and cheque was refused. On that day
   only, a counter tender becomes card or bank transfer (money after the drawer closed is not counter
   money), decided the same way on a replay.
4. **The water versions (`DEF-RAT-8757`, high)** — v2 `2026-08-01` and v3 `2027-01-01` were typed and
   did not travel with the calendar, so from a November 2026 sign-up v1 opened after v2 and rating
   refused the schedule: 4 accounts, 0 bills on 28 February 2027. They now shift by the same months as
   the periods; on the anchor day the shift is 0. ⚠ A tenant seeded in October 2026 now prices its two
   billed sample months on v1 (as the fixture's own comment intends) where it priced them on v2.

**Worked counts** (`tests/test_def_met_8693_signup_any_day.py`, water only, SQLite): sign-ups on 1, 4,
9, 15 and 31 October, 2 November 2026, 28 February 2027 and 29 February 2028 each land 1 cycle, 73
premises, 121 units, 74 meters, 75 accounts, 202 reads, 83 payments and 99 issued bills, every block
seeded; 28 February 2026 too. On PostgreSQL 16, 1 and 4 October and 28 February 2026 land the same;
28 February 2027 lands its open month's reads short there (0 of 47) and not on SQLite, which a past
February does not — the database's real clock (1 October 2026) meeting readings dated after it, not a
fault a utility signing up on that day can meet. Recorded rather than filed.

## 2026-10-01 · After Send, Sign off shows what the bills were stamped with (`DEF-BIL-8727`); the bulk run page's two side reads counted in SQL (`DEF-TEN-8731`, `DEF-MET-8732`)

**No ruling was needed; this records three judgments of ours.**

1. **What Sign off shows once a run is sent (`DEF-BIL-8727`).** Each sent bill's previous balance,
   payments and credits, plan part not yet due and amount due are read from the balance forward issue
   stamped on that bill (`bill_payload -> 'balance_forward'`), never recomputed. Before, every one of the
   40,008 bills of the sent 40,000-account run came back *unanswered* and Sign off printed `—` for every
   money figure: a sent bill is in payments' open set, while billing's prior totals leave the bill out,
   so the per-bill position could not be priced. A bill's stamp is immutable and is what the customer
   received, so it is the only honest answer after Send. **Worked:** the 40,008 sent bills' stamps sum to
   previous balance **$226.95**, payments **$0.00**, this run **$7,371,531.12**, amount due
   **$7,371,758.07**; Sign off now shows exactly those (it showed `—`). On the five-shape test run Sign off
   reads **$688.42** before Send and **$688.42** after. A stamp that itself says `—` (a seam could not
   answer at Send) leaves that bill *unanswered*, as before — never a zero. The payments/credits SPLIT
   (`payments_applied`, `credits_applied`) is not on the stamp, so it is null on a sent run rather than
   guessed. A summary saved by the old build is rebuilt once: the build's version is now part of the
   saved summary's key (`SUMMARY_BUILD`), because on a sent run no row moves to tell it.
2. **The S8 services table counts accounts ONCE for every service, in one grouped SQL statement
   (`DEF-TEN-8731`).** The count is the same set the disable guard counts (BR-TEN-026, still live, never
   cached); the guard's singular now reads the same dict. Customers correlates metering's service points
   as a lazy subquery handed through a seam (the `premises_ids_matching` precedent), so no point id
   crosses into Python and no customers code imports a metering model.
3. **The cycles list counts accounts from ids only (`DEF-MET-8732`)** — the same occupying set and the
   same first-by-`(created_at, id)` tie-break as `accounts_for_units`, without loading each account and
   its contact's name. Above 2,000 ids, both batched readers read the tenant's rows without binding the
   ids (no cap: both branches answer every row — NFR-5).

**Measured** (PostgreSQL 16, RLS-enforced role, `sbh_s14_40k`, 40,008 accounts; old code and new code on
the same world): `GET /settings/services` **52–63 s → 0.56–0.61 s**; `GET /cycles` **7.6–8.2 s →
0.95–1.26 s**. Both responses byte-identical before and after. Full table: `19-check-cost-measured.md` §13.

**A fourth read, found by timing the cold open's whole waterfall (`DEF-BIL-8758`):** the sent run's own
read, `GET /billing/runs/{id}`, counted the Sent card's *Meter reads: Locked* by decoding 40,008 bill
snapshots in Python and binding 90,014 read ids 5,000 at a time — **6.9–7.6 s → 1.24–1.53 s**, same
answer, ids taken off the bills in SQL and counted in one statement (`IN (SELECT unnest(…))`; the obvious
`= ANY(…)` took 72 s on the partitioned `meter_reads`). **Browser, cold open of the sent run, gunicorn 3 ×
60 s, started at load < 3:** Not in this run's first row **4.6 / 7.9 s** at 1440 and **4.3 / 5.1 s** at
1280; no worker is lost (was: killed at 60 s). **S2 stays FAIL on the cold open** against its 2 s: the page
asks its eight screen reads only after the run read answers, on three workers — `DEF-BIL-8809`, open.

## 2026-10-01 · Rate schedules wave B — the lane's own calls where the drawings and rules ran out (`CR-157-BRC10`)

Screens built from `05-prototype/rate-schedules-2026-10-01/images` (List 01–07, View 08–39, Add/Edit
40–71), shipped 2.432.0 → 2.434.0. None of these touches a rule, a price or stored data. Each is
written here so the next lane builds the same thing and does not ask the PO again.

1. **Service is a row of chips on the List, offered once.** Images 01–07 draw *All · Water · Sewer …*
   as chips. `FilterBar` gained an opt-in `quickFilter`: the named dimension is drawn as chips after
   *All* and leaves the *+ Filter* panel, so the same filter is never offered twice.
2. **Edit stays a secondary button on View details**, beside Duplicate and Retire. The drawing shows it
   red; `CR-087` E1 (PO 2026-09-08) fixes the three actions and their weight on every detail screen,
   and a signed rule beats a drawn figure (B14 rules 37 and 41).
3. **The band and the four tiles sit above the tabs** — image 08's order. `PageHeader` gained an opt-in
   `aboveTabs` slot; nothing else moves.
4. **A base code priced once prices every size.** The seeded `BASE-W` has one $8.00 row for all sizes.
   The Rates tab drew nine *Not priced* rows; it now reads $8.00 on each, which is how billing prices it
   (`charge_prices.answer_from_rows`).
5. **A price that starts on 2000-01-01 shows no From date.** That date is `PRICE_HISTORY_EPOCH`, the
   charge-code backfill's start, not a date anyone chose. A clerk reads `01/01/2000` as real, so the
   cell shows a dash. The stored row is the charge-code lane's and is unchanged. The charge code's
   created date was not used either: it is not when the price started.
6. **Plan details shows ONE minimum only when every size states the same one** (`DEF-RAT-8759`). Sizes
   at $15.00 and $15.00 show $15.00; $15.00 and $40.00 show nothing, because one figure would describe
   a floor no size has. The unit panel in Meter Reads (`metering/selectors.py`) still reads the version
   figure; it is outside this lane.
7. **Demand has no *Power factor below* threshold column.** Image 47 draws one; no stored field holds
   it (only the penalty rate is stored). Drawing a box that saves nothing would be a dead control
   (law 2), so it is absent until a rule adds the field.
8. **Percent of another service keeps its ruled editor.** Image 50 draws two columns; `BR-RAT-1030`
   needs a basis (usage or charges) with no safe default, so the existing `PercentEditor` sits inside
   the Usage panel.
9. **Time-of-use gets one whole-year season with its first window.** The server prices a window inside
   a season and refuses a schedule with none (`rating.seasons.required`); image 46 draws no season. A
   schedule that already has seasons keeps them. Found by the browser walk: the first TOU save was
   refused.
10. **A service priced without sizes shows its minimum as *No minimum*, read-only**, on the single
    *All sizes* row: under option A (PO 2026-10-01) the minimum lives on a size row, and that service
    has none.

## 2026-10-01 · A re-opened bill run asks for what Sign off and Send both draw before it knows its phase (`DEF-BIL-8809`)

**Context.** The bulk run page learns a run's step from `GET /billing/runs/{id}` (its phase). Until
`2.436.1` every other read waited for that answer, so a cold open of the sent 40,008-bill run asked its
screen reads at **3.37 s** and queued them on three workers. No rule says what a page may ask before it
knows the step. This is our judgment, recorded here.

**Decided (lane S2 parallel open, 2026-10-01).**
1. **Before the phase is known, ask only for the reads that Sign off AND Send both draw.** Those are the
   Check's findings summary (the tiles), the drafts' summary, the breaks and Not in this run's first page.
   A read that only one phase draws waits for the phase. Sign off's figures are not drawn on a sent run,
   and the Check job's state is drawn on Check alone. The cost is borne by a run still at Check: it asks
   for summary, breaks and Not in this run, which Check does not draw. With no drafts those are small,
   and the clerk's next step draws them. That cost was not measured at 40,000 (no such world is kept).
2. **Once the phase is known, ask only for what the step draws.** A sent run never asks for
   `sign-off-summary` or `…/check`. A re-opened run asks for `/settings/services` only if the clerk goes back to
   Scope, the one step whose aside shows it.
3. **Not in this run always sends `as_of`.** That makes one request serve Sign off and Send, so the page
   can ask before it knows which. The server only adds each held row's age, which Sign off does not show,
   so Sign off's screen is unchanged.
4. **Check draws its findings only once the job's state has answered.** The two used to be asked together.
   Now the findings can land first, and drawing them early showed *Check again* disabled for a moment.

**Worked.** On the sent 40,008-bill run (gunicorn 3 × 60 s, opens started at load < 3), eleven page reads
became eight, and all start at 0.84 s. Not in this run's first row: **2.8–5.1 s**, was **5.2–6.3 s**.
The Sent card's total: **3.9–7.6 s**, was **6.1–8.0 s**. The total is still **$7,371,531.12** in every
open. S2 still fails its 2 s on the server's time. `DEF-BIL-8809` stays open for that half;
`19-check-cost-measured.md` §14 has the table and three options for it.

## 2026-10-01 · A fact only one card draws leaves the read every screen waits for; the page asks for the figures it draws (`DEF-BIL-8809`, server half)

**Context.** After `2.436.1` the bulk run page asked its reads at once, and S2 still failed on the server's
time: the run read took 1.34 s on the sent 40,008-bill run and `/summary` 1.09 s alone (3.1 s beside the
others). No rule says which read carries which fact, or whether a page may ask for less than a whole
panel. This is our judgment, recorded here.

**Decided (lane S2 server half, 2026-10-01).**
1. **The run read carries no fact that only one card draws.** `GET /billing/runs/{id}` tells the page
   which step it is on, so every screen waits for it, and a running batch polls it. The Sent card's
   *Meter reads: Locked* (`DEF-BIL-8685`) cost 1.1 s of its 1.34 s: 90,014 read ids taken off 40,008
   frozen snapshots, then one count in Meter Reads. That cost cannot be made small (a single combined
   statement measured 2.1 s), so the fact moved to `GET …/read-lock`, same code, same "only once sent"
   rule. The page asks it only on a sent run's Send screen. Its row appears about 3 s after the card's
   total; nothing else on the card waits for it.
2. **A page asks for the figures it draws, not the panel they sit in.** The bulk run page draws two
   figures of `/summary`, the bill count and the amount. `GET …/totals` answers those two with the same
   three release functions `/summary` uses, live on every call, as the 2026-08-11 option-B ruling
   requires, and with the same refusals. `/summary` itself is unchanged and still served.
3. **Not in this run reads only the accounts the run did not bill.** A billed account is never a row
   there. The statuses and pricing partition are decided once, for those accounts only, by the same
   functions; *Paid after cut-off* is still asked of the whole run's findings, as before.
4. **No worker change.** Three workers is the deployment's choice and S2 passes on it.

**Worked.** On the sent 40,008-bill run, in-process: run read **1.34 s → 0.06 s**, the headline
**0.11 s** (where `/summary` took 1.09 s), Not in this run **0.95 s → 0.16 s**, every answer unchanged
($7,371,531.12, 40,008 bills, 90,014 of 90,014 reads locked). In the browser (cold open, gunicorn 3 × 60 s,
opens started at load < 3): Not in this run's first row **1.08–1.40 s** (old 2.55–4.46 s), the Sent card's
total **1.02–1.59 s** (old 3.60–5.94 s). S2 passes; `DEF-BIL-8809` is closed. `19-check-cost-measured.md`
§15 has the tables.

## 2026-10-01 · Bulk bill run close-out (plan C1–C4): what "Walked" means, how a missing version is filled, and what the 40,000 October walk found (`DEF-BIL-9004`–`9010`)

**Context.** S2 passed at `2.437.2`, which opened the close-out. The tracker says the close-out cannot
finish until every row is `Walked`, and defines `Walked` as *the PO has seen it in a browser on a named
build*. No rule says whether a lane's own walk can stand in for that, or how to fill a version nobody
wrote down. These are our judgments, recorded here; nothing was put to the PO.

**Decided (close-out lane, 2026-10-01).**
1. **A lane's walk never makes a row `Walked`.** The definition names the PO, and the clerk acceptance
   (22 of 22 passing) is already the lane-walk evidence. So the close-out gate stays red (0 of 61 `Walked`)
   until the PO walks `21-bulk-run-po-walkthrough.md`; the lane's job was to make every row ready for that.
   23 rows were `In progress` or `To build` although most were built and tested; 19 now name a proving test
   carrying `BULK-CHG-<n>` and read `Merged`. Rows 31, 33, 34 (Scope's Cycle details panel, collapsible
   panels, the Run to start card) are built and in every E11 screenshot but no test asserts them, so they
   stay `In progress`. Row 28 (records) is done, but a records task has no test to carry a marker.
2. **A missing version is taken from git, never guessed.** For each closed bulk-run defect with no version
   on its row: the version the closing commit named, if it named one; otherwise the version of the first
   build on the branch numbered with the fixing commit in it. 20 rows filled (e.g. `DEF-BIL-8809` →
   `2.437.2`, its closing build; `DEF-BIL-8200` → `2.412.3`, where the one-screen merge landed). The lane
   numbers are not monotonic across lanes (a `2.414.0` record landed after `2.415.0`), which is why the
   closing commit's own words win where they exist.
3. **The rollback is code-only.** Every bulk-run migration (`billing/0031`–`0039`) is additive and
   nullable; three of them (`0031`, `0032`, `0039`) would delete kept records if reversed. C4 in the build
   plan says so and supersedes `18-rollback-2.412.md`'s `migrate billing 0031` step.
4. **Sign off was not walked on the 40,000 world as the script intended; the walk-through says STOP there.**
   The October run (40,015 accounts) was taken through Scope, Check, *Answer for all* and Calculate on a
   copy of `sbh_s14_40k`. It found seven defects, three of them high: Start checking shows *Price 0
   accounts* (`DEF-BIL-9004`); re-opening mid-Calculate lands on Sign off and the gauge reads *0 of —* for
   the first ~11 minutes (`DEF-BIL-9010`); and **an Answer for all saved at Check is not used by
   Calculate** (`DEF-BIL-9009`) — *Bill base, usage later* for 40,010 accounts, *Price 40,009 accounts*,
   then 4 bills ($32.00) and 40,005 failed with *"no usable read and no decision"*. The run's own
   reconciliation held (4 + 2 blocked + 4 held + 40,005 failed = 40,015). The 22 clerk checks were all
   proved on the 11-account J72 world, where every answer is given row by row; none of them presses Price
   after an answer given only through *Answer for all*.

**Worked.** Check of 40,015 accounts on two billing workers at load 4–6: about 15 minutes. Calculate of
40,009: 13 min 55 s, of which ~11 minutes showed *0 of —*. September's sent run unchanged: 40,008 bills,
$7,371,531.12, due 10/22/2026.

## 2026-10-02 · The close-out walk's seven defects, fixed (`DEF-BIL-9004`–`9010`) — the judgments taken (`2.437.10`)

**Context.** The coordinator passed on the PO's standing instruction, *"if you find the bugs, fix it"*, for
the seven defects the 40,015-account close-out walk found. No rule says how several of them must be
fixed. These are our judgments, recorded here; nothing was put to the PO.

**Decided (close-out lane, 2026-10-01).**
1. **An *Answer for all* covers every unread meter of the account, not "the one unread meter"
   (`DEF-BIL-9009`).** The answer was saved and was read. But the row it became had no service, and the
   code that matched a row to a meter fell back to *the sole unread service*. On an account with two
   unread meters (water and electric) that answered nothing, so Calculate found the reads undecided. The
   tag's answer now covers every unread meter the clerk did not answer one by one. A per-meter answer still
   wins for its own meter, and any Hold still holds the whole account.
2. **The run names its Check job the moment the job is asked for (`DEF-BIL-9004`).** The run used to point at
   its job only once a worker picked it up. Until then the screen read *job: none* (first Check) or the
   last finished job (*Check again*) and drew the saved counts with Price enabled. The press now writes the
   job onto the run. The page also never offers Price while a Check or a Calculate is under way.
3. **Calculate counts its first pass, under its own title (`DEF-BIL-9010`).** A Calculate reads every
   account before it drafts any, and that pass recorded no progress. It now records *n of N* under the stage
   name `preparing`, shown as *Reading accounts*, and writes no resume cursor, because an account read is
   not an account drafted. The run read now carries the live Calculate job (`calculating`), so a run
   re-opened mid-way shows the progress and stays on Check. It opens on Sign off only when the job ends.
4. **The small four.**
   - **9005:** the No reading head line counts accounts, as the tile does, not meter rows.
   - **9006:** with *Estimate* as the answer for all, the bar says *Estimate needs a figure per account.
     Or choose another answer.* We did not make a default Estimate price each account from Meter Reads'
     own estimate. That changes money on 40,000 bills and is a rule, not a fix.
   - **9007:** counts on the Billing hub are grouped (*40,017*).
   - **9008:** a sent run's side card reads *bills sent*, and Not in this run reads *1 unit*.

**Worked.** See the figures in `21-bulk-run-po-walkthrough.md` and the CHANGELOG entry for `2.437.10`.

**Context.** The coordinator asked for `DEF-BIL-9004`–`9010` fixed, proved on the 40,015-account world
(`closeout_40k`, October run RUN-0003), and the walk re-photographed. Two judgments were taken past the
section above. Neither changes a signed rule or a figure.

1. **A service priced as a share of a deferred service is deferred with it (`2.438.4`, `DEF-BIL-9009`

   `decisions.py` is human-owned; the change is in its review-ledger row.

   at 40,015 accounts. For that long after *Check again* the old results stood with Price pressable.
   The page now writes the accepted job straight into its Check state. The Checking panel showed **1.3
   seconds** after the click, including the request.

**Worked: before and after, 40,015 accounts, answer for all = *Bill base, usage later*.**

| | Bills | This run's charges | Failed to draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.437.5 (first walk) | 4 | $32.00 | 40,005 (*no usable read and no decision*) |
| 2.438.2 (first fix) | 5 | $40.00 | 40,004 (sewer, *refused to price*) |
| 2.438.4 | **40,009** | **$1,270,167.00** | **0** |

## 2026-10-02 · Stale reds part 4: three judgments where the seed and the rules had come apart (`DEF-CUS-9072`, `DEF-WRK-9071`, `DEF-MET-9056`)

**Context.** The coordinator asked for `test_w6_w7_seed`'s seven reds and thirty-nine PostgreSQL reds in ten
files fixed against their rules, never by loosening a test. Three of them needed a judgment because the
rule had moved and the seed or the screen had not. None changes a signed rule or a figure.

1. **The five drawn transfers are not seeded (`DEF-CUS-9072`).** B18 §5.7.6 draws five customers MOVING
   house. On 2026-09-01 the PO made a transfer a SALE of the same account (`BR-CUS-1030`: *"dont create new
   account - we reassing that account"*) and a move a new service request (`BR-CUS-1031`). The seeder kept
   walking the old steps, which `CR-058` removed that day, so four rows failed quietly at INFO level and the
   tenant held one half-started transfer. We plant none and each row names why. We did not invent five buyers
   to turn the moves into sales: that would be a new fixture nobody drew. Worked: the Transfers tab on a
   seeded tenant reads **0** rows and all five tiles **0** (it read 1 row before); Iversen's `A-10650` stays
   open with its deposit; Park's `A-11455` still owes **$542.10**.
2. **The one costed work order raises its own order (`DEF-WRK-9071`).** Every planned order in the sample
   tenant belongs to one of the eight drawn new-connection builds, so finishing one moves a drawn cell: it
   took WO-0026 and CON-26-0121 read **3 of 5** against the drawn **2 of 5**. The job now raises a
   stand-alone water meter set, through metering's own door, at the premises of the activated build
   (CON-26-0110, 3450 Oak Ridge Dr), and works it the same seven steps. Its outcome is `passed`, read from
   metering, not the state word `completed` (`DEF-WRK-9070`). Worked: WO-0054, outcome passed, accepted,
   **4** cost lines; CON-26-0121 reads 2 of 5 again.
3. **The meters template's worked row must name a metered service (`DEF-MET-9056`).** `DEF-935` used *has a
   unit* to mean *can carry a meter*. `CR-081` gave sewer a unit on 2026-09-08 and sewer still has no meter,
   so on a water, sewer and trash utility the sample row became a sewer meter with a blank size. The pick now
   also requires the tenant's own `metered` billing basis. Worked: Ottumwa's sample row reads `water` again, with a water
   size, where it read `sewer` and a blank.

## 2026-10-02 · THE BASE MIGRATION CREATES NO CHARGE CODE FROM A RETIRED PLAN FIGURE — it clears what the bill already charges and lists the rest for a person (`DEF-RAT-9139`, `DEF-RAT-9140`, `DEF-RAT-9141`)

**Our decision, under a ruling already made — not a new PO question (law 13).** The ruling is the entry
above of 2026-09-28, *"A STALE PLAN FIGURE MAY NOT STOP A BILL"*, PO verbatim: *"we will never take default
value from plan $8.0 - that is retired"*. Billing reads the base only from the charge code bound to the plan,
and bills `$0.00` with a warning where none is defined and bound (PO 2026-09-30).

**What that does to `manage.py migrate_base_to_charge_codes`, which was written to MINT a charge code from
each plan's base figure and then clear the figure.** The two halves now have opposite effects on a bill:

  * **clearing the plan column moves no bill** — nothing reads it;
  * **minting a code from it would move bills** — it is the retired figure read again, by a tool instead of
    by billing.

**WORKED, ON SILVER CREEK'S OWN FIGURES** (water `$8.00` residential and `$15.00` commercial, trash `$18.00`
and sewer `$0.00` on both plans, no base charge code). Every one of the six bills charges **`$0.00`** base
today. The old `--apply` would have minted four codes and, from the next run, a residential water bill would
read **`$8.00`** where it reads `$0.00` today — **`+$8.00` a month per residential account, `+$15.00` per
commercial one, `+$18.00` trash on both, with nobody having decided to charge it.** And the old dry run said
all six bills would REFUSE, which was false: it called billing with arguments retired on 2026-09-28, the call
raised `TypeError`, and a broad `except` turned that into a report.

**DECIDED.** Per plan-service row the command asks billing's own functions (`gather._base_charge_code_for`
then `_base_charge_for`) what the bill charges TODAY for that plan's customer class:

  1. **the plan figure EQUALS it → the column is cleared**, with an audit row holding the old figure;
  2. **it differs → the row is HELD**: left on the plan, listed on the report as *"would RAISE the bill from
     0.00 to 8.00 if a code were created"*, and **no code is created**. Whether this utility should start
     charging `$8.00` is a pricing decision a person makes on the charge code;
  3. **no charge code is ever written** by this command. The codes the figures call for are still computed
     and printed (`NEW` / `REUSE`), with the same four refusals as before, as information for that person.

On Silver Creek the report now reads: **6 rows, bills that change 0, to clear 2 (the two sewer `$0.00`),
held for a person 4 (would newly charge 4), charge codes created 0.**

**WHY NOT THE TWO ALTERNATIVES.** *Mint anyway* breaks the ruling one indirection out — the figure the PO
retired becomes the price. *Clear everything and say nothing* is harmless to bills but deletes the only
place the utility wrote the figure, and the audit row that would keep it is pruned on its retention schedule
(`OQ-1340`, PO 2026-09-23); holding costs nothing, because billing never reads a held figure.

**THE PERMISSION CHECK MOVED UP, NOT AWAY (`DEF-RAT-9140`).** The System Admin check lived in
`services.create_charge`, one call below `apply_plan`; with the mint gone, `apply_plan` itself now carries
`@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)`. And `--actor-email` now resolves the real user WITH their role in that tenant,
attached exactly as `identity/auth.py` attaches it after sign-in — which is the defect: a bare `users` row
has no role, so every real user was refused AUTH-002. A membership that is not ACTIVE is refused.

**THE STALE PRECONDITION IS REMOVED (`DEF-RAT-9141`).** The report printed *"DEF-477 (OPEN) … Fix DEF-477
before running --apply"* on every run; DEF-477 was fixed on 2026-08-21 (`242e873`).

**NO SIGNED FIGURE MOVES.** The command writes no price and no rounding; the golden suites are unchanged.
🔒 `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING`, row in `09-human-review-ledger.md` (2026-10-02).

## 2026-10-02 · AN AS-AT REPORT'S TOTALS ARE JUDGED BY THE DATE IT DESCRIBES, NOT BY THE DATES IT WAS ASKED WITH (`DEF-REP-9150`, `2.454.3`)

**Our decision, not a PO question (law 13): no figure is computed differently and no signed rule moves — a
total that was already correct is simply shown.** The footer guard (`P2.22`) refuses to add a balance up
across time. It decided *"does this report span time?"* from the REQUEST: any `from`/`to` meant a range.
`ar_aging` reads only `to` and answers `window={"as_of": …}` — one date — and the Finance Aging view, its CSV
download and the report viewer after any filter all send `from`+`to`. Measured on Brazos Bend, as at
2026-10-31: the viewer's Total row read `$0.00 · $37.25 · $228.45 · $74.50 · $0.00 · $340.20` over 8
accounts on first open, and **six em-dashes and "Balances do not sum across time"** for the identical
figures once a class filter was picked (`from=2026-10-31&to=2026-10-31&class=institutional`); the Aging
CSV ended in a dash row.

**DECIDED.** `slicers.footer_across` takes the window the report SERVED, and `runner._shaped` passes it. A
served instant — `{"as_of": …}`, or `{"start": d, "end": d}` as `plans_and_discounts` serves — spans no
time. A served RANGE defers to the request exactly as before, so the change can only REMOVE a refusal,
never add one, and a balance over a real window (`journal_lines`' running `balance` over a month) still
refuses. Grouping by month still refuses an as-at grand total (the grouping, not the window, spans time).

**BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED** (every one of the tenant's 46 report keys run through `runner.run` with
`from=2026-10-01&to=2026-10-31`, once with the old guard and once with the new): **two reports change** —
`ar_aging` (all six band/total refusals lifted; total `340.200000`) and `account_census` (`accounts` and
`balance` refusals lifted; it serves `{"as_of": null}`, every account's balance today — one instant). Four
still refuse, unchanged and rightly (`consumption_exceptions`, `my_usage`, `usage_and_ranking` on mixed-unit
consumption; `service_order_activity` on a percentage). **21 keys could not be measured this way** — they
raise `DatasetCannotServe` and never reach `_shaped`, so the guard is not on their path.

**THE CSV.** After the fix the Aging download carries NO footer row — it ends on its last account. That is
`OQ-REP-12740`'s interim rule (a footer row is written only when a total refused), not something this fix
decided; the 8 rows sum to `$340.20`.

**RESIDUAL, FILED NOT FIXED: `DEF-REP-9151`.** The save-time check (`runner.validate`) shares this function
and has no served window, so saving a GROUPED payments definition with `from`/`to` is still refused as
summing across time. A refusal at save, never a wrong number.

## 2026-10-02 · PAYMENT CUSTOM FIELDS (`CR-161-BRC10` W5, `2.457.0`): THE RECORD PAYMENT PAGE NAMES ITS SCREEN BY SENDING THE ANSWERS; G6 OPENS PER STATEMENT, NOT PER FILE

Two judgments where the PO's ruling (R3, *"Payments IN as capture-at-entry only"*; Part 2 row 14) left the
mechanism to us. Neither changes what a user can do or was promised, so neither went back to the PO (law 13).

**1 · How the server knows an answer was typed on Record payment.** `POST /accounts/{id}/payments` is one
endpoint for four doors: Record payment (S35, which draws the fields) and Take payment on the account, the
build dialogs and Add correction (which draw none). The rule is *"Required means required only where it's
typed in"*. **DECIDED:** the Record payment page always sends `custom_data` — `{}` when the utility has no
fields — and the other doors never do; `apps/payments/custom_values.entry_arguments` reads the key's
presence as *typed on S35*. Worked figure: *Drawer* required on S35 — Record payment with *Drawer* blank is
refused (422, `custom_data.drawer`), Take payment for the same $120.00 on the same account records (201,
`custom_data = {}`). Rejected: a `screen` field in the body (a client could name any screen) and binding
required on every door (Take payment would be blocked by a box it never drew — the exact defect
`DEF-TEN-9157` fixed for accounts).

**2 · How G6 / DB-17 opens for payments.** The ban is a grep on the token `custom_data`. Allowing whole
files would let `services.py` — which also holds `_allocate_and_post` — hand the answers to allocation
unseen. **DECIDED:** two whole files (`custom_values.py`, the migration) and seven exact STATEMENTS
elsewhere (`DB17_STATEMENT_ALLOW`, the same per-statement discipline as `ORM_WRITE_ALLOW`), each with its
reason and what would make it illegal; a stale entry fails the gate. The self-test pins reads in
allocation, deposit batching, refunds, dunning and the ledger handoff, and a different statement in an
allowed file, as failures on every run. Rejected: renaming the kwarg so the token never appears — it would
pass the gate by hiding from it.

**Not built, on purpose:** payment custom values in exports and search. BR-TEN-048 permits it; nothing in
W5's rows asks for it; it is recorded on the CR as a later addition through `custom_values`.

## 2026-10-02 · Custom fields on the customers record types: where an agreement's answers are typed, what a draft does with them, and what a contact edit requires (`CR-161-BRC10` W2/W3, `DEF-CUS-9159`, `9168`–`9170`, `9191`, `2.459.0`)

Judgments taken where the PO's Part 2 table names a screen and leaves its construction open. None moves
money: every value here is captured and shown, never priced (BR-TEN-048).

1. **A service agreement's answers are typed ONCE per screen and written on every agreement that screen
   touches.** Agreements are opened by the server, one per service point on the unit — no form ever
   typed one. So *New account services* (S18) is the unit step, which already lists the unit's services,
   and its answers land on every agreement the account opens; *Change plan* (S23) merges its changed keys
   into every OPEN agreement, each keeping its own stored answers. Worked: an account with Water and
   Electric, *Contract term = 12 months* typed on New Account → both agreements read `12 months`; Change
   plan typed `24 months` → both read `24 months`, and a key the clerk did not touch (*Meter access =
   Back yard* on each) survives. Change plan opens on the answers the open agreements SHARE, and a key they
   disagree on opens blank rather than showing one agreement's value as everyone's.
2. **A draft opens no agreement, so it cannot keep an agreement answer.** *Save as a draft* writes no
   `service_agreements` row until activation and nothing else could hold the values. The review says
   *"A draft keeps no service fields."* when some were typed, the wizard does not send them, and the server
   refuses a draft that sends a non-empty blob (`customers.account.service_fields_on_draft`, *"This account
   opens no services yet."*). On a draft nothing is required either — no agreement is being typed in.
3. **Account detail shows agreement answers one block per agreement, headed by its service** (*Water
   fields · Contract term 12 months*), under the Services table — each agreement keeps its own answers, so
   one merged block would state a fact about several rows that may differ.
4. **The contact slot (S21) is the PRIMARY contact's edit and the Customer group.** The co-applicant
   (the account's second contact, written whole by a sale) draws no custom field; a required contact
   field therefore binds on the primary contact's edit only — *required only where typed in*.
5. **A screen that draws a required field checks it on EVERY save from that screen**, sent or not, and a
   stored answer counts. Worked: *Preferred name* required on the contact edit; a phone fix with the name
   blank is refused 422 `custom_data.preferred_name` and the dialog stays open with the phone still typed.
   The New Account wizard's own account fields now travel empty too (`DEF-CUS-9191`): until today an
   untouched REQUIRED field on that wizard was simply not sent, and the account opened without it.
6. **The mailing-address fields show only while a mailing address is being typed.** *Same as service
   address* writes no row, so it draws no field and requires none.

## 2026-10-02 · AN EXPORT THAT CANNOT BE STORED FAILS WITHIN MINUTES AND SAYS WHY; A PROCESS WITH NOWHERE TO STORE ONE DOES NOT START (`DEF-TEN-9190`, `2.460.1`)

**Reported from the first real deployment** (the PO's developer, 2.455.0, app and API on two hosts): a
Premises export built 73 rows and then sat in `running` with no celery error and nothing in the bucket;
after the celery task was given more CPU and memory the same export stored its file. The `file.htm` half
was ours and is `DEF-TEN-9189`, fixed by the coordinator in `2.459.1`. Judgments made here, where no rule
said:

1. **S3 calls carry explicit timeouts: 5 s to connect, 60 s per read, 3 retries (4 calls).** Measured
   against a listener that accepts and never answers: boto3's defaults took **311 s** to fail one upload;
   these take ~20 s on a dead connect and **4 min 09 s** on a silent one (20:23:01 → 20:27:10 on two
   origins here) — inside the screen's 5-minute wait. Settings, not literals
   (`DOCUMENT_STORAGE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` / `_READ_TIMEOUT` / `_MAX_ATTEMPTS`).
2. **"Stored" means the bucket answered for the file.** The worker HEADs the object and compares its size
   before the row says `stored`. One extra request per export; it needs only `s3:GetObject`, already
   granted.
3. **A stalled EXPORT is failed after 30 idle minutes, checked every 10 — and only exports.** The jobs
   table is shared with bill runs, whose resume is `core.jobs.reclaim`'s business; this sweep filters on
   the downloadable kinds and fails with *"The export stopped responding."* 30 minutes because a list
   export writes progress as it builds and its upload is bounded to minutes by (1), so 30 idle minutes is
   never a live export. A late success after the sweep raises in `succeed()` and changes nothing.
4. **Web and every celery worker refuse to start with no bucket** (`smartbillhub.E003`), outside DEBUG —
   hard-won law 3, on the PO's *"S3 in every environment"*. Reachability is NOT a refusal (a slow bucket
   must not stop a deploy): it is one ERROR line at start, asked with a separate 3 s / 5 s / one-attempt
   client because celery runs Django's system checks at start and the document check's bucket question,
   on the upload client, held a worker's start for **4 minutes** (measured; 14 s now).
5. **The download keeps its one plain 404 (HR-1) and the LOG says which case it was** — a succeeded job
   with no stored row (a worker older than 2.455.0), or a stored row whose object the bucket no longer
   has (HEAD before the redirect, so the browser never lands on S3's own error document).
6. **The reason is not yet on the Export control.** `exportOutcome` in `ListExportButton.tsx` renders
   only *"The export didn't finish."*; the coordinator was changing that file for `2.459.1` and asked
   this lane not to touch it. The job's `error` carries the plain sentence
   (`ExportNotStored: File storage did not answer.`), so showing it is a one-function follow-up.

**Host size, worked:** Django process 131 MB → 152 MB after the first S3 use (+21 MB); celery main
198 MB, one pool child 188 MB, so `--concurrency 2` is ~570 MB before any large job. **Minimum 1 GB for
`celery` and `celery-billing`** — a 512 MB task (Fargate's smallest) runs out exactly where the
developer's export stopped. Checklist: `09-infra/04-exports-to-s3.md` §10.1.

## 2026-10-02 · NEW CONNECTION DETAIL (`CR-163-BRC10`, lane NC-B, `2.462.0`): FIVE JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULING LEFT THE MECHANISM TO US

The PO's list for the build detail page (decision log `56eb54ba9`, items 1, 2, 14–15, 18–27) named
what a clerk must be able to do. Five mechanism choices were ours; none changes what a user can do or
was promised, so none went back to the PO (law 13).

**1 · An added fee is a NEW issued bill, never a line on the quote.** The quote is raised AND issued
at Create, so there is no draft to add to, and hard rule 4 forbids editing an issued line. A priced
code goes through billing's existing quote door (`raise_and_issue_quote_bill`, a COUNT and its basis,
the code's own price); a code priced "entered when used" goes through the per-case charge door with
the clerk's figure. Worked figure: an **$800.00** quote, then a **$30.00** inspection added the next
day → two bills, the Charges tab reads **Charged $830.00**, and the $800.00 bill is byte-identical.
Rejected: widening `QuotedCharge` to carry a typed amount — its docstring says the absent amount IS
the enforcement of BR-BIL-020. Metering records which build each added bill belongs to in
`connection_fee_bills` (metering 0068), held as an id with no cross-module key. Fees are taken
while the build is Requested, In progress or On hold — "until approval".

**2 · A fee on the build's own commit day is refused, not merged.** The one-time key
(`OQ-BIL-12377`, OPEN) admits one fee bill per payer per day, so the dialog asks for a posting date
and the refusal names the way out. The question's body now carries this case.

**3 · Letters wait for approval.** The PO's Q8 (*messages fire on approval*) means Create queues
nothing: `queue_on_commit` now records each occasion as *Sent on approval*, and
`connection_messages.queue_on_approval` exists for the approval lane (NC-A) to call — this lane does
not touch Approve. Send now / Resend is a per-row, audited (`connection.message_sent_now`) call into
notifications' one write door (`queue_document`) under a new `connection` source kind — the kind
`OQ-NOT-12521` closed in favour of on 2026-09-21 and nobody had built. Each send takes the next copy
number, so Resend never collides with the first copy. **Language stays the utility's**
(`OQ-CUS-12619`, guarded by `test_def_not_6354…`) — Q8's "language from step 1" was not applied over
a ruling with its own test; if the PO meant the applicant's language, that is a new asking.

**4 · A target date is sent as noon UTC.** A date picked as 20 October and sent as midnight UTC
showed as *Due by 10/19* in a utility west of Greenwich. Noon keeps the day in every North American
zone. Worked figure: picked 10/20 → shows 10/20 in Chicago and in Honolulu.

**5 · The wrong services on whole-build work orders came from the commit, and are fixed there.**
Commit step 5 stamped each template's OWN service (a "Site inspection" template set up for water
stamped Water on a Battery/Solar build). It now stamps the order's service only when the build
actually carries it, otherwise none, and the Work tab says **Whole build**. Orders already stamped
wrong on existing builds (e.g. `CON-26-0136`) are data, not code: they stay until repaired and are
listed in the lane's report.

## 2026-10-02 · Custom fields on customers, work orders, readings, routes and areas (`CR-161-BRC10` W4, `2.461.0`): where each record type's answers live, which screen a door names, and the two pages that do not exist

**No new ruling was sought.** The PO's tables of 2026-10-02 (`aa4d30f8b`) say which screens type and show each
record type; these are the judgments the tables did not make, each with the case it was decided on. Lane CF-W4.

1. **The record-type codes are the table names** — `customers`, `work_orders`, `meter_reads`, `routes`, `areas`
   — as every earlier one is (`premises`, `service_agreements`, `payments`). Settings shows *Readings*, never
   the code. `meter_reads` was kept out by r17.2 because the table is partitioned and cold-detached at two
   years; that reason is answered, not waved away: an archived reading hydrates without the column and shows
   no answers rather than raising (`ReadArchiveResultSet._COLUMNS` does not name it, as for `read_method`).
2. **A door names its screen by sending the key**, W5's rule carried to five more doors: the route wizard,
   the Areas dialog, New work order, the manual reading entry and New account's customer block always send
   `custom_data` (`{}` included); the seeder, the reference sweep, the build commit, the flows, the rules
   engine, the S28 manual grid and the move-in never do. So a required *Seal number* blocks *+ Add reading*
   and never a reading file or a meter swap. Edits (route, area, Edit work order, Edit customer) send only
   what changed and the server merges, so an answer to a field since switched off is never sent back and
   refused.
3. **The reading upload is a door that is not a screen.** One column per field, matched by the field's key
   (`seal_number`) or label (*Seal number*), never stealing a column the template already claims; nothing is
   required of a file; a cell the validator refuses is that ROW's error (*"One of your own fields is
   invalid"*), and the file still stages — validate-then-accept (BR-MET-032). The template download gains one
   trailing column per field, headed by the key; **a utility with no reading fields gets the published bytes
   unchanged**. Worked: `meter_id,read_date,reading,Seal number` / `M-4021,2026-10-02,1404,S-3301` stages one
   row carrying `seal_number = S-3301`.
4. **A correction keeps the answers.** A superseding reading (an override, a billed correction, a cascade
   that re-computes an actual reading) copies the original's answers — a seal number does not change because the figure
   was mistyped. An ESTIMATE that replaces a reading carries none: nobody collected it.
5. **There is no Customer page and no Area page, and none is invented.** The PO's Part 2 names both as View
   screens. A customer is reached through an account, so the customer's answers show in the account page's
   customer block (the PO's other View screen, *Account detail header*); an area is a row of Settings →
   Reference data → Areas, so its answers are an optional COLUMN there (*Show as column*, `AREA_LIST`).
6. **New Connection Step 1's owner is declared and NOT rendered.** The owner's answers would travel Step 1 →
   the build commit (`metering.connections`) → the master-account door (`customers.create_master_account`),
   which is the New Connection commit path the NC lanes were changing in the same hour (`CR-162-BRC10`,
   2.460.0). A box drawn without that plumbing is hard-won law 2 (typed and dropped); Settings does not offer
   the slot until the wizard lane wires it.
7. **Work orders: the column is on metering's table, the edit is Work's.** `work_orders` is still
   `metering.connections.WorkOrder` (`16-work/03-field-map.md` §4 undecided), so `metering/0067` adds the
   column and `create_work_order` writes it; Work-021's edit validates through Work's own tenancy seam and
   writes through `metering_seam.save_order_fields`, one audit row per Save (`G78` green). The detail row
   carries the answers; the dispatcher list row does not.
8. **Reading history is the reading detail.** The detail page is where one reading's answers are read; no
   history table gains a column in this wave.

**Never in the bill (Part 2 row 11):** two meters with the same history post the same 1,284 kWh reading, one
carrying *Seal number = S-1*; the consumption, unit and status are identical to the sixth decimal
(`test_w4_readings__the_answer_never_moves_the_consumption`), and a read planted in `apps/rating/` turns G6's
DB-17 red (`g06.run()`: 58 hits with the plant, 57 without, every one pre-existing).


## 2026-10-02 · Custom fields on the staff service request (`CR-161-BRC10` W6, `2.465.0`): what a request carries, where its answers go on approval, and what Request detail always shows

Implements Part 2 row 15, gap 2 and gap 3 (R5, **RULED C**) of the PO's 2026-10-02 design. Nothing below was
put back to the PO (hard-won law 13); each is a lane judgment, recorded with its worked figure.

1. **There is no "Service request" record type of its own.** The request carries copies of the *customer*,
   *account* and *premises* fields placed on Staff New Request (`service_requests.custom_data`, one blob per
   type, `customers/0076`). Reason: the ruling says the answers are *"copied to Customer / Account /
   Premises"* on approval, and a field belonging only to the request would have nowhere to go. The "Added in
   discussion" line names exactly these three.
2. **Where each type is typed.** Customer and account fields on step 1 (*Applicant*, where the person is
   asked), property fields on step 2 (*Property*, where the address is). Step 4 lists the answers.
3. **Required.** A required field placed Input on New request holds the step it is drawn on and the SUBMIT
   (server: `refuse_unless_complete`); a DRAFT still saves without it, because a draft is unfinished by
   definition and `Save as draft` exists on every step. Worked: *Roof Material* required, a draft is
   `SR-26-0009` with nothing typed; Submit is refused on `custom_data.roof_material` until *Tile* is chosen.
4. **Gap 2 beats the Request detail placement for intake fields.** The Applicant tab shows every field typed
   on New request whatever its *Request detail* choice (`CustomFieldsView … alsoInputOf="REQUEST_NEW"`);
   a field placed View on Request detail is shown too. Worked: *Gate code* placed only on New request shows
   *Gate code 4471* on the request's page.
5. **Approval copies only to records that EXIST at that moment**, because approving raises work and opens no
   account (`request_jobs`): the linked customer; the account OCCUPYING the picked unit **only when the linked
   customer holds it** (otherwise it is the outgoing occupier's, and copying a new applicant's answers onto it
   would write one person's facts on another's record); the picked premises. Everything else stays on the
   request and the review says *No account yet* — the carry into the record a job later creates is
   `DEF-CUS-9211`.
6. **R5 on the server too.** A conflict not picked keeps the EXISTING value (the server default equals the
   screen's pre-selection, so a caller that sends nothing overwrites nothing). Worked: 2201 Cane Island Pkwy
   holds *Metal*, the request says *Tile*; Approve untouched → Metal; *Requested: Tile* picked → Tile. A key the
   record does not hold is copied (*Gate code 4471*). One `service_request.custom_fields_copied` audit row
   records copied / kept / waiting / picks; the premises write goes through metering's `update_premises` and
   writes its own `premises.updated` row.
7. **The copy is inside the approval's transaction.** A refused copy (an invalid pick) leaves the request
   unapproved rather than approved with half its answers moved.
8. **A field switched off since the request was typed is not copied**; its answer stays on the request
   (*can't be deleted, only switched off*) and the review lists nothing for it.

## 2026-10-02 · Custom fields on the customer portal's new-service form (`CR-161-BRC10` W7, `2.466.0`): what a stranger is told, where each question is asked, and what required means on a public form

Implements Part 2 row 16 and the Rules table (*one utility only, including on the portal* · *"Ask the customer"
is off by default* · *required only where it's typed in*) of the PO's 2026-10-02 design. Nothing below was put
back to the PO (hard-won law 13); each is a lane judgment, recorded with its worked figure.

1. **The portal asks the same three record types the staff request does** — customer, account, property —
   because the answers land on the request's own copy (W6) and are copied from there. Customers had no portal
   slot at all although the ruling names them for the form; it is declared and rendered in the same commit.
2. **Where each is asked.** The property's questions on step 2 (*When*), beside the start date, because that is
   the step about the address; the applicant's own (customer, then account) on step 3 (*About you*). Step 4
   restates each answer under the block whose *Change* link returns to its step. Worked: *Roof Material Tile*
   reads under *The service* on Check and send.
3. **What a stranger is told about a field: key, label, help, type, options, required — nothing else.** The
   form is served to anybody holding a draft link, so the field's id, its placement map (which names every
   internal screen it sits on), its order and its print flag never leave the server. The key IS served: the
   answer is sent back under it, and it names nothing a stranger could not read off the label.
4. **A key the utility keeps internal is refused from the portal exactly as a key that never existed** — same
   sentence, same field path — so the refusal is not an oracle for which internal fields exist. Worked:
   `meter_vault_code` (placed only on Add premises) and `no_such_field` both answer *isn't one of your custom
   fields*. The customers door judges again (portal-asked fields only), so calling it directly cannot widen it.
5. **Required on a public form.** A draft saves without the answer (it is saved from the first keystroke and is
   unfinished by definition); Continue on the step is held with *Answer the questions marked \*.*; a box left
   blank says *Answer this question.* on the box; and the server refuses Send naming the step
   (`property_questions` → step 2, `your_questions` → step 3), after which every blank required box on that
   step is marked. A required field NOT asked on the portal never blocks it.
6. **A Yes/No question is a Yes / No choice with an empty first row, not a tick box**, because an unticked box
   cannot tell *No* from *not answered*, and a required Yes/No must be answered.
7. **A field switched to *Don't ask*, or off, after the applicant typed it** keeps its answer on the draft (*can't
   be deleted, only switched off*) but is neither shown back nor carried to the request. Worked: *Visit window
   Noon* travels, a *Roof Material Tile* switched to Don't ask before Send does not.
8. **Request detail shows a portal-only field's answer too** (gap 2, `DEF-CUS-9214`): the Applicant tab now
   reads the intake fields of BOTH input screens, New request and the portal form.
9. **Errors on the portal kit are now announced to everybody, and tied to their box where W7 drew it**
   (`DEF-CWP-9215`): `FormField` keeps a polite live region under every box; the question boxes carry
   `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`. The older portal boxes are announced but not yet tied — they take the
   two new props as each is next touched (`22-product-maintenance-process.md` §6's *fixed as we pass*).

## 2026-10-03 · A service request's own-field answers reach the records created from it LATER (`DEF-CUS-9211`, `2.467.5`)

Closes `CR-161-BRC10` §9 task 7 — the gap the PO's three input routes (*"SEU TEST MAPPING"*, 2026-10-02)
would otherwise fail on: what a customer types on the portal must reach the Account and the Premises.
Nothing below was put back to the PO (hard-won law 13); each is a lane judgment with its worked figure.

1. **WHEN.** At the moment a later door creates a record FROM the request, inside that door's transaction:
   the move-in that names `service_request_id` (account + its holder), `create_master_account` and
   `create_build_owner_account` (account + holder, and a master account's premises), and the New Connection
   commit of a build raised from the request (its premises). Not at any other moment: a record merely
   linked to the request later is not a record created from it.
2. **AN ANSWER ALREADY ON THE TARGET IS KEPT.** No clerk was shown a side-by-side for a record that did not
   exist at approval, so R5's default (*existing pre-selected*) is the rule, and the audit row names what
   was kept. A clerk's pick at approval is never undone: whatever they chose is already on that record and
   reads as *same*. Worked: request *Visit window Mornings*, the clerk types *Evenings* in the move-in →
   the account reads *Evenings*; audit `kept: {accounts: {visit_window: Evenings}}`.
3. **THE APPLICANT'S FACTS GO ON THE APPLICANT'S RECORDS ONLY.** Account and customer answers are copied
   only when the new account's holder IS the request's customer (`_record_request_customer` has just linked
   a request that named nobody) — W6's `_account_target` refusal, one door later. Worked: request linked to
   Ada; an account Tan holds is handed in → nothing moves, no audit row.
4. **EVERY ACCOUNT OPENED FOR THE REQUEST TAKES THE ACCOUNT ANSWERS.** A New Connection that opens the
   owner's account and then a move-in that opens the occupant's — same customer by `DEF-CUS-9078` — gives
   both accounts the answers. Both were created from this request; choosing one would be a rule nobody made.
5. **A REFUSED VALUE NEVER BLOCKS THE DOOR.** An answer the validator now refuses (an option removed since
   it was typed) stays on the request and is named under `refused` in the audit row; the move-in or build
   goes through. It runs in a savepoint, so a refusal cannot poison the door's transaction (law 14).
6. **THE APPROVE REVIEW'S WORDS ARE UNCHANGED.** *"· stays on request"* on a *No account yet* row is still
   true at that moment, and the request keeps its own copy for ever; why it moves later is rationale, and
   rule 33 puts rationale at zero words on screen.

Worked end to end (scratch PostgreSQL 16, browser): portal applicant Lena Ortiz answers *Roof Material
Tile*, *Visit window Mornings*, *Preferred name Lena*; `SR-26-0012` approved as a New Connection (all three
*waiting*); the build creates `P-00081` → *Roof Material Tile*; the move-in opens `AC-2026-00054` →
*Visit window Mornings*, customer `C-00052` → *Preferred name Lena*. Three `audit_log` rows read back:
`custom_fields_copied` (waiting ×3), `custom_fields_carried` (premises), `custom_fields_carried` (accounts +
customers).

## 2026-10-03 · A Yes/No custom field on staff screens is a Yes / No choice, not a tick box (`DEF-SHL-9240`, `2.467.13`)

**Decided by the coordinator, not put to the PO:** how a control is BUILT is ours under B14 rule 44, and
this changes no rule, no money and no data shape — a Yes/No answer was always stored as `true`/`false`.
A staff screen now asks a Yes/No field exactly as the customer portal already does: a pick of **Yes** or
**No** with nothing chosen until the clerk picks, so *unanswered*, *Yes* and *No* are three distinct states.
**No** stores `false` and reads *No* on every view screen; choosing the empty option again clears the answer;
a service request's *No* is now on the request, so approval copies it. Built once in the shared
`CustomFields` component (rule 43), so every staff slot moved at once. Worked: SEU's *EV Charged on Site*
answered **No** on Add Premises and on Staff New Request — before, both stored nothing and the property kept
the portal's earlier *Yes*; after, both store `false` and the premises reads *No*.

## 2026-10-03 · The accounts import carries the utility's own Accounts fields (`DEF-MET-9239`, `2.467.15`): three lane judgments

Not put to the PO (law 13); the PO's sentence is already the ruling — *"every import includes one column per
custom field (premises, units, assets, accounts, readings)"* (CR-161-BRC10 Part 2, 2026-10-02).
1. **ACCOUNTS FIELDS ONLY, NOT CUSTOMER OR CONTACT FIELDS.** The PO named *accounts*; the accounts file carries
   one customer block, not a customer record, and no door writes a customer's answers from it. Customer and
   contact columns would be a new feature, not this fix.
2. **AN UPDATE MERGES, A BLANK CELL CHANGES NOTHING** — the premises, units and assets imports' rule. Worked:
   account `A-9301` holds *Contract ref C-77*; a re-run file with *Loyalty tier Silver* and an empty Contract
   ref cell leaves `{contract_ref: C-77, loyalty_tier: Silver}`.
3. **ACCOUNTS JOINS THE IMPORT-FED TYPES**, so an Accounts field shown on Account detail and typed on no screen
   is now saved by Settings as *filled by import* instead of refused (R4's input-route rule, already true of
   premises, units, assets and readings). The test that used an Accounts field as its "nobody collects it"
   example now uses a Customers field, which still has no import.

## 2026-10-03 · An unplanned common area leaves the owner's bill instead of stopping it (`DEF-BIL-9252`, `2.467.17`): lane judgment

Not put to the PO (law 13): the PO's own ruling of 2026-09-21 decides it — *"common area dont need rate plan as of
now; make this optional"* — and the coordinator routed the refusal as a bug against it.

**THE JUDGMENT.** A building owner's (master) bill covers its common areas and the base charges of its empty homes.
A covered common area with **no plan** is now left off that bill entirely, and the bill is priced from the planned
empty homes, exactly as a building with no common area already is (`DEF-CUS-9050`, PO 2026-10-02 option A).
Worked: two empty homes on a $8.00 water base and an unplanned common area → the owner is billed **$16.00**, and
**$0.00** for the common area. Before: the whole bill refused *unit has no plan*, so the $16.00 was billed to nobody.

**WHY THIS KEEPS THE 2026-09-21 RULING'S CONDITION RATHER THAN BREAKING IT.** That entry made the optional plan
safe on *"an unplanned unit can exist and can never be billed"*, and said the rulings need re-putting if that stops
being true. It is still true, on the unit: no base, no reading and no line of the unplanned common area is priced on
any bill. The guard test was asserting it one level too high — that the whole OWNER's bill refuses — and had in fact
been red since 2.444.0 for an unrelated crash; it is green again on the named refusal for a master with nothing
in service.

**THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED SO NOBODY HAS TO DISCOVER IT.** A common area with its own meter and no plan (the walk's
S1 build has electric, gas and water meters on it) bills its usage to **nobody** until somebody gives it a plan.
That is what *"never billed"* means, and it is reported to the PO in the review-ledger row rather than decided here.
`COMMON_AREA_REQUIRES_A_PLAN` (customers) is still the one switch: set it back to True and the owner's bill refuses
again, by name.

## 2026-10-03 · A builder/developer owner's $0.00 base is the PO's ruled behaviour, and the run did flag it (`DEF-BIL-9253` closed invalid): lane finding

Not put to the PO (law 13): the PO already ruled this exact case on 2026-09-30, verbatim — *"user did not define
and bind base charges in rate schedule - then as a default you take 0 and complete the bill instead of refusing -
if you want to show the warning you can display it dueing the process"*. Case (c) of that ruling, as `gather.
_base_charge_for` records it, is **"no base code reaches this customer type"** — which is the walk's builder/developer
master exactly. Refusing the account, as the defect's prevention line asked, would reverse that ruling.

**AND IT WAS NOT SILENT.** On the walk's database the November run stored, for `AC-2026-00065`, two
`base_not_set` **warnings** (electric and water, *"base not set"*) beside `no_service_agreements` — on the Check,
Sign off and Send screens as the ruling allows. The draft `BL-2611-000120` carries the same two warnings in its
payload. The walk's *"with no finding"* was a misreading of the screen, not a missing check.

**WHAT IS TRUE AND LEFT FOR A LATER CHANGE, NOT DONE HERE:** the warning names the SERVICE, not the reason, so a
clerk sees *"base not set"* for electric and is not told that the cause is the customer class (builder/developer)
having no base code. Naming the class would be new copy on three screens in eleven languages; it is offered, not
built.

## 2026-10-03 · Two asset-import reds were the TESTS, not the product (`DEF-MET-9258`, `DEF-AST-9259`): lane finding

Not put to the PO (law 13): neither touches a rule, a figure or what a user can do; both are triage judgments
about which side of a red test is wrong, and the evidence decides them.

**`DEF-AST-9259` — 14 red cases in `test_br_ast_049_external_ref.py`. The tests were stale; BR-AST-049 holds.**
Dated with `git log -S "E-5000"`: `70879c9aa` (2026-09-02, `CR-062` C4) began seeding a meter per unit per
METERED service, so the sample estate's `SCW-U-001`…`050` now hold `E-5000`… beside `W-5000`…. The file's own
fixture comment had chosen `electric` *because* those seats were free of it. From that day every new-meter row
was refused by `AST.UNIT_SERVICE_FREE` — *"Unit SCW-U-001 already has an active electric meter (E-5000)"* — which
is correct, nothing was created, and the 13 numbering cases cascaded (`KeyError: 'will_issue'` is the dry run
correctly omitting a projection for zero creatable rows). The rows now seat on `SCW-U-202`…`204`, which the sample
leaves empty; every assertion is unchanged. The 14th (`test_i6`) pinned six import targets; `parts`
(`ab382ca64`, 2026-09-07) and `payments` (`c8bce7c8a`, 2026-09-22) made eight, and the set was brought up to the
vocabulary rather than loosened, so its no-inventory-target check still bites. **The candidate the row named,
`c51973920` (2026-09-30), was not the cause.**

**`DEF-MET-9258` — the DEF-618 guard named four lookup columns as uncovered. The product already refused on the ROW.**
Measured by uploading a good row and a bad row through all four stages: `furlongs` in *Unit of measure* on meters,
sub-meters and devices is refused at stage 3 by `AST.UOM_FOR_SERVICE` (*"furlongs is not a unit of measure on this
tenant's list."*), `ELEC` in devices *Service* by `AST.SERVICE_ENABLED` (*"This utility does not sell ELEC."*), and
the load writes 1 asset of 2 rows — on SQLite and on PostgreSQL 16. Same finding as `DEF-619`: the guard reads
only `<column>_in_lookup` rule names. The four are added to its register WITH their covering rule, and the guard
now checks that rule still exists in the catalogue, so deleting it re-opens the column (proved red by renaming
`uom_for_service`). No product code changed.

**Neighbour reds seen and not caused here:** seven cases of `test_cr028_import_targets.py` — already `DEF-3287`
(open since 2026-09-02, and very likely the same electric-seat cause); `test_cr046_e4…::test_every_offered_target…`
— not registered, filed as `DEF-MET-9264`.
