## 2026-10-03 — NEW CONNECTION WALK FIXES: A STORM-WATER CLASS PICKED PER UNIT IS THAT UNIT'S SIZE (`DEF-MET-9222`)

Coordinator-routed defect from the New Connection end-to-end walk (PO: *"fix all bugs"*). Judgment ours under law 13;
recorded here before it is reported.

**What was wrong.** Step 3 shows a size on every Thermal/Heat row (tonnage) and every Storm-water row (class), per
unit. Neither reached Create, so the walk's S1, S2 and S7 units carried no size and both services would bill $0.00.
Step 3 also still offered and defaulted a **Meter** for thermal, although `CR-080` (PO 2026-09-07: *"connected
tonnage - it is capacity not metering"*) stopped Create fitting one — so S2's review said **6** meters and Create made
**4**.

**What was decided.**
1. The row's size travels on `unit_services[].size_class` and Create records it on the unit under
   `UNIT_CAPACITY_CHARACTERISTIC`'s key, VALUED by `BR-TEN-171`'s ratified ladder (the call the bill makes) and in the
   ladder's own unit. *10 tons* → 10 `ton`; *Apartment building* → 6 `ERU`; *Single-family home* → 1 `ERU`.
2. **Per unit, as the screen shows it.** The PO's 2026-09-02 ruling puts storm water's size on the UNIT, and step 3
   asks for it per unit, so the class picked on a unit is that unit's. Worked: *Apartment building* on each of three
   flats is 6 ERU each, 18 ERU, **$81.00** at $4.50/ERU. The demo seed's shape — one class for the building, split
   equally (6 ERU / 3 = 2 each, **$27.00**) — is not what this screen asks, and is not changed. The difference is put
   to the PO in the review-ledger row, not decided silently.
3. A class the service does not have is refused (*"Unknown {{service}} size."*), never stored as a plausible number;
   no size sent stays BR-MET-108's stamped absence.
4. Thermal offers no device on step 3 (storm water's reason: nobody installs a ton), so the review counts only what
   Create fits. A thermal `meter` parked in an old draft is not counted either.

## 2026-10-03 — NEW CONNECTION WALK FIXES: WHICH UNIT A WORK ORDER IS RAISED ON (`DEF-MET-9223`)

Coordinator-routed defect (PO 2026-10-02 review item 17: *"ONE Applies-to + WO dropdown, row editable"*). Judgment
ours under law 13. `OQ-MET-12382` ("should a build raise one order per unit?") was cited from code and never put on the
register; this answers it from the screen the PO reviewed.

**The rule `commitWorkOrdersOf` implements, and step 5 counts:**
* an added job goes where its *Applies to* says — `unit:<label>` on that unit, `sp:<label>␟<service>` on that service
  point, *Whole build* on the build;
* a proposed job goes on every taken step-3 row whose *Work order* cell names it (the row's own pick, else the job
  proposed for that row's service — the default the cell shows). Template scope decides the count: `per_unit` is one
  order per unit, `per_asset` one per row;
* a `per_premise` job, any other scope, or a job no row names stays ONE order on the whole build.

Worked: a 2-unit build taking water with a per-unit *Meter set* — **2 orders**, one on each unit (was 1, no unit). The
same build with a per-premise *Site survey* — **1 order** on the build. Unit 2's water row switched to *Inspection* —
*Meter set* on Unit 1 and *Inspection* on Unit 2.

and future-date refusals (`DEF-CUS-9193`) — once **Company** is chosen, exactly as Tax ID already replaces the SSN.

## 2026-10-03 — NEW CONNECTION WALK FIXES: ADD UNIT TAKES THE REQUEST'S OWN SERVICES (`DEF-MET-9262`)

Coordinator decision (law 13, ours): *Add unit* on a request offers the request's own services only, and the server
refuses any other with a ≤ 6-word reason (*"This request has no {{service}}."*). Adding a NEW service to the request is
*Add service*'s job (`add_connection_service`), which already exists beside it in the same More menu.

What the walk showed and what was measured: the form listed all eleven services; the server already refused a
service the ADDRESS does not offer (`metering.service_not_at_premises`) but took any service the address offers, so on
a picked property that offers more than the request sells, a battery-and-solar request accepted a unit taking water.
The check is against the request's `connection_services` rows — what it carries — not against the address's list.

## 2026-10-03 — AMENDS "WHICH UNIT A WORK ORDER IS RAISED ON" (`DEF-MET-9223` follow-up, found by the re-walk)

That entry's rule put a proposed job only on rows
whose *Work order* cell named it. A row names ONE job, so water's *Tap and service line* and *Meter set* were named by
no row and stayed whole-build — measured on the re-walk's S2: 16 orders, 0 on a unit. **The rule is now:** a proposed
`per_unit` / `per_asset` job goes on every taken row of ITS service unless the clerk swapped that row's job away from
it, plus any row whose cell names it. Re-walk S2: 25 orders, 18 on a unit, 7 per-premise on the whole build; step 5
counted 25 before Create.

## 2026-10-03 · Three more import reds: two stale tests and a fixture that could not tell units apart (`DEF-3287`, `DEF-MET-9264`, `DEF-AST-9265`): lane finding

Not put to the PO (law 13): none moves a rule, a figure or what a user can do except one help sentence, which
follows an existing ruling's shape (judgment 3). Each is a triage judgment about which side of a red test is wrong.

**`DEF-3287` — 7 red cases in `test_cr028_import_targets.py`, open since 2026-09-02. All test-side; THREE causes,
not one.**
1. *Seat taken (5 cases).* Same cause as `DEF-AST-9259`: `70879c9aa` (2026-09-02, `CR-062` C4) seeds an electric
   meter on every `SCW-U-001`…`050`, and the committed meters fixture put new electric meters on fifteen of them.
   The product refused each correctly (*"Unit SCW-U-001 already has an active electric meter (E-5000)"*). Same
   idiom: the rows are re-seated IN THE TEST (`RESEAT`) onto units the sample leaves empty (`SCW-U-202`…, `301`…,
   `325`…); the committed CSV is shared with two other suites and is not edited. Row 15 (`SCW-U-011`, the water
   seat whose refusal IS the case) and row 12 (`SCW-U-999`) keep their refs. A guard (`_assert_seats_empty`) fails
   by name if the seed ever grows into one of those seats. The 6,000-row volume case re-seats the generator's
   cycled units the same way.
2. *A wrong count written while it was red.* The volume case asserted `unit_tagged == fixture.UNIT_COUNT` (50) —
   changed from 48 on 2026-09-02 as *"the count the GENERATOR cycles"*. `make_100k.py` cycles `i % 48` and never
   read the fixture, so that edit made the two disagree. It now reads the count off the generated file.
3. *A column list behind the product.* `test_every_declared_column_names_a_real_destination` had no entry for
   `CR-058` W7's four identity columns (`aa0fe2392`, 2026-09-01) nor for the `parts` and `payments` targets. Each
   is now given its real destination, and the three identifiers are checked against
   `import_runs.ACCOUNT_IDENTIFIER_FIELD` rather than merely listed.

**One assertion was against a SUPERSEDED rule, and it is restated, not loosened.**
`test_insert_and_update_touches_spec_fields_and_never_billing_ones` asserted that a re-upload never changes a
meter's multiplier. The PO reversed that on 2026-09-30 (*"we need to override it in case of upload"*,
`DEF-AST-8099`). The case could not see the ruling because its meter was never created after 2026-09-02. Once the
seat was fixed it went red on the ruling. Renamed `…overrides_billing_fields_and_audits_the_change`; it now asserts
the multiplier moves 200 → 50 AND that the change is audited before/after — what the ruling kept (`BR-AST-012`).

**`DEF-MET-9264` — the identifier-rule test listed six targets of eight. Judgments, one per target:**
* `parts` → **file-provided, like `accounts`.** No part-number series exists, the number is the utility's,
  required, and the upsert match key. The `accounts` assertions run on it — including that the column's help says
  the number is theirs and that a blank row is rejected. `part_no` declared no help, so it now does:
  *"Your own part number. A row without one is rejected."* (two sentences under B14 rule 33's six-word cap). That
  is the one on-screen change in this entry, at import stage 2.
* `payments` → **a third shape: issued by us and never offered.** `payment_no` comes from the `PMT-` series inside
  `record_payment`, and the target is insert-only (hard rule 4), so there is no update for a column to match on.
  The cases assert `payment_no` is absent from the downloaded sample and from stage 2, and that *Insert & update*
  is refused for this target.

**`DEF-AST-9265` — the 250-cart worker test named units by label.** `_estate` labels units `Unit 0`…`Unit 4`. With
the sample utility seeded (`JOBS_EAGER=true`), other units are also called `Unit 1`…, so four of the five labels
were ambiguous. Measured on PostgreSQL 16 before the fix: `[50, 0, 0, 0, 0] == [50, 50, 50, 50, 50]`. Now named by
unit number, the `test_def_met_9258` idiom.

The seeded job templates still proposed *Meter set* (per asset, the gate) for thermal and *Net meter swap* (per
asset) for solar after `CR-080` (2026-09-07) and `DEF-MET-9037` (2026-10-02) took that hardware off a build. The re-walk's
S2 raised two of each. **Both starters leave the seed** (thermal 3 → 2 jobs, solar 4 → 3; the seed is 22 starters, was
24). **Judgment, ours (law 13):** B18 §8.1 gated thermal on the meter set because it was the step that finished the
connection; with no meter the last physical step is *Service connection*, which is fire's seeded shape for the same kind of
device-less, unit-scoped service — so thermal's gate moves there, and gates stay at 8. Solar stays ungated (PTO names no
step). Existing tenants: `metering/0070` deactivates the two starters and moves the gate **only where the row is still the
untouched seed** (sample-tagged, v1, one published version, nothing in the bundle written after it, same name/scope/
sequence/flag); an edited one is counted and left alone, and the gate never moves while the tenant's own thermal gate stands.

## 2026-10-03 — PO RULING: A CARD OR ACH PAYMENT ENTERED TWICE IS WARNED "LOOKS LIKE A DUPLICATE", AND THE CLERK CONFIRMS (`DEF-PAY-9263`, `BR-PAY-1199`) — BUILT

**PO, verbatim:** *"Same card or ACH payment entered twice - B Warn "Looks like a duplicate", and let the clerk confirm"* —
option B of three (refuse · warn · allow). **Worked case it was ruled on:** account AC-2026-00060 holds two **$30.00**
card payments, same day, both reference **`AUTH-S8-0030`** (PY-261002-0093 and -0094), from a request page walked twice;
both were saved with no word to the clerk. The only duplicate check was the cheque one (`BR-PAY-880`, bank + number).

**Built (2.469.0):** at the four staff doors that record card or ACH — *Record payment* on the account, the *Record a
payment* page (S35), the request page's *Take payment*, and New Connection step 4 — a card/ACH payment matching an
earlier one on **account + amount + reference + payment day** is not saved on the first press. The screen shows
*Looks like a duplicate* with the earlier payment's receipt number, date, amount and reference, and two buttons:
*Go back* and *Record anyway*. *Record anyway* saves it, and the audit row says the warning was overridden and names
the earlier payment. On step 4 the whole build waits: nothing is written until the clerk confirms (`BR-MET-112`).

**Our judgments, recorded rather than asked (law 13):** (1) *same day* is the posting day in the utility's own
timezone (`BR-TEN-081`); (2) the reference is compared trimmed and case-blind — `auth-s8-0030` is the same
authorisation; (3) the earlier row must itself be card or ACH, a `payment` (not a credit or adjustment), not failed,
not a reversal and not reversed — a reversed payment's money came back, so re-entering it is the correction, the
same exemption the cheque rule makes; (4) no reference typed means no warning — nothing makes two $30.00 card
payments the same payment without one; (5) *card or ACH* is the seeded codes `card` and `ach`; a tender a utility adds
itself is not warned on; (6) a processing (uncleared) card payment counts as recorded.

**Not in scope, and why:** the customer portal and gateway webhooks (nobody is at a screen to confirm, and hard rule
6's idempotency key already stops a gateway's repeat), imports, the partner feed, and the multi-account tender door
(`POST /customers/{id}/payments`) — none was among the doors the ruling named. Cheque handling is unchanged. No
amount, allocation or status rule moved.

## 2026-10-03 — THE APP FRAME'S WORDS IN TEN CATALOGUES: ONE NOUN PER MODULE, AGREEING WITH ITS PAGE (`DEF-SHL-9320`) — OUR JUDGMENT, NOT ASKED

**Why:** the PO, looking at the Japanese discount list, asked why the screen was in two languages. Part of it is the
utility's own data (a discount's name stays as typed); the frame is ours. Its sidebar still read *Work* (ja, es-MX, hi,
id, ko) and *Runbooks* (all ten), and the Meter Reads item was a VERB — French *Lit* (also "bed"), Italian *Legge*
(also "law"), Portuguese *Lê*, Indonesian *Membaca*, Korean 읽기, Japanese 読み取り. `CR-165` §15 and `CR-166` §15 had
each recorded the shell words as "not this CR", so the frame belonged to nobody.

**Method (B14 rules 33 and 35, the `CR-165`/`CR-166` §15 precedent):** one word per idea per catalogue, the word that
catalogue already uses most for it, counted; a nav label stays at three words or fewer; and **the nav word and the
heading of the page it opens are the same word** — where they disagreed, the better of the two was written into both.

**The words, and the count that chose each where there was a choice:**
* **Meter Reads** — fr *Relevés* (63 values against 12 for *Lit*), it *Letture* (66 against 13), pt-BR *Leituras* (72
  against 7), id *Pembacaan* (182 against 35), ko 검침 (568 against 57), ja 検針 (555 against 79). de nav
  *Zählerstände* → *Ablesungen*, because the module's own heading, kickers and runbook category all say *Ablesungen*
  (255 values contain *Ablesung*). The page heading and kicker (`metering.reads.title`/`.kicker`) and the asset page's
  *Reads* tab moved with it. hi रीडिंग and es/es-MX *Lecturas* were already right.
* **Work** — the word the Settings groups and the module's kickers already use: es-MX *Trabajos* (as es), hi कार्य
  (186 against 38 for the transliteration वर्क, which the Work list kicker also loses), id *Pekerjaan*, ja 作業, ko 작업.
  de *Außendienst*, fr *Interventions*, it *Lavori*, pt-BR *Serviços de campo* were already natural and stay.
* **Runbooks** — ja ランブック, ko 런북, hi रनबुक: the catalogue's own established word, which the module's other 15
  keys already used; only the nav and the page heading were in Latin letters. **In the seven Latin-script catalogues
  the established word was the English one**, so the module's whole term moved, all 17 keys: de *Abläufe* / *Ablauf*,
  es and es-MX *Procedimientos*, fr *Procédures*, it *Procedure*, pt-BR *Procedimentos*, id *Prosedur*. A nav word
  that differed from "My runbooks" on the page it opens would have been the inconsistency this fixes, one level down.
* **Units** — ja ユニット (225 values against 153 for 単位, which is a unit of MEASURE), ko 세대 (as `CR-166` §15 ruled),
  id *Unit* (183 against *Satuan*, also a measure); the Units page heading moved with it.
* **Premises** — ja 敷地 (was 敷地内, "inside the grounds"); es and es-MX page heading *Fincas* → *Inmuebles* (28
  values against 13) so it agrees with the nav.
* **Assets** — the page heading was English in es-MX, hi, id, ja, ko; it now reads the nav's word. id nav *Aktiva* (a
  balance-sheet term) → *Aset* (56 against 10); it nav *Attività* ("activities") → *Cespiti*, the page's own word.
* **Payments** — ja nav 支払い → 入金, the page's word. The breadcrumb for *Outstandings* had become "exceptional"
  (it), "highlights" (pt-BR), "outstanding performance" (ko) and "extraordinary" (id); it now reads the tab's own word
  (*Debitori*, *Devedores*, 미수 고객, *Penunggak*; ja 未払い金, a payable, → 未収先).
* **Finance** — ja 金融 / ko 금융 mean banking; → 財務 / 재무. Its breadcrumbs lost the English *AR* and *remittance as
  a money transfer* (id, ja, ko).
* **Bell, user menu, breadcrumb label** — the empty bell no longer reads "you are all trapped" (id, ja), "you are all
  caught" (fr, it); *unread* agrees in gender; Italian and Portuguese no longer call the breadcrumb "grated bread".

**Left on purpose:** de *Dashboard* (the German software word; *Übersicht* is already the payments summary), fr
*Notifications* and *Cycles* (French words), *9+*. `en.json` was not touched: its *Outstandings* crumb over a tab
called *Debtors* is an English inconsistency for the payments screen's own owner, not a copy error. The version line
is a number and is not translated.

* **Two-factor, in the user menu** — the photographs showed the long form wrapping onto two lines in six languages
  (English does not). It now reads the short form each language's own software uses: de *Zwei-Faktor-Anmeldung*, es
  and es-MX *Verificación en dos pasos*, fr *Double authentification*, it *Verifica in due passaggi*, pt-BR
  *Verificação em 2 etapas*; its disabled-reason sentence names it the same way.

**Proof:** `10-scripts/shell_i18n_frame_walk.mjs`, photographs in `08-qa/shell-i18n-2026-10-03/`. Rollback: 2.481.3.
The walk (fails on a blank frame, English left in the frame, a sidebar label
cut off, or a sidebar or user-menu item wrapping — it caught the two-factor wrap above before the fix and reads clean
after), its output and 22 photographs (frame, and frame with the user menu open, × 11) in
`08-qa/shell-i18n-2026-10-03/`. Rollback: 2.481.3.


## 2026-10-06 — PO RULING: A FIELD TECHNICIAN AT THE STAFF WEB APP IS TOLD, IN TWO SENTENCES, THAT THEY HAVE NO ACCESS AND WHERE TO SIGN IN — AN EXCEPTION TO B14 RULE 33 FOR THIS ONE MESSAGE (`DEF-IDN-9777`)

**What the PO saw.** After `DEF-IDN-9748` (2.548.2), a Field Technician who signs in to the STAFF web app sees
*"Sign in on the field app."* in two places: the sign-in page's error box, with *Field app* as a plain line under it
that does not look like a link, and the staff shell's 403 page, which was that one line and a small *Field app*
button on an empty page.

**The ruling, verbatim, 2026-10-06.** The PO asked for *"a clear message Field Technicans are suppose to login into
Field Technican Mobile app; They dont have access to Staff portal"*. Shown a six-word version, they answered *"We need
longner sentence 8 to 10 owords"*. Shown the two sentences below, they answered: *"this si correct - please update -
Field Technicians do not have access to the staff portal. Please sign in on the Field Technician mobile app
instead."*

**What is built (2.549.5).** Both places show exactly:

> Field Technicians do not have access to the staff portal.
> Please sign in on the Field Technician mobile app instead.
> **[Open the field app]**

One shared component, `07-frontend/src/components/FieldAppNotice.tsx`. On the sign-in page it is the red error box
with the two sentences and a primary button; on the 403 page it is a centred card (the same signed-out card sign-in
uses), the first sentence as its heading, the second under it, and the button full width. The button goes where the
old control went — the field app's sign-in, `/{tenant}/work/mobile/signin`; on the 403 page it ends the web session
first, as before. All eleven catalogues carry the two sentences and the button in their own words (rule 35).

**Scope — the coordinator's reading of the PO's choice (a), recorded as OURS so it can be reopened:** this is an
exception to B14 rule 33's six-word cap **for this one message on these two screens only**. Rule 33 is unchanged
everywhere else, and this is not a precedent for any other over-cap string — like the two rulings of 2026-09-24
already stamped on rule 33, it covers the words the PO was shown. B14 rule 33 carries the exception, dated, in its
text and in its status cell.

**One finding on the way, written down rather than fixed here:** `G33` (refusal copy length) does not see this
message at all — `G32`'s refusal key set does not include `identity.signIn.fieldAppOnly` or
`identity.signIn.webAppOnly`, because the server raises them through a named constant. So the old six-word sentence
was never actually checked by the gate that caps refusals, and the new one would pass it unseen. Filed as its own
defect row (`DEF-GOV-9783`); the exception above is a PO ruling and does not depend on the gate.


## 2026-10-06 — THE MAIN METER SIZES THE CONNECTION; A SUB-METER UNDER IT DOES NOT (`DEF-MET-9773`, `2.549.9`)

**Decided by the coordinator, built by lane MET-9773 (maintenance).** Not put to the PO: it moves no rate, no
price and no signed figure, and it narrows the 2026-08-27 entry (*two meters on one service point disagreeing
answer None*) to what that entry was about — two METERS. It never considered a sub-meter or a device hanging off
a meter (BR-AST-003).

**The worked case.** Rosa Delgado, 300 Willow Court Apt 2B (move-in matrix M2): main water meter W-M2 is 3/4"
(`W-34`); her irrigation sub-meter SW-M2, under it on the same connection, is 5/8" (`W-58`). The size reader took
both as claims on the connection's size, called them a disagreement, and her first bill refused *"This
connection's size is not recorded"* — with both sizes recorded. A bill run would have refused her the same way.
**Now her water is priced at 3/4", from her main meter.**

**The judgment where the instruction ran out — what "sub-meter" means for the rule.** Leaving out every asset with
a parent would have broken the commonest submetering shape: an apartment whose ONLY water meter is a sub-meter of
the building's master, which stands on another unit. On the apartment's own connection that sub-meter is the top,
and its size is the apartment's size. So the rule is: **an asset is left out of the size only when its parent
stands on the SAME connection.** Same-connection is the set the reader already used (currently on the unit, on
the unit's service point for that service).

**Kept, deliberately:** two top-level meters on one connection with two sizes still answer *unresolved*, and the
bill still refuses by name. **A side effect worth stating:** an UNSIZED main meter with a sized sub-meter used to
take the sub-meter's size — pricing the connection off the wrong device, silently; it now reads *size not
recorded* and the bulk Check names the MAIN meter. The bulk Check's inline *set size* writes to the main meter
only (it used to overwrite the sub-meter's own recorded size too). One set feeds all three
(`metering.selectors._connection_top_assets`), so the meter read, the meter named and the meter written cannot
drift.

**Trash and fire are unaffected:** a counting service is priced per asset through its own read
(`metering.billable_size_groups`), which this change does not touch; fire's `$84.00` worked figure does not move.


## 2026-10-06 — A MOVE-IN'S VISIT IS RAISED ON ITS METER'S SERVICE OR REFUSED BY NAME BEFORE SAVE; THE SAMPLE SET SEEDS VISIT TEMPLATES PER METERED SERVICE (`DEF-WRK-9784`, `DEF-CUS-9785`) — OUR JUDGMENT, NOT ASKED

**What happened.** M6 (Foundry Works Fabrication Inc., electric + gas + water + solar) booked two visits on step 1:
*Opening read* for electric meter E-M6 and *Reconnect visit* for gas meter G-M6. Both were the sample set's WATER
templates — the only visit templates the tenant had, because `_seed_flow_visit_templates` seeded `plan.primary`
alone. Work rightly refused each (`work.order.template_wrong_service`), the whole raise is one savepoint, so the
move-in completed with **0 of 2** work orders, a warning the screen printed as the raw code
`work_orders_not_raised`, and nothing in the server log.

**Four judgments, all ours (nothing here touches a rule, a price or money):**

1. **A wrong pick is REFUSED, not warned.** `BR-WRK-055` keeps a move-in from waiting on a RAISE (a crew that cannot
   be booked); it never asked a move-in to accept an input Work will certainly refuse. So a template of another
   service than its *For* meter is refused by name — on step 1 (the row says *Template is for another service.* and
   Continue holds) and again before the move-in is written (`from_flows.check_order_rows_on_unit`, called from
   `services._move_in` and the move's *Add work order*). Every other raise failure keeps the warning posture.
2. **A row's list is its meter's service.** A row naming a meter lists that service's templates plus every job type
   with no template of that service (raised by type); a row naming no meter keeps the whole offer, each entry naming
   its service when more than one is offered. A typed row on a meter never borrows another service's template
   (`_default_template(..., fits)`); with none of its service it raises the type alone, as it always could. A clerk
   who picks the visit FIRST and the meter after gets the SAME visit (name and job type) of the meter's service when
   one exists — *Reconnect visit* pointed at the gas meter becomes gas's — and the refusal only when none does.
3. **Seed per metered service.** `CR-062` C3 split `plan.metered` (per service) from `plan.primary` (*the first
   one*). A visit is done TO a meter, so it is per service. The primary is `metered[0]` and is seeded first, so its
   template numbers do not move; on M6's utility the six templates now exist for electric, water and gas.
4. **A failed raise is logged.** `_raise_flow_work` writes one WARNING line on `smartbillhub.customers` naming the
   flow, its id, how many orders were asked for and the refusal key. Support can now find a lost visit without a
   person reading the done screen.

**The screen half (`DEF-CUS-9785`).** `warningText` read only `customers.account.warning.<code>`. A warning that
carries its own `message_key` (all three of Work's: not raised / not assigned / not scheduled) is now read through
that key when no code-keyed sentence exists, with its params; a code-keyed sentence still wins and an unknown code
still renders. No new string in any catalogue.

**Worked figure.** M6 before (2.549.9, lane MVI-E2E-3): 2 visits asked, **0** raised, 1 warning printed as a code;
**125 PASS · 3 FAIL**. After (2.549.13, a fresh world): **2 of 2** raised — WO-0053 *Opening read* of ELECTRIC (ST-0025)
on E-M6, WO-0054 *Reconnect visit* of GAS (ST-0034) on G-M6 — no warning about work, **153 PASS · 1 FAIL** (the one is
`DEF-BIL-9793`, sewer on the first bill, another lane's). CR-171 §29 has the record.


## 2026-10-06 — SEWER FOLLOWS WATER ONLY AT AN ADDRESS THAT OFFERS SEWER (`DEF-BIL-9793`, `2.549.15`)

**Decided by lane BIL-9793 (maintenance), our judgment under law 13, not put to the PO** — it reconciles two signed
rules rather than making a new one, and moves no rate, price or signed figure. Flagged as NOT shown to the PO in the
review ledger.

**The two rules.** (1) PO 2026-09-30, option B: *"No service point for % of services · Sewer is taken whenever its
basis service (water) is on the bill"*. (2) `BR-MET-119` (PO 2026-08-26): a premises DECLARES which services the
address offers, and a unit may never take one it does not — a meter for a service the address does not offer is
refused at the door. Option B removed sewer's service POINT from the question; the question put to the PO was A
(keep a sewer point with no meter) against B (no point), and the worked case shown was a unit at an address WITH
sewer losing its `$76.50`. **Nobody asked what happens at an address that offers no sewer**, and read literally
option B bills sewer there — the one service the address rule could not reach, because it has no door.

**The worked case (move-in matrix M6, CR-171 §28.1).** Foundry Works Fabrication Inc., 5 Foundry Way Bay 3, plan
`SCW-IND`. The address offers electric, gas, water and solar. Its first bill carried **`$38.25` sewer usage (90% of
water volume) and a `$9.00` sewer base, and taxed both** (State 6.25% and County 2.00% on `$1,133.01` included the
`$47.25`).

**The judgment.** Sewer follows water **at an address that offers sewer**. Where the premises' list of services is
recorded and sewer is not on it, sewer is *not in service* — no line, and the clerk's review list names it, exactly
as for any plan service the property has no connection for (`BR-BIL-301`). **Where nobody ever recorded the list
(`NULL`, `DEF-762`), nothing narrows** and sewer follows water exactly as before, because *not asked* is not *offers
nothing*. Applies to every `%`-of-service, not only sewer, and to the bill run and the one-time bill alike (both
price through `gather.gather_account`).

**Who it changes.** Only an account whose address lists its services and leaves sewer out while its plan prices
sewer. Searched on every lane world database on the shared PostgreSQL 16 cluster: 200 issued sewer lines, **none**
at such an address — no issued bill needs a credit.


## 2026-10-06 — NEW CONNECT STEP 2: THE "THIS PLAN" BLOCK IS REDRAWN SO A CLERK SEES EVERYTHING THE PLAN BINDS (`DEF-CUS-9821`)

**The PO's words, verbatim, in order.** (1) *"In this screen all component bind in plan like rate, charge,code, base
reate, taxes, discount needs to visible this data is required for clark while attaching the plan based on data clark
will take decision"*. (2) On the drawing (artifact `9poRZzcU1ooxCw9A78jXgy`): *"We dont want any section on step 2
should be changed - only Services and plan - to be updated using the artifact redrawing has been given"*. (3) *"okay -
please do these changes - New Connect step 2: what changes"*.

**What was shown and agreed (the table the PO said "okay" to).**
* **No change:** page title, step bar, every section above *Services and plan*, the Utility services chips, the Plan
  dropdown (same control; picking a plan refreshes the block), the footer buttons.
* **Replaced:** today's *This plan* facts and the *What each service is priced at* table become one *This plan* block:
  a summary strip (Code · Version + status · In force · Account type · Minimum bill · Covers x of y services); a
  warning line only when true; **Base charges** and **Usage rates** open; **Other charges**, **Deposit**, **Taxes**,
  **Discounts**, **Outside city** collapsed, each with a one-line summary (Taxes: *"2 · 8.00% total"*); *Open the
  plan ↗* and every code, schedule, tax and discount name open their own page in a new tab; footer *"Figures come
  from the plan, for Residential accounts at this address."*
* **Not built:** the drawing's yellow proposal note and its *What each part is for* legend.

**Worked figure (the drawing's own).** Solar, base code BASE-SOL `$10.00` a month, Residential; Battery, its schedule
names no base code → the line *"Battery: its rate schedule names no base code."* with *Choose a base code ↗*, and
Battery's base row reads *Not chosen*. Battery's blocks show unit prices to four places (`0–500 kWh · $0.0425`), every
amount at two (hard rule 2's unit-price exception).

**Our judgments under it (law 13, not put to the PO).**
1. **One read, the plan details page's own.** `GET /plans/{id}` already serves the step its summary AND
   `plan_reads.plan_sections`; the step reads it once and the block narrows it to the services the address takes. No
   second reader.
2. **The owner's class narrows the BASE only**, through a new optional `?classes=` on `GET /plans/{id}` that feeds the
   same class narrowing the plan's own classes feed today — because the bill picks a base by the ACCOUNT's class. Other
   charges, deposits and taxes keep every class row the plan carries, as the drawing shows (Deposit: Residential
   *and* Commercial). Absent `classes`, the read is byte-identical to before.
3. **"Names no base code" means the schedule's version in force names none** (`base_charge_code_id` empty) — the same
   fact `DEF-RAT-9797`'s *Choose a base code* list reads. The base row shows *Not chosen* where no code serves
   (none or several); where one pooled code serves, it is shown, since it is what the bill charges.
4. **Five small additions to the read, each a fact the drawing prints and nothing served:** base `named` and
   `classes` (the code's class names); tax `customer_classes` (names; empty = every class); deposit `refundable`
   (the code's type is *refundable*); discount `enrolment_mode` and `proof_required` (from the version in force).
   Additive keys; no figure, no money path, no rule moves.
5. **The sentence "This figure could not be shown. It is not zero — no amount reached this cell." never appears in
   this block**; an absent figure is a dash.
6. **One component** (B14 rule 43), `features/rating/planSections/ThisPlanBlock.tsx`, mounted only on New Connect
   step 2; move-in's *See full rates* is untouched in this change.

## 2026-10-06 — PO "GO AHEAD START IT": SEVEN NEW CONNECT FIXES, IN THE ORDER N1, N3, N4, N5, N6, N7, N2 (`DEF-CUS-9822`..`9828`)

**The PO's go, verbatim: *"go ahead start it"*, said of the seven-row table of New Connect step 1/step 2 reports
(the PO's own words in each row).** Filed as the PO's reports, one row each, before any code:

| Row | Defect | The PO's words | What is built |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | `DEF-CUS-9822` | Sub-category is hardcoded | Sub-category offers the sub-types the utility set up under the chosen category (the list move-in and request capture read); cleared when the category changes; sent to the account as move-in sends it |
| N3 | `DEF-CUS-9823` | *"add document, attach another document button is not required"* | One button, *Attach a file* |
| N4 | `DEF-CUS-9824` | Uploaded by is blank | The signed-in clerk's name and the moment of attaching, in the utility's zone and date format |
| N5 | `DEF-CUS-9825` | No way to preview | View (eye) on a draft file and on a document linked from the request |
| N6 | `DEF-CUS-9826` | *"give the hide and view button with that fields so user can view while entering"* | Show/Hide on SSN and Driver's licence, owner and co-applicant; masked by default |
| N7 | `DEF-CUS-9827` | *"while adding co-applicant do not show owner type, sub-category, person and company etc"* | A short co-applicant form: Full name, Email, Phone, Date of birth, Gov-ID |
| N2 | `DEF-CUS-9828` | Only partly prefilled after Approve | Every answer the request holds arrives, filling only empty fields; the request's documents are LINKED (not copied) and reach the owner's account at Create |

**Our judgments under the go (law 13, not put to the PO):**
* **N2 fills only what is EMPTY.** The old prefill overwrote name, email and phone with the request's on every
  resume; a clerk's typing now wins. A matched premises still wins over the applicant's address.
* **N2 never copies an SSN or a licence.** The request's are shown as *ends 1234* beside the box; the box stays
  empty (BR-CUS-092(c), last four only).
* **N3: the *expected, not yet brought* row is DELIBERATELY not offered on New Connect** — it never was: step 1
  refused a row with no file before this change (nothing exists until Create, so a promise has nowhere to live). An
  empty box still answers *"Choose a file to attach."*
* **N7: the co-applicant stays a person** (`partyKind = person` always). Its company Tax ID path is not drawn.


## 2026-10-06 — THE PORTAL SHOWS A TAX CERTIFICATE AS "EXEMPT FROM <TAX> · RUNS OUT <DATE>", WITHOUT ITS NUMBER (`DEF-CWP-9795`, `2.555.2`)

**Decided by lane DEF-CWP-9795 (maintenance), our judgment under law 13, not put to the PO** — it moves no rule, no
money and no data; it makes the customer's own page say what the bill already does.

**The fault.** PO ruling (A) 2026-10-05 (`DEF-CUS-9724`): a certificate removes only the tax it names, so a move-in
that records one leaves the blanket `tax_exempt` flag false. The portal's *Your account* read only that flag, so M5's
church (Grace Fellowship of Cedar Ford, certificate against the City of Cedar Ford utility tax, to 12/31/2028) saw
**no Tax panel at all** while its bill dropped the City's 2.00%.

**The judgments.** (1) The portal reads the staff page's own read (`customers.seams.account_tax_exemptions` →
rating's `exemption_certificates_for_account`), never a second one; only LIVE certificates show — an expired one has
reinstated the tax, and revoked ones never arrive. (2) **The certificate number is NOT shown.** The portal
blueprint (rendered p48) draws no tax facts on the account card, `08-screen-layouts.md` draws the panel as
*From / Runs out*, and `US-CWP-031` TC-5 already ruled the number is the utility's record, not the customer's —
so the brief's condition ("only if the drawing shows it") is not met. (3) The drawn *From* row is labelled
**"Exempt from"** (rule 33: a label of two words; *From* alone reads as a sender under a "Tax exempt" heading), one
*Exempt from / Runs out* pair per live certificate. (4) The blanket exemption reads exactly as before — one *Runs
out* row — because it covers every tax and has no tax to name. Worked: the church's panel reads **Tax exempt ·
Exempt from City of Cedar Ford utility tax · Runs out Dec 31, 2028 · Certificate On file**; Marcus Bell's blanket
exemption still reads **Runs out Mar 31, 2027 · Certificate On file**.
## 2026-10-06 — THE PORTAL ASKS THE ADDRESS IN PARTS AND THE APPLICANT'S CATEGORY (`DEF-CWP-9817`, `DEF-CWP-9818`, `2.555.0`)

**PO RULING (category), verbatim, relayed by the coordinator the same day:** *"How should a portal
applicant give their customer category? Show the full Category and Sub-category dropdowns from Settings
on step 3, and let the applicant pick from all seven categories and their sub-categories. The clerk can
still change it."* → **RULED (b).** What was shown: Kyle Mark's request arrives *"Type: Not yet
classified"*; options (a) *My home · My business · Something else* as a suggestion the clerk confirms,
(b) the full dropdowns, (c) the clerk only, as today. We recommended (a); the PO chose (b).

**PO REPORT (address):** Start service step 1 takes the address as one *"House number and street"* box
plus a unit, where the Customer Portal blueprint (p31, read as an image) draws Street address · Town ·
ZIP code · *Is there a unit or apartment number?*. Step 3's rail showed exactly what was typed — the PO's
screenshot read *"Haustin Towers 2"*. `BR-CUS-1091` (PO 2026-09-22, *"correct address will be on presmies
but first time you will ahve to take the details to match it"*) had been applied to the staff capture only.

**Our judgments under law 13 — not put to the PO:**
1. **Category REQUIRED, sub-category optional.** The request otherwise arrives unclassified, which is the
   thing the ruling fixes; the staff capture's step gate asks the category and nothing of the sub-type, so
   the portal mirrors it. Worked: Kyle Mark picks *Commercial*, leaves Sub-category on *Optional*, and
   Send goes; with neither, Continue on step 3 reads *"Choose a category first."*
2. **The list is the clerk's list.** Active and not stopped (`legacy`, which Settings' *Stop offering*
   sets — `DEF-CUS-9808`), with active sub-categories, in the same order. The guest sees codes and names,
   never ids. A category with no sub-categories shows *"None for this category"* rather than an empty box.
3. **A pick that stops being offered between step 3 and Send writes nothing and does not refuse the
   application** — `_portal_service_rows`' rule for a service switched off in the same window. Refusing a
   stranger's whole application at the last button for a Settings change they cannot see is worse than a
   request arriving *Not yet classified*, which is today's behaviour.
4. **Not `set_customer_category`.** That is the clerk's act under a staff role; the portal writes the same
   two columns through the customers module's own portal door with its own validation and a
   `service_request.category_set` audit row (actor: the portal reporter).
5. **Town and ZIP are required on step 1; State is not asked** (the blueprint draws none; a utility serves
   its own state). Without town and ZIP the match falls back to a guess on the street alone, which is the
   defect. ZIP is five digits or ZIP+4, the kit's `US_ZIP`.
6. **The match is the staff matcher** (`metering.address_match`, narrowing in SQL), and only ONE exact row
   is a match. Worked: `31 Palm Ct, Austin, 78702` matches Pine Hill's premises; `31 Palm Ct, Austin,
   78701` did match before (street alone) and now does not — a stranger was being shown another ZIP's
   services and fees. A near match is not offered to the applicant (the blueprint's *ADDRESS NOT
   RECOGNISED — offers the nearest matches* state is not built; noted, not filed as built).
7. **One US-format line, composed by the server.** `1841 Quarry Hill Ct, Apt 12, Silver Creek, TX 78611`:
   the matched premises' own address when there is one, otherwise the typed parts with the utility's own
   state from the company profile (none if the profile holds none — never a guess). A bare unit number or
   letter is written with USPS's `#` (`12` → `#12`), because `…Hill Ct, 12, Silver Creek` reads as a second
   house number. The head, the rail, Check and send and the resumed head all print this one line.
8. **Step 1 hands step 2 the TYPED parts, never the matched line.** It used to pass the premises' composed
   line on a match, which then became `address_as_given` — the applicant recorded as having said the
   register's spelling (`BR-CUS-070`).
9. **Track shows no address at all and is unchanged** — the anonymous Track read deliberately carries no
   address (`BR-CWP-024`); nothing there printed the typed box.
10. **"Or use my location" (drawn on p31) is NOT built** — there is no location read on the portal and it
    is outside this lane.
11. **The staff request's *Address as given* now prints the town and ZIP the applicant gave**
    (`1841 Quarry Hill Ct, Apt 12 · Silver Creek, 78611`); it passed no locality and printed the street alone.
12. **The pick lands in the request's *Customer category* row, NOT in *Asked for › Type*.** The question put to
    the PO quoted *"Type: Not yet classified"*; on the request page that row (and the head's *NOT YET
    CLASSIFIED*) is the JOB classification — move-in or new connection — which the clerk settles. The ruling names
    *"all seven categories and their sub-categories"* from Settings, which is the customer category, so that is
    what was built; *Type* still reads *Not yet classified* until the clerk classifies the job. Reported to the
    coordinator in plain words rather than re-asked (law 13).

## 2026-10-06 — NEW CONNECT N2: WHERE THE REQUEST'S ANSWERS LAND — OUR JUDGMENTS, NOT ASKED (`DEF-CUS-9828`, `2.556.1`)

**Decided by lane NCT-01 under the PO's go of the same day (law 13); nothing put to the PO.**
* **The applicant's unit (`Apt-12`) goes to step 3 as a unit, not into step 2's *Unit, apt. or suite*.** Step 2's box is
  the PREMISES' postal line (*"Units are named on step 3"*, the 2026-09-28 drawing's own note); writing `Apt-12` there
  would put one flat's number on the whole building's address. Step 3's pattern gets prefix `Apt`, 12 to 12, which the
  product labels **`Apt 12`** — only for an address the resolver did not match and a pattern nobody has typed.
* **Fill only what is EMPTY, everywhere.** The clerk's typing wins over the request; the old prefill overwrote name,
  email and phone on every resume. A matched premises still wins over the applicant's words.
* **The sub-type arrives only under the class the draft holds** — a sub-type under another category is no answer.
* **SSN and licence: last four only, shown under the EMPTY box as *Provided on the request · ends 1234*** (5 words + the
  figure, rule 33's FACT). Never copied into the box and never sent.
* **Where the bill goes:** the staff capture's parts, else the portal draft's — and only over a mailing block the clerk
  has not touched.
* **The request's documents are LINKED:** listed on step 1 with who brought them and the verdict already recorded, and
  filed on the owner's account at Create through the move-in's own `carry_request_documents` (one stored file).
* **A New Connect co-applicant still reaches nothing on the server** (`DEF-CUS-9830`, filed, open) — prefilling it from
  the request makes the gap more visible, not larger.

## 2026-10-06 — PO RULING: A NEW CONNECT CO-APPLICANT IS SAVED AS A CO-OWNER ON THE NEW ACCOUNT, THE WAY MOVE-IN SAVES ONE; ONLY HER NAME IS REQUIRED (`DEF-CUS-9830`)

**Question shown to the PO, verbatim:** *"Where does a New Connect co-applicant get saved? (a) Save her the way move-in
does: a co-owner on the new account, SSN scrambled so staff see only the last four digits. It's the same record and
the same rules you signed this morning (Riya G). (b) Remove the co-applicant section"* — with the example **Maria
Mark**, added as co-applicant on Kyle Mark's New Connect.

**PO, verbatim:** *"1. Where does a New Connect co-applicant get saved? (a) Save her the way move-in does: a co-owner on
the new account, SSN scrambled so staff see only the last four digits. It's the same record and the same rules you
signed this morning (Riya G). - but make SSN, Email, Phone , DOb optional for co applicant"*.

**What it means, built by lane NCT-02:**
* **Option (a).** At *Create*, the co-applicant typed on New Connect step 1 is written as a co-owner on the owner's new
  account, through the SAME service move-in uses (`customers.move_in_people.pop` → `write_at_complete`, the
  `account_co_owners` record signed this morning). Her SSN and driver's licence are stored scrambled; staff and the
  audit row see the last four only. An audit row is written, as move-in writes one.
* **Only her name is required.** Email, phone, date of birth, SSN and driver's licence may be left blank; each is
  checked for its format only when it is given. The record already allows every one of them to be blank — nothing about
  the protected record or its migration changes.
* **Worked example:** a clerk adds *Maria Mark* as co-applicant with only her name. On *Create* she is saved as a
  co-owner on Kyle's new account; email, phone, date of birth and SSN are blank. Had the clerk typed SSN `123-45-6789`,
  staff would see `•••• 6789` and nothing more.
* **A co-applicant prefilled from a request (`DEF-CUS-9828`, N2) is the same co-applicant** and is saved the same way.
* **The ruling names New Connect's co-applicant only.** Move-in's own co-owner form is not changed by this ruling.

## 2026-10-06 — NEW CONNECT FOLLOW-UPS FROM NCT-01's PHOTOGRAPHS: OUR JUDGMENTS, NOT ASKED (`DEF-CUS-9834`..`9837`, `2.557.0`)

**Decided by lane NCT-02 (law 13); nothing put to the PO.**
1. **The portal's photo ID was never losing its type in the product.** The real portal attaches each file ON a
   requirement (`DEF-CWP-9167`, ruling A) and the request stores it as `proof_of_identity` / `proof_of_address_or_occupancy`;
   NCT-01's walk uploaded with no requirement, which files `other` (*Anything else*). The walk is corrected
   (`10-scripts/nct02_new_connect_co_applicant_walk.mjs` sends `photo_id`). **The type reads *Proof of identity*, the
   request's own word** — the same word the request page prints for the same file — not *Photo ID*, which would be a
   third vocabulary for one document.
2. **A portal file's uploader is the APPLICANT, named with the role: *Kyle Mark (applicant)*.** Known from the stored
   file's own process (`stored_by_process = portal.application_documents`, written only by `attach_from_portal`), never
   guessed from an empty `uploaded_by`. The request page and New Connect read the same field, so both say it.
3. **State: the utility's own (`tenants.state` as a code, `TX`), only into an EMPTY box and only when the request gives
   none.** Served beside the applicant's words (`utility_state`), never into `address_state_as_given`. A matched premises
   still wins.
4. **Taxes: *<count> · <total>% total* for THE ACCOUNT'S class.** The total is the server's (hard rule 2), now computed
   for `?classes=` (the owner's category from step 1) — a residential owner on `RES-STD` reads **2 · 2.00% total**
   (Bexar County 2.00%; the 6.25% State tax is Commercial and Industrial only). With no single figure the count stands
   alone. A flat tax is not a percentage: it is named beside the total (*· 1 flat*), never added to it. The count stays
   every tax the table lists.
5. **Discounts: by NAME** in the summary (*Autopay discount 0.50% · Municipal account 20.00% · Paperless billing
   $1.00*); the table already read names. The drawn *Paperless* / *Senior* are illustrations (B14 rule 37); the names
   are the utility's own.
6. **The account page's Co-applicant group lists the account's co-owners** under the second contact it already showed,
   with the same three facts (name, email, phone) and never an identifier. It read only `contacts`, so a co-owner saved
   by move-in — and now by New Connect — was invisible on the account. The pencil still edits the contact.
7. **A company owner's co-applicant becomes an owner or officer**, by the holder's kind, exactly as move-in decides it.
8. **Move-in's own co-owner card requires only Full name too** (its card and its server), so the ruling's *optional*
   matches move-in already; move-in is not changed by this lane.

## 2026-10-07 — FIXES FROM THE 2.560.3 END-TO-END WALK: OUR JUDGMENTS, NOT ASKED (`DEF-MET-10013`, `2.561.1`)

**Decided by lane E2E-FIXES (law 13); nothing put to the PO.** Worked case: the City answers *2670 Sequoia* with the
building's point (42.300000, -83.790000, key `…-0000`) and unit A's (42.300010, -83.790010, key `…-000A`), one parcel.
1. **A unit row is drawn *2670 Sequoia Pkwy · Unit A*** — the catalogue's existing word for a unit plus the City's own
   label, so no new string and the same words the wizard already uses for *Unit 1*.
2. **Picking the unit: the property takes the BUILDING's point (42.300000), the first unit is named *A* and takes the
   unit's own point (42.300010) and key** (hard rule 8; `BR-MET-1162`). The screen now sends the picked row's key, and
   the server's live re-check takes THAT row rather than whichever row on the parcel the City lists first.
3. **If the City sends a unit and no building row, the property gets NO point** — never the unit's, which is the
   defect. The City check fills it later.
4. **The unit's point goes only onto a unit carrying the City's label.** A clerk who renames the unit or asks for none
   gets the unit's point nowhere: unit A's point on a unit called *1* would be a claim the City never made.
5. **A pick now holds until the clerk edits the address.** It used to be dropped one render after every pick (the panel
   goes quiet once the picked address is in the box, and any quiet state cleared the parcel), so every pick was saved
   as a TYPED address marked *Not checked yet*, with the form's point. Only a City that cannot be asked clears it now.
   Not changed: the Asset map and the Work order map (PO ruling 2026-10-07).
6. **`DEF-CUS-10014` (`2.561.2`): the request autosave's starting point FOLLOWS the loaded form until the clerk first
   acts on the page (a key, a pointer, an input), then freezes.** Not an 800 ms timer, and not frozen on the very first
   render either: applying a request's values ripples through derived fields for a render or two, and a starting point
   frozen at once would send an untouched request back to itself. Measured case (walk A8 on 2.560.3): form loaded at
   2,544 ms, date typed at 3,057 ms, the timer took the typed date as the starting point at 3,349 ms, no save was sent.
   Now the keystroke at 3,057 ms freezes the starting point at the loaded date and the change is sent 0.6 s later.
7. **`DEF-PAY-10015` (`2.561.3`): a payment agent's payment reads *taken by USPayments*** — the connector's own
   name from its manifest, the spelling the Connectors screen already prints, so one provider has one name. The
   provider is read from the payment's own key (`agent|pay_uspayments:…`); a counter payment still names nobody.
8. **`DEF-PAY-10016`: a reversed payment's Cancel refusal reads *Already reversed.*, and its status cell adds the
   reason under the unchanged status** (*Cleared* · *Returned by the bank*). The status itself is not moved: a
   reversal is a new row (hard rule 4) and `reversal.py` keeps the original's status by design. One new catalogue
   string in eleven languages; three words.
9. **`DEF-INT-10018`: a partner connector's FIRST SUCCESSFUL CALL moves its status from *untested* to *working*.**
   The brief suggested deriving the header from the APIs' states; that would undo `DEF-INT-5597` (PO 2026-09-17:
   *"it should be for conenctor not for APis"*), so the connector's own status moves instead, once, on the evidence
   a test of a they-call-us connector would have given. Worked: USPayments untested → one lookup answered 200 →
   *Working*; a refused payment (400) leaves it *untested*. Only *untested* moves; a failing connector staying
   *Working* is still `DEF-INT-5598`.

## 2026-10-09 — PLANS & RATES HISTORY IN WORDS, NO DATABASE IDS: OUR JUDGMENTS, NOT ASKED (`DEF-RAT-10029`, `2.562.3`)

The PO reported, with screenshots of City of Queen West on 2.562.0: *"On These screen Internal DB Codes are shown when user click on History button view details screen; please correct them"*. B14 rule 31 (PO: *"no Databse ID on screen - that is a rule"*) decides the what; these are the how, decided here and not put back to the PO.

1. **The SERVER words the history, once, and the list and the dialog both read it** (`apps/rating/history_words.py::history_rows`). The screen used to walk the two stored payloads itself (`diffFields`), which can only ever print what the payload holds — a key and an id. Resolving names needs the database (customer classes, taxes, jurisdictions, charge codes, rate schedules, discounts, people), so the walk moved to where the names are. Worked, from the local walk: *Tier 1 · Rate: $4.24 → $4.50*, *Amount: $75.00 → $7.50*, *Discounts: None → Autopay discount*, *Tax jurisdictions: City, County, … → None*.
2. **This SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-09 judgment recorded in `RateChanges.test.tsx`** that the compliance history shows the stored strings byte for byte (`3.200000 → 3.450000`) so a regulator can match the filing. A clerk reads this screen, and the PO's report is what it looked like. Money now shows at 2 places and a unit price at up to 4 (hard rule 2 and its 2026-10-02 exception). **The byte-for-byte copy is not lost: the CSV export still carries both stored payloads and the actor id**, unchanged, for a regulator.
3. **A foreign id that cannot be resolved reads `—`, never the id**, and a last-line filter strips any uuid that reaches the words whatever branch produced it. An internal key is dropped (ids, `*_display` duplicates, `*_unavailable` markers, version counters, timestamps, the reason — it has its own column).
4. **A row stored with no "before" says *Earlier values not kept* and lists the saved values against `—`.** Not *Created*: every plan-version publish before this fix stored no before, so most such rows are a v2 or v3, and *Created* would be false. The PO's *"and 89 more"* row becomes 14 plain lines.
5. **The publish path now stores the before** (`plan_writes.new_version` reads the plan before its own writes; `publish_version` reads it before the version goes live) **and the after once the plan's terms mirror the new version** — v2's $12.00 minimum had read $10.00. Worked (test): *Minimum bill: $10.00 → $12.00*, *Taxes: None → State tax*, *Customer classes: Every customer class → Commercial, Residential*, and nothing else.
6. **Labels are English words served by the server**, the precedent `plan_reads._LABELS` already set for the plan's Audit tab; only the screen's own chrome is catalogued (four new keys, eleven languages). An empty customer-class list reads *Every customer class* (`DEF-RAT-5768`: a plan naming none is for every class); any other empty list reads *None*.
7. **Published by** names the person who applied a BULK change (the batch's actor) and is a dash for a single change — it showed the batch cell (a batch uuid or *Single change*) before. **Batch** reads *Bulk change* / *Single change*.
8. **The reason is the clerk's own sentence and is not touched.** *"The amount changed"* on the PO's row was typed on the plan-version form; it looked wrong only because the change column claimed ninety changes beside it.
9. **Found, not fixed:** the plan VERSION's own stored snapshot has the same stale-terms fault as point 5 (`DEF-RAT-10031`), which the plan's Versions tab diffs. Left for its own lane: it changes what a stored version record says.

## 2026-10-12 · FIX A BILL REVAMP — FOUR STEPS NAMED *BILLS · FIX · CHECK · SEND* (RULED), AND THE SHAPE PUT TO THE PO (RECORDED BEFORE ANY BUILD)

**Ruled.** PO, verbatim: *"Now we need to revamp bill correction"*, *"we need ot make it user friendly for user to do fix a bill"*, *"can you sue 1 word for each step and keep it meaningful"*, then *"okay with this"* on this table:

| # | Step | What the user does | Leaves the step with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Bills** | Picks one of the 3 options, picks the customer, run or price, and sees the list of bills it covers | A fixed list of bills |
| 2 | **Fix** | Picks one reason and types the correct value if one is needed (reading, rate, amount) | The old bill and the new bill side by side |
| 3 | **Check** | Reads the plain summary: what the customer owes now, whether there's a refund, the new due date | The customer's outcome understood |
| 4 | **Send** | Ticks "I checked the amounts" and presses Send for approval. The approver opens the same step and presses Approve and issue. | The case is waiting for approval, then the corrected bills go out |

**This SUPERSEDES the step labels** *What and why · The correction · What it changes · Generate and send* (`billing.fix.step.*`, built to Billing blueprint §06 p129–p144). The four-step COUNT does not change. The layout reference the PO named is the One-Time Bill redesign artifact (`claude.ai/artifact/DYnXV9VSuKxoRtXFhmFJrB`): option cards, a four-step rail, one searchable account box with an account card, collapsible panels, a sticky summary, and an "I checked the amounts" tick before the send button.

**Asked for by the PO and proposed by us; NOT yet ruled, and NOT to be built until confirmed** (the PO's standing instruction this session: *"record all the cahnges first"*):
1. **The scope options must be "unique, no overlap"** (PO: *"we need to keep this uniqie no overlap"*). Proposed: three options. **One customer** (1a one bill · 1b several months, ticked from that account's sent bills) · **One billing run** (2a whole run · 2b one service in the run · 2c one plan in the run) · **A price mistake** (From–To across all runs). This drops `cycle`, and `plan`/`service` stop being kinds of their own.
2. **Two dimensions, not one** (PO, on rate/tax/charge code listed under "A price mistake": *"this become sub type insnt it"*). The option says WHOSE bills (the Bills step) and the reason says WHAT was wrong (the Fix step). Reasons keep the three seeded classes (`correction_reasons.SEEDED_REASON_CLASSES`: re-price · credit only · reprint only), and the five routed reasons become links. Proposed per-option reason matrix: One customer, all 13 · One run, wrong rate/plan, wrong tax, missed charge, charge in error, template or language · Price mistake, wrong rate/plan, wrong tax, missed charge, charge in error. For a price mistake only, the Bills step asks for the dates AND what was wrong, so that "Bills = the final list of bills" holds for all three options.
3. Proposed: **goodwill only under One customer** · **a price mistake is re-price only** · **the price is fixed in Plans & Rates first**, never typed into the wizard.
4. **The case is opened at Send rather than at step 1's Continue.** Measured on the local demo tenant on 2026-10-12: Continue on step 1 POSTs `/corrections` (201, `pending_approval`), and re-entering the same bill is then refused by `BR-BIL-048` (*"already inside an unresolved correction case"*). So a clerk who looks and walks away leaves a case that blocks the bill.
5. **⚠ A COLLISION WITH A WRITTEN RULE, NAMED RATHER THAN ASSUMED:** the proposed "For finance" panel, which keeps the debits and credits closed on Check, meets `BR-BIL-044` (PROPOSED), whose code comment reads *"nine sections, all required, none collapsible away"*. Our recommendation: closed for the clerk, open for the approver. The approver is who `BR-BIL-044` protects (*"it is the whole of what the approver is shown"*).

## 2026-10-12 · FIX A BILL REVAMP — THE PO'S SHAPE INSTRUCTIONS ON THE MOCK-UP, IN THE ORDER GIVEN (NOT YET BUILT)

The mock-up is `claude.ai/artifact/UZVnmZQ4m3SJsh6d4L867M` (example data). Each instruction below is the PO's own, given while reviewing it. Together they supersede the shape proposed earlier the same day.

3. **Find account is a searchable dropdown** (name, account number or address). The sub-option is a **dropdown whose choices depend on the option**. PO: *"this should be drop down based on single or bulk"*.
4. **"Not done here" is a bulleted list.** Each item is a situation followed by a link to the screen that handles it.
5. **Every reason has input fields for the correct value, including the reprint reasons.** PO: *"in reprint case also - we hsould provide inputs field to make the cahnges - every case"*. A reprint shows *What changes on the page* as field · was · becomes.
6. **Re-pricing lets the user choose the plan AND the version.** The default is shown, and it can always be changed. PO: *"When we say wrong plan - you ahve to allow user to select the plan and plan version"*, and *"we can show the default , but we have to allow them to choose"*.
7. **ONE TABLE OF CORRECTIONS, NOT A COMPONENT PER KIND.** PO: *"Instead of that if we do Table array … select correct prices/rates. then user can add one otr mulitple correctiosn as per requirements - then can add rate scheudle, changrece code except base charges, taxes, disocunt etc and then say apply this to 1 or more bill"*.    | Column | Content |

   | Item | The plan, schedule, code, authority or programme |
   | Change | What happens to that item |
   | New value | The value to use |
   | Apply to | One or more of the picked bills |

   **Base charges are not a row of their own**, because they come with the plan version. The reason preloads a row: wrong rate → a plan-version row · wrong tax → a tax row · missed charge → a charge-code *Add* row · charge in error → a charge-code *Remove* row. The reading, period and theft reasons keep their own inputs, and the table sits under them for any price fix made at the same time.

Each service is its own section, with its rate type, its base charge, and its usage lines by type:

   - on-peak and off-peak lines
   - peak demand in kW
   - seasonal halves
   - a % of another service
   - flat per unit

   After the services come charge codes, discounts (programme + version), subtotal, **taxes per authority with their base**, and total. Every line shows quantity × unit price. **The rows line up across the two sides by line**, so a change of rate type shows as "—" on one side.

## 2026-10-12 · ONE-TIME BILL: THE TYPED READING BEATS A COMMITTED ONE IN THE PERIOD — WHAT HAPPENS TO THE COMMITTED ONE (`DEF-BIL-10067`, after-walk)

**Judgment (AI, lane OTB-FIX-2), applying the PO's ruling of 2026-10-12 — *"the draft is priced on the reading entered"*.** The after-walk (`05-prototype/otb-after-2026-10-12/README.md`) found the typed reading still lost: AC-2026-00012, W-9011, previous 2.9 on 31 Aug, a committed 8.0 already on file for 29 Sep, typed 4.6. Usage showed 1.7 kgal; the Rates table, step 3 and the draft priced 5.1. Metering's overlay keeps a committed read over a typed one, which is right for the move-out wizard (`DEF-CUS-5931`) and wrong here.

1. **One-time bill only, every service, split or not:** the typed reading prices the preview and the draft, counted from the dial the period opens at — 4.6 − 2.9 = **1.7 kgal**; water at $8.00 + 1.7 × $4.00 = **$14.80**, not $28.65 on 5.1. A per-entry option on metering's overlay (`KEYED_WINS_OVER_COMMITTED`); its default, and the move-out wizard, are unchanged.
2. **The draft is priced on the reading step 2's Continue SAVED** at that value (`KEYED_SAVED_ONLY`) — same two dials, same arithmetic, so the preview total equals the draft total — and names it, so issue locks the **4.6** and not the 8.0. Continue now keeps the typed value on the request (it used to clear it) and does not post it twice. A typed value that was never saved prices nothing: the draft refuses, as `DEF-BIL-8300` ruled.
3. **The committed 8.0 is not billed and not locked by this bill, and nothing here edits or voids it.** In Meter Reads it is still the reading that COUNTS for 29 Sep (BR-MET-1189: the higher-consumption sibling, 5.1 against 1.7). If the 8.0 is a mistake the clerk corrects it in Meter Reads; this bill does not decide which reading was true. Where the NEXT cycle bill opens after this one is `DEF-BIL-5270`'s anchor and was not re-checked here.
4. **A cut service shares the typed reading by days** across its parts (1.7 → 0.793333 + 0.906667, the PO's own split); a committed read inside one part is not used for this bill — kept, a typed 60 beside a committed 100 kgal part billed 160.
5. **Not covered:** a meter with time-of-use windows or a meter exchange inside the period keeps its committed read; one typed total cannot restate several registers.
| 2026-10-12 | **RATE IMPACT — ONE CAPACITY, ONE VERSION: THE GRAND TOTAL NEVER COUNTS AN ACCOUNT'S MONTH TWICE (`CR-179-BRC10`, walk of 2026-10-12).** The browser walk (`05-prototype/rate-impact-2026-10-12/walk/README.md`) modelled *Sample — Residential water (inclining tiers)* 5/8" on the version in force (2026-10-01) **and** on the older 2026-08-01 version. It got two groups holding the **same 40 accounts** and the **same billed $7,991.50**, and the grand total added both: **$35,350.50 = $19,367.50 + $7,991.50 + $7,991.50**, where the true billed figure is **$27,359.00**. The test world reproduces it in small: RI-A's $100.00 of water read **$200.00** (`revenue_now` 200.0000 for 1 account). **Why it double counted:** confirmed rule 3 (PO 2026-10-12, *"this is also correct"*) makes revenue now the SCHEDULE's billed revenue whichever version is picked, so a second version of the same capacity is the same accounts' same money again. **What the record says:** CR-179 §3 gives one group per schedule (+ version) and a grand total; the drawing (`04-inputs.png`, `05-result.png`) models every schedule on ONE version and sums distinct schedules — it draws no side-by-side alternatives. So the record does not settle a second version of one capacity, and the reading taken is the one that **can never double count: a capacity of a schedule or charge code is modelled on ONE version per run.** A row putting the same item and capacity on a second version is refused at the input — *"Row 5: one version per capacity."* (`reports.rateImpact.refusal.capacityOnTwoVersions`, eleven catalogues). Two versions of one schedule at DIFFERENT capacities stay lawful (5/8" on v3, 1" on v2) and cannot overlap, because an account is in a group only when every capacity it holds is typed for that group — worked: RI-A 5/8" on v2 $100.00 + RI-B 1" on v1 $300.00 = **$400.00**, the same as the one-version run. Comparing two versions of one capacity is two runs. **No money rule moved:** billed revenue, the flat arithmetic and every signed figure are unchanged; this only stops one run adding the same billed dollars twice. Tests: `06-backend/tests/test_cr179_rate_impact.py::test_tc_walk_one_capacity_on_two_versions_is_refused_never_counted_twice` and `…_two_versions_at_different_capacities_count_each_account_once`. | Coordinator decision (law 13 — no signed rule collides; the drawing and CR-179 §3 agree with it) | `CR-179-BRC10` |
10. **One table holds every reason.** PO: *"in the fix bill - all reason show me in following table array section - Correct prices and rates"*, and *"merge this both section - What was wrong … Correct prices and rates"*. The Fix step has ONE section, **What was wrong**:
    - Each row has the columns: *What was wrong* (every reason, grouped re-price · credit only · reprint only) · Item · Billed / change · Should be · Apply to · a bin icon to remove the row (PO: *"instead of remove action - just use icon for remove"*).
    - **There is no separate reason dropdown.** *What happens* is derived from all the rows together by `BR-BIL-042`, re-price > credit only > reprint only. So a goodwill row beside a reading row rides on the re-priced bill as a credit line.
    - *Not done here* sits under the same table.
    - Wrong rate schedule and wrong discount join the reasons as rows.
    - A reprint row lists *What changes on the page* below the table.
11. **Plan, rate and deposit are separate reasons.** PO: *"in whhat was wrong section we should keep plan are rate seperate option like wrong pla, wrong rate, wrong deposit etc"*.
    - **Wrong plan** picks a plan and its version.
    - **Wrong rate** picks a rate schedule and its version.
    - **Wrong deposit** sets the deposit amount on the bill. A deposit is held money, so it is not taxed, and it posts to customer deposits held (a liability), never to revenue.
12. **The end-to-end walk is J-FIX-TWENTY** (`08-qa/01-e2e/journeys/J-FIX-TWENTY-the-fix-a-bill-scenario-suite.md`). PO: *"all your task are correct"*. That confirms the task list, including the new `correction_case_items` table. The walk covers:

## 2026-10-12 · FIX A BILL REVAMP — FIVE JUDGMENTS THE SERVER LANE TOOK WHERE THE RULES RAN OUT (`CR-180-BRC10` B1–B10, built)
**Judgment (AI, CR-180 server lane). No signed rule moves, and no ❄️ B4/B5 figure moves: the golden suite is unchanged.** Worked on the test world, the repo's own water ladder. July register 1150 → 1200 is 50 kgal: 20.00 + 65.00 + 280.00 + base 8.00 = **$373.00**. The reading should have been 1180, which is 30 kgal: **$213.00**. The delta is **−$160.00**, posted as two entries, never one net entry: a credit note for 373.00 and a new bill for 213.00.
1. **The original's one-off charge lines are carried onto the re-priced bill at their billed figures.** A fresh gather regenerates only recurring and auto-apply codes (BR-RAT-117). A late fee, a connection charge or a deposit on the original would otherwise silently drop off a bill whose only fault was a reading. A late fee is a ❄️ B4 figure, so it is carried and never re-computed. A *charge billed in error* row removes the line it names. The legacy restatement path is unchanged.
2. **Goodwill beside a re-priced row uses the signed concession, run between the release and the new bill's issue.** That is DR write-off, CR customer credit, tax excluded (PO 2026-08-11/12). The new bill's issue then draws the credit down. Worked: 213.00 re-priced, with 10.00 goodwill, leaves 203.00 to pay. It is not a negative line on the new bill: OQ-152 allows a negative bucket only on the discount contra-revenue account, and the ruled account for a concession is write-off.
3. **A correction in a closed month posts both of its entries in the earliest open month.** This applies to the credit note (`post_credit_note_reversal`) and to the new bill (`posting_seam._book_date` for a rebill). BR-BIL-045 states it for a correction, and the one-time ruling of 2026-10-12 says *"as corrections do"*. But the ledger refuses a closed date and expects the caller to post forward, so until now no bill in a closed month could be corrected (J-FIX-TWENTY S11). Worked: July closed, both entries dated 1 Aug, and the preview names it (`posting_period` 2026-08, warning `posting_period_is_not_the_bill_period`).
4. **A *wrong discount — add* row cannot grant a discount the account is not enrolled in.** BR-RAT-069 makes the enrolment the grant and BR-RAT-110 makes the plan's binding the offer. A correction re-reads both as of the bill's service date. So an enrolment made after the bill is picked up, and a programme that does not reach the bill is refused: *enrol the account first*.
5. **A correction's posting month and new due date are derived exactly as issue will derive them.** The due date comes from the original run's bill date plus the cycle's due days, because the rebill run copies both. Worked: run bill date 1 Aug + 21 days = **22 Aug**. They are served before approval (B8, `DEF-BIL-5381`).
Also found: the legacy case loop handed `execute_credit_only` a `date` where it needs a `datetime`, so every class-C case run through `/execute` raised before writing. The argument is fixed. The loop's goodwill amount, the bill's own delta of 0.00, is reported and not changed: item cases do not take that path.

## 2026-10-13 · ⚖️ RULED: MOVE-OUT'S COMPLETE CREATES THE FINAL BILL AS A DRAFT, BEFORE THE ACCOUNT CLOSES (`DEF-CUS-10093`, option B)

**The report.** A beta user said *"bills are not yet generated during move out process"*, and the PO asked for an end-to-end move-out walk across every kind of account. The walk confirmed the report on every utility (`05-prototype/move-out-walk-2026-10-12/README.md`):
- Step 3 prices the final bill (Ana Alvarez, AC-2026-00001: **$186.36** for 1–12 Oct) but creates nothing.
- Complete then closes the account.
- After that, no bill run bills it, and One-time bill → Final refuses a closed account (`final_bill.py`: *"The final bill therefore has to be produced BEFORE the move-out writes the close"*).
- The screen's *"Billing raises it on its run"* was false. It has been removed.

The question of how step 3 should reach the real invoice was flagged on 2026-09-20 and never settled (decision log 2026-09-20, *"Two things this ruling does NOT decide"*).

**Put to the PO with three options and Ana's figure:**
- (A) a link out to One-time bill → Final, with readings typed twice and a bill that can be forgotten forever;
- (B) Complete creates the draft final bill from step 3's figures, just before the close;
- (C) Billing allows a final bill after the close.

**Ruled, verbatim: *"Go with this - I recommend B: nothing can be forgotten, readings are typed once, and the clerk still reviews the bill before it goes out."***

**What B means:**
1. Pressing **Complete** creates the final bill as a **DRAFT** through the existing engine (`final_bill.py`, BR-BIL-013), from the same readings and move-out date step 3 priced.
2. This happens in the same act as the close and **before** the close is written. If the draft cannot be created, the move-out does not complete, and the refusal is shown.
3. Ana's draft is **$186.36**, equal to step 3. The two figures must match: a test pins it.
4. The move-out screen still **issues nothing**. The drawing's p112 *"NO BILL IS ISSUED BY THIS SCREEN"* holds, because a draft is not an issued bill.
5. The clerk reviews and sends the draft from Billing. Drafts carry *Approve* / *Cancel draft* since 2.570.0. Sending a draft whose account the move-out has since closed must be ALLOWED, because the bill was raised while the account was billable. That is the only carve-out, and only for a final draft created by a move-out.
6. The completion screen names the draft (bill number and amount) and links to it.
7. Because the bill now exists, the deposit settlement, the refund of a credit and the move of a balance to the master or owner account run against it exactly as the existing move-out rules say (no write-off, 2026-10-12; no dispute hold).

**Taken here, not asked (law 13): `DEF-BIL-10095`.** A computed quantity (a prorated tier share) shows at most **2 decimals**, trailing zeros dropped: *193.5483870967741935483870968 kWh* reads **193.55 kWh**. Unit prices keep up to 4 places (2026-10-02 ruling) and amounts keep 2. Only the display changes; the stored value does not.

## 2026-10-13 · FIX A BILL (`CR-180-BRC10`) RELEASED IN 2.573.0 — THE WALK'S FIVE QUESTIONS: TWO TAKEN HERE, THREE PUT TO THE PO

The J-FIX-TWENTY walk (`05-prototype/fix-a-bill-walk-2026-10-12/README.md`) walked 19 of 20 scenarios and fixed 22 defects. It left five questions open.

**Taken here (law 13). Neither is a money rule; both follow from a rule already signed:**
- **Q3, a wrong-plan choice that bills one of the account's services at $0.** **Warn, do not refuse.** A plan that does not cover a service the account takes is sometimes the correction itself. The Fix row shows *"Water is not on this plan. It bills $0.00."* beside the choice. Built with the speed fix.
- **Q5, bulk figures that change between Send and approval.** **Refuse the approval, exactly as for one customer.** `BR-BIL-044` binds approval to the previewed artifact whatever the scope. The one-customer refusal (`DEF-BIL-10099`) is extended to bulk.

**Put to the PO (each is a money or customer-promise rule):**
1. Whether re-pricing uses schedule versions added after the bill was issued. In S15, a 0.5% tax cut raised 37 of 38 bills.
2. The due date of a corrected bill whose original due date has passed. A corrected August bill came out due 09/22/2026.
3. Whether shortening a period trims usage when no reading exists at the new start.

**Open:** `DEF-BIL-10091`. Bulk preview, Send and approval each take about 3 minutes on 38 bills, against production's 60-second request limit. The fix moves bulk pricing into a background job with progress on screen. That is an architecture choice inside approved scope, so no PO question was needed.

**⚖️ RULED 2026-10-13: the three questions put to the PO from the J-FIX-TWENTY walk (entry above).**

A correction re-prices on the price versions in force **for the bill's own service period, as they stand today**, including a version for that period that was added or changed after the bill was sent.
   - **This is what the engine already does**, so nothing changes.
   - The S15 result (a 0.5% tax cut raised 37 of 38 September bills, because electric gained 15/20 Sep versions after those bills went out) is **correct behaviour**, not a defect. The recommendation that was put to the PO (bill-date prices) is NOT adopted.
2. **The due date of a corrected bill. CONFIRMED** (PO: *"this is correct"*). The new bill is due on **the correction (issue) date plus the account's usual days to pay**. Worked: corrected on 10/13 with 20 days to pay = due **11/02/2026**. A customer is never late on a bill they have just received.
3. **Usage when a period is shortened and there is no reading on the new end date. CONFIRMED** (PO: *"this is correct"*). Usage is **shared by days**, exactly as base charges are prorated. Worked: 1–30 Sep shortened to 1–20 Sep bills 20/30 of the period's usage. The line says **"usage shared by days"**.

Items 2 and 3 are built with `DEF-BIL-10091`'s lane, because they touch the same correction files.
