## 2026-10-13 · BULK FIX A BILL RUNS IN THE BACKGROUND (`DEF-BIL-10091`) — AND THE TWO RULINGS ABOVE, BUILT

**What was slow, measured** on a copy of the demo database (PostgreSQL 16), the September run re-opened to its S15 state, 48 bills, *Local tax 2% → 1.5%*:

| Step | Before | After (request) | After (background job) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preview | 190.1 s (182.7 s on a first run) | 0.05 s | 19.5 s |
| Send | 182.1 s | 0.02 s | 0.15 s |
| Approve and issue | 195.0 s | 0.02 s | 32.9 s (48 issued, 0 failed) |

A production web worker is killed at 60 s, so every one of the three "before" figures was a failed request in production.

**Where the time went.** Each bill was gathered about 4.75 times (the September bills are cut at the 15 and 20 Sep electric versions), each gather asking the database about 2,000 questions, most of them identical for every bill (the same tax rows, the same tiers). And Send and approval each priced the whole run again. Judgments taken (law 13 — none is a money rule; each follows a signed rule):

1. **The bulk pass prices under the read memo the bill run and the bulk Check already use** (`seam_batch.pass_cache` + `core.batch_reads.batch`, opened per 500 bills). A memo inside one computation, never a stored answer (the `seam_batch` ruling). It is opened only on the read-only pass, never while a bill is being issued. This alone took the preview from 190 s to 19.5 s.
2. **Bulk preview, Send and Approve-and-issue are background jobs** on billing's own queue, with progress on screen (*"Working out 48 bills · 12 done"*). One customer stays in the request: measured on the same copy, 2.2 s preview, 1.7 s Send, 2.0 s approve.
3. **Send opens the case from the stored preview and prices nothing.** The figures it pins are the ones the clerk's screen was drawn from (`preview_hash`). The check that a price moved since is made ONCE, at approval (Q5 above), where it binds. A preview's per-bill rows are kept in `correction_job_bills` and paged from there (NFR-3); a clerk's older unsent previews lose their rows when they start a new one, so a 40,000-bill run does not leave 40,000 rows per keystroke.
4. **Approval prices each re-priced bill once** (writes nothing), refuses before recording the approval if a figure moved (Q5, bulk and one customer alike), and hands what it gathered to the issue, so no bill is gathered twice. At most 2,000 bills' data is kept for that; beyond it the issue gathers again (a bound on memory, never on how many bills a case holds — NFR-5).
5. **A bulk Send needs the background preview it opens from** (`preview_job_id`); without one it is refused with *"Check the bills again."* No production client sent a bulk Send without a preview.
6. **No worker running: refused, never queued into a void** (`billing.correction.noWorker`, DEF-2487's rule). A deployment running jobs eagerly (local, demo) runs them in the request as before.

**The two rulings above (items 2 and 3), built in the same change:**
- **Due date.** The rebill's run now carries the CORRECTION date as its bill date, so issue's own derivation gives *correction date + days to pay*. The preview serves the same figure from its business date. Measured on the copy: corrected 10/13 with 20 days → **due 11/02/2026**, the PO's worked figure. The CS-36 tests that asserted *"a correction buys no grace"* (the original due date) are amended to the ruling, quoted.
- **Usage shared by days.** A period shortened with no reading on its new end date bills the bill's own reading × new days ÷ old days, and the new bill's service says *"usage shared by days"*. Before, the shortened window found no reading and the bill was refused. Worked: 50 kgal over 1–31 Jul, shortened to 1–20 Jul → 32.258065 kgal → **$240.65**. A reading ON the new end date keeps its usage (1–28 Jul stays $375.61).

**Q3 (warning) built:** a Wrong plan row whose plan bills a service the old bill charged at $0.00 shows *"Water is not on this plan. It bills $0.00."* beside the row and does not refuse.

**Found and fixed on the way:** `DEF-BIL-10108` — Send had lost its transaction when `DEF-BIL-10103` put a helper between `open_at_send` and its decorator.

**Not done here, stated:** a bill cut at a mid-period price change whose period is ALSO shortened shares nothing by days (its parts are read for their own windows) — no ruling covers that combination and none is guessed.

## 2026-10-13 · RETURNING CUSTOMER AT MOVE-IN — FOUR PO RULINGS (`CR-181-BRC10`)

Put to the PO in plain English with Viktor Valdez's case (SCW-U-022, closed 17-Sep-26 with a balance; his record holds only name and phone, so today's rule can never find him). PO verbatim: *"Q1 C both; Q2 - Reopen, for the same unit only ; Q3 - give opton to use whether pay it now or carry itr - Must pay first · Carry it onto the reopened account · Clerk chooses"* and *"Q4 - keep 5 years right now"*.

1. **Q1 → C.** *Search customer ID* also shows **same name and phone** (a weaker level) and **the unit's last occupant**, each with what their accounts still owe. ⚠ **SUPERSEDES IN PART** the 2026-10-05 ruling (1) *"if match based on our logic then we say match if it is not then we dont say it"* — its *found* and *possible* stand; two levels are added below them.
2. **Q2 → reopen, same unit only.** The closed account on THIS unit may be reopened (same number, history kept); another unit gets a new account. BR-CUS-017 is unchanged.
3. **Q3 → the clerk chooses** *Must pay first* or *Carry it onto the reopened account*.
4. **Q4 → 5 years**, a tenant setting defaulting to 5 ("right now").

## 2026-10-13 · RETURNING CUSTOMER — HOW THE FOUR RULINGS WERE BUILT: NINE JUDGMENTS OF OURS (lane REOPEN, `CR-181-BRC10`; law 13, none put to the PO)

Built from the four rulings above. Worked on the PO's own case: Viktor Valdez (C-00022, record holds a name and a phone), AC-2026-00022 on SCW-U-022, closed owing **$84.20**.

1. **The two new levels, exactly.** *Same name and phone* (`name_phone`): the name and the phone both agree and nothing New Connection's Q5 counts does. *Lived here last* (`last_occupant`): the search names the move-in's unit (`unit_id`) and the name typed is the name of a customer on that unit's most recently closed account (a cancelled move-in never lived there); a name alone is enough only here, because the unit narrows it to one household. Q5's *found* and *possible* are unchanged and New Connection's own answer is unchanged. **The email the clerk types is not used:** a customer row holds no email (it lives on an account's contact), so there is nothing on file to compare. The request Approve dialog's search (`DEF-CUS-10043`, the same function) now also shows *same name and phone*; it sends no unit, so never *lived here last*.
2. **What "owes" means for *pay first* is the books' AR for the account NET of the credit Payments holds for it**, floored at $0.00 (`move_in_reopen.outstanding`). Worked: AR $84.20; an $84.20 payment the allocator cannot meet a bill with is CARRIED as credit and leaves AR at $84.20 — measured on AR alone, *pay first* could never be satisfied by paying. Net: $84.20 − $84.20 = **$0.00**, Complete opens. A negative credit (a bounced payment, OQ-132) adds to it. The search's accounts table keeps its own rule (AR, `DEF-CUS-9756`); the reopen offer shows the net figure.
3. **Reopen is an UPDATE of the account row and nothing else that is money** (hard rule 4): status back to the move-in's occupying status, `opened_at` = the move-in date, `closed_at` cleared, and the move-in's own preferences (category, sub-type, autopay, paperless, texts, exemption, eligibility). Number, currency, premises, unit and deposit register are the account's own and do not move. NEW service agreements start on the move-in date; the old ones keep their `ended_on`. The deposit and fees run through the move-in's own steps on today's unit plan, exactly as for a new account. The previous dates are kept twice: the `account.reopened` audit row's *before*, and `move_in_reopenings`.
4. **A new table, `move_in_reopenings`, not a column on `move_records`** — that row is shared by four flows and a reopen is the move-in's alone. Written once at Complete, never updated (BR-CUS-152's posture). RLS in the same migration (`customers/0083`).
5. **The guards are refused BY NAME before the transaction opens:** another unit (`customers.moveIn.reopen.otherUnit`) · not closed or a cancelled move-in (`…notClosed`) · closed before the window (`…tooOld`) · the customer linked on step 2 does not hold the account (`…otherCustomer`) · somebody occupies the unit (the existing `customers.account.unit_already_occupied`) · a move-in date on or before the day it closed (the existing BR-CUS-056 sentence — `_make_occupying` compares only with OTHER accounts, so the account's own last day is checked here). BR-CUS-017 itself is still enforced once, under the unit lock, by `_make_occupying`.
6. **The window is measured from the tenant's today**, not the move-in date, on S66 *Billing defaults* as *Reopen closed accounts within* N years (`reopen_within_years`, default **5**, range 0–50, **0 = never**). Worked: closed 31 Jan 2020, today 13 Oct 2026 → 6 years → *Closed too long ago to reopen.*; set to 10 → offered.
7. **The balance choice is asked only when something is owed (or the books cannot say).** Nothing owed → no question and nothing recorded. *Carry* → the figure at Complete is recorded ($84.20). *Pay first* → refused while owed; once paid, recorded as *pay first, $0.00*. Books unreadable → *pay first* refused (fail closed), *carry* recorded with no figure — never a $0.00 nobody derived (DEF-127).
8. **The clerk pays through Payments' own form.** *Must pay first* opens the account page's `RecordPaymentModal` on the OLD account (the same `POST /accounts/{id}/payments`), then asks the search again so the figure on screen is the ledger's. Customers writes no payment row.
9. **A reopened account keeps its people:** the contact the clerk typed fills only EMPTY fields on its primary contact (it is created only when the account holds none), and a mailing address is added only when it has none. **And the earlier move-in record keeps its own date:** `move_in_date_of` reads the record's `effective_on`, not the account's new `opened_at`, once a later move-in has reopened that account. Audit action names follow the dotted convention: `account.reopened`, `move_in.reopen_balance` (the CR's task line said `account_reopened`).

**Consequences found and filed, not fixed here:** the Move-outs list reads `accounts.closed_at`, so a reopened account's earlier move-out leaves that list (its record stays) — and cancelling a reopened move-in would close the account with its old history's dates lost. `DEF-CUS-10125` and `DEF-CUS-10126`.

*"A1 … when we get high consumption expectation is we will immedately send it high consumption alert to get in portal in app msage or warning and possible email also. plus you can show her option 1; A2 … option 1 - just say - high usage ; A3 … high conumption alert; A4 … send her Email; A5 … Option 2 Tell them as soon as the reading is flagged. - this is corerct"*

6. **A6 — not answered; our default (law 13):** "high" is the staff read-validation rule (BR-MET-020 / BR-MET-120: above 200% of normal AND above the service's absolute floor), so staff and customer always agree. Reversible.

1. **B1 — during the hold the account bills its base (standing) charge only, no usage**, by the day (the existing `vacation_hold` status, class billable-base-only).
2. **B2 — field visit optional:** the clerk ticks *Field visit needed* on approval, which raises a shut-off work order for the stop date and a turn-on work order for the restart date.
3. **B3 — minimum 10 days, maximum 12 months, both tenant settings** ("for time being"). ⚠ **Worked consequence, stated so it is not a surprise:** SR-26-0017 asks for 3 days and is therefore refused at approval under these defaults.

## 2026-10-14 · RECEIVABLES BY SERVICE: WHAT IS STILL OWED IS SHARED IN PROPORTION — INSIDE THE ALLOCATION ORDER ALREADY SET (C1 → a)

PO verbatim: *"C1 … Option (a) In proportion: the payment is shared by each service's part of the bill. Water owes $40, Sewer owes $20, total $60 ✔ do this now; coan you confirm tht we have decided the order in setting? based on actual code?"*

**What the code already decides (measured, answered to the PO):**
- **Between bills:** oldest bill first — `allocation_order`, Settings → Billing defaults, ONE value `oldest_invoice_first` (BR-PAY-010).
- **Within a bill:** by CHARGE CLASS, tenant-set — `allocation_class_order` on the same page, default **usage + base → taxes → tenant-defined class → fees** (BR-PAY-010 as amended 2026-08-11/12, BR-PAY-038; `apps/payments/allocation.py` `DEFAULT_CLASS_ORDER`). The PO's own figure: 100.58 + 8.30 + 15.00 + 5.00 = 128.88; a 120.00 payment meets 100.58, 8.30, 11.12 of the 15.00, and the late fee stays at 0.00.
- **There is no SERVICE order.** Allocation rows are kept per class per bill, never per service line — so water usage and sewer usage share one "usage + base" pot.

**So (a) is applied INSIDE that order, not instead of it (our judgment, law 13):** the class order says how much of each class is still owed; what is owed in a class is then shared across services in proportion to each service's part of that class on the bill. Worked: water 80.00 + sewer 40.00 (usage + base 120.00) + tax 8.00 + late fee 5.00 = 133.00; paid 60.00 → usage + base receives 60.00, leaving 60.00 owed = **water 40.00 + sewer 20.00**; tax 8.00 and fee 5.00 untouched. A tax or fee line that names its service follows it; one that names none is reported on its own row, never guessed onto a service. The rows foot to the ledger receivable or the report says so.

## 2026-10-14 · G2 BUILT — five calls the ruling left to us (`DEF-PAY-10140`, lane COUNTER-CODE)

1. **The next number is one past the HIGHEST on that base, never the smallest gap.** Codes are never deleted, so the two only differ if a row is written behind the service; "one past the highest" keeps the numbers in the order the tills were opened. Bianca 06:24 → `CTR-261013-BS`, 13:04 → `CTR-261013-BS-2`, Ben Sato later → `CTR-261013-BS-3`.
2. **The day in the code stays the UTC date of `opened_at`.** That is what every code ever shown was built from (rows are read back in UTC), so keeping it is what makes "no earlier code changes" true. A clerk opening after 19:00 in Houston therefore gets the NEXT day's date in the code — pre-existing, unchanged, and not this ruling's to move; noted as an open item rather than fixed silently.
3. **A system till (ACH/wire money, nobody sat at it) stores no code** and is labelled `CTR-{day}-SYS` exactly as before; one per tenant per day, so it cannot clash, and no person reaches it.
4. **The screen shows the server's own catalogue sentence for any refusal** (via the one refusal path, `refusalText`), and two refusals got their own words: *"This counter does not exist."* and *"Two counters share this code."* (the safety net, which can now only fire for rows with no stored code). Server prose (`detail`) still never reaches the screen (BR-SHL-020 r2).
5. **Two terminals choosing the same code at the same instant both succeed**: the database's unique index refuses the second INSERT and the open retries inside a savepoint (law 14), proved on PostgreSQL.
## 2026-10-14 · TEMPORARY STOP — HOW THE FOUR RULINGS WERE BUILT: TWELVE JUDGMENTS OF OURS (`CR-183-BRC10`)
Built from the PO's B1–B4 of the same day (entry above, verbatim there). Nothing below is a new ruling; each is a judgment where the rulings ran out, recorded before reporting (law 9/10). Rules minted: `BR-CUS-1120` (the temporary stop — B1, B2, B4) and `BR-CUS-1121` (the limits — B3).
1. **The hold is its own record, and the requests point at it.** Table `temporary_stops` (customers `0084`, RLS in the same file): account, stop from, restart on, reason, status (`requested → scheduled → on_hold → ended`, plus `refused` / `cancelled`), the field-visit tick and its two work-order numbers. The portal ask is `request`; *Restart my service now* is `restart_request`; a clerk's counter stop has no request. Columns on `service_requests` would have had to hold a hold that outlives its request and is ended by a second one.
2. **The type is read from that row, never from the sentence.** A portal stop ask reads *Temporary stop* on the list and the page from the moment it arrives; approval writes `outcome = temporary_stop` (or `restart_now`). Neither joins `JOB_OUTCOMES`, so the generic Approve can never offer them, and `decide_outcome` / `approve_and_raise` refuse a temporary-stop request by name (`customers.temporaryStop.useItsOwnApproval`) — the PO's SR-26-0017 report.
3. **A restart date is required to approve.** B3's maximum is a length, and a hold with no end has none; the portal still lets a customer leave it blank, and the clerk fills it in the Approve window.
4. **How the limits are measured:** days = restart date − stop date (13 Oct → 16 Oct is **3**), at least `temporary_stop_min_days` (10); the restart date no later than the stop date plus `temporary_stop_max_months` (12) calendar months; at approval the stop date may not be in the past. The clerk may change both dates in the window and what is approved is what is checked.
5. **The limits are an APPROVAL rule, not a door rule.** The portal stores any ask; refusing it at the door would leave the customer no request for a clerk to answer. SR-26-0017 therefore arrives, is typed, shows *At least 10 days.* in the window, and Approve is disabled with that reason.
6. **Ending:** *Restart now* approved, or a clerk's *End now*, sets the restart date to today and the account is active from today (B4: *"billing returns to normal from that day"*). A hold not yet started, or started today, is **cancelled** instead — no day was spent on hold.
7. **The clock** is `apply_due`, run hourly per utility by the beat entry `customers.temporary_stop_clock` (the cut-date watch's fan-out), idempotent by status; an approval or counter stop dated today moves the account at once through the same function. Each move writes `audit_log` (`account.temporary_stop_started` / `_ended` on the account, `temporary_stop.*` on the hold) and an account-history period (`attribute_history`). Only `accounts.status` moves; the account stays open and no service agreement is touched.
8. **The field visit (B2)** raises two *Disconnection/Reconnection* work orders on the account through Work's seam (`from_flows.raise_temporary_stop_visits`): source `disconnect` due the stop date and `reconnect` due the restart date. A refusal is reported, never raised (BR-WRK-055). ⚠ Moving the dates afterwards does **not** move the two work orders (open item).
9. **One live hold per account**, refused by name (`alreadyOnHold`); a hold may start only on an account whose status is in class `billable` (active).
10. **A refused restart ask changes nothing on the hold** (it runs to its own date) and frees the portal button for another ask.
11. **Billing (T5) — the class follows the days.** Measured before the fix: a June period, hold from 21 June, 412 kWh read on 28 June at $0.12, base $18.50 — the run gathered the account as `billable_base_only` (its status that day) and drafted **$18.50**; the 412 kWh × $0.12 = **$49.44** consumed on the active days was billed by nobody, because the next bill opens on this period's closing read. `billing.gather._behavior_class_for_period`: a hold covering every day of the period is base-only; a hold covering some days leaves the period billable and the meter prices the usage (the hold days add none — supply off or nobody home). The base charge runs on hold days and active days alike (B1), so `service_days` is not reduced: **$18.50 + $49.44 = $67.94**. An account a clerk set to `vacation_hold` by hand has no hold row and bills exactly as before. ⚠ A period partly on hold whose meter was NOT read meets the run's ordinary missing-read decision (estimate / hold) over the whole period (open item).
12. **The counter stop** (account page) takes the same limits; the clerk is the approver, so it starts `scheduled` with no request.
**Settings:** S66 *Billing defaults* › *Shortest temporary stop* N days (`temporary_stop_min_days`, default 10, 1–365) and *Longest temporary stop* N months (`temporary_stop_max_months`, default 12, 1–60), both `BR-CUS-1121`.
## 2026-10-14 · HIGH CONSUMPTION ALERT — HOW A1–A5 WERE BUILT: SEVEN JUDGMENTS OF OURS (`CR-182-BRC10`, lane HIGHUSE)
The PO's five rulings are the entry above. These are the places the rulings ran out and we decided (law 13), each with the figure it was checked on — Maria's water meter at `1408 Elm St · A`, twelve months averaging ~4,000 gal, then a September reading of **40,000 gal** (10×, Susan Cook's case).
1. **The alert IS the flagged reading — no alert table.** "One alert per reading" is the email's queue key (`usage_alert`, the reading's id, `email`), which the database already holds unique (hard rule 6). "Resolved when a corrected reading is no longer high" is the correction itself: it is a new head and the portal reads heads only. A second table would be a second copy that could disagree with the reading. Checked: correcting 40,000 gal to 4,100 gal removes the Home alert and writes no second email.
2. **Told once per collection.** A correction that is STILL high (40,000 → 40,010 gal) does not email again — the customer was already told about that reading; the portal shows the replacement's own flag. Checked: 1 email after the correction, not 2.
3. **"Open" means: the meter's latest reading, flagged, not yet billed.** A newer reading closes it; once billed (`mark_read_billed`, which billing's issue calls), Home shows *Your last bill is higher than usual · See why →* instead, read off the LAST bill's own frozen read ids. One Home item per meter, so a water and a gas meter both flagged draw two.
4. **Email only, and SMS removed from the SET-12 row.** The event offered `Email+SMS` (CR-009's requirement); the PO chose email (A4). An SMS toggle with no wording and no writer would be a promise (BR-NOT-018). `notifications/0022` switches the row ON for every utility whose row is still the untouched seeded default (event OFF, email OFF, no audit row for it), removes its SMS channel row, and leaves alone — and logs — any row a System Admin saved.
5. **The utility's switch governs the EMAIL, not the portal.** A1's in-app warning is the reading's own flag, not a queued message, so a utility that turns *High usage alert* off on SET-12 stops the email and Susan still sees the warning on Home and the tag on Readings. Checked: rule off → 0 emails, Home still `high_consumption`.
6. **The email is seeded in the utility's default variant only**, like every seeded class: a message goes in the utility's default language (`OQ-CUS-12619`, *"emails in English"*), and a utility publishes other languages as variants on the designer. The portal words ARE in all eleven catalogues. Existing utilities get the seeded body through the operator's door (`manage.py seed_demo --tenant <x>`, `seed_notice_templates`), as every class added since provisioning has; until then a queued alert HOLDS with the missing-template reason rather than being invented.
7. **The words on screen are kept to B14 rule 33.** Chip *High consumption alert* (A3's own words, 3); fact *Water reading on 09/30/2026: unusually high.* (6); door *See your readings*. Bill note *High usage* (A2, 2 words). Bill notice *Your last bill is higher than usual.* + *See why →* — the PO's own wording. No ratio, no "normal" figure and no threshold anywhere on screen or in the email: how the utility judges "high" is rationale.
Kept under `OQ-1164`'s *"keep all of them"*: the email is a kept document kind (`high_usage_alert`, filed under `metering`; `tenancy/0062`), so it does not HOLD forever once a provider is connected (`DEF-NOT-8450`'s fault). Staff side unchanged: *Bill as is / Investigate* is exactly as before.
## 2026-10-14 · RECEIVABLES BY SERVICE — FIVE JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULING RAN OUT (`CR-184-BRC10`, lane ARSVC, law 13)
The PO's C1 → a (the "RECEIVABLES BY SERVICE … (C1 → a)" entry) says what is owed in a class is shared across services in proportion, inside the tenant's class order. Building it met five cases the ruling does not name; each is ours to decide and is decided here, with its figure, before code depended on it.
1. **Money that recorded no class** (every allocation before `payments/0015`, credit applications, releases) is walked through the tenant's CURRENT `allocation_class_order`; a stored `allocation_classes` breakdown always wins. Worked: bill water 80.00 + sewer 40.00 + tax 8.00 + fee 5.00, 125.00 paid with no breakdown — default order owes tax 3.00 + fee 5.00; a tenant ordering fees before taxes owes tax 8.00 and fee 0.00.
2. **A bill asking something other than its lines** (budget billing, BR-BIL-072) has its class remainders scaled to what it asks, so the rows still sum to the bill. Counted on the report (`bills_shared_against_what_they_ask`).
3. **A line kind no class places** (`minimum`, `adjustment`, `discount`, `deposit` — `OQ-128` stays OPEN): an unpaid bill is owed line for line; a part-paid one is shared by plain proportion over all its lines and counted (`bills_shared_without_class_order`). Nothing is placed in a class.
4. **Rounding**: exact fractions, each share cut down to 4 dp, leftover units one at a time to the largest cut-off fraction, ties by row order (services by code, then class rows). 100.00 over three equal lines → 33.3334 + 33.3333 + 33.3333; the rows always sum to the bill exactly.
5. **A line naming no service** lands on its class's own row (*Taxes*, *Fees*, *Usage & base*, *Other charges*); a bill with no lines on *Other charges*. Never on a service.
And the ageing's Service chip (Finance → Who owes you) now counts each bill's service SHARE; a water 80.00 + electric 40.00 bill filtered to *water* reads 80.00 where it read 120.00. No B4/B5 figure and no golden test moves — this reads allocations and writes nothing.
## 2026-10-14 · G3 BUILT — CORRECTION CASE NUMBERS (`DEF-BIL-10147`), AND FIVE CALLS THE RULING DID NOT MAKE
Built as ruled: a case takes its number at Send from the tenant series **Correction case**, default `CC-{YYYY}-{000}`, editable on Settings → Numbering (the row is last in *Billing & payments*); existing cases numbered once, oldest first; a deleted series leaves the case unnumbered and never blocks. Our judgments, written down so they can be disputed here (law 13):
1. **The series restarts every January** (seeded `yearly`, the only series that is). The PO's example is `CC-2026-001`; a year in the number with a counter that never restarts would print `CC-2027-214` for the first case of 2027. A tenant switches it off on the Numbering tab. *Not shown to the PO* — on the review-ledger row's agenda with the plain-English question.
2. **The older open path is numbered too.** `bulk_corrections.open_case` (the `reason_codes` body, still served) opens a case straight into *waiting for approval*, so opening IS its Send. Both writers call `corrections.allocate_case_no` inside their own transaction.
3. **The date is the Send's business date (`as_of`)**, never a clock (BR-TEN-043); a bulk Send uses the date its preview was priced for. A Send dated into a year the series has already left is opened unnumbered with `numbering_restart_backdated` rather than refused — the ruling says a numbering gap never blocks.
4. **The backfill dates each case by `created_at` in the tenant's own timezone**, follows the sink's restart rule exactly, advances the counter, skips a tenant whose series row is gone, and is NOT reversed (a printed number is never taken back — BR-TEN-035).
5. **The absence is recorded on the audit row** (`numbering_gap` on `correction.case_sent` / `correction.case_opened`), never on screen: the three screens keep their existing words for the one case a deleted series leaves unnumbered.
**Found, not changed:** the bill page's *What happened* table draws only once a credit note or replacement exists (`hasChain`), so a case waiting for approval is not on the bill page at all — the number appears there from approval on. Reported to the coordinator rather than widened here.


## 2026-10-14 · RATE SCHEDULE EDIT: "EFFECTIVE FROM" IS PREFILLED WITH THE FIRST DAY OF NEXT MONTH; SEASONAL PRICES COME BACK ON EDIT (PO "go A")

Two defects reported on Ann Arbor's *Bryant Solar and Battery Service Pilot Rate* (seasonal, kW-DC): on Edit, step 2's *Price per kW-DC* column and the Review step were blank; and *Effective from* on Review was empty. PO verbatim on the date: *"My recommendation: A. … If the current version starts later than next month (a future-dated rate already filed), the prefill becomes the day after that start, so the server never refuses it. -correct go A"*.

1. **Effective from — prefill = the first day of next month** in the tenant's own calendar (BR-TEN-043; worked: today 10/14/2026 → **11/01/2026**), **or the day after the current version's start when that is later** (the server refuses a start on or before it). A suggestion, editable. Applies only when starting a new version from the live one; a parked draft keeps the date the clerk typed and a correction shows no dates (both unchanged, DEF-RAT-6448 / DEF-RAT-5833). *Effective to* stays blank (DEF-RAT-5833).
2. **Seasonal prices** are stored as rate lines tagged with the season's name; reopening must read each season's price from its line (the view tab already does), so step 2, Review and a no-change save keep them.
## 2026-10-14 · BALANCE TO OWNER AND THE OWNER SUMMARY — HOW D4 AND D5 WERE BUILT: TEN JUDGMENTS OF OURS (CR-185-BRC10)

Built from the two rulings above (*"LANDLORD D2–D5"*). Nothing here re-opens them; these are the places the rulings did not reach and we decided (law 13).

**D5 — the posting.**
1. **The amount is the settlement's own 2-dp shortfall** — the figure on the screen the clerk confirmed (`$1,053.78` on the walk), finalized once by B4's half-up rule. The ledger refuses a third decimal (BR-LED-025), and posting the stored 4-dp figure would make the books a second rounding site.
2. **The book date is never a clock:** the move-out day the caller states (`as_of`, the wizard's moved-out date) or, where none is stated (the move-out record states no terms), the account's own close date `accounts.closed_at`. Neither → refused by name (*"Give the move-out date first."*).
3. **One entry per departing account** — key `transfer|<tenant account>|balance_to_owner`. A re-delivery returns the first entry and writes nothing; a replay asking a DIFFERENT figure is refused rather than answered "posted". A second press of the button after it posted is refused `no_shortfall`, because the residue has moved.
4. **A refused posting refuses the whole decision** — the entry and the decision's audit row are one transaction. A decision recorded as tied back while the books did not move is exactly what `OQ-1250` kept off the screen.
5. **Source type `transfer`** — BR-REP-008's existing word and LE-1's fixture shape, so the Journal and a statement call the line *Transfer* (catalogue word added in eleven languages). The `US-LED-001` contract row *"Master-account balance transfer"* already existed; it is now cited to D5 and has a product caller.
6. **Collect and payment plan still post nothing** and say so on the decision.
7. **The consequence dialog now says the first half of the drawing — *"$186.40 moves to A-10001 now."* — and still not *"settles at zero"*,** because whether the tenant's account stands at zero depends on what else it owes.

**D4 — the report.**
8. **The owner is the customer who holds master accounts; the report is opened on ANY of their master accounts** (the account search narrowed to master accounts, in the viewer) and widened to every master account LIVE-linked to that customer. A master with no customer link shows that one property only.
9. **Sections are read from the stored bill line:** a base line that names its unit (`<unit> · <service> base charge`, the form `DEF-CUS-9050` writes) is an EMPTY UNIT; every other base, usage and minimum line is the COMMON AREAS; fees, taxes and adjustments are OTHER owner charges. `invoice_lines` stores no unit, so this is the only mark there is; it is stated in `billing.reporting.OWNER_SUMMARY_CLASSIFIED_BY`. Worked: Maple Rentals 12 Oak St $15 + $40, 40 Elm Ave $30, 9 Pine Rd $0 → **$85**.
10. **The period is the bill's ISSUE date (posting basis); only bills that stand count** (issued, paid — void and corrected are replaced by their rebills). One row per property, paged on the server; the grand total is the owner's, never the page's. Placed under Customers · Statements. *Print* is the browser's print of the viewer (no PDF renderer exists on this deployment), offered only where the report declares itself printable.


## 2026-10-14 · BALANCE TO OWNER IS POSTED AT THE MOVE-OUT COMMIT, NOT AT STEP 3 (coordinator ruling, CR-185-BRC10, fixes DEF-CUS-10152)

Engineering ruling, not a PO question — the PO ruled that the money moves AT MOVE-OUT, so moving it before the move-out exists is a defect. The first build posted at the wizard's step 3; the walk then had a move-out refused (an unrelated read rule) and the books were left with the tenant in credit by $461.57 and the owner owing $1,006.06 for a move-out that never happened.

1. **Step 3 records and previews only** (on an account still open): `posting: {posted: false, posts_at: "move_out_completion", amount, to_account_no}`; the screen says *"$400.13 moves to AC-2026-00053 at completion."*
2. **The commit posts it**: the wizard sends `shortfall_path: "transfer"` with `POST /accounts/{id}/move-out`; `services.move_out` posts the one AR→AR entry inside its own transaction, after the final bill is drafted, for what is owed then (prior balance + drafted final bill − deposit, interest and credit). A refused commit rolls the entry back; a retry posts once (one key per departing account).
3. **Our judgment where the ruling did not reach (law 13):** the coordinator's wording was *"after the final bill is issued"*; the move-out commit only DRAFTS the final bill (PO 2026-10-13, DEF-CUS-10093 — the clerk sends it from Billing), so the amount includes the drafted bill's total and the tenant's receivable reads below zero until that bill is sent. Walk: AC-2026-00043 $82.26 + $322.97 − $5.10 credit = **$400.13** posted; tenant −$317.87 until the $322.97 bill is sent, then $5.10, met by its $5.10 credit.
4. **The move-out record** (account already closed) still posts at once, dated the close — the move-out exists.
5. **No owner account at commit** refuses the whole move-out by name, exactly as step 3 refuses it. **Nothing owed at commit** posts nothing and says `nothing_owed_at_move_out`.


## 2026-10-14 · BALANCE TO OWNER MOVES ONLY MONEY THAT IS IN THE BOOKS — PENDING AT COMMIT, POSTED WHEN THE FINAL BILL IS ISSUED (coordinator ruling, CR-185-BRC10, supersedes point 3 of the entry above; DEF-CUS-10152)

Coordinator ruling, verbatim essentials: *"the transfer must move only money that is IN THE BOOKS. So: at move-out commit, record the tie-back as PENDING (amount preview shown; nothing posted)"* · *"POST the AR→AR entry when the move-out's FINAL BILL IS ISSUED … for the amount then actually owed on the closed tenant account (prior balance + the issued final bill − deposit/interest/credit applied), idempotent per departing account"* · *"If the drafted final bill is voided/deleted instead of issued, nothing posts and the tie-back stays pending (visible on the move-out record)"* · *"If the move-out drafts no final bill (nothing to bill), post at commit as now"* · *"Move-out record page (already closed, bill already issued): post at once as now."*

This replaces point 3 of the entry above, which posted the drafted bill's total at commit and left the tenant's receivable below zero (walk: AC-2026-00043 at −$317.87) until the bill was sent.

1. **A new table, `balance_tie_backs`** (customers, migration 0085, RLS FORCE), one row per departing account: `pending` → `posted` (with the journal entry and the amount) or `nothing_owed`, exactly once. It is a promise and its outcome, never a money record — the money is the journal entry it names.
2. **At commit with a drafted final bill:** row `pending`, preview = prior + drafted bill − deposit, interest and credit; NOTHING posted. The completion screen says *"$X · Moves to the owner when the final bill is sent"*.
3. **When that bill is issued** (`apps/billing/issue.py`, after the bill's own entry, its deposit legs and the credit drawdown, in its own savepoint, never raised — BR-BIL-055): billing asks customers through `billing/customers_seam.post_pending_balance_to_owner` (resolved by name, B1). Customers reads the account's AR position from the LEDGER (every payment already credited it on receipt, so the unapplied credit is NOT subtracted again — DEF-CUS-10151), finalizes to 2 dp and the ledger posts ONE entry DR AR (owner) / CR AR (tenant). Worked on the test fixture: arrears $500.00 + final bill $T − deposit $153.50 (150.00 + 3.50 interest) → tenant $0.00, owner + (346.50 + T), AR control moves only by T − 153.50.
4. **Our judgment where the ruling did not reach (law 13):** (a) the amount comes from the BOOKS after issue rather than re-running the settlement, because issue has already applied the deposit and the credit, and the settlement would subtract them a second time; (b) ANY final bill issued for the account settles a pending tie-back, not only the one drafted at commit — a voided draft followed by a fresh final bill is the same move-out's bill; (c) a draft that billing REFUSED at commit refuses the whole move-out (DEF-CUS-10093), so there is no pending-with-no-bill case at commit; (d) on the move-out record a closed account with a final draft still waiting is recorded pending too, rather than posting money that bill has not put in the books yet; once nothing waits, the record posts at once, which is how a clerk settles a tie-back whose draft was voided; (e) owed ≤ $0.00 at issue is recorded `nothing_owed` and nothing posts.
5. **Idempotent per departing account** twice over: the row moves once, and the ledger key is still `transfer|<account>|balance_to_owner`. A re-issue, a retry of the hand-off or a second final bill posts nothing new.
6. **The move-out record and the account** both read the row and show *Moves to the owner when the final bill is sent* or *Posted*, with the figure.

## 2026-10-14 · A BALANCE MOVED TO THE OWNER CARRIES THE TENANT'S BILL SHARES WITH IT; THE OWNER SUMMARY SHOWS IT AND FOOTS TO THE BOOKS; CASH CLEARS ON RECEIPT (`DEF-REP-10159`, `DEF-REP-10158`, `DEF-PAY-10157`)

Three defects from the combined walk (steps 7, 8 and 9). Each is a seam between two features that were walked apart. Nothing here re-opens a ruling: these are our calls where the rulings did not reach (law 13), each with its figure.

**1 · Receivables by service after a balance moves to the owner (`DEF-REP-10159`).** CR-185 D5 moves a departing tenant's residue to the owner as ONE journal entry, AR to AR, and touches no bill. Receivables by service (CR-184) reads open bills, so it went on naming the tenant: walk copy as at 2027-03-31, AC-2026-00044 (closed) owing **$365.21** and the owner AC-2026-00053 **$2.00**, while the books said tenant **$0.00**, owner **$367.21**.
- **Our call:** the move SETTLES the tenant's open bills **oldest due date first**, as a payment would, and whatever part of a bill it settles is owed by the OWNER instead — **with that bill's own service shares** (cut in proportion by CR-184's own rounding rule, so they foot to the cent) **and that bill's own due date**, so the owner's debt ages from when the tenant's did. Worked on the walk's figures: tenant bills $344.26 (water 200.00 + electric 144.26, due 06-30) and $20.95 (water 11.00 + sewer 9.95); $365.21 moved → tenant on no row; owner **water 211.00 · electric 144.26 · sewer 9.95** beside its own **$2.00** fee = **$367.21**, the books' figure. A part move of $100.00 takes the June bill's 200.00 : 144.26 → owner **water 58.0956 · electric 41.9044**, tenant keeps $265.21.
- **Why not a separate "Transferred" row:** the PO's C1 → a rule is that a debt is reported on the service it was billed for; a *Transferred* row would be the one debt in the report on no service, and the over-90 figure for electric would fall the day a tenant moved out.
- **Read from the journal entry, never the tie-back promise** (`ledger.reporting.balance_to_owner_moves`, book date ≤ as-of). A reversal mirror of the entry nets it away. A part of a move with no open bill left behind it (an imported balance) is on NO row and is COUNTED on the report (`balance_moved_to_owner_without_an_open_bill`), never placed on a service; the foot against the ledger states the difference as before. Moved, not created: the report's total and its foot figure do not change.
- **Not fixed here and filed:** the AR ageing (Reports › AR ageing, the dashboard tiles, Who owes you › Service) reads the same open bills in SQL and still names the tenant — `DEF-REP-10160`.

**2 · The Owner summary (`DEF-REP-10158`).** Mill Pond's summary for 10/01–11/30 read **$2.00** (one paper-fee bill) while the owner owed **$367.21**, $365.21 of it moved from AC-2026-00044 in the same period: the summary read bills only (judgment 10 of the entry above) and the move is not a bill.
- **Our call:** a fourth column, ***Moved from tenants***, per property — the balances moved onto that property's master account with a BOOK date in the period — and part of the property's total and the grand total. Mill Pond: other charges **$2.00** + moved **$365.21** = **$367.21**.
- **And it foots, or it says by how much:** a tile ***In the books*** — what the owner's accounts owe in the ledger at the end of the period — beside the grand total. Equal → nothing more is said (Mill Pond: **$367.21 = $367.21**). Different → one sentence, *"The total differs from the books."*, with both figures and the difference in the served detail; nothing is adjusted. They differ whenever something was owed before the period or something was paid in it (e.g. the owner pays the $2.00 → books $365.21, difference −$2.00), which is why the summary states the books rather than letting a reader take the grand total for the balance. The word pair is rule 34's (*In the books*).

**3 · Cash at a counter clears on receipt (`DEF-PAY-10157`).** $25.00 cash taken into CTR-261102-DW-2 on Ana (AC-2026-00001) stayed **processing**: Record a payment left *Clearing date* blank, so the server posted nothing and Ana still owed **$1,181.38**, while the Check box said *"$25.00 goes to this account. It meets the oldest bills first."*
- **The rules already answer it, so this is a fix and not a ruling:** BR-PAY-021 — clearing is *"when money is actually received"*; BR-PAY-039 — cash posts **on receipt** DR 1010 Undeposited funds / CR 1200 AR, and reconciliation later makes it cash; `counter_receipts` already clears what a counter takes *"the same minute"*; the CR-137 cancel entry says *"a cash payment at a window is cleared the same minute"*.
- **Our call:** on Record a payment and on the account's Record payment, **CASH proposes its posting date as the clearing date** (BR-PAY-033's *"pre-fill logic always, override always"*) — the clerk can change it or empty it. **Only cash.** A cheque and a money order are instruments that clear when the bank honours them (the till already stamps a cheque while it is `processing`, on purpose); card, ACH and wire settle through a processor. Those still open blank.
- **And the Check box no longer promises what will not happen:** with no clearing date it says *"It meets no bill until cleared."* instead of naming the oldest bills.
- The server is unchanged: an explicit empty clearing date is still `processing`, so an API caller and every other door behave exactly as before. Measured on a private copy, 2026-10-14, through counter CTR-261014-DW: Ana, $25.00 cash → `PY-261014-0086` **cleared** 10/14, allocated $25.00, JE-101426-0493 DR 1010 Undeposited funds / CR 1200 AR $25.00, Ana's receivable **$187.92 → $162.92** (walk evidence: `05-prototype/walk-fixes-payments-reports-2026-10-14/`).
## 2026-10-14 · A REOPENED ACCOUNT'S NEXT BILL STARTS THE DAY AFTER ITS FINAL BILL — DRAFT OR SENT (coordinator decision, engineering; fixes DEF-CUS-10154)

**The case (combined walk 2026-10-14, step 4):** Viktor Valdez, AC-2026-00022, moved out 10/12; the move-out's Complete drafted his final bill **BL-2610-000251, $205.38, 10/01–10/12** (760 kWh + 11 kgal). He came back on 10/14 and CR-181 reopened the SAME account. The October run then billed **BL-2611-000269, $292.15, 10/01–10/31**, measured from the 09/29 billed reads (1,123 kWh, 15 kgal — the 10/09 and 10/12 reads inside it). If the draft is sent, 10/01–10/12 is charged twice (~$201 of usage).

**The decision (coordinator, engineering — no signed rule or money figure moves):**

1. The final bill stays a valid bill for the earlier tenancy. The reopen does not void it and does not refuse; the clerk may still send it.
2. The reopened account's next bill period starts the **day after the final bill's period end** — **10/13–10/31** for Viktor — whether the final bill is still a draft or has been sent. Usage is measured from the final bill's own closing reads (10/12), so no day and no unit of usage is on two bills.
3. If the final draft is cancelled (Billing → Cancel draft deletes it), nothing covers those days any more and the next bill starts on its normal cycle start.

**How it is built:** one filter, `billing.selectors.billed_position_q()` — every issued bill **plus** a live move-out final draft (`bill_type='final'` carrying the `created_by_move_out` marker, `DEF-CUS-10093`) — used by all four "how far has this account been billed" reads: `runs.last_issued_window`, `runs._payload_read_ids`, `selectors.last_issued_service_period_end` and the bulk Check's prime (`batch_seams.prime_billing_history`). The Check's existing overlap rule (fixed-charge case 4, PO 2026-09-30) then shortens the account's period to the day after, and the register anchor counts up from the read the final bill named. Any other draft — a cycle run's, a One-time tab final — is still not an anchor. The move-out date guard (`last_issued_invoice_period_end`) is unchanged: it asks about documents that left the building.

**Worked on the test fixture** (`tests/test_def_cus_10154_reopen_after_final_draft.py`): opened 1 June, read 13,800 → 14,100 on the 12 June move-out (300 kWh, final draft 1–12 June), reopened 14 June, read 14,400 on 30 June. June run before: 1–30 June, **600 kWh**; after: **13–30 June, 300 kWh**, draft or sent; draft cancelled: 1–30 June, 600 kWh.

## 2026-10-15 — USAGE TAB "MONTH BY MONTH": READ ON, SOURCE, PREVIOUS / CURRENT READING AND THE HIGH/LOW CHECK (PO: "go ahead")

**Asked (PO, screenshot of ACC-02 Usage tab):** *"the table should show the rules like high consumption, low consumption also. In an column, also the read on and the source column is not showing any data … Also show previous."* Shown in chat as seven steps with a worked row; PO reply verbatim: *"go ahead"*.

**What was shown and is now ruled:**
1. The month's real read details are served off `meter_read_monthly_usage.source_read_ids` (the reads already store `read_at`, `source`/`read_method`, `prior_value`, `current_value`, `status`).
2. Columns: **Month · Usage · Previous reading · Current reading · Read on · Source · Check**. Worked row shown: *Sep 2026 · 204,207 gal · 1,240,310 · 1,444,517 · 09/28/2026 · Manual (walk-by) · High*.
3. **Check** is a chip — High (danger), Low (warning), Zero, Estimated, or OK — read from the read's own stored status.
4. An account with two or more services shows **one row per service per month** with a Service column, so each meter's date and readings stay apart (hard rule 3).
5. A month with no reading keeps *No reading* and leaves the other cells empty — not *Not recorded*.
6. A month summing several reads shows the LATEST read's date and source, plus a small *2 readings* note.
7. Tests, browser walk, release.

**Also promised, before building:** confirm why Jun and Jul 2026 both read exactly 229,537 gal on the PO's account, and whether the figures are meter readings shown as usage or one read counted twice — and tell the PO which.

Closes `DEF-CUS-5146` (Read on / Source stated absent) and `DEF-CUS-10162` (no previous/current reading, no check result).

## 2026-10-15 — AN ESTIMATE BEHIND A LATER ACTUAL READING IS NOT COUNTED TWICE (`DEF-MET-10163`; PO: "go with 1 and 3")

**Put to the PO in plain English with the worked figure:** AC-2026-00049 electric — actual 09/24 (1,200 kWh), bill-run estimate dated 09/30 (560 kWh), actual 10/06 covering 09/24–10/06 (1,200 kWh). Monthly usage showed September **1,760 kWh** and counted the 560 again inside October's 1,200. The PO's own account showed Jun and Jul both at exactly **229,537 gal** — the likely same shape (July an estimate equal to the only month on file). Options: (1) once an actual reading covers an estimate's days, the estimate stops counting in monthly usage; (2) count both and note the overlap; (3) also stop a bill run estimating days a later actual already covers. Recommended 1 + 3. **PO verbatim: *"go with 1 and 3"*.**

**Ruled:**
1. **Monthly usage** — an estimate whose days are covered by a later actual reading on the same meter/register (the actual's prior-read date is on or before the estimate's date) no longer counts in `meter_read_monthly_usage`. Worked: September 1,760 → **1,200 kWh**; October stays 1,200. The estimate row itself is NOT deleted or edited (it may be on a bill — hard rule 4); it is only left out of the monthly sum.
2. **Bill run** — a bill run does not create an estimate for a period a later actual reading on that meter already covers; it uses the actual (or skips the estimate) instead.
3. **Bills already issued are not changed.** Neither half re-prices or re-opens an issued bill.

## 2026-10-15 — DEF-MET-10163 AS BUILT: FOUR READINGS OF OURS UNDER THE "1 AND 3" RULING (lane MV10163)

The PO ruled the section above (*"go with 1 and 3"*). The rule is theirs; these readings of it are ours, written down so nobody asks again (law 13). None collides with a signed rule, none moves a ❄️ B4/B5 figure.

1. **AN ESTIMATE THE LATER ACTUAL ALREADY TRUED UP STILL COUNTS.** The ruling's test — *"the actual's prior-read date is on or before the estimate's date"* — is also true of the ordinary case: an estimate on file BEFORE the next actual is posted, where BR-MET-029's true-up writes that actual NET of the estimate and names it in `trues_up_read_ids`. There the two together equal the register difference and nothing is counted twice; dropping the estimate would lose its days. So an estimate is left out only when the covering actual did **not** true it up. Worked: 09/24 actual (3,976 → 5,176), estimate 09/30 560 kWh on file, then 10/06 read 6,376 posted → the post trues up to 640 kWh; September stays **1,760**, October **640**, total 2,400 = the register difference. The defect's case (actual on file first, estimate after) → September **1,200**, October **1,200**, total 2,400. Asserted in `tests/test_def_met_10163_covered_estimate.py`.
2. **"SAME METER / REGISTER" IS THE ASSET AND THE CHANNEL, AND ANY ACCOUNT.** The covering actual is looked for on the meter, not only within the account, because the next occupant's reading on the same meter covers the same days. When a reading is posted, the accounts holding an estimate on that meter are restated with it (`monthly_usage_service.with_estimate_holders`); a billed estimate's save restates its own account once the issue commits.
3. **"USES THE ACTUAL (OR SKIPS THE ESTIMATE)" IS BUILT AS *SKIP*, THROUGH THE RULED *BILL BASE, USAGE LATER* PATH** (PO 2026-09-30, fixed-charge case 1, option A). A covered service raises no missing-read decision; its base bills now and its usage waits for the next bill, which prices the later reading from the last reading billed. Pricing the later reading on THIS bill would move a reading dated after the period's end into the period — a new money rule nobody signed. An `estimate` answer already on file for a covered service (given before the reading arrived) is not applied. Worked: Aug 31 read 1,000; 10/06 read 1,012 posted before the September run → September bills its base and no estimate; October bills **12 kWh** — 12 billed for 12 measured (before: a clerk estimate plus the 12).
4. **HISTORY IS RESTATED BY THE EXISTING COMMAND, NOT A DATA MIGRATION** — `manage.py backfill_monthly_usage --all-tenants` (or `--tenant <subdomain>`), once after deploy, the way `DEF-871`'s history was restated. It is idempotent: an unchanged month writes nothing. Nothing about an issued bill moves (clause 3 of the ruling): estimate rows are never edited or deleted, only left out of the monthly sum.
