## 2026-10-17 — MOVE-IN ALL UNITS: HOW THE RULING WAS BUILT (lane MVIN-ALL, `DEF-CUS-10190`)

Building the two PO entries directly above. These are the judgments the code needed where the ruling's words stopped; none moves a signed figure or collides with a signed rule except where stated.

1. **A disconnected account settles through the CLOSE-OUT, not a move-out.** The ruling reads *"Disconnected ✔ via move-out first (cut reading prefilled)"*. `close_out.py` §1 is a signed PO ruling (2026-08-27, BR-CUS-430) that a cut customer is never closed by a move-out — *"to a regulator those are not the same event"* — and `services.move_out` refuses a non-occupant by name. The close-out IS this product's settlement of a cut account (final bill raised at the cut, `closed_at` = the cut date, the cut reading the last one on every meter), so the next occupant opens on the cut reading, which is what *"cut reading prefilled"* asks. Worked: Dora, cut 2026-08-01 owing $612.75 → the move-in's row says *Start close-out*; the close-out writes `closed_at` 2026-08-01 and the $612.75 stays owed on her account; the clerk lands back on the parked move-in, opening reads carried from the cut reading; the new account's move-in raises a reconnect job dated the move-in day.
2. **"Move-out in progress" is read from the draft store.** A move-out has no state on `accounts` before it commits; the one place an unfinished move-out exists is a `wizard_parks` row (`flow='move_out'`) naming the account. BR-SHL-048 (c) said a draft cannot HOLD a unit — it was about a draft blocking writes; the 2026-10-17 ruling is that the move-in refuses while one is open, so the search reads it and `services._move_in` refuses it. Pre-existing parked move-outs now show their unit as *Move-out in progress*, which is the ruling.
3. **Start move-out writes the old occupant's move-out as a DRAFT** (`POST /move-ins/handover`): move-out date = the move-in date − 1 day, a link back to the parked move-in, nothing else written. Worked: move-in 2026-10-18 → move-out draft dated 2026-10-17; the account stays Active until the clerk finishes that move-out.
4. **The leaving settles the hold and the case in EVERY move-out, not only one raised from a move-in.** A live temporary stop ends on the move-out date and its open turn-on job is cancelled (nobody is coming back to have it turned on); an open disconnect case short of the cut is stopped with a fourth, system-only reason `customer_left` (not offered in the clerk's stop modal; `stop_by_hand` still refuses it). The balance and any payment plan stay on the old account — nothing moves money.
5. **The opening reads are carried only on the way back** (`?carry=reads`): `DEF-CUS-6362` keeps an ordinary move-in's boxes empty because an untouched prefilled box records a reading nobody took; here the reading was taken minutes earlier on the move-out. Each box takes the closing reading's VALUE; its DATE is the move-in day, not the closing day — found on the walk (`DEF-CUS-10191`): the closing day's same value is the same reading, which the read door files as already recorded (BR-MET-1189), so the new account got no opening read. Worked: Priya Petrov's E-5015 closes at 5,205 on 10/16; the new account opens with 5,205 on 10/17, 0 kWh between — BR-CUS-056's *"the next day from the same reading"*.
6. **Leaving ends BOTH of a hold's jobs** (`DEF-CUS-10194`, walk W5): the shut-off and the turn-on, when still open.
7. **Pending activation includes a New Connection still waiting on approval** (`CR-162-BRC10`) in the search; the commit keeps that case's own existing refusal.
## 2026-10-17 — GAP E BUILT: A CUSTOMER SENDS THEIR OWN READING (`DEF-CWP-10175`, `US-CWP-042`) — FIVE JUDGMENTS WHERE THE SIGNED RULES RAN OUT

Built to `BR-CWP-067` / `BR-CWP-074` as ruled (no question re-asked, law 13). The screen is `CWP-035` at the drawing's own address `/:tenant/portal/usage/submit`, opened from *Send a reading* on Readings (`CWP-034`); the write is `POST /api/:tenant/portal/accounts/{id}/readings/send` (GET on the same path is the form's frame). The reading goes through Meter Reads' own stage → validate → commit, posts with source **`customer`** (the fourth value; `models.READ_SOURCES` and B2 `meter_source` stamped), and a warned figure posts with `accept_with_flag` exactly as a staff event reading does (`BR-MET-129` (1)). Worked figures from the tests: `153,040 → 153,300` on 2 Sep is received clean with **260 gal** used and `source=customer`; `+80,000` against a ~4,010 average is received **flagged** (`high`, ratio ≈ 20×) and still posts; a reader's later `153,400` makes the two consumptions **260 + 100 = 360 = 153,400 − 153,040**, so nothing is charged twice (`BR-CWP-069`).

Five judgments, ours to make and written down rather than put to the PO:
1. **An ERROR still refuses; only a WARNING is accepted-and-flagged.** `BR-CWP-070`/`074` say a failing reading is not refused. Every high/low/days/window check in this product is a WARNING and is accepted. An ERROR — a figure **below** the last one (`negative_usage`), a retired meter, a committed duplicate of a different kind — is a row the pipeline cannot post for a clerk either without a human disposition, and posting it would post a negative consumption. `US-CWP-042` TC-4 asks for exactly this (*"not silently accepted"*). The refusal is a field error on the input: *That is below your last reading.*
2. **The door refuses three things before the pipeline sees them:** a date after today, a date before the register's last reading, and an unreadable figure — each a field error tied to its box. The form's date opens on today.
3. **The meter is addressed by its meter NUMBER and named on screen by service and SERIAL** (B14 rule 31). A meter not currently assigned to the account's own unit is the same **404** as one that does not exist (`BR-CWP-010`), so a customer cannot probe a neighbour's meter numbers. Any principal holding the account in its session set may send — there is no `submit` permission in the portal's vocabulary and a reading moves no money.
4. **Self-read OFF means the Readings action is ABSENT, not held**, and both verbs of the endpoint refuse (`portal.selfRead.notOffered`) — `US-CWP-042` TC-7, `BR-CWP-093`. The old `HeldButton` and its hold rows (`holds.ts`, `unbuiltScreens.ts`) are released in the same commit.
5. **The drawing's *WHAT HAPPENS TO IT* box said *held, not billed yet* and that line is superseded by `BR-CWP-074`** — the screen says *we record it straight away* / *same rules as our readers* / *or we call if it looks odd*. **`BR-CWP-068` (lands awaiting review) is stamped SUPERSEDED** in the module's business rules. The **photo stays held** (DF-4, a signed deferral): the picker shows its sentence and there is no file input.

Not built here: a pre-send live warning (*"that is 5,900 gallons in two days"*) — the result screen states the ratio after sending instead (*That is about 19 times your usual.*), because the only honest source of that figure is the server's own validation, which runs on commit.

## 2026-10-17 — SEASONAL FLAT CHARGE (SOLAR + BATTERY): DATED PRICES ENTERED BY HAND IS ACCEPTED

**Asked (PO):** a utility bills Solar and Battery with a seasonal flat charge (Summer $75, Winter $25) plus 4% residential tax, a late fee and the balance forward; *"We do'nt wanrt to change any code or billing logic"* — show the setup from the actual code. Shown: charge codes BASE-SOL / BASE-BAT with dated "All sizes" price rows ($75 06/01–09/30, $25 10/01–05/31), a 4% residential Tax attached to the plan, capacity rate schedules (solar and battery are capacity services), the plan, and the engine order with the October 2026 worked bill ($25 × 2 services = $50.00 + tax $2.00 = $52.00, + $40.00 balance forward = $92.00). Gap shown: no REPEATING seasonal fixed charge — seasons only apply to usage-priced schedules.
**PO verbatim:** *"this is okay - user is okay with manual changes tiwce ina year"*. So the seasonal fixed charge is set by **dated price rows entered twice a year on each base code** — no build. Not a defect.
**Still open with the PO:** the late fee is calculated by `billing.late_fee.assess_late_fee_for_plan` but no step of the bill run calls it, so no bill carries a late fee (DEF-1081 / OQ-420 era); two questions put: once per late bill vs every month unpaid; payment-plan customers charged or not.

## 2026-10-17 — THE LATE FEE IS APPLIED BY THE BILL RUN, AND MAY BE FLAT OR A PERCENTAGE (PO: "we have to fix it"; "we ahve to allow flat as we wll %age")

**Shown:** the late-fee formula `billing.late_fee.assess_late_fee_for_plan` is built (BR-BIL-001 as amended: `max(min, pct × overdue)` after due date + grace, nothing under a $25.00 overdue balance; GT-8 $542.10 → **$8.13**), but **no step of the bill run calls it**, so no bill carries a late fee. Worked: September bill $100.00 due 09/21, grace to 09/26, paid 10/05 → October bill should carry **$5.00**; today it carries nothing. **PO verbatim: *"this is good - we have to fix it"*.**
**Flat late fee — PO verbatim: *"we ahve to allow flat as we wll %age"*.** Shown: a LATE code saved with amount rule *Flat* $10.00 silently yields **$0.00** (only `percent` and `min_amount` are read). Ruled: a late fee may be a **flat amount** (e.g. $10.00 whatever the overdue amount) or a **percentage with an optional minimum**; both only after due date + grace and only at ≥ $25.00 overdue. **The B4/B5 ❄️ figures do not move** — GT-8's $8.13 is the percentage path, unchanged. This adds an option beside the frozen formula rather than altering it; recorded for the human-review ledger as shown with the $10.00 / $8.13 figures.
**Two policy points, settled from the repo rather than re-asked (law 13):**
1. **Payment-plan customers** — already ruled: BR-CUS-043 / BR-BIL-073 (PO 2026-08-11, OQ-138): the plan's ARREARS are paused per the plan's own late-fee election; **the current month's bill is late-feed like anybody else's**.
2. **Frequency — ours (judgment): ONCE PER LATE BILL.** BR-PAY-017's ladder names one late-fee rung per bill (*due+3 reminder → late fee → 10-day → 5-day → 48h*); charging every month on the same unpaid bill would be a compounding penalty no signed rule names. A bill that stays unpaid is chased by the ladder, not re-fined. Changing this is one setting later if the PO asks.

**Same day, PO verbatim on frequency: *"once per billing period"*.** This SUPERSEDES point 2 above (our "once per late bill" judgment). Ruled reading: **at most ONE late fee per account per billing period** — each bill run checks the account once; if an overdue amount ≥ $25.00 is past due date + grace (by the date money arrived), one fee is added to that period's bill, computed on the overdue portion at that run. If it is still overdue at the next period's run, that period gets its own single fee. Never two fees in one period, however many bills are late. Worked: bill A $100 due 09/21 unpaid, bill B $80 due 10/21 unpaid → October run: one fee on $100 overdue = max($5, $1.50) = **$5.00**; November run: one fee on $180 overdue = max($5, $2.70) = **$5.00**.

**Same day, PO verbatim on payment plans: asked *"Should a customer on a payment plan be charged late fees?"* — *"no"*.** This SUPERSEDES the "settled from the repo" point 1 above and the late-fee clause of **BR-CUS-043 / BR-BIL-073** (PO 2026-08-11, OQ-138: *"the current month's bill is chased like anybody else's, including its late fee"*). From 2026-10-17: **an account with a LIVE payment plan is charged NO late fee** — neither on the arrears the plan spreads nor on its current month's bill — for any billing period in which the plan is live. Dunning/disconnect scope is NOT changed by this sentence (it named late fees only). Worked: Ana on a live 6-instalment plan, October bill $62 unpaid past grace → **$0.00 late fee** (was $5.00 under BR-BIL-073). The plan's per-plan late-fee election becomes moot for the fee itself. BR-CUS-043 and BR-BIL-073 to be stamped SUPERSEDED-IN-PART in the build commit.

## 2026-10-17 — READING GAPS A, F, D: FOUR JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULING DID NOT REACH (lane Assets/Reads/Billing/Work)

Built under the ruling above (`DEF-AST-10182`, `DEF-MET-10183`, `DEF-WRK-10184`), on the shared `MeterReadingEntry` (PO, same day: *"use same code components"* … *"for meter reading, date and fetch"*). Nothing below needed the PO; each is recorded so the next lane builds the same thing (law 13).

1. **Retire — the new meter's opening read date defaults to the RETIRE date and may not be after today.** Worked case: retire `M-4022` on 16 Aug 2026 naming spare `M-9101`, type `12` → the reading lands on `M-9101` dated 16 Aug; set the date to 20 Aug (after today) and the wizard and the server both refuse (*"Read date is after today."* / `assets.replacement_opening_read_future`). A forward-dated retire with an opening read must name a past date, because a reading cannot be taken on a day that has not happened. An opening read with no replacement is refused by name; a blank one records nothing. The old meter's FINAL read date stays unbounded (`DEF-MET-4974`'s reasoning is unchanged).
2. **Add reading — Fetch only on a ONE-register meter.** The head-end answers one figure per meter; on a three-register time-of-use meter it cannot be put on *On-peak* or *Off-peak* without guessing, and a reading filed against the wrong register is permanent (MR-25, `DEF-797`'s 412 kW billed as 14 kWh). A multi-register meter is typed exactly as before, with ONE date for the visit drawn on the first register.
3. **One-time bill step 2 — the reading column now comes BEFORE its date column.** The two cells are one shared component which draws Fetch, the reading, then the date, so the headings follow that order. Fetch asks *as of* the row's read date (the bill's); a fetched reading carries the head-end's own day — 318.9 kgal read 28 Sep fills value AND date on a 30 Sep bill. A move-out's FIXED date is not moved by a fetch.
4. **Work — an accepted field reading posts under the event of WHY THE JOB WAS RAISED (the order's `source`), and three events are APPENDED to BR-MET-128's five: `reconnect`, `meter_read`, `exchange`.** Mapping (one table, `apps/work/seams/metering_seam.FIELD_READ_EVENT_BY_SOURCE`): move-out → `move_out`; move-in → `move_in`; transfer → `transfer`; disconnect and the non-pay rule → `disconnect`; reconnect → `reconnect`; new connection → `new_connect`; Reads→Work meter read → `meter_read`; Assets and the asset-age rule (meter exchanges) → `exchange`; anything else (dispatcher, service request, alerts, failed outcome) → `meter_read`, never `new_connect`. Worked case: a move-out visit reads `48,221 kWh` on `E-40161` → its history tag reads *Move-out*; the same job raised by a reconnection reads *Reconnect*. The job TYPE is not used — free text a utility renames, so reading an event out of it would be guessing. There is no database CHECK on `event_context`, so no migration. The read detail now draws the event tag BR-MET-128 always promised (*"Both render on the read detail"*) and nothing drew.

## 2026-10-17 — A $0.00 CAPACITY LINE IS LEFT OFF THE BILL; MUNICIPAL SOLAR IS SETUP, NOT CODE (PO: "please start these changes")

**Shown:** solar and battery are capacity services; a utility charging a flat $25/$75 must set the per-kW rate to $0, and each bill then prints `Solar capacity 6 kW × $0.00 = $0.00` beside the real base charge. Options A accept / **B hide the $0.00 capacity line (recommended)** / C price per kW. **PO verbatim, replying to the eight-item list whose item 8 was "Hide $0.00 capacity line when the per-kW price is $0 — Waiting for your yes": *"please start these changes"*** — read as yes to B. Ruled: when a capacity line prices to exactly $0.00 because its rate is $0, it is not printed on the bill or the portal; the base charge and tax are unchanged; installed equipment must still be recorded on each unit.
**Also shown and agreed, no build:** a *Municipal Solar* rate = capacity schedule at $4.00/kW + base charge code BASE-MSOL $10.00 "All sizes" + the 4% tax → 6 kW: $24.00 + $10.00 + $1.36 = **$35.36**.
## 2026-10-17 — DEF-MET-10164 AS BUILT: FIVE JUDGMENT CALLS WHERE THE RULING WAS SILENT (lane decision, not a PO ruling)
Built to the entry above. Where the ruling did not say how, the lane chose, and each choice is recorded here so the next lane builds the same thing:
1. **A "dates-only" re-import row is judged per row: its only non-empty values are OUR number (`premise_no` / `unit_no`) and Created.** Such a row, under *Insert & update*, changes Created on the record it names and nothing else — no other column, owner, plan or number — and writes one audit row `premises.created_date_corrected` / `unit.created_date_corrected`, before `{created_at: old}` → after `{created_at: new, run_no}`, actor = the importer. Re-running the same correction writes no second row. Under *Insert* it is refused as already on file (the 2026-08-27 ruling). The three "what a new record needs" rules (`PRM.ADDRESS_REQUIRED`, `UNT.LABEL_REQUIRED`, `UNT.PARENT_PREMISE_ON_FILE`, plus `PRM.OWNER_COLUMN_EMPTY`) step aside for that row shape only; a number we never issued is still refused. A file mapping only number + Created skips the "required column unmapped" refusal. An ordinary upsert row that also carries Created corrects it too, with the same audit row. Worked: P-00082 created 10/17/2026 → file `Premise ID,Created / P-00082,07/04/1999` → Created 07/04/1999, Age 27 yrs 3 mos, `updated_at` unchanged.
2. **Created is stored as the START of that day on the utility's own clock** (`datetime.combine(day, 00:00, tenant zone)`), so the screen — which reads the instant back in the same zone — shows the same day. Worked: `03/14/1996` → `1996-03-14T00:00:00-06:00`.
3. **The export writes Created as IS-9's timestamp** (`created_at`, tenant zone with offset), and the importer reads that exact form back so an exported list round-trips. **Age is not exported**: a file keeps no today to subtract from.
4. **The Created refusals are short (B14 rule 33) and still name both sides (BR-MET-117 (2))**: `14/03/1996 is not MM/DD/YYYY.` / `Use MM/DD/YYYY.`; future: `Date is in the future.` / `Use today or an earlier date.` "Today" is the tenant's day.
5. **Age counts whole months by anniversary, clamped to the month end** (`07-frontend/src/lib/age.ts`): 31 Jan → 28 Feb is `1 mo`; 29 Feb 2024 → 28 Feb 2025 is `1 yr`; same day is `0 days`. Both the Created and the Age header send `sort=created`; on Age, ▲ therefore means oldest record first.
Also: the headers `Premise ID`, `Unit No` and `Unit ID` now auto-map to the number column (found by the walk — a `Premise ID,Created` file mapped only the date and was refused for a missing address).
## 2026-10-17 — READING GAPS C, B AND ENTER OPENING READ: FOUR JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULING RAN OUT (Accounts lane)
Built under the ruling above (`DEF-CUS-10165` / `10166` / `10167`), all three screens through ONE shared component, `features/metering/MeterReadingEntry.tsx` (PO, same day: *"use same code components"* … *"for meter reading, date and fetch"*). Our judgments, none of them a money rule:
1. **What "a lawful read date" is.** Not after the tenant's today, not before that meter's last committed reading — **the same day as the last reading is lawful** (two readings in a day happen). Held on the screen (`readDateProblem`) and on the server (`customers.services._refuse_bad_read_dates`), by row. **Only a row that carries `read_at` is checked**: a row without one still takes the flow's own date, so a parked draft from before this column commits exactly as it did. Worked case: meter M-7301 last read 08/01/2026, move-in 10/15/2026, today 10/17 → 10/12 accepted (stored 10/12), 10/30 refused *"Read date is after today."*, 07/15 refused *"Earlier than the last reading."*
2. **Mark as cut: a reading is required per meter UNLESS the clerk ticks *No access*.** `commit_cut` already has a no-read path (no `final_reads` → it cuts and bills to the last reading on file, which is what every cut did before), and a crew that cut at the curb stop without reaching the dial is real, so refusing the cut would block a lawful act; leaving every box optional would let a hurried cut post nothing silently. A ticked meter sends no row; **nothing new is stored** — no column records the tick, the absent reading is the fact.
3. **Mark as cut posts the closing readings BEFORE the cut bill** (it was after). Until today nothing sent `final_reads`, so the order was invisible; the moment the dialog takes a reading, posting it after the bill would leave the reading the clerk typed unbilled by the bill the PO ruled makes a later one unnecessary (2026-08-30, *"when we disconnect - we generate final bill at that time itself - so later bill is not required"*). Move-out already orders it this way (`DEF-CUS-10093`). Same transaction: a refused reading still refuses the whole cut. **Worked figure from the walk:** AC-2026-00003, E-5002 at 5,774 on 10/08, closing reading 5,810 on 10/12 → the cut bill BL-2610-000251 bills **1,336 kWh** (1,300 + 36); in the old order the same cut bills 1,300 and the 36 waits for a bill that, after `disconnected`, the bill run never raises.
4. **Move-in step 1 sends every opening read DATED** (`datedReadsDraft`): an untouched Read date still FOLLOWS a changed move-in date on screen (deferred as `""`), and at commit it is sent as the date the box showed, so the server bounds what the clerk saw rather than filling a default it does not check. An emptied box is its own value (`READ_DATE_CLEARED`) and holds Continue — *Enter the read date.*

## 2026-10-17 — SOLAR/BATTERY BILL THE SUM OF INSTALLED kW; A TENANT-ADDED SIZE CARRIES ITS OWN CAPACITY (PO: "this correct , start the fix")

**Reported (PO, Ann Arbor Sustainable Energy):** a Municipal Solar rate at $14 per kW, size `SOL -P47.84 · Solar Panal 47.84` added under Settings, two PV assets (47.84 and SOL-P10) on one unit; the draft billed **2 KW @ $14.00 = $28.00**. Expected the sum of kW × rate.
**Investigated (code):** `billing/stages/measure_consumption.bills_installed_capacity` sums kW only when the tariff's `billed_unit` equals the service's `capacity_uom` EXACTLY; the rate's unit is saved as `KW` (draft prints "2 KW"), so it fell to the COUNT of assets. Second cause: kW per size comes only from the platform's ratified ladder (`tenancy/service_size_classes.py`, SOL-P1…P10, BAT-…); a tenant-added `MeterSizeClass` has code + name and NO capacity, so its kW is unknown and the bill would be refused ("equipment not on file") once the unit matched.
**PO, verbatim:** *"you ahve to count capacity and not [count] of assets"*; then briefly *"dont implment decismal pint right now on capacity"*; then, **superseding that**, confirming the five-fix table that says *"enters its kW (e.g. 47.84), stored to 4 decimals"* and *"47.84 + 10 = 57.84 kW × $14 = $809.76"*: ***"this correct , start the fix"***. The latest statement governs: **decimal capacity IS in scope.**
**Ruled fixes:** (1) a tenant-added solar/battery size class carries a capacity number (kW, stored to 4 dp); built-in sizes keep their values; (2) unit matching is case-insensitive for kW/kWh-type units, or the rate form offers the unit from a list; (3) the rate form warns when a solar/battery rate is FLAT priced per kW and suggests Capacity; (4) the bill run Check names the asset whose size has no kW; (5) tests on the worked figure **47.84 + 10 = 57.84 kW × $14.00 = $809.76**, walk, release.

**Same day, PO verbatim:** *"do not hard code anything - we need to stay with logi and make logical corrections; it should able to handle dyanmic capacities and calcualte based on logic"*. Binding on the solar/battery capacity build: every size class's capacity is DATA on its row and is resolved by one generic lookup (built-in sizes seeded into the same column, not a second code path); sum-versus-count stays driven by the service's configured billing basis / capacity unit, never a list of service names; unit matching is a generic normalisation applied identically wherever units are compared; no code, number or name is special-cased for the reporting utility's 47.84 kW.
## 2026-10-17 — BUILT: THE $0.00 CAPACITY LINE IS NOT EMITTED AT ALL; FOUR JUDGMENTS MADE WHERE THE RULING STOPPED (`DEF-RAT-10210`)
Builds the entry above (option B). **Where:** engine stage 3, `06-backend/apps/rating/pricing/stages/price_usage.py` (🔒), `_without_zero_rate_installed_lines`. A new `ModelConfig.charges_per_installed_unit` property says which configs count, because the stage may not name a model (BR-RAT-044). **Worked figures, from tests and a browser walk:** solar 6 kW at $0/kW with BASE-SOL $25.00 and a 4% tax gives ONE solar line of $25.00, tax $1.00, total $26.00. Before this change the bill carried a second line, `6 kW × $0.00 = $0.00`. Municipal Solar is unchanged: 6 kW × $4.00 = $24.00 + $10.00 + $1.36 = **$35.36**. In the walk, solar 6 kW + battery 10 kW, both at $0/kW with $25.00 bases, gave $25.00 + $25.00 + $2.00 = **$52.00**, with no $0.00 line on the Charges tab, the bill as sent, the PDF or the portal.
Four judgments, each ours to make under law 13:
1. **The engine, not the screens.** Every surface reads what stage 3 emits: the bill-run review, the one-time preview, the stored `invoice_lines`, the document and the portal. Dropping the line there means no `$0.00` row is ever written, and an export or statement nobody listed cannot print one. The line carried no money, so no total, tax base or minimum basis moves. No signed GT prices a capacity rate of zero, and golden stayed green.
2. **The RATE decides, not the amount.** A line is dropped only when its `unit_price` is exactly 0 (and its amount is 0). **0 kW at $4.00 = $0.00 still prints**, because it tells a clerk the equipment sums to zero. Equipment with no recorded size is still held before pricing (`installed_capacity_unresolved`), which keeps *"installed equipment must still be recorded on each unit"*. A line with no rate (`None`) is never dropped.
3. **Scope is the summed capacity line and the `capacity` model.** That means solar, battery, storm water or any service whose installed sizes sum (`installed_sum_line`), plus a config with a capacity spec. **Counted services (trash, fire, `per_size_line`) are out of scope:** their per-item charge is joined with the base into ONE bill line, so there is no separate $0.00 row. A METERED $0 line is not a capacity line and is emitted as before (`test_7`).
4. **Already-issued bills are not re-rendered.** Hard rule 4 leaves the rows alone, and the bill as sent stays what the customer received. A presentation filter for old bills was considered and rejected: a reprint that disagrees with the paper the customer holds is a worse failure than one $0.00 line on a past bill.
## 2026-10-17 — THE LATE FEE IN THE BILL RUN, AS BUILT: FIVE LANE JUDGMENTS WHERE THE RULINGS RAN OUT (DEF-BIL-10200, DEF-BIL-10201)
Built from the three rulings above (applied by the run; flat or percentage; once per billing period; no late fee on a live payment plan). The arithmetic is unchanged — ❄️ GT-8 is still `max($5.00, 1.5% × $542.10)` = **$8.13** through `late_fee.assess_late_fee`, called as it always was. Where the rulings did not say, the lane decided, and each is written here with its figure so it can be overruled in one sentence (law 13: none of these is a fact only the PO holds, so none was put to them).
1. **A payment that arrives before grace runs out counts as on time.** `late_fee.overdue_portion` (BR-BIL-071) credits only money that arrived on or before the DUE date, so a customer paying in full on day three of a five-day grace would still be fined at the next run — the grace would grant nothing. The ruling's own words are *"past due date + grace (by the date money arrived)"*, so the run's base is `late_fee.overdue_after_grace`: what was unpaid when grace ran out, a payment on time when grace had not elapsed on the day it arrived (the 2026-08-11 strictly-after boundary, both modes). Worked: $100.00 due 09/21, grace to 09/26 — paid **09/24 → $0.00**; paid **10/05 → $5.00** (the PO's example). `overdue_portion` itself is untouched.
2. **"Once per billing period" is measured from the account's previous bill.** A bill that went late since the account's previous bill (its grace ran out after that bill's date — the day the previous run looked) counts what was unpaid when grace ran out, even if paid since; a bill already late at the previous run counts only what is STILL unpaid. So a bill paid late is fined once, by the next run; a bill still unpaid is fined again by each later period. Worked on the ruling's own figures: A $100 due 09/21 unpaid, B $80 due 10/21 unpaid → October **$5.00** on $100, November **$5.00** on $180; A paid 10/05 → October **$5.00**, November **nothing**. An account that already holds a locked bill for this period carrying a fee on its late-fee code gets none (a second run over one period).
3. **The fee bills unless a clerk waives it — it is not a decision that holds the account.** The Check's other decisions keep an account under *Need a decision* until answered (changes row 45); the late fee is the rule the run applies, so an unanswered one bills (`decisions.DEFAULT_ANSWERS`) and the account reads Ready. Waive is per account only — *Answer for all* with Waive is refused (`set_standing_answer`, BR-BIL-003), and the screen offers no bulk control on that tag. A waiver needs no typed reason (BR-BIL-003's existing behaviour on this case, unchanged).
4. **The $25.00 floor reads a per-utility setting that has no storage yet.** OQ-157 is CLOSED (a per-utility setting, $25.00 seeded), but no settings key exists; `late_fee_run._floor` reads `late_fee_balance_floor` from Billing defaults when a utility has one and the ruled $25.00 otherwise — so every utility reads $25.00 today. Adding the key and its Settings field is a separate change, recorded in the hand-back.
5. **Disputes are not touched.** OQ-420 is OPEN (nothing records how much of a bill is disputed); BR-MET-133 clause 2 already holds a disputed account out of the run, so no disputed figure is invented.
**Flat late fee, as built:** a LATE code with amount rule *Flat* charges its flat amount for the account's class on the run's bill date (Flat $10.00 on $900.00 overdue → **$10.00**); a flat code stating no amount for the class REFUSES that account by name rather than charging $0.00; a percent penalty at 0% with no minimum is refused on the charge-code form and by the server (*"Enter a percent or a minimum."*).
## 2026-10-17 — DEF-RAT-10220 AS BUILT: ONE CAPACITY COLUMN FOR EVERY SIZE, ONE UNIT RULE AT BOTH POINTS (lane decision under the ruling above and the PO's "do not hard code anything")

**PO, verbatim, relayed by the coordinator mid-build:** *"do not hard code anything - we need to stay with logi and make logical corrections; it should able to handle dyanmic capacities and calcualte based on logic"*. Applied as: capacity is DATA on the size-class row, read generically; sum-versus-count stays configuration (`capacity_uom_for_service`); the unit match is a generic normalisation applied identically at both comparison points; tests use several capacities and a second summing service.
**Worked figure, as built and walked:** SOL-P47.84 (47.84 kW, tenant-added) + SOL-P10 (10 kW) on a FLAT $14.00-per-`KW` schedule = **57.84 kW × $14.00 = $809.76** (walk BEFORE on the base build: **2 KW × $14.00 = $28.00**). Battery in the tests: tenant sizes 3.5 kW and 120 kW + BAT-10 = **133.5 kW × $3.00 = $400.50**. Trash still **3 × $15.00 = $45.00**; fire's price list still **$60.00 + 2 × $12.00 = $84.00**.
**Judgments where the ruling ran out (each recorded so nobody re-asks):**
1. **One column for every size, built-in included.** `meter_size_classes.capacity NUMERIC(18,4) NULL`. Built-in summing sizes are SEEDED with the ratified ladder's figure (`ServiceSizeClassLookupHandler.seed`) and BACK-FILLED for existing tenants (`tenancy/0064`, frozen values, RLS-scoped per tenant). **The tenant's row wins**, for a built-in code too (SOL-P10 edited to 12 kW bills 12 kW). The ladder stays a runtime fallback ONLY where a tenant holds no row with a figure (a tenant never seeded, a test that seeds nothing) — kept because removing it would silently turn every such case into a refusal; it never overrides a row.
2. **Which services ask for a capacity is configuration, not a list:** every service whose sizes sum (`capacity_uom_for_service` set) — solar, battery (kW), thermal (ton), broadband (Mbps), storm water (ERU). The ruling named solar and battery; the other three were already summing services, so the same field appears for them. A summing size REQUIRES a capacity > 0 with at most 4 decimals; a capacity on a counted or banded size (trash, fire, water…) is refused (`settings.sizeClasses.capacityNotApplicable`) rather than silently dropped. `/settings/services` now publishes `capacity_uom` per service, and the Settings form and the rate form read it — the screen names no service.
3. **One unit rule, `core.units.same_unit`: white space and letter case are spelling, never a conversion.** Used by `bills_installed_capacity` AND by every BR-RAT-038 gate on the same pair (`normalize._gate_uom`, the capacity/TOU/demand models' re-checks), so the two points cannot disagree. Consequence beyond the ruling: a metered read in `KWH` against a tariff in `kWh` now passes the gate (it refused before). `kWh` vs `MWh` still refuses. ⚠ Case-folding makes `mW` and `MW` one key; no unit this product stores differs from another by case alone today — if one ever does, units need a real identity, not a string. The per-unit TAX check (`compute_tax`) was left exact: a different pair (a tax rule's unit), not named by the ruling.
4. **The refusal names the asset by its NUMBER** (`PV-00001: size has no capacity.`, key `billing.check.capacityUnknownAssets`) — an asset with no size, or a size with no capacity for this service, asked one code at a time through the SAME seam the total uses. It rides `GatherProblem.message_key/clerk_detail/message_params`, which the bill-run Check, the one-time bill and the move-out draft already serve (walked on the one-time bill only); the existing check code `installed_capacity_undetermined` is unchanged.
5. **The rate form warns, it does not block:** FLAT priced per the service's summing unit shows *"Priced per kW. Consider Capacity."* (two sentences ≤ 6 words, B14 rule 33). FLAT per kW still bills the summed capacity correctly. The unit picker already offers the tenant's uom list (no free text), so nothing changed there.
6. **Walk finding, filed and fixed red-first — `DEF-BIL-10221`:** the one-time bill's Services row read *"2 KW · PV-00001, PV-00002"* / *"Billed · 2 KW"* above a bill line of 57.84 kW. A summing row now carries `installed {quantity, unit}` and no count unit: *"2 assets · PV-00001, PV-00002"*, *"Billed · 57.84 kW"*.
**Ids:** the allocator offered `DEF-10185`, inside 10165–10215 held by sibling lanes, so `DEF-RAT-10220` (coordinator mapping) and `DEF-BIL-10221` (verified free with `allocate.py defect --verify`).
### 2026-10-17 — lane ACCOUNT-AGE: four engineering judgments inside the ruling above (`DEF-CUS-10180`, `DEF-CUS-10181`; ids moved from 10165/10166 on the coordinator's reservation)
Recorded before hand-back (step W). None changes a figure the PO was shown; each is where the ruling was silent.
1. **"Plus any migrated opening balance" ages an account only while that money is still owed.** Opening buckets are append-only and never shrink when paid, and OQ-530 carries the opening balance onto the account's FIRST bill. So the buckets count while (a) the account has never been billed, or (b) its first bill is still unpaid; then the older of the two dates wins. Worked: `90+` migrated 08/31/2026, first bill due 09/20 unpaid → 10/17 reads **90+ (138 days)**; the same account after that bill is paid, with a second bill due 10/07 unpaid → **Current (10 days)**, not 90+ for ever. Residue, stated: an opening-only account paid before any bill holds an unallocated credit this read does not subtract — it ages as it did before. Code: `apps/customers/selectors.ageing_anchor_expressions`; tests `test_an_older_opening_bucket_wins_over_the_first_bill`, `test_once_the_first_bill_is_paid_the_opening_money_stops_ageing`.
2. **The bill half is Who owes you's own statement, not a copy.** `payments.billing_seam._debtor_positions` was split out of `outstanding_positions_page` unchanged and is composed by the Accounts list as a correlated subquery; an undated open bill anchors on today (Current, as `outstandings.bucket_for(None)`). Test `test_the_band_is_the_same_figure_who_owes_you_uses` compares the two screens on nine boundary days.
3. **The download writes Account age as an ISO 8601 duration** (`P7Y7M`, `P4M`, `P12D`), not the screen's words: IS-9 writes machine values (`true`/`false`, never Yes/No) and the screen's words are in eleven languages. Aging is written in the filter's own spellings (`current`, `31-60`, `61-90`, `90+`) with days past due beside it.
4. **The import's Opened column reads ISO always and MM/DD/YYYY when that is the tenant's date format** — BR-MET-117 (1) forbids format sniffing, so a DD/MM/YYYY tenant's `03/01/2012` is 3 January. A future Opened date is refused per row (`ACC.OPENED_NOT_FUTURE`, "Opened date 2026-11-16 is in the future." / "Use the day it opened. Leave blank if unknown."); an unreadable one is `ACC.VALUES_PARSE`'s refusal, as before. The hidden "Since" column on the list is kept (it is the same date, column-chooser only).

## 2026-10-21 — Invoice Cloud real-time balance and immediate posting: four rulings, and "Cleared" redefined product-wide

**Context.** Invoice Cloud asked for two Partner API changes:
1. `consumer-info` returns the latest outstanding balance.
2. `make-payment` saves their payments so they apply to the bill immediately. Their request: *"Save Invoice Cloud payments as 'cleared' (pass the payment date as cleared_at) … In the API response to Invoice Cloud only, show 'cleared' as 'posted'. Inside our system, keep the status as 'cleared', not 'posted'."*

Investigated and put to the PO in plain tables:
- `consumer-info` already computes the balance live on every call: Σ issued bills' own charges + migrated opening − Σ non-`processing`, non-deposit payments (reversing rows negative) + issued/cleared refunds.
- An Invoice Cloud payment saved as `processing` never meets a bill, so it never moves that balance.
- In this product, bank reconciliation is recorded on the DEPOSIT BATCH (open → matched → reconciled), never on the payment.

**Rulings (PO, 2026-10-21, verbatim):**
1. **No Invoice Cloud payment is ever stored as `cleared` at the moment it is posted.** *"we cannot mark payment clear yet"* and *"we have to return posted and internal status also should be posted or processing"*. Invoice Cloud and our records use one word, `posted`. This **supersedes the partner's own instruction** quoted above (*"keep the status as 'cleared', not 'posted'"*).
2. **No backfill.** *"not payment record as of now; so this is not valid"*. No Invoice Cloud payment exists in `processing` on any utility today.
3. **A payment dated in a closed accounting period is accepted** (option B). *"Option B - accept it"*. The payment keeps its true payment date, which still decides late fees. Its journal entry is dated into the first open period through `close.resolve_entry_date`, the BR-TEN-038 auto-forward that `ledger/posting._refuse_if_period_closed` names as the caller's job for *"a payment that genuinely arrived late"*. The closed period is untouched.
4. **"Cleared" is redefined product-wide as "reconciled with the bank"** (option C of three). *"i will go with option C"*. A payment is `posted` when the money is taken and applied, and becomes `cleared` when its deposit batch is reconciled with the bank statement. The options shown were:
   - A: keep `cleared` = money arrived;
   - B: `posted` → `cleared` for Invoice Cloud only;
   - C: the same, for every payment.

   The PO was told C's size and that it needs a hard-rule-4 ruling.

**What these supersede, stated rather than assumed:**
- `OQ-PAY-12627` (Invoice Cloud payment `cleared` or `processing`?) is answered by neither: **`posted`**.
- The 2026-09-24 acceptance that Invoice Cloud sees our real status (`processing`) is superseded by ruling 1.
- **BR-PAY-021's clearing definition** (*"clearing = when money is actually available"*) moves to **"clearing = when the payment's deposit batch is reconciled"**. That is a signed payments rule, and it fans out to BR-PAY-021, BR-PAY-025, US-PAY-022, the payments blueprint and every document that cites them. **That fan-out is NOT done in this entry.** It travels with the build, after the open points below are ruled.

**Open, and not built until ruled (put to the PO the same day):**
- **Hard rule 4.** Today a payment row may change status only while `processing` (`trg_payment_immutable`, `payments/0014`). `posted` → `cleared` at reconciliation changes the status of a locked money row. That is a new narrowing of hard rule 4, which CLAUDE.md says only an explicit ruling may make.
- **Cheques.** Is a counter cheque `processing` until the bank confirms it, then `posted`, then `cleared` at reconciliation? Or does it go straight from `processing` to `cleared`?
- **Existing data.** What happens to payments already stored as `cleared` whose batch is not reconciled (`cleared` → `posted`)? That rewrites locked rows.
- The deposit-batch, balance and allocation reads that select `cleared` today must accept `posted`. Measured: 17 `PAYMENT_CLEARED` uses in 21 backend files, plus 9 front-end files.

## 2026-10-21 (later) — The payment lifecycle, stated by the PO for every method

Follows the entry above ("Cleared" redefined as reconciled with the bank). **PO, verbatim:** *"whether invoice cloud, or any other payment provider, or counter, or lockbox or any payment method - first they will pot the payment - so we crete the record and add posting date; then later money is recieved in the bank account ; uitlity will reconcile it bank statement that time it is cleared with clearing date; whn new bill is created and this payment is applied in the bill that time payme tis reconciled; when paymet is posted ; we need to change the opening balance formalue so that opening balance reflect the new opening balance; if payment is cancled then it will not be considered; reconciled ayment cannot be cancelled; cleared payment cannot be cancled ; in those cases refunds or credits will be issued; you will ahve to take refunds or credits into account while calcualting opening balance; we need to do what is correct"*.

**Ruled:**
1. **Every method starts the same way.** Invoice Cloud, any payment provider, counter, lockbox: the record is created **`posted`**, with its posting date. This answers the cheque question put the same day: a cheque is `posted` at entry too.
2. **`cleared`, with the clearing date, happens when the utility reconciles the bank statement** and the money is in the bank.
3. **The opening balance reflects a payment from the moment it is `posted`.** The formula changes so that `posted` payments count. Today only non-`processing` payments count, and nothing is ever written as `posted`.
4. **A `cancelled` payment is never counted.**
5. **A `cleared` payment cannot be cancelled, and neither can a reconciled one.** A refund or a credit corrects them instead.
6. **Refunds and credits are part of the opening balance.**
   - Refunds already count today: issued and cleared refunds are added back.
   - A credit note already counts as a CREDIT-type payment row (`billing/payments_seam`, `already_posted_source="credit_note"`).
   - Whether `billing.Adjustment` rows count is to be verified in the build.

**Put back to the PO the same day, because a word carries two meanings:**
- *"when new bill is created and this payment is applied in the bill that time payment is reconciled"*. Is "reconciled" a third payment status after `cleared`, or the fact that the payment appeared on a bill?
- Today a payment is applied to open bills **at posting**, which is what Invoice Cloud asked for.
- What `processing` is still for, if anything, and how a bounced (`failed`) payment is treated.

## 2026-10-21 (later still) — No "Reconciled" payment status: a payment is applied at posting; the bill cut-off case confirmed

**PO, on what "reconciled" meant:** *"it means it is applied to the bill … bill was for $80 + previous balance fo $120 = $200; this is opening balance; payment made during reporting period is $150 ; now when next bill is created you will consider $200 as opening andpayment as $150 and new opening balance is $50; when this is done Im saying reconciled; but if youa re applying the payment to last bill immediately ; then opening balance changes and taking into acount for next bill you may not required reconiled status"*.

**Shown back to the PO:** under balance forward, $200 − $150 = $50 at the next bill. Under this product, the $150 is applied the moment it is posted, the balance reads $50.00 at once, and the next bill prints previous $200 − payments since the last bill $150 = $50. Same figure, earlier.
- Counted once only: the bill counts payments posted after the previous bill was issued, or after its `payments_through` stamp.
- Which bill showed the payment is already in the bill's payload.

**Ruled:**
1. **There is no "Reconciled" payment status.** Statuses are **`posted` → `cleared`**, plus `cancelled` (only from `posted`). Refunds and credits correct a `cleared` payment.
2. **A payment is applied to open bills at posting**, for every method.
3. **The cut-off case, PO verbatim:** *"this si correct case"*. A payment posted after the bill run's cut-off but before the bill goes out shows on the following bill, while the balance drops the moment it is posted.

The "processing / failed" question of the previous entry follows from ruling 1 there (*"first they will post the payment"*):
- New payments start `posted`; `processing` is no longer written by new payments.
- A bounce after posting uses the existing reversal: a negative row that re-opens the bill.
- Existing `processing` / `failed` rows stay as they are and never count in the balance.

## 2026-10-21 — Payment application and its accounting entry under "posted at posting": confirmed unchanged

Shown to the PO from the code (`payments/allocation.py`, `payments/ledger_seam.post_payment_cleared`):
1. **Which bill first:** oldest first (default; newest first is a utility setting). **Invoice Cloud uses specific bill**: it names the bill, and anything above what that bill owes becomes account credit. A clerk may split, or carry as credit.
2. **Which charges first:** usage + base → taxes → the utility-defined class → fees last, editable per utility on Billing defaults. Worked: a $120.00 payment on a $128.88 bill pays $100.58, then $8.30, then $11.12 of the $15.00 service fee, and $0.00 of the $5.00 late fee, leaving $8.88.
3. **The entry is not split by charge type:** DR undeposited funds (or the tender's holding account) $120.00 / CR accounts receivable $120.00. Overpaying $150.00 on $128.88 gives CR AR $128.88 + CR customer credit balances $21.12.
4. **The per-charge split** is kept in the allocation rows and their per-class child rows (tax actually collected, $8.30).
5. **Bank reconciliation:** DR bank / CR undeposited, with any bank fee as its own line.
6. **What this plan changes:** only WHEN the money is applied and the entry is written (at posting rather than clearing) and the entry date (the posting date, forwarded to the first open month if closed). Order, classes, split rows and entry lines are unchanged.

**PO, verbatim:** *"as of now this is correct - if we receive any feedback from csutome weill see later"*. **Ruled:** all six stand as shown, including Invoice Cloud's specific-bill application with the excess carried as credit. Revisit only on customer feedback.

**Still open from the same thread:** batch grouping for providers.
- (A) one batch per provider per day across all tenders, which needs a narrow exception to the 2026-09-22 *"a batch is one till and one tender"* ruling;
- or (B) a system till per provider per day, with one batch per tender.

It turns on whether Invoice Cloud pays out one deposit a day or one per tender. Existing `cleared` payments (task 22) are also still open.

## 2026-10-21 — Deposit batches: one batch ID per till or per provider, per day, all tenders together (supersedes 2026-09-22's "one till and one tender")

**Shown to the PO**, after they corrected two rows of the previous table (*"this is one batch only - it will ahve 1 batch ID not 2"* for a till's cash and cheques; *"no it will be sepearte batch iD"* for Paymentus beside Invoice Cloud):

| Payments on 14 Oct | Who / where | Batch ID |
|---|---|---|
| Dana's counter: cash $300 | Dana's till | Batch 1: Dana · 14 Oct |
| Dana's counter: cheques $500 | Dana's till | Batch 1 too |
| Sam's counter: cash and cheques | Sam's till | Batch 2: Sam · 14 Oct |
| Invoice Cloud: card and bank transfer | Invoice Cloud | Batch 3: Invoice Cloud · 14 Oct |
| Paymentus: card | Paymentus | Batch 4: Paymentus · 14 Oct |
| Lockbox file | Lockbox | Batch 5: Lockbox · 14 Oct |

**PO, verbatim:** *"this is correct"*.

**Ruled:**
1. One deposit batch per day for each counter TILL, and one for each PROVIDER or CHANNEL (Invoice Cloud, Paymentus, lockbox, …). All tenders share the batch.
2. The batch ID is stamped the moment the payment is posted, for every method.
3. A batch carries a total per tender. Worked: Dana · 14 Oct = cash $300.00 + cheques $500.00 = **$800.00**.
4. Reconciling the batch moves each tender's money from its own holding account to the bank in one entry, and moves every member payment `posted` → `cleared`.

**Supersedes:** the 2026-09-22 ruling and BR-PAY-025 as amended that day, *"a batch is one till and one tender"* (keyed `(tenant, session, method)` by `payments/0033`, `uq_deposit_batches_session_method`, `deposit_batches.method` NOT NULL). The single shared SYSTEM till for non-counter money becomes a till (or batch owner) per provider or channel per day.

The schema and BR-PAY-025 fan-out travel with the build. Still open: existing `cleared` payments (task 22).

## 2026-10-21 — New World / Logos receipt XML: attributes on a `<ROOT>` document; five answers

**The defect, reported by the PO:** our generator writes every field as a child element under `<Receipts>`. New World's format, confirmed by their template and by an accepted file from another vendor, puts every field as an ATTRIBUTE on its element, under `<ROOT>`.
- `VoidedFlag` is `"0"` / `"1"`.
- The three dates are MM/DD/YYYY.
- Every attribute is always present, written `""` when empty.
- Field names, GL mapping, tender mapping, schedule and SFTP delivery do not change.
- Validate before writing to the outbox.
- Generate a new test file and flag it for a fresh SFTP test; the earlier test proved nothing about this format.

**Five questions put; PO answers verbatim:**
1. **The XSD:** *"this was only as exmaple; not required"*. No XSD is committed or validated against. **Our judgment** (the pipeline check is still required by point 6 of the report): the automated check validates against the CONFIRMED TEMPLATE the PO pasted, encoded in code. It checks:
   - the root and the element tree;
   - the exact attribute set per element, each always present;
   - `VoidedFlag` ∈ {0, 1};
   - dates MM/DD/YYYY;
   - amounts as `9,2`.

   A file that fails is never written to the outbox or served.
2. **Card fields:** *"Option A — Always write all four as `""`"*. `ReceiptPaymentCreditCardNumber`, `…CreditCardType`, `…CreditCardExpirationDate` and `…CreditCardValidationNumber` are always present and always empty. `G130` changes from "the names never appear" to "they never carry a value". This supersedes the CR-132 "NOT BUILT" posture **for the names only; card data stays out of the product**.
3. **ProjectCode1–3 at transaction level:** the PO repeated the question without choosing. **Our judgment** (law 13: decide and record): follow the confirmed template. It carries ProjectCode1–3 only on `ReceiptTransactionGLDistributionLevel`, so they are **removed from `ReceiptTransactionLevel`**. They stay empty on the distribution level, as ruled 2026-09-22.
4. **The partner receipts API:** *"Option A — Both switch: one builder, one correct shape"*.
5. **The fresh SFTP test:** *"Option B — Test with a new day that hasn't been sent yet"*. No re-send of a day already delivered, and no delivery record removed.

## 2026-10-21 — CR-186-BRC10 lane PAY-CORE: nine judgments of ours building "posted, then cleared" and the batch per till or provider (law 13; none put to the PO except item 4's question)

Built on the seven 2026-10-21 rulings above. These are the places the rulings did not reach and we decided, with the figure each was checked on.

1. **Who owns a provider's batch: a SYSTEM TILL PER (day, channel), not a key on the batch.** `counter_sessions.channel` (`payments/0051`), one till per tenant per day per channel (`uq_counter_sessions_system_day_channel`), and its ONE batch holds every tender (`deposit_batches.method` NULL, `uq_deposit_batches_session_all_tenders`). Every reader of *whose deposit is this* already walks `deposit_batches.session` (Deposits list, the bankable rule, counter screens, `trg_deposit_batch_needs_session`), so a channel reaches all of them with no second owner column to keep in step. **Worked:** 14 Oct — Invoice Cloud card $40 + ACH $60 → ONE batch $100.00; Paymentus $25.00, lockbox $10.00 and office $15.00 → three more batch IDs.
2. **The channel vocabulary.** The provider named in the idempotency reference is the channel (`webhook|invoice_cloud:TID…` → `invoice_cloud`; `agent|pay_uspayments:…` → `pay_uspayments`); a remittance file is `lockbox`; money a clerk keys in with no till (card or ACH over the phone, a move-in fee) is `office`. `record_payment(deposit_channel=…)` names one outright and wins.
3. **A payment posted for a day whose batch is already MATCHED or RECONCILED joins no batch at posting and the nightly cut puts it in the cut day's batch**, keeping its own posting date. The ruling says *"joins today's batch"*; the posting path reads no clock (BR-TEN-043, gate G6), and the cut is the one caller that knows which day today is. `matched` counts as sealed because its total is already tied to a bank line. The result carries `deposit_batch_deferred` so nothing is silent. **Worked:** Invoice Cloud 14 Oct batch reconciled 16 Oct; a $30.00 Invoice Cloud payment dated 14 Oct arrives 17 Oct → the 17 Oct cut banks it in the 17 Oct Invoice Cloud batch.
4. **UNRECONCILE STAYS AVAILABLE AND ITS MEMBERS STAY `cleared` — PUT TO THE PO AS A QUESTION, because the alternative removes a capability.** Hard rule 4's new door opens `posted` → `cleared` only, and `cleared` → `posted` is no transition the PO ruled. Refusing Unreconcile once members have cleared would remove BR-PAY-004's *"Unreconcile is the only reversal"* for every new batch. So Unreconcile re-opens the BATCH for rework (and reverses the reconciliation entry, as before), each payment keeps its first clearing date, and a re-reconcile clears only members still `posted`. **Question for the PO:** keep that, or refuse Unreconcile once its payments have cleared?
5. **A cancel is refused while the payment's batch is MATCHED** (*"Unmatch the deposit first"*), because a cancel changes a total the bank line is already tied to. In an OPEN batch the cancelled member leaves the total (`reconciliation.banked_members`): Dana's $800.00 batch with a $300.00 cash payment cancelled reads $500.00, and the reconciliation credits only the $500.00 the holding account still holds (the cancelled receipt and its mirror net to zero there).
6. **The clearing date is the reconciliation's book date** (the bank line's posting date unless a caller names one), stored as midnight in the utility's own zone (OQ-153's anchor). Each cleared payment writes `payment.cleared` to `audit_log` (hard rule 7).
7. **Credits and adjustments recorded through `record_payment` are `posted` too and never join a batch** (BR-PAY-1121 unchanged). **Account transfers' two adjustment legs and a counter receipt's attached record keep `cleared`:** neither is money taken by any method, neither has a bank leg, and as `posted` they would offer Cancel on one half of a transfer or on a record whose books were posted elsewhere.
8. **The receipt's ledger posting key keeps its event word `cleared`** (`payment|<id>|cleared`). It is an idempotency key, not a label; renaming it would let a replay across the change post a second entry.
9. **CONSEQUENCE REPORTED, NOT CHANGED: the clearing-basis reports now show a payment only after its batch is reconciled.** BR-REP-001 dates *Payments by method*, the payments dataset and the collected-tax basis by `cleared_at`; since `cleared` means reconciled, money posted today appears there days later (it is counted in their existing *posted but not yet cleared in this window* note). The Dashboard's month mix moved to the posting date. Whether those reports should move to the posting basis is the PO's, filed as a defect for the record.

Proof: `06-backend/tests/test_cr186_paycore.py`, `test_cr186_paycore_pg.py` (the trigger both ways on PostgreSQL 16). Review-ledger row CR-186-BRC10 (PAY-CORE).
10. **A cancelled move-in REFUNDS a posted payment and calls off only a legacy `processing` one** (`cancel.uncleared_payments_for_account` stays `processing`-only). A posted payment is money taken and applied; the PO's signed J6 statement of 2026-10-06 makes such money a refund request when a move-in is cancelled, exactly as it did for a cleared one. Widening the call-off to `posted` would silently cancel the $25.00 cheque Nilesh handed over instead of raising the $25.00 refund request the PO signed. Recorded the same day as items 1-9 (lane PAY-CORE).
## 2026-10-21 — lane BAL-IC (CR-186-BRC10): six engineering judgments inside the balance and Invoice Cloud rulings

Built under the seven 2026-10-21 entries above. Nothing here is a new rule; each is where the rulings ran out.

1. **The counted set is an ALLOW list in one file, `apps/payments/balance_rule.py`.** `BALANCE_COUNTED_PAYMENT_STATUSES` = `posted`, `cleared`, `reversed` (the negative row a bounce writes). Every reader used to say *"every payment except processing"*, so `failed` (a cheque voided at the counter) and `cancelled` joined the counted side with no edit near a balance (`DEF-PAY-10340`). An allow list puts a seventh status on the NOT-counted side until somebody decides here. Worked, as shown to the PO: $150.00 bill − $120.00 posted = **$30.00**; + $20.00 refund = **$50.00**; a $50.00 failed cheque used to read **$100.00** and now reads **$150.00**.
2. **The three *last payment* reads use `RECEIPT_STATUSES` (posted, cleared)** — debtors, the disconnect panel and the portal tile. The portal tile read `cleared` only; under ruling 2 (`cleared` = reconciled) every new payment would have vanished from it for days while the balance had already moved. A reversing row is not a *last payment*.
3. **S32's *taken today* tile and `unapplied_cash` use the counted set too.** Before: *taken today* excluded only processing; `unapplied_cash` counted `failed`. Both are the same set applied, not a new rule. S32's *cleared this month* method mix is NOT changed: it reads `cleared` by `cleared_at`, which now means bank-reconciled — filed `DEF-PAY-10342` rather than re-defined here.
4. **The Invoice Cloud reply carries `deposit_batch_id` and `deposit_batch_code`**, read with `getattr(..., None)` from payments' `RecordedPayment` so the door works before lane PAY-CORE publishes them; null when payments stamped none, never a guess. The ruling says *"payment number and batch ID"*; the code is the human one a partner can quote (Batch 3: Invoice Cloud · 14 Oct).
5. **The partner reference words moved with the meaning; the codes did not.** `posted` = *"Taken and applied to the account"*, `cleared` = *"Reconciled with the bank statement"*. A partner keys on the code.
6. **"Shown on bill BL-…" on the payment detail page is NOT built.** The bill's `balance_forward` payload stamps totals and an optional `payments_through` date, never the payments it counted, so which bill showed a payment is not recorded — only derivable by re-running the bill's window. Building it would be a second statement of that window. Reported to the coordinator.

**Verified, nothing to change:** `billing.Adjustment` has no writer anywhere in `apps/` (`grep "Adjustment.objects.create"` finds the model only), so no adjustment row can exist to count; a goodwill concession is a credit note, which is a credit-type payment row and is counted. If a writer is ever added, it must join the formula.

## 2026-10-21 — CR-186 combined run: an Invoice Cloud payment naming a bill already paid in full is carried as credit (our judgment)

Found by the combined PostgreSQL run of the two CR-186 lanes. A payment is now applied **at posting**, so an earlier payment can settle the named bill in full. Invoice Cloud's second genuine payment naming that bill was then refused `422`: the bill was no longer open. The partner had already taken the customer's money.

**Judgment (ours, within the PO's ruling of 2026-10-21, specific bill: *"anything above what it owes becomes account credit"*):** a bill that owes nothing takes the whole payment as account credit (`ORDER_CARRY_CREDIT`), journalled DR clearing / CR customer credit balances, and used by the next bill. That is the ruling's own arithmetic at the limit: owes $0, so everything above it is credit. Built in `integrations/seams/payments.record_partner_payment`, with a test.

Also from the same run:
- **`tests/test_cr186_balance_counts_posted_and_cleared.py` used to plant `failed` / `processing` / `cancelled` payments by UPDATEing a recorded row.** That passed only on SQLite. On PostgreSQL, `payments/0051`'s trigger (correctly) refuses a `posted` row moving to anything but `cleared` or `cancelled`.
- The helper now inserts those rows in their status, and reaches `cleared` through the one allowed move.
- The trigger was not changed.

## 2026-10-21 — Two CR-186 follow-up rulings: Unreconcile puts cleared payments back to Posted; clearing-basis reports move to the posting date

Put to the PO in plain English with a figure, answered by choosing the recommended option of each.

1. **Undoing a bank reconciliation after its payments have cleared — ALLOWED, AND THE PAYMENTS GO BACK TO `posted`.** Shown: *"A clerk reconciles the 14 Oct deposit of $800, then spots a mistake and undoes it."* PO chose *"Allow, back to Posted"* — *"Undo stays allowed and the $800 of payments go back to Posted until the batch is reconciled again. Needs one more database exception: Cleared → Posted, only through the undo."* **Supersedes PAY-CORE item 4 above** (members stayed `cleared` and kept their first clearing date). **Hard rule 4 widened a second time, and only this far:** a `cleared` payment may move to `posted`, clearing `cleared_at` back to NULL, through `payments/0052`'s fourth list (`unclearing`), read only when the old status is `cleared` and the new is `posted`, and only inside the Unreconcile service (a transaction-local setting the trigger checks). Every other column of a cleared row stays frozen; `cancelled` stays frozen; DELETE is refused in every status. A re-reconcile clears the members again with the new reconciliation's date. Each un-clear writes `payment.uncleared` to `audit_log`. **Worked:** 14 Oct batch $800 (cash $300, cheques $500) reconciled 16 Oct → all three `cleared`, cleared 16 Oct; Unreconcile → all three `posted`, no clearing date, balance unchanged at every step (posted and cleared both count); re-reconciled 17 Oct → `cleared`, cleared 17 Oct.
2. **Reports dated by clearing date move to the POSTING date.** Shown: *"a card payment taken 14 Oct and reconciled 16 Oct shows in the 16 Oct report."* PO chose *"Posting date"* — *"The 14 Oct payment appears in the 14 Oct report, the day the money was taken and applied."* Applies to *Payments by method*, the payments dataset and the collected-tax basis (`DEF-PAY-10321`), and to the S32 Payments summary method mix (`DEF-PAY-10342`, same question). They count `posted` + `cleared` by posting date. Supersedes PAY-CORE item 9's *"consequence reported, not changed"* and BR-REP-001's clearing-date basis for those reads.

## 2026-10-21 — The native field app (React Native) lives in this repo, in its own folder: twelve conflicts and how each is handled (PO: *"this is correct and i want to handle it as per your suggestion"*)

Context: the *SMART360 Next Field App* design canvas (16 architecture decisions, AD-01 React Native) is to be built in this repository, in a separate folder, with its own React Native component kit. Measured against the code on 2026-10-21 (version 2.589.0), the conflicts with the existing web app and how each is handled — ruled as a whole by the PO, verbatim above:

1. **Library versions** — `07-frontend` is React 18.3.1 / TypeScript ~5.5; React Native needs React 19. The field app gets its **own `package.json` and lockfile**; no shared npm workspace yet.
2. **Design tokens** — web tokens are CSS (`tokens.css` + the Tailwind theme). A shared `tokens.ts` becomes the one source; until the web reads it, a test fails when its values drift from `tokens.css`. The web tokens are not rewritten in the same change.
3. **Translations** — the 11 catalogues in `07-frontend/src/i18n/locales`, written through `10-scripts/i18n_fanin.py`. Field-app words carry their own `field.*` prefix or files, through the same tool; no shared key is retired without searching both apps.
4. **Version** — one product version; the field app shows it and keeps its own app-store build number. `field-app/package.json` joins `G35` and `allocate.py version`.
5. **Gates** — `10-scripts/gates/common.py` scans only `07-frontend/src` and `06-backend/apps`. The field-app source is added, each gate decides whether it applies, and each prints how many field-app files it read (law 7's blind-spot shape).
6. **Backend** — `06-backend/apps/work` is reused; new endpoints (device login, capture credential) go in their own small PRs; `openapi/schema.json` is regenerated by its tool, never hand-merged (law 5).
7. **Migrations** — one branch at a time adds migrations to a module; merge main first, renumber if it moved.
8. **Shared registers** — `allocate.py`, `file_defect.py`, `close_defect.py`, `merge_register.py`; a CR number block reserved for the field-app branch in `14-id-reservations.md`; field-app defects carry a module prefix.
9. **The existing web field app** (`07-frontend/src/features/work/mobile/`, its service worker, `FieldAppNotice`) — untouched until T-72 decides retire or fallback; `FieldAppNotice` is repointed to the app store in the change that ships the native app.
10. **Component kits** — the native kit in the field app's own `src/components`, same component names and props as the web kit, different rendering; the native type ramp (AD-08) is written into B14 before building.
11. **Signed rules** — one change request supersedes BR-WRK-045 (*"The phone is a WEB APP"*) and records the 16 decisions before any field-app code merges.
12. **Branches and builds** — a dedicated field-app branch that merges main often; only it touches the field-app folder (CODEOWNERS line); the folder stays out of the Docker build and builds with Expo/EAS.

**Not yet decided, ours to propose:** the folder's name (`field-app/` as the canvas draws it, or a numbered top-level folder beside `07-frontend`). Nothing above is built yet; this entry records the plan so the next lane follows it.
