Where the builder has no name, the account's primary contact is used, as before.
5. **`DEF-NOT-10460` closed: the PDF now reaches the provider.** The dispatcher hand-off reads the files named on the email row and passes their bytes; SMTP and Gmail send `multipart/mixed` (text + HTML first, PDF after), SendGrid and Postmark send their attachment arrays, Microsoft 365 sends a file attachment. A file that cannot be read **holds the email and retries** rather than sending it without the PDF its body promises.
6. **The agreement emails greet by first name in the languages whose greeting is informal** (en, es, es-MX, hi, fr-FR, id-ID, pt-BR): *"Hi Ada,"*, not *"Hi Okonjo, Ada,"* — found on the browser walk, where the request read *"Hi Okafor, Ade,"* while the welcome beside it read *"Welcome, Ade."*. de, it-IT, ja-JP and ko-KR keep the full name, because their greeting is the formal register. Seeded wording only; nothing is released yet, so no utility holds the old text.
## 2026-10-22 — Staff invitation link: how it was built (lane STAFF-INVITE, our judgment, recorded rather than put to the PO — law 13)

Built under `CR-188-BRC10` and the three PO rulings of 2026-10-22 above. Each of these is a choice the rulings left to us:

1. **The public address is the setting that already existed — `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN` (`DEF-CWP-9717`) — not a new one.** Answer 3 asked for *"one server setting for the product's public address"*; it was already there, typed per environment and read by `core.public_origin`. A second variable for one fact is two places to type it. The new helper is `core.public_origin.public_app_link(path, query=None)`, `None` when the setting is unset or malformed (law 3). The portal reset lane uses the same.
2. **When email cannot leave, nothing is queued and no link is minted.** A bill queued while email is off goes out later and is still true; a sign-in link would arrive expired or already replaced. So Create user asks the dispatcher's own route first and, if it says no, answers `not_sent` with the reason (no provider / sending off / status unknown / no public address / no email on the user). The user is created in every case and the on-screen password is shown, as the PO kept it.
3. **A link is void on ANY password change**, not only when a newer link is issued or the temporary password is reset. Worked case: Sam is invited Monday and signs in with the on-screen password Tuesday; without this, the Monday email would still let whoever reads Sam's mailbox set another password until the following Monday.
4. **The link's life is a Security setting, "Emailed link lasts": 1, 2, 3, 7 or 14 days, default 7** (BR-IDN-025's figure, so nobody moves). Seven matches today's temporary password; fourteen covers a hire who starts in a fortnight.
5. **Resend invitation is offered on INVITED rows only** — an active member is reset, not invited.
6. **The two emails are SET-12 events (`staff_user_invited`, `staff_password_reset`), Staff & system, email only**, so Settings → Templates reads them as *in use* and a utility can see them on Settings → Notifications. Each states its own recipient — *"Sent to the person whose sign-in it is, at their own email address."* — because BR-NOT-021's sentence (the admin who acted, plus every System Admin) is false for a sign-in link.
7. **The queue kind is `staff_access`**, with no print floor (no postal address exists for staff). The full link sits in the queued row's merge facts until it is sent, as the customer portal's reset link already does; `password_links` keeps only a SHA-256 hash. **The sent email is KEPT** (OQ-1164, entry above) under the new document kind `account_access_email` (`tenancy/0065`), and the kept copy has the link replaced by *"[one-time link removed from the kept copy]"*. The mechanism is generic: a template class names its credential tokens (`catalogs.TemplateClass.credential_tokens`) and `frozen_documents.redact_credentials` replaces their rendered values at freeze. Found by the browser walk: without a kind the invitation waited queued for ever (`DEF-IDN-10366`).
8. **Instant send** (*"this should be instant email"*): `services.send_now(message_ids)` marks the rows `priority = 100` and, on commit, enqueues one `notifications.send_now` job on the new `account_access` queue (consumer `celery-account-access`), which runs the dispatcher's own path for those rows with quiet hours skipped. A failure leaves the row queued; the ordinary cycle now claims highest priority first. Under `JOBS_EAGER=true` (local development) every job runs inline, this one included.

## 2026-10-22 — Portal password reset: what a blank box gets, what the link is, and what happens with no public address (DEF-CWP-10380, DEF-CWP-10381; lane PORTAL-RESET)

**The report (PO, 2026-10-22):** a blank email on the portal's *Forgot your password?* page was sent, answered 200 and confirmed with *"Check your inbox"*; a registered email also answered 200 and no email ever arrived, because the class `portal_password_reset` had no wording; Settings → Templates had no such template. **Reproduced on build 2.594.1 before any change:** `{"email": ""}` → `200 {"ok":true,"reason":"check_your_email"}`; `not-an-email` → the same 200; a registered address → one queue row with `template_id=None, template_version=None` and `render_context={"reset_token": …}` — no pin, so it holds at dispatch forever, and no link a person could click.

**Judgments where the rules ran out (recorded, not put to the PO — law 13):**
1. **A blank or malformed box is refused, with 400, and that discloses nothing.** BR-CWP-038 is about an ADDRESS (whether it has a login). What is refused here is what was TYPED, decided before any table is read, so a 400 says nothing about who is a customer. Keys `portal.reset.email_required` / `portal.reset.email_invalid`, on the wire and in the 11 catalogues. The screen refuses the same input without calling the API. Every well-formed address still gets the identical 200 (BR-CWP-038 stands, PO ruling of the same day); the unknown-address answer is one isolated function (`api._reset_answer_for_unknown_address`).
2. **The link** is `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN` + `/{utility}/portal/forgot-password?ref=<code row>&token=<secret>`, built by `core.public_origin.public_app_link` (the shared helper; no `PUBLIC_APP_URL` was added — the setting already existed). The forgotten-password route draws the *choose a new password* form when it carries both, and **takes them off the address bar on opening**, so the token does not sit in history. A query and not a `#fragment` because the shared helper's contract is a query; worked example: `https://app-sand.bynry.com/pine-hill/portal/forgot-password?ref=0b9…&token=Xq3…`.
3. **No public address configured → nothing is minted and nothing is queued**, one audit row `portal_credential.reset_not_sent` (*"not sent: the public address is not configured"*), and the customer sees the same 200. Minting a code without sending it would supersede the person's previous live link for one that never left the building.
4. **The tenant's password policy is checked BEFORE the link is spent.** `reset-password` used to verify (and so CONSUME) the token first: a new password one character short lost the customer their link. A policy refusal now leaves the link usable. The policy is no secret — the screen prints its minimum.
5. **Equal timing on both branches.** The unknown-address branch spends one password-hash check (`equalise_timing`); the registered branch spent none, so it answered ~100 ms FASTER. It now spends the same one. The email itself is handed to `notifications.services.send_now` (the instant send ruled the same day), which defers to commit and a background job — nothing is sent inside the request.
6. **The link's lifetime** is the utility's `SecurityPolicy.password_link_valid_days` (the staff-invite lane's setting, one setting for staff and customer links, `CR-145-BRC08`'s reasoning), read through the portal's identity seam; 7 when there is no row or the column has not landed — today's value.
7. **No SET-12 rule for it.** A reset link is asked for by the person who then waits for it; a utility able to switch it off could lock every customer out. It is sent by name (`catalogs.SENT_DIRECTLY`), and Settings shows it *in use*.
8. **Template tokens are single braces** — `{customer_name}`, `{utility_name}`, `{reset_link}` (+ `{support_phone}`, `{support_email}`, `{utility_website}`) — the product's own convention (`rendering.TOKEN_RE`), not `{{ }}`. `{reset_link}` is mandatory content in every variant. The body states **no lifetime**: that is the setting's, and a figure in wording would drift.
9. **Language:** the utility's Regional default (`OQ-CUS-12619`), resolved through the variant ladder; wording written natively for every registry language (`account_access_wording.WORDING`), `en` as the `default` variant.

**Two findings filed, not fixed here (scope):** `DEF-CWP-10382` (on *Set up your login*, a refused password shows nothing — the 422 body is not the client's refusal envelope and the test mocks a shape the wire cannot produce) and `DEF-CWP-10383` (the enrolment code email/SMS has no wording either, so no enrolment code is ever sent — the same defect as 10381 one door over).
10. **A reset email is a credential and is not frozen** (`frozen_documents.FREEZE_EXEMPT_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_TYPES = {"portal"}`). Found while proving the send: the dispatcher's freeze step HOLDS any email whose class has no ruled document kind (`FREEZE_KIND_UNRULED`), so even with wording the reset email would never have left. Freezing it instead would keep a live sign-in link write-once for years. The portal's source kind is already "not a document" (`correspondence_reads.NOT_A_DOCUMENT_SOURCE_TYPES`, `DEF-CWP-4411`). ⚠ **The staff-invite lane's `staff_access` rows meet the same hold** unless their source kind is exempted the same way — told to the coordinator.
11. **No SET-12 rule; it is a writer-reached class** (`rule_catalog.WRITER_REACHED_CLASSES`), `account_message`'s precedent: a switch that swallowed it would lock customers out while the screen said *check your email*.
12. ⚠ **ITEM 10 IS SUPERSEDED THE SAME HOUR by the coordinator's entry *"Account-access emails are KEPT like every other document, with the one-time link or code REDACTED in the kept copy"*.** The `portal` freeze exemption is withdrawn. Built instead: `portal_password_reset` → document kind `account_access` (`tenancy/0065`, `ck_stored_documents_kind` 52 → 53, filed under `notifications`); the class declares `credential_tokens = {"reset_link"}` (`catalogs.TemplateClass.credential_tokens`), and `frozen_documents.redact_credentials` replaces that value with *"[one-time link removed from the kept copy]"* in the kept copy only — the live send carries the real link. Worked figure: the kept `.eml` reads *"Choose a new password here: [one-time link removed from the kept copy]"*; its content hash is the stored document's hash.

## 2026-10-22 — CR-189 judgments: how "update your registered email" is built (lane PORTAL-EMAIL, recorded, not put to the PO)

These are build choices made inside the PO's rulings of the same day. None of them changes a signed rule.

1. **The registered email is both addresses.** When the change is confirmed, two things move together: the email the customer signs in with, and the email on the customer's contact record for every account they hold. The contact record moves through the same door the signed-in *My details* save uses. Worked case: Maria Alvarez has a login as `maria.alvarez@example.test` and one account. She confirms `maria.new@example.test`. Her sign-in, her contact email, her notice and her reset link all follow that address.
2. **No login yet: the email still changes, then the screen points to sign-up.** The contact email moves the same way and no reset link is sent, because there is no password to reset. The last screen says *"Now set up your login."* with a door to `/enrol`. Sign-up then sends its own code to a contact on file, so nothing is weakened.
3. **The new address is never stored before it is confirmed.** The confirmation code is bound to the address: the row holds a hash of the code and the address together. So the same code typed beside a different address is refused. Nothing changes until the code comes back.
4. **An address that is someone else's login gets the same answer and no code.** Refusing it on screen would tell anyone holding a bill whether that address banks online with this utility. The screen says a code was sent; no email goes out; an audit row records *"not sent: the address is another customer's portal login"*. That customer's confirmation can never succeed. If this is a real person with two logins, the office fixes it.
5. **The contacts are offered as masked options, chosen by an opaque key.** The key is a keyed hash of the destination under the server's secret and this one lookup. The browser never holds a phone number or a database id (B14 rule 31). Primary contact first, then oldest, which matches the enrolment code's choice.
6. **The lock is this form's own: five tries, then fifteen minutes.** It reuses the guest lookup's numbers (`BR-CWP-023`), keyed per utility, per form and per address. The answer to a miss is one sentence, *"We couldn't find that account."*, for every kind of miss.
7. **One proof buys one change.** Confirming retires every live code of this flow for the account.
8. **Lifetimes are the product's existing ones.** Codes last `CODE_TTL_MINUTES` (ten). The screen shows the minutes the server sends, not a typed number. The reset link is the forgot-password link, through the same issuer.
9. **The screen is `CWP-079`, at `/{tenant}/portal/update-email`.** It is CR-068 §9's next free id, allocated in the same commit.
10. **The portal's one-time code got its wording here (`DEF-CWP-10402`).** The code to a contact on file is the same message sign-up sends. It had a queue row and no template, so an emailed code never went out. It is now an Account access class, written in all 11 languages. Like the two new classes, it is kept under the `account_access_email` document kind, and `{code}` is a credential token, so the kept copy holds no live code. The text-message copy still waits for an SMS provider.

**Found while building, filed rather than fixed:**
- `DEF-CWP-10400`. The "call the office" ending says staff update the email and the customer then uses *Forgot your password?*. Today a clerk's email correction deliberately does **not** move the portal sign-in (`OQ-CUS-12350`, OPEN since 2026-09-13). So the reset at the new address finds no login and sends nothing. **This needs a PO answer to `OQ-CUS-12350`**; it was not decided here.
- `DEF-CWP-10401`. Item 2 of the forgot-password entry above says a signed-in email change is confirmed by a code to the new address. That is not built, and the 2026-09-04 ruling it cites says the opposite.

## 2026-10-22 — One-time link secrets travel in the URL FRAGMENT, not the query string; and how the three account-access lanes were merged into one design (coordinator decision; lane MERGE-ACCESS)

**The decision (coordinator, 2026-10-22, our judgment — law 13; no signed rule moves):** a one-time secret in an emailed link must not sit in the query string, because the web server, any proxy and any CDN in front of the app write the full request line, query included, to their logs, and those logs outlive the link. The part after `#` is never sent to any server by a browser. So:

1. **`core.public_origin.public_app_link(path, query=None, *, fragment=None)`.** The secret goes in `fragment` (`urlencode`d after `#`); `query` stays for anything that is not a secret. Fails closed exactly as before: no usable `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN` → `None`.
2. **The staff set-password link** (`CR-188-BRC10`) is now `https://<app>/<utility>/set-password#token=<secret>` (was `?token=`). **The customer portal's reset link** (`DEF-CWP-10381`) is now `https://<app>/<utility>/portal/forgot-password#ref=<code row>&token=<secret>` (was `?ref=…&token=…`). The reset link sent at the end of *Update your email* (`CR-189-BRC10`) is the same link from the same issuer, `credentials.send_reset`.
3. **Both pages read the fragment first, then the query, and take both off the address bar on open** (`07-frontend/src/routing/linkSecret.ts` + the hook `useLinkSecret.ts`, shared by `SetPasswordPage` and the portal's `ForgotPassword`). The secret is held in state, then history is replaced with the same path, every other query parameter kept, no fragment — so Back and a screenshot of the bar hold nothing. ⚠ **The hook re-reads on every location change, not only on mount**, because a link that differs from the open page only by its fragment does NOT reload the document: the merge walk pasted the emailed reset link into the tab already showing *Forgot your password?* and, with a read-once page, stayed on the ask form with the secret left in the address bar. A query-string link never had this case (changing the query reloads), which is why the pre-merge pages could read once.
4. **Backward compatibility: a link already emailed with `?token=` keeps working for its whole lifetime** (the utility's `password_link_valid_days`, at most 14 days). Nothing on the server ever read the secret from a URL — both endpoints take it in the POST body — so compatibility lives entirely in the two pages, which accept either form and prefer the fragment when both carry a value. The query fallback can be deleted once the longest-lived pre-change link has expired (14 days after this release ships); until then removing it would turn a valid emailed link into *"Link not valid"*.
5. **Redaction is unchanged:** the kept copy replaces the whole rendered link (the catalogue's `credential_tokens`), so it holds neither form.

**Worked example.** Before: an invitation for Sam at Brazos Bend read `https://app.example/brazosbend/set-password?token=Qx7…`, and the proxy's access log for the click held `GET /brazosbend/set-password?token=Qx7…` — a usable credential for seven days in a file the utility's IT keeps for ninety. After: the email reads `…/set-password#token=Qx7…`, the log holds `GET /brazosbend/set-password`, and the token reaches the server only inside the POST to `auth/password-link/check`.

**Supersedes, in the entries above (left as written; append-only):** item 2 of *"Portal password reset: what a blank box gets, what the link is…"* (the `?ref=<code row>&token=<secret>` shape) and the query-string link shape in *"Staff invitation link: how it was built"*. Their other items stand.

**How the three lanes were reconciled at merge (STAFF-INVITE owns the shared mechanisms; PORTAL-RESET and PORTAL-EMAIL build on them):**
- **One wording file**, `notifications/account_access_wording.py`, whose `WORDING` now holds six classes — `staff_user_invite`, `staff_password_reset_link`, `portal_password_reset`, `portal_enrolment_code`, `portal_email_change_code`, `portal_email_changed_notice` — each written in all 11 registry languages. It was three separate add/add files.
- **One document kind, `account_access_email`** (`tenancy/0065_cr188…`), for all six. PORTAL-RESET's own `tenancy/0065` adding a kind named `account_access` was deleted; 53 kinds, not 54.
- **One redaction function**, CR-188's `frozen_documents.redact_credentials(row, payload) -> bytes` with `REDACTION_MARKER`. PORTAL-RESET's second `redact_credentials(row, artifact)` and `CREDENTIAL_REDACTED` had **auto-merged without a conflict** as a silent redefinition (the later definition wins in Python) plus a second call on the same path — removed. Credential tokens per class: `{sign_in_link}` (staff), `{reset_link}` (portal reset), `{code}` (both code classes); the changed-email notice carries none.
- **One migration graph leaf per app.** PORTAL-RESET's `notifications/0023_def_cwp_10381…` was folded into CR-188's `0023_cr188_priority_and_account_access` (`portal_password_reset` joined its `CODES`, plus the audit dependency the seeder needs). Neither 0023 had been applied to the kept dev database, which stood at `0022`. PORTAL-EMAIL's `0024_cr189_portal_email_update` now depends on that 0023. Leaves: notifications `0024`, tenancy `0065_cr188`, identity `0014_cr188`.
- **Who decides "in use" for a class no SET-12 rule names.** The staff classes have SET-12 events (`staff_user_invited`, `staff_password_reset`). The four portal classes have none on purpose — each is asked for by the person waiting for it — so they are listed both in `catalogs.SENT_DIRECTLY` (Settings → Templates shows them *in use*) and in `rule_catalog.WRITER_REACHED_CLASSES` (the unruled-wording gap does not count them), each with its writer named.
- **One reset issuer.** *Update your email* calls `credentials.send_reset` unconditionally; its pre-merge fallback called `queue_reset` without a link and would have queued an email with nothing to click.
- `DEF-CWP-10383` (PORTAL-RESET: the enrolment code is never sent) and `DEF-CWP-10402` (PORTAL-EMAIL: the same class had no catalogue entry) are the same fault found twice. The EMAIL half is built by `CR-189-BRC10`; the SMS copy still waits for an SMS provider, so `DEF-CWP-10383` is marked partially fixed rather than closed.

## 2026-10-22 — Service request acknowledgement built: the judgments the ruling left to us (`DEF-CUS-10445`, lane SR-ACK)

These follow from the ruling above (*"Service request acknowledgement: target date, default 15 days, service type name"*) and are recorded rather than asked (law 13).

**1 · What `{service_type}` names.** A request carries no "type" when it is submitted: its job type (new connection, move-in…) is decided at review, and nothing in Settings names request types. What it does carry is the services the applicant asked for, and Settings → Services is where those have their names. So `{service_type}` is the requested services' names, in the catalogue's order: *"Water"*, *"Electric, Water"*. Never the code.
- The names are the platform catalogue's (`Water`, `Storm water`), the same source the plan-change email uses. No translated service name is stored on the server, so a non-English utility's letter carries the catalogue name.
- No service asked for → the named absence `——`.

**2 · What `{target_date}` is.**
- The customer's preferred date is the request's connection date. If that is blank, it is the earliest date written against one of its services.
- With neither, it is the request date (the day it was submitted, on the utility's clock) plus **`service_request_default_target_days` WORKING days** — weekends and the utility's own holidays skipped.
- **Why working days.** A staff New Request already opens its Connection date *"15 working days"* ahead (PO 2026-09-22, *"make it default add 15 working days"*), held in a constant `CONNECTION_DATE_WORKING_DAYS = 15`. That is the same fact — when service is aimed at when the customer named no date. Two different 15s, one in calendar days and one in working days, would tell a clerk and an applicant two different dates. So ONE setting now drives both, counted one way, and the constant is gone (*"don't do any hardcoding"*).
- Worked (no holidays in the window): submitted Thursday 22 Oct 2026, no date given, setting 15 → **11/12/2026**. Setting moved to 7 → **11/02/2026**. A holiday in the window pushes it one working day further.
- The setting is a new rule-page family on tenancy (`service-requests`). It is seeded 15, has a minimum of 0 and no maximum (`NFR-5`). It is edited at Settings → Reference data → Accounts → **Service requests**, shown in working days.
- The portal's own *"how long to connect"* figure (`portal/availability.WORKING_DAYS_TO_CONNECT`) is a separate promise on a separate screen and is not changed here.
- The seeded sentence says *"Our target date for it is 11/30/2026."* It says *target*, never *we will connect you on*, because it is not a booked visit.

**3 · Name and address.**
- The name is the applicant's as typed. When it is blank and the matched customer holds exactly one account, it comes from the account holder through the shared customer-details builder. Two accounts or none → no account is named.
- The address: a premises or unit the clerk picked (or the resolver matched) is walked to (hard rule 8): *"77 Bluestem Ln · B, Katy, TX 77494"*. Otherwise it is the typed address with its town, state and postcode: *"1408 Elm St, Austin, TX 78704"*. It is composed by the same builder the welcome email uses.
- Only the acknowledgement changed. The approval, refusal and more-information letters keep the typed street.

**4 · Which paths send it.**
- Staff New Request submit, fee and no-fee, both pass every value.
- A clerk's added message in an acknowledgement class carries the same facts.
- **The customer portal sends no acknowledgement and still does not.** `create_from_portal` records `ACK_NO_ADDRESS` on purpose (`BR-CWP-028`, *"the reference is the entire record of the interaction"*). Starting to email portal applicants is new behaviour and is not part of this ruling. It is reported to the coordinator, not built.

**5 · Existing utilities.** `notifications 0024` republishes the new wording for both classes only where the published default copy is byte-for-byte the old seed. A utility that edited its wording keeps it. Copper-bynry's *"We received your request for {service_type} on …"* now fills, because the class allows both tokens and the caller passes them.
## 2026-10-22 — How the stuck bill email was fixed: four judgments (lane BILL-EMAIL, `DEF-BIL-10530`)

Building the ruling above. No new rule; these are the points where the ruling did not say, decided and written down (law 13).

1. **Which wording.** Email and text take the wording the bill's event names on Settings → Notifications: *Bill ready* → `email_bill_ready` / `sms_bill_ready`, *Bill corrected* → `email_corrected_bill`. (The per-utility template a System Admin can store on SET-12D is read only by its *Send test*, by every writer today; this fix does not change that.) A corrected bill has no text wording of its own, so a text about one uses `sms_bill_ready` (*"your new bill is ready"*, which is true of a replacement). Print and the portal keep the bill layout.
2. **Fail at once, not after three tries.** A message's wording is fixed when it is queued, so one that cannot be found now never will be. It fails on its first try with *No wording found for this message.* and the try is counted (`1`). Retrying three times would only delay the clerk seeing it.
3. **Print and the portal are not changed.** They carry the bill itself. A portal copy of a bill still shows *Waiting* on the staff queue after a cycle, as before (`DEF-NOT-10532`, filed rather than changed here, because what the customer's portal shows depends on it).
4. **Rows already stuck.** Every email, text or in-app message still waiting whose wording link points at something that is not a message template is marked failed once, with *Linked to the wrong wording. Not sent.* and one audit entry each. None is sent. Example: Daniel Thomas's one-time bill email on AC-2026-00071 goes from *Waiting · 0 tries* to *Failed*; his paper and portal copies are untouched.

**Not done, and why:** the bill-ready email says the bill *"is attached to this email"*, and this branch has no way to attach a file to an email yet (the shared attachment piece is still being built by another lane). Until it lands the email goes out with that sentence and no attachment (`DEF-BIL-10531`).

## 2026-10-22 — Merging the four email branches into one build (lane MERGE-EMAILS): migration order, and two items left open by MERGE-MOVEIN (our judgment, recorded rather than put to the PO — law 13)

**What was merged, onto 2.594.3:** MERGE-ACCESS (staff invitation link, portal password reset, update your email — `CR-188-BRC10`, `CR-189-BRC10`), MERGE-MOVEIN (move-in messages, the 7-day click-to-accept agreement, PDF attachments on every email provider — `CR-190-BRC10`), SR-ACK (`DEF-CUS-10445`) and BILL-EMAIL (`DEF-BIL-10530`).

**1 · Migration order.** Four branches each wrote the "next" notifications migration from the same base, and two wrote the next tenancy one. None had been applied on a shared database, so the account-access migrations keep their numbers and the others move behind them, contents unchanged: notifications `0023_cr188` → `0024_cr189` → **`0025_cr190_welcome_first_bill_wording`** (was `0023`) → **`0026_def_cus_10445_service_request_ack_wording`** (was `0024`) → **`0027_def_bil_10530_fail_stuck_bill_emails`** (was `0023`); tenancy `0065_cr188` → **`0066_def_cus_10445_service_request_settings`** (was `0065`). One leaf per app; `makemigrations --check` clean.

**2 · The delete icon on a signed agreement copy (open item 1 from MERGE-MOVEIN) — not a defect; nothing changed.** The signed copy is filed as a `contract` document. The server refuses to remove a `contract` (or `system`) document with **409 `BIZ-LOCKED`** (`customers/account_documents.py`, proved by `tests/test_cr094_m_account_document_withdrawal.py`), and the Documents list draws its Remove icon **disabled, with the reason as its label** (*"Contract files cannot be removed"*). That is `BR-SHL-025` (CONFIRMED): *"forbidden actions on visible screens render disabled-with-reason"* — a clerk who finds no icon learns nothing, a clerk who finds a disabled one learns the rule. **Hiding it would break that signed rule**, so it stays drawn and disabled. Worked: Ade Okafor accepts the service agreement on 22 October; the stamped PDF appears in his account's Documents; the clerk sees 👁 (opens it) and a greyed − whose label says why; a `DELETE` sent by hand answers 409 and the file stays.

**3 · Agreement emails already seeded with "Hi {customer_name}" (open item 2) — no data migration.** The click-to-accept emails first exist in this merge: release 2.594.3 has no `agreement_wording.py` and no agreement email class at all, and the two classes are planted at FIRST USE (`agreement_templates.ensure_seeded`, insert-missing), not by a migration. So every utility on a released build will be planted the `{first_name}` wording the first time it sends one. The old greeting exists only in throwaway lane databases: counted 2026-10-22 on this host, **26 of 26** agreement template rows in `sbh_agreement_walk` (lane AGREEMENT's walk copy) carry `{customer_name}`, while the shared dev database `smartbillhub` holds **0** agreement rows among its 50 templates (and `sbh_moveinmsg_walk` 0). A migration that rewrites only untouched copies would therefore change **0 rows on any real database** while adding a 🔒 migration to review; the safe path and doing nothing are the same outcome here. If a build containing the old wording is ever found deployed, the `0025`/`0026` pattern (republish only byte-identical published copies) is the fix.

**4 · One seeder for language-planted emails.** CR-188 put its account-access emails in the provisioning seeder with one variant per registry language; CR-190 gave its two agreement emails their own planter that ran only when the first agreement was sent. Kept apart, a new utility would see six account-access templates on Settings → Templates from day one and no agreement email until a move-in had already sent one. They are one mechanism now (`seed_templates.LANGUAGE_WORDING`); `agreement_templates.ensure_seeded` is a thin door onto it, still called at send time for older utilities. Same words, same source line. Worked: a utility provisioned today gets **59** classes as `default` variants (was 57 on A, 51 on 2.594.3), **41** of them email; the agreement emails arrive with their 12 language variants each.

**5 · Found and fixed in the merge, not new rules:** the screen-id map listed the two new public routes in the opposite order from `App.tsx` (its test was red on the union); two new English strings said *Tick* (`DEF-SHL-6351`'s American-English test was red on them) and now say *Check*.

**Left open, reported:** `DEF-BIL-10531` (the bill-ready email says the bill is attached and it is not) was filed because BILL-EMAIL's branch had no way to attach a file; MERGE-MOVEIN's attachment mechanism (`notifications.attachments`, every email adapter) is now in the same build, so it can be wired — that is its own change, not this merge. `DEF-NOT-10532` and `DEF-CUS-10445` stay open for the release.

## 2026-10-22 — Building the Templates + Notifications move and "mail server in Connectors only": the judgments the three rulings left to us (lane SETTINGS-MOVE, `DEF-NOT-10533`, `DEF-NOT-10534`; recorded, not put to the PO — law 13)

Builds the three entries above: Q4 of *Corrected bills*, *Templates and Notifications sit together under Settings → Configure*, and *The four placement details* (which removed the cross-links). Worked case throughout: Springfield Water Utility, whose Custom SMTP connector reads host `smtp.office365.com`, sender `billing@springfieldwater.example`.

1. **The new addresses.** Configure's tab id is `reference-data` (CR-001 kept it so old links resolve), so Configure → Notifications is `/settings/reference-data/notifications`. Its tabs are `/…/notifications/messages` and `/…/notifications/blocked`; a rule page is `/…/notifications/<event key>`, exactly as before one level down.
2. **Where each old address goes.** `/settings/notifications` → `/settings/reference-data/notifications`. `/settings/notifications/messages`, `/blocked` and `/<event key>` → the same last segment under the new home. `/settings/notifications/rights` → the 10-day disconnection notice on Templates (`/settings/reference-data/templates?template=disconnect_notice_10_day`), because that is the letter the wording prints on. `/settings/notifications/sender` → Connectors' Custom SMTP page (`/settings/integrations/email_smtp`), because that is where the mail server now lives.
3. **Customer rights wording on Templates.** It shows under the letter on the detail page of each disconnection notice (`disconnect_notice`, `…_10_day`, `…_5_day`, `…_48_hour`) — the PO's *"next to the disconnection letter it prints on"*. One card, the same component, the same server write; editing stays System Admin only (the server's own gate, unchanged). The red *platform wording* warning travels inside the card, as before.
4. **The bell's link.** One line at the foot of the bell menu, *Messages needing attention*, shown whether or not the bell holds anything, so Daniel's bounced email is one click from any screen. It is shown to every role; a role that may not open the list meets the list's own refusal, which is the same rule every other Settings link follows.
5. **The mail-server status on Configure → Notifications.** A read of the connector, never a form: *Active: Custom SMTP (smtp.office365.com)*, the sender `billing@springfieldwater.example`, the connector's state in Connectors' own words (*Working*, *Not tested yet*, *Not working*, *Not set up*, *Turned off*), and *Open Connectors*. With no connector it reads *No mail server connected*. *Active* is used only when the connector can actually send (switched on, with a password); a connector that exists but cannot send shows its host and its state without the word *Active*.
6. **One true line per channel.** Computed on the server from live state and served on `GET /notification-settings` as `channel_lines`, so the screen holds no second opinion:
   - Email: switch off → *Not switched on*; switch on and a connector that can send → *Sending through Custom SMTP (smtp.office365.com)* (the host only for a mail server; a bulk email service reads *Sending through SendGrid*); its last test failed → *Custom SMTP is not working*; nothing connected → *No mail server connected*.
   - Text message: switch off → *Not switched on*; on and connected → *Sending through <provider>*; on with no text provider this platform can connect → *Waiting for a text provider*; on, connectable, not connected → *No text provider connected*.
   - Printed letter (no switch, BR-BIL-036): a connected print vendor → *Sending through <vendor>*; otherwise → *Waiting for a print vendor*.
   Each is a fact of at most six words plus the host (B14 rule 33). The waiting count stays beside it. *"Always on — print is the floor"* goes: the floor is still enforced by the server, and the line now says what actually happens to the letter.
7. **The move of typed values, once.** Migration `integrations/0016`. For every utility whose `notification_settings` holds a mail server, port, user or sender address: if it has a Custom SMTP connection (production first), each of those four that the connection LACKS is copied in; a value the connection already has wins and is left alone. A utility with none gets a Custom SMTP connection created *Not set up* and switched off — 0004's absent-password shape, because those columns never held a password. Each utility changed writes one audit row (`integration_connection.smtp_settings_moved`, before and after of the copied fields only). Worked figure: Springfield's connector has host `smtp.office365.com` and no sender; the old form held host `mail.springfield.example` and sender `billing@springfieldwater.example` → the connector keeps `smtp.office365.com` and gains the sender. Re-running changes nothing.
8. **The old columns.** `notification_settings.smtp_host`, `smtp_port`, `smtp_username`, `smtp_secret_ref` and `sender_from_address` are read by nothing after this commit and are listed for removal in `apps/notifications/models.py`'s docstring. They are not dropped here, for 0004's reason: a column dropped in the commit that stops reading it leaves no way back if the copy was wrong.
9. **The refusal.** `PATCH /notification-sender` and `PATCH /notification-settings` refuse any of `smtp_host`, `smtp_port`, `smtp_username`, `smtp_secret_ref`, `sender_from_address` by name, with the clerk sentence *"Set this on Connectors."*; the field is named in the refusal's field list. `GET /notification-sender` stays and serves the connector read, so nothing that reads it breaks.

## 2026-10-22 — Building the corrected-bill rulings Q1–Q3: the judgments the rulings left to us (lane CORRECTED-BILL, `DEF-BIL-10535`, `DEF-BIL-4454`; recorded, not put to the PO — law 13)

Builds the three rulings of *"Corrected bills: the clerk picks the channels; every bill also emails whenever an email is on file …"* above. Worked case throughout: Daniel Thomas, AC-2026-00071, paperless off, `daniel.thomas@yopmail.com` on file, original bill queued `pdf_print` only (the old rule), corrected for a wrong reading.

1. **What "the original bill's channels" pre-selects.** The original's queued rows are read through `delivery_seam.deliveries_for_bill`. An `email` row among them → **Both**; otherwise → **Paper**. Print is on every bill, so *Email* and *Both* queue the same two rows (`DELIVERY_CHOICES`); *Both* is the honest name for what went. A one-customer case over several months takes the union of its bills. For Daniel: his original went by post only, so the step opens on **Paper**, and the clerk can pick **Both** because an email is on file.
2. **A body with no choice** (an older screen, a script) is issued on that same pre-selection, computed by the server. Never on a guess: the original's rows are the fact the ruling names.
3. **"Email on file" is the address the email would go to** — the customers read the queue already addresses by (`delivery_recipients_for_account`, primary contact first). One answer to *can we email them*, so the screen's grey option and the queue's address cannot disagree. Email or Both with none → refused by name, `billing.correction.delivery_no_email` (*"No email on file."*).
4. **Bulk cases are not offered the choice.** The ruling is about Fix-a-bill's one approval step for a bill; a case across a run reaches hundreds of accounts whose originals differ, and one answer for all of them would overwrite each account's own channels. A bulk case keeps each account's own channels — which, after Q2, include email whenever one is on file. A `delivery` sent on a bulk case is refused by name rather than ignored (a silently ignored field is worse than a refusal, law 14's lesson).
5. **Q2's consumers, re-argued one by one** (grep of `delivery_channel_election_for_account`):
   - the bill queue (`delivery_seam.elected_channels`) and the correction preview's channel line (`correction_answer._channels`) — **take the new rule**; that is what Q2 is.
   - the portal's *Paperless* switch (`portal/seams/customers_seam.delivery_election`, `portal/selectors.py`'s account card) — **keeps reading the customer's own preference**. It shows what the customer chose; reading the new bill rule would show *Paperless: on* for every customer with an email, and switching it off would appear to do nothing.
   - Work's visit messages (`notifications/work_customer_messages`) — **keep the preference**. Q2 is *every bill*; a visit text or email was never a bill.
   - both now read a new published read, `customers.selectors.channel_preference_for_account` — the old function's body, unchanged (paperless → email, text reminders → sms).
   - the agreement letter (`customers/agreements.py`, paper only when not paperless) reads `accounts.paperless` directly and is untouched.
6. **Where the sixteen sentences live.** One template class per seeded reason, `correction_reason_<code>` (e.g. `correction_reason_wrong_read`), category Billing, kind Email, named *"What changed · Wrong reading"* — the clerk's own reason words from Fix-a-bill. Each has a `default` variant (the English) and one published variant per written language, through the same insert-missing language seeder as the account-access and agreement emails, so a utility edits each on Templates and a release never overwrites its edit. Existing utilities are planted by `notifications 0028`. Their *in use* state follows `email_corrected_bill`'s, because they are printed only inside it.
7. **Which language, and several reasons.** At queue time the sentence is taken in the utility's default language (`BR-NOT-006` as amended 2026-09-23): its published variant in that language, else the published `default` variant, else the platform wording. A case with several reasons lists one sentence per reason, in the case's order, separated by a space. For Daniel: *"What changed: We corrected your meter reading."*
8. **The token check, and its scope said out loud.** A test walks every token in the seeded bodies of the three wordings a BILL is queued as (`email_bill_ready`, `sms_bill_ready`, `email_corrected_bill`, every language) and fails on one with no source. A source is a key `delivery_seam.bill_render_context` sets, or a utility-identity token stamped at render. `{correction_reason}` was the one with no source. The other seeded classes are filled by other senders and are NOT walked by this check; the test prints how many classes it skipped beside how many it checked (law 7).

## 2026-10-22 — Move-out final bill email, built: our judgments where the ruling left the detail to us (DEF-NOT-10536, lane MOVEOUT-EMAIL)

Builds the ruling *"Move-out final bill email: sent at completion with the draft figures, at normal priority (no instant email); details and PDF filled in"* above. Nothing here reverses it; each point below is a choice the ruling did not make, recorded before the code (law 13: ours to decide).

1. **The attached PDF is the page issue would keep, rendered without changing the draft.** A draft has no template pin and no due date, so the print path (`GET /invoices/{id}/document.pdf`) refuses a draft. Billing therefore renders the draft through the same renderer issue uses (`documents.render_invoice`), with the pin issue would resolve for that account and the issue-time stamps (masthead, balance forward, usage history, bill copy, plan instalment) applied inside a savepoint that is then rolled back. The draft row is unchanged; the PDF is stored write-once under the email row (document kind `move_out_final_bill`) and named on it with `notifications.attachments`. A test issues the same draft afterwards and compares the kept page with the attached one.
2. **The due date is the one issue will stamp**: the bill date (the move-out date) plus the cycle's due days. Worked: moved out 12 Oct, 21 due days → **due 2 Nov**.
3. **Closing reads, one line per meter register read on or after the move-out date**, as `<meter number>: <reading> <unit>` — e.g. `W-5043: 2645 kgal` and `E-5046: 21550 kWh`. The reading is printed as stored, trailing zeros dropped, no thousands mark (unambiguous in every language). A register that was estimated has no dial reading and is left out. A unit with no closing reading leaves the whole paragraph out rather than printing a dash.
4. **No final bill drafted** (every day already on an issued bill): the email still goes at completion, as it does today, and the *"attached / total due"* paragraph and the attachment are left out. **A drafted bill whose page cannot be produced**: the email is not queued and the move-out's result says so; the move-out itself completes. An email saying *"your final bill is attached"* with nothing attached is a wrong email.
5. **`{unit}`** stays in the palette for a utility's own wording that still reads *"{final_read} {unit}"*: it is filled only when every closing reading shares one unit. The platform's wording prints the unit inside each reading line.
6. **Wording**: the platform's own wording is rewritten in all eleven languages, each in its own voice (`move_out_wording.py`, the agreement emails' table shape). A migration republishes the platform `default` wording only where a utility has not edited it, and plants the ten language variants beside it; an edited copy is left exactly alone.
7. **Priority**: `PRIORITY_NORMAL`, through the ordinary dispatch cycle and quiet hours. It never calls `send_now`.
8. **"Total due" is the figure the attached bill prints as Total due** — the previous balance plus this bill — not the bill's current charges. Found on the browser walk the same evening: Ana Alvarez's move-out drafted $388.98 of charges over a $187.92 balance, the PDF said **Total due 576.90**, and the first build's email said **$388.98**. Two documents in one envelope must not disagree. A customer in credit is told **$0.00**, which is the bill's own headline for a credit.

## 2026-10-22 — Who moves the portal sign-in email, built: the judgments the two rulings left to us (lane SIGNIN-EMAIL; `OQ-CUS-12350` closed, `DEF-CWP-10400`, `DEF-CWP-10401`)

These follow from *"Who moves the portal sign-in email: the clerk's choice, and a signed-in customer confirms by code"* above and its read-back (*"Your understanding is correct"*). They are recorded, not put back (law 13). No signed rule moves.

**The clerk's tick box (Q1).**
1. **Both clerk doors get it.** A clerk changes a customer's email in two places: *Edit customer* (`PATCH /customers/{id}`, every account the person holds) and the account's *Customer* pencil (`PATCH /accounts/{id}/contact`, that account's primary contact). Both accept `portal_sign_in: true`. The label is the PO's own words, *"Also use this as the portal sign-in email"*, unticked every time the dialog opens.
2. **When it shows.** *Edit customer*: only when that customer has a portal login (the row now serves `has_portal_login`). The account pencil: only when the account has **exactly one** login (`portal_access.logins == 1`). A joint account with two logins does not say whose login the primary contact is, so the box is not offered there and the server refuses the flag by name; the clerk opens *Edit customer* for that person instead.
3. **What a tick does, on save, in one transaction.** The contact email changes as before. The login's email becomes the same address (normalised). One audit row `portal_credential.email_changed` names the clerk (`actor_user_id`) and holds both addresses masked. The OLD sign-in address gets `portal_email_changed_notice`. The NEW address gets the forgot-password link from the one issuer, `credentials.send_reset` (link secret in the fragment). Both go to the instant sender.
4. **Ticked over an address that is already the sign-in email:** nothing moves, nothing is sent. Ticked with the email box blank: refused by name, *"Sign-in needs an email."*. Ticked over an address that is ANOTHER customer's login: refused by name to the clerk, *"Another customer signs in with this."*, and nothing is saved. A clerk is signed-in staff; `BR-CWP-038`'s silence protects the anonymous forgot-password page, not the back office.
5. **No public address configured:** the login still moves and the notice still goes; `send_reset` writes its own *"not sent"* audit line, as it already does.
6. **Worked case.** Maria Alvarez is locked out and calls. The clerk opens *Edit customer*, types `maria.new@example.test`, ticks the box and saves. Her login moves from `maria.alvarez@example.test`; that old address gets *"Your Pine Hill Water registered email was changed"*; `maria.new@example.test` gets *"Choose a new password here: …#ref=…&token=…"*. That is the *"Call the office"* ending working.

**The signed-in change (Q2).**
7. **Two new signed-in calls**, `POST portal/my-details/email/start {email}` and `POST portal/my-details/email/confirm {ref, code, email}`, in `email_update.py` beside the locked-out flow, reusing its pieces: the code is bound to the address (`bound_secret`), keyed to the LOGIN (purpose `email_update_signed_in`), ten minutes, six tries.
8. **An address that is another customer's login gets the same answer and no code**, exactly as the locked-out flow does, and for the same reason.
9. **Confirmed:** the contact email moves on every account in the session through the `contact_detail` door (`services.update_own_contact_details`, unchanged), the login moves, the old sign-in address gets the notice. No reset link: the customer is signed in and still knows their password.
10. **`POST my-details/save` no longer moves the email.** An email equal to the one shown is dropped, so a phone or mailing-address save still works; a different one is refused by name, *"Confirm a new email by code."*. Phone and postal address save exactly as before (the ruling's own scope).
11. **The two emails reuse the existing classes**, `portal_email_change_code` and `portal_email_changed_notice`. Both are already written in all 11 languages, account-access, instant, and kept with the code redacted. Their words (*"the registered email for your customer portal"*) are the sign-in email. A third class with the same words would be two templates a utility edits and keeps in step.

**The screen on the portal.** *My details* keeps one email box. When it differs from the email on file, *Save changes* saves the rest and sends a code to the new address; a code step appears under the box (*"We sent it to m•••@example.test. It lasts 10 minutes."*, six-digit box, *Confirm ✓*, *Send it again*, *Keep my old email*). After the code, *"Email changed."*

**Superseded here (left as written; append-only):** `customer_edit.py`'s *"NO PORTAL CREDENTIAL MOVES"* and `REFUSED_FIELDS["portal_email"]` citing `OQ-CUS-12350` as open; `CustomerEditDialog`'s *"Portal sign-in does not move."* is now the unticked sentence only; `save_my_details`'s *"no second proof"* for the email field (`BR-CWP-103` still holds for phone and postal address).

## 2026-10-22 — Bill email sends a link instead of the PDF; service-request target date in working days excluding holidays; portal requests get the acknowledgement when the email is valid

Three questions put to the PO.

**1. The bill-ready email says "it is attached to this email" and nothing is attached (`DEF-BIL-10531`).** We recommended attaching the bill PDF. **PO, verbatim:** *"can't we sent link instead"*. **Ruled:** the bill email carries a LINK to the bill, not an attachment. The sentence "it is attached to this email" goes. **Still to settle:** which link — one that opens the bill in the customer portal (sign-in needed), or a secure link that opens the bill's PDF without signing in. Put to the PO the same turn.

**2. The service-request target date's 15 days (`DEF-CUS-10445`).** **PO, verbatim:** *"Yes exclude holidays"*. **Ruled:** working days, skipping weekends and the utility's holidays. This is how lane SR-ACK built it (worked: SR-26-0067 submitted Thu 22 Oct → 11/13/2026, Veterans Day skipped). One setting drives both the acknowledgement and New Request's Connection date. Judgment 1 of the SR-ACK entry is confirmed.

**3. Portal service requests and the acknowledgement email.** Until now a portal request got no email, by design (`ACK_NO_ADDRESS`, BR-CWP-028). **PO, verbatim:** *"yes if we have valid email"*. **Ruled:** a request made in the customer portal gets the same acknowledgement email as a staff-entered one when the applicant gave a valid email address. With no email, or an invalid one, nothing is sent and the screen confirmation stands. Normal priority. This supersedes BR-CWP-028's no-acknowledgement for the email case.

## 2026-10-22 — The bill email's link opens the bill PDF directly, with no sign-in (completes item 1 of the entry above)

Asked which link the bill email carries: (A) the bill in the customer portal, sign-in needed, or (B) a secure link that opens the bill PDF directly, unique, secret and expiring, like the move-in agreement link. We recommended A. **PO, verbatim:** *"b direct PDF link"*.

**Ruled:** every bill email carries a direct link to that bill's kept PDF. The line "it is attached to this email" is replaced by the link line.

**Our judgments (law 13; the PO named no number):**
- The link lasts **30 days**. That is a utility SETTING seeded at 30, editable beside the agreement link's days, never a constant (*"don't do any hardcoding"*).
- The link serves the bill's FROZEN PDF, the one kept at issue, never a re-render.
- The secret travels after `#` like the other one-time links. It is never written to a server log.
- An expired or unknown link shows a short page with the utility's phone. It never shows another customer's bill.
- Each open is audited, with the bill and the time but not the IP's owner.
- The corrected-bill email gets the same link to the corrected bill.

## 2026-10-22 — Portal requests get the acknowledgement when the email is valid, built: the judgments ruling 3 left to us (lane PORTAL-SR-ACK, `DEF-CWP-10539`; recorded, not put to the PO — law 13)

Builds ruling 3 of *"Bill email sends a link instead of the PDF; service-request target date in working days excluding holidays; portal requests get the acknowledgement when the email is valid"* above (*"yes if we have valid email"*). Worked case throughout: Kyle Mark applies for water at 1408 Elm St, Austin, TX 78704 on the portal, Thursday 22 Oct 2026, no start date.

1. **One letter, one path.** The portal sends the SAME acknowledgement a clerk's submit sends, through the same body: same two classes (the fee one only when a receipt exists, which a portal request never has), same facts (`acknowledgement_facts`), the utility's default language, normal priority through the ordinary dispatch cycle. `send_acknowledgement` was guarded to staff roles (`@require_role`), so its body moved into a private function that both doors call: the staff function keeps its guard and calls it; `create_from_portal` calls it with the role-free portal actor, as `note_from_portal` and `withdraw_from_portal` already do. No second way of composing the letter exists. Kyle's email: *"We have your request for Water at 1408 Elm St, Austin, TX 78704 … Our target date for it is 11/13/2026."* (15 working days, Veterans Day skipped).
2. **What "valid" means.** Django's own `validate_email`, the same check the portal's sign-in and account forms use (`portal.credentials.email_refusal`). A format check, never a deliverability one. `kyle.mark@example.test` is valid; `kyle.mark@example`, `kyle.mark at example.test` and a blank box are not.
3. **No email or a bad one: nothing is queued and the row says what it said before.** The request keeps the absence reason every portal request has always carried (`applicant_supplied_no_email_or_phone`), and no extra timeline line is written. The applicant still has the reference on screen (BR-CWP-028's part that stands).
4. **Every portal door that makes a request gets it** — start service, report a problem, quick ask, plan request, dispute, question, stop/restart, restart now, hardship — because they all make the request through `create_from_portal`, and the ruling names portal requests, not one form.
5. **The staff path is not changed.** The validity check sits on the portal door only. A clerk's submit still queues to whatever email the clerk typed; checking that is a different question nobody asked.
6. **A failed queue never loses the request.** The notifications call runs in its own savepoint (law 14) and the request is made either way; a refusal is recorded on the request as a staff one is.
7. **Who the trail names.** The timeline and audit rows carry no user (the portal is never a person, `BR-CWP-021`), exactly as the request's own creation does.

**Superseded here:** `BR-CWP-028`'s *"a guest has no inbox we hold, so the reference is the entire record"* for the case where the guest gave a valid email (stamped in `04-docs/05-modules/15-portal/02-business-rules.md`); `create_from_portal`'s docstring *"NO ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS SENT"*; item 4 of the SR-ACK entry above (*"The customer portal sends no acknowledgement and still does not"*), left as written because this log is append-only.

## 2026-10-22 — The bill email's PDF link: how lane BILL-LINK builds it (DEF-BIL-10531; judgments the two rulings above left to us)

The PO ruled the bill email carries a direct, secret, expiring link to the bill's kept PDF (*"b direct PDF link"*), and we already judged 30 days, a setting. These are the remaining choices, ours under law 13, written before the code.

1. **Where the link's record lives: billing.** A `bill_links` table holds one row per link: the bill, a SHA-256 digest of the secret (never the secret), when it was made and when it stops working, under the same row-level tenant policy as every tenant table. It copies the agreement link's token pieces (256 random bits, digest lookup, constant-time compare); the two now share one small helper, `core/link_tokens.py`, so there is one token scheme and not two.
2. **A link is made when the bill's delivery is queued**, inside the issue, so the email row carries it. A corrected bill is a new bill, so its email gets its own link to the corrected bill. The old bill's link keeps opening the old bill until it expires: it is the bill that customer was sent.
3. **A bill link may be opened as often as the customer likes until it expires.** It is not single use like an agreement: reading your bill twice is normal. Every open writes an audit row (the bill and the time, nothing about who opened it).
4. **Worked figure:** a bill issued on 22 Oct 2026 at 10:00 with the setting at 30 opens until 21 Nov 2026 at 10:00, and the email says *"This link works until 11/21/2026"*. A utility that sets 14 gets 5 Nov 2026. The setting is on Settings → Customer portal beside the agreement link's days, 1 to 90 like that one.
5. **The address is `/{utility}/portal/bill#token=…`.** The page reads the secret from after the `#`, takes it off the address bar, and asks the server with the secret in the request BODY. No address the server or a proxy logs ever holds it.
6. **Expired, unknown, another utility's, or a bill with no kept PDF:** one page, *"This link has expired"* and the utility's phone. The same answer for every case, so a stranger learns nothing. A bill with no kept PDF is refused rather than re-drawn (the ruling: the kept PDF, never a re-render).
7. **The link line is optional in the email.** If a host has no public address configured the link cannot be built; the paragraph is left out and the rest of the email goes, rather than printing a dash where a link should be. `{bill_link}` is a credential: the kept copy of the email has it removed, as a sign-in link is.
8. **The old sentence is replaced only where the utility never edited it.** A migration republishes the default wording where the published version is byte-for-byte the old seeded text (the `notifications/0026` pattern); an edited email is the utility's own words and is left alone. Bill-ready and corrected-bill wording is now seeded in all eleven languages.

## 2026-10-22 — Corrected-bill rulings Q1–Q3: three facts found while building (lane CORRECTED-BILL, `DEF-BIL-10535`, `DEF-BIL-4454`; recorded, not put to the PO — law 13)

Amends the judgments entry *"Building the corrected-bill rulings Q1–Q3"* above; that entry is left as written.

1. **Seventeen sentences, not sixteen.** `billing/correction_reasons.SEEDED_REASON_CLASSES` holds 17 codes: the 16 Fix-a-bill offers, plus `wrong_rate_plan`, kept because cases opened before the plan/rate split (CR-180) still cite it. A rebill of such a case would print `——` without it, so it has a sentence too (*"We corrected the plan and rate on your bill."*). A test pins the set to `SEEDED_REASON_CLASSES`, so a new reason with no sentence goes red.
2. **The portal copy is a floor of its own.** Every bill also queues a `portal` row whatever the clerk picks. *Paper* therefore means print (and portal) with no email, and *Both* means print, email (and portal). Daniel's corrected bill reads back as `pdf_print` + `email` (+ `portal`).
3. **Where the clerk's choice is recorded.** The clerk's answer is returned on the approve-and-issue result (`result.delivery`) and is visible on the queue rows themselves. It is not added to the `correction.approved` audit row, because that row is written by the shared case loop that bulk cases also use.

## 2026-10-22 — Portal acknowledgement: only a request that names a service, and the state on an application's address (lane PORTAL-SR-ACK, `DEF-CWP-10540`, `DEF-CWP-10541`; our judgments, recorded, not put to the PO — law 13)

Found on the browser walk of `DEF-CWP-10539` (shipped in 2.596.1).

1. **A portal ask that names no service gets no acknowledgement email (`DEF-CWP-10540`).** The PO's ruling (*"yes if we have valid email"*) was about SERVICE requests, and the letter is written for one: *"We have your request for {service_type} … Our target date for it is …"*. A bill question, a dispute, a copy of a bill, a plan or hardship ask, a stop/restart names no service, so the letter read *"We have your request for —— at 14 Oak St"* with a 15-working-day target date for a copy of a bill (SR-26-0065 on the walk copy). So the email goes only when the request has at least one service row AND the email is valid. Every other portal ask keeps exactly its behaviour before `DEF-CWP-10539`: nothing queued, absence reason `applicant_supplied_no_email_or_phone`. Worked: Kyle Mark's Start service application for Water with `kyle.mark@example.test` → one email; Lee Park's *copy of a bill* with `lee.park@example.test` → none. The staff path is unchanged.
2. **The application's acknowledgement carries the state (`DEF-CWP-10541`).** The portal asks no state (the blueprint draws none; the draft model says *"the utility's own state is assumed"*), and the form already shows the applicant one: `selectors.draft_service_address` writes the matched premises' state, else the utility's own (`tenancy_seam.utility_state`, the company profile's state as a two-letter code). The request now receives that same state in `address_state_as_given` at Send — the state the applicant saw on *Check and send* — so the email reads *"900 Walk Lane, Rosenberg, TX 77471"* as the screen did. No new form field. A utility with no state on its profile sends none, as the screen shows none (law 3). `address_state_as_given` joins the guest whitelist beside the town and ZIP it was missing from.

## 2026-10-22 — One greeting for every letter: the bill, the statement and the property-sale letters use the shared builder (lane GREETING, `DEF-NOT-10542`; our judgment, recorded, not put to the PO — law 13)

Found on lane BILL-LINK's browser walk: bill BL-2610-000251 greeted *"Hi Miller,,"* because the contact is stored *"Miller, Sarah"* and `billing.delivery_seam.bill_render_context` took the first word of the name. The rule is already ruled (2026-09-07 first word; 2026-10-22 CR-190 MOVEIN-MSG: surname-first greets the given name, a company is greeted by its whole name) and lives in ONE function, `notifications.customer_context.greeting_name`. Three more writers still split the name themselves: `billing.statement` (first word, same fault) and the three property-sale letters in `notifications.transfer_events` (everything after the last comma — so *"Sarah Miller"* was greeted *"Hi Sarah Miller,"*). All four now call `greeting_name`; no second parser.

1. **No given name → the whole name, never a stray comma.** *"Miller,"* (a comma with nothing after it) now greets *"Miller"*, not *"Miller,"*. Worked: *"Miller, Sarah"* → Sarah · *"Sarah Miller"* → Sarah · *"Sarah"* → Sarah · *"Miller,"* → Miller · *"Acme Holdings LLC"* as a company → Acme Holdings LLC.
2. **The bill keeps its snapshot name (BR-BIL-030) and makes no query.** `bill_render_context` runs once per bill inside `issue_invoice` and is tested to make zero queries, so it passes the name stamped at gather to `greeting_name` rather than re-reading the customer. The bill payload carries no person/company kind, so a company on a bill (and on a statement or a sale letter, whose writers hold no kind either) is still greeted by the first word of its name, as before this fix. That residual is filed as its own defect rather than solved by reading the customer on every bill.

## 2026-10-23 — Portal application fee: the applicant chooses Pay now or Pay later, and the acknowledgement says which (direction ruled; three details put back)

Raised by lane PORTAL-SR-ACK. A portal application carries an unpaid **$10.00** application fee (Ann Arbor), and its acknowledgement says *"Nothing is charged for making a request."* We recommended sending the fee wording. **PO, verbatim:** *"Provide an option for the user to choose whether to pay the $10.00 application fee now or later, and display the applicable fee message accordingly."*

**Ruled (direction):**
- The portal application asks the applicant *Pay now* or *Pay later* for the application fee.
- The acknowledgement states the matching fee sentence. *"Nothing is charged"* is never sent on a request that carries a fee.

**Signed rulings it touches, stated rather than assumed (law 13):**
- 2026-09-22 *"THE APPLICATION FEE IS RAISED AT APPROVAL, NOT AT CAPTURE"*. Its reason was that an abandoned or refused application must not leave a charge behind. *Pay now* takes money before approval.
- 2026-09-23 *"NO APPLICATION FEE IS EVER CARRIED TO AN ACCOUNT — IT IS PAID OR WAIVED"*. *Pay later* must therefore still end paid or waived, never as a balance on an account.
- 2026-09-22 *"`Collect later` LOSES ONE [door]"*. That was the STAFF capture form, and it is not reversed by this. The portal gets its own choice.

Three details were put to the PO the same turn: what *Pay later* means, what happens to a *Pay now* fee if the request is refused or withdrawn, and how *Pay now* is paid. Nothing is built until they are answered.

## 2026-10-23 — Portal application fee: paid online at submission, no "Pay later", not refunded (supersedes the "choose Pay now or Pay later" direction above)

The three details put back in the entry above.

**PO, verbatim:**
1. *"if there is a application or service fee then consumer will have to pay it online; they can't say pay later"*
2. *"That is application fee it is not refunded generally many time utilities charger 0 application fees"*
3. *"3A"* (card on the same screen, through the portal's existing online payment, and the request is submitted only once the payment succeeds).

**Ruled:**
- **No choice is offered.** A portal application or request that carries an application or service fee greater than $0.00 must be paid online by card on its last step. The request is submitted only when the payment succeeds. A failed or abandoned payment submits nothing and leaves no charge.
- **A fee of $0.00, or no fee, means no payment step.** The acknowledgement says *"Nothing is charged for making a request."* (worked case: many utilities charge $0.00).
- **The fee is not refunded** if the request is later refused or withdrawn. It is an application fee.
- **The acknowledgement for a paid request** states the fee received, e.g. *"We received your $10.00 application fee."* using the fee acknowledgement class.

**Supersedes, for PORTAL requests only:**
- 2026-09-22 *"THE APPLICATION FEE IS RAISED AT APPROVAL, NOT AT CAPTURE"*. A portal fee is paid, and recorded as revenue, at submission. Its "no charge left behind" reason still holds, because an unpaid portal application is never submitted.
- The "choose" direction of the entry above.

**Unchanged:**
- staff-entered requests (the fee is raised at approval, and is paid or waived, 2026-09-22/23);
- *"no application fee is ever carried to an account"*.

## 2026-10-23 — Portal application fee paid online: how it is built (`CR-191-BRC10`, lane PORTAL-FEE; our judgments, law 13)

Building the ruling above. The rules ran out on nine points; each is decided here, before code, with its figure.

1. **The money is a `counter_receipts` row, not a `payments` row.** A portal applicant has no account, and *"no application fee is ever carried to an account"* (2026-09-23). The counter fee already lives in `counter_receipts`; the portal fee joins it with method `card`. One table for every application fee, whoever took it.
2. **The same two postings the counter uses, both at submission.** Collection: DR the card method's clearing account, else `1010 Undeposited funds` · CR `2400 Customer credit balances`. Then at once: DR `2400` · CR the application-fee charge code's own revenue account. The receipt lands in state `earned`, the state a refused counter fee lands in, because a portal fee is non-refundable from the moment it is paid. **Worked (Ann Arbor, `$10.00`):** DR 1010 10.0000 / CR 2400 10.0000, then DR 2400 10.0000 / CR 4600 10.0000. `2400` nets to zero.
3. **The charge comes first and the writes come after, in one transaction.** The card is charged before anything is written. A decline or a silent provider writes nothing in customers or payments; the integrations run row stays, which is that module's own record of the attempt. On approval, ONE transaction writes the request, its fee line, the receipt, both journal entries, the audit rows and the acknowledgement.
4. **The idempotency key is `appfee:<tenant>:<draft token>:<attempt token>`.** The browser mints the attempt token once per visit to the last step, as quick pay does, and mints a new one after a decline. A retry with the same token is one debit at the provider. If the first attempt committed, the retry finds the draft already submitted and returns the same reference without charging. **Worked:** press twice, or lose the response and retry → one request, one receipt, one pair of postings.
5. **The fee is re-read at submit and compared, never trusted.** The screen sends the fee it showed; if the utility's price differs now, the submit is refused with *"The amount changed. Please look again."* before the card is touched.
6. **Receipt number = the request number; the provider's reference goes in `confirmation`.** The acknowledgement prints the receipt number, and `appfee:…` is not something a person can read down a telephone. **Worked:** *"You paid $10.00 by card. Your receipt number is SR-26-0042."*
7. **The acknowledgement keeps the existing fee class wording.** *"You paid {fee_amount} by {fee_method}. Your receipt number is {receipt_no}."* already states the amount received, in the region's money format. The PO's *"We received your $10.00 application fee."* was an example (*"e.g."*), so no template or migration is touched. The screen's own Sent panel says *"We received your $10.00 application fee."*
8. **Approval, refusal and withdrawal move no money.** The line is collected, so the fee condition reads `$0.00` outstanding. Approval's release finds the receipt already `earned` and posts nothing; refusal does the same; withdrawal never touched money. Staff-entered requests are unchanged.
9. **A utility with a fee above $0.00 and no card provider connected cannot take portal applications.** That is what *"they can't say pay later"* means where there is no way to pay. The last step shows the held reason, *"Card payment is not available."*, and the button stays off. This is reported to the PO as a consequence, not asked as a question.

Not in scope: quick asks, reports, questions and disputes carry no application fee (`create_from_portal` adds one only for `application=True`), so they are unchanged.

## 2026-10-23 — Portal accessibility, Group A (contrast, F-01 and F-09): the new colours confirmed

**Context.** Bynry's Senior QA tester assessed the SMART360 customer portal against WCAG 2.1 AA: axe-core in Chrome, Firefox and Safari engines, keyboard, forms, and VoiceOver.
- The findings: 24, sharing nine root causes, Groups A–I.
- The contract with the City of Ann Arbor (Exhibit A §3) promises contrast and focus by week 6, chart text by week 10, status messages by week 12, and an Accessibility Conformance Report within 12 weeks. The bill PDF is Attachment 1 row 16.

**The tester's working rules, binding on every group:**
- fix the shared root cause;
- list every similar place before changing anything;
- any colour change shows old value, new value and ratio, and is confirmed first;
- remove no features or fields and weaken no validation;
- English and Spanish for any new text (we write all 11 catalogues);
- no real customer data;
- a product decision is asked, never guessed.

**Group A as reported:**
- 204 text elements fail 4.5:1 on 22 of 23 pages; 161 of them are `#7d7979` (`text-neutral-600`) at 4.30:1 on white.
- The worst is `#9b9797` on `#f3f2f2` at 2.58:1.
- Input and select borders are `#d7d3d3` at 1.48:1, where 3:1 is required.

**Measured by us.** These are shared tokens in `styles/tokens.css` / `tailwind.css`, used by the staff app too: grey-600 456 uses, 202 in the portal. There are no hard-coded copies.

**Proposed, and confirmed by the PO/QA, verbatim:** *"this is correct"* —

| Use | Old | New | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Secondary text, grey-600 token | `#7d7979` | `#6b6767` | 5.58 on white · 5.00 on `#f3f2f2` · 4.54 on `#eae7e7` |
| Lightest text (grey-500 used AS TEXT) | `#9b9797` | moved to the new grey-600; the grey-500 token itself is unchanged | 5.58 / 5.00 |
| Field and select borders | `#d7d3d3` | `#8c8888`, a NEW field-border token used only by inputs and selects | 3.50 on white · 3.14 on `#f3f2f2` |
| Dividers and card lines | `#d7d3d3` | unchanged | no 3:1 rule applies |

**Still open, put the same day:**
- (2) whole product or portal only;
- (3) a utility's brand colour that fails with white text (sample `#EC3013` = 4.20);
- the three product questions on F-18, F-17 and F-11.

The inventory and baseline (read-only) start now. No colour is changed until (2) is answered.

**Ruled:**
1. The three colours of the entry above are confirmed again.
2. **They apply to the WHOLE product**: the shared tokens change, so the staff back office darkens too. One standard everywhere (B14 rules 44 and 45). This is not a portal-only override.

**PO/QA, verbatim:** *"1 … Option A; 2 … A (recommended) It still switches instantly. Focus stays on the selector, and a screen reader hears "Showing account AC-2026-00057" or "Página en español". Each selector's label says it changes the page.; 3 … A (recommended) The number is removed. "Phone removed." If she has text reminders on, she is told: "Text reminders stop without a phone.""*

**Ruled:**
1. **F-18.** A badly formed email gets a field error BEFORE sending, on forgot-password and sign-in: *"Enter a full email address, like name@example.com."* An empty password gets *"Enter your password."* Everything else is unchanged: forgot-password's single message for every well-formed address plus the "Update your registered email" link (2026-10-22, BR-CWP-038), and sign-in's one message for a wrong email or password. Nothing reveals whether an account exists.

Asked whether keyboard users should switch the language/account selector with Enter (arrow keys alone not switching) while a mouse pick switches at once. **PO/QA, verbatim:** *"Arrow keys will switch only"*, then *"Start B and C group"*.

**Our reading (law 13, stated so a later reader can check it):** the arrow keys DO switch, exactly as a pick does today. No Enter step is added. This is consistent with the F-17 answer of the same day ("It still switches instantly"). On every switch:

## 2026-10-23 — Portal accessibility, Group H (bill PDF, F-06): tagged PDFs through a PDF library, Liberation Sans, new documents only, every customer PDF

**Measured by us:**
- The bill PDF is written by our own standard-library writer (`billing/documents.py`) with the Base-14 fonts, which by design are never embedded.
- It has no structure tree, no `/Lang` and no title setting. That is the whole of the QA tester's veraPDF result: PDF/UA-1, 7 rules, 360 checks, on BL-2609-000651.
- The same frozen payload already serialises to HTML with real headings and tables.
- Other customer PDFs: agreements (`customers/agreements.py`), and statements and final bills (through the bill writer).
- Issued documents are write-once (hard rule 4).

**PO/QA, verbatim:** *"1 … B … 2 … A. Liberation Sans … 3 … A. New bills only. The old ones stay as issued.; 4 … A. Everything a customer receives: bills, final bills, statements, agreements, reminders, disconnection notices, receipts, letters."*

**Ruled:**
1. **Customer PDFs are produced by a PDF library that writes tagged PDF/UA-1 (WeasyPrint) from the document's existing HTML serialisation.** This reverses our own 2026-08 engineering choice of "no PDF library" (`documents.py`'s docstring); it was never a PO ruling. The server image gains the library and its system dependencies. Hard-won law 4 applies: a running host gets it only when its image is rebuilt.
2. **The font is Liberation Sans, embedded and subset.** It is metrically identical to Helvetica and Arial, so layouts do not move.
   - Consequence, stated rather than asked (law 13): Liberation Sans has no Devanagari, Japanese or Korean glyphs.
   - The Base-14 fonts have none either, so Hindi, Japanese and Korean PDFs are no worse than today.
   - Their non-Latin text stays a known gap, filed as a defect, not silently patched with another font.
3. **New documents only.** Documents already issued stay exactly as kept. No accessible copy of an old bill is generated.
4. **Scope: every PDF a customer receives** — bills, final bills, statements, agreements, reminders, disconnection notices, receipts and letters. Staff-only prints (work orders, day packs, reports) are out of scope.

**Proof.**
- veraPDF PDF/UA-1 must report 0 failed rules on a sample of every in-scope type × utility layout × language.
- The new PDF's text and money figures must equal the old writer's for the same payload; any difference fails a test.
