## 2026-10-23 — Group A colour build: four judgments where the ruling ran out (lane A11Y-A-COLOUR)

These are ours to decide (law 13). Each is written before the code that depends on it.

**1. "The dark ink" is black, `#000000`.**
- It is the dark ink the product already uses for text on a tenant's colour: the brand mark (`apps/tenancy/brand.py` `INK_DARK`, OQ-800(a), 2026-08-30), mirrored in `BrandMark.tsx`.
- It is the only reading under which the ruling's own worked case is corrected. On `#EC3013`: white **4.20**, black **5.00**. The product's text ink `#201e1d` scores **3.95**, which is WORSE than white.
- **Consequence for (b), stated plainly:** with black as the dark ink, every colour reaches 4.5:1 with white or black. The weakest case is where they tie, at **4.58:1** (the OQ-800(a) derivation). So the Company → Profile refusal is built, tested and wired, and **with today's inks it can never fire.** It fires only if the dark ink is changed. This is reported to the PO; nothing is invented to make it fire.

**2. Hover and pressed get their own ink.** The primary button darkens on hover (`88%` of the brand, rest black) and on press (`72%`). With black text that can fail: `#EC3013` hover **4.02**, pressed **2.96**. So each of the three steps picks its own ink by the same rule. On `#EC3013`: rest black 5.00, hover white 5.22, pressed white 7.10. No new colour is introduced.

**3. A utility with no colour of its own is corrected too.** It shows the product accent `#ec3013`, which is the same colour as the sample and fails the same way. The portal frame applies the rule to that default.

**4. Staff screens keep their present text on the accent.** Ruling (a) names the portal. The kit now reads one variable for "text on the accent", which is `--color-bg` everywhere except inside the portal frame. That leaves staff primary buttons at `#f3f2f2` on `#ec3013` = **3.76:1**. It is reported as open, not changed.

**Found while building, reported and NOT changed (each needs a colour the tester has not confirmed):**
- Brand-coloured TEXT and links on white: `#EC3013` on white = **4.20:1**.
- Staff fields are filled `#eae9e9`, where the new field border reads **2.89:1**. It reads 3.50 on the portal's white fields.

## 2026-10-23 — Portal accessibility, Groups B and C: how they are built (lane A11Y-BC; our judgments, law 13)

Building the two entries above. The rules ran out on these points; each is decided here, before code, with its figure. Inventory and before/after: `08-qa/a11y-portal-2026-10/group-bc-inventory.md`.

1. **One announcer per frame, two regions.** `PortalShell` and `GuestFrame` each mount one always-present polite region and one assertive region (only one frame is ever on screen). A form's result goes to polite, a refusal or error summary to assertive. The SAME sentence twice (two failed sign-ins) is announced twice: each message replaces the region's child node rather than its text. Worked: two wrong passwords in a row → *"Those details do not match."* heard twice.
2. **The field wires itself.** `FormField` publishes its id, its error, its helper and `required` to the box inside it, so `TextInput`, `SelectInput`, `DialInput` and `PortalDateField` set `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby` (helper, then error) and `aria-required` with no prop passed. An explicit prop still wins. **`aria-required`, never the native `required`**: the native one would let the browser's own bubble replace our message, which is a visible change and a different sentence in each browser.
3. **A required box left empty is caught on the screen, before sending.** The message is *"Fill this in."* / *"Rellene este campo."* (one key, `portal.form.required`; an instruction of three words, B14 rule 33). It applies only where the field is ALREADY drawn with the asterisk, so no field becomes required that was not, and nothing the server checks is removed (validation is added in front, never taken away). Worked: Sign in with both boxes empty → two field errors, the summary, nothing sent.
4. **The error summary.** On a failed submit a box headed *"Check these fields"* / *"Revise estos campos"* appears at the top of the form, one link per field (*"Email: Enter a full email address, like name@example.com."*), and takes focus. A link moves focus into its box. It is drawn only after a failed submit, so a form at rest looks exactly as before.
5. **Focus after a submit.** Fail → the summary (or, when the server refused with no field to name, the refusal sentence itself). Success → the result sentence, or the heading of the next step or screen.
6. **Focus after a page change.** On every change of address INSIDE the portal (not the first load), focus moves to the page's `h1` and the page is announced once, politely, through ONE entry point (`announcePage`). Lane A11Y-D owns page titles and may pass the title to that entry point; we read the `h1` text until then. Worked: *Bills* from the tab bar → focus on *"Bills"*, heard once.
7. **Opened and replaced content.** An Ask card's *Ask →* moves focus to the form's heading; *Back to the list* returns focus to the card that opened it. The same helper serves every open/replace/close pair on the inventory.
8. **The selectors (F-17, ruled).** After a switch the element is re-found by its `data-` attribute and refocused, because the page re-renders under it. The announcement is in the NEW language: *"Showing account AC-2026-00057"* / *"Mostrando la cuenta AC-2026-00057"*, *"Page in English"* / *"Página en español"*. The labels say they change the page: *"Account (changes the page)"*, *"Language (changes the page)"*, with the matching Spanish.
9. **A disabled button's reason (F-22).** The kit's `CommitButton` and `HeldButton` draw the reason as a sentence under the button and point the button at it with `aria-describedby`; `title` stays for the mouse. Every hand-built `disabled title=` on the inventory moves onto the kit. This is the arrangement `HeldButton` and `HeldCommit` already draw, so no new look is introduced.
10. **F-11, My details.**
    - The phone check is the portal's existing one (`applications.phone_ok`: ten digits once punctuation is gone, or eleven starting with 1) and the ZIP check is the existing `US_ZIP` (five digits or ZIP+4). They are not loosened or tightened; a test holds the customers copy equal to the portal one. Worked: `abc` → *"Enter a 10-digit phone number."*; `1` → *"Enter a 5-digit ZIP."*; `(281) 555-0164` and `77471-1234` save.
    - An empty phone box REMOVES the phone on every account the login holds, and the response says so (`phone_removed`). *"Phone removed."* is shown; *"Text reminders stop without a phone."* is added when any of those accounts has text reminders on. **The text-reminder switch itself is not turned off** — the ruling tells the customer, it does not change her setting, and switching it off would be a second change she did not ask for.
    - *"Saved on 0 accounts."* is never shown. A save that changed nothing reads *"No changes were saved."* / *"No se guardó ningún cambio."*.
    - A blank ZIP is allowed (the mailing address is optional); only a malformed one is refused.
11. **F-18.** Sign-in checks the email's shape with the same pattern forgot-password already uses (`EMAIL_SHAPE`) and an empty password, before sending. Sign-in's single sentence for every wrong email or password is untouched (BR-CWP-004, BR-CWP-038).
    - **Amended the same day, while building:** the ruled sentence *"Enter a full email address, like name@example.com."* goes in a NEW screen-only key, `portal.form.emailFormat`, used by sign-in and forgot-password for a malformed address. The server's own refusal key `portal.reset.email_invalid` (*"Please enter a valid email."*) is left as it was, because the ruled sentence is **seven words** and `G33` holds every server refusal to six (B14 rule 33). Rewording the server key would have needed the G33 baseline widened, which this lane may not do. A malformed address never reaches the server from the screen, so a customer sees the ruled sentence; only a direct API caller sees the old one.
    - **Stated, not assumed (law 13):** the ruled sentence is itself one word over B14 rule 33's six-word cap for an instruction. We built the PO's words verbatim, as the later and more specific ruling; if the cap should win, the shortest faithful form is *"Enter a full email, like name@example.com."* (six words).

## 2026-10-23 — Portal application fee: one charge per application, even across a reload (`DEF-PAY-10554`, `CR-191-BRC10`, lane PORTAL-FEE-2; our judgments, law 13)

**What was wrong.** Judgment 4 of *"Portal application fee paid online: how it is built"* made the card key `appfee:<tenant>:<draft token>:<attempt token>`, with the attempt token minted by the browser once per visit. If the card was approved and the request then could not be written, and the applicant reloaded the page before pressing again, the browser minted a new attempt token, so the provider saw a NEW key and could debit `$10.00` a second time. There is no void or refund path, and the fee is not refunded (PO 2026-10-23). **Judgment 4's key is SUPERSEDED by the rules below; judgments 1–3 and 5–9 are unchanged.**

**Ruled by us (the rules ran out; nothing here touches a price, a posting or a signed figure):**

1. **The server makes the key and keeps it on the draft.** Key = `appfee:<tenant id>:<draft id>:<fee to four places>:<declines so far>`, stored in `portal_application_drafts.fee_idempotency_key` before the card is charged, and presented on every attempt for that draft until it is submitted. The browser's attempt token is no longer read. The draft's database id is used, not its link token, because the key is sent to the card provider and printed in the receipt's `confirmation`, and the link token is the applicant's secret. A key DERIVED from facts is safe here although `gateway.mint` warns against one: one draft is one application and is paid once, so two genuine charges on one key cannot exist.
2. **Before charging, the draft is asked whether a charge was already approved.** Our gateway adapter interface has four methods (validate, test, execute, describe) and none looks a charge up by key, so there is nothing to ask the provider. So the moment the provider approves, the approval (reference, amount, currency, brand, last four, run id) is written to `portal_application_drafts.fee_charge_approved` in its OWN transaction block (a savepoint when nested; law 14), BEFORE the request is written. If the request write then fails, that row stays. Every later attempt finds it and records that charge instead of charging. It is not cleared on submit; it is the draft's record of the money it took.
3. **A decline moves the key on; silence does not.** A provider answers a reused key with its first answer, so after a definite decline the decline count goes up by one and the next press uses a new key. After no answer (a timeout) the key is kept, because the money may have moved and the same key is what stops a second debit.
4. **A kept approval is never charged again, whatever the price does.** If the utility changes the fee after an approved charge and before it is recorded, the attempt does not compare the screen's figure, ask for a card or ask the provider; it hands the kept approval to the request write. ⚠ The customers module's own door still refuses an approved amount that is not the CURRENT fee, so in that narrow case every retry answers *"We could not record that payment."* and charges nothing; the approval stays on the draft. That residual is `DEF-PAY-10568`, filed rather than solved here, because which figure wins is a money rule on another module's door.
5. **A draft holding an approved charge it never recorded is not deleted by the 30-day clean-up.** Deleting it would remove our only record (outside integrations' run row) that the applicant paid.

**Worked (Pine Hill, `$10.00`):** draft `d-1` → key `appfee:<t>:d-1:10.0000:0`. Approved → the approval is written on the draft. The request write fails → *"We could not record that payment."*. The applicant reloads (new browser token) and presses again → the draft's approval is found, the provider is NOT asked, and ONE request, ONE counter receipt and TWO postings (DR 1010 10.0000 / CR 2400 10.0000, DR 2400 10.0000 / CR 4600 10.0000) are written. Provider runs: 1. A declined first press → key `…:10.0000:0` declined, the next press uses `…:10.0000:1`. A new draft `d-2` → key `appfee:<t>:d-2:10.0000:0` and charges normally.
## 2026-10-23 — Group H (F-06, `DEF-BIL-10546`): build judgments for tagged customer PDFs, recorded before the switch

Lane A11Y-H, under the Group H ruling of the same day. Where the rules ran out, these are ours (law 13), each with its figure.

**Baseline, measured before any change.** veraPDF 1.28.2, PDF/UA-1, on fake data:
- 20 bill samples (5 layouts × a West Des Moines-like and an Ann Arbor-like set-up × English and Spanish customers) and 4 agreements (sent and stamped, English and Spanish).
- **Every one fails the same 7 rules:** 6.2-1, 7.1-3, 7.1-8, 7.1-10, 7.1-11, 7.2-34, 7.21.4.1-1. Failed checks per bill: 321 to 574. Per agreement: 27 to 32.
- That matches QA's BL-2609-000651 (7 rules).

**Judgments:**
1. **Which writer.** A draft gets the tagged page. That covers the pre-issue render kept at issue, a move-out's drafted final bill and the layout preview, so every bill issued from now on is tagged. An already-issued bill keeps its kept original. Where none exists (issued before v2.88.0), its re-render stays on the old writer: ruling 3, *"New bills only"*. The old writer is kept for that and for the parity test.
2. **A bill's language is English.** Every label on a bill is English and no bill has ever been printed in another language, so `/Lang` is `en`. A Spanish-speaking customer's bill carries their own name and the utility's own message under English labels, as today. A Spanish bill does not exist to tag. The agreement's `/Lang` is the language it was published in (its body is nearly every word).
3. **Characters Liberation Sans cannot draw print as `?` and are named**, exactly as the old writer did (OQ-150, *"print a substitution"*). No fallback font is allowed to supply them. Worked: a Japanese agreement body of 18 characters prints 18 `?` on both writers. Hindi, Japanese and Korean stay a filed gap.
4. **The usage table says what the printed page said.** An unread month shows `—` (never `0`), an estimated month shows `13*`, and a `* estimated` note follows. The HTML used to show an empty cell and a separate row of bare `E`s. A screen reader would announce those as "blank" and "E".
5. **The remittance barcode is decoration.** It is drawn from the same bars at the same width, as a background, so the tagged file marks it as an artifact. The line printed under it is the text. The logo's text alternative is the stamped utility name plus "logo".
6. **Reminders, disconnection notices, receipts and letters are not PDFs today.** They freeze as text and the print vendor receives text (`notifications/frozen_documents.py`). There is no inaccessible PDF to switch. Making them PDFs is new work (CR-049 task 6), filed rather than built here.

**The cost, measured, stated rather than hidden.**
- Median of 5 renders of the Ann Arbor-like sample bill, after a discarded warm-up, on 4 cores: **0.524 s tagged against 0.0055 s for the old writer.**
- A 2,000-bill cycle run therefore spends about **17 more minutes** of one worker's time at issue.
- Bill runs issue in background jobs (`billing/run_jobs.py`), not in a 60-second web request. A single-bill issue (a correction, a one-time bill) adds about half a second.
- Filed as a performance defect to measure on a real run, not assumed to fit.

## 2026-10-23 — Portal accessibility, Groups D and E: how it is built (lane A11Y-D; our judgments, law 13)

Building the two Group D and Group E entries above. Measured first on a private copy of the Pine Hill fixture, every one of the portal's 55 routes (53 reachable with this login), signed out and in, English and Spanish: 212 page loads (`08-qa/a11y-portal-2026-10/group-d-inventory.md`). The rules ran out on eight points; each is decided here, before code, with its figure.

1. **`<html lang>` is set in one place, the i18n instance, for both apps.** Every language switch in the portal and the staff app goes through it, and the first load does too. **Worked:** switch to Español → `<html lang="es">`; before, 106 of 106 Spanish page loads still said `en`.
2. **The tab title is read from the page's own h1, by one component at the portal's root.** An open dialog's heading wins over the page. While no heading is drawn (loading), the title is the utility's name alone. A per-page title call was rejected: 55 routes would carry 55 second copies of their headings, free to drift. **Worked:** `/pay` → *"Find your bill · Pine Hill Water & Power"*; in Spanish *"Busque su factura · Pine Hill Water & Power"*. Before, all 212 loads read *"SMART360 Next"*. The portal has **no dialogs today** (0 `role="dialog"` in `src/portal`), so the dialog rule has nothing to title yet. The middle dot is joined in code, not held in a catalogue: both halves are already in the reader's language, and a key holding only `{{page}} · {{utility}}` would be eleven copies of one glyph. Lane A11Y-BC's page announcement speaks the same page name.
3. **Heading levels come from the nesting, not the look, and only where the portal asks.** The portal's root declares that a section heading is an h2. A panel, a form section or an errand card takes that level and hands the next one to what it contains. Outside the portal no level is declared, so every staff screen keeps its h3, byte for byte. Each heading keeps its own size class, and `global.css` sets only the font size per tag, which that class overrides. So nothing moves visually; the after-scan compares every heading's computed size. **Worked:** `/my-details/preferences` went h1 *How we contact you* → h3 *PAPER*; now it goes h1 → h2.
4. **A signed-out visit to a signed-in address shows the shared failure card, and its first line becomes the page's level-1 heading in the portal only.** It stays the same `<p>` with the same class, marked `role="heading" aria-level="1"`, so it looks the same. **Worked:** 36 signed-in addresses × 2 languages = 72 loads with no heading at all before.
5. **The utility's emergency notice above every guest page's h1 becomes an h2.** It is a frame notice drawn before the page title, so an h2 there is not a skipped level. The tests allow nothing deeper than an h2 above the h1.
6. **One wording for a card action's name, in all eleven catalogues** (`portal.actionName`): `{{label}}: {{value}}`. French writes `{{label}} : {{value}}` and Japanese uses a full-width colon. *(Amended the same day during the build: the placeholders were first named `{{action}}`/`{{card}}`; renamed to the shape `G15` already accepts as language-neutral, so no allow-list moved.)* The arrow is dropped from the name, because a screen reader would read *"right arrow"* mid-name. **Worked:** *"Start →"* in the *Pay a bill* card is named *"Start: Pay a bill"*; a document row's eye icon *"Open this document: BL-2610-000052"*. Links that share a name AND a destination (every *Pay* goes to `/pay-now`) are left, because 2.4.4 asks only that one name not mean two places.
7. **Language names keep their own spelling and gain their own `lang`.** That covers the selector options, *"Also written in"*, and the name inside the help fallback sentence. The sentence is cut at the name, so no catalogue line is re-keyed. A help answer's body carries the language the server chose for it.
8. **One name per function (Group E ruling 1):** Home's *"Ask for a plan"* takes each catalogue's existing *"Ask for a payment plan"* wording. *Your account*'s *"Equipment"* door uses *"Meters and equipment"*, the Usage page's words. The signed-in Requests heading *"Your requests"* takes each catalogue's existing wording for that list. No new translation was invented for any of the three.

**Not changed, and reported:**
- Quick pay's and Pay now's no-receipt states share the h1 *"We cannot show that receipt here"*. These are refusal states, not pages, and rewording one is a product choice.
- A help answer's own question, drawn as its h1, is not marked with the answer's language. The shared page header takes its title as plain text.
- The *Check and send* summary line names the chosen language inside a joined text line.
- Bill emails declare no language at all (`email_format.py`'s wrapper has no `<html lang>`). The bill PDF declares `/Lang en` and is printed in English (Group H, `DOCUMENT_LANGUAGE`).

## 2026-10-23 — Group A, the eight remaining colour decisions: all agreed as recommended

Put to the PO/QA as a table with old values, new values and ratios. **Verbatim:** *"For this we are agreed to your recommondation"*.

**Ruled:**
1. **The dark ink on a light brand fill is black `#000000`.** `#EC3013` with black reads 5.00. Our text colour `#201e1d` reads 3.95, worse than white's 4.20.
2. **Brand colour used as TEXT** (kicker labels, links, outline buttons) takes the brand's own hover shade automatically: the brand mixed 88% with black, e.g. `#EC3013` → `#D02A11`. Ratios: 4.20 → 5.22 on white, 3.75 → 4.67 on `#f3f2f2`.
3. **Company → Profile also refuses a brand colour** that cannot reach 4.5:1 as text on white even after that darkening, or 3:1 as a focus ring on white and on `#f3f2f2`. The message says why. Worked case: `#F5C518` is refused.
4. **The future-step circle and last year's chart bar** move `#d7d3d3` → `#8c8888` (1.48 → 3.50). Option B: no reliance on the exemption.
5. **A switched-off errand card keeps grey-500 text.** It is an inactive control, exempt (2.59).
6. **Staff form fields are filled white** (border 2.89 → 3.50).
7. **Staff primary buttons use the same automatic text-colour rule as the portal** (3.76 → 5.00 on `#EC3013`).
8. **The bill PDF footer and absent-value grey** move `#97918e` → `#6b6767` (3.11 → 5.58).

## 2026-10-23 — Group A, the eight decisions: how they are built (lane A11Y-A-FINISH; our judgments, law 13)

Building the entry above, *"Group A, the eight remaining colour decisions"*. The rules ran out on these points; each is decided here, before code, with its figure.

1. **The dark ink stays black `#000000`.** It is already `INK_DARK` in `lib/contrast.ts` and in `apps/tenancy/brand.py`; nothing moves.
2. **One new variable for brand-coloured TEXT, `--color-accent-text`, set by the same frame code as the inks** (`GuestFrame.tsx` `brandStyle`, which `PortalShell` and `PortalApp` already use).
   - The shade is the brand mixed 88% with black. When that is still under 4.5:1 on `#f3f2f2`, the share of brand drops ONE point at a time (87%, 86% …) until it reaches 4.5. One point at a time keeps the shade as close to the utility's own colour as the rule allows.
   - Worked: `#EC3013` → `#D02A11` at 88% (5.22 on white, 4.67 on `#f3f2f2`). `#E8590C` is 4.03 on `#f3f2f2` at 88%, so it goes on to 82%, `#BE490A` (5.06 / 4.53). `#1D3557` → `#1A2F4D` (13.48 / 12.07).
   - A utility with no colour shows our accent `#ec3013` and gets the same `#D02A11`.
   - **Staff screens are unchanged**: outside the portal frame the variable is `var(--color-accent)`. The decision names the portal's kickers, links and outline buttons, and the lane brief scopes it to the portal. Staff brand-coloured text (`#ec3013` on `#f3f2f2`, 3.76) is reported, not changed.
   - Which classes move: every `text-accent` the portal renders (36 in `src/portal`, plus the shared panel kicker, outline and link buttons, row-action menu, page-header back link and active tab, the failure card's link, the modal kicker and the required `*`). Borders, fills, the focus ring and the chart bars keep `--color-accent`: they are not text, and 3:1 is what they need.
3. **Company → Profile's second refusal reads the PRIMARY colour only.** `brand_accent_hex` is drawn nowhere (`DEF-CWP-3737`), so refusing it as text would refuse a colour no one can see. The old fill refusal still reads both.
   - Refused when the 88% shade is under 4.5:1 on white, OR the colour itself is under 3:1 on white or on `#f3f2f2` (the focus ring).
   - As before, an unchanged colour is never refused, so a utility that already has one can still save the tab; the frame darkens its text.
   - Worked: `#F5C518` — shade `#D8AD15` 2.12 on white; ring 1.63 / 1.46 → refused. `#EC3013` — 5.22; ring 4.20 / 3.76 → saved. `#E8590C` — 4.50; ring 3.58 / 3.20 → saved.
   - The message is a new key, `settings.company.hex_too_light`: *"Too light for text on white. Choose a darker color."* (two sentences of 6 and 4 words, B14 rule 33), in all 11 catalogues.
4. **The future-step circle and last year's bar use the existing `--color-field-border` token (`#8c8888`).** It is the value the decision names, and a second token with the same value would be two names for one colour. The token's comment now lists the three uses. Dividers stay `#d7d3d3`.
5. **Staff fields are filled white through a new token, `--color-field-fill: #ffffff`,** on the four shared field rules (`.input`, `.view` fields, the app-bar search, the table pager select) and the kit's `AffixField`. On the portal `--color-surface` is already white, so nothing there moves. Worked: border 2.89 on `#eae9e9` → 3.50 on white.
6. **Staff primary buttons:** the stylesheet default of `--color-on-accent`, `-600` and `-700` moves from `--color-bg` to the inks the rule picks for our stock accent ramp: black on `#ec3013` (5.00), white on `#dd2b0f` (4.74) and on `#ae1800` (7.17). Staff screens show no tenant colour, so the stock ramp is the only fill they can show.
7. **The bill PDF's `#97918e` → `#6b6767`** in the tagged page's stylesheet in `billing/documents.py` (`--faint`: the absent value and the remittance stub's dashed rule). **The old writer's `FAINT` is NOT changed.** It now prints only re-renders of bills issued before v2.88.0, and Group H ruling 3 keeps those exactly as issued. The parity test compares text and money, not colour, so it is unaffected.

## 2026-10-24 — FOUR PO ANSWERS ON THE FIELD APP'S OPEN QUESTIONS (closes `OQ-FLD-12795`, `12796`, `12797`, `12800`)

Put as a table with a worked example and options each; answered verbatim:

Worked: Dana's job closed Monday 2 November leaves her phone at the first app start on or after 16 November.
3. **`OQ-FLD-12797` — certificate pinning: the issuing authority's key plus one backup authority's key, replaced at least 60 days before either expires — and NOT hard-coded.** PO: *"Trust the certificate issuer's key plus one backup issuer, replaced through an app update at least 60 days before either expires. plese dont hardcode it use settings - security values set in staff portal"*. **Our reading of HOW (law 13, recorded rather than re-asked):** the pin set lives in **Settings › Security** in the staff portal (each pin, its label and its expiry date); the phone downloads it with its other settings and keeps it. **A pin list can only be trusted if it arrives over a connection that is already pinned**, so the build carries the current set as a starting point and the server's list replaces it from then on; a list that would leave the phone with no valid pin is refused and the last good set kept. The portal warns 60 days before any pin expires. Worked: the issuer renews in 2027; the office adds the new issuer's key in Settings › Security in December 2026, every phone picks it up at its next sync, and no app update is needed.
4. **`OQ-FLD-12800` — the Work module blueprint is not required.** PO: *"not required"*. Work stays built to the blueprint's §1–§14; §15–§21 are not a source for this product and nothing is stubbed on them.

## 2026-10-24 — Route findings with no rule: BOTH the technician and the office may create the job (confirms `BR-WRK-067`'s reading)

Put to the PO with the worked case *Dana finds a broken seal on meter W-4471 on Elm Street; Brookfield has no rule for broken seals* and three options — A both (as built), B office only, C technician only. **PO, verbatim:** *"A. Both (as built, recommended)"*. ## 2026-10-24 — MQ-026: STARTING A JOB ACCEPTS IT; A NOT-YET-STARTED JOB CAN BE DECLINED WITH A REASON

Put to the PO with the worked case *the office assigns WO-0028 to D. Ortiz; she opens it on the phone and starts the safety checks*, and three options — A an Accept button, B starting the job counts as accepting, C drop the acceptance rule. **PO, verbatim:** *"B. Starting the job counts as accepting (recommended)- i am okay with this option but then reject icon or button should be there, to give a option to technician to refuse the job, you can suggest a better word for this button or icon"*.
**Built as:** (1) the first **Start** or **Open the job** on an assigned, unaccepted job sends the server's accept (`POST work/mobile/jobs/{id}/accept`) ahead of any of that job's work, so BR-WRK-059 holds and the office sees *"Accepted 08:05 by D. Ortiz"*; items already refused with *accept the job first* are resent automatically once the accept lands. (2) **The word is "Decline"** (our choice, the PO having asked us to suggest one): it matches the server's own act (`POST …/decline`, *"I can't take it"*), it is one word, and it does not collide with **Hand back**, which already exists for a job the technician has STARTED and returns it to the queue. So: **before starting → Decline** (a ✕ beside Start on the job card and on the job screen), **after starting → Hand back** (unchanged). Decline asks for a reason (a short list plus *Other* with a note), keeps the job on the technician's list marked *Declined* until the dispatcher reassigns it, and shows the office *"Declined by D. Ortiz — Not enough time"*. Worked: Dana is assigned WO-0031 at 07:40, taps ✕ Decline → *Not enough time*; the dispatcher's board shows it declined and reassigns it to Marco.

## 2026-10-24 — MQ-006: THE CODE FROM THE OFFICE SETS THE UTILITY (closes the never-filed `TENANT_SOURCE_QUESTION`)

Put to the PO with three options — A the office's code sets the utility, B a utility field on sign-in, C one build per utility — and the worked case *the Houston office adds Mark, Mark types `K7QM2P`, sees "City of Houston", sets a password and signs in with email + password from then on*. **PO, verbatim:** *"A. The code from the office sets the utility (recommended) - this is correct option , but how will you ensure the code is always unique?"*
**How uniqueness is guaranteed (our design, given to the PO in reply):** codes are drawn at random from 31 unambiguous characters (no 0/O, 1/I/L) — 31⁶ ≈ 887 million possible codes; every code ever issued is recorded in ONE platform-wide register with a **database UNIQUE constraint**, so two utilities can never hold the same code — the database refuses the second and a new one is drawn (a collision, at today's volumes, is about one in a million per code). **A code is never reused**, even after it expires or is used. The register stores a keyed hash of the code, never the code itself. Guessing is held off by the 7-day life, single use, and a limit on wrong tries per phone and per network address on the utility-free check door. Worked: Houston issues `K7QM2P`; when Brookfield's draw also lands on `K7QM2P`, the database refuses it and Brookfield's admin is shown `P3XW9A` instead — neither office ever sees the clash.

**2026-10-24, later — the uniqueness design CONFIRMED by the PO.** Shown the six safeguards as a table (one list for all utilities; the database refuses a duplicate and a new code is drawn, *Houston `K7QM2P`, Brookfield redrawn to `P3XW9A`*; ≈887 million codes; never reused; stored as a keyed fingerprint; 7 days, once, wrong tries limited). **PO: "this is correct".** ⚠ **One line of what was shown needs precision, and it was given to the PO in the same reply:** *"the limit follows Settings › Security"* is true only once the code has named the utility — the wrong-email count on that utility's code follows its `lockout_max_failed`. The utility-free lookup itself, which runs BEFORE any utility is known, is limited per phone and per network address by a platform-wide limit, because no utility's setting can apply to a request that has not yet named one.

## 2026-10-24 — MQ-031 / DEF-FLD-10589: A FONT-SIZE CHANGE IS HANDLED IN PLACE, AND THE LABELS ARE RE-MEASURED THROUGH THE LINE HEIGHT, NOT BY REMOUNTING THE APP

PO approved the fix for MQ-031 (*"yes"*): Android 16 aborted the field app ~1.7 s after the font size went 1.0 → 2.0 (1 try in 2), and after 2.0 → 1.0 every button label sat top-left until force-stop. **Cause:** MainActivity's `configChanges` lacked `fontScale` and `density`, so Android recreated the activity under a live React host. **Fix, part 1 (as approved):** `field-app/plugins/withFontScaleConfigChanges.js` adds both, keeping the eight existing values. **Our judgment, part 2 (law 13 — no rule covers it):** the approved sketch suggested re-keying the app root on `fontScale`. Reading React Native 0.79 showed it would NOT work: Fabric's C++ text-measure cache is keyed on the string, its layout attributes and constraints, and on Android the system font scale is not in that key, so a remounted label gets its OLD size back — and a remount throws away the open job and any half-typed reading. So: (a) the plugin also overrides `MainActivity.onConfigurationChanged` to emit `didUpdateDimensions` (RN 0.79 forwards a configuration change only to the light/dark module); (b) `ThemeProvider` reads `useWindowDimensions().fontScale` and every line height on the type ramp gains `measureKey(fontScale)` — **exactly 0 at the scale the app started at**, and at any other scale a distinct value of at most ~0.2 sp, under a pixel. A different line height is a different cache key, so every label is measured at today's size; no state is lost. **Worked:** a 15-pt body label launched at 1.0 has line height 23; at 2.0 it is 23.2 and is measured afresh; back at 1.0 it is 23 again. **Font scaling is not capped** — 200% stays supported. Not proved on a device (none in the container); the native override was compiled against signature stubs taken from React Native 0.79.6's source, not against React Native itself.

## 2026-10-24 — MQ-033 read formats, the server: how it is built (`CR-192-BRC10`, lane MQ033-SERVER, task 10 of 13; our judgments, law 13 — not put to the PO)

Built on the three rows above, which are the requirement. Where they ran out, these are ours, each with the worked case it was checked against (the PO's *"Water monthly walk v1"* illustration, B14 rule 37: *Seal intact?* yes/no; a photo when it is *No*; *Meter condition* Good/Damaged/Missing raising a repair on *Damaged*).

1. **The job "type" a question raises is a published Work job TEMPLATE.** Work raises a job only from a template (`BR-WRK-008`) and a template carries its type, so `raise_work = {on_answer, template_id}`. Worked: *Damaged* on MTR-0471 → one *Meter repair* job, `WO-…`, anchored on the meter, its finding's detail naming the reading's key and `meter_read_id`.
2. **It goes through Work's route-finding raise path, as a finding of a new kind `read_answer`, converted `by_read_format`** (`work/0050` widens two CHECKs by one value each). Not offered to the phone (`FINDING_KINDS` unchanged) and no Work rule can be written on it. Idempotent on reading + question (key `read-answer:<reading key>:<question key>`): the same item resent raises nothing; another meter answering *Damaged* raises its own. An unpublished template leaves the finding OPEN for a person (*Route findings*), as a rule's refused raise does.
3. **"Every reading" means every reading with a FIGURE; "can't read" every *could not read***. Read the other way, *can't read* would be a subset of *every reading* and pointless. An answer to a question not asked is kept and flagged `not_asked`.
4. **"Out of range" is the ENGINE's range verdict** (a HIGH, LOW or ZERO warning — not every flag; a vacant-unit flag is not out of range) **or the reader's accepted-anyway** (R80). Worked: 71,400 against a last dial of 47,700 → asked; 48,400 → not asked.
5. **"Once per stop" is satisfied by any reading at the same stop, route and capture day**, this request or an earlier one. Worked: 1318 Maple holds MTR-0471 and MTR-0472 — the gate code answered on the first satisfies the second.
6. **A version the server does not hold, or a draft id, keeps the answers flagged `version_unknown`**; a missing required answer is a row with `required_missing`. The reading's own result never changes (`BR-MET-1216`).
7. **A follow-up must name an EARLIER question** (lower order) with an answer that question can receive; reordering a follow-up above its parent, renaming or deleting a question another follows up on, are refused by name. Earlier-only makes a cycle impossible by construction.
8. **A raise happens for a reading stored as posted or recorded.** A reading on a field-added meter awaiting acceptance (R85) raises nothing now, and nothing re-runs it at acceptance — REPORTED, not built.
9. **Retire is refused while a route, cycle or service default points at the format** (*"replace it later"* = move the pointer first); a never-published format cannot be retired (there is nothing to retire and no delete door).
10. **The cycle and route pointers are written with a one-column UPDATE**, because MQ-033 task 9 is changing the same two tables' assignment columns in parallel.
11. **Export columns and Reads-list answer columns are task 13's**; the `answer[<key>]=<value>` filter and the answers on the reading detail are built here.

## 2026-10-24 — MQ-033 task (9) BUILT: who may assign a reader, who may BE one, what leaves the phone, and the ONE read window (our judgments, law 13)

Built under the reader-assignment ruling above (Reads → cycle → Routes; `CR-029` D6 and `OQ-343` superseded for that tab only — both rows stamped the same commit). Where the ruling said nothing, we decided, and these are the decisions:
1. **Who may assign:** System Admin and Billing Clerk (`AdminOrClerk`). Who walks a route this month is reading WORK, which `BR-MET-011` as narrowed makes writable on Reads; an Executive reads, a field technician never reaches it. The route's DEFINITION (members, walk order, cycle) stays System Admin's in Settings.
2. **Who may be a reader:** an **ACTIVE** login of this utility whose role is **Field technician**. An invited login (no password yet), a deactivated one, a clerk, and another utility's technician are all the same refusal (*"Pick an active field technician."*). Worked: Brookfield's clerk ticks RT-001 and RT-002 and picks Ray Reader → both routes are Ray's, two audit lines (`route.reader_changed`, old → new by name); picking Dana (System Admin) is refused and nothing moves.
3. **Many routes, all or nothing:** one unknown or foreign route id refuses the whole request as not-found — a bulk assign half-applied over a typo would leave the clerk guessing which half. Re-saving the same reader is not an event (no audit line).
4. **On screen:** the Reader column and a bulk *Assign reader* on the Routes TAB only; the Overview panel's seven columns stay as drawn. The row action sits in the `…` overflow with *Print sheet* (B14 rule 15: upload stays the one visible icon, and a menu of one item is not allowed). *Unassign* clears every route in the dialog that has a reader.
5. **The phone:** after a COMPLETE download, a route the server no longer lists for this technician leaves the phone with its stops and readings; one with captures not yet sent STAYS until they are sent (R60) — the start-up purge's own rule, now one shared helper. A download that fails part-way removes nothing.
6. **No wake-up push yet — a stated absence.** `work/push.py` addresses a technician's devices only from inside Work's own jobs; there is no Work seam a metering service may call to say *"this login's routes changed"*. The phone gets the change on its next sync, which is the delivery (the push is the doorbell). Building it is a Work-side seam, reported, not guessed.
7. **ONE read window (`DEF-MET-10588`):** every read window — the Reads cycle list and page, the read-time window check and the chase list — now uses the EFFECTIVE start day Settings already showed (the first run anchors, `OQ-340`); the stored day is used only where nothing anchors the cycle. **Worked, Brookfield CY-001:** stored start day 10, first run on the 14th, 5 days → **14–18 Oct** on Reads and Settings alike; Reads printed 10–14 Oct before. The stored day is not rewritten. ⚠ The Reads cycle list's *Read window* SORT is still the stored `start_day` column (`selectors.CYCLE_SORTS`), so a list sorted by window can order a cycle by its stored day — recorded, not changed here.

## 2026-10-24 — MQ-033 read formats, the phone: how it is built (`CR-192-BRC10`, lane MQ033-PHONE, task 12 of 13; our judgments, law 13 — not put to the PO)

Built on the four MQ-033 rows above and the server lane's eleven judgments. Where they ran out, these are ours, each checked against the PO's illustration used as test data (B14 rule 37): *Seal intact?* yes/no, a photo when it is *No*, *Meter condition* Good/Damaged/Missing, plus *Why so high?* (out of range), *Why not read* (can't read) and *Gate code* (once per stop) — `field-app/tests/sync/support/serverReadFormat.json`, locked to the server by `06-backend/tests/test_mq033_phone_shape.py`.

1. **The questions are asked in ONE sheet at the moment of saving, from every screen that saves a reading** (RW-09, RW-10, RW-15, RW-16, RW-17 — `useReadForm` in `field-app/src/screens/reads/ReadQuestions.tsx`). The answers travel inside the reading's own item, and *out of range* and *can't read* are only known once the figure or the reason is decided, so the figure is taken from the meter exactly as before and the questions follow it. No save path can skip them. Worked: 52,410 gal on MTR-0471 → *Save and next* → the sheet shows *Seal intact?*, *Meter condition*, *Gate code*; nothing is in the outbox until *Save reading*.
2. **A required question shown and unanswered blocks *Save reading* with one warning sentence** — *"Answer 2 more questions."* — the required-step-photo pattern (`DEF-FLD-10583`): a warning notice, the button disabled, the sentence as its accessibility hint. Worked: *Seal intact?* No → the photo follow-up appears; with the gate code typed it reads *"Answer 1 more question."*; the photo clears it.
3. **A follow-up's answer is dropped from the item when it is not shown**, and a typed number or date the server could not read (`12a`, `2026-13-01`) counts as unanswered and is not sent — each would only come back flagged (`not_shown`, `wrong_type`).
4. **"Out of range" on the phone is the phone's own range warning or the reader's *accept anyway*** (R80) — the server's judgment 4 uses its engine; where they disagree the server flags, never refuses. Worked: 71,400 against 40,000–56,000 → *Accept anyway* → *Why so high?* is asked.
5. **"Once per stop" is not asked again at the same stop (route + premises) on the same capture day, on the phone's own calendar, once another reading there answered it.** Worked: the gate code answered at MTR-0471 is not asked at MTR-0472, 1318 Maple. The server counts any reading at the stop (its judgment 5), so the second reading is not flagged.
6. **Which format a reading uses: the route's entry for the METER's service** (`route.read_formats[]`, per service); a meter with no service on a route of one format uses it; otherwise none. **A reading with a format but nothing to ask is still stamped** with the version and an empty `answers` (it was taken under that version).
7. **A photo answer is a photograph OF THE READING**: declared as a route photo exactly like the reader's own, listed in the item's `photos`, and named by its id in the answer — so it uploads through the existing route-photo path and nothing new travels.
8. **A version the route names that the phone could not download reads as a plain reading** (no stamp, no questions) until the next download fetches it from `GET work/mobile/read-formats/versions/{id}`. The walk is never held up for want of a form. REPORTED: nothing tells the reader the form is missing.
9. **The receipt's `needs_review` is shown on RW-13 as one warning fact** — *"The office will check the answers."* — and blocks nothing (BR-MET-1216). The issues themselves are the office's.
10. **A number question shows no unit**: the server's question carries none (`question_dict`), and inventing one would break hard rule 3's *never assume*. REPORTED to task 11 if a unit is wanted.
11. **Labels, help and list options are the utility's words, shown verbatim, never translated** (they are not ours). Only the sheet's own controls are catalogue words (14 keys, all eleven catalogues, B14 rules 33 and 35).

## 2026-10-24 — MQ-033 task (13) BUILT: seeing the read-format answers — on the reading, as a Reads filter, in the export (`CR-192-BRC10`; our judgments, law 13 — not put to the PO)

Built under *"SUMMARY CONFIRMED"* above (*"shown on the reading, filterable in Reads lists and exported"*). Where the ruling said nothing, these are ours, each checked against the PO's *"Water monthly walk v1"* illustration (B14 rule 37):
1. **The reading's page gains a seventh group, *Read format*, in the right column under *Location*:** the format's name and version (*Water monthly walk · v2*), *Needs review* when any answer was flagged, then each question in the utility's OWN words (tenant prose, never translated) with its answer — yes/no in words, a list joined, a photo as a thumbnail that opens the picture — the flag's words beside a flagged answer (a flagged answer is kept, `BR-MET-1216`, so it is shown, never hidden), and the job an answer raised by its NUMBER (*WO-4870*), linked. **A reading that carried no format shows no panel** — it reads exactly as before formats existed, and a panel saying so would be rationale (B14 rule 33).
2. **A photo answer's bytes are served at `GET reads/photos/{id}/content`**, any office role, same-origin (`DEF-WRK-9594`'s reason), `nosniff`, `no-store`; a neighbour's or an unlanded photo is the same 404.
3. **The Answer filter is `+ Answer` beside `+ Filter`, a small dialog** (the estimate precedent: two fields, one outcome, back to the list): type part of a question or a format name (a SERVER search, `GET reads/answer-questions`, paged — NFR-3), pick the question, then pick the value (yes/no and list questions offer their choices; a date is the date input, B14 rule 7; anything else is typed). **Only questions of PUBLISHED formats' current versions are offered, and never a photo question** (a photograph has no value to match). Any office role may read the list, because a Billing Clerk filters Reads and Settings → Reads is not theirs.
4. **The URL carries the server's own spelling, `answer[<key>]=<value>`**, AND-ed, one removable chip per answer. It is not an `f.` filter (a question key is the utility's own, so no screen can declare it), so its grammar is kept by hand in `readAnswersShared.ts`. **The key is format-blind, as task 10 built it**: two formats sharing a key are filtered together; the dialog names each question's format so a clerk can see which one they picked.
5. **The export gains one column per (format, question key) that the EXPORTED rows carry, after the capability row's columns**, headed *"<format> · <question label>"* — *"Electric walk · Meter condition"* — with the NEWEST present version's words (the key, not the wording, is the answer's identity). A cell is the stored answer as text: yes/no as `true`/`false` (the export's own boolean words), a list joined with the export's separator, a photo as its reference id, a flagged answer as what was sent; an unanswered question is an empty cell, never a guessed *no*. **A file whose rows carried no format is byte-for-byte the file it was.** The list's answer filters travel in the export body and narrow the file (BR-SHL-011). The answers are read ONE query per streamed chunk, never per row, so the file still streams.
6. **Answer columns IN the Reads list table are NOT built — reported, not guessed.** List rows carry no answers (adding them is a per-page batched read on every list request), and the column chooser has no per-tenant dynamic columns: its columns are the screen's declared set, kept per user by key. Doing it cleanly is a kit change, which the task said to skip rather than force.

## 2026-10-24 — DEF-WRK-10601 / DEF-WRK-10595: UNABLE TO READ REACHES THE OFFICE, AND THE WEB TECHNICIAN PAGE HOLDS A READING UNTIL ITS REQUIRED PHOTO (PO: *"yes start both"*; our judgments, law 13)

**What was wrong.** The phone sends a job reading in three shapes — a figure `{reading_id, value, unit}`, words `{reading_id, value_text}`, and *Unable to read* `{reading_id, value: null, unit, unable_to_read: true}`. The server's `set_reading` knew a figure and (for a text-kind row) words, and refused *Unable to read* as `work.reading.value_not_a_number`, so the item stayed on the phone and the office never learned the meter could not be read. Separately, the web technician page's Readings pane saved a reading on blur even when its photo was Required, which the phone stopped doing under MQ-020 (row above, *"MQ-017: A STEP WITH A REQUIRED PHOTO…"*).

**Our judgments, none put to the PO:** (1) *Unable to read* is accepted for EITHER kind and is never refused — not for its missing figure, not for its unit (a text reading sends `unit: ""`; with no figure there is no consumption for hard rule 3 to check), and not for state (TECHNICIAN SYNC DESIGN, 2026-10-04). (2) It is stored on the job's own reading row as two new columns (`work/0051`: `unable_to_read`, `unable_reason`), with `value`, `value_text` and `in_range` cleared, so the posting path skips it as *no value captured* and no meter read is invented. A later figure or words clears the flag. (3) The reason is whatever words the phone sends as `unable_reason` (or `reason`); **today's phone sends none**, so we did not borrow the Reads module's can't-read reason list — a job reading has no such field, and inventing a list would be a rule nobody ruled. (4) The office sees it as **"Unable to read"**, plus *" · <reason>"* when there is one, on the order's Readings; `close_readiness` lists it under `flagged` (kind `unable_to_read`, never blocking) and counts it as answered, as the phone's own count does. (5) On the web technician page a reading whose photo is Required is **held, not saved**: the typed figure stays in the field, the row reads *"Take 1 photo to save this reading."*, and it is saved the moment the photo is attached. A reading with no required photo saves on blur as before. *Unable to read* is not on the web pane at all, and on the phone it is not blocked (the MQ-020 commit says so), so nothing changes for it. **Also fixed, at the coordinator's instruction as inside the same approval (`DEF-WRK-10602`):** the web pane sent every reading as `{value, unit}`, so a TEXT reading typed there was refused `work.reading.value_required` — the same class as DEF-WRK-10601 on the other client. It now shows the words as typed and sends the phone's own text shape `{reading_id, value_text, unable_to_read: false}`, asserted against the shared fixture; and `readings_captured` counts a text reading's words, as the phone does. Worked: a three-reading job; the technician marks *Final read, old meter* unable; it syncs (was refused), the order reads *Unable to read*, 1 of 3 answered, 0 meter reads posted.

## 2026-10-26 — Route-change notification BUILT (DEF-MET-10606): one push per reader per change, words on the phone

**What the PO ruled** (the two 2026-10-26 sections above): assigning, reassigning or unassigning a route's reader notifies the technician — new reader and old reader — as the existing wake-up-and-sync push. **What was ours to decide, decided here** (law 13 — no re-ask):
- **One push per reader per request, however many routes moved.** Bulk-assigning five routes from Ray to Mia sends Mia ONE push (*"5 new routes"*) and Ray ONE push (*"5 routes removed"*); one route sends *"New route: RT-001 · Silver Creek"* to the new reader and *"Route removed: RT-002"* to the old. Re-saving the same reader sends nothing (it is not a change and writes no audit row).
- **After the commit only.** Metering asks work through its own seam (`metering.seams.notify_route_readers` → `work.route_push.notify_routes_changed`) with `transaction.on_commit`; a rolled-back assignment sends nothing. A push that cannot be queued never undoes the assignment — the phone still gets it on its next download.
- **The push carries counts and, for one route, its code and name — no address, no customer.** The PHONE renders the words from its own catalogue (eleven languages), so the technician reads them in the language they chose; the server sends no English (B14 rule 35). It is a sixth push kind, `route_change`, on its own Android channel *"Route changes"* at ordinary importance.
- **On the phone the push downloads the routes** (the same download the Reads tab runs: a new route appears, a removed one leaves unless it holds unsent readings). While the app is open the server's wordless copy is silenced and the phone shows its own one-line worded copy; a tapped push downloads but does not show the line twice.
- **Audit:** one row per push, *pushed to phone* or *waiting for the phone* from a count of the reader's registered phones, never *pushed* when nothing was addressed. As for every push today, no push provider is configured (`work/push.py` says so); the phone's download is the delivery.

## 2026-10-26 — DEF-MET-10609 BUILT: THE ONE CAN'T-READ LIST, IN SETTINGS AND ON A JOB READING (our judgments under *"yes do it"*, law 13)

**What was built, against the ruling above.** Settings → Configure → Reference data → READS now has a *Can't-read reasons* card beside *Read formats*, opening a paged list (Name · Type · Status · Used) with *+ Add reason*, rename, move up/down, switch on/off and delete. A job reading's *Unable to read* on the phone (FF-20) opens the SAME picker RW-17 uses (now one component) plus an optional note; the phone sends the reason's CODE and the note; the office's order page reads *"Unable to read · Dog"* with the note under it. A job's bundle carries the switched-on list, kept where RW-17 already reads it, so a technician with no route still has it offline.

**Our judgments, none put to the PO:** (1) **A new reason is added by NAME only; its code is minted from the name** (`Flooded pit` → `flooded_pit`, then `flooded_pit_2`; a name with no Latin letters gets `reason`, `reason_2`) **and never changes** — readings already store it, and nobody sees it (B14 rule 31). Rename changes the name only; a request naming `code` is refused. A starting reason may be renamed too: the words are the utility's. Two reasons may not share a name (case ignored), because a technician picking between two *Dog*s cannot tell them apart. (2) **Reorder is one place at a time** (*Move up* / *Move down*), not a drag of the whole list, so it works on any page of a paged list (NFR-3); at either end it does nothing rather than refusing. (3) **USED counts both kinds of reading** — route readings naming the code and job readings answered with it — and Metering asks Work for the second count through its seam rather than reading Work's table. A starting reason is never deletable (BR-TEN-036); an own reason with any use is refused with *"Already used. Switch it off instead."*. (4) **A job reading's reason that is not on the switched-on list is KEPT and MARKED, never refused** (TECHNICIAN SYNC DESIGN: no field record dropped): a reason switched off after the phone downloaded, an older phone's free words, or an unknown code all store as sent; the answer and the audit row carry `unable_reason_known: false`; the office reads the reason's name when the list holds it (switched off or not) and what the phone sent otherwise. (5) **The note is stored on the job reading itself** (`work/0052`, one nullable column) and cleared, with the reason, when a figure or words later answer the reading. (6) **On the phone, *Record* needs a reason when the phone holds a list; a phone that has no list yet says *"No reasons on this phone yet."* and records without one** — the answer is never blocked for want of a download. Worked: a technician marks *Final read, old meter* unable, picks *Dog*, types *Barking at the gate*; the order reads *Unable to read · Dog* with the note under it, 1 of 3 readings answered, 0 meter reads posted; the utility then tries to delete *Dog* and is told it can only be switched off.

## 2026-10-26 — MQ-019: the app locks after 5 minutes AWAY, not immediately on backgrounding; its own system pop-ups never count (amends the field-app security rule)

**PO, verbatim:** *"A. Lock only after 5 minutes away (recommended) and start MQ-021"*. **Supersedes** `04-docs/05-modules/18-field-app/12-security.md:66` *"Five minutes idle, and immediately on backgrounding"* → **five minutes idle, and five minutes away**: leaving the app (Maps for Navigate, the phone for Call, the home screen) locks it only if the technician is away 5 minutes or more; a cold start still opens locked. **And regardless of the timer, a "background" report caused by the app's OWN system pop-up never counts as leaving** — a permission dialog (camera, location, notifications), a settings screen the app opened, the fingerprint prompt. Shown first: Android reports its permission dialog as backgrounding, so answering *Don't allow* or *While using the app* locked the app mid-job (seen 2/2); the trade-off table (a 2-minute customer call no longer asks for the password; a phone stolen while the app was backgrounded stays unlocked up to 5 minutes, the same limit already accepted for idle). Root cause: `field-app/src/session/SessionProvider.tsx:36–37` locks on any `background`/`inactive`.

**Built 2026-10-26 (`DEF-FLD-10614`), and three judgments of ours where the ruling ran out (law 13; not re-asked).** One constant: `AUTO_LOCK_AWAY_MS` is `AUTO_LOCK_IDLE_MS` by name. The guard is one helper, `field-app/src/session/systemInteraction.ts`, used by every place the app asks the platform for something; a source-scan test counts the nine sites and fails an unwrapped one. **(1) Idle before leaving does not add to time away.** The idle clock does not run while the technician is away (an Android timer can fire in the background), and a return under five minutes counts as a touch — so Dana idle 4 minutes, then a 2-minute call, comes back UNLOCKED; without this the idle check would have locked her the second she returned, which is the defect the PO just ruled out wearing a different hat. **(2) The microphone ask (dictation) and the platform file picker (FF-60 *A file*) are guarded too** — they were not in the list shown, and they are the app's own system screens in exactly the same way as a permission dialog. A *Call* or *Navigate* hand-off is NOT guarded: that is leaving, and it is the case the five minutes is for. **(3) A settings visit the app opened never counts, however long** — `Linking.openSettings` resolves the moment the settings screen launches, before Android reports the background, so its guard holds until the app is active again; a failed launch releases it.

Found by the MQ-027 lane (`DEF-FLD-10612`), which declined to print that sentence because it was false.

## 2026-10-26 — CR-194-BRC10 BUILT: refused field work kept for the office (our judgments under *"store on both"*, law 13)

**Built `2.603.0`.** The server now keeps a copy of every refused field item (`work_refused_items`, `BR-WRK-063` amended, `BR-WRK-071`), both doors (job sync and route reads); Work → From the field → **Refused work** lists them; the phone's refused row says *The office will review this.* only when the answer carried `kept_for_office`. **Judgments where the ruling ran out, recorded before the report** (all in `CR-194-BRC10` §3): (1) one copy per key; a resend refused again updates it and a copy already marked reviewed stays reviewed; (2) the copy is written in its OWN savepoint after the item's rolled back, and a copy that fails is answered WITHOUT the flag — never a promise nobody kept (proved on PostgreSQL 16: a `division by zero` inside the copy leaves items 1 and 3 committed; with the copy's savepoint stripped, the whole batch is lost); (3) the copy is never a receipt and never stores the capture token; (4) *Apply to job* re-runs the kind's normal apply path AS THE OFFICE PERSON under the item's own key with a receipt — so the phone's resend is then a duplicate and leaves its outbox — and the captor on the receipt stays the technician; it is refused with the reason when the job is closed, cancelled or accepted, when the service refuses it now (e.g. `gal` on a `kWh` job), or when the copy came through the route-reads door; (5) a declared photograph whose bytes never arrived is shown as *still on the phone*; delivered bytes are kept and shown; (6) items for another utility's job keep nothing; a no-token group on a job of THIS utility that is not the sender's (404) is kept; (7) the action label is **Apply to job** (three words, B14 rule 33) for the plan's *"Apply to the job"*. Worked figure: D. Ortiz's three readings on WO-0028 after it went to M. Chen — three refusals on the phone, one group row *WO-0028 · 3 items · This job was reassigned. The office will review this.*, three copies for the office, *Apply to job* posts 40001 kWh to the job and the phone's resend answers *duplicate*.

## 2026-10-26 — Certificate pinning is OFF in the beta (preview) build, ON for go-live

**PO, verbatim:** *"B. Switch the check off for the beta"*. Context shown first: since 2.600.0 the field app pins the server's certificate issuer (`OQ-FLD-12797`, PO 2026-10-24 — issuer + one backup, from Settings › Security); the build's starting list is ISRG Root X1 + GTS Root R1 (`field-app/app.json` `extra.pins`), and if smartbillhub.bynry.com chains to another issuer (e.g. Amazon Root CA) the phone refuses every connection and says *"No signal"* — the tester's activation and sign-in both failed that way on 2.603.0. Options put: A keep the check and correct the issuer, B switch it off for the beta. **Ruled B.** The **preview (beta) profile builds without pinning**; the **production profile keeps it ON** and must not ship without a valid issuer list — a release check fails a production build that has pinning off. **Risk accepted for the beta:** no protection against a fake server on public Wi-Fi (a tester's password and test data could be read there). Also built regardless: a refused certificate reads *"Can't verify the server. Contact the office."* and an outdated server *"The server needs an update."*, never *"No signal"*. **Before go-live:** confirm the real issuer from the browser padlock, put it and its backup in the build and in Settings › Security, and turn pinning on.

## 2026-10-27 — Field app Sync sends nothing while showing ONLINE: "start A to F" (`DEF-FLD-10624`)

**What the PO saw (Android emulator, smartbillhub.bynry.com, city-of-houston):** a job finished offline (a step, a signature refusal with a photo, the close); airplane mode off; FF-50 Sync showed **ONLINE**, **"16 waiting"**, **"Last reached the server 11:33"**. Pressing *Sync now* again and again, and restarting the app, changed nothing for **15 minutes**; the office still showed *"Not accepted yet"*. The server's access log for the run shows **zero** `/api/city-of-houston/work/mobile/` and **zero** `/auth/token` requests — the phone sent nothing at all.

**Causes put to the PO (A–F; E was not part of this lane's brief) and the ruling, verbatim:** *"start A to F"*.
- **A.** FF-50 says why nothing went, in one short fact (B14 rule 33): *Could not reach the server.* · *Sign in again.* · *The server had a problem. Trying again.* · *Run timed out. Try again.* (plus the existing *Can't verify the server…*, *The server needs an update.*, *Update the app.* and a *Too many syncs. Wait a minute.* for a 429) — from the run's result, and from the waiting items' saved `last_error` when the screen opens.
- **B.** A send that reached the server records the time, so *Last reached the server* moves (`touchPush` was never called).
- **C.** A MANUAL *Sync now* clears the backoff of the signed-in technician's waiting items before sending. Automatic runs (the 15-minute timer, coming forward, reconnecting) keep backoff.
- **D.** A job's group is due when its FIRST waiting item is due — the rule `nextBatch` already follows — so a backing-off later item never holds the earlier ones.
- **F.** Every step of a run has a time limit, the network check included (a check that does not answer counts as *unknown — try anyway*, never *no signal*), so a hung step ends the run and the next *Sync now* starts a fresh one.

**Found in the code while building it, and built under the same ruling because it is already signed law, not a new rule:** the app **never renews the one-hour access token** — `SessionManager.refresh()` exists and nothing calls it — so an hour after sign-in every call fails ON THE PHONE as *"no access token"* before a request is made. That is exactly *zero `/auth/token` and zero `/work/mobile/` requests*. Security §1 already says the access token is *"one hour, refreshed whenever there is a signal"* (`security/credentials.ts`), so a run with a signal now renews it first. A refresh token the server no longer takes still ends at *Sign in again.*

**Judgment (ours, recorded):** a purge that does not finish in its time limit is let go and the run carries on. The purge only deletes SETTLED rows and UPLOADED photographs, which no send reads, so R63's *never mid-upload* is about not starting a purge during an upload, and holding every send behind a stuck purge forever is the worse failure.
