## 2026-10-27 — FB-004 added to the sync fix: "yes add G to K to the sync fix, start" (`DEF-FLD-10629`)

**What the PO reported (FB-004, 2026-10-26 ~18:37, Android, reader Sam Curran, route RT-001):** meters read and saved with 4 photos; FF-50 Sync showed **ONLINE**, **"12 waiting"**, **"Last reached the server 18:37"**, **"Photos 4 uploading · 0 of 4 · 0 MB left"**, **"On this phone · Jobs 0 of 0"**. *Sync now* showed no spinner, no result and no error, and the readings never appeared in web Reads.

**Why:** the pull travels under the ACCESS token, so *Last reached the server* moved; every SEND travels under the captor's CAPTURE credential (Security §3), and with that credential missing or expired `sendPending` skipped the reader's whole route and only counted it (`skippedNoToken`), which nothing showed. A failed renewal (`renewCapture`) was silent too. Route photos upload only once their declaration is answered with an address, so they sat at *0 of 4* labelled *uploading*. *On this phone* counted jobs only.

**Ruling, verbatim:** *"yes add G to K to the sync fix, start"*.
- **G.** Before sending, a signed-in technician whose capture credential is missing or expired is renewed first (with a signal). If that still fails, FF-50 says **"Sign in again to send."**, how many items wait, and a *Sign in again* button into the existing sign-in flow. Never silent. Another captor's items on a shared phone read **"Waiting for {{name}} to sign in."**
- **H.** *Sync now* shows **"Sending…"** while it runs (button busy), then **"Sent {{count}}."** or the reason from A.
- **I.** A photo whose declaration has no upload address yet reads **"Waiting for readings"** (a route photo) or **"Waiting for its work"** (a job photo), never *uploading*; the progress bar counts only photos able to upload.
- **J.** *On this phone* also shows the reader's **Routes** (e.g. *"Routes 1 · 12 meters"*).
- **K.** A red-first test of FB-004 through the app and a fake server.

## 2026-10-27 — VAPT round, code side: five judgment calls the rulings left to us (lane VAPT-CODE, 2.604.0)

Ours, not put to the PO (law 13) — each is a detail inside a ruled change, recorded so the next lane builds the same thing.
1. **The lockout message carries the SETTING, not the time left.** A Dana locked at 09:00 under a 5-minute policy who tries again at 09:02 reads *"Try again in 5 minutes"*, not *"3 minutes"* — the PO approved the sentence with *M = the utility's own setting* (remediation doc §2 test row 2), and a countdown would be a second message nobody approved.
2. **The web sign-in's browser-side lockout line is REMOVED, not reworded.** It said *"after 5 failed attempts sign-in pauses for 15 minutes"* from a count kept in the browser, whatever the utility had set — the hardcoded 5/15 the PO ruled out (*"should not be hardcoded"*). The server now names the lock, so the browser no longer guesses; key `identity.signIn.lockedOut` retired in all eleven catalogues.
3. **"Heavy actions" (A3) is one list by method and path** in `core/throttling.py` — exports, imports and their commit/load, bulk actions, bill-run start/calculate/issue/release/catch-up, print sets, collections run, report *run now*, runbook runs, integration run/export (13 patterns, 32 routes). **Reading a report on screen is NOT heavy**: it is paged, a clerk flips filters faster than ten a minute, and A1 already bounds it; the remediation doc's test row 8 (*"open 20 screens quickly → never a 429"*) decides it.
4. **A stored SVG logo is served as its PNG copy under a NEW ETag (`<ref>.png`)**, so a browser that cached the SVG under the old ETag fetches the PNG instead of being told *304 — keep what you have*. No stored file is deleted; the SVG stays in the store beside its PNG.
5. **A 429 on a field-app sync is "wait", never "refused".** It waits the server's `Retry-After` (else a minute) with no attempt counted; before this it was marked refused and shown on the Sync screen as something the technician had to resend.

## 2026-10-27 — A reading's photos: free to change until the reading is saved, add-only after (PO, FB-002 / FB-003)

**PO ruling 2026-10-27, verbatim: *"go with recommendation"*** — on the recommendation put to them after FB-002 (reader Sam Curran, meter W-5005, route RT-001: the camera screen showed a black panel and no camera view, the photo was shown nowhere afterwards, and tapping the photo count opened the camera again) and FB-003 (the saved reading said *"0 photos"*).
- **Before a reading is saved**, the reader sees every photo taken for it as a row of thumbnails and may open one full size, **Retake** it (the new photo takes its place) or **Remove** it, freely. Nothing has been kept yet, so nothing is lost.
- **After it is saved**, the reading and its photos are the evidence: the reader may open each photo full size and may **Add photo**, and nothing else — no Retake and no Remove. A photo added after saving is declared against the same reading (R123) and **counts on that reading**: a reading saved with 1 photo that gets 1 more reads *"2 photos"*.
- The camera screen shows the **live camera view** with the stamp over it as a preview; *Take the photo* takes it from that view, and the stamp is still burned into the pixels (R94).

Our own calls inside the ruling (law 13): a photo belongs to its reading by a **`route_read_id` written on the handset's `photo` row at capture** (handset migration `0006`, back-filled), never by the reading's capture key — a key changes when a reading is corrected, and a photo added later is its own act with its own key, which is exactly how FB-003's *"0 photos"* arose. A removed draft photo's file is deleted from the phone; it was never declared, so nothing travels.

## 2026-10-27 — FB-003: the position is captured automatically, never by a button (PO)

PO, verbatim: *"no need of new button , capture the position automatically ; if user has location permission not enabled asked the user to give permission , when user takes the photo record the lat,long positions"*, then *"go with recommendation, start"* on the two figures put to them.
- **No permission yet:** opening the route or the camera shows Android's own *Allow location?* prompt. Refused with *Don't ask again*: one line *"Location is off for this app."* with *Open settings* — the only control left, because Android allows no other path.
- **Phone's Location off:** Android's own *Turn on location?* dialog.
- **Saving a reading:** the best recent fix from the background watch; with none, wait **up to 10 seconds** for one, then save without — the reader is never blocked.
- **Saved without a position:** the first fix within **5 minutes** of saving is sent automatically as a SEPARATE fact, *"Position added at 18:35"* — never written as if present at save (hard rule 4, add-never-change; `BR-MET-1202` phone position at capture). After 5 minutes nothing is attached: the reader has likely moved, and a far position is false evidence.
- **A photo** records lat, lng, accuracy and time at the shutter, on its record and in the burned-in stamp; without a fix it gets the same 5-minute late position.
- **The office** sees the position and its time; a late one reads *added at 18:35* beside the saved time.
Worked case put to the PO: a reading saved 18:32:48 with no fix; a ±10 m fix arrives 18:35 → *"Position added at 18:35 ±10 m"*; a fix first arriving 18:38 attaches nothing.

## 2026-10-27 — FB-009: Scan and Enter manually ask the server when the phone does not hold the meter (PO)

PO, verbatim: *"your understanding is correct ; start FB-009"*. It applies the ruling already made — **2026-10-26 "MQ-046 … offline search covers ASSIGNED meters only"**: offline the phone searches the meters it holds; online the server searches every meter of the utility (`GET work/mobile/assets/search`, N9). Nothing new was ruled; FF-38 Scan simply never reached the server half that FF-41 Asset search already had.
- **The report:** reader Sam Curran, Android, online: Home › *Scan a meter* reads barcode `AR-TEST-SN1` correctly and says *"No meter with this code"*; *Enter manually* + *Find* says the same. `AR-TEST-SN1` exists on the web and is on none of his jobs or routes, so the phone does not hold it.
- **Built:** the phone's own match first (serial, badge, device ID — unchanged). Not found and a signal: the same server search FF-41 asks; a hit whose **serial or asset number equals the code** (case-insensitive, trimmed) is the meter, and it opens exactly as FF-41 opens a server hit — kept on the phone with its premises, then FF-39. On a job, *Not this job's meter* still applies to a server hit.
- **Words:** while asking, *"Searching the utility…"*; no signal and not on the phone, *"Not on this phone."* + FF-41's own *"A signal searches the whole utility."*; the server answered with no exact match, *"No meter with this code"*; the server failed, *"Search failed. Try again."*
- **Our call (law 13):** only an EXACT serial or asset-number hit counts as the scanned meter. The server search also matches prefixes, addresses and account numbers, and a scan that opened the first prefix hit would open the wrong meter with confidence. Worked case: scanning `AR-TEST-SN1` opens that meter; scanning `AR-TEST` (a prefix of it) says *"No meter with this code"*.

## 2026-10-27 — FB-003 position, as built: our calls inside the ruling (DEF-FLD-10632, DEF-MET-10633)

Built to the entry *"FB-003: the position is captured automatically, never by a button (PO)"* above. Nothing new was put to the PO; these are our own calls (law 13), each with its worked case.
- **Where the reader is asked:** on opening the route summary (RW-02), the walk (RW-05) and the camera (RW-14) — once per opening. Refused once (Android will ask again): nothing is drawn, and the next opening asks again. Refused with *Don't ask again*: *"Location is off for this app."* + *Open settings*; coming back from settings asks again, so the line goes as soon as it is switched on.
- **"Best recent fix" means fresh:** the watch's held fix is used at save only if it is at most 2 minutes old (the handset's existing staleness rule, `FIX_STALE_MS`); older, the save asks for a fix and waits up to 10 seconds. Worked: a 12-minute-old fix from the previous street is not used.
- **The 5 minutes run from the save to the FIX's own time**, and a fix older than the save never counts as late. Both the phone and the server apply it; the server sends back a late position outside it (`position_too_late`). Worked: saved 18:32:48 → a fix at 18:35:00 is kept; at 18:38:00 it is not; one stamped 18:32:18 is not a late one.
- **Only the first late position is kept.** A second one for the same reading is answered as a duplicate (acknowledged, not stored), by a database index rather than a read-then-write.
- **Where it is stored:** a `field_reads` row of the new kind `position`, pointing at the reading or photo it belongs to (`position_for`). The reading's own row is never updated (hard rule 4's spirit). The office reading page shows *"<lat>, <lng> · ±10 m · added at 18:35"* beside *"Saved"*.
- **A photo taken before the reading is saved** gets the fix at its own shutter; a photo with no fix at the shutter gets the late position counted from the reading's save (the moment it was declared).
- **Not covered, reported:** a JOB's photos (the job channel) — the job door has no item for a late position; and on the office page, a route photo added AFTER the reading was saved is not listed with the reading, because the server's photo declaration does not name its reading.

## 2026-10-28 — FB-019 started; FB-011 deferred with the recommendation accepted (PO)

PO, verbatim, 2026-10-28: *"start FB-019 and skip the FB-011 issue for now , go with recommendation"*.

**(1) FB-019 — a photo added to a saved reading is refused as damaged (`DEF-FLD-10637`).** Reported by technician Jeremy on Android 2.606.0, route reads: a reading saved, then *Add photo* on *The reading* → after Sync, *"7 refused — needs you"*, including *"4 items · This photo is damaged. Take it again."*; retaking repeats it. Cause: adding a photo after saving queued TWO items of kind `photo` — the photo's declaration (id + fingerprint) AND an empty "act" item with neither — and the server refuses the empty one as damaged. The declaration also never named its reading, so the office could not list the photo under it. **The fix, as recommended and accepted:**
- **Phone:** adding a photo to a saved reading queues ONE item, the declaration, naming the reading it belongs to (the reading's capture key — the identity the server already holds it under). FB-003's position on the photo (the shutter's, or a late one within 5 minutes) and FB-002's photo count are unchanged.
- **Server:** the declaration's reading is checked — same utility, same reader, same route — and the photo is linked to it. An unknown reading is sent back *"Photo waits for its reading."* (resent once the reading has arrived); another reader's or another route's is sent back *"Not your reading. Call the office."*
- **Office:** the reading's page lists the photo with the reading's own photos, marked *"Added after saving"*.
- **Phones already holding the refused empty items:** they are settled as sent at the next sync when their photo's declaration was accepted — nothing is lost, because the empty item never carried anything the declaration does not.
- Worked case: reading saved 09:14 with 1 photo, 2 photos added at 09:16 → Sync sends 1 reading + 3 declarations, 0 refused; the office reading lists 3 photos, the last 2 marked *"Added after saving"*. Before the fix: 1 reading + 3 declarations + 2 empty items, 2 refused.

**(2) FB-011 — a meter's history is always empty on the phone (`DEF-FLD-10638`, OPEN, DEFERRED).** FF-40 (`field-app/src/screens/raise/AssetHistoryScreen.tsx`) renders only `asset.history`, which no sync ever fills, and the server has no mobile history door. **Deferred by the PO.** When it is built, the recommendation the PO accepted is: **the last 10 visits, at most 24 months back**, downloaded with the day's work for job and route meters, and fetched on open (when online) for a meter found by search. Worked case: a meter visited 14 times in 30 months shows its 10 most recent visits inside the last 24 months; one visited twice, 26 and 30 months ago, shows none.

## 2026-10-28 — FB-014: a phone whose clock disagrees with the server is never refused; every time it sends is shifted onto the server's clock (PO)

PO, verbatim, 2026-10-28: *"how will you handle : when technician uploadds the work job if server and mobile phone time does not match in that case job should be synced with the server accept the future time."* Shown the design below and accepted it: *"start FB-014"*.

**The report (`DEF-FLD-10639`).** Android, WO-0171, about 12:02: Sync showed *"1 refused — Time · WO-0171 · That time is in the future."* *Fix and send again* had nothing to fix; sending again was sometimes accepted and sometimes refused; the office's status for WO-0171 changed only after a delay. Cause: the phone stamps every time from its OWN clock, and the server refused any labour time later than its own clock with zero tolerance (`work.labour.moment_in_future`; the close's *Finished* and a field-raised order's capture time the same). A phone running a few minutes fast is refused until the server's clock catches up — which is why a resend sometimes worked.

**What was shown and accepted:**
- **Every send carries the phone's own clock reading at the moment of sending** (`X-Device-Time`). The server computes **offset = server now − phone now** once for that send, and **shifts every time in that send by the offset before storing it**: job times, the close's *Arrived* and *Finished*, labour moments, readings' capture times, photos, and positions' fix times.
- **Never refused for a clock difference of any size, in either direction.**
- **The phone's original time and the offset are kept with the record** (the close's field data, the labour audit row, the sync's audit row), for audit.
- **The phone's Sync screen warns** *"Phone clock is N min fast. Fix the time."* (or *slow*) when the difference is more than 5 minutes — **the work still goes**.
- **The office sees** *"Phone clock was N min fast"* on the job when the difference was more than 5 minutes.
- **Worked case shown:** phone 12:07:30, server 12:02:30 → offset −5 min; a job finished at 12:07 phone time is stored as 12:02.
- **Why not store the future times as sent:** labour is priced from finished − arrived and the meter read is dated from the close (`BR-TEN-043`, `BR-WRK-003`, `BR-WRK-020`); a time in the future misprices labour and can date a read on tomorrow.

**Recorded judgment calls (ours, not put to the PO):**
1. **The limitation, stated:** the offset is measured at SEND time. Work captured offline days earlier is corrected exactly as long as the phone's clock was not changed between capture and send. If it was (the technician fixed the clock before syncing), the old work is shifted by the NEW offset and is wrong by the size of that fix; nothing on the server can detect it. A shifted time still later than the server's now (only possible that way) is clamped to now, never refused.
2. **A difference of 2 seconds or less is not shifted** — that is network delay, not a wrong clock, and shifting by it would make a replayed time item look like a correction. Offsets are whole seconds.
3. **A send with NO clock reading** (an older build, curl): behaves as before except that a time up to 5 minutes ahead of the server is clamped to the server's now rather than refused; further ahead is still refused by name, because without a reading the server cannot tell a fast clock from garbage.
4. **The refusal already on phones** (`work.labour.moment_in_future`, `work.raise.captured_in_future`) is now *Send again*, not *Fix and send again* — there is nothing on the phone to fix, and once the phone runs this build the resend carries its clock and is accepted.
5. **Labour minutes are unchanged by the shift** — arrival and finish move by the same offset, so 12:05 → 12:47 on a phone 5 min fast is stored 12:00 → 12:42, still 42 minutes.

**FB-014, built the same day — and why the office saw WO-0171's status late (recorded 2026-10-28).** The phone sends each technician-time correction through its own server door, one at a time, in capture order. **When that door REFUSED the time (*"That time is in the future"*), the phone stopped sending the rest of that job until the next sync run** — every 15 minutes, or 5 minutes after coming back to the foreground — so the CLOSE queued behind it reached the server late and the office's status changed late. A refusal is final for that one item (it waits on the Sync screen), so it no longer holds the job: the next items go in the same run, exactly as a batch already carries on past a refused item. A network failure still stops the job, so capture order holds; a refused ACCEPT still stops it, because everything behind it needs the accept. **A second, smaller delay is on the office side and is unchanged:** the Work › Orders list and the order page do not poll and do not refresh on returning to the tab (`refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, 30-second freshness), so an office user sees a close the next time the page loads or the list is re-queried. Changing that is a product-wide caching choice, not this defect, and is reported rather than made here.

## 2026-10-28 — Certificate pinning in the field app is DROPPED as a go-live requirement: option A1, the code stays dormant (`CR-195-BRC10`)

**PO, verbatim:** *"start A1"*. **What was shown first, in plain English:** the field app does not need its own certificate pinning to go live. Android already checks the server's certificate against the phone's built-in list of trusted authorities, and a fake server on public Wi-Fi fails that check. Pinning adds protection only against two rarer things: a real authority wrongly issuing a certificate for our domain, or a rooted phone. On 2.603.0 the pins (ISRG Root X1 and GTS Root R1) did not match the issuer of smartbillhub.bynry.com and every technician was locked out — the risk the pins carry today is an outage, not an attack. **Option A1 (ruled):** keep the pinning code but leave it switched OFF in BOTH builds — the beta (`preview`) and the store (`production`) — so it can be switched on later by configuration alone (`FIELD_APP_PINNING=on` plus a correct issuer list), with no new code; HIDE everything a user would see of it (the Settings › About line on the phone, the *Field app certificates* card on the staff portal's Settings › Security); rely on Android's standard certificate validation.

**Evidence shown to the PO, verified on the code 2026-10-28:**
- **Pinning off means the library is never initialised:** `field-app/src/security/pinning.ts` `start()` (about line 205) returns before touching the native module, and `refresh()` never asks for or adopts a server key list.
- **No TLS bypass anywhere:** no `rejectUnauthorized`, `trustAll` or `allowInvalid` in the field app's source or config, and no `network_security_config` (no custom trust, no cleartext permission).
- **What Android does on its own:** the app targets SDK 35 (Expo SDK 53's default). Since API 24 an app trusts only the SYSTEM certificate authorities — a certificate authority a user installs on the phone is ignored — and since API 28 plain `http://` is blocked.
- **The 2.603.0 outage came from the pins, not from the server:** ISRG/GTS did not match the server's actual issuer.

**What we built under it (our calls, law 13):**
1. **Unset now means OFF.** `FIELD_APP_PINNING` is `off` unless it says exactly `on`, in `app.config.ts` and in the phone's `pinningMode`; both EAS profiles also say `off` explicitly in `eas.json`. Hard-won law 3 (*the unsafe option is the one you type*) is applied rather than broken: the safety floor is the operating system's validation, which no configuration can turn off, and a pinning list that is wrong is what locks the fleet out — so pinning is now the option you type. A production build with pinning off is ALLOWED; with `on` typed, it pins exactly as before and still fails the build when the issuer list is malformed.
2. **The internal state is renamed `off_for_beta` → `off_by_config`.** It was never shown to a user; the name was simply no longer true.
3. **The server address must be `https://`.** `http://` is now refused as *No server set*. No build profile uses `http` (the `development` profile names no server at all), so no development exception was added.
4. **The staff portal card is hidden by one platform setting**, `SBH_FIELD_APP_PINNING_ENABLED` (default false), served to the Security tab as `field_app_pinning_enabled`. The stored key lists, `GET/PUT settings/security-policy/field-app-pins` and the phone's `field_app_pins` in its settings answer are untouched, so the card returns by setting one value.
5. **Kept, unchanged:** the honest connection errors — *"Can't verify the server. Contact the office."* for a refused certificate (it still fires: Android's own check refuses a fake server the same way), *"The server needs an update."*, and *No signal* only for a real dropped connection.
6. **Separate from the VAPT round** (`09-infra/06-vapt-remediation-2026-10.md` is not touched).

**PENDING VERIFICATION — two checks, recorded so nobody reads this as proven:**
1. **DevOps to confirm the real issuer of smartbillhub.bynry.com** (the certificate chain on the production host). Needed only if pinning is ever switched back on.
2. **One test-phone run with a mitmproxy certificate authority installed on the phone:** the app must refuse and say *"Can't verify the server"*. This proves on a real handset that a user-installed authority is ignored.

## 2026-10-28 — CORRECTION to the 2026-10-26 entry *"Certificate pinning is OFF in the beta (preview) build, ON for go-live"*

That entry is left as written (the log is append-only). **One sentence in it overstated the risk:** *"Risk accepted for the beta: no protection against a fake server on public Wi-Fi (a tester's password and test data could be read there)."* **That is wrong.** With pinning off the phone still runs Android's standard certificate check, which refuses a fake server on public Wi-Fi: the attacker cannot present a certificate for smartbillhub.bynry.com that chains to an authority the phone trusts. What pinning adds on top is protection against **a wrongly issued but genuine certificate for our domain**, or **a rooted phone** whose system trust store has been altered. Its *"Before go-live … turn pinning on"* step is also superseded by the entry above: pinning is not a go-live requirement.

5. The phone keeps its copy of a photo until the server confirms it has the bytes (unchanged — `field-app/src/sync/photos.ts` deletes the file only on a `staged`/`landed` answer).

**The worked case (WO-0171, FB-015):** *Send photos over mobile data* was ON, a job with a photo was completed on mobile data, and Sync read *"Photos · All sent"*, *"1 of 1 · 0 MB left"* AND *"Photos wait for wi-fi."* at once; the web order showed no photo. Under option A that phone sends the photo on mobile data with no setting touched, and the wi-fi line does not appear.

**SUPERSEDES `R54` / `BR-FLD-00054`** (*"Photographs wait for wi-fi unless the technician says otherwise — a setting inside the app, defaulting to off on mobile data"*, CONFIRMED 2026-10-20/21). Stamped SUPERSEDED with this date in `04-docs/05-modules/18-field-app/02-business-rules.md`, `06-epics/EP-FLD-09-kit-sync-settings.md`, `03-field-map.md`, `09-component-inventory.md` and in `field-app/src/screens/me/prefs.ts`.

**Lane judgment recorded (not put to the PO):** the label is the PO's own four words, *Photos on wi-fi only*, although B14 rule 33 caps a label at three; the PO named the setting in the ruling, and a ruling's wording beats a rule's paraphrase of it. The old key `handset.sync.photosOnMobileData` is deleted on first start and never read again — per point 3 its value no longer decides anything.

## 2026-10-28 — FB-013: a cleared balance STOPS the money-check step; the technician may close "Not done — payment received" (three PO rulings, recorded verbatim, with what was shown)

**The report (FB-013, web):** the Disconnection/Reconnection template's steps have no payment-check setting, so how does a technician know the balance was cleared on a job assigned three days ago?

**What was shown to the PO, in plain English with a figure:** a disconnect job assigned on Monday for a $312.40 arrear; the customer pays $312.40 on Wednesday morning; the technician arrives Wednesday afternoon and the phone's fresh read (under five minutes old) says the balance is $0.00. Should the phone stop the disconnect, or only warn?

**(a) PO, verbatim:** *"When the balance is cleared, should the phone stop the disconnect step, or only warn? Stop it, with 'Hand back to office'… Your earlier rule (warned, never blocked) stays for stale balances"*. So a FRESH read showing the balance cleared STOPS the money-check step. **R17 (`BR-FLD-00017`) is unchanged for stale money**: older than the step's bar is warned, never blocked, and proceeding is recorded unverified.

**(b) PO, verbatim:** *"is techncian can upload without performing disconnection work order can he upload with remark that payment is done and push the job to server"* — shown and accepted (*"start FB-013"*): at the stopped step the technician gets two buttons, **Close — payment received** and **Hand back to office**. Close opens the Close screen with a new outcome **Not done — payment received** and a prefilled, editable remark *"Customer has paid. Not disconnected."*; times as usual; photo optional; it syncs like any close (offline it queues). Offered ONLY when the phone saw the balance cleared FRESH (within the step's own freshness bar); stale or no signal ⇒ only the existing warning (proceed recorded unverified, or hand back) and NO paid close. The balance and latest payment the phone saw (amount, date, as-at) are stored with the close. Office: the work order reads *Closed · Not done — payment received* with the remark, the times and the money seen; filterable in the Work list; a notice *"WO-0171 · Not disconnected — payment received"*.

**(c) Also shown and standing:** R18 (`BR-FLD-00018`) — no code knows what a disconnect is. The stop keys off the template step's `money_fresh_minutes` only.

**Our judgments where the rulings ran out (law 13 — ours to decide and write down):**
1. **"Cleared" is exact:** the money answer's OWING figure (`owing`, else `balance`) at four decimals (hard rule 2) is **≤ 0.0000**, in the account's currency. A credit balance is cleared. A figure withheld (contractor, R26) or unavailable is NOT cleared — no stop, no paid close.
2. **"Fresh" is the stopped step's own bar** (`money_fresh_minutes` on that task), measured from the server's `as_at` to the moment the phone showed the stop — never the global five minutes.
3. **The server is STRICT.** A close with outcome `not_done_payment_received` is REFUSED (back to the technician, R48) unless it carries the phone's snapshot (`field_data.money_seen`: balance, currency, as_at, the step, when it was checked) proving a fresh, cleared read on a step that declares a money check. With a snapshot it is accepted and the server RE-READS the account's money at the close and stores BOTH under `field_data.payment_received` — `phone` (what was seen) and `server` (what the server read, with its own as-at). The phone's snapshot is never trusted blindly: it is stored as what was seen, beside the server's own read.
4. **The token is `not_done_payment_received`**, a SIXTH value of `work_orders.outcome` (`ck_work_orders_outcome` widened in a migration); its R4 word on the office's queue filter is `not_done_paid`. `BR-FLD-00004` (four outcomes) is AMENDED to five technician outcomes by ruling (b).
5. **"Filterable in the Work list" is built on the Field desk's Results list (the acceptance queue), which already filters by outcome.** The dispatcher's Orders list shows OPEN jobs only — a closed job never appears in it — and `BR-WRK-026` fixes it at exactly six filters; a seventh there would filter nothing and collide with a signed rule. So `BR-WRK-026` does NOT move.
6. **The office notice replaces the plain *closed in the field* bell for a paid close** (one bell per close, never two): event `not_done_paid`, bell *"{{order}} · Not disconnected — payment received"*.
7. **The template editor's control is per step:** *Check payment before this step* (tick), minutes (default 5, at least 1) and an optional fee charge code (FF-61's R111 question). There is no shared charge-code picker component in the web kit, so the code is typed; the server already stores it as text.
8. **Sample data:** the sample *Disconnect visit* template's cut step and the sample *Reconnect visit*'s restore step carry a five-minute check — for NEW sample utilities only; a template already published is never rewritten (a published template changes by a new version, which is the utility's act).

## 2026-10-29 — A chart account's CODE may be changed by a System Admin even when the account is used; the new code applies everywhere at once, the old one is kept as "formerly" (`CR-196-BRC10`; amends BR-LED-040 and US-LED-005 for CODE only)

**PO, verbatim:** *"in many cases utilities are giving there own GL codes; which means we have to ability to change existing GL code as per the given utility for that specific tenant; even if they are used ; if user update them they should be applicable after the updation."*

**Approved behaviours (shown and approved, as listed to the PO):**
1. Chart of accounts › Edit: the CODE is editable even when the account is used; unique within the tenant.
2. Save shows a confirmation with usage counts: *"This code is used on N bills and N payments. The new code applies everywhere from now on."*
3. It applies everywhere at once — everything references the account by id, not by its code.
4. The old code is kept as history (old, new, who, when) in `audit_log` and shown on the account as *"formerly 4100"*.
6. TYPE stays locked once used.
7. Delete stays refused when used; Disable stays available.
8. The signed story rule US-LED-005 (*"code and type frozen once anything posts"*, built as BR-LED-040) is AMENDED for CODE only, dated, in the ledger module's business rules and the story, every citing document stamped.

**Four questions, each answered A, with the worked example shown:**
- **Q1 — A.** Past entries and old reports show the NEW code everywhere, with "formerly" kept. *Shown:* Solar Service is `4150` from January to September and becomes `0117-080-1000-0000-7110` on 1 October; the September GL report then shows `0117-080-1000-0000-7110` *"(formerly 4150)"*.
- **Q2 — A.** Allowed even when the account was in a closed month or an export already sent, with a warning: *"Already exported for Sep 2026. Re-exports will show the new code."*
- **Q3 — A.** Type is locked once used. *Shown:* tax account `0117-…-7126` typed Expense by mistake — the fix is a new Liability account and a re-map, never a re-type.
- **Q4 — A.** Only a System Admin may change a code; clerks keep name editing.

**PO, on the four risks put to them:** risks 1 and 2 — re-seeding finds accounts by code, and tax is recognised by the `2200` prefix — *"this is ok we will seed it and then chnage it or cutomize it as per utility"*. Risks 3 (default lookups by code: `ledger/selectors.py` ~220/~543/~557, `services.py` ~694) and 4 (re-exports show the new code): *"ok do not make chnages"*. **So the default lookups and the exports are NOT changed.**

**OUR JUDGMENT where the ruling ran out (law 13 — recorded as ours, not asked again):** the PO's own workflow, *"seed it and then change it"*, FAILS on the very next deploy unless two invisible guards exist, so we build exactly these two and nothing else from risks 1–2:
- **5a — re-seeding identifies a seeded account by a fixed internal key, not by its code.** `ledger_accounts.seed_key` (new, nullable) holds the code the account was SEEDED or MINTED under; it is set at seed time, back-filled for existing rows whose code is a seed code or a 2200-series tax code, NEVER shown on screen and NEVER changed by a code edit. The reference sweep (`_create_missing_accounts`, run on every `migrate`) skips a seed row whose key is already held.
- **5b — the tax-liability check also accepts an account whose `seed_key` is in the 2200 series**, and keeps accepting a code with the `2200` prefix exactly as today.
- **Worked case:** a utility renames `4150` → `0117-080-1000-0000-7127` and its tax account `2200-01` → `0117-080-1000-0000-7126`. On the next deploy, **without 5a** the sweep finds no `4150` and creates an EMPTY duplicate *4150 Solar service revenue* beside the renamed one (and would do the same for any seeded row); **without 5b** a tax remittance against `…-7126` is REFUSED (*"not in the signed 2200 tax-payable series"*) and the account drops off the tax filing report and the month-end remittance check, while still holding the liability.
- **Two consequences of 5a we also decided:** the 2200-nn allocator counts a renamed tax account's key as well as live codes (otherwise renaming `2200-01` away would let the next authority be numbered `2200-01` again, which BR-LED-023 forbids and which the key's uniqueness would refuse); and an account's *finance-signed* and *seeded* flags on the chart read the key, so a renamed unsigned account cannot start reading as finance-signed (US-LED-017 TC-5).
- **"Formerly" is stored on the account, not only in `audit_log`.** `audit_log` is pruned on its retention schedule (PO 2026-09-23, OQ-1340: *"when audit log is delete - it is deleted thats okay"*), so "formerly 4150" read from the audit trail would silently vanish from the account after a year. The history (old, new, who, when) is kept in a ledger-owned column `ledger_accounts.code_history`, AND an audit row `ledger_account.code_changed` {old, new} is written (hard rule 7; the action spelt in the family the chart already writes — `ledger_account.created`, `.updated` — so the audit filter finds it beside them).
- **Not changed, and said so:** the remitting basis per tax authority on Finance controls is keyed by the authority's account CODE (`reporting._remitting_basis_by_authority`), so renaming a tax account shows that authority's basis as *not set* until it is chosen again — a default lookup by code, the PO's risk 3, left as ruled and filed as a defect so it is counted.

## 2026-10-29 — A cut and a restoration TELL THE CUSTOMER: "Service disconnected" and "Service restored" (PO, "1 A, 2 A, 3 A, 4 A" then "start")

**What the PO reported.** After *Mark as cut* (Customer 360 → Disconnect case; `POST /api/<tenant>/accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/cut`, `customers.disconnects.commit_cut`) the customer is told NOTHING: the cut takes the closing read, raises the final bill, charges the $75.00 reconnection fee and writes *Disconnected*, and no email or text is queued. Settings → Notifications holds only the PRE-cut notices (the 10-day / 5-day / 48-hour disconnect notice ladder, the disconnect SMS supplement, the door hanger) and no post-cut template. `restore_service` sends nothing either.

**Shown, and ruled verbatim *"1 A, 2 A, 3 A, 4 A"*, then *"start"*:**
1. **A — send BOTH.** *Service disconnected* when the cut is recorded, and *Service restored* when service is restored.
2. **A — email and SMS**, each only where the customer has that contact and (for SMS) has consented to texts; never to a closed contact.
3. **A — automatic, ON by default**, and each utility can switch either off on Settings → Notifications (rules).
4. **A — we write a short default safety text**, and each utility edits it on Settings → Templates. Disconnected: keep taps and valves closed until service is restored; do not reconnect yourself — it is unsafe and an offence; medical or critical-care need → call {support_phone}. Restored: open taps slowly; report leaks or the smell of gas.

**Also shown and accepted:** use the ONE shared pipeline (`notifications.services.queue_document`, the rules catalogue, the templates, the recipient and consent checks, the dispatcher and the timeline) — new code only for two rule entries, the templates, two fact-gathering queue functions and two call sites; and EXTEND the shared account-message helper `customer_events._queue_account_message` (email-only today) to take channels, instead of writing a second path.

**Worked figure put to the PO:** a customer owing $612.75 is cut on 24 August; the email reads *balance owed $612.75 · reconnection fee $75.00 · total to restore $687.75*, with the closing reading WITH its unit (`W-5043: 2645 kgal`), and the text carries the total and the support number.

**Our judgments where the rulings ran out (law 13 — recorded, not re-asked):**
1. **The two events ride source kind `account`** (no print floor — BR-NOT-024 names invoice, payment, notice and plan, and a post-cut notice is none of them, so a utility switching it off gets nothing) and live in the **Collections** category beside the disconnect notice, because the moment is collections'.
2. **The key is the CASE plus the act**, derived (`uuid5(case, "disconnected"|"restored")`), never the bare case id: `account_closed` already keys on the case id under the same source kind, so a bare case key would dedupe the closing letter into the cut notice. A replayed call finds its own rows and writes nothing (rule 6).
3. **Figures after the cut:** `reconnection_terms` reads the position once (`to_clear`, fee already inside it after the cut, `fee_in_arrears`). So *total to restore* = that position, *reconnection fee* = the fee, *balance owed* = position − fee. Before-the-cut basis (fee not yet in AR) is handled too: balance = position, total = position + fee. An unreadable position prints a named absence, never $0.00 (BR-CUS-015).
4. **SMS without consent writes a row that says `no_sms_opt_in` and sends nothing** — the payment receipt's precedent (A15 made visible), so *did we tell them?* always has an answer. No contact at all → the row carries `no_email_address` / `no_mobile_number`.
5. **The restoration link** is the customer portal's quick-pay page, `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN/<subdomain>/portal/pay`; with no public origin configured the paragraph carrying it is left out (law 3), never a relative link.
6. **Languages:** the eleven-language shape of `move_out_wording` (one module, B14 rule 35) — lane-authored defaults each utility edits.

## 2026-10-29 — Messages needing attention: a default attention view, safe bulk re-queue, the last attempt's error, and "Fix address and retry" for THIS message only (PO, "1A 2A 3B 4B, start") — `DEF-NOT-10650`

**What the PO reported.** Settings → Reference Data → Notifications → *Messages needing attention* has no attention-only filter (it lists every message, failures sorted first), no bulk re-queue selection, no error diagnostics beyond a one-line *Last error*, and no way to correct a recipient.

**Shown, and ruled verbatim *"1A 2A 3B 4B, start"*:**
1. **A — the screen OPENS on *Needing attention*.** A switch *Needing attention · All messages*, with a count on *Needing attention*.
2. **A — checkboxes on the rows that can be re-queued**, plus *Select all on this page*, and an explicit second action **"Select all N matching"** (capped at **500**). A bar reads *"N selected · Re-queue · Clear"*. **An empty selection NEVER means all.** The result is a toast with per-row tallies, e.g. *"48 re-queued. 2 could not be: already sent."*
3. **B — *Fix address and retry* changes ONLY this message's delivery.** It does NOT update the customer's contact record. The failed message stays as the record and a NEW message is queued to the corrected address; the audit trail records old → new, who and when.
4. **B — the error details panel shows the LAST attempt only.** No per-attempt history store.

**Our judgments where the rulings ran out (law 13 — recorded, not re-asked):**
1. **"Needing attention" is `models.ATTENTION_STATUSES` and nothing else** — failed, bounced, bounced (hard), bounced (soft), complained. It is the tuple the triage sort, the partial index and `delivery_ops.failures` already read, so the view, the sort and the count cannot disagree. `held` is NOT added: a held row is a returned letter released by address verification on the account (BR-PAY-018), not by anything on this screen; a held row that is also failed still appears, with no checkbox.
2. **"Select all N matching" is resolved by the SERVER from the same filter the list used** (`GET /outbound/selection`), and the ids it returns are what the re-queue posts. It returns every matching row, re-queueable or not, so the tallies say what could not move and why; above 500 it refuses with a sentence and selects nothing. The 500 is a per-ACTION ceiling the PO set, not a per-tenant cap (NFR-5): narrowing the view and repeating reaches every row.
3. **The re-queue toast is composed on the screen from the server's per-row codes**, in the clerk's language, rather than the server's English `toast` string.
4. **Fix address and retry is offered on email and text rows only** (print, in-app and portal carry no address a clerk can type), and only on failed, bounced, bounced (hard) and bounced (soft) rows. It is refused on sent and delivered rows (the customer has it), on held rows (address verification releases those), on queued rows (the original would still go out — two messages), and on complained rows (the person asked not to be mailed). The new message is the same document, template version and figures, at the next free copy number (`copy_no`), and it does NOT add a second paper copy: the print floor already went out at copy 0.
5. **The link from the new message to the old one is the audit row** (`delivery.retried_to_new_address`, before = the failed message and its address, after = the new message and its address). No column and no migration: one row per correction already answers *who, when, old, new*. A customer email or phone is MED class (pii-inventory), which audit payloads may carry (BR-AUD-006).
6. **The error panel shows the provider's reference labelled as theirs** (it is the provider's id, which support quotes to them), never our own message id (B14 rule 31).

## 2026-10-29 — The automatic past-due reminder follows the Settings rule and the customer's contacts; a printed letter for a customer with no email and no SMS consent; history says Sent only for what was queued (PO, "1A 2A 3A 4B, start") — `DEF-PAY-10651`

**What the PO reported** (*"Tier 1 Dunning Past-Due Reminder Missing Email & SMS Queue Hooks"*, Scenario 6A). The nightly collections run takes an account to ladder rung 1 at due date + 3 days and calls the friendly reminder with no channels, so it defaulted to paper only; the template it asked for was the synthesised name `collections_reminder_friendly`, which exists nowhere, so even the paper row could never render; the Settings → Notifications rule *Past-due reminder* (email `email_past_due`, SMS `sms_past_due`) was never read; and the account's notice history recorded **Sent** for every channel whatever was queued, and the ladder advanced the account on it. Worked: an account due 1 Oct, run on 4 Oct, with an email address and SMS consent — the customer received nothing, the history read *Sent · pdf_print*, and the next run moved on to the 10-day notice as though they had been reminded.

**Shown, and ruled verbatim *"1A 2A 3A 4B, start"*:**
1. **A — the automatic Tier 1 reminder uses the Settings › Notifications rule `past_due_reminder`**: its on/off and its channels (today email + SMS), per customer's contacts and consent — email if the account has an address, SMS only with SMS consent; the templates are that rule's (`email_past_due`, `sms_past_due`).
2. **A — a customer with no email and no SMS consent gets a PRINTED past-due reminder letter**, seeded (editable, 11 languages, wording under `seed_templates`' conventions).
3. **A — the timing stays the signed `BR-PAY-017` due date + 3 days.** No change.
4. **B — no list of historic false "Sent" rows is produced.** History stays as it is; the bug is fixed going forward.

**Our judgments where the rulings ran out (law 13 — recorded, not re-asked):**
1. **The printed letter is the EXISTING `dunning` class, not a new one.** `catalogs.LISTINGS` already carries `dunning` as *"Past-due reminder · Print"*, `BR-NOT-008` already says the friendly step renders it, and the manual Send-notice wizard's *Friendly* tone already previews it. Minting `letter_past_due` beside it would put two print templates called *Past-due reminder* on Settings › Templates, one of which nothing sends. What the ruling asked for — seeded, editable, eleven languages — is done to `dunning`: its `default` stays A13's quoted sentence and a variant is planted per registry language (`past_due_letter_wording`, B14 rule 35), on new utilities at provisioning and on existing ones by migration. The rule `past_due_reminder` gains a **Print** channel whose template is `dunning`, ON by default, so a utility can see and switch the letter.
2. **Print goes out ONLY when no digital channel can reach the customer** (ruling 2's reading: the letter is the fallback, not a third copy). So the reminder is queued under its own message kind, `reminder`, which carries **no print floor**. ⚠ **This narrows `BR-NOT-024` for the friendly reminder and is stated, not assumed:** that rule floors every `notice`, and the reminder used to ride `notice`. Ruling 1 (the rule's on/off decides) and ruling 2 (paper only for a customer we cannot otherwise reach) cannot both hold under a floor that survives the master switch, so the reminder leaves the floored kind. **The disconnection notices stay on `notice` and keep the floor** — nothing about a legal notice moves. Worked: 1,000 overdue accounts, 700 with email — before, 1,000 letters would have been floored onto paper (had any rendered); now 300 letters, 700 emails.
3. **One path for both doors.** The nightly run (`collections_schedule` → `ladder.run_ladder`) and the manual S35 *Send reminder* (`notices_by_hand` → `ladder.step_one`) both reach `notices.send_reminders`, which asks `apps.notifications.past_due_reminder` (resolved by name, B1) for the channels and queues through it. The channels a caller passes no longer choose the reminder's channels; the rule and the customer do. **`tone` is dropped from the reminder** — the friendly reminder has one template set, and the firm/final tones were always disconnect tiers (`TONE_TO_STEP`), not reminder wordings.
4. **History says Sent per channel ONLY for a message actually queued by this call.** Otherwise one *skipped* row per channel with a named reason: `rule_off` (the event, or the only reachable channel, switched off), `no_contact` (no address on the channel, and no postal address for the letter), `no_sms_consent`, `template_missing` (no published version to render — the row is not queued at all, because a row that can never render is the defect), `queue_problem` (written but held — the do-not-send list). **A reminder with zero queued messages is not a step taken**: the ladder does not advance and the next run tries again. ⚠ **The consequence, stated so it can be overruled cheaply:** a utility that switches *Past-due reminder* OFF stops the ladder at rung 1 for every account — the 10-day notice is never reached, because rung 1 never completes. That is what *"rule off ⇒ nothing queued and the ladder does not advance"* means; if the PO wants *off* to mean *skip the reminder and carry on*, it is one line in `ladder._send`.
5. **A re-run the same day writes nothing twice.** The queue key is the account, the kind and the business DATE (`ladder_notice_source_id(..., occasion=on_date)`): the same day finds its own rows (`created=False`, history row `already_noticed_today`), and next month's reminder is a new document rather than the old row found again — without the date the second cycle's reminder could never be queued.
6. **SMS quiet hours (`BR-NOT-009`) are the dispatcher's, unchanged** — a queued `sms_past_due` row holds outside the send window; this lane proves it and reimplements nothing.

## 2026-10-29 — TEXT MESSAGES (SMS) ARE BUILT NOW, THROUGH ONE SHARED PLATFORM TWILIO ACCOUNT (PO, *"1A 2A 4B 5 US 6A(ONly Stop option is required), start"*) — `CR-198-BRC10`

⚠ **THIS SUPERSEDES THE PO'S 2026-09-17 RULING ON SMS** — *EMAIL AS A PLATFORM SERVICE*, row 7: *"Is text/SMS in scope now or later?"* → ***"later"*** (*"`sms_twilio` stays `coming_soon` with no adapter"*). From today SMS is in scope and is built. Every *SMS v1.1* deferral (`BR-INT-001`'s *Twilio SMS (v1.1)*, `BR-PAY-017`'s *"SMS Twilio seam"*, `provider_seam.DEFERRED_UNTIL["sms"] = "v1.1"`, the manifest's `Disposition(kind="coming_soon", wave="v1.1")`) is stamped SUPERSEDED with this date in the same change.

**Shown, and ruled verbatim *"1A 2A 4B 5 US 6A(ONly Stop option is required), start"*:**
1. **A — build SMS now.**
2. **A — every existing SMS message goes**, each governed by its own Settings › Notifications rule (bill ready, past-due, disconnect notices, field visit, outage, disconnected/restored, …). No new message kinds; the rules decide which texts exist.
3. *(answered separately)* **The public callback address** — the PO will supply each server's value from DevOps. We add ONE server setting, `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`; unset, no status callback is asked for and the Integrations card says so (law 3).
4. **B — ONE SHARED PLATFORM Twilio account**, not one per utility — the same shape as email (2026-09-17, ruling 3: *"our account - we will provdie servcie to utilities as platform provider"*). The credentials are SERVER secrets (`TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` + `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `TWILIO_API_KEY_SID` + `TWILIO_API_KEY_SECRET` for sending with the Auth Token still needed to check Twilio's callback signature), never in a tenant row, never on a screen, never in a log.
5. **US** — the first customer is in the United States, so **A2P 10DLC registration applies** (a brand and a campaign registered with the carriers before any volume is sent). That makes **Messaging Service SID support required**, and it is built.
6. **A, STOP only** — a customer replying **STOP** puts the number on the do-not-text list AND turns OFF that account's *SMS reminders* tick, audited, through the customers module's own service. ⚠ **START and HELP are NOT built** (PO: *"ONly Stop option is required"*). Twilio's own Advanced Opt-Out answers HELP and START at the carrier level; a customer who sends START is re-allowed by Twilio but stays on OUR list and keeps the tick OFF until a clerk turns it back on — the safe direction.

**Our judgments where the rulings ran out (law 13 — recorded, not re-asked):**

1. **ONE PLATFORM SENDER BY DEFAULT, WITH A PER-UTILITY SENDER HELD BY THE SERVER — NEVER BY THE UTILITY.** The email precedent gives each utility its own sender identity (the decision log of 2026-09-17: *"the emails will say they come FROM THE UTILITY"*), so the equivalent here is a per-utility Messaging Service. But a utility must never be able to TYPE one: a Messaging Service SID is not a secret, and a clerk who typed another utility's SID would text that utility's customers from that utility's number. So the map lives in the SERVER's environment, set by DevOps alongside the 10DLC campaign: `TWILIO_SENDER_BY_UTILITY="riverbend:MG…;ottumwa:+15155550100"` (subdomain → a Messaging Service SID or an E.164 From number). A utility not on the map sends through the platform default, `TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID` (preferred, required for 10DLC) or `TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER`. **Exactly one of From / MessagingServiceSid goes on each request.** **Worked case:** Riverbend's 10DLC campaign is approved on Messaging Service `MG…A1`; DevOps adds `riverbend:MG…A1`; Riverbend's past-due text goes out with `MessagingServiceSid=MG…A1`, and a second utility with no entry goes out on the platform's `MG…P0`. Nothing a utility types changes either.
2. **A STOP IS APPLIED TO EVERY UTILITY THAT SHARES THAT SENDER AND HAS TEXTED THAT NUMBER — AND TO NO OTHER.** A reply arrives at one tenant-less address (a shared sender has no utility in its webhook URL). Twilio's own opt-out on a Messaging Service already blocks the number for every utility sending through it, so recording it for exactly the utilities that (a) send through the sender the reply was addressed to and (b) have an SMS on record to that number is the truth, not a leak. Each write runs inside that utility's own tenant context. A utility that never texted the person is untouched; if it texts them later Twilio answers `21610` and that failure suppresses the number for it then.
3. **STATUS CALLBACKS CARRY THE UTILITY IN THEIR ADDRESS** — `{PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL}/api/{utility}/integrations/platform/sms_twilio/status` — because WE build that URL per message, so the tenant is the path (BR-TEN-003) and a callback for one utility cannot touch another's message.
4. **THE SIGNATURE IS CHECKED AGAINST THE ADDRESS WE PUBLISHED, NOT THE ONE THE REQUEST CLAIMS.** Twilio signs `URL + every POST field sorted by name` with HMAC-SHA1 and the account's Auth Token. We rebuild the URL from `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` + the request's path and query, so a proxy rewriting `Host` cannot make a forged call verify. Wrong token, a changed field or a different URL → `401` and NOTHING is saved. Constant-time comparison.
5. **A DELIVERY STATUS IS SAVED ONCE PER (MESSAGE, STATUS)** — Twilio retries callbacks, so `sent` then `delivered` are two rows and a repeated `delivered` is one. Twilio's words map to ours: `queued`/`accepted`/`sending`/`sent` → *in transit* (the row stays `sent`), `delivered` → `delivered`, `undelivered`/`failed` → `failed` keeping Twilio's `ErrorCode`. `21610` (*the person replied STOP*) also suppresses the number.
6. **PACING IS THE DISPATCHER'S, AT 60 A MINUTE PER SENDER** — the manifest's existing `rate_limit_per_minute=60`, one long-code's honest rate. A 10DLC campaign may allow more; raising it is a one-line manifest change once the campaign's throughput is known.
7. **SMS DISPATCH IS LIFTED ONLY WHEN THE PLATFORM CREDENTIALS ARE PRESENT.** With them absent the channel reads *Waiting for a text provider*, every SMS row rests `queued` with `provider_status_unknown` exactly as today, and the Test button refuses by name. The utility's own *Turn texts on* switch and each customer's *SMS reminders* tick still both have to say yes.
8. **NO REAL PHONE IS PROVED FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT.** Outbound HTTPS to Twilio is not reachable here and no Twilio test credentials are configured; every proof is against a mocked HTTP layer and a fake Twilio endpoint, and says so.

## 2026-10-29 — A work order raised for a customer WITHOUT a date tells them "Work order logged"; the technician stays on the phone push; preparation instructions per template; no visit messages for disconnect-type jobs (PO, "1A 2A 3B 4A, start") — `DEF-WRK-10652`

**The report (PO, 2026-10-29):** *"Work Order Raised Dual-Notification Missing for Customer & Assigned Field Technician"* — raised `WO-0085` with a customer and a technician and saw nothing go to either.

**What was shown first — much of it is already built (`CR-168-BRC10` SRV-5, `apps/work/visit_notices.py`):** the customer is told *booked* on the first assign/schedule that leaves a customer job with a date (rule `appointment_window`, email `service_appointment` + SMS `sms_visit_booked`), *moved*, *on the way* and *completed*; the technician gets a field-app PUSH on assignment (`dispatch.push_after_assign` / `apps/work/push.py`), and a job assigned at its raise (`raise_svc.raise_work_order` → `dispatch.record_act(push=False)`) pushes after the commit.

**Reproduced before any code (harness, SQLite shim, Brazos Bend, the real `raise_svc.raise_work_order`, assignee D. Ortiz):**
| Raise | Customer channels elected | Customer rows written | Technician |
|---|---|---|---|
| no date | none (the account default) | **0** | push job |
| with a date | none (the account default) | **0** — `visit_message_no_channel_elected` | push job |
| no date | email + SMS | **0** — no message exists for an undated raise | push job |
| with a date | email + SMS | **2** — `service_appointment` (email) + `sms_visit_booked` (SMS), both `queued` | push job |

So `WO-0085` showed nothing for up to THREE independent reasons, and only the first is this defect: **(1)** a job raised without a date has no customer message at all; **(2)** a visit message honours the customer's own election (`accounts.paperless` → email, `accounts.sms_reminders` → SMS) and **both default OFF** on a new account — unlike a bill, which since `DEF-BIL-10535` emails whenever an address is on file; **(3)** on this deployment `email_dispatch_active` and `sms_dispatch_active` are both **False**, so even a written row rests `queued` and is never sent. The harness tenant also has no support phone, so `{support_phone}` renders as the named absence `——`. (2) and (3) are NOT changed by this ruling and are stated here so the next report is read against them.

**Shown, and ruled verbatim *"1A 2A 3B 4A, start"*:**
1. **A — a NEW customer message "Work order logged"** when a job WITH A CUSTOMER is raised WITHOUT a date or window: order number, type, address (walked from the premises, hard rule 8), *"we'll confirm a date"*, support phone. The existing *booked* still follows when a date is given later. **Never both for one raise**: raised WITH a date ⇒ only *booked*.
2. **A — the technician's notice stays the field-app PUSH only. No technician email.**
3. **B — preparation instructions per work-order TEMPLATE**: a new editable field on the template (worked: meter exchange *"Clear 3 ft around the meter box."*; leak check *"Turn off irrigation."*), copied onto the job at raise like the template's other fields (`BR-WRK-008`), and shown in the customer's *logged*, *booked* and *moved* messages as the token `{prep_instructions}`. When the template's is blank, a **utility-level default** applies, seeded *"Please give our technician clear access to the meter: unlock gates and keep pets inside."*
4. **A — no logged / booked / moved customer message for collections or emergency disconnect-type jobs**, decided by a TEMPLATE setting and never by a type name (R18's posture: no code knows what a disconnect is): *"Send customer visit messages"*, ON by default, OFF on the seeded disconnect / reconnect templates. The existing disconnect notices cover those customers.

**Our judgments where the rulings ran out (law 13 — recorded, not re-asked):**
1. **Both new template fields live on `wot_details`, Work's own one-row-per-template table, and are copied onto `work_order_details`** — the same pair that already carries the four `show_*` flags, so the copy rides `order_copies.write_copies` and no foreign table is touched (G78). A job raised with NO template reads the switch ON and the utility default text.
2. **The utility default lives on `work_settings.visit_prep_default`** (Work's own policy row). NULL — every utility until somebody edits it — reads the seeded sentence above; an EMPTY string is a utility that deliberately wants no default, and the token is then blank. Read and set through `GET/POST /work/settings/visit-messages`.
3. **The switch gates every CUSTOMER visit message the template governs — logged, booked, moved, on the way and done** — because a disconnect crew announcing *"on the way"* to the customer being cut is exactly what ruling 4 exists to stop, and the disconnect notices already speak for that visit. The back-office notices (at risk, declined, blocked) and the technician's push are NOT gated.
4. **"Seeded disconnect / reconnect templates" is read from the TEMPLATE's own type**, not its name: every sample template whose type is the lookup row seeded as the disconnect or the reconnect type is seeded with the switch OFF, at provisioning and once for existing utilities by migration. After that it is the utility's switch.
5. **The editor round-trips both fields, and a save that does not mention them KEEPS them** (an absent key is *unchanged*, never *reset to the default*) — the money-check fields were lost exactly by an editor whose save dropped what it did not send.
6. **Rule `work_order_logged`** — customer audience, email + SMS, default ON, timing `on_raise`, templates `service_work_order_logged` (email) and `sms_work_order_logged` (SMS). The logged key is one per JOB, so a replay or a repeated call writes nothing twice. The new and the amended default wordings reach a NEW utility at provisioning and an existing one on its next `seed_notice_templates` run; a template a utility has already published keeps its own wording (the token is offered, never forced into their text).

**Addendum to the `DEF-WRK-10652` entry above (2026-10-29, same lane) — two further judgments made while building, recorded rather than re-asked (law 13):** (7) a raise that gives the job only a DUE DATE (a deadline, not a visit) is told *logged* unless an assignment at the raise already booked it — a due date tells the customer nothing about when someone will come; (8) an undated job's messages carry NO appointment date and NO window (the old context wrote *"any time that day"* even with no day at all). **And one fact for the next lane:** a utility that EDITED its booked/moved email keeps its own wording and shows no preparation line until it adds `{prep_instructions}` itself (`notifications/0032` republished only byte-identical seeded copies — 3 on the walk harness).

## 2026-10-29 — Templates, notifications and communication: twelve questions ruled in one message (PO)

Put to the PO as question · real example · options; ruled verbatim *"A1 C,A2 A,A3 A,A4 B,B1 A,B2 -Not required,B3 A,B4 A,B5 A,C1 -Restore = Reconnect request, D1 A,D2 A,E- E1,E2,E3,E4 we will provide the detail our devops will set the details in env file"*, then *"Start the changes related to this questions, Don't start the changes related to redesign of template"*.
- **Templates redesign (recorded, NOT to be built yet):** A1 **C** — only legal notices (disconnect, collections) need a System Admin's approval; everything else publishes in one click. A2 **A** — placeholders only from the allowed list; an unknown one blocks saving. A3 **A** — a variant is channel × language × customer category. A4 **B** — only the utility's switched-on languages are offered. Mock-up: claude.ai artifact "Templates Redesign".
- **B1 A** — visit messages (logged, booked, moved, on the way, done) go by EMAIL whenever the account has an address, as bills do; SMS still needs consent. Example shown: Rosa has an email but never ticked paperless → she now gets the booked email.
- **B2 — not required**: no screen for the utility default preparation text (the endpoint stays).
- **B3 A** — the past-due reminder prints only when nothing digital reaches the customer (BR-NOT-024's always-print floor narrowed for the reminder; disconnect notices keep it). Example: 1,000 overdue, 700 with email → 300 letters. Ratifies DEF-PAY-10651's judgment 1.
- **B4 A** — the past-due reminder rule OFF means SKIP the reminder and carry on to the 10-day notice as normal (reverses the as-built "stop the ladder").
- **B5 A** — the ten non-English versions of the new letters/messages are reviewed by a native speaker before go-live; we list exactly which texts.
- **C1 — "Restore = Reconnect request"**: the "Put service back on" step is a RECONNECT REQUEST (it currently refuses Confirm with "This step is not built yet", DEF-CUS-10657).
- **D1 A** — a failed message retried to a corrected address shows "Retried to a new address" and leaves "Needing attention".

## 2026-10-29 — C1 "Restore = Reconnect request": what it maps to in the model (lane judgment, recorded before building; DEF-CUS-10657)

**The ruling, verbatim:** *"C1 -Restore = Reconnect request"* (entry above). Judgment recorded here under law 13 — the model offers ONE reading, so nothing goes back to the PO.

**What already existed (measured 2026-10-29):** a disconnect case moves `cut → reconnecting → restored`. `disconnects.mark_reconnecting` is the explicit staff act that moves `cut → reconnecting`, records what was still owed (`owed_at_reconnection`, who and when on its `audit_log` row) and raises the reconnect field job through `services._raise_flow_work` (CR-070 wave P, `BR-WRK-055` — the state never waits for the job). `disconnects.restore_service` is the act that moves `reconnecting → restored`, puts the account status back and queues *Service restored* (DEF-NOT-10649). Nothing in Work calls back into customers when a reconnect job closes, and `BR-PAY-036` (signed) says restoration *"stays an explicit, audited staff action"*. The S148 screen *Put service back on* serves BOTH steps (`reconnection_readiness.step`), and its Confirm refused on both with *"This step is not built yet"*.

**The reading built:**
1. **Confirm on *Put service back on* for a CUT case = the reconnect request.** It calls `mark_reconnecting` (case → `reconnecting`, never refused for an unpaid balance — `BR-CUS-1097`) and raises one reconnect work order for every row the clerk left on *Work order* that has no job yet, using the utility's own reconnect template for that service (the row raise's resolver, `reconnect_read._reconnect_template_for`). Rows on *Remote* or *No visit* raise nothing. Service is NOT restored by this act and no *Service restored* message is sent.
2. **The request's status shows on the case**: the state reads *reconnecting*, and the case record carries the reconnect job(s) with `raised · done · accepted` and each `WO-` number, beside the cut visit.
3. **Completing the request = Confirm on the same screen once the case is *reconnecting*** (the record's *Restore service* door opens it). That calls `restore_service`: case → `restored`, account status back, *Service restored* queued exactly once. **Closing the field job does NOT restore by itself** — `BR-PAY-036` makes restoration an explicit staff act, so the job's state is SHOWN to the clerk (done / accepted) and never gates or triggers the restoration.
4. **The record, `BR-CUS-1097`:** what was owed, who and when are written at the request (as before) AND at the restoration (`owed_at_restoration` added to `restore_service`'s audit row, because the rule says *"at the moment service was restored"* and the two moments are now days apart). *What had been paid* stays the named absence `paid_against_arrears_not_read` (`DEF-PAY-6074`).

**Worked example:** Brett Calloway's water was cut on 20 Sep; he owes **$1,204.50** including the **$75.00** fee, pays **$400.00** and agrees a plan. The clerk opens *Put service back on*, sees **$804.50 still owed. You may continue.**, leaves Water on *Work order* and confirms on 26 Sep → the case reads *reconnecting*, **WO-** reconnect job raised for Water, audit row records **$804.50 owed**, the clerk and 26 Sep; no message yet. On 27 Sep the crew closes the job; the case shows *1 raised · 1 done*. The clerk opens *Restore service* and confirms → case `restored`, account back to *Active*, audit row records **$804.50 owed at restoration**, the clerk and 27 Sep, and one *Service restored* email (and text if he opted in) is queued.

**Why not the other reading (field close restores automatically):** it needs Work to call into customers on close, which `BR-PAY-036` forbids in substance (restoration is a staff act), and it would let a crew's tap put an account back into billing with no clerk having looked at the money. Reversible: if the PO later wants auto-restore on an accepted close, it is one seam call from Work's close path.
