## 2026-10-29 — Building B1, B3, B4, B5, D1, D2 of the twelve-question message: what was built and the judgments where the rulings ran out (lane) — `DEF-WRK-10663` · `DEF-PAY-10664` · `DEF-NOT-10665` · `DEF-CUS-10653`

**Built** against the entry *"Templates, notifications and communication: twelve questions ruled in one message"* above. The templates redesign (A1–A4) and C1 were not touched by this lane.

**B1 A — visit messages by email whenever an address is on file (`DEF-WRK-10663`).** `notifications.work_customer_messages` now reads the BILL's channel election, `customers.selectors.delivery_channel_election_for_account` — email when the primary contact has an email (or the customer chose paperless), SMS only with `accounts.sms_reminders` — instead of `channel_preference_for_account` (the paperless tick). Worked, as a test: Elena Rivera, `elena.rivera@example.com` on file, paperless OFF, texts OFF → assigning her job queues ONE `service_appointment` email to that address and no text; with no email on file and no text consent → nothing, `visit_message_no_channel_elected`. **Scope checked, not assumed:** `_elected` has exactly one caller (`queue_visit_message`), which serves only the five visit events (`work_order_logged`, `appointment_window`, `visit_moved`, `technician_on_the_way`, `completion_receipt`). The other readers of the customer's own preference — the portal's *Paperless* switch (`portal/seams/customers_seam.delivery_election`) and the portal account card (`portal/selectors.py`) — still read `channel_preference_for_account` and do not move; bills already read the bill election; the back-office Work notices (`work_escalations`) and the technician push read neither. **Judgment:** *"as bills do"* includes a paperless customer with NO email on file getting an email row that says *no address* — the bill's own behaviour since `DEF-BIL-10535`, and what the visit message already did for a paperless customer before today.

**B3 A — ratified (`DEF-PAY-10651`).** `BR-NOT-024` stamped *AMENDED 2026-10-29* in `04-docs/05-modules/10-notifications/02-business-rules.md` (the reminder rides `reminder`, which has no print floor; `notice` keeps it); a SIGN-OFF row appended to the review ledger for exactly this statement, not a rewrite of the row above it. The decision log's B3 line calls it *judgment 1*; in the `DEF-PAY-10651` entry it is the SECOND numbered judgment — the content is the same.

**B4 A — rule off skips the reminder and the ladder carries on (`DEF-PAY-10664`).** Three judgments, each stated so it can be overruled cheaply:
1. **The account moves to rung 1 with NO last-notice date.** `_advance(noticed=False)` writes the tier and `tier_sent_on` but leaves `last_notice_on`, because the collections screen prints that date as when the customer was last written to and nobody was. The 10-day notice's day is unaffected either way — `rung_due_on` counts from the bill's due date (due + 13), never from the reminder. Worked, as a test: bill due 1 Oct, rule off; 4 Oct → *Not sent · rule off*, tier `friendly`; 13 Oct → still `friendly`; 14 Oct → `first_10_day`.
2. **`rule_off` covers the two cases the reminder already records as `rule_off`:** the event switched off, and the letter's Print switch off for a customer nothing digital reaches (`past_due_reminder.plan` writes `rule_off` for both — both are the utility's deliberate switch). Every other reason (`no_contact`, `template_missing`, `queue_problem`, medical hold) still does not advance, so the honest-history rule of `DEF-PAY-10651` stands.
3. **Only the nightly ladder carries on.** A clerk's own *Send reminder* on S35 (`ladder.step_one`) with the rule off still answers *not sent · rule off* and moves nothing — a person who pressed *send* is told it did not go, rather than finding the account a rung further on.

**B5 A — the review list** is `12-governance/translation-review-2026-10-29.md`: per language, the five texts written today in that language (service disconnected / restored, email + SMS; the printed `dunning` letter) and the SIX texts that exist in English only (work order logged email + SMS; the booked email, moved email and booked SMS that gained a *Before we arrive* paragraph; the default preparation sentence). **The six are a finding, not a review item:** no translation exists, so under today's preferred-language ruling those customers get English.

**D1 A — retried to a new address leaves *Needing attention* (`DEF-NOT-10665`).** **Judgment — how a row knows it was retried:** a LATER copy of the same message (same source, same channel, higher `copy_no`) whose address differs from this row's. It is read from the queue, NEVER from the `delivery.retried_to_new_address` audit row, because `audit_log` is pruned on a retention schedule (hard rule 4, `OQ-1340`) and the message would come back into *Needing attention* the day its audit row went. A later copy to the SAME address (a resend that fixed nothing) does not count. One definition, `attention.needing_attention`, serves the filter and the count; every listed row carries `retried_to_new_address`, and the status cell reads *Retried to a new address* under *All messages*. *Fix address and retry* stays offered on such a row — a second correction is still a correction.

**D2 A — every message type named (`DEF-CUS-10653`).** `catalogs.LISTINGS` holds **87** classes at runtime (68 in the literal block, 19 more added by `LISTINGS.update` — the agreement pair and seventeen *What changed* reasons); **83** had no `notifications.templateClass.<code>` key. All 83 are written in eleven catalogues: English is the listing's own name in US spelling (*installment*), the seventeen reasons reuse each catalogue's own Fix-a-bill reason wording after *What changed ·*, and the rest are lane-authored in each language. `tests/test_def_cus_10653_template_class_names.py` reads `LISTINGS` and every catalogue, so a class added without a name goes red, naming it (law 2).

## 2026-10-29 — Templates: customer-category variants, New variant, Make live again — five judgments where the rulings ran out (`CR-199-BRC10` S1–S3, lane TPL-SRV-VAR)

Recorded before the build was reported (step W). Built under A1 C, A3 A, A4 B and B of the same day; none of these needs the PO, and each is cheap to overrule.

1. **"Customer category" is the utility's own customer classes, not programmes.** The axis already existed on the rows (`notification_templates.category`, `default` = All customers) but was validated against a hardcoded four. It now accepts `default` plus the utility's ACTIVE `account_types` codes (tenant-owned since 2026-09-17). The drawing's *Low-income* option is a drawn value (B14 rule 37): a discount programme cannot key a variant, because an account holds several enrolments at once and nothing orders them, so "the most specific variant" would have no answer. Every existing row was already `default`, so "existing rows become All customers" needed no data migration.
2. **At queue time the account's class is read once** when a writer names only the account (every writer today). Worked: a commercial account's past-due reminder now pins the published *Commercial* wording; an account with no class, or no Commercial wording, pins All customers exactly as before.
3. **The customer's language beats a closer category match** — the fallback ladder's steps 3 and 4 swapped. Worked: Rosa, residential, Español; Springfield has *Residential · English* and *All customers · Español* published → she now gets the Spanish one (the old order sent her the residential English one, which contradicts ruling B's *"English wherever no Spanish version is published"*).
4. **"The utility's switched-on languages" (A4 B) is derived, because no switch exists.** Measured: tenancy holds ONE Regional language and a platform list of twelve. Switched on = the utility's own language + every language it has ITSELF written a template version in (the platform seeds several classes in all twelve languages, so counting seeded rows would switch everything on for everyone) + every language one of its customers has chosen as preferred. Worked: an English-language utility where some accounts prefer Español → *New variant* offers English and Español, and refuses Japanese by name. If the PO wants an explicit Settings switch instead, `template_variants.offered_languages` is the one function that changes.
5. **Make live again writes a NEW version, it never moves the live pointer back.** v1 → v2 → v3 live; *Make v1 live again* writes **v4 holding v1's stored wording**, publishes it, and archives v3 (an earlier version counts as published when it went out — including the platform's seeded v1, which carries no author and, measured, sometimes no publish time) — v1 keeps its own first publish date, v3 "stays in history", messages already pinned to v1 or v3 render what they rendered (BR-BIL-026), new messages pin v4. The row records `restored_from_version = 1` (migration `notifications/0036`, write-once) rather than only `audit_log`, which is pruned (`OQ-1340`). **Legal notices** — A1 C — are read from the existing flag, the catalog making the regulator reference `{state_puc_ref}` mandatory (the disconnection notice and its three tiers): for those the copy stays a DRAFT for a System Admin to publish, and the live version keeps going out. Contract classes are refused (a contract version is published for a date); their path is the existing *Restore* to a dated draft.

**D2, one more judgment the walk forced (same lane, same day).** On the walk database the *Already sent* list of `AC-2026-00001` still read *"A message"* on four rows after every class had its name — the printed and portal copies of the account's BILLS, which carry NO template class (`template_code` is NULL: a bill is laid out by the bill template, not a message class). Such a row is now named by its source kind through the queue screen's own vocabulary (`notifications.queue.source.invoice` → *Bill*), and *"A message"* stays only for a class the catalogue genuinely does not know. Proved by `07-frontend/src/features/customers/communicationHistoryNames.dom.test.tsx` (RED before: `expected 'A message' to be 'Bill'`).

## 2026-10-29 — Rich email wording is stored as a closed text markup; every customer email goes out in the utility's frame (lane TPL-SRV-EMAIL judgments, `CR-199-BRC10` S4–S7)

Judgments made where rulings 1A, 2A and A2 A ran out — recorded under law 13, nothing goes back to the PO. Rule: `BR-NOT-1042`.

1. **Storage form: a closed text markup, not HTML and not a JSON tree.** `**bold**` · `[label](target)` · `[[label|target]]` (button) · `- item` · blank-line paragraphs — the mock-up's own syntax, which the editor's four buttons write. Anything else is text and is escaped. A target is `https://…` or one link placeholder. **Why:** a parser that knows five shapes cannot be talked into a sixth; a sanitiser over stored HTML is an allow-list that must be right about every tag a browser knows. It also leaves the plain-text part of every existing email byte-identical (proved by test).
2. **The format belongs to the VERSION**, `plain` | `rich`, default `plain` (every existing version), frozen once published by a second trigger beside `0006`'s (`notifications/0037`) — a rich body re-read as plain prints its markup.
3. **Plain format still reads the markup** (image 04): the plain-text part turns `[[Pay now|{pay_link}]]` into `Pay now: https://…`; only the HTML formatting is dropped.
4. **Values are substituted inside the parsed markup, never before parsing** — so a customer value can never become a link or a tag. Raw HTML is refused at save and removed at render.
5. **The preview no longer refuses an unknown placeholder** (image 17): it renders `{bogus}` as typed and lists the same error the save refuses with. The save still refuses.
6. **Link placeholders:** a token is a link if its name ends `_link` (no hand-kept list). `{pay_link}` and `{portal_link}` are supplied by the renderer from `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN` and offered on every email class addressed to an account holder (those carrying `{account_no}`); `{bill_link}` stays billing's per-bill credential. A typed address must be `https://`; a resolved one may be `http` only because a developer's `PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN` is.
7. **The frame carries no words of ours.** Band = utility name (+ logo); footer = name · mailing address. The drawing's *"You receive this because… Email preferences"* is not built: no preferences page exists, and an English sentence would be wrong on a Spanish email.
8. **The logo image comes from the API's public host** (`PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` + `/api/<utility>/settings/company/logo/file?v=<ref>`, the one public logo address). Unset → the band shows the name alone.

**Worked figure:** Pat Rivera, AC-004211, rich "Bill ready" → a **Pay now** button to `https://<app>/brazosbend/portal/pay`; plain-text part `Pay now: https://<app>/brazosbend/portal/pay`; header band Brazos Bend blue `#1B5E9E`, white type, linked to `https://brazosbendutilities.com`.

**Addendum to *"Templates redesign, screens lane"* above (judgments 6–8, made while building, CR-199-BRC10):**

6. **The wording is on the LEFT and the document keeps three fifths.** The drawing (`02`) puts *Wording* first and *Preview* second — arrangement, so the drawing's. The width split is not a drawn ruling (B14 rule 37), while CR-076 item 2's *"60 is for A big paper showing real document"* is the PO's own — so the frame is `2fr` wording, `3fr` document (`notificationsKit.DESIGNER_FRAME`).
7. **The 2026-09-08 consequence sentence stays, under the Channel picker.** *"Each is edited and published separately…"* was ruled (*"yes please"*) beside the old surface switcher; the Channel picker IS that switcher, so the sentence is the picker's help line, drawn only when the notice has another channel.
8. **The send-test dialog (`12`) confirms; it does not take an address yet.** `POST …/queue-test` sends to the signed-in user, and the drawn editable address has no server field behind it. The dialog says where the test goes in the server's own sentence; a typed address is the server's to add.

**Addendum (judgment 9, CR-199-BRC10 screens lane, made while wiring lane B's endpoints):** a legal notice's *Send for approval* (`13`, PO ruling A1 C) SAVES the wording as a draft and publishes nothing; the live version keeps going out until a System Admin publishes that draft from History, and that publish IS the approval. The server serves no separate approval queue (`CR-199-BRC10` §5 names `needs_approval` and `make-live-again`'s `sent_for_approval` outcome, both of which also stop at a draft), so the bar follows the same rule. **Worked:** the 10-day disconnect notice, v2 live — the clerk edits and presses *Send for approval* → v3 is saved as a draft, customers still get v2; a System Admin opens History and publishes v3.

## 2026-10-29 — Messages follow the customer's language: BUILT, with four judgments of ours (`CR-199-BRC10` lane TPL-SRV-LANG)

Builds the PO's option B above (*"Question: which language should messages be sent in? - B"*). **One place decides:** `apps/notifications/message_language.language_for`, run by `queue_document` for every pin it resolves. Writers keep passing the utility's default as `language=`, which now means *the fallback*; `queue_document` reads the account's `preferred_language` itself from `account_id`, so every writer that names an account (bills, receipts, notices, past-due reminders, connection letters, transfers, work visits, the Communication dialog, plan-change letters) obeys without being edited. A pin is never re-asked, so a reprint renders its pinned language. Worked, and asserted: Rosa (Español, English-default utility) → Spanish *Bill ready* where published; English past-due reminder where not.

**Judgments, recorded rather than asked (law 13):**
1. **An applicant with no account yet uses the language on the request.** The ruling names the customer's preferred language; before an account exists, the request's `preferred_language` is that customer's stated choice. So the move-in acknowledgement, approval, refusal, more-info and extra messages pass it as `preferred_language=`.
2. **`es-MX` finds `es` wording** — the 2026-10-02 New Connection judgment, now applied to every message.
3. **The fallback is the utility's own language variant first, then `default`** — a Spanish-default utility's English-preferring customer, with no English published, gets the utility's Spanish, not the bare `default` row. "The utility's default variant" read as the variant in the utility's language.
4. **The per-language customer count** (`GET /template-languages`) counts accounts (not customers), files no-preference accounts under the utility's default, keeps codes exact (`es-MX` ≠ `es`), and lists exactly the switched-on languages lane TPL-SRV-VAR derived for *New variant* (`template_variants.offered_languages`), so a count and a variant join on one `value`.

Also on the screen: the move-in / new-account field and the move detail fact read *Preferred language* (were *Portal language*), and the portal application form's label likewise, in all eleven catalogues.

## 2026-10-29 — Templates list: what the chips, the Languages column and the Status filter count — five judgments (lane TPL-SRV-FACETS, `CR-199-BRC10`, `DEF-NOT-10672`)

Our judgments where the drawing (`01-list.png`) and the rulings ran out; none put to the PO (law 13). Served by `apps/notifications/template_list.py`; tests `06-backend/tests/test_cr199_template_list_facets.py`.

1. **A row's status is ONE of three, exactly as its pill reads:** *Draft waiting* (a saved draft exists) beats *Published* (a live undated version) beats *Not published*. So the three Status counts add up to the list, and a row under the *Published* filter never shows the *Draft waiting* pill. *Needs approval* (a legal notice, A1 C) is a separate fact and a fourth option. Worked figure on the seeded utility: a Spanish draft started on one published class moves that row from *Published* to *Draft waiting*; *Published* drops by one, *Draft waiting* rises by one, the total stays 87.
2. **A language is *written* for a template when some variant in that language holds a draft or a published version** — wording that goes out or is about to. Archived-only wording is *not written*: nothing of it goes out. The languages are the switched-on set from `template_variants.offered_languages` (A4 B), never a second list.
3. **The Language filter returns the templates written in that language**, and its count is that number. A language the utility has not switched on falls back to the whole list (BR-SHL-011), never an empty one.
4. **The server serves a language as its BCP-47 tag only, and the screen names it** (`languageName`, as the workspace already does). The server keeps no table of language names and a language's own name is not a catalogue line (B14 rule 35), so a served `label` could only have been the tag again; the screen's `label` reads were changed in the same commit, with a test.
5. **The rows stay filtered in Python, argued on this list's own facts:** a row is a template CLASS, platform vocabulary (87 on this date), identical on every tenant — T7 and T5 list the same 87 rows, so the row count never grows with accounts. What grows with the tenant (its variants and versions) is now read in three grouped statements for the whole list instead of three per row: **257 statements for one page before, 11 after** (measured on the seeded utility; a test holds it under 40). Server pagination (NFR-3) is unchanged; every facet counts over the whole filtered catalogue, never a page.

## 2026-10-29 — Address search, lane B (portal): what was built and ten judgments where the rulings ran out (`CR-200-BRC10` S7–S9, F1–F5; `DEF-CWP-10680/10681/10682`)

Built from PO 1A, 2A and *Ask us* A (entries above). Recorded rather than asked (law 13):

1. **The suggestion carries the STATE too** — street, town, state, ZIP. The ruled example prints it (*"2155 Hemlock Dr, Ann Arbor, MI 48108"*); it says nothing about who lives there. No id, no premise number, no name, no unit, no occupancy (`BR-CWP-021`, B14 rule 31) — asserted on the body's KEYS.

## 2026-10-29 — Address search, lane A (staff): how a multi-word term is RANKED in the top search bar, and which fields each of the five searches now matches (team judgment, `CR-200-BRC10` S1–S6)

**The rule built (PO 3A, unchanged):** the typed term is split on spaces and commas; EVERY word must match at least one of the search's fields (`icontains`); one word behaves exactly as before. One shared matcher, `core.search.matches_every_word`, used by all five staff searches; each module keeps its own field list. Still one SQL statement, still paged in SQL, no cap.

**Judgment 1 — ranking in the top search bar ranks on the FIRST word.** `prefix_then_recency` puts a row first when its identifier (premises number / unit number) STARTS WITH the term. With the whole phrase, "P-0012 Oak" could never start any identifier, so the band would go dead for every multi-word search. A clerk who leads with a number leads with it as the first word, so the first word decides the band; for one word that is the whole term, so single-word ranking is unchanged. The kernel's `prefix_then_recency` is not changed (eight other modules use it); metering passes the first word.

**Judgment 2 — the field lists.** Worked example: "12 Oak 2B" (a street word, a street word, a unit label) now finds Apt 2B at 12 Oak St in all three unit searches, and 12 Oak St itself in all three premises searches; a decoy Apt 2B at 40 Elm St, Katy is not found.
- Premises searches (list, picker, top bar) share: street, town, ZIP, premises number, premises name, **and the label or number of a unit inside it** (PO 3A: *"each typed word may match the address or the unit label, on Units and Premises lists"*). The Premises LIST keeps its three extra fields (owner, the utility's own reference, the City's parcel id); the picker still does not match the owner (its own docstring's reason stands).
- Unit searches (Units list, Move-in picker, top bar) share: unit label and number, plus the building's street, town, ZIP, premises number and name — walked to `premises` (hard rule 8; no address on a unit). The Units list keeps its meter-number leg and Move-in keeps its account/customer/meter legs, both still matched on the WHOLE phrase as an alternative (they are identifiers, not words of an address).
- ZIP (`postal_code`) is new everywhere; nothing any search matched before was dropped.
- `metering.selectors.unit_ids_matching` (used by the assets and customers searches, not by any of the five) is deliberately NOT changed here.

## 2026-10-30 — Lockbox audit LBX-03: NO "returned items" import; how a lockbox payment lives (PO)

Context: a tester's lockbox audit (LBX-01…11, analysed against the code 2026-10-30). LBX-03 proposed a new *Returned items* import that reverses payments from the bank's returned-items report.

**PO, verbatim:** *"do not buld in payments capablity ; consumers will send casj, check , money order to the lockbox; lockbox third party provider or utiltiy themself enters all payments in the system , they will open counter/ till to make the enteries ; the Actual money and check is deposited in banks ; bank statment will tell wheter money cleared or NSF or boumce the cjeck if its settled ; if NSF payment will revers along with NSF penalty"*.

**So:** (1) **LBX-03 is NOT built** — no returned-items import, no import that reverses payments. (2) The flow the product serves, in the PO's words: customers send cash, cheques and money orders to the lockbox → the lockbox provider OR the utility enters every payment, at an open counter/till → the money and cheques are deposited at the bank → the **bank statement** says whether each cleared, or bounced (NSF) → **an NSF payment is reversed together with the NSF penalty**. The next question put to the PO is a table of how the system handles each step today.

## 2026-10-30 — Lockbox audit: what is fixed, what is not, and three answers (PO)

**PO, verbatim:** *"LBX-05 Returned and fee lines only counted- we will fix this;LBX-06 -we will fix; fix LBX-07;LBX-08 need fix ; LBX-09 ;LBX-10 ; LBX-11 Do not implement"*, then *"Q1. May a bank-statement line that isn't a deposit post to the books?-A · Q2. Will any utility you're onboarding send lockbox files only in a bank format (BAI or EDI 823) rather than CSV?-A · Q3. Should we keep the bank's original file so staff can download it?-Use the bank file for reconcilation to create the records we do not need to save the bank file in the system"*.
- **To fix:** LBX-05 (returned-item and fee statement lines become actionable), LBX-06 (imported lockbox payments get a payment method), LBX-07, LBX-08 (in-file duplicate cheque flagged and held; de-duplicate on account + cheque, never cheque alone; finish removing the old pipeline per `OQ-PAY-12579`), LBX-09 (statement lines dated after the import, or outside the statement period, refused by name), LBX-10 (singular/plural in the Reverse dialogs).
- **Not to build:** LBX-11 (incoming-files screen) and LBX-03 (returned-items import, entry above).
- **Q1 = A — batch decision "G3" is RULED: a bank-statement line that is not a deposit MAY post.** Matching a returned line to its payment's reversal moves the reversed amount from the holding account to cash; explaining a bank-fee line posts it to Bank fees (6800) against cash. Worked (tester's data): RET1029-01 −$76.40 and RET1029-02 −$154.00 matched → $230.40 holding → cash; FEE1031 −$24.00 → Bank fees; the period ties: books cash = bank $616.10, holding $0.00. Balanced pairs through the ledger posting service only (hard rule 5).
- **Q2 = A — lockbox files are CSV only for now;** the connection offers CSV alone (the five other formats removed until a reader exists; a named customer's need re-opens it). Folds `DEF-INT-4240`.
- **Q3 — the bank's original file is NOT stored.** It is read to create the records (payments / statement lines) and only its fingerprint is kept for duplicate detection, as today. No download, no retention change.
- **Not answered in this message, still open:** LBX-01 ($0.00 batch cannot be reconciled), LBX-02 (stale error in the difference dialog), LBX-04 (the bank's own words on a reversal), the customer's NSF penalty on a bounce (today never added — `nsf_fee_not_added`), and whether a bounce is reversed from the statement line.

## 2026-10-30 — The NSF penalty is charged on a bounce, priced Account › Unit › Plan › Charge code, never hard-coded (PO)

Put to the PO as an eleven-step table of the lockbox flow as the system handles it today; PO, verbatim: *"your understanding is correct"*, and on step 9 (*"The NSF penalty is charged to the customer — Not added … `nsf_fee_not_added`"*): *"Do not hardcode check NSF Account> Unit> Plan> Charge code"*. With the PO's flow of the same day (*"if NSF payment will revers along with NSF penalty"*).
**So:** reversing a payment for reason *Returned by the bank* (`nsf`) also charges the customer the NSF penalty, its amount resolved by walking **the account → its unit → that unit's plan → the plan's NSF charge code** (`rating.selectors.charge_by_code`; BR-BIL-019 forbids a hand-typed amount, BR-BIL-007 puts the line write in billing). Worked: cheque 4102 $76.40 bounces on AC-2026-00003, whose unit's plan carries NSF $30.00 → balance $76.40 + $30.00 = **$106.40**; the Reverse dialog shows "+$30.00 NSF fee" before Confirm. **Coordinator judgment (law 13, recorded rather than asked):** the fee is added automatically with the reversal and shown before Confirm; no waive tick is built (the PO's flow says the payment reverses *along with* the penalty — a waiver is a later ask if wanted). When the plan carries no NSF charge code, the reversal still goes through and the screen says no NSF fee is set on that plan (named, never a guessed $0.00). Supersedes the `nsf_fee_not_added` gap.

**PO, verbatim:** *"Q1. When a cheque bounces, should the NSF penalty be added to the customer's account automatically?- A ; Q2. Where should a bounced cheque be reversed from?-A or user can do manually from payments and account these three are correct ;Q3 (from before): may the bank's own fee on the statement post to the books?-A"*.
1. **Q1 = A — SUPERSEDES the coordinator's "no waive tick" judgment in the entry above.** The NSF penalty is added automatically with an `nsf` reversal, shown as "+$30.00 NSF fee" before Confirm, and the clerk may UNTICK it **with a reason** (e.g. the bank's own error), audit-logged. Worked: 4102 $76.40 → $106.40 with the fee; unticked "bank error" → $76.40 and the reason on the history.
2. **Q2 — three places, all correct:** (a) from the **bank statement line** ("RET1029-01 −$76.40" → *Match to payment* finds cheque 4102 by amount + cheque number → Reverse with the NSF fee, in one step; the line then counts as explained and posts holding → cash per G3); (b) manually from **Payments › Payments list**; (c) manually from **Accounts › (account) › Payments**. A bounce reversed by hand in (b)/(c) is later matched to its statement line, never reversed twice.
3. **Q3 = A** (repeats the earlier answer): explaining a statement's bank-fee line posts it to Bank fees.

## 2026-10-30 — NSF penalty and Bank memo BUILT: how the plan's NSF code is found, and five lane judgments (lane NSF-FEE, `DEF-PAY-10698`, `DEF-PAY-10699`)

Builds the three rulings above (*"The NSF penalty is charged on a bounce…"*, *"NSF penalty can be unticked with a reason…"*, *"LBX-04 … Bank memo"*). **Worked, asserted in `06-backend/tests/test_def_pay_10698_nsf_fee.py`:** cheque 4102 $76.40 bounces on an account whose unit's plan lists NSF $30.00 → one $30.00 fee bill, issued → the account owes **$106.40**; replayed → still one fee; plan without an NSF code → reversal recorded, result names `nsf_fee_not_set_on_plan`, owes **$76.40**; reason *data entry error* → no fee; unticked with *"bank error"* → owes **$76.40**, reason on the audit row and the payment's history; PY-…-0098 (cheque 4102) Bank memo *"NSF"* and 4103 *"ACCOUNT CLOSED"* in one bulk run → each on its own REVERSING row and shown as *"Bank memo: NSF"*.
**Judgments where the rulings ran out (law 13 — recorded, not asked):**
1. **Which of a plan's codes IS its NSF fee: a DECLARED flag on the charge code, `charges.is_nsf_fee` (`rating/0068`), read through the plan's Charges list** — never the code string (the reason `is_base` gives: a utility may call it `RET-CHK`). The seeded `NSF` (`lookup_defaults.json` V2.48.0.15, `seed_demo`) declares it, and `rating/0068` marks the `NSF` penalty row every existing tenant already holds, once, per tenant under RLS — `rating/0027`'s precedent for `LATE`. A plan listing two marked codes charges none and says so (`nsf_fee_ambiguous_on_plan`), never by order. `plan_charge_rules.amount_override` is NOT read: *"no plan cannot override prices"* (PO 2026-08-19). **Settings has no tick for the flag yet** → `DEF-RAT-10739`.
2. **The fee is an ISSUED fee bill, due the day the item came back (`due_days=0`)** — raised through the reconnection fee's own door (`fee_bill.raise_and_issue_charge_fee`, DEF-708), so issue stamps the code's GL and the ledger posts it (rule 5); a new invoice, nothing edited (rule 4). Inside the reversal's transaction, in a SAVEPOINT (law 14): any refusal is a named outcome and the reversal stands.
3. **A second bounce on the same account on the same day charges no second fee** (`nsf_fee_not_raised`): the fee bill is keyed account + kind + day (`one_time_run_key`, signed 🔒). Changing that key is not a lane's edit → `DEF-PAY-10740`.
4. **The Bank memo lives in the reversing row's existing `memo` column** (no migration): it is the only free text a reversal carries, the original is never edited, and the single Reverse dialog's *Memo* box is relabelled *Bank memo* (≤ 60, refused over). `payment_row` serves `bank_memo` on reversing rows only, so a payment's own memo is never relabelled as the bank's.
5. **In bulk, the untick and its reason apply to the whole run; the fee and the Bank memo are per payment.** One reason a clerk types for a run of cheques the bank returned together; each payment's fee is its own plan's.
**One service for every door** (Payments list, an account's Payments tab, and lane LBX-B's statement line): `apps.payments.reversal.reverse_payment(actor, *, payment_id, returned_on, reason="nsf", …, charge_nsf_fee=True, nsf_fee_waive_reason=None, bank_memo=None, idempotency_reference=…)`. Preview: `GET /payments/{id}/nsf-fee?on=`.
## 2026-10-30 — Lane PAY-F: held credit shown from the books; a late fee a payment cancelled stops release (judgment calls, L2-01 / L2-06 / L3-07)

Recorded before reporting (step W). No new rule — each implements the 2026-10-30 *"Payments audit by level"* ruling.

- **L2-01 (DEF-PAY-10707) — the header balance is the ledger's 1200 + 2400 for the account, not `payments/account_balance.py`.** The brief said reuse the kiosk/portal balance (open bills − held credit). It was NOT reused for the account screen, for two reasons found in the code: (1) the header, the S17 row and the finance KPI are one LEDGER derivation by DEF-127's rule, and `account_balance` reads open BILLS, which do not include a migrated opening balance posted to 1200 — switching would show $0.00 over real arrears; (2) `credit.apply_credit_at_issue` posts nothing, so after a carried credit is drawn down the 2400 line still holds it — 1200 − subledger credit would then overstate by that credit, while 1200 + 2400 stays right in both states. Worked: Farid pays **$170.00** on **$165.00** → 1200 **0.00**, 2400 **−5.00** → header **−$5.00**; Kevin's second **$259.23** → **−$259.23**; a **$150.00** deposit credits 2000 deposit liability and moves nothing. In the normal case the two derivations agree (the kiosk also reads −$5.00). The receivable reads (`outstanding`, statements, disconnect worklists, AR tie-out) keep 1200 only. The Credits tab lists held credit from `GET /accounts/{id}/credit-sources` (deposits already excluded) with **Refund** (the existing raise form, account and amount filled in, still two-person approval) and **Apply now** (the existing reapply with `release: []`, so only the held part moves; posts nothing, as reapply always has).
- **L2-06 (DEF-BIL-10708) — release REFUSES rather than re-prices.** The gate is where a person signs for the figures; changing them inside the signature would sign for numbers nobody was shown. A draft carrying a late fee (a `fee` line on the late-fee code the account's plan names; any charged fee line where the run saved no plan — fails closed) whose account has a payment changed after the draft was worked out is refused: *"re-check N account(s)"*. Re-working those bills (`reprice_accounts` or *Work out the bills* again) clears it. Worked: Xander's **$226.00** due 10 Jun unpaid at drafting → **$5.00** fee; his payment of 9 Jun loaded after drafting → release refused naming **1** account; after re-working, **$0.00** fee. A payment that arrived AFTER grace keeps the **$5.00** (BR-BIL-071 cuts both ways). Only late-fee drafts are affected — usage, base and tax are not payment facts. The 60-second sweep (`billing.check.sweep`, installed by `BillingConfig.ready`) is configured: it rides `celery-beat` and the default `celery` worker in `docker-compose.yml`. It refreshes the Check's findings only; it never re-works a draft, which is why the gate is needed.
- **L3-07 (DEF-BIL-10709) — the late-fee list sweeps once per opening.** The pane's first read sweeps; later pages and the debounced search send `sweep=0` (absent = sweep, so every other caller is unchanged). The count is never the cached tag count over rows that have not arrived; loading and failed states are drawn. *Find account* matches the account number or the customer's name, through customers' published search.

Builds the audit's L3-02, L1-07, L2-04 and Q3 = A, and checks L2-12 and the PO's outage sentence (Q4). **Judgments where the rulings ran out (law 13 — recorded, not put back):**

The five-try limit is unchanged. **Not changed, filed for the next lane:** `customers/agreement_public_api._client_ip` reads the first header value the same way to record who accepted an agreement (`DEF-CUS-10745`).

Every miss still answers the one sentence "We cannot find that bill." A case-insensitive search was not used so the bill-number index still serves the lookup.
3. **L2-04 — the returned-payment email is rewritten and the printed letter gets words** (`DEF-PAY-10744`). Both are seeded defaults a utility edits (the OQ-244 posture), in eleven languages (ten lane-written, listed in `translation-review-2026-10-29.md` for the native-speaker review, PO B5 A). They name the amount, the date it was paid, the cheque or reference, the Bank memo, the NSF fee, the new balance and the due date. Worked: Ben Zabala's $63.00 returned with Bank memo "NSF" and the plan's $30.00 fee → *"Your payment of $63.00 … was returned by your bank … Bank memo NSF … Returned payment fee $30.00 … Your balance is now $93.00."* **(a) No fee → no fee line**, never "$0.00": the fee, the memo, the reference and the due date are each an optional paragraph that is left out when there is nothing to say (no fee on the plan, or the clerk unticked it with a reason). **(b) The due date is the earliest due date among the account's open bills after the bounce** (the re-opened bill and the fee bill, which is due on the day it is raised). **(c)** A utility whose email is still the old seed gets the new wording by migration `notifications/0038`; an edited copy is left alone. This also answers **OQ-260 (b)** — the NSF fee now has a token, `{nsf_fee}`, filled from the fee the reversal charged.
4. **Q3 = A — Print receipt** (`DEF-PAY-10743`). A button on the recorded-payment panel and on the payment page opens the receipt in a window of its own and prints it — one page by construction, nothing of the app around it. It shows the utility's name and mark, the PY- number, date, account, who paid, amount, method (and cheque/reference), the bills paid, the balance remaining (from the books, now), and the clerk and counter when it was taken at one. Worked: Rosa pays $68.00 cash on a $100.00 bill at Dana's counter → the receipt reads $68.00, BL-…, balance remaining $32.00, served by Dana, counter CTR-…. It is a read: nothing is queued or sent.
5. **L2-12 and Q4 — what was checked, measured in `tests/test_pay_g_receipts_go_out.py`.** Every payment door (counter, kiosk, store file, online) ends in the one service that queues the receipt: a printed copy, an email and a text. **For a receipt to go out a utility needs:** *Receipt on record-payment* on (it ships on) · *Payment received* on, per channel, in Settings › Notifications (email and text) · the email (and text) channel switched on in the dispatch settings — they ship OFF · a connected email provider (and, for text, the platform Twilio account configured on the server) · the customer's email address (or a phone number with text consent) · and the dispatch schedule running for that utility. **Printed receipts never leave by themselves** — no print vendor is connected; they wait in the outbound table, and Print receipt is how paper reaches a customer at the counter. **The outage, checked against the PO's sentence:** while the provider is DISCONNECTED or the channel is off, a receipt waits with status `queued` and no attempt counted, and goes out on the first run after it is back — exactly as the PO said. **But a provider that is connected and FAILING is tried three times (now, +5 minutes, +20 minutes); after the third failure the receipt rests `failed` and does NOT go out on its own when the provider recovers** — a re-queue sends it. **For the bulk *Send receipts* lane:** read `outbound_messages.status` on the receipt rows (`source_type = 'payment'`, `source_id` = the payment): `queued` = waiting, skip it; `failed` (or no row) = send.

## 2026-10-30 — LBX-05 and LBX-09 built: a returned line and a fee line post; future and out-of-period lines refused (lane LBX-B, `DEF-PAY-10694`, `DEF-PAY-10695`)

**Built on the PO's G3 = A and Q2 of the same day.** Worked on the tester's lockbox day (DEP-261026-0007, six cheques **$870.50**; 4102 **$76.40** and 4103 **$154.00** returned; statement 26–31 Oct: +870.50, −76.40, −154.00, −24.00). **Before:** holding **−$230.40**, books cash **$870.50** against the bank's **$616.10**. **After** matching both returns and posting the fee: holding **$0.00**, books cash **$616.10** = bank, **$24.00** in Bank fees. Asserted in `06-backend/tests/test_lbx05_09_statement_lines_post.py` — on SQLite, and on PostgreSQL 16 under a non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS role (33 passed, 1 skipped across this file, its PostgreSQL companion and the bank-rec suite).
1. **What posts.** *Match to payment*: DR the holding account the cheque's RECEIPT debited (read off the receipt entry, never today's tender mapping) / CR cash, for the line's amount. *Bank fee*: DR Bank fees (by the `bank_fees` designation) / CR cash. One balanced pair each, through the ledger posting service, keyed `bank_line|<id>|<event>`. The order against the batch's reconcile does not matter — matching first leaves holding +870.50 / cash −230.40 until the reconcile, and the same 0.00 / 616.10 after it (asserted).
2. **Lane judgment — an ordinary *Explain* still posts nothing.** The PO's worked case names a returned cheque and a bank fee. A free GL pick posting against cash would let *"customer paid the bank directly"* land in accounts receivable with no payment behind it. So only the two ruled actions post; *Explain* stays *Recorded*, and the statement's *"Recorded, not in the books"* line still shows it. The *"Unmatched bank lines are counted only"* note is retired with its eleven catalogue keys.
3. **Lane judgment — Q2's three places, one reversal.** *Match to payment* lists BANKED payments of the line's amount, posted within 60 days before the line (BR-PAY-011's ACH window), the cheque number in the line's text ranking first. A payment already reversed by hand LINKS to that reversal; one not reversed is reversed in the same step, reason *Returned by the bank*. One line ↔ one reversal is held by the service and by two partial uniques (`payments/0053`). The NSF fee untick-with-a-reason and the *Bank memo* (LBX-04, the line's own text) are passed to lane NSF-FEE's fee-aware `reverse_payment` (`eb36ee5bd`), and the match answers with what happened to the penalty. **Found doing it, filed not fixed (`DEF-PAY-10742`):** a bounce on an account that is not billable — the tester's 4103 is on a CLOSED account — aborts the whole reversal, because the NSF fee quote reads the billable scope outside its own refusal handling.
4. **Lane judgment — one bank fee is posted once (the coordinator's item 5).** A fee typed on a single Reverse already posts DR 6800 / CR cash. When the statement's fee line arrives, *Bank fee* offers that posted fee and LINKS the line to it, posting nothing (a third partial unique stops a second line claiming it). Worked: Reverse 4102 with a $24.00 bank fee, then link FEE1031 → 6800 stays **$24.00**, not $48.00. **The bank-fee field is NOT added to bulk Reverse:** a bulk field would be typed per item while the bank charges one statement line for several items (the tester's single −$24.00), and the statement line is now the one place the bank's own figure is posted from. Recorded rather than asked (law 13); a later ask re-opens it.
5. **LBX-09.** A line dated after the import moment (the caller's `imported_at` — no clock read, G6) or outside the statement period is refused naming the line, its reference and its date; nothing is written. Worked: imported 26 Oct, *"line 2 (RET1029-01, 2026-10-29) is dated after this import"*.
6. **Screens held (PO 2026-10-30, relayed by the coordinator: *"please do not proceed without confirming with me for drawing related chnages"*).** The screen half already pushed in `fb49fb1d0` — *Match to payment* / *Bank fee* in the import review's FIX column, the two forms, *In the books* / *Recorded* on explained rows, and an *In the books* panel on the reconciliation statement — is listed for the PO and NOT extended; showing the NSF fee amount in the Match form waits for that confirmation.

## 2026-10-30 — Lane PAY-J: bulk Send receipts and bulk Reapply BUILT — four judgments (recorded, not asked; `DEF-PAY-10747`)

Builds *"Q4 settled: bulk Send receipts AND bulk Reapply are built"* above. The Payments list's bulk bar now holds Reverse · Refund · **Send receipts (N)** · **Reapply (N)**, each running once per ticked payment through `POST /payments/{id}/bulk-receipt` and `POST /payments/{id}/bulk-reapply` (`apps/payments/bulk_acts.py`), which call the existing single-payment services and nothing else. Per-row result panel; every press audit-logged. **Worked, asserted in `06-backend/tests/test_pay_j_bulk_receipts_reapply.py` and `payJBulkReceiptsReapply.dom.test.tsx`:** 20 ticked after the 29 Oct outage — 5 whose email receipt rested `failed`, 15 still `queued` → **"5 sent · 15 waiting for the email service"**; exactly 5 new email rows (copy 1); pressed again → 20 waiting, nothing written; provider back → all 15 go out. A customer with no email → **"No contact on file"** beside the payment number, nothing queued.
1. **Email only.** The ruling's case and the PO's sentence are about the email provider; a printed receipt has no vendor and a text has its own switch. Widening to text is one more channel in `bulk_acts.CHANNELS`.
2. **What each email row state does.** `queued` with an address → waiting (skipped, never doubled — the coordinator's judgment) · no address on the row → no contact on file · `failed` → re-queued as the next copy through the existing `resend_receipt` → sent · no email row at all → the first-time `queue_receipt_for_recorded_payment` (idempotent on copy 0) → sent · `sent`/`delivered` → already sent · bounced/complained/unsubscribed → could not be delivered · held → address on hold. Reading the status stays right if a later lane makes provider failures keep retrying instead of resting `failed` (they then simply read as waiting).
3. **Bulk Reapply moves only what the payment still HOLDS as credit**, onto its account's open bills oldest first, releasing nothing it already meets (`release=()`) — the account screen's *Apply now*, per ticked payment. The ruling's case (5 lockbox cheques that arrived before their bills) is exactly that; a payment sitting on the WRONG bill is still corrected from its row's Reapply, where the clerk names the bill. The held amount is capped by the account's credit position, because a refund draws on the account, not a payment. Worked: cheque $76.40 recorded with no open bill, bill BL-PJR-000 $76.40 issued after → **Reapply → $76.40 onto BL-PJR-000**; pressed again → *nothing to reapply*.
4. **Refused by name, never skipped:** still processing · reversed, cancelled or failed · a reversing row · a deposit or payment-plan down payment. The bar refuses these before sending (the same predicate the server applies); the audit reason on each bulk reapply reads *"Bulk reapply from the Payments list: held credit to open bills, oldest first"*. No confirm dialog: neither act collects anything from the clerk, and both are safe to repeat.

## 2026-10-30 — Lane PAY-FOR: the "Pay for…" screen and the "Credit on account" receipt BUILT — five judgments (recorded, not asked)

Builds Q4 = A (*"build the "Pay for…" screen as in the mock-up, all six pieces including the "Pay units" button"*, `DEF-PAY-10706`) and W4 = A (`DEF-PAY-10770`). **Worked, asserted:** Grand Vista (AC-2026-00618) pays units 101–108 with cheque #5521 for **$1,003.60** — nine bills on eight accounts (unit 103 owes September's $40.00 and October's $92.10) → **8 payments**, every bill paid, eight balanced entries, nothing on the master; **$1,003.61** → *Left to allocate $0.01*, Record payment blocked, nothing sent; **$1,023.60** with **$20.00** typed on the master's row → 9 payments, the master's $20.00 meets no bill and carries as its credit; no open counter → the server's till sentence, nothing written. Hugo Hollis pays **$68.00** cash meeting no bill → the receipt prints **"Credit on account $68.00"** (it printed "Balance remaining $0.00"); a $165.00 bill paid $100.00 → "Balance remaining $65.00". Tests: `06-backend/tests/test_def_pay_10706_pay_for_screen_body.py`, `test_def_pay_10770_receipt_credit.py` (SQLite and PostgreSQL 16, non-superuser NOBYPASSRLS role), `payForSeveral.dom.test.tsx`, `payUnitsDoor.dom.test.tsx`, `printReceipt.dom.test.tsx`.
1. **Which server route is called is decided by the payer's KIND, not by a control.** A master account → `POST /accounts/{id}/premises-payments` (its units); any other account → that account's CUSTOMER → `POST /customers/{id}/payments` (the customer's accounts). The mock-up draws one picker, *Landlord or customer*, so the screen has one picker and no second switch. An account with no customer link says *"No customer on this account."*
2. **Each account is one part; each box is one bill.** The boxes are per bill (unit 103 shows two); the server's parts are per account, so an account's boxes are summed into one part with `apply_to: "split"` and a target per bill. A box at 0.00 is not sent. Each box starts at what its bill still owes (the mock-up's first state); the clerk types the cheque amount and *Left to allocate* reaches $0.00.
3. **The master's row posts `carry_credit`, and the master's OWN open bills are not listed.** The mock-up draws units and the credit row only. With `carry_credit` the leftover is held as the landlord's credit rather than silently meeting a hallway bill the clerk was never shown. On a customer's accounts the row is the picked account's; if that account also has bills on the screen, the credit is added to its part and what no target takes carries as credit.
4. **The "not ready" sentence is the kit's blocked-commit strip, not a line in the box.** The mock-up writes *"Allocate the rest first."* inside the "what this will do" box; the kit's `FormPage` states why a commit is disabled in its own strip above the buttons (BR-SHL-025), so the box says only what will happen (*"8 payments · $1,003.60 · From one Cheque #5521. Ready to record."*) and the strip says *"Allocate the rest first."* / *"More allocated than paid."* (B14 rule 44: our UI standard builds what the drawing arranges.) The mock-up's purple *NOT IN THE DRAWING* marks are review marks and are not built.
5. **"Pay units" carries the master in router STATE, never the URL** (B14 rule 31), and sits after *Close out* in the account's action row, shown only on a master, with Record payment's guard. A refresh on the opened page loses the pre-fill and leaves the clerk on *One account* — the cost of keeping the id out of the address. **W4:** the receipt reads the same signed net position the account header reads (`ar_positions(with_held_credit=True)`); the receipt EMAIL's figure is unchanged (the flag stays off for it) — one surface per ruling.

## 2026-10-31 — P1 and P2 built: three lane judgments where the ruling left the detail open (lane STMT-3)

Built to *"Twelve open payment questions answered (PO)"* P1 (a1-3, a2-2, a2-3) and P2 = A — `DEF-PAY-10785`…`10788`. Three details the ruling did not state, decided here and not put back to the PO (law 13):
1. **Which number is "the cheque number from the line" (a2-3).** The bank's text is free words, so the server serves `search_hint` = the **last number of three or more digits standing on its own** in the line's text: `RET1029-01 CHK 4102` → `4102`; `RETURNED ITEM #4103` → `4103`; `RET1029-01` → nothing (1029 is glued to RET, 01 is two digits), and the search then opens empty and lists every amount match, as before. It only fills a box the clerk can clear; candidates are still filtered by amount, date and deposit. One function, `bankrec_read.cheque_number_in`, read by both screens.
2. **Blank vs untouched Bank memo (a2-2).** The form always sends what the box holds when it reverses: edited words are the reversal's memo, a box the clerk empties means **no memo**, over 60 characters is refused before anything moves. A request that sends no `bank_memo` at all keeps the line's own words (the 2026-10-30 behaviour). A match that **links** to a hand reversal reverses nothing, so the memo box is not shown and nothing is sent — that reversal keeps the memo it was given.
3. **Where a1-3's words sit.** On the import review the FIX cell reads *In the books* then `RET1029-01 → Clara Castillo · AC-2026-00003`; on Reconciliation's *In the books* panel the reference cell reads the same sentence. Account NUMBER, never an id (B14 rule 31); a part the server cannot name is left out, and a fee line (no payment) shows just its reference.
P2: the reconciliation row's two buttons come from the server (`actions`, money-out lines only) and open the **same** `MatchReturnForm` / `BankFeeForm` and the same two endpoints as the import review — no second form, no second server path. Worked on PostgreSQL 16: 4103 reversed by hand on 3 Nov, RET1029-02 matched from Reconciliation **links** (one reversal, not two), holding 0.00, cash 616.10 = bank 616.10, Bank fees 24.00 once.

## 2026-10-31 — FB-023: what the technician sees about money on a field job (PO, F1–F6)

Analysis put to the PO: every phone treats every technician as a contractor (the phone never learns "employee"; downloaded jobs carry no account; nothing loads on open), so FB-013's cleared-balance rules (2026-10-28) cannot be reached on a real phone. Proposal of fields shown: balance owed, its age, last payment (amount · date · Posted/Cleared), tender name, reconnect fee, the verdict line, payment plan, disconnect notice, owed when reconnect was asked. Never card or bank details.
**PO, verbatim:** *"F1 … A check live when the job opens (keep the last figure with its age when offline) · F2 … A yes: the step stops, and "posted, not cleared" is shown and saved · F3 … A only technicians on a contractor crew (as the server does today) · F4 … B a fifth tick "Balance & payments" · F5 … A yes, disconnect jobs only · F6 … A make the phone honour all four"*.
1. **F1 = A** — the balance is checked live when a job's money screen opens; offline, the last figure is shown with its age. No balance is carried in the morning download.
2. **F2 = A** — a POSTED (not yet bank-cleared) payment counts as paid for the step: the step stops, and "posted, not cleared" is shown and saved with the close.
3. **F3 = A** — a technician is a contractor only when on a contractor crew (`money._is_contractor`, as the server does today); staff on no crew see money. The phone learns this from the morning download.
4. **F4 = B — a fifth template tick "Balance & payments"** under *What the technician sees on the job* (coordinator recommended always-on; the PO chose the tick). **Coordinator judgment, recorded under law 13 rather than asked:** the tick controls whether the BALANCE CARD and payment facts are DISPLAYED; it does NOT switch off FB-013's safety check — a disconnect step still reads the balance and still stops with "Balance cleared. Do not disconnect." when it is cleared (2026-10-28 FB-013, signed), whatever the tick. Default for existing templates: ticked (so nothing visible today disappears).
5. **F5 = A** — payment plan status and the disconnect notice (type · date · amount) are shown on DISCONNECT jobs only (new server fields through the payments/customers seams).
6. **F6 = A** — the phone honours all four existing ticks (Account & premise summary · Asset card · Access notes & hazards · Appointment window & customer phone) — today they are saved and ignored.
Not yet built; the round ends with one APK (2026-10-31).

## 2026-10-31 — FB-022: a lower reading is warned, never refused; several readings in one cycle are all accepted (PO)

Context: DevOps's log for FB-022 (City of Houston, 29 Oct 10:34:58 UTC) shows `field_reads.sync_reads` line 1348 deleting a reading the engine turned away while its photo in the same batch still points at it (`FieldRead.photo_for`, protected) → `ProtectedError` → 500 on every resend. **PO, verbatim:** *"reading refusal : if the current reading is less than previous reading it shows warning to technician , but do not refuse the reading accept"* and *"also accept multiple readings for one cycle in same month"*.
1. **A reading lower than the previous one is ACCEPTED** — stored and posted with a "lower than the last reading" warning flag, never refused by the server (supersedes the engine treating it as an ERROR that refuses the row; consistent with BR-FLD-00081 "the handset warns and accepts" and BR-MET-129 "warnings post with their flags and are dispositioned after commit"). The technician sees the warning on the phone before saving (as today) and nothing is refused after sync.
2. **Several readings of one meter in one billing cycle (one month) are ALL ACCEPTED** — extends BR-MET-1189 (two readings on the same DATE are both kept) to different dates within the cycle; none is refused as a duplicate.
**Open, put to the PO the same turn:** which reading BILLS when one is lower than the last, and which of several readings in a cycle bills.

## 2026-10-31 — P7, P8, P9, P11 and P12 built: four lane judgments where the ruling left the detail open (lane PAY-L)

Built to *"Twelve open payment questions answered (PO)"* P7, P8, P9, P11 and P12 = A — `DEF-RAT-10739`, `DEF-PAY-10782`, `DEF-PAY-10778`, `DEF-PAY-10783`, `DEF-MET-10784`. Four details the ruling did not state, decided here and not put back to the PO (law 13):
1. **P7 — one NSF fee per PLAN, refused where it would be made.** The bounce already refuses two marked codes on one plan by name (*"Two NSF fees on this plan. None charged."*), so the tick refuses to CREATE that state: ticking `RETCHK` on a plan that already lists `NSF` reads *"{plan} already charges NSF."*, and a plan's Charges list naming two marked codes reads *"NSF is this plan's NSF fee."* It is per plan, not per utility — two plans may each charge a different code, which is what the walk Account › Unit › Plan › Charge code is for. Worked: `RETCHK` $35.00 ticked → cheque 4102 ($76.40) bounces → the account owes **$111.40**.
2. **P8 — the amount is NOT compared.** The ruled words are *"same card/ACH reference repeats on the same account and day"*, so `AUTH 88412` for $40.00 and then $12.00 the same day warns the second. One authorisation is one payment. Only `card` and `ach` carry an authorisation; a cash note is never matched, and a cheque number stays `BR-PAY-880`'s refusal. The 2026-10-03 test case *"same AUTH-S8-0030, $30.01"* moved from "saved silently" to "warned". BR-PAY-1199 and its review-ledger row say so; the review row puts the amount question back on the agenda in plain words rather than as a question now.
3. **P11 — which ONE warning, when a payment carries several.** Money first: *open bills could not be read* (not applied), then *awaiting finance approval* (not in the books), then the replay, then *a receipt has no recipient*. The figures (received, applied, credit, the bills met) are facts and stay; the ledger sentence and *"This money met no bill…"* are deleted (B14 rule 33), and the receipt number moves into the first sentence: **"Recorded. Receipt # PY-261031-0007"**.
4. **P12 — the sentence stays at six words.** The ruled example reads *"This file was already loaded as IMP-…"* — seven words, over G33's six-word cap for a refusal. The catalogue already says **"File already loaded as IMP-0012."**, the same fact in plain words, so it is kept; what the PO saw and objected to was the line UNDER it, *"HTTP 409 · BIZ-IDEMPOTENT · ref …"*. That support line is now drawn only for a failure with no sentence (nothing answered, a 5xx, the generic *Something went wrong*, or a key no catalogue holds), on all seven import targets, at upload and at commit — the reference still reaches support on the strip's `data-br-ref`, in the audit row and in the server log.

## 2026-10-31 — Which reading bills: a lower reading waits for a clerk; the latest approved reading in a cycle bills (PO, R1 A · R2 A)

Put as question · real example · options. **PO, verbatim:** *"R1 - A R2 - A"*.
- **R1 = A — a reading lower than the last is NOT billed until a clerk reviews it** (rollover, misread or meter change). Worked: previous 4,812, new 4,790 → stored with "lower than last reading", excluded from billing; the bill run treats that meter as having no usable reading for the cycle (the tenant's existing missing-reading behaviour — estimate or hold — applies) until the clerk dispositions it (accept as rollover / mark misread / meter change). No automatic rollover.
- **R2 = A — with several readings in one cycle, the LATEST approved reading bills.** Worked: cycle 1–31 Oct, readings 5,010 (10 Oct), 5,140 (24 Oct), 5,155 (30 Oct) → 5,155 bills. **Coordinator judgment (law 13, recorded):** BR-MET-1189 (2026-10-04, two readings on the SAME DATE → the highest approved & validated counts) stands for a same-date tie; R2 picks across dates (latest date wins; on that date, BR-MET-1189's highest). A reading under R1's review is not "approved" and is skipped, so the latest approved one before it bills.
🔒 Billing-selection change → `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` with a review-ledger row stating these two worked figures.

## 2026-10-31 — FB-033: availability from the phone reaches the office (PO, D1–D4)

Analysis: the phone saves Available / On break / Off duty locally only; its send is a stub that always fails ("Dispatch not told yet."); the server has no door, no "on break" value, no "since" time; the web reads `technicians.status` correctly but it never moves. **PO, verbatim:** *"D1 - A D2 -A D3 -A D4 - B"*.
- **D1 = A** — assigning a job to an Off-duty technician **warns (red) and is allowed** (2026-09-23 ruling 2: a guideline, never a block). Worked: Dana Off duty at 16:10, WO-4830 assigned for tomorrow → red "Off duty" warning, assignment accepted.
- **D2 = A** — **On break is a warning only** (the phone already tells the technician emergencies still reach them).
- **D3 = A** — jobs already assigned stay with the technician when they go Off duty; the office board marks them "assignee off duty" for a dispatcher to decide; nothing moves automatically.
- **D4 = B — Off duty and End shift are SEPARATE.** **Coordinator judgment (law 13, recorded):** Off duty is a status the technician sets and can undo the same day (Off duty → Available puts them back), stored with its time and history; it records NO shift end. End shift keeps its own rule unchanged (BR-WRK-069: `off_today`, a `TechnicianShiftEnd` record, reset next morning, one per day); after End shift the phone's chip reads Off duty (it is off for the rest of the day) but the two facts stay distinct in history and on the web (Crews: "Off duty · since 15:30" vs "Shift ended · 17:02").
Also recorded (coordinator judgments in the analysis): an office-set Unavailable beats anything the phone sends; a late offline change counts from the tap time and never overwrites a newer office change. Not yet built (awaiting "start").

## 2026-10-31 — FB-023 built: the judgments the rulings left to the lane (law 13, recorded rather than asked)

Built on the PO's F1–F6 of the same date (entry *"FB-023: what the technician sees about money on a field job"*). Worked case throughout: Aaron Bruner's $241.38 disconnect.
1. **Where the phone learns employee/contractor (F3).** The phone syncs through the change feed, never `GET work/mobile/today`, so `technician.employment` rides on EVERY change-feed page as well as on the day read, from `money.employment_of` — the same contractor-crew test the money read withholds by. A phone that has not heard (an older server) hides the money AND shows no *Contractor* chip, because that word would be untrue.
2. **What a "disconnect job" is (F5).** One raised to disconnect: `work_orders.source` is `disconnect` (the wizard's cut visit) or `dunning_auto` (the non-pay rule). A disconnect a dispatcher raised by hand reads `dispatcher` and carries no plan or notice — the server does not guess from the type's name (R18).
3. **Plan status (F5).** Only an ACTIVE plan has a status; a proposed or unsigned plan reads as none. *Behind* = at least one instalment due before today not met by its due date (payments' own `outstanding_installments`, judged on the posting date). Worked: plan of 6 × $45.00 from 15 Aug, Aug paid, Sep and Oct not → on 20 Oct *Behind* (2 missed); all three paid on their due dates → *On track*.
4. **The notice (F5).** The LATEST notice on the account's OPEN disconnect case: its type (Reminder / 10-day / 48-hour), its date, and the case's *amount owed at open* — notices carry no amount of their own. A notice on a closed case is history and reads as none. Worked: *48-hour notice · 16 Oct · $241.38*.
5. **The last figure (F1).** Kept on the handset per technician and per JOB (a shared tablet never shows one login's figure to another), with the server's own as-at stamp; it leaves with the job. The money is read per job, so a job need not know its account.
6. **"Posted, not cleared." (F2)** is SAVED with every paid close; it is SHOWN only while *Balance & payments* is ticked, like every other payment fact. The stop itself is the same either way (owing $0.00).
7. **The four ticks on the phone (F6).** *Account & premise summary* off hides the customer's name and account number — the ADDRESS and *Navigate* stay, because the technician still has to get there. *Asset card* off hides FF-15's asset card, FF-25's meter card and the meter number on FF-26/27. *Access notes & hazards* off hides the premise notes on FF-28. *Appointment window & customer phone* off hides the window on FF-15/FF-25 and the *Call* button.
8. **The fifth tick on Reconnect (F4).** Off: the arrears and fee cards are hidden and the plain *Leave it off / Reconnect* pair is shown; what the phone knew (fee outstanding, a stale figure) still travels with the close for the office (C1: a reconnect is never refused for owing).

## 2026-10-31 — FB-022 built: what the lane decided where the two rulings left detail open (lane FB-022)

Built to *"FB-022: a lower reading is warned, never refused…"* and *"Which reading bills… (PO, R1 A · R2 A)"* — `DEF-MET-10796`, `DEF-MET-10797`, `DEF-FLD-10793..10795`. Judgments recorded here, not put back to the PO (law 13):
1. **The 500 itself (`DEF-MET-10796`) is fixed for EVERY refusal, not only the lower reading.** A reading the pipeline still refuses (any other engine error, or the pipeline refusing the batch) now takes what hangs off it: a photo added to it is refused `photo_reading_refused`, a late position `position_reading_refused`, each naming the reading's key and reason; both rows and the photo's pending upload link are deleted in the same transaction; nothing acknowledged, so the phone keeps both and a replay gets the same answer. Reproduced first exactly as DevOps's log: `ProtectedError … 'FieldRead.photo_for'`.
2. **"Accepted with a warning" is built at the FIELD door only.** A field reading whose ONLY engine error is `negative_usage` is posted (`accept_with_flag`, reason naming FB-022); its status stays `negative_usage` and its consumption stays EMPTY (BR-MET-052: never invented). An office file keeps BR-MET-052's resolve-before-post — the ruling was about the technician.
3. **R1 is read as "awaiting a clerk" = status `negative_usage`** (`selectors.AWAITING_REVIEW_READ_STATUSES`). Billing skips such a reading when it picks the closing reading; with none left in the period the meter is the missing-reading case (`no_read` → the tenant's estimate-or-hold), NOT the `read_flagged` exception it would have been.
4. **And a later reading is not measured from it** (`services._prior_actual_head`). Not asked of the PO, and it is what R1 means in money: 4,812 → 4,790 (flagged) → 4,900 measures **88**, never **110**. Without it, accepting lower readings would have over-billed the month after every misread.
5. **R2 needed no new code beyond 3**: billing already closes at the latest head in the period and sums the chain (`DEF-BIL-9016`), so 5,010 / 5,140 / 5,155 → **5,155**; with 4,790 as the latest and awaiting a clerk → **5,140**. BR-MET-1189 still decides a same-date tie.
6. **Several readings in one cycle were already stored** (only the SAME value in the same cycle is BR-MET-016's error); the test now proves all three are kept.
7. **Gap, filed not built:** a clerk's tools for a flagged reading today are *correct the value* (supersede) and the asset exchange. There is no "accept as rollover" for a reading posted with `negative_usage` and no consumption — the billing-side rollover accept (`DEF-BIL-9076`) covers a wrap the engine already computed.

## 2026-10-31 — FB-030: a technician's history is the last 14 days, kept on the phone (PO)

FB-030: the technician cannot look back at readings taken and work orders completed. Analysis: history screens show only the phone's own cache (closed jobs and turned-in routes purged at 14 days, photos deleted on server receipt — R61), a job closed on the web or another phone never appears in Completed (the card carries no outcome or completed time), and on a phone the Completed card opens no record. **PO, verbatim:** *"this is right user wants to keep last 14 days work as a reference after that completed jobs and sync pictures can be removed from phone /tab"*; and to "how far back": *"14 days"*.
**So:** history is **14 days, on the device** — no "Earlier" tab and no server history list beyond 14 days (the analysis's S2/S4/S5 and P4/P5 are dropped). **R61 is SUPERSEDED for this one point:** a photo's file is kept on the phone/tablet until its job or route leaves the 14-day window, then deleted with it (never before server receipt — that half of R61 stands). **Coordinator judgments (law 13):** (1) the server's job card carries outcome and completed time, so a job closed on the web or another phone shows in Completed for its 14 days; (2) a new phone, a reinstall or a remote sign-out is refilled with the technician's last 14 days of closed jobs and turned-in routes on first sync, so the reference survives a lost handset (photos for refilled work load on tap, not stored); (3) a Completed card opens the full record on phones (problem, what was done, readings with units, parts by quantity, signature, photos), and the phone keeps the debrief and signer it used to discard; (4) My reads drills into each reading of a route; (5) no money and no speed figures in history; (6) storage: 14 days of photos is estimated well under the 500 MB footprint target and the existing 200 MB document cap is separate.

FB-031: a job's help document (e.g. "Meter exchange SOP") never opens; the phone says "Downloads at next sync" for ever. Analysis found three faults: (1) the template's "Meter exchange" starter pack adds the SOP and phone rows EMPTY (no file, no number) and the phone mislabels "no file" as a pending download; (2) the 4-hour storage link is never renewed after one failed download; (3) the shipped app has no document opener wired, so even a downloaded file shows "Cannot open this file." Put to the PO: **A** in-app viewer (adds a few MB) · **B** hand it to the phone's own PDF app. **PO, verbatim:** *"B. Hand it to the phone's own PDF app ("Open with…"). Simpler, but it leaves our app, and a phone without a PDF app can't open it."*
**So:** a downloaded document opens through the operating system's "Open with…" (Android: a content URI to the installed viewer; iOS: the system share/preview sheet). **Coordinator judgments (law 13):** the file is still downloaded and stored on the device for offline use; a phone with no app able to open the file shows "No app can open this." (B14 rule 33); the phone is served the file from our own API with the technician's credential (never-expiring, own-job only) instead of a 4-hour storage link; a failed download re-fetches the job's bundle next sync; "No file attached." and "No number." replace the false "Downloads at next sync"; a template cannot be published with a document row lacking a file or a phone row lacking a number; a file added to a template reaches open, not-started jobs.
