**Same day, photos 3 days (PO).** Shown where history lives (menu › Work › Completed: Today · This week · Earlier; menu › Reads › My reads: This week · This cycle · Earlier), what a record shows, and an estimate of 50–200 MB for 14 days of photos. **PO, verbatim:** *"keep photos only for 3 days"*. **So:** job and reading RECORDS stay on the device 14 days; a photo's FILE stays 3 days (from its job's close or its route's turn-in, and never before the server has it), then is deleted. **Coordinator judgment (law 13):** a photo older than 3 days still appears in the record and loads on tap from the server (own work only, short-lived link, not stored); with no signal it reads "Needs signal". Estimate: ~10–40 MB of photos on the device.

## 2026-10-31 — FB-033 built: the judgments the rulings left to the lane (law 13, recorded rather than asked)

Built on the PO's D1–D4 of the same date (entry *"FB-033: availability from the phone reaches the office (PO, D1–D4)"*; `DEF-FLD-10799`, `BR-WRK-072`). Worked case: Dana Field.
1. **What a late tap does.** The tap carries the moment it was pressed (moved onto the server's clock, FB-014). It moves the status only if it is not older than the status's own time (`technicians.status_since`). Worked: *On break* pressed at 10:42 with no signal; the office sets her status at 11:00; the tap arrives at 11:20 → kept in the history (`applied = false`, `newer_change`), status unchanged. A tap more than 5 minutes ahead of the server is refused ("That time has not come yet.").
2. **Office *Unavailable* wins, always.** A phone tap while she is Unavailable is recorded (`office_unavailable`) and changes nothing; only the office sets her back. The office can no longer set *On break* or *Off duty* by hand (those are the technician's words); its three are unchanged.
3. **After End shift.** *Off duty* or *On break* tapped after End shift is recorded and leaves *Shift ended* in place (`shift_ended`) — End shift is the more specific fact. *Available* after End shift DOES apply: she has come back.
4. **Next morning.** An *Off duty* or *On break* left from an earlier day is returned to *on shift* by the existing hourly morning sweep on her next working day (as End shift is, BR-WRK-069), one audit row each. An office Unavailable is never touched.
5. **What the office sees.** Crews and the technician page: *Off duty · since 15:30*, *On break · since 10:42*, *Shift ended · 17:02* (an *Off today* the office set by hand reads *Off today*, because no End shift holds it). The assign picker: a red *Off duty since 16:10* pill or a warning *On break since 10:42* beside the name — whatever day the job is for (D1's worked case is a job for tomorrow) — and the name stays choosable. *Off that day* is not shown beside *Off duty*. The schedule board: an Off-duty technician still holding jobs that day reads *Assignee off duty* (D3).
6. **The phone.** The tap goes through the outbox (kind `availability`), so it sends when there is signal, once. After each sync the phone reads the office's status back: an office *Unavailable* shows on the chip; after End shift the chip reads *Off duty*. A tap still waiting to send is never overwritten by the read-back. "Dispatch not told yet." is retired.
7. **Advice reads the utility's own today.** `advice.py` asked about the SERVER's date (`date.today()`), so from 19:00 in a UTC−5 utility *off today* was asked about tomorrow. It now uses the utility's zone.

## 2026-10-31 — FB-028 built: the judgments the rulings left to the lane (law 13, recorded rather than asked)

Built on the PO's three FB-028 rulings of the same date (W2 = B; W1 + W3 = C; field-raised disconnects = B and the limit on the template). Defects `DEF-WRK-10800`, `DEF-WRK-10801`, `DEF-FLD-10802`, `DEF-FLD-10803`. Worked figures throughout: Patel/Dana at 77 Cedar Ct, $18.40 and $804.50 against a $25.00 limit; a 10-day notice of 26 Oct ending 5 Nov.
1. **"At or below" is inclusive.** The PO's words were *"reduces below 25 dollors"*; the coordinator's entry reads *"at or below"*. Built inclusive: $25.00 exactly enables Reconnect. Compared as digits at 4 places, never as a float.
2. **Which jobs are gated: only those RAISED ON SITE** (a `work_field_raises` row exists). The office-requested reconnect (2026-10-29 C1) is never refused for owing, unchanged. A job carries no gate when its template has no Reconnect limit.
3. **Templates already carrying a payment check get $25.00** (`work/0064` data step), so day one is gated at the PO's figure rather than not at all. A new template's limit appears in the builder when a step ticks *Check payment*, prefilled 25.00. With no payment check nothing is sent (null).
4. **The notice period** is the open case's latest notice date plus the days its tier names — 10-day notice +10, 48-hour notice +2; a Reminder starts no disconnect period. The period's last day still stops (*"Notice period ends 5 Nov. Leave it on."* on 31 Oct and on 5 Nov; free on 6 Nov). No notice at all does not stop the step (not ruled; reported).
5. **"Protected" = any protection customers holds in force**: a medical certificate, a kept payment plan, or a weather moratorium (B18 §5.8.3's three) — the same list the ladder itself may not cut through.
6. **"The office is told"** = one `audit_log` row (`work.order.step_stopped`, reason and the figure the phone saw) and the existing back-office *blocked* notice, once per job and reason. A fifth notice kind is the notifications module's call.
7. **Stale on a raised reconnect cannot pass** (*"Check the balance with signal."*); a CONTRACTOR (R26, no figure) cannot pass either and reads *"Ask the office to check the balance."* — *Reconnect anyway* is not offered on a gated job.
8. **A raised disconnect with no figure ever read waits** (*"Check the balance with signal."*), because its notice and protection are unknown. With an OLD figure, R17's warning still governs the balance, but the notice and protection it carried still stop the step (dates and a list, not a balance).
9. **W3's warning sits on the job page (FF-15)**, above Start, from the job's own copy of the advice (`details.skill_advice`), so it shows offline too.
10. **The raise is not pushed** (the raiser's own phone made the call and fetches the job after the answer). The *Raised on site* row still lands `pending`; *Accept* now reads *"Marks it seen. It stays assigned."* and changes no assignment; *Refuse* still cancels with a reason.
11. **After Send the screen stays** with *Send now* and *Open job* (W2 = B: no provisional job). *Open job* goes live when the server's answer has put the numbered job on Today; *Done* goes back where FF-37 was opened.

## 2026-10-31 — FB-031 built: the judgments the ruling left to the lane (law 13, recorded rather than asked)

Built to the PO's **B** and the coordinator judgments above (`DEF-FLD-10805`, rules `BR-FLD-00136` and `BR-WRK-073`). Where the detail was still open the lane chose, and records why:

1. **A typed label on a document row is marked, not refused.** The ruling says a template cannot be published *"with a document row lacking a file"*. Publish is refused for an EMPTY document row (and a phone row with no digit), which is the starter pack's case. A row naming a typed label written before uploads existed (*STD-EL-004*, the sample data's five; *SOP-114* in 69 test files) is shown *No file* on the builder and *No file attached.* on the phone, and still publishes — refusing it would stop every such template from being republished until somebody finds a file for it. If the PO wants those refused too, it is one line in `templates_svc._refuse_empty_help`.
2. **"Not started" = planned, and queued, scheduled or on the way.** A job ON SITE, completed, on hold or cancelled keeps the help it was given (the record of what the technician had in hand); only help moves, never the other five copies.
3. **The refresh happens when the help collection is saved**, not at publish — jobs are already copied from the template's current rows at creation, so the same rows reaching not-started jobs is the consistent reading. The job's `updated_at` is touched so the phone's change feed sends it again and the bundle is re-fetched.
4. **The phone stores no new column.** The fetch address is kept in `document.url` (our own path, with the file's name as the `#fragment` so the copy keeps its extension and the phone's own app knows its type); `url` empty on a server document = *No file attached.* No handset migration, so no collision with another lane's.
5. **"Older than four hours" is measured from when the bundle wrote the row** (`document.updated_at`), which is when the link was issued to the phone. Only a STORAGE link ages; our own route never expires.
6. **iOS cannot say "no app"** — the system sheet always opens (Quick Look, Files). *No app can open this.* fires on Android (no activity for the intent) and on an iOS build with no sheet at all.
7. **Native modules:** `expo-intent-launcher ~12.1.5` and `expo-sharing ~13.1.5`, the versions `npx expo install` picks for SDK 53; neither needs a config plugin. OTA is off, so this reaches a phone only in a new native build.


## 2026-10-31 — FB-030 built: what the lane decided where the two rulings left detail open (lane FB-030)

Built under the PO's two FB-030 rulings above (*"14 days"*; *"keep photos only for 3 days"*), `DEF-FLD-10806`. Where the rulings and the coordinator's judgments left a choice, the lane chose, and records it here (law 13: ours to decide and write down).
1. **"Own" for a closed job = held it at the close (the assignee) OR logged crew time on it (`work_order_labour`), completed inside 14 days** (`mobile._history_q`). One predicate, used by the first sync's refill, the delta, the bundle, the job-photo door and the GET evidence routes (`require_own_record`). **Every write door keeps `_own_job_or_404` (assignee only)** — a helper reading history can never close, reopen or change the job. Day 15 is a 404 for a helper; the assignee's admission to their own job is unchanged.
2. **The refill is the change feed's existing full pass, widened** — no new endpoint for jobs. A no-cursor first sync now sends the open jobs AND the 14-day closed ones; the delta also carries a helper's job when the lead closes it. Paged by the feed's keyset, no cap (NFR-3/5).
3. **A closed job's bundle carries a `record`** (debrief from `field_data.problem_found`/`what_i_did`, the signature's kind, name or reason, and time, and the photographs by the phone's own id). No money, no speed: no balance, no labour/travel minutes, no part price — the tablet record's labour and travel figures and the card's labour minutes were REMOVED from history on both form factors (judgment (5)).
4. **Route readings refill through a new metering door, `GET work/mobile/reads/history`** (the reader's own readings on routes they turned in during the 14 days, paged in SQL), asked ONCE per technician per store (`sync_state` `route_history`), re-asked only if a refill was cut short. **No new index**: `field_reads.reader_id` is a foreign key and already carries an index; on PostgreSQL 16 the read is served by it (a composite `(tenant, reader, received_at)` was drafted as metering `0083`, measured, found unneeded and withdrawn before push — one fewer 🔒 migration).
5. **"Short-lived link, never stored" is built as a credentialed same-origin read, not a bearer URL**: `GET work/mobile/photos/{photo_id}/content` (job) and `GET work/mobile/reads/photos/{photo_id}/content` (route), `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, requested only on a TAP and shown with `cache: 'reload'`. Stricter than a 4-hour bearer link (nothing that outlives the request leaves the server) and needs no new storage kind for route photographs, whose bytes live on `field_read_photos`. Own work only: a job photo by rule 1, a route photo by its `reader_id`.
6. **The phone keeps what it captured**: a server-completed card fills `closed_at`/`outcome` only where empty; a bundle's record and reading values fill only where empty; a refilled reading never overwrites one with the same capture key.
7. **A turned-in route of the last 14 days stays on the phone even when the server stops listing it** (it is history, not an assignment); one older goes with the purge.
8. **FB-022's "lower than last" on a refilled reading is the server's word** (`meter_reads.status = negative_usage`), stored in a new phone column `route_read.lower_than_last` (phone migration 0007); on the phone's own readings it is derived from the previous value (`figures.verdict`).
9. **A photo whose job and route have both left the phone** (taken away by the office): its file and row go 7 days after the upload — the sent-work figure — since there is no record left to show it in.
10. **The drill**: My reads' route card still opens RW-27; RW-27 now lists every reading taken on the route (paged), and a reading opens its record as RW-28 pushed with a `readId`. No new screen id (the 92-screen design table is unchanged).
